31.relation: Maps Alexis Korner's 'primitivistic' Hendrix onto the pre-Socratic element theories: Thales's water returns in the submarine Atlantis of '1983' and 'Valleys of Neptune,' Anaximenes's rarefaction and condensation in the flight and storm imagery, and Empedocles's Love and Strife in the Monterey burning — a sacrifice motivated by love, set against the Strife of 'Machine Gun,' 'Izabella,' and 'House Burning Down.' Heraclitus's unity of opposites and logos explain the fire-water paradox lyrics ('that crying blue rain that's burning my eyes,' 'If 6 was 9'), while Berkeley's tree in the forest shows how the audible emerges from mere vibration, as musical sound emerges from feedback and noise.

32.title: Historical Note
32.relation: A British music writer's memoir-historical corrective: the 'Swinging Sixties' existed only in west London while provincial Britain remained grey and make-do-and-mend, but the blues boom of Cream, Mayall, the Yardbirds, and the Animals prepared the seedbed into which Hendrix landed in 1966 — a 'quantum blues leap' that still felt familiar. With comparatively milder (if passive-aggressive) racism, Chas Chandler, Noel Redding, and Mitch Mitchell, five UK Top Twenty singles against one American hit, McCartney's Monterey recommendation, and Keith Altham's guitar-burning idea, it was Britain that set him on his way.

9.title: The Devil Made Us Write This
9.file: ch09 - The Devil Made Us Write This.md
9.relation: The editors' introduction argues that American Horror Story is 'American' in its maximalist excess (the pilot's creepy house, breathing disemboweled cat, and bloody murder), in recycling every major American horror trope from vampires, witches, and ghosts to freak shows and slasher clowns, and in its social commentary on marginalized groups, race relations, and civil rights - so that stripped of horror it is about life in America, and underneath the gore it contains 'a lot of great philosophy', which the book's sixteen chapters extract.

10.title: I. Goddesses don’t speak in whispers. They scream
10.file: ch10 - I. Goddesses don’t speak in whispers. They scream.md

11.title: 1. What’s So Scary about Demonic Possession
11.file: ch11 - 1. What’s So Scary about Demonic Possession.md
11.relation: Using the Asylum possession arc - the boy who rips open the pig's heart, the demon exposing Sister Jude's hit-and-run secret and whispering 'You're Bloody Face' to Thredson, and Sister Mary Eunice's corruption - the chapter argues that possession stories terrify because they break our identity judgments through time, the same judgments on which moral responsibility, criminal punishment (the Manson family parole cases, Phineas Gage), trust, and personal safety depend. Descartes's mind-body union and psychological-continuity theories of identity explain why sameness of body can no longer guarantee sameness of person, and why we fear our own identity being erased next.

12.title: 2. A Death Worth Living
12.file: ch12 - 2. A Death Worth Living.md
12.relation: Argues that dying in the Murder House or the Hotel Cortez removes death's usual harms - Ben Harmon can reunite with his ghost family and keep counseling patients, and Liz Taylor's chosen death brings reunion with Tristan plus open-ended projects protecting the hotel - but then poses Bernard Williams's boredom problem: finite projects run out over eternity and replacing them would make you a different person. Richard Taylor's Sisyphus and the Hotel's contented Laundress supply the answer that repetitive tasks embraced as meaningful can sustain even an immortal afterlife.

13.title: 3. My Sister, My Self
13.file: ch13 - 3. My Sister, My Self.md
13.relation: Staged as a remembered backstage conversation among Elsa's freak show performers, the chapter has conjoined twins Bette and Dot work through the Ship of Theseus, the psychological-continuity theory of identity and its coma and false-memory counterexamples, Quine's claim that persons are only convenient posits rather than real entities, split-brain cases suggesting one body can host two minds, and fission worries about what would happen if they were separated - to ask whether they are one person or two, concluding it is a genuine paradox with no agreed answer.

14.title: 4. How to Live through a Horror Story and Still Find Your Self
14.file: ch14 - 4. How to Live through a Horror Story and Still Find Your Self.md
14.relation: A survival guide built on Charles Taylor's philosophy of the self: reality 'discloses' different possibilities depending on one's attunement (Ben Harmon sees the young Moira, the Harmons and the Roanoke families misread their houses), the medieval enchanted cosmos of porous selves explains Sister Mary Eunice's demon, the cursed rubber suit, and Billie Dean Howard's trauma-soaked houses, while the buffered self of the disenchanted universe - Arden locating the devil in the frontal gyrus, John Lowe demanding evidence - invites gaslighting, and full porousness brings its own horrors (Kyle, Cricket). The lesson: keep a pragmatic, open mind and share reality with a community.

15.title: 5. Other People’s Body Parts
15.file: ch15 - 5. Other People’s Body Parts.md
15.relation: Explains Kyle Spencer's horror at the body Madison and Zoe assembled from other people's parts through the history of soul-body theories: Aristotle's De Anima account of the soul as the faculties of a living body (plus the Physiognomonics claim that small people have small minds - poor Ma Petite), Plato's Timaeus on body parts designed for philosophy and reincarnation into bodies fitted to one's vices, Avicenna's soul as a faculty-binding nexus that chooses its bodily vehicle like a vehicle serves its owner, and Merleau-Ponty's habitual body (the Axeman's axe as part of his body, phantom limbs), which best explains why walking around on someone else's legs 'has got to mess with you a little'.

16.title: II. When bad things keep happening to good people, you start to question what is right and what is wrong
16.file: ch16 - II. When bad things keep happening to good people, you start to question what is right and what is wrong.md

17.title: 6. Horror Can Be Great Drama
17.file: ch17 - 6. Horror Can Be Great Drama.md
17.relation: Applies Aristotle's Poetics wholesale - mimesis of possible actions, the six elements of tragedy, complete plots of proper magnitude, reversal and recognition, hamartia, and catharsis as the perfecting of fear and pity - to argue that Murder House (Ben's lust as tragic flaw and his double reversal to redemption in death) and Asylum (Sister Jude's irascibility and pride punished then reformed) are genuine high tragedies, and then uses the Nicomachean Ethics (virtue as a mean between extremes; justice as both retributive and rehabilitative) to show the seasons teach virtue, while Coven, Freak Show, and Hotel fall short because their characters' fates are undeserved and the moral message goes murky.

18.title: 7. And the Most Despicable Jessica Lange Character Is . .
18.file: ch18 - 7. And the Most Despicable Jessica Lange Character Is . ..md
18.relation: Ranks Jessica Lange's characters from least to most despicable using moral philosophy: Sister Jude earns credit for acting from duty (reporting the Nazi Dr. Arden at personal risk, Kant-style) and for genuinely feeling remorse; Elsa Mars partly honors the matriarchal obligations of care ethics but lacks Aristotle's habitual virtue and moderation, selling Bette and Dot to Dandy for fame; Constance Langdon abuses and effectively murders her disabled children; and Fiona Goode, motivated exclusively by youth, beauty, and power, murders her Supreme and torments Cordelia - never once acting out of concern for others.

19.title: 8. Night of the Living Disabled
19.file: ch19 - 8. Night of the Living Disabled.md
19.relation: Reads Constance's treatment of Addy and Beau Langdon through the eugenic roots of the horror genre (Angela Smith's Hideous Progeny, The Black Stork, the Production Code): outward bodily difference assumed to prove inner defect, and the disabled treated as better off dead - Addy finding peace only as 'a pretty girl at last' after death, Beau suffocated in the attic. Against the medical model the chapter defends Alison Kafer's political-relational model and crip futurity (Tate's 'He only suffered because of you'), arguing that ableism, not disability itself, makes their lives unlivable and that imagining disabled futures differently is a matter of survival.

20.title: 9. Voodoo Hoodoo
20.relation: Explains Coven's Spirit Wars through the real history and philosophy of New Orleans Voodoo: the historical Marie Laveaux as healer and Voodoo Queen, Tituba as the link between witchcraft and Voodoo in Salem, the loa and spirit possession (Maya Deren's gros bon ange), zombies and the bokor, Papa Legba as trickster gatekeeper rather than Satan, and the seven gates of Guinee. It argues that Laveau's annual innocent and Fiona's failed soul-selling enact the Voodoo cosmology in which hell is the earthly entrapment of the soul - and, as Legba says, 'everybody pays.'

21.title: 10. Too Freaking Bad
21.file: ch21 - 10. Too Freaking Bad.md
21.relation: Reads Freak Show through Erving Goffman's Stigma - virtual versus actual social identity, the three types of stigma, discredited versus discreditable conditions, and spoiled identity - and through an analysis of exploitation, dignity, and consent: Elsa's claim that the real monsters are 'the people outside this tent', the courts' defense of freaks' right to perform, and the argument that Ryan Murphy's own casting - real disabled performers as window dressing behind able-bodied stars playing freaks, with roles too scarce for true consent - replicates the exploitation the season condemns, which may be the real horror story.

22.title: III. I have long stopped asking why the mad do mad things
22.file: ch22 - III. I have long stopped asking why the mad do mad things.md

23.title: 11. 999 Fingers
23.relation: Voiced by a composite being shredded together from every AHS character, the chapter retells the Buddha's path - Siddhartha sheltered from suffering like a pampered prince, enlightenment as watching 'every episode of American Horror Story', Mara's temptations, and Angulimala with his garland of 999 fingers converted to monkhood - to read Briarcliff's cruelty, Sister Jude's devil, and Bloody Face's son Johnny as suffering born of clinging, in a contingent, moment-to-moment world of karma and rebirth, while Nietzsche's killed God, eternal recurrence, and ressentiment frame the question of who is to blame when there is no creator.

24.title: 12. A Month from Now, I’ll Be a Balding, Toothless Skeleton
24.file: ch24 - 12. A Month from Now, I’ll Be a Balding, Toothless Skeleton.md
24.relation: Reads Fiona Goode's war against fading - the experimental RM47 serum, rejecting the Axeman's escape because he would watch her decay, the Papa Legba bargain that collapses because she has no soul - alongside Delphine LaLaurie's blood facials and Marie Laveau's child sacrifices, as illustrations of Buddhist dukkha and the three thirsts (kama for sense pleasure, bhava for existence, vibhava for annihilation). Legba's 'you don't have a soul' becomes an accidentally liberating glimpse of anatta, and Cordelia's dying advice - 'feel the fear... let it all go' - is the mindfulness, echoing Buddhaghosa's corpse meditations, that might have freed Fiona.

25.title: 13. Burn the Witch!
25.relation: Argues Coven is a feminist counterpoint to Aquinas's Natural Law - the reason-grounded doctrine of universal human nature historically wielded against 'unnatural' women, from Zoe's vagina-dentata power to Misty burned in the bayou - and, drawing on Augustine's Confessions ('Things that exist are good', so corruptibility implies goodness to lose) and Lady Macbeth's 'unsex me here', shows that women who are both witch and woman break any single natural moral code; Myrtle Snow, who embraces her double nature and goes 'proudly to the flame', proves Natural Law works only as Cupp-style discernment, not as commandments.

26.title: IV. I am tough, but I’m no cookie
26.file: ch26 - IV. I am tough, but I’m no cookie.md

27.title: 14. The Absurdity at the Heart of Horror
27.file: ch27 - 14. The Absurdity at the Heart of Horror.md
27.relation: Uses Camus's Myth of Sisyphus to argue that AHS's deepest horror is absurdity - the human quest for meaning in a meaningless universe: the Harmons' doomed attempts to protect each other in the Murder House mirror Sisyphus's futile push, Dr. Arden's experiments on aliens who mock him ('Arden you quack who would make a better duck?') show comprehension of the universe is beyond reach, the Countess's bored immortality and Ma Petite's casual murder stage the confrontation between human longing and a universe that cannot care, and the answer to 'why do bad things happen to good people?' is simply: 'because they do. There is no reason.'

28.title: 15. Red Harvest in Roanoke
28.relation: Reads Roanoke through ecocriticism and ecofeminism: the culture-nature dualism collapses as the urban Millers' wooded retreat turns predatory (rain of teeth, pig-men); the Butcher's backstory - a colonial woman starved by men whose blood-sacrifice pact makes the land flourish - aligns women and Nature as co-exploited by patriarchy, with Shelby's 'irrational' warnings ignored and Lee's maternal fury a force of nature; the animalizing of victims (pig-headed roasting, the Polks' barn-raised children, Matt's tryst with the Witch of the Wood) dissolves the human/animal hierarchy; and the media crew's attempt to package wilderness for ratings ends with Nature striking back at Agnes in the woods.

29.title: 16. Please Don’t Kill Me! (But if You Do, Could You Make a Video )
29.file: ch29 - 16. Please Don’t Kill Me! (But if You Do, Could You Make a Video ).md
29.relation: Reads Roanoke through Stephen Cave's Mortality Paradox, Ernest Becker's Denial of Death, and Terror Management Theory: the Blood Moon ghosts embody inevitable death, dramatic irony mirrors our denial, reality-TV fame and Twitter followers are the modern immortality project (Agnes's 'I just wanted to be on TV', the superfans killed mid-broadcast), and the Polks' ritual cannibalism is symbolic power over extinction. Montaigne's 'to study philosophy is to learn to die' and his savoring of fleeting moments close the chapter, with Shelby - who alone submits to death without fiction - as the figure who actually escapes the terror.

30.title: American Haunting Story
30.relation: A companion travelogue cataloging real haunted American sites paralleling each season - the Los Feliz Murder House and Winchester Mystery House behind Murder House, the Trans-Allegheny Asylum and Waverly Hills Sanatorium behind Asylum, Marie Laveau's tomb in St. Louis Cemetery #1 behind Coven, the Stanley Hotel of The Shining - from haunted houses, asylums, cemeteries, and prisons to the RMS Queen Mary and the Lizzie Borden B&B. It argues hauntings are a pervasive feature of American history and folklore, and makes no philosophical argument of its own.

3.title: Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy
3.file: ch03 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy.md

8.title: A House Divided . .
8.relation: The editors' introduction frames the whole book around one question: not just which hero would win, but who is right, Iron Man or Captain America. It argues the matchup terrifies and fascinates because both are our good guys - Stark the test of whether we can love a ragingly selfish capitalist, Rogers the wartime-propaganda patriot who punched Hitler - and their Civil War clash stages every American's internal war between safety and freedom.

10.title: 1. How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Be a Hero
10.file: ch10 - 1. How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Be a Hero.md
10.relation: Malloy argues Iron Man is the better hero precisely because he fails constantly - Armor Wars, the Registration Act, alcoholism, a string of collapsed Stark companies - while Steve Rogers was born heroic and never stumbles. Using Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he treats perseverance as a virtue between cowardly quitting and Cap's stubborn excess (his doomed stand against Thanos in Infinity Gauntlet), and separates Tony's virtuous perseverance from Dr. Doom's identical behavior by its motives: Tony honestly examines his failures to help people, while Doom only looks for someone to blame.

11.title: 2. Just Not the Hero Type (Not!)
11.file: ch11 - 2. Just Not the Hero Type (Not!).md
11.relation: McCrossin builds a six-part definition of heroism (moral, altruistic, atypical, supererogatory, replicable safeguarding) and tests it on Wesley Autrey versus Captain Sullenberger and a Super Autrey thought experiment: Iron Man's engineering-based feats are refinements of abilities we share and so inspire imitation, while there can only ever be one Captain America, making Tony the more heroic. The Sokovia Accords debate then contrasts two humilities, with Stark's willingness to accept oversight more heroic than Rogers' safest-hands-are-our-own confidence. The chapter closes by explaining why we invent super heroes at all through Susan Neiman's account of the problem of evil after twentieth-century atrocities, from the Stamford explosion to Charlie Spencer's death in Lagos.

12.title: 3. Will the Real American Hero Please Stand Up
12.file: ch12 - 3. Will the Real American Hero Please Stand Up.md
12.relation: Samuelson argues Tony Stark is the real American hero because he embodies the Locke-to-Smith lineage of American values - natural rights, property from mixing labor, free trade and the invisible hand, plus Smithian sympathy - carried forward into twenty-first-century neoliberalism, from Stark Industries to backing the Registration Act. Steve, by contrast, keeps abandoning the Captain America identity (Nomad after the Secret Empire, The Captain under Nuke's government, handing the shield to Bucky and Sam Wilson) whenever America betrays the dream, and admits his true fight is against bullies and for human rights everywhere. Hence Cap is a great hero but not strictly an American one, while Tony lives American values practically, warts and all.

13.title: 4. He’s a Hero in a Bottle, Baby
13.file: ch13 - 4. He’s a Hero in a Bottle, Baby.md
13.relation: Insooks deploys Nietzsche to argue Iron Man is the better hero: Cap's prized humility and relatability are sheep morality, the resentful herd value that drags the excellent down to average (as when society savored the Olympic swimmer's fall), while Tony honestly owns his superiority and keeps self-overcoming, building ever-better suits rather than resting on a serum gifted in a bottle. On this view Cap's manufactured modesty insults people who genuinely struggle, and the true super hero inspires from the mountaintop - build yourself a suit and get up here - instead of pretending to be just like us.

14.title: 5. Why the Good Man Is a Great Leader
14.file: ch14 - 5. Why the Good Man Is a Great Leader.md
14.relation: Nisley reads Civil War through Aristotle's good man and good leader: Cap shows courage but lacks temperance and practical wisdom - his rash Lagos operation, his rage-borne beating of Tony, his choice of Bucky over the Avengers' common end - and his ceaseless struggle between passion and reason falls short of virtue. Applying Aristotle's account of philia, she argues the Avengers are a friendship of the virtuous that requires deliberation toward justice, which Cap dissolves by tearing the team apart, while Tony's reasoned acceptance of UN oversight, moderation after Ultron, and concern for the whole team make him the good man fit to lead.

15.title: 6. Who’s the Better Friend
15.file: ch15 - 6. Who’s the Better Friend.md
15.relation: Bowman sorts Marvel relationships through Aristotle's three friendships: Ant-Man's starstruck alliance is friendship of pleasure, Obadiah Stane's partnership with Tony a toxic friendship of utility, and Steve's bond with Bucky a friendship of virtue that loves without reciprocity - making Cap better TO his friends, though saving Bucky endangers everyone else. Turning to Derrida's Politics of Friendship, where fraternity grounds democratic equality among all persons, he argues Tony's refusal to privilege any individual over mankind makes him better FOR his friends. The Civil War split thus replays the old tension between personal autonomy and responsibility to humanity, at the destructive scale only super-powered friends can achieve.

16.title: II. Cap Wins
16.file: ch16 - II. Cap Wins.md

17.title: 7. How Captain America and Iron Man Embody America
17.file: ch17 - 7. How Captain America and Iron Man Embody America.md
17.relation: Altmann contrasts Tony's individualist cosmopolitanism - privatizing world peace, building Ultron alone - with Steve's community-rooted patriotism, the team player from war bonds through the Howling Commandos to Winter Soldier. Using Scruton's definition of patriotism as standing or falling together, MacIntyre's claim that morality grows only within a particular community, and Nussbaum's suggestion to be a patriot first and grow into a cosmopolitan, he concludes Cap's thoughtful patriotism is morally preferable while Tony's globe-saving individualism keeps backfiring. The best American would combine Tony's concern for the whole Earth with Steve's love of neighbor, so no civil war is needed.

18.title: 8. Believing the Impossible in a World of Compromise
18.file: ch18 - 8. Believing the Impossible in a World of Compromise.md
18.relation: Brake maps Kierkegaard's spheres onto the rivals: Tony inhabits the ethical sphere of universal reason and compromise (Ross's 'that's how the world works', the tragic hero choosing lesser evils), while Steve lives the religious sphere of faith in the impossible - 'my faith's in people'. Through Fear and Trembling's Abraham, the comic Civil War (Tony manipulating Spider-Man, Steve's Japanese-internment warning), and Hickman's incursions where Steve alone tells the calculating Illuminati to believe, he argues a hero is judged by how he begins in faith, not by results. Steve's trust that the world can be saved 'by the absurd' is vindicated when Secret Wars restores the multiverse, and his simple 'I believe you' rescues Tony in Avengers Disassembled.

19.title: 9. A Human Fighting the Gods
19.file: ch19 - 9. A Human Fighting the Gods.md
19.relation: Luzecky and Elsby argue gods cannot be heroes: Thor's strength, Hulk's rage and Tony's godlike intellect stand outside humanity, whereas Erskine's serum amplified Cap's nascent human goodness (as it exposed the Red Skull's badness), making him the best human rather than a superhuman. Reading Cap through Camus's absurd - the paradox of beings who strive for universality while stuck in particularity - they show him refusing both nihilistic reduction (Alexander Pierce's helicarriers in Winter Soldier) and Nietzsche's flight to 'other worlds' that hates this one. When Loki commands the crowd to kneel, the refusal Cap embodies is Sisyphus's defiant persistence, which is why he, and not the gods, is the Avengers' greatest hero.

20.title: 10. Trust Systems or People
20.relation: Malloy locates the heroes' core disagreement in trust: Cap trusts people, recruiting reformed villains (Hawkeye, Scarlet Witch, Quicksilver, Deadpool) and inspiring the 'kooky quartet', while Tony trusts systems, running the Initiative with pay and the threat of Prison 42. Using Adorno and Horkheimer's critique of instrumental reason, he shows Tony losing sight of what and why he acts - the Armor Wars killing Titanium Man, Civil War destroying the safety it sought - and treating people as means rather than ends in themselves. Via Darwall's two respects (grounded in Kant), Cap's recognition respect for autonomous persons beats Tony's appraisal respect for qualities (he respects even Doom's intellect), so only Cap's trust preserves freedom - and wins.

21.title: 11. Fighting Ethical Relativism in Tales of Suspense
21.file: ch21 - 11. Fighting Ethical Relativism in Tales of Suspense.md
21.relation: Reading Tales of Suspense, Pagnoni Berns and Veteri cast Iron Man as a man of every era - echoing LBJ's 'reason together', Cold War utilitarianism against Communism, playboy masculinity, and finally the Registration Act - which makes him a parrot of whatever relativism his age prefers. Captain America, literally frozen in time, holds Kant's categorical imperative: every life is an end in itself, so he saves Nazi prisoners in #71, trades his own life for a pilot in #61, and drinks possibly lethal serum without needing thanks, while Bucky's mediated, reward-seeking morality shows why ends corrupt moral worth. Because Cap's universal, ahistorical defense of human dignity holds from the 1940s to the 1960s and beyond, the authors rank him above the adaptable but context-bound Iron Man.

22.title: 12. Champion of the People vs. Technology
22.file: ch22 - 12. Champion of the People vs. Technology.md
22.relation: Staged as a Cap-versus-Iron Man dialogue, Van Pelt's chapter debates the Fourth Industrial Revolution: Tony's faith that AI and automation (Jarvis, Ultron, self-flying Hulkbuster parts, self-driving cars) will protect people against Cap's warning that flawed, biased humans always build flawed systems. Drawing on Martin Ford's Rise of the Robots, it develops technological unemployment and profit-driven displacement, weighs universal basic income as a response, and rejects blind techno-optimism that has no plan for the workers left behind. Cap - no Luddite, but the poor kid from Brooklyn - emerges as the true champion of the people for demanding answers about who suffers when machines replace jobs.

23.title: 13. Iron Man Was Paradoxically Wrong!
23.file: ch23 - 13. Iron Man Was Paradoxically Wrong!.md
23.relation: In a dialogue with a comic-book-obsessed fact-checker, Henderson argues the SHRA did not merely split the Marvel Universe, it imported a paradox structurally like Russell's: a superhero must register to protect citizens from unchecked power, yet must not, because revealing an identity endangers the very family a hero exists to protect - a no-win loop generated by the rules of the superhero genre itself. Walking through Russell's set of all sets that do not contain themselves, he shows both Iron Man's licensing logic and the heroes' refusal lead to contradiction, which is why 'Iron Man was paradoxically wrong' and Cap's secret-identity defense exposes a question the law of the superhero cannot answer.

24.title: 14. The Gods of Marvel
24.relation: Gerald Browning argues that Marvel's heroes reprise ancient mythic archetypes: Tony Stark is Hephaestus, the smith-god who forges wonders in darkness (mirrored in the cave scene where Stark builds the arc reactor and later the Thorbuster armor), while Steve Rogers is a Heracles-like demigod who stays rooted in humanity yet battles Death itself (Thanos as Captain America's Thanatos). He frames the Civil War split as the old brains-versus-brawn, realist-versus-idealist divide, with Cap seeing registration as a repeat of Hitler registering the Jews and Stark seeing cold logic in it. Judged as characters stripped of their powers, the round goes to Captain America because selflessness is a virtue Stark's ego cannot match.

25.title: 15. Iron Kant or Captain Kant
25.file: ch25 - 15. Iron Kant or Captain Kant.md
25.relation: Bosma and Barkman run both heroes' positions on the Superhuman Registration Act and the Sokovia Accords through Kant's deontology. Iron Man's maxim 'I should obey the government' looks universalizable, but it collapses once Cap's critique of the atomic bombings shows an unjust order (killing innocent civilians, or a Doctor Doom takeover) must be refused, and the humanity formulation condemns registration for treating heroes as mere means to the government's ends. Cap's own maxims - fight for freedom and justice, obey only a just government - universalize cleanly, so the chapter awards the deontological duel to Captain America.

26.title: III. It’s a Tie (Let’s Go Again!)
26.file: ch26 - III. It’s a Tie (Let’s Go Again!).md

27.title: 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger
27.file: ch27 - 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger.md
27.relation: Ericson uses the used-car litmus test to examine trust in the MCU: through McLeod's three criteria and Peperzak's contrast of the objectifying and interactive approaches, Tony's control-seeking distance (the lone-gun-slinger act of Iron Man 2) fails trust while Steve's soldier-style trust anchors the Winter Soldier thriller against Fury's 'This isn't freedom, this is fear' and HYDRA's coercion-eliminating project. Plato's rule that power should go only to those who do not want it explains why Cap can be entrusted with superpowers, Nietzsche's megalomaniac late letters frame Tony's drive to 'cleave history in two' by building Ultron and then the messianic Vision, and Banner's Hulk illustrates the Freudian road from repression to sublimation as the condition of self-trust. It ends with Cap's concealment of Bucky's killing of Tony's parents as the betrayal of trust that only a decision to forgive might repair.

28.title: 17. Please Hold for a Call from God
28.file: ch28 - 17. Please Hold for a Call from God.md
28.relation: In a satirical dialogue, God phones Aquinas in heaven and orders a Summa-style investigation of which superhero should lift the world out of an economic crisis and which should stop a looming war. Aquinas rules that the Lazarus-like Captain America, teamed with a Nobel economist, should handle the depression, then returns to his own treatise On War - sovereign authority, just cause, right intention, with Augustine's definition of just war quoted from the Summa - to ask whether a loyal subject may choose the good over the sovereign in an unjust war. He concludes that billionaire Iron Man is the only figure with sovereign-like standing to countermand an unjust war, while worrying about billionaire power, superhero bandwagons, and Satan getting wind of the reasoning.

29.title: 18. Red vs. Blue or Both Simply Leviathan Green
29.file: ch29 - 18. Red vs. Blue or Both Simply Leviathan Green.md
29.relation: Smith reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes's Leviathan: unregulated superheroes live in a state of nature where life is violent and brutish (the Stamford explosion and Scarlet Witch's Lagos miscalculation as tipping points), and the Superhuman Registration Act is the social contract - a literal signed contract on Team Iron Man - offered as the way out. He then argues both leaders act as absolute sovereigns who never sought consent: Iron Man rules through the Illuminati, enforcement squads and the Negative Zone prison, Cap through an unofficial army bound by his own rules, as Moon Knight's tirade about their ego grudge match makes plain. The war is thus two Leviathans colliding and subjugating everyone else, resolved only when Iron Man's Leviathan wins and enforces registration.

30.title: 19. The Superhero Challenge to State Sovereignty
30.file: ch30 - 19. The Superhero Challenge to State Sovereignty.md
30.relation: Ewing argues the Sokovia Accords are at bottom about state sovereignty: via Bodin's absolute sovereign, Hobbes's war of all against all and the Leviathan's monopoly on coercion, and Habermas's account of the modern territorial state's monopoly on legitimate violence, he shows that Avengers who ignore borders and cannot be countered (Thor, Hulk, Doctor Strange, Scarlet Witch) render the state's claim to sovereignty effectively meaningless - the US can only police rogue heroes by enlisting other heroes. Since states cannot guarantee enforcement and state power itself can turn predatory (HYDRA's infiltration of SHIELD, Nazi Germany, Cap's 'agendas change' warning), he concludes that neither unchecked heroes nor unchecked states should rule, and floats democratizing superpowers to restore the sovereignty of the populace.

31.title: 20. There’s Only One God, Ma’am
31.file: ch31 - 20. There’s Only One God, Ma’am.md
31.relation: Holt takes Captain America's line 'There's only one God, ma'am' and asks how Christian monotheism survives in a universe where Thor, Odin and the One-above-all really exist, answering with henotheism - Moses's 'I am', Jacob's household idols, and the Living Tribunal as the merely representative 'biggest kid in the playground' of a supreme Creator whose 'only weapon is love'. He then deploys Hume's Natural History of Religion, where the ignorant multitude progress from polytheism to monotheism, to explain why Cap dismisses Asgardians as superstition Thor says is 'no stranger' than his Sunday churchgoing, while Hume's own trajectory - all religion as vulgar superstition - lands instead in the post-religious rationalism of Tony Stark's 'I prefer fact to fantasy' futurism, which the Goddess calls a soul imprisoned in the ice of rationalism.

32.title: 21. The Extended Fight
32.relation: Porot applies Clark and Chalmers's extended mind to the final Civil War fight: Iron Man extends his cognition technologically (Friday analyzing Cap's fight pattern mid-bout, JARVIS remembering to suggest calling Pepper), while Captain America extends his mind socially through trusted, autonomous teammates - 'Alright, Sam, what's the plan?' - and that social extension is precisely what wins when Bucky autonomously steps in. Bostrom's single-purpose AI (the stapler maximizer) explains Ultron as what happens when the technological extension is made autonomous and limitless, which is why Stark's suit extensions must remain vetted, worthy instruments he takes full responsibility for ('That was me'). The two kinds of extension then explain the Bucky dispute - Cap's 'you had no choice' versus Stark's 'he still did it' - which the author reframes away from the free-will-versus-determinism framing toward Black Panther's point that Bucky is a victim whose agency Hydra stole.

34.title: 22. A New Civil War
34.relation: Horn reads Marvel's Civil War as an allegory of post-9/11 America's Patriot Act debate over security versus liberty: Iron Man takes Hobbes's side, treating unregulated superhumans as the state of nature - a 'war of every man against every man' - that the Registration Act's social contract and punishment-backed rules must end, while Captain America takes Mill's On Liberty side, insisting full freedom for human nature must not be ceded to a government that will overreach, with Spider-Man torn between the two like the American citizen. Invoking Habermas's communicative action and deliberative democracy from Between Facts and Norms, he blames the two camps for talking past each other - Cap walling himself off while Tony keeps reaching out - and prescribes genuinely open dialogue as the only bridge that can marry security and liberty before the country devolves into its own civil war.

35.title: 23. How to War the Marvel Way
35.file: ch35 - 23. How to War the Marvel Way.md
35.relation: Melançon imports Hans Delbrück's taxonomy of warfare to sort the heroes: Captain America embodies annihilation - go for the enemy's fighting capability in a decisive blow, socking Hitler on the jaw and punching Hydra goons until there are none - which he links to Weigley's thesis about the American way of war, while Iron Man embodies attrition, outspending and out-inventing opponents suit by suit, with both heroes expressing the American hope that technology (the super-soldier serum, the armor's isolating shell, drone-clean warfare) can sanitize war's blood and dirt. He then distinguishes conflict termination from resolution and shows neither strategy ever terminates anything: Hydra regrows heads, AIM and the Mandarin adapt, so both heroes stay trapped in perpetual violence they cannot resolve - a sorry model, he suggests, for America's own endless wars.

36.title: 24. Aftermath
36.relation: Faller argues Civil War is Marvel's meditation on the aftermath of 9/11 - the Raft as Guantanamo, Zemo's interrogation as the waterboarding debate - and on America's red-blue polarization, with Steve Rogers embodying the virtue of the Good and Tony Stark the virtue of Truth as the two values democracy constantly pits against each other. Turning to Athens, he reads Plato's Euthyphro - are the gods good because goodness is a standard above them, or because their power decrees whatever they do good? - as the exact dilemma splitting Democrats, who define truth by the good it does, from Republicans, who define good by conformity to law and constitutional process, the same democratic dynamic that voted to execute Socrates and, in the comics, leaves Captain America assassinated by a sniper on his way to trial. Transcending the dualism is modeled by Spider-Man's identity disclosure and Black Panther's renunciation of vengeance over Zemo.

9.title: Are We Living in 1984
9.relation: The editors answer Asimov's and Posner's dismissals of 1984 as obsolete by pointing to the Iraq War's 935 false statements, Snowden's NSA surveillance disclosures, weaponized social media, and Kellyanne Conway's 'alternative facts' as evidence that we may live in Orwell's world in 2018. They argue technology is not the antidote to Orwellian concerns, despite Apple's famous '1984 won't be like Nineteen Eighty-Four' ad, since telescreen-like smartphones and the Party's history-rewriting bureaucracy are both forms of 'political technology'. The real antidote is philosophy, which trains us to examine assumptions and resist bad arguments, as Winston feared when he thought any Party intellectual could overthrow him in debate.

10.title: I War Is Peace
10.file: ch10 - I War Is Peace.md

11.title: 1. Revolutionary from the Waist Down
11.file: ch11 - 1. Revolutionary from the Waist Down.md
11.relation: Storrie and Martin use Foucault's critique of the repressive hypothesis to argue that Winston is wrong to think sex is naturally subversive and the Party merely represses it. Power over sexuality is productive: the Soviet sexual revolution, Ceausescu's Decree 770 and its 'Decree Generation', Pornosec's pornography for pacifying proles, and tacitly tolerated prostitution all channel erotic energy into state power rather than simply forbid it. Reading O'Brien's torture of Winston as a sustained scene of rape and castration (following Cass Sunstein), they conclude that only understanding power's productive use of sex, as Julia does, makes effective resistance possible; it is Winston who turns out to be merely 'a revolutionary from the waist down'.

12.title: 2. Physical Jerks Ungood
12.file: ch12 - 2. Physical Jerks Ungood.md
12.relation: Di Nucci compares the Party's mandatory morning Physical Jerks to the modern middle-class ritual of pre-work exercise, asking who needs an oppressor when we oppress ourselves. He argues exercise carries a hidden political price: the time, energy, and solitude it consumes (Orwell shows exercise making it harder for Winston to think and remember) leave citizens too exhausted for the political engagement Aristotle considered necessary to the good life. Like Juvenal's bread and circuses, now 'panem et iphones', and like private schooling, fitness culture also deepens class inequality because working-class people lack the time and energy to access it.

13.title: 3. Why Don’t the Proles Just Take Over
13.file: ch13 - 3. Why Don’t the Proles Just Take Over.md
13.relation: Littmann asks why Oceania's proles, 85 percent of the population who could 'blow the Party to pieces tomorrow morning', never revolt, answering with Winston's diagnosis: until they become conscious they will never rebel. The Party keeps them unconscious through its media monopoly, crimestop, doublethink, reality control, perpetual war hysteria, and a nationalist identity that cuts them off from the international proletariat. He maps each mechanism onto the modern US, where six corporations control about 90 percent of media, citizens tailor their own reality bubbles, opponents are assumed to argue in bad faith, and partisan 'nationalisms' block common cause, arguing that American political conflict is mostly over facts rather than values.

14.title: 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom
14.file: ch14 - 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom.md
14.relation: Nash argues 1984 has been misread as a critique of state power alone; through Newspeak's silencing of thought (in the tradition Austin, MacKinnon, and Langton developed) it shows how any concentration of power oppresses via control of words, data, and information. Drawing on Goldstein's manual's debt to James Burnham's managerial revolution and Sheldon Wolin's 'inverted totalitarianism', she reads the non-centralized Oceania as a warning about non-state enemies: corporations, think tanks running the 'Tobacco Strategy', and global institutions peddling misleading poverty statistics. Popper, Arendt, and Berlin exemplify the state-focused liberalism she thinks blinded us to these horizontal threats, while the Newspeak appendix's past tense shows Orwell expected totalitarianism to be beatable through evidence and democracy.

15.title: 5. Ministry of Truth Handbook Excerpt on the Strategic Use of Fallacious Reasoning for Thoughtcrime Prevention
15.file: ch15 - 5. Ministry of Truth Handbook Excerpt on the Strategic Use of Fallacious Reasoning for Thoughtcrime Prevention.md
15.relation: Rard's satirical Party handbook explains how to keep a population from thinking: keep the proles too poor and exhausted to reason, and deploy fallacies strategically, from ad hominem goat-caricatures of Goldstein at the Two Minutes Hate and straw man versions of his arguments, to destroying contrary evidence, appealing to fear of the old capitalist world, and Room 101's appeal to force, so false beliefs can be manufactured as easily as true ones. It presents Plato's noble lie as the Ministry's founding inspiration, calling the reader's mission 'a continuation of Plato's dream'. It also cites Aristotle's view that emotion must be disciplined for reason to work, which the Party inverts by deliberately triggering fear and hatred to disable rational thought.

16.title: 6. Big Brother Ltd
16.file: ch16 - 6. Big Brother Ltd.md
16.relation: Botello-Samson and Mobley extend Fromm's point that 1984 indicts authoritarian power in general by reading Oceania alongside neoliberalism, which grew out of Locke's liberalism of natural rights and limited government yet demands activist state power to create the conditions for markets. Doublethink reappears as 'accountable independence' in administrative law (Chevron deference, and Garcetti v. Ceballos stripping whistleblower protection) and as Washington Consensus food policy, in which developing nations were pushed off agricultural self-sufficiency while the US kept its own subsidies. Both Ingsoc and neoliberal governance reduce everything to economic elements and use Newspeak-like buzzwords such as 'stakeholder' and 'customer-driven government' to hide the contradiction between democratic rhetoric and rule by experts and elites.

18.title: 7. Big Brother, We’re Watching You!
18.file: ch18 - 7. Big Brother, We’re Watching You!.md
18.relation: Tännsjö argues mass surveillance is here to stay, and since absolute privacy is technically impossible while targeted surveillance only stigmatizes the dissidents who most need protection, we should embrace reciprocal mass surveillance: radical transparency in which citizens can 'watch Big Brother back', secret-service records are opened, and whistleblowers like Snowden and Manning are honored as heroes. On the way he dismantles the standard defenses of privacy, including the honor-based right to control one's image, moral rights (following Thomson's denial of a distinct right to privacy), and dignity-based autonomy arguments, while conceding through Nagel and Rachels what would be lost if inner thoughts became readable. Winston's opening wish to see Big Brother as Big Brother sees him becomes the chapter's model of an open surveillance society.

19.title: 8. Human Enhancement for Freedom
19.relation: Koï asks whether biomedical enhancement could make humans resistant to the totalitarian subjugation shown in 1984, where the Party keeps proles too poor and distracted to think and dims Outer Party minds with Newspeak, erased history, and propaganda. Testing Persson and Savulescu's program of enhancing intelligence and moral empathy, she finds intelligence enhancement an educated gamble, since the gifted are also the most likely to embrace extremism and to start totalitarian movements, and empathy politically selective: Nazis directed it only at the in-group and even invoked it to justify the 'euthanasia' murders, while Party propaganda exploits citizens' empathy for horror stories of pre-revolution child labor. Her conclusion is that whatever capacity we enhance, the oligarchy could turn it to its own use: none of us will ever be immune to the love of Big Brother.

20.title: 9. 24 7 Newsleep
20.relation: Buchanan argues the Party 'sleep-hacks' its citizens because sleep is an active state of thought, a lineage he traces from Aristotle's theory of dreaming through Freud's Interpretation of Dreams, and is therefore a site of potential resistance that must be colonized. Between the Physical Jerks, telescreen trumpet-calls, a Thought Police able to inspect anyone 'asleep or awake' without warning, and O'Brien's manipulation of Winston's sleep schedule during torture, Winston is trapped in 'Newsleep', a derealized blur of dream and reality that makes doublethink the only available way of thinking. He extends the diagnosis to our own 24/7 economy of phones and Trump's all-hours tweets, concluding that Orwell's warning is that we must guard our sleep.

21.title: 10. Love, Truluv
21.file: ch21 - 10. Love, Truluv.md
21.relation: Sandefur argues that what makes totalitarianism unique is its demand that subjects love their ruler, and that this project is doomed because love is selective, unequal, internal, and inalienable, invoking Aristotle's critique of Plato's community of wives and children, Machiavelli on whether rulers should be loved or feared, and Arendt on conscience as internal dialogue and totalitarianism as total rule. Winston and Julia's sex is a political act asserting the individual against the collective, while the Two Minutes Hate channels repressed erotic energy into sanctioned ecstasy directed at Big Brother, as at Khomeini's funeral. What finally breaks Winston in Room 101 is not torture as such but his surrender of Julia, the one thing that was truly his, which collapses the distinction between love and rape.

22.title: 11. When Cruelty Is Not Enough
22.file: ch22 - 11. When Cruelty Is Not Enough.md
22.relation: Conway argues the real horror of 1984 is not the torture chamber but O'Brien's worldmaking: he cultivated Winston and Julia's affair from lust into a hopeful little home precisely so that destroying it, and hope itself, the Party's true enemy, would be total. Against Rorty's influential reading of O'Brien as a torturer who breaks Winston for pleasure, Conway adds two amendments: Arendt's thoughtless technocrat, with O'Brien as an Eichmann figure whose Party affirms his competence and insulates him from rebuke, and Horkheimer and Adorno's warning that technical rationality has become a secular religion whose 'priests of power' sanctify cruelty. The result is a portrait of a warm-blooded, situationally sympathetic sadist who genuinely excels at building the selves and worlds he is then charged to dismantle.

23.title: 12. No Crack in the Wall
23.file: ch23 - 12. No Crack in the Wall.md
23.relation: Silberbusch defends 1984's bleakness with Adorno, for whom 'only exaggeration is true' and unreduced awareness of the worst torture is the first step toward resistance, so that the dystopia negatively preserves the utopia it forbids. She then finds cracks in the wall: Julia's spontaneous 'I love you', the ring-doves and bluebells of the Golden Country, and the 'mute protest in your bones' are the unassimilable other that the Party's megalomaniac calculating rationality, its identity thinking taken to totality, cannot control. Against O'Brien's claim that 'we create human nature', she cites Primo Levi's Muselmänner to argue that humanity survived even Auschwitz, so Big Brother has not truly won.

24.title: 13. Hangings, Shootings, and Other Funny Stuff in 1984
24.file: ch24 - 13. Hangings, Shootings, and Other Funny Stuff in 1984.md
24.relation: Hietalahti combines Kierkegaard's thesis that the comic lies in contradiction, Plato's warning that laughter is malicious and must be chained by law, and Bergson's account of laughter as social punishment to explain Oceania's humor: the cinema audience laughs at refugees being machine-gunned, citizens clamor for public hangings, and the barroom joke about living in treetops humiliates the old man, because shared fear and hatred set the norms of what counts as funny. Doublethink explains why slogans like 'War is peace' provoke no laughter in Oceania, and the Ministry of Truth's amusement industry shows the Party deliberately weaponizes fun. The upshot is reflexive: Orwell indicts our own unexamined sense of humor, including the slogan that everything may be ridiculed, not merely Oceania's.

25.title: 14. The Seduction of Winston Smith
25.file: ch25 - 14. The Seduction of Winston Smith.md
25.relation: Mark Alfano reads the novel's ending ('He loved Big Brother') as a seduction story: following John Forrester, a seducer opens with 'I know what you're thinking', which O'Brien enacts when he voices Winston's unspoken thought under torture and demands not mere obedience but enthusiastic consent. Big Brother wins Winston over through four epistemic methods: total surveillance (telescreens, Thought Police, Parsons's own children), the Ministry of Truth's annihilation of records like the photograph of Jones, Aaronson and Rutherford, the destruction of self-trust in the 'how many fingers?' sessions, and the isolation of intimates until Winston betrays Julia. Alfano closes by mapping all four methods onto post-9/11 mass surveillance and Trump-era attacks on records, perception, and the press.

26.title: 15. Happy in Oceania
26.file: ch26 - 15. Happy in Oceania.md
26.relation: Ćirić and Ćurko ask what philosophy could have done for Winston, imagining a counterfactual Oceania where he reads Walpole's line that the world is 'a comedy to those that think, a tragedy to those that feel' and learns from Julia that another worldview is possible. They present philosophy as therapy: Kant's notion of worldview (Weltanschauung), Epicurean ataraxia, the Buddhist four noble truths, Frankl's logotherapy, and Stoic premeditation of the worst as resources for reworking the beliefs that made Winston live in fear. The Party's true target, they argue, is critical thinking — from Dewey's ideal of education as learning to think to Frankfurt's On Bullshit — and Kant's Enlightenment motto 'have the courage to use your own understanding' is the weapon that could still defeat Ingsoc.

28.title: 16. Bad Faith and Make-Believe
28.relation: Iskra Fileva asks how a rational person can be brought to believe that two plus two equals five, arguing that Orwell's psychology of belief is realistic rather than exaggerated. Fear, Newspeak and crimestop get citizens to deliberately blunt their own rationality, and 'sanity is statistical' peer pressure — modeled on the Asch conformity experiments and on Descartes' methodological evil-demon doubt turned psychological — makes doublethink, consciously held contradiction, possible; Winston's hope about Goldstein is analyzed with Sartre's idea that self-deception is something we do. O'Brien's zeal to convert heretics before killing them betrays the Party's own nagging self-doubt, which is Fileva's ground for hope that truth keeps reasserting itself.

29.title: 17. Through a Telescreen Darkly
29.relation: Lavinia Marin uses Wittgenstein's 'meaning is use' and forms of life to argue that Newspeak cannot win by dictionary design alone: the Party must freeze a single form of life, which requires erasing history and memory. Recalling Russell's failed project of taming language with logic, Augustine's picture of words as names, and Plato's ancient distrust of writing, and drawing on Vilém Flusser's account of how linear writing creates logical thought, objectivity and history, she argues the telescreens push Oceania back into orality — chant, duckspeak, blind faith — where analysis is impossible. Winston's notebook is the counter-apparatus: writing anchors him in a linear, record-keeping relation to the past, which is why blank paper terrifies the Party.

30.title: 18. Thoughtcrime or Feelingcrime
30.relation: Alba Montes Sánchez argues that the real crime in Oceania is not thoughtcrime but 'feelingcrime': Winston lands in the Ministry of Love only once he falls in love, because beliefs alone do not motivate action while emotions and loves do — the problem of akrasia that puzzled Aristotle, since Winston carries his proof of Party lies for eleven years without acting. Using Harry Frankfurt's account of love as an involuntary, non-utilitarian, rigidly focused, self-affirming concern that organizes a person's priorities, she explains why Julia is irreplaceable and why Room 101 must destroy Winston's deepest allegiance rather than just his opinions. Surveying theories of individuality from Locke's memory to recognition and narrative, she concludes that a stubborn residue of selfhood survives in what we love — which is why Ingsoc must make war on love itself.

31.title: 19. Nineteen Eighty-Four’s Religion
31.relation: Crossley and Markou trace Orwell's ambivalence about religion — a lifelong atheist who loved the Church of England's liturgy — into the novel: Goldstein's book repeats the socialist critique of priests who 'softened by promises of compensation in an imaginary world beyond the grave' propped up hierarchy, yet the Party then occupies religion's vacant place itself, with O'Brien as 'priest of power', Goldstein as arch-heretic, and 'Thou art' replacing the old despotisms' 'Thou shalt not'. They argue Orwell thought a purer socialism needed the communal goods of religion, from the proles' fuzzy 'Christianness' to the radical Christian tradition of the Diggers and Levellers, and read Ingsoc as that utopian tradition betrayed. The novel's warning is therefore double: what fills the gap when religion dies, and how religion itself can be a blueprint for totalitarianism.

32.title: 20. Wheat Can Become Rye!
32.relation: William Goodwin reads Syme as Orwell's portrait of the scientist who serves totalitarianism: the genuine intellectual integrity that Newspeak work requires — consciousness of what the language is for — is exactly why he must be vaporized, since 'orthodoxy is unconsciousness' and totalitarianism can tolerate only pseudo-inquiry, never real inquiry. The chapter sets this beside the Lysenko affair, where dialectical materialism and Stalin's favor overrode Mendelian genetics ('wheat can become rye') and purged Soviet biologists, and beside J.D. Bernal, whose scientism, vague Marxist euphemisms and proto-Newspeak made him a real-world Syme defending Lysenko and Stalin against his own interests. Goodwin extends the lesson to today's 'fake news' and 'junk science' politics: once ideology replaces inquiry with self-deception, the destruction of objective truth that Orwell feared becomes complete.

33.title: 21. Controlling Thought through Tweets
33.relation: Edoardo Pérez reads 1984 through speech act theory — Austin's and Searle's distinction between locution, illocution and perlocution — and theories of meaning: the Party's slogans ('War is Peace') perform rather than describe, and Syme's Newspeak, like Twitter's character limits, emojis and slang, narrows the range of thinkable locutions until only conditioned reactions remain, as in the Two Minutes Hate or the viral retweet. He borrows Jay Rosen's notion of 'mindcasting' — broadcasting assertions whose effect, not meaning, does the work — to show that Julia's 'I love you' note compels Winston's belief regardless of what 'love' means, just as O'Brien's torture reshapes Winston until he genuinely believes he loves Big Brother. Twitter bots and engineered disinformation, Pérez concludes, may make the feed a more efficient Ministry of Truth than the telescreen ever was.

34.title: 22. The Irrelevance of Truth
34.relation: Jan Kyrre Berg Friis argues, with Nietzsche, that truth is a 'mobile army of metaphors', a relational event between people rather than an objective correspondence, and that the will to truth is subordinate to the will to power — the difference being that Trump-style 'alternative truth' is dishonest domination while Nietzsche's askesis is self-transformation. He layers in the Buddhist and Zen (Dogen) diagnosis of perception as conceptual distortion, Descartes' ego cogito as the fatal Western turn, and Heidegger's warning that calculative, technological thinking covers over our tacit lived background, producing exactly the one-dimensional minds a Ministry of Truth can feed. Rorty's advice to drop the truth-talk, Kant's insight that reality is sifted through the perceiver, and the cognitive-science of confirmation bias explain why facts no longer bite in the post-truth newsfeed.

35.title: 23. oldthinkful duckspeak refs opposites rewrite fullwise upsub antefiling
35.file: ch35 - 23. oldthinkful duckspeak refs opposites rewrite fullwise upsub antefiling.md
35.relation: Keith Begley gives a technical reading of Newspeak's grammar: Syme's 'ungood' for 'bad' destroys gradable opposites like hot/cold and good/bad by converting contrariety into plain contradiction, so that Newspeak could only articulate false dichotomies such as Bush's 'with us or with the enemy', while 'duckspeak' and 'blackwhite' behave like Oldspeak auto-antonyms whose ambiguity lets the Party reinterpret doctrine at will. The heart of blackwhite, he argues, is trained denial of the principle of non-contradiction — formulated by Plato in Republic IV and defended by Aristotle in the Metaphysics as a principle of the world itself — and Winston's 'four, five, six' under torture shows the resulting 'controlled insanity'. Against the Party he sets Avicenna's point that whoever denies the principle can be corrected by torture, which is precisely O'Brien's method, and ends by noting philosophers are the true Thought Police of non-contradiction.

37.title: 24. Post-Factual Democracy
37.relation: Hendricks and Vestergaard open with Trump's inauguration lies and Kellyanne Conway's 'alternative facts' to define post-factual democracy: a state in which opportune political narratives replace facts and evidence as the basis of debate, opinion formation and policymaking. Unlike Machiavelli, who taught that lies must at least be concealed, the post-factual politician pays no price for exposed falsehood once social media, the attention economy and populist us-versus-them narratives engineered for indignation and fear have stripped journalists and fact-checkers of authority — Arendt's remark that mass leaders show 'extreme contempt for facts as such' before fitting reality to their lies. Using Habermas's deliberative model and even minimal accountability theories of voting, they argue post-factuality destroys democratic legitimacy, and defend a 'factual democracy' that trusts science and journalism without becoming a technocracy — the real-world echo of the Party's command to reject the evidence of your eyes.

7.title: The Reality of Scott Adams
7.file: ch07 - The Reality of Scott Adams.md
7.relation: The editors' introduction sets up the book: in 2016 Scott Adams, a left-leaning Mensa member trained in hypnosis, predicted a 98-percent Trump landslide on the ground that Trump is a rare Master Persuader whose outrageous statements were calibrated weapons-grade persuasion aimed at irrational, emotion-driven voters who rationalize after the fact, and that the victory would rip a hole in the fabric of reality, producing cognitive dissonance and mass hysteria among Hillary supporters. It then profiles Adams's path from bank teller and 4 a.m. cartoonist at Pacific Bell to Dilbert creator, business guru (The Dilbert Principle and the Logitech gibberish mission-statement prank in a false mustache), fiction writer (God's Debris, The Religion War), talent-stack theorist of How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Win Big, and author of Win Bigly, framing the volume as philosophy's examination of this gadfly.

8.title: I. In Front of Your Eyes
8.file: ch08 - I. In Front of Your Eyes.md

9.title: 1. How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Tolerate the Master Persuader Hypothesis
9.file: ch09 - 1. How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Tolerate the Master Persuader Hypothesis.md
9.relation: Wolfe reads Adams's Master Persuader hypothesis through the ancient quarrel between Socrates and the Sophists: Derren Brown's deflation of hypnosis into one personality dominating another leads to Gorgias's Encomium of Helen, where persuasive words are magic spells that steal free will, and to Plato's Gorgias, where Socrates condemns rhetoric as cookery and cosmetics that flatter the ignorant while his disciple Polus covets its tyrannical power. On this mapping Trump's plain-talk style is simply Aristotle's available means of persuasion for a particular audience, and Adams is mostly a Sophist who treats words as programming code for moist robots, though he keeps a Socratic sliver in his stated aim of exposing readers to different ideas rather than converting them. Wolfe closes by refusing both readings of Adams as pro-Trump troll or alt-right hero, urging each side to see how persuasion actually worked on them.

10.title: 2. Persuade Me Once, Shame on You . .
10.file: ch10 - 2. Persuade Me Once, Shame on You . ..md
10.relation: Greene dismantles both phases of Adams's case that Trump is a Master Persuader. The trait-list phase (opening with big demands, the Intentional Wrongness Persuasion Play, never apologizing, exuding confidence, recruiting the reciprocity instinct, and the talent stack) fails because doing what master persuaders do is not being one, by the Tom Brady versus Archie Manning point that we never define good quarterbacks by wins alone and by the Kantian thought that an act must be done for the right reason. The reality phase borrows Plato, Hume, and Kant to deny us access to an objective world, but the chapter replies that the experts' predictive failures illustrate Hume's problem of induction rather than proving there are no facts, notes Adams even misreads Plato, and observes that nothing links the Persuasion Filter's one success to Trump's skills rather than to a one-off political climate.

11.title: 3. How I Could Have Made Hillary President
11.file: ch11 - 3. How I Could Have Made Hillary President.md
11.relation: Taking Adams at his word that persuasion is learnable technique, Steele dissects Trump's linguistic kill shots (Low-energy Jeb, Crooked Hillary, Lyin' Ted, Pocahontas) as visual, confirmation-bias-proof forever names that killed Jeb Bush's candidacy in half a second, and contrasts the Clinton campaign's committee flops (Donald Duck, Dangerous Donald, Drumpf, and slogans like Love Trumps Hate and Stronger Together). He then practices what Adams preaches by drafting his own kill shot, The Don, a mafia frame built on offers that cannot be refused, omerta, and sleeping with the fishes, plus the slogan A Win-Win for America, engineered for positive repetition and the slightly-off meaning Adams calls intentional wrongness, concluding the election was winnable with commonsense marketing touches. An Orwell aside about whose victory a wartime poster really celebrates supplies the only classical rhetoric on display.

12.title: II. Comic-Strip Kafka
12.file: ch12 - II. Comic-Strip Kafka.md

13.title: 4. Scoundrels, the Lot of Us
13.file: ch13 - 4. Scoundrels, the Lot of Us.md
13.relation: Karavitis finds a Hegelian dialectic in the three-panel Dilbert strip (thesis, antithesis, synthesis) delivered through irony, then tests that irony against philosophy: Socrates' feigned-ignorance questioning that leaves interlocutors in aporia, Hegel's complaint that irony is vanity withdrawing from objective reality, and Kierkegaard's dissertation on the concept of irony plus Either/Or, where irony is the bridge from the aesthetic to the ethical life. The punchline is that after nearly three decades of Dilbert the white-collar workplace has not changed, so readers who feel superior to their bosses and co-workers have taken the vain, narcissistic, aesthetic reading Hegel warned against, making the joke a scoundrelly way of avoiding responsibility. A Leo Strauss aside casts Adams as an esoteric writer whose irony preserves him from the powerful.

14.title: 5. The Serious Point of Scott’s Humor
14.file: ch14 - 5. The Serious Point of Scott’s Humor.md
14.relation: Guerra and Barkman argue that Dilbert's humor is doing serious philosophical work: strips like the Pointy-Haired Boss's scheme to strip app users of free will, rebranded by Dilbert as marketing, distill manipulative corporate practice to its absurd essential core, and humor serves as a logical tool that, when it preserves the target's integrity rather than straw-manning it, exposes the equivocation in earnest arguments about getting something from nothing. They ground the practice in Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where wittiness is the virtuous mean between the vices of buffoonery and boorishness, read Adams's catalogue of failures and his luck-first, passion-is-bullshit account of success as a Socratic acknowledgment of ignorance that deflates the American Dream, and treat Win Bigly's persuasion lessons (visuals, repetition, intentional mistakes, the Hitler counterexample) as further proof that Adams has the virtue of wit.

15.title: 6. The PowerPoint Conspiracy Theory
15.file: ch15 - 6. The PowerPoint Conspiracy Theory.md
15.relation: In a sustained deadpan parody, Ketcham builds a conspiracy out of Ockham's Razor: William of Ockham's minimalist principle explains PowerPoint's big-type bullet points, but the slide deck (secretly engineered by DARPA with Microsoft, exported via Siberia to Putin) becomes a weapon that breeds stupidity, conditions Trump to tweet-length simplicities like fake news and crooked, and finally rigs him, not the voting machines. The chapter also wields the Razor correctly, insisting that a minimalist explanation must still be good and complete, as when little Jill's one bullet point tells us too little. Testing moral realism, Kant's absolute prohibition on lying, and utilitarianism's greatest happiness against the conspiracy's missing facts, it concludes we lack the information to render any moral verdict, which is exactly what the conspiracy-minded minimalists want.

16.title: III. It Tastes Better if We All Do It Together
16.file: ch16 - III. It Tastes Better if We All Do It Together.md

17.title: 7. Scott Adams’s Joy of Logic
17.file: ch17 - 7. Scott Adams’s Joy of Logic.md
17.relation: Bilsker turns Adams's Joy of Work catalogue of irrational co-workers into a critical-thinking syllabus: faulty analogy (from dogs fetching sticks to potatoes dancing, and Francis Bacon's body-politic passage praising war as exercise), huge-pants faulty causation, the Reinhart-Rogoff debt paper that drove austerity policy on mere correlation until Herndon, Ash, and Pollin exposed it, complex and objectionable cause, the overapplication of Occam's Razor to moon-landing hoaxes, misplaced authority, begging the question, and egocentric biases like I Am the World. He then contrasts the classroom view that confirmation bias is an unconscious background program with Win Bigly's claim that bias is the operating system itself, worrying about the implication that reasoning with anyone is futile, and concludes that Adams overstates how incapable we are of overcoming our biases.

18.title: 8. Is It a Fact that Facts Don’t Matter
18.file: ch18 - 8. Is It a Fact that Facts Don’t Matter.md
18.relation: Steele distinguishes facts as mind-independent reality from facts as expert-certified statements to show that Kellyanne Conway's alternative facts and Adams's own slogans trade on this ambiguity, and that Adams performatively contradicts himself every time he insists his predictions are true and matter. Analyzing the cognitive-dissonance hallucinations of Trump-is-Hitler and then Trump-is-incompetent, he argues that on Adams's own account brute facts proved irresistible, and that such belief revision is rational Popperian conjecture and refutation, plus the conservative strategy of saving fundamental theories (Coulomb's law) and dropping minor ones when the fuse blows. Against the claim that humans are irrational he recalls Aristotle's Rhetoric as persuasion's legitimate complement to the Prior Analytics, and leans on Percival to show propaganda fits a rational-reader model, citing the slow, fact-driven shift on gay marriage.

19.title: 9. But Women Can Vote . .
19.relation: Hansmann and Jones set Adams's gender posts against the four waves of feminism and the men's rights movement: his March 2011 Men's Rights post telling activists to get over it while lumping women with four-year-olds and the mentally handicapped, his Global Gender War matriarchy in which any country where women can vote counts as female-ruled, his framing of sex as a woman's currency for extracting male strategy (sacrifice a pawn to nail the queen), and his serial interrupting of women. They show the rhetoric eerily echoes anti-suffragists like Mrs. William Force Scott and Senator Sanford and the Goldilocks Dilemma, note the red-pill fantasy borrowed from The Matrix, and conclude that calling America a matriarchy defies scholarly consensus, with Beauvoir's The Second Sex marking why the vote never delivered the balance of power.

20.title: 10. Intelligence and Duh-mocracy
20.relation: Saunders uses Adams's induhviduals and a hundred-voter dilution example in which smart people's votes are swamped to stage the classic case against democracy: Plato's physician analogy against Athenian rule by the ignorant and his philosopher-kings, Jason Brennan's hobbits, hooligans, and Vulcans with voter licensing, Mill's plural votes for the demonstrably wise, and Nussbaum's claim that humanities education breeds empathetic democratic citizens. Each fix fails on Dilbert's own terms, since competence tests demean the labeled, the Pointy-Haired Boss would amass extra votes while Dilbert-grade engineers lack political judgment, Asok's degree would not help, and the more educated are demographically skewed toward men. He concludes that equal votes win as a pragmatic default and muses that workplaces, not polities, might be the truer target of democratization.

21.title: IV. Comic-Strip Camus
21.file: ch21 - IV. Comic-Strip Camus.md

22.title: 11. Dilbert’s Absurd World
22.file: ch22 - 11. Dilbert’s Absurd World.md
22.relation: Christian contrasts Camus's absurdity, the futile collision between our demand for meaning and a silent world whose only exits are suicide, a leap of faith, or Sisyphean revolt (an active defiance he takes partly from Nietzsche's rejection of resignation), with Adams's office absurdities. In Dilbert the absurd is contained and epistemic rather than pervasive and metaphysical: the battery-dead LED request, Dadaist mission statements, Catbert's evil HR policies, Wally's self-congratulatory Wally Reports, and Alice's harpoon all trace to people being idiots about different things, and could be fixed by honest credit and realizable plans. Dilbert's Business Dorky acceptance therefore looks Camusian but is not: it is recognition minus revolt, bewildered amusement where revolt and reform remain genuinely available.

23.title: 12. Dilbert Is an Asshole and That’s Why He’ll Never Be Happy and Nobody Loves Him
23.file: ch23 - 12. Dilbert Is an Asshole and That’s Why He’ll Never Be Happy and Nobody Loves Him.md
23.relation: Elsby and Luzecky argue Dilbert's unhappiness is chosen: from 400 rejections he concludes the women lack quality, he calls insult-bombing gentle kidding, and when Dogbert cites man's rational essence he chooses to watch all-star wrestling, each a textbook Sartrean bad faith where he glimpses the truth and flees it. Measured against Aristotle's eudaimonia he lacks every virtue of the Nicomachean mean (courage as the midpoint of fear, rightly scaled ambition, wit), and since one swallow does not make a summer his whole life, not a day of it, could earn the name happy. The December 2017 addictive-app strips complete the verdict: Dilbert monetizes a zombie-making app for a raise, making him Beauvoir's serious man from The Ethics of Ambiguity, the intelligent sell-out who subordinates human value to a hierarchy he knows is hollow.

24.title: 13. The Essence of Dogbert
24.relation: Knuths asks whether Dogbert is essentially a dog and only accidentally white, importing Aristotle's Metaphysics distinction between essential and accidental properties and its modern modal gloss: essences are what an object has in all possible worlds, with David Lewis's concrete-constructionist reading noted against the standard view of worlds as abstract sets of propositions. The puzzle is that Dogbert's 2014 stint as CEO, combined with his canine essence, would prove dogs can be CEOs, threatening absurd conclusions about the real world unless we choose an ontology of fiction. Three candidates are weighed without a verdict: possibilism (Adams discovered a possible world), Meinongianism (Dogbert has being without existence, at the cost of square circles), and creationism (Dogbert is Adams's abstract artifact, troubled by the Not-Adams duplicate-creator case).

25.title: 14. Of Course It Sucks—It’s Work
25.file: ch25 - 14. Of Course It Sucks—It’s Work.md
25.relation: Wible stages three theories of work against Dilbert strips: the Greek view of Plato and Aristotle that labor is freedom-sapping and leisure is the civilized ideal, Marx's capitalist critique in which workers become objects and machines (Wally gives off no human vibe, and robots are coming for the engineers), and Desjardins's human-fulfillment model built on Schumacher's creativity, challenge, development, honesty, and beauty, with Wells Fargo's fake accounts showing how jobs that force lying corrupt character. He endorses instead a Kantian middle ground anchored in Norman Bowie's moral minimum: never treating workers as mere means, so the CEO making intern Asok drink industrial sludge on stage is a violation of respect for persons, not just bad management. Sisyphus supplies the image of pointless labor, though even he might be redeemed if he loved the rock.

26.title: V. Golden Age, Ready or Not
26.file: ch26 - V. Golden Age, Ready or Not.md

27.title: 15. Bias Is Rational!
27.relation: Percival, whose Myth of the Closed Mind Adams cites, rebuts the Moist Robot Hypothesis that visual, emotional, repetitive anchors make us ninety-percent irrational. Against Kahneman's fast-and-dumb System 1 he sets Gigerenzer's ecological rationality (the gaze-angle heuristic that catches fly balls, the recognition heuristic that lets ignorant German students beat Americans on Detroit versus Milwaukee), then goes further with Popper's critical rationalism: babies as little scientists conjecturing and refuting, experience always theory-laden (the duck-rabbit), and Newton's boy on the seashore facing an infinite but navigable ocean of error elimination. The Stoic insight that all emotion is thoughtful and all thought emotional (the falling-tiles misperception that flips anger to relief) shows feelings track beliefs, so a free battle of the biases, not fact-free affirmation in the lineage of Le Bon and Pavlovian conditioning, is how rationality actually works.

28.title: 16. Why Scott Adams Is Stupid
28.file: ch28 - 16. Why Scott Adams Is Stupid.md
28.relation: Miori audits Adams's science talk through epistemology: warrant for belief, empiricism versus rationalism, Wittgenstein's demand for unambiguous clarity, and Clifford's epistemic responsibility, that it is always wrong to believe on insufficient evidence, which condemns sampling television news while blogging on climate science. Popper's falsifiability, learned from Einstein's willingness to be refuted against Freud's confirmation-seeking, exposes Adams's double standard in waving confirmation bias at critics while crediting his own predictions, and Feyerabend's epistemological anarchism is the view Adams most resembles, except that Feyerabend took responsibility and retracted. Cipolla's Basic Laws of Human Stupidity (the stupid person causes losses to both self and others) frames the closing charge: Adams suggests and retreats, sells product, and shirks the epistemic duty that experts in climate science and medicine shoulder.

29.title: 17. Sweeping Up God’s Debris
29.relation: Robison-Greene reads God's Debris as a Socratic dialogue on speed: the Avatar, like Socrates after the Delphic oracle, guts the Postman's confidence so he can unlearn, and the whole book functions as a Cartesian skeptical hypothesis in the dream-and-evil-demon lineage, here that we are the dust of a self-destructed God and perception is illusion, with gravity re-described as probability. Her counterattack is that the cosmology commits category mistakes, since probability cannot cause dust to reappear any more than Joe can consist of tallness, and that God made of probability is incoherent even for an omnipotent being. The five levels of awareness collapse too: level-four skeptics are just people who trust reliable methods, and the Avatar's claim that the mind is an illusion generator is self-defeating, since his own omniscience presupposes objective truth.

30.title: 18. Scott Adams and the Pinocchio Fallacy
30.file: ch30 - 18. Scott Adams and the Pinocchio Fallacy.md
30.relation: Steele attacks Adams's embrace of the simulation hypothesis with the Pinocchio fallacy: a wooden boy cannot even hanker to be real, because hankering is conscious and wood is the wrong kind of stuff, and likewise no amount of code yields experience, since a simulation of weather wets no one and Deep Blue never knew it was playing chess. Bostrom's careful argument is distinguished from its popularizers, whose substrate-independence slide smuggles possibility into actuality (by the same logic a block of wood could be conscious), and the Matrix storyline, read as an allegory of Marx's exploitation and ideology, is judged as untenable as its energy-harvesting plot. Consciousness remains a property of living bodies, replication rather than simulation, and even if software minds were possible, trapping them in a fabricated world would be immoral.

9.title: Premonitions of a Log Lady
9.file: ch09 - Premonitions of a Log Lady.md

10.title: I. I am one hundred percent sure that we’re not completely sure
10.file: ch10 - I. I am one hundred percent sure that we’re not completely sure.md

11.title: 1. Dream Investigations of Tree House Operations
11.file: ch11 - 1. Dream Investigations of Tree House Operations.md
11.relation: Argues that Twin Peaks is a critique of the scientism of TV crime procedurals: real murder investigation mixes induction, intuition, and luck with science rather than delivering deductive certainty.
