plato-cave.relation: Luzecky and Elsby argue that Twin Peaks is genuine art because, against Plato's condemnation of mimetic art as confusing copies to be exiled, it fulfills Aristotle's Poetics: art's essential function is dramatic reversal, surprising and transfixing us (Dougie's absurd casino win, the dancing Man from Another Place). Drawing on Gadamer's 'Spiel' (play/game) and Ingarden's schematized, incomplete artworks, they contend the work of art exists only as an ongoing rhythmic 'to and fro' between image and viewer—so we complete the Red Room scene by participating in it, moving it from potentiality to actuality.

plato-cave.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
plato-cave.title: The Matrix, the Cave, and the Cogito
plato-cave.relation: Conard argues that The Matrix alludes to Plato's cave (the pod-bound humans mistaking the program for reality, Neo's painful ascent) and to Descartes' dream argument and evil-genius doubt (the singular consciousness generating the Matrix), but betrays their spirit by rejecting transcendence and the a priori. Because the film is 'Christianity without God'—Neo can only remake the shadow-world of the Matrix, not touch ultimate reality—it grounds knowledge in a subjective gut feeling ('being the One is just like being in love') rather than Descartes' intellectual intuition of God or Plato's rational grasp of the Forms, leaving no answer to whether life outside the Matrix is itself another illusion.

plato-cave.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
plato-cave.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
plato-cave.relation: McFarland reads Soderbergh's Solaris as a meditation on recollection, recognition, and repetition, grounding it in Platonic recollection (the Phaedo, the cave, and the Symposium's love as desire) and Augustine's Confessions, where memory strains toward an elusive beloved-as-God, the 'cruel miracle' of present absence. When Solaris materializes Rheya, Chris Kelvin first jettisons the 'bad copy' but then, tempted by Snow, embraces Deleuze's endless degraded repetition of copies to erase his guilt over her suicide. Against this, Gibarian voices a Kierkegaardian call (Repetition, Either/Or) that there are 'only choices'; McFarland faults Chris, like Odysseus choosing Kalypso's island, for choosing the deathless eternal present over the human world of forward-moving choice.

plato-cave.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
plato-cave.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
plato-cave.relation: LaRocca argues Burton's 'Ed Wood' (1994) is a metafilm that, via Baudrillard's simulacra and Plato's cave/dialectic, transforms how we watch Wood's 'bad' films. He casts Wood as a cave-dweller and naive literalist who conflates representation with reality ('film equals life,' 'that was perfect'), while Burton is the Platonic dialectician who posits two worlds and provokes thought. He distinguishes two interacting metafilm types—biographical simulacrum (a hyperreal Ed Wood with no original, per Baudrillard's 'artificial resurrection') and mimetic reenactment (loyal remakes of Wood's films)—so that Martin Landau's Lugosi and Parker-as-Fuller's non-acting reveal the emotional 'affect without illusion' latent in Wood's work.

plato-cave.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
plato-cave.title: The Work of Art in the Age of Embedded Journalism Fiction versus Depiction in Zero Dark Thirty
plato-cave.relation: Evans argues that Kathryn Bigelow's Zero Dark Thirty fails morally and epistemically because its immersive 'boots-on-the-ground' realism traps the viewer inside Maya's single point of view, so we can never see the CIA torture program's lunacy the way an outside witness would. Drawing on Wittgenstein's Tractatus claim that the subject is a limit of the world (the eye that cannot see itself), she shows how the film effaces its own privileged viewpoint to pass off a partial view as impartial reality. Against this she sets a Platonic point that genuine reality is glimpsed only through fiction that ironically juxtaposes contrasting viewpoints, citing scenes like the SEALs' banter and Maya's final weeping where the film briefly becomes true art. The 'depiction is not endorsement' defense collapses because the narrative logic still credits torture with finding bin Laden.

plato-cave.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
plato-cave.title: 16_LaRocca_Chapter_015.html
plato-cave.relation: Dan Geva re-reads Dziga Vertov's The Man with the Movie Camera as a coherent philosophy of documentary he calls 'praxis' or 'cine-seeing the invisible,' distilling ten 'diktats' (Unplayed Cinema, Life-Caught-Unawares, the interval theory of montage, etc.). He argues Vertov, like Plato, Marx, Nietzsche and Freud, privileges hidden depths over surface appearance, and reads the dialectical move from 'film fact' to 'film thing' as a Hegelian synthesis rather than a paradox. Crucially he aligns Vertov's Kino-Eye truth with Heidegger's notion of truth as aletheia (a partial unconcealment) rather than correspondence, tying the camera's revelation of the invisible to Heidegger's meditation on technology and seeing.

plato-cave.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
plato-cave.title: Plato, Habermas, and the Demonic Cobb
plato-cave.relation: Murphy treats Following as a provocation keyed to the copy of Plato's Republic glimpsed in The Blonde's apartment: Cobb, who slips unseen into houses and lives and reads people's 'boxes,' is the shepherd with the Ring of Gyges, able to act unjustly without ever facing detection. Against Glaucon's challenge the chapter weighs Socrates's answer that injustice enslaves and disorders the soul—but notes that Nolan shows Cobb victorious, a 'demonic' figure with all of Socrates's abilities and none of his love of justice, who drags Bill and The Blonde into a cave of illusion rather than out of one. Habermas supplies the modern retort: our rationality and sanity depend on the communicative action, truth, and fairness of a shared lifeworld, commitments a sociopathic loner like Cobb cannot renounce without taking refuge in mental illness, though the film never shows Cobb paying that price. Man of Steel's Clark Kent clutching the Republic while letting himself be bullied, and Jonathan Kent's fatal secrecy, become the counterimage of someone who consistently wills justice at personal cost, the closest Nolan comes to showing why justice is worth choosing.

plato-cave.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
plato-cave.title: 12. A Cave of His Own Making
plato-cave.relation: Golden reinterprets Plato's Allegory of the Cave to argue Chuck enslaves himself in a 'cave of his own making'—his hypochondriacal electromagnetic hypersensitivity—to keep Jimmy accountable and to exact vengeance for Jimmy's unpunished childhood thefts. Using Aristotle's De Anima psychology and the function argument, he places Chuck's imagination (phantasia) below reason: Chuck retains the rationality to serve clients like Mesa Verde and to detect Jimmy's document fraud, but sinks below the Golden Mean into the vices of meanness (short of kindness) and cowardice (short of courage) toward his brother. He adds Kierkegaard's Repetition: Chuck is stuck in backward-looking 'recollection' of vengeance and cannot make the forward, committed 'repetition' of simply being Jimmy's brother.

plato-cave.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
plato-cave.title: 2. Socrates’s City and Seldon’s Galaxy
plato-cave.relation: Goldberg maps Plato's Republic onto Asimov's Foundation Trilogy: Socrates's three-class city (Guardians, Auxiliaries, Producers ruling by knowledge of the Forms) parallels Seldon's galaxy (Second Foundationers, First Foundationers, and everyone else, ruling by the abstract mathematics of psychohistory), with the tyrannical Thrasymachus paralleling the Mule. He shows the Prime Radiant functions as Plato's Allegory of the Cave, and that both Guardians and Second Foundationers govern through 'noble lies' (the metals myth; the Encyclopedia sham and the Second Foundation's fake destruction), then questions whether those lies are truly noble given doubts about objective truth.

plato-cave.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
plato-cave.title: 1. A Man for All Seasonings
plato-cave.relation: Shaffer uses Brillat-Savarin's distinction between direct and reflective taste and Hume's 'Of the Standard of Taste' to argue gastronomic expertise is only the acquired ability to describe tastes richly, not a superior sense. He then casts Bourdain as a culinary Socrates who, like the freed prisoner in Plato's allegory of the cave, returns to lead provincial eaters out of the darkness of narrow experience toward cultural tolerance.

plato-cave.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
plato-cave.title: Stephen King and the Art of Horror
plato-cave.relation: Littmann stages a mock trial of King's horror using classical aesthetics: Plato prosecutes, condemning fiction as lies that misrepresent gods, afterlife, and paternal authority (Carrie's mother, Jack Torrance, the Loser's Club disobeying elders) and corrupt morals through spectacle. Aristotle counters that Poetics-style poetry is 'more philosophical than history' and that tragedy's catharsis purges pity and fear, which King echoes in Danse Macabre's claim that horror lances real terrors via Danny Torrance, Paul Sheldon, and Louis Creed. Hume's 'Of Tragedy' explains why we enjoy fictional suffering (Pennywise, Annie Wilkes) we would hate in life; Littmann finally revises Hume, arguing horror's pleasure is the spur to imagination rather than mere appreciation of artistic skill.

plato-cave.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
plato-cave.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
plato-cave.relation: Baron, a new father, weighs whether to let his son Maxwell consume violent popular media (from Halloween to SpongeBob, Grand Theft Auto, and Schindler's List) by testing three hypotheses. He uses Plato's Republic warning against exposing the young to stories they can't interpret for the 'causal hypothesis'; Aristotle's Poetics on learning pleasure from painful images for the 'edification hypothesis'; and Aristotle's account of tragic catharsis (homeopathic vs allopathic purging) for the 'catharsis hypothesis,' concluding that context matters more than ratings and that fathers watching alongside their children are the decisive influence.

plato-cave.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
plato-cave.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
plato-cave.relation: Porn journalist Gram Ponante's foreword riffs on Plato's Allegory of the Cave, casting porn as the shadows on the cave wall and the viewer as both prisoner and fire. He argues that unlike the manipulated prisoners, the porn viewer actively projects meaning onto a deliberately thin surface — forgiving porn its fake 'MILF' and 'schoolgirl' labels because the images 'become what we want them to be.' Porn is 'a cave to be filled in,' and adding plot or realism only breaks the fantasy by making the images less available for projection.

plato-cave.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
plato-cave.title: GARDENING
plato-cave.relation: Cotton reads the grower image in Plato's Phaedrus—the wise gardener who sows seed in proper soil for a slow harvest rather than the frivolous 'gardens of Adonis'—as Plato's model of philosophical education as natural growth. The educator plants logoi (discourse) in a 'proper soul,' where it must be cultivated by the learner's own reflection and eventually reproduces itself in others, against Thrasymachus's vessel model of pouring knowledge in. She connects this to the Republic's cave, the Apology's gadfly, and the Symposium/Theaetetus images of pregnancy and midwifery, then argues Plato's own aporetic, contradiction-laden dialogues and the corpus as a whole act as the wise grower, teaching readers to become 'gardeners of their own souls.'

plato-cave.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
plato-cave.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
plato-cave.relation: Thorsby reads 'getting high' as a rupture of ordinary, unreflective consciousness and asks why cannabis use grows fastest in the affluent capitalist West. He pairs Plato's allegory of the cave—ordinary consciousness as prisoners mistaking shadows for reality—with Marx's account of alienation and commodity fetishism, in which workers are estranged from the products of their labor and see value as inhering in things rather than in human labor. Drawing on Fromm's 'having vs. being,' he argues that cannabis offers a momentary escape from and critique of this alienated consciousness, though it cannot cure it.

plato-cave.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
plato-cave.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
plato-cave.relation: Ken Burak describes teaching yoga in his philosophy class — a 'three wheels' exercise moving from the true self behind our masks to the Upanishadic identity of Atman and Brahman ('Thou Art That') — to give students embodied access to the universal/particular problem. He reads Western philosophy from Plato's Phaedo (Socrates seeking death as liberation of soul from body) through Descartes' doubt as a 2500-year practice of pratyahara (sense-withdrawal), one limb mistaken for the whole journey, and asks what asana and this long retreat could each bring the other.

plato-cave.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
plato-cave.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
plato-cave.relation: J. Lenore Wright reads the Quest through the Western journey-narrative, both outward (Plato's climb out of the cave, Augustine's conversion) and inward (Descartes's methodological doubt turning toward the cogito). Frodo's leaving the Shire and freely accepting the Ring dramatizes the outward journey and the limits of freedom, while the wounding-and-healing of Sam, Merry, and Pippin marks an existential journey toward the Nietzschean charge to 'become who you are.' Wright contrasts the Yea-saying hobbits, transformed into resilient masters, with Nay-sayers Smeagol and Saruman locked in inauthentic self-pity, and argues Tolkien's ordinary pilgrims show that binding oneself to the good makes ordinary life extraordinary.

plato-cave.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
plato-cave.title: index
plato-cave.relation: This composite chapter argues philosophy through several comics. Jeremy Barris pairs Plato's dialogues with Amazing Spider-Man, using the allegory of the cave, the Forms, and Platonic love/eros to show that Spider-Man's bodily beauty, awkwardness, and self-trivializing irony draw readers toward goodness the way Plato says lust for beautiful bodies leads the soul upward to truth. Iain Thomson reads Moore and Gibbons's Watchmen as a 'deconstruction of the hero,' running Rorschach, Ozymandias and Dr. Manhattan through Nietzsche's Ubermensch and 'do not throw away the hero in your soul,' Heidegger's authentic 'choosing one's hero' and the uncanny, Kierkegaard's knight of faith, and Baudrillard's idea that an extreme realization destroys its own idea. Laura and Paul Canis read Daniel Clowes's Ghost World through Sartre's existentialism: Enid's post-high-school 'three o'clock' limbo enacts thrownness, abandonment, radical freedom and the flight from it into bad faith, contrasting Enid's authentic self-creation with Rebecca's settled conformity. Aldo Regalado's essay treats Tarzan, Superman, Captain America and the Black Panther as responses to modernity and race.

plato-cave.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
plato-cave.title: NOTES
plato-cave.relation: William Irwin's introduction argues philosophy must engage popular culture rather than fear it as Plato feared Homer and the poets. He invokes Plato's allegory of the cave to make the case that the philosopher who has left the cave must return and 'learn to see the shadows again'—use The Simpsons, The Matrix and Seinfeld as the vernacular through which prisoners can be led out—and answers Adorno-style culture-industry worries that mass entertainment is mere opiate. He closes by echoing Aristotle's serious treatment of the popular art (tragedy) of his day as warrant for treating today's pop culture philosophically.

plato-cave.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
plato-cave.title: NOTES
plato-cave.relation: Irwin asks 'what is popular culture?', rejecting Noel Carroll's 'mass art' accessibility criterion (using the Sex Pistols, Slipknot and the Beatles as counterexamples of inaccessible-yet-popular art) and Walter Benjamin's aura/mechanical-reproduction account, settling on popular culture as 'artifacts and subjects of mass interest and appreciation.' He rebuts Adorno's and Zizek's culture-industry charge that pop culture (e.g. The Matrix, The X-Files) ideologically ensnares audiences, and again deploys Plato's cave and the returning prisoner—citing Socrates meeting interlocutors where they are—to justify using pop culture as a bridge to philosophy while warning against 'abuse' (studying pop culture as philosophy).

plato-cave.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-cave.title: 2. Twilight Zone as Philosophy 101
plato-cave.relation: Marinucci uses The Twilight Zone as a triple introduction to philosophy, the show, and the handbook, arguing that philosophy is defined not by necessary-and-sufficient conditions but by Wittgensteinian family resemblance and salient features (curiosity, depth, abstraction, controversy) learned through MacIntyre-style immersion in a practice. She reads episodes as thought experiments: the amnesiac astronaut in 'Where Is Everybody?' and living-doll/robot episodes echo Plato's cave and Descartes's Method of Doubt about appearance versus reality, Nagel's 'what is it like to be a bat?' frames the problem of other minds, and episodes like 'The Shelter' and 'It's a Good Life' dramatize the tension between egoism and altruism and social conformity, including feminist gaslighting in 'Twenty Two.'

plato-cave.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-cave.title: 41. Blade Runner as Philosophy What Does It Mean to Be Human
plato-cave.relation: Shanahan argues Blade Runner is philosophical despite Ridley Scott's denial, using the replicants (Roy Batty, Rachael, Leon) as defamiliarizing 'mirrors' for the human condition. He shows the Nexus-6 replicants satisfy Descartes' two criteria for a thinking soul (linguistic flexibility, novel problem-solving) while human characters like Deckard prove as cold and empathy-deficient as the machines, collapsing the human/replicant distinction the Voight-Kampff test presumes. He then reads Rachael's implanted memories through Locke's memory theory of personal identity, Roy's 'tears in rain' death through Epicurean worries about finitude, and frames the whole via Plato's Cave line 'they are like us' — the replicants model our own concerns with memory, death, and the meaning of a temporally bounded life.

plato-cave.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-cave.title: 48. The Matrix as Philosophy Understanding Knowledge, Belief, Choice, and Reality
plato-cave.relation: Perez reads the Matrix trilogy as a sustained argument about how choosing what to believe and 'know' shapes the reality we live in. He opens with Descartes' dream problem and cogito, contrasting Descartes' foundationalism with Rorty's anti-foundationalism to explain Cypher's choice to reject reality for the Matrix's certitude, and uses Searle's brute vs. institutional facts (the cookies, the steak, 'there is no spoon') to show social reality is constructed. Against the fatalism of the Oracle, Architect, and Merovingian, he argues nearly every character makes free choices, and resolves the tension via Hume's compatibilism — liberty requires necessity, and choices gain meaning only in response to causality — while noting agent-causation objections (Reid, O'Connor, Rowe) that make Neo's 'Because I choose to' significant. Gettier's justified-true-belief critique and Plato's Cave frame the knowledge and enlightenment themes.

plato-cave.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-cave.title: 64. George Carlin as Philosopher It’s All Bullshit. Is It Bad for Ya
plato-cave.relation: Engels reads Carlin's insistence that 'it's all bullshit, and it's bad for ya' as a defense of truth over comforting illusion, mapping his bits onto Plato's Allegory of the Cave (Carlin dragging audiences up from shadows like 'prostitution is immoral' or 'the American Dream' to expose deeper essences), Nozick's Experience Machine (Carlin's sun-worship chosen because it is real, not a pleasing fiction), and Clifford/Beauvoir on the ethics of belief and the 'serious world.' Bits on rights, the sanctity of life, homelessness/'houselessness,' and 'proud to be an American' show Carlin arguing that false beliefs breed complacency and harm, so there are moral reasons to prefer truth.

plato-cave.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-cave.title: 78. The Witness as Philosophy How Knowledge Is Constructed
plato-cave.relation: Cuddy asks what epistemology Blow built into The Witness's frustrating puzzles and its windmill videos (Burke, Feynman, Moriarty, Spira, Gangaji). He rejects the sophistic/Protagorean 'knowledge depends on the observer' reading (most puzzles have objective, inductive-and-deductive solutions, e.g. the yellow-glass bunker) and the strict scientific realism of the Burke video defended by Putnam's no-miracles argument. Using Plato's cave and the aporia of Socrates' Meno (the puzzle's 'ah-ha' epiphanies), and Kuhn's incommensurable paradigm shifts (the game's 'hard left turns' forcing players to overhaul their understanding), he concludes the game argues that true knowledge is attainable, individually and collectively, though reached by a nonlinear, paradigm-shifting route rather than pure realism or relativism.

plato-forms.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
plato-forms.title: The Fates of Socrates and Seinfeld
plato-forms.relation: William Irwin compares Jerry and Socrates: the 'Jerry problem' of whether the fictional Jerry is the real Jerry (complicated by Seinlanguage) mirrors the Socratic problem of separating Socrates from Plato's dialogues. Jerry, like Socrates the gadfly, provokes his circle with questions that hunt for essences - the black-and-white cookie, 'is soup a meal?' - and shares Socrates' irony (the 'War: What Is It Good For?' gag in 'The Marine Biologist' works exactly like Socratic shamming ignorance). But where Socrates died serenely per the Apology and Phaedo, Jerry is self-absorbed and ends the series convicted under the Good Samaritan law, doing his stand-up 'gadfly' routine for prison inmates - an examined life, but not an exemplary one.

plato-forms.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
plato-forms.title: The Seinfeldians as Fixed Essences
plato-forms.relation: Mark Conard notes the show's relentless recurrences - Kramer sliding through the door, 'Newman!', George's firings, the Puddy on-again-off-again loop - and asks whether this is Nietzsche's eternal recurrence. It cannot be, since Nietzsche's cosmos is a flux of recombining centers of force; things recur in Seinfeld precisely because nothing changes. The Seinfeldians are instead fixed Platonic Forms or essences: 'The Bizarro Jerry' proves it, since only an unchanging archetype can have an exact opposite (Kevin, Gene, Feldman, Vargas), and the backwards episode 'The Betrayal' works only because characters exempt from time and change cannot develop.

plato-forms.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
plato-forms.title: Unknown
plato-forms.relation: Irwin argues the cave story's real point is Plato's Theory of Forms: life inside the Matrix, like ordinary sensory life, is a realm of copies - sunsets, just acts, really good noodles - imitating Beauty, Justice and Goodness themselves. He reads 'there is no spoon' and Morpheus's 'no one can be told what the Matrix is' as Plato's claim that the Forms are grasped by intellect rather than senses, and explains Neo's amnesia and the film's deja vu through Plato's doctrine of recollection (anamnesis), with the soul beholding the Forms between incarnations.

plato-forms.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
plato-forms.title: Unknown
plato-forms.relation: Developing thesis four, the chapter takes Morpheus's 'What is real?' seriously: if the real is just 'electrical signals interpreted by your brain', then virtual reality is as real as reality, and Neo's noodle-bar memories—experienced, coherent, and shared with other plugged-in minds—correspond to something that happened, by Hume's empiricism, coherence, and pragmatist standards alike. To the cyberskeptic's objection that cyberspace is not real space, the chapter answers with Plato's non-spatial Forms (and Kant on space as a form of intuition), closing that if simulations someday shape our lives more than the unsimulated world, the hyperreal Baudrillard describes will be, pragmatically, more real.

plato-forms.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
plato-forms.title: Going Mental
plato-forms.relation: Argues Harry's question rests on a false dilemma between 'in the head' and 'real', which Dumbledore's reply dissolves. It distinguishes merely-in-the-head items (Hermione as fictional character) from mind-independent ones (Emma Watson, King's Cross), then surveys philosophers who make the mental real: Plato's forms via broomsticks as imperfect copies of the ideal essence, Descartes's rationalism, Kant's mind-constituted objects, Berkeley's 'to be is to be perceived', Mill's phenomenalism, and Yogacara Buddhism's consciousness-fabricated emptiness.

plato-forms.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-forms.title: What Wisdom Requires
plato-forms.relation: Explains what wisdom demands: subordinating the loud, here-and-now deliverances of the senses and emotions to reason and the larger picture — as in Plato's wise person contemplating the eternal Forms and the Republic's long course of training, the Bhagavad-Gita's detachment, and Stoic meditative practice. It argues experience is nonetheless central (a sixteen-year-old Captain Marvel could not have it), cites Stick's parting from Matt Murdock in Daredevil over uncontrolled emotion, and uses Casablanca to mark the cultural shift that makes us doubt the larger picture's claims.

plato-forms.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-forms.title: Superheroes and the Ring of Gyges
plato-forms.relation: The chapter's heart: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges and 'harsh view' of human nature — justice as the weak's compact against the strong, a lineage running from Hobbes to Nietzsche — are powerfully denied by superheroes and by Frodo, who resist the power of the ring. Socrates' tripartite soul and justice-as-psychic-harmony are read as preparation for the Republic's real answer, the ascent to the eternal Form of the Good, which the chapter extends through Aristotle's teleology and virtue ethics: super-powered people, denied any standard social role, must wrestle with what their potential is for — from Kingdom Come's retired Superman and Spider-Man 2's Peter Parker to Astro City's Samaritan, with Uncle Ben's 'With great power comes great responsibility' as the upshot.

plato-forms.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-forms.title: Finding a Strong Basis for the Good
plato-forms.relation: Argues that loving role models give a motivation but not yet a reason to be good, available to everyone: Plato grounds goodness in a universe whose deep character is just — a metaphysical vision Augustine and C.S. Lewis found religiously congenial — while Kierkegaard grounds the duty of neighbor-love in our relationship to the God who created us out of nothing for eternal life, whose love shown in Christ lets even the persecuted face the double danger with hope. The chapter ends by noting the puzzling absence of religion from the X-Men's world: were its homo religiosus inhabitants to ask what universe they inhabit, they might find in loving the neighbor their deepest connection to the One who perfectly loves them.

plato-forms.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-forms.title: Switching Identities
plato-forms.relation: Maps Superman and Batman onto Plato and Aristotle — the otherworldly philosopher of the heavenly Good versus the this-worldly master of logic and applicable science — then argues that Bruce Wayne's years of intentional self-transformation may have swapped the mask, making Batman the core identity and Bruce the disguise. With Mark Waid, he sees Superman inwardly embracing his alien otherness as the path of authenticity, both cases yielding a fused "heterosis" of identities; Aristotle, Pascal and William James back the closing lesson that who we are is a matter of what we repeatedly do, so every mask may eventually become the face.

plato-forms.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
plato-forms.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Takes Digory's dying remark 'It's all in Plato' as the key to the Chronicles. It compares the Professor's guided questioning of Peter and Susan about Lucy's wardrobe testimony to the Socratic method, though noting he supplies evidential maxims rather than eliciting a virtue-definition as Socrates does with Cephalus on justice. It maps Underland in The Silver Chair onto the Allegory of the Cave (Rilian bound in his silver chair like the chained prisoners, the Green Witch's enchantment that denies any world beyond), observing that the Witch 'plays Aristotle' by ridiculing Aslan as an invented perfect Form, while Puddleglum's 'stand by the play-world' speech echoes Socrates's reply to Glaucon that the ideal pattern is none the worse for being unrealizable. Finally it reads the 'real Narnia' of The Last Battle ('world within world, Narnia within Narnia') as Christian Platonism, with the nested heavens even raising Plato's Third Man problem.

plato-forms.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
plato-forms.title: U2 and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: McCoy reads U2's early longing songs through the Symposium: Aristophanes' split-beings myth turns 'New Year's Day' into a song about incompleteness whose separated lovers also stand for Poland under Soviet domination, and Diotima's ladder of love reads 'I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For' and 'City of Blinding Lights' as stages ascending from bodily beauty toward the soul and then to Beauty itself. Against a tragic reading, she argues that by Diotima's account the restless lover on the ascent 'begets' discourses and songs, so 'With or Without You' is a song of surrender rather than despair. October's 'Gloria' and 'With a Shout' get the Augustinian ending: the restless heart finds in God the object Romantic love never supplies.

plato-forms.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
plato-forms.title: U2 and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Tollefsen revives Plato's ancient quarrel between philosophy and poetry: artistic imitations, three removes from the Forms and aimed at the soul's emotional part, stir 'imitative emotions' - purer, shorter-lived, effort-free surrogates for the real labors of love, faith and community - and he builds a four-stage account of the U2 formula (idealized transcendent love in the lyrics, religious imagery fusing lover and God, the Edge's Big Music crescendo, and the concert 'you' extended to the crowd, as in the Elevation-tour 'I Will Follow' with its 'Amazing Grace' bells) to show U2 are masters of exactly this seduction. The healing fans felt after September 11th may therefore be an image of redemption rather than the reality. Where Aristotle and Aquinas would educate the emotions rather than suppress them, Tollefsen's quarrel is with imitation itself; his verdict is that U2 suffer from Misplaced Artistic Pretension - high imagery where honest trash (or genuine complexity) would do.

plato-forms.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
plato-forms.title: James Bond and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Getachew maps Plato's Republic archetypes onto the Bond universe: the appetite-ruled Tyrant is Goldfinger, Zorin, Stromberg and the SPECTRE megalomaniacs; the spirit-ruled Guardian is 007, compared to Alcibiades and to Medea's vengeful fury (Bond letting Trevelyan fall 'For me'); and the reason-ruled Philosopher-King is M, whose ideal republic of common children and expendable numbers mirrors MI6's recruitment of orphans and its treatment of Bond as '007', never a person. She then challenges Plato's preference for the eternal Forms and immortality, using Freud on transience and Heidegger's being-toward-death (via Tolstoy's Ivan Ilych) to argue that mortality and risk are what make life worth living. Bond's stylish risk-taking, like the cello-case downhill escape, shows we need a balance between the Guardian and the man of thought.

plato-forms.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
plato-forms.title: Rhetoric and Bullshit
plato-forms.relation: Following Jeremy Campbell's The Liar's Tale, the chapter argues that the truth/lies binary is oversimplified: even 'the sky is blue' depends on contested definitions and 'God is good' on the speaker's concepts, so we must separate capital-T Truth — the immutable, incorruptible kind Plato located beyond the flawed physical realm of perfect Forms, which made him scorn rhetoric and the Sophists as teachers of disguise — from lower-case, situated, perspectival truths. It then recruits Nietzsche, for whom humans have no 'organ' for Truth but a natural instinct for falsehood (shared with camouflaging animals), and Ken Gemes's reading of doctrinal Truth as a ritualized fiction manufactured to maintain institutional and religious power. On this view postmodernism studies truth within the shifting domain of language rather than denying objective reality.

plato-forms.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
plato-forms.title: To Know … and Believe
plato-forms.relation: Gallagher reads Lost's Rose through Aquinas: faith is 'mid-way between knowledge and opinion,' sharing the certainty of episteme and the imperfection of doxa, so Rose's 'I just know' about Bernard's survival and her island cure confuses what she believes with what she knows. Aquinas' five ways ground natural knowledge that God exists, and the castaways' failures are diagnosed as sins against faith — Charlie's despair is acedia while Rose's certainty is the presumption (praesumptio) of elevating faith to demonstrated knowledge; the lesson is that faith perfects reason without replacing it.

plato-forms.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
plato-forms.title: To Nest or Not to Nest
plato-forms.relation: Halwani and Jones read The Birds as Hitchcock's warning about romantic love: love compromises autonomy through joint decision-making, emotional dependence, and exposure to contingencies like jealousy, betrayal, sickness, and death. Plato's Symposium stages the alternatives, Socrates's ladder of love culminating in the eternal Form of Beauty versus Alcibiades's speech for the painful, contingent love of a unique person, and Nussbaum's reading underscores that these two visions of romantic love are mutually exclusive. In the film, bird attacks strike whenever Melanie, Mitch, Annie, or Lydia treat love as a game or possession, while the caged lovebirds, the only birds that never attack, show that only love sealed in a 'gilded cage' could be cost-free; lovers must instead face love's price wisely, maturely, and courageously.

plato-forms.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
plato-forms.title: Curtain Down
plato-forms.relation: Silberstein reads Rear Window as a self-reflexive film about film-watching: the shades rise like a curtain, the courtyard apartments play like frames on a filmstrip, and wheelchair-bound Jeff with his binoculars is the movie spectator - the courtyard is Plato's cave and we are the chained prisoners watching shadows (copies of copies of the forms). The chapter stages the Plato-versus-Aristotle debate over imitative art from Republic Book X and the Poetics, then argues the film vindicates both: Jeff's voyeurism breeds detachment and misjudgment (he misreads Lisa, Miss Torso, the composer and the newlyweds), yet the same watching awakens - the song 'Lisa' saves Miss Lonelyhearts from suicide, Thorwald is brought to justice, and Jeff and the audience leave the theater wiser about fantasy, boredom and their own lives.

plato-forms.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
plato-forms.title: Pink Floyd From Pompeii to Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: George Reisch's introduction reads the 1971 Live at Pompeii film, with the band playing to no audience inside a circular stone amphitheatre, as an ironic anticipation of The Wall, tracing how Waters's fury at stadium crowds (culminating in the 1977 Montreal spitting incident that spawned the wall concept) had not yet arrived. It frames the band's post-Barrett move from psychedelic whimsy to minimal formalism as philosophical stripping-away: Barrett wrote like an Aristotle fascinated by odd particulars ('Lucifer Sam,' 'The Gnome'), whose puzzlement at his impenetrable cat prefigures Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' and the problem of other minds, while Waters pursued Plato's monolithic 'forms' of time, money, and madness. On this reading Dark Side's closing 'the sun is eclipsed by the moon' indicts Being itself, making life essentially and permanently tragic, a circular trap signaled by The Wall's interlocking 'we came in?' and 'Isn't this where...'

plato-forms.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
plato-forms.title: You Can’t Tell the Players Without a Program
plato-forms.relation: Auxier revives Plato's ancient quarrel with the poets — the Republic's banishment of imitators whose pretty words are copies that stir the masses' feelings, the philosopher-king's city, the Ion's contempt for rhapsodes, Socrates' wisdom as Delphic acknowledgment of ignorance — while branding Plato an elitist and 'Poetry NIMBY.' He then stages a fantasy dithyramb contest at the Meadowlands where Dylan ('Subterranean Homesick Blues') and Springsteen ('Blinded by the Light') trade internal rhymes and alliteration before Weird Al's palindromes deflate Bob's seriousness. The virtuous poet wins all nine Muses by wooing their mother Mnemosyne — tapping the collective memory of the race with gratitude and discipline — which explains why Springsteen, unlike the prideful Dylan who lost the Muses, retains moral authority; the philosophers, needless to say, are just jealous of the bar.

plato-forms.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
plato-forms.title: Will You Say Yes
plato-forms.relation: Bruce finds Nietzsche's eternal return in the NES Zelda's clockless, endlessly restartable structure: the same game recurs every time you press start, yet since the player changes, each playthrough manifests the forces anew, and the demon's question 'do you desire this once more?' becomes 'do you will to play once more?'. Link's growth through eight dungeons to face Ganon is read as will-to-power, personal strength and self-overcoming rather than mere domination, and saying yes to the struggle is amor fati. Against Plato's two-worlds doctrine of Forms and the Christian after-worldly (both Nietzsche's targets), the original Zelda offers no guide, no Bible, and no linear time to a final judgment: this looped world is the only one, so it must be affirmed.

plato-forms.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
plato-forms.title: Zelda and Reality
plato-forms.relation: Havstad and Jahng inventory every Zelda across the series (royal, wise, resolved, foreseeing, yet passive, imprisoned, even turned to stone in The Minish Cap or asleep through all of Adventure of Link) and read the maiden typology through Beauvoir's The Second Sex: woman as Idea, modeled on Plato's Forms, gives men a feminine ideal that real women are then judged against, and 'women are not born, but made' explains how femininity is a male-defined myth serving male interests. Zelda is the glorified yet objectified prize whose passivity lets Link's transcendence happen, and Aonuma's 'reality over realism' design philosophy explains why such stereotypes feel true to players. Sheik and Tetra, who act while disguised as (or turned into) something other than the princess, are the promising cracks in the ideal.

plato-forms.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
plato-forms.title: Conscious Unity “There’s No Place Like Home”
plato-forms.relation: McLachlan maps the whole story onto Schelling's romantic eschatology: gray Kansas is the Ungrund, the boring unconscious unity; the tornado (and Dorothy Gale as 'the gale') is the alienating rupture; and 'there's no place like home' is conscious unity regained through love of concrete, limiting others—richer than the unity she left because it now contains real relationships. Each companion's quest begins in egoism (the Scarecrow as an almost perfect Platonist, all disembodied contemplation like the spider-watching Spinoza; the Tin Man's self-loving imperviousness to pain), while evil in Oz—Miss Gulch's totalizing order, the Witches' slave states, the hidden Wizard—is Schelling's second evil: the attempt to control everything and abolish the freedom of others. Against escape-eschatologies (Plato's shadow-world, Bunyan's Pilgrim who flees his family crying 'eternal life,' Dante turning from Beatrice to the divine light), the Schellingian lesson is that even God becomes personal through relation—which is why the Dainty China Princess's refusal to be a mantel ornament marks the exact point of Dorothy's education in love.

plato-forms.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
plato-forms.title: I Ain’t Gonna Tell You One Thing that You Really Ought to Know . . . Ooh!
plato-forms.relation: Scott Calef reads the black 'Object' on the Presence cover—which Storm Thorgerson calls not a presence but a hole—to argue that absence permeates Zep's album art (the cut-out wheel of III, the die-cut windows of Physical Graffiti, the spindle holes of Coda) and that holes are a genuine metaphysical puzzle: immaterial yet extended, seemingly causal, and hard to see on a causal theory of perception. Descartes's immaterial soul is compared to holes (both non-physical, though holes suspiciously have size and location), Plato's Forms explain how the Object and we ourselves partake of both Being and Non-Being, and Hume's failure to find a self in introspection makes the self 'a hole'. Kierkegaard and Heidegger connect nothingness to the anxiety of death—fitting an album made after Plant's near-fatal crash—Socrates's two alternatives about death frame the end, and Wittgenstein's 'not a something but not a nothing either' caps the Object's dual nature.

plato-forms.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
plato-forms.title: The Sacrificial Lamb
plato-forms.relation: Argues Astro Boy re-enacts the sacrificial logic of the atomic age: Atomu is the nuclear-powered copy of the dead Tobio, born from Dr. Tenma's refusal to accept mortality, and his repeated self-sacrifice for humans who discard him (as in 'Save the Classmate,' where the rescued boys' parents still want him removed) shows him functioning as Heidegger's 'standing-reserve' — an object valued only as stored power, with humans themselves next in line. Drawing on Plato's Republic anxiety over originals and copies, Adorno and Horkheimer's dialectic of enlightenment, and Rey Chow's account of mimesis as the sign left by sacrifice, the chapter reads the series as mourning an innocence that became impossible after Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

plato-forms.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
plato-forms.title: The Good Gossip
plato-forms.relation: Borge weighs Jimmy Sirrel's claim that the best team always wins and the rest is gossip against Alex Ferguson insisting his side played better in a 1–4 defeat to Liverpool, framing the dispute as football Nominalism (only particular matches and results exist) versus football Platonism (an ideal way of playing exists over and above results). He rejects the Platonic ideal as metaphysically impossible—two perfect teams could never both score on every chance while conceding nothing, and style comparisons like catenaccio versus Brazil 1970 collapse without appeal to results—and instead uses possible-worlds counterfactuals: a team can be 'really' best yet unlucky when it creates objective scoring opportunities, like John Terry's slipped 2008 Champions League penalty or Spain's wrongly disallowed golden goal against South Korea in 2002, that go in across the closest possible worlds. Since Liverpool's deeply unfair 2005 comeback in Istanbul is celebrated as a classic, football is fiction and drama rather than a fairness-measuring contest, and the resulting what-if moaning is the good gossip that makes barstool debate worthwhile.

plato-forms.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
plato-forms.title: How Beckenbauer and Zidane Practiced the Four Cardinal Virtues
plato-forms.relation: Coumoundouros explains soccer greatness through three Platonic ideas: the Form of the footballer, which Pelé (1,281 goals, three World Cups, the save by Banks his header 'infected' with greatness and the infamous miss against Uruguay) and Maradona (the Hand of God and the Goal of the Century past five English defenders) approximate as near-perfect imitations, with position-specific Forms like forward Form for Pelé and attacking-midfielder Form for Maradona. Excellence as performing a proper function well (Republic 353a) then accounts for modern players—Ronaldo's evolved winger role, Henry converted by Wenger into a striker, Marta averaging a goal per game proving women's soccer equals the men's. Finally the Republic's four cardinal virtues grounded in the tripartite soul apply off and on the pitch: Beckenbauer playing the 1970 'Game of the Century' with a fractured clavicle and marshaling the 1974 final shows courage, wisdom, and moderation in just balance, while Zidane's 2006 head-butt on Materazzi shows the spirited part overwhelming reason, and with it greatness itself.

plato-forms.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
plato-forms.title: Beyond Picasso and Ronaldo Living Artfully
plato-forms.relation: Elcombe asks whether Cristiano Ronaldo, transferred to Real Madrid for $131 million—more than Picasso's Garçon à la Pipe fetched at its record 2004 auction—can be an artist like Picasso. Traditional metaphysics built on Plato's perfect Forms and Aristotle's necessary-and-sufficient conditions locks Art in a special museum realm that soccer, as a purposive sport whose beauty is only a byproduct, can never enter, leaving the game merely 'beautiful', not Art. Dewey's Art as Experience reorients the question from what art is to what art does: artworks are consummations of experience, moments of 'thatness'—that meal, that storm, that Ronaldo free kick—that lift us out of the mundane while remaining within the game's durable rules and history (Ronaldo's artistry grows from Zidane, Maradona, Cruyff, Pelé). On this pragmatist view Ronaldo is an artist in the act, the six-year-old testing a new turn on the pitch lives artfully too, and soccer's artistry becomes groundwork for communication, democracy, and the good life—doing more real work than a painting almost no one ever sees.

plato-forms.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
plato-forms.title: Aww, . . . Poor Monster. Should We Feel Sorry for the Carrionites
plato-forms.relation: Hewitt treats the Carrionites — word-wielding beings of 'The Shakespeare Code' who do science without numbers — as a test of Hartry Field's Science Without Numbers and hence of the Quinean indispensability argument for Platonism about mathematics: if numbers are unavoidable in our best physics, they exist. Surveying Field's Newtonian case, Balaguer's mathematics-free quantum mechanics, and the objections to each, he concludes that even Carrionite physics would not refute numbers — the Carrionites would merely lack our knowledge of them, so the poor monsters are missing out.

plato-forms.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
plato-forms.title: A Beautiful Destiny
plato-forms.relation: Asks whether the Dalek casing can literally be beautiful, contrasting Kant's aesthetics (free beauty as the mind's fit with reality versus merely 'dependent' beauty of Davros-designed purpose) with Hegel's claim that beauty is thought embodied in matter, peaking in the human form, and Plato's view (via Nehamas's Phaedrus reading) that beauty begins the desire to care for a thing. Alexander of Hales's beauty-within-the-order and the Fourth Doctor's 'Genesis of the Daleks' echo, then Rosenkranz's aesthetic inferno where ugliness exists only as beauty's negation, show beauty and monstrosity need not be opposites. The conclusion is deliberately open: the puzzle forces us into metaphysics about mind and reality, not mere taste.

plato-forms.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
plato-forms.title: He’s Got to Make His Own Mistakes
plato-forms.relation: Cole pits Plato against Walter Benjamin to vindicate the imitation of Rush: Plato's cave makes art a shadow twice removed from the Forms, and on that view a perfect copy is impossible and every cover degraded, while Peart's 'Limelight' calls the stage a 'gilded cage' that is 'just a prettified cave' yet, with 'we are merely players' (via Shakespeare), makes performing the way out rather than deeper in. Benjamin's translator essay, with its 'language forest' echo and 'pure language', shows how Rush's cover of 'Summertime Blues' on Feedback layers Blue Cheer and the Who into one perception, and how live variations of 'Witch Hunt' and the premature chord of 'Turn the Page' let error overtake and become the new original. The chapter exceeds Aristotle's principle of non-contradiction in 'pure language', where original, copy, and fan covers (Rock Band failures, the South Park 'Lil' Rush' flub, Rick Mercer's drum lesson) are fragments of one greater vessel, so errors are portals of discovery.

plato-forms.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
plato-forms.title: Smashing Critics’ Pumpkins
plato-forms.relation: Reisch reconstructs the rock-critical case against Rush ('pretentious', 'ridiculous', Greg Kot's jibe that Peart drums 'like he's working out a calculus formula') as resting on an implicit Platonism: the Forms fix what a 'real' rock'n'roll band is, so a band mixing rock with philosophy, literature, and mathematical precision seems to violate the metaphysical grain of the universe rather than merely disappoint a taste. He explains the Forms through Plato's trees and the Form of the song ('La Villa Strangiato' and 'Happy Birthday'), reads Jack Black's 'one atom' praise of Peart as mathematics-as-highest-knowledge, and treats the 'Aristocrats' joke and UFO mocking Geddy Lee as incongruity humor at kinds illicitly combined. Dropping the Platonic metaphysics of kinds collapses the critics' syllogism into a bare insistence that different is bad, which is the revenge Gene Simmons ('What kind of band is Rush? It's Rush.') and Billy Corgan ('they just don't fit in a neat box') already delivered.

plato-forms.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
plato-forms.title: Guardian Training
plato-forms.relation: Roger Travis argues Plato would welcome Halo as guardian training: mimesis is really 'playing epic pretend,' and Halo, like the Homeric epics that were Athens' textbooks, trains players in a way of life. Plato's Republic Book 10 critique—the painted bed as copy of a copy of the Form of Bed—warns that playing Master Chief could let appetite rule, yet the Laws' admission that the ideal city's politeia is itself a mimesis turns the tables: the Republic is its own training simulation of philosophic pretend. Re-imagining the cave as prisoners tied to couches playing Super Mario Bros, he argues Halo's dutiful NPCs and waking-to-duty player (literal cryo-wakeups in Combat Evolved and Halo 3) make it philosophy in Plato's own sense, with Aristotle's catharsis leavening the verdict.

plato-forms.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
plato-forms.title: I Listen to Public Radio
plato-forms.relation: Natasha Liebig reads Squidward as Schopenhauer made flesh: his endless craving for musical fame and revenge on Squilliam exemplifies the blind, irrational will-to-live whose frustration just is suffering, so even success could never satisfy him and others' joys (SpongeBob and Patrick playing) become his bellum omnium. Yet Squidward's clarinet, self-portraits and dance are Schopenhauer's aesthetic escape — will-less contemplation of universal Ideas, with music the most metaphysical art — granting fleeting moments of peace until his neighbors interrupt. The chapter closes on the irony that Schopenhauer's genius is childlike, so SpongeBob and Patrick's effortless wonder may make them the truer artists.

plato-forms.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
plato-forms.title: That Far-Away Look
plato-forms.relation: Lahr argues that Holmes's crime-solving is an art rather than a forensic science: like his inspiration Oscar Wilde, Holmes is an aesthete whose 'aesthetic sight' perceives the criminal-artist's design in clues, so that Watson the philistine ('What ineffable twaddle!') consistently misses what is self-evident to Holmes. He suggests Plato would say Holmes sees only the perfect Forms behind appearances, and reads the BBC adaptations accordingly: in The Case of the Silk Stocking Holmes's trance-like perception of the victims' pedicured feet reveals a killer with a foot fetish, while Sherlock's 'A Study in Pink' renders his insight as first-person vision with on-screen data. The queer coding (the Diogenes Club, Moriarty's 'hereditary tendencies,' Holmes as Wilde's physical and temperamental double) links Holmes to the first sexologists' puzzle of how marginal men recognize one another at a glance.

plato-forms.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
plato-forms.title: What’s Really Real
plato-forms.relation: Traces the 'veil' theme from Parmenides' dokos and the Indian maya to Ed Fletcher seeing 'the fabric of reality split open' in 'Adjustment Team' and the shadow world of 'Jon's World.' It locates Dick's enduring conviction that the empirical world is not ultimately real in the Plato he was given at UC Berkeley — the archetypal realm of Forms behind sensory appearances — and in his professed affinity for Spinoza's Deus sive natura, alongside the Pre-Socratics he devoured.

plato-forms.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
plato-forms.title: Chapter 14 - Trauma of the Real
plato-forms.relation: Introduces Paul Livingston's part with Dick's confession that reading Plato in college convinced him the empirical world was not truly real, then retells the cave of Republic Book VII in detail: prisoners bound since birth watching shadows of puppets cast by a fire. The cave becomes the frame for Dick's fiction — the 'reality' our percept-systems report is a show of images, and the philosophical quest is the prisoner's turn toward the archetypal reality behind the scenes.

plato-forms.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
plato-forms.title: Breakthrough to the Real
plato-forms.relation: Details the disorienting breakthrough in which characters learn that they themselves are fakes: Rachael's distress at her implanted memories ('How can it not know what it is?'), Deckard's paper unicorn in the director's cut confirming his own replicant status, and Ragle Gumm's soft-drink stand dissolving into a slip of paper reading 'SOFT-DRINK STAND' in Time Out of Joint. Each case maps onto the freed cave prisoner's discovery, and the disorientation is pressed onto the viewer: how can I be sure my own life and memories are not a fabrication?

plato-forms.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
plato-forms.title: Reality Is Not Real
plato-forms.relation: Contrasts Plato, for whom breakdown leads to a deeper and truer reality, with Dick's characters, whose breakthroughs lead only to another shifting reality — then introduces Jacques Lacan's three registers (the Real, the Imaginary, the Symbolic) as the positive account of Dick's 'sense of the real.' For Lacan, ordinary 'reality' — the accountant's respectable job, even the value of money — is purely Symbolic and Imaginary, and 'reality is not Real'; the Real is encountered only when that symbolic order breaks down, as in psychosis.

plato-forms.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
plato-forms.title: Remembrance of Being, Passed
plato-forms.relation: Reads Ubik's anti-chronological regressions — rocket to jet to biplane, 1992 decaying into 1939 — through Dick's 'orthogonal time' peeling onion-like layers toward greater Being, which Dick himself compared to Plotinus's concentric emanations from the One beyond all language and comprehension. Dick's 1974 pink-light experience is interpreted as Platonic anamnesis, recovered memory of the forms in a parallel time-stream, shading into the Gnostic conviction that our flawed material universe was created by an imperfect god.

plato-forms.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
plato-forms.title: Let the Blues Be
plato-forms.relation: Sartwell declares the Stones 'a cosmic essence, a Platonic Form, of rock music': where the Beatles passed through mannerist, baroque and rococo decadence to an aesthetic dead end, Keith stripped the rock lick to its essence from 'Satisfaction' through 'Gunface.' Invoking Plato's view that Forms are remembered and discovered — essences that are both our origin and our destiny — he argues the Stones reverted continually to the origins of their music in blues, country and soul while exposing the center of the center. Beggar's Banquet through Exile on Main Street, he proposes, just is rock music, achieving one's own essence as a legitimate aesthetic project.

plato-forms.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
plato-forms.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Fitzpatrick asks whether Klosterman's low-culture project (tribute bands, Toby Keith, the McNuggets diet) is mere titillation or genuinely valuable. Bentham's pushpin-versus-poetry hedonism matches Klosterman's rejection of 'guilty pleasures,' while Aristotle's eudaimonia — and Plato's forms, on which a tribute band is a copy of a copy of a copy — condemns a life of amusement. Mill resolves the question twice over: higher and lower pleasures justify ranking Klosterman's contemplative criticism above mere sensation, and On Liberty's free market of ideas shows that even false or partial low-culture claims (about Garth Brooks, Spurlock's Super Size Me) keep high culture's truths from decaying into unexamined dogma.

plato-forms.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
plato-forms.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Richard Rosenbaum asks how Gaiman's gods, abstract concepts made flesh who live or die by human belief, could exist, starting from Plato's Forms (Odin as personified battle-wisdom, Media as media) and the Allegory of the Cave, which gives new meaning to a protagonist literally named Shadow. Finding Forms too independent to need believers, he upgrades the metaphysics with Leibniz's Monadology: if everything, bodies and ideas alike, is composed of perception-bearing monads, then shared beliefs can agglomerate, 'level up' into a soul, and become a living god walking around America. Chalmers's hard problem of consciousness, panprotopsychism, and the claim that information has interdependent physical and phenomenal aspects supply the final mechanism, so collective belief realized phenomenally must become physically embodied, in contrast to the dualism of Descartes that made mind-body interaction mysterious.

plato-forms.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
plato-forms.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Rard tests whether objective morality survives the apocalypse by running four theories against Season Two: Plato's Forms explain universal truths about walkers ('walkers survive so long as their brains are relatively undamaged') but cannot handle white lies or changed circumstances, and Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Rick's rush from the shot Carl as rashness and Shane's supply run as courage, yet virtues prove relative and luck-dependent in a collapsed world. Natural law founders on clashing intuitions — Merle's racism and Hershel's barn of walkers each claim self-evidence. The chapter's center is Nietzschean: Hershel's barn is slave morality that pities the 'sick,' Maggie breaks from it, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and opening of the barn enact a will-to-power master morality without joy, while Rick alone moves toward amor fati — embracing the world as it is, refusing guilt over Lori's affair, and insisting the baby be born into the Walk Age.

plato-forms.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
plato-forms.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Mudde and Piercey argue Curb depicts Nietzschean nihilism made humdrum: in Larry's world 'the highest values devalue themselves,' so Ted Danson's 'anonymous' donation is leaked for glory, a terrorist warning becomes leverage in a tiff with Mindy Reiser, and strangers judge everyone constantly because no one is a moral authority. The Platonic and Aristotelian answers to what 'the good' is have no purchase here; moral language survives only as a hollow shell, which is MacIntyre's 'simulacra of morality,' and his own remedy—rebuilding communities that give moral rules a point—fails because on Curb community is hell ('I'd rather have the thieves than the neighbors'). Since ought no longer implies can, the show is tragic, though the Tourettic chef's opening night in 'The Grand Opening,' where Larry leads a communal torrent of obscenities in solidarity, offers a fragile glimpse of doing a little good.

plato-forms.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
plato-forms.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Rick Mayock stops a fictional Jeopardy! clock to apply Plato's divided line: most contestants, like the cave prisoners rewarded for predicting shadow sequences, trade in doxa - conjecture (eikasia) and belief (pistis) - while the Meno's slave boy shows how Socratic questioning ties true opinions down into knowledge. Winning requires only dianoia, hypothetical reasoning from hypotheses and definitions, never noesis, the dialectic that ascends to the eternal Forms; the Phaedo's example of perfect 'equality' shows why the 'Aha!' of recognition is re-cognition by an immortal soul already acquainted with the Forms. Watson, lacking such a soul, can clear a buzz threshold but never have an Aha! moment - it is Daedalus's statue, lifelike but sure to run away from the truth unless tied down.

plato-forms.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
plato-forms.title: Psych and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: C. Scott Sevier argues Henry deliberately recreated Shawn as Aristotle's 'another self' - Lassiter's 'which one?' joke in the kidnapping episode makes the identity explicit - and reads this through Plato's Symposium: via Diotima's ladder of love and the doctrine of forms, Henry achieves immortality by reproducing beauty in his son's educated soul, not just his body. The chapter then frames Shawn's fierce independence against his constant recourse to Henry's voice as the collision between medieval deference to authority and the modern ideal of autonomy in Descartes and Kant, showing that both thinkers quietly borrowed from Augustine (the causal adequacy principle, the good will), so Shawn's 'autonomy' is itself the product of his father's training - an internalized authority indistinguishable from his own.

plato-forms.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
plato-forms.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Archibald reads Gillian through Plato's Phaedo. The Argument of Opposites - cyclical deaths and rebirths that the immortal soul survives - maps onto the rape at thirteen that killed the child pageant girl and birthed a survivor, her shift into caretaker to control the stroked-out Commodore, and her final drugged regression before Nucky ('Nucky he did something very bad to me'). The Theory of Forms explains her treatment of roles as interchangeable: Jimmy is son, lover, and husband-Form rather than a person to mourn, Angela's death is merely an opportunity for rebirth, and the Jimmy-lookalike Roger can be dressed with his dog tags as 'James' - Forms changing shape while remaining, to Gillian, undamaged.

plato-forms.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
plato-forms.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: William Rodriguez argues Branagh's 1994 Mary Shelley's Frankenstein deliberately overturns what Plato's account of art as mimesis that forms character, and Colin McGinn's aesthetic theory of virtue (G-beings versus E-beings), lead us to expect - that beauty of soul shows in beauty of body - since the handsome Victor is the moral degenerate while De Niro's hideous creature is a moral virtuoso whose first words are 'friend' and 'father.' The beautiful Frankenstein family harbors ugliness: Oedipal scenes between Victor and his mother Caroline, the wedding that makes Elizabeth 'brother, sister no more; husband and wife,' and Victor's relish in abandoning his creation. The creature's questions - 'Do I have a soul?', 'Who am I?' - and his secret harvest for the peasant family credit moral worth to the ugly, so the monster fascinates us because the monster is us: evil may be attractive and lurking inside rather than deformed and outside.

plato-forms.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
plato-forms.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: A pub dialogue applies Aristotle's De Anima, where the soul is the first principle of living things, to cloning: since a living clone must have an emergent, unrepeatable soul, successfully cloning dinosaurs brings new life into existence, which is good, so cloning itself is ethical. It then argues that neither unguided natural selection nor a divine dragon-slayer who nonetheless allowed cloning technology gives us reason not to revive dinosaurs, against Malcolm's 'they had their shot'. But drawing on Plato's forms, it condemns Hammond for controlling rather than merely containing: the lysine contingency and enforced sterility leave the dinosaurs shadows of what they could be, denied their natural flourishing.

plato-forms.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
plato-forms.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Edwards argues that gene banks assume genes are the essence of a species, which he reads as a modernized Platonism: unchanging forms written in DNA, the same craving Hammond expresses in wanting to show people 'something that wasn't an illusion'. Following Hans Jonas's reading of Darwin, in which conditions rather than essence explain what an organism is, he casts Wu as the Platonist and Malcolm's 'life finds a way' as the evolutionary rebuttal in their debate over breeding control. The moral is that freezing DNA cannot save species, because what makes an animal what it is includes the vanished environment, so we should preserve habitats rather than entrust preservation to 'the hands of engineers'.

plato-forms.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
plato-forms.title: Dracula and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Wolfe asks what makes Stoker's mustachioed Count, Lugosi's, Dell Comics' science-hero Dracula, The Electric Company's malt-drinker, Blade's Drake, and Hotel Transylvania's overprotective dad all 'Dracula'. Plato's theory of Forms promises a shared ideal essence, but comparing particulars (origins from Vlad Tepes to Judas Iscariot, blood-drinking vs vanilla malts) finds no common thread, his 'Allegory of Dracula's Dungeon' recasts the cave to suggest Dracula may be only a shadow of some other Form like 'the undead', and the Republic's condemnation of art as imitation of imitation implies a fictional character may have no Form at all. Wolfe's own answer: the ideal Dracula is an outsider, an aristocrat, and a feeder on others, with everything else up for grabs.

plato-forms.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
plato-forms.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Using 'Flowers for Charlie', where a placebo pill convinces two scientists and even the Waitress that Charlie has become a genius, the chapter asks what actually makes something philosophy. Sounding smart is not philosophy: big words, the Sokal-style hoax paper submitted to a leading journal, and the 'Guru Effect' of credulous admirers all fail, yet Charlie's pronouncements turn out true by sheer luck - which is exactly Edmund Gettier's problem of epistemic luck illustrated with the broken-clock example. Since we can never verify our premises or our reasoning, the chapter sides with Aristotle's response to Plato's theory of forms that we can never determine what a thing is, only what it is not, and concludes the show is philosophical precisely because the Gang is the exact antithesis of reality, truth, and right action.

plato-forms.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
plato-forms.title: 16. Divine Hatred—Dalek Beauty
plato-forms.relation: Bowman uses 'Asylum of the Daleks' - where the Daleks preserve broken, insane Daleks as embodiments of 'divine hatred' - to test whether beauty is objective or subjective. Plato's Theory of Forms explains how hatred could be beautiful (the more a thing instantiates its Form, the more beautiful it is), while the Hume-Kant antinomy of beauty, Kant's disinterested judgment of taste (illustrated by Rory and Amy's invested judgments of each other versus the TARDIS's detached 'pretty'), and Nietzsche's account of beauty leading to divinity frame the Dalek hive mind's shared conceptual scheme. Since Kant says beauty is a symbol of morality, the Asylum-as-museum reveals Dalek values - which is why human-on-the-inside Clara is enshrined under maximum security, and why the Doctor is sickened to learn that he is himself an object of Dalek beauty.

plato-forms.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
plato-forms.title: Of the Simple and Complex
plato-forms.relation: The book's introduction argues that Downton Abbey's genius is letting universal moral and social realities burst forth in particular incidents: the snuffbox affair makes Thomas a classic villain (stealing, defaming Bates) and Bates a Christ-, Socrates-, or Confucius-type innocent, showing that moral clarity is beautiful rather than superficial. It reads the Thomas-Bates-Grantham hierarchy as an invitation to think about 'greater and lesser,' tying propriety (Confucius), dharma, and justice (Aristotle) to paying attention to social difference, which Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. It closes by insisting the characters are more complex than their types - Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law - and previews the volume's themes of Humean 'small morals' (etiquette), women's rights, work, place, and war.

plato-forms.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
plato-forms.title: 7. Pratchett’s Republic
plato-forms.relation: Kempner maps Plato's Republic onto Ankh-Morpork: Vetinari is the Philosopher King, the Watch of Guards! Guards! are the Guardians who devote themselves to the good of the whole community, and Platonic justice as keeping everything in its right place is Vetinari's guild-licensing, topiary-tending rule - including the jail cell whose locks are all on the inside. Against Plato's banishment of poets, The Truth shows words serving the just city: William de Worde's pursuit of 'the big truth' exposes the frame-up of Vetinari and extends the circle of Guardians to the free press. The chapter concludes that Pratchett keeps Plato's ideal only by bending it to observable reality - Vetinari rules for the city rather than remaking its people.

plato-forms.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
plato-forms.title: 3. There’s Only One God and His Name Is Death
plato-forms.relation: McKeever observes that central characters rarely die suddenly and unexpectedly in art even though such deaths define our emotional lives, and argues this is a 'representational limit of art,' like Hollywood ugliness and costume-drama archaic speech. Using Plato's theory of art as a copy of a copy (a picture of Tyrion's chipped goblet imitating the Form of the goblet) and Aristotle's catharsis, he then argues Martin overcomes the limit through epic scale: with so many viewpoint characters, Ned can die at the end of season one and Joffrey mid-season-four because attention simply shifts, so making a work epic is the general cure for what art cannot represent.

plato-forms.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
plato-forms.title: 2. If I Don’t Listen to My Imaginary Friend, Why the Fuck Should I Listen to Yours
plato-forms.relation: Kreider stages a chat between Plato and Aristotle about the show. On Plato's account, mimesis is an imitation of an imitation of the Forms, so Elliot's imaginary friend, his fake persona with Krista, and the Mr. Robot personality are intellectually and morally dangerous deceptions that let him commit terrorism without his rational self's consent; yet the Republic's censored poetry for the auxiliaries explains how fsociety's masked videos teach true beliefs, and how Elliot uses the fictional Mr. Robot to educate himself toward ideas he already knew were right. Aristotle's Poetics then defends imitation as natural and instructive - the show is a cautionary tragedy, and the Mr. Robot crutch is how Elliot eventually steps up to claim responsibility.

plato-forms.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
plato-forms.title: 14. Is E Corp an Evil Person
plato-forms.relation: Wood asks what E Corp ontologically is: on Plato's theory, it would participate in a Form of Corporation, while Aristotle's primary substances show E Corp is not an individual at all - just a name for ways people interact. Corporate personhood (from 1819 contract rights through Citizens United and Hobby Lobby) makes it a legal person whose responsibility diffuses 'almost to the point of evaporation,' and Kant's humanity formula explains the unease: a legal fiction with no intentions or dignity can never respect persons as ends, which is why Angela's quest for a moral 'who' behind Washington Township ends only with the two ordinary executives Price hands her.

plato-forms.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
plato-forms.title: 10. Hendrix Out of the Cave
plato-forms.relation: Scores 'Are You Experienced?' and 'Purple Haze' against the Allegory of the Cave: the backwards guitar and reversed cymbals are the painful, clumsy ascent from shadows toward the Form of the Good, with Hendrix as the initiator who must first drag the prisoner violently and then gently — 'come on across to me... we'll hold hands.' 'Purple Haze' becomes the midway delirium between cave and sun ('don't know if I'm coming up or down,' 'scuse me while I kiss the sky'), and the chapter concludes that the psychedelia is philosophical — consciousness opened by liberation from received opinion, not by LSD — warning the freed prisoner not to remain a pale copy of Plato or Hendrix.

plato-forms.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
plato-forms.title: 17. The Cry of Love
plato-forms.relation: Reads Hendrix as a romantic idealist on a Platonic-Neoplatonic arc: 'Room Full of Mirrors' shatters the cave wall and its projections toward The One, whose presence is pursued through eros with the veiled Beloved of Plotinus — the semi-divine feminine of 'Little Wing,' 'One Rainy Wish,' and 'Angel.' Hegel's Zeitgeist and world-spirit then frame the planned First Rays of the New Rising Sun as music meant to carry humanity's collective evolution, with Hendrix as Hegel's 'spiritual workman' and self-described messenger ('I am only a messenger and you are a Sheep in the process of evolution').

plato-forms.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
plato-forms.title: 13. Reason and Catharsis
plato-forms.relation: Argues that Twin Peaks frees viewers from the "tyranny of rationality" by refusing to make sense: Plato's sensible-versus-intelligible finger example explains our habit of abstracting concepts to resolve contradiction (the pale horse in the living room, Diane's texts, Dougie-as-tulpa), but Lynch keeps adding facts — the frog-moth crawling into the girl in Part 8 — that no framework absorbs. Drawing on Nietzsche's Twilight of the Idols claim that Socrates made rationality a treatment for weakness, and on the existentialist pairing of despair and freedom in a meaningless universe, the chapter says viewers can either demand the irrational fit their rationality like inauthentic existentialists or let go. Trela's alternative reading of Aristotle's catharsis — emotions purged of their connection to reality and felt for once in themselves — explains why we can savor the show's absurdity without despair, precisely because that world is not ours.

plato-forms.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
plato-forms.title: 12. Putting the Fun Back in Non-refundable
plato-forms.relation: Defends Snatched against its 37 percent Rotten Tomatoes score by retracing art criticism from Plato's claim, grounded in his theory of copies and originals, that art is an inferior imitation of reality, to Hume's 'Of the Standard of Taste', where value judgments track social values and refined experts may devalue works that offend their morals. Against moralistic critics, the chapter argues some art, like Guernica or 'Football Town Nights', exists to upset us.
