It then reads the film through Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: Emily's guilt-free firing scene and her cajoling her deflated mother toward Ecuador enact the refusal of socially manufactured guilt, putting the 'fun' back in non-refundable.

plato-forms.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
plato-forms.title: 7. The Mind Flayer through a Gnostic Lens
plato-forms.relation: Ewing reads the Mind Flayer as the Demiurge of the Upside Down, a dark derivative copy of our world complete with replicated Castle Byers and school decorations: he surveys Plato's Timaeus craftsman who shapes chaotic matter on the model of the Forms, Plotinus's One and its secondary demiurge, and the Gnostic variants, from the Valentinian just-but-imperfect craftsman to the Sethian Yaldabaoth, a serpent-faced false god who steals divine power. Because the Mind Flayer hive-minds Will and the demodogs, wants to conquer our dimension as a 'master race,' and hates the real world rather than serving it, the chapter concludes it matches the Sethian evil Demiurge, an incorporeal entity playing at being god.

plato-forms.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
plato-forms.title: 30. Socratic Superheroism
plato-forms.relation: Stages a dialogue between Socrates and Nebula to build a four-part scorecard of 'Socratic Heroism' — question all assumptions, intellectual humility (Socrates before the Delphic oracle: 'I am very conscious that I am not wise at all'), improve society without ever doing injustice, and courage unto death (the gadfly of the Apology) — then scores Thanos 0 for 4: 'I am incapable of error' and 'reality can be whatever I want' are the very opposites of humility and of objective, heavenly truth. It nominates Doctor Strange as the MCU's Socratic hero, whose humbling at Kamar-Taj, willingness to hand over the Time Stone against the obvious choice, and trust in the one winning future among 14,000,605 pass the tests.

plato-forms.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
plato-forms.title: Hope for the Future
plato-forms.relation: Applies Dewey's The Public and Its Problems to Alien and Aliens: the real villain is not the Xenomorph but a United Americas too weak to govern Weyland-Yutani, whose crude cost-benefit erasure of the Nostromo crew's interests shows a state that has lost the public's voice. Ash's arrogant 'perfect organism' objectivity, the appeal to blameworthy 'human nature,' and faith that big business runs everything illustrate Dewey's targets - Plato's static Forms, economic determinism, and rugged individualism - and since beliefs are habits of action (Peirce), the Company's deeds expose its professed principles as negligible fictions.

plato-forms.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
plato-forms.title: Just How Dark are the Dark Avengers
plato-forms.relation: Donovan and Richardson read Osborn's Dark Avengers through the Republic: Osborn is a modern Thrasymachus for whom justice is merely the advantage of the stronger, managing Bullseye's murder of Lindy and the team's image exactly as Glaucon's ring of Gyges predicts—villains like Moonstone, Daken, and Venom appearing good while doing injustice. Captain America, who tells Stark 'who made you the moral compass of us?', embodies the Socratic belief in a justice beyond human advantage, backed by the Forms and the allegory of the cave. Ms. Marvel, Noh-Varr, and Ares choose being just over appearing just, defecting or dying (Ares torn in half during the Siege) rather than serve Osborn's fraud.

plato-forms.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
plato-forms.title: Pretending to Talk about It
plato-forms.relation: Travis claims everyone misses the point of both Plato's cave and BioShock, and reads the post-assassination self-destruct sequence as the game's cave moment: though you may roam Ryan's office shooting walls ('active inaction', like the escaped prisoner contemplating the form of the Good), the sequence will not resolve until you insert the item, exposing 'a man chooses, a slave obeys' as hollow. The harvest-versus-save equivalence (Tenenbaum's gifts cancel the ADAM loss) is likewise a stroke of genius, not a flaw, because it shows in-game 'ethical choices' are as meaningless as the prisoners' shadow-naming contests. Since both cave and game run on mimesis, playing pretend, the way forward is to 'pretend to talk about it': performing philosophy through play as Plato's dialogues stage Socrates.

plato-forms.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
plato-forms.title: Of the Simple and Complex
plato-forms.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Downton's quaint domestic plots burst with universal moral and social meaning beneath their surface. Using the season 1 snuffbox incident, in which Thomas frames the innocent Bates for theft, it shows how the episode stages archetypal villainy and innocence akin to the universal figures of Plato's Republic and world mythology, so the 'simple' plot is morally clear rather than superficial. It then reads the hierarchy of Thomas, Bates, and Lord Grantham through Confucian propriety and Aristotelian justice, suggesting that justice partly consists in attention to 'greater and lesser,' something Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. Finally it insists that as concrete persons all three are morally mixed (Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law, Grantham is generous to tenants but cold to his daughters), and that this complexity is what rewards philosophical reflection, along with Hume's 'small morals' of etiquette.

plato-forms.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
plato-forms.title: Notes
plato-forms.relation: Tracing Fallout's own censorship history — the GURPS licensing cancellation threat, the invisibility of child NPCs in the European release, the moral panic after Columbine — the chapter asks whether it is wrong to simulate evil, framing the issue with Morgan Luck's gamer's dilemma. Plato's cave and the Forms ground the 'media impacts morals' worry: games are shadows of shadows whose simulated vice accumulates 'a large evil in our souls', which is also why Lucy's Vault upbringing leaves her underprepared for the wasteland's emotions. Against this, Aristotle's catharsis and Schulzke's claim that Fallout trains phronesis support depicting wrongdoing as practice for moral judgment, so the chapter concludes the right wrongs to depict are whichever maximize the simulation of choice, with Braun's player-controlled Tranquility Lane simulation as the dystopian counter-model.

plato-forms.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
plato-forms.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Patterson maps the Comics Code censorship debate onto Plato's Republic Book X, where imitative art is thrice removed from the Forms (the god's table, the carpenter's table, the painter's picture) and feeds the passionate soul, versus Aristotle's Poetics, where imitation is natural and tragedy's pity and fear yield catharsis. The O'Neil-Adams run embodies Aristotle: the slum story where a black tenant asks why Green Lantern helps 'orange skins' and 'purple skins' but never 'black skins,' the Ulysses Star land dispute, and Speedy's heroin addiction broke Code taboos so readers would learn from engagement rather than distance. Within the comic, Hal plays the establishment Platonist who would change an unjust law rather than disobey it and Green Arrow the Aristotelian activist, so their friendship dramatizes the ancient quarrel over whether art corrupts or teaches.

plato-forms.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
plato-forms.title: Rowling as an Inkling
plato-forms.relation: Argues Dumbledore's remark dissolves a false dilemma: the Hermione-as-idea versus Emma Watson contrast shows that existing in the head need not mean unreal. It then surveys thinkers who agree that mind and reality overlap: Plato's forms (the many broomsticks as imperfect copies of the ideal broomstick), Descartes on knowing essences by reason, Kant's mind-constructed objects, Berkeley's esse est percipi, Mill's phenomenalism, and Yogacara Buddhism's consciousness-fabricated emptiness, concluding that what is in the head can be genuinely real.

plato-forms.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
plato-forms.title: 12 The Shadow Realities of Indiana Jones
plato-forms.relation: Matthew Crippen and Matthew Dixon read the franchise's caves through Plato's allegory: in Crusade, stand-ins for God (the Cross of Coronado, the Grail, with the decoy chalices as shadows of a representation) appear underground, while Indy's self-realizations with his father occur at sunlit cave mouths, inching from shadow toward the Good. They fuse this with newer, active accounts of truth — James's 'truth happens to an idea' realized in the leap from the lion's head, Dewey on poetry as revelation, and Heidegger's aletheia as unconcealment — while Nietzsche's critique shows Platonic fictions can still be life-enhancing. The father and son 'shadow' one another (with Oedipal overtones through Elsa) until Henry Sr. relinquishes the Grail to save 'Indiana,' his path out of the cave.

plato-forms.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
plato-forms.title: Notes
plato-forms.relation: Tanswell takes Plato's side against Plato: where Republic Book VII mocks geometers who talk of 'squaring' and 'applying' as if math were practical doing, and Platonist foundationalism (Frege and Russell, ever-revising) treats proofs as revealing the eternal abstract structure of unchanging mathematical objects — modeled as a mighty load-bearing LEGO tower built from the base up — picture proofs show the activity is the point. Two diagrammatic proofs (the infinite series of triangles yielding 1/3, and the Pythagorean theorem via inflated, rotated, recombined triangles) work exactly like LEGO instruction booklets: sequences of pictures guiding a series of actions we must perform. With Wittgenstein's 'The mathematical proposition says to me: Proceed like this!', he proposes a 'LEGO account of diagrammatic proofs' on which mathematics, like LEGO, is fundamentally about what we do — building, playing, proving — not just about objects.

plato-forms.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
plato-forms.title: Will You Say Yes
plato-forms.relation: Michael Bruce ('Zeldathustra') reads the original Legend of Zelda through Nietzsche's thought of eternal recurrence: with no game clock, the ability to save, and looped enemy patterns, every playthrough repeats the same structure, and the player faces the demon's question — do you will to play once more and innumerable times more? The Triforce's split between Wisdom and Power becomes Nietzsche's opposition of the will-to-truth and the will-to-power, with Link's dungeon-by-dungeon self-overcoming enacting amor fati. Against Plato's two-world doctrine of Forms and the Christian after-worldly, the chapter insists the game (like life) gets its meaning from this world only — experimentation, repetition as training, and saying yes.

plato-forms.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
plato-forms.title: Zelda and Reality
plato-forms.relation: Joyce Havstad and Iris Jahng catalogue the women of Zelda — Zelda's many incarnations, Impa, the Twinrova sisters, the oracles Din and Nayru, Midna — finding the typologies of maiden, mother, and crone, then explain them with Beauvoir's The Second Sex: the myth of woman (Mother, Wife, Idea), femininity as made rather than born, and woman's enforced passivity against man's transcendence. Zelda is woman as Idea, traced to Platonic Forms: young, beautiful, virtuous, and radically passive (turned to stone in The Minish Cap, asleep through The Adventure of Link, imprisoned in nearly every game), an object that exists to motivate Link's heroism. Significantly, only the masculine-garbed Sheik and the pirate Tetra escape passivity, a shift the authors link to Miyamoto's design philosophy of 'reality over realism' and to changing conceptions of women.

plato-forms.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
plato-forms.title: NOTES
plato-forms.relation: Daniel Gallagher uses Aquinas to read Lost as a drama about mistaking finite goods for the ultimate good: Jack's hope in curing, Kate's in deceiving, Jin's in his father-in-law's employment, Locke's in Anthony Cooper, and the Virgin Mary statues full of heroin all instantiate Aquinas's approaching-Peter analogy, where we know only confusedly that someone (the perfect good) is coming toward us. Desmond's and Charlie's paralysis before the good is the sin of acedia, Rose's faith that the island itself healed her cancer is presumption, and her certainty that Bernard is alive illustrates Aquinas's claim - framed through Plato's episteme versus doxa - that faith sits midway between knowledge and opinion. The chapter closes on the harmony of faith and reason, from the Five Ways' first efficient cause to Eko's dying 'I ask for no forgiveness,' grounded in Augustine's restless heart that finds no peace until it rests in God.

plato-forms.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
plato-forms.title: The Office and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Nys uses Brent's quiz grievance about Mr. Spock (half-Vulcan, half-human) and his Crufts pedigree-dog analogy, Gareth's 'look at the ears' classification test, the dwarf/midget/elf/pixie interrogation of Alex, and Tim and Dawn's 'lethal blow' prank to introduce the problem of natural kinds. Realist answers come from Kripke (water is H2O whatever we call it), Aristotle's matter-and-form essences, and the DNA evidence separating Bornean clouded leopards from mainland cousins, while Wittgenstein's language games and Quine's point that our innate similarity senses mislead support the constructivist that we lay classification on an unstructured world. The verdict: nature supplies real differences but never carves itself into kinds, and the line-drawing remains up to us.

plato-forms.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
plato-forms.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
plato-forms.relation: Reads South Park's music through the Greek doctrine of ethos: Sextus Empiricus' story of Pythagoras sobering drunk youths with slow aulos tunes and Plato's banishment of the soft Ionian and Lydian modes anticipate episodes where music directly changes behavior — Slayer's 'Raining Blood' scattering the hippie horde in 'Die Hippie Die', Cher blasted at the ATF standoff, and the Brown Noise in 'World Wide Recorder Concert'. Plato's tripartite soul maps how the Succubus's 'Morning After' spell enchants Chef's appetitive soul until the boys reverse the melody, while the Sirens' cosmic harmony in the Republic's Myth of Er links back to pitch-planet correspondences. Against Plato's view of music as inferior imitation, Schopenhauer's claim that music copies the Will itself explains why Grandpa's Enya torture in 'Death' communicates despair better than argument; authenticity judgments (Phil Collins appreciated only on Ritalin, Cartman's cynically reworded Faith + 1 hits) echo Plato's demand that music imitate the good.

plato-forms.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
plato-forms.title: Notes
plato-forms.relation: Uses Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy and Lacan's ethics of psychoanalysis to argue season two failed as tragedy because feminist morality became the inflated 'Good' that blocks the transgression of limits through which Dionysian wisdom is won. Season one works because Rust's philosophy filters the Carcosa horrors without moralizing, whereas season two — failing Aristotle's catharsis model and repeating Euripides' mistake — represses the sexual knowledge troubling Velcoro, Bezzerides, and Woodrugh, so Dionysus returns only as money and violence, as in The Bacchae. Ani's arc is read through Nietzschean ressentiment toward her father and Freud's return of the repressed, with Kantian sexual dignity ('maybe you were put on earth for more than fucking') and the male gaze as the contemporary Good the show never crosses.

plato-forms.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
plato-forms.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
plato-forms.relation: Rard tests whether any morality survives the apocalypse with an objective basis: Plato's Forms fail to capture changing facts (Hannah the bicycle girl decaying from mom to walker) and white lies, and Aristotle's function-based virtue ethics proves too relative and luck-dependent for survivors like Rick (rashness at Carl's shooting) and Shane (courage fetching supplies, rage at the barn). Nietzsche then supplies the frame: Hershel's barn of pitied 'sick people' is Christian slave morality that guilts the strong, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and forcing open of the barn doors grope toward a master morality 'for the Walker Age' without ever achieving nobility. Rick alone approaches the higher type, refusing to judge Lori's affair, insisting the baby be born, and embracing the post-walker world as one he would choose again.

plato-forms.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
plato-forms.title: Between Two Camps in the Witcher
plato-forms.relation: Kammerer reads the Witcherverse's magic through the fault line between 'big tent' Platonism (top-down causation from a source, a great chain of being of nested celestial spheres) and modern naturalism (bottom-up mechanism). The Season of Storms exchange in which Geralt tells Dandelion that meteoric swords gather power descending through elemental planes - without denying those planes exist - shows Sapkowski keeping both worldviews alive, while Novigrad's Eternal Fire pogrom in The Witcher 3 mirrors fourth-century Alexandria's wars over magic and Christianity. Heidegger's 'metaphysics grounds an age' and his critique of enframing nature as standing-reserve frame Yennefer's instrumental view of magic and her djinn-summoning in The Last Wish, and Plotinus's Enneads supplies the vision of true magic as internal to a cosmic emanation rather than a mere technology.

plato-forms.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
plato-forms.title: The Beauty of the Game
plato-forms.relation: The Brands stage a broadcast-booth debate about whether a championship game was 'beautiful,' with Dickie V defending Hume's subjectivism ('beauty is in the eye of the beholder' and the expert's delicacy of taste) and Billy defending Plato's objective Form of Beauty. Jim exposes each side's flaw (Hume's circular appeal to experts, Plato's third-man regress from the Parmenides/Aristotle) and proposes a synthesis: games have 'outer beauty' (universally observable fluid motion, like improvised jazz or dance) and 'inner beauty' (the strategy and reason the knowledgeable fan grasps), reconciling the objective and subjective.

plato-forms.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
plato-forms.title: Fourteenth Hole Plato and Confucius on the Form of Golf From the Real to the Ideal
plato-forms.relation: Stephen Laumakis stages a thought experiment pitting Plato the Idealist against Confucius the Realist/Pragmatist on how to think about and play golf. On Plato's theory of Forms, every club, ball and swing is an imperfect copy of a timeless, unchanging Form—there is a 'perfect' swing (Tiger Woods, Ernie Els) that par and the handicap system let us measure ourselves against, so golf is about striving toward the Ideal. Confucius, read through the 'Great Learning' and 'Analects' (li, ren, self-cultivation, unrelenting practice), instead prizes the situation-sensitive sage who negotiates each bad lie (Phil Mickelson's flop shots). Laumakis concludes the good golfer must integrate both: pursue perfection while wielding practical wisdom about when to go for it and when to lay up.

plato-forms.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
plato-forms.title: Losing Beautifully
plato-forms.relation: Starting from Brad Gilbert's 'winning ugly' against McEnroe, the chapter argues that if one can win ugly one can also lose beautifully, and that aesthetic judgment is intrinsic to tennis. It uses Plato's account of techne (craft as true, knowledge-grounded art, versus mere imitation) and Plato's warning against 'lovers of sights and sounds' who stop at appearance rather than reaching Beauty itself, alongside Walton on aesthetic value as pleasurable admiration, to place tennis among the performing arts. It distinguishes physical ugliness (strokes vs. game style, e.g., the retriever) from psychological ugliness (legitimate vs. illegitimate gamesmanship), holding that McEnroe's manipulative rages make a win improper to admire while Federer's full range embodies beautiful play.

plato-forms.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
plato-forms.title: Human Nature and Freedom in Adaptation
plato-forms.relation: Ganssle uses Adaptation's four main characters to test Sartre's claim that existence precedes essence against Walker Percy's account of immanence and transcendence. Laroche, endlessly adaptable ('Done with fish'), embodies Sartrean radical freedom and pure immanence; Donald owns his love ('You are what you love, not what loves you') and lives without bad faith; Orlean and Charlie are paralyzed in bad faith, unable to choose. Ganssle contrasts Sartre's rejection of a fixed human nature (grounded in atheism, against Plato's and Augustine's Forms) with Percy's view that persons are unlike infinitely mutable orchids, arguing the film sides with Percy: the antiessentialist self is 'lost in the cosmos.'

plato-forms.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
plato-forms.title: 13. Reason and Catharsis
plato-forms.relation: Elsby and Luzecky argue that we compulsively rationalize Twin Peaks (tulpas, pale-horse omens, Diane-as-tulpa) the way we abstract concepts to tame the contradictory sensible world (Plato's long-and-short finger), but Lynch—especially in Part 8—deliberately thwarts this, exposing what Nietzsche in Twilight of the Idols calls the post-Socratic tyranny of rationality. They offer an alternative reading of Aristotelian catharsis (via Trela): because the fictional world is not ours, we can experience its irrationality and absurdity, emotions purged of their tie to reality, as freedom rather than the existential despair the absurd would cause in our own world.

plato-forms.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
plato-forms.title: Nietzsche and the Meaning and Definition of Noir
plato-forms.relation: Mark Conard uses The Postman Always Rings Twice and Goodis's Night Squad to survey the failed attempts to define noir (genre, style, cycle, mood) and contrasts two theories of definition: Socrates/Plato's search for the essential form versus Nietzsche's flux metaphysics, in which no stable 'being' exists behind becoming and language falsifies a world in motion, making essences and definitions fictions ('I am afraid we are not rid of God because we still have faith in grammar'). He proposes that noir is best understood as an American artistic response to Nietzsche's death of God, the loss of transcendent meaning and value that produces noir's pessimism, alienation, and moral disorientation, citing Sam Spade shrugging off his partner's murder and Ole Andersen passively awaiting his killers. Ironically, the same flux that makes noir what it is (the death of God) is what makes noir impossible to define.

plato-forms.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
plato-forms.title: 2001 A Philosophical Odyssey
plato-forms.relation: Stoehr interprets Kubrick's 2001 as inducing a feeling of disembodied presence through unrooted camerawork (contrasted with Ford's The Searchers), matching its theme of technology severing us from the natural world and our bodies. Drawing on Heidegger's Dasein and Hubert Dreyfus's On the Internet, he argues there are no context-free Archimedean standpoints and stages the Plato-versus-Nietzsche debate over the body: Plato's Phaedo prizes the soul's escape from the body, while Nietzsche's Zarathustra affirms embodied, situated existence. HAL's seeming humanity underscores that machines lacking bodies cannot fully replicate human intelligence.

plato-forms.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
plato-forms.title: The Matrix, the Cave, and the Cogito
plato-forms.relation: Conard argues that The Matrix alludes to Plato's cave (the pod-bound humans mistaking the program for reality, Neo's painful ascent) and to Descartes' dream argument and evil-genius doubt (the singular consciousness generating the Matrix), but betrays their spirit by rejecting transcendence and the a priori. Because the film is 'Christianity without God'—Neo can only remake the shadow-world of the Matrix, not touch ultimate reality—it grounds knowledge in a subjective gut feeling ('being the One is just like being in love') rather than Descartes' intellectual intuition of God or Plato's rational grasp of the Forms, leaving no answer to whether life outside the Matrix is itself another illusion.

plato-forms.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
plato-forms.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
plato-forms.relation: Baltzer-Jaray uses Kant's phenomena/noumena split, Plato's Forms, and Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' to ask whether Jack Skellington can know the essence of Christmas and whether Vincent Malloy can know what it is to BE Vincent Price. She argues Jack's lab-experiments on presents and snowflakes ('Jack's Obsession') can only yield phenomena, never the noumenal essence, so Kant would permit belief but not knowledge; Vincent, watching only Price's horror roles, grasps a mere phenomenal fragment. Via Nagel she concludes neither can occupy another's subjective viewpoint, so the lesson of both films is to celebrate otherness through communication rather than trying to be someone else.

plato-forms.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
plato-forms.title: 19_LaRocca_Chapter_018.html
plato-forms.relation: Rick Altman dismantles four and a half 'fallacies' that let film theory ignore sound: the historical fallacy (sound as a late add-on), the ontological fallacy (image alone is cinema), the reproductive fallacy (recording reproduces rather than represents sound), the nominalist fallacy, and the half-fallacy of indexicality. In the nominalist section he explicitly frames the dispute over whether the 'same' sound heard from different seats shares a real identity as the medieval realism-versus-nominalism debate, casting Plato and Augustine as the realists and William of Ockham as the nominalist, and warning that ultra-nominalism about sound jeopardizes shared understanding. He uses Peirce's index/icon/symbol distinction to argue electronics has desacralized cinema's indexicality.

plato-forms.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
plato-forms.title: Aww, . . . Poor Monster. Should We Feel Sorry for the Carrionites
plato-forms.relation: Simon Hewitt uses the Carrionites, who wield words instead of numbers, to ask whether science can be done without mathematics, a question in the philosophy of mathematics about mathematical Platonism (numbers existing outside space and time). He lays out the Quinean indispensability argument, then reviews Hartry Field's number-free Newtonian gravity and Mark Balaguer's attempt on Quantum Mechanics as "Carrionite physics," noting both fall short. He closes arguing that even if numbers were dispensable for science, our knowledge of mathematical truths still suggests numbers exist.

plato-forms.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
plato-forms.title: A Beautiful Destiny
plato-forms.relation: Clive Cazeaux asks whether the Daleks can be beautiful, canvassing theories of beauty to resolve the puzzle of a monster being beautiful. He distinguishes Kant's higher natural beauty (and his suspicion of 'dependent,' purpose-designed beauty like the Dalek casing) from Hegel's view that beauty in art, perceiving thought in matter, is higher, and finds Plato most helpful: to call the Daleks beautiful is Platonic love, being drawn to engage with them as a wholly-other form of life whose design succeeds. He surveys Alexander of Hales, Rosenkranz's aesthetic inferno, and formalism (the Krutikov design parallel) without a final verdict, showing the dispute turns on metaphysics.

plato-forms.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
plato-forms.title: 22. Punk Rock Saves Lives
plato-forms.relation: R.W. Main argues punk saves lives by replacing the myth of purity - the ideal behind one-drop rules, eugenics, and moral exclusion - with a philosophy of filth that revalues the rejected and abject, letting the outcast reclaim agency. He stages Diogenes the Cynic's street-living, shameless filth as the original punk counterpoint to Plato's perfect Forms and philosopher-king (Plato the 'sell-out'), and enlists Nietzsche's claims that morality denies life while art saves it. Camus's Sisyphus closes the argument: punk's freedom is revolt, giving the gods the middle finger since 'there is no fate that cannot be surmounted by scorn'; more concretely, punks save lives as anti-bullies, the 'Duncan Effect' of Some Kind of Wonderful and SHARPS skinheads protecting misfits.

plato-forms.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
plato-forms.title: 20. The Mystery of Math
plato-forms.relation: Barta and Lee cast the debate over whether math is invented or discovered as Protagoras versus Pythagoras, mapped onto Foundation. Protagorean relativism ('man is the measure') and modern formalism (Hilbert, Poincaré) appear in the Empire's politicized, self-serving use of math and Gaal Dornick's culturally contingent base-ten counting, while Plato and Aristotle rebut relativism via the Theaetetus and the Law of Non-Contradiction ('if Hari's a liar, he dies'). Pythagorean realism/mathematical Platonism—numbers as the fundamental reality—appears in Luminism's holy number three, Kalle's poetic proofs, and the Foundationists' quasi-religious faith that psychohistory reveals reality's mathematical structure, with Gödel, Quine-Putnam indispensability, and Wigner's 'unreasonable effectiveness' as modern heirs and Aristotle as the standing critic.

plato-forms.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
plato-forms.title: 8. What Are You Hearing
plato-forms.relation: Wissner analyzes how the musical scores of dream/imagination episodes signal states of being, framing music through Plato (music as mimetic yet man-made and 'unreal,' functioning as image-evoking signs) and Aristotle (music forms images of character and, via ethos, can alter minds and moods). She shows how electronic instruments, reverberation, whole-tone and repeated melodies mark dream versus reality in 'Perchance to Dream,' 'A Stop at Willoughby,' 'Twenty-Two,' 'Shadow Play,' and 'The Midnight Sun,' arguing the scores answer whether characters are dreaming, awake, imagining, alive, or dead through contextual musical signs.

plato-forms.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
plato-forms.title: MOTHERHOOD
plato-forms.relation: Laura Newhart narrates coming to know Kevin, her son adopted from Guatemala, first through monthly photographs and then in person, repeatedly finding her interpretations 'fuzzy and incomplete.' She frames this epistemic problem with Plato's Republic – Socrates' hierarchy in which a two-dimensional image is inferior in being and truth to the physical object, which is inferior to the eternal Form or soul – concluding that because we are bound to changing physical bodies, the soul is hardest to know, so she and Kevin may never fully know each other, a shared condition rather than a failure.

plato-forms.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
plato-forms.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
plato-forms.relation: John D. Norton poses three sailing paradoxes — how a wind-powered boat sails into the wind, faster than the wind, and whether 'making its own wind' makes it a perpetual-motion machine — echoing Zeno's paradoxes of motion and measure as engines of philosophical clarity. He resolves the first two by rejecting the causal truism that an effect cannot exceed or oppose its cause (the wind's force, resolved into drive and beam components against a resistant hull, is the real cause), using this to argue causal principles are elastic labels grafted onto science, never laws it must obey. For the third he builds an idealized wind-turbine boat thought experiment showing created-wind energy is exactly consumed by counter-force, and debates James Brown's Platonist view (that thought experiments 'see' laws in a Platonic realm, like grasping the ideal triangle) against his own deflationary view that they are merely picturesque argument.

plato-forms.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
plato-forms.title: BLUES
plato-forms.relation: Ron Bombardi argues there are two incompatible histories of the blues, tracing the split to Plato's and Aristotle's opposed views of difference. Using Ian Hacking's 'making up people,' he says the 'orthodox' tale treats the blues as the product of a distinct kind of people (Platonic kinds generating individuals), while the 'unorthodox' tale — the hybrid, cosmopolitan music of the Mississippi Sheiks — fits Aristotle's nominalism, where only individuals exist and forms are things 'in name only.' Invoking the Socratic 'know thyself,' he concludes the blues has no essence and that the 'pay your dues' authenticity maxim reduces persons to social kinds and perpetuates the very oppression the blues protests; the blues, he says, is finally 'ours.'

plato-forms.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
plato-forms.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
plato-forms.relation: Clark uses Barry Schwartz's Paradox of Choice and the characters of Sex and the City to argue that too much dating choice turns people into unhappy 'maximizers' who seek the absolute best, rather than 'satisficers' content with the merely excellent. She traces how Charlotte, Miranda, Carrie, Big, and Samantha each attain their maximized 'ideal' mate (Trey, Robert Leeds, Petrovsky/Big, Richard Wright) and find it hollow, only becoming happy when they 'settle' for a reciprocal partner (Harry, Steve, John, Smith) after the post-9/11 shift in the series' mood. She frames maximizing as clinically narcissistic (choosing a mate as a mirror of oneself) and invokes Plato to warn that trying to make the ideal real yields only disappointment.

plato-forms.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
plato-forms.title: 8. Star Wars
plato-forms.relation: Rowlands reads Star Wars as Manichaean (light vs dark side of the Force) and contrasts it with Plato, for whom evil is merely absence of good and the form of the good is most real, an idea Augustine (via Plotinus) folded into Christianity. Siding with Lucas that Darth Vader's evil is palpably real, he then uses Nietzsche's 'Dionysus against the Crucified': the Christian strategy represses drives (Freudian repression), the 'hippy' strategy merely expresses them, but greatness requires sublimation into higher forms. Vader taps his dark side but fails to sublimate, so he is a flawed unbalanced megalomaniac (like Nietzsche's Borgia/Napoleon), not a true Ubermensch living life as art.

plato-forms.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
plato-forms.title: NOTES
plato-forms.relation: Ted Cohen denies there is any sound argument from 'X is better than Y' to 'it is better to like X,' using Bach vs. Elvis vs. Milton Babbitt on complexity to show the criterion collapses. He reframes art around 'communities of appreciation'—citing Augustine's claim that a people is defined by what it loves in common—and reports (via a blues club in Memphis and the Marriage of Figaro) that what all appreciators of a work share is 'nothing' but their love of it, a Goodman-style nominalism. He challenges Kant's insistence that genuine aesthetic judgments claim universality, arguing real appreciative communities are less-than-universal overlapping circles.

plato-forms.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-forms.title: 27. Squid Game as Philosophy The Myths of Democracy
plato-forms.relation: The chapter argues that Squid Game exposes five 'myths' of democracy by showing how its trappings mask control by the wealthy few. Using Aristotle's Politics and Nicomachean Ethics it attacks the myth of free choice (the players' consent is coerced by debt) and the failure to cultivate virtue and transparency (Gi-hun deceives Il-nam in the marble game); it uses Sen and Nussbaum's capability approach to deny genuine empowerment; and it applies Plato's Phaedo two-worlds doctrine to argue the game instantiates no true form of truth, beauty, goodness, or justice. Il-nam's tie-breaking vote and Player 111's advantages illustrate that equality is only superficial, leaving a Hobbesian war of all against all inside a democratic shell.

plato-forms.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-forms.title: 93. Asterios Polyp as Philosophy Master of Two Worlds
plato-forms.relation: Richards reads Mazzucchelli's Asterios Polyp as a visual meditation on universals versus particulars and the abstract versus concrete, using its CMYK color coding and character styles (Asterios as cool geometric solids, Hana as warm crosshatching) to stage Plato's two worlds. Asterios, a 'paper architect' living in perfect uninstantiated abstraction, undergoes an inverted Hero's Journey (Campbell's monomyth) down into the concrete world—building an actual treehouse, telling the Ise shrine story—to become 'master of two worlds,' reconciling Form and matter, universal and particular, and accepting impermanence just as an asteroid closes on Earth.

socratic-ignorance.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
socratic-ignorance.title: The Fates of Socrates and Seinfeld
socratic-ignorance.relation: William Irwin compares Jerry and Socrates: the 'Jerry problem' of whether the fictional Jerry is the real Jerry (complicated by Seinlanguage) mirrors the Socratic problem of separating Socrates from Plato's dialogues. Jerry, like Socrates the gadfly, provokes his circle with questions that hunt for essences - the black-and-white cookie, 'is soup a meal?' - and shares Socrates' irony (the 'War: What Is It Good For?' gag in 'The Marine Biologist' works exactly like Socratic shamming ignorance). But where Socrates died serenely per the Apology and Phaedo, Jerry is self-absorbed and ends the series convicted under the Good Samaritan law, doing his stand-up 'gadfly' routine for prison inmates - an examined life, but not an exemplary one.

socratic-ignorance.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
socratic-ignorance.title: Unknown
socratic-ignorance.relation: Irwin parallels Neo's mission with Socrates' divine commission from the Oracle at Delphi to 'wake up' Athens: both are driven by a single question ('What is the Matrix?' versus 'What is the good life?'), both are charged by the authorities, and both sting a complacent public. He explains the Socratic method through the Euthyphro exchange on holiness, where a follow-up question ('Is the holy holy because the gods approve it, or do they approve it because it is holy?') exposes Euthyphro's ignorance, and introduces Socrates' mantra 'I know nothing' as the humility that launches his quest just as Neo's lack of self-knowledge launches his.

socratic-ignorance.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
socratic-ignorance.title: Unknown
socratic-ignorance.relation: Irwin compares the film's kitchen-table Oracle with the Pythia at Delphi: both utter cryptic prophecies that seekers misread, from Croesus's doomed war to Morpheus's certainty that Neo is the One, and both make self-knowledge the real key to interpretation. He reads the 'Temet Nosce' sign and the cookie scene through the Delphic maxims 'Know thyself' and 'Nothing in excess', arguing Neo fulfills the prophecy only when he comes to know and believe in himself, and closes by linking Socrates' gadfly mission and 'the unexamined life is not worth living' to Fight Club, Boys Don't Cry, and Memento.

socratic-ignorance.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
socratic-ignorance.title: Last Pitch
socratic-ignorance.relation: Reid argues that baseball and Socratic elenchus are both constructed to cultivate aretē, excellence. She maps four parallels onto concrete moments: both live off uncertainty (pre-game jitters, the 2001 Rivera–Gonzalez Series finish), both require risking failure (Ted Williams playing a doubleheader to protect his .400, Kirk Gibson's hobbling 1988 homer off Dennis Eckersley, Billy Beane's fear beside Lenny Dykstra), both demand active self-testing (Lou Gehrig retiring when complimented on a routine play), and both impose an obligation to return and challenge others — Plato's cave allegory, Socrates the gadfly, the aging champion who applauds the record-breaker. The Delphic oracle's riddle, that Socrates is wisest in knowing his ignorance, is the batter's-box humility every at-bat demands.

socratic-ignorance.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
socratic-ignorance.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Gareth Matthews contrasts Plato's serene Phaedo — Socrates conducting a seminar on immortality, death as the cure for life's ills, 'we owe a cock to Asclepius' — with Gibson's prolonged torture, while noting deep parallels: both men were condemned by large courts on religious charges (impiety, blasphemy) with political subtexts. Socrates in the Apology models facing death through Socratic ignorance ('to fear death is to think oneself wise when one is not'), and Matthews argues Gibson's magnified suffering makes Christ an icon of an atonement nobody could imitate rather than a model for our own deaths; only the Gethsemane prayer and 'why hast thou forsaken me' (read via Cullmann) can actually help a believer face dying.

socratic-ignorance.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
socratic-ignorance.title: The One Question I Could Not Answer
socratic-ignorance.relation: Comic writer Mark Waid, hired by DC editor Dan DiDio to re-imagine Superman in Superman: Birthright, is stumped by the question 'Why does he do what he does?' He argues that post-9/11 kids see the Big Blue Boy Scout as an ultraconservative protector of a corrupt status quo, making him irrelevant to a generation that knows heroes from metal detectors and assassinated visionaries. Invoking Socrates' claim that the genuine search for wisdom begins with admitting we do not know, Waid resolves to unlearn a lifetime of Superman lore, and locates the key to the character's motivation in Kal-El's utter aloneness: he is the sole survivor of Krypton and 'doesn't belong here'.

socratic-ignorance.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
socratic-ignorance.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Kevin Kinghorn uses virtue epistemology (Sosa, Code) to solve the puzzle of why Uncle Andrew alone hears only roaring when Aslan sings Narnia into being: he fails all four intellectual virtues. He does not value truth for its own sake (unlike Frank the Cabby), indulges wishful thinking (like Edmund defending the Witch for Turkish Delight, or imagining Jadis fancies him), lets fear dictate belief (terror of the animals he has vivisected), and lacks Socratic self-knowledge, which the dragonized Eustace painfully acquires. A closing reading of Prince Caspian has each character's ability to see Aslan track their earlier trust in Lucy's testimony: sin blinds, and faith produces its own authenticating evidence.

socratic-ignorance.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
socratic-ignorance.title: Poker and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Young reads David Sklansky's fundamental theorem of poker — play as if you could see all the cards — through Aristotle and Husserl. Aristotle's phronesis and virtue-as-habituation explain how excellent players come to perceive the particulars (pot odds, opponent tendencies, the best possible hand) and stay unharmed even when losing with the best play, while Husserl's Cartesian Meditations, translated hand-by-hand into poker terms, supply analogical appresentation for knowing the other minds seated across the table. Chris Moneymaker's 2003 'Bluff of the Century' all-in with nothing against Sammy Farha shows how bluffing randomizes play and lets you shape the truth you seek, until a slow-played quad aces ends the night in Socratic humility about the limits of knowledge.

socratic-ignorance.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
socratic-ignorance.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: 'The Dream of a Bullshit-Free Culture' argues Frankfurt revives a centuries-old philosophical tradition: Socrates searching for genuinely wise people rather than purveyors of hearsay, Descartes' Meditations discarding every belief short of certainty, and Hume's forkcondemning divinity-school metaphysics that contains neither abstract nor experimental reasoning to the flames. The twentieth-century apotheosis is the Vienna Circle, whose Rudolf Carnap dissected Heidegger's 'Das Nichts selbst nichtet' as mere appearance of meaning, calling metaphysicians 'musicians without musical ability'. The editors cast Frankfurt as the latest carrier of this Enlightenment anti-bullshit torch, with the book's popularity reconnecting seminar-room philosophy to the marketplace and voting booth.

socratic-ignorance.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
socratic-ignorance.title: The Talking Cure for Our Culture
socratic-ignorance.relation: Young argues South Park is perceived as dangerous for the very reasons Socrates was executed — corrupting the youth and impiety — and that like Socrates it is really a gadfly promoting the examined life. Cartman is read through Arendt's Eichmann: evil as thoughtlessness, the inability to think from another's standpoint or ask if one can live with oneself, while Kyle and Stan's dialogues (such as deliberating Stan's grandfather's euthanasia request in 'Death') model the perspective-taking Arendt calls thinking. A final Freudian section explains the show's vulgarity as essential: jokes work like dreams, releasing repressed drives so the culture can talk through what it forbids.

socratic-ignorance.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
socratic-ignorance.title: How to do Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Johnson argues through Colbert's satire that truth is neither individual ('My Truth') nor cultural ('wikiality' — a Wikipedia entry does not become true by consensus), since relativism is self-contradictory and implies slavery was not wrong before abolition. He deploys Locke's attack on 'enthusiasm' to show 'truthiness' is circular reasoning — sure because one is sure — and dismantles the 'right to my opinion' as a bid to shield beliefs from evidence, closing with Socrates' model: when evidence runs out, admit ignorance and keep doing philosophy.

socratic-ignorance.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
socratic-ignorance.title: “You Rationalize” Jackie Brown’s Pragmatism
socratic-ignorance.relation: K. Silem Mohammad argues Jackie Brown is a study in aporia and Wittgensteinian aspect perception: Ray Nicolette's purple/white bag paralysis, Ordell's 'Is that Rutger Hauer?' mistake, Jackie on the LAX moving walkway, and 'Across 110th Street' turning diegetic all force a re-description of experience within particular language games. The thrice-repeated Del Amo money switch-off adds no information but displays the characters' differing aspects of one event. Against Ordell's mind-fucking 'logical chains', Jackie's 'that's what you do to go through with the shit you start, you rationalize' embodies a pragmatist view of reason as context-bound use, matched by Max's calmly uncertain 'I think I do. Good enough?'

socratic-ignorance.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
socratic-ignorance.title: You Can’t Tell the Players Without a Program
socratic-ignorance.relation: Auxier revives Plato's ancient quarrel with the poets — the Republic's banishment of imitators whose pretty words are copies that stir the masses' feelings, the philosopher-king's city, the Ion's contempt for rhapsodes, Socrates' wisdom as Delphic acknowledgment of ignorance — while branding Plato an elitist and 'Poetry NIMBY.' He then stages a fantasy dithyramb contest at the Meadowlands where Dylan ('Subterranean Homesick Blues') and Springsteen ('Blinded by the Light') trade internal rhymes and alliteration before Weird Al's palindromes deflate Bob's seriousness. The virtuous poet wins all nine Muses by wooing their mother Mnemosyne — tapping the collective memory of the race with gratitude and discipline — which explains why Springsteen, unlike the prideful Dylan who lost the Muses, retains moral authority; the philosophers, needless to say, are just jealous of the bar.

socratic-ignorance.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
socratic-ignorance.title: Where Do We Go from Here
socratic-ignorance.relation: David Kyle Johnson argues that Colbert's gut-thinking persona (the Harriet Miers 'I know her heart' bit, 'that's my right' on the Panama Canal) satirizes a real and widespread vice, and he refutes the philosophies behind it. Individual and moral relativism collapse into self-contradiction and absurdity ('Lincoln was not assassinated' would be 'true for' someone; Hitler could not be condemned), while gut-justification is what Locke called 'enthusiasm' - a belief that is 'its own proof,' circular like the prophet whose revelation needs no burning bush. Following Jamie Whyte, he dismantles the 'right to my opinion' (running example: the friend who insists on a grassy-knoll shooter despite the melon-head evidence): there is no epistemic or moral right to undefended belief, and no right to intellectual comfort. Against this he holds up Socrates, wisest because he alone admitted ignorance, and insists philosophy and politics progress only through argument, so truthiness is never an acceptable substitute.

socratic-ignorance.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
socratic-ignorance.title: Colbert Is (the Tragedy and Comedy of) America, and So Are We
socratic-ignorance.relation: Ralkowski asks whether Colbert is America's Socrates, comparing Colbert's ironic interviews (Caitlin Flanagan on feminism, Harvey Mansfield on manliness, Howard Dean's superdelegates, the ABC Stephanopoulos-Gibson debate) to Socrates' definitional refutations of Euthyphro and the Athenian elite. Like Socrates in Plato's cave allegory, Colbert is a shadow on the wall undermining truthiness from within, yet both fail: audiences laugh, guests collect the campaign-donation 'Colbert Bump,' and nothing changes, making America the self-satisfied one who is ignorant of its ignorance. Through Nehamas's contrast of Socratic and Platonic irony and the Symposium's demand that the greatest work read as both tragedy and comedy, the chapter concludes Colbert may be America's Plato — condemning and laughing at us like a Sisyphean liberator who knows we will not leave the cave.

socratic-ignorance.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
socratic-ignorance.title: World of Warcraft and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: The editors' introduction, framed as an in-game quest log ('Read a Philosophy Book,' reward: +21 Intellect), argues that WoW is a profound cultural phenomenon that deserves philosophy because the world is virtual but the people, guilds, and Blizzard developers behind it are real. It models philosophizing on Socrates' claim that he knew he did not know, inviting readers to honestly examine the guiding principles they already rely on when playing and living. Chapters can be tackled in any order like a quest log, and the goal is a more open mind about gamer life rather than final answers.

socratic-ignorance.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
socratic-ignorance.title: Alone into the Desert
socratic-ignorance.relation: Audits Duniverse lives by Socrates's standard—the condition of the soul over wealth and power, with justice, courage, temperance, and wisdom—finding Baron Harkonnen utterly wanting, 'Leto the Just' compromised by forgery and concubinage, Paul unjust in his myth-making holy war (though Plato's Republic would smile on ruling myths), and the Fremen admirable in temperance and courage but fatally sure of themselves where Socrates prized knowing that you do not know. Aristotle's function argument and golden mean follow: Paul's first worm-ride is courage between rashness and cowardice, but Paul's and Leto II's extreme, humanity-saving selflessness has no excess to moderate and so breaks the doctrine of the mean. The author concludes Socrates is too harsh and Aristotle closer, yet even he fails: sometimes the best life requires extreme virtue and even injustice, as with the two Atreides emperors.

socratic-ignorance.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
socratic-ignorance.title: Know Thyself
socratic-ignorance.relation: George Reisch's introduction frames the volume with Martha Stout's claim that one in twenty-five people is a conscience-free sociopath who hides in plain sight, arguing that we viewers do the hiding work for them just as Deb, LaGuerta and Batista's assumptions shield Dexter. It presents Dexter's incessant inner questioning as the show's philosophical hook and previews the book's competing verdicts on Harry's Code: monster, Kantian-style model actor, utilitarian good, aesthete, or superhero. It ends by inverting Socrates: normally we point 'know thyself' inward, but the real epistemic danger is the sociopath next door, so our skepticism should aim at the guy in forensics - unless we are ourselves among the one-in-twenty-five, in which case Socrates' injunction to self-examination was spot on.

socratic-ignorance.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
socratic-ignorance.title: Secret Revealed . . . I Wonder
socratic-ignorance.relation: Robert Vuckovich reads 'The Secret Box' through Plato's Theaetetus — wonder as the birth of philosophy, with Patrick playing Socratic midwife to SpongeBob's desire to know — and Hobbes's diagnosis of curiosity as 'a lust of the mind' that obsesses and torments until satisfied. SpongeBob's masked break-in turns epistemic desire into what Cicero condemns as 'knavery that wears the mask of wisdom', nearly destroying the friendship, while the Charmides ideal of self-knowledge as temperance is exactly what he lacks. The episode ends like a Platonic dialogue in aporia: SpongeBob peeks but does not search, learns nothing, and Patrick still guards the secret.

socratic-ignorance.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
socratic-ignorance.title: Chapter 32 - “The Exit Door Leads In”
socratic-ignorance.relation: Eric Beck reads 'The Exit Door Leads In' as a modernized Platonic dialogue: like Oedipus before the Sphinx, the average salesman Bob Bibleman wins mandatory university admission by answering a computerized waiter's riddle, staging the Delphic 'Know Thyself' against Plato's Gorgias ideal of self-mastery, while Plato's Socrates in Charmides disclaims healthy self-knowledge. When Bibleman's terminal spills classified engine schematics, he decides not on universal principle but on what he thinks the authorities want; his honest answer that he would have handed them over anyway gets him expelled for failing a test he could not read, a double bind showing self-knowledge is contingent and situational. Dick thus revises knowing oneself as negotiation of the state's expectations rather than discovery of an essence, though the ending - Bibleman paying the computer after deciding not to - leaves open that he may one day rebel and need re-education.

socratic-ignorance.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
socratic-ignorance.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Vannatta explains why Seinfeld reruns now fall flat through Klosterman's neologism 'unironically': since about 1991 irony has become the invisible background of American comedy, a pervasive detachment that David Foster Wallace named and that Jedediah Purdy's For Common Things attacks as the gap between phenomenon and essence. Against Purdy's ironist (Seinfeld's Jerry, mastered by irony, believing in nothing but his own interests), the chapter sets Kierkegaard's Socrates, whose 'infinite absolute negativity' and confessing ignorance serve a truth he cannot define, and asks whether Klosterman, probing the gap between Bono's rehearsed car-ride persona and his inner self, is master of irony or mastered by it. The answer places Chuck midway between the two jailed ironists, Socrates and the Seinfeld finale: like Socrates he knows his own ignorance and serves the undefined idea of self-understanding, but only through pop-culture resemblance (KISS where Jerry used Superman), unable to master irony any more than he can bite his own teeth.

socratic-ignorance.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
socratic-ignorance.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Curko and Greguric read Klosterman's glam-rock fandom as a problem of identity and masks: Nietzsche's Apollonian-Dionysian split casts Chuck as a self-controlled Apollonian writing about Dionysian excess in Guns N' Roses, Motley Crue, and Whitesnake, while Descartes's remark that actors wear masks to hide their shame introduces the tribute band Paradise City, a 'real copy' whose members would have no personalities left if they fully succeeded. The authors extend the mask question to Facebook and online avatars, where media saturation makes us 'copies without the original' and identity stops being self-same. They end by crowning Klosterman a modern Socrates of 'Know thyself' and a Stoic exemplar: admire your heroes like Satriani but do not steal their identities, control what you can (never your reputation or your time of death), and keep daring the endless search for self-knowledge.

socratic-ignorance.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
socratic-ignorance.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Daniel Wanless reads Jeopardy! through the Meno: contestants can formulate the right question only because the answer is already given, just as Socrates answers Meno's paradox by claiming that all inquiry is recollection of truths the immortal soul already holds - latent knowledge that explains how Ken Jennings buzzes in before he consciously knows the response. A priori logical ability (the slave boy's doubled square, the law of non-contradiction applied to which of three cities is southernmost) guides the search for answers, while Final Jeopardy!'s blind wagering embodies Kierkegaard's 'life is only understood backwards, but it must be lived forwards.' Socrates would bet it all, Wanless concludes, because the unexamined life is not worth living: his whole life was preparation for the ultimate Final Jeopardy!, lived in the form of a question.

socratic-ignorance.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
socratic-ignorance.title: Futurama and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Mills-Knutsen reads the Brain Spawn - floating brains whose pain at others' thoughts drives them to dumb life down and finally to hoard all knowledge in the Infosphere ('The Day the Earth Stood Stupid,' 'The Why of Fry') - as Futurama's funhouse mirror of the West's distrust of intellectuals, from Pandora and Eve to Frankenstein and comic-book evil geniuses. Fry, the delta-brainwave-lacking hero made stupid by doing 'the nasty in the pasty,' stabs the Big Brain with Bonfire of the Vanities and later banishes the Brains to another dimension, just as Athens executed Socrates. A close reading of Plato's Apology - Socrates's feigned ignorance exposing everyone else's, his demand of free meals in lieu of exile, and his prophecy of even more annoying successors - maps onto the Big Brain's snobbery and onto universities (Wernstrom's tenure scam in 'A Big Piece of Garbage,' Amy's doctorate in 'That Darn Katz!') as society's way of paying intellectuals to stay out of the way.

socratic-ignorance.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
socratic-ignorance.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Christopher Lauer argues Cohen's lyrics seduce through Socratic irony as Kierkegaard analyzes it in The Concept of Irony: ostentatious self-concealment that makes hearers aware of the gap between words and intentions, building 'personality' and promising intimacy. Songs like 'Closing Time,' 'Everybody Knows,' and 'Democracy' oscillate between cynical third-person verdicts and sudden second-person address, offering a hidden sincerity only to withdraw it - an erotic improvement on Plato's Socrates that dissolves its own ironic distance. 'Hallelujah' and 'Anthem' make the program explicit, treating brokenness as the space in which love develops, while 'Tower of Song' shows the bleak side: irony collapsing into pure cynicism, the singer speaking sweetly from the Tower long after all promises of genuine intimacy have been disavowed.

socratic-ignorance.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
socratic-ignorance.title: 22. The Dao of Master Westley
socratic-ignorance.relation: Doll tests each character against the Dao: Confucius's identification of the Dao with tradition and ritual fails because Florinese tradition is exactly what enables Humperdinck's murder and war plans, so she turns to Laozi's De and wu-wei, diagnosing Vizzini's fatal overconfidence (he lacked Socratic knowledge of his own ignorance), Humperdinck's paranoia, and Buttercup's passivity as failures to sense when to act and when to refrain. Westley emerges as Zhuangzi's ideal - like Cook Ting the butcher, mastering skills until instinct suffices: adapting through the Fire Swamp, treating Vizzini's death as 'an appropriate death', yet sparing Inigo and Fezzik because killing them would be against nature, which is why the giant and the Spaniard accept him as their sage.

socratic-ignorance.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
socratic-ignorance.title: 8. Should Jane Get to Be Bored
socratic-ignorance.relation: Daniel Addison defends Louie's 'you don't get to be bored' admonishment of Jane in 'Country Drive' against Mathew Remski's charge that it transfers adult anxiety, pointing to Louis's Conan 'forever empty' monologue and reddit advice as proof that Louis insists on facing despair rather than fleeing it. The real aim, he argues, is Socratic: Louis wants Jane and the plane-complaining generation brought to aporia, the perplexity Plato's Socrates induces in the Meno's slave boy so that, no longer thinking he knows, he 'would be glad to find out.' Aristotle grounds the optimism - every human by nature desires to know, philosophy begins in wonder, and our deepest happiness lies in contemplating - so Louis's 'everything's amazing' tirade is a demand that we become philosophical rather than 'kinda satisfied' consumers. Boredom, on this reading, is failed wonder, and Louie is playing Socrates to his daughter.

socratic-ignorance.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
socratic-ignorance.title: 22. Unmasking the World and Its Heroes
socratic-ignorance.relation: Mapping both heroes onto Plato's cave, the chapter argues each must first see past shadows: Bruce abandons revenge on Joe Chill to change Gotham's whole idea of justice, its citizens climb out of apathy when the Dark Knight ferries refuse the Joker's detonators, and Clark needs Jonathan Kent ('It's not to score touchdowns') and Jor-El to learn what his powers are for. Socrates' Apology supplies the mask's rationale - the just man must lead a private life to survive, so secret identities protect loved ones from Luthor's kryptonite stabbing and FBI kidnapping - and Plato's warning that the returned cave-escapee would be killed explains why the heroes must lead by hope rather than force. The oracle story's lesson that wisdom is knowing that you know nothing grounds the close: anyone can be a hero, as Batman tells Gordon about the coat around a boy's shoulders.

socratic-ignorance.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
socratic-ignorance.title: 3. The Only Chapter in This Book You Need to Read!
socratic-ignorance.relation: Writing as two bickering versions of himself from different universes, Karavitis reads Deadpool Kills Deadpool as showing that the multiverse of Deadpools is the delusion of a single narcissist: the alternate 'Pools' are mirror-image projections of himself (Lacan's mirror stage), his self-love is Rousseau's pathological amour propre rather than healthy amour de soi, and his claim to be the progenitor of all reality is solipsism—hence there is no fourth wall. Freud, Fromm, and Marcuse supply rival diagnoses of that narcissism, from arrested development to proto-fascist willfulness to authentic rebellion against social control through unconscious conformity. A closing twist argues philosophers who claim sole access to truth are the same solipsistic narcissists, which would make Socrates, who never claimed a final answer, the only true philosopher.

socratic-ignorance.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
socratic-ignorance.title: 19. Deadpool Can’t Know Fear
socratic-ignorance.relation: Borrowing Socrates' definition of courage as remaining steadfast in the face of danger and choosing death above dishonor, the chapter argues that Deadpool's healing factor removes his risk of death, so he cannot experience the fear of helpless annihilation, cannot display courage, and is not an anti-hero but 'post-heroic.' Worse, mapping Luttwak's post-heroic warfare of drones and ballistic missiles onto his invulnerability, the chapter shows how fighting Deadpool drags opponents like the ULTIMATUM contract army and Crossbones into a trap where they can never test his courage and are stripped of their role as defenders, becoming mere targets. It closes that having a little fear and the chance to overcome it might be better than being unable to die.

socratic-ignorance.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
socratic-ignorance.title: 4. Scoundrels, the Lot of Us
socratic-ignorance.relation: Karavitis finds a Hegelian dialectic in the three-panel Dilbert strip (thesis, antithesis, synthesis) delivered through irony, then tests that irony against philosophy: Socrates' feigned-ignorance questioning that leaves interlocutors in aporia, Hegel's complaint that irony is vanity withdrawing from objective reality, and Kierkegaard's dissertation on the concept of irony plus Either/Or, where irony is the bridge from the aesthetic to the ethical life. The punchline is that after nearly three decades of Dilbert the white-collar workplace has not changed, so readers who feel superior to their bosses and co-workers have taken the vain, narcissistic, aesthetic reading Hegel warned against, making the joke a scoundrelly way of avoiding responsibility. A Leo Strauss aside casts Adams as an esoteric writer whose irony preserves him from the powerful.

socratic-ignorance.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
socratic-ignorance.title: 5. The Serious Point of Scott’s Humor
socratic-ignorance.relation: Guerra and Barkman argue that Dilbert's humor is doing serious philosophical work: strips like the Pointy-Haired Boss's scheme to strip app users of free will, rebranded by Dilbert as marketing, distill manipulative corporate practice to its absurd essential core, and humor serves as a logical tool that, when it preserves the target's integrity rather than straw-manning it, exposes the equivocation in earnest arguments about getting something from nothing. They ground the practice in Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where wittiness is the virtuous mean between the vices of buffoonery and boorishness, read Adams's catalogue of failures and his luck-first, passion-is-bullshit account of success as a Socratic acknowledgment of ignorance that deflates the American Dream, and treat Win Bigly's persuasion lessons (visuals, repetition, intentional mistakes, the Hitler counterexample) as further proof that Adams has the virtue of wit.

socratic-ignorance.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
socratic-ignorance.title: 6. No Wisdom to Offer You
socratic-ignorance.relation: Distinguishes public intellectuals like Chomsky, who deliver their own conclusions, from public philosophers who get audiences thinking for themselves, and argues Schumer is the latter. Her memoir claim that she has 'no wisdom to offer' is set beside the Socratic ignorance of Plato's Apology, where wisdom is worth nothing. Sketches like 'Football Town Nights', whose coach condemns rape only to praise violent domination, and 'The Trial of Bill Cosby' withhold conclusions and force viewers to work out for themselves the links between football and rape culture, or between un-conflicted entertainment and justice.

socratic-ignorance.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
socratic-ignorance.title: 9. A Rose by Any Other Brand
socratic-ignorance.relation: Callis treats Gilead's rise as a marketing campaign, reading it through Thom Braun's philosophy of branding built on Heraclitus (brands as false stability amid flux, the 'hidden connection' of the 'Balm in Gilead' hymn), Socratic questioning that Gilead forbids its citizens, Plato's brand-as-becoming, and Aristotle's four causes (the Sons of Jacob as efficient cause, the subjugation of women as the brand's function). She argues the brand was doomed because its core premise—that women exist to breed—is false, so Waterford's quip that love is 'lust with a good marketing campaign' foreshadows its Shakespearean collapse. The resistance works the other way: handmaids reclaiming their real names ('My name is June—and I will survive') is what breaks the brand.

socratic-ignorance.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
socratic-ignorance.title: 7. Rick and Morty as Socratic Television
socratic-ignorance.relation: The chapter argues Harmon and Roiland write the show as Socratic dialogue: in 'Mortynight Run' Morty's confident moral position (saving Fart from Krombopulos Michael is right) is dismantled until Morty himself pulls the trigger, leaving him in aporia; in 'Auto Erotic Assimilation' Summer's faith in freedom is razed by Unity's happy paternalist hive and the nipple-shaped race war it unleashes; and 'Look Who's Purging Now' refuses to choose between liberalism and conservatism when the post-purge town instantly re-founds the Festival. Like Socrates in Plato's Meno, the show's goal is not to teach lessons but to reduce viewers to confusion, because doing philosophy begins there.

socratic-ignorance.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
socratic-ignorance.title: 3. Wonder and Philosophy as a Way Home
socratic-ignorance.relation: Nathan and Leilani Mueller argue the theme song's 'neighborly day in this beautywood' makes beauty a transcendental leading to wisdom, as in Plato's Symposium ascent to loving the beautiful itself and Aquinas's convertibility of truth, goodness, and beauty. Reading Rogers's questioning of batteries and boxes (episode 1655) through the Meno's genuine curiosity and Pierre Hadot's account of philosophy as a way of life, they tour the show's three philosophical spaces: the domestic living room, the community visit (blind saxophonist Eric Kloss), and Make-Believe as thought experiment.

socratic-ignorance.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
socratic-ignorance.title: 4. The Gently Socratic Inquiry of Fred Rogers
socratic-ignorance.relation: Ben Lukey and Steve Bein, veterans of p4c Hawai'i, argue Rogers ran a 'gently Socratic' community of inquiry on television: unlike Socrates the public gadfly who made asses of interlocutors, Rogers created intellectual safety, treating Daniel Striped Tiger's 'What does assassination mean?' (after MLK's murder) and the Officer Clemmons kiddie-pool scene as philosophy with children. Using Dr. Tom Jackson's Good Thinker's Toolkit to show children are philosophers, they defend 'little p philosophy' as activity over 'Big P Philosophy' as content, casting Rogers and Socrates as midwives rather than lecturers.

socratic-ignorance.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
socratic-ignorance.title: 21. You Gotta Be Bad if You Wanna Be Good
socratic-ignorance.relation: Shearer argues the show dismantles ethical dualism, the good/evil binary that sorts people wholly into the Good Place or the Bad Place and that underwrites real-world 'us versus them' thinking. Following Aristotle, being good is a learnable skill like reading or an instrument, acquired by practice and unlearning, not a fixed nature. Following Socrates in the Apology, progress begins with admitting you do not know, and the chapter shows that the characters who self-generate that admission, Eleanor confessing and Michael realizing he loves the humans, grow the most, while Jason's moral neutrality exposes a case the Good Place/Bad Place binary cannot classify at all.

socratic-ignorance.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
socratic-ignorance.title: 30. Socratic Superheroism
socratic-ignorance.relation: Stages a dialogue between Socrates and Nebula to build a four-part scorecard of 'Socratic Heroism' — question all assumptions, intellectual humility (Socrates before the Delphic oracle: 'I am very conscious that I am not wise at all'), improve society without ever doing injustice, and courage unto death (the gadfly of the Apology) — then scores Thanos 0 for 4: 'I am incapable of error' and 'reality can be whatever I want' are the very opposites of humility and of objective, heavenly truth. It nominates Doctor Strange as the MCU's Socratic hero, whose humbling at Kamar-Taj, willingness to hand over the Time Stone against the obvious choice, and trust in the one winning future among 14,000,605 pass the tests.

socratic-ignorance.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
socratic-ignorance.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Barad maps fifth-century Athens onto contemporary America to cast Stewart as a Socratic reformer confronting modern sophists, advertisers, pundits and media figures who make weaker arguments appear stronger without caring about truth, exemplified by Ed Helms admitting network stories are pre-written from 'conventional wisdom' and Ann Coulter's conformity-peddling. She details the shared method: flattering the 'expert', feigned ignorance, and layer-by-layer questioning that traps targets like Rumsfeld ('It may not seem like much, but for this administration it's a huge policy shift') in contradiction, with Socratic irony doing the work of Stewart's awestruck deadpan and mute astonished reactions to Bush clips. Against Bill O'Reilly's 'stoned slacker' charge she cites the Annenberg finding that the show's young audience is better informed, and weighs Ken Tucker's 'monkey' question through the Crossfire 'I'm not going to be your monkey' exchange, concluding that, like Socrates facing trial and execution, Stewart uses irony as means and truth as end.

socratic-ignorance.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
socratic-ignorance.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Decker asks whether the 'Stephen Colbert' persona is the ironist of the Romantics and Rorty: the precise inverse of Socrates, who was declared wisest by the Delphic oracle precisely because he knew he knew nothing. Through Schlegel's Romantic irony, Hegel's complaint that the ironist abdicates responsibility, Kierkegaard's reading of Socrates as standing ironically above every relationship, and Rorty's ironist with her radically doubtable 'final vocabulary', he reads Colbert's self-redescription, Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear, and Super PAC stunt as exposing the contingency of political selves. Yet truthiness at its worst is dangerous subjectivism, and the chapter ends with Colbert breaking persona before Congress ('I like talking about people who have no power') as the non-ironic face that keeps the irony honest.

socratic-ignorance.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
socratic-ignorance.title: The Sorcerer Socratic
socratic-ignorance.relation: Timm argues Strange follows Socrates' path from arrogance to Socratic heroism: the hand injury forces intellectual humility (the Oracle-at-Delphi moment), the Ancient One's keyhole metaphor and astral-form lesson ('to show you just how much you don't know') enact the Socratic method of questioning the supposedly wise, and the astral projection is literally the examined life — Socrates' unexamined life not worth living. Strange's commitment to protecting humanity from interdimensional evil parallels the gadfly who risks death to improve Athens, his refusal to do injustice even under pressure echoes the Crito, and his repeated willingness to die for others (facing Dormammu, holding the Shambler back) completes the Socratic Hero profile.

socratic-ignorance.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
socratic-ignorance.title: We Can All Be Socratics Supreme
socratic-ignorance.relation: Pape uses the Ancient One's keyhole metaphor to argue that all knowledge is partial and biased: Bacon's confident scientific method ('human knowledge and human power meet in one') is itself just a useful belief, while Socratic awareness of one's ignorance — knowing that you have blind spots, even if you cannot see them — is the real wisdom. She reads the film's running gags as bias lessons (the 'Mister Doctor' exchange, Strange mistaking the wifi password 'Shamballa' for a mantra, the noble-savage prejudice) and feminist critiques of impartiality as itself partial.
