The whitewashing controversy around Tilda Swinton's Ancient One — weighed against the Fu Manchu stereotype of the 1963 comics and Iron Man 3's Mandarin-as-Trevor-Slattery subversion — shows how filmmakers can confront the biases they cannot simply remove.

socratic-ignorance.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
socratic-ignorance.title: Knock and the Door Will Be Opened… Eventually
socratic-ignorance.relation: The chapter reads Strange pounding on Kamar-Taj's door as Kierkegaard's passionate collision with 'that which thought cannot think': the materialist surgeon hits the unknown as a frontier, takes offense at the Ancient One's talk of healing through belief, and can only proceed by surrendering intellectual control ('I control it by surrendering control?'). It applies Kierkegaard's two teachers from Philosophical Fragments: Pangborn is healed the Socratic way, recollecting a power already within him, while the Ancient One's astral knock-out and eviction of Strange acts like the god as teacher, forcing him to discover that he is untruth, until faith becomes 'controlling magic by surrendering to it.'

socratic-ignorance.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
socratic-ignorance.title: Alone into the Desert
socratic-ignorance.relation: Has Socrates and Aristotle rate the good life in the Duniverse: the Baron fails every Socratic virtue (breaking his promise to Yueh, intemperance, betrayal), Duke Leto is 'Leto the Just' yet forges certificates and plans adultery, Paul's theocratic myth-making is unjust despite his temperance and courage, and the Fremen are brave and temperate but fatally unquestioning, lacking the Socratic awareness of ignorance that would have saved them from manipulation. Aristotle's function argument, his doctrine of the mean (Paul's worm-riding as courage between rashness and cowardice), and his external goods are then applied, but the author finally breaks with both philosophers: Paul's and Leto II's extreme selflessness admits no mean, their unjust oppression can still be right, and such extreme self-sacrifice may be the best life of all.

socratic-ignorance.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
socratic-ignorance.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.relation: Abraham Schwab turns Ygritte's 'You know nothing, Jon Snow' into a theory of epistemic humility: Jon misreads wildling courtship norms, Sam's dragonglass shatters on wight Small Paul, Lord Mormont assumes Mance fights like a southern king and pays for it at the Fist of First Men, while Arya's accurate self-knowledge keeps her alive. Formalizing with justified true belief - Sam's lucky dagger thrust is not knowledge, and the Watch's warranted belief that the dead Othor was harmless justifies falsity - he uses Lysa's letter, which sent Ned to King's Landing on a lie, to ask what justification is: Descartes's absolute certainty is too strict, reliabilism vindicates testimony ('dark wings, dark words'), so that only Sansa need witness Ned's beheading for the Starks to know it, and between Melisandre's circular dogma about Azor Ahai and total skepticism, moderate skepticism best governs belief - a humility the south lacked about the Horn of Winter.

socratic-ignorance.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
socratic-ignorance.title: 21. You Gotta Be Bad if You Wanna Be Good
socratic-ignorance.relation: Argues that no one can improve without first admitting they are bad: the rigid Good Place/Bad Place binary is ethical dualism whose cracks show in Mindy St. Claire's Medium Place and Jason, a naive moral neutral who fits neither side. Socrates' Apology supplies the method — wisdom is knowing what you do not know, so self-aware fault-finding precedes growth — while Aristotle's account of virtue as learned by practice, like an instrument, grounds the claim that goodness can be acquired even in the afterlife, though unlearning old habits is harder. Eleanor's trash storm, Tahani's failed party, and Chidi's theory-practice gap mark each character's admissions of error, and the worst offenders, Eleanor and Michael, improve most because they confess unprompted.

socratic-ignorance.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
socratic-ignorance.title: Harry’s Cloak, the Ring of Gyges, and the Temptations of Power
socratic-ignorance.relation: The chapter reads Tom Riddle as Plato's unfit ruler: from the orphanage ('I can make them hurt if I want to') he violates Kant's dictum never to use persons merely as means, treating even his 'friends' as followers, killing Lily despite Snape's devotion, and splitting his soul for Horcruxes. Dumbledore, offered the Ministry repeatedly yet refusing because 'power was my weakness and my temptation,' has the Socratic self-knowledge that he cannot be trusted with power, and that self-awareness, not flawless virtue, is what keeps him from Grindelwald's and Voldemort's path and makes him the series' nearest philosopher-ruler.

socratic-ignorance.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
socratic-ignorance.title: NOTES
socratic-ignorance.relation: Reads the show's eclipse icon against Plato's sun of the good — goodness has become hard to discern — and tests four theories of evil on the characters: Socrates' claim that no one errs knowingly is half-confirmed since villains like Angela and Nathan always take themselves to be doing right; Aristotle's akrasia and vice as an excess or deficiency of disposition fit Sylar's blood-scrawled 'Forgive me' apartment and his uncontrolled hunger; and Nietzsche's Übermensch and pre-Christian master morality raise the uncomfortable question of why Sylar preying on inferiors is not heroic like Achilles. The chapter's endorsed answer is Gilligan's ethics of care: the heroes are good because they care — Matt for Molly and Daphne, Bennet for Claire — while evil is the absence of care, though Bennet's authoritarian, family-only care shows that care itself must be both widened and restrained.

socratic-ignorance.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
socratic-ignorance.title: a2.xhtml
socratic-ignorance.relation: Bassham reads The Hobbit as a story of moral growth: the comfort-loving Bilbo who trembles like jelly at the dwarves' plans grows into the hobbit who volunteers to carry the Ring to Mordor. Growth in wisdom comes from Socratic self-examination (learning how little one knows) and from broadened experience of the wide world; growth in virtue comes either from sudden conversion (Thorin's Scrooge-like deathbed repentance) or, as Aristotle taught, from slow habituation - Bilbo's repeated courageous and generous acts (sparing Gollum, returning the elf-keys, giving up the Arkenstone) build lasting character. Seneca's view that hardship strengthens supplies the framework for why Bilbo's trials on the road ennobled rather than broke him.

socratic-ignorance.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
socratic-ignorance.title: Notes
socratic-ignorance.relation: Argues that Underwood's fourth-wall asides are the show's device for dramatizing the Platonic being-versus-seeming distinction: his public performances (reassuring Blythe over the leaked education bill, the confessional letter typed on the Underwood typewriter to destroy Walker, goading the President into appointing a special prosecutor) are contradicted point by point by what he tells the camera. The chapter reads Frank as a Ring of Gyges success story — the show so far teaches it is better to be the bad guy who seems good — while Socrates' examined life from the Apology and Crito shows Frank never asks why he wants power, and his cockiness is the opposite of Socratic ignorance. It closes with the Gorgias' contrast of Sophistic rhetoric (producing belief, not knowledge) and Machiavelli's advice to feign, casting Frank as the manipulator of opinion Socrates called a tyrant's politics.

socratic-ignorance.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
socratic-ignorance.title: Notes
socratic-ignorance.relation: Gray argues Frank's fourth-wall asides dramatize Plato's being-versus-seeming distinction: the camera confidences reveal the true motive behind the public performance, as in the Blythe education-bill martyrdom gambit, the deliberately failed persuasion of Walker over the special prosecutor, and the seduction letter typed on the Underwood typewriter. The chapter reads Frank as winning the Ring of Gyges bet — enjoying adultery, corruption, and murder while seeming good — exactly the outcome the Republic sets out to refute. Against this it sets Socrates' examined life and Apology profession of ignorance: Frank pursues power without asking to what end, and his mastery of rhetoric over knowledge makes him the Sophist of the Gorgias rather than Plato's true politician, with Machiavelli's dissembling prince as his model.

socratic-ignorance.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
socratic-ignorance.title: If Not on the Island of Ethical Subjectivism, Then Where
socratic-ignorance.relation: George Wrisley uses Lost as a testing ground against ethical subjectivism and cultural relativism: the disagreement over Sayid shooting young Ben (monster or innocent child?) motivates relativism, but the Argument from Disagreement fails for the same reason Locke and Mr. Eko's button dispute does not change what will actually happen if it goes unpushed. Simple subjectivism makes every judge infallible (the Man in Black could declare his murders right) and dissolves genuine disagreement between Jacob and his brother over killing their 'mother,' while cultural relativism makes the Dharma Initiative's torture of Sayid 'right' and would have ruled Martin Luther King Jr. wrong. He concludes that Lost's ambiguous cases - Michael's murder of Ana Lucia and Libby, Ben killing Jacob, Jack extorting Ben on the operating table - invite viewers to seek objective grounds Socratically, questioning their own moral judgments with further 'why's.

socratic-ignorance.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
socratic-ignorance.title: And Now, Deep Thoughts…
socratic-ignorance.relation: Reynolds places comedy on a spectrum from philosophy to satire to smart-assery and argues SNL mostly sits at the silly end: Gumby, Mr. Robinson, Hermione's cleavage, and Hobbit Office are parody with an absurd twist but no constructive target, unlike genuine satire such as Mr. Bill. He develops the comparison through Aristophanes' Clouds, whose caricature of Socrates at the Thinkery helped send him to his death, and through the 'Playboy Philosophy' sketch with Belushi as Socrates. Socrates himself emerges as a satirist: the oracle of Delphi, his claim to know only that he knows nothing, and his elenchus that unmasks the supposedly wise are read as comedy in the service of seriousness, before the chapter concedes SNL's absurdism is philosophical mainly in mocking an absurd world.

socratic-ignorance.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
socratic-ignorance.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
socratic-ignorance.relation: Kirby reads the 'Imaginationland' trilogy as a satire of post-9/11 America interpreted through Ulrich Beck's world risk society: the Pentagon generals, still thinking in Cold War categories like 'Project X' and Chinese imagination portals, embody Beck's denial response and end up voting to nuke Imaginationland, while Cartman's Rambo-style self-interest embodies the apathetic response. Socrates' practice of demanding definitions frames the chapter's question of what terrorism actually is (via Hoffman's five criteria), and Socratic ignorance about what one does not know is contrasted with the worse condition of not being able to know what you do not know. Kyle's courtroom speech that imaginary beings like Luke Skywalker and Santa are 'realer' than most real people, and Butters' creative power to imagine Santa back to life, point to Beck's cosmopolitan 'transformation': imagination and cross-border cooperation as the way out of risk panic.

socratic-ignorance.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
socratic-ignorance.title: 22. Unmasking the World and Its Heroes
socratic-ignorance.relation: Claims the Superman-vs-Batman debate misses the point: both heroes are cave-escapers who must first see beyond appearances—Bruce renouncing vengeance on Joe Chill and then shaking Gotham from apathy (the ferries refusing the Joker's detonators), Clark learning from Jonathan and Jor-El that his powers are not for touchdowns but to lead humanity out by example. Masks serve the Socratic warning of the Apology that the just man must act privately to survive—Jonathan Kent dies keeping Clark's secret—yet risk becoming their own trap, from Smallville's Red Kryptonite ring to Batman's sonar surveillance that Lucius Fox calls too much power for one person. The chapter closes on Socratic ignorance and Man of Steel's genesis chambers: a hero, like Socrates, knows his wisdom is worth nothing, and anyone who chooses can be one.

socratic-ignorance.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
socratic-ignorance.title: I Knew Everything When I Was Young: Examining the Wisdom of Youth
socratic-ignorance.relation: Weighs Betty's 'I knew everything when I was young' against James's 'I don't know anything' using Aristotle's theoretical versus practical wisdom and Nozick's criteria, finding Betty wise: she knows what matters ('To kiss in cars and downtown bars'), the means ('Chase two girls lose the one'), the long view, and how to handle the dilemma of forgiving James. Plato's Meno recollection doctrine and 'seven' ('Before I learned civility I used to scream ferociously') support the claim that the young can possess moral clarity adults lose. James's apology shows wisdom in action (Kekes) and Socratic intellectual humility, while 'tolerate it', 'Dear John', and All Too Well's dinner-party scene illustrate Spear on gaslighting via presumed epistemic superiority of older men.

socratic-ignorance.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
socratic-ignorance.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
socratic-ignorance.relation: Gilmore reads Unforgiven as Socratic wisdom done in images — the recognition that we do not know what we really want. He analyzes the opening montage (shadowed windows, the cut prostitute) as Freud's Primal Scene, the audience forced to interpret sex and violence without adequate concepts, which he calls the primal scene of philosophy itself. Drawing on Huizinga's Homo Ludens and Leone's Once Upon a Time in the West, he frames the gunslinger as a 'Bad Man at play' for mortal stakes, free of the repressions civilization demands. William Munny's banal Christianized 'goodness' versus the terrifying Bad Man that drink releases dramatizes Thoreau's 'quiet desperation' and a godless world where deserving is irrelevant.

socratic-ignorance.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
socratic-ignorance.title: 5. To Resist Despair
socratic-ignorance.relation: Peterson defines being punk through three interlocking virtues - authenticity (via Varga and Guignon's account as used by Heidegger, Beauvoir, and Sartre), Sartrean freedom ('existence precedes essence'), and questioning authority, defended with Robert Paul Wolff's argument that obeying authority cancels autonomy. The Slits' Palmolive, Alice Bag, Johnny Ramone's cheap Mosrite, and Harley Flanagan show DIY as the punk response to Sartrean facticity, Operation Ivy's 'Knowledge' recalls Socratic ignorance as punk humility, and she concludes that even SLC Punk's Stevo going to Harvard can remain punk, since only striving to live authentically counts.

socratic-ignorance.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
socratic-ignorance.title: The Last Supper Game
socratic-ignorance.relation: This editor's introduction frames Bourdain as a modern philosopher by playing a variation on his 'Last Meal' game and choosing Bourdain as the ideal dinner companion. It argues that Bourdain's professed humility about how little he knows ('realizing how small I am, and unwise') echoes Socratic ignorance and the love of wisdom, and previews the volume's questions about happiness, authenticity, taste, and freedom.

socratic-ignorance.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
socratic-ignorance.title: Chapter 11 Socratic Irony in Twain’s Skeptical Religious Jeremiads
socratic-ignorance.relation: Jacquette demands a precise definition of Twain's much-invoked irony, adopting Vlastos's/Quintilian's formula that irony says the contrary of what is meant while letting the real meaning be recovered. He classifies Twain's irony as local vs. global and comic vs. sober (tragic/historical): 'Personal Recollections of Joan of Arc' is globally ironic (falsely presented as de Conte's eyewitness manuscript), while the relic-mocking passages of 'The Innocents Abroad' (St. Luke's Madonna, kegs of true-cross nails, three skulls of John the Baptist) are local comic irony. Jacquette concludes Twain's irony is distinctively Socratic: like Socrates interpreting the Delphic oracle, Twain makes a moral and epistemic virtue of ridiculing experts who claim to know what no one can know about God, sin, and the afterlife.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: George and Virtue—Like Oil and Water
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Daniel Barwick runs George through Aristotle's function argument and finds him wanting: a paradigm of 'the many' who thinks happiness is fortune and momentary victories over others (free parking, perfect airport pickups) rather than activity of the soul in accordance with virtue. His 'do the opposite' epiphany in 'The Opposite' embraces the more extreme vice rather than steering toward the rationally chosen mean, and his self-hatred, laziness, and pleasure-seeking fail all three of Aristotle's tips for hitting the mean. Since George will never practice virtuous action until it becomes habit, Barwick concludes George is doomed to his miserable existence - which is, conveniently for us, why he is funny.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Elaine, Kramer, and Newman Not Wise
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Aeon Skoble argues Seinfeld explicates Aristotelian virtue ethics against utilitarian and Kantian rivals: Jerry's 'I don't want to be an orgy guy' and George's fear of becoming 'one of those guys' ask what sort of person to be, not which rule to follow. George's 'do the opposite' in 'The Opposite' is an update of the Delphic oracle - only he who recognizes his own idiocy (Socratic ignorance) can act well, with Jerry deducing the logic and serving as his phronemos, alongside Superman. Elaine's rule-worship and Jujyfruits utilitarianism backfire, Kramer lacks the social dialectic virtue needs, and the ironic appeals to Newman as arbiter expose the paradox that choosing a role model wisely already requires the wisdom one lacks.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 1 - Homer and Aristotle
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Raja Halwani evaluates Homer against Aristotle's four character types (virtuous, continent, incontinent, vicious), arguing Homer is not virtuous and is genuinely vicious in the domain of food and drink (eating Frank Grimes's marked sandwich, the 64 slices of American cheese), while shuttling between continence and incontinence elsewhere. He catalogues Homer's lack of practical wisdom (phronesis) through gaffes like inferring the Bear Patrol works because there are no bears, and his lack of genuine friendship since he has only drinking buddies. Homer is judged neither malicious nor wholly vicious, so we pity him for his Springfield upbringing and the Simpson gene, and the chapter closes by crediting his 'in-your-face humanity'—his unregulated 'love of life'—as an admirable but dangerous ethical trait that does not make him an admirable person.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 4 - Marge’s Moral Motivation
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Gerald Erion and Joseph Zeccardi present Marge as an everyday Aristotelian whose bravery (The Springfield Connection, escaping the Movementarian commune), temperance, and generosity each hit the mean between Springfield's vicious extremes, and whose eudaimonia is achieved through the good of her family. They contrast her reason-driven conscience with Ned Flanders's divine command theory—consulting Reverend Lovejoy over whether to play capture-the-flag on the sabbath—and side with Marge, invoking Plato's Euthyphro to argue that morality cannot simply be a function of God's commands. Marge emerges as a 'Christian-flavored Aristotelian' who cultivates virtue by habituation and models it for Lisa and Bart.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Aeon Skoble uses Tolkien's characters to defend Aristotelian virtue ethics against Kantian and utilitarian rivals. Sam's loyalty is a virtue because critically directed at a worthy friend while Wormtongue's loyalty to Saruman is not; Sméagol's instant murder of Déagol reveals prior vice that let the Ring corrupt him quickly, whereas Bilbo resists it for sixty years; Aragorn's temperance and teachableness contrast Boromir's resentment and pride. Working through Aristotle's doctrine of the mean (courage between cowardice and rashness), practical wisdom, and the phronemos as role model, he argues that rule-following cannot capture moral perception (do we owe truth to Black Riders?) and that utilitarianism absurdly requires Galadriel's foresight.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Kant, Aristotle, and the Cheater
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Answering Cal Ripken's Socratic question 'What is cheating?' (raised by Sammy Sosa's corked bat and Gaylord Perry's spitball), Randolph Feezell stages a dialogue between Abbey's Kantian absolutism, Trev's traditionalism, and Ron's win-at-all-costs realism. Kant's categorical imperative grounds the absolutist: intending to break a rule to gain an edge is making yourself an arbitrary exception to rules that bind all players equally. Aristotle's virtue ethics then lets the traditionalist say that some strategic rule-breaking belongs to a sport's 'prescriptive atmosphere' (stealing signs, the balk pickoff, catching framing), since honesty and courage are means between excess and defect guided by judgment rather than exceptionless rules, while corking a bat stays cheating because it defies the tradition and hides from umpires.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Why Not to Buy the Porsche
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Skoble uses Manhattan's confrontation scene — Isaac telling Yale 'you're too easy on yourself... you'd rather buy the Porsche' over the hominid skeleton — to build an account of integrity as fidelity to correct moral principles, requiring an integrated character in which reason and desire agree. He distinguishes integrity from mere consistency (the 'consistent Nazi') and from stubbornness, and models it on Plato's just person who 'harmonizes the three parts of himself'. Aristotle's account of habituation defends Isaac's slippery slope: Yale's repeated lies for expediency are forming the kind of character who would inform on friends, so integrity is an objective yardstick of a well-lived life, as Isaac's amends to Tracy at the end confirms.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Just What They Say It for I Never Knew”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: South argues Allen's signature old recordings from the American songbook are a philosophical device grounded in Aristotle: the Rhetoric's view that emotions carry cognitive orientations that reshape judgment, and the Politics' claim that music forms character, explain why songs comment on the plots they score. He reads Hannah and Her Sisters through 'You Made Me Love You', 'Bewitched, Bothered and Bewildered', and 'I'm in Love Again' — scoring Elliot's inconstancy, Mickey's 'You don't deserve Cole Porter' judgment of Holly, and her growth into someone whose new musical taste signals ethical maturity — and Everyone Says I Love You as a darker cycle where fantasy and finitude ('It's Later Than You Think') drive the compulsion to love again. The happy ending is precisely why Allen called the film a 'cop out': its music says love fades and is out of our control, while the plot pretends otherwise.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: NOTES
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Argues Snape's redemption is gradual virtue-building rather than instant transformation, since vice and virtue are habits built up over time and his resentments persist even as his actions serve the good. His doe Patronus, matching Lily's, manifests Aristotle's beloved as a second self, his remorse, an emotion he shares with Harry but Voldemort cannot feel, begins to knit his damaged soul whole, and Harry's forgiveness, naming his son Albus Severus for 'the bravest man I ever knew', completes the arc love began.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jonathan Sanford distinguishes necessity of the end, of compulsion, and of nature to argue Christ's passion was both necessary and free: justice requires reparation for the harmony Adam and Eve broke, God cannot simply waive it without making a mockery of sin, yet no compulsion operates on Christ — unlike the blind inner drives Nietzsche's will to power or Schopenhauer's will would represent. Using Aristotle, he argues Christ's fully virtuous character (practical wisdom plus courage and temperance become a 'second nature') makes disobedience nearly unimaginable, and his divinity makes it impossible, so his choice 'could not have been different' precisely because it was perfectly free; the Gethsemane agony shows not division in the God-man but the difficulty of holding his human and divine wills in unity.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Superheroes and the Ring of Gyges
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter's heart: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges and 'harsh view' of human nature — justice as the weak's compact against the strong, a lineage running from Hobbes to Nietzsche — are powerfully denied by superheroes and by Frodo, who resist the power of the ring. Socrates' tripartite soul and justice-as-psychic-harmony are read as preparation for the Republic's real answer, the ascent to the eternal Form of the Good, which the chapter extends through Aristotle's teleology and virtue ethics: super-powered people, denied any standard social role, must wrestle with what their potential is for — from Kingdom Come's retired Superman and Spider-Man 2's Peter Parker to Astro City's Samaritan, with Uncle Ben's 'With great power comes great responsibility' as the upshot.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Reasons to Be Moral
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Extracts two candidate answers from Spider-Man — Reason One, that immorality rebounds on you (Uncle Ben's death), tested and weakened by the Ms. Poore poverty-theft case, and Spider-Man's agonized "Because it is right" to the Green Goblin, the Kant-and-Bradley motive of duty — and finds both insufficient to show morality is rational. It then tests Plato's answer that only the moral have harmony of soul (reason governing appetite and spirit) against Flash Thompson and self-forgiving sinners, and Aristotle's "virtue is its own reward" against the thought experiment of virtuous Arachnid-Girl rotting in prison while the fraudulent Norm Osborne flourishes.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Switching Identities
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Maps Superman and Batman onto Plato and Aristotle — the otherworldly philosopher of the heavenly Good versus the this-worldly master of logic and applicable science — then argues that Bruce Wayne's years of intentional self-transformation may have swapped the mask, making Batman the core identity and Bruce the disguise. With Mark Waid, he sees Superman inwardly embracing his alien otherness as the path of authenticity, both cases yielding a fused "heterosis" of identities; Aristotle, Pascal and William James back the closing lesson that who we are is a matter of what we repeatedly do, so every mask may eventually become the face.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Bill Davis argues that Narnia works as a classical moral-education environment: against Experiment House's science-worship, Narnia supplies the three ingredients Aristotle and Aquinas require, namely instruction, virtuous exemplars to imitate (Reepicheep's courage, Puddleglum's temperance), and habituation through repeated right action, which together transform Peter's indecision, Edmund's treachery, Lucy's envy, and Jill's timidity. What finally lasts beyond Narnia, he contends, is a transforming encounter with Aslan: Eustace's dragon skin torn off by the Lion, Jill's drink at the stream where 'there is no other stream,' and Digory's tearful confession. He closes by arguing today's self-esteem-based character education cannot replicate this, since it pursues virtue from love of self rather than love of the good.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Poker and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Young reads David Sklansky's fundamental theorem of poker — play as if you could see all the cards — through Aristotle and Husserl. Aristotle's phronesis and virtue-as-habituation explain how excellent players come to perceive the particulars (pot odds, opponent tendencies, the best possible hand) and stay unharmed even when losing with the best play, while Husserl's Cartesian Meditations, translated hand-by-hand into poker terms, supply analogical appresentation for knowing the other minds seated across the table. Chris Moneymaker's 2003 'Bluff of the Century' all-in with nothing against Sammy Farha shows how bluffing randomizes play and lets you shape the truth you seek, until a slow-played quad aces ends the night in Socratic humility about the limits of knowledge.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: U2 and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Werther answers Tollefsen with Aristotle's Politics: musical images of character effect real 'change[s] of soul', so a three-premise argument concludes that repeated exposure to U2's images of fine character and good action can habituate delight in virtue - King's courage in 'Pride (In the Name of Love)' (whatever the botched time of day, and as proved when Adam Clayton stepped between Bono and an FBI-confirmed death threat), the indignation and shame at global poverty in 'Crumbs from Your Table', and the compassion of 'Miracle Drug' for the locked-in writer Christopher Nolan. 'Exit' purges the band's demons and 'Until the End of the World' offers purification through holy fear, matching the medical and religious readings of Aristotelian catharsis. C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man closes the case: without the aid of trained emotions the intellect is powerless, so a culture raised on U2's feelings may be better prepared to act well than one raised on syllogisms alone.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Hey, Let’s Get the Stuff We Need!” Putting the Mall in Its Place
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Matthew Walker reads Dawn of the Dead through Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics and Politics: the survivors' mall orgy curdles into boredom ('What have we done to ourselves?'), illustrating pleonexia, the graspingness for more than one's share of the goods of fortune that Aristotle roots in an unlimited desire for mere living - which may even explain why Romero's dead return, grasping from beyond the grave for more un-death. Aristotle's dismissal of the life of enjoyment as fit for cattle, his account of eudaimonia as the life in which our rational capacities flourish, and his defense of acquisition bounded by the good life explain why unlimited consumption zombifies the living, and why Peter and Fran must finally leave the mall empty-handed.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: James Bond and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Taliaferro and Le Gall rebut Paul Johnson's 1958 charge that Doctor No combines 'the sadism of a schoolboy bully', adolescent sex longings, and suburban snobbery. They show Bond kills for justice rather than spite (his reluctant assignment against von Hammerstein in 'For Your Eyes Only'), that Colonel Sun repudiates de Sadean torture before dying, and that the disturbing 'semi-rape' passage of The Spy Who Loved Me reflects Vivienne Michel's voice, not Bond's conduct. They read Bond's eros as an ironic use of the medieval courtly-love and Mariology tradition in which sex redeems 'lost women' like Pussy Galore, defend his dress and manners through the ancient heroic tradition (Theseus's fatal neglect of the white sails, Leonidas combing his beard at Thermopylae), and conclude Bond is a chivalric, comic hero - a 'delightful impossibility' in Aristotle's Poetics' sense who embodies Socratic soldierly virtue and Platonic optimism.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Lessons Learned
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: McAleer maps The Office onto Aristotle's ethics: David Brent is the buffoon who is 'the slave of his sense of humor,' Gareth the literalist boor who cannot take a joke, and Tim the ready wit whose irony responds to the situation — together illustrating that a virtue is a qualitative mean of acting and feeling appropriately, fixed by practical wisdom rather than rules. That humor cannot be codified mirrors the uncodifiability of Aristotelian ethics, and wit's very status as a virtue shows Aristotle's morality is broader than modern duty-and-outcome ethics: it aims at the flourishing (eudaimonia) of the whole person.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Questioning Everything The Birds
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The Deavels argue that Hitchcock's suspense is fundamentally epistemological. In the social world, heroines in love - Constance in Spellbound, Lina in Suspicion, Rose in The Wrong Man - must weigh mounting evidence of their beloveds' guilt against the Aristotelian premise that character is consistent because virtue and vice are habits: Constance rightly bets that J.B.'s gentleness with her proves he is no murderer, Lina reasonably concludes Johnnie may poison her, and Rose survives only by inventing a persecutory 'they'. With The Birds the question widens to nature itself: Mrs. Bundy's ornithology assumes past bird behavior predicts future behavior, and the film's terror is Hume's worry that causal order may be an unfounded projection, leaving Mitch to stake his family's escape on the humble observed pattern that attacks come in waves.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Just Like Mary Shelley, Just Like Frankenstein”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Chuck Ward uses 'Mama Tried' (the meek family's rebel son doing life without parole) and the mysterious birthmark in 'Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleloo' to ask whether character is fixed from birth, setting the songs' fatalism against Aristotle's account of character as habituated choice and Plato's claim that traits tend to be inherited. He surveys behavioral genetics, twin studies, The Bell Curve, and the supposed 'criminality gene' before arguing that genetic determinism is a mistaken reductionism: like the groovy atmosphere of a Dead show, which shapes the very individuals who produce it, complex systems admit top-down causation, so genes never act alone. The chapter's payoff is that the songs' studied ambiguity — mama tried, yet 'that leaves no one but me to blame' — shows art expressing, rather than resolving, the tension between free will and determinism.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Unchained” The Inspired Anger of a Religious Man
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dan Haggerty uses Aristotle's account of anger as a virtuous mean—felt at the right people, time, and degree—to show that songs like 'San Quentin,' 'The Man in Black,' and 'Oney' express justified anger at real injustices done to prisoners and workingmen, contra pop psychology's blanket rejection of anger. He then coins 'inspired anger' (drawing on Plato's Ion: the artist possessed and blown away by emotion): a painful, hopeless desire for a justice or restoration that can never be, exemplified by Cash's 'Hurt' video and its regret over irrecoverable time—mourning rather than self-pity or depression. The chapter closes with 'Unchained' as a prayer showing how a Christian like Cash can live with this futile desire rather than argue it away.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Redemption
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Stephen Bilynskyj tests John Hick's soul-making theodicy—that God allows suffering because virtues like courage, temperance, and compassion need pain to form—against Cash's life and songs. Using Aristotle on habituation by pleasure and pain (Cash's first amphetamine euphoria and the ostrich-attack painkillers as missed occasions for temperance) and Aquinas on innate aptitude and divinely infused virtue, he argues virtue can form without suffering (by genes or miracle), so soul-making alone cannot justify evil, as Cash himself implies about his mother's grief after Jack's death. Cash instead locates redemption in Christ's suffering ('Redemption,' 'Why Me, Lord?'), while the intervention by his son John Carter shows pain still occasioning real growth in temperance.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Learning from Our Mistakes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Tamplin defends democracy through the Baltar election: Roslin's attempted theft failed, the voters' bad choice produced the New Caprica occupation, and this is exactly what Plato and Aristotle predicted of democracy as the deviant rule of the many, contrasted with Aristotle's polity aimed at the common advantage and a virtue 'every city' must care for. A thought experiment — an infallible computer advising citizens on every choice — shows that following it would abolish democracy, whose value lies not in results but in Aristotle's freedom, 'living as one wants.' Only by being allowed to frak things up can citizens learn from their mistakes, the road Apollo points to in his 'Crossroads' trial speech about collective shame, which is why Baltar's acquittal is a good sign.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Dorothy Growing Up in the Land of Oz
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: McCall and Auxier use Aristotle's virtue ethics to unpack the Wizard's claim to be 'a good man but a bad wizard' and to argue that no external token—the diploma, heart watch, or medal—can confer virtue, which is cultivated only through practice and experience. Each companion lacks something specific: the Scarecrow the intellectual virtues and phronesis, the Tin Man the feelings and stable states of character that regulate emotion, the Lion the sophrosyne that balances thinking and feeling into courage as the mean between recklessness and cowardice. Aristotle's three grades of friendship (utility, pleasure, virtue) frame the companions' bond with Dorothy, and MacIntyre's account of virtues internal to practices explains why the Wizard's public recognition still matters. Dorothy herself begins as the child Aristotle says cannot yet be virtuous—fleeing Miss Gulch in Kansas—but by defending Toto against the Lion and leading the quest she grows into a responsible moral agent, which is what her delayed homecoming requires.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Roll Credits
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dunn contrasts Baum's book, where evil is wonderfully 'small'—Dorothy melts the Witch in a fit of righteous anger at a stolen Silver Shoe, and personal plus social virtues (kindness repaid by the field-mice Queen) reliably conquer it—with the 1939 film, which smuggles back the 'heartaches and nightmares' Baum banished and resolves the Witch only by an accidental stroke of luck. He sorts Oz's harms into moral evils (the Witch's enslavements, the Wizard's frauds) and natural evils (the cyclone, the Deadly Poppy Field), cites Hume's catalogue of the world's ills, and observes that Baum needs neither Kant's postulate of God and a future life to join virtue with happiness nor John Hick's 'vale of soul-making' theodicy—Oz simply delivers the reward. Dorothy's abundant virtue at age five rebukes Aristotle (children, he says, cannot be virtuous or happy) and instead embodies Rousseau's Emile, natural goodness uncorrupted by civilization, while Chesterton's Doctrine of Conditional Joy and Tolkien's insistence on serious, non-technological magic frame the Old-World Christian outlook that Baum's demystified American fairy tale—and the movie's ending—quietly betray.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: This Is Really Happening (So Do Something)
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Milsky argues that Radiohead practice what environmental virtue ethics preaches, organizing the chapter around Aristotle's akrasia (Nicomachean Ethics VII): Sting, who champions rainforests while advertising Jaguar and topping the 'dirtiest band' carbon table, acts against his own better judgment, whereas Radiohead — confronted with an audit showing their 2003 and 2006 tours emitted roughly 11,368 tons of CO2, mostly from fans driving — changed their actual practice (venues near public transit, car-pool lots, sea freight instead of air, LED lighting and auxilary power units). He reads the King Canute imagery of The Eraser and lines from 'The Clock' and 'And It Rained All Night' as environmental narrative in the tradition of Thoreau's Walden and Leopold's Sand County Almanac, obligating listeners to act or risk akrasia themselves, and presents the band's Friends of the Earth 'Big Ask' commitment as linking environmental virtue to human flourishing. 'Idioteque'''s 'this is really happening' becomes the wake-up call to the akratic fan driving to Lollapalooza with a bottled water.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Livin’ and Dyin’ in Three-Quarter Time”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Randall Auxier uses Buffett's catalog to think about fortune and fate, reading Buffett's bold career moves (walking out on Nashville for the beach, later annexing it via 'It's Five o'Clock Somewhere') through Machiavelli's advice to marry Fortuna and master her tricks with virtù. Against Aristotle's demanding answer that only aretē, moral excellence, defends happiness against bad luck, he takes Vico's middle path: natural causes, moral causes, and the occasions of fortune are gathered under providence, so Buffett's seaplane crash ('God, Buddha, St. Christopher, my guardian angel... luck, and the United States Navy water-survival training') shows any fate can be turned to good ends for others. Sorting Buffett's songs into places, times, meetings, sentiments, and thoughts — the key sentiment being the wistful — the chapter lands on contentment as gratitude: being 'livin' and dyin' in three-quarter time.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Transformers and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Eyestone argues Transformers are genuinely alive with souls by applying Aristotle's De Anima: self-motion, perception, and intellect fit Ratchet (who tells Buster 'I'm a machine, and I hear you!'), and even the troublesome nutritive faculty is secured, since Energon ingestion, agelessness, and building each other suit naturally immortal, semimortal beings whose reproduction resembles Primus's creation. He extends arete to machines - Megatron has the excellence of a military leader but not of a person, while Optimus's chosen, trained goodness (Grimlock's 'Autobot training,' the Aerialbots' decision in 'War Dawn') makes him virtuous - and answers his title question 'why not?', since Aristotle's mortal soul gives Transformers no worse a shot at heaven than we have.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Transformers and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Plauche grounds Optimus Prime's line 'Freedom is the right of all sentient beings' in 'Aristotelian liberalism': since Energon, like our food, is scarce and requires labor and creativity, any volitional artificial life needs a moral code whose standard is flourishing (following Foot's natural goodness), cultivating intellectual and moral virtues from prudence, independence, and honesty to benevolence and courage. Ricardo and Mises's law of association - illustrated by Ratchet and a human mechanic both profiting from specialization despite Ratchet's absolute superiority - plus the ruinous cost of war give even superior aliens reason to respect our rights to life, liberty, and property rather than enslave or exterminate us, as Megatron would.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Explaining Moral Doubt
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Steven Gimbel reads the Formidable Opponent segment - red-tie Colbert debating blue-tie Colbert - as a glimpse of authentic moral deliberation that the flip-flop-phobic punditry satirized by the show (and Jon Stewart's Crossfire rant) has abandoned. Moral doubt is good because perspectives are partial and the Enlightenment 'marketplace of ideas' of Locke and Mill tests beliefs only through challenge. It has a source: 'morally right' bundles five dimensions - the actor's character shaped by habit (Aristotle's virtue ethics), the act itself judged by Kant's categorical imperative, the pleasure-versus-pain consequences tallied Bentham-style, the rights of the person affected from Locke and Hobbes's social contract, and the special care obligations of close relationships (Noddings and Ruddick) - and hard cases like abortion and flag burning are exactly where these dimensions pull apart. So emulate the dueling Colberts: fear not the flip-flop, since deciding which value trumps which requires open-minded conversation with oneself.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Sin, Play, and the “Synagogues of Satan”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Rachael Sotos argues the Report performs Platonic play: like the divine puppet of Plato's Laws with its competing cords, Colbert reveals what moves us (fear, hope, the ThreatDown bears, the 'golden cord' of the good) and so teaches freedom through play. Colbert's pompous self-authority - claiming to be 'the canon and measure' of virtue in I Am America - parodies Aristotle's serious man (spoudaios, megalopsychos) and the sophists Protagoras and Prodicus with their Orpheus voices, proving Heraclitus right that 'time is a child at play' and Aristotle wrong that play is mere medicinal rest. Tracking the war on fun from Chrysostom through Aquinas's eutrapelia (there is sin in a lack of play) to Erasmus's Praise of Folly and the Puritans' ban on theaters as 'Synagogues of Satan,' she reads Colbert's playing-at-sin - the man-seed eugenics bit, the 'black friend' boasts, the Ellen DeGeneres Paradox on Wikiality - as Erasmian folly that heals America's Puritan hangover in the culture wars.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Four 'Phase Three' essays on world conquest. Terjesen asks whether Doctor Doom's magnanimity (Aristotle's great-souledness, contra the unity-of-virtues thesis Aquinas held and Philippa Foot qualified) makes him less villainous than The Authority, whose purely consequentialist paternalism - like Doom's Emperor Doom or Ozymandias's plot - usurps a free choice no mere power can justify. Barringer reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes: the Stamford explosion and unrestrained superpowers recreate the state of nature, the Registration Act is the surrender of freedom to a sovereign, and Stark, Richards, and Pym repeat Hobbes's flawed faith in 'scientific' deductive politics, sealed by the clone-Thor killing of Goliath. Hillerbrand and Sandburg pit Rorschach's Kantian deontology (no compromise, not even to save the world) against Ozymandias's utilitarian murder of three million New Yorkers in Watchmen, arguing via Laplace's Demon that even Dr. Manhattan - nihilist or Schopenhauerian recluse - cannot verify the outcome, so watchmen can be trusted only by knowing their limits. Ostrander's fictional NSC interview has Amanda Waller's Suicide Squad defended with Benthamite utility, the rejection of natural rights as 'nonsense on stilts,' and the Augustinian just-war criteria of just cause, right intent, and proportionality, while the interviewer exposes how conveniently those limits bend.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: This Is Our World
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Miguel Sicart reads the 'Gnome Tea Party' — dozens of nearly nude gnome warriors parading in Ironforge to protest Warrior-class nerfs until Blizzard banned their accounts — as non-violent protest in the tradition of Thoreau and Gandhi. Against Blizzard's models of players-as-consumers and players-as-troublemakers, which he traces to Huizinga's Homo Ludens, he argues that players are Homo poieticus: creative beings who make the values they play by and act on them. Using the 'Flourishing Ethics' framework built from Aristotle's virtue ethics and Wiener's information ethics, he concludes that WoW's architectures of control and account-banning are an unethical design that damages players' capacity to flourish — Azeroth is our world too.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: You Don’t Have to Be Like Him to Like Him
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Levitt reads Monk through Aristotle's virtue ethics: a man of character whose police virtues survive Trudy's murder but whose phobias produce akrasia — in the pilot he knows he must descend the germ-filled sewer to save Sharona and freezes anyway, doing the right thing only at agonizing cost. Virtue as habit and the golden mean (friendliness as the mean between obsequiousness and standoffishness) frame his slow progress toward acting rightly without thinking, which is also why Stottlemeyer cannot recommend his reinstatement — he doubts the illness, not the man. Aristotle's three friendships sort Monk's relationships: utility (the department, employer Sharona), pleasure, and virtue — Natalie, who after watching Monk save Julie's fish over the priceless moon rock saw her late husband's goodness in him. Ethos, pathos, logos and catharsis then explain viewer identification: watching Monk move from akrasia toward balance (Dr. Kroger's 'N. Hope' note that turns out to mean New Hope) lets audiences identify with, and be ennobled by, a character we would never want to be.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Redemption and Hope for the Future
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Peters applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics account of courage — the mean between confidence and fear, shown only in facing an honorable death in war for a noble motive — to Colin MacLeod's two-thousand-year hunt for Marcus Octavius, the Immortal Roman who killed his wife Moya, in Highlander: The Search for Vengeance. Because MacLeod fights from pain and rage, 'like wild beasts,' and secretly seeks death as refuge from grief ('to seek death as a refuge from poverty, or love... is not the act of a brave man'), Aristotle would judge him a coward despite his fearlessness — Amergan the spirit guide diagnoses him the same way. Redemption comes only when Dahlia and the villagers threatened by Marcus's new Rome give him a noble cause and hopefulness: he becomes their general, fights with discipline instead of rage, and turns Marcus's own quickening to destroying the virus, illustrating the chapter's closing thought that for an Immortal dying is easy and living courageously is hard.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Forgiveness and the Fenway Faithful
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Rory Kraft uses Aristotle's virtue ethics to explain why Red Sox Nation forgave Tim Wakefield (whose mistake Aaron Boone turned into the 2003 ALCS-ending homer) and Ted Williams, but scapegoated Bill Buckner for 'the error' and eventually cast off Manny Ramirez. Because Aristotle judges a complete life, one swallow does not make a summer, Buckner's .991 fielding percentage and 2,715 hits should contextualize his lapse, yet some acts are bad without degrees like Aristotle's adultery, theft and murder, and a World Series-deciding error crossed that line. Kraft distinguishes Aristotle's categories, Wakefield's mistake (ignorance of Boone's changed plan) versus Buckner's misadventure (contrary to reasonable expectation) versus Manny's voluntary injustices, concluding that learning when to forgive players who are family taught the Nation what forgiveness itself means, sealed by Buckner's 2008 standing ovation.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Tie Goes to the Runner
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: St. Martin runs the Fenway 'pink hat' controversy through Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: the virtuous fan is the mean between the deficient bandwagoner who waves at NESN cameras mid-pitch and the excessive diehard who memorizes Dice-K's ERA to belittle others. Terry Francona's courage in sending Dave Roberts in the 2004 ALCS (versus a reckless Ortiz steal attempt) illustrates virtue as the mean between cowardice and foolhardiness, and Aristotle's contrast between the love of honor and the love of contemplation shows both pink hatters and stats-obsessed diehards err by making fandom about themselves. She concludes that accepting fans in any color hat is the truly virtuous mean.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Hey, Let’s Get the Stuff We Need!” Putting the Mall in Its Place
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Matthew Walker reads Dawn of the Dead's survivors, who loot the mall, gorge, grow bored, and degenerate into glitzy despair beside the zombies clawing to get back in, through Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics and Politics. Peter's 'They're us' is glossed by pleonexia, the grasping disposition to want more, which Aristotle roots in being serious about mere living rather than living well, and the quartet's hedonistic 'sweet life' is the life of enjoyment Aristotle dismisses as fit for cattle because it atrophies the rational capacities that make us human. Romero is no Puritan scold: material goods remain instrumentally useful and the mall a sanctuary, but like Aristotle he shows a life of unlimited acquisition is a kind of living death, which is why Peter and Fran must leave empty-handed.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents because they meet Aristotle's test of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgment that 'evildoers... taste better') and retain free will, since their blood-lust is a craving not a compulsion and Louis's rat diet in Interview with the Vampire, like Angel's in Buffy, proves an alternative exists. TASTE, full potential, and spiritual peace all fail to justify human blood, because killing a person brings more unnecessary suffering than killing a rat, the same suffering-based principle that condemns factory farming. The 'cold clammy consistency' punchline: since humans need not eat meat, condemning vampire blood-drinkers while dining on chicken, pork, and beef is hypocrisy, because we are vampiric too and only our choice of which life to ingest separates the monstrous from the virtuous.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 10 - Why Can’t We Be Virtual Friends
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Condella tests Facebook friendship against Aristotle's three kinds (pleasure, utility, virtue) from Nicomachean Ethics VIII-IX and Cicero's De Amicitia: the average user's 281 friends far exceeds true philia, which needs time, reciprocated goodwill, and shared 'conversation and thought'. He grants that Facebook's status updates share conversation and thought and maintain ties across distance, evoking the Seinfeld episode where Jerry refuses Keith Hernandez's too-early request to help him move. But because no one has ever helped a friend move on Facebook, virtual presence cannot make us better people, and Facebook's artificial buoying of dead friendships of utility risks quantity crowding out the few deep friendships that matter.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Extra Time
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Kent argues soccer is Aristotle's favorite sport because everything in both is organized around the goal: the four causes explain shinguards (plastic, curved shape, Mitre's workers, protection) and the game itself, with the final cause—scoring—defining a thing's identity and goodness, so two differently made balls are both soccerballs if kicked toward a net. Soccer best fulfills sport's three purposes (physical and moral discipline, theatrical imitation with catharsis, recreation): its ninety minutes of uninterrupted continuity force hundreds of renewed acts of self-mastery in Aristotle's sense of courage and the right amount, its single referee with limited powers embodies Aristotle's preferred limited monarchy, and Argentina's sportsmanlike throw-in returning the ball after Cameroon kicks it out for an injured player exemplifies equity—making a rightful exception to the letter of the law. Own goals, where a defender's error harms his own side, supply the hamartia of Aristotelian tragedy, giving fans a healthy catharsis of pity and fear.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Final Whistle
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Andrew Lambert defends the rationality of being a football fan by updating Aristotle: living well in a liberal consumer democracy demands an accessible source of beauty, catharsis, belonging, public discourse, and altruism, and fandom trains exactly these sensibilities — from his childhood prayers for Everton to the 1914 Christmas Truce match and supporters' trusts that own clubs like Exeter City. The mature 'fan of football' takes an ironic view of the 'loyal fan's' tribal passions, gaining the practical wisdom that keeps rivalry (the Liverpool–Everton derby, the 1969 'Football War') from curdling into violence. Fandom thus answers critics who dismiss it as consumerist escapism or bad faith.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Fighting Talk
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The editors' introduction argues that philosophy and fighting have been companions since Socrates the soldier and Plato the wrestler (whose name means 'broad shouldered' from the gym), and that each can illuminate the other. It tours the volume through concrete cases: budo courtesy drawn from Shinto, Confucianism and Zen; the Shaolin monks' exercises as a route to Buddhahood; Western chivalry and Gordon Marino's boxing as educations in Aristotelian courage; fencing's egoism and value; and the Stoicism of karate and utilitarianism of Kano's judo. Philosophy clarifies fighting traditions, while fights supply puzzles for ethics, aesthetics, and the philosophy of mind.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Free Your Mind, and Your Roundhouse Will Follow
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Young argues that dojo courtesy is not the fantasy that good manners win fights (Napoleon and the Karate Kid's Johnny lost on skill, not rudeness) but the framing of a craft within a way of life. He maps Aristotle's techne/ethos distinction onto the Japanese jutsu/do pairing to show founders like Kano, Funakoshi and Ueshiba treated fighting as one part of a whole ethical character, reads his seiza apology to an injured yellow belt through Confucian ren, li, yi and shu, and traces Shinto purity into the sincerity (kime) of committed sparring. His black-belt humiliation by seniors becomes Zen's 'courtesy of brutal': ego-deflating violence that trains no-mindedness (muga, Takuan Soho's fudoshin).

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Way of the Place
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Beattie uses Henri Lefebvre's account of the production of space to read the dojo as a 'differential space' practitioners actively create against abstract, conformist space. He shows how bow-ins, founder portraits, Japanese counting, mats, dogi and belt hierarchies mark ownership, bind the school to a lineage, separate 'dojo' from 'street', and shape bodies and safety (with Kendo's door-side seating and MMA's display of physique as hierarchy written into space). Play matters too: Aristotle's point that virtues are built by habit explains how playing at combat in a safe place breeds real courage, and the whole exercise teaches a moving balance between inside and outside.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Jousting for Virtue
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Farrell argues that the medieval code of chivalry is a living case study for Aristotle's virtue ethics: Lancelot, 'mekest in hall and sternest to his foe', embodies the paradox C.S. Lewis names as meek and fierce 'to the nth', which Farrell reads as Aristotle's courage, the golden mean between cowardice and rashness, exercised 'to the right extent, at the right time, with the right motive'. The joust, meanwhile, was a proving ground where knightly virtues became second nature through habituated practice, since as Aristotle says 'it is no easy task to be good'. Western martial arts, he concludes, are 'moral kung fu': a fencing match with one's own standards of virtue.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Boxing, a School for Virtues
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Marino answers colleagues who call college boxing 'teaching violence' with an Aristotelian defense: courage is the mean between fearlessness and excessive fear, and the ring is one of the few workshops where fear is actually practiced. He cites Wacquant's boxing gym as 'a school of morality' in Durkheim's sense, Rotella's 'education at the fights', and boxers like Maja Cavlovic and George Foreman on how training takes over when fear hits, to argue boxing forges emotional self-command. His challenge to his own students: 'How can you be consistently honest or just if you don't have the mettle to take a hit?'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: In All Fucking Seriousness
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Arp asks why well-placed 'fucks' in Onion headlines like 'Guy In Philosophy Class Needs To Shut The Fuck Up' are funny, and answers with the golden mean traced to Aristotle and Confucius, who both prized self-control and being a good role model to children: swearing is virtuous when it hits the mean between the vice of too much (gangsta rap's every-other-word profanity, the cemetery gardener's rant, Glengarry Glen Ross) and the vice of too little. He sorts Onion stories into vice tables—'Loved Ones Recall Local Man's Cowardly Battle With Cancer' illustrates the vice of cowardice, with courage as the hitting-the-mark mean—and concludes that a well-placed fuck is both funny and virtuous precisely because so many people treat the word as taboo.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: World Death Rate Holding Steady At 100 Percent
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dan Miori, a palliative-care physician assistant, uses Onion medical stories — 'Loved Ones Recall Local Man's Cowardly Battle With Cancer,' the 'Vehicular Manslaughter Doctor,' animal hoarder Tricia McCory's 'I'm A Diseased And Deformed Animal Lover,' and the Terry Schiavo American Voices — to survey how end-of-life decisions actually get made. He runs each dilemma through Mill's consequentialism, Kant's deontology, and Aristotle's virtue ethics (with Monty Python's Philosopher's Song as running gag), then through Beauchamp and Childress's four principles of medical ethics, showing that McCory's kindness to dying animals fails autonomy and nonmaleficence because kindness can be cruel. The chapter closes by restoring 'euthanasia' to its Greek meaning of 'good death,' arguing that accepting the 100 percent death rate means planning ahead with living wills and honest bad-news delivery rather than dying tube-filled in an ICU.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Allons-y into the Starry Heavens
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Smith reads the Doctor–Rose tragedy through Kantian deontology: shaped by Plato's four virtues and Aristotle's virtue ethics into a good will, both must still choose duty over inclination, so in 'Parting of the Ways' and the Battle of Canary Wharf in 'Doomsday' they each act from the categorical imperative — sacrificing their love to save humanity — because love, as Kant warns, impels partiality. Even in 'Journey's End' the Doctor sends Rose to Pete's World with the meta-crisis Doctor for the greater good, ending alone under Kant's starry heavens and the moral law within.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Why the Doctor Is So Special
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Applying Singer's animal-liberation concept of speciesism — judging moral worth by capacity to feel pain rather than by intelligence or likeness — the authors argue the Daleks are 'super-speciesist' and that Lumic's emotional inhibitors make the Cybermen the same failure, unable to share a universe with unlike beings. Since emotions are judgments that can be educated into fitting responses (Nussbaum, Aristotle), and since Daleks infused with Rose's or Diagoras's DNA collapse into empathetic beings, the chapter concludes that emotion and empathy are why the Daleks will never win and why the Doctor, marked by his companions, is special among Time Lords.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: I Am the Bad Wolf
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Answers Davros's charge that the Doctor fashions companions into weapons by examining his character through virtue ethics: his unifying virtue is Heideggerian 'authentic concern', always offering aggressors like the Nestene or the Sycorax a choice so they become genuinely responsible, as in the fly-swatting thought experiment. Companions instead act from compassion, which lacks impartiality and produces the 'Bad Wolf Syndrome' (Rose's Dalek genocide, Martha's Osterhagen Key, Jack's warp star). Since for Aristotle a friend is 'another himself', the companions' actions are in a sense the Doctor's own yet founded on a distorted disposition, which is why he runs from his past.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Spice of Meaning
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Mines Dune for an account of the meaningful life by contrasting the Harkonnens, who amass power for its own sake and grind Yueh's very identity to dust, with the Fremen, whose rigid rituals give meaning but suffocate anyone who lives entirely inside them—with Duke Leto's abolition of the beggars' water-towel custom as the failure case in between. Following Aristotle's method of starting from 'the views of the wise,' the chapter argues virtue is an open-ended, formulaless skill: rising above inherited identities while repairing the social bonds they sustain, as Paul and Jessica do by breaking selected Fremen rules and leaving the sietch stronger. The worm-rider, feet shifting on sand above a creature that can never be fully controlled, is the closing image of a struggle that never finally resolves.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Alone into the Desert
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Audits Duniverse lives by Socrates's standard—the condition of the soul over wealth and power, with justice, courage, temperance, and wisdom—finding Baron Harkonnen utterly wanting, 'Leto the Just' compromised by forgery and concubinage, Paul unjust in his myth-making holy war (though Plato's Republic would smile on ruling myths), and the Fremen admirable in temperance and courage but fatally sure of themselves where Socrates prized knowing that you do not know. Aristotle's function argument and golden mean follow: Paul's first worm-ride is courage between rashness and cowardice, but Paul's and Leto II's extreme, humanity-saving selflessness has no excess to moderate and so breaks the doctrine of the mean. The author concludes Socrates is too harsh and Aristotle closer, yet even he fails: sometimes the best life requires extreme virtue and even injustice, as with the two Atreides emperors.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Sweet Miracles of (Secular) Faith, Hope, and Love
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Florek reconstructs Peart's ethics as Aristotelian virtue ethics: aiming at eudaimonia rather than feeling good, 'Freewill' chooses autonomy and responsibility as virtues, and 'Vital Signs' adds persistence and courage ('courageous convictions will drag the dream into existence'), with a compassionate expansion toward ordinary sufferers in 'Distant Early Warning', 'Red Sector A' ('I must help my mother stand up straight'), and 'Everyday Glory'. Peart's existential consciousness then confronts finitude ('Time Stand Still', the fading memory of 'Vapor Trail'), contingency ('Roll the Bones' — 'Why does it happen? Because it happens'), and the absurd of Sartre and Camus ('The Stars Look Down' — an indifferent universe that answers nothing). The 1997-98 tragedies turn this existential consciousness tragic, and the post-tragic resolution of Vapor Trails and 'Faithless' is a secular faith in hope and love — Peart's answer to 1 Corinthians 13 without God — grounded in being loved by Carrie Nuttall.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: You Control Your Urges—They Do Not Control You
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Waller and McAlear first rebut the amoral reading: Dexter does feel (he sobs over Rita, loves Deb, misses Harry) and does control his urges through the Code, so morality applies to him, and the Dark Passenger is merely everyone's socially unacceptable desires - the very thing that gives rise to moral codes. They then test the three theories: Aristotelian virtue ethics mostly fails because murder admits no mean and Harry's Code teaches killer's skills rather than virtues (though its 'don't kill innocents' dispositions are genuine virtues); utilitarianism fails even in rule-utilitarian form - via the organ-harvesting doctor and Harry's own utilitarian guilt over Laura Moser's death - because Dexter kills because the Code requires it, not because it maximizes happiness. What fits is dark deontology: like Kant's argument that murderers consent to their own execution out of respect for their rationality, Dexter kills only killers, acts from duty rather than enjoyment, and treats 'don't get caught' as a condition for the possibility of his true imperative.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Becoming a Real Boy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Phillip Deen places Dexter on the scale of character types from Book VII of Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics - temperate, morally strong (Angel Batista), morally weak (Deb), self-indulgent (Masuka), and the beast - rejecting the Socratic view that vice is mere ignorance, and argues Dexter is neither self-indulgent nor simply beastly but a 'morally strong beast.' The decisive test is Kant's tribunal of conscience and the morality-versus-prudence question: Dexter gathers proof before killing, feels remorse for Jonathan Farrow, and tells Trinity 'No, but I want to be' morally superior - yet his delight at Doakes's death exposes mere prudence. Deen closes with Brian's Heideggerian offer of authenticity ('you could be yourself around me') refused: Dexter hopes that by pretending the feelings are there he may one day 'turn into a real boy.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Why Is It the Best Day Ever
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Nicole Pramik argues SpongeBob is Aristotle's self-mastered man: his daily cheerfulness is eudaimonia, a happiness earned by practicing virtue as the mean between vices of excess and deficiency. The chapter tests each mean with episodes — courage between cowardly isolation ('I Had an Accident') and recklessness ('A Life in a Day'), honor between Patrick's under-the-rock humility and Squidward's Easter-Island vanity, honesty in 'Hooky' and 'Wet Painters', and good temper mended with Patrick in 'New Student Starfish' and 'The Fry Cook Games'. His moderation in pleasure and wealth, contrasted with Mr. Krabs's stinginess, and his F.U.N. Song friendship (Aristotle's greatest external good) show the golden mean served up on a sesame seed bun.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Best Kind of Friend
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Ruth Tallman tests Holmes and Watson against Aristotle's requirement in the Nicomachean Ethics that perfect friendship exists only between the 'alike in excellence': since the two live by irreconcilable moral codes (Holmes's cocaine and burglaries versus Watson's clean living and law-abidingness), Aristotelian moral naturalism denies they can be true friends at all, despite the raw panic in 'The Three Garridebs' proving mutual devotion. Recasting the pair as moral pluralists with different 'good for me's, she argues Holmes is actually the better friend, an 'integrity-promoting' friend who urges Watson to stay home from the Milverton burglary to honor Watson's own code, while the proselytizing Watson, who nags about cocaine yet tags along anyway, repeatedly violates his own integrity.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Game’s Afoot
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Littmann poses Holmes's cocaine habit as philosophy's classic akrasia puzzle: Socrates denies weakness of will, treating it as mis-measured pleasure in which nearer pleasures loom larger — the King of Bohemia risking scandal for Irene Adler's company, Sir George Burnwell's gambling, Holmes's immediate relief of boredom — while Aristotle objects in the Nicomachean Ethics that reason really is clouded by passion, the way 'Black Peter' Carey's murderous violence is clouded by rum, so the cure is habituated practice rather than a science of measuring pleasures. Aristotle's account fits our sense that Holmes, 'the most perfect reasoning and observing machine,' knowingly chooses the lesser good. The verdict is that this is the one case Holmes failed to solve: it was Watson, not Holmes's own reason and will, who 'weaned him from that drug mania.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Flanders reads Killing Yourself to Live as asking whether dying can be good for the person who dies: Jeff Buckley's 'Hallelujah' and Kurt Cobain's myth became deeper and more successful only after the fact, as if death were a career move.
