He answers with Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where the fortunes of descendants can affect the happiness of the dead: our life-stories outlive their authors, so fans' posthumous devotion can really benefit Buckley, though no posthumous fame can add virtue that was never lived (Michael Jackson's rehabilitation cannot touch how he actually lived). Klosterman's road trip ultimately undercuts the question: the earnest Great White concert mourners remember what truly was there, while Cobain's fans retroactively invent meaning to gain 'credibility by mourning retrospectively', so worshipping the rock dead manufactures an inauthentic afterlife, and Klosterman must kill the unserious fan in himself to live.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Wayne Yuen uses The Graveyard Book to teach the good life: Bod's family's murder, like students owing their existence to the Holocaust, is an unalloyed moral evil that still enables a better life, and Saul Smilansky's distinction between being 'sorry for' and 'sorry that' lets Bod benefit without endorsing the tragedy. His graveyard education is Aristotelian, virtues acquired through practice and models, from the Owenses' duty and Silas's wisdom to 'righteous indignation' against school bullies and friendship with Scarlett as intrinsically valuable, all building toward eudaimonia. The existentialist virtue of authenticity (attributed to Sartre and Kierkegaard) explains why Bod must be 'nobody but himself' rather than a copy of the vampire Silas, why the scavenged identities of the ghouls mark inauthenticity, and why wiping Scarlett's memory threatens her authenticity, resolving the apparent conflict between virtue and being oneself because bravery or wisdom is relative to the individual.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Answers Walt's claim that drug laws are arbitrary by separating legality from morality and defending objective moral principles, chief among them do-no-harm and a 'clear-headedness principle' obligating us to shun mind-clouding substances - a principle it attributes to thinkers from the Buddha to Kant while borrowing Aristotle's ideal of becoming brave, temperate, just, and wise. It sorts drugs by whether they cloud the mind rather than medical-versus-recreational, weighing coffee, Hank's cigars and homebrew, Skyler's cigarettes, and meth's 1200-percent dopamine spike (Spooge's neglected kid in 'Peekaboo'). Verdict: meth use is straightforwardly immoral, and therefore so are selling and cooking it - meeting Douglas Husak's challenge to actually give reasons for condemnation.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Stages the standard three-way ethics debate on Walt: deontology's universalizability (Kant) absurdly forbids killing Krazy-8 even to save Walt's family, utilitarianism (Mill) licenses both cooking meth and murdering dealers - a outright contradiction - while Aristotle's virtue ethics judges character rather than acts and convicts Walt of vice: he endangers his family, misses Holly's birth, habituates himself into Heisenberg, and defrauds his school. Because acts and consequences alone cannot see character, virtue ethics is offered as the needed complement. The closing move widens the lens to America itself, arguing the capitalist success ethos and our appetite for anti-heroes like Tony Soprano and Dexter reveal a society that praises viciousness - 'we are what we repeatedly do.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Greeley argues the zombie crystallizes specifically modern fears: with Aristotle and Aquinas he reads walkers as humans stripped of their essential nature and potential, which Rick's uncustomary eulogies ('I'm sorry this happened to you') acknowledge. Following Philippe Aries, he ties modern death anxiety to urbanization, hidden cemeteries, and the loss of religious consolation, citing the CDC arc where Jenner's science offers only a self-destruct and Jacqui falls back on 'the wrath of God.' Rousseau's thesis that society corrupts explains why the survivors in the woods seem more alive — warlord Guillermo turns out to be protecting nursing-home patients and pizza-deliverer Glenn becomes a hero — while the 'Bradbury's Storewide Sale' sign, the Walmart trampling, and Fromm's shift from utopias to dystopias suggest the shuffling horde is an image of our own consumerist, distracted, dehumanized modernity.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Littmann answers the charge that D&D is a waste of time with Aristotle: pleasure is good as an end in itself, humanity's function is thinking, so even munchkin power-gaming and 4E combat roles are worthwhile intellectual activity under the function argument. He then treats D&D as participatory art—improvisational storytelling offering catharsis (smacking goblins to purge aggression) and the Poetics' license to explore what could be, like the dwarf chieftain grieving a disintegrated son or deciding what a friend owes the thief in the scorpion nest. A good DM, on this Aristotelian view, makes plots unfold with internal probability and characters act from consistent personality, yet 'just playing my character' never excuses ruining another player's fun, since artistic value never suspends the virtues governing how we treat people.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Merli argues that good role-playing refutes Aristotelian virtue ethics: decent players convincingly play genuinely evil thieves and morally mediocre players play truly virtuous paladins, so the skill of judging what the virtuous agent would do cannot require being virtuous or having the habituated emotions McDowell, Hursthouse, and Jacobson say are necessary to 'see what to do'. Using a dice-guessing versus unverifiable aura-reading analogy, he shows that the virtue ethicist's escape—denying non-virtuous players can get it right—makes virtuous judgment look fraudulent and untestable. Because role-playing demands active first-person deliberation rather than the passive reception of literary fiction, it exposes that judging rightly and being virtuous are distinct skills, with implications for how habituation and moral education work.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Cooke defends his three-year lawful-evil wizard campaign against religious and secular critics by dismantling each style of argument. The propaganda charge fails because D&D rulebooks present no 'attitudes for export' about the real world; the puzzle of imaginative resistance dissolves once Can'tian and Won'tian readings are rejected for a 'Hardian' view that some things are merely hard to imagine, undercutting Dadlez's explanation of the Romulan spy's angry opponents; and the Werther-effect-style empirical case against D&D collapses on the data like parallel panics over jazz, video games, and pornography. The remaining character-warping objection—the Platonic and Aristotelian habituation worry that enjoying evil play mistrains the sentiments Hume warned about—turns unfalsifiable in the way repressed-desire claims do, leaving a firm moral gap between imagining evil and doing it.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Wire and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Grinnell reads Rawls's dotted case lists, Marimow's rip-and-run, Burrell's 'dope on the table,' and Prez being told he teaches the test rather than math as Aristotle's function argument gone wrong: professionals who reduce their purpose to stats and pleasing bosses are 'doing well' instead of 'doing good,' which is just what Plato says badly governed cities reward with honor. The characters who grasp their real function - Daniels refusing cheap felony stats, Bunk refusing to turn cases black without the true murderer, Freamon hunting bodies in vacants despite Landsman's fury - defy the Game at career cost, while Colvin's Hamsterdam and McNulty's fake killer show the opposite failure of zealous judgment without humility or rule of law. The chapter ends on the paradox that trusting professional judgment risks messes, but defining professions by numbers eliminates excellence altogether.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Wire and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Trerise argues Omar is virtuous in Aristotle's full sense: honest on the stand ('I robs drug dealers... I got the shotgun, you got the briefcase'), courageous, consistent, and generous, with even his vengefulness a mean between extremes given a world where no one else will check Avon or Marlo - unlike Marlo he never guns on citizens and even pays Prop Joe for clock repairs. Virtue theory's attention to context separates his killings of Stinkum, Savino, and Stringer from Marlo's power-consolidating murders and shows him achieving whatever eudaimonia his world allows, though his obsession after Stringer's setup, which got Tosha killed, marks his one real excess. The catch is exemplification - Omar is disturbed that children play at being Omar, and Michael becomes the new him - yet the chapter concludes that some vigilantism is a social necessity on the streets and that Omar's swapped body tag names the injustice done to the street's truly virtuous.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Wire and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Cooper argues The Wire stages two rival pictures of power: Hobbes's New School, where power is 'present means to some future apparent good', the good is only the apparently good relative to each desire, and honor is reputation indifferent to whether it is earned through love or fear (Clay Davis's graft, Ziggy's leather jacket, Avon displaying Brandon's mutilated body to 'send a message', Marlo spending exorbitant sums and torturing Butchie so his name keeps ringing out), and the Old School of Aristotle and Aquinas, where power is oriented to perfection and objective goods like family, friendship, and truth. Against the fear-based honor of the kingpins he sets McNulty's failed redemption and the successful reforms of Cutty's boxing gym, Walon's sobriety, and Bubs, whose prudence in taking the Sun job, temperance, justice at the Viva House, and fortitude in facing Sherrod's death embody the cardinal virtues, showing that even in the 'dark corner of the American experiment' virtue has the power to move.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Massimo Pigliucci reads Rise as a Greek tragedy of hubris and asks whether Will Rodman dosing his father with ALZ-112 was wrong, first dissolving the 'it's unnatural' objection and probing the cure/enhancement border with Daniels's Peter-and-Johnny growth-hormone case, vaccination-as-enhancement, and Eubulides's bald-man paradox. He then runs the decision through three ethical theories: Millian consequentialism condemns it by its results (his father dies and humanity goes extinct, though chimp happiness might outweigh that), Kant's humanity formula condemns using his father as an unconsenting experimental subject, and Aristotelian virtue ethics vindicates Will's compassion and courage - Pigliucci's own view, since sometimes our best is just not enough. He closes by rejecting Baylis and Robert's technological-inevitability thesis (we abandoned the Concorde, CFCs, and nuclear weapons before) and lets Jacobs's plunge into San Francisco Bay stand as the penalty for market hubris.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Psych and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Patricia Brace maps Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics categories of friendship onto Psych: Shawn's first-season ties to the SBPD are friendships of utility, the shared hobbies and bar nights (tap dancing in 'Feet Don't Kill Me Now,' 'Neil Simon's Lover's Retreat') build friendships of pleasure, and Shawn-Juliet matures from utilitarian boundaries into erotic friendship. Lassiter's lie-detector threat to protect Juliet in 'Shawn Rescues Darth Vader' and the lifelong Shawn-Gus bond ('Gus Walks into a Bank') approach complete friendship grounded in virtue, while the Henry-Shawn paternal friendship heals as Shawn develops the golden mean, and the vicious Mr. Yin and Yang - full of regret, incapable of complete friendship - show the life without it.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jennifer Swanson asks whether Alicia can 'have it all', starting from Aristotle: Peter fails the moral virtues (faithfulness, honesty, courage), Jackie's intrusive moments undermine her kindness since Aristotle's unity of the virtues ties them together, and Eli Gold's perfect frankness leaves no room for perfect tact. Following Michael Slote's partial values and impossibility of perfection, she argues career and family are paired values in which gaining one loses the other, as Alicia discovers being pulled between Molly the nanny, Cary's 'she'll have something to fall back on', Diane's partner-track warning, and dumping Will after Grace's twelve butt-dials in 'Parenting Made Easy'. Since perfection is impossible in principle, the answer is balance across all the values of a good life, not Caitlin's retreat into 'I just want to be a mom'.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: John Fitzpatrick asks whether voters should care that Alicia stands beside Peter, from the Season One resignation press conference to the finale's withheld hand. After a rapid tour of right-action theories grounded in the show - Eli Gold's egoism, Peter's 'pitted' evidence tip as consequentialism, Alicia keeping Jonas Stern's dementia secret as deontology, the Florrick-Childs no-children pact as social contract - he turns to Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: eudaimonia as a life weaving pleasure, friendship, and practical activity, in which mentors like Will and Diane let us contemplate virtue in others and improve our own character. His conclusion: Alicia's endorsement matters not because she is a good wife but because she is a good person whose judgment reveals Peter's character.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The Azevedos read Plato's Republic Book I as a manual for professionalism: Socrates argues the practitioner - doctor, ruler, lawyer - serves the patient, citizen, and client rather than himself, while Thrasymachus's cynicism that injustice pays and people only seem just is embodied by Eli Gold ('I lie for a living') and by stunt lawyers Nancy Crozier, Patti Nyholm, Louis Canning, and the secretive Jonas Stern. Alicia answers with Aristotle's virtue ethics: professionalism as a cluster virtue cultivated through habituated action, hitting the mean and doing the right thing at the right time for the right reasons. Saint Alicia shows how costly being good all the time is, yet the chapter sides with her striving for virtue over Thrasymachus's goldbrick glory.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Brace and Kingsbury use the Nicomachean Ethics to argue that Nucky, Chalky, and Margaret mistake pleasure and the mere instruments of happiness - tailored suits, money, useful connections, the appearance of virtue - for Aristotle's stable, self-sustaining virtuous activity, so their lives stay unstable and empty. Nucky 'buys' even Jimmy and Margaret, Chalky's jail-cell staging with David Copperfield shows how fragile his facade of cultivation is, and Margaret's acquisitions end in blackmail and in bribing God over Emily's polio. Only Richard Harrow, the Tin Man whose collage-clippings represent a happiness he believes he can never have, moves toward real Aristotelian friendship through Jimmy's 'Of course I would; right down to the last bullet' - the philia Aristotle calls most necessary for a happy life.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jeff Ewing argues the moral fabric of Ender's Game is virtue-ethical, first testing Ender's leadership against Plato's cardinal virtues, tripartite soul, and rigid class hierarchy of the Republic, then finding Aristotle a far better fit. Ender's trademark use of the minimum force necessary against Stilson, Bonzo, and the buggers sits at Aristotle's mean between cowardice and excess, while his adaptability and disregard for rules and hierarchy only count as virtues in Aristotle's framework - though his ignorance of crucial facts explains why xenocide, like his beatings, fell outside the mean.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Danielle Wylie uses Aristotle's conditions for voluntary action - control and knowledge - to argue Ender's planetary strike is one of his 'mixed cases' made under coercion and factual ignorance, so praise and blame attach elsewhere: Graff and Rackham, who foresaw the attack and could easily have stopped it, meet both conditions through culpable omission. Borrowing Rachels' Smith-and-Jones drowning case to show moral responsibility can exist without causal responsibility, she ends with Ender's non-blameworthy 'taking responsibility' as Speaker for the Dead.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Devil and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: George Dunn asks whether the Joker's 'some men just want to watch the world burn' motivelessness even makes sense. Against Baumeister's 'Myth of Pure Evil' and the Socratic-Aristotelian thesis that all wrongdoing aims at some apparent good, he tests Kant's claim that no human can be a diabolical being, Claudia Card's definition of diabolical evil as engineering others' moral corruption, and the Satan of Job as prosecuting accuser - which fits the Joker's ferry 'social experiment' and his breaking of Harvey Dent. The upshot is that the Joker's evil, fed by pride and the wish for credit for the conflagration, is instrumental, pathological, and banal after all, its best answer being the convict who throws the detonator out the window.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Homeland and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: April Marratto and Adam Barkman use Foucault's appropriation of Bentham's panopticon - surveillance whose mere threat disciplines - to read Carrie's illegal watches on the Brody house, the family's stay in the safe house, and Dana's discovery that speech about her father's Islam is policed. Against Foucault's claim that freedom is an illusion maintained by power, the chapter sets Aristotle's view that freedom is a self-directed will choosing rightly (Dana making amends for the hit-and-run) and Rousseau's social contract, under which citizens trade equal freedoms for equal protection. Both would endorse Saul forcing Brody's detox for the country's sake, concluding absolute freedom is neither possible nor desirable.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter argues Finn is not yet a true hero but is on a quest to become one: against rule systems like Mill's greatest-happiness utilitarianism and Kantian respect for persons, virtue ethics asks not 'what should I do' but 'who should I be', and Aristotle's point that children lack fully developed practical reason explains why Finn's good intentions misfire - removing Donny exposes the house people to Why-wolves, and Penny's trick humiliates him in the City of Thieves. Martha Nussbaum's ideal of every person as free and of equal dignity grounds heroism in the common good, and her work on literature and popular culture explains how watching Finn's exaggerated choices trains our own moral judgment. Citing Franco and Zimbardo's psychology of real heroes - empathy, risk tolerance, persistence - and closing with Seneca's 'how nobly you live', it concludes that since Aristotelian virtue is a habit, anyone can start by admitting they suck at heroism and practicing, as Jake's advice puts it.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Justified and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter argues Boyd Crowder personifies coolness - composure, wily cleverness, unconventionality, intelligence, likability - as shown in the 'Cottonmouth' payroll-robbery scene where he turns his flip phone into a room bug, overhears Kyle planning to blow him up in the mine, and lets the plotters kill themselves. Jon Cotton borrows Wittgenstein's family-resemblance model to define coolness as an indefinable cluster of traits (with Dewey Crowe as the agreed uncool case), and reaches back to Socrates' defining of ethical virtues and the Republic's just, well-ordered soul to argue that coolness is a genuine ethical virtue - the excellence of a properly functioning person - in a scientific, post-religious ethics.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Justified and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter diagnoses Raylan with Aristotle's akrasia (lack of self-restraint): Art's 'lost cause' lecture, Arlo's boast that he has never shot anyone, and Boyd's 'you wake up in the morning pretending that you are not the bad guy' all charge him with acting on passion against his own calculations - sleeping with witness Ava, resuming adultery with Winona when her ring comes off. Because Raylan feels regret, the Aristotelian mark of the unselfrestrained person who knows his condition, he is curable and lacks self-restraint by habit rather than nature (Nicky Augustine's limo verdict: 'it's not who you are'). The chapter reads Raylan's signature move - forcing men to draw first so their deaths count as justified - as a perversion of justice by an akratic who is not wicked, and the series arc as his slow acquisition of self-restraint.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Noel measures Jobs against the four cardinal virtues from Plato's Republic and finds him wanting: imprudent (NeXT, the Lisa), unjust (taking the GUI from Xerox PARC, 'more fun to be a pirate'), intemperate (cruel outbursts like the 'dogshit for icing' cake), with only a brash, mind-changing courage. Drawing on Aristotle's golden mean from the Nicomachean Ethics, Nietzsche's master-slave morality and his Will to Power line about the man who 'determines values' for millennia, and Joseph Campbell's hero's journey, he argues entrepreneurs are a breed apart whose real virtues are independence of mind, vision, and audacity—and that Jobs, the anti-social creator who would not fit in, changed the world precisely because the cardinal virtues were 'prison walls' to him.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Kyle Alkema and Adam Barkman ask what would make the Gang happy and answer with Aristotle's virtue ethics: happiness is long-run flourishing built on virtuous habits, with the golden mean (courage between cowardice and recklessness) as the rule for choice. The Gang instead lives a 'Reverse Virtue Ethic' - trying extremes first by crude trial and error, like sniffing gasoline to check that it is gasoline - along three roads: quick money (welfare crack scams, robbing their own parents' house), lust (the D.E.N.N.I.S. System's seduce-and-abandon script, where Dennis cheerfully accepts the charge of sociopathy), and validation ('You're not gay, you're just really, really vain'). Their residual Catholicism supplies consciences and limits - Mac's talk of God smiting them, confession, fears of Hell - but no reasoned morality, leaving them trapped in 'one day at a time' gratification as reverse role models.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Adam Henschke argues that Frank Reynolds, of all people, is a role model - not a virtuous man overall, but virtuous in one structural sense. Using Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, each Gang member's project is diagnosed as the vice of excessive self-delusion: Charlie's Waitress obsession he cannot see through even at her musical rejection, Dee's acting stardom she will not work for and that ends in suicide-adjacent despair, Mac's muscle-bound self-image despite 'diabitis', and Dennis's Golden God delusion culminating in 'the implication' and his car stash of 'fetish shit'. Rickety Cricket embodies the opposite vice, total loss of the capacity to imagine oneself otherwise (via Catriona Mackenzie's relational autonomy), and Frank charts the Aristotelian mean between the two - he rejected his delusive country-club life, knows exactly what he chose with Roxy, and his plans succeed where the Gang's fail - making 'What would Frank do?' a genuine exercise of practical wisdom.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 17. The Friends of a Time Lord
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Littmann applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics taxonomy of friendship - pleasure, usefulness, and mutual goodness - to fifty years of Doctor-companion pairings, from the Hartnell Doctor's glee touring Vortis with Ian to New Series companions chosen as friends who routinely save the day, from Barbara's Dalek revolt to Clara saving every incarnation of the Doctor. He argues Aristotle would still judge the Doctor's friendships defective: they are short-lived, unequal in station, intellect, and morality, and the companions cannot know him well enough (not even his name) for the perfect friendship of the good. Littmann then corrects Aristotle on two counts: friends need not be moral experts to serve as moral critics (Rose in 'Dalek,' Amy in 'A Town Called Mercy'), and the Doctor's favoritism toward his companions - risking worlds to save them, as when Rory weighs Amy's life against the universe in 'The Big Bang' - shows that preferring friends over strangers is itself his most frequent moral failing.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 13. Dauntless Courage
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The Bocks test whether the Dauntless are brave or merely reckless using Plato's Laches and Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics. Socrates refutes Eric's definition of courage as never surrendering - the Scythian cavalry fights while fleeing, and endurance without wisdom is foolhardiness - while Aristotle locates courage as the mean between rashness and cowardice, acquired by habituation ('we become brave by doing brave acts'), which redeems much Dauntless training: Tris jumps onto the roof a second time without hesitation because practice has shaped her. Fearlessness is neither necessary nor sufficient - Four ignores his four fears rather than lacking them, and only madmen feel none - so the brave person fears the right things, at the right time, for noble ends: Eric is ruthless rather than courageous, while Tris's mother's sacrifice and Tris's taking Caleb's place at the death-serum lab show courage aimed at the good of others, with Four's grieving perseverance showing it can even serve self-preservation out of love.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 18. The Virtues of Choosing Your Faction
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Pascoe contrasts Aristotle's and Kant's theories of virtue through the Choosing Ceremony. On Aristotle's account virtues are taught (intellectual) and then habituated into character (moral), tied to one's function, so Susan flourishes because aptitude, upbringing, and choice align while the transfer Al withers - but Tris, Divergent with multiple aptitudes, needs Kant instead: natural virtues are mere 'gifts of nature' that become good only through good will, and her perfect duties to herself and imperfect duties regarding family and faction can justify choosing Dauntless over staying in Abnegation. Kant wins the day: because a corrupted community like Eric's Dauntless redefines bravery into obedience, Tris must think for herself - 'maybe I am wired like the Divergent' - choosing her virtues out of duty and self-respect rather than inheriting them.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 19. Why Divergent are Actually Convergent
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Schenkewitz argues Chicago's downfall is built into its ideal: each faction drills a single virtue through total lifestyle discipline - Abnegation's mirror rules and gray houses, Candor's black and white dress - until 'you become what you do,' but a solitary virtue inverts into its own vice once it is cut off from the others: Erudite's knowledge becomes a lust for power, Dauntless bravery cruelty, Candor honesty callousness, Amity peace passivity, Abnegation selflessness stifling. The Divergent, who naturally hold all the virtues together in one unified character, are therefore the city's apex rather than its disease: Tris never stops being Abnegation while being Dauntless, and her worth lies in negotiating among virtues and making real choices from real alternatives, unlike the faction archetypes. Justice, the chapter concludes, requires the convergence of all the virtues within each person - the Divergent are actually convergent.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 5. The Morality of Manners
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dougherty argues that at Downton manners are not incidental etiquette but a central means of demonstrating moral character and respect. Matthew's shift from calling valeting 'a very silly occupation for a grown man' to valuing Molesley's role shows decorum tracking his growing respect; Branson's tweed suit at white-tie dinners and 'uniforms of oppression' display disrespect even where his politics are sound; Sir Richard's parting boorishness betrays a lack of moral character; and the Dowager Countess's polished barbs prove manners can serve as a mask for self-interest rather than virtue. The framework combines Nancy Sherman's 'aesthetic of character,' Aristotle's person of extraordinary virtue whose goodness must appear in particular ways, and Sarah Buss's idea that good manners constantly remind us that others are worthy of respect.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 5. Back from the Dead
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Devlin and Cooper trace Rick's moral arc as a struggle between Mill-style consequentialism - twisted by the apocalypse into a 'Greatest Survival Principle' of mere survival (Dawn Lerner's Grady, Enid's 'JSS') - and Aristotelian virtue ethics. Shane's murder of Otis, the Governor's rule over Woodbury and killing of Martinez and Pete, and Terminus's cannibalism all show survival-only reasoning dissolving humanity, a decline the show underlines with literal mirror reflections of Shane as a walker. Rick falls after killing Shane and nearly trades Michonne to the Governor, is brought back by Lori's judging vision and the sight of Carl going cold, and reclaims virtues as habits grown like Hershel's seeds - 'We get to come back' (4.8 'Too Far Gone') - though Seasons 4 and 5 leave him balancing a harder character, down to 'We didn't want to waste the bullets,' with the drive to survive.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 13. Carol’s Transformation
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Delfino and Lesinski trace Carol's arc from abused wife (Ed's beatings, Sophia's death, "I didn't think I could be strong") to the judge-jury-executioner she once refused to be, reading the transformation through Aristotle's claim in the Nicomachean Ethics that repeated actions forge moral character. They then evaluate her killings: the murder of Karen and David fails on both act- and rule-utilitarian grounds (it did not stop the flu, and Glenn and Sasha survived while the group was shattered), whereas killing the delusional Lizzie is defensible both utilitarianly and by Aquinas's natural-law exception that an evildoer may be killed for the welfare of the whole community when no public authority remains. Her confession to Tyreese and Tyreese's forgiveness complete the phoenix rebirth symbolized by the burning walkers in "Consumed."

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 12. Should I Really Stop That Rhyming
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Yuen uses the rhyming scene to analyze annoyance - rhyme hijacks Vizzini's attention, the Goldman/Morgenstern interruptions betray invested expectations, and fans' endless quotation is annoying through sheer repetition - concluding that annoyance is irreducibly relative and contextual. Aristotle's virtue theory supplies the moral frame: friendliness and wittiness, golden means between obsequiousness and surliness, buffoonery and boorishness, make being annoying a character flaw that damages the communal eudaimonia Aristotle takes the good life to require. Since these virtues may be supererogatory ideals rather than obligations, Yuen borrows Kant's imperfect duty to develop one's talents to explain why Inigo had to become a master swordsman - failing to hone the skill his one great goal demands would be a failure of self-respect.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 3. When to Hate and When to Be Irate
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Daniel Alloy opens with Aristotle's demand that one be angry 'as and when and for as long as one ought' and builds a theory distinguishing anger (a response to a specific offense, seeking proportional payback) from hatred (a response to a thing's very existence, seeking its destruction). He tests the theory on Louis's bits - hating deer as a class and fantasizing about giving them AIDS, the six-year-old 'Jizzanthapuss,' the Pig Newtons fight with a three-year-old, the Cinnabon clerk, the 'Awesome Possum' hipster, and the justified driver who yells 'suck a sack of dicks.' He argues justified hatred is impossible, since it would require a pure-malevolence being that could not be an autonomous person, so hatred is always wrong while properly proportioned anger remains a necessary part of the moral life. Kant supplies the self-respect dimension ('one who makes himself a worm cannot complain if people step on him'): failing to get angry at real wrongs done to you or your children signals a character deficiency, not virtue.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 5. How Heroes Argue
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: LaBauve opens with a staged Justice League debate over rescuing the Joker's hostages, where Batman's emotional, vengeance-tinged appeal loses to Superman's trust-based plea, and reads it through Aristotle's On Rhetoric: Batman persuades almost entirely by pathos (the relatable brokenness of Nolan's trilogy) with detective's logos, while Superman balances pathos, logos, and above all ethos, since Aristotle calls the speaker's character the strongest appeal. Against Max Landis's claim that Superman is irrelevant, he pairs the Death of Superman with Nietzsche's "God is dead" parable and the Kill Bill monologue to argue that Superman is a mythology of virtue - alongside real moral heroes like Gandhi, King, and Jesus - showing humans the ideal they ought to become, so Superman not only wins but must win.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 9. Masks, Hearts, and Superheroes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dupree and Fuš build an independent definition of the "true superhero" from identity statements (Batman = Bruce Wayne, Clark Kent = Superman): only an essentially human character who forges near-superhuman excellence through cultivated virtue can count, and Aristotle's virtue ethics supplies the standard. Batman qualifies - his refusal to kill the Joker shows the struggle for the golden mean between foolhardiness and cowardice, and Gotham Knights #31 shows how far he plans to avoid killing - whereas powers merely given, Superman's Kryptonian biology or the Green Lantern ring (their update of Gyges's Ring), bestow no virtue, as Kyle Rayner's and Guy Gardner's early careers show. Since Clark Kent is "in his heart" the alien Superman while Bruce Wayne is merely Batman's mask, Batman is a true superhero and Superman is not.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 11. Can a Leopard Change Its Shorts
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Alloy asks whether Rincewind - the wizard who runs from Twoflower, the Dungeon Dimensions, and the Agatean Empire alike - is really a coward. Aristotle's doctrine of the mean frames cowardice as the deficiency of fear-regulation between foolhardy Cohen the Barbarian and true courage, with character traits describing, explaining, and predicting Rincewind's flight. But the situationist challenge - Harman's reading of the cookie, hurry, and obedience experiments - denies that character traits exist, and the replies available to the virtue ethicist (Miller's continence/incontinence distinction, Alfano's 'dodge') leave almost nobody with virtues or vices, so the chapter concludes Rincewind cannot be a coward: cowardice, like the leopard's shorts, was never there to begin with.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 10. Virtue Rising
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Darci Doll argues the Rising exposes the Society's intellectual oppression—each Color denied education and fed 'noble lies' about its role—and that lifting it sparks an 'Intellectual Reformation' proving Color does not dictate potential: Darrow out-performing Golds, Orion the un-carved Blue, Ragnar and Sefi exceeding their station. She uses Plato's Republic (producers, auxiliaries, guardians, the lower orders kept obedient by Noble Lies like the Reds' terraforming myth) as the Society's blueprint, then turns to Aristotle: potential is realized only through the right environment, instruction, and habituated character, and Darrow's practical wisdom—testing himself, reassessing after Titus and Cassius, doing what makes him his best self—lets him flourish and lead. Aristotle's critique of utility-only relations explains why the Society's alliances expire (Antonia executed once useless) while Darrow and Mustang's virtue friendships and just rule endure, opening a society where everyone, including women and lowColors denied opportunity rather than ability, can maximize potential.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 7. Jon Snow, a Misshapen Christ Figure
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Rosa argues Westeros is a moral wasteland stripped of exemplars - heroes die, and vice spreads by imitation, as with Joffrey, Ramsay, and the Mountain - so Jon Snow functions as the series' Christ figure: the humble hidden king revealed in Bran's vision, the reformer uniting wildlings and Watch against death, killed by his brothers in 'Mother's Mercy' and risen in 'Home.' Using Aristotle's virtue ethics - Bran's archery lesson as the image of eudaimonia, hamartia as missing the mark, character formed by watching and imitating exemplars like Ned at the deserter's execution - the chapter claims the world is redeemable only through 'minority moral reform' embodied in a complete life, as with Jesus, Gandhi, and Martin Luther King Jr.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 31. Paying the Iron Price
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Hansberger reads Theon's return to the Iron Islands as an Aristotelian failure of virtue: excess lust toward Yara on the road, the 'small soul' of gold-bought jewelry where Balon demands iron-price honor, and the rashness rather than courage of trying to hold Winterfell with twenty men. But Balon's virtues are the vices of a piratical society that rewards reaving and rape, and through Charles Taylor's ethics of authenticity the chapter argues Theon's deeper failure is not knowing who he is - Stark or Greyjoy - so Ramsay's breaking of him into Reek completes a collapse of self that began at home; authenticity, it concludes, depends on virtue and social relations, which is why Theon can only begin to recover by choosing to serve Yara.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 3. Can Charlie Brown Be Happy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter asks why Charlie Brown is unhappy despite being kind, active, and engaged, and answers with ancient virtue ethics: happiness is not winning or approval but ethical self-transformation, so his dependence on others' regard ('How did the other team feel?') is the real problem. It diagnoses him with Daniel Haybron's three dimensions of happiness - strong on engagement but lacking attunement (nervous, self-conscious) and endorsement (cheerlessness) - and asks why his shyness so irritates the gang. Epictetus's image of Socrates playing ball at his trial and Cicero's dancing analogy supply the Stoic remedy: losing costs no virtue, what he controls is being ethical, and how you play the game is everything.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 12. Aaugh! Why Is Being Moral So Hard
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter claims Schulz's humor is built on moral failure and illustrates the three main moral theories with specific strips: utilitarianism via Bentham's 'sovereign masters' of pain and pleasure and Charlie's 'to make others happy' (with Lucy noting nobody is making her happy), Kantian deontology via Sally's crayon lie and Snoopy's 'I haven't bitten anyone on the leg recently' as fulfilling a negative duty, and Aristotle's virtue ethics via the failed steal of home (foolhardy rather than courageous), the unmailed Valentine (cowardly), the golden mean, and Joe Shlabotnik as a hopeless role model. Charlie gritting his teeth shows mistaking a virtue's external markers for the virtue itself. It concludes we fit none of the theories well, yet Peanuts keeps a spirit of hope - happiness is a warm puppy, and Charlie's grit is genuine even if he cannot see it.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 15. Good Citizen Deadpool
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Using Aristotle's Politics, the chapter splits the good man from the good citizen and argues that the Marvel Universe's 'city' needs mercenaries to keep its balance between heroes and villains, as in Deadpool vs Thanos where the In-Betweener steps in when Death is imprisoned and the balance tips toward Chaos. Deadpool's contract killing - hitting Hydra and AIM targets heroes won't touch - fulfills his role in that city, so he can be a good citizen without being a good man, a standard of all-around virtue that Colossus, the 'boy scout' produced by CGI, better fits. The thought experiment of an assassin for 'Deadpooltopia' shows how a dreadful man can still be a good citizen by serving his city's own idea of the good.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 2. If I Don’t Listen to My Imaginary Friend, Why the Fuck Should I Listen to Yours
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Kreider stages a chat between Plato and Aristotle about the show. On Plato's account, mimesis is an imitation of an imitation of the Forms, so Elliot's imaginary friend, his fake persona with Krista, and the Mr. Robot personality are intellectually and morally dangerous deceptions that let him commit terrorism without his rational self's consent; yet the Republic's censored poetry for the auxiliaries explains how fsociety's masked videos teach true beliefs, and how Elliot uses the fictional Mr. Robot to educate himself toward ideas he already knew were right. Aristotle's Poetics then defends imitation as natural and instructive - the show is a cautionary tragedy, and the Mr. Robot crutch is how Elliot eventually steps up to claim responsibility.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 15. Reset Virtues
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Doll argues Elliot approximates Aristotelian virtue despite his vices: he craves eudaimonia, uses practical wisdom to recognize the harm the 5/9 hack caused innocent people ('I'll own it all'), and habituates himself against vice by confessing, exposing Ray's website, and restraining Mr. Robot even at the cost of Adderall binges and prison. Leon's 'existence could be beautiful, or it could be ugly, but that's on you' frames the choice of a life to fight for, and Krista's counsel leads Elliot to the golden mean of a 'handshake' with Mr. Robot - integrating the two identities rather than annihilating one - while the viewer serves as the if/then programming keeping him virtuous.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 6. Horror Can Be Great Drama
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Applies Aristotle's Poetics wholesale - mimesis of possible actions, the six elements of tragedy, complete plots of proper magnitude, reversal and recognition, hamartia, and catharsis as the perfecting of fear and pity - to argue that Murder House (Ben's lust as tragic flaw and his double reversal to redemption in death) and Asylum (Sister Jude's irascibility and pride punished then reformed) are genuine high tragedies, and then uses the Nicomachean Ethics (virtue as a mean between extremes; justice as both retributive and rehabilitative) to show the seasons teach virtue, while Coven, Freak Show, and Hotel fall short because their characters' fates are undeserved and the moral message goes murky.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 1. How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Be a Hero
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Malloy argues Iron Man is the better hero precisely because he fails constantly - Armor Wars, the Registration Act, alcoholism, a string of collapsed Stark companies - while Steve Rogers was born heroic and never stumbles. Using Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he treats perseverance as a virtue between cowardly quitting and Cap's stubborn excess (his doomed stand against Thanos in Infinity Gauntlet), and separates Tony's virtuous perseverance from Dr. Doom's identical behavior by its motives: Tony honestly examines his failures to help people, while Doom only looks for someone to blame.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 5. Why the Good Man Is a Great Leader
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Nisley reads Civil War through Aristotle's good man and good leader: Cap shows courage but lacks temperance and practical wisdom - his rash Lagos operation, his rage-borne beating of Tony, his choice of Bucky over the Avengers' common end - and his ceaseless struggle between passion and reason falls short of virtue. Applying Aristotle's account of philia, she argues the Avengers are a friendship of the virtuous that requires deliberation toward justice, which Cap dissolves by tearing the team apart, while Tony's reasoned acceptance of UN oversight, moderation after Ultron, and concern for the whole team make him the good man fit to lead.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 5. The Serious Point of Scott’s Humor
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Guerra and Barkman argue that Dilbert's humor is doing serious philosophical work: strips like the Pointy-Haired Boss's scheme to strip app users of free will, rebranded by Dilbert as marketing, distill manipulative corporate practice to its absurd essential core, and humor serves as a logical tool that, when it preserves the target's integrity rather than straw-manning it, exposes the equivocation in earnest arguments about getting something from nothing. They ground the practice in Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where wittiness is the virtuous mean between the vices of buffoonery and boorishness, read Adams's catalogue of failures and his luck-first, passion-is-bullshit account of success as a Socratic acknowledgment of ignorance that deflates the American Dream, and treat Win Bigly's persuasion lessons (visuals, repetition, intentional mistakes, the Hitler counterexample) as further proof that Adams has the virtue of wit.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 15. The Evil in These Woods
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Tests three accounts of evil against the show. Augustine's privation theory — evil as nothingness, forged against Manichean dualism — fails to capture a Twin Peaks that is genuinely Manichean, with the Experiment vomiting BOB out of the Trinity blast and the Black and White Lodges in eternal conflict; Ricoeur's symbolism of defilement fits the filthy-haired BOB, the sooty Woodsmen, and the frog-moth contaminating the sleeping girl. The decisive framework is Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics triad of vice, incontinence, and bestiality: Ben Horne's and Laura's weakness of will, the town's ordinary vices, and BOB's appetite-only bestiality ("I don't need anything. I want") versus Windom Earle, whose intact but corrupted reason — the macabre chess game, murdering Catherine beside Cooper, hunting Cooper's soul — makes him, per Aristotle's claim that vice is worse than bestiality, the show's truly evil person and proof that evil is human and fightable.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Buddha ex Machina
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Lyons applies Masahiro Mori's uncanny valley to the hosts, whose near-human faces and movements turn initial revulsion into empathy — doubling it because the hosts suffer under programming humans would resist. She then argues, through Aristotle's virtue and vice and Nietzsche's discipline of great suffering, that hosts like Maeve (returning for her daughter) and Dolores ('I choose to see the beauty') display more 'human excellence' than the guests: Logan's hand-stabbing cruelty is mere vice and the Man in Black's scalping sadism falls under Aristotle's bestial. Humanity, she concludes, is a way of behaving rather than a way of being, and Mori's hope that robots may carry buddha-nature completes the title's reversal of machine and god.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “I Always Felt this Place was Missing a Real Villain. Hence, My Humble Contribution.”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Eberl asks whether living out Sizemore-style fantasies can reveal or only corrode character: applying Aristotle's account of virtues and vices as habituated dispositions, he argues William's three decades in the park habituated the vices that made him the Man in Black — the park reveals rather than suspends the self — while cruelty toward humanlike hosts hardens us toward people, as Aquinas and Kant warn about kindness to animals. Against Ford's claim that humans are wantons in tight loops, Maeve's editing of her own code after learning her escape was scripted makes her a Frankfurtian person who aligns first-order desires with second-order volitions, grounding her narrative identity and personhood. William too attains personhood by actualizing a second-order desire for a different life, with the hosts' free fight back evoking Nietzsche's will to power and Nozick's point that we want to actually do things, not merely experience them.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 9. Wherever the Road Leads
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Watkins takes the recurring road image ("Runnin' Down a Dream," "Kings Highway," "Learning to Fly") as a probe of whether the future is open. Against determinism and Aristotle-style fatalism she argues from lived experience: we cannot feel our choices as unfree, and even a determined world would remain unpredictable, so Petty's open road wins. His optimism in "It'll All Work Out" needs no faith in a good outcome, only the passing of time under our feet, and persistence then becomes an Aristotelian virtue required for eudaimonia, a duty owed to the kind of beings we are, and Sartrean authenticity in which Petty made himself through his project of rock'n'roll.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 19. If Everyone’s Special, … Is Anyone Special
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Grace Wehniainen defends 'you are special' against the Fox & Friends 'evil man' charge by separating intrinsic from extrinsic value: on Rogers's 1 Corinthians 12 and Genesis 1:27 reading, worth is God-given and unearned, like the family dog whose napping life has intrinsic value (with Tom Regan's agreement) regardless of tricks. Specialness as 'belonging specifically to a particular person' needs no trophies, only Socratic self-examination before the mirror, Aristotle's true versus vulgar self-love from the Nicomachean Ethics, and Albert Ellis's self-acceptance over performance-based self-esteem.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: On Philosophers and Drag Queens
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Drag Race is an unexplored philosophical playground because it builds on marginalized black and Latinx queer herstory and because RuPaul, whose creed of love and self-improvement makes her a philosopher in her own right, has made the show her magnum opus. It invokes Plato's cave to explain why philosophers crave the 'untucked' version of everything RuPaul shows on stage. Its central move is a virtue-ethics reading of the show's judging: Ru's demand that a queen first be fierce, and through fierceness achieve charisma, uniqueness, nerve and talent, mirrors Aristotle's question of what makes a good person, with fierceness playing the role phronesis plays in securing the other virtues. Comparing queens like Silky Nutmeg Ganache, Jinkx Monsoon, Yara Sofia and Sharon Needles, it poses 'what makes a good drag queen?' as a live philosophical problem.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 4. Is It Immoral to Read Someone to Filth
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Birnie stages Alexis Michelle's hurt at the Season 9 body-shaming reads against Bianca Del Rio's 'rolodex of hate' to ask whether reading is immoral. He surveys the philosophical ethics of humor — Plato's Philebus on laughter as malicious delight in others' self-ignorance, Hobbes's 'sudden glory', Schopenhauer on why ridicule hurts, the Stoics' ideal of never laughing, Aristotle's eutrapelia as the golden mean between vulgar buffoon and boor, the Spencer–Freud relief theory, and Bergson's laughter as society's corrective — before endorsing the play theory: reads are consensual mock-aggression, verbal sport honed by marginalized black and Latinx ball culture. From this he derives three guidelines (play signals and consent, timing and audience given the show's younger mainstream viewers, openness to challenge) and concludes Katya's bus-stop read of Roxxxy was acceptable while stereotype reads need care.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 14. Is Kant the Reason Everyone Hates Moral Philosophy Professors
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Duindam defends Kant against the charge that he makes moral philosophy professors insufferable, walking through maxims and the two-question Categorical Imperative test with frozen-yogurt and stealing examples, and arguing that Kant's notorious 'you cannot lie to the murderer' essay is an obscure legal point whose actual test permits lying to demons. On the trolley, the bridge, and Michael's forced organ-harvesting scenario, Kant's humanity formula, never treat persons merely as means, explains both Chidi's refusal to kill Eleanor and the difference between switching tracks and pushing a man. Tahani's sixty billion dollars in charity earning no points, and Eleanor's fruitless 'What's My Motivation' blitz versus her costly confession, vindicate Kant's claim that only a good will gives actions moral worth, while Aristotle supplies the closing lesson that being good takes practice, not just study.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 21. You Gotta Be Bad if You Wanna Be Good
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Shearer argues the show dismantles ethical dualism, the good/evil binary that sorts people wholly into the Good Place or the Bad Place and that underwrites real-world 'us versus them' thinking. Following Aristotle, being good is a learnable skill like reading or an instrument, acquired by practice and unlearning, not a fixed nature. Following Socrates in the Apology, progress begins with admitting you do not know, and the chapter shows that the characters who self-generate that admission, Eleanor confessing and Michael realizing he loves the humans, grow the most, while Jason's moral neutrality exposes a case the Good Place/Bad Place binary cannot classify at all.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 23. Where Thanos Got Lost
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Diagnoses where Thanos 'got lost' via Wittgenstein's aspect perception (the duck-rabbit, the Thanos-chin-as-panini memes): morality concerns not just choosing but seeing, and Thanos's impoverished worldview — shaped by a lifetime of rejection, drawn from the novel Thanos: Titan Consumed — lets him see life only as 'the condition of living things,' never as 'the existence of individuals,' so erasing half of all individuals strikes him as a moral act. His single-minded reading of Titan's collapse becomes confirmation bias ('I'm the only one who knows that'), and his final plan to erase everything proves he never saw the individual-existence aspect at all: his starting point, not his reasoning, is missing information.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 28. How Captain Rogers Became a Good Man
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Traces Steve Rogers's arc from Erskine's charge — 'Not a perfect soldier, but a good man' — through Aristotle's virtue ethics (virtues are learned, none innate, each a mean between vices like courage between cowardice and rashness) to argue that the perfect soldier's obedience is not itself a virtue, so saving Bucky in Winter Soldier, outlaw leadership in Civil War, and gracious command in Endgame move Cap from black-and-white moral absolutism into the grey area where real virtue lives. The payoff is worthiness: only after pain has refined him can he lift Mjölnir, and the chapter warns that a 'perfect soldier' Cap — Thanos's ideological twin — might have heard the Mad Titan out.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 12. What about Della Street
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Birondo evaluates Della Street through moral psychology and Aristotelian virtue ethics: she is an excellent secretary in the role-specific sense (the Gregg shorthand that traps Robert Caddo's contradiction outside The Lonely Heiress crime scene) and supplies the 'woman's angle' the office needs, while Perry displays Aristotle's practical wisdom in court but a failure of recognition toward her, under-crediting her and kissing her for her 'feminine charms' upon her skullduggery in ways that today would be sexual harassment. The chapter also applies Aristotle on habituation through Mrs. Caddo's 'wildcat' tantrums hardening into character, and asks whether Della's team-playing beyond her duties is admirable, sad, or itself the product of mid-century sexism.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Aristotle to the Rescue
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Yim applies Aristotle's three kinds of friendship from the Nicomachean Ethics to the show: Tracy with Grizz and Dot Com in 'Hardball', and Tracy with Jenna in 'Flu Shot', are friendships of utility that dissolve when the benefit ends, while Liz and Jenna's long shared history looks deep but remains mutual usefulness between ambitious colleagues. Liz and Jack, by contrast, evolve from David-versus-Goliath adversaries in the pilot into something like virtuous friendship, culminating in 'Retreat to Move Forward' when Liz humbles herself with a terrible improv routine and a shirt-ripping dance to save Jack's standing before the Six Sigma crowd. The chapter argues the show thereby dramatizes that self-sacrificial goodwill is what makes a friendship worth the risk.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Explains Gob's professional failure through Aristotle's account of practices realizing their aims: Gob understands that illusions should surprise and delight, and he is motivated, but he lacks the craft-virtues of the modern illusionist as methodical engineer of experience, namely doggedness, diligence, technical knowhow, and above all humility. Instead he exhibits hubris, the excess opposite the mean, believing magic lives 'in here' in his heart; the 'Sword of Destiny' fiasco (a real sword, Buster's fake hand, a botched surgery) and the yacht that merely sinks show his failure is of character, compounded by the Dunning-Kruger effect that leaves him opaque to himself.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Interrogates Gob's catchphrase 'I've made a huge mistake': on Aristotle's account of hexis, the mean of truthfulness and proper pride, and justice as proportional distribution, Gob's prison-escape key stunt and 'Hermano' jealousy make him wicked rather than merely error-prone, since he lacks grasp of his own injustices. Hume's sentimentalist reply is that immorality is a nonrational moral sense refined only through experience, so mistakes could educate Gob, except he roofies away his one growth moment with Steve Holt (!). MacIntyre's practices (the Magician's Alliance versus non-practitioner Gob) and the narrative unity of character explain why a man who tells no coherent story of himself ends up with no wisdom.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Let there be an Ending!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Southworth and Tallman ask why fans blame Hank Pym for Ultron's killings while never crediting Magneto for fathering two heroes, and answer with Aristotle's account of character formed by habitual imitation, renewed as 'moral exemplarism': praise and blame track exemplarship, not biology. Scott Lang earned credit because he actively taught Cassie right and wrong, making her the hero Stature; T'Chaka and stepmother Ramonda shaped T'Challa, while Heinrich Zemo's Nazi upbringing warped Helmut into the new Baron Zemo. The Avengers themselves—Cap's patient mentoring of Hawkeye, Stark hiring ex-con Scott Lang—function as moral exemplars for reformed villains, so the mentoring 'parents', not the siring ones, deserve the credit or blame.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Neither Gods nor Beasts But Political Animals
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Spanakos denies the official line that the Avengers assemble from necessity—Thor beats Loki alone—arguing instead through Aristotle that the team is a polis: heroes join for safety but stay for the good life, since outside the polis one is either a god or a beast. Ms. Marvel's miserable solo run (unrecognized by Stilt-Man, a 'Where Are They Now?' has-been) ends only when she returns to lead the Mighty Avengers among friends who share her arete; the self-loathing Jessica Jones finds eudaimonia through philia with Carol, Luke Cage, and the team that delivers her baby; even the arrogant Hank Pym regains excellence by defending Tony and leading a new team. Even gods like Thor and near-beasts like the Hulk, the chapter concludes, need the Avengers to flourish.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Avengers Rehabilitate!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Terjesen asks whether Cap's Kooky Quartet-style rehabilitation really works, pitting Aristotle's fixed-character virtue ethics against John Doris's situationist 'local traits' (backed by Milgram's experiments): Hawkeye succeeded because his regional traits—hotheadedness and a need for approval—were redirected to heroism, not erased, as when he cheats the Grandmaster to save the universe. Aristotle's continence-versus-virtue and vice-versus-incontinence distinctions explain why Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch keep backsliding, why Moonstone's true viciousness defeats rehabilitation while Songbird and MACH-1 reform. Against deterrence and retributivist theories of punishment, rehabilitation is defensible when applied early and to the unhardened—the Avengers Academy children and Young Avenger Patriot—so the Avengers can rehabilitate as well as avenge.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Lacking Balance
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Stephen Kershnar argues that Batman's hatred of criminals is not a vice but a virtue, since hating what is evil is the morally appropriate attitude toward wrongdoers like the Joker or Batman: Year One's brutal Detective Flass. Against Aristotle's person-focused Virtuous-Persons Theory he defends a 'Virtuous-Thoughts-and-Actions Theory,' illustrated by Gordon's retaliatory beating of Flass and Batman elbow-smashing a pimp in Year One. The chapter closes on the golden mean of balanced love and hate: Batman's virtuous hatred leaves his life isolated and unflourishing, showing that virtue does not guarantee eudaimonia.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Leaving the Shadow of the Bat
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Carsten Fogh Nielsen stages Aristotle against Kant on moral education: Aristotle says we become just by doing just acts and imitating exemplary people, as Robin imitates Batman, while Kant objects that every example must first be appraised by principles of morality and that imitation breeds heteronomy rather than autonomy. The Gordon-Yindel disagreement over Batman in The Dark Knight Returns shows people can genuinely clash about who counts as morally exemplary in the first place. Dick Grayson resolves the tension by using the courage, skills, and integrity Batman instilled in him to stand up to Batman and become Nightwing, proving emulation can be the route to, not the enemy of, Kantian autonomy.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Learning from Our Mistakes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Tamplin uses Baltar's landslide win on the New Caprica issue and Roslin's attempted election theft to argue democracy's guarantee of bad decisions is its saving feature: Plato and Aristotle ranked democracy among bad regimes because the many rule for private advantage rather than the common good, and Baltar's campaign of 'hope rather than truth' exploits exactly that weakness. A thought experiment about an oracle computer that always selects the best option shows that following it would abolish self-determination, the freedom to 'live as one wants' that democracy values above results. Only by choosing and frakking up (settling New Caprica, suffering the occupation, Apollo's shame speech at Baltar's trial) can citizens confront their role, learn from mistakes, and move toward Aristotle's polity aiming at virtue, making self-determination the mediating value between freedom and virtue.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Greg Littmann tests Sheldon's geek existence against Aristotle's ideal of living well: since humanity's distinctive function is reason (the DVD-player-and-screwdriver argument), a life devoted to thought like Sheldon's — down to his fantasy of being a thinking satellite in orbit — has genuine Aristotelian worth. The chapter argues Aristotle could even bless geek obsessions, because poetry explores universal hypotheticals (Terminator causal loops, Superman's laundry) and adventure fiction purges emotion much as tragedy's catharsis does. But Sheldon's arrogance ('Captain Arrogant'), rigid clinging to his spot on the couch, and selfishness toward Leonard and Howard would earn failing marks in virtue, so the modern geek gets a mixed yet partly vindicating report card.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Kowalski maps Aristotle's three kinds of friendship onto the gang: pleasure-friendships (Halo and paintball nights, and Raj's fury when Howard abandons their kite fight for a jogger), utility-friendships (Sheldon's failed Friendship Algorithm bid on Kripke for lab access, and the roommate agreement's Friendship Rider invoked over the CERN trip). Complete friendship — mutual care for the other's own sake between moral equals — looks closest in Leonard and Sheldon, yet Sheldon's pancake-breakfast apology collapses the moment Leonard refuses to take him to Switzerland ('Drat. No Frodo for you'), exposing contractual utility where genuine care should be. The chapter concludes no pairing in the show achieves Aristotle's rare complete friendship, and asks whether similarity is really required for true 'besties.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Sayles sorts the show's technology use by Aristotle's doctrine of the mean: healthy supplements (Raj webcamming his parents in India, Sheldon and Amy's video dates) versus unhealthy substitutes (Penny's Age of Conan spiral into unwashed hair and sick days, Sheldon living as a 'mobile virtual presence device,' one-sided 'virtual vengeance' videos against Penny's Wi-Fi theft and Kripke's helium prank). Since the mean is relative to the person and situation rather than a mathematical midpoint, moderation must be found case by case, and man as a social being must keep his social skills exercised. The chapter finds Penny and Amy — not the four scientists — best model balanced technology use.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Barkman diagnoses four mama's boys: Raj's selective mutism under his parents' webcam meddling, Sheldon's comfort-seeking from a fundamentalist mother ('Soft Kitty,' mandatory grace), Howard's learned helplessness with his foghorn mother, and Leonard raised as Beverly's lab subject, his hugging machine echoing the wire-mother monkey experiment. Plato and Aristotle ground the charge of injustice — receiving less than one's station deserves, and wrongs against intimates are 'more terrible' — so parents bear special obligations their neglect breaches, a contemporary point pressed in the care-ethics tradition of Noddings. Cognitive-dissonance theory and Putman's Aristotelian 'psychological courage' prescribe honest self-reckoning for mothers and sons alike, with Leonard furthest along after confronting Beverly in 'The Maternal Congruence.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Zeccardi and Ma deconstruct the film's hierarchical dichotomy between Walter's rule-obsessed ethical generalism (Shabbas rules, 'MARK IT ZERO!') and the nihilists' particularist 'Zere ARE no ROOLZ', using Derrida and Culler's method of undermining the opposition the text privileges. Each extreme fails: Walter's principles collide in the beeper dilemma, and active Nietzschean nihilism makes the nihilists unpredictable cowards. The Dude emerges as an Aristotelian agent of virtue whose phronesis perceptively weighs contextual facts (Smokey's disputed toe, the carpet-pissers' false assumption) against principles, making 'What would the Dude do?' a question about character rather than rules.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jollimore and Jones diagnose three 'very unDude' vices: Walter's rule rigidity, which confuses Kant's hypothetical rules of games (don't cross the foul line) with categorical moral ones and needs 'rules all the way down' to ward off nihilism; the Big Lebowski's hypocritical inauthenticity, a fake achiever living on his daughter's allowance who collapses facedown before his own rug; and the exclusionism with which everyone shuts Donny out of the conversation. Against these the Dude exhibits Aristotelian virtue as good judgment (knowing when rules don't apply), the Golden Mean between Walter and the nihilists, and Singer-style inclusion — 'he's in bed with everybody' — making him an authentic man of humor and perspective.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: What Not to Do as a Parent
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter pinpoints Marie's failure in Arkangel using Feinberg's parental-rights framework: by filtering out every fright (the neighbor's dog, her father's stroke) she violated Sara's right to an open future, misconstrued her welfare and protection rights, and stunted the empathy that makes a child a fully functioning human being. Aristotle's golden mean frames over-parenting as a vice of excess — as damaging as neglect — and Ruddick's maternal ethics of care also convicts Marie, since mothering requires fostering growth and social acceptability, not just preserving life. The Philip K. Dick comparison lands the conclusion: an android is distinguished from a human only by lacking empathy, so Marie has manufactured a partial android rather than raised a child.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “Oh, honey, I’ll do anything for you”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Using Rachel's Ashley Too doll, the chapter distinguishes robots as instruments (Kevin's MAUZR mouse) from social robots designed to be perceived 'as being present in the way a person is,' and invokes Heidegger's 'Question Concerning Technology' to argue that social robots break the instrumentalist picture: it is our empathy - triggered even by the insubstantial hologram Ashley Eternal - that they exploit. The Aristotelian test of friendship (we emulate those we admire, and friendship forms virtuous character) shows Ashley Too fails: her flattery installs false confidence, and because she never requires Rachel to attend to another's needs, she models no real friendship.
