Girard's mimetic desire explains Rachel's borrowed aspiration to become Ashley O and Jack's emulation of their dead mother, so the chapter concludes robot 'friends' are poor friends - not because they are machines, but because a real friendship is 'an education in the social virtues.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 6 Panther Virtue The Many Roles of T’Challa
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: White applies Aristotle's virtue ethics to T'Challa's many roles — Panther Tribe chieftain, king, Avenger, ambassador, brother, husband — arguing that virtues like the honesty and courage his fellow heroes praise need practical wisdom (phronesis) to guide action when roles conflict, as when he chooses country over rescuing Storm from trial, spies on the Avengers as king, or abducts a businessman as a matter of national security. Through tragic dilemmas like destroying Wakanda's vibranium to keep it from Doctor Doom ('a king must make terrible choices'), he shows such choices haunt without dirtying character, and that over-adopting roles is itself a failure of the golden mean, evidenced by T'Challa feeling 'imprisoned' by a kingship he never chose.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Changing Fate or Being Changed by Fate
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Colombo and Jones read Brave through Aristotle's virtue ethics and Heraclitus's 'character is fate': the dispute between Merida and Elinor over 'what is a queen' is whether royalty is a mere position or a character requiring cultivated excellence and habituated 'second nature,' which Elinor's poise displays and Merida's hot temper lacks. Merida's witch's bargain to 'change my fate' only scrambles fortune (turning Elinor into a bear) until she follows the riddle 'mend the bond torn by pride,' replacing pride with empathy — and only then, at the Mor'du confrontation where fate, fortune, and character converge, can it be said her fate was changed rather than she by it.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: A Strange Ending
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Manninen applies virtue epistemology — built on Aristotle's virtue ethics and golden mean — to the four students of the Ancient One, asking not what they knew of the mystic arts but how they knew it. Strange's photographic memory exemplifies reliabilist epistemic ability, while Montmarquet's responsibilist virtues (impartiality, intellectual courage) are measured against Pangborn's self-serving magic, Kaecilius's courage without impartiality, and Mordo's epistemic rigidity and blind deference to authority ('no more questions'), each a vice of excess or deficiency. The Book of Cagliostro frames Wong's 'no knowledge in Kamar-Taj is forbidden, only certain practices,' and Strange emerges closest to the balanced intellectual character, though Aristotle demands consistency, not a single virtuous act.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Sorcerer So Human
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter argues Strange fails Aristotle's golden mean at both stages of his life: as a surgeon he chose cases for money and fame (greed and gluttony rather than generosity and temperance), and as Sorcerer Supreme he swings to the opposite extreme of total self-denial, refusing sleep, love, and friendship with Clea, Wong, and the Ancient One, since relationships between unequals cannot be the reciprocal philia Aristotle demands. It reads his hardest choices—the Dark Dimension left to Dormammu to save Earth, the Illuminati destroying parallel Earths during the incursions, and spending the last drop of the panacea on Wong rather than the world—as tragic dilemmas that show both the virtue ethicist's need for judgment and a defensible-but-excessive partiality toward friends.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 5. The Morality of Manners
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dougherty argues that in Downton manners are not incidental etiquette but a central means of demonstrating and cultivating moral character, above all respect for persons, though they can also mask its absence. Matthew's growth from calling valeting 'a very silly occupation' to honoring Molesley's dignity, and Branson's journey from tweed defiance ('uniforms of oppression') to worrying that a tuxedo is insufficient for the Dowager's dinner, show manners tracking their growing respect for the Crawleys as particular individuals. The chapter anchors this in Aristotle's person of visible virtue, Nancy Sherman's 'aesthetic of character,' and Sarah Buss's claim that manners constantly remind us that others are worthy of respect, while Sir Richard's boorishness and the Dowager Countess's weaponized courtesy show manners failing or serving self-interest. Mrs. Crawley's etiquette-breaking kindness, praised even by Violet, complicates the picture by showing care can be morally outrun by propriety.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Spice of Meaning
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Builds, in Aristotle's manner of starting from the views of the wise, a three-way comparison: the Harkonnens seek power for its own sake and hollow Dr. Yueh into an instrument, the Fremen live meaningful but suffocating lives inside unquestioned ritual identity, and the Atreides model a virtue with no formula. Duke Leto's abolition of the beggars' water-towel ritual and his politically motivated spilling of water at the dinner party show good intentions failing when they break bonds of meaning without renewing them, while Paul and Jessica break Fremen rules in ways that repair social bonds and leave a more just society. The chapter ends with the worm-rider on shifting sand as the image of a never-finished, context-sensitive struggle for meaning.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Alone into the Desert
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Has Socrates and Aristotle rate the good life in the Duniverse: the Baron fails every Socratic virtue (breaking his promise to Yueh, intemperance, betrayal), Duke Leto is 'Leto the Just' yet forges certificates and plans adultery, Paul's theocratic myth-making is unjust despite his temperance and courage, and the Fremen are brave and temperate but fatally unquestioning, lacking the Socratic awareness of ignorance that would have saved them from manipulation. Aristotle's function argument, his doctrine of the mean (Paul's worm-riding as courage between rashness and cowardice), and his external goods are then applied, but the author finally breaks with both philosophers: Paul's and Leto II's extreme selflessness admits no mean, their unjust oppression can still be right, and such extreme self-sacrifice may be the best life of all.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Littmann recruits Aristotle to answer the charge that D&D is a waste of time: by the function argument the best human life is one of thinking well, and D&D counts even as hack-and-slash, since munchkin optimization and 4e combat roles are logic puzzles, while role-playing is improvisational theater and therefore art. Aristotle's two art-functions are applied to play: catharsis, so that smacking goblins with a mace (his first cleric Brother Silverwolf) purges aggression and fear, and the Poetics' point that poetry explores 'a kind of thing that might be', so a dwarf chieftain losing a son to disintegration or rescuing a thief from stormclaw scorpions makes players reflect on parenthood and what friends owe each other. A good DM, Aristotle-style, keeps events within internal probability (no medusa petrifying someone facing away), players must act in character (the lawful good paladin cannot ride past the bandit-attacked peasant, and 'just playing my character' does not excuse the assassin murdering the magic-user at the inn), yet D&D's fully participatory, player-authored art can still accommodate unaligned and evil PCs.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Merli argues from alignment role-play against Aristotelian virtue ethics: a morally decent player convincingly runs a vicious treacherous thief who frames others for murder, and a 'moral mediocrity' runs a genuinely good paladin, so the ability to judge what the virtuous agent would do is one thing and being virtuous another. This undermines the McDowell/Hursthouse/Jacobson line that only the virtuous, with habituated emotional responses, can 'see what to do' — the role-playing skill works off-line, without feeling the character's fear or sharing its motives, so right-action judgment does not require trained emotion. He adds that if the virtue ethicist retorts that non-virtuous players never really get it right, the contrast between guessing dice in a fist (verifiable success) and claiming to read auras (unverifiable) shows the retort makes virtue look fraudulent, and that role-playing, unlike reading Austen, demands active deliberation from another's point of view, exposing abilities literary examples miss.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jeff Ewing asks which moral theory governs the novel, finding deontology absent and a contest between Graff's utilitarian recruiting pitch and a virtue-ethical focus on character: the I.F. allowed a 'Third' because it wanted Ender's traits rather than his acts. Mapping Plato's cardinal virtues and tripartite-soul politics against Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he argues Ender's minimum-force self-defense, adaptability, and disregard for hierarchy are Aristotelian virtues, while his killings of Stilson, Bonzo, and the buggers fall outside the mean only because he lacked the intellectual virtue of grasping his full situation.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Eric Silverman asks whether the Amazon series' Lucy and Maximus should have children, framing the wasteland through Hobbes's state of nature where life is 'nasty, brutish, and short' and even vaults are limiting experiments. He lays out Benatar's Harm Argument (pain outweighs pleasure, so procreation is procreational Russian roulette) and Shiffrin's Consent Argument (no one consents to being born, as Sartre's 'I did not ask to be born' concedes), then rebuts them: Socrates, the Stoics, and Aristotle make virtue and meaning rather than pleasure the goal of life, so a harsh wasteland full of people needing help suits a virtuous, sacrificial life like the hero's exile at the end of the original Fallout. Parental proxy consent legitimizes procreation as it does children's medical decisions, and Kant's universalization test defeats the demand for pre-natal consent, since universalizing it would eliminate the very rational beings whose consent it protects - so Lucy's 'Okey dokey!' optimism wins.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Trevor Hedberg asks whether 'Kill Everything' playthroughs of New Vegas are wrong, from the Goodsprings opening (where the player may massacre both Powder Gangers and settlers) to installing a mod that makes Freeside's unkillable children killable. He rejects the empirical aggression argument (the evidence is mixed and effects tiny, and alcohol or contact sports set a precedent) and the Kantian disrespect argument, since Fallout's NPCs - stuck on terrain, repeating dialogue - lack the rational agency the Humanity Formulation protects. The best case against virtual slaughter is Aristotle's virtue ethics: courage as the mean between recklessness and cowardice, eudaimonia as activity in accord with virtue, so the morality of playing turns on motives - exploring narratives or seeking combat challenge can be innocent, but killing for the pleasure of settlers' horrified flight corrodes character.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter maps four schools of ethics onto Fallout 4's Commonwealth: Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Preston Garvey's settlement defense as the mean between recklessness and cowardice and temperance as moderate chem use; Kant's Categorical Imperative is tested on stealing ammo in Concord and on the Battle of Bunker Hill choice to warn the Railroad, where loyal silence to Father fails universalization and treats synths merely as means. Aquinas's natural law ethics, keyed to the telos of power armor, workbenches, and Pip-Boys, condemns the Institute's creation of synths by analogy to the IVF debate while still demanding dignity for synths who already exist. Finally, Bentham's utilitarianism is the one framework under which Father's Institute — adaptive labor force, scientific progress, stability and order — can sincerely believe itself morally justified.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Quagmire: Virtue and Perversity
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Miller uses Aristotle to assess whether Quagmire's sex obsession is a vice. Eudaimonia, not the fleeting pleasure of 'giggity-giggity', is the telos of action, and Quagmire aims at pleasure, so he is not flourishing; Aristotle's dissipated person, pained by absent pleasures, 'must have been thinking of Quagmire.' The Cleveland-Loretta-Quagmire affair episode ('The Cleveland-Loretta Quagmire') supplies paradigm cases of the Golden Mean: Cleveland first shows a deficiency of anger (apologizing to his cheating wife) then an excess (near-homicide), while Quagmire's boxing match shows courage between rashness and cowardice. On temperance, Quagmire is a slave to his sex drive (roofies, the diary 'Jackpot'), yet the chapter ends by defending him: he cares for Joan, distracts the social worker to rescue Stewie, and is honest about his passions, making him 'the most virtuous pervert he can be.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Other Children: The Importance of Meg and Chris
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dohnimm argues Meg and Chris matter because they lack essence: unlike predictable one-gag characters (pervert Quagmire, homicidal Stewie), their traits are accidental — Meg stays Meg after her 'Don't Make Me Over' makeover, Chris stays Chris despite flashes of artistic talent. On Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, character (hexis) explains action, but Meg and Chris are inexplicable (Chris hitting on his mother, claiming 'My dad is smarter than your dad' when they share one). The Isen and Levin dime-in-the-phone-booth helping experiment grounds the situationist alternative: tiny situational factors, not character, predict helping — Quagmire is predictable, but Chris (speaking hip-hop, covering himself in honey for ants) is not. Finally, Sartre's bad faith reframes them: appealing to fixed character is fleeing our radical freedom, so the 'anti-characters' Meg and Chris are the show's most realistic and philosophically honest figures.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Robert Arp and Sarah Fisk test three moral theories against objectification in Final Fantasy: Kant's ban on using rational beings as mere means (Kuja's manipulation of Queen Brahne, the Geostigma children of Advent Children), Mill's greatest-happiness principle (Yuna's and Aeris's self-sacrifice), and Aristotle's character-based virtue ethics (Hojo and Sephiroth as vicious, Aeris as virtuous). They argue Kantianism generates a stalemate between 'moral sanctity' and 'moral autonomy' camps over cases like Guardian Force summoning in FFVIII, and utilitarianism a stalemate over mandatory self-sacrifice, leaving virtue ethics, Aristotelian or Nietzschean, as the view that escapes both, ending with the question 'Aeris or a Cloud?'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Albert Anglberger and Alexander Hieke contrast Ned, the virtue ethicist's genuinely good man, with Cersei, a 'minimally extended' egoistic consequentialist whose only morally relevant subjects are herself and her children. Aristotle's apparatus does the work: phronesis lets Ned rank his daughters' lives above honesty when he confesses falsely ('the lies we tell for love'), his 'you're too fat for your armor' quip shows the golden mean among competing virtues, and Cersei's unbalanced maternal love is excess, hence not a virtue. They then unsettle moral judgment itself: utilitarianism would license the Slaver's Bay slaveholders, virtue ethics lacks action rules and cross-cultural agreement (charity is no Dothraki virtue), and Martin's POV narration gives direct access to Ned's inner life but only Varys's and Littlefinger's unreliable reports about Cersei - so our verdicts on her, like real-life judgments of others, rest on shaky evidence.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Arya's arc from Needle to answering 'No one' is read as Aristotelian virtue ethics fused with East Asian philosophy: virtues are habits acquired only through practice, so the Water Dance's endless drills and martial-arts blocks that must become automatic mirror the honest person who tells the truth without deliberating. Syrio's lessons - 'looking is not seeing,' the story of the ordinary tomcat the other bravos mistook for a fabulous beast, being fully present with your trouble - teach Zen seeing and mindfulness, while 'be like water' and the steel that must be part of your arm embody Laozi's effortless wu wei. The Faceless Men's initiation, from discarding her possessions to the literal removal of Arya's face, becomes the Zen slaying of the ego, making her a 'Zen-Ninja-Aristotelian' on the path to eudaimonia.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 21. You Gotta Be Bad if You Wanna Be Good
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Argues that no one can improve without first admitting they are bad: the rigid Good Place/Bad Place binary is ethical dualism whose cracks show in Mindy St. Claire's Medium Place and Jason, a naive moral neutral who fits neither side. Socrates' Apology supplies the method — wisdom is knowing what you do not know, so self-aware fault-finding precedes growth — while Aristotle's account of virtue as learned by practice, like an instrument, grounds the claim that goodness can be acquired even in the afterlife, though unlearning old habits is harder. Eleanor's trash storm, Tahani's failed party, and Chidi's theory-practice gap mark each character's admissions of error, and the worst offenders, Eleanor and Michael, improve most because they confess unprompted.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Southworth uses the War of Light to ask what role emotion should play in moral reasoning: Sinestro rules Korugar through fear, the Star Sapphires kidnap Sinestro Corps prisoners to convert them to love, Atrocitus's rage was forged by the Manhunters' massacre, Larfleeze hoards, and the Blue Lanterns merely hope that hope matters. On Aristotle's account every corps errs by excess: Atrocitus's rage makes him miss chances to kill Sinestro, Fatality's love benches John Stewart from saving his friends, and even the Green Lanterns' will-only ideal fails, since total fearlessness is itself vicious and Plato's picture has reason directing emotion like a general directing soldiers. He ends by defending Mill's utilitarianism: the Guardians' real failure was not detachment but pretending to be detached, and reading them as flawed 'benevolent, disinterested spectators' vindicates the Corps while explaining their moral growth after Scar and the Blackest Night.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: NOTES
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The section argues that vice and virtue are habits built up over time: Snape still rages at Harry-as-James and sneers at Tonks's wolf Patronus as 'weak,' yet his own doe Patronus, matching Lily's, is the magical emblem of his transformation by love. Contrasting friends, who strengthen the soul's integrity by sharing joys and sorrows, with Voldemort, whose Horcruxes give him eight 'selves' while making him less human, it reads remorse as what knits a damaged soul back together, sealed by Harry's forgiveness and the name 'Albus Severus.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: NOTES
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Against the obvious reading of Voldemort's loveless begetting, the section argues he is 'not his mother's son': he imitates Marvolo and Salazar Slytherin, while Merope, on Aristotle's principle that we are what we consistently do, redeemed herself by stopping the potion, renouncing magic entirely, and choosing love over hate at the cost of her life. Character is destiny only if forged by genuinely free choices rather than blood or fate, so Merope shows not even the most tragic beginnings are destined for darkness, while Voldemort, who never loved and never wanted a friend, chose otherwise, leaving Harry as the true mother's son, shielded by 'a more ancient and powerful magic than any potion.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: NOTES
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Uses William James's marginal motto, sow a thought and reap a destiny, together with Aristotle's account of how repeated acts shape the soul, to argue that Voldemort's maimed afterlife-state is the cumulative result of freely chosen evil he can no longer muster remorse to undo. Setting Heidegger's atheism against Rowling's depicted afterlife, and adding Locke's character-and-memory identity, Kant's postulate that harmony of virtue and happiness requires an afterlife, and Pascal on why the soul's immortality must concern us, it concludes that if Rowling is right, every choice here is infinitely consequential.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: a2.xhtml
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Bassham reads The Hobbit as a story of moral growth: the comfort-loving Bilbo who trembles like jelly at the dwarves' plans grows into the hobbit who volunteers to carry the Ring to Mordor. Growth in wisdom comes from Socratic self-examination (learning how little one knows) and from broadened experience of the wide world; growth in virtue comes either from sudden conversion (Thorin's Scrooge-like deathbed repentance) or, as Aristotle taught, from slow habituation - Bilbo's repeated courageous and generous acts (sparing Gollum, returning the elf-keys, giving up the Arkenstone) build lasting character. Seneca's view that hardship strengthens supplies the framework for why Bilbo's trials on the road ennobled rather than broke him.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: a8.xhtml
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Garcia argues Tolkien writes with a virtue-ethical moral theory: Middle-earth peoples are characterized by moral traits (noble eagles, cruel orcs), intentions matter (Bilbo is not to blame for the discomforting barrel escape because he meant rescue, and he turns back through the mountain tunnels because loyalty and courage demand it), and the book's drama is the tension between Aristotle's 'great-souled' proper pride and Aquinas' Christian humility. Thorin's pride (self-styled 'King under the Mountain', refusing Bard's just claim), Smaug's vanity that Bilbo flatters to find the bare patch, and the dragon-sickness illustrate pride as vice, while Bilbo's growth - believing after the spiders that 'there was more in him' yet accepting Gandalf's 'you are only quite a little fellow in a wide world' with a laugh - exemplifies correct self-assessment between vanity and undue humility.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: a20.xhtml
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Watson uses the company's decisions under uncertainty - whether to approach the troll-fire that nearly gets them eaten, the elf-lights in Mirkwood, Bilbo's descent of Smaug's tunnel - to teach decision theory: expected utility (assigning probabilities and values shows they should have stayed put rather than follow the troll-light), conditional probability (the Mirkwood lights are treated as dependent events, dodging the gambler's fallacy), and simplifying the outcome set. He then judges Bilbo by Aristotle's doctrine that courage is the mean between the vice of cowardice and the vice of rashness, felt with respect to the appropriate passion, fear: Bilbo fears as he should (kettle-whistles and jelly-trembles), avoids unforced risks, yet risks death for his companions' lives - so he has acted courageously and is developing, not yet fully possessing, the virtue, which Aristotle says requires long practice.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Johnson sorts Frank's six friendships through Aristotle's three kinds: Freddy and Meechum are friendships of pleasure (ribs and candor; loyalty and sex), while Doug, Cathy Durant, Tusk, and Jackie Sharp are friendships of utility that dissolve when usefulness ends - Jackie endorsing Dunbar being the proof. Even Frank's marriage fails the test of true friendship, since Aristotle holds that only good people can mirror each other's character, and badness corrupts the self-knowledge friendship provides. Because Aristotle deems friendship 'most indispensable for life' and eudaimonia requires virtuous activity joined to good fortune, the chapter ends hoping Frank can still choose the good for its own sake - a hope Claire's walkout after Iowa badly dents.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 1 Acting Without Thinking The Sagacity of Indiana Jones
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Justin Kitchen rebuts the consequentialist charge (voiced by Big Bang Theory's Amy Farrah Fowler) that Indy plays no role in Raiders' outcome — the Nazis would have opened the Ark and died anyway — by shifting to virtue ethics: Indy's goodness lies in his character, not his consequences. His spontaneous 'I'm making this up as I go' decisions are read as Stoic sage-like action flowing from the two-stage moral education depicted in The Young Indiana Jones Chronicles, from Krishnamurti's lesson on death to Epictetus's 'winter training' in practice. The cardinal virtues as knowledge explain his instinctive courage (lifeboat, lead-lined refrigerator) and temperance (running past treasure), while his snake panic, his flash of greed at the Grail in Crusade, and his strained bonds with Marion and his father show he is a hero approaching but not yet attaining sagehood.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 3 The Virtues that Made the Man, and the Man Who Became the Legend The Adventures in Philosophy of Young India
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Robert Mentyka reads The Adventures of Young Indiana Jones through Aristotle: Kazantzákis's causality lesson in 'Travels with Father' introduces the four causes, which the chapter applies to the TV series itself, and the final cause grounds ethics — eudaimonia is the ultimate end of all action, as young Indy learns when the Mata Hari affair in 'Demons of Deception' shows that pleasure cannot deliver fulfillment. Virtue is a mean between extremes (courage between cowardice and recklessness), acquired through vigilant practice and through community, illustrated by Indy swinging between caution and recklessness with Nancy Stratemeyer and Pancho Villa, and by exemplars like Albert Schweitzer and Ernest Hemingway. The 'adventures that made the man' were really the virtues and the people that shaped him, completed when Crusade and Crystal Skull have him accept his roles as son and father.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 13 Pride and Prudence in the Pursuit of Knowledge Indiana Jones, René Belloq, and Irina Spalko
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Argues that the desire to know is natural and good (Aristotle's Metaphysics, Socrates via Plato's Meno) only when bounded by moral limits, using Gilbert Meilaender's warning that curiosity becomes a vice when driven by pride or the lust for power. René Belloq opens the Ark seeking a personal audience with God and is incinerated; Irina Spalko demands 'tell me everything you know' from the interdimensional beings at Akator and her eyes burn out; prudent Indy tells Marion 'Don't look, no matter what happens' and leaves before the beings' 'big gift' of knowledge. The chapter concludes that pride must give way to prudence when unlocking the secrets of the universe.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Can You Find Your Moral Compass
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Donovan and Richardson test Tony's moral compass in 'Armor Wars' and 'Extremis' against the three major schools. Utilitarianism fails because Tony will not sacrifice even one innocent for the greater good — he changes tactics to save a single pilot from the Raiders and rages when the Controller's human zombie dies — and Kantian deontology fails because Tony bends rules ('lives to mean more than rules') and is driven by emotion rather than pure reason. Aristotle fits: Tony is obsessed not just with doing good but with being good, snarling at his own reflection, asking filmmaker Pillinger 'Have you changed anything? Me neither,' until Extremis lets him 'be the Iron Man inside and out,' uniting agent and deed as Aristotelian character requires.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Relax, Tony—You’re Safe!
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Nielsen uses the unity-of-virtue thesis (UVT) to ask how morally flawed Tony can be a virtuous Iron Man. Plato's Meno and Laches — Nicias' 'thoughtful courage' versus mere rashness — explain why apparently brave villains like Doctor Doom, Iron Monger, and the Mandarin are actually fearless rather than courageous, while Aristotle's distinction between natural virtue and full virtue plus prudence explains how Tony can be courageous yet intemperate with alcohol and women. Susan Wolf's argument that practical knowledge is essentially unified justifies UVT while making perfect virtue an unreachable ideal, so flawed, striving Stark — unlike Doom — is about as virtuous as a human being gets.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: NOTES
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Taliaferro and Kastrul ask what the reader would do in the castaways' place, using Aristotle's view that character is a disposition to act under other conditions to assess Mr. Eko, Ben, Michael, Charlie, and Sawyer: people are not merely what they do but what they would do. Plato's Ring of Gyges, quoted at length, tests whether characters like Sun behave honestly only when watched. Against the idea that the island could reverse all values, they argue morality cannot be completely relative to context - invoking Chesterton's 'Thou shalt not steal' on the remotest star - and place Lost in the island-narrative tradition of the Odyssey and Robinson Crusoe as a story of the journey of the soul.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Real World Island
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Patricia Brace and Rob Arp argue Lost redeems characters who stop objectifying others and instead freely 'objectify' themselves for the greater good. Kant's ban on treating persons as mere means condemns Ben's lifelong manipulation and Ben's use of Sayid as an assassin, yet autonomy justifies chosen self-sacrifice like Charlie's Looking Glass suicide mission, Claire volunteering as bait for Ethan, and Jack becoming the new Jacob. Mill's utilitarianism makes Kate's shooting of the Man in Black a fair trade saving her friends, while Aristotle's virtues - respect against objectification, courage in Jack's death at the cliff, the engrained honesty of reformed con man Jim LaFleur, Kate's character-building motherhood of Aaron - complete the three-theory survey.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “All That Is Solid Melts into Air”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dunn reads Mad Men through Plato's Republic: the passions are the 'mad masters' Cephalus describes, embodied in Pete Campbell's au pair indiscretion and remorse, and because passions cannot tell staged appearance from reality, the mimetic perfection of Don's 'You're a whore' scene with Betty grips viewers exactly as Plato feared televised drama would, watering the parts of the soul that should be ruled. He extends the point to advertising: Don's 'I make pictures where people appear to be in love' and 'love was invented by guys like me to sell nylons' work because mimesis bypasses reason and attaches feeling to images, while Aristotle's account of imitation shows drama can also train virtue by making us delight in what we should. Marx and Engels' 'all that is solid melts into air' frames the title sequence, where Don's office dissolves past advertising images revealed as empty simulacra, until the final shot restores the convincing façade of his confidence.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “To a Place Where We Know We Are Loved”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Myers grades the moral development of the Sterling Cooper cast with Kohlberg's justice stages and Gilligan's ethics of care in order to find Aristotelian friendships, which require equals in moral development who wish each other good for the other's sake. Don and Peggy emerge as moral equivalents, each hiding a dark secret (the stolen identity; the baby given away) and each having done for the other what no one else could, from the hospital visit ('Move forward') to Don's 'nobody understands that, but you do' recruitment pitch; Joan and Roger form a second pair whose mutual esteem survives his marriage to Jane and her departure, shown when he trusts her to build Sterling Cooper Draper Pryce. Closing with Aristotle's claim that friendship holds states together, the chapter gives the new agency a better-than-average chance because these friendships are 'not for sale.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Whisper Things Into My Brain: Metallica, Emotion, and Morality
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Robert Fudge weighs whether Metallica's emotionally violent music corrupts or improves moral character. Against Plato's banishment of passion-stirring art (anger in 'Enter Sandman', indignation in '. . . And Justice for All'), he uses Aristotle's catharsis and the golden mean of healthy anger: 'One' purges pity and fear, and Hetfield's 'St. Anger' purged the rage behind his alcoholism. He then extends Adam Smith's empathy-based account - imaginative placement in the landmine victim's or addict's position - to argue the songs refine moral judgment, even making us question Kant's absolute duty against suicide by confronting the case where the body is a 'holding cell'.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Uses Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics account of wit as a character virtue lying in a mean to map the UK office: David Brent is the buffoon of excess, the 'slave of his sense of humor' who cannot not joke (the 'crack of Dawn' line, the cruel Post-It Notes firing prank on Dawn), Gareth Keenan the boor of deficiency whose literalism leaves him unable to make or take a joke, and Tim Canterbury the ready wit whose responsive irony ('Does anybody have the right time?') hits the mean. Because humor, like morality, is uncodifiable - there is no Having a Sense of Humor for Dummies - the trio illustrates that virtue is qualitative appropriateness guided by practical wisdom, not moderation or rule-following.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: It’s Good to Be a Fan if …
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Barrett uses Bill Swerski's Super Fans to map a spectrum of fandom from casual to moderate to Super Fan, then applies Aristotle's doctrine of the mean to the virtues and vices of fandom: knowing trivia is a virtue (the Trekkies sketch), admiring athletic excellence is noble, but excess becomes licentious obsession, Shatner's 'Get a life!', heart attacks at Ditka's, and spending Thanksgiving with da Bears instead of family. Deficiency appears in bandwagon fans who lack commitment and loyalty, and the Red Sox fans' hospitalized heartbreak shows misplaced priorities in grief. Moderate fandom, loyal to people first and teams second, is the virtuous mean.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Mussett asks whether Peter Parker's painful life counts as a good life by testing five philosophers' answers against the comics and films. Kurtz's secular humanism finds Peter wanting in pleasure and acclaim (Uncle Ben dead by his inaction, J. Jonah Jameson's smear campaigns), while Rand's Objectivism condemns Spider-Man as the embodiment of the 'morality of sacrifice' she rejected, noting Steve Ditko's Objectivist devotion. Epictetus scores Peter highly on duty but fails him on self-mastery, since his happiness hinges on attachments to Aunt May and MJ he cannot control; Frankl would see Peter's meaning in his irreplaceable responsibility, evidenced by his refusal of Dr. Judas Traveller's offer of a peaceful life at the cost of innocents (Amazing Spider-Man #402); and Aquinas vindicates Peter's suffering as good pain in a virtuous, charitable life.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Sanford argues, through the arc of the Raimi trilogy, that Peter becomes good by becoming the narrator of his own life. On Aristotle's Poetics — a story has a beginning, middle, and end, and art imitates life — and MacIntyre's claim that man is a 'story-telling animal' whose life is 'the unity of a narrative quest,' Peter's involuntary obligations (orphanhood, Uncle Ben's death, the spider bite, love for MJ) ground the voluntary ones, and his quest is to use his great powers responsibly. Tracking Aristotle's categories, Peter moves from incontinence (vengeance on Flint Marko, the jazz-club strut in Spider-Man 3) through continence to genuine virtue, and his practice of telling his own story — 'it's the choices that make us who we are' — models how we must get our own stories straight to flourish.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Eberl reads Jax's Season 5 dilemma (Tara's ultimatum to leave SAMCRO or lose his family) through Aristotle's account of virtue as character cultivated by habituation in a polis. SAMCRO nurtures genuine virtues—Opie's selfless loyalty, courage under fire, the club's communal generosity toward Donna and Lyla—alongside vices like Clay's greed and Tig's lust, with the golden mean distinguishing Bobby's critical loyalty from Chuckie's obsequiousness and Juice's rash minefield charge. Fr. Ashby's fight to keep Abel in Belfast away from Jax's cycle of violence, and the contrast between Deputy Chief Hale's law-abiding ideals and Mayor Hale's self-serving development, illustrate Aristotle's claim that legislators and environments make citizens good or bad. The chapter concludes that Jax's very mix of virtue and vice—the 'savage' needed to head the table—may be what reform requires, at moral cost.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Presents three ancient alternatives to SAMCRO's warrior ethic. Diogenes the Cynic, 'the earliest of all the fathers of anarchy,' matches J.T.'s Harley-commune ideal — reject greed, convention, and wage slavery like Tig punching the clock at Teller-Morrow — but the chapter argues pure anarchy regenerates hierarchy: with no authority, revenge becomes the only justice and 'a big guy like Clay' mugs 'a small guy like Chuckie.' Plato's Republic supplies the reformist pole — impartial justice for all citizens rather than loyalty circles, rulers picked from proven warriors for wisdom (Tara belongs healing, not scheming), family curbed where it breeds Gemma-style favoritism — yet proves too authoritarian, so Aristotle's function argument (reason as the human ergon), virtue, and the three kinds of friendship (SAMCRO's pleasure-friendships, Clay–Unser's usefulness) sketch a livable middle way with duties even to strangers.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jerold Abrams reads J. J. Abrams's Kirk as Aristotle's megalopsychos and 'god among men' from the Politics: too excellent to be a mere crewmember, disdainful of rank, speaking openly from love and hate, and a law unto himself. The four-on-one bar fight, reprogramming the unwinnable Kobayashi Maru, declaring 'Some should be' above the Prime Directive to Pike, and his exile to frozen Delta Vega (like the Argonauts stranding Heracles) all enact Aristotle's dilemma that a society must either exile such a man or submit to his monarchy. Spock, a great-souled man himself, becomes Kirk's 'second self' in Aristotle's truest friendship once Kirk takes the captain's chair.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Applies Aristotle's three friendships to Trek: Ferengi Rules of Acquisition dealings and treaties as utility friendships, Bashir and O'Brien's darts and racquetball as friendship of pleasure, and virtuous friendship as requiring emotion, mutual goodwill, and irreplaceable intrinsic valuing - which emotionless Data fails at with Jenna D'Sora in "In Theory". The core argument, following Badhwar, is that consequentialism is logically and psychologically incompatible with virtuous friendship: Spock's "needs of the many" maxim and Data's "for the greater good" experimentation on Geordi in "Descent, Part II" show friends being treated as sacrificeable instruments, while the Kobayashi Maru cheat shows consequentialist reasoning blessing outcomes over means. Kirk's reversal - "the needs of the one outweigh the needs of the many" in The Search for Spock - and T'Pol's years caring for the amnesiac Archer in "Twilight" exemplify acting out of friendship rather than for any further goal.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Jedi and Sith Ethics “Similar in Almost Every Way”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Shea, Archer, and Banning argue that Star Wars' moral framework is natural law ethics in the tradition of Aristotle and Aquinas: the light side humanizes (Force healing, Qui-Gon's spirit surviving death, Grogu curing Greef Karga) while the dark side dehumanizes (Maul's bisection, Palpatine's deformation, Anakin's disfigurement), and apparent counterexamples like Luke's lost hand always trace back to prior vice. Aquinas's claim that the most general principles of natural law can never be blotted out explains why 'there is still good in' Vader and why redemption is always possible. The Jedi and Sith codes embody opposed views of human nature — relational, altruistic, and accepting of mortality versus atomistic, egoistic, and obsessed with cheating death through midi-chlorian manipulation.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: A New Sound for Star Wars
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Belluomini applies Aristotle's Politics Book 8 - music imitates emotion and thereby forms character - to Ludwig Goransson's Mandalorian score, showing how the bass-recorder motif and the 'broken children's tune' of Grogu's Theme render the compassion and conflict Din hides beneath his helmet, from the hovercrib encounter to the mudhorn rescue. Because well-ordered, balanced emotional movements dispose listeners toward virtue, the swelling orchestral versions that score Din taming the blurrg or his rock-styled confidence in 'Mando is Back' cultivate the viewer's own courage, care, and honor alongside the show's moral argument. Aristotle's intellectual enjoyment - delight in the fit between music and imitated feeling - explains why Gorransson's thematic recall makes the season feel like one film, culminating in the farewell cue that ties Grogu's goodbye to their first meeting.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “And I, I'm All the Jedi!”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Okapal uses Aristotle's three friendships to frame the saga as a story of desert children seeking community: utility friendships like Hondo Ohnaka's and the Sith Rule of Two, where Darth Bane's apprentice is a mere instrument and Sidious calls Maul, Tyranus, and Vader 'easy to replace', stand against the other-regarding virtuous friendships of Obi-Wan, Kanan, and the Rey-Finn-Poe triad, where friends sacrifice for each other's sake as Ezra learns about Kanan in 'A World Between Worlds'. Luke's premature departure for Cloud City fails the 'for the other's sake' test Yoda poses. Rey can only choose the Jedi community knowingly once she learns she is Palpatine's granddaughter, and her closing claim 'I'm Rey Skywalker' is a choice between two value systems - the plural, other-regarding Jedi Code versus the self-regarding 'I' of the Sith Code - making friendship and community, not blood, the root of identity.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 9. Masks, Hearts, and Superheroes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Dupree and Fuš argue from identity statements: Bruce Wayne is 'just a mask' for Batman, while Clark Kent is in his heart Superman, so only an essentially human character can be a true superhero. On their Aristotelian definition — virtue ethics, the golden mean, flourishing through self-developed excellence — Batman's no-kill rule (sparing even the Joker), his planned avoidance of lethal force in Gotham Knights #31, and his balance against extremes make him the true hero, whereas Superman's given god-powers (killing Zod in Man of Steel, tyrant in Red Son) mirror power rings as Gyges's ring: possession without earned virtue.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Forte maps the Richmond cast onto Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: Rebecca, Nate, Roy, and Jamie begin incontinent or near-vicious; courage is the mean between Nate's cowardice and Roy's rashness; and their friendless misery illustrates why friendship (utility, pleasure, complete) is necessary for eudaimonia. Ted's coaching works as a modern strengths-based complement to Aristotelian habituation - Phoebe's Princess-and-Dragon play tempers Roy, Jamie's competitiveness is redirected into team play, Nate misses the mean and becomes mean - and the finale's 'progress over perfection' framing shows all of them as works in progress toward teloi.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Arvan argues the show is really about positive masculinity - what it is to be a good man - read through Aristotle's virtue ethics: toxic masculinity (Rupert's domination, Jamie Sr.'s abuse, Nate's cruelty, Ted's suffer-in-silence self-reliance) is vice at an extreme, while the show's good men hit the golden mean by 'womaning up.' Led Tasso works as context-appropriate toughness, Roy's hug of Jamie and the darts speech's 'be curious, not judgmental' blend masculine and feminine virtues, phronesis is learned from experience as Beard teaches Nate forgiveness, and even Rupert's downfall shows vice backfiring as Aristotle predicts.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Belluomini argues the show's score and soundtrack do genuine aesthetic and moral work, applying Aristotle's Politics Book VIII claim that music imitates emotion and disposes us toward virtue. He analyzes Celeste's 'Strange' narrating the divorce-signing and intercut romances, 'Wise Up' underscoring Rebecca's brave break with John Wingsnight, 'Piano Joint' carrying Rebecca's confession to Ted, 'She's a Rainbow' scoring Roy's run back to Nelson Road, 'Roy Walk Off' as a Jaws-style sentimental motif, and 'Spiegel im Spiegel' under Rebecca's anti-Super-League speech, closing with Schopenhauer's point that fitting music is a scene's most accurate commentary.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “See, This Dame Walks In”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Catlyn Origitano sorts Veronica's relationships through Aristotle's three kinds of friendship in the Nicomachean Ethics: Keith and Cliff McCormack's referral exchange is a friendship of utility, Logan and Dick's partying a friendship of pleasure, and Wallace's bond with Veronica utility fraying into his complaint 'How about you do me a favor for once?' when reciprocity turns one-sided. Perfect friendship of virtue requires mutual trust between genuinely good people, and the chapter's audit finds no one qualifies — Wallace lies and cheats, Logan supplied the GHB and ran from the Tijuana fire, and Veronica's snooping and 'I'm not built that way' refusal to trust disqualify her too. She concludes that noir Neptune itself, where 'the people you love let you down,' may block perfect friendship, though the movie-era Veronica, retired from detection, might at last be ready for one.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Rard tests whether any morality survives the apocalypse with an objective basis: Plato's Forms fail to capture changing facts (Hannah the bicycle girl decaying from mom to walker) and white lies, and Aristotle's function-based virtue ethics proves too relative and luck-dependent for survivors like Rick (rashness at Carl's shooting) and Shane (courage fetching supplies, rage at the barn). Nietzsche then supplies the frame: Hershel's barn of pitied 'sick people' is Christian slave morality that guilts the strong, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and forcing open of the barn doors grope toward a master morality 'for the Walker Age' without ever achieving nobility. Rick alone approaches the higher type, refusing to judge Lori's affair, insisting the baby be born, and embracing the post-walker world as one he would choose again.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: P A R T T W O
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Three Part Two essays. Robert Loftis argues Moore and Gibbons use Ozymandias's squid attack to indict consequentialism — Veidt uses New York's dead as mere means to world peace, and Dr. Manhattan's 'Nothing ever ends' shows the utilitarian ledger dissolves into an infinite future — while Rorschach's 'never compromise' mantra is a counterfeit deontology rationalizing fascist thuggery, the comic's real target being anyone who sets himself up as guardian of society ('Who watches the watchmen?'). Mark White argues the potbellied second Nite Owl is the truest hero on Aristotelian terms: his courage in the tenement fire and the prison break hits the mean between Laurie's caution and Rorschach's recklessness, making him a flourishing moral exemplar whom John Doris's situationism fails to unseat. Alex Nuttall asks whether Rorschach was wrong to walk out and expose Veidt, using Kant's murderer-at-the-door case to show there is a duty not to lie but no duty to tell the truth (blame falls on Veidt), while act and rule utilitarianism both counsel silence.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Buddha ex Machina
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Siobhan Lyons applies Mori's 'uncanny valley' to the hosts' physical and personality evolution (Ford's jerky old model versus seamless newer hosts, Maeve and Clementine), noting empathy grows as they near sentience. She argues via Aristotle's account of virtue, vice, and brutality that the guests and technicians (Logan's casual cruelty, the Man in Black's beastly sadism) fall short of human excellence while the suffering, consciousness-seeking hosts transcend it, treating humanity as a way of behaving rather than being, and casting the hosts as Derridean undecidables. Invoking Nietzsche on suffering as the cultivator of greatness and Mori's 'Buddha in the robot,' she claims the hosts earn a humanity the biological humans merely inherit.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “I Always Felt this Place was Missing a Real Villain. Hence, My Humble Contribution.”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Jason Eberl argues Westworld cultivates real moral character: using Aristotle's account of virtue and vice as habituated dispositions, he shows William's thirty years of habitual killing make the Man in Black his genuine 'second nature,' not merely a vacation persona, citing Aquinas and Kant on how cruelty to animals (or human-like hosts) hardens moral character. Drawing on Frankfurt's second-order desires and narrative identity, he contends Maeve attains personhood by reprogramming her own first-order desires, while Ford views most humans as wantons trapped in first-order loops. He concludes the park can both corrupt (William) and potentially free hosts to flourish as self-authoring persons rather than devolve into wantons whose 'violent delights have violent ends.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Origin and Desires as Monster Makers in the Witcher
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Swanstrom and Lyle test medieval theories of monstrosity against the show: Stregobor's Curse of the Black Sun echoes Aristotle's, Avicenna's, and Aquinas's celestial-influence explanations of fetal mutation (though even they would not convict Renfri by birthday alone), while Yennefer's spine and infertility invoke Aquinas on failed generation and women as 'deformed males,' with witchers cast as Aquinas's mules - an engineered, infertile natural kind. They argue that neither origin nor appearance but motivation and virtue make a monster: Renfri's revenge, Nivellen's rape of the priestess, and Stregobor's vivisection of girls are Aristotelian 'bestial' habit and vicious character, not mean-relative virtue. Geralt's shifting telos, from monster-slayer protecting humans to protector of Ciri (knighted by Queen Meve), shows even a mutant can develop virtue, so mutations, heritage, and gender cannot be what monstrosity is.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Notes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: A mother-daughter pair tracks Wonder Woman's and Harley Quinn's costume histories (the 1990s Artemis-era near-thong Diana, the New 52 brothel-styled Harley) and argues with Aristotle that sexualized drawing strips both characters of phronesis, the practical wisdom a virtuous agent needs - the wisdom by which an outmatched Wonder Woman talks Strife into carrying her to safety and Harley exploits the Joker's vanity to beat him. The paradox: the more provocatively each is drawn, the less she can succeed as moral hero or anti-hero, since objectification replaces goal-directed cunning with one-dimensional sex display. The New 52's armor-clad, Hephaestus-consulting Wonder Woman shows phronesis restored.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: To Hack or Not to Hack
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Kennedy asks how a great player like Kareem (the NBA's career foul leader) can be excellent while fouling so much, and answers that deontology (Kant's categorical imperative) and utilitarianism (Mill's greatest-happiness principle) can condemn dangerous 'goon' fouling but cannot explain why the legal Hack-a-Shaq strategy still feels 'clownish.' Invoking Shaq's self-nickname 'the Big Aristotle,' he argues Aristotelian virtue ethics fits better: the excellent player, like the person of good character, perceives the situation rightly and fouls (or risks a foul) at the right time in the right way, so excellence is a habit of seeing well rather than rule-following.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Hardwood Dojos
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Bassham and Hamilton distill six success principles from coaches Smith, Pitino, Summitt, and Krzyzewski and show each echoes great philosophers, treating the court as a 'dojo' or place of enlightenment. Setting goals and pursuing excellence through habit map to Aristotle's eudaimonia and doctrine of habituation (Shaq the 'Big Aristotle' given the Nicomachean Ethics by Phil Jackson); the emphasis on outworking adversity and controlling only one's own effort maps to Stoics like Seneca, Epictetus, and Marcus Aurelius, as when Summitt and Dean Smith tell players to control what they can and accept the rest.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Zen Master and the Big Aristotle
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Allhoff and Vaidya argue against the skeptic that philosophy is useless 'bullshit' (nodding to Frankfurt's book) by showing how Phil Jackson's coaching applies it. Jackson's Zen Buddhism, especially zazen meditation and selfless 'triangle offense' play, teaches players to empty the ego and stay in the present, transforming Jordan from point-maker to play-maker; and Jackson's gift of Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics to Shaquille O'Neal, who then dubbed himself 'the Big Aristotle,' illustrates Aristotle's doctrine that excellence (his improved free-throw shooting, his generosity) is a habit built by repetition.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Plato and Aristotle on the Role of Soul in Taking the Rock to the Hole
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Daniel Gallagher reads Patrick Sparks's 2005 Elite Eight free-throw clank and miracle buzzer-beater through Plato's tripartite soul: the rational part failed at the line but the spirited part carried the off-balance game-tying three, while the Republic's three classes map onto basketball's workers (Steve Nash's passes), warriors (Dennis Rodman's rebounding), and rulers (John Stockton's leadership). Aristotle's four character types structure learning a jump shot - vicious, weak, self-controlled, and finally virtuous, as reason and inclination harmonize through repetition ('we are what we repeatedly do') - and the golden mean governs shot selection between the ball hog and the compulsive passer, with Michael Jordan as the player whose habituated instincts find the mean. Against Kantian armchair ethics, the jump shot and Kareem's sky hook were discovered by trial and error: virtuous performers set the standard, and we become good shooters by watching and imitating them.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Hoosiers and the Meaning of Life
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Michael Peterson argues that Hoosiers is a microcosm of life's meaning: Aristotle's eudaimonia frames the characters' searches (Norman Dale rebuilding his career, Shooter his self-esteem and his bond with son Everett), and Dale's 'in my book, we're going to be winners' speech shows that character, unselfish teamwork, and playing to potential - virtue learned by doing, as coaching models moral instruction - matter more than the scoreboard against South Bend Central. The film's second chances (Principal Summers's clean slate, Whit's return, Dale's hiring of the town drunk Shooter) reveal that character alone is insufficient: mercy and forgiveness, which Hannah Arendt traces to Jesus, reframe an unchangeable past and open a future. Peterson then surveys worldviews - naturalism (Bertrand Russell's 'accidental collocations of atoms'), postmodernism (Derrida's deconstruction), Hinduism's Atman-Brahman - and argues only Christian theism, in which God's nature is love (Aquinas), can ground the character and forgiveness the film dramatizes.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Michael Austin argues that a truly Olympic greatness requires moral, not merely athletic, excellence, reading Aristotle's magnanimity (megalopsychia, 'greatness of soul') as the crowning virtue that unifies all others. He tests this against three Olympians: bobsledder Eugenio Monti, who lent a rival team a part and lost gold; sprinter Wilma Rudolph, who forced her homecoming parade to be integrated; and runner Emil Zatopek, who gave away his gold medal and defied the Soviet invasion of Prague. Using Robert Adams's idea of 'modules of virtue,' he explains why some champions show self-control in sport but not in life, whereas the magnanimous person holds every virtue across every domain.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Through an imagined Greek play featuring the Spartan 'trembler' Aristodemus and an Avery-Brundage-like IOC president, Jesus Ilundain-Agurruza argues for rethinking the Olympic motto and creed around three Greek virtues, aretE (excellence), andreia (courage), and kalon (noble beauty), grounded in Aristotle's virtue ethics, the mean, and eudaimonia. Using the Spartans exercising on the eve of Thermopylae, he defends a collaborative, non-instrumental conception of competition against record-obsession and cheating, exemplified by Eugenio Monti and Cecil Healy. He closes with Camus's Sisyphus, arguing the athlete pushes the rock in the spirit of aretE, spending energy joyfully 'just because,' turning punishment into sport.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Heather Reid interprets the Olympic Charter's first Fundamental Principle through the ancient ideal of aretE, arguing the metaphysical structure of sport, contests that create purposeless obstacles, exists to cultivate and celebrate human excellence rather than to beat opponents or make money. Citing Plato the wrestler, Suits's definition of game-playing, and Homer's funeral games, she maps five virtues onto sport: eusEbeia (reverence for ideals beyond oneself), andreia (courageous endurance in agOn), sOphrosynE (harmonious power and control), dikaiosynE (justice as rule-order and proper function), and sophia (the athlete's pursuit of truth about human capacity, akin to 'flow'). The goal she proposes is the 'Olympian soul.'

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Grinnell applies Aristotle's classification of friendship (utility, pleasure, and complete character-friendship between equals in excellence) to Million Dollar Baby and Gran Torino. Frankie/Maggie and Walt/Thao begin as incomplete, utility relationships across barriers of age, sex, and culture, then ripen into character-friendships of 'other selves' who pursue each other's good. He resolves the apparent paradox that friendship demands bringing about a death: Frankie euthanizes Maggie against his own wishes to honor her autonomy and whole-life excellence, while Walt engineers his own death and deceives Thao to spare him a vengeance that would destroy his character — each an Aristotelian sacrifice of self-interest for the friend that preserves the friendship's excellence.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Right and the Good without God
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter builds the case that Whedon's fiction grounds ethics without God: Foy's Lockean social-contract reading of the Firefly crew and Kant's person-as-end analysis explain why Mal insists Saffron is 'not to be bought' in 'Our Mrs. Reynolds' and why Loki's possession of Hawkeye and Jasmine's enthrallment of her worshippers are the Whedonverse's paradigm wrongs. Spike's arc—from selfish ally, through the 'Triangle' troll fight and 'Intervention' torture, to the 'Chosen' sacrifice—is read through Aristotelian habituation into virtue, while Angel's Darla-arc firing of Team Angel and the Better Days temple-money and Inara plots show where respecting rights and being a good person can come apart. Finally the Euthyphro dilemma, plus replies to Pojman and Craig (self-sacrifice is not 'stupid'), argue that Angel's 'Epiphany' ethic—doing what matters with no glorious end or divine reward—shows morality is neither arbitrary nor motivationally crippled without God.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Not the Crime, but the Man Sherlock Holmes and Charles Augustus Milverton
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Rozema examines 'The Adventure of Charles Augustus Milverton,' in which Holmes burgles a blackmailer's house, feigns an engagement to the maid, and watches Milverton's murder without intervening. He argues that Kantian deontology (too abstract to judge rectification) and consequentialism (paralyzed by unpredictable outcomes) both fail to assess Holmes's acts, whereas Plato and Aristotle's virtue ethics fits: judging the man's character over the isolated act. Citing Plato's 'true falsehood' vs. 'falsehood in words' and Aristotle on voluntary acts and the storm-tossed captain jettisoning cargo, he concludes a virtuous person may rightly do what is normally forbidden against a vicious foe like Milverton.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Aristotle and MacIntyre on Justice in 25th Hour
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Conard uses Lee's 25th Hour to test Aristotle's claim that justice is inseparable from community and necessary for eudaimonia, and MacIntyre's charge that liberal individualist society lacks any common good. Comparing the greedy Wall Street broker Frank (an Aristotelian overreacher driven by pleonexia) with the drug dealer Monty (fairer, though convicted under unjust Rockefeller laws), he argues Monty is not unjust yet still cannot flourish in a fragmented New York. Monty's profane bathroom 'fuck you' soliloquy dramatizes the city's incommensurable values, while the post-9/11 fellow-feeling offers a fleeting glimpse of the shared good MacIntyre says modern society lacks.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Sanders reads Kubrick's heist film The Killing through Stoic ethics, casting Johnny Clay (Sterling Hayden) as a member of the 'cult of the cool' whose reticence and final resigned 'What's the difference?' surrender embody apatheia and acceptance of fate/logos. He tests Spencer Selby's claim that Clay and the sharpshooter Nikki must fail because their motives are immoral, arguing instead via an Aristotelian principle (virtues are stable dispositions) that their sudden lapses—the flimsy suitcase, Nikki's racial slur that loses him the lucky horseshoe—are Kubrick stacking the deck rather than genuine character. He closes by weighing Clay's life against models of a meaningful life (exuberance/romanticism vs. rationalism/self-fulfillment), faulting Clay for never subjecting his chosen ends to self-critical reason.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Action and Integrity in The Fugitive
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Skoble challenges the standard view of noir as morally ambiguous, arguing each episode of The Fugitive is a self-contained morality play in which Richard Kimble makes tough decisions by clearly defined standards of right and wrong. He tests ethical frameworks against the episodes: Kant's categorical imperative cannot capture Kimble, who lies in every episode to survive, whereas Aristotle's virtue ethics explains his trained emotional responses, as when he tells the migrant workers in 'Ill Wind' 'For a doctor, every life is worth saving' while saving Lieutenant Gerard from a pitchfork, and again in 'Corner of Hell' from moonshiners. Kimble's integrity, understood as fidelity in action to principles reached through reflection, reconciles his lawbreaking with his morality and, via Plato's account in the Republic of the just person who 'harmonizes the three parts of himself,' constitutes the psychological wholeness that sustains his four-year quest. The essay closes with the finale, where Kimble clears his name, Gerard kills the one-armed man, and Kimble finally walks in sunlight.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Civilization and Its Discontents The Self-Sufficient Western Hero
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Den Uyl builds a composite philosophic picture of self-sufficiency from Aristotle's autarkeia (reason-guided virtuous activity, requiring external goods and civilization) and Spinoza's freedom as acting from one's own nature guided by adequate ideas, then tests it on John Ford's heroes. In The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance, Tom Doniphon is 'procedurally' self-sufficient in the precivilized West while Ransom Stoddard embodies civilized reason, and neither can inhabit the other's world. He argues the western's deepest value is Emersonian self-reliance—fidelity to one's own unique nature (the 'cactus rose')—which civilization threatens even as it enables Aristotelian flourishing.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: From Dollars to Iron The Currency of Clint Eastwood's Westerns
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: McNaron traces Clint Eastwood's evolving western hero from the amoral 'Man with No Name' to The Outlaw Josey Wales, using Will Wright's plot typology plus Nietzsche, Aristotle, and Kierkegaard. He reads the Eastwood antihero's 'manly nihilism' and prizing of strength and style through Nietzsche's master/slave morality and perspectivism, his virtues (self-control, phronesis) through Aristotle, and his elevation of the aesthetic over the ethical/religious against Kierkegaard's stages. The film's central claim—that only words with 'iron' behind them (Josey and Ten Bears's pact) can found genuine community, unlike government's 'double tongues'—grounds a transcendental argument about the conditions for authentic community and justified vengeance.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: The Cost of the Code Ethical Consequences in High Noon and The Ox-Bow Incident
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Ken Hada reads High Noon and The Ox-Bow Incident through Nussbaum's neo-Aristotelian critique of Kantian duty. Will Kane's absolute, self-sacrificing return to face Frank Miller and Major Tetley's honor-bound insistence on hanging the accused both exemplify the Kantian categorical imperative applied without regard to consequences. The essay argues that the films themselves undermine this code: Kane's triumph brings no joy and Tetley's rigid 'reason' masks self-interest and produces the lynching of three innocent men. Following Nussbaum, it holds that attention to particulars, emotion, and social context—embodied by Davies in Ox-Bow—yields more just moral perception than blind allegiance to an absolute rule.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: Is Oskar Schindler a Good Man
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Ebertz treats Schindler's List as a thought experiment on what makes a person good, judging Oskar Schindler against Kantian and virtue-ethical standards. On Kant he fails: many acts (lying, bribery, infidelity) violate the categorical imperative, and even his rescues spring from growing partial attachment to 'his Jews' rather than rational duty or a good will. On Aristotelian virtue ethics he only selectively exercises virtues, so is not fully 'good' either; Ebertz resolves the tension with a Principle of Moral Exemplarity, holding Schindler up as a flawed but genuine moral example whose care promotes human flourishing.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: “So You Can Be My ‘John G.’”
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Eberl asks whether Leonard Shelby is morally culpable for killing Teddy, since the Leonard who tattoos the false clue and the Leonard who pulls the trigger are sundered by anterograde amnesia. Locke's forensic, memory-based concept of personhood suggests the shooting Leonard is not the same person as the one who set the trap, while Aquinas's analysis of concomitant, consequent, and antecedent ignorance makes Leonard culpable for deliberately willing his own ignorance yet not for the amnesiac moment of the killing itself. Hume's causal criterion of psychological continuity explains why Leonard can still rationally set a goal for his future self by making Teddy his 'John G.' The chapter closes on Aristotle: Leonard's ease in framing an innocent man betrays a corrupted moral character built on habit, and by turning himself into a 'living instrument'—Aristotle's definition of a slave—he has traded his dignity for the telos of an endless revenge quest.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: I Am the Bad Wolf
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Roman Altshuler answers Davros's charge that the Doctor is a 'destroyer of worlds' using Aristotelian virtue ethics. He argues the Doctor's chief virtue is not compassion but Heideggerian 'authentic concern': offering aggressors (the Nestene, Sontarans, the Master) a genuine choice so they become responsible for escalating, illustrated by the fly-swatter thought experiment. Companions, being 'another self' (Aristotle on friendship), make their acts partly the Doctor's own, yet their human 'Bad Wolf Syndrome' lets compassion override the impartial concern that requires respecting choice, which is why the Doctor runs from what his companions do in his name.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 10. Cas Is Family
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Doll traces Castiel's arc from a cold Divine-Command/utilitarian 'hammer of the Lord' to a member of the Winchester family through Aristotle's ethics. She argues Cas learns to contemplate and act on the chief good under Dean's tutelage, pursuing eudaimonia by habituation despite repeated failures (becoming a false god, the Leviathans), and that his bond with Sam and Dean grows through Aristotle's three friendships—utility, pleasure, and finally the rare true friendship of virtuous character—culminating in his self-sacrificing declaration of love that defeats Billie.

aristotle-virtue-ethics.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
aristotle-virtue-ethics.title: 30. Good Guys Don’t Wear White
aristotle-virtue-ethics.relation: Lindsey Schwartz argues punk is virtue ethics in action: a DIY version of Aristotle's account of becoming virtuous through practice, habituation, and practical wisdom, where no one ever simply IS good and the point is perpetual becoming.
