aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Robison-Greene asks whether there are principled standards for 'shipping' TV couples and applies Platonic-Aristotelian flourishing criteria (long-term safety, emotional needs, trust, and mutual growth toward virtue) to Piper's options: Alex fails on safety and trust (selling Piper out, the perjury advice), Larry fails on empathy and growth, so by real-life standards we should ship none of them. She concludes shipping is mostly aesthetic, then proposes minimal moral rules for our attitudes toward fictional relationships: never ship Pornstache, respect consent, and never let race, gender, or orientation decide.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 17. The Friends of a Time Lord
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Littmann applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics taxonomy of friendship - pleasure, usefulness, and mutual goodness - to fifty years of Doctor-companion pairings, from the Hartnell Doctor's glee touring Vortis with Ian to New Series companions chosen as friends who routinely save the day, from Barbara's Dalek revolt to Clara saving every incarnation of the Doctor. He argues Aristotle would still judge the Doctor's friendships defective: they are short-lived, unequal in station, intellect, and morality, and the companions cannot know him well enough (not even his name) for the perfect friendship of the good. Littmann then corrects Aristotle on two counts: friends need not be moral experts to serve as moral critics (Rose in 'Dalek,' Amy in 'A Town Called Mercy'), and the Doctor's favoritism toward his companions - risking worlds to save them, as when Rory weighs Amy's life against the universe in 'The Big Bang' - shows that preferring friends over strangers is itself his most frequent moral failing.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 5. Overcoming Evil with Love
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Bogosian argues the film locates evil not in human nature itself, as Jeanine claims when she calls human nature 'the enemy,' but in cultivable vices - Al's jealousy and fear of failure leading to attempted murder and suicide, Eric's and Jeanine's lust for power - and that only altruistic, self-sacrificial love can counteract them. With Aristotle's point that friendship is essential to developing virtue and to the good life, he shows the faction system fails on its own terms: a single virtue in isolation corrupts (Candor's truth without kindness), and a system that removes real moral and political freedom destroys the flourishing it promises. Tris's parents' sacrifices and the Tris-Four relationship - honest training advice, protection of her Divergence, and the gun-to-her-own-forehead scene where love breaks the simulation's grip - model the love that overcomes the corrupt system.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 18. The Virtues of Choosing Your Faction
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Pascoe contrasts Aristotle's and Kant's theories of virtue through the Choosing Ceremony. On Aristotle's account virtues are taught (intellectual) and then habituated into character (moral), tied to one's function, so Susan flourishes because aptitude, upbringing, and choice align while the transfer Al withers - but Tris, Divergent with multiple aptitudes, needs Kant instead: natural virtues are mere 'gifts of nature' that become good only through good will, and her perfect duties to herself and imperfect duties regarding family and faction can justify choosing Dauntless over staying in Abnegation. Kant wins the day: because a corrupted community like Eric's Dauntless redefines bravery into obedience, Tris must think for herself - 'maybe I am wired like the Divergent' - choosing her virtues out of duty and self-respect rather than inheriting them.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 4. Finding One’s Place and Being Useful
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Karavitis argues that work, not social class, is Downton's real theme, sorting characters in a two-by-two matrix of class membership against acceptance or rejection of the existing social order. Those who accept their place stagnate - Violet ('We don't work,' 'What is a weekend?'), Robert the mismanaging custodian, the perpetually jobless Molesley - while those who reject it flourish: Isobel's drive to be 'useful,' Sybil's nursing ('I feel useful for the first time in my life'), Gwen's hidden typewriter, Alfred's Ritz training. He surveys Rousseau on work's role in inequality, Smith on the division of labor, and Marx on labor and ideology on the negative side, and Aristotle, Russell's 'In Praise of Idleness,' and Pieper on leisure and personal projects on the positive side, ending with the prediction that automation will soon give everyone the Crawley daughters' problem of what to do with a life without work.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 18. Doctor, Heal Thyself
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: McClelland argues Lecter is a flawed healer: reading Starling's FBI disgrace as social exclusion, he shows how Lecter's hypnotic drugs and deep-hypnosis 'treatment' let her revisit and metabolize her repressed rage at her dead father — the parental imago he named back in Silence of the Lambs — producing a chrysalis-like metamorphosis completed when she defies Krendler at the dinner and asks for more of his brains. The healing is symmetric, since Starling's insight into Lecter's own Mischa fixation releases him too, and the chapter closes with an Aristotelian verdict — choice reveals character, and whether the couple's Buenos Aires partnership counts as good depends on long-term flourishing we have not yet seen.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 5. Back from the Dead
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Devlin and Cooper trace Rick's moral arc as a struggle between Mill-style consequentialism - twisted by the apocalypse into a 'Greatest Survival Principle' of mere survival (Dawn Lerner's Grady, Enid's 'JSS') - and Aristotelian virtue ethics. Shane's murder of Otis, the Governor's rule over Woodbury and killing of Martinez and Pete, and Terminus's cannibalism all show survival-only reasoning dissolving humanity, a decline the show underlines with literal mirror reflections of Shane as a walker. Rick falls after killing Shane and nearly trades Michonne to the Governor, is brought back by Lori's judging vision and the sight of Carl going cold, and reclaims virtues as habits grown like Hershel's seeds - 'We get to come back' (4.8 'Too Far Gone') - though Seasons 4 and 5 leave him balancing a harder character, down to 'We didn't want to waste the bullets,' with the drive to survive.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 12. Should I Really Stop That Rhyming
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Yuen uses the rhyming scene to analyze annoyance - rhyme hijacks Vizzini's attention, the Goldman/Morgenstern interruptions betray invested expectations, and fans' endless quotation is annoying through sheer repetition - concluding that annoyance is irreducibly relative and contextual. Aristotle's virtue theory supplies the moral frame: friendliness and wittiness, golden means between obsequiousness and surliness, buffoonery and boorishness, make being annoying a character flaw that damages the communal eudaimonia Aristotle takes the good life to require. Since these virtues may be supererogatory ideals rather than obligations, Yuen borrows Kant's imperfect duty to develop one's talents to explain why Inigo had to become a master swordsman - failing to hone the skill his one great goal demands would be a failure of self-respect.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 14. The End of Inigo Montoya
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Elsby and Luzecky read Inigo through Aristotle's doctrine of the four causes: his life is organized by a final cause, revenge on the Six-Fingered Man as the thing that is 'just good', which explains every action from fencing drills to eating breakfast. The famous mantra works because habit embodies the final cause - repeating 'My name is Inigo Montoya' lets trained movement carry him through wounds that should end the fight. When revenge is achieved the chain of ends terminates and 'Inigo Montoya' ends with it, which is why his rebirth as the Dread Pirate Roberts is needed; the chapter generalizes that our habits, not grand outside purposes, are how final causes give lives their ends.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 8. Should Jane Get to Be Bored
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Daniel Addison defends Louie's 'you don't get to be bored' admonishment of Jane in 'Country Drive' against Mathew Remski's charge that it transfers adult anxiety, pointing to Louis's Conan 'forever empty' monologue and reddit advice as proof that Louis insists on facing despair rather than fleeing it. The real aim, he argues, is Socratic: Louis wants Jane and the plane-complaining generation brought to aporia, the perplexity Plato's Socrates induces in the Meno's slave boy so that, no longer thinking he knows, he 'would be glad to find out.' Aristotle grounds the optimism - every human by nature desires to know, philosophy begins in wonder, and our deepest happiness lies in contemplating - so Louis's 'everything's amazing' tirade is a demand that we become philosophical rather than 'kinda satisfied' consumers. Boredom, on this reading, is failed wonder, and Louie is playing Socrates to his daughter.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 3. When Clone Club Looks for Answers
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Maps two ancient accounts of happiness onto the two clones we meet first. Cosima is the Aristotelian: like her fellow biologist Aristotle she holds that knowing truth for its own sake is essential to human flourishing, so she demands Sarah's briefcase ("the answers are in the briefcase"), studies a murdered sister's autopsy, and accepts Leekie's offer of unfettered research even inside Dyad. Alison is the Epicurean: happiness is the removal of pain and protection from threat, so she wants nothing to do with the C-word, hunts her monitor only to restore her safety, and signs Leekie's contract for the promise that her family will be left alone.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 14. Re Production
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Framed as leaked Project memoranda, the chapter argues Projects Leda and Castor embody philosophy's male-rational/female-reproductive dichotomy: Aristotle's function argument defined the human good (eudaimonia) through rationality while relegating women to reproduction, and the clones' engineered diseases literalize the split — fatal illness of the reproductive organs in the Leda clones, of the brain in the Castor. Simone de Beauvoir's Second Sex supplies the critique: "woman" treated as synonymous with womb, the Other denied the rich self-definition granted men, visible in Leda's passive unmonitored clones versus Castor's self-aware, active brothers. Combining a redeemed Aristotle (practical wisdom shows virtuous potential is not set by biological sex) with Beauvoir's free, independent woman, the chapter concludes both reproductive and rational autonomy must be restored to the clones of both sexes.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 7. Jon Snow, a Misshapen Christ Figure
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Rosa argues Westeros is a moral wasteland stripped of exemplars - heroes die, and vice spreads by imitation, as with Joffrey, Ramsay, and the Mountain - so Jon Snow functions as the series' Christ figure: the humble hidden king revealed in Bran's vision, the reformer uniting wildlings and Watch against death, killed by his brothers in 'Mother's Mercy' and risen in 'Home.' Using Aristotle's virtue ethics - Bran's archery lesson as the image of eudaimonia, hamartia as missing the mark, character formed by watching and imitating exemplars like Ned at the deserter's execution - the chapter claims the world is redeemable only through 'minority moral reform' embodied in a complete life, as with Jesus, Gandhi, and Martin Luther King Jr.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 29. The Best of Friends
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Geyer sorts Game of Thrones friendships by Aristotle's three kinds in the Nicomachean Ethics. Robert and Ned's bond, formed in Jon Arryn's fosterage and shared war, is friendship of pleasure, which frays over Rhaegar's 'dragonspawn'; Tyrion and Bronn is friendship of utility, dissolving exactly as Aristotle predicts when Lollys's marriage pays better than a trial by combat in 'Mockingbird'; and Jon and Sam, each valuing the other's character for its own sake at the Wall, approach the only true friendship - the virtue friendship - supporting the claim that eudaimonia needs such relationships alongside external goods.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 3. Can Charlie Brown Be Happy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The chapter asks why Charlie Brown is unhappy despite being kind, active, and engaged, and answers with ancient virtue ethics: happiness is not winning or approval but ethical self-transformation, so his dependence on others' regard ('How did the other team feel?') is the real problem. It diagnoses him with Daniel Haybron's three dimensions of happiness - strong on engagement but lacking attunement (nervous, self-conscious) and endorsement (cheerlessness) - and asks why his shyness so irritates the gang. Epictetus's image of Socrates playing ball at his trial and Cicero's dancing analogy supply the Stoic remedy: losing costs no virtue, what he controls is being ethical, and how you play the game is everything.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 15. Reset Virtues
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Doll argues Elliot approximates Aristotelian virtue despite his vices: he craves eudaimonia, uses practical wisdom to recognize the harm the 5/9 hack caused innocent people ('I'll own it all'), and habituates himself against vice by confessing, exposing Ray's website, and restraining Mr. Robot even at the cost of Adderall binges and prison. Leon's 'existence could be beautiful, or it could be ugly, but that's on you' frames the choice of a life to fight for, and Krista's counsel leads Elliot to the golden mean of a 'handshake' with Mr. Robot - integrating the two identities rather than annihilating one - while the viewer serves as the if/then programming keeping him virtuous.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 13. Burn the Witch!
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Argues Coven is a feminist counterpoint to Aquinas's Natural Law - the reason-grounded doctrine of universal human nature historically wielded against 'unnatural' women, from Zoe's vagina-dentata power to Misty burned in the bayou - and, drawing on Augustine's Confessions ('Things that exist are good', so corruptibility implies goodness to lose) and Lady Macbeth's 'unsex me here', shows that women who are both witch and woman break any single natural moral code; Myrtle Snow, who embraces her double nature and goes 'proudly to the flame', proves Natural Law works only as Cupp-style discernment, not as commandments.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 2. Physical Jerks Ungood
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Di Nucci compares the Party's mandatory morning Physical Jerks to the modern middle-class ritual of pre-work exercise, asking who needs an oppressor when we oppress ourselves. He argues exercise carries a hidden political price: the time, energy, and solitude it consumes (Orwell shows exercise making it harder for Winston to think and remember) leave citizens too exhausted for the political engagement Aristotle considered necessary to the good life. Like Juvenal's bread and circuses, now 'panem et iphones', and like private schooling, fitness culture also deepens class inequality because working-class people lack the time and energy to access it.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 8. Human Enhancement for Freedom
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Koï asks whether biomedical enhancement could make humans resistant to the totalitarian subjugation shown in 1984, where the Party keeps proles too poor and distracted to think and dims Outer Party minds with Newspeak, erased history, and propaganda. Testing Persson and Savulescu's program of enhancing intelligence and moral empathy, she finds intelligence enhancement an educated gamble, since the gifted are also the most likely to embrace extremism and to start totalitarian movements, and empathy politically selective: Nazis directed it only at the in-group and even invoked it to justify the 'euthanasia' murders, while Party propaganda exploits citizens' empathy for horror stories of pre-revolution child labor. Her conclusion is that whatever capacity we enhance, the oligarchy could turn it to its own use: none of us will ever be immune to the love of Big Brother.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 12. Dilbert Is an Asshole and That’s Why He’ll Never Be Happy and Nobody Loves Him
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Elsby and Luzecky argue Dilbert's unhappiness is chosen: from 400 rejections he concludes the women lack quality, he calls insult-bombing gentle kidding, and when Dogbert cites man's rational essence he chooses to watch all-star wrestling, each a textbook Sartrean bad faith where he glimpses the truth and flees it. Measured against Aristotle's eudaimonia he lacks every virtue of the Nicomachean mean (courage as the midpoint of fear, rightly scaled ambition, wit), and since one swallow does not make a summer his whole life, not a day of it, could earn the name happy. The December 2017 addictive-app strips complete the verdict: Dilbert monetizes a zombie-making app for a raise, making him Beauvoir's serious man from The Ethics of Ambiguity, the intelligent sell-out who subordinates human value to a hierarchy he knows is hollow.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 21. A Response to Professor Pieixoto
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Doll writes a fictional keynote by 'Professor Anadicrad' answering Pieixoto's 'our job is not to censure but to understand': the fact that we view the past through an anachronistic lens does not forbid normative judgment, since Aristotle's practical wisdom—honed by hindsight, aiming at the golden mean and eudaimonia—gives historians a standard for judging whether a society cultivated virtue or vice. Gilead fails that standard spectacularly: it banned the reading that shapes values, reduced women to reproductive function, and required heteronormative forced procreation, blocking the relationships and habits flourishing needs. Beauvoir corrects even Aristotle's own biology-based view of women, and the chapter closes that a purely descriptive history would doom us to repeat Gilead's atrocities.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 9. Wherever the Road Leads
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Watkins takes the recurring road image ("Runnin' Down a Dream," "Kings Highway," "Learning to Fly") as a probe of whether the future is open. Against determinism and Aristotle-style fatalism she argues from lived experience: we cannot feel our choices as unfree, and even a determined world would remain unpredictable, so Petty's open road wins. His optimism in "It'll All Work Out" needs no faith in a good outcome, only the passing of time under our feet, and persistence then becomes an Aristotelian virtue required for eudaimonia, a duty owed to the kind of beings we are, and Sartrean authenticity in which Petty made himself through his project of rock'n'roll.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 3. Paul’s Lick It Up Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Courtland Lewis reads Paul Stanley's autobiographies (Face the Music, Backstage Pass) and songs as a worked-out life philosophy. Stanley's turn from chasing approval to confronting his inner pain exemplifies Socrates' unexamined-life dictum; 'Reason to Live' is glossed through Camus's Sisyphus — ground your reason to live in something indestructible, your own self-chosen meaning — while Plato's Ion explains Stanley's mix of learned craft and divine-inspired performance. Aristotle's flourishing through moderation appears in the advice not to overplay 'Rock and Roll All Nite,' and Lewis adds Locke and Rousseau on how laws, boundaries, and education create rather than restrict freedom, closing with Stanley's 'questioning ourselves is not a weakness' as Socratic wisdom.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 4. Knights in Satan’s Service
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Donald Presley debunks the claim that KISS are 'Knights in Satan's Service' by showing the pitchfork Satan is a pop-culture invention — tracing the Adversary from the Book of Job through Zoroastrian influence, Dante, and Milton — and arguing that branding Gene's Demon persona or songs like 'God of Thunder' and 'Unholy' as evil commits the informal fallacy of missing the point. He then argues, ironically, that KISS's actual values — hard work, self-empowerment, sexual freedom, indulgence without harming others — overlap substantially with the real LaVeyan Satanism of The Satanic Bible and with Aristotle's ideal of moderately indulging natural goods (sex, alcohol, success) for the sake of flourishing. The conclusion: KISS is not Satanic, but its life-affirming message coincidentally mirrors Satanism's actual teachings, and Christians, KISS, and Satanic virtues can coexist.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 10. KISS Was Made for Lovin’ You
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Courtland Lewis categorizes virtually the entire KISS catalogue by kind of love. Using Nicholas Wolterstorff's distinctions, he sorts erotic-activity songs ('Uh! All Night,' 'Deuce'), erotic-attachment songs ('I Still Love You,' 'Calling Dr. Love'), and erotic-attraction songs ('I Was Made for Lovin' You,' 'Hotter than Hell'), flags the disturbing near-statutory trio ('Christine Sixteen,' 'Goin' Blind,' 'Domino'), and adds non-erotic attachment, philia ('Childhood's End'), agape ('I Will Be There'), and the thirty-three percent of songs advocating a way of life ('Lick It Up' as an anti-suicide anthem of self-reclamation). He concludes with Aristotle and Plato on flourishing and Wolterstorff's claim that lives are 'shot through with love,' inviting readers to re-sort the lists with better reasons.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Aristotle to the Rescue
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Yim applies Aristotle's three kinds of friendship from the Nicomachean Ethics to the show: Tracy with Grizz and Dot Com in 'Hardball', and Tracy with Jenna in 'Flu Shot', are friendships of utility that dissolve when the benefit ends, while Liz and Jenna's long shared history looks deep but remains mutual usefulness between ambitious colleagues. Liz and Jack, by contrast, evolve from David-versus-Goliath adversaries in the pilot into something like virtuous friendship, culminating in 'Retreat to Move Forward' when Liz humbles herself with a terrible improv routine and a shirt-ripping dance to save Jack's standing before the Six Sigma crowd. The chapter argues the show thereby dramatizes that self-sacrificial goodwill is what makes a friendship worth the risk.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Liz Meets the Elephant in the Room
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Barkman reads 'Rosemary's Baby' as staging second-wave feminism in Rose Howard's comfort-sacrificing activism against third-wave feminism in Liz, who sells her dignity for the $10,000 Followship Award and likes comfort and the status quo. Sartre's existence precedes essence supplies third-wave feminism's non-essentialist claim that anyone can be a feminist in any manner, while an Aristotelian essentialist standard of human flourishing shows Liz's 'have it all' optimism, from the wedding dress bought in 'SeinfeldVision' to the adoption schemes of 'Do-Over', is a delusion because career and family each demand everything. Jack's confession that 'you have to choose' lands the chapter's verdict that the third-wave promise leaves women in Liz's predicament.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Neither Gods nor Beasts But Political Animals
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Spanakos denies the official line that the Avengers assemble from necessity—Thor beats Loki alone—arguing instead through Aristotle that the team is a polis: heroes join for safety but stay for the good life, since outside the polis one is either a god or a beast. Ms. Marvel's miserable solo run (unrecognized by Stilt-Man, a 'Where Are They Now?' has-been) ends only when she returns to lead the Mighty Avengers among friends who share her arete; the self-loathing Jessica Jones finds eudaimonia through philia with Carol, Luke Cage, and the team that delivers her baby; even the arrogant Hank Pym regains excellence by defending Tony and leading a new team. Even gods like Thor and near-beasts like the Hulk, the chapter concludes, need the Avengers to flourish.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Lacking Balance
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Stephen Kershnar argues that Batman's hatred of criminals is not a vice but a virtue, since hating what is evil is the morally appropriate attitude toward wrongdoers like the Joker or Batman: Year One's brutal Detective Flass. Against Aristotle's person-focused Virtuous-Persons Theory he defends a 'Virtuous-Thoughts-and-Actions Theory,' illustrated by Gordon's retaliatory beating of Flass and Batman elbow-smashing a pimp in Year One. The chapter closes on the golden mean of balanced love and hate: Batman's virtuous hatred leaves his life isolated and unflourishing, showing that virtue does not guarantee eudaimonia.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Greg Littmann tests Sheldon's geek existence against Aristotle's ideal of living well: since humanity's distinctive function is reason (the DVD-player-and-screwdriver argument), a life devoted to thought like Sheldon's — down to his fantasy of being a thinking satellite in orbit — has genuine Aristotelian worth. The chapter argues Aristotle could even bless geek obsessions, because poetry explores universal hypotheticals (Terminator causal loops, Superman's laundry) and adventure fiction purges emotion much as tragedy's catharsis does. But Sheldon's arrogance ('Captain Arrogant'), rigid clinging to his spot on the couch, and selfishness toward Leonard and Howard would earn failing marks in virtue, so the modern geek gets a mixed yet partly vindicating report card.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Evans defends the Penny–Sheldon friendship as genuine by three universal marks — mutual care (two Saturnalia-miracle hugs), intimacy (keeping Penny's community-college secret; friends who direct and interpret each other's conduct), and shared activity (singing 'Soft Kitty' in the round) — and then argues its deep differences are not an obstacle but the engine of moral growth. Against Aristotle's similarity-based complete friendship, oriented to a shared eudaimonia, he offers a modern pluralist account: Sheldon's self-aware jokes, dancing, and social awareness and Penny's physics lessons show each growing toward the other's way of flourishing without becoming alike, which a friend as similar as Amy could never force.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Eberl asks whether the Dude's 'pure abiding' is happiness: he runs Bentham's utility calculus on Dude-style pleasures (bowling's fecundity, the rug's purity, attending Marty's dance quintet for long-term rent goodwill) and Mill's higher/lower pleasures (Maude's vaginal art versus Logjammin'). Aristotle's verdict is that the Dude is not flourishing — his pleasures are incomplete, losable (the burned Torino), and he neglects his rational, social nature — yet Aristotle also ranks friendship with Walter and Donny highly, and Pieper's leisure, built on Aquinas's contemplation, gives the Dude's leisure a partial defense: he is incomplete but not bad, and he 'lives' while achievers merely make a living.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: O'Loughlin reads Walter biting off a nihilist's ear and the Dude refusing to walk out on league play as concrete realizations of ancient friendship: Aristotle's eudaimonia requires friends as 'second selves' whose shared activity (bowling in the friends' company) structures the excellent life, while Epicurus's Garden ordered life around simple pleasures and ataraxia, with friendship supplying pleasant memory and a kind of immortality after death. Because we moderns claim friendship's value without practicing its costs, the Dude's priorities look comic yet pierce us — and Donny's death, the Ralph's coffee can, and 'let's go bowling' become Epicurean commemoration rather than irreverence.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 6 Panther Virtue The Many Roles of T’Challa
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: White applies Aristotle's virtue ethics to T'Challa's many roles — Panther Tribe chieftain, king, Avenger, ambassador, brother, husband — arguing that virtues like the honesty and courage his fellow heroes praise need practical wisdom (phronesis) to guide action when roles conflict, as when he chooses country over rescuing Storm from trial, spies on the Avengers as king, or abducts a businessman as a matter of national security. Through tragic dilemmas like destroying Wakanda's vibranium to keep it from Doctor Doom ('a king must make terrible choices'), he shows such choices haunt without dirtying character, and that over-adopting roles is itself a failure of the golden mean, evidenced by T'Challa feeling 'imprisoned' by a kingship he never chose.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Sorcerer So Human
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The chapter argues Strange fails Aristotle's golden mean at both stages of his life: as a surgeon he chose cases for money and fame (greed and gluttony rather than generosity and temperance), and as Sorcerer Supreme he swings to the opposite extreme of total self-denial, refusing sleep, love, and friendship with Clea, Wong, and the Ancient One, since relationships between unequals cannot be the reciprocal philia Aristotle demands. It reads his hardest choices—the Dark Dimension left to Dormammu to save Earth, the Illuminati destroying parallel Earths during the incursions, and spending the last drop of the panacea on Wong rather than the world—as tragic dilemmas that show both the virtue ethicist's need for judgment and a defensible-but-excessive partiality toward friends.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 4. Finding One’s Place and Being Useful
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Karavitis argues that work, not social class, is Downton's real theme, sorting characters in a two-by-two matrix of class membership versus acceptance or rejection of the social order: the Dowager's 'we don't work' stagnation, Isobel and the Crawley sisters' redemptive projects, Molesley's grateful endurance, and the escapes of Gwen, Alfred, and Branson. The Anna scene, in which she answers her attacker Mr. Green with trained servant courtesy moments after the assault, shows how work 'becomes' us, while the alphabetical ordering of the opening credits suggests that only fulfilling work, not class position, matters. Rousseau, Adam Smith, and Marx frame the negative view of work (agriculture breeding inequality, the pin factory's deadening division of labor, wage exploitation and ideology), against which the chapter endorses Aristotle's pleasures of play and leisure, Russell's 'In Praise of Idleness,' and Pieper, predicting that automation will soon force everyone to confront what leisure is for.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The End of the Story
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Takes the Bene Gesserit Gom Jabbar test as defining humanity as the capacity to endure pain and act for the species rather than chew off one's leg like an animal, reading Paul's habit of walking into traps (Arrakis, the Tleilaxu ghola Hayt in Dune Messiah) and the Atreides ethic of self-sacrifice as passing that test. It ties the Butlerian Jihad's ban on making 'a machine in the likeness of a man's mind' to modern dependence on phones, computers and spell-checkers, echoing Mohiam's claim that removing the crutch 'forced human minds to develop' the two schools of math and politics. With Aristotle it argues that the politics of community and contemplation are the human talents machines atrophy, and ends by casting modern consumers (Harkonnen-like, 250 gallons of water per quarter pounder) as animals caught in a self-made environmental trap.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Alone into the Desert
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Has Socrates and Aristotle rate the good life in the Duniverse: the Baron fails every Socratic virtue (breaking his promise to Yueh, intemperance, betrayal), Duke Leto is 'Leto the Just' yet forges certificates and plans adultery, Paul's theocratic myth-making is unjust despite his temperance and courage, and the Fremen are brave and temperate but fatally unquestioning, lacking the Socratic awareness of ignorance that would have saved them from manipulation. Aristotle's function argument, his doctrine of the mean (Paul's worm-riding as courage between rashness and cowardice), and his external goods are then applied, but the author finally breaks with both philosophers: Paul's and Leto II's extreme selflessness admits no mean, their unjust oppression can still be right, and such extreme self-sacrifice may be the best life of all.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Littmann recruits Aristotle to answer the charge that D&D is a waste of time: by the function argument the best human life is one of thinking well, and D&D counts even as hack-and-slash, since munchkin optimization and 4e combat roles are logic puzzles, while role-playing is improvisational theater and therefore art. Aristotle's two art-functions are applied to play: catharsis, so that smacking goblins with a mace (his first cleric Brother Silverwolf) purges aggression and fear, and the Poetics' point that poetry explores 'a kind of thing that might be', so a dwarf chieftain losing a son to disintegration or rescuing a thief from stormclaw scorpions makes players reflect on parenthood and what friends owe each other. A good DM, Aristotle-style, keeps events within internal probability (no medusa petrifying someone facing away), players must act in character (the lawful good paladin cannot ride past the bandit-attacked peasant, and 'just playing my character' does not excuse the assassin murdering the magic-user at the inn), yet D&D's fully participatory, player-authored art can still accommodate unaligned and evil PCs.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Quagmire: Virtue and Perversity
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Miller uses Aristotle to assess whether Quagmire's sex obsession is a vice. Eudaimonia, not the fleeting pleasure of 'giggity-giggity', is the telos of action, and Quagmire aims at pleasure, so he is not flourishing; Aristotle's dissipated person, pained by absent pleasures, 'must have been thinking of Quagmire.' The Cleveland-Loretta-Quagmire affair episode ('The Cleveland-Loretta Quagmire') supplies paradigm cases of the Golden Mean: Cleveland first shows a deficiency of anger (apologizing to his cheating wife) then an excess (near-homicide), while Quagmire's boxing match shows courage between rashness and cowardice. On temperance, Quagmire is a slave to his sex drive (roofies, the diary 'Jackpot'), yet the chapter ends by defending him: he cares for Joan, distracts the social worker to rescue Stewie, and is honest about his passions, making him 'the most virtuous pervert he can be.'

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Eric Silverman argues Game of Thrones explodes the storybook link between virtue and worldly happiness: Ned, 'one man in ten thousand,' is betrayed and executed, so Plato's claim that the just person is happy must mean psychic order rather than material flourishing - reason ruling spirit and appetite - as with Bran, who flourishes as a greenseer though he will never walk again. Cersei is Plato's tyrant, her soul ruled by insatiable appetite and paranoia, so no external goods can ever satisfy her, while Aristotle's correction - virtue necessary but not sufficient for eudaimonia, which also needs health, friends, and good fortune - explains why both Ned (virtue without external goods) and Cersei (goods without virtue) end up unhappy. Finally he inverts Pascal's Wager: since playing the game of thrones risks total loss (torture, humiliation, death) for limited gain, and even winning hollows you out - Robert confesses he was 'never so alive as when I was winning this throne or so dead as now that I've won it' - only a fool would play.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Arya's arc from Needle to answering 'No one' is read as Aristotelian virtue ethics fused with East Asian philosophy: virtues are habits acquired only through practice, so the Water Dance's endless drills and martial-arts blocks that must become automatic mirror the honest person who tells the truth without deliberating. Syrio's lessons - 'looking is not seeing,' the story of the ordinary tomcat the other bravos mistook for a fabulous beast, being fully present with your trouble - teach Zen seeing and mindfulness, while 'be like water' and the steel that must be part of your arm embody Laozi's effortless wu wei. The Faceless Men's initiation, from discarding her possessions to the literal removal of Arya's face, becomes the Zen slaying of the ego, making her a 'Zen-Ninja-Aristotelian' on the path to eudaimonia.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Using the Nicomachean Ethics and the Rhetoric, the chapter vindicates the pleasure readers take in Salander's Taser-and-tattoo revenge on Bjurman: Aristotle distinguishes revenge, done for the satisfaction of the one wronged, from punishment, and requires that the wrongdoer know who avenges and why—which is why Lisbeth waits until Bjurman wakes before inking i am a sadistic pig, a pervert and a rapist across his torso. Proper anger on the right grounds is a virtue (hatred alone is corrosive), Larsson is cast as the rhetorician who must keep our trust to 'put the judge into a certain frame of mind,' and the revenge emerges as the deliberated, rational means toward the end Aristotle calls eudaimonia: independence from a bogus guardianship and a life worth living, since under 'proportionate reciprocity' those who cannot requite evil with evil are slaves.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Human Flourishing and the Preservation of Dying Cultures
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The chapter defines communitarianism, the view that flourishing requires membership in a tradition-bound community, and reads the Death Eaters' blood-purity mantra as its violent extreme, noting Voldemort kills the Muggle Studies teacher for advocating cultural mixing and 'the dwindling of the purebloods.' Aristotle's claim that humans are 'political animals' grounds the idea that identity is community-constructed, illustrated by Harry's 'Boy Who Lived' identity and his misery 'under the stairs' cut off from the wizarding world; the chapter ends by weighing cultural preservation against individual liberty, as in debates over the oppression of women in traditional cultures.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: NOTES
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The chapter stages Jeremy Waldron's challenge, whether people need rootedness in an ancestral culture the way they need food, clothing, and shelter, through the question of whether centaurs like Firenze should stay in the Forbidden Forest or assimilate into the wizarding world. It answers with a cosmopolitan reading of Harry's victory: his fluency in both Muggle and wizard worlds and his fellowship with Ron, Muggle-born Hermione, half-giant Hagrid, werewolf Lupin, part-veela Fleur, and centaur Firenze show that flourishing in the modern world requires moving among cultures rather than preserving purity.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Ugly
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Argues the ugliest defect is curricular: Hogwarts teaches only vocational magic, giving students the tools of power without the wisdom to use them, and so fails Adler's three aims of secondary schooling and the aims every major philosopher of education defended, Plato's wisdom and just society, Aristotle's eudaimonia, Locke's virtue and wisdom, Rousseau's natural education, Kantian character, and Deweyan growth. Even allowing that Dumbledore's office is a school of virtue outside class, most students never get his mentorship, leaving wizards ill-equipped for problems like anti-Muggle bigotry.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Johnson sorts Frank's six friendships through Aristotle's three kinds: Freddy and Meechum are friendships of pleasure (ribs and candor; loyalty and sex), while Doug, Cathy Durant, Tusk, and Jackie Sharp are friendships of utility that dissolve when usefulness ends - Jackie endorsing Dunbar being the proof. Even Frank's marriage fails the test of true friendship, since Aristotle holds that only good people can mirror each other's character, and badness corrupts the self-knowledge friendship provides. Because Aristotle deems friendship 'most indispensable for life' and eudaimonia requires virtuous activity joined to good fortune, the chapter ends hoping Frank can still choose the good for its own sake - a hope Claire's walkout after Iowa badly dents.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Sorts Frank's six friendships using Aristotle's three types: Freddy and Meechum are friendships of pleasure, Doug, Durant, Tusk, and Jackie friendships of utility, while Claire-despite 'I love that woman more than sharks love blood'-cannot be a true friend of the good because true friendship requires two people of good character seeing themselves in each other. Since Aristotle ties friendship to flourishing, the chapter ends hoping that Frank, who has good fortune but neither good character nor true friends, may yet choose virtue and the good life.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 3 The Virtues that Made the Man, and the Man Who Became the Legend The Adventures in Philosophy of Young India
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Robert Mentyka reads The Adventures of Young Indiana Jones through Aristotle: Kazantzákis's causality lesson in 'Travels with Father' introduces the four causes, which the chapter applies to the TV series itself, and the final cause grounds ethics — eudaimonia is the ultimate end of all action, as young Indy learns when the Mata Hari affair in 'Demons of Deception' shows that pleasure cannot deliver fulfillment. Virtue is a mean between extremes (courage between cowardice and recklessness), acquired through vigilant practice and through community, illustrated by Indy swinging between caution and recklessness with Nancy Stratemeyer and Pancho Villa, and by exemplars like Albert Schweitzer and Ernest Hemingway. The 'adventures that made the man' were really the virtues and the people that shaped him, completed when Crusade and Crystal Skull have him accept his roles as son and father.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Here Lies an Avenger
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The Pattersons read 'The Mask in the Iron Man' as moral education: Tony's repeated 'I have a good life' litany maps onto Aristotle's eudaimonia — friends like Rhodey, Pepper, and Happy, wealth, health, sobriety, and life itself as goods chosen for the sake of happiness — while Niebuhr's community of value makes the Avengers the community of trust and loyalty that grounds those ideals. Tony fails as teacher when the sentient armor kills Whiplash, cannot grieve with him, and fails Aristotle's friendship test of willing good for the friend for his own sake, its identity dangerously conflated with Tony's. The reversal comes when Tony lives the virtue of self-sacrifice — dying 'because I'm an Avenger' — and the armor, finally grasping nobility, rips out its own mechanical heart to save him, earning the grave marker 'Here lies Iron Man, Avenger.'

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Uses Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics account of wit as a character virtue lying in a mean to map the UK office: David Brent is the buffoon of excess, the 'slave of his sense of humor' who cannot not joke (the 'crack of Dawn' line, the cruel Post-It Notes firing prank on Dawn), Gareth Keenan the boor of deficiency whose literalism leaves him unable to make or take a joke, and Tim Canterbury the ready wit whose responsive irony ('Does anybody have the right time?') hits the mean. Because humor, like morality, is uncodifiable - there is no Having a Sense of Humor for Dummies - the trio illustrates that virtue is qualitative appropriateness guided by practical wisdom, not moderation or rule-following.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Sanford argues, through the arc of the Raimi trilogy, that Peter becomes good by becoming the narrator of his own life. On Aristotle's Poetics — a story has a beginning, middle, and end, and art imitates life — and MacIntyre's claim that man is a 'story-telling animal' whose life is 'the unity of a narrative quest,' Peter's involuntary obligations (orphanhood, Uncle Ben's death, the spider bite, love for MJ) ground the voluntary ones, and his quest is to use his great powers responsibly. Tracking Aristotle's categories, Peter moves from incontinence (vengeance on Flint Marko, the jazz-club strut in Spider-Man 3) through continence to genuine virtue, and his practice of telling his own story — 'it's the choices that make us who we are' — models how we must get our own stories straight to flourish.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Jason Eberl uses the amusement park of 'Shore Leave', Omicron Ceti III's spore paradise in 'This Side of Paradise', Landru's hedonistic 'red hour', and the Borg's relentless efficiency to argue that edifying play and leisure are necessary for intellectual, moral, and spiritual flourishing. Following Josef Pieper's Leisure, with Nozick's experience machine (applied to 'The Thaw' and Barclay's holodiction), Aristotle's 'we work in order to be at leisure', and Aquinas on wonder, he contrasts mere utility (bonum utile) with the common good a drone-only Collective can never have. He concludes that thoughtfully watching Star Trek is itself worthwhile leisure: science-fiction thought experiments that serve Socrates's examined life.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: David Kyle Johnson argues Kirk is a jerk for dismantling utopias—the machine-god Vaal in 'The Apple' and the spore colonists of Omicron Ceti III in 'This Side of Paradise'—whose members were happy, healthy, and arguably free. Taking up objections from the Mission Log podcast, he rebuts the 'stagnation' and 'drug' charges by testing the utopias against Aristotle's eudaimonia and Maslow's self-actualization, and exposes the appeal-to-nature fallacy behind 'artificial happiness'. Using Rousseau on primitive simplicity and Nozick's libertarian minimal state, he concludes that the real threat to freedom is Kirk himself (and a Federation that, as Eddington says, assimilates without telling you), and that at minimum cultural relativism forbids wrecking harmless societies.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Jedi and Sith Ethics “Similar in Almost Every Way”
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Shea, Archer, and Banning argue that Star Wars' moral framework is natural law ethics in the tradition of Aristotle and Aquinas: the light side humanizes (Force healing, Qui-Gon's spirit surviving death, Grogu curing Greef Karga) while the dark side dehumanizes (Maul's bisection, Palpatine's deformation, Anakin's disfigurement), and apparent counterexamples like Luke's lost hand always trace back to prior vice. Aquinas's claim that the most general principles of natural law can never be blotted out explains why 'there is still good in' Vader and why redemption is always possible. The Jedi and Sith codes embody opposed views of human nature — relational, altruistic, and accepting of mortality versus atomistic, egoistic, and obsessed with cheating death through midi-chlorian manipulation.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: “And I, I'm All the Jedi!”
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Okapal uses Aristotle's three friendships to frame the saga as a story of desert children seeking community: utility friendships like Hondo Ohnaka's and the Sith Rule of Two, where Darth Bane's apprentice is a mere instrument and Sidious calls Maul, Tyranus, and Vader 'easy to replace', stand against the other-regarding virtuous friendships of Obi-Wan, Kanan, and the Rey-Finn-Poe triad, where friends sacrifice for each other's sake as Ezra learns about Kanan in 'A World Between Worlds'. Luke's premature departure for Cloud City fails the 'for the other's sake' test Yoda poses. Rey can only choose the Jedi community knowingly once she learns she is Palpatine's granddaughter, and her closing claim 'I'm Rey Skywalker' is a choice between two value systems - the plural, other-regarding Jedi Code versus the self-regarding 'I' of the Sith Code - making friendship and community, not blood, the root of identity.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Begley and Biondi argue Ted is an ethical egoist in the Aristotelian-Randian sense: like Howard Roark of The Fountainhead (Ted's favorite book), he is a self-loving creator who loves his work, has a 'self-sufficient ego' immune to others' approval, and pursues long-range values, so his kindness and biscuits are rational self-interest, not selflessness. Against Hobbesian psychological egoism they distinguish genuine egoists from narcissists like Rupert and hedonists like Season 1 Jamie, defend Ted's divorce and the curse-reverse ceremony as only apparent sacrifices, and read his panic-attack therapy arc as the egoist's project of achieving inner wholeness.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Forte maps the Richmond cast onto Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: Rebecca, Nate, Roy, and Jamie begin incontinent or near-vicious; courage is the mean between Nate's cowardice and Roy's rashness; and their friendless misery illustrates why friendship (utility, pleasure, complete) is necessary for eudaimonia. Ted's coaching works as a modern strengths-based complement to Aristotelian habituation - Phoebe's Princess-and-Dragon play tempers Roy, Jamie's competitiveness is redirected into team play, Nate misses the mean and becomes mean - and the finale's 'progress over perfection' framing shows all of them as works in progress toward teloi.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Loftin argues the Diamond Dogs enact Aristotle's complete friendship: Jamie and Rebecca fail at friendship because they misconceive the good as self-gratification, and following Philippa Foot's natural-kind account of human good (plus Cicero on goodwill and C. S. Lewis's Four Loves) he shows friendship is an intrinsic good of human beings as such. Ted's vulnerability before Beard, Nate, and Higgins invites them into virtuous activity, Higgins's defection from Rebecca's sabotage scheme displays friendship against a relationship fueled by hurt, and Nate's status-hunger explains why he mistakes Ted's laughter and Rupert's patronage for friendship.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Notes
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Wible asks whether Ted's friendliness with players and staff constitutes moral friendship, testing it against Aristotle's three friendship types, Hume on solitude, and Bennett Helm's conditions (shared activity, intimacy, mutual care) plus a power-imbalance requirement Kant's respect for persons underwrites. This condemns Rebecca and Sam's relationship as a conflict of interest too risky to permit, questions Led Tasso and benching decisions, yet concludes that Aristotle's virtue friendship between coach and player is possible and preferable to Drewe's limited utility-friendship, since Ted's virtuous friendships make players better people while still knowing when to prioritize team over individual.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: “I Always Felt this Place was Missing a Real Villain. Hence, My Humble Contribution.”
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Jason Eberl argues Westworld cultivates real moral character: using Aristotle's account of virtue and vice as habituated dispositions, he shows William's thirty years of habitual killing make the Man in Black his genuine 'second nature,' not merely a vacation persona, citing Aquinas and Kant on how cruelty to animals (or human-like hosts) hardens moral character. Drawing on Frankfurt's second-order desires and narrative identity, he contends Maeve attains personhood by reprogramming her own first-order desires, while Ford views most humans as wantons trapped in first-order loops. He concludes the park can both corrupt (William) and potentially free hosts to flourish as self-authoring persons rather than devolve into wantons whose 'violent delights have violent ends.'

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Hardwood Dojos
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Bassham and Hamilton distill six success principles from coaches Smith, Pitino, Summitt, and Krzyzewski and show each echoes great philosophers, treating the court as a 'dojo' or place of enlightenment. Setting goals and pursuing excellence through habit map to Aristotle's eudaimonia and doctrine of habituation (Shaq the 'Big Aristotle' given the Nicomachean Ethics by Phil Jackson); the emphasis on outworking adversity and controlling only one's own effort maps to Stoics like Seneca, Epictetus, and Marcus Aurelius, as when Summitt and Dean Smith tell players to control what they can and accept the rest.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Hoosiers and the Meaning of Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Michael Peterson argues that Hoosiers is a microcosm of life's meaning: Aristotle's eudaimonia frames the characters' searches (Norman Dale rebuilding his career, Shooter his self-esteem and his bond with son Everett), and Dale's 'in my book, we're going to be winners' speech shows that character, unselfish teamwork, and playing to potential - virtue learned by doing, as coaching models moral instruction - matter more than the scoreboard against South Bend Central. The film's second chances (Principal Summers's clean slate, Whit's return, Dale's hiring of the town drunk Shooter) reveal that character alone is insufficient: mercy and forgiveness, which Hannah Arendt traces to Jesus, reframe an unchangeable past and open a future. Peterson then surveys worldviews - naturalism (Bertrand Russell's 'accidental collocations of atoms'), postmodernism (Derrida's deconstruction), Hinduism's Atman-Brahman - and argues only Christian theism, in which God's nature is love (Aquinas), can ground the character and forgiveness the film dramatizes.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Vince Lombardi and the Philosophy of Winning
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Belliotti reconstructs Vince Lombardi's 'winning isn't everything, it's the only thing' as a deeper philosophy of pursuing excellence and perfection as process values, not victory as such. He rebuts Marxist charges (via Sage) that competitive sport is mere capitalist superstructure by arguing, with Marx and Nietzsche, that hard creative labor and self-overcoming are human goods in themselves rather than mere capitalist demands. Lombardi is cast as a 'grand transcender' whose danger of fascism arises only when winning becomes an end in itself.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: On Fumbling the Ball
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Fry uses fumbles—Tony Romo's botched hold, Jerome Bettis's near-disaster saved by Roethlisberger, Leon Lett's showboating—as psychodramas illustrating the fragility of the good life. He invokes Aristotle's worry that one cannot call a life happy until it is complete, and Thomas Nagel's 'moral luck' (the negligent truck driver) to argue our culpability for fumbling, on the field and in life, is shaped by contingency, so responses should be discriminating. He draws on Frankfurt on caring and closes on redemption through effort, luck, and grace.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: First Hole Golf and the Importance of Play
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Al Gini defends play as intrinsically valuable and essential to being human, drawing on Huizinga's three criteria of 'true play' and William James's ideal of the amateur who plays 'for the love of it.' Using his golf-obsessed father as an extended case, he shows how golf functions as a self-contained, absorbing 'refuge from ordinary life' that delivers completion, coordination, and cooperation, echoing Plato's claim in the Republic and Laws that sport forms both person and community. The chapter treats golf as an end in itself whose joy sustains a flourishing life rather than as a means to external reward.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Michael Austin argues that a truly Olympic greatness requires moral, not merely athletic, excellence, reading Aristotle's magnanimity (megalopsychia, 'greatness of soul') as the crowning virtue that unifies all others. He tests this against three Olympians: bobsledder Eugenio Monti, who lent a rival team a part and lost gold; sprinter Wilma Rudolph, who forced her homecoming parade to be integrated; and runner Emil Zatopek, who gave away his gold medal and defied the Soviet invasion of Prague. Using Robert Adams's idea of 'modules of virtue,' he explains why some champions show self-control in sport but not in life, whereas the magnanimous person holds every virtue across every domain.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Through an imagined Greek play featuring the Spartan 'trembler' Aristodemus and an Avery-Brundage-like IOC president, Jesus Ilundain-Agurruza argues for rethinking the Olympic motto and creed around three Greek virtues, aretE (excellence), andreia (courage), and kalon (noble beauty), grounded in Aristotle's virtue ethics, the mean, and eudaimonia. Using the Spartans exercising on the eve of Thermopylae, he defends a collaborative, non-instrumental conception of competition against record-obsession and cheating, exemplified by Eugenio Monti and Cecil Healy. He closes with Camus's Sisyphus, arguing the athlete pushes the rock in the spirit of aretE, spending energy joyfully 'just because,' turning punishment into sport.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Heather Reid interprets the Olympic Charter's first Fundamental Principle through the ancient ideal of aretE, arguing the metaphysical structure of sport, contests that create purposeless obstacles, exists to cultivate and celebrate human excellence rather than to beat opponents or make money. Citing Plato the wrestler, Suits's definition of game-playing, and Homer's funeral games, she maps five virtues onto sport: eusEbeia (reverence for ideals beyond oneself), andreia (courageous endurance in agOn), sOphrosynE (harmonious power and control), dikaiosynE (justice as rule-order and proper function), and sophia (the athlete's pursuit of truth about human capacity, akin to 'flow'). The goal she proposes is the 'Olympian soul.'

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Authoritarian Tennis Parents Are Their Children Really Any Worse Off
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Kevin Kinghorn asks whether authoritarian tennis parents (like the family of prodigy Jan Silva) harm their children's well-being, and tests three theories of the good life. He rejects Aristotle's perfectionist eudaimonia because the 'uniqueness of reason' criterion fails, substituting his own perfectionist-yet-mental-state view that well-being consists in the felt experience of connecting with others. He defends a Mill-style hedonism of higher and lower pleasures against Robert Nozick's experience-machine objection, arguing the machine only refutes the claim that we desire mental states, not that well-being consists in them, and dismisses desire-satisfaction theories and Feinberg's 'right to an open future' as failing to show that lost autonomy itself lowers a child's flourishing.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Me and You Identity, Love, and Friendship in the Films of Charlie Kaufman
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Den Uyl argues that Kaufman's films are really about friendship rather than romance, reading them through Aristotle's character friendship (the friend as 'other self' and mirror of self-knowledge) and Montaigne's ideal of a free, voluntary friendship that also engages the body. Charlie's fictional twin Donald in Adaptation externalizes the integrity Charlie lacks, and only after internalizing Donald can he say 'I love her'; Caden in Synecdoche fails because he looks only at himself. Love succeeds, on this reading, only when grounded in the self-sufficiency and self-respect that make one capable of an 'other self,' as Eternal Sunshine's Joel and Clementine haltingly discover.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Eastwood, though no academic, does 'practical philosophy' through his films as a craftsman who inherits and then revises genres (revising the Western in Unforgiven, rethinking rugged individualism in Million Dollar Baby and Gran Torino). Invoking MacIntyre's claim that we are only co-authors of interlocking narratives, it reads Eastwood's focus on decisive moral choices (Francesca's refusal to leave in Bridges of Madison County, Butch Haynes in A Perfect World) as a 'laboratory of moral psychology' echoing Aristotle's 'choice discriminates character.' It ties his concern with loss, justice, and Aristotelian friendship and flourishing (Grinnell on Million Dollar Baby) to a Socratic 'know thyself,' arguing his philosophizing is implicit and nonverbal rather than argued in words.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Grinnell applies Aristotle's classification of friendship (utility, pleasure, and complete character-friendship between equals in excellence) to Million Dollar Baby and Gran Torino. Frankie/Maggie and Walt/Thao begin as incomplete, utility relationships across barriers of age, sex, and culture, then ripen into character-friendships of 'other selves' who pursue each other's good. He resolves the apparent paradox that friendship demands bringing about a death: Frankie euthanizes Maggie against his own wishes to honor her autonomy and whole-life excellence, while Walt engineers his own death and deceives Thao to spare him a vengeance that would destroy his character — each an Aristotelian sacrifice of self-interest for the friend that preserves the friendship's excellence.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Symbolism, Meaning, and Nihilism in Quentin TaranTino's Pulp Fiction
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Conard reads Pulp Fiction as a study of American nihilism in Nietzsche's 'God is dead' sense: with no transcendent framework of value, Jules and Vincent orient their lives by transient pop-culture icons (Jack Rabbit Slim's, the Fonz) and by Marsellus Wallace's arbitrary power, so the mysterious briefcase has worth only because he wills it. He contrasts this void with Aristotelian ethics, where a thing's good lies in realizing its rational essence. Jules's transformation begins when he survives the misfired shots and reinterprets his Ezekiel 25:17 recitation as a call to be 'the Shepherd,' while Butch's choice of the samurai sword over the baseball bat signals a return to an objective warrior code beyond the empty pop icons.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: “Please Make Me a Real Boy” The Prayer of the Artificially Intelligent Jason T. Eberl
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Eberl argues that HAL 9000 in 2001 and David in A.I. present sufficient evidence of personhood, testing them against the Turing test, behaviorism, and Boethius's definition of a person as an individual substance of a rational nature. He uses Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition to explain the deadly struggle between humans and their self-conscious creations, reading Bowman's disconnection of HAL and the Flesh Fair's destruction of Mechas as humans failing to recognize persons. Invoking Aristotle's telos and virtue, he claims the Flesh Fair's real moral crime is precluding Mechas from pursuing their own flourishing, while David's Pinocchio-like leap of faith marks him as person-like.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Conard uses Mean Streets' guilt-ridden Charlie to survey conceptions of unhappiness against three definitions of happiness: beatitude (Aquinas), pleasure (Mill's hedonism), and flourishing (Aristotle's eudaimonia). He reads Charlie as damned in his own Catholic eyes, then invokes Nietzsche's Genealogy that religion manufactures guilt from internalized instinct, Plato's disordered soul and akrasia to explain Charlie's conflicting desires, and Schopenhauer's and Freud's pessimism that suffering is our natural state. He argues Charlie reaches dysdaimonia by acquiring vices and pursuing an ignoble (gangster) life, closing with Plato's Symposium and Sartre's facticity/transcendence to cast unhappiness as an ontological lack at the heart of human desire.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Aristotle and MacIntyre on Justice in 25th Hour
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Conard uses Lee's 25th Hour to test Aristotle's claim that justice is inseparable from community and necessary for eudaimonia, and MacIntyre's charge that liberal individualist society lacks any common good. Comparing the greedy Wall Street broker Frank (an Aristotelian overreacher driven by pleonexia) with the drug dealer Monty (fairer, though convicted under unjust Rockefeller laws), he argues Monty is not unjust yet still cannot flourish in a fragmented New York. Monty's profane bathroom 'fuck you' soliloquy dramatizes the city's incommensurable values, while the post-9/11 fellow-feeling offers a fleeting glimpse of the shared good MacIntyre says modern society lacks.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Civilization and Its Discontents The Self-Sufficient Western Hero
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Den Uyl builds a composite philosophic picture of self-sufficiency from Aristotle's autarkeia (reason-guided virtuous activity, requiring external goods and civilization) and Spinoza's freedom as acting from one's own nature guided by adequate ideas, then tests it on John Ford's heroes. In The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance, Tom Doniphon is 'procedurally' self-sufficient in the precivilized West while Ransom Stoddard embodies civilized reason, and neither can inhabit the other's world. He argues the western's deepest value is Emersonian self-reliance—fidelity to one's own unique nature (the 'cactus rose')—which civilization threatens even as it enables Aristotelian flourishing.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 9 Neil Young’s Search for the Simple Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Watson and Riches reinterpret "A Man Needs a Maid" not as simple misogyny but as Young's ambivalent inner conflict between craving companionship and fearing the pain of intimacy. They read his pursuit of the "simple life" ("Heart of Gold," avoidance of reading) through Epicurean simplicity, Aristotle's eudaimonia, Bowlby/Freudian avoidant attachment and cognitive dissonance, and Sartre's "bad faith" as self-deception, set against Thoreau's chosen solitude and Aristotle's claim that the non-social being is "beast or god."

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Love, Value, and the Human Destiny in Interstellar
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: The chapter stages Interstellar's conflict between Cooper's partial love for his own family and Professor Brand's species-level duty as a question about the intrinsic value of humanity. Using Aristotle's account of friends and children as 'other selves' and of happiness as the one end sought for its own sake, it argues that the species survives only as a byproduct of particular, partial loves, so Plan B's bank of 5,000 faceless embryos could not preserve 'us' in any meaningful sense. Kant's unconditional dignity of rational persons supplies Brand's premise that our existence enriches the universe, but the chapter turns Kant against him: Brand's monstrous lie to the Endurance crew treats persons as mere means to an end they do not share, trampling the very dignity it claims to save. It closes by asking what value colonizing Edmunds's planet would destroy—ecosystems, microbial life, and possibly other rational persons whose dignity we would be obliged to respect—should humanity refuse to 'go gentle into that good night.'

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 10. Cas Is Family
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Doll traces Castiel's arc from a cold Divine-Command/utilitarian 'hammer of the Lord' to a member of the Winchester family through Aristotle's ethics. She argues Cas learns to contemplate and act on the chief good under Dean's tutelage, pursuing eudaimonia by habituation despite repeated failures (becoming a false god, the Leviathans), and that his bond with Sam and Dean grows through Aristotle's three friendships—utility, pleasure, and finally the rare true friendship of virtuous character—culminating in his self-sacrificing declaration of love that defeats Billie.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 8. Straight Edge and How to Live the Good Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Tierney reads Straight Edge hardcore (Minor Threat, Ian MacKaye, the black X) as punk's answer to the ancient question of the good life: sXe abstinence embodies Aristotle's eudaimonia through habitual virtue, maps onto the Buddha's first three noble truths (craving causes suffering, so quit the booze) and the three poisons, and Epictetus's concern only for what is within our power, while Mill's pleasure-based higher/lower pleasures serve as the dissenting voice. Spinoza on being ruled by emotions and on self-love supports the DIY self-mastery of MacKaye's Dischord Records, but the chapter weighs the scene's zealotry - Rollins reading death lists, Maximum Rock'n'Roll gatekeeping and the Biafra beating - against integrity that leaves room for dissent.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: 5. Friendship, Fun, Freedom, Food, and the Future
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Le Gall and Taliaferro read Bourdain's Libya and Iran episodes of Parts Unknown through Pierre Hadot's 'philosophy as a way of life,' arguing that Gaddafi and Khomeini were failed Platonic philosopher-kings. They interpret ordinary Libyans and Iranians eating Uncle Kentucky chicken, playing pinball, or hosting feasts as popular 'spiritual exercises' — tatonnement — showing how the personal becomes political and how friendship, fun, freedom, and food nourish the Socratic care of the soul.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Lessons Learned
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: McAleer uses the British Office to teach Aristotle's virtue ethics, treating wit as a character virtue that is a mean between the vices of buffoonery (excess) and boorishness (deficiency). David Brent is the buffoon, slave to his need to be thought funny; Gareth Keenan the literalist boor who cannot take or get a joke; and Tim Canterbury the ready-wit whose ironic humor is appropriate to circumstance. McAleer argues wit shows Aristotle's morality is broader than duty or outcome, aiming at eudaimonia, and that humor's uncodifiability, like Wittgenstein's remarks, mirrors how virtue requires practical wisdom rather than rules.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: House and the Life of Reason
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Henry Jacoby argues that despite House's line that we are 'selfish, base animals crawling across the Earth,' House lives a meaningful life. Rejecting God-, soul-, and afterlife-based meaning (House's Euthyphro-style objections and his '97 Seconds' near-death experiment), Jacoby locates meaning in the Socratic examined life and Aristotle's life of reason as humanity's proper function. House's relentless curiosity and puzzle-solving, tied to action and to saving lives, exemplify reason governing desire and yield eudaimonia - so 'doing things changes things,' and House, however miserable he seems, leads the examined, meaningful life.

aristotle-eudaimonia.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
aristotle-eudaimonia.title: Oh, the Places You’ll Go! The Examined, Happy Life
aristotle-eudaimonia.relation: Benjamin Rider reads Oh, the Places You'll Go! through Socrates' claim that the unexamined life is not worth living.
