But Balon's virtues are the vices of a piratical society that rewards reaving and rape, and through Charles Taylor's ethics of authenticity the chapter argues Theon's deeper failure is not knowing who he is - Stark or Greyjoy - so Ramsay's breaking of him into Reek completes a collapse of self that began at home; authenticity, it concludes, depends on virtue and social relations, which is why Theon can only begin to recover by choosing to serve Yara.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 12. Aaugh! Why Is Being Moral So Hard
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: The chapter claims Schulz's humor is built on moral failure and illustrates the three main moral theories with specific strips: utilitarianism via Bentham's 'sovereign masters' of pain and pleasure and Charlie's 'to make others happy' (with Lucy noting nobody is making her happy), Kantian deontology via Sally's crayon lie and Snoopy's 'I haven't bitten anyone on the leg recently' as fulfilling a negative duty, and Aristotle's virtue ethics via the failed steal of home (foolhardy rather than courageous), the unmailed Valentine (cowardly), the golden mean, and Joe Shlabotnik as a hopeless role model. Charlie gritting his teeth shows mistaking a virtue's external markers for the virtue itself. It concludes we fit none of the theories well, yet Peanuts keeps a spirit of hope - happiness is a warm puppy, and Charlie's grit is genuine even if he cannot see it.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 18. No End to Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Four vignettes pin philosophical problems to Peanuts' marginal characters: Camus's absurd - caring beings condemned to an uncaring universe - is answered by Sally's School Building, which grows a heart and drops bricks on her enemies; the 95472 kids motivate a tour of personal identity (same soul, same body, memory) through the Ship of Theseus; Pigpen's dirt raises Sartre's bad faith (facticity, transcendence, being-for-others) - we prize his authenticity over cleanliness - and Aristotle's golden mean, which moderates cleanliness while crediting his curiosity as a virtue; and finally the ontology of fictional characters asks whether the Kite-Eating Tree and Red Baron really exist inside the fiction and whether The Peanuts Movie's changed Charlie Brown counts as canon.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 4. How Much Deadpool Is Too Much Deadpool
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: The chapter argues Deadpool is entertaining because of, not despite, his excesses: his gratuitous violence and rapid-fire wisecracks breach the disciplined hero ideal, measured against Zeno of Citium's stoic dichotomy of control (accept the torture you cannot change, master your response) and Aristotle's golden mean between deficient and excessive force, which Wade flouts when he savors punishing Ajax instead of finishing quickly. Bakhtin's carnival excess explains the grotesque, orifice-obsessed humor that mocks 'normal' decency, and Derrida's 'internal drifting' (via Poe's Purloined Letter) frames Deadpool's first appearance being FedExed back to sender and his threshold position, where gags spill across comic, game, and film frames—making vigilante justice 'a supplement to the supplement' of law and exposing how each medium works.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 6. Horror Can Be Great Drama
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Applies Aristotle's Poetics wholesale - mimesis of possible actions, the six elements of tragedy, complete plots of proper magnitude, reversal and recognition, hamartia, and catharsis as the perfecting of fear and pity - to argue that Murder House (Ben's lust as tragic flaw and his double reversal to redemption in death) and Asylum (Sister Jude's irascibility and pride punished then reformed) are genuine high tragedies, and then uses the Nicomachean Ethics (virtue as a mean between extremes; justice as both retributive and rehabilitative) to show the seasons teach virtue, while Coven, Freak Show, and Hotel fall short because their characters' fates are undeserved and the moral message goes murky.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 7. And the Most Despicable Jessica Lange Character Is . .
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Ranks Jessica Lange's characters from least to most despicable using moral philosophy: Sister Jude earns credit for acting from duty (reporting the Nazi Dr. Arden at personal risk, Kant-style) and for genuinely feeling remorse; Elsa Mars partly honors the matriarchal obligations of care ethics but lacks Aristotle's habitual virtue and moderation, selling Bette and Dot to Dandy for fame; Constance Langdon abuses and effectively murders her disabled children; and Fiona Goode, motivated exclusively by youth, beauty, and power, murders her Supreme and torments Cordelia - never once acting out of concern for others.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 1. How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Be a Hero
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Malloy argues Iron Man is the better hero precisely because he fails constantly - Armor Wars, the Registration Act, alcoholism, a string of collapsed Stark companies - while Steve Rogers was born heroic and never stumbles. Using Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he treats perseverance as a virtue between cowardly quitting and Cap's stubborn excess (his doomed stand against Thanos in Infinity Gauntlet), and separates Tony's virtuous perseverance from Dr. Doom's identical behavior by its motives: Tony honestly examines his failures to help people, while Doom only looks for someone to blame.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 5. Why the Good Man Is a Great Leader
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Nisley reads Civil War through Aristotle's good man and good leader: Cap shows courage but lacks temperance and practical wisdom - his rash Lagos operation, his rage-borne beating of Tony, his choice of Bucky over the Avengers' common end - and his ceaseless struggle between passion and reason falls short of virtue. Applying Aristotle's account of philia, she argues the Avengers are a friendship of the virtuous that requires deliberation toward justice, which Cap dissolves by tearing the team apart, while Tony's reasoned acceptance of UN oversight, moderation after Ultron, and concern for the whole team make him the good man fit to lead.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 5. The Serious Point of Scott’s Humor
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Guerra and Barkman argue that Dilbert's humor is doing serious philosophical work: strips like the Pointy-Haired Boss's scheme to strip app users of free will, rebranded by Dilbert as marketing, distill manipulative corporate practice to its absurd essential core, and humor serves as a logical tool that, when it preserves the target's integrity rather than straw-manning it, exposes the equivocation in earnest arguments about getting something from nothing. They ground the practice in Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where wittiness is the virtuous mean between the vices of buffoonery and boorishness, read Adams's catalogue of failures and his luck-first, passion-is-bullshit account of success as a Socratic acknowledgment of ignorance that deflates the American Dream, and treat Win Bigly's persuasion lessons (visuals, repetition, intentional mistakes, the Hitler counterexample) as further proof that Adams has the virtue of wit.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 12. Dilbert Is an Asshole and That’s Why He’ll Never Be Happy and Nobody Loves Him
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Elsby and Luzecky argue Dilbert's unhappiness is chosen: from 400 rejections he concludes the women lack quality, he calls insult-bombing gentle kidding, and when Dogbert cites man's rational essence he chooses to watch all-star wrestling, each a textbook Sartrean bad faith where he glimpses the truth and flees it. Measured against Aristotle's eudaimonia he lacks every virtue of the Nicomachean mean (courage as the midpoint of fear, rightly scaled ambition, wit), and since one swallow does not make a summer his whole life, not a day of it, could earn the name happy. The December 2017 addictive-app strips complete the verdict: Dilbert monetizes a zombie-making app for a raise, making him Beauvoir's serious man from The Ethics of Ambiguity, the intelligent sell-out who subordinates human value to a hierarchy he knows is hollow.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 21. A Response to Professor Pieixoto
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Doll writes a fictional keynote by 'Professor Anadicrad' answering Pieixoto's 'our job is not to censure but to understand': the fact that we view the past through an anachronistic lens does not forbid normative judgment, since Aristotle's practical wisdom—honed by hindsight, aiming at the golden mean and eudaimonia—gives historians a standard for judging whether a society cultivated virtue or vice. Gilead fails that standard spectacularly: it banned the reading that shapes values, reduced women to reproductive function, and required heteronormative forced procreation, blocking the relationships and habits flourishing needs. Beauvoir corrects even Aristotle's own biology-based view of women, and the chapter closes that a purely descriptive history would doom us to repeat Gilead's atrocities.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 17. A Word from a Man Mister Rogers Ruined
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Nicolas Michaud, whose mother was murdered and who asked that her killer get help rather than die, constructs and then refutes the case that Rogers ruined boys by teaching gentleness: against the Thrasymachus line from Republic Book I that justice is for suckers and competition is everything, he argues Rogers's 'three ways to ultimate success: be kind' defines success as happiness; against 'forgiveness is weakness,' he deploys Aristotle's virtue of mildness, being ready to pardon rather than exact penalty, and a rereading of 'turn the other cheek' as claiming equal standing, so that forgiving is strength, not submission.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 4. Is It Immoral to Read Someone to Filth
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Birnie stages Alexis Michelle's hurt at the Season 9 body-shaming reads against Bianca Del Rio's 'rolodex of hate' to ask whether reading is immoral. He surveys the philosophical ethics of humor — Plato's Philebus on laughter as malicious delight in others' self-ignorance, Hobbes's 'sudden glory', Schopenhauer on why ridicule hurts, the Stoics' ideal of never laughing, Aristotle's eutrapelia as the golden mean between vulgar buffoon and boor, the Spencer–Freud relief theory, and Bergson's laughter as society's corrective — before endorsing the play theory: reads are consensual mock-aggression, verbal sport honed by marginalized black and Latinx ball culture. From this he derives three guidelines (play signals and consent, timing and audience given the show's younger mainstream viewers, openness to challenge) and concludes Katya's bus-stop read of Roxxxy was acceptable while stereotype reads need care.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 15. Chidi’s Indecision
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Vannatta argues Chidi's indecision exposes the shared flaw of the Big Three theories, Kantian deontology, Bentham and Mill's consequentialism, and Aristotle's virtue ethics of the golden mean: their rationalism pretends moral conflict can be eliminated by applying the correct rule, when Chidi's trolley terror shows moral situations are experienced as genuinely uncertain. Dewey's 'Three Independent Factors in Morals', the Good of desire, the Right of duty, and the Virtuous of communal praise, legitimizes that felt uncertainty and explains Eleanor's talent for finding option C between binary dilemmas. The chapter concludes that the show's real, unspoken moral theory is care ethics: partiality, relationship maintenance, and moral growth through the experience of being cared for, as Eleanor learns from Chidi's friendship rather than his lectures.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 28. How Captain Rogers Became a Good Man
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Traces Steve Rogers's arc from Erskine's charge — 'Not a perfect soldier, but a good man' — through Aristotle's virtue ethics (virtues are learned, none innate, each a mean between vices like courage between cowardice and rashness) to argue that the perfect soldier's obedience is not itself a virtue, so saving Bucky in Winter Soldier, outlaw leadership in Civil War, and gracious command in Endgame move Cap from black-and-white moral absolutism into the grey area where real virtue lives. The payoff is worthiness: only after pain has refined him can he lift Mjölnir, and the chapter warns that a 'perfect soldier' Cap — Thanos's ideological twin — might have heard the Mad Titan out.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 3. Paul’s Lick It Up Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Courtland Lewis reads Paul Stanley's autobiographies (Face the Music, Backstage Pass) and songs as a worked-out life philosophy. Stanley's turn from chasing approval to confronting his inner pain exemplifies Socrates' unexamined-life dictum; 'Reason to Live' is glossed through Camus's Sisyphus — ground your reason to live in something indestructible, your own self-chosen meaning — while Plato's Ion explains Stanley's mix of learned craft and divine-inspired performance. Aristotle's flourishing through moderation appears in the advice not to overplay 'Rock and Roll All Nite,' and Lewis adds Locke and Rousseau on how laws, boundaries, and education create rather than restrict freedom, closing with Stanley's 'questioning ourselves is not a weakness' as Socratic wisdom.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 4. Knights in Satan’s Service
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Donald Presley debunks the claim that KISS are 'Knights in Satan's Service' by showing the pitchfork Satan is a pop-culture invention — tracing the Adversary from the Book of Job through Zoroastrian influence, Dante, and Milton — and arguing that branding Gene's Demon persona or songs like 'God of Thunder' and 'Unholy' as evil commits the informal fallacy of missing the point. He then argues, ironically, that KISS's actual values — hard work, self-empowerment, sexual freedom, indulgence without harming others — overlap substantially with the real LaVeyan Satanism of The Satanic Bible and with Aristotle's ideal of moderately indulging natural goods (sex, alcohol, success) for the sake of flourishing. The conclusion: KISS is not Satanic, but its life-affirming message coincidentally mirrors Satanism's actual teachings, and Christians, KISS, and Satanic virtues can coexist.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-golden-mean.title: “Well, It Got Big Laughs”
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Barkman uses Confucius (ren, yi, li, and zheng ming, treating each person according to what he or she is) and Aristotle (eudaimonia, virtue as a habituated mean between extremes, practical wisdom) to indict 30 Rock for valorizing Jack's 'semi-virtuous path', the smug middle between best and worst announced in 'Do-Over'. He catalogues injustices the show laughs off: Liz's serial lies about her age, hobbies, and adoption; Jack's priority flu shots for the powerful in 'Flu Shot'; Tracy's insubordination about dogfighting in 'Rosemary's Baby'; and Kenneth's servility as everyone's punching bag. On liberality and piety, Jack's confession that 'capitalism is my religion' and Liz's 'I pretty well do whatever Oprah tells me' show the show settling for semi-virtue, which the chapter says even comedy must not endorse.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Explains Gob's professional failure through Aristotle's account of practices realizing their aims: Gob understands that illusions should surprise and delight, and he is motivated, but he lacks the craft-virtues of the modern illusionist as methodical engineer of experience, namely doggedness, diligence, technical knowhow, and above all humility. Instead he exhibits hubris, the excess opposite the mean, believing magic lives 'in here' in his heart; the 'Sword of Destiny' fiasco (a real sword, Buster's fake hand, a botched surgery) and the yacht that merely sinks show his failure is of character, compounded by the Dunning-Kruger effect that leaves him opaque to himself.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Interrogates Gob's catchphrase 'I've made a huge mistake': on Aristotle's account of hexis, the mean of truthfulness and proper pride, and justice as proportional distribution, Gob's prison-escape key stunt and 'Hermano' jealousy make him wicked rather than merely error-prone, since he lacks grasp of his own injustices. Hume's sentimentalist reply is that immorality is a nonrational moral sense refined only through experience, so mistakes could educate Gob, except he roofies away his one growth moment with Steve Holt (!). MacIntyre's practices (the Magician's Alliance versus non-practitioner Gob) and the narrative unity of character explain why a man who tells no coherent story of himself ends up with no wisdom.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Lacking Balance
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Stephen Kershnar argues that Batman's hatred of criminals is not a vice but a virtue, since hating what is evil is the morally appropriate attitude toward wrongdoers like the Joker or Batman: Year One's brutal Detective Flass. Against Aristotle's person-focused Virtuous-Persons Theory he defends a 'Virtuous-Thoughts-and-Actions Theory,' illustrated by Gordon's retaliatory beating of Flass and Batman elbow-smashing a pimp in Year One. The chapter closes on the golden mean of balanced love and hate: Batman's virtuous hatred leaves his life isolated and unflourishing, showing that virtue does not guarantee eudaimonia.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Becoming One
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: The chapter reads Baltar's head-Six and Caprica Six's head-Baltar through the gothic Double and Doppelganger tradition and Dissociative Identity Disorder: Number Six is Baltar's repressed guilt over betraying humanity ('I'm your subconscious frakking with your mind'), letting him escape responsibility for signing execution orders in 'Precipice,' while Gina Six serves as a tangible Double. Plato's Symposium myth of the split self frames Baltar and Six as two halves of one whole, since he cannot function without some version of Six present, physical or hallucinated. The resolution is Aristotle's golden mean from Book Two of the Nicomachean Ethics: like integration therapy for DID, virtue is a balance between extremes rather than eliminating one side, so Baltar and Six's child Hera may embody the balanced union of human and Cylon.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Sayles sorts the show's technology use by Aristotle's doctrine of the mean: healthy supplements (Raj webcamming his parents in India, Sheldon and Amy's video dates) versus unhealthy substitutes (Penny's Age of Conan spiral into unwashed hair and sick days, Sheldon living as a 'mobile virtual presence device,' one-sided 'virtual vengeance' videos against Penny's Wi-Fi theft and Kripke's helium prank). Since the mean is relative to the person and situation rather than a mathematical midpoint, moderation must be found case by case, and man as a social being must keep his social skills exercised. The chapter finds Penny and Amy — not the four scientists — best model balanced technology use.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Jollimore and Jones diagnose three 'very unDude' vices: Walter's rule rigidity, which confuses Kant's hypothetical rules of games (don't cross the foul line) with categorical moral ones and needs 'rules all the way down' to ward off nihilism; the Big Lebowski's hypocritical inauthenticity, a fake achiever living on his daughter's allowance who collapses facedown before his own rug; and the exclusionism with which everyone shuts Donny out of the conversation. Against these the Dude exhibits Aristotelian virtue as good judgment (knowing when rules don't apply), the Golden Mean between Walter and the nihilists, and Singer-style inclusion — 'he's in bed with everybody' — making him an authentic man of humor and perspective.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Michaud asks whether the Dude's sloth is a vice and answers no: from Russell's 'In Praise of Idleness' he argues that overwork chiefly serves the rich — exactly how the Big Lebowski exploits the Dude as unpaid courier while sneering 'The bums will always lose' — and from Aristotle's and Cicero's moderatio he argues the Dude practices a mean between frantic work and paralysis, working hard when it matters (the drop, the rug). The fable of the ant and the grasshopper, retold, shows both die anyway, while the Dude 'works at being unemployed' and enjoys the time he has — sloth, ironically, does a kind of work.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
aristotle-golden-mean.title: What Not to Do as a Parent
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: The chapter pinpoints Marie's failure in Arkangel using Feinberg's parental-rights framework: by filtering out every fright (the neighbor's dog, her father's stroke) she violated Sara's right to an open future, misconstrued her welfare and protection rights, and stunted the empathy that makes a child a fully functioning human being. Aristotle's golden mean frames over-parenting as a vice of excess — as damaging as neglect — and Ruddick's maternal ethics of care also convicts Marie, since mothering requires fostering growth and social acceptability, not just preserving life. The Philip K. Dick comparison lands the conclusion: an android is distinguished from a human only by lacking empathy, so Marie has manufactured a partial android rather than raised a child.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 6 Panther Virtue The Many Roles of T’Challa
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: White applies Aristotle's virtue ethics to T'Challa's many roles — Panther Tribe chieftain, king, Avenger, ambassador, brother, husband — arguing that virtues like the honesty and courage his fellow heroes praise need practical wisdom (phronesis) to guide action when roles conflict, as when he chooses country over rescuing Storm from trial, spies on the Avengers as king, or abducts a businessman as a matter of national security. Through tragic dilemmas like destroying Wakanda's vibranium to keep it from Doctor Doom ('a king must make terrible choices'), he shows such choices haunt without dirtying character, and that over-adopting roles is itself a failure of the golden mean, evidenced by T'Challa feeling 'imprisoned' by a kingship he never chose.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Greg Littmann imagines Aristotle auditioning for Black Sabbath in 1970 to argue the band satisfies the Poetics and Politics: music that gives pleasure, even the "perverted modes" working-class audiences enjoy, is legitimate art, and Sabbath's darkness works as catharsis, purging fear and pity as Greek tragedy did through Oedipus, the doomed figure in black of "Black Sabbath", the betrayed and ignored Iron Man, and the hopeless narrator of "Paranoid". Songs like "War Pigs", "Electric Funeral", and "Children of the Grave" also do what Aristotle says poetry does better than history, imagining alternative futures that spur citizens to political thought, while the band's drug lore maps onto the Aristotelian mean: beer and a little weed yes, heroin and cocaine never, and Ozzy's firing shows the price of intemperance.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aristotle-golden-mean.title: A Strange Ending
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Manninen applies virtue epistemology — built on Aristotle's virtue ethics and golden mean — to the four students of the Ancient One, asking not what they knew of the mystic arts but how they knew it. Strange's photographic memory exemplifies reliabilist epistemic ability, while Montmarquet's responsibilist virtues (impartiality, intellectual courage) are measured against Pangborn's self-serving magic, Kaecilius's courage without impartiality, and Mordo's epistemic rigidity and blind deference to authority ('no more questions'), each a vice of excess or deficiency. The Book of Cagliostro frames Wong's 'no knowledge in Kamar-Taj is forbidden, only certain practices,' and Strange emerges closest to the balanced intellectual character, though Aristotle demands consistency, not a single virtuous act.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Sorcerer So Human
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: The chapter argues Strange fails Aristotle's golden mean at both stages of his life: as a surgeon he chose cases for money and fame (greed and gluttony rather than generosity and temperance), and as Sorcerer Supreme he swings to the opposite extreme of total self-denial, refusing sleep, love, and friendship with Clea, Wong, and the Ancient One, since relationships between unequals cannot be the reciprocal philia Aristotle demands. It reads his hardest choices—the Dark Dimension left to Dormammu to save Earth, the Illuminati destroying parallel Earths during the incursions, and spending the last drop of the panacea on Wong rather than the world—as tragic dilemmas that show both the virtue ethicist's need for judgment and a defensible-but-excessive partiality toward friends.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Alone into the Desert
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Has Socrates and Aristotle rate the good life in the Duniverse: the Baron fails every Socratic virtue (breaking his promise to Yueh, intemperance, betrayal), Duke Leto is 'Leto the Just' yet forges certificates and plans adultery, Paul's theocratic myth-making is unjust despite his temperance and courage, and the Fremen are brave and temperate but fatally unquestioning, lacking the Socratic awareness of ignorance that would have saved them from manipulation. Aristotle's function argument, his doctrine of the mean (Paul's worm-riding as courage between rashness and cowardice), and his external goods are then applied, but the author finally breaks with both philosophers: Paul's and Leto II's extreme selflessness admits no mean, their unjust oppression can still be right, and such extreme self-sacrifice may be the best life of all.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Jeff Ewing asks which moral theory governs the novel, finding deontology absent and a contest between Graff's utilitarian recruiting pitch and a virtue-ethical focus on character: the I.F. allowed a 'Third' because it wanted Ender's traits rather than his acts. Mapping Plato's cardinal virtues and tripartite-soul politics against Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he argues Ender's minimum-force self-defense, adaptability, and disregard for hierarchy are Aristotelian virtues, while his killings of Stilson, Bonzo, and the buggers fall outside the mean only because he lacked the intellectual virtue of grasping his full situation.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Notes
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Trevor Hedberg asks whether 'Kill Everything' playthroughs of New Vegas are wrong, from the Goodsprings opening (where the player may massacre both Powder Gangers and settlers) to installing a mod that makes Freeside's unkillable children killable. He rejects the empirical aggression argument (the evidence is mixed and effects tiny, and alcohol or contact sports set a precedent) and the Kantian disrespect argument, since Fallout's NPCs - stuck on terrain, repeating dialogue - lack the rational agency the Humanity Formulation protects. The best case against virtual slaughter is Aristotle's virtue ethics: courage as the mean between recklessness and cowardice, eudaimonia as activity in accord with virtue, so the morality of playing turns on motives - exploring narratives or seeking combat challenge can be innocent, but killing for the pleasure of settlers' horrified flight corrodes character.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Family Guy and God: Should Believers Take Offense?
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: VanArragon, a believer and fan, compares Family Guy's religious mockery (Peter asking at communion whether Christ was 'wasted 24 hours a day', God hitting on women in a bar, the pope left dangling from a statue, the fake Passion of the Christ II trailer) with The Simpsons' gentler treatment (dream-God, Barney's innocent blunders), finding Family Guy deliberately offensive without tact or sympathy. He tests two defenses: Kant's requirement to treat people as ends rather than means (mocking believers for laughs uses them as mere means) and Aristotle's virtue of moderation in laughter (the show pushes toward the extreme of nothing-is-sacred, unlike Gary Larson's Far Side). Conceding the show raises real questions (transubstantiation, God's gender, Stewie finding God 'deliciously evil' in the Old Testament), he concludes the offense is not justified by any benefit, yet the portrayals are so absurd that believer-fans do not actually laugh at God and need not take offense.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Quagmire: Virtue and Perversity
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Miller uses Aristotle to assess whether Quagmire's sex obsession is a vice. Eudaimonia, not the fleeting pleasure of 'giggity-giggity', is the telos of action, and Quagmire aims at pleasure, so he is not flourishing; Aristotle's dissipated person, pained by absent pleasures, 'must have been thinking of Quagmire.' The Cleveland-Loretta-Quagmire affair episode ('The Cleveland-Loretta Quagmire') supplies paradigm cases of the Golden Mean: Cleveland first shows a deficiency of anger (apologizing to his cheating wife) then an excess (near-homicide), while Quagmire's boxing match shows courage between rashness and cowardice. On temperance, Quagmire is a slave to his sex drive (roofies, the diary 'Jackpot'), yet the chapter ends by defending him: he cares for Joan, distracts the social worker to rescue Stewie, and is honest about his passions, making him 'the most virtuous pervert he can be.'

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Greg Littmann asks what sort of life is worth living by holding Final Fantasy protagonists and FFXI Online players up to three standards. Hobbes's egoism and defense of absolute monarchy condemn the altruistic, authority-defying heroes (AVALANCHE, the rebels of FFII and FFVI) while partly approving the gil-grubbing, rule-breaking FFXI player; Mill's utilitarianism praises the world-saving heroes but condemns grinding down beastmen and rates most gaming a lower pleasure; Aristotle's function argument and golden mean find heroes like Yuna immoderately self-sacrificial yet credit ordinary FFXI adventurers with genuinely virtuous moderation, helping others while keeping their own interests in view.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Albert Anglberger and Alexander Hieke contrast Ned, the virtue ethicist's genuinely good man, with Cersei, a 'minimally extended' egoistic consequentialist whose only morally relevant subjects are herself and her children. Aristotle's apparatus does the work: phronesis lets Ned rank his daughters' lives above honesty when he confesses falsely ('the lies we tell for love'), his 'you're too fat for your armor' quip shows the golden mean among competing virtues, and Cersei's unbalanced maternal love is excess, hence not a virtue. They then unsettle moral judgment itself: utilitarianism would license the Slaver's Bay slaveholders, virtue ethics lacks action rules and cross-cultural agreement (charity is no Dothraki virtue), and Martin's POV narration gives direct access to Ned's inner life but only Varys's and Littlefinger's unreliable reports about Cersei - so our verdicts on her, like real-life judgments of others, rest on shaky evidence.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 15. Chidi’s Indecision
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Surveys the 'Big Three' through the show: Kantian deontology (Chidi's boots lie, Tahani's mere-means charity), Bentham and Mill's utilitarianism (Jason's alligator frame-up, the trolley simulation), and Aristotle's golden mean (courage between Jason's rashness and Chidi's paralyzed deficiency), arguing their shared rationalism cannot accommodate the real uncertainty Chidi feels. John Dewey's 'Three Independent Factors in Morals' — the Good, the Right, and the Virtuous as irreducible — explains why Chidi sees only binaries while Eleanor finds 'option C' and imagines the Medium Place. The chapter concludes the show's unstated moral theory is care ethics: relational selves, justified partiality toward friends, and moral growth through the experience of being cared for, as when Chidi models care rather than lecturing it.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Southworth uses the War of Light to ask what role emotion should play in moral reasoning: Sinestro rules Korugar through fear, the Star Sapphires kidnap Sinestro Corps prisoners to convert them to love, Atrocitus's rage was forged by the Manhunters' massacre, Larfleeze hoards, and the Blue Lanterns merely hope that hope matters. On Aristotle's account every corps errs by excess: Atrocitus's rage makes him miss chances to kill Sinestro, Fatality's love benches John Stewart from saving his friends, and even the Green Lanterns' will-only ideal fails, since total fearlessness is itself vicious and Plato's picture has reason directing emotion like a general directing soldiers. He ends by defending Mill's utilitarianism: the Guardians' real failure was not detachment but pretending to be detached, and reading them as flawed 'benevolent, disinterested spectators' vindicates the Corps while explaining their moral growth after Scar and the Blackest Night.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
aristotle-golden-mean.title: NOTES
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Reads the show's eclipse icon against Plato's sun of the good — goodness has become hard to discern — and tests four theories of evil on the characters: Socrates' claim that no one errs knowingly is half-confirmed since villains like Angela and Nathan always take themselves to be doing right; Aristotle's akrasia and vice as an excess or deficiency of disposition fit Sylar's blood-scrawled 'Forgive me' apartment and his uncontrolled hunger; and Nietzsche's Übermensch and pre-Christian master morality raise the uncomfortable question of why Sylar preying on inferiors is not heroic like Achilles. The chapter's endorsed answer is Gilligan's ethics of care: the heroes are good because they care — Matt for Molly and Daphne, Bennet for Claire — while evil is the absence of care, though Bennet's authoritarian, family-only care shows that care itself must be both widened and restrained.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
aristotle-golden-mean.title: a8.xhtml
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Garcia argues Tolkien writes with a virtue-ethical moral theory: Middle-earth peoples are characterized by moral traits (noble eagles, cruel orcs), intentions matter (Bilbo is not to blame for the discomforting barrel escape because he meant rescue, and he turns back through the mountain tunnels because loyalty and courage demand it), and the book's drama is the tension between Aristotle's 'great-souled' proper pride and Aquinas' Christian humility. Thorin's pride (self-styled 'King under the Mountain', refusing Bard's just claim), Smaug's vanity that Bilbo flatters to find the bare patch, and the dragon-sickness illustrate pride as vice, while Bilbo's growth - believing after the spiders that 'there was more in him' yet accepting Gandalf's 'you are only quite a little fellow in a wide world' with a laugh - exemplifies correct self-assessment between vanity and undue humility.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
aristotle-golden-mean.title: a20.xhtml
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Watson uses the company's decisions under uncertainty - whether to approach the troll-fire that nearly gets them eaten, the elf-lights in Mirkwood, Bilbo's descent of Smaug's tunnel - to teach decision theory: expected utility (assigning probabilities and values shows they should have stayed put rather than follow the troll-light), conditional probability (the Mirkwood lights are treated as dependent events, dodging the gambler's fallacy), and simplifying the outcome set. He then judges Bilbo by Aristotle's doctrine that courage is the mean between the vice of cowardice and the vice of rashness, felt with respect to the appropriate passion, fear: Bilbo fears as he should (kettle-whistles and jelly-trembles), avoids unforced risks, yet risks death for his companions' lives - so he has acted courageously and is developing, not yet fully possessing, the virtue, which Aristotle says requires long practice.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 3 The Virtues that Made the Man, and the Man Who Became the Legend The Adventures in Philosophy of Young India
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Robert Mentyka reads The Adventures of Young Indiana Jones through Aristotle: Kazantzákis's causality lesson in 'Travels with Father' introduces the four causes, which the chapter applies to the TV series itself, and the final cause grounds ethics — eudaimonia is the ultimate end of all action, as young Indy learns when the Mata Hari affair in 'Demons of Deception' shows that pleasure cannot deliver fulfillment. Virtue is a mean between extremes (courage between cowardice and recklessness), acquired through vigilant practice and through community, illustrated by Indy swinging between caution and recklessness with Nancy Stratemeyer and Pancho Villa, and by exemplars like Albert Schweitzer and Ernest Hemingway. The 'adventures that made the man' were really the virtues and the people that shaped him, completed when Crusade and Crystal Skull have him accept his roles as son and father.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 20 Timeless Artifacts and Aging Humans Indiana Jones and the Philosophy of Time
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Uses Aristotle's Rhetoric portrait of elderly men and his golden mean — the prime of life between rash youth and feeble age — to explain fan anxiety about aging Harrison Ford ('Raiders of the Lost AARP'), then turns to Heidegger's claim that human life does not happen in time but is time: mortals are finite beings whose worth decays, while the Ark, the Grail, and Belloq's buried pocket watch gain value outside 'vulgar' linear time, and only ready-to-hand 'things' that do something (a face-melting Ark, a healing Grail) matter rather than mere objects like the decapitated Brody statue. Augustine's Confessions frames the gap between clock time and lived 'inner' duration (Indy's 'all my life' hunting the Cross versus Marcus's counting of years), and Bakhtin's 'adventure time' explains the films' condensed, history-flouting chronology in which the character Indy never ages even as Ford does.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Can You Find Your Moral Compass
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Donovan and Richardson test Tony's moral compass in 'Armor Wars' and 'Extremis' against the three major schools. Utilitarianism fails because Tony will not sacrifice even one innocent for the greater good — he changes tactics to save a single pilot from the Raiders and rages when the Controller's human zombie dies — and Kantian deontology fails because Tony bends rules ('lives to mean more than rules') and is driven by emotion rather than pure reason. Aristotle fits: Tony is obsessed not just with doing good but with being good, snarling at his own reflection, asking filmmaker Pillinger 'Have you changed anything? Me neither,' until Extremis lets him 'be the Iron Man inside and out,' uniting agent and deed as Aristotelian character requires.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Lesson and Legacy of Din, Nayru, and Farore
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Charles Joshua Horn asks whether power belongs beside wisdom and courage in the Triforce. Kant's good will shows all three pieces are morally neutral — Link and Zelda act from duty rather than reward, so courage and wisdom could be misused just as easily as Ganondorf misuses power. Plato's Ring of Gyges shows power does not automatically corrupt (Ganondorf chose to steal the Triforce for the Gerudo), and Socrates's answer to Glaucon explains why Ganondorf's ill-gotten wealth and honor leave him morally bankrupt. Aristotle's doctrine of the mean then gives the goddesses' intended use: Link's courage sits between cowardice and rashness (he gathers map, compass, and weapon before the boss room), Zelda's wisdom is really prudence, and Ganondorf's vice is power in excess.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Whisper Things Into My Brain: Metallica, Emotion, and Morality
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Robert Fudge weighs whether Metallica's emotionally violent music corrupts or improves moral character. Against Plato's banishment of passion-stirring art (anger in 'Enter Sandman', indignation in '. . . And Justice for All'), he uses Aristotle's catharsis and the golden mean of healthy anger: 'One' purges pity and fear, and Hetfield's 'St. Anger' purged the rage behind his alcoholism. He then extends Adam Smith's empathy-based account - imaginative placement in the landmine victim's or addict's position - to argue the songs refine moral judgment, even making us question Kant's absolute duty against suicide by confronting the case where the body is a 'holding cell'.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Uses Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics account of wit as a character virtue lying in a mean to map the UK office: David Brent is the buffoon of excess, the 'slave of his sense of humor' who cannot not joke (the 'crack of Dawn' line, the cruel Post-It Notes firing prank on Dawn), Gareth Keenan the boor of deficiency whose literalism leaves him unable to make or take a joke, and Tim Canterbury the ready wit whose responsive irony ('Does anybody have the right time?') hits the mean. Because humor, like morality, is uncodifiable - there is no Having a Sense of Humor for Dummies - the trio illustrates that virtue is qualitative appropriateness guided by practical wisdom, not moderation or rule-following.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
aristotle-golden-mean.title: It’s Good to Be a Fan if …
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Barrett uses Bill Swerski's Super Fans to map a spectrum of fandom from casual to moderate to Super Fan, then applies Aristotle's doctrine of the mean to the virtues and vices of fandom: knowing trivia is a virtue (the Trekkies sketch), admiring athletic excellence is noble, but excess becomes licentious obsession, Shatner's 'Get a life!', heart attacks at Ditka's, and spending Thanksgiving with da Bears instead of family. Deficiency appears in bandwagon fans who lack commitment and loyalty, and the Red Sox fans' hospitalized heartbreak shows misplaced priorities in grief. Moderate fandom, loyal to people first and teams second, is the virtuous mean.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Eberl reads Jax's Season 5 dilemma (Tara's ultimatum to leave SAMCRO or lose his family) through Aristotle's account of virtue as character cultivated by habituation in a polis. SAMCRO nurtures genuine virtues—Opie's selfless loyalty, courage under fire, the club's communal generosity toward Donna and Lyla—alongside vices like Clay's greed and Tig's lust, with the golden mean distinguishing Bobby's critical loyalty from Chuckie's obsequiousness and Juice's rash minefield charge. Fr. Ashby's fight to keep Abel in Belfast away from Jax's cycle of violence, and the contrast between Deputy Chief Hale's law-abiding ideals and Mayor Hale's self-serving development, illustrate Aristotle's claim that legislators and environments make citizens good or bad. The chapter concludes that Jax's very mix of virtue and vice—the 'savage' needed to head the table—may be what reform requires, at moral cost.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
aristotle-golden-mean.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Young argues that South Park is perceived as dangerous for exactly the reasons Socrates was tried and executed in Plato's Apology: both 'corrupt the youth' by mocking religion, questioning authority, and exposing that the supposed teachers (Mr. Garrison's flip-flopping creationism, Mrs. Broflovski's moral panics, the 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip) do not know what they think they know. He diagnoses Cartman as an Eichmann figure whose banal, thoughtless evil—feeding Scott Tenorman his parents, torturing Muslims with farts—consists in the inability to think from another's standpoint, while Kyle and Stan's friendship embodies Arendt's dialogic thinking and Aristotle's mean between ideological extremes, as when they see both the merit and the smugness of hybrid drivers in 'Smug Alert'. Freud's theory that jokes break through repression explains why the show's vulgarity is essential rather than gratuitous: it verbalizes what culture silences so that it can be thought through, making South Park a Socratic gadfly rather than a corrupter.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-golden-mean.title: A New Sound for Star Wars
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Belluomini applies Aristotle's Politics Book 8 - music imitates emotion and thereby forms character - to Ludwig Goransson's Mandalorian score, showing how the bass-recorder motif and the 'broken children's tune' of Grogu's Theme render the compassion and conflict Din hides beneath his helmet, from the hovercrib encounter to the mudhorn rescue. Because well-ordered, balanced emotional movements dispose listeners toward virtue, the swelling orchestral versions that score Din taming the blurrg or his rock-styled confidence in 'Mando is Back' cultivate the viewer's own courage, care, and honor alongside the show's moral argument. Aristotle's intellectual enjoyment - delight in the fit between music and imitated feeling - explains why Gorransson's thematic recall makes the season feel like one film, culminating in the farewell cue that ties Grogu's goodbye to their first meeting.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 9. Masks, Hearts, and Superheroes
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Dupree and Fuš argue from identity statements: Bruce Wayne is 'just a mask' for Batman, while Clark Kent is in his heart Superman, so only an essentially human character can be a true superhero. On their Aristotelian definition — virtue ethics, the golden mean, flourishing through self-developed excellence — Batman's no-kill rule (sparing even the Joker), his planned avoidance of lethal force in Gotham Knights #31, and his balance against extremes make him the true hero, whereas Superman's given god-powers (killing Zod in Man of Steel, tyrant in Red Son) mirror power rings as Gyges's ring: possession without earned virtue.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Notes
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Forte maps the Richmond cast onto Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: Rebecca, Nate, Roy, and Jamie begin incontinent or near-vicious; courage is the mean between Nate's cowardice and Roy's rashness; and their friendless misery illustrates why friendship (utility, pleasure, complete) is necessary for eudaimonia. Ted's coaching works as a modern strengths-based complement to Aristotelian habituation - Phoebe's Princess-and-Dragon play tempers Roy, Jamie's competitiveness is redirected into team play, Nate misses the mean and becomes mean - and the finale's 'progress over perfection' framing shows all of them as works in progress toward teloi.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Notes
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Arvan argues the show is really about positive masculinity - what it is to be a good man - read through Aristotle's virtue ethics: toxic masculinity (Rupert's domination, Jamie Sr.'s abuse, Nate's cruelty, Ted's suffer-in-silence self-reliance) is vice at an extreme, while the show's good men hit the golden mean by 'womaning up.' Led Tasso works as context-appropriate toughness, Roy's hug of Jamie and the darts speech's 'be curious, not judgmental' blend masculine and feminine virtues, phronesis is learned from experience as Beard teaches Nate forgiveness, and even Rupert's downfall shows vice backfiring as Aristotle predicts.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
aristotle-golden-mean.title: P A R T T W O
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Three Part Two essays. Robert Loftis argues Moore and Gibbons use Ozymandias's squid attack to indict consequentialism — Veidt uses New York's dead as mere means to world peace, and Dr. Manhattan's 'Nothing ever ends' shows the utilitarian ledger dissolves into an infinite future — while Rorschach's 'never compromise' mantra is a counterfeit deontology rationalizing fascist thuggery, the comic's real target being anyone who sets himself up as guardian of society ('Who watches the watchmen?'). Mark White argues the potbellied second Nite Owl is the truest hero on Aristotelian terms: his courage in the tenement fire and the prison break hits the mean between Laurie's caution and Rorschach's recklessness, making him a flourishing moral exemplar whom John Doris's situationism fails to unseat. Alex Nuttall asks whether Rorschach was wrong to walk out and expose Veidt, using Kant's murderer-at-the-door case to show there is a duty not to lie but no duty to tell the truth (blame falls on Veidt), while act and rule utilitarianism both counsel silence.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Origin and Desires as Monster Makers in the Witcher
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Swanstrom and Lyle test medieval theories of monstrosity against the show: Stregobor's Curse of the Black Sun echoes Aristotle's, Avicenna's, and Aquinas's celestial-influence explanations of fetal mutation (though even they would not convict Renfri by birthday alone), while Yennefer's spine and infertility invoke Aquinas on failed generation and women as 'deformed males,' with witchers cast as Aquinas's mules - an engineered, infertile natural kind. They argue that neither origin nor appearance but motivation and virtue make a monster: Renfri's revenge, Nivellen's rape of the priestess, and Stregobor's vivisection of girls are Aristotelian 'bestial' habit and vicious character, not mean-relative virtue. Geralt's shifting telos, from monster-slayer protecting humans to protector of Ciri (knighted by Queen Meve), shows even a mutant can develop virtue, so mutations, heritage, and gender cannot be what monstrosity is.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Plato and Aristotle on the Role of Soul in Taking the Rock to the Hole
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Daniel Gallagher reads Patrick Sparks's 2005 Elite Eight free-throw clank and miracle buzzer-beater through Plato's tripartite soul: the rational part failed at the line but the spirited part carried the off-balance game-tying three, while the Republic's three classes map onto basketball's workers (Steve Nash's passes), warriors (Dennis Rodman's rebounding), and rulers (John Stockton's leadership). Aristotle's four character types structure learning a jump shot - vicious, weak, self-controlled, and finally virtuous, as reason and inclination harmonize through repetition ('we are what we repeatedly do') - and the golden mean governs shot selection between the ball hog and the compulsive passer, with Michael Jordan as the player whose habituated instincts find the mean. Against Kantian armchair ethics, the jump shot and Kareem's sky hook were discovered by trial and error: virtuous performers set the standard, and we become good shooters by watching and imitating them.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Fourth Hole “Quiet…Please!” Reflections on Golf and Civility
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: McNaron argues that golf promotes civility both empirically and normatively through its rules (self-scoring, self-called penalties) and its etiquette (silence during a swing, care for the course). Using an Aristotelian virtue-ethics frame plus Kekes's 'conduct according to custom' and Calhoun's expressivist account of civility as communicating respect, he treats civility as a mean acquired by habituation and opposes it to skloka, the petty hostility of win-at-all-costs sport. He defends golf's quiet against charges of classism, reads Tiger Woods's outburst at a shutter-clicking photographer as justified anger at an etiquette breach, and names the Ryder Cup's jingoism, boorish spectators, and intrusive media as threats to golf's civil, contemplative character.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Ninth Hole Is Golf Inherently Irrational
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Shier asks why it is not insane to deliberately place obstacles (rules, hazards) between oneself and one's goal, quoting Woodrow Wilson and Mike Seabrook on golf's 'essential lunacy.' He distinguishes internal goals (holing the ball in fewest strokes) from external goals (challenge, competition, fresh air) and, echoing Aristotle, argues excellent conditions lie at the mean between too-hard and too-easy: the regulatory and environmental restrictions make internal goals difficult precisely so external goals become achievable, so the obstacles are rational, not irrational. Using Bernard Suits's view of games as 'the voluntary attempt to overcome unnecessary obstacles,' he applies the framework to handicapping, ad hoc anti-Tiger course changes, and distance technology that threatens golf's characteristic skill set.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Through an imagined Greek play featuring the Spartan 'trembler' Aristodemus and an Avery-Brundage-like IOC president, Jesus Ilundain-Agurruza argues for rethinking the Olympic motto and creed around three Greek virtues, aretE (excellence), andreia (courage), and kalon (noble beauty), grounded in Aristotle's virtue ethics, the mean, and eudaimonia. Using the Spartans exercising on the eve of Thermopylae, he defends a collaborative, non-instrumental conception of competition against record-obsession and cheating, exemplified by Eugenio Monti and Cecil Healy. He closes with Camus's Sisyphus, arguing the athlete pushes the rock in the spirit of aretE, spending energy joyfully 'just because,' turning punishment into sport.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Roberts argues that across Lee's 'Father Knows Best' trilogy (Pushing Hands, The Wedding Banquet, Eat Drink Man Woman) the clash between traditional Confucian values and Western modernity is best resolved by the virtue ethics of Confucius and Aristotle rather than by deontology or utilitarianism. Master Chu literally refusing to be pushed, the Gaos accepting Winston's homosexual relationship, and Chef Chu adapting to his daughters all require Aristotle's golden mean and habituated virtue, which accommodate special relationships and situations. Kant's categorical imperative (rejecting paternalism as treating persons as means) and Mill's harm principle are shown to be too rule-bound to reconcile tradition with modern individualism.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: LaRocca reads The Insider as a study of contracts, conscience and courage. He argues that when Jeffrey Wigand stops calculating consequences ('Fuck it. Let's go to court.') he becomes a Kantian: his testimony has moral worth because it is done from duty and the categorical imperative, not from the utilitarian hedonic calculus of Bentham and Mill that Bergman, Wallace and Scruggs press on him. Wigand's whistleblowing is then framed through Aristotle's account of courage as a mean between recklessness and cowardice, with Wigand as the 'citizen soldier' who acts from conscience while Mike Wallace exemplifies the coward who exceeds in fear.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Bamboozled Philosophy through Blackface
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Flory argues Bamboozled deliberately makes its own audience laugh at Mantan's blackface coon routines to force self-reflection on how minstrel stereotypes still shape perceptions of African Americans. He reads Pierre Delacroix's shifting defenses of the show (free speech, art, 'get over slavery,' a simple-minded 'who is to judge' moral relativism) through Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance,' and his self-loathing through Fanon's struggle with racialization. Flory frames Lee as an Aristotelian gadfly: like Socrates, Lee arouses appropriately proportioned righteous anger (the Golden Mean) at injustice and goads viewers to philosophize, punishing Delacroix, Manray, and the Maumaus in a Manichaean moral structure to drive home minstrelsy's dehumanizing harm.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
aristotle-golden-mean.title: A Spielbergian Ethics of the Family in Saving Private Ryan and The Color Purple
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Clewis defines a 'Spielbergian ethics of the family,' a care-based virtue ethics holding that we owe unique obligations to family and close friends grounded in personal identity, and contrasts it with utilitarian and Kantian approaches. In Saving Private Ryan the squad-as-family and the Ryan brotherhood explain why Miller says Ryan must 'earn this' and why living an ordinary good life suffices; in The Color Purple sisterhood (Nettie/Celie), fatherhood, and motherhood ground obligations of care, forgiveness, and reconciliation. He evaluates the view's feasibility while warning it neglects wider social influences and the is/ought gap.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 30. Good Guys Don’t Wear White
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Lindsey Schwartz argues punk is virtue ethics in action: a DIY version of Aristotle's account of becoming virtuous through practice, habituation, and practical wisdom, where no one ever simply IS good and the point is perpetual becoming. Punk heroes serve as Aristotelian exemplars - Ian MacKaye (self-reliance, straight edge, Dischord Records), Jeff Ott (near-obscene value coherence, rejecting 'ought implies can' while defending Green Day from sellout pieties), Billie Joe Armstrong (humility, giving his guitar to a fan) - and Protest the Hero exemplifies the doctrine of the mean, where courage is calculation of the right action relative to circumstances, not moderation. Punk's pendulum between pious self-deprivation and soulless self-compromise is the space between vices, and its ethic is learned by doing: 'Try. Try. Try.'

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 6. The Morality of Mike’s Manifesto
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: The Gibsons analyze Mike Ehrmantraut's code—'if you make a deal with somebody, you keep your word'—through virtue ethics and Stoicism. Aristotle's function argument and Golden Mean partly vindicate Mike's counsel toward temperance and restraint (not carrying a gun, sparing the Salamanca driver), yet Aristotle's claim that 'bad people are full of regrets' marks him as a flawed 'wicked' man given his inner turmoil over breaking his son. They read his calm as Stoic (Marcus Aurelius's Meditations on controlling the mind, Spartan simplicity), and weigh Kant's intent-based defense of his killing the dirty cops Hoffman and Fensky against Mill's social-rule view of sanctionable wrongs.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 12. A Cave of His Own Making
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Golden reinterprets Plato's Allegory of the Cave to argue Chuck enslaves himself in a 'cave of his own making'—his hypochondriacal electromagnetic hypersensitivity—to keep Jimmy accountable and to exact vengeance for Jimmy's unpunished childhood thefts. Using Aristotle's De Anima psychology and the function argument, he places Chuck's imagination (phantasia) below reason: Chuck retains the rationality to serve clients like Mesa Verde and to detect Jimmy's document fraud, but sinks below the Golden Mean into the vices of meanness (short of kindness) and cowardice (short of courage) toward his brother. He adds Kierkegaard's Repetition: Chuck is stuck in backward-looking 'recollection' of vengeance and cannot make the forward, committed 'repetition' of simply being Jimmy's brother.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
aristotle-golden-mean.title: 6. Authenticity in a World of Bullshido
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Falcioni uses Aristotle's doctrine of the mean and Gillian Russell's 'epistemic viciousness in the martial arts' to read Bourdain's obsession with Brazilian jiu-jitsu as a struggle to cultivate the virtues of humility, courage, and authenticity against the vices of 'bullshido' (fraudulent martial arts). He connects Bourdain's craving for BJJ's brutal, ego-slaying honesty to a Heideggerian authenticity, while noting Bourdain's return to old vices near the end.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Lessons Learned
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: McAleer uses the British Office to teach Aristotle's virtue ethics, treating wit as a character virtue that is a mean between the vices of buffoonery (excess) and boorishness (deficiency). David Brent is the buffoon, slave to his need to be thought funny; Gareth Keenan the literalist boor who cannot take or get a joke; and Tim Canterbury the ready-wit whose ironic humor is appropriate to circumstance. McAleer argues wit shows Aristotle's morality is broader than duty or outcome, aiming at eudaimonia, and that humor's uncodifiability, like Wittgenstein's remarks, mirrors how virtue requires practical wisdom rather than rules.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
aristotle-golden-mean.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Nease lays out a game plan for raising ethical children, using Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics – eudaimonia as a flourishing life, virtue as the mean between extremes, and the master-skills of practical wisdom and self-control – as the core, mocking 'character counts' posters as no substitute for early habit-formation. He folds in Kant's motive of duty, Nietzsche's will-to-power (glossed via Janet Jackson's Control) as the drive to master oneself, and argues empathy (Theodor Lipps' inner imitation), self-awareness, concentration (Husserl's foreground/background), and a respect for justice must be cultivated to 'stack the deck' toward a good adult.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
aristotle-golden-mean.title: MOTHERHOOD
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Nin Kirkham applies neo-Aristotelian virtue ethics to define the 'virtues of motherhood' as character dispositions that let a mother flourish (achieve eudaimonia) qua mother. She elaborates three virtues – endurance (commitment, selflessness, and long-view 'vision,' likened to endurance running), liberality (knowing when to let a child go), and moral exemplarity – each analyzed as an Aristotelian mean between vices of excess and deficit, and argues good mothering is learned by example and does not license judging other mothers against one's own ideal.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
aristotle-golden-mean.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Crista Lebens narrates a C-Scow sail on an inland lake — preparing the boat, casting off, coming about, capsizing, returning to the pier — as a journey toward Aristotelian eudaimonia (human flourishing). She argues sailing demands phronesis (practical wisdom) as body-knowledge, that coming about requires the Greek 'middle path' between being 'in irons' and capsizing, and that competence 'cannot be faked' so sailing forces one to live 'in truth' (via Werth's and Kierkegaard's account of the crowd 'in untruth'). Using Borgmann's device/thing distinction, she casts the sailboat as a 'thing' that calls forth skilled engagement, unlike the powerboat as a 'device' of consumption, and links truth to the beauty of a well-trimmed sail.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
aristotle-golden-mean.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Jesse Steinberg and Michael Stuckart distinguish instrumental from intrinsic value (using Frankena's list) across sailing's gear, knowledge, and aesthetics, then argue via Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics that sailing is a route to eudaimonia through the cultivation of virtue. They show sailing exemplifies courage as the golden mean between cowardice and foolhardiness (deciding whether to go out in twenty-knot winds, judging teen solo circumnavigators), being hard-working (the mean between laziness and workaholism), and cleverness (jury-rigging, navigation). They contend sailing demands a broader, deeper range of virtues than golf, bowling, or power-boating, making it an especially rich — though not the only — path to a flourishing, happy life.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Keleher applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics to coffee, arguing that eudaimonia (flourishing, not mere pleasant feeling) is rational activity in accordance with virtue, that the human ergon is reason, and that money, pleasure, and honor are only instrumental to it. She illustrates the golden mean and phronêsis with coffee choices—the temperate drinker like Katherine or Samantha calibrates cups to her own tolerance and circumstances rather than a fixed number—and distinguishes the truly virtuous drinker from the merely continent one who still craves the forbidden 750-calorie frappuccino. She coins the minor virtue of 'javavity,' the habit of drinking good coffee the right way for the right reasons with the right feeling, and suggests that were Aristotle alive, coffee would join his 'external goods,' the proper equipment for doing noble acts.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Andrew Aberdein traces the historical 'interpenetration' of philosophy and pornography — from the French book trade's 'livres philosophiques' and Diderot, d'Argens's Thérèse philosophe, and Sade, back through Aretino's courtesan dialogues to Plato's Symposium (the root of 'platonic love'). He dwells on the medieval 'Lay of Aristotle,' where Phyllis rides Aristotle like a horse, using the image to stage two readings: Aristotle's, that nature (and woman) must submit to the golden mean of reason, versus Phyllis's, that nature cannot. He closes with a paradox aimed at MacKinnon-style subordination arguments: if John Norman's Gor novels show philosophy is less persuasive than porn, then any persuasive argument for censorship must have a false conclusion.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Schick asks whether humans need to alter consciousness (Weil, Maslow's hierarchy, Siegel's animal examples of reindeer, elephants, and rats seeking intoxicants) and concludes we have no such need, though we can flourish from it. He applies Sen and Nussbaum's capabilities approach, arguing cannabis enhances Nussbaum's second (bodily health, via endocannabinoids and medical uses) and fourth (senses, imagination, thought, via enriched music perception and possible creativity) capabilities. Citing Aristotle's and the Buddha's golden mean against abuse, and evidence of no lasting brain harm, he judges paternalistic prohibition an unjustified deprivation of the capabilities needed for a good life.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Brian Treanor argues from Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics that climbing is a crucible for cultivating virtues (arete) that contribute to flourishing (eudaimonia), stressing that virtue is acquired by habituation and lies in a mean 'relative to us'—so casting off on the Bachar-Yerian is courage for a 5.11 leader but rashness for a 5.9 climber. He shows how climbing's self-imposed 'rules' (Tejada-Flores' games) forge courage (feeling the right balance of fear and confidence, as in John Sherman's Fisher Towers epic and Steve House's judicious retreats on K7), humility (honestly measuring oneself against pioneers who used inferior gear, per Chouinard and Messner's 'murder of the impossible'), and reverence for nature (Thoreau, Muir, Brower). His thesis is that in a coddled, technological world climbing is uncommonly well suited to building these excellences of character.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
aristotle-golden-mean.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Baker dismisses common objections to tattoos (shallow individuality, permanence, ugliness) as aesthetic rather than moral, then uses Greco-Roman virtue ethics—quoting Seneca's Moral Epistles on the soul, the balanced psyche, and matching one's norms to one's motivations—to isolate her real target: the 'tough tattoo.' She argues that a badass or tough-guy tattoo appropriates an outlaw subculture's imagery and, per Seneca's warning that approving a little violence approves it all, cultivates a vicious rather than virtuous psyche. Recalling friends who bragged about beatings, she invokes Socratic self-examination ('know thyself') to test whether looking tough is an accurate or worthy self-representation.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
aristotle-golden-mean.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Leigh Duffy pairs the yogic balance of sthira (strength/steadiness) and sukha (ease/openness) in asana with Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, prompted by her own stress-induced seizure while teaching the Nichomachean Ethics. She argues both frameworks make virtue/right balance 'relative to us' — the correct warrior I or the courageous or good-tempered act depends on the individual and moment — and both require self-knowledge and practical reason. Cultivating the mean of sthira and sukha on the mat becomes her model for finding balance among work, relationships, and self-care off it.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
aristotle-golden-mean.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Julinna Oxley argues that yoga ethics is best understood as an Aristotelian virtue ethic rather than a rule-set: the yamas and niyamas name character traits to cultivate, not commands (citing Iyengar that 'violence is a state of mind, not a diet'). Laying out virtue ethics' elements — habituation, the mean, practical reason, community — she derives two paramount 'yogic virtues,' mindfulness and self-discipline/self-improvement, that are relative to each practitioner and community, so no single diet or lifestyle (e.g., vegetarianism, teetotaling) is universally required for the virtuous yogi off the mat.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
aristotle-golden-mean.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: John Rowan and Patricia Hallen build an extended elevator metaphor for dating (Ann and Bob riding floors, pushing buttons to raise or lower intimacy, gravity pulling toward breakup) to capture Heraclitus's insight that a relationship is a reality in constant change, while invoking Plato to insist the conceptual reality of a relationship is as real as physical objects. They define dating as gauging the possibility of eventual commitment, cite Hume's canoe image for implicit communication of shared destination, and ground their strategies—be yourself, go slowly, communicate, befriend—in Aristotle's virtue ethics, treating honesty, courage, and loyalty as habits lying in the golden mean between deficiency and excess (e.g., the Look Who's Talking date who overshares is 'excessively honest').

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
aristotle-golden-mean.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Aeon Skoble uses the characters to argue for Aristotelian virtue ethics over Kantian duty and utilitarian consequence, since right action flows from developed character and practical reason rather than rule-following. He reads Sam's loyalty and Aragorn's temperance as genuine virtue, Boromir as flawed-but-decent (undone by resentment and pride), and Smeagol's swift murder of Deagol as proof the Ring's corrupting power depends partly on prior character. Skoble contends Kant's rules would make Sam's loyalty no better than a Ringwraith's, and utilitarianism's demand for foreknowledge suits only Galadriel, so virtue ethics best fits Tolkien's flawed, developing heroes.

aristotle-golden-mean.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
aristotle-golden-mean.title: Lessons Learned
aristotle-golden-mean.relation: Sean McAleer uses the British Office to teach Aristotle's virtue ethics, treating wit as a virtue that is a mean between the vices of buffoonery (excess) and boorishness (deficiency). David Brent is the buffoon, 'the slave of his sense of humor,' who jests inappropriately; Gareth is the boorish literalist who cannot take or get a joke; Tim is the ready-wit whose ironic humor is appropriate to the situation, exercising practical wisdom (phronesis).
