care-ethics.relation: Hamington surveys a hundred Facebook users and argues, through care ethics — Noddings's 'here I am' disposition and her natural versus ethical caring — that Facebook can make us more ethical, because the stream of small particulars about friends supplies the knowledge that is a necessary condition for caring. He uses Benhabib's concrete other to explain how status updates make distant lives 'real' to us, and confesses his own de-friending of a student over a racist comment as a case of Facebook's convenience making it easy not to care. The chapter ends by claiming Facebook dissolves the binary of close friend versus nodding acquaintance into a postmodern range of fluid, mediating friendships, while insisting caring is learned through the body and merely extended, not replaced, in virtual space.

care-ethics.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
care-ethics.title: Toward Caring
care-ethics.relation: Sylvia models the Doctor on feminist care ethics: Gilligan's response to Kohlberg's justice-tinged scales and Noddings's distinction between natural caring (for Rose, Martha, Peri in 'The Caves of Androzani') and ethical caring, which explains his forgiveness of the Master and compassion for Dalek Caan after genocides. Against utilitarian impartiality — which cannot say why he should save his companion over a stranger — the relationship itself grounds the obligation, while his vengeful moment facing the lone Dalek in 'Dalek' shows what caring burnout looks like.

care-ethics.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
care-ethics.title: Beyond Lies the Other
care-ethics.relation: The section reads Dick's first published story, 'Beyond Lies the Wub,' as the origin of his career-defining theme: the jovial, philosophic wub survives the captain who sees only fresh meat because its empathy is so total it can exchange minds with the man about to slaughter it. Defining empathy as seeing the world from another's viewpoint plus sympathizing (which the cornering cat, predicting the rat's moves, lacks), it ends with Dick's Exegesis: an evil magician-deity occludes our minds until a savior in trash form restores them, and without such a revelation you, the reader, are 'nothing but a robot.'

care-ethics.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
care-ethics.title: Can a Blade Runner Love a Robot
care-ethics.relation: The section contrasts Dick's bleaker novel, where J.R. Isadore's love for the androids dies when they cut the legs off his rare spider and Deckard's union with Rachael is the 'summa of falsity and mechanical motions' that fuels his resolve to destroy them, with the film's redemptive romance built on Rachael being 'more human than human.' It argues the movie preserves Dick's thesis anyway: Roy Batty's final act of saving the enemy who hunted him shows the empathy that makes the replicants persons, perhaps more than human.

care-ethics.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
care-ethics.title: How to Build a Moral Robot
care-ethics.relation: This section draws design morals from Dick's warnings: machines built as ersatz humans deny the value of being human, robotic sexual partners are doomed deceptions (the novel's Deckard-Rachael encounter is the case study), and a genuine artificial moral agent needs empathy 'logically equivalent to agape,' though a machine reasoning on sound moral principles could still count as a limited moral agent with proportionate rights and responsibilities. The Three Stigmata's Palmer Eldritch, returned from deep space as a machine treating humans as resources, shows that the netherward pull toward machinehood threatens humans themselves.

care-ethics.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
care-ethics.title: He Ain’t Heavy, He’s My Other
care-ethics.relation: This section stages Levinas's infinite responsibility for the Other against Heidegger's tendency to treat others as tools for warding off death: J.R. Isidore's one-way care for androids who vivisect a spider, Dick's 'The Android and the Human' warning that androidization means becoming predictable means, and the treatment of animals as the litmus test of humanity. The self becomes real through selfless action (Tagomi saving a stranger, Sweetscent returning to his wife), and because the height separating self and Other descends from Descartes's idea of infinity, meeting the face of the poor stranger, from Radio Free Albemuth's beggar to The Adjustment Bureau's Chairman, is an encounter with God.

care-ethics.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
care-ethics.title: Fifty Ways to Love Your Other
care-ethics.relation: The section reads Levinas's demand to experience the Other's suffering in the Other's place as Dick's empathy made literal: the shifting points of view that blur heroes and villains, Felix Buckman's tears, Molinari developing his people's symptoms, and the empathy boxes bonding users to Mercer's endless stoning, a fraud whose falsity is beside the point because the concern is the real thing. Villains are precisely those who refuse the transfer, and the ordinary one-way gift, buying a stranger a drink with no return, enacts the Golden Rule: even if the universe isn't real, Melina is right, kiss each other anyway.

care-ethics.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
care-ethics.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Jonas-Sebastien Beaudry reads Neverwhere's magic invisibility as a model of real social invisibility: after Richard helps the injured Door he loses his job, his fiancee Jessica, and even the ability to be perceived, joining the homeless, slaves, and Jews under Nazism as people excluded from the moral community whose needs no longer register. Using Arendt's banality of evil to explain everyday indifference and Richard Rorty on torturers who fail to see a 'real' human, he distinguishes radical from partial invisibility, shown in Jessica stepping over the bleeding Door and misreading her need as 'sleep it off.' The remedy is Iris Murdoch's 'loving gaze' of just and careful attention, which seizes Richard before he can rationalize, backed by a practical wisdom about whose needs matter, so that acknowledging the invisible, down to apologizing to a rat in London Below, is what makes both them and us better.

care-ethics.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
care-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Olson opens with her own first session, in which the DM steered her toward a 'sexy Eladrin' miniature in high heels, and asks why women stay away from D&D. She argues the game's mechanics are egalitarian—identical power lists for male and female characters, echoing Plato's Republic claim that women guard the city by the same nature as men—and that party cooperation embodies the relational, care-based feminist ethic Marilyn Friedman and Angela Bolte oppose to male-coded individualism. The trouble is culture, not system: sexualized miniatures that objectify female bodies, tokenism, harassment, and marketing that ignores women, to which female gamers respond by playing male characters like Jenni Dowsett, designing separatist systems such as Portal Worlds, or, like Shelly Mazzanoble, claiming D&D for the 'inner girl'.

care-ethics.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
care-ethics.title: The Wire and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: The Rochas argue that the only two women in the Game, Snoop on the street side and Kima on the police side, embody a 'militant feminism' in the lineage of the Black Panthers' Kathleen Cleaver and the Weather Underground's Bernardine Dohrn: women can excel at anything men can, including violence (Snoop as Marlo's natural soldier, repurposing a Hardware Barn nail gun, wearing womanhood only as a costume), and violence is justified when used for just ends (Kima overcoming fear to police). They then use Gilligan and Noddings's care ethics to explain the finale: Kima's dedication to relationships and care for the overlooked homeless victims lets her discern that McNulty and Freamon's fake-serial-killer scheme is an immoral masculinized rationalization, so she turns in her friends and becomes the show's moral conscience.

care-ethics.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
care-ethics.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Jonas-Sebastien Beaudry defends a 'moderate speciesism' built on relationships rather than individual capacities: Taylor's trial strips him of clothes, name, and speech - the symbols of ethical community - showing how institutional speciesism rationalizes domination behind the Sacred Scrolls' Declaration-of-Independence-style self-evidence. Against Singer's anti-speciesist challenge that any distinctively human capacity is shared by some animals or missing from some humans, he argues both camps wrongly pedestal intrinsic traits, and reads Taylor's love for the mute Nova together with the failed Project Nim as showing that within-species bonds of love, care, and family are genuinely and justifiably valuable without licensing mistreatment. Bernard Williams's 'The Human Prejudice' - should we surrender to superior invading aliens? - marks where impartial anti-speciesism leads, while Zaius's 'Man is evil' and the doomsday-bomb ending show extreme speciesism as self-fulfilling prophecy.

care-ethics.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
care-ethics.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Kathleen Poorman Dougherty sets Kant's universal, emotion-free morality (echoed in Kohlberg's justice stages and Judge Abernathy's 'blind court' claim in 'Infamy') against Carol Gilligan's care ethic, which she says fits Saint Alicia far better: Alicia's practical advice to Jennifer Lewis in the pilot, driving Kenny home in 'Home', and telling Kenny's father 'I care a lot more about your son than he does' show connection producing both better morality and better lawyering. Feminist theorists like Nel Noddings and Sara Ruddick treat this care orientation as morally superior, not merely different, but the chapter's later sections weigh the cost: Kalinda's burnout warning, Alicia's resentment at always hand-holding clients, and the double bind by which women absorb society's unpaid caring labor. The verdict is that care is genuinely moral, but it must become a shared burden.

care-ethics.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
care-ethics.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: The chapter argues HIMYM offers two complementary feminist icons: Robin embodies personal autonomy and independence - fighting from 'but, um' early-morning shifts to lead anchor, and grieving infertility as stolen autonomy rather than lost motherhood - while Lily, and even more Marshall, exemplify Carol Gilligan's feminist care ethics with its emphasis on emotion over impartiality, cooperation over competition, and partiality toward loved ones. Aristotle's golden mean supplies the test Robin passes by balancing career and love instead of pushing one to an extreme. The twist that a male character best exemplifies care ethics, with Lily bridging the two moral outlooks, is offered as the show's progressive complexity about gender.

care-ethics.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
care-ethics.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Robison-Greene argues Rawlsian ideal theory breaks down at Litchfield: Soso's hunger strike gets only cosmetic concessions from Caputo, Sophia's WAC human-rights platform loses to Taystee's realism, and Piper learns the council 'is basically bullshit,' showing how idealization made by the powerful ignores the lived facts of Mendoza's abusive marriage, Jimmy's 'compassionate' death sentence, and Sophia's denied hormones. Against taking a 'moral holiday' in prison, she proposes care ethics, with role-based duties sensitive to actual circumstances, as the morality that fits life inside, and suggests non-ideal theory may fit the outside world too.

care-ethics.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
care-ethics.title: 5. Every Lonely Monster Needs a Companion
care-ethics.relation: Gadsden asks why a near-omnipotent Time Lord needs companions at all and tests four hypotheses against his solo meltdowns—executing Solomon in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship,' nearly murdering Jex in 'A Town Called Mercy,' and declaring himself 'Time Lord Victorious' in 'The Waters of Mars.' He rejects the Lord Acton power-corrupts hypothesis via Glaucon's ring story in Plato's Republic, since powerless companions offer no threat of reprisal or dishonor, and qualifies J.J. Sylvia's care-ethics 'empathetic link' because the Doctor cares for non-human species like the Star Whale too. He favors two answers: Hume's fact/value gap as a millennium-long moral myopia ('I can't see it anymore,' the deleted 'Flesh and Stone' confession), and Aristotle's point in the Nicomachean Ethics that only virtuous friends—moral peers who mirror us—can expose the Doctor's blind spots, like his 'God Complex.'

care-ethics.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
care-ethics.title: 12. Should We Really Care about the Crawleys
care-ethics.relation: Jones takes up the charge that loving Downton seduces viewers into admiring inequality, and answers that the Crawleys deserve our care because birth, not choice, gave them their position, so they should be judged only by what they do with it: Grantham paying for Mrs. Patmore's eye surgery, Violet throwing the flower contest after Isobel's challenge, the family gradually embracing Branson. He reads the show as a manifesto for social change through sympathetic contact between classes rather than Irish-style revolt - befriend the rich and their good nature will start to level the playing field. His own objection is that this makes change partly the responsibility of the less privileged, from Thomas being asked to soften Carson's homophobia to the poor being asked to be nice to the rich today.

care-ethics.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
care-ethics.title: 11. I Ain’t No Hollaback Girl!
care-ethics.relation: Callens explains Carol's killing of Lizzie in "The Grove" through Kohlberg's stages of moral development, arguing Carol reasons at the post-conventional level (pre-apocalypse law and punishment no longer bind) while Rick, Hershel, and Daryl stay conventional, and then layers Maslow's hierarchy of needs on top: because survival needs are perpetually threatened, characters regress between stages, and only self-actualized Carol accepts reality and makes group-preserving choices like executing Lizzie and mercy-killing Karen and David. Gilligan's justice-versus-care critique supplies the gendered frame - Carol moves to the middle of the justice-care continuum, her diminished care (unlike Season Two's grief over Sophia) is what makes her post-conventional, and her non-lethal Terminus rescue contrasts with Rick's summary execution of Gareth.

care-ethics.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
care-ethics.title: 12. They Just Want Me to Be Like Them
care-ethics.relation: Castro and Beisecker diagnose Lizzie's walker fixation as prolonged grief disorder: she displaces grief for her father onto the walker "Nick," denies final death ("They're just different"), and treats reanimation as a viable form of life she might join ("Maybe I should change"). They argue Carol's suppressive guardianship - the "look at the flowers" distraction and calling Lizzie weak and confused - aggravated the avoidance at the root of the disorder, so Lizzie's "transformation" of Mika was a misguided moral experiment rather than murder by a monster. The chapter contrasts Tyreese's affirming care ("You each do things your own way") as the guardianship that might have saved the girls, and notes Carol's refusal to let Lizzie reanimate denies her the dying-wish courtesy the group once granted Jim.

care-ethics.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
care-ethics.title: 7. And the Most Despicable Jessica Lange Character Is . .
care-ethics.relation: Ranks Jessica Lange's characters from least to most despicable using moral philosophy: Sister Jude earns credit for acting from duty (reporting the Nazi Dr. Arden at personal risk, Kant-style) and for genuinely feeling remorse; Elsa Mars partly honors the matriarchal obligations of care ethics but lacks Aristotle's habitual virtue and moderation, selling Bette and Dot to Dandy for fame; Constance Langdon abuses and effectively murders her disabled children; and Fiona Goode, motivated exclusively by youth, beauty, and power, murders her Supreme and torments Cordelia - never once acting out of concern for others.

care-ethics.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
care-ethics.title: 11. The Mother of All Bombs
care-ethics.relation: Uses Hannah Arendt's On Violence — violence begets a more violent world, and WWII birthed the cold war rather than peace — to read Part 8, where the Trinity test, via the entity Judy/Mother, births BOB, whose garmonbozia-hunger is nuclear-age destruction feeding on female pain. Carol Gilligan's account of patriarchal silencing of women's voices (Naido's shut eyes, Laura's violated diary, the Persephone pattern of girls who must "die") and Gilbert and Gubar's dying "Angel in the House" frame Laura as both born from the Fireman and Señorita Dido as an antidote to the Bomb and destroyed by the mother wound Sarah Palmer carries. Against the toxic masculinity of Mr. C, Richard, and Chad, the show's good men — Cooper, the Trumans, Hawk, Bobby — embody Gilligan's ethic of care, and the chapter ends by demanding America put down its weapons and listen to women.

care-ethics.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
care-ethics.title: 9. Machines Who Care
care-ethics.relation: Weiss reads 'The Lonely' and 'I Sing the Body Electric' as anticipations of today's debate over 'relational artifacts' — Turkle's sociable robots, the Sparrows' claim that robotic aged care is unethical, Coeckelbergh's rebuttal — asking, with Anne, whether an electric grandma 'doesn't sound so good.' Corry's Alicia and the children's electric grandma show care being bought as an assembly-line product for the lonely, and he presses the details: why the caring robots are female and serve water, why Alicia arrives in a box and is summarily shot in the face when no longer needed, and what it says about a culture that maroons people in loneliness and then sells the technical fix.

care-ethics.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
care-ethics.title: 15. June the Stoic
care-ethics.relation: Lequien asks how June might endure Gilead and answers with Epictetus: like the slave-philosopher, she can locate freedom in what is 'up to her'—detaching from her body during the Ceremony ('What he is fucking is the lower part of my body'), relinquishing property, and learning not to call husband or daughter her own. He tests alternatives—Camus's question of suicide (the shatterproof glass), utilitarianism (the coerced 'We are very happy'), Tronto's care ethics (Gilead smothers the sorority that could make care meaningful), and the Particicution as a licensed Two Minutes Hate—before concluding that 'Nolite te bastardes carborundorum' functions as June's Stoic mantra: mastery of her own responses is the one victory the Sons of Jacob cannot take.

care-ethics.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
care-ethics.title: 14. Friends Don’t Lie
care-ethics.relation: Bowman tests Hawkins friendships against Aristotle's three kinds in the Nicomachean Ethics: Dustin and Lucas's shared-comics pleasure collapses into rivalry over Max, Nancy and Jonathan's utility ends once Will and Barb are found, and Barb's fatal poolside loyalty to Nancy, though one-directional, is a friendship of virtue. Nietzsche's ideal of friends who strengthen us through conflict recasts those very fights (Lucas confronting Eleven's power misuse) as the best friendship, care ethics (Gilligan and Noddings) makes the mutual one-caring Party the real answer to who teaches Eleven friendship, and Derrida's Politics of Friendship grounds democracy and society itself in such everyday reciprocity, which is why Eleven's 'friends don't lie' compass pulls her back from Kali's violence to close the gate.

care-ethics.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
care-ethics.title: 24. Fred Rogers and the Ethics of Care
care-ethics.relation: A.G. Holdier places Rogers squarely in the care ethics of Gilligan and Noddings: against Kohlberg's justice stages (the Heinz dilemma recast with Henrietta Pussycat and X the Owl), care means Joan Tronto's four elements of attentiveness, responsibility, competence, and responsiveness, shown in the Clemmons kiddie pool, the Soviet guest understood through an interpreter, and 'just the way you are.' Extending care to animals via Rogers's vegetarianism and Carol Adams's 'absent referent,' and to the self via the closing benediction, he argues Rogers embodied care as particular, embodied practice rather than formula.

care-ethics.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
care-ethics.title: 15. Chidi’s Indecision
care-ethics.relation: Vannatta argues Chidi's indecision exposes the shared flaw of the Big Three theories, Kantian deontology, Bentham and Mill's consequentialism, and Aristotle's virtue ethics of the golden mean: their rationalism pretends moral conflict can be eliminated by applying the correct rule, when Chidi's trolley terror shows moral situations are experienced as genuinely uncertain. Dewey's 'Three Independent Factors in Morals', the Good of desire, the Right of duty, and the Virtuous of communal praise, legitimizes that felt uncertainty and explains Eleanor's talent for finding option C between binary dilemmas. The chapter concludes that the show's real, unspoken moral theory is care ethics: partiality, relationship maintenance, and moral growth through the experience of being cared for, as Eleanor learns from Chidi's friendship rather than his lectures.

care-ethics.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
care-ethics.title: Introduction
care-ethics.relation: Book introduction: recounts how the 1979 cast were the first casualties of the Chestburster scene (real butcher-shop organs, Veronica Cartwright fainting), then previews the volume's payload - personhood questions about Ash, Bishop, David and the Ripley clone; Marx on why Weyland-Yutani sacrifices crews for profit; Plato's Republic on children in warfare via Newt; Lovecraftian cosmic horror; feminist readings of Ripley as care ethicist and mother; and continental takes - Xenomorphs as Nietzsche's Ubermensch, Camus on Ripley-8's refusal to commit suicide, and Sartre on a Xenomorph's right to resist us.

care-ethics.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
care-ethics.title: Not Bad, for a [Wo]man
care-ethics.relation: Argues Ripley's crossed-heart promise to Newt shows partialist care rightly overriding impartial justice: Kant, Mill, and Rachels demand everyone count for one, but Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg and Noddings's carer-cared-for relation - completed in Newt's 'I knew you'd come' - explain why Ripley duct-tapes two guns together and descends into the hive. Her flexible, relational problem-solving (the lighter-sprinkler trick against the Facehuggers, learning the pulse rifle) beats Gorman's mission-first command, and the trolley-style arithmetic she rejects when the one on the tracks is her little girl is not a moral failing; even nuking the Queen's eggs raises Singer-style speciesism questions.

care-ethics.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
care-ethics.title: A Professional, a Mother, and Someone Who Cares
care-ethics.relation: Asks whether Ripley is a feminist and answers 'only sometimes': her quarantine refusal ('Yes, I read you. The answer is negative') and her reasons for killing the Alien3 specimen ('a lot of innocent people will die') invoke rules, chain of command, and anonymous future victims - Kohlberg's post-conventional reasoning, not Gilligan's care voice - whereas the hot-chocolate scene with Newt and the unhesitating hive rescue exhibit the care-focused feminism of Gilligan and Noddings. Against the status-oriented reading of Vasquez's 'have you ever been mistaken for a man?' exchange, Ripley emerges as atypical of either stereotype: a professional, a mother, and someone who cares.

care-ethics.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
care-ethics.title: Repairing Our Worlds
care-ethics.relation: Fice reads ATLA through the feminist ethics of care, using Joan Tronto's phases of caring-about, taking care of, and care-giving to analyze Katara: freeing Aang from the iceberg, offering to heal Zuko's scar in the Crystal Catacombs, and her full arc as the Painted Lady feeding, healing, and freeing a polluted village. Care also misfires ('Imprisoned') and is devalued as feminine 'women's work' when Toph calls Katara motherly ('The Runaway'), a myth the chapter rejects. Care scales politically too: the Gaang's defeat of Fire Nation imperialism is care repairing the world, while Azula's indifference to Ty Lee and Mai marks her villainy.

care-ethics.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
care-ethics.title: Repairing Our Worlds
care-ethics.relation: Fice reads Katara through Joan Tronto's care ethics, tracking the phases in episodes: 'caring about' the refugees on 'The Serpent's Pass' and Zuko's scar in the Crystal Catacombs, 'taking care of' in freeing Aang from the iceberg, and 'care-giving' in 'The Painted Lady,' where she feeds, heals, and cleans up a polluted factory town. Care misfires are part of the theory, as when she pushes Haru to earthbend in 'Imprisoned' and gets him arrested, and Toph's 'motherly' jab lets the chapter reject the myth that care is essentially feminine, citing bell hooks. The larger claim is political: the Gaang's war against Fire Nation imperialism is care at world scale, repairing the world so its people can live well.

care-ethics.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
care-ethics.title: What Not to Do as a Parent
care-ethics.relation: The chapter pinpoints Marie's failure in Arkangel using Feinberg's parental-rights framework: by filtering out every fright (the neighbor's dog, her father's stroke) she violated Sara's right to an open future, misconstrued her welfare and protection rights, and stunted the empathy that makes a child a fully functioning human being. Aristotle's golden mean frames over-parenting as a vice of excess — as damaging as neglect — and Ruddick's maternal ethics of care also convicts Marie, since mothering requires fostering growth and social acceptability, not just preserving life. The Philip K. Dick comparison lands the conclusion: an android is distinguished from a human only by lacking empathy, so Marie has manufactured a partial android rather than raised a child.

care-ethics.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
care-ethics.title: Learning from Mia’s Mistakes
care-ethics.relation: The chapter grades each of Mia's escalations in Crocodile — helping Rob hide the cyclist's body, killing Rob fifteen years later, then killing Shazia, her husband, and baby Ali to keep the secret — under Kant's categorical imperative (the cover-up cannot be universalized and treats persons as means), the utilitarian calculus (which also condemns every killing once the widow's suffering and Mia's guilt are counted), and feminist care ethics, which rejects her defense that she killed to protect her family because care obligations never cancel proportionality and others' rights. Aristotle's virtue ethics supplies the diagnosis: Mia's undoing is lack of practical wisdom — every split-second choice (which she never had time to deliberate) went wrong because she lacked virtuous habits. The chapter urges practicing everyday virtue so we never take the first step down her path.

care-ethics.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
care-ethics.title: How Far I'll Go
care-ethics.relation: Maps the four waves of feminism onto Disney princess history: Snow White, Cinderella, and Aurora as chattel passed from parents to fairies to princes, betraying even first-wave rights; Beauvoir's 'one is not born but becomes a woman' and Friedan's feminine mystique explaining why the original trio's happiness is measured by marriage. Third-wave princesses are read with Wolf's beauty myth (Ariel and Jasmine as iron maidens), Butler's gender performativity, and Gilligan's care ethics (Ariel's and Belle's contextual, caring moral reasoning versus their fathers' principles). The fourth-wave princesses from Tiana to Moana need no man at all while male leads (Naveen, Flynn, Kristoff, Maui) become vulnerable sidekicks, ending with #GiveElsaAGirlfriend and the thought that equality is balance rather than sameness.

care-ethics.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
care-ethics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Olson's first D&D Encounters session handed her a sexualized female miniature in a chainmail bikini and high-heeled boots, and the chapter audits the game as a feminist would: research on the 'token girl' and male-default storytelling, women like Dowsett pushed to play male characters to be taken seriously, and harassment ranging from 'date at least one of the party or bring food' to condescension toward women in the industry. Against this she argues the rules themselves are egalitarian — identical power pools for male and female characters, embodying Plato's Republic claim that women 'are by nature the same with respect to guarding the city', and even the evil deities are stereotyped symmetrically (scheming Lolth and Tiamat versus war-god patrons of power) — while the collaborative party structure (clerics healing strikers, shared goals) has exactly the care-ethical, anti-individualist flavor Friedman and Bolte attribute to women's moral perspectives. Sexism is thus a consequence of unreflective practices, marketing that ignores women, and industry culture rather than the game; all-female systems like Portal Worlds are a real response but, she worries, separatism risks deepening the divide.

care-ethics.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Opening from the author's own grief — she nearly stopped playing Fallout 4 because its murdered spouse and kidnapped son echoed the loss of her real infant son — the chapter applies the ethics of care of Gilligan, Noddings, and Tronto to Fallout's wasteland. Care relationships structure the games: the Fallout 3 father whose flight from Vault 101 propels the plot, Dogmeat's loyal responsiveness as relational reciprocity, and the Fallout 4 son Shaun, where caring for your child collides with caring for a Commonwealth his Institute endangers. Settlement-building, faction choice (Lyons's Brotherhood handing out clean water versus the Railroad's liberation of synths), and even the Black Widow perk path that saves Megaton all become care-laden moral acts — care as protest against the wasteland's ethos of bare survival.

care-ethics.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
care-ethics.title: Lois: Portrait of a Mother (Or, Nevermind Death, Motherhood is a Bitch)
care-ethics.relation: Empey frames mothering (following Sara Ruddick's 'Maternal Thinking') as a disciplined response to a child's demands of preservation, growth, and social acceptability — even for a matricidal psychopath like Stewie. Lois cultivates the virtues of prudence (safeguarding the Rainy Day Fund against Peter's volcano insurance), tolerance, and peacefulness (enduring Stewie's lamp blows and Peter's laziness; her two Christmas and 'Lethal Weapons' violent eruptions are cured by appeals to her motherhood). The chapter then turns political: drawing on Okin, Williams, and Hays, it shows mothers' vulnerability by marriage, the incompatibility of the 'ideal worker' and 'intensive mother' models, and Peter's devaluing of Lois's theater directing. Peter's basement bar, where Lois sings nightly while minding the kids, models the institutional coordination (family plus economy) mothers need — until Peter's jealousy wrecks it.

care-ethics.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
care-ethics.title: 15. Chidi’s Indecision
care-ethics.relation: Surveys the 'Big Three' through the show: Kantian deontology (Chidi's boots lie, Tahani's mere-means charity), Bentham and Mill's utilitarianism (Jason's alligator frame-up, the trolley simulation), and Aristotle's golden mean (courage between Jason's rashness and Chidi's paralyzed deficiency), arguing their shared rationalism cannot accommodate the real uncertainty Chidi feels. John Dewey's 'Three Independent Factors in Morals' — the Good, the Right, and the Virtuous as irreducible — explains why Chidi sees only binaries while Eleanor finds 'option C' and imagines the Medium Place. The chapter concludes the show's unstated moral theory is care ethics: relational selves, justified partiality toward friends, and moral growth through the experience of being cared for, as when Chidi models care rather than lecturing it.

care-ethics.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
care-ethics.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Donovan and Richardson read the Maltusian split, with the male Guardians banning emotion through the Book of Oa on Oa and the female Zamarons leaving to found the violet light of love on Zamaron, as the Western association of men with reason and women with emotion. They deploy Gilligan's different-voice reply to Kohlberg, the Pythagorean table of opposites via Genevieve Lloyd, Hegel's exclusion of women from the public sphere, and Jaggar's liberal-feminist critique of 'ahistorical' reason, whose comic-book analogue is the third law banning relationships between Lanterns. The chapter ends by arguing the standoff is a false dichotomy the comics themselves begin to dissolve: Kyle's 'Lanterns with heart' speech to the Guardians, the repeal of the third law, and the Indigo Tribe's plan to recombine the seven corps into the white light of creation.

care-ethics.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
care-ethics.title: NOTES
care-ethics.relation: Reads the show's eclipse icon against Plato's sun of the good — goodness has become hard to discern — and tests four theories of evil on the characters: Socrates' claim that no one errs knowingly is half-confirmed since villains like Angela and Nathan always take themselves to be doing right; Aristotle's akrasia and vice as an excess or deficiency of disposition fit Sylar's blood-scrawled 'Forgive me' apartment and his uncontrolled hunger; and Nietzsche's Übermensch and pre-Christian master morality raise the uncomfortable question of why Sylar preying on inferiors is not heroic like Achilles. The chapter's endorsed answer is Gilligan's ethics of care: the heroes are good because they care — Matt for Molly and Daphne, Bennet for Claire — while evil is the absence of care, though Bennet's authoritarian, family-only care shows that care itself must be both widened and restrained.

care-ethics.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
care-ethics.title: NOTES
care-ethics.relation: Explains the seemingly incomprehensible things Heroes characters do for family by sorting their motives into three theories of family obligation: universal justice (framed by Socrates confronting Euthyphro for prosecuting his own father), care ethics' partiality to loved ones, and Confucian role-based duty with its asymmetrical parent–child, husband–wife, and sibling obligations. Noah Bennet turns out to be Confucian in practice ('I'm your father, Claire Bear') despite his universalist Company rhetoric, Hiro defies Kaito's Confucianism for the greater good while Kaito still teaches him the sword because that is a father's role, Niki and Janice act from care while D.L. and Micah act from roles, Mohinder's duty is Confucian sonship to his dead father, and the Haitian kills his own brother Baron precisely because stopping him is his brotherly role.

care-ethics.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
care-ethics.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Averill argues that Katniss's morality is built on care for particular people rather than impartial principle: she volunteers for Prim, protects Rue because the girl resembles her sister, and spares a wounded District 2 soldier at the Nut because he recalls her father and the Seam. Measured against Kant's impartial justice perspective (embodied by Thresh sparing Katniss to repay a debt to Rue), she falls short — but Gilligan's care perspective and Noddings's distinction between natural and ethical caring recast this as a valid, even heroic, moral development. Using Noddings, the chapter traces Katniss's arc from natural care for Prim toward ethical care for strangers and even enemies, and reads her assassination of Coin as care for all of Panem's future children rather than revenge. Care, the chapter concludes, can even justify violence when it protects the vulnerable.

care-ethics.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
care-ethics.title: 5 Feminism and Indiana Jones A Field Guide
care-ethics.relation: Kate Schmidt applies feminist media tests (Bechdel, sexy lamp, Mako Mori, Pierce, Landau) to show the films usually fail — Willie is a screaming prop and human shield in Temple, the eyelid-writing student exists only to display Indy's sex appeal, and all four films fail the Bechdel Test — while Marion, Spalko, and above all Elsa in The Last Crusade are mixed cases with partial autonomy. Drawing on Iris Marion Young's account of women as Other and Carol Gilligan's care ethics, she argues Crusade is the series' most feminist film not for its women but for its men: Indy's open hurt after Elsa's betrayal and the father-son reconciliation embody care ethics against 'boys don't cry' toxic masculinity. She concludes that one can love flawed media without endorsing its sexism.

care-ethics.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Kolb reads the whole franchise through Carol Gilligan's ethics of care and the ecofeminism of Ariel Salleh and Mary Mellor: Max begins as a caregiver in an egalitarian marriage, Toecutter's gang and the Citadel embody toxic masculinity, and Aunty Entity shows women can administer patriarchal capitalism too. In Fury Road, 'We are not things,' the milking mothers, and water branded as Aqua Cola literalize Salleh's claim that capitalist patriarchy treats women and nature as resources. The Vuvalini, the Keeper of the Seeds, Max washing in mother's milk, and his voluntary blood transfusion to Furiosa enact the ethic of care as the film's saving alternative to domination.

care-ethics.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
care-ethics.title: “To a Place Where We Know We Are Loved”
care-ethics.relation: Myers grades the moral development of the Sterling Cooper cast with Kohlberg's justice stages and Gilligan's ethics of care in order to find Aristotelian friendships, which require equals in moral development who wish each other good for the other's sake. Don and Peggy emerge as moral equivalents, each hiding a dark secret (the stolen identity; the baby given away) and each having done for the other what no one else could, from the hospital visit ('Move forward') to Don's 'nobody understands that, but you do' recruitment pitch; Joan and Roger form a second pair whose mutual esteem survives his marriage to Jane and her departure, shown when he trusts her to build Sterling Cooper Draper Pryce. Closing with Aristotle's claim that friendship holds states together, the chapter gives the new agency a better-than-average chance because these friendships are 'not for sale.'

care-ethics.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
care-ethics.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
care-ethics.relation: Frames the show's tension between the masculine public sphere (the chapel table, guns, club politics) and the feminine domestic sphere that actually sustains life, using Aristotle's oikos/polis division and Arendt's The Human Condition on the public/private realms. Gemma, dismissed as 'just an old lady,' proves the private sphere's power: she brought the club to Charming, orchestrates Jax's rise to the presidency, and converts her rape by Weston's LOAN goons into family solidarity that puts Jax's VP patch back on. Gilligan's and Baier's ethics of care then reads Lyla's abortion as a caring choice about family size, Tara's 'my job as your old lady is to be strong when and where you can't be' as care turned to strength, and Gemma's care curdling into retributive justice against Clay.

care-ethics.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Argues Star Trek functions like the Greek myths Nussbaum describes: modern tales of transformation (Gary Mitchell in "Where No Man Has Gone Before", Charlie X, Roger Korby) that let audiences judge what makes someone human. It rejects the Cartesian reading (Richard Hanley's Is Data Human?) in which Data's humanity is just a matter of being a rational mind, and develops instead a feminist, developmental account of personhood drawn from Annette Baier: persons are "second persons" who learn the arts of personhood from caretakers. Data, Seven of Nine, and Voyager's Doctor, all lacking real childhoods and families, must learn play, touch, love, and interdependence from their crews, with Janeway modeling family for Seven and Kes socializing the Doctor. Picard's farewell to Shinzon in Nemesis and to Data's B-4 caps the claim that humanity is an achievement of self-improvement in relationship, not a fixed essence.

care-ethics.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
care-ethics.title: “So, What Happens If You Take That Thing Off ”
care-ethics.relation: Ebner charts Din Djarin's moral development from a rights-based frame - hierarchy, Guild rules, 'I can bring you in warm, or I can bring you in cold' - to Carol Gilligan's ethics of care, a shift catalyzed by Kuiil's lessons ('You can trade', 'I have spoken') and completed by the Child. He re-reads Gilligan's pharmacy dilemma through 'The Sin', where Mando hijacks a speeder droid at gunpoint, and 'The Marshal', where trading with Cobb Vanth recasts the armor dispute as responsibility toward a threatened town rather than a contest of rights. Djarin's helmet decisions - refusing Omera, unmasking for Mayfeld's facial scan, and finally removing the helmet to say goodbye to Grogu - track his metamorphosis from rules and entitlements to responsibilities and relationships.

care-ethics.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
care-ethics.title: So Mother for That: Taylor Swift and Childless Mothering
care-ethics.relation: Lucy Britt and Brian Britt trace the fan practice of calling childless Swift 'mother' back to the Black and queer ballroom house mothers of Paris Is Burning (Carmen Xtravaganza, Willi Ninja), whose original meaning - relational care and leadership in found families - was mostly lost when Swifties appropriated the term. Using Simone de Beauvoir on femininity, Judith Butler's culturally constructed body, and Audre Lorde on Black mothering as resistance, they argue Swift functions as a postmodern, queered mother whose revisiting of her 'eras' teaches fans to mother their own past selves. Yet her individualism ('You're on your own, kid') blocks the relational politics of care that Joan Tronto's caring democracy and Adriana Cavarero's maternal inclination demand.

care-ethics.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Young uses bell hooks's patriarchal masculinity (with Kate Manne on misogyny as enforcement) to read the show: Jamie is patriarchal terror's product, Rupert's promiscuity and Rebecca's subjection are two sides of male control, and Roy Kent's 'hard man' persona inherits the hardness Nietzsche praised and philosophy's traditional suspicion of emotion. Against this, hooks's definition of love as the will to nurture spiritual growth explains Ted's coaching, the training-room exorcism's shared vulnerability, Sam's openness, and Nate's status-hunger as the struggle to invert the gender pyramid, ending with Nate refusing Rupert's poisoned patriarchal gifts.

care-ethics.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
care-ethics.title: NOTES
care-ethics.relation: Chotiner tests Sarah Connor's plan to shoot Miles Dyson (one innocent life for three billion) against Bentham and Mill's utilitarianism and against Kant's deontology, showing both stall: utilitarianism licenses harvesting the author's organs for transplant patients, while Kant forbids using Dyson as a mere means and even condemns the mall kid's protective lie to the T-1000. Through Kohlberg's Heinz dilemma and Carol Gilligan's discovery that girls reason to preserve relationships rather than from abstract principles, he argues T2 stages the film's own answer: John and the reprogrammed T-101 care for Dyson's wounds and enlist him in destroying his research instead of using or sparing him on principle. 'I know now why you cry' caps the claim that morality needs the emotional capacity to care, not just rational maxims, with Sarah's gender-role reversal (she blasts through the elevator roof while the Terminator is the 'perfect mother') framing the whole argument.

care-ethics.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: This multi-author epilogue collects short 'cutting-room-floor' reflections on poignant WoT quotes. Cooke reads Ingtar's confession as the existential fear of historical oblivion (historia as both history and story) driving a patriot into Darkfriendship. DeVan uses Covril's oak-and-wind metaphor to argue arguments strengthen through opposition, marshaling Confucius, Proverbs, al-Kindi, Milton, and Socrates's unexamined life. Held reads Min's arranged-marriage counsel with Nietzsche's amor fati and Epictetus's Heracles to reject resentment of unchosen fate. Pike reads Nynaeve sentencing the sul'dam through Carol Gilligan's and Annette Baier's ethics of care versus obligation (care can judge more harshly, per C.S. Lewis). Xhignesse reads the oak-and-willow line as Aesop woven into Randland's background.

care-ethics.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Johnson-Moxley tests Perez's lasso of truth - which makes people face truths about themselves, like being dragged from Plato's cave - against four ethical touchstones: Kantian duty (truth-telling as a perfect duty, respect for autonomy), utilitarianism, virtue ethics, and care ethics. Cases drive the argument: binding Ares so he sees his apocalypse annihilates what he rules, freeing Vanessa from Dr. Psycho's false memories only with her permission, and lashing two warlords into 'twins of pain' to end bloodshed. She concludes via Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity that compelling truth is justified only to restore someone's rational self-direction, never paternalistically, with Gandhi's satyagraha ('truth-force') as the model of active, compassionate truth-telling.

care-ethics.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Bein argues Wonder Woman uniquely fuses two supposedly incompatible moralities: bushido - Nitobe's eight samurai virtues, Sun Tzu's benevolence of ending war swiftly, worthy-opponent rituals mirrored in superhero costumes - and the feminist ethics of care Gilligan and Noddings built against a Western canon (Aristotle, Kant) that called women too emotional for morality. Wonder Woman's killing of Maxwell Lord to free Superman is re-read as the care-ethical beach case: saving your own child over a stranger's is not a failure of impartiality, and in his Gotham-versus-Themyscira invasion thought experiment she would defend Gotham because its people are vulnerable non-combatants, not because a utilitarian ledger favors it.

care-ethics.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
care-ethics.title: Notes
care-ethics.relation: Chavez, Gavaler, and Goldberg trace Marston's 'Love Leader' kink - bracelets of submission, Venus girdles, Paradise Island bondage games, Earth One's collaring of Steve Trevor - to nineteenth-century maternalist feminism, then map the care ethics of Gilligan, Noddings, and Tronto onto both the comic and real-world BDSM. Reform (later Transformation) Island embodies a care-based alternative to punishment: rather than retribution, von Gunther and Irene are transformed by loving authority into people who save their captors, and Wonder Woman rescues the drowning villain Eviless because 'Aphrodite's Law commands us to save lives always - enemies or not.' The BDSM community's 4Cs (consent, communication, caring, caution) turn out to be Tronto's four elements of care, so the good dominant just is the good care-giver.

care-ethics.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
care-ethics.title: Fifth Hole How Golf Builds and Shapes Moral Character
care-ethics.relation: Beller and Stoll ask why empirical moral-reasoning research finds that sport generally does not build character, yet golfers score highest of all athletes. Using Aristotle's account of right conduct and Lickona's triad of moral knowing, feeling, and acting, they argue character forms through role models, social environment, and cognitive dissonance, supported by neuroplasticity research on the brain's capacity for moral growth. They contrast golf's self-policing tradition (Bobby Jones, Meg Mallon, Greg Norman, the film Bagger Vance) with the gamesmanship coached in team sports, and address Gilligan's 'different voice' by reporting that female golfers reason at least as highly as males, concluding that golf's honor-bound moral community sets it apart.

care-ethics.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
care-ethics.title: 11. The Mother of All Bombs
care-ethics.relation: Kolb argues Laura Palmer embodies the 'Angel in the House' ideal (Gilbert and Gubar) whose perfection is a beautiful dead girl, and reads The Return's linkage of the Trinity bomb to BOB/Judy through Arendt's On Violence—violence begets a more violent, hostile world that especially victimizes women. Using Gilligan's In a Different Voice, she shows how women's voices (Naido/Diane, the Log Lady, Laura's diary) are silenced by toxic masculinity (Mr. C, Richard, Chad), while the 'good men' embody an ethic of care; the manufactured post-war social order names its bombs after mothers and treats women as perfect-yet-fallen others.

care-ethics.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
care-ethics.title: Angel, Angelus, and Personal Identity
care-ethics.relation: The chapter uses the Wes–Holtz dispute over whether Angel owes punishment for Angelus's murders (Holtz's body-continuity view, glossed via Hobbes) to test theories of personal identity across the Whedonverse. It argues the shows present a Platonic separate soul as the metaphysical locus of identity — Fred ceasing to exist when Illyria consumes her soul, the shaman's soul-jar in 'Awakening,' the Judge finding Angelus 'clean' — while Angel's felt guilt, Darla's and Spike's resurrections, Buffy's and Faith's body switch, and Dollhouse's wiped Actives press the Lockean memory theory and Parfit's psychological-continuity successor. The Angel/Angelus case — eidetically shared memories but radically disconnected intentions, desires, and ethical sensibilities, developed over some 200 episodes — is offered as a richer cinematic counterexample than Locke's Day-Man/Night-Man or Parfit's fission triplet, forcing Neo-Lockeans to choose between memory chains and other psychological connections, and supporting Amy Kind's point that identity alone is not what matters for moral responsibility. Whedon's own verdict follows Parfit in discarding numerical identity but turns toward an ethics of care: what matters is staying properly psychologically connected to those one loves, so one 'finds out who you are' by being countable-on in ethically significant action.

care-ethics.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
care-ethics.title: Conclusion
care-ethics.relation: The conclusion synthesizes the book's case that Whedon philosophizes, building a Shaw-style hierarchy from illustrating theories (Connor as Robert Kane's libertarian agent, 'stirred up' between Darla's and faux-Cordelia's competing visions) through ethical and metaphysical complexity ('Man on the Street,' Angel/Angelus) to epistemic endorsement of a Whedonian worldview. It reads Angel's epiphany — 'if there's no bigger meaning, then the smallest act of kindness is the greatest thing in the world' — as a negative project against the thesis that ethics without God is incoherent, since Whedon's God-ambiguous fiction shows noble self-sacrifice (Buffy for Dawn, Cordy for Angel, Simon for River) that remains worthwhile regardless of cosmic justice. Following Mulhall's use of Socrates as an exemplar of ethically significant living, it casts Angel the Champion as a comparable exemplar grounded in authenticity, care-based relationships, and the transformation of moral character. It closes by extending the film-as-philosophy debate to television, deploying Carroll's gaze/glance distinction to argue nothing in principle keeps quality TV — from The Twilight Zone and Star Trek to Buffy and Angel — from being philosophy in action.

care-ethics.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
care-ethics.title: A Spielbergian Ethics of the Family in Saving Private Ryan and The Color Purple
care-ethics.relation: Clewis defines a 'Spielbergian ethics of the family,' a care-based virtue ethics holding that we owe unique obligations to family and close friends grounded in personal identity, and contrasts it with utilitarian and Kantian approaches. In Saving Private Ryan the squad-as-family and the Ryan brotherhood explain why Miller says Ryan must 'earn this' and why living an ordinary good life suffices; in The Color Purple sisterhood (Nettie/Celie), fatherhood, and motherhood ground obligations of care, forgiveness, and reconciliation. He evaluates the view's feasibility while warning it neglects wider social influences and the is/ought gap.

care-ethics.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
care-ethics.title: 10 Listening with Neil’s Vulnerable Voice and the Ethics of Care
care-ethics.relation: Jostedt argues that Young's raw, high "dental" singing voice (contrasted with Dylan's nasal sneer) invites empathetic "listening-with" rather than the detached individualism of Kant's deontology or Mill's utilitarianism. Drawing on Gilligan's In a Different Voice, Jane Addams and the ethics of care's emphasis on relatedness, he shows how songs like "Ohio," "Stringman," "Cortez the Killer" and the album Trans (evoking his son's cerebral palsy) make listeners feel with the downtrodden and disabled.

care-ethics.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
care-ethics.title: A Better Way of Living Your Life
care-ethics.relation: Laura Geuy Akers argues the Doctor lives by a relational ethics of care rather than deontology, utilitarianism, or virtue ethics. Drawing on Noddings's care ethics and Buber's I-Thou versus I-It stance, she shows the Doctor responds to particular others (insisting the Ood is "a he, not an it," addressing each companion individually before surrender) and even ethically cares for the Master. She pairs this with Nussbaum's and Kant's accounts of wonder and the sublime, arguing the Doctor's human companions (Rose, Martha, Donna) restore his sense of wonder and give his immortal life meaning.

care-ethics.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
care-ethics.title: Toward Caring
care-ethics.relation: J.J. Sylvia argues the Doctor, though male, is an ideal exemplar of the feminist ethics of care developed by Carol Gilligan (against Kohlberg's justice-only scale) and Nel Noddings. Contrasting the caring "Doctor" with the dominating "Master," he uses Rita Manning's account of caring as responsiveness and obligation to argue that an ethics of care, unlike impartial utilitarianism, explains why the Doctor should save his companion over a stranger. Noddings's natural-versus-ethical caring explains the Doctor forgiving the Master and offering compassion to Dalek Caan, and companions supply reciprocal care that guards against burnout.

care-ethics.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
care-ethics.title: You’re Basically “a Stuffed Animal Made by Grandma”
care-ethics.relation: Renee Kyle contrasts Dr. House's detached 'doctor knows best' justice ethic with Dr. Cameron's feminist ethic of care drawn from Carol Gilligan's In a Different Voice. Cameron builds trusting relationships, sees patients as embedded in social networks, and refuses to deceive or bully (as with Ezra and the newborns in 'Maternity'), whereas House treats patients as abstract puzzle-pieces. Kyle also voices the feminist worry that valorizing care can lead women to care at personal cost, as when Cameron's own grief over her dead husband derails her professional judgment.

care-ethics.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
care-ethics.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
care-ethics.relation: Nease lays out a game plan for raising ethical children, using Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics – eudaimonia as a flourishing life, virtue as the mean between extremes, and the master-skills of practical wisdom and self-control – as the core, mocking 'character counts' posters as no substitute for early habit-formation. He folds in Kant's motive of duty, Nietzsche's will-to-power (glossed via Janet Jackson's Control) as the drive to master oneself, and argues empathy (Theodor Lipps' inner imitation), self-awareness, concentration (Husserl's foreground/background), and a respect for justice must be cultivated to 'stack the deck' toward a good adult.

care-ethics.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
care-ethics.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
care-ethics.relation: Terjesen defends a distinctively paternal form of caring against care ethics' maternal bias. Reviewing Kohlberg's moral-development scale, Gilligan's justice-vs-care orientations, and Noddings' 'engrossment' model of caring, he argues these frameworks make it seem fathers like his own undemonstrative Norwegian dad don't care. He reconceives 'paternalism' (via Gerald Dworkin's soft paternalism and examples like Darth Vader and Bambi's father) as tough-love caring focused on the child's future self, complementary to maternal caring and distinct from the impersonal justice orientation.

care-ethics.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
care-ethics.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
care-ethics.relation: Mattern argues the heart of good fatherhood is mercy – 'faithful, compassionate love' – as an attitude of the heart, not a technique. Drawing on Aquinas's account of habitus and his ranking of mercy among the greatest virtues, plus Gabriel Marcel's 'creative fidelity,' Solovyov, Jean Vanier, and Karol Wojtyla on love as affirming another's value, he contrasts remote, justice-oriented fathers with empathic ones. He illustrates with overlapping Venn-diagram circles of father and child and with responding to his 7-year-old son's shoplifting through listening and repair rather than spanking.

care-ethics.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
care-ethics.title: MOTHERHOOD
care-ethics.relation: Chris Mulford, a nurse and lactation consultant, analyzes infant feeding as an ethical question of rights, duties, and responsibilities, drawing on a feminist ethic of care and the claim that women learn empathy through caregiving (linked to oxytocin's role in birth and nursing). She argues that the right at stake is the mother-child dyad's 'protection from interference' with breastfeeding, that no mother is saddled with a solitary duty to breastfeed, and that the duty toward breastfeeding falls on the whole community; she frames the mother's dependency on 'the kindness of strangers' via A Streetcar Named Desire and the innate 'breast crawl.'

care-ethics.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
care-ethics.title: MOTHERHOOD
care-ethics.relation: Maureen Sander-Staudt uses a feminist ethic of care – especially Carol Gilligan's mole-and-porcupine fable of reciprocal accommodation – to argue that pressuring women to nurse privately or covered imposes 'lactational burkas.' She runs public breastfeeding through the Miller obscenity test to show it is not obscene, opening with Gloria Steinem's 'If men could menstruate' to imagine 'milkmen,' and cites the Emily Gillette Freedom-flight ejection, Facebook's photo removal, the Janet Jackson Superbowl scandal, and PETA's human-milk proposal to expose hypocritical, biologically reductive double standards about the female breast.

care-ethics.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
care-ethics.title: You’re Basically “a Stuffed Animal Made by Grandma”
care-ethics.relation: Kyle contrasts House's detached, impartial "ethic of justice" with Dr. Cameron's feminist ethic of care, drawn from Carol Gilligan's In a Different Voice. Cameron builds trusting relationships, refuses to deceive patients, and attends to their social networks — letting parents hold their dying baby in "Maternity," defending Ezra's autonomy in "Informed Consent." But Kyle also presses the standard critique that valorizing care can cost the carer: Cameron's own grief over her dead husband derails her professional judgment in "Acceptance" and pushes her toward Houselike tactics.

care-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
care-ethics.title: 14. The Doctor as Philosopher The Collectivist-Realist Pacifism of the Doctor and the Quest for Social Justice
care-ethics.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a 'collectivist-realist pacifist': morally opposed to war yet willing, as a last resort, to use lethal force for social justice. She places the Doctor on Cady's warism-to-pacifism continuum (past absolute and collectivist pacifism), augmenting it with Martin Luther King Jr.'s realist pacifism — ethical appeals 'undergirded by constructive coercive power' — and Gandhi's ahimsa and belief that no one is beyond redemption (the Doctor sparing Davros, offering enemies a choice). She tests Kant's duty ethics and respect for persons (Rule 1: the Doctor lies), Ross's prima facie duties, Mill's utilitarianism ('The Fires of Pompeii,' 'The Beast Below'), Gilligan/Noddings care ethics, and Wolterstorff's 'life of needs,' and reads 'The Day of the Doctor' as a Rawlsian veil of ignorance brokering Zygon-human peace.

care-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
care-ethics.title: 25. The Mandalorian as Philosophy “This Is the Way”
care-ethics.relation: The chapter argues that The Mandalorian defends virtue ethics with care as the primary virtue. It maps Mando's creed and 'Canons of Honor' (strength, honor, loyalty, death) onto Stoicism's discipline of desire and cardinal virtues, quoting Marcus Aurelius and Seneca, and reads his transformation after adopting Grogu as Aristotelian moral development toward eudaimonia and flourishing. Using Stocker's critique of impartialist ethics and Noddings's and Slote's ethics of care, Belluomini argues Mando's caring relation with Grogu, his engrossment and motivational displacement, and his removing his helmet at the end show that care ranks highest among the virtues and should guide our own 'Way.'

care-ethics.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
care-ethics.title: 4. The Good of the Doctor
care-ethics.relation: The chapter distinguishes aesthetic 'good' (taste, beauty of the Daleks) from ethical 'good,' then tests the Doctor against the major moral theories: utilitarianism (rejected when Sarah Jane urges exterminating the Daleks in 'Genesis of the Daleks'), Kantian duty ethics (the Doctor's 'never met anyone who wasn't important' and attempts to save Davros and the Master), virtue ethics (the Eleventh Doctor guarding Christmas in 'The Time of the Doctor'), and feminist care ethics. Concluding that none quite fits because the Doctor values non-rational beings and feels compassion, the author proposes the Doctor follows Wolterstorff's 'ethic of need'—justice as meeting the needs of all—consistent with 'getting in the thick of things' as a flâneur.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
care-ethics-noddings.title: Elaine’s Moral Character
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Sarah Worth asks whether Elaine is a feminist icon or 'just one of the boys.' Elaine passes every liberal-feminist benchmark - a Tufts education, the only steady career (Pendant Publishing, then the J. Peterman catalogue), financial and emotional independence - but fails the ethic of care: her dating ethics run on pettiness (dumping men for not offering pie, for dirty bathrooms, over Puddy's high-fiving), the 'spongeworthy' episode commodifies her own relationships, she shows no maternal instinct toward the ugly baby, and she secretly resents George's engagement. The conclusion: being one of the boys does not a feminist make, though Elaine still models an independence the women of Friends and Frasier lack.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
care-ethics-noddings.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Answers the title with 'fugheddaboutit' - Carmela is no feminist - but argues she reasons as a Gilligan-style care ethicist. Her moral voice evolves from Church-based justice arguments against Angie's divorce ('Commendatori'), through the justice-tradition confrontation with Dr. Krakower's refusal of 'blood money' ('Second Opinion'), to mature care ethics that balances self with others when she throws Tony out after the Svetlana revelation ('Whitecaps'). Using Noddings on reciprocity and 'total engrossment', the chapter reads the marriage's failure as failed caring, and the Furio romance and the Georgetown ricotta-pie intimidation as care reasoning that defies the submissive female stereotype feminists fear care ethics valorizes.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
care-ethics-noddings.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Cynthia Freeland reads the film's women through feminist ethics of care: the two Marys function like a Greek-chorus of grieving observers, while Claudia and Veronica — and the casting of Bellucci as the repentant whore opposite Morgenstern's ageless Madonna — lock them into the virgin/whore double bind. Using Carol Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg's Kantian standard and Nel Noddings's and Sara Ruddick's point that mothering is reflective 'attentive' work, she argues Gibson's Mary is one-dimensional: flashbacks of 'I am here' show maternal instinct, never moral deliberation. She ends by suggesting the historical Jesus, like Socrates, was more radical toward women than the film, and that Irigaray's reading of Christ's bleeding wounds as a feminized maternal body sits oddly with Gibson's muscular, 'take it like a man' Savior.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
care-ethics-noddings.title: U2 and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: The authors apply Gilligan's and Noddings' ethics of care to U2: 'Bad' shows the speaker as Noddings' 'one-caring', and 'Sometimes You Can't Make It on Your Own' - Bono caring for his dying father through anger and resentment - exemplifies care's insistence on the particular relationship over universal rules, refusing abstraction even of the usual songwriting metaphors. 'Peace on Earth' names the Omagh bomb's dead (Sean, Julia, Gareth, Ann, Breda) and 'Van Diemen's Land' refuses both IRA and British sides, showing care ethics rejecting the utilitarian accounting and the Kantian universalizability arguments that could rationalize such violence. They conclude U2 are philosophical rather than political feminists: Gilligan's 'different voice' is not a woman's voice, and the band's connected knowing - debt relief sung as connection in 'Beautiful Day' - makes maternal thinking 'loud, rhythmic, catchy, even cool'.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
care-ethics-noddings.title: Explaining Moral Doubt
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Steven Gimbel reads the Formidable Opponent segment - red-tie Colbert debating blue-tie Colbert - as a glimpse of authentic moral deliberation that the flip-flop-phobic punditry satirized by the show (and Jon Stewart's Crossfire rant) has abandoned. Moral doubt is good because perspectives are partial and the Enlightenment 'marketplace of ideas' of Locke and Mill tests beliefs only through challenge. It has a source: 'morally right' bundles five dimensions - the actor's character shaped by habit (Aristotle's virtue ethics), the act itself judged by Kant's categorical imperative, the pleasure-versus-pain consequences tallied Bentham-style, the rights of the person affected from Locke and Hobbes's social contract, and the special care obligations of close relationships (Noddings and Ruddick) - and hard cases like abortion and flag burning are exactly where these dimensions pull apart. So emulate the dueling Colberts: fear not the flip-flop, since deciding which value trumps which requires open-minded conversation with oneself.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
care-ethics-noddings.title: 12 - Care Ethics, Friendship, and facebook
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Hamington surveys a hundred Facebook users and argues, through care ethics — Noddings's 'here I am' disposition and her natural versus ethical caring — that Facebook can make us more ethical, because the stream of small particulars about friends supplies the knowledge that is a necessary condition for caring. He uses Benhabib's concrete other to explain how status updates make distant lives 'real' to us, and confesses his own de-friending of a student over a racist comment as a case of Facebook's convenience making it easy not to care. The chapter ends by claiming Facebook dissolves the binary of close friend versus nodding acquaintance into a postmodern range of fluid, mediating friendships, while insisting caring is learned through the body and merely extended, not replaced, in virtual space.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
care-ethics-noddings.title: A Better Way of Living Your Life
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Akers argues the Doctor follows neither rule deontology, utilitarian calculation, nor virtue ethics, but a relational ethics of care in Noddings's and Slote's sense, expressed as Buber's I-Thou stance — insisting an enslaved Ood is 'a "he," not an "it"' and addressing Donna, Jack, and Rose each as individuals in 'Journey's End'. Linking this to Nussbaum's claim that wonder widens moral concern and to Kant's dynamic and mathematical sublime, she argues the Doctor needs human companions like Rose, Martha, and Donna as a human-scale reference point that renews his wonder — and with it his ethics — while his wiping of Donna's memory shows the care tradition's dangers of power imbalance.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
care-ethics-noddings.title: Toward Caring
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Sylvia models the Doctor on feminist care ethics: Gilligan's response to Kohlberg's justice-tinged scales and Noddings's distinction between natural caring (for Rose, Martha, Peri in 'The Caves of Androzani') and ethical caring, which explains his forgiveness of the Master and compassion for Dalek Caan after genocides. Against utilitarian impartiality — which cannot say why he should save his companion over a stranger — the relationship itself grounds the obligation, while his vengeful moment facing the lone Dalek in 'Dalek' shows what caring burnout looks like.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
care-ethics-noddings.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Kathleen Poorman Dougherty sets Kant's universal, emotion-free morality (echoed in Kohlberg's justice stages and Judge Abernathy's 'blind court' claim in 'Infamy') against Carol Gilligan's care ethic, which she says fits Saint Alicia far better: Alicia's practical advice to Jennifer Lewis in the pilot, driving Kenny home in 'Home', and telling Kenny's father 'I care a lot more about your son than he does' show connection producing both better morality and better lawyering. Feminist theorists like Nel Noddings and Sara Ruddick treat this care orientation as morally superior, not merely different, but the chapter's later sections weigh the cost: Kalinda's burnout warning, Alicia's resentment at always hand-holding clients, and the double bind by which women absorb society's unpaid caring labor. The verdict is that care is genuinely moral, but it must become a shared burden.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
care-ethics-noddings.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Skyler King uses the Gang's inheritance war over their dead mother's possessions as a metaphor for greed versus need, pressing our duties to those in extreme suffering. Peter Singer's utilitarian argument - prevent bad without sacrificing anything of comparable significance, absolute poverty is bad, therefore we ought to give - makes charity a requirement rather than a nicety, condemning Dennis's luxury purchases and crowning Bruce Mathis, the one character who consistently donates, as the utilitarian exemplar. Nel Noddings's feminist ethics of care counters that we owe help only to those within reach whose good we can see 'completed in the other' - so Mac and Dennis wronged Charlie by refusing him shelter in the recession, but owe nothing to children overseas - and the chapter weighs Dee-style objections that this licenses caring only when inconvenienced, closing with the question 'is it always sunny in your Philadelphia?'

care-ethics-noddings.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
care-ethics-noddings.title: 16. Who Am I to You
care-ethics-noddings.relation: James Okapal sets up the Kantian view — moral agency, shown by passing the contradiction-in-conception test (which Wallace's 'all should be masters of slaves' fails), is the precondition of moral status, so non-agents like replicants, on Tibor Machan's extension of Kant to animals, matter no more than toasters — against the ethics of care of Nel Noddings and Carol Gilligan. On the care reading, K's and Batty's final acts of ethical caring, like Joi's risky choices for K, confer moral status on another and thereby constitute moral agency, reversing the Kantian order. Empathy, not universalizable reason, is what removes bricks from Joshi's wall.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
care-ethics-noddings.title: 24. Fred Rogers and the Ethics of Care
care-ethics-noddings.relation: A.G. Holdier places Rogers squarely in the care ethics of Gilligan and Noddings: against Kohlberg's justice stages (the Heinz dilemma recast with Henrietta Pussycat and X the Owl), care means Joan Tronto's four elements of attentiveness, responsibility, competence, and responsiveness, shown in the Clemmons kiddie pool, the Soviet guest understood through an interpreter, and 'just the way you are.' Extending care to animals via Rogers's vegetarianism and Carol Adams's 'absent referent,' and to the self via the closing benediction, he argues Rogers embodied care as particular, embodied practice rather than formula.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
care-ethics-noddings.title: Not Bad, for a [Wo]man
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Argues Ripley's crossed-heart promise to Newt shows partialist care rightly overriding impartial justice: Kant, Mill, and Rachels demand everyone count for one, but Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg and Noddings's carer-cared-for relation - completed in Newt's 'I knew you'd come' - explain why Ripley duct-tapes two guns together and descends into the hive. Her flexible, relational problem-solving (the lighter-sprinkler trick against the Facehuggers, learning the pulse rifle) beats Gorman's mission-first command, and the trolley-style arithmetic she rejects when the one on the tracks is her little girl is not a moral failing; even nuking the Queen's eggs raises Singer-style speciesism questions.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
care-ethics-noddings.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Barkman diagnoses four mama's boys: Raj's selective mutism under his parents' webcam meddling, Sheldon's comfort-seeking from a fundamentalist mother ('Soft Kitty,' mandatory grace), Howard's learned helplessness with his foghorn mother, and Leonard raised as Beverly's lab subject, his hugging machine echoing the wire-mother monkey experiment. Plato and Aristotle ground the charge of injustice — receiving less than one's station deserves, and wrongs against intimates are 'more terrible' — so parents bear special obligations their neglect breaches, a contemporary point pressed in the care-ethics tradition of Noddings. Cognitive-dissonance theory and Putman's Aristotelian 'psychological courage' prescribe honest self-reckoning for mothers and sons alike, with Leonard furthest along after confronting Beverly in 'The Maternal Congruence.'

care-ethics-noddings.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
care-ethics-noddings.title: Notes
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Opening from the author's own grief — she nearly stopped playing Fallout 4 because its murdered spouse and kidnapped son echoed the loss of her real infant son — the chapter applies the ethics of care of Gilligan, Noddings, and Tronto to Fallout's wasteland.
