Care relationships structure the games: the Fallout 3 father whose flight from Vault 101 propels the plot, Dogmeat's loyal responsiveness as relational reciprocity, and the Fallout 4 son Shaun, where caring for your child collides with caring for a Commonwealth his Institute endangers. Settlement-building, faction choice (Lyons's Brotherhood handing out clean water versus the Railroad's liberation of synths), and even the Black Widow perk path that saves Megaton all become care-laden moral acts — care as protest against the wasteland's ethos of bare survival.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
care-ethics-noddings.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Averill argues that Katniss's morality is built on care for particular people rather than impartial principle: she volunteers for Prim, protects Rue because the girl resembles her sister, and spares a wounded District 2 soldier at the Nut because he recalls her father and the Seam. Measured against Kant's impartial justice perspective (embodied by Thresh sparing Katniss to repay a debt to Rue), she falls short — but Gilligan's care perspective and Noddings's distinction between natural and ethical caring recast this as a valid, even heroic, moral development. Using Noddings, the chapter traces Katniss's arc from natural care for Prim toward ethical care for strangers and even enemies, and reads her assassination of Coin as care for all of Panem's future children rather than revenge. Care, the chapter concludes, can even justify violence when it protects the vulnerable.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
care-ethics-noddings.title: Notes
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Bein argues Wonder Woman uniquely fuses two supposedly incompatible moralities: bushido - Nitobe's eight samurai virtues, Sun Tzu's benevolence of ending war swiftly, worthy-opponent rituals mirrored in superhero costumes - and the feminist ethics of care Gilligan and Noddings built against a Western canon (Aristotle, Kant) that called women too emotional for morality. Wonder Woman's killing of Maxwell Lord to free Superman is re-read as the care-ethical beach case: saving your own child over a stranger's is not a failure of impartiality, and in his Gotham-versus-Themyscira invasion thought experiment she would defend Gotham because its people are vulnerable non-combatants, not because a utilitarian ledger favors it.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
care-ethics-noddings.title: Notes
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Chavez, Gavaler, and Goldberg trace Marston's 'Love Leader' kink - bracelets of submission, Venus girdles, Paradise Island bondage games, Earth One's collaring of Steve Trevor - to nineteenth-century maternalist feminism, then map the care ethics of Gilligan, Noddings, and Tronto onto both the comic and real-world BDSM. Reform (later Transformation) Island embodies a care-based alternative to punishment: rather than retribution, von Gunther and Irene are transformed by loving authority into people who save their captors, and Wonder Woman rescues the drowning villain Eviless because 'Aphrodite's Law commands us to save lives always - enemies or not.' The BDSM community's 4Cs (consent, communication, caring, caution) turn out to be Tronto's four elements of care, so the good dominant just is the good care-giver.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
care-ethics-noddings.title: Exploring The Cabin in the Woods
care-ethics-noddings.relation: The chapter reads The Cabin in the Woods as Whedon and Goddard doing philosophy: the facility's ritual sacrifice of the five campers is given an explicit utilitarian defense (quoting Mill's greatest-happiness principle) through the Director's plea that Dana kill Marty to avert the apocalypse, which the film ultimately counters through the friends' care-based obligations. Drawing on Nel Noddings's ethics of care and Aristotle's claim that the severity of our duties varies with the closeness of relationships — and on Whedonverse parallels like Buffy refusing to sacrifice Dawn in 'The Gift' — it recasts the ending as an implicit counterargument to classic utilitarianism: Dana does nothing impermissible by refusing to murder her friend, so utilitarianism is false, while Dana's genuine dilemma is deliberately left unresolved in Socratic aporia. It then extends the ethics of care into a theory of the horror genre, reading Whedon's 'inoculation against real fear' as an Aristotelian catharsis that requires relatable characters who care for one another, and takes the film's monitors, two-way mirrors, and voyeurism scenes (Hadley's callousness, the control-room ogling of Jules) as a metalevel invitation to audit our own desensitization to pointless screen suffering.

care-ethics-noddings.title: A Better Way of Living Your Life

care-ethics-noddings.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
care-ethics-noddings.title: MOTHERHOOD
care-ethics-noddings.relation: George Dunn asks whether classical theism can call God 'Mother,' beginning with the Book of Job (taught in his Problem of Evil course) and the divine name Shadday's link to womb-love and 'blessings of breasts and womb.' He works through Anselm's 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived,' the attributes of impassibility and incorporeality, and Aquinas's doctrine of analogy, arguing Aquinas wrongly rejected maternal God-language because he swallowed Aristotle's biology of woman as 'defective and misbegotten'; drawing on Nel Noddings's caring 'receptivity' and Julian of Norwich, Dunn contends divine impassibility should yield to a maternal, receptive God, with a nod to Homer Simpson's burrito paradox.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
care-ethics-noddings.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Cassidy, through an interior monologue of a shopper eyeing Indonesian-made sandals, weighs individual responsibility for consumerism. She contrasts Singer's drowning-child duty to relieve suffering with Pogge's 'you break it, you buy it' claim that the Global North caused Southern poverty, then uses Scheffler's 'restricted' common-sense responsibility and Cannon's butterfly-effect virtues (replacing the American Dream's acquisitiveness with interconnectedness). Adapting Claudia Card, she distinguishes three senses of responsibility — credit (backward-looking blame), management (of one's lifestyle), and care-taking — and, invoking Noddings's ethics of care, argues that since globalization's impact is uncertain we should shift from assigning blame to caring *about* distant workers, buying less out of boredom-driven habit.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
care-ethics-noddings.title: You’re Basically “a Stuffed Animal Made by Grandma”
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Kyle contrasts House's detached, impartial "ethic of justice" with Dr. Cameron's feminist ethic of care, drawn from Carol Gilligan's In a Different Voice. Cameron builds trusting relationships, refuses to deceive patients, and attends to their social networks — letting parents hold their dying baby in "Maternity," defending Ezra's autonomy in "Informed Consent." But Kyle also presses the standard critique that valorizing care can cost the carer: Cameron's own grief over her dead husband derails her professional judgment in "Acceptance" and pushes her toward Houselike tactics.

care-ethics-noddings.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
care-ethics-noddings.title: 50. The Cabin in the Woods as Philosophy Cinematic Reflections on Ethical Complexity, Human Nature, and Worthw
care-ethics-noddings.relation: Kowalski argues Whedon and Goddard's The Cabin in the Woods stages a clash between classical utilitarianism and an ethics of care, and cinematically favors the latter. The Facility, sacrificing five campers to placate the Ancient Ones and save humanity, embodies Mill's greatest-happiness reasoning, but its callous celebration while Dana suffers on the dock undercuts that view. When the Director tells Dana she must kill her only remaining friend Marty to save the world, Dana's refusal is defended via Noddings's care ethics and Aristotle's claim that obligations track close personal relationships (special obligations), with Aristotle's Poetics catharsis and Plato's Leontius grounding the film's theory of worthwhile horror: 'people are more important than humanity.'

feminism.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
feminism.title: Elaine’s Moral Character
feminism.relation: Sarah Worth asks whether Elaine is a feminist icon or 'just one of the boys.' Elaine passes every liberal-feminist benchmark - a Tufts education, the only steady career (Pendant Publishing, then the J. Peterman catalogue), financial and emotional independence - but fails the ethic of care: her dating ethics run on pettiness (dumping men for not offering pie, for dirty bathrooms, over Puddy's high-fiving), the 'spongeworthy' episode commodifies her own relationships, she shows no maternal instinct toward the ugly baby, and she secretly resents George's engagement. The conclusion: being one of the boys does not a feminist make, though Elaine still models an independence the women of Friends and Frasier lack.

feminism.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
feminism.title: 9 - Simpsonian Sexual Politcs
feminism.relation: Dale and James Snow use head counts of Springfield's population, episode listings, and guest stars to show the show extends rather than satirizes television's conservative sexual politics: a roughly 4:1 male-to-female recurring cast with four to five times as many episodes centered on Homer or Bart as on Marge or Lisa. Marge, they argue, remains Virginia Woolf's 'Angel in the House'—continuous with June Cleaver and the 1950s sitcom mother rather than a gross exaggeration of motherhood like Burns's capitalism—and her way of life is openly despised even by Lisa. Lisa the feminist idealist is needed for psychic balance but kept to roughly 15 percent of episodes, and the authors close by crediting her slow moral influence on Bart and Homer while noting the dumb guys still hold center stage.

feminism.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
feminism.title: Unknown
feminism.relation: The chapter contrasts the films' opening codes—digital green bits versus amorphous cellular pink—and invokes the feminist critique that western philosophy, from Plato's transcendent Forms through Augustine and Aquinas to Descartes's identity as mind not body, is a male quest for escape from the flesh that The Matrix repeats with its sleek leather-clad stars. It then reads both Keanu's Neo and Jude Law's Ted as 'pretty', graceful, penetrated male heroes paired with stronger women, setting up the analysis of scenes of male penetration.

feminism.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
feminism.title: Unknown
feminism.relation: The chapter reads eXistenZ's gender reversals against The Matrix: Allegra Geller is the computer whiz and decision-maker while Ted Pikul is frightened and hysterical, fitted with his bioport in a homoerotic black-market scene where Gas quips about the 'stud finder'. Port penetration in eXistenZ is sensual, messy, and risky, tied through imagery to eating and sex (licking the bioport, frog bellies bursting with blood, the gristle-gun that shoots teeth), so Cronenberg's 'New Flesh' undermines the stereotypes that The Matrix, with its male hero, father figure Morpheus, and female love interest, boringly preserves.

feminism.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
feminism.title: “The Graduation” Autonomy and the Relational Self
feminism.relation: Jessica Prata Miller reads Buffy through Carol Gilligan's care perspective: Buffy's self is relational (the Scooby Gang, 'Dawn is a part of me' in 'The Gift'), her moral reasoning contextual rather than rule-bound (caging Oz instead of killing the werewolf, rejecting Riley's Initiative 'demons bad' abstraction), and her emotions a moral resource ('My emotions give me power'). She also weighs the criticisms — Buffy's secret harboring of Angel exposed in 'Revelations,' and Faith's utilitarian 'plus column' defense of hiding a killing, which Buffy rejects ('I am' the one who cries over the bystander). Comparing the three Slayers, Miller argues only Buffy attains moral autonomy: Kendra's unquestioning obedience and Faith's hyper-individualistic action-hero isolation both fail, while Buffy's 'I like to think of it as graduation' break from the Watchers' Council shows autonomy achieved within, not against, relationships.

feminism.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
feminism.title: The Noir Consequences of Sex Eros, Death, and the Possibility of Love
feminism.relation: Thomas Hibbs reads BtVS as feminist noir: like classic noir it traps characters in labyrinths where the past bears down on the present (Buffy torn from heaven in 'After Life,' Angel's gypsy curse in 'Innocence,' the psych-ward ending of 'Normal Again'), and it rejects both Enlightenment optimism and the Nietzschean beyond-good-and-evil self-creation Hibbs finds in neo-noir like Body Heat and Thelma and Louise. Sex in Sunnydale always carries noir consequences — Angel losing his soul at the moment of 'true happiness,' Buffy's self-lacerating Spike affair ending in his attempted rape — so the show is skeptical of sexual liberation while recovering a classical eros as longing for wholeness. The Season Six finale locates the 'true essence of magic' in sacrificial love: Xander's yellow-crayon plea in 'Grave' reaches the 'spark of humanity' in Willow where all force fails.

feminism.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
feminism.title: No Damsel in Distress
feminism.relation: Mimi Marinucci argues Buffy's violence tracks what agents do, not what they are: souled Angel and chip-enabled Spike receive moral consideration, willing human evildoers like Ford ('Lie to Me') and Ethan Rayne are fought, and Buffy's 'impression of Gandhi' in 'Anne' claims violence can rightly answer injustice. Building on William R. Jones's King–Malcolm X–Mao spectrum and Hannah Arendt's warning that doing violence habituates the agent, she reads the Slayer's fight as symbolic resistance to rape and women's oppression (bloodsucking as rape metaphor in 'Buffy vs. Dracula,' Spike's assault after Buffy ends the affair). The cost is real — 'Restless' reveals the First Slayer's primeval rage and staking with 'Mr. Pointy' mirrors sexualized violence — so she ends by endorsing tempered, appropriate violence (Buffy's Tai Chi training with Angel) over both passivity and aggression.

feminism.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
feminism.title: Softball The Good Is the Enemy of the Best
feminism.relation: Heaphy asks whether softball limits women's potential to be equals on the baseball diamond, using feminist philosophy to explain why women are steered to the 'soft' game. Judith Williamson's analysis of women in mass culture and Simone de Beauvoir's woman-as-invisible-Other explain why female players — the AAGPBL's skirts and charm school, Toni Stone and Mamie Johnson in the Negro Leagues, Ila Borders in the minors — are covered as women first and ballplayers second. Iris Marion Young's 'Throwing Like a Girl' supplies the phenomenology: women throw differently not from anatomy but from experiencing the body as a burden, a socially produced self-fulfilling prophecy. Softball, 'the good,' becomes the enemy of the best — women playing hardball — by letting society postpone hard questions about gender.

feminism.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
feminism.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Answers the title with 'fugheddaboutit' - Carmela is no feminist - but argues she reasons as a Gilligan-style care ethicist. Her moral voice evolves from Church-based justice arguments against Angie's divorce ('Commendatori'), through the justice-tradition confrontation with Dr. Krakower's refusal of 'blood money' ('Second Opinion'), to mature care ethics that balances self with others when she throws Tony out after the Svetlana revelation ('Whitecaps'). Using Noddings on reciprocity and 'total engrossment', the chapter reads the marriage's failure as failed caring, and the Furio romance and the Georgetown ricotta-pie intimidation as care reasoning that defies the submissive female stereotype feminists fear care ethics valorizes.

feminism.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
feminism.title: The Feminist Debate So Far
feminism.relation: Anne Collins Smith announces the chapter's thesis: in Rowling's universe love crosses hierarchical boundaries and defeats evil most effectively precisely when it does not compete, as self-sacrifice and kindness overwhelm greed and ambition without fighting them on their own terms. She claims this pattern resonates with radical feminism, and sets up a survey of feminist scholarship on Harry Potter before examining love's role in the books.

feminism.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
feminism.title: Radical vs. Liberal Feminism
feminism.relation: Surveys the divided feminist reception of the series: Schoefer, Heilman, and Dresang charge it with reinforcing gender stereotypes, from giggling girls to the absence of any woman as heroic as Harry or wise as Dumbledore, while Kern, Zettel, and Gladstein defend it on contextual grounds, Lavender's silliness mirroring Dean and Seamus, Trelawney mirroring Lockhart, and Umbridge and Bellatrix commanding as much fear as any male Death Eater. The giggling debate, with Zettel's refusal 'to tell girls that the only way to be valid human beings is to turn themselves into boys', stages the disagreement the chapter will recast as liberal versus radical feminism.

feminism.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
feminism.title: More Wonderful and More Terrible than Death
feminism.relation: Distinguishes liberal feminism, historically grounded in Wollstonecraft, Harriet Taylor Mill, and John Stuart Mill, which holds women are autonomous persons who succeed on equal but masculine-coded terms, as in Gladstein's praise of McGonagall and Hermione, from radical feminism's analysis of the sex/gender system that forces masculine and feminine traits into rigid, ranked pairs. It reads Zettel's defense of Molly Weasley's mothering and Gallardo-C. and Smith's 'Cinderfella' interpretation, evil as 'phallic power and ambition' even in Umbridge, good as feminine-coded kindness and selflessness in Harry, as radical-feminist readings, noting thinkers from St. Gertrude to Gandhi and C.S. Lewis have likewise insisted love and compassion belong to full humanity.

feminism.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
feminism.title: The Triumph of Love
feminism.relation: Tracks love's escalation across the series as a force that overwhelms evil without competing: Lily's skin-deep sacrificial love repels Quirrell in Sorcerer's Stone, Harry spares Pettigrew out of love for Lupin and Sirius, his love for Sirius expels Voldemort's possession at the Ministry, and Dumbledore names it 'a force that is at once more wonderful and more terrible than death'. In Deathly Hallows love extends to Kreacher, Griphook, and Dobby, and culminates in Harry's astonishing plea that Voldemort 'try for some remorse', his redefinition of manhood in 'be a man', and victory through willing sacrifice and a single defensive spell rather than a duel, vindicating traditionally feminine values over hypermasculine domination.

feminism.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
feminism.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Cynthia Freeland reads the film's women through feminist ethics of care: the two Marys function like a Greek-chorus of grieving observers, while Claudia and Veronica — and the casting of Bellucci as the repentant whore opposite Morgenstern's ageless Madonna — lock them into the virgin/whore double bind. Using Carol Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg's Kantian standard and Nel Noddings's and Sara Ruddick's point that mothering is reflective 'attentive' work, she argues Gibson's Mary is one-dimensional: flashbacks of 'I am here' show maternal instinct, never moral deliberation. She ends by suggesting the historical Jesus, like Socrates, was more radical toward women than the film, and that Irigaray's reading of Christ's bleeding wounds as a feminized maternal body sits oddly with Gibson's muscular, 'take it like a man' Savior.

feminism.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
feminism.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Wilkerson borrows the social contract tradition — Hobbes's mutual-restraint founding, radicalized by Pateman's sexual contract and Mills's racial contract — to recast antifat bias as a systematic breach of the social contract enforced by medicine (hallway weigh-ins, weight lectures instead of care), employment, transit seating, and TV fat jokes. Against Atkins's medical discourse of the 'obesity epidemic' she assembles Health at Every Size evidence, trans-fat and high-fructose corn syrup data, and the documented health damage of stigma and dieting itself, concluding that Atkins profits from recasting social problems as individual failings. Atkins for Life's success stories (Kerry Feather's volleyball and new husband, Luann Lockhart's proud daughter) are read as testimony that dieting works as ritual self-abasement purchasing group membership — hence Fat Liberation's 'another world is possible.'

feminism.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
feminism.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Bentley argues Atkins 'masculinized' dieting: since meat is coded male (the hunter's large game, yang, 'strong as an ox') and dieting female, a diet whose emblematic meal is steak, bacon, and creamed spinach let men come out of the dieting closet — Terry Free's competitive wager, business-school professors trading weight charts, and half-male Atkins success stories against Jenny Craig's sixteen men. The symbolism runs both ways: women now order steak openly, while 'white trash' foods like pork rinds ($840 million in 2003 sales) gained middle-class respectability, a class crossing she explains through Bourdieu's Distinction — taste, habitus, and cultural capital.

feminism.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
feminism.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Argues that Narnia is 'unfriendly to the feminine' by reading Susan's exclusion from Aslan's country at the end of The Last Battle ('no longer a friend of Narnia', too interested in nylons and invitations) as the fate of the one heroine who stays stereotypically feminine. It shows that the admired girls (Lucy, Aravis, Jill) succeed only by approximating a masculine standard of adventure, applying Beauvoir's point that measuring women against a male norm implies something wrong with femaleness itself. It further traces how evil in Narnia wears a feminine face: the Green Witch seduces Prince Rilian into Underland, the White Witch tempts Edmund and Digory where the girls resist, and the Witch's Lilith/Jinn lineage ties women to the Fall via 'Daughters of Eve'.

feminism.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
feminism.title: Poker and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Housel surveys a century of poker on screen — from the Tombstone Birdcage Theater's 'bird in a gilded cage' through Maverick, The Gambler, Rounders, and ESPN's Tilt with its brothel-break 'Matador' — to show women cast as eye-candy, damsels, or flukes (Joanne Woodward winning a high-stakes game without knowing how to play). Against the myth stands Annie Duke, who beat her brother Howard on the way to the 2004 Tournament of Champions title. The argument: poker rewards reading and projecting emotion, so women socialized into emotional intelligence hold an edge over macho men who suppress it — a retooled Stoicism fusing Epictetus's 'make the best use of what is in your power' with Gilligan's care ethics, backed by Nietzsche's trust in the senses and Sun Tzu's 'pretend inferiority and encourage his arrogance.'

feminism.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
feminism.title: U2 and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The authors apply Gilligan's and Noddings' ethics of care to U2: 'Bad' shows the speaker as Noddings' 'one-caring', and 'Sometimes You Can't Make It on Your Own' - Bono caring for his dying father through anger and resentment - exemplifies care's insistence on the particular relationship over universal rules, refusing abstraction even of the usual songwriting metaphors. 'Peace on Earth' names the Omagh bomb's dead (Sean, Julia, Gareth, Ann, Breda) and 'Van Diemen's Land' refuses both IRA and British sides, showing care ethics rejecting the utilitarian accounting and the Kantian universalizability arguments that could rationalize such violence. They conclude U2 are philosophical rather than political feminists: Gilligan's 'different voice' is not a woman's voice, and the band's connected knowing - debt relief sung as connection in 'Beautiful Day' - makes maternal thinking 'loud, rhythmic, catchy, even cool'.

feminism.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
feminism.title: The Male Vampire as Metrosexual . . . Sort Of
feminism.relation: Joan Grassbaugh Forry asks how conventional standards of beauty, femininity, and masculinity operate in the vampire aesthetic of Interview with the Vampire, Buffy, and Queen of the Damned. Using Foucault's figure of the soldier whose body is 'made' by discipline, and Bartky and Bordo's feminist extension of it to dieting, deportment, and ornamenting the female body, she argues vampires expose the ideology of natural beauty: they are youthful, elegant, and effortlessly beautiful - no gym, no reflection - so their beauty is pure naturalness with the discipline erased. Gender decides the payoff: ultra-feminine female vampires (Drusilla's dresses and tea parties, Akasha, childlike Claudia) are femmes fatales whose threat must be punished by death, ridicule, or infantilization, while feminized male protagonists (Louis, Angel, Spike painting his nails and watching Passions - the 'metrosexual') win audience identification and tragic dignity. Beauty, in short, is a shield for the male vampire and a death sentence for the female.

feminism.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
feminism.title: Good Definitions
feminism.relation: The definitional taxonomy at work: MacKinnon and Dworkin's Model Law defines pornography as 'the sexually explicit subordination of women', but backfires in Canadian law into raids on gay bookshops while mainstream pornography survives - reference drift from an intended sense-only change. The three theories of rape (traditional property crime, liberal sex-without-consent, radical feminist 'terrorist institution' of male subordination) show definitions track theories and must be argued for, with the radical redefinition risking a tone-dilution that would 'trivialize legitimate rape'.

feminism.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
feminism.title: You’re Basically “a Stuffed Animal Made by Grandma”
feminism.relation: Renee Kyle sets House's detached "doctor knows best" medicine against Cameron's practice to argue for Carol Gilligan's feminist ethic of care: Cameron builds trust, refuses to deceive or bully (defending Ezra's control over his body in "Informed Consent"), and sees patients as embedded in relationships, arranging for parents to hold their newborn in "Maternity," where House sees only abstract puzzles. The chapter also presses the standard feminist worry that valorizing care can backfire: Cameron's unresolved grief stops her from telling terminal patients the truth, and by "Que Sera Sera" she secretly injects a patient who wants to leave the hospital, so that caring too much turns her into House.

feminism.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
feminism.title: A Fork in the Road
feminism.relation: Anderson contrasts two American freedoms through Springsteen and Tracy Chapman: the negative freedom of 'Racing in the Street,' 'Thunder Road,' and 'Born to Run' — Thoreauvian wildness, the outlaw who blows off duty, wins the dude from L.A.'s money and 'little girl' as a prize, then finds her crying on her daddy's porch — against the positive freedom of Chapman's 'Fast Car' heroine, who initially sees the fast car as a way to 'be someone' but finally sends the aimless drinker off and seeks empowerment of her own abilities. Drawing on Margaret Fuller (men squander freedom on appetite and domination), Charlotte Perkins Gilman (male-built structures channel women's freedom through men), and Nussbaum (flourishing, failure built into the structure), he argues that male negative freedom is dialectically coupled to women's oppression, that justice must trump the call of the wild, yet that men's own collateral damage — desolation, alienation — must also be addressed.

feminism.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
feminism.title: With or Without Starbuck
feminism.relation: Ewan Kirkland argues BSG's gender-free surface, unisex bunks and a Starbuck who never has to defend her right to fly, masks a default masculinity under Adama's patriarchal regime: Ellen is killed off as the negative femme fatale, Kat and Cain die or turn monstrous, and 'The Farm' literalizes feminist fears of patriarchal medicine turning women into breeders. Starbuck confounds the sexualizing male gaze, never objectified, repeatedly rescuing men and reversing damsel-in-distress plots, yet her success is entirely masculinized, bought by becoming like a man. Her New Caprica captivity as Leoben's simulated wife literalizes the feminist critique of compulsory heterosexuality, and her death in 'Maelstrom', submitting to her former kidnapper, suggests the series contains its most transgressive heroine.

feminism.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
feminism.title: Human, Machine, or Something In-between
feminism.relation: Heather Rolufs maps Boomer Sharon and Caprica Six onto Eve and Lilith: Boomer's unwitting shooting of Adama parallels Eve eating the fruit before she could understand disobedience, raising whether her free will was ever real, while Baltar repeats Adam's blame-shifting and Six gains the rebuttal Eve never had. The Lilith material from the Alphabet of Ben Sira and the Zohar explains Six's red-dressed seduction of Baltar and her ambivalent violence, snapping a baby's neck as a mercy before the attack yet later risking herself to return Hera. The chapter argues the show lets these demonized first women of myth be reread as neither machines nor demons but human.

feminism.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
feminism.title: Mirror, Mirror
feminism.relation: Sailors convicts Dorothy of being the stereotypical female of Baum's and Fleming's versions, disowning responsibility for killing both witches and living to please others, then contrasts her with Elphaba of Wicked as a feminist hero who leaves home, protects Animals, and mixes 'hot' male and 'cold' female anger into a single fury. She reads Elphaba's indeterminate gender through Marilyn Frye's point that easily identifiable groups are the easiest to oppress, through de Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but becomes a woman' and Mill's line that the 'nature of women' is an eminently artificial thing. Singer's liberation logic, together with the Wollstonecraft-Taylor 'Vindication of the Rights of Brutes' episode and the ecofeminist link between the oppression of women and animals, is applied to Elphaba's Animal-rights activism and her position as 'neither man nor beast,' before the Witch's mirror recognition of Dorothy forces the author to soften her verdict.

feminism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
feminism.title: “Happily Ever After, Now and Then”
feminism.relation: Erin McKenna explains how a feminist can love Buffett by reading 'Fins' and 'Why Don't We Get Drunk (and Screw)' as critiques of predatory land sharks rather than endorsements, and 'Margaritaville' as a man admitting 'it's my own damn fault.' Against Rousseau's pliable helpmate ideal of woman she sets Wollstonecraft's Vindication — equal education and personhood for women — and Charlotte Perkins Gilman's pragmatist-feminist case that women's economic, physical, and mental dependence stunts everyone. Buffett's novels then pass the Gilman test: Desdemona, Trevor Kane, Cleopatra Highbourne, and Sophie are smart, independent women, and the male leads must reform their habits to earn them, aiming at Desdemona's 'happily ever after, now and then' instead of the fairy-tale ending.

feminism.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
feminism.title: The Emotion-Reason Dilemma, Part II
feminism.relation: Pribram places Monk and Dr. House in the tradition of the brilliantly rational but emotionally plagued detective (Dragnet's emotionless Joe Friday vs Cracker's Fitz), arguing both shows treat excessive emotion as the price of genius: Monk's OCD is tied to his pattern-spotting ('You're a freak of nature'), and when medication cures the OCD in 'Mr. Monk Takes His Medicine' his detective genius vanishes. She applies Foucault's Birth of the Clinic to House's subtracting of the patient, but shows both series critique that modernist rationality through Eve in 'One Day, One Room', who forces House to face the rationally inexplicable. Using feminist scholarship (Jaggar, Alberti, Battersby), she argues the opposition of male reason to female emotion is a historically specific construction, and offers the best friends Stottlemeyer and Wilson as integrated alternatives who pay for their balance with ordinariness: polarization equals greatness, integration signals the mundane.

feminism.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
feminism.title: Looking Inwards
feminism.relation: Barber, Bryce, and Davis test Donna Haraway's emancipatory cyborg thesis against Gunslinger Girl, where the Social Welfare Agency 'adopts' orphaned and abused girls (Henrietta, Rico, Triela, Elsa, Claes), rebuilds their bodies as cybernetic weapons, and drug-conditions them into loyal assassins paired with male handlers. They argue the series realizes none of Haraway's post-gender potential: conditioning erodes memory and autonomy (Rico coolly shoots the porter Emilio who befriended her; Elsa murders her handler Lauro and kills herself; Triela suffers pointless menstrual cramps in a wombless body), while the girls' kawaii styling, teddy bears, and school uniforms make them objects of the male gaze whose cuteness disguises lethal power. The cyborgs' victimization ultimately reinforces traditional gender hierarchy and mirrors conformity-pressured Japanese youth, so the cyborg has 'regressed' from the autonomous heroines of Ghost in the Shell or Battle Angel Alita.

feminism.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
feminism.title: The Last Resort
feminism.relation: Petersen recounts fighting off a man who threatened to rape and kill her, and argues that karate, not feminist doctrine or therapy, made her a real feminist by rewiring her self-concept, fear responses and relationships. Against the Lara Croft fantasy she sets practical self-defense doctrine ('don't be there'; assertiveness, not aggression, with the bus pest), Australian, US and UN statistics on violence against women, and the Guthrie study of Chicago's feminist Thousand Waves dojo. She frames the transformation with Foucault's 'care of the self': karate's practices of the self give women power through knowledge, so that by black-belt time enduring harassment simply 'isn't who she is'.

feminism.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
feminism.title: Area Man And Woman Wonder What They Are Good For
feminism.relation: Benatar uses The Onion's 'Area Man' to stage the Hart–Devlin debate: Lord Devlin made the man on the Clapham omnibus's 'real feeling of reprobation' the test for when law may enforce society's morality against private homosexual acts, and H.L.A. Hart replied that shared values can be wicked (Nazi Germany) and that societies transform rather than disintegrate when values change—confirmed by Onion Area Men who hate their gay coworker, have gay sex to dodge the office blood drive, or have spent eight years 'experimenting,' none of which dissolved Britain or America. The chapter adds the feminist complaint that treating the Area Man as the norm erases Area Woman, and closes with Joel Feinberg's crowded-bus thought experiment from Offense to Others: average disgust is relevant to regulating public offense but never decisive, so the ordinary person interests legal philosophy without being its arbiter.

feminism.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
feminism.title: Banal Sex
feminism.relation: Marinucci reads The Onion's sex coverage as 'terminally ambiguous': 'Nation's Gays Demand Right To Library Cards,' 'Massachusetts Supreme Court Orders All Citizens To Gay Marry,' and 'New Bill Would Defend Marriage From Sharks' ridicule the idea that gay marriage threatens straight marriage, while 'Area Homosexual Saves Four From Fire: Heroic Neighbor Praised, Gay' exposes how heterosexism defines gay people sexually while heterosexual men pass as normal, natural, and neutral. Yet the paper also trades in gay stereotypes and mocks the very framework—characters like Amanda Oppel ('Lesbian Identity Ends Abruptly Mid-Junior Year'), the 'Bar Skanks Announce Plans To Kiss,' and Bruce Heffernan of 'Why Do All These Homosexuals Keep Sucking My Cock?' both defy and seem to reaffirm the stability of sexual identity categories. Weighing queer theory (via Jagose) and Golden's fluid 'elective lesbians' against the parody of 'Grad Student Deconstructs Take-Out Menu,' she concludes the paper's stance is deliberately undecidable, perhaps recommending we stop over-thinking sex and treat minority sexual identities as banal, as in 'Gay Couple Has Banal Sex.'

feminism.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
feminism.title: “I Want to Look Around Me Now”
feminism.relation: Charts Rush's gradual saturation with synthesizers, sequencers, and electronic percussion from 'Subdivisions' and 'Distant Early Warning' to 'Time Stand Still,' explaining the adoption through Wajcman's gradual-modification model and feminist analyses of technology as a male skill domain — including de Beauvoir's point that technical prowess underwrites virility, which the author applies to Rush fans' valorizing of the trio's chops. It closes by casting the band's handling of music technology as Bourdieu's habitus, granting Rush 'relative autonomy' from the hi-tech pressures of the 1980s.

feminism.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
feminism.title: Specimen Watching
feminism.relation: Jason Davis applies Adorno's 'identity thinking' - the way concepts swallow particulars as specimens of the already-known - to argue Dexter is a consumer of serial killers who never asks what makes his victims what they are, only that they fit the type, from therapist Emmett Meridian on down. The same concept-machine works on animals: Buddy's buried bones and the show's predator imagery exploit the criminological animal-abuse link, letting Davis ask whether cruelty-taskforce laws quietly practice speciesism; and Carol J. Adams' sexual politics of meat connects the Ice Truck Killer's blood-drained, butcher-cut women to a meat-eating culture whose objectification makes women and animals interchangeable. Finally, the chapter notes that the women of Dexter - Deb, Rita, LaGuerta, Lila, Christine - are all written without female friendship, a homosocial specimen-class whose sameness feminist philosophers expose, so that when Dexter 'takes back the night', the 'invisible hookers' stay invisible.

feminism.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
feminism.title: After All, Who’s the Toughest Critter in Bikini Bottom
feminism.relation: Denise Du Vernay argues Sandy Cheeks is the show's one proof of feminist messaging: a liberal feminist who attains equality within the status quo as scientist, bodybuilder and 'smartest one in Bikini Bottom', while a materialist feminist reading would worry most about SpongeBob's exploitation as Mr. Krabs's worker and property ('Welcome to the Chum Bucket'). She reads 'Squirrel Jokes' as a lesson in how stereotypes spread ('stupidity isn't a virus, but it sure is spreading like one'), catalogs the show's tired female stereotypes (nagging Karen, bratty Pearl), and defends SpongeBob and Sandy against Focus on the Family's 2005 gay-panic attacks as the sexualizing of asexual children's characters.

feminism.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
feminism.title: Pleased to Meet You
feminism.relation: Blames "the Father of All Pissing Contests" — the Cold War — for forcing English boys who love women into songs hostile to them ("Under My Thumb," "Stupid Girl," "Yesterday's Papers"), and argues two theses: the Stones don't hate women, this culture hates women; and the men who call the goddess's servants "fags" are the ones who built and maintain that misogynistic culture. The Dionysian frenzy of the 1960s took a dark turn as 1968's death toll (Vietnam, MLK, RFK) exposed the world the manly men had built: the Beatles quit, "but the Stones looked the demon square in the eye and guessed its name."

feminism.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
feminism.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
feminism.relation: A feminist media-studies audit: the first two seasons flunk most feminist criteria (Skyler the pregnant homemaker, Marie the kleptomaniac, Jane existing mainly to develop Jesse), but seasons three and four deepen everyone - Walt's agonized Krazy-8 decision curdles into the lily-of-the-valley child-poisoning, while Skyler seizes the household, launders money through the car wash, and fixes Ted's IRS crisis, 'breaking bad' herself. Gus's hinted homosexuality with Max is praised for quietly rocking heteronormative assumptions. Conclusion: by Season Four the title applies to Skyler too, and her depth alone nearly passes any analytical test a feminist scholar might employ.

feminism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
feminism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Ashley Barkman argues that feminism is unrealistic and inefficient in the apocalypse: citing sex-difference research such as Bandura's Bobo doll experiments, she claims masculine aggression and strength are what leadership requires when authority must be asserted physically, as when Rick pipes Merle and shoves Daryl, or Shane tackles Ed and Jim. The quarry laundry scenes stage the debate - Jacqui's protest at 'all the Hattie McDaniel work' versus Lori's 'this isn't about women's rights... doing what needs to be done' - and Barkman sides with Lori, treating the division of labor as survival logistics under a natural-law premise that it is moral to act according to nature. Andrea the sharpshooter and Michonne the swordswoman show women can excel as heroic exceptions without leading, and the chapter concludes leadership should stay with good men like Rick.

feminism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
feminism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Pye and O'Sullivan use Judith Butler's claim that gender is performative to read the walkers as genderless: they keep the trappings of biological sex but perform no gender, and like drag queens they 'trouble gender' when the little girl walker turns to face Rick. The survivors, by contrast, drag patriarchy along as cultural baggage - Lori telling Carl 'I'm a girl, you talk to him' while Shane teaches frogs, Ed bullying the laundry line, the men confiscating Andrea's gun while Daryl keeps his crossbow - though counter-examples (Andrea and Amy fishing for the camp, Guillermo's camp of caretaking 'vatos' led by a former custodian and a nurse, Rick teaching Andrea the safety) show gender can be learned differently. Invoking Rorty's thought that assumptions become visible only when their contradictories sound plausible, they argue survival itself demands shedding these roles, since the genderless dead threaten everyone equally.

feminism.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
feminism.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Duncan reads Larry and Jeff as the two unlivable extremes of American masculinity: Larry the neurotic impotent, paralyzed by generalized Freudian anxiety (hiding Jeff's porn, fleeing the thong-wearing therapist, self-sabotaging with Lucy Lawless over his testicle injury), and Jeff the secondary narcissist who philanders without guilt, seducing Funkhouser's sister Bam-Bam and then dismissing her as crazy. Following Hegel via Jessica Benjamin, she argues both pathologies stem from failed mutual recognition—the man-child never learned to see others as subjects—and Kimmel's 'great secret of manhood' (we are afraid of other men) explains how masculine ideals produce the fear and judgment behind Larry's neurosis. Larry and Jeff's flawed but real friendship, and Leon's model of challenging Larry to be better while asking for help himself, offer glimpses of an alternative, ethically invested masculinity.

feminism.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
feminism.title: The Wire and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The Rochas argue that the only two women in the Game, Snoop on the street side and Kima on the police side, embody a 'militant feminism' in the lineage of the Black Panthers' Kathleen Cleaver and the Weather Underground's Bernardine Dohrn: women can excel at anything men can, including violence (Snoop as Marlo's natural soldier, repurposing a Hardware Barn nail gun, wearing womanhood only as a costume), and violence is justified when used for just ends (Kima overcoming fear to police). They then use Gilligan and Noddings's care ethics to explain the finale: Kima's dedication to relationships and care for the overlooked homeless victims lets her discern that McNulty and Freamon's fake-serial-killer scheme is an immoral masculinized rationalization, so she turns in her friends and becomes the show's moral conscience.

feminism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
feminism.title: Psych and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Mona Rocha asks whether Psych is sexist given Shawn's eighth-grade-girl caricature of Juliet in 'Spellingg Bee' and the secret knowledge kept from the show's women, then argues it is not: the women's inferior epistemic position is a byproduct of the con, not misogynist gatekeeping, because Shawn works collaboratively and non-hierarchically, shares credit (solving Lassiter's Back Bay Killer case for him in 'From the Earth to Starbucks'), gives the Chief the glory in 'There Might Be Blood,' and confronts the oilrig chauvinist outright. The contrast is The Mentalist, where Patrick Jane's withholding of deductions from Lisbon - going behind her back in 'Red Hair and Silver Tape' and getting evidence thrown out in 'Blood Money' - enacts patriarchal paternalism that undermines female leadership.

feminism.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
feminism.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The editors introduce the book by contrasting The Good Wife with earlier law shows like Law and Order: for the first time we see lawyers at home, and the central figure is Alicia Florrick, juggling teenagers, a firm in bankruptcy, and a marriage wrecked by Peter's prostitution scandal while keeping up appearances as the 'good wife' and taking lover Will Gardner. They argue the show refuses a single right answer - her choices are selfish, cowardly, vengeful, or simply her being true to herself - and that her growth as a woman, mother, and lawyer challenges preconceived social norms about women and about lawyers. Philosophy enters as the natural sequel: ethics, justice, feminism, privacy rights, epistemology, and social-political philosophy are all sewn into the episodes.

feminism.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
feminism.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Celine Morin reads Alicia's love life through the Greek triad agape, eros, and philia as laid out in Plato's Symposium: her unconditional agape for Peter is eroded by his demands for forgiveness ('Stripped', 'Boom'), while the Socratic myth of Eros born from Penia's lack explains why she tells Will their affair is 'romantic because it didn't happen'. She argues Alicia abandons the romantic soul-mate model of her pearl-necklace marriage for Giddens's egalitarian 'pure relationship' with Will, but stays moored to the old family structure, hesitating on the doorstep in the Season Three cliffhanger 'The Dream Time'. Her discovery of feminism through Diane Lockhart is what lets Alicia weigh leaving that structure without destroying her family.

feminism.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
feminism.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Karen Adkins argues the show exposes the 'choice' to stay home as neither free nor innocent: Betty Friedan's Feminine Mystique and Linda Hirshman's Get to Work frame how Alicia's more-promising-than-Will-or-Peter career was sacrificed to Peter's ambitions and now constrains her, while Peter's 'thanks for playing the breadwinner', Cary's condescension in 'Fleas', and Jackie's 'we stay in the shadows' speech treat her work as a hobby. The show's feminism goes bland, she contends, when Alicia declines to fight Caitlin's resignation in 'Long Way Home' and endorses choice feminism against her own history. The chapter's evidence runs both ways, though: the 'We're not the cops, honey' double standard, and Alicia's mom skills and lawyer skills flowing productively between nursery and deposition room.

feminism.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
feminism.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Offered as a salute to The Good Wife's female lawyers (Alicia, Diane, Caitlin, Geneva Pine, Dana Lodge, Elsbeth Tascioni), this piece collects good, bad, and memorable real women attorneys: pioneers Bettisia Gozzadini, Arabella Mansfield, Myra Bradwell - barred by Justice Bradley's 'wife and mother' dictum in Bradwell v. Illinois - and Charlotte E. Ray; notorious figures like accused murderer Mary Leonard; and trailblazers Gloria Allred, Sandra Day O'Connor, Constance Baker Motley, and Ruth Bader Ginsburg. The parade of firsts grounds the show's fictional women in the real feminist struggle to enter and practice the legal profession.

feminism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
feminism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Caroline Mosser treats the creature's tragedy as humanist prejudice rather than necessity: the blind De Lacey accepts the eloquent creature sight unseen, so he passes Alan Turing's test, and only the sighted family's terror at his body rejects him - bias against the artificial, not reason. She reads the creature's development through fire, language, and revolution as Rousseau's progression from natural innocence to corruption by society, and Donna Haraway's cyborg as the figure he prefigures: an unfaithful illegitimate offspring who rebels against his father and undermines patriarchal Western self/other dualisms. The chapter concludes that society cannot accept enhanced or posthuman beings until it finds a middle ground beyond its binary grids of good/bad and Self/Other, since otherwise any new life we create will be Othered, hated, and oppressed like Frankenstein's.

feminism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
feminism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Mike Kugler argues Shelley's novel tests the radical idealism of her father William Godwin, her mother Mary Wollstonecraft, and her husband Percy: Victor's Promethean project of perfecting humanity in isolation, away from the 'intimate circle' of family and friends, produces a creature whose natural benevolence is destroyed only by repeated exclusion, first by the De Laceys. Drawing on Rousseau's and Wollstonecraft's view that children raised by benevolent parents develop their innate sympathy, the chapter reads the creature as an abandoned child - a new Adam who becomes a Satanic rebel when every community rejects him - and Victor's attempt at reproduction without women and mothers as the novel's deepest violation. The redemptive counterfactual is adoption: what if Victor had raised the creature in his home, as his father did Elizabeth?

feminism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
feminism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The chapter reads Robin's series-long arc as an argument for non-essentialist feminism against Carol Gilligan's suggestion that all women share fundamental traits and rules. Caught between Lily's Dreamhouse-Barbie domesticity and the Career-Barbie ideal her father forcibly raised her into - mocked by kindergartners at career day, 'called slut' by Marshall for a one-night stand in 'The Naked Man' - Robin keeps trying to live one prescribed path entirely and is miserable both times. Only when she stops choosing between the boxes, marrying Barney while still never wanting children, does the show endorse the non-essentialist feminism of Deborah Rhode and Drucilla Cornell: a woman may custom-tailor her own happy ending.

feminism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
feminism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The chapter argues the Bro Code's real value lies not in getting laid but in structuring homosocial bonds, listing its best articles (loyalty, equality, generosity) alongside its most sexist ones (the Hot/Crazy Scale, Article 101). Karioris explains men's competitive relations through hegemonic masculinity - the school-bully dominance that forces all masculinities to compete and pushes women out - and invokes Foucault's 'Friendship as a Way of Life' for how bonds between men can escape taboo and emotional distance. Robin as wingwoman ('a better Ted than Ted') and the gang's gender transgressions show the Code can be amended toward equality, with Aristotle's friendship of mutual cooperation and benefit, 'quid pro bro', as the standard.

feminism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
feminism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The chapter argues HIMYM offers two complementary feminist icons: Robin embodies personal autonomy and independence - fighting from 'but, um' early-morning shifts to lead anchor, and grieving infertility as stolen autonomy rather than lost motherhood - while Lily, and even more Marshall, exemplify Carol Gilligan's feminist care ethics with its emphasis on emotion over impartiality, cooperation over competition, and partiality toward loved ones. Aristotle's golden mean supplies the test Robin passes by balancing career and love instead of pushing one to an extreme. The twist that a male character best exemplifies care ethics, with Lily bridging the two moral outlooks, is offered as the show's progressive complexity about gender.

feminism.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
feminism.title: Girls and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Frost argues that critics who call Girls unwatchable because Hannah steals the hotel housekeeper's tip and the characters are unlikeable are watching television the wrong way. Using Adorno's 'How to Look at Television,' he shows how mainstream standardized shows (Friends and its copies) pre-digest viewing, how Sex and the City exemplifies Adorno's ideological 'fake-realism,' and how hidden messages of adjustment work through audience identification - none of which Girls permits with its raw sex scenes, Hannah's unglamorous body, and Jessa's non-judged promiscuity. Because identification with Hannah, Marnie, and Jessa (the diary-reading, the request to Laird for heroin) is impossible, Girls escapes the culture industry and exercises the viewer's critical faculties toward the Kantian autonomy and emancipation Adorno demands - which is also why role-model feminist criticism (Catherine Scott's) misses the point.

feminism.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
feminism.title: Girls and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Robison-Greene defends Girls against the twin criticisms that it is bad feminism (Hannah 'sluttin' around' jokes, Adam's degrading sex with Hannah) and irresponsibly all-white. She argues there is no single correct conception of feminism from which to judge Dunham, that 'demeaning sex is anti-feminist, so portraying it is anti-feminist' is an invalid argument (by analogy with portraying racism in 12 Years a Slave), and notes MacKinnon's dominance view that sex itself may be inherently demeaning only to conclude the debate is legitimate, not settled against the show. On race, she contends Dunham writing authentically from her own half-Jew, half-WASP experience produces better art than tokenism would, and that the obligation to fix representation falls on networks and creators with the relevant experience, not on punishing one writer.

feminism.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
feminism.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The chapter uses Adventure Time's gender play - Fionna and Cake, princesses holding nearly all political power in Ooo, Jake as terrified helicopter dad, Mannish Man's parody of manliness - to ask what being a man or woman really means. Following Judith Butler's Gender Trouble, it argues sex does not fix gender: the Lumpy Space King and Queen share one body, Flame King is a flame in a suit, and Butler's critique of the MIT 'master gene' experiment shows how the assumption that men and women are opposites smuggles cultural convention into science. Finn is read as performing masculinity - Billy worship, dungeon codes, the endless 'Dungeon Train' - caught in a crisis of masculinity between what society says a man is and who he is, with the ghost of Shoko in 'The Vault' and the accepted grass sword as steps toward a heroism that is his own.

feminism.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
feminism.title: Justified and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The chapter surveys Harlan's gendered violence - Ava's killing of Bowman, the routine roughing-up of Audrey's working girls, Robert Quarles's childhood prostitution - and uses Catharine MacKinnon's account of patriarchal power imbalance to explain victim-blaming, underreporting, and police disbelief of trauma responses in domestic-violence and rape cases. On prostitution it weighs sex-positive feminism against the objectification worry, concluding via Teri's line about 'sucking hillbilly dicks for money' that Audrey's women have little real choice even under Ava's management. Finally it brings in bell hooks's third-wave point that oppression cannot be split from race and class, plus Peggy McIntosh's invisible backpack of white privilege, to read Noble's Holler's isolation and the bombed black church as evidence that patriarchy in Justified is always also racial and economic.

feminism.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
feminism.title: Justified and Philosophy
feminism.relation: The chapter argues Mags Bennett is the show's 'outlaw mother', read through feminist media theory: she escapes Laura Mulvey's male gaze as an unkempt older woman viewers are never invited to look at pleasurably, defies the institution of motherhood described by Adrienne Rich (hammering Coover's hand as tough love), and literalizes Andrea O'Reilly's outlaw mothering - questioning the 'shoulds' of motherhood and not always putting children first. Stuart Hall's encoding/decoding model explains how audiences can hold her simultaneously as the poisoned-apple-pie murderer of Walt McCready and the maternal folk hero of the whoop-de-do. Her Black Pike reversal - the community speech followed by selling out the mountain for Doyle's sons - seals the portrait of a mother whose love is indistinguishable from strategy.

feminism.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
feminism.title: 16. Female Integrity in Times of Change
feminism.relation: Melanie Abbott combines Bernard Williams's view of integrity - publicly and consistently standing up for the beliefs that make you you - with Kant's good will to define a 'right sort' of holding fast that separates the virtuous woman from the fanatic, then tests it on five Crawley women. Sybil's unwavering egalitarianism (eloping with Branson, nursing, women's rights), Edith's uneven growth (the Gregson affair, journalism, her secrecy over Marigold at the Drewes' farm), Mary's shift from custom to moral agency (upholding Matthew's will, pig farming, standing up to Robert), Cora's quiet push for a voice, and even Violet's late flexibility show integrity as growth through change. The chapter's 'Sybil effect' is that the sister with the fewest doubts becomes the model the others gradually follow.

feminism.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
feminism.title: 21. Buttercup and the Eternal Feminine
feminism.relation: Archibald reads Buttercup wholly through Beauvoir's The Second Sex: as the farm's natural leader she is not yet 'woman as Other', but Humperdinck's ultra-feminized public presentation, the arranged marriage, the old woman's 'Queen of Filth' nightmare, and the men dismissing her advice all enact the myth of the eternal feminine that punishes a woman for asserting herself. Her leap toward the shrieking eels becomes an emblem of autonomy that society punishes, the 'privilege' of compliance a curse that leaves her suicidal, and the closing image of the couple riding together as one sketches Beauvoir's ideal of a relationship founded on mutual liberty.

feminism.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
feminism.title: 20. Feminists Can Take a Joke
feminism.relation: Argues Louis performs feminist philosophy by writing marginalized voices into his work: Rick's poker speech about what 'faggot' means to gay men who hear it during beatings, Vanessa's seven-minute 'So Did the Fat Lady' confrontation that leaves Louie silenced, and his Daily Show reflection on learning that rape polices women's lives. The chapter does not excuse his slurs ('cunt,' 'nigger,' 'faggot'), but contends his admitted fallibility is what keeps a broad, mixed audience listening—the guy who came for masturbation jokes leaves having heard about rape culture—so feminism and comedy are not natural enemies.

feminism.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
feminism.title: 13. How to Be a Dwarf
feminism.relation: Using Carrot (a human raised in a dwarf mine who is accepted as a dwarf), Cheery Littlebottom (an openly female dwarf), and Gladys the golem, the chapter argues that social identity is neither biology nor a one-time choice but an ongoing performance that must also be recognized by insiders and outsiders. It applies de Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' to Cheery's creation of a female dwarf gender against the deep-downers' equality that treats every dwarf as male, and reads the black ribboners versus the Magpyrs as assimilation versus doubling down on identity. Essentialist outsiders like Fred Colon and the Campaign for Equal Heights fail because they cling to stereotypes when individuals like Cheery or Carrot do not fit the mold, while Vetinari's indifference and Mrs. Cake's accommodations leave identity to those who must choose and perform it.

feminism.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
feminism.title: 19. The Alchemy of Flat Worlds
feminism.relation: Staged as Professor Moby Dickens Melville's 'Philosophy of Worlds' course uniting Discworld wizards with the geometric Flatlanders of Abbott's novella, the chapter contrasts a storytelling, narrative-causality philosophy of Discworld with Flatland's mathematical, hierarchy-obsessed rationalism, and extends the contrast to physics (wizards favor loop quantum gravity, Flatlanders string theory) and theology (Hex's self-designed universe and words of power versus Flatland's circle-priests who rule women declared 'deficient in Reason'). When a Flatlander woman, Ms. Transversal, protests that calling the new softer approach 'feminine' repeats Abbott's sexism, the class closes with the narrator's suggestion, from a chalk-nub's-eye view, that everything we know may reflect the direction from which we see rather than the truth itself.

feminism.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
feminism.title: 11. Leda, Castor, and Their Families
feminism.relation: Shows how the clones queer the normative family: clones as such are "biological outlaws" (via Stephanie Turner's reading of Ripley in Alien), Siobhan turns out to be the genetic half-sister of the clones cloned from her own mother Kendall, and the chosen family — Felix the "brother sestra," Kira's aunties, Helena's dream baby shower — repeatedly rebuilds kinship outside blood and marriage. Against this stands the stripping of reproductive agency: the infertility sequence written into the Leda clones, Coady's weaponized sterilizing virus, and above all Helena, whose eggs are harvested and implanted by Henrik and Gracie's father without consent. The chapter's conclusion is that Orphan Black's blood families are abusive and controlling while the non-normative chosen families of Clone Club are where love and consent actually live.

feminism.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
feminism.title: 12. Not Why but Who
feminism.relation: Reads the mothers of Orphan Black through Freud and Lacan: Dr. Coady is the "phallic mother" at the center of the Castor clones' Oedipal drama (Rudy's kiss, the DNA trophies brought home to Mom), Tomas is Helena's abusive false father, Rachel is the child of a shattered Oedipal triangle, and the Symbolic Order that makes men active rational subjects and women passive reproductive objects is mirrored in the defects — neurological for the male clones, reproductive for the female. The chapter then brings in Luce Irigaray to show the show rewriting these stereotypes: the clones' spectrum of personalities and their constant impersonations destabilize fixed gender categories, and the many equally "real" mothers (Mrs. S., Amelia, Alison, Kendall) burst the woman-equals-womb equation. Beth's counsel to the delirious Sarah — "Stop asking 'Why?' and start asking 'Who?'" — becomes the feminist move from mechanism to women as active subjects.

feminism.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
feminism.title: 13. Sisterhood’s Back in Orphan Black
feminism.relation: Recounts the rise and fall of second-wave sisterhood — the dream of a unified female voice that erased differences of race, class, sexuality, and nation until the 1980s backlash killed it — and argues Orphan Black resurrects a corrected version through Rosi Braidotti's posthumanism. The clones, disposable bodies of biogenetic capitalism, build a sisterhood that celebrates difference (grunge Sarah, dreads-and-lab-coat Cosima, suburban Alison, savage Helena) rather than enforcing sameness, and that welcomes the Others the Seventies excluded — gay Felix, Black Art, Hindu Raj — while white Western men like Paul remain the surveillance agents of the backlash. Through posthumanism's dissolution of fixed human identity, the chapter claims, feminism's old ideal returns both transformed and inclusive.

feminism.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
feminism.title: 17. Wade Wilson Fights Like a Girl
feminism.relation: Staged as a Socratic dialogue in a professor's office, the chapter tests Peter Coogan's definition of the superhero (mission, powers, identity) against the Deadpool movie and finds Wade qualifies while mocking the genre. It then argues the film subverts the superhero genre's sexist conventions: Vanessa refuses the damsel role by grabbing the bar mercenary's crotch and later skewering Francis herself, Angel Dust knocks Colossus out, and Negasonic Teenage Warhead is 'a damsel to the rescue.' Applying Laura Mulvey's male gaze, it shows the camera lingering on Deadpool's body and adopting Vanessa's viewpoint in the Calendar Girl scene, with the Women in Refrigerators trope, Gwen Stacy's death, and the Hawkeye Initiative as evidence of what the movie overturns.

feminism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
feminism.title: 1 Introduction
feminism.relation: Smith introduces his project of explaining the subordination of women and blacks philosophically and empirically by comparing the social contract liberalism of Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau with Marxism, building on Carole Pateman's Sexual Contract and Charles Mills's Racial Contract/Contract and Domination, which show the classic contracts were male supremacist and white supremacist. He argues sexual and racial egalitarianism is about politics and power, cataloguing nine power bases women and blacks should acquire, and stresses that because family and state are historically connected (Aristotle's Politics, Hobbes's 'little kingdoms', Locke's conjugal society, Rousseau's family as the oldest society, Engels's 'first class oppression' of the female by the male), equality in marriage may be a precondition for equality in society. He defends Marxism against Mills's dismissal of it as moribund, endorses MacKinnon's linking of sexism and racism while arguing (with Linda LaRue and Du Bois) that the racial contract has been more tyrannical than the sexual contract, and closes with Walzer's definition of egalitarianism as a society free of domination.

feminism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
feminism.title: 5 The Changing Bases of Sexual Politics, 1960–2020
feminism.relation: Measuring women's progress since 1960 by access to the nine power bases, the chapter shows women using the size/solidarity base to launch the modern feminist movement - Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique as its manifesto, NOW as its vehicle, Ms. as its outlet and Gloria Steinem as its charismatic leader - and how law followed: the accidental Smith amendment adding sex to the 1964 Civil Rights Act, Reed and Frontiero subjecting sex classifications to scrutiny under the 14th Amendment, Griswold and Roe/Casey making reproductive control (which Justice Blackmun called 'necessary for the complete emancipation of women') a condition of women's power, and the 1970s no-fault divorce revolution that Engels's liberation program had demanded. It then charts each base statistically: the narrowing labor-force and wage gaps, women's still minor share of the bourgeoisie, the reversal of the college gender gap and Women's Studies programs built on the Black Studies model, women's entry into cabinet, Court, Congress, clergy and the military, secularization that weakens the religion base behind Elizabeth Cady Stanton's old challenge, and a new moral consensus that unequal treatment of women is wrong.

feminism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
feminism.title: 6 Wives and Husbands The Marital Power Struggle
feminism.relation: Taking Susan Okin's 'the personal is political' and Kate Millett's Weberian herrschaft against Locke's public/private dichotomy, the chapter reviews the empirical studies of marital power (Blood and Wolfe, Blumstein and Schwarz, Steil) and finds money is the master base in marriage: the husband's income and occupational prestige set his say, working wives gain power but couples conspire to understate wives' earnings ('manning up and womaning down'), while knowledge and status are the next strongest resources. Authority from religion, tradition and morality still favors husbands (Ephesians' 'wives submit yourselves unto your husbands' alongside the philosophers' 'abler and stronger'), violence persists from the rule of thumb to marital rape and murder despite legal change, housework remains women's burden - Beauvoir's never-won 'battle against dust', Engels's 'leaden boredom', Davis's industrialization proposal and Okin's demand that it be shared - and sex itself works as a power base in the bedroom, with MacKinnon diagnosing heterosexuality as the linchpin of gender inequality. The chapter ends with black couples' comparatively egalitarian patterns traced by Angela Davis to slave-quarters equality, Schwarz's rare 'peer marriages', and the Marxist (Okin, the Swedish model) versus liberal (Wilson, the Japanese model) readings of family change.

feminism.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
feminism.title: 13. Burn the Witch!
feminism.relation: Argues Coven is a feminist counterpoint to Aquinas's Natural Law - the reason-grounded doctrine of universal human nature historically wielded against 'unnatural' women, from Zoe's vagina-dentata power to Misty burned in the bayou - and, drawing on Augustine's Confessions ('Things that exist are good', so corruptibility implies goodness to lose) and Lady Macbeth's 'unsex me here', shows that women who are both witch and woman break any single natural moral code; Myrtle Snow, who embraces her double nature and goes 'proudly to the flame', proves Natural Law works only as Cupp-style discernment, not as commandments.

feminism.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
feminism.title: 9. But Women Can Vote . .
feminism.relation: Hansmann and Jones set Adams's gender posts against the four waves of feminism and the men's rights movement: his March 2011 Men's Rights post telling activists to get over it while lumping women with four-year-olds and the mentally handicapped, his Global Gender War matriarchy in which any country where women can vote counts as female-ruled, his framing of sex as a woman's currency for extracting male strategy (sacrifice a pawn to nail the queen), and his serial interrupting of women. They show the rhetoric eerily echoes anti-suffragists like Mrs. William Force Scott and Senator Sanford and the Goldilocks Dilemma, note the red-pill fantasy borrowed from The Matrix, and conclude that calling America a matriarchy defies scholarly consensus, with Beauvoir's The Second Sex marking why the vote never delivered the balance of power.

feminism.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
feminism.title: 3. Laura Palmer—Madonna and Whore
feminism.relation: Applies Freud's Madonna-whore complex — "where such men love, they have no desire, and where they desire, they cannot love" — to Laura Palmer's split between homecoming queen/Meals on Wheels volunteer and cocaine-prostitute, arguing the contradiction exists only in a mindset that forces women into two poles, which BOB weaponizes with his "dirty and sleazy" refrain. The chapter surveys explanations of the complex (incest fear, paternity anxiety, alpha-male identity visible in Leo and Jacques), and then indicts the Fireman as a feminist "nice guy": his Part 8 creation of Laura as a golden orb of purity sent to redeem the world of the Bomb is the ultimate Madonna role, a Christ-like burden that is what makes her the target BOB must debase. Even her friends' names — Maddie and Donna — spell Madonna.

feminism.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
feminism.title: 10. The Miss Twin Peaks Award Goes To . .
feminism.relation: Sorts the power of Twin Peaks' women into power-over (getting others to do what you want) and power-to (abilities and resources of one's own), and argues the first is fatally dependent on its targets. Josie's flirtation and tears control Pete and Harry — the negligee scene defusing his questioning — until Andrew, Catherine, and the obsessed Eckhardt prove immune, leaving her dissolving into the wood of the Great Northern; Audrey similarly manipulates Ben into the department-store job and a manager into the perfume counter, but is drugged and hostage once Blackie resists, and only regains standing by learning to run the business. Nadine's adrenaline strength shows pure power-to, and Lana Budding Milford's hypnotic hold on every man (but not the Miss Twin Peaks jury with its female member) marks the limit of charm-based power.

feminism.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
feminism.title: 11. The Mother of All Bombs
feminism.relation: Uses Hannah Arendt's On Violence — violence begets a more violent world, and WWII birthed the cold war rather than peace — to read Part 8, where the Trinity test, via the entity Judy/Mother, births BOB, whose garmonbozia-hunger is nuclear-age destruction feeding on female pain. Carol Gilligan's account of patriarchal silencing of women's voices (Naido's shut eyes, Laura's violated diary, the Persephone pattern of girls who must "die") and Gilbert and Gubar's dying "Angel in the House" frame Laura as both born from the Fireman and Señorita Dido as an antidote to the Bomb and destroyed by the mother wound Sarah Palmer carries. Against the toxic masculinity of Mr. C, Richard, and Chad, the show's good men — Cooper, the Trumans, Hawk, Bobby — embody Gilligan's ethic of care, and the chapter ends by demanding America put down its weapons and listen to women.

feminism.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
feminism.title: 13. The Laughter and the Fury
feminism.relation: Situates Inside Amy Schumer between Aristotle's Poetics dictum that valor in a woman is inappropriate, his Politics claim of female inferiority, and the 1970s French feminists: Cixous's 'Laugh of the Medusa' breaking up truth with laughter and Irigaray's strategic mimesis. Kolb reads stereotype-performing sketches with violent endings, such as the 'I'm So Bad' women devouring a waiter's face and the 'You Are Gorgeous' anthem rewarding a faked miscarriage and an N-word rap, as resubmitting women to stereotypes to explode them. Casting-couch opener '2 Girls, 1 Cup', 'Focus Group', and '12 Angry Men' hold up a mirror to the male gaze and to the rage it produces when women stop performing for it.
