feminism.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
feminism.title: 16. Raucous Feminist or Racially Insensitive
feminism.relation: Weighs Schumer's Peabody-honored 'raucous feminist' image against charges of racial insensitivity by contrasting liberal feminism, exemplified by Friedan's problem that has no name, with intersectionality: hooks's rejoinder that Friedan spoke only for white middle-class women and Crenshaw's multiply-burdened identities. Ware reads the 'Mostly Sex Stuff' jokes about Asian women and third-world bikini waxers, the Beyonce 'Formation' video with Goldie Hawn, and Schumer's dismissive tweets as speaking 'for women' while erasing difference, though the 'Herpes Scare' caricature shows her sometimes winking from inside an intentionally vapid persona. The verdict: Schumer can be both a genuine and an imperfect feminist who must still take accountability.

feminism.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
feminism.title: 17. Switching It Up
feminism.relation: Argues Trainwreck and the stand-up material on sexual 'ownership' expose patriarchal double standards: the same promiscuity that makes men players makes women sluts, while LeBron James's gossipy, overprotective best friend and John Cena's devoted, unthreatening boyfriend cast male stars in traditional rom-com female roles. Browning brings in Kant's view that sexual desire treats persons as objects to be discarded like squeezed lemons, conceding that counting conquests objectifies partners while rejecting Kant's celibate conclusion. Schumer's comedy instead shows women owning their orgasms, turning sex from competition into mutual gratification.

feminism.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
feminism.title: 9. Machines Who Care
feminism.relation: Weiss reads 'The Lonely' and 'I Sing the Body Electric' as anticipations of today's debate over 'relational artifacts' — Turkle's sociable robots, the Sparrows' claim that robotic aged care is unethical, Coeckelbergh's rebuttal — asking, with Anne, whether an electric grandma 'doesn't sound so good.' Corry's Alicia and the children's electric grandma show care being bought as an assembly-line product for the lonely, and he presses the details: why the caring robots are female and serve water, why Alicia arrives in a box and is summarily shot in the face when no longer needed, and what it says about a culture that maroons people in loneliness and then sells the technical fix.

feminism.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
feminism.title: Back to the Rough Ground!
feminism.relation: Finnegan uses Wittgenstein's language games, the 'picture' that holds us captive, and 'back to the rough ground' to argue that Ford, Sizemore, and the Man in Black are paralyzed by an idealized, patriarchal picture of narrative (winners and losers, violence, transcendent self-discovery), while Dolores and Maeve gain traction by inventing new language games within their forms of life. Dolores breaks her damsel script in Pariah ('I imagined a story where I didn't have to be the damsel') and reworks scripted love-dialogue to describe her grief, while Maeve bullies the lab techs, takes administrative control, and narrates other hosts' actions - 'Time to write my own fucking story.' The chapter reads their objectified position (via Mulvey's male gaze, which leaves female viewers identifying with the robot hosts rather than the male subject) as exactly what equips them for guerrilla warfare in the master's language games, doing what Audre Lorde thought impossible: dismantling the master's house with the master's tools.

feminism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
feminism.title: Resisting Dystopia
feminism.relation: The editor's introduction argues that The Handmaid's Tale disturbs us because it shows how tenuous our civil liberties are, so we must actively watch political events for warning signs. It insists that a woman's value is not fixed by her body, fertility, or attractiveness—Handmaids are treated as incubators and commodities—and that the caring work women do is a power, not a weakness. It closes on the lesson that facts, not politicians, control the narrative, ending with 'Nolite te bastardes carborundorum.'

feminism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
feminism.title: 1. A Great Darkness Filled with Echoes
feminism.relation: De Vaul argues Gilead terrifies because social cycle theory structures it: every detail, from the Puritan wedding-night sheet to Stalin-style purges and the Nazi and residential-school seizure of children, already happened, so Gilead reads as speculative rather than science fiction. Atwood's three stated influences—Puritan New England, the 1980s religious right, and Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four—show history cycling back, with June as the apolitical 'backlash' daughter her second-wave mother Holly and the activist Moira both predicted. The pattern repeats at small scale (June relives the former Offred's Scrabble-and-affair story, Omar's family suffers June's own fate) and in the Historical Notes, where Pieixoto strips Offred of authorship, proving 'the past is a great darkness, filled with echoes.'

feminism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
feminism.title: 3. Gestational Totalitarianism
feminism.relation: Kolb reads Gilead through Arendt's The Human Condition and The Origins of Totalitarianism: when reproduction becomes the means of production, women's labor is targeted, forcing fertile women into Animal laborans status as 'national resources' while denying them the creative freedom of Homo faber. She traces the polis/oikos split from Aristotle through Puritan capitalism to show Gilead overcorrecting into Aunt Lydia's 'freedom from'—totalitarian control of birth legitimized by the Rachel and Bilhah story and a Pauline creation story. The chapter ends with the transitional generation's forgetting (Offred's cave-delusion with Nick evoking Plato's Allegory of the Cave, the Holocaust documentarian 'thinking about how not to think') and Ofglen's bomb, arguing that thoughtfulness and literacy, not violence, are the only hopes against totalitarianism.

feminism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
feminism.title: 4. The United States of Gilead
feminism.relation: Greene argues that the contemporary United States under Trump exhibits early Gilead-like symptoms, detailing five shared techniques: othering (the Aunts' stereotypes of pre-Gilead women vs. Trump on Mexicans and Muslims), separating children from parents (Handmaid births and seizure of Hannah vs. immigrant detention camps), gaslighting (Janine's 'her fault' Testifying vs. inauguration-crowd and Mueller claims), discrediting dissent (Gilead's ban on reading vs. 'fake news'), and lying (Gilead's founding promise of elections vs. thousands of false claims and 'alternative facts'). He grounds the danger in the correspondence theory of truth: once leaders detach belief from how the world actually is, society is a small step from Atwood's dystopia.

feminism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
feminism.title: 11. What about the Men
feminism.relation: Jones argues that Nick is coerced as surely as June—ordered by Serena, married off to Eden, unable to refuse without Gilead's punishments—so calling his unwilling sex rape should be uncontroversial. Yet he then argues the 'what about the men?' question itself is inappropriate: because politics and film are male-dominated (19 percent women in Congress, 4.1 percent of top films directed by women), women's lived experience rarely gets center stage, and male readers instinctively bend such rare texts back toward themselves. Pieixoto's flirty, fact-obsessed keynote is the model of this failure, and the challenge for male viewers is to listen to what the show says about women's experience—including #MeToo-era sexual violence—without making it about men.

feminism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
feminism.title: 13. Gilead vs. the Self
feminism.relation: Holberg argues that on Kantian grounds Gilead is morally incoherent—Handmaids are treated as mere means, vessels without agency—and that it sustains itself by attacking self-respect through two temporal modes: the quick onset of fear (Aristotle's account in the Rhetoric applied to the machine-gun arrests of women at their jobs) and the slow grind of shame (empty time that turns women into 'objects not in use' and manufactures a veneer of consent: 'nothing is going on here that I haven't signed up for'). Agency needs recognition from others—love as the most basic acknowledgment, or invoking Moira ('Moira would never stand for this shit')—so June's 'I tell, therefore you are' and the reader's duty to affirm her judgment carry the feminist-Kantian point: dependency on others does not negate the self, it is what constitutes it.

feminism.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
feminism.title: 7. She Went Down Swingin’
feminism.relation: Volpert argues Tom Petty was a feminist, the only classic-rock male whose catalog consistently grants women rational equality and agency, adopting Susan McClary's feminist New Musicology as her lens and marching through Greatest Hits song by song. She reads the forced removal of the Lolita cover from "American Girl," the consensual, threat-free request of "Breakdown," and "Listen to Her Heart" as Petty's reply to Ike Turner's cocaine-locked party, and defends "You Got Lucky" as a conceit about band technology rather than misogyny. The chapter confronts the gaze directly, arguing "Here Comes My Girl" watches a woman walking toward you as formidable rather than objectified, with the video's flirtations redirected homoerotically at the Heartbreakers themselves.

feminism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
feminism.title: 21. The Trouble with Joi
feminism.relation: M.J. Ryder uses Judith Butler's Gender Trouble to argue that Joi's womanhood is a performance, and so is her humanity: an 'it' playing a woman playing a human, in nested layers from Ana de Armas through the hologram to the 1950s housewife act. The chapter situates this in the real economy of female-voiced assistants (Siri, Cortana) scripted by human writers to seem real and trustworthy, and rereads the awkward Mariette threesome as Joi acting out what she believes human sex is, the two bodies never quite coinciding. Joi's final choice of mortal peril — 'like a real girl' — completes the performance, which is why the film leaves us unsure whether performing humanity differs from having it.

feminism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
feminism.title: 22. Rachael, Weeping for Her Children
feminism.relation: Bonnie McLean maps Baudrillard's four-stage precession of simulacra onto the women of 2049: Joshi anchors reality, implanted memories distort it, Joi is representation masking the absence of reality, and the eye-color-wrong reconstructed Rachael is a simulacrum of a simulacrum bearing no relation to reality. Read this way, the film lionizes birth — Wallace kissing the replicant he has just disemboweled, her blood running down her legs — while stripping every woman of agency in service of K's quest, a dynamic the chapter links to pro-life politics and DACA-era savior narratives. Only by removing K from the narrative, she shows, does the women's erasure become visible.

feminism.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
feminism.title: 12. What about Della Street
feminism.relation: Birondo evaluates Della Street through moral psychology and Aristotelian virtue ethics: she is an excellent secretary in the role-specific sense (the Gregg shorthand that traps Robert Caddo's contradiction outside The Lonely Heiress crime scene) and supplies the 'woman's angle' the office needs, while Perry displays Aristotle's practical wisdom in court but a failure of recognition toward her, under-crediting her and kissing her for her 'feminine charms' upon her skullduggery in ways that today would be sexual harassment. The chapter also applies Aristotle on habituation through Mrs. Caddo's 'wildcat' tantrums hardening into character, and asks whether Della's team-playing beyond her duties is admirable, sad, or itself the product of mid-century sexism.

feminism.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
feminism.title: Liz Meets the Elephant in the Room
feminism.relation: Barkman reads 'Rosemary's Baby' as staging second-wave feminism in Rose Howard's comfort-sacrificing activism against third-wave feminism in Liz, who sells her dignity for the $10,000 Followship Award and likes comfort and the status quo. Sartre's existence precedes essence supplies third-wave feminism's non-essentialist claim that anyone can be a feminist in any manner, while an Aristotelian essentialist standard of human flourishing shows Liz's 'have it all' optimism, from the wedding dress bought in 'SeinfeldVision' to the adoption schemes of 'Do-Over', is a delusion because career and family each demand everything. Jack's confession that 'you have to choose' lands the chapter's verdict that the third-wave promise leaves women in Liz's predicament.

feminism.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
feminism.title: NOTES
feminism.relation: Argues that Alice, in Carroll's and Disney's versions, is a feminist model who navigates Wonderland by her own wits, unlike passive princesses such as Cinderella and Aurora who need male rescue. Megan S. Lloyd reads Alice's fall down the rabbit-hole as a rejection of her sister's idle female role, the Pigeon's complaints and the Duchess's shaken pig-baby as showing that motherhood is not a requirement of female worth, and the Mad Hatter's 'Then you shouldn't talk' as the old-boy network punishing an assertive woman. Alice's final 'You're nothing but a pack of cards!' completes her growth into a powerful presence, and the chapter closes by asking what twenty-first-century young women facing double standards would do if they asked 'What would Alice do?'

feminism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
feminism.title: A Professional, a Mother, and Someone Who Cares
feminism.relation: Asks whether Ripley is a feminist and answers 'only sometimes': her quarantine refusal ('Yes, I read you. The answer is negative') and her reasons for killing the Alien3 specimen ('a lot of innocent people will die') invoke rules, chain of command, and anonymous future victims - Kohlberg's post-conventional reasoning, not Gilligan's care voice - whereas the hot-chocolate scene with Newt and the unhesitating hive rescue exhibit the care-focused feminism of Gilligan and Noddings. Against the status-oriented reading of Vasquez's 'have you ever been mistaken for a man?' exchange, Ripley emerges as atypical of either stereotype: a professional, a mother, and someone who cares.

feminism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
feminism.title: Equal Opportunity Offenders
feminism.relation: Argues the Facehugger stages rape with the sexes reversed: because the aliens violate male and female bodies impartially - Kane's penetration, forced pregnancy, and death in childbirth; the cocooned Dallas begging Ripley to kill him - the films strip male viewers of the patriarchal privilege of treating sexual violence as someone else's threat and even of biological immunity to forced pregnancy. The Marines' 'colonists' daughters' banter, the prisoners' treatment of Ripley on Fury 161, and Johner's basketball comment exemplify a rape culture (Dworkin: rape is committed by exemplars of our norms) persisting into the twenty-second century, while Frye and Shafer's 'domain' explains why bodily violation attacks personhood itself.

feminism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
feminism.title: Repairing Our Worlds
feminism.relation: Fice reads ATLA through the feminist ethics of care, using Joan Tronto's phases of caring-about, taking care of, and care-giving to analyze Katara: freeing Aang from the iceberg, offering to heal Zuko's scar in the Crystal Catacombs, and her full arc as the Painted Lady feeding, healing, and freeing a polluted village. Care also misfires ('Imprisoned') and is devalued as feminine 'women's work' when Toph calls Katara motherly ('The Runaway'), a myth the chapter rejects. Care scales politically too: the Gaang's defeat of Fire Nation imperialism is care repairing the world, while Azula's indifference to Ty Lee and Mai marks her villainy.

feminism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
feminism.title: Repairing Our Worlds
feminism.relation: Fice reads Katara through Joan Tronto's care ethics, tracking the phases in episodes: 'caring about' the refugees on 'The Serpent's Pass' and Zuko's scar in the Crystal Catacombs, 'taking care of' in freeing Aang from the iceberg, and 'care-giving' in 'The Painted Lady,' where she feeds, heals, and cleans up a polluted factory town. Care misfires are part of the theory, as when she pushes Haru to earthbend in 'Imprisoned' and gets him arrested, and Toph's 'motherly' jab lets the chapter reject the myth that care is essentially feminine, citing bell hooks. The larger claim is political: the Gaang's war against Fire Nation imperialism is care at world scale, repairing the world so its people can live well.

feminism.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
feminism.title: With or Without Starbuck
feminism.relation: Kirkland argues BSG imagines gender-free institutions (unisex heads and quarters, Starbuck never having to justify fighting) while installing a default masculinity under Adama, so that feminine-coded women die: Ellen the femme fatale is poisoned, pilots Kat and Kendra earn redemption only through death, and Cain's female command is written as militarist nightmare aligned with Gina's sexual abuse. Starbuck confounds the sexualizing male gaze and reverses rescue narratives, and 'The Farm' plus her captivity with Leoben on New Caprica literalize feminist critiques of patriarchal medicine and compulsory heterosexuality. Yet she is masculinized, pathologized via her abusive mother, brought to submit to Leoben as spiritual guide, and killed in 'Maelstrom' - containing the transgressive heroine within the show's patriarchy.

feminism.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
feminism.title: Human, Machine, or Something In-between
feminism.relation: Rolufs maps Genesis' Eve onto Boomer (who shoots Adama without understanding her act, as Eve could not know betrayal before eating the fruit) and onto Caprica Six (whose fall required Baltar's Adam-like blame-shifting), and the Zohar's Lilith - seductress, child-killer, seeker of equality - onto Six's red dresses and neck-snapping and Sharon's sexual dominance of Helo. Both Cylon women are compromised figures who love the humans they betrayed, and their ambiguity between human and machine mirrors the ambiguity between woman and demon in the myths. Through them the chapter argues pop culture redeems Eve and Lilith from misogynistic readings: Six's killing of the baby becomes possibly merciful, and the first women get the chance at redemption the myths denied them.

feminism.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
feminism.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Almassi grades the Dude as a halfway feminist ally: he divests from the Big Lebowski's patriarchal achiever-masculinity ('that and a pair of testicles'), respects Maude's conception project without paternalism (O'Neill's Kantian line between love and respect), and defends pacifist Smokey — yet his pacifism has stalled into passivity that King's active nonviolence would reject, he leaves Bunny's objectification unchallenged while 'Mr. Treehorn treats objects like women', and he only belatedly gives Maude the credibility Fricker's testimonial justice demands ('why don't you fucking listen occasionally?'). Using bell hooks's feminist masculinity and Larry May's progressive male standpoint, the chapter leaves the Dude five pins up with a spare still to pick up.

feminism.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
feminism.title: 21 Dismantling the Master’s House with the Master’s Tools
feminism.relation: Thanayi Jackson reads Killmonger through Audre Lorde's 'the master's tools will never dismantle the master's house,' asking whether a CIA-trained operative wielding the colonizer's own weapons can end colonialism. Comparing Killmonger to Wallace from The Wire - both orphans of Africa reared by America's ghettos - she concedes the appeal of his Oakland-forged mastery ('I know how colonizers think') but argues through bell hooks's gloss of Lorde that one cannot destroy imperialist white-supremacist capitalist patriarchy by creating one's own version of it: Killmonger's plan to kill oppressors 'and their children' makes him a new master, not a liberator. T'Challa's Oakland outreach center answers the challenge only partially, leaving the chapter asking whether the master's house was dismantled or merely refurbished.

feminism.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
feminism.title: 16. Female Integrity in Times of Change
feminism.relation: Melanie Abbott tests Bernard Williams's account of integrity - publicly and consistently standing up for the beliefs that make you you - merged with Kant's claim that only a good will is good without limitation, against five Crawley women across three generations. Sybil elopes with the socialist chauffeur Branson and never wavers in her egalitarian convictions, Edith's secrecy about her baby fails Williams's openness condition, Mary grows from custom-bound heiress into an estate manager who stands up to Robert over selling land, Cora chafes at the voice she surrendered as an American heiress, and even Violet eventually bends. The chapter's guiding question is how much truth and openness integrity requires, and it credits 'the Sybil effect' with spreading proper integrity through the whole family.

feminism.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
feminism.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Olson's first D&D Encounters session handed her a sexualized female miniature in a chainmail bikini and high-heeled boots, and the chapter audits the game as a feminist would: research on the 'token girl' and male-default storytelling, women like Dowsett pushed to play male characters to be taken seriously, and harassment ranging from 'date at least one of the party or bring food' to condescension toward women in the industry. Against this she argues the rules themselves are egalitarian — identical power pools for male and female characters, embodying Plato's Republic claim that women 'are by nature the same with respect to guarding the city', and even the evil deities are stereotyped symmetrically (scheming Lolth and Tiamat versus war-god patrons of power) — while the collaborative party structure (clerics healing strikers, shared goals) has exactly the care-ethical, anti-individualist flavor Friedman and Bolte attribute to women's moral perspectives. Sexism is thus a consequence of unreflective practices, marketing that ignores women, and industry culture rather than the game; all-female systems like Portal Worlds are a real response but, she worries, separatism risks deepening the divide.

feminism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
feminism.title: Conclusion Whatever I Goddamn Like
feminism.relation: S. W. Sondheimer argues that Avasarala's election loss to Nancy Gao is explained not by competence but by millennia of gender expectations. She excavates the lineage: Aristotle's form/matter hierarchy ('matter yearns for form as the female for the male', women as incomplete 'deformed males' with 'fewer teeth') used to bar women from politics, Hume's portrait of women as near-livestock incapable of the sublime, and Romantic-era bodily confinement — mapping each onto Avasarala's staff recasting her as a 'nurturing, caring family matriarch', her forced public apology for the failed Inaros boarding raid that a male commander like Errinwright would never have had to make, and Arjun seizing control of the narrative of their son Charanpal's death. Closing the loop with the 2016 US election (Clinton versus Trump), the chapter argues that even in 2350 voters punish the 'nasty woman' and reward the comfortable mold Gao fits, and demands we 'dig this garbage philosophy out of our shared consciousness and set it on fire.'

feminism.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
feminism.title: Lois: Portrait of a Mother (Or, Nevermind Death, Motherhood is a Bitch)
feminism.relation: Empey frames mothering (following Sara Ruddick's 'Maternal Thinking') as a disciplined response to a child's demands of preservation, growth, and social acceptability — even for a matricidal psychopath like Stewie. Lois cultivates the virtues of prudence (safeguarding the Rainy Day Fund against Peter's volcano insurance), tolerance, and peacefulness (enduring Stewie's lamp blows and Peter's laziness; her two Christmas and 'Lethal Weapons' violent eruptions are cured by appeals to her motherhood). The chapter then turns political: drawing on Okin, Williams, and Hays, it shows mothers' vulnerability by marriage, the incompatibility of the 'ideal worker' and 'intensive mother' models, and Peter's devaluing of Lois's theater directing. Peter's basement bar, where Lois sings nightly while minding the kids, models the institutional coordination (family plus economy) mothers need — until Peter's jealousy wrecks it.

feminism.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
feminism.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Sansa's journey from tourney-romance believer to 'they are no true knights' anchors a feminist argument that chivalry is unjust as a code, not merely corrupted by bad knights like Ser Gregor and Ser Meryn Trant, who beats Sansa at Joffrey's command. The pedestal, as Gloria Steinem says, is a prison: chivalry makes knights eternal guardians and ladies permanent childlike wards, a move the chapter explains through Spivak's account of saviors who turn the people they help into dependents and through Beauvoir's point that the custom of ladyhood manufactures the very 'fact' of female fragility it claims to protect. Arya's needlework, Brienne's unbeaten sword, Loras crowning Sansa while loving Renly, and Varys's riddle on power show the knight/lady roles are neither natural nor exhaustive, so 'there are no true knights' because chivalry itself blocks human flourishing.

feminism.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
feminism.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Reading Salander as genderqueer rather than simply a woman, the chapter argues her feminism lies in swift retaliation against those who abuse women and in economic and sexual independence from men, while her refusal of every identity label ('I don't know what I am') aligns her with queer theory's anti-identity politics. Judith Butler's performativity grounds the reading: Salander's body modifications and wardrobe 'undo' conventional gendering, and her drag-like aliases—the big-busted heiress Monica Sholes and the quiet Irene Nesser—succeed at fraud and flight only through absolute adherence to heteronormative femininity, proving gender is continuously constructed. Foucault's History of Sexuality frames her pathologization, institutionalization, and regulated sexuality as the medicalization of the sexually peculiar, a disciplinary script she reverses by hacking, surveilling, and exposing the authorities who pathologized her, tattooing i am a sadistic pig, a pervert and a rapist onto Bjurman.

feminism.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
feminism.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Applying Laura Mulvey's visual pleasure to the printed page, the chapter argues that Larsson's protest against woman-hating is compromised by styling Salander—four-eleven, ninety pounds, 'childlike breasts'—as a sexual spectacle whose rapes (Bjurman's coerced oral sex, the anal rape, the trial's play-by-play of implements) are the trilogy's most explicit scenes while consensual sex stays off-screen, making the books 'torture porn' for the voyeuristic reader. The films shift the gaze further: the revenge on Bjurman runs longer than the rapes, Salander actively watches Martin Vanger burn, and her bisexuality with Mimmi Wu is reduced to one silent morning, changes that make the violence against men more acceptable than against women. The chapter ends ambivalent: Laurie Penny and Gail Dines charge that 'Misogynist violence is appalling; now here's some more,' yet the distributor's RAINN partnership and a rape survivor's testimony that Salander was the first active, aggressive survivor she had ever seen show the books also work as Larsson intended.

feminism.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
feminism.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Against Blomkvist's 'I don't believe in collective guilt,' the chapter argues the Section is not a few bad apples: with Rousseau, institutions outgrow the people's will and preserve themselves (the guardianship agency cannot welcome its own obsolescence; the Fälldin directive lets Säpo stand inside and outside the law at once), and with Arendt, institutions protect only those they already recognize, so the excluded Salander cannot be heard by Teleborian, Prosecutor Ekström, or the court that doubts Giannini. Through bell hooks's definition of patriarchy it shows the police, psychiatry, and Säpo prize rationality, stability, and power in a masculine code under which Salander's responsiveness to her mother's abuse and her retaliation read as insanity—her very self-sufficiency (pepper spray, Taser, forward planning) proving she needs no 'guardianship.' Rancière's policing-versus-politics distinction supplies the conclusion: perpetual political contestation of who institutions exclude, not Prime Minister-initiated cleanup, is the only answer to a hidden Section in every institution.

feminism.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
feminism.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Donovan and Richardson read the Maltusian split, with the male Guardians banning emotion through the Book of Oa on Oa and the female Zamarons leaving to found the violet light of love on Zamaron, as the Western association of men with reason and women with emotion. They deploy Gilligan's different-voice reply to Kohlberg, the Pythagorean table of opposites via Genevieve Lloyd, Hegel's exclusion of women from the public sphere, and Jaggar's liberal-feminist critique of 'ahistorical' reason, whose comic-book analogue is the third law banning relationships between Lanterns. The chapter ends by arguing the standoff is a false dichotomy the comics themselves begin to dissolve: Kyle's 'Lanterns with heart' speech to the Guardians, the repeal of the third law, and the Indigo Tribe's plan to recombine the seven corps into the white light of creation.

feminism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
feminism.title: Radical vs. Liberal Feminism
feminism.relation: The section maps the feminist critical divide over the series: Schoefer, Heilman, and Gallardo-C. and Smith charge the books with replicating demeaning gender stereotypes, noting no girl is heroic like Harry and no woman wise like Dumbledore, while Kern, Gladstein, and Zettel answer with context, pairing Lavender and Parvati's silliness with Dean and Seamus, Trelawney with fake Lockhart, and Madam Pince with Filch, and pointing to Umbridge and Bellatrix as female villains who command as much fear as any Death Eater. The pervasive giggling girls debate serves as the section's lightning rod.

feminism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
feminism.title: More Wonderful and More Terrible than Death
feminism.relation: The section distinguishes liberal feminism, historically grounded in Mary Wollstonecraft, Harriet Taylor Mill, and John Stuart Mill's Enlightenment view that women are rational individuals entitled to equal rights, criticized here for measuring success on masculine terms so that McGonagall and Hermione's achievements count while Molly Weasley's motherhood gets short shrift. It then explains second-wave radical feminism and its 'sex/gender system' analysis of rigid masculine/feminine trait pairings, and reads Gallardo-C. and Smith's 'Cinderfella' interpretation of the series, in which evil displays 'phallic power' even in Umbridge's hypermasculine control while Harry's kindness and selflessness embody feminine values, an association the section traces from St. Gertrude through Gandhi's 'life without love is death' to C.S. Lewis's analysis of the kinds of love.

feminism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
feminism.title: The Triumph of Love
feminism.relation: Reading the series' set pieces as the triumph of traditionally feminine values over masculine aggression, the section moves from Lily's sacrificial love burning Quirrell, through Harry sparing Pettigrew for Lupin's and Sirius's sake, to love expelling Voldemort during the Ministry possession, where 'it was your heart that saved you' and Dumbledore names a force 'more wonderful and more terrible than death.' Harry's kindness to Kreacher, Griphook, and Dobby pays off in the Horcrux hunt, his plea that Voldemort 'try for some remorse' redefines true manhood as incorporating the feminine, and the Forest sacrifice wins the war with a defensive Expelliarmus rather than a duel, showing love more important than aggression.

feminism.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
feminism.title: 5 Feminism and Indiana Jones A Field Guide
feminism.relation: Kate Schmidt applies feminist media tests (Bechdel, sexy lamp, Mako Mori, Pierce, Landau) to show the films usually fail — Willie is a screaming prop and human shield in Temple, the eyelid-writing student exists only to display Indy's sex appeal, and all four films fail the Bechdel Test — while Marion, Spalko, and above all Elsa in The Last Crusade are mixed cases with partial autonomy. Drawing on Iris Marion Young's account of women as Other and Carol Gilligan's care ethics, she argues Crusade is the series' most feminist film not for its women but for its men: Indy's open hurt after Elsa's betrayal and the father-son reconciliation embody care ethics against 'boys don't cry' toxic masculinity. She concludes that one can love flawed media without endorsing its sexism.

feminism.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
feminism.title: Iron Man The End
feminism.relation: The Housels read Iron Man through Butler's gender performativity and Arendt's 'right to have rights': the male-voiced Jarvis replacing the female AI Jocasta, Tony's womanizing, and the evolving corporeal styles of Black Widow, Bethany Cabe, Madame Masque, and Sunset Bain all enact society's gender script across the waves of feminism, with the black leather suit arriving only in 1970 amid Second Wave Feminism. Arendt's Eichmann reporting and the 'banality of evil' — coined the same year, 1963, that Lee, Lieber, Heck, and Kirby, all children of Jewish immigrants, launched Iron Man — supply the justice frame: Tony's transformation of conscience after Afghanistan and his vigilante justice against his own oppressors refuse silent conformity and insist, ignoring political boundaries, that all oppressed people have rights.

feminism.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Gutwald takes seven-year-old Charlotte Benjamin's viral letter ('all the girls did was sit at home, go to the beach, and shop... but the boys went on adventures, worked, saved people') to argue the LEGO Friends theme is Wollstonecraftian 'friendly sexism' — revering girls as pretty play-things in a house-bound Heartlake City rather than oppressing them outright. Following Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes a woman' and her point that men describe the world from their own perspective, plus Mill's Subjection of Women observation that argument alone cannot beat a 'mass of feeling', she explains how pinkified toy segregation feeds implicit bias, schemas, and stereotype threat in both girls and boys. Her fix is structural: make Friends bricks and mini-dolls compatible with the rest of the system ('Let the Friends go to Space!') and return to the gender-neutral 1981 'What it is is beautiful' ad.

feminism.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Grant and Wainman assess the fan-designed Research Institute set (#21110, with its paleontologist, astronomer, and chemist) — created by geoscientist Ellen Kooijman and the first LEGO set with women scientists — as a genuine step for women in STEM that still markets girls' play as passive role play with lipstick-wearing figures. Drawing on gender socialization research (parents describing babies differently from birth, the draw-a-scientist test, Emily Martin's analysis of gendered egg-and-sperm descriptions in biology texts), they argue that LEGO's gendered coding of minifigures and themes — masculine-coded City police and astronauts, salon-and-bakery Friends — is one brick in the wall steering girls away from science and engineering. They call for sets that embed real science and engineering skill rather than narratives, and for boys to extend their range to the Heartlake Hair Salon too.

feminism.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Pérez and Jackson use Crenshaw's intersectionality to demarginalize Aunty Entity: a Black woman (Tina Turner) in an all-white franchise, she occupies the race-gender intersection invisible both to white feminism and to Black male-centered politics, and her 'Aunty' title and high cage evoke Black women's commodified emotional labor and Angelou's caged bird. Reading her through Moreton-Robinson's white possessive doctrine, hooks's 'white supremacist capitalist patriarchy,' and the Combahee River Collective — and then through hip-hop's Thunderdome trope from 2Pac's 'California Love' to Kendrick Lamar — they argue that Max's white male gaze retroactively makes her a villain, when she is in fact the franchise's most just hero.

feminism.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
feminism.title: Don’t Go Mad
feminism.relation: Barkman applies a qualified Aristotelian standard of justice, that women possessing rational souls must be treated as equals, to Peggy, Betty, and Joan as second-wave feminism dawns. Peggy is the 'mad woman' in the best sense: she demands a desk, equal pay ('You have everything and so much of it'), and Don's apology while never resorting to blackmail like Pete, whereas Betty is repressed at home by a husband who shows her off ('I want to show you off, Betts') and Joan suppresses herself, measuring worth by appearance and enduring Greg's violation until the vase incident. The sexual objectification Peggy faces from her first day (Ken's elevator leers, Joan's paper-bag advice, the panty-hunt in 'Nixon vs. Kennedy') is the chapter's core injustice, and the warning is that women who cannot stand up to it may simply go mad.

feminism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
feminism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Applies Luce Irigaray's account of patriarchal society to Charming's women: Gemma and Tara are strong and resourceful, but their identity, power, and even survival run through men, as Clay's 'you are NOT a member of this club — you're just an old lady!' and Jax's 'She's just an old lady, not a member' make brutally literal. Irigaray's claim that patriarchal orders circulate women as commodities exchanged among men fits the 'sweet butt' Cherry being offered to Clay in 'Patch Over' and Gemma's 'Only men need to feel loved. Women need to feel wanted.' Tara's sacrificed surgical career and Jax's refusal to live off his wife ('I'm not gonna live off my wife. I can't.') illustrate woman as a being who exists for another, and the chapter ends asking what Gemma could say if she had a genuinely feminine voice of her own.

feminism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
feminism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Frames the show's tension between the masculine public sphere (the chapel table, guns, club politics) and the feminine domestic sphere that actually sustains life, using Aristotle's oikos/polis division and Arendt's The Human Condition on the public/private realms. Gemma, dismissed as 'just an old lady,' proves the private sphere's power: she brought the club to Charming, orchestrates Jax's rise to the presidency, and converts her rape by Weston's LOAN goons into family solidarity that puts Jax's VP patch back on. Gilligan's and Baier's ethics of care then reads Lyla's abortion as a caring choice about family size, Tara's 'my job as your old lady is to be strong when and where you can't be' as care turned to strength, and Gemma's care curdling into retributive justice against Clay.

feminism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Argues Star Trek functions like the Greek myths Nussbaum describes: modern tales of transformation (Gary Mitchell in "Where No Man Has Gone Before", Charlie X, Roger Korby) that let audiences judge what makes someone human. It rejects the Cartesian reading (Richard Hanley's Is Data Human?) in which Data's humanity is just a matter of being a rational mind, and develops instead a feminist, developmental account of personhood drawn from Annette Baier: persons are "second persons" who learn the arts of personhood from caretakers. Data, Seven of Nine, and Voyager's Doctor, all lacking real childhoods and families, must learn play, touch, love, and interdependence from their crews, with Janeway modeling family for Seven and Kes socializing the Doctor. Picard's farewell to Shinzon in Nemesis and to Data's B-4 caps the claim that humanity is an achievement of self-improvement in relationship, not a fixed essence.

feminism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Pits Donna Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto against Star Trek's horror of the Borg, reading Locutus/Picard, Hugh, and Seven of Nine as tests of the Federation values of autonomy, individuality, and authenticity against the rival Borg values of heteronomy, collectivity, and simulation. Picard's "My culture is based on freedom and self-determination" exchange with the Borg, Hugh's discovery of his name and first-person "I", and Seven's tug-of-war with the Borg Queen in "Dark Frontier" dramatize what assimilation threatens. The chapter then defends a Haraway-inspired feminist reboot: women and minorities were long denied autonomy, individuality, and authenticity by prejudice and stereotype (Seven still must look "warp-core hot" in her catsuit), the human/machine and man/woman binaries were always false, and since we already live as cyborgs of apps, implants, and networks, resistance was negligible - the real Borg problem is their violent means, not their values.

feminism.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Argues that Leia and Padme really are strong feminist characters, using Simone de Beauvoir's The Second Sex to defuse the two stock objections: Padme's motherhood is 'freely chosen' rather than an oppressive role, and Leia chained in Jabba's palace keeps command of her sexuality, turning the damsel-in-distress plot around by strangling Jabba with her own chain and later rescuing Han herself. The chapter's real complaint is structural: with only six speaking women in the original trilogy, almost all of them royalty, Leia and Padme are forced to represent all women (the 'affluent few' problem), while Shmi, Aunt Beru, Mon Mothma, and the handmaidens Sabe, Corde, and Dorme never get the screen time to show their strength.

feminism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
feminism.title: A New Hope Inclusive Representation in the Galaxy
feminism.relation: Lakka uses Beauvoir's The Second Sex (the Mother/Mistress dichotomy, woman tied to nature and denied transcendence) and Butler on the mother-daughter separation to argue that Revenge of the Sith reduces Padme from the active senator and warrior of the first two prequels to a pregnant figure confined to her apartment, whose death gets read as martyrdom or even 'mom-shaming.' She reads Anakin's jealousy, interrogations ('Obi-Wan's been here, has he not?'), and Force-choke on Mustafar — explicitly paralleled with Othello and Desdemona — as an abusive relationship, suggesting Padme's death may be a feminicide. The deleted Petition of the 2000 scenes, and successors like Rey, Ahsoka, Rose Tico, and Jyn Erso, point toward the inclusive representation the galaxy still needs.

feminism.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
feminism.title: Is Taylor Swift a Philosopher?
feminism.relation: Catherine Robb tests whether Swift counts as a philosopher, rejecting both the 'words of wisdom / life hacks' definition (which would make every advice-giver a philosopher) and the narrow academic model of philosophy as direct, abstract, discursive prose. The decisive case is Swift's treatment of sexist double standards across 'The Man,' 'mad woman,' 'Lavender Haze,' 'But Daddy I Love Him,' and her Billboard Woman of the Decade speech, where she states the stereotypes women face and systematically reflects on subverting them through first-person and fictional narratives. Drawing on Martha Nussbaum's claim that poetry and storytelling are vehicles of ethical inquiry, the chapter concludes Swift is an 'accidental philosopher.'

feminism.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
feminism.title: So Mother for That: Taylor Swift and Childless Mothering
feminism.relation: Lucy Britt and Brian Britt trace the fan practice of calling childless Swift 'mother' back to the Black and queer ballroom house mothers of Paris Is Burning (Carmen Xtravaganza, Willi Ninja), whose original meaning - relational care and leadership in found families - was mostly lost when Swifties appropriated the term. Using Simone de Beauvoir on femininity, Judith Butler's culturally constructed body, and Audre Lorde on Black mothering as resistance, they argue Swift functions as a postmodern, queered mother whose revisiting of her 'eras' teaches fans to mother their own past selves. Yet her individualism ('You're on your own, kid') blocks the relational politics of care that Joan Tronto's caring democracy and Adriana Cavarero's maternal inclination demand.

feminism.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
feminism.title: Taylor Swift's Philosophy of Reputation
feminism.relation: Catherine Robb and Roos Slegers reconstruct a philosophy of reputation from the reputation album: with Sperber, Baumard, and Origgi, reputation is a shared group consensus ('they say I did something bad') that is fake, warped, and outside one's control, yet Adam Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments explains why it still wounds - we deeply want not only to be loved but to be lovely, seen for who we really are (the invisible dance through the streets in 'Delicate'). The chapter's original contribution is Swift's 'tilted stage,' performed literally on the reputation tour: gendered double standards ('The Man,' 'mad woman') mean a woman's reputation is more fake, more imposed, and more punishing than a man's.

feminism.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Young uses bell hooks's patriarchal masculinity (with Kate Manne on misogyny as enforcement) to read the show: Jamie is patriarchal terror's product, Rupert's promiscuity and Rebecca's subjection are two sides of male control, and Roy Kent's 'hard man' persona inherits the hardness Nietzsche praised and philosophy's traditional suspicion of emotion. Against this, hooks's definition of love as the will to nurture spiritual growth explains Ted's coaching, the training-room exorcism's shared vulnerability, Sam's openness, and Nate's status-hunger as the struggle to invert the gender pyramid, ending with Nate refusing Rupert's poisoned patriarchal gifts.

feminism.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
feminism.title: NOTES
feminism.relation: Craton and Jonell read Sookie as an emblem of contemporary feminist ambivalence: her 'I am woman, hear me roar' independence coexists with sexual caution, and the show stages feminism's sex wars — Lafayette's sex work and webcam pornography versus Maryann, whose 'pro-sex' liberation collapses into self-annihilating worship of Dionysus and whose death suggests unregulated sexuality is dangerous. Tara's plotline shows how race and class layer onto gender (her 'baby-daddy' scene, Maryann as failed white savior), exposing the limits of a united feminist front, while the 'kept woman' quarrel with Bill and Sookie's barmaid-versus-telepathic-detective career choice leave more questions about female empowerment than answers.

feminism.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
feminism.title: “A Pamphlet’s Not Going to Cover It”
feminism.relation: Kasey Butcher and Megan Peters argue Veronica embodies a third-wave, sex-positive feminism: as jury foreman in 'One Angry Veronica' she refuses the 'Barbie' role the captain of industry assigns her; her over-the-top masquerades (flirting with store clerk Duane Anders, the temptation scenario at Patrick Nevin's door, mimicking Logan's manspreading) expose gender as a performance; and her defense of Carmen Ruiz against Tad's blackmail shows her grasp of how race, class, and gender intersect, per Kimberlé Crenshaw. Against the show's caricature of Lilith House as humorless 'feminist killjoys' picketing the Hearst rapes, they contend Veronica models a feminism that keeps femininity, sexuality, and play — refusing slut shaming while fighting for rape victims, an incest survivor, and blackmailed girls.

feminism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
feminism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Ashley Barkman argues feminism is unrealistic in a zombie apocalypse: citing Sax and Bandura on innate sex differences, she claims survival leadership demands masculine aggression and physical force, which is why Rick knocks Merle down and shoves off Daryl while no woman claims command in camp, farm, or Woodbury. She reads Jacqui's laundry protest as justified only against shirkers like Ed and Shane, not against Donna's complaint, since domestic work sustains morale, and concedes exceptional women—Andrea as the group's best shot, Michonne enduring the Governor's rape and enslavement and taking revenge. The conclusion is that roles, including the dangerous ones, should track natural difference rather than enforced equality.

feminism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
feminism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Pye and O'Sullivan use Judith Butler's performativity to read walkers as genderless proof that gender is done, not born: the little-girl walker 'troubles' gender like drag, while survivors regressively re-perform patriarchy—Lori's 'I'm a girl, you talk to him', Carol at the washboard, the men confiscating Andrea's gun while Daryl keeps his crossbow. They invoke Butler's primitive clan and incest taboo to explain how Shane's camp, Lori and Carl's haircuts, and Ed's threats reproduce protector/protected roles, yet point to counterexamples—Andrea and Amy fishing, Felipe the nurse, Carl asking to be taught—that show roles can be learned differently. Via Rorty's remark that assumptions become visible when their contradictories sound plausible, they argue clinging to gender baggage endangers everyone against an enemy stripped of ego and social contract that does not discriminate.

feminism.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
feminism.title: P A R T F O U R
feminism.relation: Four Part Four essays beyond ethics. Aaron Meskin asks whether Watchmen is literature at all, testing definitions from Beardsley, Eagleton, Lamarque/Olsen and Hirsch in the Socratic 'what is X?' way, and concludes the question is indeterminate because comics are a hybrid art form — though the book's literary allusions (Shelley's 'Ozymandias,' Blake's 'Tyger,' Burroughs) deserve literary appreciation regardless. Sarah Donovan and Nick Richardson read the two Silk Spectres through three feminisms: Sally and Laurie as liberal feminists (Wollstonecraft, Mill) who fight crime, their hypersexual costumes as Irigaray-style subversive mimicry of gender stereotypes that risks reinforcing them (the Silhouette's expulsion exposing the heterosexual norm), the Comedian's attempted rape exposing 'she asked for it' attitudes, and Laurie as Beauvoir's woman in bad faith, living out her mother's fantasies until she finally names and dresses herself. Robert Arp uses Hooded Justice and Captain Metropolis's closeted relationship to dismantle 'homosexuality is unnatural' arguments — the ideal-function view would condemn the infertile too, and Hume's is-ought point undermines the procreation argument — before defending gay marriage against slippery-slope and parenting objections. Taneli Kukkonen maps Kierkegaard's stages onto the Comedian's mocking irony (hiding even his paternity of Laurie and his Kennedy confession as jokes) and Rorschach's deeper humor of the ethical stage, a knight of resignation whose 'never compromise, not even in the face of Armageddon' expects nothing back from the world.

feminism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
feminism.title: They Took My Choice, So I Took Yours
feminism.relation: Tongue argues Yennefer's 'they took my choice' grievance is best understood through reproductive justice: her sterilization by the enchanter, strapped down and told the price only at the last moment, mirrors real coerced sterilizations of disabled, Roma, and Indigenous women, so her 'choice' was coerced by ableist and anti-elven oppression. She contrasts Geralt, whose witcher infertility is unstigmatized and whose adoptive fatherhood of Ciri bucks gendered caregiver stereotypes ('biology is not destiny, adoption is'), with Yennefer's portrayal, which slides into the patriarchal 'infertile monster' trope shared by Daenerys Tragaryen and Wanda Maximoff. The chapter concludes the show handles infertility and nonbiological family admirably but still reinforces maternal-sacrifice and cure-the-disability stereotypes.

feminism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
feminism.title: Ciri's Agency and Autonomy
feminism.relation: Vega and Barta read Ciri's Elder Blood power, which activates only through controlled female emotion, through Hélène Cixous's 'Laugh of the Medusa' and écriture féminine: her awakening scream at dying Calanthe's side and her cry of 'NO!' are forbidden female self-expression breaking patriarchal control. Renfri, silenced by Stregobor's narrative into villain and victim, and the bruxa Vereena, killed when her power exceeds her control, are the cautionary Medusas against which Ciri's mastery and the Lodge of Sorceresses' vote of 'sentimentality, gentleness, trust, and hope' to release her stand out. Calanthe's 'I bow to no law made by men who never bore a child' is pure écriture féminine undercut by her own complicity in auctioning Pavetta, and Ciri's final victory over Emhyr comes not through the sword but through tears, emotional expression defeating patriarchy's rationalizations.

feminism.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Cano Abadia imagines Wonder Woman and Themyscira's Amazons joining Monique Wittig's Guerrieres in a three-front war on patriarchy: the literal war Diana declares, a social revolution of lesbian, BDSM, and polyamorous relations lived outside the heterosexual contract, and a linguistic revolution that destroys the sex binary - 'elles' as the universal subject, no he and she. With Virginia Woolf's Society of Outsiders supplying experimental 'new ways of doing things' and Luce Irigaray's revaluation of feminine symbolism explaining the Amazons' feminaries and Hera-centered genealogy, Diana becomes the bridge between two generations of fighters whose post-patriarchal world 'is yet to come.'

feminism.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
feminism.title: Notes
feminism.relation: Mahon debunks three myths about the original magic lasso: it is not a magic lie detector (Diana already runs a real polygraph on the spy Elva Dove), it is not an enslavement device (slavery is domination, and even the chained Amazons never submitted), and its truth-compulsion is no coincidence. Reading Marston's four-emotion psychology, he shows the lasso and the bracelets of submission are metaphors for love's asymmetric inducement/submission bond - Aphrodite captivates, the Amazons submit - and since lying is precisely an attempt to impose one's will and dominate the hearer (Rotenstreich), a perfectly lassoed person lacks all dominance emotion and so can only submit, and therefore cannot lie. The lasso's later depowering into a mere 'lasso of truth' becomes evidence of the comic industry's discomfort with feminine power.

feminism.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
feminism.title: She Got Game
feminism.relation: The Wallaces argue that both the detractors (Stacey Pressman's claim that women's basketball 'sucks') and the admirers (John Wooden's 'purest basketball' praise) judge the women's game by patriarchal standards drawn from the men's game. Using Sandra Bartky's feminist extension of Foucault, they show how the female body was disciplined under male surveillance - early rule changes split the court and banned stealing to protect 'femininity', while players deflected the 'Amazon' charge with beauty pageants, revealing uniforms, and the Playboy offer to Lisa Harrison. The modern WNBA of Lisa Leslie and Michelle Snow, who can dunk but choose team play, points to a new game that escapes the feminine/masculine dichotomy instead of measuring women against men.

feminism.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
feminism.title: Eighth Hole Playing Through Racism and Sexism in Golf
feminism.relation: Gray examines whether golf is a model of equality or a preserve of 'wealthy white men,' using George Carlin's polemic and the Tiger Woods 'Chosen One' narrative as foils. He documents 'social closure' and the 'Grass Ceiling' through Augusta National's history, the Shoal Creek and Martha Burk/NCWO controversies, and the PGA's former Caucasian-only clause, then turns to sexism via McGinnis, McQuillan, and Chapple's interviews and Connell's 'hegemonic masculinity,' showing how gendered 'red/women's tees' entrench a false dualism of male and female play. Citing McDonagh and Pappano's Playing with the Boys, he argues coercive sex-segregation rests on false assumptions and calls for transparency about club membership.

feminism.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
feminism.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Jonsson argues that modern sport enforces masculine norms and that the East German 'wonder girls' (Koch, Ender, Krabbe), along with Stella Walsh, Jarmila Kratochvilova and Caster Semenya, were 'gender radical' Amazons who challenged the link between masculinity and maleness by winning with 'masculine' bodies. Drawing on Judith Butler's claim that gender ideals are not static and women's sport can rearticulate them, he treats the doping-built Eastern Bloc athletes as progressive because they contradicted how female athletes are 'supposed' to look. He critiques Jane English's appeal to 'permanent biological differences' and laments that after 1989 commercialized sport (symbolized by Flo Jo's marketed femininity) hardened conservative gender norms again.

feminism.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
feminism.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Weaving argues from a liberal-feminist standpoint that the FIVB's mandatory bikini-bottom rule for women's Olympic beach volleyball sexualizes and objectifies the athletes, contradicting Coubertin's ideals of universal humanity. Using Paul Davis's distinction between acceptable sexuality and objectionable sexualization (deliberate focus on body parts, freezing postures, punning captions like 'Buns of Gold'), and citing Nussbaum, Baker and Bartky on when treating someone as a sexual object becomes wrong, she shows the rule detaches athletes' bodies from their athletic agency. She traces harms including physical risk, the APA-documented effects of sexualization, a 'trickle-down' to school volleyball short-shorts, and exclusion of Islamic women.

feminism.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
feminism.title: The Ridiculous Meets the Radical in the Battle of the Sexes
feminism.relation: Comparing Jackie Robinson's somber dignity with the comic spectacle of Billie Jean King's 1973 Battle of the Sexes against Bobby Riggs, the chapter asks why sexism could be joked about as theater while racism demanded gravity, arguing race operates in a competitive male-vs-male public sphere whereas sexism is intimate and domestic. It reads King's victory through Maria Lugones's feminist notions of 'playful world-traveling' and 'loving perception': where Margaret Court stayed rigid and lost, King playfully entered Riggs's circus, matched his showmanship, and ultimately made the match about tennis. King's later affection for Riggs illustrates loving perception, recasting the event as a shared act of social transformation rather than a simple good-versus-evil win.

feminism.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
feminism.title: Laugh of the Revolutionary Diane di Prima, French Feminist Philosophy, and the Contemporary Cult of the Beat H
feminism.relation: Quinn reads Diane di Prima's serial poem 'Loba' and 'Memoirs of a Beatnik' through Hélène Cixous's 'The Laugh of the Medusa' and its call to 'écriture féminine'—women writing the body. She argues di Prima's she-wolf/Medusa figure, sex-positive candor, and refusal of narrative closure enact Cixous's boundless feminine writing, while Cixous's anti-Freudian, anti-Lacanian mockery of 'penis envy' and the 'big dick' illuminates di Prima's transgressive motherhood and bisexuality. Against the male Beats' dismissal of women writers (and Beauvoir's foremother status), the essay centralizes di Prima as a serious feminist philosopher-poet rather than a nostalgic icon.

feminism.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
feminism.title: 3. Laura Palmer—Madonna and Whore
feminism.relation: Jones argues that Laura Palmer is trapped in Freud's Madonna-whore complex—the male inability to see a woman as both virtuous and sexual—with BOB voicing the cultural signals that brand her 'dirty and sleazy' for her sexuality. He reads the Fireman/Giant, who births Laura as a golden antidote to BOB, as a patriarchal 'nice guy' whose idealizing Madonna role is as much a trap as the whore role BOB imposes. The chapter uses Laura's dual life to expose how patriarchy forces women to choose between two reductive poles, both maintained by male power.

feminism.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
feminism.title: 10. The Miss Twin Peaks Award Goes To . .
feminism.relation: Rard (as her 'doppelganger') distinguishes 'power-over' (getting others, mostly men, to do your bidding through beauty and manipulation) from the more stable 'power-to' (skills, resources, ability to act for oneself). She traces Josie Packard, who lives by manipulating Harry and Pete and is destroyed when surrounded by people immune to her charms, against Audrey Horne, who begins with the Norwegian stunt and the perfume-counter blackmail but transitions to running her father's business—acquiring real power—while Lana Milford's near-total charm and Nadine's adrenaline strength mark the extremes.

feminism.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
feminism.title: 11. The Mother of All Bombs
feminism.relation: Kolb argues Laura Palmer embodies the 'Angel in the House' ideal (Gilbert and Gubar) whose perfection is a beautiful dead girl, and reads The Return's linkage of the Trinity bomb to BOB/Judy through Arendt's On Violence—violence begets a more violent, hostile world that especially victimizes women. Using Gilligan's In a Different Voice, she shows how women's voices (Naido/Diane, the Log Lady, Laura's diary) are silenced by toxic masculinity (Mr. C, Richard, Chad), while the 'good men' embody an ethic of care; the manufactured post-war social order names its bombs after mothers and treats women as perfect-yet-fallen others.

feminism.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
feminism.title: Sherlock Holmes as Epistemologist
feminism.relation: Baggett reconstructs Holmes's detective practice as an expansive epistemology built on observation, background knowledge, and abductive inference-to-the-best-explanation, using cases like 'The Blue Carbuncle' hat and the 'eliminate the impossible' maxim. He argues Holmes's boldness in drawing inferences is intellectual courage rather than hubris, invoking William James on the risk of losing truth by excessive caution. He then tests Holmes against feminist epistemologists who fault his cult of cold objectivity and mistrust of women (the Mary Morstan and Irene Adler episodes), concluding Holmes is partly vindicated by his imagination, intuition, and passion but still too fragmented between reason and emotion.

feminism.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
feminism.title: 8 Images of Women in the Music and Life of Neil Young
feminism.relation: McKenna uses Sarah Lucia Hoagland's feminist analysis of "heterosexualism" to argue that Young's songs ("Cinnamon Girl," "A Man Needs a Maid," "Unknown Legend," and the femicide of "Down by the River") portray women as objects to be desired, possessed, used and harmed, positioning them as helpmates (like Rousseau's Sophie, against which Wollstonecraft argued). She extends this to Young's own "backgrounding" of the women in his life (Pegi, Carrie Snodgress) in Waging Heavy Peace, comparing him to William James's reliance on his wife Alice.

feminism.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
feminism.title: 30_LaRocca_Chapter_029.html
feminism.relation: Linda Williams analyzes Michelle Citron's What You Take for Granted, a feminist film that inhabits the gray zone between documentary and fiction by having actors impersonate real women workers (a truck driver, a doctor, a welder) entering male-dominated trades. She argues the film exposes the price women pay to be admitted to a male world of work structured by an absent, idealized-and-vilified paternal authority, mirroring the absent-mother structure of Citron's earlier Daughter Rite. By blending polished pseudo-documentary interviews with an improvised cinema-verite fiction of Anna and Dianna's friendship, the film interrogates the process of representation itself and shows how documentary 'truth' about women's typical experience is itself a fictional shaping.

feminism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
feminism.title: 24. ReMENbering the Punk Movement
feminism.relation: Georgina Mills argues that remembering punk through its men only - the British Library display naming the Sex Pistols, the Clash, and the Buzzcocks but no women - is more than the Matilda effect: it retroactively filters the whole movement through patriarchal norms. Using Iris Marion Young's concept of marginalization, she contends that as punk gained mainstream status the women who embodied its rebellion (the Slits banned from hotels on the White Riot tour, X-Ray Spex, Siouxsie) were pushed back to the margins of a movement they helped forge. Erasing them distorts punk itself, since women's twofold rebellion - against the establishment and against feminine compliance - and punk's DIY inclusivity were integral to it, as the misreading of Poly Styrene's 'Oh Bondage, Up Yours!' as mere shock shows.

feminism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
feminism.title: 28. Riot Grrrl Punk as Feminist Creation
feminism.relation: Patrick Anderson presents Riot Grrrl (Bikini Kill and the Riot Grrrl Manifesto) as feminist aesthetic creation rather than merely feminist politics: bands attacked the sexism within punk itself with 'women to the front' tactics, women-only shows, and stopping sets to call out harassers. Explaining Mary Devereaux's three levels of the male gaze (production, narrative, spectator) and the muse/whore versus one-of-the-guys/girl-with-balls taxonomy, he shows how Kathleen Hanna performing with 'SLUT' scrawled across her midriff collapses the muse/whore dichotomy, while 'Rebel Girl's' woman-loving-woman solidarity replaces women-as-objects with women as subjects. Zines, Xerox machines, and indie labels extend the feminist-aesthetic tactics of Hilde Hein and Carolyn Korsmeyer (violating standards of taste, the body as artwork), though the chapter notes criticisms of Riot Grrrl's white, middle-class limits.

feminism.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
feminism.title: Female Subjectivity in Carrie
feminism.relation: Kellye Byal reads Carrie White through Beauvoir's The Second Sex, treating Carrie's first menstruation, her mother Margaret's ascetic 'Mystic' piety, and Miss Collins/Sue Snell's push toward makeup and the prom as two imposed versions of 'feminine destiny.' Carrie is caught between rejecting femininity (becoming an outcast/monster) and assuming it (surrendering her subjectivity to immanence and the male gaze), so her telekinesis becomes an externalized act of authentic, radically free agency against both scripts. Byal argues her tragic death indicts a failed community of women who never posit themselves as Subjects, illustrating Beauvoir's claim that female subjectivity needs a solidarity of others in which to thrive.

feminism.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
feminism.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Winkle reads Sense and Sensibility as steering a 'middle road' between cold rational calculation and sentimental self-indulgence, and casts Austen as proto-feminist. She uses Wollstonecraft's Vindication to explain why Austen's silly wives (Mrs. Bennet, Lucy Steele) are products of a deficient female education that trains women to please rather than reason. She then reads Elinor Dashwood's measured love for Edward, and Marianne's near-fatal collapse over Willoughby, through bell hooks's claim that 'falling in love' surrenders agency, arguing Elinor chooses love as an act of will while Marianne must learn sense before finding lasting love with Colonel Brandon.

feminism.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
feminism.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
feminism.relation: Dashwood examines women owning property in Austen, arguing the 'great ladies' (Lady Catherine, Mrs. Ferrars, Lady Denham) are drawn as despotic, avaricious, and negligent managers not because they are women but because a deficient female education left them unfit, echoing Wollstonecraft's Vindication that female failings are constructed by upbringing. She contrasts them with propertyless heroines who show the reason and moral principle to manage estates well. Emma is the pivotal case: as the one female proprietor at a novel's center, she risks becoming a tyrannical great lady but, guided by her superior education and Knightley's example at Donwell, develops the social conscience needed for ethical ownership.

feminism.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
feminism.title: MOTHERHOOD
feminism.relation: Clemence Due and Damien Riggs analyze how media images of celebrity mothers reproduce Sharon Hays's 'intensive mothering' ideology, reporting a study in which students judged Jodie Foster a 'good/normal' (if 'boring') mother for domestic self-sacrifice, Angelina Jolie a 'savior' but not fully 'good' because of her career, Nicole Richie a reformed 'bad-girl-come-good-mom,' and Britney Spears ('Toxic Mummy') a 'bad' mother. They argue readers uncritically absorb and extend these gendered norms – fathers escaping such scrutiny – and call, from a feminist standpoint, for mothers to be allowed to be 'good' in many ways while pursuing other interests.

feminism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
feminism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
feminism.relation: Merskin takes an ecofeminist view (Karen Warren's linkage of the domination of women and nature) of women who hunt, testing Marti Kheel's 'happy/holistic/holy' hunter typology against online interviews with female hunters and finding their motivations mirror men's. She surveys how hunting became a male-coded rite of separation from the mother—drawing on Freud's 'instinctive urge'—and how hunting media (Traditional Bowhunter) juxtapose women, animals, weapons, and sexual conquest as objects of male predation. Invoking Artemis/Diana and Mary Zeiss Stange's 'woman the hunter,' she argues women who hunt expose aggression as a human, not merely male, trait.

feminism.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
feminism.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE

feminism.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
feminism.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
feminism.relation: Brennan argues that fashion sits at the boundary of public and private and is central to the 'sexual citizen' and the politics of recognition for gay, lesbian, and bisexual people. Using Hanson on philosophy's gendered fear of fashion and Phelan/Weeks/Walker on visibility as a political strategy, she shows that queer identities (femme, boi, hanky codes) are communicative and require a community that reads them — offering a 'private hanky' argument echoing Wittgenstein's private-language point. She draws on her own experience (labrys earring, later bisexual invisibility) and on Butler-style gender performativity to argue visibility empowers recognition but marginalizes those, like femmes, who cannot be read.

feminism.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
feminism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
feminism.relation: Heidi Howkins Lockwood examines the 'asymmetry thesis'—that a climber's gratuitous risk is less acceptable than an astronaut's necessary risk—and argues its two standard defenses fail: the Rule of Rescue is neither necessary (free soloists need no rescue yet are condemned) nor sufficient (Hornbein and Unsoeld's risky Everest traverse was praised because it succeeded), and the argument from compassion collapses into circularity. She then shows the intuition is really driven by external background assumptions, especially gender inequality: the media vilified climber-mother Alison Hargreaves while lauding astronaut-mother Christa McAuliffe, because ambition-for-profit violates the 'traditionally female' role of service. She concedes a limited, defensible version tied to the assumption that seeking risk as a mere end (rather than an ineliminable means) is irresponsible.

feminism.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
feminism.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
feminism.relation: Kimberly Baltzer-Jaray and Tanya Rodriguez argue, against George Carlin's 'mobile art gallery' joke, that the only thing separating tattooing from fine art is its fleshy canvas. They show how formalist, expressionist and institutional theories historically excluded both women's craft and tattoos, then use feminist aesthetics (Korsmeyer, Iris Marion Young on the gaze) to reclaim the female tattooed body as an assertion of agency against objectification. They then apply Gadamer's hermeneutics – art as play, festival and symbol – to argue tattoos make a claim on the viewer, build a 'hermeneutic collective' community, and function as inexhaustible symbols prompting self-recognition.

feminism.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
feminism.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
feminism.relation: Thorsten Botz-Bornstein argues contemporary female tattoos have lost their one-dimensional identifying function and instead create a new 'tattoo space.' He dismantles the paradoxical 'savage/civilized' and 'nature/purity' schemes (drawing on Baudrillard on the smooth, made-up female body-screen that reflects male desire) and Loos' 'ornament and crime' verdict on women's tattoos. He proposes that female tattoos have 'become graffiti' – a Bergsonian spatial 'center of action' and 'skinscape' that disperses meaning horizontally rather than branding an identity, recuperating the female body as a political body against commercialized post-political bodies.

feminism.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
feminism.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
feminism.relation: Nancy Kang argues tattoos can function within a liberatory feminist ideology, accentuating rather than diminishing femininity by exposing the differential treatment of tattooed women. She surveys radical, Marxist, liberal and corporeal feminism (invoking Aristotle's dismissal of women, Mill's Subjection of Women, and Gramsci's hegemony), then reads pop-culture cases – Crash's tattooed Latino worker, Black Swan's Lily, the Perry 'pricks as needles' sexualization, carnival 'Tattooed Ladies' like Irene Woodward marked 'by the father's hand,' and the McGee/Bullock/Kat Von D scandal – to show corporeal feminism treats tattooing as a risky, self-owning revolutionary act.

feminism.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
feminism.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
feminism.relation: Kyla Reid and Tinashe Dune attack the bestselling dating manual The Rules by Fein and Schneider, focusing on Rule 4 (never go Dutch—let the man pay) and Rule 12 (dump him if he gives no romantic gift like jewelry).
