existentialism.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
existentialism.title: 16. Doppelgängers, Doubles, and Tulpas
existentialism.relation: Bunce reads Twin Peaks' pervasive doubling as dramatizing self-loss versus self-mastery. Cooper is good because he integrates his rational and mystical sides into an authentic whole, while BOB is a parasitic, one-dimensional inhabiting spirit and Laura chooses death over becoming BOB. He explains self-loss through La Rochefoucauld and Rousseau on amour-propre and the modern craving for esteem (Josie's masks versus Norma's refusal to become a brand), and traces the doppelganger motif from Jean Paul's satire of Fichte's clear I/not-I distinction to Dostoyevsky's The Double—arguing that, unlike Jean Paul, Twin Peaks affirms an authentic, whole self one is responsible for.

existentialism.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
existentialism.title: Foreword
existentialism.relation: Robert Porfirio's foreword traces film noir's dark sensibility to a native strain in American culture rather than only to imported existentialism, running from Puritan gloom through Poe, Melville, and Hawthorne to the hard-boiled pulp of Hammett, Chandler, and Woolrich. He argues that William James's pragmatism sounded the death knell of the Emersonian/Thoreauvian transcendentalist faith in self-reliance and nature, leaving the way open for Darwinism, Freudianism, and Nietzschean pessimism to reduce the individual to a 'waif amidst forces.' He connects this to the Germanic emigres who brought expressionist style, suggesting they were drawn to an American darkness already present, and closes wondering what post-9/11 neo-noir will make of the same fear and paranoia.

existentialism.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
existentialism.title: Introduction
existentialism.relation: Mark Conard's introduction opens with thumbnail plots of Double Indemnity, The Maltese Falcon, and Out of the Past to ask what noir has to do with philosophy, then frames the definitional problem (genre, style, cycle, or mood) as itself a philosophical question about essence. It surveys the volume's thirteen essays, noting that French existentialism was contemporaneous with classic noir (1941-58, Maltese Falcon to Touch of Evil) and shares its themes of moral ambiguity, reason versus passion, and pessimism even without direct influence. It previews the arguments to come, including Nietzsche's death of God as a lens on noir, neo-noir realism, Aristotelian tragedy and catharsis, and Schopenhauer's parallels in Ride the Pink Horse.

existentialism.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
existentialism.title: Nietzsche and the Meaning and Definition of Noir
existentialism.relation: Mark Conard uses The Postman Always Rings Twice and Goodis's Night Squad to survey the failed attempts to define noir (genre, style, cycle, mood) and contrasts two theories of definition: Socrates/Plato's search for the essential form versus Nietzsche's flux metaphysics, in which no stable 'being' exists behind becoming and language falsifies a world in motion, making essences and definitions fictions ('I am afraid we are not rid of God because we still have faith in grammar'). He proposes that noir is best understood as an American artistic response to Nietzsche's death of God, the loss of transcendent meaning and value that produces noir's pessimism, alienation, and moral disorientation, citing Sam Spade shrugging off his partner's murder and Ole Andersen passively awaiting his killers. Ironically, the same flux that makes noir what it is (the death of God) is what makes noir impossible to define.

existentialism.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
existentialism.title: Cherchez la Femme Fatale The Mother of Film Noir
existentialism.relation: Read Mercer Schuchardt argues that The Jazz Singer (1927) should be considered the first film noir because it is the first mass-medium announcement of Nietzsche's death of God, staged as the death of Papa Rabinowitz and the old prescriptive Judaism. He reads the film through a three-stage deicide (God as God, then one god among many, then a stage prop for Jakie's voice) and through a Jungian/Neumann anima-animus opposition of the word-based patriarchal religion versus the image-based maternal love that wins out, mirroring film displacing scripture. He ties this to Porfirio's existential pessimism that undercuts happy endings, casting Jakie's blackface Broadway triumph as a bittersweet, angst-ridden creation of meaning after the loss of transcendent value, and traces later 'existential detective' descendants like I Heart Huckabees and Fight Club.

existentialism.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
existentialism.title: Film Noir and the Meaning of Life
existentialism.relation: Steven Sanders uses film noir to motivate philosophical reflection on the meaning of life, reading its pessimistic sensibility (Touch of Evil, Detour, Out of the Past, D.O.A., Vertigo) as the presupposition that life is meaningless per se. He runs through Schopenhauer's pessimistic arguments from the vanity and transience of existence, Nagel's rebuttal that our not mattering in a million years does not stop things mattering now, and the tension between Sartrean existentialist freedom and noir's Freudian fatalism of the inescapable past. He then lays out three models of meaninglessness (Baier's worthlessness and purposelessness, Camus/Nagel's absurdity met with irony), reading noir protagonists as ironists, before rejecting the noir view that life must be meaningless and arguing that meaning is a matter of degree, requiring realizable projects of positive value.

existentialism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
existentialism.title: Introduction
existentialism.relation: Editor Jerold Abrams argues Kubrick's whole filmography forms a coherent 'cinematic existentialism' in which a free subject stands against a cold, uncaring world, synthesized with strands of Stoicism and pragmatism. He surveys the volume's essays as variations on this theme: Camus' absurd in Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove, Nietzschean flux in Full Metal Jacket, Heideggerian being-toward-death and authenticity in Paths of Glory, and Nietzsche's overman as the Star Child in 2001. The essay ties specific films (the ape's femur, HAL, Humbert, the Overlook) to the claim that each Kubrick subject must invent its own meaning in a meaningless universe.

existentialism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
existentialism.title: Understanding the Enemy The Dialogue of Fear in Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove Elizabeth F. Cooke
existentialism.relation: Cooke reads Kubrick's Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove through Camus' absurdism, arguing that facing fear and meaninglessness is a task each person must do alone. In Fear and Desire the detached Lieutenant is Camus' lucid 'stranger,' while mad Sidney and death-seeking Mac fail by fleeing into fantasy or false hope; the interchangeable soldiers and doubled enemy general dramatize the sheer contingency of which side one is on. In Dr. Strangelove the individual is dissolved into insane institutions (Ripper, Strangelove, the Doomsday Machine, the War Room round table), so that Sartrean bad faith becomes systemic and no one can face the absurd honestly.

existentialism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
existentialism.title: Existential Ethics Where the Paths of Glory Lead Jason Holt
existentialism.relation: Holt uses Paths of Glory to illustrate existential ethics, framing the doomed 701st Regiment as 'thrown' beings-toward-death who retain full freedom in how they meet their fate. He resolves the 'paradox of existentialism' (denying objective values while commanding authenticity) by treating authenticity as a formal, second-order virtue like integrity: Colonel Dax is sincere and consistent, General Mireau an inauthentic hypocrite acting in bad faith. Addressing weakness of will (Roget's cowardice) and the condemned Paris 'dying well' before the firing squad, Holt argues that courage—an Aristotelian character virtue—is the smuggled-in content that grounds any formalist existential ethics.

existentialism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
existentialism.title: Where the Rainbow Ends Eyes Wide Shut Karen D. Hoffman
existentialism.relation: Hoffman reads Eyes Wide Shut as Kubrick's most optimistic film, tracing how Bill and Alice Harford are 'awakened' to the uncontrollable power of sexual desire and thereby strengthen their marriage. Bill's Kantian confidence—that principled duty guarantees fidelity—is shattered by Alice's confession of overwhelming desire for the naval officer, which exposes their fidelity as mere moral luck. Through the models, Marion, Domino, and the anonymous masked orgy at Somerton (where sex is impersonal 'bodies touching bodies'), Bill seeks but fails to feel Eros; the couple finally choose a consciously chosen fidelity, and Alice's closing 'fuck' insists raw desire belongs inside marriage, which Hoffman links to Kierkegaard's view of marital love living and winning in time.

existentialism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
existentialism.title: Knockout! Killer’s Kiss, the Somatic, and Kubrick Kevin S. Decker
existentialism.relation: Decker reads Killer's Kiss (and later 2001, A Clockwork Orange, Eyes Wide Shut) through Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of the lived body ('I am my body'), recovering the somatic that Socrates and Plato's Phaedo denigrated. In Killer's Kiss the boxing match, the mannequin-warehouse fight where bodies become weapons, spatial camera work, and the theme of contingency foreground embodiment; 2001 makes viewers feel their own bodies in space, and A Clockwork Orange's Ludovico 'cure' rewires the body-mind. Drawing on pragmatists Shusterman and Sullivan and on Foucault's biopower, he argues the anonymous masked bodies of Eyes Wide Shut turn Merleau-Ponty's projective intentionality into domination rather than communication.

existentialism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
existentialism.title: Rebel without a Cause Stanley Kubrick and the Banality of the Good Patrick Murray and Jeanne Schuler
existentialism.relation: Murray and Schuler argue Kubrick's unifying sensibility is a dogmatic Hellenistic-style skepticism (via Hume's 'The Sceptic' and Seneca) that yields 'the banality of the good': in a world of cosmic futility and near-state-of-nature human nature, decent characters like Dax are helpless while the wicked (Barry Lyndon, Alex, Quilty) have vitality. They read Kubrick's Playboy remarks on human insignificance as Humean size/duration tropes, and diagnose his Sartrean 'create your own meaning' answer as a self-refuting false philosophy. Using Marx's critique of Hegel's accommodation to capitalism, they contend Kubrick's skepticism and irony merely reflect the 'bourgeois horizon' rather than comprehending it, ending in present-pleasure hedonism ('fuck' as the last word of Eyes Wide Shut).

existentialism.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
existentialism.relation: Karen D. Hoffman reads The Last Temptation of Christ and Bringing Out the Dead through Sartre's distinction between the for-itself (transcendence) and the in-itself (immanence), arguing both reluctant saviors are tempted into bad faith. Scorsese's Jesus, tempted on the cross to abandon his mission and live as an ordinary husband and father, passively drifts toward a life of pure immanence that denies his human transcendence, until (following Kazantzakis's 'sprouting of wings' image via Judas) he reclaims his choice to be crucified. Frank Pierce inversely faces a false transcendence—the temptation to think of himself as God, or to escape via drugs, violence, or suicide—and resists it, allowing the vegetative Mr. Burke to die. Hoffman frames avoiding either exaggeration as the path to authentic Sartrean humanity and grace.

existentialism.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.relation: Sanders's introductory survey frames Mann's cinema as suffused with existentialist themes—alienation, freedom, authenticity, and existential choice—citing Sartre's 'condemned to be free' as the key to protagonists like Thief's Frank and Heat's Neil McCauley, who choose personal truth over surrender. It maps the volume's essays: Nietzschean will to power in the crime films, Levinas's ethics of the Other in Thief and Collateral, and Lockean/Rousseauian visions of nature in The Last of the Mohicans. Mann's outsiders repeatedly face the fateful, doom-laden choices (McCauley abandoning Eady to kill Waingro) that define existential man.

existentialism.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.relation: Palmer casts the protagonists of The Jericho Mile and Thief as 'outsiders' in Colin Wilson's sense—men 'awakened to chaos'—read through Camus's Myth of Sisyphus. Rain Murphy, running endless meaningless laps and hurling away the timer, is Mann's Sisyphus: his fate belongs to him, the struggle itself filling his heart. Thief's Frank, who 'gets to where nothin' means nothin',' shreds his dream-collage and destroys everything rather than be owned by Leo, enacting the absurd hero's scorn for a Hobbesian 'war of all against all' where law lacks connection to justice.

existentialism.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.relation: Sanders argues Mann's action serves existentialist ideas: identity, freedom, authenticity, and death. In Thief, Frank's insistence on 'the yield of my labor' and his self-immolating exit dramatize the individualist maximizer whose choice of principle—echoing Sartre's young man and Kierkegaard's 'purity of heart is to will one thing'—cannot be given from outside. The Miami Vice episode 'Heart of Darkness' is read as a morality play on authenticity: undercover agent Artie Lawson's flight into the fantasy persona is a bad-faith masquerade that ends in suicide, mirroring Crockett's own anxiety about his Sonny Burnett alter ego.

existentialism.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.relation: Rybin links Mann's style-versus-substance debate to the existential self-definition of his characters, focusing on Public Enemies. Dillinger, who tells Billie 'the only thing that's important is where somebody's going,' is not yet an icon but is 'becoming Dillinger' as the film unfolds. In the penultimate scene, watching Clark Gable in Manhattan Melodrama—'die the way you lived, all of a sudden'—Dillinger achieves authentic self-definition by claiming the gangster myth as his own identity, a Warshovian 'experience of art'; Mann's editing collapses the space between Dillinger and the screen just before Dillinger is gunned down, the cost of authentic selfhood.

existentialism.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.relation: Pomerance argues Public Enemies inverts the gangster genre's convention of the 'ecstatic' criminal viewed from law's judgmental exterior: Mann's handheld camera penetrates Dillinger's private, breathing, interior world (contrasting the mechanized, plan-driven Purvis), likening the film to Fantastic Voyage's journey inside a body. Drawing repeatedly on Walter Benjamin's Arcades Project—the flâneur who is 'utterly undiscoverable,' the bourgeois transformation of nature into interior—he reads the FBI's cataloging of Dillinger as modernity reducing an integrated person to a collectible 'public enemy,' culminating in the head shot that is both execution and publicity image.

existentialism.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
existentialism.relation: Skrodzka reads Thief and Collateral as exercises in deontology grounded in Levinas's ethics of responsibility to the Other. Frank's violent courtship of Jessie and his final destruction of his possessions, and Max's crashing of the cab after Vincent's interpellation, are staged as the self's annihilating opening to the face of the Other (glimpsed in the rearview mirror as Max's doppelganger). Using Bauman's account of liquid-modern disconnection and a leftist critique of late capitalism, she argues Mann grounds Levinasian ethics in physical labor, and defines Vincent's evil as that which is 'knowing but unknowable,' deaf to the Other's call.

existentialism.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
existentialism.relation: Spicer argues that the noir antihero embodies existentialism's darker side (alienation, contingency, dread), and that neo-noir intensifies this via European neo-modernism. In Point Blank, Boorman renders Walker's revenge as possibly a dying hallucination, using repetition, doubling, and drained color so that the story becomes an existentialist meditation on desire, faulty memory, and fragile identity. In Memento, Nolan's reverse-chronology 'Mobius strip' structure and Teddy's claim that memories are subjective interpretations leave Leonard's identity in tatters, ending both films on profound existential ambiguity.

existentialism.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
existentialism.relation: Gilmore reads Chinatown as neo-noir that is itself a kind of philosophy, engaging the hermeneutics of suspicion (Nietzsche, Freud, Marx) and existentialist alienation. Curly eating the venetian blinds signals a desire to recover a less painful blindness; Jake Gittes's 'conceptual scotomas' (Dennett) and hubris make him miss counternarratives, paralleling Oedipus as detective. Using Freud on the uncanny and doppelgangers (Jake doubled with Hollis Mulwray and Noah Cross) and Aristotle's Poetics on catharsis and the sublime, Gilmore argues 'Chinatown' names the abyss where every narrative is undone, and that facing this dark sublimity is the way of wisdom.

existentialism.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
existentialism.title: The Existential Frankenstein
existentialism.relation: McMahon gives an existential reading of Whale's Frankenstein and Shelley's novel through Heidegger's being-toward-death and Ernest Becker's denial of death. Victor Frankenstein exemplifies Becker's 'defiant Promethianism,' the offensive denial that seeks to conquer death, and the monster personifies death itself. She argues his obsession erodes his humanity, estranges him from others, and generates moral dilemmas, illustrating Heidegger's claim that only authentic acceptance of mortality restores individuality and genuine community, so that mastering death would make us monsters.

existentialism.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
existentialism.relation: Abrams's editorial introduction argues that Kubrick's whole filmography forms a coherent cinematic existentialism in which the isolated self stands against a cold, uncaring world. It threads the individual Kubrick films through named philosophers - Camus's absurd in Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove, Nietzsche's flux and Overman in Full Metal Jacket and 2001, Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death in Paths of Glory, Kant's marriage-morality in Eyes Wide Shut - and notes Kubrick blends this existentialism with Stoicism (The Killing) and pragmatism. It frames each contributor's essay as reading one film through that lens.

existentialism.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
existentialism.relation: Cooke reads Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove as studies of how we face Camus's absurd. In Fear and Desire the detached Lieutenant is Camus's lucid 'stranger,' while Sidney goes mad and Mac chooses a suicidal assassination as false meaning; each faces death alone, so it is not tragedy. In Dr. Strangelove the individual is dissolved into insane institutions - Ripper, Bat Guano, the War Room round table - so no one can face the absurd lucidly; Cooke uses Sartre's bad faith to name how men become mere representatives of their institutions, and contrasts both films with Descartes's and Plato's method of certainty.

existentialism.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
existentialism.relation: Holt reads Paths of Glory as an illustration of existential ethics. The doomed men of the 701st are 'thrown' (Heidegger) into a suicidal attack on the Ant Hill, and the film contrasts the authentic Colonel Dax - sincere, consistent, refusing Mireau's command out of integrity - with the inauthentic, bad-faith General Mireau. Holt resolves the 'paradox of existentialism' by treating 'be authentic' as a formal meta-value, and argues that authenticity ultimately rests on the Aristotelian virtue of courage, shown when Paris 'dies well' before the firing squad despite an earlier failure of nerve.

existentialism.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
existentialism.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
existentialism.relation: Biderman and Devlin use Traffic's four intertwined characters to test Kantian moral absolutism, applying the three formulations of the categorical imperative: Helena's decision to have witness Eduardo Ruiz murdered fails universalization, while Javier's whistleblowing on General Salazar (motivated only by duty, refusing reward) passes the autonomy formula. They argue Kant handles these cleanly but strains on DEA agent Montel's revenge (treating Carlos as a means) and outright fails on drug-czar Robert Wakefield's conflict between two absolute duties, to nation and to his addicted daughter. Following Sartre's critique that the categorical imperative is too abstract for concrete dilemmas, they show Soderbergh siding with existentialist choice as Robert invents his own law and quits to save his daughter.

existentialism.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
existentialism.title: An Introduction to the Philosophy of TV Noir
existentialism.relation: Sanders's introduction argues that TV noir is an autonomous art form in which film noir's themes are aufgehoben (Hegel's term: preserved and transcended, not negated), and that noir television dramatizes philosophical questions about alienation, relativism, freedom, and meaning. He surveys the volume's arguments: Fitzgibbons on Naked City's conflation of the normal with the moral, Skoble's counterexample of moral clarity in The Fugitive (Richard Kimble), Lee's morally ambiguous John Drake in Secret Agent, and his own readings of Miami Vice's 'sunshine noir' and Crockett's merger with his undercover persona Sonny Burnett. He frames Part 2 through Sartre and Camus, contrasting their call for engagement and defiance with classic noir's passive doomed protagonists (D.O.A.'s Frank Bigelow, The Prisoner's Number 6), and applies Camus's man of revolt to Jack Bauer in 24. He also raises standing objections: Nagel's ironic alternative to Camus's scorn, the incoherence of 'nothing matters' applied to Tony Soprano, and the Foucault/Lyotard-style postmodern critique of institutional power he finds in Crime Story.

existentialism.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
existentialism.title: “Do Not Forsake Me, Oh, My Darling” Loneliness and Solitude in Westerns
existentialism.relation: Biderman argues that the western hero's solitude carries philosophical benefits, distinguishing being alone from feeling lonely (McCauley in Heat: 'I'm alone, I'm not lonely'). Epistemically he likens the silent, self-reliant hero (Kane in High Noon, Shane, Munny in Unforgiven, Blondie) to Descartes retreating into methodological doubt and solipsistic solitude to secure knowledge. Ethically he sets Aristotle's claim that man is a social animal (so the friendless hero cannot flourish) against Stoic detachment and Sartrean/existentialist authenticity, concluding the hero must be 'lone' because his heroism is inseparable from his chosen solitude.

existentialism.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
existentialism.title: Order without Law The Magnificent Seven, East and West
existentialism.relation: Skoble compares The Magnificent Seven with Kurosawa's Seven Samurai, arguing the farming villages are not Hobbesian anarchies needing a sovereign but Lockean communities with a 'grown' social order that merely lack reliable enforcement against bandits. Using Hayek's distinction between spontaneous order (kosmos) and planned order (taxis), he shows the farmers legitimately hire gunslingers/ronin for self-protection rather than surrendering to private-justice worries. The warriors' willingness to honor an unenforceable contract ('That's just the kind you've got to keep') is grounded in a self-created ethics linking the Bushido/Zen and existentialist idea that one's honor and selfhood consist in one's actions.

existentialism.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
existentialism.title: 9 Neil Young’s Search for the Simple Life
existentialism.relation: Watson and Riches reinterpret "A Man Needs a Maid" not as simple misogyny but as Young's ambivalent inner conflict between craving companionship and fearing the pain of intimacy. They read his pursuit of the "simple life" ("Heart of Gold," avoidance of reading) through Epicurean simplicity, Aristotle's eudaimonia, Bowlby/Freudian avoidant attachment and cognitive dissonance, and Sartre's "bad faith" as self-deception, set against Thoreau's chosen solitude and Aristotle's claim that the non-social being is "beast or god."

existentialism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
existentialism.title: “Howzat!” Prometheus Is a Fast Bowler
existentialism.relation: Kevin S. Decker argues the Doctor's morality is an "ethics of ambiguity" poised between Romanticism and existentialism, not any formula. Rejecting positivism, deontology, and utilitarianism as fits for the Doctor, he reads the Doctor's freedom, wandering, and rejection of Time Lord values through Sartre's radical freedom and bad faith (the student torn between mother and Free French) and Beauvoir's "adventurer" who confers value by choosing. The Romantic search for the infinite in small things and the Prometheus myth frame the Doctor as a liberating, self-defining moral exemplar.

existentialism.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
existentialism.title: NOTES
existentialism.relation: Jeremy Barris argues that Lost dramatizes the structure of life itself, using Heidegger's claim that the inquirer's own being is the clue to all questions and his notion of 'thrownness' to read the castaways' accidental arrival as a mirror of our own bewildering birth into circumstances we did not make. He reframes the show's central puzzle as 'the question of life after birth,' contends against Sartre and Camus that life is neither fully sensible nor fully absurd but a half-understood riddle, and invokes Wittgenstein's On Certainty to show that total doubt is impossible because understanding senselessness presupposes understanding something.

existentialism.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
existentialism.title: 13. No Place like a Non-Place
existentialism.relation: Pagnoni Berns, Juvé, and Aguilar apply Marc Augé's concept of the 'non-place'—transit spaces (roads, airports, ships, hotels, malls) of anonymity and 'supermodernity' that confer no identity—to the show's empty landscapes. Postwar gender and identity crises play out in 'Passage on the Lady Anne' (slowness versus speed), 'The Hitch-Hiker' and 'The Passersby' (the road as a non-place where dead women refuse their fate), 'Will the Real Martian Please Step Up?', 'Nightmare at 20,000 Feet,' 'The Parallel,' 'The After Hours,' and 'The Four of Us Are Dying,' where identification briefly pierces anonymity, often fatally.

existentialism.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
existentialism.title: Chapter 10 Mark Twain’s Serious Humor and That Peculiar Institution
existentialism.relation: Kramer argues, against Davenport, that Twain can be simultaneously serious and funny, using humor to attack the 'spirit of seriousness'—the dogmatic certitude and epistemic closure Sartre and Beauvoir describe—rather than sincerity itself. Drawing on Schopenhauer's account of seriousness and Beauvoir's remark that the mystified slave takes his condition as natural, Kramer shows Twain's satire of Christianity ('Little Bessie,' 'Letters from the Earth,' the anti-adultery commandment, the Philippines massacre) exposing the incongruity between professed omnibenevolence and real suffering. Like Democritus the 'laughing philosopher' and a Socratic ironist, Twain undermines complacent certainty without offering dogmatic Truth in its place.

existentialism.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
existentialism.title: MOTHERHOOD
existentialism.relation: Elizabeth Butterfield reads her exhausting early motherhood through Simone de Beauvoir's The Ethics of Ambiguity and The Second Sex, arguing that 'the ideal mother,' like 'true womanhood,' is a social construction and that a mother is 'freedom in situation,' never a mother 'the way a stone is a stone.' She recasts Beauvoir's 'serious man' as the 'serious mother' who flees her freedom into the Motherhood Religion, and invokes Sartre's 'condemned to be free' and 'Hell is other people' (No Exit) to advocate the honest, self-aware 'genuine mother' over inauthentic self-sacrifice.

existentialism.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
existentialism.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
existentialism.relation: Hernandez contrasts 'dark' existentialism — Sartre's café-bound claim that hell is other people and that the self is imprisoned in others' looks (illustrated by Starbucks' Pike Place backlash reshaping its identity), and Camus's absurd alienation — with an 'optimistic existentialism' that finds meaning in community. Drawing on Kierkegaard's Christian love, Jaspers's 'encounter,' Marcel's turn toward the other (her Sweet Eugene's pregnancy story), and above all Buber's I–Thou versus I–It, she argues the coffee community (neighborhood boards, fair-trade activism, the neighborly cup) is an existential ground where isolated bodies-toward-death create shared hope by treating each patron as a Thou rather than a discarded It.

existentialism.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
existentialism.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
existentialism.relation: Sadler argues black coffee, unlike ceremonial tea, is the realist emblem of our anxious, isolated postmodern condition, and that the chain coffeehouse is a 'non-place' of public anonymity that only simulates the sociality we crave. Against Aristotle's confident view of humans as social animals whose eudaimonia presupposes a settled social order, she sets Nietzsche's alienated individual free to create values — then argues Nietzsche errs: using the trivial cappuccino-vs-latte choice, she shows (via Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Korsgaard) that even solitary choices need reasons intelligible to others, so individual choice cannot be self-justifying and our search for meaningful, non-arbitrary lives is irreducibly social.

existentialism.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
existentialism.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
existentialism.relation: Eric Bronson reads the elves of Rivendell and especially Lothlorien through the 'merrier' existentialists, arguing that lasting joy requires facing the abyss and still affirming life, and knowing, as Nietzsche urged, what to remember and what to forget. Galadriel sings in dark times yet is burdened by remembering too much, unable to let go of her cursed past, so her regret shows the danger Jaspers and Arendt also diagnosed of losing oneself. When she refuses Frodo's Ring and chooses to 'diminish and remain Galadriel,' she embodies the existentialist's affirmation and trust in one's own inner light.

existentialism.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
existentialism.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
existentialism.relation: J. Lenore Wright reads the Quest through the Western journey-narrative, both outward (Plato's climb out of the cave, Augustine's conversion) and inward (Descartes's methodological doubt turning toward the cogito). Frodo's leaving the Shire and freely accepting the Ring dramatizes the outward journey and the limits of freedom, while the wounding-and-healing of Sam, Merry, and Pippin marks an existential journey toward the Nietzschean charge to 'become who you are.' Wright contrasts the Yea-saying hobbits, transformed into resilient masters, with Nay-sayers Smeagol and Saruman locked in inauthentic self-pity, and argues Tolkien's ordinary pilgrims show that binding oneself to the good makes ordinary life extraordinary.

existentialism.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
existentialism.title: Who is Who
existentialism.relation: The introduction argues that Doctor Who and philosophy share a common origin in wonder (quoting Plato's Socrates and Aristotle) and traces the show's shifting worldview across the eleven Doctors. It claims early Who embodied Enlightenment 'positivism' (the pro-science Hartnell/Pertwee eras) but that the post-1996 and post-2005 series turned toward Romanticism and Sartrean/de Beauvoirian existentialism, framing the surviving Doctor's post-Time War 'angst,' homelessness and burden of freedom through existentialist themes.

existentialism.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
existentialism.title: index
existentialism.relation: This composite chapter argues philosophy through several comics. Jeremy Barris pairs Plato's dialogues with Amazing Spider-Man, using the allegory of the cave, the Forms, and Platonic love/eros to show that Spider-Man's bodily beauty, awkwardness, and self-trivializing irony draw readers toward goodness the way Plato says lust for beautiful bodies leads the soul upward to truth. Iain Thomson reads Moore and Gibbons's Watchmen as a 'deconstruction of the hero,' running Rorschach, Ozymandias and Dr. Manhattan through Nietzsche's Ubermensch and 'do not throw away the hero in your soul,' Heidegger's authentic 'choosing one's hero' and the uncanny, Kierkegaard's knight of faith, and Baudrillard's idea that an extreme realization destroys its own idea. Laura and Paul Canis read Daniel Clowes's Ghost World through Sartre's existentialism: Enid's post-high-school 'three o'clock' limbo enacts thrownness, abandonment, radical freedom and the flight from it into bad faith, contrasting Enid's authentic self-creation with Rebecca's settled conformity. Aldo Regalado's essay treats Tarzan, Superman, Captain America and the Black Panther as responses to modernity and race.

existentialism.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
existentialism.title: NOTES
existentialism.relation: Carolyn Korsmeyer uses Aristotle's Poetics dictum that the 'probable impossible' beats the possible improbable to argue popular narrative can actually conduct philosophy, not merely illustrate it. Her central case is that the TV series Angel—the ensouled, guilt-cursed vampire who concludes 'if nothing we do matters, then all that matters is what we do'—independently arrives at the same existentialist position as Simone de Beauvoir's The Ethics of Ambiguity, with no textual borrowing. She contrasts The Matrix's dramatically sustained Cartesian dream-doubt against the 'improbable impossible' Dallas dream-season, showing why one is a philosophical vehicle and the other bankrupt.

existentialism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
existentialism.title: 15. Grey’s Anatomy as Philosophy Ethical Ambiguity in Shades of Grey
existentialism.relation: The chapter argues that Meredith Grey embodies Simone de Beauvoir's existentialist ethics from The Ethics of Ambiguity, rejecting the childlike 'spirit of seriousness' that treats moral rules as absolute. Through episodes where Meredith stabilizes a bomb inside a patient's chest, coaches a death-row inmate to induce his own brain death, switches an Alzheimer's-trial placebo for Adele, and commits insurance fraud to treat an immigrant child, it shows her breaking institutional protocol to positively will the freedom of others while owning her choices. It contrasts her authentic embrace of moral ambiguity and risk against Shepherd's, Bailey's, and Webber's rule-bound seriousness or self-interest, framing medical dilemmas as an ambiguous moral realm where no single correct answer exists.

existentialism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
existentialism.title: 52. Fight Club as Philosophy I Am Jack’s Existential Struggle
existentialism.relation: Oya reads Fincher's Fight Club in existentialist, nonethical terms as the story of the unnamed narrator 'Jack' and his struggle for an authentic, self-governed life. Consumerism (the 'Ikea nesting instinct'), the masculinity of underwear ads, religion, and finally Tyler Durden's hunter-gatherer creed are all rejected as externally imposed answers that deny authenticity; Fight Club and Project Mayhem merely swap one alienation for another. Jack's shooting himself to purge Tyler dramatizes self-affirmation. The chapter grounds this in Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity ('the genuine man will not agree to recognize any foreign absolute'), contrasts Nietzsche and Unamuno on self-affirmation, cites Hobbes on the brutish state of nature to condemn Tyler's utopia, and invokes Plato's cave to argue a comfortable but externally governed life is still not authentic.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
existence-precedes-essence.title: No Exit and The Vault Sartre and Seinfeld on the Inescapability of Others
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Jennifer McMahon defends the heretical reading of Sartre as a relational theorist of the self: in Being and Nothingness consciousness is a nothingness, not an essential ego, and only the Other - 'the Other accomplishes... to see ourselves as we are' - lets us grasp ourselves as objects. Seinfeld illustrates this better than Sartre's own suspicion of others: Jerry's identity exists only through his entanglement with George, Kramer, and Elaine (change them and you get a 'bizarro-Jerry'), and the finale's prison cell ('The Vault') replays No Exit's locked room with the trial's parade of wounded minor characters - except that Seinfeld's chattering foursome shows friendship as a positive, not hellish, dependency.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
existence-precedes-essence.title: Unknown
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter walks through Nausea as the ordinary-world twin of the red pill: Roquentin, an unremarkable 1930s historian, is unravelled by a beach pebble, a handshake like 'a fat white worm', a door-knob that seems to grab him back, and finally the chestnut tree's 'naked World' - discovering that existence is a gelatinous, unjustifiable 'messy suffering' and that the order, names, and values we take for reality are only a veneer consciousness projects onto an indeterminate whole. His nausea is the horror of authenticity before it becomes anything else, the price Neo pays for swallowing the pill.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
existence-precedes-essence.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Dallas Willard defends the film's excess of violence as its whole point: it visualizes human evil as beyond the remedies of education, law, or counseling (the route Plato and Aristotle tried), with Satan — the androgynous figure carrying the smug dwarf through the scourging crowd — explaining why only Christ's non-resistant embrace of the cross can break evil's grip. Against the passive reading of 'the Passion,' he argues Jesus 'played' his judges, deliberately laying down his life to inaugurate the kingdom of God. The argument leans on the hidden God (deus absconditus): God stays hidden, contra Sartre's 'no nature' self-creation and closer to Pico della Mirandola, so that we can freely make ourselves, which is also why demanding 'more evidence' misses what belief in God requires.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
existence-precedes-essence.title: Sick of Love
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Krein and Levin read Dylan's portraits of fallen socialites in "Like a Rolling Stone," "Just Like a Woman," and "To Ramona" as critiques of bad faith - characters who hide from freedom and responsibility in consumerist status games, in Sartre's sense that existence precedes essence. But Beauvoir's Second Sex exposes the cost: the women Dylan praises ("Girl from the North Country," "One More Cup of Coffee") are praised precisely for staying in immanent, pastoral passivity, denied the transcendence that for Beauvoir constitutes full humanity. Borrowing Benjamin's and Buck-Morss's notion of modern "dreamworlds," they finally read Dylan's pastoral utopias as a counter-dreamworld spun after the collapse of the mass-utopian promise of consumer happiness.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
existence-precedes-essence.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Auxier uses the question 'Would Bruce Springsteen ride a Honda?' as an ontological probe: Honda embodies defensible middle-class values while a Harley is not primarily a machine but 'a decision about life and what makes it valuable', a suicide machine Jesus could have ridden into Jerusalem and whose absence would render Easy Rider meaningless even if Fonda rode some other Harley. His own boyhood purchase of a Honda XL 70 over the Harley Z90 becomes a lesson in Heideggerian honesty, since he knew he belonged on a Honda, while buyers who choose for appearances are consumed by das Man, the they-self that lives inauthentically through images and slogans. Using Husserl's method of imaginative variation on the question, he concludes that the Harley as cultural icon represents an existential decision and the life that follows from it.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
existence-precedes-essence.title: A Nietzschean Conclusion
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Slowik argues the Pythons have a positive existentialist message: Kafka's bureaucratic insanity, where ordinary people beat helplessly against irrational rules, recurs in the 'Cheese Shop' and 'Dead Parrot' sketches, and Camus's Sisyphus lives on in the monotonous lives of Palin's city stockbroker and the accountant who dreams of lion taming — repetition without Sisyphus's defiance. The core claim is that Python endorses individual-centered existentialism: Brian's 'You've got to think for yourselves. You're all individuals!' is the troupe's rare direct statement of Sartre's 'existence precedes essence', confirmed by Cleese's and Palin's interviews about resisting those who tell you how to behave, a theme the chapter extends through Nietzsche's critique of moral tradition and organized Christianity. Sartrean bad faith explains Python's stereotyped characters — the aggressive policeman, the pepperpots, and Mr. Praline insisting 'I am not a loony!' while demanding a fish license for his halibut — while Arthur Pewtey's meek 'Right. Right.' and Ron Obvious's physical limits raise nature/nurture objections to Sartrean freedom. The 'Nietzschean Conclusion' is that Monty Python itself exemplifies will to power as 'giving style' to one's character, constantly overcoming its own formulas rather than repeating what succeeded.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
existence-precedes-essence.title: Poker and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Sanders splits poker into two philosophical styles. The Rationalist — Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason, Pascal's domestication of chance into probability — plays like Sklansky, Chris Ferguson, and Howard Lederer, whose temptation is the paralysis of analysis; the Existentialist — Sartre's existence precedes essence, Camus' scorn for the absurd, Kierkegaard's leap of faith taken without decisive evidence — plays like Gus Hansen calling Antonio Esfandiari's $334,000 all-in re-raise with ten-high. A Russell-and-Popper-style regress of predictions (knowing a prediction changes its outcome) becomes the tournament 'hall of mirrors' of intentions read in Phil Ivey and Johnny Chan, and the chapter lands on Richard Taylor's existentialist point that meaning comes from committed doing, at the table as in life.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
existence-precedes-essence.title: Poker and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Vernezze uses Dostoevsky to make gambling existential: Notes from Underground's insistence that will trumps reason ('what do I care for the laws of nature and arithmetic?') and The Gambler's portrait of the calculating gambler — who loses like everyone else and worships money with a 'German' soul — prefigure existentialism's three traits: lost confidence in reason, despair as part of the human condition, and the willed overcoming of absurdity (Camus' Sisyphus happy, Sartre's condemned freedom). Dostoevsky's own roulette addiction fuels the reading, with Amarillo Slim and Brunson's side bets as heirs. The Cincinnati Kid's climax clinches it: Lancey Howard 'making the wrong move at the right time' by chasing a straight flush proves poker's essence lies beyond reason — a truly Dostoevskean activity.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
existence-precedes-essence.title: Identities, Selves, and Others
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Patterson uses Thornhill's being mistaken for the fictitious George Kaplan to test theories of personal identity: the body theory fails a CIA thought experiment in which a Kaplan double is slowly rebuilt from Thornhill's own replaced cells; Locke's memory theory fails on amnesia scenarios and circularity, since one cannot have memories of a self unless one already has a self; and Parfit's psychological continuity survives, with Thornhill drifting along a 'Psychological Spectrum' toward 'one hundred percent Kaplan' as he plays the spy. The chapter then turns existentialist: with Sartre, no essential nature fixes who Thornhill is, so he is totally responsible for the self his choices create, from 'Expedient Exaggerations' to risking death on Mount Rushmore. Charles Taylor's claim that a self exists only in dialogue with a community explains why Eve and others literally help make Thornhill into the person he becomes.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
existence-precedes-essence.title: Lonesome Day
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Calef asks how fictional story-songs can teach: lyrics yield neither know-how nor know-that, since Plato's Theaetetus shows true belief is not knowledge (the 'Meeting Across the River' narrator's plan works only by luck). The answer is a third kind — knowing what something is like: 'The River' lets a comfortable listener inhabit Mary's husband's slide into a dry marriage, and 'Nebraska' lets us feel Starkweather's numb void, 'what it's like to have no soul.' Aristotle's Poetics (we delight in imitation because learning pleases; poetry is more philosophic than history because it speaks in universals) explains why sad songs satisfy us, and Sartre's universal human condition grounds the empathy that makes The Rising render 9/11 ('You're Missing,' 'Empty Sky') thinkable at a personal scale.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Avatar Unparalleled Opportunities
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Cuddy asks how gamers relate to BSG videogame avatars — as an extension of the ego or a disposable other — using Freud's id/ego/superego to cast the avatar as a socially safe venue for reconciling forbidden desires (piloting a Cylon Raider) with the superego's demands. Against Rehak's claim that gamers simply drop the avatar when losing, he enlists Sartre: blaming the game or 'cheating' opponents is bad faith, a denial of the freedom to create one's own essence, with Lee's '33' debate about responsibility for the Olympic Carrier and Baltar's vacillation as in-show parallels. Sartre's facticity bounds the freedom — hard missions are fixed facts to deal with — so the gamer, like Adama's fleet, must take responsibility within limits.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
existence-precedes-essence.title: Why I Can Play Zelda for Four Hours Straight
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Fellela reads Link's endless drudgery (slashing grass for rupees, collecting bottles, leaving the final Ganon fight at a 'permanent pause') through existentialism: Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' is dramatized in Ocarina of Time's opening, where Link must acquire sword, fairy, and skills to make himself the hero, and Nietzsche's 'God is dead' call to become gods is answered by Link restoring meaning to a hostile Hyrule. Camus' Sisyphus figures the repetitive world-saving quest as an absurd hero's owned task, and Frankl's logotherapy (meaning as the tension between what one is and what one should become) explains why humiliating menial tasks, in camp or in laundromats or in Zelda, become bearable and even meaningful. Link's fixed options even illustrate Frankl's point that freedom is the stance we take toward conditions, not freedom from them.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Missionary
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Christopher Hoyt reads Buffett's escape from Catholicism as a case study in secular meaning-making after Nietzsche's death of God, taking the Mardi Gras ritual of Folly swatting Death out of town as Buffett's core spiritual attitude — interpreted the way Wittgenstein criticized Frazer, as an expression of our stance toward death rather than mere magic. Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' frames the post-1960s task of self-definition without God, while Marx's alienation explains what the persona of *Jimmy* refuses: the impersonal work and borrowed values that leave moderns living an alien narrative, like McGuane's character Skelton in Ninety-Two in the Shade. The twist is that *Jimmy*'s pop-culture vocabulary — Tully Mars built from Donovan's Reef and Slim Pickens, Bogart, the Brylcreem jingle — is itself authentic, and the 'semi-true story' of the myth tells deeper truths than a literal biography could, making Buffett something like a pop prophet for late modernity.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Three 'Phase Four' essays. Moseley reads the Joker across Batman #1, The Killing Joke, The Dark Knight, A Death in the Family, and Dark Knight Returns as a 'moral monster' who knowingly does evil - and, following Anscombe and Scanlon's guise-of-the-good analysis, pursues aesthetic 'higher values' in a Camus-like affirmation of the absurd, embracing the irrationality Batman's rational moral order cannot fathom. Levin uses X-gene biology (Beast's explanation in Astonishing X-Men, genotype vs phenotype, M-Day) to strip Magneto's Homo sapiens superior claim of any genetic or phenotypic basis, then argues via the moral community of rational persons (Kant's criterion) that mutants and humans share one moral community, condemning both the Registration Act and mutant separatism. O'Neil's prose piece traces Harvey Dent from Calvinist certainty through the acid that scars him to cosmic doubt - quantum randomness, many worlds, Sartre's condemnation to freedom - until Nietzsche's amor fati lets him embrace duality and let the scarred two-headed coin decide good and evil.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
existence-precedes-essence.title: True Selves Found or Made
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Theodore Schick reconstructs Aleister Crowley's philosophy of Thelema to explain Jimmy Page's devotion—Boleskine Manor, The Equinox bookstore, the Zoso sigil, 'Do what thou wilt shall be the whole of the law' etched in Led Zeppelin III's run-out groove—and reads 'Stairway to Heaven' stanza by stanza as an allegory of awakening to the True Will. He then dismantles the framework: no spell has ever worked under controlled conditions (post hoc fallacy), Sartre's existence precedes essence denies any divinely written True Will or human nature, and Schopenhauer (via Einstein) argues we can do what we want but cannot want what we want. Using second-order desires and autonomy, the chapter concludes that selves are made, not found—so even if a True Will existed, following a program we did not write would make us 'loyal plastic robots', not free.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
existence-precedes-essence.title: Mr. Monk’s Greatness
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Lewis argues Monk is Nietzsche's Übermensch. Sketching Sartre's existence-precedes-essence through the contrast between the designed wipe and self-defining humans, the chapter claims Monk creates his own essence through choices — keeping the coffee table askew in memory of Trudy, 'dirtying' his house in 'Mr. Monk Makes a Friend,' drinking stream water in 'Mr. Monk Gets Cabin Fever' — and lives by self-prescribed values (hourly flossing, bagged tissues, relentless truth-seeking) that separate him from the herd of the Court of Public Opinion. The comparison with Stottlemeyer — Nietzsche's lookalike with the mustache, 'the quintessential man' of the herd — inverts the expected hierarchy: 'He was a yardstick for me, of both detection and character' ('Mr. Monk Goes to Mexico') shows the badge-carrying everyman is the inferior one. Monk therefore challenges the macho sci-fi stereotype of the superman: the Übermensch can be gentle and kind, fight for truth and a cleaner world, and still have room to improve ('What does not kill me makes me stronger').

existence-precedes-essence.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
existence-precedes-essence.title: Manny
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Santaniello reads five nonconformist Red Sox through ethical theory. Ruth's sale to New York becomes a Kantian case: he tore up his signed three-year contract and demanded a trade while expecting others to keep promises, violating the categorical imperative on promise-keeping. Ted Williams's lifelong war with the 'Knights of the Keyboard' exemplifies existentialist authenticity ('It just wouldn't have been me' tipping his cap), Spaceman Bill Lee embodies Sartre's condemned freedom and existence precedes essence, Jim Rice's Hall of Fame delay is Aristotle's failure to hit the mean between silent deficiency on Boston's racism and excess toward reporters, and Manny's 'Gas is up and so am I' money grab shows Aristotle's point that wealth is an incomplete end pursued for the sake of something else.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
existence-precedes-essence.title: A Reply to facebook Critics
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Wittkower answers critics who call Facebook broadcast narcissism by way of Sartre: Facebook actions (pokes, the Disney Princess quiz, cats friending cats on Catbook) have no given meaning, so users and their friends create it, which is why there are 'so many different Facebooks'. He takes up Sunstein's 'Daily Me' echo-chamber worry and Hegel's claim that real freedom means choosing within community, arguing Facebook merely makes the dialectic between chosen and unchosen communities explicit. Against the charge that status updates are trivial, he deploys Nietzsche's Last Man and Schopenhauer's cheese-mite microscope to defend caring about a friend's sandwich from the inside of a shared life.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
existence-precedes-essence.title: Living the Absurd Life
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Krein asks why he has spent fifteen years on karate when pepper spray and avoidance would serve self-defense better, and answers with existentialism rather than Buddhism. Nietzsche's death of God and Sartre's claim that existence precedes essence leave life objectively meaningless, but the dojo supplies a self-contained standard for Sartrean transcendence (kata quality is judged within the art), trains the courage and clarity authenticity requires, and enforces excuse-free responsibility: in sparring you either score or you don't. Studying a traditional martial art is thus a heroic, 'act without hope' defiance of the absurd.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
existence-precedes-essence.title: Let Your Heart Be the Anchor and the Beat of Your Own Song
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Berti reads Neil Peart's 1997-98 catastrophes (his daughter's car accident, his wife's cancer death) and the 55,000-mile Ghost Rider motorcycle exile through Sartrean existentialism: existence precedes essence, so with no God-given script Peart must author his own reactions, exactly as Sartre's student had to choose between mother and Resistance. The chapter tracks alienation ('I do not know who I am'), the duty to choose rather than lean on outside voices, and 'The Pass' as the voice telling a suicidal teenager to walk back from the razor's edge. Thoreau's Walden retreat supplies the model for the healing road, and Peart's own directives ('keep moving; kick your own ass, gently') enact 'Freewill' and 'Something for Nothing': we are the ones who choose, and the choice to live made all that followed (re-marriage, Vapor Trails, five more tours) possible.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
existence-precedes-essence.title: Bad or Bad Faith
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Rebecca Steiner Goldner reads the show through Sartre's Being and Nothingness: Dexter's watching is the Look that crystallizes his victims into a fixed essence - Matt Chambers can never again reinvent himself in a new town - and the kill room stages the demanded shame and confession ('Look at what you did!'), echoing Sartre's caught peeping-Tom. She then argues Dexter's belief that he was born a killer, that his Dark Passenger leaves him no choice, is itself bad faith: existence precedes essence, and by Sartre's account even the reformed thief remains responsible for his past, as with Jeremy Downs and Dr. Meridian. We viewers root for Dexter because we see the freedom he denies - and love him because he never makes the authentic choice to abandon his murderous project.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
existence-precedes-essence.title: What Does A Scanner See
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter answers Arctor's question with Sartre: the gambler cannot observe his way out of deciding again, because consciousness is a nothingness with no determinate essence to be observed, so a scanner used to find yourself 'sees nothing', and Fred watching his own footage is bad faith, hiding from freedom behind presumed facts about himself. Butler then flips the bleakness into Sartre's optimism, reading Dick's 'I myself, I am not a character in this novel: I am the novel' as the author freely remaking his life through the book, his first written without amphetamines, after the break-in he suspected he had staged himself.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
existence-precedes-essence.title: Chapter 23 - Lonely Wolves
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Travis Paterson's introduction reads A Scanner Darkly as Dick's most autobiographical novel and explains Arctor's disgust at the over-happy Brown Bear Lodge audience through Sartre's Nausea: Roquentin's discovery that existence is sheer contingency, that we are superfluous, vaguely alarmed beings who cannot define existence as necessity. Arctor never finds Roquentin's slender chance of acceptance, so the nausea curdles into addiction and the wolf parable, the magnificent lone wolf shot to protect the meager, over-fed animals, poses the chapter's question of why the sensitive outsider is the one sacrificed.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
existence-precedes-essence.title: A Footloose Man
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Dick expounds Sartre's 'Existentialism Is a Humanism' through the essentialist picture — a God-given blueprint, like Keith's Bentley designed before manufacture — against Sartre's claim that we exist first and invent essences afterward, marriage and family included. Monogamy thus emerges as a human choice mandated by Western authority and imposed on conquered peoples, not an absolute ethic handed down from heaven, a freedom humans exercise even in dropping Deuteronomy's stoning rule. Keith, Mick and Simone discarded the inherited tradition of monogamy, while Charlie Watts chose to stick with it.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
existence-precedes-essence.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Robert Tally Jr. reads The Graveyard Book as 'spectral existentialism': Bod's climax, 'I'm Nobody Owens. That's who I am,' is Sartre's existence precedes essence made literal, a self made rather than found, and the climactic claiming of the name enacts the self-ownership of the nursery-rhyme pauper 'who nobody owns.' Heidegger supplies the uncanny not-at-home-ness (unheimlich) of the graveyard, which Tally, citing Foucault's 'Of Other Spaces,' calls a heterotopia, while Silas the vampire embodies Lukacs's transcendental homelessness and Kierkegaardian anxiety is transmuted by Bod into the spectral gift of Fear he wields on his bullies. The identity-leeching ghouls named after the Duke of Westminster and the 33rd President are the avatars of bad faith, and the Jacks' attempt to dodge the prophecy fulfills it like Oedipus's, showing that Bod's fate, too, is self-made.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Kempner reads The Walking Dead through Sartre's 'Existentialism Is a Humanism': with God and the old value-system gone, survivors who cling to pre-made essence die — Hershel keeps his zombified son locked in the barn awaiting restoration, and Shane tries to steal Rick's old cop-and-husband identity rather than live his own existence. Rick's waking in the hospital is a rebirth: he first exists in the new world, then creates a way of being human, and his relapses into the sheriff uniform nearly get him killed. Carl shooting Shane to save his father completes the family's existential freedom (children are no longer 'innocent'), walkers — without will or choice — are the ultimate inauthentic beings, and the volume's tagline, 'forced to finally start living,' makes the zombie world a sternly optimistic humanist story.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
existence-precedes-essence.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Reads Larry as a textbook existentialist: his agonizing over trivia ('Doctor?... Pharmacist?') instantiates Heideggerian anxiety and Sartrean anguish, because every choice, even yanking his 5 wood out of a casket in 'The 5 Wood,' proclaims an image of how everyone ought to live. Since existence precedes essence there is no fixed human nature for Larry to appeal to; he must author his values alone, which the chapter says also makes him an optimist ('I'm not an inventor, but I'm an improver'). Larry dispels others' bad faith when he tells Susie she obviously can share the brownie recipe in 'The Benadryl Brownie,' and his baldness crusade, firing the toupee-wearing chef Phil Dunlap in 'The Grand Opening,' is a demand for authenticity about one's facticity. The 'Larry David Stare' is analyzed through Sartre's Look: the squinter tries to inspect another consciousness empirically and necessarily fails, since the other's freedom can never be objectified.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
existence-precedes-essence.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Robison-Greene reads the returning soldiers through Camus and Sartre. War reveals the absurd - Jimmy's Argonne story of the German soldier who would not die even in a hopeless situation strips life of inherent value - and Van Alden's fervent Christianity is the escapist response to absurdity, bad faith that denies his own desires. Jimmy and Richard are trapped in bad faith over facticity and transcendence, Richard pinned by 'the look' of a community that only sees his ruined face ('Hell is other people'); neither fully becomes an absurd hero like Meursault, since Richard still craves meaningful ties, but Jimmy finally embraces the absurd at the War Memorial, arranging his own death with the calm of a man who 'died in the trenches, years back.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
existence-precedes-essence.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter uses Sartre to diagnose Barney's fixed persona of suits, womanizing, and Bro Code worship as bad faith: having freely chosen to become the suited businessman who stole Shannon, Barney now acts as if those are his only options, denying his radical freedom. Hardy maps Sartre's own examples onto the show - Wendy the Waitress play-acting a stereotypical waitress, the woman who ignores the knee-touch, Barney tuning out criticism with 'I'm awesome' - and reads emotions, via Sartre's Sketch for a Theory of the Emotions, as magical transformations of the world like Marshall's 'best burger' quest and the Bob Barker paternity story. Barney's love for Robin and his secret reunion of Marshall and Lily are the moments he breaks out of bad faith and chooses freely against his persona.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Devil and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Elizabeth Butterfield reads The Devil's Advocate through Sartre: Kevin Lomax's 'You set me up!' excuse - after defending the guilty Gettys and Cullen and abandoning MaryAnn - is textbook bad faith, a lie to himself about his own free choices. Milton the Devil plays existentialist, insisting 'I'm no puppeteer... I only set the stage. You pull your own strings,' until Kevin admits his vanity, his drive to win, motivated every choice. Radical freedom entails radical responsibility, and Kevin's final suicide is his last free act, chosen to keep coming out on top, while free will remains the one limit the Devil cannot breach.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
existence-precedes-essence.title: Homeland and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Talia Morag reads Brody's colliding roles - Marine, congressman, father, Muslim, follower of Abu Nazir - and Carrie's unstable ones (CIA agent, bipolar patient, lover) through Korsgaard's notion of practical identities, whose contradictory obligations (kill and not kill) demand reconciliation. Following Kierkegaard's advice to rethink labels like 'Christian', Brody reinterprets his suicide tape as acting 'as a Marine' against domestic enemies - a rationalizing move the chapter treats as bordering on bad faith - while Dana's phone call in 'Marine One' reasserts the father identity and stops the bombing. Carrie's 'Q&A' re-description of Brody as a good man and future hero shows identities are constructed through choices, Sartre's point that we are not summaries of our past.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
existence-precedes-essence.title: Girls and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Archibald reads Jessa as Girls' quintessential existentialist: her unbothered abortion ('I'm offended by all the supposed to's'), her 'I am a junkie' honesty, and her refusal to blame her rough past (Sartrean facticity) enact existence precedes essence and Camus's embrace of the absurd. Kierkegaard's 'the crowd is untruth' and 'leveling' explain her contempt for rehab group conformity, while her panic marriage to Thomas-John after Katherine's motherly intervention is diagnosed as bad faith and angst. Her assisting the dying Beadie's suicide attempt - and calling 911 when Beadie recants - becomes the chapter's closing confrontation with Camus's one serious philosophical question, answered by living 'without appeal.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
existence-precedes-essence.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Walker contrasts Pennsatucky's Christian fundamentalism with Piper's secular humanism (Kurtz's six features) in their 'Fool Me Once' confrontation. With no God, Sartre's existence precedes essence makes Piper condemned to create her own meaning: owning her crime to her mother and confessing the Pennsatucky prank, while Red and Vee play Sartre's cafe waiter, reducing themselves to chef and dealer, and Pennsatucky's 'defender of the unborn' persona is de Beauvoir's sub-man sheltering behind ready-made values. Marx's opium-of-the-people analogy explains why comforting, unverifiable belief can block the authentic, responsible pursuit of a meaningful life.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
existence-precedes-essence.title: 3. I Want You to Survive
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Seth Walker asks what makes a life worth saving, testing the show's survival choices against instrumental value (usefulness to the group) and Tom Regan's subject-of-a-life criterion of inherent value. Shane's sacrifice of Otis for Carl, Lori's fatal pregnancy and Judith's birth, the Governor's obsession with Meghan, and the hunts for Sophia all show that neither usefulness nor Regan's equal, non gradated inherent value explains why children are selectively elevated - and perceived 'innocence' fails with the colder Carl and with Lizzie. He concludes with Bob Stookey's line in 4.10 'Inmates' ('Not everything has to mean something... but it can'): following Sartre's claim that man is nothing but what he makes of himself, the survivors are condemned to be free and must make their survival mean something, as Daryl and Carol's search for Sophia did.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
existence-precedes-essence.title: 1. The Actor Tells the Truth
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Reisch argues Bowie's parade of characters (Ziggy, Aladdin Sane, the Diamond Dogs persona) was never metaphysical chameleonry but a postwar, cold-war project: by crediting himself only as 'the actor' and calling Dylan out as Robert Zimmerman's artifice, Bowie exposed the 'denim and hippies' authenticity cult as itself a construction. Diamond Dogs' '1984' and 'Big Brother' tie this to the era's totalitarian nightmares of manipulable humanity, and Sartre's 'Man is nothing else but that which he makes of himself' becomes 'the first principle of Bowie' - only constant reinvention keeps us from being fooled by ourselves or others, even at the anguished cost of 'Who Can I Be Now?'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
existence-precedes-essence.title: 7. Being for Red
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Courtland Lewis asks who Darrow is—Red, Gold, hybrid, savior—and surveys theories of the self: Plato's immortal soul ruling the body, Descartes's cogito as thinking thing, and Hume's denial that introspection ever reveals more than a stream of perceptions (we never experience a soul, only thinking). Freud's id-ego-superego offers a secular soul, but Sartre carries the chapter: Darrow is being-for-itself, perpetually projecting what he is not, tortured by the Look of others—Eo seeing a savior, Mustang holding him at gunpoint, Roque's betrayed friendship—and prone to bad faith through 'guardrails' like the Vale, excuses about Eo and Uncle Narol, and pining for Mustang instead of owning his choice. Since existence precedes essence, Darrow is nothing but the sum of his free choices, and to live otherwise is to choose slavery.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
existence-precedes-essence.title: 5. Guilty of Being a Dwarf
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Engels runs Tyrion's arc through Sartre's existentialism: his facticity as a dwarf makes everyone from Catelyn to Tywin presume his guilt, while 'Never forget what you are, wear it like armor' states the Sartrean authenticity of owning facticity while freely choosing one's essence. Catelyn's dagger accusation, the comic confession at the Eyrie, the wildfire ship at Blackwater, and the trial outburst ('I am guilty of a far more monstrous crime: the crime of being a dwarf') show him choosing rather than being defined; the murders of Shae and Tywin dramatize the slide into bad faith - embracing the 'monster' essence others assigned - before his choice to join Daenerys resumes the burden of self-creation.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
existence-precedes-essence.title: 2. 3eanuts and the Existential Schulz
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter introduces existentialism and reads Peanuts through it: Charlie Brown's defeats expose the 'groundlessness' of value, and the 3eanuts web project (deleting each strip's final gag panel) restores the despair that punchlines normally defuse. It explains Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' and the ideal of authenticity versus passively inhabiting roles, Heidegger's care and Dasein (even in despair there is an inner place where it happens), and Camus's absurd and Sisyphus revolting against a fate he cannot change. Lucy's hillside sermon ('WELL, LIVE IN IT, THEN!') and the final image of Charlie running at the football figure his revolt: he keeps kicking because in that moment a world without boxes exists in him.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
existence-precedes-essence.title: 8. Facing Up to the Realities
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Argues that 'Machine Gun' and its Berkeley introduction ('people... fighting wars... within themselves, not facing up to the realities') make Hendrix an existentialist: since existence precedes essence, each of us lives multiple realities we must author responsibly. The lyric variants diagnose Sartrean bad faith twice over — 'evil man make me kill ya' is the helplessness that denies freedom, 'fight like a farmer' the blame that locates failure out there — before the reprise's acceptance ('let your bullets fly like rain') and free judgment ('I know all the time you're wrong') achieve authenticity amid the solo's sonic battlefield.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
existence-precedes-essence.title: Conclusion An Infinity of Possibilities
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Engels reads William's transformation through Sartre's existential project: the white-hatted William and the black-hatted Man in Black are not a hidden true self finally revealed but two successive free choices of oneself, and the Man in Black's claim that the park showed him 'who he really is' is bad faith — a denial of his freedom that lets him absolve himself of cruelty, just as Ford's deathbed pivot cannot erase the facticity of his role in the hosts' suffering. Maeve's choice to leave the train is analyzed as her first self-chosen end and value judgment, suggesting a programmed android can begin constructing her own project despite Sartre's humanism. The open-ended finale — hosts free to fight back, the Man in Black smiling as he is shot — embodies Sartre's 'I am an infinity of possibilities' and the burden of being condemned to be free.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
existence-precedes-essence.title: 10. On Being and Meeseeks
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter asks what kind of being Mr. Meeseeks is and answers with Sartre: despite being 'created to serve a singular purpose', Meeseeks exhibit subjectivity, from the self-assertion of 'I'm Mr. Meeseeks!' to transcendence in envisioning Jerry's fixed golf swing and the anguish, forlornness, and despair of 'Meeseeks and Destroy' ('Your failures are your own, old man!'), so they must be beings-for-itself whose existence precedes essence, freely choosing accomplishment as their meaning. Along the way it glosses Sartre's facticity with Morty's hopeless crush on Jessica, essence-precedes-existence with the butter-passing robot, and bad faith with Jerry's assumed mediocrity and Beth's shrinking of herself into horse surgeon, wife, and mother until Mr. Meeseeks reminds her she is still an individual.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
existence-precedes-essence.title: 20. Sympathy for the Existential Devils
existence-precedes-essence.relation: James McLachlan reads the films through Sartre: replicants are made like penknives, with an essence before existence, and their drama is going 'off baseline' — the freedom of nothingness by which Batty murders his maker-gods (Tyrell the Father, Chew and Sebastian the trinity) and K disobeys everyone. Sartre's Satan from his Baudelaire biography, Blake's Orc and the Marriage of Heaven and Hell's contraries, and the Great Chain of Being's contradiction between filling one's place and moral freedom frame Luv as a perfect penknife, a 'good angel' who fulfills her vocation, while Batty and K are redeemed by the love that breaks their programming. 'More human than human' turns out to mean: existence precedes essence.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
existence-precedes-essence.title: 13. The Origins of Self-Love
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Anna Marie Fennell reads RuPaul's 'If you can't love yourself, how in the hell you gonna love somebody else?' through theories of self-love.
