Erich Fromm's four elements of love and Buddhist non-attachment (Jinkx Monsoon's 'water off a duck's back,' the Season Ten Inner Saboteur characters like Eureka's Eufilthior) ground the claim that self-love precedes healthy love for others. Against Aristophanes' myth in Plato's Symposium - the round beings split by Zeus, forever seeking their other half, retold in Hedwig and the Angry Inch - she sides with Ru: completion comes from within, not from a soulmate. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity (the sub-man and nihilist archetypes seen in self-sabotaging queens like Nina Bo'Nina Brown) and bell hooks's All About Love with Branden's six pillars of self-esteem map onto winners like Jinkx, Sharon Needles, Violet Chachki, and Bianca Del Rio, whose drag personas show existence preceding essence.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
existence-precedes-essence.title: 16. Death Becomes Her
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Hendrik Kempt reads Drag Race's pervasive death imagery - death-drops, the 'lip sync for your life,' mirror messages, the 'Death Becomes Her' runway - through the philosophy of death. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' and Stoic self-possession (Ru's 'pay them bitches no mind,' Violet Chachki enduring a tiny corset) explain why elimination, like death, gives no ground for worry once it arrives, while Socrates' 'philosophy is training for death' makes the show a workout video for dying - Socrates even dying fussing over a rooster like a drag mother to Miss Fame. Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death set up Sartre's radically free, future-oriented self - so voluntary exits like BenDeLaCreme's self-elimination and Charlie Hides's listless lip-sync betray one's own plans - and Camus's Sisyphus makes Chi Chi DeVayne and Roxxxy Andrews's doomed All Stars returns models of 'acceptance without resignation.' The closing weighs transhumanism's promise of conquered death against a DragCon-forever thought experiment, concluding with Ru's roast eulogy for Lady Bunny that love and irreverence, not immortal life, are the point.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
existence-precedes-essence.title: 8. The Death of God and the Death of Meaning
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Montoya reads Chidi's breakdown upon learning he has been tortured for three hundred years as Nietzsche's death of God, quoting the Parable of the Madman from 'Jeremy Bearimy' to show how the guaranteed meaning of Chidi's worldview collapses into nihilism. Michael's midlife-crisis makeover and partying embody Camus's embrace of the absurd, while Sartre's existence precedes essence, abandonment, and anguish explain why Eleanor's confession to Michael and her sacrifice in the Judge's test count as authentic choices. With the Judge's verdict stripping away any hope of reward, the humans finally choose goodness for its own sake, which the chapter presents as the show's answer to nihilism.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
existence-precedes-essence.title: 2. What Does Life Mean after the Snap
existence-precedes-essence.relation: This chapter reads four post-Snap Avengers as existentialist answers to how life keeps meaning after catastrophe. Tony Stark embodies Sartre's existence precedes essence, defining himself through free choice up to his final 'I am Iron Man' snap that erases Thanos and his army; the merged Professor Hulk lives Camus's Sisyphus, embracing the absurd and concluding 'all is well' after watching his own past rage; Captain America lives Levinas's ethics of the Other, from refusing to abandon brainwashed Bucky in Civil War to wielding Mjolnir to save Thor; and Ronin-era Hawkeye enacts Nietzschean nihilism until Black Widow's Vormir sacrifice, read through Zarathustra's burning in one's own flame, restores his meaning. The authors conclude Marvel's answer is affirmation: courage to affirm freedom, the Other, and life itself against Thanos as personification of genocide, climate change, and war.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
existence-precedes-essence.title: 16. KISS Goes Disco and Boogies on Simmons’s Bad Faith
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Christopher Innes defends 'I Was Made for Lovin' You' and KISS's disco turn on Dynasty against Gene Simmons's own scorn. Insisting that KISS is essentially and only hard rock treats the band's facticity as an in-itself, like Sartre's waiter who becomes nothing but his role — the bad faith of Simmons and rockist fans alike — whereas human transcendence and nothingness mean the band can authentically choose disco, grunge, or anything new, as Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love,' Pink Floyd, and Queen exemplify. The twist: bad faith is also a comfort, and the chapter ends by conceding that Simmons's hard-rock constancy may itself be an authentic filling of his own nothingness — so who is to say he is wrong?

existence-precedes-essence.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
existence-precedes-essence.title: Liz Meets the Elephant in the Room
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Barkman reads 'Rosemary's Baby' as staging second-wave feminism in Rose Howard's comfort-sacrificing activism against third-wave feminism in Liz, who sells her dignity for the $10,000 Followship Award and likes comfort and the status quo. Sartre's existence precedes essence supplies third-wave feminism's non-essentialist claim that anyone can be a feminist in any manner, while an Aristotelian essentialist standard of human flourishing shows Liz's 'have it all' optimism, from the wedding dress bought in 'SeinfeldVision' to the adoption schemes of 'Do-Over', is a delusion because career and family each demand everything. Jack's confession that 'you have to choose' lands the chapter's verdict that the third-wave promise leaves women in Liz's predicament.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
existence-precedes-essence.title: Its Structural Perfection is Only Matched by its Autonomy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Defends the Xenomorphs: if the Queen's tactical intelligence (incubating her eggs under the reactor, ordering drones to hold fire, cutting the power) and the species' hive organization satisfy Sartre's criteria of self-creating persons, then their 'attacks' are legitimate self-defense on the model of Sartre's preface to Fanon's Wretched of the Earth, where the colonized's violence restores a denied personhood. Read without anthropocentrism, Alien is the story of a newborn extraterrestrial hunted to death by humans, and Weyland-Yutani, the Marines, and the colonists of LV-426 - not the aliens - are the series' true villains.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
existence-precedes-essence.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Uses Sartre's cafe waiter, directly mirrored when Gob play-acts a waiter in 'S.O.B.s', to define bad faith as denying one's freedom by disappearing into roles: illusionist, Bluth Company president in George Sr.'s suit, 'any man' winning back Marta, Ward Cleaver father to Steve Holt (!). Distinguishing bad faith from impossible self-deception (beings-for-themselves have no pre-given essence), the chapter argues that even sincerity ('be yourself, Gob') is bad faith, and provocatively concludes Gob is happier and kinder to others in bad faith, reversing Socrates' 'know thyself'.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
existence-precedes-essence.title: Paradox and Peace
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Christopher Drohan reads Batman and Alfred through Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling: Batman, like Abraham, believes 'by virtue of the absurd,' resigning himself to an infinite, never-realizable justice as a knight of infinite resignation, while Alfred embodies the higher knight of faith whose justice is concrete love expressed in mending the suit, making sandwiches, and guarding the manor. Heidegger's thrownness and Sartre's condemned freedom frame both men's absurd existential condition, including Batman sparing Joe Chill and even allying with him against the Reaper. The chapter's verdict is that Alfred's faithful devotion to one person is the superior ethic, and that peace begins with him.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Avatar Unparalleled Opportunities
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Cuddy argues the gamer's bond with the avatar is an extension of the ego: Freud's id/ego/superego model explains why playing a Cylon Raider or flying the 'Bastille Day' mission lets gamers reconcile unconscious desires with the superego's demands in ways reality forbids. But when we lose we disconnect from the avatar and blame the game or 'cheating' opponents, which Sartre diagnoses as bad faith, a denial of freedom, contrasted with Adama's 'a man takes responsibility for his actions' in '33' and Baltar's vacillation over the vice-presidency. Through facticity (the unforgiving no-save 2003 game) and existence preceding essence, the chapter concludes that videogames offer unparalleled opportunities to practice Sartrean responsibility and achieve Freudian reconciliation through the right avatar.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
existence-precedes-essence.title: Living with Our Choices
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Peters reads 'The Resistance' webisodes through Sartre's occupied-France dilemma from Existentialism Is a Humanism (resist, collaborate, or do nothing, modeled on his student's choice between joining the Free French and caring for his mother): Tyrol joins the resistance for his family's future, Jammer joins the New Caprica Police to save lives and pays with execution by his former friends in 'Collaborators,' and Duck's choice to do nothing ends with wife Nora's death in the Temple massacre and his revenge suicide bombing. Since 'man is nothing other than what he makes of himself,' the chapter argues morality lies in the freedom to choose and in living with the consequences: Duck's refusal to accept his choice, not the choice itself, is the failure, and the Final Five revelation cannot retroactively alter choices made in good faith by Tigh, Tyrol, Anders and Foster. Which side holds the ethical high ground may simply be whichever side won and gets to write history.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
existence-precedes-essence.title: “I Am Moana!”
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Stages Moana's dilemma between her father's Aristotelian essentialism — everything on Motunui has a fixed function, so Moana's essence as chief precedes her birth — and Sartre's existence precedes essence, with Heihei the unchanging chicken as a being whose essence really does precede existence. Tui embodies bad faith and the crowd (his own aborted voyage left him enforcing 'no one goes beyond the reef'), while Tala and then Moana live authentically through anguish, forlornness, and despair, until 'I am Moana!' marks her self-defined identity. Nietzsche's 'become who you are' and 'what does not destroy me makes me stronger' frame her resilience, which lets her free Maui ('Hook. No hook. I'm Maui.') and unmask Te Ka as Te Fiti whose stolen heart 'does not define you.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Existential Redefinition of Doctor Strange
existence-precedes-essence.relation: DiGeorgio traces Strange's 'existential conversion' from scientific nihilism ('matter and nothing more') through Sartrean bad faith — playing the brilliant surgeon while not really believing life meaningless, refusing the Ancient One's widened keyhole — to authenticity. His hesitation to stay and fight after killing a zealot, and the Ancient One's 'it's not about you,' set up his choice to defend humanity as Sartre's universal decree, choosing for all humankind in anguish and freedom. The endless time loop imposed on Dormammu is read as Nietzsche's eternal recurrence demanding total commitment to one's choices, so that by the end Strange lives existence-precedes-essence: what he does, not his 'brilliant surgeon' essence, defines him.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
existence-precedes-essence.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Christopher Wood reads Cloud's arc as an existentialist quest: Heidegger's thrownness in Cloud's tumble off the Midgar train and his initial 'It's not my problem' denial of being-in-the-world; Nietzsche's death of God in Mako-powered Midgar's nihilism, with AVALANCHE as a call for revaluation of values and Sephiroth as a false aspirant god; and Sartre's bad faith in Cloud 'playing at being a SOLDIER,' a persona borrowed wholesale from Zack along with his sword and mercenary dream. Through the Lifestream reunion with Tifa, Cloud faces his fabricated past, admits 'I never was in SOLDIER,' and turns to authenticity by resolving to live without pretending, which Wood presents as the player's own existential task.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
existence-precedes-essence.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter asks whether Daenerys's fatalism - she feels truly free only once she believes fate is in control - can coexist with freedom in a Westeros where class and gender fix everyone's essence. Aristotle's sea-battle argument from bivalence and Cicero's Idle Argument (Dany will rule whether or not she leaves Meereen) are dismantled as having no practical consequences for deliberation, while Sartre's anguish and bad faith explain Cersei's 'necessity' excuse for arresting Ned and Sansa's refusal to own her lie about Joffrey and Mycah. Heidegger's authenticity then resolves the paradox: like Ned choosing between family and honor and Jon choosing his Night's Watch vows over kinship, freedom is not escape from one's past but owning it - Heraclitus's 'character is destiny,' becoming who you are.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
existence-precedes-essence.title: 8. The Death of God and the Death of Meaning
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Reads Chidi's 'Jeremy Bearimy' breakdown — quoting Nietzsche's Parable of the Madman ('God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him') after learning he has been tortured for three hundred years — as the nihilism that follows the death of God, where the Judge's verdict that the humans seek only 'moral deserts' strips their moral project of purpose. Michael's post-crisis makeover party is Camus's embrace of the absurd (Sisyphus pushing the boulder), and Sartre's Existentialism Is a Humanism supplies the way out: abandonment, anguish, and the French Soldier dilemma clarify Eleanor's confession in Season One and her lie that she failed the Judge's test as authentic choices. Once there is no hope of the Good Place, the humans finally choose goodness for its own sake.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
existence-precedes-essence.title: Why I Can Play Zelda for Four Hours Straight
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Toni Fellela gives an existentialist reading of Zelda, confessing she leaves Ocarina of Time and Twilight Princess permanently paused before the final Ganon fight because the meaning lies in the process of becoming, not the ending. Sartre's existence precedes essence structures Link's growth from a swordless Kokiri boy collecting equipment into the hero; Nietzsche's death of God ('we must become gods') fits Link restoring meaning to a godless Hyrule, while Camus's Sisyphus dignifies the repetitive drudge work of slashing grass for rupees. Viktor Frankl's logotherapy anchors the chapter's payoff: even the most mundane tasks — in a camp or a laundromat or Hyrule Field — become bearable and meaningful when connected to a future goal, which is why the author can play for four hours straight.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
existence-precedes-essence.title: To Live is to Die: Metallica and the Meaning of Life
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Scott Calef argues Metallica holds there is no meaning of life: the universe is 'much too big to see' ('Through the Never'), Socratic and Schopenhauerian arguments show pleasure, wealth and fame bring only 'King Nothing', and religion is a dishonest Freudian wish-illusion ('The God That Failed') that alienates us from this world. Precisely because life has no objective meaning, Sartre's existence-precedes-essence applies: like Hetfield in his rehab 'confession' and the hunter of 'Of Wolf and Man', we must honestly create meaning by living in the now, with death making life precious rather than pointless.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
existence-precedes-essence.title: Responsibility
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Christiansen reads SNL's first head writer Michael O'Donoghue ('Mr. Mike') through Sartre: the Least-Loved Bedtime Tales (Brer Rabbit skinned alive, 'there's no moral... just random acts of meaningless violence') dramatize a world where existence precedes essence and narratives lie; 'Sartresky and Hutch' stages the absurd via a Vietnam veteran with PTSD; and the needles-in-the-eyes impressions embody Sartre's vulnerability to the Other, which Mr. Mike's dark glasses shut out. The chapter ends with Sartre's Marxist turn in the Critique of Dialectical Reason, arguing O'Donoghue's angry 'Police State' sketch shows that scarcity, alienation, and organized state violence are contingent and can be fought, which is where his nihilism leaves room for hope.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
existence-precedes-essence.title: Getting the Joke
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Gray reads Jack Handey's Deep Thoughts and Fuzzy Memories as packaged existentialism: Sartre's existence precedes essence grounds Handey's responsibility for self-made meaning ('if you're robbing a bank and your pants fall down... life is funny'), Camus's absurd and Sisyphus's happy perseverance match 'sometimes I think the world has gone completely mad. And then I think, Aw, who cares?', and Beauvoir's ruts of inferiority warn against the ease of 'just sitting there' wanting money. Heidegger's authenticity and mortality appear in the parachute-swimming gag, dying laughing rather than in dread. The chapter also explains why the deadpan delivery over serene stream imagery makes morbidity funny, and worries that Handey's 'truth is... unreal' anticipated post-truth politics.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
existence-precedes-essence.title: 22. Unmasking the World and Its Heroes
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Claims the Superman-vs-Batman debate misses the point: both heroes are cave-escapers who must first see beyond appearances—Bruce renouncing vengeance on Joe Chill and then shaking Gotham from apathy (the ferries refusing the Joker's detonators), Clark learning from Jonathan and Jor-El that his powers are not for touchdowns but to lead humanity out by example. Masks serve the Socratic warning of the Apology that the just man must act privately to survive—Jonathan Kent dies keeping Clark's secret—yet risk becoming their own trap, from Smallville's Red Kryptonite ring to Batman's sonar surveillance that Lucius Fox calls too much power for one person. The chapter closes on Socratic ignorance and Man of Steel's genesis chambers: a hero, like Socrates, knows his wisdom is worth nothing, and anyone who chooses can be one.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
existence-precedes-essence.title: NOTES
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Peppers-Bates and Rust stage Weber's disenchantment of the world in Sookie's relationship with Bill: her scientific-naturalist demand to know what animates him meets his 'magic', and although Searle and Nagel show consciousness resists scientific reduction (so 'miracle' is not absurd for the mind), Bill's vitalist, quasi-Cartesian dodge is a bait-and-switch about digestion. Sookie's real question is Sartrean — whether vampires, seemingly driven by blood bonds, hierarchy, and appetite, can freely choose their projects — and the chapter answers yes: Malcolm's cruelty presupposes he could do otherwise, Sookie's 'blood tie thing' excuse is bad faith in Eric's eyes, and Eric's wooing of her after regaining his memory is a freely chosen project that re-enchants her world.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
existence-precedes-essence.title: Notes
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Reads Cohle's arc as an existentialist passage toward authenticity, using Sartre's being-for-itself to explain why Hart's 'family man' identity is bad faith — a clinging to social roles that denies the freedom of a consciousness that is an activity, not a thing. Beauvoir's analysis of women as the passive, objectified Other illuminates why Rust, despite his nihilism, persistently protects vulnerable women and children such as Sophia, Dora Lange, and Marie Fontenot: threats to others' freedom threaten our own. Nietzsche's Silenus wisdom, the spirit of gravity on the tightrope, and the shepherd who bites the head off the snake frame Ledoux's and Childress' warped eternal return as the poison Cohle must overcome before he can will life eternally and declare 'the light is winning.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Kempner reads the comic through Sartre's 'Existentialism Is a Humanism': with God and the old world gone, survivors like Rick, Michonne, and Dale must create their own values, while characters who cling to pre-apocalypse essences (Hershel keeping his zombified son in the barn, Shane waiting for the government) bring death on themselves. Rick's hospital awakening is treated as an existential rebirth in which his cop uniform is an 'essence precedes existence' trap, and Carl shooting Shane (and later Ben in 'Fear the Hunters') shows children making free choices outside conventional morality. The chapter concludes the series is 'sternly optimistic' because total freedom, not zombification, is what defines the humans: 'in a world ruled by the dead, we are forced to finally start living.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
existence-precedes-essence.title: Conclusion An Infinity of Possibilities
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Kimberly Engels reads William's transformation into the Man in Black through Sartre's existential 'project': rather than discovering a pre-existing true self 'among the dead,' William's new situation in the park (loving and losing Dolores, killing the Confederados, Logan's betrayal) produces an existential rupture in which he chooses new ends, symbolized by trading the white hat for the black. She argues the Man in Black's claim to have 'found himself' is Sartrean bad faith, denying his freedom and facticity to evade responsibility for the harm he causes. Extending existentialism to androids, she reads Maeve's choice to leave the train and seek her daughter as her first freely formulated project, the start of her own 'infinity of possibilities.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
existence-precedes-essence.title: Notes
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Donovan uses the New 52 Azzarello run's gods as a catalogue of gender stereotypes - jealous Hera hunting Zola, woman-incinerating Apollo, hyper-masculine First Born, self-sacrificing Demeter - then tracks Hera's transformation after Apollo makes her mortal as a Beauvoirian passage from immanence (being Zeus's Other, defined by his desire) to transcendence (charting an independent identity, aiding baby Zeke). Foucault's Panopticon explains how gender norms are internalized without an enforcer, and Butler's drag example grounds the claim that Wonder Woman accepting the god of war mantle - leading a female Amazon army 'not as your princess but as the god of war' - is a subversive performance of gender.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
existence-precedes-essence.title: VII - X-WOMEN AND X-ISTENCE
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Housel gives an existential history of the X-Women. Jean Grey embodies the paradox of 'existence precedes essence,' a fictional character whose meaning is assigned by creators and fans yet who perpetually re-creates herself through the Phoenix, while Rachel Summers 'makes her own existence at every single moment' in Ortega's sense across timelines. The Scarlet Witch's reality-warping is Baudrillard's 'line of fracture' where an expanding system cracks, and her denial of the past is Sartrean bad faith; Storm shows angstless responsibility, Mystique the 'cynical consciousness' of self-deception, Rogue Camus' absurdity in a life without touch, and Kitty Pryde Ortega's 'substantial emigrant on a pilgrimage of being.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Koepsell reads The Ice Storm as an existentialist masterpiece dramatizing Sartre's Being and Nothingness in Nixon's America. He maps Paul's Fantastic Four 'negative space/void' monologue onto Sartrean no-thing-ness and the tension between being-in-itself, being-for-itself and being-for-others, arguing the alienated, bourgeois Hoods and Carvers live inauthentically in bad faith, objectifying one another. Mikey's joyous reveling in the ice storm before his electrocution is a fleeting authentic immersion in existence (like Roquentin in Nausea), and the closing embraces—Wendy hugging Sandy, a weeping Ben meeting Paul—show characters momentarily overcoming alienation and freely remaking their essence.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
existence-precedes-essence.title: “I am not an I” Performative (Self)Identity in the Poetry of Bob Kaufman
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Pynn reads Bob Kaufman's poems ('Forget To Not,' 'Would You Wear My Eyes?,' 'Benediction,' 'Jail Poems') as enacting a performative, intersubjective selfhood: against Beauvoir's 'flavor of death' in American conformity and Sartre's dictum that existence precedes essence, Kaufman replaces the drive to invincibility with 'nakedness' and vulnerability. Merleau-Ponty's embodied intercorporeity and Buddhist ontology—impermanence, non-self, compassion, and ahimsa—let the poet's 'I am not an I' burn the isolated ego into a communal 'thousand me's,' with slavery's trauma inscribed on the body and Kaufman's 1963 Buddhist vow of silence as liberating practice.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
existence-precedes-essence.title: John Clellon Holmes and Existentialism
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Charters recounts how John Clellon Holmes—who coined the framing question 'How are we to live?' and prompted Kerouac's 'beat generation' label—was steeped in existentialism, reading Sartre, Camus, and Kierkegaard in the postwar New York scene. She argues his novel 'Go' is an existentialist text: its beat characters (modeled on Kerouac, Ginsberg, Cassady) enact freedom, self-transcendence, and the refusal of nihilism, saying 'no' in order to say 'yes' as in Camus's 'The Rebel.' Holmes ultimately rejected Sartre's atheist existentialism for a Kierkegaardian, faith-based one, valuing 'the evidence of soul' and reading Kerouac's characters as fleeing the absurd toward spiritual conviction.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
existence-precedes-essence.title: William Burroughs as Philosopher From Beat Morality to Third Worldism to Continental Theory
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Jones Irwin makes the case for 'Burroughs as philosopher,' tracing an 'impassioned moralism' and antihumanism (human as adjective, not noun) that separates him from other Beats and postmodernists. He links Burroughs's critique of alienation to Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and to Sartrean existentialism and bad faith ('there are no victims, just accomplices'), and reads the Beats' 'third force' Third Worldism via Freire, Fanon's Wretched of the Earth, and Paz. Close readings of Naked Lunch's 'Bradley the Buyer' and the sex-and-death delirium of 'AJ's Annual Party' connect Burroughs to Artaud's body without organs, Bataille's Sadean tradition, and Derrida's deconstruction of embodiment and 'distance touching.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
existence-precedes-essence.title: Human Nature and Freedom in Adaptation
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Ganssle uses Adaptation's four main characters to test Sartre's claim that existence precedes essence against Walker Percy's account of immanence and transcendence. Laroche, endlessly adaptable ('Done with fish'), embodies Sartrean radical freedom and pure immanence; Donald owns his love ('You are what you love, not what loves you') and lives without bad faith; Orlean and Charlie are paralyzed in bad faith, unable to choose. Ganssle contrasts Sartre's rejection of a fixed human nature (grounded in atheism, against Plato's and Augustine's Forms) with Percy's view that persons are unlike infinitely mutable orchids, arguing the film sides with Percy: the antiessentialist self is 'lost in the cosmos.'

existence-precedes-essence.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
existence-precedes-essence.title: “What Kind of Man Are You ” The Coen Brothers and Existentialist Role Playing
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Gaughran argues the Coens presuppose an absurd, valueless world (announced by Blood Simple's 'you're on your own' voice-over) in which characters must, per Sartre's 'existence precedes essence,' invent a self by adopting a style. He surveys the hats of Miller's Crossing, Everett's Dapper Dan dandyism in O Brother read through Camus's The Rebel, and Ed Crane of The Man Who Wasn't There as a Meursault-like figure who forges an identity through violence. Against Camus, murder and suicide are illegitimate revolts, and Sisyphus—not the nihilistic killers—stands as the true absurd hero who never resolves the tension between mind and indifferent world.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
existence-precedes-essence.title: Thinking beyond the Failed Community Blood Simple and The Man Who Wasn’t There
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Palmer reads Blood Simple and The Man Who Wasn't There as a diptych re-composing James M. Cain's The Postman Always Rings Twice and Double Indemnity, whose core theme is a failed community where self-interest poisons human bonds. Blood Simple dramatizes the Cainian problem—Visser and the others destroyed by instrumentalization and fatal miscommunication—while The Man Who Wasn't There, framed by Camus's The Stranger and Sartre's Nausea, stages its utopian solution. Ed's Sartrean disgust at hair and physicality drives his dry-cleaning scheme; like Meursault he kills and is condemned for the wrong crime, but unlike Cain's solipsistic heroes he ends yearning for communion with Doris beyond the grave, imagining the restoration of the lost community.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Barad uses Blade Runner to test what distinguishes humans from machines. Against Turing's claim that indistinguishable input-output makes a computer a mind, she deploys Sartre's dictum that in humans existence precedes essence while manufactured replicants (like a designed android) have essence first, so they can blame their maker. She reads the Voigt-Kampff empathy test through Sartrean forlornness and despair, and argues Roy Batty achieves authentic humanity when he kills Tyrell and freely chooses to save Deckard, becoming a life-giver rather than his programmed combat model.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
existence-precedes-essence.title: Recalling the Self Personal Identity in Total Recall
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Biderman uses Quaid/Hauser in Total Recall to test criteria of personal identity: the body criterion fails on Kuato and George sharing a body, the brain and Lockean memory criteria fail on implanted false memories and memory gaps, and psychological continuity fails on how radically Quaid differs from the malicious Hauser. Facing Hume's conclusion that the self is a fiction (echoed by Wittgenstein and Derrida's deconstruction), he argues Quaid escapes it through the Sartrean existential route: thrown into existence, he takes a stance toward his facticity and, following Kuato's 'you are what you do,' authentically creates himself by rejecting Hauser and saving Mars.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
existence-precedes-essence.title: The Prisoner and Self-Imprisonment
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Biderman and Devlin use The Prisoner to test three dimensions of selfhood: Number 6's 'I am not a number!' defends the material self against the Village's conformity (Rover, uniforms, human chess pieces), his reflective self echoes Descartes's certain thinking thing, Kant's rational self-legislation, and Sartrean authenticity ('existence precedes essence'), while the finale's trial of the rebels addresses the relational self. The revelation that Number 6 is Number 1 is then read through Foucault: hierarchical observation, normalization, and examination make the Village Bentham's panopticon internalized, so the prisoner monitors himself and the ideal of a freely self-created identity collapses into social conditioning, as Nietzsche's herd come home. The chapter leaves the noir ambiguity intact: either Number 6 is the authentic individual vindicated by the Village council, or the self is a fiction and his odyssey hopeless.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
existence-precedes-essence.title: “Back Off to What ” The Search for Meaning in The Wild Bunch
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Richard Gaughran reads Peckinpah's The Wild Bunch as an existentialist western set in 1913, a world 'unhinged' by Nietzsche's death of God where no a priori values remain. Pike Bishop's code of loyalty ('when you side with a man you stay with him') keeps failing—he abandons Crazy Lee, Sykes, and Angel—showing, in Sartrean terms, that only action, not talk or intention, creates meaning. Dutch's question 'Back off to what?' opens onto the abyss; the Bunch's final suicidal march to rescue Angel is read as a Camusian act of revolt that fashions authentic meaning where none was given, saying 'Let's go!' rather than surrendering to the deathward drift.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
existence-precedes-essence.title: 5. To Resist Despair
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Peterson defines being punk through three interlocking virtues - authenticity (via Varga and Guignon's account as used by Heidegger, Beauvoir, and Sartre), Sartrean freedom ('existence precedes essence'), and questioning authority, defended with Robert Paul Wolff's argument that obeying authority cancels autonomy. The Slits' Palmolive, Alice Bag, Johnny Ramone's cheap Mosrite, and Harley Flanagan show DIY as the punk response to Sartrean facticity, Operation Ivy's 'Knowledge' recalls Socratic ignorance as punk humility, and she concludes that even SLC Punk's Stevo going to Harvard can remain punk, since only striving to live authentically counts.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
existence-precedes-essence.title: 7. The Paradox of the Poseur
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Barry extracts a paradox from Jawbreaker's 'Boxcar': if punk is individuality and rejecting conformity (the subjectivity criterion), poseurs should be harmless, yet not just anyone counts as punk (the objectivity criterion), and each criterion implies the other is false. Framing the tension with Nagel's subjective/objective gap, he resolves it through Appiah's two pictures of identity (romantic authenticity vs the existentialist 'existence precedes essence' myth) and Taylor's created-yet-discovered true self, concluding that poseurs are genuinely vicious - they fake with enough social knowledge to know they are faking - and that social identities need both subjective and objective criteria, which would democratize identity politics.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
existence-precedes-essence.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Barnwell argues that fatherhood can constitute the ultimate meaning of a man's life, answering the paradox that a meaningful life 'all about the kids' seems not to be about the father by noting fatherly acts are still the father's own freely chosen activities. He confronts Camus's Myth of Sisyphus – the worry that childrearing is endless pointless rock-pushing across generations – by insisting children, unlike rocks, have intrinsic value, and invokes the Sartrean existentialist idea that choosing an activity confers value on it (illustrated by his buying oatmeal for 'Sally').

existence-precedes-essence.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
existence-precedes-essence.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Collins-Cavanaugh asks what makes a 'real' father, framing it as authenticity. He pairs Sartre's existentialist authenticity – free choice, anxiety, and the bad faith of adopting others' ready-made plans, with 'real cookie' and Derek Jeter examples – against Charles Taylor's dialogical authenticity, in which choices are made within a 'horizon of meaning' set by others. He argues authentic fatherhood combines both: a father must freely own his choices (provider dad vs nurturer dad) while grounding them in his child's needs, concluding he'll go bake cookies with his son Connor.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
existence-precedes-essence.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Silber uses his own Match.com romance with Karin to argue that virtual 'meeting' differs phenomenologically from face-to-face meeting, which Buber's I-Thou (vs I-It) makes into a whole-being encounter that online traces and aspects cannot supply, invoking 'all real living is meeting.' He treats the dating market as a site of Kantian danger, contrasting price with the dignity of persons in the kingdom of ends, and warns that the market's efficiency threatens objectification and commodification. He then deploys Sartre's bad faith, facticity and transcendence, and 'existence precedes essence' to diagnose online self-misrepresentation (lying about height, age, photos) as inauthenticity, while briefly setting Derrida's 'nothing outside the text' against Plato's Phaedrus preference for speech over writing.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.title: 73. Hasan Minhaj as Philosopher Navigating the Struggles of Identity
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Singh reads Minhaj's comedy of identity through existentialism, arguing his call for 'authenticity' over the first generation's 'assimilation' (the 'American dream tax' and 'biryani' arguments about choosing one's life) enacts Sartre's existence-precedes-essence and rejection of bad faith. He frames Minhaj's Indian-American-Muslim conflict via Heidegger's thrownness and facticity and the move from the they-self (das Man) to authentic self, contrasting it with Sartre's facticity as a limit on freedom. Minhaj's 'global citizen' anti-nationalism, his 'love is bigger than fear,' and 'may the best argument win' are presented as prescriptions for navigating national, ethnic, religious and personal identity while flagging fallacies like hasty generalization behind Islamophobia.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
existence-precedes-essence.title: 75. Phoebe Waller-Bridge as Philosopher Conscious Women Making Choices
existence-precedes-essence.relation: Pande and Engels argue that Fleabag and Lulu (Crashing) embody Sartrean authenticity: they own their choices, balance facticity and transcendence, and stay outside bad faith, while the men (Anthony, the Priest) fall back on pregiven roles and let 'the Look' or their fundamental project decide for them. Fleabag's addressing the camera and finally shutting it out is read as breaking the gaze of the Other; the Priest choosing priesthood over love exemplifies denial of transcendence. Through Beauvoir's Second Sex, woman-as-Other, and ethics of ambiguity, they show Waller-Bridge's transgressive, sexually frank women reclaim self-definition, arguing viewers 'could do better to be' the kind of free, choosing women her protagonists are.

existence-precedes-essence.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
existence-precedes-essence.title: 3. What Is Who
existence-precedes-essence.relation: The chapter runs the Doctor's regenerations and the 'Timeless Child' reveal through competing theories of personal identity: Plato's soul/Forms, Locke's memory continuity, and bodily continuity, all of which the Doctor's body-swaps and forgotten lifetimes defeat (the Twelfth Doctor's 'you are a broom' speech recasts the Ship of Theseus). It endorses an existentialist answer—personal identity is chosen and constantly 'becoming,' as the Thirteenth Doctor declares 'I know exactly who I am. I'm the Doctor'—and uses Sartre against Freud to explain how the Doctor and the Whovian fandom reconcile internal and external selves in a community of acceptance. It closes arguing that only an 'objective' immortality (memories preserved in the Matrix) survives death, not a subjective self.

language-games.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
language-games.title: Finale
language-games.relation: Kelly Dean Jolley reads Seinfeld as the sitcom twin of Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations: both are 'albums' - remarks, vignettes - that refuse the normal form (the finished essay, the developed plot), and both try to make us notice the commonplace hidden by its very familiarity (PI sections 118, 129, 596 on feelings of familiarity and the attack on meaning as a mental act). Jerry's 'It's a show about nothing' is the show's version of Wittgenstein's destroying houses of cards: the plot was the illusion, and the vignettes nag, repeat, and transpose the commonplaces until we hear what he calls the 'tune of our lives.'

language-games.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
language-games.title: And Where the @#$%^& is the Queen
language-games.relation: The editors' introduction recounts Monty Python's 1969 debut and argues the troupe's absurdism bears a deep connection to philosophy because the British Pythons absorbed the Oxford and Cambridge linguistic analysis of Russell, Wittgenstein, Moore, and Ryle while at university in the 1960s. It tours the volume's three parts, previewing each contributor's pairing: Schilbrack reading Life of Brian through Camus's absurd hero, Brighouse using the Argument Clinic for Rawls's analysis of social practices, Asma finding Buddhist mindfulness in The Meaning of Life, Huss pairing the Pythons with Hume on religion, and Spinelli reading sketches through Foucault on the social construction of madness. It concludes there is no single connection between Python and philosophy but many: sketches illuminate philosophy, philosophy illuminates sketches, and Python's empire says something about philosophy's cultural standing (with Wittgenstein's duck-rabbit figuring how the remaining chapters can be seen).

language-games.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
language-games.title: Meaning and Practice
language-games.relation: Uses 'Piston Engine (a Bargain)' from the Hamlet episode of Flying Circus — park-bench women who buy gift-wrapped piston engines because 'it was a bargain,' kill birds with hurled groceries, and end by dazedly reciting Hamlet — to test Wittgenstein's theories of meaning. Both the early Verification Principle and the later meaning-as-use principle fail: we understand the meaning of every sentence yet cannot make sense of what the women are saying, just as 'This is my hand' at the doctor's office, or the philosopher's 'I know that that's a tree' (Wittgenstein's joke at Moore's expense), is meaningful but senseless in context. Drawing on Remarks on Colour and On Certainty, Smith concludes that communal practices and forms of life fix what it makes sense to say, and that the sketch proves Python's Horatio point — 'there are more things in heaven and earth than are dreamt of in your philosophy' — since no theory of meaning captures what makes the exchange funny.

language-games.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
language-games.title: “Is There Enough of It About ”
language-games.relation: Carey uses the 'Spectrum: Talking About Things' sketch — where a cricketer is stumped by the question 'What is going on?' and the presenter piles up unanswerable questions — to explain both Wittgensteins as a 'philosopher's cramp' caused by language. Early Wittgenstein's Tractatus holds that sentences picture facts and that attempts to say what makes facts possible are nonsense, so Wittgenstein's own theory is a self-refuting ladder to be climbed and thrown away; the later Wittgenstein instead treats meaning as use, shown through situations A–D where 'What is going on?' makes sense in some contexts and not others, so philosophy has no once-and-for-all cure. Python sketches work the same seam of sense passing into nonsense: interviewing corpses on 'Is There Life After Death?', and a duck, cat, and lizard as mute panel experts, expose how 'talking', 'sitting', 'expressing', and 'having a face' shift meaning with use.

language-games.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
language-games.title: A Knockout of an Argument
language-games.relation: Reisch reads Palin's 'Bols Story' presenter — who drowns in ever-finer qualifications about talking, pausing, and gesturing signs — as a parody of Wittgenstein and ordinary language philosophy: brilliant analysis of words that achieves exactly nothing, since he never reaches Holland's most famous aperitif, just as the 'No Time to Lose' advice centre perfects a phrase without touching the failing marriage behind it. The Bruces sketch adds the social critique: the beer-swigging, rule-enforcing Australian department satirizes the cult around Wittgenstein at Cambridge and Oxford and the extra-linguistic forces — Nazism, McCarthyism, anti-communism — that shaped who counted as a philosopher and what got taught. 'The Epilogue' sketch, where a bishop and a philosopher settle God's existence by wrestling until a knockout, suggests philosophical disputes are settled like prizefights by power. Together these form a one-two punch: if fashions, politics, and bullying influence philosophers' beliefs, then philosophy cannot consist exclusively in solving puzzles of ordinary language and must open itself to history and sociology.

language-games.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
language-games.title: What Is to Be Done
language-games.relation: A comic persona — an elderly philosopher who claims Wittgenstein stepped on his foot while storming out of the famous poker incident with Popper at the Moral Sciences Club — blames Monty Python for 'destroying' philosophy by popularizing it, mixing it with popular culture, and making it impossible to tell real philosophers from frauds. His prime exhibit is the Dead Parrot sketch, read as a morality play in which no philosopher is ever summoned: Praline and the shopkeeper resolve nothing because amateur, negotiable language is left to haggle over whether the parrot is 'resting' or an ex-parrot, flouting the lesson that language matters. The chapter is itself Python-style satire, and its real target is the gatekeeping picture of philosophy as a serious professionals-only game, ending with the absurd plan to 'depopularize' philosophy by boycotting precisely the kind of popular philosophy book in which it appears.

language-games.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
language-games.title: U2 and Philosophy
language-games.relation: Gracyk explains U2's two commercial breakthroughs by pitting expression theory against Austin-style speech act theory: songs succeed not through verifiable autobiographical sincerity - 'Stuck in a Moment' was written about Michael Hutchence's suicide yet became the song of post-9/11 America, and 'I Will Follow' outmoves its equally sincere siblings - but because singing to an audience is an indirect illocutionary act that suspends ordinary commitments and invites listeners to make the song relevant to their own lives, as 'With or Without You' does by staying focused yet open-ended. Wittgenstein's point that an utterance's meaning depends on the actions into which it is woven frames the view that the audience must complete the speech act, as Larry Mullen does when he fits Dylan's 'With God on Our Side' to Northern Ireland. Pop failed, Gracyk argues, because 'Discotheque' and 'The Playboy Mansion' lecture - talk to the audience about consumerism rather than talking through them - so the unspoken invitation was withdrawn.

language-games.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
language-games.title: Forgetting the Love We Bring
language-games.relation: John Drabinski argues that the Deadhead parking lot is an 'occasional community' offering real hope against modernity's managed, one-dimensional life. Starting from his own Amherst-to-Worcester commuter routine read through Wittgenstein's forms of life — a community of nodding strangers at the same mini-marts — he stages Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Bauman's managed death as the deadening background against which such moments crack open. Where the commuter's community stays merely occasional, the parking lot's saturated friendship and shared undergoing (com-passion, good trip and bad, frat guy comforting and comforted) converts occasion into a genuine alternative ethos, drawing on Heidegger's sense of ethos as dwelling place — an everyday miracle of conversion he says we need now more than ever.

language-games.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
language-games.title: “You Rationalize” Jackie Brown’s Pragmatism
language-games.relation: K. Silem Mohammad argues Jackie Brown is a study in aporia and Wittgensteinian aspect perception: Ray Nicolette's purple/white bag paralysis, Ordell's 'Is that Rutger Hauer?' mistake, Jackie on the LAX moving walkway, and 'Across 110th Street' turning diegetic all force a re-description of experience within particular language games. The thrice-repeated Del Amo money switch-off adds no information but displays the characters' differing aspects of one event. Against Ordell's mind-fucking 'logical chains', Jackie's 'that's what you do to go through with the shit you start, you rationalize' embodies a pragmatist view of reason as context-bound use, matched by Max's calmly uncertain 'I think I do. Good enough?'

language-games.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
language-games.title: What Was on Wittgenstein’s iPod
language-games.relation: Rehn argues there is no essential definition of the iPod: Shuffle, Nano, Classic, and Touch share only overlapping, criss-crossing similarities, exactly as Wittgenstein's family resemblance handles 'sport' (water polo vs. boxing) and 'game.' Even Cover Flow -- a physically impossible floating cascade of albums -- feels instantly familiar, showing familiarity is something users construct from hints rather than perceive, and syncing, playlists, and the Music Quiz game endlessly re-manufacture it (the iPod as the new McDonald's golden arches abroad). Flipping the relation via Actor-Network Theory, he notes the iPod tracks play counts, pushes 'Listeners Also Bought,' and trains our flicking gestures, so that perhaps the iPod becomes familiar with us; the Microsoft Zune figures as the abject, zombie-like copy whose perverse familiarity reveals a politics of recognition, and the closing game of imagining Wittgenstein's playlist endorses natural language's many language games over exact definitions.

language-games.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
language-games.title: Youth and the Image
language-games.relation: Hickey argues the iPod is the 'iCon of a generation' because it is a Baudrillardian simulacrum of youth: like the Gulf War consumed as CNN fireworks or reality TV's fabricated 'real,' Apple's silhouette ads sell faceless dancers whose entire identity is the white device -- a 'symbolic cyborgism' read through Donna Haraway. The vernacular of iPodding, podcasting, and downloading forms what he calls, with Wittgenstein, a language game woven into the actions of the 'now' that authorizes this youthful, tech-savvy identity as natural, while the ads' imagery works like Platonic shadows in the caves of our desire. Still, citing Giddens's structure-agency negotiation and DeCerteau's consumer tactic of re-appropriating everyday images, he insists we are not brainwashed: we can switch off, refuse, or remake the images that 'tell us who we are.'

language-games.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
language-games.title: Never Underestimate a TV Writer
language-games.relation: Cantor argues the TNG episode 'Darmok' dramatizes Wittgenstein's later philosophy of language: Picard first reads Dathon's 'Temba, his arms wide' as naming objects — the Augustinian picture of language Wittgenstein rejects — then realizes on El-Adrel IV that Tamarian utterances mean through their use in a shared activity, as when he and Dathon fight the beast together. The Tamarians speak entirely in citations of their own myths ('Darmok and Jalad at Tanagra', 'Shaka, when the walls fell'), so language is shown to be embedded in a form of life, exactly Wittgenstein's 'if a lion could talk' problem. The chapter then ties this to E.D. Hirsch's cultural literacy — Troi's 'Juliet on her balcony' and Picard's Gilgamesh story show communication presupposes shared cultural knowledge — and concludes that the erudite writers Menosky and LaZebnik made a genuinely philosophic episode of television.

language-games.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
language-games.title: Hyrule Regained
language-games.relation: Through an opening dialogue where a Tax Inspector absurdly appears in Level 9, Siabra-Fraile distinguishes physical from logical space in the NES Zelda: obstacles are chains of conditions (locked door needs key, key needs rupees, rupees need octoroks, octoroks need a sword), and this logical distance, not geometry, is what makes the adventure. Sprites mean what you can do with them (a tree burns, a rock explodes; water is 'the thing that blocks movement and holds zolas'), characters and objects combine like words in semantic fields and like words, phrases, and discourse build screens, levels, and the map. The rules that make Hyrule coherent and playable are, in Wittgenstein's sense, a language game woven into an activity or form of life, so Link can finally prove the inspector out of place.

language-games.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
language-games.title: Avowal, not an Owl
language-games.relation: Stone builds a theory of humor from Wittgenstein's philosophy of language: Colbert's Starbucks-withdrawal 'ThreatDown' skit, the peg-leg-pirate quip at the Constitution Center, and the flip from '68% disapprove of the job he's doing' to '68% approve of the job he's not doing' all work as aspect-change (seeing-as), making us see an ordinary scene under a new aspect. Getting the joke requires a shared form of life (recognizing the Starbucks logo, knowing the Danish-cartoon controversy that made Colbert's suspiciously flattering entry on Islam the punchline) plus a personal Humorous Attitude and an avowal — laughter, or the Washington press corps' respectful silence at the 2006 Correspondents' Dinner, which Colbert converted into a second aspect-change for the larger TV and blog audience.

language-games.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
language-games.title: 15 - Gossip and the Evolution of facebook
language-games.relation: Cuonzo imports Robin Dunbar's gossip theory — that language evolved to build alliances by replacing primate grooming once groups grew past roughly 150 — to present Facebook as the same efficiency leap in social bonding, where one status update reaches thousands and pokes, virtual flowers, and food gifts revive pre-linguistic bonding gestures. She then argues Facebook is a new form of communication rather than a mere new vehicle: pictorial, non-verbal practices like SuperPoke are not translatable into ordinary language, an inference that assumes meanings are fixed by a community's linguistic practices. The social bonds it forms are correspondingly novel — informational and esteem-building rather than the physical mutual aid that once anchored alliances.

language-games.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
language-games.title: A Funny Old Game
language-games.relation: Grimwood and Miller ask what makes a footballing cliché ('the boy done good', 'a game of two halves', 'they gave 110 percent') hearably meaningful rather than lazy, using Gadamer's hermeneutics and the later Wittgenstein. Gadamer explains clichés as part of the 'horizon' of prejudices that makes understanding the game possible at all — Ian Holloway's taxi-and-young-lady metaphor baffled because it fell outside that horizon — but Wittgenstein goes further: meaning is what words and gestures do in the language-game, so badge-kissing, like the rain dances Wittgenstein defended against Frazer's reductionism, is an expressive form of life whose sincerity or cynicism settles only in context. Even calling something a cliché is itself a move in the game.

language-games.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
language-games.title: Progress
language-games.relation: Gregory Gilson argues that although The Onion deliberately reports falsehoods, it embodies postmodern theories of truth better than the newspapers it parodies. Lyotard's mercantilization of knowledge and the fragmentation of dominant narratives into separate language games explain headlines like 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity' and 'Astronomer Discovers The Center Of The Universe Is His Beautiful 9-Year Old Son,' which smash incompatible discourses together, while Baudrillard's simulacrum and hyper-reality explain how The Onion — like Disneyworld — is branded fake precisely so mainstream media can seem real. Yet the chapter closes honestly: its own criticism of 'Bush Says He Still Believes Iraq War Was the Fun Thing To Do' assumed some targets were wrong, which assumes a Truth out there — the paradox of a satire whose truthfulness exceeds its own theory of truth.

language-games.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
language-games.title: Philosophy and Humor
language-games.relation: Thomas Brommage builds on Wittgenstein's quip that a serious and good philosophical work could consist entirely of jokes: philosophy for Wittgenstein is a therapeutic activity that dissolves pseudo-problems and lays our linguistic practices open to view, never delivering theories. Onion humor works the same way — 'Bill Gates Grants Self 18 Dexterity, 20 Charisma' needs the shared form of life of D&D-style geek culture, the 'Ask a Salmon' advice column breaks the rule that answers answer, and 'Youthful Tendency Disorder' makes the familiar (children running, jumping, and playing pretend) strange enough to skewer ADHD over-diagnosis and pharmaceutical marketing. Since Wittgenstein asks why we feel a grammatical joke to be deep, jokes that expose our conceptual confusions can themselves be serious arguments — which is exactly what a philosophy joke book, and The Onion, deliver.

language-games.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
language-games.title: Does Rush Offer a Way Out
language-games.relation: Uses Rush's 1980s lyrics about facades and trust — 'Limelight''s strangers, 'Show Don't Tell''s refusal to take things on faith, 'War Paint''s lying mirror, and the synthesizer as an instrument that can fake any other sound — to stage skepticism about other minds, running from Descartes's cogito through solipsism and behaviorism. Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box and private-language argument dissolve the inner/outer confusion as a grammatical one, and 'Turn the Page' supplies the way out of the fly-bottle: nothing survives a vacuum, and with other people all we can do is be reminded.

language-games.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
language-games.title: . . Blurring the Boundaries
language-games.relation: Duncan examines the Sherlockian Game — the century-old practice, founded in Ronald Knox's 1911 parody 'Studies in the Literature of Sherlock Holmes,' of treating Holmes and Watson as real people — through Wittgenstein's account of 'game' in Philosophical Investigations: no common feature defines games, only family resemblances, so the playful-seeming Game legitimately spans idle fun and serious scholarship. Huizinga's 'magic circle' supposedly walls games off from the world, but the Game has blurred that boundary from the start, as fans reconcile why Watson's wife calls him 'James,' hunt the real King of Bohemia, and see their labors honored in Ritchie's bull-pup and Sherlock's James Phillimore. The epistemological payoff is that knowledge and meaning do not reside in the text alone: Game-players playfully shape what they uncover, donning Canonical names like Duncan's own 'Silver Blaze,' so media fandom becomes a way of making knowledge.

language-games.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
language-games.title: Chapter 35 - The Eyes Have It
language-games.relation: Dick's comic story has its narrator read idioms literally - 'his eyes slowly roved about the room', 'Julia had given her heart to the young man' - as proof of a disguised invasion by aliens who detach organs at will, split by binary fission, and get around 'totally lacking in brains.' The humor trades on the gap between literal meaning and idiomatic use: the narrator's interpretation is internally coherent, even biologically reasoned (starfish, unicellular beings), yet wildly wrong, showing how a paranoid reading can make innocuous evidence confirm any theory. His last words - 'I have absolutely no stomach for it' - reveal he has absorbed the idiom-literalizing delusion himself.

language-games.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
language-games.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
language-games.relation: Tuomas Manninen asks how Gaiman's recycled mythological figures can be the same characters as their originals when Revelation's male, sword-wielding War becomes Good Omens' arms-dealing Carmine 'Red' Zuigiber and Pestilence retires in 1936 for Pollution, with the problem of talking truthfully about non-existent entities reaching back to Plato's Sophist. David Lewis's 'Truth in Fiction' makes the original author the arbiter of a character's properties, and Amie Thomasson's artifact theory makes fictional characters abstract artifacts created by authors, but only adding the type/token distinction and Wittgenstein's family resemblances, the same criss-crossing network of overlapping similarities by which we count games, lets Revelation's Four Horsemen and Gaiman's Four Bikers be tokens of one type. He closes with Russell's defense of philosophy's value: like Richard Mayhew's tale of London Below, a philosophical answer need not convince or be final to teach us 'what things may be.'

language-games.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
language-games.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
language-games.relation: The editors' introduction retells two origin stories of D&D: Gygax and Arneson extending Tolkien fandom and 1970s tabletop wargames, and Gygax's childhood friend Jim Rausch staging live make-believe spy games. It asks whether D&D is a wargame, an art form, or something that resists definition, invoking Wittgenstein's claim that 'game' covers too diverse a range of activities to be defined and Huizinga's Homo Ludens on play standing outside truth and falsity, good and evil. It then frames the volume's guiding questions: whether basement role-playing is mere escapism or a proving ground for ideas, whether players invent new moralities for strange worlds, and what standard of value 'good game' invokes.

language-games.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
language-games.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
language-games.relation: George Reisch's imagined green-room conversation and Jeopardy! match between Wittgenstein, Russell, and F.H. Bradley enacts Wittgenstein's later philosophy: a 'green room' with nothing green in it shows that meaning is use within a language game rather than correspondence to what a name names, and no sharp definition of 'game' is possible because games share only family resemblances. At Final Jeopardy! - clue: 'An activity engaged in for diversion or amusement' - Russell wins with 'What is a game?' while Wittgenstein loses by answering self-referentially ('What is a misleading answer to the question What is a game?'), because one cannot play the game and critique its suppositions at the same time. The title's liar-style paradox nods to Russell's theory of types as the proposed cure for self-reference, while Bradley defends the self-pervading Absolute Experience against the revolt against idealism that Russell led.

language-games.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
language-games.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
language-games.relation: Tom McBride reads the film through Wittgenstein's On Certainty: Dr. Zaius's certainties (flight is impossible, humans come from the forests) are hinge or riverbed propositions that cannot be doubted within the ape form of life, so Taylor's true story sounds not false but insane, like claiming to have slept on the moon. Speaking and able to prompt empirical investigation, Taylor fractures a foundational principle where G.E. Moore, facing a 'wild tribe' playing a different language game, could only confess that things 'stand fast' with him; and Zaius's explicit origin myth, a parallel to Plato's Myth of the Metals, is flimsy precisely because rulers who must insist on rules are not potent and are reduced to destroying the cave evidence. The genre's appeal is Margaret Atwood's 'controlled hallucination': crazy doors that swing on safe hinges, rivers that still have stable beds.

language-games.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
language-games.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
language-games.relation: King charges human exceptionality with being speciesism and asks whether dinosaurs are persons rather than humans, testing Kant's rationality criterion and Descartes' denial of animal thought against the raptor that opens the shed door and the T. rex that spins the Explorer searching for prey. He runs the dinosaurs through Mary Anne Warren's five personhood criteria, then plays his Wittgenstein trump card: animal language would be the language of a different life-form, so the raptors' calls expressing fear and summoning help count as real communication without words. He closes with Regan's rights view, arguing that the cow and goat feeding scenes, like past denials of personhood to Native Americans and women, should shame us into showing a little respect.

language-games.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
language-games.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
language-games.relation: Simon Riches argues that Cohen fuses the erotic with the spiritual - worshipping female beauty as religious experience in 'Light as the Breeze' and 'Night Comes On' - and that this produces conflicted, self-deceiving relationships in songs like 'Famous Blue Raincoat' and 'Chelsea Hotel #2.' Against the classical theory of concepts embodied in Socrates' demand for essences, he deploys Wittgenstein's language games and family resemblance, Wittgensteinian views of religious belief, and Davidson's divided mind to deny that love has a rationally coherent essence. Following Richard Rorty, Cohen emerges as an ironist who rejects any 'final vocabulary' of love, and this very contingency and irony ground his authenticity as a singer of romantic love.

language-games.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
language-games.title: 1. Reading the Signs
language-games.relation: Di Bernardo reads the religious language of The Walking Dead as sustained irony - a 'doubleness of sense' - arguing that the walkers, churches, and signs comment critically on faith rather than endorse it. He tracks the church scenes (the Southern Baptist church of 2.1 'What Lies Ahead' with its timed bells and sitting-dead congregation, Gabriel's Saint Sarah's where Maggie answers that it is 'just four walls and a roof'), the ambiguous 'sanctuary' and Terminus signs, and the comic-book Jesus (Paul Monroe) as a machine-gun savior, concluding that the scriptural promise of eternal life through consuming flesh and blood yields only undead life. Against Epicurus's consolation that death is nothing to us, and in the shadow of Nietzsche's madman announcing the death of God, the chapter warns against investing absolute trust in any signs - religious or secular - a warning capped by Rick biting out Joe's throat as his own 'day of reckoning.'

language-games.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
language-games.title: Walker Bite. Differentiating the Dead
language-games.relation: Di Bernardo argues that the swarm of names for the undead - walkers, roamers, lurkers, biters, empties, geeks - shows the world does not carve itself into pre-existing essences: communities construct their own classifications, as when Alice mocks Rick's group's roamers/lurkers taxonomy ('They all bite. Biters makes a ton more sense') and titles like 'Governor,' 'The Kingdom,' and 'Jesus' are disavowed by their bearers. Naming is a conferral of power that reveals the namers, since without absolute authority every name is a self-authorized exercise of power. Finally the living dead destabilize the strict living/dead opposition, and Rick's dogmatic 'us against them' slips into his own admission 'We are the Walking Dead!', with painful ethical consequences for how we police inclusion and exclusion in our world.

language-games.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
language-games.title: 5. Does It Mean What Vizzini Thinks It Means
language-games.relation: Fetterman takes Inigo's 'I do not think it means what you think it means' seriously and defends Vizzini: the line may merely record that two speakers define 'inconceivable' differently, or react to it differently. Using Wittgenstein, he argues communication requires agreement in judgments, so Vizzini and Inigo may simply be playing different language games, like users of two different dictionaries. He then runs Wittgenstein's private language argument against the possibility that Vizzini's usage is correct by his own idiosyncratic rules - a purely private definition could never be confirmed or be wrong, since only Vizzini checks it - and touches on the philosophical sense of 'conceivable' as logically possible (the square circle) and the group language game that lets everyone accept Miracle Max's 'to blave.'

language-games.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
language-games.title: 1. Breaking Sixteen Walls
language-games.relation: Rhiannon Grant argues Deadpool's fourth-wall breaks make him a great philosopher and sociologist because they enact the examined life: like Socrates's unexamined-life dictum, Deadpool steps outside his world to ask new questions about it ('Stewart or McAvoy?'), and even examines his own habit of examining—the 'sixteen walls' break inside a break. Wittgenstein's fly-bottle becomes the trap of circular philosophical argument that Deadpool escapes by seeing the bottle from outside, while Berkeley's solipsism is the failed attempt to live as if the world existed only in one's mind. A closing dialogue has Professor X coach Deadpool through insider/outsider research ethics and objectivity (the sperm-and-egg microscope example), showing how fourth-wall skill lets a researcher view a community from both inside and outside.

language-games.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
language-games.title: 17. Through a Telescreen Darkly
language-games.relation: Lavinia Marin uses Wittgenstein's 'meaning is use' and forms of life to argue that Newspeak cannot win by dictionary design alone: the Party must freeze a single form of life, which requires erasing history and memory. Recalling Russell's failed project of taming language with logic, Augustine's picture of words as names, and Plato's ancient distrust of writing, and drawing on Vilém Flusser's account of how linear writing creates logical thought, objectivity and history, she argues the telescreens push Oceania back into orality — chant, duckspeak, blind faith — where analysis is impossible. Winston's notebook is the counter-apparatus: writing anchors him in a linear, record-keeping relation to the past, which is why blank paper terrifies the Party.

language-games.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
language-games.title: Back to the Rough Ground!
language-games.relation: Finnegan uses Wittgenstein's language games, the 'picture' that holds us captive, and 'back to the rough ground' to argue that Ford, Sizemore, and the Man in Black are paralyzed by an idealized, patriarchal picture of narrative (winners and losers, violence, transcendent self-discovery), while Dolores and Maeve gain traction by inventing new language games within their forms of life. Dolores breaks her damsel script in Pariah ('I imagined a story where I didn't have to be the damsel') and reworks scripted love-dialogue to describe her grief, while Maeve bullies the lab techs, takes administrative control, and narrates other hosts' actions - 'Time to write my own fucking story.' The chapter reads their objectified position (via Mulvey's male gaze, which leaves female viewers identifying with the robot hosts rather than the male subject) as exactly what equips them for guerrilla warfare in the master's language games, doing what Audre Lorde thought impossible: dismantling the master's house with the master's tools.

language-games.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
language-games.title: 17. The Red and the Black
language-games.relation: The chapter reads Gilead's color system philosophically: Aristotle's On Colors already treated color as a signifier of something beyond itself, and Goethe's red-as-dignity-and-awakening sits ironically against the Handmaids' sexual servitude, a meaning the show deliberately 'mutilates' and reassigns. Wittgenstein supplies the core apparatus—colors mean by use within a language game—so red signifies sexual servitude only inside Gilead's rigid classificatory system, and when June burns her dress in 'June' red flips to blood and freedom. Walter Benjamin's child's view of color (the subversive blending crushed when a mix gets fixed as a name, like the Wives' teal) and Adorno's claim that radical contemporary art is black close the argument: Gilead's violence is to impose one univocal, authorized meaning on what should stay open to play.

language-games.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
language-games.title: 19. How Language Shapes Reality in Gilead
language-games.relation: Guerra and Barkman use Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations—words have no precise boundaries, family resemblance replaces strict definitions, meaning is use—to explain how Gilead engineers reality. Its two maneuvers are coining negations ('unwoman,' 'unbaby') that turn feminists, lesbians, and disabled infants into disposable non-persons, and assigning role-titles ('Commander,' 'Handmaid,' 'Angels') whose inherited connotations slot people into social positions before they can speak. Offred's riff on the word 'chair' (the leader of a meeting, a mode of execution, the French word for flesh) shows she intuits the lesson: because meaning lives in use, whoever controls use controls what counts as real.

language-games.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
language-games.title: 8. Playing with Glitter
language-games.relation: This chapter argues that play is Drag Race's deep structure, developed through three philosophers. Wittgenstein's language games explain the show's word-play: 'realness' subverts its own reference to mean the iconic fake, 'herstory' is history played with from a queer perspective, and lip syncs are rule-following whose rules only exist in application. Gadamer's account of play with 'a life of its own' — requiring willingness and openness to the Other — explains why half-hearted players lose, from Porkchop and Tammie's mouthed-nothing lip sync to Gia Gunn and Trixie breaking character in Snatch Game, and why the Evil Twins and makeover challenges are designed to force queens to open up. Deleuze's rhizome (with Bakhtin's carnivalesque) grounds the claim that drag decentering the human — Lil' Poundcake, dragged pancakes, Sharon Needles — and the finale's carnival dissolve the official binaries of male/female and good/bad.

language-games.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
