He exposes the irony that most 'British' vegetables were themselves appropriated introductions, mirroring Kew's plant-hunting empire.

virtue-ethics.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
virtue-ethics.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
virtue-ethics.relation: Pam Sailors distinguishes two kinds of high-altitude climber: the goal-oriented 'summiteer,' who pursues the summit at all costs for self-affirmation and may neglect others, and the process-oriented 'mountaineer,' who seeks relationship with the mountain, attains self-transcendence, and feels moral responsibility for comrades. Drawing on J. S. Russell and Jonathan Simon, and on cases like the 2006 abandonment of David Sharp versus Dan Mazur giving up his summit to save Lincoln Hall, she argues both types find value in dangerous sport but that the mountaineer—exhibiting courage, compassion, and care—is the morally better person. She backs this with Reinhold Messner, Ed Viesturs, and Sherpa judgment that mountains are not conquered but simply allow, or do not allow, us to climb them.

virtue-ethics.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
virtue-ethics.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
virtue-ethics.relation: Agnafors asks whether free soloing is morally permissible, opening with soloists dropping ice chips into his coffee cup to show soloing is not purely private. He tests Locke's natural rights to life and liberty (concluding no act is truly private since rescues, taxpayers, and grieving families are affected), Aristotle's virtue ethics (worrying that habitual risk-taking forms a reckless character), and Bentham and Mill's consequentialism (Bill's confidence-boosting solo of Nutcracker versus Derek Hersey's fatal fall). He concludes no universal answer exists, offering one rule: the soloist must carefully weigh all these considerations beforehand.

virtue-ethics.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
virtue-ethics.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
virtue-ethics.relation: Baker dismisses common objections to tattoos (shallow individuality, permanence, ugliness) as aesthetic rather than moral, then uses Greco-Roman virtue ethics—quoting Seneca's Moral Epistles on the soul, the balanced psyche, and matching one's norms to one's motivations—to isolate her real target: the 'tough tattoo.' She argues that a badass or tough-guy tattoo appropriates an outlaw subculture's imagery and, per Seneca's warning that approving a little violence approves it all, cultivates a vicious rather than virtuous psyche. Recalling friends who bragged about beatings, she invokes Socratic self-examination ('know thyself') to test whether looking tough is an accurate or worthy self-representation.

virtue-ethics.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
virtue-ethics.title: SERIAL KILLERS
virtue-ethics.relation: Brophy puts Showtime's Dexter Morgan on 'ethical trial' before the reader-as-jury, applying four tests. Utilitarianism approves because killing killers maximizes happiness (the Ticking Time Bomb analogy); Kant's categorical imperative and even Kant's own endorsement of executing murderers cast Dexter as a 'just executioner' applying a dark golden rule; virtue theory finds Dexter progressing toward moderation and flourishing as a 'warrior' in his social role; and Rawls's veil of ignorance suggests one would consent to Dexter patrolling one's neighborhood. Brophy concludes Dexter is morally excusable, perhaps praiseworthy.

virtue-ethics.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
virtue-ethics.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
virtue-ethics.relation: Iyengar-tradition teacher Jeff Logan argues that yoga philosophy — mythology such as the warrior Virabhadra behind virabhadrasana and Hanuman behind hanumanasana — must be taught alongside asana, or practice becomes 'mere acrobatics.' Using the parking-lot and door-cutting anecdotes to show yamas like non-harm and selflessness ignored, and citing a childhood-diet study, he contends teachers should not preach the eight limbs but embed subliminal precepts in physical cues ('extend your legs straight and true'), so students come to live rather than merely know yoga's virtue ethics.

virtue-ethics.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
virtue-ethics.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
virtue-ethics.relation: Julinna Oxley argues that yoga ethics is best understood as an Aristotelian virtue ethic rather than a rule-set: the yamas and niyamas name character traits to cultivate, not commands (citing Iyengar that 'violence is a state of mind, not a diet'). Laying out virtue ethics' elements — habituation, the mean, practical reason, community — she derives two paramount 'yogic virtues,' mindfulness and self-discipline/self-improvement, that are relative to each practitioner and community, so no single diet or lifestyle (e.g., vegetarianism, teetotaling) is universally required for the virtuous yogi off the mat.

virtue-ethics.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
virtue-ethics.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
virtue-ethics.relation: Ethics professor Paul MacNeill argues ethics is intrinsic to yoga and knowable only through practice, not by mining texts — a Western reason-first bias that trivializes it. He shows the yamas and niyamas are counter-measures aimed at samadhi (paralleling how Aristotle's virtues aim at eudaimonia, though yoga subordinates reason), and that Vedanta's transcendent and Kashmir Shaivism's immanent metaphysics both function as instruments toward expanded awareness. From that dissolution of the separate self, he claims, compassion flows naturally, so Hatha yoga's asana and pranayama dissolve the ingrained bodily/mental habits that block ethical, equilibrium-born action.

virtue-ethics.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
virtue-ethics.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
virtue-ethics.relation: John Rowan and Patricia Hallen build an extended elevator metaphor for dating (Ann and Bob riding floors, pushing buttons to raise or lower intimacy, gravity pulling toward breakup) to capture Heraclitus's insight that a relationship is a reality in constant change, while invoking Plato to insist the conceptual reality of a relationship is as real as physical objects. They define dating as gauging the possibility of eventual commitment, cite Hume's canoe image for implicit communication of shared destination, and ground their strategies—be yourself, go slowly, communicate, befriend—in Aristotle's virtue ethics, treating honesty, courage, and loyalty as habits lying in the golden mean between deficiency and excess (e.g., the Look Who's Talking date who overshares is 'excessively honest').

virtue-ethics.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
virtue-ethics.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
virtue-ethics.relation: Joshua Heter mounts a virtue-theoretic case against being set up on blind dates, using Aristotle's notion of telos and the distinction between fleeting 'hot-fudge happiness' and eudaimonia, the flourishing of a well-lived life (illustrated by long-married Bill and Fran). He argues a 'guy's' function is achieved by exercising his whole nature, and dramatizes this with Zoo-bear versus Wild-bear: the zoo-fed bear has its hunger and safety met but cannot flourish because it never hunts or roams, just as matchmaking meets the romantic need while letting a man's 'social muscles' atrophy. Invoking Aristotle's philia (and Nussbaum on Aristotelian virtue), he concedes friends mean well but recommends they merely introduce people and let things progress naturally rather than force an 'unnatural' match.

virtue-ethics.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
virtue-ethics.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
virtue-ethics.relation: Aeon Skoble uses the characters to argue for Aristotelian virtue ethics over Kantian duty and utilitarian consequence, since right action flows from developed character and practical reason rather than rule-following. He reads Sam's loyalty and Aragorn's temperance as genuine virtue, Boromir as flawed-but-decent (undone by resentment and pride), and Smeagol's swift murder of Deagol as proof the Ring's corrupting power depends partly on prior character. Skoble contends Kant's rules would make Sam's loyalty no better than a Ringwraith's, and utilitarianism's demand for foreknowledge suits only Galadriel, so virtue ethics best fits Tolkien's flawed, developing heroes.

virtue-ethics.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
virtue-ethics.title: It’s Not That Simple
virtue-ethics.relation: O'Mathuna uses 24's Jack Bauer to stage the ethics of torture through the "ticking bomb" argument. He frames it with deontology (torture treats persons as mere means), utilitarianism (Shue's ticking-bomb calculus, Mike Novick's "a few may die to save millions"), and virtue ethics (what torture does to Jack and Agent Burke). Marshalling the UN Convention, evidence that torture usually fails (Jack endures Chinese torture; Fayed is tricked, not broken), and its spread to innocents like Audrey Raines, he concludes the sanitized fictional case misrepresents torture's real degradation.

virtue-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
virtue-ethics.title: 3. Star Trek as Philosophy Spock as Stoic Sage
virtue-ethics.relation: Pigliucci argues that Gene Roddenberry built an implicit argument for Stoicism into Star Trek's Spock, contra both the 'suppressed emotion / stiff upper lip' caricature and Farren's claim that Kirk is the truer Stoic. Reading Spock's talk of 'emotion' as the disruptive pathe and his 'logic' as the broad Stoic study of reason, he shows Spock embodying the dichotomy of control ('my legs, they're broken'), the four cardinal virtues, and Stoic cosmopolitanism aboard the Enterprise. Drawing on Brouwer's account of the sage, he tracks Spock's development from prokopton toward sagehood, cultivating eupatheiai like love and friendship (the Wrath of Khan sacrifice) and declaring 'logic is the beginning of wisdom, not the end.'

virtue-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
virtue-ethics.title: 27. Squid Game as Philosophy The Myths of Democracy
virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter argues that Squid Game exposes five 'myths' of democracy by showing how its trappings mask control by the wealthy few. Using Aristotle's Politics and Nicomachean Ethics it attacks the myth of free choice (the players' consent is coerced by debt) and the failure to cultivate virtue and transparency (Gi-hun deceives Il-nam in the marble game); it uses Sen and Nussbaum's capability approach to deny genuine empowerment; and it applies Plato's Phaedo two-worlds doctrine to argue the game instantiates no true form of truth, beauty, goodness, or justice. Il-nam's tie-breaking vote and Player 111's advantages illustrate that equality is only superficial, leaving a Hobbesian war of all against all inside a democratic shell.

virtue-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
virtue-ethics.title: 39. Harry Potter as Philosophy Five Types of Friendship
virtue-ethics.relation: Okapal uses the Harry Potter films to expand Aristotle's theory of philia (friendship/love), which recognizes friendships for virtue, pleasure, and utility grounded in other-regarding concern, intimacy, choice, and a surrounding community. He argues the films show that friendships for pleasure and utility each come in beneficent and maleficent forms distinguished by whether motivations are other-regarding or purely self-regarding: the Quidditch team and the Harry-Ginny romance are beneficent pleasure-friendships (Ginny hides the Prince's book out of concern for Harry), while the Hermione-McLaggen date and Ron-Lavender fling are maleficent and short-lived. Slughorn's Slug Club is a beneficent utility-friendship of mutual advantage one may freely leave, whereas Voldemort's Death Eaters are maleficent, with all benefit flowing one way and no exit, yielding five types of friendship and locating Gryffindor's courage, inclusiveness, and loyalty as the ground of virtuous friendship.

virtue-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
virtue-ethics.title: 65. Louis CK as Philosopher The King and His Fall
virtue-ethics.relation: Marra Henrigillis first shows CK as 'philosopher king of comedy'—his cell-phone/'forever empty' bit echoing Buddhist and Stoic teaching on sitting with suffering, his 'why?' bit echoing Quine on not ontologizing, his 'So Did The Fat Lady' episode exposing how society denies fat women full humanity—then uses his 2017 misconduct scandal to stage competing verdicts: the feminist case for banning him (rape culture, power dynamics), Plato on censoring vicious art, Mill's four-part defense of free expression and Nozick's free-market/entitlement view against cancellation, and Aristotle's virtue ethics (character judged over a whole life) plus Pompa's prison-education view that no one is only their worst act.

virtue-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
virtue-ethics.title: 82. Planescape Torment as Philosophy Regret Can Change the Nature of a Man
virtue-ethics.relation: Gubka argues that Planescape: Torment answers Ravel's riddle 'What can change the nature of a man?' with 'regret,' read through Aristotle's claim that virtues are developed by habitually practicing virtuous action. The Nameless One's regret over betraying Deionarra and over the innocents killed to sustain his immortality motivates redemptive acts—apologizing to Deionarra, surrendering his immortality—shifting his alignment toward Good. The chapter rebuts Hobbes's Psychological Egoism (TNO's genuinely altruistic self-sacrifice) and Spinoza's warning that regret only doubles misery, arguing instead that apt regret is a golden-mean virtue between remorselessness and self-condemnation whose very painfulness makes it motivating.

virtue-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
virtue-ethics.title: 94. Yes, Roya and Philosophy The Art of Submission
virtue-ethics.relation: Goldberg, Gavaler, and Chavez use Trotman and Denich's Yes, Roya—where Roya dominates Joe and Wylie professionally (publishing under Joe's name) and sexually, all consensually—to ask how the three major Western ethical theories can accommodate consensual dominant/submissive relationships. They argue Aristotle's virtue ethics handles them via unequal friendships (submissives depending more, within a mean), Kant's Formula of Universal Law permits them once consent is built into the maxim (aligning with the Formula of Humanity), and Mill's utilitarianism sanctions them because justice and felt safety, grounded in consent, follow from the Greatest Happiness Principle.

virtue-ethics.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
virtue-ethics.title: 4. The Good of the Doctor
virtue-ethics.relation: The chapter distinguishes aesthetic 'good' (taste, beauty of the Daleks) from ethical 'good,' then tests the Doctor against the major moral theories: utilitarianism (rejected when Sarah Jane urges exterminating the Daleks in 'Genesis of the Daleks'), Kantian duty ethics (the Doctor's 'never met anyone who wasn't important' and attempts to save Davros and the Master), virtue ethics (the Eleventh Doctor guarding Christmas in 'The Time of the Doctor'), and feminist care ethics. Concluding that none quite fits because the Doctor values non-rational beings and feels compassion, the author proposes the Doctor follows Wolterstorff's 'ethic of need'—justice as meeting the needs of all—consistent with 'getting in the thick of things' as a flâneur.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Elaine, Kramer, and Newman Not Wise
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Aeon Skoble argues Seinfeld explicates Aristotelian virtue ethics against utilitarian and Kantian rivals: Jerry's 'I don't want to be an orgy guy' and George's fear of becoming 'one of those guys' ask what sort of person to be, not which rule to follow. George's 'do the opposite' in 'The Opposite' is an update of the Delphic oracle - only he who recognizes his own idiocy (Socratic ignorance) can act well, with Jerry deducing the logic and serving as his phronemos, alongside Superman. Elaine's rule-worship and Jujyfruits utilitarianism backfire, Kramer lacks the social dialectic virtue needs, and the ironic appeals to Newman as arbiter expose the paradox that choosing a role model wisely already requires the wisdom one lacks.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 1 - Homer and Aristotle
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Raja Halwani evaluates Homer against Aristotle's four character types (virtuous, continent, incontinent, vicious), arguing Homer is not virtuous and is genuinely vicious in the domain of food and drink (eating Frank Grimes's marked sandwich, the 64 slices of American cheese), while shuttling between continence and incontinence elsewhere. He catalogues Homer's lack of practical wisdom (phronesis) through gaffes like inferring the Bear Patrol works because there are no bears, and his lack of genuine friendship since he has only drinking buddies. Homer is judged neither malicious nor wholly vicious, so we pity him for his Springfield upbringing and the Simpson gene, and the chapter closes by crediting his 'in-your-face humanity'—his unregulated 'love of life'—as an admirable but dangerous ethical trait that does not make him an admirable person.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Aeon Skoble uses Tolkien's characters to defend Aristotelian virtue ethics against Kantian and utilitarian rivals. Sam's loyalty is a virtue because critically directed at a worthy friend while Wormtongue's loyalty to Saruman is not; Sméagol's instant murder of Déagol reveals prior vice that let the Ring corrupt him quickly, whereas Bilbo resists it for sixty years; Aragorn's temperance and teachableness contrast Boromir's resentment and pride. Working through Aristotle's doctrine of the mean (courage between cowardice and rashness), practical wisdom, and the phronemos as role model, he argues that rule-following cannot capture moral perception (do we owe truth to Black Riders?) and that utilitarianism absurdly requires Galadriel's foresight.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Jonathan Sanford distinguishes necessity of the end, of compulsion, and of nature to argue Christ's passion was both necessary and free: justice requires reparation for the harmony Adam and Eve broke, God cannot simply waive it without making a mockery of sin, yet no compulsion operates on Christ — unlike the blind inner drives Nietzsche's will to power or Schopenhauer's will would represent. Using Aristotle, he argues Christ's fully virtuous character (practical wisdom plus courage and temperance become a 'second nature') makes disobedience nearly unimaginable, and his divinity makes it impossible, so his choice 'could not have been different' precisely because it was perfectly free; the Gethsemane agony shows not division in the God-man but the difficulty of holding his human and divine wills in unity.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Daredevil’s Faith as a Source of Strength
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Testing whether Daredevil's fearlessness is really the vice of rashness, Morris invokes Aristotle's doctrine that every virtue is a mean between two vices, with courage between cowardice and foolhardiness - but since fear is not the only brake on recklessness, prudence can do that work instead, as when Matt calmly backs down from Iron Man's federal authority in Born Again. He concludes that the religious values Matt absorbed - love of neighbor, respect for truth, concern for justice - supply exactly the guidance prudence needs, making faith a distinct form of spiritual strength.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Foreword
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Cornel West argues that Plato's dialogues invented philosophy as a Socratic genre of cross-examination and bold frank speech (parrhesia) about ordinary life, and that hip-hop music - like the spirituals, blues, and jazz - enacts that same parrhesia against conventional morality and entrenched power. He claims reading hip hop philosophically demands metaphilosophical subtlety, showing how paideia, phronesis, and parrhesia operate in the work of cultural producers under free-market fundamentalism and authoritarianism. Because the racial dimension of hip hop is inescapable, he says philosophers must break their discipline's silence on race and music (neglected figures like Du Bois and Alain Locke alongside Aristotle, Kant, and Rorty), closing with Cicero's Socrates who turned philosophy from the heavens to earth and William James's pragmatism that took it from the academy to the streets.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Poker and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Young reads David Sklansky's fundamental theorem of poker — play as if you could see all the cards — through Aristotle and Husserl. Aristotle's phronesis and virtue-as-habituation explain how excellent players come to perceive the particulars (pot odds, opponent tendencies, the best possible hand) and stay unharmed even when losing with the best play, while Husserl's Cartesian Meditations, translated hand-by-hand into poker terms, supply analogical appresentation for knowing the other minds seated across the table. Chris Moneymaker's 2003 'Bluff of the Century' all-in with nothing against Sammy Farha shows how bluffing randomizes play and lets you shape the truth you seek, until a slow-played quad aces ends the night in Socratic humility about the limits of knowledge.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: “Hey, Let’s Get the Stuff We Need!” Putting the Mall in Its Place
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Matthew Walker reads Dawn of the Dead through Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics and Politics: the survivors' mall orgy curdles into boredom ('What have we done to ourselves?'), illustrating pleonexia, the graspingness for more than one's share of the goods of fortune that Aristotle roots in an unlimited desire for mere living - which may even explain why Romero's dead return, grasping from beyond the grave for more un-death. Aristotle's dismissal of the life of enjoyment as fit for cattle, his account of eudaimonia as the life in which our rational capacities flourish, and his defense of acquisition bounded by the good life explain why unlimited consumption zombifies the living, and why Peter and Fran must finally leave the mall empty-handed.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents - rational by Aristotle's standard of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgments about evildoers tasting better) and free despite their blood-craving, since craving is a strong preference, not the compulsion of the heroin addict or the castaway drinking seawater. Since animal blood is a viable alternative (Louis's rats, Angel and Spike's butcher's blood), the justifications for drinking human blood - taste, reaching full potential, spiritual peace - all fail against the principle that a world with less unnecessary suffering is better. Then the consistency argument turns on us: factory-farmed meat inflicts unnecessary suffering for the sake of taste while vegetarianism is fully viable, so condemning vampires while eating chicken is inconsistent - we as human beings are vampiric.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: James Bond and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Taliaferro and Le Gall rebut Paul Johnson's 1958 charge that Doctor No combines 'the sadism of a schoolboy bully', adolescent sex longings, and suburban snobbery. They show Bond kills for justice rather than spite (his reluctant assignment against von Hammerstein in 'For Your Eyes Only'), that Colonel Sun repudiates de Sadean torture before dying, and that the disturbing 'semi-rape' passage of The Spy Who Loved Me reflects Vivienne Michel's voice, not Bond's conduct. They read Bond's eros as an ironic use of the medieval courtly-love and Mariology tradition in which sex redeems 'lost women' like Pussy Galore, defend his dress and manners through the ancient heroic tradition (Theseus's fatal neglect of the white sails, Leonidas combing his beard at Thermopylae), and conclude Bond is a chivalric, comic hero - a 'delightful impossibility' in Aristotle's Poetics' sense who embodies Socratic soldierly virtue and Platonic optimism.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Lessons Learned
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: McAleer maps The Office onto Aristotle's ethics: David Brent is the buffoon who is 'the slave of his sense of humor,' Gareth the literalist boor who cannot take a joke, and Tim the ready wit whose irony responds to the situation — together illustrating that a virtue is a qualitative mean of acting and feeling appropriately, fixed by practical wisdom rather than rules. That humor cannot be codified mirrors the uncodifiability of Aristotelian ethics, and wit's very status as a virtue shows Aristotle's morality is broader than modern duty-and-outcome ethics: it aims at the flourishing (eudaimonia) of the whole person.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Dorothy Growing Up in the Land of Oz
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: McCall and Auxier use Aristotle's virtue ethics to unpack the Wizard's claim to be 'a good man but a bad wizard' and to argue that no external token—the diploma, heart watch, or medal—can confer virtue, which is cultivated only through practice and experience. Each companion lacks something specific: the Scarecrow the intellectual virtues and phronesis, the Tin Man the feelings and stable states of character that regulate emotion, the Lion the sophrosyne that balances thinking and feeling into courage as the mean between recklessness and cowardice. Aristotle's three grades of friendship (utility, pleasure, virtue) frame the companions' bond with Dorothy, and MacIntyre's account of virtues internal to practices explains why the Wizard's public recognition still matters. Dorothy herself begins as the child Aristotle says cannot yet be virtuous—fleeing Miss Gulch in Kansas—but by defending Toto against the Lion and leading the quest she grows into a responsible moral agent, which is what her delayed homecoming requires.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Transformers and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Plauche grounds Optimus Prime's line 'Freedom is the right of all sentient beings' in 'Aristotelian liberalism': since Energon, like our food, is scarce and requires labor and creativity, any volitional artificial life needs a moral code whose standard is flourishing (following Foot's natural goodness), cultivating intellectual and moral virtues from prudence, independence, and honesty to benevolence and courage. Ricardo and Mises's law of association - illustrated by Ratchet and a human mechanic both profiting from specialization despite Ratchet's absolute superiority - plus the ruinous cost of war give even superior aliens reason to respect our rights to life, liberty, and property rather than enslave or exterminate us, as Megatron would.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Tie Goes to the Runner
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: St. Martin runs the Fenway 'pink hat' controversy through Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: the virtuous fan is the mean between the deficient bandwagoner who waves at NESN cameras mid-pitch and the excessive diehard who memorizes Dice-K's ERA to belittle others. Terry Francona's courage in sending Dave Roberts in the 2004 ALCS (versus a reckless Ortiz steal attempt) illustrates virtue as the mean between cowardice and foolhardiness, and Aristotle's contrast between the love of honor and the love of contemplation shows both pink hatters and stats-obsessed diehards err by making fandom about themselves. She concludes that accepting fans in any color hat is the truly virtuous mean.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents because they meet Aristotle's test of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgment that 'evildoers... taste better') and retain free will, since their blood-lust is a craving not a compulsion and Louis's rat diet in Interview with the Vampire, like Angel's in Buffy, proves an alternative exists. TASTE, full potential, and spiritual peace all fail to justify human blood, because killing a person brings more unnecessary suffering than killing a rat, the same suffering-based principle that condemns factory farming. The 'cold clammy consistency' punchline: since humans need not eat meat, condemning vampire blood-drinkers while dining on chicken, pork, and beef is hypocrisy, because we are vampiric too and only our choice of which life to ingest separates the monstrous from the virtuous.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Final Whistle
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Andrew Lambert defends the rationality of being a football fan by updating Aristotle: living well in a liberal consumer democracy demands an accessible source of beauty, catharsis, belonging, public discourse, and altruism, and fandom trains exactly these sensibilities — from his childhood prayers for Everton to the 1914 Christmas Truce match and supporters' trusts that own clubs like Exeter City. The mature 'fan of football' takes an ironic view of the 'loyal fan's' tribal passions, gaining the practical wisdom that keeps rivalry (the Liverpool–Everton derby, the 1969 'Football War') from curdling into violence. Fandom thus answers critics who dismiss it as consumerist escapism or bad faith.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Jousting for Virtue
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Farrell argues that the medieval code of chivalry is a living case study for Aristotle's virtue ethics: Lancelot, 'mekest in hall and sternest to his foe', embodies the paradox C.S. Lewis names as meek and fierce 'to the nth', which Farrell reads as Aristotle's courage, the golden mean between cowardice and rashness, exercised 'to the right extent, at the right time, with the right motive'. The joust, meanwhile, was a proving ground where knightly virtues became second nature through habituated practice, since as Aristotle says 'it is no easy task to be good'. Western martial arts, he concludes, are 'moral kung fu': a fencing match with one's own standards of virtue.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: World Death Rate Holding Steady At 100 Percent
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Dan Miori, a palliative-care physician assistant, uses Onion medical stories — 'Loved Ones Recall Local Man's Cowardly Battle With Cancer,' the 'Vehicular Manslaughter Doctor,' animal hoarder Tricia McCory's 'I'm A Diseased And Deformed Animal Lover,' and the Terry Schiavo American Voices — to survey how end-of-life decisions actually get made. He runs each dilemma through Mill's consequentialism, Kant's deontology, and Aristotle's virtue ethics (with Monty Python's Philosopher's Song as running gag), then through Beauchamp and Childress's four principles of medical ethics, showing that McCory's kindness to dying animals fails autonomy and nonmaleficence because kindness can be cruel. The chapter closes by restoring 'euthanasia' to its Greek meaning of 'good death,' arguing that accepting the 100 percent death rate means planning ahead with living wills and honest bad-news delivery rather than dying tube-filled in an ICU.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The End of the Story
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Reads the Gom Jabbar test as Herbert's definition of humanity: Paul endures Mohiam's pain box because a human stays in the trap to turn it on the trapper and protect the species, while an animal only chews off its own leg. The Butlerian Jihad's ban on 'a machine in the likeness of a man's mind' is applied to our own iPod-and-PDA dependence, with Mentat Thufir Hawat showing that losing the machine-crutch 'forced human minds to develop,' in line with Aristotle's phronesis and the politics of the common good (and Plato's contemplation as the core of happiness). The chapter closes by turning the human/animal test on the modern West—Baron Harkonnen-like consumers whose water-hungry beef habit makes us the trap of our own environmental collapse.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Spice of Meaning
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Mines Dune for an account of the meaningful life by contrasting the Harkonnens, who amass power for its own sake and grind Yueh's very identity to dust, with the Fremen, whose rigid rituals give meaning but suffocate anyone who lives entirely inside them—with Duke Leto's abolition of the beggars' water-towel custom as the failure case in between. Following Aristotle's method of starting from 'the views of the wise,' the chapter argues virtue is an open-ended, formulaless skill: rising above inherited identities while repairing the social bonds they sustain, as Paul and Jessica do by breaking selected Fremen rules and leaving the sietch stronger. The worm-rider, feet shifting on sand above a creature that can never be fully controlled, is the closing image of a struggle that never finally resolves.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Yours Is Superior, therefore I Concede to You
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Adam Barkman evaluates King Neptune's kingship through Dante's De Monarchia: kingship is God-ordained, justice means treating each being according to its nature, and a true king is a servant-leader who must possess the four cardinal virtues and three theological ones. Neptune ('I'm the king. That's what I do', before executing a crown polisher and smiting at every problem) has courage but lacks prudence and temperance; Triton has prudence without courage; and levelheaded Mindy would be the best ruler, though Dante's tradition would disqualify her because she is female. The chapter concludes neither Neptune nor Triton has enough virtue or political knowledge to be a good king, and reform rather than deposition is the Dantean answer.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: A Rolling Stone Gathers . . . Happiness
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Brings in Epicurus, speaking through Cicero, to correct the Cyrenaics: pursue pleasure rationally, declining pleasures that purchase greater later pains—Keith's drug-related legal bills, 'Sister Morphine's' desperation—and sometimes enduring pain for greater pleasure later, like kicking junk to enjoy raising children. Advocating simple living, a hierarchy of pleasures ranked by sober reasoning, and prudence (phronesis) as the chief virtue, it pictures modern Epicureans at a rock festival passing out condoms and running the needle exchange.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Jonas-Sebastien Beaudry reads Neverwhere's magic invisibility as a model of real social invisibility: after Richard helps the injured Door he loses his job, his fiancee Jessica, and even the ability to be perceived, joining the homeless, slaves, and Jews under Nazism as people excluded from the moral community whose needs no longer register. Using Arendt's banality of evil to explain everyday indifference and Richard Rorty on torturers who fail to see a 'real' human, he distinguishes radical from partial invisibility, shown in Jessica stepping over the bleeding Door and misreading her need as 'sleep it off.' The remedy is Iris Murdoch's 'loving gaze' of just and careful attention, which seizes Richard before he can rationalize, backed by a practical wisdom about whose needs matter, so that acknowledging the invisible, down to apologizing to a rat in London Below, is what makes both them and us better.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Barkman takes Andrea's mermaid-necklace question ('I don't think those rules apply any more') as a test of natural law: self-evident principles — general beneficence (Glenn's 'shit creek' rescue, Morgan's warning that it 'takes away a piece of your soul'), special beneficence toward family (Lori's 'Don't be so trusting,' Morales's 'best for my family'), and piety (Guillermo staying with the abandoned elders) — still bind after the state's collapse, while 'do not steal' is merely derived, so the unowned necklace is fair game and Rick could take some but not most of Andrea's food. Aristotle's practical wisdom resolves the cannibal hunters' collision between preserving their lives and not killing innocents — starving is the morally preferable choice — since virtue weighs principles 'all things considered.' Against Carol's 'we can make new rules' relativism the natural law outlives governments, and Father Gabriel errs by calling walkers 'abominations,' conflating bad (dysfunctional) with evil (willful) — whereas the Governor, who knowingly ignores the moral law, reduces himself to walker level.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Merli argues that good role-playing refutes Aristotelian virtue ethics: decent players convincingly play genuinely evil thieves and morally mediocre players play truly virtuous paladins, so the skill of judging what the virtuous agent would do cannot require being virtuous or having the habituated emotions McDowell, Hursthouse, and Jacobson say are necessary to 'see what to do'. Using a dice-guessing versus unverifiable aura-reading analogy, he shows that the virtue ethicist's escape—denying non-virtuous players can get it right—makes virtuous judgment look fraudulent and untestable. Because role-playing demands active first-person deliberation rather than the passive reception of literary fiction, it exposes that judging rightly and being virtuous are distinct skills, with implications for how habituation and moral education work.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Wire and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: McAleer ranks three Season-long deceptions - Sobotka's smuggling least wrong, McNulty's fake serial killer worse, Templeton's fabricated Sun stories worst - and argues that only the agents' motives and character explain the degrees of wrongness, against Mill's claim that motive has nothing to do with an action's morality and Kant's distinction between acting in accordance with and from duty. Aristotle's virtue ethics and his difference between practical wisdom and mere cleverness vindicate these verdicts: Sobotka lies to save a dying union, McNulty's cleverness is corrupted by his need to be the smartest boy in the room while Lester's additions lack all wisdom, and Templeton lies from naked careerism with no redemption arc. The chapter closes with the 'Haynes Principle' - 'you need a lot of context to seriously examine anything' - as the case for a messier, character-based moral philosophy.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Wire and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Grinnell reads Rawls's dotted case lists, Marimow's rip-and-run, Burrell's 'dope on the table,' and Prez being told he teaches the test rather than math as Aristotle's function argument gone wrong: professionals who reduce their purpose to stats and pleasing bosses are 'doing well' instead of 'doing good,' which is just what Plato says badly governed cities reward with honor. The characters who grasp their real function - Daniels refusing cheap felony stats, Bunk refusing to turn cases black without the true murderer, Freamon hunting bodies in vacants despite Landsman's fury - defy the Game at career cost, while Colvin's Hamsterdam and McNulty's fake killer show the opposite failure of zealous judgment without humility or rule of law. The chapter ends on the paradox that trusting professional judgment risks messes, but defining professions by numbers eliminates excellence altogether.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Re-examining 'The Enchiridion!' trial by trial - the gnome illusions, the ogre whose dollar Finn steals and then returns, the dark mage's brain world, the wallop given the Key-per in devil pajamas - the chapter argues Finn wins the hero's handbook without being righteous: he is brave, tender and ingenious, but gullible, hasty and violent, slaying whatever he is told is evil and running from the gnome test. Epictetus's Stoic Enchiridion supplies the standard the show's book lacks: only virtue matters, wealth, fame and comfort are indifferents, and a real handbook teaches how to lose, age and admit mistakes, not just how to win, which is exactly what Billy's quit-heroism shows Ooo's greatest hero never learned. Because bravery without good judgment could as easily serve a Nazi, a terrorist or the Lich, Finn's lack of practical wisdom means the 'most righteous hero' in Ooo is an impetuous boy - proof of how morally broken the Land of Ooo is.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: The chapter argues Finn is not yet a true hero but is on a quest to become one: against rule systems like Mill's greatest-happiness utilitarianism and Kantian respect for persons, virtue ethics asks not 'what should I do' but 'who should I be', and Aristotle's point that children lack fully developed practical reason explains why Finn's good intentions misfire - removing Donny exposes the house people to Why-wolves, and Penny's trick humiliates him in the City of Thieves. Martha Nussbaum's ideal of every person as free and of equal dignity grounds heroism in the common good, and her work on literature and popular culture explains how watching Finn's exaggerated choices trains our own moral judgment. Citing Franco and Zimbardo's psychology of real heroes - empathy, risk tolerance, persistence - and closing with Seneca's 'how nobly you live', it concludes that since Aristotelian virtue is a habit, anyone can start by admitting they suck at heroism and practicing, as Jake's advice puts it.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Reading Finn's first season as a three-stage hero's journey - winning the Enchiridion on Mount Cragdor, being tested in 'Business Time', 'City of Thieves', 'Ocean of Fear' and 'Henchman', then doubly confirmed when Billy recognizes him - the chapter extracts a working handbook of heroism from his stumbles. Its lessons: heroism needs reason as much as courage (thinking through the gnome 'illusions', knocking himself unconscious to beat the Fear Feaster), plain luck plays a real and uneven part in saving Jake from the ogre, retribution should be temporary (the ogre's returned dollar), and heroes must check their sources (Penny's con). The deepest tension is that justice and compassion, instinct and reason, violence and non-violence must be perpetually balanced - Billy's nonviolent way becomes its own injustice when Finn medicates villagers without consent - so a real hero is simply someone who never stops trying to hold the balance.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Meyer reads Jobs through 'individualistic perfectionism'—the Aristotelian tradition (via Rasmussen and Den Uyl, and Veatch) on which flourishing is objective to human nature yet agent-relative, an endless striving unique to each person's talents rather than Kant's by-the-book categorical imperative applied impersonally to all. Jobs embodied this: the 'bicycle of the mind' faith that reason and tools extend human efficiency, practical wisdom weighing goods like friendship, health, and art through Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, experimental self-discovery (Zen, calligraphy, fruitarian diets), and the exile-to-NeXT-to-Pixar-to-iMac arc of constant re-evaluation—so the right question is not whether Jobs 'was' a moral perfectionist but whether each of us keeps striving in our own key.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Adam Henschke argues that Frank Reynolds, of all people, is a role model - not a virtuous man overall, but virtuous in one structural sense. Using Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, each Gang member's project is diagnosed as the vice of excessive self-delusion: Charlie's Waitress obsession he cannot see through even at her musical rejection, Dee's acting stardom she will not work for and that ends in suicide-adjacent despair, Mac's muscle-bound self-image despite 'diabitis', and Dennis's Golden God delusion culminating in 'the implication' and his car stash of 'fetish shit'. Rickety Cricket embodies the opposite vice, total loss of the capacity to imagine oneself otherwise (via Catriona Mackenzie's relational autonomy), and Frank charts the Aristotelian mean between the two - he rejected his delusive country-club life, knows exactly what he chose with Roxy, and his plans succeed where the Gang's fail - making 'What would Frank do?' a genuine exercise of practical wisdom.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 14. Re Production
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Framed as leaked Project memoranda, the chapter argues Projects Leda and Castor embody philosophy's male-rational/female-reproductive dichotomy: Aristotle's function argument defined the human good (eudaimonia) through rationality while relegating women to reproduction, and the clones' engineered diseases literalize the split — fatal illness of the reproductive organs in the Leda clones, of the brain in the Castor. Simone de Beauvoir's Second Sex supplies the critique: "woman" treated as synonymous with womb, the Other denied the rich self-definition granted men, visible in Leda's passive unmonitored clones versus Castor's self-aware, active brothers. Combining a redeemed Aristotle (practical wisdom shows virtuous potential is not set by biological sex) with Beauvoir's free, independent woman, the chapter concludes both reproductive and rational autonomy must be restored to the clones of both sexes.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 10. Virtue Rising
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Darci Doll argues the Rising exposes the Society's intellectual oppression—each Color denied education and fed 'noble lies' about its role—and that lifting it sparks an 'Intellectual Reformation' proving Color does not dictate potential: Darrow out-performing Golds, Orion the un-carved Blue, Ragnar and Sefi exceeding their station. She uses Plato's Republic (producers, auxiliaries, guardians, the lower orders kept obedient by Noble Lies like the Reds' terraforming myth) as the Society's blueprint, then turns to Aristotle: potential is realized only through the right environment, instruction, and habituated character, and Darrow's practical wisdom—testing himself, reassessing after Titus and Cassius, doing what makes him his best self—lets him flourish and lead. Aristotle's critique of utility-only relations explains why the Society's alliances expire (Antonia executed once useless) while Darrow and Mustang's virtue friendships and just rule endure, opening a society where everyone, including women and lowColors denied opportunity rather than ability, can maximize potential.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 30. Trying to Do Good with Arya, Tyrion, and the Hound
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Thomas sets Aristotle's practical wisdom against Bentham's utility calculus and Kant's consequence-proof rules, then watches all three struggle in season six. Arya's merciful refusal to poison Lady Crane backfires when the Waif kills her more painfully anyway; Tyrion's compromise with the Masters - phasing out slavery gradually, 'I trust their self-interest' - nearly loses Meereen when they attack by sea; and the resurrected Hound, after Brother Ray's massacre, concludes that 'lots of horrible shit in this world gets done for something larger than ourselves,' so being good in Westeros, as everywhere, means choosing without being able to know the consequences in advance.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 15. Reset Virtues
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Doll argues Elliot approximates Aristotelian virtue despite his vices: he craves eudaimonia, uses practical wisdom to recognize the harm the 5/9 hack caused innocent people ('I'll own it all'), and habituates himself against vice by confessing, exposing Ray's website, and restraining Mr. Robot even at the cost of Adderall binges and prison. Leon's 'existence could be beautiful, or it could be ugly, but that's on you' frames the choice of a life to fight for, and Krista's counsel leads Elliot to the golden mean of a 'handshake' with Mr. Robot - integrating the two identities rather than annihilating one - while the viewer serves as the if/then programming keeping him virtuous.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 5. Why the Good Man Is a Great Leader
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Nisley reads Civil War through Aristotle's good man and good leader: Cap shows courage but lacks temperance and practical wisdom - his rash Lagos operation, his rage-borne beating of Tony, his choice of Bucky over the Avengers' common end - and his ceaseless struggle between passion and reason falls short of virtue. Applying Aristotle's account of philia, she argues the Avengers are a friendship of the virtuous that requires deliberation toward justice, which Cap dissolves by tearing the team apart, while Tony's reasoned acceptance of UN oversight, moderation after Ultron, and concern for the whole team make him the good man fit to lead.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 21. A Response to Professor Pieixoto
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Doll writes a fictional keynote by 'Professor Anadicrad' answering Pieixoto's 'our job is not to censure but to understand': the fact that we view the past through an anachronistic lens does not forbid normative judgment, since Aristotle's practical wisdom—honed by hindsight, aiming at the golden mean and eudaimonia—gives historians a standard for judging whether a society cultivated virtue or vice. Gilead fails that standard spectacularly: it banned the reading that shapes values, reduced women to reproductive function, and required heteronormative forced procreation, blocking the relationships and habits flourishing needs. Beauvoir corrects even Aristotle's own biology-based view of women, and the chapter closes that a purely descriptive history would doom us to repeat Gilead's atrocities.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: On Philosophers and Drag Queens
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Drag Race is an unexplored philosophical playground because it builds on marginalized black and Latinx queer herstory and because RuPaul, whose creed of love and self-improvement makes her a philosopher in her own right, has made the show her magnum opus. It invokes Plato's cave to explain why philosophers crave the 'untucked' version of everything RuPaul shows on stage. Its central move is a virtue-ethics reading of the show's judging: Ru's demand that a queen first be fierce, and through fierceness achieve charisma, uniqueness, nerve and talent, mirrors Aristotle's question of what makes a good person, with fierceness playing the role phronesis plays in securing the other virtues. Comparing queens like Silky Nutmeg Ganache, Jinkx Monsoon, Yara Sofia and Sharon Needles, it poses 'what makes a good drag queen?' as a live philosophical problem.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 12. What about Della Street
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Birondo evaluates Della Street through moral psychology and Aristotelian virtue ethics: she is an excellent secretary in the role-specific sense (the Gregg shorthand that traps Robert Caddo's contradiction outside The Lonely Heiress crime scene) and supplies the 'woman's angle' the office needs, while Perry displays Aristotle's practical wisdom in court but a failure of recognition toward her, under-crediting her and kissing her for her 'feminine charms' upon her skullduggery in ways that today would be sexual harassment. The chapter also applies Aristotle on habituation through Mrs. Caddo's 'wildcat' tantrums hardening into character, and asks whether Della's team-playing beyond her duties is admirable, sad, or itself the product of mid-century sexism.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Olympic Tetherball A Final Lesson on Moral Frailty
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: The chapter asks whether Kenneth the page is a Kantian rule absolutist who never makes exceptions, or an Aristotelian 'contextual absolutist' who sees that the right act depends on circumstances, as when he runs the Hill Witch ruse to scare Tracy into eating well. Jack's lifeboat hypothetical and rigged-elevator test bounce off Kenneth's refusal to believe in hypothetical situations, but Jack's gift of illegal cable exposes Kenneth's moral frailty when he enjoys the stolen channels. It concludes that Kenneth's gullibility, trust, and loyalty make his simple moral vision both admirable and easily corrupted, and that the real lesson is facing our failures with resolve rather than shame.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: “Well, It Got Big Laughs”
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Barkman uses Confucius (ren, yi, li, and zheng ming, treating each person according to what he or she is) and Aristotle (eudaimonia, virtue as a habituated mean between extremes, practical wisdom) to indict 30 Rock for valorizing Jack's 'semi-virtuous path', the smug middle between best and worst announced in 'Do-Over'. He catalogues injustices the show laughs off: Liz's serial lies about her age, hobbies, and adoption; Jack's priority flu shots for the powerful in 'Flu Shot'; Tracy's insubordination about dogfighting in 'Rosemary's Baby'; and Kenneth's servility as everyone's punching bag. On liberality and piety, Jack's confession that 'capitalism is my religion' and Liz's 'I pretty well do whatever Oprah tells me' show the show settling for semi-virtue, which the chapter says even comedy must not endorse.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: The Bocks test three answers to the good life against the show: Howard as hedonist (laser-obstacle-strip-chess, the 'whore of Omaha') read through Bentham, Mill's higher and lower pleasures, and Aristippus; ethical egoism via Glaucon's ring of Gyges and Howard's offer to Skype rather than visit the deported Raj; and Hobbes's state of nature and social contract read into Sheldon's roommate agreement, whose lack of a Hobbesian sovereign leaves 'I settle all ties' arbitrary and rule-following too thin for ethics. Aristotle's virtue and practical wisdom crown Leonard — the nucleus of the social group, as Amy says — as the closest thing to the phronimos. The gang's sabotage of Dennis Kim with a manufactured girlfriend closes the chapter by asking who really ruined whose life.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Zeccardi and Ma deconstruct the film's hierarchical dichotomy between Walter's rule-obsessed ethical generalism (Shabbas rules, 'MARK IT ZERO!') and the nihilists' particularist 'Zere ARE no ROOLZ', using Derrida and Culler's method of undermining the opposition the text privileges. Each extreme fails: Walter's principles collide in the beeper dilemma, and active Nietzschean nihilism makes the nihilists unpredictable cowards. The Dude emerges as an Aristotelian agent of virtue whose phronesis perceptively weighs contextual facts (Smokey's disputed toe, the carpet-pissers' false assumption) against principles, making 'What would the Dude do?' a question about character rather than rules.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Learning from Mia’s Mistakes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: The chapter grades each of Mia's escalations in Crocodile — helping Rob hide the cyclist's body, killing Rob fifteen years later, then killing Shazia, her husband, and baby Ali to keep the secret — under Kant's categorical imperative (the cover-up cannot be universalized and treats persons as means), the utilitarian calculus (which also condemns every killing once the widow's suffering and Mia's guilt are counted), and feminist care ethics, which rejects her defense that she killed to protect her family because care obligations never cancel proportionality and others' rights. Aristotle's virtue ethics supplies the diagnosis: Mia's undoing is lack of practical wisdom — every split-second choice (which she never had time to deliberate) went wrong because she lacked virtuous habits. The chapter urges practicing everyday virtue so we never take the first step down her path.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 6 Panther Virtue The Many Roles of T’Challa
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: White applies Aristotle's virtue ethics to T'Challa's many roles — Panther Tribe chieftain, king, Avenger, ambassador, brother, husband — arguing that virtues like the honesty and courage his fellow heroes praise need practical wisdom (phronesis) to guide action when roles conflict, as when he chooses country over rescuing Storm from trial, spies on the Avengers as king, or abducts a businessman as a matter of national security. Through tragic dilemmas like destroying Wakanda's vibranium to keep it from Doctor Doom ('a king must make terrible choices'), he shows such choices haunt without dirtying character, and that over-adopting roles is itself a failure of the golden mean, evidenced by T'Challa feeling 'imprisoned' by a kingship he never chose.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The End of the Story
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Takes the Bene Gesserit Gom Jabbar test as defining humanity as the capacity to endure pain and act for the species rather than chew off one's leg like an animal, reading Paul's habit of walking into traps (Arrakis, the Tleilaxu ghola Hayt in Dune Messiah) and the Atreides ethic of self-sacrifice as passing that test. It ties the Butlerian Jihad's ban on making 'a machine in the likeness of a man's mind' to modern dependence on phones, computers and spell-checkers, echoing Mohiam's claim that removing the crutch 'forced human minds to develop' the two schools of math and politics. With Aristotle it argues that the politics of community and contemplation are the human talents machines atrophy, and ends by casting modern consumers (Harkonnen-like, 250 gallons of water per quarter pounder) as animals caught in a self-made environmental trap.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Spice of Meaning
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Builds, in Aristotle's manner of starting from the views of the wise, a three-way comparison: the Harkonnens seek power for its own sake and hollow Dr. Yueh into an instrument, the Fremen live meaningful but suffocating lives inside unquestioned ritual identity, and the Atreides model a virtue with no formula. Duke Leto's abolition of the beggars' water-towel ritual and his politically motivated spilling of water at the dinner party show good intentions failing when they break bonds of meaning without renewing them, while Paul and Jessica break Fremen rules in ways that repair social bonds and leave a more just society. The chapter ends with the worm-rider on shifting sand as the image of a never-finished, context-sensitive struggle for meaning.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Notes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Tracing Fallout's own censorship history — the GURPS licensing cancellation threat, the invisibility of child NPCs in the European release, the moral panic after Columbine — the chapter asks whether it is wrong to simulate evil, framing the issue with Morgan Luck's gamer's dilemma. Plato's cave and the Forms ground the 'media impacts morals' worry: games are shadows of shadows whose simulated vice accumulates 'a large evil in our souls', which is also why Lucy's Vault upbringing leaves her underprepared for the wasteland's emotions. Against this, Aristotle's catharsis and Schulzke's claim that Fallout trains phronesis support depicting wrongdoing as practice for moral judgment, so the chapter concludes the right wrongs to depict are whichever maximize the simulation of choice, with Braun's player-controlled Tranquility Lane simulation as the dystopian counter-model.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Albert Anglberger and Alexander Hieke contrast Ned, the virtue ethicist's genuinely good man, with Cersei, a 'minimally extended' egoistic consequentialist whose only morally relevant subjects are herself and her children. Aristotle's apparatus does the work: phronesis lets Ned rank his daughters' lives above honesty when he confesses falsely ('the lies we tell for love'), his 'you're too fat for your armor' quip shows the golden mean among competing virtues, and Cersei's unbalanced maternal love is excess, hence not a virtue. They then unsettle moral judgment itself: utilitarianism would license the Slaver's Bay slaveholders, virtue ethics lacks action rules and cross-cultural agreement (charity is no Dothraki virtue), and Martin's POV narration gives direct access to Ned's inner life but only Varys's and Littlefinger's unreliable reports about Cersei - so our verdicts on her, like real-life judgments of others, rest on shaky evidence.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Using the Nicomachean Ethics and the Rhetoric, the chapter vindicates the pleasure readers take in Salander's Taser-and-tattoo revenge on Bjurman: Aristotle distinguishes revenge, done for the satisfaction of the one wronged, from punishment, and requires that the wrongdoer know who avenges and why—which is why Lisbeth waits until Bjurman wakes before inking i am a sadistic pig, a pervert and a rapist across his torso. Proper anger on the right grounds is a virtue (hatred alone is corrosive), Larsson is cast as the rhetorician who must keep our trust to 'put the judge into a certain frame of mind,' and the revenge emerges as the deliberated, rational means toward the end Aristotle calls eudaimonia: independence from a bogus guardianship and a life worth living, since under 'proportionate reciprocity' those who cannot requite evil with evil are slaves.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: How Revealing Are Our Choices
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: The chapter builds on Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics account of choice (prohairesis) as 'deliberative desire' for things within our power and a better test of character than actions, then distinguishes three senses of choice. Internal-choice is Draco deciding but failing to kill Dumbledore; act-choice is Dumbledore's poor youthful choices; and motive-choice is captured by Kant's two shopkeepers who both refuse to cheat customers, one from fear of jail and one from honesty, so that only knowing the motive reveals the choice's moral worth.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: 13 Pride and Prudence in the Pursuit of Knowledge Indiana Jones, René Belloq, and Irina Spalko
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Argues that the desire to know is natural and good (Aristotle's Metaphysics, Socrates via Plato's Meno) only when bounded by moral limits, using Gilbert Meilaender's warning that curiosity becomes a vice when driven by pride or the lust for power. René Belloq opens the Ark seeking a personal audience with God and is incinerated; Irina Spalko demands 'tell me everything you know' from the interdimensional beings at Akator and her eyes burn out; prudent Indy tells Marion 'Don't look, no matter what happens' and leaves before the beings' 'big gift' of knowledge. The chapter concludes that pride must give way to prudence when unlocking the secrets of the universe.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Relax, Tony—You’re Safe!
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Nielsen uses the unity-of-virtue thesis (UVT) to ask how morally flawed Tony can be a virtuous Iron Man. Plato's Meno and Laches — Nicias' 'thoughtful courage' versus mere rashness — explain why apparently brave villains like Doctor Doom, Iron Monger, and the Mandarin are actually fearless rather than courageous, while Aristotle's distinction between natural virtue and full virtue plus prudence explains how Tony can be courageous yet intemperate with alcohol and women. Susan Wolf's argument that practical knowledge is essentially unified justifies UVT while making perfect virtue an unreachable ideal, so flawed, striving Stark — unlike Doom — is about as virtuous as a human being gets.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Argues that the standard trio of moral failure - malice (Creed ogling Pam, Andy sabotaging Dwight with the toll-receipt trick), weakness of will (Jan returning to Michael, Meredith relapsing with alcohol), and ignorance (Pam trading away Jim's teapot in 'Christmas Party') - misses a fourth category: moral blindness, embodied by Michael Scott, who can recite moral rules but cannot see when they apply (his Martin Luther King name tag on Diversity Day, defending Phyllis from Todd Packer with a harassing kiss, the fake-firing prank on Pam). Against Plato's view that all wrongdoing is ignorance, the chapter claims knowledge of rules neither helps nor harms decency; what matters is moral perception - seeing what a situation requires - shown by Jim getting Dwight to the hospital and rescuing the Dundies, Pam protecting the Dwight-Angela secret, and Toby patiently answering Dwight's anatomy questions.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Uses Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics account of wit as a character virtue lying in a mean to map the UK office: David Brent is the buffoon of excess, the 'slave of his sense of humor' who cannot not joke (the 'crack of Dawn' line, the cruel Post-It Notes firing prank on Dawn), Gareth Keenan the boor of deficiency whose literalism leaves him unable to make or take a joke, and Tim Canterbury the ready wit whose responsive irony ('Does anybody have the right time?') hits the mean. Because humor, like morality, is uncodifiable - there is no Having a Sense of Humor for Dummies - the trio illustrates that virtue is qualitative appropriateness guided by practical wisdom, not moderation or rule-following.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: I Knew Everything When I Was Young: Examining the Wisdom of Youth
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Weighs Betty's 'I knew everything when I was young' against James's 'I don't know anything' using Aristotle's theoretical versus practical wisdom and Nozick's criteria, finding Betty wise: she knows what matters ('To kiss in cars and downtown bars'), the means ('Chase two girls lose the one'), the long view, and how to handle the dilemma of forgiving James. Plato's Meno recollection doctrine and 'seven' ('Before I learned civility I used to scream ferociously') support the claim that the young can possess moral clarity adults lose. James's apology shows wisdom in action (Kekes) and Socratic intellectual humility, while 'tolerate it', 'Dear John', and All Too Well's dinner-party scene illustrate Spear on gaslighting via presumed epistemic superiority of older men.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Notes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Arvan argues the show is really about positive masculinity - what it is to be a good man - read through Aristotle's virtue ethics: toxic masculinity (Rupert's domination, Jamie Sr.'s abuse, Nate's cruelty, Ted's suffer-in-silence self-reliance) is vice at an extreme, while the show's good men hit the golden mean by 'womaning up.' Led Tasso works as context-appropriate toughness, Roy's hug of Jamie and the darts speech's 'be curious, not judgmental' blend masculine and feminine virtues, phronesis is learned from experience as Beard teaches Nate forgiveness, and even Rupert's downfall shows vice backfiring as Aristotle predicts.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Barkman distinguishes the self-evident natural law (general beneficence, special preference for family, piety to parents as Confucius taught, duties to the weak) from derivative rules like 'do not steal' and from positive law, concluding that Andrea's mermaid necklace looting question in 'Guts' is really about whether natural law still binds when the state has collapsed. He argues it does: Andrea's necklace is unowned and free to take, Rick taking surplus food from Andrea would be justified by equal claims to survival, and Carol's 'we can make new rules' polygamy proposal fails because the natural law is prior to any government. The cannibal hunters of Issues #61-66 show what happens without virtue and Aristotle's practical wisdom for weighing conflicting principles, and walkers are bad but not evil, while a Governor-like human who ignores the natural law 'reduces himself to the level of a walker.'

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Notes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: A mother-daughter pair tracks Wonder Woman's and Harley Quinn's costume histories (the 1990s Artemis-era near-thong Diana, the New 52 brothel-styled Harley) and argues with Aristotle that sexualized drawing strips both characters of phronesis, the practical wisdom a virtuous agent needs - the wisdom by which an outmatched Wonder Woman talks Strife into carrying her to safety and Harley exploits the Joker's vanity to beat him. The paradox: the more provocatively each is drawn, the less she can succeed as moral hero or anti-hero, since objectification replaces goal-directed cunning with one-dimensional sex display. The New 52's armor-clad, Hephaestus-consulting Wonder Woman shows phronesis restored.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Notes
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Tobienne reads Wonder Woman as sophia personified and a rhetorician in Aristotle's sense, whose real weapon is persuasion: he dissects the Rucka 'Lies' dialogue where she talks the feral Cheetah back to her humanity ('You are a WOMAN... You are my FRIEND!') and her verbal disarmament of a mind-sick Power Girl while holding her in a headlock. Nicomachean Ethics VI grounds the claim that practical wisdom recognizes the need for friends - each woman needs the other - and Wonder Woman's own submission to Athena and Aphrodite explains how the lasso of loving authority, not brute force, disarms Man's World.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: To Hack or Not to Hack
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Kennedy asks how a great player like Kareem (the NBA's career foul leader) can be excellent while fouling so much, and answers that deontology (Kant's categorical imperative) and utilitarianism (Mill's greatest-happiness principle) can condemn dangerous 'goon' fouling but cannot explain why the legal Hack-a-Shaq strategy still feels 'clownish.' Invoking Shaq's self-nickname 'the Big Aristotle,' he argues Aristotelian virtue ethics fits better: the excellent player, like the person of good character, perceives the situation rightly and fouls (or risks a foul) at the right time in the right way, so excellence is a habit of seeing well rather than rule-following.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Wizard versus the General
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Walls argues Bob Knight ('the General') is a greater coach than John Wooden ('the Wizard') on two criteria. First, drawing on Aristotle's remark that a good general makes the most of the troops at his disposal and Mortimer Adler's proportional standard of achievement, he says Knight won three titles with far less NBA talent while Wooden always had all-stars like Alcindor and Walton. Second, on integrity (Sophocles' 'fail with honor' over 'win by cheating'), he contrasts Knight's clean, high-graduation-rate program against widely alleged NCAA violations by UCLA booster Sam Gilbert, concluding Knight's temper flaws damage his legacy less than cheating damages Wooden's.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: Third Hole Finding the (Fair)Way with Confucius and Ben Hogan
aristotle-practical-wisdom.relation: Laumakis builds an analogy between pursuing excellence in golf and living a flourishing human life, then contrasts two models. Reading Confucius's Great Learning and Analects onto golf, he casts a repeating swing as a 'well-ordered kingdom' rooted in self-cultivation, and reinterprets ren, li, yi, and xiao so the 'authoritative player' masters the game through ritual practice, a teacher-parent (xiao), and doing what is appropriate in each lie. Against this social conception he sets Ben Hogan's Five Lessons as a 'rugged individualist' account stressing solitary practice and personal responsibility, and proposes a contextual pluralism as a mean between communitarian absolutism and individualist relativism.

aristotle-practical-wisdom.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
aristotle-practical-wisdom.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
