Flynn argues this vision is dangerous: by insulating justice from deliberation and depicting it as revelatory and divine, it derides the discursive, civil processes (Habermas-style communicative action) actually needed to make justice 'ours,' risking mere private vengeance — 'deserve's got nothin' to do with it.'

punishment-theory.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
punishment-theory.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
punishment-theory.relation: Knight and McKnight use Northrop Frye's master genres to chart Eastwood's move from romance (the superior hero who defends a community, as Jed Cooper in Hang 'Em High, the Stranger in High Plains Drifter, Harry Callahan in Dirty Harry) toward tragedy with Mystic River, where Jimmy Markum kills the innocent Dave as his daughter's murderer and, like Oedipus, recognizes his error too late. They read the law-versus-justice tension through Aristotle's point in the Nichomachean Ethics that the lawful and the just are not coterminous, and cite McClelland glossing Walt Kowalski's self-sacrifice in Gran Torino as a supreme instance of Aristotelian practical wisdom (phronesis) that solves multiple problems at once.

punishment-theory.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
punishment-theory.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
punishment-theory.relation: Skoble uses Taxi Driver's Travis Bickle to probe when vigilantism is justified, invoking Locke's claim that in civil society individuals delegate private vengeance to the state for objectivity. He argues Travis's rescue of the trapped child prostitute Iris is legitimate (the police won't help, she can't help herself) while his plan to assassinate Senator Palantine is madness, drawing the key line between correctly identifying a deserving target and mere perceived evil (contrasting Travis with Death Wish's Kersey, Batman, and Klan lynch mobs). He closes with Socrates' 'unexamined life' as the remedy: contemplating justice so we can confront real badness rather than turn away.

punishment-theory.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
punishment-theory.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
punishment-theory.relation: D'Aries and Hirsch read Paul Thomas Anderson's Hard Eight as a neo-noir moral inversion: the aging criminal Sydney seeks atonement not through religious penance but through selfless love, rescuing John and Clementine while removing the loathsome Jimmy (who knows Sydney killed John's father). They contrast him with Melville's Bob le flambeur and Besson's The Professional, where convention demands the criminal be punished. Sydney escapes formal justice but is sentenced to a 'prison without bars' of self-loathing (the bloodstained cuff), and the authors warn that such sympathy-for-the-devil inversions verge on nihilistic moral relativism.

punishment-theory.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
punishment-theory.title: Terrorism, Counterterrorism, and “The Story of What Happens Next” in Munich
punishment-theory.relation: Foy reads Munich's Operation Wrath of God as Spielberg's argument for retribution over vengeance in state counterterrorism. Yvonne's Marcuse/Hegel relativism and the agents' 'think of yourself as a soldier' language-games are dismissed as Avner's psychological breakdown shows morality is objective. Foy deploys Nozick's five procedural differences between retribution and revenge and Kant's view of retribution as impersonal and rational, echoes Socrates in the Crito (retaliation harms one's own soul) via Avner's decay, and cites Aristotle's 'war for the sake of peace' and jus in bello discrimination/proportionality in the Hamshari and Jeanette assassinations.

punishment-theory.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
punishment-theory.title: Reflections from the Abyss Herzog’s Philosophy of Death
punishment-theory.relation: M. Blake Wilson traces Herzog's philosophy of death and the 'abyss' across Grizzly Man and Into the Abyss, examining how Herzog frames human, animal, and self-killings and refuses the retributive impulse. Against Kant's demand that murderers must die and Matthew Kramer's purgative rationale for capital punishment, Wilson enlists Nietzsche's warnings about the drive to punish and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us,' while contrasting Herzog's 'ecstatic truth' with the 'accountant's truth' via journalistic and bear-attack literature (Jans, Herrero) that accuses Herzog of a 'Hollywoodized' portrait of Treadwell. He coins 'vivicide' for the killing of a human by a non-human animal and questions whether Bear 141 committed murder or was merely a scavenger.

punishment-theory.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
punishment-theory.title: 14. Did Bourdain Go #MeToo Far
punishment-theory.relation: Finn tests Catharine MacKinnon's 'Rape Redefined' — rape as sex compelled by inequality rather than lack of consent — against Bourdain's #MeToo allyship and his payment to Asia Argento's teenage accuser Jimmy Bennett. She argues MacKinnon's power-based standard could recognize Argento's act as assault, and reframes Bourdain's hush-money payment, via the Wendat/Huron compensation practices in Graeber and Wengrow, as a compassionate vengeance-staying reparation consistent with his empathy.

punishment-theory.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
punishment-theory.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
punishment-theory.relation: Earleywine dissects the moral versus practical arguments over prohibition, attacking legal moralism—the drug-czar claim (Bennett, Wilson) that use is wrong simply because it is immoral—as circular, and noting that the law does not criminalize every immoral act (broken contracts, lying). He shows purported moral arguments collapse into utilitarian harm estimates that the data undercut, since use rates are essentially orthogonal to policy across Amsterdam, Australia, Portugal, and US states. He then weighs anti-prohibition rights arguments (religion, privacy in Ravin, property via Szasz, self-determination) and closes on proportionality: owning a harmless plant merits no punishment.

punishment-theory.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
punishment-theory.title: The Justification of Torture-Horror Retribution and Sadism in Saw, Hostel, and The Devil's Rejects
punishment-theory.relation: Jeremy Morris analyzes torture-horror through two questions: is the torture justified, and is the audience's enjoyment justified? He reads Saw's Jigsaw traps, Seven, and Last House on the Left as explorations of Kantian retributivism and lex talionis, where punishing the autonomous wrongdoer respects his autonomy. For purely sadistic films like Hostel, The Devil's Rejects, and Texas Chainsaw Massacre, he argues (via Humean sentimentalism against Kantian rationalism) that Cook's or Otis and Baby's infectious glee makes the torturer's delight the source of horror. A fully empathetic viewer can share both the victim's suffering and the torturer's joy without endorsing torture, so the genre is not immoral 'torture-porn.'

punishment-theory.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
punishment-theory.title: So, Case Closed – Right
punishment-theory.relation: Mark White asks why Batman doesn't kill the Joker, using the question to contrast utilitarianism (kill one to save the Joker's future victims) with deontology (killing is wrong regardless of consequences), and Batman's own agent-centered refusal. He runs Foot and Thomson's trolley problem and the transplant surgeon case, then modifies them: the Joker is the guilty one who created the danger, his future victims are uncertain, and killing him would be 'prepunishment' for crimes not yet committed. White, a self-described deontologist, concludes the case is genuinely hard and admits great good might have come from killing the Joker, using comics as thought experiments about killing to prevent future killing.

punishment-theory.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
punishment-theory.title: 53. Tarantino as Philosopher Vengeance – Unfettered, Uncensored, but Not Unjustified
punishment-theory.relation: Johnson treats Tarantino's post-2000 filmography as an argument that vengeance is morally permissible when proportionate and directed at the genuinely guilty: Beatrix in Kill Bill, Shosanna in Inglourious Basterds, and Django all get celebrated revenge, while The Hateful Eight is used to distinguish vengeance from retribution and legal versus 'frontier' justice via Nozick's and Bacon's definitions. He rebuts common and historical objections—reading Plato's Gorgias as endorsing due punishment, arguing Spinoza's monism and Hobbes's and Locke's social-contract views do not forbid proportional revenge, and citing Nietzsche and Beauvoir's Eye for an Eye (her refusal to pardon the collaborator Brasillach) to conclude cost-free, proportional revenge can be justified though mercy remains praiseworthy.

punishment-theory.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
punishment-theory.title: 5. Monsters and Evil in Doctor Who
punishment-theory.relation: The chapter defines a 'moral monster' as one who delights in evil acts, arguing (via Jonathan Glover and Laurence Thomas) that Hitler-style evil is all-too-human, not alien. Using Hume's claim that action springs from passion, it contends the emotionless Cybermen are a mere force of nature (bad but not evil), whereas the Daleks, driven by hatred, tribalism, and a closed belief system, are genuinely evil monsters; the manipulating Master mirrors our everyday lying. It then examines retributive justice through Solomon's execution in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship' and 'A Town Called Mercy,' rejecting purely backward- or forward-looking punishment (citing Rawls on utilitarianism's injustice) in favor of the Doctor's needs-based, 'reprobative' punishment, mercy, and self-forgiveness over the Time War.

aristotle-friendship.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
aristotle-friendship.title: 1 - Homer and Aristotle
aristotle-friendship.relation: Raja Halwani evaluates Homer against Aristotle's four character types (virtuous, continent, incontinent, vicious), arguing Homer is not virtuous and is genuinely vicious in the domain of food and drink (eating Frank Grimes's marked sandwich, the 64 slices of American cheese), while shuttling between continence and incontinence elsewhere. He catalogues Homer's lack of practical wisdom (phronesis) through gaffes like inferring the Bear Patrol works because there are no bears, and his lack of genuine friendship since he has only drinking buddies. Homer is judged neither malicious nor wholly vicious, so we pity him for his Springfield upbringing and the Simpson gene, and the chapter closes by crediting his 'in-your-face humanity'—his unregulated 'love of life'—as an admirable but dangerous ethical trait that does not make him an admirable person.

aristotle-friendship.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
aristotle-friendship.title: Erotic Love and Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Maps Aristotle's three levels of friendship onto Buffy's three boyfriends: Riley is a utility friendship chosen for the rational goal of a 'normal' boyfriend (echoed by Warren's robot April and the Buffybot, which prove programmed perfection cannot be loved), Spike is a pleasure friendship driven by passion and danger that Buffy ends in 'As You Were,' and Angel is a complete friendship where each values the other for his own sake despite the gypsy curse. This lets the authors solve Aristotle's love paradox (is erotic love chosen or does it choose us?) by adding Augustine's and William of Ockham's third power of the soul, the will: an arational faculty that values the other as an end in himself, neither rationally chosen nor irrationally caused.

aristotle-friendship.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
aristotle-friendship.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Gregory Bassham distills six keys to happiness from Tolkien's hobbits and elves: delight in simple pleasures (Epicurus on natural pleasures, Thoreau's Walden simplicity), making light of troubles (Sam's star above Mordor, with Marcus Aurelius and Augustine on courage and hope), friendship (Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics read against Sam, Merry, and Pippin refusing to let Frodo go alone), good character, beauty and creativity (Lothlórien versus Mordor, 'flow'), and wonder (Tom Bombadil, Frodo's 'recovery' of fresh vision at Cerin Amroth). He argues Tolkien thereby becomes a philosophical guide, pointing from the Shire and Rivendell to a richer, more joy-filled life.

aristotle-friendship.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
aristotle-friendship.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jorge Gracia contrasts Sam and Gollum as two hobbits of the same nature and culture seeking the same happy life, so their success and failure are instructive for ordinary people like us. Gollum's happiness is solitary possession of the Ring - he murders Déagol for it and ends 'into the dust' - while Sam's is fellowship in the Shire with Rosie and Frodo, pursued through loyalty and giving (spending Galadriel's seed-box to restore the Shire). The pivotal episode is Gollum's trembling caress of Frodo's knee, 'the most tragic moment in the Tale', squandered when Sam's jealous rebuke drives him back to treachery. With Aristotle on friendship and self-love, the chapter concludes that happiness is achievable only in a social context and its key is love.

aristotle-friendship.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
aristotle-friendship.title: Kierkegaard Lays It Down
aristotle-friendship.relation: Willie Young uses the sacrifice bunt (Derek Jeter's perfect one versus Placido Polanco's failed one) to test philosophical accounts of sacrifice. Aristotle treats bunting for teammates as friendship and civic virtue in the polis, while Seneca's Stoic sacrifices only to exercise virtue itself, detached from particular friends and refusing retaliation for hit batters. Hegel's modern ideal of self-renunciation makes the player a cog in the team machine (the Big Red Machine), obeying the manager's calculations; against this, Kierkegaard's Abraham, whose absolute duty to God is 'higher than the universal' through infinite resignation, exposes baseball's mechanical, manager-ordered sacrifice and asks whether the game trains obedient citizens who sacrifice as they are told.

aristotle-friendship.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
aristotle-friendship.title: Love and Self-Discovery
aristotle-friendship.relation: Mary Nichols argues The Curse of the Jade Scorpion answers The Maltese Falcon: where Sam Spade's cynicism leaves society no reason to trust its lone hero, C.W. Briggs, unknowingly stealing for the magician Polgar while hypnotized, is saved by love, friendship, and the office community of North Coast Casualty. The jade scorpion's trance, meant to cover crime, uncovers truth, as C.W. and Betty Ann admit under hypnosis the love and fear their waking selves hide, so that 'crystal clear' memory and self-knowledge, rather than Spade's rejection of dreams, free them from both the curse and crime. Against the noir world and Lester's 'comedy is tragedy plus time', the chapter holds that everyone has 'a little bit of larceny' in them and that experiences of love, friendship, and community are what form the character that keeps it in check.

aristotle-friendship.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
aristotle-friendship.title: Snape’s Choice
aristotle-friendship.relation: Defines love, with Aristotle, Aquinas, and M. Scott Peck, as willing the good of the other for the other's own sake, and reads Snape's double-agent life as love expressed in action despite real hatred: he protects Harry's enemies at constant risk while disliking most of them. His Occlumency, the skill to lie to Voldemort's face, reveals both strength and weakness, for rather than renouncing love as Voldemort did he only conceals it, and his dying gift of memories to Harry, revealing that Harry is a Horcrux, must be freely offered because his thoughts can never be taken.

aristotle-friendship.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
aristotle-friendship.title: Unknown
aristotle-friendship.relation: Because we each view life from our own inside vantage point, friends provide the external perspective self-knowledge requires: Hermione makes Harry see his insensitivity to Cho Chang, the trio helps Neville overcome his shyness, and Hagrid teaches Ron not to wreck friendship over petty jealousy. By contrast, characters without close friends - the Dursleys, Lockhart, Slughorn - stagnate, since honest friends are 'a mirror in which we see ourselves as we really are.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: Chapter 9 - Batman and Friends Aristotle and the Dark Knight’s Inner Circle
aristotle-friendship.relation: Opens Matt Morris's chapter by asking whether Batman — more inner-solitary than Spider-Man or Daredevil, whose civilian alter egos enjoy ordinary friendships — could have or be a friend at all. It quotes Ecclesiastes and Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics line 'Without friends no one would choose to live, though he had all other goods,' as deployed in Loeb's Hush, to set up the analysis of Batman's inner circle of Robin, Alfred, and the rest.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: From Aristotle to the Bat-Cave
aristotle-friendship.relation: Lays out the chapter's analytical tool: Aristotle's three kinds of friendship — utility (mutual practical benefit), pleasure (mutual enjoyment), and complete or virtue friendship between committed, roughly equal good people, 'one soul in two bodies.' Noting that the ancient Greek concept is broader than today's 'friend,' it then turns this threefold taxonomy onto Batman's closest relationships to see whether any rises to the highest form.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: Batman and Robin
aristotle-friendship.relation: Applies Aristotle's categories to Batman and Dick Grayson: Robin receives training, gadgets, and a mission (utility) and enjoys the mentorship (pleasure), repaying the huge imbalance with the love and honor Aristotle says the lesser friend owes. Aristotle's claim that the young's pleasure friendships are unstable explains Dick's growth into Nightwing; their later renewed camaraderie as near-equals 'moves in the direction of a complete friendship, but never seems to arrive at quite that high a plateau.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: The Bat, Harvey Dent, and Two-Face
aristotle-friendship.relation: Treats Batman's bond with District Attorney Harvey Dent as a utility friendship built on shared, extralegal zeal for justice — until acid scarring turns Dent into Two-Face. Using Aristotle's rules that a virtue friendship must end with an incurably vicious person but not be cut off rashly, the chapter argues further that even a utility friendship cannot survive one friend's viciousness when the other is virtuous — 'collaboration with corruption corrupts' — so Batman must bury the friendship despite surgery and therapy aimed at restoring the old Dent.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: The Cop and the Vigilante
aristotle-friendship.relation: Analyzes Batman and Jim Gordon as Aristotle's friendship of utility: the Bat-Signal and police information serve both men's missions, exactly as Bruce's 'I need an inside man' monologue in Batman: Year One intends. The chapter explains why it never deepens into pleasure — Batman's guardedness about his identity and Gordon's doubts about his unpredictability — and shows its fragility: if Batman ever killed, or Gordon had to arrest him, the reciprocity would end. A rebuffed dinner-party invitation dramatizes that they are colleagues 'ultimately no more.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: Batman and Catwoman
aristotle-friendship.relation: Classifies Batman's attraction to Catwoman as Aristotle's friendship of pleasure: they relish their bat-and-cat chases, she is neither his mentee nor his colleague, and Aristotle's view that romances are pleasure friendships fits what they have. The chapter argues her underlying goodness — she does not kill and often abandons thefts that could harm Batman — explains the attraction and why, after her reform into a neighborhood protector, Batman finally trusted her with his identity as Bruce Wayne.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: The Butler and the Man of the Manor
aristotle-friendship.relation: Examines Bruce and Alfred: real mutual utility (Alfred's lifelong service and quasi-parental role against shelter and income), yet Aristotle's requirement of equality blocks complete friendship — Bruce is always the boss and Alfred always the butler, each bound by an overriding sense of mission. The chapter argues any change, Alfred quitting or Bruce dismissing him, would itself be an alienating act of disloyalty, so this closest of relationships is destined never to ascend higher than it stands.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: The Elusiveness of a Complete Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Argues that Batman himself is chiefly responsible for the elusiveness of complete friendship: the promise to his murdered parents consumes the personal investment such friendship needs, so everyone — Gordon, Dent, the Robins, Batgirl, Alfred — must fit into the mission, as his Hush confession to Catwoman ('I am not very good at this. Having friends.') shows. Aristotle's remark that the good man is a friend to himself lets the chapter cast Bruce and Batman as 'one soul in two personae,' the only virtue friendship left to him. It closes as a cautionary tale: a life of mission can cost the balance — and the friendship — that a good and happy life requires.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: A Partnership for Living Well
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter's core argument: Aristotle's Politics defines a city as 'a partnership for living well,' and the family is the most intimate such partnership — the Fantastic Four exemplify it. Ben's loyalty to the friend who disfigured him, serving as Reed's conscience, is explained through all three Aristotelian friendships: utility (the belonging he finds nowhere else, from Avengers stints to wrestling), pleasure (the sibling-style war with Johnny he secretly enjoys), and complete friendship — strongest between Reed and Ben, inseparable from Reed's guilt over the one miracle he cannot perform: restoring his friend's human form.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: The Family During Turmoil
aristotle-friendship.relation: Surveys the team's turmoil — Ben's walkabouts, Johnny's bids for independence, Reed and Sue's marital strife and suburban experiments, Reed's 'for his own good' secrecy about Ben's cure — to argue that members leave and return not from duty but from a mutual affinity: only within the family do they feel complete and develop their potential best. It also honestly flags the family's dysfunction, reading Ben's departures as a child running away from home and his squabbles with Johnny as sibling rivalry for Reed and Sue's parental attention.

aristotle-friendship.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
aristotle-friendship.title: The Ethos of Teamwork
aristotle-friendship.relation: Concludes that the Fantastic Four achieve Aristotle's complete friendship and become 'partners for a greater good': unlike Avengers-style teams whose friendships are mainly self-oriented, the Four's bond is unselfish love aiming at the good of the other. The chapter adds that they turn the family's protective instinct outward, so the world's ordinary citizens live like children under their care.

aristotle-friendship.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
aristotle-friendship.title: Poker and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Hamilton, unsettled that his seventeen-year-old daughter Tess has taken up poker, sorts the game's motives three ways. Competition is morally justified as a mutual quest for excellence with respect for worthy opponents (Robert Simon; Phil Hellmuth's tilt as the counterexample to Brunson's class); fellowship is Aristotle's three friendships — utility, pleasure, and the virtue friendship that shapes character — enacted in his father's VFW games and in Louise and Sailor Roberts keeping vigil when Brunson had four months to live, with Kant's rare moral friendship and C.S. Lewis's side-by-side companionship filling it out; but profit-playing invites the three-phase slide into pathological gambling addiction. His verdict: the motive decides the morality — poker is justified for competition and friendship, not for profit.

aristotle-friendship.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
aristotle-friendship.title: Dorothy Growing Up in the Land of Oz
aristotle-friendship.relation: McCall and Auxier use Aristotle's virtue ethics to unpack the Wizard's claim to be 'a good man but a bad wizard' and to argue that no external token—the diploma, heart watch, or medal—can confer virtue, which is cultivated only through practice and experience. Each companion lacks something specific: the Scarecrow the intellectual virtues and phronesis, the Tin Man the feelings and stable states of character that regulate emotion, the Lion the sophrosyne that balances thinking and feeling into courage as the mean between recklessness and cowardice. Aristotle's three grades of friendship (utility, pleasure, virtue) frame the companions' bond with Dorothy, and MacIntyre's account of virtues internal to practices explains why the Wizard's public recognition still matters. Dorothy herself begins as the child Aristotle says cannot yet be virtuous—fleeing Miss Gulch in Kansas—but by defending Toto against the Lion and leading the quest she grows into a responsible moral agent, which is what her delayed homecoming requires.

aristotle-friendship.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
aristotle-friendship.title: A Happy Ending
aristotle-friendship.relation: Bickham asks why Dorothy is so eager to leave heroic, Technicolor Oz for the gray, childless, Gulch-dominated farm, and whether, like Hamlet's delay, her rash choice can be evaluated as hers rather than her author's. Aristotle's account of the good life as the exercise of our highest capacities, requiring friends and material goods, makes Oz look like the better home for the competent twelve- or thirteen-year-old he takes Dorothy to be, against the hedonisms of Aristippus, Epicurus, and Bentham and Plato's body-denying dualism. But caring about Dorothy first needs defending from the paradox of fiction, which he works through Currie's simulation theory and Walton's make-believe emotions before dissolving the puzzle: storytelling suspends the reign of logic, so wishing Dorothy well is natural. Finally Heidegger's being-toward-death shows 'happily ever after' is impossible anywhere, and he throws the problem to the reader: write a happy ending for Dorothy in Kansas.

aristotle-friendship.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
aristotle-friendship.title: Transformers and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Watson and Arp ask whether Ironhide and Chromia's embrace means Autobots can love, rejecting programmed loving behavior, implanted souls, and wired-in human brains as insufficient for genuine personhood, then sort Transformer relationships into Western conceptions of love. Empedoclean cosmic Love and Strife map onto Primus versus Unicron; Platonic philia ascends to the Form of Beauty, with Transformer souls originating in and returning to the All Spark; Aristotle's three friendships separate Optimus and Sparkplug's virtue-friendship from Megatron and Starscream's mere utility; and Stoic-Kantian equal love explains Autobots saving Decepticons who immediately try to kill them, alongside Christian agape in Autobot family bonds.

aristotle-friendship.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
aristotle-friendship.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

aristotle-friendship.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
aristotle-friendship.title: You Don’t Have to Be Like Him to Like Him
aristotle-friendship.relation: Levitt reads Monk through Aristotle's virtue ethics: a man of character whose police virtues survive Trudy's murder but whose phobias produce akrasia — in the pilot he knows he must descend the germ-filled sewer to save Sharona and freezes anyway, doing the right thing only at agonizing cost. Virtue as habit and the golden mean (friendliness as the mean between obsequiousness and standoffishness) frame his slow progress toward acting rightly without thinking, which is also why Stottlemeyer cannot recommend his reinstatement — he doubts the illness, not the man. Aristotle's three friendships sort Monk's relationships: utility (the department, employer Sharona), pleasure, and virtue — Natalie, who after watching Monk save Julie's fish over the priceless moon rock saw her late husband's goodness in him. Ethos, pathos, logos and catharsis then explain viewer identification: watching Monk move from akrasia toward balance (Dr. Kroger's 'N. Hope' note that turns out to mean New Hope) lets audiences identify with, and be ennobled by, a character we would never want to be.

aristotle-friendship.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
aristotle-friendship.title: It’s Time for the Other Walkie-Talkie
aristotle-friendship.relation: Dodge puts Monk on the case of friendship's nature, structured by Aristotle's three kinds from the Nicomachean Ethics: Hal Tucker's fake buddy act in 'Mr. Monk Makes a Friend' is pure utility, while Natalie's is virtue-friendship — she is his friend 'in spite of' the job since 'he doesn't pay her that much.' The friend as mirror and 'second self' grounds the claim that Stottlemeyer, Sharona, Natalie and Randy reflect Monk's excellence back to him, and Bacon's point that a friend redoubles joys and cuts griefs in half is shown when they stay up all night during his suicide watch. Seneca's Stoic counsel — judge a person long before admitting him, then hold nothing back — is exemplified by Natalie's fish-over-moon-rock test of Monk's character, while Montaigne's once-in-centuries friendship in which two selves blur fits only Trudy, whose dying words 'bread and butter' tell Monk they belong together. Plato's Lysis (the 'great cosmic swirly' Monk cites in 'Mr. Monk and the Bully') opens the puzzle Socrates could not solve, and the single walkie-talkie his father gave him shows why the chapter's verdict — Monk now has friends — matters.

aristotle-friendship.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
aristotle-friendship.title: 10 - Why Can’t We Be Virtual Friends
aristotle-friendship.relation: Condella tests Facebook friendship against Aristotle's three kinds (pleasure, utility, virtue) from Nicomachean Ethics VIII-IX and Cicero's De Amicitia: the average user's 281 friends far exceeds true philia, which needs time, reciprocated goodwill, and shared 'conversation and thought'. He grants that Facebook's status updates share conversation and thought and maintain ties across distance, evoking the Seinfeld episode where Jerry refuses Keith Hernandez's too-early request to help him move. But because no one has ever helped a friend move on Facebook, virtual presence cannot make us better people, and Facebook's artificial buoying of dead friendships of utility risks quantity crowding out the few deep friendships that matter.

aristotle-friendship.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
aristotle-friendship.title: 13 - What Are Friends For
aristotle-friendship.relation: Bloor reads Facebook anxiety through Heidegger's diagnosis of technological nihilism — an efficiency-driven 'being-in-the-world' with no shared arbiter of what matters — borrowing Dreyfus's HAL 9000 example from 2001: A Space Odyssey to show humans enhancing themselves like any other raw material. He argues Facebook's speed lures users into unreflective sharing and standardized behavior where the quirky authentic 'I' dissolves into Heidegger's 'one,' and recruits Aristotle's view that only a few deep friendships morally form us to warn that hundreds of contacts fragment that benefit. Adorno on leisure as mere recuperation between bouts of work frames the therapist who keeps Facebook strictly professional, and the chapter concludes the fault lies in ourselves, not the tools — suggesting a week offline as a test.

aristotle-friendship.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
aristotle-friendship.title: I Am the Bad Wolf
aristotle-friendship.relation: Answers Davros's charge that the Doctor fashions companions into weapons by examining his character through virtue ethics: his unifying virtue is Heideggerian 'authentic concern', always offering aggressors like the Nestene or the Sycorax a choice so they become genuinely responsible, as in the fly-swatting thought experiment. Companions instead act from compassion, which lacks impartiality and produces the 'Bad Wolf Syndrome' (Rose's Dalek genocide, Martha's Osterhagen Key, Jack's warp star). Since for Aristotle a friend is 'another himself', the companions' actions are in a sense the Doctor's own yet founded on a distorted disposition, which is why he runs from his past.

aristotle-friendship.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
aristotle-friendship.title: Why Is It the Best Day Ever
aristotle-friendship.relation: Nicole Pramik argues SpongeBob is Aristotle's self-mastered man: his daily cheerfulness is eudaimonia, a happiness earned by practicing virtue as the mean between vices of excess and deficiency. The chapter tests each mean with episodes — courage between cowardly isolation ('I Had an Accident') and recklessness ('A Life in a Day'), honor between Patrick's under-the-rock humility and Squidward's Easter-Island vanity, honesty in 'Hooky' and 'Wet Painters', and good temper mended with Patrick in 'New Student Starfish' and 'The Fry Cook Games'. His moderation in pleasure and wealth, contrasted with Mr. Krabs's stinginess, and his F.U.N. Song friendship (Aristotle's greatest external good) show the golden mean served up on a sesame seed bun.

aristotle-friendship.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
aristotle-friendship.title: The Best Kind of Friend
aristotle-friendship.relation: Ruth Tallman tests Holmes and Watson against Aristotle's requirement in the Nicomachean Ethics that perfect friendship exists only between the 'alike in excellence': since the two live by irreconcilable moral codes (Holmes's cocaine and burglaries versus Watson's clean living and law-abidingness), Aristotelian moral naturalism denies they can be true friends at all, despite the raw panic in 'The Three Garridebs' proving mutual devotion. Recasting the pair as moral pluralists with different 'good for me's, she argues Holmes is actually the better friend, an 'integrity-promoting' friend who urges Watson to stay home from the Milverton burglary to honor Watson's own code, while the proselytizing Watson, who nags about cocaine yet tags along anyway, repeatedly violates his own integrity.

aristotle-friendship.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
aristotle-friendship.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Wayne Yuen uses The Graveyard Book to teach the good life: Bod's family's murder, like students owing their existence to the Holocaust, is an unalloyed moral evil that still enables a better life, and Saul Smilansky's distinction between being 'sorry for' and 'sorry that' lets Bod benefit without endorsing the tragedy. His graveyard education is Aristotelian, virtues acquired through practice and models, from the Owenses' duty and Silas's wisdom to 'righteous indignation' against school bullies and friendship with Scarlett as intrinsically valuable, all building toward eudaimonia. The existentialist virtue of authenticity (attributed to Sartre and Kierkegaard) explains why Bod must be 'nobody but himself' rather than a copy of the vampire Silas, why the scavenged identities of the ghouls mark inauthenticity, and why wiping Scarlett's memory threatens her authenticity, resolving the apparent conflict between virtue and being oneself because bravery or wisdom is relative to the individual.

aristotle-friendship.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
aristotle-friendship.title: The Wire and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Fisher argues The Wire makes homosexuality a source of excellence: Omar and Kima blend masculine and feminine traits in something like Butler's gender-performative terms, build Aristotelian friendships of virtue (Kima and Cheryl pushing each other's careers), and can make the sacrifices - solitude, giving up family - that excellence in the drug war demands, while the homophobia of the streets and the precinct forces them to keep proving themselves. Omar's crossword comfort with 'them myths' frames him as a contemporary Socrates: a mentor-lover of boys, accused of amorality by Levy much as Socrates was charged with corrupting Athens's youth, answering with a Socratic reversal ('I got the shotgun, you got the briefcase'), and dying for his code in the city he would not leave. The chapter reads the show's refusal of coming-out storylines - Rawls's silent gay-bar cameo, Snoop's never-confirmed sexuality - as its most radical statement about sexuality in America.

aristotle-friendship.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
aristotle-friendship.title: Psych and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Patricia Brace maps Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics categories of friendship onto Psych: Shawn's first-season ties to the SBPD are friendships of utility, the shared hobbies and bar nights (tap dancing in 'Feet Don't Kill Me Now,' 'Neil Simon's Lover's Retreat') build friendships of pleasure, and Shawn-Juliet matures from utilitarian boundaries into erotic friendship. Lassiter's lie-detector threat to protect Juliet in 'Shawn Rescues Darth Vader' and the lifelong Shawn-Gus bond ('Gus Walks into a Bank') approach complete friendship grounded in virtue, while the Henry-Shawn paternal friendship heals as Shawn develops the golden mean, and the vicious Mr. Yin and Yang - full of regret, incapable of complete friendship - show the life without it.

aristotle-friendship.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
aristotle-friendship.title: Psych and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: C. Scott Sevier argues Henry deliberately recreated Shawn as Aristotle's 'another self' - Lassiter's 'which one?' joke in the kidnapping episode makes the identity explicit - and reads this through Plato's Symposium: via Diotima's ladder of love and the doctrine of forms, Henry achieves immortality by reproducing beauty in his son's educated soul, not just his body. The chapter then frames Shawn's fierce independence against his constant recourse to Henry's voice as the collision between medieval deference to authority and the modern ideal of autonomy in Descartes and Kant, showing that both thinkers quietly borrowed from Augustine (the causal adequacy principle, the good will), so Shawn's 'autonomy' is itself the product of his father's training - an internalized authority indistinguishable from his own.

aristotle-friendship.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
aristotle-friendship.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: John Fitzpatrick asks whether voters should care that Alicia stands beside Peter, from the Season One resignation press conference to the finale's withheld hand. After a rapid tour of right-action theories grounded in the show - Eli Gold's egoism, Peter's 'pitted' evidence tip as consequentialism, Alicia keeping Jonas Stern's dementia secret as deontology, the Florrick-Childs no-children pact as social contract - he turns to Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: eudaimonia as a life weaving pleasure, friendship, and practical activity, in which mentors like Will and Diane let us contemplate virtue in others and improve our own character. His conclusion: Alicia's endorsement matters not because she is a good wife but because she is a good person whose judgment reveals Peter's character.

aristotle-friendship.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
aristotle-friendship.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Brace and Kingsbury use the Nicomachean Ethics to argue that Nucky, Chalky, and Margaret mistake pleasure and the mere instruments of happiness - tailored suits, money, useful connections, the appearance of virtue - for Aristotle's stable, self-sustaining virtuous activity, so their lives stay unstable and empty. Nucky 'buys' even Jimmy and Margaret, Chalky's jail-cell staging with David Copperfield shows how fragile his facade of cultivation is, and Margaret's acquisitions end in blackmail and in bribing God over Emily's polio. Only Richard Harrow, the Tin Man whose collage-clippings represent a happiness he believes he can never have, moves toward real Aristotelian friendship through Jimmy's 'Of course I would; right down to the last bullet' - the philia Aristotle calls most necessary for a happy life.

aristotle-friendship.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
aristotle-friendship.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jeffery Nicholas argues Card tries to write Ender as Nietzsche's self-sufficient superman - Graff's isolation program, the will to power, and Rackham's 'humanity does not ask us to be happy' - but the novel actually vindicates Aristotle's claim in the Politics that man is a political animal who cannot flourish without friends. Ender's difference from the beast-like Peter and the hive-minded buggers, his longing for Valentine, Alai, and Petra, and his despair in isolation show that friendship, not domination, is what makes him human.

aristotle-friendship.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
aristotle-friendship.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter argues Barney is best understood as a committed ethical egoist, distinguishing egoism from egotism, immoralism, and moral skepticism through the Playbook's Scuba Diver scam. Ainsworth rejects psychological egoism (Joey's view in Friends) using evolution and apparent counterexamples like Marshall's Christmas Eve deliveries, then uses Glaucon's ring of Gyges from the Republic to ask whether anyone would resist injustice with guaranteed impunity. The friendship objection is dissolved via Aristotle's 'a friend is another self': once friends are included in the ego, saving Marshall's relationship or rushing to Ted's hospital bed counts as self-interest, constrained like chess by absolute rules such as the Bro Code's Article 150.

aristotle-friendship.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
aristotle-friendship.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter argues the Bro Code's real value lies not in getting laid but in structuring homosocial bonds, listing its best articles (loyalty, equality, generosity) alongside its most sexist ones (the Hot/Crazy Scale, Article 101). Karioris explains men's competitive relations through hegemonic masculinity - the school-bully dominance that forces all masculinities to compete and pushes women out - and invokes Foucault's 'Friendship as a Way of Life' for how bonds between men can escape taboo and emotional distance. Robin as wingwoman ('a better Ted than Ted') and the gang's gender transgressions show the Code can be amended toward equality, with Aristotle's friendship of mutual cooperation and benefit, 'quid pro bro', as the standard.

aristotle-friendship.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
aristotle-friendship.title: Homeland and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Brittany Lorenz and Adam Barkman apply the Greek four-loves framework (storge, eros, philia, agape) to Homeland's relationships. Terrorism breaks storge by destroying comfort in familiar places; broken eros appears in the Brody-Jessica-Mike-Carrie square and Mira's lover who loves 'making love' rather than her; philia falters because Brody hides his Islam from Jessica, and Abu Nazir's bond with Brody is Aristotle's friendship of utility, dissolving when the advantage ceases. Brody's agape for country is broken because fighting abroad violates his prior duties as husband and father, so the show offers only glimpses of loves that might be redeemed.

aristotle-friendship.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
aristotle-friendship.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Robison-Greene asks whether there are principled standards for 'shipping' TV couples and applies Platonic-Aristotelian flourishing criteria (long-term safety, emotional needs, trust, and mutual growth toward virtue) to Piper's options: Alex fails on safety and trust (selling Piper out, the perjury advice), Larry fails on empathy and growth, so by real-life standards we should ship none of them. She concludes shipping is mostly aesthetic, then proposes minimal moral rules for our attitudes toward fictional relationships: never ship Pornstache, respect consent, and never let race, gender, or orientation decide.

aristotle-friendship.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
aristotle-friendship.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Elsby and Luzecky use Nicomachean Ethics VIII to sort Litchfield's bonds: Red's kitchen empire runs on friendships of utility that dissolve when her pipeline closes, race pre-assigns everyone's default friends, and Vee, who sleeps with RJ before having him killed, is incapable of friendship in any sense. The chapter locates genuine Aristotelian friendship only in Red's concern that Nicky stay off heroin (wishing her good for her own sake) and reads Red's sparing of Vee, held by a plastic bag, as respect without care, the recognition of a kindred quality that distinguishes Red from her evil counterpart.

aristotle-friendship.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
aristotle-friendship.title: 5. Every Lonely Monster Needs a Companion
aristotle-friendship.relation: Gadsden asks why a near-omnipotent Time Lord needs companions at all and tests four hypotheses against his solo meltdowns—executing Solomon in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship,' nearly murdering Jex in 'A Town Called Mercy,' and declaring himself 'Time Lord Victorious' in 'The Waters of Mars.' He rejects the Lord Acton power-corrupts hypothesis via Glaucon's ring story in Plato's Republic, since powerless companions offer no threat of reprisal or dishonor, and qualifies J.J. Sylvia's care-ethics 'empathetic link' because the Doctor cares for non-human species like the Star Whale too. He favors two answers: Hume's fact/value gap as a millennium-long moral myopia ('I can't see it anymore,' the deleted 'Flesh and Stone' confession), and Aristotle's point in the Nicomachean Ethics that only virtuous friends—moral peers who mirror us—can expose the Doctor's blind spots, like his 'God Complex.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
aristotle-friendship.title: 17. The Friends of a Time Lord
aristotle-friendship.relation: Littmann applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics taxonomy of friendship - pleasure, usefulness, and mutual goodness - to fifty years of Doctor-companion pairings, from the Hartnell Doctor's glee touring Vortis with Ian to New Series companions chosen as friends who routinely save the day, from Barbara's Dalek revolt to Clara saving every incarnation of the Doctor. He argues Aristotle would still judge the Doctor's friendships defective: they are short-lived, unequal in station, intellect, and morality, and the companions cannot know him well enough (not even his name) for the perfect friendship of the good. Littmann then corrects Aristotle on two counts: friends need not be moral experts to serve as moral critics (Rose in 'Dalek,' Amy in 'A Town Called Mercy'), and the Doctor's favoritism toward his companions - risking worlds to save them, as when Rory weighs Amy's life against the universe in 'The Big Bang' - shows that preferring friends over strangers is itself his most frequent moral failing.

aristotle-friendship.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-friendship.title: 5. Overcoming Evil with Love
aristotle-friendship.relation: Bogosian argues the film locates evil not in human nature itself, as Jeanine claims when she calls human nature 'the enemy,' but in cultivable vices - Al's jealousy and fear of failure leading to attempted murder and suicide, Eric's and Jeanine's lust for power - and that only altruistic, self-sacrificial love can counteract them. With Aristotle's point that friendship is essential to developing virtue and to the good life, he shows the faction system fails on its own terms: a single virtue in isolation corrupts (Candor's truth without kindness), and a system that removes real moral and political freedom destroys the flourishing it promises. Tris's parents' sacrifices and the Tris-Four relationship - honest training advice, protection of her Divergence, and the gun-to-her-own-forehead scene where love breaks the simulation's grip - model the love that overcomes the corrupt system.

aristotle-friendship.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
aristotle-friendship.title: 16. What Do We Really Owe Our Parents
aristotle-friendship.relation: Karavitis uses Tris and Tobias to stage the filial-piety debate: Tris, who loves her parents and learns to see them with adult eyes after discovering their hidden pasts, remains 'allegiant' to the end, while the abused Tobias owes Marcus and Evelyn nothing and reaches only a cautious adult reconciliation with his mother. After surveying Confucian xiao (with Mencius, and Buddhism's forced accommodation of it) and the Abrahamic commandments on one side, and Norman Daniels's and Jane English's autonomy-based arguments that children never consented to be born and so owe nothing on the other, he concludes no rational argument mandates filial duties from adult children. Aristotle's three types of friendship supply the one defensible model: only when adult children and parents meet as virtuous equals can a chosen, consensual relationship carrying care, gratitude, and love arise - so 'as adults, we owe our parents nothing,' though love may freely flow.

aristotle-friendship.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
aristotle-friendship.title: 6. The Psychiatrist as Sociopathic God
aristotle-friendship.relation: Hassert takes Lecter's 'First principles, Clarice' at its Aristotelian word - nature is revealed through capacities and action, as an acorn's telos is not pumpkins and a kitten will never be a Great Dane - to explain Lecter's psychiatry: he reads each patient's essence and potential, prescribing Mason Verger's face-peeling so appearance finally matches essence, and force-raising Will toward equality so that Aristotelian perfect friendship between the alike-in-virtue (which Franklyn's flattery can never reach) might become possible. Reading God through Augustine's account of evil as the destruction of a preexisting good and Mischa's murder, the chapter argues that Lecter emulates a capricious deity - 'Typhoid and swans - it all comes from the same place' - and, unlike Nietzsche, does not pronounce God dead but merely misconceptualized, while his friendships fail because he must corrupt the other into his own image rather than love an equal.

aristotle-friendship.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
aristotle-friendship.title: 10. The Light from Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Pavelich sets Aristotle's account of friendship - recognized and reciprocated goodwill between equals, perfected in the friendship of the good who 'share our souls', a standard met only by Jack and Bella Crawford - against Nietzsche's friendship as striving between overmen, who honor 'one's best enemy' in the friend and grow through conflict. He reads Hannibal's treatment of Will (hiding the encephalitis, framing him, serving the Nietzschean trout) as Nietzschean friend-making - Lies that are supposed to spur Will's growth, consistent with an Übermensch who tells Will 'Killing must feel good to God' and says 'I don't hide from God' - while Will's masquerade of friendship is betrayal in both senses, since Will seeks an Aristotelian soulmate and finds a killer he must stop. Because each betrays the other, neither Aristotelian nor Nietzschean friendship survives, though the moments before the Mizumono bloodbath - Hannibal inviting Will to just walk away - glimpse a real friendship already made impossible.

aristotle-friendship.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
aristotle-friendship.title: Walker Bite. If I Don’t Save the World, I Have No Value
aristotle-friendship.relation: This Walker Bite uses Eugene Porter's exposed lie about being the scientist who can cure the outbreak (5.5 "Self Help") to ask what makes a person valuable once their usefulness collapses. Eugene himself sums up an instrumental view of his own worth - "If I don't cure the disease, if I don't save the world, I have no value" - and admits he sabotaged the bus to stall the DC mission. Against this, Tara's "We're friends. We have each other's backs... You're stuck with us. No matter what" argues that persons are valued for themselves within a community rather than as means, and the chapter lands on Abraham's "people need people" as the real ground of Eugene's place in the group.

aristotle-friendship.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
aristotle-friendship.title: 2. Why Men of Action Don’t Lie
aristotle-friendship.relation: Mahon maps the film's non-romantic relationships onto Aristotle's philia: the loyal friendship of Inigo and Fezzik under Vizzini's abuse, expanded into a four-person 'family' once Westley, who defeated and spared them with respect, joins them to storm the castle. He argues deception in the film tracks the absence of philia - bad men incapable of friendship (Vizzini, Humperdinck, Rugen) lie to anyone, while friends never lie to each other and the early duels are sportsmanlike. Westley's line 'We are men of action. Lies do not become us' encodes an honor code that real men do not lie to real men even when enemies (hence Westley cheats Vizzini in the Battle of Wits with both goblets poisoned, and the chapter analyzes the resulting triple- and quadruple-bluff regress), while the one exception - Westley letting Buttercup stay deceived about Humperdinck - exposes the code's chauvinism, matching Aristotle's view that philia in its purest form exists only between male equals.

aristotle-friendship.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
aristotle-friendship.title: 10. Virtue Rising
aristotle-friendship.relation: Darci Doll argues the Rising exposes the Society's intellectual oppression—each Color denied education and fed 'noble lies' about its role—and that lifting it sparks an 'Intellectual Reformation' proving Color does not dictate potential: Darrow out-performing Golds, Orion the un-carved Blue, Ragnar and Sefi exceeding their station. She uses Plato's Republic (producers, auxiliaries, guardians, the lower orders kept obedient by Noble Lies like the Reds' terraforming myth) as the Society's blueprint, then turns to Aristotle: potential is realized only through the right environment, instruction, and habituated character, and Darrow's practical wisdom—testing himself, reassessing after Titus and Cassius, doing what makes him his best self—lets him flourish and lead. Aristotle's critique of utility-only relations explains why the Society's alliances expire (Antonia executed once useless) while Darrow and Mustang's virtue friendships and just rule endure, opening a society where everyone, including women and lowColors denied opportunity rather than ability, can maximize potential.

aristotle-friendship.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
aristotle-friendship.title: 29. The Best of Friends
aristotle-friendship.relation: Geyer sorts Game of Thrones friendships by Aristotle's three kinds in the Nicomachean Ethics. Robert and Ned's bond, formed in Jon Arryn's fosterage and shared war, is friendship of pleasure, which frays over Rhaegar's 'dragonspawn'; Tyrion and Bronn is friendship of utility, dissolving exactly as Aristotle predicts when Lollys's marriage pays better than a trial by combat in 'Mockingbird'; and Jon and Sam, each valuing the other's character for its own sake at the Wall, approach the only true friendship - the virtue friendship - supporting the claim that eudaimonia needs such relationships alongside external goods.

aristotle-friendship.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
aristotle-friendship.title: 15. We’re on Your Side, Charlie Brown
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter asks why Charlie Brown never abandons the friends who torment him and answers with friendship philosophy: Aristotle's three kinds of friendship fit the gang (pleasure-based childhood play - baseball, trick-or-treating, Christmas plays - as the nursery for later perfect friendships of good will), while Marilyn Friedman's 'moral growth' and 'moral empiricism' explain how even Lucy's blunt 'snap out of it' gives Charlie perspectives from 'reliable moral witnesses.' Annette Baier's account of trust as accepted vulnerability redeems his 'gullibility': better to risk the pulled football than live in an atmosphere of suspicion. The 'Our Manager' uniform of Charlie Brown's All-Stars and the decorated tiny Christmas tree show that on the things that matter his friends can always be trusted to take his side - and Charlie is always first to forgive.

aristotle-friendship.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
aristotle-friendship.title: 14. I’m an X-Man!
aristotle-friendship.relation: Daniel Alloy argues Deadpool keeps insisting 'I'm an X-Man!' because being a hero is not a private choice but a social standing: with Aristotle's beast-or-god line about those who cannot live in society and Hegel's account of mutual recognition in the Phenomenology of Spirit, he contends Wade needs heroes he recognizes to recognize him as one in return. The Thunderbolts ('the selfish Avengers') and X-Force recruited him as a merc and so could not grant that recognition, and Cable offers approval from superiority rather than recognition between equals—a friendship of utility where Wade wants one of virtue. Only Captain America's Avengers card treats him as an equal, and even that recognition must be completed by the whole hero community before Wade can accept himself as the hero he already is.

aristotle-friendship.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-friendship.title: 5. Why the Good Man Is a Great Leader
aristotle-friendship.relation: Nisley reads Civil War through Aristotle's good man and good leader: Cap shows courage but lacks temperance and practical wisdom - his rash Lagos operation, his rage-borne beating of Tony, his choice of Bucky over the Avengers' common end - and his ceaseless struggle between passion and reason falls short of virtue. Applying Aristotle's account of philia, she argues the Avengers are a friendship of the virtuous that requires deliberation toward justice, which Cap dissolves by tearing the team apart, while Tony's reasoned acceptance of UN oversight, moderation after Ultron, and concern for the whole team make him the good man fit to lead.

aristotle-friendship.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
aristotle-friendship.title: 6. Who’s the Better Friend
aristotle-friendship.relation: Bowman sorts Marvel relationships through Aristotle's three friendships: Ant-Man's starstruck alliance is friendship of pleasure, Obadiah Stane's partnership with Tony a toxic friendship of utility, and Steve's bond with Bucky a friendship of virtue that loves without reciprocity - making Cap better TO his friends, though saving Bucky endangers everyone else. Turning to Derrida's Politics of Friendship, where fraternity grounds democratic equality among all persons, he argues Tony's refusal to privilege any individual over mankind makes him better FOR his friends. The Civil War split thus replays the old tension between personal autonomy and responsibility to humanity, at the destructive scale only super-powered friends can achieve.

aristotle-friendship.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
aristotle-friendship.title: 18. War Means Fighting and Fighting Includes Philosophizing
aristotle-friendship.relation: Vuckovich reads 'Still Valley' as a moral battlefield: Confederate scout Sgt. Paradine finds a witchcraft handbook that has frozen a Union patrol before Gettysburg, and Glaucon's Ring of Gyges account from the Republic — the really unjust person winning without scruple while seeming just — frames the temptation of an invisible, effortless victory. Aristotle's friendships of shared wickedness illuminate his bond with the witchman Teague, who exploits Paradine's desperation to pass on his own curse, until Paradine casts the handbook into the campfire, choosing a principle of fairness over a Devil-guaranteed win and accepting the shame of a 'Pyrrhic loss.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
aristotle-friendship.title: 14. Friends Don’t Lie
aristotle-friendship.relation: Bowman tests Hawkins friendships against Aristotle's three kinds in the Nicomachean Ethics: Dustin and Lucas's shared-comics pleasure collapses into rivalry over Max, Nancy and Jonathan's utility ends once Will and Barb are found, and Barb's fatal poolside loyalty to Nancy, though one-directional, is a friendship of virtue. Nietzsche's ideal of friends who strengthen us through conflict recasts those very fights (Lucas confronting Eleven's power misuse) as the best friendship, care ethics (Gilligan and Noddings) makes the mutual one-caring Party the real answer to who teaches Eleven friendship, and Derrida's Politics of Friendship grounds democracy and society itself in such everyday reciprocity, which is why Eleven's 'friends don't lie' compass pulls her back from Kali's violence to close the gate.

aristotle-friendship.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
aristotle-friendship.title: Aristotle to the Rescue
aristotle-friendship.relation: Yim applies Aristotle's three kinds of friendship from the Nicomachean Ethics to the show: Tracy with Grizz and Dot Com in 'Hardball', and Tracy with Jenna in 'Flu Shot', are friendships of utility that dissolve when the benefit ends, while Liz and Jenna's long shared history looks deep but remains mutual usefulness between ambitious colleagues. Liz and Jack, by contrast, evolve from David-versus-Goliath adversaries in the pilot into something like virtuous friendship, culminating in 'Retreat to Move Forward' when Liz humbles herself with a terrible improv routine and a shirt-ripping dance to save Jack's standing before the Six Sigma crowd. The chapter argues the show thereby dramatizes that self-sacrificial goodwill is what makes a friendship worth the risk.

aristotle-friendship.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
aristotle-friendship.title: Neither Gods nor Beasts But Political Animals
aristotle-friendship.relation: Spanakos denies the official line that the Avengers assemble from necessity—Thor beats Loki alone—arguing instead through Aristotle that the team is a polis: heroes join for safety but stay for the good life, since outside the polis one is either a god or a beast. Ms. Marvel's miserable solo run (unrecognized by Stilt-Man, a 'Where Are They Now?' has-been) ends only when she returns to lead the Mighty Avengers among friends who share her arete; the self-loathing Jessica Jones finds eudaimonia through philia with Carol, Luke Cage, and the team that delivers her baby; even the arrogant Hank Pym regains excellence by defending Tony and leading a new team. Even gods like Thor and near-beasts like the Hulk, the chapter concludes, need the Avengers to flourish.

aristotle-friendship.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
aristotle-friendship.title: BSFs Best Superfriends Forever
aristotle-friendship.relation: Daniel Malloy argues Batman and Superman are friends who disagree about friendship itself: Superman practices Aristotle's highest philia between good men who are 'another self' and true equals, symbolized by the kryptonite ring he trusts Batman to use on him should he go rogue, while Batman's friendship is Nietzschean, loving in his friend the overman 'as your cause' in the one equal he respects as a rival. Stories like Tower of Babel, Bruce Wayne: Fugitive, and the Brother Eye satellite show Batman manipulates everyone except this one peer, and that he never fights Superman fairly because he does not need to. Their fundamental, unresolvable differences, Malloy concludes, are exactly what strengthen the World's Finest friendship.

aristotle-friendship.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-friendship.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Kowalski maps Aristotle's three kinds of friendship onto the gang: pleasure-friendships (Halo and paintball nights, and Raj's fury when Howard abandons their kite fight for a jogger), utility-friendships (Sheldon's failed Friendship Algorithm bid on Kripke for lab access, and the roommate agreement's Friendship Rider invoked over the CERN trip). Complete friendship — mutual care for the other's own sake between moral equals — looks closest in Leonard and Sheldon, yet Sheldon's pancake-breakfast apology collapses the moment Leonard refuses to take him to Switzerland ('Drat. No Frodo for you'), exposing contractual utility where genuine care should be. The chapter concludes no pairing in the show achieves Aristotle's rare complete friendship, and asks whether similarity is really required for true 'besties.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-friendship.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Barkman diagnoses four mama's boys: Raj's selective mutism under his parents' webcam meddling, Sheldon's comfort-seeking from a fundamentalist mother ('Soft Kitty,' mandatory grace), Howard's learned helplessness with his foghorn mother, and Leonard raised as Beverly's lab subject, his hugging machine echoing the wire-mother monkey experiment. Plato and Aristotle ground the charge of injustice — receiving less than one's station deserves, and wrongs against intimates are 'more terrible' — so parents bear special obligations their neglect breaches, a contemporary point pressed in the care-ethics tradition of Noddings. Cognitive-dissonance theory and Putman's Aristotelian 'psychological courage' prescribe honest self-reckoning for mothers and sons alike, with Leonard furthest along after confronting Beverly in 'The Maternal Congruence.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
aristotle-friendship.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Evans defends the Penny–Sheldon friendship as genuine by three universal marks — mutual care (two Saturnalia-miracle hugs), intimacy (keeping Penny's community-college secret; friends who direct and interpret each other's conduct), and shared activity (singing 'Soft Kitty' in the round) — and then argues its deep differences are not an obstacle but the engine of moral growth. Against Aristotle's similarity-based complete friendship, oriented to a shared eudaimonia, he offers a modern pluralist account: Sheldon's self-aware jokes, dancing, and social awareness and Penny's physics lessons show each growing toward the other's way of flourishing without becoming alike, which a friend as similar as Amy could never force.

aristotle-friendship.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
aristotle-friendship.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: O'Loughlin reads Walter biting off a nihilist's ear and the Dude refusing to walk out on league play as concrete realizations of ancient friendship: Aristotle's eudaimonia requires friends as 'second selves' whose shared activity (bowling in the friends' company) structures the excellent life, while Epicurus's Garden ordered life around simple pleasures and ataraxia, with friendship supplying pleasant memory and a kind of immortality after death. Because we moderns claim friendship's value without practicing its costs, the Dude's priorities look comic yet pierce us — and Donny's death, the Ralph's coffee can, and 'let's go bowling' become Epicurean commemoration rather than irreverence.

aristotle-friendship.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
aristotle-friendship.title: “Oh, honey, I’ll do anything for you”
aristotle-friendship.relation: Using Rachel's Ashley Too doll, the chapter distinguishes robots as instruments (Kevin's MAUZR mouse) from social robots designed to be perceived 'as being present in the way a person is,' and invokes Heidegger's 'Question Concerning Technology' to argue that social robots break the instrumentalist picture: it is our empathy - triggered even by the insubstantial hologram Ashley Eternal - that they exploit. The Aristotelian test of friendship (we emulate those we admire, and friendship forms virtuous character) shows Ashley Too fails: her flattery installs false confidence, and because she never requires Rachel to attend to another's needs, she models no real friendship. Girard's mimetic desire explains Rachel's borrowed aspiration to become Ashley O and Jack's emulation of their dead mother, so the chapter concludes robot 'friends' are poor friends - not because they are machines, but because a real friendship is 'an education in the social virtues.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aristotle-friendship.title: The Sorcerer So Human
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter argues Strange fails Aristotle's golden mean at both stages of his life: as a surgeon he chose cases for money and fame (greed and gluttony rather than generosity and temperance), and as Sorcerer Supreme he swings to the opposite extreme of total self-denial, refusing sleep, love, and friendship with Clea, Wong, and the Ancient One, since relationships between unequals cannot be the reciprocal philia Aristotle demands. It reads his hardest choices—the Dark Dimension left to Dormammu to save Earth, the Illuminati destroying parallel Earths during the incursions, and spending the last drop of the panacea on Wong rather than the world—as tragic dilemmas that show both the virtue ethicist's need for judgment and a defensible-but-excessive partiality toward friends.

aristotle-friendship.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
aristotle-friendship.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jeffery Nicholas contrasts the superman Card seems to write — Graff's isolated Ender conditioned to impose his will like Nietzsche's overman, for whom happiness is only the feeling of overcoming resistance — with Aristotle's claim that man is a political animal who cannot flourish without friends. Peter is Aristotle's 'tribeless, lawless, hearthless' beast, the speechless buggers lack a common good until the queen communicates with Ender, and Ender's despair lifts only through friendship with Valentine, Alai, and Petra, proving the novel a meditation on 'without friends no one would choose to live.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-friendship.title: Snape’s Choice
aristotle-friendship.relation: The section reads Snape's double life through the definition of love shared by writers from Aristotle to Aquinas, willing the good of the other for the other's own sake: he protects people he dislikes because his love for Lily wills their good. As an Occlumens he empties himself of feeling to lie to Voldemort's face, concealing rather than renouncing his love for Lily, and only while dying from Nagini's bite does he freely offer Harry the memories revealing that Harry is a Horcrux.

aristotle-friendship.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-friendship.title: Unknown
aristotle-friendship.relation: Because we each view life from our own 'personal mini-cam,' we can be too close to ourselves to see truly, so friends serve as honest mirrors in which we see ourselves as we really are. Hermione shows Harry his insensitivity to Cho, the trio helps Neville overcome his painful shyness, and Hagrid teaches Ron that friendship should not be wrecked by petty jealousy, while the friendless Dursleys, Lockhart, and Slughorn never progress in self-understanding.

aristotle-friendship.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jackson reads the show through Rousseau's contrast between the general will and a pathological 'corporate will': Frank discards Freddy the moment his criminal past goes viral, Tusk and Walker's old friendship curdles into mutual blackmail, and Remy and Jackie trade intimacy for career protection - all reducing Aristotle's true friendship to friendships of utility and pleasure subordinated to institutions that treat persons as means. Rousseau's account of civilization degrading natural self-love (amour de soi) into vanity (amour-propre) explains why Washington's corporate ethos leaves no friends, only 'loose ends' to be eliminated, from Zoe pushed onto the platform to Doug hunting Rachel. The chapter ends with 'Man is born free, but is everywhere in chains' as the verdict on corporate personhood's conquest of human bonds.

aristotle-friendship.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Johnson sorts Frank's six friendships through Aristotle's three kinds: Freddy and Meechum are friendships of pleasure (ribs and candor; loyalty and sex), while Doug, Cathy Durant, Tusk, and Jackie Sharp are friendships of utility that dissolve when usefulness ends - Jackie endorsing Dunbar being the proof. Even Frank's marriage fails the test of true friendship, since Aristotle holds that only good people can mirror each other's character, and badness corrupts the self-knowledge friendship provides. Because Aristotle deems friendship 'most indispensable for life' and eudaimonia requires virtuous activity joined to good fortune, the chapter ends hoping Frank can still choose the good for its own sake - a hope Claire's walkout after Iowa badly dents.

aristotle-friendship.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Reads the show through Rousseau's contrast between the general will and a pathological 'corporate will': governments and corporations are sociopathic artificial persons that depersonalize their agents, degrading natural self-love (amour de soi) into status-hungry amour-propre. On this account Frank's break with Freddy ('just a good customer'), the Tusk-Walker alliance, and Remy and Jackie's bought loyalties are Aristotelian friendships of utility or pleasure crushed under the corporate will, never true friendship, leaving Washington with 'honor without virtue' and men 'everywhere in chains'.

aristotle-friendship.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Sorts Frank's six friendships using Aristotle's three types: Freddy and Meechum are friendships of pleasure, Doug, Durant, Tusk, and Jackie friendships of utility, while Claire-despite 'I love that woman more than sharks love blood'-cannot be a true friend of the good because true friendship requires two people of good character seeing themselves in each other. Since Aristotle ties friendship to flourishing, the chapter ends hoping that Frank, who has good fortune but neither good character nor true friends, may yet choose virtue and the good life.
