aristotle-friendship.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
aristotle-friendship.title: Here Lies an Avenger
aristotle-friendship.relation: The Pattersons read 'The Mask in the Iron Man' as moral education: Tony's repeated 'I have a good life' litany maps onto Aristotle's eudaimonia — friends like Rhodey, Pepper, and Happy, wealth, health, sobriety, and life itself as goods chosen for the sake of happiness — while Niebuhr's community of value makes the Avengers the community of trust and loyalty that grounds those ideals. Tony fails as teacher when the sentient armor kills Whiplash, cannot grieve with him, and fails Aristotle's friendship test of willing good for the friend for his own sake, its identity dangerously conflated with Tony's. The reversal comes when Tony lives the virtue of self-sacrifice — dying 'because I'm an Avenger' — and the armor, finally grasping nobility, rips out its own mechanical heart to save him, earning the grave marker 'Here lies Iron Man, Avenger.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
aristotle-friendship.title: NOTES
aristotle-friendship.relation: Fosl argues that although the survivors' internal order looks Lockean - Jack's uncoerced leadership, natural rights, minimal government - and is bonded by Rousseauan pity and Humean sympathy (Kate staying in the cage with Sawyer, 'live together, die alone'), the show's deepest political logic follows Carl Schmitt's friend-enemy distinction: the survivors cohere only in opposition to the Others, torture is excused in liberal terms, and conflicts end in redemptive violence, with Jack both killing the enemy and dying a Christlike sacrifice. Hobbes's absence from the character names signals the show's rejection of a war of all against all among the survivors, yet the finale's divine manipulation of the castaways, with Jacob treating people as means against Kantian autonomy, repudiates the liberal hope of a rational peace altogether.

aristotle-friendship.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
aristotle-friendship.title: NOTES
aristotle-friendship.relation: Michael Austin asks what adult children owe their fathers through Jack and Christian Shephard (the drunken-surgery cover-up, 'You don't have what it takes') and Locke and Anthony Cooper (the kidney con, the defenestration). He weighs Jane English's view that parental sacrifice creates friendship rather than debt - so Locke owed Cooper nothing, and true friends like Hurley and the crib-building Locke never keep accounts - against Sidgwick's three possible sources of filial obligation (relationship quality, biological tie, gratitude for services) and David Mellow's debt-of-gratitude argument. Austin concludes that the mutual needs of parents and children - Miles reaching for Pierre Chang in 1974, Jack and Christian's reconciliation in the church - best explain what they owe each other.

aristotle-friendship.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
aristotle-friendship.title: “To a Place Where We Know We Are Loved”
aristotle-friendship.relation: Myers grades the moral development of the Sterling Cooper cast with Kohlberg's justice stages and Gilligan's ethics of care in order to find Aristotelian friendships, which require equals in moral development who wish each other good for the other's sake. Don and Peggy emerge as moral equivalents, each hiding a dark secret (the stolen identity; the baby given away) and each having done for the other what no one else could, from the hospital visit ('Move forward') to Don's 'nobody understands that, but you do' recruitment pitch; Joan and Roger form a second pair whose mutual esteem survives his marriage to Jane and her departure, shown when he trusts her to build Sterling Cooper Draper Pryce. Closing with Aristotle's claim that friendship holds states together, the chapter gives the new agency a better-than-average chance because these friendships are 'not for sale.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-friendship.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Arp and Watson sort Dunder Mifflin's relationships into five conceptions of love: Roy's erotic 'best sex of your life' Valentine's offer to Pam as blind eros; Angela and Dwight's pursuit of an idealized mate read through Plato's Forms and the Symposium's ascent to Beauty; Aristotle's three friendships, under which the office's alliances are mere utility while Jim and Pam's teapot sacrifice in 'Christmas Party' approaches virtue friendship; the Stoic-Kantian 'equal loving' of universal respect, laughed at when Michael ranks himself with Bono and Lincoln; and agape-style family loyalty that leads Dwight to supply Michael his urine in 'Drug Testing'. The chapter concludes that Michael exemplifies a selfishness Western philosophy has no name for, failing at every form of love.

aristotle-friendship.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
aristotle-friendship.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Spanakos asks why Spider-Man is called 'friendly' by testing Peter's relationships against Aristotle's three philias (pleasure, utility, virtue) and the proportionality principle that the morally inferior friend should love the superior more — a principle that breaks down for a superhero as godlike as Spider-Man. Peter's secrecy and self-sacrifice block true Aristotelian fellowship with MJ, whose crush on Spidey is mere fantasy-love, and Harry's friendship rests on pleasure and utility, failing every Aristotelian test. Yet against philia the chapter sets Christian agape (St. Basil, John 15, C.S. Lewis's Four Loves): unconditional, self-sacrificial love for the unlovable, which Peter practices toward his betrayers and which Harry finally enacts when he dies saving Peter in Spider-Man 3 — an agape that makes him Peter's equal.

aristotle-friendship.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
aristotle-friendship.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Eberl reads Jax's Season 5 dilemma (Tara's ultimatum to leave SAMCRO or lose his family) through Aristotle's account of virtue as character cultivated by habituation in a polis. SAMCRO nurtures genuine virtues—Opie's selfless loyalty, courage under fire, the club's communal generosity toward Donna and Lyla—alongside vices like Clay's greed and Tig's lust, with the golden mean distinguishing Bobby's critical loyalty from Chuckie's obsequiousness and Juice's rash minefield charge. Fr. Ashby's fight to keep Abel in Belfast away from Jax's cycle of violence, and the contrast between Deputy Chief Hale's law-abiding ideals and Mayor Hale's self-serving development, illustrate Aristotle's claim that legislators and environments make citizens good or bad. The chapter concludes that Jax's very mix of virtue and vice—the 'savage' needed to head the table—may be what reform requires, at moral cost.

aristotle-friendship.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
aristotle-friendship.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Takes Tig's misplaced revenge on Laroy—which kills Veronica Pope and triggers Damon Pope's burning of Tig's daughter and Opie's prison murder—together with the club's unconditional convoy rescue in 'To Be, Act 1' to ask whether loyalty is a virtue. It tests three accounts: the Aristotelian view (via Ladd's 'loyal Nazi is a contradiction') that only the virtuous can be loyal, which would deny that SAMCRO members can be loyal at all; the Humean view that loyalty is bigoted partiality; and the Kantian point that only the good will is unconditionally good, so loyalty can serve any wrongdoing. The chapter defends Ewin's line that loyalty is good in itself but issues in right action only joined with virtue, while the Stahl frame-up of Opie and Donna's death show the dark enforcement side—'rats deserve to die, end of story.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
aristotle-friendship.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Presents three ancient alternatives to SAMCRO's warrior ethic. Diogenes the Cynic, 'the earliest of all the fathers of anarchy,' matches J.T.'s Harley-commune ideal — reject greed, convention, and wage slavery like Tig punching the clock at Teller-Morrow — but the chapter argues pure anarchy regenerates hierarchy: with no authority, revenge becomes the only justice and 'a big guy like Clay' mugs 'a small guy like Chuckie.' Plato's Republic supplies the reformist pole — impartial justice for all citizens rather than loyalty circles, rulers picked from proven warriors for wisdom (Tara belongs healing, not scheming), family curbed where it breeds Gemma-style favoritism — yet proves too authoritarian, so Aristotle's function argument (reason as the human ergon), virtue, and the three kinds of friendship (SAMCRO's pleasure-friendships, Clay–Unser's usefulness) sketch a livable middle way with duties even to strangers.

aristotle-friendship.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jerold Abrams reads J. J. Abrams's Kirk as Aristotle's megalopsychos and 'god among men' from the Politics: too excellent to be a mere crewmember, disdainful of rank, speaking openly from love and hate, and a law unto himself. The four-on-one bar fight, reprogramming the unwinnable Kobayashi Maru, declaring 'Some should be' above the Prime Directive to Pike, and his exile to frozen Delta Vega (like the Argonauts stranding Heracles) all enact Aristotle's dilemma that a society must either exile such a man or submit to his monarchy. Spock, a great-souled man himself, becomes Kirk's 'second self' in Aristotle's truest friendship once Kirk takes the captain's chair.

aristotle-friendship.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Applies Aristotle's three friendships to Trek: Ferengi Rules of Acquisition dealings and treaties as utility friendships, Bashir and O'Brien's darts and racquetball as friendship of pleasure, and virtuous friendship as requiring emotion, mutual goodwill, and irreplaceable intrinsic valuing - which emotionless Data fails at with Jenna D'Sora in "In Theory". The core argument, following Badhwar, is that consequentialism is logically and psychologically incompatible with virtuous friendship: Spock's "needs of the many" maxim and Data's "for the greater good" experimentation on Geordi in "Descent, Part II" show friends being treated as sacrificeable instruments, while the Kobayashi Maru cheat shows consequentialist reasoning blessing outcomes over means. Kirk's reversal - "the needs of the one outweigh the needs of the many" in The Search for Spock - and T'Pol's years caring for the amnesiac Archer in "Twilight" exemplify acting out of friendship rather than for any further goal.

aristotle-friendship.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Littmann shows Luke, Leia, and Han repeatedly put friends and family above the galaxy's freedom - Luke abandoning Dagobah for Bespin, the Jabba rescue, refusing to kill Vader - in the tradition of Homer's heroes, then submits them to Athenian scrutiny. Socrates's refusal to escape his Athens prison and his implicit just agreement with the city set civic duty over friendship; Plato would abolish the guardians' family and censor the Zeus-Kronos patricide myth yet approves of Luke sparing Vader; Aristotle prizes philia but holds citizens belong to the state. He concludes the philosophers mostly win: heroic loyalty is often moral failure, and good moral reasoning asks how many people an action affects, not just whom you love.

aristotle-friendship.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-friendship.title: Humanoids and Droids Having Sex
aristotle-friendship.relation: Munn and Weijers argue that Lando and L3-37 in Solo display all the hallmarks of friendship and one-sided romantic love: Lando abandons self-preservation to carry the injured L3 to the Falcon and endorses her droid-emancipation crusade, while L3 tells Qi'ra she has considered a relationship with him but finds them 'not compatible'. Testing Bennet Helm's four accounts of love (union, deep mutual caring, valuing, emotional state) against the film, they conclude humanoid-droid love is genuinely possible, and that L3's claim that sex with Lando 'works' is plausible once sex is defined broadly as any activity yielding sexual reward. They ground droid friendship in Aristotle's incomplete versus complete friendships, contrasting the rewarding partnerships of R2-D2 with Anakin and BB-8 with Poe against the merely strategic Han-Lando Sabacc rivalry.

aristotle-friendship.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
aristotle-friendship.title: “And I, I'm All the Jedi!”
aristotle-friendship.relation: Okapal uses Aristotle's three friendships to frame the saga as a story of desert children seeking community: utility friendships like Hondo Ohnaka's and the Sith Rule of Two, where Darth Bane's apprentice is a mere instrument and Sidious calls Maul, Tyranus, and Vader 'easy to replace', stand against the other-regarding virtuous friendships of Obi-Wan, Kanan, and the Rey-Finn-Poe triad, where friends sacrifice for each other's sake as Ezra learns about Kanan in 'A World Between Worlds'. Luke's premature departure for Cloud City fails the 'for the other's sake' test Yoda poses. Rey can only choose the Jedi community knowingly once she learns she is Palpatine's granddaughter, and her closing claim 'I'm Rey Skywalker' is a choice between two value systems - the plural, other-regarding Jedi Code versus the self-regarding 'I' of the Sith Code - making friendship and community, not blood, the root of identity.

aristotle-friendship.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
aristotle-friendship.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Goguen reads the Winchesters through two masculine ideals: the warrior (Dean and Michael, chivalric protection culminating in Dean's 'protecting Sam... it's who I am') and the sovereign (Sam and Lucifer, whose freedom is analyzed with Isaiah Berlin's negative and positive liberty, with nods to Hobbes's absolute sovereign and Nietzsche's Übermensch). The show's stoic culture, where 'baring my soul like a freaking girl' is an insult, keeps the L-word unspoken, making Ellen's dying 'I will always love you, baby' to Jo a foil the brothers cannot match. Plato's Symposium, via Aristophanes' myth of split soulmates, and Aristotle's claim that the purest love is between virtuous male friends make sense of the 'psychotically, irrationally, erotically codependent' bond, and the chapter concludes that true masculinity requires embracing the seemingly supernatural: love.

aristotle-friendship.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Begley and Biondi argue Ted is an ethical egoist in the Aristotelian-Randian sense: like Howard Roark of The Fountainhead (Ted's favorite book), he is a self-loving creator who loves his work, has a 'self-sufficient ego' immune to others' approval, and pursues long-range values, so his kindness and biscuits are rational self-interest, not selflessness. Against Hobbesian psychological egoism they distinguish genuine egoists from narcissists like Rupert and hedonists like Season 1 Jamie, defend Ted's divorce and the curse-reverse ceremony as only apparent sacrifices, and read his panic-attack therapy arc as the egoist's project of achieving inner wholeness.

aristotle-friendship.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Forte maps the Richmond cast onto Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: Rebecca, Nate, Roy, and Jamie begin incontinent or near-vicious; courage is the mean between Nate's cowardice and Roy's rashness; and their friendless misery illustrates why friendship (utility, pleasure, complete) is necessary for eudaimonia. Ted's coaching works as a modern strengths-based complement to Aristotelian habituation - Phoebe's Princess-and-Dragon play tempers Roy, Jamie's competitiveness is redirected into team play, Nate misses the mean and becomes mean - and the finale's 'progress over perfection' framing shows all of them as works in progress toward teloi.

aristotle-friendship.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Loftin argues the Diamond Dogs enact Aristotle's complete friendship: Jamie and Rebecca fail at friendship because they misconceive the good as self-gratification, and following Philippa Foot's natural-kind account of human good (plus Cicero on goodwill and C. S. Lewis's Four Loves) he shows friendship is an intrinsic good of human beings as such. Ted's vulnerability before Beard, Nate, and Higgins invites them into virtuous activity, Higgins's defection from Rebecca's sabotage scheme displays friendship against a relationship fueled by hurt, and Nate's status-hunger explains why he mistakes Ted's laughter and Rupert's patronage for friendship.

aristotle-friendship.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Wible asks whether Ted's friendliness with players and staff constitutes moral friendship, testing it against Aristotle's three friendship types, Hume on solitude, and Bennett Helm's conditions (shared activity, intimacy, mutual care) plus a power-imbalance requirement Kant's respect for persons underwrites. This condemns Rebecca and Sam's relationship as a conflict of interest too risky to permit, questions Led Tasso and benching decisions, yet concludes that Aristotle's virtue friendship between coach and player is possible and preferable to Drewe's limited utility-friendship, since Ted's virtuous friendships make players better people while still knowing when to prioritize team over individual.

aristotle-friendship.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
aristotle-friendship.title: 18. War Means Fighting and Fighting Includes Philosophizing
aristotle-friendship.relation: Vuckovich reads 'Still Valley' through Glaucon's Ring of Gyges: Sgt. Paradine, handed a witchcraft handbook that freezes the Union army before Gettysburg, confronts the temptation of costless, unearned victory, and his burning of the handbook rather than renounce God preserves a principle worth more than winning. Aristotle's claim that bad men can be friends through shared wickedness explains the witchman Teague's bond with Paradine, an 'alliance' that recruits the desperate soldier to do the Devil's dirty work. The chapter ends on the shameful secret legacy: even burying the episode leaves Paradine with a private war in his conscience, a pyrrhic loss for a fighting man who almost surrendered what he holds sacred.

aristotle-friendship.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
aristotle-friendship.title: “See, This Dame Walks In”
aristotle-friendship.relation: Catlyn Origitano sorts Veronica's relationships through Aristotle's three kinds of friendship in the Nicomachean Ethics: Keith and Cliff McCormack's referral exchange is a friendship of utility, Logan and Dick's partying a friendship of pleasure, and Wallace's bond with Veronica utility fraying into his complaint 'How about you do me a favor for once?' when reciprocity turns one-sided. Perfect friendship of virtue requires mutual trust between genuinely good people, and the chapter's audit finds no one qualifies — Wallace lies and cheats, Logan supplied the GHB and ran from the Tijuana fire, and Veronica's snooping and 'I'm not built that way' refusal to trust disqualify her too. She concludes that noir Neptune itself, where 'the people you love let you down,' may block perfect friendship, though the movie-era Veronica, retired from detection, might at last be ready for one.

aristotle-friendship.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Hoffman and Kolmes use Aristotle's friendship as 'another self' and Kant's 'exchange of welfare' to value the pre-New 52 Superman-Wonder Woman friendship (Rucka's heart-to-hearts, Superman choosing to save Wonder Woman over Lois's father), then argue DC's 2011 reboot of the pair into a romance exemplifies Brake's amatonormativity and the heteronormative 'When Harry Met Sally' assumption that cross-gender closeness must be sexual. Diana's answer to Lois - 'We're just good friends' - becomes a refusal to rank friendship below romance. The erasure matters beyond comics: it denies role models for cross-gender friendship and stigmatizes bi and pansexual people as incapable of friendship at all.

aristotle-friendship.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
aristotle-friendship.title: Notes
aristotle-friendship.relation: Tobienne reads Wonder Woman as sophia personified and a rhetorician in Aristotle's sense, whose real weapon is persuasion: he dissects the Rucka 'Lies' dialogue where she talks the feral Cheetah back to her humanity ('You are a WOMAN... You are my FRIEND!') and her verbal disarmament of a mind-sick Power Girl while holding her in a headlock. Nicomachean Ethics VI grounds the claim that practical wisdom recognizes the need for friends - each woman needs the other - and Wonder Woman's own submission to Athena and Aphrodite explains how the lasso of loving authority, not brute force, disarms Man's World.

aristotle-friendship.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-friendship.title: Building Communities One Gym at a Time
aristotle-friendship.relation: Webb uses Indiana high school basketball to argue the communitarian case against liberal individualism: drawing on MacIntyre, Sandel, and Walzer, he contends communities (not rights-bearing individuals) are the source of meaning, and that small-town gyms like the New Castle Fieldhouse were public spaces that built genuine community. He reads Rick Mount's choice of hometown fame over the pros, the Milan miracle, and the abolition of Indiana's single-class tournament as evidence that mass media and national sport replace real 'face-to-face' communities with 'virtual' ones, using Conseco Fieldhouse's nostalgic theming as his prime example of that loss.

aristotle-friendship.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
aristotle-friendship.title: The Beauty of the Game
aristotle-friendship.relation: The Brands stage a broadcast-booth debate about whether a championship game was 'beautiful,' with Dickie V defending Hume's subjectivism ('beauty is in the eye of the beholder' and the expert's delicacy of taste) and Billy defending Plato's objective Form of Beauty. Jim exposes each side's flaw (Hume's circular appeal to experts, Plato's third-man regress from the Parmenides/Aristotle) and proposes a synthesis: games have 'outer beauty' (universally observable fluid motion, like improvised jazz or dance) and 'inner beauty' (the strategy and reason the knowledgeable fan grasps), reconciling the objective and subjective.

aristotle-friendship.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
aristotle-friendship.title: Football and Aristotle'S Philosophy of Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Gallagher maps Aristotle's three kinds of philia onto football: friendship of utility (the quarterback needing his offensive linemen), of pleasure (Friday-night high school and college ball), and of shared goodness (Bo Schembechler's bond with Anthony Carter, who deflected reporters to teammates). He reads the Steelers dynasty and Paterno's locker-room 'love' through Aristotle's 'concord' and 'a single soul in two bodies,' and answers Bertrand Russell's worry about violent competition by insisting football is grounded in philia, not enmity.

aristotle-friendship.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
aristotle-friendship.title: Seventeenth Hole More Than a Playing Partner Golf and Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Andy Wible argues that although golf looks like the ultimate solitary sport, it is unusually good at fostering friendship, and analyzes friendship through Aristotle's three kinds (utility, pleasure, and the highest, based on the friend's good character), supplemented by Laurence Thomas (choice, equality, mutual trust) and Blum on care as a moral phenomenon. Golf's long unhurried rounds, self-called penalties, handicap system, shared memorable shots, and retirement communities build the intimacy, trust and equality Aristotle prizes, and Robert Simon's 'mutual quest for excellence' reconciles competition with goodwill. Wible then confronts friendship's partiality—exclusionary country clubs and the sex-segregated LPGA—using Marilyn Friedman's voluntary friendship communities to argue clubs should drop discrimination on race, sex, religion and orientation while keeping friendship's care and loyalty.

aristotle-friendship.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
aristotle-friendship.title: Friendship, Rivalry, and Excellence
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter uses Aristotle's three friendships (pleasure, usefulness, virtue) to ask how tennis rivals competing for one prize can be friends, illustrating pleasure with Borg and Gerulaitis, usefulness with the tense but genuine Ashe-McEnroe Davis Cup bond, and virtue with the Evert-Navratilova rivalry that grew into deep mutual care despite a competitive women's tour. It adds C. S. Lewis's view that friends stand side by side absorbed in a shared thing, then reads Jimmy Connors as a Nietzschean Ubermensch whose master-morality drive to dominate makes him, paradoxically, the best 'star friend' by pushing rivals to their limits. It closes unresolved on whether the tension between friendship and rivalry can ever be eliminated.

aristotle-friendship.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
aristotle-friendship.title: Me and You Identity, Love, and Friendship in the Films of Charlie Kaufman
aristotle-friendship.relation: Den Uyl argues that Kaufman's films are really about friendship rather than romance, reading them through Aristotle's character friendship (the friend as 'other self' and mirror of self-knowledge) and Montaigne's ideal of a free, voluntary friendship that also engages the body. Charlie's fictional twin Donald in Adaptation externalizes the integrity Charlie lacks, and only after internalizing Donald can he say 'I love her'; Caden in Synecdoche fails because he looks only at himself. Love succeeds, on this reading, only when grounded in the self-sufficiency and self-respect that make one capable of an 'other self,' as Eternal Sunshine's Joel and Clementine haltingly discover.

aristotle-friendship.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
aristotle-friendship.title: Charlie Kaufman, Philosophy, and the Small Screen
aristotle-friendship.relation: Chambers reads Kaufman's TV sitcom Ned and Stacey through queer theory, arguing its marriage-of-convenience premise stages a critique of 'the normal.' Because Ned and Stacey only play at being husband and wife and never desire the romantic telos, the show troubles heteronormativity more than the openly gay Will & Grace, whose characters chase marriage and family. Chambers uses Butler's Lacanian notion of masquerade to claim there is no 'real' husband or wife beneath the role, only role-playing, and ties this to the philia (not eros) bond of the leads and to the masquerade running through Kaufman's films.

aristotle-friendship.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-friendship.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-friendship.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Eastwood, though no academic, does 'practical philosophy' through his films as a craftsman who inherits and then revises genres (revising the Western in Unforgiven, rethinking rugged individualism in Million Dollar Baby and Gran Torino). Invoking MacIntyre's claim that we are only co-authors of interlocking narratives, it reads Eastwood's focus on decisive moral choices (Francesca's refusal to leave in Bridges of Madison County, Butch Haynes in A Perfect World) as a 'laboratory of moral psychology' echoing Aristotle's 'choice discriminates character.' It ties his concern with loss, justice, and Aristotelian friendship and flourishing (Grinnell on Million Dollar Baby) to a Socratic 'know thyself,' arguing his philosophizing is implicit and nonverbal rather than argued in words.

aristotle-friendship.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-friendship.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aristotle-friendship.relation: Grinnell applies Aristotle's classification of friendship (utility, pleasure, and complete character-friendship between equals in excellence) to Million Dollar Baby and Gran Torino. Frankie/Maggie and Walt/Thao begin as incomplete, utility relationships across barriers of age, sex, and culture, then ripen into character-friendships of 'other selves' who pursue each other's good. He resolves the apparent paradox that friendship demands bringing about a death: Frankie euthanizes Maggie against his own wishes to honor her autonomy and whole-life excellence, while Walt engineers his own death and deceives Thao to spare him a vengeance that would destroy his character — each an Aristotelian sacrifice of self-interest for the friend that preserves the friendship's excellence.

aristotle-friendship.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
aristotle-friendship.title: “And It’s Such a Beautiful Day!” shame and Fargo
aristotle-friendship.relation: Hanrahan and Stearns read Fargo through Aristotle's theory of shame and its link to friendship, sorting the characters into his moral hierarchy: Gaear is the shameless self-indulgent man, Jerry is the morally incontinent one whose flickers of shame (before Scotty, before the swindled customer) stay inert against his greed, and Marge is the exemplar of excellence. They argue that a capacity for shame requires valuing others non-instrumentally, which the co-conspirators cannot do because they relate only through friendships of utility (Carl and the prostitute, Jerry using his son). Marge's friendship-of-the-good with Norm grounds both her decency and her ability to mediate others' shame, and her 'it's such a beautiful day' expresses the same noninstrumental valuing that makes moral concern possible.

aristotle-friendship.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
aristotle-friendship.title: On Being Horrible (and an Angel)
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter runs Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge from the Republic against the Whedonverse: invisibility in 'Out of Mind, Out of Sight' and 'Gone' (where even Buffy takes a self-serving 'vacation from herself'), the invincibility ring in 'In the Dark' that Angel destroys rather than uses, and the Buffy-Faith body switch in 'Who Are You?' as the unjust person with a virtuous reputation versus the just person misunderstood. Plato's tripartite-soul answer is only partly confirmed—Faith spirals into torment after killing the deputy mayor, but Saffron cons without any inner turmoil—so the chapter turns to Aristotle: the good life needs external goods, above all friendship and community. This explains why Whedon's wrongdoers (Woody in Toy Story, Jayne in 'Ariel,' Gunn, Stark, Buffy in 'Revelations') must atone before their communities, why Mal's 'you only need a few [good people]' rebukes Saffron, and why both Dr. Horrible and Captain Hammer are tragic—each lives alone and friendless, having squandered Penny.

aristotle-friendship.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
aristotle-friendship.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
aristotle-friendship.relation: Sanders reads Casino as a dramatization of ethical egoism, using the parasitic bond between Nicky Santoro and Ace Rothstein to ask whether an egoist who treats a friend as a mere instrument can have real friendship. He distinguishes 'maximizing' egoism (Nicky's ruinous take-everything drive, ending in his beating death) from a 'satisficing' egoism that restricts its own dispositions, arguing against Blum, Wilcox and an Aristotelian objection that only the maximizing version is truly incompatible with friendship. Aristotle's account of virtue and friendship supplies the standard the film's egoists fall short of.

aristotle-friendship.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
aristotle-friendship.title: Watsons, Adlers, Lestrades, and Moriarties On the Nature of Friends and Enemies
aristotle-friendship.relation: Tallon applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics taxonomy of friendship—of use, of pleasure, and of virtue—to Holmes's relationships, plus Aquinas on friends helping each other flourish. The Baker Street Irregulars and Mrs. Hudson are friends of use; Holmes has few friends of pleasure; Watson is the friend of virtue, an 'other self' sharing virtue, support, and activity (getting Holmes off cocaine, taking a bullet). Inverting the account, he classifies Holmes's enemies as competitor (Irene Adler), rival/'frenemy' (Lestrade and Gregson), and foe (Moriarty), arguing a foe—an anti-self—can never become a friend.

aristotle-friendship.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
aristotle-friendship.title: Love, Value, and the Human Destiny in Interstellar
aristotle-friendship.relation: The chapter stages Interstellar's conflict between Cooper's partial love for his own family and Professor Brand's species-level duty as a question about the intrinsic value of humanity. Using Aristotle's account of friends and children as 'other selves' and of happiness as the one end sought for its own sake, it argues that the species survives only as a byproduct of particular, partial loves, so Plan B's bank of 5,000 faceless embryos could not preserve 'us' in any meaningful sense. Kant's unconditional dignity of rational persons supplies Brand's premise that our existence enriches the universe, but the chapter turns Kant against him: Brand's monstrous lie to the Endurance crew treats persons as mere means to an end they do not share, trampling the very dignity it claims to save. It closes by asking what value colonizing Edmunds's planet would destroy—ecosystems, microbial life, and possibly other rational persons whose dignity we would be obliged to respect—should humanity refuse to 'go gentle into that good night.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: I Am the Bad Wolf
aristotle-friendship.relation: Roman Altshuler answers Davros's charge that the Doctor is a 'destroyer of worlds' using Aristotelian virtue ethics. He argues the Doctor's chief virtue is not compassion but Heideggerian 'authentic concern': offering aggressors (the Nestene, Sontarans, the Master) a genuine choice so they become responsible for escalating, illustrated by the fly-swatter thought experiment. Companions, being 'another self' (Aristotle on friendship), make their acts partly the Doctor's own, yet their human 'Bad Wolf Syndrome' lets compassion override the impartial concern that requires respecting choice, which is why the Doctor runs from what his companions do in his name.

aristotle-friendship.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
aristotle-friendship.title: 10. Cas Is Family
aristotle-friendship.relation: Doll traces Castiel's arc from a cold Divine-Command/utilitarian 'hammer of the Lord' to a member of the Winchester family through Aristotle's ethics. She argues Cas learns to contemplate and act on the chief good under Dean's tutelage, pursuing eudaimonia by habituation despite repeated failures (becoming a false god, the Leviathans), and that his bond with Sam and Dean grows through Aristotle's three friendships—utility, pleasure, and finally the rare true friendship of virtuous character—culminating in his self-sacrificing declaration of love that defeats Billie.

aristotle-friendship.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
aristotle-friendship.title: NOTES
aristotle-friendship.relation: Michael W. Austin applies Jane English's claim that adult children owe their parents 'nothing' to the fraught father-son relationships of Lost. He works through Jack and Christian Shephard's operating-room cover-up, Locke being conned out of a kidney and paralyzed by Anthony Cooper, and Sawyer's murder-suicide father to argue that parental sacrifices create debts only on the commonsense view English rejects. English's alternative is that such sacrifices ideally generate friendship rather than obligation, which Austin illustrates with the unbookkept mutual aid among Sawyer, Kate, Hurley, and Locke, contrasting Jack's line 'I'm not one of his friends' about retrieving his dead father.

aristotle-friendship.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
aristotle-friendship.title: 18. War Means Fighting and Fighting Includes Philosophizing
aristotle-friendship.relation: Vuckovich analyzes 'Still Valley,' where Confederate Sergeant Paradine can win the Civil War using a witchcraft handbook that freezes Union troops but only by renouncing God. He reads Paradine's temptation through Glaucon's Ring of Gyges myth in Plato's Republic (the committed unjust man who outdoes enemies without scruple) and Aristotle's friendships of shared pleasure (Paradine and the witchman Teague bonded by hatred of the enemy). Paradine burns the handbook rather than damn the Confederacy, preserving a core principle of fairness even at the cost of an easy victory—winning isn't everything.

aristotle-friendship.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: Stephen King and Aristotelian Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Bertha Alvarez Manninen reads The Body (Stand by Me) and Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption through Aristotle's Nicomachean and Eudemian Ethics on the three friendships. Andy and Norton/the guards exemplify friendships of utility (the tax help, the Rita Hayworth poster), the boys' tree-house camaraderie and Vern/Teddy exemplify pleasure friendships that dissolve as characters change, while Gordie-and-Chris and Andy-and-Red model enduring friendships of virtue rooted in mutual good will, shared confidences, and cultivating each other's excellence. Manninen then presses Aristotle: his strict 'only good men' criterion and his debt-bound, property-like view of the parent-child bond fail the flawed-but-loyal Andy/Red and the abusive fathers in The Body, showing human friendship is more complex than his taxonomy allows.

aristotle-friendship.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Marinucci's editorial introduction surveys the volume, framing Austen's six novels as a body of work with philosophical value across love/marriage, morality/virtue, wealth/class, concepts, and zombie mashups. It previews each contributor's thesis: Bufacchi reading Anne Elliot and the Bennets through Fricker's epistemic injustice, Dougherty aligning Austen's ideal marriage with Aristotelian complete friendship, Lindenmuth pairing Austen with Nietzsche on marital happiness, and Bane's Marxist reading of the 1940 Pride and Prejudice film. It argues Austen is an 'accidental philosopher' whose insight into social relations, especially women's vulnerability, carries philosophical weight.

aristotle-friendship.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Dougherty argues Austen's ideal marriage mirrors Aristotle's complete friendship, where the friend is loved for who they are and becomes a 'second self.' She sorts Austen's relationships into Aristotle's three kinds: utility (Emma and Mrs. Elton, Charlotte and Mr. Collins), pleasure (Lydia and Wickham, the fading Emma-Harriet bond), and complete friendship grounded in mutual good character (Jane and Bingley, Elizabeth and Darcy, Emma and Knightley). Central is the 'second self' as mirror: Darcy's letter and Knightley's rebukes let Elizabeth and Emma see themselves ('Till this moment I never knew myself'), so marriage-as-friendship improves self-knowledge and virtue and must not be left to chance as Charlotte urges.

aristotle-friendship.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
aristotle-friendship.title: Chapter 1
aristotle-friendship.relation: Verene argues that cooking marks the transition from nature to culture, reading Plato's Protagoras myth of Prometheus (fire and the practical arts) and the Republic's claim that a city's first need is food as evidence that humans alone 'eat' rather than 'feed.' Tracing Greco-Roman banquets, Vico's account of Roman dining, and Brillat-Savarin's Physiology of Taste, he connects the ordered courses of a proper meal to Aristotle's view of imagination as rooted in memory and to friendship at table. He ends by mapping Brillat-Savarin's gourmandism onto Epicurus's distinction between kinetic pleasures (eating fine food) and catastematic pleasure (ataraxia, the settled well-being of good health and stored memories of shared meals).

aristotle-friendship.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
aristotle-friendship.title: Chapter 2
aristotle-friendship.relation: Verene interprets Plutarch's Dinner of the Seven Wise Men, in which Thales, Solon, Bias and the others gather at Corinth under Periander and turn a plain dinner into a symposium on good government, household economics, and the soul. He reads their exchanges through Aristotle: Thales' claim that a ruler's happiness is to die naturally in old age is glossed by Aristotle's eudaimonia (no one is called happy until life is complete), the assigned-seating companions exemplify Aristotle's friendship of utility, and the pivot from politics to home management mirrors Aristotle linking Politics to Economics. Solon's Stoic argument that dependence on food enslaves the soul, and Thales' correction of the Ethiopian king's riddle-answers (virtue not God as most helpful), show the Seven speaking as philosophers rather than gourmets, with Epicurus invoked on death being nothing to the living.

aristotle-friendship.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
aristotle-friendship.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-friendship.relation: Carreras, writing as a son, examines the ethical tension in the father-son relationship between using a father's inevitable influence and fostering the son's autonomy. Opening with Aristotle on parents loving children as 'something of himself,' he uses the case of Jerry (a lawyer) pressuring his son Jose (who loves 18th-century English literature) to argue for a 'foundational view' of autonomy – that the best life is one embraced 'from the inside,' likened to seeing without a value-blindfold – and advises fathers to ask 'Is this what he truly wants, or what I want?'

aristotle-friendship.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
aristotle-friendship.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
aristotle-friendship.relation: This span closes the walk-of-shame semiotics and then applies ancient ethics to college relationships. Puka defends long-distance college relationships through Aristotle's account of philia—arguing (provocatively, per Aristotle) that love is an activity, so being apart 'murders' love unless couples make Skype, sexting, and texting into the relationship's real medium rather than a substitute. Stephens brings Epicurus and Lucretius to 'friends with benefits': since sexual passion is a natural-but-unnecessary desire that breeds anxiety and love is a wound to the mind, while friendship is necessary for ataraxia, he concludes students should skip the sex and keep the friend—'friends are the real benefits,' echoing Tina Turner's 'What's Love Got to Do with It?' Levine/Mongeau and Smith/Morrison supply communication-research data on how FWB relationships form, are negotiated (usually not), and often end when one partner 'catches feelings.'

aristotle-friendship.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
aristotle-friendship.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-friendship.relation: Editors Kristie Miller and Marlene Clark introduce the volume by opening with Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics claim that the human drive to couple is even stronger than the drive to live as a political being and that fulfillment rests in loving relationships. They frame dating as a rule-governed 'game' with aims and strategies and preview each contributor's essay—Jenkins on flirting, Langan on conservative men, Samp and Cohen against unconditional love, the elevator metaphor, cyberdating, evolutionary seduction, and Colyvan's game-theoretic mate search—tying age-old ethical questions about treating partners well to new work in evolutionary psychology, decision theory, and the ethics of online romance.

aristotle-friendship.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
aristotle-friendship.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jennifer Samp and Andrew Cohen argue against the Notebook-style romantic ideal of unconditional love, casting dating as a 'calculated exchange' explained by social-exchange and interdependence theory (comparison level and comparison level of alternatives). Adopting Aristotle's distinction between friendships of utility/pleasure and 'complete friendships' in which one values the friend as 'another self' and as an end in itself, they hold the best romances are complete friendships—yet insist even these must be conditioned. Their key thought experiment: a genuinely boundless love would survive discovering one's partner is a child-molesting murderer; since it should not, 'true love knows bounds' and remains part of a good life only because it can be defeated by such reasons.

aristotle-friendship.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
aristotle-friendship.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-friendship.relation: Mary Beth Yount asks whether being 'crazy in love' really resembles mental illness, noting lovesickness was a diagnosis for nearly two millennia and that love's mood swings mimic bipolar or schizophrenic symptoms. She organizes the analysis around the four Greek loves—eros (with Plato's ladder from physical beauty to the Forms, i.e., 'Platonic love'), philia (Aristotle's Nicomachean friendship of good character), storge (familial affection), and agape (C.S. Lewis's unconditional charity)—arguing a full romance blends all four. She then surveys Fisher, Aron, and Brown's fMRI work showing romantic love as a dopamine-driven mammalian mate-choice drive stronger than the sex drive, and the 'protest'/'resignation' stages of rejection, to reassure daters their craziness is normal biology, not disorder.

aristotle-friendship.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
aristotle-friendship.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-friendship.relation: Joshua Heter mounts a virtue-theoretic case against being set up on blind dates, using Aristotle's notion of telos and the distinction between fleeting 'hot-fudge happiness' and eudaimonia, the flourishing of a well-lived life (illustrated by long-married Bill and Fran). He argues a 'guy's' function is achieved by exercising his whole nature, and dramatizes this with Zoo-bear versus Wild-bear: the zoo-fed bear has its hunger and safety met but cannot flourish because it never hunts or roams, just as matchmaking meets the romantic need while letting a man's 'social muscles' atrophy. Invoking Aristotle's philia (and Nussbaum on Aristotelian virtue), he concedes friends mean well but recommends they merely introduce people and let things progress naturally rather than force an 'unnatural' match.

aristotle-friendship.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
aristotle-friendship.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
aristotle-friendship.relation: Hamilton reads the pick-up-artist 'Game' (Mystery, Style, negs, peacocking, the Alpha frame) against Aristotle's great-souled magnanimous man, arguing that the jerk and the PUA succeed because they inadvertently mimic the Megalopsuche's self-containment and indifference to others' approval. He contends the ethical route is to genuinely acquire that character through habituation ('we become brave by acting bravely') rather than fake it, so the nice guy's supplication fails while true magnanimity requires the full virtues. He then uses Aristotle's three grades of friendship (utility, pleasure, and the highest disinterested philia) to argue that erotic relationships can rise to real friendship only where partners are equals, citing When Harry Met Sally on whether men and women can be friends.

aristotle-friendship.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
aristotle-friendship.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Gregory Bassham mines the happy communities of the Shire, Rivendell, and Lothlorien for six keys to happiness: delight in simple things (linked to Epicurus's natural pleasures and Thoreau's Walden simplicity), making light of troubles, close friendship (grounded in Aristotle's claim that friendship is the greatest external good), good character, cherishing beauty and creativity, and recovering wonder. He argues Tolkien's hobbits and elves illustrate what modern happiness research confirms, so Tolkien functions as a philosophical guide to a more joy-filled life.

aristotle-friendship.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
aristotle-friendship.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.relation: Jorge Gracia contrasts Sam and Gollum, two hobbits of shared nature and culture who both pursue happiness but reach opposite ends. Gollum's happiness is possession of the Precious, a thing, sought in isolation and won by murdering Deagol, which destroys him; Sam's happiness is fellowship in the Shire with Frodo and Rosie, and his love for Frodo lets him surrender the Ring where Gollum cannot. Drawing on Aristotle's tie between happiness, one's nature, and friendship, Gracia concludes that for ordinary beings happiness is achievable only in a social context whose key is love expressed as loyalty and sharing.

aristotle-friendship.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: 12. Firefly as Philosophy Social Contracts, Political Dissent, and Virtuous Communities
aristotle-friendship.relation: Kowalski argues that Firefly and Serenity embody a distinctive political theory he calls 'Since I Found Serenity' (SIFS). The mindless, savage Reavers represent Hobbes's state of nature, showing government is necessary; but the Alliance's torture of River, the Miranda/Pax atrocity, and the murderous blue-gloved agents and Operative make a Hobbesian reading untenable and vindicate Locke's natural rights and right of revolution — Mal's 'I aim to misbehave' broadcast of the Miranda file is Lockean civil disobedience. He then presses the tacit-consent problem (the Browncoats cannot leave the 'Verse) and supplements Locke with Aristotle's friendship and community: Serenity's crew becomes a virtuous mobile commonwealth where friendship (Simon forgiving Jayne, Mal's 'love keeps her in the air') turns a commonwealth into a good-life community.

aristotle-friendship.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: 13. Arrested Development as Philosophy Family First What We Owe Our Parents
aristotle-friendship.relation: Phillips uses the dysfunctional Bluths to ask what, if anything, adult children owe their parents. Against Sidgwick's reluctance and various grounds for filial obligation, he argues negatively through the family: George Sr. and Lucille never meet the motivation and above-duty conditions for a debt of gratitude; adopted Lindsay's absentee mothering of Maeby shows biology alone grounds nothing; and Michael's dutiful-son and overbearing-father roles show the social role of 'parent' is not enough (Hardimon's 'reflectively acceptable' roles). Positively, deploying Aristotle's three friendships (utility, pleasure, virtue), he argues that only a voluntary friendship of virtue grounds special obligations — illustrated when a rock-bottom, 'useless' Gob and George Sr. finally bond as near-equals, the show's closest thing to genuine friendship.

aristotle-friendship.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: 38. The Big Lebowski Nihilism, Masculinity, and Abiding Virtue
aristotle-friendship.relation: Fosl argues that The Big Lebowski critiques traditional masculine ideals (soldier, tycoon, detective, patriarch) and offers in The Dude an alternative 'abiding' virtue rooted in Epicurean contented poverty and ataraxia (his simple pleasures, White Russians, and indifference to property), Aristotelian civic friendship or philia with Walter and Donny that holds a divided polity together, and a Wittgenstein/Aristotle-informed flexibility about applying rules that positions The Dude at a mean between Walter's rigid absolutism and the nihilists' deficiency. Most centrally the film confronts Nietzschean European nihilism ('God is dead'); The Dude answers it as a halfway Ubermensch through comedy, friendship, and Kierkegaardian and Camusian existential repetition (bowling as rolling the rock, Sisyphus made meaningful), abiding and reproducing his form of life against despair, death, and disillusionment.

aristotle-friendship.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
aristotle-friendship.title: 39. Harry Potter as Philosophy Five Types of Friendship
aristotle-friendship.relation: Okapal uses the Harry Potter films to expand Aristotle's theory of philia (friendship/love), which recognizes friendships for virtue, pleasure, and utility grounded in other-regarding concern, intimacy, choice, and a surrounding community. He argues the films show that friendships for pleasure and utility each come in beneficent and maleficent forms distinguished by whether motivations are other-regarding or purely self-regarding: the Quidditch team and the Harry-Ginny romance are beneficent pleasure-friendships (Ginny hides the Prince's book out of concern for Harry), while the Hermione-McLaggen date and Ron-Lavender fling are maleficent and short-lived. Slughorn's Slug Club is a beneficent utility-friendship of mutual advantage one may freely leave, whereas Voldemort's Death Eaters are maleficent, with all benefit flowing one way and no exit, yielding five types of friendship and locating Gryffindor's courage, inclusiveness, and loyalty as the ground of virtuous friendship.

philosopher-king.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
philosopher-king.title: 2 - Lisa and American Anti-intellectualism
philosopher-king.relation: Aeon Skoble argues Lisa's treatment on the show captures America's love-hate relationship with expertise: she saves Homer's life by talking Dr. Nick through heart surgery and exposes political corruption, yet her intellectualism is itself made the butt of jokes. He sorts legitimate appeal to authority from the informal fallacy version and from the relativism that declares all opinions equally valid, tracing the problem to democratic equality. The Mensa episode 'They Saved Lisa's Brain'—where Lisa, Professor Frink, and the Comic Book Guy rule Springfield with censorious, Star Trek-inspired decrees—is read as satirizing not only Homer's mob but Plato's philosopher-kings themselves, whose utopian rule of the wise proves unstable and foolish.

philosopher-king.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
philosopher-king.title: 11 - The Simpsons Atomistic Politics and the Nuclear Family
philosopher-king.relation: Paul Cantor argues that beneath the satire The Simpsons affirms the nuclear family: the foster-care episode, where the children go to the Flanderses and Homer and Marge to a 'family skills class', shows they belong with their real parents not for piety or child-rearing expertise but because of attachment to one's own—against both the therapeutic nanny state and Flanders-style self-righteous religiosity. He connects this defense of the family to Springfield as a classical polis of local, accessible institutions (Skinner, Wiggum, Quimby, even locally produced Itchy & Scratchy), where distrust of remote power cuts across party lines. The Mensa utopia episode serves as a comic refutation of Plato's philosopher-kings—Homer leads the 'counterrevolution of the stupid' and Stephen Hawking pronounces that 'the smartest of us can be the most childish'—echoing Nietzsche's remark that Kant defended the common man against the learned.

philosopher-king.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
philosopher-king.title: Unknown
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter contrasts two theories of liberation: the Platonic one, where an exceptional external liberator - a philosopher-king, or the traditional God-man savior the film's characters initially expect - leads humanity out of illusion, and Kant's Enlightenment alternative that 'the slaves can only be truly free if they free themselves', with Jesus recast as the model of our own inner potential rather than a miracle-working savior. The film's arc, it argues, moves from Choi's 'my own personal Jesus Christ' (a caricature of liberation) to a finale that overturns all expectations of an external savior.

philosopher-king.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
philosopher-king.title: Unknown
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter concludes that the One is a universal Teacher rather than an exceptional Superman-Savior: liberation cannot come from a Philosopher King or an all-powerful benefactor, since sleeping humanity already rejected the unearned happiness the AI's first Matrix offered. Neo's closing promise of 'a world without rules and controls, without borders or boundaries, a world where anything is possible' echoes Jesus's 'the works that I do, shall he do also' - he shows others how to be like him, so 'the One may be the first superhuman being, but he is not the last'.

philosopher-king.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
philosopher-king.title: Plato and Dumbledore Separated at Birth
philosopher-king.relation: David Lay Williams and Alan J. Kellner open their essay with paired epigraphs from Dumbledore ('Those who are best suited to power are those who have never sought it') and Plato ('A city in which those who are going to rule are least eager to rule is necessarily best'). Against Lord Acton's dictum that power corrupts, they present Plato's ingeniously simple solution - power must never reside with those who lust for it, since disinterest paradoxically makes the best rulers - and announce that this lesson is central to the climax of the entire Harry Potter series.

philosopher-king.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
philosopher-king.title: Fudge and Umbridge The Lessons of Obviously Unfit Power-Brokers
philosopher-king.relation: The section draws a biography-by-biography parallel between Plato and Dumbledore: each lived through upheaval (the Peloponnesian War, the Thirty, and Socrates' execution; Grindelwald and Voldemort), each renounced a political career after disillusion, and each turned from politics to education, founding the Academy and leading Hogwarts. It explains the Republic's philosopher-rulers and their four cardinal virtues, argues that intelligence alone (Lex Luthor, Hannibal Lecter) plus excessive self-love disqualifies a ruler, and introduces Glaucon's Ring of Gyges as Plato's test of incorruptibility - a legend it says Rowling revives in Harry's invisibility cloak.

philosopher-king.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
philosopher-king.title: Voldemort and Dumbledore Two Tempted by Power
philosopher-king.relation: The authors run Plato's criteria on the wizarding world's obviously unfit power-brokers. Umbridge fails as a ruler: her 'I must not tell lies' blood-quill detentions and multiplying Educational Decrees expose a lust for power that grows with her authority, and she lacks all the cardinal virtues, especially self-control. Fudge's insecurity proves equally corrupting - his denial of Voldemort's return, smearing Harry in the press, and tilting Harry's Wizengamot hearing (moving its time to exclude Dumbledore) all serve only to keep him in office, so both, like Plato's tyrants, lose the power they clutch at.

philosopher-king.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
philosopher-king.title: Harry’s Cloak, the Ring of Gyges, and the Temptations of Power
philosopher-king.relation: This section contrasts Voldemort and Dumbledore as two figures tempted by power. Tom Riddle's egocentrism - frightening and controlling other children at the orphanage, treating his 'friends' as mere followers, killing Lily, and splintering his soul for Horcruxes - violates Kant's dictum never to use persons merely as means and fits Plato's category of the least trustworthy rulers. Dumbledore, though tempted in youth by Grindelwald's 'for the greater good' schemes and later by Marvolo Gaunt's ring, is venerable for Socratic self-knowledge: knowing 'I was not to be trusted with power,' he repeatedly refused the Ministry and so promoted justice by teaching.

philosopher-king.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
philosopher-king.title: NOTES
philosopher-king.relation: The concluding section argues that Harry passes Plato's Ring of Gyges test, which Rowling rebuilds around the Invisibility Cloak: unlike Gyges, Harry never uses invisibility for selfish gain, refuses Scrimgeour's offer of his dream job, hunts Horcruxes rather than making them, and at eleven pulls the Sorcerer's Stone from his pocket precisely because Dumbledore's enchantment lets only someone who wants to find but not use it do so. This indifference to the lure of power, joined to courage, justice, and self-restraint, is the Platonic quality that makes Harry fit to rule.

philosopher-king.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
philosopher-king.title: Palpatine’s Legacy
philosopher-king.relation: Decker reconstructs Palpatine's career as a case study in how democracies die: using Aristotle's definition of tyranny and the precedent of Pisistratus and Julius Caesar, he shows Palpatine manufacturing the Separatist threat so the Senate grants him emergency powers - a twist on Machiavelli's loved-versus-feared dictum in which playing the reluctant democrat is itself the means to absolute rule. The Attack of the Clones debate between Anakin ('Someone wise' should make people agree) and Padme becomes a clash between Leo Strauss's philosopher-king ideal of rule by the virtuous few and John Dewey's conception of democracy as a way of life trusting the intelligence of common people, with Rousseau's social contract framing the stakes. The chapter concludes that democratic ends require democratic means and that unaccountable 'watchers' - Straussian statesmen or Anakins - are exactly the path to Empire.

philosopher-king.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
philosopher-king.title: From Rhyme to Reason This Shit Ain’t Easy
philosopher-king.relation: The editors' introduction argues that hip hop and philosophy are both street-born examinations of life in pursuit of wisdom: Socrates's elenchus is likened to MC lyrical battles and call-and-response (his interrogations compared to Rakim's technique, his execution for corrupting the youth to the fate of a controversial rapper), while Plato's philosopher-king parallels Kurtis Blow and Run-D.M.C. claiming thrones. After a Bronx hip-hop history sketch (Kool Herc, BDP's "The Bridge is Over"), they frame the volume around hip hop's suppressed fifth element of knowledge and preview its pairings: Aquinas and Rakim on God, Plato and Lauryn Hill on love, Sartre and Lil' Kim's gaze, Kant and Ice Cube on punishment, Hegel and Nas, Hobbes and Dead Prez, Mill and Chappelle on epithets. Record companies don't own hip hop and universities don't own philosophy, they conclude - both belong to whoever understands, loves, and respects them.

philosopher-king.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
philosopher-king.title: U2 and Philosophy
philosopher-king.relation: Delancey asks why anyone should take moral and political cues from a rock band and answers via Heidegger: in a mediascape where a few corporations orchestrate what everyone hears, the mass tune is das Man ('Numb'), and adopting it is inauthenticity - so U2, who believe what they sing for their own reasons ('Mothers of the Disappeared' against the official line on Latin America), may be among the most authentic voices available. Plato's tripartite soul and Aristotle's golden mean supply the thesis that reason needs rightly trained passion: the righteous anger of 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and 'Silver and Gold' and the resolve of 'Walk On' are practical wisdom in song, the emotions democracy requires. Against Plato's philosopher-king and his noble lies, Delancey argues utopia can only be fostered, not enforced - so in a democracy, if you want to change the world, you may have to sing to people.

philosopher-king.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
philosopher-king.title: James Bond and Philosophy
philosopher-king.relation: Getachew maps Plato's Republic archetypes onto the Bond universe: the appetite-ruled Tyrant is Goldfinger, Zorin, Stromberg and the SPECTRE megalomaniacs; the spirit-ruled Guardian is 007, compared to Alcibiades and to Medea's vengeful fury (Bond letting Trevelyan fall 'For me'); and the reason-ruled Philosopher-King is M, whose ideal republic of common children and expendable numbers mirrors MI6's recruitment of orphans and its treatment of Bond as '007', never a person. She then challenges Plato's preference for the eternal Forms and immortality, using Freud on transience and Heidegger's being-toward-death (via Tolstoy's Ivan Ilych) to argue that mortality and risk are what make life worth living. Bond's stylish risk-taking, like the cello-case downhill escape, shows we need a balance between the Guardian and the man of thought.

philosopher-king.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
philosopher-king.title: You Can’t Tell the Players Without a Program
philosopher-king.relation: Auxier revives Plato's ancient quarrel with the poets — the Republic's banishment of imitators whose pretty words are copies that stir the masses' feelings, the philosopher-king's city, the Ion's contempt for rhapsodes, Socrates' wisdom as Delphic acknowledgment of ignorance — while branding Plato an elitist and 'Poetry NIMBY.' He then stages a fantasy dithyramb contest at the Meadowlands where Dylan ('Subterranean Homesick Blues') and Springsteen ('Blinded by the Light') trade internal rhymes and alliteration before Weird Al's palindromes deflate Bob's seriousness. The virtuous poet wins all nine Muses by wooing their mother Mnemosyne — tapping the collective memory of the race with gratitude and discipline — which explains why Springsteen, unlike the prideful Dylan who lost the Muses, retains moral authority; the philosophers, needless to say, are just jealous of the bar.

philosopher-king.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
philosopher-king.title: And the Winner Is
philosopher-king.relation: Lynch pits Plato against the Shaolin monks on the nature of the self that martial training is supposed to master. Plato's Republic makes the athlete-warrior Guardian a harmonious, rationally ruled tripartite soul whose bravery is 'remembering what ought and ought not to be feared', trained so reason governs aggression; Buddhism instead dissolves the self into five impermanent aggregates (illustrated by the chariot analogy) and reads mushin as a direct taste of no-self. He awards the practical decision to the Buddhist fighting monks, since no-self explains martial spontaneity and naturally arising compassion, while admitting Plato's substantive rational soul is not strictly refuted.

philosopher-king.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
philosopher-king.title: The Ideal Candidate
philosopher-king.relation: Nathan Zook uses the 'Royal Krabby' election from Vote for SpongeBob and the global-warming plot of SpongeBob Goes Green to weigh democracy. Mr. Krabs's rigged election, run only to sell patties, exemplifies C. Wright Mills's power elite manipulating the appearance of popular rule; Plato would bar Producer-class SpongeBob and Squidward from ruling and prefers educated Guardians, while Mill defends each citizen's liberty to choose and democracy's alliance with education (SpongeBob learns about global warming from Sandy). Aristotle's polity — citizens administering the state for the common interest — makes SpongeBob the ideal candidate because he saves Bikini Bottom without claiming power.

philosopher-king.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
philosopher-king.title: Rule of the Wise
philosopher-king.relation: Updates Plato's rule of the wise to the pre-cogs of 'Minority Report,' noting that Socrates' 'divine sign' made him a kind of pre-cog. It then argues expertise cannot be operationalized — self-proclaimed authorities from Sarah Palin to Barack Obama disagree, and there is no accepted test of who the experts are — closing with Plato's own comparison of voters to children choosing between the doctor's medicine and the confectioner's candy, which explains why the Founders added the Electoral College.

philosopher-king.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosopher-king.title: A Palace Revolution
philosopher-king.relation: The fantasy election brings in Plato's Republic: Richards's defense attorney Bill Carter functions as his Ring of Gyges, letting him vanish from legal consequences and raising Plato's question of whether we act justly only from fear of punishment. The tripartite soul is mapped onto Keef — appetites (drugs, sex, Jagger's 'Bitch'), spirit (the Glimmer Twins' rivalry), rationality (busting his head reaching for a library book) — and justice becomes the harmony under rationality's rule. In the ideal city of philosopher kings, auxiliaries, and workers, the sign at the gate reads 'NO POETS, NO ROCK'N'ROLLERS': Richards is exactly the corrupting poet Plato bars.

philosopher-king.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosopher-king.title: Shout and Scream and Kill the King
philosopher-king.relation: The election plays out: Richards blows away the auxiliaries with 'Play with Fire' and whips the working-class appetites into a frenzy (put on Exile on Main Street after a few rounds to test Plato's fear of the poets). Young Keef's soul is appetite-led — the 'Blue Lena' Bentley with its hidden drug compartment embodies a spirit in service of drugs and artistic hunger, with rationality demoted to scoring the fix. The resulting Republic of Keef, driven fast on the edge of a cliff, vindicates Plato's warning that wherever the appetites lead, tyranny soon follows — as the author concedes through his own pipe-smoking.

philosopher-king.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
philosopher-king.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
philosopher-king.relation: Greg Littmann maps Ape City onto Plato's Republic class by class: orangutan rulers who legislate, censor, and propagandize; gorilla warriors who enforce; chimpanzee producers who do all the work - including, pointedly, the science Plato made no provision for; and humans as the 'barbarians' Plato says may be enslaved or exterminated. The overlaps are detailed: the Sacred Scrolls' first article of faith functions as the noble lie's myth of the metals, orangutan funerals promise heaven to keep gorillas unafraid of death, and Zaius's erasing of Taylor's dust-writing and blowing up of the archaeological cave enact the rulers' duty to supervise stories. But the films also refute Plato: hereditary orangutans show that power corrupts philosopher kings, Dr. Honorius's 'reason' is dogma serving the faith, the gelding threat that finally breaks Taylor cracks the tripartite-soul analogy of justice, and democracy's rough virtue is that it lets us remove rulers 'without sticking anybody with iron spears.'

philosopher-king.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
philosopher-king.title: Justified and Philosophy
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter reads season two's families through Engels's Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State: Mags performs the patriarch's role of accumulating and bequeathing wealth (the Black Pike payout 'sufficient to provide for my kin for generations'), Arlo fails it by hoarding nothing for Raylan, and Ava joins Boyd's crime precisely when he hands her the mine money for her mortgage - a moment the author calls borderline prostitution, as Engels predicts. Hegel's Philosophy of Right, where the family exists for love and for forming free moral beings who must leave it, exposes the Bennetts' failure on both counts, while Aristotle's Politics (the polis is prior to the family) and Plato's Republic (rulers without private families, children raised in common) ground the claim that feuding clans need the state. The Kentucky-fried twist: when government and coal companies treat mountain families as spoil, family is sometimes all you've got.

philosopher-king.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
philosopher-king.title: 8. Plato’s Chicago
philosopher-king.relation: Littmann systematically maps Roth's Chicago onto Plato's Republic: like Marcus, Plato rejects democracy after Athens executed Socrates; both dissolve the family ('faction before blood' versus children raised in common and bred by state schedule); Erudite's IQ-selected leadership mirrors the rigorously trained philosopher-rulers, Dauntless the warrior class whose purely physical training Plato warns turns 'savage and harsh,' Abnegation's poverty the guardians's communism of property, and the factionless the powerless producers - with Plato's noble lie about the metals matching the Erudite's propaganda and serums as instruments of control. The shared flaw, he argues, is concentrated power without external checks, which corrupted Abnegation, corrupts every Dauntless leadership change, and would corrupt Plato's guardians too. The lesson is not to hand power to the least vicious but for democratic voters to confront their own ignorance - or end like Roth's America, in apocalyptic war.

philosopher-king.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
philosopher-king.title: 14. You Have to Be Good before You Can Be Smart
philosopher-king.relation: The Bocks argue that the Erudite pairing of ignorance with knowledge is morally loaded: with Linda Zagzebski's and James Montmarquet's virtue epistemology, high-end knowledge requires intellectual virtues like the courage to test your beliefs publicly, so you really do have to be good before you can be smart. The Erudite manifesto's curriculum omits the humanities that open the mind, and its IQ-only leadership test fails Plato's requirement that philosopher kings love wisdom itself and, like the freed cave-prisoner, return to benefit society - which is why Jeanine, driven by lust for power and concealment of the truth beyond the fence, is 'a poor example of a philosopher king.' Both the Erudite and the Bureau reason as consequentialists ('Knowledge is power... power to do good') to justify slaughtering Abnegation and experimenting on unconsenting Chicagoans, when the pursuit of knowledge must be constrained by informed consent and human dignity.

philosopher-king.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
philosopher-king.title: 7. Pratchett’s Republic
philosopher-king.relation: Kempner maps Plato's Republic onto Ankh-Morpork: Vetinari is the Philosopher King, the Watch of Guards! Guards! are the Guardians who devote themselves to the good of the whole community, and Platonic justice as keeping everything in its right place is Vetinari's guild-licensing, topiary-tending rule - including the jail cell whose locks are all on the inside. Against Plato's banishment of poets, The Truth shows words serving the just city: William de Worde's pursuit of 'the big truth' exposes the frame-up of Vetinari and extends the circle of Guardians to the free press. The chapter concludes that Pratchett keeps Plato's ideal only by bending it to observable reality - Vetinari rules for the city rather than remaking its people.

philosopher-king.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
philosopher-king.title: 9. Pierce’s Republic
philosopher-king.relation: Randall Jensen maps the Society onto Plato's Republic (Brown has said he drew on it): the Color hierarchy parallels the Myth of the Metals' gold, silver, and bronze souls, the Golds' scorn for Demokracy echoes Book VIII's account of degeneration into tyranny, and Leto's 'We are Plato's philosopher kings' claims a mantle Plato himself doubted anyone could ever fill. Darrow's story is the Allegory of the Cave run from below—a Helldiver literally raised in a mine, blinded by surface light, whose return to a shrunken, grayer garden mirrors the philosopher's homecoming—except Plato never imagined the prisoner carved into a Gold. The Noble Lie survives as the terraforming myth fed to lowReds while the surface has been habitable for centuries, and the chapter weighs Darrow's gospel ('we choose who we are') against Plato's caveats: you can choose who to be only within limits, if you are lucky and greatly helped.

philosopher-king.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
philosopher-king.title: 6. The Self-Willed and Ignorant Law
philosopher-king.relation: Marc Cole argues the Reich's and Japan's governments have the structure of Plato's Republic: supreme power in a political expert who is above the law and manages citizens' work, breeding, education, and music from cradle to grave — in some ways more controlling than the Nazis, since Plato abolishes the family outright.
