John Smith's son Thomas, condemned to death by a law blind to particular circumstances, embodies the Statesman's 'self-willed and ignorant' law, and after weighing the doctor/patient defense of rule by expertise, the chapter sides with democratic republics and warns that multiplying laws and state management inches us toward Plato's republic or the Reich.

philosopher-king.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
philosopher-king.title: 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger
philosopher-king.relation: Ericson uses the used-car litmus test to examine trust in the MCU: through McLeod's three criteria and Peperzak's contrast of the objectifying and interactive approaches, Tony's control-seeking distance (the lone-gun-slinger act of Iron Man 2) fails trust while Steve's soldier-style trust anchors the Winter Soldier thriller against Fury's 'This isn't freedom, this is fear' and HYDRA's coercion-eliminating project. Plato's rule that power should go only to those who do not want it explains why Cap can be entrusted with superpowers, Nietzsche's megalomaniac late letters frame Tony's drive to 'cleave history in two' by building Ultron and then the messianic Vision, and Banner's Hulk illustrates the Freudian road from repression to sublimation as the condition of self-trust. It ends with Cap's concealment of Bucky's killing of Tony's parents as the betrayal of trust that only a decision to forgive might repair.

philosopher-king.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
philosopher-king.title: 10. Intelligence and Duh-mocracy
philosopher-king.relation: Saunders uses Adams's induhviduals and a hundred-voter dilution example in which smart people's votes are swamped to stage the classic case against democracy: Plato's physician analogy against Athenian rule by the ignorant and his philosopher-kings, Jason Brennan's hobbits, hooligans, and Vulcans with voter licensing, Mill's plural votes for the demonstrably wise, and Nussbaum's claim that humanities education breeds empathetic democratic citizens. Each fix fails on Dilbert's own terms, since competence tests demean the labeled, the Pointy-Haired Boss would amass extra votes while Dilbert-grade engineers lack political judgment, Asok's degree would not help, and the more educated are demographically skewed toward men. He concludes that equal votes win as a pragmatic default and muses that workplaces, not polities, might be the truer target of democratization.

philosopher-king.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
philosopher-king.title: 7 Should Wakanda Take Over the World The Ethics of International Power
philosopher-king.relation: Littmann asks whether Wakanda should take over the world, staging N'Jobu's and Killmonger's 'Wakanda could rule them all... the right way' plan against the history of benevolently justified empire: Roman civilization of barbarians, Kipling's white man's burden, and Mill's trusteeship argument for educating non-Europeans toward democracy. Plato's Republic case for rule by the wisest initially favors Wakandan conquest, but Kant's Perpetual Peace condemnation of conquering 'European savages,' Mill's own four reasons imperial rule goes wrong (ignorance of local conditions, lack of sympathy, partiality, exploitation), and Diderot's claim that distance from home erodes moral restraint convince him domination breeds abuse; he endorses Nakia's aid-and-refuge outreach and Mill's hope that the 'aristocracy of nationality' will one day look as wrong as racism.

philosopher-king.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
philosopher-king.title: The Burden of the End of the World
philosopher-king.relation: Reads Naomi's escape from collapsing Ganymede — sedating Amos to leave the freighter, then stepping out before a crowd of more than a hundred stranded Belters to propose saving only the youngest — as Arendt's 'doing' politics, action justified by the seeing-and-being-seen of shared speech rather than by the strategic 'making' calculus Melissa and Amos use to justify abandoning the crowd. Naomi must alternate between the two — Champa's measured violence organizes the crowd — without letting making become the ethical metric, because, as she says, 'every shitty thing we do makes the next one that much easier.' Marco embodies politics reduced to pure making (abandoning six million on Ceres), Holden stays trapped in righteous strategizing that never defeats the protomolecule's uncertainty, and the chapter closes on Arendt's story of Plato's philosopher-king: trying to eliminate uncertainty by preemptive rule only multiplies risk, so resilience comes from doing politics together.

philosopher-king.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
philosopher-king.title: Notes
philosopher-king.relation: Dal Barco maps Lucy's arc in the Amazon series onto Plato's cave stage by stage: Vault 33's fake sky, curated history lessons, and Vault-Tec-managed information are the shadow-puppet show, her first step into the sun after Hank's abduction by Moldaver is the freed prisoner's blinding ascent, the hidden hospital vault tempts her (and Maximus, who wants to stay) like the return to the cave, and the truth - her father helped orchestrate the nuclear war, her mother is now a ghoul - plays the role the sun and the Good play in the Republic. Plato's claim that only the educated philosopher who has seen beyond the cave should govern (Republic 496a, 519a-d) explains why Lucy, unlike the frightened Norm or the tempted Maximus, goes back out into the wastes: she is becoming the philosopher-ruler whose hard-won knowledge enables Moldaver to restore power to the surface and begin a civilization no longer built on shadows. The chapter answers its own question - yes, it was worth leaving the vault for the truth.

philosopher-king.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
philosopher-king.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
philosopher-king.relation: Barkman retells Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, a shepherd's invisibility ring used to seduce the queen and murder the king, as Lord Acton's claim that absolute power corrupts, and answers with Plato: injustice disorders the tripartite soul, so the unjust sacrifice the happiness that matters most. The Guardians of the Universe are Plato's guardians writ cosmic, wise enough to rule themselves; Yalan Gur fell only when the yellow weakness was removed from his ring, Sinestro never had the wisdom ('You have never understood us'), and Hal's lapses, resigning for Carol Ferris and the Emerald Twilight rampage, are ignorance of the proper value of things rather than evil, since 'Hal's not evil... He believes he's acting for the right reasons.' The power ring is a modern Ring of Gyges, and Plato's test explains both who passes it and who fails.

philosopher-king.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosopher-king.title: Plato and Dumbledore Separated at Birth
philosopher-king.relation: Opening 'Dumbledore, Plato, and the Lust for Power,' the chapter pairs Dumbledore's 'those who are best suited to power are those who have never sought it' with Plato's 'a city in which those who are going to rule are least eager to rule is necessarily best.' Against Lord Acton's resigned 'power corrupts,' it presents Plato's remedy, reserving power for the reluctant rather than the power-hungry, as the lesson of the entire series' climax.

philosopher-king.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosopher-king.title: Fudge and Umbridge The Lessons of Obviously Unfit Power-Brokers
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter draws tight parallels between Plato's political life and Dumbledore's: both watched gifted, power-hungry pupils betray their cities (Alcibiades and Tom Riddle), both recoiled from tyrannical regimes (the Thirty under Critias; the duel with Grindelwald that killed his sister), and both turned from politics to education, founding the Academy and leading Hogwarts. It explains the Republic's philosopher-rulers, their four cardinal virtues, and the decades of training meant to 'distinguish the Potters from the Malfoys,' then introduces Glaucon's Ring of Gyges as Plato's test of who can resist invisible power, the legend Rowling mirrors in the Deathly Hallows and Harry's invisibility cloak, with Voldemort's unicorn-blood survival showing how the tyrant's life burns short.

philosopher-king.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosopher-king.title: Voldemort and Dumbledore Two Tempted by Power
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter grades would-be Ministers of Magic on Plato's ruler criteria: Dolores Umbridge fails utterly, her 'I must not tell lies' blood-quill detentions and multiplying Educational Decrees exposing a lust for power that grows with her authority and a total lack of courage, wisdom, justice, and self-control. Cornelius Fudge's insecurity breeds dictatorial damage control, trashing Harry in the press and rigging his hearing over the dementor attack on Dudley, so that craving power, he loses it; both are Platonic object lessons in how not to rule.

philosopher-king.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosopher-king.title: Harry’s Cloak, the Ring of Gyges, and the Temptations of Power
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter reads Tom Riddle as Plato's unfit ruler: from the orphanage ('I can make them hurt if I want to') he violates Kant's dictum never to use persons merely as means, treating even his 'friends' as followers, killing Lily despite Snape's devotion, and splitting his soul for Horcruxes. Dumbledore, offered the Ministry repeatedly yet refusing because 'power was my weakness and my temptation,' has the Socratic self-knowledge that he cannot be trusted with power, and that self-awareness, not flawless virtue, is what keeps him from Grindelwald's and Voldemort's path and makes him the series' nearest philosopher-ruler.

philosopher-king.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosopher-king.title: NOTES
philosopher-king.relation: The chapter argues Harry passes the Ring of Gyges test that Voldemort fails: despite years of invisible freedom under the Cloak he never exploits it, refuses Scrimgeour's offer of his dream job to serve the whole wizarding community, hunts Horcruxes instead of making them, and at eleven alone retrieves the Sorcerer's Stone from the Mirror of Erised precisely because he does not want to use it. This indifference to the lure of power is exactly the Platonic qualification Dumbledore and Plato both demand of those fit to rule.

philosopher-king.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
philosopher-king.title: Notes
philosopher-king.relation: Argues the Underwoods' success is not far-fetched fiction but the structural outcome four critics of democracy predict. Plato's Republic supplies the spine: the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decays through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, whose love of freedom invites the tyrant — Peter Russo with his random desires is the democratic soul, Frank the tyrannical soul ruled by one illicit appetite, doomed to the fear and friendlessness Book 9 describes (which Season 3 delivers). Hobbes and Hegel then explain why monarchy may beat popular rule (the monarch's private interest aligns with the public's; the monarch lets a people will as one), and Marx reframes the whole show economically — SanCorp, Tusk and Feng as capitalists, the laid-off shipyard workers as proletariat, and AmWorks as self-interested politicians flirting with expropriation. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government gives the democratic reply — elections force responsiveness, participation educates citizens — so the burden falls on viewers to keep elections fair, the press free, and checks on unscrupulous politicians effective.

philosopher-king.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
philosopher-king.title: Notes
philosopher-king.relation: Shea argues the Underwoods' rise is structurally guaranteed rather than far-fetched, surveying democracy's critics: Plato's Republic Books 8-9 has the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decay through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, where a 'protector'-tyrant like Frank exploits the drones and the people's love of freedom (Russo as the prototypical democratic soul, Tusk as the oligarch-in-fact), while the tyrant ends fear-ridden and friendless — precisely Frank's Season 3. Hobbes and Hegel then reverse the verdict, arguing monarchy aligns the ruler's private interest with the public good and lets a people will as one instead of a formless mass — the insight Tom Yates has about voters identifying with the Underwoods as people — and Marx reframes it economically: SanCorp, Tusk, and Feng are the capitalist structure, and Frank's AmWorks, entitlement cuts, and nationalization threats show self-interested politicians siding with a growing proletariat. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government supplies the democratic reply — responsiveness, better information, and citizen participation mean an Underwood cannot last if we keep fair elections, a free press, and real checks.

philosopher-king.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
philosopher-king.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
philosopher-king.relation: Anne Torkelson reads Panem through the Republic and the Laws: because mousike imitates states of soul and slowly molds character, Socrates polices music and poetry in the just city and fears innovation in musical modes, and the Capitol's own outlawing of songs quietly confirms music's power. She shows 'The Meadow Song' replacing Katniss's grief with hope and inspiring the flowers for Rue, the forbidden 'Hanging Tree' planting the Socratic question of whether an unjust life is a fate worse than death (paralleling Socrates's own unjust execution, the hemlock, and the nightlock pact Katniss, Gale, and Peeta make), and Rue's four notes mutating from an orchard work-signal into a salute of defiance when the District 11 man whistles them on the Victory Tour, at the cost of his life. Music, which Katniss dismisses as 'somewhere between hair ribbons and rainbows,' turns out to be the force that shapes her character and carries the revolution.

philosopher-king.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
philosopher-king.title: Over Four Thousand Words to Say No
philosopher-king.relation: Spanakos asks whether Stark's assembling, disassembling, and reassembling of the Avengers and his unseen-hand management of Civil War make him the Republic's philosopher guardian, and answers no. Tony fits the surface profile — the gold-souled ruler of Socrates' noble lie, the elite training, indifference to money, the technê of an MIT engineer who envisions the future — but he lacks epistêmê: he never climbs from the cave's shadows to grasp the forms of justice and the good, and his appetites (womanizing in The Ultimates, 'Demon in a Bottle') show a soul where passion is not ruled by reason. His puppet mastery is reactive problem-solving guided by each situation, not philosophy, and reading him as a philosopher king is our failure to read The Republic meditatively, as Ortega y Gasset urged.

philosopher-king.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
philosopher-king.title: Notes
philosopher-king.relation: Barkman and Alkema map Plato's Republic onto the fall of the Old Republic: the bickering Senate and Anakin's 'someone wise' exchange with Padme enact democracy's degeneration into tyranny, with Palpatine as Plato's werewolf-like protector-tyrant and Dooku's Sith name 'Tyranus' marking Thrasymachus's justice-as-strength as Sith doctrine. The Jedi approximate Plato's philosopher-guardians - courageous, temperate, reluctant to rule, surrendering their children to the Temple much like the Republic's breeding deceptions and noble lies. Justice as each part doing its own work applies to the tripartite soul as much as the state, and the chapter closes that democracy survives Endor but only if truth stays a beacon of the light side.

philosopher-king.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
philosopher-king.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
philosopher-king.relation: Steve Benton reads Burton's Sleepy Hollow as a meditation on rationality and anti-intellectualism, contrasting it with Washington Irving's original where brainy Ichabod is run out of town. Burton's Ichabod, a rationalist constable, prevails only after tempering his faith in science with emotion, intuition, and the spirit world associated with his mother and Katrina—the paper-disk toy (bird/cage) symbolizing how head and heart must spin together. Benton maps the film's models of rationality onto Plato's philosopher-king and distrust of the mob and Hobbes's war of all against all (Burton's corrupt New York and Sleepy Hollow) versus the collaborative, democratic reason of Locke, Mill's On Liberty, and Dewey, invoking Aristotle and Nussbaum on emotion's role in practical wisdom; he leaves open whether the film is transgressive or a conventional 'woman heals cold rational man' Hollywood tale.

philosopher-king.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
philosopher-king.title: 22. Punk Rock Saves Lives
philosopher-king.relation: R.W. Main argues punk saves lives by replacing the myth of purity - the ideal behind one-drop rules, eugenics, and moral exclusion - with a philosophy of filth that revalues the rejected and abject, letting the outcast reclaim agency. He stages Diogenes the Cynic's street-living, shameless filth as the original punk counterpoint to Plato's perfect Forms and philosopher-king (Plato the 'sell-out'), and enlists Nietzsche's claims that morality denies life while art saves it. Camus's Sisyphus closes the argument: punk's freedom is revolt, giving the gods the middle finger since 'there is no fate that cannot be surmounted by scorn'; more concretely, punks save lives as anti-bullies, the 'Duncan Effect' of Some Kind of Wonderful and SHARPS skinheads protecting misfits.

philosopher-king.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
philosopher-king.title: 17. Psychohistory’s Noble Lie
philosopher-king.relation: Silcox explains why readers forgive Seldon's confessed lie that the Encyclopedia Galactica 'is a fraud, and always has been' by comparing it to Socrates's noble lie in Plato's Republic, which Popper and I.F. Stone condemn as antidemocratic. He contrasts the two—Socrates's lie preserves an existing kallipolis while Seldon's brings about a distant political goal that requires trusting psychohistory—and weighs them against modern transparency doctrines: Bentham's consequentialist case for publicity and Rawls's publicity condition grounding autonomy, plus Nguyen's worry that transparency distorts expert 'cognitive islands.' He concludes that a genuinely predictive science of history might rationally lead us to treat political transparency as negotiable, which is why Hari Seldon remains a noble hero despite 'engineering the narrative.'

philosopher-king.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
philosopher-king.title: 5. Friendship, Fun, Freedom, Food, and the Future
philosopher-king.relation: Le Gall and Taliaferro read Bourdain's Libya and Iran episodes of Parts Unknown through Pierre Hadot's 'philosophy as a way of life,' arguing that Gaddafi and Khomeini were failed Platonic philosopher-kings. They interpret ordinary Libyans and Iranians eating Uncle Kentucky chicken, playing pinball, or hosting feasts as popular 'spiritual exercises' — tatonnement — showing how the personal becomes political and how friendship, fun, freedom, and food nourish the Socratic care of the soul.

philosopher-king.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
philosopher-king.title: GARDENING
philosopher-king.relation: Evans presents Texcotzingo, the hilltop garden-retreat of the fifteenth-century Texcocan king Nezahualcoyotl, as the achievement of an Aztec philosopher-king who was landscape designer, hydraulic engineer and statesman. She argues the botanical garden as a genre—a 'green encyclopedia' cataloguing a realm's flora—was pioneered by Aztec kings, and that within an animist cosmos where mountains and water pulse with sacred spirit, Nezahualcoyotl's aqueduct, pools and terraced gardens made the hill a living embodiment of the altepetl (the 'water-hill' city-state). The garden thus symbolically enacts his political domain, dynastic history (three pools for three ancestral capitals) and cosmic order, even as she cautions his reputation as poet and monotheist was inflated by later Spanish and Christian chroniclers.

philosopher-king.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
philosopher-king.title: 29. Frank Herbert’s Dune as Philosophy The Need to Think for Yourself
philosopher-king.relation: Reading the Sci Fi Channel miniseries Frank Herbert's Dune and Children of Dune, Littmann argues the saga warns against letting leaders or religions think for us: Paul Atreides fakes being the Fremen Mahdi, wages a holy war, and founds a theocratic tyranny that Alia and Leto II carry to worse extremes. He sets Plato's Republic (the guardian class, the noble lie, rule by the wise) and Hobbes against pro-democracy thinkers—Locke's consent and natural rights, Mill's harm principle, Dewey's democracy—then cites Locke, Paine and Russell on religion's dangers, closing with W.K. Clifford's 'ethics of belief' that one must not accept religious claims without sufficient evidence. The chapter reads Paul's dictatorship and the Bene Gesserit's engineered messiah as dramatizations of the historical abuses of concentrated and religious power.

informal-fallacies.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
informal-fallacies.title: 2 - Lisa and American Anti-intellectualism
informal-fallacies.relation: Aeon Skoble argues Lisa's treatment on the show captures America's love-hate relationship with expertise: she saves Homer's life by talking Dr. Nick through heart surgery and exposes political corruption, yet her intellectualism is itself made the butt of jokes. He sorts legitimate appeal to authority from the informal fallacy version and from the relativism that declares all opinions equally valid, tracing the problem to democratic equality. The Mensa episode 'They Saved Lisa's Brain'—where Lisa, Professor Frink, and the Comic Book Guy rule Springfield with censorious, Star Trek-inspired decrees—is read as satirizing not only Homer's mob but Plato's philosopher-kings themselves, whose utopian rule of the wise proves unstable and foolish.

informal-fallacies.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
informal-fallacies.title: The Defense Rests
informal-fallacies.relation: Arp uses 'Chef Aid' — cartoon Johnnie Cochran's 'If Chewbacca lives on Endor, you must acquit' — to introduce the red herring fallacy, then teaches the basics of logic through South Park: Cartman's Tooth Fairy argument as deduction, Towelie's appearances as induction, and episodes like 'The Entity,' 'Weight Gain 4000,' and 'Butt Out' illustrating hasty generalization, slippery slope, false dilemma, appeal to inappropriate authority, and ad hominem. His point is that Parker and Stone deliberately violate logical principles for humor, and that spotting fallacies matters because bad reasoning drives laws, policies, and the beliefs people die for.

informal-fallacies.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
informal-fallacies.title: End Game
informal-fallacies.relation: Arp and Milarker use Zelda examples to teach informal logic: Rob's 'all gamers are geeks' is a hasty generalization, the argument that the original Zelda is chronologically first commits equivocation (Earth release order is not Hyrule chronology, since Miyamoto named Ocarina of Time earliest), and debates over banning violent games trade in false dilemmas, ad hominem, and slippery slopes. The chapter sets out premises, conclusions, deductive versus inductive arguments, validity and soundness, strength and cogency, with worked examples from Clawshot reasoning to Best Buy Wii lines. Its point is that fallacious reasoning harms real lives, so readers should audit every argument in the book and in the gaming world.

informal-fallacies.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
informal-fallacies.title: Psych and Philosophy
informal-fallacies.relation: Michaud argues that Shawn's whole psychic career runs on fallacies of relevance - the red herring of claiming to be psychic to dodge arrest, plus ad hominem mockery that deflects Lassiter's fraud accusations - so the show's comedy turns on bad logic being used to lead people to true conclusions. Socrates supplies the opposing voice: like the Sophists who argued any side for money, Shawn reasons for convenience and amusement, and his deception is an inconsistency of the kind Socrates refused in Plato's Crito, where he would not bribe his way out of a death sentence. An invented Platonic-style dialogue has Socrates question Shawn until he concedes that lying breeds more lying and harm - 'her name is Truth!' - before Shawn escapes the elenchus by spotting lipstick on Socrates's collar. The chapter leaves the verdict open: Shawn saves lives and raises the world's happiness, but his trickery also trains Santa Barbara to reason badly and trust con artists.

informal-fallacies.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
informal-fallacies.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
informal-fallacies.relation: Fenner Tanswell uses 'Reynolds vs. Reynolds: The Cereal Defense' - the Gang's in-bar trial over Frank's blind driving versus Dennis's cereal-at-the-wheel - as a catalogue of crooked thinking. We get valid forms distinguished from soundness (modus ponens with 'if poop is funny, then Frank pooped in the bed'; Charlie's modus tollens from Frank's no-donkey-brains certificate), then the fallacies: the argument from ignorance by which Dennis's lacking a certificate proves him donkey-brained, Dee's ad hominem against Mac, Dennis's appeal to authority, and Mac's 'Science Is a Liar Sometimes' poster, which equivocates between mere skeptical doubt (even Descartes's) and reasonable doubt by straw-manning science as claiming infallibility. True to form, the Gang convicts Dee 'for comedy rather than on any logical basis.'

informal-fallacies.title: 5. Ministry of Truth Handbook Excerpt on the Strategic Use of Fallacious Reasoning for Thoughtcrime Prevention
informal-fallacies.relation: Rard's satirical Party handbook explains how to keep a population from thinking: keep the proles too poor and exhausted to reason, and deploy fallacies strategically, from ad hominem goat-caricatures of Goldstein at the Two Minutes Hate and straw man versions of his arguments, to destroying contrary evidence, appealing to fear of the old capitalist world, and Room 101's appeal to force, so false beliefs can be manufactured as easily as true ones. It presents Plato's noble lie as the Ministry's founding inspiration, calling the reader's mission 'a continuation of Plato's dream'. It also cites Aristotle's view that emotion must be disciplined for reason to work, which the Party inverts by deliberately triggering fear and hatred to disable rational thought.

informal-fallacies.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
informal-fallacies.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
informal-fallacies.relation: Dempsey catalogs how The Daily Show and The Colbert Report expose political rhetoric by ridicule: ad hominem attacks on Judge Anna Diggs Taylor's wiretapping ruling, the straw man 'cut and run' distortion of John Murtha, Zell Miller's RNC outrage, false dilemmas ('with us or with the terrorists', Colbert's 'great president or the greatest president?'), slippery slopes from same-sex marriage to snake marriage, Tony Snow's equivocation on 'fit for duty', and Sam Brownback's question-begging snowflake-baby presentation against stem-cell research. He then treats emotional appeals (the 9/11-saturated 2004 RNC, Kerry's 'reporting for duty', Colbert's fear-mongering 'ThreatDown' and flag-wrapped patriotism) and spin as the systematic use of persuasive language: euphemism and dysphemism ('socialist', 'war on ______'), rhetorical definition of abortion as 'murder', 'Polish that Turd' jobs-number spinning, the GOP memo read aloud on Fox News, and Bush's Iraq-versus-North Korea double standard. Montages lay the talking-point machinery bare, and the chapter argues a critically informed citizenry is the democratic defense against elites who distrust the public with the truth.

informal-fallacies.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
informal-fallacies.title: Thinkin' is Freakin' Sweet: Family Guy and Fallacies
informal-fallacies.relation: A logic primer built from Family Guy clips: it teaches premises and conclusions by reconstructing Peter's Y2K bomb-shelter argument in 'DaBoom,' contrasts deduction with induction via Brian's fart-powered descent in 'Wasted Talent' and the show's 'remember the last time?' flashbacks, and then diagnoses named fallacies. Stewie's vow to destroy all vegetables after one bad broccoli exemplifies hasty generalization, Peter's smear campaign against Lois's candidacy in 'Running Mates' is ad hominem, Francis Griffin's hellfire pronouncements in 'Holy Crap' are appeal to inappropriate authority, and Peter's 'if Liza is wrong, then I don't want to know what right is' shows blind deference to celebrity.

informal-fallacies.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
informal-fallacies.title: End Game
informal-fallacies.relation: Robert Arp and Dennis Milarker teach informal logic through Zelda, opening with Arp's own fallacious 'all gamers are geeks' hasty generalization and stereotypes about Miyamoto's Japanese heritage. They standard-form arguments about which Zelda game is chronologically first, distinguish deductive from inductive reasoning (the Best Buy Wii camp-out, expectations for The Adventure of Link's side-scrolling perspective), and run through fallacies: inappropriate authority, the Atari false dilemma (the TV was on channel 4), equivocation on release order versus story order, ad hominem, and the slippery slope against Doom and Grand Theft Auto. The lesson is that Ganon and gamers alike must give good arguments, since bad reasoning shapes laws, beliefs, and lives.

informal-fallacies.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
informal-fallacies.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
informal-fallacies.relation: Arp uses the show as a logic textbook: his own prejudice against Goth kids and Officer Barbrady's post-Atlas Shrugged ban on books illustrate hasty generalization, Cartman's 'if you do drugs, then you're a hippie' chain and the Tooth Fairy syllogism illustrate deductive argument, and Towelie's appearances illustrate inductive strength. A fallacy catalog follows: Johnny Cochran's 'If Chewbacca lives on Endor, you must acquit' in 'Chef Aid' as red herring, Mrs. Broflovski's 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip as slippery slope, Mrs. Marsh's cookie outburst in 'Clubhouses' as hasty generalization plus slippery slope, Father Maxi's hell pronouncements as appeal to inappropriate authority, and cartoon Rob Reiner in 'Butt Out' as ad hominem. The chapter's claim is that Parker and Stone deliberately violate logical principles episode after episode to expose absurd beliefs, because how people reason shapes the laws they make and the beliefs they die for.

sophist-relativism.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
sophist-relativism.title: 2 - Lisa and American Anti-intellectualism
sophist-relativism.relation: Aeon Skoble argues Lisa's treatment on the show captures America's love-hate relationship with expertise: she saves Homer's life by talking Dr. Nick through heart surgery and exposes political corruption, yet her intellectualism is itself made the butt of jokes. He sorts legitimate appeal to authority from the informal fallacy version and from the relativism that declares all opinions equally valid, tracing the problem to democratic equality. The Mensa episode 'They Saved Lisa's Brain'—where Lisa, Professor Frink, and the Comic Book Guy rule Springfield with censorious, Star Trek-inspired decrees—is read as satirizing not only Homer's mob but Plato's philosopher-kings themselves, whose utopian rule of the wise proves unstable and foolish.

sophist-relativism.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
sophist-relativism.title: The Common Good versus the Greater Good
sophist-relativism.relation: Maps Voldemort onto the Sophists - Thrasymachus's claim that the unjust always come out ahead - through his pattern of exploiting followers' trust for power and pleasure, while Plato's two-pronged reply runs: cosmic justice in the afterlife (the flayed child beneath the bench as Voldemort's just fate, sealing it by refusing remorse) and the intrinsic goodness of justice via the tripartite soul with reason ruling spirit and appetite, the four cardinal virtues, and the health analogy. Harry, seeking Dumbledore's wisdom, showing courage in facing death, and devoted to justice for wizards and Muggles, embodies the moral life as the rational choice, while Voldemort's snakelike appearance externalizes his disordered, sick soul.

sophist-relativism.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
sophist-relativism.title: So, What’s the Bottom Line
sophist-relativism.relation: James Klagge, defining terms in Socratic fashion, distinguishes bootlegs like Great White Wonder from piracy and argues unreleased Dylan material (the New York Blood on the Tracks, "Blind Willie McTell," the 1966 Live concert) has genuine musical and historical value. He rejects the Sophist view that morality is just self-interest and the relativist "everybody's doing it" defense, then weighs the artist's Lockean property and privacy rights against fans' rights of access, noting legal-but-immoral and illegal-but-moral cases in the spirit of Martin Luther King's civil disobedience. His verdict: bootlegging is morally acceptable when royalties are fair, stolen tapes are not used, and mainly public performances circulate.

sophist-relativism.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
sophist-relativism.title: The Blessings of Tranquility
sophist-relativism.relation: Michael Chiariello takes Dylan's "the truth is true whether you wanna believe it or not" as a correspondence theory of truth, then rejects both the gospel-era absolutism of "Precious Angel" and the relativism (from Protagoras' man-the-measure to modern subjectivism) that would make Dylan's changes of course harmless. The alternative he defends is Pyrrhonian skepticism in Sextus Empiricus's sense: truth is objective but never fully assured, so suspending judgment yields tranquility. Dylan's career - from the ambiguous "Blowin' in the Wind" through "Watching the River Flow" and "Things Have Changed" to the two versions of "Every Grain of Sand" ("the reality of man" vs "a perfect finished plan") - embodies this balanced, non-dogmatic search the way of God designed it.

sophist-relativism.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sophist-relativism.title: Philosophy versus Bullshit
sophist-relativism.relation: The chapter claims that 'equal respect' in modern democracies has been distorted into a 'dumbing-up' relativism — 'I'm valid, you're valid' — which conflates the equal right to voice opinions with their equal intellectual merit and so leaves nothing that counts as bullshit. It illustrates this through the 'democratization of expertise' and management-speak ('downsizing', 'mission statements'), which mimics profundity while evading awkward facts, and it tests and rejects the quasi-Nietzschean ressentiment story of timid citizens dragging discourse down to a common denominator. To get the full measure of the phenomenon it expands Frankfurt's and Cohen's typologies into seven kinds of bullshit, adding clarifiable unclarity, plain rubbish, irretrievable speculation, pretension, and evasion.

sophist-relativism.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sophist-relativism.title: Bullshit as a Call to Open-Mindedness
sophist-relativism.relation: Steve Fuller opens by asking whether bullshit detection coarsens the detector: Nietzsche and H.L. Mencken embraced the debunker's role (Mencken coining 'bunk'), while Ibsen's The Wild Duck and Hedda Gabler dramatize the need for a 'life lie', and detectors who find bullshit everywhere slide from nihilism into dogmatism. He re-reads bullshit as sophistry — the Sophists taught that securing your audience's belief is the only knowledge you need, against Socrates's attack and Plato's coining of 'rhetoric' to demonize them — and faults Frankfurt for calling the bullshitter 'indifferent' to truth when the accomplished bullshitter must be a keen student of what people tend to regard as true. The Sokal affair and Benjamin Franklin's 'economical with the truth' lead to his Kantian mapping of bullshitters (rationalists selecting among already-imaginable alternatives) against bullshit detectors (empiricists demanding evidence), which the scientific method will dialectically synthesize.

sophist-relativism.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
sophist-relativism.title: Introduction
sophist-relativism.relation: Introduces Part I by casting South Park, The Daily Show, and The Colbert Report as modern Socratic gadflies. It previews Young's comparison of the show's 'corruption of the youth' controversies to Socrates' trial, Arp's use of Johnnie Cochran's Chewbacca Defense to teach logic and fallacies, and Johnson's use of Colbert's 'wikiality' and 'truthiness' to attack relativism and the myth that everyone has a right to their opinion.

sophist-relativism.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
sophist-relativism.title: Sin, Play, and the “Synagogues of Satan”
sophist-relativism.relation: Rachael Sotos argues the Report performs Platonic play: like the divine puppet of Plato's Laws with its competing cords, Colbert reveals what moves us (fear, hope, the ThreatDown bears, the 'golden cord' of the good) and so teaches freedom through play. Colbert's pompous self-authority - claiming to be 'the canon and measure' of virtue in I Am America - parodies Aristotle's serious man (spoudaios, megalopsychos) and the sophists Protagoras and Prodicus with their Orpheus voices, proving Heraclitus right that 'time is a child at play' and Aristotle wrong that play is mere medicinal rest. Tracking the war on fun from Chrysostom through Aquinas's eutrapelia (there is sin in a lack of play) to Erasmus's Praise of Folly and the Puritans' ban on theaters as 'Synagogues of Satan,' she reads Colbert's playing-at-sin - the man-seed eugenics bit, the 'black friend' boasts, the Ellen DeGeneres Paradox on Wikiality - as Erasmian folly that heals America's Puritan hangover in the culture wars.

sophist-relativism.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
sophist-relativism.title: It-Getting The Truth about Truthiness
sophist-relativism.relation: Ethan Mills runs a 'Better Know a Skeptic' four-parter applied to the show: Pyrrhonian skepticism (Sextus Empiricus's suspension of judgment and living by appearances, played out in the Jon-says-worst-versus-Stephen-says-greatest Bush debate), Modern skepticism (Montaigne's fideist custom-worship and Hume's dream argument for why knowledge of couches, Doritos, and presidents is impossible), and Indian skepticism (Nagarjuna's circle that means of knowledge cannot be established without things known, illustrated with Stephen Sr. and Stephen Jr. as both father and son, plus Jayarasi's destruction of epistemology). He adds 'political skepticism' - the American sense that political knowledge is impossible - which breeds wikiality, an internet relativism ('reality we just agreed on') that the WØRD's own bullet points ('Wikipedia can tell a lie') undermine. Truthiness, he concludes, is Stephen's false cure for political skepticism: commitment without facts, a 'truthiness of the appearances'; but Sextus shows skeptics can still act on appearances without dogmatism, so we can vote and argue on the best evidence, as in Sagan's science-as-democracy, without certainty.

sophist-relativism.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
sophist-relativism.title: 1. How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Tolerate the Master Persuader Hypothesis
sophist-relativism.relation: Wolfe reads Adams's Master Persuader hypothesis through the ancient quarrel between Socrates and the Sophists: Derren Brown's deflation of hypnosis into one personality dominating another leads to Gorgias's Encomium of Helen, where persuasive words are magic spells that steal free will, and to Plato's Gorgias, where Socrates condemns rhetoric as cookery and cosmetics that flatter the ignorant while his disciple Polus covets its tyrannical power. On this mapping Trump's plain-talk style is simply Aristotle's available means of persuasion for a particular audience, and Adams is mostly a Sophist who treats words as programming code for moist robots, though he keeps a Socratic sliver in his stated aim of exposing readers to different ideas rather than converting them. Wolfe closes by refusing both readings of Adams as pro-Trump troll or alt-right hero, urging each side to see how persuasion actually worked on them.

sophist-relativism.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
sophist-relativism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
sophist-relativism.relation: Barad maps fifth-century Athens onto contemporary America to cast Stewart as a Socratic reformer confronting modern sophists, advertisers, pundits and media figures who make weaker arguments appear stronger without caring about truth, exemplified by Ed Helms admitting network stories are pre-written from 'conventional wisdom' and Ann Coulter's conformity-peddling. She details the shared method: flattering the 'expert', feigned ignorance, and layer-by-layer questioning that traps targets like Rumsfeld ('It may not seem like much, but for this administration it's a huge policy shift') in contradiction, with Socratic irony doing the work of Stewart's awestruck deadpan and mute astonished reactions to Bush clips. Against Bill O'Reilly's 'stoned slacker' charge she cites the Annenberg finding that the show's young audience is better informed, and weighs Ken Tucker's 'monkey' question through the Crossfire 'I'm not going to be your monkey' exchange, concluding that, like Socrates facing trial and execution, Stewart uses irony as means and truth as end.

sophist-relativism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
sophist-relativism.title: The Common Good versus the Greater Good
sophist-relativism.relation: Casts the Harry-Voldemort conflict as Socrates versus the Sophists: Thrasymachus's Republic claim that the unjust always come out ahead describes Voldemort's exploitation of his followers' trust exactly. The flayed child under the chair at King's Cross enacts Plato's afterlife justice, and the Republic's tripartite soul and cardinal virtues explain why Harry's reason-ruled courage, wisdom, and justice make the moral life the rational choice, as rational as choosing bodily health over chronic illness.

sophist-relativism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
sophist-relativism.title: Notes
sophist-relativism.relation: Nina Rosenstand reads 'The Measure of a Man' as a Kantian defense of Data's personhood: Maddox's sentience criteria concede intelligence and self-awareness, and Picard—prompted by Guinan's warning that a ruling for Maddox means an army of android slaves—shows a rational being must be treated as an end in himself, never dismantled merely for Starfleet's benefit. Bentham's utilitarianism supplies the contrast (an army of Datas would maximize happiness), while the episode's title ironizes Protagoras's 'man is the measure of all things', since the measure here is rationality rather than humanity. Louvois's open verdict becomes precedent for Lal, the exocomps, and Voyager's Doctor, and a metaphor for real struggles for recognition.

sophist-relativism.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
sophist-relativism.title: Notes
sophist-relativism.relation: MacMullan argues Darth Plagueis is a paradox for Plato: wisdom as reason ruling spirit and appetite should be impossible for a Sith who feeds on passion, yet Plagueis stays patient, restrained, and rational for over a century. He reads Sidious's 'I will make it legal' and the Sith Code as Thrasymachus's 'justice is the advantage of the stronger,' and notes Plagueis even shares Plato's noble lie and eugenic breeding programs. Finding that Plato's prediction of self-destruction fails for Plagueis, the chapter turns to Nietzsche: master morality, the will to power, and life beyond good and evil better explain a Sith who cherishes bodily life and seeks to conquer death where Yoda and Socrates calmly disdain 'crude matter.'

sophist-relativism.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
sophist-relativism.title: Naked City: The Relativist Turn in TV Noir
sophist-relativism.relation: Fitzgibbons argues that when The Naked City became the hour-long Naked City in 1960, TV noir underwent a 'relativist turn': episodes like 'Ooftus Goofus,' 'To Walk Like a Lion' (Arnold Platt's sympathetic embezzlement), and 'Memory of a Red Trolley Car' (Professor Johns, who refuses to save his own life) conflate the normal with the moral and leave viewers wondering whether conventionally wrong choices 'might not have been right in some way.' He traces this message to Ruth Benedict's cultural relativism, reconstructs her difference argument (from varying moral codes, as with Protagoras's 'man is the measure') and her conceptual argument (morality as socially approved habits), and shows both are invalid, the latter resting on the false assumption that 'morality' has one real definition. He then presses three objections to cultural relativism, including that its anti-ethnocentrism claim is a disguised absolute moral claim, making the position inconsistent, and that determining cultural membership collapses it into individual relativism, which licenses absurd conclusions like a moral right to rob and kill on Tuesdays.

sophist-relativism.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
sophist-relativism.title: 13. Chuckrates v. The Saulphists
sophist-relativism.relation: Staged as a mock disciplinary-board trial, the chapter casts Chuck McGill as Socrates and Jimmy as a Sophist to replay Plato's dialectic-versus-rhetoric quarrel. Chuck prosecutes Jimmy as a mere rhetorician who 'makes the weaker argument defeat the stronger,' quoting the Gorgias, Apology, and Republic, while Jimmy counters that Socrates was himself a self-righteous show-off and that the legal system runs on Sophistic persuasion (juries, opening statements) as much as on truth. The Board's verdict finds Chuck blind to his own rhetoric and Jimmy a quintessential but empathetic Sophist, using the McGill brothers to argue that law fuses dialectic and rhetoric just as ancient Athens did.

sophist-relativism.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
sophist-relativism.title: 20. The Mystery of Math
sophist-relativism.relation: Barta and Lee cast the debate over whether math is invented or discovered as Protagoras versus Pythagoras, mapped onto Foundation. Protagorean relativism ('man is the measure') and modern formalism (Hilbert, Poincaré) appear in the Empire's politicized, self-serving use of math and Gaal Dornick's culturally contingent base-ten counting, while Plato and Aristotle rebut relativism via the Theaetetus and the Law of Non-Contradiction ('if Hari's a liar, he dies'). Pythagorean realism/mathematical Platonism—numbers as the fundamental reality—appears in Luminism's holy number three, Kalle's poetic proofs, and the Foundationists' quasi-religious faith that psychohistory reveals reality's mathematical structure, with Gödel, Quine-Putnam indispensability, and Wigner's 'unreasonable effectiveness' as modern heirs and Aristotle as the standing critic.

sophist-relativism.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
sophist-relativism.title: 1. A Man for All Seasonings
sophist-relativism.relation: Shaffer uses Brillat-Savarin's distinction between direct and reflective taste and Hume's 'Of the Standard of Taste' to argue gastronomic expertise is only the acquired ability to describe tastes richly, not a superior sense. He then casts Bourdain as a culinary Socrates who, like the freed prisoner in Plato's allegory of the cave, returns to lead provincial eaters out of the darkness of narrow experience toward cultural tolerance.

sophist-relativism.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
sophist-relativism.title: How to do Philosophy
sophist-relativism.relation: Johnson uses Stephen Colbert's coinages to refute relativism and gut-thinking. 'My Truth' represents individual relativism and 'Wikiality' cultural relativism, both of which Johnson rejects via the correspondence theory of truth and counterexamples like slavery and Nazi Germany. 'Truthiness' is intuitionism, which Johnson attacks using Locke's critique of 'enthusiasts' who reason in a circle, and he argues that appeals to 'a right to my opinion' reveal indifference to truth. Following Socrates, he concludes we should defend beliefs with argument and admit ignorance rather than trust the gut.

sophist-relativism.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
sophist-relativism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
sophist-relativism.relation: Judith Barad argues Stewart plays reformer in America as Socrates did in Athens, both confronting sophists—now advertisers, spin doctors, and media pundits like Coulter and O'Reilly—who teach persuasion detached from truth. She maps the Daily Show correspondents' interview technique (flatter the 'expert,' expose a contradiction) directly onto the Socratic method, and reads Stewart's ironic self-deprecation, feigned confusion, and one-on-one listening as Socratic irony deployed, like Socrates', as a means to truth rather than mere entertainment, culminating in the Crossfire confrontation with Carlson and Begala.

sophist-relativism.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
sophist-relativism.title: NOTES
sophist-relativism.relation: Matthews argues that certain children's books are 'subversive' in a Socratic sense: they problematize concepts adults assume they command, challenging adult epistemic authority the way Socrates exposed the pretended knowledge of Athens' elite. Morris the Moose raises Aristotelian questions of natural kinds and essence-versus-accident; Leese Webster probes the concept of art; The Shrinking of Treehorn destabilizes 'normal' child development; Frog and Toad's 'The Garden' dramatizes the post hoc, ergo propter hoc fallacy about causation. In the Ozma of Oz Tik-Tok discussion, nine-year-old Paul reconstructs an argument that only brains think, which Matthews aligns with Searle's claim in The Mystery of Consciousness that consciousness is caused by specific neurobiological processes; he explicitly distinguishes his subversive stories from those promoting Pyrrhonian skepticism or Protagorean relativism.

sophist-relativism.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
sophist-relativism.title: How to do Philosophy
sophist-relativism.relation: David Kyle Johnson uses Stephen Colbert's 'wikiality' and 'truthiness' to attack individual and cultural relativism, arguing (via the correspondence theory of truth and counterexamples like slavery and Nazi Germany) that truth is not relative to persons or cultures. He deploys Locke's critique of 'enthusiasm' to show gut thinking is circular, and invokes Socratic admission of ignorance against the claim of a 'right to your opinion.' The upshot is a method: defend beliefs with argument, be agnostic when evidence is lacking.

sophist-relativism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
sophist-relativism.title: 78. The Witness as Philosophy How Knowledge Is Constructed
sophist-relativism.relation: Cuddy asks what epistemology Blow built into The Witness's frustrating puzzles and its windmill videos (Burke, Feynman, Moriarty, Spira, Gangaji). He rejects the sophistic/Protagorean 'knowledge depends on the observer' reading (most puzzles have objective, inductive-and-deductive solutions, e.g. the yellow-glass bunker) and the strict scientific realism of the Burke video defended by Putnam's no-miracles argument. Using Plato's cave and the aporia of Socrates' Meno (the puzzle's 'ah-ha' epiphanies), and Kuhn's incommensurable paradigm shifts (the game's 'hard left turns' forcing players to overhaul their understanding), he concludes the game argues that true knowledge is attainable, individually and collectively, though reached by a nonlinear, paradigm-shifting route rather than pure realism or relativism.

authenticity.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
authenticity.title: 3 - Why Maggie Matters Sounds of Silence, East and West
authenticity.relation: Eric Bronson uses Maggie's shooting of Mr. Burns and her pacifier-blocked silence to ask whether a being without language can think, citing Wittgenstein's 'limits of my language mean the limits of my world' and the baby-translator episode 'Brother, Can You Spare Two Dimes?'. He reads Maggie through Sartre's study of Flaubert in The Family Idiot—speech as the means of integration into society and the parental 'mandate to live'—noting that Maggie flourishes and starts speaking under the Flanderses' attention. Contrasting the Western word-worship begun with Socrates with Eastern traditions of silence (Confucius, the Tao Te Ching, Zen enlightenment), he ends darkly with Heidegger, whose praise of authentic silence over idle talk is condemned by his own silence during the Nazi era, drawing the lesson that voices like Maggie's must be heard, not drowned out.

authenticity.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
authenticity.title: Popping a Bitter Pill Existential Authenticity in The Matrix and Nausea
authenticity.relation: The chapter frames Neo's red/blue choice as the existential choice between authenticity - honest awareness of a condition without inherent purpose or design - and inauthenticity, named as Sartre's bad faith, Camus's intellectual suicide, and Heidegger's 'levelling down of all possibilities'. It notes the irony that although existentialists praise authenticity, their literary portraits make authentic characters anxious, alienated, and near-mad while the inauthentic remain tranquil - raising the possibility that ignorance is bliss and the blue pill is wiser - before promising an argument, via The Matrix and Sartre's Nausea, for the red pill.

authenticity.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
authenticity.title: Unknown
authenticity.relation: The chapter sets Neo and Cypher as the two poles of authenticity: Neo's unplugging is agony, like the prisoner dragged from Plato's cave - atrophied limbs, eyes that hurt because 'never used them before', and the cognitive shock of the 'desert of the real' - while Cypher, freed young and worn down by years of fear and gag-inducing goop, sells out the crew for a steak he knows does not exist: 'ignorance is bliss'. McMahon asks us to sympathize with Cypher, since in his place, facing perpetual annihilation, 'we too might opt for the illusion'.

authenticity.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
authenticity.title: Unknown
authenticity.relation: The chapter walks through Nausea as the ordinary-world twin of the red pill: Roquentin, an unremarkable 1930s historian, is unravelled by a beach pebble, a handshake like 'a fat white worm', a door-knob that seems to grab him back, and finally the chestnut tree's 'naked World' - discovering that existence is a gelatinous, unjustifiable 'messy suffering' and that the order, names, and values we take for reality are only a veneer consciousness projects onto an indeterminate whole. His nausea is the horror of authenticity before it becomes anything else, the price Neo pays for swallowing the pill.

authenticity.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
authenticity.title: Unknown
authenticity.relation: The chapter concedes authenticity's costs - the truths of death, suffering, and meaninglessness are hard to stomach, and inauthenticity is the social norm that makes the authentic person feel alienated and even mad (Roquentin's 'crazy loon category', The Matrix's 'hardware' people who fight unplugging) - but argues the red pill still wins. Inauthenticity never eradicates anxiety (the 'splinter in the mind'), only misattributes it to mundane causes like jobs and cars, and it costs freedom and genuinely informed choice; authenticity ends the flight from being and yields a serenity Roquentin finds when existence becomes 'a perfect free gift'.

authenticity.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
authenticity.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Lenore Wright reads Sam and Frodo's Quest through the two journey motifs of Western philosophy: the journey out (Plato's cave, structuring Augustine's Confessions and Descartes' escape from the senses' deceptions) and the journey inward (the cogito, self-transformation, with Nussbaum's claim that literature gives philosophy a body). Frodo's steps out of the Shire-cave - selling Bag End, 'I will take the Ring, though I do not know the way' - create the Fellowship and its freedoms, while Boromir attains self-knowledge only at death's door and Gandalf, Aragorn, and Sam are remade by the road. Against classical heroes like Theseus and Odysseus, Sam and Frodo are modern pilgrims - Nietzschean Yea-sayers becoming who they are, with Heideggerian 'potentiality-for-Being' - whereas Sméagol and Saruman live inauthentically, defined by their pasts.

authenticity.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
authenticity.title: Inauthenticity and Fascism
authenticity.relation: David Detmer treats Zelig, the mock-documentary 'chameleon man' who turns black, Chinese, fat, or a Nazi depending on his company, as a stark dramatization of personal identity and the existentialist critique of inauthenticity. After rejecting the memory, bodily-continuity, and immaterial-soul criteria of identity, the chapter takes the existentialist line, quoting Heidegger on Dasein's selfhood, that a self is its choices, projects, and commitments, so Zelig's chameleonism is self-estrangement motivated by fear and the craving to be liked. Politically, the chapter draws Allen's lesson that genocides happen not because millions go mad but because millions passively conform, made literal by Zelig appearing at a Hitler rally, and supports it with Asch's conformity experiments and Milgram's obedience studies.

authenticity.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
authenticity.title: Hope
authenticity.relation: Jill Gordon reads Another Woman as a film about self-knowledge structured by Socrates' self-seeing eye from Plato's Alcibiades I: just as an eye sees itself only in another eye, the emotionally walled-off philosophy professor Marion Post finally sees her own repression by overhearing the 'other woman' Hope's therapy through a vent. Each of her relationships, with husband Ken, brother Paul, renounced lover Larry, stepdaughter Laura, and friend Claire, mirrors back truths ('she stands above people and evaluates them') that her self-deception refuses until her dream stages her own analysis and the final session describes her own life exactly. Counting the irrecoverable cost of her chances (Larry, the aborted child), the chapter closes with Rilke's 'Archaic Torso of Apollo', 'You must change your life', as the command Marion finally obeys, yielding a hard-won and still hopeful transformation.

authenticity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
authenticity.title: The Approaching Battle
authenticity.relation: Introduces the chapter's Heideggerian frame: authenticity comes from facing mortality rather than evading it, against the Epicurean advice to be unconcerned since death is merely the end of experience and so happens to no one; death's imminence forces us to define ourselves and not live half-asleep. Harry, death-marked since infancy, lives authentically where Voldemort lives inauthentically, with Plato's dictum that true philosophers make dying their profession as ancient corroboration.

authenticity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
authenticity.title: King’s Cross Station
authenticity.relation: Reads Harry's march into the Forbidden Forest as paradigmatic Heideggerian authenticity: knowing he must die to destroy the soul-fragment in him, his senses sharpen, gratitude wells up for what he never fully valued, and he accepts that he is not fetching his dead loved ones but joining them. The Godric's Hollow gravestone first strikes him as a Death Eater creed of defeating death, and Colin Creevey's return to battle at fourteen shows the same clear-eyed embrace of mortality.

authenticity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
authenticity.title: Reap a Destiny
authenticity.relation: Reads the King's Cross limbo through Heidegger's counsel to choose a hero from the past and gain insight through dialogue with them: Dumbledore appears not as a king of that place but as the humble penitent, confessing his youthful hunger for glory, and the way-station evokes purgatory. The flayed child beneath the bench shows Voldemort's soul beyond repair - his fear of death drove the very choices that now give him reason to fear it - and Tolkien's remark that The Lord of the Rings is really about 'death and the desire for deathlessness' (Sauron pouring his life-force into the One Ring) frames the motif.

authenticity.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
authenticity.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Bruce Reichenbach reads the film's choreographed pas de deux as three distinct theories of atonement: the conquest dance with Satan in Gethsemane (crushing the serpent of Genesis 3:15, Satan's final scream) enacts the Christus victor view of the Church Fathers; Simon of Cyrene's reluctant co-bearing of the cross illustrates Abelard's moral-influence view, though Gibson shows resilient fortitude rather than the love Abelard's theory requires to transform Simon; and Mary's mirrored 'parallel dance' makes her a co-redemptrix sharing her son's agony. Against this he sets Heidegger — Jesus grasps his death with anticipatory resolve, thrownness, and the 'moment of vision' with Mary, but dies for the Other rather than to authenticate his own life — and faults the film for omitting Anselm's (and Swinburne's) substitutionary atonement entirely: no sin, repentance, reparation, or penance appears, unlike Maximilian Kolbe's real substitution at Auschwitz.

authenticity.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
authenticity.title: Only a Jedi Can Save Us Forgetting and Recollecting
authenticity.relation: Abrams reads the saga through Heidegger's philosophy of technology: the lightsaber Luke learns to feel as an extension of his body is the authentic 'ready-to-hand,' while the Death Star - a massive mechanical eye that enfames Alderaan on its viewscreen before destroying it - embodies the 'present-at-hand' gaze of enframing that converts nature into standing reserve (clone and droid armies, stormtrooper armor). Yoda on Dagobah is perfect attunement, an authentic being-in-the-world who is 'at home' with being, and the Force parallels Heidegger's being: everywhere, easily forgotten. Anakin's slide - slave of Watto, severed hand replaced by cybernetics, final encasement in Vader's armor - is progressive enframing and forgetting of his own being, and Luke's 'the name of your true self... you've only forgotten' is the recollection of being by which the Jedi, not a god, saves us.

authenticity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
authenticity.title: Switching Identities
authenticity.relation: Maps Superman and Batman onto Plato and Aristotle — the otherworldly philosopher of the heavenly Good versus the this-worldly master of logic and applicable science — then argues that Bruce Wayne's years of intentional self-transformation may have swapped the mask, making Batman the core identity and Bruce the disguise. With Mark Waid, he sees Superman inwardly embracing his alien otherness as the path of authenticity, both cases yielding a fused "heterosis" of identities; Aristotle, Pascal and William James back the closing lesson that who we are is a matter of what we repeatedly do, so every mask may eventually become the face.

authenticity.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
authenticity.title: The Possibility of Authenticity The Life We Choose
authenticity.relation: Gines reads hip hop's sexual imagery through Black feminist thought - Tupac's feud with C. Delores Tucker over "Wonder Why They Call U Bitch", Patricia Hill Collins's controlling images of the jezebel and welfare mother, bell hooks on the slave-rooted devaluation of Black womanhood, Nelly's "Tip Drill" video with a credit card swiped between a woman's buttocks, Jay-Z's "Big Pimpin'". Applying Sartre's keyhole gaze from Being and Nothingness and his Anti-Semite and Jew point about hierarchical societies, she argues the gaze under racism and sexism is non-reciprocal - women are seen without seeing - and that Lil' Kim's reversal of it reinforces rather than subverts the stereotypes; Butler's gender performativity then frames the closing Sartrean choice of authenticity or inauthenticity, Nas's "I Can" and "the life we choose."

authenticity.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
authenticity.title: The Ends of Despair From “Things Have Changed” to “Love and Theft”
authenticity.relation: Rick Furtak traces an existential arc through Dylan's later albums, reading Blood on the Tracks ("Tangled Up in Blue," "You're a Big Girl Now") as Camus's absurd divorce between a mind that cares and a world that has gone silent, and Heideggerian care as what the narrator loses in "Simple Twist of Fate." "Brownsville Girl" and "Most of the Time" embody Kierkegaard's knight of infinite resignation - hope abandoned but the precious past never forgotten - while "Not Dark Yet" and "Things Have Changed" mark the nadir of despair. On Love and Theft ("Mississippi," "Sugar Baby") the singer turns toward an absurd, Kierkegaardian faith that keeps caring and even loves without demanding that life make sense.

authenticity.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
authenticity.title: Sick of Love
authenticity.relation: Krein and Levin read Dylan's portraits of fallen socialites in "Like a Rolling Stone," "Just Like a Woman," and "To Ramona" as critiques of bad faith - characters who hide from freedom and responsibility in consumerist status games, in Sartre's sense that existence precedes essence. But Beauvoir's Second Sex exposes the cost: the women Dylan praises ("Girl from the North Country," "One More Cup of Coffee") are praised precisely for staying in immanent, pastoral passivity, denied the transcendence that for Beauvoir constitutes full humanity. Borrowing Benjamin's and Buck-Morss's notion of modern "dreamworlds," they finally read Dylan's pastoral utopias as a counter-dreamworld spun after the collapse of the mass-utopian promise of consumer happiness.

authenticity.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
authenticity.title: Synthesis
authenticity.relation: Elizabeth Brake asks what freedom Dylan's outlaw persona - refusing Maggie's Farm, possessive love, and conformity - actually wins, framing the answer with Berlin's two concepts of liberty. Dylan's negations look like Berlin's negative freedom, but Hegel's critique of the "freedom of the void" shows mere refusal ends in emptiness, so she reconstructs a Millian and Emersonian ideal of self-realization for which negative liberty is only the condition. "To live outside the law, you must be honest" supplies the synthesis: outside social law the free person answers to the Emersonian law of his own nature and to undistorted honesty with others, a more severe morality Dylan shares with Emerson and Nietzsche.

authenticity.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
authenticity.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Auxier uses the question 'Would Bruce Springsteen ride a Honda?' as an ontological probe: Honda embodies defensible middle-class values while a Harley is not primarily a machine but 'a decision about life and what makes it valuable', a suicide machine Jesus could have ridden into Jerusalem and whose absence would render Easy Rider meaningless even if Fonda rode some other Harley. His own boyhood purchase of a Honda XL 70 over the Harley Z90 becomes a lesson in Heideggerian honesty, since he knew he belonged on a Honda, while buyers who choose for appearances are consumed by das Man, the they-self that lives inauthentically through images and slogans. Using Husserl's method of imaginative variation on the question, he concludes that the Harley as cultural icon represents an existential decision and the life that follows from it.

authenticity.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
authenticity.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Responding to the Guggenheim's record-breaking 'The Art of the Motorcycle' show, Rollin argues that Dickie's institutional theory explains how motorcycles became art but not why people lined up, and offers three aesthetic lenses: Marinetti's Futurist celebration of machine speed, danger, and rebellion; Dewey's 'an experience', which every ride exemplifies, from his two-week trips with his son to the blown engine rescued by a ranch truck and the canned-spaghetti feast; and the Bauhaus doctrine that form follows function, making customized Harleys industrial sculpture that appreciates in value. He closes with Heidegger: riding's regular face-to-face with 'the possibility of the impossibility of one's being' is a call to authenticity and the final warrant for calling the motorcycle a fountain of aesthetic experience. American Indians revering Harleys as 'iron horses' illustrate the freedom and speed at the core of the bike's aesthetic pull.

authenticity.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
authenticity.title: U2 and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Soper tracks Bono's public identity work across three paradigms: pre-modern Irish-Catholic inheritance, including a Du Boisian 'double consciousness' of the colonized Irish; the modernist artist-as-visionary, where Nietzsche, Freud and Marx destabilize the self and the Shalom fellowship nearly ends the band; and the postmodern masks of the Fly, Mirrorball Man and MacPhisto on the Zoo TV media collage, read via Lacan for 'Mofo' and via Baudrillard's simulacra for the 'Even Better than the Real Thing' video with its wax Beatles and cyber-sex imagery. Lyotardian skepticism toward grand ideologies explains the band's refusal of fanaticism in 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and 'Two Hearts Beat as One'. Soper concludes that Bono fuses all three into a 'Postmodern Christian Pragmatism' that keeps Christian conviction and debt-relief activism while adopting postmodern playfulness without collapsing into ironic detachment.

authenticity.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
authenticity.title: U2 and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Delancey asks why anyone should take moral and political cues from a rock band and answers via Heidegger: in a mediascape where a few corporations orchestrate what everyone hears, the mass tune is das Man ('Numb'), and adopting it is inauthenticity - so U2, who believe what they sing for their own reasons ('Mothers of the Disappeared' against the official line on Latin America), may be among the most authentic voices available. Plato's tripartite soul and Aristotle's golden mean supply the thesis that reason needs rightly trained passion: the righteous anger of 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and 'Silver and Gold' and the resolve of 'Walk On' are practical wisdom in song, the emotions democracy requires. Against Plato's philosopher-king and his noble lies, Delancey argues utopia can only be fostered, not enforced - so in a democracy, if you want to change the world, you may have to sing to people.

authenticity.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
authenticity.title: U2 and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Benfell reads U2's apocalyptic songs through Heidegger rather than through eschatological doctrine: 'The Playboy Mansion' depicts fallenness in the 'they', a consumerist paradise with 'no time for sorrow' that lets us flee our own death, while the angel's fall in Wenders' films evoked by 'Stay' and the day-to-day constraints of 'Some Days Are Better than Others' illustrate thrownness, and 'Gone' existential guilt as an unpayable debt. A verse-by-verse reading of 'Until the End of the World' - the Judas-at-the-last-supper reading as one register - shows the speaker moving from 'passing time' and playing roles in the 'they' to anxious guiltiness and the call of conscience, reaching for the one whose resolute waiting models anticipatory resoluteness. The 'end of the world', he concludes, is the end of the speaker's own world: U2's apocalyptic imagery calls listeners to authentic, finite existence, not to prediction of last things.

authenticity.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
authenticity.title: Heil Heidegger Dracula’s Willing Executioners
authenticity.relation: Adam Barrows reads Stoker's Dracula through Being and Time: the staking of Lucy is the liberation of a true humanity trapped in a deathless shell, and Dracula's endless, mirror-less, selfless existence is Heideggerian inauthenticity - the 'they' that tranquilizes the dying, Renfield's seduction repeating the neighbors' comforting, the refusal of being-toward-death - so vampire-hunting becomes a philosophical task of enforcing authentic, death-claiming being. The chapter then turns the critique on Heidegger himself: his Nazi membership and fundamental ontology's contempt for the everyday leave a gap for racial purity thinking, making Van Helsing's 'butcher work' look like the ritual expulsion of the inauthentic from ontological purity, and asking whether, in adaptation after adaptation, we are Dracula's willing executioners.

authenticity.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
authenticity.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
authenticity.relation: David Hart uses Heidegger's Being and Time to explain Batman's dedication without reducing it to trauma-determined compulsion: Alfred's butler's-world illustrates being-in-the-world and the thrown-project, and Bruce's confrontation with death, culminating in the bleeding alley scene of Miller's Batman: Year One, is Angst, the recognition of finitude that strips ordinary meanings away. Seen this way, "I shall become a bat" is an authentic, responsible choice of a whole life rather than a mechanical effect of childhood trauma. Hart concludes that Heidegger's analysis dissolves the free will versus determinism debate, since Batman neither blindly follows causes nor chooses from nowhere.

authenticity.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
authenticity.title: Reap a Destiny
authenticity.relation: Jonathan and Jerry Walls read Deathly Hallows philosophically: Harry's willing march into the Forbidden Forest is Heideggerian authenticity, confronting being-toward-death, while Voldemort's horcruxes and the maimed King's Cross stowaway are the inauthentic flight from mortality that ruins the soul. The afterlife scene raises the stakes of this life: by James's "sow a thought... reap a destiny," Aristotle's habituation, and Locke's memory-based identity, Voldemort's lifelong refusal of remorse fixes his character beyond repair, and Kant and Pascal supply reasons why belief in an afterlife transforms morality. Dumbledore's purgatory-like repentance, contrasted with Voldemort's fate, shows that our choices reap a destiny we must live with forever.

authenticity.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
authenticity.title: Previews and Opening Credits
authenticity.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Hitchcock is a profound artist whose classic films are organized around ideas, citing Chabrol and Rohmer's claim that each film rests on a 'formal postulate,' so that philosophical issues arise directly from his cinematic motifs. It previews four features of Hitchcock's vision the volume will explore: an anti-utopian outlook on a fallen world perpetually at risk of chaos, an existentialist affirmation of self-definition through choice and commitment, a construal of spectatorship as flight from commitment and authenticity, and an anticipation of later thinking on the social roles of women. It closes with acknowledgments to the contributors, series editor Bill Irwin, and Open Court.

authenticity.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
authenticity.title: Bad Faith
authenticity.relation: Lee reads the 'Breakdown' episode of Alfred Hitchcock Presents existentially: when the executive Callou coldly fires Humka and hangs up on his despair, he treats a person as a thing, Buber's 'I-It' pseudo-listening where Humka sought an 'I-Thou' dialogue with the godlike source of authority in his world. Heidegger's account of inauthenticity explains the mask of rational control behind which Callou hides, and Sartre's bad faith names the self-deception by which he pretends his godlike management of others is justifiable.
