Paralyzed and taken for a corpse after a car crash, Callou can be saved only when rational strategy fails and he finally weeps: the single tear reveals his caring nature, Jessie addresses him person-to-person, and, vulnerable before God and others, he becomes an authentic self, Hitchcock's pointed moral for bosses who give an employee the sack.

authenticity.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
authenticity.title: I’ll Get Up and Fly Away
authenticity.relation: Ian Duckles and Eric Rubenstein use the community's losses of Pigpen and Jerry Garcia to ask whether death is bad, running Epicurus's argument that being dead is no experience and hence no harm, the tedium-of-immortality argument that eternal life would eventually exhaust every fundamental desire, and Socrates's Phaedo claim that death frees the soul to philosophize — which disturbingly implies Pigpen's early 'burn out' was the better fate. Their resolution is Heidegger: authentically confronting death as the end of all possibilities strips socially imposed values (consumerist 'keeping up with the Joneses') and frees us to create our own projects, so mortality itself is something to be grateful for. On this reading the Deadhead counterculture — rejecting 1950s suburban scripts for free love, psychedelics, and life on tour — lived Heideggerian authenticity, and it is better to fade away (like Garcia) than to burn out (like Pigpen).

authenticity.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
authenticity.title: Does Johnny Rotten Still Hate Pink Floyd
authenticity.relation: Reisch argues that Johnny Rotten's 'I hate Pink Floyd' T-shirt was a provocation aimed at the band everyone loved, since Pink Floyd was the exception to late-1970s corporate blandness rather than a symptom of it. Tracing the band from Syd Barrett's disintegration (the ever-changing 'Have You Got It Yet?', his unrecognizable 1975 walk-in at the Wish You Were Here sessions) through the Dark Side triumph and the Waters/Gilmour split, he contends that Pink Floyd 'was punk long before the Ramones and the Sex Pistols.' Where punk used two-minute power chords, Pink Floyd meticulously sharpened an ax to grind: 'Have a Cigar' and 'Welcome to the Machine' dissect the industry machine that cages and commodifies artists, and the whole project attacks the inauthenticity, alienation, and tragedy of modern life.

authenticity.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
authenticity.title: We Don’t Need No Indoctrination
authenticity.relation: Detmer argues the four classic albums from Dark Side to The Wall form a unified meditation on alienation, from others, work, nature, and oneself, and reads Waters's stated 'political and philosophical' aims through the existentialists. 'Breathe''s rabbit digging one hole after another illustrates Marx's alienated labor (the worker 'only feels himself freely active in his animal functions'), echoed by Russell on industrialism's life against instinct and Camus on the day the 'why' arises; 'Time''s missed starting gun dramatizes our thrown condition and Heidegger's claim that only facing mortality head-on cures the inauthenticity of living as 'they' do, while Gilmour's improvised solos model the spontaneity such authenticity requires. 'Money' is a satire of greed confirmed by 'Dogs,' whose self-rationalizing climbers end 'dragged down by the stone,' and 'Us and Them' attacks artificial divisions (soldiers manipulated by map-movers, racism's 'black and blue,' the old man who dies 'for the want of the price of tea and a slice'). 'Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2)' indicts indoctrination, being told what to think, rather than education itself, making independent critical thought the road to the Sartrean autonomy and responsibility the chapter urges.

authenticity.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
authenticity.title: Authentic Cash
authenticity.relation: Butler rehearses how the Johnny Cash persona was socially manufactured: Sam Phillips coined the name "Johnny Cash" for its rebellious marketing value, "Folsom Prison Blues" narrates a prison term Cash never served (and borrowed from Jimmie Rodgers and Gordon Jenkins), and the Man in Black image began as an accident of black shirts at a Memphis church performance. Against Jung's persona-as-mask and Dr. Phil's "authentic core self," and armed with George Herbert Mead's social theory of the self, he argues authenticity is not fidelity to a hidden inner essence but active engagement with the social processes shaping one's identity, the way paper money gains "cash value" through use. Cash invested the imposed persona with value by sincerely living it (for example, writing "Man in Black" to give the black clothes his own meaning), so the construct became genuinely his identity.

authenticity.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
authenticity.title: Reason to Believe When There’s None
authenticity.relation: Couch takes a night drive through Springsteen's road songs guided by Karl Jaspers's 'ultimate situations' — death ('Wreck on the Highway,' the bottomless gorge under the cruise-controlled life), suffering (the never-ending badlands, shared in Tom Joad's ghost), struggle (violent like 'Johnny 99,' loving as the search for 'one clear moment of love and truth'), and guilt ('Everybody's got a secret, Sonny'; 'you learn to sleep at night with the price you pay'). Jaspers's Existenz-philosophy — built on Kierkegaard's inward self and Nietzsche's diagnosis of the herd, against Kant's optimism about knowledge — explains the songs' endless border-crossings as attempts to evade limits that cannot be evaded, and the fear that turns 'your God filled soul' to 'devils and dust.' The answer to how there's a 'Reason to Believe' is Jaspers's leap of philosophic (not religious) faith toward the unknowable Transcendent, chosen in complete freedom.

authenticity.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
authenticity.title: Epilogue
authenticity.relation: Auxier's epilogue teaches readers to build playful 'ontologies' from the book's list of Springsteen's proper names — imagining Elvis's .44 Magnum ('Betsy') traveling from a Vegas evidence room into 'Johnny 99' and '57 Channels,' and asking 'Would Bruce ride a Honda?' He borrows Heidegger's idea that the answer already lives in the question, and uses das Man — the inauthentic 'they-self' that chooses by appearances — to contrast Harley riders who confront an existential decision with Honda's self-conserving middle-class pragmatism. The Harley as 'suicide machine' (like Captain America in Easy Rider, like Jesus's passion) embodies freedom and authenticity; Foucault's Borgesian Chinese encyclopedia reminds us that orders of things are conventional, so the ontology itself is one imaginative path among many.

authenticity.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
authenticity.title: If You Think that You’re Strong Enough . .
authenticity.relation: Matthew Lampert argues that Radiohead's stock theme of "alienation" is exactly Heideggerian inauthenticity: das Man's platitudes made audible in "Fitter Happier," the falling into the world's "uninhibited hustle" of "Ripcord" and "Let Down," and the tranquility that hides both the problem and any exit. He traces the band's arc from the punk-romantic fix of "Anyone Can Play Guitar" (choose and win yourself, form a band) to a deeper diagnosis on The Bends and OK Computer, where Heidegger's Ge-stell and standing-reserve show that in a technological framework only further technological solutions to technological alienation are available. Following "Why Poets?" and Holderlin's question, he concludes that Kid A makes Radiohead the poets in a desolate time: by risking disappearance itself ("How to Disappear Completely," "Idioteque") and singing alienation in its fullness rather than offering false hope, they stare into the abyss where "the more brightly do the ways into the saving power begin to shine."

authenticity.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
authenticity.title: Jimmy Buffett “Singer of Inordinate Tunes” and Heideggerian Troubadour
authenticity.relation: Drew Dalton takes Buffett's claim that 'we don't just enjoy our escapism — we NEED it' as an admission that being itself is burdensome, overturning the Plato–Augustine–Leibniz consensus that it is good to be. Since 'Margaritaville is nowhere' — it is on no map and can never be reached — what we long for is not a better vacation but release from having to be at all, which is why even on holiday in Key West we still dream of escape. Heidegger's Being and Time supplies the framework: thrownness, being-toward-death, anxiety, and guilt reveal existence as a weight we never chose, so the escapist longing to be otherwise than ourselves is the 'inauthentic' flight Heidegger describes (without moral condemnation), and Levinas's On Escape confirms that 'it is precisely from all that is weighty in being that escaping sets forth.'

authenticity.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
authenticity.title: The Missionary
authenticity.relation: Christopher Hoyt reads Buffett's escape from Catholicism as a case study in secular meaning-making after Nietzsche's death of God, taking the Mardi Gras ritual of Folly swatting Death out of town as Buffett's core spiritual attitude — interpreted the way Wittgenstein criticized Frazer, as an expression of our stance toward death rather than mere magic. Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' frames the post-1960s task of self-definition without God, while Marx's alienation explains what the persona of *Jimmy* refuses: the impersonal work and borrowed values that leave moderns living an alien narrative, like McGuane's character Skelton in Ninety-Two in the Shade. The twist is that *Jimmy*'s pop-culture vocabulary — Tully Mars built from Donovan's Reef and Slim Pickens, Bogart, the Brylcreem jingle — is itself authentic, and the 'semi-true story' of the myth tells deeper truths than a literal biography could, making Buffett something like a pop prophet for late modernity.

authenticity.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
authenticity.title: Moving On
authenticity.relation: Frazier reads the show through Freud: Stephen play-acts both the repressed religious-right superego (Dobson, Hagee, his terror of bug sex) and the aggressive American id, so his improvised irony — shielding his crotch from Michael Stipe, mangling Teddy Roosevelt's big-stick maxim for Joe Sestak, sneering at the women's-softball sportsmanship story — works as therapeutic catharsis that lets viewers laugh at and tame their own aggression and hang-ups. Against MacIntyre's charge that irony corrodes culture, he enlists Kierkegaard's picture of the ironist who outdoes a view's 'ludicrous enthusiasm' (the U.S.A.! chant at Naomi Wolf, the gun-control interview that collapses into a case against itself), concluding that the man who merely played the true patriot was the more authentic American.

authenticity.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
authenticity.title: Authentic Rock
authenticity.relation: Theodore Gracyk asks whether Zeppelin's uncredited borrowings—Willie Dixon's 'You Need Love' into 'Whole Lotta Love', Spirit's 'Taurus' into 'Stairway to Heaven', Jake Holmes's 'I'm Confused' into 'Dazed and Confused'—undermine their status as an authentic rock band whose value supposedly rests on sincere self-expression and original songwriting. Using Hanslick's thought experiment as staged by Little Roger and the Goosebumps's 'Gilligan's Island (Stairway)' parody and Handel's recycling of his own music into the Messiah, he argues a song's expressive power comes from the interaction of words and music (guarding against the fallacies of division and composition), and that by itself music is neither angry nor spiritual. Since Zeppelin's instrumental arrangements diverge radically from their sources and the lawsuits turned on Plant's lyrics, the chapter concludes that transformation, not narrow originality, grounds their genius—so the rock-versus-pop authenticity standard must be loosened.

authenticity.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
authenticity.title: One Last Anguished Existential Scream
authenticity.relation: Argues Neon Genesis Evangelion and Akira dramatize a justified anxiety about humanity's evolutionary future: SEELE's Human Instrumentality Project — dissolving everyone into the Sea of LCL because separate, mutually harming individuals have 'run the course' of their evolution — is Heideggerian anxiety (the objectless unease that breaks us out of 'the They') curdled, via Mary Midgley's 'fatalism,' into the belief that genes, Moore's Law, or 'the Market' leave no room for human choice. Akira's Numbered Children, who sacrifice themselves to remove Tetsuo and save Kaneda, model the responsible alternative: accepting that the power is coming, screaming about it, and still choosing how humanity faces it rather than abdicating to fate.

authenticity.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
authenticity.title: The Authentic Red Sox Fan, or The Importance of Turning off NESN and Finding
authenticity.relation: Corey McCall asks what makes a 'true' Red Sox fan, contrasting the beer-soaked bleacher loudmouth with one-hundred-year-old honorary batboy Arthur Giddon, and treats the nostalgia and resentment around the 2004 bandwagon as the Enlightenment problem of authenticity in miniature. Through Kant's 'Sapere aude' and the ideal of autonomy, he argues the authentic fan is the critical fan who uses reason about the team (questioning Francona's moves, judging whole careers) instead of losing herself in uncritical devotion, reading Jason Varitek's 2004 muzzle of A-Rod as the moment the team's identity crystallized for fans who wanted to be like him. With the Curse gone, fans are freed from fated suffering but inherit Kant's burden of autonomously choosing how fandom will define them, since circumstances no longer decide.

authenticity.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
authenticity.title: Only an Ortiz Can Save Us Heidegger’s Revelation of Being
authenticity.relation: James Pontuso reads Red Sox history through Heidegger: technology that turns the world into 'standing reserve' breeds the anxious 'everydayness' of the mediocre Pinky Higgins teams, while the run of near-misses from 1967 through Bucky Dent in 1978 and Buckner in 1986 threw fans into an authentic encounter with tragedy, mortality and the mystery of Being that the Yankees' free-agent 'technology of power' could never teach. Fenway Park, quirky and continuous with the pre-Hitler past, serves as 'home' in Heidegger's homeless age, and the literati's tragic framing of the team (language as the house of Being) made its fate a matter of existential weight rather than mere sport. David Ortiz's 2004 ALCS heroics then function as Heidegger's longed-for revelation of Being, the answer to 'only a god can save us,' after which fans have lived through all three states: everydayness, tragic anxiety, and wonder.

authenticity.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
authenticity.title: Manny
authenticity.relation: Santaniello reads five nonconformist Red Sox through ethical theory. Ruth's sale to New York becomes a Kantian case: he tore up his signed three-year contract and demanded a trade while expecting others to keep promises, violating the categorical imperative on promise-keeping. Ted Williams's lifelong war with the 'Knights of the Keyboard' exemplifies existentialist authenticity ('It just wouldn't have been me' tipping his cap), Spaceman Bill Lee embodies Sartre's condemned freedom and existence precedes essence, Jim Rice's Hall of Fame delay is Aristotle's failure to hit the mean between silent deficiency on Boston's racism and excess toward reporters, and Manny's 'Gas is up and so am I' money grab shows Aristotle's point that wealth is an incomplete end pursued for the sake of something else.

authenticity.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
authenticity.title: Heil Heidegger Dracula’s Willing Executioners
authenticity.relation: Adam Barrows reads Stoker's Dracula through Being and Time: Stoker's staking of Lucy is framed as liberating the 'true' human from the 'false' Undead, and Mina urges pity on the trapped soul, exactly the structure of Heidegger's claim that only facing one's own death alone makes life a bounded, authentic whole. Dracula emerges as the inauthentic 'they' incarnate, with no reflection in mirrors, no fixed likeness in portraits, and a seduction of tranquilizing delay that mirrors how das Man lulls the dying away from their death, so vampire hunting becomes a philosophical task of forcing authenticity on the deathless. The chapter then reverses the charge: given Heidegger's Nazism, Van Helsing's gleeful 'butcher work' and the hunters' expulsion of 'inauthentic' beings from ontological purity implicate audiences as Dracula's 'willing executioners' in a ritual with chilling fascist overtones.

authenticity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
authenticity.title: A Reply to facebook Critics
authenticity.relation: Wittkower answers critics who call Facebook broadcast narcissism by way of Sartre: Facebook actions (pokes, the Disney Princess quiz, cats friending cats on Catbook) have no given meaning, so users and their friends create it, which is why there are 'so many different Facebooks'. He takes up Sunstein's 'Daily Me' echo-chamber worry and Hegel's claim that real freedom means choosing within community, arguing Facebook merely makes the dialectic between chosen and unchosen communities explicit. Against the charge that status updates are trivial, he deploys Nietzsche's Last Man and Schopenhauer's cheese-mite microscope to defend caring about a friend's sandwich from the inside of a shared life.

authenticity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
authenticity.title: 6 - You Can’t Front on facebook
authenticity.relation: Marinucci opens with Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Plato's Republic - invisibility licenses injustice because we care about seeming good - and maps it onto Suler's six factors of online disinhibition (anonymity, invisibility, asynchronicity, solipsism, dissociation, minimized authority). Facebook, she argues, lacks all six: real names and offline friends, near-synchronous news feeds, and the integration of every audience from mom to students into one space keep us inhibited. That inhibition is a good thing, since it prevents 'fronting' - presenting a false face to each audience - so Facebook identity integration can foster more authentic self-expression.

authenticity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
authenticity.title: 7 - Why I Am Not a Friend
authenticity.relation: Thalos argues she is not a 'friend' on Facebook because bonding requires credible, fixed self-presentation, and a profile 'can lie like a rug' since everything on it is elective and revisable at whim. Through Sartre's phenomenology of the gaze - being displaced from Subject to object-for-another when caught in another's look - she explains why face-to-face interaction alone builds the mutual bonds and social intelligence we rely on. With Beauvoir she shows how the gaze also carries power, marking woman as the Other, and warns that Facebook's plastic faces offer choice without traction, inhibiting both true bonding and resistance to subjugating looks.

authenticity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
authenticity.title: 8 - Playing Around with Identity
authenticity.relation: Wandel and Beavers take Groundhog Day's Phil Connors as the model of trying on selves, and apply Goffman's dramaturgical Presentation of Self to see Facebook as a stage where users experiment with identity. Because friends from every part of life watch at once, a 'restraint of accountability' disciplines pretending, much like childhood pretend play or a fraternity's teasing calls members to account for their oddities. Against critics who see fragmentation and narcissism, they argue this dynamic can support becoming who one already is - a more authentic, grounded self - closing with Plato's 'Life must be lived as play'.

authenticity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
authenticity.title: 13 - What Are Friends For
authenticity.relation: Bloor reads Facebook anxiety through Heidegger's diagnosis of technological nihilism — an efficiency-driven 'being-in-the-world' with no shared arbiter of what matters — borrowing Dreyfus's HAL 9000 example from 2001: A Space Odyssey to show humans enhancing themselves like any other raw material. He argues Facebook's speed lures users into unreflective sharing and standardized behavior where the quirky authentic 'I' dissolves into Heidegger's 'one,' and recruits Aristotle's view that only a few deep friendships morally form us to warn that hundreds of contacts fragment that benefit. Adorno on leisure as mere recuperation between bouts of work frames the therapist who keeps Facebook strictly professional, and the chapter concludes the fault lies in ourselves, not the tools — suggesting a week offline as a test.

authenticity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
authenticity.title: 18 - Gatekeeper, Moderator, Synthesizer
authenticity.relation: Butera casts Facebook's three core features as instruments of control: friending is a 'gatekeeper' admitting selected others, the status update a 'moderator' constantly re-authoring the avatar's identity for multiple audiences, and the News Feed a 'synthesizer' that assembles a filtered pseudo-community where friends can be hidden or stalked invisibly. Reading this through Baudrillard's 'promiscuity' of communication networks — the extermination of the interstitial space where the social happens — and Kierkegaard's case that a meaningful life requires openness to the unknown, he weighs unrestricted community as authentic contact against the gated community that keeps exchange meaningful. The defunct no-privacy experiment Buddytown serves as counterpoint, and he concludes that some gatekeeping is essential lest connectivity become an overwhelming flood of nonsense.

authenticity.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
authenticity.title: Refereeing in the World
authenticity.relation: Crowe uses Sartre to explain why refereeing is existentially anguished: in the moment of decision — Grosso's fall over Neill's outstretched legs at the 2006 World Cup — the referee is radically free and solely responsible, and that anguish drives the six familiar referee types into bad faith. The stickler hides behind the letter of Law 12 as Sartre's student hid behind ethical formulas, the ditherer repeats the woman who leaves her hand inert on her date's, the poseur and frustrated player over-act the café waiter's role, and the postman and tough guy play the 'champion of sincerity' who treats character as fixed. The ideal is the authentic referee 'refereeing in the world' — Collina disallowing his own awarded goal at San Siro and explaining why to Inter — who owns his contingency: 'This is what I have chosen.'

authenticity.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
authenticity.title: Living the Absurd Life
authenticity.relation: Krein asks why he has spent fifteen years on karate when pepper spray and avoidance would serve self-defense better, and answers with existentialism rather than Buddhism. Nietzsche's death of God and Sartre's claim that existence precedes essence leave life objectively meaningless, but the dojo supplies a self-contained standard for Sartrean transcendence (kata quality is judged within the art), trains the courage and clarity authenticity requires, and enforces excuse-free responsibility: in sparring you either score or you don't. Studying a traditional martial art is thus a heroic, 'act without hope' defiance of the absurd.

authenticity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
authenticity.title: I Am the Bad Wolf
authenticity.relation: Answers Davros's charge that the Doctor fashions companions into weapons by examining his character through virtue ethics: his unifying virtue is Heideggerian 'authentic concern', always offering aggressors like the Nestene or the Sycorax a choice so they become genuinely responsible, as in the fly-swatting thought experiment. Companions instead act from compassion, which lacks impartiality and produces the 'Bad Wolf Syndrome' (Rose's Dalek genocide, Martha's Osterhagen Key, Jack's warp star). Since for Aristotle a friend is 'another himself', the companions' actions are in a sense the Doctor's own yet founded on a distorted disposition, which is why he runs from his past.

authenticity.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
authenticity.title: No Heart to Lie
authenticity.relation: Reuland uses YouTube drum covers of 'The Body Electric', 'Subdivisions', and 'YYZ' to analyze Rush's 'aesthetic of replicability': songs built as artifacts meant to be reproduced note-for-note, signaled by literal codes like the Morse-code intro to 'YYZ' and the binary '1001001' the android of 'The Body Electric' must crack to become human. He explains why critics deride this anti-expressive virtuosity by way of Amiri Baraka's racial coding of technique, Pierre Bourdieu's account of how 'natural' taste is legitimated while studied learning bears class stigma, and Mary Bucholtz's picture of nerds as hyper-white; the fans' literal meritocracy parodies the information economy's promise that skill converts directly into success. Finally he reads 'Limelight' as Rush's skepticism toward performance as a 'gilded cage' of inauthenticity, so that play-along videos recode performance as self-improvement that cannot be faked.

authenticity.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
authenticity.title: A Story in Search of a Narrator
authenticity.relation: Brian Gregor reads Dexter through Charles Taylor's 'self-interpreting animal': Dexter's identity is not a fixed thing but comes into being through self-interpretation within an inescapable framework of value, so even his 'Am I good? Am I evil?' rebellion and the Nietzschean Übermensch reading fail to escape the deeper convictions about innocence, evil and desert that Harry's Code presupposes - as his guilt over the innocent Farrow shows. The chapter interprets Dexter's serial failures at being 'seen' - Harry's 'only one who really saw me', Brian's fraternal 'you can be yourself with me', Lila's probing, and Miguel Prado as Aristotle's friend, 'another self' - as Hegelian struggles for recognition that collapse because his real self can never come into the open. Finally, drawing on MacIntyre's narrative account of identity, it argues Dexter is literally a story in search of a narrator, whose selfhood persists through flashbacks, blood slides and noir-style voice-overs, and whose humanity shows in the need to have his account of himself heard and corrected by another.

authenticity.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
authenticity.title: Becoming a Real Boy
authenticity.relation: Phillip Deen places Dexter on the scale of character types from Book VII of Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics - temperate, morally strong (Angel Batista), morally weak (Deb), self-indulgent (Masuka), and the beast - rejecting the Socratic view that vice is mere ignorance, and argues Dexter is neither self-indulgent nor simply beastly but a 'morally strong beast.' The decisive test is Kant's tribunal of conscience and the morality-versus-prudence question: Dexter gathers proof before killing, feels remorse for Jonathan Farrow, and tells Trinity 'No, but I want to be' morally superior - yet his delight at Doakes's death exposes mere prudence. Deen closes with Brian's Heideggerian offer of authenticity ('you could be yourself around me') refused: Dexter hopes that by pretending the feelings are there he may one day 'turn into a real boy.'

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: The Cardinal Mystery of Creation
authenticity.relation: The chapter completes the Heidegger arc: where danger is grows the saving power, so Deckard's first thoughts on finding the toad (U.N. stars and reward money) expose his alienation from any authentic relation to the world, yet he ends 'devoted' to the electric toad because 'The electric things have their lives, too.' Roy Batty's tears-in-rain speech becomes the film's expression of the same saving power: wonder at the mystery of Being is what essentially ensouls humans and replicants alike.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: You’ve Been Adjusted
authenticity.relation: The chapter tracks the Hollywood upgrades: the 'bald and fat and old' administrator of 'The Minority Report' becomes Tom Cruise, the 'miserable little salaried employee' of 'We Can Remember It for You Wholesale' becomes Arnold Schwarzenegger, and real-estate clerk Ed becomes Matt Damon running for Congress. It contrasts The Adjustment Bureau's David Norris, whose defiance of the Chairman's Plan is rewarded with the girl, with Ed Fletcher of 'Adjustment Team', who grovels ('don't de-energize me') and is released only because he is too minor to matter. The upshot: Dick wrote about authenticity, not heroes, and the films swap ordinary endurance for larger-than-life agency.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Scott versus Linklater
authenticity.relation: The chapter contrasts the directors, Scott's muscular, sensory-assaulting urban noir versus Linklater's quiet, rotoscoped suburban everyday, and their fidelity to the source: quoting Edelstein, Blade Runner misses the novel's empathy-centered psychological complexity, while A Scanner Darkly foregrounds its author with Dick's face appearing in the scramble suit, the closing Author's Note, and Dick's daughters on a faithfully recreated Orange County set. The evaluative criterion throughout is authenticity to Dick, which Linklater preserves and Scott wildly transforms.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Deckard versus Arctor
authenticity.relation: The chapter sets Ford's redemptive Deckard against Keanu Reeves's Bob Arctor, the everyman who spies on himself and disintegrates on Substance D, noting the shared scaffolding (lawman, shadowy supplier Tyrell/New Path, nemesis with doubtful humanity, woman in identity crisis) that only highlights the divergence: Deckard is educated into humanity through Rachael while Arctor is progressively dehumanized, with Donna/Audrey betraying rather than redeeming him. It leans on Dick's 'The Android and the Human' definition of becoming an android as being 'pounded down, manipulated, made into a means without one's knowledge or consent', so that Blade Runner imagines androids becoming human where A Scanner Darkly shows humans becoming androids, with even nature (New Path's corn fields) enlisted in the enslavement.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Through a Screen, Darkly
authenticity.relation: The chapter argues A Scanner Darkly is consciously about the media itself: rotoscoping inserts a critical break between viewer and screen, exposing our love of scanning and being scanned, an edge that Hollywood, itself invested in media technology, habitually blunts. Against the blockbuster escape it cites Dick's 'How to Build a Universe that Doesn't Fall Apart Two Days Later', where ordinary people's heroism lies in quiet refusals ('they cannot be compelled to be what they are not'), and ends with Deckard's 'unnatural self' and Arctor's 'soul sickness', both of whom endure, which is where their and our heroism lies.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: How Animals Make Us Human
authenticity.relation: The chapter contrasts the novel, where humanity is secured through empathetic relations with scarce real animals (Deckard hating his electric sheep's 'tyranny' because it does not know he exists), with the film, where photographs do the validating: Rachael's 'Look, it's me with my mother' treats the photo as a self-grounding artifact, which the chapter explains via Baudrillard's precession of simulacra, supplemented by Sontag's point that photos act as surrogate relations documenting the loved one's absence. Deckard's piano covered in old sepia photos then reads as overcompensation: abundant evidence, no current relationships, a hint that he may be an android.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: The Lives of Electric Others
authenticity.relation: The chapter follows Deckard past despair at universal fakery (the toad electric, Mercer a set) to his muted epiphany, 'The electric things have their lives, too', and his 'Mercer isn't fake... unless reality is fake', asking whether this extends his circle of moral concern to electric beings or merely concedes the inescapability of virtuality. It reads the film's origami unicorn and Deckard's willingness to make a life with Rachael as parallel acceptances, ending with Iran ordering 'one pound of artificial flies that really fly around and buzz' for the toad her husband is devoted to.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Phil Chews the Fat
authenticity.relation: The chapter closes on VALIS's opening gambit, 'I am Horselover Fat, and I am writing this in the third person to gain much-needed objectivity', and Dick's proliferating self-theories (vitamin C overdose, alien telepathy, past lives, Gnostic revelation) across VALIS, Radio Free Albemuth and the Exegesis. Butler weighs the bad-faith reading, that Dick was nailing down a determinate identity to escape the responsibility to choose, against Dick's own android-human essays, in which the authentic human acts spontaneously and throws off masks, concluding that Dick's refusal to settle on any one theory of himself was his playful, Sartrean way of knowing he is not an android.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Freedom and Madness
authenticity.relation: Updates the McCarthyite stakes of pre-guilt with Michelle Bachmann's 'anti-American' probing and the Guantánamo detainees who are 'too dangerous to transfer but not feasible for prosecution.' Dick's own post-2-3-74 spiral — after the pink light he was writing in his Exegesis about telepathic crab-clawed invaders from Sirius — becomes the case study for the book's closing practical problem: how to free yourself from received social, political, and religious determination without careering into drugs, isolation, or madness.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Ma or Machine
authenticity.relation: Takes Dick's Exegesis self-description ('I am a fictionalizing philosopher') and his twin questions — what is ultimately real, what constitutes the authentic human being — to argue that for Dick the difference between real and fake humans is empathy, not materials. The Adjustment Bureau's emotionally detached bureaucratese ('We are fully licensed to make such corrections') repels, while in 'Human Is' the Rexorian colonizing cruel Lester's body behaves 'more truly human' than the genetic human he replaced.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Chapter 20 - If the Universe Isn’t Real, How Should We Treat Other People
authenticity.relation: Andrew M. Butler's introduction opens with the ambiguous endings of Total Recall, Minority Report, and Blade Runner (the fade to white, the too-neat reunion, the improbable sunset) to pose skeptical doubt about whether any of Dick's realities are real, surveying Eye in the Sky, Flow My Tears, Time Out of Joint, and Next. Against the thought that if nothing is real nothing matters, it sets Eric Sweetscent returning to his failing wife, and introduces Dick's aim to fuse Hebrew monotheism with Heidegger's philosophy of thrownness, noting that Levinas made the attempt first and that for Dick the authentic human is the one who cares for others.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Freedom Without Origins
authenticity.relation: The section rejects randomness as a foundation for freedom, quantum indeterminacy being Epicurus's swerve again, since actions tracing to random particle events are no more mine than law-determined ones, then turns to the ethical problem: if Hauser volunteered and Cohaagen's story is true, freedom-as-origination would require Quaid to become Hauser again, Mercedes included. Quaid's verdict ('The guy's a fucking asshole') shows freedom is also changing course to do what is right; as Lowe says in 'We Can Remember It for You Wholesale,' what defines us is 'not a memory but a desire,' and in breaking with his past Quaid decisively becomes free.

authenticity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
authenticity.title: Cultural Minority Report
authenticity.relation: This section asks whether the outsider can live in society with dignity, using Charles Taylor's politics of recognition, the claim that dominant societies commit an egregious harm when they refuse to affirm a subculture's value, to read Arctor and his friends as a subculture whose leftover American dream is recognition. Parallels with indigenous ceremonies, typecast immigrant youth, and French assimilation pressure frame the novel's question: can pluralist America include drug culture, or does the ethical order that preaches pluralism have limits the Arctors have already hit?

authenticity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
authenticity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Vannatta's introduction frames the volume with a traffic-intersection metaphor: Klosterman's campaign against the phrase 'guilty pleasure' questions whether the one-way roads of high and low culture are real at all, and the contributors deliberately violate the traffic rules (Kierkegaard meets KISS, Baudrillard meets Britney Spears). It reads Klosterman's line that 'nothing is ever in and of itself' through Kant's noumena-phenomena distinction: like Kant's knowing subject, we never reach the in-itself but only perspectives refracted through rock bands, sports teams, and TV. The introduction presents the Guns N' Roses tribute band Paradise City (identity effaced to imitate an equally constructed identity) and the rock-death road trip of Killing Yourself to Live as Klosterman's way of recovering authenticity, arguing that living with the possibility of one's own death is more authentic than fleeing it.

authenticity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
authenticity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Vannatta explains why Seinfeld reruns now fall flat through Klosterman's neologism 'unironically': since about 1991 irony has become the invisible background of American comedy, a pervasive detachment that David Foster Wallace named and that Jedediah Purdy's For Common Things attacks as the gap between phenomenon and essence. Against Purdy's ironist (Seinfeld's Jerry, mastered by irony, believing in nothing but his own interests), the chapter sets Kierkegaard's Socrates, whose 'infinite absolute negativity' and confessing ignorance serve a truth he cannot define, and asks whether Klosterman, probing the gap between Bono's rehearsed car-ride persona and his inner self, is master of irony or mastered by it. The answer places Chuck midway between the two jailed ironists, Socrates and the Seinfeld finale: like Socrates he knows his own ignorance and serves the undefined idea of self-understanding, but only through pop-culture resemblance (KISS where Jerry used Superman), unable to master irony any more than he can bite his own teeth.

authenticity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
authenticity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Vannatta starts from Klosterman's confession that his first dates run on three and a half dates' worth of contrived material, and asks how self-knowledge is possible at all if, as Errol Morris tells Klosterman, we have no privileged access to our own minds. After a tour through Descartes's cogito, Kant's unity of apperception, Freud's unconscious, and Foucault's discourse-constructed subject, the chapter argues with Foucault's Ramist logic of similarity that Klosterman's thought really works by resemblance, mapping his exes onto members of KISS and hearing a dead friend in every Replacements song. Heidegger supplies the resolution: thrown into the crowd's world, we recover ourselves only through its inauthentic pop culture, and Klosterman's 'living is dying, little by little' and obsessive rock-death writing enact being-toward-death as the condition of authenticity.

authenticity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
authenticity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Flanders reads Killing Yourself to Live as asking whether dying can be good for the person who dies: Jeff Buckley's 'Hallelujah' and Kurt Cobain's myth became deeper and more successful only after the fact, as if death were a career move. He answers with Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where the fortunes of descendants can affect the happiness of the dead: our life-stories outlive their authors, so fans' posthumous devotion can really benefit Buckley, though no posthumous fame can add virtue that was never lived (Michael Jackson's rehabilitation cannot touch how he actually lived). Klosterman's road trip ultimately undercuts the question: the earnest Great White concert mourners remember what truly was there, while Cobain's fans retroactively invent meaning to gain 'credibility by mourning retrospectively', so worshipping the rock dead manufactures an inauthentic afterlife, and Klosterman must kill the unserious fan in himself to live.

authenticity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
authenticity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Brittingham reads Klosterman's celebrity interviews through Kierkegaard's The Sickness unto Death, taking the self as a synthesis of the immediate and the symbolic, finite and infinite. Britney Spears, who claims never to have thought about the sexual iconography behind her curtain, embodies the despair of ignorance in not knowing one has a self; Bono, embarrassed by his messianic 1980s posturing and wishing to shed that iconic self while remaining 'self-conscious about being self-conscious', embodies despair at not willing to be oneself; Metallica's Some Kind of Monster breakdown, with rehab, a hired therapist, and Kirk Hammett dreading having to take out the trash, embodies defiant despair, the 'king without a country' who would be absolute master of himself. Jeff Tweedy's uncool acceptance of both his suburban dad-life and his silly symbolic persona, plus Kierkegaard's remedy of resting transparently in the power that established us, mark the only way to be 'for real' rather than full of shit.

authenticity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
authenticity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Klosterman's own epilogue responds to being philosophized about: he understands the book exists because he is 'famous enough' to sell philosophy to readers who do not buy philosophy, and that its favorite source, Sex, Drugs, and Cocoa Puffs, is his least logical book — which is exactly why it sold. He diagnoses his central tension (entertaining writing about unsolvable ideas, consumed by audiences who want only one half), admits via the Lennon 'the pseuds will love it' anecdote that he is an unreliable narrator writing willfully misleading art, and disclaims any intent to persuade anyone of anything. A footnote concedes the chapter on McLuhan that he absorbed McLuhan's ideas 'by accident,' while disputing that the problem of authenticity has been solved — the through-line of his claim that all fifteen hundred pages of his work are about the difference between the 'real' and 'reality.'

authenticity.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
authenticity.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Wayne Yuen uses The Graveyard Book to teach the good life: Bod's family's murder, like students owing their existence to the Holocaust, is an unalloyed moral evil that still enables a better life, and Saul Smilansky's distinction between being 'sorry for' and 'sorry that' lets Bod benefit without endorsing the tragedy. His graveyard education is Aristotelian, virtues acquired through practice and models, from the Owenses' duty and Silas's wisdom to 'righteous indignation' against school bullies and friendship with Scarlett as intrinsically valuable, all building toward eudaimonia. The existentialist virtue of authenticity (attributed to Sartre and Kierkegaard) explains why Bod must be 'nobody but himself' rather than a copy of the vampire Silas, why the scavenged identities of the ghouls mark inauthenticity, and why wiping Scarlett's memory threatens her authenticity, resolving the apparent conflict between virtue and being oneself because bravery or wisdom is relative to the individual.

authenticity.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
authenticity.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Robert Tally Jr. reads The Graveyard Book as 'spectral existentialism': Bod's climax, 'I'm Nobody Owens. That's who I am,' is Sartre's existence precedes essence made literal, a self made rather than found, and the climactic claiming of the name enacts the self-ownership of the nursery-rhyme pauper 'who nobody owns.' Heidegger supplies the uncanny not-at-home-ness (unheimlich) of the graveyard, which Tally, citing Foucault's 'Of Other Spaces,' calls a heterotopia, while Silas the vampire embodies Lukacs's transcendental homelessness and Kierkegaardian anxiety is transmuted by Bod into the spectral gift of Fear he wields on his bullies. The identity-leeching ghouls named after the Duke of Westminster and the 33rd President are the avatars of bad faith, and the Jacks' attempt to dodge the prophecy fulfills it like Oedipus's, showing that Bod's fate, too, is self-made.

authenticity.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
authenticity.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Argues Heisenberg is not an alter ego but Walt finally escaping the Prufrock-like bad faith of his pre-cancer life: the pork-pie-hat persona acknowledges the absurd, owns his freedom and responsibility, and so achieves the authenticity Camus and Sartre demand. Walt becomes Camus's Sisyphus - rebelling against death, social norms, and Skyler, owning his rock with silent joy - citing the fulminated-mercury showdown with Tuco in 'Crazy Handful of Nothin'', running down Gus's dealers in 'Half Measures', and confessing to Skyler in 'No Mas'. The chapter closes that, like Sisyphus, we must imagine Walt happy.

authenticity.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
authenticity.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Uses Heidegger to read the show's very structure: the pilot's in-medias-res Winnebago crash throws us into Walt's timeline the way Dasein is thrown into time, and the flashbacks to Sandia Labs and 'nowhere to go but up' show his has-been shaping his futurity. Walt's diagnosis makes being-toward-death an overwhelming presence and exposes the failure of his calculative, goal-setting thinking, with the 'Fly' monologue about the perfect moment to die as his turn toward Heidegger's meditative thinking. By dwelling on his own death, the chapter argues, Walt inches toward an authentic being-toward-death - living each moment as if it were his last.

authenticity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
authenticity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Kempner reads The Walking Dead through Sartre's 'Existentialism Is a Humanism': with God and the old value-system gone, survivors who cling to pre-made essence die — Hershel keeps his zombified son locked in the barn awaiting restoration, and Shane tries to steal Rick's old cop-and-husband identity rather than live his own existence. Rick's waking in the hospital is a rebirth: he first exists in the new world, then creates a way of being human, and his relapses into the sheriff uniform nearly get him killed. Carl shooting Shane to save his father completes the family's existential freedom (children are no longer 'innocent'), walkers — without will or choice — are the ultimate inauthentic beings, and the volume's tagline, 'forced to finally start living,' makes the zombie world a sternly optimistic humanist story.

authenticity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
authenticity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Round argues the real horror of The Walking Dead is humanity itself, read through existentialism: walkers cannot choose, so the humans who attack, torture, and steal from each other are the true 'zombie Other.' She traces Rick's self-made, revisable moral code — from law-enforcer to 'You kill? You die' to killing Dexter — as authentic situation-based morality, paralleled with Kierkegaard's Abraham and with Abraham Ford's confession 'I did what I wanted to do' set against Eugene's bad-faith 'I did what I had to do.' Suicides like Jim, Jacqui, and Carol embody existential angst before an absurd world, the Governor's Woodbury is an Adorno-style inauthentic hierarchy that manipulates its people, and Rick's 'WE ARE THE WALKING DEAD!' speech uses facticity to insist the group admit what they have already become.

authenticity.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
authenticity.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Zanelotti takes up the charge that Larry is a self-hating Jew, from whistling Wagner to 'The End,' where learning he is a gentile turns him into a churchgoing enthusiast who sings 'Go Tell It on the Mountain' and gives Richard Lewis his kidney. Sartre's bad faith diagnoses both poles: Larry denying his facticity by imagining he can simply shed his Jewish past and re-adopt it at will, and critics who demand he live up to an 'authentic' Jewish essence; Marx's false consciousness, meanwhile, explains the self-hating baldy who buys into the haired agenda. Using Ronald de Sousa's rejection of the 'Just Joking Defense'—we are accountable for laughter because we let ourselves become people who cannot restrain it—the chapter argues the show sets a comic frame that mocks bad faith rather than Judaism. Its deeper target, via Nietzsche's death of God, is the overenthusiastic meaning we manufacture when faith is 'curbed,' which is why Larry ridicules only public displays of religion, not belief itself.

authenticity.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
authenticity.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Reads Larry as a textbook existentialist: his agonizing over trivia ('Doctor?... Pharmacist?') instantiates Heideggerian anxiety and Sartrean anguish, because every choice, even yanking his 5 wood out of a casket in 'The 5 Wood,' proclaims an image of how everyone ought to live. Since existence precedes essence there is no fixed human nature for Larry to appeal to; he must author his values alone, which the chapter says also makes him an optimist ('I'm not an inventor, but I'm an improver'). Larry dispels others' bad faith when he tells Susie she obviously can share the brownie recipe in 'The Benadryl Brownie,' and his baldness crusade, firing the toupee-wearing chef Phil Dunlap in 'The Grand Opening,' is a demand for authenticity about one's facticity. The 'Larry David Stare' is analyzed through Sartre's Look: the squinter tries to inspect another consciousness empirically and necessarily fails, since the other's freedom can never be objectified.

authenticity.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
authenticity.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Grants that Larry looks like the Romantic ideal of the authentic self, Rousseau's amour de soi turned into candid self-expression, but argues his authenticity collapses into egoism: petty commandments about chicken skewers and beach jackets, one-strike firings like the toupee-wearing chef, and ceaseless sincerity tests. Through Sartre's categories Larry is bad faith in both directions, the 'cowardly bastard': he denies transcendence ('I can't help it') and hides behind fabricated personas, faking concern over a sick dog and exaggerating his Jewishness to the kidney consortium. Charles Taylor's The Ethics of Authenticity supplies the verdict that self-creation needs 'pre-existing horizons of significance,' so Larry's 'anything goes' authenticity is really moral relativism and justified self-interest, with Ayn Rand's virtue of selfishness as its unwanted philosophical ally. The chapter closes that only a relational authenticity, like the African ideal of ubuntu, could redeem Larry, and he lacks it, so 'maybe authenticity isn't for everyone.'

authenticity.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
authenticity.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Shaun May uses Heidegger's being-in-the-world to mark off the human: Caesar correcting Charles's fork grip shows a grasp of the unspoken norms governing equipment, and the apes of the 1968 film, surgeons with scalpels and years of training, inhabit the same world of projects, skills, and tools that Heidegger says other animals lack. Language seals the difference: Taylor's syntax, Zaius's carefully ordered 'The Almighty created the ape in his own image,' and socially learned practices like pointing and map-reading stand against Nim Chimpsky's syntax-free signing and chimps' failure to understand pointing. Caesar's foresight in stealing the ALZ-113 before leading the escape extends this to Heideggerian temporality, and the ape uprising becomes a move toward authenticity, lives owned as a meaningful narrative whole.

authenticity.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
authenticity.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: The editors introduce the book by contrasting The Good Wife with earlier law shows like Law and Order: for the first time we see lawyers at home, and the central figure is Alicia Florrick, juggling teenagers, a firm in bankruptcy, and a marriage wrecked by Peter's prostitution scandal while keeping up appearances as the 'good wife' and taking lover Will Gardner. They argue the show refuses a single right answer - her choices are selfish, cowardly, vengeful, or simply her being true to herself - and that her growth as a woman, mother, and lawyer challenges preconceived social norms about women and about lawyers. Philosophy enters as the natural sequel: ethics, justice, feminism, privacy rights, epistemology, and social-political philosophy are all sewn into the episodes.

authenticity.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
authenticity.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: The chapter diagnoses the show's identity crises through Heidegger's Being and Time: Marshall's Goliath National Bank drudgery is anxiety over thrownness - the rent, the bills, the situation he never chose - while Lily's prom-night bolt to San Francisco is anxiety over freedom and possibility, and both fail anticipatory resoluteness, the commitment to be yourself while shouldering what you did not choose. das Man ('everybody's doing it') explains the gang's absorbed everydayness. Kierkegaard supplies the problem of time (life understood backwards but lived forwards) and Fear and Trembling's contrast between Abraham's leap of faith into the absurd and the 'demonic': Barney courts legendary moments yet manipulates uncertainty so he never becomes anyone new - the identity crisis that never ends.

authenticity.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
authenticity.title: The Devil and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Nick Jones asks whether worshipping the Devil and doing evil can ever be good, and answers: artistically yes. Using the transgression that defines extreme metal - blasphemy, church burnings, and Varg Vikernes's murder of Euronymous - he argues Satanic metal's immoral features can enhance its artistic value when they achieve three aims: rebellion, blasphemy, and authenticity. Genuine theistic Satanists who really believe in the Devil they invoke do all three best, though the chapter ends by conceding the cupboard of actual theistic Satanist metalheads is empty.

authenticity.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
authenticity.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Christopher Ketcham narrates a night listening to Dear Heather during a café blackout, in which darkness becomes Eugene Minkowski's 'lived space' - more personal than light, with auditory space as its own dark space - and Cohen's voice leads him down into a shared funk of loss and depression. Through Heidegger he diagnoses his own shrunken, past-bound, thrown existence and reinterprets being-toward-death not as a downward spiral but as being toward his own remaining possibilities, and through Freud's death drive he names the 'unobtrusive death wish' he had let dwell unchallenged in him. The essay closes with a Heideggerian resolve toward resoluteness and future possibility, glimpsing a street-worn 'Suzanne' in the dark as hope rather than absence.

authenticity.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
authenticity.title: Girls and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Archibald reads Jessa as Girls' quintessential existentialist: her unbothered abortion ('I'm offended by all the supposed to's'), her 'I am a junkie' honesty, and her refusal to blame her rough past (Sartrean facticity) enact existence precedes essence and Camus's embrace of the absurd. Kierkegaard's 'the crowd is untruth' and 'leveling' explain her contempt for rehab group conformity, while her panic marriage to Thomas-John after Katherine's motherly intervention is diagnosed as bad faith and angst. Her assisting the dying Beadie's suicide attempt - and calling 911 when Beadie recants - becomes the chapter's closing confrontation with Camus's one serious philosophical question, answered by living 'without appeal.'

authenticity.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
authenticity.title: Girls and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Addis uses Heidegger to explain why Hannah cannot 'rewrite her world': her enframing habit treats everything and everyone (Laird, Marnie, Adam) only in terms of feeding her 'writer' identity, so her world stays tiny even in vast New York. Heideggerian world, thrownness (Jessa's surprise wedding Shoshanna attends in white, Charlie's departure), and the power of art to de-enframe structure contrasts with Marnie, whose singing - prompted by Ray's question - expands her horizons. Hannah's crying-at-her-desk realization at the ad agency is read as her one genuine acceptance of thrownness, though her enframed self-absorption pulls her back.

authenticity.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
authenticity.title: Girls and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Crossley reads the millennials of Girls through Sartre's anguish: Hannah, cut off financially in the pilot, is 'condemned to be free' in a recession that owes her nothing, and Marnie's firing from the gallery ('I don't know what I want... I wish someone would tell me') confronts her with facticity and the terror of self-determination. Marnie's flight into wishing for a moral dictator and her later choice to sing map the bad faith/authenticity distinction, as does Hannah swapping her hoarder-story reading for a pretentious piece on death to please Ray. Even Jessa's total rejection of the 'supposed to's' is outed as its own bad faith, and the ad-agency arc shows twenty-first-century authenticity is inevitably compromised by the need to eat.

authenticity.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
authenticity.title: Girls and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Van Loon explains the q-tip scene ('On All Fours') as Kierkegaardian anxiety made flesh: freed by her parents and facing the e-book deadline, Hannah confronts the infinity of possibilities and, like Sartre's vertigo over the cliff, shoves the q-tip into her ear - embracing all possibilities at once and relapsing into bad faith by becoming a victim of fate. Each girl handles freedom differently: Shoshanna remains in an innocence prior to freedom, Jessa jokes her way out of seriousness, Marnie denies her anxiety. Against these, the Season Two FaceTime call to Adam models Kierkegaard's leap of faith and the 'knight of faith' - surrendering, making oneself vulnerable, and accepting that anxiety will return.

authenticity.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
authenticity.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Pardi argues Jobs lived philosophically as an existentialist: the 'Steve Jobs Roll Your Own Calculator Construction Set' anecdote shows design by touch and intuition rather than master plans, every detail of a product mattered because it belongs to a life narrative of 'making a ding in the universe,' and he avoided both Kierkegaard's despair (the gap between actual and possible self) and Sartrean bad faith—quoted from Being and Nothingness—by never lying to himself about his products, calling faulty work 'shit' and redoing it. Against him stands Bill Gates the pragmatist, whose utilitarian Windows-for-every-desk business and 'rationality only goes so far' humility embody William James's pragmatic method, while Jobs's Zune taunt ('we made the iPod for ourselves') shows the existentialist refusing to compromise authenticity for market share.

authenticity.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
authenticity.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Charlotte Knowles tests each Gang member against Heidegger's Being and Time: getting lost in the averageness of what 'they' do (das Man) is inauthenticity, but authenticity is not freakish uniqueness - Charlie's milk-steak, magnets, and bird-law delusions are unconventional without being authentic - rather a transformed relation to everyday roles in which one endorses the life one leads. Frank partly passes, having chosen squalor and owning it ('I'm going to get really weird with it'), yet unknowingly lives out Rambo as a cultural script; Dee consciously performs the Sex and the City script; Dennis is ruled by beauty norms (make-up, girdle, chemical peel); and Mac, despite the tough talk, is Frank's 'follower' hiding his relationship with Carmen. The upshot is that authenticity and inauthenticity are matters of degree, never either/or, and are not moral verdicts - Dennis could be an authentic rapist - so the Gang's norm-defiance does not make them authentic, bitches.

authenticity.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
authenticity.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Hoyt argues the show's core lesson is dropping the little lies we tell ourselves: Bennett calls his crush on Daya 'love' to excuse framing Mendez, Pornstache is a man performing a blustering guard (Sartrean bad faith), and Larry and Polly's 'love just happened' dodges responsibility for betrayal. Piper's arc (the Colt 45 scene in '40 Oz. of Furlough') shows the payoff of authenticity, while Healy's Safe Place is a fantasy that cannot will a change of worldview. Using Wittgenstein's aspect-seeing from Philosophical Investigations, he shows how characters and viewers miss ethically significant meanings, like Taystee's shower 'compliment' as intimidation and Piper's convenient blindness to Soso's humanity when selling her for a blanket.

authenticity.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
authenticity.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Neal reads Litchfield through Sartre's No Exit: Alex, the ex who both agonizes and galvanizes Piper, makes the other inmates, not the walls, the hell of prison, just as Piper shouts 'I love you and I fucking hate you.' The 'Scared Straight' episode ('Bora Bora Bora') drives the deeper point when Piper tells Dina that the real punishment is coming face to face with who you are: 'I'm scared that I'm not myself in here and I'm scared that I am.' Stripped of distractions, Piper undergoes an existential crisis that forces the self-awareness authenticity requires, though prison's limits keep a fully authentic life out of reach.

authenticity.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
authenticity.title: 11. Louis C.K.’s No-Bullshit Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Marie Snyder uses Sartre's existentialism to unpack Louis's Conan monologue about the 'forever empty': with God gone we are condemned to be free, thrown into a world with no ready-made purpose and alone with our choices - which explains both the cellphone distraction economy and the Live in Portland bit that 'even if you're with someone, you're alone.' Authenticity means ruthlessly honest self-awareness and owning every choice with no excuses - Sartre's waiter example, the claim that there is no cowardly temperament, and Louis's refusal to let 'a flaw in the human male' excuse the tits bit or porn masturbation. Since in choosing for ourselves we choose for all humanity, Snyder pairs Sartre's universalized responsibility with Louis's 'act in a way that, if everybody acted that way, things would work out,' and reads intimate others, as in the Sartre-Beauvoir open relationship, as mirrors that reflect us back to ourselves against the connectionless 'we're just cummers' porn culture. Bad faith - self-deception, distraction, blame - is the fallenness Louis keeps diagnosing in his audiences and confessing in himself.

authenticity.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
authenticity.title: 12. Confronting the “Forever Empty”
authenticity.relation: Argues that Louis's 2013 Conan 'forever empty' confession—welcoming the sadness of listening to Bruce Springsteen alone in his car instead of texting—is an exemplary case of existentialist authenticity: Heideggerian anxiety discloses the nothingness beneath our projects, and Sartre's radical freedom, facticity, and bad faith explain why texting while driving and other distractions are escapes from self-creation. It then contrasts Eddie in Louie's 'Eddie' episode, whose suicide plan is a bad-faith loss of care and passion, with the 'Late Show' trilogy, where Janet exposes Louie's bad faith over the Letterman audition and he ends by shouting 'I did it!' at the Ed Sullivan Theater after Tardigan's scam.

authenticity.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
authenticity.title: 5. The Human Being in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction
authenticity.relation: Extends Walter Benjamin's analysis of art under mechanical reproduction to human cloning: as photography and film stripped artworks of their "aura" (their unique link to an origin) while democratizing art, cloning strips human beings of Hannah Arendt's "natality" — our connection to a unique beginning — while democratizing human nature itself. The chapter argues this is liberation, not loss: Sarah is as human as Felix or Kira, denying the clones' humanity would strip the naturally born of their own freedom ("Either Sarah and her sisters are human, or no one is"), and Tony Sawicki's chosen trans identity shows that once natality stops being destiny, authenticity and autonomy become possible for the first time. The only truly immoral path is Leda and Castor's — treating the bioengineered as property, as Rachel was raised to treat herself.

authenticity.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
authenticity.title: A Farewell to David Bowie
authenticity.relation: The editor's farewell argues that Bowie's greatness lay in relentless transformation joined to honesty: unlike acts from Kiss to Miley Cyrus whose theatrics are mere spectacle 'in an Aristotelian sense,' Bowie's characters (Ziggy, the Thin White Duke, simulating fellatio with Mick Ronson) opened a discussion of gender and 'the multiple ways of being in the world.' Tracing the career from parents' fear of rock through the Eno-shaped Berlin trilogy's symbolist minimalism and the despised continuity of 'Changes,' it reads The Next Day as a defacement of 'Heroes' and Blackstar as a Mapplethorpe-like series of self-portraits made while unflinchingly facing death.

authenticity.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
authenticity.title: 1. The Actor Tells the Truth
authenticity.relation: Reisch argues Bowie's parade of characters (Ziggy, Aladdin Sane, the Diamond Dogs persona) was never metaphysical chameleonry but a postwar, cold-war project: by crediting himself only as 'the actor' and calling Dylan out as Robert Zimmerman's artifice, Bowie exposed the 'denim and hippies' authenticity cult as itself a construction. Diamond Dogs' '1984' and 'Big Brother' tie this to the era's totalitarian nightmares of manipulable humanity, and Sartre's 'Man is nothing else but that which he makes of himself' becomes 'the first principle of Bowie' - only constant reinvention keeps us from being fooled by ourselves or others, even at the anguished cost of 'Who Can I Be Now?'

authenticity.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
authenticity.title: 9. When Jumpin’ Jack Flash Met Ziggy Stardust
authenticity.relation: Auxier reads the 1973 Jagger-Bowie intimacy and rivalry ethically: Keith Richards's portrait of Mick's envy frames Kierkegaard's Either/Or warning against the aesthetic life and the Kantian morality-duty wedding Bowie fled, against Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity, which demands that one own one's freely chosen hollowing-out without appeal to any authority. Beauvoir's bad faith and authenticity then explain the outcome - Bowie beat Jagger by killing Ziggy, firing the Spiders, and finally making his very death a persona ('authentically Bowie'), while Jagger, forever only the Stones' singer, can respond only in bad faith, because 'hell is other people': each glimpsed the faker in the other.

authenticity.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
authenticity.title: 12. David Bowie’s Sincerity
authenticity.relation: Cooper distinguishes sincerity - communicating a self to an audience - from authenticity, and uses Critchley's reading of Bowie's visible seams ('maybe we're lying,' 'saying no but meaning yes') to argue that openly displayed artifice can carry real feeling, even as 'Conversation Piece' and the suffocating mask of 'The Mask' dramatize language's failure to transmit a self. Descartes's cogito secures self-certainty but not communication - Bowie stays 'a thinker, not a talker' - and against the Nietzschean 'Supermen' whose self-creation shades into self-alienation, Bowie moves past cold postmodern irony to a new sincerity that admits its own insincerity ('It's not the side-effects of the cocaine... I'm thinking that it must be love!').

authenticity.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
authenticity.title: 5. Guilty of Being a Dwarf
authenticity.relation: Engels runs Tyrion's arc through Sartre's existentialism: his facticity as a dwarf makes everyone from Catelyn to Tywin presume his guilt, while 'Never forget what you are, wear it like armor' states the Sartrean authenticity of owning facticity while freely choosing one's essence. Catelyn's dagger accusation, the comic confession at the Eyrie, the wildfire ship at Blackwater, and the trial outburst ('I am guilty of a far more monstrous crime: the crime of being a dwarf') show him choosing rather than being defined; the murders of Shae and Tywin dramatize the slide into bad faith - embracing the 'monster' essence others assigned - before his choice to join Daenerys resumes the burden of self-creation.

authenticity.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
authenticity.title: 2. 3eanuts and the Existential Schulz
authenticity.relation: The chapter introduces existentialism and reads Peanuts through it: Charlie Brown's defeats expose the 'groundlessness' of value, and the 3eanuts web project (deleting each strip's final gag panel) restores the despair that punchlines normally defuse. It explains Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' and the ideal of authenticity versus passively inhabiting roles, Heidegger's care and Dasein (even in despair there is an inner place where it happens), and Camus's absurd and Sisyphus revolting against a fate he cannot change. Lucy's hillside sermon ('WELL, LIVE IN IT, THEN!') and the final image of Charlie running at the football figure his revolt: he keeps kicking because in that moment a world without boxes exists in him.

authenticity.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
authenticity.title: 16. European Intellectuals Follow Charlie Brown!
authenticity.relation: The chapter traces how European intellectuals legitimized Peanuts: Eco read the strip as mass culture whose repeated patterns expose a microcosm of the human condition (children warped by industrial civilization, Lucy as contemporary values incarnate), while Bassano di Tufillo finds 'sociable individualism' and, via Bateson and aboriginal spirituality, an ecological vision granting animals, trees, and school buildings equal dignity. It then applies Heidegger's distinction between calculative and reflective thinking to management: Lucy's rigid direction of the Christmas play ('You've got to have respect for your director!') is calculative leadership that treats people as resources, while Charlie Brown's refusal of the All-Stars sponsor - which would have expelled girls and Snoopy - models the authentic, reflective organization that values dignity and diversity over results.

authenticity.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
authenticity.title: 8. Mr. Robot, Mad Son of Noir
authenticity.relation: Hoyt places Mr. Robot in the film noir tradition born when world war proved Nietzsche's point that God is dead: as with Bogart's Spade turning in Brigid in The Maltese Falcon, the noir hero's task is existential self-definition - guarding integrity in a world without truth, justice, or absolute meaning. But where classic noir blamed gangsters, neo-noir from Chinatown through Fight Club to Mr. Robot points at capitalism and unbeatable conspiracies (Price apparently able to bend the federal government itself), and the show's cold blue offices and 'shortsighting' framings show characters breaking under the pressure of choices no space protects.

authenticity.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
authenticity.title: 3. Mermen and Dismemberment
authenticity.relation: Contends that Hendrix's discord is philosophy-as-discord: 'I Don't Live Today' (the Native American dead-in-life), the Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' with its bombs and sirens against sporting-event sentimentality, 'Machine Gun,' and 'House Burning Down' lacerate listeners so they actually feel war's atrocities instead of parroting patriotic clichés. Against this the chapter sets the oceanic, womb-like escape fantasies of '1983 (A Merman I Should Turn to Be)' and 'Valleys of Neptune,' treating them through Schopenhauer as metaphysical consolation, Marx's opiate, and Nietzsche's 'hangman's metaphysics,' and concludes that Hendrix finally refuses such world-denying illusions — and Heideggerian inauthentic withdrawal — in favor of existential engagement with suffering here and now.

authenticity.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
authenticity.title: 6. Quicker than the Wink of an Eye
authenticity.relation: Defends Hendrix against the Allan Bloom-style charge that sixties self-expression was mere decadence by reading his life as Charles Taylor's ideal of authenticity: self-determining freedom replacing the older external goods of Plato's Good, Aristotle's polis, or Aquinas's God. The biography — the broken home behind 'Castles Made of Sand,' the rolling-stone mobility Dylan anthemed, the London synthesis of blues, rock, soul, and jazz, 'Watchtower''s 'let us not talk falsely now,' and the accusations of race desertion answered by the Watts commitment and 'House Burning Down' — becomes the development of an authentic voice, closing with Cornel West's 'tragi-comic poet' and the humanist manifesto of 'Bold as Love.'

authenticity.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
authenticity.title: 7. A Life Along the Watchtower
authenticity.relation: Reads 'All Along the Watchtower' as a dialogue between the Joker's Sartrean being-and-nothingness ('none of them along the line know what any of it is worth') and the Thief's Heideggerian reply — being-toward-death, anticipatory resoluteness, care, and the fallen 'they.' It argues Hendrix lived this struggle: the mirror-smashing of 'A Room Full of Mirrors,' the unborn speaker of 'Belly Button Window' who will throw himself into the world rather than be thrown, and the 'Electric Church Music' built to cut through 'they'-thinking and return listeners to child-like authenticity. Gramsci's point that oppressor and oppressed alike internalize the oppressor's message names the hegemony Hendrix's third way — neither victim nor revolutionary — simply denies.

authenticity.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
authenticity.title: 8. Facing Up to the Realities
authenticity.relation: Argues that 'Machine Gun' and its Berkeley introduction ('people... fighting wars... within themselves, not facing up to the realities') make Hendrix an existentialist: since existence precedes essence, each of us lives multiple realities we must author responsibly.
