The lyric variants diagnose Sartrean bad faith twice over — 'evil man make me kill ya' is the helplessness that denies freedom, 'fight like a farmer' the blame that locates failure out there — before the reprise's acceptance ('let your bullets fly like rain') and free judgment ('I know all the time you're wrong') achieve authenticity amid the solo's sonic battlefield.

authenticity.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
authenticity.title: 13. Did Jimi Play Rock
authenticity.relation: Flips Joel Rudinow's 'Can White People Sing the Blues?' to ask whether a very black musician can play a genre that by the late sixties had become white property. With Wittgenstein's family resemblance — musical kinds lack necessary and sufficient conditions — it traces rock's migration from Chuck Berry and the Sanctified churches to the Stones and Beatles, diagnosing the 'Jimi problem': his blackness rendered his rock inauthentic (Christgau's 'psychedelic Uncle Tom,' radio bans) at the same time as his rock rendered him inauthentically black. The chapter endorses Hendrix's own refusal of labels — 'You don't need labels, man' — as a caution against unreflective categorization.

authenticity.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
authenticity.title: 16. Doppelgängers, Doubles, and Tulpas
authenticity.relation: Reads the show's doubles through the danger of self-loss. La Rochefoucauld's amour-propre explains Josie Packard, whose courtier-like dissimulation ("she could survive by being what other people wanted to see") erodes her true self, while Norma refuses to feign virtue for critic M.T. Wentz or Walter Lawford's rebranding; Rousseau's account of esteem-seeking in modern society covers Sheriff Cable and Chad, who value Teresa Banks and the Log Lady only by others' judgment, against the Blue Rose agents whose values come from within. Jean Paul's doppelgänger, invented to satirize Fichte's I/not-I and intersubjective recognition, uncannies the Palmer home (Leland the abusing father), but the chapter concludes the show sides with Dostoyevsky rather than Jean Paul: Laura, like Mitya Karamazov, owns both her good and wicked halves, Leland splits, and Cooper's moral goodness is a wholeness — authenticity — that his doppelgänger lacks.

authenticity.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
authenticity.title: 5. The Funny Thing about Being Yourself
authenticity.relation: Reads Schumer's comedy as Nietzschean self-creation: like the tightrope walker over the abyss she confronts who she is, says 'Yes' to life in the spirit of the eternal recurrence and amor fati, and 'gives style' to her character by wearing mistakes as badges of honor, notably reclaiming her paparazzi photos in the Leather Special. Balke then casts her as Rorty's ironist, whose continual burning of old material keeps her free of a 'final vocabulary' in a contingent world, with 'Amy Goes Deep' doing the Rortian work of testing herself against others. He closes with George Herbert Mead's account of a self formed through social interaction with significant others.

authenticity.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
authenticity.title: 13. No Place like a Non-Place
authenticity.relation: Pagnoni Berns, Juvé, and Aguilar apply Marc Augé's concepts of non-place and supermodernity to the show's empty roads, ocean liners, airplanes, hotel rooms, and shopping malls, reading them as geographies of the postwar identity crisis (women in the workforce, jobless veterans, the salesman husband) behind the American Dream. 'The Hitch-Hiker' and 'The Passersby' figure the dead who cannot accept death as travelers on anonymous roads; 'Nightmare at 20,000 Feet' makes Bob Wilson's real struggle the anonymity of the modern passenger rather than the gremlin; and 'The After Hours' and 'The Four of Us Are Dying' show intimacy and recognition intruding fatally into spaces built only for clients and strangers.

authenticity.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
authenticity.title: Keep a Little Soul
authenticity.relation: Section introduction to the ethics chapters, framed by Petty’s October 2017 death: it argues his real achievement was working to be timeless — the shelved 1982 outtake “Keep a Little Soul” sounding native in 2018 — and that he “lived what he believed,” chasing dreams despite guaranteed heartache, refusing to explain his songs, and standing up to record-company executives. It closes by describing Petty’s political thought as “a deontology that puts duty to the fans first,” invokes Nietzsche as appreciating the gesture of turning the volume up rather than snoozing through the Reagan years, and sketches the volume’s five philosophical “buds”: epistemology, aesthetics, ontology, and two ethics chapters on the outcast and heartbroken as redeemable antiheroes of the everyday.

authenticity.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
authenticity.title: 9. Wherever the Road Leads
authenticity.relation: Watkins takes the recurring road image ("Runnin' Down a Dream," "Kings Highway," "Learning to Fly") as a probe of whether the future is open. Against determinism and Aristotle-style fatalism she argues from lived experience: we cannot feel our choices as unfree, and even a determined world would remain unpredictable, so Petty's open road wins. His optimism in "It'll All Work Out" needs no faith in a good outcome, only the passing of time under our feet, and persistence then becomes an Aristotelian virtue required for eudaimonia, a duty owed to the kind of beings we are, and Sartrean authenticity in which Petty made himself through his project of rock'n'roll.

authenticity.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
authenticity.title: 10. Change of Heart
authenticity.relation: Auxier names Petty the master of "liminal moments" when something is finally seen for what it is (the betrayed lover's realization behind "You Got Lucky," the unknown pain of "American Girl"), then stages the 1929 Davos debate between Cassirer's humane, Goethe-reading phenomenology and Heidegger's Angst before the abyss, being-toward-death, and the "moment of vision." He indicts Heidegger's Nazism and betrayal of Husserl as what "Petty-ness," the asshole-beast crouching in everyone's darkdeepdown, becomes when it wins, contrasting Petty's public apology for the Confederate flag and his cease-and-desist to George W. Bush. The chapter ends with the unguarded Petty smile as "Here Comes My Girl" made philosophy, an instance of authentic being-with-others that Heidegger declared impossible.

authenticity.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
authenticity.title: 19. The Citadel of Ricks Is Untruth
authenticity.relation: The chapter reads Rick C-137's war on the Citadel through Kierkegaard's claim that the crowd is untruth: the Council of Ricks is the leveling public, envying and punishing the passionate individual ('You're a rogue Rick, irrational, passionate'), as Rick J-22's breakdown over Simple Rick's wafers in 'The Ricklantis Mixup' dramatizes, while our Rick stays himself by refusing consensus. From Philosophical Fragments, via Socrates's maieutic midwifery, it draws Kierkegaard's ethics of selfhood: one person can only be the occasion for another's self-knowledge and must then push them away to become individuals. That is exactly Rick's advice to Beth in 'The ABCs of Beth', to leave Jerry, saddle her universe, and become herself, since only Beth can make Beth.

authenticity.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
authenticity.title: How to Make Something Strange Even Stranger
authenticity.relation: Andrew Winters's introduction argues the show appeals both to those who lived the Eighties and those who wish they had: plastic, story-rich 1980s childhoods (D&D, bikes, walkie-talkies) versus a present of single-bit tweets, likes, and Instagram-filtered self-display where we look to others for confirmation instead of creating worlds together. It then previews the volume's essays on horror's appeal, whether monsters like Dart are all evil, friendship and civil disobedience, the Shadow Monster within ourselves, Will's possession and identity, nostalgia and forgetting, and Eleven's faith and heroism as a guide to meaningful living, closing with Hopper's 'Mornings are for coffee and contemplation.'

authenticity.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
authenticity.title: 5. Another Day in the Neighborhood
authenticity.relation: Sydney Ball and Eric Mohr interleave a college student's Tuesday with her six-year-old self watching the show: Plato's Republic (439c) on the rational part overruling the appetitive frames procrastination and lost youthful energy, Kant's autonomy frames doing what you should without being told, and Heidegger's 'They' frames her supermarket jealousy, dissolved by complimenting a stranger's shoes just as Henrietta Pussycat overcame jealousy of Grandpere's fancy granddaughter Collette (episodes 1176-1180). The lesson, learned from Mister Rogers's words about stopping, is authenticity: 'I like you just the way you are.'

authenticity.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
authenticity.title: 16. Loved into Being
authenticity.relation: Scott Parker argues Fred Rogers converged on Carl Rogers's person-centered approach without ever studying it: genuineness ('The greatest gift you ever give is your honest self'), acceptance (unconditional positive regard: 'I like you just the way you are'), and empathic understanding (the nursery-school doggie-ear exchange) form the facilitative climate that lets children grow toward Kierkegaard's 'that self which one truly is.' With Margaret McFarland's 'attitudes aren't taught, they're caught' and her 'love clay in front of the children,' he shows Mister Rogers as the teacher who liked his viewers into being.

authenticity.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
authenticity.title: 18. Lessons from Fred Rogers’s Dao
authenticity.relation: John Thompson reads Rogers as a Zhuangzian sage without claiming he was a Daoist: the show's spare sets and simple cast embody the uncarved block and Zhuangzi's Dao present 'in the piss and shit' of the everyday; its refusal of 'bombardment' pace is Cook Ding slowly carving the ox and xiaoyaoyou, free and easy wandering, as when X the Owl must wait for Cousin Mary's visit. The post-9/11 'look for the helpers' PSAs, the Burger King parody he publicly rebuffed, and the Emmys ten seconds of silence mark Rogers as a zhenren, a genuine person at home in ziran.

authenticity.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
authenticity.title: 6. Looking for Realness
authenticity.relation: Gilpin and Nagy define Drag Race realness as an ongoing process of performative becoming read through Heidegger's Dasein: being-in-the-world and being-with others in the werkroom and Untucked, historicity in the childhood-photo rituals, Jinkx's 'Lunch with RuPaul' and the show's Stonewall and HERstory numbers, and freedom as authenticity, as when Monique Heart describes finding liberation only once she 'put on a wig and a dress'. They then filter this through Goffman's dramaturgy — self-expression versus self-presentation, impression management, and fronts of setting, appearance and manner — arguing that Drag Race collapses Goffman's front stage/backstage divide because backstage vulnerability is itself a required performance. Realness ultimately demands perceived emotional vulnerability plus commercially viable professionalism, and RuPaul alone validates which queens have achieved it.

authenticity.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
authenticity.title: 8. The Death of God and the Death of Meaning
authenticity.relation: Montoya reads Chidi's breakdown upon learning he has been tortured for three hundred years as Nietzsche's death of God, quoting the Parable of the Madman from 'Jeremy Bearimy' to show how the guaranteed meaning of Chidi's worldview collapses into nihilism. Michael's midlife-crisis makeover and partying embody Camus's embrace of the absurd, while Sartre's existence precedes essence, abandonment, and anguish explain why Eleanor's confession to Michael and her sacrifice in the Judge's test count as authentic choices. With the Judge's verdict stripping away any hope of reward, the humans finally choose goodness for its own sake, which the chapter presents as the show's answer to nihilism.

authenticity.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
authenticity.title: 16. Is Hell Other People
authenticity.relation: Berk compares the show to Sartre's No Exit, where Garcin, Inez, and Estelle are locked in a drawing room as each other's torturers, and notes that Michael's experiment 'in the spirit of Sartre' fails because the four humans befriend and improve each other instead. She then corrects the standard reading: Sartre himself insisted 'Hell is other people' is conditional on twisted, bad-faith relationships of over-dependence on others' judgment, as with Tahani's craving for her parents' approval, and the footnote in Being and Nothingness about a 'radical conversion' to authenticity leaves room for healthy relations. Read this way, the show's message that flawed people can find salvation through each other is compatible with, not a refutation of, Sartre.

authenticity.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
authenticity.title: 23. Like Boxing Gloves of Sadness
authenticity.relation: Benko argues the show's deepest target is selfishness understood as inauthenticity: an over-investment in a self whose real motivations, Tahani's name-dropping, Chidi's moral filibustering, Jason's Acidcat fiasco, Eleanor's aggressive solitude, are hidden from the person herself. Drawing on Charles Guignon's account of authenticity, he shows that being true to yourself is not enough unless your self-expression enables others to become their authentic selves too, which is why Chidi's keeping of his promises across all 802 reboots is the show's moral core and why treating people as mere means fails on Kantian grounds. Eleanor's final willingness to lose Chidi rather than her better self demonstrates authenticity reoriented toward others, the show's answer to Schur's fourth-car-at-the-left-turn driver.

authenticity.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
authenticity.title: 16. KISS Goes Disco and Boogies on Simmons’s Bad Faith
authenticity.relation: Christopher Innes defends 'I Was Made for Lovin' You' and KISS's disco turn on Dynasty against Gene Simmons's own scorn. Insisting that KISS is essentially and only hard rock treats the band's facticity as an in-itself, like Sartre's waiter who becomes nothing but his role — the bad faith of Simmons and rockist fans alike — whereas human transcendence and nothingness mean the band can authentically choose disco, grunge, or anything new, as Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love,' Pink Floyd, and Queen exemplify. The twist: bad faith is also a comfort, and the chapter ends by conceding that Simmons's hard-rock constancy may itself be an authentic filling of his own nothingness — so who is to say he is wrong?

authenticity.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
authenticity.title: Final Act
authenticity.relation: Shaw argues everyone at 30 Rock performs a role that shields them from Sartrean radical freedom: Kenneth is Sartre's cafe waiter in bad faith, believing television is America's true art form and willing to 'die at my post' for NBC, while Jack psyches himself up with corporate slogans and Jenna's 'Black Tie' candor about marrying the last Hapsburg to be taken care of is the rare moment of good faith. Butler's gender performativity explains Jack's masculinity as a repeated script, from his Glengarry Glen Ross 'always be talking' allusion to Baldwin's brass-balls speech to his homosocial man-crushes on Don Geiss and Dick Cheney. Plato's wariness of imitation, Nietzsche on hypocrisy hardening into character, and Santayana's tragic mask frame the closing thought: the actors know they are performing, but the characters, like us, do not.

authenticity.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
authenticity.title: Conclusions, Capes, and Cowls
authenticity.relation: Jason Howard asks how Batman keeps from becoming what he fights, answering with Heidegger's authentic conscience against Rousseau's innate moral-sense view. Bruce's guilt over his parents' death is reinterpreted in a Heideggerian 'moment of vision': the bat through the window summons Dasein out of the they-self, so becoming Batman is not vengeance but the call of an authentic conscience that owns guilt, fallenness, and death. Batman's return from alcoholic retirement in The Dark Knight Returns shows conscience as 'the loyalty of existence to its own Self,' a freedom-toward-death that makes him instructive rather than merely heroic.

authenticity.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
authenticity.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
authenticity.relation: David Hart uses Heidegger to dissolve the question of whether Batman is determined by childhood trauma or freely chooses his mission. Heidegger's being-in-the-world and thrown-project, illustrated by Alfred the butler for whom the clock is essentially something to dust, replace the subject-object picture that grounds both free-will and determinism talk. Read this way, the bat crashing through the window in Batman: Year One is Bruce's Angst-laden confrontation with death as 'the possibility of my own impossibility,' through which he freely takes up the project of being Batman when nothing forced him to.

authenticity.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
authenticity.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Jollimore and Jones diagnose three 'very unDude' vices: Walter's rule rigidity, which confuses Kant's hypothetical rules of games (don't cross the foul line) with categorical moral ones and needs 'rules all the way down' to ward off nihilism; the Big Lebowski's hypocritical inauthenticity, a fake achiever living on his daughter's allowance who collapses facedown before his own rug; and the exclusionism with which everyone shuts Donny out of the conversation. Against these the Dude exhibits Aristotelian virtue as good judgment (knowing when rules don't apply), the Golden Mean between Walter and the nihilists, and Singer-style inclusion — 'he's in bed with everybody' — making him an authentic man of humor and perspective.

authenticity.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
authenticity.title: Two Philosophies, Two Compasses to Navigate Life
authenticity.relation: Against 'Hang the DJ,' where Frank and Amy's coaching system assigns partners and expiration dates inside a simulated dating park, the chapter argues a Stoic would refuse to sign up: delegating judgments to the coach violates Epictetus's dichotomy of control, and the endless date-cycle fails all four virtues, treating dates (like Amy's bored lovemaking) as means rather than inherently worthy persons. An existentialist reading via Sartre says nearly every system-arranged relationship is bad faith - couples act as if compatible against the expiry they were given, as Frank and Nicola do - and only Frank and Amy's open-ended, freely chosen relationship escapes it, so their 'fuck off' to the system is a leap of faith that 998 of 1000 simulated couples make, which is how the app computes its 99.8% match. The authors close with Camus's absurd, doubting that the real Frank and Amy, who cannot rebel against an app that tells them they belong together, will fare as well as their simulations.

authenticity.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
authenticity.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Decker asks whether the 'Stephen Colbert' persona is the ironist of the Romantics and Rorty: the precise inverse of Socrates, who was declared wisest by the Delphic oracle precisely because he knew he knew nothing. Through Schlegel's Romantic irony, Hegel's complaint that the ironist abdicates responsibility, Kierkegaard's reading of Socrates as standing ironically above every relationship, and Rorty's ironist with her radically doubtable 'final vocabulary', he reads Colbert's self-redescription, Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear, and Super PAC stunt as exposing the contingency of political selves. Yet truthiness at its worst is dangerous subjectivism, and the chapter ends with Colbert breaking persona before Congress ('I like talking about people who have no power') as the non-ironic face that keeps the irony honest.

authenticity.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
authenticity.title: “Your Heart Knows”
authenticity.relation: Argues that Disney's Mulan transplants a distinctly modern Western ideal of the authentic self ('true to your heart,' 'Reflection') into a Confucian honor culture where the self is constituted by roles and relationships, filial piety (xiao), and ren as the virtue that binds people into larger wholes — which is why the film flopped in China. The matchmaker debacle, Fa Zhou's 'I will die doing what's right,' and the family's shame show a culture where dishonor stains the whole family and even luck (the cricket Cri-Kee) fixes moral standing, conflicting with Western assumptions about individual responsibility. The chapter ends by noting Mulan now resonates with young Chinese viewers, asking whether the Western individualist self is a truth about humanity or a cultural export that, like the Huns, has scaled the Great Wall.

authenticity.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
authenticity.title: “I Am Moana!”
authenticity.relation: Stages Moana's dilemma between her father's Aristotelian essentialism — everything on Motunui has a fixed function, so Moana's essence as chief precedes her birth — and Sartre's existence precedes essence, with Heihei the unchanging chicken as a being whose essence really does precede existence. Tui embodies bad faith and the crowd (his own aborted voyage left him enforcing 'no one goes beyond the reef'), while Tala and then Moana live authentically through anguish, forlornness, and despair, until 'I am Moana!' marks her self-defined identity. Nietzsche's 'become who you are' and 'what does not destroy me makes me stronger' frame her resilience, which lets her free Maui ('Hook. No hook. I'm Maui.') and unmask Te Ka as Te Fiti whose stolen heart 'does not define you.'

authenticity.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
authenticity.title: He’ll Be There For You, No Matter What
authenticity.relation: The chapter walks through the three Toy Story films as three conceptions of freedom: freedom as control (Andy's stable room versus Sid's despotism, and Woody's collapse when Buzz displaces him), freedom as faithful identity (Woody torn between the 'Andy' on his boot and the Roundup Gang's museum future), and freedom as self-giving (Woody's sacrifices in Sid's house and the escape from Sunnyside). Lotso embodies control curdled into tyranny after Daisy replaces him, ruling a 'no owners means no heartbreak' utopia that is really a dystopian lie, while Andy giving the toys to Bonnie shows that the freest act is choosing another's good over your own.

authenticity.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
authenticity.title: Death Gives Meaning to Life
authenticity.relation: Lee reads Strange's car crash as Heideggerian angst and the Call of conscience that ends his 'ontic' life of treating patients as reputation-building problems, forcing a choice between authenticity and a mask. Kaecilius and Dormammu embody the inauthentic flight from death (Kaecilius going 'beyond good and evil' Nietzsche-style), while the Ancient One's confession — drawing on the Dark Dimension only until Strange could replace her, then stretching one moment into a thousand to watch the snow — models accepting mortality. Dormammu's torment in Strange's time loop is compared to Camus's Sisyphus, supporting the thesis that without an ending life is endless repetition, so 'death gives meaning to life.'

authenticity.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
authenticity.title: 1. Finding the Meaning of Life in Downton Abbey
authenticity.relation: Blessing pits Steve Jobs's 'Do What You Love' creed (and Oprah's 'follow your bliss') against Downton's world of inherited roles, where nobody from Anna to Lady Mary chooses their work. She distinguishes happiness from meaningfulness, since Matthew's war wounds and Mary's grief over his death are painful yet deeply meaningful, and tests subjectivist theories such as Nietzsche's meaning-as-passionate-process against Nozick's demand that a meaningful life leave permanent traces and Susan Wolf's hybrid 'loving objects that are worthy of love.' Kant's duty to develop one's talents rather than idle for pleasure, and Lord Grantham's self-description as 'a custodian, not an owner,' anchor the show's counter-ethos of duty over desire, embodied in Carson, Mrs. Hughes, and Mrs. Patmore's pride in unloved, socially necessary work. The chapter concludes that Downton validates hard honest work as an end in itself, challenging the narcissism of the 'holy You' and expressive individualism.

authenticity.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
authenticity.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Christopher Wood reads Cloud's arc as an existentialist quest: Heidegger's thrownness in Cloud's tumble off the Midgar train and his initial 'It's not my problem' denial of being-in-the-world; Nietzsche's death of God in Mako-powered Midgar's nihilism, with AVALANCHE as a call for revaluation of values and Sephiroth as a false aspirant god; and Sartre's bad faith in Cloud 'playing at being a SOLDIER,' a persona borrowed wholesale from Zack along with his sword and mercenary dream. Through the Lifestream reunion with Tifa, Cloud faces his fabricated past, admits 'I never was in SOLDIER,' and turns to authenticity by resolving to live without pretending, which Wood presents as the player's own existential task.

authenticity.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
authenticity.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: The chapter asks whether Daenerys's fatalism - she feels truly free only once she believes fate is in control - can coexist with freedom in a Westeros where class and gender fix everyone's essence. Aristotle's sea-battle argument from bivalence and Cicero's Idle Argument (Dany will rule whether or not she leaves Meereen) are dismantled as having no practical consequences for deliberation, while Sartre's anguish and bad faith explain Cersei's 'necessity' excuse for arresting Ned and Sansa's refusal to own her lie about Joffrey and Mycah. Heidegger's authenticity then resolves the paradox: like Ned choosing between family and honor and Jon choosing his Night's Watch vows over kinship, freedom is not escape from one's past but owning it - Heraclitus's 'character is destiny,' becoming who you are.

authenticity.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
authenticity.title: 8. The Death of God and the Death of Meaning
authenticity.relation: Reads Chidi's 'Jeremy Bearimy' breakdown — quoting Nietzsche's Parable of the Madman ('God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him') after learning he has been tortured for three hundred years — as the nihilism that follows the death of God, where the Judge's verdict that the humans seek only 'moral deserts' strips their moral project of purpose. Michael's post-crisis makeover party is Camus's embrace of the absurd (Sisyphus pushing the boulder), and Sartre's Existentialism Is a Humanism supplies the way out: abandonment, anguish, and the French Soldier dilemma clarify Eleanor's confession in Season One and her lie that she failed the Judge's test as authentic choices. Once there is no hope of the Good Place, the humans finally choose goodness for its own sake.

authenticity.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
authenticity.title: 16. Is Hell Other People
authenticity.relation: Puts the show beside Sartre's No Exit, its acknowledged inspiration: Michael's neighborhood, like Garcin, Inez, and Estelle's drawing room, locks flawed people together to torture each other, but the four humans keep helping each other instead ('we improved each other, and the four of us became a team'). Against the standard reading, it uses Sartre's 1964 preface ('if relations with someone else are twisted... that other person can only be Hell'), the Being and Nothingness footnote about a 'radical conversion' from bad faith to authenticity, and his late remark that 'Heaven is each other' to argue the two works are compatible: other people are Hell only under dependence on their judgment — Season One Tahani's condition — while authentic relationships can succeed.

authenticity.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
authenticity.title: 23. Like Boxing Gloves of Sadness
authenticity.relation: Begins with Schur's traffic-light story — the fourth car sneaking through the left-turn arrow as 'negative twenty points' — to argue the show is, before it is about ethics, an attack on selfish inauthenticity: Tahani's name-dropping charity, Eleanor's lunch-table declaration of friendlessness, Chidi's moral filibustering, and Jason's Acidcat gig each pursue a self at others' expense. Using Charles Guignon's On Being Authentic and Kant's language of means and ends, it traces the movement from authenticity that uses others to an authenticity that lives for others — Chidi's 802 unconditional yeses, Michael's shift from torturer to self-sacrificer to paralyzed would-be hero, and Eleanor giving up Chidi in 'Pandemonium' as the endpoint. Being true to yourself, the show teaches, is only ethical when it helps others be their truest selves.

authenticity.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
authenticity.title: The Approaching Battle
authenticity.relation: Frames death as philosophy's ultimate question and contrasts the Epicurean advice to be unconcerned since death is simply the end of us with Heidegger's authenticity: boldly facing that death may come at any moment keeps us from living half-asleep, a view Plato anticipated by teaching that true philosophers make dying their profession. Harry, confronted with death from infancy, lives authentically, while Voldemort's flight from death marks him as the inauthentic case the essay traces through the Deathly Hallows death march.

authenticity.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
authenticity.title: King’s Cross Station
authenticity.relation: Reads Harry's walk into the Forbidden Forest, knowing he must die so the fragment of Voldemort's soul dies with him, his senses sharpening and gratitude welling for everything he never fully valued, as Heideggerian coming to terms with mortality rather than morbid brooding. Colin Creevey, the underage wizard who sneaks back to fight and falls, is offered as a second example of authentic living that recognizes limitations and seizes opportunities regardless of belief in an afterlife.

authenticity.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
authenticity.title: Reap a Destiny
authenticity.relation: Interprets the King's Cross scene through Heidegger's counsel to choose an exemplar from the past and dialogue with them: Dumbledore, freshly repentant for his youthful hunger for glory, plays exactly that role in a way-station likened to purgatory, while the flayed child-like creature under the chair is Voldemort's soul beyond help. The chapter closes by linking his fear-driven quest for deathlessness to Tolkien's One Ring, in which Sauron poured his own life-force, both fantasy dark lords undone by the desire for deathlessness.

authenticity.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
authenticity.title: Notes
authenticity.relation: Treats Frank's soliloquies-strangling the dog's 'useless pain', the Peachoid eulogy that goads a grieving congregation toward hating God, urinating on his father's grave 'to seem more human'-as a Heideggerian tour of concealment and disclosure, where truth is disclosure rather than correspondence and Frank alienates himself from responsibility and even from being human. Quoting Iris Murdoch on how fiction makes goodness seem dull and invoking Roth's 'theodicy of protest', the chapter warns that Frank's shuffling of morality into maneuver relaxes our moral guard about blame, God, and evil.

authenticity.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
authenticity.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Coatney explains why Katniss fails at everything she fakes — the disastrous first propos ('that is how a revolution dies'), the studio Mockingjay shoots, the cover-story mission to kill Snow — through Rousseau's distinction between amour de soi (natural self-love) and amour-propre (vanity born of society): she is a natural person in a corrupt world of seeming. The chapter contrasts district self-preservation with Capitol vanity (Posy asking green-skinned Octavia 'Are you sick?'), and reads Haymitch's smooth deception as a costlier, self-destroying alternative to Katniss's inability to dissimulate. Since Rousseau doubts any return to the state of nature, Katniss's refusal to flee into the woods — 'I'm going to stay right here and cause all kinds of trouble' — shows her Nietzsche-noted fate of being punished for her virtue, still preferable to becoming like Effie.

authenticity.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
authenticity.title: 7 Indiana Jones and Existential Self-Affirmation
authenticity.relation: Daniel Tilsley reads The Last Crusade as an excavation of identity: the fedora Fedora bestows after young Indy's defeat, the twenty-six-year quest for the Cross of Coronado ('All my life'), and the chosen name 'Indiana' (taken from the family dog) are acts of Nietzschean self-affirmation — amor fati and the willingness to will the Eternal Recurrence of one's life. The villains fail because they seek external artifacts to patch deficient lives, whereas the Grail Knight, like Camus's Sisyphus, authentically affirms his endless task of guarding the cup. The arc completes when Henry Sr. finally calls his son 'Indiana' while hanging from the abyss, recognizing the man he chose to become, and Crystal Skull repeats the pattern with Mutt and the fedora's eventual inheritance.

authenticity.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
authenticity.title: 9 Homeward Bound with Indiana Jones
authenticity.relation: Charles Taliaferro and Annalissa Lane use Gabriel Marcel's creative fidelity — being 'at home' with oneself, others, and the sacred through availability ('avec') and presence rather than treating persons as furniture — to chart Indy's growth across all four films. Willie and Indy's vanity-driven near-tryst in Temple, the partnership of convenience with Marion in Raiders, the Zeppelin reckoning with Henry Sr. ('I was less important to you than people who had been dead for 500 years'), and the honest jeep argument about the broken engagement in Crystal Skull mark stages from self-deception toward being fully present to another. The church wedding closing Crystal Skull completes the journey into openness to the sacred, showing that home is a way of being rather than a place.

authenticity.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
authenticity.title: The Face Shield Is a Mirror Iron Man and You
authenticity.relation: Gangle reads Stark's escape from the Ten Rings' cave and his press-conference conversion ('I have more to offer this world than just making things to blow up') through Heidegger's 'Question Concerning Technology.' Analyzing the armor via Aristotle's four causes (alloy, blueprints, Stark and Jarvis, the making of a hero) shows technology as a world-revealing, creative mode whose modern essence reduces nature and people to 'standing-reserve.' By becoming the armor — 'a pilot without the plane' — Stark unites technological might with individual conscience, using technology subversively to resist technology's own logic of power without accountability, an example of Heideggerian authentic existence the reader is called to imitate.

authenticity.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
authenticity.title: Notes
authenticity.relation: Miller reads Emmet's arc from 'Tell me what to do, and I'll do it!' conformity toward Vitruvius' 'embrace what is special about you' as a Heideggerian journey from das Man — the anonymous 'one does not do that' of the they-self, named in her notes — toward authenticity. LEGO play exemplifies the ready-to-hand engaged dealing with equipment that is more primordial than detached present-at-hand analysis, moods like boredom disclose the exhaustion of Lord Business's 'calculative thinking', the technological enframing that treats everything as standing-reserve, and art (Heidegger's Van Gogh shoes, a #KeepBuilding ad) reveals hidden cultural truths. Heidegger's 'Only if we are capable of dwelling, only then can we build' grounds her claim that LEGO's 'new toy everyday' recyclability sustains the meditative, sustainable building the book's ethos demands — even while admitting the movie is itself a masterful advertisement.

authenticity.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
authenticity.title: It Worked
authenticity.relation: Lee reads Jack, Locke, and Desmond as studies in Sartrean bad faith and authenticity: Christian Shephard's Red Sox fatalism is determinism as an excuse for moral failure, Locke swings from a Kierkegaardian leap of faith (pushing the button as his Abraham-and-Isaac trial) into nihilism when the Pearl film suggests the button is a psychological experiment, and Desmond's Humean skepticism yields to sacrificial faith in the fail-safe. He argues Jacob is the show's greatest con man, so Jack's acceptance of destiny in 'The End' remains a free choice rather than predestination. The finale's sideways world then moves Lost from secular existentialism to religious existentialism, read through Buber's I-Thou relation in Sawyer and Juliet's 'It worked' reunion and the all-religions church, where as Gandhi held every path leads to the same place.

authenticity.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
authenticity.title: Existential Values
authenticity.relation: Belliotti tests Roger Sterling against three existential standards. Kierkegaard's aesthetic stage fits him 'crisply': his quips about the chase, drinking 'because it's what men do,' and the penny-jar view of marriage reveal flight from commitment and terror of boredom, and even his twenty-year marriage to Mona lacked Kierkegaard's passionate inwardness, making it objectively true but existentially inauthentic. Measured by Nietzsche he falls between the last man who wants an agency 'where everybody has a summer house' and the will-to-power grand transcender he never becomes, oscillating between frustration and boredom; measured by Heidegger he settles for chatter, clings to fixity, and reflects on mortality only briefly after his heart attacks. The verdict: significantly inauthentic, capped by the blackface 'My Old Kentucky Home' serenade that makes Don whisper 'Can we go?'

authenticity.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
authenticity.title: The Metal Militia and the Existentialist Club
authenticity.relation: Jeremy Wisnewski claims Metallica is an existentialist band: Kill 'Em All answers Camus' absurd by creating meaning through chosen, expressive projects ('Metal Militia', 'Motorbreath'), Ride the Lightning's catalogue of deaths ('Fight Fire with Fire' to 'Fade to Black') individualizes us in the Heideggerian confrontation with our own death, and Master of Puppets dramatizes Sartrean bad faith - the 'Sanitarium' label, the soldier as 'Disposable Hero', the addict's lost freedom. He concludes that accusing Metallica of selling out with the Black Album is itself bad faith, since authenticity has no fixed content.

authenticity.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
authenticity.title: The Struggle Within: Hetfield, Kierkegaard, and the Pursuit of Authenticity
authenticity.relation: Philip Lindholm reads Metallica through Kierkegaard's demand for subjectivity: the soldier in 'One' crying 'Oh please God help me' exemplifies becoming a single individual before God against the untruth of the crowd, and 'The Struggle Within' stages Either/Or's passionate choice that decides the self. He then shows Hetfield himself living the inauthentic masked life Kierkegaard condemns - 'I was James Hetfield of Metallica' - until rehab forced the honest self-disclosure ('The God That Failed' and 'Until It Sleeps' mourning his parents) that marks a move toward authentic individuality.

authenticity.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
authenticity.title: Metallica's Existential Freedom: From We to I and Back Again
authenticity.relation: Rachael Sotos reads Metallica's career as an existentialist quest for authentic freedom: the Arendtian shared 'we' of the early speed-metal community (Kill 'Em All), the Heideggerian 'I' attuned to death that breaks from das Man (Ride the Lightning's 'Fade to Black'), and the Kierkegaardian leap out of the over-technical system of . . . And Justice for All - compared to Kierkegaard's critique of Hegel - into the embodied groove of the Black Album. Sartre's bad faith explains the rock-star traps, and Some Kind of Monster shows the 'we' must be tended: therapy and a democratic band restore Arendtian public freedom.

authenticity.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
authenticity.title: The Office and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Pits authenticity - understood both as self-discovery and as existentialist self-creation after Sartre and Heidegger, requiring self-knowledge and meaningful relationships - against happiness as subjective well-being, in a case study of Michael Scott. Michael's closest 'friendships' are relationships of convenience (Dwight's betrayal in 'The Coup', the fear-induced Packer bond, self-destructive Jan), his 'Packer norms' of locker-room humor are unshakeable, and Shelley Taylor-style positive illusions (his self-image as progressive on Diversity Day, 'The World's Best Boss' mug) keep his moods afloat while truth-tellers like Jan and the Chili's bar patrons knock them down. The conclusion challenges Socrates' dictum: since Michael is psychologically incapable of achieving authenticity, perhaps for some people the examined life is simply not available, and trying for it only produces misery.

authenticity.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
authenticity.title: The Office and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Lonergan and Wisnewski read 'Grief Counseling' and 'Safety Training' as a case study in death-denial: Michael cannot parse the euphemism 'we lost Ed Truck,' Kelly must teach him to be sad, and Creed's report of the decapitation forces the Heideggerian realization that death is his own not-to-be-outstripped possibility, not just a fact of life. The office deflects with movie plots and euphemism (Jim's 'seriously hurt' about the rooftop stunt), Pam's eulogy for Toby's bird shows how mourning ritual copes with mortality, and Michael's longing to be remembered - hospital wings named after him, saving his own life - exemplifies Kierkegaard's 'world-historical' life as an ego defense, with living subjectively the recommended but unexplained alternative. Becker's thesis that all culture is a fabricated protest against death frames the whole chapter.

authenticity.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
authenticity.title: Getting the Joke
authenticity.relation: Gray reads Jack Handey's Deep Thoughts and Fuzzy Memories as packaged existentialism: Sartre's existence precedes essence grounds Handey's responsibility for self-made meaning ('if you're robbing a bank and your pants fall down... life is funny'), Camus's absurd and Sisyphus's happy perseverance match 'sometimes I think the world has gone completely mad. And then I think, Aw, who cares?', and Beauvoir's ruts of inferiority warn against the ease of 'just sitting there' wanting money. Heidegger's authenticity and mortality appear in the parachute-swimming gag, dying laughing rather than in dread. The chapter also explains why the deadpan delivery over serene stream imagery makes morbidity funny, and worries that Handey's 'truth is... unreal' anticipated post-truth politics.

authenticity.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
authenticity.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Weighs Marx against Heidegger on whether SAMCRO should fight its history. Teller-Morrow read as petit-bourgeois capitalism turns the Mayans' pilot-episode raid into industrial sabotage and Nero's escort business into exploitation; read through Proudhon, Kropotkin, and Emma Goldman — whose essay John Teller found quoted on a Nevada wall — the club is an anarcho-syndicalist commune with democratic chapel votes, Kropotkin's mutual aid to widows like Lyla, and Tara as its socialized healthcare. Heidegger's historicity gives the resolution: Jax cannot escape the past (the Irish deal only with Clay; 'The sting of that betrayal ain't gonna fade') but can appropriate it authentically, and Pope's forced choice of a victim in 'Laying Pipe' confronts him with being-toward-death.

authenticity.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
authenticity.title: Notes
authenticity.relation: Pits Donna Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto against Star Trek's horror of the Borg, reading Locutus/Picard, Hugh, and Seven of Nine as tests of the Federation values of autonomy, individuality, and authenticity against the rival Borg values of heteronomy, collectivity, and simulation. Picard's "My culture is based on freedom and self-determination" exchange with the Borg, Hugh's discovery of his name and first-person "I", and Seven's tug-of-war with the Borg Queen in "Dark Frontier" dramatize what assimilation threatens. The chapter then defends a Haraway-inspired feminist reboot: women and minorities were long denied autonomy, individuality, and authenticity by prejudice and stereotype (Seven still must look "warp-core hot" in her catsuit), the human/machine and man/woman binaries were always false, and since we already live as cyborgs of apps, implants, and networks, resistance was negligible - the real Borg problem is their violent means, not their values.

authenticity.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
authenticity.title: Purpose or Futility
authenticity.relation: Tiernan reads Din Djarin as an Abraham figure from Fear and Trembling: like Kierkegaard's knight of faith, he teleologically suspends the ethical when he surrenders Grogu to the Jedi despite paternal attachment, just as Abraham consented to sacrifice Isaac. The chapter maps his journey onto Kierkegaard's three stages - the aesthetic temptation of settling down with Omera on Sorgan, the ethical duty of the Resol'nare and the Way, and the religious leap of faith in which purpose is regained by being given up. To become a true Mandalorian he must paradoxically abandon the creed that defines him, twice removing the helmet he swore never to remove - for the Morak facial scan and to bid Grogu farewell.

authenticity.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
authenticity.title: 17. Batman’s Mask in Aristotle’s Drama
authenticity.relation: Reads Batman's defining difference—the mask—through Aristotle's Poetics: Batman is mimesis, a theatrical performance (the prosopon) engineered to produce pity, fear, and suspense, while unmasked, transparent Superman is the more Platonic figure who wants the Mirror of Truth in All-Star Superman to confirm Clark Kent is his real self. Batman's acting literally beats Superman in The Dark Knight Returns, where the fight is won by a staged death from a fake-heart pill, and his 'Feat of Clay' interrogation shows him performing cruelty to weaponize criminals' imaginations. Because the role is imitable—Robin, Batman Incorporated, the Sons of Batman—'Batman is an idea' anyone can become, whereas Eco's 'Myth of Superman' explains why the unimitatable alien preserves rather than changes his world.

authenticity.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
authenticity.title: Stained Glass Windows in My Mind: Modality in the Imagery of Taylor Swift
authenticity.relation: Reads Swift's imagery as modal logic: David Lewis's counterfactuals distinguish indicative from counterfactual conditionals in 'the 1', Kripke's rigid designators show that 'If I was a man / Then I'd be the man' posits an impossible world (a man could not be Taylor Swift), while 'Would've, Could've, Should've' assigns the counterfactual's antecedent to the perpetrator, not the young narrator. Kierkegaard's 'dizziness of freedom' and despair, with Heidegger's authenticity and das Man, frame counterfactual dwelling as both celebrity performance ('mirrorball') and a route to ownedness, with 'right where you left me' as the delusional extreme and 'it's time to go' as the release. Aristotle's catharsis explains how engaging these might-have-beens in song purges regret for listeners.

authenticity.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
authenticity.title: Notes
authenticity.relation: Latta uses James Hollis's Jungian 'Middle Passage' - the midlife collapse of our tacit contract with the universe and of the provisional personality built in life's first half - to read Ted's arc with Dr. Sharon Fieldstone: her bike accident and self-disclosure, his panic attacks, and his confession about his father's suicide force him to drop the coach persona and choose an authentic second half. The chapter interprets Ted's move to London as both flight from and working-through of paternal trauma, his distance from son Henry as the wound it exposes, and closes with Kierkegaard's journal demand to find 'a truth which is truth for me,' which Ted finds in the return home to Kansas.

authenticity.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
authenticity.title: NOTES
authenticity.relation: Daniel Malloy asks whether the T-101's self-destruction in the steel mill was suicide, and whether it was justified, opening with Camus's claim that suicide is philosophy's only serious problem and the ambiguous case of Socrates' hemlock. Using Heidegger, he argues the learning-mode Terminator qualifies as Da-sein whose death is being-toward-death — the end of possibility — so the T2 machine dies authentically while the T3 machine's 'We'll meet again' is inauthentic self-deception. Kant condemns the act because the Terminator uses itself merely as a means, and Kant cannot even conceive of its genuine conflict of duties (preserve its life vs. prevent Skynet), while Bentham-style utilitarianism initially endorses the sacrifice but is refuted by hindsight: Skynet rises anyway, and consequentialism gives no credit for noble motives. The chapter ends by concluding that dying for a cause is illogical, since the dead surrender all control over the meaning of their actions.

authenticity.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
authenticity.title: 13. No Place like a Non-Place
authenticity.relation: The chapter reads the show through Marc Auge's 'non-place,' the anonymous transit space of supermodernity: the slow ocean liner of 'Passage on the Lady Anne' against accelerated modern life, Nan Adams's road in 'The Hitch-Hiker,' the Civil War road of 'The Passersby,' the diner of 'Will the Real Martian Please Stand Up?,' the airplane cabin of 'Nightmare at 20,000 Feet,' and the hotel rooms and ninth-floor mall of 'The After Hours' and 'The Four of Us Are Dying.' In these spaces of interchangeable anonymity, emptied by postwar consumerism and shifting gender roles, identity crises play out, and only moments of identification, or fatally being recognized, as Archie Hammer is by Andy Marshak's father, restore or destroy a self.

authenticity.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
authenticity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Kempner reads the comic through Sartre's 'Existentialism Is a Humanism': with God and the old world gone, survivors like Rick, Michonne, and Dale must create their own values, while characters who cling to pre-apocalypse essences (Hershel keeping his zombified son in the barn, Shane waiting for the government) bring death on themselves. Rick's hospital awakening is treated as an existential rebirth in which his cop uniform is an 'essence precedes existence' trap, and Carl shooting Shane (and later Ben in 'Fear the Hunters') shows children making free choices outside conventional morality. The chapter concludes the series is 'sternly optimistic' because total freedom, not zombification, is what defines the humans: 'in a world ruled by the dead, we are forced to finally start living.'

authenticity.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
authenticity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
authenticity.relation: Round argues modern zombie fiction's real horror is humanity, reading The Walking Dead existentially: Rick builds meaning through self-imposed missions, revises his morals ('You kill, you die' then killing Dexter anyway), and demands in his 'We ARE the walking dead' speech (Issue #24) that the group admit their new nature instead of hiding in bad faith behind old rules. Kierkegaard's Abraham illuminates Rick's suspension of universal ethics, while Sergeant Abraham Ford's confession 'No. I did what I wanted to do' models owning one's choices, and his angst after Eugene's lie shows the cost of projected meaning collapsing. Camus supplies persistence against the absurd (suicides like Jim, Jacqui, and Carol exert the only control left), and Adorno's Marxist critique frames the Governor's Woodbury as an inauthentic hierarchy that denies its people authentic choice.

authenticity.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
authenticity.title: Nothing Is Ever Black or White
authenticity.relation: Miechels maps Witcher 3 onto Heidegger's Being and Time: with no character creator, the player is thrown into Geralt's fixed identity, the 'Butcher of Blaviken' with cat eyes whom villagers spit at, in a war-torn Velen he did not choose. Projection appears in the Triss-or-Yennefer romance (where refusing to choose is still a choice) and in the Bloody Baron, whose guilt shows that his war trauma and alcoholism never excused his choices: 'nothing is ever black and white' does not absolve him. Falling into das Man shows up in Gwent rounds, map question marks, and above all online walkthroughs of the 'optimal choice' for Willis's burned forge, which let players evade the responsibility of deciding for themselves.

authenticity.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
authenticity.relation: The editors' introduction argues that the unifying theme of Lee's films is the struggle for authentic self-identity, framed through Charles Taylor's dialogical self and Kierkegaard's line that anxiety is the dizziness of freedom. It surveys how Confucian virtues (ren, li, xiao) and Daoist wu-wei play out across Pushing Hands, The Wedding Banquet, Eat Drink Man Woman, Crouching Tiger, Sense and Sensibility, Brokeback Mountain and others, treating each protagonist as caught between traditional obligation and personal desire. It invokes Nietzsche's claim that all philosophy is autobiography to justify reading Lee's films (he said 'it's all in my films') as a coherent authorial philosophy.

authenticity.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
authenticity.relation: Dale and Foy argue that across Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Hulk and Brokeback Mountain, Lee presents a pessimistic, Sartrean philosophy of identity in which authentic selves are irreconcilable with a hostile social world. They read Jen's caged gender rebellion and Jade Fox's rejection, Bruce's suppressed origins and rage-fueled transformation, and Ennis and Jack's concealed love as hidden identities that produce dislocation, deception and disorder. Invoking Kierkegaard and Heidegger's dasein on authenticity and Foucault's Discipline and Punish, they show society disciplining deviance so each hero is displaced or destroyed—Jack beaten to death like Matthew Shepard, the Hulk exiled to the Amazon.

authenticity.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
authenticity.title: “There’s No More Watching” Artifice and Meaning in Synecdoche, New York and Adaptation
authenticity.relation: Hill argues that Adaptation and Synecdoche, New York both dramatize artists (the character Charlie Kaufman and Caden Cotard) struggling to portray 'real life' through artifice, and that Kaufman achieves authenticity not through neorealist naturalism but through surrealism and fantasy. He distinguishes the existentialist sense of authenticity—living self-awarely and choosing outside a community's rules (via Macquarrie)—from cinematic realism, tracing Kaufman's fusion of inner and outer life to Fellini's 8½. The chapter reads Synecdoche as an unflinching, near-horror examination of what it costs to make honest art, concluding its buried message is that creation is meaningless unless shared.

authenticity.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
authenticity.relation: Douglas McFarland argues that Hereafter is philosophical in Nehamas's sense of an 'art of living': its three characters (Marie, George, the boy Marcus) must fashion meaning in the face of absence and abandonment rather than settle the existence of an afterlife. He aligns their struggles with Augustine's grief over his mother's death in the Confessions, Montaigne's 'I portray not being but becoming' and his revision of Socrates' Phaedo claim that philosophy is practice for death, and Sartre's view that God's absence grounds the freedom to make meaning through work. George's turn from listening to the dead to genuinely seeing the living Marcus, and his letter to Marie, mark authentic self-fashioning in the here and now.

authenticity.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
authenticity.title: Raising Arizona as an American Comedy
authenticity.relation: Gilmore reads Raising Arizona as a classical comedy (bad-beginning-to-good-ending) about the American 'optative mood' of self-creation, using Hi McDunnough's outlaw-to-family arc and his name-as-height-metaphor to figure Emerson's aspirational American self. He deploys Plato's two kinds of cave-laughter to distinguish the film's 'tender,' welcoming comedy (Hi and Ed, Gale and Evelle) from mocking ridicule, and frames Hi's need to abandon outlaw identity via Heidegger's Augenblick and Badiou's 'event' sparked in Ed's mug-shot flash. Nietzsche on dreams-as-origin-of-metaphysics grounds the film's dream/reality tension, and Hi's over-identification with the outlaw universal is glossed as Sartrean bad faith.

authenticity.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
authenticity.title: Self-Creation, Identity, and Authenticity A Study of A History of Violence and Eastern Promises
authenticity.relation: Daniel Moseley distinguishes metaphysical from practical problems of personal identity, arguing A History of Violence and Eastern Promises explore the practical: who Tom/Joey and Nikolai really are, as a matter of self-creation and self-discovery of a 'practical identity' (Korsgaard). Using Sartre's bad faith and Cavell on movie-star 'individualities,' plus Charles Taylor's critique of individualist authenticity, he argues even the wicked Semyon exemplifies authenticity, so authenticity is not a moral ideal, and Nikolai's decent double life may be worth being less authentic.

authenticity.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
authenticity.title: 16. Doppelgängers, Doubles, and Tulpas
authenticity.relation: Bunce reads Twin Peaks' pervasive doubling as dramatizing self-loss versus self-mastery. Cooper is good because he integrates his rational and mystical sides into an authentic whole, while BOB is a parasitic, one-dimensional inhabiting spirit and Laura chooses death over becoming BOB. He explains self-loss through La Rochefoucauld and Rousseau on amour-propre and the modern craving for esteem (Josie's masks versus Norma's refusal to become a brand), and traces the doppelganger motif from Jean Paul's satire of Fichte's clear I/not-I distinction to Dostoyevsky's The Double—arguing that, unlike Jean Paul, Twin Peaks affirms an authentic, whole self one is responsible for.

authenticity.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
authenticity.title: 17. Through Plastic Our Secrets Seen
authenticity.relation: Winters uses Schopenhauer's World as Will and Idea to argue that the townsfolk (Shelly, Leo, Ben, Josie, Ed, and Laura) do not freely choose the lives they despise but are driven by the blind will, and so live double lives whose secrets a single death exposes. Laura, unlike the others who mismanage their passions, was denied the chance to develop her own values, so she pursued danger, drugs, and prostitution to see herself through her own eyes; death, he argues, reveals true character (the townsfolk's rush to bury her, their guilt), turning Socrates' unexamined-life dictum uneasy—sometimes what examination reveals is a monster we would rather not see.

authenticity.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
authenticity.title: Introduction
authenticity.relation: Editor Jerold Abrams argues Kubrick's whole filmography forms a coherent 'cinematic existentialism' in which a free subject stands against a cold, uncaring world, synthesized with strands of Stoicism and pragmatism. He surveys the volume's essays as variations on this theme: Camus' absurd in Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove, Nietzschean flux in Full Metal Jacket, Heideggerian being-toward-death and authenticity in Paths of Glory, and Nietzsche's overman as the Star Child in 2001. The essay ties specific films (the ape's femur, HAL, Humbert, the Overlook) to the claim that each Kubrick subject must invent its own meaning in a meaningless universe.

authenticity.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
authenticity.title: Existential Ethics Where the Paths of Glory Lead Jason Holt
authenticity.relation: Holt uses Paths of Glory to illustrate existential ethics, framing the doomed 701st Regiment as 'thrown' beings-toward-death who retain full freedom in how they meet their fate. He resolves the 'paradox of existentialism' (denying objective values while commanding authenticity) by treating authenticity as a formal, second-order virtue like integrity: Colonel Dax is sincere and consistent, General Mireau an inauthentic hypocrite acting in bad faith. Addressing weakness of will (Roget's cowardice) and the condemned Paris 'dying well' before the firing squad, Holt argues that courage—an Aristotelian character virtue—is the smuggled-in content that grounds any formalist existential ethics.

authenticity.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
authenticity.title: Seeking Authenticity
authenticity.relation: The chapter argues that Whedon's heroes—Angel resisting the demon within in Pylea, Spike earning back his soul, Simon Tam abandoning his medical career for River, Echo asserting control over her Dollhouse imprints, and Buzz Lightyear redefining himself—live authentically by owning their values against depersonalizing forces, while Captain Hammer and Serenity's Operative are the true 'monsters' who surrender their identities to social roles and blind institutional loyalty. It then asks whether Whedon is a thoroughgoing Sartrean existentialist and answers no: the 'Paradiso Paradigm' (Mal returning the medicine in 'The Train Job') and Willow's 'Choices' speech show objective moral value independent of autonomous choice, making Whedon more Socratic than Sartrean. Rawls supplies the synthesis: heterogeneous life plans (Xander, Oz, Lorne) pursued within objective social conditions—basic rights, liberties, and opportunities—that make authentic self-formation possible for everyone.

authenticity.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
authenticity.title: Conclusion
authenticity.relation: The conclusion synthesizes the book's case that Whedon philosophizes, building a Shaw-style hierarchy from illustrating theories (Connor as Robert Kane's libertarian agent, 'stirred up' between Darla's and faux-Cordelia's competing visions) through ethical and metaphysical complexity ('Man on the Street,' Angel/Angelus) to epistemic endorsement of a Whedonian worldview. It reads Angel's epiphany — 'if there's no bigger meaning, then the smallest act of kindness is the greatest thing in the world' — as a negative project against the thesis that ethics without God is incoherent, since Whedon's God-ambiguous fiction shows noble self-sacrifice (Buffy for Dawn, Cordy for Angel, Simon for River) that remains worthwhile regardless of cosmic justice. Following Mulhall's use of Socrates as an exemplar of ethically significant living, it casts Angel the Champion as a comparable exemplar grounded in authenticity, care-based relationships, and the transformation of moral character. It closes by extending the film-as-philosophy debate to television, deploying Carroll's gaze/glance distinction to argue nothing in principle keeps quality TV — from The Twilight Zone and Star Trek to Buffy and Angel — from being philosophy in action.

authenticity.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.relation: Sanders's introductory survey frames Mann's cinema as suffused with existentialist themes—alienation, freedom, authenticity, and existential choice—citing Sartre's 'condemned to be free' as the key to protagonists like Thief's Frank and Heat's Neil McCauley, who choose personal truth over surrender. It maps the volume's essays: Nietzschean will to power in the crime films, Levinas's ethics of the Other in Thief and Collateral, and Lockean/Rousseauian visions of nature in The Last of the Mohicans. Mann's outsiders repeatedly face the fateful, doom-laden choices (McCauley abandoning Eady to kill Waingro) that define existential man.

authenticity.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.relation: Sanders argues Mann's action serves existentialist ideas: identity, freedom, authenticity, and death. In Thief, Frank's insistence on 'the yield of my labor' and his self-immolating exit dramatize the individualist maximizer whose choice of principle—echoing Sartre's young man and Kierkegaard's 'purity of heart is to will one thing'—cannot be given from outside. The Miami Vice episode 'Heart of Darkness' is read as a morality play on authenticity: undercover agent Artie Lawson's flight into the fantasy persona is a bad-faith masquerade that ends in suicide, mirroring Crockett's own anxiety about his Sonny Burnett alter ego.

authenticity.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.relation: Rybin links Mann's style-versus-substance debate to the existential self-definition of his characters, focusing on Public Enemies. Dillinger, who tells Billie 'the only thing that's important is where somebody's going,' is not yet an icon but is 'becoming Dillinger' as the film unfolds. In the penultimate scene, watching Clark Gable in Manhattan Melodrama—'die the way you lived, all of a sudden'—Dillinger achieves authentic self-definition by claiming the gangster myth as his own identity, a Warshovian 'experience of art'; Mann's editing collapses the space between Dillinger and the screen just before Dillinger is gunned down, the cost of authentic selfhood.

authenticity.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
authenticity.relation: Corne unpacks Vincent Hanna's tirade in Heat against his wife's ex-husband's 'dead-tech, postmodernistic, bullshit house.' He reads the smashing of the television and the headless sculpture through Bataille's Against Architecture (buildings as latent prisons of authority) and Jameson's diagnosis of postmodern depthlessness and the silence of affect. Using Hegel, Hugo and Ruskin on architecture's obligation to tell the truth, and especially Frankfurt's On Bullshit, Corne argues the house is 'bullshit' because it is indifferent to truth; Vincent's workaholism becomes a Frankfurtian discipline, and the film reflexively treats truth, authenticity and space as a problem.

authenticity.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
authenticity.title: The Existential Frankenstein
authenticity.relation: McMahon gives an existential reading of Whale's Frankenstein and Shelley's novel through Heidegger's being-toward-death and Ernest Becker's denial of death. Victor Frankenstein exemplifies Becker's 'defiant Promethianism,' the offensive denial that seeks to conquer death, and the monster personifies death itself. She argues his obsession erodes his humanity, estranges him from others, and generates moral dilemmas, illustrating Heidegger's claim that only authentic acceptance of mortality restores individuality and genuine community, so that mastering death would make us monsters.

authenticity.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
authenticity.relation: Abrams's editorial introduction argues that Kubrick's whole filmography forms a coherent cinematic existentialism in which the isolated self stands against a cold, uncaring world. It threads the individual Kubrick films through named philosophers - Camus's absurd in Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove, Nietzsche's flux and Overman in Full Metal Jacket and 2001, Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death in Paths of Glory, Kant's marriage-morality in Eyes Wide Shut - and notes Kubrick blends this existentialism with Stoicism (The Killing) and pragmatism. It frames each contributor's essay as reading one film through that lens.

authenticity.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
authenticity.relation: Holt reads Paths of Glory as an illustration of existential ethics. The doomed men of the 701st are 'thrown' (Heidegger) into a suicidal attack on the Ant Hill, and the film contrasts the authentic Colonel Dax - sincere, consistent, refusing Mireau's command out of integrity - with the inauthentic, bad-faith General Mireau. Holt resolves the 'paradox of existentialism' by treating 'be authentic' as a formal meta-value, and argues that authenticity ultimately rests on the Aristotelian virtue of courage, shown when Paris 'dies well' before the firing squad despite an earlier failure of nerve.

authenticity.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
authenticity.relation: Ryan Weldon reads Selina Kyle's transformation into Catwoman in Batman Returns through Sartre's existentialism and Beauvoir's The Second Sex. Pre-death Selina is Sartre's inauthentic 'waiter,' performing a servile secretary role in bad faith, and Beauvoir's objectified Other, defined by Max Shreck and the men who dismiss her. Her murder and feline resurrection free repressed drives, and her refusal of Batman's fairy-tale rescue—'I couldn't live with myself'—plus her choice to kill Shreck are cast as an assertion of facticity and transcendence, an authentic (if unfinished) self-creation that rejects the roles available to women rather than reaching a stable ending.

authenticity.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
authenticity.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
authenticity.relation: McMahon argues Burton's death-saturated corpus functions as modern memento mori that fosters Heideggerian authenticity by arousing the uncanny and honest awareness of being-toward-death. She supplements Freud's account of the unheimliche (which she says wrongly substitutes castration anxiety for the primal fear of death) with Heidegger's link of angst, uncanniness, and finitude in 'Being and Time,' plus Terror Management Theory. Reading 'The Nightmare Before Christmas,' 'Corpse Bride,' and 'Dark Shadows,' she shows Jack, Bonejangles's Dance of Death, Emily, and vampire Barnabas use animation, comedy, and romance to make death palatable, and contrasts these films with Nozick's escapist experience machine—Burton supplements reality rather than replacing it.

authenticity.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
authenticity.title: Noir et Blanc in Color: Existentialism and Miami Vice
authenticity.relation: Sanders reads Miami Vice as existentialist 'sunshine noir,' where color and pastel locations carry noir alienation, and Crockett and Tubbs live rootless lives with shambles of romances and a culturally impoverished compass (Bolt, Buddy Holly, Buffett, Beckett, Betts). The episode 'No Exit' (Bruce Willis as arms dealer Tony Amato, whose wife Rita shoots him at the courthouse steps) is analyzed through Sartre's being-in-itself/being-for-itself conflict and 'hell is other people,' from which Danto says 'there is no exit.' 'Heart of Darkness' presents Ed O'Neill's undercover FBI agent Arthur Lawson, who prefers his Artie Rollins persona and hangs himself after debriefing, as a failure of authenticity and flight into bad faith that Crockett recognizes as his own peril as Sonny Burnett. Crockett's amnesia arc ('Mirror Image' through 'Redemption in Blood' and 'Bad Timing'), where he believes he is Burnett working for the Manolo organization, is resolved through Sartrean existential recognition and a freely chosen dangerous mission that restores his identity, since the Kierkegaardian leap of faith is unavailable in the show's secular world; Sanders also attacks Sartre's sanction of revolutionary violence in his preface to Fanon and Beauvoir's defense of Sade.

authenticity.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
authenticity.title: The Prisoner and Self-Imprisonment
authenticity.relation: Biderman and Devlin use The Prisoner to test three dimensions of selfhood: Number 6's 'I am not a number!' defends the material self against the Village's conformity (Rover, uniforms, human chess pieces), his reflective self echoes Descartes's certain thinking thing, Kant's rational self-legislation, and Sartrean authenticity ('existence precedes essence'), while the finale's trial of the rebels addresses the relational self. The revelation that Number 6 is Number 1 is then read through Foucault: hierarchical observation, normalization, and examination make the Village Bentham's panopticon internalized, so the prisoner monitors himself and the ideal of a freely self-created identity collapses into social conditioning, as Nietzsche's herd come home. The chapter leaves the noir ambiguity intact: either Number 6 is the authentic individual vindicated by the Village council, or the self is a fiction and his odyssey hopeless.

authenticity.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
authenticity.title: 1 Primal and Spontaneous Neil Young’s Aesthetics of Authenticity
authenticity.relation: Forest argues that Neil Young's habit of keeping early, flawed takes with Crazy Horse ("audio verite") embodies an aesthetic of authenticity as primal spontaneity. He reads Young through Emerson's self-reliance and trust in first impressions, Nietzsche's Apollonian/Dionysian split (Harvest vs. Tonight's the Night, Young's onstage abandon on "Like a Hurricane"), Benjamin's loss of aura in mechanical reproduction, and Collingwood's art/craft distinction, contending that the "garage band" imperfections of jams like "Down by the River" let fans identify with the band's expressive, un-repeatable moment.

authenticity.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
authenticity.title: 2 Neil Young and Creativity
authenticity.relation: Berger surveys Young's repeated claim that he does not intentionally compose but "receives" songs, comparing himself to a radio station or microphone and echoing Schubert's "I remember it." He illuminates this with C.S. Peirce's categories of firstness (feeling), secondness (reaction) and thirdness (thought/signs), arguing that Young's refusal to "judge" lyrics like "Tell Me Why" or "Cowgirl in the Sand" protects the originary feeling, and that songs communicate feeling through Peircean icons and metaphors rather than deliberate rational design.

authenticity.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
authenticity.title: 4 Extended Mind and the Music of Trans
authenticity.relation: Umbaugh reads Young's synthesizer/Vocoder album Trans, written amid efforts to communicate with his quadriplegic son Ben ("Transformer Man"), alongside Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind thesis and its Parity Principle. He uses examples (Otto's notebook, bartenders' glassware, navigation, Dennett on the elderly) to argue cognition couples with external scaffolding, and parallels the "unnatural" reception of Trans (like the homophobic anti-disco backlash) with resistance to extended cognition, concluding both Trans and the extended mind are authentic once the "natural/artificial" boundary is questioned.

authenticity.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
authenticity.title: 6 Neil Young and American Indians Politics, Lyrics, and Authenticity
authenticity.relation: Hester critiques Young's treatment of American Indians, arguing "Cortez the Killer" idealizes the Aztecs into Montaigne-style "noble savages," makes their sacrifices seem voluntary, and ultimately centers Young's own lost-love lament rather than the conquest's real victims. He shows "Pocahontas" objectifies and commodifies a Native woman (the "thousand pelts" line, Young's cavalier interview remarks) as cultural appropriation and "playing Indian," yet notes Young's genuine activism (Honor the Treaties) leaves fans wanting to credit his good intentions.

authenticity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
authenticity.title: I Am the Bad Wolf
authenticity.relation: Roman Altshuler answers Davros's charge that the Doctor is a 'destroyer of worlds' using Aristotelian virtue ethics. He argues the Doctor's chief virtue is not compassion but Heideggerian 'authentic concern': offering aggressors (the Nestene, Sontarans, the Master) a genuine choice so they become responsible for escalating, illustrated by the fly-swatter thought experiment.
