master-slave-morality.relation: Duncan Gale reads Raiders through Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: the Nazis' contempt for those they exploit ('They hire only strong backs and they pay pennies') enacts master morality, while their ressentiment-driven project is itself a fatal misreading — both of the Ark and of Nietzsche, whom Walter Kaufmann shows was distorted by his anti-Semitic sister rather than responsible for it. Indy emerges as an overman candidate whose improvised self-legislation ('I'm making this up as I go,' casually shooting the scimitar-wielding warrior) creates life-affirming values, unlike Belloq, who has no code at all. The finale inverts the death of God: the Nazis die because they disturb a divine power they cannot harness, while America's de facto agnosticism — warehousing the Ark with 'top men' — proves the survivable response to nihilism.

master-slave-morality.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
master-slave-morality.title: Can We Play Beyond Good and Evil
master-slave-morality.relation: Kristina Drzaic and Peter Rauch split Zelda play into two modes: the designed ludus game, in which Link is morally good by default (he cannot lie, steal, or hurt innocents), and player-generated paidia play through glitches, like making Link fly in Ocarina of Time or unlocking the Fierce Deity a day early in Majora's Mask, which crash the game but lie outside the story's morality. Using Caillois and Frasca on ludus versus paidia, they map this onto Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil: Link exemplifies slave morality (pity, patience, humility, avoiding fear) while the paidia player is a value-creating master who honors power and secrecy in gaming culture. The conclusion is that good-and-evil in videogames is welded to ludus, and some players just want to be naughty.

master-slave-morality.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
master-slave-morality.title: Each of Us Would See Ourselves
master-slave-morality.relation: The Teschners cast Don as a Nietzschean creator of value in technological culture: his nihilism ('There is no big lie. There is no system. The universe is indifferent') and 'What you call love was invented by guys like me to sell nylons' embody anti-foundationalism, while the beatnik Roy plays the resentful slave mentality whose passion lives only off what it despises. Don's creative process (sleep on it, 'forget it, and an idea will jump in your face') mirrors the camel-lion-child metamorphoses of Zarathustra, and the collapse of the principium individuationis explains his fluid identities from Dick Whitman to the 'Adam and Eve' fantasy with Rachel. Heidegger's techné frames the Kodak Carousel as genuine art, a revealing that transfigures 'a hell of a gadget' into 'a place where we know we are loved,' at the tragic price of a man outside community, and the falling figure of the credits is one 'we would each see ourselves' in.

master-slave-morality.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
master-slave-morality.title: This Search Goes On: Christian, Warrior, Buddhist
master-slave-morality.relation: William Irwin traces Hetfield's journey through three sets of virtues: rejecting the Christian virtues of his Christian Science upbringing ('The God That Failed' as Nietzschean slave morality and Marx's opium of the masses), adopting the warrior virtues of Kill 'Em All (life as Hobbesian war, Nietzsche's will to power and 'no remorse'), and finally embracing Buddhist virtues on St. Anger. The warrior code fails without stoicism and collapses into addiction and despair, while the four noble truths - suffering caused by craving ('Frantic', 'Sweet Amber') - fit Hetfield's recovery and growing compassion.

master-slave-morality.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
master-slave-morality.title: Metallica, Nietzsche, and Marx: The Immorality of Morality
master-slave-morality.relation: Peter Fosl argues Metallica's moral critique of religion in 'Leper Messiah' and 'The God That Failed' continues Nietzsche's genealogy of Christian slave morality born of ressentiment and Marx's 'opium of the people': religion gathers a docile herd, denies this world, and exercises power through sin and forgiveness. He diagnoses the band as often stuck in Nietzsche's incomplete nihilism - 'To Live is to Die' longs nostalgically for the Kingdom of Salvation - while 'Escape' and the sheer creative power of the music show a genuine Nietzschean transvaluation and overcoming of Christianity.

master-slave-morality.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
master-slave-morality.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
master-slave-morality.relation: Uses Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals to explain why viewers root for SAMCRO's criminals: the Sons embody master morality, the warrior virtues of strength, boldness, and reverence for worthy enemies—seen in Jax's elaborate trap that gets Jimmy O killed and Opie executes Stahl in the Season 3 finale, and in Clay sparing Marcus Alvarez. Agent Stahl personifies ressentiment: after Otto disfigures her she vows 'I'm gonna bury these assholes,' dressing revenge as justice and respecting no one, while principled 'good guys' like Potter and Deputy Chief Hale internalize the slave morality of equality and sympathy. The lambs-and-birds-of-prey passage frames our unease at Jax dismissing Tig's murder of an unarmed woman as 'collateral damage,' and the chapter ends by weighing whether a world without noble 'blond beasts' like Jax would be Nietzsche's tragedy.

master-slave-morality.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
master-slave-morality.title: 7. How Batman Cowed a God
master-slave-morality.relation: Reider reads Batman as Nietzsche's aristocratic 'good' man — pagan wrath and vengeance without shame, his no-kill rule in Under the Red Hood mere pride, like Achilles dragging Hector's body — and Superman as the unwitting pawn of slave morality, his Kent-farm humility, guilt, and protect-the-weak ethos the very values the resentful revolt installed. The provocation: a god whose morality favors the weak may secretly wish to be overcome, so the imagined confrontation where Batman growls 'follow the plan or I'll take you out myself' lets Superman feel happily, honestly human again — which is also why Wonder Woman pursues Batman and Clark pines for the domineering Lois.

master-slave-morality.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
master-slave-morality.title: Notes
master-slave-morality.relation: Takes Nietzsche's 'man is the cruelest animal' and argues the show's real exploration of cruelty lies not in the cult's crimes, which stay mysterious, but in the Cohle–Hart relationship, whose private cruelties are closer to the human condition. It explains human cruelty through theory of mind — knowing we make others suffer — and through the moral vocabulary of desert, karma, and Schadenfreude (Nietzsche's slave morality inventing hell) that hides our pleasure in suffering, which Nietzsche sees as the key to life-affirmation against Buddhist and Christian world-denial. The chapter maps Hart as Dionysian energy and Cohle as Apollonian form, and reads Rust's 2012 talk of eternal recurrence as a ruse concealing his search for a Nietzschean moment of ecstatic affirmation of all the cruelty he has caused and endured.

master-slave-morality.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
master-slave-morality.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
master-slave-morality.relation: Rard tests whether any morality survives the apocalypse with an objective basis: Plato's Forms fail to capture changing facts (Hannah the bicycle girl decaying from mom to walker) and white lies, and Aristotle's function-based virtue ethics proves too relative and luck-dependent for survivors like Rick (rashness at Carl's shooting) and Shane (courage fetching supplies, rage at the barn). Nietzsche then supplies the frame: Hershel's barn of pitied 'sick people' is Christian slave morality that guilts the strong, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and forcing open of the barn doors grope toward a master morality 'for the Walker Age' without ever achieving nobility. Rick alone approaches the higher type, refusing to judge Lori's affair, insisting the baby be born, and embracing the post-walker world as one he would choose again.

master-slave-morality.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
master-slave-morality.title: Friendship, Rivalry, and Excellence
master-slave-morality.relation: The chapter uses Aristotle's three friendships (pleasure, usefulness, virtue) to ask how tennis rivals competing for one prize can be friends, illustrating pleasure with Borg and Gerulaitis, usefulness with the tense but genuine Ashe-McEnroe Davis Cup bond, and virtue with the Evert-Navratilova rivalry that grew into deep mutual care despite a competitive women's tour. It adds C. S. Lewis's view that friends stand side by side absorbed in a shared thing, then reads Jimmy Connors as a Nietzschean Ubermensch whose master-morality drive to dominate makes him, paradoxically, the best 'star friend' by pushing rivals to their limits. It closes unresolved on whether the tension between friendship and rivalry can ever be eliminated.

master-slave-morality.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
master-slave-morality.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
master-slave-morality.relation: Gilmore reads Unforgiven as Socratic wisdom done in images — the recognition that we do not know what we really want. He analyzes the opening montage (shadowed windows, the cut prostitute) as Freud's Primal Scene, the audience forced to interpret sex and violence without adequate concepts, which he calls the primal scene of philosophy itself. Drawing on Huizinga's Homo Ludens and Leone's Once Upon a Time in the West, he frames the gunslinger as a 'Bad Man at play' for mortal stakes, free of the repressions civilization demands. William Munny's banal Christianized 'goodness' versus the terrifying Bad Man that drink releases dramatizes Thoreau's 'quiet desperation' and a godless world where deserving is irrelevant.

master-slave-morality.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
master-slave-morality.title: “Takin’ ’er Easy for All Us Sinners” Laziness as a Virtue in The Big Lebowski
master-slave-morality.relation: Douglass and Walls read the Dude's 'principled laziness' as a coherent ethos and test it against the film's rival worldviews: the villains' hollow nihilism (which they distinguish from Nietzsche's will to power and death-of-God), Bunny's Aristippan hedonism versus Epicurus, the Big Lebowski's Nietzschean master-morality egoism, and Walter Sobchak's rules-worship read through Kant's categorical imperative and Locke's social contract. They argue dude-ism works as a personal path to contentment but, lacking any objective standard, cannot condemn true evil like Bunny's threatened murder, exposing its purposeless-universe premise as its real flaw.

master-slave-morality.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
master-slave-morality.title: Chaos, Order, and Morality Nietzsche’s Influence on Full Metal Jacket Mark T. Conard
master-slave-morality.relation: Conard argues Full Metal Jacket dramatizes Nietzsche's flux metaphysics: reality is ceaseless becoming with no fixed identities, so Sergeant Hartman's attempt to erase the recruits' individuality (shaved heads, nicknames, identical drills) is a doomed imposition of order on chaos. Private Pyle, who alone keeps his real name and uniqueness, embodies the folly of that project; his murder of Hartman and suicide unleash the chaos of the film's Vietnam half. Reading collapsed oppositions (combatant/civilian, male/female, sacred/profane) and Hartman's 'God has a hard-on for marines' line, Conard concludes that in a Nietzschean world after the death of God, absolutist morality fails and not all killings are alike—Joker's mercy killing of the sniper being humane where Pyle's is senseless.

master-slave-morality.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
master-slave-morality.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
master-slave-morality.relation: Hibbs argues that nihilism, a working assumption in neo-noir, turns the noir protagonist's quests pointless, absurd, and thus comic, and that the Coen brothers exemplify this comic response. Using Nietzsche on nihilism, the 'last man', the 'pathos of distance', and aristocratic self-creation, he reads films like The Silence of the Lambs and Cape Fear as celebrating the 'super-antihero'. The Big Lebowski comically levels nihilism (Walter: the German nihilists are 'cowards'; nihilism cannot be lived), while Fargo and Raising Arizona affirm family and fertility, a 'banality of goodness' answering Arendt's banality of evil, letting nature's comedy perpetuate itself.

master-slave-morality.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
master-slave-morality.title: From Dollars to Iron The Currency of Clint Eastwood's Westerns
master-slave-morality.relation: McNaron traces Clint Eastwood's evolving western hero from the amoral 'Man with No Name' to The Outlaw Josey Wales, using Will Wright's plot typology plus Nietzsche, Aristotle, and Kierkegaard. He reads the Eastwood antihero's 'manly nihilism' and prizing of strength and style through Nietzsche's master/slave morality and perspectivism, his virtues (self-control, phronesis) through Aristotle, and his elevation of the aesthetic over the ethical/religious against Kierkegaard's stages. The film's central claim—that only words with 'iron' behind them (Josey and Ten Bears's pact) can found genuine community, unlike government's 'double tongues'—grounds a transcendental argument about the conditions for authentic community and justified vengeance.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 1. How to De-Nazify Nietzsche’s Philosophical Anthropology
master-slave-morality.relation: Golomb argues the Nazi reading of the will to power as military conquest confuses Nietzsche's Macht (sublimated spiritual power) with Kraft (brute force) and Gewalt (violence), showing through Human, All Too Human and Daybreak that self-overcoming and creative sublimation, not domination, define the Übermensch. He builds a typology of 'positive' versus 'negative' power in which the anti-Semite figures as the vengeful, ressentiment-driven 'slave,' and insists Nietzsche's morality is not naturalistic—power must be transfigured by self-education—so his anthropology stands beyond the eugenic and racial distinctions central to Nazi ideology, even in the misused 'blond beast' passage.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 2. Misinterpretation as the Author’s Responsibility (Nietzsche’s fascism, for instance)
master-slave-morality.relation: Berel Lang asks whether an author is responsible for being misinterpreted, defining a 'Fascist Minimum' (priority of the state over the individual, plus natural inequality asserted through war) and testing Nietzsche against it. He finds Nietzsche flatly rejects the first condition—his 'coldest of all cold monsters' attacks on the state and nationalism—and accepts the second only with heavy qualification. Lang locates Nietzsche's partial culpability in a 'Fallacy of Composition' by which readers like Bäumler transposed individual will to power onto the collective state, arguing that Nietzsche, foreseeing this abuse, chose not to 'build a fence' around his meaning and so bears responsibility 'up to a point.'

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 4. Nietzsche and “Hitler”
master-slave-morality.relation: Nehamas puts 'Hitler' in scare-quotes to pose an abstract problem—does Nietzsche's ideal of nobility permit the evil hero?—rooting it in the Greek notion of aretê and Plato's Republic. He argues Nietzsche's own doctrine that 'there is no doer behind the deed' (Genealogy I:13) collapses the split between noble soul and noble action, so that deeds confer status; using the case of the police torturing a random woman and the fortuitousness of the Jews' extermination, he contends that when what separates us from victims is mere accident we are their peers, and Nietzsche needs the very doer/deed distinction he attacks in order to reject morality absolutely, so his refusal to condemn the evil hero can be refuted on Nietzschean grounds.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 5. Nietzsche and the Jews
master-slave-morality.relation: Brinker surveys Duffy-Mittelman, Santaniello, and Yovel to argue that reading Nietzsche as simply pro-Jewish oversimplifies a genuine ambivalence toward the 'Jewish race' running through all periods of Jewish history. He shows that in The Antichrist Nietzsche separates ressentiment from decadence: Jesus is the 'most perfect decadent' incapable of hatred, while Paul and the priests embody ressentiment, and the Jews, being too strong to be decadent, cunningly poison their conquerors with a faith they do not share—an old anti-Semitic stereotype transplanted into new soil. Brinker concludes this ambivalence, plus Nietzsche's post-Zarathustra equation of equality, democracy, and socialism with slave-morality decadence, is exactly what let the Nazis manipulate him.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 6. Nietzsche contra Wagner on the Jews
master-slave-morality.relation: Yovel reads Nietzsche's break with Wagner as a self-overcoming that freed him to hand Wagner's redemptive role—catalyst of a new Dionysian Europe—to the modern secular Jews Wagner despised. He maps a structured ambivalence: fierce anti-anti-Semitism (grounded philosophically in Nietzsche's rejection of nationalism, racism, the state-cult, and ressentiment) coexisting with a fierce critique of ancient 'priestly' Judaism as the genealogical root of Christian slave morality. Contrasting Nietzsche with Wagner's Judaism in Music, he shows Wagner legitimized public hate-speech (dramatized in Siegfried's gratuitous loathing of Mime) while Nietzsche prized self-mastery, so the two men's later Nazi abuse—by Elisabeth and Winifred, the two 'women-priests'—rests on opposite relations to what each actually held.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 7. Between the Cross and the Swastika A Nietzschean Perspective
master-slave-morality.relation: Wistrich answers the charge that Nietzsche was a philosophical godfather of fascism by marshalling his biography and letters—the 'shoot all anti-Semites' twilight notes, the rupture with the anti-Semite Förster and with Wagner, the praise of Heine, Offenbach, and Spinoza. He distinguishes Nietzsche's demonization of Christianity and priestly Judaism as the 'slave revolt in morals' from his admiration for biblical and Diaspora Jews as Europe's toughest race and a possible catalyst of the Übermensch, arguing that the Nazi and Hitlerian echoes (via Table Talk and Rosenberg's forgeries) grossly distort a 'good European' who denounced nationalism, racism, and the state-cult, and would have been repelled by the swastika.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 8. Ecce Caesar Nietzsche’s Imperial Aspirations
master-slave-morality.relation: Conway argues Nietzsche was not fascism's father but its 'godfather': openly contemptuous of nationalism and anti-Semitism, yet sharing its primal impulses. He reconstructs Nietzsche's fantasy of reviving a Roman-style pan-European empire (the 'new ruling caste' of Beyond Good and Evil), reading his admiration for Pilate's 'noble scorn'—'one Jew more or less, what does it matter?'—as Nietzsche's own ventriloquized wish to assimilate and neutralize the Jews he both needed and feared as the arch-enemies of empire. The chapter ties this imperial will to power and revaluation of noble-versus-slave values to Nietzsche's ambivalent Judeophobia, showing his cosmopolitanism was shallower than he claimed.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 10. The Elisabeth Legend The Cleansing of Nietzsche and the Sullying of His Sister
master-slave-morality.relation: Holub dismantles the postwar 'Elisabeth legend' by which Schlechta, Kaufmann and Roos scapegoated Förster-Nietzsche to rehabilitate Nietzsche from his fascist reputation. Examining her actual forgeries and biographical writings, he shows they never made Nietzsche more nationalist or anti-Semitic—indeed she consistently and accurately recorded his opposition to anti-Semitism and was herself not a biological racist. He concludes the responsibility lies with Nietzsche himself: his praise of war, cruelty, hierarchy, slavery and European hegemony, and his rhetorical hyperbole, made his thought genuinely susceptible to Nazi appropriation.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 11. Nietzsche, Mussolini, and Italian Fascism
master-slave-morality.relation: Sznajder examines how Nietzsche entered Italian Fascism through two bridging figures. Gabriele D'Annunzio relocated Nietzsche from philosophy into literature, staged the 'Übermensch' and 'live dangerously' as an aesthetic politics at Fiume and in the Carta del Carnaro, aestheticizing mass politics in ways fascism inherited. Mussolini, reading Beyond Good and Evil and the Genealogy from his socialist years, seized on the will to power, transvaluation and anti-egalitarian elitism (Rome undone by 'the pale Jews') as a virile theory of revolution. The chapter stresses the paradox that official fascism never listed the individualist, anti-statist Nietzsche as a godfather even as his vocabulary pervaded it.

master-slave-morality.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
master-slave-morality.title: 14. Critique as Apologetics Nolte’s Interpretation of Nietzsche
master-slave-morality.relation: Stackelberg critiques Ernst Nolte's essentialist reading, in which Nietzsche's Ecce Homo 'party of life' and its call for the 'ruthless destruction of all that is degenerate' furnish the counter-concept of extermination mirroring Marx, dignifying fascism as an anti-Bolshevik European civil war. He shows Nolte must explain away Nietzsche's denunciations of anti-Semitism, nationalism, the Reich and Wagner, and counters that Nazism was itself a moralistic 'slave revolt'—the ascetic, purity-seeking mentality Nietzsche attacked—so that Nietzsche's real susceptibility to Nazi use lies in his shared anti-egalitarian enemies and his refusal of concrete social analysis, not in an exterminatory program.

master-slave-morality.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
master-slave-morality.title: Metallica, Nihilism, and Nostalgia
master-slave-morality.relation: Peter Fosl reads Metallica lyrics through Nietzsche's and Marx's critiques of Christianity: 'Leper Messiah' and 'The God that Failed' cast religion as a slave morality born of ressentiment and as Marx's 'opium' that pacifies the exploited. He asks whether Metallica achieves Nietzsche's transvaluation of values or stays trapped in 'incomplete nihilism' - songs like 'One' and 'To Live is to Die' longing nostalgically for the God that failed - while 'Escape' and 'The Four Horsemen' point toward a life-affirming overcoming of Christianity.

master-slave-morality.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
master-slave-morality.title: “They Have a Plan”
master-slave-morality.relation: Robert Sharp maps Battlestar Galactica's Cylon uprising onto Nietzsche's slave revolt in morality. The enslaved Cylons, like Nietzsche's early Christians under Rome, invent the concept of a soul and a single loving God to invert their masters' master morality, turning powerlessness (meekness, equality, faith) into virtue. Through Leoben's preaching to Starbuck and the Cylons' commune-like equality versus the Colonials' Greek-style polytheistic hierarchy, Sharp shows the powerless creating new values out of resentment to overturn those in power.

master-slave-morality.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
master-slave-morality.title: Chapter 14 Moral Value and Moral Psychology in Twain’s “Carnival of Crime”
master-slave-morality.relation: Boardman treats Twain's 'The Facts Concerning the Recent Carnival of Crime in Connecticut'—in which a narrator kills his personified conscience (a shabby dwarf) and gleefully commits a spree of crimes—as staging an 'exasperating metaphysical question' about the value and psychology of morality. On a Nietzschean reading the narrator becomes an Overman revaluing values, seeing conscience as the internalized lie of slave morality; on a Humean reading conscience is moral feeling (not reason), so once it is destroyed the narrator can still reason about right yet has no motive to act morally, illustrating the oak-tree and willful-murder arguments that vice lies in sentiment, not relations or facts. Boardman concludes both interpretations fit yet neither settles whether Twain endorses or lampoons the result—our horror at the crimes is what makes the story funny.

master-slave-morality.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
master-slave-morality.title: 8. Star Wars
master-slave-morality.relation: Rowlands reads Star Wars as Manichaean (light vs dark side of the Force) and contrasts it with Plato, for whom evil is merely absence of good and the form of the good is most real, an idea Augustine (via Plotinus) folded into Christianity. Siding with Lucas that Darth Vader's evil is palpably real, he then uses Nietzsche's 'Dionysus against the Crucified': the Christian strategy represses drives (Freudian repression), the 'hippy' strategy merely expresses them, but greatness requires sublimation into higher forms. Vader taps his dark side but fails to sublimate, so he is a flawed unbalanced megalomaniac (like Nietzsche's Borgia/Napoleon), not a true Ubermensch living life as art.

master-slave-morality.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
master-slave-morality.title: Metallica, Nihilism, and Nostalgia
master-slave-morality.relation: Fosl argues that Metallica's lyrics echo Nietzsche's and Marx's moral critiques of Christianity: songs like "Leper Messiah" and "The God that Failed" cast religion as slave-morality ressentiment, mind-control, and Marx's "opium of the people." He then asks whether the band achieves a Nietzschean transvaluation or lapses into the very nihilism Nietzsche said Christianity breeds — reading "To Live is to Die" and "One" as nostalgic death-wish, but "Escape" and "The Four Horsemen" as genuine defiant self-overcoming after the death of God.

master-slave-morality.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
master-slave-morality.title: “They Have a Plan”
master-slave-morality.relation: Sharp maps Battlestar Galactica's Cylon uprising onto Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: the enslaved Cylons, like Nietzsche's early Christians under Rome, invent a slave morality that inverts their masters' values, condemning human pride and greed while exalting a single loving God, souls, and equality. He shows Leoben preaching the soul to Starbuck and the Cylons' consensus-based commune as the powerless revaluing weakness into virtue, converting their polytheistic, master-moral human creators much as Christianity converted Rome.

ressentiment.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
ressentiment.title: 5 - Thus Spake Bart On Nietzsche and the Virtues of Being Bad
ressentiment.relation: Mark Conard asks whether Bart could be a Nietzschean ideal, tracing Nietzsche's path from Schopenhauer's will/representation split in The Birth of Tragedy—where art redeems us from the horror of existence, with Lisa cast as the Socratic theoretical optimist whose reason never fixes Springfield's absurdity—to the later view that there is no 'being behind the doing', a condition cartoons embody perfectly since Bart is nothing but the sum of his misdeeds. He explains master and slave morality, with Nelson's bullying as master morality and the slaves' ressentiment inventing 'evil', before concluding Bart fails as Übermensch: he defines himself only reactively against authority, as Lisa diagnoses in the Brad Goodman episode, and collapses when the repressive milieu disappears. Bart thus exemplifies the post-Nietzschean danger of nihilism, though the show itself may perform the artistic 'discharge of the nausea of absurdity' Nietzsche praised in Greek comedy.

ressentiment.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
ressentiment.title: Persuasion As Drama
ressentiment.relation: Karl Schudt contends that Nietzsche's genealogy of slave morality cannot be refuted by reason (Nietzsche denies reason itself), so drama must persuade where dialectic cannot: a believable story of a Nietzschean life acts as an empathic experiment. Faith is constructed as the Nietzschean ideal — strong, healthy, ruthless ('Find a couple of studs, use them, and discard them'), dismissive of reflection ('You think too much') — serving Mayor Wilkins, whom Schudt reads as a genuine Übermensch sacrificing mankind's mass for his ascension. Watching her world collapse (the accidental killing in 'Bad Girls', her mirror scene in 'Who Are You?', the torture of Wesley and confession on Angel) gives viewers an Aristotelian pity-and-fear warning that the unjust life ends badly, completing her 'leap from Nietzsche to Socrates.'

ressentiment.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
ressentiment.title: The Gift of Baseball
ressentiment.relation: McDaniels reads the Negro Leagues through Nietzsche's account of resentment as revolt and Cornel West's tragic philosophy of resistance: excluded from the white majors after Cap Anson's 1887 stand against George Stovey, black players converted resentment into counter-narratives of excellence, with Satchel Paige, Josh Gibson, and Buck O'Neil showboating and clowning in the tradition of plantation dance, gallows humor, and the blues. The call-and-response sermon scene from The Bingo Long Traveling All-Stars & Motor Kings — Bingo Long on the mound answered by the crowd like a black church congregation — shows performance as ritual that sustains community, while bell hooks's 'absence of presence' frames remembering as resistance to hegemonic definitions of race. The chapter closes with the author's grandfather, for whom Robinson, Aaron, Mays, and Paige proved with every pitch 'We're American Too.'

ressentiment.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
ressentiment.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Argues the show's underlying moral vision is Nietzschean passive nihilism filtered through film noir. Tony, unlike the active nihilist who converts value-collapse into self-overcoming, sinks into resentment and life-negation: he wants to rip the throat of the 'happy wanderer', therapy never redeems him, and he quits it with 'I'm a fat fucking crook from New Jersey' in 'Calling All Cars'. The chapter traces the noir lineage (Tony watching White Heat, the Godfather references, Bogart imagery at Satriale's) and reads A.J.'s 'D-Girl' existentialism (Camus's The Stranger, 'There is no God') and Livia's 'It's all a big nothing' as the family inheritance of meaninglessness and death-dread.

ressentiment.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
ressentiment.title: Why Are the X-Men Good
ressentiment.relation: Systematically rejects candidate explanations of the X-Men's goodness: not self-interested calculation (the world's hostility undercuts it, blunting Magneto's argument), not innate constitution (Magneto chose otherwise, and the Cyclops–Wolverine–Jean Grey triangle shows ordinary desires), not fear of punishment, and not Nietzschean pity or herd resentment — the X-Men are the strong and healthy ones. The chapter's positive account: love of the good is learned through relationships with those who are good to us, from Xavier's loving school that gradually transforms Wolverine and Magneto's Nazi-scarred past to Peter Parker's formative upbringing by Uncle Ben and Aunt May.

ressentiment.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
ressentiment.title: Tarantula’s End
ressentiment.relation: Goldblatt and Necarsulmer pair Dylan's Tarantula with Nietzsche's "The Tarantulas" from Zarathustra: both are books of advice, renaming, and stream-of-consciousness flow whose sections cohere through signature and attitude rather than narrative (the same Foucauldian author function). Both embody the intuitive artist of Plato's Ion and Nietzsche's Ecce Homo - the poet as medium whose language arrives as inspiration, all language being fresh or stale metaphor. Tarantula's vengeful vignettes and "Idiot Wind" dramatize the ressentiment Zarathustra warns against, its impenetrable juxtapositions ("harmonica battalions," "funeral landlord") work as Derridean catachresis - metaphor whose transfer fails yet exerts aesthetic force - and the book's dream of the burning tenement leaves Dylan unable, and absolved, to look back.

ressentiment.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
ressentiment.title: Getting Right with Brian (Just in Case)
ressentiment.relation: Reads Life of Brian through Nietzsche's madman: the crowd's laughter at Brian's market sermons ('consider the lilies... have the birds got jobs?') enacts the death of the cheerless, pathos-soaked God, with Brian as a sincere 'divine idiot' who escapes ressentiment by falling idiotically below the dialectic rather than rising above it as an Übermensch. Bergson's account of the comic — rigidity invisible to its bearer, 'as though wearing the ring of Gyges with reverse effect' — explains why the Pythons' straight men, British class consciousness, and the Roman/British empires ('Romani ite domum,' the centurion's Latin lesson) are funny, and why Britons and Romans can laugh at themselves while Americans cannot. Pivoting from Jorge's war on laughter in Eco's The Name of the Rose, the chapter closes with a Pascal's-wager parody: having laughed at Brian, you have already wagered your immortal soul on God being British — the sort of God who can take a joke.

ressentiment.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
ressentiment.title: Philosophy versus Bullshit
ressentiment.relation: The chapter claims that 'equal respect' in modern democracies has been distorted into a 'dumbing-up' relativism — 'I'm valid, you're valid' — which conflates the equal right to voice opinions with their equal intellectual merit and so leaves nothing that counts as bullshit. It illustrates this through the 'democratization of expertise' and management-speak ('downsizing', 'mission statements'), which mimics profundity while evading awkward facts, and it tests and rejects the quasi-Nietzschean ressentiment story of timid citizens dragging discourse down to a common denominator. To get the full measure of the phenomenon it expands Frankfurt's and Cohen's typologies into seven kinds of bullshit, adding clarifiable unclarity, plain rubbish, irretrievable speculation, pretension, and evasion.

ressentiment.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
ressentiment.title: Metallica, Nihilism, and Nostalgia
ressentiment.relation: Peter Fosl reads Metallica's lyrics ("Leper Messiah," "The God That Failed," "One," "To Live Is to Die," "Escape") as extending Nietzsche's and Marx's critiques of Christianity: religion as slave morality born of ressentiment and as opium deadening the oppressed, illustrated by the landmine veteran of "One" pleading with a silent God and Hetfield's abandoned-childhood grief. He argues the band often falls into the "incomplete nihilism" Nietzsche predicted, lamenting God's failure and longing nostalgically for the Christian meaning it can no longer believe in rather than transvaluating values. Yet the defiance of "The Four Horsemen" and "Escape" and the band's creative power show it also working toward an overcoming of Christian nihilism, confirmed for Fosl by Hetfield's post-rehab health.

ressentiment.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
ressentiment.title: “They Have a Plan”
ressentiment.relation: Robert Sharp reads the Cylon uprising in Battlestar Galactica as Nietzsche's slave revolt in morality: enslaved by humans, the Cylons react with resentment and overturn their masters' values, just as early Christians did under Rome. The humans keep a master morality (Colonial polytheism, warrior elites, call signs like Apollo and Athena), while Cylon monotheism, doctrines of the soul (Leoben's sermons to Starbuck, Gina's suicidal faith), equality, and consensus government reproduce slave morality's move from bodily weakness to spiritual superiority. The New Caprica occupation debate among the Cavils, Six, and Boomer, and D'Anna's boxing, show the former slaves seeking not just destruction but conversion of their masters to a religion that makes Cylons equal.

ressentiment.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
ressentiment.title: Are We Going Too Far
ressentiment.relation: David Kyle Johnson distinguishes revenge (personal, emotional, unlimited) from retribution and argues that 'Tarantino's view'—mercy should be common practice yet revenge can be justified—is consistent: Jules buys Pumpkin and Honey Bunny's lives but never waives a right of vengeance, since they never wronged him. He tests the view against Bushido, showing Beatrix's revolt against her lord Bill violates the samurai code, and against karma, which makes revenge unnecessary. After finding that Hobbes, Locke, Nietzsche and Socrates all leave revenge's justification open, he defends it—citing Budd's 'that woman deserves her revenge'—so long as the punishment fits the crime and spares innocents, as when Beatrix refuses to make herself even by killing Vernita's daughter Nikki.

ressentiment.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
ressentiment.title: Meaning The Final Frontier
ressentiment.relation: Biderman and Devlin read The Wrath of Khan as a Nietzschean test of whether revenge can ground a meaningful life after the death of God: Kirk, stuck 'flying a goddamn computer console' as an admiral, and the Genesis project seek meaning through creation without God, while Khan, broken by exile on Ceti Alpha V, chooses vengeance. Using Nozick's contrast between impartial retribution and personally satisfying revenge, and Nietzsche's will to power, master-slave morality, and ressentiment, they argue Khan had the superhuman gifts and independence from herd morality of a candidate Overman, but let revenge enslave him — culminating in Genesis turned weapon and his dying 'For hate's sake . . . I spit my last breath at thee,' a resounding No to life. Spock's mirror-image self-sacrifice, which affirms life, is offered as the better Nietzschean Overman.

ressentiment.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
ressentiment.title: What Mr. Colbert Has Taught Us (Besides Everything)
ressentiment.relation: In full truthiness voice, Michaud explains Colbert's failed 2008 presidential run — the South Carolina Democratic Executive Council's 13-3 vote keeping him off the ballot — as exactly what Nietzsche predicted: the resentful weak, the 'sheep,' hold the super-man down by redefining meekness as strength. He walks through will-to-power as self-overcoming, the lambs-and-birds-of-prey parable from the Genealogy, and Christianity as slave morality, then 'corrects' Nietzsche by relocating slave morality in the liberal media rather than God, ending with Colbert as the man of the future who 'affirms life without resentment.'

ressentiment.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
ressentiment.title: The Will to Nothingness, or What Happens when the Red Sox Win
ressentiment.relation: Nolen Gertz runs the Sox-Yankees rivalry through Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morals: the Steinbrenner Yankees are masters whose 'good' simply means strong and winning, while Sox fans are slaves whose 'Yankees suck!' is ressentiment's imaginary revenge, intensified into the most spiritual and poisonous hatred by eighty-six years of impotence. The priestly slaves defeated the masters by cleverness rather than force, mirrored when Epstein's sabermetric 'religion' of prospects and projections terrified the Yankees into converting, building a farm system and embracing the slavish virtues they had scorned. The final twist is Nietzsche's will to nothingness: once the masters fell in 2004 the fans' suffering lost its meaning, breeding bandwagon guilt, pink-hat resentment and nihilistic exhaustion, so freedom requires a transvaluation that lets fans simply enjoy watching baseball.

ressentiment.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
ressentiment.title: Life A Celebration
ressentiment.relation: Reads John Simm's Master as Nietzsche's most advanced nihilist: having seen the universe die at Utopia, he judges life valueless and converts ressentiment into a joyful will to nothingness, dancing to the Scissor Sisters over his victims. The Ninth Doctor's arc in 'Dalek' mirrors this danger ('What are you changing into?') until he refuses to destroy the last Dalek, beginning his yes-saying to finite life. Following Deleuze's reading, the Doctor defeats the Master not with Martha's gun but with forgiveness ('I forgive you') and her storytelling network, embodying the Übermensch who carries his affirmation into the abyss of the end of the universe.

ressentiment.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
ressentiment.title: Psych and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Malloy maps Nietzsche's three metamorphoses onto Shawn's life: the camel who carried Henry's burdensome training and the expectation he become a cop, the lion who slew the dragon 'Thou shalt' by stealing a car at eighteen and ending Henry's dream, and the child who creates his own values of fun, laughter, and silliness - defended as genuinely Nietzschean since the Overman must overcome the 'spirit of gravity.' Gus and Lassiter figure as last men, the herd animals Shawn manipulates and pities (Lassie's literal crap list a study in ressentiment), while only Pierre Despereaux and Mr. Yin count as true rivals because only fellow Overmen, forging values beyond good and evil, can genuinely challenge Shawn. The chapter closes on the Overman's dilemma - loneliness, backsliding into the herd, or trying to make Overmen of others - which explains why Shawn treats his friends and enemies the way he does.

ressentiment.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
ressentiment.title: Psych and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Ruiz casts Lassiter as Nietzsche's slave - his worth defined reactively against Shawn, his advice that 'all romance ends in despair or death' reproducing the Judeo-Christian slave revolt in morality that turned weakness into virtue - and Shawn as the master, a self-propelled wheel who bakes a pineapple cake in an Easy Bake oven for nineteen hours whether or not anyone is watching. Shawn's generosity (helping the wrongly accused, the ghost-struck, and the deluded, once even crediting a cat with solving murders in '9 Lives') is read as the noble overflow of superabundant power rather than pity, and his hostage-saving risk-taking as will to power understood as self-mastery. Even the central lie gets a dialectical reading - like art, pretending to be psychic reveals the truth hidden behind appearances - though the chapter concedes Shawn's slavish moments, from daddy issues to his obsession with one-upping Declan in 'Shawn 2.0.'

ressentiment.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
ressentiment.title: Futurama and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Piven argues Zapp Brannigan's 'sexlexia' - his deluded velour-and-spanking seductions of Leela and his relief at finding Lee Lemon is a woman - typifies a whole cast of clueless lovers (Fry coaching Zoidberg's courtship of Edna, Morgan Proctor's mess fetish, Bender coldly dumping the Planet Express ship in 'Love and Rocket'). Kant's condemnation of masturbation as self-abuse that throws away one's personality and violates humanity in one's own person is exposed as unsupported prejudice, and Nietzsche's claim that morality projects fear, envy, and disgust onto the despised other explains why 'perversion' is an arbitrary cultural judgment. Freud, Stoller, and McDougall then recast perversion as unconscious flight from anxiety and death, so the show's kink - up to the Monsterpus of The Beast with a Billion Backs and Amy's 'general sluttiness' - mirrors our own sexlexia and existential dread.

ressentiment.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
ressentiment.title: Girls and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Sirvent and Avery take Shoshanna's Listen, Ladies! advice book to ask whether rules can govern romance, contrasting Kantian rule-duty ethics (Ray's dating rules that are 'not commandments') with Bentham-Mill utilitarian calculation (Jessa's 'depends on the virgin'). Kierkegaard and Nietzsche - extended through Žižek's Lacanian 'Big Other' of God, Duty, or Utility - show such impersonal systems let us dodge responsibility: Jessa plays Kierkegaard's aesthete escaping boredom, while Hannah's 'just to be an asshole' boss seduction and the Marnie-Elijah hookup express ressentiment and self-hatred. Their positive proposal is Aristotelian virtue ethics - becoming a certain kind of person - completed by Butler's Undoing Gender: to be ethical you must risk being 'undone by each other,' as Adam demands of Hannah ('You don't wanna know me').

ressentiment.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
ressentiment.title: 7. How Batman Cowed a God
ressentiment.relation: Reider reads the two heroes through Nietzsche's genealogy of morals: Superman's humility, guilt, empathy, and farmer-parent values (he is Clark Kent at heart, keeping the alter ego to unload the burden of his power) are textbook slave morality, making him the unwitting pawn of the weak rather than Nietzsche's Übermensch, while Batman's pride, wrath, and vow of vengeance - he refuses to kill the Joker or Robin's attacker not from respect for life but from aristocratic pride - revive the pagan "good" of Achilles dragging Hector's body. From this he builds a deliberately provocative strategic claim: because slave morality leaves Superman secretly craving to be bested and made ordinary again, the merely human Batman can stare down and "cow" the god in their showdowns, winning the psychological war Wonder Woman's and Lois's preferences supposedly confirm.

ressentiment.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
ressentiment.title: 7. David Bowie, Political Philosopher
ressentiment.relation: Hill reconstructs Bowie's political odyssey as a working-out of what freedom and oppression are: 'Cygnet Committee' repudiates revolution powered by resentment (echoing Nietzsche on socialism's despotic annihilation of the individual), 'Big Brother' and Diamond Dogs diagnose the crowd's flight from freedom into leadership, and the Nietzschean self-as-artwork - 'give style to one's character,' the 'mortal with potential of a superman' - curdles into the Thin White Duke's 'rock stars are fascists' collapse of celebrity into totalitarian leadership. The Berlin Trilogy then turns the critique inward: 'Heroes'' ironic lovers unmask romantic anti-totalitarianism (either side of the Antifaschistischer Schutzwall), 'Neuköln' discovers immigrants' mere survival, and Lodger's 'Fantastic Voyage' lands on structural, Marxist questions of how 'we' are to become free.

ressentiment.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
ressentiment.title: 4. He’s a Hero in a Bottle, Baby
ressentiment.relation: Insooks deploys Nietzsche to argue Iron Man is the better hero: Cap's prized humility and relatability are sheep morality, the resentful herd value that drags the excellent down to average (as when society savored the Olympic swimmer's fall), while Tony honestly owns his superiority and keeps self-overcoming, building ever-better suits rather than resting on a serum gifted in a bottle. On this view Cap's manufactured modesty insults people who genuinely struggle, and the true super hero inspires from the mountaintop - build yourself a suit and get up here - instead of pretending to be just like us.

ressentiment.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
ressentiment.title: 26. Thanos’s Mistake
ressentiment.relation: Argues Thanos embodies Nietzschean master morality — his will as its own justification, 'the hardest choices require the strongest wills,' echoing the Melian dialogue's 'the strong do what they will, the weak suffer what they must,' with Doctor Strange answering in kind ('you'll find our will equal to yours') — while the Avengers speak from slave morality, judging by intentions and branding genocide evil. Thanos's real error, though, is a categorical one: imposing a technical quantity fix (a one-time 50 percent cull) on a social relationship problem, since Hardin's carrying-capacity logic and the St. Matthew Island reindeer show populations must self-limit like apex predators, making his correction a mere stopgap that confuses quantity with relationship.

ressentiment.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
ressentiment.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Reads Bluth contradiction through Kant's categorical imperative: Lindsay's lie about her shopgirl job, Gob's jealousy bred by comparative parenting, and George Michael's conformist drift show both the imperative's force and the danger of its empty formalism, while the 'Afternoon Delight' double entendres test whether good intentions suffice for Kantian worth. Nietzsche then answers that morality itself is the contradiction: virtue manufactured from ressentiment ('weakness is being lied into something meritorious'), the will to power turned inward as nihilism, with self-overcoming and value creation as the exit; Mary Douglas's joke theory closes the chapter by explaining why all this contradiction is comic and why the joke is on Gob.

ressentiment.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
ressentiment.title: Amos Is No Superman
ressentiment.relation: Pankaj Singh reads Amos through Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: Amos' division of people into 'bad ones, ones you follow, and ones you need to protect', his outsourcing of moral judgment to Naomi and Holden ('Naomi wouldn't like it'), his fearlessness, and his violent spontaneity make him 'evil' by slave morality yet good by master morality. Unlike Prax, who has to be stopped from shooting Strickland out of ressentiment, Amos kills without revenge ('I am that guy'), and his fistfights with Miller and Alex discharge hostility immediately so it never poisons — the strong natures Nietzsche praises that 'form, mold, recuperate and forget.' His 'crew comes first' and 'better to go down swinging' express the will to power as discharge of strength rather than mere self-preservation, but because he never sublimates or overcomes his drives, the chapter concludes Amos is no Übermensch — 'but then again, who is?'

ressentiment.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
ressentiment.title: Notes
ressentiment.relation: Argues the Underwoods act out historian James Truslow Adams' warning that the American dream, severed from the question of values, degenerates into a means-first pursuit of power — 'burning the barn to find our penny in the hay'. Using Nietzsche's ressentiment and above all Max Scheler's account of its systematic repression of emotion, the chapter reads Claire's repressed longings for motherhood (the 'What will we leave behind?' scene), integrity and love erupting as spite against those who embody what she sacrificed: firing and persecuting the pregnant Gillian Cole, destroying Adam Galloway, and abandoning Megan Hennessey. Michael Corrigan's suicide in his Russian cell — an integrity she cannot drag down to her level — finally shatters her ressentiment, and the chapter ends with her walking out of the White House as the escape Adams' question demands.

ressentiment.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
ressentiment.title: Notes
ressentiment.relation: Palm and Stikkers read the Underwoods through James Truslow Adams's American dream as a question of values gone rotten: lacking ends, they pursue power for its own sake while repressed longings (Frank's Sentinel camaraderie, song, and friendship; Claire's motherhood — 'What will we leave behind?') erupt as the ressentiment Nietzsche introduced and Max Scheler systematized, hating those who embody the sacrificed values. Claire's hatred thus targets Gillian Cole's pregnancy and integrity (fired, then threatened with letting her child 'wither and die') and Adam Galloway's freedom and love — Scheler's pedestal-smashing pattern — after the slave-morality-like repression of her normal human affects. The ressentiment finally shatters when Michael Corrigan refuses to betray himself and hangs himself in Petrov's cell: Claire tells the cameras the truth and walks out on Frank at the end of Season 3, free of the resentment.

ressentiment.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
ressentiment.title: “Have Done” with the Past
ressentiment.relation: Fritz applies Nietzsche's On the Uses and Disadvantages of History for Life and the Genealogy to the dialectic of remembering and forgetting: Pete cannot 'have done' with anything, so Ken Cosgrove's Atlantic Monthly story and Peggy's promotion become 'vermin' that eat into him, his reactive rancor and entitlement driving him to make Trudy broker his bad talking-bear story. Peggy is the opposite extreme of active forgetting, from not registering her own pregnancy to telling Pete flatly 'I had your baby and I gave it away. I wanted other things,' after Don's hospital advice that 'This never happened. It'll shock you how much this never happened.' Don knows forgetting is the strength of strong natures (the $5,000 offer to Adam, 'my life only goes in one direction, forward'), yet the Carousel's home-movie slides and other external triggers keep forcing the past back on him, so only Peggy fully inhabits the Nietzschean ideal.

ressentiment.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
ressentiment.title: Metallica, Nietzsche, and Marx: The Immorality of Morality
ressentiment.relation: Peter Fosl argues Metallica's moral critique of religion in 'Leper Messiah' and 'The God That Failed' continues Nietzsche's genealogy of Christian slave morality born of ressentiment and Marx's 'opium of the people': religion gathers a docile herd, denies this world, and exercises power through sin and forgiveness. He diagnoses the band as often stuck in Nietzsche's incomplete nihilism - 'To Live is to Die' longs nostalgically for the Kingdom of Salvation - while 'Escape' and the sheer creative power of the music show a genuine Nietzschean transvaluation and overcoming of Christianity.

ressentiment.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
ressentiment.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: Uses Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals to explain why viewers root for SAMCRO's criminals: the Sons embody master morality, the warrior virtues of strength, boldness, and reverence for worthy enemies—seen in Jax's elaborate trap that gets Jimmy O killed and Opie executes Stahl in the Season 3 finale, and in Clay sparing Marcus Alvarez. Agent Stahl personifies ressentiment: after Otto disfigures her she vows 'I'm gonna bury these assholes,' dressing revenge as justice and respecting no one, while principled 'good guys' like Potter and Deputy Chief Hale internalize the slave morality of equality and sympathy. The lambs-and-birds-of-prey passage frames our unease at Jax dismissing Tig's murder of an unarmed woman as 'collateral damage,' and the chapter ends by weighing whether a world without noble 'blond beasts' like Jax would be Nietzsche's tragedy.

ressentiment.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
ressentiment.title: 7. How Batman Cowed a God
ressentiment.relation: Reider reads Batman as Nietzsche's aristocratic 'good' man — pagan wrath and vengeance without shame, his no-kill rule in Under the Red Hood mere pride, like Achilles dragging Hector's body — and Superman as the unwitting pawn of slave morality, his Kent-farm humility, guilt, and protect-the-weak ethos the very values the resentful revolt installed. The provocation: a god whose morality favors the weak may secretly wish to be overcome, so the imagined confrontation where Batman growls 'follow the plan or I'll take you out myself' lets Superman feel happily, honestly human again — which is also why Wonder Woman pursues Batman and Clark pines for the domineering Lois.

ressentiment.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
ressentiment.title: Notes
ressentiment.relation: Uses Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy and Lacan's ethics of psychoanalysis to argue season two failed as tragedy because feminist morality became the inflated 'Good' that blocks the transgression of limits through which Dionysian wisdom is won. Season one works because Rust's philosophy filters the Carcosa horrors without moralizing, whereas season two — failing Aristotle's catharsis model and repeating Euripides' mistake — represses the sexual knowledge troubling Velcoro, Bezzerides, and Woodrugh, so Dionysus returns only as money and violence, as in The Bacchae. Ani's arc is read through Nietzschean ressentiment toward her father and Freud's return of the repressed, with Kantian sexual dignity ('maybe you were put on earth for more than fucking') and the male gaze as the contemporary Good the show never crosses.

ressentiment.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
ressentiment.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
ressentiment.relation: McDaniels reads Tommie Smith and John Carlos's 1968 Mexico City raised-fist protest as an expression of an 'oppositional consciousness' rooted in the memory of slavery and Jim Crow. He deploys Nietzsche's notion of ressentiment, the oppressed sufferer's rebellion against a dominant slave-making morality and need to release rage, and Cornel West's 'prophetic pragmatism', which frames struggle as tragic yet guided by integrity and justice, to interpret the sprinters' silent gesture. He also invokes the athletes' Du Boisian 'twoness' as black athletes and citizens, casting Smith and Carlos in a Douglass-to-Edwards lineage of public dissent as a vehicle of black liberation.

ressentiment.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
ressentiment.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
ressentiment.relation: Palmer reads The Shining through Fredric Jameson's account of postmodernity as a 'perpetual present' that has lost its past and can only cannibalize it as pastiche and nostalgia film. He argues Kubrick's film enacts an 'anti-nostalgia' that invokes the nostalgic impulse—Jack Torrance's wish to escape an empty present into the Overlook's endless 1921 party—only to destroy him with it, refusing the genre's happy-ending wish-fulfillment. Drawing on Baudrillard's image of art 'adrift in a kind of weightlessness' merely 'playing with the pieces,' he casts Jack, endlessly typing 'All work and no play,' as the failed postmodern artist trapped between times, reduced to pointless Nietzschean ressentiment, with the film's Nietzschean death-of-God flux underlying its refusal of stable meaning.

ressentiment.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
ressentiment.title: Life A Celebration
ressentiment.relation: Adam Riggio uses Deleuze's reading of Nietzsche to cast the Simm Master as a nihilist who, having seen the valueless dying universe at Utopia, wills nothingness and universal destruction out of ressentiment. The Doctor is Nietzsche's Overman who overcomes the reactive forces of revenge: in 'Dalek' he recognizes his own vengefulness and turns from it, and in 'Last of the Time Lords' he defeats the Master not with Martha's fake gun but by saying 'I forgive you,' affirming finite life with a 'beneficent Yes-saying' rather than surrendering to enmity.

ressentiment.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ressentiment.title: Introduction
ressentiment.relation: Golomb and Wistrich frame the volume's guiding question—how Nietzsche came to be called the philosopher of the Third Reich—by walking through the 1934 photograph of Hitler before Nietzsche's bust, Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche's and Alfred Bäumler's appropriations, and Mussolini's 'live dangerously' slogan. They argue the Nazi reading rests on a confusion of Nietzsche's spiritual Macht with brute Kraft, and stress his anti-nationalism, anti-anti-Semitism, and admiration for the Jews as future 'creators of values,' concluding he was a prophet of the nihilistic vacuum Nazism filled rather than its godfather.

ressentiment.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ressentiment.title: 5. Nietzsche and the Jews
ressentiment.relation: Brinker surveys Duffy-Mittelman, Santaniello, and Yovel to argue that reading Nietzsche as simply pro-Jewish oversimplifies a genuine ambivalence toward the 'Jewish race' running through all periods of Jewish history. He shows that in The Antichrist Nietzsche separates ressentiment from decadence: Jesus is the 'most perfect decadent' incapable of hatred, while Paul and the priests embody ressentiment, and the Jews, being too strong to be decadent, cunningly poison their conquerors with a faith they do not share—an old anti-Semitic stereotype transplanted into new soil. Brinker concludes this ambivalence, plus Nietzsche's post-Zarathustra equation of equality, democracy, and socialism with slave-morality decadence, is exactly what let the Nazis manipulate him.

ressentiment.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ressentiment.title: 6. Nietzsche contra Wagner on the Jews
ressentiment.relation: Yovel reads Nietzsche's break with Wagner as a self-overcoming that freed him to hand Wagner's redemptive role—catalyst of a new Dionysian Europe—to the modern secular Jews Wagner despised. He maps a structured ambivalence: fierce anti-anti-Semitism (grounded philosophically in Nietzsche's rejection of nationalism, racism, the state-cult, and ressentiment) coexisting with a fierce critique of ancient 'priestly' Judaism as the genealogical root of Christian slave morality. Contrasting Nietzsche with Wagner's Judaism in Music, he shows Wagner legitimized public hate-speech (dramatized in Siegfried's gratuitous loathing of Mime) while Nietzsche prized self-mastery, so the two men's later Nazi abuse—by Elisabeth and Winifred, the two 'women-priests'—rests on opposite relations to what each actually held.

ressentiment.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ressentiment.title: 7. Between the Cross and the Swastika A Nietzschean Perspective
ressentiment.relation: Wistrich answers the charge that Nietzsche was a philosophical godfather of fascism by marshalling his biography and letters—the 'shoot all anti-Semites' twilight notes, the rupture with the anti-Semite Förster and with Wagner, the praise of Heine, Offenbach, and Spinoza. He distinguishes Nietzsche's demonization of Christianity and priestly Judaism as the 'slave revolt in morals' from his admiration for biblical and Diaspora Jews as Europe's toughest race and a possible catalyst of the Übermensch, arguing that the Nazi and Hitlerian echoes (via Table Talk and Rosenberg's forgeries) grossly distort a 'good European' who denounced nationalism, racism, and the state-cult, and would have been repelled by the swastika.

ressentiment.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ressentiment.title: 8. Ecce Caesar Nietzsche’s Imperial Aspirations
ressentiment.relation: Conway argues Nietzsche was not fascism's father but its 'godfather': openly contemptuous of nationalism and anti-Semitism, yet sharing its primal impulses. He reconstructs Nietzsche's fantasy of reviving a Roman-style pan-European empire (the 'new ruling caste' of Beyond Good and Evil), reading his admiration for Pilate's 'noble scorn'—'one Jew more or less, what does it matter?'—as Nietzsche's own ventriloquized wish to assimilate and neutralize the Jews he both needed and feared as the arch-enemies of empire. The chapter ties this imperial will to power and revaluation of noble-versus-slave values to Nietzsche's ambivalent Judeophobia, showing his cosmopolitanism was shallower than he claimed.

ressentiment.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ressentiment.title: 14. Critique as Apologetics Nolte’s Interpretation of Nietzsche
ressentiment.relation: Stackelberg critiques Ernst Nolte's essentialist reading, in which Nietzsche's Ecce Homo 'party of life' and its call for the 'ruthless destruction of all that is degenerate' furnish the counter-concept of extermination mirroring Marx, dignifying fascism as an anti-Bolshevik European civil war. He shows Nolte must explain away Nietzsche's denunciations of anti-Semitism, nationalism, the Reich and Wagner, and counters that Nazism was itself a moralistic 'slave revolt'—the ascetic, purity-seeking mentality Nietzsche attacked—so that Nietzsche's real susceptibility to Nazi use lies in his shared anti-egalitarian enemies and his refusal of concrete social analysis, not in an exterminatory program.

ressentiment.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
ressentiment.title: Metallica, Nihilism, and Nostalgia
ressentiment.relation: Peter Fosl reads Metallica lyrics through Nietzsche's and Marx's critiques of Christianity: 'Leper Messiah' and 'The God that Failed' cast religion as a slave morality born of ressentiment and as Marx's 'opium' that pacifies the exploited. He asks whether Metallica achieves Nietzsche's transvaluation of values or stays trapped in 'incomplete nihilism' - songs like 'One' and 'To Live is to Die' longing nostalgically for the God that failed - while 'Escape' and 'The Four Horsemen' point toward a life-affirming overcoming of Christianity.

ressentiment.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
ressentiment.title: “They Have a Plan”
ressentiment.relation: Robert Sharp maps Battlestar Galactica's Cylon uprising onto Nietzsche's slave revolt in morality. The enslaved Cylons, like Nietzsche's early Christians under Rome, invent the concept of a soul and a single loving God to invert their masters' master morality, turning powerlessness (meekness, equality, faith) into virtue. Through Leoben's preaching to Starbuck and the Cylons' commune-like equality versus the Colonials' Greek-style polytheistic hierarchy, Sharp shows the powerless creating new values out of resentment to overturn those in power.

ressentiment.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
ressentiment.title: Metallica, Nihilism, and Nostalgia
ressentiment.relation: Fosl argues that Metallica's lyrics echo Nietzsche's and Marx's moral critiques of Christianity: songs like "Leper Messiah" and "The God that Failed" cast religion as slave-morality ressentiment, mind-control, and Marx's "opium of the people." He then asks whether the band achieves a Nietzschean transvaluation or lapses into the very nihilism Nietzsche said Christianity breeds — reading "To Live is to Die" and "One" as nostalgic death-wish, but "Escape" and "The Four Horsemen" as genuine defiant self-overcoming after the death of God.

ressentiment.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
ressentiment.title: “They Have a Plan”
ressentiment.relation: Sharp maps Battlestar Galactica's Cylon uprising onto Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: the enslaved Cylons, like Nietzsche's early Christians under Rome, invent a slave morality that inverts their masters' values, condemning human pride and greed while exalting a single loving God, souls, and equality. He shows Leoben preaching the soul to Starbuck and the Cylons' consensus-based commune as the powerless revaluing weakness into virtue, converting their polytheistic, master-moral human creators much as Christianity converted Rome.

ubermensch.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
ubermensch.title: 5 - Thus Spake Bart On Nietzsche and the Virtues of Being Bad
ubermensch.relation: Mark Conard asks whether Bart could be a Nietzschean ideal, tracing Nietzsche's path from Schopenhauer's will/representation split in The Birth of Tragedy—where art redeems us from the horror of existence, with Lisa cast as the Socratic theoretical optimist whose reason never fixes Springfield's absurdity—to the later view that there is no 'being behind the doing', a condition cartoons embody perfectly since Bart is nothing but the sum of his misdeeds. He explains master and slave morality, with Nelson's bullying as master morality and the slaves' ressentiment inventing 'evil', before concluding Bart fails as Übermensch: he defines himself only reactively against authority, as Lisa diagnoses in the Brad Goodman episode, and collapses when the repressive milieu disappears. Bart thus exemplifies the post-Nietzschean danger of nihilism, though the show itself may perform the artistic 'discharge of the nausea of absurdity' Nietzsche praised in Greek comedy.

ubermensch.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
ubermensch.title: Persuasion As Drama
ubermensch.relation: Karl Schudt contends that Nietzsche's genealogy of slave morality cannot be refuted by reason (Nietzsche denies reason itself), so drama must persuade where dialectic cannot: a believable story of a Nietzschean life acts as an empathic experiment. Faith is constructed as the Nietzschean ideal — strong, healthy, ruthless ('Find a couple of studs, use them, and discard them'), dismissive of reflection ('You think too much') — serving Mayor Wilkins, whom Schudt reads as a genuine Übermensch sacrificing mankind's mass for his ascension. Watching her world collapse (the accidental killing in 'Bad Girls', her mirror scene in 'Who Are You?', the torture of Wesley and confession on Angel) gives viewers an Aristotelian pity-and-fear warning that the unjust life ends badly, completing her 'leap from Nietzsche to Socrates.'

ubermensch.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
ubermensch.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
ubermensch.relation: Douglas Blount tests Nietzsche against Sauron, whose forging and grasp of the One Ring - even striving to supplant Ilúvatar - enacts the will to power, exploitation, the death of God, and the ideal of the Übermensch. He argues that in Middle-earth the naked will to power appears not as a brave new humanity but as plain evil, and that Tolkien answers Nietzsche not with argument but with a rival portrait: Gandalf's self-sacrifice on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm, Frodo's mercy to Gollum that becomes Middle-earth's salvation, and Sam's humble refusal of 'Samwise the Strong'. Judged by Nietzsche's own aesthetic criterion of taste, Tolkien's vision of community, humility, and abnegation is the more beautiful - and therefore the more compelling - portrait of reality.

ubermensch.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
ubermensch.title: And There Is No Escape
ubermensch.relation: Abrams reads Allen through Foucault's panopticon: modern society is unlimited voyeurism in which the medieval God whose 'eyes are on us always' has been replaced by the omniscient gaze of Film — Cliff's exposé documentary forcing Lester to watch his own life in Crimes and Misdemeanors, Tom Baxter stepping off the screen in The Purple Rose of Cairo, and the nested eavesdropping layers of Another Woman, which he counts to infinity via Noël Carroll's 'mass art'. Against Mary Nichols's virtue-ethics reading, he argues Allen's ethics is Nietzschean self-fashioning: Judah lives 'beyond good and evil' where Raskolnikov failed, Allan Felix sheds the Bogart alter ego and 'gives style' to his character in Play It Again, Sam, while Eve in Interiors stages Hegel's master–slave dialectic, the 'master' artist dependent for her identity on those she objectifies.

ubermensch.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
ubermensch.title: A New Lease of Life for the Undead
ubermensch.relation: The editors' introduction surveys the twenty-first-century vampire and zombie boom (Twilight, True Blood, Zombieland, Fido, Pride and Prejudice and Zombies, Humans Versus Zombies, zombie walks) and asks why zombies specifically fascinate us. It proposes that the vampire embodies a Nietzschean super-humanity beyond good and evil, still charged with unheeded guilt, while the zombie is sub-Nietzschean: a Spinozan force of decomposition, a completely non-moral interaction of matter with other matter. Zombies work as hyperdead memento mori through which we imagine our own annihilation and our transformation into something posthuman, even as they are repackaged as one more consumer product distracting us from the very Real they reflect.

ubermensch.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
ubermensch.title: James Bond and Philosophy
ubermensch.relation: Matheson examines the 'master animal' imagery saturating Fleming's novels - Donovan Grant's reptilian physique in From Russia with Love, Blofeld's animal magnetism, villains feeding victims to sharks and crocodiles - as an exercise in Social Darwinism where, as Mr. Big puts it, wolves live by wolf's laws and sheep call them criminals. Using Nietzsche's Übermensch, the blond beast of the Genealogy, and Zarathustra's self-overcoming, she distinguishes Apollonian eaters like M (who curb appetite) from doomed Dionysian gluttons like Giuseppe Petacchi, arguing that Fleming makes dining and will power the test of who counts as an Overman. Bond differs from his megalomaniac foes only in keeping his own will to power and stomach under control, and the chapter closes by warning that Hollywood's romanticizing of the master animal keeps us valuing a brutally primitive masculinity Fleming himself mocked as a 'cardboard booby'.

ubermensch.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
ubermensch.title: James Bond and Philosophy
ubermensch.relation: Landa argues that Bond's apparent defense of democracy against Übermensch villains is itself profoundly Nietzschean: Bond's exquisite, disciplined hedonism (the Minton-china breakfast, disgust at Mr. Du Pont's 'eating like a pig'), his obsessive competitiveness at baccarat and golf, and his contempt for mass democracy mark him as an aristocratic bourgeois hero in Nietzsche's mold. The gambling scenes enact a Calvinist logic of predestination in which losing at Casino Royale devastates Bond because his very worth depends on winning, and the 'human muck' he defends at Blades turns out to be the exclusive elite. Dr. No, Mr. Big, Drax, and Blofeld are cast as evil, explicit Nietzscheans while Bond serves a good, unspoken Western Nietzscheanism - so the Cold War showdown with Blofeld, who invokes Nietzsche by name, is elitism fighting counterfeit elitism, making Bond 'a secret agent in the service of Nietzscheanism'.

ubermensch.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
ubermensch.title: Rupert’s Response and Responsibility
ubermensch.relation: Biderman and Jacobowitz read Rope through Nietzsche: Brandon and Philip strangle their classmate David as would-be Nietzschean supermen, acting on mentor Rupert Cadell's cocktail-party theory that murder can be an art for a superior few. The chapter explains the will to power, the Ubermensch, and the death of God, then argues Brandon is no superman: he kills from weakness and a bully's need for an audience, mistaking crass destruction for the refined self-creation Nietzsche demanded, just as the fascist appropriation of Nietzsche fails. Rupert's horrified final speech, renouncing 'superior or inferior beings' and insisting each of us is 'a separate human being,' raises whether a teacher can disavow responsibility when students act out his provocative ideas: ideas have consequences, and the only true test of a philosophy is whether we can live by it.

ubermensch.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
ubermensch.title: Like Caine in Kung Fu
ubermensch.relation: Bence Nanay and Ian Schnee argue Pulp Fiction is genuinely Nietzschean, but not by celebrating violence: the film stages the crisis of meaning after God's death through two reactions to chance. Vincent is the passive nihilist—dogmatically insisting the six bullets mean nothing, inheriting gangster values unquestioned, modeling himself on Elvis—while Jules's 'moment of clarity' makes him a Nietzschean free spirit who creates perspective-relative meaning and breaks the cycle of violence by buying Ringo and Honey Bunny's lives. His plan to 'walk the earth, like Caine in Kung Fu' reworks Zarathustra's wandering, and the running toilets gag marks Vincent's blindness to the significance of events, which is why only one of them survives.

ubermensch.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
ubermensch.title: Meaning The Final Frontier
ubermensch.relation: Biderman and Devlin read The Wrath of Khan as a Nietzschean test of whether revenge can ground a meaningful life after the death of God: Kirk, stuck 'flying a goddamn computer console' as an admiral, and the Genesis project seek meaning through creation without God, while Khan, broken by exile on Ceti Alpha V, chooses vengeance. Using Nozick's contrast between impartial retribution and personally satisfying revenge, and Nietzsche's will to power, master-slave morality, and ressentiment, they argue Khan had the superhuman gifts and independence from herd morality of a candidate Overman, but let revenge enslave him — culminating in Genesis turned weapon and his dying 'For hate's sake . . . I spit my last breath at thee,' a resounding No to life. Spock's mirror-image self-sacrifice, which affirms life, is offered as the better Nietzschean Overman.

ubermensch.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
ubermensch.title: “Sometimes You Just Have to Bow to the Absurd”
