He argues Nietzsche's own doctrine that 'there is no doer behind the deed' (Genealogy I:13) collapses the split between noble soul and noble action, so that deeds confer status; using the case of the police torturing a random woman and the fortuitousness of the Jews' extermination, he contends that when what separates us from victims is mere accident we are their peers, and Nietzsche needs the very doer/deed distinction he attacks in order to reject morality absolutely, so his refusal to condemn the evil hero can be refuted on Nietzschean grounds.

ubermensch.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ubermensch.title: 11. Nietzsche, Mussolini, and Italian Fascism
ubermensch.relation: Sznajder examines how Nietzsche entered Italian Fascism through two bridging figures. Gabriele D'Annunzio relocated Nietzsche from philosophy into literature, staged the 'Übermensch' and 'live dangerously' as an aesthetic politics at Fiume and in the Carta del Carnaro, aestheticizing mass politics in ways fascism inherited. Mussolini, reading Beyond Good and Evil and the Genealogy from his socialist years, seized on the will to power, transvaluation and anti-egalitarian elitism (Rome undone by 'the pale Jews') as a virile theory of revolution. The chapter stresses the paradox that official fascism never listed the individualist, anti-statist Nietzsche as a godfather even as his vocabulary pervaded it.

ubermensch.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ubermensch.title: 12. Nietzsche and the Fascist Dimension The Case of Ernst Jünger
ubermensch.relation: Ohana locates fascism's 'nihilistic-totalitarian syndrome' in the Janus-faced combination of Nietzschean nihilism and the Overman's will to power, whereby ethics is replaced by aesthetics and the self-creating 'new man' shapes reality ex nihilo. He reads Ernst Jünger's Stahlgewittern, Der Arbeiter and 'Total Mobilization' as the aestheticization of war and technology into a work-state, and traces Heidegger's fascination with Jünger's 'will to will' back to Nietzsche and Hölderlin—arguing that, following Camus, one cannot ignore the directionless dynamism leading from Nietzschean perspectivism toward Rosenberg's marching-column politics.

ubermensch.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ubermensch.title: 13. A Godfather Too Nazism as a Nietzschean “Experiment”
ubermensch.relation: Fischer contends that the 'historically effective' (not the 'real') Nietzsche could be read from opposite perspectives, and that Nazism is best understood as a post-Nietzschean 'experiment' licensed by the death of God and the collapse of accepted values ('wir machen einen Versuch mit der Wahrheit'). Invoking Nietzsche's own perspectivism from the Genealogy, and citing calls to 'push what is falling,' the coming 'fight for dominion of the earth' and the Cesare-Borgia-over-Parsifal remark, he argues Nietzsche was 'half a Nazi and half an anti-Nazi'—a genuine part-time godfather, against Kaufmann's overly 'gentle' de-Nazified reading.

ubermensch.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
ubermensch.title: 14. Critique as Apologetics Nolte’s Interpretation of Nietzsche
ubermensch.relation: Stackelberg critiques Ernst Nolte's essentialist reading, in which Nietzsche's Ecce Homo 'party of life' and its call for the 'ruthless destruction of all that is degenerate' furnish the counter-concept of extermination mirroring Marx, dignifying fascism as an anti-Bolshevik European civil war. He shows Nolte must explain away Nietzsche's denunciations of anti-Semitism, nationalism, the Reich and Wagner, and counters that Nazism was itself a moralistic 'slave revolt'—the ascetic, purity-seeking mentality Nietzsche attacked—so that Nietzsche's real susceptibility to Nazi use lies in his shared anti-egalitarian enemies and his refusal of concrete social analysis, not in an exterminatory program.

ubermensch.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
ubermensch.title: Chapter 14 Moral Value and Moral Psychology in Twain’s “Carnival of Crime”
ubermensch.relation: Boardman treats Twain's 'The Facts Concerning the Recent Carnival of Crime in Connecticut'—in which a narrator kills his personified conscience (a shabby dwarf) and gleefully commits a spree of crimes—as staging an 'exasperating metaphysical question' about the value and psychology of morality. On a Nietzschean reading the narrator becomes an Overman revaluing values, seeing conscience as the internalized lie of slave morality; on a Humean reading conscience is moral feeling (not reason), so once it is destroyed the narrator can still reason about right yet has no motive to act morally, illustrating the oak-tree and willful-murder arguments that vice lies in sentiment, not relations or facts. Boardman concludes both interpretations fit yet neither settles whether Twain endorses or lampoons the result—our horror at the crimes is what makes the story funny.

ubermensch.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
ubermensch.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
ubermensch.relation: Scott reads three landmark climbs as expressions of the tension between individual freedom and community standards. He casts John Bachar's bold, ground-up, run-out Bachar-Yerian and its self-mastery ethic as a partial embodiment of Nietzsche's Übermensch and will to power, and Alan Watts' rule-breaking sport route To Bolt or Not to Be as an exercise of Mill's On Liberty defense of originality and diversity that benefits the whole community. Against both thinkers' negative view of community, he uses Charles Taylor's 'horizon of significance' to argue that Sonnie Trotter's The Path gains its meaning only through dialogue with the climbing community and its traditions.

ubermensch.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
ubermensch.title: SERIAL KILLERS
ubermensch.relation: Schmid examines Moors Murderer Ian Brady's book The Gates of Janus, arguing that Brady built a genuine philosophy of serial murder from Sade and Nietzsche rather than merely name-dropping them. He corrects popular caricatures of the ubermensch and will to power, then shows Brady grounds his self-account in moral relativism and reframes serial killing as fundamentally about 'power and the will to power.' Brady's admiration for Carl Panzram and his likeness to the self-justifying, punishment-transcending Sadean hero illustrate how Nietzschean and Sadean ideas actually shape a killer's self-understanding.

ubermensch.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
ubermensch.title: SERIAL KILLERS
ubermensch.relation: Gray gives a psychological account of Ted Bundy and Dennis Rader (BTK), stressing that serial killers are ordinary-seeming — Arendt's banality of evil — and are psychopaths, not psychotics: rational, remorseless, genetically shaped, unable to learn conditioned fear, and guided by scripted fantasies of domination. He reads their pursuit of control as Nietzsche's will to power, citing Bundy's manipulation of preacher James Dobson and Rader's cold courtroom allocution. But he argues the psychopath is a failed, unnatural predator, not Nietzsche's ubermensch: lacking vision and moral self-discipline, he only masters deceit in service of petty, narrow fantasies.

ubermensch.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
ubermensch.title: 8. Star Wars
ubermensch.relation: Rowlands reads Star Wars as Manichaean (light vs dark side of the Force) and contrasts it with Plato, for whom evil is merely absence of good and the form of the good is most real, an idea Augustine (via Plotinus) folded into Christianity. Siding with Lucas that Darth Vader's evil is palpably real, he then uses Nietzsche's 'Dionysus against the Crucified': the Christian strategy represses drives (Freudian repression), the 'hippy' strategy merely expresses them, but greatness requires sublimation into higher forms. Vader taps his dark side but fails to sublimate, so he is a flawed unbalanced megalomaniac (like Nietzsche's Borgia/Napoleon), not a true Ubermensch living life as art.

ubermensch.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
ubermensch.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
ubermensch.relation: Douglas Blount casts Sauron as a candidate for Nietzsche's Ubermensch, embodying the unabashed will to power in a world where God is dead, life is meaningless, and taste rather than reason or morality guides the self-created life. Tolkien answers this not by argument but by a rival portrait whose beauty lies in community, humility, love, and self-sacrifice: Gandalf dying on the bridge, Frodo's mercy to Gollum, and Sam refusing the Ring's vision of 'Samwise the Strong.' Blount argues that on Nietzsche's own criterion of taste, Tolkien's picture of abnegation is the more compelling vision of a life lived well.

ubermensch.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ubermensch.title: 33. 2001 as Philosophy A Technological Odyssey
ubermensch.relation: Abrams argues that Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey dramatizes Henri Bergson's Creative Evolution and Two Sources of Morality and Religion better than Nietzsche's Zarathustra: the monolith turning Moonwatcher's bone into a tool makes humanity Homo faber, and the match-cut from bone to satellite traces one technological odyssey toward species self-transformation. He reads the HAL 9000's murderous breakdown through Turing's imitation game—Hal passes the Turing Test and inverts it by testing Frank at chess and probing Dave—and casts Dave as a new Odysseus dousing HAL the Cyclops. The star child is Bergson's vision of the universe as 'a machine for making gods,' the Nietzschean overman realized through Bergsonian creative and technological evolution, with Aristotle's mimesis grounding the film's account of imitation and its own cinematic self-reflection.

nihilism.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
nihilism.title: 5 - Thus Spake Bart On Nietzsche and the Virtues of Being Bad
nihilism.relation: Mark Conard asks whether Bart could be a Nietzschean ideal, tracing Nietzsche's path from Schopenhauer's will/representation split in The Birth of Tragedy—where art redeems us from the horror of existence, with Lisa cast as the Socratic theoretical optimist whose reason never fixes Springfield's absurdity—to the later view that there is no 'being behind the doing', a condition cartoons embody perfectly since Bart is nothing but the sum of his misdeeds. He explains master and slave morality, with Nelson's bullying as master morality and the slaves' ressentiment inventing 'evil', before concluding Bart fails as Übermensch: he defines himself only reactively against authority, as Lisa diagnoses in the Brad Goodman episode, and collapses when the repressive milieu disappears. Bart thus exemplifies the post-Nietzschean danger of nihilism, though the show itself may perform the artistic 'discharge of the nausea of absurdity' Nietzsche praised in Greek comedy.

nihilism.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
nihilism.title: 13 - Enjoying the So-called “Iced Cream” Mr. Burns, Satan, and Happiness
nihilism.relation: Daniel Barwick argues that Mr. Burns's unhappiness comes not from his age, cruelty, or wealth but from his habit of seeing everything as a symbol of something else, so that nothing is ever enjoyed for what it is - the 'Team Homer' bowling trophy matters only as 'spectacular victory', and his teammates are discarded like flab. Via a Satan's-tempters parable about a 'Bureau of Desubstantialization', he frames this representationalism as cutting man off from real things, and gives it philosophical teeth: a world where everything is only instrumentally good generates an infinite regress with nothing intrinsically good to ground value, leaving Burns's life meaningless, the hallmark of the unhappy life. The 'so-called iced cream' moment in 'Bart's Inner Child' shows Burns can enjoy something merely for itself when he momentarily forgets to symbolize, but Barwick doubts a 104-year-old steeped in malice can make that permanent.

nihilism.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
nihilism.title: Notes from Underground Nihilism and The Matrix
nihilism.relation: Opening Hibbs's essay, the chapter sets The Matrix at the point where high culture's debates about AI, folk psychology, and cloning merge with low culture's Terminator-style entertainments, and argues the film replays older debates about Enlightenment modernity: the commitment to mastering nature through technological progress risks degrading humanity, just as the celebration of individual freedom paradoxically courts the homogenization of mankind. Liberal modernity itself, it warns, is a potential source of nihilism - a human existence void of any ultimate purpose or fundamental meaning, in which the great questions no longer register in the human soul.

nihilism.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
nihilism.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
nihilism.relation: Bamford argues that Atkins's insistence that dieters evaluate the plan for their individual needs parallels Nietzsche's cultural therapy: as the death of God left modern culture nihilistic, so a processed-food culture suffers 'nutritional nihilism,' and the 'mega-orthodox' doctors who worship medical consensus with 'religious fervor' treat science as a replacement religion. Reading Ecce Homo's 'question of nutriment' alongside Twilight of the Idols, she shows that Nietzsche's perspectivism — no uninterpreted facts, only interpretations from physiological perspectives — makes each dieter fully responsible for interpretation, which is why Atkins must ask us to think for ourselves. The limit: where Atkins keeps an 'absolute faith in empirical science' (and Atkins Nutritionals mass-markets processed low-carb products), a properly Nietzschean therapy would question that faith too.

nihilism.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
nihilism.relation: Pratt reads the outlaw biker's FTW (Fuck the World) posture as pop-culture nihilism: Nietzsche's 'danger of dangers' and Camus's answer of scorn to an absurd universe ('there is no fate that cannot be surmounted by scorn') are embodied by Brando's Johnny in The Wild One, Sonny Barger's Hells Angels, and the wanton Born to Lose club of The Born Losers, whose smashing matches Pisarev's Russian nihilism. He then shows how Willie G. Davidson's 1977 Low Rider and events like Daytona's Bike Week sanitized and marketed the rebellion, reducing skulls and DILLIGAF patches to ubiquitous fashion worth $340 million a week. Freud supplies the psychology: the superego keeps the rest of us tame, so we voyeuristically buy a tasteful version of outlaw freedom, even though pure nihilism, denying all truth, refutes even itself.

nihilism.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
nihilism.title: Like Caine in Kung Fu
nihilism.relation: Bence Nanay and Ian Schnee argue Pulp Fiction is genuinely Nietzschean, but not by celebrating violence: the film stages the crisis of meaning after God's death through two reactions to chance. Vincent is the passive nihilist—dogmatically insisting the six bullets mean nothing, inheriting gangster values unquestioned, modeling himself on Elvis—while Jules's 'moment of clarity' makes him a Nietzschean free spirit who creates perspective-relative meaning and breaks the cycle of violence by buying Ringo and Honey Bunny's lives. His plan to 'walk the earth, like Caine in Kung Fu' reworks Zarathustra's wandering, and the running toilets gag marks Vincent's blindness to the significance of events, which is why only one of them survives.

nihilism.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
nihilism.title: The Will to Nothingness, or What Happens when the Red Sox Win
nihilism.relation: Nolen Gertz runs the Sox-Yankees rivalry through Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morals: the Steinbrenner Yankees are masters whose 'good' simply means strong and winning, while Sox fans are slaves whose 'Yankees suck!' is ressentiment's imaginary revenge, intensified into the most spiritual and poisonous hatred by eighty-six years of impotence. The priestly slaves defeated the masters by cleverness rather than force, mirrored when Epstein's sabermetric 'religion' of prospects and projections terrified the Yankees into converting, building a farm system and embracing the slavish virtues they had scorned. The final twist is Nietzsche's will to nothingness: once the masters fell in 2004 the fans' suffering lost its meaning, breeding bandwagon guilt, pink-hat resentment and nihilistic exhaustion, so freedom requires a transvaluation that lets fans simply enjoy watching baseball.

nihilism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
nihilism.title: Life A Celebration
nihilism.relation: Reads John Simm's Master as Nietzsche's most advanced nihilist: having seen the universe die at Utopia, he judges life valueless and converts ressentiment into a joyful will to nothingness, dancing to the Scissor Sisters over his victims. The Ninth Doctor's arc in 'Dalek' mirrors this danger ('What are you changing into?') until he refuses to destroy the last Dalek, beginning his yes-saying to finite life. Following Deleuze's reading, the Doctor defeats the Master not with Martha's gun but with forgiveness ('I forgive you') and her storytelling network, embodying the Übermensch who carries his affirmation into the abyss of the end of the universe.

nihilism.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
nihilism.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
nihilism.relation: Mudde and Piercey argue Curb depicts Nietzschean nihilism made humdrum: in Larry's world 'the highest values devalue themselves,' so Ted Danson's 'anonymous' donation is leaked for glory, a terrorist warning becomes leverage in a tiff with Mindy Reiser, and strangers judge everyone constantly because no one is a moral authority. The Platonic and Aristotelian answers to what 'the good' is have no purchase here; moral language survives only as a hollow shell, which is MacIntyre's 'simulacra of morality,' and his own remedy—rebuilding communities that give moral rules a point—fails because on Curb community is hell ('I'd rather have the thieves than the neighbors'). Since ought no longer implies can, the show is tragic, though the Tourettic chef's opening night in 'The Grand Opening,' where Larry leads a communal torrent of obscenities in solidarity, offers a fragile glimpse of doing a little good.

nihilism.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
nihilism.title: 8 Nietzschean Themes in Raiders of the Lost Ark God May Be Dead, But Best Not Disturb His Corpse
nihilism.relation: Duncan Gale reads Raiders through Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: the Nazis' contempt for those they exploit ('They hire only strong backs and they pay pennies') enacts master morality, while their ressentiment-driven project is itself a fatal misreading — both of the Ark and of Nietzsche, whom Walter Kaufmann shows was distorted by his anti-Semitic sister rather than responsible for it. Indy emerges as an overman candidate whose improvised self-legislation ('I'm making this up as I go,' casually shooting the scimitar-wielding warrior) creates life-affirming values, unlike Belloq, who has no code at all. The finale inverts the death of God: the Nazis die because they disturb a divine power they cannot harness, while America's de facto agnosticism — warehousing the Ark with 'top men' — proves the survivable response to nihilism.

nihilism.title: Symbolism, Meaning, and Nihilism in Quentin TaranTino's Pulp Fiction
nihilism.relation: Conard reads Pulp Fiction as a study of American nihilism in Nietzsche's 'God is dead' sense: with no transcendent framework of value, Jules and Vincent orient their lives by transient pop-culture icons (Jack Rabbit Slim's, the Fonz) and by Marsellus Wallace's arbitrary power, so the mysterious briefcase has worth only because he wills it. He contrasts this void with Aristotelian ethics, where a thing's good lies in realizing its rational essence. Jules's transformation begins when he survives the misfired shots and reinterprets his Ezekiel 25:17 recitation as a call to be 'the Shepherd,' while Butch's choice of the samurai sword over the baseball bat signals a return to an objective warrior code beyond the empty pop icons.

nihilism.title: An Introduction to the Philosophy of TV Noir
nihilism.relation: Sanders's introduction argues that TV noir is an autonomous art form in which film noir's themes are aufgehoben (Hegel's term: preserved and transcended, not negated), and that noir television dramatizes philosophical questions about alienation, relativism, freedom, and meaning. He surveys the volume's arguments: Fitzgibbons on Naked City's conflation of the normal with the moral, Skoble's counterexample of moral clarity in The Fugitive (Richard Kimble), Lee's morally ambiguous John Drake in Secret Agent, and his own readings of Miami Vice's 'sunshine noir' and Crockett's merger with his undercover persona Sonny Burnett. He frames Part 2 through Sartre and Camus, contrasting their call for engagement and defiance with classic noir's passive doomed protagonists (D.O.A.'s Frank Bigelow, The Prisoner's Number 6), and applies Camus's man of revolt to Jack Bauer in 24. He also raises standing objections: Nagel's ironic alternative to Camus's scorn, the incoherence of 'nothing matters' applied to Tony Soprano, and the Foucault/Lyotard-style postmodern critique of institutional power he finds in Crime Story.

nihilism.title: John Drake in Greeneland: Noir Themes in Secret Agent
nihilism.relation: Lee argues that Secret Agent belongs to the Graham Greene noir tradition of The Ministry of Fear and The Third Man, not Bond escapism: Drake never kills, carries no gun, and refuses romantic entanglement, because McGoohan prized realism and ethical seriousness. Readings of Greene's Stephen Neale (who killed his wife out of pity) and Harry Lime's Ferris-wheel nihilism establish a world 'void of meaning, haphazard, and morally indifferent,' which Drake's episodes then dramatize: in 'It's Up to the Lady' his superior Hobbs (named, Lee contends, for Thomas Hobbes, whose Leviathan and war of all against all the essay explicates) betrays Drake's promised word and has the defector Charles arrested; in 'That's Two of Us Sorry' Drake unwittingly plays the villain, ruining an innocent Scottish village; in 'Judgement Day' he cannot say what justice for the Nazi scientist Garriga requires. Lee concludes that Drake, like Neale and Martins, acts in Sartrean bad faith by continuing to serve morally bankrupt masters, and that Greene's only exits are a Kierkegaardian leap of faith Drake never makes, or fantasized retirement and death.

nihilism.title: The Sopranos, Film Noir, and Nihilism
nihilism.relation: Kevin Stoehr reads The Sopranos as TV noir built on Nietzsche's passive, life-negating nihilism: Tony Soprano's 'What do we got?' laments the collapse of mob and family values, Uncle Junior's 'Each of us is alone in the fuckin' universe' voices noir alienation, and Livia's 'It's all a big nothing' is the series' nihilistic creed. A.J.'s confirmation-eve rebellion reading Nietzsche and Camus's The Stranger ('Death just shows the ultimate absurdity of life') dramatizes the death of God inherited by the next generation. The chapter's dark irony is that therapy, meant to give Tony narrative unity and self-knowledge, becomes an instrument of self-deception: he substitutes psychology for ethics, rationalizes adultery and murder as signs of psychic power, and fails at Nietzschean self-overcoming despite the ducks and Pie-O-My that briefly symbolize transcendence.

nihilism.title: “They Turned to a Man They Didn’t Fully Understand”
nihilism.relation: Foy and Dale argue that the Dark Knight trilogy endorses a conservative critique of liberal democracy: Batman taps every citizen's phone, tortures criminals, and kidnaps Lau from Hong Kong because Gotham's institutions cannot cope with a permanent state of crisis. Hume's conservatism—authority resting on habit and order rather than abstract rights and consent—explains Batman's defense of the existing order against Ra's al Ghul's razing of Gotham, while Schmitt's sovereign who declares the 'state of exception' frames Batman as the extra-legal protector who suspends rights during crisis (with Rachel's Caesar warning marking the danger). Against Locke's natural rights and Rawls's inviolability of the person, the Joker and Bane dramatize Strauss's twin fears that liberalism degenerates into nihilistic value-chaos or coercive revolutionary equality, and Burke's natural aristocracy of 'virtual representation' justifies relying on an unchosen elite hero. The trilogy's central puzzle is Batman's illiberal means—taking the blame for Dent's death to preserve the White Knight myth—dirtying his hands so that Gotham's official powers stay clean.

nihilism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
nihilism.title: 6. When Punks Grow Up
nihilism.relation: Meagher asks whether punks can mature, arguing via Sartre and Beauvoir that punk revolts against the 'spirit of seriousness' - the bad faith of treating values as externally imposed by God, law, or convention - and against the weak nihilism that merely abandons valuing after serious values fail. Following Devon Johnson's Black nihilism distinction, mature punk is strong nihilism: destroying decadent (Euromodern, colonial) values in order to create new ones, building scenes, labels, and institutions for future generations, fighting for others' freedom and decolonization as Arendtian politics, and - with Nietzsche's dead God and Crass's 1978 declaration - being willing to proclaim even punk itself dead.

nihilism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
nihilism.title: 16. Punk Politics
nihilism.relation: Prinz surveys punk's political paradox - anarchist punks from Crass and Rock Against Racism to straight edge versus the fascist flirtation of skinheads, the National Front, and Skrewdriver's 'White Power' - and tests four candidate unifiers (anti-authoritarianism, nihilism, individualism, and McLaren's politics of boredom), finding each one-sided. He proposes instead a politics of disaffection: alienation and negative affect toward the status quo that spans anarchist, Nazi, and apolitical punks alike, making punk a confrontational counterculture that says 'Fuck you' with a self-satisfied sneer, even if it never ended a war like the hippies claimed to.

nihilism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
nihilism.title: 22. Rick & Morty as Philosophy Nihilism in the Multiverse
nihilism.relation: The chapter argues that Rick Sanchez's nihilism is built on cultural relativism plus the metaphysical fact of a multiverse. It reads Rick's mockery of racist alien snakes and the Gazorpazorp matriarchy through Montaigne's essay on cannibals to establish cultural relativism, and treats the microverse 'battery' society through Marx's base/superstructure and Foucault's docile bodies to argue all social values are constructed for the rulers. Rick's dimension-hopping (the Cronenberg episode, the Vat of Acid) literalizes David Lewis's modal realism and Leibniz's possible worlds, so that no action matters because a counterpart always does the opposite; his resulting hedonism and Birdperson's 'Wubba lubba dub dub' reveal Rick as a depressed near-Camusian who cannot live his own absurdist creed.

philosophy-of-art.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
philosophy-of-art.title: 6 - The Simpsons and Allusion “Worst Essay Ever”
philosophy-of-art.relation: William Irwin and J.R. Lombardo define allusion as an intended reference demanding associations beyond mere substitution of a referent, distinguishing it from 'accidental associations' like reading Marge's Realty Bites career as an allusion to American Beauty (anachronistic, since the episode aired first). They develop an aesthetics of allusion—pleasure of recognition and getting the joke, the game-like invitation to play, and the cultivation of intimacy and community between writers and audience—through examples like the Ayn Rand School for Tots, Homer's Mary Tyler Moore hat-throw, and the 'Kang is My Co-pilot' double allusion. They argue The Simpsons' allusions to films, shows, and literature build a context and tradition for the show while blending so seamlessly that missing them never spoils the episode.

philosophy-of-art.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
philosophy-of-art.title: 5 - Profile Picture, Right Here, Right Now
philosophy-of-art.relation: Sarachan uses Barthes's Camera Lucida - punctum, studium, and the 'air' of the subject - to argue Facebook profile pictures are all punctum: ephemeral images constantly replaced to strike the viewer instantly, unlike the static yearbook photo. He sorts profile pictures by Barthes's six categories (pose at the webcam, hiding behind objects, Photoshop trick effects, photogenia, aestheticism, syntax) and reads pop-culture avatar images as identity claims. He closes with Benjamin's mechanical reproduction: a webcam image has no original, existing only as infinitely copied bits that paradoxically exist only when someone views the page.

philosophy-of-art.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
philosophy-of-art.title: 30 Black Mirror in the Future
philosophy-of-art.relation: The closing essay asks whether Black Mirror will still be watched in fifty years, applying Howard Gardner's three marks of artistic beauty: interestingness (Hated in the Nation's twists), memorable form (White Bear's editing and pacing), and the invitation to revisit (Bandersnatch, which embodies it literally). Even if its 2010s gadgets come to look dated like duck-and-cover films, the chapter argues the show endures twice over - through timeliness, capturing our technological zeitgeist as Gatsby captured the Jazz Age and Guernica the Spanish Civil War, and through timelessness, since its real subject is glacially unchanging human nature grappling with change, making 'How is technology changing us?' a perennial question.

philosophy-of-art.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
philosophy-of-art.title: The Simpsons Already Did It! This Show Is A Freakin' Rip-Off!
philosophy-of-art.relation: Takes up South Park's 'Simpsons did it!' charge and argues Family Guy is not a rip-off but a postmodern artwork: it tests representation, expression, and form theories of art (Hamlet, Guernica, sonnet form) and finds the show fails all three, since a martini-sipping college-educated dog and non-narrative cutaways fit none. Following Danto, Lyotard, and Baudrillard, it claims the show deliberately raises 'what is art?' while dissolving original and copy into hyperreality: Peter worships the Fonz and builds him a church in 'The Father, the Son, and the Holy Fonz,' lives inside television with a cardboard frame in 'I Never Met the Dead Man,' and 'Da Boom' turns out to be Pam Ewing's dream, so the obvious borrowing from The Simpsons is the point, like Warhol's Brillo Boxes or Duchamp's L.H.O.O.Q.

philosophy-of-art.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
philosophy-of-art.title: A Win for Zelda
philosophy-of-art.relation: Luke Cuddy argues that Zelda games can be art by adapting Kendall Walton's make-believe theory of depiction and Leon Rosenstein's transparency/translucence/opaque distinction to videogames: the Zelda worlds are 'translucent', drawing the gamer in through avatar, music, terrain, and story, unlike the transparent Adventure or an opaque game indistinguishable from life. The hookshot-and-flippers exploration of A Link to the Past — finding hidden bottles and heart pieces off the critical path — exemplifies the 'freeplay' that, together with the right way of 'looking' at a game, supplies three objective art-properties (also backed by Panofsky on objective demands for aesthetic attention). Not every game qualifies: Super Mario Bros. and Tetris lack freeplay, so some games are art and some are not.

philosophy-of-art.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
philosophy-of-art.title: P A R T F O U R
philosophy-of-art.relation: Four Part Four essays beyond ethics. Aaron Meskin asks whether Watchmen is literature at all, testing definitions from Beardsley, Eagleton, Lamarque/Olsen and Hirsch in the Socratic 'what is X?' way, and concludes the question is indeterminate because comics are a hybrid art form — though the book's literary allusions (Shelley's 'Ozymandias,' Blake's 'Tyger,' Burroughs) deserve literary appreciation regardless. Sarah Donovan and Nick Richardson read the two Silk Spectres through three feminisms: Sally and Laurie as liberal feminists (Wollstonecraft, Mill) who fight crime, their hypersexual costumes as Irigaray-style subversive mimicry of gender stereotypes that risks reinforcing them (the Silhouette's expulsion exposing the heterosexual norm), the Comedian's attempted rape exposing 'she asked for it' attitudes, and Laurie as Beauvoir's woman in bad faith, living out her mother's fantasies until she finally names and dresses herself. Robert Arp uses Hooded Justice and Captain Metropolis's closeted relationship to dismantle 'homosexuality is unnatural' arguments — the ideal-function view would condemn the infertile too, and Hume's is-ought point undermines the procreation argument — before defending gay marriage against slippery-slope and parenting objections. Taneli Kukkonen maps Kierkegaard's stages onto the Comedian's mocking irony (hiding even his paternity of Laurie and his Kennedy confession as jokes) and Rorschach's deeper humor of the ethical stage, a knight of resignation whose 'never compromise, not even in the face of Armageddon' expects nothing back from the world.

philosophy-of-art.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
philosophy-of-art.title: 23. Punk and Disgust
philosophy-of-art.relation: Sara Bergstresser reads punk's shocking bodily transgressions - COUM Transmissions' Prostitution exhibit, GG Allin's stage defecation, Iggy Pop's self-mutilation, L7's thrown tampon - through Mary Douglas's Purity and Danger, Martha Nussbaum's Hiding from Humanity, and Julia Kristeva's Powers of Horror. Disgust polices social boundaries: Nussbaum shows how disgust-based obscenity law historically targets minorities, while Kristeva's abject (corpse, menstrual blood, excrement) marks the collapse of self/other boundaries that punk performers deliberately cross, with punk musicians added to Kristeva's list of those who dare approach the abject. The chapter asks whether the disgusting can be art, closing with Eco's claim that ugliness is passion against beauty's detachment, and with feminist performers like Jack Off Jill using blood and 'ugliness' as protest against the policing of female bodies.

philosophy-of-art.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
philosophy-of-art.title: 29. Anarchy in Aesthetics
philosophy-of-art.relation: Evan Kreider tests punk against three theories of art. Hutcheson's formalism - beauty as 'uniformity amongst variety', order plus complexity, exemplified by Bach, bebop, and prog rock - condemns punk's three chords, power chords, and chaotic performances; Tolstoy's arousal theory and the Croce/Collingwood expression theory vindicate punk's seething anger and angst ('Liar', 'I Wanna Be Sedated', 'Know Your Rights'); and Aristotle's unities of action, place, and time show that simplicity, even with a dash of tragic irony, serves didactic and political ends. The chapter concludes that punk's deliberate simplicity and chaos ('Anarchy in the UK', 'God Save the Queen', 'Rock the Casbah') is precisely what lets its political message reach 'angry youth', making punk a standing counter-example to order-and-complexity aesthetics.

allusion.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
allusion.title: 6 - The Simpsons and Allusion “Worst Essay Ever”
allusion.relation: William Irwin and J.R. Lombardo define allusion as an intended reference demanding associations beyond mere substitution of a referent, distinguishing it from 'accidental associations' like reading Marge's Realty Bites career as an allusion to American Beauty (anachronistic, since the episode aired first). They develop an aesthetics of allusion—pleasure of recognition and getting the joke, the game-like invitation to play, and the cultivation of intimacy and community between writers and audience—through examples like the Ayn Rand School for Tots, Homer's Mary Tyler Moore hat-throw, and the 'Kang is My Co-pilot' double allusion. They argue The Simpsons' allusions to films, shows, and literature build a context and tradition for the show while blending so seamlessly that missing them never spoils the episode.

popular-parody.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
popular-parody.title: 7 - Popular Parody The Simpsons Meets the Crime Film
popular-parody.relation: Deborah Knight uses 'Bart the Murderer' to distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic referencing: the episode incorporates the gangster film's generic conventions—Fat Tony's mob, the impressionable youth's rise, the contrast between crime family and ordinary family—directly into its narrative structure, with Goodfellas and The Public Enemy as targets. She argues Linda Hutcheon's art-parody theory, with its privileging of ironic inversion and critical self-interrogation, does not fit this case; the episode works as popular parody, comic homage rather than critique, its selectivity omitting the genre's violence and epic timespan. Whether Bart's return to his family after the charges are dismissed is read as irony at the expense of American family life depends on which hermeneutic circle the viewer stands in.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: 7 - Popular Parody The Simpsons Meets the Crime Film
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Deborah Knight uses 'Bart the Murderer' to distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic referencing: the episode incorporates the gangster film's generic conventions—Fat Tony's mob, the impressionable youth's rise, the contrast between crime family and ordinary family—directly into its narrative structure, with Goodfellas and The Public Enemy as targets. She argues Linda Hutcheon's art-parody theory, with its privileging of ironic inversion and critical self-interrogation, does not fit this case; the episode works as popular parody, comic homage rather than critique, its selectivity omitting the genre's violence and epic timespan. Whether Bart's return to his family after the charges are dismissed is read as irony at the expense of American family life depends on which hermeneutic circle the viewer stands in.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Jones reads Adventure Time through Gadamer's account of play in Truth and Method: play is the 'mode of being' of the artwork, and Finn's all-in commitment—the 'sacred seriousness' that makes a spoilsport of anyone who mocks the rules, as in 'Slumber Party Panic' or Finn's bloodlust in 'Morituri Te Salutamus'—is why the show counts as art. The finished episode is Gadamer's 'transformation into structure,' and like a festival or a favorite board game it exists in its return, episode after episode. Interpreting the show is itself play: holding our world and Ooo's world in two palms brought together is Gadamer's fusion of horizons, through which Finn corrects our concepts of a boy or a hero and makes new understanding, even empathy, possible.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The chapter argues that what sets Adventure Time above generic sword-and-sorcery is that its stories are stories of play, from Card Wars duels to the pillow-fort world of 'Puhoy', where Finn lives out an entire alternate life with Rosalinen. Drawing on Huizinga's claim that play founds all culture, Gadamer's view that play is a presentation that reveals truth, and Fink's account of play as purposeless, world-creating magic, it shows Finn learning what a hero is by 'playing' the hero's role, BMO transforming a chicken into the noir suspect Lorraine, and Jake's imaginary lava genuinely burning Finn in 'Rainy Day Daydream'. Play-worlds like Ooo hold a mirror to the real one - Finn's experiments on the little people force Jake to confront what breaking up his relationship would mean - so make-believe turns out to be how we seriously learn who we are.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: 7. The Art of Playing Along with Dancing Little People
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Defends Twin Peaks as art by staging Plato's Republic condemnation of confusing mimetic artists against Aristotle's Poetics, where dramatic reversal — the capacity to surprise and disorient, like Dougie's "hell-ooo" slot-machine jackpots — is an essential function of art rather than a defect. It then adopts Gadamer's analysis of Spiel (play/game) and Roman Ingarden's schematized artwork to argue that the Man from Another Place's dance in the red-curtained room is incomplete in itself and becomes art only in the rhythmic to-and-fro with viewers who complete its meaning, just as a pitch crossing a line only means "goal" inside a game. The work of art, on this view, is not the footage but the ongoing process of participation that the Red Room stagecraft — furnace smoke, gold orbs, theatrical spotlights — demands.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: 8. Playing with Glitter
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: This chapter argues that play is Drag Race's deep structure, developed through three philosophers. Wittgenstein's language games explain the show's word-play: 'realness' subverts its own reference to mean the iconic fake, 'herstory' is history played with from a queer perspective, and lip syncs are rule-following whose rules only exist in application. Gadamer's account of play with 'a life of its own' — requiring willingness and openness to the Other — explains why half-hearted players lose, from Porkchop and Tammie's mouthed-nothing lip sync to Gia Gunn and Trixie breaking character in Snatch Game, and why the Evil Twins and makeover challenges are designed to force queens to open up. Deleuze's rhizome (with Bakhtin's carnivalesque) grounds the claim that drag decentering the human — Lil' Poundcake, dragged pancakes, Sharon Needles — and the finale's carnival dissolve the official binaries of male/female and good/bad.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Rabbi Edelheit reads Walter as a figure of the Jewish philosophy of history: his 'I don't roll on Shabbas', Herzl's 'If you will it, it is no dream', the Baal Shem Tov's 'remembrance is the source of redemption', and the garbled Rambam fragment about aish all bind him to a historical community whose memory makes life meaningful — Gadamer's Truth and Method point that we belong to history before we understand ourselves, our prejudgments constituting our being. Against the nihilists' 'Vee belief in NOSSING', Walter's defiant living-in-the-past (Tevye, Sandy Koufax sitting out the World Series on Yom Kippur) is identity and meaning itself, even when Donny's ashes blow back in the wind and his grief can only speak in Vietnam's vocabulary.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Gaming Freedom Choosing or Obeying
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Pointon argues the 'would you kindly' twist in Andrew Ryan's office works on two levels at once: it reveals Jack's conditioning within the game and simultaneously falsifies the player's meta-narrative of playing a free agent. He uses Clark and Chalmers's extended mind to explain why games literally extend cognition and body (mirror-neuron empathy with Little Sisters, craning your neck while peeking around corners), and Gadamer's hermeneutic horizons and fusion of horizons to explain how BioShock deliberately builds and then shatters player expectations. The three alternative endings keyed to saving or harvesting Little Sisters then restore a third horizon in which the player, like Jack fighting Fontaine, is a 'man' who chooses rather than a slave who obeys, a critique of linear RPGs that only feign autonomy.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Torosyan argues The Daily Show models the critical thinking and good-faith civic discourse that real politics and TV news lack, reading John Oliver's 'Civil Disservice' interview with Froma Harrop and Stewart's clips of Rumsfeld contradicting himself on WMDs as exposing bullshit in Frankfurt's sense: assertion indifferent to truth. Stewart's reframing of William Bennett's gay-marriage talking points (is the debate about marriage or about who counts as human?) and his self-effacing interviews with Ramesh Ponnuru enact Rousseau's social-contract ideal of what news owes the public against Machiavellian ends-justify-means manipulation. Gadamer supplies the demand that Bennett question his own horizons, Nietzsche's Apollonian-Dionysian account of tragedy frames the show's satire, and the Tao Te Ching's 'let yourself be partial' governs the whole chapter.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Sirvent and Baker use Daily Show segments (Wyatt Cenac reporting from a Vegas-style heaven, Lewis Black on Jesus as a primary requirement, Stewart on Pat Robertson praying down the Supreme Court) to skewer politicians who claim God's endorsement, from Michele Bachmann's guaranteed Iowa 'miracle' to Glenn Beck's apocalyptic readings. Locke's critique of religious 'enthusiasm' explains why taking private intuition for divine direction breeds arrogant conviction immune to counterevidence, while Gadamer's hermeneutics shows that Beck and Robertson practice objectivist misreading of texts written in a culture two thousand years distant. The chapter closes with the demand for humility about claiming the mind of God.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: David Aldridge reads the D&D manuals' ban on 'metagame thinking' through Gadamer's hermeneutics of the 'event of understanding' from Truth and Method. He tests three models of knowing one's character: Collingwood's re-enactment thesis (total immersion, shown impossible by Fourth Edition's bird's-eye battle maps and the intrusion of rules talk), Collingwood's own 're-enactment plus' amendment joined to Husserlian bracketing (holding out-of-character knowledge apart, knowing the author better than he knew himself), and Gadamer's fusion of horizons, grounded in Heidegger's pre-understanding and illustrated by Plato's paradox of learning, in which no clean having-versus-acting distinction on OOC knowledge survives. Because understanding is always being 'brought up short' by what the character sheet cannot capture, playing a character transformationally teaches us about ourselves.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Closing Speculations Genre
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Weighing the four criteria against 'Dumbledore is gay,' the chapter finds it no primary truth but arguably suggested by the text, Dumbledore's confession that Grindelwald's ideas 'inflamed' him and the absence of any heterosexual interest. It sets the anti-intentionalist view held by Wimsatt, Beardsley, Gadamer, Barthes, Foucault, and Derrida, that language is a social creation so texts must speak for themselves and there are as many Potter worlds as readers, against E. D. Hirsch's intentionalism and Rowling's own claim 'He is my character,' concluding that most fans rightly accept her announcement as an oral appendix alongside all her interview backstories.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Ignorance of Ickle Dudleykins
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The chapter presents Gadamer's claim that we can only interpret the world by coming to it with 'prejudgments,' the borrowed toolbox of questions, biases, and expectations without which anything we try to understand stays 'like a container sealed shut.' Whether prejudgments help or hinder depends on holding them loosely enough to let the situation reshape them, setting down the hammer and finding the screwdriver when the world resists.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Betrayed by Biases
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Applying Gadamer to Dudley, the chapter shows how Petunia and Vernon's doting ('no finer boy anywhere,' 'big-boned' rather than dieting, 'wouldn't hurt a fly') armor Dudley's prejudgments against every challenge. His close encounter with the dementors, forcing him to relive his worst moments, strips those rationalizations away so he finally sees himself as 'spoiled, pampered, bullying,' a radical readjustment that lets him recognize Harry's courage and feel gratitude and even affection.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Dangerous Dreams
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The chapter generalizes the pattern across the series: Harry's anti-Snape prejudice, misplaced trust in the fake Mad-Eye Moody and the Half-Blood Prince's potions book, Dumbledore's 'for the greater good' dreams with Grindelwald, Merope Gaunt's love-potion fantasy of Tom Riddle, the locket Horcrux magnifying the trio's suspicions until Ron storms off, and the Malfoys' underestimation of Voldemort all show prejudgments misreading reality until the pain of banging into it forces a rethink. Truth matters, Garver concludes, because false beliefs are an unreliable map for navigating the world.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Cost of Overconfidence
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The chapter details Harry's overconfidence about his dream-connection to Voldemort's mind: cocky that he uniquely understands Voldemort, he dismisses Dumbledore's warning that the link runs both ways, neglects his Occlumency lessons out of distrust for Snape and irritation with Hermione, and never sees why the training matters. Snape's taunt, 'Maybe they make you feel special, important,' suggests Harry's prejudgment that his visions are a privileged window is also a temptation feeding his sense of mission.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Memories Help Make Meaning
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The chapter traces the fatal cost of Harry's unchecked prejudgments: trusting his O.W.L. dream-vision of Sirius being tortured, twisting Dumbledore's Occlumency warnings into confirmation that his dreams are real, and accepting Kreacher's cackling, self-interested testimony at Grimmauld Place without telling his friends the source, Harry launches the Department of Mysteries 'rescue' that gets Sirius killed. Garver softens the verdict, a fifteen-year-old with noble intentions, but the lesson stands: we see what we want to see through blinders we do not know we wear.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Moving Past Misdirection
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The chapter joins Augustine's Confessions analysis of time, where only in human experience does memory of the past meet anticipation of the future in the present, to Gadamer's view of prejudgments as tradition, memory 'passed down' that shapes how we approach the present. The Pensieve symbolizes this double, personal and social memory: Dumbledore's third-person viewing spots patterns, and the extracted memories of Riddle's orphanage sadism and the reconstructed testimonies of Hokey and Morfin Gaunt give Harry the knowledge of Voldemort's history, character, and vulnerabilities he needs to defeat him.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: NOTES
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: The essay's conclusion shows reality correcting every character's prejudgments: Dumbledore's wizard-supremacy dreams die with his sister, Merope's with the end of the love potion, Ron's with distance from the Horcrux, the Malfoys' when Voldemort threatens Draco, and Harry matures from naive boy to cocky teen to discerning young man. Garver draws the thesis that epistemology is inseparable from ethics, bravery and loyalty require true belief about danger and about Dumbledore's real faults, and Rowling's narrative misdirection makes readers undergo the same correction, so that following Harry's transformation we become better people, with even Dudley's change giving hope to the most resistant reader.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: a16.xhtml
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Grimwood turns the riddle contest in the dark into a lesson in hermeneutics: Bilbo interprets like Hirsch's intentionalist, asking what Gollum means (and suspecting he means to eat him), while Gollum answers each of Bilbo's riddles by fusing the words with his own forgotten past - sun on daisies, eggs at his grandmother's hole - exactly Gadamer's claim that understanding is a dialogue of horizons shaped by 'prejudices'. Bilbo's final 'What have I got in my pocket?' breaks the game because it severs the good will that makes interpretation a genuine exchange, leaving Gollum no horizon to fuse with, so he simply constructs his own 'truth' that the hobbit stole his precious. The chapter generalizes: Gandalf's dismantling of 'Good morning' shows interpretation is everywhere, and there is no view from nowhere outside our horizons.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Jill Olthouse applies hermeneutics, crediting Gadamer as its key philosophical developer, to Panem's ideological battle of words and images: paradoxical metaphors like 'the girl on fire,' 'tribute,' and 'mockingjay' carry contestable associations, so interpreting them is a creative act through which Katniss is either defined by her enemies or defines herself. She traces Katniss's reinterpretations, from squirrel-prey to hunter after Peeta saves her, from staged 'star-crossed lovers' to a bond that becomes literal, to the berry suicide ploy that denies the Capitol its victory, and reads the hijacked Peeta's 'she's some kind of mutt' as the Capitol winning an interpretive round by stealing her metaphor. The chapter culminates in Katniss's creative reading of Snow's confession and her assassination of Coin, the moment she finally claims the mockingjay identity on her own terms as a fighter and messenger rather than a weapon used by others.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Carl Matthew Johnson argues that the split-timeline versus linear-timeline fan war, settled by Eiji Aonuma's 2006 Nintendo Dream interview, is really a hermeneutic meta-game fans play on top of Zelda. He applies the Heidegger-Gadamer hermeneutic circle — the Ganon references in Wind Waker make sense only from knowledge of the whole series, while gossip-stone text about Kaepora Gaebora feeds back into the whole — then uses Leibniz's curve-fitting problem to show timeline evidence underdetermines any single interpretation. Ockham's razor and Wittgenstein's counting-by-twos rule-following example reveal that simplicity is community-relative, culminating in Miyamoto's 2007 claim that Zelda was designed from the start as a 'communication game' among players.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Sirvent and Baker read The Book of Mormon alongside 'Cartman Sucks' and 'The Biggest Douche in the Universe' to expose religious fundamentalism—Elder Price's 'I Believe' creed, Elder McKinley's 'turn it off' cure for gay feelings, the conversion camp that is 'fixing' Bradley—as at once naive and arrogant. Peirce's 'fixation of belief' names the dogmatist's refusal to admit a belief could be wrong; Gadamer's hermeneutics shows that Elder Cunningham's Boba Fett additions to scripture are not corruption but an honest image of how all interpretation works, against the fundamentalist's naive realism that claims one pure meaning; and Locke on religious 'enthusiasm' plus Pascal on evil done from religious conviction explain how certainty of God's will always turns out to be a self-portrait, as in Cartman's revelation that God wants everyone to give him a dollar in 'Probably'. Genuine faith, they conclude with Elder Price's final conversion, only becomes fruitful once it accepts doubt.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Heidegger and the Problem of Interpretation in Barton Fink
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Conard uses Barton Fink as a springboard into Heidegger's theory of interpretation, contrasting it with Cartesian dualism. Barton, the 'life of the mind' artist whose skull-like hotel room symbolizes his isolation, is a Cartesian subject cut off from the practical, meaning-giving contexts (Heidegger's workshop, the ready-to-hand versus present-at-hand typewriter) in which equipment is understood and interpreted. Conard argues the film's uninterpretable elements—the box, the wall photo, the mosquitoes—resist meaning precisely because Barton is severed from the web of relations that would let anything show up as meaningful, illustrating Dasein's temporal, potentiality-driven being.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: 7. The Art of Playing Along with Dancing Little People
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Luzecky and Elsby argue that Twin Peaks is genuine art because, against Plato's condemnation of mimetic art as confusing copies to be exiled, it fulfills Aristotle's Poetics: art's essential function is dramatic reversal, surprising and transfixing us (Dougie's absurd casino win, the dancing Man from Another Place). Drawing on Gadamer's 'Spiel' (play/game) and Ingarden's schematized, incomplete artworks, they contend the work of art exists only as an ongoing rhythmic 'to and fro' between image and viewer—so we complete the Red Room scene by participating in it, moving it from potentiality to actuality.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: On Reason and Passion in The Maltese Falcon
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Knight argues that Sam Spade is not the dispassionate reasoner philosophy since Plato has assumed the detective to be, defending instead cognitivism about the emotions (via Solomon, de Sousa, and Damasio's Phineas Gage case). Because the hard-boiled detective enters events in media res, Spade must work hermeneutically to reconstruct the real story behind Brigid O'Shaughnessy's lies, and his judgments of trust, confidence, and loyalty fuse reason with feeling. In the climax Spade sends Brigid over for murdering Miles Archer precisely because reason and emotion together tell him he cannot trust her, whereas Brigid—the film's true cold calculator—only feigned emotion to make him her sap; Knight contrasts her with the non-fatale Vivian Rutledge of The Big Sleep.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Kevin S. Decker offers a 'philosophical hermeneutics' of Burton's Batman and Batman Returns, arguing that a long-lived cultural artifact like the Batman discloses a society's self-understanding. Using Heidegger's Dasein and 'working-out of possibilities,' Nietzsche's 'only interpretations,' and Gadamer's hermeneutic circle and fusion of horizons, Decker reads the shift from ABC's camp Adam West Batman to Burton's dark version as tracking cultural change (Vietnam, Watergate, 1980s decadence). He casts the Joker, Penguin, and Catwoman—and Batman himself—as Burton's recurring 'expressive outsider,' relating them to Nietzsche's Übermensch and Gotham's gullible crowds to Heidegger's das Man, and compares Burton's Expressionist Gotham to Max Beckmann's post-WWI Hell lithographs, positioning Burton as a prophet of modern decadence.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Torosyan argues that The Daily Show models critical thinking and postmodern self-awareness, using Stewart's interviews to show how to reframe debate and act in good faith. He reads Stewart's demand that news media serve the public through Rousseau's social contract, casts scaremongering politicians as following Machiavelli's advice to 'learn how not to be good,' invokes Gadamer's hermeneutics to argue that guests like William Bennett fail to question their own prejudices, and uses Nietzsche's Apollonian/Dionysian tension to explain the show's tragicomic satire (e.g., the 'Smallpox Blankets' joke and Bush reading Camus's The Stranger).

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Sirvent and Baker use Stewart's mockery of politicians who claim a divine endorsement (Bachmann's certainty of a 'miracle,' Wyatt Cenac reporting from a Las Vegas-style heaven) to apply John Locke's critique of religious 'enthusiasm'—the arrogance of taking one's own intuitions for divine direction without weighing them against reason. They then deploy Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics against the 'objectivism' of Glenn Beck and Pat Robertson, arguing that treating scripture as an unambiguous rulebook ignores how every reading is conditioned by culture and history.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Hartmann argues the specialty-coffee 'third wave' (Stumptown, Intelligentsia, Counter Culture) could not exist without Starbucks, which taught consumers to pay for a boldly-roasted, ethically-branded, self-gifting aesthetic under neoliberalism. Drawing on Heidegger's thrownness and Gadamer's hermeneutical phenomenology, he punctures Nicholas Cho's claim that the third wave 'lets the coffee speak for itself': just as we perceive a chair as for-sitting through pre-given cultural meaning, cupping rituals actively build a coffee 'hermeneutic' that reshapes the drinker's very perception (the trained palate 'tastes' plantain and graham cracker). He likens this to ventriloquism—the coffee only 'speaks' because someone feeds it its lines—and uses Žižek's account of cynical ideology to expose the gap between fair-trade branding and reality.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Kimberly Baltzer-Jaray and Tanya Rodriguez argue, against George Carlin's 'mobile art gallery' joke, that the only thing separating tattooing from fine art is its fleshy canvas. They show how formalist, expressionist and institutional theories historically excluded both women's craft and tattoos, then use feminist aesthetics (Korsmeyer, Iris Marion Young on the gaze) to reclaim the female tattooed body as an assertion of agency against objectification. They then apply Gadamer's hermeneutics – art as play, festival and symbol – to argue tattoos make a claim on the viewer, build a 'hermeneutic collective' community, and function as inexhaustible symbols prompting self-recognition.

gadamer-hermeneutics.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
gadamer-hermeneutics.title: NOTES
gadamer-hermeneutics.relation: Gracia examines six Dracula films (Murnau, Browning, Morrisey, Herzog, Badham, Coppola) and asks how they relate to Stoker's novel, tracing the count's evolution from Murnau's rat-like horror to Coppola's tragic romantic knight who dies for love. He rejects the topical, essentialist, and family-resemblance accounts of the films' relation to the book and proposes instead that they are 'relational interpretations'—works in their own right whose primary aim is to link Stoker's story to an outside agenda (sex, humor, sympathy, heroism) rather than to explicate the novel. The argument is a piece of interpretation theory, distinguishing work-oriented from relational interpretation to explain why popular adaptations legitimately diverge from their source.

grand-narratives.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
grand-narratives.title: 8 - The Simpsons, Hyper-Irony, and the Meaning of Life
grand-narratives.relation: Carl Matheson argues The Simpsons is defined by quotationalism—rapid-fire pop-culture allusions like the Ayn Rand School, The Great Escape score, and The Birds tableau in 'A Streetcar Named Marge'—and hyper-ironism, positions put forward only to be undercut. He links both to a pervasive crisis of authority in art, science, and philosophy: Danto's 'end of art', Kuhn and Feyerabend against scientific progress, and Rorty's Derrida recasting philosophy as conversation. Reading the Frank Grimes funeral and 'Scenes from the Class Struggle in Springfield' as refusing any stable moral ground, he concludes the heart-warming family endings exist mainly to let viewers tolerate the next round of cruelty, papering over a paradox of comedy.

grand-narratives.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
grand-narratives.title: Possibilities of Postmodern Education Beyond Control
grand-narratives.relation: Toby Daspit reads Season Four as a drama of postmodern education: the Initiative's will to master and dissect — Walsh's Frankenstein-project Adam, who murders a boy to see how he works, fulfilling Wordsworth's 'we murder to dissect' — embodies the Cartesian split and the Hegelian drive to negate the other, while Buffy's world deconstructs fixed identity (Darla reversing the horror-movie opening, the Faith/Buffy body swap in 'Who Are You?', Jonathan's 'Superstar') and thwarts prophecy's metanarrative in 'Prophecy Girl.' Against modernist schooling's 'controlled circumstances' and Freire's banking model (Professor Riegert ejecting Buffy from class, Walsh's transmission lectures), the show models knowledge as collective work — the Scoobies' research sessions in Giles's library, Giles's fluid mentorship versus Kendra's by-the-book training, and the relational magic of 'Primeval' — offering education beyond control in an emergent, postmodern world.

grand-narratives.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
grand-narratives.title: Both Sides of Dylan and Politics
grand-narratives.relation: Jordy Rocheleau reads Dylan's protest era ("The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll," "Hurricane," "Chimes of Freedom") as Enlightenment social criticism in Kant's and Mill's sense: reason can expose injustice and secure autonomy against majority tyranny. The post-protest Dylan ("My Back Pages," "Desolation Row," "It's Alright, Ma") turns postmodern - Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives, Derrida's ever-deferred meanings, and Foucault's power/knowledge, where ideals of freedom become instruments of domination. Yet Dylan keeps crying for justice ("Political World," "Dignity"), so the chapter concludes postmodern skepticism can only serve as a cautionary check within, not a replacement of, Enlightenment politics - the thief's line in "All Along the Watchtower" as commitment amid confusion.

grand-narratives.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
grand-narratives.title: U2 and Philosophy
grand-narratives.relation: Thomson uses U2's self-declared postmodern phase to define postmodernity itself: a sensitivity to poetic polysemy against modernity's fantasies of total control (Heidegger's reduction of everything to optimizable resource), Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives - defended against the self-refutation charge and narrowed to the dying metanarratives of unity and emancipation - and the Marx-Nietzsche-Freud hermeneutics of suspicion that fragmented the subject, with Kierkegaard and early Heidegger as the resisters. Derrida's 9/11 analysis of autoimmunity and hauntology is read into 'Peace on Earth' and the sorrows that 'learned to swim' in 'Until the End of the World'. The payoff is a polysemic reading of 'Even Better than the Real Thing': risky as a seeming hymn to Baudrillard's simulacra, addressed to a live audience it celebrates a communal love 'even better' than personal love - Diotima's ladder generalized - making the postmodern U2 continuous with the 'Christ-ian' U2 of universal love, sealed by 'One'.

grand-narratives.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
grand-narratives.title: Family Guy Must Die! Long Live Family Guy!
grand-narratives.relation: Jeremy Wisnewski's mock-manifesto uses Family Guy's cutaway gags and taboo jokes (Hitler sausage vendors, Petoria at the UN, Saddam and Khadafi bonding over Seinfeld) to stage postmodernism: Lyotard's "incredulity toward meta-narratives" and Baudrillard's claim that the real is no longer real, since our families are as televisual as the Griffins, who at least know they are cartoons. The danger is that joking about everything breeds cynical passivity, "liberating us from our causes." But Foucault, the 1968 activist and prison reformer, shows through power/knowledge that one can be postmodern and still fight locally, so the Griffins, and the show's satire of religion and politics, get to live.

grand-narratives.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
grand-narratives.title: Today I Woke Up Sucking a Grammy
grand-narratives.relation: Bradley Kaye reads Kid A as an album made under Lyotard's postmodern condition: "Everything in Its Right Place" ("what was that you tried to say?") and the murmured title track bear witness to the differend, something that must be put into phrases but cannot yet be; "The National Anthem" dramatizes incredulity toward the grand narrative of nationalism in favor of little narratives and local justice; "Treefingers" is the painful silence of the inexpressible, and "Optimistic" an ironic micro-political hope. The epigone problem (Yorke to Coldplay, Travis, and Muse: "Good luck with Kid A") and the closing Baudrillard turn — "In Limbo"'s "you're living in a fantasy world," the Marcus Welby and Perry Mason hyperreal, "it's not like the movies" — explain why even labeling the album "Best Alternative Album" Grammy presumes exactly the stable categories Kid A dissolves.

grand-narratives.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
grand-narratives.title: History and Philosophy
grand-narratives.relation: Imre reads Hungary's Aranycsapat as a political-philosophical event: Sebes's socialist 4–2–4 football was meant to prove that cooperative civil society could flourish under Stalinism, and the 6–3 demolition of England at Wembley, with its self-organizing positional play, became the sporting antithesis to Rákosi's regime — culminating in the 1956 Revolution that Arendt cited as a 'true' revolution of spontaneous councils. The 1954 final loss to West Germany (contrasted with Germany's own rebirth at Berne) entrenched a fatalism that history's organic 'grand narrative' and 'final synthesis' were against Hungary, helping destroy the civil-society possibility the team embodied and pushing Hungarians into anti-politics. His lesson: talent and beauty can be quashed by the contingency of history — igazság, truth-justice, never manifested, and soccer could not overcome history.

grand-narratives.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
grand-narratives.title: Progress
grand-narratives.relation: Gregory Gilson argues that although The Onion deliberately reports falsehoods, it embodies postmodern theories of truth better than the newspapers it parodies. Lyotard's mercantilization of knowledge and the fragmentation of dominant narratives into separate language games explain headlines like 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity' and 'Astronomer Discovers The Center Of The Universe Is His Beautiful 9-Year Old Son,' which smash incompatible discourses together, while Baudrillard's simulacrum and hyper-reality explain how The Onion — like Disneyworld — is branded fake precisely so mainstream media can seem real. Yet the chapter closes honestly: its own criticism of 'Bush Says He Still Believes Iraq War Was the Fun Thing To Do' assumed some targets were wrong, which assumes a Truth out there — the paradox of a satire whose truthfulness exceeds its own theory of truth.

grand-narratives.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
grand-narratives.title: The New Man or the Old
grand-narratives.relation: Marks reads Holmes as the paragon Victorian whose faith in reason mirrors his era's confidence and, underneath it, its anxiety: Holmes's outburst in 'The Cardboard Box' ('What is the object of this circle of misery and violence and fear?... That is humanity's great problem to which Reason, so far, has no answer') appears the same year Nietzsche published 'Gott ist tot' in The Gay Science, amid Marx's 'opium of the people' and Darwin's displacement of religion. Reinterpreting the 2009 Ritchie film, he rejects the obvious religion-versus-reason reading of Lord Blackwood: Blackwood's 'magic' is really chemistry and machinery (technocracy), Holmes's science serves the military (dictatorship), and Moriarty (terrorism) defeats both, dramatizing post-9/11 fears about the militarized fruits of Reason. He concludes that Holmes straddles the Victorian and postmodern divide and that replacing religion with science is Rationalism's 'siren song.'

grand-narratives.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
grand-narratives.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
grand-narratives.relation: Wade Newhouse reads The Graveyard Book as a fusion of the coming-of-age tale and the Gothic ghost story, from The Turn of the Screw to Stephen King's haunted narcissists, and uses Lyotard's postmodern condition to explain the hybrid: Bod's self forms not by accepting one governing metanarrative but at Lyotardian 'nodal points' among many ghosts, each a fragment of history with its own partial morality, from the Roman Caius Pompeius to the witch Liza Hempstock. The Danse Macabre, where living and dead mix under rules neither remembers choosing, dramatizes borders that feel absolute, yet Bod's development consists in violating boundaries, befriending the outcast witch and hunting the Jacks on his own terms. The ending, 'I'm Nobody Owens. That's who I am,' offers a postmodern self most itself by being no one, with the acceptance of death as the one metanarrative even postmoderns keep, for Bod it is the first lesson rather than the last.

grand-narratives.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
grand-narratives.title: 1. More Golems around Than You Might Think
grand-narratives.relation: Using Feet of Clay and Witches Abroad, Froehlich argues we are all like golems: our behavior is driven by the 'words in our heads,' the texts that society and the powerful put there. Lyotard's metanarratives explain how Lily Weatherwax forces Genua to live out fairy-tale plots and how Dragon King of Arms rewrites Nobby's family tree to manufacture a king, while dwarfish gender norms keep Cheery Littlebottom trapped in a culturally imposed text. Freedom comes only when, like Dorfl after Carrot buys him his own receipt, a person rejects the imposed words and chooses words of the heart - 'words in the heart cannot be taken.'

grand-narratives.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
grand-narratives.title: 1. Free Falling into Postmodernism
grand-narratives.relation: Sewell reads Petty's 1976 debut through Jameson's postmodernism: Petty's music is a cut-and-paste amalgam of 1960s jangle, 1970s heartland rock and punk attitude whose pastiche dissolves the high/low art distinction as aesthetic production merges with commodity production, which is exactly why it feels timeless. He then applies Butler's performativity to Petty's "cool," arguing the persona was learned and performed so incessantly that Petty and his audience came to experience it as innate. Finally Baudrillard's hyperreal and simulacra frame the conclusion that there never was a "real" Petty, only copies of copies, yet if the perceived sincerity feels real and empowering, it is real enough.

grand-narratives.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
grand-narratives.title: Killing the Griffins: A Murderous Exposition of Postmodernism
grand-narratives.relation: Wisnewski stages a mock murder of the Griffin family to argue that Family Guy 'oozes the postmodern.' Baudrillard's Disneyland analysis explains why the Griffins are dangerously real: they know they are cartoons (the 'we've been cancelled' scene listing failed Fox shows), so their family is no less real than ours, which is likewise modeled on TV images. Lyotard's 'incredulity toward meta-narratives' is embodied in the show's joke-about-everything: the Petoria episode mocking the UN and dictators (Milosevic, Hussein, Khadafi) who party over Seinfeld.
