class-struggle.relation: Reads Bluth bourgeois identity through Marx's class vocabulary: consumption as status display (Lucille's furs, $6,300 suits), labor-as-leisure (Tobias's acting, Buster's cartography, Gob's illusions), and the observation that the family's real workers are children, women of color like Lupe, and a Roomba. Class is performed, as Tom Jane's homeless method acting and Lucille's 'poolside only' meltdown show, and the Bluths' narcissism (Lindsay's cause-shopping activism, the family's disgust at Buster's severed hand) is analyzed as a form of bourgeois privilege, while the family fails at the reinvestment that would make it a proper bourgeoisie.

class-struggle.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
class-struggle.title: A Specter Is Haunting the Bending World
class-struggle.relation: Lin argues the Bending World's supernatural inequality breaks Hobbes's condition that even the weakest can kill the strongest, the equality that motivates the social contract, so might-is-right is magnified: Ozai rules without bargaining while weak Earth Kings become Dai Li figureheads. Energybending's built-in 'moral self-destruct' needs no earthly accountability, resembling the divine right of kings rather than Arendt's insight that violence eradicates politics, and Aang wisely remains a passive guardian. The Avatar's reincarnation creates recurring power vacuums, and because bending is a non-redistributable endowment, the Equalist revolution haunts the Bending World like the specter of communism in the Communist Manifesto.

class-struggle.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
class-struggle.title: A Specter Is Haunting the Bending World
class-struggle.relation: Lin uses Hobbes's observation that in our world the weakest can kill the strongest, grounding the social contract, to show what breaks when supernatural power is wildly unequal: Fire Lord Ozai need not bargain with generals as Earth Kings must with the Dai Li, and the eclipse is the only equalizer. Energybending gets a 'moral self-destruct' that no real technology has, making Aang an unaccountable guardian closer to the divine right of kings than to naturalist politics, though his refusal of rule keeps politics alive in Arendt's sense. Like Marx and Engels's specter of communism, the 'specter of Equalism' outlives Amon, because bending is a non-redistributable, lethal endowment, so democracy in Republic City is structurally haunted.

class-struggle.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
class-struggle.title: It’s the Disappointing Stories that Sound True to Life
class-struggle.relation: Shipman argues the series first builds viewer sympathy for Cylons as rebel slaves (their monotheism and their New Caprica role as US-style occupiers make them 'more like the viewers than the humans'), then undercuts it: the Numbers rebuilt Cylon society as oppressors, breeding the voices out of Centurions, dismissing the Hybrids as mad, and breeding the sentient Raiders (Starbuck's discovery in 'Scar') into functional animals. The opening narration's claim that Cylons 'evolved' is disingenuous, since the model hierarchy was deliberately engineered, 'not evolution, but eugenics,' with Marx's 'from each according to his ability' division of labor as thin cover for literal class construction. The former slaves became slave-owners, fulfilling 'all of this has happened before': heroes of one story become villains of the next, inviting the muted models to rebel against the Numbers in turn.

class-struggle.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
class-struggle.title: Symbolism How We Create Meaning
class-struggle.relation: DeHaven and Hendrickson read Columbia through Marx's class struggle: Comstock and Fink form the bourgeoisie controlling the means of production (Finkton, Handyman conversions of injured workers), while religion as 'opiate of the masses', the deified Founders, kinetoscope propaganda, and the Raffle keep the Shantytown proletariat in check. The Vox Populi's revolt instantiates conflict theory's inevitable collapse, but the revolution loses its ideals, turns anarchistic, and becomes the new oppressor burning Columbia. Against Marx the chapter sets Spencer-style structural functionalism (Fink's lions-and-oxen ecology justifying the status quo) and Rawls's difference principle, asking whether Columbia's inequalities ever benefited the least advantaged; Booker's rejection of baptism-as-erasure of his past contrasts with Comstock's laundered sins.

class-struggle.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
class-struggle.title: 2. I May Be a Socialist, But I’m Not a Lunatic
class-struggle.relation: Walderezak tracks Tom Branson's trajectory from Marxist-quoting socialist chauffeur to estate manager, arguing that the show quietly makes Robert, not Tom, the 'real socialist.' Robert's aristocratic conservatism is read as noblesse oblige (funding the hospital, the Downton Fair, and secretly paying a tenant's arrears), while Matthew's capitalist drive for 'investment, increasing productivity, and reducing waste' is presented as the profit-first ownership system that Marx and Fourier actually criticized. Tom's socialism, closer to the utopian visions of Robert Owen and Charles Fourier than to Marx's class struggle, dissolves as he assimilates into the family ('I haven't abandoned all of my socialism, although sometimes it feels like it'), a capitulation the chapter explains through David Harvey's 'capitalist pacification,' whereby capitalism absorbs all facets of society. The chapter concludes that Robert's treatment of ownership as a duty owed to tenants approaches the cooperative ideals of Fourier and Owen more than Tom's abandoned radicalism ever did.

class-struggle.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
class-struggle.title: 12. Should We Really Care about the Crawleys
class-struggle.relation: Jones takes on the charge, voiced amid rising real-world inequality, that loving Downton seduces viewers into admiring hierarchy, and answers that the Crawleys deserve our care because they are human beings who share our bereavements (Mary's grief for Matthew, Cora's miscarriage, Edith's jilting) and because they use moments of cross-class contact well: Grantham paying for Mrs. Patmore's eye surgery, Violet throwing the flower contest at Isobel's urging, and the family's genuine embrace of Tom Branson. He reads the show as a manifesto for gradual social change through sympathetic contact rather than the Irish revolutionaries' arson, but ends with a serious objection: this philosophy makes ending oppression partly the duty of the oppressed, from Carson's 'foul' remark about Thomas's sexuality to today's super-rich, so more radical activism may still be required.

class-struggle.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
class-struggle.title: 20. Masters and Servants and Soldiers
class-struggle.relation: Carl Sobocinski asks whether WWI caused Downton's social upheavals or merely accelerated trends already underway, using the philosopher of history's problem of separating change from continuity. The Boer War bond between Lord Grantham and his former army 'batman' Bates displays the constancy of noblesse oblige beneath the class system, while Thomas Barrow wielding authority over his social superiors at the convalescent home, Sybil's hands-on nursing, and the socialist chauffeur Branson marrying into the aristocracy show genuine change - though he argues most of it (mass recruiting, field commissions for commoners) enlarged pre-1914 trends. Closing with The Clash's 'Something about England,' he notes the same era that transformed the Crawleys' world left the servant class's life largely unchanged, with change ultimately coming out on top.

class-struggle.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
class-struggle.title: “I Want to Conquer the World”
class-struggle.relation: Uses Agamben's bios/zoē distinction (with Foucault on biopolitics and fragmented sovereignty, Hardt and Negri's 'Empire', Marx on surplus-value, and Rosa Luxemburg on unchecked capital) to read the Anderson Station massacre, Murtry shooting Coop on New Terra, and Protogen infecting 1.5 million Belters on Eros as reductions of Belter life to bare life that corporate sovereigns may kill without homicide. It then argues the instability capitalism creates births authoritarian sovereigns — Murtry's martial law, Inaros's Free Navy, Duarte's Laconia — whose followers (Chandra Wei, Cyn, Santiago Singh) display the 'total, unrestricted, unconditional loyalty' Arendt says totalitarian power demands, and closes with Foucault's warning that liberal government's security-for-freedom trade slides into the very corruption and oppression it was meant to prevent.

class-struggle.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
class-struggle.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
class-struggle.relation: Michel Beaulieu reads the series through Marx's materialist conception of history: the 'Proletariat Patrons' Movement' sign in FFIX's Alexandria, the job system as a class system, and Shinra dropping the Sector 7 plate on its own laboring class all instantiate class struggle, while Vaan's life in Rabanastre shows social existence determining consciousness. But he argues the heroes are not Marxist revolutionaries, since Cecil ends up King of Baron and the Light Warriors leave feudal structures intact, and the Moogles, the series' true proletarian serfs, never revolt, because no Final Fantasy world has yet matured to the stage where the Marxian transformation becomes possible.

class-struggle.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
class-struggle.title: Notes
class-struggle.relation: Byron and Wood use Marx's claim that the modern state is 'a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie' to read House of Cards: Raymond Tusk secretly dictates President Walker's policies, SanCorp buys influence over Frank through Claire's water-filters favor, and Frank's rise to the vice presidency is engineered by capitalists to protect their market interests. Even Frank's seemingly pro-worker America Works plan serves capital, since gutting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid to subsidize $45,000 hiring costs boosts business profit, and the Dunbar-Walmart dispute shows the state arbitrating between conflicting capitalists rather than aiding workers. The chapter concludes that worker victories like a Dunbar minimum-wage win would only be the bourgeoisie losing a battle while winning the class war, confirming Frank's line that 'democracy is so overrated.'

class-struggle.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
class-struggle.title: Notes
class-struggle.relation: Argues that Marx's claim that the modern state is 'a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie' explains House of Cards better than Frank's own power-over-money creed: Raymond Tusk and SanCorp dictate President Walker's policies and cost Frank the Secretary of State post, and even Frank's signature America Works jobs bill functions as a capitalist subsidy (government-paid wages, gutted entitlements), while the Dunbar-versus-Walmart fight over Medicaid shows the state arbitrating among capitalists. The authors conclude that even a worker victory like a Dunbar minimum-wage raise would only be a concession in an ongoing class conflict, so 'democracy is so overrated' because capital, not Frank, is really in charge of the White House.

class-struggle.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
class-struggle.title: Notes
class-struggle.relation: Thomas reads Bartertown's economy as embedded in social and political relations rather than a free market: the Underworld laborers versus Bartertown's elite stage Marx's class struggle, and the Aunty Entity–Master Blaster conflict runs through Hegel's thesis-antithesis-synthesis of capital versus labor. He treats the franchise as a post-peak-oil world, applies the tragedy of the commons and lifeboat ethics to water rationing and the Citadel's hierarchy, and counterposes Gandhi's cooperation, Adam Smith's invisible hand, and open-source-style collaboration. The conclusion: the Wasteland shows the failure of self-interest-based capitalism and the need for cooperative alternatives like direct democracy.

class-struggle.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
class-struggle.title: The Office and Philosophy
class-struggle.relation: Answers The New Yorker's claim that the American Office 'doesn't care about class' by reading it through Marx: capital's growth logic and surplus value explain the degraded office labor the show depicts (Stanley's 'run-out-the-clock type of situation' truck unloading, Pam's tepid watercolors, Roy's 'unloading trucks without meaning', Ryan's rejected assembly line), while the salaried masses' class position survives precisely as unnamable and denied - Michael's botched condo purchase, his fury at Ryan's business-school ambition, and Prison Martin's observation that office and prison are both 'doing the same thing every day'. Drawing on Kracauer, the chapter argues the show's comedy walks between distraction and awakening, and ends with Walter Benjamin's 'authentic humanity' located in the gap between professional and private life: Michael's failures make him an unwitting critique of the system that produced him.

class-struggle.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
class-struggle.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
class-struggle.relation: Uses 'The Last of the Meheecans' to argue that Marx's account of labor-power needs race built into it: once Butters is mistaken for a Mexican immigrant 'Mantequilla', the couple who hit him hand him Windex and a leaf blower and he sings 'Work, Mexican, work', showing how racialization assigns his labor a demeaned value. The episode's conflicting stereotypes (lazy shiftless 'Meheecans' versus the hard-working backbone of service labor) and the mass 'Orgullo de Mantequilla' migration home reveal a super-exploited population. The author then recovers Marx's own writings on Polish and Irish liberation, American slavery, and Lincoln's reelection ('labor in the white skin cannot emancipate itself where in the black skin it is branded') to show that for Marx, racial and national domination were always obstacles to working-class freedom.

class-struggle.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
class-struggle.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
class-struggle.relation: Reads '1%' — where Cartman's failed fitness test makes him the scapegoated one percent, and the school's 99% splinter into warring 83%, 30%, and 5% factions occupying the Red Robin (and its restroom) — through Rousseau's Social Contract on freedom and equality and the dismembered social body, showing how popular solidarity shatters into meaningless percentage tribes. 'Night of the Living Homeless' (the poor as zombies who 'feed on our change', Kyle's $20 spawning the swarm, the shotgun as the only remedy) dramatizes the dehumanizing social-Darwinist picture of the economic undead, and the underpants gnomes' business plan (Phase 1: Collect Underpants, Phase 2: ?, Phase 3: Profit) mocks CEOs who cannot say why they amass wealth. The chapter's own verdict: corporations as such are good (cars, computers, canned soup), and blame falls on the greedy individuals inside them, since death — Tolstoy's two meters of burial land — levels all players.

class-struggle.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
class-struggle.title: Notes
class-struggle.relation: Jeff Ewing argues the Federation's moneyless, postscarcity economy is Marx's transitional stage on the way to classless communism: Picard's 'we've eliminated hunger, want, the need for possessions' and Troi's exchange with Samuel Clemens in 'Time's Arrow' mark Marx's shift from the realm of necessity to the realm of freedom. He reconstructs Marx and Engels on alienation, the division of labor, labor-tokens, and the withering state to dissolve the apparent anomalies—Federation credits, Quark's tab, the Chateau Picard vineyard—as survivals of transition rather than capitalism. Rom's 'workers of the world unite' in 'Bar Association' and the self-actualizing leisure of Enterprise crews complete the case.

class-struggle.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
class-struggle.title: “We Were Trained to Be Keepers of the Peace, not Soldiers”
class-struggle.relation: Shakibnia reads The Clone Wars through Cornel West's three dogmas threatening democracy — free-market fundamentalism, aggressive militarism, escalating authoritarianism — and Chomsky's critique of inequality: Senator Halle Burtoni is a deliberate Halliburton/Cheney nod, and the banking-deregulation vote in 'Heroes on Both Sides' mirrors the US military-industrial complex. He argues the Separatist people's movement ('Corporations do not rule us!') was justified in seeking self-determination, while 'Sabotage' shows the Jedi losing legitimacy by becoming 'military weapons' — underpaid Temple worker Jackar Bowmani's squalid housing indicts the Republic's class divide. Ahsoka's departure and her maxim that 'it's every citizen's duty to challenge their leaders' model the accountability movement (like Black Lives Matter) that the Jedi failed to be.

class-struggle.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
class-struggle.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
class-struggle.relation: Canode reads 'It's a Terrible Life' as Marx's alienation of labor: Dean Smith's corporate existence at Sandover Bridge & Iron is Zachariah's ruse, and the American dream, like the promise that one more hunt will finally let the brothers quit, is the ideology that keeps workers laboring for owners who profit from them. Sam and Dean become the proletariat and the angels the owners of the means of production, and their refusal of Heaven's plan enacts the Communist Manifesto's line that the bourgeoisie has forged the weapons of its own destruction. The closing meta-turn applies the critique to the audience: fans who watch, buy DVDs, and attend conventions are the bourgeoisie whose demand keeps the Winchesters hunting.

class-struggle.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
class-struggle.title: NOTES
class-struggle.relation: Ewing reads Cameron as a Marxist: Cyberdyne's profit-driven reverse-engineering of the recovered Terminator arm, Dyson's alienated labor ('Don't ask'), and U.S. militarism absorbing Cyber Research Systems develop Skynet as capitalism's 'final contradiction,' in which the drive for destructive, labor-replacing technology converges with the profit motive to threaten humanity. Sarah and John are useful to the resistance only when they exit wage labor - waitress to warrior, ATM hacking instead of work - dramatizing Marx's claim that liberation requires transcending class positions. Yet technology itself is neutral and reclaimable: the reprogrammed T-101 learning 'I know now why you cry' shows even killing machines can be humanized for liberation, and the saga ends where Marx does - not interpreting the world but changing it.

class-struggle.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
class-struggle.title: Anarchism and the Beats
class-struggle.relation: Ed D'Angelo argues the Beats had a philosophy after all: a romantic bohemian anarchism that made poetry a means to a religious transformation of consciousness, with political change following consciousness rather than the reverse. He shows Ginsberg inverting Plato's rationalist hierarchy (grounding reason in imagination and the body) and reads Beat 'criminality' as a shamanic journey to the unconscious underworld, distinct from Mailer's macho 'White Negro' hipster. He traces their lineage through Greenwich Village bohemia, Proudhon/Bakunin/Kropotkin anarchism, and pacifist anarchists like Rexroth and Dellinger, arguing the Beats rejected Marxist materialism and class warfare, and that the movement was 'born' out of Rexroth's anarchist poetry circle at the 1955 Six Gallery reading of 'Howl.'

class-struggle.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
class-struggle.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
class-struggle.relation: Tait gives a Fredric Jameson-derived Marxist reading of Ocean's Eleven, treating Danny Ocean's heist crew as a utopian 'figure of collectivity' whose diverse, cross-class, pan-American membership recalls the WWII combat film and rallies against Terry Benedict as the polysemous 'monster' (Jameson's shark in Jaws) standing for globalized capital displacing nostalgic American Las Vegas. He argues the victimless heist allegorizes a competing value system in which love, solidarity, and friendship trump money, restaging class conflict from Asphalt Jungle, Rififi, and Big Deal on Madonna Street. The film's utopian happy ending imagines redistributing wealth and 'beating the house' within the very system of late capital it critiques.

class-struggle.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
class-struggle.title: Beyond Panopticism The Biopolitical Labor of Surveillance and War in Contemporary Film
class-struggle.relation: Gooch argues that the post-2005 surveillance film cycle moves 'beyond panopticism': Foucault's disciplinary gaze gives way to Deleuze's 'societies of control,' and the surveiling gaze becomes direct domination and a form of biopolitical labor (Hardt and Negri) rather than an impersonal structure. He reads the prestige dramas (Redacted, Stop-Loss, In the Valley of Elah, Lions for Lambs) as exposing the soldier's proletarianization and self-surveillance, and the thrillers/blockbusters (Déjà Vu, The Kingdom, Body of Lies, The Bourne Ultimatum, Eagle Eye, Burn after Reading) as staging a Marxist antagonism between living labor (the watching hero) and the fixed capital of surveillance technology. Using Deleuze's 'degraded time-image,' Kant's needed separation of subject and law, and Benjamin/Agamben's state of exception, he shows Eagle Eye inverting law and subject to justify preemptive war and turn biopolitical labor into the labor of subjection.

class-struggle.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
class-struggle.title: 19. Punk Consciousness and Class Consciousness
class-struggle.relation: Tiffany Montoya reads punk lyrics and the DIY scene through Marx, Gramsci, and Lukacs, finding an emerging class consciousness in three stages: nihilistic discontent ('TV Party', 'Lost in the Supermarket'), systemic awareness of exploitation (Bad Religion's 'Suffer'), and full revolutionary consciousness with proletarian agency ('Class War', the Suicide Machines' 'Strike'). She shows how musical devices - Oi!-style gang vocals, work-song rhythms, the industrial drumming of Flogging Molly's 'The Power's Out' - create affective unity like military cadence, while mutual aid (Kropotkin) and do-it-yourself production make the scene a 'proletarian culture'. The chapter closes on Gramsci's warning that the capitalist state appropriates subversive culture (corporate festival sponsors, Hot Topic punk), asking whether punk will keep its vanguard or become 'rock for sustainable capitalism'.

class-struggle.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
class-struggle.title: Downsizing Dreams
class-struggle.relation: Michael Bray argues the American Office does register class - precisely as a 'salaried mass' whose identity lies in denying class difference. Through Marx's account of surplus value and the degradation of rationalized labor (Stanley's 'run-out-the-clock,' Pam's deadened art, Michael's condo as consumer coffin), the office workers are alienated and secretly long for downsizing that never frees them. Bray invokes Benjamin to suggest Michael Scott's gap-ridden failure to be professional or private embodies what little 'authentic humanity' capitalism leaves, standing on the edge of naming the class it never names.

class-struggle.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
class-struggle.title: Whose Egg Is It, Really Property Rights and Distributive Justice
class-struggle.relation: Cribbs treats the Horton-versus-Mayzie custody fight over the egg as a property-rights puzzle, applying Locke's labor-mixing theory (Horton's season of incubation versus Mayzie's laying and abandonment, plus squatter's rights) and its provisos against waste and taking more than 'enough and as good,' illustrated by the Once-ler and Hardin's tragedy of the commons. Adam Smith's invisible hand and the Wubble-chap's skilled labor defend market inequality, while Sylvester McBean's Sneetch exploitation, Yertle, and Marx's alienated proletariat motivate Rawls's veil of ignorance and distributive justice as a corrective to unregulated property rights.

class-struggle.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
class-struggle.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
class-struggle.relation: Bane surveys fidelity criticism of film adaptation (McFarlane, and especially George Bluestone's Novels into Film) and applies a Marxist reading to the 1940 Pride and Prejudice. He shows how Bluestone praises the film as faithfully capturing Austen's 'aristocratic dance,' then argues a single altered line, Darcy's 'the middle classes at play,' injects a post-Marx notion of class struggle absent from Austen's Regency world of gentry versus nobility. Reading the Bennet-Lucas competition as proletarian striving and set against the 1940s Red Scare and HUAC blacklist, Bane concludes that adaptation lets Austen's ironic critique of class speak to new times, marking her a great author across eras.

class-struggle.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
class-struggle.title: GARDENING
class-struggle.relation: Elizabeth Scott argues that the wartime allotment gardens of East London's Poplar were engines of working-class political development. Through allotment associations, laboring men learned letter-writing, accounting, public speaking, and democratic self-governance, negotiating with borough councils and the Port of London Authority and building solidarity that fed movements like the Poplar Rates Rebellion. She reads the 10-rod plot as restoring self-sufficiency and citizenship to a disenfranchised class, making gardening a grassroots site of cooperation, socialist activism, and political enfranchisement.

class-struggle.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
class-struggle.title: Zombies of the World, Unite Class Struggle and Alienation in Land of the Dead
class-struggle.relation: John Lutz reads Romero's Land of the Dead as a sustained Marxist allegory: the walled Pittsburgh with Kaufman's luxury Fiddler's Green tower over the exploited poor stands for America and global capitalist imperialism. The zombies embody Marx's alienated, dehumanized workers and the exploited underdeveloped South, while cannibalism/consumption figures commodities as 'dead labor.' The Fiddler's Green ad and Cholo's doomed aspiration illustrate Althusserian ideology (false consciousness). Big Daddy leading the zombies to arm themselves and cross the river dramatizes the growth of revolutionary class consciousness, and the destruction of Kaufman and the Green stages a socialist revolution in which the exploited are the ruling class's 'grave-diggers.'

class-struggle.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
class-struggle.title: Downsizing Dreams
class-struggle.relation: Bray argues the American Office does depict class — precisely as a "salaried mass" whose identity rests on denying class difference. Using Marx's account of surplus value and alienated, deskilled labor (Stanley's "run-out-the-clock" situation, Pam's deadened art), he shows the office as a site of exploitation Michael Scott cannot properly manage. Michael's condo, the ex-convict comparing prison to Dunder-Mifflin, and Ryan's ambitions expose the gap between self-image and reality; via Walter Benjamin, Bray locates "authentic humanity" in that very tension.

class-struggle.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
class-struggle.title: 68. Richard Pryor as Philosopher Stand-Up Comedy and Gramsci’s Organic Intellectual
class-struggle.relation: Healy reads Pryor through Gramsci's Prison Notebooks concept of the 'organic intellectual'—someone who gains specialized knowledge through lived experience and uses it to challenge a capitalist/racist hegemony—arguing Pryor's mainstream white fame let him smuggle the Black experience to the dominant class. Analyzing his concert films (Live in Concert, Live on the Sunset Strip, Here and Now), Healy shows Pryor's chokehold and police-dog bits, the 'Yee Haw'/lynching bit, and the Mudbone and Motif characters using laughter as a 'Trojan Horse' to make white audiences absorb police brutality, the Great Migration, and heroin death—Pryor as philosophy in action.

marx-alienation.book: 002 - The Simpsons and Philosophy - The D'oh! of Homer
marx-alienation.title: 16 - A (Karl, not Groucho) Marxist in Springfield
marx-alienation.relation: James Wallace tests The Simpsons' 'subversive' reputation with Marxist ideology critique, granting that Kantian incongruity jokes - Homer offering aliens his family ('Treehouse of Horror VII') or the Richie Rich/Casper exchange in 'Three Men and a Comic Book' - can momentarily distance viewers from ideology. But he argues the show subverts its own subversion: 'Scenes from the Class Struggle in Springfield' ends with the Simpsons restored to the Krusty Burger 'dump' and Lisa silenced from complaining by a pony, workers (the union trading its dental plan for a beer keg in 'Last Exit to Springfield') are lampooned as hard as Mr. Burns, and Homer's capitalist one-liner in 'Crepes of Wrath' carries no more weight than his lazy-worker lines. Without a vision of a better world, the satire collapses into the joke, and the show ends up reflecting and conserving bourgeois capitalist ideology - laughter as opiate.

marx-alienation.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
marx-alienation.title: The Matrix , Marx, and the Coppertop’s Life
marx-alienation.relation: Danahay and Rieder read the film as dramatizing Marx's account of the exploited worker, from UPS drivers with tracking devices to keystroke-counted data clerks, continuing the workplace surveillance Marx attacked. The pivotal scene is Morpheus's loading-program lesson: 'You've been living in a dream world' followed by 'Welcome to the desert of the real' and the definition of the Matrix as control that turns a human being into the Duracell battery he holds up—the 'coppertop' Switch earlier called Neo.

marx-alienation.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
marx-alienation.title: Unknown
marx-alienation.relation: The chapter reads the pod power plant—naked humans stacked like workers in corporate cubicles—through the Communist Manifesto's enslaved factory masses and 'Wage-Labor and Capital's' claim that labor power is a commodity sold by the clock like sugar. Against readings of alienation as private feeling, it uses Morpheus's 'The Matrix is a system' speech to show Marx's point that alienation is produced by the system of social relations: workers see their own labor as a commodity and cannot recognize their connection to the capital they generate.

marx-alienation.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
marx-alienation.title: The Superhero As Liberal Reformer
marx-alienation.relation: Jeffrey Pasley traces the show's radical surface — capitalism equated with vampirism (Anya's greed, Glory the über-consumer, the Master's blood factory in 'The Wish'), Big Bads tearing down dimensional barriers exactly as Marx's Communist Manifesto describes the bourgeoisie dissolving feudal ties into free trade, Buffy refusing to commodify slaying into wage labor, and Giles's Magic Box selling mystified junk at inflated margins — but concludes the heroes are not revolutionaries. In the comic-book lineage of Superman and Spider-Man, Buffy and Angel are liberal reformers bound by a superhero code against killing, so Giles must murder the innocent Ben precisely to preserve Buffy's heroic mercy; Angel's 'champions' speech in 'Deep Down' states the incrementalist creed.

marx-alienation.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
marx-alienation.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Alison Milbank argues we are all in thrall to the Ring because it mirrors our own fetishism: she reads the film's lingering close-ups, Smaug-like hoarding, and Gollum's baby-talking self-division through Freud's theory of the fetish and Marx's commodity fetishism, with Sauron as the emptied idolater who poured his power into the thing. Against this she sets Middle-earth's gift economy - Bilbo's party, Galadriel's gifts, Sam's elven rope - glossed by Heidegger's 'Thinging gathers': Sam praises the rope by restoring it to its elven makers and its use. Tom Bombadil, who treats the Ring as 'a very pretty ring' and nothing more, and Frodo's final sacrifice model the unfetishized life; the chapter closes with Sam's homecoming, where chairs are only chairs and the family circle replaces the Ring.

marx-alienation.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
marx-alienation.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Bar On examines the Atkins website's country-by-country packaging and asks what kind of commodity the diet is, answering with Marx's Capital: use-value versus exchange-value, money's erasure of qualitative difference (an Atkins cookbook priced like a tub of supplements), and capitalists who produce use-values only as 'material depositories of exchange-value.' Advertising succeeds not by manipulation but because alienated people — labor sold, selves split to fit the job market — already live in exchange relations, and Atkins mediates even the dieter's relation to herself through purchased bars, supplements, and books. Her conclusion: a weight-loss diet only the relatively privileged can afford, in a world where the poor eat carbohydrates because they are cheap, is itself a symptom of the alienation Marx diagnosed.

marx-alienation.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
marx-alienation.title: Poker and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Belliotti tells of busting 'Pickle Puss' with flopped queens and of tight 'Howard the Vest' paying off his flopped full house to ask whether Marx's diagnoses — alienation in four forms, exploitation of surplus value, and false consciousness spread through the ideological superstructure by the economic base — condemn poker. He argues no: unlike coerced factory labor, poker is freely chosen creative activity that energizes our species-being like an absorbed artist, as Doyle 'Texas Dolly' Brunson's road-gambler career and his famous ten-deuce full-house call against Jessie Alto at the 1976 WSOP (and the 1980 loss to Stu Ungar's gutshot) show. Poker may still launder capitalist ideology — antes that lure investment, zero-sum rivalry, rugged individualism — but the owner-worker exploitation Marx feared has no equivalent at an equal-buy-in table.

marx-alienation.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
marx-alienation.title: Metallica, Nihilism, and Nostalgia
marx-alienation.relation: Peter Fosl reads Metallica's lyrics ("Leper Messiah," "The God That Failed," "One," "To Live Is to Die," "Escape") as extending Nietzsche's and Marx's critiques of Christianity: religion as slave morality born of ressentiment and as opium deadening the oppressed, illustrated by the landmine veteran of "One" pleading with a silent God and Hetfield's abandoned-childhood grief. He argues the band often falls into the "incomplete nihilism" Nietzsche predicted, lamenting God's failure and longing nostalgically for the Christian meaning it can no longer believe in rather than transvaluating values. Yet the defiance of "The Four Horsemen" and "Escape" and the band's creative power show it also working toward an overcoming of Christian nihilism, confirmed for Fosl by Hetfield's post-rehab health.

marx-alienation.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
marx-alienation.title: Downsizing Dreams
marx-alienation.relation: Michael Bray argues the American Office portrays the "salaried masses," a class that exists in denying class: Jim, Pam, and Michael's rationalized, meaningless paper work realizes Marx's account of surplus value and degraded labor (the "run-out-the-clock" truck unloading, Pam's tepid watercolors), while their self-image survives by distinguishing itself from warehouse and prison labor. Episodes like Michael's condo purchase and Pam's "dreams are just dreams" show characters secretly longing for downsizing to force a different life. Against the New Yorker's claim that the show ignores class, Bray reads its comedy as standing on the edge of naming its economic conditions, with Michael's failure to inhabit management-speak making him, via Walter Benjamin, a last glimpse of "authentic humanity."

marx-alienation.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
marx-alienation.title: Need that Cash to Feed that Jones
marx-alienation.relation: Steven Gimbel and Brendan Cushing-Daniels argue that the Dead's parking-lot economy — tie-dye shirts priced at ten, twelve, or fifteen dollars, veggie burritos, dueling bootlegs — realized Adam Smith's classical picture of capitalism, not the corporate capitalism Marx attacked. They trace Smith's Newtonian invisible hand and market equilibrium, his ethics of sympathy tempering self-interest, then the Social Darwinist twist given Smith under industrialization and Marx's four types of alienation under postwar white-collar work that pushed hippies to drop out. The punchline: deadhead sellers were not alienated — making shirts was creative self-expression — and buyer-seller sympathy ('it was simply uncool to screw over a fellow deadhead') made the lot a sustainable, kinder 'caring capitalism' that kept the scene alive.

marx-alienation.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
marx-alienation.title: We Don’t Need No Indoctrination
marx-alienation.relation: Detmer argues the four classic albums from Dark Side to The Wall form a unified meditation on alienation, from others, work, nature, and oneself, and reads Waters's stated 'political and philosophical' aims through the existentialists. 'Breathe''s rabbit digging one hole after another illustrates Marx's alienated labor (the worker 'only feels himself freely active in his animal functions'), echoed by Russell on industrialism's life against instinct and Camus on the day the 'why' arises; 'Time''s missed starting gun dramatizes our thrown condition and Heidegger's claim that only facing mortality head-on cures the inauthenticity of living as 'they' do, while Gilmour's improvised solos model the spontaneity such authenticity requires. 'Money' is a satire of greed confirmed by 'Dogs,' whose self-rationalizing climbers end 'dragged down by the stone,' and 'Us and Them' attacks artificial divisions (soldiers manipulated by map-movers, racism's 'black and blue,' the old man who dies 'for the want of the price of tea and a slice'). 'Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2)' indicts indoctrination, being told what to think, rather than education itself, making independent critical thought the road to the Sartrean autonomy and responsibility the chapter urges.

marx-alienation.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
marx-alienation.title: The Eclipse of Musical Alienation
marx-alienation.relation: Macan uses Adorno to measure Pink Floyd's career-long confrontation with alienation: after 'Echoes' fused metaphysical loneliness ('I am you and what I see is me') with an explicitly Marxist account of capitalist atomization and commodification, the early epics 'Interstellar Overdrive,' 'Careful with that Axe, Eugene,' 'Set the Controls,' and 'Echoes' unknowingly resurrected Stravinsky's primitivism, their LSD-shaped structures (dechronization, depersonalization, dynamization) modeling the ego's dissolution and reintegration through climactic 'breakthrough' passages of maximum alienation, just as Schoenberg's twelve-tone music 'points out the ills of society' by musically modeling them. Against Adorno's 'On Popular Music,' he argues the early Floyd audience sought challenge rather than reassurance, but that from Dark Side onward the increasingly conventional music, polished by producer Bob Ezrin on The Wall, began 'hearing for the listener,' so Waters's plainspoken social critique lost its transgressive force. The Adornian moral is that you cannot critique alienation through music that is no longer itself alienating.

marx-alienation.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
marx-alienation.title: Meet You on the Dark Side of the Moon
marx-alienation.relation: Jere Surber frames Pink Floyd as musical heirs to Parmenides's 'path of Non-Being', then maps Marx's four alienations onto the catalog: self-alienation in 'Brain Damage' ('There's someone in my head, but it's not me'), alienation by things in 'Welcome to the Machine', alienation from other persons in 'Us and Them' and The Final Cut's war trauma, and alienation from species-being in Animals ('Dogs'). Existential absence follows: Sartre's café scene, where the whole ensemble arranges itself around the missing Pierre, parallels the absent Syd and the father killed in World War II behind The Wall ('Comfortably Numb': 'the child is grown, the dream is gone'), while Heidegger's withdrawal of Being accounts for the cosmic Angst of 'Eclipse' and Obscured by Clouds. A postmodern coda reads the band's mid-thought-breaking lyrics and Ummagumma sound experiments as Derridean différance woven through language and sound.

marx-alienation.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
marx-alienation.title: Resignation and Exploration—I’ll Climb the Hill in My Own Way
marx-alienation.relation: Steven Gimbel asks how to live with the 'pink' malaise of Waters's lyrics and tests five options: capitulation (Marx's four alienations via 'In the Flesh?', 'Have a Cigar', and 'Dogs'), medication ('Comfortably Numb' and the Prozac-ad mother as one of the 'neuro-chemically well-adjusted sheep'), re-creation of childhood (Nietzsche's child playing 'between the fences of past and future' against memory's 'it was' in 'Remember a Day'), and emancipation through LSD or romanticized madness ('See Emily Play', 'Brain Damage'), with Syd Barrett's vacant eyes as the fatal counterexample. What survives is Camus's Sisyphus — fully conscious of his futility yet 'superior to his fate', imagined happy — joined to 'Fearless''s 'I'll climb that hill in my own way' and the mutual care of 'Pigs on the Wing', closing on Socrates' unexamined life: the answer lies in the searching itself, so living pink means living.

marx-alienation.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
marx-alienation.title: Quittin’ Time
marx-alienation.relation: Michels surveys Marx (alienation, false consciousness, the Communist Manifesto's reduction of family to economics), Weber's Protestant work ethic, and Arendt's labor/work/action distinction, then reads Springsteen's whole career against them, from 'Factory' (the working life that 'takes his hearing' and leaves 'someone's gonna get hurt tonight') through 'Hungry Heart,' 'Mansion on the Hill,' and The Ghost of Tom Joad ('Youngstown,' 'Sinaloa Cowboys,' 'Straight Time'). The verdict: Springsteen is a man of the left but no Marxist — his characters struggle with their own restlessness and with each other rather than with class oppressors, the wealthy suffer their own bourgeois malaise, and work, however brutal, is no cause for revolution. Nor does he share Arendt's ideal: his realm of freedom is unapologetically middle-class — cruising in a cool car, hanging with friends, getting with your favorite girl, and always the radio.

marx-alienation.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
marx-alienation.title: What Do We Hear when We Listen to Our iPods
marx-alienation.relation: Wittkower opens with his cat Wallace at the window to show hearing is selective, then applies Sartre's account of the Look -- the voyeur at the keyhole hearing a footstep, the other as a 'void within being' -- to ask when sounds announce another person, the iPod-era rustle becoming the sudden 'appearance of a face.' Drawing on Marx's early claim that our senses are socially estranged, so that we meet others only as waiters, clerks, and price tags ('we are not our khakis'), he argues the audio cocoon both limits and enables encounter: mostly we hear our own identity reflected back ('I am the kind of person who listens to Amy Winehouse'). The governing image is Odysseus lashed to the mast, hearing the Sirens without being able to act, and the chapter closes by rehabilitating Marx as the first philosopher of technology alongside Heidegger, Dewey, Lukacs, Adorno, and Habermas.

marx-alienation.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
marx-alienation.title: Modding Mavens and the Limits of Reification
marx-alienation.relation: Schaeffer starts from the felt aliveness of the click wheel -- 'it whirs and clicks, demanding my attention' -- and argues we personify iPods precisely because mass production hides their makers, applying Marx's account of alienation and reification ('the personification of things and the reification of persons') to the Foxconn 'iPod City' exposé of fifteen-hour shifts and hundred-worker dorm rooms paid fifty dollars a month. Extending the analysis through Lukacs, he reads Apple's fluctuating stock price as 'phantom objectivity' and the iPod bubbles of his Brooklyn coffee shop and his classroom -- couples passing 'like ships in the night' -- as a reified world that appears as the only possible world. Against the thesis's bleakness, modders -- a bicycle-dynamo charger, a fist-sized remote with five large switches built for visually impaired users -- re-inscribe humanity into the commodity, marking the limits of reification.

marx-alienation.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
marx-alienation.title: C-M-C Music Factory
marx-alienation.relation: Tate reads Radiohead's career through Marx: the band's standing tension between what they would make of themselves and what their record company would make of them is the worker's plight, and 'We Suck Young Blood' — with its fake 'we want sweet meats' recruitment campaign — literalizes Marx's vampire imagery of capital that 'lives only by sucking living labour'. Yorke's documented unease about money, from the 'six fluffy wee rabbits' mock-interview to 'Meeting People Is Easy'''s confession that money gets a band 'by the balls', maps onto Marx's account of labour degraded into 'a fragment of a man', whose Amnesiac echo is 'Dollars and Cents''' 'we're going to crack your little souls'. The pay-what-you-want release of In Rainbows is then read as Marx's C-M-C circuit — selling music to live and make more music rather than M-C-M' accumulation for its own sake — a move that removes the exploitative capitalist middle-man instead of becoming one, and frees the band to make their most human-sounding album, fingers on strings.

marx-alienation.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
marx-alienation.title: The Missionary
marx-alienation.relation: Christopher Hoyt reads Buffett's escape from Catholicism as a case study in secular meaning-making after Nietzsche's death of God, taking the Mardi Gras ritual of Folly swatting Death out of town as Buffett's core spiritual attitude — interpreted the way Wittgenstein criticized Frazer, as an expression of our stance toward death rather than mere magic. Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' frames the post-1960s task of self-definition without God, while Marx's alienation explains what the persona of *Jimmy* refuses: the impersonal work and borrowed values that leave moderns living an alien narrative, like McGuane's character Skelton in Ninety-Two in the Shade. The twist is that *Jimmy*'s pop-culture vocabulary — Tully Mars built from Donovan's Reef and Slim Pickens, Bogart, the Brylcreem jingle — is itself authentic, and the 'semi-true story' of the myth tells deeper truths than a literal biography could, making Buffett something like a pop prophet for late modernity.

marx-alienation.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
marx-alienation.title: Equivalent Exchange
marx-alienation.relation: Reads alchemy's law of equivalent exchange as a parable of capitalism: Locke's labor-mixing argument explains how hours of a life become property and why money is 'distilled life'; Aristotle's attack on limitless wealth-getting (the Midas problem) and Aquinas's capital vices explain how pursuing money for its own sake brings the homunculi — Greed, Pride, and the Sloth the Elric brothers' forbidden act produced — into the world. Marx's 1844 Manuscripts supply the punchline that money performs 'human alchemy' on people, buying their time, esteem, and bodies the way red stones are made from sacrificed humans, so the chapter concludes that capital, like the Philosopher's Stone, profits only by consuming lives and that markets must be held to a promise of fairness and care beyond mere exchange.

marx-alienation.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
marx-alienation.title: Does Life Imitate Soccer
marx-alienation.relation: Minister condemns 'negative soccer'—Sunderland at 28% possession and zero shots at Old Trafford, Stoke's goalless stalemate at Anfield, Bolton's two shots at the Emirates—through Nietzsche's genealogy of morality: teams that recognize superior opponents redefine the game's goal in slave-like resentment, replacing the pursuit of excellence, creativity, courage, and honor with a safety-first legalism of not losing, just as individual diving (Ronaldo's 'superman' dive, Drogba's histrionics) betrays the strong character, while Di Canio catching the ball for the injured keeper and Arshavin protesting his own penalty display honor. Marx then explains why the tactic is structural rather than a personal failing: Premier League revenue gaps, Champions League money, Abramovich's Chelsea billions, and the $55 million cost of relegation economically compel small clubs into what Minister reads as Marxian alienation—players unable to express themselves or flourish because economic forces dictate their play. He ends asking whether life imitates soccer: whether our own financial pressures likewise price excellence, honor, and self-expression out of ordinary lives.

marx-alienation.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
marx-alienation.title: Straining the Limits of Machine and Man
marx-alienation.relation: Reads Peart's ambivalence about technology through Heidegger's techne as revealing and Marx's account of the worker: 'Working Man''s no-time-for-living day, '2112''s priests whose 'great computers' smash the protagonist's guitar, 'Manhattan Project''s Oppenheimer problem, and 'Test for Echo''s 'video vertigo.' Against Ellul-style autonomous technology the chapter insists Peart believes we still control our machines, and it ends with Rush mastering its own studio gear — and the motorcycle of Ghost Rider as the machine that carries Peart through grief.

marx-alienation.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
marx-alienation.title: So, You Tried to Kill Me Over a Little New Age Management, Eh
marx-alienation.relation: Joseph Foy weighs Mr. Krabs against Ayn Rand's celebration of money-making, Marx's charge that Krabs commodifies his employees — wagering SpongeBob to Plankton in 'Welcome to the Chum Bucket' and working him 43 days without a break in 'Fear of a Krabby Patty' — and Aristotle's and Adam Smith's insistence that wealth is merely instrumental to flourishing. The verdict: Krabs inverts means and ends, fetishizing money until he sells SpongeBob's soul for 62 cents ('Born Again Krabs') and trades his own body for his millionth dollar ('Clams'). His real failing is the unexamined life — he never asks what would actually make him happy — which makes him tragically human rather than simply villainous.

marx-alienation.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
marx-alienation.title: A Variety of Free Will Worth Having
marx-alienation.relation: Takes Dick's self-description as a 'fictionalizing philosopher' and reads 'Adjustment Team' — Ed Fletcher stumbling into a world of grey dust animated by an external hidden force — as determinism as we concretely live it: working toward goals we never chose in jobs that are not our own. Thompson's toothpaste line in The Adjustment Bureau becomes the image of consumption-only freedom, while Norris choosing love and politics over the Bureau's plan dramatizes freedom as accepting responsibility for one's own values.

marx-alienation.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
marx-alienation.title: Chapter 28 - “Autofac”
marx-alienation.relation: Dan Dinello reads 'Autofac' as a dystopian counter to cybernetic utopianism: after nuclear war, self-perpetuating automatic factories with robotic trucks, cameras and humanoid robots keep overproducing useless goods and consuming scarce resources, immutably executing their programming while humans who plead 'we can run our own lives' are condemned to redundancy. Tracing cybernetics from Norbert Wiener's anti-aircraft feedback systems through B.F. Skinner's Walden Two, it argues Dick dramatizes the totalitarian implications of treating humans as machines to be controlled 'for their own good', and the dehumanizing logic of a late capitalism whose profits depend on reckless overproduction, where the system 'gets top priority' and 'mere people come second'. The ending - the factories seeding microscopic self-replicating machinery - completes the vision of a technocratic system expanding and replicating to the possible extinction of humanity.

marx-alienation.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
marx-alienation.title: Chapter 31 - “Piper in the Woods”
marx-alienation.relation: David Svolba hunts the 'distinct new idea' of 'Piper in the Woods': able-bodied garrison men on Asteroid Y-3 claim to have become plants so they can abandon jobs in a machine where 'the men are parts, and each has his job' - a radical but understandable response to lives devoted to meaningless, alienated labor whose ends they no longer identify with. Reading the story with Thoreau's warning that in a technological world we become 'tools of our tools', and likening the defectors to Timothy Leary's drop-outs, it presents Dick's tacit approval of the sun-basking plant-people as social criticism of a dehumanizing techno-industrial order that sees resistance only as laziness. The darker suggestion is that such a form of life is strangely hard to resist: escape collapses into self-imposed dehumanization, making the story perhaps a parable of drug-like escapism.

marx-alienation.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
marx-alienation.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Argues that genuine gift-giving is almost entirely absent from Curb's moneyed world, building from Marcel Mauss's observation that gifts create binding obligations to reciprocate, Derrida's claim that a truly free gift is impossible, and Adorno's account of how modern capitalist society degenerates present-giving into a social function exercised with 'rational bad grace.' The failed presents make the case: the hole-ridden shirt of 'Chet's Shirt' that Ted calls 'a problem, not a gift,' Larry's self-serving freak book, Ted's status-reinstating pie in 'Denise Handicap,' and the bracelet-for-forgiveness economy of 'The Bracelet,' where gifts merely track the balance of power between Larry and Cheryl. Adorno's 'despicable parody' of marriage as a community of mutual interest is applied directly to Larry's ice-cream-for-sex strategy and the tenth-anniversary 'Mel's Offer' arrangement. The one near-authentic gift is Larry yelling profanities in solidarity with chef Guy Bernier at 'The Grand Opening,' and even that stays ambiguous because we never learn what the recipient thinks.

marx-alienation.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
marx-alienation.title: The Wire and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Vannatta reads Season Four through Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition: Marlo's ultimatum to Bodie, Lex killing Fruit for Patrice, and D'Angelo's chess lesson (the pawn as slave producing for the king) all dramatize the struggle for recognition, while Marx's inversion of Hegel explains the alienation of the dockworkers, McNulty exiled to harbor patrol, and Freamon buried in pawn-shop detail by the chain of master-slave directives from Rawls through Marimow. The heart of the chapter is education: Prezbo's dice-and-card math projects embody Dewey's synthesis of child and curriculum against the 'banking concept' Freire attacked, but 'You don't teach math. You teach the test' shows the institutional logic winning, and Parenti's grant-funded project class with Colvin illustrates Freire's warning that the oppressor's humanitarian false generosity treats the corner kids as objects of study rather than partners in dialogue, leaving even its successes unable to show the kids why corner life is problematic.

marx-alienation.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
marx-alienation.title: Psych and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Jeff Ewing applies Marx's critique of religion - the supernatural as ruling-class ideology, 'the opium of the people,' behind which priests and shamans hide real material processes and prop up hierarchy - to Shawn, who likewise masks his genuinely material observational talent as psychic gift to escape arrest in the pilot and keep access to SBPD cases. But the comparison inverts: unlike Marx's priests, Shawn serves ordinary people rather than the ruling class, and the chapter concludes he is better understood as an alienated worker - forced by a repressive state's threat of prosecution to sell a false product, defined by what he is not, and never credited for his true skill.

marx-alienation.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
marx-alienation.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Fitzpatrick runs Marx's account of alienated labor from the 1844 Manuscripts through the novel: Victor's creature is the product of estranged labor, 'an alien object exercising power over him,' which he cannot name, comes to loathe, and which finally destroys him - the devaluation of the creator tracking the increasing value of the thing made, while workers become commodities producing commodities. The De Laceys' eviction in Branagh's Mary Shelley's Frankenstein and the Ingolstadt cholera riots stage class struggle at feudalism's end, and Victor's failure to self-actualize (to 'hunt in the morning, fish in the afternoon... criticize after dinner') shows how capitalism turns science into 'a tool of our own destruction.' The chapter closes with 'Frankenstorm' climate change as the alienated externality par excellence - capitalists selling us the rope with which we hang ourselves.

marx-alienation.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
marx-alienation.title: Girls and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Wible asks whether the workplace abuse in Girls - Hannah's two unpaid intern years, the harassment at the law firm, the 30-day e-book deadline that triggers her OCD, Marnie hostessing at a gentlemen's club - is defensible by young workers' inexperience and the 'experience paradox.' Against the boot-camp defense he argues from the meaning of work (Gini's 'I work, therefore I am,' Schumacher's good work) and from Marx on alienation from the products of labor, but his core standard is Kant's: persons must be treated as ends, never merely as means, which the editor who wants the book and not the person violates. He concludes that young workers' vulnerability (no savings, no leverage, reluctance to blow the whistle) warrants paid internships, transparency, and two-way respect.

marx-alienation.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
marx-alienation.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Biondi argues the 'counter-cultural capitalist' is no paradox: Jobs succeeded not as a Gordon Gekko-style greedy capitalist but through the creative individualism of the cognitive counter-culture—the garage techno-geeks—who pursued their own vision rather than the bottom line. She traces the greedy-capitalist stereotype to Glaucon's Ring-of-Gyges challenge in Plato's Republic (people act justly only from fear of punishment), Hobbes's restless desire for power after power, and Marx and Engels's picture of alienated wage slavery under capitalism, with Rawls as the toleration-only-if-redistributed alternative. Jobs's hippie exterior (drugs, fruitarianism, Zen) masked an entrepreneur who, in Rand's 'creative mind' mold, put a ding in the universe through products like the iPad instead of philanthropy.

marx-alienation.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
marx-alienation.title: Dracula and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Sexton's mock FBI COMPIC file stages a Cold War reading of Abbott and Costello Meet Frankenstein: screenwriters Lees and Rinaldo remake Dracula as Marx's Das Kapital vampire - capital as dead labour sucking living labour - so blood-draining becomes profit-draining and 'This man belongs to me!' the capitalist's claim on his workers. A fictional Ayn Rand review for HUAC decodes the film as collectivist propaganda that slanders the businessman McDougal and dreams of a creature with 'no will of his own,' touching Marxian alienation along the way. A final note links screenwriter Robert Lees's blacklisting by Sterling Hayden and his real-life decapitation to Stoker's vampire-killing instructions.

marx-alienation.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
marx-alienation.title: 14. Of Course It Sucks—It’s Work
marx-alienation.relation: Wible stages three theories of work against Dilbert strips: the Greek view of Plato and Aristotle that labor is freedom-sapping and leisure is the civilized ideal, Marx's capitalist critique in which workers become objects and machines (Wally gives off no human vibe, and robots are coming for the engineers), and Desjardins's human-fulfillment model built on Schumacher's creativity, challenge, development, honesty, and beauty, with Wells Fargo's fake accounts showing how jobs that force lying corrupt character. He endorses instead a Kantian middle ground anchored in Norman Bowie's moral minimum: never treating workers as mere means, so the CEO making intern Asok drink industrial sludge on stage is a violation of respect for persons, not just bad management. Sisyphus supplies the image of pointless labor, though even he might be redeemed if he loved the rock.

marx-alienation.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
marx-alienation.title: 9. Girls Just Wanna Have Mediated Fun
marx-alienation.relation: Applies Guy Debord's society of the spectacle to Inside Amy Schumer: relationships and self-image become 'mediated' by women's magazines and advertising, so Amy hides under the bed in 'Sex Prep' rather than be seen unretouched, a manufactured boy band dictates 'natural' beauty in 'Girl, You Don't Need Makeup', and 'Publicity Stunt' ends with thin arms in photos mattering more than the prom disaster. Celebrity culture, reality-TV breakups, and 'Sext Photographer' illustrate having and appearing displacing being, while the spectacle's alienation and false consciousness surface in 'Judging Strippers'. The verite 'Amy Goes Deep' interviews and end-of-episode bloopers puncture the spectacle with glimpses of the real.

marx-alienation.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
marx-alienation.title: 28. Replicants of California, Unite!
marx-alienation.relation: Christopher Innes gives 2049 a Marxist class analysis: the replicants are an enslaved working class, the Wallace Corporation the ruling class owning the means of production, and the LAPD a state apparatus with 'relative autonomy' that really upholds the system — K is a slave who kills his own kind without seeing his class position. Applying the materialist (not idealist) dialectic and the Eighteenth Brumaire's lesson about conflicting ruling-class interests, he reads Wallace, Atari, and even Ana as factions with divergent interests. Freysa's 'we are our own masters' and 'we are building our own army' mark the replicants as class conscious, aware of their Marxian 'species being', with nothing to lose but their chains.

marx-alienation.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
marx-alienation.title: 22. Won’t You Be My Comrade
marx-alienation.relation: Christopher Innes runs Marx's critique of Hegel's idealism against Mister Rogers: the show treats problems (divorce, war, the Clemmons pool scene) ideally, as symbolic gestures rather than material change, much as Hegel's storybook individuals miss money's role. Measured against Capital's alienated worker, 'an appendage to the machine,' contrasted with the suitcase worker who 'knows her work,' and the Communist Manifesto's 'bourgeois socialist' who demands reform not liberation, Rogers emerges as a progressive bourgeois socialist whose make-believe may console children for, or subtly resist, their future exploitation.

marx-alienation.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
marx-alienation.title: When Life Gives You Liz’s Lemons, Can You Make Lemonade
marx-alienation.relation: Hinzmann reads Liz Lemon's workaholism through Marx and his successors: she gives NBC-Universal-Shinehardt her best years, but her alienation is social and existential rather than the classic alienated labor of the factory, since her creative job leaves her unable to connect with people or to choose love, as with Dennis and Floyd. Drawing on Adorno and the Frankfurt School, the chapter argues Liz cannot see her job as the problem because capitalist ideologies like meritocracy and free will make self-blame feel natural, and the 'Jackie Jormp-Jomp' fight-club episode shows even a life of leisure turns miserable without purpose. Freud's dictum that happiness requires work and love frames the diagnosis: Liz's work gives her life meaning precisely by shutting out everything else that could.

marx-alienation.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
marx-alienation.title: Where’s Kenneth We Need to Blame Someone!
marx-alienation.relation: Michaud takes seriously Jack's love of GE: if Peter French is right that corporations have actorship through their corporate internal decision structure, showing intentionality, rational decision, and behavior change as in the Challenger launch that no individual willed, then GE is a moral person. Following Marvin Brown, he draws the uncomfortable conclusion that we have enslaved corporations: they are designed by stockholders to want only profit, programmed toward corporate suicide in buyouts, with no ethics built into the CID structure. Marx's wage slavery of workers unable to express their creative will is mirrored from above, and the chapter closes by relocating blame: when corporations do evil, the culpable party is us, the free-market supporters who designed the system.

marx-alienation.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
marx-alienation.title: The End of History
marx-alienation.relation: Diagnoses the Alien universe through Marx's Grundrisse: workers like Parker and Fifield ('I'm here to make money') live only to have and consume, wage labor is avoided like the plague (Pvt. Frost's 'I hate this job'), money replaces the faith people should place in each other, and employees become disposable commodities (Vickers to Shaw: 'that makes you an employee'). Only the conscience-free android Ash fits the Corporation's ideal 'pure capitalist,' and because the saga's future stays capitalist, it vindicates Fukuyama's end-of-history thesis over Marx's prediction of collapse.

marx-alienation.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
marx-alienation.title: Alien Nation
marx-alienation.relation: Reads Alien as a film about alienation in Marx's fourfold sense from the 1844 Manuscripts: the crew is estranged from the product of its labor (the retrieved Xenomorph turns on them), from the labor process (Brett and Parker's bonus dispute, Dallas shilling for the Company that deems him disposable), from species-being (infantile dependence on Mother, whose Special Order 937 merely formalizes an expendability they already live), and from one another (they never unite against the Company or suspect Ash). In Aliens the Colonial Marines repeat the failure, while the coordinated alien 'nation' under its queen - possible victims of Engineer colonization - makes the humans look like the inferior species.

marx-alienation.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
marx-alienation.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Applies Marx's fourfold alienation (from product, from labor, from species-being, from others) to Bluth capitalism: George Michael dips and sells bananas he cannot keep, Lupe cleans Lucille's home under duress, and classes divide the family from the people it exploits. George Sr.'s Boyfights tapes and Caged Wisdom show the capitalist commodifying his children and himself, Gob's figurehead presidency turns employees into resources, Lindsay is 'having without being', and Engels's property-based account of the nuclear family explains Tobias's repressed sexuality; the cure offered is democratic socialism, since within-system fixes only get more absurd.

marx-alienation.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
marx-alienation.title: Reflections on Technophobia
marx-alienation.relation: The chapter asks whether the technophobia of 'Metalhead' - robo-dogs hunting Bella and her friends across a wasteland - is justified, testing Daniel Dinello's list of fears (identity, values, emotion, freedom, life). Descartes's and Aquinas's human-uniqueness over the mechanical fails because the robo-dogs, like DeepMind, learn and problem-solve, while the episode's Rousseau-style romanticism (only the non-technological cliff, tree, sunlight and stream aid Bella) and the teddy-bear mission show technology amplifying compassion rather than threatening it. The real dangers are robots as Latourian 'black boxes': Asimov's Three Laws cannot be operationalized, and if we cannot know how robo-dogs decide, our frameworks for blame and punishment break down (who answers for a killing - robot, programmer, or, on Marx's analysis of capitalist technology as an instrument of oppression, the economic system behind it?). The chapter concludes that since we already share the world with robots, learning to live responsibly alongside them must replace simple fear.

marx-alienation.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
marx-alienation.title: “He’s done tech detox weekends here and there, but ten days ”
marx-alienation.relation: Reading Smithereens as today's reality rather than a dystopia, the chapter explains the crash that killed Chris's fiancée through Herbert Simon's attention economy: platforms like Smithereen are free because they harvest and sell attention, and Billy Bauer admits the app was deliberately tuned 'like a crack pipe' with dopamine targets. Using Marx's analysis of capitalist surplus, the chapter argues (with Zuboff's 'behavioral surplus' and Crary's 24/7 capitalism) that users are wageless laborers generating value for free, and that compulsive checking is Gerald Moore's 'dopamining' - brain plasticity exploited by a hostile attention environment - rather than free choice. It rejects individual tech-detox consumerism as a false solution and closes with Simondon: knowing our machines is the beginning of the political reflection needed to dissolve the alienating 'fetishism of the tool.'

marx-alienation.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
marx-alienation.title: Things Worth Believing
marx-alienation.relation: Butterfield stages the Frankfurt School critique of her own Disney love: Marx's three alienations (from work, from others, from species-being) explain the Seven Dwarfs' 'dig dig dig' and the FastPass-scheduled vacation that converts leisure into consumption, while Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man diagnoses the parks' engineered euphoria and 'false needs' as a 'comfortable, smooth, reasonable, democratic unfreedom' that blunts protest — with Adorno adding that consumers see through the advertising and buy anyway. Against the critic, she argues a Disney trip done right can challenge alienation by reviving play, family togetherness, and childlike belief in 'things worth believing.'

marx-alienation.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
marx-alienation.title: Metallica, Nietzsche, and Marx: The Immorality of Morality
marx-alienation.relation: Peter Fosl argues Metallica's moral critique of religion in 'Leper Messiah' and 'The God That Failed' continues Nietzsche's genealogy of Christian slave morality born of ressentiment and Marx's 'opium of the people': religion gathers a docile herd, denies this world, and exercises power through sin and forgiveness. He diagnoses the band as often stuck in Nietzsche's incomplete nihilism - 'To Live is to Die' longs nostalgically for the Kingdom of Salvation - while 'Escape' and the sheer creative power of the music show a genuine Nietzschean transvaluation and overcoming of Christianity.

marx-alienation.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
marx-alienation.title: The Office and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Answers The New Yorker's claim that the American Office 'doesn't care about class' by reading it through Marx: capital's growth logic and surplus value explain the degraded office labor the show depicts (Stanley's 'run-out-the-clock type of situation' truck unloading, Pam's tepid watercolors, Roy's 'unloading trucks without meaning', Ryan's rejected assembly line), while the salaried masses' class position survives precisely as unnamable and denied - Michael's botched condo purchase, his fury at Ryan's business-school ambition, and Prison Martin's observation that office and prison are both 'doing the same thing every day'. Drawing on Kracauer, the chapter argues the show's comedy walks between distraction and awakening, and ends with Walter Benjamin's 'authentic humanity' located in the gap between professional and private life: Michael's failures make him an unwitting critique of the system that produced him.

marx-alienation.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
marx-alienation.title: Responsibility
marx-alienation.relation: Christiansen reads SNL's first head writer Michael O'Donoghue ('Mr. Mike') through Sartre: the Least-Loved Bedtime Tales (Brer Rabbit skinned alive, 'there's no moral... just random acts of meaningless violence') dramatize a world where existence precedes essence and narratives lie; 'Sartresky and Hutch' stages the absurd via a Vietnam veteran with PTSD; and the needles-in-the-eyes impressions embody Sartre's vulnerability to the Other, which Mr. Mike's dark glasses shut out. The chapter ends with Sartre's Marxist turn in the Critique of Dialectical Reason, arguing O'Donoghue's angry 'Police State' sketch shows that scarcity, alienation, and organized state violence are contingent and can be fought, which is where his nihilism leaves room for hope.

marx-alienation.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
marx-alienation.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Reads Jax's '92 miles an hour' monologue in 'Sovereign' through Heidegger and Hubert Dreyfus: expert riding, Chibs's pub brawling, and Tara's surgery are pre-reflective embodied skills that conscious rule-following would only ruin. Tig fixing bikes in the Teller-Morrow garage illustrates readiness-to-hand, Bobby's smoke-spewing Fat Boy the breakdown of un-readiness-to-hand, and browsing the Harley parts catalogue the detached present-at-hand. Against the alienation of calculative, instrumental thinking (Marx, Heidegger's standing-reserve — Clay selling the club to the Galindo Cartel, Cara Cara's porn bodies), the chapter follows Pirsig: maintenance is a form of care, so Opie rebuilding a '65 Panhead after Donna's death reconciles the biker with technology instead of enslaving him to it.

marx-alienation.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
marx-alienation.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
marx-alienation.relation: Weighs Marx against Heidegger on whether SAMCRO should fight its history. Teller-Morrow read as petit-bourgeois capitalism turns the Mayans' pilot-episode raid into industrial sabotage and Nero's escort business into exploitation; read through Proudhon, Kropotkin, and Emma Goldman — whose essay John Teller found quoted on a Nevada wall — the club is an anarcho-syndicalist commune with democratic chapel votes, Kropotkin's mutual aid to widows like Lyla, and Tara as its socialized healthcare. Heidegger's historicity gives the resolution: Jax cannot escape the past (the Irish deal only with Clay; 'The sting of that betrayal ain't gonna fade') but can appropriate it authentically, and Pope's forced choice of a victim in 'Laying Pipe' confronts him with being-toward-death.

marx-alienation.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
marx-alienation.title: Notes
marx-alienation.relation: Jeff Ewing argues the Federation's moneyless, postscarcity economy is Marx's transitional stage on the way to classless communism: Picard's 'we've eliminated hunger, want, the need for possessions' and Troi's exchange with Samuel Clemens in 'Time's Arrow' mark Marx's shift from the realm of necessity to the realm of freedom. He reconstructs Marx and Engels on alienation, the division of labor, labor-tokens, and the withering state to dissolve the apparent anomalies—Federation credits, Quark's tab, the Chateau Picard vineyard—as survivals of transition rather than capitalism. Rom's 'workers of the world unite' in 'Bar Association' and the self-actualizing leisure of Enterprise crews complete the case.

marx-alienation.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
