brain-in-a-vat.title: Inside the Helmet What Do Football Players Know
brain-in-a-vat.relation: Geivett uses football to illustrate epistemology, distinguishing factual (propositional) from competence (skill) knowledge through what running backs and quarterbacks must know and enact under split-second pressure, including 'football physics' vectors on a rollout pass. He treats the athlete's need to be mindful of knowledge amid stadium noise as a lesson in reliable belief, then critiques classroom skeptics who deploy Descartes's evil-demon and the brain-in-a-vat thought experiment, arguing mere logical possibility is no evidence for skepticism.

brain-in-a-vat.title: eXistenZial Angst
brain-in-a-vat.relation: Duncan Pritchard reads eXistenZ as staging radical skepticism with existential force: unlike the standard brain-in-a-vat scenario, the game 'creeps up' on Ted and Allegra so they feel the transition from reality to doubt, producing angst. Invoking Wittgenstein's On Certainty (doubt radicalized is madness), he argues sanity requires belief but not true belief, so the pair achieve a new doxastic equilibrium. He also reads the spinal 'bioport' pod as a case of Clark and Chalmers's extended cognition, where technology becomes part of and subverts the agents' cognitive processes.

brain-in-a-vat.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
brain-in-a-vat.title: Skepticism Outside the Matrix
brain-in-a-vat.relation: Lawrence uses The Matrix to raise Cartesian skepticism: Neo's deception dramatizes Descartes's dream argument and evil demon, the computer-run Matrix being a technological version of the demon. He argues even Morpheus cannot be certain he has truly awakened ('the Matrix within the Matrix'), so the only certainty is Descartes's cogito. Drawing on Russell's 'Appearance and Reality,' he then argues that even setting aside Matrix scenarios, naive realism fails, since a chair's color, texture, solidity and shape are all perception-relative, leaving the external world's nature deeply uncertain.

brain-in-a-vat.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
brain-in-a-vat.title: MOTHERHOOD
brain-in-a-vat.relation: Sara Goering uses the fantasy of a child 'off button' as a thought experiment, situating it alongside Plato's Ring of Gyges, the brain-in-a-vat, and personal-identity puzzles to argue that such control would be overused and would treat children as objects rather than developing subjects. She then turns reflexive, critiquing thought experiments themselves – including Rawls's veil of ignorance (via Okin and Benhabib) and Susan Brison's critique of personal-identity cases – for diverting from the messy real world, arguing that the off-button fantasy really signals the need for 'distributed mothering' and structural support; she illustrates with The Matrix, Multiplicity, Harry Potter, and Woolf's 'room of one's own.'

brain-in-a-vat.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
brain-in-a-vat.title: Horror and the Idea of Everyday Life On Skeptical Threats in Psycho and The Birds

Nickel argues horror has an epistemological value structurally parallel to philosophical skepticism: it maliciously rips away the tacit 'cognitive trust' backing our everyday actions. In Psycho, Marion Crane's isolation and misplaced trust in the seemingly normal Norman Bates enacts the skeptical premise that the ordinary person you rely on could murder you. Like Hume returning to backgammon, viewers can only resume everyday life, which Nickel says horror exposes as a necessary but insecure construction.

brain-in-a-vat.title: 2. The Matrix

brain-in-a-vat.title: Skepticism Outside the Matrix
brain-in-a-vat.relation: Matt Lawrence uses The Matrix to stage the skeptical problem, running Descartes's dream argument and evil-demon method of doubt (the Matrix as a technological demon) and even a 'Matrix within the Matrix' to show Morpheus cannot know he is awake. experience-machine.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
experience-machine.title: Unknown
experience-machine.relation: The authors diagnose Cypher's betrayal as hedonism - the assumption that pleasure alone makes life worth living - and answer it with Nozick's experience machine: would we, like Cypher trading the Nebuchadnezzar for a steak and a rich actor's life, plug in forever? Since we want to do things rather than merely have the experience of doing them, want to be a certain kind of person rather than an 'indeterminate blob', and want genuine contact with reality, Cypher's choice is immoral while Neo's embrace of 'the desert of the real' gives his life real moral value - Mill's Socrates dissatisfied over the pig satisfied.

experience-machine.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
experience-machine.title: Unknown
experience-machine.relation: Schick quotes Nozick's experience-machine passage at length and catalogs the parallels with the Matrix: floating in a tank, electrodes stimulating the brain, experiences indistinguishable from reality, the only difference being that Nozick's users unplug every two years. He rehearses Nozick's three reasons not to plug in - we want to do things rather than merely experience doing them, we want to be a certain sort of person rather than an 'indeterminate blob', and we want contact with a deeper reality - then turns the lesson on the Oracle's world: do the freed make real choices either, or are their choices pre-ordained?

experience-machine.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
experience-machine.title: You’re Living in a Fantasy World, This Beautiful World
experience-machine.relation: Sylvia argues that the split-screen 'All I Need' video made for MTV's anti-trafficking EXIT project — an American child's comfortable day intercut with a child laborer finishing the very shoes the American takes off — argues against child labor more powerfully than a standard utilitarian argument, because it joins Aristotle's ethos, pathos, and logos instead of relying on logos alone. Using the cognitive/expressive distinction, he claims the song also argues by turning listeners back on themselves ('I only stick with you because there are no others'). He then deploys Nozick's experience machine: we are all plugged into a Baudrillardian, Matrix-like media hyperreality that can make exploitation fade into background images, and the video's slap in the face 'punctures the hyperreality', showing how emotion can do argumentative work that rigorous argument cannot.

experience-machine.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
experience-machine.title: Forward! Into the Breach
experience-machine.relation: Silcox and Cogburn test Nozick's three reasons for refusing the experience machine against Azeroth. Respawning kobolds and endlessly repeated quests threaten Nozick's 'we want to do things' objection — yet play genuinely changes other players and their characters, which is what the massive multiplayer element adds over a solo machine. Attribute scores let a dullard play a genius, but as with the wheelchair-bound woman who played Doom to 'get my legs back,' piloting a warrior is still something you do, like a pilot flying a plane. Against Nozick's 'man-made reality' complaint they argue that WoW, like great art, stays open to unbounded interpretation and even surprises its own designers, so the human appetite for fun is more robust and complicated than Nozick allowed.

experience-machine.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
experience-machine.title: The Power of Choice
experience-machine.relation: Rennett tests Cobb's choice to leave Limbo against Nozick's three reasons for refusing the experience machine: we want to actually do things (raise his real children, not loving projections), to be a certain kind of person (Yusuf's dream-den addicts are 'indeterminate blobs'), and to touch something deeper than a man-made world. He then recruits Berkeley's esse est percipi to explain Mal's sincerity - she perceives Limbo and remembers it, so for her it is real - and argues that shared dreams differ from private dreams and the experience machine because they leave waking traces, like Mal's bullet in Arthur's leg. The chapter ends by making reality a matter of choice: like the cave prisoners of Plato's allegory, each character believes a world, and Cobb's ignoring of the top is his choice to live in the world with his children.

experience-machine.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
experience-machine.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
experience-machine.relation: Jason Iuliano reads the Gang's 'no restrictions' motto as egoistic hedonism in the tradition of Aristippus of Cyrene: pleasure alone is intrinsically good, and specifically present, bodily, personal pleasure - exactly how Mac defends his fifty-pound weight gain and the pair's decision to smoke crack. The doctrine is shown in action through the Gang's treatment of Rickety Cricket, used as a mere instrument while his life is ruined without a flicker of guilt, and through get-rich-quick schemes from the impulse-bought boat to running for comptroller purely for the bribe. Robert Nozick's Experience Machine then shows why hedonism fails - we want to actually do things, be a certain kind of person, and touch reality, not float as an 'indeterminate blob' - and Mill's paradox of hedonism explains the Gang's misery: pursuing pleasure directly is precisely what drives it away.

experience-machine.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
experience-machine.title: “I Always Felt this Place was Missing a Real Villain. Hence, My Humble Contribution.”
experience-machine.relation: Eberl asks whether living out Sizemore-style fantasies can reveal or only corrode character: applying Aristotle's account of virtues and vices as habituated dispositions, he argues William's three decades in the park habituated the vices that made him the Man in Black — the park reveals rather than suspends the self — while cruelty toward humanlike hosts hardens us toward people, as Aquinas and Kant warn about kindness to animals. Against Ford's claim that humans are wantons in tight loops, Maeve's editing of her own code after learning her escape was scripted makes her a Frankfurtian person who aligns first-order desires with second-order volitions, grounding her narrative identity and personhood. William too attains personhood by actualizing a second-order desire for a different life, with the hosts' free fight back evoking Nietzsche's will to power and Nozick's point that we want to actually do things, not merely experience them.

experience-machine.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
experience-machine.title: 1. The Genuine Article
experience-machine.relation: Written in the voice of a non-C-137 Rick, the chapter argues that whether the Beth at the end of 'The ABCs of Beth' is a clone doesn't matter, because our reverence for 'the genuine article' (like the original US Constitution) is romantic packaging, and a functional clone is as good as the original. It tests Robert Nozick's experience machine, whose three objections supposedly show we value genuine reality intrinsically, against Rick's pragmatism of believing what is useful, and reads 'The Wedding Squanchers' (Rick turning himself in to the Federation) as proof that his family is both instrumentally and intrinsically valuable to him. Your answer to the clone question, it concludes, is a Rorschach test revealing what you place intrinsic value on.

experience-machine.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
experience-machine.title: The Value of Finitude
experience-machine.relation: The chapter tests each motive for uploading to San Junipero and finds it wanting: Kantian cosmic justice fails because the resort neither rewards the good nor can punish the wicked; Tolstoy's cosmic-insignificance dread fails because a finite life can still be meaningful, and even Epicurus and Lucretius deflate the fear of death (while Nagel notes death's evil lies in foreclosed possibilities, and Williams's Makropulos case warns eternal life breeds boredom). Nozick's experience machine is the closest analogy, but the chapter argues San Junipero differs — residents know it is digital and share it with other conscious people — before Nussbaum's argument lands: without finitude there is no risk, so no courage, sacrifice, or deep love, which is why Kelly's forty-nine real years with Richard outweigh forever with Yorkie.

experience-machine.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
experience-machine.title: Heaven is a Place on Earth
experience-machine.relation: The chapter argues Black Mirror's perception tech works because the brain constructs experience top-down (predictive coding), so implants like Playtest's mushroom, Arkangel's filter, and Men Against Fire's MASS can inject perceptions and suppress error signals - and Cooper's total VR illusion defeats every one of Descartes's strategies (memory continuity, cross-checking the senses, reason) for telling dream from reality, killing him seconds after implantation. Nozick's experience machine illuminates Danny's preference for Striking Vipers X over his marriage and Arkangel's lesson that filtering Sara's childhood perceptions left her unable to read danger or emotion. Foucault's panopticon (via Bentham) frames White Christmas's cookie interrogation modeled on real police deception (Frazier v. Cupp), the MASS implant's manufacture of 'roach' targets for killing, and Nosedive's self-imposed social ratings as modern perceptual discipline - with only trusted others (Catarina, Susan, Kelly) punching through the manipulation.

experience-machine.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
experience-machine.title: Happily Ever After
experience-machine.relation: Runs Descartes' dreaming argument and evil-genius doubt on Aurora, for whom the scenario is literal: Maleficent is an actually existing deceiver who could have enchanted her whole life in a dungeon. G. E. Moore's common-sense proof — 'here is a hand,' dubbed the Pinocchio test after the real boy — and the Moorean shift answer the skeptic, illustrated by Maleficent deploying Zeno's paradox to stop Prince Phillip's sword, where Phillip rightly clings to the more certain premise that motion is possible. Nozick's experience machine explains why Aurora should care: we want to actually be good and live real lives rather than merely experience them, so authentic 'happily ever after' requires knowing our experiences are backed by reality.

experience-machine.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
experience-machine.title: The Power of Choice
experience-machine.relation: Rennett stages Ariadne's 'who would want to be stuck in a dream for ten years?' against Nozick's experience machine: Nozick's three reasons for staying unplugged (doing rather than merely experiencing, being a determinate person, contact with a reality deeper than human construction) map onto Cobb's reasons for leaving Limbo — he wants to actually raise his children, be a good father, and love children who can love him back rather than projections. Against Nozick, the chapter enlists Berkeley's esse est percipi to explain Mal's choice: a perceived world is real, and Inception's shared dreams pass Berkeley's intersubjective test in ways private dreams cannot (Cobb apologizes to Arthur for being shot; dream acts carry waking consequences). It concludes that reality becomes what we choose to believe — Cobb's final refusal to watch the top, like the cave prisoners rejecting release, is the power of choice.

experience-machine.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
experience-machine.title: Through the Mist and the Madness: Metallica's Message of Nonconformity, Individuality, and Truth
experience-machine.relation: Thomas Nys argues Metallica's early message of nonconformity and individuality ('Metal Militia', 'Motorbreath') converges with Mill's On Liberty: conformity withers human capacities and breeds a stagnant society. Mill's higher pleasures and Nozick's experience machine show why real happiness requires autonomy and earned achievement rather than passive pleasure - the point of 'Escape''s 'Life's for my own to live my own way'. He reads 'Leper Messiah' and 'Eye of the Beholder' as Metallica's versions of Mill's defense of free inquiry and truth against mindless conformity and censorship.

experience-machine.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
experience-machine.title: Notes
experience-machine.relation: Jason Eberl uses the amusement park of 'Shore Leave', Omicron Ceti III's spore paradise in 'This Side of Paradise', Landru's hedonistic 'red hour', and the Borg's relentless efficiency to argue that edifying play and leisure are necessary for intellectual, moral, and spiritual flourishing. Following Josef Pieper's Leisure, with Nozick's experience machine (applied to 'The Thaw' and Barclay's holodiction), Aristotle's 'we work in order to be at leisure', and Aquinas on wonder, he contrasts mere utility (bonum utile) with the common good a drone-only Collective can never have. He concludes that thoughtfully watching Star Trek is itself worthwhile leisure: science-fiction thought experiments that serve Socrates's examined life.

experience-machine.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
experience-machine.title: XI - PROFESSOR X WANTS YOU
experience-machine.relation: Robichaud asks what a new mutant like Storm ought to do: join the X-Men, the Brotherhood, or neither. Distinguishing prudential from moral oughts, he argues desire-satisfaction beats Bentham's pleasure-pain account of well-being via an adaptation of Nozick's experience machine ('Eugor,' a child given Rogue's exact mental life), then evaluates both teams' agendas nonconsequentially. Building on Ronald Dworkin's three grounds for civil disobedience, policy-based, justice-based, and integrity-based, he argues peaceful persuasion is not obviously mandatory for mutants facing registration and a weaponized cure: resistance short of violence is permitted on all three grounds, and when the state turns lethal, even violent resistance becomes permissible.

experience-machine.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
experience-machine.title: Sixteenth Hole Golf and the Meaning of Life
experience-machine.relation: Randy Lunsford uses Annika Sorenstam's early retirement to ask what makes golf—and life—meaningful, surveying religious versus scientific accounts of purpose and E. J. Bond's claim that meaning comes from pursuing objectively valuable ends, not just satisfying desire. He tests Epicurean hedonism and Nozick's experience machine (we want to really shoot the course record, not merely feel we did), Taylor's reworking of the Sisyphus myth (meaning via injected desire), and Schopenhauer's pessimism that satisfied desire only yields boredom. He argues golf's very finitude—eighteen holes, like a mortal life—gives it meaning, so excellence, relationships, playing by the rules, and taking responsibility for each shot are what make both golf and life worthwhile.

experience-machine.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
experience-machine.title: Authoritarian Tennis Parents Are Their Children Really Any Worse Off
experience-machine.relation: Kevin Kinghorn asks whether authoritarian tennis parents (like the family of prodigy Jan Silva) harm their children's well-being, and tests three theories of the good life. He rejects Aristotle's perfectionist eudaimonia because the 'uniqueness of reason' criterion fails, substituting his own perfectionist-yet-mental-state view that well-being consists in the felt experience of connecting with others. He defends a Mill-style hedonism of higher and lower pleasures against Robert Nozick's experience-machine objection, arguing the machine only refutes the claim that we desire mental states, not that well-being consists in them, and dismisses desire-satisfaction theories and Feinberg's 'right to an open future' as failing to show that lost autonomy itself lowers a child's flourishing.

experience-machine.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
experience-machine.title: The Russell-Wartenberg Debate
experience-machine.relation: The chapter sets the book's standard for 'philosophy in action' by staging Bruce Russell's skepticism against Thomas Wartenberg's defense of the film-as-philosophy thesis: Russell holds that narrative films can at most raise questions or furnish counterexamples, so The Matrix merely inspires the viewer's own argument for external-world skepticism, while Wartenberg replies that The Matrix screens Descartes's evil-deceiver hypothesis so effectively that viewers are themselves deceived into skeptical doubt, accomplishing for audiences what Socrates did to his interlocutors. Wartenberg's reading of Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind — where Dr. Mierzwiak's memory-erasure technology presents utilitarianism (via Mary's dialogue) and then a counterexample to it — is tested, and the author proposes the film targets hedonism more directly, working as a reverse variant of Nozick's experience machine that defends autonomy over happiness. Kant's obscure Transcendental Deduction is invoked to show that even canonical philosophical texts are ambiguous, blunting the explicitness objection. The chapter concludes that negative projects — modus tollens counterexamples cinematically conveyed — are where film most plausibly philosophizes, preparing the ground for reading the Whedonverse.

experience-machine.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
experience-machine.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
experience-machine.relation: McMahon argues Burton's death-saturated corpus functions as modern memento mori that fosters Heideggerian authenticity by arousing the uncanny and honest awareness of being-toward-death. She supplements Freud's account of the unheimliche (which she says wrongly substitutes castration anxiety for the primal fear of death) with Heidegger's link of angst, uncanniness, and finitude in 'Being and Time,' plus Terror Management Theory. Reading 'The Nightmare Before Christmas,' 'Corpse Bride,' and 'Dark Shadows,' she shows Jack, Bonejangles's Dance of Death, Emily, and vampire Barnabas use animation, comedy, and romance to make death palatable, and contrasts these films with Nozick's escapist experience machine—Burton supplements reality rather than replacing it.

experience-machine.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
experience-machine.title: Spinning Tops and Brains in Vats
experience-machine.relation: William Lindenmuth reads Inception's ambiguous ending through Robert Nozick's experience machine, arguing that Cobb's choice of his real children over the dream-Mal ('you're just a shade of my real wife') shows we want our dreams to be reality, not reality to be a dream. He deploys Nozick's three reasons against plugging in - we want to do things, not merely seem to; we want to be a certain kind of person ('It's not who I am underneath, but what I do that defines me'); and a man-made reality confines and limits us - while invoking Bernard Williams's tedium of immortality for Cobb's fifty dream-years with Mal and Wittgenstein's talking lion for the alienation those years create. On this reading the wobbling top matters, because choosing limbo would be 'a kind of suicide,' the difference between the film ending as tragedy or not.

experience-machine.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
experience-machine.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
experience-machine.relation: Theodore Bach argues that consuming porn co-opts the mind-reading 'simulation heuristic' (the same process behind the Mr. Tees airport puzzle), so that a viewer like 'Max' watching Naughty Office simulates being the boss rather than objectively watching. This explains porn's popularity, the money shot (a prop that keeps the viewer inside the off-line simulation), and why heterosexual men watch penises — they simulate their own. Invoking Nozick's experience machine and extending MacKinnon's critique via simulation and motor-imagery research, Bach warns that simulating aggressive, degrading acts toward women may transfer those dispositions into the real world.

experience-machine.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
experience-machine.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
experience-machine.relation: Brophy warns of a coming 'pornographic singularity' when veridical, immersive, interactive, unbounded virtual reality (extrapolated from Second Life, Rapelay, and Sony's brain-stimulation patent) makes hypersex and hyper-romance supplant real intimacy. He uses Baudrillard's hyperreal/simulacra to explain how airbrushed models and 'pornbots' render real women 'just bad porn', invokes Nozick's experience machine as literally realized, and argues that utilitarianism and Kant's humanity formula fail to condemn using pornbots, so only Aristotelian virtue theory locates the wrong—the user malfunctions and cannot flourish as escalating deviance (furries, age-play, rape games) conditions vice. His bleak prophecy is that unbounded virtual desire will corrode families and community.

experience-machine.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
experience-machine.title: BLUES
experience-machine.relation: Jesse Steinberg argues that doubt — a pervasive blues theme (B. B. King's 'nobody loves me but my momma,' Otis Spann's 'another mule kickin' in my stall,' Buddy Guy's 'I Smell a Rat') — supports Descartes's external-world skepticism, since knowledge would require ruling out the dreaming hypothesis. Against the 'I don't care' hedonistic reply he deploys Nozick's experience machine to show we value authentic reality over mere pleasant appearance, and he rejects contextualism as a solution. Endorsing Socrates' examined life, he settles for strong justification rather than certainty, reading Charley Patton's 'can't tell my future, can't tell my past' as the blues' honest coping with irreducible doubt.

experience-machine.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
experience-machine.title: 31. Inception as Philosophy Choose Your Dreams or Seek Reality
experience-machine.relation: Johnson uses Nolan's Inception—Cobb's dream-heists, the ambiguous spinning top, and the case that the whole film may be a dream—to test the moral Todd McGowan draws from it: that since we can't be sure what is real, we should abandon the quest for reality and choose the dream (his object of desire, his children) as Cobb does at the end. He evaluates six defenses of that moral, rejecting Descartes' skeptical dream/evil-demon problem (answered by abduction and by Plato's cave and Nozick's experience machine showing true belief is valuable), Baudrillard's denial of reality, Locke/Kant on the unknowable noumenal world, and Kierkegaard's leap of faith and Pascal's Wager, before softening it with Hume's return from skepticism to backgammon: entertain the doubt, then walk away when your children walk in.

experience-machine.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
experience-machine.title: 64. George Carlin as Philosopher It’s All Bullshit. Is It Bad for Ya
experience-machine.relation: Engels reads Carlin's insistence that 'it's all bullshit, and it's bad for ya' as a defense of truth over comforting illusion, mapping his bits onto Plato's Allegory of the Cave (Carlin dragging audiences up from shadows like 'prostitution is immoral' or 'the American Dream' to expose deeper essences), Nozick's Experience Machine (Carlin's sun-worship chosen because it is real, not a pleasing fiction), and Clifford/Beauvoir on the ethics of belief and the 'serious world.' Bits on rights, the sanctity of life, homelessness/'houselessness,' and 'proud to be an American' show Carlin arguing that false beliefs breed complacency and harm, so there are moral reasons to prefer truth.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Unknown
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: The authors diagnose Cypher's betrayal as hedonism - the assumption that pleasure alone makes life worth living - and answer it with Nozick's experience machine: would we, like Cypher trading the Nebuchadnezzar for a steak and a rich actor's life, plug in forever? Since we want to do things rather than merely have the experience of doing them, want to be a certain kind of person rather than an 'indeterminate blob', and want genuine contact with reality, Cypher's choice is immoral while Neo's embrace of 'the desert of the real' gives his life real moral value - Mill's Socrates dissatisfied over the pig satisfied.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Unknown
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Taking Cypher as the test case—juicy steak versus gruel, 'Ignorance is bliss'—the chapter argues the film unintentionally proves Cypher right: the Matrix offers not just sensual pleasure but everything down to Mill's 'higher faculties' (museums, Shakespeare, love, friendship), while the real world is a gray wasteland. Only truth and freedom speak for choosing reality, and the crew's red-pill idealism makes the film an old-fashioned, unpostmodern Hollywood morality tale about liberation rather than the postmodern story it elsewhere tells.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
higher-lower-pleasures.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Devin Brown uses Eustace, who dodges work on Dragon Island until he wakes as a dragon and discovers he would rather be hungry among human friends than comfortable alone, to contrast Epicurean hedonism and Tom Sawyer's work-avoidance with Mill's higher pleasures and the 'Sherlock Holmes philosophy of work.' Weighing Aristotle's contemplative life against Lewis's love of quests, he reads Father Christmas's tailored gifts and 'everyone must do what he can do best' as an Acorn Philosophy of Vocation with a Marxian 'from each according to his ability' echo, condemns wrong livelihoods like Governor Gumpas's slave trade, and closes on leisure and Aristotle's golden mean, which Lewis turns into 'golden extremes.'

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Not to Put Too Fine a Point on It
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Richard Greene asks why becoming Undead is bad for the one who becomes Undead and why we rank it worse than death, restricting himself to unfriendly vampires and zombies (setting aside soulful exceptions like Angel, Spike, Louis, and Ed from Shaun of the Dead). He tests Nagel's deprivation view (vampires gain infinite experiences, so nothing is deprived) and Williams's desire-frustration view (undeath replaces rather than frustrates desires: scotch for blood, pork roast for raw flesh), then Mill's better-Socrates-dissatisfied comparison and the thought that the Undead's evil nature makes undeath objectively bad. Each fails, so he concludes undeath is not objectively bad, only comparatively bad, and one might as well make the best of it.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Good Guy Vampires
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Robert Arp models the vampire's ontology with substance versus property dualism - Rice's vampires whose souls outlast the stake versus Blade's vampires who perish with their bodies - and uses Mill's distinction between lower bodily and higher mental pleasures from Utilitarianism to explain how vampires can both feel nothing bodily and suffer mentally (the opening quotation's regret at missing the wind in one's hair). Their real plight is the hedonistic paradox: pleasure pursued for its own sake yields pain, mistaken pleasures (Lestat on the dead twins, Blade's rave), or the boredom of an immortality that has 'seen it all.' The good guy vampires from Barnabas Collins to St. Germain escape by pursuing higher pleasures and activities for their own sake, vindicating Mill's closing advice that only those whose minds are fixed on something other than their own happiness find it.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
higher-lower-pleasures.title: John Henry, the Steam-Engine, and Folsom Prisoners
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Mulnix pairs Cash with John Stuart Mill on the priority of quality of life over mere life: Mill's 1868 Parliament speech defends capital punishment as more humane than the "living tomb" of life imprisonment, and Cash agrees in the Folsom liner notes (the prisoner envying the cockroach that can leave) and in "The Mercy Seat," where the electric chair becomes both mercy and the throne of God. Mill's higher and lower pleasures, competent judges, and On Liberty's individuality illuminate Cash's gallery of fools, the "Folsom Prison Blues" narrator who shot a man just to watch him die, the mother-defying Billy Joe of "Don't Take Your Guns to Town," characters whose unreflective rebellion squanders rational freedom. John Henry, by contrast, exercised his higher faculties against the steam-engine and so died happy, proving the chapter's Millian thesis that freedom matters as a means to self-directed, deliberated happiness.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
higher-lower-pleasures.title: “Condemned to Be a Member of This Lowest of Species”
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Arp uses Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from the Republic to ask whether unlimited power must corrupt the just: Q's career of meddling ('Encounter at Farpoint', 'Q Who?', 'The Q and the Grey') shows the corrupted case, while Riker given Q-powers in 'Hide and Q' helps his friends instead, a counterexample Glaucon can resist by pleading insufficient time. He then explains the Q's misery — Quinn's bored suicidal plea in 'Death Wish' — through the hedonistic paradox, refining it with Mill's distinction between bodily lower pleasures and mental higher ones and Aristotle's account of the lasting pleasure of completed states like beating the ship's computer at chess. The conclusion is that Q's 'condemnation' to mortality in 'Déjà Q' reveals the human condition as enviable: it is precisely our lacking unlimited power, pleasure, and immortality that drives the striving for truth, justice, goodness, and love.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Four 'Phase Two' essays on the nature of evil. Arp argues that in V for Vendetta V is a utilitarian user of persons just like the fascist Norsefire state - using Dascombe as a shield and torturing Evey 'for her own good' - so Kant's demand to treat humanity never merely as a means condemns the hero-as-villain, though 'moral autonomy' Kantians complicate the verdict. Poon stages the Aquinas-Ockham debate over will and intellect as Magneto reprograms Sentinels against New York (Ultimate X-Men #05), arguing the will cannot choose against the intellect's judgment, so supervillains like Magneto, Ra's al Ghul, and Apocalypse act for what seems good to them with a deeply flawed conception of the good. Robichaud uses Superman Returns, Civil War, and Captain America vs the Red Skull to test Mackie's error theory, prescriptivism, expressivism, and moral relativism, defending moral objectivism against the Modern Age's gray morality. Sylvia IV and Walters use Bentham, Mill's higher and lower pleasures with competent judges, and Railton's ideal-advisor moral realism to dismantle Mojo's defense that his Spineless Ones' ratings-driven bloodsports are just desire-satisfaction, indicting our own reality TV.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Not to Put Too Fine a Point on It
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Richard Greene asks why becoming Undead is bad for the one who becomes Undead, and why it seems worse than death, testing vampire and zombie cases against the standard accounts of death's badness. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' sets the experiential-blank frame, but Nagel's deprivation view fails because immortal vampires lose far fewer goods than they gain, and Williams's desire-frustration view fails because zombification replaces desires (scotch for blood) rather than frustrating cancelled ones. Mill's 'better Socrates dissatisfied than a pig satisfied' comparison also falls short since it yields only comparative, not objective, badness; Greene concludes Undeath is dreaded because the Undead do evil things, but no argument shows it is objectively bad, so one might as well make the best of it.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Good Guy Vampires
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Robert Arp models the vampire's unlife with substance and property dualism (a cursed soul persisting after the staked body in Rice and Stoker versus perishing with it in Blade), then uses Mill's distinction between lower bodily feelings and higher mental pleasures from Utilitarianism to explain how vampires can lament, in higher-pain, their inability to enjoy wind in their hair or wine. The hedonistic paradox dooms Lestat-style pleasure-seekers: seeking pleasure for its own sake yields either the pain of frustration (Louis's dead-twins trick) or boredom across immortal lifetimes ('it's somewhat boring, living forever'), while Aristotle's completed-state pleasures suggest the way out. Good guy vampires from Barnabas Collins to St. Germain escape the paradox by pursuing higher pleasures and activities for their own sake, confirming Mill's closing counsel that only those fixed on objects other than their own pleasure find happiness.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
higher-lower-pleasures.title: This Is the Age of Steel
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Littmann asks what a genuinely logical creature would do and grades the Cybermen against three accounts of reason: Hobbes's self-preservation and social contract, which the survival-focused Cybermen of 'The Tenth Planet' roughly satisfy but their later wars of conquest betray; Mill's utilitarianism, whose greatest-happiness principle, higher pleasures, liberty, and individuality condemn emotion-stripping, forced 'upgrades', and uniformity; and Hume's claim that reason alone motivates nothing, under which perfectly logical but emotionless Cybermen would simply do nothing at all. The upshot is that Cyberman 'logic' is incoherent — no theory of reason makes them rational.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
higher-lower-pleasures.title: How Can I Compete with Geniusness
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Timothy Dunn uses 'Patrick SmartPants', where a brain-coral transplant turns Patrick into a genius who abandons SpongeBob, to ask whether the happy ignoramus or the discontented genius lives better. After sketching a subjectivist defense of Patrick's choice to revert ('knowledge can never replace friendship'), the chapter tests Mill's hedonistic utilitarianism: since competent judges rank higher pleasures qualitatively above lower ones, Mill's dictum that it is better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied condemns Patrick's destruction of his own higher capacities. Dunn then presses two objections — that people's actual lower-pleasure preferences may be genuine rather than socially produced, and that the capacity for higher pleasure seems worthless without its actual experience — leaving Mill's verdict in tension.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
higher-lower-pleasures.title: To Riff or Not to Riff
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Stages Bentham's hedonism through the riff-versus-soliloquy question: 'push-pin is of equal value with the arts and sciences of music and poetry,' pleasures differing only in quantity, so a Keith Richards riff that out-pleases Hamlet's 'To be or not to be' is simply the greater pleasure, and ranking pleasures 'higher' or 'lower' is prejudice. The chapter closes by noting Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus even expands the moral community to animals, setting up Mill's dissent on behalf of higher pleasures.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Monkey Man
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Takes Mill's side against the 'doctrine of the swine' slur on hedonism: music belongs to the higher pleasures produced by distinctively human faculties. The chapter then asks whether Darwinian continuity between humans and other primates undermines Mill's divide—whether the pleasures of rock'n'roll, which evolved primates developed alongside language and cave painting, rely more on our animal or uniquely human faculties, with 'Monkey Man' as the emblematic case.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Only Rock’n’Roll
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Has the reader listen to 'It's Only Rock'n'Roll (But I Like It)' through headphones: the forty-four-second mark where a chorus and guitar part that sound like a horn section morph into a Chuck Berry riff shows that hearing is built from a lifetime of learned musical expectations. Quoting Mill's Autobiography on how music's pleasure 'fades with familiarity,' it argues the reverse happens too—a dynamic listener can be newly surprised by songs heard a zillion times.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Tell Me, Sister Dopamine
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Explains the Stones' pleasures neurochemically: a two-phase dopamine rush of anticipation and reward behind the spine-tingling moment of a song, the same pathway as life's four F's—feeding ('The Spider and the Fly'), fighting ('Street Fighting Man'), fleeing ('Before They Make Me Run'), and sex—and the one heroin exploits. Because there is no time to process every stimulus, prediction-making brains let mental models pass for reality, which is why frustrated and fulfilled musical expectations carry such a charge.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Some Things Just Stick in Your Mind
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Shows how the twelve-bar I-IV-V blues schema works by delaying, frustrating, and finally satisfying learned expectations, citing Huron's Sweet Anticipation. From the performer's side, Keith's 'Guitar Workshop' study of Jimmy Reed—leaving notes out and droning open strings at maximum unresolved tension—explains the jacked-up chords of 'Jumpin' Jack Flash' and 'Gimme Shelter,' plus the fake-horn trick heard in 'It's Only Rock'n'Roll.'

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Satisfaction
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Adjudicates the higher/lower dispute by disambiguating 'higher': a moral ranking Bentham rejects as prejudice, or a neurobiological-evolutionary distinction about distinctively human capacities that Mill can accept. Adopting Martha Nussbaum's reading of Mill in 'Mill between Aristotle and Bentham,' it concludes that rock'n'roll is both a lower pleasure (the same four-F dopamine pathways Keith insists on) and a higher one, imagining Mill teleported onto the tour bus for the demonstration.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Fitzpatrick asks whether Klosterman's low-culture project (tribute bands, Toby Keith, the McNuggets diet) is mere titillation or genuinely valuable. Bentham's pushpin-versus-poetry hedonism matches Klosterman's rejection of 'guilty pleasures,' while Aristotle's eudaimonia — and Plato's forms, on which a tribute band is a copy of a copy of a copy — condemns a life of amusement. Mill resolves the question twice over: higher and lower pleasures justify ranking Klosterman's contemplative criticism above mere sensation, and On Liberty's free market of ideas shows that even false or partial low-culture claims (about Garth Brooks, Spurlock's Super Size Me) keep high culture's truths from decaying into unexamined dogma.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Dracula and Philosophy
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Arp starts from Dracula's inability to love or find satisfaction and his awareness of it, then deploys Sidgwick's hedonistic paradox: pursuing pleasure for its own sake yields pain whether or not the pleasure is found, through mistaking pain for pleasure (Lestat on the dead twins), boredom, or emptiness. Mill's distinction between lower bodily and higher mental pleasures explains how vampires can enjoy the bodily pleasure of blood yet lament lacking joy and love, while substance versus property dualism (Plato as the substance dualist) frames whether the Count's soul survives when his body crumbles to dust. Aristotle's Book X pleasures of completed states and the 'virtuous vampires' from Barnabas Collins to St. Germain show the only escape from the dilemma: pursue activities for their own sake and higher mental pleasures rather than bodily pleasure alone.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
higher-lower-pleasures.title: 6. To the Pain
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Robison-Greene imagines the table of contents of Count Rugen's definitive book on pain, using the Zoo of Death and The Machine as her case studies. Bentham's dimensions of pain - intensity, duration, and propinquity - organize the analysis of Westley's torture, including Rugen's tactic of leaving The Machine beside the prisoner so anticipation itself hurts, and the metaphysical oddity of having years stolen from the far end of one's life. Mill's higher and lower pleasures explain why the orangutan's prolonged death disturbs us more than other kills (a chimpanzee can reflect on what is happening to her), and Singer's speciesism grounds the argument that animals' pain behavior shows they suffer, so inflicting it merely because they are animals is indefensible; by contrast Westley's empathy lets him out-sadist the sadists with the 'to the pain' speech.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
higher-lower-pleasures.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: The Bocks test three answers to the good life against the show: Howard as hedonist (laser-obstacle-strip-chess, the 'whore of Omaha') read through Bentham, Mill's higher and lower pleasures, and Aristippus; ethical egoism via Glaucon's ring of Gyges and Howard's offer to Skype rather than visit the deported Raj; and Hobbes's state of nature and social contract read into Sheldon's roommate agreement, whose lack of a Hobbesian sovereign leaves 'I settle all ties' arbitrary and rule-following too thin for ethics. Aristotle's virtue and practical wisdom crown Leonard — the nucleus of the social group, as Amy says — as the closest thing to the phronimos. The gang's sabotage of Dennis Kim with a manufactured girlfriend closes the chapter by asking who really ruined whose life.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
higher-lower-pleasures.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Eberl asks whether the Dude's 'pure abiding' is happiness: he runs Bentham's utility calculus on Dude-style pleasures (bowling's fecundity, the rug's purity, attending Marty's dance quintet for long-term rent goodwill) and Mill's higher/lower pleasures (Maude's vaginal art versus Logjammin'). Aristotle's verdict is that the Dude is not flourishing — his pleasures are incomplete, losable (the burned Torino), and he neglects his rational, social nature — yet Aristotle also ranks friendship with Walter and Donny highly, and Pieper's leisure, built on Aquinas's contemplation, gives the Dude's leisure a partial defense: he is incomplete but not bad, and he 'lives' while achievers merely make a living.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
higher-lower-pleasures.title: “Exit Game”
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Reading 'Striking Vipers' through its closed- and open-door imagery, the chapter asks whether Danny and Karl's virtual sex as Lance and Roxette is adultery, testing the question with Plato's Ring of Gyges (what people do when no one can see them), Locke's memory theory (if Danny remembers Roxette's sex acts, is Roxette Danny?), and behaviorist replies that only physical penetration counts. Nietzsche supplies the chapter's frame: his master/slave morality and his view of life as self-created representational art explain how the characters' hidden, mind-only moral inversion creates real existential meaning in virtual sex. The episode's fusion of bodily and mental pleasure is said to break down Mill's higher/lower pleasures distinction - 'lower' physical virtual pleasures yield a 'higher' sense of wholeness - and Schopenhauer's insatiable striving plus Husserl's meaning-conferring perception underwrite the conclusion that virtual love can be real, with Danny and Theo's once-a-year open marriage endorsed as an act-consequentialist balance between monotonous fidelity and escapist fantasy.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Greg Littmann asks what sort of life is worth living by holding Final Fantasy protagonists and FFXI Online players up to three standards. Hobbes's egoism and defense of absolute monarchy condemn the altruistic, authority-defying heroes (AVALANCHE, the rebels of FFII and FFVI) while partly approving the gil-grubbing, rule-breaking FFXI player; Mill's utilitarianism praises the world-saving heroes but condemns grinding down beastmen and rates most gaming a lower pleasure; Aristotle's function argument and golden mean find heroes like Yuna immoderately self-sacrificial yet credit ordinary FFXI adventurers with genuinely virtuous moderation, helping others while keeping their own interests in view.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Through the Mist and the Madness: Metallica's Message of Nonconformity, Individuality, and Truth
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Thomas Nys argues Metallica's early message of nonconformity and individuality ('Metal Militia', 'Motorbreath') converges with Mill's On Liberty: conformity withers human capacities and breeds a stagnant society. Mill's higher pleasures and Nozick's experience machine show why real happiness requires autonomy and earned achievement rather than passive pleasure - the point of 'Escape''s 'Life's for my own to live my own way'. He reads 'Leper Messiah' and 'Eye of the Beholder' as Metallica's versions of Mill's defense of free inquiry and truth against mindless conformity and censorship.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Notes
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Greg Littmann tests utilitarianism against Star Trek's heroes, reading Spock's 'the needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few' (The Wrath of Khan, Into Darkness) as Bentham's greatest-happiness principle, with Kirk's radiation-chamber death as its mirror image. He uses Mill's higher and lower pleasures to contrast the TNG crew's improbably refined holodeck tastes with Kirk's Argelius shore leave and Quark's 'Vulcan Love Slave', and Hume's slave-of-the-passions thesis to defend emotion against Vulcan suppression. Against Janeway killing Tuvix, Sisko's conspiracy in 'In the Pale Moonlight', and Kirk letting Edith Keeler die, he notes Trek never shows the many actually harmed, but sides with the utilitarians: favoring friends and the few is arbitrary discrimination.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Authoritarian Tennis Parents Are Their Children Really Any Worse Off
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Kevin Kinghorn asks whether authoritarian tennis parents (like the family of prodigy Jan Silva) harm their children's well-being, and tests three theories of the good life. He rejects Aristotle's perfectionist eudaimonia because the 'uniqueness of reason' criterion fails, substituting his own perfectionist-yet-mental-state view that well-being consists in the felt experience of connecting with others. He defends a Mill-style hedonism of higher and lower pleasures against Robert Nozick's experience-machine objection, arguing the machine only refutes the claim that we desire mental states, not that well-being consists in them, and dismisses desire-satisfaction theories and Feinberg's 'right to an open future' as failing to show that lost autonomy itself lowers a child's flourishing.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
higher-lower-pleasures.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Conard uses Mean Streets' guilt-ridden Charlie to survey conceptions of unhappiness against three definitions of happiness: beatitude (Aquinas), pleasure (Mill's hedonism), and flourishing (Aristotle's eudaimonia). He reads Charlie as damned in his own Catholic eyes, then invokes Nietzsche's Genealogy that religion manufactures guilt from internalized instinct, Plato's disordered soul and akrasia to explain Charlie's conflicting desires, and Schopenhauer's and Freud's pessimism that suffering is our natural state. He argues Charlie reaches dysdaimonia by acquiring vices and pursuing an ignoble (gangster) life, closing with Plato's Symposium and Sartre's facticity/transcendence to cast unhappiness as an ontological lack at the heart of human desire.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
higher-lower-pleasures.title: 8. Straight Edge and How to Live the Good Life
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Tierney reads Straight Edge hardcore (Minor Threat, Ian MacKaye, the black X) as punk's answer to the ancient question of the good life: sXe abstinence embodies Aristotle's eudaimonia through habitual virtue, maps onto the Buddha's first three noble truths (craving causes suffering, so quit the booze) and the three poisons, and Epictetus's concern only for what is within our power, while Mill's pleasure-based higher/lower pleasures serve as the dissenting voice. Spinoza on being ruled by emotions and on self-love supports the DIY self-mastery of MacKaye's Dischord Records, but the chapter weighs the scene's zealotry - Rollins reading death lists, Maximum Rock'n'Roll gatekeeping and the Biafra beating - against integrity that leaves room for dissent.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
higher-lower-pleasures.title: 16. Fine Dining with Children Starving
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Barta and Miranda pose Bourdain's Haiti dilemma — feasting on camera while people starve — as Peter Singer's 'Shallow Pond' / drowning-child argument about affluence and obligation. They test justifications for luxury from Bentham's intensity-vs-extent calculus, Mill's higher/lower pleasures, and Sidgwick's dualism of practical reason, then use Singer's Expanding Circle to show how Bourdain extended moral consideration to the poor, the foreign, and (partially) non-human animals through his work.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Musselman, Frohardt, and Lynch defend adult cannabis use through Mill's Harm Principle, using the hypothetical 'Patrick the pot smoker'—a professional who grows and smokes moderately on Friday nights—to argue that competent adults' self-regarding conduct is their own affair and does not violate the 'distinct and assignable obligations' Mill owes to family. They marshal health data (no lung-cancer link, negligible secondhand exposure, neuroprotective effects) to rebut the harm-to-others claim, and invoke Mill's higher intellectual pleasures plus the Michael-Phelps case to argue prohibition wastes resources better spent on the greater harms of alcohol and tobacco.

higher-lower-pleasures.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
higher-lower-pleasures.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
higher-lower-pleasures.relation: Prompted by the avalanche death of his climbing partner Charlie on the Super Couloir, Paul Charlton uses Mill's hedonistic utilitarianism to ask whether the risks of climbing can be ethically justified, insisting that blindly accepting risk is indefensible but deliberate, reasoned risk can be right. He weighs climbing's costs (frivolity, self-focus, danger to self and to grieving family) against its intrinsic value (joy, friendship, aesthetic experience) and instrumental value (cultivating human excellence, psychological growth, reprioritized lives), invoking Mill's higher/lower pleasures to argue quality of happiness matters, not just quantity. His conclusion is that climbing can be justified only when it produces more overall good than any alternative use of that time, leaving each climber to run the calculation for their own case.

web-of-belief.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
web-of-belief.title: Unknown
web-of-belief.relation: Nixon asks whether Neo's harrowing post-pill experiences justify believing Morpheus's story, given that knowledge is justified true belief and testimony alone would be foolish to believe. He argues the belief is self-defeating: if Neo discards twenty-five years of experience as machine-fed lies, he loses the interpretive rules of thumb (people don't lie, heads don't pop off, objects exist unobserved) needed to justify any new experience, so by epistemological holism he cannot be justified in concluding he was ever in the Matrix - even though the audience, with the bigger picture, knows he is right.

web-of-belief.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
web-of-belief.title: Unknown
web-of-belief.relation: Nixon tests whether the Matrix story is even conceptually coherent by asking whether we can make sense of someone whose beliefs are almost all false. Through the Cletus dialogue ('Bears are scary... Are they animals? News to me') he argues that belief attribution requires concept possession, and concept possession requires a background of true beliefs, so total falsehood is unintelligible - a meaning-holist point he credits to Quine, Davidson and Sellars - though he concedes the machines could still make most of our beliefs false, so the Matrix Possibility survives.

web-of-belief.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
web-of-belief.title: No Shoes for Muskrats How the 1956 Olympic Games Destroyed Indonesian Art
web-of-belief.relation: Hardcastle recounts how his talk pairing analytic philosophy with Python clips became a touring hit, framing the appeal through Hume's gap between the 'easy and obvious' philosophy that moves people — today's popular culture, including Python — and the 'accurate and abstruse' philosophy that became analytic philosophy. His solution reconceives philosophy as the construction and examination of conceptual schemes rather than a search for truth, with Python supplying what philosophy cannot: conceptual schemes lived from the inside, as when the Dead Parrot shopkeeper embodies Quinean holism by holding that the parrot is alive no matter the evidence, adjusting his other beliefs ('pining for the fjords') to save it, or when 'Nudge Nudge' shows two pub-goers with wholly different schemes chatting without either noticing. We laugh, he concludes, because a new conceptual scheme is by definition unfamiliar and surprising — which is why laughter, unlike disgust, is tied to intelligence, and why philosophy done well is surrounded by the laughter of contemplating what it suggests.

web-of-belief.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
web-of-belief.title: “The Cheese Shop,” Episode 33, Monty Python’s Flying Circus, “Salad Days”
web-of-belief.relation: This is Hardcastle's full talk: analytic philosophy's two revolts map onto Python clips, beginning with the logical positivists' revolt against metaphysics, whose cornerstone verifiability criterion self-destructs because it cannot verify itself. The positivist collapse hands philosophy to Quine's semantic holism — statements face experience 'not individually but only as a corporate body' — which the Dead Parrot sketch enacts as Praline the verificationist checking experiences against the shopkeeper-holist who preserves 'pining for the fjords' by adjusting other statements, and again in the Black Knight, who maintains 'None shall pass' through the loss of every limb. Holism's darker consequence, that no shared axioms are guaranteed so reason cannot found society, appears in the 'Argument Clinic' and in 'Nudge Nudge' as two men effectively speaking different languages in different worlds, while the witch-burning logic illustrates empirically bad human reasoning. The Cheese Shop sketch crowns the continental side — Mr. Mousebender an existentialist hero choosing cheese in an unfeeling world, Mr. Wensleydale the burden of life returning negative answers like Sisyphus's rock — and the Bruces' Philosophers Song is declared the best history of philosophy because it is sung.

web-of-belief.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
web-of-belief.title: Poker and Philosophy
web-of-belief.relation: Ellis analyzes expert poker as thought attribution, spelling the iterations out to the sixth order in a Big Slick hand against T.J. Cloutier, then argues via Quine's 'gavagai' rabbit and Davidson's interpretationism that attributing thoughts to opponents requires assuming deep shared belief — which explains why pros misread novices whose minds they cannot model. The centerpiece is Dan Harrington's reconstruction of Daniel Negreanu's 2004 river raise against Freddy Deeb as a set of fourth-order-or-below attributions (Deeb will read a small raise as a lure bet and fold the best hand), not one towering thought. It ends asking how anyone ever learns what an opponent thinks from actions that are a vector of beliefs and desires, and notes poker forces rare deep agreement among strangers worldwide.

web-of-belief.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
web-of-belief.title: Evidence Rewarded
web-of-belief.relation: Goldwater reads Bill James's sabermetric revolution through Quine: science is a continuation of common sense, but mature science replaces the 'animal sense of similarity' (being a Yankee, batting average, RBI) with predictive, league- and park-adjusted categories, turning atomistic box-score tallies into holistic statistics that acquire meaning only from the whole web of data. Because science recognizes only repeatable types, it cannot countenance miracles—Carlton Fisk's 1975 homer greeted by the 'Hallelujah Chorus,' Dave Roberts's steal in 2004—whose meaning lies in happening exactly once. His resolution: GMs like John Henry and Theo Epstein need Quinean prediction, while fans keep the religious language of faith, hope, and redemption.

web-of-belief.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
web-of-belief.title: Psych and Philosophy
web-of-belief.relation: Jones argues that Shawn's 'psychic' act is really hypersensory perception (HSP) - noticing cat fur, fine print, blood spatter - feeding inference to the best explanation (IBE), the natural abductive method Sherlock Holmes mislabels deduction, with Clever Hans and Ilga Kirks as real-world parallels. Applying IBE with Ockham's Razor to the two hypotheses 'he's psychic' versus 'he's hyper-observant,' she concludes the natural explanation should win for everyone: Lassiter's skepticism tracks the evidence, Gus knows better despite believing in ghosts, and Chief Vick shouldn't buy the supernatural story either. Juliet's belief survives only through background supernatural beliefs, a psychic-friendly culture, and ignoring the clues Gus feeds Shawn, which the chapter diagnoses as the same public misunderstanding of the scope and limits of science that keeps most Americans believing in ESP.

web-of-belief.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
web-of-belief.title: 11. Should We Execute the Erudite
web-of-belief.relation: Michaud and Watkins ask whether Roth is right that the knowledge-hoarding Erudite are so dangerous we might need to eliminate them, and answer that knowledge is dangerous in three ways. Following Foucault ('it is impossible for knowledge not to engender power'), the powerful define what counts as knowledge - from the church blessing feudalism to the medical community pathologizing gay and transgender people - and following Piaget, new knowledge threatens the interconnected belief schemas (diagrammed as beliefs resting on beliefs) that keep 'faction before blood' and our sense of being special stable, which is why Divergents, evolution, and Copernicus provoke such violent disequilibrium. A Descartes-style simulation scenario - you may be inside Roth's world right now, weeded out for reading the books - and David Lewis's point that investigating knowledge destroys it then show that the real danger is not knowledge but the arrogance of certainty: Jeanine was never a true Erudite.

web-of-belief.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
web-of-belief.title: 25. Should Catelyn Have Trusted Brienne
web-of-belief.relation: McNabb and Andrews ask whether Catelyn was warranted in trusting Brienne as her sworn sword after Brienne failed to save Renly, and test two theories of warrant. On accessibilist coherentism, Catelyn's accessible evidence - Brienne's prowess, her devastation at Renly's death, 'Renly's death was no fault of yours' - fits her web of beliefs like a new strand in a spider's web; on Plantinga-style proper functionalism, illustrated by the accident-created Labman replica and the Lord of Light randomizing a design plan, Catelyn's naturally formed belief that Brienne is trustworthy is warranted if her faculties are properly functioning, truth-aimed, and well designed - which Brienne's record through rescuing Sansa vindicates.

web-of-belief.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
web-of-belief.title: 8. Is It a Fact that Facts Don’t Matter
web-of-belief.relation: Steele distinguishes facts as mind-independent reality from facts as expert-certified statements to show that Kellyanne Conway's alternative facts and Adams's own slogans trade on this ambiguity, and that Adams performatively contradicts himself every time he insists his predictions are true and matter. Analyzing the cognitive-dissonance hallucinations of Trump-is-Hitler and then Trump-is-incompetent, he argues that on Adams's own account brute facts proved irresistible, and that such belief revision is rational Popperian conjecture and refutation, plus the conservative strategy of saving fundamental theories (Coulomb's law) and dropping minor ones when the fuse blows. Against the claim that humans are irrational he recalls Aristotle's Rhetoric as persuasion's legitimate complement to the Prior Analytics, and leans on Percival to show propaganda fits a rational-reader model, citing the slow, fact-driven shift on gay marriage.

web-of-belief.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
web-of-belief.title: 6. But What Does It Mean
web-of-belief.relation: Argues that asking "what does it mean?" of Twin Peaks is the wrong question, because Lynch builds the show out of aesthetically incomplete material. Kant's "purposiveness without purpose" and the free play of understanding and imagination explain the opening credits' waterfalls, pines, and mill blades, while Russell's incomplete symbols ("the present king of France is bald") model the swaying traffic light and Harriet's "full blossom of the evening," and Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence applies to Black Lodge clues like "the man in the smiling bag" and the Arm's whoops, which support many consistent but unprovable interpretations. Susanne Langer's account of film as a dream-like virtual present, capped by Part 8's atomic-bomb sequence, grounds the claim that Lynch means viewers to complete the meaning themselves.

web-of-belief.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
web-of-belief.title: Wonderland and the Real World
web-of-belief.relation: Extracts three problems of induction from Alice's misadventures: predicting the future (Hume's problem: nothing rationally compels Humpty Dumpty to agree the world will not turn into Wonderland at 6 a.m. tomorrow), proving whose dream it is (Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence: Tweedledee can accommodate any evidence within the theory that Alice exists only in the Red King's dream), and translating Wonderese (Quine's indeterminacy: pointing at the White Rabbit cannot fix whether natives mean the rabbit, its parts, or its stages, nor what 'muchness' means). Brendan Shea shows Alice succeeding where the creatures fail by the criteria Hume and Quine endorse: experimentation, simplicity, conservatism of belief, and a principle of charity in translation.

web-of-belief.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
web-of-belief.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
web-of-belief.relation: Reads the 'Sad Sack' photograph, which Wayne Jarvis sees as Iraqi WMD bunkers and Barry Zuckerkorn sees as Tobias's testicles, through the Duhem-Quine thesis of underdetermination and Kuhn's theory-ladenness of observation: the dominant 'George Sr. the traitor' paradigm dictates what is seen and nearly mobilizes Buster for war, while Barry's rival theory creates a crisis that only the omniscient narrator resolves. Kuhn's five criteria for theory choice (accuracy, consistency, scope, simplicity, fruitfulness) are applied to the rival 'theories', and George Michael's failed eye exam dramatizes the skeptical moment when no lens lets you see clearly, showing knowledge is a social and political position.

web-of-belief.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
web-of-belief.title: NOTES
web-of-belief.relation: Hare treats mass photography—from the daguerreotype through digital cameras, Abu Ghraib snapshots, and diagnostic imaging—as making everyone a practicing epistemologist caught between two folk tenets: the photo as mirror of reality and as manipulation of reality. Defending photography as a genuine causal 'mode of seeing' (a prosthetic like telescopes), he proposes 'flexible realism,' adjusting Dewey's warranted assertibility and virtue-epistemology standards to context, and invokes William James's defense of beneficial 'overbeliefs' when National Geographic images strengthen confidence in one's own culture. Reading the Fallujah lead-pipe photo debate between editors Sullivan and Kushner, he uses Quine's recalcitrant-experience and web-of-belief holism—extended by Morton White's 'holistic pragmatism'—to show moral, epistemic, sensory, and emotional claims are tested together, and frames photography's democratization via Walter Benjamin's mechanical reproduction and loss of aura.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
ghost-in-the-machine.title: The Machine-Made Ghost Or, The Philosophy of Mind, Matrix Style
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Holt announces his menu: after setting aside the standard ports of entry - Descartes's malicious demon, the brain-in-a-vat remade as body-in-a-vat, and the truth-versus-happiness question - he takes up the philosophy of mind his title advertises, the 'machine-made ghost' playing on the 'ghost in the machine' picture of the mind as a spirit inhabiting the body. He previews two entrees - arguing that artificial minds are possible and that mental states are brain states - and for dessert a solution to the hard problem of consciousness.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Unknown
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Holt runs a crash course in the mind-body problem: Descartes's thinking, unextended mind - the 'ghost in the machine' he also hears in the Police album - fails to explain how essentially different substances interact; behaviorism mistakes the evidence for mental states (dispositions to say 'Ouch!') for what the evidence is evidence of; so he defends materialism, the view that mental states are brain states, against the objections that it makes mind causally inert (epiphenomenal) and that pain is multiply realizable, teasing that the Matrix machines could in principle feel silicon pain.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Wave Goodbye from the Catbus
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Heinricy argues anime is the richest medium for posthuman theory because it shows bodies 'in a state of becoming' rather than as grotesque boundary violations: Miyazaki's Catbus and Totoro, Haku's dragon transformation and Chihiro's pig parents in Spirited Away, and the cursed pig-headed aviator of Porco Rosso all treat morphing bodies as possibility, not horror. She sorts anime posthumanism into two valences: a 'Ghost in the Machine' dream of consciousness leaving the body altogether (Motoko merging with the net in Ghost in the Shell), which she rebuts via N. Katherine Hayles's point that consciousness is embodied and would change with any new body, and hybrid configurations like mecha (Gundam, Robotech) where body and machine drive each other. Following Donna Haraway, she contends we are all already cyborgs — vaccines, engineered food, treated water — and credits Japan's nuclear history (via Susan Napier) and its shape-shifting folklore for why anime embraces rather than fears the transformed body.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Who Wants to Be Human Anyway
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Reads Kenji Kawai's thrice-repeated minyo 'Ghost theme' as the key to Major Kusanagi's quest in Ghost in the Shell and Innocence: each richer orchestration tracks her progress from manufactured shell, through the diving-scene worry that only others' treatment makes her human, to merging with the Puppet Master. Using Koestler's holons — individuals preserved while functioning within an evolving whole — and his view of consciousness as emergent (itself a rejection of both Descartes's immaterial soul and Ryle's dismissal of the 'ghost in the machine'), the chapter argues Oshii first celebrates the Major's Atman-like self-transcendence, then subverts Koestler in Innocence by making machines human: the ghost-dubbed gynoids act as a voiceless pack while the Major, still recognizably herself, aids Batou from the net — and Kawai's music literally gives the dolls a voice.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Cyborg Goddess
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Reads Ghost in the Shell as Donna Haraway's 'Cyborg Manifesto' made flesh: Major Kusanagi is built not born, has no sexuality or romance, and relegates male partners to sidekicks, enacting Haraway's post-gender cyborg that breaks the dualisms binding women to body, nature, and reproduction. The chapter traces the 'ghost' back through Koestler to Ryle's mockery of Descartes's mind-body dualism, reads the genderless, net-born Puppet Master as the Singularity of transhumanist philosophy, and interprets the Major–Puppet Master fusion — urged to 'come out of the shadows and into the light' in an explicit Plato's-cave gesture — as a posthuman, techno-spiritual 'Cyborg Goddess' that renders both gender and humanity obsolete.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Do You Think Androids Have Souls
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: The chapter sets up strong versus weak AI through Rachael's account of the Rosen Association's strategy of iterating models until one is indistinguishable, then brings in Gaita's 'non-speculative conception' of a soul via Wittgenstein's remark that 'My attitude towards him is an attitude towards a soul.' Heidegger's warning that technology tempts us to treat others as mere means is dramatized in Deckard's realization after meeting the predatory bounty hunter Phil Resch that he had been viewing androids, and hence himself, as means; his half-measure of wishing other androids did the retiring shows how far he still has to go.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Hess asks whether the monster has a soul and makes him the test case between physicalism (Kim, Churchland, van Inwagen) and dualism: recasting Frank Jackson's Mary as a color-blind monster who learns every physical fact about color vision, receives new eyes on Walton's ship, and then learns the 'what it is like' of seeing red for the first time, he argues there are nonphysical mental facts, so physicalism is false. He then runs Plantinga's argument that we are not our bodies or brains through a machine that replaces the monster's parts and hemispheres one by one while he stays conscious, and adds near-death out-of-body evidence like Maria's window-ledge shoe to suggest we can exist disembodied. The upshot is symmetric: whatever we conclude about the monster's soul we must conclude about our own - so be careful about assuming who does and does not have a soul, even monsters.

ghost-in-the-machine.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
ghost-in-the-machine.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
ghost-in-the-machine.relation: Spyros Petrounakos reads Frankenstein as a Cartesian narrative whose external events run parallel to the inner worlds of Victor and the creature, from Victor's solitary conception of 'bestowing animation upon lifeless matter' to his imprisonment in a truth nobody would believe when Justine's life is at stake.
