buddhist-non-self.relation: Argues that Aang's energybending victory over Ozai vindicates a Buddhist conception of power against Ozai's equation of power with domination: the Lion Turtle's 'unbendable spirit' is not resistance but thorough vulnerability, achieved through the true heart (overcoming the five hindrances mapped onto Aang's sensory desire, ill will, dullness, restlessness, and doubt across the series) and the true mind (overcoming the fundamental delusion of a self separate from others, learned from Huu in 'The Swamp' and Guru Pathik). The merging of Aang's and Ozai's spirits is pictured by the metaphor of Indra's net, and Indra's own Jataka victory, halting his assault to protect eagle hatchlings and disorienting the demons, parallels Aang's refusal to win by killing. Drawing on a Zen story of the abbot who could 'be run through by a sword without batting an eye', the chapter concludes that Aang's fearlessness flows from compassion, so that weakness by Ozai's standard is precisely the power that defeats him.

buddhist-non-self.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhist-non-self.title: Journey’s End and a Vision of a New Community
buddhist-non-self.relation: Reads Aang's quest through the Karmapa Ogyen Trinley Dorje's book Interconnected: like the seventeenth Karmapa, identified at age seven and taken from his family, Aang learns that an exalted title complicates friendship and that freedom is self-control rather than the rugged individualism of the American hero's quest. Training episodes (Katara's jealous competition in 'The Waterbending Scroll', Jeong Jeong's warnings, the Toph-versus-Katara sifu debate in 'Bitter Work') show moral training as communal, widening from Team Avatar as adoptive family toward universal compassion, with Aang's refusal to open the seventh chakra illustrating how local attachment can obstruct universal love. Zuko's counter-arc from competition, isolation, and betrayal to humility, forgiveness, and contentment shows compassion turning an enemy into a friend, and the finale's simultaneous battles (White Lotus liberating Ba Sing Se, Sokka and Toph destroying the fleet) affirm that Aang wins as an 'interdependent individual', never alone.

buddhist-non-self.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
buddhist-non-self.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
buddhist-non-self.relation: LoPresti uses 'This Week in God' segments (Ed Helms refereeing a Hindu-versus-Mayan 'faith-off', Colbert's roast line that all religions are infinite paths to accepting Jesus, Rob Corddry's purification rituals and God Exchange stock ticker) to lay out exclusivism, inclusivism, and pluralism as responses to religious diversity. Inclusivism like Colbert's 'anonymous Christian' logic is exposed as intellectual imperialism that erases genuinely distinct teachings such as the Buddhist non-self and impermanence, while the chapter defends a deep pluralism against the relativism that makes 'all religions equally true' meaningless. Its eulogy for the God Machine borrows Marx's view of religion as an instrument of mass control to explain why religious humor now survives only through a political lens.

buddhist-non-self.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
buddhist-non-self.title: Hakuna Matata, Bodhisattva
buddhist-non-self.relation: Sets up Disney's maxim 'Hey kid, you can be a hero' as the direct opposite of Zen's 'Hey kid, you can be a buddha': escapism versus liberation, told through the life of Dogen, whose monastic choice parallels Disney hero narratives. Mickey in Steamboat Willie — a bundle of still frames with no sound and no real 'he' — illustrates the Buddha's three marks of existence (emptiness, impermanence, frustration), and the chapter argues Disney products are calibrated distractions from these marks while Dogen counsels facing them, with Ariel's Andersen fate as the price of fantasy. It closes on Disney's merchandising machine (Yoda, Star Wars sequels, direct-to-video cash grabs) as everything the countercultural minimalist Yoda or Baloo's bare necessities stand against, concluding that real hakuna matata is accepting impermanence rather than escaping it.

buddhist-non-self.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
buddhist-non-self.title: 4. Can We Do Enough Good
buddhist-non-self.relation: Interrogates Chidi's question 'why do we choose to be good?' through Hobbes's selfish state of nature, Rousseau's hardwired compassion (Michael's 'little voice' in Eleanor's head), and Hume's bundle theory extended Buddhist-style to a non-self, which grounds Michael's plea to Judge Gen that bad communities made the four humans bad and a better community (Team Cockroach, the Brainy Bunch) can make them good. Nietzsche's account of how communities define their own customs as 'good' then exposes the deeper flaw: the afterlife's accountants impose their in-group's preferences on all humanity, which is why even Doug Forcett's point-maximizing life cannot clear the bar. The chapter ends by asking Michael's real question: who gets to decide what's good?

buddhist-non-self.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
buddhist-non-self.title: a9.xhtml
buddhist-non-self.relation: The chapter argues Tolkien's clearest moral in The Hobbit is against possessiveness, starting from Aquinas' definition of greed as 'immoderate love of riches': dragon-sickness ruins Thorin and drowns the Master of Lake-town starving in the wilderness with his gold, and Gollum shows the isolating end of a life organized around a 'precious'. Buddhism reframes the diagnosis - Gollum's craving (tanha) is rooted in ignorance (avidya) of the self's illusoriness, since grasping enriches a self that does not exist, per the Four Noble Truths - while Laozi's 'he who knows he has enough is rich' and Thoreau's 'a man is rich in proportion to the things he can afford to let alone' are embodied by Beorn and the gift-giving, nearly government-less hobbits. Bilbo's generosity - giving away the Arkenstone worth 'more than a river of gold', taking only two small chests, later giving Sting and the mithril coat to Frodo - is the book's counter-example to greed.

buddhist-non-self.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
buddhist-non-self.title: Notes
buddhist-non-self.relation: Kahn argues LEGO play embodies the Buddhist teaching of impermanence that the Buddha states in the Digha Nikaya ('Impermanent are all component things...'): his childhood urge to superglue creations and Finn's father's Kragle dramatize the clinging that produces anxiety when things change, from brick formulations to discontinued sets and even funerals' wilting flowers. The LEGO Star Wars Death Star illustrates non-self — no Death Star exists apart from its 3,803 pieces, and no self apart from shifting aggregates — and the five aggregates (form, sensation, perception, formations, consciousness) are unpacked through building experiences like discovering a daughter has opened the mint Taj Mahal set. Tibetan sand mandalas, painstakingly built then ritually dissolved, model the ceremonial demolition of LEGO creations, teaching acceptance of change without sliding into a nihilistic 'why bother building at all'.

buddhist-non-self.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
buddhist-non-self.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
buddhist-non-self.relation: Godwin reads Spider-Man 3's black-suit episode as a question about the self: with the symbiote amplifying his anger, is Peter still Peter? Against Hume's and the Buddha's bundle theories, on which the self is only an imagined aggregate of thoughts and feelings, and Reid's common-sense simple self, she advances the pragmatist 'social self' of Peirce, James, Dewey, and Mead, updated as Engel's biopsychosocial model: Peter's identity is a shifting web of biology, psyche, and relationships (Aunt May, MJ, Harry) expressed in actions and character. Eddie succumbs to the symbiote because, as Dewey says of the slave to his own blind desires, hatred constitutes who he is, while Peter's thicker web of good relations lets him shed the suit at the church bell.

buddhist-non-self.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
buddhist-non-self.title: 23. I Fight Crime in My Sleep
buddhist-non-self.relation: A Fight Club-style Arkham case study: a patient's hallucinated Superman companion is diagnosed by a Buddhist psychiatrist who explains the three marks of existence—impermanence, non-self, and dissatisfaction—arguing superheroes impose order and a fabricated second self on a world that resists both, so Superman's super-intellect and even flight are distractions (levitation should be ignored; the Buddha-eye beats x-ray vision) while Batman's violence and psychosis, compared to American Psycho's Patrick Bateman, make awakening impossible—both are victims of Mara. A robber literally named David Hume objects that the heroes' law and order is grounded on what ought to be rather than what is, and a Gandhi quote on preferring one's own bad government explains why Batman finally kryptonites his alien 'friend.' The verdict inverts the book's debate: conquering the deceiver within is the only superpower worth having.

buddhist-non-self.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
buddhist-non-self.title: Notes
buddhist-non-self.relation: Reads Rust's 'dream inside a locked room' and 'everybody is nobody' monologues through the dream-argument and illusion-of-self traditions: the Upanishads and Advaita's atman/brahman, Vasubandhu's Buddhist non-self, Zhuangzi's butterfly dream, Plato's Theaetetus, and Descartes' dream doubt, plus Metzinger's self-model neuroscience. It diagnoses Rust as a neuro-nihilist in Metzinger's sense and defines his predicament with Nietzsche's nihilist, who judges the world as it is that it ought not to be, while noting Schopenhauer misread India's religions as pessimistic. Thompson argues nihilism is a deep insight gone awry — the self is not a thing but an enacted process like dancing — and reads Rust's final near-death experience of love as proof that transcendence of the dream of being a person is possible.

buddhist-non-self.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
buddhist-non-self.title: The Zen Master and the Big Aristotle
buddhist-non-self.relation: Allhoff and Vaidya argue against the skeptic that philosophy is useless 'bullshit' (nodding to Frankfurt's book) by showing how Phil Jackson's coaching applies it. Jackson's Zen Buddhism, especially zazen meditation and selfless 'triangle offense' play, teaches players to empty the ego and stay in the present, transforming Jordan from point-maker to play-maker; and Jackson's gift of Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics to Shaquille O'Neal, who then dubbed himself 'the Big Aristotle,' illustrates Aristotle's doctrine that excellence (his improved free-throw shooting, his generosity) is a habit built by repetition.

buddhist-non-self.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
buddhist-non-self.title: Twelfth Hole Midround and Midlife Defining Moments
buddhist-non-self.relation: Andy Wible uses defining mid-round shots (the water ball on Augusta's twelfth, the shank that ruins a round) as a way into theories of personal identity, asking why some events make us who we are. He runs through body theory, Descartes's soul theory ('I think, therefore I am'), and Locke's memory theory (the prince-and-cobbler case), refining it with Shoemaker's quasi-memories, to argue that memory is central to identity and explains why a golfer cannot shake a bad shot. He then weighs the Buddhist/Humean/Heraclitean denial of a permanent self as a coping tool ('someone else hit the shank') and debates whether the beta-blocker Propranolol, which dulls adrenaline-fixed memories, could ethically erase the yips much as it treats PTSD.

buddhist-non-self.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
buddhist-non-self.title: Genius All the Time The Beats, Spontaneous Presence, and Primordial Ground
buddhist-non-self.relation: Marc Olmsted reads Beat spontaneity through Tantric (Vajrayana) Buddhism, arguing that 'first thought, best thought' and Kerouac's 'Mind is shapely, art is shapely' rest on the view that enlightenment/awareness is already present and need only be recognized. He maps Ginsberg's poetics onto the Tantric terms Ground, Path, and Fruition, tying shamatha-vipashyana practice and the doctrine of anatta (no-self) to the poet catching the first pre-conceptual thought. Ginsberg's Blake visions, his study under Trungpa and Gelek Rinpoche, and Burroughs's cut-up 'homemade yankee tantra' are offered as evidence that Beat composition enacts a Buddhist recognition of primordial, empty, self-existing awareness.

buddhist-non-self.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
buddhist-non-self.title: 2. Know Thyself, Agent Cooper!
buddhist-non-self.relation: De Carvalho reads Cooper's ordeal in the Black Lodge as a journey of self-knowledge, distinguishing 'knowing yourself' (your feelings, as Laura sought with Dr. Jacoby) from 'knowing your Self' in the deep sense of Vedanta's Brahman and Tibetan Buddhism's Mind. He sets Hume's bundle theory—the failure to catch a self behind the perceptions—against the Hindu Swami's ocean-and-waves image of an eternal Self beyond thought, and reads Cooper's confrontation with his screaming-Laura and doppelganger visions via the Tibetan Book of the Dead and Jung's shadow: facing his fears with imperfect courage, Cooper fails to integrate his shadow and is split in two.

buddhist-non-self.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
buddhist-non-self.title: 25. Close Your Eyes, Breathe, and Stick It to the Man
buddhist-non-self.relation: Seth Walker presents the Buddha ('Sid', Noah Levine's 'original rebel') as a punk who abandoned palace privilege after seeing sickness, aging, and death, teaching the four noble truths as a revolt against craving, caste, and blind tradition - the five precepts become 'punk-cepts'. He links Buddhist practice to punk through Straight Edge abstinence (Minor Threat's X), Brad Warner's Hardcore Zen, and 'skillful means', arguing that an inner rebellion must accompany the outer one since drugs and mindless violence are poorly channeled revolt. The Situationist International's 'spectacle' of passive consumption and Socially Engaged Buddhism (ordaining trees against deforestation, Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation, grounded in the doctrine of non-self) show both traditions demanding permanent revolution and community.

buddhist-non-self.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
buddhist-non-self.title: “How Could Anyone Fall in Love with a Toaster ” Cylons as Persons
buddhist-non-self.relation: James McRae reads Battlestar Galactica through Zen Buddhism: the fleet's annihilation and constant death illustrate the Four Noble Truths' duhkha, arising from ignorant attachment and violating interdependent arising (no-self and impermanence). Cylon death-and-resurrection parallels karma and rebirth ('all of this has happened before'), Leoben acts as a koan-wielding roshi unsettling Starbuck's assumptions, and Nishida's kenotic God as Absolute Nothingness matches the Cylons' 'we're all God.' Because Cylons feel pain, suffer cognitively, and earn karma, McRae concludes they are persons capable of satori who should seek compassionate reconciliation with humans.

buddhist-non-self.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
buddhist-non-self.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
buddhist-non-self.relation: LoPresti uses the 'This Week in God' segments (the God Machine, Ed Helms's Hindu-vs-Mayan 'faith-off,' Colbert's inclusivist White House roast) to lay out three responses to religious diversity—exclusivism, inclusivism, and pluralism—and defends John Cobb's Whiteheadian process-metaphysics pluralism. He insists the distinct concepts of religions be respected rather than collapsed, citing Buddhist impermanence and no-Self and the South Asian Atman/Brahman as unique and non-reducible, and closes by reading the show's turn to political framing of religion through Marx's claim that religion is a mechanism for controlling the masses.

buddhist-non-self.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
buddhist-non-self.title: MOTHERHOOD
buddhist-non-self.relation: Sheryl Tuttle Ross applies three of the Buddhist noble truths – pain is inevitable, pain arises from attachment, suffering can end – to contemporary mothering, contrasting the Buddhist acceptance of pain with Bentham's utilitarian pleasure-maximizing. Drawing on Thich Nhat Hanh's mindfulness and the doctrines of impermanence and no-self, she offers 'mommy meditations' (breathe, become aware, recognize social scripts, respond kindly) and reads the novel I Don't Know How She Does It, whose 'Court of Motherhood' dramatizes the guilt-inducing scripts mindfulness helps mothers see through to experience beauty in ordinary moments.

buddhist-non-self.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
buddhist-non-self.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
buddhist-non-self.relation: Geisz reads his daily morning coffee ritual through Buddhist metaphysics: the pre-caffeine grogginess and its transient relief illustrate saṃsāra and duḥkha, the First Noble Truth, driven by self-centered craving (the Second). The transience of the perfect-temperature cup shows impermanence (anitya), and the question of whether a 'self' pre- or post-coffee exists is answered by anatman — he offers three hypotheses (full self dormant, half coffee-cyborg, self created ex Coffea) then dissolves them into no-self plus dependent arising, where the cup and drinker are empty nodes in a web of physical, economic, and karmic conditions. Each intentional sip lays down karma that binds tomorrow's 'me' further into the cycle.

buddhist-non-self.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
buddhist-non-self.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
buddhist-non-self.relation: Lynch, a tattooed Buddhist philosophy professor, tests his largely Buddhist body art (an Om-mani-padme-hum armband, Bodhidharma, the Buddha's face, the eight-spoked Wheel and lotus, a double-vajra) against the Buddha's Three Marks of Existence. He argues a 'permanent' tattoo need not contradict impermanence any more than Gruzalski's washed-away sandcastle if approached mindfully, that custom ink need not reify a self given the chariot analogy of no-self (which he links to Hume's bundle view), and that the pain of tattooing directly instantiates dukkha and can become an object of meditation and compassion. Mindful tattooing, he concludes, can itself be authentic Buddhist practice.

buddhist-non-self.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
buddhist-non-self.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
buddhist-non-self.relation: Abby Thompson, a somatic psychologist, sets Raja yoga metaphysics (five koshas, a blissful true self distinct from the ego, nadis and chakras as energy flow) beside clinical psychology's brain-chemistry, DSM model, arguing the two paradigms are complementary. Using warrior II and camel pose plus the neuroscience maxim 'neurons that fire together wire together,' she shows how yoga trains self-regulation, distinguishes constructive discomfort from injurious pain, and can serve as complementary therapy — with instructors bearing therapist-like responsibility for the emotional vulnerability and transference that arise on the mat.

buddhist-non-self.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
buddhist-non-self.title: “How Could Anyone Fall in Love with a Toaster ” Cylons as Persons
buddhist-non-self.relation: McRae reads Battlestar Galactica through Zen Buddhism, using Dogen and the Four Noble Truths. The fleet's relentless suffering (the "33" jumps, the Olympic Carrier), impermanence (Roslin's dwindling headcount), and no-self frame duhkha; Leoben functions as a roshi whose koan-like preaching makes Starbuck and Adama question their false ideals, and the Cylon death-and-resurrection cycle parallels karma and rebirth. Because Cylons feel and are cognitively aware of pain and can accrue karma, McRae concludes they are persons capable of satori, so human and Cylon liberation are intertwined.

buddhist-non-self.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
buddhist-non-self.title: 42. Up in the Air as Philosophy Buddhism and the Middle Path
buddhist-non-self.relation: Duffy reads Ryan Bingham's arc in Up in the Air as a Zen Buddhist parable paralleling Hesse's Siddhartha. Ryan preaches an 'empty backpack' philosophy of nonattachment and treats the miles as their own point, but Duffy argues he only intellectually grasps the four noble truths — dukkha, its cause in attachment (tṛṣṇā), and the eightfold path — until his failed attachment to Alex and his mentorship of Natalie make him actually suffer. Like Siddhartha with his son, Ryan learns wisdom must be experienced, that the anattā (non-self) doctrine undercuts the identity he built on his job, and that the goal is not escaping the world but living the Middle Path within it, present to suffering rather than spinning silver linings.

buddhism.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
buddhism.title: Unknown
buddhism.relation: Brannigan reads the film's mirror imagery through the Buddha's mirror instruction to his son Rahula: Neo touching the dripping mirror and becoming the mirror marks his awakening to the naked truth (aletheia as nakedness) that his world is a programmed illusion, Smith's dark sunglasses distort while Morpheus's mirrored glasses clarify, and Neo's reflection in the spoon-bending boy's spoon signals clarity. 'There is no spoon' parallels the Zen mondo where neither flag nor wind moves but only mind, and shows that reflected images are not reality - the world is maya. The deepest lesson is anatman: just as there is no spoon there is no Neo, no fixed self, and Rahula's lesson grounds the interdependence (pratityasamutpada) of all actions on others.

buddhism.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
buddhism.title: Unknown
buddhism.relation: Brannigan tests whether The Matrix is a Buddhist film and finds four incongruities: its Zoroastrian good-versus-evil dualism (the system and those in it as 'enemies') against karuna and metta, its glorified gun violence ('guns, lots of guns') against ahimsa, its crass language against right speech, and its human-centeredness against the Buddha-nature of all sentient beings, including 'sentient programs'. He concedes the slaughter might be read symbolically as slaying the mind's three poisons, as Manjusri's sword does, but rejects calling the result 'American Buddhism'. He concludes the film is a deliberate syncretism of Christianity, Platonism, and Buddhism that still conveys the Buddhist message of liberation from the mind.

buddhism.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
buddhism.title: Unknown
buddhism.relation: The chapter argues the film is by no means a Christian movie: Neo is a violent, far-from-sinless mere human savior; the fundamental human problem is ignorance and illusion (Gnostic and Eastern) rather than sin and alienation from God; the rebels' belief that Neo is the reincarnation of the earlier liberator mirrors the Dalai Lama search the Wachowskis cite, though reincarnation is rejected by all major Christian sects; and 'there is no spoon' asserts the illusoriness of empirical reality that Christianity denies. The film's malleable, cyclical time and the Wachowskis' answer that faith is 'in oneself' complete a syncretistic tapestry the essay goes on to examine as religious pluralism.

buddhism.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
buddhism.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
buddhism.relation: Jennifer McMahon and Steve Csaki compare Tolkien with Zen Buddhism and Taoism on four themes while insisting on the real differences. Tolkien's talking trees (Old Man Willow, Treebeard's 'half awake' forest) invite comparison with Buddhist universal sentience and Dogen's walking mountains, but Tolkien anthropomorphizes where Buddhism grants non-human modes of sentience; the hobbits' ties to the Shire echo dependent origination, though Tolkien's stewardship and preference for the domesticated Shire over sinister wild nature remain Western. Frodo's succession of mentors (Bilbo, Gandalf, Aragorn, and the unlikely 'Master Samwise') parallels the Zen master-student relation, while Tolkien's war of light against darkness - nine Walkers against nine Riders - is decisively not the Taoist balance of yin and yang, for Taoists destroying either cosmic force would itself produce evil.

buddhism.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
buddhism.title: Ballparks, Dojos, and Other Places of Enlightenment
buddhism.relation: Bassham argues that the core advice of hitting instructors like Ted Williams ('get a good ball to hit') and Charley Lau ('tension is the enemy') echoes Zen Buddhist principles, walking through patience, relaxation, self-knowledge, visualization (Reggie Jackson, Willie Stargell, Barry Bonds's on-deck imagery), practice, Bruce Lee-style kime concentration, and mushin or no-mind. Mickey Mantle going 0-for-30 after over-thinking Ted Williams's hitting tips, and Tony Gwynn's 'see the ball and react,' show how conscious analysis interferes with the muscle memory a half-second fastball demands. If kendo is practiced in a dojo — a 'place of enlightenment' — he concludes, ballparks and batting cages may be dojos too, with the caveat that Cobb, Ruth, and Mantle hardly model egoless humility.

buddhism.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
buddhism.title: What’s Wrong with Generalization
buddhism.relation: Brannigan uses Japanese baseball to ask what is wrong with cultural generalization. He presents the Bushido case — samurai-style self-denial, absolute loyalty (Kawakami's Yomiuri Giants), Suisha Tobita's 'training of death,' resolve (konjo), team harmony (wa), and a relational self grounded in Buddhism's no-self and Confucian identity-through-relationships — then tests it against counter-evidence: Sadaharu Oh's flamingo swing owed as much to individual talent and Hiroshi Arakawa's unconventional kendo-and-aikido coaching as to sensei imitation, the 'new breed' (Ochiai, Egawa) flouts the old ways, and William Kelly's 'Whiting problem' warns against polarizing Japanese and American baseball. The chapter's 'three strikes' against the label 'Japanese baseball' conclude that generalizations become dangerous when treated as monolithic nets cast over an entire culture.

buddhism.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
buddhism.title: “A New Broom Sweeps Clean, but an Old Broom Knows Every Corner”
buddhism.relation: Callis interweaves a memoir of the teenage boyfriend who played her Dark Side and later killed himself with an account of Easy Star Records' 2003 reggae remake, Dub Side of the Moon, arguing that the album's themes of time, money, materialism, and madness translate naturally into Rasta reasoning. Nyabinghi drumming, singjay toasting, and bong-bubble effects re-read 'Money' (the cash register replaced by a lighter firing the chalice) and 'Time' (Ranking Joe's 'Time is the master') through Rasta rejection of Babylon, anti-capitalist subsistence, and 'soon come' patience, which she glosses with the Buddhist principle that things happen in their own time. The reggae setting, she concludes, weaves all this pain and madness, from Barrett's collapse to her own ghosts, into something more optimistic than the original ever sounded.

buddhism.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
buddhism.title: There is No Dark Side of the Moon Really. Matter of Fact It’s All Dark
buddhism.relation: Johnston reads The Dark Side of the Moon through Buber's I and Thou: modern life traps us in the I-It mode of experience, from 'Welcome to the Machine' to teachers who treat students as replaceable Its ('Hey, teacher, leave us kids alone!') and Horkheimer's instrumental reason that turns personnel into 'human resources,' while the album repeatedly calls us to the I-You encounter, from 'Echoes'' strangers whose glances meet ('I am you and what I see is me,' Waters's origin of empathy) to 'Breathe''s 'don't be afraid to care.' He links the opening heartbeat and the breath of 'Breathe' to Buber's eternal You, defends Buddhism against Buber's charge that enlightenment is worldless monologue (the Buddha becomes one with the world, a perfect reciprocity like the innate You of the womb), and accepts Nietzsche's point that the Enlightenment's abstract God is dead while insisting, with Buber, that encounter with the eternal You remains possible. The album itself, he concludes, resists degenerating into an It: even if 'the sun is eclipsed by the moon,' the light persists and Dark Side can be the antidote to the It-world.

buddhism.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
buddhism.title: Alchemic Heroism
buddhism.relation: Reads Edward and Alphonse Elric as a single composite 'alchemic hero' who fuses Japanese heroic archetypes: the dual-hero rooted in the Izanami-Izanagi creation myth and yin-yang complementarity (brash yang Ed, calm yin Al whose armored body actually fights better), the student hero forged by Izumi Curtis's brutal island training, and the wandering redemption seeker atoning for the forbidden attempt to resurrect their mother. It argues that the sacrifice built into this fusion — Al's lost senses, puberty, and body — mirrors Japan's own cultural alchemy of absorbing Buddhism, Confucianism, and yin-yang thought while retaining a coherent national identity.

buddhism.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
buddhism.title: Fighting Talk
buddhism.relation: The editors' introduction argues that philosophy and fighting have been companions since Socrates the soldier and Plato the wrestler (whose name means 'broad shouldered' from the gym), and that each can illuminate the other. It tours the volume through concrete cases: budo courtesy drawn from Shinto, Confucianism and Zen; the Shaolin monks' exercises as a route to Buddhahood; Western chivalry and Gordon Marino's boxing as educations in Aristotelian courage; fencing's egoism and value; and the Stoicism of karate and utilitarianism of Kano's judo. Philosophy clarifies fighting traditions, while fights supply puzzles for ethics, aesthetics, and the philosophy of mind.

buddhism.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
buddhism.title: What Monkey Should Have Known
buddhism.relation: Mortensen opens with Monkey from Journey to the West beating six robbers to death despite Tripitaka's protest, and asks whether a practitioner of budo can be a Buddhist. He defends three principles, Take No Life, No First Strike and Stop Before Harm, qualifying them via the Upaya-kausalya Sutra's sea captain, Funakoshi's 'there is no first strike in karate', Ueshiba's purely defensive aikido, the initiator's bad karma, and the exception of multiple attackers; then he applies them to weapons, arguing that wooden weapons (the jo, Musashi's bokken, above all the humble walking stick, the 'last legal weapon') fit the precepts where the katana does not. Monkey, in short, should have carried a stick.

buddhism.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
buddhism.title: All for Love
buddhism.relation: Jerry Piven argues Dexter's void is not genetic sociopathy but trauma: witnessing his mother's chainsaw murder and lying in her blood deadened his feelings, and each ritualized kill restages that catastrophe with the roles reversed, Dexter mastering death as the angel of it, reducing the murderer to a drop of blood he imprisons on a slide. Reading Harry's ghost as a Hamlet-father super-ego, he contends Dexter kills not only to master trauma but to please the father who channels his rage - murder 'for love' - and then generalizes: Arendt's banality of evil, Pascal on the void and faith, Kierkegaard and Heidegger on fleeing despair into conformity, Buddhist emptiness, and Becker-style terror-management findings explain how ordinary people, frightened of death and hungry for a leader's approval, can be manipulated into sanctioned slaughter, from Abu Ghraib to jihadism.

buddhism.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
buddhism.title: Halo as a Catalyst for a Buddhism Videogame
buddhism.relation: Luke Cuddy uses Halo 3 checkpoints and emulator save states—two mutually exclusive Flood-fight outcomes both in some sense true—to make David Lewis's possible worlds and modal truth concrete, with Leibniz as the doctrine's ancestor. Halo's infinite lives make players genuinely angry, and the chapter argues this is upaya territory: like the father in the Lotus Sutra's parable of the burning house, the game promises mastery (the goat-, deer-, and ox-carts) to lure players toward something greater outside it. Master Chief becomes a Bodhisattva whose avatar slides between extension of self and other, provoking the 'who am I?' crisis that reveals the ego as empty at the ultimate level of the Two-Fold Truth, while the Dalai Lama's enemies-as-teachers turns the seven-year-old who pwns you into practice in the first two Noble Truths' suffering and anger.

buddhism.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
buddhism.title: The Awakened One
buddhism.relation: Callis reads Holmes as a Buddhist practitioner despite the cocaine and the cigars in the coalscuttle: 'You see, but you do not observe' and 'The emotional qualities are antagonistic to clear reasoning' match Vipassana bare attention and the Theravada ideal of the cool, rational, emotionally distant sage, and his improvised violin scraping works like Thich Nhat Hanh's walking meditation — a witness without commentary. The picture is completed by Doyle's Buddhism of Ceylon in The Sign of Four, Holmes's two years 'spending some days with the head lama' in Tibet ('The Empty House'), and his sitting 'like some strange Buddha' in 'The Veiled Lodger.' She maps his method onto the Yoga Sutras' dharana, dhyana, and samadhi — patient attention to the blood-scratched plaster, sustained fixation on the crime scene, ego-surrendering contemplation — making Holmes an 'awakened one' who loves truth for its own sake while Watson lives on autopilot.

buddhism.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
buddhism.title: Do We Give Shakespeare the Last Word
buddhism.relation: Kapper reads Inception as epistemology rather than metaphysics - not what is real but how we could know - running from Plato's Theaetetus (the first dream-recognition question) through Descartes's deceptive demon and Freud's royal road to the unconscious, to Wittgenstein's point that 'I may be dreaming' is senseless because the remark itself would be dreamed, and Heraclitus's line that only the waking share a common world. The Ariadne thread is the clue: as in the Theseus myth, dream architecture gives the labyrinth a shareable narrative place, but only a hint, never a way to wake. He then goes east - Zhuangzi's butterfly, Indra's net of mutually reflecting jewels, Schopenhauer's universe dreamed by a single dreamer, William James's many consciousnesses - to ask how many times we must die before waking, ending with Buddhism: 'Buddha means awakened one', and Cobb's turning from the top enacts Nirvana, where the real-versus-dream question stops pertaining.

buddhism.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
buddhism.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
buddhism.relation: Liane Heller pairs Cohen and Schopenhauer - born and died on September 21st, the autumnal equinox - as two explorers of the world's irrational negativity who both retreat to 'a room' to create. Schopenhauer's directionless Will, his pessimism about a life of constant suffering, his notorious misogyny in 'On Women,' and his ascetic denial of the will-to-live (with his contempt for Judaism and preference for the Upanishads and Buddhist compassion) are set against Cohen's affirmation that love is 'the only engine of survival,' his five-year Zen retreat that could not hold him, and his return to the Judaism of the 'little Jew who wrote the Bible.' A closing imagined dialogue has a humbled Schopenhauer confronted with Cohen's self-compassion and ordinary joys, admitting the limits of his own field of vision.

buddhism.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
buddhism.title: 3. Tris Finds Enlightenment
buddhism.relation: Rhine argues that Tris's heroism rests on Buddhist practice: her breath-counting on the Ferris wheel and inside Four's fear landscape, her emotional intelligence, and her awareness of the parental 'voices in her head' are classic meditative disciplines for calming the ego whose clinging, on the Buddhist account, is the cause of suffering (dukkha). She reads Abnegation's gray houses, plain food, and four-times-a-year mirror as ritual ego-diminishment - a middle way between indulgence and the extreme asceticism the Buddha rejected - that explains why most Divergent arise from Abnegation. Contemporary neuroscience is then recruited: the amygdala-versus-prefrontal-cortex struggle Will describes, and monks' heightened gamma waves, explain how Tris can see the simulation as a simulation, like Neo in The Matrix, and act while others are paralyzed by fear.

buddhism.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
buddhism.title: 6. Bowie the Buddhist
buddhism.relation: Muchall reads 'Quicksand' and 'Where Are We Now?' as suffused with Tibetan Buddhism: 'Don't believe in yourself' voices the anatta teaching Bowie absorbed studying with Chime Rinpoche and from Chogyam Trungpa, whose 'spiritual materialism' warns that ego converts even spirituality and ideologies to its own use. After retelling the Buddha's life, the Four Noble Truths' three kinds of dukkha, and the five aggregates that reveal no permanent self, the chapter maps the song's 'ragged hole' and bardos onto the Tibetan Book of the Dead's after-death journey, and reads Bowie's morphing personas as lived acknowledgment that there is no fixed self - 'there's nothing in here.'

buddhism.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
buddhism.title: 13. The Origins of Self-Love
buddhism.relation: Anna Marie Fennell reads RuPaul's 'If you can't love yourself, how in the hell you gonna love somebody else?' through theories of self-love. Erich Fromm's four elements of love and Buddhist non-attachment (Jinkx Monsoon's 'water off a duck's back,' the Season Ten Inner Saboteur characters like Eureka's Eufilthior) ground the claim that self-love precedes healthy love for others. Against Aristophanes' myth in Plato's Symposium - the round beings split by Zeus, forever seeking their other half, retold in Hedwig and the Angry Inch - she sides with Ru: completion comes from within, not from a soulmate. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity (the sub-man and nihilist archetypes seen in self-sabotaging queens like Nina Bo'Nina Brown) and bell hooks's All About Love with Branden's six pillars of self-esteem map onto winners like Jinkx, Sharon Needles, Violet Chachki, and Bianca Del Rio, whose drag personas show existence preceding essence.

buddhism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
buddhism.title: Preface
buddhism.relation: Aaron Ehasz, ATLA's head writer, reflects that the show tested its characters' belief systems against their humanity: Aang's attempt to comfort himself with Buddhist detachment fails when Appa is taken, and he cannot let go of his love for Katara to unblock his final chakra and enter the Avatar State. Yet Uncle Iroh shows the opposite lesson, since by studying Water Tribe ideas he invents lightning redirection, the technique that lets Zuko survive his father and lets Team Avatar save the world. The preface concludes that philosophy both limits and unlocks human potential, capped with a joke about Hegel and hard ice cream.

buddhism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
buddhism.title: Introduction
buddhism.relation: De Cruz and De Smedt argue that ATLA subverts the Chosen One trope: Aang's training is slow and non-linear, he needs dedicated teachers, and saving the world is a team effort in which Katara leads and Sokka plans. The show's central theme is oneness, voiced by Guru Pathik's 'illusion of separation' ('The Guru') and Huu's banyan-grove tree ('The Swamp'), which the editors trace to Daoist, Huayan Buddhist (Fazang's golden lion), and Indigenous traditions of interdependence. They frame the volume's engagement with genocide, imperialism, ecological destruction, and Ba Sing Se's authoritarian denial as proof that philosophy is needed for human flourishing.

buddhism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
buddhism.title: The Wisdom of Combination
buddhism.relation: Isrow maps each bending art to its real martial art and source philosophy: Katara's Taiji waterbending embodies Daoist wu-wei when she forgoes revenge on Yon Rha ('The Southern Raiders'); Toph's Hong Jia earthbending expresses the Buddhist eightfold path's Right Speech through her insistence on truth; Zuko's Northern Shaolin firebending enacts the Four Noble Truths, his desire-driven suffering ending only when he abandons chasing the Avatar; and Aang's Daoist Baguazhang airbending makes freedom openness to change, shown in his receptivity to Iroh's advice. The Avatar's true power is combining these character strengths, not merely wielding four elements.

buddhism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
buddhism.title: What Can We Learn
buddhism.relation: Argues ATLA repeatedly dissolves false alternatives rather than solving conflicts, modeling the Buddha's middle way from the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta: refuse the two extremes instead of picking one. Earth is the case study — Bumi is both crazy and wise, Toph both blind and the most powerful bender, and 'The Cave of Two Lovers' shows the first earthbenders using their art for love, with Oma ending the feud by declaring the war over rather than destroying both villages. Aang's energybending against Ozai dissolves the kill-or-be-killed framework, Bumi's 'neutral jing' rejects fight-or-flight, and Toph's life refutes the capable-vs-helpless and girl-vs-fighter dichotomies her parents impose.

buddhism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
buddhism.title: Fearlessness and Power
buddhism.relation: Rebuts Ozai's taunt 'you are still weak' with a Buddhist reading of energybending: Aang wins not by domination but because his unbendable spirit is total vulnerability, a true heart that has abandoned the five hindrances (sensory desire, ill will, dullness, restlessness, doubt — each traced through the chakras, the Serpent's Pass, and 'Nightmares and Daydreams') and a true mind freed from the fundamental delusion of a separate self that 'The Swamp' and 'The Guru' dissolve. The spirit-merging with Ozai is read through Indra's net, and Aang's merciful halt mirrors Indra's Jataka victory where compassion for eagle hatchlings — not force — defeats the demons. Fearlessness, on Sylvia Boorstein's Zen story, is the natural corollary of compassion, so Aang's weakness by Ozai's standard is precisely his power.

buddhism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
buddhism.title: Journey’s End and a Vision of a New Community
buddhism.relation: Reads Aang's journey alongside the Karmapa Ogyen Trinley Dorje's Interconnected: both bear exalted titles that isolate them from friendship (Aang forbidden to play with peers and taken from Gyatso; Dorje taken from his family at seven), and both learn that heroism is relational — the series replaces the rugged-individual hero's quest with a communal model in which Katara, Sokka, Toph, Pakku, Jeong Jeong, and Zuko co-author Aang's moral training. Aang's refusal to open the seventh chakra over his attachment to Katara illustrates the Karmapa's warning that local attachment can block universal compassion, and Zuko's path from betrayal to forgiveness shows enemies as people enslaved to their own disturbing emotions. Aang ends as the Karmapa's 'interdependent individual', victorious only alongside the White Lotus and his friends.

buddhism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhism.title: Preface
buddhism.relation: Head writer Aaron Ehasz asks what philosophy is for in ATLA and answers with the writers' unconscious conclusion: characters' belief systems are always tested against their humanity, and Aang's Buddhist detachment fails him twice, once when he loses Appa and once when opening the final chakra demands he let go of Katara. The counterexample is Iroh, whose study of Water Tribe techniques lets a firebender invent lightning redirection, the skill that lets Zuko survive his father and lets the saga resolve. So philosophy is not crushed by human need but is the key that unlocks humanity's potential, provided we stay open to ideas from other cultures.

buddhism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhism.title: Introduction
buddhism.relation: The editors argue ATLA subverts the Chosen One trope: Aang learns slowly and non-linearly, needs a teacher for each element, stays weaker than Katara or Toph in specific skills, and saving the world is a team effort in which he is neither leader nor brains. They identify the show's unifying theme as oneness, the 'illusion of separation' voiced by Guru Pathik and the swampbender Huu, and trace it to East and South Asian schools such as Huayan and Chan Buddhism and to Indigenous traditions. Philosophy is presented as the tool the show itself uses against genocide, imperialism, and ecological destruction, with Ba Sing Se's 'no war' denial as the cautionary case.

buddhism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhism.title: Sometimes We Can Let Go
buddhism.relation: Sets the intuition that angry blame is how we hold people responsible (Strawson; Katara's useful fury at Pakku's sexism, Iroh's 'whatever you do to that spirit, I will unleash on you tenfold') against the Senecan and Buddhist verdict that anger is greedy for revenge, and reads ATLA as modeling ways to hold people responsible without toxic anger. In 'The Southern Raiders' Katara neither forgives Yon Rha nor kills him, showing that blame can be set down when expressing it is pointless, while she forgives Zuko in Lucy Allais's 'wiping the slate clean' sense because his past betrayal no longer speaks to his present character. Iroh's handling of the mugger in Ba Sing Se ('I was never angry; I was afraid that you had lost your way') models responding to the suffering behind wrongdoing with compassion instead of blame, and Zuko's self-anger is diagnosed as hypocritical self-blame whose antidote is self-compassion: acknowledging how he himself was hurt is what finally lets him take ownership of his wrongs.

buddhism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhism.title: Fearlessness and Power
buddhism.relation: Argues that Aang's energybending victory over Ozai vindicates a Buddhist conception of power against Ozai's equation of power with domination: the Lion Turtle's 'unbendable spirit' is not resistance but thorough vulnerability, achieved through the true heart (overcoming the five hindrances mapped onto Aang's sensory desire, ill will, dullness, restlessness, and doubt across the series) and the true mind (overcoming the fundamental delusion of a self separate from others, learned from Huu in 'The Swamp' and Guru Pathik). The merging of Aang's and Ozai's spirits is pictured by the metaphor of Indra's net, and Indra's own Jataka victory, halting his assault to protect eagle hatchlings and disorienting the demons, parallels Aang's refusal to win by killing. Drawing on a Zen story of the abbot who could 'be run through by a sword without batting an eye', the chapter concludes that Aang's fearlessness flows from compassion, so that weakness by Ozai's standard is precisely the power that defeats him.

buddhism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhism.title: Overcoming Dilemmas
buddhism.relation: Frames Aang's conflict between his Avataric duty to restore balance even by killing Ozai and his Air Nomad duty of ahimsa as a genuine dilemma only if both obligations are non-negotiable (Tessman's negotiable and non-negotiable duties), then argues the show resolves it because Sublime Ahimsic Practice, the Four Sublime States joined to non-harm, reshapes the very conditions the dilemma rests on. Aang's cultivation of loving-kindness and his grasp of dependent origination (Huu's banyan-grove insight that everything is interconnected) keep him open to the world, which is what leads him to the Lion Turtle; energybending then lets him stop Ozai without killing, dissolving the kill-or-be-killed framework rather than choosing a horn. The Avataric role itself is read as Daoist yin-yang balance-keeping, and the chapter links Aang's triumph to the lessons of Gandhi, Martin Luther King Jr., and nonviolent movements: becoming different people changes which options the world affords.

buddhism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
buddhism.title: Journey’s End and a Vision of a New Community
buddhism.relation: Reads Aang's quest through the Karmapa Ogyen Trinley Dorje's book Interconnected: like the seventeenth Karmapa, identified at age seven and taken from his family, Aang learns that an exalted title complicates friendship and that freedom is self-control rather than the rugged individualism of the American hero's quest. Training episodes (Katara's jealous competition in 'The Waterbending Scroll', Jeong Jeong's warnings, the Toph-versus-Katara sifu debate in 'Bitter Work') show moral training as communal, widening from Team Avatar as adoptive family toward universal compassion, with Aang's refusal to open the seventh chakra illustrating how local attachment can obstruct universal love. Zuko's counter-arc from competition, isolation, and betrayal to humility, forgiveness, and contentment shows compassion turning an enemy into a friend, and the finale's simultaneous battles (White Lotus liberating Ba Sing Se, Sokka and Toph destroying the fleet) affirm that Aang wins as an 'interdependent individual', never alone.

buddhism.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
buddhism.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
buddhism.relation: Lynch tests the fan claims that the Dude is 'the Duddha' or a practicing Daoist: the Dude has wu wei in his effortless arts of bowling and abiding and shares Zhuangzi's withdrawal from society (the Nixon bowling poster, learning from drunks, Donny's ashes scattered with naturalistic acceptance), but lacks Daoist metaphysics, the Dao's inexpressibility, and any articulated views. The Buddha parallels are real — nonattachment, practice over theory (the poisoned-arrow parable), compassion for Bunny — yet Gautama's radical discipline and middle path are the opposite of the Dude's laziness, so Dudeism emerges as an undisciplined American cousin, and the Dude follows 'just his way and his alone'.

buddhism.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
buddhism.title: a4.xhtml
buddhism.relation: Bronson argues that walking is a philosophical practice against modern placelessness (Giddens' 'phantasmagoric' locality): Thorin survived Smaug's attack because as a youth he 'was a good adventurous lad, always on the move', and Tolkien's wise figures - slow, flower-stopping Tolkien himself, Gandalf who 'went to look ahead' and was brought back 'by looking behind', Bilbo's silent walking, Beorn's bear-travels - all practice attentive movement through place. He backs this with Montaigne's retirement to his tower and bringing thoughts back to the orchard, Thoreau's woods-walking that must be spiritual as well as physical, the Tao Te Ching's 'good travelers leave no tracks' and Zhuangzi's wandering virtues, and Buddhist walking meditation from the Buddha's wandering monks to Thich Nhat Hanh's peace steps.

buddhism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
buddhism.title: Do We Give Shakespeare the Last Word
buddhism.relation: Kapper treats Inception as a hip epistemological puzzle — unlike The Matrix, the question is not what is real but how we could know — and follows Ariadne's thread (her mythological clue-giving names the chapter) through the tradition: Plato's Theaetetus and Descartes's supremely cunning deceiver pose 'Am I dreaming now?', Wittgenstein shows the doubt is senseless since 'if I am dreaming, this remark is being dreamed as well', Freud makes dreams the royal road to the unconscious, and Heraclitus says only the waking share a common cosmos. The payoff is Eastern: Zhuangzi's butterfly, Indra's net of mutually reflected jewels, and Schopenhauer's single-dreamer universe turn waking up into an endless regress, so the Buddhist ideal of the awakened one — nirvana, where the ideas of real and dream cease to pertain — becomes the reading of Cobb turning away from the top.

buddhism.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
buddhism.title: Notes
buddhism.relation: Kahn argues LEGO play embodies the Buddhist teaching of impermanence that the Buddha states in the Digha Nikaya ('Impermanent are all component things...'): his childhood urge to superglue creations and Finn's father's Kragle dramatize the clinging that produces anxiety when things change, from brick formulations to discontinued sets and even funerals' wilting flowers. The LEGO Star Wars Death Star illustrates non-self — no Death Star exists apart from its 3,803 pieces, and no self apart from shifting aggregates — and the five aggregates (form, sensation, perception, formations, consciousness) are unpacked through building experiences like discovering a daughter has opened the mint Taj Mahal set. Tibetan sand mandalas, painstakingly built then ritually dissolved, model the ceremonial demolition of LEGO creations, teaching acceptance of change without sliding into a nihilistic 'why bother building at all'.

buddhism.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
buddhism.title: Buddha ex Machina
buddhism.relation: Siobhan Lyons applies Mori's 'uncanny valley' to the hosts' physical and personality evolution (Ford's jerky old model versus seamless newer hosts, Maeve and Clementine), noting empathy grows as they near sentience. She argues via Aristotle's account of virtue, vice, and brutality that the guests and technicians (Logan's casual cruelty, the Man in Black's beastly sadism) fall short of human excellence while the suffering, consciousness-seeking hosts transcend it, treating humanity as a way of behaving rather than being, and casting the hosts as Derridean undecidables. Invoking Nietzsche on suffering as the cultivator of greatness and Mori's 'Buddha in the robot,' she claims the hosts earn a humanity the biological humans merely inherit.

buddhism.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
buddhism.title: Beat U-topos or Taking Utopia on the Road The Case of Jack Kerouac
buddhism.relation: Adamo argues Kerouac's 'On the Road' is a new kind of utopian text: because classical collective utopias (Plato's Republic through More) were judged by Berlin, Popper, and Arendt to slide into totalitarianism and to conflict with political liberalism's individualism, Kerouac relocates utopia from place to the individual life lived 'on the road' (u-topos = no-place). He reads Sal Paradise's disillusion with Dean Moriarty—who uses people up—versus his admiration for Mississippi Gene and the hobos as dramatizing J. S. Mill's harm principle, fused with the Buddhist vow to harm no living thing, radicalizing personal liberty as perpetual movement without injury to others.

buddhism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
buddhism.title: 25. Close Your Eyes, Breathe, and Stick It to the Man
buddhism.relation: Seth Walker presents the Buddha ('Sid', Noah Levine's 'original rebel') as a punk who abandoned palace privilege after seeing sickness, aging, and death, teaching the four noble truths as a revolt against craving, caste, and blind tradition - the five precepts become 'punk-cepts'. He links Buddhist practice to punk through Straight Edge abstinence (Minor Threat's X), Brad Warner's Hardcore Zen, and 'skillful means', arguing that an inner rebellion must accompany the outer one since drugs and mindless violence are poorly channeled revolt. The Situationist International's 'spectacle' of passive consumption and Socially Engaged Buddhism (ordaining trees against deforestation, Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation, grounded in the doctrine of non-self) show both traditions demanding permanent revolution and community.

buddhism.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
buddhism.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
buddhism.relation: James Whitehill treats sailing his Cape Cod catboat, named Garuda, as a Zen practice modeled on Zen archery (kyudo) and tea ceremony. He organizes it into 'outer work' (technique and ritualized performance) and 'inner work' (cultivating ki energy through breathing and belly-awareness, then 'self-forgetting'), quoting Dogen's dictum that studying the self is forgetting the self, and forgetting the self is being authenticated by all things. The goal is a boat-and-sailor unity in which the sailor 'sails without sailing' — reaching, through mundane repetitive discipline rather than a sought-after peak experience, a nirvana-like state where wind, wave, and self merge.

buddhism.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
buddhism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
buddhism.relation: Eric Swan argues that climbing embodies the principles and spirit of Zen, the experience of 'ordinary mind' finding the extraordinary in the ordinary and living fully in the present. Tracing Zen from the Buddha's Flower Sermon and Bodhidharma through Suzuki's 'Beginner's Mind' and Huineng's finger-and-moon, he maps Zen's four training paths—physical work, zazen (sitting meditation), koans, and interviews with masters—onto climbing: routes are like koans solved by insight and action rather than logic, 'being in the zone' is meditative absorption, and breath-regulation at the crux is zazen in motion. He holds up free soloist Derek Hersey, grinning hundreds of feet up Eldorado Canyon, and Chris Sharma, who writes of flowing 'like water' on the rock, as modern Zen masters who dissolve the separation between self, climb, and world.

buddhism.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
buddhism.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
buddhism.relation: Jennifer McMahon and Steve Csaki test Buddhist and Taoist parallels in the novel and find many only apparent. Tolkien's talking trees and ents anthropomorphize nature and grant it human-like consciousness, whereas Buddhism attributes sentience to all beings without projecting human consciousness, and Tolkien privileges domesticated over wild nature and stewardship over membership in nature. His master-student chain (Bilbo, Gandalf, Aragorn, 'Master Samwise') genuinely echoes the Zen necessity of the right master, as in Dogen's mushroom-cook mentor; but his good-versus-evil war, with light privileged over a personified dark power to be defeated, contradicts Taoism's yin-yang balance in which evil is imbalance, not a force to destroy.

buddhism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
buddhism.title: 42. Up in the Air as Philosophy Buddhism and the Middle Path
buddhism.relation: Duffy reads Ryan Bingham's arc in Up in the Air as a Zen Buddhist parable paralleling Hesse's Siddhartha. Ryan preaches an 'empty backpack' philosophy of nonattachment and treats the miles as their own point, but Duffy argues he only intellectually grasps the four noble truths — dukkha, its cause in attachment (tṛṣṇā), and the eightfold path — until his failed attachment to Alex and his mentorship of Natalie make him actually suffer. Like Siddhartha with his son, Ryan learns wisdom must be experienced, that the anattā (non-self) doctrine undercuts the identity he built on his job, and that the goal is not escaping the world but living the Middle Path within it, present to suffering rather than spinning silver linings.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
buddhist-impermanence.title: Unknown
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Brannigan reads the film's mirror imagery through the Buddha's mirror instruction to his son Rahula: Neo touching the dripping mirror and becoming the mirror marks his awakening to the naked truth (aletheia as nakedness) that his world is a programmed illusion, Smith's dark sunglasses distort while Morpheus's mirrored glasses clarify, and Neo's reflection in the spoon-bending boy's spoon signals clarity. 'There is no spoon' parallels the Zen mondo where neither flag nor wind moves but only mind, and shows that reflected images are not reality - the world is maya. The deepest lesson is anatman: just as there is no spoon there is no Neo, no fixed self, and Rahula's lesson grounds the interdependence (pratityasamutpada) of all actions on others.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
buddhist-impermanence.title: Mind the Mindfulness
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Reads The Meaning of Life as a sustained reductio of transcendentalism — the two-world metaphysics shared by Plato, Augustine, and Vedanta's Brahman/atman — arguing that the film's dehumanizing sketches (the machine that goes 'ping,' the 'every sperm is sacred' father selling his children, the Vegas-style Christmas in Heaven) show how otherworldly belief overrides this-worldly compassion. It parallels the Buddha's scriptural critiques: the Agganna sutta against caste, the no-self (anatta) doctrine against the Bhagavad Gita's soul that licenses Krishna to tell Arjuna killing is a favor, and impermanence (anicca) against the fantasy of eternal bliss. Python's grotesque — Creosote's explosion, the organ-donor lady's 'Galaxy Song' despair — matches Buddhist corpse meditations, while the film steers between hedonism (Creosote) and nihilism (the housewife who surrenders her liver) toward the Buddha's Middle Way and, against everyday distraction (the boardroom's 'people are not wearing enough hats,' the couple who think Schopenhauer begins with an S), toward mindfulness (sati).

buddhist-impermanence.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
buddhist-impermanence.title: “How Could Anyone Fall in Love with a Toaster ” Cylons as Persons
buddhist-impermanence.relation: James McRae reads Battlestar Galactica through Zen Buddhism: the fleet's sleepless FTL jumps in "33" and Roslin's dwindling survivor counts enact the four noble truths, Leoben's interrogation scenes teach that suffering comes from ignorant attachment, and Dogen's no-self and impermanence frame the show's interdependent characters. Cylon resurrection, D'Anna's serial deaths, and the prophecy that "all of this has happened before" model karma and samsara, while Nishida's kenotic God of Absolute Nothingness makes sense of Six and Leoben's God of love. Because Cylons feel pain, fear death away from a resurrection ship, and act volitionally, McRae concludes they are persons in the Buddhist sense, owed the compassion of the Eightfold Path.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
buddhist-impermanence.title: Analyzing Emptiness
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Paul Gass reads the Dead's hippie milieu (the Beats, the Acid Tests, Buddhist-monk lyricist Peter Monk) as a conduit for Buddhist doctrine, taking the 'Eyes of the World' chorus as an invitation to awaken to Buddha-nature. He explains the Four Noble Truths, karma, and the five aggregates to argue the self is an illusion, using the image of a flame passed between lighters at a Dead show to picture rebirth without a persisting soul. The chapter then presents Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka middle way — emptiness itself must not be clutched as an absolute truth — and reads the 'redeemer... wagon loaded with clay' verse of 'Eyes of the World' as the Mahayana bodhisattva liberating all beings, with emptiness finally discarded like the boat after crossing the river.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
buddhist-impermanence.title: The Awakened One
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Callis reads Holmes as a Buddhist practitioner despite the cocaine and the cigars in the coalscuttle: 'You see, but you do not observe' and 'The emotional qualities are antagonistic to clear reasoning' match Vipassana bare attention and the Theravada ideal of the cool, rational, emotionally distant sage, and his improvised violin scraping works like Thich Nhat Hanh's walking meditation — a witness without commentary. The picture is completed by Doyle's Buddhism of Ceylon in The Sign of Four, Holmes's two years 'spending some days with the head lama' in Tibet ('The Empty House'), and his sitting 'like some strange Buddha' in 'The Veiled Lodger.' She maps his method onto the Yoga Sutras' dharana, dhyana, and samadhi — patient attention to the blood-scratched plaster, sustained fixation on the crime scene, ego-surrendering contemplation — making Holmes an 'awakened one' who loves truth for its own sake while Watson lives on autopilot.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
buddhist-impermanence.title: 6. You’re Gonna Die
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Ethan Mills uses the Buddha and Epicurus to show that Louis meets death with laughter instead of fear. The Buddha's diagnosis of dukkha ('dissatisfactoriness') explains the Blu-Ray player and cellphone bits - consumer desire just restarts the craving cycle - and impermanence frames both the Amia heartbreak that Dr. Bigelow reframes as 'misery is wasted on the miserable' and Louie's 'life isn't that long... it's happy math' reflection, while rebirth would only make things worse since you would have to repeat junior high forever. Epicurus's argument that death is nothing to us (where death is, you are not) grounds Louie's 'lots of things happen after you die, just none of them include you,' backed by atomism - at death our atoms scatter - and by gods who, like Louie's maybe-God with no heaven, guarantee no immortality. The USO duckling episode models the payoff: comedy defuses our deepest anxiety about annihilation the way it defuses the soldiers' tension in Afghanistan.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
buddhist-impermanence.title: 23. I Fight Crime in My Sleep
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Staged as a Fight Club parody in which a Buddhist psychiatrist, Dr. Quinzel, evaluates a costumed narrator sent to Arkham, the chapter argues neither hero is close to awakening: Batman's crime-fighting is craving that perpetuates dukkha, his secret identities a twice-constructed self that the Buddha's no-self teaching dissolves, and his violence fails the test that 'hostility is never appeased by hostility.' Superman fares no better - his super-intellect imposes illusory order on impermanence, his flight and X-ray vision are distractions beside the Buddha-eye and tapas, and as one of the titans of the six realms he is further from Buddhahood than a human - while the doctor defines justice as karma rather than retaliation and finds Batman one step from American Psycho's Bateman. Only conquering Mara, one's own inner deceiver, is 'the only superpower worth having,' and the closing reveal that the doctor has a plan of her own for 'Mr. Kent' caps the diagnosis.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
buddhist-impermanence.title: 17. Dialog with the Buddha
buddhist-impermanence.relation: A Platonic-style fictional dialogue in which a newly enlightened "Canadian Buddha" walks out of the northern Ontario bush to the Prolethean farm and debates Tomas, Henry, and Bonnie over whether clones are abominations. Using karma, rebirth, the gandhabba that carries consciousness-flux to a new embryo, the no-soul doctrine, and the eightfold path, the Buddha argues clones are ordinary beings of the karmic flux — like the split bacterium, nothing unnatural — but that cloning multiplies clinging: hosts crave immortality through copies, each clone inherits the host's whole accumulated karma, and Henry's dream of training an army of Helena-clones would only deepen the unsatisfactoriness the Buddha's mustard-seed lesson says clinging to the dead always brings. Only ending the cycle through enlightenment releases anyone; the clone, like the lost child, is not the one you lost.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
buddhist-impermanence.title: 6. Bowie the Buddhist
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Muchall reads 'Quicksand' and 'Where Are We Now?' as suffused with Tibetan Buddhism: 'Don't believe in yourself' voices the anatta teaching Bowie absorbed studying with Chime Rinpoche and from Chogyam Trungpa, whose 'spiritual materialism' warns that ego converts even spirituality and ideologies to its own use. After retelling the Buddha's life, the Four Noble Truths' three kinds of dukkha, and the five aggregates that reveal no permanent self, the chapter maps the song's 'ragged hole' and bardos onto the Tibetan Book of the Dead's after-death journey, and reads Bowie's morphing personas as lived acknowledgment that there is no fixed self - 'there's nothing in here.'

buddhist-impermanence.book: 110 - Hamilton and Philosophy - Revolutionary Thinking
buddhist-impermanence.title: The Buddha’s Middle Way
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Reconstructs the Buddha's teaching as a Middle Way on three levels: socially between householder ritualism and renouncer asceticism, in monastic life between indulgence and austerities, and metaphysically between every permutation of existence and non-existence. It details the Enlightenment's three insights, the Four Noble Truths (dukkha better rendered 'unsatisfactoriness' grounded in the impermanence of all conditioned things), and dependent origination as the 'regularity of things'. Against the standard reading of anatta as 'there is no self', it argues the Buddha denied only independent existence and shifted inquiry from ontology to the workings of the cognitive apparatus (the five khandhas), citing his refusal to answer the Unanswered Questions. It also gives the Buddha's specific critiques of brahmin claims to authority, the purposelessness of ritual, and reliance on tradition over one's own experience. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
buddhist-impermanence.title: 2. Zen and the Art of Guitar Burning
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Argues Hendrix's art worked like a Zen transmission outside words and doctrine: Nansen's cat, the Buddha's silent flower sermon, Zeami's hidden flower in Noh, and Linji burning the sutras frame the guitar-burning, playing with his teeth, and the backwards tape of 'Are You Experienced?' as skillful means that shock listeners out of dualistic discrimination into pure suchness. The Woodstock sequence — the 'Star-Spangled Banner' followed seamlessly by 'Purple Haze' and the 'Instrumental Solo' — is read as an eschatological passage from the death-symbolism of the national anthem to a Zen-like experiential beginning, with Hendrix acting as a Bodhisattva whose Stratocaster is the master's stick of compassion.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
buddhist-impermanence.title: 11. 999 Fingers
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Voiced by a composite being shredded together from every AHS character, the chapter retells the Buddha's path - Siddhartha sheltered from suffering like a pampered prince, enlightenment as watching 'every episode of American Horror Story', Mara's temptations, and Angulimala with his garland of 999 fingers converted to monkhood - to read Briarcliff's cruelty, Sister Jude's devil, and Bloody Face's son Johnny as suffering born of clinging, in a contingent, moment-to-moment world of karma and rebirth, while Nietzsche's killed God, eternal recurrence, and ressentiment frame the question of who is to blame when there is no creator.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
buddhist-impermanence.title: 12. A Month from Now, I’ll Be a Balding, Toothless Skeleton
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Reads Fiona Goode's war against fading - the experimental RM47 serum, rejecting the Axeman's escape because he would watch her decay, the Papa Legba bargain that collapses because she has no soul - alongside Delphine LaLaurie's blood facials and Marie Laveau's child sacrifices, as illustrations of Buddhist dukkha and the three thirsts (kama for sense pleasure, bhava for existence, vibhava for annihilation). Legba's 'you don't have a soul' becomes an accidentally liberating glimpse of anatta, and Cordelia's dying advice - 'feel the fear... let it all go' - is the mindfulness, echoing Buddhaghosa's corpse meditations, that might have freed Fiona.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
buddhist-impermanence.title: 14. After the Blackout
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Martin Muchall treats the offscreen Blackout as an emblem of the moral catastrophe diagnosed in MacIntyre's After Virtue: our moral vocabulary has shattered into emotivist hissing and clapping, with Roy's murder of Tyrell, his 'God of biomechanics', staging the death of God and the 'everything is permitted' that follows. Utilitarian pleasure and Kantian cold reason (Spock, who must tell the truth to the murderer at the door) have both failed, leaving neoliberal hypercapitalism — corporate psychopathy, the orphanage sweatshop, the Baseline as workplace performance review — as the real villain. Against this, K's ending models the Buddha: everything is impermanent, there is no self to defend, and his selfless, empathetic death points to a morality grounded in evolved and cultivable altruism.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
buddhist-impermanence.title: Hakuna Matata, Bodhisattva
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Sets up Disney's maxim 'Hey kid, you can be a hero' as the direct opposite of Zen's 'Hey kid, you can be a buddha': escapism versus liberation, told through the life of Dogen, whose monastic choice parallels Disney hero narratives. Mickey in Steamboat Willie — a bundle of still frames with no sound and no real 'he' — illustrates the Buddha's three marks of existence (emptiness, impermanence, frustration), and the chapter argues Disney products are calibrated distractions from these marks while Dogen counsels facing them, with Ariel's Andersen fate as the price of fantasy. It closes on Disney's merchandising machine (Yoda, Star Wars sequels, direct-to-video cash grabs) as everything the countercultural minimalist Yoda or Baloo's bare necessities stand against, concluding that real hakuna matata is accepting impermanence rather than escaping it.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
buddhist-impermanence.title: Notes
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Kahn argues LEGO play embodies the Buddhist teaching of impermanence that the Buddha states in the Digha Nikaya ('Impermanent are all component things...'): his childhood urge to superglue creations and Finn's father's Kragle dramatize the clinging that produces anxiety when things change, from brick formulations to discontinued sets and even funerals' wilting flowers. The LEGO Star Wars Death Star illustrates non-self — no Death Star exists apart from its 3,803 pieces, and no self apart from shifting aggregates — and the five aggregates (form, sensation, perception, formations, consciousness) are unpacked through building experiences like discovering a daughter has opened the mint Taj Mahal set. Tibetan sand mandalas, painstakingly built then ritually dissolved, model the ceremonial demolition of LEGO creations, teaching acceptance of change without sliding into a nihilistic 'why bother building at all'.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
buddhist-impermanence.title: 23. I Fight Crime in My Sleep
buddhist-impermanence.relation: A Fight Club-style Arkham case study: a patient's hallucinated Superman companion is diagnosed by a Buddhist psychiatrist who explains the three marks of existence—impermanence, non-self, and dissatisfaction—arguing superheroes impose order and a fabricated second self on a world that resists both, so Superman's super-intellect and even flight are distractions (levitation should be ignored; the Buddha-eye beats x-ray vision) while Batman's violence and psychosis, compared to American Psycho's Patrick Bateman, make awakening impossible—both are victims of Mara. A robber literally named David Hume objects that the heroes' law and order is grounded on what ought to be rather than what is, and a Gandhi quote on preferring one's own bad government explains why Batman finally kryptonites his alien 'friend.' The verdict inverts the book's debate: conquering the deceiver within is the only superpower worth having.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
buddhist-impermanence.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
buddhist-impermanence.relation: Kang argues Lee's Taking Woodstock desexualizes and 'recloset[s]' Elliot Tiber's gay coming-out memoir, substituting a fluid 'queer' openness for Tiber's political gay identity and framing his homosexuality as an incidental, situationally-straight product of the festival (the woman-centered threesome, the chaste kiss with Paul). Drawing on Sedgwick, Butler and Foucault's history of sexuality, she critiques how the film neutralizes homophobia and omits the gay Buddhist mentor Georgette, whose teaching on karma, samsara and dukkha grounds Tiber's self-acceptance and unconditional love—reducing a gay everyman's struggle to one 'not-normal freak' among a hundred thousand.

buddhist-impermanence.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
buddhist-impermanence.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
