immortality.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
immortality.title: A Plausible View
immortality.relation: Reconstructs Slughorn's lesson to young Tom Riddle, that murder rips the soul and the torn piece can be hidden in a Horcrux, an act 'against nature', and argues that because Voldemort's intellect and magical powers remain intact while his capacity to charm gives way to rule by fear and his body becomes snake-like, Rowling's soul must be the sentimental one: our humanity, love, and moral conscience. On this view the soul is damaged by supreme evil and can be repaired only through remorse, which is exactly what Harry urges on Voldemort ('be a man... try for some remorse') before the final killing curse rebounds.

immortality.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
immortality.title: NOTES
immortality.relation: Steps outside the fiction to ask whether Rowling's hybrid soul theory is actually plausible, answering probably not: neuroscience shows no brain events lacking physical cause, mind-body interaction remains the classic obstacle for any dualism, and it is doubly implausible that an immaterial substance would be responsible only for our deepest emotions and conscience. The differing physical powers of ghosts, Resurrection Stone shades, and Horcrux-souls make the metaphysics even harder, though the chapter concedes that a fictional soul picture that vividly dramatizes what we care about needs no truth to make a terrific story.

immortality.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
immortality.title: The Integrity Objection
immortality.relation: Draws Voldemort's inversion in full: each Horcrux rips and destabilizes his soul (Hermione notes only excruciating remorse could reunite it, a pain that could destroy him), his attempt on baby Harry leaves him disembodied vapor parasitic on others' blood and limbs, in stark contrast to the feasting, affection, and romance of Harry's circle. The Godric's Hollow inscription 'the last enemy that shall be destroyed is death' and Hermione's claim that the soul survives whatever happens to the body ground the contrast between Voldemort's unmourned, mundane death and the honored, grieved dead - Dobby, Fred, Lupin, Tonks, Colin Creevey.

immortality.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
immortality.title: Reap a Destiny
immortality.relation: Reads the King's Cross limbo through Heidegger's counsel to choose a hero from the past and gain insight through dialogue with them: Dumbledore appears not as a king of that place but as the humble penitent, confessing his youthful hunger for glory, and the way-station evokes purgatory. The flayed child beneath the bench shows Voldemort's soul beyond repair - his fear of death drove the very choices that now give him reason to fear it - and Tolkien's remark that The Lord of the Rings is really about 'death and the desire for deathlessness' (Sauron pouring his life-force into the One Ring) frames the motif.

immortality.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
immortality.title: NOTES
immortality.relation: Argues via William James's 'sow a thought... reap a destiny' and Aristotle's account of how repeated action incrementally shapes the soul that Voldemort's flayed remnant is a character fully forged by choices, stuck with itself forever - a postmortem fate Heidegger's atheism cannot frame but Rowling's afterlife can. The section weighs Locke's memory-and-character account of identity, Kant's postulate that harmony of virtue and happiness requires an afterlife, and Pascal on why the immortality question must govern how we live, and ends asking whether Voldemort's evil is ignorance, as Plato held, or a cultivated appetite that only vice can satisfy.

immortality.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
immortality.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Gareth Matthews contrasts Plato's serene Phaedo — Socrates conducting a seminar on immortality, death as the cure for life's ills, 'we owe a cock to Asclepius' — with Gibson's prolonged torture, while noting deep parallels: both men were condemned by large courts on religious charges (impiety, blasphemy) with political subtexts. Socrates in the Apology models facing death through Socratic ignorance ('to fear death is to think oneself wise when one is not'), and Matthews argues Gibson's magnified suffering makes Christ an icon of an atonement nobody could imitate rather than a model for our own deaths; only the Gethsemane prayer and 'why hast thou forsaken me' (read via Cullmann) can actually help a believer face dying.

immortality.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
immortality.title: In It for the Long Run
immortality.relation: Adds Reason Five — being moral always pays in the long run, where the long run includes life after death — arguing that a perfectly good and all-powerful God would not set up a moral order that penalizes virtue, so Peter Parker's virtue is guaranteed its reward beyond this life. It notes that Eastern reincarnation-plus-karma makes the same promise (the more virtuous this life, the better the next), and that since Peter, Uncle Ben and Aunt May would never water morality down, the morally serious are pushed toward these metaphysical guarantees.

immortality.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
immortality.title: Chapter 16 - Superman and Kingdom Come The Surprise of Philosophical Theology
immortality.relation: Opens the philosophical-theology chapter by mapping Superman onto Christ: Kal-El sent by his father Jor-El from dying Krypton in a rocket parallels Jesus sent by the Father to Bethlehem, both alien saviors raised as small-town boys. It announces eschatology — final things, ultimate outcomes, whether the hope for justice is an empty utopian dream — as the lens through which the graphic novel Kingdom Come will be read.

immortality.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
immortality.title: Hope, Obligation, and the Big Picture
immortality.relation: Argues whether Wonder Woman's "must" really binds Superman — whether he is obliged to leave the Fortress and fight again — depends on one's eschatology or big-picture worldview. It contrasts Christian theism's purposeful culmination with naturalism, whose outlook is fixed by Bertrand Russell's "unyielding despair" passage: accidental collocations of atoms, no preservation beyond the grave, and all human achievement buried beneath the debris of a ruined universe, heroism included.

immortality.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
immortality.title: Gloom, Doom, and Morality
immortality.relation: Works out naturalism's moral cost: no purpose behind our existence, no blueprint for life, Russell's hope that sensitive souls can love the tragic beauty of it anyway, and the Wilson-Ruse claim that ethics is "an illusion fobbed off on us by our genes," which loses its grip once seen through — like Macbeth's dagger. Against this it sets Kant's moral faith: morality makes rational sense only if we postulate God and immortality so virtue is finally rewarded, and the chapter concludes naturalism offers no deep basis for the life-risking duties a hero like Superman faces.

immortality.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
immortality.title: A Theological Basis for Super-Heroics
immortality.relation: Proposes that Christian theism's doctrines of heaven, hell and Christ's return resolve the truth/justice tension by grounding moral obligation in God's perfectly moral nature and guaranteeing that justice prevails. It rebuts Maggin's claim that faith in a power greater than ours breeds inaction: God works through human co-creators, so Superman still has a duty to do what he can, and the objective hope of ultimate justice is exactly the corrective that despairing Superman and tyrannical, fear-ruling Batman in Kingdom Come both lack.

immortality.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
immortality.title: Hope and the Human Challenge
immortality.relation: Reads Superman's return — "Up in the sky!", the crowd hailing "the second coming of Superman" at the UN — as the enacted theology of Kingdom Come: hope in a greater power revives a world "hungry for hope" and draws the other heroes back to the fray. The Spectre's charge to the preacher Norman McCay, "you exist to give hope," voices the chapter's conclusion that a supernatural eschatology holds hope, truth, and individual responsibility together in a way naturalism's unyielding despair cannot.

immortality.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
immortality.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Observes that only Talking Animals enter Aslan's country when Narnia ends in The Last Battle, then critically examines Lewis's case against wider animal salvation: derivative immortality through human love (Sarah Smith's train of beasts in The Great Divorce), compensation of animal pain in an afterlife, Lewis's follow-Descartes claim that most animals are sentient but not conscious enough to feel pain or have a surviving 'self'. The chapter argues each point fails: the physiological evidence shows animals suffer, resurrection or God-given souls remain possible (Strawberry's transformation into a winged Talking horse), and a compensatory hereafter is still the most promising answer to why a loving God permits the fawn's miserable death. Aquinas's rational-creature hierarchy frames the Talking/Dumb divide, and the Hindu-Buddhist rebirth theodicy is considered and rejected as unbiblical.

immortality.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
immortality.title: Look Up, Look Up
immortality.relation: James Spiegel reads Dylan's God-haunted songwriting through philosophy of religion, sorting strong Augustinian-Aquinian providence ("Every Grain of Sand," "When He Returns") from the weak, risk-taking God of "Highway 61 Revisited" and "Joey." Dylan's moral judgmentalism combined with theological determinism makes him a compatibilist in Augustine's mold, while "Disease of Conceit" and "Pressing On" ("it run in my vein") press the compatibilist puzzle that Plantinga's libertarian power of contrary choice is meant to solve. Original sin becomes the "disease of conceit," and Socrates' Phaedo plus Kant's three postulates - God, freedom, immortality - ground Dylan's hope that "death is not the end," closing with Love and Theft's "Look up, look up."

immortality.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
immortality.title: Deserving to Be a Vampire
immortality.relation: Ted Preston asks whether becoming a vampire would be morally good or desirable, working through Forever Knight's Nick draining his lover, Blade feeding on stored blood, and The Lost Boys' promise that Michael will 'never grow old'. He argues vampires are not evil by nature: if they cannot control their hunger they are pitied rather than blamed (though we remain Aristotle-responsible for choosing to become addicted), and consensual, non-lethal feeding is no worse than mortals eating animals, since the bite only becomes murder by choice. Against Epicurus's claim that death is nothing to us, he uses Furley and Nussbaum's deprivation view - death vindictively empties our long-term projects like marriage or a career - so vampiric immortality genuinely preserves value, while the standard boredom objection fails because there are repeatable pleasures in a changing world. The thought experiment ends as moral psychology for mortals: since neither of us will become a vampire, live a life that would be worthy of eternity.

immortality.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
immortality.title: Oh Yes, There Will Be Blood
immortality.relation: Rachel Robison asks why blood, of all substances, carries metaphysical powers in vampire lore - Elizabeth Bathory's youth-giving baths, Dracula's control over Mina once she drinks his blood, Sookie's bond with Bill in True Blood. Her explanation is historical: the ancient cardiocentric view (Aristotle, Empedocles, Chrysippus placing the rational center in the heart and making blood its product) plus Galenic humorism and bloodletting made blood the carrier of the self, so drinking someone's blood plausibly transmits bits of their personal identity, knowledge, and even domination over one's free will. She then tests the show's synthetic 'True Blood': either some essential property of blood (or of the act of drinking it) carries the power, or the legend is parasitic on our lingering habit of locating emotion and character in the heart ('hot blooded') - either way the myth stays credible because our metaphors of blood never died.

immortality.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
immortality.title: “They Have a Plan”
immortality.relation: Robert Sharp reads the Cylon uprising in Battlestar Galactica as Nietzsche's slave revolt in morality: enslaved by humans, the Cylons react with resentment and overturn their masters' values, just as early Christians did under Rome. The humans keep a master morality (Colonial polytheism, warrior elites, call signs like Apollo and Athena), while Cylon monotheism, doctrines of the soul (Leoben's sermons to Starbuck, Gina's suicidal faith), equality, and consensus government reproduce slave morality's move from bodily weakness to spiritual superiority. The New Caprica occupation debate among the Cavils, Six, and Boomer, and D'Anna's boxing, show the former slaves seeking not just destruction but conversion of their masters to a religion that makes Cylons equal.

immortality.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
immortality.title: Reap a Destiny
immortality.relation: Jonathan and Jerry Walls read Deathly Hallows philosophically: Harry's willing march into the Forbidden Forest is Heideggerian authenticity, confronting being-toward-death, while Voldemort's horcruxes and the maimed King's Cross stowaway are the inauthentic flight from mortality that ruins the soul. The afterlife scene raises the stakes of this life: by James's "sow a thought... reap a destiny," Aristotle's habituation, and Locke's memory-based identity, Voldemort's lifelong refusal of remorse fixes his character beyond repair, and Kant and Pascal supply reasons why belief in an afterlife transforms morality. Dumbledore's purgatory-like repentance, contrasted with Voldemort's fate, shows that our choices reap a destiny we must live with forever.

immortality.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
immortality.title: Encore
immortality.relation: Randall Auxier adopts 'I trust Phil' — Phil Lesh the bass player who hears the whole sound — as his epistemic principle for asking whether death is to be dreaded, staging the essay around interview riffs with Deadheads Dale, Robbie, and Cory. Socrates in the Phaedo and the Buddha's Four Noble Truths converge on welcoming death — samsara is the 'Samsonite Scenario', bad luggage your own wishing keeps repacking — while Hume's Dialogues make God's power, goodness, and evil an inconsistent triad, so immortality is 'not that cool'. Kant's postulates (God, freedom, immortality) and categorical imperative prove too rule-bound for creative life; Whitehead's self-creativity and 'objective immortality of the past' supply the real bass line: even God cannot unmake what you have played, and the properly Grateful response is gratitude for the chance to add your riff to the Acid Test.

immortality.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
immortality.title: I’ll Get Up and Fly Away
immortality.relation: Ian Duckles and Eric Rubenstein use the community's losses of Pigpen and Jerry Garcia to ask whether death is bad, running Epicurus's argument that being dead is no experience and hence no harm, the tedium-of-immortality argument that eternal life would eventually exhaust every fundamental desire, and Socrates's Phaedo claim that death frees the soul to philosophize — which disturbingly implies Pigpen's early 'burn out' was the better fate. Their resolution is Heidegger: authentically confronting death as the end of all possibilities strips socially imposed values (consumerist 'keeping up with the Joneses') and frees us to create our own projects, so mortality itself is something to be grateful for. On this reading the Deadhead counterculture — rejecting 1950s suburban scripts for free love, psychedelics, and life on tour — lived Heideggerian authenticity, and it is better to fade away (like Garcia) than to burn out (like Pigpen).

immortality.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
immortality.title: Memories Are Made of This
immortality.relation: Randall Jensen asks whether Cash's hope of reunion with the dead ('Meet Me in Heaven,' 'If We Never Meet Again This Side of Heaven') is even coherent, using the 'One Piece at a Time' Cadillac and a hypothetical 1954 Plymouth to retell the Ship of Theseus puzzle about identity through part replacement. He canvasses Platonic dualism from the Phaedo (Cash is his soul, the body a rusty cage), the materialist hope that God can reassemble a resurrected body despite dispersed matter, and the psychological-continuity view that persons are 'made of memories,' ending on the duplication problem: if God made two heavenly bodies both carrying Cash's memories, which one would be Cash?

immortality.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
immortality.title: Into the Future
immortality.relation: Hanley dismantles the four claimed human/Cylon differences: artificial reproduction is in principle possible for us; prosthetics already blur what we are made of; model copies differ like identical twins (Boomer is not Athena); and resurrection has human analogues — he proposes an SDTR (scanning, death, transmission, replication) model and uses van Inwagen's replica-switch account of bodily resurrection while rejecting soul-based reincarnation on Lockean grounds, since consciousness rather than soul is the criterion of identity. He defends reproductive cloning as reproduction, not replication (a clone is your child, not your copy), and reads Athena's memories of Tyrol as evidence she is a replicated Boomer. The upshot: being a Cylon is nothing to fear — 'I am a Cylon, and so are you.'

immortality.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
immortality.title: Embracing Death
immortality.relation: David Vessey argues the humanoid Cylons' resurrection denies them the 'successful death' that makes a life meaningful: like Greek heroes governed by moira or Socrates drinking the hemlock, mortals must be able to see life as a completed whole that death can crown, with how one lived shaping what death means. Cylon deaths (dying out of range of a resurrection ship, D'Anna being boxed) are always failures or shames, and their religion carries no after-death stakes, unlike Socrates' philosophical preparation for death. Camus's Sisyphus shows agency and the option of suicide remain necessary for meaning, while Plato's Symposium model of immortality through children is the only one left to the Cylons, via mortal human-Cylon babies like Hera.

immortality.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
immortality.title: Game Over
immortality.relation: Janssen argues Zelda is quietly obsessed with death: turning the console off models death as pure absence of experience, which we cannot otherwise comprehend, and gives the gamer a comforting structured formula in place of a chaotic universe. Link, resurrected endlessly to serve the player, is condemned to Hegelian purgatory and what Bernard Williams called the tedium of immortality, while dungeon bosses, who die once and stay dead, are the only genuinely mortal, hence most human, beings in Hyrule. The Wind Waker prologue's eternally returning Hero does suggest Plato-style dualism with an immortal soul, but the chapter notes that Nietzsche's assault on faith destroyed dualism's credibility, leaving the series as a vessel for both materialist nothingness and romantic reincarnation.

immortality.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
immortality.title: Transformers and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Eyestone argues Transformers are genuinely alive with souls by applying Aristotle's De Anima: self-motion, perception, and intellect fit Ratchet (who tells Buster 'I'm a machine, and I hear you!'), and even the troublesome nutritive faculty is secured, since Energon ingestion, agelessness, and building each other suit naturally immortal, semimortal beings whose reproduction resembles Primus's creation. He extends arete to machines - Megatron has the excellence of a military leader but not of a person, while Optimus's chosen, trained goodness (Grimlock's 'Autobot training,' the Aerialbots' decision in 'War Dawn') makes him virtuous - and answers his title question 'why not?', since Aristotle's mortal soul gives Transformers no worse a shot at heaven than we have.

immortality.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
immortality.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
immortality.relation: The editors' introduction argues that His Dark Materials is philosophy-rich rather than a mere children's fantasy: its metaphysics of parallel worlds, dæmons, angels, armored bears, and mulefa poses genuine epistemic questions and ethical dilemmas. It frames the volume around the controversy over whether exposing children to Pullman's anti-religious vision is spiritual violence or an education in thinking for oneself like Lyra. It also sets up the trilogy's alternative afterlife, where Lyra frees the dead from the drab land of the dead to dissolve into Dust, and flags dæmons as puzzles of personal identity and soul-body interaction.

immortality.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
immortality.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Harris and Baer use the Boatman scene ('Pan is me... we'd die') to test criteria of personal identity against the trilogy: Lyra and Will's inference to a thinking third part, the ghost, reenacts Descartes's dualist reasoning about mind-body distinctness, Iorek's lack of a ghost exemplifies the same-body criterion, and Pantalaimon's instant shape-shifting favors the psychological criterion, spelled out through Locke's prince-and-cobbler memory thought experiment and Parfit's psychological connectedness and continuity. They ask whether Lee Scoresby's dissolution into conscious atoms that reunite with Hester's counts as genuine survival, best accommodated by Locke's consciousness criterion or a panpsychist matter criterion, with Chalmers cited as the contemporary defender of conscious matter. The chapter closes with individuation, whether Lyra and Pan are one person or two, applied to a Primal Fear-style multiple-personality murder trial, the hypothetical of Pan killing someone while Lyra is innocent, and living wills in persistent vegetative states.

immortality.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
immortality.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Greene applies the philosophy of death to Pullman's worlds, starting from the Epicurean puzzle that death is bad only if experienced, so it cannot be bad, plus the asymmetry puzzle about prenatal non-existence, then testing the Deprivation View (Father Gomez's bullet would rob Lyra of Oxford, the alethiometer, and love) and the Desire-Frustration View (Iorek's frustrated desires) against a universe whose dead do persist as ghosts. The world of the dead, with its harpies, eternal boredom, and the pain of leaving Pan with the Boatman, seems to refute Epicurus by making death a miserable experience after all. But the twist reframes everything: the dead who stream through Will's knife-hole to dissolve into Dust are choosing death over the afterlife, and since for them the good things of life are already off the table, death is not bad at all, which is exactly why they choose it.

immortality.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
immortality.title: I Ain’t Gonna Tell You One Thing that You Really Ought to Know . . . Ooh!
immortality.relation: Scott Calef reads the black 'Object' on the Presence cover—which Storm Thorgerson calls not a presence but a hole—to argue that absence permeates Zep's album art (the cut-out wheel of III, the die-cut windows of Physical Graffiti, the spindle holes of Coda) and that holes are a genuine metaphysical puzzle: immaterial yet extended, seemingly causal, and hard to see on a causal theory of perception. Descartes's immaterial soul is compared to holes (both non-physical, though holes suspiciously have size and location), Plato's Forms explain how the Object and we ourselves partake of both Being and Non-Being, and Hume's failure to find a self in introspection makes the self 'a hole'. Kierkegaard and Heidegger connect nothingness to the anxiety of death—fitting an album made after Plant's near-fatal crash—Socrates's two alternatives about death frame the end, and Wittgenstein's 'not a something but not a nothing either' caps the Object's dual nature.

immortality.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
immortality.title: Deserving to Be a Vampire
immortality.relation: Ted Preston asks whether becoming a vampire would be morally good or desirable, working through The Lost Boys, Underworld, Blade, Forever Knight, and Interview with the Vampire. He argues vampirism is not intrinsically immoral: if vampires cannot restrain their feeding we pity rather than blame them, though with Aristotle we still hold people responsible for choosing to become the kind of being that cannot; and feeding need be no worse than mortal carnivory, since consensual feeding (Blade's stored blood, Karen Jenson's donation, Madeleine's offer to Louis) makes the bite more like dentistry with consent than assault. On desirability he weighs Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' against the Furley-Nussbaum claim that death deprives a life of its long-term projects and relationships, concluding immortality's appeal is rational and that boredom is not inevitable in a changing world. The thought experiment ends in ethics: vampire or mortal, a life's worth depends on choices, so live a life worthy of eternity.

immortality.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
immortality.title: Oh Yes, There Will Be Blood
immortality.relation: Rachel Robison asks why mythology — from Elizabeth Bathory's blood baths to Dracula's control over Mina once she drinks his blood, and True Blood's Sookie sensing and desiring Bill and then Eric — credits blood with immortality, youth, erotic compulsion, and shared knowledge, including the vampire's dark inversion of the Eucharist. Her answer runs through the history of philosophy and medicine: Aristotle, Empedocles, and Chrysippus located rationality in the heart and made blood its product, while Galen's humoral theory and bloodletting treated blood as the carrier of health, temperament, and identity — so blood naturally reads as the vehicle of personal identity, free will, and even knowledge, explaining how drinking it could transmit a maker's self to Sookie or Mina. She then asks whether the synthetic 'True Blood' of HBO's show could carry the same powers, concluding it works only if some property is shared with real blood or if the power attaches to the act of drinking what is taken as blood.

immortality.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
immortality.title: Here They Are ... Ready to Outsit Eternity
immortality.relation: Argues that regeneration helps show life after death is logically possible: the successive Doctors (Fourth to Fifth in 'Logopolis') prove identity survives radical personality change, so a perfected heavenly Joe would still be Joe. Testing whether identity lies in body or memory, he contrasts John Smith in 'Human Nature' (same body, so same person) with the 'Journey's End' Doctor-clone whose replicated memories Rose rejects ('But he's not you'), favoring bodily continuity. This leaves the unavailability-of-atoms problem, which he solves with van Inwagen's theory that God removes and preserves our bodies at death like a divine cryonicist, echoing the Fourth Doctor's 'ready to outsit eternity' tribute in 'The Ark in Space'.

immortality.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
immortality.title: Gotta Have Soul
immortality.relation: The chapter tests a Soul Continuity Rule: the wub and Hauser survive because their souls do, though Locke himself denies the soul is the person, and Leibniz's King-of-China bargain, become the richest man if you forget everything, shows why, since it would amount to being annihilated while a King of China is created in your place. Kant's case of one mental life relayed across a chain of souls yields just one person, and the rule's practical failure is evidential: nothing could tell one soul with swapped psyches from swapped souls in the same body.

immortality.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
immortality.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Priebe builds a tongue-in-cheek 'Chuckism,' showing that Klosterman's books accidentally supply every element of a religion's formula: a bearded dude-deity, scripture, interpretive community, rules, and an afterlife (heaven as an always-neon Las Vegas, earthly life as purgatory sized by SIDS and 102-year-olds, plus a theory of reincarnation). Her ten commandments — thou shalt rock, swear, name-drop, be illogical, use footnotes — are mined from his actual writing style and its deliberate bad syllogisms. Under the blasphemy sits a serious claim: religion's structure is arbitrary and its orthodoxy enforceable, while Chuck's creed that 'living is dying, little by little' and 'life is tourism' answers the meaning-of-life question the older faiths evade.

immortality.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
immortality.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Archibald reads Gillian through Plato's Phaedo. The Argument of Opposites - cyclical deaths and rebirths that the immortal soul survives - maps onto the rape at thirteen that killed the child pageant girl and birthed a survivor, her shift into caretaker to control the stroked-out Commodore, and her final drugged regression before Nucky ('Nucky he did something very bad to me'). The Theory of Forms explains her treatment of roles as interchangeable: Jimmy is son, lover, and husband-Form rather than a person to mourn, Angela's death is merely an opportunity for rebirth, and the Jimmy-lookalike Roger can be dressed with his dog tags as 'James' - Forms changing shape while remaining, to Gillian, undamaged.

immortality.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
immortality.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Hess asks whether the monster has a soul and makes him the test case between physicalism (Kim, Churchland, van Inwagen) and dualism: recasting Frank Jackson's Mary as a color-blind monster who learns every physical fact about color vision, receives new eyes on Walton's ship, and then learns the 'what it is like' of seeing red for the first time, he argues there are nonphysical mental facts, so physicalism is false. He then runs Plantinga's argument that we are not our bodies or brains through a machine that replaces the monster's parts and hemispheres one by one while he stays conscious, and adds near-death out-of-body evidence like Maria's window-ledge shoe to suggest we can exist disembodied. The upshot is symmetric: whatever we conclude about the monster's soul we must conclude about our own - so be careful about assuming who does and does not have a soul, even monsters.

immortality.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
immortality.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Michaud and Watkins blame Crichton and Malcolm for frightening us away from science, arguing that most life does not 'find a way' and that science is the shield keeping vulnerable humanity a step ahead of extinction by meteors, plagues, and predators. They take up Rousseau's anti-Enlightenment longing to return to nature and reject it, arguing that humility comes from science itself (a 13.72-billion-year-old Earth, Sagan's 'star stuff' making us the universe become conscious of itself), not from abandoning it. Hammond, not science, embodies the real arrogance: he was so certain he could not fail that he tested the park on his own grandchildren.

immortality.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
immortality.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Nicolas Michaud argues that when you go extinct you do not come back, dismantling our three hopes: the soul, cloning, and an essential self. Cloning a T. rex yields a new individual 'Rex' with her own perspective, not the original; the soul cannot both be beyond science's reach and record memories and move bodies; and he deploys Gilbert Ryle's view that 'soul' is a language mistake - a mind is just what a functioning brain does, the way 'Jurassic Park' is just buildings, dinosaurs, staff, and money working together, ceasing when the functioning stops. A Hammond stripped by Alzheimer's and atom-replacement of every memory, trait, and particle still gets called John Hammond, so there is no essence over time: we already die constantly and never notice, which is why a second extinction holds no fresh terror.

immortality.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
immortality.title: The Devil and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Robert Arp's introduction opens with Halloween culture and his own seminarian past to ask whether belief in the Devil can survive scrutiny. He lays out a 'just deserts' argument - Hitler, Stalin, and Mao died unpunished while Job, Socrates, and Thomas More died unrewarded, so God, the Devil, Heaven, and Hell must exist to balance the scales - and then answers it with Freud's projection critique (religion as wishful thinking for comfort and moral control) and with the neuroscience tying the mind to a dying brain, which undermines the soul that Hell would punish. The chapter frames the whole book's project: testing devil-belief with arguments and evidence rather than taking it on authority.

immortality.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
immortality.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Timothy P. Jackson argues Cohen is the closest thing today to a Biblical prophet - a 'strong poet' in Harold Bloom's sense, wearing a coat of many colors drawn from Judaism, Christianity, Buddhism, Taoism, and Sufism, sustained by an 'epistemic humility' that lives between dogmatism and doubt. Cohen leads Christian texts back to their Hebraic origins, critiques every arrogant nationalism including Israel (Book of Mercy, psalm 27), and gave his Tel Aviv concert profits to Israeli-Palestinian reconciliation. Jackson reads Cohen's equanimity at his business manager's embezzlement trial as forgiveness overcoming resentment, weighs his hesed/agape-style unconditional love against his failures in erotic love, and ends with Cohen's reticence about personal immortality - a prophet for the living.

immortality.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
immortality.title: Dracula and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Mahon argues that vampiric immortality is a curse not because it brings decrepitude (against Swift's Struldbruggs model, since Dracula and his brides keep eternal youth) but because intelligent vampires know endless boredom awaits: following Bernard Williams and Shelly Kagan, boredom replaces death as the inevitable evil, giving vampires a Heideggerian 'being-toward-undeath' and 'being-toward-endless-pain'. Dracula's risky move from castle, brides, and slaves in Transylvania to London is read as the boredom escape it is, and since vampires still resist destruction, Mahon weighs the tedium curse against the alternative curse of compelled psychopathic bloodlust, concluding that staking Dracula is involuntary euthanasia - a mercy killing.

immortality.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
immortality.title: Dracula and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Ketcham's invented chronicle sends Dracula and a village rabbi to 1194 Cairo to interrogate Maimonides: can resurrection - one of the thirteen principles of faith - apply to a soulless undead being, and is his blood-drinking a divinely imposed penance? Maimonides answers from the Guide for the Perplexed and the Letter on Resurrection, offering that intelligence is the essence of the soul yet judging the Count a likely trickster, while Dracula presses that no scientific evidence of dust becoming flesh exists. The diarist closes with the heretical worry that Maimonidean resurrection - no food, drink, or sex - might itself be a kind of undeath.

immortality.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
immortality.title: 17. The Miracle of True Love
immortality.relation: Elsby and Luzecky use the Phaedo to make sense of Westley being 'mostly dead': Socrates's cyclical argument that opposites generate each other, Aristotle's distinctions between contradictories and contraries, and the observation that life and death here come in degrees together recast life and death as spectrum concepts rather than strict opposites. True love emerges as a second opposite of death: answering Simmias's objection that a soul, like a lyre's harmony, perishes with its instrument, they argue true love is a harmony binding persons and actions that persists beyond the particular lovers - which is how the film's miracle of true love conquers death.

immortality.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
immortality.title: 10. Gods Are Overrated
immortality.relation: Michaud grants that Superman is godlike and turns Hume's problem of evil on him: if Superman is all-powerful, all-knowing, and good, why does suffering persist that he could prevent at super-speed - the desert animal dying painfully for no purpose, the crimes that happen while he picnics with Lois - and the free-will defense and "it's all part of the plan" excuses fail him even worse than they fail God. Superman then becomes our excuse for doing nothing, and like belief in immortality and the afterlife (holy wars where no one "really" dies, prayers instead of feeding the starving) he dulls our sense that this life is all we get. Reading Nietzsche's "God is dead" as the discovery that we keep gods only to feel special and saved, Michaud concludes we would live more meaningful, Batman-like self-reliant lives if the savior-Superman were dead to us.

immortality.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
immortality.title: 22. Cocking a Snook at Death, and Getting Away with It Does the Personification of Death Make It Less Scary
immortality.relation: Asking whether Pratchett's personified Death makes mortality less scary, the chapter reads Reaper Man's claim that belief created Death—the moment a living thing grasped non-existence, Death came into being—as a co-arising of dualistic concepts, and surveys psychopomps from Thanatos and Azrael to Yama and even modern assisted-dying organizations. Windle Poons's several kinds of death in Reaper Man ground the distinctions between animalistic, mindistic, and personistic death, showing that whether someone counts as dead can turn on which conception of the person is doing the counting. The closing meditation on Pratchett's own posterior cortical atrophy and the documentary Choosing to Die argues that conceptualizing death in advance—in living wills and bedside conversations with loved ones—is what lets us meet 'THERE'S JUST ME' a little less afraid.

immortality.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
immortality.title: 11. Immortality Is Misery
immortality.relation: In dialogue with Deadpool himself, John Altmann tests whether immortality is a blessing: Bentham's utilitarianism would prize a healing factor that lets Wade dive into a gamma meltdown to save the Southern Hemisphere for free, and Nietzsche would hail him as an Übermensch for refusing the Mithras Directive's Messiah and preserving humanity's freedom to create its own values rather than adopt herd morality. Bernard Williams gets the last word: since personalities become fixed—Wade stays a mercenary across every run, Zenpool notwithstanding—an endless life curdles into boredom and misery, so immortality is punishment rather than power unless one could radically change who one is.

immortality.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
immortality.title: 2. A Death Worth Living
immortality.relation: Argues that dying in the Murder House or the Hotel Cortez removes death's usual harms - Ben Harmon can reunite with his ghost family and keep counseling patients, and Liz Taylor's chosen death brings reunion with Tristan plus open-ended projects protecting the hotel - but then poses Bernard Williams's boredom problem: finite projects run out over eternity and replacing them would make you a different person. Richard Taylor's Sisyphus and the Hotel's contented Laundress supply the answer that repetitive tasks embraced as meaningful can sustain even an immortal afterlife.

immortality.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
immortality.title: 9. Voodoo Hoodoo
immortality.relation: Explains Coven's Spirit Wars through the real history and philosophy of New Orleans Voodoo: the historical Marie Laveaux as healer and Voodoo Queen, Tituba as the link between witchcraft and Voodoo in Salem, the loa and spirit possession (Maya Deren's gros bon ange), zombies and the bokor, Papa Legba as trickster gatekeeper rather than Satan, and the seven gates of Guinee. It argues that Laveau's annual innocent and Fiona's failed soul-selling enact the Voodoo cosmology in which hell is the earthly entrapment of the soul - and, as Legba says, 'everybody pays.'

immortality.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
immortality.title: 16. Please Don’t Kill Me! (But if You Do, Could You Make a Video )
immortality.relation: Reads Roanoke through Stephen Cave's Mortality Paradox, Ernest Becker's Denial of Death, and Terror Management Theory: the Blood Moon ghosts embody inevitable death, dramatic irony mirrors our denial, reality-TV fame and Twitter followers are the modern immortality project (Agnes's 'I just wanted to be on TV', the superfans killed mid-broadcast), and the Polks' ritual cannibalism is symbolic power over extinction. Montaigne's 'to study philosophy is to learn to die' and his savoring of fleeting moments close the chapter, with Shelby - who alone submits to death without fiction - as the figure who actually escapes the terror.

immortality.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
immortality.title: 7. Eleanor and the Meaning of Afterlife
immortality.relation: Yang frames Eleanor's predicament as a dilemma: a finite life seems drained of value by its ending, while an immortal one collapses into boredom or into the disconnection of the 802 memory-wiped reboots. Camus's Sisyphus and Richard Taylor's desire-fulfillment view prove inadequate, so he adopts Susan Wolf's account of meaning as loving what deserves to be loved, which Eleanor's study of moral philosophy, her friendships, and her romance with Chidi satisfy even without God or eternity. John Martin Fischer's narrative approach then redeems the reboots as self-contained episodes, and Eleanor's note to herself in Scanlon's book shows memory wipes need not sever the story of a life.

immortality.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
immortality.title: 18. Heaven Is Other People
immortality.relation: Mayward examines the show's eschatology, arguing its points algorithm critiques the popular picture of Hell as eternal conscious torment, in the lineage of Jonathan Edwards, while missing historic Christian teaching about embodied resurrection. He then reads the series through Levinas, for whom ethics arises in the face-to-face encounter with the Other prior to any impersonal judgment, a structure mirrored in the show's two-shots and in Eleanor's spontaneous good deeds done before she understands them, and through Dietrich Bonhoeffer's 'religionless Christianity', in which Michael's self-sacrifice and the humans' repentance enact responsibility for neighbors without hope of reward. Salvation in the show is intersubjective transformation: where Sartre said Hell is other people, The Good Place suggests Heaven is other people.

immortality.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
immortality.title: 16. The Defeat of Death
immortality.relation: JD Lyonhart asks which of four philosophies of death Endgame adopts: embracing death as natural balance (Thanos's view, where the Snap keeps life in check), denying it, grimly accepting it, or defeating it. Opening with Schopenhauer's 'Death is the muse of philosophy,' he sketches Plato's Meno argument that the slave boy's innate knowledge requires a pre-existing, hence immortal, soul, and then argues the film starts with Tony's acceptance of death as final before completing a trajectory that runs from Yinsen's sacrificial death in the cave, through Tony's cruciform fall through the wormhole in The Avengers, to a Christ-like defeat of death in Endgame where Tony dies facing death head-on so others may live. The film avoids cheap denial by sitting in five years of grief before the triumph, mirroring the Christian pattern in which Easter cannot be celebrated without Good Friday.

immortality.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
immortality.title: 21. I Plucked My Soul Out of Its Secret Place
immortality.relation: Traces the Soul Stone across comics and film — Thanos courting Death, the Vormir 'a soul for a soul' trade of Gamora, and Natasha's parallel sacrifice for Clint in Endgame — reading it through sacrifice and resurrection motifs from the Binding of Isaac and asking why the film's Thanos must complete the offering Abraham was spared. It contrasts Thanos, who styles himself a god but is a 'false god,' an idol beside the sentient being that existed before all realities and became the six Infinity Gems, with Adam Warlock, who dwells in the Soul World and 'knows his soul' (the chapter's title borrows Claude McKay's poem), while Thanos is driven by destiny — 'I ignored my destiny once. I cannot do that again.'

immortality.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
immortality.title: Equal Opportunity—for Deities
immortality.relation: Barkman argues the Marvel Universe's 'One-Above-All'—depicted as Stan Lee and Jack Kirby—is the eternal Judeo-Christian Creator, and arranges its beings in a graded hierarchy: the Living Tribunal as God's judge, cosmic beings like Eternity and Galactus, elders, sky fathers Odin and Zeus, down to mortals, with only God eternal and everything else, gods included, able to die yet enduring by His decree. Ontological rank guarantees nothing morally—Mephisto, the Goddess, and Hera are powerful and wicked, and even Hercules can be beaten by the Wrecking Crew. A free-will theodicy answers where evil came from: 'no other gods before me' never denied other gods' existence but commands loving the Good above all, which mortal Avengers like Thor, loving justice perfected by sacrificial love, manage as well as any deity.

immortality.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
immortality.title: Into the Future
immortality.relation: Hanley dismantles the four alleged human-Cylon differences: humans are also 'made' (by God), contain non-organic parts, come as identical twins, and expect to survive death, so religious believers already believe they are Cylons. He defends reproductive cloning as reproduction not replication (a clone is your child, not your copy), models Cylon resurrection as scanning-death-transmission-replication, and shows van Inwagen's replica-swap account of bodily resurrection faces the same worries about blank bodies and which body returns. Following Locke's consciousness criterion, that a soul independent of body and memory explains none of our identity judgments, he rejects karma-based reincarnation without memory, proposes a fission-style plot-fix for Athena's impossible memories of Tyrol, and ends with Cylons settling ancient Earth: 'I am a Cylon, and so are you.'

immortality.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
immortality.title: Embracing Death
immortality.relation: Vessey asks whether the humanoid Cylons' resurrection makes meaningful life impossible. Humans can aim at a 'successful death' - Socrates drinking the hemlock, the Greek warrior accepting his moira - in which dying completes a life understood as a whole oriented to something larger; a Cylon's death is a mere reset (download), and the exceptions available, dying out of range of a resurrection ship or D'Anna's boxing, occur only through failure or shame and so cannot contribute to meaning. Plato's Symposium link of children to immortality is inverted, since Cylons can only have mortal human-Cylon babies; what separates the Cylons from Sisyphus is not purpose but the option to opt out, which mortality forces on humans and resurrection denies the Cylons.

immortality.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
immortality.title: To the Third Power . .
immortality.relation: Wolfe argues the original series is 'deeply Mormon' in ontology though not in epistemology: Kobol anagrams Kolob, the Quorum of Twelve and 'sealing' marriages mirror LDS structure, and the Beings of Light's 'as you are now, we once were; as we are now, you may become' restates Lorenzo Snow's deification couplet, while Count Iblis, like the Mormon Satan, can only rule those who freely yield - agency is supreme. Because none of this is required to follow the show, later licensees could rebuild the metaphysics: the Maximum Press comics incoherently (free will violated when inconvenient), Richard Hatch's novels with a new pure-blood-of-Kobol cosmology, and Ronald Moore with a circular 'all this has happened before' replacing eternal progression.

immortality.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
immortality.title: The Value of Finitude
immortality.relation: The chapter tests each motive for uploading to San Junipero and finds it wanting: Kantian cosmic justice fails because the resort neither rewards the good nor can punish the wicked; Tolstoy's cosmic-insignificance dread fails because a finite life can still be meaningful, and even Epicurus and Lucretius deflate the fear of death (while Nagel notes death's evil lies in foreclosed possibilities, and Williams's Makropulos case warns eternal life breeds boredom). Nozick's experience machine is the closest analogy, but the chapter argues San Junipero differs — residents know it is digital and share it with other conscious people — before Nussbaum's argument lands: without finitude there is no risk, so no courage, sacrifice, or deep love, which is why Kelly's forty-nine real years with Richard outweigh forever with Yorkie.

immortality.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
immortality.title: 13 The Ancestral Plane Metaphysical Mystery or Meaningful Metaphor
immortality.relation: Kowalski treats the Heart-Shaped Herb's Ancestral Plane visits as a test case for Cartesian substance dualism: if T'Challa truly embraces T'Chaka's soul, the film commits to bodies and souls as distinct substances, with the film's own analogy — Shuri remotely driving T'Challa's car from her lab — standing in for soul-body interactionism. But Princess Elisabeth's interaction problem (how a non-physical soul could be embraced, seen, or chemically affected) makes dualism implausible, so he argues the second and third visits work better as metaphor: Killmonger's audience with N'Jobu and T'Challa's 'You were wrong! All of you!' confrontation with his ancestors dramatize taking stock of how one's father shaped who one is, with T'Challa's sunlit third visit symbolizing his choice not to be bound by that past.

immortality.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
immortality.title: 14 The Afterlife of Erik Killmonger in African Philosophy
immortality.relation: Paul Dottin argues that Black Panther lore inherited the racist 'Hamitic Hypothesis' (crediting Egypt rather than sub-Saharan Africa for Wakanda's civilization) and that Ta-Nehisi Coates and Ryan Coogler begin a Wiredu-style conceptual decolonization of it. Taking Killmonger's dying wish to be buried with the ancestors who jumped from slave ships literally, the chapter asks which African metaphysics could make his postmortem survival of substance, subjectivity, and setting rationally intelligible. It rejects Cartesian substance dualism (illustrated by T'Challa defeating the demon Mephisto only after trapping his spirit in a body) in favor of Wiredu's Akan quasi-physicalism and Adeofe's Yoruba theory of destiny (ipin) and inner head (ori-inu), then ranks Killmonger's afterlife options from limbo through the Ancestral Plane to deification as the ocean deity Olokun.

immortality.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
immortality.title: I think we've all arrived at a very special place, eh Spiritually Ecumenically Grammatically —Captain Jack Spa
immortality.relation: Miller uses Disney deaths to stage the philosophy of death: Plato's immortal soul and Phaedo's affinity argument illuminate Frollo's lust-driven plunge into hellfire, while Epicurus's atomism, his 'death is nothing to us' argument applied to Marlin's terror in Finding Nemo, and Lucretius's symmetry argument are tested against Coco, where Ernesto's forgotten 'final death' versus Hector's restored place on the ofrenda makes posthumous harm plausible. Aquinas's 'my soul is not me' grounds embodiment, Confucius makes Mulan's risking death for father, ancestors, and country a virtuous Confucian death, and Deloria's indigenous web of relations reads Mufasa's Circle of Life, Moana's grandmother, and Brother Bear's ancestral spirits.

immortality.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
immortality.title: The Investigator Must, Therefore, Relinquish the Hat
immortality.relation: Stages the Platonic, Aristotelian, and Thomistic theories of the soul as a prizefight over whether the protomolecule-built Investigator that haunts Holden in Season 4 — wearing Miller's civilian clothes and fedora rather than the vac suit he died in — contains any of Joe Miller's soul and so has a right to his identity. Plato's separately surviving, reincarnating soul would never bond to a non-corporeal construct only Holden can see, one that glitches into a rigid 'Miller-puppet'; Aristotle's hylomorphism (with Aquinas's survive-until-resurrection compromise weighed) says the protomolecule merely watched and copied Miller — 'Copied, hijacked, reused but didn't comprehend.' The verdict turns on the Investigator's replay of Miller's self-sacrifice on Ilus, mirroring Miller diverting Eros: it is re-run programming, not soul, so the philosophers claim the hat and the Investigator must relinquish it.

immortality.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
immortality.title: 7. Eleanor and the Meaning of Afterlife
immortality.relation: Builds a dilemma from 'Existential Crisis': Michael's prospective retirement (via Todd May's Death) makes finitude look meaning-destroying, while the humans' endless existence — 802 reboots, Mindy St. Claire's eternal Cannonball Run II in the Medium Place — threatens boredom and disconnection from past selves. Testing God-free answers, it runs through Camus's Sisyphus, Richard Taylor's desire-fulfillment view, Susan Wolf's requirement that we love what deserves to be loved (Eleanor's philosophy study, friendship with Tahani, romance with Chidi), and John Martin Fischer on free authorship and narrative order (Eleanor's note to herself in What We Owe to Each Other). Conclusion: Eleanor and friends can lead meaningful lives even if damned and repeatedly rebooted.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: Introduction
immortality.relation: The introduction argues, citing Plato's saying that philosophy begins in wonder, that children's fantasy like Rowling's is a natural home for philosophy, since young readers can be nourished by ideas they cannot fully digest, like Fang gnawing a dragon bone. It canvasses the volume's guiding questions: whether love is the most powerful magic, whether souls exist and can be split by Horcruxes, what Animagi and boggarts teach about personal identity, whether choices reveal more than abilities, and whether Snape can be redeemed. It closes by framing the book in the Blackwell series tradition of using pop culture to teach philosophy, updating the 2004 Open Court volume now that all seven novels are out.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: Unknown
immortality.relation: This section of the soul chapter lays out the Cartesian view: the immaterial soul explains only language and higher-level cognition, while material causes suffice for sensation, which consigns nonhuman animals to soullessness. It applies the view to Rowling's borderline creatures, such as owls that understand human speech and Crookshanks's suspicious intelligence, before introducing materialism as the fourth conception of the soul.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: Ghosts and “Going On”
immortality.relation: The section argues that everyday talk of soul mates, soulful art, and baring one's soul is metaphorical talk about our deepest emotions, love, and conscience, not commitment to an immaterial substance, and that even materialists can keep the vocabulary rather than translate Hoagy Carmichael into talk of C-fibers firing. It then forecasts the chapter's conclusion about Rowling: her Potter-world soul mixes this sentimental view with metaphysics borrowed from the Cartesian and sentience views.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: The Dementor’s Kiss
immortality.relation: The section argues that materialism is false in the Potter universe by cataloguing the ways souls outlive bodies: Hermione's claim that a sword through Ron would leave his soul untouched, the voices beyond the Ministry's veil, Nearly Headless Nick's ghostly imprint of a wizard who refused to 'go on,' Voldemort's wraith-like survival, and the 'neither ghost nor truly flesh' shades summoned from Voldemort's wand and by the Resurrection Stone. It sets up dementors and Horcruxes as the next tests of what souls are.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: Horcruxes
immortality.relation: Using Lupin's account of the Dementor's Kiss, in which the victim goes on existing as an empty shell with no sense of self or memory, the section rules out the life-source and sentience views of the soul and probably the Cartesian view too, since a soulless Barty Crouch Jr. might still perceive the room. The author proposes the soulless state is like severe dementia or Lockhart after his backfired memory charm, raising the question of what, if anything, makes the shell still a person.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: A Plausible View
immortality.relation: Reconstructing Slughorn's lesson to young Riddle, the section argues that because Voldemort's brain, senses, and magical powers survive his soul being ripped into seven, the Cartesian and sentience views are excluded and Rowling must hold the sentimental view: the soul is our capacity to love and our moral conscience. Voldemort's snake-faced transformation and his followers' fear-based loyalty, where even Bellatrix worships his power rather than being charmed, dramatize his lost humanity, and only remorse, which Harry begs him to 'try for' before the rebounding curse kills him, could have repaired the damage.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: NOTES
immortality.relation: The concluding section of the soul essay asks whether Rowling's combined theory is likely true and answers probably not: there is no evidence of immaterial causes of brain events, the centuries-old mind-body interaction problem looms, and it is especially implausible that a separate substance handles only our deepest emotions and moral traits, with the added wrinkle that souls in the story display different physical powers depending on which spell conjures them. Yet it concedes that implausible metaphysics is no flaw in fiction that makes vivid what we care about and 'makes for a terrific story.'

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: NOTES
immortality.relation: Surveys near-death-experience research from Moody's Life after Life to Susan Blackmore's debunking explanations (oxygen starvation, cultural variation) and argues the skeptical conclusion does not follow: a child's vision of her living dog Sparky on the other side could still be a genuine divinely created revelation happening wholly inside her head. It reads Harry's King's Cross way-station the same way, since wizards can channel themselves through portraits, ghosts, and Legilimency, and closes with Emerson's Over-Soul claim that moments of faith deserve to be ascribed more reality than ordinary experience.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: The Inversion of Voldemort
immortality.relation: Sharpens the remorse-versus-regret contrast through Voldemort's cold regret after having Nagini kill Snape, and shows true remorse at work in Dumbledore's confession about the Resurrection Stone ring, his arranged death at Snape's hand, and his tearful self-disclosure to Harry at King's Cross. Harry too must die to be regenerated: letting Voldemort strike him destroys the Horcrux inside so that his soul becomes whole and completely his own, while lesser purgings, like his furious outburst at Ron and Hermione, and his love for Ginny complete the pattern of dying to the old self.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: The Integrity Objection
immortality.relation: Completes the inversion: each Horcrux rips and destabilizes Voldemort's soul, and only excruciating remorse could put it back together, something he will never attempt, while his evil literally disembodies him until he lives parasitically on the blood and limbs of others. Against this, Hermione's gloss on the Potters' gravestone, the last enemy that shall be destroyed is death, means the soul survives whatever happens to the body, grounding the contrast between Voldemort's pathetic, unmourned end and the honored deaths of Dobby, Fred, Lupin, Tonks, and Colin Creevey.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: Reap a Destiny
immortality.relation: Interprets the King's Cross scene through Heidegger's counsel to choose an exemplar from the past and dialogue with them: Dumbledore, freshly repentant for his youthful hunger for glory, plays exactly that role in a way-station likened to purgatory, while the flayed child-like creature under the chair is Voldemort's soul beyond help. The chapter closes by linking his fear-driven quest for deathlessness to Tolkien's One Ring, in which Sauron poured his own life-force, both fantasy dark lords undone by the desire for deathlessness.

immortality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
immortality.title: NOTES
immortality.relation: Uses William James's marginal motto, sow a thought and reap a destiny, together with Aristotle's account of how repeated acts shape the soul, to argue that Voldemort's maimed afterlife-state is the cumulative result of freely chosen evil he can no longer muster remorse to undo. Setting Heidegger's atheism against Rowling's depicted afterlife, and adding Locke's character-and-memory identity, Kant's postulate that harmony of virtue and happiness requires an afterlife, and Pascal on why the soul's immortality must concern us, it concludes that if Rowling is right, every choice here is infinitely consequential.

immortality.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
immortality.title: Game Over
immortality.relation: Anna Janssen reads Zelda as a meditation on death: Link embodies the worst version of immortality, an eternal purgatory of endless resurrection for the player's benefit, while the dungeon bosses — who stay dead once defeated — are the only truly mortal, and hence most human, beings in Hyrule. Hegel's demand that man reconcile himself with mortality, Nietzsche's erosion of dualist soul-belief, and Bernard Williams's worries about the tedium of immortality frame the discussion, with Wind Waker's reincarnating hero giving the immortal-soul view its due. Turning off the console becomes a metaphor for the unknowable nothingness of death, and the series' formula and save-games a structured coping alternative to a chaotic universe.

immortality.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
immortality.title: 10. Gods Are Overrated
immortality.relation: Michaud runs Hume's problem of evil against a Superman who is nearly all-powerful, all-knowing, and good yet takes dates with Lois while animals and children suffer pointlessly — and unlike God he cannot hide behind mystery, only laziness. God-like protectors breed excuses ('Superman is our great excuse' for doing nothing about homelessness or starving children), and belief in afterlife and divine rescue cheapens this life; following Nietzsche's death of God, the chapter argues we should stop believing in saviors, face the infinite night, make our own meaning, and be more like Batman — self-reliant people who try to save others themselves.

immortality.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
immortality.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Delfino and Taylor ask whether Morgan's zombified wife Jenny is a person, weighing Boethius's 'individual substance of a rational nature', Aquinas's image-of-God intellectual soul, and Kantian dignity against Peter Singer's speciesism challenge to the person/animal moral line. They then argue walkers are 'impossible beings' like square-circles: Jenner's brain-stem-only reanimation cannot explain Hannah the bicycle girl crawling without organs, walkers smelling Rick in the rain, or cafeteria walkers moving for weeks without energy. On either the soul view or materialism walkers are not persons, so Morgan should shoot, and zombies fascinate because they are metaphysical projections of our fears, caught between being and nonbeing.

immortality.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
immortality.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
immortality.relation: McClelland opens with the Buddha's claim that all life is suffering and reads Eastwood's aging-hero films (The Eiger Sanction, Firefox, Unforgiven, In the Line of Fire, Blood Work, Mystic River, Million Dollar Baby, Gran Torino) as grounding two opposed inductions on the meaning of loss. The 'pessimistic induction' holds that many losses—Maggie's paralysis, Dave Boyle's abuse, Munny's dead—are irremediable, supporting an Aristotelian view that death dissolves the person with the body. The 'optimistic induction' draws on the science of ecological resilience to argue losses can be navigated with others' help; Walt's autonomous, meaning-making death exemplifies resilience. Hereafter's agnosticism about survival leaves Eastwood's own verdict on surviving death as 'I don't know.'

immortality.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
immortality.title: The Grim Reaper on Baker Street
immortality.relation: Glass-Turner examines death across the Holmes canon, opening with Kierkegaard's claim that death's explanation discloses the explainer's own inner being and pairing Holmes with TV's Dr. House as materialist puzzle-solvers who rule out the supernatural ('no ghosts need apply'). She weighs Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' against the wrongness of murder, then argues Holmes's pig- and cadaver-experiments coexist with reverence for the dead and hints of belief in an afterlife ('compensation hereafter' in 'The Veiled Lodger'), reading him via William James as open to more than the physical. She closes on Holmes's calm acceptance of his own Reichenbach death and Conan Doyle's later turn to spiritualism after his wife's death.

immortality.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
immortality.title: Spinning Tops and Brains in Vats
immortality.relation: William Lindenmuth reads Inception's ambiguous ending through Robert Nozick's experience machine, arguing that Cobb's choice of his real children over the dream-Mal ('you're just a shade of my real wife') shows we want our dreams to be reality, not reality to be a dream. He deploys Nozick's three reasons against plugging in - we want to do things, not merely seem to; we want to be a certain kind of person ('It's not who I am underneath, but what I do that defines me'); and a man-made reality confines and limits us - while invoking Bernard Williams's tedium of immortality for Cobb's fifty dream-years with Mal and Wittgenstein's talking lion for the alienation those years create. On this reading the wobbling top matters, because choosing limbo would be 'a kind of suicide,' the difference between the film ending as tragedy or not.

immortality.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
immortality.title: Here They Are ... Ready to Outsit Eternity
immortality.relation: Michael Hand uses the Doctor's regeneration to argue that life after death is logically possible. Because the First-through-Tenth Doctors are the same person despite total personality change (a dandy becoming a clown), identity is distinct from personality, so a god perfecting flawed Joe for heaven need not make him someone else. He then tests the replica theory against 'Journey's End' (the metacrisis Doctor) and 'Human Nature' (John Smith), concluding we favor bodily continuity, and endorses van Inwagen's 'divine cryonicist' solution to the unavailability-of-atoms problem, echoing the Doctor's 'ready to outsit eternity' praise of frozen humanity in 'The Ark in Space'.

immortality.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
immortality.title: 5. Could Hell Be Any Worse than Doc Benton’s Immortality
immortality.relation: Hellwig uses Dean's choice of Hell over Doc Benton's organ-replacement immortality in 'Time Is on My Side' to examine medical immortality. He pairs Dean's worry—that maiming and replacing your body makes you unrecognizably human—with Bernard Williams's Makropulos argument that immortality ends in categorical-desire-exhausting boredom, adding a third condition to Williams: a recognizably human life requires being able to self-identify with one's own body, illustrated by real disfigurement cases and Aubrey de Grey's biogerontology.

immortality.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
immortality.title: Reap a Destiny
immortality.relation: Jonathan and Jerry Walls read Harry Potter's Deathly Hallows through the question of death and afterlife. Harry's willing death-march models Heidegger's authenticity and being-toward-death, while Voldemort's terror of death makes him inauthentic. At King's Cross the maimed Voldemort-soul embodies William James's 'sow a character, reap a destiny': having refused remorse, he has become evil beyond repair, whereas the repentant Dumbledore has grown. Against Heidegger's atheism, Rowling's Christian resurrection imagery, backed by Locke on memory-identity, Kant, and Pascal, makes our character-forming choices infinitely consequential.

immortality.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
immortality.title: “Sometimes Dead Is Better”
immortality.relation: Katherine Allen reads Pet Sematary and The Tommyknockers as bioconservative fables staging the transhumanism debate: Louis's resurrected, 'fundamentally wrong' cat Church and cannibal son Gage, and Bobbi's tooth-shedding 'New Improved' becoming, dramatize Kass, McKibben and Fukuyama's warning that erasing our limits erases our humanity. Against them she sets Nick Bostrom's 'Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant,' in which death is an unquestioned evil we should slay, and Bernard Williams's worry about the tedium of immortality. King's insistence that 'sometimes dead is better,' and that forbidden knowledge (the Micmac ground, the buried ship) works like an addiction, sides with the deathist view that mortality and finitude give life its meaning.

immortality.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
immortality.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
immortality.relation: Allred applies Heidegger's Being and Time – the world as a meaningful context of projects, the hammer-as-tool example, and death as what makes projects meaningful – to contrast the father's world with the 'man-child' world of Seth Rogen's Judd Apatow characters (especially Knocked Up). He argues fatherhood reveals the fragility of all projects, using Plato's account of seeking immortality through children and Paul Celan's poem 'Epitaph for François' about his stillborn son to show that after a child is born the parent's world is forever haunted by the possibility of its emptiness.

immortality.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
immortality.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
immortality.relation: Bill Davis explains why Arwen relinquishes elvish immortality and why Aragorn and Frodo accept death as a 'gift,' contrasting the Ringwraiths' cursed undeath (an Aristotelian frustration of their mortal nature) with genuine mortality. He surveys real-world responses to death: Socrates' calm confidence in the soul, Lucretius's and the existentialists' liberation through annihilation, and worries from Bernard Williams and others about the tedium of immortality, which Boethius answers with a timeless heaven. Davis argues Arwen chooses a finite life of deep love over deathless boredom, and that all three accept death trusting Iluvatar's love promises a world remade beyond the circles of the world.

immortality.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
immortality.title: Reap a Destiny
immortality.relation: The Walls brothers read Harry Potter's confrontation with death through Heidegger's authenticity and being-toward-death: Harry's calm march to the Forbidden Forest and Colin Creevey's sacrifice exemplify accepting mortality, while Voldemort's terror of death makes him inauthentic. The King's Cross scene lets Dumbledore be Harry's Heideggerian hero from the past; via William James's "sow a thought … reap a destiny," Aristotle, Locke on memory-identity, and Kant on the afterlife, they argue our choices forge a character — and Voldemort's refusal of remorse seals his ruin.

immortality.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
immortality.title: 1. The Good Place as Philosophy Moral Adventures in the Afterlife
immortality.relation: Engels argues that NBC's The Good Place, though premised on a merit-based afterlife, actually argues morality should not be grounded in afterlife reward. When Eleanor, Chidi, Jason, and Tahani learn the point system and can no longer earn points, they form the 'Soul Squad' to be virtuous for virtue's sake, echoing Aristotle's telos and Kant's claim that acting from fear of hell is a heteronomous, non-moral motive. She reads the unfair points system (no human admitted in 521 years) through Rawls's Veil of Ignorance and shifts the show toward rehabilitative justice, and treats the Good Place residents' boredom via Bernard Williams's tedium-of-immortality argument, with Chidi's 'wave returns to the ocean' speech mapped onto Hindu atman/Brahman and moksha.

immortality.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
immortality.title: 54. The Man from Earth as Philosophy The Desirability of Immortality
immortality.relation: Berk brings The Man from Earth—about John Oldman, a 14,000-year-old non-aging man—into dialogue with Bernard Williams's 'The Makropulos Case,' which argues immortality must become boring and identity-destroying (the dilemma of exhausted versus radically changed categorical desires). Against these 'immortality curmudgeons,' the chapter argues John's mild boredom, enduring loves, friendships, and pursuit of knowledge show an immortal life can stay worth living, invoking Fischer's 'repeatable pleasures.' It also engages Nussbaum's 'Mortal Immortals' and Beauvoir's All Men Are Mortal (the miserable Fosca), which tie courage and love to finitude and sacrifice, noting John is only 'medically' rather than 'genuinely' immortal and so can still make sacrifices.

immortality.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
immortality.title: 6. Religion, Loss, and Afterlife
immortality.relation: The chapter asks whether Doctor Who is a religion, testing it against Hopfe's and Ninian Smart's criteria and concluding it is best understood as a Humanist-and-religious 'philosophy'—sacred and 'holy' (Otto) but lacking a genuine transcendent 'unseen.' On loss, it uses Kierkegaard's 'aesthetic life' and 'rotation method' to explain why we fear endings and regenerations, urging viewers to root life in lasting meaning rather than fleeting pleasure. On death, it deploys Socrates in the Apology and Phaedo and Aristotle on courage (Jabe, Harriet Jones, Donna sacrificing themselves) to argue death is nothing to fear, and reads the Matrix and Nethersphere as the show's two Socratic afterlife options.

buddhist-karma.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
buddhist-karma.title: Unknown
