the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 18. Russian Doll as Philosophy Life Is Like a Box of Timelines
the-absurd.relation: The chapter treats Russian Doll's time loops (Season One) and time portals (Season Two) as vehicles for the metaphysics of time, comparing them to Groundhog Day and canvassing presentism, eternalism, and the growing-block theory. It argues the show is committed to a Parfit-style 'multiple timelines' solution to the problem of whether looped characters are numerically identical, and rejects a Berkeleyan idealist alternative. Its climax reads Nadia through Camus's Myth of Sisyphus: unable to change significant past events, she becomes an 'absurd hero' who embraces her family and lot in life, smiling in the mirror, so Season Two's lesson (echoing Nietzsche's eternal recurrence) is that meaning comes from owning one's circumstances.

the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 22. Rick & Morty as Philosophy Nihilism in the Multiverse
the-absurd.relation: The chapter argues that Rick Sanchez's nihilism is built on cultural relativism plus the metaphysical fact of a multiverse. It reads Rick's mockery of racist alien snakes and the Gazorpazorp matriarchy through Montaigne's essay on cannibals to establish cultural relativism, and treats the microverse 'battery' society through Marx's base/superstructure and Foucault's docile bodies to argue all social values are constructed for the rulers. Rick's dimension-hopping (the Cronenberg episode, the Vat of Acid) literalizes David Lewis's modal realism and Leibniz's possible worlds, so that no action matters because a counterpart always does the opposite; his resulting hedonism and Birdperson's 'Wubba lubba dub dub' reveal Rick as a depressed near-Camusian who cannot live his own absurdist creed.

the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 49. A Serious Man as Philosophy The Elusiveness of Moral Knowledge
the-absurd.relation: Biderman reads the Coens' A Serious Man through Beauvoir's figure of the 'serious man' (from The Ethics of Ambiguity), the man who craves a single absolute value and blinds himself to moral complexity: physics professor Larry Gopnik, beset by divorce, a bribing student Clive, and Sy Ableman's death, seeks moral knowledge that would let him be such a man. The chapter argues Larry's quest fails across cognitivist, noncognitivist, and pluralist accounts of moral knowledge, showing moral knowledge to be elusive if not impossible. The film's Kafkaesque fables (the Dibbuk, the Goy's Teeth, Rabbi Nachtner's 'L'olam ha-ba', Schrodinger's cat, and the Binding of Isaac in Caravaggio's painting) all stage the absurd collapse of interpretation, echoing the Book of Job, which Maimonides read as a parable rather than history.

the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 51. Magnolia As Philosophy Meaning and Coincidence
the-absurd.relation: Engelen interprets Paul Thomas Anderson's Magnolia as a meditation on sense-making and Camus's notion of the absurd: the film's raining frogs and the interlocking coincidences (Sydney Barringer's death, the narrator's insistence that 'this cannot be one of those things') stage our compulsion to find meaning colliding with a universe that yields none. He reads characters' struggles with trauma and regret through Epictetus's Stoic dichotomy of control and Jung's synchronicity, and the 'Wise Up' sing-along as a call to accept what cannot be changed. The chapter endorses Camus's third response to the absurd—neither denial nor suicide but defiant acceptance—linking it to Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and Nagel's take on life's meaning.

the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 77. Journey as Philosophy Meaning, Connection, and the Sublime
the-absurd.relation: Hamer argues Journey works through the interplay of connection, the sublime and meaning. The wordless multiplayer bond with an unnameable stranger before vast vistas dramatizes emotional connection where the ancestors' greed failed. The looming mountain and immense dunes evoke the sublime, read through Burke's pleasurable terror and Kant's mathematical and dynamical sublime (imagination overwhelmed while reason comprehends; feeling power over a nature that cannot harm the deathless player, then rebirth surpassing the sublime into joy). The cyclical return to the start recasts the game as Camus's Myth of Sisyphus: a meaningless repeated ascent that players nonetheless replay, so we must imagine the Traveler — and ourselves — happy to make the beautiful repetition our own.

the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 89. The Joker as Philosopher Killing Jokes
the-absurd.relation: Brake reads Moore and Bolland's The Killing Joke as staging Camus's absurd: the Joker tortures Commissioner Gordon to prove the world is random and unjust ('one bad day') and that reason, tied to continuous memory, should be abandoned for a fragmented 'multiple choice' self. Drawing on Nietzsche's wave-like unstable self (via Morrison's 'super-sane' Joker) and Foucault on how madness haunts modern reason, the chapter argues Batman and Gordon also flirt with madness, while questioning whether the Joker, seeking revenge, has really embraced the absurd or is more rational than he admits.

the-absurd.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-absurd.title: 91. Deadpool’s Killogy as Philosophy The Metaphysics of a Homicidal Journey Through Possible Worlds
the-absurd.relation: Manninen argues that Cullen Bunn's Deadpool 'Killogy' is best read through David Lewis's genuine modal realism and counterpart theory: when Deadpool enters the Nexus of All Realities and finds piles of distinct Spider-Man corpses, he discovers other worlds are concrete and their inhabitants are counterparts, not identical selves, refuting Plantinga's actualist transworld identity. Framing Deadpool as an anti-Sisyphean 'hero' who tries to end the Absurd (the Continuity) by killing everyone rather than affirming it as Camus's Sisyphus does, the chapter supplements Lewis with Thomasson's artifact theory of fiction to handle the literary characters of the Ideaverse.

thrownness.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
thrownness.title: Unknown
thrownness.relation: The chapter concedes authenticity's costs - the truths of death, suffering, and meaninglessness are hard to stomach, and inauthenticity is the social norm that makes the authentic person feel alienated and even mad (Roquentin's 'crazy loon category', The Matrix's 'hardware' people who fight unplugging) - but argues the red pill still wins. Inauthenticity never eradicates anxiety (the 'splinter in the mind'), only misattributes it to mundane causes like jobs and cars, and it costs freedom and genuinely informed choice; authenticity ends the flight from being and yields a serenity Roquentin finds when existence becomes 'a perfect free gift'.

thrownness.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
thrownness.title: U2 and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Malpas takes The Joshua Tree as an album about place: its desert imagery and restless movement ('Where the Streets Have No Name', 'I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For' as 'an anthem of doubt more than faith') carry the listener from Ireland to Reagan's America to Pinochet's Chile, while its political references - Ethiopian famine, El Salvador, Dublin high-rises - always work through concrete locations rather than abstract ideals. Using Heidegger on homelessness as the inability to dwell, and Marx and Engels' 'all that is solid melts into air', he argues that modernity has not erased our relatedness to place but covered it over. The album's desolation is therefore readable the other way: belonging is constituted through care, commitment and uncertain journeying in the places we already are ('Heartland').

thrownness.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
thrownness.title: U2 and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Benfell reads U2's apocalyptic songs through Heidegger rather than through eschatological doctrine: 'The Playboy Mansion' depicts fallenness in the 'they', a consumerist paradise with 'no time for sorrow' that lets us flee our own death, while the angel's fall in Wenders' films evoked by 'Stay' and the day-to-day constraints of 'Some Days Are Better than Others' illustrate thrownness, and 'Gone' existential guilt as an unpayable debt. A verse-by-verse reading of 'Until the End of the World' - the Judas-at-the-last-supper reading as one register - shows the speaker moving from 'passing time' and playing roles in the 'they' to anxious guiltiness and the call of conscience, reaching for the one whose resolute waiting models anticipatory resoluteness. The 'end of the world', he concludes, is the end of the speaker's own world: U2's apocalyptic imagery calls listeners to authentic, finite existence, not to prediction of last things.

thrownness.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
thrownness.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
thrownness.relation: David Hart uses Heidegger's Being and Time to explain Batman's dedication without reducing it to trauma-determined compulsion: Alfred's butler's-world illustrates being-in-the-world and the thrown-project, and Bruce's confrontation with death, culminating in the bleeding alley scene of Miller's Batman: Year One, is Angst, the recognition of finitude that strips ordinary meanings away. Seen this way, "I shall become a bat" is an authentic, responsible choice of a whole life rather than a mechanical effect of childhood trauma. Hart concludes that Heidegger's analysis dissolves the free will versus determinism debate, since Batman neither blindly follows causes nor chooses from nowhere.

thrownness.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
thrownness.title: We Don’t Need No Indoctrination
thrownness.relation: Detmer argues the four classic albums from Dark Side to The Wall form a unified meditation on alienation, from others, work, nature, and oneself, and reads Waters's stated 'political and philosophical' aims through the existentialists. 'Breathe''s rabbit digging one hole after another illustrates Marx's alienated labor (the worker 'only feels himself freely active in his animal functions'), echoed by Russell on industrialism's life against instinct and Camus on the day the 'why' arises; 'Time''s missed starting gun dramatizes our thrown condition and Heidegger's claim that only facing mortality head-on cures the inauthenticity of living as 'they' do, while Gilmour's improvised solos model the spontaneity such authenticity requires. 'Money' is a satire of greed confirmed by 'Dogs,' whose self-rationalizing climbers end 'dragged down by the stone,' and 'Us and Them' attacks artificial divisions (soldiers manipulated by map-movers, racism's 'black and blue,' the old man who dies 'for the want of the price of tea and a slice'). 'Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2)' indicts indoctrination, being told what to think, rather than education itself, making independent critical thought the road to the Sartrean autonomy and responsibility the chapter urges.

thrownness.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
thrownness.title: Jimmy Buffett “Singer of Inordinate Tunes” and Heideggerian Troubadour
thrownness.relation: Drew Dalton takes Buffett's claim that 'we don't just enjoy our escapism — we NEED it' as an admission that being itself is burdensome, overturning the Plato–Augustine–Leibniz consensus that it is good to be. Since 'Margaritaville is nowhere' — it is on no map and can never be reached — what we long for is not a better vacation but release from having to be at all, which is why even on holiday in Key West we still dream of escape. Heidegger's Being and Time supplies the framework: thrownness, being-toward-death, anxiety, and guilt reveal existence as a weight we never chose, so the escapist longing to be otherwise than ourselves is the 'inauthentic' flight Heidegger describes (without moral condemnation), and Levinas's On Escape confirms that 'it is precisely from all that is weighty in being that escaping sets forth.'

thrownness.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
thrownness.title: Only an Ortiz Can Save Us Heidegger’s Revelation of Being
thrownness.relation: James Pontuso reads Red Sox history through Heidegger: technology that turns the world into 'standing reserve' breeds the anxious 'everydayness' of the mediocre Pinky Higgins teams, while the run of near-misses from 1967 through Bucky Dent in 1978 and Buckner in 1986 threw fans into an authentic encounter with tragedy, mortality and the mystery of Being that the Yankees' free-agent 'technology of power' could never teach. Fenway Park, quirky and continuous with the pre-Hitler past, serves as 'home' in Heidegger's homeless age, and the literati's tragic framing of the team (language as the house of Being) made its fate a matter of existential weight rather than mere sport. David Ortiz's 2004 ALCS heroics then function as Heidegger's longed-for revelation of Being, the answer to 'only a god can save us,' after which fans have lived through all three states: everydayness, tragic anxiety, and wonder.

thrownness.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
thrownness.title: Chapter 27 - Time in Unfixed Are You
thrownness.relation: Written backwards in homage to 'Your Appointment Will Be Yesterday', this section argues that the self is found in the future more than the present: we understand objects through the actions they afford and ourselves through goals, projects and commitments, so the present moment has very little to do with who we 'really' are. Drawing on Edmund Husserl's 'protention' and Martin Heidegger's existence-as-possibilities, it shows that we hear a melody's building tension as an already-present resolution, and that the past stays present without being recalled - when the phone rings on the couch, where it was is simply there for you. Invoking Don Fallis's 'Lies, Incorporated', it adds that every remembering rewires history to fit our current view, so in memory we travel into the past just as surely as protention carries us into possible futures.

thrownness.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
thrownness.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Vannatta starts from Klosterman's confession that his first dates run on three and a half dates' worth of contrived material, and asks how self-knowledge is possible at all if, as Errol Morris tells Klosterman, we have no privileged access to our own minds. After a tour through Descartes's cogito, Kant's unity of apperception, Freud's unconscious, and Foucault's discourse-constructed subject, the chapter argues with Foucault's Ramist logic of similarity that Klosterman's thought really works by resemblance, mapping his exes onto members of KISS and hearing a dead friend in every Replacements song. Heidegger supplies the resolution: thrown into the crowd's world, we recover ourselves only through its inauthentic pop culture, and Klosterman's 'living is dying, little by little' and obsessive rock-death writing enact being-toward-death as the condition of authenticity.

thrownness.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
thrownness.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Uses Heidegger to read the show's very structure: the pilot's in-medias-res Winnebago crash throws us into Walt's timeline the way Dasein is thrown into time, and the flashbacks to Sandia Labs and 'nowhere to go but up' show his has-been shaping his futurity. Walt's diagnosis makes being-toward-death an overwhelming presence and exposes the failure of his calculative, goal-setting thinking, with the 'Fly' monologue about the perfect moment to die as his turn toward Heidegger's meditative thinking. By dwelling on his own death, the chapter argues, Walt inches toward an authentic being-toward-death - living each moment as if it were his last.

thrownness.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
thrownness.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: The chapter diagnoses the show's identity crises through Heidegger's Being and Time: Marshall's Goliath National Bank drudgery is anxiety over thrownness - the rent, the bills, the situation he never chose - while Lily's prom-night bolt to San Francisco is anxiety over freedom and possibility, and both fail anticipatory resoluteness, the commitment to be yourself while shouldering what you did not choose. das Man ('everybody's doing it') explains the gang's absorbed everydayness. Kierkegaard supplies the problem of time (life understood backwards but lived forwards) and Fear and Trembling's contrast between Abraham's leap of faith into the absurd and the 'demonic': Barney courts legendary moments yet manipulates uncertainty so he never becomes anyone new - the identity crisis that never ends.

thrownness.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
thrownness.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Christopher Ketcham narrates a night listening to Dear Heather during a café blackout, in which darkness becomes Eugene Minkowski's 'lived space' - more personal than light, with auditory space as its own dark space - and Cohen's voice leads him down into a shared funk of loss and depression. Through Heidegger he diagnoses his own shrunken, past-bound, thrown existence and reinterprets being-toward-death not as a downward spiral but as being toward his own remaining possibilities, and through Freud's death drive he names the 'unobtrusive death wish' he had let dwell unchallenged in him. The essay closes with a Heideggerian resolve toward resoluteness and future possibility, glimpsing a street-worn 'Suzanne' in the dark as hope rather than absence.

thrownness.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
thrownness.title: Homeland and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Roberto Sirvent and Ian Diorio ask what the state really asks soldiers to die for: not Hobbes-and-Locke's rational social contract, since we are Heideggerian thrown into the wreckage of democracy rather than a pure founding state, but a nation that makes itself sacred. MacIntyre's charge that killing for the nation-state is 'killing for the telephone company' frames the analysis of America's civil liturgies - oaths (semper fidelis), flag ritual mirrored eerily in Brody burying Jessica's thrown Quran, saints, martyrs, and Saul pitting belief in America against belief in Allah. Augustine's civitas dei names the result: America as chosen city of God, and Islam terrifies the West because its creed claims devotion above any national flag.

thrownness.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
thrownness.title: Girls and Philosophy
thrownness.relation: Addis uses Heidegger to explain why Hannah cannot 'rewrite her world': her enframing habit treats everything and everyone (Laird, Marnie, Adam) only in terms of feeding her 'writer' identity, so her world stays tiny even in vast New York. Heideggerian world, thrownness (Jessa's surprise wedding Shoshanna attends in white, Charlie's departure), and the power of art to de-enframe structure contrasts with Marnie, whose singing - prompted by Ray's question - expands her horizons. Hannah's crying-at-her-desk realization at the ad agency is read as her one genuine acceptance of thrownness, though her enframed self-absorption pulls her back.

thrownness.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
thrownness.title: 10. Change of Heart
thrownness.relation: Auxier names Petty the master of "liminal moments" when something is finally seen for what it is (the betrayed lover's realization behind "You Got Lucky," the unknown pain of "American Girl"), then stages the 1929 Davos debate between Cassirer's humane, Goethe-reading phenomenology and Heidegger's Angst before the abyss, being-toward-death, and the "moment of vision." He indicts Heidegger's Nazism and betrayal of Husserl as what "Petty-ness," the asshole-beast crouching in everyone's darkdeepdown, becomes when it wins, contrasting Petty's public apology for the Confederate flag and his cease-and-desist to George W. Bush. The chapter ends with the unguarded Petty smile as "Here Comes My Girl" made philosophy, an instance of authentic being-with-others that Heidegger declared impossible.

thrownness.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
thrownness.title: Paradox and Peace
thrownness.relation: Christopher Drohan reads Batman and Alfred through Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling: Batman, like Abraham, believes 'by virtue of the absurd,' resigning himself to an infinite, never-realizable justice as a knight of infinite resignation, while Alfred embodies the higher knight of faith whose justice is concrete love expressed in mending the suit, making sandwiches, and guarding the manor. Heidegger's thrownness and Sartre's condemned freedom frame both men's absurd existential condition, including Batman sparing Joe Chill and even allying with him against the Reaper. The chapter's verdict is that Alfred's faithful devotion to one person is the superior ethic, and that peace begins with him.

thrownness.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
thrownness.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
thrownness.relation: David Hart uses Heidegger to dissolve the question of whether Batman is determined by childhood trauma or freely chooses his mission. Heidegger's being-in-the-world and thrown-project, illustrated by Alfred the butler for whom the clock is essentially something to dust, replace the subject-object picture that grounds both free-will and determinism talk. Read this way, the bat crashing through the window in Batman: Year One is Bruce's Angst-laden confrontation with death as 'the possibility of my own impossibility,' through which he freely takes up the project of being Batman when nothing forced him to.

thrownness.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
thrownness.title: NOTES
thrownness.relation: Barris argues Lost fascinates because it dramatizes the basic structures of life itself: the castaways are Heideggerian thrown into an island none of them chose, brought there by Desmond's lapse at the Swan and by interlocking backstories such as Sawyer's bar conversation with Jack's father. Against the existentialist claim (Sartre, Camus) that life is simply absurd, he uses Wittgenstein's On Certainty - doubting everything presupposes certainties - to argue life is a riddle of partial sense, which is why the show's connections between Hurley and Libby or Jack and Desmond always hint at meaning without resolving it. The finale answers only the question of life after death, leaving life after birth as open as our own.

thrownness.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
thrownness.title: Nothing Is Ever Black or White
thrownness.relation: Miechels maps Witcher 3 onto Heidegger's Being and Time: with no character creator, the player is thrown into Geralt's fixed identity, the 'Butcher of Blaviken' with cat eyes whom villagers spit at, in a war-torn Velen he did not choose. Projection appears in the Triss-or-Yennefer romance (where refusing to choose is still a choice) and in the Bloody Baron, whose guilt shows that his war trauma and alcoholism never excused his choices: 'nothing is ever black and white' does not absolve him. Falling into das Man shows up in Gwent rounds, map question marks, and above all online walkthroughs of the 'optimal choice' for Willis's burned forge, which let players evade the responsibility of deciding for themselves.

thrownness.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
thrownness.title: Economies of Time in Clockers
thrownness.relation: Gilmore reads Clockers through DuBois's double-consciousness, arguing the film's dualities—the clockers' street dealing mirroring capitalist 'logic of maximum performance,' kronos versus kairos time, Hyde's commodity versus gift economies, systemic versus personal racism—make white and black viewers alike feel the anguish of Strike and Victor. The Gran Fury as predatory law, the slave-block-style police shakedown watched by Strike's mother, and Rocco seeing only his own reflection in Victor's eye illustrate Heideggerian thrownness and self-love-as-racism. Invoking Peirce's 'evolutionary love' (Radio Raheem's Right Hand/Left Hand speech), Rorty's renarrativization of who counts as 'white,' and Dewey's 'art is more moral than moralities,' Gilmore casts Lee as a pragmatist renarrativizing hate into love.

thrownness.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
thrownness.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
thrownness.relation: David Hart explains Batman's origin through Heidegger's Being and Time: Bruce Wayne is a 'thrown-project' whose world (like Alfred's butlering) shows up through chosen possibilities. Witnessing his parents' murder confronts Bruce with Angst and being-toward-death, and in Miller's Year One the bat crashing through the window lets him authentically choose 'I shall become a bat.' Hart argues this dissolves the free-will/determinism binary - Bruce's choice is neither causally compelled by trauma nor wholly unconditioned, but an authentic self-determination amid thrown possibilities.

thrownness.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
thrownness.title: NOTES
thrownness.relation: Jeremy Barris argues that Lost dramatizes the structure of life itself, using Heidegger's claim that the inquirer's own being is the clue to all questions and his notion of 'thrownness' to read the castaways' accidental arrival as a mirror of our own bewildering birth into circumstances we did not make. He reframes the show's central puzzle as 'the question of life after birth,' contends against Sartre and Camus that life is neither fully sensible nor fully absurd but a half-understood riddle, and invokes Wittgenstein's On Certainty to show that total doubt is impossible because understanding senselessness presupposes understanding something.

thrownness.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
thrownness.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
thrownness.relation: Hartmann argues the specialty-coffee 'third wave' (Stumptown, Intelligentsia, Counter Culture) could not exist without Starbucks, which taught consumers to pay for a boldly-roasted, ethically-branded, self-gifting aesthetic under neoliberalism. Drawing on Heidegger's thrownness and Gadamer's hermeneutical phenomenology, he punctures Nicholas Cho's claim that the third wave 'lets the coffee speak for itself': just as we perceive a chair as for-sitting through pre-given cultural meaning, cupping rituals actively build a coffee 'hermeneutic' that reshapes the drinker's very perception (the trained palate 'tastes' plantain and graham cracker). He likens this to ventriloquism—the coffee only 'speaks' because someone feeds it its lines—and uses Žižek's account of cynical ideology to expose the gap between fair-trade branding and reality.

thrownness.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
thrownness.title: 1. Frankenstein
thrownness.relation: Using the De Niro monster of Branagh's Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, Rowlands argues absurdity arises from a clash between the view of ourselves from the inside (a locus of meaning) and from the outside (sub specie aeternitatis, insignificant). The monster is assembled from second-hand parts and thrown into a hostile world he did not choose, just as we are stitched together by genes and environment we did not choose (Sartre/Heidegger thrownness). He develops Camus's Myth of Sisyphus, arguing the horror is futility not difficulty, to frame the problem of the meaning of life that underlies every deep philosophical problem.

thrownness.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
thrownness.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
thrownness.relation: Hart uses Heidegger's Being and Time to explain Batman beyond the free-will/determinism binary. Dasein is a "thrown-project" always being-toward-death; Alfred's world of trays and clocks illustrates the interpretive horizon of a chosen life. Witnessing his parents' murder confronts Bruce Wayne with Angst and his own finitude, and — as in Miller's Year One, where a bat crashes through the window and he decides "I shall become a bat" — he authentically chooses his crime-fighting mission rather than being mechanically driven by trauma or vengeance.

thrownness.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
thrownness.title: 73. Hasan Minhaj as Philosopher Navigating the Struggles of Identity
thrownness.relation: Singh reads Minhaj's comedy of identity through existentialism, arguing his call for 'authenticity' over the first generation's 'assimilation' (the 'American dream tax' and 'biryani' arguments about choosing one's life) enacts Sartre's existence-precedes-essence and rejection of bad faith. He frames Minhaj's Indian-American-Muslim conflict via Heidegger's thrownness and facticity and the move from the they-self (das Man) to authentic self, contrasting it with Sartre's facticity as a limit on freedom. Minhaj's 'global citizen' anti-nationalism, his 'love is bigger than fear,' and 'may the best argument win' are presented as prescriptions for navigating national, ethnic, religious and personal identity while flagging fallacies like hasty generalization behind Islamophobia.

thrownness.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
thrownness.title: Welcome Aboard the TARDIS—It’s Bigger on the Inside
thrownness.relation: The author argues that Doctor Who functions as a 'great educator' that shapes viewers' reality and their conception of the good life, framing our birth into the world as being 'thrown' into a new environment we must assimilate. He applies Hegel's historical dialectic to the Doctor-versus-Daleks conflict, treating the Doctor (wisdom, liberty, compassion) and the Daleks (obedience, hatred, conquest) as opposing theses whose ongoing struggle synthesizes the wider universe's fear of the Daleks. Drawing on Carroll and Danesi, he claims pop culture like Doctor Who validates experience and creates collective structures of meaning, and that our chosen first Doctor becomes the interpretive framework through which we judge every later one.

objectification.book: 003 - The Matrix and Philosophy - Welcome to the Desert of the Real
objectification.title: Unknown
objectification.relation: The chapter catalogues the film's penetration scenes—the Agents' scorpion bug forced through Neo's navel, its bloody extraction, the fetal pod farm and 'birth' down the flush tube, the acupuncture rebuilding, the neck-plug uploads, and finally the bullets he becomes immune to—arguing that Neo's arc ends in a perfect, closed body with no vulnerability and no relation to actual flesh. It attacks the gender stereotypes: Trinity is reduced to a decorative, nurturant sidekick who never hacks and exists as love interest, the Oracle is a cookie-baking 'Mammy' figure, and there are no female Agents—the machines are sexist too.

objectification.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
objectification.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Cynthia Freeland reads the film's women through feminist ethics of care: the two Marys function like a Greek-chorus of grieving observers, while Claudia and Veronica — and the casting of Bellucci as the repentant whore opposite Morgenstern's ageless Madonna — lock them into the virgin/whore double bind. Using Carol Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg's Kantian standard and Nel Noddings's and Sara Ruddick's point that mothering is reflective 'attentive' work, she argues Gibson's Mary is one-dimensional: flashbacks of 'I am here' show maternal instinct, never moral deliberation. She ends by suggesting the historical Jesus, like Socrates, was more radical toward women than the film, and that Irigaray's reading of Christ's bleeding wounds as a feminized maternal body sits oddly with Gibson's muscular, 'take it like a man' Savior.

objectification.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
objectification.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
objectification.relation: A café dialogue pits second-waver Marie against third-waver Dorothy over whether Atkins can be a feminist tool: Marie wields the feminist critique of Cartesian dualism (Descartes made the mind essential and the body animal, and women were stigmatized as body), Foucault's internalized surveillance — 'every mirror becomes a guard, every scale an alarm,' with Lifetime Maintenance as 'maniacal' hyper-vigilance — Lorde's 'master's tools,' and Young's 'Throwing Like a Girl.' Dorothy answers with Our Bodies, Ourselves self-knowledge, Title IX athletes like Venus and Serena Williams, Frye's Willful Virgin, and existentialist facticity and bad faith (we are in bad faith when we abdicate control), defending dieting as a chosen women's project. The exchange ends drawish, over Brazilian waxes, French women, and whether ugliness is a feminist virtue.

objectification.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
objectification.title: The Possibility of Authenticity The Life We Choose
objectification.relation: Gines reads hip hop's sexual imagery through Black feminist thought - Tupac's feud with C. Delores Tucker over "Wonder Why They Call U Bitch", Patricia Hill Collins's controlling images of the jezebel and welfare mother, bell hooks on the slave-rooted devaluation of Black womanhood, Nelly's "Tip Drill" video with a credit card swiped between a woman's buttocks, Jay-Z's "Big Pimpin'". Applying Sartre's keyhole gaze from Being and Nothingness and his Anti-Semite and Jew point about hierarchical societies, she argues the gaze under racism and sexism is non-reciprocal - women are seen without seeing - and that Lil' Kim's reversal of it reinforces rather than subverts the stereotypes; Butler's gender performativity then frames the closing Sartrean choice of authenticity or inauthenticity, Nas's "I Can" and "the life we choose."

objectification.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
objectification.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Kieffner applies Foucault's deployment of sexuality to show how power centers constructed biker sexual stereotypes: the psychiatric profession behind Time's 1970 'Motorcycle Syndrome', the press that sexualized the Van Buren sisters and filled Easyriders with centerfolds, police 'gauntlets' that pull over bikes but not cars (and ask Raw Thunder's Char Zack if she is a lesbian), and even Harley-Davidson's own 'mystique' video deploying eroticism to sell bikes and HOG memberships. Following Foucault's rule of the tactical polyvalence of discourse, he ends with resistance within the same power structure: riders' rights organizations videotaping police encounters, and the tactical discourses of queer, lesbian, and female riders, from Evelyn Greenway's 1921 'Do it with a motorcycle' onward, who refuse the labels of sexual outlaw and gender traitor.

objectification.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
objectification.title: The Male Vampire as Metrosexual . . . Sort Of
objectification.relation: Joan Grassbaugh Forry asks how conventional standards of beauty, femininity, and masculinity operate in the vampire aesthetic of Interview with the Vampire, Buffy, and Queen of the Damned. Using Foucault's figure of the soldier whose body is 'made' by discipline, and Bartky and Bordo's feminist extension of it to dieting, deportment, and ornamenting the female body, she argues vampires expose the ideology of natural beauty: they are youthful, elegant, and effortlessly beautiful - no gym, no reflection - so their beauty is pure naturalness with the discipline erased. Gender decides the payoff: ultra-feminine female vampires (Drusilla's dresses and tea parties, Akasha, childlike Claudia) are femmes fatales whose threat must be punished by death, ridicule, or infantilization, while feminized male protagonists (Louis, Angel, Spike painting his nails and watching Passions - the 'metrosexual') win audience identification and tragic dignity. Beauty, in short, is a shield for the male vampire and a death sentence for the female.

objectification.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
objectification.title: James Bond and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Arp and Decker examine Bond's objectification of women - using a dancing girl as a human shield in the Goldfinger pre-credits sequence, M ordering Bond to 'pump her for information' - through three moral theories. Kant's humanity formula condemns treating women as sexual tools, but Kantian autonomy generates a stalemate since consensual, reciprocal liaisons like Bond and Anya Amasova's might qualify as permissible; Millian utilitarianism condemns the male gaze by its long-term social costs yet stalls against pro-sex feminist counterarguments. They settle on Aristotelian virtue ethics - the mean between extremes, with respect as the key virtue against the power-centered virtue of Machiavelli, Hobbes, and Nietzsche - to argue objectification is vicious, and they trace Bond's moral progress from skipping the young Bibi in For Your Eyes Only to the reciprocal relationships with Kara Milovy, Pam Bouvier, Wai Lin, and Jinx.

objectification.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
objectification.title: This Has All Happened Before and It Will All Happen Again
objectification.relation: Rennes reads the miniseries opening — Six's kiss of death with the Armistice officer — through postcolonial theory: Vergès's 'colonial family romance,' in which the human metropole adopts Cylons as perpetually subordinate children, and Bhabha's ambivalence and mimicry ('almost the same, but not quite'). The humans police difference first by appearance (toaster, skin-job slurs; the Centurion reflected in Helo's toaster) and then by blood, but métissage — Hera, whom Roslin tries to abort and then hides — exposes the categories as social constructions, since as D'Anna says, 'This stuff all looks the same.' Hera's menace is that acknowledging her means acknowledging human complicity in creating Cylon slaves, collapsing the colonial romance ('happily never after').

objectification.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
objectification.title: The Secret Plot of ‘Baby Boomers’
objectification.relation: Chess proposes that BSG is 'a narrative about queer reproduction,' combining Haraway's cyborg with Butler's heteronormativity to coin 'technoqueer': Cylons embody fears that technology makes heterosexual reproduction unnecessary. Helo's 'I'm in love with a woman I know isn't a woman,' the 'you can't rape a machine' debate after the Pegasus assault, and download-resurrection as asexual reproduction all mark Cylons as queer others — yet the Cylons' obsession with conceiving Hera, paralleled with The L Word's Bette and Tina, shows them trapped between rejecting and emulating heteronormativity, farming human women at the Cylon 'Farm' while craving legitimate babies. Hera's birth terrifies Roslin because it legitimizes the technoqueer and with it human reproductive obsolescence.

objectification.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
objectification.title: It’s the Disappointing Stories that Sound True to Life
objectification.relation: Shipman argues that the re-imagined Cylons, having rebelled as slaves, recreated oppression inside their own society: the human-form Numbers rule over mute Centurions (voices literally bred out, like banning slave literacy), animalized Raiders, and dismissed 'insane' Hybrids, whose sentience ('Scar' shows strategy and self-preservation) the Numbers willfully deny. The division of labor echoes Marx's 'from each according to his ability,' but assignments are engineered by their makers, and the model-making program is eugenics rather than evolution — the series' own word 'evolved' is, he says, disingenuous. Hence the Numbers lose the moral superiority their victimhood earned, and the scriptural 'all of this has happened before' implies the subaltern models may rebel next.

objectification.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
objectification.title: With or Without Starbuck
objectification.relation: Ewan Kirkland argues BSG's gender-free surface, unisex bunks and a Starbuck who never has to defend her right to fly, masks a default masculinity under Adama's patriarchal regime: Ellen is killed off as the negative femme fatale, Kat and Cain die or turn monstrous, and 'The Farm' literalizes feminist fears of patriarchal medicine turning women into breeders. Starbuck confounds the sexualizing male gaze, never objectified, repeatedly rescuing men and reversing damsel-in-distress plots, yet her success is entirely masculinized, bought by becoming like a man. Her New Caprica captivity as Leoben's simulated wife literalizes the feminist critique of compulsory heterosexuality, and her death in 'Maelstrom', submitting to her former kidnapper, suggests the series contains its most transgressive heroine.

objectification.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
objectification.title: Zelda and Reality
objectification.relation: Havstad and Jahng inventory every Zelda across the series (royal, wise, resolved, foreseeing, yet passive, imprisoned, even turned to stone in The Minish Cap or asleep through all of Adventure of Link) and read the maiden typology through Beauvoir's The Second Sex: woman as Idea, modeled on Plato's Forms, gives men a feminine ideal that real women are then judged against, and 'women are not born, but made' explains how femininity is a male-defined myth serving male interests. Zelda is the glorified yet objectified prize whose passivity lets Link's transcendence happen, and Aonuma's 'reality over realism' design philosophy explains why such stereotypes feel true to players. Sheik and Tetra, who act while disguised as (or turned into) something other than the princess, are the promising cracks in the ideal.

objectification.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
objectification.title: I’m Gonna Crawl
objectification.relation: Richard Wilson and Emma Rees apply Freud's theory of fetishism—the boy's disavowal of castration displaced onto a substitute object—to Zeppelin's lyrics and imagery. 'Trampled Underfoot' continues Robert Johnson's 'Terraplane Blues' car-as-lover convention, 'Custard Pie' and 'Black Dog' turn women into consumable food (Freud's cannibalistic pregenital sexual organization), and 'The Lemon Song' and 'Whole Lotta Love' avert the castrating vagina, with the Seattle red snapper episode read through the vagina dentata myth. The band's misogyny ('Soul of a woman was created below' in 'Dazed and Confused', echoing Lear), the voyeuristic die-cut windows of the Physical Graffiti cover, and Plant's cock-rock persona in The Song Remains the Same all illustrate how fetishistic substitution neutralizes the threatening female body and explains the band's compulsive doomed-relationship songs; the authors briefly borrow Marx's language of commodification for the woman-car-drugs as status objects.

objectification.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
objectification.title: Looking Inwards
objectification.relation: Barber, Bryce, and Davis test Donna Haraway's emancipatory cyborg thesis against Gunslinger Girl, where the Social Welfare Agency 'adopts' orphaned and abused girls (Henrietta, Rico, Triela, Elsa, Claes), rebuilds their bodies as cybernetic weapons, and drug-conditions them into loyal assassins paired with male handlers. They argue the series realizes none of Haraway's post-gender potential: conditioning erodes memory and autonomy (Rico coolly shoots the porter Emilio who befriended her; Elsa murders her handler Lauro and kills herself; Triela suffers pointless menstrual cramps in a wombless body), while the girls' kawaii styling, teddy bears, and school uniforms make them objects of the male gaze whose cuteness disguises lethal power. The cyborgs' victimization ultimately reinforces traditional gender hierarchy and mirrors conformity-pressured Japanese youth, so the cyborg has 'regressed' from the autonomous heroines of Ghost in the Shell or Battle Angel Alita.

objectification.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
objectification.title: Textually Transmitted Disease
objectification.relation: Traces hentai from Hokusai's 'Diver and Two Octopi' through the 1920s eroguro journals to the Lolita Anime and Cream Lemon OVAs, then asks whether even this extreme material has value as fantasy. The chapter frames the media-effects debate with Aristotle's Poetics catharsis (revived by Feshbach and tentatively supported by Milton Diamond's finding that Japanese rape rates fell as pornography spread) against Plato's Republic worry that sensational works license irrationality (updated by the Disinhibition, Desensitization, and Cultivation theories), and concludes that hentai's real harm is attitudinal rather than behavioral: its ritual 'breaking' of strong women and sex-as-something-done-to-passive-girls cultivates misogyny and a dehumanizing view of sex.

objectification.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
objectification.title: Banal Sex
objectification.relation: Marinucci reads The Onion's sex coverage as 'terminally ambiguous': 'Nation's Gays Demand Right To Library Cards,' 'Massachusetts Supreme Court Orders All Citizens To Gay Marry,' and 'New Bill Would Defend Marriage From Sharks' ridicule the idea that gay marriage threatens straight marriage, while 'Area Homosexual Saves Four From Fire: Heroic Neighbor Praised, Gay' exposes how heterosexism defines gay people sexually while heterosexual men pass as normal, natural, and neutral. Yet the paper also trades in gay stereotypes and mocks the very framework—characters like Amanda Oppel ('Lesbian Identity Ends Abruptly Mid-Junior Year'), the 'Bar Skanks Announce Plans To Kiss,' and Bruce Heffernan of 'Why Do All These Homosexuals Keep Sucking My Cock?' both defy and seem to reaffirm the stability of sexual identity categories. Weighing queer theory (via Jagose) and Golden's fluid 'elective lesbians' against the parody of 'Grad Student Deconstructs Take-Out Menu,' she concludes the paper's stance is deliberately undecidable, perhaps recommending we stop over-thinking sex and treat minority sexual identities as banal, as in 'Gay Couple Has Banal Sex.'

objectification.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
objectification.title: Specimen Watching
objectification.relation: Jason Davis applies Adorno's 'identity thinking' - the way concepts swallow particulars as specimens of the already-known - to argue Dexter is a consumer of serial killers who never asks what makes his victims what they are, only that they fit the type, from therapist Emmett Meridian on down. The same concept-machine works on animals: Buddy's buried bones and the show's predator imagery exploit the criminological animal-abuse link, letting Davis ask whether cruelty-taskforce laws quietly practice speciesism; and Carol J. Adams' sexual politics of meat connects the Ice Truck Killer's blood-drained, butcher-cut women to a meat-eating culture whose objectification makes women and animals interchangeable. Finally, the chapter notes that the women of Dexter - Deb, Rita, LaGuerta, Lila, Christine - are all written without female friendship, a homosocial specimen-class whose sameness feminist philosophers expose, so that when Dexter 'takes back the night', the 'invisible hookers' stay invisible.

objectification.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
objectification.title: The Honorable, the Woman
objectification.relation: Mona Rocha and James Rocha charge that Holmes's 'deduction' is really Humean induction, and that his inductive shortcuts about women, tricking Mrs. Smith in The Sign of the Four, reading Mary Sutherland's pacing as a love affair, and dismissing Lady Frances Carfax as a 'stray chicken in a world of foxes', are hasty generalizations made dangerous by gender stereotype. Watson is worse: his 'experience of women... over many nations and three continents' reads Mary Morstan's soul off her face and grants full courtesy only to the beautiful intruder of 'The Solitary Cyclist', a feminist case study in objectification. Irene Adler's escape in 'A Scandal in Bohemia', disguising herself as a young man and outwitting the fire ruse, is Doyle's deliberate proof that treating women as a class fails, making her a proto-feminist decades before Poirot's Rossakoff or Spade's O'Shaughnessy.

objectification.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
objectification.title: Deckard versus Arctor
objectification.relation: The chapter sets Ford's redemptive Deckard against Keanu Reeves's Bob Arctor, the everyman who spies on himself and disintegrates on Substance D, noting the shared scaffolding (lawman, shadowy supplier Tyrell/New Path, nemesis with doubtful humanity, woman in identity crisis) that only highlights the divergence: Deckard is educated into humanity through Rachael while Arctor is progressively dehumanized, with Donna/Audrey betraying rather than redeeming him. It leans on Dick's 'The Android and the Human' definition of becoming an android as being 'pounded down, manipulated, made into a means without one's knowledge or consent', so that Blade Runner imagines androids becoming human where A Scanner Darkly shows humans becoming androids, with even nature (New Path's corn fields) enlisted in the enslavement.

objectification.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
objectification.title: Violence, Rock, and the Rolling Stones
objectification.relation: Applying the three orders, Surber sorts the Stones' violences: Imaginary violence flows from frustrated desire — 'you can't ever get what you want' — heard in 'Play with Fire' and the unnervingly threatening last line of 'Dead Flowers', and in the frenzied fan mobs that nearly killed Keith once Decca made him a spectacle. Symbolic violence is carried by words and images, and he charges the lyrics with two standing varieties: the objectification of women in 'Under My Thumb' and racial stereotyping in 'Brown Sugar' and the N-word quoted in 'Sweet Black Angel'. Behind both, the Real's economics quietly enables the whole scene, since concert violence is unintelligible apart from the transfer of millions of fans' small cash payments into record-corporation accounts.

objectification.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
objectification.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Olson opens with her own first session, in which the DM steered her toward a 'sexy Eladrin' miniature in high heels, and asks why women stay away from D&D. She argues the game's mechanics are egalitarian—identical power lists for male and female characters, echoing Plato's Republic claim that women guard the city by the same nature as men—and that party cooperation embodies the relational, care-based feminist ethic Marilyn Friedman and Angela Bolte oppose to male-coded individualism. The trouble is culture, not system: sexualized miniatures that objectify female bodies, tokenism, harassment, and marketing that ignores women, to which female gamers respond by playing male characters like Jenni Dowsett, designing separatist systems such as Portal Worlds, or, like Shelly Mazzanoble, claiming D&D for the 'inner girl'.

objectification.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
objectification.title: The Devil and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Jones, Hansmann, and Stachura trace the trope of woman as the Devil's handmaiden - Eve and Lilith, succubae and Sirens, the sixteenth-century witch hunts, down to 'maneater' and 'Poison' rock songs and Blurred Lines - arguing it perpetuates patriarchal power. They apply Beauvoir's The Second Sex: woman constructed as the perpetual Other, defined as secondary to man with sexuality at the heart of her Othering, and extend the analysis with Gloria Anzaldua's Borderlands and mestiza consciousness, which rejects the gender binary the woman-as-Devil trope depends on.

objectification.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
objectification.title: Girls and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Mahon and Walker rebrand the seven deadly sins for Girls: Self-Absorption as Augustine's 'love of one's own excellence' (Hannah pitching her e-book at her editor's funeral, calling her grandmother 'the old Flo Job... sluttin' around'), Entitlement for Hannah's 'voice of my generation' demands and Marnie's rage at Charlie's success, and Sleeping Around as the John Paul II point about reducing a person to an object of gratification - Adam's fantasy sex with Hannah and his degradation of Natalia. Envy (Hannah on Tally's tragedy), gluttony in drug-fueled relapses (Aquinas's five ways), flakiness as Kant's indolent free-rider who needs others but never helps (Jessa missing her own abortion), and Senecan irritability (Jessa spitting at the Bushwick party, Ray's hatreds, Shoshanna's 'whiny nothings' outburst) complete the survey - redeemed by the girls' stubborn friendship.

objectification.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
objectification.title: Girls and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Adleberg asks whether Jessa is right that she is not 'the ladies.' Against Shoshanna's common-sense biological determinism and pop-neuroscience like Brizendine's 'male brain' (refuted via brain plasticity and Fausto-Sterling), she deploys Butler's point that identity categories are always normative and exclusionary (Marnie's 'that's what men do' to Charlie) and Beauvoir's and Spelman's social constructionism - mothers already treating infants differently - to show gender is made, not born. With Haslanger's call to resist unjust gender meanings, she concludes that neither conforming (Marnie craving dominant Booth Jonathan) nor defying stereotypes (Jessa's bathroom sex, 'what if I want to feel like I have udders?') should be compulsory; only objectifying harm, as with Adam and Natalia, is wrong.

objectification.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
objectification.title: Justified and Philosophy
objectification.relation: The chapter surveys Harlan's gendered violence - Ava's killing of Bowman, the routine roughing-up of Audrey's working girls, Robert Quarles's childhood prostitution - and uses Catharine MacKinnon's account of patriarchal power imbalance to explain victim-blaming, underreporting, and police disbelief of trauma responses in domestic-violence and rape cases. On prostitution it weighs sex-positive feminism against the objectification worry, concluding via Teri's line about 'sucking hillbilly dicks for money' that Audrey's women have little real choice even under Ava's management. Finally it brings in bell hooks's third-wave point that oppression cannot be split from race and class, plus Peggy McIntosh's invisible backpack of white privilege, to read Noble's Holler's isolation and the bombed black church as evidence that patriarchy in Justified is always also racial and economic.

objectification.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
objectification.title: 17. Sin, My Young Man, Is When You Treat People as Things
objectification.relation: Taking Granny Weatherwax's definition that sin 'is when you treat people as things' and Vetinari's that sin is not saying no to evil, the chapter reads Discworld through C. S. Lewis's argument that a universal Law of Human Nature—felt on the Disc by dwarfs, trolls, and even atheists—points to a divine lawgiver. The enchanted wolf in Witches Abroad, whose agony every witch intuits as wrong and who is granted a merciful death and human funeral, shows that shared moral intuition at work, and grounds the chapter's notes on Pratchett's own campaign for assisted dying. Finally, the Assassins' Guild, which only inhumes the rich who can afford bodyguards under its motto nil mortifi sine lucre, illustrates John Paul II's 'structures of sin': killing sanctified by contract and city law, treating people as things.

objectification.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
objectification.title: 11. Leda, Castor, and Their Families
objectification.relation: Shows how the clones queer the normative family: clones as such are "biological outlaws" (via Stephanie Turner's reading of Ripley in Alien), Siobhan turns out to be the genetic half-sister of the clones cloned from her own mother Kendall, and the chosen family — Felix the "brother sestra," Kira's aunties, Helena's dream baby shower — repeatedly rebuilds kinship outside blood and marriage. Against this stands the stripping of reproductive agency: the infertility sequence written into the Leda clones, Coady's weaponized sterilizing virus, and above all Helena, whose eggs are harvested and implanted by Henrik and Gracie's father without consent. The chapter's conclusion is that Orphan Black's blood families are abusive and controlling while the non-normative chosen families of Clone Club are where love and consent actually live.

objectification.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
objectification.title: 17. Sex, Consent, and Rape in Westeros
objectification.relation: Underwood distinguishes the legal consent of fifteenth-century-style Westeros - under the conjugal-debt doctrine neither Drogo nor Ramsay legally raped their wives, while every Cersei-Jaime union was treasonous regardless of desire - from the moral standard of consent developed from Alan Wertheimer's work. Applying his fraud and disregard cases, she argues Sansa's marriage obtained through Littlefinger's deception and Daenerys's coerced early nights with Drogo are immoral though legal, and proposes 'reciprocal subjectivity' as the criterion: Ramsay treats Sansa purely as an object, but the scene at Joffrey's body shows Jaime raping Cersei while still loving her as a subject, proving mutual recognition is necessary yet not sufficient for morally permissible sex.

objectification.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
objectification.title: 17. Wade Wilson Fights Like a Girl
objectification.relation: Staged as a Socratic dialogue in a professor's office, the chapter tests Peter Coogan's definition of the superhero (mission, powers, identity) against the Deadpool movie and finds Wade qualifies while mocking the genre. It then argues the film subverts the superhero genre's sexist conventions: Vanessa refuses the damsel role by grabbing the bar mercenary's crotch and later skewering Francis herself, Angel Dust knocks Colossus out, and Negasonic Teenage Warhead is 'a damsel to the rescue.' Applying Laura Mulvey's male gaze, it shows the camera lingering on Deadpool's body and adopting Vanessa's viewpoint in the Calendar Girl scene, with the Women in Refrigerators trope, Gwen Stacy's death, and the Hawkeye Initiative as evidence of what the movie overturns.

objectification.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
objectification.title: 6 Wives and Husbands The Marital Power Struggle
objectification.relation: Taking Susan Okin's 'the personal is political' and Kate Millett's Weberian herrschaft against Locke's public/private dichotomy, the chapter reviews the empirical studies of marital power (Blood and Wolfe, Blumstein and Schwarz, Steil) and finds money is the master base in marriage: the husband's income and occupational prestige set his say, working wives gain power but couples conspire to understate wives' earnings ('manning up and womaning down'), while knowledge and status are the next strongest resources. Authority from religion, tradition and morality still favors husbands (Ephesians' 'wives submit yourselves unto your husbands' alongside the philosophers' 'abler and stronger'), violence persists from the rule of thumb to marital rape and murder despite legal change, housework remains women's burden - Beauvoir's never-won 'battle against dust', Engels's 'leaden boredom', Davis's industrialization proposal and Okin's demand that it be shared - and sex itself works as a power base in the bedroom, with MacKinnon diagnosing heterosexuality as the linchpin of gender inequality. The chapter ends with black couples' comparatively egalitarian patterns traced by Angela Davis to slave-quarters equality, Schwarz's rare 'peer marriages', and the Marxist (Okin, the Swedish model) versus liberal (Wilson, the Japanese model) readings of family change.

objectification.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
objectification.title: 9. But Women Can Vote . .
objectification.relation: Hansmann and Jones set Adams's gender posts against the four waves of feminism and the men's rights movement: his March 2011 Men's Rights post telling activists to get over it while lumping women with four-year-olds and the mentally handicapped, his Global Gender War matriarchy in which any country where women can vote counts as female-ruled, his framing of sex as a woman's currency for extracting male strategy (sacrifice a pawn to nail the queen), and his serial interrupting of women. They show the rhetoric eerily echoes anti-suffragists like Mrs. William Force Scott and Senator Sanford and the Goldilocks Dilemma, note the red-pill fantasy borrowed from The Matrix, and conclude that calling America a matriarchy defies scholarly consensus, with Beauvoir's The Second Sex marking why the vote never delivered the balance of power.

objectification.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
objectification.title: 3. Laura Palmer—Madonna and Whore
objectification.relation: Applies Freud's Madonna-whore complex — "where such men love, they have no desire, and where they desire, they cannot love" — to Laura Palmer's split between homecoming queen/Meals on Wheels volunteer and cocaine-prostitute, arguing the contradiction exists only in a mindset that forces women into two poles, which BOB weaponizes with his "dirty and sleazy" refrain. The chapter surveys explanations of the complex (incest fear, paternity anxiety, alpha-male identity visible in Leo and Jacques), and then indicts the Fireman as a feminist "nice guy": his Part 8 creation of Laura as a golden orb of purity sent to redeem the world of the Bomb is the ultimate Madonna role, a Christ-like burden that is what makes her the target BOB must debase. Even her friends' names — Maddie and Donna — spell Madonna.

objectification.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
objectification.title: 15. Are There Certain Things We Should Not Talk About
objectification.relation: Reads Schumer's taboo-breaking through The Second Sex: man makes woman the mysterious Other, and silences around menstruation, aging, and wives' desire keep that mystery intact. 'Last Fuckable Day' dramatizes the expiry of the idolized 'real woman', 'Sex Prep' shows the metamorphosis into a sex-representation collapsing into hiding under the bed, and '12 Angry Men' stages a male jury defining a woman's value. Ehrnberger argues Schumer's demystifying candor, from publishing her teenage journals to calling herself a 'flawed fuckup', dissolves the Other's aura and restores power, exactly as Beauvoir predicted when women assert themselves as human beings.

objectification.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
objectification.title: 17. Switching It Up
objectification.relation: Argues Trainwreck and the stand-up material on sexual 'ownership' expose patriarchal double standards: the same promiscuity that makes men players makes women sluts, while LeBron James's gossipy, overprotective best friend and John Cena's devoted, unthreatening boyfriend cast male stars in traditional rom-com female roles. Browning brings in Kant's view that sexual desire treats persons as objects to be discarded like squeezed lemons, conceding that counting conquests objectifies partners while rejecting Kant's celibate conclusion. Schumer's comedy instead shows women owning their orgasms, turning sex from competition into mutual gratification.

objectification.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
objectification.title: 19. How to Feel Pretty
objectification.relation: A satirical monologue voiced by 'The Patriarchy' that catalogs women's impossible, contradictory beauty demands: a painted face that must look natural, effortless long hair, a body that is simultaneously too fat and too thin, sexual availability that must never look eager, accomplishments that are unattractive, and finally a pretty death. The screed makes vivid that the standards exist only to keep women judging themselves as garbage, nailing the dynamic with Schumer-specific gags like 'Milk Milk Lemonade' as both a women-are-people reminder and a butt showcase, and Amy's 'catch a dick' line, before mocking workplace 'merit' talk that promotes Jim.

objectification.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
objectification.title: 9. Machines Who Care
objectification.relation: Weiss reads 'The Lonely' and 'I Sing the Body Electric' as anticipations of today's debate over 'relational artifacts' — Turkle's sociable robots, the Sparrows' claim that robotic aged care is unethical, Coeckelbergh's rebuttal — asking, with Anne, whether an electric grandma 'doesn't sound so good.' Corry's Alicia and the children's electric grandma show care being bought as an assembly-line product for the lonely, and he presses the details: why the caring robots are female and serve water, why Alicia arrives in a box and is summarily shot in the face when no longer needed, and what it says about a culture that maroons people in loneliness and then sells the technical fix.

objectification.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
objectification.title: Back to the Rough Ground!
objectification.relation: Finnegan uses Wittgenstein's language games, the 'picture' that holds us captive, and 'back to the rough ground' to argue that Ford, Sizemore, and the Man in Black are paralyzed by an idealized, patriarchal picture of narrative (winners and losers, violence, transcendent self-discovery), while Dolores and Maeve gain traction by inventing new language games within their forms of life. Dolores breaks her damsel script in Pariah ('I imagined a story where I didn't have to be the damsel') and reworks scripted love-dialogue to describe her grief, while Maeve bullies the lab techs, takes administrative control, and narrates other hosts' actions - 'Time to write my own fucking story.' The chapter reads their objectified position (via Mulvey's male gaze, which leaves female viewers identifying with the robot hosts rather than the male subject) as exactly what equips them for guerrilla warfare in the master's language games, doing what Audre Lorde thought impossible: dismantling the master's house with the master's tools.

objectification.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
objectification.title: In Closing, The Naked Truth
objectification.relation: Meyer sorts Westworld's abundant nudity into three aesthetic registers. First, Kenneth Clark's nude: Dolores's opening chair pose and the perfected, fabricated host bodies are idealized, created art-forms serving the creators' control. Second, John Berger's analysis of the nude as spectacle of male dominance: the Man in Black watching Armistice bathe (a Susannah-and-the-Elders voyeurism), the gold-painted women at El Lazo's orgy as 'nudity as a form of dress' for male desire, and techs' 'fuck puppet' treatment of Maeve, which she reverses by re-appropriating the language of fucking. Third, Leo Steinberg's incarnation symbolism: host nudity signals machines becoming human - shameless like prelapsarian Adam and Eve, mortal and sexed, 'ensouled' - so that Maeve overriding her programming to reclaim her daughter is the birth of the human-host, the mirror-image of God becoming man.

objectification.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
objectification.title: Resisting Dystopia
objectification.relation: The editor's introduction argues that The Handmaid's Tale disturbs us because it shows how tenuous our civil liberties are, so we must actively watch political events for warning signs. It insists that a woman's value is not fixed by her body, fertility, or attractiveness—Handmaids are treated as incubators and commodities—and that the caring work women do is a power, not a weakness. It closes on the lesson that facts, not politicians, control the narrative, ending with 'Nolite te bastardes carborundorum.'

objectification.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
objectification.title: 7. She Went Down Swingin’
objectification.relation: Volpert argues Tom Petty was a feminist, the only classic-rock male whose catalog consistently grants women rational equality and agency, adopting Susan McClary's feminist New Musicology as her lens and marching through Greatest Hits song by song. She reads the forced removal of the Lolita cover from "American Girl," the consensual, threat-free request of "Breakdown," and "Listen to Her Heart" as Petty's reply to Ike Turner's cocaine-locked party, and defends "You Got Lucky" as a conceit about band technology rather than misogyny. The chapter confronts the gaze directly, arguing "Here Comes My Girl" watches a woman walking toward you as formidable rather than objectified, with the video's flirtations redirected homoerotically at the Heartbreakers themselves.

objectification.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
objectification.title: 22. Rachael, Weeping for Her Children
objectification.relation: Bonnie McLean maps Baudrillard's four-stage precession of simulacra onto the women of 2049: Joshi anchors reality, implanted memories distort it, Joi is representation masking the absence of reality, and the eye-color-wrong reconstructed Rachael is a simulacrum of a simulacrum bearing no relation to reality. Read this way, the film lionizes birth — Wallace kissing the replicant he has just disemboweled, her blood running down her legs — while stripping every woman of agency in service of K's quest, a dynamic the chapter links to pro-life politics and DACA-era savior narratives. Only by removing K from the narrative, she shows, does the women's erasure become visible.

objectification.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
objectification.title: 23. The Future Is Female … Robots!
objectification.relation: Emily Cox-Palmer-White applies Deleuze and Guattari's 'becoming-woman' to the mechanical women of both films: the girl as universal other, a vacuum or absence at the center of femininity, is exactly what lets Rachael, Pris, Luv, and Joi destabilize the patriarchal world that manufactured them. Wallace's drones undressing the barren replicant with their gaze before he slashes her womb gives the male gaze a literal, lethal form, while the Joi-Mariette sync scene stages the frightening interchangeability of women under that gaze. Deckard's 'Her eyes were green' — a lie, since Rachael's eyes were brown — refuses the premise that women are replaceable products.

objectification.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
objectification.title: 25. Less Human than Human
objectification.relation: Leah Schade and Emily Askew read replicants as undocumented Latinx immigrants: Sapper's grub farm parallels an ICE raid on a meatpacking plant and the deportation cell of 'Justo', blade runners mirror enforcement agents hunting 'illegals', and the miracle child maps onto DACA Dreamers whom well-meaning liberals recast as superhuman saviors at the cost of their ordinary personhood. Using Mary Midgley's personhood criteria — the ability to suffer, emotional fellowship, minding what happens to one — they argue replicants, like migrants, plainly qualify, and that 'illegality' is a constructed status, not a moral fact. The chapter warns that messianic sacrifice narratives, however sympathetic, re-objectify the very people they mean to defend.

objectification.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
objectification.title: 12. An Intimate Look at Paul Stanley’s Love
objectification.relation: Robert Grant Price maps Paul Stanley's catalogue onto four loves. Eros as soulmate-love follows Aristophanes' split-beings myth from Plato's Symposium ('Forever,' 'Every Time I Look at You'); self-love follows Aquinas's demand that it be 'rightly ordered,' so Stanley's machismo songs pass while Gene's 'I' fails as disordered egomania; bodily love is defended as bawdy dramatic monologue — foreplay between lovers rather than instruction in reducing women to sex objects; and love of life is secularized agape praise in 'I'm Alive,' 'Shout It Out Loud,' and the very title Alive!. Price then asks why love drives art at all, weighing the transcendentals (true, good, beautiful) against the Scruton-versus-Craig-Martin can-of-shit debate, and reads 'Reason to Live' as the claim that only rightly ordered love can ground a life.

objectification.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
objectification.title: Equal Opportunity Offenders
objectification.relation: Argues the Facehugger stages rape with the sexes reversed: because the aliens violate male and female bodies impartially - Kane's penetration, forced pregnancy, and death in childbirth; the cocooned Dallas begging Ripley to kill him - the films strip male viewers of the patriarchal privilege of treating sexual violence as someone else's threat and even of biological immunity to forced pregnancy. The Marines' 'colonists' daughters' banter, the prisoners' treatment of Ripley on Fury 161, and Johner's basketball comment exemplify a rape culture (Dworkin: rape is committed by exemplars of our norms) persisting into the twenty-second century, while Frye and Shafer's 'domain' explains why bodily violation attacks personhood itself.

objectification.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
objectification.title: History Will Judge
objectification.relation: Livingston reads Razor through George Lakoff's nation-as-family metaphor: Cain's Pegasus is the Strict Father family (the world is dangerous, Belzen shot for disobedience, Gina tortured for intelligence, Kendra's humiliating 'birth slap'), while Adama's Galactica is the Nurturant Parent (empathy, questioning authority, 'it's not enough to survive; one has to be worthy of surviving'). She traces how military kill-conditioning, desensitization plus objectifying 'toaster' and 'it' language, turns Kendra into 'a razor' and a PTSD case, while Apollo and Kendra hybridize the two family models on Pegasus. Adama's closing 'history will have to make its judgments' frames the chapter's claim that understanding Cain's context matters more than villainizing, and that humanity's worthiness depends on the balance struck between our idealized parents.

objectification.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
objectification.title: With or Without Starbuck
objectification.relation: Kirkland argues BSG imagines gender-free institutions (unisex heads and quarters, Starbuck never having to justify fighting) while installing a default masculinity under Adama, so that feminine-coded women die: Ellen the femme fatale is poisoned, pilots Kat and Kendra earn redemption only through death, and Cain's female command is written as militarist nightmare aligned with Gina's sexual abuse. Starbuck confounds the sexualizing male gaze and reverses rescue narratives, and 'The Farm' plus her captivity with Leoben on New Caprica literalize feminist critiques of patriarchal medicine and compulsory heterosexuality. Yet she is masculinized, pathologized via her abusive mother, brought to submit to Leoben as spiritual guide, and killed in 'Maelstrom' - containing the transgressive heroine within the show's patriarchy.

objectification.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
objectification.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
objectification.relation: Almassi grades the Dude as a halfway feminist ally: he divests from the Big Lebowski's patriarchal achiever-masculinity ('that and a pair of testicles'), respects Maude's conception project without paternalism (O'Neill's Kantian line between love and respect), and defends pacifist Smokey — yet his pacifism has stalled into passivity that King's active nonviolence would reject, he leaves Bunny's objectification unchallenged while 'Mr. Treehorn treats objects like women', and he only belatedly gives Maude the credibility Fricker's testimonial justice demands ('why don't you fucking listen occasionally?'). Using bell hooks's feminist masculinity and Larry May's progressive male standpoint, the chapter leaves the Dude five pins up with a spare still to pick up.

objectification.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
objectification.title: “Smother Him in the Crib”—Booker
objectification.relation: Origitano reads Elizabeth through Beauvoir and Frye: Columbia's propaganda infantilizes and objectifies her ('the Seed of the Prophet', 'Lamb', 'Specimen', always defined relative to a man), the tower literalizes Frye's birdcage of systematic oppression, and her confinement for an uncontrollable power mirrors women caged by a supposed natural inferiority. Booker's rescue only grants freedom, echoing Beauvoir's point that women have 'only received' what men are willing to give, so Elizabeth remains caged as his poker chip, her lock-picking skills formed by captivity and her tears dismissed as foreign. Her emancipation comes through action and collective solidarity, allying with Lady Comstock's ghost, taking control of Songbird, and finally drowning Booker/Comstock as equals, which enacts Beauvoir's claim that liberation must be won, not granted.

objectification.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
objectification.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
