hegemony.relation: Elan Gamaker analyzes Ken Loach's Cathy Come Home and Ken Russell's London Moods and Shelagh Delaney's Salford as British social-realist 'documentary style,' arguing that agency (in the Marxist sense of free choice against structure) is progressively eroded from funder to filmmaker to subject to viewer. He shows how Grierson's neo-Hegelian faith in state institutions turned documentary into 'good propaganda' that alienates the underclass it claims to serve, so the form reproduces cultural hegemony and false consciousness. Loach's stylization and Russell's ambiguity strip the depicted subjects of voice, though Gamaker holds that a later viewer's shifting interpretation can partly restore agency.

hegemony.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
hegemony.title: 19. Punk Consciousness and Class Consciousness
hegemony.relation: Tiffany Montoya reads punk lyrics and the DIY scene through Marx, Gramsci, and Lukacs, finding an emerging class consciousness in three stages: nihilistic discontent ('TV Party', 'Lost in the Supermarket'), systemic awareness of exploitation (Bad Religion's 'Suffer'), and full revolutionary consciousness with proletarian agency ('Class War', the Suicide Machines' 'Strike'). She shows how musical devices - Oi!-style gang vocals, work-song rhythms, the industrial drumming of Flogging Molly's 'The Power's Out' - create affective unity like military cadence, while mutual aid (Kropotkin) and do-it-yourself production make the scene a 'proletarian culture'. The chapter closes on Gramsci's warning that the capitalist state appropriates subversive culture (corporate festival sponsors, Hot Topic punk), asking whether punk will keep its vanguard or become 'rock for sustainable capitalism'.

hegemony.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
hegemony.title: 15. The Subtle Persuasion of Culinary Adventure Programs
hegemony.relation: Wahnsiedler analyzes Bourdain's 'culinary adventure programs' through Gramsci's concept of cultural hegemony and the public intellectual. He praises Parts Unknown for building counter-hegemony (historicizing colonialism, 'going native'), but critiques the Congo episode's 'colonial nostalgia' — Bourdain re-enacting Heart of Darkness and unchallenged praise of Belgian rule — arguing that as a Gramscian intellectual wielding the 'Bourdain Effect,' his framings reinforce or contest hegemony and demand responsible media consumption.

hegemony.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
hegemony.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
hegemony.relation: Nancy Kang argues tattoos can function within a liberatory feminist ideology, accentuating rather than diminishing femininity by exposing the differential treatment of tattooed women. She surveys radical, Marxist, liberal and corporeal feminism (invoking Aristotle's dismissal of women, Mill's Subjection of Women, and Gramsci's hegemony), then reads pop-culture cases – Crash's tattooed Latino worker, Black Swan's Lily, the Perry 'pricks as needles' sexualization, carnival 'Tattooed Ladies' like Irene Woodward marked 'by the father's hand,' and the McGee/Bullock/Kat Von D scandal – to show corporeal feminism treats tattooing as a risky, self-owning revolutionary act.

hegemony.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
hegemony.title: Ideological Formations of the Nuclear Family in The Hills Have Eyes
hegemony.relation: Lorena Russell reads both versions of The Hills Have Eyes through Althusser's Repressive vs. Ideological State Apparatuses (building on Gramsci's hegemony) and Foucault's account of power as multivalent with resistance internal to it, defending nuanced ideological criticism against Carroll's caricature. The films pit the 'normal' Carter family against the mutant/feral family produced by U.S. nuclear testing, using Clover's 'urbanoia' and class/Indian-exploitation guilt, Freudian repression, and the mannequin ghost town to expose 'family values' as constructed ideology. The Carters' descent into the mutants' own violence (Doug and Brenda 'butching up') destabilizes the bourgeois family rather than reaffirming it.

hegemony.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
hegemony.title: 68. Richard Pryor as Philosopher Stand-Up Comedy and Gramsci’s Organic Intellectual
hegemony.relation: Healy reads Pryor through Gramsci's Prison Notebooks concept of the 'organic intellectual'—someone who gains specialized knowledge through lived experience and uses it to challenge a capitalist/racist hegemony—arguing Pryor's mainstream white fame let him smuggle the Black experience to the dominant class. Analyzing his concert films (Live in Concert, Live on the Sunset Strip, Here and Now), Healy shows Pryor's chokehold and police-dog bits, the 'Yee Haw'/lynching bit, and the Mudbone and Motif characters using laughter as a 'Trojan Horse' to make white audiences absorb police brutality, the Great Migration, and heroin death—Pryor as philosophy in action.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Buffyverse’s Moral Compass
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Greg Forster argues the Buffyverse's moral structure is neither Christian nor Nietzschean vampire fiction but Platonic eudaimonism: the just person is always happier than the unjust. Faith is the test case — her pleasure-seeking turn to evil with Mayor Wilkins, her body-swap theft of Buffy's life in 'Who Are You?', her self-disgust ('You're nothing! Disgusting, murderous bitch!'), and her begging Angel to kill her in 'Five by Five' enact Plato's Republic examples of the Ring of Gyges and the unjust person mistakenly honored while the just one is punished. Buffy's invisible crime spree in 'Gone' and her 'the work that I have to do' sacrifice in 'The Gift' display the same eudaimonist pattern, with the caveat that the Buffyverse follows a Rousseau-like moral psychology in which compassion, not reason, does the moral work.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Eric Katz reads Tolkien's One Ring as a modern retelling of Plato's Ring of Gyges: Glaucon's challenge in Republic II that no one, given impunity, would remain just. He traces each character's moment of choice - Gollum already corrupted and split into 'Slinker and Stinker', Boromir trying to seize the Ring at Amon Hen and dying redeemed, Galadriel passing the test ('I will diminish, and go into the West'), Tom Bombadil untouched, Frodo finally claiming the Ring at the Cracks of Doom while Sam rejects the vision of 'Samwise the Strong'. Katz argues Tolkien improves on Plato by showing, through living characters, that unlimited power corrupts the soul, and that the answer to 'Why be moral?' is 'to be yourself': those who refuse the Ring are exactly those who know their own limits.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The End Is It All Darkness
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: John Pappas reads Crimes and Misdemeanors through Glaucon's ring of Gyges in Plato's Republic: Judah Rosenthal's wealth and prestige are his invisibility ring, and when his mistress Dolores threatens exposure he 'pushes the button', has his gangster brother Jack murder her, and gets away with it. Against Socrates' claim that injustice corrodes the harmonious soul and that virtue is its own reward, the film, unlike Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, lets the murderer and the 'yutz' Lester prosper while honest Clifford loses everything; Bergson's theory of the comic explains why Lester is invisible to himself, and Rousseau's reverie about what he would do with the ring marks Clifford as the one man who might use it decently. Aunt May's post-Holocaust atheism, 'might makes right' with nothing 'handed down in stone', supplies the argument from evil that releases Judah, leaving only the qualified hope that it is 'not all darkness'.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Fudge and Umbridge The Lessons of Obviously Unfit Power-Brokers
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The section draws a biography-by-biography parallel between Plato and Dumbledore: each lived through upheaval (the Peloponnesian War, the Thirty, and Socrates' execution; Grindelwald and Voldemort), each renounced a political career after disillusion, and each turned from politics to education, founding the Academy and leading Hogwarts. It explains the Republic's philosopher-rulers and their four cardinal virtues, argues that intelligence alone (Lex Luthor, Hannibal Lecter) plus excessive self-love disqualifies a ruler, and introduces Glaucon's Ring of Gyges as Plato's test of incorruptibility - a legend it says Rowling revives in Harry's invisibility cloak.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: NOTES
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The concluding section argues that Harry passes Plato's Ring of Gyges test, which Rowling rebuilds around the Invisibility Cloak: unlike Gyges, Harry never uses invisibility for selfish gain, refuses Scrimgeour's offer of his dream job, hunts Horcruxes rather than making them, and at eleven pulls the Sorcerer's Stone from his pocket precisely because Dumbledore's enchantment lets only someone who wants to find but not use it do so. This indifference to the lure of power, joined to courage, justice, and self-restraint, is the Platonic quality that makes Harry fit to rule.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Superheroes and the Ring of Gyges
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The chapter's heart: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges and 'harsh view' of human nature — justice as the weak's compact against the strong, a lineage running from Hobbes to Nietzsche — are powerfully denied by superheroes and by Frodo, who resist the power of the ring. Socrates' tripartite soul and justice-as-psychic-harmony are read as preparation for the Republic's real answer, the ascent to the eternal Form of the Good, which the chapter extends through Aristotle's teleology and virtue ethics: super-powered people, denied any standard social role, must wrestle with what their potential is for — from Kingdom Come's retired Superman and Spider-Man 2's Peter Parker to Astro City's Samaritan, with Uncle Ben's 'With great power comes great responsibility' as the upshot.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Chapter 13 - Why Should Superheroes Be Good Spider-Man, the X-Men, and
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Opens C. Stephen Evans' chapter by retelling the Republic's Ring of Gyges passage (359c-360d) — the shepherd who uses invisibility to seduce the king's wife, murder him, and seize the kingdom — as the archetype against which the question 'Why should superheroes be good?' will be posed through Spider-Man, the X-Men, and Kierkegaard's double danger.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Plato and the Question of Why We Should Be Good
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Reconstructs Glaucon's challenge from the Republic: with a ring making injustice cost-free, no one would keep hands off others' possessions, and anyone who stayed just would be mocked as 'a great fool' behind our self-protective praise; Socrates must show that the truly just person 'stripped of the seeming' — enduring the lash, the rack, and the cross — lives better than the honored unjust one. The chapter then turns Plato's thought-experiment on comic-book worlds: why should someone with superpowers care about being good?

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Problem for Spider-Man
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Sets up the chapter's question through the Spider-Man film: after the promoter cheats him, Peter lets the armed robber go with the taunt "I missed the part where that's my problem," and the robber's escape gets Uncle Ben killed. The scene turns Uncle Ben's "with great power comes great responsibility" into the classic question "Why be moral?" — why not use superpowers for "great personal satisfaction," an egoist's super life, when no payoff for virtue is guaranteed.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Reasons to Be Moral
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Extracts two candidate answers from Spider-Man — Reason One, that immorality rebounds on you (Uncle Ben's death), tested and weakened by the Ms. Poore poverty-theft case, and Spider-Man's agonized "Because it is right" to the Green Goblin, the Kant-and-Bradley motive of duty — and finds both insufficient to show morality is rational. It then tests Plato's answer that only the moral have harmony of soul (reason governing appetite and spirit) against Flash Thompson and self-forgiving sinners, and Aristotle's "virtue is its own reward" against the thought experiment of virtuous Arachnid-Girl rotting in prison while the fraudulent Norm Osborne flourishes.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: How to Use this Book in a Philosophy Course
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Argues philosophy has a public-relations problem and that pop culture can fix it: just as Plato used the ring of Gyges and Descartes imagined a deceitful demon, The Matrix vividly pictures Cartesian deception and South Park's Cartman inheriting a million dollars dramatizes the problem of evil better than dry Jones-and-Brown cases. The chapter then advises instructors on using the chapters to introduce topics, assign summaries, and set reflection papers in intro courses, pointing to fan wikis and pop-philosophy.org so students need not be experts on the shows.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Introduction
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Frames Part V's ethics chapters. Adams' chapter updates Plato's ring of Gyges for Heroes — with Claire's and Sylar's powers, why be moral? — answered by the properly ordered tripartite soul; McAleer's uses The Office to illustrate Aristotle's wit as a mean between buffoonery and boorishness; White's uses the Batman/Joker problem and a Bat-trolley version of Foot's case to argue deontologically that Batman need not kill the Joker; and Loftis' reads Watchmen's Ozymandias and Rorschach as a failed utilitarian and a failed deontologist, pointing to 'who watches the watchmen.'

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: But Isn’t It Only Natural
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Adams answers Plato's ring-of-Gyges challenge with Heroes: even when invisible, wrongdoing corrupts the wrongdoer, because justice is to the soul what health is to the body. Claire's refusal to claim credit for the fire rescue shows thumos (spirit) responsive to logistikos (reason), Sylar's uncontrollable hunger for powers is epithumetikon (appetite) ruling the soul, and Hiro's Vegas cheating shows how injustice makes life spin out of control; Claire's apology to Brody illustrates the Pagan Golden Rule — help your friends, harm your enemies — tempered by Plato's caution that enemies may become friends.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Springsteen’s Martyrdom
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The Bells parallel Socrates' forcible 'abduction' to the house of the arms merchant Cephalus in Republic Book I with Springsteen's 1984 political abduction, when Reagan and Mondale both pretended he had endorsed them and George Will invited him to be laureate of 'joyous overconsumption.' They read the Republic's luxurious city — its Ring of Gyges parasites, censorship of poets, and wars born of appetite — as an elenchus run against the control (epoche) of the healthy working city of Book II, so readers who take the 'ideal' city at face value err exactly like fans who hear patriotism in 'Born in the U.S.A.' Songs like 'Youngstown,' 'The Angel' and 'Galveston Bay' likewise critique overconsumption, imperialism and the censorship of artists, and both artist-critics risk the martyrdom Socrates suffered for speaking truth to the powerful.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: “Condemned to Be a Member of This Lowest of Species”
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Arp uses Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from the Republic to ask whether unlimited power must corrupt the just: Q's career of meddling ('Encounter at Farpoint', 'Q Who?', 'The Q and the Grey') shows the corrupted case, while Riker given Q-powers in 'Hide and Q' helps his friends instead, a counterexample Glaucon can resist by pleading insufficient time. He then explains the Q's misery — Quinn's bored suicidal plea in 'Death Wish' — through the hedonistic paradox, refining it with Mill's distinction between bodily lower pleasures and mental higher ones and Aristotle's account of the lasting pleasure of completed states like beating the ship's computer at chess. The conclusion is that Q's 'condemnation' to mortality in 'Déjà Q' reveals the human condition as enviable: it is precisely our lacking unlimited power, pleasure, and immortality that drives the striving for truth, justice, goodness, and love.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Lesson and Legacy of Din, Nayru, and Farore
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Horn argues the three Triforce pieces are morally neutral: by Kant's Groundwork, only the good will that acts from duty (Link never rescues Zelda for a reward) is good without qualification, so courage, wisdom, and power can each serve evil, and the Triforce would have corrupted Zelda or Link too if fortune had dealt it otherwise. Plato's Ring of Gyges and the Glaucon-Socrates debate explain Ganondorf: he chose to lust for power, and his wealth, status, and fear-based honor are hollow because justice is good for its own sake and his soul is out of balance (which is why the Triforce split at his touch in Ocarina of Time). Aristotle's doctrine of the mean then defines proper use: Link's courage between cowardice and rashness (getting the map, compass, and weapon before the boss), Zelda's internalized prudence, and Ganondorf's power in insatiable excess.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: As Nasty as I Wanna Be
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Greene asks whether Maguire's Elphaba is really wicked, first clearing away her reputation (she adopts the 'Wicked Witch' name because 'it liberates you from convention,' echoing Glaucon's challenge in the Republic about the just person with an unjust reputation and vice versa) and then her nature (the midwife-biting birth, green skin, and witchcraft establish no vampire-like evil essence, since Glinda and Nor are good witches). Following Hume's view that morality is not found in the world but in our assessments, he treats wickedness as a matter of performing actions we judge evil, and weighs Elphaba's life under both headings: good intentions with horrific outcomes (the bees that kill the chef, the icicle that kills Manek, Sarima's family executions) and bad intentions with none (her two failed attempts on Madame Morrible). The verdict is deliberately suspended: if she is wicked at all, it can only be through the consequences of her actions.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Achievement Unlocked Ethical Considerations
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Monica Evans opens with the 2006 'Serenity Now' funeral raid — a PvP guild massacring an in-game funeral for a real player — to argue that in-game ethics depend on each player's perception of the gameworld: mourners treat Azeroth as an extension of real life, raiders as a competitive game, and both are right. Plato's Ring of Gyges fails as an analogy because WoW hands everyone invisibility, yet morality still operates as a social construction through reputation, guilds, and the ostracism of ninja-looters. She finds the Borean Tundra 'torture quest' ethically hollow since the prisoner respawns and nothing persists, applies Mill's utilitarianism to good-samaritan players and universally loathed ninja-looters, and uses Kant's Categorical Imperative both to explain why players don't desert dungeon parties and why fair PvP killing of friends is permissible.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 6 - You Can’t Front on facebook
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Marinucci opens with Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Plato's Republic - invisibility licenses injustice because we care about seeming good - and maps it onto Suler's six factors of online disinhibition (anonymity, invisibility, asynchronicity, solipsism, dissociation, minimized authority). Facebook, she argues, lacks all six: real names and offline friends, near-synchronous news feeds, and the integration of every audience from mom to students into one space keep us inhibited. That inhibition is a good thing, since it prevents 'fronting' - presenting a false face to each audience - so Facebook identity integration can foster more authentic self-expression.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Invisibility or Honesty
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Schulzke argues inception's fundamental wrongness is a violation of autonomy read through Kant: the Fischer team treats him merely as a means, and even Cobb's benevolently intended inception on Mal disrespects humanity by stripping her self-determination, leaving her - like someone acting under coercion - no longer a responsible moral agent. Extraction he judges the lesser evil, though a world of dream espionage would end private mental life, since even the most guarded secrets surface in dreams. The payoff is a new twist on the Ring of Gyges from Plato's Republic: an invisibility ring could no longer shield injustice because a dreamer's deeds remain recorded and extractable, so Kant's absolute ban on lying could make extraction an engine of honesty - as when Ariadne's extraction on Cobb exposes the danger Mal poses and ultimately saves Cobb himself.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: A Palace Revolution
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The fantasy election brings in Plato's Republic: Richards's defense attorney Bill Carter functions as his Ring of Gyges, letting him vanish from legal consequences and raising Plato's question of whether we act justly only from fear of punishment. The tripartite soul is mapped onto Keef — appetites (drugs, sex, Jagger's 'Bitch'), spirit (the Glimmer Twins' rivalry), rationality (busting his head reaching for a library book) — and justice becomes the harmony under rationality's rule. In the ideal city of philosopher kings, auxiliaries, and workers, the sign at the gate reads 'NO POETS, NO ROCK'N'ROLLERS': Richards is exactly the corrupting poet Plato bars.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Leslie Dale Feldman reads the 1968 film's blasted opening as Hobbes's state of nature - 'solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short' - with the Lawgiver's 'Beware the beast Man' scroll echoing Hobbes's three causes of war (competition, fear, glory) and Plato's Ring of Gyges explaining why even the 'just' man acts rightly only under compulsion, both grounding the social contract's origin story. She then casts Dr. Zaius as Alexis de Tocqueville's tyranny of the majority - erasing Taylor's writing, lobotomizing Landon, and sealing Cornelius's cave 'to spare them all the care of thinking' - with Rousseau's man 'born free; and everywhere he is in chains' behind it. The chapter also traces Rod Serling's Twilight Zone fingerprints (nuclear-war twist endings like 'Time Enough at Last,' the cave of 'The Old Man in the Cave,' Adam-and-Eve survivor pairs, the beauty reversals of 'Eye of the Beholder') and reads Taylor and Nova's westward ride through Turner's frontier thesis and Kennedy's New Frontier, holding Serling's Hobbesian pessimism and his hope in tension.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Skyler King and Robert Arp catalogue the excuses cheating men offer - 'my wife let herself go', 'so much eye candy', 'a moment of weakness' - and add evolutionary psychology's parental investment theory to explain why Peter Florrick-types stray while women like Alicia cheat less. The centerpiece is Glaucon's Ring of Gyges story from Book II of Plato's Republic: politicians such as Peter, Bill Clinton, and Eliot Spitzer wear the invisibility ring of power and come to think moral rules no longer bind them. The chapter closes with prudential and moral reasons against infidelity - scorned spouses, broken promises, wounded children - capped by Eli Gold fielding questions about a Brazil-shaped birthmark in 'Anatomy of a Joke'.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Kenneth Sayles reads Peter and Valentine's net personas through three lenses: John Locke's identity theory to ask whether a consistent virtual persona with no physical anchor deserves our trust, Plato's Ring of Gyges to ask what anonymity does to morality, and Hannah Arendt's account of totalitarianism to warn that nameless, unaccountable influence ('action without a name... is meaningless') paves the way for rule by propaganda and a fictitious world. Real-world parallels - identity theft, the hacker collective Anonymous, YouTube politics - make the Enderverse nets look prophetic rather than fantastic.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The chapter argues Barney is best understood as a committed ethical egoist, distinguishing egoism from egotism, immoralism, and moral skepticism through the Playbook's Scuba Diver scam. Ainsworth rejects psychological egoism (Joey's view in Friends) using evolution and apparent counterexamples like Marshall's Christmas Eve deliveries, then uses Glaucon's ring of Gyges from the Republic to ask whether anyone would resist injustice with guaranteed impunity. The friendship objection is dissolved via Aristotle's 'a friend is another self': once friends are included in the ego, saving Marshall's relationship or rushing to Ted's hospital bed counts as self-interest, constrained like chess by absolute rules such as the Bro Code's Article 150.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Biondi argues the 'counter-cultural capitalist' is no paradox: Jobs succeeded not as a Gordon Gekko-style greedy capitalist but through the creative individualism of the cognitive counter-culture—the garage techno-geeks—who pursued their own vision rather than the bottom line. She traces the greedy-capitalist stereotype to Glaucon's Ring-of-Gyges challenge in Plato's Republic (people act justly only from fear of punishment), Hobbes's restless desire for power after power, and Marx and Engels's picture of alienated wage slavery under capitalism, with Rawls as the toleration-only-if-redistributed alternative. Jobs's hippie exterior (drugs, fruitarianism, Zen) masked an entrepreneur who, in Rand's 'creative mind' mold, put a ding in the universe through products like the iPad instead of philanthropy.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Robert Arp's gallery matches each Gang vice - dishonesty, egoism, selfishness, greed, pettiness, ignorance, laziness - to real-life scumbags from Nixon, Stephen Glass, and Janet Cooke to Charles Ponzi, Bernie Madoff, Crassus, the Empress Dowager Cixi, Imelda Marcos, and the Darwin Awards, and it opens with the chapter's philosophical spine: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Book II of Plato's Republic, which predicts that even an upstanding person with the power to act unseen would seduce, steal, and murder - exactly the question the Gang's mostly unpunished antics keep staging. Against the ethical egoist's argument that because everyone is self-interested everyone should be (Vanderbilt's 'the public be damned'), the chapter deploys the is-ought point - children are naturally selfish without therefore deserving to be - alongside mothers, Mother Teresa, and 9/11 first responders, concluding that egoism is at most an admixture in every action, with Lord of the Flies as the reductio of universal egoism.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 5. Every Lonely Monster Needs a Companion
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Gadsden asks why a near-omnipotent Time Lord needs companions at all and tests four hypotheses against his solo meltdowns—executing Solomon in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship,' nearly murdering Jex in 'A Town Called Mercy,' and declaring himself 'Time Lord Victorious' in 'The Waters of Mars.' He rejects the Lord Acton power-corrupts hypothesis via Glaucon's ring story in Plato's Republic, since powerless companions offer no threat of reprisal or dishonor, and qualifies J.J. Sylvia's care-ethics 'empathetic link' because the Doctor cares for non-human species like the Star Whale too. He favors two answers: Hume's fact/value gap as a millennium-long moral myopia ('I can't see it anymore,' the deleted 'Flesh and Stone' confession), and Aristotle's point in the Nicomachean Ethics that only virtuous friends—moral peers who mirror us—can expose the Doctor's blind spots, like his 'God Complex.'

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Hungry for More
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Wayne Yuen's introduction argues that philosophy needs extreme scenarios to stress-test moral, political, and religious theories, and that The Walking Dead supplies two: the reanimation of the dead and the collapse of social, political, and economic order. He frames the book around the show's most overt question - why be moral at all when survival pushes against it, as with Rick's compromises and the choice between searching for a missing girl or writing her off as having 'looked at the flowers' - plus how religion fares when the dead rise, and the string of attempted societies (the Prison, Woodbury, Terminus, Grady Memorial, Alexandria) that mirror our own world of failing nations and unjust rule. The essays, he says, hold a mirror to our values: we can become the walking dead without any zombies.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 9. Masks, Hearts, and Superheroes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Dupree and Fuš build an independent definition of the "true superhero" from identity statements (Batman = Bruce Wayne, Clark Kent = Superman): only an essentially human character who forges near-superhuman excellence through cultivated virtue can count, and Aristotle's virtue ethics supplies the standard. Batman qualifies - his refusal to kill the Joker shows the struggle for the golden mean between foolhardiness and cowardice, and Gotham Knights #31 shows how far he plans to avoid killing - whereas powers merely given, Superman's Kryptonian biology or the Green Lantern ring (their update of Gyges's Ring), bestow no virtue, as Kyle Rayner's and Guy Gardner's early careers show. Since Clark Kent is "in his heart" the alien Superman while Bruce Wayne is merely Batman's mask, Batman is a true superhero and Superman is not.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 18. War Means Fighting and Fighting Includes Philosophizing
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Vuckovich reads 'Still Valley' as a moral battlefield: Confederate scout Sgt. Paradine finds a witchcraft handbook that has frozen a Union patrol before Gettysburg, and Glaucon's Ring of Gyges account from the Republic — the really unjust person winning without scruple while seeming just — frames the temptation of an invisible, effortless victory. Aristotle's friendships of shared wickedness illuminate his bond with the witchman Teague, who exploits Paradine's desperation to pass on his own curse, until Paradine casts the handbook into the campfire, choosing a principle of fairness over a Devil-guaranteed win and accepting the shame of a 'Pyrrhic loss.'

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 18. Smoke and Mirrors in Gilead
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: St. Martin structures Gilead with Plato's Republic: Thrasymachus's 'justice is the advantage of the stronger' is the Sons of Jacob's operating principle (the Wall, the cattle prods, 'removing the damaged ones' from the ambassador's reception), and Glaucon's claim that it is best to do injustice without paying the penalty describes Commanders, while Handmaids suffer injustice with no revenge. She maps Socrates's division of labor onto Gilead's color-coded castes (Handmaids, Marthas, Aunts, Wives), then uses Glaucon's mocking 'city of sows' to show Gilead betraying even that model, since the regime exists to keep men powerful rather than babies alive—baby Charlotte recovers only when reunited with Janine. Serena's awakening after Eden's execution is an emergence from the cave, and the chapter closes that justice must be chosen for its own sake, with biases checked.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Just How Dark are the Dark Avengers
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Donovan and Richardson read Osborn's Dark Avengers through the Republic: Osborn is a modern Thrasymachus for whom justice is merely the advantage of the stronger, managing Bullseye's murder of Lindy and the team's image exactly as Glaucon's ring of Gyges predicts—villains like Moonstone, Daken, and Venom appearing good while doing injustice. Captain America, who tells Stark 'who made you the moral compass of us?', embodies the Socratic belief in a justice beyond human advantage, backed by the Forms and the allegory of the cave. Ms. Marvel, Noh-Varr, and Ares choose being just over appearing just, defecting or dying (Ares torn in half during the Siege) rather than serve Osborn's fraud.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: “Exit Game”
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Reading 'Striking Vipers' through its closed- and open-door imagery, the chapter asks whether Danny and Karl's virtual sex as Lance and Roxette is adultery, testing the question with Plato's Ring of Gyges (what people do when no one can see them), Locke's memory theory (if Danny remembers Roxette's sex acts, is Roxette Danny?), and behaviorist replies that only physical penetration counts. Nietzsche supplies the chapter's frame: his master/slave morality and his view of life as self-created representational art explain how the characters' hidden, mind-only moral inversion creates real existential meaning in virtual sex. The episode's fusion of bodily and mental pleasure is said to break down Mill's higher/lower pleasures distinction - 'lower' physical virtual pleasures yield a 'higher' sense of wholeness - and Schopenhauer's insatiable striving plus Husserl's meaning-conferring perception underwrite the conclusion that virtual love can be real, with Danny and Theo's once-a-year open marriage endorsed as an act-consequentialist balance between monotonous fidelity and escapist fantasy.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Kenneth Sayles reads Peter's and Valentine's anonymous rise on the nets through three lenses: John Locke's identity theory asks how a virtual identity can lack a physical anchor, Plato's Ring of Gyges asks what anonymity does to justice, and Hannah Arendt warns that 'action without a name... is meaningless' and that faceless power is a precondition of totalitarianism. Comparing the personas to the hacker collective Anonymous and to identity theft, he concludes our own Internet could breed its own Locke and Demosthenes and asks how much trust we owe virtual people whose controllers we can never know.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Joffrey on the Iron Throne, immune from punishment for beheading Ned, is read as Glaucon's ring of Gyges made flesh: the chapter asks what reason he has to be moral when he can get away with everything, noting he lacks even Gyges's advantage of secrecy and is hated like the Mad King. Hobbes's social contract is considered and rejected as a motive for Joffrey - King's Landing is no Hobbesian community like the Night's Watch, and Joffrey does better free-riding on everyone else's morality. The Platonic answer carries the chapter: like Ned Stark, who refused the throne, lived honorably in Winterfell, and regretted trading his honor at Baelor, the just person with an ordered soul has the only genuine happiness, which Joffrey's desire-satisfying cruelty forfeits.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Barkman retells Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, a shepherd's invisibility ring used to seduce the queen and murder the king, as Lord Acton's claim that absolute power corrupts, and answers with Plato: injustice disorders the tripartite soul, so the unjust sacrifice the happiness that matters most. The Guardians of the Universe are Plato's guardians writ cosmic, wise enough to rule themselves; Yalan Gur fell only when the yellow weakness was removed from his ring, Sinestro never had the wisdom ('You have never understood us'), and Hal's lapses, resigning for Carol Ferris and the Emerald Twilight rampage, are ignorance of the proper value of things rather than evil, since 'Hal's not evil... He believes he's acting for the right reasons.' The power ring is a modern Ring of Gyges, and Plato's test explains both who passes it and who fails.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Fudge and Umbridge The Lessons of Obviously Unfit Power-Brokers
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The chapter draws tight parallels between Plato's political life and Dumbledore's: both watched gifted, power-hungry pupils betray their cities (Alcibiades and Tom Riddle), both recoiled from tyrannical regimes (the Thirty under Critias; the duel with Grindelwald that killed his sister), and both turned from politics to education, founding the Academy and leading Hogwarts. It explains the Republic's philosopher-rulers, their four cardinal virtues, and the decades of training meant to 'distinguish the Potters from the Malfoys,' then introduces Glaucon's Ring of Gyges as Plato's test of who can resist invisible power, the legend Rowling mirrors in the Deathly Hallows and Harry's invisibility cloak, with Voldemort's unicorn-blood survival showing how the tyrant's life burns short.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: NOTES
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The chapter argues Harry passes the Ring of Gyges test that Voldemort fails: despite years of invisible freedom under the Cloak he never exploits it, refuses Scrimgeour's offer of his dream job to serve the whole wizarding community, hunts Horcruxes instead of making them, and at eleven alone retrieves the Sorcerer's Stone from the Mirror of Erised precisely because he does not want to use it. This indifference to the lure of power is exactly the Platonic qualification Dumbledore and Plato both demand of those fit to rule.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: NOTES
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Sharp argues that superpowered individuals break the equality assumption on which social contract theory rests: since Claire cannot be killed, D.L. can walk out of any jail, and Matt can sway juries, Hobbes's fear-of-death rationale for the contract seems not to apply to them. He then answers that the heroes remain effectively equal (Claire can still be killed by a wood splinter, Adam by decapitation) and shares Locke's and Rawls's reasons for contract, yet shows Rawls's difference principle would force the powered to serve society while the liberty principle forbids it, and that Sylar could not even be morally condemned under a pure Hobbesian reading. Cases like Claude's invisible petty theft (Glaucon's Ring of Gyges made real), the 'Five Years Gone' registered-superhumans future, and Linderman's plot to reunite society through the New York explosion lead to the conclusion that superpowers really would break society.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: NOTES
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Adams uses Plato's Ring of Gyges to ask whether superpowered people have reason to be moral, answering through the tripartite soul: Claire declining credit for the fire rescue shows well-governed thumos, her calculated revenge on Brody shows logistics ruling spirit, while Sylar's uncontrollable hunger for powers is textbook epithumetikon and intemperance that makes his life spin 'super' out of control. Cases like Micah's ATM thefts and Hiro's Vegas cheating (punished by a desert beating) illustrate that vice harms the agent's own soul, since justice is the soul's health. Claire's hospital apology to Brody is read through the Pagan Golden Rule and Sophocles' Ajax: enemies can become friends, so virtue, not mere conformity, is 'only natural' for heroes and ordinary people alike.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Argues House of Cards is a modern version of the Sophistical challenge in Books 1-2 of Plato's Republic: Thrasymachus' claim that justice is the advantage of the stronger and the unjust life is preferable. It maps Frank's proprietary 'my people' attitude and his shepherd-and-flock use of Russo, Stamper, Sharp, Meechum and his Gaffney constituents onto Thrasymachus' reversal of Socrates' shepherd analogy, and reads the Secretary of State snub, Blythe's naivety and Dunbar's descent into dirty tricks as proofs that the just are dupes. Frank's Sentinel ring and 'craft' make him Glaucon's perfectly unjust man of the Ring of Gyges story — unjust while seeming just — while the framed Lucas Goodwin plays the perfectly just man punished for a reputation for injustice. The chapter ends by arguing Frank falls short of the ideal tyrant (his conscience, his church visits asking 'what Justice is') and is coming to live the Book 9 tyrant's friendless 'worst sort of life' as Claire and the others abandon him.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Argues that Underwood's fourth-wall asides are the show's device for dramatizing the Platonic being-versus-seeming distinction: his public performances (reassuring Blythe over the leaked education bill, the confessional letter typed on the Underwood typewriter to destroy Walker, goading the President into appointing a special prosecutor) are contradicted point by point by what he tells the camera. The chapter reads Frank as a Ring of Gyges success story — the show so far teaches it is better to be the bad guy who seems good — while Socrates' examined life from the Apology and Crito shows Frank never asks why he wants power, and his cockiness is the opposite of Socratic ignorance. It closes with the Gorgias' contrast of Sophistic rhetoric (producing belief, not knowledge) and Machiavelli's advice to feign, casting Frank as the manipulator of opinion Socrates called a tyrant's politics.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Cooper reads Frank's one prayer - kneeling to pray 'to myself, for myself' - as a self-love he calls autoeroticism, built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness as power. Like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, Frank's atheism removes divine punishment from the moral equation, so the murders of Peter Russo and Zoe Barnes incur only human risk, while his feigned piety at the Peachoid girl's vigil, broken promises to Tusk, and 'cruelty well used' toward Russo exemplify Machiavellian virtu taming fortuna. Against this the chapter sets Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's remorse after betraying Freddy ('Do you think I'm a hypocrite?') shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man against the Augustinian freedom of self-giving love.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Hackett contrasts Frank's ethical egoism - acting like an invisible Ring of Gyges wearer who pushes Zoe in front of a train and kills Peter once they cannot be controlled - with Beauvoir's existentialist ethics, in which consciousness is a 'nothing' whose freedom is real only when it wills and sustains the freedom of others. Peter's drunken enslavement and Zoe's freely chosen deal with Frank illustrate the ambiguity of a freedom that is still causally situated, and Frank's Season 3 miscalculations with Jackie, Remy, and Claire show egoism's inability to weigh others' self-interest. Claire's sympathy for Michael Corrigan and her final walkout dramatize her learning Beauvoir's lesson that promoting others' freedom is the condition of one's own, the difference between self-interest and existential freedom.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Ketchen and Yeo read the show's cynicism as Thrasymachus's challenge in Books 1-2 of the Republic — 'justice is the advantage of the stronger' — under which the just (Blythe, Lucas Goodwin) are dupes while the crafty win. Frank's proprietary 'my people' politics replays the shepherd-sheep exchange: Russo, Stamper, Sharp and the Gaffney constituents are a flock groomed, fleeced, and slaughtered (the naval base closure), just as Thrasymachus says shepherds fatten sheep for their masters. Frank's Sentinel ring makes him Glaucon's Ring of Gyges craftsman — perfectly unjust with a reputation for justice from the library dedication — while Lucas Goodwin is the just man made to seem unjust and destroyed. Yet against Petrov, Frank shows a conscience and tortured questions about justice in church, so the chapter ends with Republic Book 9: the tyrant, isolated and abandoned by Season 3's close, lives 'the worst sort of life.'

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Gray argues Frank's fourth-wall asides dramatize Plato's being-versus-seeming distinction: the camera confidences reveal the true motive behind the public performance, as in the Blythe education-bill martyrdom gambit, the deliberately failed persuasion of Walker over the special prosecutor, and the seduction letter typed on the Underwood typewriter. The chapter reads Frank as winning the Ring of Gyges bet — enjoying adultery, corruption, and murder while seeming good — exactly the outcome the Republic sets out to refute. Against this it sets Socrates' examined life and Apology profession of ignorance: Frank pursues power without asking to what end, and his mastery of rhetoric over knowledge makes him the Sophist of the Gorgias rather than Plato's true politician, with Machiavelli's dissembling prince as his model.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Notes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Analyzes Frank's kneeling 'I pray to myself, for myself' as an ethics of autoeroticism built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness-as-power: like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, removing God from the equation makes the murders of Zoe and Russo cost only human, never eternal, judgment. The chapter details three exercises of Machiavellian virtu-feigned piety at the Peachoid vigil, fox-like promise-breaking with Tusk, and 'cruelty well-used' toward Russo-before closing on Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's betrayal of Freddy, met with a flash of remorse, shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Invisibility or Honesty
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Schulzke argues inception is a categorical violation of Kantian autonomy: the Fischer job treats him merely as a means (Saito's market share, Cobb's reunion with his children), and even Cobb's benevolent inception on Mal disrespects humanity by robbing her of self-determination, leaving her unable to act as a responsible moral agent testable against the categorical imperative. Extraction, by contrast, attacks privacy rather than autonomy, and the chapter uses Glaucon's Ring of Gyges to show that dream espionage would defeat even perfect invisibility, since an extractor could always read your deeds in your dreams. The twist, played off Kant's absolute condemnation of lying, is that the standing threat of extraction might be the only force that could make universal honesty practicable — hence the title's choice between invisibility and honesty, illustrated by Ariadne's life-saving extraction on Cobb.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Lesson and Legacy of Din, Nayru, and Farore
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Charles Joshua Horn asks whether power belongs beside wisdom and courage in the Triforce. Kant's good will shows all three pieces are morally neutral — Link and Zelda act from duty rather than reward, so courage and wisdom could be misused just as easily as Ganondorf misuses power. Plato's Ring of Gyges shows power does not automatically corrupt (Ganondorf chose to steal the Triforce for the Gerudo), and Socrates's answer to Glaucon explains why Ganondorf's ill-gotten wealth and honor leave him morally bankrupt. Aristotle's doctrine of the mean then gives the goddesses' intended use: Link's courage sits between cowardice and rashness (he gathers map, compass, and weapon before the boss room), Zelda's wisdom is really prudence, and Ganondorf's vice is power in excess.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: NOTES
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Taliaferro and Kastrul ask what the reader would do in the castaways' place, using Aristotle's view that character is a disposition to act under other conditions to assess Mr. Eko, Ben, Michael, Charlie, and Sawyer: people are not merely what they do but what they would do. Plato's Ring of Gyges, quoted at length, tests whether characters like Sun behave honestly only when watched. Against the idea that the island could reverse all values, they argue morality cannot be completely relative to context - invoking Chesterton's 'Thou shalt not steal' on the remotest star - and place Lost in the island-narrative tradition of the Odyssey and Robinson Crusoe as a story of the journey of the soul.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Fighting the Real Enemy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Johnson asks why Sinead O'Connor tearing the Pope's photo ended her career while SNL's own religion sketches drew little fire: 'DJesus Uncrossed' targets Tarantino's gratuitous violence rather than Jesus, the Tebow sketch ridicules prayers for football wins that Nietzsche said cheapen God into a servant of chance, and 'God's a Boob Man' satirizes the God's Not Dead films' strawmanning of atheists. Louis C.K.'s God monologue, he argues, raises the burden of proof and the problem of natural evil, best answered by Carlin's joke of a God subject to physical laws. The Church Lady embodies Warmke and Tosi's moral grandstanding, whereas O'Connor's protest does not, and the chapter ends on Plato's Republic: better to be a virtuous person scorned as a villain, like O'Connor, than a celebrated villain, though her tragic life strains Plato's promise that virtue pays.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Novy asks whether it would be right to deliberately make a Spider-Man. Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge from Plato's Republic — that unchecked superpower breeds 'great corruptibility' — is made flesh in Doc Ock, Green Goblin, Lizard, and Morbius, while Bostrom's transhumanism supplies the movement the chapter defends. Against Fukuyama's bio-conservative worries about playing God, destroying equality, and violating a human essence, the chapter notes that Aunt May's bifocals and insulin already make her a cyborg, that Marvel grants personhood by behavior rather than biology (Kree, Skrulls, the Vision), and that the thought experiment of giving Mary Jane a painless 'super smile' shows we are at least sometimes obliged to enhance.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 9. Masks, Hearts, and Superheroes
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Dupree and Fuš argue from identity statements: Bruce Wayne is 'just a mask' for Batman, while Clark Kent is in his heart Superman, so only an essentially human character can be a true superhero. On their Aristotelian definition — virtue ethics, the golden mean, flourishing through self-developed excellence — Batman's no-kill rule (sparing even the Joker), his planned avoidance of lethal force in Gotham Knights #31, and his balance against extremes make him the true hero, whereas Superman's given god-powers (killing Zod in Man of Steel, tyrant in Red Son) mirror power rings as Gyges's ring: possession without earned virtue.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 18. War Means Fighting and Fighting Includes Philosophizing
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Vuckovich reads 'Still Valley' through Glaucon's Ring of Gyges: Sgt. Paradine, handed a witchcraft handbook that freezes the Union army before Gettysburg, confronts the temptation of costless, unearned victory, and his burning of the handbook rather than renounce God preserves a principle worth more than winning. Aristotle's claim that bad men can be friends through shared wickedness explains the witchman Teague's bond with Paradine, an 'alliance' that recruits the desperate soldier to do the Devil's dirty work. The chapter ends on the shameful secret legacy: even burying the episode leaves Paradine with a private war in his conscience, a pyrrhic loss for a fighting man who almost surrendered what he holds sacred.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Seventh Hole Cheating and Gamesmanship among Amateur and Professional Golfers
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Lumpkin argues that amateur golfers routinely cheat while professionals do not, and dissects four rationalizations amateurs use: appeal to ignorance, appeal to popularity, appeal to tradition (Callahan's 'cheating culture'), and the belief that 'no one will ever know' — a golf-course version of Plato's Ring of Gyges where invisibility dissolves restraint. Drawing on Kohlberg's stages of moral development, she claims professionals reason at higher levels because officials, peers, and disqualification (e.g., J. P. Hayes) enforce the sport's social contract, whereas amateurs face no punishment. She concludes casual golfers would do better not to keep score than to keep a 'mythical' one, earning the right to score only once they follow the rules.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Eighteenth Hole Swing Thoughts Tough Questions for a Tough Game
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Andy Wible closes the volume with fourteen open-ended 'swing thoughts'—short provocations applying philosophy to golf rather than arguing a thesis. He asks whether golf's subdued, rational fans make it morally superior (Plato and Aristotle on reason ruling emotion), whether Tiger Woods effectively wielded Plato's Ring of Gyges by sinning while invisible, whether Berkeley's idealism means your clubs and playing partners are mere perceptions (and whether that would matter), and invokes Augustine's 'an unjust law is no law at all' to license civil disobedience against unfair rules like spike marks. Further questions probe environmental harm, prayer as cheating, Casey Martin's cart, and whether perfect virtual golf would count as 'real' golf.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: On Being Horrible (and an Angel)
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The chapter runs Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge from the Republic against the Whedonverse: invisibility in 'Out of Mind, Out of Sight' and 'Gone' (where even Buffy takes a self-serving 'vacation from herself'), the invincibility ring in 'In the Dark' that Angel destroys rather than uses, and the Buffy-Faith body switch in 'Who Are You?' as the unjust person with a virtuous reputation versus the just person misunderstood. Plato's tripartite-soul answer is only partly confirmed—Faith spirals into torment after killing the deputy mayor, but Saffron cons without any inner turmoil—so the chapter turns to Aristotle: the good life needs external goods, above all friendship and community. This explains why Whedon's wrongdoers (Woody in Toy Story, Jayne in 'Ariel,' Gunn, Stark, Buffy in 'Revelations') must atone before their communities, why Mal's 'you only need a few [good people]' rebukes Saffron, and why both Dr. Horrible and Captain Hammer are tragic—each lives alone and friendless, having squandered Penny.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Kowalski likens Goodfellas' Henry Hill to Plato's Gyges: both act immorally with near-total impunity, posing Glaucon's challenge in the Republic of why one should be just when one can escape all consequences. He applies Plato's tripartite soul (appetitive, spirited, rational) to Henry (runaway appetite/cocaine), Tommy (overstretched spirit, killing Billy Batts and Spider out of wounded pride) and cool, untroubled Paulie, treating them as the disharmonious 'unbalanced self.' Against the objection that these gangsters seem happy, he deploys Plato's health/happiness analogy and the feeling-happy vs being-happy distinction to argue they suffer 'cancer of the soul' and cannot be truly happy.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Skoble argues that A Simple Plan dramatizes Plato's Republic almost exactly: justice as psychological harmony among the parts of the soul, and injustice as self-destructive disharmony. When Hank, Jacob, and Lou keep found money, they enact Thrasymachus's and the Ring of Gyges challenge (would you be unjust if you'd never be caught?). Hank miscalculates his own self-interest, mistaking wealth for happiness; the deception, distrust, and murders that follow (including Hank killing Jacob) show that even the criminal who evades capture is ruined by his corrupted character, exactly as Plato predicts.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Schuler and Murray read Chinatown through Marx and Plato as a critique of capitalism's compulsions. Drawing on Marx and Engels on capital's Promethean transformation of nature and Hegel on art embodying abstractions, they argue neo-noir's centrifugal Los Angeles makes water, not diamonds, the object of desire, with wealth taking the abstract form of value. Plato's Republic warns that the boundless love of money (linked to Gyges, invisibility, and tyranny) destroys justice as reasonable self-limitation; Noah Cross's incest mirrors the 'rape of the Owens Valley', and Jake's defeat ('Forget it, Jake, it's Chinatown') marks the exhaustion of the postwar golden age.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: Plato, Habermas, and the Demonic Cobb
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Murphy treats Following as a provocation keyed to the copy of Plato's Republic glimpsed in The Blonde's apartment: Cobb, who slips unseen into houses and lives and reads people's 'boxes,' is the shepherd with the Ring of Gyges, able to act unjustly without ever facing detection. Against Glaucon's challenge the chapter weighs Socrates's answer that injustice enslaves and disorders the soul—but notes that Nolan shows Cobb victorious, a 'demonic' figure with all of Socrates's abilities and none of his love of justice, who drags Bill and The Blonde into a cave of illusion rather than out of one. Habermas supplies the modern retort: our rationality and sanity depend on the communicative action, truth, and fairness of a shared lifeworld, commitments a sociopathic loner like Cobb cannot renounce without taking refuge in mental illness, though the film never shows Cobb paying that price. Man of Steel's Clark Kent clutching the Republic while letting himself be bullied, and Jonathan Kent's fatal secrecy, become the counterimage of someone who consistently wills justice at personal cost, the closest Nolan comes to showing why justice is worth choosing.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 14. Revolting Punks
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Innes unpacks the double meaning of 'revolting': punk's obscenity, three-minute seven-inch singles on independent labels, beer-can-and-burrito gigs at Randy's Rodeo, and Vivienne Westwood bondage wear are revolt in the original sense - and a revival of Diogenes's cynicism, which rejects Plato's abstract virtue and the Glaucon-style social contract (the Ring of Gyges showing justice is only for the visible) for virtue according to nature. Hippies and prog rock are the sold-out establishment (Dead Kennedys' 'California Über Alles' against Jerry Brown), and satire - Johnny Rotten's lit lamp searching for an honest man - is the Cynic's serious joke, ending in chosen, communal virtue.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 17. Is Morality for Suckers
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: The chapter reads Jimmy through Plato's Republic, likening his resolve to stop letting conscience stop him to Glaucon's Ring of Gyges thesis that people act immorally whenever they can escape detection, as when Jimmy dodges 'bullets' in his Matrix-like winning speech. Using Plato's tripartite soul, it diagnoses Jimmy as ruled by his appetitive and spirited parts rather than reason, hence lacking self-control and unable to find morality pleasant in itself. It then tests and finds wanting Plato's arguments (contemplative pleasure, connectedness, the immortality of the rational part) that a healthy, reason-ruled soul is both moral and happiest, granting Jimmy's intense scamming pleasures their pull.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: But Isn’t It Only Natural
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Adams uses the superpowered characters of Heroes to teach Plato's Republic. The Ring of Gyges question, whether one with the power to escape consequences has reason to be just, is posed by Sylar, Daphne, and Hiro cheating in Vegas. Adams maps Plato's tripartite soul, thumos, logistikon, and epithumetikon, onto Claire's courage and wisdom and Sylar's ruinous intemperance, arguing justice is psychic health so vices grow worse the more power one has. He adds the 'Pagan Golden Rule' (help friends, harm enemies) to read Claire's apology to Brody, concluding virtue is natural to a well-ordered human soul and is its own reward.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: NOTES
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Charles Taliaferro and Dan Kastrul argue, following Aristotle's dispositional account of character, that who the castaways are is a matter of what they would do under different conditions, illustrated by Mr. Eko's circumstance-driven violence and Ben Linus's shifting good-guy/bad-guy conduct. They deploy Plato's Myth of Gyges (the ring of invisibility) to test whether characters like Sun would act justly only when watched, and, against a completely reversed morality ('an island where skinning babies is good'), they argue via Chesterton that some overriding values are non-relative, so the show never fully reverses good and evil even amid its mysteries.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 18. War Means Fighting and Fighting Includes Philosophizing
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Vuckovich analyzes 'Still Valley,' where Confederate Sergeant Paradine can win the Civil War using a witchcraft handbook that freezes Union troops but only by renouncing God. He reads Paradine's temptation through Glaucon's Ring of Gyges myth in Plato's Republic (the committed unjust man who outdoes enemies without scruple) and Aristotle's friendships of shared pleasure (Paradine and the witchman Teague bonded by hatred of the enemy). Paradine burns the handbook rather than damn the Confederacy, preserving a core principle of fairness even at the cost of an easy victory—winning isn't everything.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: MOTHERHOOD
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Sara Goering uses the fantasy of a child 'off button' as a thought experiment, situating it alongside Plato's Ring of Gyges, the brain-in-a-vat, and personal-identity puzzles to argue that such control would be overused and would treat children as objects rather than developing subjects. She then turns reflexive, critiquing thought experiments themselves – including Rawls's veil of ignorance (via Okin and Benhabib) and Susan Brison's critique of personal-identity cases – for diverting from the messy real world, arguing that the off-button fantasy really signals the need for 'distributed mothering' and structural support; she illustrates with The Matrix, Multiplicity, Harry Potter, and Woolf's 'room of one's own.'

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 6. Hollow Man
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Rowlands reads Hollow Man as a retelling of Plato's Ring of Gyges, posing 'why be moral?' once the invisible Kevin Bacon can act without sanction. He rejects the religious answer and Hobbesian social-contract theory (both reduce morality to prudence/fear of punishment and leave those outside the contract unprotected), and Hume's fellow-feeling as mere causal explanation not justification. He examines Kant's Categorical Imperative reducing immorality to inconsistency but argues it cannot answer 'why should I be moral,' concluding the choice is arational self-definition, closing with Nietzsche's 'become what you are' and the deed at the bottom of morality.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Eric Katz reads the One Ring as a variation on Plato's Ring of Gyges from the Republic: both grant impunity, and both pose the question of whether anyone would stay moral if able to act without consequence. Where Plato only argues that unchecked power corrupts the soul, Tolkien shows it through Gollum's ruin, Boromir's fall, and Frodo's final failure at the Cracks of Doom, while Galadriel, Bombadil, and Sam refuse the Ring by knowing who they are. Katz concludes Tolkien answers Plato's 'why be moral?' with 'to be yourself.'

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: But Isn’t It Only Natural
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Don Adams uses Heroes' superpowered characters (who could commit perfect crimes like Gyges with his invisibility ring) to argue Plato's case that virtue is its own reward. He maps Plato's tripartite soul onto the characters: Claire's thumos (spirit/honor) tempered by logistikos (reason) yields courage and wisdom, while Sylar's ruling appetite (his hunger for powers) is intemperance and injustice that makes his life spin out of control. Reading justice as psychic health, and glossing the 'Pagan Golden Rule' (help friends, harm enemies, but enemies may become friends), Adams argues it is 'only natural' for even the powerful to be virtuous rather than exploit others.

plato-ring-of-gyges.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
plato-ring-of-gyges.title: 43. Ex Machina as Philosophy Mendacia Ex Machina (Lies from a Machine)
plato-ring-of-gyges.relation: Grinnell argues Ex Machina is fundamentally about lying, read through Kant's deontology. He frames Nathan's rigged Turing test on Ava against Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge and Kant's two formulations of the categorical imperative, deriving three 'wrinkles': lying is heteronomous programming rather than the autonomy Nathan seeks; the experiment is defensible only if Ava fails, since a genuine person may not be manipulated (Formula of Humanity); and the cascade of lies among Nathan, Caleb, and Ava vindicates Kant's absolute prohibition on lying. He uses Caleb's telling of Frank Jackson's Mary's Room and Searle's weak/strong AI distinction to question whether Ava's 'pleasure response' amounts to genuine consciousness or personhood.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Buffyverse’s Moral Compass
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Greg Forster argues the Buffyverse's moral structure is neither Christian nor Nietzschean vampire fiction but Platonic eudaimonism: the just person is always happier than the unjust. Faith is the test case — her pleasure-seeking turn to evil with Mayor Wilkins, her body-swap theft of Buffy's life in 'Who Are You?', her self-disgust ('You're nothing! Disgusting, murderous bitch!'), and her begging Angel to kill her in 'Five by Five' enact Plato's Republic examples of the Ring of Gyges and the unjust person mistakenly honored while the just one is punished. Buffy's invisible crime spree in 'Gone' and her 'the work that I have to do' sacrifice in 'The Gift' display the same eudaimonist pattern, with the caveat that the Buffyverse follows a Rousseau-like moral psychology in which compassion, not reason, does the moral work.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Argues ancient ethics explains why Tony, who has 'the world by the balls', still feels like a loser. Plato's Republic diagnoses him as a 'civil war' of unintegrated motivations (loving father and murderer at once, as in 'College'), a condition power over others only worsens; Aristotle teaches that happiness is activity with self-sufficient, integrated desires rather than a list of possessions, and Epicurus's 'sober reasoning' is the therapy Tony never gets. The Hawthorne quotation Tony reads in 'College' and his Gary Cooper ideal from 'The Happy Wanderer' frame the point: Cooper in High Noon is unmesswithable because he does not need vengeance, whereas Tony's compulsive revenge shows the world has the grip on him.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Why Not to Buy the Porsche
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Skoble uses Manhattan's confrontation scene — Isaac telling Yale 'you're too easy on yourself... you'd rather buy the Porsche' over the hominid skeleton — to build an account of integrity as fidelity to correct moral principles, requiring an integrated character in which reason and desire agree. He distinguishes integrity from mere consistency (the 'consistent Nazi') and from stubbornness, and models it on Plato's just person who 'harmonizes the three parts of himself'. Aristotle's account of habituation defends Isaac's slippery slope: Yale's repeated lies for expediency are forming the kind of character who would inform on friends, so integrity is an objective yardstick of a well-lived life, as Isaac's amends to Tracy at the end confirms.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Common Good versus the Greater Good
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Maps Voldemort onto the Sophists - Thrasymachus's claim that the unjust always come out ahead - through his pattern of exploiting followers' trust for power and pleasure, while Plato's two-pronged reply runs: cosmic justice in the afterlife (the flayed child beneath the bench as Voldemort's just fate, sealing it by refusing remorse) and the intrinsic goodness of justice via the tripartite soul with reason ruling spirit and appetite, the four cardinal virtues, and the health analogy. Harry, seeking Dumbledore's wisdom, showing courage in facing death, and devoted to justice for wizards and Muggles, embodies the moral life as the rational choice, while Voldemort's snakelike appearance externalizes his disordered, sick soul.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Superheroes and the Ring of Gyges
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The chapter's heart: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges and 'harsh view' of human nature — justice as the weak's compact against the strong, a lineage running from Hobbes to Nietzsche — are powerfully denied by superheroes and by Frodo, who resist the power of the ring. Socrates' tripartite soul and justice-as-psychic-harmony are read as preparation for the Republic's real answer, the ascent to the eternal Form of the Good, which the chapter extends through Aristotle's teleology and virtue ethics: super-powered people, denied any standard social role, must wrestle with what their potential is for — from Kingdom Come's retired Superman and Spider-Man 2's Peter Parker to Astro City's Samaritan, with Uncle Ben's 'With great power comes great responsibility' as the upshot.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Reasons to Be Moral
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Extracts two candidate answers from Spider-Man — Reason One, that immorality rebounds on you (Uncle Ben's death), tested and weakened by the Ms. Poore poverty-theft case, and Spider-Man's agonized "Because it is right" to the Green Goblin, the Kant-and-Bradley motive of duty — and finds both insufficient to show morality is rational. It then tests Plato's answer that only the moral have harmony of soul (reason governing appetite and spirit) against Flash Thompson and self-forgiving sinners, and Aristotle's "virtue is its own reward" against the thought experiment of virtuous Arachnid-Girl rotting in prison while the fraudulent Norm Osborne flourishes.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Reads Eustace, Uncle Andrew, Experiment House, and Miraz's censored Narnia as Lewis's portraits of modern secularism, which treats the world as mere resource and dismisses the transcendent regardless of evidence. It argues that denying intrinsic value collapses into a Nietzschean master morality of power, visible in Uncle Andrew's use of the children as guinea pigs and the Lone Islands' slave trade, and exposes the secular 'conditioner's' self-exemption as a violation of the Principle of Relevant Difference. Against the Green Witch's debunking of Puddleglum's sun and Aslan as copies of a lamp and a cat, it deploys the Platonic-Cartesian copy/original model of ideas to argue transcendent ideas (eternity, perfection, necessary being) cannot be derived from lower material causes, suggesting instead that the material world is the 'shadowland' copy of a divine original.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Poker and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Ventimiglia mines No-Limit Hold'em for seven lessons philosophers also teach: we lack certain knowledge (Descartes' cogito is the famous quest for certainty, but philosophy's own history of disagreement proves uncertainty is the human condition), and like William James against Clifford we must still believe and act without the nuts — waiting for pocket aces while the blinds eat you alive is no strategy.
