Risking everything echoes Thoreau's escape from lives of quiet desperation, trusting hunches over arithmetic follows Thoreau and Peirce's sentimentalism, and the Darwin-and-Spencer competition of tournament poker hides a deeper cooperative social contract: get caught cheating and you are out of the game. It closes with Plato's four classic virtues from the Republic — wisdom, courage, moderation, and the justice of a balanced soul — as the perfection of a poker player.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
plato-tripartite-soul.title: U2 and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Tollefsen revives Plato's ancient quarrel between philosophy and poetry: artistic imitations, three removes from the Forms and aimed at the soul's emotional part, stir 'imitative emotions' - purer, shorter-lived, effort-free surrogates for the real labors of love, faith and community - and he builds a four-stage account of the U2 formula (idealized transcendent love in the lyrics, religious imagery fusing lover and God, the Edge's Big Music crescendo, and the concert 'you' extended to the crowd, as in the Elevation-tour 'I Will Follow' with its 'Amazing Grace' bells) to show U2 are masters of exactly this seduction. The healing fans felt after September 11th may therefore be an image of redemption rather than the reality. Where Aristotle and Aquinas would educate the emotions rather than suppress them, Tollefsen's quarrel is with imitation itself; his verdict is that U2 suffer from Misplaced Artistic Pretension - high imagery where honest trash (or genuine complexity) would do.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
plato-tripartite-soul.title: James Bond and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Getachew maps Plato's Republic archetypes onto the Bond universe: the appetite-ruled Tyrant is Goldfinger, Zorin, Stromberg and the SPECTRE megalomaniacs; the spirit-ruled Guardian is 007, compared to Alcibiades and to Medea's vengeful fury (Bond letting Trevelyan fall 'For me'); and the reason-ruled Philosopher-King is M, whose ideal republic of common children and expendable numbers mirrors MI6's recruitment of orphans and its treatment of Bond as '007', never a person. She then challenges Plato's preference for the eternal Forms and immortality, using Freud on transience and Heidegger's being-toward-death (via Tolstoy's Ivan Ilych) to argue that mortality and risk are what make life worth living. Bond's stylish risk-taking, like the cello-case downhill escape, shows we need a balance between the Guardian and the man of thought.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Introduction
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Frames Part V's ethics chapters. Adams' chapter updates Plato's ring of Gyges for Heroes — with Claire's and Sylar's powers, why be moral? — answered by the properly ordered tripartite soul; McAleer's uses The Office to illustrate Aristotle's wit as a mean between buffoonery and boorishness; White's uses the Batman/Joker problem and a Bat-trolley version of Foot's case to argue deontologically that Batman need not kill the Joker; and Loftis' reads Watchmen's Ozymandias and Rorschach as a failed utilitarian and a failed deontologist, pointing to 'who watches the watchmen.'

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
plato-tripartite-soul.title: But Isn’t It Only Natural
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Adams answers Plato's ring-of-Gyges challenge with Heroes: even when invisible, wrongdoing corrupts the wrongdoer, because justice is to the soul what health is to the body. Claire's refusal to claim credit for the fire rescue shows thumos (spirit) responsive to logistikos (reason), Sylar's uncontrollable hunger for powers is epithumetikon (appetite) ruling the soul, and Hiro's Vegas cheating shows how injustice makes life spin out of control; Claire's apology to Brody illustrates the Pagan Golden Rule — help your friends, harm your enemies — tempered by Plato's caution that enemies may become friends.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Evaluating Zelda
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Frome tackles the paradox of fiction through Wind Waker: why do we fear Gohma, feel sad when Link leaves his grandmother on Outset Island, or care when Tetra's identity is revealed, though we know none of it is real? He rejects the illusion theory (we never suspend disbelief enough to call the police), Carroll's thought theory (fear is too fast and too vivid for mere thoughts), and Walton's pretend theory (involuntary pretending and the uniform way all players see the sail break it). Instead he argues for a multi-level mind, modeled on Plato's divided soul in the Republic and Fodor's mental modules: local unconscious appraisals react to the fire as if real, while a global appraisal of reality-status keeps us in our chairs.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
plato-tripartite-soul.title: How Beckenbauer and Zidane Practiced the Four Cardinal Virtues
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Coumoundouros explains soccer greatness through three Platonic ideas: the Form of the footballer, which Pelé (1,281 goals, three World Cups, the save by Banks his header 'infected' with greatness and the infamous miss against Uruguay) and Maradona (the Hand of God and the Goal of the Century past five English defenders) approximate as near-perfect imitations, with position-specific Forms like forward Form for Pelé and attacking-midfielder Form for Maradona. Excellence as performing a proper function well (Republic 353a) then accounts for modern players—Ronaldo's evolved winger role, Henry converted by Wenger into a striker, Marta averaging a goal per game proving women's soccer equals the men's. Finally the Republic's four cardinal virtues grounded in the tripartite soul apply off and on the pitch: Beckenbauer playing the 1970 'Game of the Century' with a fractured clavicle and marshaling the 1974 final shows courage, wisdom, and moderation in just balance, while Zidane's 2006 head-butt on Materazzi shows the spirited part overwhelming reason, and with it greatness itself.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
plato-tripartite-soul.title: And the Winner Is
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Lynch pits Plato against the Shaolin monks on the nature of the self that martial training is supposed to master. Plato's Republic makes the athlete-warrior Guardian a harmonious, rationally ruled tripartite soul whose bravery is 'remembering what ought and ought not to be feared', trained so reason governs aggression; Buddhism instead dissolves the self into five impermanent aggregates (illustrated by the chariot analogy) and reads mushin as a direct taste of no-self. He awards the practical decision to the Buddhist fighting monks, since no-self explains martial spontaneity and naturally arising compassion, while admitting Plato's substantive rational soul is not strictly refuted.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
plato-tripartite-soul.title: You Don’t Always Get Along
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The chapter animates Hume's bundle as a 'little republic' of mental citizens without a universal citizen, staging a dialogue between Person-Hume, who cannot believe there is no self, and Philosopher-Hume, who counsels beer and billiards. It traces the view back to Plato's Republic: the tripartite soul (with Freud's id-ego-superego as a modern rerun), the example of desiring and refusing the same cold beer when you must collect your mother from the airport, and Leontius raging at his own eyes before the corpses, cross-chatter as civil strife among inner citizens, exactly what the doctors diagnose as Fred's symptom.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
plato-tripartite-soul.title: A Palace Revolution
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The fantasy election brings in Plato's Republic: Richards's defense attorney Bill Carter functions as his Ring of Gyges, letting him vanish from legal consequences and raising Plato's question of whether we act justly only from fear of punishment. The tripartite soul is mapped onto Keef — appetites (drugs, sex, Jagger's 'Bitch'), spirit (the Glimmer Twins' rivalry), rationality (busting his head reaching for a library book) — and justice becomes the harmony under rationality's rule. In the ideal city of philosopher kings, auxiliaries, and workers, the sign at the gate reads 'NO POETS, NO ROCK'N'ROLLERS': Richards is exactly the corrupting poet Plato bars.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Shout and Scream and Kill the King
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The election plays out: Richards blows away the auxiliaries with 'Play with Fire' and whips the working-class appetites into a frenzy (put on Exile on Main Street after a few rounds to test Plato's fear of the poets). Young Keef's soul is appetite-led — the 'Blue Lena' Bentley with its hidden drug compartment embodies a spirit in service of drugs and artistic hunger, with rationality demoted to scoring the fix. The resulting Republic of Keef, driven fast on the edge of a cliff, vindicates Plato's warning that wherever the appetites lead, tyranny soon follows — as the author concedes through his own pipe-smoking.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Auxier argues that Klosterman's signature lists always carry an 'immanent order' of value, illustrated by the twenty-two teenagers' simultaneous classroom thoughts in Downtown Owl and his own contested ranking of the five greatest rock bands. He reads the seventeen-page sober conversation between Julia and Vance, printed with 'what she meant' and 'what he meant' under each remark, through Kant's extensive versus intensive magnitudes: the spoken words are an extensive whole, but the multiple unshared perspectives form an intensive whole no list can exhaust, which is why philosophers crave the 'tug of necessity' that intensive relations never deliver. Plato's Leontius, who rubbernecked at corpses despite his disgust, explains both Klosterman's TMI confessions in Killing Yourself to Live and the 'recoil of the shit-canon' by which we learn to order our desires, while Julia's carbon-monoxide death in the blizzard shows the world converting intensive possibilities into extensive necessity.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Greg Littmann stages Plato's hypothetical review of American Gods under the Republic's charges against poetry: the novel is full of 'greatest of all lies' about gods behaving badly, from Odin and Loki's sacrificial plot to Czernobog's head-smashing, gods degrading themselves into lesser forms like Horus the road-kill-eating hawk and Media as Lucille Ball, and characters ruled by passion rather than reason, from Mad Sweeney drinking himself to death to Thor's suicide, corrupting a soul that should be governed by rationality. Against this he sets Aristotle's Poetics: listening to music and intellectual leisure are valuable in themselves, fiction is more philosophic than history because it shows what could happen, the impossible is justified when it astounds, and catharsis through pity for figures like the weeping Mad Sweeney purges rather than corrupts. Because American Gods' absurd premise unfolds with internally probable, character-consistent events (loyal Shadow, loving Laura, grifter Odin), it satisfies Aristotle's requirement that fantasy make artistic sense.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Greg Littmann maps Ape City onto Plato's Republic class by class: orangutan rulers who legislate, censor, and propagandize; gorilla warriors who enforce; chimpanzee producers who do all the work - including, pointedly, the science Plato made no provision for; and humans as the 'barbarians' Plato says may be enslaved or exterminated. The overlaps are detailed: the Sacred Scrolls' first article of faith functions as the noble lie's myth of the metals, orangutan funerals promise heaven to keep gorillas unafraid of death, and Zaius's erasing of Taylor's dust-writing and blowing up of the archaeological cave enact the rulers' duty to supervise stories. But the films also refute Plato: hereditary orangutans show that power corrupts philosopher kings, Dr. Honorius's 'reason' is dogma serving the faith, the gelding threat that finally breaks Taylor cracks the tripartite-soul analogy of justice, and democracy's rough virtue is that it lets us remove rulers 'without sticking anybody with iron spears.'

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Hirschbein has Freud analyze the audience first: like Van Alden, the repressed hypocrite whose true self erupts in drowning Sebso and burning his workplace tormentor, we watch Nucky and Jimmy as avatars of our own repressed aggression and lust. Freud's contest of Eros and Thanatos - his reframing of Plato's tripartite soul as id, ego, and superego - explains why civilization demands renunciation while spectacle like Boardwalk supplies vicarious gratification, with Milgram's and Zimbardo's experiments showing how thin the civilized veneer is. Jimmy's seduction by his mother and killing of the Commodore enact the Oedipus complex writ large, Freud's primal-horde story of the sons' parridical revolt against the father, and the show's catharsis is what lets us live with the sin.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Jeff Ewing argues the moral fabric of Ender's Game is virtue-ethical, first testing Ender's leadership against Plato's cardinal virtues, tripartite soul, and rigid class hierarchy of the Republic, then finding Aristotle a far better fit. Ender's trademark use of the minimum force necessary against Stilson, Bonzo, and the buggers sits at Aristotle's mean between cowardice and excess, while his adaptability and disregard for rules and hierarchy only count as virtues in Aristotle's framework - though his ignorance of crucial facts explains why xenocide, like his beatings, fell outside the mean.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Devil and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Jennifer Baker asks whether the Devil does ethics any good and answers no. Against the tempter hypothesis she sets the traditional virtue ethics of Plato, Aristotle, the Stoics, and the Epicureans, where bad behavior traces to habituated vice rather than demons, and the cure is consciously cultivating virtues by hitting the mean between excess and deficiency - Johnny's practiced honesty, the Evangelical cousin's marital vows. She faults the Devil as a one-size-fits-all explanation of evil, a glamour machine (via Postrel and the Romantic Satan of Blake, Byron, and Milton), and a scare tactic the Epicureans warned corrupts character, closing with Plato's divided-soul counsel to aim at long-term goods and a dismissal of Luther's spite-drinking stratagem.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
plato-tripartite-soul.title: 15. Death Begets Death
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The Bocks trace Darrow's education out of vengeance: in Plato's tripartite soul the spirited part (anger) must obey reason, and Aristotle's virtue of mildness—anger at the right things, toward the right people, for the right length of time—is the golden mean between slavish and irascible that Darrow has not yet reached. Darrow learns the difference when he hands Titus over to Cassius's vendetta and admits 'That wasn't justice': retribution in Kant's lex talionis tradition must be dispassionate and proportional, while vengeance is past-oriented and insatiable, and Darrow's own bombing of the Ganymede docks shows how troubling even his 'justice' remains. Against Darrow's violent justice-in-love the chapter sets Martin Luther King Jr.'s agape and loving-forgiveness—Sevro hanging and then forgiving Cassius, Darrow forgiving Tactus, Mustang pulling her brother's legs for a merciful death—closing with King's warning that constructive ends can never justify destructive means, and Darrow's own admission that 'the war is not over.'

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
plato-tripartite-soul.title: 11. The Unruly Woman
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Sets Plato's Republic case against the poets, with its censored storytellers, heroes who bear misfortune quietly, and worry that comedy feeds the soul's appetitive part, against Schumer's program of celebrating flaws. Young Amy raiding her roommate's hidden Twinkies and lasagna illustrates the appetitive soul overruling reason, and memoir chapters like 'Secret Bad Habits' do exactly what Plato feared by licensing readers to enjoy what they would be ashamed to confess. Li argues that the unruly women of Schumer, Dunham, Broad City, and Kaling legitimately answer Plato's ancient quarrel by representing messy, complicated female experience rather than modeling virtue.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
plato-tripartite-soul.title: 5. Another Day in the Neighborhood
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Sydney Ball and Eric Mohr interleave a college student's Tuesday with her six-year-old self watching the show: Plato's Republic (439c) on the rational part overruling the appetitive frames procrastination and lost youthful energy, Kant's autonomy frames doing what you should without being told, and Heidegger's 'They' frames her supermarket jealousy, dissolved by complimenting a stranger's shoes just as Henrietta Pussycat overcame jealousy of Grandpere's fancy granddaughter Collette (episodes 1176-1180). The lesson, learned from Mister Rogers's words about stopping, is authenticity: 'I like you just the way you are.'

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Death
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Reads Alien3's Fury 161 through impurity and contagion: Mary Douglas's 'matter out of place,' Foucault's confinement of the mad (the YY-chromosome inmates quarantined as social infection; Golic's fixation on the 'dragon' as Schopenhauer's madness of a fixed idea), Hegel and Schelling's philosophies of biology in which disease, decline, and death are necessary moments of life, and Plato's virtue-as-health of the soul. Ripley's fall into the molten lead embraces Schelling's 'indifference' of freedom and its enemy - she refuses Bishop's quack offer to 'deal with the malignancy' so Weyland-Yutani can never harvest the queen inside her.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Jeff Ewing asks which moral theory governs the novel, finding deontology absent and a contest between Graff's utilitarian recruiting pitch and a virtue-ethical focus on character: the I.F. allowed a 'Third' because it wanted Ender's traits rather than his acts. Mapping Plato's cardinal virtues and tripartite-soul politics against Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he argues Ender's minimum-force self-defense, adaptability, and disregard for hierarchy are Aristotelian virtues, while his killings of Stilson, Bonzo, and the buggers fall outside the mean only because he lacked the intellectual virtue of grasping his full situation.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Eric Silverman argues Game of Thrones explodes the storybook link between virtue and worldly happiness: Ned, 'one man in ten thousand,' is betrayed and executed, so Plato's claim that the just person is happy must mean psychic order rather than material flourishing - reason ruling spirit and appetite - as with Bran, who flourishes as a greenseer though he will never walk again. Cersei is Plato's tyrant, her soul ruled by insatiable appetite and paranoia, so no external goods can ever satisfy her, while Aristotle's correction - virtue necessary but not sufficient for eudaimonia, which also needs health, friends, and good fortune - explains why both Ned (virtue without external goods) and Cersei (goods without virtue) end up unhappy. Finally he inverts Pascal's Wager: since playing the game of thrones risks total loss (torture, humiliation, death) for limited gain, and even winning hollows you out - Robert confesses he was 'never so alive as when I was winning this throne or so dead as now that I've won it' - only a fool would play.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Southworth uses the War of Light to ask what role emotion should play in moral reasoning: Sinestro rules Korugar through fear, the Star Sapphires kidnap Sinestro Corps prisoners to convert them to love, Atrocitus's rage was forged by the Manhunters' massacre, Larfleeze hoards, and the Blue Lanterns merely hope that hope matters. On Aristotle's account every corps errs by excess: Atrocitus's rage makes him miss chances to kill Sinestro, Fatality's love benches John Stewart from saving his friends, and even the Green Lanterns' will-only ideal fails, since total fearlessness is itself vicious and Plato's picture has reason directing emotion like a general directing soldiers. He ends by defending Mill's utilitarianism: the Guardians' real failure was not detachment but pretending to be detached, and reading them as flawed 'benevolent, disinterested spectators' vindicates the Corps while explaining their moral growth after Scar and the Blackest Night.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Barkman retells Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, a shepherd's invisibility ring used to seduce the queen and murder the king, as Lord Acton's claim that absolute power corrupts, and answers with Plato: injustice disorders the tripartite soul, so the unjust sacrifice the happiness that matters most. The Guardians of the Universe are Plato's guardians writ cosmic, wise enough to rule themselves; Yalan Gur fell only when the yellow weakness was removed from his ring, Sinestro never had the wisdom ('You have never understood us'), and Hal's lapses, resigning for Carol Ferris and the Emerald Twilight rampage, are ignorance of the proper value of things rather than evil, since 'Hal's not evil... He believes he's acting for the right reasons.' The power ring is a modern Ring of Gyges, and Plato's test explains both who passes it and who fails.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Common Good versus the Greater Good
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Casts the Harry-Voldemort conflict as Socrates versus the Sophists: Thrasymachus's Republic claim that the unjust always come out ahead describes Voldemort's exploitation of his followers' trust exactly. The flayed child under the chair at King's Cross enacts Plato's afterlife justice, and the Republic's tripartite soul and cardinal virtues explain why Harry's reason-ruled courage, wisdom, and justice make the moral life the rational choice, as rational as choosing bodily health over chronic illness.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
plato-tripartite-soul.title: NOTES
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Adams uses Plato's Ring of Gyges to ask whether superpowered people have reason to be moral, answering through the tripartite soul: Claire declining credit for the fire rescue shows well-governed thumos, her calculated revenge on Brody shows logistics ruling spirit, while Sylar's uncontrollable hunger for powers is textbook epithumetikon and intemperance that makes his life spin 'super' out of control. Cases like Micah's ATM thefts and Hiro's Vegas cheating (punished by a desert beating) illustrate that vice harms the agent's own soul, since justice is the soul's health. Claire's hospital apology to Brody is read through the Pagan Golden Rule and Sophocles' Ajax: enemies can become friends, so virtue, not mere conformity, is 'only natural' for heroes and ordinary people alike.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Notes
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Argues the Underwoods' success is not far-fetched fiction but the structural outcome four critics of democracy predict. Plato's Republic supplies the spine: the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decays through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, whose love of freedom invites the tyrant — Peter Russo with his random desires is the democratic soul, Frank the tyrannical soul ruled by one illicit appetite, doomed to the fear and friendlessness Book 9 describes (which Season 3 delivers). Hobbes and Hegel then explain why monarchy may beat popular rule (the monarch's private interest aligns with the public's; the monarch lets a people will as one), and Marx reframes the whole show economically — SanCorp, Tusk and Feng as capitalists, the laid-off shipyard workers as proletariat, and AmWorks as self-interested politicians flirting with expropriation. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government gives the democratic reply — elections force responsiveness, participation educates citizens — so the burden falls on viewers to keep elections fair, the press free, and checks on unscrupulous politicians effective.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Over Four Thousand Words to Say No
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Spanakos asks whether Stark's assembling, disassembling, and reassembling of the Avengers and his unseen-hand management of Civil War make him the Republic's philosopher guardian, and answers no. Tony fits the surface profile — the gold-souled ruler of Socrates' noble lie, the elite training, indifference to money, the technê of an MIT engineer who envisions the future — but he lacks epistêmê: he never climbs from the cave's shadows to grasp the forms of justice and the good, and his appetites (womanizing in The Ultimates, 'Demon in a Bottle') show a soul where passion is not ruled by reason. His puppet mastery is reactive problem-solving guided by each situation, not philosophy, and reading him as a philosopher king is our failure to read The Republic meditatively, as Ortega y Gasset urged.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Evaluating Zelda
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Jonathan Frome tackles the paradox of fiction through Wind Waker: why do we fear Gohma, feel sad when Link leaves his grandmother on Outset Island, and feel touched when Aryll gives him her telescope, given that none of it is real? He rejects the illusion theory (we never call the police when Aryll is kidnapped), Carroll's thought theory (on-screen monsters act too fast for conscious thought), and Walton's pretend theory (we cannot voluntarily stop seeing the sail as a sail). Instead he proposes a multi-level mind — drawing on Plato's Republic (the thirsty non-drinker and Leontius and the corpses) plus Fodor's modules and Grodal's local/global appraisals — on which lower-level processes react to Hyrule as real while the global appraisal knows it is only a game.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Notes
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Writing as a mechanic, Gordon argues Max embodies Plato's Republic: like the ship-of-state navigator, only someone who knows justice may rule, and the Myth of the Charioteer — reason holding the reins over spirit and appetite — explains why the Nightrider's unchecked spirit crashes while the cool-headed, deliberative Max endures. On punishment, Plato's rejection of retaliation (the unjust should be made just, not harmed) interrogates Max's execution of Johnny the Boy, while Polemarchus's 'render to each his due' frames the just-deserts debate. Mill's harm principle then justifies Max's force against the gangs once the state and its courts have vanished, leaving Max an administrator of street justice.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
plato-tripartite-soul.title: “All That Is Solid Melts into Air”
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Dunn reads Mad Men through Plato's Republic: the passions are the 'mad masters' Cephalus describes, embodied in Pete Campbell's au pair indiscretion and remorse, and because passions cannot tell staged appearance from reality, the mimetic perfection of Don's 'You're a whore' scene with Betty grips viewers exactly as Plato feared televised drama would, watering the parts of the soul that should be ruled. He extends the point to advertising: Don's 'I make pictures where people appear to be in love' and 'love was invented by guys like me to sell nylons' work because mimesis bypasses reason and attaches feeling to images, while Aristotle's account of imitation shows drama can also train virtue by making us delight in what we should. Marx and Engels' 'all that is solid melts into air' frames the title sequence, where Don's office dissolves past advertising images revealed as empty simulacra, until the final shot restores the convincing façade of his confidence.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
plato-tripartite-soul.title: “I’m Enjoying the Story So Far, but I Have a Feeling It’s Not Going to End Well”
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: South uses 'New Amsterdam' to examine how social convention, not personal authority, constrains agency: Bert Cooper's 'New York City is a marvelous machine' and 'There are other rules... His mother is Dorothy Dyckman Campbell' reveal that Pete's value lies in a name he doesn't understand, just as Don's authority dissolves before forces neither he nor Pete consented to. Reading through Plato's Republic city-soul analogy and Adeimantus's warning that changes in music insinuate themselves 'little by little' into character and laws, the chapter shows Pete missing the worth of his old-family name, the Bethlehem Steel man missing that steel cannot be advertised like flour, and Don, despite seizing a fresh identity, quietly conforming to the suburban corporate script he claims never to have envisioned. The Kennedy-assassination pitch to Peggy ('The way that they saw themselves is gone') and Conrad Hilton's 'It's business' close on Plato's caution: the city's gears keep turning, and 'people don't change' may be the show's last word.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Alcoholica: When Sweet Amber Becomes the Master of Puppets
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Bart Engelen reads 'Master of Puppets' and Hetfield's alcoholism as a case study in akrasia: the Socratic paradox from Plato's Protagoras, Plato's divided soul from the Republic, and Aristotle's weak-willed agent who knows the good but cannot act on it all describe the addict's 'struggle within'. Using Frankfurt's distinction between first- and second-order desires, he argues Hetfield became an 'unwilling addict' - and genuinely irrational - only when he stopped endorsing his desire to drink, and that recovery works through pre-commitment strategies like rehab, avoiding drinking cues, and relying on others.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Office and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Tests the deceptions swirling around Dwight: Kant's two arguments against lying (universalizing the maxim 'lie whenever it saves face', and treating the deceived as a mere means) are set against Plato's noble lie from the Republic - Michael's empty 'Assistant Regional Manager' title may be a morally tolerable verbal lie because after 'The Fight' it restores their friendship, though it does not medicate the office as Plato's lie does the city. Epicurus' claim that only what is experienced can harm you ('what you don't know can't hurt you') is refuted by the thought of Angela's hypothetical fake love for Dwight: undetected deception is itself a harm. Finally Dwight's self-deception (believing the false promotion, Jim's telekinesis prank, the fax from his future self) is modeled by dividing the self - Plato's tripartite soul versus Descartes' simple, indivisible mind - suggesting cognitive science's modular brain as the better picture, and asking whether one can even wrong oneself.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
plato-tripartite-soul.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Reads South Park's music through the Greek doctrine of ethos: Sextus Empiricus' story of Pythagoras sobering drunk youths with slow aulos tunes and Plato's banishment of the soft Ionian and Lydian modes anticipate episodes where music directly changes behavior — Slayer's 'Raining Blood' scattering the hippie horde in 'Die Hippie Die', Cher blasted at the ATF standoff, and the Brown Noise in 'World Wide Recorder Concert'. Plato's tripartite soul maps how the Succubus's 'Morning After' spell enchants Chef's appetitive soul until the boys reverse the melody, while the Sirens' cosmic harmony in the Republic's Myth of Er links back to pitch-planet correspondences. Against Plato's view of music as inferior imitation, Schopenhauer's claim that music copies the Will itself explains why Grandpa's Enya torture in 'Death' communicates despair better than argument; authenticity judgments (Phil Collins appreciated only on Ritalin, Cartman's cynically reworded Faith + 1 hits) echo Plato's demand that music imitate the good.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Notes
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Tim Challans treats Kirk, Picard, Archer, and Janeway as case studies in moral psychology, with the captain as Plato's charioteer balancing the horses of Spock's logic and McCoy's feeling. He reads Picard's 'there are four lights' coercion in 'Chain of Command' and his Locutus guilt in 'Family' through Rawls's shame/guilt distinction and Nancy Sherman's 'moral injury', while Kirk's 'I need my pain' refusal of Sybok and Archer's Xindi-era regrets show commanders owning guilt, regret, and remorse. Drawing on Nussbaum's 'upheavals of thought' and Hume's passions, he argues that a rare, well-integrated moral psychology—pride tempered by humility, as Q's lesson in 'Tapestry' demonstrates—is what qualifies the one-in-a-million starship captain.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Notes
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: MacMullan argues Darth Plagueis is a paradox for Plato: wisdom as reason ruling spirit and appetite should be impossible for a Sith who feeds on passion, yet Plagueis stays patient, restrained, and rational for over a century. He reads Sidious's 'I will make it legal' and the Sith Code as Thrasymachus's 'justice is the advantage of the stronger,' and notes Plagueis even shares Plato's noble lie and eugenic breeding programs. Finding that Plato's prediction of self-destruction fails for Plagueis, the chapter turns to Nietzsche: master morality, the will to power, and life beyond good and evil better explain a Sith who cherishes bodily life and seeks to conquer death where Yoda and Socrates calmly disdain 'crude matter.'

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Notes
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Barkman and Alkema map Plato's Republic onto the fall of the Old Republic: the bickering Senate and Anakin's 'someone wise' exchange with Padme enact democracy's degeneration into tyranny, with Palpatine as Plato's werewolf-like protector-tyrant and Dooku's Sith name 'Tyranus' marking Thrasymachus's justice-as-strength as Sith doctrine. The Jedi approximate Plato's philosopher-guardians - courageous, temperate, reluctant to rule, surrendering their children to the Temple much like the Republic's breeding deceptions and noble lies. Justice as each part doing its own work applies to the tripartite soul as much as the state, and the chapter closes that democracy survives Endor but only if truth stays a beacon of the light side.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Notes
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Compares the noir detective's relation to Vinci with Socrates' gadfly role in Athens from the Apology, arguing both operate at the city's center and its margins as instruments of collective self-examination. Via Deleuze's 'Philosophy of Crime Novels' it contrasts the classic detective as an agent of truth (Poe, Christie) with the hard-boiled detective as an agent of action who stirs the system — Ani's undercover infiltration of the businessmen's party — forcing what Deleuze calls the 'power of falsehood' to reveal and conceal. Plato's Republic city–soul analogy then frames Velcoro, Bezzerides, and Woodrugh as disordered souls mirroring Vinci's corrupt class structure, whose cases restore equilibrium without achieving Platonic justice.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Plato and Aristotle on the Role of Soul in Taking the Rock to the Hole
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Daniel Gallagher reads Patrick Sparks's 2005 Elite Eight free-throw clank and miracle buzzer-beater through Plato's tripartite soul: the rational part failed at the line but the spirited part carried the off-balance game-tying three, while the Republic's three classes map onto basketball's workers (Steve Nash's passes), warriors (Dennis Rodman's rebounding), and rulers (John Stockton's leadership). Aristotle's four character types structure learning a jump shot - vicious, weak, self-controlled, and finally virtuous, as reason and inclination harmonize through repetition ('we are what we repeatedly do') - and the golden mean governs shot selection between the ball hog and the compulsive passer, with Michael Jordan as the player whose habituated instincts find the mean. Against Kantian armchair ethics, the jump shot and Kareem's sky hook were discovered by trial and error: virtuous performers set the standard, and we become good shooters by watching and imitating them.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Paul Cantor and Peter Hufnagel use Nietzsche's essay 'Homer's Contest' to argue that the competitive spirit the Greeks called thumos links philosophy and athletics, presenting Plato's dialogues as 'the Olympics of philosophy' in which Socrates is the last man standing. They trace thumos as the spirited third part of the soul in Plato's Republic, the guardians' quality that reason must tame through gymnastics and music, and as the force Socrates enlists to win the thumotic youths Glaucon and Adeimantus to philosophy. They then read Achilles in the Iliad and its funeral games in Book XXIII as a build-up/discharge/calm cycle of thumos, offering athletics as Homer's alternative channel for the same warlike energy.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Heather Reid interprets the Olympic Charter's first Fundamental Principle through the ancient ideal of aretE, arguing the metaphysical structure of sport, contests that create purposeless obstacles, exists to cultivate and celebrate human excellence rather than to beat opponents or make money. Citing Plato the wrestler, Suits's definition of game-playing, and Homer's funeral games, she maps five virtues onto sport: eusEbeia (reverence for ideals beyond oneself), andreia (courageous endurance in agOn), sOphrosynE (harmonious power and control), dikaiosynE (justice as rule-order and proper function), and sophia (the athlete's pursuit of truth about human capacity, akin to 'flow'). The goal she proposes is the 'Olympian soul.'

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Spartacus and the Second Part of the Soul Gordon Braden
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Braden argues that Kubrick's Spartacus, despite its chaotic production, coheres around Plato's tripartite soul as mediated by Plutarch's analysis of Roman politics. He maps the film's rivalries onto to thymoeides, the soul's 'second' spirited part governed by philotimia (love of honor): Crassus's obsessive hamilla with Gracchus, and his skewed contest with Spartacus over Varinia and Antoninus. Reading Draba's trident-throw and Crassus's closing 'now I fear him' as the spirited part's competitiveness overrunning reason, Braden shows the gladiatorial paired combat mirroring republican politics on its way to the Principate.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
plato-tripartite-soul.title: On Being Horrible (and an Angel)
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The chapter runs Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge from the Republic against the Whedonverse: invisibility in 'Out of Mind, Out of Sight' and 'Gone' (where even Buffy takes a self-serving 'vacation from herself'), the invincibility ring in 'In the Dark' that Angel destroys rather than uses, and the Buffy-Faith body switch in 'Who Are You?' as the unjust person with a virtuous reputation versus the just person misunderstood. Plato's tripartite-soul answer is only partly confirmed—Faith spirals into torment after killing the deputy mayor, but Saffron cons without any inner turmoil—so the chapter turns to Aristotle: the good life needs external goods, above all friendship and community. This explains why Whedon's wrongdoers (Woody in Toy Story, Jayne in 'Ariel,' Gunn, Stark, Buffy in 'Revelations') must atone before their communities, why Mal's 'you only need a few [good people]' rebukes Saffron, and why both Dr. Horrible and Captain Hammer are tragic—each lives alone and friendless, having squandered Penny.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Kowalski likens Goodfellas' Henry Hill to Plato's Gyges: both act immorally with near-total impunity, posing Glaucon's challenge in the Republic of why one should be just when one can escape all consequences. He applies Plato's tripartite soul (appetitive, spirited, rational) to Henry (runaway appetite/cocaine), Tommy (overstretched spirit, killing Billy Batts and Spider out of wounded pride) and cool, untroubled Paulie, treating them as the disharmonious 'unbalanced self.' Against the objection that these gangsters seem happy, he deploys Plato's health/happiness analogy and the feeling-happy vs being-happy distinction to argue they suffer 'cancer of the soul' and cannot be truly happy.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Conard uses Mean Streets' guilt-ridden Charlie to survey conceptions of unhappiness against three definitions of happiness: beatitude (Aquinas), pleasure (Mill's hedonism), and flourishing (Aristotle's eudaimonia). He reads Charlie as damned in his own Catholic eyes, then invokes Nietzsche's Genealogy that religion manufactures guilt from internalized instinct, Plato's disordered soul and akrasia to explain Charlie's conflicting desires, and Schopenhauer's and Freud's pessimism that suffering is our natural state. He argues Charlie reaches dysdaimonia by acquiring vices and pursuing an ignoble (gangster) life, closing with Plato's Symposium and Sartre's facticity/transcendence to cast unhappiness as an ontological lack at the heart of human desire.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Skoble argues that A Simple Plan dramatizes Plato's Republic almost exactly: justice as psychological harmony among the parts of the soul, and injustice as self-destructive disharmony. When Hank, Jacob, and Lou keep found money, they enact Thrasymachus's and the Ring of Gyges challenge (would you be unjust if you'd never be caught?). Hank miscalculates his own self-interest, mistaking wealth for happiness; the deception, distrust, and murders that follow (including Hank killing Jacob) show that even the criminal who evades capture is ruined by his corrupted character, exactly as Plato predicts.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
plato-tripartite-soul.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Braden argues that Kubrick's Spartacus, despite its chaotic production, coheres around Plato's tripartite soul as mediated by Plutarch's analysis of Roman politics. He maps the film's gladiatorial paria and the Crassus–Gracchus rivalry onto to thymoeides, the spirited/competitive middle part of the soul that Plutarch renders as philotimia (love of honor) driving the alpha males of classical history. The central thesis is that Crassus (Laurence Olivier) is ruled by this competitive second part: his skewed hamilla with Spartacus plays out not just on the battlefield but through the erotic triangle over Varinia and Antoninus ('he steals my boy, I steal his girl'), so the Republic falls to a coup driven by the restless, honor-seeking part of the soul.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
plato-tripartite-soul.title: Action and Integrity in The Fugitive
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Skoble challenges the standard view of noir as morally ambiguous, arguing each episode of The Fugitive is a self-contained morality play in which Richard Kimble makes tough decisions by clearly defined standards of right and wrong. He tests ethical frameworks against the episodes: Kant's categorical imperative cannot capture Kimble, who lies in every episode to survive, whereas Aristotle's virtue ethics explains his trained emotional responses, as when he tells the migrant workers in 'Ill Wind' 'For a doctor, every life is worth saving' while saving Lieutenant Gerard from a pitchfork, and again in 'Corner of Hell' from moonshiners. Kimble's integrity, understood as fidelity in action to principles reached through reflection, reconciles his lawbreaking with his morality and, via Plato's account in the Republic of the just person who 'harmonizes the three parts of himself,' constitutes the psychological wholeness that sustains his four-year quest. The essay closes with the finale, where Kimble clears his name, Gerard kills the one-armed man, and Kimble finally walks in sunlight.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
plato-tripartite-soul.title: 11. A Punk by Any Other Name would Smell as Rotten
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Grewal treats punk as a comedy of self-negation - a counter-culture that must negate even itself - and traces its lineage through Plato's Leontius story (thumos, the spirited part of the soul, dividing a man against his own eyes as he gorges on corpses, punks as 'living dead') to Diogenes the Cynic, 'Socrates gone mad', whose exile, public masturbation, dog-persona, and mocking of Plato make him Diogenes the Punk. Beauvoir's adulteress from The Second Sex and Rousseau of the Reveries supply the punk logic of adultery and exile - a continual breaking of attachments down to Socrates's barefoot ignorance - so that punk, mocking any ascent from the cave, becomes the ruthless pursuit of the rootless.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
plato-tripartite-soul.title: 17. Is Morality for Suckers
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The chapter reads Jimmy through Plato's Republic, likening his resolve to stop letting conscience stop him to Glaucon's Ring of Gyges thesis that people act immorally whenever they can escape detection, as when Jimmy dodges 'bullets' in his Matrix-like winning speech. Using Plato's tripartite soul, it diagnoses Jimmy as ruled by his appetitive and spirited parts rather than reason, hence lacking self-control and unable to find morality pleasant in itself. It then tests and finds wanting Plato's arguments (contemplative pleasure, connectedness, the immortality of the rational part) that a healthy, reason-ruled soul is both moral and happiest, granting Jimmy's intense scamming pleasures their pull.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
plato-tripartite-soul.title: 1. Is Rationality an Illusion
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Litman and Zelcer argue that Foundation dramatizes Hume's thesis that reason is the slave of the passions: the robot Demerzel (Daneel Olivaw) and the mutant Mule accomplish history by directly amplifying emotions like Seldon's pride, after which their victims' reason confabulates rational justifications (motivated reasoning). They trace the emotion-versus-reason debate from Plato's tripartite charioteer soul through Aristotle's rational animal and Christian moral psychology to Hume's secularized version, and use the Wye rebellion and Pritcher's converted loyalty to show emotional manipulation works like an optical illusion, persisting even once the victim knows about it.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
plato-tripartite-soul.title: But Isn’t It Only Natural
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Adams uses the superpowered characters of Heroes to teach Plato's Republic. The Ring of Gyges question, whether one with the power to escape consequences has reason to be just, is posed by Sylar, Daphne, and Hiro cheating in Vegas. Adams maps Plato's tripartite soul, thumos, logistikon, and epithumetikon, onto Claire's courage and wisdom and Sylar's ruinous intemperance, arguing justice is psychic health so vices grow worse the more power one has. He adds the 'Pagan Golden Rule' (help friends, harm enemies) to read Claire's apology to Brody, concluding virtue is natural to a well-ordered human soul and is its own reward.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
plato-tripartite-soul.title: BLUES
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: The editors' introduction argues blues and philosophy are close kin in confronting the struggling soul. It reads Lightnin' Hopkins's 'Lonesome Dog' through Plato's tripartite soul from Republic IX — the howling 'dog' is the appetitive part — but claims the blues achieves a 'blues harmony' rather than Plato's reason-ruled harmony. It casts Socrates, calm before execution in the Phaedo, as having a 'bluesy sensibility' that rises above worry through philosophizing, invokes Bentham's claim that the capacity to suffer is what matters morally to gloss the blues as knowledge of suffering, and likens the blues' triumphant affirmation to Nietzsche's positivity.

plato-tripartite-soul.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
plato-tripartite-soul.title: But Isn’t It Only Natural
plato-tripartite-soul.relation: Don Adams uses Heroes' superpowered characters (who could commit perfect crimes like Gyges with his invisibility ring) to argue Plato's case that virtue is its own reward. He maps Plato's tripartite soul onto the characters: Claire's thumos (spirit/honor) tempered by logistikos (reason) yields courage and wisdom, while Sylar's ruling appetite (his hunger for powers) is intemperance and injustice that makes his life spin out of control. Reading justice as psychic health, and glossing the 'Pagan Golden Rule' (help friends, harm enemies, but enemies may become friends), Adams argues it is 'only natural' for even the powerful to be virtuous rather than exploit others.

will-to-power.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
will-to-power.title: Persuasion As Drama
will-to-power.relation: Karl Schudt contends that Nietzsche's genealogy of slave morality cannot be refuted by reason (Nietzsche denies reason itself), so drama must persuade where dialectic cannot: a believable story of a Nietzschean life acts as an empathic experiment. Faith is constructed as the Nietzschean ideal — strong, healthy, ruthless ('Find a couple of studs, use them, and discard them'), dismissive of reflection ('You think too much') — serving Mayor Wilkins, whom Schudt reads as a genuine Übermensch sacrificing mankind's mass for his ascension. Watching her world collapse (the accidental killing in 'Bad Girls', her mirror scene in 'Who Are You?', the torture of Wesley and confession on Angel) gives viewers an Aristotelian pity-and-fear warning that the unjust life ends badly, completing her 'leap from Nietzsche to Socrates.'

will-to-power.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
will-to-power.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Eric Bronson places Tolkien among the 'sometimes merry' existentialists: Nietzsche's artist who says Yes amid catastrophe and needs 'the power to forget', Jaspers on machines estranging us from our past, and Arendt on Eichmann's obedient inhumanity and the few who create joy in dark times. The elves' songs in Rivendell and Lórien are joy born of sorrow and dispossession - Galadriel suffers because she remembers too much, trying to 'embalm time', while Arwen forgoes immortality for Aragorn. Her refusal of the Ring ('I will diminish, and go into the West, and remain Galadriel') embodies the existentialist affirmation: trust your own light, know what to remember and what to forget.

will-to-power.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
will-to-power.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Douglas Blount tests Nietzsche against Sauron, whose forging and grasp of the One Ring - even striving to supplant Ilúvatar - enacts the will to power, exploitation, the death of God, and the ideal of the Übermensch. He argues that in Middle-earth the naked will to power appears not as a brave new humanity but as plain evil, and that Tolkien answers Nietzsche not with argument but with a rival portrait: Gandalf's self-sacrifice on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm, Frodo's mercy to Gollum that becomes Middle-earth's salvation, and Sam's humble refusal of 'Samwise the Strong'. Judged by Nietzsche's own aesthetic criterion of taste, Tolkien's vision of community, humility, and abnegation is the more beautiful - and therefore the more compelling - portrait of reality.

will-to-power.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
will-to-power.title: An Empire of Fear and Trembling
will-to-power.relation: Cameron reads the Emperor's dominion through Hegel's master-slave dialectic and struggle for recognition: fear is the Empire's currency, from Alderaan's destruction as visible demonstration ('fear will keep the local systems in line') to Vader's deliberately undefined threats ('The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am'), while hatred binds the Sith Master to Maul, Dooku, and Vader. Because the master can never win recognition from an unequal slave, Palpatine's will-to-power rule is a historical dead end, whereas the slave - Anakin laboring in Watto's shop, Luke overcoming his fear in the cave and under Yoda - can transform himself through work and courage. Vader's final turn is thus his achievement of a new self-consciousness, recognizing himself as 'something other than a slave' at the moment Luke's unshakeable faith forces the truth on him.

will-to-power.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
will-to-power.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Tim Mosteller identifies Lewis's Tao from The Abolition of Man with Aquinas's Natural Law, an objective moral order knowable by all rational beings, and maps three responses onto Narnian characters: wholehearted acceptance (Peter, Lucy, Tirian, Reepicheep), selective 'Innovators' who pick and choose (Shift and Miraz, with Nietzsche's invented master-values as the philosophical extreme), and total rejection by 'Conditioners' (Ginger the Cat, who reverts to dumb beast, and Uncle Andrew, who loses the animals' speech). Individual laws are illustrated by Mr. Tumnus freeing Lucy, Aslan scratching Aravis for her gladness at the slave girl's beating, Nikabrik's treacherous Realpolitik, Lucy's eavesdropping spell in the Magician's book, and Jill's showing-off at the cliff.

will-to-power.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
will-to-power.title: A Meditation on the Word
will-to-power.relation: Randall Auxier and Eileen Townsend fictionalize the history of philosophy as vampire predation in letters, emails, and IMs (1983-2009) between the 800-year-old Etienne Lavec - a student of Siger de Brabant who drained Thomas Aquinas over the Summa's Treatise on Angels, which wrote vampires out of existence - and Paulie, a freshman turned at Memphis State. Lavec recounts tasting Pico, Spinoza, Hegel, and the willing Kierkegaard, sparing Nietzsche who 'stole some of my ideas about free death', and contrasts vampire self-knowledge (embracing desire) with the Socratic beginning in affirmed ignorance. The centerpiece is Foucault: Lavec summarizes his genealogies of how institutions create the sick, the mad, the prisoner, and the pervert, fails to drain him, and is then haunted for decades by posthumous publications, taunting 'nietzsche26' emails, and finally a catacombs trap - power/knowledge that refuses to die. Lavec's embedded 'Meditation on the Word' recasts the Logos of John's Gospel so that vampires are the uncreated darkness at the boundary of the divine Word, pure self-grounding desire 'beyond good and evil', while the closing Twilight-era chats satirize Stephenie Meyer's sparkling, abstinent Edward as Foucauldian 'sin by words'.

will-to-power.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
will-to-power.title: James Bond and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Matheson examines the 'master animal' imagery saturating Fleming's novels - Donovan Grant's reptilian physique in From Russia with Love, Blofeld's animal magnetism, villains feeding victims to sharks and crocodiles - as an exercise in Social Darwinism where, as Mr. Big puts it, wolves live by wolf's laws and sheep call them criminals. Using Nietzsche's Übermensch, the blond beast of the Genealogy, and Zarathustra's self-overcoming, she distinguishes Apollonian eaters like M (who curb appetite) from doomed Dionysian gluttons like Giuseppe Petacchi, arguing that Fleming makes dining and will power the test of who counts as an Overman. Bond differs from his megalomaniac foes only in keeping his own will to power and stomach under control, and the chapter closes by warning that Hollywood's romanticizing of the master animal keeps us valuing a brutally primitive masculinity Fleming himself mocked as a 'cardboard booby'.

will-to-power.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
will-to-power.title: James Bond and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Landa argues that Bond's apparent defense of democracy against Übermensch villains is itself profoundly Nietzschean: Bond's exquisite, disciplined hedonism (the Minton-china breakfast, disgust at Mr. Du Pont's 'eating like a pig'), his obsessive competitiveness at baccarat and golf, and his contempt for mass democracy mark him as an aristocratic bourgeois hero in Nietzsche's mold. The gambling scenes enact a Calvinist logic of predestination in which losing at Casino Royale devastates Bond because his very worth depends on winning, and the 'human muck' he defends at Blades turns out to be the exclusive elite. Dr. No, Mr. Big, Drax, and Blofeld are cast as evil, explicit Nietzscheans while Bond serves a good, unspoken Western Nietzscheanism - so the Cold War showdown with Blofeld, who invokes Nietzsche by name, is elitism fighting counterfeit elitism, making Bond 'a secret agent in the service of Nietzscheanism'.

will-to-power.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
will-to-power.title: Rupert’s Response and Responsibility
will-to-power.relation: Biderman and Jacobowitz read Rope through Nietzsche: Brandon and Philip strangle their classmate David as would-be Nietzschean supermen, acting on mentor Rupert Cadell's cocktail-party theory that murder can be an art for a superior few. The chapter explains the will to power, the Ubermensch, and the death of God, then argues Brandon is no superman: he kills from weakness and a bully's need for an audience, mistaking crass destruction for the refined self-creation Nietzsche demanded, just as the fascist appropriation of Nietzsche fails. Rupert's horrified final speech, renouncing 'superior or inferior beings' and insisting each of us is 'a separate human being,' raises whether a teacher can disavow responsibility when students act out his provocative ideas: ideas have consequences, and the only true test of a philosophy is whether we can live by it.

will-to-power.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
will-to-power.title: Will You Say Yes
will-to-power.relation: Bruce finds Nietzsche's eternal return in the NES Zelda's clockless, endlessly restartable structure: the same game recurs every time you press start, yet since the player changes, each playthrough manifests the forces anew, and the demon's question 'do you desire this once more?' becomes 'do you will to play once more?'. Link's growth through eight dungeons to face Ganon is read as will-to-power, personal strength and self-overcoming rather than mere domination, and saying yes to the struggle is amor fati. Against Plato's two-worlds doctrine of Forms and the Christian after-worldly (both Nietzsche's targets), the original Zelda offers no guide, no Bible, and no linear time to a final judgment: this looped world is the only one, so it must be affirmed.

will-to-power.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
will-to-power.title: What Mr. Colbert Has Taught Us (Besides Everything)
will-to-power.relation: In full truthiness voice, Michaud explains Colbert's failed 2008 presidential run — the South Carolina Democratic Executive Council's 13-3 vote keeping him off the ballot — as exactly what Nietzsche predicted: the resentful weak, the 'sheep,' hold the super-man down by redefining meekness as strength. He walks through will-to-power as self-overcoming, the lambs-and-birds-of-prey parable from the Genealogy, and Christianity as slave morality, then 'corrects' Nietzsche by relocating slave morality in the liberal media rather than God, ending with Colbert as the man of the future who 'affirms life without resentment.'

will-to-power.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
will-to-power.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Auxier argues the trilogy is narrated on a Nietzschean lattice rather than being a mere inverted Milton: after tracing the Paradise Lost, Genesis 6, and Pseudepigrapha sources (Azazel as the model for Asriel, Metatron from Third Enoch, Dust from Milton's warring particles), he reads Mrs. Coulter's speech to Father MacPhail about seeking God out and giving him 'the gift of death' as Nietzsche's death of God fused with a description of Nietzsche's own final dementia. Will and Lyra become overman and overwoman beyond good and evil: Will rises by his will and his willingness to kill (the alethiometer's verdict 'He is a murderer' makes him a worthy companion), while Lyra commands both truth and lies, the alethiometer embodying truth as 'a mobile army of metaphors.' But the chapter's payoff is critical: Pullman does not endorse Nietzsche, since in a world where the will to power dominates, the overwoman Mrs. Coulter has no place and falls with Asriel and Metatron into the Abyss, while Xaphania's teaching offers a disciplined, workful imagination as an alternative.

will-to-power.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
will-to-power.title: Stop That Persistent Clicking
will-to-power.relation: Paul Brown argues that Warcraft II begins by saving the player from boredom and ends by offering something like eternal happiness. Kierkegaard's 'rotation of crops' from Either/Or explains why Medivh and the Orcs grow bored into war and how console play relieves the living room's intellectual dead zone, with Heidegger supplying the definition of boredom; Nietzsche's will to power accounts both for the player's overt domination of peasants and sheep ('Stop that persistent clicking') and for the sublimated, ascetic self-overcoming of mastering the game, which Maslow redescribes as growth-needs and peak experiences. Kierkegaard's third, religious existence stage — subjective faith giving 'eternal happiness' — is playfully applied to becoming 'contemporary' with the game itself.

will-to-power.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
will-to-power.title: A (Bronx) Cheer to the Red Sox “Without Whom, Not as Much”
will-to-power.relation: Writing as a Yankees fan, Konig asks what makes a championship worth wanting: after Schopenhauer's picture of endless striving as suffering, he brings in Richard Taylor (meaning lies in the activity itself, never its completion) and then Nietzsche's will to power, which seeks worthy resistance to overcome. Thought experiments—a childhood 'big game' that turns out to be tee-ball, and the 2004 Sox trouncing the minor-league Atlantic League—show a title without worthy opposition is hollow. Hence the Yankees' twentieth-century dominance would mean nothing without the Red Sox as the sustained, worthy enemy (Bucky Dent, the Pedro-Zimmer melee, the 2004 ALCS collapse included).

will-to-power.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
will-to-power.title: A Meditation on the Word
will-to-power.relation: Randall Auxier and Eileen Townsend stage the chapter as fiction: letters, emails, IMs, and texts (1983-2009) between the ancient vampire Étienne Lavec and the newly turned Memphis student Paulie, through which shifting vampire pop culture — Anne Rice, Buffy, True Blood, and Twilight's sparkling, animal-only Cullens — is debated. Lavec's embedded 'Meditation on the Word' recasts the Johannine Logos so that vampires are pure desire, the uncreated darkness at the border of God's light, and his biography enacts the thesis: a Latin Averroist student of Siger de Brabant who drained Aquinas over the Summa's Treatise on Angels writing vampires out of existence, and a collector who hunted or interviewed Royce, Pico della Mirandola, Descartes, Spinoza, Hegel, Kierkegaard, and Nietzsche, whose 'free death' and 'beyond good and evil' he claims as stolen vampire ideas. The running gag and argument is Foucault, whose account of institutions (medicine, psychology, prison) creating their objects Lavec endorses as the order of desire, but who, half-undead after Lavec's failed bite and taunting him anonymously as 'nietzsche26', finally lures him into a trap in the Paris catacombs.

will-to-power.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
will-to-power.title: Oh to Be a Gooner
will-to-power.relation: Kilpatrick reads Nietzsche's madman's question 'what sacred games shall we have to invent?' as answered by the stadium: after the death of God, soccer has replaced religion as the shared narrative where modern communities make and worship heroes. Using The Birth of Tragedy, he reads a goal as an Apollonian–Dionysian fusion—the scorer's individuated ecstasy merging with the collective joy of teammates and fans—and, on Nietzsche's claim that existence is justified only as an aesthetic phenomenon, argues the game is defensible only when played creatively and artistically rather than by negative, win-at-all-costs tactics. Nietzsche's rejection of nationalism (the state as 'the new idol', the 'good European', Zarathustra's 'children's land') means club over country, and Wenger's Arsenal—with its dietary and training laboratory at London Colney cultivating an Overman, its Invincibles season, and its young, passport-blind signings—emerges as the club Nietzsche would support through its very will-to-power.

will-to-power.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
will-to-power.title: Life A Celebration
will-to-power.relation: Reads John Simm's Master as Nietzsche's most advanced nihilist: having seen the universe die at Utopia, he judges life valueless and converts ressentiment into a joyful will to nothingness, dancing to the Scissor Sisters over his victims. The Ninth Doctor's arc in 'Dalek' mirrors this danger ('What are you changing into?') until he refuses to destroy the last Dalek, beginning his yes-saying to finite life. Following Deleuze's reading, the Doctor defeats the Master not with Martha's gun but with forgiveness ('I forgive you') and her storytelling network, embodying the Übermensch who carries his affirmation into the abyss of the end of the universe.

will-to-power.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
will-to-power.title: Deeply Dissecting Dexter
will-to-power.relation: Deborah Mellamphy uses Nietzsche's masks - 'every profound spirit needs a mask,' the will to power that requires deception for self-preservation - to explain both why Dexter's crafted normalcy works and why only the characters conscious of their own masks (Doakes, Lila, Brian, Trinity) see through his. Nietzsche's perspectivism and 'Truth and Lie in the Extra-Moral Sense' then dissolve any true self beneath the mask: if truths are 'worn out metaphors,' Dexter's question 'If you play a role long enough... does it ever become real?' has no stable answer. Following Sarah Kofman's reading, the chapter asks whether we are all 'but this veil itself' and concludes that Dexter goes a step beyond Nietzsche by locating the truth of identity in the many layered masks themselves.

will-to-power.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
will-to-power.title: That Naive Cube! How Long Must I Suffer This
will-to-power.relation: Nicholas Michaud inverts the show's morality through Nietzsche: Plankton's tenacity, ambition and self-overcoming make him a super-organism driven by the will to power (traced to Schopenhauer's will to live), while Bikini Bottom's lionizing of SpongeBob's mediocrity is slave morality that judges by intentions to keep the strong down. Quoting the lambs and birds of prey from On the Genealogy of Morals and the 'incurably mediocre' passage from Beyond Good and Evil, he argues Plankton is the unsung hero who treats SpongeBob as an equal, Krabs a mere exploiter — and SpongeBob, who makes mediocrity contagious, the true villain.

will-to-power.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
will-to-power.title: His Work Is Its Own Reward
will-to-power.relation: Timothy Sexton argues the real Overman is not Doyle's flat 'calculating machine' but Jeremy Brett's Granada Holmes: the sneer with which he frees the Blue Carbuncle thief and the 'I am not retained by the police' outburst show him stepping beyond the herd's good-and-evil after the death of God. Brett's theatrical style, from the pivot before Lady Brackenstall in 'The Abbey Grange' to 'Gentlemen, we can do better than that' in 'The Norwood Builder', enacts Nietzsche's grand art of giving style to one's character, sublimating nihilistic dread into the pleasure of proving superiority. Where Rathbone-era Sherlocks solve crimes for truth, justice and the Victorian Way, Brett's Holmes makes the work its own reward, satisfying Nietzsche's demand that the Overman 'attain satisfaction with himself'.

will-to-power.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
will-to-power.title: Dandelions on My Cloud
will-to-power.relation: Uses 'Dandelion'—truth as a bright yellow flower that blows away—to mark the withering of Enlightenment confidence in plain, visible truth under deconstruction. Kierkegaard's 'truth is subjectivity' explains why truth on 'Get Off of My Cloud' cannot be shared directly ('Don't hang around 'cause two's a crowd'), and Nietzsche goes further: there is no truth to find, only wills to power making truths—'you can't always get what you want... you just might find you get what you need.'

will-to-power.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
will-to-power.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Framed by Dick's wait in a Klosterman signing line, the chapter asks how a critic acquires rock-star power. Plato's Ion supplies the magnet chain of inspiration (muse, poet, rhapsode, spectator), which puts Klosterman near the spectator end — he 'only got to second base' with the muse Thalia until Downtown Owl. Nietzsche's master and slave moralities then explain the critic's ascent: Klosterman is the cunning slave-priest who seizes power from warrior-artists through wit and articulate opinion, exactly as priestly values overthrew warrior values. Dick half-endorses the diagnosis, admits he prefers the slave's world of safety, and concludes that power — even the power to sell books and pay rent — is how we stay alive.

will-to-power.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
will-to-power.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: A close scene-reading of the pilot argues Nietzsche's will to power explains Walt's transformation: he is repeatedly 'out willed' by Chad's chair-scrape, Bogdan's register demands, and Hank's birthday-party toasts, until the cancer diagnosis powers his 'Fuck you... and your eyebrows!' reversal at the car wash. Walt's decision to cook, declared to Jesse as 'I am awake', is presented as the Ubermensch's creation of his own morality - family provision over society's 'drugs are bad' - and the phosphine-gas killing of Emilio as his ultimate exertion of will. The chapter concludes Nietzsche would have been a fan of the show.

will-to-power.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
will-to-power.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Scores Walt and Mad Men's Don Draper against Nietzsche's Overman and Last Man: Roger Sterling (and the early, passive Jesse) are Last Men, while Walt moves from weak negation of the status quo to genuine self-affirmation - 'going under' in the 'Crawl Space' crawl hole and emerging in 'Face Off' having poisoned Brock and out-created Gus, which the chapter takes as proof that in a capitalist world two creators cannot coexist. Killing Gus is framed as accepting the eternal recurrence of joy and sorrow, willing even his own bad acts. Don, by contrast, negates far more than he creates, and the chapter ends by asking why viewers empathize with the one failed Overman and find the other inspiring.

will-to-power.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
will-to-power.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Rard tests whether objective morality survives the apocalypse by running four theories against Season Two: Plato's Forms explain universal truths about walkers ('walkers survive so long as their brains are relatively undamaged') but cannot handle white lies or changed circumstances, and Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Rick's rush from the shot Carl as rashness and Shane's supply run as courage, yet virtues prove relative and luck-dependent in a collapsed world. Natural law founders on clashing intuitions — Merle's racism and Hershel's barn of walkers each claim self-evidence. The chapter's center is Nietzschean: Hershel's barn is slave morality that pities the 'sick,' Maggie breaks from it, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and opening of the barn enact a will-to-power master morality without joy, while Rick alone moves toward amor fati — embracing the world as it is, refusing guilt over Lori's affair, and insisting the baby be born into the Walk Age.

will-to-power.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
will-to-power.title: The Wire and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Clifton measures Omar against four Nietzschean criteria for the overman: as a free spirit he is 'in the wind, so to speak,' detached from home, money, and eventually even lovers like Brandon and Butchie; as a non-dogmatist about truth he uses it as a tool, lying under oath at Bird's trial yet sparing Brother Mouzone when the lie no longer holds; and as a noble of the Genealogy he is an active hunter who embraces the will to power, telling Wee-Bey 'you come at the king, you best not miss.' But Omar fails the fourth test, value-creation: his code keeps the good/evil scale intact rather than overturning it, so in the Three Metamorphoses he remains the lion who slays 'Thou Shalt' but never becomes the value-creating child. The verdict, in Nietzsche's own phrase, is that Omar is noble but 'human, all too human.'

will-to-power.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
will-to-power.title: Psych and Philosophy
will-to-power.relation: Ruiz casts Lassiter as Nietzsche's slave - his worth defined reactively against Shawn, his advice that 'all romance ends in despair or death' reproducing the Judeo-Christian slave revolt in morality that turned weakness into virtue - and Shawn as the master, a self-propelled wheel who bakes a pineapple cake in an Easy Bake oven for nineteen hours whether or not anyone is watching.
