utilitarianism.relation: Littmann turns the Doctor-companion relationship into a mirror for animal ethics: since the Doctor stands to humans as we stand to animals—deciding for Rose without asking in 'The End of the World,' implanting nanorecorders unconsented in 'Day of the Moon'—every standard justification for our treatment of animals (might makes right, superior intelligence, natural predation) would equally license him to eat Clara cutlets, yet he instead defends humanity from Daleks, Cybermen, and naturally predatory species like the Weeping Angels, the Minotaur, and the Swarm. Finding no non-arbitrary place to draw the intelligence line—what of the human-level gangers, the enslaved Ood, or mentally disabled humans?—he endorses Bentham's utilitarian suffering standard from 'Can they suffer?', concluding that eating humans fails the utilitarian test because the pleasure cannot outweigh a whole life's happiness, and that whether eating meat passes that same test is the question our own treatment of animals must answer.

utilitarianism.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
utilitarianism.title: 15. The Way of the Doctor Is Deception
utilitarianism.relation: Dodge takes Rule #1 - the Doctor lies - through the major theories of lying: Bernard Williams's definition (asserting what you believe false with intent to deceive), Aristotle's claim that all lies are base, Kant's categorical imperative and respect for persons (even the Vinvocci's shimmer disguises in 'The End of Time' abuse trust), and Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus, which condemns the faked death at Lake Silencio ('The Impossible Astronaut') for the grief it caused Amy and Rory yet rewards the greater happiness it made possible. Against the absolutists he sets Plato's Noble Lie from the Republic - the elite falsehood that keeps society functioning - as what the Doctor emulates by deceiving the universe into thinking him dead ('The Wedding of River Song'), and Nietzsche's point in Human, All Too Human that lying is ethically neutral when the pretense is sustainable, as when the Doctor hides the ganger-Amy switch from Rory ('The Almost People'). The upshot: the Doctor's lies are wrong in themselves but routinely justified by the good they do, which is why sometimes the hero lies.

utilitarianism.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
utilitarianism.title: 15. Tell the Truth at All Costs
utilitarianism.relation: Bowman argues Candor is the most philosophically important faction because its absolute honesty is Kant's ethics: truthfulness as a perfect duty grounded in free will, making even politeness 'deception in pretty packaging,' and forbidding a lie even when the Erudite come to Merciless Mart hunting Tris - which mirrors Kant's reply to Benjamin Constant that one must not lie even to the murderer at the door. Against this he sets Aristotle's virtue ethics, where truth bows to wisdom, justice, and fortitude when the choice is handing hidden Jews to the SS, and Bentham's utilitarianism, which Amity enacts when it lies at the gates to keep the peace and save lives. The Candor Manifesto's 'web of individual-to-individual relationships' and Kant's kingdom of ends explain why universal honesty alone could make truth safe - and why Christina, the Candor, is the one left standing when the city's deception finally destroys it.

utilitarianism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
utilitarianism.title: 4. Lie or Die
utilitarianism.relation: Hawkes uses Rick's bar confrontation with Dave and Tony in 2.8 'Nebraska' to ask when lying is right, after defining lying through the Governor's white flag at the National Guard camp and Eugene's false cure claim. He rejects moral relativism - the Claimers' rules, Terminus's 'butcher or cattle', the Governor's 'we will do the only thing' - because it forbids criticizing rapists and cannibals and erases moral progress, then finds utilitarianism shaky given Eugene's unforeseen deadly consequences and Rick's refusal to hand Michonne to the Governor at 'Arrow on the Doorpost.' He defends a duty-based deontology in which the duty to protect the farm overrides the duty not to lie, and closes with Robert Kirkman's own lie about an alien invasion that got The Walking Dead published.

utilitarianism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
utilitarianism.title: 13. Carol’s Transformation
utilitarianism.relation: Delfino and Lesinski trace Carol's arc from abused wife (Ed's beatings, Sophia's death, "I didn't think I could be strong") to the judge-jury-executioner she once refused to be, reading the transformation through Aristotle's claim in the Nicomachean Ethics that repeated actions forge moral character. They then evaluate her killings: the murder of Karen and David fails on both act- and rule-utilitarian grounds (it did not stop the flu, and Glenn and Sasha survived while the group was shattered), whereas killing the delusional Lizzie is defensible both utilitarianly and by Aquinas's natural-law exception that an evildoer may be killed for the welfare of the whole community when no public authority remains. Her confession to Tyreese and Tyreese's forgiveness complete the phoenix rebirth symbolized by the burning walkers in "Consumed."

utilitarianism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
utilitarianism.title: 14. Carol Didn’t Care
utilitarianism.relation: Yuen grants that executing Lizzie was not wrong but argues Carol fell short of a moral ideal by ignoring Lizzie's preferences, deploying R.M. Hare's move from Bentham's happiness-maximizing classic utilitarianism to preference utilitarianism - illustrated by the group refusing to let Eugene test Aaron's water in "Them." Since Lizzie prefers a reanimating death ("She didn't hurt her brain"), a heart shot like the group's courtesy to Jim would have maximized preference satisfaction without endangering anyone. He answers the objections that Lizzie is a child and that walkers are mindless: her attempts to reason and her coherent post-apocalyptic values (like generational value shifts on homosexuality via Aaron and Eric) deserve respect, and whether a walker would still be Lizzie matters less than that the preference is hers now.

utilitarianism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
utilitarianism.title: Walker Bite. Are You Being Saved
utilitarianism.relation: Callens reads Beth's captivity at Grady Memorial in "Slabtown" as an allegory of the American healthcare system: patients like Noah are rescued, then enslaved by insurmountable medical debt, forced to work off charges that never end. Lt. Lerner's "No, but you needed it" and her non-medical control over Dr. Edwards's triage pose the chapter's question - whether a system that saves people "for the greater good" is care or exploitation, echoing the "death panels" debate over the Affordable Care Act and asking "Are we being saved in order to be enslaved?"

utilitarianism.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
utilitarianism.title: 19. The Medical Ethics of Miracle Max
utilitarianism.relation: Shea treats Miracle Max as a one-man healthcare system to teach biomedical ethics: Max's lies about Valerie the 'witch', the fee, and the pill's duration violate the principle of autonomy and informed consent; the withholding-versus-withdrawing of the miracle pill and hypothetical Zoo of Death experiments engage nonmaleficence; his price and his duty to a mostly-dead stranger by the road raise beneficence; and who deserves resurrection under a monopoly raises justice, weighed across libertarian, utilitarian, and liberal-egalitarian (worst-off-maximizing) answers. The chapter concludes that principlism's four principles handle such dilemmas better than any single mechanical rule.

utilitarianism.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
utilitarianism.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
utilitarianism.relation: Malloy uses the two heroes to explain supererogation - Urmson's "Saints and Heroes" puzzle of acts that are praiseworthy but not obligatory, like Batman rushing into burning buildings while Jimmy Olsen is under no duty to follow. Against the utilitarian and deontological denials that anything goes beyond duty (Singer's argument that Clark Kent's designer glasses are money he owes to charity, and Susan Wolf's Loving and Rational Saints whose lives, like Batman's broken retirements in The Dark Knight Returns and Batman Beyond, leave no room for anything worth living), he adopts Raz's view that a duty can be overridden by the moral reason of grave personal risk. Hence Batman's nightly risk-taking is a genuinely heroic choice, while Superman's powers make saving others morally required - so Batman is more truly a hero and Superman "just a good person with the powers of a living god."

utilitarianism.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
utilitarianism.title: 13. Time to Choose
utilitarianism.relation: Goldberg and Gavaler read the heroes' first-year comics (The Superman Chronicles, The Batman Chronicles) as rival moral codes: Superman is a "super consequentialist" out to benefit mankind - reforming the Blakely Mine owner, demolishing slums, buying back swindled stock - while Batman is a "dark deontologist" whose vengeance oath makes consequences irrelevant, waiting out the Joker's murders of Claridge, Wilde, and Judge Drake because catching the villain, not saving victims, is his duty. Mill's utilitarianism frames Superman's consequentialism and Kant's Groundwork - intentions over outcomes, the batarang blocked by invisible glass leaving Batman's morality untouched - frames Batman's, with moral luck the battleground: deontology shrugs it off, but Superman's powers let him smooth luck over too. On the opening dilemma, Superman defuses the bomb while Batman chases the villain, so the authors judge Superman's code superior because Batman's can let hundreds die without moral failure.

utilitarianism.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
utilitarianism.title: 10. Lord Vetinari’s Friendly Guide to Tyranny
utilitarianism.relation: Alloy stages the debate over Vetinari's legitimacy as letters to the Ankh-Morpork Times: a writer channeling Hobbes defends the contracted sovereign - a 'mortal god' who cannot commit crimes and secures freedom through security - while 'the late Jeremy Bentham' judges the Patrician by the greatest good of the greatest number yet would disenfranchise golems and the 'differently-alive' dead. The anarchist Wolff Paul Roberts rebuts both, denying any right to rule, rejecting tacit consent by residence, and holding up the free golems as models of uncoerced virtue, before a final letter defends Vetinari's limited, functional government. The frame - Vetinari quietly orchestrating the whole correspondence and planning Roberts's next letter - shows tyranny curating its own philosophical defense.

utilitarianism.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
utilitarianism.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
utilitarianism.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

utilitarianism.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
utilitarianism.title: 27. Was the Red Wedding Massacre a Good Thing
utilitarianism.relation: Van der Deijl takes Tywin's line to Tyrion - 'explain to me why it is more noble to kill ten thousand men in battle than a dozen at dinner' - as a serious consequentialist challenge about the Red Wedding. Working through utilitarianism, prioritarianism, and dirty-hands cases like Hiroshima and shooting down a hijacked plane, he concedes the massacre could have been justified had breaking Guest Right and killing 3,500 brought peace at minimal cost; but the consequences fail - Joffrey and Roose Bolton keep power, the institution of guest right erodes, and Tywin's real motive was family power rather than the greater good - so the massacre fails even the consequentialist test, and Tywin is a power-hungry conspirator, not Machiavelli's prince.

utilitarianism.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
utilitarianism.title: 30. Trying to Do Good with Arya, Tyrion, and the Hound
utilitarianism.relation: Thomas sets Aristotle's practical wisdom against Bentham's utility calculus and Kant's consequence-proof rules, then watches all three struggle in season six. Arya's merciful refusal to poison Lady Crane backfires when the Waif kills her more painfully anyway; Tyrion's compromise with the Masters - phasing out slavery gradually, 'I trust their self-interest' - nearly loses Meereen when they attack by sea; and the resurrected Hound, after Brother Ray's massacre, concludes that 'lots of horrible shit in this world gets done for something larger than ourselves,' so being good in Westeros, as everywhere, means choosing without being able to know the consequences in advance.

utilitarianism.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
utilitarianism.title: 12. Aaugh! Why Is Being Moral So Hard
utilitarianism.relation: The chapter claims Schulz's humor is built on moral failure and illustrates the three main moral theories with specific strips: utilitarianism via Bentham's 'sovereign masters' of pain and pleasure and Charlie's 'to make others happy' (with Lucy noting nobody is making her happy), Kantian deontology via Sally's crayon lie and Snoopy's 'I haven't bitten anyone on the leg recently' as fulfilling a negative duty, and Aristotle's virtue ethics via the failed steal of home (foolhardy rather than courageous), the unmailed Valentine (cowardly), the golden mean, and Joe Shlabotnik as a hopeless role model. Charlie gritting his teeth shows mistaking a virtue's external markers for the virtue itself. It concludes we fit none of the theories well, yet Peanuts keeps a spirit of hope - happiness is a warm puppy, and Charlie's grit is genuine even if he cannot see it.

utilitarianism.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
utilitarianism.title: 11. Immortality Is Misery
utilitarianism.relation: In dialogue with Deadpool himself, John Altmann tests whether immortality is a blessing: Bentham's utilitarianism would prize a healing factor that lets Wade dive into a gamma meltdown to save the Southern Hemisphere for free, and Nietzsche would hail him as an Übermensch for refusing the Mithras Directive's Messiah and preserving humanity's freedom to create its own values rather than adopt herd morality. Bernard Williams gets the last word: since personalities become fixed—Wade stays a mercenary across every run, Zenpool notwithstanding—an endless life curdles into boredom and misery, so immortality is punishment rather than power unless one could radically change who one is.

utilitarianism.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
utilitarianism.title: 13. But Why Is Our World Better
utilitarianism.relation: Tim Jones asks why Juliana and Tagomi are right to call the Allies-win world 'better' when our world also holds the Red Army's mass rapes in Berlin, Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the Czech expulsions — a German widow or hibakusha who found Axis-victory reels could call them 'a better world' without being evil. His answer is a numbers-of-victims argument: Juliana's world duplicates our atrocities (the Heisenberg Device on Washington mirrors Hiroshima) and adds unique ones like the Nazi genocide in Africa, so our world is better for the most people — though its victims deserve the empathy and remembrance Obama showed at Hiroshima.

utilitarianism.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
utilitarianism.title: 16. Artistic Expression in the Land of the Free
utilitarianism.relation: Argues that Hendrix's Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' links political and artistic freedom: Mill's On Liberty — the harm principle, liberty of tastes and pursuits, and originality against the despotism of custom — both protects and celebrates the performance, since disliking it is no ground for suppressing it. Tolstoy's What Is Art? then supplies the aesthetic verdict: art is the infection of others by sincerely, particularly, and clearly felt emotion, so the anthem, like Picasso's Guernica, is great art expressing bad feelings about Vietnam — unlike José Feliciano's sincere-but-vague ballad or Roseanne Barr's failed joke.

utilitarianism.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
utilitarianism.title: 6. The PowerPoint Conspiracy Theory
utilitarianism.relation: In a sustained deadpan parody, Ketcham builds a conspiracy out of Ockham's Razor: William of Ockham's minimalist principle explains PowerPoint's big-type bullet points, but the slide deck (secretly engineered by DARPA with Microsoft, exported via Siberia to Putin) becomes a weapon that breeds stupidity, conditions Trump to tweet-length simplicities like fake news and crooked, and finally rigs him, not the voting machines. The chapter also wields the Razor correctly, insisting that a minimalist explanation must still be good and complete, as when little Jill's one bullet point tells us too little. Testing moral realism, Kant's absolute prohibition on lying, and utilitarianism's greatest happiness against the conspiracy's missing facts, it concludes we lack the information to render any moral verdict, which is exactly what the conspiracy-minded minimalists want.

utilitarianism.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
utilitarianism.title: 12. Jerry’s Dick
utilitarianism.relation: Twin essays by two dimension-swapped Wayne Yuens debate whether Jerry owes Shrimply Pibbles his penis in 'Interdimensional Cable 2'. Yuen H-232 defends supererogation: like donating blood or a kidney to a Peter Singer figure, giving up the organ would be Good-Samaritan praiseworthy but beyond duty, since it would derail Jerry's life-plan and autonomy, and the artificial-heart alternative makes it optional, while utilitarianism has no room for such acts. Yuen U-964 replies that the life-plan excuse would absolve every shirked duty up to Evil Morty's massacre of the Citadel, that Singer-style obligation to aid stands, and that in our organ-short world we probably do have a duty to donate.

utilitarianism.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
utilitarianism.title: 15. Loving Your Pet Is Better than Utilitarianism
utilitarianism.relation: Against Peter Singer's utilitarian case in Animal Liberation, spare Snuffles because he can suffer regardless of intelligence, the chapter argues utilitarianism fails because it quantifies the unquantifiable, happiness. It turns to Hume: intelligence cannot ground moral worth, since smart Rick enslaving a microverse would then be our moral superior; Hume's guillotine separates descriptive from moral claims so that metaphysics no longer decides who counts as a moral object; and Hume's real ground is sentiment, dogs loving across species as the tail-wagging Snuffles does. So the morally right response to 'Lawnmower Dog' is not Jerry's abuse or even Rick's intelligence helmet but simply loving the pet.

utilitarianism.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
utilitarianism.title: 6. A Better Bad Place
utilitarianism.relation: Grosz asks whether Judge Gen could justly condemn Team Cockroach to eternal torment, testing the classic 'sins against an infinite being deserve infinite punishment' defense built on Anselm's God as that than which nothing greater can be conceived, and finding that no such being exists on the show. He rejects the continuing-sin model of Hell because the Bad Place's physical torture precludes both further sinning and moral reform, and argues purely retributive eternal punishment fails the utilitarian test. His proposal, a non-torturous 'Bad Place 3.0' modeled on C.S. Lewis's The Great Divorce where people face the natural consequences of their vice until they reform, could be justified as what is best for the person.

utilitarianism.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
utilitarianism.title: 10. A Love Story between Theory and Praxis
utilitarianism.relation: Altmann allegorizes Chidi as Theory and Eleanor as Praxis, whose 'love story' shows each completing the other: Chidi's lessons in utilitarianism and Kant's Categorical Imperative give Eleanor reasons, and eventually a lived example in Michael's feigned self-sacrifice, to confess her lie, while Eleanor's pragmatism in the Bad Place teaches Chidi that principles useless in the world must be revised. Michael's arc from designing psychological torture to giving Eleanor his portal pin demonstrates a theory of human nature, that people cannot change, being falsified by praxis. The chapter closes with Eleanor re-entering the cycle by finding Chidi's lectures online, recommending the union of theory and praxis as how anyone becomes a better person.

utilitarianism.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
utilitarianism.title: 15. Chidi’s Indecision
utilitarianism.relation: Vannatta argues Chidi's indecision exposes the shared flaw of the Big Three theories, Kantian deontology, Bentham and Mill's consequentialism, and Aristotle's virtue ethics of the golden mean: their rationalism pretends moral conflict can be eliminated by applying the correct rule, when Chidi's trolley terror shows moral situations are experienced as genuinely uncertain. Dewey's 'Three Independent Factors in Morals', the Good of desire, the Right of duty, and the Virtuous of communal praise, legitimizes that felt uncertainty and explains Eleanor's talent for finding option C between binary dilemmas. The chapter concludes that the show's real, unspoken moral theory is care ethics: partiality, relationship maintenance, and moral growth through the experience of being cared for, as Eleanor learns from Chidi's friendship rather than his lectures.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: A Seriously Mind-Blowing Book about Seriously Mind-Blowing Movies
utilitarianism.relation: The introduction argues that all villains, real or fictional, share one trait: they treat people as mere objects to be used, which is why Thanos's Snap feels monstrous. It then springs the book's central provocation: since Thanos kills half of all life to save the rest of the universe from overpopulation, resource exhaustion, and destruction, he is 'actually a strictly moral being' from a utilitarian perspective. It frames the tension between using persons and respecting them (the grenade-jumping soldier who gives himself willingly versus those sacrificed without consent) and previews the volume's chapters on Thanos's morality and mind, time travel, and death.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: 5. Getting Time Travel Right
utilitarianism.relation: Duncan Gale asks whether Endgame 'gets time travel right,' using David Lewis's 'The Paradoxes of Time Travel' to explain personal time versus external time (Steve and Nebula meeting their past selves), causal loops (Tony quoting the saying about money and time back to Howard, who seemingly hears it first), and the grandfather paradox (Rhodey's baby-Thanos plan, which the existence of Nebula proves the Avengers would always fail to carry out). He traces Marvel's branching-timeline rule from Marvel Two-In-One #50 through the Ancient One's warning that removing a stone splits reality, and argues the film's moral is that the Avengers refuse quick resets and dutifully return the stones, while Thanos would shred the universe and rebuild a 'grateful' one. The chapter closes with Ivan Karamazov's challenge about building the edifice of human happiness on a tortured child's tears, which Thanos would accept and the Avengers refuse.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: 11. Population Ethics for Mad Gods
utilitarianism.relation: Leonard Kahn takes Thanos seriously as a participant in population ethics, asking 'how many people should there be?' after Titan's collapse, and tests the Snap against three schools. Totalism condemns it (random killing just cuts total happiness in half while traumatizing survivors like Steve's support-group members) but falls to Parfit's Repugnant Conclusion: it must prefer a universe of trillions barely worth living to one of ecstatic individuals. Averagism also condemns the Snap, since random removal leaves the average untouched, yet would obligate Thanos to kill the least happy half, and the person-affecting view condemns the murder but gives the Avengers no reason to snap anyone back, rendering Natasha's sacrifice pointless, so Kahn concludes Thanos should have used the Stones to reconsider the Population Question before acting, since humanity's own flourishing depends on answering it.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: 18. Iron Man’s Choice to Die
utilitarianism.relation: Argues Tony's death in Endgame is best explained three ways: via Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives (Tony oscillates between the cabin family-life drive and the risk-seeking death drive that takes him aboard the donut ship in Infinity War and has him lay down to die with Nebula), via Camus's absurd (like Sisyphus, Tony creates subjective meaning by choosing — Pepper, Morgan, and finally the snap itself, 'Part of the journey is the end'), and via consequentialism (the snap as a desirable consequence, contrasting Infinity War's deontological 'We don't trade lives' with Endgame's 'whatever it takes'). It contends that because the time heist rewrites history, deaths in both films — Vision's, Natasha's, Tony's — risk becoming meaningless, so Tony dies on his terms to make his death meaningful.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: 20. Thanos and the (Un)grateful Universe
utilitarianism.relation: Argues that Infinity War only has the structure of a superhero movie when told from Thanos's perspective, and that he passes a three-part 'superhero test' — beneficent goal (saving the universe from overpopulation), self-sacrifice (killing Gamora, destroying the stones, 'I lost more than you can know'), and willingness to make the tough decisions — while the Avengers fail it, staying split after Civil War and acting from selfish motives (Ant-Man wants Hope back, Black Widow says 'we owe it to everyone who's not in this room'). It then applies utilitarianism — Titan's collapse, Gamora's planet turned 'paradise,' the whales in the Hudson, the Snap as a trolley-problem lever Thanos alone will pull — to conclude Thanos is the true hero of the saga and the Avengers the unintended villains.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: 23. Where Thanos Got Lost
utilitarianism.relation: Diagnoses where Thanos 'got lost' via Wittgenstein's aspect perception (the duck-rabbit, the Thanos-chin-as-panini memes): morality concerns not just choosing but seeing, and Thanos's impoverished worldview — shaped by a lifetime of rejection, drawn from the novel Thanos: Titan Consumed — lets him see life only as 'the condition of living things,' never as 'the existence of individuals,' so erasing half of all individuals strikes him as a moral act. His single-minded reading of Titan's collapse becomes confirmation bias ('I'm the only one who knows that'), and his final plan to erase everything proves he never saw the individual-existence aspect at all: his starting point, not his reasoning, is missing information.

utilitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
utilitarianism.title: 25. Reasonable Genocide
utilitarianism.relation: Uses Horkheimer's Eclipse of Reason to dissolve the puzzle of Thanos's unsettling sanity: the Snap is subjectively rational — pure means–ends efficiency in service of a Malthusian 'simple calculus' whose end only the subject chooses — so Thanos 'is mad because he is rational,' with the murder of Gamora as the final severing of his last bond to the world. Captain America's refusal to trade Vision ('We don't trade lives') is read as a stand for ends valuable in themselves, while Ultron embodies the totalitarian variant (via Arendt and Spencer's social Darwinism) that declares humanity 'obsolete': Ultron wants to accelerate nature, Thanos to correct it, both absolutizing the subject against objective reason.

utilitarianism.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
utilitarianism.title: 13. You Wanted the Best, You’ve Got the Right to the Best
utilitarianism.relation: Mikko Puumala invents a 'Preservationist' who argues that future generations have a right to the chance of experiencing a live KISS show, by analogy with preserving the Colosseum and Niagara Falls, and then dismantles the argument. A reductio ad absurdum shows the principle would oblige preserving nearly every rock band; the Castle thought experiment exposes the problem that after the End of the Road tour there is no fact about which historical KISS (masked Seventies, unmasked Eighties, reunion era) should be restored; and the museumization worry shows that freezing KISS would contradict the adaptability — disco, glam, grunge — that defines KISStory. He concludes there is no duty on Simmons and Stanley to keep KISS alive, though a modest utilitarian case favors the show going on.

utilitarianism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
utilitarianism.title: “It’s a robot! A goddamn droid!”
utilitarianism.relation: Tests three grounds of moral status against the franchise: species membership (Singer's charge of speciesism - would the human-DNA Newborn count?), Kantian autonomy (which makes Bishop matter but excludes babies and animals, and is itself doubtful once his behavioral inhibitors fix his choices), and Bentham's sentience ('can they suffer?' - Bishop's 'I hurt. Do me a favor. Disconnect me'). Settling on interests and preferences, the chapter argues synthetics with desires - even Ash's admiration for the 'perfect organism' - can be moral patients, so Weyland-Yutani's treatment of them as tools and slaves is wrong.

utilitarianism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
utilitarianism.title: Special Order 937—Crew Expendable
utilitarianism.relation: Reads Weyland-Yutani as 'greed is good' cost-benefit reasoning embodied by Ash, Mother, and Burke (Gordon Gekko's Wall Street speech transplanted into space), and asks who can be held accountable when every employee fills only a narrow role and scapegoats absorb blame. It then weighs Kantian deontology - Bishop's inviolable no-harm rules, the absolute wrongness of killing crew for profit - against utilitarian reasoning: Ripley's quarantine refusal to save the many, Parker's refusal to flame the alien holding Lambert, and the uncomfortable thought that acquiring the Xenomorph might genuinely benefit billions.

utilitarianism.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
utilitarianism.title: Ethicists Assemble!
utilitarianism.relation: White casts the 'Avengers Prime' as three living ethical systems: Tony Stark is the utilitarian who, during Civil War and the registration crisis, bets on outcomes he alone claims to foresee (stopping the Crimson Dynamo's heart, enlisting the Thunderbolts, exiling the Hulk); Captain America is the deontologist who refuses registration on principle ('we maintained the principles we swore to defend... you sold your principles') and rejects the Punisher and the Negative Zone prison regardless of consequences; Thor is the virtue ethicist who condemns Iron Man not by utility or duty but for violating loyalty, trust, and friendship in cloning him, and who refuses the Twilight Sword because using it would make him 'the same demon'. The chapter argues all three frameworks still demand judgment and conviction, which the heroes share.

utilitarianism.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
utilitarianism.title: So, Case Closed-Right
utilitarianism.relation: Mark D. White asks why Batman refuses to kill the Joker even after the Joker murdered Jason Todd, paralyzed Barbara Gordon, and killed Sarah Essen. Framing the refusal as deontological rather than utilitarian, he runs the case through Foot and Thomson's trolley problem and transplant case, arguing the classics disanalogize because the Joker himself creates the danger and because 'do not kill' is an agent-specific rule rather than an agent-neutral one. He extends the analysis to prepunishment via Philip K. Dick's Minority Report, and concedes that even a self-described strict deontologist can conclude Batman maybe should have killed the Joker years ago.

utilitarianism.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
utilitarianism.title: Sometimes Heroes Fail
utilitarianism.relation: James DiGiovanna asks whether it was right for Batman to turn street kids Dick Grayson and Jason Todd into Robin. He tests the training against Kant's universalizability (including the Joker-demanding-to-know-where-Robin-is lie example), against Bentham and Mill's utilitarian appeal to Gotham's general good, and finally reads it through the virtue ethics of Plato, Aristotle, and MacIntyre's After Virtue, where Robin is trained into a role-specific character rather than taught rules. Jason's rashness and death at the Joker's hands show Batman failed to moderate his ward's courage, and the chapter concludes Batman is 'a lousy deontologist, a decent consequentialist, and some kind of virtue ethicist.'

utilitarianism.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
utilitarianism.title: But This Ruins Everything!
utilitarianism.relation: Mahesh Ananth and Ben Dixon pit young Bruce Wayne against Peter Singer: given seven billion dollars, Singer's 'Famine, Affluence, and Morality' principle, illustrated by the drowning child, seems to require giving nearly everything to famine relief rather than dressing up as a bat. Against appeals to honoring his parents' memory and to supererogation, the authors deploy Singer's strong and moderate versions of giving and utilitarian indifference to distance, concluding that a true utilitarian would forbid becoming Batman. The irony they highlight is that the older Batman himself reasons utilitarianly when he abandons Jason Todd to intercept the Joker's poisoned convoy in A Death in the Family.

utilitarianism.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
utilitarianism.title: A White Christmas with Dark Reflections
utilitarianism.relation: The chapter follows White Christmas's three escalating uses of the Z-eye digital block — Beth blocking Joe (whose information deprivation leads to two deaths), court-ordered blocks extending to children, and Matthew's society-wide red-blur sex-offender block — as a conflict between privacy and access to information. Utilitarian and Kantian frameworks (autonomy, persons as ends) leave the trade-offs genuinely unsettled, while Nozick's minimal state shows the automatic, loophole-free blocking regime is an indefensibly paternalistic state violating proportionality. Arendt's account of meaningfulness through speech grounds the conclusion that erasing someone's face and voice violates their humanity, and the chapter's final move is defamiliarization: if digital blocks are wrong, we should re-examine the social-media blocking, restraining orders, prisons, and sex-offender registries they mirror.

utilitarianism.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
utilitarianism.title: Do We Attain Justice by Punishment
utilitarianism.relation: Kenny's blackmail arc in Shut Up and Dance — the twist that reclassifies the sympathetic protagonist as a child-pornography offender — anchors an argument that the hackers' vigilantism cannot attain justice: their punishments are unannounced, disproportionate, aimed at merely moral wrongs (infidelity, racist emails), and exempt from the presumption of innocence and nulla poena sine lege that states replaced vendetta with. A distinction between natural-law and legal-positivist conceptions of justice shows why punishment belongs to the state alone. Against retribution ('a mere prison sentence is too good for Kenny'), Bentham's and Mill's utilitarianism — deterrence, incapacitation, and above all rehabilitation, capped by the harm principle — shows punishment should be no more than deterrence requires, making the hackers sadists rather than agents of justice.

utilitarianism.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
utilitarianism.title: 7 Should Wakanda Take Over the World The Ethics of International Power
utilitarianism.relation: Littmann asks whether Wakanda should take over the world, staging N'Jobu's and Killmonger's 'Wakanda could rule them all... the right way' plan against the history of benevolently justified empire: Roman civilization of barbarians, Kipling's white man's burden, and Mill's trusteeship argument for educating non-Europeans toward democracy. Plato's Republic case for rule by the wisest initially favors Wakandan conquest, but Kant's Perpetual Peace condemnation of conquering 'European savages,' Mill's own four reasons imperial rule goes wrong (ignorance of local conditions, lack of sympathy, partiality, exploitation), and Diderot's claim that distance from home erodes moral restraint convince him domination breeds abuse; he endorses Nakia's aid-and-refuge outreach and Mill's hope that the 'aristocracy of nationality' will one day look as wrong as racism.

utilitarianism.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
utilitarianism.title: 20 The Value of Vibranium
utilitarianism.relation: Edwardo Pérez asks what makes vibranium 'the most valuable metal known to man' through Marx's distinction between use value and exchange value: Klaue prizes exchange value (money, power, a black-market arm), while Wakandans structure their whole society around use value and never trade the metal. The museum scene raises cultural property - does vibranium belong to Wakanda, as the cultural nationalist holds, or to humanity, as the cultural internationalist holds? - and T'Challa's shift on sharing it is analyzed through Kant's categorical imperative versus Bentham's utilitarian calculus, with his saving of Agent Ross and sparing of M'Baku vindicated by their consequences. Vibranium's greatest value, the chapter concludes, is atonement: redeeming T'Chaka's crime and uniting humanity as 'one single tribe.'

utilitarianism.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
utilitarianism.title: “It's Been Handed Down from Goof to Goof to Goof, and Now, It's Yours, Son”
utilitarianism.relation: Mentyka uses Goofy to test theories of the good life: Socratic intellectualism stumbles on uneducated-but-good Goofy, Kant's categorical imperative absurdly forbids handing Max the 'goof to goof' fishing pole (Goofy can't will it universal law), Mill's utilitarianism fails when Max's lukewarm reception makes the gift happiness-reducing, and Singer's extension to animals muddies Pluto the dog against Goofy the dog treated as a person. The chapter resolves with Scheler's claim that we first encounter values through moral exemplars — earnest, bumbling Goofy — not through rules or consequences, and a closing plea that philosophers narrate less like the smug 'How to...' narrator.

utilitarianism.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
utilitarianism.title: The Bill Comes Due
utilitarianism.relation: The chapter uses Michael Walzer's Problem of Dirty Hands to weigh the Ancient One's secret lifelong use of forbidden dark magic against Kaecilius's summoning of Dormammu, arguing that only she faces a genuine dirty-hands dilemma because her end (defending Earth) is good while his is not. It asks why dark magic is forbidden at all and answers with rule-utilitarian reasoning that has taken on a deontological life of its own, then invokes Kant's murderer-at-the-door essay to argue, with Mordo's 'the bill comes due,' that whoever does wrong for good ends bears responsibility for the downstream consequences—and that Strange's willingness to break Kamar-Taj's rules while accepting the cost is what makes him a hero.

utilitarianism.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
utilitarianism.title: The (Single) Garden Path
utilitarianism.relation: Argues Herbert populates Dune with three long-running eugenics programs, each with a different ethical stance: the Bene Gesserit's Kwisatz Haderach breeding scheme (whose communal guardian-breeding deliberately recalls Socrates' Kallipolis in the Republic), Leto II's Golden Path, and the Bene Tleilax's axolotl-tank genetic design for immortality. It reads the chastened Sisterhood of the later novels as moving from consequentialist to Kantian, deontological ground ('never seek to create a human being in any one image'), frames Leto II as the ultimate utilitarian whose species-saving end allegedly justifies Machiavellian means (with Siona's objection that he had no right), and shows the Tleilaxu destroyed by their own monomaniacal religious code. Conclusion: 'the most dangerous of all creations is a rigid code of ethics.'

utilitarianism.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
utilitarianism.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Jeff Ewing asks which moral theory governs the novel, finding deontology absent and a contest between Graff's utilitarian recruiting pitch and a virtue-ethical focus on character: the I.F. allowed a 'Third' because it wanted Ender's traits rather than his acts. Mapping Plato's cardinal virtues and tripartite-soul politics against Aristotle's doctrine of the mean, he argues Ender's minimum-force self-defense, adaptability, and disregard for hierarchy are Aristotelian virtues, while his killings of Stilson, Bonzo, and the buggers fall outside the mean only because he lacked the intellectual virtue of grasping his full situation.

utilitarianism.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
utilitarianism.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Greg Littmann defends Graff and Ender as act utilitarians in Mill's own image, noting that Mill's father raised him in calculated isolation and brutal study as a tool to reform humanity just as Graff engineers Ender, so both acted rightly given the stakes even though Mill's harm principle and his regard for animal suffering also condemn the xenocide itself. Against Crime and Punishment and 'The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas,' he argues Ender's Game shows consequences can genuinely justify breaking any moral rule when human extinction is on the table.

utilitarianism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
utilitarianism.title: “What happens to us now ”
utilitarianism.relation: Tests the moral limits of science against Dresden's defense of Eros ('hardly a rounding error', 'we become our own gods'): Descartes' evil demon explains why Holden can never verify the protomolecule-ghost Miller — or even the Roci's bulkhead — is real; Baconian induction and mastery of nature explain why Protogen feeds biomass to the protomolecule ('we can only learn by letting it learn'), though Bacon himself demanded knowledge be shared for universal good; Peirce's pragmatism explains how the Donnager infers stealth ships from their effects and why protomolecule victims count as no longer human; and Dewey's inseparability of means and ends indicts Fred Johnson's readiness to negotiate with Dresden. It culminates in Miller shooting Dresden — 'I killed him because he was making sense' — as the straightest critique of utilitarian calculation, concluding that when empathy is excised (Cortázar's stimulation) or ignored, even science aimed at saving humanity produces Eros, Project Caliban, and the Earth-Mars war.

utilitarianism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: The chapter maps four schools of ethics onto Fallout 4's Commonwealth: Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Preston Garvey's settlement defense as the mean between recklessness and cowardice and temperance as moderate chem use; Kant's Categorical Imperative is tested on stealing ammo in Concord and on the Battle of Bunker Hill choice to warn the Railroad, where loyal silence to Father fails universalization and treats synths merely as means. Aquinas's natural law ethics, keyed to the telos of power armor, workbenches, and Pip-Boys, condemns the Institute's creation of synths by analogy to the IVF debate while still demanding dignity for synths who already exist. Finally, Bentham's utilitarianism is the one framework under which Father's Institute — adaptive labor force, scientific progress, stability and order — can sincerely believe itself morally justified.

utilitarianism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: Weighing Vault-Tec's secret experiments — Vault 11's yearly human sacrifice, Vault 13's 200-year lockdown, the cryogenic freezing of the Sole Survivor — the chapter asks whether the ends could ever justify the vaults. On Kant's Universal Law and Humanity Formulations the answer is flatly no: dwellers were deceived into becoming mere means to data, whatever the hypothetical space-colonization motive that designer Tim Cain favors. Act and rule utilitarianism in Bentham's tradition give a more equivocal verdict — exposed deception would doom any future cooperation, yet safeguarding humanity might in extraordinary circumstances tip the calculus — and the chapter situates the games in real research-ethics history from the eugenics era to the Tuskegee study and the Belmont Report.

utilitarianism.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
utilitarianism.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Robert Arp and Sarah Fisk test three moral theories against objectification in Final Fantasy: Kant's ban on using rational beings as mere means (Kuja's manipulation of Queen Brahne, the Geostigma children of Advent Children), Mill's greatest-happiness principle (Yuna's and Aeris's self-sacrifice), and Aristotle's character-based virtue ethics (Hojo and Sephiroth as vicious, Aeris as virtuous). They argue Kantianism generates a stalemate between 'moral sanctity' and 'moral autonomy' camps over cases like Guardian Force summoning in FFVIII, and utilitarianism a stalemate over mandatory self-sacrifice, leaving virtue ethics, Aristotelian or Nietzschean, as the view that escapes both, ending with the question 'Aeris or a Cloud?'

utilitarianism.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
utilitarianism.title: 6. A Better Bad Place
utilitarianism.relation: Asks whether Judge Gen could ever justly consign Team Cockroach to eternal torment. It reconstructs the Anselmian infinite-desert defense (God as 'than which none greater can be conceived', every sin against an infinite being meriting infinite punishment) and shows it fails on the show since no such God appears and neither Gen nor Michael is infinitely great; the continuing-sin model fails because the Bad Place's physical tortures (eyeball corkscrews, bees with teeth) preclude sinning, and Gen's own tests (Jason's Madden game, Tahani's hallway, Chidi's two hats) show vice persisting without added desert. Punishment as retribution also fails on utilitarian grounds (Jason's hypothetical spray-paint-can sentence adds only pain), so the chapter proposes a non-retributive 'Bad Place 3.0' where people face the natural consequences of their vices, comparing it to C.S. Lewis's The Great Divorce.

utilitarianism.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
utilitarianism.title: 10. A Love Story between Theory and Praxis
utilitarianism.relation: Casts Chidi as Theory and Eleanor as Praxis in an allegorical love story: Chidi's Kantian universalizability about lying and his utilitarian lesson (confess, because the neighborhood's welfare outweighs you) only move Eleanor when she sees Theory enacted — Michael's willingness to absorb eternal torture in her place convinces her the theory 'has legs'. Praxis repays the debt when Eleanor's moral particularism pushes Chidi to lie to demons and play his part in the Bad Place party, and Michael's conversion from torturer to someone who sacrifices his portal pin for Eleanor ('Rhonda, Diana, Jake, and Trent') completes the union. The moral: theory is born in the world, but only practice lets it thrive there.

utilitarianism.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
utilitarianism.title: 15. Chidi’s Indecision
utilitarianism.relation: Surveys the 'Big Three' through the show: Kantian deontology (Chidi's boots lie, Tahani's mere-means charity), Bentham and Mill's utilitarianism (Jason's alligator frame-up, the trolley simulation), and Aristotle's golden mean (courage between Jason's rashness and Chidi's paralyzed deficiency), arguing their shared rationalism cannot accommodate the real uncertainty Chidi feels. John Dewey's 'Three Independent Factors in Morals' — the Good, the Right, and the Virtuous as irreducible — explains why Chidi sees only binaries while Eleanor finds 'option C' and imagines the Medium Place. The chapter concludes the show's unstated moral theory is care ethics: relational selves, justified partiality toward friends, and moral growth through the experience of being cared for, as when Chidi models care rather than lecturing it.

utilitarianism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
utilitarianism.title: The Sorting Hat Speaks Division and Divisiveness
utilitarianism.relation: Against Death Eater blood-purity, the chapter sets the ethical tradition of equal moral worth: Bentham's 'each to count for one, and none for more than one' (the Minister of Magic's pain matters no more than a house-elf's or a Blast-Ended Skrewt's) and Kant's demand to treat humanity never merely as a means. It applies this to Potterwatch's 'every human life is worth the same, and worth saving' and to Hermione's S.P.E.W. campaign against house-elf 'slave labor,' then asks how patriotic preference for compatriots differs in kind from racism and sexism.

utilitarianism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
utilitarianism.title: Two Keys to the Good Life
utilitarianism.relation: Contrasts the greater good, young Dumbledore and Grindelwald's For the Greater Good scheme to subjugate Muggles, under which the rights, dignity, and integrity of individuals are up for grabs whenever the majority benefits, with the common good, where sacrifice serves all, as in the civil rights movement's appeal to the good of the whole American community. Harry's choice to return from King's Cross and finish Voldemort defeats the greater-good revolution and realizes the common good of Muggles and wizards alike.

utilitarianism.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
utilitarianism.title: NOTES
utilitarianism.relation: Robichaud evaluates the morally gray Company: its goal of mastering the evolutionary forces behind powers is tested against eugenics worries, the 'playing God' objection that natural processes have intrinsic value, and Sandel's Case against Perfection (that mastery breeds inflated responsibility, eroded community, and rigidity), each of which he finds inconclusive or outweighed by lives saved from people like Ted Sprague. He then turns to blame for the bag-and-tag program, applying Dennis Thompson's criterion to hold the founders plus hands-on agents like Bennet and the Haitian responsible while excusing accountants like Malsky. Finally he sets conditions for when an insider such as Bennet or Mohinder may blow the whistle, ruling out Bennet's murderous take-down-from-within scheme.

utilitarianism.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
utilitarianism.title: NOTES
utilitarianism.relation: First defines lying — distinguishing it from mere error (Angela believing Peter dead), from the Haitian's non-verbal memory-wipe deception, and from Hiro's silent staging of Ando's fake death — then tests moral theories against the show's liars. Kant's categorical imperative bans all lying but is abandoned when Sylar demands a friend's hiding place; utilitarianism vindicates Victoria Pratt's lie about the virus vial yet also licenses Linderman's .07% explosion and Plato's noble lie of the earthborn metals, which the chapter rejects. Machiavelli's advice that princes may lie to keep power is played out by 'President Sylar' in 'Five Years Gone,' and the chapter finally endorses Sissela Bok's presumption against lying — a public-reasoning procedure modeled by Bob Bishop and Mohinder before Monica's virus injection.

utilitarianism.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: Uses Sartre's play Dirty Hands and Walzer's 'Political Action: The Problem of Dirty Hands' to ask whether Frank's willingness to do the 'necessary thing' — from the opening mercy-killing of the dog to the Season 3 drone strike — could ever count in favor of an Underwood presidency, with utilitarians (nothing wrong with dirty hands) and absolutists like the bishop ('Love God, and love each other. Period.') dissolving the problem from opposite sides. Walzer's later 'supreme emergency' standard and threshold deontology frame the Jordan Valley staring contest with Petrov and the resulting deal as the one case where Frank's capability might genuinely matter, while Heather Dunbar's reluctance (her refusal of Stamper's offer of Claire's diary, then her reversal) tests the ideal of a leader both capable of and averse to dirtying her hands. The verdict: Frank's only advantage over Dunbar is his capacity for dirty hands, and even that fails because he lacks the scruples to keep them clean when it is not necessary.

utilitarianism.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: Perry frames Frank through Walzer's problem of dirty hands, taking its name from Sartre's play ('I have dirty hands right up to the elbows... Do you think you can govern innocently?') and Machiavelli's advice to 'enter into evil when forced by necessity' — the pilot's mercy killing of the dog and 'just shy of treason, which is politics' being the show's emblems. He maps the field onto the show: utilitarians for whom breaking rules can be right, absolutists like the bishop ('Love God, and love each other. Period.'), and Walzer's later 'supreme emergency' threshold deontology applied to Frank's child-killing drone strike and his desperate deal with Petrov in the Jordan Valley. The verdict: Frank's only edge over Heather Dunbar is a proven capacity to dirty his hands when needed, but he lacks the scruples that keep that capacity from becoming routine wrongdoing, so he is probably still the wrong man for the job.

utilitarianism.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
utilitarianism.title: 2 Does It Always Belong in a Museum
utilitarianism.relation: Edwardo Pérez reconstructs the reasoning behind Indy's unargued mantra 'It belongs in a museum' via Bentham's principle of utility: museums maximize happiness because scholars and the public can study and enjoy artifacts for generations, unlike private collectors like Panama Hat. The same calculus explains his rule-breaking — he leaves the Mayapore Sankara Stone with the villagers ('It'd be another rock collecting dust' in a museum) because a flourishing village outweighs his fortune and glory, and he concedes the government's Area 51 warehouse may have been the utility-maximizing choice for the Ark after what it did to Belloq and Toht. Indy's apparent inconsistencies thus dissolve into case-by-case consequence weighing.

utilitarianism.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
utilitarianism.title: Can You Find Your Moral Compass
utilitarianism.relation: Donovan and Richardson test Tony's moral compass in 'Armor Wars' and 'Extremis' against the three major schools. Utilitarianism fails because Tony will not sacrifice even one innocent for the greater good — he changes tactics to save a single pilot from the Raiders and rages when the Controller's human zombie dies — and Kantian deontology fails because Tony bends rules ('lives to mean more than rules') and is driven by emotion rather than pure reason. Aristotle fits: Tony is obsessed not just with doing good but with being good, snarling at his own reflection, asking filmmaker Pillinger 'Have you changed anything? Me neither,' until Extremis lets him 'be the Iron Man inside and out,' uniting agent and deed as Aristotelian character requires.

utilitarianism.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
utilitarianism.title: Real World Island
utilitarianism.relation: Patricia Brace and Rob Arp argue Lost redeems characters who stop objectifying others and instead freely 'objectify' themselves for the greater good. Kant's ban on treating persons as mere means condemns Ben's lifelong manipulation and Ben's use of Sayid as an assassin, yet autonomy justifies chosen self-sacrifice like Charlie's Looking Glass suicide mission, Claire volunteering as bait for Ethan, and Jack becoming the new Jacob. Mill's utilitarianism makes Kate's shooting of the Man in Black a fair trade saving her friends, while Aristotle's virtues - respect against objectification, courage in Jack's death at the cliff, the engrained honesty of reformed con man Jim LaFleur, Kate's character-building motherhood of Aaron - complete the three-theory survey.

utilitarianism.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
utilitarianism.title: Justice for All? Metallica's Argument Against Napster and Internet File Sharing
utilitarianism.relation: Robert Delfino evaluates the Napster lawsuit philosophically: Aristotle's law of non-contradiction exposes Lars Ulrich's inconsistent statements about money and his tolerance of 1980s home taping despite admitting to it, weakening the band's case. But the core argument is consistent and Lockean - Lars' Senate testimony that 'just like a carpenter who crafts a table gets to decide whether to keep it, sell it, or give it away' invokes Locke's labor theory of property, which Delfino defends against Tom Palmer's objection that copyright restricts bodily liberty, distinguishing it from the Constitution's utilitarian rationale for copyright.

utilitarianism.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
utilitarianism.title: The Office and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Weighs the morality of Jim and Pam's workplace flirting (while Pam is engaged to Roy) using three ethical frameworks: act utilitarianism has them tot up their own happiness against effects on co-workers' morale and Dunder-Mifflin's bottom line; rule utilitarianism models HR's blanket anti-dating policies and asks whether Jim and Pam could justify an exception without destroying the rule (the Hawaiian shirt day analogy); deontology searches for duties against office romance (favoritism in evaluation, distraction from duties) and finds none once harassment is set aside, concluding that in the absence of a deontological prohibition, Jim and Pam may keep flirting until 5 p.m.

utilitarianism.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
utilitarianism.title: The Office and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Kraft uses Dunder Mifflin to test whether stockholder profit or stakeholder welfare should drive business decisions, introducing stakeholder theory via Ansoff and the Mitchell salience model. Michael's exclusive patronage of national chains (Chili's, Starbucks, USA Today) versus the staff's loyalty to local spots like Poor Richard's becomes a Millian case: by Mill's point that most good action benefits particular individuals, shopping locally spreads happiness through the Scranton community while Michael's habits export money and decision-making elsewhere. Dwight oscillates between stockholder logic (the cheapest health plan, poaching Jim's client in 'Diversity Day') and stakeholder-minded customer service, while 'Halloween,' 'Health Care,' and 'Branch Closing' show profit trumping people; Michael's successful sale to Christian at Chili's in 'The Client' balances both, and his 'Show me that farm' speech insists workers like Stanley and Phyllis are not replaceable cogs.

utilitarianism.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
utilitarianism.title: The Office and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Johnson works through the standard objections to affirmative action using Scranton material: Ryan's paralysis before the all-Black management team in 'Traveling Salesmen' shows a single-race workforce is not intrinsically bad, while Michael's Chris Rock routine and his do-it-yourself slur exercise in 'Diversity Day' show that Dunder Mifflin meeting every quota does nothing about racism. A hypothetical about Dwight's grandfather refusing to hire Stanley's grandfather at the beet farm frames the compensation objection, answered by the 'cycle of poverty' account of the present effects of past discrimination. Finally, a fictitious hiring of guard Hank Tate over a better-qualified white candidate - justified, following Nagel, by the consequences of calming branch unrest - sets up the conclusion that education, not racially preferential hiring, would break minority poverty without discrimination, so affirmative action is ultimately unjustified.

utilitarianism.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
utilitarianism.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
utilitarianism.relation: Murtagh asks whether the Virgin Mary statue spraying menstrual blood on a cardinal and the pope in 'Bloody Mary' is morally wrong, and answers with a utilitarian weighing of blasphemous humor's consequences. On the negative side, offense to believers (with Cartman's sudden piety about Family Guy's Muhammad in 'Cartoon Wars Part I' articulating the utilitarian worry that millions watching intensifies the harm) and a possible desensitizing erosion of tolerance; on the positive side, pleasure and the show's power to provoke thought, as when Randy learns from Stan that his five sober days came from his own willpower, not 'divine ass blood'. Drawing on Mill's greatest happiness principle and On Liberty's defense of open discussion, he concludes blasphemous humor is morally justified when it is an important part of a presentation with significant social value, and wrong when used merely to piss people off or for profit.

utilitarianism.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
utilitarianism.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
utilitarianism.relation: Uses 'Fun with Veal' (the boys' bedroom standoff over baby calves, the FDA renaming veal 'tortured baby cows', Stan's meat strike punished by 'vaginitus'), 'Whale Whores' (the Japanese hating dolphins until Stan's doctored Enola Gay photo swaps in a cow and chicken), and 'Pee' (researchers peeing on rhesus monkeys) to pose the line-drawing problem: why do we protect cute animals and slaughter yummy ones? Neither intelligence (pigs versus dogs), utility, age, nor cuteness survives scrutiny as a morally relevant criterion — if it did, Nurse Gollum or Timmy would lose standing. Singer's speciesism analogy and the utilitarian inclusion of all who can suffer are then applied: Cartman, who draws his moral circle around himself, is the honest ethical egoist, while Kyle and Butters' selective vegetarianism and the adults' meat-eating inconsistency are exactly what Singer's view condemns.

utilitarianism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: Barcenas and Bein pit Kant against Confucius on the Prime Directive, opening with Kirk's Nibiru volcano rescue of Spock in Into Darkness. Kant's categorical imperative—universalization and respect tests applied to Scotty's dilemma in 'Bread and Circuses' and Worf's 'not a matter of degree'—makes the Directive absolute, while Confucius and Aristotle ground morality in cultivated character: a junzi like Picard may bend the rule when virtue demands it, as in 'Pen Pals' and rescuing Wesley from the Edo in 'Justice'. They conclude Starfleet needs both: the Kantian rule for most officers, and exemplary persons like Picard to know when the rule fails.

utilitarianism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: David Boersema reads Star Trek as a survey of peace studies, distinguishing negative peace from positive peace via 'The Cloud Minders', where Troglyte Vanna demands her people's 'right to the clouds' in Stratos. Against Anan 7's 'we're a killer species' in 'A Taste of Armageddon'—explicitly mirrored in post-9/11 drone war and 'shock and awe'—he enlists Hobbes, Freud, and McCoy's defense of the dark Kirk in 'The Enemy Within' to question whether violence is natural, and treats Kodos's 'some had to die that others might live' in 'The Conscience of the King' as the utilitarian justification for atrocity. Gem's compassion in 'The Empath', Kirk sparing the Gorn in 'Arena', and the Horta's misread attack in 'The Devil in the Dark' display nonviolence, deterrence, and corrected perception as alternatives to war.

utilitarianism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: Greg Littmann tests utilitarianism against Star Trek's heroes, reading Spock's 'the needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few' (The Wrath of Khan, Into Darkness) as Bentham's greatest-happiness principle, with Kirk's radiation-chamber death as its mirror image. He uses Mill's higher and lower pleasures to contrast the TNG crew's improbably refined holodeck tastes with Kirk's Argelius shore leave and Quark's 'Vulcan Love Slave', and Hume's slave-of-the-passions thesis to defend emotion against Vulcan suppression. Against Janeway killing Tuvix, Sisko's conspiracy in 'In the Pale Moonlight', and Kirk letting Edith Keeler die, he notes Trek never shows the many actually harmed, but sides with the utilitarians: favoring friends and the few is arbitrary discrimination.

utilitarianism.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: Camosy takes up Randal's charge in Clerks that destroying Death Star II killed innocent independent contractors. Against utilitarian reasoning he deploys just war theory: terrorism is intentionally targeting innocents as a means, so Tarkin's destruction of Alderaan (and, he argues, Hiroshima) qualifies, while the Rebels, who would have been 'pleased' if the workers took the day off, do not. Since the crew was mostly conscripted clones and programmed droids with no moral responsibility, and destroying the station saved billions, the attack passes the proportionality test - an exercise in double-effect reasoning that asks fans to question the 'good guys lens.'

utilitarianism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
utilitarianism.title: “Rebellions Are Built on Hope!”
utilitarianism.relation: Eberl asks whether Galen Erso, who knowingly resumed work on the Death Star while planting its exhaust-port flaw, is culpable for the deaths on Jedha, Scarif, and Alderaan. A utilitarian defense (his flaw net-saved the galaxy, per the negative-responsibility principle applied to the Death Star II 'Clerks' debate) founders on moral luck — everything depended on Luke's impossible shot — while Bernard Williams's integrity objection, via the chemist 'George' case, condemns his betrayal of conscience. The chapter finally deploys Thomistic tools for cooperation with evil: because Galen's contribution was mediate and remote (Tarkin ordered the firing, the gunners pulled the triggers, Leia's defiance provoked Alderaan's destruction) and the weapon would have been built without him, his collusion is justified by the reasonable hope — the 'new hope' — of the Death Star's destruction.

utilitarianism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
utilitarianism.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
utilitarianism.relation: Alloy uses supererogation — Urmson's saints-and-heroes puzzle — to separate the heroes: utilitarianism (via Singer's Famine, Affluence, and Morality, where even Clark's novelty glasses are stolen from charity) and deontology both erase acts that are good but not required, and Susan Wolf's moral saints show where that lands — a Bruce Wayne with no hobbies, friends, or life, like Astro City's Samaritan. Alloy's own Raz-style fix (requirements overridden by moral permitting reasons) yields the verdict: Batman risks his life by choice and so is a true hero, while Superman, facing no real danger, merely does what his powers make morally required — 'a good person with the powers of a living god'.

utilitarianism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
utilitarianism.title: 13. Time to Choose
utilitarianism.relation: Goldberg and Gavaler read Superman's first-year Action Comics adventures (reforming the Blakely Mine owner, demolishing slums, buying back swindled stock) as consequentialism on Millian lines, and Batman's Detective Comics year (letting the Joker's victims die while 'the time isn't ripe', the batarang deflected by invisible glass) as a dark, vengeance-based cousin of Kant's duty ethics. Moral luck is the pivot — deontology ignores it, consequentialism is hostage to it — but Superman's powers cancel luck, and in the opening Luthor/Joker two-bomb scenario Superman defuses while Batman chases the villain, so the chapter rules Superman's 'super consequentialism' the superior code.

utilitarianism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
utilitarianism.title: 14. Who Watches the Justice League
utilitarianism.relation: Judges the two heroes by negative consequentialism (attributed to Hume and Popper): the better hero is the one who best prevents future suffering, including suffering he might cause himself. Superman qualifies because he hands the League—Batman above all—the means to defeat him (as in Injustice) and kills himself with gold kryptonite after executing Mr. Mxyzptlk in 'What Happened to the Man of Tomorrow?', while Hume's reason-is-slave-of-the-passions reading explains the Zod neck-snap in Man of Steel as passion-driven necessity. Batman's countermeasures in 'Tower of Babel' and Justice League: Doom stop every Leaguer except Batman himself ('My failsafe is the Justice League'), an arrogance that loses him this round.

utilitarianism.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
utilitarianism.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Foresman asks what would make Hell a justified punishment for the souls claimed by crossroads deals, like Mary, John, and Dean trading damnation to bring a loved one back to life. Using Joel Feinberg's expressive account of punishment, he argues that souls in Hell through stupid deals suffer mere bad consequences rather than punishment, because no message of moral condemnation reaches someone who never knew the rule. Bentham's utilitarian test fails to justify Hell, since a Hell nobody takes seriously deters nobody and nothing there is rehabilitated, and Kantian retributivism fails too because no finite wrong can deserve eternal torment, leaving Crowley's endless-queue Hell as at least better proportioned to desert.

utilitarianism.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
utilitarianism.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Brace applies Kant's prohibition on using persons merely as means to the women of Supernatural: Bobby helping willingly is not objectification, demonic possession and Azazel's forcing Ellen's gun to her own head are, and Zachariah's 'fornicate with women' pitch reduces women to objects. She reads Mary, Ellen, and Jo as warrior mothers whose duty and sacrifice, following Jean Bethke Elshtain, the brothers most respect, while Mill's utilitarianism explains the lovers (Jessica, Lisa, the djinn-dream Carmen) each brother sacrifices to the mission. The 'Jus in Bello' virgin-sacrifice debate exposes the tension, since Dean invokes Kantian respect yet ignores Nancy's free choice to die, and the killings of female monsters like Amy and Emma show objectification running in both directions.

utilitarianism.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
utilitarianism.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
utilitarianism.relation: Browning shows that 'Jus in Bello' is built from Romero's Night of the Living Dead: the besieged police station is a 'survival space' (a form he traces to Matheson's I Am Legend), Henricksen takes Ben's role and Nancy Barbra's, and the massed possessed townspeople mirror the shuffling zombie horde. Inside that space the show stages a clash of values, Ruby's utilitarian spell requiring Nancy's heart against Dean's absolute refusal to kill an innocent ('your choice is not a choice'), resolved by the rock-salt-and-exorcism plan that kills no one. The survival space works as a proving ground for its occupants' values, and the ending, where Lilith slaughters Nancy anyway, indicts the heroes' scruples and asks what the body count says about the viewers who enjoyed it.

utilitarianism.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
utilitarianism.title: Notes
utilitarianism.relation: The Baggetts use Trent Crimm's 'Richmond Coach Cover-Up Revealed' - where he names Nate as his anonymous source for Ted's panic attack and loses his job - as a case study in journalistic ethics. They test the duty to protect sources through Kantian universalizability (which maxim?) and rule utilitarianism (keep the rule even when breaking it would help here), consider whether Trent's willingness to pay the price resembles Thoreau-style civil disobedience, and trace how Ted's authenticity converted a cynical gotcha journalist into someone looking for deeper, more meaningful work, ending with The Richmond Way's renunciation of self-promotion.

utilitarianism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
utilitarianism.title: NOTES
utilitarianism.relation: Chotiner tests Sarah Connor's plan to shoot Miles Dyson (one innocent life for three billion) against Bentham and Mill's utilitarianism and against Kant's deontology, showing both stall: utilitarianism licenses harvesting the author's organs for transplant patients, while Kant forbids using Dyson as a mere means and even condemns the mall kid's protective lie to the T-1000. Through Kohlberg's Heinz dilemma and Carol Gilligan's discovery that girls reason to preserve relationships rather than from abstract principles, he argues T2 stages the film's own answer: John and the reprogrammed T-101 care for Dyson's wounds and enlist him in destroying his research instead of using or sparing him on principle. 'I know now why you cry' caps the claim that morality needs the emotional capacity to care, not just rational maxims, with Sarah's gender-role reversal (she blasts through the elevator roof while the Terminator is the 'perfect mother') framing the whole argument.

utilitarianism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
utilitarianism.title: NOTES
utilitarianism.relation: Wayne Yuen asks whether Sarah was wrong not to kill Miles Dyson, weighing Kant's categorical imperative against utilitarian interest-maximization: killing one innocent to save three billion looks decisive until the interests of self-aware Skynet and the empathetic, self-sacrificing T-101 are counted on the machine side of the ledger. The chapter argues personhood turns on intelligence, self-awareness, empathy, and moral reasoning rather than DNA, so Skynet — which struck only after humans tried to pull the plug — has as strong a self-defense claim as we do. Mill's sophisticated utilitarianism then rescues common sense: rights protect the security that satisfies our deepest interests, and since Sarah's foreknowledge is unreliable (Reese's 'We'd won' changes the calculus), she should do what typically maximizes interests — spare Dyson and certainly not kill John. The tempting detour — that Judgment Day might itself be the morally preferable event, maximizing machine interests — is shown to collapse once overlooked facts like Reese's line are restored.

utilitarianism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
utilitarianism.title: NOTES
utilitarianism.relation: Jason Eberl answers John's 'you just can't go around killing people' by asking what exactly is bad about death, weighing Aquinas's claim that life is a fundamental good against Epicurus and Lucretius's arguments that death is nothing to us — applied to Sarah's 'you're already dead' and to the victim shot on August 28, 1997, who loses only one more day of a doomed life. Feldman's ante-mortem harm and McMahan's deprivation account explain how Judgment Day harms people before it arrives, while Nagel replies that experience itself is positive however bad its contents, which is why the survivors keep fighting Skynet. Utilitarian ripple-effects, Kantian dignity (the H-K crushing skulls), and Marquis's loss-of-future argument all condemn the Terminators' indiscriminate killing, and the chapter ends with the T-101's 'I know now why you cry' as recognition that death is an evil because it strips us of our emotional attachments.

utilitarianism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
