Fantasy legitimately fuels infatuation, courtship, idealization, and the imagined future lovers share, but Scottie's remodeling of Judy (the grey suit, the hair, the necklace) becomes blinding projection that denies the beloved's irreplaceable particularity despite her plea to be loved 'just the way I am.' Judy's need to be loved makes her complicit in her own erasure, a Laingian 'knot' in which acting on her motive defeats it, while the film maieutically draws this analysis from the viewer, as Socrates drew geometry from the slave in the Meno.

philosophy-of-love.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
philosophy-of-love.title: Love Gone Good
philosophy-of-love.relation: Johnson reads Cash as practicing "philosophy as a way of life" rather than theorizing: his love-gone-bad songs ("Cocaine Blues," "I shot a man in Reno," the addictions he chose) honor the descent into darkness, aligned with Socrates going down to Piraeus in the Republic, Nietzsche's Zarathustra descending into the depths, and biblical descents from Jacob at the Jabbok to Jonah to Christ, while his love-gone-good songs ("Daddy Sang Bass," "Man in Black") show the turn outward through which love interrupts darkness without erasing it. He frames this with Gabriel Marcel's "creative fidelity" (being at the disposal of others), Paul Tillich's courage to be, in which love is stronger than the nonbeing of death, and Sartre's Existentialism Is a Humanism, where wanting my freedom obligates me to want everyone's. The Man in Black thus carries "a little darkness" on his back while insisting "all God's children ain't free," a lived, political-ethical philosophy rather than a doctrine.

philosophy-of-love.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
philosophy-of-love.title: Conclusion June Love Beyond the Jordan
philosophy-of-love.relation: Sennett builds "June Love" out of June Carter Cash's documented love, from the "Hurt" video's staircase glance to Rosanne Cash's eulogy that June saw your potential and "lifted them up" for you to see, and the love that steadied John through addictions and infidelity for thirty-five years. He stages the philosophy-of-love dilemma between appraisal theories (Velleman, grounding love in Kantian dignity that demands respect but cannot justify loving John rather than anyone) and bestowal theories (Irving Singer, on which love projects value and so cannot be justified at all), with Frankfurt's volitional account as a side note, and proposes June Love, loving the beloved's potentiality, as the hybrid that is both objective and active and can justify loving this person. He also distinguishes June Love from codependence: enabling entrenches the addict's destruction, whereas June's confronting-and-encouraging love, echoed in "Ring of Fire" and "Far Side Banks of Jordan," called Cash to transformation while leaving him himself.

philosophy-of-love.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
philosophy-of-love.title: The Kiss
philosophy-of-love.relation: Auxier reads 'Born to Run' as Peter Pan's seduction of Wendy, drawing on Barrie's novel: Mrs. Darling's withheld kiss becomes Peter in Wendy's imagination, the narrator at the nursery window ('Wendy let me in') offers the everlasting kiss, and the glockenspiel is Tinkerbell. The philosophical war is imagination versus reason: Descartes — Captain Hook — wields the chiliagon and the cogito to convict imagination of unreliability, while Vico's imaginative universals (Wendy, Captain Hook, the city-as-altar with its downtown heart and necropolis, which is why Newark and Camden's decay strikes us as defilement) show that reason itself is a modification grown from myth, memory, and Darwin's crocodile of natural history. Since 'I imagine, therefore I am' grounds what 'I think' presupposes, the lonely rider can take Mrs. Darling's kiss 'quite easily' — the song's climax teaches Wendy to fly to a Neverland outside time where the kiss lasts forever.

philosophy-of-love.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
philosophy-of-love.title: It’s Time for the Other Walkie-Talkie
philosophy-of-love.relation: Dodge puts Monk on the case of friendship's nature, structured by Aristotle's three kinds from the Nicomachean Ethics: Hal Tucker's fake buddy act in 'Mr. Monk Makes a Friend' is pure utility, while Natalie's is virtue-friendship — she is his friend 'in spite of' the job since 'he doesn't pay her that much.' The friend as mirror and 'second self' grounds the claim that Stottlemeyer, Sharona, Natalie and Randy reflect Monk's excellence back to him, and Bacon's point that a friend redoubles joys and cuts griefs in half is shown when they stay up all night during his suicide watch. Seneca's Stoic counsel — judge a person long before admitting him, then hold nothing back — is exemplified by Natalie's fish-over-moon-rock test of Monk's character, while Montaigne's once-in-centuries friendship in which two selves blur fits only Trudy, whose dying words 'bread and butter' tell Monk they belong together. Plato's Lysis (the 'great cosmic swirly' Monk cites in 'Mr. Monk and the Bully') opens the puzzle Socrates could not solve, and the single walkie-talkie his father gave him shows why the chapter's verdict — Monk now has friends — matters.

philosophy-of-love.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
philosophy-of-love.title: 10 - Why Can’t We Be Virtual Friends
philosophy-of-love.relation: Condella tests Facebook friendship against Aristotle's three kinds (pleasure, utility, virtue) from Nicomachean Ethics VIII-IX and Cicero's De Amicitia: the average user's 281 friends far exceeds true philia, which needs time, reciprocated goodwill, and shared 'conversation and thought'. He grants that Facebook's status updates share conversation and thought and maintain ties across distance, evoking the Seinfeld episode where Jerry refuses Keith Hernandez's too-early request to help him move. But because no one has ever helped a friend move on Facebook, virtual presence cannot make us better people, and Facebook's artificial buoying of dead friendships of utility risks quantity crowding out the few deep friendships that matter.

philosophy-of-love.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
philosophy-of-love.title: Love and Doctors
philosophy-of-love.relation: Asks whether 'the Doctor' is a Kripkean rigid designator naming one individual or a non-rigid role filled by different people, using the Ninth Doctor's deathbed doubts and the Time Crash memory loop to settle on the rigid reading. He then deploys Locke's body/organism/person distinctions, Parfit's overlapping psychological-connectedness fix to Reid's transitivity objection (Sarah Jane across 1983-1996-2006), and the amnesia-prone regenerations and the Valeyard to show the organism survives regeneration while the person might not. Finally he argues that because DoctorTwo in 'Journey's End' shares all the Doctor's psychologically connected memories of Rose, fission makes them two persons with equal claim, so Rose gets the person she actually loved.

philosophy-of-love.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
philosophy-of-love.title: Surviving Fusion
philosophy-of-love.relation: Amy Kind asks whether the Holmes who marries Laurie R. King's Mary Russell could still be Holmes, weighing Aristophanes' speech in Plato's Symposium (Zeus split the original spherical humans, and love seeks our lost half) against Derek Parfit's fusion case from Reasons and Persons, in which two people grow into one body, which we would all find horrifying. Against Nozick's account of love as becoming a 'we', Delaney's merger and Gaylin's 'fused identity', she deploys Marilyn Friedman's federation model, lovers as sovereign states forming a flexible third entity, to argue that Holmes and Russell's marriage survives because its fusion reshapes identity without obliterating it: his 'half a creature with two brains and four eyes' and her refusal of the nickname 'Zherlock Mary' show both lovers keeping separate selves.

philosophy-of-love.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
philosophy-of-love.title: Nagging Spouses and Robotic Home-Wreckers
philosophy-of-love.relation: The chapter shows Hollywoodization reaching romance: the film gives us a bachelor Deckard and a shy, rescue-worthy Rachael in a classic love story that ends with the couple fleeing together, while the novel gives Deckard a badgering wife Iran and a Rachael Rosen who is a sociopath seducing him precisely so that killing androids like her becomes impossible. Knight-rescues-damsel becomes nebbish-manipulated-by-a-psychopathic-machine, and the chapter insists this wholesale rewriting of Dick's ideas about love and marriage carries philosophical implications that are easy to miss.

philosophy-of-love.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
philosophy-of-love.title: How to Tell if You Are Really Just a Robot
philosophy-of-love.relation: Using Imposter's Spence Olham, Rachel in Blade Runner, and 'The Electric Ant,' the section asks how anyone could verify they are not a machine with implanted memories and drives, noting that Dick wrote himself into Garson Poole and re-enacted Poole's drastic self-experimentation in his decades of drug use. It then argues Dick's real criterion is agape, the spontaneous, unconditional love of ancient and Christian philosophy, which robots can simulate but never experience since they love only because programmed: 'You are a robot if you cannot experience empathy.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
philosophy-of-love.title: Can a Blade Runner Love a Robot
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section contrasts Dick's bleaker novel, where J.R. Isadore's love for the androids dies when they cut the legs off his rare spider and Deckard's union with Rachael is the 'summa of falsity and mechanical motions' that fuels his resolve to destroy them, with the film's redemptive romance built on Rachael being 'more human than human.' It argues the movie preserves Dick's thesis anyway: Roy Batty's final act of saving the enemy who hunted him shows the empathy that makes the replicants persons, perhaps more than human.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: Pretty Pairs
philosophy-of-love.relation: Auxier ranks the Glimmer Twins against other songwriting pairs — Lennon-McCartney as a corporation rather than a cooperation, the Gershwins and John-Taupin as split lyricist-composer teams, Page-Plant and Waters-Gilmour as fellow full collaborations — and argues Mick and Keith matter most philosophically because they 'actually always loved each other', like twin sons of different mothers and a bickering married couple. Citing Christopher Andersen's love-triangle story of the Edith Grove flat, he claims the creative process is inseparable from eros in the ancient sense, with jealousy and envy as its close companions. Two huge personalities locked in one room without blowing up the house is what makes their collaboration so philosophically interesting.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: The Rolling Stones and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Closing track-list of Chapter 9, pairing songs from Exile on Main St. with Liz Phair's song-for-song answer Exile in Guyville under the heading of romantic and sexual exile. 'Loving Cup' meets 'Mesmerizing' as unrequited lust from male and female sides, 'Happy' meets 'Fuck and Run' on whether lasting attachments are possible, and 'Ventilator Blues' meets 'Divorce Song' on the loaded-gun violence of failing relationships. The pairing argues Phair and Jagger/Richards map the same territory of oversexed dissatisfaction from opposite perspectives.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: Chapter 13 - You Can’t Always Get What You Want
philosophy-of-love.relation: Luke Dick opens Chapter 13 with Sartre's 1947 line about marriage taboos versus contraceptives in college back yards and sets Western monogamy — inherited through church and institutions, with divorce thanks to Henry VIII — against the Stones' womanizing image, 'Some Girls' included. A timeline frames the test: Sartre and Beauvoir's 1927 pact of open love, Jagger fashioning himself Don Juan incarnate ('Sexually, yes. Financially, no. Philosophically, trying'), Charlie Watts' steadfast 1964 marriage, and Keith stealing Anita from Brian Jones. The chapter asks whether humans are cut out for monogamy at all.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: Saw Her Today at the Reception
philosophy-of-love.relation: Dick reads 'You Can't Always Get What You Want' as an anatomy of wanting to keep something and let it go at once, locating the revelation not in Mr. Jimmy or the demonstration but in the reception scene, where Mick confronts that love will never fulfill his expectations. He generalizes to ordinary life: domestic routine can blissfully stabilize a meaningful life or leave the heart 'looking bored behind the drum set,' and rock stardom's surfeit of mates only multiplies the strain. This raises the chapter's governing question — what is a tradition, and should it dictate anything?

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: Practiced at the Art of Deception
philosophy-of-love.relation: Dick diagnoses Jagger's contradiction: he wants to be both knight and sorcerer, accepted by the aristocratic tradition while living out 'Some Girls,' but you cannot be establishment and counterculture at once. The pendulum swings from sleeping with Keith's girlfriend Anita — passion fulfilled, tradition left a vacuous hole — back home to Marianne while he craves the next mistress. This incongruous moral bearings problem guarantees Mick's unfulfillment, the very tension 'You Can't Always Get What You Want' sings of.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: Glass of Wine in Her Hand
philosophy-of-love.relation: Dick portraits Keith as Bacchus incarnate, guided by camaraderie and a will for collective hedonistic comfort rather than any defined moral impulse, with romantic and platonic lines blurred — everyone nearby drinks the vapors from his cauldron. The chaos works inside the circle but turns deadly on contact with a world that needs yellow lines: Marlon running amok on the '76 tour, partners straying while Keith passes out. His verdict: Keith would be dead if he hadn't been a Rolling Stone.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: If You Try Sometimes . .
philosophy-of-love.relation: Dick closes with Charlie Watts near seventy, married to Shirley Ann Shepherd since 1964, whose only indulgence at Hugh Hefner's Playboy mansion in 1972 was the billiard room. He weighs explanations — little impulse for sexual diversity, indifference to passion's initial stages, or resilience compelled by promises and tradition — while admitting marriages are tense, burning things where fatigue is common. Watts endures as he drums: he doesn't drop the beat when his arms get tired.

philosophy-of-love.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
philosophy-of-love.title: Gimme that Old Time Religion
philosophy-of-love.relation: Carries the frenzy back to the Eleusinian Mysteries and the Dionysian festivals that were falling into ill repute by Plato's day: Socrates himself was an initiate, and Plato wrote on how eros makes humans "mad with passion," whitewashed his teacher in the Symposium, and claimed Socrates never got drunk. Plato also held that certain kinds of music ignite desire and lead to weakness and "effeminacy," associating manliness with rational self-restraint and advocating banning such modes — in short, "no Stones concert allowed in Plato's city."

philosophy-of-love.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
philosophy-of-love.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Mistich and McCullough read Klosterman's desire essays through the psychoanalytic-philosophical tradition. 'This Is Emo' — 'No woman will ever satisfy me' — is glossed with Žižek, Lacan, and Butler: desire is not meant to be fulfilled, and satisfaction would only kill it, so Klosterman's failed Waldorf Astoria romance is structurally inevitable. Kojève's Hegelian thesis that all desire is desire for the other's recognition explains Billy Joel's tragic craving for rock-critic canonization, the cereal-box hunger to be 'cool,' and Klosterman's three-week ultimatum to Diane, while Freud's theory of fantasy shows how pop culture (Lloyd Dobler, internet porn) scripts the romantic and sexual desires it then frustrates.

philosophy-of-love.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
philosophy-of-love.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Celine Morin reads Alicia's love life through the Greek triad agape, eros, and philia as laid out in Plato's Symposium: her unconditional agape for Peter is eroded by his demands for forgiveness ('Stripped', 'Boom'), while the Socratic myth of Eros born from Penia's lack explains why she tells Will their affair is 'romantic because it didn't happen'. She argues Alicia abandons the romantic soul-mate model of her pearl-necklace marriage for Giddens's egalitarian 'pure relationship' with Will, but stays moored to the old family structure, hesitating on the doorstep in the Season Three cliffhanger 'The Dream Time'. Her discovery of feminism through Diane Lockhart is what lets Alicia weigh leaving that structure without destroying her family.

philosophy-of-love.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
philosophy-of-love.title: Futurama and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Lewis argues that Futurama's answer to the fear of being forgotten - Zoidberg thriving on negative attention, Bender's billion-cubit statue and the Shrimpkins' forced worship both failing - is to become existentially intertwined with others through friendship, love, and family. Bender's arc in 'A Pharaoh to Remember' is read through Camus's Sisyphus: life itself is meaningless, but our freedom lets us fill it with meaning, which Bender finds not in monuments or worship but in seeing others remember him. Fry's devotion in 'Godfellas' and 'Jurassic Bark' (Seymour waiting outside Panucci's forever), Bender's Big Score, the holophonor opera of 'The Devil's Hands Are Idle Playthings,' and Yancey naming his son after Fry in 'The Luck of the Fryish' show remembrance surviving inside the people we have shaped, including the viewers.

philosophy-of-love.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
philosophy-of-love.title: Futurama and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Taft pairs Fry with Don Quixote: both are media-saturated characters who live as if inside fiction, break the fourth wall, and are dismissed as madmen - Fry scripting a finale for Single Female Lawyer to placate the Omicronians in 'When Aliens Attack,' Quixote blaming enchanters whenever his fantasies misfire. The chapter asks where reality ends and fiction begins, contrasting the Canon's charge that novels merely delight with the Priest's reply that stories display the beauty of a mind - dramatized when Fry's holophoner music, not worm-given strength or the Robot Devil's hands, is what moves Leela in 'Parasites Lost' and 'The Devil's Hands Are Idle Playthings.' Ending with the opera that spills into its own audience until Hermes sings 'Is this really happening or just being staged?,' the chapter argues a life of enchantment can bend reality toward fantasy - Fry authors his own story just as Quixote's neighbors finally beg him to ride again.

philosophy-of-love.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
philosophy-of-love.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Mirko Garasic reads Victor as the Modern Prometheus of the myth Plato tells in the Protagoras: like the Titan punished for stealing fire, Victor's purely technical gift of life fails because, as Zeus tells Hermes, justice and reverence must be shared by all or cities cannot exist. The chapter's real subject is love - Prometheus suffers for loving the humans he made, and the creature asks for a female companion while Victor's hate-filled destruction of her unleashes the second wave of revenge. Tim Burton's Frankenweenie splits this love/hate dualism: young Victor's tear over Sparky makes the experiment work, the classmates' prize-greed and the xenophobic mayor produce the real monsters, and Mr. Rzykruski teaches that science severed from emotion is empty. Via Zygmunt Bauman's liquid modernity, Garasic concludes that our own detached, networked isolation is the danger: scientific progress alone never makes a better society, love and community do.

philosophy-of-love.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
philosophy-of-love.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Mike Kugler argues Shelley's novel tests the radical idealism of her father William Godwin, her mother Mary Wollstonecraft, and her husband Percy: Victor's Promethean project of perfecting humanity in isolation, away from the 'intimate circle' of family and friends, produces a creature whose natural benevolence is destroyed only by repeated exclusion, first by the De Laceys. Drawing on Rousseau's and Wollstonecraft's view that children raised by benevolent parents develop their innate sympathy, the chapter reads the creature as an abandoned child - a new Adam who becomes a Satanic rebel when every community rejects him - and Victor's attempt at reproduction without women and mothers as the novel's deepest violation. The redemptive counterfactual is adoption: what if Victor had raised the creature in his home, as his father did Elizabeth?

philosophy-of-love.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
philosophy-of-love.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones argues Ender's genius is empathy cashed out through game theory: from Plato's Laches on courage to Hume's account of sympathy, sizing up the enemy's thinking is the winning strategy, and Ender's love ('in that very moment I also love him') reframes conflicts with Peter and the buggers so they can end rather than merely be won. His one failure is never extending this empathy to Graff and Rackham, so he cannot see that his final battleroom rule-breaking - 'the enemy's gate is down' - is exactly the move the adults' larger game was designed to produce.

philosophy-of-love.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
philosophy-of-love.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Christopher Lauer argues Cohen's lyrics seduce through Socratic irony as Kierkegaard analyzes it in The Concept of Irony: ostentatious self-concealment that makes hearers aware of the gap between words and intentions, building 'personality' and promising intimacy. Songs like 'Closing Time,' 'Everybody Knows,' and 'Democracy' oscillate between cynical third-person verdicts and sudden second-person address, offering a hidden sincerity only to withdraw it - an erotic improvement on Plato's Socrates that dissolves its own ironic distance. 'Hallelujah' and 'Anthem' make the program explicit, treating brokenness as the space in which love develops, while 'Tower of Song' shows the bleak side: irony collapsing into pure cynicism, the singer speaking sweetly from the Tower long after all promises of genuine intimacy have been disavowed.

philosophy-of-love.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
philosophy-of-love.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Simon Riches argues that Cohen fuses the erotic with the spiritual - worshipping female beauty as religious experience in 'Light as the Breeze' and 'Night Comes On' - and that this produces conflicted, self-deceiving relationships in songs like 'Famous Blue Raincoat' and 'Chelsea Hotel #2.' Against the classical theory of concepts embodied in Socrates' demand for essences, he deploys Wittgenstein's language games and family resemblance, Wittgensteinian views of religious belief, and Davidson's divided mind to deny that love has a rationally coherent essence. Following Richard Rorty, Cohen emerges as an ironist who rejects any 'final vocabulary' of love, and this very contingency and irony ground his authenticity as a singer of romantic love.

philosophy-of-love.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
philosophy-of-love.title: Homeland and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Brittany Lorenz and Adam Barkman apply the Greek four-loves framework (storge, eros, philia, agape) to Homeland's relationships. Terrorism breaks storge by destroying comfort in familiar places; broken eros appears in the Brody-Jessica-Mike-Carrie square and Mira's lover who loves 'making love' rather than her; philia falters because Brody hides his Islam from Jessica, and Abu Nazir's bond with Brody is Aristotle's friendship of utility, dissolving when the advantage ceases. Brody's agape for country is broken because fighting abroad violates his prior duties as husband and father, so the show offers only glimpses of loves that might be redeemed.

philosophy-of-love.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
philosophy-of-love.title: Girls and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: McCrossin asks whether Adam's Season Two finale run across Brooklyn to break down the door of a dangerously unraveling Hannah ('I was always here') is heroic, set against Hannah's 'You don't need to be like a hero' chair-and-mattress scene and Adam's 'I don't want to help... I was doing it because I love you' quarrel. He argues an act is heroic - being an 'Extraordinary Samaritan' like Wesley Autrey, the Subway Samaritan, unlike the trained Sullenberger - only when done on purpose to help, not from obligation, training, or love's compulsion, testing the point with Batman's motives. Since Adam insists no one ever does anything from a want to help, his rescue's heroic status is left genuinely open.

philosophy-of-love.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
philosophy-of-love.title: Girls and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Fisher explains the show's cycle - the girls want someone only while that person rejects them - through psychoanalytic theories of desire. Freud supplies the id/ego/superego machinery (cocaine-era Hannah dancing to 'I Don't Care (I Love It)' as pure id; Dunham's body-critical audience as the superego), while Lacan's desire - the 'untold' that must be named (Hannah's bedroom kink questions to Eric), drive, and jouissance beyond the pleasure principle - shows desire circling its object and never being satisfied, as when Hannah's e-book deal collapses into her worst OCD episode. Žižek's objet a as the object-cause of desire reads Marnie loving Charlie only once he is over her: desire reproduces itself rather than reaching its goal.

philosophy-of-love.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
philosophy-of-love.title: Girls and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Zurba reads all four girls through Julia Kristeva's adolescent malady: the faith that 'there certainly can not not be an absolutely satisfying other,' which curdles into a 'kamikaze syndrome' of nihilism and self-destruction when the ideal love object disappoints. Hannah's idealized Adam ('too absent, too present or too weird') fails her, producing self-deprecating sex, compulsive counting, and the q-tip collapse; Marnie's disappointment becomes boredom and cruelty toward Hannah; Jessa's absent father leaves her 'swimming without a life vest' on heroin; Shoshanna invests hers in Sex and the City pastiche yet alone learns to love Ray as he is. Following Kristeva (and Freud) the cure is not the perfect partner but love as psychic openness, imagination, and treating the self as 'a work in progress.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
philosophy-of-love.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Robison-Greene asks whether there are principled standards for 'shipping' TV couples and applies Platonic-Aristotelian flourishing criteria (long-term safety, emotional needs, trust, and mutual growth toward virtue) to Piper's options: Alex fails on safety and trust (selling Piper out, the perjury advice), Larry fails on empathy and growth, so by real-life standards we should ship none of them. She concludes shipping is mostly aesthetic, then proposes minimal moral rules for our attitudes toward fictional relationships: never ship Pornstache, respect consent, and never let race, gender, or orientation decide.

philosophy-of-love.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
philosophy-of-love.title: 5. Overcoming Evil with Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Bogosian argues the film locates evil not in human nature itself, as Jeanine claims when she calls human nature 'the enemy,' but in cultivable vices - Al's jealousy and fear of failure leading to attempted murder and suicide, Eric's and Jeanine's lust for power - and that only altruistic, self-sacrificial love can counteract them. With Aristotle's point that friendship is essential to developing virtue and to the good life, he shows the faction system fails on its own terms: a single virtue in isolation corrupts (Candor's truth without kindness), and a system that removes real moral and political freedom destroys the flourishing it promises. Tris's parents' sacrifices and the Tris-Four relationship - honest training advice, protection of her Divergence, and the gun-to-her-own-forehead scene where love breaks the simulation's grip - model the love that overcomes the corrupt system.

philosophy-of-love.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
philosophy-of-love.title: 3. Matthew’s Dark Side
philosophy-of-love.relation: Wills uses Georg Simmel's The Philosophy of Money to argue Matthew's two-season arc is a corruption story rather than a romance: the principled middle-class lawyer who vows Downton will not change him, calls valeting 'a very silly occupation,' and wants to dress himself gradually lets wealth enchant him, dodges reviewing the entail, and returns for Mary. He reads the Mary-Matthew match as an economic transaction that neatly solves the succession problem - money as the aristocracy's toy, Mary becoming part of the deal - against Anna and Bates's money-free courtship as the show's only genuinely loving relationship. The chapter ends by turning Simmel's warning on the audience: we root for the couple because we are as powerless before wealth's charm, and as greedy for it, as Matthew is.

philosophy-of-love.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
philosophy-of-love.title: 23. Justice in Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Adam Barkman and Noah van Brenk read Downton through C. S. Lewis's four loves (storge, eros, philia, agape) and Plato's Republic definition of justice as each thing performing its role, arguing that agape satisfies justice and then transcends it by loving the naturally unlovable. Their examples are Anna and Bates's forged thirty-pound note for the jobless Molesley, Bates and Lord Grantham sparing Thomas prison after the Jimmy incident by introducing 'a little kindness into the equation,' and Lavinia refusing Matthew's justice-only dismissal of her after his paralyzing injury. False agape appears in Thomas's manipulation of the nanny and in Vera Bates's possessive 'love,' which ends in her suicide staged as Bates's crime.

philosophy-of-love.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
philosophy-of-love.title: 24. Climbing the Ladder of Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Brendan Shea matches each speech of Plato's Symposium to a Downton plot: Phaedrus's love-inspired heroism to Thomas defending Jimmy from the robbers, Pausanias's legally shaped 'heavenly love' to Mary's path from the Pamuk scandal to wholehearted commitment with Matthew, Eryximachus's love as order to Carson and Mrs. Hughes, Aristophanes's split halves to Anna and Bates, and Agathon's tongue-in-cheek praise of love to Edith's missteps. Socrates's ladder of love then structures Sybil and Tom's romance as physical attraction ascending into love of moral beauty and wisdom - her nursing, his estate stewardship - making love the engine that gives the characters' lives meaning and, as the final rung hints, makes philosophers of them all.

philosophy-of-love.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
philosophy-of-love.title: 17. The Miracle of True Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Elsby and Luzecky use the Phaedo to make sense of Westley being 'mostly dead': Socrates's cyclical argument that opposites generate each other, Aristotle's distinctions between contradictories and contraries, and the observation that life and death here come in degrees together recast life and death as spectrum concepts rather than strict opposites. True love emerges as a second opposite of death: answering Simmias's objection that a soul, like a lyre's harmony, perishes with its instrument, they argue true love is a harmony binding persons and actions that persists beyond the particular lovers - which is how the film's miracle of true love conquers death.

philosophy-of-love.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
philosophy-of-love.title: 6. Driven by Love to Go to War
philosophy-of-love.relation: John Karavitis deploys Alain Badiou's account of love as a contingent encounter founding the 'Two scene'—seeing the world from the perspective of difference—to argue that Darrow and Eo were never truly in love: their glade conversation, his 'nobility of obedience' against her 'live for more,' was two monologues, and you cannot love a memory. He then diagnoses Darrow as a narcissist in Rousseau's sense of amour-propre—self-love turned vanity that lies to itself—whose quest serves to manage his shame at failing to protect Eo, citing Erich Fromm on narcissism's path to fascism and Aristotle on habituation into Gold ways. Only the Jackal's stone-table imprisonment shatters the narcissism ('Man is no island'), letting Darrow embrace agape, with Ovid's Echo and Narcissus and the haemanthus framing the trilogy as a warning against self-love.

philosophy-of-love.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
philosophy-of-love.title: 1. Charlie’s Eternal Quest for the Little Red-Haired Girl
philosophy-of-love.relation: The chapter reads Charlie Brown's lifelong, unconsummated longing for the never-seen Little Red-Haired Girl as a quest narrative without closure: like Beckett's Vladimir and Estragon he cannot act, and like Camus's Sisyphus he is an absurd hero whose dignity lies in persisting (the 2,120 lunch hours, the losing team, the pulled football) without reward. Using Lacan's account of desire - the wish for the Other's recognition, suspended between the demand for need and the demand for love - it argues Schulz keeps her invisible (except one 1998 silhouette) precisely so Charlie's desire stays in permanent suspension, like a Hitchcock MacGuffin. The closing section attacks The Peanuts Movie (2015) for betraying this existential vision: by showing the girl, rewarding Charlie with a kiss, and swapping Sisyphean defiance for 'believe in yourself' truisms, it delivers Sisyphus from his rock and so kills what made him admirable.

philosophy-of-love.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
philosophy-of-love.title: 4. Hendrix—Freedom and Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: The editor asks where Hendrix's 'bestness' lies by testing whether he was ever free: his songs demand freedom ('If 6 Was 9,' 'Stone Free,' 'Freedom,' 'Ezy Ryder') but never assert that the human condition is free, and his caffeine-style appetites, exploitative contracts, and management suggest determination rather than liberty. A detour through 'Hey Joe' as premeditated murder — compared with Othello and the Ice-T 'Cop Killer' affair — argues that fabricated narrators make it impossible to glean an artist's own moral sense from songs. He concludes that Hendrix's deepest mastery was the treatment of love, from 'The Wind Cries Mary' to 'Little Wing,' making him the sixties' most powerful spokesman for love rather than freedom, per the quoted 'when the power of love overcomes the love of power.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
philosophy-of-love.title: 9. Are You Experienced
philosophy-of-love.relation: Proposes an 'experientialism' — subjective conscious experience as fundamental reality, defended against eliminativists who would explain experience away as illusion — and finds its moral core in Martin Buber: the title song and 'May This Be Love' call the beloved out of an I-It world ('made out of gold and can't be sold') into reciprocal I-You relation ('take hold of my hand'), while 'The Wind Cries Mary,' 'Purple Haze,' and 'Manic Depression' lament love that is absent or unreciprocated. Experiences feel most intensely real, the chapter argues, when the Platonic order of love puts what matters most at stake — which is why kissing the sky, even without being kissed back, is worth recommending.

philosophy-of-love.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
philosophy-of-love.title: 10. Love, Truluv
philosophy-of-love.relation: Sandefur argues that what makes totalitarianism unique is its demand that subjects love their ruler, and that this project is doomed because love is selective, unequal, internal, and inalienable, invoking Aristotle's critique of Plato's community of wives and children, Machiavelli on whether rulers should be loved or feared, and Arendt on conscience as internal dialogue and totalitarianism as total rule. Winston and Julia's sex is a political act asserting the individual against the collective, while the Two Minutes Hate channels repressed erotic energy into sanctioned ecstasy directed at Big Brother, as at Khomeini's funeral. What finally breaks Winston in Room 101 is not torture as such but his surrender of Julia, the one thing that was truly his, which collapses the distinction between love and rape.

philosophy-of-love.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
philosophy-of-love.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Clayman uses 'The Lonely' as a case study for whether Corry's love for the robot Alicia is true love, classifying it through C.S. Lewis's four loves (charity, affection, friendship, Eros) and their gift-, need-, and appreciative-love qualities. He deploys Peirce's pragmatic maxim to read the meaning of 'truly loving' off its practical effects, answers the objection that a machine beloved involves prejudice with Singer's speciesism, and borrows Kendall Walton's 'Fearing Fictions' to explain how Corry, knowing Alicia is a machine, 'becomes fictional' and role-plays a believer — concluding he showed affection and friendship born of loneliness, not Eros, since he would not sacrifice his place on the ship for her.

philosophy-of-love.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
philosophy-of-love.title: 1. Do You Long for Having Your Heart Interlinked
philosophy-of-love.relation: Timothy Shanahan asks whether K and Joi's relationship counts as romance, sex, and love, using Locke's definition of a person as a thinking, reflective being to ask whether a programmed AI can love, and weighing Joi's programming against the determinism that may bind human lovers too. He reads the Joi-Mariette-K sex scene through Plato's Symposium myth of severed halves seeking union, substance dualism, and a Kant-inspired 'controlled hallucination' view of perception, concluding all sex is a person-to-person conscious connection through bodily intermediaries. Deckard's rejection of Wallace's replica Rachael is explained with a Mona Lisa forgery analogy: an indistinguishable copy still lacks the irreplaceable original person. The baseline question 'Do you long for having your heart interlinked?' frames love as the longing of lonely cells of awareness to connect.

philosophy-of-love.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
philosophy-of-love.title: 15. I, Thou, and the Neighborhood
philosophy-of-love.relation: James McLachlan pairs Rogers's 'holy ground' between television set and viewer with Buber's turn from ecstatic religion to the everyday after failing the young visitor of 1914 who came to him in need: the I-You relation of full presence versus the I-It of use is what 'It's You I Like' sings. Against Sartre's 'Hell is other people' and Augustine's reading of the burning bush as the omnipotent God, Rogers and Buber (with Rosenzweig's translation of God's name as 'the One who will be present') make listening, presence, and everyday 'twinklings' the substance of neighborly love.

philosophy-of-love.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
philosophy-of-love.title: 29. I Am Iron Man
philosophy-of-love.relation: Reads Tony Stark's fifteen-year transformation — from Yinsen's 'Is this the last act of defiance of the great Tony Stark?' in the cave to the final snap — through Maurice Blondel's philosophy of action, where meaning comes from what we will and do rather than what we know, each willed action building toward an ultimate end. It frames the journey as taking on an infinite responsibility for the other (Levinas's register): the wormhole flight in The Avengers, the armor-around-the-world obsession after the Scarlet Witch's vision, Ultron, Civil War, and finally the snap as the pure act of radical love that answers Yinsen's 'Don't waste your life.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
philosophy-of-love.title: 10. KISS Was Made for Lovin’ You
philosophy-of-love.relation: Courtland Lewis categorizes virtually the entire KISS catalogue by kind of love. Using Nicholas Wolterstorff's distinctions, he sorts erotic-activity songs ('Uh! All Night,' 'Deuce'), erotic-attachment songs ('I Still Love You,' 'Calling Dr. Love'), and erotic-attraction songs ('I Was Made for Lovin' You,' 'Hotter than Hell'), flags the disturbing near-statutory trio ('Christine Sixteen,' 'Goin' Blind,' 'Domino'), and adds non-erotic attachment, philia ('Childhood's End'), agape ('I Will Be There'), and the thirty-three percent of songs advocating a way of life ('Lick It Up' as an anti-suicide anthem of self-reclamation). He concludes with Aristotle and Plato on flourishing and Wolterstorff's claim that lives are 'shot through with love,' inviting readers to re-sort the lists with better reasons.

philosophy-of-love.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
philosophy-of-love.title: 11. Excess (I Love It)
philosophy-of-love.relation: Robert Vuckovich reads KISS's sex songs through Aristippus of Cyrene's hedonism: immediate bodily pleasure is the highest good, so the 'urge to merge' of 'Fits Like a Glove,' the whips of 'Sweet Pain,' the persuasion of 'Nothin' to Lose,' and the stewardess encounter of 'Room Service' are candid validations of pleasure — morally acceptable where desire and consent are mutual. Aristippus's cautions (the prostitute visit, the three courtesans he declined, his non-exclusive arrangement with Lais) ground the chapter's limits on excess, mirrored in Gene passing girls to Point Blank's guitarist and Paul's shift to quality over quantity. The Cyrenaic alternation of work and play matches KISS's 'God Gave Rock'n'Roll to You II' ethic — sweat first, then indulge — and Cicero's report that the body is 'nature's canon and rule' closes the case.

philosophy-of-love.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
philosophy-of-love.title: 12. An Intimate Look at Paul Stanley’s Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Robert Grant Price maps Paul Stanley's catalogue onto four loves. Eros as soulmate-love follows Aristophanes' split-beings myth from Plato's Symposium ('Forever,' 'Every Time I Look at You'); self-love follows Aquinas's demand that it be 'rightly ordered,' so Stanley's machismo songs pass while Gene's 'I' fails as disordered egomania; bodily love is defended as bawdy dramatic monologue — foreplay between lovers rather than instruction in reducing women to sex objects; and love of life is secularized agape praise in 'I'm Alive,' 'Shout It Out Loud,' and the very title Alive!. Price then asks why love drives art at all, weighing the transcendentals (true, good, beautiful) against the Scruton-versus-Craig-Martin can-of-shit debate, and reads 'Reason to Live' as the claim that only rightly ordered love can ground a life.

philosophy-of-love.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
philosophy-of-love.title: Love American Style
philosophy-of-love.relation: Klayman asks whether the android Vision can love the human Scarlet Witch, working through C.S. Lewis's four loves to show affection, friendship, Eros, and charity are all open to human-android pairs, with their marriage best read as Eros—preoccupation with one irreplaceable self rather than sexual desire. Peter Singer's attack on speciesism is extended into 'organicism', the prejudice that dismisses synthetic beings: the Vision suffers, has interests, and laments that 'we artificial life-forms are still the least accepted', so denying androids love is arbitrary bias. Peirce's pragmatic maxim settles the question by practical effects—the Vision's care, kindness, attentiveness, and intimacy with Wanda just are loving—whether the lover is flesh or machine.

philosophy-of-love.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
philosophy-of-love.title: Taking the Leap (It’s Not Fair)
philosophy-of-love.relation: Against the natural reading that Be Right Back fails because AshBot is a poor copy, the chapter argues that even a perfect duplicate, AshBot+, would not be Ash: like a perfect forgery of a twenty-dollar bill, it would share all intrinsic but none of Ash's relational properties (being Martha's beloved, the coming father of her child), which also exposes a fission paradox for psychological-continuity theories. Nozick's account of love as a 'we' — shared memory, autonomy, and well-being — explains why Martha cannot trade up or replace a dead partner without destroying the self constituted by the relationship. Parfit's view that only psychological continuity matters is then rejected: because Martha's relationship survives only if Ash does, survival itself matters, and Martha must mourn rather than cling to a specter.

philosophy-of-love.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
philosophy-of-love.title: Anti‐love Shows What Love Is
philosophy-of-love.relation: The chapter takes Irma Thomas's 'Anyone Who Knows What Love Is (Will Understand)?' - the song Brooker plants across five episodes - as the key to the series, defining love with Aquinas (to love is to wish the good by which the beloved flourishes, rooted in proper self-love, on an Aristotelian base) and evil as the void left where that good is withheld. Each episode that plays the song features characters who mishear it: Hot Shot's judges take Abi's sacrificial love song as an audition for submission to WraithBabes, Joe misreads Beth's song as meant for him and kills Beth's father in the resulting void, and Mia in Crocodile refuses the self-sacrificing loving act of confessing, murdering to fill the gap. Callow's pig-for-a-princess self-sacrifice, Theo's speech about commitment, and digital Walton dying to protect a copy of his son Tommy are the exceptions that know what love is, so the chapter concludes Black Mirror is as much about a world emptied of love as about dangerous technology.

philosophy-of-love.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
philosophy-of-love.title: Robots and Romance
philosophy-of-love.relation: Contrasts Disney's 'Irrational Matriarchy and Patriarchy' families (Triton destroying Ariel's grotto, Mother Gothel exploiting Rapunzel, Frollo imprisoning Quasimodo) with its Family Unity Model, using the Filmer–Locke debate: parents are stewards, not owners, and children have Locke's liberty to leave and choose marriage. The positive model is built on John Paul II's theology of the body — Quasimodo's 'Heaven's Light' versus Frollo's 'Hellfire' as gift-love versus using Esmeralda as an object of lust — with the Beast transformed into virtue by Belle's self-sacrificing love. It then answers Beauvoir's charge that housewifery is immanent drudgery with Elastigirl and Edna Mode's 'Done properly, parenting is heroic,' closing with WALL-E and EVE's hand-hold waking screen-addled humans back to family life.

philosophy-of-love.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
philosophy-of-love.title: We Can Fix this Hand in Hand
philosophy-of-love.relation: Heit reads Frozen through Marion's claim that 'I love you' usually certifies the speaker's ego: Anna's knocking ('Do you want to build a snowman?') is love as the risky question 'Does anyone out there love me?' asked despite years of rejection, while Hans's whirlwind engagement is Marion's 'vanity' masquerading as love. Against the prince-saves-princess script, the act of true love that thaws Anna's frozen heart turns out to be her own self-giving gesture toward Elsa, showing that true love overcomes fear rather than fulfilling one's own needs.

philosophy-of-love.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
philosophy-of-love.title: 3. Matthew’s Dark Side
philosophy-of-love.relation: Wills deploys Georg Simmel's The Philosophy of Money, with its thesis that growing wealth corrodes individuality, to reread Matthew Crawley's courtship of Mary as corruption rather than romance: the man who vows Downton won't change him soon accepts Molesley's valeting, savors finding no grounds to challenge the entail, and returns to the fortune he claimed to renounce. He contrasts their 'relationship of convenience,' which conveniently solves the succession problem, with the penniless Anna and Bates courtship as the show's picture of love uncontaminated by money. The darker claim is that viewers are corrupted alongside Matthew, rooting for a marriage that serves the estate's economic structure, so the show indicts our own captivity to wealth.

philosophy-of-love.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
philosophy-of-love.title: 23. Justice in Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Adam Barkman and Noah van Brenk apply C.S. Lewis's four loves to Downton, arguing that every love requires Platonic justice - each thing treated according to its role, as in the servants' 'My Lord' hierarchy and Bates's equal right to a fair trial - but that agape, sacrificial love, satisfies justice and then transcends it by loving the unlovable. Anna and Bates's forged thirty-pound note for the destitute Molesley, Bates sparing his hated enemy Thomas from prison, and Lavinia refusing Matthew's 'think of me as dead' dismissal are true agape, while Vera Bates's possessive blackmail and Thomas's scheme against the nanny merely ape it. The upshot is Lord Grantham's line to Alfred: do not abandon your beliefs, 'just introduce a little kindness into the equation' - justice tempered by mercy in both directions.

philosophy-of-love.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
philosophy-of-love.title: 24. Climbing the Ladder of Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Brendan Shea reads Downton's romances through each speech of Plato's Symposium in turn. Phaedrus's love-inspired heroism explains Thomas taking a beating to save Jimmy; Pausanias's contrast of common and heavenly love maps onto Mary learning to work within social rules rather than around them (Pamuk versus Matthew); Eryximachus's orderly love is Carson and Mrs. Hughes's skilled, harmonious running of the house; Aristophanes's severed halves fit Anna and Bates merging their lives through prison and rape; and Agathon's naive praise diagnoses Edith's misdirected pursuit of love. Finally Socrates's ladder of love - desire for immortality ascending from one beautiful beloved to moral beauty itself - is played out by Tom and Sybil, whose romance leads him from chauffeur to estate manager and her from fashionable life to nursing, exactly as the ladder predicts.

philosophy-of-love.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
philosophy-of-love.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones treats Ender's conflicts as games analyzable by von Neumann's minimax theorem and the theory of zero-sum, imperfect-information games, arguing Ender wins by redefining the game itself ('the enemy's gate is down') while his empathy fails only with Graff, whose larger game Ender never suspects because he never treats the adults as the enemy. He unpacks Ender's claim that to understand an enemy is to love him through Socrates' words in Plato's Laches on courage, Hume's account of sympathy, and the Christian agape of 'love your enemies,' mapping a continuum from sympathy through empathy to love.

philosophy-of-love.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
philosophy-of-love.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Why do Berger, Cecilia, Harriet, Salander, and Figuerola all bed the unprepossessing Blomkvist? Testing Kant's claim that sexual desire makes 'the loved person an Object of appetite... a lemon which has been sucked dry,' the chapter argues his appeal is that he treats women as ends in themselves—he works beside them as equals, is 'not going to compete with you' with Figuerola, and never manipulates or controls—so his sex is the least objectifying in a Sweden full of men who hate women. Against Kant and Baumrim, Irving Singer's reply that desire can respond to the whole person explains why his no-strings honesty attracts powerful women, though his refusal to define, own, or 'cherish' any lover—walking in on Erika just as Salander arrives with the Elvis cabin ad—still leaves Salander heartbroken and Figuerola in sadness.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Introduction
philosophy-of-love.relation: The introduction argues, citing Plato's saying that philosophy begins in wonder, that children's fantasy like Rowling's is a natural home for philosophy, since young readers can be nourished by ideas they cannot fully digest, like Fang gnawing a dragon bone. It canvasses the volume's guiding questions: whether love is the most powerful magic, whether souls exist and can be split by Horcruxes, what Animagi and boggarts teach about personal identity, whether choices reveal more than abilities, and whether Snape can be redeemed. It closes by framing the book in the Blackwell series tradition of using pop culture to teach philosophy, updating the 2004 Open Court volume now that all seven novels are out.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Snape and the Many-Splendored Thing
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section opens the Deavels' chapter with the puzzle of Dumbledore's 'ironclad reason' for trusting Snape even after Snape kills him, recalling McGonagall's 'he trusted... always,' and names the answer: Snape's unrequited love for Lily, which leads circuitously to his redemption. It previews the philosophical questions about the nature and varieties of love and its power to blind judgment that the chapter will bring to Snape's story.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: The Abandoned Boys
philosophy-of-love.relation: Surveying eros, philia, and agape, from the Weasleys' romantic love to Voldemort's never having wanted a friend to 'God is love,' the section draws on Plato's Symposium, where crude physical desire is progressively refined toward the beautiful and divine, to argue that love is primarily a choice of the will rather than a feeling. Hence Snape's continuing dislike of Harry is no evidence against his transformation by love; acting for others' good despite his emotions is precisely the testimony to it.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Snape the Occlumens
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section positions Snape as the third 'abandoned boy' beside Harry and Voldemort, a half-blood from an unhappy home for whom Hogwarts, as Harry observes, is where all three 'found home.' Voldemort chose power, selfishness, and a fragmented psyche while Harry opened his heart to friends and grew into integrity, and the section asks what makes this 'complicated amalgam of darkness and light,' Dumbledore's double agent and killer, tick.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Snape’s Choice
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section reads Snape's double life through the definition of love shared by writers from Aristotle to Aquinas, willing the good of the other for the other's own sake: he protects people he dislikes because his love for Lily wills their good. As an Occlumens he empties himself of feeling to lie to Voldemort's face, concealing rather than renouncing his love for Lily, and only while dying from Nagini's bite does he freely offer Harry the memories revealing that Harry is a Horcrux.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: A Work in Progress
philosophy-of-love.relation: Tracing Snape's love from the greedy boyhood watching of Lily and the Mudblood rupture through his plea to save Lily alone, which draws Dumbledore's 'You disgust me,' the section judges it short of Aristotle's beloved as a 'second self,' since he wanted Lily's good only as it related to him. Diotima's teaching in the Symposium that 'love is wanting to possess the good forever' and Benedict XVI's love as 'an ongoing exodus out of the closed inward-looking self' frame how Snape's unrequited love gradually 'gives birth in beauty' to virtue in him.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: NOTES
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section argues that vice and virtue are habits built up over time: Snape still rages at Harry-as-James and sneers at Tonks's wolf Patronus as 'weak,' yet his own doe Patronus, matching Lily's, is the magical emblem of his transformation by love. Contrasting friends, who strengthen the soul's integrity by sharing joys and sorrows, with Voldemort, whose Horcruxes give him eight 'selves' while making him less human, it reads remorse as what knits a damaged soul back together, sealed by Harry's forgiveness and the name 'Albus Severus.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Little Hangleton
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section collects the love-potion material of Half-Blood Prince: Fred and George's 'violently pink products' at Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, Amortentia's mother-of-pearl sheen and the smell of freshly mown grass that Hermione dare not finish naming, Slughorn's warning that it causes 'a powerful infatuation or obsession' rather than love, and Ron's Romilda Vane episode from spiked Chocolate Cauldrons. This sets up the chapter's question of what kind of person would actually use one, answered by Voldemort's mother.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Real Love or Mere Infatuation
philosophy-of-love.relation: Retelling Dumbledore's reconstruction for Harry, the section sets Merope Gaunt's love potion beside the Imperius Curse, one of the three unforgivable curses that robs victims of their will, as the two ways she might have won Tom Riddle Sr., noting that Harry immediately pairs them as will-robbing magic. Dumbledore's guess that Merope 'could not bear to continue enslaving him' and stopped dosing him, only to be abandoned and left to die, raises the chapter's question of what this loveless origin has to do with the prophecy.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: Not His Mother’s Son
philosophy-of-love.relation: The section argues Merope did not truly love Riddle Sr. because the potion stole his freedom: doing what you want is necessary but not sufficient for freedom, which also requires the ability to do otherwise, the 'libertarian' freedom Tom lacked. It canvasses Harry Frankfurt and the compatibilists who deny that doing-otherwise is necessary yet concedes even they would deny Tom freely loved Merope, and extends the argument to potions taken on oneself, which cheat us of becoming better persons through the hard work of real relationships.

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: NOTES
philosophy-of-love.relation: Against the obvious reading of Voldemort's loveless begetting, the section argues he is 'not his mother's son': he imitates Marvolo and Salazar Slytherin, while Merope, on Aristotle's principle that we are what we consistently do, redeemed herself by stopping the potion, renouncing magic entirely, and choosing love over hate at the cost of her life. Character is destiny only if forged by genuinely free choices rather than blood or fate, so Merope shows not even the most tragic beginnings are destined for darkness, while Voldemort, who never loved and never wanted a friend, chose otherwise, leaving Harry as the true mother's son, shielded by 'a more ancient and powerful magic than any potion.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
philosophy-of-love.title: The Triumph of Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Reading the series' set pieces as the triumph of traditionally feminine values over masculine aggression, the section moves from Lily's sacrificial love burning Quirrell, through Harry sparing Pettigrew for Lupin's and Sirius's sake, to love expelling Voldemort during the Ministry possession, where 'it was your heart that saved you' and Dumbledore names a force 'more wonderful and more terrible than death.' Harry's kindness to Kreacher, Griphook, and Dobby pays off in the Horcrux hunt, his plea that Voldemort 'try for some remorse' redefines true manhood as incorporating the feminine, and the Forest sacrifice wins the war with a defensive Expelliarmus rather than a duel, showing love more important than aggression.

philosophy-of-love.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
philosophy-of-love.title: Notes
philosophy-of-love.relation: Southworth and Tallman defend the Underwood marriage by way of Richard Wasserstrom's three grounds for condemning adultery (promise breaking, deception, pain): Frank and Claire's openly negotiated nonmonogamy - Frank disclosing the Zoe affair over breakfast, the Meechum threesome, Claire's nights with Adam Galloway - breaks no promise and involves minimal deception, so it is morally permissible. They reject Vincent Punzo's dualist claim that sex must merge souls, arguing that view rests on unverifiable theology and sets people up for guilt. The marriage's real strength is its egalitarian mutuality - Claire's sabotage of the watershed bill works as tit-for-tat strategy that restores the partnership - and agreed nonmonogamy suits Frank's bisexuality better than monogamy, which would force him to give up part of what it means to be Frank.

philosophy-of-love.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
philosophy-of-love.title: Notes
philosophy-of-love.relation: Defends the Underwoods' open marriage by applying Wasserstrom's account of adultery (wrong via promise-breaking, deception, and pain): Frank and Claire's mutually negotiated nonmonogamy-frank transparency with Claire about Zoe, Claire rushing home to Frank from Adam's-apartment avoids all three wrongs, and Punzo's dualist claim that sex merges souls is rejected as unverifiable and damaging. It reads the marriage as an egalitarian partnership whose tit-for-tat renegotiation after Claire's watershed-bill sabotage and their agreed childlessness ('I promise you freedom from that') show that nonmonogamy strengthens rather than corrodes their bond.

philosophy-of-love.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
philosophy-of-love.title: The Office and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Arp and Watson sort Dunder Mifflin's relationships into five conceptions of love: Roy's erotic 'best sex of your life' Valentine's offer to Pam as blind eros; Angela and Dwight's pursuit of an idealized mate read through Plato's Forms and the Symposium's ascent to Beauty; Aristotle's three friendships, under which the office's alliances are mere utility while Jim and Pam's teapot sacrifice in 'Christmas Party' approaches virtue friendship; the Stoic-Kantian 'equal loving' of universal respect, laughed at when Michael ranks himself with Bono and Lincoln; and agape-style family loyalty that leads Dwight to supply Michael his urine in 'Drug Testing'. The chapter concludes that Michael exemplifies a selfishness Western philosophy has no name for, failing at every form of love.

philosophy-of-love.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
philosophy-of-love.title: Dysfunctional Family Feud The No Special Obligations View
philosophy-of-love.relation: Southworth and Tallman use David Spade's 'falling star' joke about Eddie Murphy, and Murphy's twenty-year SNL boycott, to test three theories of familial obligation against the show's self-described 'family.' The role-based Just Because View, identified with Confucian filial piety, condemns Spade's disrespect toward an SNL elder but also forbids Murphy's divorce from the family; the contractarian Reciprocity View says Spade owes Dennis Miller but not Murphy, unless Murphy's saving the early show counts; and Jane English's No Special Obligations View, on which family should work like friendship, love rather than debt, clears Spade entirely. Sketches from the Vogelchecks' kissing family to Dysfunctional Family Feud supply the counterexamples.

philosophy-of-love.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
philosophy-of-love.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Taliaferro and Little ask whether Spider-Man can champion justice and love Mary Jane at the same time, framed by Mandela's tension between obligations to family and to community. Through paired scenarios — rescuing an endangered coworker at possible mortal cost versus a lover's plea to become a surgeon rather than join a deadly crime-fighting unit — they conclude that justice trumps romance in unforeseen emergencies, while romance can rightly govern the choice of a vocation. For Spider-Man the two fuse rather than conflict, since MJ loves him partly for his commitment to justice, though Gwen Stacy's death on the bridge — where his webbing snapped her neck — shows a hero can lose both at once.

philosophy-of-love.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
philosophy-of-love.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Spanakos asks why Spider-Man is called 'friendly' by testing Peter's relationships against Aristotle's three philias (pleasure, utility, virtue) and the proportionality principle that the morally inferior friend should love the superior more — a principle that breaks down for a superhero as godlike as Spider-Man. Peter's secrecy and self-sacrifice block true Aristotelian fellowship with MJ, whose crush on Spidey is mere fantasy-love, and Harry's friendship rests on pleasure and utility, failing every Aristotelian test. Yet against philia the chapter sets Christian agape (St. Basil, John 15, C.S. Lewis's Four Loves): unconditional, self-sacrificial love for the unlovable, which Peter practices toward his betrayers and which Harry finally enacts when he dies saving Peter in Spider-Man 3 — an agape that makes him Peter's equal.

philosophy-of-love.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
philosophy-of-love.title: Notes
philosophy-of-love.relation: Taliaferro and Beck trace a philosophy of love through Anakin: fatherless, he attaches compulsively to Shmi and then Padme, refusing the Stoic limits on control that Yoda and Epictetus teach, so that love curdles into the vow to 'stop people from dying.' Vader's fatherhood is the caricature of love - offering Luke power instead of care - until Luke's compassion and Vader's final self-sacrifice redeem it. The lesson: love must be tempered by humility about what Zeno and the Stoics placed outside our control, and broken family bonds can be partly repaired through costly self-sacrifice.

philosophy-of-love.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
philosophy-of-love.title: Humanoids and Droids Having Sex
philosophy-of-love.relation: Munn and Weijers argue that Lando and L3-37 in Solo display all the hallmarks of friendship and one-sided romantic love: Lando abandons self-preservation to carry the injured L3 to the Falcon and endorses her droid-emancipation crusade, while L3 tells Qi'ra she has considered a relationship with him but finds them 'not compatible'. Testing Bennet Helm's four accounts of love (union, deep mutual caring, valuing, emotional state) against the film, they conclude humanoid-droid love is genuinely possible, and that L3's claim that sex with Lando 'works' is plausible once sex is defined broadly as any activity yielding sexual reward. They ground droid friendship in Aristotle's incomplete versus complete friendships, contrasting the rewarding partnerships of R2-D2 with Anakin and BB-8 with Poe against the merely strategic Han-Lando Sabacc rivalry.

philosophy-of-love.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
philosophy-of-love.title: “Wherever I Go, He Goes”
philosophy-of-love.relation: Bishop and Bishop map The Mandalorian's Outer Rim onto a taxonomy of power: Nevarro's lawlessness is Hobbes's state of nature out of which sovereigns like Palpatine ('a safe and secure society') carve order by social contract, the Guild's codes and Djarin's creed exemplify Foucault's disciplinary power, and the Client's and Dr. Pershing's harvesting of Grogu's biology - like the Kaminoans' cloning of Jango Fett - is biopower. Against this 'binds of power' ontology they set Grogu's helpless generation of love, a 'little way' that converts Djarin, Omera, Cara Dune, and Greef Karga, and culminates in Djarin twice unhelmeting for Grogu's sake, proposing an ontology of love rather than power as the galaxy's alternative.

philosophy-of-love.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
philosophy-of-love.title: Overcoming Death through the Force of Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Lawler reads the nine-film saga as a love story in three acts structured by Plato: Anakin and Padme's passionate love - which Diotima's ladder in the Symposium treats as the necessary first rung the Jedi wrongly condemn - drives his fall, in a Phaedrus-style conflict between the upward rational horse and the downward sensuous one. The original trilogy centers the detached Platonic love of Luke and Leia, while the Rey-Kylo 'dyad in the Force' fulfills Aristophanes' halfling myth of reunited other halves and brings balance, just as Alcibiades' failure to climb beyond the first rung parallels Anakin's fixation on one person. When Ren revives the dead Rey in a Romeo-and-Juliet inversion, the chapter concludes Yoda was wrong: the Force transforms into the dead rather than them into it.

philosophy-of-love.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
philosophy-of-love.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Goguen reads the Winchesters through two masculine ideals: the warrior (Dean and Michael, chivalric protection culminating in Dean's 'protecting Sam... it's who I am') and the sovereign (Sam and Lucifer, whose freedom is analyzed with Isaiah Berlin's negative and positive liberty, with nods to Hobbes's absolute sovereign and Nietzsche's Übermensch). The show's stoic culture, where 'baring my soul like a freaking girl' is an insult, keeps the L-word unspoken, making Ellen's dying 'I will always love you, baby' to Jo a foil the brothers cannot match. Plato's Symposium, via Aristophanes' myth of split soulmates, and Aristotle's claim that the purest love is between virtuous male friends make sense of the 'psychotically, irrationally, erotically codependent' bond, and the chapter concludes that true masculinity requires embracing the seemingly supernatural: love.

philosophy-of-love.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
philosophy-of-love.title: Taylor Swift on the Values and Vulnerability of Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Uses 'hoax' to ask why we cling to love even when it harms us, answering with three values of love drawn from Swift's catalogue: Frankfurt's selfless devotion in 'I'm Only Me When I'm With You' and 'illicit affairs' ('For you, I would ruin myself'), Velleman and Iris Murdoch's loving attention that sees value in a lover's gap-toothed smile in 'Ours', and Vida Yao's escape from alienation in 'Sweet Nothing' and 'Dress'. Benjamin Bagley's 'mutual improvisation' explains why losing a lover means losing a secret language and color palette in 'illicit affairs' and 'Question...?', and why 'cardigan' needs Dessner while 'mirrorball' needs Antonoff. The chapter concludes that what makes love valuable also makes us vulnerable to the lover who 'knew the password', which is why 'hoax' is haunting yet hopeful.

philosophy-of-love.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
philosophy-of-love.title: Notes
philosophy-of-love.relation: Baggett asks whether Rupert is beyond the grace the show extends to everyone else. She surveys theories of forgiveness - Butler's change of emotion, treatment and performative accounts, and Stump's Aquinas-based framework grounding forgiveness in the love that desires another's good and union, separable from reconciliation - then applies Aristotle's corrupted bad person whose vice 'makes moral truths invisible' as Rupert's limit case. Ted's darts-based tough love is contrasted with Sassy's vengeful certainty and Deborah's cheap grace, and the chapter leaves Rupert's turnaround possible but entirely his choice, while his choices have already been making him.

philosophy-of-love.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
philosophy-of-love.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Klayman treats 'The Lonely' as a case study on whether Corry's love for the robot Alicia is true love. Using C.S. Lewis's four loves plus Peirce's pragmatic maxim (a concept's meaning is its practical effects), he argues Corry showed affection and appreciation but not Eros: he gave Alicia nothing, needed her merely against loneliness, and boarded the ship without sacrificing anything for her. Denying that a machine could be loved, he adds, would be a prejudice akin to Singer's speciesism, and Kendall Walton's 'Fearing Fictions' explains how Corry becomes fictional alongside a make-believe person.

philosophy-of-love.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
philosophy-of-love.title: Notes
philosophy-of-love.relation: DeVan uses Rand's marriage to Aviendha, Elayne, and Min (and Jordan's own two-girlfriend anecdote) to survey ethical frameworks on polyamory, arguing the answer depends on which lens one uses. Sorting love into the Greek types (ludus, eros, mania, pragma, storge, philia, agape), he runs romantic, sexual, and marital polyamory through emotivism (Ayer), ethical egoism (Ayn Rand, the Forsaken), cultural relativism and social contract (Hobbes, the Aiel), natural law and Kantian duty (the Mahabharata's Draupadi, Genesis), divine command and religion (Judaism, Christianity, Islam), and consequentialism/utilitarianism, rights, and Aristotelian/virtue ethics, invoking Cadsuane's cattle analogy and Brad Wilcox's data favoring monogamy.

philosophy-of-love.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
philosophy-of-love.title: Friendship in the Wild
philosophy-of-love.relation: Vardar argues that the Witcher 3 ending players most prefer, Ciri becoming a witcher, is reached precisely when the player curbs curiosity and limits love with respect, as Kant requires of ideal friendship in the Metaphysics of Morals. She reads the snowball-fight encouragement, letting Ciri face the Lodge sorceresses alone, cheering the destruction of Avallac'h's lab, and refusing the visit to Emperor Emhyr as choices that balance Kantian love and respect, while the alternative choices wound Ciri's pride or undermine her autonomy. George Herbert Mead's 'taking the role of the other' explains how playing both Geralt and Ciri in turn lets the player develop the perspectives needed for this moral friendship, a lesson the game carries into real-life friendships.

philosophy-of-love.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
philosophy-of-love.title: Notes
philosophy-of-love.relation: Mahon debunks three myths about the original magic lasso: it is not a magic lie detector (Diana already runs a real polygraph on the spy Elva Dove), it is not an enslavement device (slavery is domination, and even the chained Amazons never submitted), and its truth-compulsion is no coincidence. Reading Marston's four-emotion psychology, he shows the lasso and the bracelets of submission are metaphors for love's asymmetric inducement/submission bond - Aphrodite captivates, the Amazons submit - and since lying is precisely an attempt to impose one's will and dominate the hearer (Rotenstreich), a perfectly lassoed person lacks all dominance emotion and so can only submit, and therefore cannot lie. The lasso's later depowering into a mere 'lasso of truth' becomes evidence of the comic industry's discomfort with feminine power.

philosophy-of-love.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
philosophy-of-love.title: Seventeenth Hole More Than a Playing Partner Golf and Friendship
