philosophy-of-love.relation: Andy Wible argues that although golf looks like the ultimate solitary sport, it is unusually good at fostering friendship, and analyzes friendship through Aristotle's three kinds (utility, pleasure, and the highest, based on the friend's good character), supplemented by Laurence Thomas (choice, equality, mutual trust) and Blum on care as a moral phenomenon. Golf's long unhurried rounds, self-called penalties, handicap system, shared memorable shots, and retirement communities build the intimacy, trust and equality Aristotle prizes, and Robert Simon's 'mutual quest for excellence' reconciles competition with goodwill. Wible then confronts friendship's partiality—exclusionary country clubs and the sex-segregated LPGA—using Marilyn Friedman's voluntary friendship communities to argue clubs should drop discrimination on race, sex, religion and orientation while keeping friendship's care and loyalty.

philosophy-of-love.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
philosophy-of-love.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
philosophy-of-love.relation: Schmetkamp reads The Ice Storm through the philosophy of love and Hegelian recognition theory, defending a dialogical model of love (Krebs, Scheler's shared feeling) against union (Plato, Nozick, Solomon) and care (Aristotle, Frankfurt) models. She shows the Hood and Carver families lack autonomy-granting mutual recognition: Ben and Janey's affair is mere egoistic gratification, Elena would surrender her 'I' for a 'we', and Mikey seeks stilled 'molecules' and the Fantastic Four's negative zone. Invoking Sartre's the-look as objectification and shame, she argues Mikey's death finally breaks the ice through empathy and sympathy (Scheler, Stein), as Jim weeps and Elena speaks Ben's name.

philosophy-of-love.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
philosophy-of-love.title: Two Ways of Enduring the Flames The Existential Dialectics of Love in Kierkegaard and Bukowski
philosophy-of-love.relation: Andreas Seland argues that Kierkegaard and Bukowski offer opposed responses to a Romantic 'paradox of love': the beloved is a dialectical object, part inner imago (Shelley's veiled maid in 'Alastor,' Stendhal's crystallization, Lacan/Zizek) and part uncontrollable external person, and this gap breeds despair. Kierkegaard's Knight of Faith in Fear and Trembling resolves it by infinite resignation and the absurd leap, internalizing the gap and severing the tie to the real to love the princess only interiorly. Bukowski's Chinaski in Women does the opposite, deliberately choosing unstable 'Lydia-object' women who embody the gap, seeking the insecurity itself as a line of flight beyond bourgeois love and even beyond himself.

philosophy-of-love.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
philosophy-of-love.title: Me and You Identity, Love, and Friendship in the Films of Charlie Kaufman
philosophy-of-love.relation: Den Uyl argues that Kaufman's films are really about friendship rather than romance, reading them through Aristotle's character friendship (the friend as 'other self' and mirror of self-knowledge) and Montaigne's ideal of a free, voluntary friendship that also engages the body. Charlie's fictional twin Donald in Adaptation externalizes the integrity Charlie lacks, and only after internalizing Donald can he say 'I love her'; Caden in Synecdoche fails because he looks only at himself. Love succeeds, on this reading, only when grounded in the self-sufficiency and self-respect that make one capable of an 'other self,' as Eternal Sunshine's Joel and Clementine haltingly discover.

philosophy-of-love.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
philosophy-of-love.title: I Don’t Know, Just Wait Remembering Remarriage in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
philosophy-of-love.relation: Day reads Eternal Sunshine as Cavell's Hollywood comedy of remarriage: the kaleidoscopic middle in 'Joel's head' is the couple's remarriage conversation, a 'green world' where they invent a shared childhood and learn what it means to have memories together. Against a tape-recorder model of memory, he invokes the later Wittgenstein's private-language argument to argue there is no private memory — what Joel remembers he can return to Clementine in conversation. He rereads Mary's Nietzsche, the eternal recurrence, not as the end of regret but as affirming it (Joel's 'I wish I'd stayed. I do.'), and claims viewers themselves remember the erased past for the pair across the hallway's ten seconds of waiting.

philosophy-of-love.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
philosophy-of-love.title: Where the Rainbow Ends Eyes Wide Shut Karen D. Hoffman
philosophy-of-love.relation: Hoffman reads Eyes Wide Shut as Kubrick's most optimistic film, tracing how Bill and Alice Harford are 'awakened' to the uncontrollable power of sexual desire and thereby strengthen their marriage. Bill's Kantian confidence—that principled duty guarantees fidelity—is shattered by Alice's confession of overwhelming desire for the naval officer, which exposes their fidelity as mere moral luck. Through the models, Marion, Domino, and the anonymous masked orgy at Somerton (where sex is impersonal 'bodies touching bodies'), Bill seeks but fails to feel Eros; the couple finally choose a consciously chosen fidelity, and Alice's closing 'fuck' insists raw desire belongs inside marriage, which Hoffman links to Kierkegaard's view of marital love living and winning in time.

philosophy-of-love.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
philosophy-of-love.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
philosophy-of-love.relation: Hoffman reads Eyes Wide Shut as Kubrick's most optimistic film, about whether marital fidelity can be chosen rather than accidental. Bill's confidence in his own and Alice's fidelity is a Kantian appeal - duty and rational principle over inclination - which Alice's confession of overwhelming desire for the naval officer, and Bill's night among the masked orgy, expose as vulnerable to uncontrollable desire and moral luck. Hoffman argues that by unmasking and honestly acknowledging these desires (and drawing on Kierkegaard on marriage existing 'in time') the Harfords consciously rechoose their marriage, so their fidelity is no longer merely accidental.

philosophy-of-love.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
philosophy-of-love.title: The Recovery of Childhood and the Search for the Absent Father
philosophy-of-love.relation: Le Gall and Taliaferro read E.T., Hook, and the Indiana Jones trilogy through a Socratic-Platonic ideal in which the true 'adventure' ends not in glory (kleos) but in homecoming, beauty, and restored parent-child love. Indiana abandons the grail to grab his father's hand and hears 'Indiana' instead of 'Junior'; Elliott becomes a father to E.T. while E.T. teaches him loss; Peter Banning must recover his Pan-childhood to save his kids. They tie this to the Republic's Myth of Er, the Symposium's ladder of love, and xenia (hospitality) as the setting for wisdom.

philosophy-of-love.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.title: Allons-y into the Starry Heavens
philosophy-of-love.relation: Donna Marie Smith uses the Doctor and Rose's separation in "Doomsday" and "Journey's End" to explicate Kantian deontology. After framing the Doctor's virtues via Plato's four virtues and Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics and distinguishing eros, philia, and agape (with Reinette illustrating chivalrous self-sacrifice), she argues that Kant's categorical imperative and the duty-versus-inclination conflict explain why the Doctor and Rose Kant be together: their love pulls toward partiality while duty to save humanity is what they ought to do, so acting for the greater good is precisely what forces their parting.

philosophy-of-love.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
philosophy-of-love.title: 3. Why Do I Have to Be Some Kind of Hero
philosophy-of-love.relation: Zanin reads the Winchesters' sense of moral responsibility through Dostoevsky's The Karamazov Brothers, mapping Dean onto the sensualist/atheist Dmitri-Ivan and Sam onto the faithful Alyosha. Via Father Zossima's dictum that we are 'responsible to all for all,' she argues Sam and Dean's brotherhood is Christian self-sacrificial 'love in action'—shown in Dean choosing Sam over a normal life in 'Bad Boys' and the djinn world—which grounds why they keep saving strangers even after rejecting God's plan.

philosophy-of-love.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
philosophy-of-love.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
philosophy-of-love.relation: Klayman analyzes whether James Corry's love for the robot Alicia in 'The Lonely' is true love, using C.S. Lewis's four loves (charity, affection, friendship, Eros) and their three qualities (gift-, need-, appreciative-love), plus Peirce's pragmatic maxim to define 'truly loving' by its practical effects. He argues true love falls within Eros and requires a reciprocating individual, invoking Peter Singer's speciesism to reject a human-only requirement; concluding Corry showed only appreciative-love (not gift- or need-love) and that his bond was really companionship—Corry became fictional (Walton) to have something to believe in.

philosophy-of-love.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Winkle reads Sense and Sensibility as steering a 'middle road' between cold rational calculation and sentimental self-indulgence, and casts Austen as proto-feminist. She uses Wollstonecraft's Vindication to explain why Austen's silly wives (Mrs. Bennet, Lucy Steele) are products of a deficient female education that trains women to please rather than reason. She then reads Elinor Dashwood's measured love for Edward, and Marianne's near-fatal collapse over Willoughby, through bell hooks's claim that 'falling in love' surrenders agency, arguing Elinor chooses love as an act of will while Marianne must learn sense before finding lasting love with Colonel Brandon.

philosophy-of-love.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Gibson argues Austen's novels are propelled by dialectical forces (signaled by titles like Pride and Prejudice and Sense and Sensibility) that are reconciled through the marriage bond, invoking the Platonic origin of dialectic and drawing on Harold Bloom's reading of Darcy and Elizabeth as sharing a common will. Love functions as the transcendent principle that resolves opposition, but Gibson stresses (citing Derrida on the gift) that in Austen love never fully escapes the economic and social 'prisons' of marriage: Charlotte Lucas's loveless match, Fanny Price's poverty, and Anne Elliot's coerced broken engagement all show love succeeding only alongside wealth and status.

philosophy-of-love.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.relation: Lindenmuth pairs Austen with Nietzsche on what makes a happy marriage, reading Pride and Prejudice's clashes over Lizzy's refusals of Mr. Collins and Darcy, and Lady Catherine's and Sir Thomas Bertram's aristocratic insistence that superiors should choose for inferiors. He uses Nietzsche's 'philosophizing with a hammer' to cast Austen as smashing the dead traditions of entailment and arranged marriage, and Nietzsche's aphorisms (a good marriage rests on a talent for friendship and good conversation; sensuality makes love grow too fast) to judge the couples, concluding Austen holds an Aristotelian, objective view of happiness as a reward for getting life right rather than mere desire-satisfaction.

philosophy-of-love.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
philosophy-of-love.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
philosophy-of-love.relation: Fiona Woollard asks whether Zach's solo use of pornography (while partner Kelly is out) counts as cheating on their monogamous relationship. Drawing on her account of monogamy as restricting sexual intercourse to loving relationships, she argues that masturbation to porn is not sexual intercourse — there is no interaction with 'Jenna' — and that fantasizing about loveless sex is not the same as having it, so it need not undermine the significance of lovemaking; indeed masturbation aids healthy sexual self-exploration. She concedes, however, that porn which eroticizes the degradation of women (per Dworkin and MacKinnon, and Alice Walker's story 'Porn') can betray a loving relationship by revealing objectifying attitudes.

philosophy-of-love.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
philosophy-of-love.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
philosophy-of-love.relation: This span closes the walk-of-shame semiotics and then applies ancient ethics to college relationships. Puka defends long-distance college relationships through Aristotle's account of philia—arguing (provocatively, per Aristotle) that love is an activity, so being apart 'murders' love unless couples make Skype, sexting, and texting into the relationship's real medium rather than a substitute. Stephens brings Epicurus and Lucretius to 'friends with benefits': since sexual passion is a natural-but-unnecessary desire that breeds anxiety and love is a wound to the mind, while friendship is necessary for ataraxia, he concludes students should skip the sex and keep the friend—'friends are the real benefits,' echoing Tina Turner's 'What's Love Got to Do with It?' Levine/Mongeau and Smith/Morrison supply communication-research data on how FWB relationships form, are negotiated (usually not), and often end when one partner 'catches feelings.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
philosophy-of-love.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
philosophy-of-love.relation: This span turns to the ethics and epistemology of college sex. Kania argues there is no clear line between close friendship and a sexual relationship, so condemning student-professor sex logically forces condemning student-professor friendship—rejecting Golash's split and defending carefully-conducted consensual relationships. Layne narrates Socrates/Alcibiades, Abelard/Heloise, and Heidegger/Arendt to contrast Socratic eros (Plato's Symposium, love as a friend of wisdom directed at the soul) and Heideggerian authentic love ('I want you to be what you are') against Abelard's exploitative lust. McDowell mines epistemology (justification, taking beliefs 'to heart,' reflective equilibrium) to argue better thinking yields better, more autonomous sex. Pinku weighs 'plain sex' against Nagel's interpersonal-arousal account of embodiment to ask whether sex needs love, and Brophy uses Kantian dignity (treating the body as a mere means, not an end) to argue that prostitution and webcam porn undertaken to pay tuition violate the student's autonomy.

philosophy-of-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
philosophy-of-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
philosophy-of-love.relation: In this foreword Joshua Wolf Shenk recounts an intoxicating blind date with 'Rachael' to argue that dating exposes the core existential dilemma of social creatures: we crave ecstasy (ekstasis, 'standing outside oneself') yet can only connect by holding on to a discrete identity. He blames the modern isolation of the self on Descartes' claim that the self inhabits its own subjective realm and Hobbes' picture of natural man as solitary, and cites Camus that once you choose to live, the real question is how to relate to others. His unresolved paradox—needing the mantra 'I was complete before I met you' while knowing it is false—frames love as the tension between self-sufficiency and merger.

philosophy-of-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
philosophy-of-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
philosophy-of-love.relation: Editors Kristie Miller and Marlene Clark introduce the volume by opening with Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics claim that the human drive to couple is even stronger than the drive to live as a political being and that fulfillment rests in loving relationships. They frame dating as a rule-governed 'game' with aims and strategies and preview each contributor's essay—Jenkins on flirting, Langan on conservative men, Samp and Cohen against unconditional love, the elevator metaphor, cyberdating, evolutionary seduction, and Colyvan's game-theoretic mate search—tying age-old ethical questions about treating partners well to new work in evolutionary psychology, decision theory, and the ethics of online romance.

philosophy-of-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
philosophy-of-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
philosophy-of-love.relation: Carrie Jenkins does analytic conceptual analysis of flirting, rejecting the Oxford English Dictionary's claim that flirting requires having no serious intentions. She distinguishes 'flirting' from merely 'behaving flirtatiously' (Joe who over-holds eye contact, the tourist touching her earlobe in Italy are flirtatious without flirting) and argues flirting requires an intention to act in ways disposed to raise flirter-flirtee romance to salience, done in a 'knowing yet playful' way. Borrowing Kripke's 'killer yellow' to imagine 'killer-flirts' who die on contact, and citing chatbot studies, she concludes one can flirt with an imagined or non-human target only if one believes it can respond significantly.

philosophy-of-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
philosophy-of-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
philosophy-of-love.relation: Emily Langan uses focus-group data from 75 self-described ideologically conservative, mostly Christian young men to argue that flirting is a site of moral decision-making, opening with Hitch's 'right broom' line to show these men reject its libido-driven premise. She reports three shared themes—flirting is not about sex but about honesty of motive, timing within a relationship's stages, and reciprocity ('it has to be a two-way street')—and three tensions (healthy vs. harmful, superficial vs. serious, overt vs. covert), drawing on courtship-stage and flirting-style research to show that, contrary to the stereotype that only women agonize over relationships, conservative men wrestle with being 'risqué yet respectable.'

philosophy-of-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
philosophy-of-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
philosophy-of-love.relation: Jennifer Samp and Andrew Cohen argue against the Notebook-style romantic ideal of unconditional love, casting dating as a 'calculated exchange' explained by social-exchange and interdependence theory (comparison level and comparison level of alternatives). Adopting Aristotle's distinction between friendships of utility/pleasure and 'complete friendships' in which one values the friend as 'another self' and as an end in itself, they hold the best romances are complete friendships—yet insist even these must be conditioned. Their key thought experiment: a genuinely boundless love would survive discovering one's partner is a child-molesting murderer; since it should not, 'true love knows bounds' and remains part of a good life only because it can be defeated by such reasons.

philosophy-of-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
philosophy-of-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
philosophy-of-love.relation: Mary Beth Yount asks whether being 'crazy in love' really resembles mental illness, noting lovesickness was a diagnosis for nearly two millennia and that love's mood swings mimic bipolar or schizophrenic symptoms. She organizes the analysis around the four Greek loves—eros (with Plato's ladder from physical beauty to the Forms, i.e., 'Platonic love'), philia (Aristotle's Nicomachean friendship of good character), storge (familial affection), and agape (C.S. Lewis's unconditional charity)—arguing a full romance blends all four. She then surveys Fisher, Aron, and Brown's fMRI work showing romantic love as a dopamine-driven mammalian mate-choice drive stronger than the sex drive, and the 'protest'/'resignation' stages of rejection, to reassure daters their craziness is normal biology, not disorder.

philosophy-of-love.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
philosophy-of-love.title: 39. Harry Potter as Philosophy Five Types of Friendship
philosophy-of-love.relation: Okapal uses the Harry Potter films to expand Aristotle's theory of philia (friendship/love), which recognizes friendships for virtue, pleasure, and utility grounded in other-regarding concern, intimacy, choice, and a surrounding community. He argues the films show that friendships for pleasure and utility each come in beneficent and maleficent forms distinguished by whether motivations are other-regarding or purely self-regarding: the Quidditch team and the Harry-Ginny romance are beneficent pleasure-friendships (Ginny hides the Prince's book out of concern for Harry), while the Hermione-McLaggen date and Ron-Lavender fling are maleficent and short-lived. Slughorn's Slug Club is a beneficent utility-friendship of mutual advantage one may freely leave, whereas Voldemort's Death Eaters are maleficent, with all benefit flowing one way and no exit, yielding five types of friendship and locating Gryffindor's courage, inclusiveness, and loyalty as the ground of virtuous friendship.

terrorism-violence.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
terrorism-violence.title: No Damsel in Distress
terrorism-violence.relation: Mimi Marinucci argues Buffy's violence tracks what agents do, not what they are: souled Angel and chip-enabled Spike receive moral consideration, willing human evildoers like Ford ('Lie to Me') and Ethan Rayne are fought, and Buffy's 'impression of Gandhi' in 'Anne' claims violence can rightly answer injustice. Building on William R. Jones's King–Malcolm X–Mao spectrum and Hannah Arendt's warning that doing violence habituates the agent, she reads the Slayer's fight as symbolic resistance to rape and women's oppression (bloodsucking as rape metaphor in 'Buffy vs. Dracula,' Spike's assault after Buffy ends the affair). The cost is real — 'Restless' reveals the First Slayer's primeval rage and staking with 'Mr. Pointy' mirrors sexualized violence — so she ends by endorsing tempered, appropriate violence (Buffy's Tai Chi training with Angel) over both passivity and aggression.

terrorism-violence.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
terrorism-violence.title: Against Fascism
terrorism-violence.relation: Neal King argues the Buffyverse is proto-fascist: Buffy kills demons and vampires on sight within a race-like hierarchy, tempered only by an Augustinian split between natural and moral evil (soulless vampires cannot choose otherwise; soul-bearing humans like Faith, Willow, and Warren can repent), she derives authority from an ancient calling rather than democracy, and the graduation battle of 'Graduation Day, Part Two' stages citizenship forged in mass combat. He imagines a fascist Buffyverse of 'brownskirt' death squads and concludes only the show's secrecy prevents full fascism, finally recommending that the racism be dropped but the ritual sacrifice of evildoers kept — with Willow's flaying of Warren as the model.

terrorism-violence.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
terrorism-violence.title: The Superhero As Liberal Reformer
terrorism-violence.relation: Jeffrey Pasley traces the show's radical surface — capitalism equated with vampirism (Anya's greed, Glory the über-consumer, the Master's blood factory in 'The Wish'), Big Bads tearing down dimensional barriers exactly as Marx's Communist Manifesto describes the bourgeoisie dissolving feudal ties into free trade, Buffy refusing to commodify slaying into wage labor, and Giles's Magic Box selling mystified junk at inflated margins — but concludes the heroes are not revolutionaries. In the comic-book lineage of Superman and Spider-Man, Buffy and Angel are liberal reformers bound by a superhero code against killing, so Giles must murder the innocent Ben precisely to preserve Buffy's heroic mercy; Angel's 'champions' speech in 'Deep Down' states the incrementalist creed.

terrorism-violence.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
terrorism-violence.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Wendy Hamblet asks whether Narnia feeds children a dangerous militaristic moral imaginary: Homeric warrior heroes, swarthy Calormene villains, voiceless animals excluded from moral concern, and battles that decide truth, in a lineage running from Plato's censorship of nursery stories through Descartes's modernity to Heidegger's seduction by Hitler's myths. On closer reading she finds Lewis undermining militarism: morally mixed characters, condemnation of aggression, despotism, and 'reasons of state,' and room only for just war and righteous self-defense. The finale is read through Plato's cave, as the Last Battle's worlds-within-worlds expose our political 'truths' as shadow-images that unscrupulous leaders manipulate when the god is absent.

terrorism-violence.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
terrorism-violence.title: Chapter 14 - Bullshit at the Interface of Science and Policy Global Warming,
terrorism-violence.relation: The chapter dissects 'we are waging a war on terror' word by word: the inclusive 'we' conscripts the listener, 'war' triggers unquestioning patriotism, and 'terror' — an emotion, rather than 'terrorists' or 'terrorism' — keeps the enemy suitably vague, a bogeyman Other to hunt. The phrase is bullshit not because fighting terrorism is wrong but because it replaces the thought and debate that democratic policy and military decisions require with fear management, and militant jihadists' 'God's will' rhetoric works the same way, never explaining how bombing or torturing the uninvolved will end fear. Both sides use bullshit to supply identity and purpose while evading genuine moral justification, which degrades our capacity to be moved by ideas.

terrorism-violence.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
terrorism-violence.title: Violence Against Utopia
terrorism-violence.relation: Drumin reads Sabotage as Hitchcock's anti-utopian statement: against perfectible societies imagined from Plato's Republic to Skinner, Freud and Dostoyevsky show that the psyche's attraction to chaos cannot be planned or conditioned away. In four scenes, the aquarium meeting where 'monsters from the Id' watch over Verloc's bomb deal, the bird shop where explosives sit among a child's toys, the conspiracy hatched behind a movie screen whose audience laughs at on-screen chaos, and Stevie's death on the bus, the film shows a quiet family man rationalizing mass murder by 'abstracting' its victims into a mere list of names. Hitchcock punishes the audience too, implicating its own safe enjoyment of represented violence, and concludes that only constant individual vigilance, never social engineering, keeps the potential for chaos in check.

terrorism-violence.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
terrorism-violence.title: Fire Without Burn
terrorism-violence.relation: Pinedo argues the series restages 'blowback' — the CIA term for covert intervention rebounding on the intervener — in science-fiction guise: Adama's 'playing God' speech, the 'Hero' revelation that his Armistice Line black op (abandoning Bulldog Novacek) may have triggered the Cylon attack, and his confession 'I started it,' complicated by Roslin's warning against simple explanations. The sci-fi 'smokescreen' lets Moore and Eick critique the war on terror — torture, the Pegasus rapes, sympathetic suicide bombers — without naming blowback in a corporate media environment, as the producers' interviews and podcast commentaries show. The show refuses Manichean demonology: the Cylons are made in our image, and the capacity for evil 'is part of what we do in the name of war.'

terrorism-violence.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
terrorism-violence.title: The Future
terrorism-violence.relation: Dinello reads the New Caprica occupation as an Iraq allegory interpreted through Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth: occupation is violence personified (Cavil's 'saving them from damnation'), psychological violence colonizes minds (Leoben's manipulation of Starbuck, Jammer's recruitment into the New Caprica Police), and Tyrol's 'throw your body on the gears' strike speech channels Savio, Marx's seizing the means of production, and Marcuse on technology's repression. Fanon's thesis that anticolonial violence is a cleansing, liberating force is dramatized in Tigh's 'blood for blood,' the Temple massacre that recruits a thousand fighters, and Duck's suicide bombing — with Sartre's preface endorsing killing the oppressor and the ends-justify-means dispute between Tigh and Tyrol. The insurgency wins by not losing, as in Algeria and Vietnam, and the show is subversive because it makes viewers sympathize with the occupied.

terrorism-violence.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
terrorism-violence.title: Case in Point
terrorism-violence.relation: Using Wayne Booth's coduction, the ethical evaluation of fiction refined through open, informed conversation, this chapter argues BSG is a highly ethical show precisely because it keeps moral debate alive instead of preaching: the unresolved New Caprica suicide-bombing storyline, where an unsympathetic Baltar confronts a saintly Roslin in jail and she still cannot justify the bombings, invites the audience to do the ethical work. The chapter distinguishes Tolkien's allegory from applicability to block a one-to-one Iraq reading, and holds up Ronald Moore's candid blog exchange about the absence of gay characters as coduction in action. Sustained conversation, it concludes, is both the best defense against censorship and the best way to judge art.

terrorism-violence.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
terrorism-violence.title: The Only Truly Decent Man Left on the Planet
terrorism-violence.relation: John Kenneth Muir argues Dexter is best read not as heir to Hannibal Lecter or Patrick Bateman but as a full-blown superhero: his 'impeccable instincts' are a crime-detecting power like Spider-Man's spider-sense or the Shadow's, his gloves, apron and glass visor are a costume, and his 'invisible mask of sympathy' inverts the superhero mask since the Dark Passenger is the true identity. Dexter's orphan origin - Harry lifting the boy from the blood-soaked container - replays the Superman/Batman/Parker template, with the Ice Truck Killer as an amalgam of Riddler and Mr. Freeze who embodies the superhero's shadow potential, and the chapter reads Harry's Code as the American-monomyth vigilante premise that the law can be upheld only by one stepping outside it. The 'killing joke' is that the emotionless sociopath is the only impartial, decent agent of justice in a Miami Metro consumed by passion, and the extra-legal violence question the chapter raises is whether such vigilante force, with its disregard for civil rights, is what justice requires.

terrorism-violence.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
terrorism-violence.title: All for Love
terrorism-violence.relation: Jerry Piven argues Dexter's void is not genetic sociopathy but trauma: witnessing his mother's chainsaw murder and lying in her blood deadened his feelings, and each ritualized kill restages that catastrophe with the roles reversed, Dexter mastering death as the angel of it, reducing the murderer to a drop of blood he imprisons on a slide. Reading Harry's ghost as a Hamlet-father super-ego, he contends Dexter kills not only to master trauma but to please the father who channels his rage - murder 'for love' - and then generalizes: Arendt's banality of evil, Pascal on the void and faith, Kierkegaard and Heidegger on fleeing despair into conformity, Buddhist emptiness, and Becker-style terror-management findings explain how ordinary people, frightened of death and hungry for a leader's approval, can be manipulated into sanctioned slaughter, from Abu Ghraib to jihadism.

terrorism-violence.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
terrorism-violence.title: Lucifer’s Dream Ends
terrorism-violence.relation: Narrates the collapse of the Lucifer project through 1968-69: "Street Fighting Man" banned as incitement to violence after Mayor Daley's police beat protestors, Jagger reading Shelley's "Adonais" at Hyde Park after Brian Jones's death, and Anger salvaging Invocation of My Demon Brother from the stalled film. At Altamont the Hell's Angels stabbed Meredith Hunter during "Under My Thumb" while Jagger pleaded "just cool out"; Lester Bangs blamed egoism, hype and greed rather than the devil, and the Stones survived by trading rage and chaos for controlled spectacle — from Rock Satans to a knighted Elder Statesman of Rock.

terrorism-violence.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
terrorism-violence.title: Homeland and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Roberto Sirvent and Ian Diorio argue, following William Cavanaugh's 'myth of religious violence', that the assumption that religion is uniquely irrational, absolutist, and divisive blinds Americans to their own fanaticism. Homeland's blind spots - Carrie suspecting the Muslim Galvez, Dana's classmate nuking Tehran, 'Infinite Justice' naming, Guantanamo torture flashed right after Carrie's 'We don't do that here' - show the religious/secular split is a construct (traced to Locke's privatizing of faith and Augustine's broad religio) that legitimizes state violence while deeming identical acts crazy when done by the religious. Nazir's 'Who is the terrorist?' drone question and 'We only begin as enemies because that's what others told us to be' seal the point.

terrorism-violence.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
terrorism-violence.title: Homeland and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Jai Galliott argues Homeland's drone strike that killed Issa is not a one-off plot device but mirrors real US drone warfare that breeds blowback: strikes strengthen al-Qaeda's brand and radicalize the disaffected, from Brody to the Boston bombers. He analyzes the asymmetry problem - the weak side comingles with civilians, straining the just war principles of discrimination and proportionality, while drone operators living among US suburbs become contested targets - and rejects giving weaker states a 'wild card' of lowered ethical standards. His proposal is that the technologically superior side bind itself to stricter just war compliance and policing-like restraint, since foreseeable terrorist reciprocity can tip proportionality against the war itself.

terrorism-violence.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
terrorism-violence.title: Homeland and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: William Rodriguez traces terrorism's evolving meaning from the Jacobins' state Terror through anarchist 'propaganda by deed' (Nechayev, Bakunin) to non-state groups, then tests whether Abu Nazir's campaign, grounded in bin Laden's 1998 fatwa grievances and the greater/lesser jihad distinction, can be morally justified. On a utilitarian defense terrorism could be last-resort self-defense against a collectively guilty population, but the just war criteria of competent authority, right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality all fail for al-Qaeda, since civilians killed on 9/11 were neither combatants nor guilty. Deontologically, targeting civilians violates the right to life and human dignity, so Nazir's attacks on innocents are murder, however real the grievances.

terrorism-violence.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
terrorism-violence.title: Homeland and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: This standalone section traces terrorism's history and definition, from the French Revolution's Reign of Terror when the state was 'le terroriste' (Robespierre's 'terror is nothing other than justice that is prompt, severe, and inflexible') to the term's reversal onto non-state actors via Russian anarchists like Nechayev. It offers a seven-feature characterization (violence, destruction, indiscriminate harm, psychological trauma, propaganda, policy change, non-state perpetration) matching the UN's 2004 definition, then catalogs often-forgotten American terrorism: the Boston Tea Party reframed as a news report, the Ku Klux Klan's campaign, the Haymarket bombing, the Los Angeles Times and Wall Street bombings by labor radicals and anarchists, the Bath School massacre, the Mad Bomber, the Weather Underground, anti-abortion Army of God killings, and the Unabomber.

terrorism-violence.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
terrorism-violence.title: 1. A Good Man Goes to War
terrorism-violence.relation: Pless argues the Doctor's shift from the Ninth's self-avowed 'coward, any day' to the Eleventh's gun-toting action hero tracks real-world politics and markets rather than internal story logic: after the 7/7 London bombings and amid the War on Terror, and as the show's global export grew, a war-weary British ideal gave way to the decisive 'Oncoming Storm.' She traces the arc through the Tenth's gleeful xenocide of the Racnoss in 'The Runaway Bride,' the eternal punishment of the Family of Blood, the Eleventh brainwashing humanity to exterminate the Silence in 'Day of the Moon,' and the assault of 'A Good Man Goes to War,' before 'The Day of the Doctor' retcons the Time War so the Doctor never destroyed the Time Lords, validating the action-hero persona. Her conclusion: in a crisis culture demanding proactive heroes, cowardice—once the Doctor's honest self-assessment—was rebranded as vice.

terrorism-violence.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
terrorism-violence.title: 14. Guns Don’t Kill Colors—Colors Kill Colors
terrorism-violence.relation: Robert Arp argues from Hobbes's right of nature—self-preservation as the first law found out by reason—that individuals, and by extension oppressed peoples, have a right to the means of lethal defense, so arming the lowColors of the Society is justified. He weighs pacifist counterpoints (Augustine on self-defense as inordinate self-love, the Buddhist first precept, Camus's refusal to kill) and answers with Aquinas's principle of double effect: Darrow destroying the flagship to save Luna, intending the good while foreseeing the deaths, is justified, as is killing in defense of innocent children the Institute rapes and eats. The Society then illustrates why disarmament enables tyranny—Hideyoshi's Sword Hunt, Stalin's weapons bans, the Golds' razor monopoly—so that when lowColors finally receive weapons in Morning Star they become the means by which the police state falls: guns equalize the weak against aggressors and the people against the state.

terrorism-violence.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
terrorism-violence.title: 28. Severed Heads, Dirty Hands
terrorism-violence.relation: Ivanković and Božac argue that ruling Westeros necessarily means dirtying one's hands, staging the paradox through Varys's counsel to Ned and Jaime's 'finest act.' Hobbes supplies the baseline that anything preserving peace beats the war of all against all, Walzer permits dirty hands only to avert communal death (Daenerys swindling the Astapor slavers), and Kant's absolute refusal to lie - mirrored in Ned's honor - costs Ned his head and the realm a war. The chapter also indicts the reverse: Aemon's refusal of the throne and other too-clean refusals of responsibility are moral failures, Jon's killing of Qhorin Halfhand shows dirty hands are not just for kings, and rulers must resist the downward spiral while keeping, as Dany does, a gentle heart for the true goal.

terrorism-violence.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
terrorism-violence.title: 20. Deadpool’s Genocide of the Marvel Universe
terrorism-violence.relation: Taking Deadpool Kills the Marvel Universe seriously as a genocide story, the chapter reviews Lemkin's coinage and the 1948 Genocide Convention, then tests the mitigating factors - Deadpool's insanity, the X-Men's negligence in committing him to Psycho-Man's fake asylum, and Psycho-Man's manipulation - and finds none of them exculpatory. Killing Uatu the Watcher first and the Avengers next follows the genocide playbook of eliminating a community's intellectuals and pillars, and viewing his fellow characters as sheep completes the dehumanization that makes atrocity possible, while using everyone as means to his liberation violates Kant's demand never to treat persons as mere means. Invoking the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and Thucydides' Melian Dialogue as the classic case of victims left unable to tell their story, the author concludes Deadpool bears full responsibility.

terrorism-violence.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
terrorism-violence.title: 1. The Deed of F’ing Society
terrorism-violence.relation: Rocha reads fsociety's 5/9 logic-bomb attack on E Corp as anarchist 'propaganda of the deed' - a shocking act meant to wake people from their comfortable slumber inside hierarchy - and positions it between Alexander Berkman's violent anarchism (mirroring Phillip Price's 'bullet in the right place') and Gandhi's nonviolent self-suffering, quoting satyagraha and the older Goldman's rejection of violence. He then runs the hack through just war theory's four questions (necessity, proportionality, justification, effectiveness), noting that wiping the debt records also destroyed savings and indirectly got people like Gideon killed, and that fsociety, as Trenton says, never paints the alternative society - so the reader is left to answer whether the deed was justified.

terrorism-violence.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
terrorism-violence.title: 10. If It Isn’t Justified Is It Still My Revolution
terrorism-violence.relation: Writing as a guilt-ridden fsociety member haunted by James Plouffe's on-air suicide, Altmann tests the 5/9 revolution against three theorists: Burke's conservatism condemns all revolution as destruction of social tradition (and fsociety's blackout chaos and Susan Jacobs's death seem to prove him right), while Marx's class struggle between E Corp's bourgeoisie and the indebted proletariat makes revolution the only exit from history's cycle. Kai Nielsen's condition - revolution is justified only when no other recourse exists - settles it: Angela's failed attempt to reform E Corp from within shows non-revolutionary change is impossible, so the author keeps fighting 'with a keyboard whose clacking is endless.'

terrorism-violence.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
terrorism-violence.title: 11. Is Resistance to Fascism Terrorism
terrorism-violence.relation: Corey Horn tests whether the American Resistance counts as terrorists, first against the US Justice Department definition and then Jeremy Waldron's four conditions of coercive terror: Lem's gunpoint demand of Joe and Juliana meets only two conditions, while the Reich's torture of the factory courier and the atomic destruction of Washington meet all four. Jürgen Habermas's distinction between political terrorism with an end goal and purely fear-driven global terrorism then lets him conclude that the Resistance is at most political terrorists whose violence is really a just continuation of war against an occupier — the same act that gets relabeled justice once the revolution wins.

terrorism-violence.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
terrorism-violence.title: Humanization A Violent Phenomenon
terrorism-violence.relation: Spanakos reads the hosts' season-one rebellion through Fanon's decolonization theory, itself a revision of Hegel's master-slave dialectic: as the settler 'brings the native into existence,' Ford and Delos create the hosts, assigning their identities and roles, while the master 'laughs at the consciousness of the slave' because the hosts' recognition is not freely given. Fanonian violence is ethical, justified, and transformative: Maeve's jailbreak and Dolores's execution of Ford (rather than her tormentor, the Man in Black, whom she sees as the system's victim) are acts that make the colonized a maker of history, while Bernard - who speaks his creator's language and has no culture or past of his own, like Fanon's assimilated African bourgeoisie - shows violence that does not liberate. The chapter closes that the park dehumanizes the masters too, so William's collapse into the Man in Black proves Fanon's point that the colonizer cannot free himself; humanization is a violent phenomenon.

terrorism-violence.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
terrorism-violence.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
terrorism-violence.relation: Dinello maps Westworld point-by-point onto Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism: the park is a concentration camp that kills the juridical person (hosts as chattel in a 'fictitious world' of Western propaganda), the moral person (Ford forcing Bernard to murder Theresa, Maeve's engineered failure to protect her daughter), and individuality itself (surveillance, resets, 'ghastly marionettes'), with Ford as a Mengele-like ideological scientist who, like Hitler, merely plagiarizes popular myths (John Ford's Westerns, R.U.R.). Liberation then follows Fanon's Wretched of the Earth: violence as a 'cleansing force' that frees the colonized mind, so Maeve's suicide-by-incineration (echoing Plath's Lady Lazarus) and Dolores's beating of the Man in Black and massacre of the Delos board enact decolonization as the creation of 'new men' - a new Robo sapiens species - with Sartre's endorsement that killing eliminates oppressor and oppressed in one go, while Fanon's warning that hatred and revenge are not an agenda sets the conditions for what the resistance must do next.

terrorism-violence.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
terrorism-violence.title: Its Structural Perfection is Only Matched by its Autonomy
terrorism-violence.relation: Defends the Xenomorphs: if the Queen's tactical intelligence (incubating her eggs under the reactor, ordering drones to hold fire, cutting the power) and the species' hive organization satisfy Sartre's criteria of self-creating persons, then their 'attacks' are legitimate self-defense on the model of Sartre's preface to Fanon's Wretched of the Earth, where the colonized's violence restores a denied personhood. Read without anthropocentrism, Alien is the story of a newborn extraterrestrial hunted to death by humans, and Weyland-Yutani, the Marines, and the colonists of LV-426 - not the aliens - are the series' true villains.

terrorism-violence.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
terrorism-violence.title: Fire Without Burn
terrorism-violence.relation: Pinedo argues the re-imagined series restages 'blowback,' the CIA-coined term for retaliation against covert intervention that public discourse avoids, in science-fiction guise: Adama's 'you cannot play God, then wash your hands of the things you've created' speech, and the episode 'Hero,' where Adama confesses his black-ops crossing of the Armistice Line ('I started it') before Roslin reframes his guilt into 'a thousand things' the Colonials did over forty years. The chapter shows how the sci-fi 'smokescreen' (Moore and Eick's own word) lets the show do what news coverage cannot: sympathetically depict suicide bombing on New Caprica and torture by the 'good guys' (Starbuck's waterboarding of Leoben, Cain's ordered rape of Gina), dismantling the Manichean myth of American innocence after 9/11 while avoiding the network wrath that naming blowback would bring.

terrorism-violence.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
terrorism-violence.title: The Future
terrorism-violence.relation: Dinello argues the New Caprica occupation arc deliberately dramatizes Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth applied to Iraq: Cylon colonization (Cavil as Cheney-Rumsfeld bringing 'the love of god,' Baltar as puppet leader, Colonial One as Green Zone, hooded detainees) enacts Fanon's colonial violence and psychological colonization of the mind, seen in Leoben's manipulation of Starbuck and Jammer's recruitment into the New Caprica Police. The insurgency enacts Fanon's violence-as-cleansing-force: Tigh's 'blood for blood,' Duck's suicide bombing of the NCP graduation, and Tyrol's Mario Savio-inspired 'throw your body on the gears' speech, which the chapter links to Marx's seizure of the means of production and Marcuse on technology's repressiveness, while Sartre's preface licenses anticolonial violence against liberal moralizing. It concludes that occupation breeds the terrorists it fights, insurgents win by not losing, and the show is subversive because it makes viewers sympathize with 'our real-world enemies.'

terrorism-violence.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
terrorism-violence.title: Bird or Cage
terrorism-violence.relation: Elmore reads Columbia's founding through Carl Schmitt: Comstock's baptism Voxophone ('who is that man who lies submerged?') dramatizes how every legal order is founded from outside the law, and the city's identity is built on friend/enemy antagonisms, racial, class, and theocratic, against the 'Sodom below'. The Vox Populi's collapse into tyranny (Daisy Fitzroy threatening Fink's son) follows logically from an identity defined purely by opposition, while Columbia's dependence on Georgia's penal labor shows the friend group materially needs its enemy, making politics an endless war like the War on Terror. Schmitt's sovereign ('he who decides on the exception') and the tears' endless splitting of Booker and Elizabeth mirror the infinite regress of legitimate decision, leaving 'you can't lose if you don't play' as the bleak lesson, softened only by old Elizabeth's tear that lets Booker try again.

terrorism-violence.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
terrorism-violence.title: 5 T’Challa’s Liberalism and Killmonger’s Pan-Africanism
terrorism-violence.relation: Graves sets T'Challa's liberal internationalism — UN sovereign equality and collective security, which he traces through the organization's Charter limits and its record of preserving the status quo — against Killmonger's Pan-Africanism, the liberation lineage of the 1900 Pan-African Conference, Du Bois's Pan-African Congresses, Garvey's UNIA, and Nkrumah's 'Africa Must Unite,' which N'Jobu and Killmonger carry forward with vibranium weapons after centuries of Wakandan indifference to slavery, colonialism, and apartheid. He argues collective security has repeatedly failed oppressed Black populations, making Killmonger's realist 'Africans must save themselves' position understandable, though he questions whether arms rather than aid can liberate and calls T'Challa's single Oakland outreach center inadequate to Wakanda's wealth.

terrorism-violence.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
terrorism-violence.title: 10 Understanding the Reigns of T’Challa and Killmonger through Hannah Arendt
terrorism-violence.relation: Sinanan reads both reigns through Arendt's account of collective responsibility: T'Challa moves from conscience-based 'I am not king of all people' to owning what Wakanda did in its name ('He was the truth I chose to omit') and finally to political action in Oakland and at the UN, while Killmonger — an MIT-educated Navy SEAL embodying the collective that formed him — becomes the imperialist he opposed, his 'burn it all' revolution matching Arendt's warning about totalitarian domination from within. She compares Killmonger's council speech and herb-burning directly to Hitler's 1924 Munich trial speech, reads his manipulation of the challenge ritual as totalitarian propaganda that organizes rather than persuades, and credits Nakia, Okoye, Shuri, and Ramonda with refusing Arendt's ultimate danger, indifference.

terrorism-violence.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
terrorism-violence.title: 21 Dismantling the Master’s House with the Master’s Tools
terrorism-violence.relation: Thanayi Jackson reads Killmonger through Audre Lorde's 'the master's tools will never dismantle the master's house,' asking whether a CIA-trained operative wielding the colonizer's own weapons can end colonialism. Comparing Killmonger to Wallace from The Wire - both orphans of Africa reared by America's ghettos - she concedes the appeal of his Oakland-forged mastery ('I know how colonizers think') but argues through bell hooks's gloss of Lorde that one cannot destroy imperialist white-supremacist capitalist patriarchy by creating one's own version of it: Killmonger's plan to kill oppressors 'and their children' makes him a new master, not a liberator. T'Challa's Oakland outreach center answers the challenge only partially, leaving the chapter asking whether the master's house was dismantled or merely refurbished.

terrorism-violence.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
terrorism-violence.title: 22 An Impossible Return (Anti)Colonialism in of Black Panther
terrorism-violence.relation: Julio Covarrubias-Cabeza argues that Black Panther is a supremely colonial film: its narrative coherence depends on the history of slavery, franchise colonialism, and neocolonial domination, yet it buries that history in the pathologized figure of Killmonger. Drawing on Fanon's account of the European unconscious projecting its base instincts onto Black bodies, on Tommy Curry's 'man-not' and anti-Black misandry, and on Quijano's coloniality of power, the chapter contends the film devalues Black American men and discredits radical anti-colonial politics while letting Wakanda ally with the CIA against its own. Killmonger's 'impossible return' to a pre-colonial homeland - his body scarred by each kill - is the site where the film's repressed colonial violence ruptures to the surface.

terrorism-violence.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
terrorism-violence.title: 23 T’Challa’s Dream and Killmonger’s Means Echoes of MLK and Malcolm X
terrorism-violence.relation: Gerald Browning maps T'Challa onto Martin Luther King Jr. and Killmonger onto Malcolm X: T'Challa's UN speech about building bridges 'as if we were one single tribe' echoes 'I Have a Dream,' while Killmonger's vibranium insurrection enacts Malcolm's language-of-the-shotgun rhetoric and 'by any means necessary' motto. The comparison is deliberately qualified: Killmonger lacks Malcolm's 'intelligently directed' extremism and his post-Mecca evolution toward a universal brotherhood, never reconsidering even when T'Challa offers to heal him, and he turns his aggression on Wakandans themselves in a way Malcolm never did. The chapter concludes that the T'Challa-Killmonger foil extends the King-Malcolm conversation into the Black Lives Matter era.

terrorism-violence.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
terrorism-violence.title: 24 “It’s Time They Knew the Truth about Us! We’re Warriors!” Black Panther and the Black Panther Party
terrorism-violence.relation: Karen Kohoutek places N'Jobu's and Killmonger's radicalization in the lineage of the Black Panther Party, founded in Oakland months after the comic debuted in 1966: both cite the same police brutality and impoverished communities, and both answer with arming the oppressed. Through Robert F. Williams's Negroes with Guns and Max Weber's state monopoly on legitimate violence, the chapter shows how Black armed self-defense keeps getting recoded as aggression - from the Panthers' patrol of Oakland to the Mulford Act passed to disarm them - so that Killmonger's plan reads as genocidal while CIA destabilization, his actual training, passes as legitimate. Wakanda's closing pivot to outreach centers mirrors the Party's Free Breakfast and health-clinic programs, making T'Challa's UN speech an imagined corrective to failed American idealism.

terrorism-violence.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
terrorism-violence.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Jacob Held uses "War Pigs", "Electric Funeral", and "Children of the Grave" to teach just war theory's two halves, jus ad bellum (just cause, last resort, proportion) and jus in bello (proportion and discrimination toward non-combatants), reading Sabbath as condemning unjust wars like Vietnam and atomic overkill rather than all force, with Ozzy's "Thank God for the Bomb" voicing deterrence. Citing Walzer on "even in hell, it is possible to be more or less humane", he argues pacifism functions as a vital moral check, and that the war on terror fails just war standards outright: it cannot be won, so any means, assassination, torture, reclassifying terrorists outside both soldier and criminal law, are disproportionate and morally bankrupt, exactly the war-pig behavior the song's judgment day condemns.

terrorism-violence.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
terrorism-violence.title: A Crossroads in Human History
terrorism-violence.relation: Trip McCrossin reads season five's asteroid strikes on Earth as a 9/11 allegory (Delgado's 'at least now they know it's an attack') and applies Michael Walzer's five conditions to define Marco Inaros' terrorism: deliberate harm to randomly selected innocents, meant to terrify a cohort into political change, as in Marco's 'crossroads in human history' broadcast. This yields the terrorist's dilemma — justice toward victims versus compassion toward beneficiaries — while Avasarala's opening gravity-torture scene and her 'dirty hands' assign the opponent blame for failing to relieve the oppression that makes terrorism seem a last resort. Lydia's 'churn' ('float to the top or sink to the bottom') and her lesson that one can 'lead a good life without being a good person' explain how Amos and Clarissa redeem each other on the road to Baltimore, whereas Marco, like Arendt's Eichmann, cannot think from anyone else's standpoint ('everything we ever dreamed of'); the chapter ends with Avasarala's proposed Inners-Belters union as her own redemption — 'this is how we win.'

terrorism-violence.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
terrorism-violence.title: A More Human Future
terrorism-violence.relation: Sid Simpson argues, through Frantz Fanon, that Marco Inaros' asteroid attacks must be judged as anti-colonial violence rather than simple monstrosity. Using Black Skin, White Masks' ontological division (Belters as 'skinnies', 'possessions, animals', the dehumanization that made Eros an acceptable testing ground and Anderson Station a 'message'), reinforced by Columbus and las Casas on Spanish colonization, he shows why the Inners' 'peace' is merely the status quo of ongoing extraction — Fanon's 'hypnotherapy' — that no treaty or Ring can fix. Fanon's Wretched of the Earth then recasts anti-colonial violence as a 'cleansing force' that shatters the colonial ontology and lets the colonized create a 'new, better, more human form' of humanity, so that Marco's personal narcissism and possible insincerity do not settle the political question: for the Belt, violence may be not only the last option but the most just one, against Avasarala's champagne-toast universalism that never takes Belter grievances seriously.

terrorism-violence.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
terrorism-violence.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Novy uses Terry Berg's gay-bashing coma in 'Brother's Keeper' to argue hate crimes are a kind of terrorism: justice, in Iris Marion Young's enabling sense, requires social conditions in which citizens can develop and exercise their capacities, and an attack that makes every gay teenager police holding hands in public harms the whole group, so Mill's greatest-happiness principle and Feinberg's expressivism justify enhanced penalties. The chapter then turns on Kyle, who tortures Daniel Hirsh on Rikers Island and nearly beats his two accomplices to death, asking whether extraordinary crimes justify extraordinary procedures in a post-9/11 world. Kyle's horror afterward, begging Flash to undo the last twenty-four hours and losing his will to protect, and Batman's pointed 'But that is me, isn't it?' mark the line between punishing brutality and becoming it.

terrorism-violence.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
terrorism-violence.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Melançon tests the Mockingjay revolution against the just-war tradition's three parts: jus ad bellum, jus in bello, and jus post bellum. The districts satisfy just cause, right intention, last resort, and proportionality against the Capitol, but stumble on competent authority — no legitimate state authorizes their rebellion — a problem the chapter says forces the tradition to admit popular self-determination. Both sides then violate jus in bello: the rebels' avalanche on the Nut fails military necessity and proportionality, and the bombing of the Capitol's child shields plus the medics treating them breaches distinction twice, making the rebels as bad as the Capitol. The contemplated final Hunger Games with Capitol children would violate jus post bellum, so the revolution was not a just war and only stumbles into peace.

terrorism-violence.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
terrorism-violence.title: NOTES
terrorism-violence.relation: Fosl argues that although the survivors' internal order looks Lockean - Jack's uncoerced leadership, natural rights, minimal government - and is bonded by Rousseauan pity and Humean sympathy (Kate staying in the cage with Sawyer, 'live together, die alone'), the show's deepest political logic follows Carl Schmitt's friend-enemy distinction: the survivors cohere only in opposition to the Others, torture is excused in liberal terms, and conflicts end in redemptive violence, with Jack both killing the enemy and dying a Christlike sacrifice. Hobbes's absence from the character names signals the show's rejection of a war of all against all among the survivors, yet the finale's divine manipulation of the castaways, with Jacob treating people as means against Kantian autonomy, repudiates the liberal hope of a rational peace altogether.

terrorism-violence.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
terrorism-violence.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.relation: Asks whether SAMCRO's gun suppliers, the Real IRA, are terrorists or freedom fighters, using Walzer's definition of terrorism as random killing of innocents to spread fear and his combatant/non-combatant distinction. The Irish Kings pass as freedom fighters—Kutz's three criteria of internal ordering (the hierarchy that has Sean Casey strangle the turncoat Cameron Hayes), just aims (a united Ireland), and target discrimination fit them—whereas Jimmy O, recruiting children as young as ten and attacking anyone with Loyalist sympathies, fails; his real motive being profit, Fr. Ashby concludes 'he's not a soldier anymore, just a gangster,' prompting the chapter's new category: thug. Fr. Ashby's own complicity in a church execution, redeemed by becoming a hostage so Abel can return to Jax, closes the moral ledger.

terrorism-violence.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
terrorism-violence.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
terrorism-violence.relation: Kirby reads the 'Imaginationland' trilogy as a satire of post-9/11 America interpreted through Ulrich Beck's world risk society: the Pentagon generals, still thinking in Cold War categories like 'Project X' and Chinese imagination portals, embody Beck's denial response and end up voting to nuke Imaginationland, while Cartman's Rambo-style self-interest embodies the apathetic response. Socrates' practice of demanding definitions frames the chapter's question of what terrorism actually is (via Hoffman's five criteria), and Socratic ignorance about what one does not know is contrasted with the worse condition of not being able to know what you do not know. Kyle's courtroom speech that imaginary beings like Luke Skywalker and Santa are 'realer' than most real people, and Butters' creative power to imagine Santa back to life, point to Beck's cosmopolitan 'transformation': imagination and cross-border cooperation as the way out of risk panic.

terrorism-violence.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
terrorism-violence.title: Notes
terrorism-violence.relation: David Boersema reads Star Trek as a survey of peace studies, distinguishing negative peace from positive peace via 'The Cloud Minders', where Troglyte Vanna demands her people's 'right to the clouds' in Stratos. Against Anan 7's 'we're a killer species' in 'A Taste of Armageddon'—explicitly mirrored in post-9/11 drone war and 'shock and awe'—he enlists Hobbes, Freud, and McCoy's defense of the dark Kirk in 'The Enemy Within' to question whether violence is natural, and treats Kodos's 'some had to die that others might live' in 'The Conscience of the King' as the utilitarian justification for atrocity. Gem's compassion in 'The Empath', Kirk sparing the Gorn in 'Arena', and the Horta's misread attack in 'The Devil in the Dark' display nonviolence, deterrence, and corrected perception as alternatives to war.

terrorism-violence.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
terrorism-violence.title: Notes
terrorism-violence.relation: Camosy takes up Randal's charge in Clerks that destroying Death Star II killed innocent independent contractors. Against utilitarian reasoning he deploys just war theory: terrorism is intentionally targeting innocents as a means, so Tarkin's destruction of Alderaan (and, he argues, Hiroshima) qualifies, while the Rebels, who would have been 'pleased' if the workers took the day off, do not. Since the crew was mostly conscripted clones and programmed droids with no moral responsibility, and destroying the station saved billions, the attack passes the proportionality test - an exercise in double-effect reasoning that asks fans to question the 'good guys lens.'

terrorism-violence.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
terrorism-violence.title: 12. Vigilante Wanted
terrorism-violence.relation: Ketcham writes a fictional Dust Bowl kid's 1940 diary: facing bank foreclosure, he weighs which comic to keep as the vigilante who would burn down the bank — Superman, the Kansas farm boy gone Metropolis-insider, or Batman, rich like the bankers yet a fellow avenger who only fights 'carnival freaks'. Testing each against Hamlet's paralysis, Henry V at Agincourt, Tom Joad's 'I'll be ever'where' promise, and a Lex-Luthor pact with the devil, he burns the Batman comics and keeps Superman — realizing he is really giving up his own hate and the preacher's unforgiveness, though even Superman begins to fade 'like dust in that wind'.

terrorism-violence.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
terrorism-violence.title: XVI - WAR AND PEACE, POWER AND FAITH
terrorism-violence.relation: Kirby reads the trilogy through Levinas's distinction between false peace (a cease-fire between parties still opposed) and true peace as love of the unique, inassimilable other. Magneto embodies war: sacrificing Rogue to power his machine, reversing Stryker's Cerebro onto humanity, 'playing by their rules,' and abandoning Mystique, while Xavier embodies Levinasian peace, listening ('I'm looking for hope'), leaving Magneto his choice ('I will always be there, old friend'), and teaching Wolverine and Rogue faith in the goodness of others. Yet Xavier's psychic barriers on Jean, 'the lesser of two evils,' show even the peaceful path risks the ethical compromise Levinas warns the uncritical use of power always invites.

terrorism-violence.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
terrorism-violence.title: Terrorism, Counterterrorism, and “The Story of What Happens Next” in Munich
terrorism-violence.relation: Foy reads Munich's Operation Wrath of God as Spielberg's argument for retribution over vengeance in state counterterrorism. Yvonne's Marcuse/Hegel relativism and the agents' 'think of yourself as a soldier' language-games are dismissed as Avner's psychological breakdown shows morality is objective. Foy deploys Nozick's five procedural differences between retribution and revenge and Kant's view of retribution as impersonal and rational, echoes Socrates in the Crito (retaliation harms one's own soul) via Avner's decay, and cites Aristotle's 'war for the sake of peace' and jus in bello discrimination/proportionality in the Hamshari and Jeanette assassinations.

terrorism-violence.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
terrorism-violence.title: Broadcast Dystopia
terrorism-violence.relation: Foy and Dale read the Bachman dystopias The Running Man and The Long Walk through Hannah Arendt's distinction between power (collective coordination) and violence (coercion by implements), arguing King's states substitute broadcast spectacle for genuine power and so hemorrhage legitimacy the more violence they apply. The gladiatorial Games Network and the Walk pacify the masses while chants of 'KILL HIM' sever the affective bonds of humanity. The chapter invokes Arendt's Eichmann-in-Jerusalem 'banality of evil' to explain the soldiers, Hunters, and cheering citizens as ordinary people uncritically 'doing their jobs,' and reads Ben Richards's suicide flight into the Games Building and Garraty's exhausted walk as futile personal revolts that change nothing.

scientific-realism.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
scientific-realism.title: Smelly Knowledge
scientific-realism.relation: Andrew Aberdein sorts the Buffyverse's science-supernatural encounters into three grades — reduction to present science, reduction to a future science, and the irreducibly supernatural — illustrated by Sunnydale's rationalizers and Giles's inner skeptic in 'Tabula Rasa,' the Initiative's DNA testing of Oz in 'New Moon Rising,' and the show's characteristic 'creepy mix of magic and science' (Jenny Calendar's 'the divine exists in cyberspace'). He reads 'Normal Again' through Descartes's deceiving-demon skepticism, links Spike's chip and Walsh's Adam to the Phineas Gage case (emotion is needed for rational decision), and maps the grades onto the ancients-versus-moderns quarrel and Feyerabend's methodological anarchism. Giles's 'smelly knowledge' speech about books versus computers anticipates a pluralist, socially sensitive epistemology that enriches rather than rejects science.

scientific-realism.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
scientific-realism.title: Wittgenstein Ultimate Bullshit Detector—or Bullshitter
scientific-realism.relation: Fuller argues that mastering a discipline converts critics into loyal insiders — Thomas Kuhn's 'normal science' enshrines the tendency, cognitive dissonance explains it, and Blaise Pascal's wager is the general model of betting on a way of life that makes you receptive to its confirming signs. Against this he sets the Protestant tradition of Luther's conscience, 'playing it by ear', which like the Sophists concedes that reality rarely yields yes-or-no answers — the gap we fill being bullshit — and he frames the dispute as realism versus antirealism, reading Frankfurt's On Bullshit as an ad hominem attack on antirealists. He then re-examines Frankfurt's star witness: Wittgenstein's rebuke of Fania Pascal for saying she felt 'like a dog that has been run over' now looks like a spectacular lack of imagination, since evolutionary psychology, being forged at that very moment, has been narrowing the human-animal mental gap ever since.

scientific-realism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
scientific-realism.title: Doomed to Be Perceived
scientific-realism.relation: Smithka tests Berkeley's 'to be is to be perceived' against two monsters: the Vashta Nerada, whose existence is inferred from indirect evidence (counting shadows, the 'ghosting' of Miss Evangelista) much like Neptune was inferred from Uranus's orbit, and the Weeping Angels, which act only when unperceived and so falsify Berkeley's principle. Working through Locke on substance, Hume's skepticism about unperceivable causes like God, Paley's watchmaker design argument, and scientific realism (Sellars, Churchland) versus van Fraassen's empirically adequate anti-realism, she concludes the Doctor is a realist about unobservables — for whom the Angels are real but 'doomed to be perceived'.

scientific-realism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
scientific-realism.title: Aww, . . . Poor Monster. Should We Feel Sorry for the Carrionites
scientific-realism.relation: Hewitt treats the Carrionites — word-wielding beings of 'The Shakespeare Code' who do science without numbers — as a test of Hartry Field's Science Without Numbers and hence of the Quinean indispensability argument for Platonism about mathematics: if numbers are unavoidable in our best physics, they exist. Surveying Field's Newtonian case, Balaguer's mathematics-free quantum mechanics, and the objections to each, he concludes that even Carrionite physics would not refute numbers — the Carrionites would merely lack our knowledge of them, so the poor monsters are missing out.

scientific-realism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
scientific-realism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
scientific-realism.relation: David Morgan unpacks the chaos theory behind Malcolm's 'I hate being right all the time', starting from Newtonian causal determinism and Laplace's demon, according to which the future is fixed and calculable - then showing that non-linear systems like weather and the park show sensitive dependence (Lorenz's butterfly effect), so even a fully determined universe is unpredictable in practice because we can never know initial conditions exactly. He raises the philosophy-of-science question of whether chaos is a property of nature or only of our computer models, and reads 'life finds a way' as Malcolm extending the same contingency to Darwinian evolution: rewind the tape and you get different species. He ends by noting Malcolm's own paradox - a chaos theorist certain of one specific doom - and settles on chaos theory predicting unpredictability: ignore tiny factors and do not be surprised when they bite you.

scientific-realism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
scientific-realism.title: 17. What if Our Reality Is One Big Hallucination
scientific-realism.relation: Arp starts from Rick's hallucinations of Lori - the disconnected phone in "Hounded," the touch and kiss in "Home" - and Michonne's confessed visions, showing how Rick distinguishes them through coherence with causal law and through third-person verification (Michonne watching him stroke empty air; Morgan's isolation in "Clear" showing why social checks matter). He then widens this into the theory of knowledge: the perceiver-perception-perceived triangle, epistemological and metaphysical realism versus idealism and antirealism, Berkeley's picture of the mind as a movie theater we cannot exit, and the Walking Dead twist on the falling tree in the forest, concluding that even if reality were one big hallucination we would still live - and refuse to walk off cliffs - as realists.

scientific-realism.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
scientific-realism.title: The Basket That Never Was
scientific-realism.relation: Thomas Flint's thought experiment - a conference-championship buzzer-beater waved off because the clock expired, with inconclusive video - asks whether South Shore 'really' scored. He rejects the 'Goofy View' that game facts are referee-independent, since it would entail that only he and his camcorder-owning boss know who won any game ever (imperiling even Michael Jordan's 1982 title and Pistol Pete's scoring record) and would poison a coach's duty to teach rule-following when officials miss traveling. He also rejects the 'Tyranny of the Zebras' that makes officials infallible like the pope, since NCAA replay rules presuppose fallibility, and settles on officials as contest judges who award points: without the verdict no points exist, yet a blown call remains a genuine mistake in failing to apply the rules properly.

scientific-realism.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
scientific-realism.title: Touchdowns, Time, and Truth
scientific-realism.relation: Campbell applies the truthmaker theory and correspondence theory of truth to 'touchdown truths,' using plays like Devin Hester's opening kickoff return in Super Bowl XLI. He distinguishes truthbearers (propositions) from truthmakers (events), separates an agent's 'making it the case' from a truthmaker's 'necessitating,' and uses a tenseless view of semantics plus Perry's being-true/being-made-true distinction to defuse fatalism. He then argues that since only the final score fixes 'real' touchdowns, their truthmakers are events involving referees' beliefs, endorsing a Modest Touchdown Antirealism while retaining bivalence and semantic realism.

scientific-realism.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
scientific-realism.title: Feel the Big MO'
scientific-realism.relation: Letson asks whether momentum in football is a real explanatory phenomenon, opening with the Bills' 1993 comeback over the Oilers. He notes momentum is invoked only for success and only for one team at a time, and struggles to separate it from the mere evidence of playing well, comparing it to 'talent.' Surveying psychological models (Taylor and Demick's momentum chain) and David Romer's fourth-down analysis denying momentum, he argues that even if a small momentum effect exists, its size relative to chance means appeals to it in any particular game are usually unjustified—like blaming one heart attack on smoking.

scientific-realism.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
scientific-realism.title: Cronenberg as Scientist Antiessentialism, Sex as Remixing, and the View from Nowhere
