scientific-realism.relation: Peter Ludlow argues Cronenberg's true horror is scientific antiessentialism: The Fly, Shivers, Videodrome, and eXistenZ collapse the supposedly essential boundaries between human and fly, organic and mechanical, real and virtual, sane and mad, good and evil. Drawing on Quine's rejection of essence, Kripke's empirical essentialism, and Darwinian biology, he reads Brundle's fusion and Renn's VCR-stomach as showing we have no essence; sex is 'remixing' of information to lock out parasites, and Cronenberg narrates from Nagel's impersonal 'view from nowhere' where humans are not special.

scientific-realism.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
scientific-realism.title: The Fiction of Truth in Fiction Some Reflections on Semantics and eXistenZ
scientific-realism.relation: Graham Stevens uses eXistenZ to attack David Lewis's possible-world semantics for truth in fiction. Lewis analyzes 'according to the fiction f, p' as truth in the world(s) where the story is told as known fact; but eXistenZ's nested game-within-a-game ending, where even the characters cannot tell whether 'we are still in the game,' deliberately has no determinate world in which its events are fact. Stevens concludes fictions need not correspond to complete determinate worlds and proposes a stringent view: nothing is true in a fiction unless the fiction explicitly asserts it.

scientific-realism.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
scientific-realism.title: Eliminating the Impossible Sherlock Holmes and the Supernatural
scientific-realism.relation: Blanchette uses the Guy Ritchie film's Lord Blackwood 'resurrection' and 'The Hound of the Baskervilles' to ask whether a supernatural explanation is ever admissible. Drawing on Draper's definition of nature vs. the supernatural, Plantinga's natural-vs-logical necessity distinction, and Hume on miracles, he argues miracles are naturally impossible but not logically impossible unless nature is proven a closed system. He defends a truth-aimed methodology (pursue natural causes until the best explanation of failure is that none exists), showing Holmes rightly debunks both cases while thought experiments reveal conditions under which a supernatural verdict would become the rational inference.

scientific-realism.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
scientific-realism.title: 03_LaRocca_Chapter_002.html
scientific-realism.relation: Carroll offers a critical reconstruction of Andre Bazin's film theory, separating Bazin's lasting achievement as a historian of film style from his dubious metaphysical commitments. He shows how Bazin championed 'spatial realism'—deep-focus, long-take sequence shots as in Renoir's Rules of the Game and Welles's Citizen Kane—against Soviet and Hollywood montage, on the grounds that unedited homogeneous space imparts authenticity, grants the spectator freedom to discover meaning, and preserves the ambiguity of reality. Carroll treats Bazin's claim that recording realism is cinema's essential destiny as an anti-realist target to be demythologized, defending the study of film-realist style while rejecting the essentialist evolutionary scheme underneath it.

scientific-realism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
scientific-realism.title: Doomed to Be Perceived
scientific-realism.relation: Paula Smithka uses the Vashta Nerada and Weeping Angels to examine perception and the reality of unobservables. She sets Berkeley's "to be is to be perceived" against Locke's hidden substance and Hume's empiricist skepticism (and Paley's design argument), then distinguishes direct from indirect perceptual evidence, using the shadows, skeletal remains, and Neptune's discovery to frame scientific realism versus van Fraassen's antirealism. The Weeping Angels invert Berkeley, existing only when unperceived and turning to stone when observed, so for them to be is NOT to be perceived.

scientific-realism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
scientific-realism.title: Aww, . . . Poor Monster. Should We Feel Sorry for the Carrionites
scientific-realism.relation: Simon Hewitt uses the Carrionites, who wield words instead of numbers, to ask whether science can be done without mathematics, a question in the philosophy of mathematics about mathematical Platonism (numbers existing outside space and time). He lays out the Quinean indispensability argument, then reviews Hartry Field's number-free Newtonian gravity and Mark Balaguer's attempt on Quantum Mechanics as "Carrionite physics," noting both fall short. He closes arguing that even if numbers were dispensable for science, our knowledge of mathematical truths still suggests numbers exist.

scientific-realism.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
scientific-realism.title: 16. Better Call Saul Because Chuck’s Condition Is Real
scientific-realism.relation: The chapter treats Chuck McGill's electromagnetic hypersensitivity as a case study in the metaphysics and phenomenology of medicine, asking whether an unmeasurable condition is 'real.' It contrasts a realist demand for a biomarker with an anti-realist, phenomenological stance that privileges Chuck's first-person lived experience, and blames Cartesian mind-body dualism for medicine's split between neurology and psychiatry that leaves Chuck uncared for. Reading his blackouts, space blanket, and nocebo-driven coma as psychosomatic, it argues that stigmatizing 'crazy' media portrayals of Chuck worsened his isolation and that a whole-person, first-person-narrative approach was needed.

scientific-realism.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
scientific-realism.title: 14. Beyond Loyalty and Disloyalty
scientific-realism.relation: Bartolo Alegre uses Seldon's trial claim that 'scientific truth is beyond loyalty and disloyalty' to ask whether even formal sciences like logic can be biased. Against Bogdanov's and Lenin's Marxist idea of a 'proletarian logic,' he shows that logical principles (non-contradiction, explosion) have been revised by paraconsistent logicians on purely mathematical grounds, using Hardin's symbolic-logic decoding of the Anacreon message and Orwell's doublethink as illustrations. Drawing on Popper's rejection of uninformative contradictions, Kuhn's sociological account of scientific change, and Lakatos's rational reconstruction, he argues science transcends individual scientists' loyalties only through a diverse, competing community of experts, as when Hummin's loyalty to humanity pushed Seldon to make psychohistory practical.

scientific-realism.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
scientific-realism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
scientific-realism.relation: Pigliucci uses the 'Evolution, Schmevolution' series and the Dover trial to argue that intelligent design is not science because it is unfalsifiable and invokes supernatural causation. He cites Popper's falsificationism (and Popper's recantation about Darwinism), contrasts Descartes's rationalism with Hume's empiricism to characterize science as a tentative blend of the two, flags Feyerabend's 'anything goes' as an irrational view of knowledge, invokes Aristotle's eudaimonia to argue meaning in life is a personal work in progress, and turns Dembski's theistic-evolution concession into a Pyrrhic victory via the problem of evil ('argument from bad design').

scientific-realism.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
scientific-realism.title: 16. The Pleasure of the Twist
scientific-realism.relation: Scales argues that Twilight Zone twist endings mirror Kuhn's account of scientific revolutions: seeded anomalies accumulate until a 'paradigm shift' makes us reinterpret everything, as in 'To Serve Man' ('It's a cookbook!'), 'The Lateness of the Hour,' and 'The Hitch-Hiker.' He ties Kuhn's theory-ladenness of observation (the anomalous playing-card experiment) to Paul Churchland's connectionist, prototype-based bottom-up neurophilosophy, concluding the pleasure of the twist is the dopamine reward for deploying a new prototype—the same jolt we get from a joke or a genuine insight.

scientific-realism.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
scientific-realism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
scientific-realism.relation: Graziano rejects the 'orthodox view' that a climbing grade like Serenity Crack's 5.10d is subjective (beauty in the eye of the beholder) and argues for realism about grades. Using Locke's primary/secondary quality distinction and his dispositional account of hardness, he defends 'relationalism': a grade is a real disposition of the rock to challenge a standard climber in standard conditions, just as hardness is a real disposition. He supports this with Pinched Rib changing from 5.7 to 5.10b when a hold broke, and argues the orthodox view confuses what a grade IS with how we determine it, rejecting even the 'weakly objective' money analogy.

scientific-realism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
scientific-realism.title: 78. The Witness as Philosophy How Knowledge Is Constructed
scientific-realism.relation: Cuddy asks what epistemology Blow built into The Witness's frustrating puzzles and its windmill videos (Burke, Feynman, Moriarty, Spira, Gangaji). He rejects the sophistic/Protagorean 'knowledge depends on the observer' reading (most puzzles have objective, inductive-and-deductive solutions, e.g. the yellow-glass bunker) and the strict scientific realism of the Burke video defended by Putnam's no-miracles argument. Using Plato's cave and the aporia of Socrates' Meno (the puzzle's 'ah-ha' epiphanies), and Kuhn's incommensurable paradigm shifts (the game's 'hard left turns' forcing players to overhaul their understanding), he concludes the game argues that true knowledge is attainable, individually and collectively, though reached by a nonlinear, paradigm-shifting route rather than pure realism or relativism.

pragmatism.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
pragmatism.title: Pals
pragmatism.relation: Madeline Muntersbjorn uses Season Four's Initiative-versus-Scoobies conflict to dissolve the Science Wars: Professor Walsh's secret, unfalsifiable Project 314 makes her Karl Popper's bad scientist, while Buffy's gang embodies Feyerabend's pluralism and Peirce-and-James pragmatism — Buffyverse rules are probabilistic rather than deterministic, and the gang welcomes anyone willing to ask questions and do research. Her three ideals — pluralism, pragmatism, pals — culminate in 'Primeval,' where the combo-Buffy enjoining spell (Willow's spirit, Xander's heart, Giles's mind, Buffy's hand) literally enacts James's meliorism: the world may be saved if each agent does their level best, together. Walsh dies alone because she has no pals; Buffy saves the world 'a lot' because she does.

pragmatism.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
pragmatism.title: “A New Hope”
pragmatism.relation: Long stages William Clifford's ethics of belief against William James's will to believe, with Luke Skywalker as James's exemplar. Clifford's shipowner story condemns faith as 'wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone,' which would convict Luke of immorality when he switches off his targeting computer and trusts the Force; James replies that where a choice is intellectually undecidable and a genuine option - live, forced, and momentous, like Luke's turn to the Jedi life or Obi-Wan's response to Leia's hologram - pragmatic faith is justified and even salvific. Faith can create truths: Han flying into the asteroid field, Luke's unjustified belief that there is good in Vader bringing Anakin back, the author's faith in his students, and Martin Luther King Jr.'s dream - all illustrating 'a new hope.'

pragmatism.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
pragmatism.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Auxier, an Atkins dieter, argues the diet works for the reason Dewey gives in Human Nature and Conduct: habits built in calm moments are the bulwark against desire in crisis, and Atkins succeeds by reshaping which gratifications are habitually available — 'a steak for the black eye of desire.' He then transfers Atkins's physiology to thinking: television and advertising serve 'conceptual carbs,' packaged bundles of doubt, emotion, and readiness to act that bypass inquiry and leave the public 'intellectually diabetic' and ideological. Peirce's pragmatic maxim is translated into an eight-step mental exercise (worked through a parent's tattoo-or-piercing doubt about a teenage daughter), while Descartes's hyperbolic doubt is discarded in favor of pragmatism's 'genuine doubt.'

pragmatism.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
pragmatism.title: (Positive) Violence of Self-Discipline
pragmatism.relation: Shusterman opens with Plato and Socrates' ancient quarrel against poetry - banning the artists from the Republic, much as rap is demonized today - and rejects Aristotle's catharsis strategy of quarantining art from life, applying pragmatist aesthetics (Dewey, James, and the Du Bois-Alain Locke lineage) to argue that rap's aesthetic violence of beat, scratch, and "Bring the Noise" is life-enhancing force, with reality rap's metaphysics of mix and flow against Plato's changeless Forms. Reading KRS-One's "Stop the Violence" movement born from Scott LaRock's killing, Guru's "Choice of Weapons" (a mic or a gun), and Jeru the Damaja's command to "kill in thyself", he concludes rap overcomes bad violence not by abolishing violence but by channeling it into lyrical battle and the positive violence of self-discipline.

pragmatism.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
pragmatism.title: U2 and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Soper tracks Bono's public identity work across three paradigms: pre-modern Irish-Catholic inheritance, including a Du Boisian 'double consciousness' of the colonized Irish; the modernist artist-as-visionary, where Nietzsche, Freud and Marx destabilize the self and the Shalom fellowship nearly ends the band; and the postmodern masks of the Fly, Mirrorball Man and MacPhisto on the Zoo TV media collage, read via Lacan for 'Mofo' and via Baudrillard's simulacra for the 'Even Better than the Real Thing' video with its wax Beatles and cyber-sex imagery. Lyotardian skepticism toward grand ideologies explains the band's refusal of fanaticism in 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and 'Two Hearts Beat as One'. Soper concludes that Bono fuses all three into a 'Postmodern Christian Pragmatism' that keeps Christian conviction and debt-relief activism while adopting postmodern playfulness without collapsing into ironic detachment.

pragmatism.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
pragmatism.title: James Bond and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Abrams explains Peirce's three modes of inference (deduction proves, induction shows, abduction merely suggests) and reconstructs, abduction by abduction, Bond's rapid chain of guesses in The World Is Not Enough: from the odd smell and foam on his fingers to the urea-coated fertilizer bomb he unknowingly delivered, the shared motto 'there's no point living if you can't feel alive' exposing Elektra's alliance with Renard, and her guilty subject-changing. He also covers the negative art: Bond plants false clues with Q's gadgets (the fingerprint re-printer, the cloaked Vanquish) while villains like Carver recode reality by sinking the Devonshire to frame the Chinese, and both sides try to force each other into false abductions. Bond wins because his mind is more playful - Peirce's 'musement', Eco's creative abduction, and an encyclopedic education - making 007 the superior player in what is ultimately a game of chance and strategy.

pragmatism.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
pragmatism.title: Tough and Tender, The Dead Keep Truckin’
pragmatism.relation: Gary Ciocco traces a line from Emerson and James through Kerouac, Ginsberg, and Neal Cassady to the Grateful Dead: Emerson's nonconformist 'infinitude of man' and James's 'live options' and religious appetite for being 'more fully alive' become, in the Beats, the project of living life itself as art ('the only people for me are the mad ones'). He argues the Beats splintered because each chased an atomistic, individual epiphany — Kerouac swinging wholesale from tender- to tough-minded temperament — while the Dead turned the same Jamesian hunger into a shared communal religious experience, a 'kindler, gentler' scene that better achieves Aristotle's eudaimonia. Cassady, muse of On the Road and driver of the Pranksters' bus, literally connects the two movements, but the Dead's unity-in-diversity made them the evolution, not the echo, of the Beats.

pragmatism.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
pragmatism.title: “You Rationalize” Jackie Brown’s Pragmatism
pragmatism.relation: K. Silem Mohammad argues Jackie Brown is a study in aporia and Wittgensteinian aspect perception: Ray Nicolette's purple/white bag paralysis, Ordell's 'Is that Rutger Hauer?' mistake, Jackie on the LAX moving walkway, and 'Across 110th Street' turning diegetic all force a re-description of experience within particular language games. The thrice-repeated Del Amo money switch-off adds no information but displays the characters' differing aspects of one event. Against Ordell's mind-fucking 'logical chains', Jackie's 'that's what you do to go through with the shit you start, you rationalize' embodies a pragmatist view of reason as context-bound use, matched by Max's calmly uncertain 'I think I do. Good enough?'

pragmatism.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
pragmatism.title: And the Good News Second
pragmatism.relation: Auxier tests Cornel West's four marks of prophetic thinking — discernment of who bears the social cost ('Ghost of Tom Joad,' 'Born in the U.S.A.'), empathy as human connection, self-critical tracking of hypocrisy, and audacious hope (the E Street concert as galvanizing the world-weary) — and finds Springsteen nearly unmatched, yet something is missing from reading 'The Rising' as prophecy. He stages the pragmatist debate between Rorty's poetic pragmatism (poets create the vocabularies democracy lives by), West's prophetic pragmatism, and Putnam's sober reasonableness, then uses Abraham Joshua Heschel to distinguish poet from prophet: inspiration versus revelation, gratitude versus dread, the seduction-and-coercion of the call he comically retells as Jonah in Asbury Park. A true prophet would sing, with Isaiah and Jeremiah, that even the 9/11 hijackers were the rod of America's own God against its greed — so Springsteen's 'The Rising' is lamentation, not prophecy.

pragmatism.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
pragmatism.title: Back from the Edge
pragmatism.relation: McKenna and Pratt use McDermott's 'Promethean self' and meliorism to answer the riddle of Nebraska's closer 'Reason to Believe': among the dead dog, the deserted bride and the groom left at the altar, 'still at the end of every hard earned day people find some reason to believe.' They trace Springsteen's shift from escape songs ('Born to Run,' 'Thunder Road') to life at the edge ('Badlands,' 'Darkness on the Edge of Town,' and the two midnight drivers of 'State Trooper' and 'Open All Night'), arguing meaning is made by cutting and connecting relations at the margins. Belief without evidence of salvation is legitimate hope but illegitimate certainty; the reason to believe is Jamesian meliorism — making things 'not perfect, simply better.'

pragmatism.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
pragmatism.title: Hometown Security
pragmatism.relation: Keith reads 'My Hometown' — whitewashed windows, the textile mill closing, Bruce telling his son 'take a good look around' — through Putnam's Bowling Alone, Dewey's socially constituted self, and Mead, to argue that Bruce and Kate should recommit to their dying town rather than flee in the moving van. Leopold's 'two spiritual dangers in not owning a farm' and Berry's healthy community as ecosystem ground an 'enlightened localism' that avoids both the town's racist parochialism and rootless cosmopolitanism. Volunteering, local food, and town-meeting democracy are the hometown security the song's sadness calls for.

pragmatism.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
pragmatism.title: Finding Our Way
pragmatism.relation: Trudy Milburn applies Dewey's account of habit, impulse and inquiry to navigation in the series: Adama's 'I know the way to Earth' declaration starts an inquiry whose end-in-view is continuously reformulated as humans creatively combine scriptures, pulsars and constellations as signs. Roslin uses scripture at face value and other people's belief in it, which on Dewey's anti-foundationalist terms is legitimate map-making rather than piety. The Cylons, by contrast, treat their plan as God-given, cannot reinterpret signs for themselves (needing Baltar to locate Earth) and fall back on inherited habit, which is why, on Dewey's view, they are the ones who are lost.

pragmatism.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
pragmatism.title: Progress Is a Myth that Truly Makes Life Worthwhile
pragmatism.relation: Garnar contrasts the material practice of collecting CDs -- shelving some 1,500-2,000 discs by genre, the Rachels' Egon Schiele packaging, and Humean associations binding particular discs to memories like buying blue hair dye the day he got New Order's Lowlife -- with the iPod-era 'iPhenomenon' of buying songs piecemeal from iTunes. Using William James's question 'How is the practice real?' he rejects the real/virtual split, and reads the freedom of iMedia as a corollary of Marx and Engels's 'single, unconscionable freedom -- Free Trade': the solipsistic consumer never confronts the artist the way the album as artifact (Coltrane's My Favorite Things ending, he realizes, had to end with 'But Not for Me') forces him to. The body supposedly made unnecessary by 'iLiving' remains, with Foucault, a site of discipline -- eating disorders, outsourced assembly labor, e-waste -- so he keeps his iPod but defends a plurality of media and calls progress a myth.

pragmatism.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
pragmatism.title: iPublic
pragmatism.relation: Dewey takes the iPod's beauty seriously (Chris Breen's 'beautiful and intuitive' player, Donald Norman's user-centered design) and uses John Dewey's Art as Experience to ask whether iPod use can be a 'consummatory' experience that ends with us no longer the same person — hearing a bitter song as insight into the social conditions that produced it — rather than the contrived 'now' of fashion and hyper-accumulation, per Benjamin's remark that there is 'always a sense of the same in the new'. Mass production flattened the aristocratic high-culture/folk division and handed the power to define 'cool' to advertisers and the market. The pragmatist test is political: with iTunes DRM and single-user design quietly individualizing consumption (the ritual of buying the Public Enemy tape at the mall versus the frictionless one-click download), the iPod is beautiful exactly insofar as its experiences help form a public — an inclusive, participatory democratic community.

pragmatism.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
pragmatism.title: Wait, Did I Hit Pause Where’d the Remote Get to . .
pragmatism.relation: Seng takes up the fan phenomenon of syncing The Wizard of Oz with Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon and tests the three explanations fans offer: authorial intent (rejected on Pink Floyd's own repeated denials), Jungian synchronicity (rejected as needlessly complex, with the L. Frank Baum coat worn by Frank Morgan as the test case), and pure fluke. He argues the symmetries (the cash-register intro of 'Money' as Dorothy enters Technicolor, 'The Great Gig in the Sky' over the cyclone) are neither objective nor mind-created reality, but meanings made by a third factor in the experience: the viewer whose perceptual habits, in Dewey's and Louise Rosenblatt's sense, supply interpretations like reading the color-splash as prosperity or as the cost of Dorothy's lost innocence. Dorothy's own longing for home becomes the emblem of how habit, not reasoning, governs what we perceive and like.

pragmatism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
pragmatism.title: Jimmy Buffett, Cultural Infidel
pragmatism.relation: The editors argue Buffett is a philosopher despite his own denials, in the sense of Royce and Dewey: philosophy is critical reflection on living that returns to ordinary experience, and Buffett's songs, books, and concerts pass Dewey's test of rendering everyday predicaments 'more significant, more luminous, more fruitful.' They compare 'Margaritaville' to Plato's Republic — not equal in pedigree but equal in kind as occasions for philosophical practice — to defend meaning-making as a democratic practice open to Parrotheads, not just professors. Reading the album 'Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes' as a guide, they set Buffett's 'Porpoise Driven Life,' where purpose is found by sailing your own waters in the company of friends, against Rick Warren's revelation-based 'Purpose Driven Life.'

pragmatism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
pragmatism.title: “Trip Around the Sun”
pragmatism.relation: Phil Oliver pairs Buffett with William James: both hold that philosophy is 'not a technical matter' but each person's sense of what life deeply means, had in non-verbal moments of elevation as much as argued in words. The chapter's core is James's 'moral holiday' — a morally legitimate respite from care and struggle — naturalized in Buffett's 'License to Chill' and 'Trip Around the Sun' ('it's good to know it's out of my control'), joined by James's lightness about error from 'The Will to Believe' and Russell's and Dawkins's responses to cosmic annihilation. Against those who hear mere hedonism, Oliver insists Jamesian holidays are care-free but never care-less: like Thoreau's 'live deliberately' echoed in 'Growing Older But Not Up,' they renew us for the return to work, and James's ambivalence about alcohol in The Varieties of Religious Experience mirrors the risk of Buffett's frozen concoctions.

pragmatism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
pragmatism.title: “Happily Ever After, Now and Then”
pragmatism.relation: Erin McKenna explains how a feminist can love Buffett by reading 'Fins' and 'Why Don't We Get Drunk (and Screw)' as critiques of predatory land sharks rather than endorsements, and 'Margaritaville' as a man admitting 'it's my own damn fault.' Against Rousseau's pliable helpmate ideal of woman she sets Wollstonecraft's Vindication — equal education and personhood for women — and Charlotte Perkins Gilman's pragmatist-feminist case that women's economic, physical, and mental dependence stunts everyone. Buffett's novels then pass the Gilman test: Desdemona, Trevor Kane, Cleopatra Highbourne, and Sophie are smart, independent women, and the male leads must reform their habits to earn them, aiming at Desdemona's 'happily ever after, now and then' instead of the fairy-tale ending.

pragmatism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
pragmatism.title: Wonder Why We Ever Go Home
pragmatism.relation: Duke Richey maps Buffett's West — 'Ringling, Ringling,' the Rancho Deluxe soundtrack, Tully Mars — onto Josiah Royce's philosophy of community: only people who root in a place, face its history ('wise provincialism'), and sacrifice selfish desires for the whole can build Beloved Communities, a lesson enacted when cattle rustlers Jack and Cecil accept community sanction and find belonging working the Rancho Deluxe. Wallace Stegner's coral-reef metaphor from Angle of Repose supplies the image of communities built up millimeter by millimeter yet still vulnerable to pollution and over-fishing, with Royce's environmental regret (covering 'the wounds' of the landscape with gardens) anticipating the chapter's sustainability ethic. 'Wonder Why We Ever Go Home' thus asks what we really seek when we seek grace through community: not the nomadic Pickup Truck Death of every-man-for-himself, but cooperation that makes a society to match the scenery.

pragmatism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
pragmatism.title: “Where Did All the Good Songs Go ”
pragmatism.relation: Scott Pratt answers whether 'Margaritaville' is art by rejecting object-based theories (Kivy's score-compliance, the abstract perfect performance, the unrecorded instance that vanishes) for Dewey's Art as Experience: art is 'an experience,' complete and self-sufficient, followed by a reflective, evaluative second phase. He reads 'Makin' Music for the Money' as moving from solitary self-interested music-making to a community of musicians, and the Port of Spain steel-drum rehearsal of 'King of Somewhere Hot' that carried forward into the Miami concert as Dewey's two phases in action. Buffett's fly-fishing stories — the lost blue marlin that became 'a story,' the released Long Island bass that 'replenished his saline psyche' — supply Haeckel's ecological model in which music, like fishing, is an organism-environment interaction, making songs 'homemade' eco-music that belongs to listeners in its own ecosystem.

pragmatism.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
pragmatism.title: L2Design, n00b Knowledge As Design
pragmatism.relation: Sean Duncan follows a Rogue-class forum thread — Dismalstrike's detailed redesign proposals, debated by other players and acknowledged by a rare Blizzard 'blue post' — to argue that everyday players act as informal designers co-constructing knowledge about the game. Drawing on Donald Schön's reflection-in-action, itself rooted in the pragmatism of Dewey, James, and Peirce, he rejects the idea that rational facts come first and practice second: knowing how to fix the Rogue class is built through playing, posting, iterating, and revising. Knowledge construction is design, and the stakes extend beyond gaming to how literacy, learning, and civic participation should be understood in a world where play and work blur.

pragmatism.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
pragmatism.title: Beyond Picasso and Ronaldo Living Artfully
pragmatism.relation: Elcombe asks whether Cristiano Ronaldo, transferred to Real Madrid for $131 million—more than Picasso's Garçon à la Pipe fetched at its record 2004 auction—can be an artist like Picasso. Traditional metaphysics built on Plato's perfect Forms and Aristotle's necessary-and-sufficient conditions locks Art in a special museum realm that soccer, as a purposive sport whose beauty is only a byproduct, can never enter, leaving the game merely 'beautiful', not Art. Dewey's Art as Experience reorients the question from what art is to what art does: artworks are consummations of experience, moments of 'thatness'—that meal, that storm, that Ronaldo free kick—that lift us out of the mundane while remaining within the game's durable rules and history (Ronaldo's artistry grows from Zidane, Maradona, Cruyff, Pelé). On this pragmatist view Ronaldo is an artist in the act, the six-year-old testing a new turn on the pitch lives artfully too, and soccer's artistry becomes groundwork for communication, democracy, and the good life—doing more real work than a painting almost no one ever sees.

pragmatism.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
pragmatism.title: The Jihadist Way of Life
pragmatism.relation: Argues the Fremen are 'shockingly American': their Spannungsbogen self-discipline, spiritual self-sufficiency, and endurance of hardship exemplify Emerson's self-reliance, while the jihad's aim of razing the rule of the Great Houses into relations of equals echoes Dewey's democracy as a way of life—faith in the potentialities of every human nature. The parallel runs through the 'American Taliban' John Walker Lindh and Paul's blind walk into the desert, both acting on values Americans prize. Herbert's remark that people surrender judgment to leaders 'wrapped in the myth fabric of society' grounds the pragmatist point that Fremen myth-making, like America's exceptionalist self-image, works—and Alia's 'my brother is pragmatic' seals it.

pragmatism.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
pragmatism.title: Keith Richards the Prophet
pragmatism.relation: The arrest becomes legal philosophy: since statutes like 'reckless driving' are general while conduct is specific, law requires the art of judgment. Against John Austin's positivism (law as the sovereign's command backed by sanction), it adopts Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.'s 'bad man' view — law is just the prediction of what courts will in fact do — making Richards a 'prophet' of consequences, as when the band declined to raise a giant inflatable phallus in San Antonio. It closes with pragmatist accounts, Holmes's law as the 'external deposit' of our moral life and Dewey's law rooted in custom and judicial behavior, explaining why the South's history of racism and sexual anxiety seeped into Arkansas law.

pragmatism.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
pragmatism.title: Judge Richards Presides
pragmatism.relation: The farcical Fordyce proceeding — a golf-drunk judge sipping bourbon hidden in his sock, a BBC interview mid-trial, and Richards himself pounding the gavel at the press conference ('Case closed') — confirms for the author that Holmes was right: law is prediction all the way down, at every level from the bad man to the judge. It concludes that the 'devil' of rock was a projection of white southern fear and repressed libido, externally deposited in law yet too indeterminate to predict, as the Stones' motorcade escape at 2 a.m. showed.

pragmatism.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
pragmatism.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Brooks argues Klosterman is an unacknowledged heir of McLuhan's media ecology: his Fargo Rock City account of hair metal's rise through FM radio, metal magazines, and MTV's 'collective unconscious,' Britney Spears as a low-definition 'cool medium' everyone rebrands, and the 'singular club scene' as global village all do media-ecology work. But Brooks docks him fifteen percent for clinging to an authenticity fantasy — the Unabomber-essay claim that technology makes us 'never been less human' — which McLuhan's dictum that 'there is absolutely no inevitability as long as there is a willingness to contemplate what is happening' refutes. In Rorty's spirit of persuading by joshing rather than arguing, he challenges Klosterman to drop the ontology and turn his interpretive powers on real problems like compassion fatigue and Darfur.

pragmatism.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
pragmatism.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Vannatta reads Klosterman's born-again pop culture — the Left Behind novels, Victory TV's Steven, Kurt Warner's Super Bowl, Jesus Camp — as living Puritan Calvinism: original sin (Klosterman's cruel third-graders), justification by faith alone, unmediated access to God ('every man was his own priest'), and predestination that leaves uncertain whether our actions matter in the divine equation. The chapter's pivot is truth versus peace: Puritan-born-again certainty sacrifices peace for antecedent truth, from the 1675 Massachusetts settlements to Robertson and Falwell on 9/11. Against this Vannatta sets the pragmatist alternative — truth as the outcome of communal inquiry in service of peaceful living — recasting God as the web of relationships and dissolving his own childhood camp's contradiction between 'I'm Third' and its cult of competition.

pragmatism.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
pragmatism.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Ray Bossert reads American Gods as an allegory of American philosophy: like Gaiman's gods, American philosophers labor invisibly in the background while European publics canonize their thinkers, and Shadow's prison exchanges show the point, since Loki must beg him to read Herodotus ('It's cool') while Johnnie Larch's 'don't piss off people who work in airports' beats Shadow's abstract generalization in usefulness. Following Hickman's Deweyan instrumentalism, he argues the gods are survival tools humans craft from need and discard when obsolete, so Czernobog's hammer gives way to Media's television, Wednesday treats even his own son as an instrument, and the buffalo man's 'believe everything' is advice about keeping one's tools of survival working. The chapter ends on liberty: Shadow refuses to be a god because 'we don't need anyone to believe in us,' and in the Egyptian death trial he claims the most American reward, the freedom to choose his own afterlife.

pragmatism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
pragmatism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Eugene Halton retells human history as the fable of Peirce's 'degenerate monkey': a neotenous, instinct-weak blunderer (Homo errans) whose gift for abductive guessing and attunement to the intelligence of the wild was inverted by agriculture and civilization into Narcissistic self-mirroring, anthropocentric religion, and the worship of the machine. The telepathic, rubber-masked mutants of Beneath the Planet of the Apes who worship the Alpha-Omega bomb ('I reveal my Inmost Self unto my God!') become a prophecy of our own screen-mediated, empathy-poor life, from Facebook to Botox, in Huxley's pleasure-conditioning rather than Orwell's pain. Against this, the chapter holds up Armando's Franciscan empathy for Caesar and the hope of a 'planet of the regenerate monkeys' re-attuned to the community of wild life.

pragmatism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
pragmatism.title: Psych and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Amanda Lusky argues Shawn is a model pragmatist in the lineage of Peirce, James, and Dewey: he treats ideas as tools judged by consequences, is tough-minded about facts over theory (James's temperament distinction), and applies the pragmatic maxim from the squirrel-and-tree dispute to his loosely formed but working hunches. His co-operative inquiry with Gus and the SBPD - Gus's safe-cracking knowledge in 'Sixty Five Million Years Off,' passing Lassiter's polygraph in 'Shawn Rescues Darth Vader' - enacts Dewey's democratic community solving problems together, and the chapter reads his tolerance of Gus's paranormal leads ('The Devil's in the Details') as pragmatic openness that enriches Santa Barbara's democratic life.

pragmatism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
pragmatism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: The chapter compares Barney's 'True story' pronouncements with William James's pragmatism, using James's squirrel anecdote and the 'Zoo or False' monkey-mugging to ask when an evidentially undecidable dispute becomes a live practical question. Like James's pragmatic cases for free will and religious comfort, Barney's monkey story and the twenty-eight-year-old 'with some sun damage' are beliefs made true by their practical (mostly entertainment) value, then replaced like outdated theories when new evidence arrives, as James's consistency requirement demands. The divergence: the Barney Stinson (BS) theory of truth is self-serving, engineering unverifiable stories others cannot disprove, while James weighs what works for everyone's experience.

pragmatism.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
pragmatism.title: Justified and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: The chapter asks whether Boyd's survival of Raylan's bullet in the premiere was a genuine sign from God: the atheist invokes Ockham's Razor and the promise of a naturalistic explanation, while the theist replies that a world-creating God would act through the laws of nature, making such explanations neutral rather than negative evidence. It then applies William James's pragmatist standard from his study of mystical experience - judge the sign by the fruits of the Spirit (Galatians' love, joy, peace, self-control) it bears - to Boyd's prison ministry, his urging Raylan to forgive Arlo, and his meth-lab crusade. Despite Boyd's eventual apostasy after Bo murders his congregation, the author concludes he passes James's test, since faith is a maintained journey that can be lost, and the born-again Boyd still struggles - like Jacob becoming Israel - rather than scheming coldly.

pragmatism.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
pragmatism.title: 16. My Name Is—Hang on, What Was It Meant to Be Again Are You Sure Well, Okay Then . .
pragmatism.relation: Tim Jones argues the book is not really a love story but a warning about identity: against Descartes's transcendent self, the American pragmatists William James, Cooley, and Mead hold that the self is fluid and socially constituted, and Westley's serial reinvention (farm boy, Dread Pirate Roberts, Man in Black) - along with Mandy Patinkin's cathartic channeling of his father's death into Inigo - shows the freedom this mutability grants. The Goldman frame then exposes the danger: the fictionalized Goldman seizes Morgenstern's text, cuts its history, and rewrites it to his own ends, exactly as other people can seize our plastic identities and shape them for their interests rather than ours.

pragmatism.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
pragmatism.title: 7. What Kind of Revolutionary Is Mr. Robot
pragmatism.relation: Ralston traces Mr. Robot's hacktivist philosophy to David Graeber's anarchism behind Occupy Wall Street and to Anonymous's 'moralfags' who hack for a higher cause (Project Chanology as the template for fsociety), then stages the Dewey-Trotsky debate on means and ends: Trotsky's 'Their Morals and Ours' lets the end justify any means, while Dewey's means-end continuum demands experimental, democratic means suited to the end. The verdict: Mr. Robot's ends are anarchist and his means pragmatist - he will frame Terry Colby and risk lives at Steel Mountain, but rejects means like actual slavery that would betray the movement's own ideal of liberation.

pragmatism.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
pragmatism.title: 10. Play in the Real World
pragmatism.relation: Elizabeth Cooke reads Rogers's double movement, demystifying reality (the studio reveal in episode 1530, the otoscope that cannot see into minds) while insisting 'anything is possible in make-believe,' as pragmatist epistemology: rejecting Plato's two worlds and Cartesian doubt, Rogers agrees with Peirce's open-ended 'musement,' Santayana's play as a 'holiday' revealing truer selves, and James's malleable world that our creativity 'adds to.' Pretend, as when Daniel wonders if he is a mistake or children take others' perspectives in competition episodes, is how children actively learn what is most real, with George Herbert Mead explaining how perspective-taking builds the self.

pragmatism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
pragmatism.title: Hope for the Future
pragmatism.relation: Applies Dewey's The Public and Its Problems to Alien and Aliens: the real villain is not the Xenomorph but a United Americas too weak to govern Weyland-Yutani, whose crude cost-benefit erasure of the Nostromo crew's interests shows a state that has lost the public's voice. Ash's arrogant 'perfect organism' objectivity, the appeal to blameworthy 'human nature,' and faith that big business runs everything illustrate Dewey's targets - Plato's static Forms, economic determinism, and rugged individualism - and since beliefs are habits of action (Peirce), the Company's deeds expose its professed principles as negligible fictions.

pragmatism.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
pragmatism.title: Finding Our Way
pragmatism.relation: Milburn uses Dewey's account of habit, impulse, and inquiry to explain how the humans navigate: Adama's blocked plans (the decommissioning) are reoriented into a new 'end-in-view' (Earth), and the fleet continuously reformulates its route from scriptures, star charts, pulsars, and the Tomb of Athena constellations as interchangeable signs. The Cylons by contrast cannot revise - Boomer's peace initiative gets her model boxed, and even Cavil's admissions of error lead back to the same path - because they locate their plan in God rather than in constructed, revisable inquiry, needing Baltar even to interpret the signs to Earth. On Deweyan grounds the chapter concludes the humans are never lost while the Cylons are.

pragmatism.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
pragmatism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: MacMullan argues Stewart is America's most effective public intellectual working in the pragmatist tradition Cornel West describes, philosophy as continuous cultural commentary 'explaining America to itself' rather than academia's ingrown self-talk (the failure Rorty diagnosed). He shows The Daily Show performing this role through irony and critical cultural memory: the Colbert exchange rewarding Karl Rove's Plame leak with 'Chief Justice', 'Victory Lapse' on Republican outrage at Obama's bin Laden ad versus Bush's Mission Accomplished carrier landing, 'Gitmo's World', and the 'Meet the Depressed' Magic Bullet blender takedown of Obama's unkept promises. Stewart's Deweyan faith in democracy as a way of life appears in the Rally to Restore Sanity, his genuine debates with guests like David Barton and Marco Rubio, his anger at CNBC's Cramer for burning the house down with our money, and the 9/11 Zadroga Bill segments that shamed Congress into passing the law.

pragmatism.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
pragmatism.title: The Jihadist Way of Life
pragmatism.relation: Argues that the Fremen, despite their supposed Zensunni faith (which it argues was never a liberation theology), are quintessentially American: Emersonian self-reliance appears as spiritual self-sufficiency and the Spannungsbogen self-imposed delay, while Dewey's democracy as a way of life surfaces in the jihad's aim of replacing master-slave relations with relative equals under Shai-Hulud. It cites Herbert's 'Dune Genesis' on myth-making as pragmatically valuable and reads Paul, who ends Dune Messiah walking blind into the desert 'where we walk without footprints', as kin to the 'American Taliban' John Walker Lindh, whose conversion and jihad were driven by the same self-reliant, spiritual, pragmatic values.

pragmatism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
pragmatism.title: “What happens to us now ”
pragmatism.relation: Tests the moral limits of science against Dresden's defense of Eros ('hardly a rounding error', 'we become our own gods'): Descartes' evil demon explains why Holden can never verify the protomolecule-ghost Miller — or even the Roci's bulkhead — is real; Baconian induction and mastery of nature explain why Protogen feeds biomass to the protomolecule ('we can only learn by letting it learn'), though Bacon himself demanded knowledge be shared for universal good; Peirce's pragmatism explains how the Donnager infers stealth ships from their effects and why protomolecule victims count as no longer human; and Dewey's inseparability of means and ends indicts Fred Johnson's readiness to negotiate with Dresden. It culminates in Miller shooting Dresden — 'I killed him because he was making sense' — as the straightest critique of utilitarian calculation, concluding that when empathy is excised (Cortázar's stimulation) or ignored, even science aimed at saving humanity produces Eros, Project Caliban, and the Earth-Mars war.

pragmatism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
pragmatism.title: Notes
pragmatism.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

pragmatism.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
pragmatism.title: 3. Sympathy for the Devils
pragmatism.relation: Argues, against Michael, that the Soul Squad still belongs in the Bad Place: drawing on William James's conditions for actions having moral worth (foreseeable consequences, no do-overs) and his meliorism about an unfinished, responsive universe, it shows the points system is contextualist (the tricycle fix worth +4.79 or +0.04; the two Dougs' rose gifts), but the afterlife simulation is a context where nothing the humans do is consequential or permanent, so their moral growth earns no points. Worse, their growth adds net unhappiness — Michael's suffering, the demon cast's misery, Judge Gen's distress — so becoming better ironically confirms they belong in the Bad Place. Only Michael, whose retirement is a real, irreversible consequence and whose sacrifices add genuine good, deserves the Good Place.

pragmatism.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
pragmatism.title: Putting One’s Mind into a Body
pragmatism.relation: Seng reads the 2008 film's crash-and-stabilizer flying lessons as philosophy of mind: at first the armor seems to confirm Descartes' dualism, with Stark the thinking substance piloting a mechanical body and Jarvis playing the pineal gland. But Stark smashing into the ceiling while learning to fly shows the embodied mind of Dewey and Merleau-Ponty — habits, spatial existence, and the imported home preferences that make the suit feel like his own skin, so that the repulsors whir closed when he stands down before the village gunmen. Dewey's view of intelligence as acting on estimates of a situation then explains Stark's growth from selfish playboy to sharable goods (beating the merely self-interested Stane), and Jarvis counts as Stark's mind made manifest in the suit.

pragmatism.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
pragmatism.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Godwin reads Spider-Man 3's black-suit episode as a question about the self: with the symbiote amplifying his anger, is Peter still Peter? Against Hume's and the Buddha's bundle theories, on which the self is only an imagined aggregate of thoughts and feelings, and Reid's common-sense simple self, she advances the pragmatist 'social self' of Peirce, James, Dewey, and Mead, updated as Engel's biopsychosocial model: Peter's identity is a shifting web of biology, psyche, and relationships (Aunt May, MJ, Harry) expressed in actions and character. Eddie succumbs to the symbiote because, as Dewey says of the slave to his own blind desires, hatred constitutes who he is, while Peter's thicker web of good relations lets him shed the suit at the church bell.

pragmatism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
pragmatism.title: “You Like Me because I'm a Scoundrel”
pragmatism.relation: Decker asks whether Han Solo can truly evade philosophy, opening with Aristotle's Protrepticus proof that one must do philosophy either way. Han's demystifying skepticism ('no mystical energy field controls my destiny,' 'That's not how the Force works!') is paired with Wittgenstein's Tractatus, which dismisses traditional philosophical questions as senseless and offers therapy for the philosophical itch, and with Montaigne's skepticism about book learning — though Han's orphan scrumrat education exposes the class privilege behind Montaigne's 'sweet pillow' of ignorance. His anti-authoritarianism is read through Emerson (via Cornel West) and Rorty's pragmatism as anti-authoritarianism: build philosophical reflections around political hopes rather than foundations, which is why the 'everyday people' of the Disney+ era, epitomized by the scoundrel, break the spell of the Skywalker grand narrative.

pragmatism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
pragmatism.title: Lesser of Two Evils
pragmatism.relation: Horn reads the Blaviken conflict as a clash of two utilitarianisms: Stregobor locks up women born during the black sun on Benthamite grounds that maximizing humanity's happiness justifies evil, while Renfri's revenge on Stregobor follows Popper's negative utilitarianism of minimizing suffering, and Foot's runaway trolley shows both reasoning toward killing the one. Le Guin's Omelas, with its tortured child beneath a utopia, exposes where Stregobor's and Renfri's 'lesser evil' logic leads. Geralt rejects both because he deliberates as Raff Donelson's ethical pragmatist: he accepts the facts but tests options against the shared Witcher's Code values (kill only to save, never from fear), which is why he prefers not to choose at all.

pragmatism.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
pragmatism.title: Philosophers Can't Jump
pragmatism.relation: Tim Elcombe uses Dewey's pragmatist account of lived experience to read the Hoosiers scene in Butler Fieldhouse: Coach Dale's tape measure shows time and space are durable constants (the basket is ten feet in Indianapolis too), yet the awestruck Huskers will live that same space in a radically new way, and Kant and Augustine frame the gap between clock time and lived time. He argues basketball is the most 'phenomenal' game because the ticking clock creates genuine drama (Reggie Miller's 1995 buzzer three, childhood 'buzzer beater' games) and the ten-foot basket builds a vertical dimension no other sport matches, answering Scott Kretchmar's defense of event-regulated baseball. Our cultural obsession with dunking - Michael Jordan's Nike ads, Teen Wolf, Like Mike, White Men Can't Jump - expresses the human fascination with briefly defying gravity, a 'moving image of eternity'.

pragmatism.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
pragmatism.title: Knockout! Killer’s Kiss, the Somatic, and Kubrick Kevin S. Decker
pragmatism.relation: Decker reads Killer's Kiss (and later 2001, A Clockwork Orange, Eyes Wide Shut) through Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of the lived body ('I am my body'), recovering the somatic that Socrates and Plato's Phaedo denigrated. In Killer's Kiss the boxing match, the mannequin-warehouse fight where bodies become weapons, spatial camera work, and the theme of contingency foreground embodiment; 2001 makes viewers feel their own bodies in space, and A Clockwork Orange's Ludovico 'cure' rewires the body-mind. Drawing on pragmatists Shusterman and Sullivan and on Foucault's biopower, he argues the anonymous masked bodies of Eyes Wide Shut turn Merleau-Ponty's projective intentionality into domination rather than communication.

pragmatism.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
pragmatism.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
pragmatism.relation: Decker reads Killer's Kiss (with 2001, A Clockwork Orange, and Eyes Wide Shut) to recover the philosophy of the body against the Socratic-Platonic-Cartesian denigration of the somatic. Using Merleau-Ponty's existential phenomenology ('I am my body') and pragmatists like Shusterman and Sullivan, he shows Kubrick's obsessive use of space, contingency, and the visceral - Davy's boxing match, the mannequin-warehouse fight, the weightless bodies of 2001, the Ludovico brainwashing of Alex, and the anonymous masked bodies of Eyes Wide Shut - to argue that subjectivity is corporeal and that anonymity of bodies can fund Foucauldian domination rather than liberation.

pragmatism.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
pragmatism.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
pragmatism.relation: Abrams reads Kubrick's Lolita as a parody of Poe's Dupin detective story, arguing that Humbert Humbert's method is not deduction but Peirce's logic of abduction (guessing). Humbert is the 'resolvent' half of Poe's double-Dupin - all calculation and chess - and excels only at overcoded abductions (spotting a nymphet) while failing the creative, undercoded abductions needed to see that Clare Quilty, the 'creative' double, is manipulating him. Abrams maps the film onto Poe's game-analysis (chess vs. cards) and the myth of the labyrinth, with Quilty as the ever-changing Minotaur whom Nabokov and Kubrick use for authorial 'involution.'

pragmatism.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
pragmatism.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
pragmatism.relation: Sterritt 'schizoanalyzes' The Informant! by arguing that its lying protagonist Mark Whitacre, an ADM executive turned FBI informant, is a nut psychoanalysis cannot crack because he has no unconscious depth: his self is Deleuze and Guattari's rhizomatic, depthless flow of desire with 'nothing behind it' (echoing Warhol). He reads Mark's compulsive fabrication as deterritorialization against the corporation-as-psychopath, links the film to the Socratic unexamined life and to William James's open, flux-embracing empiricism (via Cassavetes), and interprets the climactic collision of Mark's voiceover and dialogue as the film itself intervening as the ultimate informant.

pragmatism.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
pragmatism.title: Mommas, Don't Let Your Babies Grow Up to Be Pragmatists
pragmatism.relation: Csaki argues that John Wayne became the ultimate cinematic cowboy because his characters embody classical American pragmatism. Using William James's squirrel-and-tree parable and Dewey's account of 'inquiry' transforming an indeterminate situation, he reads Rooster Cogburn's split-second raft decision and Wil Anderson's hiring of schoolboys in The Cowboys as pragmatic problem-solving from experience. He treats the 'code of the West' not as fixed absolutes but as rules applied pragmatically (Rooster shooting men in the back, the cowboys letting Long Hair be dragged to death), where truth is what can be assimilated, verified, and made to 'work.'

pragmatism.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
pragmatism.title: Regeneration through Stories and Song The View from the Other Side of the West in Smoke Signals
pragmatism.relation: Richard Gilmore reads Smoke Signals—the first feature written, directed, and coproduced by Native Americans—against Slotkin's myth of regeneration through violence, arguing it offers regeneration through stories and song instead. Drawing on Wilshire's claim that pragmatism is 'aboriginal,' he links Emerson and Thoreau's transcendentalism and Peirce's 'law of mind' to Deloria's American Indian metaphysics and Hyde's gift economy: Arlene's fry-bread story and Thomas's storytelling repair broken relationships, and Victor's final act of forgiving his father (and withholding that Arnold caused the fatal fire) is read as the film's central gift, completing relationships that violence had severed.

pragmatism.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
pragmatism.title: 2 Neil Young and Creativity
pragmatism.relation: Berger surveys Young's repeated claim that he does not intentionally compose but "receives" songs, comparing himself to a radio station or microphone and echoing Schubert's "I remember it." He illuminates this with C.S. Peirce's categories of firstness (feeling), secondness (reaction) and thirdness (thought/signs), arguing that Young's refusal to "judge" lyrics like "Tell Me Why" or "Cowgirl in the Sand" protects the originary feeling, and that songs communicate feeling through Peircean icons and metaphors rather than deliberate rational design.

pragmatism.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
pragmatism.title: 5 Neil Young Lover of Sun, Moon and Cars
pragmatism.relation: Anderson traces Young's environmentalism from the hippie-romantic nature worship of "After the Gold Rush" and Greendale toward a pragmatic "middle way" that reconciles his love of nature with his love of cars and recording technology (the Lincvolt project, Storytone). Drawing on Thoreau, Muir and Leopold's land ethic while rejecting the fixed prescriptions of Singer and Regan, he presents Young as an experimentalist "meliorist" who owns his own complicity in CO2 abuse and urges informed, practical, self-aware action rather than utopian or deontological solutions.

pragmatism.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
pragmatism.title: 9. Anthony Bourdain’s Inquiring Mind
pragmatism.relation: Anderson and Mauro trace Bourdain's growth from the dogmatic provocateur of Kitchen Confidential to a Peircean inquirer, using Peirce's 'The Fixation of Belief' and its four methods (tenacity, authority, a priori, inquiry). They argue Bourdain's tattooed motto 'I am certain of nothing,' his surprise and self-correction in Cambodia, Beirut, Saudi Arabia, and Haiti, and his pragmatic theory of evolving truth make him a model of the self-correcting inquiring life.

pragmatism.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
pragmatism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Terrance MacMullan argues Stewart is America's most effective public intellectual, reviving the engaged tradition of Emerson, William James, Dewey, and Du Bois against the isolation Rorty diagnosed in academics. Using Cornel West's account of pragmatism as 'explaining America to itself,' he reads segments like 'Victory Lapse,' the Karl Rove 'what honor' bit, and 'Gitmo's World' as pragmatist cultural criticism, and casts Stewart's 'Worst Responders' campaign for the 9/11 Zadroga Bill and his amicable debates with conservatives as embodying Dewey's democracy as a shared 'working faith' in people.

pragmatism.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
pragmatism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
pragmatism.relation: Decker asks whether 'Stephen Colbert' the persona is an 'existential ironist,' tracing irony from Socrates's Delphic-oracle-inspired questioning through Schlegel, Hegel (irony as freedom but an abdication of responsibility), and Kierkegaard (the ironist detached from and not taking community practices seriously). He reads Colbert's centerless self-redescription and Super PAC stunt via Rorty's 'ironist' and 'final vocabulary' (built from Nietzschean self-creation and Deweyan plasticity through language), then argues that truthiness is a dangerous subjectivism—and that Colbert, unlike a pure Rortian ironist, drops the mask to side with the powerless.

pragmatism.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
pragmatism.title: Neither Here, nor There, nor Anywhere
pragmatism.relation: Randall Auxier reads Green Eggs and Ham as a primer in Peircean pragmatism. The contrarian 'C' illustrates how thinking only begins when a problem interrupts action, and Peirce's distinction between 'genuine doubt' and settled belief-as-habit explains why C clings to 'I do not like them' without ever trying them. Auxier runs C's stubbornness through Peirce's four methods of fixing belief (Authority, A Priori, Tenacity, Science), arguing C relies on tenacity, and likens Sam-I-Am to Saint Monica pestering Augustine into genuine doubt, so that even after C eats the eggs he only knows they settled belief in one context.

pragmatism.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
pragmatism.title: Pragmatist Ethics with John Dewey, Horton, and the Lorax
pragmatism.relation: Alexander contrasts Dewey's reflective, character-centered ethics with utilitarianism and Kantian deontology using the Lorax and Horton. The Once-ler is cast as the shortsighted 'utilitarian' maximizing Thneed happiness while the Lorax, urging us to 'stop and think' about the whole ecosystem, is really a Deweyan practicing reflective morality and deliberation as 'dramatic rehearsal.' Horton's conscientious care for the Whos illustrates Dewey's 'Who Factor' and growth of character rather than cold rule-following, showing morality as the ongoing education of desire toward inclusive, shared ends.

pragmatism.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
pragmatism.title: MOTHERHOOD
pragmatism.relation: Sue Ellen Henry uses John Dewey's pragmatism, especially The Quest for Certainty and Democracy and Education, to diagnose her own 'quest for certainty' as a new mother mediating expert parenting books against her own instincts. She argues Dewey's rejection of the false dichotomy between knowledge and belief shows that a mother's home is her 'laboratory,' where experience is itself a form of knowledge; her La Leche League experience models Dewey's integrated, feedback-driven inquiry against the isolating authority of 'scientific motherhood' texts.

pragmatism.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
pragmatism.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
pragmatism.relation: Holt argues that Seinfeld's Festivus, invented by Frank Costanza as an anti-consumerist 'holiday for the rest of us,' is grounded in American pragmatism: truth is 'whatever works,' malleable and tested by results. Because commercialized Christmas fails to deliver the altruism it demands, it 'does not work' and by pragmatist standards ceases to be true, so Costanza pragmatically forges a holiday that fits his needs. Holt reads Festivus's elements pragmatically — the maintenance-free aluminum pole as a bare functional symbol, the airing of grievances as a needed cathartic release from everyday restraint, the wrestling as self-perpetuating ritual — and warns that as Festivus merchandise spreads it will lose its practicality and, being no longer pragmatic, be discarded; he closes with a mock 'airing of grievances' against philosophers including Plato and Bertrand Russell.

pragmatism.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
pragmatism.title: GARDENING
pragmatism.relation: Shapiro argues that Frederick Law Olmsted's Central Park is a major artwork realizing a 'pragmatic picturesque,' and reads the English picturesque garden as a 'diagram' (in Foucault's and Deleuze's sense) of the glance—the roving, liberated look—explicitly contrasted with Bentham's Panopticon, the diagram of the objectifying gaze. Using Derrida's paradox of the frame, he shows the picturesque hides its boundary (the ha-ha) while Olmsted inverts the diagram, making the frame explicit and admitting the city so citizens meet in democratic 'gregarious' recognition—a Platonic argument (aesthetic education in the Republic) turned pragmatic in the climate of Peirce, James and Dewey. Christo and Jeanne-Claude's 'The Gates' distills the park's diagram as a gift of time.

pragmatism.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
pragmatism.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
pragmatism.relation: David Robles's 'The Seeker' argues that declining trust in Western absolutist religion drives people toward yoga as an experiential, self-directed spirituality. His central move is that Patanjali's Yoga Sutras rank direct perception above testimony and scripture — mirroring the scientific method — so yoga functions as a 'spiritual science' harmonious with empiricism, whereas established religion rests on second-hand revelation. He distinguishes 'spiritual' (personal, inspiration-based) from 'religious' (culturally binding dogma) and casts the American 'seeker' as building a better, results-oriented, pragmatic spirituality.

pragmatism.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
pragmatism.title: Who is Who
pragmatism.relation: On regeneration and personal identity, the chapter runs Doctor Who through Leibniz's law of identity and soul-based individuation, Locke's memory criterion of personhood, and Hume's bundle theory, testing them against multi-Doctor stories, the Ganger duplicates ('The Almost People'), 'The Girl Who Waited' (closest-continuer theory) and 'City of Death.' It then shifts to physicalism (the Morbius brain) and to a pragmatist, social theory of the self (James, Dewey, Mead's 'taking the attitude of the other,' Dennett's intentional stance), reading the reintegration of identity in 'The Doctor Dances.'

pragmatism.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
pragmatism.title: NOTES
pragmatism.relation: Richard Shusterman defends the entertainment value of popular art from a pragmatist ('meliorist') stance, tracing entertainment's genealogy through Plato, Aristotle, Montaigne, Kant, Hegel, Nietzsche, Heidegger and Adorno—whose 'culture industry' opposes pleasure to cognition. Using rap (KRS-One's 'Edutainment', Public Enemy, Ice-T) and T.S. Eliot's 'superior amusement,' he argues knowledge and enjoyment are compatible. He rejects Hannah Arendt's contrast of imperishable art vs. life-serving entertainment, and critiques G.E. Moore's Principia Ethica 'method of absolute isolation' for intrinsic value, replacing it with a Deweyan transactional account in which even intrinsic values are relational and temporal.

pragmatism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
pragmatism.title: 10. Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood as Philosophy Children as Philosophers
pragmatism.relation: Baggett argues that Mister Rogers' Neighborhood was a profoundly philosophical show because it treated very young children as natural philosophers — curious, wonder-filled questioners — rather than mere proto-adults. He frames child-development theory through the rationalism/empiricism divide (Skinner's behaviorism descending from Locke's tabula rasa, Chomsky's innatism from Descartes) and champions Gareth Matthews's claim that children's 'romancing' is genuine philosophy adults should not condescend to. Rogers modeled Hadot's philosophy-as-a-way-of-life and James's and Rousseau's active learning; episodes on death (the goldfish), work, and make-believe invited the same wonder Aquinas and Hume brought to happiness and causation, treating children as members of Kant's kingdom of ends.

epistemological-anarchism.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
epistemological-anarchism.title: Pals
epistemological-anarchism.relation: Madeline Muntersbjorn uses Season Four's Initiative-versus-Scoobies conflict to dissolve the Science Wars: Professor Walsh's secret, unfalsifiable Project 314 makes her Karl Popper's bad scientist, while Buffy's gang embodies Feyerabend's pluralism and Peirce-and-James pragmatism — Buffyverse rules are probabilistic rather than deterministic, and the gang welcomes anyone willing to ask questions and do research. Her three ideals — pluralism, pragmatism, pals — culminate in 'Primeval,' where the combo-Buffy enjoining spell (Willow's spirit, Xander's heart, Giles's mind, Buffy's hand) literally enacts James's meliorism: the world may be saved if each agent does their level best, together. Walsh dies alone because she has no pals; Buffy saves the world 'a lot' because she does.

epistemological-anarchism.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
epistemological-anarchism.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
epistemological-anarchism.relation: Surveys the philosophy of science through Breaking Bad: Walt's authority trades on the trusted white-coat stereotype (Jesse's 'you're supposed to be a scientist', Tuco's CPR demand), while the chapter traces how modern science distinguished itself from alchemy via Kuhn's structure of scientific revolutions and Lakatos's research programmes, and how Feyerabend and the Traditional Knowledge movement challenge Western science's monopoly - echoed in Jesse's chili powder and the ingenious 'shake-and-bake' method. Walt and Jesse's quarrel over method resolves into an apprentice-master reconciliation ('you're an artist'), mirroring science's own shifting self-image. Ellul's grim prediction that technology, once embraced, cannot be made humane explains the ending: remission comes too late, and Walt may as well try to un-invent a weapon of mass destruction.

epistemological-anarchism.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
epistemological-anarchism.title: 16. Why Scott Adams Is Stupid
epistemological-anarchism.relation: Miori audits Adams's science talk through epistemology: warrant for belief, empiricism versus rationalism, Wittgenstein's demand for unambiguous clarity, and Clifford's epistemic responsibility, that it is always wrong to believe on insufficient evidence, which condemns sampling television news while blogging on climate science. Popper's falsifiability, learned from Einstein's willingness to be refuted against Freud's confirmation-seeking, exposes Adams's double standard in waving confirmation bias at critics while crediting his own predictions, and Feyerabend's epistemological anarchism is the view Adams most resembles, except that Feyerabend took responsibility and retracted. Cipolla's Basic Laws of Human Stupidity (the stupid person causes losses to both self and others) frames the closing charge: Adams suggests and retreats, sells product, and shirks the epistemic duty that experts in climate science and medicine shoulder.

epistemological-anarchism.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
epistemological-anarchism.title: Of Science, Sorcery, and Philosophy
epistemological-anarchism.relation: The chapter reads Strange's conversion from neurosurgeon to sorcerer as a Kuhnian paradigm shift: his medical materialism is 'normal science' puzzle-solving that keeps resisting anomalies (Pangborn's impossible recovery, the astral projection, the multiverse tour) until Kamar-Taj offers a rival paradigm with its own exemplars, which he can only adopt by learning 'knowledge how' through tedious practice. It explains incommensurability through Strange's inability to rationally persuade his old medical colleagues, then contrasts Kuhn with Popper's falsificationism, Feyerabend's 'anything goes' anarchism (sorcery once looked as disreputable as early heliocentrism), and Lakatos's progressive versus degenerating research programs to ask whether sorcery could count as a science in Strange's world.

epistemological-anarchism.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
epistemological-anarchism.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
epistemological-anarchism.relation: Cole Bowman explains the three Formic invasions as failures between 'conceptual schemes,' deploying Davidson's 'On the Very Idea of a Conceptual Scheme' — translatability, the principle of charity, and the closet analogy — alongside Kuhn's incommensurable paradigms and Feyerabend's account of how new theories eliminate old meanings. Ender donning the bugger mask in Peter's game and his final philotic bond with the hive-queen show the two schemes touching at a single shared point, making Ender 'the metal in between' who begins translating between human and Formic worlds.

falsification.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
falsification.title: Pals
falsification.relation: Madeline Muntersbjorn uses Season Four's Initiative-versus-Scoobies conflict to dissolve the Science Wars: Professor Walsh's secret, unfalsifiable Project 314 makes her Karl Popper's bad scientist, while Buffy's gang embodies Feyerabend's pluralism and Peirce-and-James pragmatism — Buffyverse rules are probabilistic rather than deterministic, and the gang welcomes anyone willing to ask questions and do research. Her three ideals — pluralism, pragmatism, pals — culminate in 'Primeval,' where the combo-Buffy enjoining spell (Willow's spirit, Xander's heart, Giles's mind, Buffy's hand) literally enacts James's meliorism: the world may be saved if each agent does their level best, together. Walsh dies alone because she has no pals; Buffy saves the world 'a lot' because she does.

falsification.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
falsification.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
falsification.relation: Steele starts from Orwell's worry that laypeople accept scientific consensus as unreflectively as tribesmen accept witch-doctors — sharpened by Lysenko and Nazi 'racial science' — and answers it with Popper's critical rationalism: since Hume's problem of induction bars proof from instances, we can only provisionally prefer theories that survive severe attempts at falsification, so trusting experts is reasonable exactly when their community tests rather than defends its theories. Kuhn's paradigms explain why dissident alternatives like Atkins talk past the dominant school (Atkins and Agatston are cardiologists, not dieticians), and the 2002–2004 studies showing improved lipids on more fat figure as the kind of surprise that precedes paradigm change. His verdict: neither trusting nor resisting experts is foolish; 'human knowledge is too important to be left to experts.'

falsification.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
falsification.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
falsification.relation: 'The Year in Bullshit' catalogues the fraud climate surrounding the book's success: James Frey's fabricated memoir A Million Little Pieces exposed on Oprah, the wholly invented author J.T. Leroy, product placement and paid word-of-mouth advertising blurring the line between ads and ordinary conversation, and scientific fraud in pharmaceutical and federal research. It invokes Karl Popper's claim that science deserves respect precisely because it falsifies its own claims, presenting headlines about fabricated results as that ideal fading. Frank Rich's verdict that 'such distinctions have long since washed away in much of our public life' supplies the chapter's explanation of the book's appeal as cultural despair.

falsification.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
falsification.title: Combatting the Two Kinds of Bullshit
