kant-humanity-formula.relation: Perez reads racism in Netflix's Witcher through Ibram X. Kendi's power-based account of racism, tracing the humans-versus-elves conflict through colorism (pointy ears and elven blood), 'drop rules' of racial purity that stigmatize Yennefer's quarter-elven lineage, and mutual dehumanization from Stregobor's 'mongrels' slur to Francesca's vow that the next genocide will be the humans'. He tests Kant's humanity formula against Nilfgaard's 'haven' for elves and the Battle of Aretuza, finding both sides guilty of using persons as mere means, then uses Suzy Killmister's three-strand dignity to explain why Calanthe's hidden heritage destroys her while Jaskier's Sandpiper smuggling and Cahir kneeling before Ciri restore dignity. Sartre's Other frames Yennefer's fluctuating identity between human and elf, and Dara laying down his hatred plus Ciri renouncing her power and taking the name Falka model Kendi's claim that being racist or antiracist is chosen moment by moment.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
kant-humanity-formula.title: Hoop Dreams, Blacktop Realities
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Bernard Jackson Jr. argues that basketball is an institution where black manhood is socially constructed (leaning on Naomi Zack's feminist point that gender identity is imposed by social designation), and that love among black players is essential to that construction while toughness is equivocal - the 'soft' label stuck to the gentlemanly David Robinson even as the Pistons walked off without congratulating the Bulls. Reading the documentary Hoop Dreams, he shows Arthur Agee and William Gates being used as commodities by recruiters, Coach Pingatore, and family expectations, invoking Marx on exploitation and 'use value' (Spike Lee's Nike-camp speech) and Kant's demand that persons be treated as ends, never merely as means. He likens William Gates's return to Chicago's Cabrini-Green as a minister to Plato's enlightened prisoner going back down into the cave.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
kant-humanity-formula.title: Virtue and Violence Can a Good Football Player Be a Good Person
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Davison defends a 'Violence Principle'—intentionally causing violent harm known to be unnecessary for a greater good is wrong—and applies it to in-the-rules football hits like Jack Tatum on Darryl Stingley and Warren Sapp on Chad Clifton. Against a consequentialist defense of intimidation, he invokes Kant's requirement to treat persons as ends, not mere means, arguing players consent to accidental injury but not intentional harm. Citing the Socratic examination of the soul, he warns of moral danger to players who use excessive force and to fans who relish violence for its own sake.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
kant-humanity-formula.title: 5. Albert Among the Chowder-Head Yokels and Blithering Hayseeds
kant-humanity-formula.relation: The Phillipses argue that abrasive forensic agent Albert Rosenfield is a model Kantian: his refusal to lie to spare Truman's feelings follows the formula of universal law, and his insistence that Truman be punished for the assault treats Truman as an autonomous end. They run Gordon Cole's manipulative lying through the universalizability test (it fails, unlike wanting pie), distinguish hypothetical from categorical imperatives via Cooper's rebuff of Audrey, and read Albert's 'I love you, Sheriff Truman' and Gandhi/King nonviolence as respect for persons as ends in themselves—duty done for the right reason.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
kant-humanity-formula.title: The Right and the Good without God
kant-humanity-formula.relation: The chapter builds the case that Whedon's fiction grounds ethics without God: Foy's Lockean social-contract reading of the Firefly crew and Kant's person-as-end analysis explain why Mal insists Saffron is 'not to be bought' in 'Our Mrs. Reynolds' and why Loki's possession of Hawkeye and Jasmine's enthrallment of her worshippers are the Whedonverse's paradigm wrongs. Spike's arc—from selfish ally, through the 'Triangle' troll fight and 'Intervention' torture, to the 'Chosen' sacrifice—is read through Aristotelian habituation into virtue, while Angel's Darla-arc firing of Team Angel and the Better Days temple-money and Inara plots show where respecting rights and being a good person can come apart. Finally the Euthyphro dilemma, plus replies to Pojman and Craig (self-sacrifice is not 'stupid'), argue that Angel's 'Epiphany' ethic—doing what matters with no glorious end or divine reward—shows morality is neither arbitrary nor motivationally crippled without God.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
kant-humanity-formula.title: Was it Morally Wrong to Kill Off Sherlock Holmes
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Terjesen asks whether Conan Doyle acted immorally in killing Holmes in 'The Final Problem,' framing it through property theory. He runs Locke's labor theory (illustrated via 'The Blue Carbuncle' gem), Proudhon and Marx's critiques, and both consequentialist and Kantian (respect-for-persons) justifications of intellectual property. He argues Conan Doyle's ownership of the iconic Holmes weakened as Paget, Gillette, Rathbone, and Dr. Joseph Bell co-authored the figure, so property rights alone can't justify the killing—but Conan Doyle's authorial dignity plus the narrative fitness of 'The Final Problem' and 'His Last Bow' make the send-off defensible.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
kant-humanity-formula.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Hoffman reads Eyes Wide Shut as Kubrick's most optimistic film, about whether marital fidelity can be chosen rather than accidental. Bill's confidence in his own and Alice's fidelity is a Kantian appeal - duty and rational principle over inclination - which Alice's confession of overwhelming desire for the naval officer, and Bill's night among the masked orgy, expose as vulnerable to uncontrollable desire and moral luck. Hoffman argues that by unmasking and honestly acknowledging these desires (and drawing on Kierkegaard on marriage existing 'in time') the Harfords consciously rechoose their marriage, so their fidelity is no longer merely accidental.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
kant-humanity-formula.title: General Patton and Private Ryan The Conflicting Reality of War and Films about War
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Fiala uses Patton's opening speech ("an army is a team… this individuality stuff is a bunch of crap") against Saving Private Ryan's mission to rescue one soldier to frame war's basic conflict between the collective and the individual, and to expose the problem of "realism" in representing war. He aligns the collectivist realist ethics of war against the just-war tradition's deontological respect for individuals as Kantian ends-in-themselves, and contrasts Patton's aerial, above-the-battle viewpoint with Private Ryan's first-person D-Day realism. Drawing on Tim O'Brien's claim that a true war story is never moral, and on Nussbaum's and Glover's moral imagination, he concludes that no film can synthesize war's public and private perspectives—mirroring the failure of moral imagination that produces war itself.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
kant-humanity-formula.title: The Duty of Reason Kantian Ethics in High Noon
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Evans argues that Marshal Will Kane in High Noon is Kant's ideal moral agent, acting from duty and a good will rather than from consequences. He shows the townsfolk, Kane's friends, Harvey Pell, Helen Ramirez, and Amy all reasoning consequentially or heteronomously (the mayor privileging the town's finances, Mildred lying about Sam per Kant's essay on the supposed right to lie), while Frank Miller's revenge is a maxim that cannot be universalized. Kane's maxim of standing against lawlessness regardless of cost satisfies all three formulations of the categorical imperative—universal law, humanity as an end, and autonomy—making him a member of the kingdom of ends and contrasting Kant with Mill's utilitarianism.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
kant-humanity-formula.title: Is Oskar Schindler a Good Man
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Ebertz treats Schindler's List as a thought experiment on what makes a person good, judging Oskar Schindler against Kantian and virtue-ethical standards. On Kant he fails: many acts (lying, bribery, infidelity) violate the categorical imperative, and even his rescues spring from growing partial attachment to 'his Jews' rather than rational duty or a good will. On Aristotelian virtue ethics he only selectively exercises virtues, so is not fully 'good' either; Ebertz resolves the tension with a Principle of Moral Exemplarity, holding Schindler up as a flawed but genuine moral example whose care promotes human flourishing.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
kant-humanity-formula.title: Love, Value, and the Human Destiny in Interstellar
kant-humanity-formula.relation: The chapter stages Interstellar's conflict between Cooper's partial love for his own family and Professor Brand's species-level duty as a question about the intrinsic value of humanity. Using Aristotle's account of friends and children as 'other selves' and of happiness as the one end sought for its own sake, it argues that the species survives only as a byproduct of particular, partial loves, so Plan B's bank of 5,000 faceless embryos could not preserve 'us' in any meaningful sense. Kant's unconditional dignity of rational persons supplies Brand's premise that our existence enriches the universe, but the chapter turns Kant against him: Brand's monstrous lie to the Endurance crew treats persons as mere means to an end they do not share, trampling the very dignity it claims to save. It closes by asking what value colonizing Edmunds's planet would destroy—ecosystems, microbial life, and possibly other rational persons whose dignity we would be obliged to respect—should humanity refuse to 'go gentle into that good night.'

kant-humanity-formula.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
kant-humanity-formula.title: 7. More Mothers, Lovers, and Other Monsters
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Brace surveys the later-season mother figures—Mary, Kelly, Jody, Rowena, Mrs. Butters, Charlie—arguing they are repeatedly used as emotional tools against the Winchesters, which she reads through Kant's warning against treating persons merely as means. She stresses loss of free will and agency: Mary's British Men of Letters 'realignment' and Mrs. Butters's coercive programming strip their autonomy and reduce them to objects/killers, while their reclaimed agency and self-sacrifice restore their Kantian standing as ends in themselves.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
kant-humanity-formula.title: 1. Scamming for Fun
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Clipsham distinguishes Jimmy and Kim's 'scamming for fun' (deceiving Ken over rare tequila in 'Switch', or a montage of pointless cons in 'Marco') from the 'scheming for benefits' of Mike, Gus, and Chuck, who lie only to secure a specific end. Using Kant's prohibition on treating people merely as means, he argues that scheming for a benefit is more disrespectful than scamming for its own sake, because the latter treats a mark as an unwitting player in a game rather than a tool. He also rejects the worry that fun-scamming corrupts character, noting Jimmy was already dishonest and that Gus and Lalo's worst vices have no root in playful deception.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
kant-humanity-formula.title: Real World Island
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Patricia Brace and Rob Arp argue that Lost characters move from blameworthy to praiseworthy by ceasing to objectify others and instead objectifying themselves for a greater good. Using Kant's formula to treat persons as ends and never mere means, they condemn Ben Linus's lifelong manipulation while crediting his tearful mea culpa over Alex and his flash-sideways sacrifice for his student. Mill's utilitarianism justifies Sayid's assassinations and Kate's shooting of Un-Locke as trades for the greater number, and Aristotle's virtue ethics of cultivated respect and courage explains Charlie's Looking Glass suicide mission and Jack's Christlike self-sacrifice at the Heart of the Island, framing self-objectification as redemption.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
kant-humanity-formula.title: Horton Hears You, Too! Seuss and Kant on Respecting Persons
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Kowalski reads Horton Hatches the Egg and Horton Hears a Who! through Kant's two formulations of the categorical imperative. Mayzie's lying promise to Horton fails the universal-law test just like Kant's lying-loan and tax-shirking (Jo-Jo) cases, while Horton's insistence that 'a person's a person, no matter how small' embodies the ends-in-themselves formula treating the Whos as ends with dignity, not things. The essay argues Horton's fidelity is heroic rather than strictly required, revising Kant's moral absolutism (the inquiring-murderer case) so that when duties conflict one should act to disrespect persons least.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
kant-humanity-formula.title: It’s Not Personal . . . It’s Just Bizzyneuss Business Ethics, the Company, and Its Stakeholders
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Pierlott frames the shareholder-versus-stakeholder debate (Friedman versus Freeman) using Aristotle's function argument to ask what makes a 'good' company, then judges business relationships by Kant's humanity formula. McBean's manipulation of the Sneetches and the digital-TV cases show consumers used merely as means; McGurk's cavalier overworking of Sneelock in If I Ran the Circus and Maitland's sweatshop defense are answered with Marx's account of labor exploitation and Aristotle's voluntary-versus-mixed actions; the Once-ler's Lorax devastation shows firms externalizing environmental costs when profit is maximized at any value unprotected by law.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
kant-humanity-formula.title: MOTHERHOOD
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Amy Kind examines the pervasiveness of parents lying to children (her own 'Bad Dream Spray') against Augustine's and Kant's absolute prohibition of lying, Mill's utilitarian permissiveness, and Sissela Bok's principle of veracity. She applies Kant's categorical imperative and formula of humanity – treating persons never merely as means – to argue that because young children have not fully developed their rational natures, the Kantian wrong of lying is mitigated, while illustrating the debate with South Park's Kyle reading Descartes, A Few Good Men's 'you can't handle the truth,' and Seinfeld's George Costanza ('it's not a lie if you believe it').

kant-humanity-formula.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
kant-humanity-formula.title: MOTHERHOOD
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Bertha Alvarez Manninen reconciles her deepened respect for fetal life (after seeing her daughter on ultrasound) with a pro-choice stance by deploying Judith Jarvis Thomson's violinist thought experiment and the real McFall v. Shimp bodily-integrity ruling. She argues that even granting the fetus full personhood, no one's right to life entitles them to another's body, buttressing this with Kant's formula of humanity that a woman must not be reduced to a mere incubating means, and calls for American mizuko-kuyo-style grieving rituals so 'pro-choice' is not conflated with 'pro-abortion.'

kant-humanity-formula.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
kant-humanity-formula.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Ashwell and Langton ask whether fashion is a 'badge of slavery' (Wollstonecraft), opening with Socrates in the *Phaedo* disdaining adornment and Rousseau's girl who becomes 'her own doll,' and using Kant's humanity formula and Nussbaum's seven-feature account of objectification. Focusing on denial of autonomy in ordinary followers, they distinguish the 'Servile Fashionista' (obeys experts) from the 'Sensible Fashionista' (follows what looks good), then argue that via Johnston's 'authority of affect' even the sensible one is under an *epistemic* bondage: fashion's extrinsic social pull is misperceived as the garment's intrinsic goodness, a projective illusion (like the Müller-Lyer) that on a Kantian view undermines agency and masks misogynist or racist norms such as straightened hair or the 'lotus feet' of stilettos.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
kant-humanity-formula.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Brophy prosecutes Santa for 'elfploitation,' treating the North Pole workshop like an overseas sweatshop (with Willy Wonka's Oompa-Loompahs and Rowling's house-elfs as parallels) and dismantling a Nozickian entitlement-theory defense: the elfs' 'consent' is coerced by their bleak alternatives, so absolute property rights fail just as Locke's desert water-hole owner must grant access. He diagnoses the elfs' apparent contentment as Marxian false consciousness, invokes Kant's humanity formula to condemn using rational elfs as mere means, and rejects the utilitarian 'greatest happiness' justification via Le Guin's Omelas and Rawls's veil of ignorance. He concludes with a call to boycott Christmas until Santa's labor practices become transparent.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
kant-humanity-formula.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
kant-humanity-formula.relation: This span turns to the ethics and epistemology of college sex. Kania argues there is no clear line between close friendship and a sexual relationship, so condemning student-professor sex logically forces condemning student-professor friendship—rejecting Golash's split and defending carefully-conducted consensual relationships. Layne narrates Socrates/Alcibiades, Abelard/Heloise, and Heidegger/Arendt to contrast Socratic eros (Plato's Symposium, love as a friend of wisdom directed at the soul) and Heideggerian authentic love ('I want you to be what you are') against Abelard's exploitative lust. McDowell mines epistemology (justification, taking beliefs 'to heart,' reflective equilibrium) to argue better thinking yields better, more autonomous sex. Pinku weighs 'plain sex' against Nagel's interpersonal-arousal account of embodiment to ask whether sex needs love, and Brophy uses Kantian dignity (treating the body as a mere means, not an end) to argue that prostitution and webcam porn undertaken to pay tuition violate the student's autonomy.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
kant-humanity-formula.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
kant-humanity-formula.relation: The essay argues that soaring tuition drives college students into sexual self-commodification—egg-selling ('Pay your tuition with eggs'), craigslist/backpage escorting, and dorm-porn webcam sites like VoyeurDorm and CocoDorm—and reads these cases through Kant's second formulation, condemning them as treating oneself and others as mere means rather than ends of intrinsic dignity. It applies Marx's notion of false consciousness to Natalie Dylan's virginity auction and Ashley Dupré's 'empowerment' claims, comparing them to women choosing high heels as internalized oppression. It uses Rousseau's Social Contract and Mill's On Liberty to argue that prostitution is a form of illegitimate 'voluntary slavery' because one cannot rightly alienate one's own inalienable freedom, and contrasts coerced cases (Helena in Singapore, Rosie Reid's traumatic auctioned deflowering, John Gechter's porn suspension from a Christian college) with less-coerced ones to argue moral concern should track the degree of circumstantial coercion.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
kant-humanity-formula.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Heather Salazar interleaves philosophical arguments with yoga exercises to awaken a 'hidden ethical self.' Using Korsgaard's notion of practical identity, she has readers meditate on their roles and conflicts, then argues in Kantian fashion that recognizing the shared reasons behind everyone's pursuits obliges us to value others as we value ourselves; extending Korsgaard, that we must value the life and happiness we prize wherever they appear, in animals and plants; and via Buddhist interdependence (the world in a cup of tea) that caring for others and the environment just is a way of caring for ourselves.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
kant-humanity-formula.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Anne Barnhill uses John Cusack's boom-box serenade in Say Anything, his poolside pleading in The Sure Thing, and Andy Bernard's 'Take a Chance on Me' serenade in The Office to defend 'prospective boundary violation'—violating a boundary that would not exist in a closer relationship in order to create that relationship. She rejects the Kantian reading of Korsgaard and Hill that treating people as ends forbids all non-rational manipulation, arguing instead that such charming pushiness is 'faking it till you make it,' which works via Aristotle's habituation whereby feelings catch up with actions. She then sets four rules (no harm, not too much closer too fast, genuinely wanting the relationship, and that the other would plausibly want it) to separate appropriate from wrong boundary violations.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
kant-humanity-formula.title: 7. Independence Day & Aliens
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Rowlands frames morality around consistency and impartiality (the golden rule), articulated by Kant's categorical/practical imperatives (treat persons as ends, not merely means) and utilitarianism's greatest happiness. Imagining philosophers arguing Independence Day's aliens out of eradicating humans, he deploys the principle of 'no moral difference without a relevant other difference' and the argument from marginal cases to defeat intelligence, telepathy, and bare species membership as morally relevant. He turns the alien-invasion parable on our factory farming of chickens and pigs (Singer-style speciesism), arguing we are crueller than the aliens and fall short of our own impartiality ideal.

kant-humanity-formula.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
kant-humanity-formula.title: 43. Ex Machina as Philosophy Mendacia Ex Machina (Lies from a Machine)
kant-humanity-formula.relation: Grinnell argues Ex Machina is fundamentally about lying, read through Kant's deontology. He frames Nathan's rigged Turing test on Ava against Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge and Kant's two formulations of the categorical imperative, deriving three 'wrinkles': lying is heteronomous programming rather than the autonomy Nathan seeks; the experiment is defensible only if Ava fails, since a genuine person may not be manipulated (Formula of Humanity); and the cascade of lies among Nathan, Caleb, and Ava vindicates Kant's absolute prohibition on lying. He uses Caleb's telling of Frank Jackson's Mary's Room and Searle's weak/strong AI distinction to question whether Ava's 'pleasure response' amounts to genuine consciousness or personhood.

deconstruction.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
deconstruction.title: Possibilities of Postmodern Education Beyond Control
deconstruction.relation: Toby Daspit reads Season Four as a drama of postmodern education: the Initiative's will to master and dissect — Walsh's Frankenstein-project Adam, who murders a boy to see how he works, fulfilling Wordsworth's 'we murder to dissect' — embodies the Cartesian split and the Hegelian drive to negate the other, while Buffy's world deconstructs fixed identity (Darla reversing the horror-movie opening, the Faith/Buffy body swap in 'Who Are You?', Jonathan's 'Superstar') and thwarts prophecy's metanarrative in 'Prophecy Girl.' Against modernist schooling's 'controlled circumstances' and Freire's banking model (Professor Riegert ejecting Buffy from class, Walsh's transmission lectures), the show models knowledge as collective work — the Scoobies' research sessions in Giles's library, Giles's fluid mentorship versus Kendra's by-the-book training, and the relational magic of 'Primeval' — offering education beyond control in an emergent, postmodern world.

deconstruction.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
deconstruction.title: Both Sides of Dylan and Politics
deconstruction.relation: Jordy Rocheleau reads Dylan's protest era ("The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll," "Hurricane," "Chimes of Freedom") as Enlightenment social criticism in Kant's and Mill's sense: reason can expose injustice and secure autonomy against majority tyranny. The post-protest Dylan ("My Back Pages," "Desolation Row," "It's Alright, Ma") turns postmodern - Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives, Derrida's ever-deferred meanings, and Foucault's power/knowledge, where ideals of freedom become instruments of domination. Yet Dylan keeps crying for justice ("Political World," "Dignity"), so the chapter concludes postmodern skepticism can only serve as a cautionary check within, not a replacement of, Enlightenment politics - the thief's line in "All Along the Watchtower" as commitment amid confusion.

deconstruction.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
deconstruction.title: The Final Word That’s Right, I Said Preliminary Thoughts
deconstruction.relation: Patton starts from wildly disputed Springsteen interpretations — Reagan's 1984 campaign use of 'Born in the U.S.A.,' Flint protesters playing 'My Hometown' as civic pride, Kerry's 'No Surrender' — and asks whether any reading is better than another. He frames the issue as Socratic dialectic versus Gorgias-style rhetoric, passes through Augustine's polysemy (multiple intended levels of meaning, as in 'I'm on fire') to Nietzsche's claim that the text disappears beneath its interpretation, extended by Foucault (truth as an instrument of power) and Derridean deconstruction. His conclusion: authorial intent cannot settle meaning, but some readings ('Born in the U.S.A.' as pro-Reagan anthem) are non-starters, otherwise it is rhetoric all the way down and the sophists win.

deconstruction.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
deconstruction.title: There Are No Unrelated Phenomena
deconstruction.relation: Dark reads Thom Yorke's solo album The Eraser as an experiment in bearing witness — from Donwood's King Canute 'Gold Cnut' cover to 'Harrowdown Hill', which eulogizes David Kelly, the UN weapons inspector whose inconvenient fact-checking of the Iraq WMD dossier preceded his death ('we think the same things at the same time / we just can't do anything about it'). Drawing on Derrida — religion is responsibility or nothing, a poem is nothing without the risk of meaninglessness, words remain under erasure — he argues that Yorke's pub-table 'collating information' ('Analyze', 'And It Rained All Night'''s 'a million engines in neutral') is a sacred, self-undermining act of attention against officialdom's insistence that this has nothing to do with that. Camus's line that crushing truths perish from being acknowledged frames the witness, and the chapter closes by hearing 'Reckoner' ('dedicated to all human beings') as the communal fulfillment of that witness.

deconstruction.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
deconstruction.title: Under-Confidence in Reason Once It’s Easier Said, then It’s Done
deconstruction.relation: Roben Torosyan turns Colbert into a negative textbook for critical thinking: the character embodies the exact opposite of the American Philosophical Association's seven critical-thinking dispositions (inquisitive, open-minded, truthseeking, systematic, analytical, judicious, confident in reason), from refusing to imagine Lisa Randall's extra dimensions, to 'the market doesn't lie' about the Bible, to placing himself above Maimonides, Socrates, and Aquinas in the stem-cell Formidable Opponent. Each section names the fallacies his shtick commits - appeal to popularity, appeal to ignorance, composition, circular reasoning, wishful thinking, appeal to consequences - using real WØRD bits like the Iraq 'no casualties' monologue and the cake-metaphor exchange about the war. The WØRD's self-undermining bullet points are read as Derridean deconstruction (différance): every assertion shot through with what differs from and defers it. Watching Colbert fail at the examined life Socrates recommended, the viewer learns to catch such abuses in pundits and in themselves.

deconstruction.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
deconstruction.title: Tallying the Total
deconstruction.relation: Kreuger applies Derrida's 'Differance' to how Rush gets valued: Hugh Syme's starman, pentagram, and bunnies are signs whose meaning defers down a chain, so no description of Geddy Lee ever touches the thing itself, and the band's twenty-four gold albums (economic value) never settle the contested question of cultural value that critics deny and fans affirm. Time defers value too: 'Time Stand Still' and the concert ticket sell a moment already gone, bootlegs and leaks chase the unrepeatable experience, and radio distance once hid songs like '2112' from value. 'The Spirit of Radio' carries the thesis in its own lyric, 'bearing a gift beyond price, almost free', where 'the words of the profits' on the studio walls measure sold value against integrity, and deferral finally emerges as Derrida's 'condition of possibility' that lets Rush's cultural value recover through Colbert, Rock Band, and I Love You, Man.

deconstruction.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
deconstruction.title: The Postmodern Condition
deconstruction.relation: Rafe McGregor claims The Hound of the Baskervilles is not a detective story at all: the hound that never bites anyone and Holmes's failure to foresee fog on Dartmoor are, via Derrida's Of Grammatology, the aporia and re-mark where the mystery-horror hierarchy of the text deconstructs. He then applies Noel Carroll's philosophy of horror, the phosphorus-painted hound as a category-crossing monster producing fear plus disgust and Grimpen Mire as horror geography, to reclassify the novel as gothic horror alongside Frankenstein, Jekyll and Hyde and Dracula. The final section ties the book's enduring mass appeal to the postmodern condition, tracing the collapse of certainty from Nietzsche's prophecies about the end of Christian values to Derrida's claim that truth is never finally available, leaving anxiety as the novel's real engine.

deconstruction.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
deconstruction.title: Out of the Cave
deconstruction.relation: Traces the light-versus-darkness metaphor tradition from Plato's cave and Socrates' unexamined life through medieval 'illumination' and the Enlightenment to St. Paul's glass darkly, then lets Nietzsche ('shadow is as needful as light') and Derrida's deconstruction of presence/absence oppositions overturn it. The Stones do the same work in song: 'Just as every cop is a criminal, and all the sinners saints' in 'Sympathy for the Devil,' with 'Here Comes the Sun' overturned by 'Paint It Black' and 'Let It Be' by 'Let It Bleed.'

deconstruction.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
deconstruction.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
deconstruction.relation: Jessie Dern uses Derrida's Rogues and The Animal that Therefore I Am to show that naming is power: Victor cries 'Devil!' before the creature has done anything, and labels like 'monster,' 'rogue,' and 'animal' are performative verdicts that reveal the labeler, who secures his own goodness by negating the Other, more than the labeled. The novel multiplies the pattern, from Justine's confessor making her 'think that I was the monster that he said I was' to Elizabeth's 'men appear to me as monsters thirsting for each other's blood,' while Victor, guarding his self-image, becomes the monster himself. Against the Nietzsche epigraph about fighting monsters, the chapter closes with Derrida's playful self-application ('the animal that therefore I am') as the move the creature never gets to make: contesting the label and claiming a name and a self.

deconstruction.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
deconstruction.title: 24. An Hour
deconstruction.relation: Argues Louis's shift to an hour-a-year of digressive storytelling—spurred by George Carlin's 'dig deeper' tribute speech and forced by fatherhood—is 'secular revelation' in Adam Phillips's sense: his wandering bits work like the free play of the signifier and free association, so the stage becomes staged therapy in Lacan's return-to-Freud mode. The chapter reads the trumpet purchase as anxiety speaking through parapraxis, the street-sign and 'suck a bag of dicks' bits through Saussure's arbitrary sign and Derrida's catachresis, and Louie following Tarese home as desire that self-consciousness cannot account for.

deconstruction.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
deconstruction.title: 4. How Much Deadpool Is Too Much Deadpool
deconstruction.relation: The chapter argues Deadpool is entertaining because of, not despite, his excesses: his gratuitous violence and rapid-fire wisecracks breach the disciplined hero ideal, measured against Zeno of Citium's stoic dichotomy of control (accept the torture you cannot change, master your response) and Aristotle's golden mean between deficient and excessive force, which Wade flouts when he savors punishing Ajax instead of finishing quickly. Bakhtin's carnival excess explains the grotesque, orifice-obsessed humor that mocks 'normal' decency, and Derrida's 'internal drifting' (via Poe's Purloined Letter) frames Deadpool's first appearance being FedExed back to sender and his threshold position, where gags spill across comic, game, and film frames—making vigilante justice 'a supplement to the supplement' of law and exposing how each medium works.

deconstruction.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
deconstruction.title: 12. Gilead as Palimpsest
deconstruction.relation: Ketcham likens Offred's existence to holocaust by degree: her name is overwritten as the Nazis tattooed forearms, and her past survives like ink bleeding through a palimpsest. Using Derrida's sous rature (via Spivak's introduction and Heidegger's crossed-out words)—the word crossed out yet necessary—he reads her memories as 'under erasure,' and through Levinas's 'useless suffering' shows how her cocooned passivity severs her from the responsibility-for-the-other in which Levinas locates freedom, which is exactly what the he-theonomy needs to rule. With Du Bois's double consciousness and the Hitler parallel, the chapter warns that ideologues promising to cure suffering—Hitler, the Sons of Jacob—only write a new, more oppressive text over the erased old one.

deconstruction.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
deconstruction.title: 16. Justice The Master Narrative
deconstruction.relation: Christiansen frames justice as our culture's master narrative and tests it through two episodes. In 'The Case of the Substitute Face', Laura Houser's retroactive misidentification of her father going overboard and the fingerprint expert's error illustrate Levinas's face of the Other as first philosophy: the face-to-face call to care and responsibility that Mason answers every time he takes on a client, including the guilty. In 'The Case of the Perjured Parrot', the parrot Casanova's testimony and the imposter-parrot trick let Derrida's deconstruction (meaning by difference, endlessly deferred) and Arendt's public-space dialogue expose how little proof witness testimony really carries, with Heidegger's care-structured Dasein and Aristotle's action-over-character view framing the closing questions about faces and witnesses.

deconstruction.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
deconstruction.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
deconstruction.relation: Zeccardi and Ma deconstruct the film's hierarchical dichotomy between Walter's rule-obsessed ethical generalism (Shabbas rules, 'MARK IT ZERO!') and the nihilists' particularist 'Zere ARE no ROOLZ', using Derrida and Culler's method of undermining the opposition the text privileges. Each extreme fails: Walter's principles collide in the beeper dilemma, and active Nietzschean nihilism makes the nihilists unpredictable cowards. The Dude emerges as an Aristotelian agent of virtue whose phronesis perceptively weighs contextual facts (Smokey's disputed toe, the carpet-pissers' false assumption) against principles, making 'What would the Dude do?' a question about character rather than rules.

deconstruction.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
deconstruction.title: The Death of Death
deconstruction.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

deconstruction.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
deconstruction.title: 11 Indiana Jones and the Quest for Agnosticism What if All Stories Are True
deconstruction.relation: Robert Grant Price observes that in Indy's world every myth — the Ark, the Sankara Stones, the Grail, and in the comics and novels Atlantis, Merlin, Noah's Ark, and the Philosopher's Stone — turns out factually true, producing a surplus of evidence for mutually exclusive religions (the personal Christian Trinity versus non-personal Brahman). Against Derrida's deconstruction and the postmodern claim that no grand narrative captures truth, in Indy's world 'the squash ball always comes back' — yet he stays agnostic, telling Spalko 'There is always another explanation.' The chapter weighs his three exits: remain agnostic, take a leap of faith as he does stepping onto the invisible bridge, or read Percival and Galahad as symbolically rather than historically true.

deconstruction.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
deconstruction.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
deconstruction.relation: The editors' introduction argues that South Park is one of TV's most important series because it lampoons the fanatical extremists of every social, ethical, economic, and religious position, modeling the fallibilist skepticism critical thinkers need (quoting Parker's line that the people screaming on both sides are the same and it is OK to laugh from the middle). It offers Peirce's account of thinking through incomplete signs and Derrida's 'play of differences' as case studies of this healthy skepticism, defends laughing at fanatics because their reasoning withers in sunlight, and previews the volume: Murtagh's 'sledgehammer' defense of blasphemous humor, Jacoby's Clifford-style case that belief without evidence is wrong, Dueck on rationally defensible faith, Gray on the 'Douche or Turd' election, and Held on gay marriage.

deconstruction.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
deconstruction.title: The Philosophy and Non-Philosophy of Potato Salad
deconstruction.relation: Scribner uses Ginsberg's 'Howl for Carl Solomon'—and Solomon's throwing potato salad at a Dada lecture—to ask whether the Beats' performative acts count as philosophy at all. He argues philosophy is constituted by self-contestation, its relation to a 'non-philosophy' of madness and raw experience, reading Solomon's silence and Ginsberg's poetic mediation through Foucault's 'Madness and Civilization' and Derrida's rebuttal in 'Cogito and the History of Madness.' Ginsberg-to-Solomon is made analogous to philosophy-to-the-Beats: a betraying translator who nonetheless must give the mute event voice, grounded in Plato's failure to banish the poets from the Republic.

deconstruction.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
deconstruction.title: From Self-Alienation to Posthumanism The Transmigration of the Burroughsian Subject
deconstruction.relation: Bolton argues William S. Burroughs's fragmented subjects—split by a parasitic 'Other Half' or word virus—are not postmodernism's dissolved nonsubjects but practitioners of a productive self-alienation. He aligns Burroughs's multiply-named, body-swapping characters (Mr. Bradley Mr. Martin, Joe the Dead) with Lacan's split subject constituted in language and with Derrida's iterable 'mark' and 'third that walks beside you' as an absent-present that dissolves binaries. Through Naked Lunch, Nova Express, and The Western Lands the Burroughsian subject transmigrates from Marxian/Hegelian alienation to N. Katherine Hayles's posthuman, gaining agency by extending into its technologized environment.

deconstruction.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
deconstruction.title: William Burroughs as Philosopher From Beat Morality to Third Worldism to Continental Theory
deconstruction.relation: Jones Irwin makes the case for 'Burroughs as philosopher,' tracing an 'impassioned moralism' and antihumanism (human as adjective, not noun) that separates him from other Beats and postmodernists. He links Burroughs's critique of alienation to Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and to Sartrean existentialism and bad faith ('there are no victims, just accomplices'), and reads the Beats' 'third force' Third Worldism via Freire, Fanon's Wretched of the Earth, and Paz. Close readings of Naked Lunch's 'Bradley the Buyer' and the sex-and-death delirium of 'AJ's Annual Party' connect Burroughs to Artaud's body without organs, Bataille's Sadean tradition, and Derrida's deconstruction of embodiment and 'distance touching.'

deconstruction.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
deconstruction.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
deconstruction.relation: Nelson argues that critics forget Soderbergh directed Erin Brockovich because they file his career under the art/commerce binary, and he uses Nietzsche's attack on the 'faith in antithetical values' and Derrida's deconstruction to expose such binaries (art/entertainment, independent/mainstream, activity/passivity) as gendered, hierarchical, and unstable. He then shows the film's real signature is a 'self-centered narration' totally focalized through Julia Roberts's Erin, so that a tension between the movie's altruistic content and its Erin-fixated form never resolves. The chapter treats the binary as a rhetorically useful but collapsing tool rather than a real opposition.

deconstruction.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
deconstruction.title: 7. Saul Goodman Stands Before the Law
deconstruction.relation: Haven reads Jimmy's transformation into Saul through Kafka's parable 'Before the Law' as interpreted by Derrida. Like Kafka's man from the country waiting at a gate made only for him, Jimmy stands before 'the Law' as an inaccessible, self-deferring promise guarded by doorkeepers—Mike at the parking booth, Howard, and truly Chuck, who secretly blocks his job. Derrida's analysis of the secret as an unfulfillable promise explains the Law's contradictions (sacred yet petty, present yet silent). Haven argues Jimmy grasps the Law's dirty secret—that it 'doesn't exist' apart from its agents—and, unlike Kafka's man, chooses the liminal outlaw space of Saul Goodman rather than waiting for admittance.

deconstruction.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
deconstruction.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
deconstruction.relation: Riter analyzes Pride and Prejudice and Zombies as mashup literature, arguing the form requires readers to know the source while denying its prestige, so Austen must be both 'dead' and 'alive.' She uses Roland Barthes's 'The Death of the Author' to explain how the loss of Austen's authorial authority opens her text to reinterpretation and legally permits Grahame-Smith's rewriting. But she argues Grahame-Smith actually attacks a caricatured 'living Jane' of popular culture (the saintly, class-obsessed romance writer) rather than the historically complex Austen, noting his inconsistency in celebrating the class-conscious zombie-slayer Lady Catherine while mocking Mrs. Bennet for the same class focus.

deconstruction.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
deconstruction.title: GARDENING
deconstruction.relation: Shapiro argues that Frederick Law Olmsted's Central Park is a major artwork realizing a 'pragmatic picturesque,' and reads the English picturesque garden as a 'diagram' (in Foucault's and Deleuze's sense) of the glance—the roving, liberated look—explicitly contrasted with Bentham's Panopticon, the diagram of the objectifying gaze. Using Derrida's paradox of the frame, he shows the picturesque hides its boundary (the ha-ha) while Olmsted inverts the diagram, making the frame explicit and admitting the city so citizens meet in democratic 'gregarious' recognition—a Platonic argument (aesthetic education in the Republic) turned pragmatic in the climate of Peirce, James and Dewey. Christo and Jeanne-Claude's 'The Gates' distills the park's diagram as a gift of time.

deconstruction.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
deconstruction.title: Making Monsters The Philosophy of Reproduction in Mary Shelley's Frankenstein and the Universal Films Frankens
deconstruction.relation: Hall reads Shelley's Frankenstein and the 1931 film and its 1935 Bride sequel through Luce Irigaray's Speculum, arguing that Victor's and Walton's quests for a whole, self-sufficient identity enact a patriarchal desire to reproduce sameness and deny the 'maternal waters,' with women reduced to mirrors that will not reflect. She uses Lacan's mirror stage and the camera's power over sight to explain how identity is fixed by being seen, and Derrida's 'Structure, Sign and Play' to recast identity as a perpetually rewritten, misshapen text. The Bride's refusing scream and the exploding phallic tower mark female desire as a negating power that disrupts patriarchal reproduction.

deconstruction.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
deconstruction.title: index
deconstruction.relation: This composite chapter argues philosophy through several comics. Jeremy Barris pairs Plato's dialogues with Amazing Spider-Man, using the allegory of the cave, the Forms, and Platonic love/eros to show that Spider-Man's bodily beauty, awkwardness, and self-trivializing irony draw readers toward goodness the way Plato says lust for beautiful bodies leads the soul upward to truth. Iain Thomson reads Moore and Gibbons's Watchmen as a 'deconstruction of the hero,' running Rorschach, Ozymandias and Dr. Manhattan through Nietzsche's Ubermensch and 'do not throw away the hero in your soul,' Heidegger's authentic 'choosing one's hero' and the uncanny, Kierkegaard's knight of faith, and Baudrillard's idea that an extreme realization destroys its own idea. Laura and Paul Canis read Daniel Clowes's Ghost World through Sartre's existentialism: Enid's post-high-school 'three o'clock' limbo enacts thrownness, abandonment, radical freedom and the flight from it into bad faith, contrasting Enid's authentic self-creation with Rebecca's settled conformity. Aldo Regalado's essay treats Tarzan, Superman, Captain America and the Black Panther as responses to modernity and race.

deconstruction.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
deconstruction.title: 70. Jerry Seinfeld as Philosopher The Assimilated Sage of New Chelm
deconstruction.relation: Stern and Gimbel argue that Seinfeld's observational comedy is 'neo-Talmudic': like the rabbis who interpret the fixed text of the Torah, Seinfeld takes an accepted 'given' (shared phenomenological experience, e.g. the milk bit) and generates surprising wisdom by viewing it from an oblique angle. They read Seinfeld's outsider vantage through Du Bois's double consciousness (the assimilated Ashkenazi Jew who sees through two lenses at once) and invoke Derrida's differance as reintegrating Jewish pluralist epistemology into Western thought, with Nietzsche's slave-revolt as an analogy for how Jewish philosophy was made invisible. The sitcom Seinfeld, by contrast, is cast as the modern 'Chelm' joke cycle, parodying that same neo-Talmudic reasoning by pushing local logic (Elaine's Jujyfruits, Schindler's List) into absurdity.

binary-oppositions.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
binary-oppositions.title: Possibilities of Postmodern Education Beyond Control
binary-oppositions.relation: Toby Daspit reads Season Four as a drama of postmodern education: the Initiative's will to master and dissect — Walsh's Frankenstein-project Adam, who murders a boy to see how he works, fulfilling Wordsworth's 'we murder to dissect' — embodies the Cartesian split and the Hegelian drive to negate the other, while Buffy's world deconstructs fixed identity (Darla reversing the horror-movie opening, the Faith/Buffy body swap in 'Who Are You?', Jonathan's 'Superstar') and thwarts prophecy's metanarrative in 'Prophecy Girl.' Against modernist schooling's 'controlled circumstances' and Freire's banking model (Professor Riegert ejecting Buffy from class, Walsh's transmission lectures), the show models knowledge as collective work — the Scoobies' research sessions in Giles's library, Giles's fluid mentorship versus Kendra's by-the-book training, and the relational magic of 'Primeval' — offering education beyond control in an emergent, postmodern world.

binary-oppositions.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
binary-oppositions.title: A Political Philosophy of Vampires
binary-oppositions.relation: Phillip Cole takes Rousseau's remark that the eighteenth-century vampire epidemics had complete legal proof - the Arnold Paole exhumations - and argues Rousseau's real point was political: authorities manufacture imaginary monsters, as in the witch craze, to exploit fear and hold power over their own populations. Freud's account of the uncanny explains why the horror is not death itself but the returning dead (the watching eyes of Scratchy in Itchy and Scratchy, versus the serene corpses of Six Feet Under, whose absurdity the show meets with wry amusement), and Julia Kristeva's abjection explains the corpse as the ultimate boundary-breaker. The vampire then resurfaces as the demonized outsider - Stoker's Dracula coded as the unassimilated Jewish immigrant, today's terrorist - exposing political borders as arbitrary fabrications. Buffy completes the collapse of the us/them binary: Angel and Spike join the slayer, and the most shocking killings (Faith's accidental human kill, Warren's stray bullet hitting Tara) are all too human, so the real subject of border policing is the community's own members.

binary-oppositions.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
binary-oppositions.title: The Verdict
binary-oppositions.relation: Turner runs an ethical audit of iPod use through Levinas's face-to-face: sharing one iPod with his wife forces 'musical justice' negotiations (veto power over a Motörhead cut, gnashing through Bette Midler), his toddler son's listening requires vigilance, and illegal downloading fails Levinas's test that morality begins by ceding 'my place in the sun' to the Other — hence Radiohead's pay-what-you-want release as the Levinasian move, and iPod cafés where strangers DJ for each other while language preserves alterity. Heidegger supplies the counterweight: the shuffle's 'openness to mystery' versus calculative mastery that reduces The Who's Tommy to the 'Pinball Wizard' riff and silences all non-digital media, just as Kant's conditions of possible experience (space, time) would silence things outside them. Derrida's point that categories contain traces of what they exclude illuminates unclassifiable marginal works — bluegrass Pink Floyd, San Francisco Symphony plays Metallica — and the verdict closes with Hölderlin's 'where danger is, grows the saving power also', exiting Plato's cave by thinking the iPod's ethics at all.

binary-oppositions.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
binary-oppositions.title: The Postmodern Condition
binary-oppositions.relation: Rafe McGregor claims The Hound of the Baskervilles is not a detective story at all: the hound that never bites anyone and Holmes's failure to foresee fog on Dartmoor are, via Derrida's Of Grammatology, the aporia and re-mark where the mystery-horror hierarchy of the text deconstructs. He then applies Noel Carroll's philosophy of horror, the phosphorus-painted hound as a category-crossing monster producing fear plus disgust and Grimpen Mire as horror geography, to reclassify the novel as gothic horror alongside Frankenstein, Jekyll and Hyde and Dracula. The final section ties the book's enduring mass appeal to the postmodern condition, tracing the collapse of certainty from Nietzsche's prophecies about the end of Christian values to Derrida's claim that truth is never finally available, leaving anxiety as the novel's real engine.

binary-oppositions.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
binary-oppositions.title: Flowers
binary-oppositions.relation: Reads the Flowers album's blooms as dark—'Ruby Tuesday' can't be chained to a life where nothing's gained, and the heliotrope becomes Derrida's figure for philosophy forever turning toward its conceptual sun of truth, knowledge, or the good. That heliotropic bias, the metaphysics of presence, is illustrated by Augustine's treatment of evil as mere privation of good, which Nietzsche's genealogy of slave morality overturns by deriving good and evil from the same source, 'beyond good and evil.'

binary-oppositions.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
binary-oppositions.title: Out of the Cave
binary-oppositions.relation: Traces the light-versus-darkness metaphor tradition from Plato's cave and Socrates' unexamined life through medieval 'illumination' and the Enlightenment to St. Paul's glass darkly, then lets Nietzsche ('shadow is as needful as light') and Derrida's deconstruction of presence/absence oppositions overturn it. The Stones do the same work in song: 'Just as every cop is a criminal, and all the sinners saints' in 'Sympathy for the Devil,' with 'Here Comes the Sun' overturned by 'Paint It Black' and 'Let It Be' by 'Let It Bleed.'

binary-oppositions.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
binary-oppositions.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
binary-oppositions.relation: William McGinney argues Jerry Goldsmith's modernist score, with its twelve-tone themes, ostinati, cuica, slide whistle, and ram's horn, carries no inherent meaning but acquires it through learned associations: its dissonance recalls Cold War modernist concert music promoted as the high art of Western freedom, while its Stravinsky-like rhythms and 'primitive' timbres mark the apes as other and feed the film's deconstruction of the human-ape, advanced-primitive, civilized-barbaric oppositions. Because Taylor is given no heroic music, the score undercuts identification with him as an anti-hero, and its modernist associations implicate the technocratic, militarized West he represents in Earth's self-destruction. The chapter's machinery is the semiotic view of Kant, Adorno, Cage, Peirce, and Saussure: music modifies a film's images the way adjectives modify nouns.

binary-oppositions.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
binary-oppositions.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
binary-oppositions.relation: Caroline Mosser treats the creature's tragedy as humanist prejudice rather than necessity: the blind De Lacey accepts the eloquent creature sight unseen, so he passes Alan Turing's test, and only the sighted family's terror at his body rejects him - bias against the artificial, not reason. She reads the creature's development through fire, language, and revolution as Rousseau's progression from natural innocence to corruption by society, and Donna Haraway's cyborg as the figure he prefigures: an unfaithful illegitimate offspring who rebels against his father and undermines patriarchal Western self/other dualisms. The chapter concludes that society cannot accept enhanced or posthuman beings until it finds a middle ground beyond its binary grids of good/bad and Self/Other, since otherwise any new life we create will be Othered, hated, and oppressed like Frankenstein's.

binary-oppositions.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
binary-oppositions.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
binary-oppositions.relation: Michael Mendelson rereads James Whale's 1931 Frankenstein as a metaphysics of appearance versus reality: the seemingly monstrous creature killed Fritz only after Fritz tormented him with fire and the whip, killed Dr. Waldman while Waldman was trying to dissect him alive, and drowned Maria in innocent play, expecting her to float like the flowers they had been throwing. The 'criminal brain' was Fritz's accident and explains less than we assume, since the creature spares Henry's fiancée when she screams and faints. The real point is alterity: otherness is a relation, not a property, and individual and social identity are built by excluding an outside where monsters reside - so the horror was inside the well-ordered village all along, the monster is us, and we are its creators.

binary-oppositions.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
binary-oppositions.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
binary-oppositions.relation: Jessie Dern uses Derrida's Rogues and The Animal that Therefore I Am to show that naming is power: Victor cries 'Devil!' before the creature has done anything, and labels like 'monster,' 'rogue,' and 'animal' are performative verdicts that reveal the labeler, who secures his own goodness by negating the Other, more than the labeled. The novel multiplies the pattern, from Justine's confessor making her 'think that I was the monster that he said I was' to Elizabeth's 'men appear to me as monsters thirsting for each other's blood,' while Victor, guarding his self-image, becomes the monster himself. Against the Nietzsche epigraph about fighting monsters, the chapter closes with Derrida's playful self-application ('the animal that therefore I am') as the move the creature never gets to make: contesting the label and claiming a name and a self.

binary-oppositions.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
binary-oppositions.title: Walker Bite. Differentiating the Dead
binary-oppositions.relation: Di Bernardo argues that the swarm of names for the undead - walkers, roamers, lurkers, biters, empties, geeks - shows the world does not carve itself into pre-existing essences: communities construct their own classifications, as when Alice mocks Rick's group's roamers/lurkers taxonomy ('They all bite. Biters makes a ton more sense') and titles like 'Governor,' 'The Kingdom,' and 'Jesus' are disavowed by their bearers. Naming is a conferral of power that reveals the namers, since without absolute authority every name is a self-authorized exercise of power. Finally the living dead destabilize the strict living/dead opposition, and Rick's dogmatic 'us against them' slips into his own admission 'We are the Walking Dead!', with painful ethical consequences for how we police inclusion and exclusion in our world.

binary-oppositions.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
binary-oppositions.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
binary-oppositions.relation: Donovan and Richardson read the Maltusian split, with the male Guardians banning emotion through the Book of Oa on Oa and the female Zamarons leaving to found the violet light of love on Zamaron, as the Western association of men with reason and women with emotion. They deploy Gilligan's different-voice reply to Kohlberg, the Pythagorean table of opposites via Genevieve Lloyd, Hegel's exclusion of women from the public sphere, and Jaggar's liberal-feminist critique of 'ahistorical' reason, whose comic-book analogue is the third law banning relationships between Lanterns. The chapter ends by arguing the standoff is a false dichotomy the comics themselves begin to dissolve: Kyle's 'Lanterns with heart' speech to the Guardians, the repeal of the third law, and the Indigo Tribe's plan to recombine the seven corps into the white light of creation.

binary-oppositions.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
binary-oppositions.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
binary-oppositions.relation: Donavan Muir argues Lost's narrative world, unlike Jane Eyre's, requires its own metaphysics, and that this metaphysics is an order of balanced binary oppositions: Jacob and the Man in Black as twins diverged at birth, the cave scale's light and dark stones that Locke knocks out of balance in 'The Substitute,' science/faith, with characters like Jack converting from one pole into its opposite. The proper model is the yin-yang in motion - the Tao as a balanced ontological flow in which interdependent opposites wax and wane - so that treating the poles as independent is the delusion that threatens the island's order. The finale, where both Jacob and the Man in Black cease to exist and the castaways are freed, enacts the Mahayana Buddhist Middle Way: enlightenment as letting go of rigid oppositions that interdependence double-negates.

binary-oppositions.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
binary-oppositions.title: Notes
binary-oppositions.relation: Pits Donna Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto against Star Trek's horror of the Borg, reading Locutus/Picard, Hugh, and Seven of Nine as tests of the Federation values of autonomy, individuality, and authenticity against the rival Borg values of heteronomy, collectivity, and simulation. Picard's "My culture is based on freedom and self-determination" exchange with the Borg, Hugh's discovery of his name and first-person "I", and Seven's tug-of-war with the Borg Queen in "Dark Frontier" dramatize what assimilation threatens. The chapter then defends a Haraway-inspired feminist reboot: women and minorities were long denied autonomy, individuality, and authenticity by prejudice and stereotype (Seven still must look "warp-core hot" in her catsuit), the human/machine and man/woman binaries were always false, and since we already live as cyborgs of apps, implants, and networks, resistance was negligible - the real Borg problem is their violent means, not their values.

binary-oppositions.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
binary-oppositions.title: Mea culpa
binary-oppositions.relation: Correcting her own initial dismissal of the show as Nancy Drew redux, the author argues Neptune is structured by a white/Hispanic racial binary laid over the millionaire/work-for-millionaires class binary, enforced through Logan's 'spic and span' jab at Weevil, Mr. Daniels's 'pumping his gas' insult, and the 'coconut' label for Latinos who cross over. Borrowing Saussure's binary oppositions and de Beauvoir's account of how a dominant group constructs a stigmatized Other, she shows the 09-ers defining themselves against everyone else, with teacher Daniels quietly siding with wealth against both boys. Bourdieu's cultural capital then explains why Wallace (basketball, scholarship, colorblind friendships) can cross boundaries that leave Weevil working as a janitor, and she concludes the show keeps race admirably visible in a supposedly postracial era.

binary-oppositions.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
binary-oppositions.relation: Nelson argues that critics forget Soderbergh directed Erin Brockovich because they file his career under the art/commerce binary, and he uses Nietzsche's attack on the 'faith in antithetical values' and Derrida's deconstruction to expose such binaries (art/entertainment, independent/mainstream, activity/passivity) as gendered, hierarchical, and unstable. He then shows the film's real signature is a 'self-centered narration' totally focalized through Julia Roberts's Erin, so that a tension between the movie's altruistic content and its Erin-fixated form never resolves. The chapter treats the binary as a rhetorically useful but collapsing tool rather than a real opposition.

binary-oppositions.title: The Northwestern McCabe and Mrs. Miller
binary-oppositions.relation: Deborah Knight and George McKnight read Altman's McCabe and Mrs. Miller as an 'end-of-genre' western in the ironic mode, using Frye's Aristotle-derived mythos to map the classic western's binary oppositions (hero/villain, community/wilderness, virgin/whore) and then show the film collapsing them. Against Nussbaum's and Booth's ethical criticism, which extols works that make us 'finely aware and richly responsible,' they argue irony is itself a moral stance of detached scrutiny: McCabe is no hero but a vulgar, unimaginative businessman crushed by the Harrison Shaughnessy company and shot in the back in the snow while the town obliviously saves its burning church, dramatizing the implosion of the western's moral vision.

binary-oppositions.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
binary-oppositions.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
binary-oppositions.relation: Donavan S. Muir argues that Lost deliberately withholds its metanarrative so viewers must construct its metaphysics, which he identifies as an order of balanced binary oppositions. Drawing on the spinning Taoist yin-yang, he reads the interdependent, mutually converting poles—Jack from man of science to man of faith, Sawyer from con man to protector—and the light/dark scales in Widmore's painting and the cave (Locke throwing out the white rock) as figures for a Tao whose balance sustains existence. Invoking Derrida's traces and Mahayana Buddhism's Middle Way and emptiness, he reads Jacob and the Man in Black as twins whose oppositions must be annihilated, so that only when both cease to exist in 'The End' are the castaways set free.

supererogation.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
supererogation.title: Buffy As a Watcher (of Sorts)
supererogation.relation: Jason Kawal tests virtue ethics's 'act as the virtuous person would act' (Hursthouse's criterion) against Xander's 'What would Buffy do?': Buffy qualifies as a moral exemplar with heroic actions (nightly patrols, the 'Gift' plunge) and saintly sacrifices (the 'Doublemeat Palace' McJob for Dawn), but imitation fails — Xander lacks her abilities, tastes, relationships, and pure bravery, and stripping those away one by one turns Buffy into a copy of Xander. Worse, much of what Buffy does is supererogatory (Giles: 'She's a hero... She's not like us' in 'The Gift,' before killing Ben himself), so ordinary people are not morally required to do what she would do. His fix: ask what a fully informed, unimpaired virtuous observer — an 'angelic Buffy looking over our shoulders,' never drugged into 'Beer Bad' cave-Buffy — would deem right for us, given our own abilities and commitments.

supererogation.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
supererogation.title: Aw, C’mon! Do I Have to Save the Day
supererogation.relation: Presses four objections to utilitarianism through superhero cases: a weakened Jean Grey dying to save Juggernaut's bus victims shows utilitarianism obliterates supererogation — she would be blameworthy whichever way she chose; Ares' demand that Wonder Woman kill an innocent girl to avert global biowar forces her against her character; Batman refusing to let an innocent-of-this-crime Joker die in The Joker: Devil's Advocate shows the theory sacrificing justice; and the Green Goblin accidentally doing great good by dragging a would-be mass shooter down Fifth Avenue shows consequences alone cannot make an intended wrong right.

supererogation.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
supererogation.title: Doing Things in Private
supererogation.relation: Skoble asks exactly what Jeff does wrong in Rear Window and whether his illicit snooping can generate genuine duties. Against a purely consequentialist verdict ('it all worked out okay'), he argues that knowledge creates conditional obligations - given what he has seen of Thorwald, Jeff's intervention is obligatory rather than supererogatory, by 'ought implies can' - and he weighs autonomy-respecting limits on intervening in Miss Lonelyhearts' despair. He then analyzes privacy as a moral right grounded in reciprocal legitimate expectations, concluding that Jeff violated no such right since everything he watched was on public display, so the ends-justify-the-means charge mostly dissolves.

supererogation.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
supererogation.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
supererogation.relation: Framed by Dickens's Jacob Marley, Walker asks whether Jobs deserved his posthumous accolades despite giving far less to charity than Bill Gates, and tests him under three frameworks. Aristotle's virtue ethics acquits him (character is judged holistically, and charity sits near the golden mean of open-handedness rather than being a checklisted duty); Mill's utilitarianism acquits him (his innovations maximized happiness and he violated no Harm Principle—though abandoning daughter Lisa counts as a harm); and Singer's drowning-child argument condemns him as near-morally-bankrupt for selling luxury gadgets while children starve. Kant both convicts (charity is an imperfect duty under the categorical imperative) and saves Jobs: treating the affluent individual as an end in himself, never merely a means to the destitute, blocks Singer's demand for giving to marginal utility.

supererogation.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
supererogation.title: 12. Should I Really Stop That Rhyming
supererogation.relation: Yuen uses the rhyming scene to analyze annoyance - rhyme hijacks Vizzini's attention, the Goldman/Morgenstern interruptions betray invested expectations, and fans' endless quotation is annoying through sheer repetition - concluding that annoyance is irreducibly relative and contextual. Aristotle's virtue theory supplies the moral frame: friendliness and wittiness, golden means between obsequiousness and surliness, buffoonery and boorishness, make being annoying a character flaw that damages the communal eudaimonia Aristotle takes the good life to require. Since these virtues may be supererogatory ideals rather than obligations, Yuen borrows Kant's imperfect duty to develop one's talents to explain why Inigo had to become a master swordsman - failing to hone the skill his one great goal demands would be a failure of self-respect.

supererogation.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
supererogation.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
supererogation.relation: Malloy uses the two heroes to explain supererogation - Urmson's "Saints and Heroes" puzzle of acts that are praiseworthy but not obligatory, like Batman rushing into burning buildings while Jimmy Olsen is under no duty to follow. Against the utilitarian and deontological denials that anything goes beyond duty (Singer's argument that Clark Kent's designer glasses are money he owes to charity, and Susan Wolf's Loving and Rational Saints whose lives, like Batman's broken retirements in The Dark Knight Returns and Batman Beyond, leave no room for anything worth living), he adopts Raz's view that a duty can be overridden by the moral reason of grave personal risk. Hence Batman's nightly risk-taking is a genuinely heroic choice, while Superman's powers make saving others morally required - so Batman is more truly a hero and Superman "just a good person with the powers of a living god."

supererogation.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
supererogation.title: 18. Superman the Super Dick
supererogation.relation: Modeled on Harry Frankfurt's analysis of 'bullshit,' the chapter defines a 'dick' as someone who willfully disregards others' needs, and argues Superman qualifies: he lets crimes proceed while he works at the Daily Planet or hunts vending-machine change, although the SuperBat storyline (Superman/Batman #53-56) shows a briefly super-powered Batman clearing every city's crime in a single night. Applying Peter Singer's famine-and-affluence argument - the penny that saves a life, the ten-cent polio vaccine - the chapter contends that saving at little or no cost to oneself is obligatory rather than supererogatory, so Superman's convenience-first choices make him a 'Super Dick.' Batman, who risks his mortal life seeking out strangers to save, does what he can and therefore escapes the charge.

supererogation.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
supererogation.title: 2. Just Not the Hero Type (Not!)
supererogation.relation: McCrossin builds a six-part definition of heroism (moral, altruistic, atypical, supererogatory, replicable safeguarding) and tests it on Wesley Autrey versus Captain Sullenberger and a Super Autrey thought experiment: Iron Man's engineering-based feats are refinements of abilities we share and so inspire imitation, while there can only ever be one Captain America, making Tony the more heroic. The Sokovia Accords debate then contrasts two humilities, with Stark's willingness to accept oversight more heroic than Rogers' safest-hands-are-our-own confidence. The chapter closes by explaining why we invent super heroes at all through Susan Neiman's account of the problem of evil after twentieth-century atrocities, from the Stamford explosion to Charlie Spencer's death in Lagos.

supererogation.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
supererogation.title: 12. Jerry’s Dick
supererogation.relation: Twin essays by two dimension-swapped Wayne Yuens debate whether Jerry owes Shrimply Pibbles his penis in 'Interdimensional Cable 2'. Yuen H-232 defends supererogation: like donating blood or a kidney to a Peter Singer figure, giving up the organ would be Good-Samaritan praiseworthy but beyond duty, since it would derail Jerry's life-plan and autonomy, and the artificial-heart alternative makes it optional, while utilitarianism has no room for such acts. Yuen U-964 replies that the life-plan excuse would absolve every shirked duty up to Evil Morty's massacre of the Citadel, that Singer-style obligation to aid stands, and that in our organ-short world we probably do have a duty to donate.

supererogation.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
supererogation.title: NOTES
supererogation.relation: Miles asks whether extraordinary power generates extraordinary obligations, testing Spider-Man's 'with great power comes great responsibility' against Claude the invisible thief and the heroes' reluctance. He uses Singer's principle of minimal obligation (Micah diverting the train from the infant; Claire's negligible risk in burning-building rescues; Hiro teleporting across distance) and Kant's perfect/imperfect obligation distinction (Niki choosing between saving Monica and mothering Micah; Noah Bennet lying to protect Claire) before deploying Fishkin's three 'explosion' objections: too many endangered people, too many capable heroes, and too many repeated rescues dilute obligation. He concludes the heroes went beyond the call of duty in saving New York, so saving the world could legitimately be their paid job, like lifeguards or soldiers.

supererogation.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
supererogation.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
supererogation.relation: Keeping asks what grounds the claim that great power brings great responsibility and answers through Good Samaritan ethics. Building on MacIntyre's account of human interdependence in family and community, and Mill's point that failing to aid can itself cause harm, he argues that Bad Samaritanism is a blameworthy harm-causing omission, so Spider-Man's rescues of strangers are obligatory negative duties rather than supererogatory favors. His vigilantism is excused because only he can stop supervillains, 'can implies ought' explains why his duties exceed ordinary people's, and his life-risking feats against the Sinister Six and Firelord still go beyond even what his enlarged duty demands.

supererogation.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
supererogation.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
supererogation.relation: Alloy uses supererogation — Urmson's saints-and-heroes puzzle — to separate the heroes: utilitarianism (via Singer's Famine, Affluence, and Morality, where even Clark's novelty glasses are stolen from charity) and deontology both erase acts that are good but not required, and Susan Wolf's moral saints show where that lands — a Bruce Wayne with no hobbies, friends, or life, like Astro City's Samaritan. Alloy's own Raz-style fix (requirements overridden by moral permitting reasons) yields the verdict: Batman risks his life by choice and so is a true hero, while Superman, facing no real danger, merely does what his powers make morally required — 'a good person with the powers of a living god'.

supererogation.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
supererogation.title: 20. What It Takes
