supererogation.relation: Argues Batman is more heroic than Superman because heroism requires supererogation and replicability: Wesley Autrey's subway rescue, done without obligation, outranks Sullenberger's 'just what we're trained for,' and unlike otherworldly Superman, Batman's human abilities let the rest of us imagine imitating him—heroism begets heroism, as Gordon's coat around young Bruce's shoulders helped make Batman. Batman is framed as the answer to the problem of evil in Susan Neiman's secular form: Rachel Dawes' challenge that good people do something, on the Rousseau side of the Enlightenment debate that morality must make evil intelligible (against Voltaire's refusal). Superman's overwhelming power makes relying on reason superfluous, so he becomes a symbol of what we can't be, while the Dark Knight models what we can.

supererogation.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
supererogation.title: Notes
supererogation.relation: McCrossin builds a six-part definition of heroism (systematic, moral, altruistic, radically atypical, supererogatory, replicable safeguarding) using Wesley Autrey's Harlem subway save against Captain Sullenberger's Hudson landing, and argues Wonder Woman is genuinely heroic because her mission is voluntary and supererogatory - she wins the contest to leave Paradise Island and can retire to it at will, unlike a compulsory Superman. He then uses the demoted, powerless Diana Prince era with I Ching to show her deeds stay in principle replicable, like Batman's rather than Superman's. The payoff: Wonder Woman works only as a 'super hero' who inspires imitation, which is how 'we' answer the problem of evil - why innocent people suffer destructive, ruthless evil.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
dichotomy-of-control.title: Emotions and Aesthetic Response
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Carolyn Korsmeyer uses BtVS to stage philosophy's ambivalence about emotion — dangerous passion versus intuitive sagacity — through three cases: anger as beast within and practical power (Xander's love spell in 'Bewitched, Bothered and Bewildered,' Willow's wish-spells in 'Something Blue,' 'My emotions give me power' to Kendra), grief as the one emotion no magic can undo (Epictetus's jug-and-child counsel set against 'The Body' and Dawn trying to resurrect Joyce), and love's non-fungibility (Anya's vengeance-demon past leaves her without the wider affection that makes singular love credible, while Spike's messy human history makes his obsession believable). She draws on Plato's wild-beast appetites and spirited element of the Republic, Aristotle on anger and emotional disposition as character, Kant's reason-above-nature picture, and Martha Nussbaum on art's particular cases. Finally she turns to aesthetic response: the show's comedy ('She saved the world a lot') regulates audience emotion, keeping the serial's catharsis from tipping into manipulation.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
dichotomy-of-control.title: “Control, Control, You Must Learn Control”
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Stephens reads Yoda as a Stoic sage: Luke's first impressions are blinded by appearance, but Yoda exhibits the Stoic virtues of patience, timeliness, focus on the present, apatheia (freedom from fear, anger, and hate), and ascetic discipline (askesis), living by the dichotomy of control. He reconstructs the contrasting 'logic of the Dark Side' - anger to hatred to aggression to the mastery of others - showing the Emperor as a tyrant who, unlike the self-mastering Stoic (Marcus Aurelius being the counterexample among rulers), seeks to control what is not up to him, so Vader's 'I must obey my master' is servitude to vice. The chapter also marks Stoic limits: the Emperor rightly rejects felt compassion but wrongly refuses beneficence and Stoic cosmopolitanism, and Stoic physicalism cannot accommodate Yoda's 'luminous beings' afterlife.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
dichotomy-of-control.title: Poker and Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Housel surveys a century of poker on screen — from the Tombstone Birdcage Theater's 'bird in a gilded cage' through Maverick, The Gambler, Rounders, and ESPN's Tilt with its brothel-break 'Matador' — to show women cast as eye-candy, damsels, or flukes (Joanne Woodward winning a high-stakes game without knowing how to play). Against the myth stands Annie Duke, who beat her brother Howard on the way to the 2004 Tournament of Champions title. The argument: poker rewards reading and projecting emotion, so women socialized into emotional intelligence hold an edge over macho men who suppress it — a retooled Stoicism fusing Epictetus's 'make the best use of what is in your power' with Gilligan's care ethics, backed by Nietzsche's trust in the senses and Sun Tzu's 'pretend inferiority and encourage his arrogance.'

dichotomy-of-control.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
dichotomy-of-control.title: Sometimes We Live No Particular Way but Our Own
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Matthew Turner argues that a 'Playin' in the Band' jam — the band drifting from the tune into long collective improvisation and back — models a Stoic solution to free will shared by Epictetus, Spinoza, and Chuang Tzu: freedom is not uncaused choosing but responding well within constraints, so by the dichotomy of control there is no point resenting the band when it flubs a climax. Spinoza's definition of the free thing as one determined by its own nature, and Chuang Tzu's butcher who cuts oxen by spirit beyond skill, show the band letting the music 'play them' — Jerry's 'Tennessee Jed' riff never played the same way twice — as learned skill becomes second nature. Because the Dead jam within banks (keys, mutual listening, ability) yet generate something genuinely new and transcended every genre of 1960s music where the Monkees merely copied the Beatles, the Stoic attitude proves creative rather than quietist, an analogue for living freely within our own constraints.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
dichotomy-of-control.title: “All Good Things Must Come to an End”
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Thorsrud casts Spock and Data's exchange in 'Unification, Part II' — Spock dispassionate by choice, Data longing for emotion — as a replay of the ancient debate between Stoics and Peripatetics over whether to eliminate or moderate the passions. The Aristotelian side is built from Data's emotion-chip rage while killing a Borg ('Descent'), his unfelt breakup with Jenna ('In Theory'), and Riker's defense of trust after Ishara's betrayal ('Legacy'): emotions are judgments with pleasure or pain, there is a right amount to feel, and invulnerability costs the 'emotional bonds that make us who we are.' The Stoic reply uses Epictetus's distinction between involuntary impressions and assent (Picard's fear on the Borg ship vs. the holodeck), Cicero's refusal to 'moderate' what is simply a fault, and Seneca on anger, exemplified by Spock's 'quite logical relief' in 'Amok Time', his calculated desperation in 'The Galileo Seven', and his saving the bigot Stiles in 'Balance of Terror' — leaving the Peripatetic conclusion that fortune's goods are not mere indifferents and we may rightly 'smile with so little provocation.'

dichotomy-of-control.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
dichotomy-of-control.title: Too Much Tequila, Or Not Quite Enough
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Doug Anderson reads Buffett as an 'American Stoic' — unlike his friend the Cynic Hunter S. Thompson, who dropped out and died, Buffett accepts his fated world of competitive capitalism and controls the one thing Stoics say we can: his own attitudes, 'changes in latitudes, changes in attitudes.' He leans on Seneca's advice to Serenus that wine and dreaming liberate the mind ('drink washes cares away') to interpret the dialectic of dreaming and drinking in 'Margaritaville,' 'Five o'Clock Somewhere,' and 'License to Chill' as Stoic self-renewal — the margarita even frees the singer to admit his own fault — with Emerson's intoxication-speaking poet as the American model. Excess is the failure mode: the expatriates of 'Banana Republics' who mistake the dream for an end state and Buffett's late-thirties hangover reckoning mark the Stoic middle path between deadening routine and 'too much tequila.'

dichotomy-of-control.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
dichotomy-of-control.title: Red Sox Fandom and Internal Harmony
dichotomy-of-control.relation: John McHugh uses his urge to confront Grady Little, who left a spent Pedro Martinez in during Game Seven of the 2003 ALCS, to ask how fans should govern the primal emotions fandom generates. Stoic self-command fails because Epictetus's advice (avoid caring about games entirely, focus only on what you control) would extinguish fandom itself, so McHugh adapts Adam Smith's impartial spectator: the virtuous fan imagines being watched by a sympathetic but emotionally distant fellow fan, settling on a Chicago Cubs fan who gets Bartman the way a Sox fan gets Buckner and Grady. He concludes that we each harbor a team of role-specific inner consciences, and the practical task is harmonizing the Red Sox-fan identity with our other identities rather than suppressing it or being consumed by it.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
dichotomy-of-control.title: An Enemy Lying in Ambush
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Fuller reads his teenage collapse while holding shiko dachi at his Eighth Kyu grading as a weakness of will, and argues that karate is Stoic discipline embodied. He explains the dichotomy of control through Epictetus's barbecue etiquette and the Kill Bill II buried-alive scene (only the Bride's years of disciplined training, not magic, break the coffin), then lays out living according to nature, Zeno's apatheia, Marcus Aurelius's Meditations, and Seneca's nightly self-examination as the model of askesis. Kata becomes 'a defiant stand against irrational emotion-chasing', and since only virtue is up to us, the enemy 'lying in ambush' is always internal: ourselves.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
dichotomy-of-control.title: Enjoy These Moments
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Earleywine argues that Rush's lyrics trained a generation in the core moves of cognitive-behavioral therapy, an idea he traces back to Epictetus before Albert Ellis and Aaron Beck rediscovered it against Freudian orthodoxy. He maps specific distortions onto specific songs: 'Witch Hunt' on dichotomous labeling, 'Distant Early Warning' ('black and whites of youth') on all-or-nothing thinking, 'Emotion Detector' on emotional reasoning, 'Vital Signs' and 'Totem' on thoughts altering perception, and 'Subdivisions' ('Conform or be cast out') as realistic critique rather than maladaptive thought. The final step, acting on examined values and savoring the present ('Time Stand Still', 'The Camera Eye', 'Chain Lightning'), makes the songs the incarnation of their own advice: just listen.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
dichotomy-of-control.title: The Stoic Warrior
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Jeff Sharpless imagines a Spartan mourning Kurt-051 and asking what his abduction, augmentation, and endless war mean, concluding his life is absurd in Camus's sense: bred as an instrument by the very humanity he is celebrated for saving. Camus's Sisyphus supplies one answer—meaning in the defiant moment of turning back down the hill, which recasts Master Chief's 'I need a weapon' as either hollow absurdity or quiet revolt. Epictetus supplies the alternative: distinguish what is up to us from what is not, withhold assent from impressions like 'we are all going to die,' and the Chief's silence becomes Stoic tranquility—though the chapter concedes Stoicism risks minimizing the injustice done to the Spartan children.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
dichotomy-of-control.title: Time Enough to Drink the Poison
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Domino reads 'The Veiled Lodger' as a drama about hope in a world after God: Holmes's 'Your life is not your own; keep your hands off it' revives Plato's Phaedo argument that we are the gods' possessions, but deist-or-atheist Mrs. Ronder is unmoved, so Holmes falls back on the Leibnizian alternative to the Stoic and Cartesian 'patience without hope' — the example of patient suffering as 'the most precious of all lessons,' grounded in Leibniz's hope that the world is no 'cruel jest.' Jefferson Hope's two pill boxes in A Study in Scarlet literalize the Leibnizian link between hope and divine justice by letting God choose who dies, while Trelawney Hope's gullibility makes the surname ironic. Mrs. Ronder's true hope was reunion with Leonardo, which his death destroyed; what saves her is a new hope founded on Watson's text, since only a writer ('I have made a slight change of name and place') can change the past.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
dichotomy-of-control.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Curko and Greguric read Klosterman's glam-rock fandom as a problem of identity and masks: Nietzsche's Apollonian-Dionysian split casts Chuck as a self-controlled Apollonian writing about Dionysian excess in Guns N' Roses, Motley Crue, and Whitesnake, while Descartes's remark that actors wear masks to hide their shame introduces the tribute band Paradise City, a 'real copy' whose members would have no personalities left if they fully succeeded. The authors extend the mask question to Facebook and online avatars, where media saturation makes us 'copies without the original' and identity stops being self-same. They end by crowning Klosterman a modern Socrates of 'Know thyself' and a Stoic exemplar: admire your heroes like Satriani but do not steal their identities, control what you can (never your reputation or your time of death), and keep daring the endless search for self-knowledge.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
dichotomy-of-control.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Billard concedes the Stoic point that we control neither our passions nor nature ('life will always find a way', Sattler's 'you never had control'), as the bucardo cloning failure shows, but argues this proves the park rushed, not that de-extinction is impossible. Dangerousness is subjective, raptor intelligence is a logistics problem rather than a metaphysical objection, and since humans have already caused the sixth mass extinction we may have a duty to bring species back. Because revived animals would be 'neo-dinosaurs' built from fragmentary DNA, de-extinction is creation rather than resurrection, less like playing God than like the transhumanist enhancement humans already practice.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
dichotomy-of-control.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: The chapter assembles real-life versions of Finn's Enchiridion, starting with Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics: the Golden Mean locates each virtue between two vices, so true courage is knowing when to fight and when to run - cowardice and 'stupidteous' recklessness as deficiency and excess - a balance Finn's all-out bravery lacks. Epictetus's Stoic Handbook (which inspired the emperor Marcus Aurelius) teaches that happiness depends only on one's own reactions and that events are good or bad by how we take them, making it a manual even the chronically disappointed Ice King could use, while Christine de Pizan's book of chivalry prepares heroes for defeat and Erasmus's Handbook of the Christian Knight with Praise of Folly makes Finn and Jake's 'foolish' mercy look righteous. Finally Kant's Groundwork supplies duty for duty's sake: by the categorical imperative, Finn was entitled to steal the ogre's dollar only if, as an ogre who had swallowed Jake, he would accept the same theft from a hero.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
dichotomy-of-control.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Mills presents Bates - lame leg, repeated prison spells, the public fall when O'Brien kicks his cane - as an Epictetan Stoic who 'manages' misfortune by confining his concern to what he controls, echoing the Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves.' The chapter explains the dichotomy of control and preferred indifferents through Thomas's enslaved pursuit of the valet post, O'Brien's soap-on-the-floor scheme, Mary's panicked engagement to Richard Carlisle, and Mrs. Hughes's proportioning of her cancer scare, and treats death as the great rejected indifferent via Pamuk, Sybil, and Matthew. It closes with Hierocles' concentric circles: the household's best moments (Sybil helping Gwen, the staff rallying to free Bates) collapse upstairs and downstairs into one family, while Thomas's closed inner circle marks his failure of Stoic virtue.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
dichotomy-of-control.title: 4. On Being a Dead Person Who Hasn’t Died Yet
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Mark Ralkowski argues that Louis's 'dead people who haven't died yet' bit sounds like Marcus Aurelius, and that Dr. Bigelow's Season Four advice about back pain, the three-legged dog, and heartbreak works as the Stoic spiritual exercises Pierre Hadot described - above all the 'view from above' that re-describes things to strip them to their true value. Epictetus's dichotomy of control explains Bigelow's core advice: pain is not 'up to us' but our judgments about it are, so Louie should adjust his expectations to nature ('every second without back pain is a lucky second') instead of demanding a pain-free life. The apparently un-Stoic counsel to savor heartbreak ('misery is wasted on the miserable') is defended as genuinely Stoic: viewing his lost love from the perspective of a dead-person-who-hasn't-died-yet, Louie can accept sadness as precious and impermanent rather than being crushed by it. The chapter concedes Louis is no philosopher, but suggests his bits - contrasted with Seinfeld's 'polished' version on Talking Funny - can be read as newly discovered Meditations for comedy audiences.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
dichotomy-of-control.title: 5. Just Want a Shitty Body
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Bekka Williams argues that Louis's 'just want a shitty body' bit restates Epictetus's central Stoic teaching - want events to happen as they do happen, because only judgments, efforts, and desires are 'up to us' while bodies, reputations, and outcomes are not. She reads the Late Show arc (Tardigan's non-offer of the job, then Louie's triumphant 'Hey Letterman, I did it!' when Letterman stays) as Epictetus's cardplayer ideal: total effort on what is controllable, calm acceptance of what is not, alongside the bits about disgusting bodies, 'do the shit out of your job,' Jane and the mango pop, and Louis's self-trained habit of intercepting impulsive desires like the motorcycle urge. Like Epictetus, Louis is presented as a truth-teller who corrects mistaken impressions even when it is unpleasant, and the chapter uses him to rebut the charge that Stoicism means not caring.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
dichotomy-of-control.title: 3. Can Charlie Brown Be Happy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: The chapter asks why Charlie Brown is unhappy despite being kind, active, and engaged, and answers with ancient virtue ethics: happiness is not winning or approval but ethical self-transformation, so his dependence on others' regard ('How did the other team feel?') is the real problem. It diagnoses him with Daniel Haybron's three dimensions of happiness - strong on engagement but lacking attunement (nervous, self-conscious) and endorsement (cheerlessness) - and asks why his shyness so irritates the gang. Epictetus's image of Socrates playing ball at his trial and Cicero's dancing analogy supply the Stoic remedy: losing costs no virtue, what he controls is being ethical, and how you play the game is everything.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
dichotomy-of-control.title: 4. How Much Deadpool Is Too Much Deadpool
dichotomy-of-control.relation: The chapter argues Deadpool is entertaining because of, not despite, his excesses: his gratuitous violence and rapid-fire wisecracks breach the disciplined hero ideal, measured against Zeno of Citium's stoic dichotomy of control (accept the torture you cannot change, master your response) and Aristotle's golden mean between deficient and excessive force, which Wade flouts when he savors punishing Ajax instead of finishing quickly. Bakhtin's carnival excess explains the grotesque, orifice-obsessed humor that mocks 'normal' decency, and Derrida's 'internal drifting' (via Poe's Purloined Letter) frames Deadpool's first appearance being FedExed back to sender and his threshold position, where gags spill across comic, game, and film frames—making vigilante justice 'a supplement to the supplement' of law and exposing how each medium works.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
dichotomy-of-control.title: 10. Defying Fate
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Benjamin Evans reads Frank as fate's plaything, Tagomi's hydrogen-bomb gambit as an attempt to steer an uncontrollable web of events, and Hitler's claim that destiny belongs only to 'some men' as political exploitation of fate-talk. Stoicism (Zeno through Marcus Aurelius) explains Ed's serenity-prayer acceptance and the sinister Nazi version in which the 'natural order' means wolves eating sheep, but the chapter's verdict follows Adorno's studies of astrology and the occult: believing in fate seeds authoritarian submission, so Juliana letting Joe sail to Mexico — trusting her own judgment over the prophetic film — is the show's Adornian heroism.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
dichotomy-of-control.title: 15. June the Stoic
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Lequien asks how June might endure Gilead and answers with Epictetus: like the slave-philosopher, she can locate freedom in what is 'up to her'—detaching from her body during the Ceremony ('What he is fucking is the lower part of my body'), relinquishing property, and learning not to call husband or daughter her own. He tests alternatives—Camus's question of suicide (the shatterproof glass), utilitarianism (the coerced 'We are very happy'), Tronto's care ethics (Gilead smothers the sorority that could make care meaningful), and the Particicution as a licensed Two Minutes Hate—before concluding that 'Nolite te bastardes carborundorum' functions as June's Stoic mantra: mastery of her own responses is the one victory the Sons of Jacob cannot take.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
dichotomy-of-control.title: 20. Getting Your Shit Together Stoic Style
dichotomy-of-control.relation: The chapter argues Rick is at his best an Epictetus-style Stoic: in 'A Rickle in Time' his total certainty keeps the split timelines perfectly synced, enacting 'choice alone is vice, choice alone is virtue'; his 'love is a chemical reaction... focus on science' speech in 'Rick Potion #9' treats passion as an impression outside the sphere of control; and his 'don't think about it' dismissal of the Hitler-cured-cancer reality applies the dichotomy of control to an unmasterable multiverse. Epictetus's model of hardship as training is vindicated by Cronenberged Jerry, whose struggle preserves his dignity in 'The Rickshank Rickdemption', and the chapter closes with the Stoic promise Rick's life shows: not pleasure but contentment.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
dichotomy-of-control.title: Two Philosophies, Two Compasses to Navigate Life
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Against 'Hang the DJ,' where Frank and Amy's coaching system assigns partners and expiration dates inside a simulated dating park, the chapter argues a Stoic would refuse to sign up: delegating judgments to the coach violates Epictetus's dichotomy of control, and the endless date-cycle fails all four virtues, treating dates (like Amy's bored lovemaking) as means rather than inherently worthy persons. An existentialist reading via Sartre says nearly every system-arranged relationship is bad faith - couples act as if compatible against the expiry they were given, as Frank and Nicola do - and only Frank and Amy's open-ended, freely chosen relationship escapes it, so their 'fuck off' to the system is a leap of faith that 998 of 1000 simulated couples make, which is how the app computes its 99.8% match. The authors close with Camus's absurd, doubting that the real Frank and Amy, who cannot rebel against an app that tells them they belong together, will fare as well as their simulations.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
dichotomy-of-control.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Mills reads Mr. Bates, the lame, twice-imprisoned, uncomplaining valet, as Downton's Epictetus, using him and the household to teach the Stoic dichotomy of control: only our judgments, desires, and actions are up to us, while jobs, reputations, and inheritances (Thomas's coveted valet post, Mary's scandal, Molesley's flower cup) are 'preferred indifferents' to be pursued without enslavement. Death figures as the great rejected indifferent, handled through Pamuk's demise and Mrs. Hughes's calm 'One day, I will die' upon finding a lump, as well as the grief of Isobel and Mary over Matthew. The closing section turns to Hierocles's concentric circles, with Sybil helping Gwen and Carson comforting Mary as drawing outsiders into the inner circle, a Stoic cosmopolitanism that Thomas, who sees the Crawleys as mere employers, fails entirely. The Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves' serves as the chapter's Stoic motto.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
dichotomy-of-control.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Dryden asks whether the Lanterns' relationships are weaknesses or strengths. Epictetus's dichotomy of control would have recruits greet the Sinestro Corps' display of their families' eyeballs with Stoic indifference, and Kant brands fear for loved ones heteronomous; yet Donna Parker refuses the ring for her children, Amnee and Matoo Pree surrender their rings rather than stop loving, and Kilowog dines with energy constructs of his dead family, showing attachments partly constitute who people are. Feminist relational autonomy resolves the tension: Kyle escapes Parallax only by grasping Hal's hand ('we don't have to do it alone'), and Soranik Natu cannot excise Sinestro's crest or parentage any more than Donchin's Huntington's-disease daughter can sever family ties, so autonomy competency means negotiating unchosen relationships rather than escaping them.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
dichotomy-of-control.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Abigail Myers runs Stoic doctrine against Katniss's biography: Zeno's thesis that only moral goodness is good (with Plutarch Heavensbee's renunciation of Capitol privilege as indifference to wealth and status), Seneca's 'On the Shortness of Life' against deferring living, Epictetus's dichotomy of control including the uncomfortable advice to kiss wife and child as mortals, and Marcus Aurelius's practical Meditations as the gentler 'Stoic for beginners' who would be president of Panem. Katniss comes out Stoic in her frugality, her mortality-shadowed appreciation of small joys, and her firm moral code, but decidedly un-Stoic in her fierce attachments to Rue, Peeta, and Prim. Yet her final choice of Peeta over Gale is itself Stoic, Myers argues: she forgives what Peeta's hijacking made him do since it was never in his control, refuses a noble friendship that would endorse Gale and Coin's slaughter of innocents, and chooses in accordance with nature and reason so as to survive as herself with her values intact.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
dichotomy-of-control.title: Notes
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Hummel maps the Jedi Order onto Epictetus's Stoicism: philosophy as a way of life, virtue through wisdom, the dichotomy of control ('some things are up to us'), and treating outcomes like flying or other people's fates as preferred indifferents within the will of the Force. Anakin falls because he misconceives power as the ability to do amazing things - stopping people from dying - instead of mastery of his own judgments, and he refuses Stoic indifference toward Shmi and Padme. The chapter also indicts the Jedi's own un-Stoic lapses: mind tricks on Watto, entering the Clone Wars, and Mace Windu's attempt to execute a subdued Sidious.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
dichotomy-of-control.title: Notes
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Taliaferro and Beck trace a philosophy of love through Anakin: fatherless, he attaches compulsively to Shmi and then Padme, refusing the Stoic limits on control that Yoda and Epictetus teach, so that love curdles into the vow to 'stop people from dying.' Vader's fatherhood is the caricature of love - offering Luke power instead of care - until Luke's compassion and Vader's final self-sacrifice redeem it. The lesson: love must be tempered by humility about what Zeno and the Stoics placed outside our control, and broken family bonds can be partly repaired through costly self-sacrifice.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
dichotomy-of-control.title: Wildest Dreams: Stoic Fate and Acceptance (Taylor's Version)
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Argues Swift is a Stoic about fate: Epictetus's warning against handing your mind to anyone who attacks you explains 'I Forgot That You Existed' as reaching the Stoic ideal of indifference, and Cicero's physical, non-supernatural causation makes the 'Getaway Car' meeting fated by the couple's pasts rather than by stars. The determinism of 'Treacherous' ('I can't decide if it's a choice / Getting swept away') is balanced by the open future of 'Blank Space', while the responsibility objection to Stoic fate is met by Epictetus's 'it is not things that disturb men but their judgments', enacted in 'Shake It Off' and the cleansing acceptance of 'Clean' and 'Wildest Dreams'.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
dichotomy-of-control.title: Notes
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Quinn argues Rebecca is the show's Stoic: Marcus Aurelius's maxims about judgments, obstacles, and morning meetings with the ungrateful map onto her recovery from Rupert - accepting reality, forgiving as a choice within her control, the lion power pose, 'every disadvantage has its advantage' - with the dichotomy of control as her operating principle. Framed by Gen X self-reliance and second-wave feminism (Friedan's problem with no name, Beauvoir's woman as Other under Rupert), the chapter follows her from vengeful boss to mentor of Keeley and Nora, Bantr-era 'bossgirl' dater of Sam, and finally the Richmond family's matriarch.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
dichotomy-of-control.title: Acknowledgment
dichotomy-of-control.relation: William Irwin diagnoses Neptune, from the 09-ers down to the PCH-ers, with status anxiety (via Alain de Botton's Status Anxiety) and prescribes the Stoic remedy: Epictetus on the insult lying in our judgment rather than the insulter, and Marcus Aurelius, the emperor who chose serenity over vengeance, show how Keith and Veronica ground self-worth in virtue no one can take away. Sartre's 'hell is other people' and the look explain how Veronica is reduced to a dumb blonde and Duncan to a murderer until he flees to Cuba, while Schopenhauer's choice between loneliness and vulgarity frames Mac's switched-at-birth longing, Wallace's basketball-bought status, and Weevil's self-made standing as PCH leader. Irwin closes by offering the show itself as Aristotelian catharsis-through-comedy, art as therapy for the viewer's own status anxiety.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
dichotomy-of-control.title: A Friend of Humanity
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Vereb argues Geralt is at best a superficial Stoic: he lives by coin and contract, ignores Stoic justice and cosmopolitan concern, and chases neither wisdom nor the view that evildoers fit a rational Logos. Instead Geralt's refusal to choose between Stregobor's and Renfri's evils, his promise-keeping, and his protection of Ciri mark him as a Kantian who treats persons as ends and does good from duty even toward people he dislikes. Yennefer is the counterpoint, a Machiavellian fox who 'plays fair' never and uses mages as catapult fodder, while Jaskier embodies Kant's imperfect duties of benevolence and hope, completing what duty-only Geralt and egoist Yennefer each lack.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
dichotomy-of-control.title: Hardwood Dojos
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Bassham and Hamilton distill six success principles from coaches Smith, Pitino, Summitt, and Krzyzewski and show each echoes great philosophers, treating the court as a 'dojo' or place of enlightenment. Setting goals and pursuing excellence through habit map to Aristotle's eudaimonia and doctrine of habituation (Shaq the 'Big Aristotle' given the Nicomachean Ethics by Phil Jackson); the emphasis on outworking adversity and controlling only one's own effort maps to Stoics like Seneca, Epictetus, and Marcus Aurelius, as when Summitt and Dean Smith tell players to control what they can and accept the rest.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
dichotomy-of-control.title: “They Don't Pay Nobody to Be Humble!” Football's Ego Problem
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Holowchak diagnoses football's ego problem—Keyshawn Johnson's deactivation, Terrell Owens's self-promotion, Deion Sanders's showboating—as fed by sensationalism (via Dewey) and statistical obsession that pull players out of the team framework. He proposes 'Aretism,' a modern progressivist ethics built on Stoic oikeiosis (Chrysippus, Cicero, Seneca, Epictetus and Hierokles's concentric circles) balancing self- and other-concern, and on Kant's injunction to treat others as ends. The virtuous athlete competes fully while respecting opponents, sport, and the 'moral zone' of Stoic sagacity.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
dichotomy-of-control.title: Heroes of the Coliseum
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Reid draws an extended analogy between big-time college football players and Roman gladiators—both socially marginalized entertainers, controlled by coaches/editors and crowds, risking their bodies for others' entertainment. Through Roman Stoicism (Seneca, Epictetus, Cicero) she argues virtus does not depend on external wealth, status, or freedom but on accepting fate and excelling within one's role, so exploited athletes can still be genuine heroes of virtue. Following Marcus Aurelius's distaste for the games, she concludes those with power over players' unjust conditions are morally obliged to improve them.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
dichotomy-of-control.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Calhoun argues Eastwood's films move from solitary violent individualism (the Man with No Name, Dirty Harry) to what he calls 'post-Christian Stoic existentialism.' Using Epictetus's actor-in-a-play image and Marcus Aurelius on doing one's duty, he reads Butch Haynes in A Perfect World and William Munny in Unforgiven as figures 'dragged by the cart' of fate who nonetheless play their assigned role with dignity, while God is absent — Nietzsche's 'death of God.' Francesca's Stoic governance of impulse in Bridges of Madison County, Frankie's Kierkegaardian choice in Million Dollar Baby, and Walt's sacrificial community-building in Gran Torino show autonomous moral agency amid cultural collapse, with faint intimations of transcendence.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
dichotomy-of-control.title: 8. Straight Edge and How to Live the Good Life
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Tierney reads Straight Edge hardcore (Minor Threat, Ian MacKaye, the black X) as punk's answer to the ancient question of the good life: sXe abstinence embodies Aristotle's eudaimonia through habitual virtue, maps onto the Buddha's first three noble truths (craving causes suffering, so quit the booze) and the three poisons, and Epictetus's concern only for what is within our power, while Mill's pleasure-based higher/lower pleasures serve as the dissenting voice. Spinoza on being ruled by emotions and on self-love supports the DIY self-mastery of MacKaye's Dischord Records, but the chapter weighs the scene's zealotry - Rollins reading death lists, Maximum Rock'n'Roll gatekeeping and the Biafra beating - against integrity that leaves room for dissent.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
dichotomy-of-control.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Gregory and Tod Bassham argue Stoicism is the seaman's philosophy of agency, teaching a clear-eyed grasp of what we can control, influence, or not control at all. Using Epictetus's play metaphor and 'you will fetter my leg but not my will,' Seneca and Marcus Aurelius on fear, they map three techniques onto sailing: cheerful resignation (Gerry Spiess righting Yankee Girl, Shackleton's James Caird crew laughing amid the Southern Ocean), self-sufficiency (splicing lines, emotional independence on a cramped boat), and negative visualization / premeditatio malorum (practicing docking under sail, imagining lost rudders). Skip Allen scuttling Wildflower and Dinelli's endurance illustrate the trichotomy of control and freedom of mind.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
dichotomy-of-control.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Kevin Krein argues that the freedom climbers report feeling is not freedom of movement, political freedom, or free will—on those measures a roped climber pinned on a ledge is less free—but the Stoic freedom of aligning one's will with what nature allows. Using Chrysippus' tethered-dog image and the Stoic identification of human logos with cosmic reason, he claims the climber who understands and accepts the mountain's conditions and wills only what it permits becomes free, which is why experienced climbers feel freest when their options are fewest. He adds Epictetus' dichotomy of control: the mountain (storms, avalanches, one's own failing body) is largely outside our power, so limiting desire to what we control—composure, choices, effort—is how a climber stays free in any conditions.

dichotomy-of-control.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
dichotomy-of-control.title: 3. Star Trek as Philosophy Spock as Stoic Sage
dichotomy-of-control.relation: Pigliucci argues that Gene Roddenberry built an implicit argument for Stoicism into Star Trek's Spock, contra both the 'suppressed emotion / stiff upper lip' caricature and Farren's claim that Kirk is the truer Stoic. Reading Spock's talk of 'emotion' as the disruptive pathe and his 'logic' as the broad Stoic study of reason, he shows Spock embodying the dichotomy of control ('my legs, they're broken'), the four cardinal virtues, and Stoic cosmopolitanism aboard the Enterprise. Drawing on Brouwer's account of the sage, he tracks Spock's development from prokopton toward sagehood, cultivating eupatheiai like love and friendship (the Wrath of Khan sacrifice) and declaring 'logic is the beginning of wisdom, not the end.'

ockham-razor.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
ockham-razor.title: Erotic Love and Friendship
ockham-razor.relation: Maps Aristotle's three levels of friendship onto Buffy's three boyfriends: Riley is a utility friendship chosen for the rational goal of a 'normal' boyfriend (echoed by Warren's robot April and the Buffybot, which prove programmed perfection cannot be loved), Spike is a pleasure friendship driven by passion and danger that Buffy ends in 'As You Were,' and Angel is a complete friendship where each values the other for his own sake despite the gypsy curse. This lets the authors solve Aristotle's love paradox (is erotic love chosen or does it choose us?) by adding Augustine's and William of Ockham's third power of the soul, the will: an arational faculty that values the other as an end in himself, neither rationally chosen nor irrationally caused.

ockham-razor.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
ockham-razor.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
ockham-razor.relation: Noel Carroll traces Halloween's Undead imagery to the Celtic Samhain and its Catholic absorption into All Hallows' Eve, then asks the paradox: why do we take pleasure in images of the death that, as Heidegger says, is the deep source of Angst we spend our lives denying? He examines Ernest Jones's Freudian analysis - the vampire as wish-fulfillment disguising an incestuous desire, horror as the price the super-ego exacts - and rejects it as theoretically expensive, invoking the demand for simpler, more economical explanation. His own hypothesis is the 'meta-fear of fear': adolescent viewers (and aging ones) use horror films and the holiday's zombie costumes to test and master fear itself, with parody and Bergson's laughter as companion devices of emotional control - a folk remedy that needs no unconscious to work.

ockham-razor.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
ockham-razor.title: Emergentism Now Can Scotty Beam Us Up
ockham-razor.relation: Tests three theories of mind against Spock's katra transfer in The Wrath of Khan and The Search for Spock and his mind melds with Kirk, the Horta, and Rock people. Descartes's divisibility argument backs the dualism the katra assumes, but the argument from parsimony (Ockham's razor), the problem of mental causation, and the conservation of energy weigh against it; Churchland's eliminative materialism plays by science's rules but runs into Nagel's 'what it is like' objection, dramatized by Geordi failing to describe anger to Data without circularity. The author lands, cautiously, on Searle-style emergentism — mind as an emergent, irreducible feature of neural complexity, as when Nomad and V'Ger exceed their programming — while conceding Kim's charge that it may be dualism in disguise.

ockham-razor.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
ockham-razor.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
ockham-razor.relation: Johnson argues that because Zelda has no single authorial vision (teams, outside developers, cryptic Aonuma interviews), the timeline is a 'communication game' fans play together. Interpretation follows the hermeneutic circle of Heidegger and Gadamer (parts inform the whole, as when Wind Waker's references to Ganon's earlier attacks make sense of the series), faces Leibnizian underdetermination since infinitely many theories fit the games, and uses Ockham's razor, whose failures (the y=2x formula) show that simplicity is relative to a community's training, as in Wittgenstein's pupil who suddenly counts '1,004, 1,008'. Hence Miyamoto's own claim that Zelda is a communication game: designers supply puzzle pieces, and the fan community creates the meaning.

ockham-razor.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
ockham-razor.title: Is Monk’s Certainty Justified
ockham-razor.relation: Rauhut tests Monk's method against two models of discovery: Holmes-style eliminatism, modeled on Popper's falsification via reductio ad absurdum, and CSI-style confirmationism in the mold of Hempel and Carnap (Gil Grissom letting evidence speak). Monk fits neither — in 'Mr. Monk and the Astronaut' he refuses to eliminate the alibi-solid Steve Wagner, and in 'Mr. Monk Falls in Love' he ignores a hatpin, a motive, and a confession pointing at Leyla. Instead Monk is an 'epiphanist': he registers every anomaly (the secretary hired from a Lamaze-class ad in 'Mr. Monk Fights City Hall', Crawford's odd phrasing 'No, she wouldn't be drinking now'), suddenly sees the one theory explaining all of them, and only afterwards manufactures shareable evidence for others. His absolute certainty, the chapter argues, rests on a metaphysical faith that only the true theory can explain every anomaly — a Leibnizian 'best of all possible ordered worlds' — the same obsession with order that makes him notice anomalies at all, though it makes him epistemically irresponsible by ordinary standards that weigh alternative hypotheses and simplicity.

ockham-razor.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
ockham-razor.title: Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New ‘Intelligent Falling’ Theory
ockham-razor.relation: Ruiz uses Onion stories—'Jesus Answers Half The Prayers At Area Roulette Table,' 'God Answers Prayers Of Paralyzed Little Boy,' 'Christianity Celebrates One Billionth Unanswered Prayer'—to argue that belief in God lacks rational justification. Following Hume's empiricism (all ideas trace to sense perception), methodological naturalism, and Ockham's Razor, he shows that feelings of God's presence, scriptural circularity, and answered prayers (riddled with selection bias) all fail as evidence, and the prayer hypothesis is unfalsifiable—a theory that explains any outcome, like the brain tumor thanking God for its surviving surgery, is supported by no evidence. He closes by dismantling Paley's watchmaker design argument through the infinite regress ('who designed God?') and by treating 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New Intelligent Falling Theory' as the reductio of design reasoning.

ockham-razor.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
ockham-razor.title: Get Serious
ockham-razor.relation: David Kyle Johnson takes Nietzsche's suggestion that God is slowly dying and reads The Onion's religion stories — the faith healer who loses a patient during a routine miracle, Kansas fundamentalists lobbying to overturn the Second Law of Thermodynamics, and 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New Intelligent Falling Theory' — as evidence of secularization. He splits blind faith (irrational belief despite evidence, as with Bush's 'Blind-Faith-Based Initiatives') from genuine faith as belief without sufficient evidence, arguing religion does science badly whenever it shields creationism from falsification. But science rests on unproven assumptions too, he shows via Hume's problem of induction, Descartes' skeptical problem, and Wittgenstein's charge that naming a 'strong nuclear force' explains no more than God pushing things down. Ockham's razor then decides for atheism — an unexplained universe is simpler than God plus a universe — though William James's will to believe leaves a door open for faith where evidence is impossible, qualified by Clifford's warning that beliefs likely to harm others are never permissible.

ockham-razor.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
ockham-razor.title: The Future of Sandy Cheeks
ockham-razor.relation: Wilson González-Espada assesses Sandy Cheeks as a portrait of the scientist: she explodes the 'Draw a Scientist' stereotype — female, socially popular, working in an open treedome that mirrors peer review — yet the show muddles the nature of science, calling inventions 'experiments' and a clipboard of math 'science'. The chapter applies Popper's falsifiability to SpongeBob's one-sided evidence that Squidward is a true friend and Newton's principle of parsimony to Sandy's ghost scare, then closes with Aldo Leopold's land ethic, reading 'Jellyfish Hunter' and 'SpongeBob's Last Stand' as environmental parables about habitat and overexploitation.

ockham-razor.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
ockham-razor.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
ockham-razor.relation: Don Fallis proposes deception rather than language as the personhood test: following Dennett, a deceiver must be a second-order intentional system who can want someone else to have a false belief, as when General Thade lies to Senator Sandar about Ari's kidnapping, Zira and Cornelius feign muteness before the Presidential Commission, and Caesar fakes his own electrocution in Conquest. The roles' reversal makes this a test for the films' mute humans too, while Descartes's beast machines, Wittgenstein on dogs that cannot simulate pain, and Lloyd Morgan's canon voice the skeptical reading of fake alarm calls and Koko's 'Cat did it.' Against them Fallis invokes Occam's Razor over Hare, Call and Tomasello's food-competition experiments: apes track who sees what, but they fail the misinformed false-belief version, so real apes may not be 'sneaky enough to be people.'

ockham-razor.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
ockham-razor.title: Psych and Philosophy
ockham-razor.relation: Jones argues that Shawn's 'psychic' act is really hypersensory perception (HSP) - noticing cat fur, fine print, blood spatter - feeding inference to the best explanation (IBE), the natural abductive method Sherlock Holmes mislabels deduction, with Clever Hans and Ilga Kirks as real-world parallels. Applying IBE with Ockham's Razor to the two hypotheses 'he's psychic' versus 'he's hyper-observant,' she concludes the natural explanation should win for everyone: Lassiter's skepticism tracks the evidence, Gus knows better despite believing in ghosts, and Chief Vick shouldn't buy the supernatural story either. Juliet's belief survives only through background supernatural beliefs, a psychic-friendly culture, and ignoring the clues Gus feeds Shawn, which the chapter diagnoses as the same public misunderstanding of the scope and limits of science that keeps most Americans believing in ESP.

ockham-razor.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
ockham-razor.title: Psych and Philosophy
ockham-razor.relation: Guidry-Grimes treats Chief Vick's hiring of Shawn as a genuine problem in applied ethics rather than a joke: the Psi hypothesis fails Ockham's Razor and no controlled study supports paranormal ability, yet Vick - unlike viewers who know Shawn is a fraud - must weigh her obligations to victims, the department, and taxpayers on the evidence she has. The chapter argues that hiring Shawn is ethically defensible given his record of solving over fifty unsolvable cases, but it catalogues the costs: false hope for distraught families (Marc Klaas's resentment of psychic tipsters), damage to Lassiter's morale, wasted resources, and the fragile public trust bound up with taxpayer money. The conclusion is a compromise: Vick is ethically required to use every tool in the arsenal, including a successful 'psychic,' only in desperate high-stakes cases where the victim's family does not object, and otherwise merely permitted.

ockham-razor.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
ockham-razor.title: The Devil and Philosophy
ockham-razor.relation: Sharon Kaye stages a fourteenth-century debate over a contradiction: Jesus truthfully prophesied that the Antichrist will come, yet the Antichrist remains free not to. Peter Aureoli denies bivalence for statements about the future, Thomas Bradwardine has God swap among infinite possible-world 'movies,' and Ockham's follower John of Mirecourt concludes that Jesus simply lied - each solution self-defeating or heretical. Using Ockham's Razor and her comic fantasy of seducing the Antichrist, Kaye argues the unsolvable prophecy problem helped discredit prophetic religion, ushered in theological determinism via Luther and Calvin, and opened a secular age.

ockham-razor.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
ockham-razor.title: 6. The PowerPoint Conspiracy Theory
ockham-razor.relation: In a sustained deadpan parody, Ketcham builds a conspiracy out of Ockham's Razor: William of Ockham's minimalist principle explains PowerPoint's big-type bullet points, but the slide deck (secretly engineered by DARPA with Microsoft, exported via Siberia to Putin) becomes a weapon that breeds stupidity, conditions Trump to tweet-length simplicities like fake news and crooked, and finally rigs him, not the voting machines. The chapter also wields the Razor correctly, insisting that a minimalist explanation must still be good and complete, as when little Jill's one bullet point tells us too little. Testing moral realism, Kant's absolute prohibition on lying, and utilitarianism's greatest happiness against the conspiracy's missing facts, it concludes we lack the information to render any moral verdict, which is exactly what the conspiracy-minded minimalists want.

ockham-razor.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
ockham-razor.title: 7. Scott Adams’s Joy of Logic
ockham-razor.relation: Bilsker turns Adams's Joy of Work catalogue of irrational co-workers into a critical-thinking syllabus: faulty analogy (from dogs fetching sticks to potatoes dancing, and Francis Bacon's body-politic passage praising war as exercise), huge-pants faulty causation, the Reinhart-Rogoff debt paper that drove austerity policy on mere correlation until Herndon, Ash, and Pollin exposed it, complex and objectionable cause, the overapplication of Occam's Razor to moon-landing hoaxes, misplaced authority, begging the question, and egocentric biases like I Am the World. He then contrasts the classroom view that confirmation bias is an unconscious background program with Win Bigly's claim that bias is the operating system itself, worrying about the implication that reasoning with anyone is futile, and concludes that Adams overstates how incapable we are of overcoming our biases.

ockham-razor.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
ockham-razor.title: We’ve Run Out of Time… or Have We
ockham-razor.relation: The chapter argues that the film's multiverse, where sorcerers 'harness energy drawn from other dimensions,' is best modeled on the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, walking through Tegmark's Level I-III multiverses, Schrodinger's cat, the double-slit experiment, and the measurement problem (Copenhagen, von Neumann-Wigner's mind-caused collapse, and Everett's branching) to show that interpreting the formalism is philosophy rather than physics. It defends many-worlds against the objections of counterintuition and Ockham's razor, and suggests that Strange trapping Dormammu in a time loop works like a quantum experiment, with branching worlds dissolving the grandfather paradox.

ockham-razor.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
ockham-razor.title: NOTES
ockham-razor.relation: Asks how to tell genuine science from pseudoscience using Chandra Suresh's rejected Activating Evolution theory, Sheldrake's morphic fields, alchemy, and Behe's intelligent design. Kuhn's picture of normal science, anomalies, and revolutions explains why Suresh would need a full-blown crisis in evolutionary theory — such as people actually flying — before the community accepts him, and why time rather than mockery settles a theory's fate. Ockham's razor condemns the unnecessary organizing principles in both Sheldrake's and Suresh's theories, and intelligent design is exposed as bad method because, like creationism, it was devised to protect a prior commitment from disconfirming fossil and cosmological evidence.

ockham-razor.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
ockham-razor.title: 10 Fact, Truth, and Evidence A Lesson from Dr. Tyree
ockham-razor.relation: Dean Kowalski stages an imagined dialogue between Indy and William E. Tyree — Harrison Ford's real Ripon College philosophy professor, whom Ford's own script rewrite placed 'right down the hall' — to show that 'archaeology is the search for fact, not truth' is self-defeating if truth is correspondence with reality. Tyree's epistemology primer (principles of evidence, inductive generalization, hypothesis testing like Indy's Sankara-stone glow prediction, and Ockham's Razor) explains Indy's resistance to the God hypothesis despite witnessing the Ark, the Grail's instant healing of Henry Sr., and the invisible bridge he crossed on guesswork rather than knowledge. The resolution: Indy practices methodological naturalism, keeping deeper truths out of archaeology, without being committed to metaphysical naturalism.

ockham-razor.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
ockham-razor.title: Notes
ockham-razor.relation: Leuenberger argues that a LEGO MOC is a surprisingly faithful model of David Lewis's Humean supervenience: the world is just a vast mosaic of local matters of particular fact — homogeneous, arbitrarily recombinable atomic bricks (fundamental properties at space-time points) with no necessary connections, Hume's 'greater denier', versus gunky Play-Doh or jigsaw pieces. Ockham's Razor motivates the view (while also able to cut against a divine master builder, whom Lewis's world lacks, though LEGO-world builders likewise stand outside their creations), and Lewis's concrete possible worlds make every build a replica rather than a creation, answered to the 'incredulous stare' by quantitative parsimony. Four-dimensionally stacked creations model change as variation along temporal parts, while the causation objection — nothing in one LEGO creation brings about the next — marks the fundamental Humean/non-Humean divide.

ockham-razor.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
ockham-razor.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
ockham-razor.relation: Carl Matthew Johnson argues that the split-timeline versus linear-timeline fan war, settled by Eiji Aonuma's 2006 Nintendo Dream interview, is really a hermeneutic meta-game fans play on top of Zelda. He applies the Heidegger-Gadamer hermeneutic circle — the Ganon references in Wind Waker make sense only from knowledge of the whole series, while gossip-stone text about Kaepora Gaebora feeds back into the whole — then uses Leibniz's curve-fitting problem to show timeline evidence underdetermines any single interpretation. Ockham's razor and Wittgenstein's counting-by-twos rule-following example reveal that simplicity is community-relative, culminating in Miyamoto's 2007 claim that Zelda was designed from the start as a 'communication game' among players.

ockham-razor.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
ockham-razor.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
ockham-razor.relation: Curry argues that angels like Anna and Castiel can reasonably be atheists, because a higher perspective confers no epistemic advantage about God: Anna admits only four angels have seen him and the rest 'take it on faith.' Aquinas's cosmological argument, illustrated by the endless causal chain behind the Impala, yields at most an uncaused first cause rather than an omnipotent, omnibenevolent one, and Paley's design argument, an Impala in the desert implies a designer, is undermined by Darwinian natural selection, which Castiel himself witnessed ('Don't step on that fish'). The free-will theodicy fails against natural evils like famine and childhood cancer, and the principle of parsimony tells angels to expect a natural explanation for their own existence, so Uriel's 'There is no will. No wrath. No God.' turns out to be rational.

ockham-razor.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
ockham-razor.title: NOTES
ockham-razor.relation: Richard Brown uses the title 'The Terminator' itself to run the debate over definite descriptions: Russell's theory of descriptions makes 'The Terminator can't be bargained with' false (there are many T-101s, and no real-life Terminator at all), while Strawson insists Kyle's utterance genuinely refers to the machine at the door. Donnellan's referential/attributive distinction is staged through Lieutenant Traxler's 'The phone book killer has no pity' — true of whoever fits the description, or of the very Terminator Sarah has in mind — and Kripke's arguments from 'Russell English,' anaphora, and indirect quotation are weighed against Devitt's pronoun-of-laziness and reference-borrowing replies. The chapter sides with Grice's modified Ockham's razor: descriptions are not semantically ambiguous, so the title is literally false but apt, since Cameron referentially means the T-101.

ockham-razor.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
ockham-razor.title: When Life Gives You Chlamydia
ockham-razor.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones explains Veronica's casework as inductive reasoning: Occam's razor dispatches Meryl's 'space laser' speculation and identifies Gia's stalker via the simplest explanation (the stalker drove off in the pick-up), while Keith's refusal to accept Abel Koontz's confession shows the razor's limits — Sheriff Lamb's laziness being Sidney Brenner's 'Occam's broom,' whisking inconvenient facts like Lilly's body temperature under the rug. Distinguishing Aristotle's particulars-to-universal induction from deduction, the chapter teaches the probability fallacy through the Mercer evidence (clippers, cologne, and GHB make it likely the rapist owns them, not that their owner is the rapist — the same confusion fueling suspicion of PCH-ers) and catalogues the fallacies — false dilemma, false cause, ad hominem, appeal to emotion — that Veronica's jealousy-driven reasoning commits in the Sully case. The chlamydia diagnosis revealing Cassidy raped her is the final lesson: new evidence overturns even well-confirmed conclusions, so certainty is a sucker's bet.

ockham-razor.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
ockham-razor.title: 19_LaRocca_Chapter_018.html
ockham-razor.relation: Rick Altman dismantles four and a half 'fallacies' that let film theory ignore sound: the historical fallacy (sound as a late add-on), the ontological fallacy (image alone is cinema), the reproductive fallacy (recording reproduces rather than represents sound), the nominalist fallacy, and the half-fallacy of indexicality. In the nominalist section he explicitly frames the dispute over whether the 'same' sound heard from different seats shares a real identity as the medieval realism-versus-nominalism debate, casting Plato and Augustine as the realists and William of Ockham as the nominalist, and warning that ultra-nominalism about sound jeopardizes shared understanding. He uses Peirce's index/icon/symbol distinction to argue electronics has desacralized cinema's indexicality.

problem-of-evil.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
problem-of-evil.title: Against Fascism
problem-of-evil.relation: Neal King argues the Buffyverse is proto-fascist: Buffy kills demons and vampires on sight within a race-like hierarchy, tempered only by an Augustinian split between natural and moral evil (soulless vampires cannot choose otherwise; soul-bearing humans like Faith, Willow, and Warren can repent), she derives authority from an ancient calling rather than democracy, and the graduation battle of 'Graduation Day, Part Two' stages citizenship forged in mass combat. He imagines a fascist Buffyverse of 'brownskirt' death squads and concludes only the show's secrecy prevents full fascism, finally recommending that the racism be dropped but the ritual sacrifice of evildoers kept — with Willow's flaying of Warren as the model.

problem-of-evil.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
problem-of-evil.title: No Big Win
problem-of-evil.relation: Reads sacrifice, salvation, and redemption in the Buffyverse as secular myth: vampires manifest the shadow-side of the human (Liam's resentment becomes Angelus, William's repressed romanticism becomes Spike's rebellion), and the contrast between soulless Spike's genuine moral growth through love of Buffy and human Xander's arrested development shows redemption is measured by 'what have you done with what you've been given.' The Purpose of Evil section argues good and evil must stay in balance because without evil there is no free choice and hence no redemption, and Angel's 'no big win' epiphany — no grand plan, only lessening suffering one kindness at a time — locates life's meaning in the journey of becoming rather than final victory.

problem-of-evil.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
problem-of-evil.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Scott Davison asks whether Tolkien's world is Manichean - two equal forces of Good and Evil - and answers no: the Ring is not 'altogether evil' in itself but animated by Sauron's infused will, and nothing, not even Sauron, is totally evil, since 'nothing is evil in the beginning'. Developing Augustine's account, he shows evil as parasitic privation - Ringwraiths wear robes 'to give shape to their nothingness', the Eye is 'a window into nothing' - and traces evil to inordinate desire: Sam stays content with his garden while Boromir, Saruman, Denethor, and Sauron reach for more than their place allows. Evil unmakes itself (Saruman dies by Wormtongue's knife), and because goodness is the world's default, there is always hope of overcoming it.

problem-of-evil.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
problem-of-evil.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Thomas Hibbs reads the Quest's ending as providential: the Ring is destroyed against Frodo's own will at the Cracks of Doom, through Gollum, exactly as Gandalf hinted when he said Bilbo was 'meant' to find the Ring, 'and not by its maker'. Providence first appears as chance - Bilbo's arrival, Aragorn's landing at the Pelennor, Gandalf 'sent back' until his task is done - and is discerned only in hindsight as the epic's dramatic unity. Against the worry that providence cancels freedom, he uses Kant on duty and dignity (Frodo's 'I will take the Ring', Sam's 'I must see it through', set against Denethor ruling his 'own end'), while noting Tolkien rejects Kant's autonomy/heteronomy split, and with Augustine he treats evil as parasitic, able only to mar itself ('Oft evil will shall evil mar').

problem-of-evil.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
problem-of-evil.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Uses the show to argue the problem of evil is evidential rather than logical, and tests each theodicy against Sopranos cases: evil as natural-law by-product (Junior's and Jackie's cancers), punishment for sin (Carmela's cancer scare, Ralph telling Father Phil his hospitalized son is God's payback in 'Whoever Did This'), God's higher morality (rejected as meaningless as 'a triangle with four sides'), long-run goods (Artie's restaurant fire), and character-building (rejected with Melfi's 'How many people have to die for your personal growth?'). The free-will defense also fails - God could have given us Meadow-like dispositions - and Tony's 'You're born to this shit' versus Melfi's insistence on genuine choice dramatizes the debate. The chapter ends with Tony as the Old Testament Yahweh writ small: a jealous, vengeful, tribal ruler whose appeal is no more mysterious than His.

problem-of-evil.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
problem-of-evil.title: From Knowledge to Faith
problem-of-evil.relation: Lawler reads Crimes and Misdemeanors through Kant's problem of the Highest Good: Judah's unpunished murder of Dolores shows a world where the wicked prosper and the good (Cliff, the blind Ben) suffer, the scandal Job complains of, while Levy's suicide shows that a bare existentialist 'yes' to life fails without love. Kant's 'I had to deny knowledge to make room for faith' is applied to the film's two visions: the deterministic, dog-eat-dog world of science and Adam Smith's economic egoism (with Hobbes's war of all against all) is only appearance, not reality. Kant's gallows example shows Judah could have discovered authentic freedom by respecting Dolores's dignity rather than seeing 'the black eyes of an insect', and the postulates of freedom, God, and immortality ground Ben's not-really-blind faith — so it is Judah who is truly blind.

problem-of-evil.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
problem-of-evil.title: The End Is It All Darkness
problem-of-evil.relation: John Pappas reads Crimes and Misdemeanors through Glaucon's ring of Gyges in Plato's Republic: Judah Rosenthal's wealth and prestige are his invisibility ring, and when his mistress Dolores threatens exposure he 'pushes the button', has his gangster brother Jack murder her, and gets away with it. Against Socrates' claim that injustice corrodes the harmonious soul and that virtue is its own reward, the film, unlike Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, lets the murderer and the 'yutz' Lester prosper while honest Clifford loses everything; Bergson's theory of the comic explains why Lester is invisible to himself, and Rousseau's reverie about what he would do with the ring marks Clifford as the one man who might use it decently. Aunt May's post-Holocaust atheism, 'might makes right' with nothing 'handed down in stone', supplies the argument from evil that releases Judah, leaving only the qualified hope that it is 'not all darkness'.

problem-of-evil.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
problem-of-evil.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Dallas Willard defends the film's excess of violence as its whole point: it visualizes human evil as beyond the remedies of education, law, or counseling (the route Plato and Aristotle tried), with Satan — the androgynous figure carrying the smug dwarf through the scourging crowd — explaining why only Christ's non-resistant embrace of the cross can break evil's grip. Against the passive reading of 'the Passion,' he argues Jesus 'played' his judges, deliberately laying down his life to inaugurate the kingdom of God. The argument leans on the hidden God (deus absconditus): God stays hidden, contra Sartre's 'no nature' self-creation and closer to Pico della Mirandola, so that we can freely make ourselves, which is also why demanding 'more evidence' misses what belief in God requires.

problem-of-evil.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
problem-of-evil.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Paul Moser answers the objection that an all-loving God could not plan His Son's torture by arguing the cross is God's scandalous self-giving love: Jesus is no mere moral guru but the unique atoning sacrifice (the mad/Satanic/Son-of-God trilemma, 'he who delivered me to you has the greater sin'), and the crucifixion is God's grand reversal where self-giving love defeats death. He attacks the 'nice god' of natural theology as domesticating idolatry — God hides His plans from 'the wise and the intelligent' — and holds that we know God not by philosophical evidence but through Gethsemane-style filial obedience ('not my will but yours'), noting that Gibson himself appears in the film driving a nail, casting all of us as the crucifiers whom God forgives.

problem-of-evil.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
problem-of-evil.title: The Fate of Evil after the Overthrow of the Empire
problem-of-evil.relation: Brown treats Luke's 'Is the Dark Side stronger?' as the problem of evil: distinguishing natural evils (the wampa, bigger fish) from moral evils (Tarkin destroying Alderaan), he surveys the Platonic craftsman working recalcitrant matter and the Manichean dualism of two gods - the Emperor as would-be 'evil incarnate' - before giving Augustine's answer. On Augustine's free-will defense, no creature is inherently evil; the origin of each moral evil is the creature's own pride and free choice, so Anakin, not the Emperor's seduction, is responsible for his turn ('I'm a Jedi. I know I'm better than this'). The chapter ends on whether evil can ever be finally defeated, arguing the Jedi prophecies of 'balance' fit a world where evil is a permanent possibility that heroism needs.

problem-of-evil.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
problem-of-evil.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Frames the problem of pain with Hume's Dialogues (Demea and Philo) and reconstructs Lewis's answer as played out on Aslan: pain is God's megaphone that rouses Edmund on the Witch's frozen sledge and strips Eustace's dragon skin in the transforming embrace. Suffering also reveals hidden strengths, as when Aslan's pursuit goads Shasta into unexpected courage, modeled on Augustine's reading of the binding of Isaac as teaching Abraham, not God, what Abraham could endure. Aravis's claw wounds are treated as retributive punishment, tear for tear, exactly proportioned to the drugged slave's whipping, which the chapter defends via Lewis's retributivist theory against purely deterrent punishment. Because divine goodness aims at making creatures good rather than merely happy, Aslan can be both good and terrible, 'not a tame lion', since free will cannot be coerced into perfection.

problem-of-evil.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
problem-of-evil.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Observes that only Talking Animals enter Aslan's country when Narnia ends in The Last Battle, then critically examines Lewis's case against wider animal salvation: derivative immortality through human love (Sarah Smith's train of beasts in The Great Divorce), compensation of animal pain in an afterlife, Lewis's follow-Descartes claim that most animals are sentient but not conscious enough to feel pain or have a surviving 'self'. The chapter argues each point fails: the physiological evidence shows animals suffer, resurrection or God-given souls remain possible (Strawberry's transformation into a winged Talking horse), and a compensatory hereafter is still the most promising answer to why a loving God permits the fawn's miserable death. Aquinas's rational-creature hierarchy frames the Talking/Dumb divide, and the Hindu-Buddhist rebirth theodicy is considered and rejected as unbiblical.

problem-of-evil.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
problem-of-evil.title: Prayer (A Euphemism for Butt-Kissing and Begging)
problem-of-evil.relation: Argues the Pythons' religious gags perform philosophy's preliminary job of challenging doctrine: the 'every sperm is sacred' family makes God a voyeur of contraception, the Life of Brian stoning (rocks flying each time anyone utters 'Jehovah') shows blasphemy law run absurd, and 'Christmas in Heaven' exposes heavenly reward as material compensation. Deploying Socrates and Plato — the Republic's ban on portraying pettiful gods, the Apology on why the virtuous need not fear death, and above all the Euthyphro — the chapter reads the witch-weighing and the Holy Hand Grenade as the ancient problem whether acts are just because God sanctions them, and the chaplain's toadying prayer against God's own 'don't grovel' as proof that sacrifice and prayer are bargaining a perfect being has no need of. The upshot is not atheism but the Socratic verdict that the mobs punishing blasphemy, not the mocked, are the real blasphemers.

problem-of-evil.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
problem-of-evil.title: U2 and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Wrathall's introduction argues U2 is philosophically interesting because its enormous popularity holds up a mirror to what 'we' care about (by Nietzsche's test of how a culture stands toward life) and because the band publicly wrestles with the contradictions of the technological-global economy: unprecedented freedom of choice paired with loss of rooted identity, and distant suffering ('Crumbs from Your Table') that we feel both powerless to fix and responsible for. Its showcase reading treats 'Miracle Drug' as a musical theodicy: Bono's plea 'God, I need your help tonight' is answered by the Edge's guitar and by the Matthew 25:35 refrain, so science and medicine count as works of Christian charity. The piece then frames the volume's essays: Plato's ascent of love in the early songs, Kierkegaardian despair after Achtung Baby, Bono's search for authentic identity, the simulacra of 'Even Better than the Real Thing', being-toward-death in the apocalyptic songs, and the Plato-versus-Aristotle quarrel over music's emotional power.

problem-of-evil.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
problem-of-evil.title: U2 and Philosophy
problem-of-evil.relation: Merrick sets XTC's 'Dear God' - being 'just struck' that no loving, all-powerful God rules this world - against U2's laments ('Wake Up Dead Man', 'Peace on Earth', '40') and Bono's reading of the Psalms as the blues shouted at God: both share outrage, but U2 adds yearning for the redemption promised in 'the story about eternity' plus Jubilee 2000-style action against debt and AIDS. He then argues the atheistic reaction to evil cannot be reason-producing, since neither divine design nor unguided evolution would give us a faculty that 'just sees' atheism from evil, any more than one that just sees there is no plant life on Mars. If God instead made us so that outrage at evil can trigger conviction that he will make all right, U2's reaction - 'Grace makes beauty out of ugly things' - can be as reasonable as visual perception.

problem-of-evil.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
