Bostrom's single-purpose AI (the stapler maximizer) explains Ultron as what happens when the technological extension is made autonomous and limitless, which is why Stark's suit extensions must remain vetted, worthy instruments he takes full responsibility for ('That was me'). The two kinds of extension then explain the Bucky dispute - Cap's 'you had no choice' versus Stark's 'he still did it' - which the author reframes away from the free-will-versus-determinism framing toward Black Panther's point that Bucky is a victim whose agency Hydra stole.

existence-risk.title: 8. Human Enhancement for Freedom
existence-risk.relation: Koï asks whether biomedical enhancement could make humans resistant to the totalitarian subjugation shown in 1984, where the Party keeps proles too poor and distracted to think and dims Outer Party minds with Newspeak, erased history, and propaganda. Testing Persson and Savulescu's program of enhancing intelligence and moral empathy, she finds intelligence enhancement an educated gamble, since the gifted are also the most likely to embrace extremism and to start totalitarian movements, and empathy politically selective: Nazis directed it only at the in-group and even invoked it to justify the 'euthanasia' murders, while Party propaganda exploits citizens' empathy for horror stories of pre-revolution child labor. Her conclusion is that whatever capacity we enhance, the oligarchy could turn it to its own use: none of us will ever be immune to the love of Big Brother.

existence-risk.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
existence-risk.title: What Really Matters
existence-risk.relation: Margarida Hermida deploys Parfit's comparison of peace, a war killing 99 percent of humanity, and one killing everyone to argue extinction is categorically worse than mass death, and makes the stakes concrete through The Expanse's threats: the protomolecule, all-out Earth-Mars-Belt war, and the Free Navy's asteroid attack that kills billions. She rejects Miller's 'stars are better off without us' pessimism by arguing human existence is a good when suffering is fought (Belter disease and Ceres trafficking are contingent injustices, not necessities), values humanity as the only species with civilization and as the universe 'starting to understand itself', and distinguishes the desirable biological colonization of lifeless worlds from the protomolecule makers' morally objectionable disregard for native life like Ilus'. Against Phil Torres' worry that human speciation means endless war, she points to the mixed Rocinante crew and Naomi's line that the real divide is 'people who want more violence and the ones who want less', concluding with Parfit's On What Matters that what matters most is avoiding the end of human history and of rational beings.

existence-risk.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
existence-risk.title: Actual Threats to Our Existence
existence-risk.relation: Leonard Kahn takes the season-four debate between Avasarala and Nancy Gao over Ring colonization and asks who should have won. Using Parfit's extinction asymmetry, Bostrom's 'astronomical waste', and Toby Ord's definition of existential risk, he calculates that the 1,300 Ring gates could make accessible between 10^34 and 10^71 future lives (versus the Epstein-drive Nauvoo's century-long crawl to Tau Ceti), yet because using the rings risks the annihilation that befell the protomolecule's creators, the loss of humanity's long-term potential outweighs Gao's 'unimaginable opportunities' — so Avasarala's caution should have won. He ends skeptically: like Socrates arguing against the execution of the Arginusae generals, philosophical Cassandras rarely prevail, Gao was probably right that ring colonization was politically inevitable, and we face the same dilemma with nuclear war, engineered pandemics, and runaway AI.

existence-risk.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
existence-risk.title: Notes
existence-risk.relation: Walter Barta presents transhumanism as a real philosophy (via Bostrom's history of the movement and 'Why I Want to Be a Posthuman When I Grow Up') that Fallout both practices and indicts: ghouls, FEV super mutants and the Children of the Cathedral, stimpak-Mentat-Jet self-medication, Brotherhood power armor, Mr. House, the Master, Robobrains, John Henry Eden, and Liberty Prime all embody enhancement or post-humanity, and the level-up loop makes every player a transhumanist. Bostrom's transhumanist value of 'the opportunity to explore' maps onto leaving Vault 13 for the open world, but the Red Queen race becomes the game's adaptive-leveling treadmill, and C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man plus Fukuyama's 'Factor-X' warn that optimization can delete what made enhancement worth wanting - as when the Overseer exiles the too-powerful Vault 13 hero and the Enclave President rationalizes genocidal bioweapons ('No price is too high for the survival of the human race'). Existential risk (Toby Ord's Precipice, Bostrom's vulnerable world hypothesis) supplies the final warning: the G.E.C.K.'s energy is also a destruction kit, and the cycle of war repeats until post-humanity or extinction.

existence-risk.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
existence-risk.title: So, That’s It No Solution
existence-risk.relation: Rieder argues Iron Man is the one 'realistic' superhero: nothing about him requires a different world, only incremental nanotech advances — precision engineering, miniaturized computing, and carbon nanotubes a hundred times stronger than steel — already pursued at MIT's Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies. He then uses Iron Man as a nanoethics case study, pitting cost-benefit analysis (with David Schmidtz's proviso that it is necessary but not sufficient for right action) against the precautionary principle exemplified by Bill Joy's call for relinquishment, asking whether an Obadiah Stane selling 'Iron Armies' to the highest bidder is a risk we may not take even if it is improbable. He leans precautionary: we may be morally required to forgo the experiment because the world's population never consented to the risk.

existence-risk.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
existence-risk.title: 3. Darwin in Metropolis
existence-risk.relation: Springett applies evolutionary biology to the debate: natural selection, fitness (Batman edges it by one child, Damian Wayne), morphospace reasoning, and biological altruism, which technically Batman satisfies better since invulnerable Superman cannot lower his own fitness. But judged as an effective helper at species scale — Gould's catastrophes, asteroids, alien invasions — Superman protects the fitness of the whole species and planet where Batman guards one city, so a closing three-premise argument crowns Superman the superior Superhero, and his habit of saving the less fit makes him a living counterexample to Social Darwinism.

existence-risk.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
existence-risk.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
existence-risk.relation: Theodore Schick treats the Rings of Power as an allegory-free meditation on externalized 'potency,' applying it to emerging genetics, nanotechnology, and robotics. He contrasts the Council of Elrond's choice to destroy the Ring with Boromir's wish to wield it, and with Bill Joy's call to relinquish dangerous research versus Drexler's promise that nanotech could end poverty and disease. Schick argues our situation differs from Middle-earth because the knowledge cannot be un-forged, so grassroots social taming, not destruction of a single artifact, is the realistic response to knowledge-enabled mass destruction.

existence-risk.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
existence-risk.title: 21. Black Mirror as Philosophy A Dark Reflection of Human Nature
existence-risk.relation: The chapter asks whether Black Mirror condemns technology or human nature, and argues for the latter: the 'black mirror' reflects the viewer's character. It tests and rejects the reading of the show as depicting Bostrom-style existential risk or superintelligence (via 'Metalhead' and 'San Junipero') and rejects that Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind coupling (the 'grain' in 'The Entire History of You,' 'Arkangel,' 'Crocodile') destroys human identity. Drawing on Frankfurt School critique—Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man—and Plato's and Aristotle's natural-versus-artificial distinction, it concludes technology is an agency-less imitation that magnifies preexisting human vices, and closes with Benjamin's reproducibility thesis and Bandersnatch's interactivity to suggest the show can prompt viewers to confront their own darkness.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Gregory Bassham distills six keys to happiness from Tolkien's hobbits and elves: delight in simple pleasures (Epicurus on natural pleasures, Thoreau's Walden simplicity), making light of troubles (Sam's star above Mordor, with Marcus Aurelius and Augustine on courage and hope), friendship (Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics read against Sam, Merry, and Pippin refusing to let Frodo go alone), good character, beauty and creativity (Lothlórien versus Mordor, 'flow'), and wonder (Tom Bombadil, Frodo's 'recovery' of fresh vision at Cerin Amroth). He argues Tolkien thereby becomes a philosophical guide, pointing from the Shire and Rivendell to a richer, more joy-filled life.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Argues ancient ethics explains why Tony, who has 'the world by the balls', still feels like a loser. Plato's Republic diagnoses him as a 'civil war' of unintegrated motivations (loving father and murderer at once, as in 'College'), a condition power over others only worsens; Aristotle teaches that happiness is activity with self-sufficient, integrated desires rather than a list of possessions, and Epicurus's 'sober reasoning' is the therapy Tony never gets. The Hawthorne quotation Tony reads in 'College' and his Gary Cooper ideal from 'The Happy Wanderer' frame the point: Cooper in High Noon is unmesswithable because he does not need vengeance, whereas Tony's compulsive revenge shows the world has the grip on him.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
epicurean-pleasure.title: Our Problems with Wisdom
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Diagnoses why we distrust wisdom: unlike the Epicureans, who trained themselves to discern real pleasure beyond immediate sensation — as Spider-Man's self-discipline wins pleasures Peter Parker could not otherwise know — we equate happiness with pleasant sensory experience; and unlike our ancestors, who saw the passions as external forces undermining freedom (Spinoza's bondage of the emotions), we follow Freud's steam-engine model in treating emotional expression as the true self. Material abundance now satisfies the small picture, making skepticism about the larger picture feasible — though, with Socrates, the chapter doubts it has made us any happier.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Devin Brown uses Eustace, who dodges work on Dragon Island until he wakes as a dragon and discovers he would rather be hungry among human friends than comfortable alone, to contrast Epicurean hedonism and Tom Sawyer's work-avoidance with Mill's higher pleasures and the 'Sherlock Holmes philosophy of work.' Weighing Aristotle's contemplative life against Lewis's love of quests, he reads Father Christmas's tailored gifts and 'everyone must do what he can do best' as an Acorn Philosophy of Vocation with a Marxian 'from each according to his ability' echo, condemns wrong livelihoods like Governor Gumpas's slave trade, and closes on leisure and Aristotle's golden mean, which Lewis turns into 'golden extremes.'

epicurean-pleasure.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
epicurean-pleasure.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Over an evening at the Iron Post biker bar, Auxier maps four habitues onto the Hellenistic schools: Cowboy, the Vietnam chopper pilot whose bar is a Garden of modest pleasures, loyalty, and withdrawal from power games, is an Epicurean; the laconic Bear, who doubts that even possessing knowledge would make us better off and suspends judgment, is a Pyrrhonian (unlike the coffee-house Carneadean); Happy Jack, the 'true nature's child' of 'Born to Be Wild' who defies convention and keeps nothing six months, is Diogenes's Cynic; and Gary, the Vietnam-damaged recovering alcoholic, is a damaged Stoic who has not reached apatheia. He concludes that bikers are postmodern pagans whose philosophy is enacted rather than propounded, a Biker Platonism that refuses the Christian-Platonic divorce of body and spirit and lives by honor, freedom, and a pagan fatalism that accepts the consequences of one's choices.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
epicurean-pleasure.title: That’s His Story and He’s Stickin’ to It
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Aaron Pratt places Buffett's 'island escapism' in the lineage of the ancient 'graceful life' philosophies: like Diogenes the Cynic, Buffett flouts social convention (pirates over Civil War generals, the beach over the rat race, 'Be good and you will be lonesome'), and like Epicurus he preaches pleasure with prudence rather than mere indulgence. 'Cheeseburger in Paradise' becomes Epicurus's command to know what you want and go get it, while the hung-over confession of 'Margaritaville' — 'I know it's my own damn fault' — supplies the Epicurean proviso that overindulgence ruins the pleasure it promises. The chapter closes by arguing that counter-cultures like Parrotheadism carry built-in safety features: careers and families force Epicurean prudence, keeping escapism a periodic liberation rather than social collapse.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
epicurean-pleasure.title: Hope
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Beck reads Snakes & Arrows as popular Epicureanism delivered by Lucretius' method: just as De Rerum Natura puts honey on the rim of the cup so Romans swallow philosophical medicine disguised as poetry, Rush's melodies smuggle reflection on pain, luck, and religion past listeners who think they are just rocking, with repeated choruses doing the work of Epicurean prolepsis. The random swerve of atoms explains 'The Larger Bowl''s unequal fortunes ('Some are blessed and some are cursed'), while the shore-watcher's relief at another's shipwreck and the concertgoer's pleasure exemplify Epicurean ataraxia. 'Faithless' and 'Armor and Sword' ('Pray and pass the ammunition') echo Lucretius' trampling of superstitious religio, and the chapter closes with Philodemus' Herculaneum scroll: don't fear god, don't worry about death.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
epicurean-pleasure.title: A Rolling Stone Gathers . . . Happiness
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Brings in Epicurus, speaking through Cicero, to correct the Cyrenaics: pursue pleasure rationally, declining pleasures that purchase greater later pains—Keith's drug-related legal bills, 'Sister Morphine's' desperation—and sometimes enduring pain for greater pleasure later, like kicking junk to enjoy raising children. Advocating simple living, a hierarchy of pleasures ranked by sober reasoning, and prudence (phronesis) as the chief virtue, it pictures modern Epicureans at a rock festival passing out condoms and running the needle exchange.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
epicurean-pleasure.title: Now I Need You More than Ever
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Finds Epicurean confirmation in two songs: 'Let's Spend the Night Together,' where thwarted desire exacts bodily suffering ('tongue's getting tied... mouth's getting dry'), and 'Sister Morphine'—first written and recorded by Marianne Faithfull—where a dying addict is too weak to drag himself across the floor for the drug that is killing him. In both, pleasures bring pains so bad they can outweigh the goodness of the pleasure sought.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
epicurean-pleasure.title: Can You Always Get What You Want
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Considers the escape route that would save the Cyrenaics: perhaps the pain in the songs is merely the frustration of not attaining pleasure, not a cost of pleasure itself, in which case the Epicurean advice to prefer simple, easy pleasures stands. Weighing song-as-fiction against the documented hedonism of Jagger (seven children by four women) and Richards (five drug trials), it concludes such men do not lack access to pleasure, so the nagging unhappiness in the songs genuinely tells against Cyrenaic hedonism.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
epicurean-pleasure.title: Satisfaction
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Delivers the verdict: Cyrenaic hedonism has been well tried by the Rolling Stones and clearly is not an effective road to happiness, so the Epicurean modification deserves its shot—keep the dedication to bodily pleasure but let prudence filter choices by their consequences. 'Waiting on a Friend' (choosing a friend over the game of 'making love and breaking hearts') and Exile's 'Happy' suggest the band already leans toward tempered hedonism and real satisfaction.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Devil and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Clint Jones argues LaVey's Satanic Bible rests on a misreading of Epicurus: genuine Epicurean hedonism is not limitless indulgence but the ordered life of the Tetrapharmakon - don't fear gods or death, the good is easy to get, pain is endurable - together with the threefold division of desires, which reserves constant gratification for natural and necessary things like water, bread, and friendship. By licensing gluttony and every whim so long as no one else is hurt, LaVeyan Satanism fails as the pleasure-as-virtue philosophy it claims to revive, leaving its followers with base, unfulfilling pleasures that are, well, Hellish.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Devil and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Magus Peter Gilmore, High Priest of the Church of Satan, reads pop culture's turn to villains - Loki outshining Thor, Ledger's Joker, Hellboy, Man of Steel's killing Superman - as the mainstream finally arriving at the Satanist party, since LaVeyans always used Satan as a symbol of self-deification ('I-theist') and carnal pride. He answers Pitkänen that Satanism needs no 'higher knowledge' and cannot include theists, and he answers Jones by citing the Satanic Bible chapter 'INDULGENCE... NOT COMPULSION': LaVey taught self-controlled indulgence and rational self-interest, not reckless abandon, and Epicurean moderation is no basis for dismissing him.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Devil and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Clint Jones answers Magus Gilmore by conceding he judged only The Satanic Bible but arguing that is the right target: even if LaVey later refined his views, he never retracted the book's Epicurean pretensions, and naming his system Epicurean is itself an appeal to an intellectual forebear. Since LaVey 'plundered' his sources - cherry-picking 'pretty gemstones rather than weightier keystones' - the foundation of Satanism remains shaky, and a Garden of Eden stripped of its Judeo-Christian trappings, Jones adds, was already a remarkably Epicurean life.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Devil and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Magus Peter Gilmore closes the exchange: LaVeyan Satanism honestly embraces the selfishness most people already live by (sharing Ayn Rand's enshrined self-interest), and Epicurus's own letters to Menoeceus - on not fearing death, choosing the most pleasant over the longest life, pragmatic justice, and the need for natural science - show deep congruence with LaVey. Against Pitkänen on Eastern religions, whose reincarnation and karmic debt he reads as denigration of carnal existence, and against Jones's shaky-foundation charge (Christianity itself was a Hebraic/Hellenic mash-up), he concludes Satanists are proud 'Hell-raisers' celebrating the only life there is.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
epicurean-pleasure.title: 4. On Being a Dead Person Who Hasn’t Died Yet
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Mark Ralkowski argues that Louis's 'dead people who haven't died yet' bit sounds like Marcus Aurelius, and that Dr. Bigelow's Season Four advice about back pain, the three-legged dog, and heartbreak works as the Stoic spiritual exercises Pierre Hadot described - above all the 'view from above' that re-describes things to strip them to their true value. Epictetus's dichotomy of control explains Bigelow's core advice: pain is not 'up to us' but our judgments about it are, so Louie should adjust his expectations to nature ('every second without back pain is a lucky second') instead of demanding a pain-free life. The apparently un-Stoic counsel to savor heartbreak ('misery is wasted on the miserable') is defended as genuinely Stoic: viewing his lost love from the perspective of a dead-person-who-hasn't-died-yet, Louie can accept sadness as precious and impermanent rather than being crushed by it. The chapter concedes Louis is no philosopher, but suggests his bits - contrasted with Seinfeld's 'polished' version on Talking Funny - can be read as newly discovered Meditations for comedy audiences.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
epicurean-pleasure.title: 15. God Started in 1983
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Uses the SNL bit of a God who has been standing in a room since 1983 to argue Louis is an 'apathetic agnostic': he cannot know whether God exists, lambastes atheists who claim certainty, and thinks the question barely matters for our lives. The chapter weighs Pascal's Wager against Epicurus's four-part cure ('Don't fear god, don't worry about death'), faults Louis's 'downstairs bathroom' bit for putting the burden of proof on atheists, reads the 'Heaven' glory-hole sketch through Clifford's ethics of belief as a rejection of faith without evidence, and ends with Louie's mother's line that you have to be good to people whether or not God is watching.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
epicurean-pleasure.title: 3. When Clone Club Looks for Answers
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Maps two ancient accounts of happiness onto the two clones we meet first. Cosima is the Aristotelian: like her fellow biologist Aristotle she holds that knowing truth for its own sake is essential to human flourishing, so she demands Sarah's briefcase ("the answers are in the briefcase"), studies a murdered sister's autopsy, and accepts Leekie's offer of unfettered research even inside Dyad. Alison is the Epicurean: happiness is the removal of pain and protection from threat, so she wants nothing to do with the C-word, hunts her monitor only to restore her safety, and signs Leekie's contract for the promise that her family will be left alone.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
epicurean-pleasure.title: 15. Happy in Oceania
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Ćirić and Ćurko ask what philosophy could have done for Winston, imagining a counterfactual Oceania where he reads Walpole's line that the world is 'a comedy to those that think, a tragedy to those that feel' and learns from Julia that another worldview is possible. They present philosophy as therapy: Kant's notion of worldview (Weltanschauung), Epicurean ataraxia, the Buddhist four noble truths, Frankl's logotherapy, and Stoic premeditation of the worst as resources for reworking the beliefs that made Winston live in fear. The Party's true target, they argue, is critical thinking — from Dewey's ideal of education as learning to think to Frankfurt's On Bullshit — and Kant's Enlightenment motto 'have the courage to use your own understanding' is the weapon that could still defeat Ingsoc.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
epicurean-pleasure.title: 13. Rick, Morty, and the Cure for Unhappiness
epicurean-pleasure.relation: The chapter diagnoses Rick's 'Wubba Lubba dub-dub' ('I am in great pain, please help me') as chronic Epicurean suffering and prescribes the tetrapharmakos, the four-part cure. Don't fear the gods: Epicurus's indifferent atomist gods versus Rick's atheism, his panic prayer in 'A Rickle in Time', and Toxic Rick's 'If god exists, it's me' as ego rather than argument. Don't fear death, since 'where death is, I am not', though infinite replacements make Rick and Morty fear each other's death rather than their own. The good is easy to get, so booze, Eyeholes, and Szechuan sauce must yield to water, friends, and family; and the terrible is easy to endure, as when Rick stops resenting Birdperson's wedding and finally turns himself in for his family.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
epicurean-pleasure.title: 8. Philosophy and the Personae
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Randall Auxier builds a characterology of the four personae using Aristotle's methods (endoxa and aporia) and the band's wealth hierarchy as his map. The Demon is Nietzsche — an uninhibited cosmopolitan beyond good and evil who philosophizes with a hammer and whispers eternal recurrence; the Starchild is Epicurus — Paul's microtia and bullied childhood formed the detached soul that Plato's Republic ties to being a philosopher, yielding ataraxia, aponia, therapy, and disciplined long-term pleasures; the Catman has Kundera's lightness of being around 'Beth'; and the Spaceman's otherworldly detachment explains both his guitar genius and the Nazi-regalia incident. The chapter's thesis: KISS succeeded because Gene and Paul's detached, centered self-knowledge let them give fans exactly what they secretly wanted.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: O'Loughlin reads Walter biting off a nihilist's ear and the Dude refusing to walk out on league play as concrete realizations of ancient friendship: Aristotle's eudaimonia requires friends as 'second selves' whose shared activity (bowling in the friends' company) structures the excellent life, while Epicurus's Garden ordered life around simple pleasures and ataraxia, with friendship supplying pleasant memory and a kind of immortality after death. Because we moderns claim friendship's value without practicing its costs, the Dude's priorities look comic yet pierce us — and Donny's death, the Ralph's coffee can, and 'let's go bowling' become Epicurean commemoration rather than irreverence.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Rempel argues the Dude is a modern Epicurean parable: Epicurus's ataraxia is freedom from disturbance achieved by limiting desires to the natural and necessary — simple food, shelter, a few friends — so the Dude's 69-cent check, whale-song baths, and contentment with four dollars ('almost five') express 'enough is enough'. Maude's easily-had, non-binding seduction fits Epicurus's classification of sex as natural but not necessary (Lucretius: choose the joys of Venus without penalty), while Walter's million-dollar ringer scheme and his 'sick Cynthia thing' personify vain, insatiable desires — 'contented poverty is an honorable estate', so the Dude may be the wealthiest man in Los Angeles County.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
epicurean-pleasure.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Kevin Fitzpatrick uses Vivi Orunitia and the self-aware Black Mages of Final Fantasy IX, who call death 'stopping,' to ask whether the fear of death is justified, answering that death harms only insofar as it frustrates a person's values, such as Vivi's morality, his thirst for knowledge, and his care for others' happiness. He brings in Epicurus's argument that death is nothing to us because the dead feel no pain, casts Necron, who wants to return all life to a painless 'zero world' because fear of death has corrupted it, as a darker Epicurean, and weighs the deprivation objection, death cheats us of future goods like Chocobo Hot and Cold, against the puzzle of when death's harm could even occur.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
epicurean-pleasure.title: “Takin’ ’er Easy for All Us Sinners” Laziness as a Virtue in The Big Lebowski
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Douglass and Walls read the Dude's 'principled laziness' as a coherent ethos and test it against the film's rival worldviews: the villains' hollow nihilism (which they distinguish from Nietzsche's will to power and death-of-God), Bunny's Aristippan hedonism versus Epicurus, the Big Lebowski's Nietzschean master-morality egoism, and Walter Sobchak's rules-worship read through Kant's categorical imperative and Locke's social contract. They argue dude-ism works as a personal path to contentment but, lacking any objective standard, cannot condemn true evil like Bunny's threatened murder, exposing its purposeless-universe premise as its real flaw.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
epicurean-pleasure.title: 2. To Eat or Not to Eat
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Barta and Miranda read Bourdain's 'good eating is all about risk' credo through Bentham's cost-benefit hedonic calculus, sorting risk/reward into Ascetic, Epicurean, Cyrenaic, and Utilitarian quadrants. They classify Bourdain's fugu-eating and drunk cliff-driving as failed calculations, his comfort-food returns as Epicurean, and his gluttonous adventures (French Laundry, Russian vodka) as Cyrenaic high-risk/high-reward living.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.title: Chapter 13 An Epicurean Consideration of Superstitions in Mark Twain and in the Good Life
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Baker reads Twain's ghost stories and superstition through Epicurean virtue ethics, which holds that false beliefs—above all the terror of death—breed empty desires that block eudaimonia. Citing Twain's Autobiography passage that 'annihilation has no terrors for me' as a near-verbatim Epicurean line, and using Lucretius and Nussbaum's 'Therapy of Desire,' she aligns Huck's disdain for a useless conscience and his rejection of wealth ('being rich ain't what it's cracked up to be') with the Epicurean pursuit of simple natural pleasures. She notes a tension: by making tall-tale-telling and Sunday-school-shirking so enjoyable, Twain the satirist spreads the very superstitions the Epicureans would eradicate, seeming to work at cross-purposes with them.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
epicurean-pleasure.title: Chapter 1
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Verene argues that cooking marks the transition from nature to culture, reading Plato's Protagoras myth of Prometheus (fire and the practical arts) and the Republic's claim that a city's first need is food as evidence that humans alone 'eat' rather than 'feed.' Tracing Greco-Roman banquets, Vico's account of Roman dining, and Brillat-Savarin's Physiology of Taste, he connects the ordered courses of a proper meal to Aristotle's view of imagination as rooted in memory and to friendship at table. He ends by mapping Brillat-Savarin's gourmandism onto Epicurus's distinction between kinetic pleasures (eating fine food) and catastematic pleasure (ataraxia, the settled well-being of good health and stored memories of shared meals).

epicurean-pleasure.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
epicurean-pleasure.title: Chapter 3
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Verene condenses the fifteen rambling books of Athenaeus's Learned Banqueters, where the character Athenaeus reports to Timocrates a multi-day banquet hosted by Larensius, threaded with catalogues of fish, wine, cups, courtesans and gluttons. He argues the sprawling work embodies dining as a two-part act of food plus discourse, and that its implicit ethic is Epicurean: Book 12's Cyrenaic doctrine that pleasure exists only in the passing moment (Aristippus) is shown to be historically superseded by Epicurus's modified hedonism, which ties bodily pleasures to ataraxia and even welcomes hetaerae like Leontion into the philosophical circle. Book 13's closing attack on the Cynics as homeless 'foul-mouthed gluttons' confirms the banqueters' preference for a regulated, prudent pursuit of pleasure at table.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
epicurean-pleasure.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Buckingham stages a phenomenology of a wasted café afternoon over three cups, arguing against a passage from Levinas's Nine Talmudic Readings that condemns the café as a 'non-place' where relaxing without obligation lets us tolerate the world's horrors. Against Levinas, he claims the coffeehouse's public 'solitude alongside others' sustains a courteous solidarity and, like the Epicurean Garden, offers necessary respite that fuels creative responsibility rather than evading the demand of the Other. He self-consciously adopts Levinas's own phenomenological method—attending to 'what is it like?'—to defend idling as the condition for responding to suffering with grace rather than grim duty.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
epicurean-pleasure.title: CYCLING
epicurean-pleasure.relation: O'Brien's editorial introduction frames gardening as engaging core philosophical questions and previews the volume. It argues that gardening promotes a good life not through hedonistic pleasure but through virtuous traits like patience and a Stoic-tinged tranquility that ancient philosophers from Epicurus to Hume prized, and it invokes Kant to cast the gardener as a visual artist. It also sketches gardens as cosmic symbols (Pythagorean ratios at Versailles) and closes on Plato's Phaedrus image of educating the soul as tending plants.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
epicurean-pleasure.title: GARDENING
epicurean-pleasure.relation: O'Brien reads Voltaire's closing injunction in Candide, 'we must cultivate our garden,' through David Hume to argue that gardening is therapy—a retreat from metaphysics and religion into the tranquility of common life. Hume rejects belief in miracles and religious 'enthusiasm' not by logic but by recalling everyday reasoning (a melon seed, not a miracle, explains melons in the greenhouse), and the gardener is the sophisticated artisan-reasoner attuned to nature's regularities. Gardening inculcates Humean virtues (industry, patience, balancing action, pleasure and indolence) and Haybron's attunement/engagement/endorsement, yielding Epicurean ataraxia; the Sisyphean gardener (Camus) fighting slugs, and Wittgenstein taking up gardening as a cure, illustrate the point.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
epicurean-pleasure.title: GARDENING
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Campbell explains why Epicurus set his school in a walled garden on the edge of Athens ('Live unnoticed'), contrasting it with the Stoics' public Stoa: the Garden was a self-sufficient community of friends pursuing ataraxia through natural, necessary pleasures and philosophy as therapy for the soul. Drawing on Lucretius's account of prehistory in On the Nature of Things, he shows the Epicureans saw cities as a decadent fall—driven by the fear of death and the gods—from a near-paradise of proto-Epicurean friendship pacts, and read the garden and the locus amoenus of pastoral picnics as a recovered golden age. Diogenes of Oinoanda's inscription imagines a future in which all become gardening philosophers and city walls become redundant.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
epicurean-pleasure.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Felipe Carvalho frames a friend 'Toby's' worry – tattoos are forever, so should one be impulsive or cautious? – as a problem about bodily freedom versus irreversible change. He rejects the hedonist position (seize the day, regret is just part of freedom) as too simple and the Millian position (drawing on Mill's On Liberty argument that one cannot freely alienate one's freedom, as in selling oneself into slavery) as too precautionary, noting his friend's happy irreversible ear surgery. He proposes a 'middle path' learned from the tattoo community: a complex interplay of motif, the tattooist-as-artist, and the body-as-canvas that lets permanence guide more principled choices – so no 'I Love Becky' tattoos.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
epicurean-pleasure.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
epicurean-pleasure.relation: This span closes the walk-of-shame semiotics and then applies ancient ethics to college relationships. Puka defends long-distance college relationships through Aristotle's account of philia—arguing (provocatively, per Aristotle) that love is an activity, so being apart 'murders' love unless couples make Skype, sexting, and texting into the relationship's real medium rather than a substitute. Stephens brings Epicurus and Lucretius to 'friends with benefits': since sexual passion is a natural-but-unnecessary desire that breeds anxiety and love is a wound to the mind, while friendship is necessary for ataraxia, he concludes students should skip the sex and keep the friend—'friends are the real benefits,' echoing Tina Turner's 'What's Love Got to Do with It?' Levine/Mongeau and Smith/Morrison supply communication-research data on how FWB relationships form, are negotiated (usually not), and often end when one partner 'catches feelings.'

epicurean-pleasure.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
epicurean-pleasure.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Gregory Bassham mines the happy communities of the Shire, Rivendell, and Lothlorien for six keys to happiness: delight in simple things (linked to Epicurus's natural pleasures and Thoreau's Walden simplicity), making light of troubles, close friendship (grounded in Aristotle's claim that friendship is the greatest external good), good character, cherishing beauty and creativity, and recovering wonder. He argues Tolkien's hobbits and elves illustrate what modern happiness research confirms, so Tolkien functions as a philosophical guide to a more joy-filled life.

epicurean-pleasure.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
epicurean-pleasure.title: 38. The Big Lebowski Nihilism, Masculinity, and Abiding Virtue
epicurean-pleasure.relation: Fosl argues that The Big Lebowski critiques traditional masculine ideals (soldier, tycoon, detective, patriarch) and offers in The Dude an alternative 'abiding' virtue rooted in Epicurean contented poverty and ataraxia (his simple pleasures, White Russians, and indifference to property), Aristotelian civic friendship or philia with Walter and Donny that holds a divided polity together, and a Wittgenstein/Aristotle-informed flexibility about applying rules that positions The Dude at a mean between Walter's rigid absolutism and the nihilists' deficiency. Most centrally the film confronts Nietzschean European nihilism ('God is dead'); The Dude answers it as a halfway Ubermensch through comedy, friendship, and Kierkegaardian and Camusian existential repetition (bowling as rolling the rock, Sisyphus made meaningful), abiding and reproducing his form of life against despair, death, and disillusionment.

thoreau-walden.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
thoreau-walden.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
thoreau-walden.relation: Gregory Bassham distills six keys to happiness from Tolkien's hobbits and elves: delight in simple pleasures (Epicurus on natural pleasures, Thoreau's Walden simplicity), making light of troubles (Sam's star above Mordor, with Marcus Aurelius and Augustine on courage and hope), friendship (Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics read against Sam, Merry, and Pippin refusing to let Frodo go alone), good character, beauty and creativity (Lothlórien versus Mordor, 'flow'), and wonder (Tom Bombadil, Frodo's 'recovery' of fresh vision at Cerin Amroth). He argues Tolkien thereby becomes a philosophical guide, pointing from the Shire and Rivendell to a richer, more joy-filled life.

thoreau-walden.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
thoreau-walden.title: Poker and Philosophy
thoreau-walden.relation: Ventimiglia mines No-Limit Hold'em for seven lessons philosophers also teach: we lack certain knowledge (Descartes' cogito is the famous quest for certainty, but philosophy's own history of disagreement proves uncertainty is the human condition), and like William James against Clifford we must still believe and act without the nuts — waiting for pocket aces while the blinds eat you alive is no strategy. Risking everything echoes Thoreau's escape from lives of quiet desperation, trusting hunches over arithmetic follows Thoreau and Peirce's sentimentalism, and the Darwin-and-Spencer competition of tournament poker hides a deeper cooperative social contract: get caught cheating and you are out of the game. It closes with Plato's four classic virtues from the Republic — wisdom, courage, moderation, and the justice of a balanced soul — as the perfection of a poker player.

thoreau-walden.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
thoreau-walden.title: Let Your Heart Be the Anchor and the Beat of Your Own Song
thoreau-walden.relation: Berti reads Neil Peart's 1997-98 catastrophes (his daughter's car accident, his wife's cancer death) and the 55,000-mile Ghost Rider motorcycle exile through Sartrean existentialism: existence precedes essence, so with no God-given script Peart must author his own reactions, exactly as Sartre's student had to choose between mother and Resistance. The chapter tracks alienation ('I do not know who I am'), the duty to choose rather than lean on outside voices, and 'The Pass' as the voice telling a suicidal teenager to walk back from the razor's edge. Thoreau's Walden retreat supplies the model for the healing road, and Peart's own directives ('keep moving; kick your own ass, gently') enact 'Freewill' and 'Something for Nothing': we are the ones who choose, and the choice to live made all that followed (re-marriage, Vapor Trails, five more tours) possible.

thoreau-walden.title: UNSC Briefing
thoreau-walden.relation: Fred Van Lente's introduction argues that Master Chief is deliberately an empty shell—faceless, ageless, mostly silent—so the player's identity grafted onto him brings both to life at once in Halo: Combat Evolved's opening cryo-wakeup tutorial. He frames the book with Thoreau's Walden claim that philosophy is living simplicity, mapping it onto the Chief's ascetic soldier existence, and on Socrates: a game worth playing is worth examining, since the unexamined game is not worth playing. He closes with Aristotle's potentiality and actuality: the game actualizes the Chief as a kicker of alien ass, and the book actualizes the series' social and philosophical potential.

thoreau-walden.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
thoreau-walden.title: Friends—Don’t Leave Home without ’Em
thoreau-walden.relation: Greg Ahrenhoerster places SpongeBob in literary history between Transcendentalism and naturalism: 'Nature Pants' is a failed Walden — SpongeBob gives away his possessions for Jellyfish Fields but his 'jellyfish instincts' fail as badly as self-reliance in London's 'To Build a Fire' — while 'Squidville' shows the industrial city's cold indifference as in Crane's Maggie. 'Jellyfish Hunter' warns that trying to exploit nature (Krabs's jelly factory) invites nature's reprisal, since civilized beings without instinct are at nature's mercy. The naturalist moral, against Transcendentalist solitude, is that we survive only through each other: visit Jellyfish Fields, but bring a friend.

thoreau-walden.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
thoreau-walden.title: Chapter 31 - “Piper in the Woods”
thoreau-walden.relation: David Svolba hunts the 'distinct new idea' of 'Piper in the Woods': able-bodied garrison men on Asteroid Y-3 claim to have become plants so they can abandon jobs in a machine where 'the men are parts, and each has his job' - a radical but understandable response to lives devoted to meaningless, alienated labor whose ends they no longer identify with. Reading the story with Thoreau's warning that in a technological world we become 'tools of our tools', and likening the defectors to Timothy Leary's drop-outs, it presents Dick's tacit approval of the sun-basking plant-people as social criticism of a dehumanizing techno-industrial order that sees resistance only as laziness. The darker suggestion is that such a form of life is strangely hard to resist: escape collapses into self-imposed dehumanization, making the story perhaps a parable of drug-like escapism.

thoreau-walden.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
thoreau-walden.title: a4.xhtml
thoreau-walden.relation: Bronson argues that walking is a philosophical practice against modern placelessness (Giddens' 'phantasmagoric' locality): Thorin survived Smaug's attack because as a youth he 'was a good adventurous lad, always on the move', and Tolkien's wise figures - slow, flower-stopping Tolkien himself, Gandalf who 'went to look ahead' and was brought back 'by looking behind', Bilbo's silent walking, Beorn's bear-travels - all practice attentive movement through place. He backs this with Montaigne's retirement to his tower and bringing thoughts back to the orchard, Thoreau's woods-walking that must be spiritual as well as physical, the Tao Te Ching's 'good travelers leave no tracks' and Zhuangzi's wandering virtues, and Buddhist walking meditation from the Buddha's wandering monks to Thich Nhat Hanh's peace steps.

thoreau-walden.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
thoreau-walden.title: Take Me to the Lakes: Transcendentalism and Ecology in Taylor Swift's folklore
thoreau-walden.relation: Reads folklore as American Transcendentalist: like Thoreau at Walden and on Mt. Katahdin, Swift's escape into the woods of 'the lakes', 'seven', and 'the last great american dynasty' dissolves the divide between body and nature and reveals a fundamental oneness linking Rebekah Harkness, her grandfather in 'epiphany', and the High Line. Against the anti-social reading of Thoreau, the chapter argues, with Emerson's return to society after 'Nature', that Swift's escapism is not selfish retreat: she hands the stories back ('Now it's up to you to pass them down'), so leaving society heals alienation and rebuilds connection, including her anxiety that fame makes her 'nothing new' answered by the endurance of folk songs.

thoreau-walden.title: The Industrious Sherlock Holmes
thoreau-walden.relation: Bassham diagnoses Holmes as a workaholic against clinical criteria (obsessive work, few relationships, perfectionism, health neglect through fasting and cocaine), then traces the rise of the Protestant work ethic (Calvin, Weber, Carlyle) and its modern decline. Drawing on Thoreau's Walden critique of 'lives of quiet desperation,' Pieper on leisure, and the 'affluenza' literature, he distinguishes pathological from benign workaholism by warning signs and by motivation. He concludes Holmes is a pathological workaholic in his symptoms but redeemed by his noble, non-materialistic motive of fighting crime and achieving justice.

thoreau-walden.title: 5 Neil Young Lover of Sun, Moon and Cars
thoreau-walden.relation: Anderson traces Young's environmentalism from the hippie-romantic nature worship of "After the Gold Rush" and Greendale toward a pragmatic "middle way" that reconciles his love of nature with his love of cars and recording technology (the Lincvolt project, Storytone). Drawing on Thoreau, Muir and Leopold's land ethic while rejecting the fixed prescriptions of Singer and Regan, he presents Young as an experimentalist "meliorist" who owns his own complicity in CO2 abuse and urges informed, practical, self-aware action rather than utopian or deontological solutions.

thoreau-walden.title: 9 Neil Young’s Search for the Simple Life
thoreau-walden.relation: Watson and Riches reinterpret "A Man Needs a Maid" not as simple misogyny but as Young's ambivalent inner conflict between craving companionship and fearing the pain of intimacy. They read his pursuit of the "simple life" ("Heart of Gold," avoidance of reading) through Epicurean simplicity, Aristotle's eudaimonia, Bowlby/Freudian avoidant attachment and cognitive dissonance, and Sartre's "bad faith" as self-deception, set against Thoreau's chosen solitude and Aristotle's claim that the non-social being is "beast or god."

amor-fati.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
amor-fati.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Eric Bronson places Tolkien among the 'sometimes merry' existentialists: Nietzsche's artist who says Yes amid catastrophe and needs 'the power to forget', Jaspers on machines estranging us from our past, and Arendt on Eichmann's obedient inhumanity and the few who create joy in dark times. The elves' songs in Rivendell and Lórien are joy born of sorrow and dispossession - Galadriel suffers because she remembers too much, trying to 'embalm time', while Arwen forgoes immortality for Aragorn. Her refusal of the Ring ('I will diminish, and go into the West, and remain Galadriel') embodies the existentialist affirmation: trust your own light, know what to remember and what to forget.

amor-fati.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
amor-fati.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Lenore Wright reads Sam and Frodo's Quest through the two journey motifs of Western philosophy: the journey out (Plato's cave, structuring Augustine's Confessions and Descartes' escape from the senses' deceptions) and the journey inward (the cogito, self-transformation, with Nussbaum's claim that literature gives philosophy a body). Frodo's steps out of the Shire-cave - selling Bag End, 'I will take the Ring, though I do not know the way' - create the Fellowship and its freedoms, while Boromir attains self-knowledge only at death's door and Gandalf, Aragorn, and Sam are remade by the road. Against classical heroes like Theseus and Odysseus, Sam and Frodo are modern pilgrims - Nietzschean Yea-sayers becoming who they are, with Heideggerian 'potentiality-for-Being' - whereas Sméagol and Saruman live inauthentically, defined by their pasts.

amor-fati.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
amor-fati.title: Tarantula’s End
amor-fati.relation: Goldblatt and Necarsulmer pair Dylan's Tarantula with Nietzsche's "The Tarantulas" from Zarathustra: both are books of advice, renaming, and stream-of-consciousness flow whose sections cohere through signature and attitude rather than narrative (the same Foucauldian author function). Both embody the intuitive artist of Plato's Ion and Nietzsche's Ecce Homo - the poet as medium whose language arrives as inspiration, all language being fresh or stale metaphor. Tarantula's vengeful vignettes and "Idiot Wind" dramatize the ressentiment Zarathustra warns against, its impenetrable juxtapositions ("harmonica battalions," "funeral landlord") work as Derridean catachresis - metaphor whose transfer fails yet exerts aesthetic force - and the book's dream of the burning tenement leaves Dylan unable, and absolved, to look back.

amor-fati.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
amor-fati.title: Will You Say Yes
amor-fati.relation: Bruce finds Nietzsche's eternal return in the NES Zelda's clockless, endlessly restartable structure: the same game recurs every time you press start, yet since the player changes, each playthrough manifests the forces anew, and the demon's question 'do you desire this once more?' becomes 'do you will to play once more?'. Link's growth through eight dungeons to face Ganon is read as will-to-power, personal strength and self-overcoming rather than mere domination, and saying yes to the struggle is amor fati. Against Plato's two-worlds doctrine of Forms and the Christian after-worldly (both Nietzsche's targets), the original Zelda offers no guide, no Bible, and no linear time to a final judgment: this looped world is the only one, so it must be affirmed.

amor-fati.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
amor-fati.title: How We Still Might Manage a Smile Being Pirates and Making Meaning
amor-fati.relation: Adam Glover reads 'A Pirate Looks at Forty' through Kristeva's intertextuality: since every text and self is a 'mosaic of quotations' pirated from pre-existing sources, Buffett's confession that he was born 'two hundred years too late' makes him an ironic pirate who can no longer believe or plunder unselfconsciously, unlike the oblivious common-sense pirate. Invoking Barthes's death of the author, he argues the pirate's life is a hard freedom to improvise multiple meanings (the ever-changing 'head uptown' variations in the song) with full responsibility for one's choices. The chapter ends weighing Camus's worry that meaninglessness makes life not worth living against the Nietzsche of The Birth of Tragedy, who answers that the meaning of life is life itself, and it sides with Buffett against Socrates's 'unexamined life' while admitting it cannot settle the question.

amor-fati.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
amor-fati.relation: Three 'Phase Four' essays. Moseley reads the Joker across Batman #1, The Killing Joke, The Dark Knight, A Death in the Family, and Dark Knight Returns as a 'moral monster' who knowingly does evil - and, following Anscombe and Scanlon's guise-of-the-good analysis, pursues aesthetic 'higher values' in a Camus-like affirmation of the absurd, embracing the irrationality Batman's rational moral order cannot fathom. Levin uses X-gene biology (Beast's explanation in Astonishing X-Men, genotype vs phenotype, M-Day) to strip Magneto's Homo sapiens superior claim of any genetic or phenotypic basis, then argues via the moral community of rational persons (Kant's criterion) that mutants and humans share one moral community, condemning both the Registration Act and mutant separatism. O'Neil's prose piece traces Harvey Dent from Calvinist certainty through the acid that scars him to cosmic doubt - quantum randomness, many worlds, Sartre's condemnation to freedom - until Nietzsche's amor fati lets him embrace duality and let the scarred two-headed coin decide good and evil.

amor-fati.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
amor-fati.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Auxier argues the trilogy is narrated on a Nietzschean lattice rather than being a mere inverted Milton: after tracing the Paradise Lost, Genesis 6, and Pseudepigrapha sources (Azazel as the model for Asriel, Metatron from Third Enoch, Dust from Milton's warring particles), he reads Mrs. Coulter's speech to Father MacPhail about seeking God out and giving him 'the gift of death' as Nietzsche's death of God fused with a description of Nietzsche's own final dementia. Will and Lyra become overman and overwoman beyond good and evil: Will rises by his will and his willingness to kill (the alethiometer's verdict 'He is a murderer' makes him a worthy companion), while Lyra commands both truth and lies, the alethiometer embodying truth as 'a mobile army of metaphors.' But the chapter's payoff is critical: Pullman does not endorse Nietzsche, since in a world where the will to power dominates, the overwoman Mrs. Coulter has no place and falls with Asriel and Metatron into the Abyss, while Xaphania's teaching offers a disciplined, workful imagination as an alternative.

amor-fati.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
amor-fati.title: Chapter 25 - Untimely Speculations
amor-fati.relation: Heath Massey's introduction to Chapter 25 opens with Nietzsche's Gay Science passage on intellects that might experience time backward, then stages the demon of eternal recurrence: every pain and joy returning in the same sequence in a world without aim, which either crushes you or becomes 'the highest formula of affirmation', amor fati. Eternal recurrence is a test of the will separating 'man' from 'overman', since one could not celebrate it while believing the world needs a divine purpose. The chapter then maps Dick's imaginative variations of temporality onto two Nietzschean tendencies - disruptions of time-sense that render characters powerless, and extraordinary temporalities that liberate them beyond finite human time, culminating in Dick's theory of supertemporality.

amor-fati.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
amor-fati.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Brandon Kempner reads Gaiman's Batman: Whatever Happened to the Caped Crusader? as Nietzschean eternal recurrence: Batman dies and is reborn as the infant Bruce Wayne to repeat his life exactly, because Gaiman first strips away every teleological ending, Catwoman kills Batman, Alfred reveals he invented the Joker, and the Moore-style domestic bliss of the Superman farewell is denied. With God dead there is no Heaven, telos, or external reward, so, like Nietzsche's Overman who creates values above the city's conventional morality, Batman's meaning can lie only in the lived repetition itself: 'the only reward you get for being Batman? You get to be Batman,' the highest formula of life-affirmation. Kempner extends the pattern to the funeral-framed rebirth of a new Dream in Sandman: The Wake, showing Gaiman's recurring obsession with cycles that have 'no endings' across his work.

amor-fati.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
amor-fati.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Rard tests whether objective morality survives the apocalypse by running four theories against Season Two: Plato's Forms explain universal truths about walkers ('walkers survive so long as their brains are relatively undamaged') but cannot handle white lies or changed circumstances, and Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Rick's rush from the shot Carl as rashness and Shane's supply run as courage, yet virtues prove relative and luck-dependent in a collapsed world. Natural law founders on clashing intuitions — Merle's racism and Hershel's barn of walkers each claim self-evidence. The chapter's center is Nietzschean: Hershel's barn is slave morality that pities the 'sick,' Maggie breaks from it, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and opening of the barn enact a will-to-power master morality without joy, while Rick alone moves toward amor fati — embracing the world as it is, refusing guilt over Lori's affair, and insisting the baby be born into the Walk Age.

amor-fati.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
amor-fati.title: The Wire and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Clifton measures Omar against four Nietzschean criteria for the overman: as a free spirit he is 'in the wind, so to speak,' detached from home, money, and eventually even lovers like Brandon and Butchie; as a non-dogmatist about truth he uses it as a tool, lying under oath at Bird's trial yet sparing Brother Mouzone when the lie no longer holds; and as a noble of the Genealogy he is an active hunter who embraces the will to power, telling Wee-Bey 'you come at the king, you best not miss.' But Omar fails the fourth test, value-creation: his code keeps the good/evil scale intact rather than overturning it, so in the Three Metamorphoses he remains the lion who slays 'Thou Shalt' but never becomes the value-creating child. The verdict, in Nietzsche's own phrase, is that Omar is noble but 'human, all too human.'

amor-fati.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
amor-fati.title: The Wire and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Brittingham argues The Wire is a Nietzschean rather than merely Aristotelian tragedy, a wrestling between the Apollonian orientation of order, statistics, and illusion (Rawls's clearance rates, Burrell's bureaucracy, Stringer's business plans) and the Dionysian reveling in the Game's chaos and suffering (Avon accepting that 'you only gotta fuck up once', McNulty's intoxicated self-destruction). Stringer is Nietzsche's 'theoretical man' whose faith that thought can correct existence, embodied in the New Day Co-Op, cannot save him from Omar's 'It ain't about money', while McNulty is the Dionysiac man inside the Apollonian institution until Freamon's 'the job will not save you' forces his resignation. The chapter closes by reading the characters' resigned embrace of their fates as Nietzschean affirmation: since neither the job, intelligence, violence, nor the gods will save you, the only response is to say yes to life anyway.

amor-fati.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
amor-fati.title: Futurama and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Laderoute reads 'The Late Philip J. Fry' - the forward-only time machine overshooting past the year one billion and the last protons to a second Big Bang and an identical universe (ten feet lower, conveniently crushing its duplicates) - as a tour of cosmology from Aristotle's static, eternal, Earth-centered heavens through the Stoics' providential determinism and fiery ekpyrosis to Big Bang cosmology and heat death, which is why the Professor is so shocked. Nietzsche's Gay Science 341 supplies the existential payoff: faced with living identically forever, one can react with horror or delight, and eternal recurrence becomes a challenge to become the person you want to be. Fry, a billion years late for his Cavern on the Green dinner, reads Leela's message carved in stone, and in the repeated universe finally arrives on time - 'That was the old Fry... he's dead now' - amor fati enacted.

amor-fati.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
amor-fati.title: The Devil and Philosophy
amor-fati.relation: Steven Neumann reads the sold-my-soul legends around Led Zeppelin ('here's to my sweet Satan' backwards on 'Stairway to Heaven'), Black Sabbath, and bluesman Robert Johnson at the Clarksdale crossroads as a parable of Nietzsche's amor fati: every joy comes bundled with suffering, so greatness means affirming the whole package. He deploys the eternal recurrence thought experiment - would you will your life, Plant's dead son and Bonham's fatal bender included, to repeat eternally? - and contrasts the ascetic denial of pleasure with Nietzsche's claim in Ecce Homo that his own sickness and obscurity made him love fate all the more.

amor-fati.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
amor-fati.title: 14. The Doctor’s Desire for Human Suffering
amor-fati.relation: Cooper reads 'Rise of the Cybermen' and 'The Age of Steel' as staging Nietzsche against Mill's pain-eradicating utilitarianism: John Lumic, who builds the Cybermen to abolish his sickness, exemplifies the life-denying herd—losing his creativity, craving 'unity and uniformity,' becoming 'a living brain with a heart of steel'—while the Doctor, answering that a life without pain would be 'you might as well kill me,' affirms suffering as the source of creativity, striving, and strength. She extends the Nietzschean reading to the Doctor's character: his guilt over the Time War double-genocide and his loneliness ('the only certainty left is that you'll end up alone') become the pain that makes him merciful, from offering Dalek Caan compassion after 'Evolution of the Daleks' to forgiving the Master in 'Last of the Time Lords,' so that mercy is, as the Genealogy of Morals says, 'the privilege of the most powerful man.'

amor-fati.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
amor-fati.title: 1. Everything’s Amazing and Nobody’s Happy
amor-fati.relation: Max Elder reads Louis through Nietzsche's Gay Science claim that all philosophy is unconscious memoir, arguing Louis's confession-like comedy reveals dark truths we would rather flee - the Conan 'everything's amazing and nobody's happy' bit, the 'I know the darkness' exchange with the Christian woman, and the Subway/Pamela scene where a homeless man bathes behind a subway violinist. Using Nietzsche's line that man alone laughs because he suffers so deeply, and The Birth of Tragedy's comic as the artistic discharge of the nausea of absurdity, the chapter argues Louis's laughter performs a gestalt switch that ties the ugly to the beautiful and so redeems it. It reads the religions-supply-meaning argument - God's mockery-laughter versus Nietzsche's holy laughter - as the reason redemption now happens in comedy clubs rather than churches, and closes with Louie's 'Country Drive' scolding of Jane ('you don't get to be bored') as Nietzschean embrace of the amazing fact of being alive.

amor-fati.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
amor-fati.title: 9. My Dharma Is the Road that Never Ends
amor-fati.relation: Reads Twin Peaks: The Return as a commitment to Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati: Cooper is trapped in an existential time loop (Dougie's relearning, Wally's Part 4 Dharma speech, the final-episode Cooper/Richard do-over) and must learn to love every horrific repetition, quoting the Gay Science demon passage and Nietzsche's Will to Power on enduring recurrence. The chapter frames Lynch and Frost as Romantics — Novalis on wonder, Isaiah Berlin's Roots of Romanticism on the artist's inner vision — who break three storytelling rules (authors create stories, protagonists solve problems, stories have endings), so that Laura's mystery stays a living Jack-the-Ripper-style mystery and the story becomes a meta-narrative co-created with viewers, echoing Buddhist pratityasamutpada and Russell's beginningless world. Cooper's finale is a Sisyphean task he accepts, making his integrity the audience's own test.

amor-fati.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
amor-fati.title: 5. The Funny Thing about Being Yourself
amor-fati.relation: Reads Schumer's comedy as Nietzschean self-creation: like the tightrope walker over the abyss she confronts who she is, says 'Yes' to life in the spirit of the eternal recurrence and amor fati, and 'gives style' to her character by wearing mistakes as badges of honor, notably reclaiming her paparazzi photos in the Leather Special. Balke then casts her as Rorty's ironist, whose continual burning of old material keeps her free of a 'final vocabulary' in a contingent world, with 'Amy Goes Deep' doing the Rortian work of testing herself against others. He closes with George Herbert Mead's account of a self formed through social interaction with significant others.

amor-fati.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
amor-fati.title: A Strange Realization
amor-fati.relation: Dunn argues that Strange begins as a foot soldier of the Baconian project (Bacon and Descartes' program of conquering nature and treating death as an enemy to be subdued, embodied in his surgical God-complex and neurogenesis research), and that its shipwreck drives him to Kamar-Taj. Using Nietzsche, he reads both Strange and Kaecilius as sick with the 'spirit of revenge against time' — Kaecilius fleeing into Dormammu's timeless Dark Dimension as Nietzsche's Hinterweltler, Strange clinging to his unrecoverable past. The climactic 'Dormammu, I've come to bargain' time loop is interpreted as Nietzsche's eternal return weaponized, and Strange's 'Pain's an old friend' as his achievement of amor fati, echoing the Ancient One's dying claim that death is what gives life meaning.

amor-fati.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
amor-fati.title: 17. Downton Abbey as Eternal Recurrence
amor-fati.relation: Christopher Ketcham provocatively equates primogeniture and entail - the legal machinery that returns Downton intact to each generation - with Nietzsche's 'greatest weight,' the eternal recurrence. Working through Lawrence Hatab's five interpretations of the doctrine, he asks whether the Abbey's continuity is cosmological (it is not, since estate taxes and squandering heirs keep chipping away), a Zarathustra-style life-affirming yes to the agrarian world against the 'nihilism' of capitalist fashion, or merely symbolic like a listing in Burke's Peerage beside fossilized dinosaur bones. His answer comes via Violet, the family, and the servants, who have 'become one with the property': the Abbey recurs only anthropomorphically, and even that stickiness is dissolving under industrialization, the death tax, and the war that killed off three royal cousins' empires.

amor-fati.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
amor-fati.title: NOTES
amor-fati.relation: Shores reads Volume 1 through Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as a self-test of life-affirmation: Adam sealed in a coffin embodies recurrence in its 'most terrible form,' Future Hiro's string map dramatizes Nietzsche's claim that every action is indissolubly tied to all others, and Linderman's speech divorcing happiness from meaning is answered by Nietzsche's demand to crave nothing more fervently than the eternal return. The chapter stresses where the show diverges: Claire insists 'the future is not written in stone' and the heroes rewrite destiny, while Arthur Petrelli ironically holds a copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra while contradicting it. Hiro's failed attempts to save Charlie and his father (Kaito's 'we cannot play God') frame the amor fati question of whether free will means changing events or willing them eternally.

amor-fati.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: Argues against the title claim of the previous chapter: Frank is a Nietzschean master type — he defines good as good-for-him, embraces pain as strength, and keeps no allegiances once Walker and Vasquez break their promise — while Peter Russo is the paradigmatic reactive slave who cannot command himself and blames others, exactly Nietzsche's 'he who cannot command himself is commanded'. But the overman requires self-overcoming, the sublimation of drives into creation, and amor fati, and Frank only dominates others for vengeful ends: his whole scheme grows from ressentiment over the Secretary of State snub, he affirms other wills merely as investments, and in Season 3 he becomes a slave to his own position. The chapter uses the Cesare Borgia misreading (better a Borgia than a Parsifal as raw material, but Borgia was no overman), Napoleon's corruption, and Goethe's creative wholeness to conclude that Frank remains 'all-too-human' — destruction without creation.

amor-fati.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: Meyer mounts the counter-case: Frank exemplifies Nietzsche's master type (good as good-for-him, 'no longer are we bound by allegiances') and Russo the slave type ('he who cannot command himself is commanded'), but the overman is a synthesis of neither. He corrects the Leopold-and-Loeb 'above the law' reading and the Cesare Borgia identification: the genuine overman sublimates strong drives into creation — Goethe's self-discipline, Beethoven's new norms — and affirms other wills in themselves rather than as instruments, which Frank never does with Zoe, Peter, or Claire. Frank's revenge-driven scheming is slave-like psychological warfare, ruling others is the 'pettiest' form of power, and by Season 3 he is the slave of his own presidency — destructive without creating, and lacking even amor fati.

amor-fati.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
amor-fati.title: 7 Indiana Jones and Existential Self-Affirmation
amor-fati.relation: Daniel Tilsley reads The Last Crusade as an excavation of identity: the fedora Fedora bestows after young Indy's defeat, the twenty-six-year quest for the Cross of Coronado ('All my life'), and the chosen name 'Indiana' (taken from the family dog) are acts of Nietzschean self-affirmation — amor fati and the willingness to will the Eternal Recurrence of one's life. The villains fail because they seek external artifacts to patch deficient lives, whereas the Grail Knight, like Camus's Sisyphus, authentically affirms his endless task of guarding the cup. The arc completes when Henry Sr. finally calls his son 'Indiana' while hanging from the abyss, recognizing the man he chose to become, and Crystal Skull repeats the pattern with Mutt and the fedora's eventual inheritance.

amor-fati.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
amor-fati.title: Will You Say Yes
amor-fati.relation: Michael Bruce ('Zeldathustra') reads the original Legend of Zelda through Nietzsche's thought of eternal recurrence: with no game clock, the ability to save, and looped enemy patterns, every playthrough repeats the same structure, and the player faces the demon's question — do you will to play once more and innumerable times more? The Triforce's split between Wisdom and Power becomes Nietzsche's opposition of the will-to-truth and the will-to-power, with Link's dungeon-by-dungeon self-overcoming enacting amor fati. Against Plato's two-world doctrine of Forms and the Christian after-worldly, the chapter insists the game (like life) gets its meaning from this world only — experimentation, repetition as training, and saying yes.

amor-fati.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: Conway reads Fury Road as a homecoming (nostos) story that overturns Homer's patriarchal template of Odysseus: Furiosa's trusted Green Place proves as idealistic as the War Boys' Valhalla, and both are diagnosed by Nietzsche's critique of idealism as 'mendaciousness in the face of what is necessary.' The cure is amor fati joined to Max's flinty realism — turn around and make a home by retaking the Citadel — while Hegel's master-slave dialectic explains Immortan Joe's unacknowledged dependency on the women he enslaves for milk, heirs, and recognition. The film ends with Furiosa raised up as a matriarchal ruler and Max departing as the self-exiled wounded healer, barred by his own guilt from the green place he helped make.

amor-fati.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: Argues Q embodies Nietzsche's revaluation of values: contemptuous of herd-like safety, Q subjects Picard and the crew to trials ("Encounter at Farpoint", "Hide and Q", "All Good Things"'s "the trial never ends") meant to force growth beyond conventional morality, seek out other "supermen", and embrace risk - Q's "bloody nose" defense after eighteen crewmen die at the Borg in "Q Who?". The Borg figure as everything Nietzschean individualism despises, a mindless collectivism that robs drones of the passion the strong need to individuate, and Q's offer to join Picard as guide pictures a friendship between Nietzsche's self-mastered few. The lesson of "Tapestry" is amor fati: Picard must embrace the Nausicaan knife fight that nearly killed him, since undoing it makes a safe, unnoticed man - though the authors finally refuse Nietzsche's harsher dictum that the weak should perish, siding with healing over Q's education-by-death.

amor-fati.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: Argues 'time is a flat circle' means neither a metaphysical cosmology nor M-theory physics nor reincarnation, but is Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as a thought experiment about how to live. Tracing Rust's pessimism and his lack of the 'constitution for suicide' (echoing Schopenhauer's claim that suicide affirms the will-to-live, with starvation as its only true denial), it shows the flat circle operating as both trap and cure: obsessing over it keeps Rust on the Yellow King case until his near-death experience becomes the 'tremendous moment' of amor fati. Heidegger's view in Being and Time that anxiety before death can empower meaningful existence frames Rust's final affirmation — escaping the flat circle by faithfully acknowledging it, through sacrifice.

amor-fati.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: Michels reads the Amazon series' first two seasons as a Nietzschean tale organized around eternal recurrence, treating the turning Wheel as Nietzsche's 'existential imperative' and greatest weight: the ferryman who dies vainly saving his son fails the test, while Loial urges the heroes to make themselves unforgettable. He maps Nietzsche's monumental, antiquarian, and critical uses of history onto Moiraine's lesson about the song of Manetheren, contrasts the Ubermensch with the 'last man,' and reads Moiraine's will to power against the ascetic, life-denying Way of the Leaf of the Tuatha'an. Lanfear and Ishamael embody nihilism and resentment, while amor fati names the life-affirming embrace of fate Nietzsche prized.

amor-fati.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
amor-fati.title: Notes
amor-fati.relation: This multi-author epilogue collects short 'cutting-room-floor' reflections on poignant WoT quotes. Cooke reads Ingtar's confession as the existential fear of historical oblivion (historia as both history and story) driving a patriot into Darkfriendship.
