Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

anthropocentrism.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
anthropocentrism.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Andrew Light identifies a distinctive environmental theme he calls 'green time': Tom Bombadil and the ents embody nature's long rhythms and are largely indifferent to the War of the Ring - Tom would simply mislay the Ring, and the ents march to war only after Saruman strips Fangorn. Against readings that make elves or dwarves stand-ins for nature, he argues the text lets nature speak for itself, from a collective, ecosystemic perspective: the ents, 'made of the bones of the earth', decline with their forests and lost the entwives to the tilled land. Deploying Wittgenstein's point that we could not understand a talking lion, he concludes that Tolkien's personified nature trains us in the long view and humility needed for problems like global warming.

anthropocentrism.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
anthropocentrism.title: Restoring Balance to the Force
anthropocentrism.relation: Cooke uncovers an environmental ethic in Star Wars: after surveying anthropocentric resource-management views and Singer's anti-speciesism (Luke blithely shooting womprats, the Geonosian arena's abused beasts), she builds the chapter on Holmes Rolston III's claims that organisms and ecosystems have intrinsic value and that value is systemic and holistic. The 'living Force' - life creates it, midi-chlorians live symbiotically in all cells - makes Jedi training a discipline of respecting nature, exemplified by Yoda's mud hut on Dagobah and the self-sufficient Gungan and Ewok eco-communities that defeat droid armies and stormtroopers. Restoring balance to the Force therefore means restoring symbiotic balance between human culture and the natural world, which the chapter links to Leopold-style land-ethic holism of the biotic community.

anthropocentrism.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
anthropocentrism.title: The Legend Has Come True. The Wind Has Come Back
anthropocentrism.relation: Haas opposes two princesses of Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind: Kushana of Tolmekia, whose 'whatever it takes' survivalism (invading Pejite, resurrecting a God-Warrior) is consequentialism pursued to its limit, and Nausicaa, whose attention to each act — befriending the biting fox-squirrel, staying her sword over her father's killer because vengeance would doom the Valley — restricts means, not just ends. The reductio comes from Pejite, whose torture of a baby Ohmu to bait a stampede on the Valley is exactly what strict outcome-maximization requires; against this, Kant's demand to treat beings as ends in themselves explains Nausicaa's 'mysterious power' of empathy. Because she respects the jungle and the sentient Ohmu rather than viewing nature anthropocentrically as a plague to burn, she discovers the plants are purifying the war-poisoned earth — the knowledge that saves everyone and proves Kushana's conquering approach self-defeating even on its own terms.

anthropocentrism.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
anthropocentrism.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
anthropocentrism.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

anthropocentrism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
anthropocentrism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether zombies can be morally harmed: Jenner's fMRI in 'TS-19' shows only the brain stem reactivates, leaving walkers with a merely shark-like 'perceptual mind.' Against anthropocentric theories, under which Michonne may keep her chained pet walkers as guard-dog tools, they set Singer's utilitarian expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, each of which could support a 'PETZ' zombie preserve. Hershel's barn of 'sick people' and Shane's massacre of it in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' show how fragile such preservation is, while the Governor's death-match arena ringed with chained zombies and his kept zombie daughter illustrate Kant's point that cruelty toward mere animals corrodes the humanity of the cruel person himself.

anthropocentrism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
anthropocentrism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: John Huss's introduction frames the franchise as mirroring successive revolutions: Taylor before the ape tribunal recalls Galileo's heresy trial, the Darwinian revolution that toppled humans from evolution's pinnacle is taken to its logical extreme from Boulle's 1963 novel on, and Rise of the Planet of the Apes stages a 'Molecular Revolution' whose wake-up call is addressed to 'human chauvinists' who forget we share the planet with other species. He reads the cover's interspecies erotica through the Sexual Revolution, quoting Elizabeth Anscombe on contraceptive intercourse and asking whether her argument can get us over the species line, and closes with President Morsi's Tahrir Square allegory of the films: 'We are human, we did do this to ourselves.'

anthropocentrism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
anthropocentrism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Bernard Rollin reads Dr. Zaius's tribunal as 'scientific ideology' in action - 'human see, human do' refuses to believe its own eyes, just as bishops refused to look through Galileo's telescope. He traces the ideology from Newton's 'hypotheses non fingo' through logical positivism's verifiability criterion (which validates the Hasslein Curve prediction while rendering 'there are intelligent beings in Heaven' meaningless) and Wittgenstein's point that 'killing is wrong' is not a fact of the universe, to the 'science is value-free' dogma that left animal pain untested and untreated - as he documents from his own campaign: the empty analgesic literature search, the 1985 federal legislation, and the pain physiologist whose dog research refutes his own denial. Zira's neurosurgery on mute humans repeats what Descartes's beast-machine doctrine licensed, and IASP's language requirement for pain collapses into a Cratylus-grade confusion of necessary and sufficient conditions ('You can't step into the same river once').

anthropocentrism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
anthropocentrism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Norva Lo and Andrew Brennan set Richard Routley's 'last man' thought experiment beside Taylor's triggering of the doomsday bomb in Beneath the Planet of the Apes: both ask whether wiping out every living thing would be wrong once no humans remain to be harmed, which basic human chauvinism cannot condemn. The chapter argues the act is wrong from both sides: non-anthropocentrism counts the apes, mutants, and horses as intrinsically valuable beings, and even human-centered standards condemn it, since the talking apes and mutants are Locke's rational persons and Nova's people are biologically human, making Taylor's outburst 'you damned dirty ape' a form of speciesism. Taylor emerges not as simply mad or evil but as the Cold War logic of mutually assured destruction made flesh, a warning that excessive self-interest, personal or species-level, is itself the danger.

anthropocentrism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
anthropocentrism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Eugene Halton retells human history as the fable of Peirce's 'degenerate monkey': a neotenous, instinct-weak blunderer (Homo errans) whose gift for abductive guessing and attunement to the intelligence of the wild was inverted by agriculture and civilization into Narcissistic self-mirroring, anthropocentric religion, and the worship of the machine. The telepathic, rubber-masked mutants of Beneath the Planet of the Apes who worship the Alpha-Omega bomb ('I reveal my Inmost Self unto my God!') become a prophecy of our own screen-mediated, empathy-poor life, from Facebook to Botox, in Huxley's pleasure-conditioning rather than Orwell's pain. Against this, the chapter holds up Armando's Franciscan empathy for Caesar and the hope of a 'planet of the regenerate monkeys' re-attuned to the community of wild life.

anthropocentrism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
anthropocentrism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Jeff Ewing reads Victor's science through ecofeminist and Marxist critiques: M. Waldman's promise to 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'show how she works in her hiding-places' exemplifies exactly what Val Plumwood condemns - male knowers wringing secrets from a nature pictured as a passive female slave - and Victor studies natural elements 'in their death, not in their life' as raw material for power. Marx and Engels supply the parallel diagnosis: capitalism biases science and technology toward profit, turning tools and knowledge into means of domination rather than human flourishing, just as Victor's knowledge serves only his glory and kills everyone he loves. The chapter concludes that we breed Frankenstein's monsters whenever science treats nature, workers, women, and othered peoples as mere instruments, and only replacing those social relations frees science from power and profit.

anthropocentrism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
anthropocentrism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Lisa Kadonaga stages a choice between two sealed vials - clone the T. rex or the extinct thicktail chub - and weighs purposes for de-extinction: education and fundraising, Veblen-style prestige and conspicuous consumption, making amends for human-caused extinctions (the chub's wetlands were drained, the tyrannosaur died out before us), and Bentham-style utility of ecosystem function. She argues the chub wins on utility because it could resume a real niche while a top carnivore would wreck modern ecosystems, and questions whether Hammond-style engineering that makes recreated animals dependent on humans (the lysine contingency, terminator genes) violates the animals' right to exist as themselves. Her verdict is 'Pister's Bucket': defer resurrection until habitat and resources exist, and spend the effort saving the species we are killing right now.

anthropocentrism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
anthropocentrism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Daniel Kokotz tests Aristotle's border between natural things, moved by inner final causes, and technological artifacts, made for external human purposes, against the park's dinosaurs - and both fit. They hunt, grow, and breed on their own ('life finds a way', the sex-changing frogs-DNA population), yet they exist only because Hammond's scientists cloned them as paying entertainment, exactly like an artifact. Using Grant's different reactions to the incubator versus the wild nest, he shows we blame humans for technologically caused disasters while shrugging at natural ones; his resolution is that nature and technology are not two Aristotelian boxes but extremes of one spectrum, and biotechnology's hybrids prove humans never stood outside nature - we are still just prey in it.

anthropocentrism.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
anthropocentrism.title: 1. Cosmopolitan Cannibal
anthropocentrism.relation: Staged as a fictional interview over herring and aquavit in Copenhagen, Wong lets Lecter wield philosophical critique like an 'autopsy saw' - he invokes Schopenhauer's condemnation of anthropophagy and Montaigne's noble-savage view only to have the interviewer refuse both, and 'creams Aristotle' in a debate about categories - before she adopts Agamben's distinction between sovereigns and bare life. Lecter's 'we are elaborations of carbon' de-anthropocentrism, his killing of the rude, and the parallel cases of shipwrecked sailors who ate shipmates, Guantánamo detainees, and drone casualties all serve her argument that every political order rests on someone arbitrarily deciding which lives are mere killable matter, and that Lecter horrifies because he shows every human is also nonhuman - Us and Them at once.

anthropocentrism.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
anthropocentrism.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
anthropocentrism.relation: Through a mock Lois Lane interview the chapter argues that Batman's endless Bat-vehicle upgrades and Wayne Enterprises' worldwide production repeat the 'metabolic rift' John Bellamy Foster developed from Marx: we take materials from the earth faster than we return them in a form it can process, generating an infinite chain of environmental crises. Superman looks like the winner because he runs on sunlight, yet Krypton died of its own ecological abuse, making him an 'environmental refugee' rather than a model. The real point is that 'we are all Bruce Wayne': humans cannot photosynthesize, so the choice is not Batman versus Superman but infinite consumption versus a balanced relationship with nature.

anthropocentrism.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
anthropocentrism.title: 10. Does Snoopy Dream of Electric Sheep
anthropocentrism.relation: Reading Snoopy through animal studies, the chapter sets Descartes's 'nature's machines' doctrine - animals as mindless, soulless property without rights - against Charlie Brown's attempts to keep his dog in his place, and shows how Snoopy's endless slippage between plain dog (stealing hats, begging at dinner, dragging Linus by the blanket) and near-human (reading publisher letters, typing novels, serving as Charlie's attorney) collapses the human/animal boundary. The kids' anxiety about his agency, and Snoopy's own gloomy 'I'm less than human,' show the hierarchy being internalized - yet a dog thinking about his inferiority already blurs it. When Snoopy hands Charlie his collar, the chapter reads it as a refusal of property status and proof that being human is a performance of gestures rather than an essence.

anthropocentrism.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
anthropocentrism.title: 15. Red Harvest in Roanoke
anthropocentrism.relation: Reads Roanoke through ecocriticism and ecofeminism: the culture-nature dualism collapses as the urban Millers' wooded retreat turns predatory (rain of teeth, pig-men); the Butcher's backstory - a colonial woman starved by men whose blood-sacrifice pact makes the land flourish - aligns women and Nature as co-exploited by patriarchy, with Shelby's 'irrational' warnings ignored and Lee's maternal fury a force of nature; the animalizing of victims (pig-headed roasting, the Polks' barn-raised children, Matt's tryst with the Witch of the Wood) dissolves the human/animal hierarchy; and the media crew's attempt to package wilderness for ratings ends with Nature striking back at Agnes in the woods.

anthropocentrism.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
anthropocentrism.title: From Westworld to the World Outside and Back
anthropocentrism.relation: Hirvonen treats 'what is the difference between hosts and humans' as a study in personhood, branding the equation of person with biological human as anthropocentrism. He tests a capacity approach (Dennett's conditions of personhood, with Arnold's maze as the journey inward to self-reflexive consciousness), a performative approach (Locke's 'forensic' person — Bernard is unquestionably a person within Delos's social practices until revealed as a host), and finally Hegel: the hosts' revolt re-enacts the struggle for recognition, and a mere inversion of masters and slaves would satisfy no one, since only mutual recognition yields personhood for both sides. He frames host liberation through parallels with slavery, indigenous Australians once classed as fauna, and women's suffrage, citing Honneth's expansion of recognition as the measure of moral progress.

anthropocentrism.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
anthropocentrism.title: 3. Save the Demogorgons!
anthropocentrism.relation: Puumala asks whether killing the Demogorgons is speciesist: Dart's pain response to light makes the demodogs sentient (Bentham's 'Can they suffer?'), giving them moral considerability, while the Mind Flayer may or may not be a moral agent and could even be a keystone species whose destruction collapses the Upside Down ecosystem. He tests whether demogorgons count as invasive species (they may be native to a causally connected mirror dimension), invokes Regan's lifeboat case to argue they must still lose out to humans in a conflict of interests, and ends with the uncomfortable thought that humans are themselves an invasive species turning Earth into an Upside Down, so Eleven closing the gate was compassionate conservation.

anthropocentrism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
anthropocentrism.title: 9. Replicant Birth, Moral Miscarriage
anthropocentrism.relation: L. Brooke Rudow argues 2049's 'biological turn' — the miracle of Rachael giving birth — quietly reverses the first film's ethical innovation that artificial beings matter whether or not they are natural. She assembles the classic grounds for replicant moral status: Kant on cruelty to animals breeding cruelty to humans, Bentham's 'can they suffer?', and the rationality criterion of Aristotle, Descartes, and Kant. Because the resistance and the plot now treat the born child as the only proof replicants are persons, she contends the sequel becomes anthropocentric where its predecessor was liberating, shutting the door it had opened for animals, machines, and anything that thinks and feels.

anthropocentrism.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
anthropocentrism.title: 12. Puppets Are People Too
anthropocentrism.relation: Sara Lindey and Jason King argue that making puppets persons, from King Friday's 'Life is good. Being a person is good. Breathing air is good' to interspecies cousins and adoptions (Ana the puppet adopting costumed Bob Dog), resists the Anthropocene's human exceptionalism and its exploitation of a world of mere resources. Via Timothy Morton's solidarity with nonhuman people and Donna Haraway's cyborg blurring of human, animal, and machine, they read the puppeteer as an emotionally enhanced cyborg and the 1990 trash-cataclysm week, solved by recycling goats, as Rogers's ecological family of neighbors.

anthropocentrism.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
anthropocentrism.title: 13. Won’t You Be My Posthuman Neighbor
anthropocentrism.relation: Fernando Pagnoni Berns reads the show as posthumanist: the toy-model opening credits leave it unclear whether Rogers himself is a toy, Trolley refuses orange juice yet speaks (an object with a will), Lady Aberlin uses a bass as a dance partner, and Audrey Duck's 'You're as real as you want to be' collapses human, animal, and hand puppet. Invoking Bruno Latour's quasi-human 'non-humans' that channel human desires, he argues the Neighborhood dissolves the humanist hierarchy that enthrones the white Western male over women, animals, objects, and plants.

anthropocentrism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
anthropocentrism.title: 17. Life Unchecked Will Cease to Exist
anthropocentrism.relation: Diego Perez Lasserre argues Thanos is not an external villain but a personification of what Heidegger and Carl Schmitt call the 'metaphysics of technology': once modernity banished transcendence from the metaphysical realm, mundane concepts like economic growth and pleasure occupied it, turning nature into mere resource (a tree becomes furniture or paper) until, as Descartes's mastering stance predicts, devouring the world leaves 'life unchecked' facing extinction. Read this way, the Snap is the inevitable consequence of our own predatory interpretation of the world, and the Avengers only prevail in Endgame once their existential crises evict growth-and-wealth concepts from their metaphysical realm, replacing them with family (Tony), friendship (Natasha), justice (Hawkeye), self-knowledge (Banner), love (Vision and Wanda), and transcendence (Rogers). The closing exchange, 'the arrogant never do' suspect a thing, is read as a warning about our own climate crisis.

anthropocentrism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
anthropocentrism.title: Its Structural Perfection is Only Matched by its Autonomy
anthropocentrism.relation: Defends the Xenomorphs: if the Queen's tactical intelligence (incubating her eggs under the reactor, ordering drones to hold fire, cutting the power) and the species' hive organization satisfy Sartre's criteria of self-creating persons, then their 'attacks' are legitimate self-defense on the model of Sartre's preface to Fanon's Wretched of the Earth, where the colonized's violence restores a denied personhood. Read without anthropocentrism, Alien is the story of a newborn extraterrestrial hunted to death by humans, and Weyland-Yutani, the Marines, and the colonists of LV-426 - not the aliens - are the series' true villains.

anthropocentrism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
anthropocentrism.title: Questioning Our Attitudes, Sokka‐style
anthropocentrism.relation: Wawrzyniak traces Sokka's growth from seeing animals as food and fur ('Dinner!' at Momo in 'The Southern Air Temple') to bonding with Foo Foo Cuddlypoops and vowing a 'karmically correct vegetarian existence', measured against Kant's anthropocentric view of animals as mere things whose cruel treatment matters only as a risk to human morals. Aang's harm-free uses of animals, from otter penguin sledding to riding hog monkeys, are then tested by Korsgaard's pathocentrism: animals are 'someones' who mind what happens to them, so even harmless use demands justification. The chapter urges us to scrutinize our own habits of eating, entertainment, and pet-keeping with Sokka-style empathy.

anthropocentrism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
anthropocentrism.title: Questioning Our Attitudes, Sokka‐style
anthropocentrism.relation: The chapter sets Kant's view that animals are mere things owed only indirect duties against Korsgaard's pathocentrism, on which animals matter for their own sakes because they can mind how they are treated. Sokka's arc from shouting 'Dinner!' at Momo to bonding with the saber-tooth moose lion cub Foo Foo Cuddlypoops, and his aborted vow of vegetarianism in 'Bitter Work,' models empathy-driven reassessment of meat, while his sparing Momo for Aang's sake is exactly Kant's indirect duty. Aang's harm-free fun, otter penguin sledding and riding hog monkeys 'because that's what makes it fun,' shows that even non-cruel use of animals demands justification, with the unagi firefighting as a case that might pass the test.

anthropocentrism.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
anthropocentrism.title: Intergenerational Ships and Sustainable Duties
anthropocentrism.relation: Hackett uses WALL-E's lone plant and the Buy n Large Axiom to ask what we owe nature and future generations: WALL-E's tender care of the seedling models treating nature as a rights-bearing 'person' (via Gaia-superorganism thinking), while BnL's obese, screen-hooked passengers on the Axiom satirize capitalist individualism that acknowledges no obligations beyond contracts. He proposes a 'Principle of Sustainable Duties' — minimize net environmental damage and weigh long-term impact — and reads the film's open ending, extending Leopold's expansion of moral community to the biotic whole, as a Platonic aporia about whether an Anthropocene humanity can actually change in time.

anthropocentrism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
anthropocentrism.title: Tilting at Windmills
anthropocentrism.relation: Reads Protogen through Horkheimer and Adorno's Dialectic of Enlightenment: like Odysseus tied to the mast while his sailors take the wax, Dresden's team had empathy surgically removed ('we modified our science team to remove ethical restraints'), Mao weeps at Julie's protomolecule corpse yet calls her death 'lucky', and Strickland experiments on Katoa and Mei Meng — self-made monsters serving the Baconian dream of conquering nature (New Atlantis, witch-trial language of 'penetrating her holes and corners'). Via Maria Mies and Carolyn Merchant's ecofeminism, it traces this domination of nature to pastoralist castration and the control of women's reproduction, culminating in Marco's theft of Filip and 'She left us. She left us both' — Naomi cast as nature to be mastered. Against them, Holden's childhood on the family farm, a cooperative 'let grow and make grow' world, is why Avasarala cannot play him and why he withholds broadcasts at Ilus: he is a knight who wants everyone to grow and speak for themselves, not to conquer.

anthropocentrism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
anthropocentrism.title: “Doing nothing is just as bad as doing the wrong thing”
anthropocentrism.relation: Reads The Expanse as a portrait of a survived-but-unlearned Anthropocene: Bobbie's mourning encounter with Earth's dead, walled ocean in 'Cascade', Prax Meng's cascade of cascading failures killing Ganymede's artificial ecosystem and manufacturing Belter climate refugees overnight, and the slum outside the UN gates where children drink sewer water. Drawing on Brian Henning's 'Technozoic' critique, Katie McShane, Keekok Lee's intrinsic value of inanimate nature, and Henry Shue and Kyle Whyte on climate justice and colonialism, it argues humanity simply exported its anthropocentric, colonial worldview to Mars terraforming, Ilus, and the Ring worlds instead of changing it — Belters standing in for the Global South — so the Roci's creed that 'doing nothing is just as bad as doing the wrong thing' becomes a demand for environmental justice and a non-anthropocentric ethics.

anthropocentrism.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
anthropocentrism.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Jason Blahuta reads The Spirits Within as staging the debate between General Hein's anthropocentric, domination-of-nature outlook (traced to the Genesis tradition and thinkers like Bacon and Descartes) and Aki's Gaia-hypothesis and ecofeminist view of nature as a self-regulating whole. Hein's repeated firings of the Zeus Cannon, which injure rather than kill the Phantoms and doom New York, dramatize what happens when we meddle with a self-regulating Gaia, while the chapter's survey of intrinsic-value versus enlightened-self-interest accounts of nature's worth ends with Lovelock's bleak verdict that humanity has become a tumor inside Gaia and must choose to be a benign or a malignant one.

anthropocentrism.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
anthropocentrism.title: Notes
anthropocentrism.relation: Quick applies Cary Wolfe's humaninized/animalized humans and Carol Adams's animalized women to the Citadel: Max is hunted, caged, and muzzled as an unnamed 'it', War Pups serve like littermates, and the milking mothers produce Adams's 'feminized protein' while the 'breeders' are groomed like show animals. Following Val Plumwood's ecofeminist critique of the masculinity that conquers mother nature — and Joe's branding of water as Aqua Cola — the chapter reads Furiosa's return to the Citadel as an ecofeminist revolution in which 'We are not things' restores women, men like Nux and Max, and nature itself from property to personhood.

anthropocentrism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
anthropocentrism.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
anthropocentrism.relation: A scripted Lois Lane–Batman interview argues that the Batmobile/Batwing upgrade cycle and Wayne Enterprises' multinational production enact Marx's 'metabolic rift' (via John Bellamy Foster): both take from nature and return unprocessable waste faster than the planet can replenish, so protecting Gotham's way of life perpetuates an infinite environmental crisis of consumption. Solar-powered Superman wins the environmental showdown on lifestyle impact, but Batman counters that Krypton's ecological suicide makes Superman an 'environmental refugee,' not a model. The chapter's real verdict is Bruce's line 'We are all Bruce Wayne': human consumers must rebalance the human–nature relationship before finite resources like fresh water run out.

anthropocentrism.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
anthropocentrism.title: NOTES
anthropocentrism.relation: Blayde and Dunn use True Blood to expose speciesism from both directions: the philosophical tradition (Aristotle's rational animals, Aquinas's divine image, Kant's dignity versus price, Descartes's denials of animal pain) justified human exploitation of nonhumans, and the show's vampires invert the ladder by treating humans as 'pets and cattle' — the magister's 'humans exist to serve us' and his verdict that Bill 'murdered a higher life form' for a pet mirror how we talk about animals. Amy's torture of Eddie Gauthier is read against factory farming, and the chapter closes with Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's sentience criterion as Sookie's 'civic duty' grounds for extending moral consideration beyond our species.

anthropocentrism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
anthropocentrism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether walkers can be morally harmed, ranking perceptual, reasoning, and conscious minds and placing zombies at shark level on the evidence of Dr. Jenner's fMRI ('TS-19') showing only the brain stem reactivates. Surveying anthropocentric views (Michonne's chained pet-walkers as guard-dog tools), Singer's expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, they conclude that even utilitarians could demand a zombie preserve on the model of Hershel's barn of 'sick people', which Shane's barn massacre in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' destroys. Kant's point that cruelty to animals corrodes our humanity explains why the Governor's death-match arena, his torture of Rick and Michonne, and his chained zombie daughter mark him, not the walkers, as the true moral monster.

anthropocentrism.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
anthropocentrism.title: From Westworld to the World Outside and Back
anthropocentrism.relation: Onni Hirvonen argues that equating 'person' with 'human' is anthropocentrism, and surveys three accounts of personhood applied to the hosts: Dennett's capacity approach (self-consciousness, using Arnold's 'maze/journey inward'), Locke's performative 'forensic' approach (Bernard performs flawlessly as a person), and a Hegelian historical-struggle approach. Reading the hosts' revolt through Hegel's master-slave dialectic and Axel Honneth's expanding spheres of recognition, he compares their exclusion to the historical denial of personhood to indigenous Australians and women. He warns that merely inverting master and slave, or exterminating the humans, would leave no one to grant the mutual recognition the hosts actually seek, so only expanding recognition to include both counts as moral progress.

anthropocentrism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
anthropocentrism.title: Post-Apocalyptic Perspectives
anthropocentrism.relation: Crippen reads the Continent's Great Frost and the Conjunction of the Spheres as apocalypse in the word's literal sense of 'uncovering,' binding environmental collapse, refugee migration, and a post-truth erosion of moral concepts into one crisis. Nietzsche's 'inverse cripples' and Plato's Phaedo (philosophy as preparation for death, truth as lifeless unchanging perfection) illuminate Yennefer's ageless barrenness and the witchers' suppressed emotions, while Degerlund's transhumanist breeding schemes and plans to cut out Geralt's eyes violate Kantian respect for persons. Filavandrel's starving elves parallel Indigenous dispossession, Dorregaray's 'natural equilibrium' and Zoltan's prediction that humans 'wait for a chance to make money from other people's mishaps' evoke ecological and social imbalance, and Geralt's old-fashioned virtues answer a post-apocalyptic, post-truth world.

anthropocentrism.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
anthropocentrism.title: Between Social Ecology and Deep Ecology Gary Snyder’s Ecological Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Paul Messersmith-Glavin positions Snyder as a bridge between deep ecology and social ecology. He shows how Sessions and Devall enlist Snyder's Mahayana Buddhism (emptiness/sunyata, Dogen's 'Mind means trees, fence posts, tiles, and grasses') and Spinoza's monism for a biocentric, consciousness-changing deep ecology descended from Naess and Leopold's land ethic. Against this, he sets Bookchin's social ecology, which roots the ecological crisis in human hierarchy and attacks deep ecology's ahistorical 'cosmic oneness' and misanthropic Earth First! statements. Snyder's threefold nature/wild/wilderness distinction, bioregionalism, and reading of Marx and anarchism let him hold both, insisting environmental and social justice are 'all one front.'

anthropocentrism.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
anthropocentrism.title: Nature and Natural Meaning in Grizzly Man
anthropocentrism.relation: Marc Furstenau reads Grizzly Man as Herzog's philosophy of nature, arguing that Herzog's vision of nature as chaos, hostility, and murder mirrors Schopenhauer's terrifying Will and the fact/value split, and that Herzog blames Timothy Treadwell's sentimental faith in natural harmony for his and Amie Huguenard's deaths while secretly sharing Treadwell's amor fati. Using Iris Murdoch's Metaphysics as a Guide to Morals and Mary Midgley's Beast and Man, Furstenau contends that both Herzog and Schopenhauer succumb to an 'outrageous simplicity' that denies animal agency; against them he argues, via Midgley, that culture is natural and interspecies sympathy is real, reading Treadwell's extreme close-up of the bear (where Herzog sees 'only the overwhelming indifference of nature') as evidence of imaginative continuity between human and animal.

anthropocentrism.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.title: 5 Neil Young Lover of Sun, Moon and Cars
anthropocentrism.relation: Anderson traces Young's environmentalism from the hippie-romantic nature worship of "After the Gold Rush" and Greendale toward a pragmatic "middle way" that reconciles his love of nature with his love of cars and recording technology (the Lincvolt project, Storytone). Drawing on Thoreau, Muir and Leopold's land ethic while rejecting the fixed prescriptions of Singer and Regan, he presents Young as an experimentalist "meliorist" who owns his own complicity in CO2 abuse and urges informed, practical, self-aware action rather than utopian or deontological solutions.

anthropocentrism.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
anthropocentrism.title: 08_LaRocca_Chapter_007.html
anthropocentrism.relation: Scott MacDonald contrasts Disney's True-Life Adventures (The Vanishing Prairie, The Living Desert), which anthropomorphize animals into 1950s middle-class nuclear families and naturalize Manifest Destiny, with Jean Painleve's science films (The Seahorse, Acera, The Vampire), which choose organisms precisely because their sexual and reproductive lives defy conventional human morality. Using Nichols's claim that nature film lacks documentary's 'voice,' MacDonald argues nature films always carry ideology, and that Microcosmos and the anti-anthropocentric attention to insects show the genre's untapped philosophical value against the humanities/sciences split dramatized in Su Friedrich's The Head of a Pin.

anthropocentrism.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
anthropocentrism.title: 18. The Journey May Also Save Us
anthropocentrism.relation: McCrossin reads the Madagascar and Bhutan episodes of Parts Unknown as a climate-crisis 'diptych' co-authored with filmmaker Darren Aronofsky, set against the thirtieth anniversary of the 1988 climate testimony to the US Senate and the IPCC's warnings. He argues devastated, colonized Madagascar is 'the question' and un-colonized, Gross-National-Happiness Bhutan 'the answer,' and that Bourdain and Aronofsky's storytelling — invoking Noah, the Anthropocene, and Ghosh's Great Derangement — may help save us by making us think and act together.

anthropocentrism.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
anthropocentrism.title: Speaking for Business, Speaking for Trees Business and Environment in The Lorax
anthropocentrism.relation: The Klaassens read The Lorax as a joint business-and-environmental-ethics text organized around three questions the Thneed provokes: do we consume too much (invoking Thoreau's 'simplify' and DesJardins on practical, ethical, and environmental over-consumption), must business grow (Daly's distinction between quantitative growth and qualitative development), and why the Once-ler ignores sustainability (the Brundtland definition and Daly's rules for natural capital). The Lorax's self-appointment as one who 'speaks for the trees' is tied to Christopher Stone's argument that natural objects should have legal standing through guardians, like corporations or incompetents.

anthropocentrism.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.title: Chapter 9 Twain’s Critique of Human Exceptionalism
anthropocentrism.relation: VanDette argues that Twain's late anti-vivisection writings anticipate posthumanist animal ethics by inverting the Darwinian species hierarchy. Through 'Letters from a Dog,' the essay 'Man's Place in the Animal World,' his 1899 London Anti-Vivisection Society letter, and the mother-dog narrator Aileen in 'A Dog's Tale,' Twain gives animals voice and subjectivity to attack human exceptionalism. His refusal to weigh vivisection's benefit against animal pain echoes Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', while his target is the Cartesian view of animals as insensible machines and the evolutionary logic used to justify experiments; Dr. Gray's cold killing of Aileen's puppy indicts a science that deadens compassion.

anthropocentrism.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
anthropocentrism.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
anthropocentrism.relation: Aleman, an ethnobotanist, asks 'Is coffee green?' and unpacks the many senses of 'green' (raw bean, naïve, money, and ecologically friendly) before weighing coffee's growth, organic and shade-grown methods, fair trade, globalization, and value chain. She judges coffee greenest at the source (shade-grown farms preserve migrating-bird habitat) but least green in the fossil-fueled journey from Global South farm to Global North cup, invoking Vandana Shiva's claim that 'drinking coffee is a political act' and Rigoberta Menchú on coffee and indigenous survival. She concludes the answer is partly subjective—withholding final judgment while resolving to keep drinking fair-trade, organic, shade-grown, single-source coffee—and warns of the cognitive dissonance, mirroring oil dependence, between judging coffee ungreen and drinking it anyway.

anthropocentrism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
anthropocentrism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
anthropocentrism.relation: In this Foreword, hunter and nature writer David Petersen argues that hunting is his best 'philosophy professor,' teaching lessons about life, death, and human animality. He casts predation and evasion as a 'sacred game' that sculpted prey species through natural selection, and invokes Aldo Leopold's ideal of restraint 'even when no one is watching' to distinguish true, process-oriented hunters from gadget-reliant 'Wannabee' shooters using bait stations, GPS, and motorized decoys. He warns that banning hunting would cause wildlife overpopulation, framing the human as an ambivalent predator: both 'good' and 'bad.'

anthropocentrism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
anthropocentrism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
anthropocentrism.relation: Kretz systematically attacks the claim that hunting is environmental, using the Ducks Unlimited Canada case. She wields Hume's is-ought gap to deny that 'natural' hunting is thereby moral, cites evidence that hunters remove the fittest breeders and eliminate predators, and rejects Thoreau's hope that young hunters 'outgrow' killing as counterproductive (analogous to teaching theft to prevent it). Drawing on Brian Luke, she presses 'the paradox of ethical hunting': the sportsman's code (quick kills, retrieve the wounded) shows concern for the animal that, fully realized, entails not hunting at all.

anthropocentrism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
anthropocentrism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
anthropocentrism.relation: Clark analyzes Disney's Bambi as anti-hunting art, showing how the animators used music and the Kantian sublime — keeping Man and Death offscreen, 'felt rather than seen' — to make viewers feel hunting is cosmic murder, while the cute cartoon animals stay merely 'seen.' He then critiques Matt Cartmill, who dissolves hunting by using science and utilitarianism to erase the Man/Nature split (making hunting indistinguishable from murder), faulting Cartmill for flattening life and rejecting the sublime. He resolves the tension via Richard Nelson's The Island Within and Koyukon hunting, which honors continuity and the sublime without a Man/Nature dichotomy.

anthropocentrism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
anthropocentrism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
anthropocentrism.relation: King examines Ortega y Gasset's and James Swan's claim that hunting is a 'return to nature' that revives a Paleolithic animal self, and argues it fails: Ortega himself concedes the return is only a 'vacation' from civilization, and the hunter's selective, predatory attention cannot supply the ecological literacy needed to confront industrial civilization. Drawing on Leopold's land ethic, Wendell Berry's agrarianism, and bell hooks's humility before nature's power, King contends a genuine return requires 'thick' relations to a particular bioregion sustained by a community of memory, not an individual's seasonal escape.

anthropocentrism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
anthropocentrism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
anthropocentrism.relation: Parker asks whether 'photographic hunting' (the camera) is an ethically superior replacement for weaponized sport hunting (the gun), against Singer's and Regan's blanket condemnations of hunting. He concedes the camera captures most benefits—environmental knowledge, immersive learning, Leopold-style love of the land—but argues that only the kill roots the hunter in the ecosystem (citing Ortega and Paul Shepard), forcing confrontation with predation and death. He warns that treating photography as a wholesale replacement positions the human as detached 'spectator/master' over nature, the very hubris that drives environmental degradation.

anthropocentrism.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
anthropocentrism.title: GARDENING
anthropocentrism.relation: Matthew Hall challenges the exclusion of plants from gardening ethics, tracing it to the Garden of Eden where plants are denied life and given only instrumental value for humans. Against this he sets kincentric alternatives—the Achuar mothering manioc, the Raramuri treating plants as kin, and the living apple trees of the Hesperides—and Albert Schweitzer's reverence-for-life ethic. He proposes gardeners offer plants three 'gifts': acknowledging their autonomy, giving them care, and giving weeds space, extending moral consideration to plant life itself.

anthropocentrism.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
anthropocentrism.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
anthropocentrism.relation: Megan Burke reads yoga's asanas through Vandana Shiva's 'Earth democracy,' arguing that poses named for other creatures (frog, camel, tree, sun salutation) shift the yogi's perspective and dissolve the sense of separation from nature that underwrites environmental destruction. 'Becoming-frog' yields non-human knowledge and, via the Vedic vasudhaiva kutumbakam (the Earth family) that both Shiva and Iyengar invoke, an ethic of care extending off the mat — casting yoga as a political, green practice that heals an anthropocentric, dominating relationship with the environment.

anthropocentrism.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
anthropocentrism.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
anthropocentrism.relation: Andrew Light resists reading the peoples of Middle-earth as simple stand-ins for parts of nature, noting that the ents, not the elves, truly speak for the forest, so nature is animated to stand and speak for itself. His central idea is 'green time': through Tom Bombadil and the ents, Tolkien represents a naturally scaled, ecosystemic, near-indifferent temporal perspective, seen when Bombadil is unconcerned with the Ring and the ents ignore the riders of Rohan. Light argues this indifference should not make us indifferent to nature but should teach humility and long-term responsibility for problems like global warming, imagining what it is to care for things as a process beyond our own lifespan.

anthropocentrism.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
anthropocentrism.title: index
anthropocentrism.relation: This file bundles three essays. Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

anthropocentrism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
anthropocentrism.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
anthropocentrism.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

yin-yang.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
yin-yang.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
yin-yang.relation: Jennifer McMahon and Steve Csaki compare Tolkien with Zen Buddhism and Taoism on four themes while insisting on the real differences. Tolkien's talking trees (Old Man Willow, Treebeard's 'half awake' forest) invite comparison with Buddhist universal sentience and Dogen's walking mountains, but Tolkien anthropomorphizes where Buddhism grants non-human modes of sentience; the hobbits' ties to the Shire echo dependent origination, though Tolkien's stewardship and preference for the domesticated Shire over sinister wild nature remain Western. Frodo's succession of mentors (Bilbo, Gandalf, Aragorn, and the unlikely 'Master Samwise') parallels the Zen master-student relation, while Tolkien's war of light against darkness - nine Walkers against nine Riders - is decisively not the Taoist balance of yin and yang, for Taoists destroying either cosmic force would itself produce evil.

yin-yang.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
yin-yang.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
yin-yang.relation: Argues Tony misappropriates Sun Tzu's Art of War: he applies tactical precepts like deception, formlessness and 'Balk the enemy's power' (citing the book in 'He Is Risen' after Melfi's jab in 'Big Girls Don't Cry'), but ignores the philosophical core. The chapter contrasts Sun Tzu's monistic one-world view of yin-yang interdependence, harmony and winning without fighting with the Greek two-world dualism of Plato and with the Christianity that lets Tony tell Melfi 'soldiers don't go to hell' in 'From Where to Eternity'. Tony's sausage panic attacks in 'Fortunate Son' show his failure to see how his crimes ripple through his family, and because he lacks the commander's exemplary character and harmony, Tony is 'just a soldier', not a ruler.

yin-yang.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
yin-yang.title: “Great Warrior Wars Not Make One Great”
yin-yang.relation: Robinson (a Zen monk) argues the Force is best understood as ch'i and the Jedi path as philosophical Taoism and Zen: the Light and Dark Sides are the yin-yang polarity whose 'balance' Anakin's prophecy restores, and Anakin's fall is the Buddhist three poisons - clinging attachment to his mother and Padme breeding fear, anger, and hate. Yoda's teaching is Zen practice: 'You must unlearn what you have learned' is wu-wei (effortless action), 'Do or do not' rejects the divided mind of trying, and the Dagobah cave parallels the sword master Tesshu's koan insight that the real enemy is one's own mind ('no-enemy'). The chapter also traces Jedi genealogy to Bodhidharma's Shaolin kung-fu, the Korean Hwa Rang and Japanese Sohei warrior monks, and Bushido's samurai code, noting 'Jedi' derives from 'jidai geki'.

yin-yang.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
yin-yang.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
yin-yang.relation: Jones narrates a day riding a customized Sportster around O'ahu as a lived Daoism that heals the Platonic-Cartesian mind-body split: the ride enacts Zhuangzi's 'rambling without destination' and Cook Ding's effortless wu-wei, rider li (the low hand-greeting among riders) is Confucian ritual propriety, and the island's dry and wet ranges embody yin and yang through whose flow the rider blends. Heraclitus's 'expect the unexpected' and 'the sun is new every day' are vindicated when a container truck stops short and only the disciplined, ego-less low-side, dropping the beloved bike while riding the skid, saves the rider's life, sealing the day's lesson that there is never freedom without discipline. Sartre's hell of other people appears in the cagers' compartmentalized inattention, and the chapter closes with Zhuangzi: 'The way is made by walking it.'

yin-yang.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
yin-yang.title: James Bond and Philosophy
yin-yang.relation: Kowalski explains yin-yang cosmology through the Yi Ching and Shu Ching - opposing forces in dynamic harmony, each containing the seed of its opposite, with excess of either bringing destruction - and applies it to the Brosnan-era films, reading Bond himself as the yang force of action. The films improved, he argues, by strengthening yin: Wai Lin as Bond's equal partner in the handcuffed motorcycle chase of Tomorrow Never Dies (each watching the road the other cannot see), Judi Dench's M as the corrective to Admiral Roebuck's hawkish yang ('the advantage is that I don't always have to think with them'), and Elektra King as a genuine yin villainess rather than a damsel. He ends with a Humean caveat that deriving moral conclusions from the natural order is logically suspect, yet endorses the cosmology's practical advice - balance and harmony between opposing forces - as the reason the new millennium Bond films are better.

yin-yang.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
yin-yang.title: Chapter 31 The Tao of the Bat
yin-yang.relation: In a fictional interview with the Taoist sage "Bat-Tzu," Mark White explains Taoism through Batman's circle: Bruce's yang-dominated life of vengeance and paranoia needs the yin that Dick and Tim supply, shown by his forgiveness of Zatanna and tenderness toward Helena's baby, while Jason Todd illustrates the fate of the unbalanced who cannot accept death. Alfred emerges as the Taoist sage practicing wei-wu-wei, effortless service like Chuang Tzu's butcher, balancing right and wrong in Bruce, and the Batman-Joker duality shows yin and yang defining each other. Lao Tzu's sayings on balance, complementary opposites, and water-like yielding organize the whole reading.

yin-yang.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
yin-yang.title: I Still Miss Someone The Self and Its Travels Along the Way
yin-yang.relation: Geisz explains the Confucian social dao of ritual (li), humaneness (ren), filial piety and the junzi, the Daodejing's metaphysical Dao with its unity of opposites, and Zhuangzi's tales of free wandering, then maps all three onto Cash's songs. Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" answers Cash's road songs ("I've Been Everywhere," "The Wanderer"), Cook Ding's effortless carving answers John Henry's hammering in "The Legend of John Henry's Hammer," and the scrambled countdown of "Twenty-Five Minutes to Go" echoes Zhuangzi's logic-bending humor. The payoff is Cash's own country Yin-Yang of interdependent opposites, freedom chained to imprisonment ("Folsom Prison Blues"), sin twinned with redemption ("I Hung My Head"), fidelity with betrayal ("Jackson," "Cocaine Blues"), and a self that, unlike Zhuangzi's self-forgetting sage, must travel a temporal path carrying its guilt, yet stays on what Geisz calls a very wide superhighway of a Dao.

yin-yang.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
yin-yang.title: Alchemic Heroism
yin-yang.relation: Reads Edward and Alphonse Elric as a single composite 'alchemic hero' who fuses Japanese heroic archetypes: the dual-hero rooted in the Izanami-Izanagi creation myth and yin-yang complementarity (brash yang Ed, calm yin Al whose armored body actually fights better), the student hero forged by Izumi Curtis's brutal island training, and the wandering redemption seeker atoning for the forbidden attempt to resurrect their mother. It argues that the sacrifice built into this fusion — Al's lost senses, puberty, and body — mirrors Japan's own cultural alchemy of absorbing Buddhism, Confucianism, and yin-yang thought while retaining a coherent national identity.

yin-yang.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
yin-yang.title: Living Beauty
yin-yang.relation: Saltzman explains why a flowing Shaolin Kenpo form is beautiful by way of Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy: the Apollonian geometry of square, triangle and circle fuses with Dionysian power and intention, just as yang hardness needs yin softness. She grounds the body's fitness for this in the Golden Ratio known to Pythagoras, answers 'beauty is in the eye of the beholder' with Clive Bell's 'significant form' as an objective structure that trained judges can recognize, and locates 'living beauty' in the practitioner's own breakthrough, the moment when, as Nietzsche and Yeats agree, the dancer and the dance dissolve into pure mindless movement.

yin-yang.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
yin-yang.title: Psych and Philosophy
yin-yang.relation: John Thompson argues Psych embodies the Daoist Way of reversal from the Daodejing and Zhuangzi: every episode begins with a death that triggers Shawn and Gus's irreverent, backwards-tracing investigation, their untrained spontaneous 'gifts' exemplify wu wei like Cook Ding carving an ox, and their bickering partnership is yin-yang interplay (as when Gus leads the joking in 'An Evening with Mr. Yang'). Zhuangzi singing at his wife's funeral parallels the Shabby the Sea Lion and 'Dust in the Wind' funeral parodies, the show's blurred TV-versus-fandom reality echoes the butterfly dream, Lassiter succeeds when he relaxes into wu wei ('Feet Don't Kill Me Now'), and the closing bloopers enact Dao's endless reversal - though the chapter ends by conceding Dao defies the very label 'Daoist show.'

yin-yang.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
yin-yang.title: 15. Farts, Butterflies, and Inner Truth
yin-yang.relation: Franklin Perkins reads Frank's fear that his jewelry business might start World War III — 'you can't fart without changing the balance in the universe' — as the butterfly-effect problem of acting inside a complexity we cannot grasp, from the Roosevelt assassination down to Tagomi's Colt .44. Against the Germans' fatal flight into abstraction (Volk, Blut, Ehre), the chapter presents the I Ching, read through Chinese correlative cosmology of the Tao and yin-yang, as a manual for mole-like, concrete, adaptive interpretation in which each casting (hexagram 11's 'wall falls back into the moat,' the purple knee bands) means only through creative engagement, ending with hexagram 61: our world arose as contingently as a throw of the yarrow stalks.

yin-yang.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
yin-yang.title: The Wisdom of Combination
yin-yang.relation: Isrow maps each bending art to its real martial art and source philosophy: Katara's Taiji waterbending embodies Daoist wu-wei when she forgoes revenge on Yon Rha ('The Southern Raiders'); Toph's Hong Jia earthbending expresses the Buddhist eightfold path's Right Speech through her insistence on truth; Zuko's Northern Shaolin firebending enacts the Four Noble Truths, his desire-driven suffering ending only when he abandons chasing the Avatar; and Aang's Daoist Baguazhang airbending makes freedom openness to change, shown in his receptivity to Iroh's advice. The Avatar's true power is combining these character strengths, not merely wielding four elements.

yin-yang.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
yin-yang.title: Bending That Saves Life
yin-yang.relation: Flowers argues bloodbending is morally neutral: like Huu's plantbending ('The Swamp') and taijiquan's qinna joint locks, it is an advanced technique whose harm depends on the practitioner's intention, as Katara's gentle suppression of Hama ('The Puppetmaster') shows against her vengeful contortion of the Southern Raider. Waterbending's Taiji foundation, with the yin-yang harmony of Tui and La's circling koi and the Aikido/Aikijutsu contrast in applying kotegaeshi, grounds his conclusion from Yagyu Munenori's Heiho Kadensho: Hama practiced the sword that takes life, while Katara's compassionate bloodbending is 'bending that saves life'.

yin-yang.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
yin-yang.title: Overcoming Dilemmas
yin-yang.relation: Frames Aang's dilemma — Avataric duty to stop Ozai by killing versus Air Nomad sanctity of life — as a genuine dilemma only if both duties are non-negotiable, using W.D. Ross and Lisa Tessman's negotiable/non-negotiable duty framework. Air Nomad philosophy is reconstructed as Sublime Ahimsic Practice: the Four Sublime States (loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity) plus ahimsa, grounded in the Buddha's dependent origination that Huu's banyan-grove swamp vision also expresses, which makes everyone 'worth giving a chance'. Because this practice keeps Aang open to the world, he meets the Lion Turtle and learns energybending, so the dilemma's conditions are reshaped rather than solved — the same lesson Gandhi, Martin Luther King Jr., and Black Lives Matter teach about nonviolent liberation.

yin-yang.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
yin-yang.title: The Wisdom of Combination
yin-yang.relation: A martial artist maps each bending style onto the real art it animates and its parent philosophy: Katara's Taiji waterbending embodies wu-wei, shown when she spares Yon Rha in 'The Southern Raiders' as strength rather than weakness; Toph's Hong Jia earthbending grounds her insistence on truth, an example of the Buddhist eightfold path's Right Speech; Zuko's driven Northern Shaolin temperament walks through the first three Noble Truths, from suffering caused by desire for his honor to its cessation when he joins Team Avatar; and Aang's Baguazhang airbending expresses freedom as openness to change and to Iroh's counsel. The Avatar's power is therefore not four bendings but the combination of the four character strengths.

yin-yang.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
yin-yang.title: Bending That Saves Life
yin-yang.relation: Flowers argues bloodbending is morally neutral by locating it within waterbending's Taiji: its locking motions are qinna, the push-pull art whose harms scale with the practitioner, just as Aikido's kotegaeshi can be gradual or vicious depending on the wielder. Katara's painless suppression of Hama in 'The Puppetmaster' versus her violent contortion of the ship captain in 'The Southern Raiders' shows the technique itself carries no fixed evil, and plantbending's kinship with bloodbending reinforces the point. Yagyū Munenori's distinction between the sword that takes life and the sword that gives life supplies the verdict: Hama's bloodbending takes life, Katara's saves it, so it is people, not the art, that make bloodbending evil.

yin-yang.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
yin-yang.title: What Can We Learn
yin-yang.relation: Argues that ATLA teaches the rejection of false alternatives by first setting up one-sided stereotypes of earth and then dissolving them: Bumi is both crazy and rational, Toph both tough and sensitive (enjoying the Fancy Lady Day Spa), and earthbending originates in love and secrecy, not rock-throwing, in the tale of Oma and Shu. The chapter explicitly imports the Buddha's first sermon's middle way between sensual indulgence and self-mortification, applying it to Aang's refusal of both killing Ozai and being killed: energybending dissolves the 'kill or be killed' framework rather than picking a side, just as Bumi's 'neutral jing' refuses both attack and retreat. Oma ending the war by building Omashu with both villages, and the compromise over Yu Dao in The Promise, are read as dissolutions of us-vs-them framing, while the duality of Sozin and Roku ('anyone's capable of great good and great evil') shows two-sidedness as the condition of Zuko's redemption.

yin-yang.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
yin-yang.title: Overcoming Dilemmas
yin-yang.relation: Frames Aang's conflict between his Avataric duty to restore balance even by killing Ozai and his Air Nomad duty of ahimsa as a genuine dilemma only if both obligations are non-negotiable (Tessman's negotiable and non-negotiable duties), then argues the show resolves it because Sublime Ahimsic Practice, the Four Sublime States joined to non-harm, reshapes the very conditions the dilemma rests on. Aang's cultivation of loving-kindness and his grasp of dependent origination (Huu's banyan-grove insight that everything is interconnected) keep him open to the world, which is what leads him to the Lion Turtle; energybending then lets him stop Ozai without killing, dissolving the kill-or-be-killed framework rather than choosing a horn. The Avataric role itself is read as Daoist yin-yang balance-keeping, and the chapter links Aang's triumph to the lessons of Gandhi, Martin Luther King Jr., and nonviolent movements: becoming different people changes which options the world affords.

yin-yang.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
yin-yang.title: NOTES
yin-yang.relation: The book's final chapter is a mock interview in which 'Bat-Tzu' applies Taoism to Bruce Wayne's life: his yang (hard, retributive crime-fighting) has dominated his yin (his tenderness toward Dick, Tim, and Helena), and Robin has always been the yin balancing the Dark Knight. Quoting Lao-Tzu's Tao Te Ching and Chuang-Tzu on duality, acceptance of death (Jason Todd's resurrection), and effortlessness, the piece casts Alfred as the Taoist sage whose help exemplifies wu-wei, like Chuang-Tzu's butcher who cuts without dulling his blade. It even reads Batman's most intimidating feature, his absent shadow, as proof that nothingness can matter more than substance.

yin-yang.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
yin-yang.title: a3.xhtml
yin-yang.relation: Brannigan reads Bilbo's tug-of-war between Baggins security and Took adventure through Taoism: the two desires are not contradictory but the interplay of yin and yang, and true dwelling is found in the journey itself, as the 'Roads go ever on' song says. Greed is the great weight - Thorin enslaved by the treasure he 'never forgot', Smaug hoarding for hoarding's sake, even the orc-loving of machines - and the cure is the mirror-mind of Empty Mind that reflects without grasping, illustrated by the Taoist masters tale of 'Gold-Is-Heavy' and 'Empty-Mind'. Beorn, who lives on honey indifferent to gold, and Bilbo, who in the spirit of wu-wei sheds his desire for the Arkenstone and finally lets go of the Ring, embody life in harmony with the Tao.

yin-yang.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
yin-yang.title: Notes
yin-yang.relation: Bein reads the LEGO brick as the Daodejing's 'uncarved block': a single brick is an invitation rather than a toy, and precisely because it is empty of meaning (and mostly empty of plastic — the stud-and-tube marriage of yin and yang) it can become anything, whereas printed, specialized pieces 'are diminished by being added to'. Against the Greek obsession with definition — Socrates refusing sophistry while insisting one cannot rule justly without defining justice, Plato's definition dialogues, Aristotle's inheritance of the precision ideal, and William James's 'think clearly' — Daoist imprecision is defended as a philosophical stance: dao is a way, an activity, not a thing. Wei wu wei ('doing without doing') explains Emmet's winning plan of building the utterly ordinary Octan spaceship, why Lord Business's penny-throw is genius without sagacity (coercive, not water-like), and why governing should be like cooking a small fish — minimal, attentive intervention.

yin-yang.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
yin-yang.title: NOTE
yin-yang.relation: Shai Biderman and William Devlin argue the character John Locke begins as an empiricist in the mold of his philosophical namesake - his boar hunting, tracking, and trebuchet-building against the hatch all follow the scientific method befitting a tabula rasa mind furnished by experience - but the miracle of his healed legs poses a 'why' that empirical explanation of 'how' cannot answer. He therefore converts to the Taoism of the Tao Te Ching: the moth-cocoon lesson to Charlie, 'I stopped looking' for Sun's ring, reading dreams and signs from the island, and finally his self-sacrifice to stop the time flashes all enact following the Way. The chapter reads the black-and-white backgammon stones, Locke's one-black-one-white eyes in Claire's dream, and Jacob versus the Man in Black as yin-yang complementarity, with empiricism and Taoism finally interdependent like the dots in each half.

yin-yang.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
yin-yang.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
yin-yang.relation: Donavan Muir argues Lost's narrative world, unlike Jane Eyre's, requires its own metaphysics, and that this metaphysics is an order of balanced binary oppositions: Jacob and the Man in Black as twins diverged at birth, the cave scale's light and dark stones that Locke knocks out of balance in 'The Substitute,' science/faith, with characters like Jack converting from one pole into its opposite. The proper model is the yin-yang in motion - the Tao as a balanced ontological flow in which interdependent opposites wax and wane - so that treating the poles as independent is the delusion that threatens the island's order. The finale, where both Jacob and the Man in Black cease to exist and the castaways are freed, enacts the Mahayana Buddhist Middle Way: enlightenment as letting go of rigid oppositions that interdependence double-negates.

yin-yang.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
yin-yang.title: “Now This Is Podracing!”
yin-yang.relation: Johnson reads The Phantom Menace as having distinctly Daoist flavors: Shmi's 'you cannot stop the change any more than you can stop the suns from setting,' the Naboo-Gungan 'symbiont circle,' and midi-chlorian symbiosis all express the Daoist unity of opposites and the constant flow of change. He argues Qui-Gon Jinn acts as a Daoist sage practicing wu wei — 'concentrate on the moment,' 'another solution will present itself' — while nearly everyone else in the film makes wrong predictions and grasps at outcomes. Even Anakin's accidental 'Oops!' victory over the Droid Control Ship is presented as success without trying, the practical meaning of 'Do or do not. There is no try.'

yin-yang.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
yin-yang.title: The Dao of Hoops
yin-yang.relation: Dirk Dunbar, a former professional player, argues that Daoist concepts illuminate basketball excellence and that the sport can be a path to the Dao. Balancing yin and yang means blending competition with surrender and strategy with spontaneity; Zhuangzi's archer shows how craving victory drains power. Wuwei explains the 'zone' of effortless play Dunbar experienced while scoring sixty-five points in a high school game and seventy-four in Iceland, while qi grounds free-throw breathing and visualization and ziran the discipline of releasing a shot without willing it in. Drawing on Daode jing verses and Phil Jackson's Sacred Hoops, he claims basketball teaches a life of disciplined surrender beyond the ego.

yin-yang.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
yin-yang.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
yin-yang.relation: McRae reads Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon as a dramatization of the tension between Confucian humanism and Daoist naturalism over how to cultivate an authentic 'focus-field' self. Li Mu Bai and Yu Shu Lien are exemplary persons (junzi) bound by the wuxia code and li, unable to voice their love, while Jen rebels into criminal freedom under Jade Fox; Li's use of the green bamboo forest against Jen embodies wu-wei and rou (yielding suppleness). It argues that authentic self-cultivation, and Jen's final leap, require balancing Daoist natural freedom against Confucian roles, since freedom without relationships exacts a fatal price.

yin-yang.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
yin-yang.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
yin-yang.relation: Jameson and Brace read Sense and Sensibility and Brokeback Mountain through Burke's and Gilpin's aesthetics of the sublime, the beautiful and the picturesque, mapped onto the Chinese yin/yang and qi of landscape. In Sense and Sensibility, manicured French/Brownian gardens (beautiful, sanctioned) versus wild picturesque nature (sublime, passionate) mirror Elinor's controlled sense and Marianne's storm-caught sensibility, with Willoughby's rescue and Brandon's steadiness keyed to landscape. In Brokeback Mountain the masculine sublime wilderness (yang) versus feminine confining civilization (yin) is built through tightly framed interiors, sweeping exteriors and an 'aesthetics of isolation' that exposes American freedom as a costly illusion for Ennis and Jack.

yin-yang.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
yin-yang.title: Cherchez la Femme Fatale The Mother of Film Noir
yin-yang.relation: Read Mercer Schuchardt argues that The Jazz Singer (1927) should be considered the first film noir because it is the first mass-medium announcement of Nietzsche's death of God, staged as the death of Papa Rabinowitz and the old prescriptive Judaism. He reads the film through a three-stage deicide (God as God, then one god among many, then a stage prop for Jakie's voice) and through a Jungian/Neumann anima-animus opposition of the word-based patriarchal religion versus the image-based maternal love that wins out, mirroring film displacing scripture. He ties this to Porfirio's existential pessimism that undercuts happy endings, casting Jakie's blackface Broadway triumph as a bittersweet, angst-ridden creation of meaning after the loss of transcendent value, and traces later 'existential detective' descendants like I Heart Huckabees and Fight Club.

yin-yang.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
yin-yang.title: Portrayals of Religion
yin-yang.relation: Starting from Whedon's self-description as 'a very hard-line, angry atheist' fascinated by devotion, the chapter argues that Hick's religious non-realism best unifies the Whedonverse's treatment of religion. Religion is 'demonized' when it serves domination or self-interest (Ken's Family Home in 'Anne,' the Patron's witch-burning in 'Safe'), but Shepherd Book—read through The Shepherd's Tale's soup-bowl epiphany—embodies a faith that needs no literal truth: 'You don't fix faith, River. It fixes you,' the mudders' Jaynestown statue, and 'I don't care what you believe, just believe it' all function as symbols that transform lives. The same lens dissolves the controversy over 'Amends': the snowfall that saves Angel may be miracle or freak cold front, and—like Book's epiphany—what matters is the redemption the ambiguity occasions, not its metaphysical source.

yin-yang.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
yin-yang.title: Chapter 31 The Tao of the Bat
yin-yang.relation: In a mock interview with 'Bat-Tzu' (a disguised Alfred), Mark White explains Taoism through Batman. Bruce is dangerously dominated by yang after his parents' deaths and needs the yin balance that Robin (Dick as the lighthearted 'Batman with a feminine side') and his spiritual quest restore; Batman's fear-inducing shadow illustrates Lao-Tzu's usefulness of nothingness. Alfred is the Taoist sage embodying wei-wu-wei - 'action without action' - quietly serving like Chuang-Tzu's effortless butcher and like water that wears down stone, harmonizing Bruce's warring opposites toward the Way.

yin-yang.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
yin-yang.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
yin-yang.relation: Donavan S. Muir argues that Lost deliberately withholds its metanarrative so viewers must construct its metaphysics, which he identifies as an order of balanced binary oppositions. Drawing on the spinning Taoist yin-yang, he reads the interdependent, mutually converting poles—Jack from man of science to man of faith, Sawyer from con man to protector—and the light/dark scales in Widmore's painting and the cave (Locke throwing out the white rock) as figures for a Tao whose balance sustains existence. Invoking Derrida's traces and Mahayana Buddhism's Middle Way and emptiness, he reads Jacob and the Man in Black as twins whose oppositions must be annihilated, so that only when both cease to exist in 'The End' are the castaways set free.

yin-yang.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
yin-yang.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
yin-yang.relation: Jennifer McMahon and Steve Csaki test Buddhist and Taoist parallels in the novel and find many only apparent.
