Like philosophy from Socrates on, Trek is presented as 'an entertaining, edifying preparation' for living by one's ideals, a life-education primer sealed with Roddenberry's advice to 'slip in a heavy idea or two.'

will-to-believe.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
will-to-believe.title: “Something to Believe In”
will-to-believe.relation: Reads Worf's crisis over the clone 'second coming' of Kahless in 'Rightful Heir' as a live, forced, and momentous option in William James's sense, where 'faith creates its own verification.' Peirce's methods of fixing belief — tenacity, authority, and science — explain why Worf cannot accept Koroth's pious fraud once Gowron's DNA test exposes the clone, while Data's own 'leap of faith' in believing he is more than a machine supplies the Jamesian model of believing without evidence. Worf's compromise — telling the Klingon people the truth but installing Kahless-the-clone as spiritual emperor because 'the words are more important than the man' — is offered as pragmatist truth: what works while staying answerable to hard facts.

will-to-believe.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
will-to-believe.title: “Trip Around the Sun”
will-to-believe.relation: Phil Oliver pairs Buffett with William James: both hold that philosophy is 'not a technical matter' but each person's sense of what life deeply means, had in non-verbal moments of elevation as much as argued in words. The chapter's core is James's 'moral holiday' — a morally legitimate respite from care and struggle — naturalized in Buffett's 'License to Chill' and 'Trip Around the Sun' ('it's good to know it's out of my control'), joined by James's lightness about error from 'The Will to Believe' and Russell's and Dawkins's responses to cosmic annihilation. Against those who hear mere hedonism, Oliver insists Jamesian holidays are care-free but never care-less: like Thoreau's 'live deliberately' echoed in 'Growing Older But Not Up,' they renew us for the return to work, and James's ambivalence about alcohol in The Varieties of Religious Experience mirrors the risk of Buffett's frozen concoctions.

will-to-believe.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
will-to-believe.title: Wishing and Dogmatism
will-to-believe.relation: Matthew Pierlott argues Colbert the satirist conflates two things his character, Stephen, merges: truthiness (trusting gut and heart over external authorities like dictionaries) and bullshit in Frankfurt's exact sense - speech indifferent to truth, which Pierlott finds in Hillary Clinton's dismissal of economists on the gas-tax holiday and likens to Steve Careill's habitual pleasantries versus Jon Stewart's honesty and Stephen's lies. He defends gut and heart as evidence-bearing tools - knowing a candidate's 'heart' from character evidence (the Westmoreland Ten Commandments interview), gut intuitions as unconsciously processed experience, and choosing which of the two Cheneys (1994 quagmire prophet or 2003 liberators booster) to trust - so in an information-saturated democracy truthiness is a necessary part of any orientation toward truth. The real enemy is dogmatism, the 'Dark Side of Truthiness' that cuts off future evidence, while wishful thinking kept modest (optimism that people are honest) can even be beneficial, a Jamesian willing-to-believe.

will-to-believe.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
will-to-believe.title: Questioning the Question
will-to-believe.relation: Hartung takes Ross's snapping reply to Armitage's repeated 'Why are you helping me?' in Armitage the Third: Poly-Matrix as a misreading: she wants a practical reason for his choice, not theoretical evidence, and since no evidence can prove an android is a person, William James's 'Will to Believe' applies — Ross's belief in her moral standing is a live, forced, and momentous genuine option (suspending judgment means she is scrapped, and losing her means losing a possible life together), so his passions may legitimately decide. He contrasts this with evidentialist cases where suspending judgment is right (the shuttle company skipping inspection; Dr. Asakura's silicon-based-life hypothesis) and with Pascal's Wager, reading Mars's church-empty, hedonistic culture of sex-tourism Seconds as one that denies genuine options and so kills Thirds. The attached original screenplay 'Eye Am,' a sequel to Magnetic Rose, extends the theme as salvage officer Nadine Beckner is lured by the AI Eva/Sam impersonating her dead husband Heintz, with Schrodinger-style observer-affected reality deciding which version becomes real.

will-to-believe.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
will-to-believe.title: Do You Believe It
will-to-believe.relation: Patrick Tiernan argues that Fenway fandom is a genuine religion: William James's four marks of mystical experience (ineffability, noetic quality, transiency, passivity) map onto memories of Buckner's error and Dave Roberts's steal, and Peter Berger's 'signals of transcendence' structure the rituals of Truck Day, the hopes of spring training, the damnation of Bucky Dent and Johnny Damon, and the humor of 'Cowboy Up.' He roots the Curse of the Bambino in New England's Puritan-Calvinist legacy of persecution and original sin (Frazee's sale of Ruth), then deploys Hume's account of superstition from 'Of Superstition and Enthusiasm' to deflate the exorcism rituals fans actually performed, from a Sox hat on Everest to dredging for Ruth's piano, as post hoc fallacies. Even so, the rituals reveal the human need for religious practice, and Maslow's peak experience renders the 2004 comeback a brush with the sacred, so the Faithful believe because they have to.

will-to-believe.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
will-to-believe.title: Futurama and Philosophy
will-to-believe.relation: Hamer tests sanity against truth using Kierkegaard's asylum anecdote - the escapee intoning 'Boom, the earth is round' proves his insanity precisely by resting it on objective fact - and applies it to 'Insane in the Mainframe,' where Fry, wrongly committed to a robot asylum, is only released once he subjectively believes he is a robot, and to 'The Sting,' where comatose Leela's plan to keep Fry's corpse under her mattress to 'prove I'm not insane' fails the same traitorous way. Pure objectivity cannot certify sanity and pure subjectivity licenses lunacy, so the chapter brings in James's 'The Will to Believe': some beliefs must be held first before their evidence can even count. Fry, who abandons his robot belief the moment his knife-nick bleeds human blood, models the justified believer who pursues the objective truth subjectively.

will-to-believe.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
will-to-believe.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
will-to-believe.relation: The chapter compares Barney's 'True story' pronouncements with William James's pragmatism, using James's squirrel anecdote and the 'Zoo or False' monkey-mugging to ask when an evidentially undecidable dispute becomes a live practical question. Like James's pragmatic cases for free will and religious comfort, Barney's monkey story and the twenty-eight-year-old 'with some sun damage' are beliefs made true by their practical (mostly entertainment) value, then replaced like outdated theories when new evidence arrives, as James's consistency requirement demands. The divergence: the Barney Stinson (BS) theory of truth is self-serving, engineering unverifiable stories others cannot disprove, while James weighs what works for everyone's experience.

will-to-believe.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
will-to-believe.title: 8. I Will Never Doubt Again
will-to-believe.relation: Watson and Guidry-Grimes ask whether Buttercup was rational to accept the evidence that Westley was dead, and whether Westley's Fire Swamp optimism and Inigo's twenty-year hunt for the six-fingered man are wishful thinking or something better. After laying out the evidentialist tradition (Descartes's rule of evidence, Hume's 'a wise man proportions his belief to the evidence,' Clifford's condemnations), they use Adrienne Martin's account of hope as 'endorsed desire plus uncertainty' to argue that value-shaped belief can be rational when it sustains well-being and character. Their conclusion expands rationality beyond evidence-tracking: hope, unlike wishful thinking, takes evidence seriously while balancing it against what makes a life good, which is why Buttercup's despair on the wedding night, not her earlier resignation, is the real failure.

will-to-believe.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
will-to-believe.title: 16. You Made Me First
will-to-believe.relation: The chapter argues that origin stories fix character: Batman, forged by watching his parents murdered (and in Burton's film by the Joker himself - 'You made me first'), is trapped by a past that sets his trajectory, since as Schopenhauer said we can do what we will but cannot will what we will. Kal-El's origin is instead an act of hope - his parents launch him into the universe believing the wildly unlikely - which the chapter reads through William James's will-to-believe, the same faith Bruce needs to jump the chasm unroped in The Dark Knight Rises. Because the past causes the future and 'I can do whatever I want' is not free will, Bruce can never escape his tragedy, while Superman's hopeful origin lets him believe, and make us believe, that we might yet fly.

will-to-believe.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
will-to-believe.title: 13. Linus’s Wager
will-to-believe.relation: The chapter stages a three-way debate over whether Linus may believe in the Great Pumpkin without evidence. Clifford's ethics of belief (the ship-owner whose wishful thinking sinks his ship) condemns Linus's sincerity-based wager; Pascal's Wager endorses it (forgoing one night of trick-or-treating costs nothing if the Pumpkin is fake and wins toys if he is real) but assumes a doxastic voluntarism we lack, since no one can make themselves believe for even a million-dollar reward. William James's 'The Will to Believe' gets the final word: if Linus's option is live, forced, and momentous with no decisive evidence either way, his leap of faith - like loving without guarantees - is morally justified whenever life would be greatly impoverished without it.

will-to-believe.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
will-to-believe.title: 16. I Should Have Known It
will-to-believe.relation: Watkins reads the later albums Mojo and Hypnotic Eye ("Power Drunk," "Burnt Out Town," "Playing Dumb," "Shadow People") through Clifford's ethics of belief: the powerful suppress their doubts like the unseaworthy shipowner and come to sincerely believe their own lies, while the overpowered hide behind the cliche that everyone is entitled to an opinion. Because belief formation is a doing inseparable from action, there is a moral obligation to hold beliefs to evidentiary standards, we should have known, and James's will-to-believe and fideist appeals (Tertullian, Pascal, Kierkegaard) offer no license for self-serving faith. Facing the evidence in front of us is the first step to telling the power-drunk it is the last time they are going to hurt us.

will-to-believe.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
will-to-believe.title: 5. Greatness or Nothingness
will-to-believe.relation: Courtland Lewis uses KISS's career gambles to compare theories of decision-making. After Tolstoy's twig-over-the-dragon allegory of mortal life, he tests W.K. Clifford's shipowner (never act without sufficient evidence) against KISS's counter-evidence bet on the Alive! live album, models the choice with Pascal's Wager, and uses the Prisoner's Dilemma to explain the flop of the four 1978 solo albums. He then argues William James's pragmatism — beliefs as rules for action, the living, forced, and momentous option that 'KISS is the best' — best explains why acting on the band's self-created narrative was authentic, with Nietzsche completing the picture: greatness requires leaping, living dangerously, tightrope-walking toward self-defined success.

will-to-believe.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
will-to-believe.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
will-to-believe.relation: Malloy examines Walter's incorrigible leaps — Bunny kidnapped herself on no evidence, the toe is a fake ('I can get you a toe by three o'clock'), the Big Lebowski can walk — through Clifford's ethics of belief (the ship-owner who sinks his passengers) and James's 'Will to Believe' reply with its living, forced, and momentous genuine options, applied to Walter's 'dabbled' pacifism and his preference for Nazism's ethos over nihilism's nothing. Walter's conversion to Judaism for Cynthia raises whether practice can will belief, tested via Pascal's wager and James's objection, and the verdict borrows Bernard Williams: we cannot choose beliefs, but Walter's reckless policy of dismissing counterevidence makes him 'not just an asshole, he is also wrong'.

will-to-believe.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
will-to-believe.title: Francis Griffin and the Church of the Holy Fonz: Religious Exclusivism and Real Religion
will-to-believe.relation: Johnson argues that Francis Griffin's Catholic exclusivism (condemning Lois the Protestant to purgatory, calling Meg a harlot, founding Peter's Church of the Holy Fonz an 'abomination') is unjustified and immoral. Using Plantinga on exclusivism and a Quagmire-style inductive argument ('SHiTE' — Scripture, Historical tradition, religious Experience — leads rival religions to incompatible truths, so it is an unreliable witness like Quagmire's false alibis), he holds that no one's religious beliefs are adequately justified. Weighing Clifford's ethics of belief (the unseaworthy ship) against James's will to believe, he concludes one may hold beliefs without evidence but may not harm others or forcibly evangelize on their basis. The heap/sorites puzzle shows no criterion marks Fonzieism as an 'unreal' religion — Peter's founding experience parallels Joseph Smith's — so the moral is religious acceptance: disagree freely, but keep your SHiTE to yourself.

will-to-believe.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
will-to-believe.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
will-to-believe.relation: Johnson uses 'Go God Go's' future of 2546—where Dawkins-style atheism has become a warring religion and otter scientists intone 'Oh my Science!'—to ask whether science and religion genuinely conflict and whether New Atheism is itself a faith. Applying abduction and the four criteria of adequacy, he argues the embellished-story hypothesis beats miracle claims about Jesus (whose legend grew Gospel by Gospel), Sathya Sai Baba, Joseph Smith, and Xenu, that Mr(s). Garrison's 'you can't disprove God' and the show's sarcasm commit an appeal to ignorance, and that Stan's water-into-wine scene with Jesus shows how easily people are fooled. He allows Kuhnian theory change in science but rejects James's will-to-believe for existence claims—the moon whale Willzyx needs evidence—and concludes Parker and Stone are unfair to Dawkins: ending religion would not end violence, but it would remove the easiest justification for it, and some answers are simply true even when unknown.

will-to-believe.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
will-to-believe.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
will-to-believe.relation: Dueck takes Stan's closing pluralism in 'Super Best Friends'—all religions have something valuable to teach, as the interfaith superheroes' combined powers defeat Blaine—and tests it against Hick's pluralism, exclusivism, and Rahner's inclusivist 'anonymous Christians', using 'Go God Go's warring atheist factions to show exclusivity is unavoidable even without God. Hume's miracle argument explains why Jesus's look-away water-into-wine trick convinces no one in the episode: testimony can never outweigh the laws of nature, so supernatural evidence resists natural evaluation. Popper's falsificationism warns that watering doctrines down to make religions compatible (the rabbit-pope of 'Fantastic Easter Special') leaves nothing to test, while James's will to believe and Plantinga's defense of exclusivism ground the conclusion that faith can be rationally justifiable where evidence runs out—beware the Blainetologists, but do not surrender ways of life that define us.

will-to-believe.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
will-to-believe.title: 16. You Made Me First
will-to-believe.relation: Starting from the Joker's 'You made me' / Batman's 'You made me first' exchange in Tim Burton's Batman, the chapter argues origin stories fix character: Bruce's witnessed trauma destines him to darkness (and we expect his death to match), while Kal-El is sent to Earth as an act of hope that the chapter reads through William James's will-to-believe—belief itself makes success possible, like Bruce's ropeless leap in The Dark Knight Rises. Against 'I can do whatever I want' free will it deploys Schopenhauer's 'we can do what we will, but we cannot will what we will': Bruce cannot will away his vengeance, and Red Son's Soviet-raised Superman shows biology and upbringing determining who Clark becomes. Superman still wins because his origin story permits the hope that Bruce's cannot.

will-to-believe.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
will-to-believe.title: Notes
will-to-believe.relation: Baggett sets W. K. Clifford's evidentialism (the negligent shipowner; believing on insufficient evidence is a 'sin against mankind') against William James's precursive faith, which permits believing ahead of the evidence when an option is forced, live, momentous, and evidentially undecided. He applies this to Sam's taping over the Dubai Air logo as social-coordination faith, Richmond's belief that it can finally beat Everton, romantic risk-taking like Roy and Keeley's, and the marriage of belief with hard work (Ted's practice tirade, Nate's False Nine), ending with James and Pascal on how evidential ambiguity about God makes a passional step of faith rational.

will-to-believe.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
will-to-believe.title: Detection and the Logic of Abduction in The X-Files
will-to-believe.relation: Abrams and Cooke map Mulder and Scully onto Holmes and Watson and onto the Clifford-James debate: Scully embodies Clifford's ethics of belief (suspend judgment without hard evidence), while Mulder's 'I Want to Believe' poster enacts James's will to believe, which lets him see what the paradigm excludes. The chapter formalizes both agents' actual method as Peirce's logic of abduction, using Eco's overcoded/undercoded/creative triad to analyze Scully's Fowley clothing inference and the mushroom episodes of 'Field Trip', and extends Peircean semiotics with Mulder's 'absence sign' (the missing nine minutes, missing acid burns, bodies taken without a trace). Kuhn's normal science versus revolution explains why Scully stays inside the FBI's paradigm while Mulder's passion makes him the revolutionary who, with Scully as error-corrector, fuses into a single 'whole person' detective facing the limits of reason.

will-to-believe.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
will-to-believe.title: Inception and Perception
will-to-believe.relation: Jamie Carlin Watson uses Inception's dream thieves to stage the dream argument for skepticism - from Socrates' puzzle to Theaetetus and Descartes's Meditations, with Sextus Empiricus's diversity-of-perception argument - and contends that totems cannot debunk it, since even Arthur's loaded die and Cobb's top cannot rule out being in your own dream, where your subconscious knows how the totem behaves. Against both believing as normal and Pyrrhonian suspension of judgment, the chapter turns to William James's will to believe (live versus dead hypotheses) and to intellectual virtues drawn from Zagzebski and Kornblith: beliefs can be valuable for reasons other than truth. The upshot is that Cobb, Arthur, and the twelve shared-dream sleepers in Yusuf's basement can believe well even if they cannot believe truly - which is why Cobb's walking away from the spinning top at the end can be read as believing carefully rather than certainly.

will-to-believe.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
will-to-believe.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
will-to-believe.relation: Silverman uses Battlestar Galactica to explore knowledge as justified true belief. Adama's 'true lie' about knowing Earth's location makes Starbuck's belief in Earth a Gettier case, a justified true belief resting on false justification. He tests Adama's testimony against Goldman's reliabilism (sight is unreliable for spotting Cylons; memory deceives Boomer and Tigh) and Hume's skepticism about testimony versus Plantinga's defense of it. Finally, against Clifford's evidentialism he deploys William James's 'will to believe,' arguing that faith in Earth is a forced, momentous choice that gives the Colonials purpose.

will-to-believe.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
will-to-believe.title: Time Belongs to the Tower
will-to-believe.relation: Auxier frames King as 'Tolkien meets Poe' and reads the Dark Tower's temporalization through the literary and psychological experience of time. Drawing on Susanne Langer's 'virtual present' and Sartre's psychology of imagination, he argues readers surrender their real present to a novel's suspended time, which he links to William James's 'will to believe' rather than mere suspension of disbelief. He uses Kant's distinction between amazement (seeing the seemingly impossible) and admiration (accepting it) to explain the psychological cost time travelers like Jake Epping and Wesley Smith should pay, faulting King for keeping ordinary heroes sane while displacing the strain onto insane 'gatekeepers,' and concludes the Tower is 'real' as the way each person binds possibility to their own lived past, present, and future.

will-to-believe.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
will-to-believe.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
will-to-believe.relation: In this Foreword, John Rousmaniere argues that sailing's 'numinous' moments — like his own experience of stillness on a becalmed ketch mid-Atlantic, when the skipper cut the engine and the crew felt suspended between sky and sea — are paths to genuine philosophical truths, not embarrassing flights of fancy. He enlists William James's 'Varieties of Religious Experience' and James's nautical metaphor for free will (the passenger who volunteers to take the helm) to argue that such mystical feelings can 'team up' with reason rather than opposing it. He insists mystery and craft must work together: piety is no substitute for seamanship (Shelley drowned in an unseaworthy boat), yet competence and numinous experience nurture each other.

will-to-believe.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
will-to-believe.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
will-to-believe.relation: Johnson argues that the Santa Claus lie is immoral and should be abandoned, giving three reasons: it is deceptive lying (Kant's absolute prohibition is too strong, but the lie lacks life-saving justification and functions as a Platonic 'noble lie' no more noble than a cult leader's); Santa robs parents of credit and warps children's moral development and trust, illustrated by anguished 'finding out' stories and Virginia O'Hanlon's letter; and it damages credulity, invoking Clifford's 'Ethics of Belief' against belief on insufficient evidence while James's 'Will to Believe' cannot rescue Santa since evidence against him is overwhelming. He recommends revealing the truth early, even via a Socratic-Method questioning game.

will-to-believe.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
will-to-believe.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
will-to-believe.relation: Roche's 'Seeing Snakes' attacks the psychedelicist claim (William James on nitrous oxide, Huxley's 'reducing valve,' Leary) that drugs including cannabis reveal reality-as-it-is. He deploys Russell's line that we 'can make no distinction between the man who eats little and sees heaven and the man who drinks much and sees snakes,' and a reliabilist demand that knowledge have a source proven reliable over independently verifiable cases, to argue drug 'revelations' are indistinguishable from delusion. Foucault is cited that drugs have 'nothing to do with truth and falsity,' and Nietzsche's Dionysian veil-of-Maya passage is used as an example of the mystical rhetoric he debunks.

will-to-believe.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
will-to-believe.title: NOTES
will-to-believe.relation: Hare treats mass photography—from the daguerreotype through digital cameras, Abu Ghraib snapshots, and diagnostic imaging—as making everyone a practicing epistemologist caught between two folk tenets: the photo as mirror of reality and as manipulation of reality. Defending photography as a genuine causal 'mode of seeing' (a prosthetic like telescopes), he proposes 'flexible realism,' adjusting Dewey's warranted assertibility and virtue-epistemology standards to context, and invokes William James's defense of beneficial 'overbeliefs' when National Geographic images strengthen confidence in one's own culture. Reading the Fallujah lead-pipe photo debate between editors Sullivan and Kushner, he uses Quine's recalcitrant-experience and web-of-belief holism—extended by Morton White's 'holistic pragmatism'—to show moral, epistemic, sensory, and emotional claims are tested together, and frames photography's democratization via Walter Benjamin's mechanical reproduction and loss of aura.

will-to-believe.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
will-to-believe.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
will-to-believe.relation: Eric Silverman uses Battlestar Galactica's Adama, who lies that he knows Earth's location, to run the Gettier problem: Starbuck's true belief that Earth exists rests on a false justification (that Adama knows), so it is justified-true-belief without being knowledge. He tests testimony via Goldman's reliabilism (sight is unreliable for telling Cylons from humans) and the Hume/Locke/Plantinga debate over testimony's epistemic role. He closes with James's 'will to believe': faith in Earth is a forced, momentous choice where agnosticism forfeits meaning, so belief without certainty can be reasonable.

hegel-geist.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
hegel-geist.title: Kierkegaard Lays It Down
hegel-geist.relation: Willie Young uses the sacrifice bunt (Derek Jeter's perfect one versus Placido Polanco's failed one) to test philosophical accounts of sacrifice. Aristotle treats bunting for teammates as friendship and civic virtue in the polis, while Seneca's Stoic sacrifices only to exercise virtue itself, detached from particular friends and refusing retaliation for hit batters. Hegel's modern ideal of self-renunciation makes the player a cog in the team machine (the Big Red Machine), obeying the manager's calculations; against this, Kierkegaard's Abraham, whose absolute duty to God is 'higher than the universal' through infinite resignation, exposes baseball's mechanical, manager-ordered sacrifice and asks whether the game trains obedient citizens who sacrifice as they are told.

hegel-geist.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
hegel-geist.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
hegel-geist.relation: Lawler charges that Gibson's atonement theology, in which the more barbaric the torture the greater the redemption, imprisons Christianity at the stage of Hegel's 'Unhappy Consciousness', where an infinite God is sundered from abject sinful humanity and a priestly mediator is needed. Reading the film through the master-slave dialectic (impotent master Pilate versus the dignified slave Simon of Cyrene; the world of separate egos as Hobbes's war of all against all), he argues that what dies on the cross is the separate ego itself, and that what rises is Geist, the 'I' that is 'We' of the loving human community. Against Tertullian's credo quia absurdum, and using Pascal's 'heart has its reasons' alongside Hegel's dialectical reason, he reads 'you are gods' and the prodigal son as teaching every person's essential divinity, so the film's own art (the Mater Dolorosa, our identification with the flesh-and-blood Jesus) implicitly undermines the separatist theology Gibson intends.

hegel-geist.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
hegel-geist.title: The Force of Love
hegel-geist.relation: Lawler identifies Hegel's Absolute Spirit with the Force: Hegel's distillation of religious history - divine nature (the Ewoks worshipping C-3PO), the Roman Empire's transcendent Unhappy Consciousness, and Christianity's Consummate Religion - maps onto the saga's movement, with Anakin's virgin birth, prophecy, fall, and Calvary-like redemption fulfilling the pattern differently from the sinless Savior. The Dark Side is the separate ego asserting 'I' against 'We' (Hobbes's war of all against all culminating in the Emperor), and sin is the belief that one is an isolated individual. Against the Jedi's Stoic detachment (Epictetus), the chapter uses Diotima's ladder of love from Plato's Symposium and Hegel's Faust to argue that only passionate, attached love - Anakin's for Padme and Luke's for his father - descends into darkness and brings the Spirit's balance, so 'the Force is with us.'

hegel-geist.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
hegel-geist.title: “Obviously, the Borg Can’t Hold Their Liquor”
hegel-geist.relation: Decker asks 'What's it like to be a Borg?' and tests whether monist metaphysics justify the Collective: Parmenides's changeless, perfect Being matches the Borg's 'bringing them closer to perfection', Spinoza's one substance (God or Nature) makes assimilationist determinism intelligible and finds truth in Seven of Nine's nostalgia for collective harmony, and Hegel's teleological Geist — the whole 'the world, aware of itself' — most closely mirrors the Borg's galactic quest for an Omega-molecule perfection of 'infinite parts functioning as one.' Yet 'I, Borg' shows Hegelian Spirit working through individuals: Hugh's redemption transforms the Enterprise crew's self-understanding, proving nothing is wholly alien and freedom can coexist with collectivity. Via Haraway's cyborgs and against Kass's 'wisdom of repugnance', the chapter concludes the Borg horrify us because the natural/artificial dualism is already obsolete in our technologized lives — 'if we are the Borg, then resistance truly is futile.'

hegel-geist.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
hegel-geist.title: Bring the Balance Back Led Zeppelin and the Hegelian Dialectic
hegel-geist.relation: Macan argues Zeppelin's contradictions — 'cock rock' versus androgyny, blues versus avant-garde sound collages, acoustic versus electric, East versus West — are Hegelian dualities driven toward monist synthesis by a World-Spirit working through the band's generation. He reads the physical riff sections and shadowy middle collages of 'Dazed and Confused' and 'Whole Lotta Love' as interpenetrating Primitive/Modern, African-American/European, and Male/Female poles; 'Stairway to Heaven''s seamless growth from recorder-and-lute evocations of Elizabethan England into full hard rock reconciles past and present (via Tolkien, the Hermit gatefold, the Lady and the Piper); and 'Kashmir' versus 'In the Light' stage Jung's East/West problem, with Crowley's Schopenhauerian will supplying the turn from wisdom sought without to wisdom found within.

hegel-geist.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
hegel-geist.title: Funny Newspaper Makes Accurate Prophecy
hegel-geist.relation: Auxier takes the September 28, 2001 Onion issue—'Hijackers Surprised To Find Selves In Hell,' published while late-night TV was still in mourning—to ask what makes some comedy permissible and durable, glancing back at Aristophanes' caricature of Socrates in The Clouds and the circle-men speech Plato puts in his mouth in the Symposium. Hegel supplies the machinery: comedy as a moment of Art within Absolute Spirit may only bring to naught what is already null, while irony that diminishes the noble degrades the ironist—which is why the Warren Commission is fair game for 'Smithsonian Janitor Finds Magic Bullet' but Martin Luther King, a World Historical Individual whose individuality embodies his movement, can never anchor the 'Mrs. Williams Finally Decides Dinner Guest Is Not Going to Show' story. Since 'the news' itself is the great nullity—partial time-slices pretending to explain complex events before their meanings are interpretable—The Onion's rapid 9/11 satire was legitimate and even prophetic, deflating the bullshit of those posing as arbiters of Objective Spirit.

hegel-geist.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
hegel-geist.title: Let It Bleed
hegel-geist.relation: Reconstructing the twins' songwriting mechanics — Keith re-voicing Mick's 'Brown Sugar' in open-G tuning, the producer Don Was shuttling between them during Bridges to Babylon as Keith sang wordless fragments that Mick turned into lyrics — Auxier argues their genius lives outside either man alone, in sparks between two interdependent, mutually wounded subjectivities. He names their destructive-yet-creative bond a classic case of what philosophers call dialectic, citing Hegel's view that cultural history is made through strife and that a Zeitgeist moves history with or without the cooperation of individuals. The Stones surfed the 1960s Zeitgeist all the way into the twenty-first century, and their willingness to 'let it bleed' kept the collaboration generative after they stopped being good mates around 1968.

hegel-geist.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
hegel-geist.title: In The Shadows
hegel-geist.relation: Auxier poses the puzzle that Mick and Keith give thoroughly contradictory accounts of their own collaboration, and asks how reliable anyone can be as an interpreter of their own creative experience. He sets Hegel against Susanne Langer as irreconcilable alternatives: for Hegel artists give sensuous expression to the objective spirit moving in history without understanding what they do, while Langer insists artists do understand but speak an untranslatable, discursively untrained language. The section ends with Mick's long shadow — the prancing frontman — having hidden Keith, the brooding semi-animal, from recognition as a creative force whose enigma now demands a theory.

hegel-geist.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
hegel-geist.title: 14. Things Can Happen that Nobody Could Imagine Only a Few Years Ago
hegel-geist.relation: Donna Marie Smith reads the series as a Hegelian drama in which the opposing forces of tradition and progress - Lord Grantham, Carson, and Violet defending the old estate world against Matthew, Sybil, and Tom Branson embracing new ideas - drive history as 'the progress of the consciousness of freedom.' Using Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right, she explains why Robert treats upholding the entail against the protests of Mary, Cora, and even Violet as his duty as custodian, while noting Hegel's own objection that such inheritance law gives family members like the Crawley women 'no right to recognition.' The war announced at the season 1 garden party is read through Hegel's experience of Napoleon at Jena and his view that war can advance Geist, and the chapter closes with telephones, electric mixers, Sybil's marriage, and Isobel Crawley concluding that tradition and change can finally coexist.

hegel-geist.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
hegel-geist.title: 13. The Madness of the Musician
hegel-geist.relation: Lampert explains why Bowie is called the first postmodern pop star - he ironically shows that 'acting like' a rock star just is being one, refusing the genius myth by cobbling influences and confessing 'I lie an awful lot' - and grounds this in Sloterdijk's cynical reason and Diderot's Rameau's Nephew, whose honest liar Lui owns the mask-wearing vices everyone else hides. Hegel's Phenomenology supplies the title: the musician's universal deception is 'the madness of the musician,' the 'I' hollowed into pure ironic distance from all its masks (Descartes's separable self become image-manipulation), yet Hegel's hint that the cynic's vain talk can rise into 'a spiritual self of truly universal worth' points beyond Bowie's hyper-real self-referentiality to punk's DIY injunction to be your own hero - and to reading all sexuality, like Bowie's, as performance.

hegel-geist.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
hegel-geist.title: 17. The Cry of Love
hegel-geist.relation: Reads Hendrix as a romantic idealist on a Platonic-Neoplatonic arc: 'Room Full of Mirrors' shatters the cave wall and its projections toward The One, whose presence is pursued through eros with the veiled Beloved of Plotinus — the semi-divine feminine of 'Little Wing,' 'One Rainy Wish,' and 'Angel.' Hegel's Zeitgeist and world-spirit then frame the planned First Rays of the New Rising Sun as music meant to carry humanity's collective evolution, with Hendrix as Hegel's 'spiritual workman' and self-described messenger ('I am only a messenger and you are a Sheep in the process of evolution').

hegel-geist.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
hegel-geist.title: 14. Things Can Happen that Nobody Could Imagine Only a Few Years Ago
hegel-geist.relation: Donna Marie Smith reads the series through Hegel's philosophy of history: the Crawleys' world is a clash of opposing forces - Lord Grantham's traditionalism against Matthew's and Branson's modernization, Violet's fear of electricity against Sybil's and Rose's embrace of the new - and this very conflict drives progress toward greater freedom. She uses Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right both to explain the entail and primogeniture that bar Mary from inheriting (the law preserves the 'house' over the immediate family, which Hegel calls an infringement of the freedom of property) and to frame Robert's refusal to challenge it as duty to his social standing outweighing personal wishes. WWI, which Hegel experienced through Napoleon's occupation of Jena, is presented as a 'march toward freedom' that breaks down class barriers and finally pushes Robert to accept change on the estate: 'Let's give it a go and see what the future brings.'

hegel-geist.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
hegel-geist.title: Yoda's Theme
hegel-geist.relation: Eldem uses Hegel's 'Force and the Understanding' from the Phenomenology of Spirit to explain Yoda's X-wing lesson: force is essential to matter rather than external to it, so 'size matters not' - lifting a rock and a ship are the same task within a relational ontology where things are constituted by bifurcated forces (gravity, magnetism) whose opposites form unities, like the light and dark sides or the Rey-Ben dyad. Geist plays the role the pre-Socratics gave the arche, and via Houlgate's reading it grounds the Force's social dimension: love as the force that binds people, explaining Vader's final sacrifice and the connections between the saga's heroes. The hero is the one who grasps this interconnection and sacrifices for community, as Yoda does when he finally raises the ship.

hegel-geist.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
hegel-geist.title: NOTES
hegel-geist.relation: Jason Blahuta reads the saga through Hegel's Philosophy of History: Sarah and John Connor are World Historical Individuals — mere 'tools' of Geist — whose attempts to rewrite history, Sarah's hit on Miles Dyson in T2 and John's second try through General Brewster in T3, can only postpone Judgment Day, never redirect it, as the T-101's line 'Judgment Day is inevitable' concedes. The cunning of reason explains why removing Dyson or Brewster is futile: historical forces merely recruit replacements, so the script gets acted out by other actors. Because the dialectic's thesis-antithesis pattern (even the young John versus his mother) yields syntheses that carry both sides forward, the chapter concludes neither species can stop the other's rise, and only full-scale battle in the moving present decides which becomes Geist's end.

constitutive-rules.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
constitutive-rules.title: The Ambiguous Consolations of Philosophy
constitutive-rules.relation: Ted Cohen shows that 'ties go to the runner' is no convention but follows from Rule 6.05(j) (the runner is out only if tagged before he touches first), then discovers that Rule 7.08(e) contradicts 6.05(j) once 6.09(a) makes a batter who hits a fair ball a runner: on a tie at first the rules say both out and safe. His letters to the National League rules committee get a polite brush-off ('there never are any ties'), and the essay meditates on how players barely know the rules (the 2000 World Series third-strike misplay, cricket's time-wasting law, the spitball rule's gaps) and how rules written 'by journeymen lawyers' charm yet fail. Philosophy's consolation is ambiguous: knowing the rules cost him his teammates' respect, who 'knew the game in some other way.'

constitutive-rules.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
constitutive-rules.title: 4 - With Friends Like These, Who Needs Enemies
constitutive-rules.relation: Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch, Mafia Wars) through Goffman's 'face' and Brown and Levinson's positive/negative politeness: recruiting friends into an application is a face-threatening imposition that becomes awkward across professor-student and parent-child hierarchies playing as nominal equals. She invokes Derrida on Mauss - 'there is no gift without bond, without bind' - to analyze the reciprocity obligations of gifting games, and finds emergent cooperative norms like PackRat pacts against tit-for-tat stealing. Players revolt when developers monetize asymmetrical play, showing communities negotiate the rules of the magic circle.

constitutive-rules.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
constitutive-rules.title: A Little bit of Messi for our Life
constitutive-rules.relation: The authors cast the contrast between disciplined European and improvisational South American football as Mill's struggle between liberty and authority: the coach's tactical orders are 'rules of opinion' the genius may defy, as Maradona did on his sixty-meter run to the Goal of the Century, while the harm principle marks the line at the 'rules of law' — FIFA's Laws of the Game. The Hand of God goal, which broke even a rule of law yet stood because 'a goal is scored when the referee says so', illustrates Searle's point that football's regulative capacity cannot guarantee its agreements, leaving a gap filled only by ethics and fair play. Following Wittgenstein's 'ethics and aesthetics are one and the same', they conclude that a bit of Messi-style rule-breaking — Messi replicated both Maradona goals in 2007 — is what makes football, and life, joyful and beautiful.

constitutive-rules.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
constitutive-rules.title: The Basket That Never Was
constitutive-rules.relation: Thomas Flint's thought experiment - a conference-championship buzzer-beater waved off because the clock expired, with inconclusive video - asks whether South Shore 'really' scored. He rejects the 'Goofy View' that game facts are referee-independent, since it would entail that only he and his camcorder-owning boss know who won any game ever (imperiling even Michael Jordan's 1982 title and Pistol Pete's scoring record) and would poison a coach's duty to teach rule-following when officials miss traveling. He also rejects the 'Tyranny of the Zebras' that makes officials infallible like the pope, since NCAA replay rules presuppose fallibility, and settles on officials as contest judges who award points: without the verdict no points exist, yet a blown call remains a genuine mistake in failing to apply the rules properly.

democracy-theory.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
democracy-theory.title: Our Big, Fat, Greek Democracy
democracy-theory.relation: Eric Bronson reads the brawling 1977-78 'Bronx Zoo' Yankees (Steinbrenner firing Billy Martin five times, Martin dragging Reggie Jackson off the field in Fenway, Jackson's dugout charge and defiant bunt) as an argument that dissent is good for democracy. Through Alexis de Tocqueville's warnings about majority conformity and democratic leveling (Nietzsche's herd mentality), he argues America needs gadflies like Socrates condemned by Athens for 'creating tension' and MLK's nonviolent troublemakers, while Adam Smith's invisible hand shows the Yankees' internal self-interest and conflict still produced championships, unlike the harmonious 1979 'We Are Family' Pirates. Dysfunctional discord, like free speech, keeps teams and democracies from going stagnant.

democracy-theory.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
democracy-theory.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
democracy-theory.relation: Kurtz, the secular humanist, argues the film is a political weapon of the Religious Right (O'Reilly, Dobson, Gingrich) that presents fantasy as fact: Gibson claims fidelity to the Gospels while borrowing torture scenes such as the bridge plunge and the savage flogging from Anne Catherine Emmerich's visions, whitewashing the historical Pilate, and erasing that Jesus, Mary, and the disciples were themselves Jews. Applying historical criticism, he contends the Gospels are anonymous, second- and third-hand missionary propaganda written forty to seventy years after Jesus, shaped by the rivalry between rabbinic Judaism and Gentile-seeking Jewish Christianity and canonized politically at Nicaea under Constantine. He concludes by defending the freedom of inquiry, skeptical scrutiny of all sacred texts, and the First Amendment's separation of church and state against the film's power to inflame anti-Semitism and the American culture war.

democracy-theory.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
democracy-theory.title: Palpatine’s Legacy
democracy-theory.relation: Decker reconstructs Palpatine's career as a case study in how democracies die: using Aristotle's definition of tyranny and the precedent of Pisistratus and Julius Caesar, he shows Palpatine manufacturing the Separatist threat so the Senate grants him emergency powers - a twist on Machiavelli's loved-versus-feared dictum in which playing the reluctant democrat is itself the means to absolute rule. The Attack of the Clones debate between Anakin ('Someone wise' should make people agree) and Padme becomes a clash between Leo Strauss's philosopher-king ideal of rule by the virtuous few and John Dewey's conception of democracy as a way of life trusting the intelligence of common people, with Rousseau's social contract framing the stakes. The chapter concludes that democratic ends require democratic means and that unaccountable 'watchers' - Straussian statesmen or Anakins - are exactly the path to Empire.

democracy-theory.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
democracy-theory.title: Bullshitting and Lying in Politics
democracy-theory.relation: Opening Mark Evans's Chapter 12: Frankfurt's claim that democracy especially breeds bullshit, since it charges every citizen with having opinions about everything - the 'Frankfurt thesis' that citizens do not care about truth. It is contrasted with the 'cynicism thesis' (citizens do not care about politics, out of well-founded disillusion with a system that fails to deliver), and both are framed by the objection as old as Plato that political understanding is an expertise we cannot all share - theses argued about, not against, democracy.

democracy-theory.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
democracy-theory.title: ‘Dumbing-Up’ Some Distortions of Democratic Equality
democracy-theory.relation: Evans argues that democratic citizens do their own share of Frankfurt-bullshitting about politics: because electoral democracy cannot admit how complex politics really is, it institutionalizes the fictional ideal of the 'well-informed' citizen, obliging voters to hold over-simplified views and politicians to pander to them. Campaigning forces candidates into dodges like the 'politics of distraction' and the empty promise to be 'a different sort of politician', producing 'Governor Schwarzenegger Syndrome' and opening space for dangerous demagogues and fundamentalisms. Following Churchill, the chapter concludes that this citizen-side bullshit vindicates the cynicism thesis only partially and gives no reason to reject democracy as 'the worst form of government except for all the others'.

democracy-theory.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
democracy-theory.title: Philosophy versus Bullshit
democracy-theory.relation: The chapter claims that 'equal respect' in modern democracies has been distorted into a 'dumbing-up' relativism — 'I'm valid, you're valid' — which conflates the equal right to voice opinions with their equal intellectual merit and so leaves nothing that counts as bullshit. It illustrates this through the 'democratization of expertise' and management-speak ('downsizing', 'mission statements'), which mimics profundity while evading awkward facts, and it tests and rejects the quasi-Nietzschean ressentiment story of timid citizens dragging discourse down to a common denominator. To get the full measure of the phenomenon it expands Frankfurt's and Cohen's typologies into seven kinds of bullshit, adding clarifiable unclarity, plain rubbish, irretrievable speculation, pretension, and evasion.

democracy-theory.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
democracy-theory.title: E Pluribus Unum
democracy-theory.relation: Auxier frames Hitchcock's Lifeboat against Garrett Hardin's 'lifeboat ethics' essay, arguing the lifeboat converts political questions into ethical ones by stranding the survivors outside law and politics ('We're on our own here. We can make our own law'). The survivors are ethical pluralists - Rittenhouse lives for money, Kovac for equality, Constance for fame, Joe for God, MacKenzie for care - and their clinging to private versions of the Good lets Nazi captain Willy, whose only principle is survival, manipulate them all. Using Maslow's hierarchy of needs, Auxier shows the boat descending to bare survival, yet argues the mob killing of Willy when he hoards water is moral outrage rather than survival-driven, and that the final rescue scene replays the opening dispute with nobody having grown - a vindication of pluralistic democracy capable of unified action.

democracy-theory.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
democracy-theory.title: What Is Truth
democracy-theory.relation: Lavaque-Manty and Mickey define populism by distinguishing its content from its discourse (via Michael Kazin), tracing the 1892 Populist Party platform and southern race-baiting demagogues like Vardaman and Huey Long, then locate Cash in that Dixie soil, his family rescued by the patronizing New Deal Dyess Colony that fed his populist distrust of elites. Cash's populism is anti-racist and pro-prisoner ("The Ballad of Ira Hayes," his empathy for convicts against tough-on-crime politics), his patriotism borders on kitsch ("Ragged Old Flag"), and "What Is Truth?" argues the young may be right, breaking with populist certainty about the obvious. The closing worry is the deep tension they pose with Locke's "the people be the judge" against democracy as "government by discussion": a Cash concert, like a mass rally, may stir people following rather than thinking, so populism's ring of truth is not yet truth.

democracy-theory.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
democracy-theory.title: Unity Born from Diversity
democracy-theory.relation: Shook narrates the 1984 Born in the U.S.A. tour — George Will's 'Yankee Doodle Springsteen' column, Reagan's Hammonton speech, Springsteen's refusal to be either campaign's tool — and reads the song as the hopeless story of a Vietnam-generation man's living death (the refinery that won't hire him, the dead brother and the Saigon woman) mistaken by flag-waving crowds for a patriotic anthem. He then maps the song's possible meanings onto democracy's possible destinies: Carl Schmitt's friend–enemy politics of national homogeneity and permanent emergency, Schlesinger's assimilationist Disuniting of America, and liberal cosmopolitanism's citizens of the world. Dewey's The Public and Its Problems wins: democracy must intelligently manage rather than eliminate diversity, each citizen holding a double loyalty to subgroup and to the democratic 'great community,' so being born in the U.S.A. is a responsibility and pride is properly placed in democratic ideals.

democracy-theory.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
democracy-theory.title: Learning from Our Mistakes
democracy-theory.relation: Tamplin defends democracy through the Baltar election: Roslin's attempted theft failed, the voters' bad choice produced the New Caprica occupation, and this is exactly what Plato and Aristotle predicted of democracy as the deviant rule of the many, contrasted with Aristotle's polity aimed at the common advantage and a virtue 'every city' must care for. A thought experiment — an infallible computer advising citizens on every choice — shows that following it would abolish democracy, whose value lies not in results but in Aristotle's freedom, 'living as one wants.' Only by being allowed to frak things up can citizens learn from their mistakes, the road Apollo points to in his 'Crossroads' trial speech about collective shame, which is why Baltar's acquittal is a good sign.

democracy-theory.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
democracy-theory.title: Walking the Tightrope
democracy-theory.relation: Louis Melancon weighs the Fleet leadership's secrets and lies: Adama's 'blind squirrel' lie about Earth, classifying the fact that Cylons look human, Roslin's faked death of the baby Hera, and Tom Zarek's secret collaboration courts on New Caprica. Democratic duty is framed as a deontological obligation of transparency grounded in the governed's trust, while the leadership repeatedly defaults to consequentialist wartime exceptions. The chapter proposes a rule-of-thumb: secrecy is justified only to hide specific information from an external threat like the Cylons, never to protect the government from its own citizens, and each violation erodes the trust on which Colonial democracy's 'soul' depends.

democracy-theory.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
democracy-theory.title: 13 - Don’t Talk to Me
democracy-theory.relation: Pitt argues the iPod is 'pernicious' not because technology is intrinsically bad — a device is judged by the uses it is put to and their consequences — but because its consequences are antisocial: silent subways, 'brainsnatched' beach-walkers, and the silenced graduate corridor where loud philosophical argument used to live. Comparing the gadget to Huxley's soma (each user programs his own blissful isolation, going so far as to avoid domestic conflict by plugging back in), he contends social skills — argument, eye contact, advocacy for ideas — are what drive both technological innovation (even Steve Jobs had a co-inventor) and functioning democracy. Hence the earbud habituation summarized as 'Don't talk to me, I'm listening to MY music!' is, he claims, one of the final nails in the coffin of the social skills a civil, democratic society needs.

democracy-theory.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
democracy-theory.title: “Its Continuing Mission”
democracy-theory.relation: Argues that Star Trek's real subject is Hegelian recognition: a society is worth living in when every member's claims count as reasons and their talents get developed. It reads 'The Measure of a Man' (Data winning legal personhood), 'The Outcast' (Riker defending the J'naii Soren), and DS9's 'Past Tense' Bell Riots as dramas of winning recognition, and maps the Romulan-Reman and Stratos-Troglyte hierarchies onto Hegel's master-slave dialectic, contrasting Descartes's solipsistic cogito with Hegel's claim that self-awareness needs another. Since recognition requires more than non-interference against Locke-style atomism, the Federation's appeal lies in positive liberties — education, open debate, guaranteed basic needs — even though the shows oddly skip elections and democratic politics, a tension the authors flag through Leonard Nimoy's praise of a world with 'no political agenda.'

democracy-theory.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
democracy-theory.title: Who Uses facebook and Why
democracy-theory.relation: Gil de Zuniga and Valenzuela report their 2009 survey of 1,482 Americans on social network site use: 41 percent of adults use them, with women, African Americans, and Hispanics using them more than white men and with use spread across income and education levels. The top motivation is staying in touch with existing family and friends, but users also meet new people, discuss issues, follow news, and join causes. They argue these patterns suggest SNSs may narrow the digital divide and support democratic participation rather than being a teenage fad.

democracy-theory.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
democracy-theory.title: Leto’s Not So Golden Path
democracy-theory.relation: Diagnoses the Duniverse's recurring collapse not, as Herbert's 'Dune Genesis' has it, in hero-worship, but in rule conducted entirely through strategic action—Habermas's term for goal-oriented, self-interested rationality—as when even the Atreides council discusses only the appearance of a constitution rather than its legitimacy. Physical stability enforced by threats never becomes normative stability: Corrino, Paul's jihad-empire, and Leto II's 3,500-year tyranny all fail because their subjects are never authors of the law, and Leto's return to Bene Gesserit-style breeding programs ignores humanity's deliberative potential. The proposed remedy is democracy—rule by the people—even against Alia's cry that 'Atreides power must never be marginalized by the chaos of democracy.'

democracy-theory.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
democracy-theory.title: The Ideal Candidate
democracy-theory.relation: Nathan Zook uses the 'Royal Krabby' election from Vote for SpongeBob and the global-warming plot of SpongeBob Goes Green to weigh democracy. Mr. Krabs's rigged election, run only to sell patties, exemplifies C. Wright Mills's power elite manipulating the appearance of popular rule; Plato would bar Producer-class SpongeBob and Squidward from ruling and prefers educated Guardians, while Mill defends each citizen's liberty to choose and democracy's alliance with education (SpongeBob learns about global warming from Sandy). Aristotle's polity — citizens administering the state for the common interest — makes SpongeBob the ideal candidate because he saves Bikini Bottom without claiming power.

democracy-theory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
democracy-theory.title: Rule of the Wise
democracy-theory.relation: Updates Plato's rule of the wise to the pre-cogs of 'Minority Report,' noting that Socrates' 'divine sign' made him a kind of pre-cog. It then argues expertise cannot be operationalized — self-proclaimed authorities from Sarah Palin to Barack Obama disagree, and there is no accepted test of who the experts are — closing with Plato's own comparison of voters to children choosing between the doctor's medicine and the confectioner's candy, which explains why the Founders added the Electoral College.

democracy-theory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
democracy-theory.title: Spinning a Bottle
democracy-theory.relation: Sets Solar Lottery's Bottle beside the Athenian kleroterion and Madison's fear of factions: because telepaths make any strategy predictable, the Bottle game is a pure game of chance like dice rather than poker. The random twitch that deposes Reese Verrick for Leon Cartwright illustrates the same logic behind Philips and Callenbach's A Citizen Legislature proposal to replace the House with a randomly selected 'portrait of the people in miniature.'

democracy-theory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
democracy-theory.title: Throwing the Rascals Out
democracy-theory.relation: Uses Joseph Schumpeter's deflationary account of elections — no meaningful popular will, just marketplace competition ensuring rotation in office — to explain Herb Moore's claim in Solar Lottery that the Bottle's random twitch prevents dictators. Since no one can be sure of holding power, a lottery guarantees turnover at least as well as elections, though it introduces the mirror-image danger of simply selecting an incompetent.

democracy-theory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
democracy-theory.title: Checks and Challenges
democracy-theory.relation: Walks through Solar Lottery's two-part selection machinery — the random Bottle plus the Challenge, an officially appointed assassin who filters out incompetent Quizmasters like the psychotic Robin Pitt — comparing them to Athenian scrutiny of officials and impeachment. It also shows how the unk underclass selling its power cards concentrates any chance of office in the hands of the rich, undercutting the lottery's democratic justification, and asks whether surviving assassination predicts governing any better than winning elections does.

democracy-theory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
democracy-theory.title: How Can Random Machinery Be Rational
democracy-theory.relation: Answers Verrick's complaint that the Bottle is irrational by distinguishing tools, which are arational, from agents who act for reasons: a lottery is inappropriate for choosing a spouse or career but rational where unpredictability or impartiality is wanted. In Solar Lottery the assassins DeFalla and Keith Pellig randomize their courses against telepaths, just as draft and green-card lotteries ensure equal chances, so random rotation in office is a rational tool for stopping anyone from holding power too long.

democracy-theory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
democracy-theory.title: Giving and Selling
democracy-theory.relation: Takes Plato's warning that those who want to rule, like Verrick, will profit from office — true philosophers rule only under compulsion — into the question of whether power cards may be given away or sold. Since we permit donating organs and having sex but criminalize selling them, letting the rich buy up the unks' tickets destroys the equal-chance rationale, the realization that leads Cartwright to see the game as stacked, and that the chapter links to Lani Guinier's smeared electoral-reform proposals.

democracy-theory.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
democracy-theory.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
democracy-theory.relation: Sienkiewicz argues that Klosterman's LeBron James 'Decision' episode on Bill Simmons's B.S. Report modeled genuine public-sphere deliberation: where ESPN's Skip Bayless scored points over whether James looked remorseful, Klosterman proposed, via Tupac's 'Only God can judge me', that the televised announcement was a statement of confidence and a refusal to play the one-dimensional reality-TV role America demanded. The chapter lays out Habermas's eighteenth-century public sphere, its salons and 'public sphere of letters' where low-stakes aesthetic arguments (Mozart then, the Guns N' Roses tribute band Paradise City now) train disinterested rational debate, and concedes Habermas's golden age is idealized historical fiction much like a Klosterman hyperthetical. Though Habermas blames commercial media for corroding rational discourse, Sienkiewicz contends that long-form podcasts like The B.S. Report and Contexts give Klosterman's pop-culture arguments the time and independence the old salons had, so arguing about Billy Joel or Ace Frehley strengthens rather than absolves democratic culture.

democracy-theory.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
democracy-theory.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
democracy-theory.relation: A provocatively sympathetic application of On Liberty: Mill's harm principle protects Jesse's drug use from punishment, and Mill's celebration of individuality and 'experiments of living' makes Walt's cooking an 'individual spontaneity' valuable precisely because it defies custom - Marie's anti-pot panic and Hank's beer-and-Cub-cigar double standard illustrating the 'magical influence of custom' and democracy's drift toward 'collective mediocrity'. Mill's temperance-era remarks that intoxication 'is not a fit subject for legislative interference' are extended from use to manufacture. The chapter's thesis: even when Walt is wrong, mere nonconformity 'is itself a service', making Heisenberg an unlikely hero of liberty and human progress.

democracy-theory.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
democracy-theory.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
democracy-theory.relation: Joseph Foy argues Jeopardy! quietly serves democracy: the breadth of its categories rewards exactly the well-rounded, informed citizenry that theorists from Tocqueville to Delli Carpini and Keeter think self-government needs, and it answers Plato's Republic worry that ordinary people are unfit to rule by showing experts and stay-at-home parents alike fluent across the board. Because civic knowledge correlates with defending First Amendment freedoms, and because the show inserts the glorification of knowledge into the public sphere while bar-trivia gatherings build Putnam-style social capital, playing along at home rehearses the habits and virtues of democratic citizenship.

democracy-theory.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
democracy-theory.title: 8. Plato’s Chicago
democracy-theory.relation: Littmann systematically maps Roth's Chicago onto Plato's Republic: like Marcus, Plato rejects democracy after Athens executed Socrates; both dissolve the family ('faction before blood' versus children raised in common and bred by state schedule); Erudite's IQ-selected leadership mirrors the rigorously trained philosopher-rulers, Dauntless the warrior class whose purely physical training Plato warns turns 'savage and harsh,' Abnegation's poverty the guardians's communism of property, and the factionless the powerless producers - with Plato's noble lie about the metals matching the Erudite's propaganda and serums as instruments of control. The shared flaw, he argues, is concentrated power without external checks, which corrupted Abnegation, corrupts every Dauntless leadership change, and would corrupt Plato's guardians too. The lesson is not to hand power to the least vicious but for democratic voters to confront their own ignorance - or end like Roth's America, in apocalyptic war.

democracy-theory.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
democracy-theory.title: 10. Amity—Directly Democratic
democracy-theory.relation: McCrossin identifies Amity's consensus circles as direct democracy - the people exercising government in person, against the republics of Abnegation, Candor, and Erudite and Dauntless's open oligarchy - and hears Tris's skepticism ('How do they get anything done?') and Tobias's admiration ('it makes them kind') echoing the 2011 public debate over Occupy Wall Street. Johanna Reyes acts as a facilitator who helps Amity's general will develop rather than articulating it, but when the planned attack on Erudite threatens innocents she leaves the faction rather than quietly mold its will, confirming Tris's worry about talk in the face of terrible deeds. Through Alexander Meiklejohn's absolutist reading of the First Amendment, the chapter then argues that New Chicago's self-government needs both uncompromisingly protected political speech and a direct-democratic dimension for working out what the common good actually is.

democracy-theory.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
democracy-theory.title: 9. Anarchy, State, and Apocalypse
democracy-theory.relation: Da Silva and McKendry test the political legitimacy of four post-apocalyptic governance types: the Claimers' anarchy that collapses into Joe adjudicating 'claims', the Governor's and Rick's dictatorships ('This is not a democracy anymore!'), the prison Council's representative democracy with the three questions as a quasi-constitution, and Terminus's quasi-theocratic cannibal creed ('You're the butcher or you're the cattle'). Using Hobbes's state of nature and war of all against all, hypothetical social contract, and the twin tests of power and morality, they judge even the benevolent Rick-tatorship unjust because concentrated power is fallible and unaccountable. They conclude, with Churchill, that the Council's imperfect democracy is the worst form of government except for all the others.

democracy-theory.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
democracy-theory.title: 6. Who’s the Better Friend
democracy-theory.relation: Bowman sorts Marvel relationships through Aristotle's three friendships: Ant-Man's starstruck alliance is friendship of pleasure, Obadiah Stane's partnership with Tony a toxic friendship of utility, and Steve's bond with Bucky a friendship of virtue that loves without reciprocity - making Cap better TO his friends, though saving Bucky endangers everyone else. Turning to Derrida's Politics of Friendship, where fraternity grounds democratic equality among all persons, he argues Tony's refusal to privilege any individual over mankind makes him better FOR his friends. The Civil War split thus replays the old tension between personal autonomy and responsibility to humanity, at the destructive scale only super-powered friends can achieve.

democracy-theory.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
democracy-theory.title: 22. A New Civil War
democracy-theory.relation: Horn reads Marvel's Civil War as an allegory of post-9/11 America's Patriot Act debate over security versus liberty: Iron Man takes Hobbes's side, treating unregulated superhumans as the state of nature - a 'war of every man against every man' - that the Registration Act's social contract and punishment-backed rules must end, while Captain America takes Mill's On Liberty side, insisting full freedom for human nature must not be ceded to a government that will overreach, with Spider-Man torn between the two like the American citizen. Invoking Habermas's communicative action and deliberative democracy from Between Facts and Norms, he blames the two camps for talking past each other - Cap walling himself off while Tony keeps reaching out - and prescribes genuinely open dialogue as the only bridge that can marry security and liberty before the country devolves into its own civil war.

democracy-theory.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
democracy-theory.title: 24. Aftermath
democracy-theory.relation: Faller argues Civil War is Marvel's meditation on the aftermath of 9/11 - the Raft as Guantanamo, Zemo's interrogation as the waterboarding debate - and on America's red-blue polarization, with Steve Rogers embodying the virtue of the Good and Tony Stark the virtue of Truth as the two values democracy constantly pits against each other. Turning to Athens, he reads Plato's Euthyphro - are the gods good because goodness is a standard above them, or because their power decrees whatever they do good? - as the exact dilemma splitting Democrats, who define truth by the good it does, from Republicans, who define good by conformity to law and constitutional process, the same democratic dynamic that voted to execute Socrates and, in the comics, leaves Captain America assassinated by a sniper on his way to trial. Transcending the dualism is modeled by Spider-Man's identity disclosure and Black Panther's renunciation of vengeance over Zemo.

democracy-theory.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
democracy-theory.title: 24. Post-Factual Democracy
democracy-theory.relation: Hendricks and Vestergaard open with Trump's inauguration lies and Kellyanne Conway's 'alternative facts' to define post-factual democracy: a state in which opportune political narratives replace facts and evidence as the basis of debate, opinion formation and policymaking. Unlike Machiavelli, who taught that lies must at least be concealed, the post-factual politician pays no price for exposed falsehood once social media, the attention economy and populist us-versus-them narratives engineered for indignation and fear have stripped journalists and fact-checkers of authority — Arendt's remark that mass leaders show 'extreme contempt for facts as such' before fitting reality to their lies. Using Habermas's deliberative model and even minimal accountability theories of voting, they argue post-factuality destroys democratic legitimacy, and defend a 'factual democracy' that trusts science and journalism without becoming a technocracy — the real-world echo of the Party's command to reject the evidence of your eyes.

democracy-theory.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
democracy-theory.title: 10. Intelligence and Duh-mocracy
democracy-theory.relation: Saunders uses Adams's induhviduals and a hundred-voter dilution example in which smart people's votes are swamped to stage the classic case against democracy: Plato's physician analogy against Athenian rule by the ignorant and his philosopher-kings, Jason Brennan's hobbits, hooligans, and Vulcans with voter licensing, Mill's plural votes for the demonstrably wise, and Nussbaum's claim that humanities education breeds empathetic democratic citizens. Each fix fails on Dilbert's own terms, since competence tests demean the labeled, the Pointy-Haired Boss would amass extra votes while Dilbert-grade engineers lack political judgment, Asok's degree would not help, and the more educated are demographically skewed toward men. He concludes that equal votes win as a pragmatic default and muses that workplaces, not polities, might be the truer target of democratization.

democracy-theory.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
democracy-theory.title: 21. Mister Rogers’s Lesson for Democracy
democracy-theory.relation: Matthew Ussia maps the Trolley's transition between Rogers's house and the Neighborhood of Make-Believe onto Habermas's public sphere: the first-week crisis, Lady Elaine's rearranging of the neighborhood, King Friday's barbed-wire wall and 'Down with the Changes!,' Chef Brockett's humiliation, shows fear collapsing the space where a democracy works through conflict. Like Habermas, who feared television debates would hijack real public talk (and contra Sartre's 'Hell is other people'), Rogers used puppets to say the unsayable, modeling the deliberative space privatized modern life threatens to close.

democracy-theory.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
democracy-theory.title: Learning from Our Mistakes
democracy-theory.relation: Tamplin uses Baltar's landslide win on the New Caprica issue and Roslin's attempted election theft to argue democracy's guarantee of bad decisions is its saving feature: Plato and Aristotle ranked democracy among bad regimes because the many rule for private advantage rather than the common good, and Baltar's campaign of 'hope rather than truth' exploits exactly that weakness. A thought experiment about an oracle computer that always selects the best option shows that following it would abolish self-determination, the freedom to 'live as one wants' that democracy values above results. Only by choosing and frakking up (settling New Caprica, suffering the occupation, Apollo's shame speech at Baltar's trial) can citizens confront their role, learn from mistakes, and move toward Aristotle's polity aiming at virtue, making self-determination the mediating value between freedom and virtue.

democracy-theory.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
democracy-theory.title: Walking the Tightrope
democracy-theory.relation: Melancon weighs the Fleet leadership's secrets and lies: Adama's false claim to know the way to Earth, concealing that Cylons look human, Roslin faking Hera's death and hiding the baby, and Zarek's secret collaboration courts on New Caprica. He argues that keeping secrets from the Cylons can be justified by the state's duty to protect, but the leadership repeatedly deceives the governed themselves, discarding the transparency democratic legitimacy requires. Deontological duty to the governed keeps losing to consequentialist reasoning, and the chapter asks what happens to Colonial democracy's 'soul' when trust between government and governed erodes.

democracy-theory.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
democracy-theory.title: Misunderestimated
democracy-theory.relation: Muir argues the 1978 original was serious political allegory rather than Moore's 'popcorn': Adar's armistice with the Cylons stands in for Carter-era detente and the SALT treaties, and the sneak attack dramatizes hard-right fears of unilateral disarmament. Adama's 'preparedness' and Sire Uri's disarmament proposal map onto the 'Peace through Strength' doctrine that carried Reagan to power, and 'Experiment in Terra' repeats the lesson as Apollo tells Terra's politicians the opposite of war is slavery, not peace.
