macintyre-tradition.relation: Michelle Saint and Peter French explain why 'Blink' is horrifying despite the Weeping Angels being beautiful, not disgusting. Using Noël Carroll's fear-plus-disgust theory of art-horror as a foil, they draw on Frankfurt's account of caring and MacIntyre's narrative identity to argue the Angels destroy personhood: by hurling Kathy Nightingale out of her time and place they strip away everything she cares about and the narrative that constitutes her self. They then revise Carroll, proposing horror is fear plus impotence: the Angels weaponize the impossible task of not blinking, exposing our powerlessness to protect our own identity.

macintyre-tradition.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
macintyre-tradition.title: 26. Be Like Johnny
macintyre-tradition.relation: George Dunn reads Johnny Ramone's transformation from Queens delinquent to disciplined band foreman through craftsmanship: the Ramones' identical uniforms, downstrokes-only rig, and synchronized stagecraft embody the tradesman's virtues, and the band's 'fun' is MacIntyre's good internal to the practice of rocking out, not external rewards like money or fame. Against punk's 'Year Zero' originality conceit, Girard's mimesis shows imitation is inescapable - even distinguishing yourself is negative imitation - so the Ramones' apprenticeship to rock-and-roll radio and the teenage band Yee Loi faithfully imitating Johnny (Mosrite replica, one-legged spin) illustrate how mastery of models produces genuine creativity and freedom, a Stoic self-sufficiency of the skilled worker. Illich's 'convivial' tools like iPhones and YouTube let DIY players build their own lane past the corporate gatekeepers.

macintyre-tradition.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
macintyre-tradition.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
macintyre-tradition.relation: LaRocca unpacks MacIntyre's After Virtue claim that Austen is 'the last great representative of the classical tradition of the virtues.' He traces MacIntyre's argument that Austen synthesizes Homeric social roles, Aristotelian practical wisdom (phronesis), and Christian humility, making constancy her master virtue (analogous to phronesis) and distinguishing genuine amiability from mere agreeableness (Knightley on Frank Churchill: 'amiable only in French'). He contrasts Austen's internal, teleological virtue with Franklin's utilitarian ledger, cites Ryle's 'gradal' Aristotelian reading of Austen's character vocabulary and C.S. Lewis on her Christian 'undeception,' and reads Fanny Price's charmless constancy as exemplary of virtue over charm.

macintyre-tradition.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
macintyre-tradition.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
macintyre-tradition.relation: Scott reads Dickens's A Christmas Carol through virtue theory, treating Scrooge's transformation as a lesson in the virtues of generosity and gratitude that constitute eudaimonia (human flourishing). Drawing on Niebuhr, he explains Scrooge's greed as an anxious, insecurity-driven quest for security through wealth that fails because flourishing depends on relationships, not money (the poor-but-happy Cratchits). He invokes MacIntyre's 'just generosity' and Aristotelian habituation to show virtues are cultivated through practice, and uses Charles Taylor's weak/strong evaluations to warn that Christmas consumerism threatens 'keeping Christmas' by reducing moral worth to preferences and purchases.

macintyre-tradition.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
macintyre-tradition.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
macintyre-tradition.relation: Joe Kraus argues Tolkien wrote The Lord of the Rings as a protest against modernism, the mood that 'all that is solid melts into air' and that the past no longer matters, voiced by Marx, Freud, and Nietzsche's 'God is dead.' Tolkien's heroes survive because they remember lore and tradition (Gandalf watching the Shire, Sam's book-learning at Cirith Ungol), while Saruman and Denethor embody modern despair: they misuse the palantir, lose faith in tradition, and can only try to destroy the present. Against Berman's claim that there is no escape from modernism, Kraus reads Middle-earth as a fantasy where clinging to tradition still yields real, tangible power and certainty.

social-darwinism.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
social-darwinism.title: Crossing the Color Line
social-darwinism.relation: The Rucks argue that Herbert Spencer's Social Darwinism supplied the ideological justification for baseball's color line — blacks were deemed genetically unfit for the game — and that the Negro Leagues disproved it. Rube Foster's Negro National League, and especially Pittsburgh's Homestead Grays and Pittsburgh Crawfords (Cum Posey, Josh Gibson, Satchel Paige, Cool Papa Bell), displayed black organizational skill and on-field excellence, with Negro League teams beating white major leaguers in barnstorming play. Drawing on Darwin's actual account of cultural evolution and Franz Boas's environmental anthropology, the chapter holds that institutions, training infrastructure, and environment — not genes — explain athletic success, as Jackie Robinson's 1947 crossing of the color line and the later rise of Latin stars like Roberto Clemente confirm.

social-darwinism.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
social-darwinism.title: Poker and Philosophy
social-darwinism.relation: Ventimiglia mines No-Limit Hold'em for seven lessons philosophers also teach: we lack certain knowledge (Descartes' cogito is the famous quest for certainty, but philosophy's own history of disagreement proves uncertainty is the human condition), and like William James against Clifford we must still believe and act without the nuts — waiting for pocket aces while the blinds eat you alive is no strategy. Risking everything echoes Thoreau's escape from lives of quiet desperation, trusting hunches over arithmetic follows Thoreau and Peirce's sentimentalism, and the Darwin-and-Spencer competition of tournament poker hides a deeper cooperative social contract: get caught cheating and you are out of the game. It closes with Plato's four classic virtues from the Republic — wisdom, courage, moderation, and the justice of a balanced soul — as the perfection of a poker player.

social-darwinism.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
social-darwinism.title: James Bond and Philosophy
social-darwinism.relation: Matheson examines the 'master animal' imagery saturating Fleming's novels - Donovan Grant's reptilian physique in From Russia with Love, Blofeld's animal magnetism, villains feeding victims to sharks and crocodiles - as an exercise in Social Darwinism where, as Mr. Big puts it, wolves live by wolf's laws and sheep call them criminals. Using Nietzsche's Übermensch, the blond beast of the Genealogy, and Zarathustra's self-overcoming, she distinguishes Apollonian eaters like M (who curb appetite) from doomed Dionysian gluttons like Giuseppe Petacchi, arguing that Fleming makes dining and will power the test of who counts as an Overman. Bond differs from his megalomaniac foes only in keeping his own will to power and stomach under control, and the chapter closes by warning that Hollywood's romanticizing of the master animal keeps us valuing a brutally primitive masculinity Fleming himself mocked as a 'cardboard booby'.

social-darwinism.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
social-darwinism.title: Need that Cash to Feed that Jones
social-darwinism.relation: Steven Gimbel and Brendan Cushing-Daniels argue that the Dead's parking-lot economy — tie-dye shirts priced at ten, twelve, or fifteen dollars, veggie burritos, dueling bootlegs — realized Adam Smith's classical picture of capitalism, not the corporate capitalism Marx attacked. They trace Smith's Newtonian invisible hand and market equilibrium, his ethics of sympathy tempering self-interest, then the Social Darwinist twist given Smith under industrialization and Marx's four types of alienation under postwar white-collar work that pushed hippies to drop out. The punchline: deadhead sellers were not alienated — making shirts was creative self-expression — and buyer-seller sympathy ('it was simply uncool to screw over a fellow deadhead') made the lot a sustainable, kinder 'caring capitalism' that kept the scene alive.

social-darwinism.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
social-darwinism.title: Don’t Be a Vegeta
social-darwinism.relation: Argues that shonen fighting anime stage a choice between Adam Smith's and Darwin's models of competition: Zoro hunting Mihawk in One Piece, Goku's technique-by-technique training, and Rock Lee's specialization show competition improving people within the limits of a human excellence, while Cell's absorbing evolutions, the Super Saiyan transformations, and Ichigo's risky hollowification represent limitless 'leveling up' that changes what you are. The chapter concludes that the Darwinian win-at-all-costs model produces the perpetually dissatisfied Vegeta, and that framing competition around being a certain kind of person (a great swordsman, not just a winner) gives life a completable aim — while conceding that Darwinians rightly warn our picture of the 'normal human' has unjustly cast off jinchūriki like Naruto and Gaara and Devil Fruit users like Luffy.

social-darwinism.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
social-darwinism.title: 3. Darwin in Metropolis
social-darwinism.relation: Springett applies evolutionary biology to the matchup: comparing fitness, adaptations, and arms races (Batman's escalating gadget war with his rogues versus Superman facing no competition at all), he concludes Superman is objectively fitter, while on the technical definition of altruism Batman is more altruistic than the invulnerable Superman, who cannot lower his own fitness. Redefining a "Superhero" as an individual who effectively raises the fitness of many others, and adding Gould's catastrophist view that species extinction is the norm, he argues a planet with Superman keeps the whole species alive through catastrophes Batman could never avert. He explicitly rejects Social Darwinism - Superman is its counterexample because he saves the less fit - and, with Dawkins, credits conscious awareness with letting us choose our own goals, crowning Superman the superior Superhero.

social-darwinism.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
social-darwinism.title: 11. Of Bats and Supermen
social-darwinism.relation: Springett argues Superman, not Batman, is the proper goal of transhumanism - Batman's training and gadgets are only a stage toward transcending the human condition - and that the eugenics and Social Darwinism objection fails because Superman directs his superior fitness at saving the less fit. Through Merleau-Ponty's embodied cognition (Lois's churning stomach over a deadline, Alfred retracing his steps and posture to recall a thought, the "Subway Superman" Wesley Autrey's instinctive track rescue) he shows that radically different bodies mean radically different minds and moral perception. That turns Nagel's "What Is It Like to Be a Bat?" into "what is it like to be Superman?" - a problem of other minds for our transhuman future, with Watchmen's Doctor Manhattan as the warning of a transcendent being who simply stops caring about humans.

social-darwinism.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
social-darwinism.title: 1. When Evolution Strikes Back
social-darwinism.relation: Tim Jones argues the Golds misread Darwin: they take themselves to be the perfected endpoint of natural selection and use the Passage and Institute to 'help Nature along' by culling weaker Golds, justifying the subjugation of lower Colors—the same social-Darwinist logic Hitler and Stalin used to dress up atrocity. Using Darwin's own contrast between natural selection and man-made selective breeding, he shows the Institute is an artificial arena and the Golds' shaping of Reds and Pinks is self-serving husbandry, not nature's work. The twist is that the very traits the Golds bred into lowReds—Helldiver knuckles, miner's endurance, drill-floor courage—are what win Darrow the Institute, the Iron Rain, and the fight against the Jackal, so their manipulated evolution becomes the tool of their own extinction, just as Quicksilver's case against the static Color hierarchy implies.

social-darwinism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
social-darwinism.title: 25. Reasonable Genocide
social-darwinism.relation: Uses Horkheimer's Eclipse of Reason to dissolve the puzzle of Thanos's unsettling sanity: the Snap is subjectively rational — pure means–ends efficiency in service of a Malthusian 'simple calculus' whose end only the subject chooses — so Thanos 'is mad because he is rational,' with the murder of Gamora as the final severing of his last bond to the world. Captain America's refusal to trade Vision ('We don't trade lives') is read as a stand for ends valuable in themselves, while Ultron embodies the totalitarian variant (via Arendt and Spencer's social Darwinism) that declares humanity 'obsolete': Ultron wants to accelerate nature, Thanos to correct it, both absolutizing the subject against objective reason.

social-darwinism.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
social-darwinism.title: It’s the Disappointing Stories that Sound True to Life
social-darwinism.relation: Shipman argues the series first builds viewer sympathy for Cylons as rebel slaves (their monotheism and their New Caprica role as US-style occupiers make them 'more like the viewers than the humans'), then undercuts it: the Numbers rebuilt Cylon society as oppressors, breeding the voices out of Centurions, dismissing the Hybrids as mad, and breeding the sentient Raiders (Starbuck's discovery in 'Scar') into functional animals. The opening narration's claim that Cylons 'evolved' is disingenuous, since the model hierarchy was deliberately engineered, 'not evolution, but eugenics,' with Marx's 'from each according to his ability' division of labor as thin cover for literal class construction. The former slaves became slave-owners, fulfilling 'all of this has happened before': heroes of one story become villains of the next, inviting the muted models to rebel against the Numbers in turn.

social-darwinism.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
social-darwinism.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
social-darwinism.relation: Abigail Mann argues that the Games only look like 'survival of the fittest': Darwinian natural selection runs on chance ('one slip in thousands') and explicitly rejects the social-Darwinist use of 'unfit' against the poor, while Darwin's Descent of Man explains the tributes' kindness through kin and group selection and an evolved moral sense, so Katniss's unhesitating volunteering for Prim is kin selection and Thresh's conflicted sparing of her shows conscience overriding self-preservation. She tests this against Kant, for whom only duty-motivated action is truly moral, which would make Thresh's inner struggle the more moral act and Katniss's instinctive sacrifice mere animal impulse, and against the egoism of Hobbes (giving to a beggar to relieve one's own distress) and Dawkins's selfish gene, answering with Hume and psychologist Daniel Batson that genuine altruism is real. Her coda: Katniss ultimately rejects Gale not only because his firebomb killed Prim but because it was engineered to trap and kill altruists, and her closing habit of listing 'every act of goodness' is the trilogy's verdict that simple kindness is not an illusion.

social-darwinism.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
social-darwinism.title: Tony Learns His Lesson
social-darwinism.relation: Terjesen tests Andrew Carnegie's 'Gospel of Wealth' — that self-made men like Tony are uniquely qualified to administer their surplus wealth and technology for the common good — against Tony's monopolization of the Iron Man armor in 'Armor Wars' (neutralizing even S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Mandroids, attacking the innocent Stingray by mistake) and his futurist manipulations during Civil War. Spencer's social Darwinism underwrites Carnegie's faith that the successful know best, while Adam Smith's skepticism about those who 'affected to trade for the public good' explains why Tony's centralized control ended in the Skrull invasion and Norman Osborn's rise. The lesson is Smithian magnanimity: Tony begins to listen when an employee corrects his volcano trench, keeping his expertise but conceding he does not always know best.

social-darwinism.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
social-darwinism.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
social-darwinism.relation: Reads '1%' — where Cartman's failed fitness test makes him the scapegoated one percent, and the school's 99% splinter into warring 83%, 30%, and 5% factions occupying the Red Robin (and its restroom) — through Rousseau's Social Contract on freedom and equality and the dismembered social body, showing how popular solidarity shatters into meaningless percentage tribes. 'Night of the Living Homeless' (the poor as zombies who 'feed on our change', Kyle's $20 spawning the swarm, the shotgun as the only remedy) dramatizes the dehumanizing social-Darwinist picture of the economic undead, and the underpants gnomes' business plan (Phase 1: Collect Underpants, Phase 2: ?, Phase 3: Profit) mocks CEOs who cannot say why they amass wealth. The chapter's own verdict: corporations as such are good (cars, computers, canned soup), and blame falls on the greedy individuals inside them, since death — Tolstoy's two meters of burial land — levels all players.

social-darwinism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
social-darwinism.title: 3. Darwin in Metropolis
social-darwinism.relation: Springett applies evolutionary biology to the debate: natural selection, fitness (Batman edges it by one child, Damian Wayne), morphospace reasoning, and biological altruism, which technically Batman satisfies better since invulnerable Superman cannot lower his own fitness. But judged as an effective helper at species scale — Gould's catastrophes, asteroids, alien invasions — Superman protects the fitness of the whole species and planet where Batman guards one city, so a closing three-premise argument crowns Superman the superior Superhero, and his habit of saving the less fit makes him a living counterexample to Social Darwinism.

social-darwinism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
social-darwinism.title: 11. Of Bats and Supermen
social-darwinism.relation: Springett argues Superman, not Batman, is the right goal for a transhumanist future: through Merleau-Ponty's embodied cognition (Lois's deadline nausea, Alfred recovering a thought by redoing his posture, real-life 'Subway Superman' Wesley Autrey's gut-level rescue) he shows bodies shape thought and morality, so a super-body means a super-mind. Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' becomes 'what is it like to be Superman' — a problem of superhero minds, with Doctor Manhattan's indifference as the cautionary case — while Superman's rescues of the less fit show transcendence need not slide into eugenics or Social Darwinism.

social-darwinism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
social-darwinism.title: NOTES
social-darwinism.relation: Phillip Seng runs the human-Skynet war through the three parts of just-war theory and finds the moral ground shakier than it looks: T2's briefing reveals Skynet launched its strike only after humans tried to pull the plug, so the machines claim the same self-defense 'just cause' humans do, while Skynet flunks last resort (it decides 'in a microsecond' with no negotiation), legitimate authority, proportionality (killing everyone to avoid being switched off), and discrimination. He then shows Sarah becoming a Terminator herself when she locks her laser sight on the innocent Miles Dyson, violating the same just-conduct rules she judges the machines by, and stopping only at his crying family. The chapter closes by doubting the war could ever have a just resolution, since the films point toward genocide rather than a peace treaty with Skynet.

social-darwinism.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
social-darwinism.title: V - MAD GENETICS THE SINISTER SIDE OF BIOLOGICAL MASTERY
social-darwinism.relation: Burnett traces Nathaniel Essex's transformation into Mister Sinister to explore the ethics of genetic mastery. Set in Darwin's 1859 London, where Essex, grieving a child, debates taking control of evolution with Darwin himself, the chapter uses Paley's natural theology and Tennyson's crisis of natural evil to frame Sinister's rejection of moral restraint, and Herbert Spencer's evolutionary ethics to argue that cooperation, not 'dog eat dog,' is what fitness actually favors. Sinister's breeding of the Summers bloodline and Bolivar Trask's Sentinels embody Galton's eugenics, and Sinister's careers as 'Dr. Windsor' and 'Dr. Milbury' behind Weapon X and the Black Womb project mirror real cases like the Tuskegee study, where researchers lost sight of the moral whole.

social-darwinism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
social-darwinism.title: Bunker Mentality or Love
social-darwinism.relation: Robin Bunce recovers how Terry Nation's original 1963 'The Daleks' encodes evil, reading the script in its Cold War, post-Cuban-Missile-Crisis context. He argues Nation dehumanizes the Daleks not by making them less rational but MORE rational: they embody the unfeeling reason of the neutron bomb that destroyed Skaro, having lost individuality, laughter, and the capacity to feel. Drawing on Richard Rorty's claim that our humanity lies in feeling for one another rather than in reason (and on Wells's Morlocks), he concludes the Daleks are the dreaded post-nuclear human future, and Ian teaches the Thals that love and empathy, not abstract moralizing, resist evil.

social-darwinism.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
social-darwinism.title: MOTHERHOOD
social-darwinism.relation: Jen Baker interrogates why unmedicated 'natural' childbirth is treated as morally superior, dissecting five senses of 'natural' and rejecting each, including a social-Darwinist appeal to evolution she deems dangerous. She engages Montaigne (via Cicero) on philosophizing as learning to die and cites Dylan Thomas and Neil Young on facing pain soberly, then turns to the Stoics' claim that pain 'is nothing to us' – arguing from a neo-Aristotelian/Stoic virtue ethics that pain has no moral value and that keeping one's wits with an epidural can preserve moral agency, so natural birth is an 'optional and amoral' thrill, not a virtue; she frames it with Bill Cosby's and Carol Burnett's labor jokes.

social-darwinism.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
social-darwinism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
social-darwinism.relation: Murray argues that the ecologically conscious climber's doubt that her single climb matters is a version of the free-rider problem, which he claims is just the sorites paradox (the paradox of the heap, illustrated with trail cairns built one stone fewer each time) applied to social life. Because 'environmental degradation' is a vaguely specified term with no precise tipping point, he draws on Timothy Williamson's account of vagueness and Richard Tuck's history of free-riding to argue climbers should act 'as if' a threshold exists and see themselves as sufficient (not necessary) causes of preservation, justifying self-restraint and quota systems.

bushido.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
bushido.title: What’s Wrong with Generalization
bushido.relation: Brannigan uses Japanese baseball to ask what is wrong with cultural generalization. He presents the Bushido case — samurai-style self-denial, absolute loyalty (Kawakami's Yomiuri Giants), Suisha Tobita's 'training of death,' resolve (konjo), team harmony (wa), and a relational self grounded in Buddhism's no-self and Confucian identity-through-relationships — then tests it against counter-evidence: Sadaharu Oh's flamingo swing owed as much to individual talent and Hiroshi Arakawa's unconventional kendo-and-aikido coaching as to sensei imitation, the 'new breed' (Ochiai, Egawa) flouts the old ways, and William Kelly's 'Whiting problem' warns against polarizing Japanese and American baseball. The chapter's 'three strikes' against the label 'Japanese baseball' conclude that generalizations become dangerous when treated as monolithic nets cast over an entire culture.

bushido.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
bushido.title: Are We Going Too Far
bushido.relation: David Kyle Johnson distinguishes revenge (personal, emotional, unlimited) from retribution and argues that 'Tarantino's view'—mercy should be common practice yet revenge can be justified—is consistent: Jules buys Pumpkin and Honey Bunny's lives but never waives a right of vengeance, since they never wronged him. He tests the view against Bushido, showing Beatrix's revolt against her lord Bill violates the samurai code, and against karma, which makes revenge unnecessary. After finding that Hobbes, Locke, Nietzsche and Socrates all leave revenge's justification open, he defends it—citing Budd's 'that woman deserves her revenge'—so long as the punishment fits the crime and spares innocents, as when Beatrix refuses to make herself even by killing Vernita's daughter Nikki.

bushido.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
bushido.title: 14. When the Stakes Are Highest
bushido.relation: John Karavitis argues the Infinity War-Endgame arc only makes sense through the alien lens of feudal Japan's warrior code as codified in Yamamoto Tsunetomo's Hagakure, where 'the way of the warrior is to be found in dying' and success is measured in death, the enemy's and one's own. He reads Thanos's sacrifice of Gamora, his calm acceptance of death in the Garden, Black Widow's and Tony's willing sacrifices, and Thor's failure to 'go for the head' at Wakanda through Olivier Ansart's concepts of ichinen (single-minded resolve) and shini-gurui (the frenzy to die), with the code's roots in Buddhism, Shinto, and Confucianism. The provocation is that Thanos, not the fractious Avengers, is the true samurai, since his voluntary destruction of the Infinity Stones shows the self-discipline the code demands.

bushido.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
bushido.title: NOTES
bushido.relation: Baldwin argues the popular view of Bushido as a moral code (Nitobe, Star Wars, Kurosawa, Campbell's Jungian hero archetype) is historically wrong: by the Hagakure, Bushido is a death-ready 'mode of action' so morally neutral that even villains like Takezo Kensei or Sylar can practice it. He traces Hiro's evolution from comic-book and video-game hero-worship, through the Yaeko betrayal that turned Kensei into Adam Monroe, toward the fearless Future Hiro ideal of 'no-mind' readiness for death (echoing D.T. Suzuki's Zen reading). Because the Meiji reforms abolished the samurai class, Hiro can never literally be a samurai, only follow Bushido analogically, which lets him remain both superhero and samurai.

bushido.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
bushido.title: Notes
bushido.relation: Bein argues Wonder Woman uniquely fuses two supposedly incompatible moralities: bushido - Nitobe's eight samurai virtues, Sun Tzu's benevolence of ending war swiftly, worthy-opponent rituals mirrored in superhero costumes - and the feminist ethics of care Gilligan and Noddings built against a Western canon (Aristotle, Kant) that called women too emotional for morality. Wonder Woman's killing of Maxwell Lord to free Superman is re-read as the care-ethical beach case: saving your own child over a stranger's is not a failure of impartiality, and in his Gotham-versus-Themyscira invasion thought experiment she would defend Gotham because its people are vulnerable non-combatants, not because a utilitarian ledger favors it.

power-knowledge.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
power-knowledge.title: Numbers as Players
power-knowledge.relation: Bennett and Martin argue that the statistics baseball fans treat as objective truth embody far more chance and convention than fans realize. Statistical theory shows luck explains roughly half the spread in 2002 batting averages (Bonds's .370 versus Larry Walker; the 2003 Ramirez–Mueller race decided by one at bat), and Jim Albert's simulation of 1,000 seasons shows about four of five World Series are not won by the most talented team. Drawing on Thomas Kuhn's history of scientific quantification and Theodore Porter's Foucauldian point that numbers 'have agency' and exercise power, they show statistics also act on the game — shaping drafting, salaries, and Hall of Fame election — so Schroeder's stats to Charlie Brown are both indispensable and misleading.

power-knowledge.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
power-knowledge.title: After . . . Word!
power-knowledge.relation: Marcyliena Morgan's afterword traces hip-hop battling to the philosophical houses and crews of Saturday kung-fu cinema (Wu-Tang's obsession included), reading hip hop's South Bronx birth through Victor Turner's ritual threshold state and defining "flow" as conscious movement within chaos to create balance and collective identity. The mantra represent-recognize-come correct, shout outs as a system of indexicality, and hip hop's counterpublic sphere function, she argues, to expose hegemony and contest Foucault's technologies of power - answering Cornel West's "ignoble paradox of modernity" - so that hip hop battles through the theoretical houses of Foucault, Bakhtin, Butler, Gramsci, and Habermas, where "there is no such thing as a dead philosopher - just one that has not been resurrected yet."

power-knowledge.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
power-knowledge.title: Both Sides of Dylan and Politics
power-knowledge.relation: Jordy Rocheleau reads Dylan's protest era ("The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll," "Hurricane," "Chimes of Freedom") as Enlightenment social criticism in Kant's and Mill's sense: reason can expose injustice and secure autonomy against majority tyranny. The post-protest Dylan ("My Back Pages," "Desolation Row," "It's Alright, Ma") turns postmodern - Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives, Derrida's ever-deferred meanings, and Foucault's power/knowledge, where ideals of freedom become instruments of domination. Yet Dylan keeps crying for justice ("Political World," "Dignity"), so the chapter concludes postmodern skepticism can only serve as a cautionary check within, not a replacement of, Enlightenment politics - the thief's line in "All Along the Watchtower" as commitment amid confusion.

power-knowledge.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
power-knowledge.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Kieffner applies Foucault's deployment of sexuality to show how power centers constructed biker sexual stereotypes: the psychiatric profession behind Time's 1970 'Motorcycle Syndrome', the press that sexualized the Van Buren sisters and filled Easyriders with centerfolds, police 'gauntlets' that pull over bikes but not cars (and ask Raw Thunder's Char Zack if she is a lesbian), and even Harley-Davidson's own 'mystique' video deploying eroticism to sell bikes and HOG memberships. Following Foucault's rule of the tactical polyvalence of discourse, he ends with resistance within the same power structure: riders' rights organizations videotaping police encounters, and the tactical discourses of queer, lesbian, and female riders, from Evelyn Greenway's 1921 'Do it with a motorcycle' onward, who refuse the labels of sexual outlaw and gender traitor.

power-knowledge.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
power-knowledge.title: Urban Idiots Foucauldian and Pythonesque
power-knowledge.relation: Using Foucault's Madness and Civilization, the chapter reads the Flying Circus sketch 'The Idiot in Society' and the 'Hermits' sketch as commentary on madness as a social construct that changes from the medieval tolerance of fools, through the Great Confinement, to modern psychiatric medicalization. Arthur Figgis, the village idiot, is nothing like Foucault's silenced asylum inmates: he speaks rationally to camera about the 'vital psycho-social service' idiots provide, deposits moss at the bank, and lectures in idiocy at the University of East Anglia — madmen who are integrated, have agency, and speak for themselves. The Pythons turn Foucault's picture upside down, since the visibly idiotic are socially integrated while the urban idiots in business suits are the ones confined behind asylum-like walls, and by making idiocy funny they restore the dialogue between reason and unreason that Foucault says the monologue of reason destroyed.

power-knowledge.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
power-knowledge.title: A Meditation on the Word
power-knowledge.relation: Randall Auxier and Eileen Townsend fictionalize the history of philosophy as vampire predation in letters, emails, and IMs (1983-2009) between the 800-year-old Etienne Lavec - a student of Siger de Brabant who drained Thomas Aquinas over the Summa's Treatise on Angels, which wrote vampires out of existence - and Paulie, a freshman turned at Memphis State. Lavec recounts tasting Pico, Spinoza, Hegel, and the willing Kierkegaard, sparing Nietzsche who 'stole some of my ideas about free death', and contrasts vampire self-knowledge (embracing desire) with the Socratic beginning in affirmed ignorance. The centerpiece is Foucault: Lavec summarizes his genealogies of how institutions create the sick, the mad, the prisoner, and the pervert, fails to drain him, and is then haunted for decades by posthumous publications, taunting 'nietzsche26' emails, and finally a catacombs trap - power/knowledge that refuses to die. Lavec's embedded 'Meditation on the Word' recasts the Logos of John's Gospel so that vampires are the uncreated darkness at the boundary of the divine Word, pure self-grounding desire 'beyond good and evil', while the closing Twilight-era chats satirize Stephenie Meyer's sparkling, abstinent Edward as Foucauldian 'sin by words'.

power-knowledge.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
power-knowledge.title: Family Guy Must Die! Long Live Family Guy!
power-knowledge.relation: Jeremy Wisnewski's mock-manifesto uses Family Guy's cutaway gags and taboo jokes (Hitler sausage vendors, Petoria at the UN, Saddam and Khadafi bonding over Seinfeld) to stage postmodernism: Lyotard's "incredulity toward meta-narratives" and Baudrillard's claim that the real is no longer real, since our families are as televisual as the Griffins, who at least know they are cartoons. The danger is that joking about everything breeds cynical passivity, "liberating us from our causes." But Foucault, the 1968 activist and prison reformer, shows through power/knowledge that one can be postmodern and still fight locally, so the Griffins, and the show's satire of religion and politics, get to live.

power-knowledge.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
power-knowledge.title: Art, Madness, and Syd Barrett
power-knowledge.relation: George Reisch reads The Wall through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: madness is not a brain lesion but a historical construction — Renaissance unreason, classical confinement, then Tuke's and Pinel's psychiatric regime in which the madman must know 'he is watched, judged, and condemned' until judgment is internalized — which explains why Pink imprisons himself brick by brick and asks at 'The Trial', 'Have I been guilty all this time?' The fascist worms and skinhead riots of 'Waiting for the Worms' are the same crusade for uniformity that drove Pink mad — Foucault's 'moral city' where 'virtue is an affair of the state' — so fascism and insanity are versions of each other, with Sartre's 'Hell is other people' from No Exit as the framing thought. Both the album ('Outside the Wall': 'the bleeding hearts and artists make their stand') and Foucault end by defending art as the last channel of unreason, and Reisch argues Syd Barrett's unanswerable absence was exactly that interrupting void powering 'Echoes', Dark Side, Wish You Were Here, and The Final Cut.

power-knowledge.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
power-knowledge.title: The Final Word That’s Right, I Said Preliminary Thoughts
power-knowledge.relation: Patton starts from wildly disputed Springsteen interpretations — Reagan's 1984 campaign use of 'Born in the U.S.A.,' Flint protesters playing 'My Hometown' as civic pride, Kerry's 'No Surrender' — and asks whether any reading is better than another. He frames the issue as Socratic dialectic versus Gorgias-style rhetoric, passes through Augustine's polysemy (multiple intended levels of meaning, as in 'I'm on fire') to Nietzsche's claim that the text disappears beneath its interpretation, extended by Foucault (truth as an instrument of power) and Derridean deconstruction. His conclusion: authorial intent cannot settle meaning, but some readings ('Born in the U.S.A.' as pro-Reagan anthem) are non-starters, otherwise it is rhetoric all the way down and the sophists win.

power-knowledge.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
power-knowledge.title: Frak-tured Finality
power-knowledge.relation: Booth argues that the 'Resistance' webisodes fracture BSG's narrative across television and Internet, forcing viewers to actively construct the story — Jammer's execution in 'Collaborators' and Duck's suicide bombing only make full sense if you pieced the webisodes together — and that this viewer-side fragmentation mirrors the characters' fractured identities. Drawing on Foucault's constructed self, Deleuze and Guattari's 'schizophrenia,' Goffman's performed roles, and Haraway's cyborg, he reads Baltar's 'Am I a Cylon?', Boomer's amnesia in 'Water,' Hera's human-Cylon hybridity, and Tigh's choice in 'Crossroads' to actively construct who he will be. The payoff: there is no central location for the self, the narrative, or Cylonhood — each becomes whole only through active construction.

power-knowledge.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
power-knowledge.title: Become a Work of Art!
power-knowledge.relation: Dumitrica reads iPod customization (skins, colors, playlists) as a Foucauldian technology of the self: identity is not a stable inner core but something continually made, as when a Facebook user who loses her 80G black iPod feels 'empty'. Against Foucault's examples of ancient care of the self and Christian confessional self-renunciation, she argues the iPod embodies the modern disciplinary self: we survey our playlists against what friends will think, dividing practices split iPod owners from users of 'lame MP3 or CD-players', and social-science-style lifestyle classifications (hip-hop vs heavy metal) shape our choices. The chapter ends by urging Foucault's aesthetic escape from pre-packaged lifestyle models — treat the self as a work of art, like the author sharing holiday photos with her father instead of plunging into a self-enclosed sonic bubble.

power-knowledge.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
power-knowledge.title: A Meditation on the Word
power-knowledge.relation: Randall Auxier and Eileen Townsend stage the chapter as fiction: letters, emails, IMs, and texts (1983-2009) between the ancient vampire Étienne Lavec and the newly turned Memphis student Paulie, through which shifting vampire pop culture — Anne Rice, Buffy, True Blood, and Twilight's sparkling, animal-only Cullens — is debated. Lavec's embedded 'Meditation on the Word' recasts the Johannine Logos so that vampires are pure desire, the uncreated darkness at the border of God's light, and his biography enacts the thesis: a Latin Averroist student of Siger de Brabant who drained Aquinas over the Summa's Treatise on Angels writing vampires out of existence, and a collector who hunted or interviewed Royce, Pico della Mirandola, Descartes, Spinoza, Hegel, Kierkegaard, and Nietzsche, whose 'free death' and 'beyond good and evil' he claims as stolen vampire ideas. The running gag and argument is Foucault, whose account of institutions (medicine, psychology, prison) creating their objects Lavec endorses as the order of desire, but who, half-undead after Lavec's failed bite and taunting him anonymously as 'nietzsche26', finally lures him into a trap in the Paris catacombs.

power-knowledge.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
power-knowledge.title: 19 - facebook, Surveillance and Power
power-knowledge.relation: Doyle and Fraser open with the Lady Shelley Sawers affair, in which Britain's new MI6 chief was exposed by his wife's public Facebook profile, to ask whether social networks democratize surveillance or perfect it. They read the CIA's social-media monitoring, the Chris Dreyfus promotion case, and Facebook's Beacon advertising scheme through Foucault — Bentham's Panopticon, the carceral continuum, regimes of truth, and the shift to statistically managing populations — arguing that narcissistic self-display makes people 'most controllable,' while Habermas's public sphere frames the hopeful side: Beacon's defeat by user protest, Glassdoor, and Iran's Twitter revolution as diffused power against the centralized state. Foucault's answer is neither utopia nor repression but an ethics of self-management for playing power games with minimum domination.

power-knowledge.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
power-knowledge.title: The Last Resort
power-knowledge.relation: Petersen recounts fighting off a man who threatened to rape and kill her, and argues that karate, not feminist doctrine or therapy, made her a real feminist by rewiring her self-concept, fear responses and relationships. Against the Lara Croft fantasy she sets practical self-defense doctrine ('don't be there'; assertiveness, not aggression, with the bus pest), Australian, US and UN statistics on violence against women, and the Guthrie study of Chicago's feminist Thousand Waves dojo. She frames the transformation with Foucault's 'care of the self': karate's practices of the self give women power through knowledge, so that by black-belt time enduring harassment simply 'isn't who she is'.

power-knowledge.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
power-knowledge.title: Morgan or Moser
power-knowledge.relation: Everitt Foster reads Dexter's first season through Foucault's History of Sexuality: the relationship with Rita, the comic attempt to 'reciprocate,' and the therapy sessions with Dr. Emmett Meridian all show the 'deployment of alliance' (kinship, family, blood) intersecting with the 'deployment of sexuality,' while the observer-observed 'spiral of power and pleasure' explains Dexter's watching as a power play - letting Rita have carnal knowledge of him would hand her control over his mask. Knowledge of his past (Joe Driscoll, Rudy's true identity) destabilizes the Morgan alliance, and the finale is Dexter's deliberate choice: he kills Brian and saves Debra ('You hurt her, you hurt me'), an act Foster identifies as Foucault's 'right of death' that affirms the identity Dexter Morgan over Dexter Moser.

power-knowledge.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
power-knowledge.title: Expansive Gameplay as Simulation
power-knowledge.relation: Felan Parker coins 'expansive gameplay' for players adding optional rules inside Halo's fixed rules—speed runs, Pacifist and Zero Shots runs, the player-invented Zombie mode later made official as Infection, and Warthog jeep jumping over the Silent Cartographer archway. This mirrors Foucault's late ethics of aesthetic self-fashioning: within the constraints of Power-Knowledge, imposing personal optional rules makes existence a work of art, which Deleuze summarizes as rules 'at once ethical and aesthetic' inventing new possibilities of life. Parker tests three readings—expansive gameplay as metaphor for self-fashioning, as a genuine practice of freedom when players problematize Halo's militarist hero worship (the Pacifist Run), and finally as a simulation of rule-based systems letting players rehearse self-fashioning at a safe scale, with the gloomy alternative that it merely replaces real practices of freedom.

power-knowledge.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
power-knowledge.title: I Love You, My Artificial Construct
power-knowledge.relation: Deckard registers an empathic 4.0 on the Voight-Kampff at the thought of retiring Luba Luft, and Resch's remark that including androids in our empathic range would leave us defenseless leads the chapter to Foucault's claim that true/real distinctions reduce to struggles for power. Bounty hunting is read as a reactionary humanism whose 'barrier' keeps humans and androids distinct because technology has otherwise made them indistinguishable — as Deckard's electric sheep, needing exactly the same care as the real one, and the electric toad ('the electric things have their lives, too') confirm.

power-knowledge.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
power-knowledge.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Franklin Allaire uses Cliff Clavin's defiant 'Who are three people who've never been in my kitchen?' on Cheers to stage the fight between modern and postmodern theories of knowledge. He rehearses Plato's Theaetetus account of knowledge as justified true belief, Descartes's cogito, and Kant's thing-in-itself as modernity's quest for objective truth via universal intersubjective agreement, then argues through Foucault and Deleuze that Trebek and the judges are gatekeepers whose power controls the narrative - his Civil War renaming example ('What is the War of Northern Aggression?') shows many knowledges competing for one answer. On this view, Cliff's insistence that different questions can fit the same answer exposes the non-objectivity of Jeopardy!'s 'objective' knowledge, making the barfly a postmodern champion.

power-knowledge.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
power-knowledge.title: The Wire and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Eckstrand uses Foucault to explain the show's central pattern that 'our thing is part of the big thing': power is exercised rather than possessed, flowing through networks in every direction, so even pawn Wallace can have kingpins, captains, and prosecutors running around after him, and McNulty's fake serial killer shows how the police-Sun-politics network can be worked from below. The stat game and standardized tests are Foucauldian power/knowledge, producing a truth ('shining up shit and calling it gold') that hides systemic crime and poverty while punishing truth-tellers like Daniels and reformers like Colvin and Freamon, and its three tools of discipline, hierarchical observation, normalizing judgment, and examination, are visible from Comstat and the project-class window to the grand jury that tames the dockworkers' union. Even reform becomes part of the machine it targets (Templeton's Pulitzer chase), so the best hope is the constant accumulation of small victories by those who keep fighting.

power-knowledge.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
power-knowledge.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Chad Timm applies Foucault's disciplinary power to the International Fleet: Graff sorts monitored children like 'formless clay,' watches them through a Battle School Panopticon of head monitors and battleroom observation, and uses constant testing and the normalizing gaze to make Ender his own overseer and construct the identity of a commander. He closes by mapping the same sort-examine-discipline circuit onto standardized testing and Race to the Top, noting Ender's flicker of resistance when the children finally see through the adults' game.

power-knowledge.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
power-knowledge.title: The Devil and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Jonathon O'Donnell reads DmC: Devil May Cry's Limbo City - demon-run banks, the Fox-News parody Raptor News, Virility soda - as the newest stage in the Devil's career. Tracing the shift from Dante's frozen, defeated Satan to Milton's active deceiver and the Black Mass's sacramental counterfeits, he argues the game's demons are both the hiders and the hidden: reality itself is the demonic lie, a counterfeit truth with nothing truer beneath it. When Dante and Vergil's WikiLeaks-style reveal frees humanity, what is unveiled is not God's order but just another contingent world, a secular tale of media institutions manufacturing 'truth' for a conforming public.

power-knowledge.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
power-knowledge.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Stephenson and Waller start from disliking bland, marketable Piper and use Foucault's Discipline and Punish to argue that Litchfield is a microcosm of State power: arbitrary unwritten rules, counts, strip searches, and constant surveillance train prisoners into docile, compliant participants in capitalism, with specialist wardens, psychologists, and lawyers molding the abnormal into the normal. Prisoners specialize too (Red's kitchen, Nicky's ear, Vee's drugs) to survive, and specialization hides the surveillance. The show itself embodies the mechanism, making viewers aware they too live under the Panopticon, though deviants like Crazy Eyes and her standing pee keep open the possibility of refusing State values.

power-knowledge.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
power-knowledge.title: 1. Drugging the Kids
power-knowledge.relation: Seymour argues that the serums of Roth's world mirror the real-world medical control of young people: with no objective test, about 6.4 million American children are diagnosed with ADHD and medicated for diverging from adult-defined 'normal' behavior, just as Amity bakes peace serum into its bread and Dauntless uses simulation and truth serums on initiates. Tris's Divergence, and especially her failure to resist the peace serum because some part of her wanted to stop feeling, shows that the desire to conform is what makes chemical control work, while Tobias (re-running his own fear landscape) and Peter (erasing his own memory) model appropriating the serums as tools of self-control. Tris's resistance to the Bureau's memory serum then becomes a vicarious experience of power for young readers who face medication for their own 'divergence.'

power-knowledge.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
power-knowledge.title: 11. Should We Execute the Erudite
power-knowledge.relation: Michaud and Watkins ask whether Roth is right that the knowledge-hoarding Erudite are so dangerous we might need to eliminate them, and answer that knowledge is dangerous in three ways. Following Foucault ('it is impossible for knowledge not to engender power'), the powerful define what counts as knowledge - from the church blessing feudalism to the medical community pathologizing gay and transgender people - and following Piaget, new knowledge threatens the interconnected belief schemas (diagrammed as beliefs resting on beliefs) that keep 'faction before blood' and our sense of being special stable, which is why Divergents, evolution, and Copernicus provoke such violent disequilibrium. A Descartes-style simulation scenario - you may be inside Roth's world right now, weeded out for reading the books - and David Lewis's point that investigating knowledge destroys it then show that the real danger is not knowledge but the arrogance of certainty: Jeanine was never a true Erudite.

power-knowledge.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
power-knowledge.title: 9. Not Knowing Serial Killers with Hannibal Lecktor
power-knowledge.relation: Davis reads Manhunter's Lecktor through agnotology - Robert Proctor's study of how ignorance is made - arguing that Lecktor runs a 'knowing game' with Will Graham, strategically withholding what he knows (the Pilgrim's lunar cycle, his fan mail from the Tooth Fairy) so that Graham must do his own dangerous 'field work' and risk becoming killer or bait, a playbook he delivers as an invented Rumsfeldian riff on known knowns and unknown unknowns. The same lens then exposes the real world: the FBI's post-Silence serial-killer panic (Jenkins's evidence that the BSU's statistics were false, capped by the USS Iowa profiling fiasco) as institutional ignorance-making that inflated the FBI's power, and Egger's 'less-dead' - marginalized victims like Kendall Francois's Poughkeepsie sex workers whom media footprints render invisible, 'the missing missing' - as the human cost of our fascination with a killer who never existed.

power-knowledge.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
power-knowledge.title: 11. A Rare Gift
power-knowledge.relation: Breikss reads the Hannibal-Will bond as Sedgwick-style homosociality filtered through gift theory: Mauss and Bataille explain how Hannibal's lavish dinner parties and mentorship function as gifts that assert dominance, overwhelming Will until his inner voice becomes Hannibal's. Girard's mimetic desire then maps the rivalry's escalation — Alana as the shared object, Will's proxy murder attempt via Matthew Brown, the killing of Randall Tier that merges the two men into the 'Willdigo', and Mason Verger as the scapegoat whose death would have purged the conflict. Foucault's reading of Bosch's 'Cutting the Stone' casts Will as the patient and Hannibal as the doctor 'far more insane than the patient', with Jack and Alana as unwitting accomplices in the psychiatric stripping of Will's life, while Bataille's Erotism frames the cannibal feasts as transgression that heightens rather than abolishes the taboo.

power-knowledge.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
power-knowledge.title: 1. More Golems around Than You Might Think
power-knowledge.relation: Using Feet of Clay and Witches Abroad, Froehlich argues we are all like golems: our behavior is driven by the 'words in our heads,' the texts that society and the powerful put there. Lyotard's metanarratives explain how Lily Weatherwax forces Genua to live out fairy-tale plots and how Dragon King of Arms rewrites Nobby's family tree to manufacture a king, while dwarfish gender norms keep Cheery Littlebottom trapped in a culturally imposed text. Freedom comes only when, like Dorfl after Carrot buys him his own receipt, a person rejects the imposed words and chooses words of the heart - 'words in the heart cannot be taken.'

power-knowledge.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
power-knowledge.title: 15. The Serious Monk’s Guide to Re-writing History
power-knowledge.relation: Framed as a monkey monk-to-be telling four bored children the 'history' of four Discworld novels, the chapter argues that history is not a record of what happened but a constructed narrative: in Wyrd Sisters the Duchess commissions Hwel's play to rewrite the murder of the king, since 'the past is what people remember, and memories are words.' In Small Gods, Brutha's photographic memory of Ephebe's burning library shows that even perfect recollection is lost unless written down, while in Thief of Time the History Monks openly rebuild time as a patchwork after the Big Crash, and Susan watches historians 'rebuilt the image of the past to suit the eyesight of today.' Drawing on W. H. Walsh's idea of history as intelligible narrative, it concludes that history is performative—what people are told it is—and that we ourselves are the crowbar that opens the box of history from the inside.

power-knowledge.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
power-knowledge.title: 6. Anti-Psychiatric Help 5¢—The Doctor is IN
power-knowledge.relation: The chapter takes Lucy's five-cent psychiatry booth as a parody that vindicates the anti-psychiatry movement's three core criticisms: an abusive doctor-patient power relation (her insults, the threat of the stool, the football gag), ineffective or harmful treatment ('Snap out of it! Five cents, please'), and the impossibility of objective mental diagnosis (Thomas Szasz, the DSM's tangled history, Big Pharma's over-prescription). Foucault's History of Madness grounds the point that madness and psychiatric expertise are historically shifting social categories rather than neutral science. Lucy's accidental mindfulness-style advice and Charlie's 'existential depression' (Yalom's death, freedom, isolation, meaninglessness) point toward alternatives, and the closing thought is that Charlie's willingness to voice his sadness destigmatizes getting help.

power-knowledge.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
power-knowledge.title: 12. Only Deadpool Is Sane
power-knowledge.relation: Chad William Timm argues Deadpool is not really insane but was made 'insane' by power: via Foucault's genealogy of madness, experts like Dr. Brighton (a robotic shell for Psycho Man) at Ravenscroft and Dr. Whitby at Crossmore, along with the courts that institutionalize him after the Hulk trial, run a knowledge/power nexus that labels, sorts, and disciplines him until he internalizes the madman identity ('I think I might actually be crazy'). Nineteenth-century psychiatry's invented link between crime and madness secured the experts' authority, and disciplinary power plus technologies of the self made Deadpool discipline himself. Deadpool Kills the Marvel Universe's 'I can see through the bull##$%' and his fourth-wall awareness become resistance to these regimes of truth, and the chapter closes by turning Socrates's examined life on the reader: be careful whom you tell.

power-knowledge.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
power-knowledge.title: 6. Who Has the Power
power-knowledge.relation: Samuelson uses Foucault to dismantle Phillip Price's creed of being 'the most powerful person in the room': power is not a possession but an operation. Elliot's men in black and the FBI's surveillance are disciplinary power - Bentham's panopticon realized in Allsafe's cube farm and the internet itself - while Angela's fight over the Washington Township leak is a struggle with biopower that no sovereign can be punished for, and Whiterose's knowledge is power-knowledge that operates anonymously no matter who holds it. If Foucault is right, Price, Mr. Robot, and Zheng are mere conduits, and no one will ever be the most powerful person in the room.

power-knowledge.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
power-knowledge.title: 1. Revolutionary from the Waist Down
power-knowledge.relation: Storrie and Martin use Foucault's critique of the repressive hypothesis to argue that Winston is wrong to think sex is naturally subversive and the Party merely represses it. Power over sexuality is productive: the Soviet sexual revolution, Ceausescu's Decree 770 and its 'Decree Generation', Pornosec's pornography for pacifying proles, and tacitly tolerated prostitution all channel erotic energy into state power rather than simply forbid it. Reading O'Brien's torture of Winston as a sustained scene of rape and castration (following Cass Sunstein), they conclude that only understanding power's productive use of sex, as Julia does, makes effective resistance possible; it is Winston who turns out to be merely 'a revolutionary from the waist down'.

power-knowledge.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
power-knowledge.title: 14. The Seduction of Winston Smith
power-knowledge.relation: Mark Alfano reads the novel's ending ('He loved Big Brother') as a seduction story: following John Forrester, a seducer opens with 'I know what you're thinking', which O'Brien enacts when he voices Winston's unspoken thought under torture and demands not mere obedience but enthusiastic consent. Big Brother wins Winston over through four epistemic methods: total surveillance (telescreens, Thought Police, Parsons's own children), the Ministry of Truth's annihilation of records like the photograph of Jones, Aaronson and Rutherford, the destruction of self-trust in the 'how many fingers?' sessions, and the isolation of intimates until Winston betrays Julia. Alfano closes by mapping all four methods onto post-9/11 mass surveillance and Trump-era attacks on records, perception, and the press.

power-knowledge.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
power-knowledge.title: 10. Babies and Pleasures
power-knowledge.relation: Wesch uses Foucault's Discipline and Punish to explain how ordinary women so quickly served Gilead: power is exercised rather than possessed, so Offred enjoying the Guardians' frustration, the 'Her fault!' Testifying, and the Particicution show everyone wielding whatever power is within reach. Gilead is a panopticon in Bentham's sense—the Eyes, paired shopping, 'Under His Eye'—where unverifiable surveillance makes citizens their own overseers, while biopower sorts desirable from undesirable populations, 'making live' fertile Handmaids (shatterproof glass against suicide) and letting Unwomen and unbabies die in the Colonies. Resistance is Foucauldian too: Offred's remembered food, Moira's bathroom gossip, and sex with Nick are the 'bodies and pleasures' that counterattack the deployment of sexuality.

power-knowledge.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
power-knowledge.title: 20. Under a Watchful Eye
power-knowledge.relation: Timm gives a full Foucauldian reading: the Sons of Jacob's biblical 'knowledge' is a regime of truth produced by power (via the genealogical method Foucault took from Nietzsche), and Gilead rules less by sovereign violence (particicutions, the Wall) than by disciplinary power that defines, sorts, confines, and retrains—precisely the asylum-prison-school trajectory of Foucault's History of Madness and Discipline and Punish. The Red Center is that institution in miniature (Janine's 'Her fault, her fault'), the black vans with painted Eyes enact Bentham's Panopticon—power 'visible and unverifiable'—and biopower's medicalized control of women's reproductive bodies ties Gilead to Iowa's 2018 fetal heartbeat law. Offred's small refusals—her hidden name, the night that is 'mine,' the act of telling her tale—are the resistance Foucault always found inside disciplinary power.

power-knowledge.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
power-knowledge.title: 11. Not from Around Here
power-knowledge.relation: Zanin applies Foucault's Abnormal lectures, where a monster is a juridico-natural being violating both the laws of nature and of society, to the show: the Demogorgon and demodogs break biology and morality, while El and Eight are biologically abnormal (psionic) and law-breaking, making them Foucauldian monsters too, as Lucas's 'maybe she's the monster?' suggests. Monsters emerge wherever power/knowledge assemblages operate, hence Hawkins Lab's MK-Ultra-style experimentation conjuring the very Demogorgon it hunts, and the chapter extends monstrosity to human 'assholes' like Brenner, Lonnie, and Billy before concluding that knowing the monster, being a freak, is a virtue and a weapon against fear.

power-knowledge.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
power-knowledge.title: 15. Abnormal Is the New Normal
power-knowledge.relation: Berns, Foronda, and Zarate read the show anachronistically (via Didi-Huberman), arguing its millennial sensibilities deliberately clash with the 1980s setting to reveal that normalcy is a shifting social discourse rather than a natural fact: Joyce defends Will's possible sexuality like no 1980s mother would, Jonathan claims freakishness as a right, and audiences mourn plain, awkward Barb. Through Foucault's three figures from Abnormal, the monster (androgynous, tomboy-coded Eleven called 'freak'), the individual to be corrected (hippie Terry Ives, 'hysterical' Joyce, un-macho boys), and the masturbator (surveillance of the most intimate life), plus biopolitics and bullying as State-sanctioned discipline, they show the abnormal are the heroes: 'The X-Men are weirdos.'

power-knowledge.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
power-knowledge.title: Death
power-knowledge.relation: Reads Alien3's Fury 161 through impurity and contagion: Mary Douglas's 'matter out of place,' Foucault's confinement of the mad (the YY-chromosome inmates quarantined as social infection; Golic's fixation on the 'dragon' as Schopenhauer's madness of a fixed idea), Hegel and Schelling's philosophies of biology in which disease, decline, and death are necessary moments of life, and Plato's virtue-as-health of the soul. Ripley's fall into the molten lead embraces Schelling's 'indifference' of freedom and its enemy - she refuses Bishop's quack offer to 'deal with the malignancy' so Weyland-Yutani can never harvest the queen inside her.

power-knowledge.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
power-knowledge.title: The Buck Stops Here
power-knowledge.relation: Argues that Earth King Kuei, not Grand Secretariat Long Feng, bears the real responsibility for Ba Sing Se's fall, because he willfully maintained ignorance of the war and of his own capital's poverty so he could enjoy palace privilege, playing with his bear Bosco and never once riding the monorail among his people. The city's ring walls work as architectural exclusion that keeps the lower ring's refugees out of elite sight, while the Dai Li's brainwashing ('there is no war in Ba Sing Se', Jet's reconditioning at Lake Laogai) actively manufactures the ignorance the King depends on. Drawing on Charles Mills's epistemology of ignorance and Fricker and Medina's work, the chapter reads Kuei's 'I can't believe I never knew' as epistemic ignorance retained because knowing would cost him his lifestyle, so the buck stops with the seemingly childlike king rather than the arch-villain behind the throne.

power-knowledge.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
power-knowledge.title: Silent Wounds
power-knowledge.relation: Argues that the Fire Nation's empire, like the United States, was founded on genocide that national narratives erase: Sozin's extermination of the Air Nomads to remove the one check on his ambitions parallels manifest destiny and massacres of Indigenous peoples such as Sand Creek and the Wiyot killings at Tuluwat. The chapter shows erasure at work inside ATLA itself, as Gran Gran repeats Fire Nation propaganda by calling the Air Nomads 'extinct' rather than victims of genocide, and the refugees of the Northern Air Temple appropriate the annihilated people's home, identity, and sacred murals for a bathhouse. Aang's discovery of Gyatso's skeleton and his grief-block on the Avatar State are read as the 'silent wounds' of genocidal trauma, with the caveat that Guru Pathik's chakra cure is far simpler than the real, ongoing healing Indigenous communities require.

power-knowledge.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
power-knowledge.title: Can You Face the Bat
power-knowledge.relation: Sarah Donovan and Nicholas Richardson use Nietzsche and Foucault to present Batman as a self-constructed identity: across Batman: Year One, Arkham Asylum, and The Dark Knight Returns, Bruce consciously builds the persona ('Yes, Father, I shall become a bat') rather than revealing a deeper true self. Foucault's constructed categories of normal and abnormal surface in Arkham Asylum's 'super-sane' Joker and the Alice in Wonderland parallels that put Batman's own sanity in question alongside Amadeus Arkham's madness. Nietzsche's will to power and eternal recurrence, via the shepherd biting the snake in Zarathustra, explain why Bruce can face the bat that others flee, becoming heroic where Arkham and Dr. Cavendish go insane.

power-knowledge.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
power-knowledge.title: Damned If You Do, and Damned If You Don’t
power-knowledge.relation: McHenry reads the re-imagined series as a holy-war allegory in which both sides weaponize religion, then asks whether that manipulation is ever moral. Adama's lie about Earth is Machiavellian statecraft (with Foucault's point that privileged knowledge holds power), yet defended as serving the greater good, while Roslin's Pythia-based campaign contrasts with Bush's faith-based fear politics. The Cylons emerge as evangelical fundamentalists whose conversion of Baltar through inner Number Six runs on fear, exactly what Madison's case for religious liberty forbids. The chapter concludes the show's own gods have sided with the Colonials.

power-knowledge.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
power-knowledge.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Chad Timm reads Battle School through Foucault's disciplinary power: monitors in the skull, sorting into armies, minute-by-minute schedules, and constant testing are the power/knowledge that constructs 'the soldier,' while the ever-possible observation of teachers and desks makes the school Bentham's Panopticon that trains students to police themselves. The proof of Ender's constructed identity is his singling out of Bean exactly as Graff singled him out on the shuttle, and Timm extends the lesson to standardized testing and Obama's 'Race to the Top.'

power-knowledge.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
power-knowledge.title: “I Want to Conquer the World”
power-knowledge.relation: Uses Agamben's bios/zoē distinction (with Foucault on biopolitics and fragmented sovereignty, Hardt and Negri's 'Empire', Marx on surplus-value, and Rosa Luxemburg on unchecked capital) to read the Anderson Station massacre, Murtry shooting Coop on New Terra, and Protogen infecting 1.5 million Belters on Eros as reductions of Belter life to bare life that corporate sovereigns may kill without homicide. It then argues the instability capitalism creates births authoritarian sovereigns — Murtry's martial law, Inaros's Free Navy, Duarte's Laconia — whose followers (Chandra Wei, Cyn, Santiago Singh) display the 'total, unrestricted, unconditional loyalty' Arendt says totalitarian power demands, and closes with Foucault's warning that liberal government's security-for-freedom trade slides into the very corruption and oppression it was meant to prevent.

power-knowledge.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
power-knowledge.title: Killing the Griffins: A Murderous Exposition of Postmodernism
power-knowledge.relation: Wisnewski stages a mock murder of the Griffin family to argue that Family Guy 'oozes the postmodern.' Baudrillard's Disneyland analysis explains why the Griffins are dangerously real: they know they are cartoons (the 'we've been cancelled' scene listing failed Fox shows), so their family is no less real than ours, which is likewise modeled on TV images. Lyotard's 'incredulity toward meta-narratives' is embodied in the show's joke-about-everything: the Petoria episode mocking the UN and dictators (Milosevic, Hussein, Khadafi) who party over Seinfeld. The chapter's twist is that Foucault's power/knowledge rescues postmodernism from cynicism: labeling Quagmire a 'pervert' situates him in power relations, but like Socrates, Jesus, Buddha, and Gandhi, deviants may just act uniquely, so we can be cynics about grand stories yet still fight locally (against the FCC, for tolerance).

power-knowledge.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
power-knowledge.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Kylie Prymus asks whether Kefka is truly mad, using Foucault's Madness and Civilization to argue that madness is a label society applies to dismiss what it cannot control, so players and heroes refute Kefka with the ad hominem 'you're crazy' rather than answering him. She then reads Kefka's 'monument to non-existence' through Nietzsche: his godlike discovery that existence has no justification echoes the death of God, our horror at him reflects slave morality's relabeling of noble strength as evil, and the heroes' appeal to purposes he lacks fails because existence is only a hypothetical imperative. Kefka ends up a failed Ubermensch who overthrows the gods but cannot overcome nihilism, leaving the World of Ruin heroes the genuinely Nietzschean task of creating meaning where none is given.

power-knowledge.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
power-knowledge.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Applying Foucault's History of Madness, the chapter argues that sanity in Westeros is an act of naming by the powerful: Joffrey literally remakes the drunken Ser Dontos into a court fool, and 'Mad King' Aerys's brutality gets labeled madness while comparable violence by Jaime (throwing Bran from the window) and Robert (ordering Daenerys's assassination) counts as sane necessity. The power/knowledge nexus and the psychiatric fusion of crime with insanity explain how Robert's personal hatred of Rhaegar hides behind a medicalized diagnosis of Targaryen madness. The chapter then tracks Foucault's shift from sovereign to disciplinary power and technologies of the self: Dontos internalizes and performs his fool identity, Dany wonders 'perhaps I am mad' at Drogo's pyre, and Catelyn's freeing of Jaime is written off by Robb's bannermen as 'a mother's madness.'

power-knowledge.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
power-knowledge.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: The chapter uses Foucault to explain how Salander could leave school without a certificate yet master Fermat-class mathematics: schools 'cut' students into fabricated 'human kinds'—the problem-solving child and the at-risk child (Popkewitz's alchemy)—and under No Child Left Behind that sorting licenses surveillance and discipline of everything an at-risk student does. Lisbeth's case shows the machinery: her correct answer marked wrong from the textbook key, her Rubik's-cube brilliance ignored, her 381 days strapped to a bed under Teleborian's silhouette-like gaze recasting Bentham's Panopticon, and her subsequent guardianship extending the watch over her money and behavior. Because power 'produces reality,' the at-risk label becomes self-fulfilling, and Lisbeth's refusal to be disciplined—her silence, tattoos, and asocial style—only supplies fresh evidence for the label.

power-knowledge.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
power-knowledge.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
power-knowledge.relation: Van Dyke uses Foucault's account of discipline and 'docile bodies' (with Susan Bordo's feminist elaboration) to explain how the Capitol rules: citizens satiated with abundance channel their hungers into fashion, body modification, and self-surveillance, and this self-focused discipline trains their attention away from the injustices that sustain them — which is how the genuinely affectionate prep team can weep over Katniss yet love the Games. She shows that District 13 disciplines just as totally through rigid schedules, rations, and punishment (the prep team chained for taking bread), so neither Snow's hidden indulgence nor Coin's overt regimentation leaves room for autonomy. Cinna's styling of Katniss demonstrates the alternative: body modification as internally generated self-expression and resistance that helps Katniss become the Mockingjay rather than a docile body.

power-knowledge.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
power-knowledge.title: Notes
power-knowledge.relation: Meyer reads the franchise through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: Max's terror of becoming a 'terminal crazy' replays madness-as-contagion, the great confinement of the mad alongside rabid animals recurs in Max's leashing and Humungus 'unleash[ing] my dogs of war,' and delirium as one step out of reason's furrow frames Johnny the Boy's 'I was sick!' plea. Applying the M'Naghten cognitive test and the wild-beast standard to Johnny the Boy, Blaster, Wez, and Nux, he concludes most followers can still tell right from wrong and remain responsible. The ultimate blame therefore falls on the cult leaders — Toecutter, Humungus, and Immortan Joe — who manufacture and exploit a shared psychosis.

power-knowledge.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
power-knowledge.title: Madness in the Mirror of Reason: Metallica and Foucault on Insanity and Confinement
power-knowledge.relation: Brian Cameron reads 'Welcome Home (Sanitarium)' and 'Frayed Ends of Sanity' through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: the sanitarium is a total institution whose surveillance and power-knowledge produce docile bodies, confining madness as a threat to the rule of reason just as the seventeenth-century Hopital General confined the idle. Madness is not a mere disease but a socially defined deviance - and a form of rebellion against conformist society - whose violent 'cure' ('violent use brings violent plans') exacts an existential cost on the rebel, as 'The Unforgiven''s bitter old man shows.

power-knowledge.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
power-knowledge.title: “We Always Have Something To Do”
power-knowledge.relation: Engels uses Foucault's Archaeology of Knowledge, authorities of delimination, and power/knowledge to show that SNL now produces rather than merely reports political truth, as when the Fey-Palin sketch shifted media blame for the Couric interview from the McCain campaign onto Palin herself. The 2016 sketches (McKinnon's Clinton as the inevitable winner, David's Sanders as a fringe idealist, Baldwin's Trump as a self-sabotaging loser) are read as discursive framings that confirmed and shaped mainstream narratives. Like Foucault's doctors defining madness, comedy writers now set the boundaries of political truth, which spotlighted sexist double standards but proved dangerous when SNL's detached writers misread working-class voters; following Foucault's 'everything is dangerous,' she concludes we always have something to do.

power-knowledge.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
