Following Merleau-Ponty's claim that art records subjective experience, the chapter treats Levine's team as artistic phenomenologists whose design question 'What is this experience we are trying to make?' turned Columbia and Elizabeth into phenomenological analyses to be read.

embodiment.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
embodiment.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
embodiment.relation: Ken Pepper uses Merleau-Ponty's Phenomenology of Perception to explain how Tony Iommi's homemade plastic fingertips work: like the blind man's cane, they are incorporated into his body schema so that he perceives the fretboard through them, refuting the Cartesian "objective body" picture on which playing would be inner plans causing finger movements. On creative freedom, the chapter stages Merleau-Ponty against Sartre's radical freedom, Iommi did choose to relearn guitar after hearing two-fingered Django Reinhardt, and his restricted two-finger chords, lighter strings, and drop tunings birthed heavy metal, but Sartre is wrong that attitude alone transcends disability, since some possibilities (playing at all without the tips) were simply not live. Only Iommi, taking up the possibilities his body-in-his-situation afforded, could have invented metal.

embodiment.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
embodiment.title: Inside the Lived Body
embodiment.relation: Pits Merleau-Ponty's embodied self against Descartes' representationalism and mind-over-matter dualism to read Inside Out: Riley's five personified emotions look like homunculi inviting an infinite regress, but the film actually shows a holistic body-subject whose emotions arise in situations and with others. Joy's campaign to keep Riley 'okay' dramatizes the futility of constant happiness and the necessity of Sadness, while Riley's hockey stick becoming an extension of her body illustrates Merleau-Ponty's claim that skillful coping lives in the body rather than in Sadness's 'mind manuals.' The chapter ends on childhood's lived present and the film's power to hold loss before us instead of pushing past it.

embodiment.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
embodiment.title: Notes
embodiment.relation: David Lawrence opens with Fallout 4's 'Blind Betrayal', where Elder Maxson orders the player to execute Paladin Danse once his synth origin is revealed, and argues that moral status is a matter of capacities - sense of self, notion of past and future, values, life-plans, moral agency - drawing on Charles Taylor's concept of a person and narrative identity, not on biological substrate. Nick Valentine's hunt for Eddie Winter in 'Long Time Coming' and Curie's chosen embodiment in 'Emergent Behavior' show machines weaving reconstructed pasts into new life-plans, while ghouls like Hancock and Raul ('Old School Ghoul') and super mutants like Fawkes (who refuses to enter the lethal radiation chamber: 'I would not rob you of that') and the community-builder Marcus prove branded monsters can be more human than human. The factions embody warring philosophies of moral status: the Institute's property-slavery of its creations, the Brotherhood's 'wisdom of repugnance' (Leon Kass), and the Railroad's capacity-based abolitionism, with DiMA's Far Harbor question - how do you know you are not a synth? - turning the issue on the player.

embodiment.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
embodiment.title: 22. Professor Stomachache Needs Neuroscience
embodiment.relation: Brings Antonio Damasio's Somatic Marker Hypothesis to Chidi's stomachaches: gut feelings are evolved, body-based shortcuts built from a lifetime of social interaction that prune options in real-time moral choice, so Chidi's classroom mastery paired with real-world collapse mirrors Damasio's ventromedial patients — except Chidi has the alarms and refuses to trust them, insisting ethics is pure calculation. Mark Johnson's moral imagination (his own draft-number dilemma) and Scanlon's contractualism (morality is other people) reinforce that we are not disembodied reasoners. Combining Dewey's 'morals is education' with Damasio's claim that somatic learning never stops, the chapter explains how Eleanor and friends keep growing morally even after death — bodies, social bonds and all.

embodiment.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
embodiment.title: NOTES
embodiment.relation: The section rejects the 'captain of a ship' picture of mind directing body, quoting Descartes himself on being so 'compounded and intermingled' with the body as to form 'a single whole,' and reads the Polyjuice episodes as proof: Harry in Runcorn's body naturally 'thunders' with a powerful voice and punches with an enormous fist, while Luna recognizes Harry through 'Barny's' face, impossible if mind and body were separable. The conclusion is that transformed people are unified man-dog wholes, and that even Muggle changes such as weight loss, learning to ride a bike, or Crouch-as-Moody show that changing our bodies changes who we are.

embodiment.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
embodiment.title: Leap of Faith
embodiment.relation: Dionne reads Cobb's 'idea is the most resilient parasite' as a claim about narrative: what gets incepted in Fischer is a story ('my father doesn't want me to follow in his footsteps'), and by the same token each of us is a collection of incepted stories rather than a stable self. Drawing on Bergson's account of perception mediated by memory and desire (Cobb's bridge triggering Mal's projection), Nietzsche's perspectivism — truth is a 'moral prejudice' and 'we must mistake ourselves' — and the embodiment of the being-in-the-world, she argues dreams differ from reality only in degree, since both are interested story-making under time pressure. The payoff is meta-filmic: Fischer is the spectator and Cobb the director, and the final spinning top becomes the audience's own totem — there is no fact of the matter, only interpretation, so watching the ending is itself the leap of faith.

embodiment.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
embodiment.title: Putting One’s Mind into a Body
embodiment.relation: Seng reads the 2008 film's crash-and-stabilizer flying lessons as philosophy of mind: at first the armor seems to confirm Descartes' dualism, with Stark the thinking substance piloting a mechanical body and Jarvis playing the pineal gland. But Stark smashing into the ceiling while learning to fly shows the embodied mind of Dewey and Merleau-Ponty — habits, spatial existence, and the imported home preferences that make the suit feel like his own skin, so that the repulsors whir closed when he stands down before the village gunmen. Dewey's view of intelligence as acting on estimates of a situation then explains Stark's growth from selfish playboy to sharable goods (beating the merely self-interested Stane), and Jarvis counts as Stark's mind made manifest in the suit.

embodiment.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
embodiment.title: Game versus Place
embodiment.relation: Douglas Wilson argues that Wind Waker's Ballad of Gales warping degrades 'environmental presence' — the feeling of being in a virtual place — by privileging destination over journey, just as Wolfgang Schivelbusch said railway travel annihilated space and time for nineteenth-century passengers. Using Castells's contrast between spaces of flows and spaces of places and Michel de Certeau's opposition of the panoptic map view to embodied everyday experience, he shows how the map-grid teleport interface turns Hyrule's ocean into abstract, disposable space. He concedes warping is a defensible design compromise, but insists that goal-oriented play crowds out the sense of place that makes virtual worlds valuable as more than games.

embodiment.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
embodiment.title: Notes
embodiment.relation: Di Summa reads Jenny Beavan's costume design as philosophy of technology: Immortan Joe's oxygen-fed carapace and the chrome-spraying War Boys visualize Heidegger's warning that technology converts nature and bodies into resources, while Max's blood-drip tether to Nux literalizes our co-dependence on machines — and on each other's flesh and blood. Through Rosemarie Garland-Thomson's staring, Sherri Irvin's body aesthetics, and Tobin Siebers's disability aesthetics, Furiosa's uncovered stump becomes an act of aesthetic exploration that defeats ableism: in this film, disability is a thing for heroes, and vulnerability is itself a human strength.

embodiment.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
embodiment.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
embodiment.relation: Spencer gives a phenomenological account of bodily transformation in the films: with Merleau-Ponty, Peter's new body changes his world — walls become surfaces to climb — and grants motor knowledge that needs no calculation, while Norman Osborn's deliberately seized powers feed pride and Doc Ock's grief shows how transformation can sweep a weak will into vice. Virtue, on Aquinas's definition as the perfection of a power, develops only through choices and habits worked out across a whole life, so ethics is deeper than rule-following. With Levinas, the call to goodness is experienced bodily: sympathy with others' suffering draws Peter out of himself — he rushes into a burning building even when powerless in Spider-Man 2 — and the Green Goblin lives a self-contradiction by feigning deafness to it, while eros for Mary Jane both distracts from and ennobles the quest.

embodiment.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
embodiment.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
embodiment.relation: Uses SAMCRO's ink—Jax's full Reaper backpiece and John Teller memorial, Opie's portrait of Donna, Tig's marine 'Death Before Dishonor,' Juice's head tattoos—to argue that personal identity lives in the body, not just the mind. Descartes's cogito opens the 'I ink, therefore I am' framing but proves too thin to connect the thinking Jax to the tattooed body, so the chapter turns to Merleau-Ponty's claim that 'it is the body which points out, and which speaks': the tattoo makes the body itself the expression, and its meaning stays inexhaustible as the wearer changes. The Kyle Hobart episode—burned and cut for failing to black out his Reaper after expulsion—shows tattoos as identity claims the community can veto, making 'fire or knife' an enforced correction of a false statement about who he is.

embodiment.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
embodiment.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
embodiment.relation: Reads Jax's '92 miles an hour' monologue in 'Sovereign' through Heidegger and Hubert Dreyfus: expert riding, Chibs's pub brawling, and Tara's surgery are pre-reflective embodied skills that conscious rule-following would only ruin. Tig fixing bikes in the Teller-Morrow garage illustrates readiness-to-hand, Bobby's smoke-spewing Fat Boy the breakdown of un-readiness-to-hand, and browsing the Harley parts catalogue the detached present-at-hand. Against the alienation of calculative, instrumental thinking (Marx, Heidegger's standing-reserve — Clay selling the club to the Galindo Cartel, Cara Cara's porn bodies), the chapter follows Pirsig: maintenance is a form of care, so Opie rebuilding a '65 Panhead after Donna's death reconciles the biker with technology instead of enslaving him to it.

embodiment.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
embodiment.title: Notes
embodiment.relation: Argues Star Trek functions like the Greek myths Nussbaum describes: modern tales of transformation (Gary Mitchell in "Where No Man Has Gone Before", Charlie X, Roger Korby) that let audiences judge what makes someone human. It rejects the Cartesian reading (Richard Hanley's Is Data Human?) in which Data's humanity is just a matter of being a rational mind, and develops instead a feminist, developmental account of personhood drawn from Annette Baier: persons are "second persons" who learn the arts of personhood from caretakers. Data, Seven of Nine, and Voyager's Doctor, all lacking real childhoods and families, must learn play, touch, love, and interdependence from their crews, with Janeway modeling family for Seven and Kes socializing the Doctor. Picard's farewell to Shinzon in Nemesis and to Data's B-4 caps the claim that humanity is an achievement of self-improvement in relationship, not a fixed essence.

embodiment.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
embodiment.title: Notes
embodiment.relation: Applies Husserl's phenomenology - noesis (the act of meaning-giving), noema (the meaning arrived at), and the life-world - to Voyager's Doctor and Seven of Nine as they build selves from conscious experience. Reads "Latent Image" (the Doctor's deleted memories of choosing Harry Kim's life over another ensign's) and "Infinite Regress" (Seven's channeling of assimilated personalities) as parallel guilt experiences whose noemata teach each that past choices remain part of identity without governing it. Their forced isolation in "One", the Doctor's unrequited love in "Someone to Watch over Me", and "Body and Soul", where the Doctor savors food and sensation through Seven's body, generate a shared noema: social interaction and embodied experience are what make a life-world, even for photons and drones.

embodiment.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
embodiment.title: Notes
embodiment.relation: Reads Jedi training through Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology and the enactivism of Varela, Thompson, and Rosch: Obi-Wan's blast-shield remote drill and Yoda's Dagobah obstacle course work because perception, thought, and action are one embodied flow rather than a perception-cognition-action 'sandwich.' Luke fails to lift the X-wing because his habits do not yet present the ship as liftable, while for Yoda 'size matters not'; and Jedi need no special Force-organ (so midi-chlorians are redundant) because skilled interaction, like Bach-y-Rita's tactile-vision subjects, determines what experience is like.

embodiment.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
embodiment.title: 11. Of Bats and Supermen
embodiment.relation: Springett argues Superman, not Batman, is the right goal for a transhumanist future: through Merleau-Ponty's embodied cognition (Lois's deadline nausea, Alfred recovering a thought by redoing his posture, real-life 'Subway Superman' Wesley Autrey's gut-level rescue) he shows bodies shape thought and morality, so a super-body means a super-mind. Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' becomes 'what is it like to be Superman' — a problem of superhero minds, with Doctor Manhattan's indifference as the cautionary case — while Superman's rescues of the less fit show transcendence need not slide into eugenics or Social Darwinism.

embodiment.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
embodiment.title: XV - MUTANT PHENOMENOLOGY
embodiment.relation: Wisnewski applies phenomenology to mutant embodiment: if consciousness is 'I can' and the body is our point of view on the world, then Kitty Pryde's walls, Nightcrawler's teleportation, Angel's flight, Madrox's duplicate spaces, and Rogue's untouchability describe genuinely different worlds, not merely different powers. Apocalypse's millennia of near-immortality and the X-Verse's reversible deaths unsettle Heidegger's being-toward-death and Becker's death-denial that organizes human culture. Concluding with Nagel's bat, he argues we cannot know what it is like to be a mutant, only what our own being-in-the-world would become if our bodily limitations changed.

embodiment.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
embodiment.title: Federer as Religious Experience
embodiment.relation: David Foster Wallace argues that watching Roger Federer live at Wimbledon delivers a near-religious experience because top sport is a prime venue for 'kinetic beauty'—a beauty rooted in human beings' reconciliation with the fact of having a body. He reads the 2006 Federer-Nadal final as a clash of the Apollonian (Federer's clinical northern artistry) against the Dionysian (Nadal's martial southern machismo), and dwells on specific Federer Moments (the reverse-thrust forehand winner against Agassi at the 2005 US Open) as instances where an athlete seems exempt from physical law. He treats Federer's grace as ineffable, defining it by what it is not, and juxtaposes the transcendent beauty of the body against the suffering body of cancer-survivor coin-tosser William Caines.

embodiment.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
embodiment.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
embodiment.relation: Kroustallis reads Lust, Caution through perception rather than hidden emotion, arguing Wong Chia Chi abandons the disengaged, sight-only aesthetic of Mrs. Mak and comes to perceive Mr. Yee's world with her whole engaged body. He uses Merleau-Ponty's Phenomenology of Perception to justify the three graphic sex scenes as bodily, essentially ambiguous cognition (the lipstick-marked cup, the flat key as motor intentionality) that links perception directly to action without unconscious representations. He frames Wong's development toward harmony via Fang Dongmei's neo-Confucian 'creative creativity' and a yin-yang polarity of meek and strong, with rain and jasmine flowers as an engaged natural environment.

embodiment.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
embodiment.title: “I am not an I” Performative (Self)Identity in the Poetry of Bob Kaufman
embodiment.relation: Pynn reads Bob Kaufman's poems ('Forget To Not,' 'Would You Wear My Eyes?,' 'Benediction,' 'Jail Poems') as enacting a performative, intersubjective selfhood: against Beauvoir's 'flavor of death' in American conformity and Sartre's dictum that existence precedes essence, Kaufman replaces the drive to invincibility with 'nakedness' and vulnerability. Merleau-Ponty's embodied intercorporeity and Buddhist ontology—impermanence, non-self, compassion, and ahimsa—let the poet's 'I am not an I' burn the isolated ego into a communal 'thousand me's,' with slavery's trauma inscribed on the body and Kaufman's 1963 Buddhist vow of silence as liberating practice.

embodiment.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
embodiment.title: High Off the Page Representing the Drug Experience in the Work of Jack Kerouac and Allen Ginsberg
embodiment.relation: Erik Mortenson argues that Kerouac's and Ginsberg's drug writing works 'through the body' to transmit the altered temporality of intoxication to the reader, using Merleau-Ponty's account of original speech and the lived body as gesture, and Deleuze and Guattari's 'Body Without Organs' and speeds. Marijuana expands the present into Kerouac's long exfoliating sentences and empathetic 'digging' (Visions of Cody, On the Road), while Benzedrine contracts it into the accelerated confessional rush of The Subterraneans; Ginsberg's LSD poems ('Lysergic Acid,' 'Wales Visitation') hit the limit of representing timelessness. The chapter concludes the writing lets the nonuser get 'high off the page' without the dependency Deleuze and Guattari warn of.

embodiment.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
embodiment.title: On Being John Malkovich and Not Being Yourself
embodiment.relation: Falzon argues that Being John Malkovich stages the Cartesian self as a nonbodily homunculus — Craig 'riding' behind Malkovich's eyes via the vision-limiting cutout and muffled audio — only to expose its absurdity when Malkovich enters his own portal and finds a world reduced to 'Malkovich, Malkovich.' As Craig learns to fully inhabit and puppeteer the body, the film shifts to Merleau-Ponty's and Dewey's embodied 'lived body' organized by habit. Reading Craig's takeover as Foucauldian subjectification through training, Falzon contrasts Craig's self-entrapping mastery with Lotte's genuine self-transcendence, her openness to being other than herself.

embodiment.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
embodiment.title: Knockout! Killer’s Kiss, the Somatic, and Kubrick Kevin S. Decker
embodiment.relation: Decker reads Killer's Kiss (and later 2001, A Clockwork Orange, Eyes Wide Shut) through Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of the lived body ('I am my body'), recovering the somatic that Socrates and Plato's Phaedo denigrated. In Killer's Kiss the boxing match, the mannequin-warehouse fight where bodies become weapons, spatial camera work, and the theme of contingency foreground embodiment; 2001 makes viewers feel their own bodies in space, and A Clockwork Orange's Ludovico 'cure' rewires the body-mind. Drawing on pragmatists Shusterman and Sullivan and on Foucault's biopower, he argues the anonymous masked bodies of Eyes Wide Shut turn Merleau-Ponty's projective intentionality into domination rather than communication.

embodiment.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
embodiment.title: 2001 A Philosophical Odyssey
embodiment.relation: Stoehr interprets Kubrick's 2001 as inducing a feeling of disembodied presence through unrooted camerawork (contrasted with Ford's The Searchers), matching its theme of technology severing us from the natural world and our bodies. Drawing on Heidegger's Dasein and Hubert Dreyfus's On the Internet, he argues there are no context-free Archimedean standpoints and stages the Plato-versus-Nietzsche debate over the body: Plato's Phaedo prizes the soul's escape from the body, while Nietzsche's Zarathustra affirms embodied, situated existence. HAL's seeming humanity underscores that machines lacking bodies cannot fully replicate human intelligence.

embodiment.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
embodiment.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
embodiment.relation: Decker reads Killer's Kiss (with 2001, A Clockwork Orange, and Eyes Wide Shut) to recover the philosophy of the body against the Socratic-Platonic-Cartesian denigration of the somatic. Using Merleau-Ponty's existential phenomenology ('I am my body') and pragmatists like Shusterman and Sullivan, he shows Kubrick's obsessive use of space, contingency, and the visceral - Davy's boxing match, the mannequin-warehouse fight, the weightless bodies of 2001, the Ludovico brainwashing of Alex, and the anonymous masked bodies of Eyes Wide Shut - to argue that subjectivity is corporeal and that anonymity of bodies can fund Foucauldian domination rather than liberation.

embodiment.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
embodiment.title: The Violated Body Affective Experience and Somatic Intensity in Zero Dark Thirty
embodiment.relation: Burgoyne argues that Kathryn Bigelow's Zero Dark Thirty places the violated body at the center of its rendering of the War on Terror, using somatic intensity and affective experience against Steven Shaviro's reading of the film as pure, affect-draining proceduralism. He traces Maya's arc from witness to coercive agent through the torture of Ammar, the Goya-like montage of interrogation videos, and the suicide-bomb killing of her friend Jessica, mapping the film onto Sarah Cole's poles of disenchanted violence (the raw, exposed flesh of the interrogations) and enchanted violence (the technologically choreographed, almost magical SEAL raid on Abbottabad, likened to Baudrillardian simulated combat). The closing unzipping of bin Laden's body bag deflates any triumph into embodied ambiguity.

embodiment.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
embodiment.title: Werner Herzog and the Documentary as a Revelatory Practice
embodiment.relation: Antony Fredriksson argues that Herzog's documentaries are not veridical fact-representations but a 'revelatory practice,' aligning Herzog's ecstatic-versus-accountant's-truth distinction with phenomenology (Merleau-Ponty, Husserl, Waldenfels). Using Merleau-Ponty's reading of Fabrice at Waterloo, he claims lived experience is contingent and pre-narrative, and that films like La Soufriere (a catastrophe that never happens), White Diamond (swifts behind the waterfall), and Echoes from a Somber Empire (the nicotine-addicted monkey) reveal the alien, attention-grabbing world beyond habitual seeing — a 'pathos' that reads the viewer rather than neutrally recording facts.

embodiment.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
embodiment.title: 06_LaRocca_Chapter_005.html
embodiment.relation: Sobchack offers a semiotic phenomenology of how real death is represented in documentary, arguing that death itself always exceeds and confounds indexical representation—we never see death, only dying and the corpse. Using Aries on the modern taboo-ing of natural death, Barthes on the traumatic photograph, and the Zapruder assassination footage whose frame-by-frame scrutiny yields only mystification, she shows why violent, abrupt mortification of the lived body is the most effective cinematic sign of death. Drawing on Heidegger's Being-toward-death and its deferral, Beauvoir's 'no such thing as a natural death,' and Merleau-Ponty's lived body, she classifies documentary's ethical 'gazes' at death (accidental, helpless, endangered, interventional, humane, professional) as inscriptions of the filmmaker's moral stance in an embodied ethical space.

embodiment.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
embodiment.title: 27_LaRocca_Chapter_026.html
embodiment.relation: Michael Fried reads Douglas Gordon and Philippe Parreno's Zidane: A Twenty-First Century Portrait, seventeen synchronized cameras trained on Zinedine Zidane through one Real Madrid match, as a portrait that lays bare a new relation between absorption and being-beheld. Set within Fried's own absorption/theatricality tradition, the film shows Zidane wholly absorbed yet acutely conscious of eighty thousand spectators ('you are never alone'), which Fried reads via Heidegger's notion that even this 'bare' absorbed consciousness discloses a shared world (underscored by the halftime global news montage). He then stages the film as evidence in the McDowell-Dreyfus dispute over whether perception is conceptual, arguing that Zidane's 'expert coping' looks 'permeated by mindedness' (McDowell) rather than the non-conceptual absorbed coping Dreyfus, following Merleau-Ponty's embodied phenomenology, describes.

embodiment.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
embodiment.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
embodiment.relation: Acton draws on her anthropological fieldwork riding to hounds in English foxhound packs to explore the human/equine partnership with the 'made hunter' horse. Using Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of the body-in-movement and Tim Ingold's notion of 'dwelling,' she argues the rider experiences the hunt through 'muscular consciousness' and 'centaur hours,' taking on the horse's senses and physicality. Trusting the sharp horse to 'work it out' — as when her hunter checked pace to avoid a collision at a jump — becomes an embodied, timeless collaboration binding rider, horse, hounds, and landscape.

embodiment.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
embodiment.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
embodiment.relation: Through the narrative of 'Aisha', a feminist who is aroused by SM imagery she has been taught to disown, Khan attacks the censorship of SM pornography and its 'monkey see, monkey do' harm hypothesis (citing declining rape rates). She names three state-inflicted harms: physical violence (prison sentences in Guglielmi and R. v. Brown), phenomenological violence—using Husserl and Merleau-Ponty's embodied phenomenology to argue courts dismiss submissives' lived reality as 'worthless'—and epistemic violence, using Foucault's power/knowledge to show how the Supreme Court of Canada in Little Sisters overrode expert and practitioner testimony about coded SM meaning. She argues SM consent and pleasure are real knowledge that censorship, aligned with MacKinnon/Dworkin anti-porn feminism, coercively erases.

embodiment.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
embodiment.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
embodiment.relation: Brunstein surveys emerging wearable technology — solar-charging jackets, the M-Dress cell-phone dress, invisibility cloaks, the Hug Shirt, Diana Eng's Heartbeat Hoodie — framed by superhero costumes (Wonder Woman's lasso, Iron Man's exoskeleton) and Haraway's 'Cyborg Manifesto.' She argues that as garments start to *do* things and integrate aesthetically, the grotesque cyborg becomes the glamorous 'supermodel' cyborg, and that this reshapes how we construct the self. Her central philosophical lens is Clark and Chalmers's 'extended mind' / active externalism (with the Tetris example): if clothing becomes a functional extension of cognition, our garments' capabilities become part of a reconstructed self.

embodiment.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
embodiment.title: GARDENING
embodiment.relation: Michael Moss examines how the British grew Brussels sprouts and other 'English' vegetables across the Empire to recreate home and 'put down roots,' reading gardens as tropes of Britishness and imperial identity. He draws on David Cooper's claim—rooted in Heidegger's and Merleau-Ponty's notions of dynamic, embodied engagement—that 'certain garden practices necessarily induce virtues,' which colonial writers invoked to justify gardening's moral and civilizing purpose. He exposes the irony that most 'British' vegetables were themselves appropriated introductions, mirroring Kew's plant-hunting empire.

embodiment.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
embodiment.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
embodiment.relation: Karlsen argues that climbing routes are genuine aesthetic objects and that judging a route beautiful is a real aesthetic judgment, not mere pleasure. Against Kant's demand that beauty require detachment (which would confine climbing to the 'merely agreeable') and against Aristotle's exclusion of the bodily senses, he distinguishes a 'line' (seen from the ground, like The Nose) from a 'route' (actually climbed) and contends that proprioception, the felt sense of bodily movement, yields information about the route itself, not just the body. Invoking the phenomenological 'transparency of experience' (Moore's diaphanousness), he concludes proprioception is an aesthetic sense that lets widely-agreed classics emerge.

embodiment.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
embodiment.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
embodiment.relation: Rachel Falkenstern argues that although tattoos seem permanent, the embodied self is changing and finite, so tattoos are 'illusions of permanence.' Using Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology she dissolves the mind/body and self/tattoo boundary (we are our bodies, the world shapes us and we shape it); using the German aesthetic tradition from Kant to Hegel she reads a tattoo as a sensuous 'appearance of freedom' and links the Romantic notion of Bildung (self-formation) to choosing ink. She adds Foucault's aesthetic self-transformation and Shusterman's somaesthetics/Deweyan pragmatism to cast tattooing as reciprocal self-expression and self-creation that offers a glimpse of infinity within finitude.

embodiment.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
embodiment.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
embodiment.relation: Lee argues that tattooing is a performative 'practice of writing' whose meaning always exceeds its origin, comparing Holocaust survivor Tova Friedman's Auschwitz number 'A27633' with the Suicide Girl Jaylin's chosen feminist ink. Drawing on Judith Butler's account of the body as a site of inscription and counter-inscription, and Walter Benjamin's 'Critique of Violence' distinguishing law-making from law-preserving force, she claims Friedman's tattoo resists the Nazi law itself while Jaylin's only satirizes heteropatriarchy. She then invokes Baudrillard's 'ecstasy of communication' and the obscene to show tattooing can desubjectify by dissolving the embodied self into pornographic information.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
sun-tzu-strategy.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Argues Tony misappropriates Sun Tzu's Art of War: he applies tactical precepts like deception, formlessness and 'Balk the enemy's power' (citing the book in 'He Is Risen' after Melfi's jab in 'Big Girls Don't Cry'), but ignores the philosophical core. The chapter contrasts Sun Tzu's monistic one-world view of yin-yang interdependence, harmony and winning without fighting with the Greek two-world dualism of Plato and with the Christianity that lets Tony tell Melfi 'soldiers don't go to hell' in 'From Where to Eternity'. Tony's sausage panic attacks in 'Fortunate Son' show his failure to see how his crimes ripple through his family, and because he lacks the commander's exemplary character and harmony, Tony is 'just a soldier', not a ruler.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
sun-tzu-strategy.title: Poker and Philosophy
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Hahn reads Doyle Brunson's Super System — 'I go into a Poker game with the idea of completely destroying it' — as applied Machiavelli: The Prince's fox and lion become the bluffer and the bully chip leader, 'better to be feared than loved' justifies cutting even old friend Sailor Roberts's throat at the table, and swift decisive attack (Tex Barch stomped out of the 2005 WSOP) avoids sowing the seeds of vengeance. Fortune rules half our events — the river card that fills an opponent's inside straight — so virtù means building dikes against the flood, as Cesare Borgia failed to do when his papal patron died. Sun Tzu's 'when able, seem to be unable' supplies the same disguise of strength in poker and in war.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
sun-tzu-strategy.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Morgan Deane maps Ender's tactics onto Sunzi's Art of War: exploiting Bonzo's hot anger, draining the enemy's martial spirit, Graff's use of 'fatal terrain' to throw students into hopeless situations, and staying 'formless' like water so opponents cannot read his plans. Drawing also on Laozi's Dao as the flow a commander must channel, Confucian role ethics in the general-as-father relation, and Legalist reward-and-punishment systems, he concludes Ender qualifies as a military genius by classical Chinese standards - at the wrenching moral cost both he and Graff pay.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
sun-tzu-strategy.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Matthew Brophy argues the I.F. neutralizes Ender's moral agency by masquerading xenocide as child's play: Rackham's paradox that total empathy with the buggers forbids killing them (Sunzi's 'know your enemy') is solved by deception, Walzer's problem of dirty hands is shifted from the child to the politicians, and Milgram-style game framing plus Foot's trolley-problem 'moral distance' show how killing grows easier at a console. Against the innocent-pawn reading, Brophy ends by suggesting Ender was a willing pawn who let himself be deceived in order to save humanity.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
sun-tzu-strategy.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Morgan Deane reads Ender's tactics as Sunzi's Art of War in action: winning all future fights by terror, exploiting Bonzo's hot anger, 'fatal terrain' when Graff stacks hopeless odds, formlessness that hides intent, and fluid toon formations that move like water — all grounded in Daoist harmony with the Way and the Confucian role-duty of the general-as-father who throws soldiers into hopeless positions to win their devotion. He also finds Legalist rewards-and-punishments in Ender's command of Dragon Army, concluding Ender qualifies as a Sunzi-style military genius whose empathy is the steep moral price of victory.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
sun-tzu-strategy.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Kody Cooper argues Ender's tortured conscience demonstrates the classical just war framework: from Augustine's axiom that peace is the end of war and the five jus ad bellum requirements, to the verdict that the Third Invasion fails right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality because the rational hive-queens were never given a real chance at coexistence. He reads the I.F.'s withholding of protection as throwing Ender into a Hobbesian state of nature where his fights with bullies count as private just wars, and concludes Ender carries the sins of the I.F. and humanity rather than his own guilt.

sun-tzu-strategy.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
sun-tzu-strategy.title: Notes
sun-tzu-strategy.relation: Bein argues Wonder Woman uniquely fuses two supposedly incompatible moralities: bushido - Nitobe's eight samurai virtues, Sun Tzu's benevolence of ending war swiftly, worthy-opponent rituals mirrored in superhero costumes - and the feminist ethics of care Gilligan and Noddings built against a Western canon (Aristotle, Kant) that called women too emotional for morality. Wonder Woman's killing of Maxwell Lord to free Superman is re-read as the care-ethical beach case: saving your own child over a stranger's is not a failure of impartiality, and in his Gotham-versus-Themyscira invasion thought experiment she would defend Gotham because its people are vulnerable non-combatants, not because a utilitarian ledger favors it.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
machiavelli-virtu.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Argues Tony is at times a practitioner of The Prince and ignores Machiavelli at his peril. He plays the fox with Junior (the figurehead-boss arrangement of 'Meadowlands', the Augustus 'never ate alone' lesson of 'Pax Soprana') and his virtù makes Richie's coup unsellable, but with Richie he seeks love instead of fear, and with Ralph he violates the advice to abstain from subjects' property and women (taking over Pie-O-My and sleeping with his goomah), which ends in Ralph's murder. Fortune, Machiavelli's river, runs through Chris's double-parked car, Janice shooting Richie, Gigi's death on the pishtoon, and the Season Four economic downturn Tony failed to build dykes against.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
machiavelli-virtu.title: Poker and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Hahn reads Doyle Brunson's Super System — 'I go into a Poker game with the idea of completely destroying it' — as applied Machiavelli: The Prince's fox and lion become the bluffer and the bully chip leader, 'better to be feared than loved' justifies cutting even old friend Sailor Roberts's throat at the table, and swift decisive attack (Tex Barch stomped out of the 2005 WSOP) avoids sowing the seeds of vengeance. Fortune rules half our events — the river card that fills an opponent's inside straight — so virtù means building dikes against the flood, as Cesare Borgia failed to do when his papal patron died. Sun Tzu's 'when able, seem to be unable' supplies the same disguise of strength in poker and in war.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
machiavelli-virtu.title: “Livin’ and Dyin’ in Three-Quarter Time”
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Randall Auxier uses Buffett's catalog to think about fortune and fate, reading Buffett's bold career moves (walking out on Nashville for the beach, later annexing it via 'It's Five o'Clock Somewhere') through Machiavelli's advice to marry Fortuna and master her tricks with virtù. Against Aristotle's demanding answer that only aretē, moral excellence, defends happiness against bad luck, he takes Vico's middle path: natural causes, moral causes, and the occasions of fortune are gathered under providence, so Buffett's seaplane crash ('God, Buddha, St. Christopher, my guardian angel... luck, and the United States Navy water-survival training') shows any fate can be turned to good ends for others. Sorting Buffett's songs into places, times, meetings, sentiments, and thoughts — the key sentiment being the wistful — the chapter lands on contentment as gratitude: being 'livin' and dyin' in three-quarter time.'

machiavelli-virtu.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
machiavelli-virtu.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Littmann tests The Prince against the real bosses behind the show - Nucky Johnson, Capone, Luciano, Rothstein, Torrio - and argues that Prohibition-era history bears out Machiavelli's rules of power. Seizing new opportunities pays (Nucky turning Atlantic City into the World's Playground, Colosimo gunned down for refusing bootlegging, Luciano eliminating Masseria and Maranzano to modernize the Mafia), and harming a rival without crushing him invites revenge (Nucky's fatal leniency toward Jimmy, Maranzano leaving the scarred Luciano alive). A ruler needs good arms, must tailor appearances to each audience (Capone's banquet murder of Anselmi and Scalise, Nucky's respectability and staged generosity), and above all must avoid hatred - the downfall of Nucky, Capone, and Luciano, and of the needlessly arrogant Rothstein, shot over a gambling debt he could easily have paid.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
machiavelli-virtu.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Ted Brown and Christie Maloyed read Ender's Game as a Cold War debate between realism and liberalism: Hobbes' state of nature grounds Graff's survival-at-all-costs logic, and Machiavelli's counsel on seizing opportunities and keeping power by force when persuasion fails shapes Peter's insight that 'the right words can change the world.' The human-Formic war becomes a Prisoner's Dilemma neither species can escape without communication, and Ender's postwar practice of governing his colony 'by persuasion rather than fiat' delivers the book's verdict that the power to persuade can outlast the power to destroy.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
machiavelli-virtu.title: 7. Machiavelli Advises the Governor
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Littmann reads The Prince as advice the Governor already follows: kidnapping Andrea and Michonne, butchering the National Guard survivors for supplies, murdering his way to leadership of Martinez's camp, and maintaining a benevolent image through Woodbury picnics and gladiatorial walker-fights while ruling through fear at the gates. Machiavelli's maxims - crush rather than lightly injure, be feared but not hated, be lion and fox, adapt to the times - explain both the Governor's successes and his failures, such as massacring his own army outside the prison or letting rage over Penny's death cost him his eye. The chapter ends by grading Machiavelli largely right about dirty hands and military power but blind to resources like medicine and fuel, and draws the real lesson: shape the political environment so Machiavellian strategies stop paying.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
machiavelli-virtu.title: 12. Margaery for Queen!
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Jones asks whether Margaery - who grooms Tommen, admits she was 'good at seeming good,' and may count as an abuser despite Westeros's norms - could still have been the best queen in the Seven Kingdoms. Against the prosecution's portrait of a cold egoist, he argues her charity to Flea Bottom's children shows a queen is good by what she does rather than why she did it, so selfish ambition welded to shrewdness can genuinely serve the common good. Comparing her with Ramsay (cruelty that provokes revolt) and Ned (benevolence without calculation that gets him killed), the chapter draws an implicitly Machiavellian conclusion - the people's best bet is hunger for power joined to the cunning to keep them onside - while doubting that cultural relativism can fully excuse her treatment of Tommen.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
machiavelli-virtu.title: 2 Power and Politics
machiavelli-virtu.relation: The chapter traces politics from the classical ethics-fused view (Aristotle's Politics, where politics exists for the sake of the good life yet also supplies one of the first justifications of patriarchy and the public/private split) to the Machiavelli-Hobbes break where politics becomes simply the possession and exercise of power, adopting Bertrand Russell's claim that power is the fundamental concept of social science. It then builds the book's central instrument, a Weber-derived analysis of nine power bases (money, knowledge/technology/information, religion, morality, authority, charisma, size/solidarity, violence, status), contrasting the Marxian reading - money as ultimately determinative, the ruling ideas of each age as the ideas of the ruling class, religion as the opium of the people, the state as a committee for managing bourgeois affairs - with the liberal-Weberian reading in which no single base is decisive. It closes by showing that Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau and Marx divide over the morality of egalitarianism (Popper's Marx moved by moral impulse versus Locke's possessive individualism), and that power is domain-specific, inert until used, skill-dependent and always relative.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
machiavelli-virtu.title: 9 T’Challa’s Machiavellian Methods
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Drake and Lloyd argue the comic-book T'Challa of 'Panther's Rage' is classically Machiavellian in a way the film's earnest king is not: he rules through fear and strategic violence against Killmonger's uprising, cultivates the appearance of The Prince's five qualities (mercy, faith, honesty, humanity, religion), and exploits Wakandan religion — letting subjects believe the Black Panther is divine, never doffing the sacred garb even when swimming with Monica — as an instrument for preserving power. Advisers like Taku ask whether T'Challa differs from Killmonger, and the chapter concludes that, sharing Machiavelli's low view of human nature, T'Challa never considers democracy and keeps his people quiescent through a divinity he knows is performance.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
machiavelli-virtu.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Ted Henry Brown and Christie Maloyed stage the Enderverse as the international-relations debate between Hobbesian realism — Graff's 'if one of us has to be destroyed...' and the human-bugger Prisoner's Dilemma where the absence of communication forces mutual defection and war — and liberal institutionalism, which Peter's Locke and Valentine's Demosthenes argue out on Earth's nets. Machiavelli supplies Peter's theory of power: fortune opens the moment, virtù seizes it with 'the right words at the right time,' and force must back persuasion when belief fades, so that 'influence is power' and governing by persuasion beats fiat.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
machiavelli-virtu.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: David Hahn argues that Spira's Yevon religion is exactly what Machiavelli and Nietzsche warned against: hope for the Calm and a Sin-free future makes Spirans otherworldly and passive, forbidding machina, revering self-sacrificing Summoner martyrs, and blaming themselves for Sin, just as just-war Christianity left Machiavelli's princes passive and dependent on mercenaries, paralleled by Seymour and Kinoc standing idle at Operation Mi'ihen. Nietzsche's slave revolt in morality explains Yevon's sanctification of meekness and death, while Machiavelli's account of religion as a political instrument, from Numa to Scipio's oath, explains why the lie of Yevon held Spira together, and why its collapse may bring either Nietzschean rebirth or Machiavellian chaos.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
machiavelli-virtu.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Marcus Schulzke reads the War of the Five Kings through The Prince: who wins the Iron Throne is decided by virtu - skill adapted to shifting circumstances - against fortuna, and morality is no guide, since actions are good or bad only as they gain or hold power. The failures illustrate the lessons: Viserys's arrogance binds him to the wrong allies, Robert's emotions make him capricious, Joffrey makes himself hated instead of feared, Ned's uncompromising honesty and trust in Littlefinger destroy him, and Robb's dependency on Walder Frey's auxiliary forces proves fatal. The true Machiavellians are the mask-wearers - Littlefinger, Arya, Jon as lion-and-fox - and above all Tyrion, who wins the Blackwater by planning, and Daenerys, who builds her own army from freed slaves and so makes her own luck.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
machiavelli-virtu.title: Notes
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Argues Frank's rise is a genuinely successful illustration of The Prince: Machiavelli's advice to be prepared not to be virtuous shows in his lying (feigning loyalty to Walker while engineering his impeachment, promising Russo the governorship), his strategic murders of Russo and Zoe, his audacity in making his own luck ('turn over the table'), and his cultivation of a pious family-man image while privately spitting on the crucifix. The chapter also lets Machiavelli criticize Frank — revenge on Tusk (better to pamper or crush), Claire's fruitless generosity at CWI, alliances with the stronger, and being feared to the point of being hated, which costs him Sharp, Remy and Claire. Finally it tests The Prince against modern democracy — party discipline, sex-scandal politics, Obama's donated Nobel money, birther smears — concluding that since Machiavellians will always adapt to whatever system exists, citizens must reward results and stop judging by image.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
machiavelli-virtu.title: Notes
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Cooper reads Frank's one prayer - kneeling to pray 'to myself, for myself' - as a self-love he calls autoeroticism, built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness as power. Like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, Frank's atheism removes divine punishment from the moral equation, so the murders of Peter Russo and Zoe Barnes incur only human risk, while his feigned piety at the Peachoid girl's vigil, broken promises to Tusk, and 'cruelty well used' toward Russo exemplify Machiavellian virtu taming fortuna. Against this the chapter sets Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's remorse after betraying Freddy ('Do you think I'm a hypocrite?') shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man against the Augustinian freedom of self-giving love.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
machiavelli-virtu.title: Notes
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Littmann tests Frank against The Prince and largely confirms the 'Machiavellian' label: his lies (playing the loyal confidant while engineering Walker's fall), his strategic murders of Russo and Zoe, his preference for weaker allies, and his manufactured piety and father stories all enact Machiavelli's advice that a prince must learn 'not to be good' while seeming merciful, faithful, and religious. But the debts run both ways: Claire's vindictive 'let's make him suffer' offends Machiavelli's pamper-or-crush rule, and modern democratic image politics (Obama donating his Nobel money, the Obama-as-Muslim smear) outperforms The Prince where voters punish fear and reward a generosity Machiavelli thought ruinous. The moral is not despair but vigilance: since Underwoods will always rise, citizens must reward genuine results rather than respond to images.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
machiavelli-virtu.title: Notes
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Fallis walks through the education-reform arc — leaking Blythe's draft, gutting collective bargaining ('I revised the parameters of my promise'), framing Rasmussen in the speakership coup, the staged brick incident, and goading Spinella into felony assault — to show Frank follows Machiavelli's counsel to be 'other than good.' Yet Frank fails at Machiavelli's how and why: he never cultivates the appearance of integrity (Blythe, Feng, and Vasquez refuse to deal with a known liar), he inspires hatred as well as fear, and he seeks power for its own sake rather than the stability of the state, which makes the BBC's Francis Urquhart the superior Machiavellian. Even the revisionist readings of The Prince — Benner's irony, Rousseau's claim that Machiavelli was exposing princes' methods like an investigative reporter, Dietz's deliberate-sabotage thesis — would not rescue Frank, since he bungles the techniques regardless of their intent.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
machiavelli-virtu.title: Notes
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Analyzes Frank's kneeling 'I pray to myself, for myself' as an ethics of autoeroticism built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness-as-power: like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, removing God from the equation makes the murders of Zoe and Russo cost only human, never eternal, judgment. The chapter details three exercises of Machiavellian virtu-feigned piety at the Peachoid vigil, fox-like promise-breaking with Tusk, and 'cruelty well-used' toward Russo-before closing on Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's betrayal of Freddy, met with a flash of remorse, shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
machiavelli-virtu.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Argues that a motorcycle club is a Machiavellian regime in miniature: Jax's Season 3 fake betrayal of the club to Stahl—actually a set-up that shortens the crew's prison time and delivers both Stahl and Jimmy O to death—shows the prince's union of lion and fox in service of the club rather than himself. J.T. figures as a founder overcome by fortuna ('each savage event was a catalyst for the next... blood was every color'), lacking the virtu to impose his vision, while Clay wields deceit and force for mere egoism that Machiavelli would refuse the name of glory. Zobelle's self-description as a 'Machiavellian fool' flooding Charming with drugs, and Jax's admission that 'you can't sit in this chair without being a savage,' frame the chapter's question of whether manipulation and violence can serve a genuine common good.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
machiavelli-virtu.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Si Sheppard reads the comic through Realist state-formation theory: Shane's leadership rests on borrowed prestige and dies with him, West Central Prison collapses into anarchy because Rick never establishes a monopoly on legitimate force—letting Tyreese's vigilante murder pass—nor any institution beyond his personal authority, while the Governor's Woodbury thrives on fear, arenas, and bread-and-circuses. Citing Machiavelli's prince who is feared rather than loved, Weber's definition of the state, and Bismarck's unifying wars, he argues the prison loses the 'second anarchy' rivalry with Woodbury for want of scouting, sabotage, coalition-building, or any command structure that survives Rick's absences. Rick's confession that he would kill everyone in the Alexandria Safe Zone to keep Lori safe is post-moral Realism, yet he was 'a bad founding father' who only finally learns to build an army instead of relying on himself.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
machiavelli-virtu.title: Wilt Versus Russell
machiavelli-virtu.relation: O'Connor frames the boyhood 'Wilt or Russell?' debate as a version of Aristotle's Politics puzzle that a man outside community is 'either a beast or a god': is dominator Wilt a basketball beast or a divine king, and is executive-team-player Russell the higher human ideal? He links Wilt's romantic individualism to Rousseau ('J.-J.') and Emerson's genius awaiting 'practical power,' and Aristotle's discussion of the natural king to the coaching dilemma of whether to make a gifted player dominate or blend. He ends by rejecting Machiavelli's 'realist' dismissal of ideals, insisting the Russellite ideal of teamwork can be higher even when domination wins more.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Raymond Belliotti reads the twenty-year Olympic career of Italian sprinter Pietro Mennea, 'The Southern Arrow,' through Machiavelli's concept of virtu, the excellence relevant to one's function that lets a person master Fortuna. He distinguishes Machiavelli's military, political, civic, moral, and artistic virtu (using the Agathocles passage and the Life of Castruccio Castracani) and argues Mennea's physical prowess, mental toughness, and turning of anti-southern prejudice into motivation exemplify athletic virtu. Machiavelli would scoff at Olympic ideals of peace and brotherhood but relish the fierce international competition and the discipline of sport that Mennea embodied through his 1980 Moscow gold and later political career.

machiavelli-virtu.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
machiavelli-virtu.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
machiavelli-virtu.relation: Mahon asks whether Ride with the Devil endorses the proverb that all's fair in love and war, locating the film's moral core in its outsiders—the German immigrant Jake, the freed slave Holt, and the young widow Sue Lee. Against Sunzi's undiscriminating claim that warfare is the art of deceit, he argues the film sides with Machiavelli's Discourses distinction between honorable ruses of war and dishonorable perfidy: the bushwhackers' wearing of Union blue and Jake's lies are ruses, but the Lawrence massacre and refusing to ambush women under a truce mark limits Jake will not cross. In love, Sue Lee's shift from romantic lying to 'now is the truth' shows honesty is finally required, so all is not fair.

machiavelli-ends.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
machiavelli-ends.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Argues Tony is at times a practitioner of The Prince and ignores Machiavelli at his peril. He plays the fox with Junior (the figurehead-boss arrangement of 'Meadowlands', the Augustus 'never ate alone' lesson of 'Pax Soprana') and his virtù makes Richie's coup unsellable, but with Richie he seeks love instead of fear, and with Ralph he violates the advice to abstain from subjects' property and women (taking over Pie-O-My and sleeping with his goomah), which ends in Ralph's murder. Fortune, Machiavelli's river, runs through Chris's double-parked car, Janice shooting Richie, Gigi's death on the pishtoon, and the Season Four economic downturn Tony failed to build dykes against.

machiavelli-ends.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
machiavelli-ends.title: Palpatine’s Legacy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Decker reconstructs Palpatine's career as a case study in how democracies die: using Aristotle's definition of tyranny and the precedent of Pisistratus and Julius Caesar, he shows Palpatine manufacturing the Separatist threat so the Senate grants him emergency powers - a twist on Machiavelli's loved-versus-feared dictum in which playing the reluctant democrat is itself the means to absolute rule. The Attack of the Clones debate between Anakin ('Someone wise' should make people agree) and Padme becomes a clash between Leo Strauss's philosopher-king ideal of rule by the virtuous few and John Dewey's conception of democracy as a way of life trusting the intelligence of common people, with Rousseau's social contract framing the stakes. The chapter concludes that democratic ends require democratic means and that unaccountable 'watchers' - Straussian statesmen or Anakins - are exactly the path to Empire.

machiavelli-ends.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
machiavelli-ends.title: Look On My Works, Ye Mighty
machiavelli-ends.relation: Ozymandias, Watchmen's smartest human vigilante, kills three million New Yorkers with a staged alien attack to avert nuclear war, and Skoble walks through the question the novel forces: can the end justify the means? The heroes' darkest hour is their acquiescence in his scheme - only Rorschach rejects the utilitarian reasoning ('Never compromise... Evil must be punished') and is killed by Dr. Manhattan to keep the secret. Skoble leaves us asking whether Ozymandias is a misunderstood savior or has 'become a monster', and whether our recoil at his act is moral clarity or weakness.

machiavelli-ends.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
machiavelli-ends.title: Poker and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Hahn reads Doyle Brunson's Super System — 'I go into a Poker game with the idea of completely destroying it' — as applied Machiavelli: The Prince's fox and lion become the bluffer and the bully chip leader, 'better to be feared than loved' justifies cutting even old friend Sailor Roberts's throat at the table, and swift decisive attack (Tex Barch stomped out of the 2005 WSOP) avoids sowing the seeds of vengeance. Fortune rules half our events — the river card that fills an opponent's inside straight — so virtù means building dikes against the flood, as Cesare Borgia failed to do when his papal patron died. Sun Tzu's 'when able, seem to be unable' supplies the same disguise of strength in poker and in war.

machiavelli-ends.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
machiavelli-ends.title: Doing Things in Private
machiavelli-ends.relation: Skoble asks exactly what Jeff does wrong in Rear Window and whether his illicit snooping can generate genuine duties. Against a purely consequentialist verdict ('it all worked out okay'), he argues that knowledge creates conditional obligations - given what he has seen of Thorwald, Jeff's intervention is obligatory rather than supererogatory, by 'ought implies can' - and he weighs autonomy-respecting limits on intervening in Miss Lonelyhearts' despair. He then analyzes privacy as a moral right grounded in reciprocal legitimate expectations, concluding that Jeff violated no such right since everything he watched was on public display, so the ends-justify-the-means charge mostly dissolves.

machiavelli-ends.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
machiavelli-ends.title: The Future
machiavelli-ends.relation: Dinello reads the New Caprica occupation as an Iraq allegory interpreted through Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth: occupation is violence personified (Cavil's 'saving them from damnation'), psychological violence colonizes minds (Leoben's manipulation of Starbuck, Jammer's recruitment into the New Caprica Police), and Tyrol's 'throw your body on the gears' strike speech channels Savio, Marx's seizing the means of production, and Marcuse on technology's repression. Fanon's thesis that anticolonial violence is a cleansing, liberating force is dramatized in Tigh's 'blood for blood,' the Temple massacre that recruits a thousand fighters, and Duck's suicide bombing — with Sartre's preface endorsing killing the oppressor and the ends-justify-means dispute between Tigh and Tyrol. The insurgency wins by not losing, as in Algeria and Vietnam, and the show is subversive because it makes viewers sympathize with the occupied.

machiavelli-ends.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
machiavelli-ends.title: Damned If You Do, and Damned If You Don’t
machiavelli-ends.relation: Bryan McHenry asks whether manipulating religious belief for political ends is ever moral, using Adama's motivational lie about Earth, Roslin's Pythia-driven 'dying leader' campaign (compared with George W. Bush's faith-based politics), and the Cylons' evangelical monotheism aimed at scaring Baltar into conversion. Machiavelli's Prince licenses rulers who use a religion they do not share, and the chapter judges Adama's hope-based use of the Earth myth and Roslin's uniting religiosity as essentially moral while the Cylons wield faith as a coercive weapon. Madison's Enlightenment demand that religion be directed by reason and conviction rather than force supplies the standard the fear-based Cylon conversion of Baltar fails.

machiavelli-ends.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
machiavelli-ends.title: The Bronze Dragonflight Invisible Leadership
machiavelli-ends.relation: Moses Wolfenstein applies The Prince to guild leadership: the infamous Dives Onyxia wipe ('50 DKP minus!') shows why being feared beats being loved — players flooded to join and even requested his abusive raid calls — so long as fear never curdles into hatred, while PUGs and battlegrounds replay Machiavelli's warning that mercenary troops are 'disunited, ambitious, without discipline, disloyal.' Against this he sets Laozi's Daodejing verse 17, where the best rulers are scarcely known by their subjects and the people credit themselves — embodied by the hidden bronze dragonflight and Chromie, and by the back-channel guild officer who invisibly paves the road to victory.

machiavelli-ends.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
machiavelli-ends.title: The (Single) Garden Path
machiavelli-ends.relation: Compares Herbert's three eugenics programs: the Bene Gesserit's centuries-long Kwisatz Haderach breeding scheme (explicitly modeled on the communal breeding of the guardians in Plato's Republic, undone when Jessica bears Paul a generation early and he escapes their control), Leto II's Golden Path breeding for Siona's invisibility to prescience, and the Tleilaxu axolotl-tank immortality that collapses when their Face Dancers out-mimic them. Each program is weighed ethically—Leto as the 'ultimate consequentialist' whose species-saving tyranny invokes Mill's utilitarianism and Machiavelli's ends-justify-the-means, the Sisterhood as shifting toward Kantian duties against using persons as mere means. Herbert's lesson: 'the most dangerous of all creations is a rigid code of ethics,' whether aimed at a single person, a single result, or a single agenda.

machiavelli-ends.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
machiavelli-ends.title: I’ve Got No Strings . .
machiavelli-ends.relation: Richard Greene asks whether it was practically rational for Dexter to trust Lumen rather than kill her, to help her revenge-kill the Fowler ring, and to train her as a killer. The good outcomes do not help - Masuka's strip-club windfall shows luck is not rationality, and Socrates' Apology argument that corrupters risk harm from those they corrupt, together with Dexter's prior disaster in training Miguel, means the consequences were not foreseeably good. Kantian tests fail too - no one could will a universal law of killing, and killing violates the victim's autonomy and humanity as an end in itself - as do decision theory and instrumentality theories, so no account of practical rationality vindicates Dexter's choices, suggesting instead that the emotionless 'wooden boy' is beginning to become a real one.

machiavelli-ends.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
machiavelli-ends.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Solves the 'riddle' of Gus by showing his empire runs on corporate instrumental rationality: the careful, emotion-disciplined Los Pollos CEO launders meth through legitimate business, treats chemists as replaceable parts (the Gale plan), and exacts revenge on the cartel in 'Salud' by drinking his own poisoned tequila. The chapter defines this as the critical theorists' amoral means-end reason - Kant's hypothetical imperative without the categorical - making Gus a sociopath who violates the injunction to treat persons as ends, and reads his cartel war through Machiavelli and Hobbes's power-first picture of the state. Gus's Two-Face-like corpse reveals the split between the rage-driven avenger of Max and the respectable mask, foreshadowing what Walt becomes.

machiavelli-ends.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
machiavelli-ends.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Si Sheppard grades The Walking Dead's three settlements by political Realism: the Governor's Woodbury - cohesive, feared rather than loved, feeding his people arena spectacle to keep them from turning on him - beats Rick's West Central Prison, which never becomes a state at all. Rick lets Tyreese's vigilante murder pass, ruling as a first-among-equals with no institutions, no constitution, and no monopoly of legitimate force in Weber's sense, then covertly guns down Thomas and Dexter while hiding behind his cop credibility - 'it's me or you' reasoning indistinguishable from Shane's. Realism cares about power, not morality, so Rick's flaw is not cruelty but the absence of institution-building: he was never a bad father, just a bad founding father, who only becomes a Realist after Alexandria falls.

machiavelli-ends.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
machiavelli-ends.title: Psych and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Robert Arp's introduction argues Psych is perfect for philosophy because Henry's games train observation and inference exactly as philosophers hone them, while Shawn's ruse shows how clever people abuse those powers to deceive - quoting Machiavelli's line that one who deceives will always find those who allow themselves to be deceived. It sets up the book's recurring ethical question about lying: lies for the liar's profit (Shawn avoiding jail in the pilot), paternalistic lies for the hearer's own good (Henry telling seven-year-old Shawn he 'blacked out' about his mother's death), and lies to benefit many (promising a terrorist freedom to find his bomb). Since Shawn's lies solve cases and save lives, the introduction suggests they may not be so bad in the end, though it admits wishing he would just come clean as a talented honest detective.

machiavelli-ends.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
machiavelli-ends.title: Psych and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: The Bock brothers ask whether Shawn's fake-psychic lie is morally permissible, testing it against Augustine's and Kant's absolute prohibitions on lying, Nietzsche's claim that all language is metaphorical (the 'Lights, Camera . . . Homicidio' acting-as-lying scene), and Machiavelli's ends-justify-the-means deception from The Prince. Using Sissela Bok's three-question test they contrast justified police undercover work - Juliet infiltrating the sorority in 'Scary Sherry' and the roller derby team in 'Talk Derby to Me' - with Shawn's ruse, which fails because it protects Shawn's own interests rather than others. They end by weighing Sorensen's bald-faced lies (Shawn's 'I know you know I'm not telling the truth') and conclude Chief Vick's genuine belief shows these are real, indefensible lies.

machiavelli-ends.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
machiavelli-ends.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Littmann tests The Prince against the real bosses behind the show - Nucky Johnson, Capone, Luciano, Rothstein, Torrio - and argues that Prohibition-era history bears out Machiavelli's rules of power. Seizing new opportunities pays (Nucky turning Atlantic City into the World's Playground, Colosimo gunned down for refusing bootlegging, Luciano eliminating Masseria and Maranzano to modernize the Mafia), and harming a rival without crushing him invites revenge (Nucky's fatal leniency toward Jimmy, Maranzano leaving the scarred Luciano alive). A ruler needs good arms, must tailor appearances to each audience (Capone's banquet murder of Anselmi and Scalise, Nucky's respectability and staged generosity), and above all must avoid hatred - the downfall of Nucky, Capone, and Luciano, and of the needlessly arrogant Rothstein, shot over a gambling debt he could easily have paid.

machiavelli-ends.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
machiavelli-ends.title: The Devil and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: James Edwin Mahon dismantles the 'sympathy for the Devil' puzzle by testing three accounts of diabolical evil: Machiavelli's prince ('learn how not to be virtuous') shows self-interest is mere amoral Realpolitik; Schopenhauer's malice and Schadenfreude ('injure all people as far as you can') are still self-interested pleasure; and only Kant's 'diabolical will' - doing evil because it is evil, Paradise Lost's 'Evil, be thou my good' - truly captures the Devil, though Kant deemed it impossible for humans. Hence nobody actually likes the Devil; people like the intelligence, charm, and underdog status of the characters who play him in The Devil's Advocate and Angel Heart.

machiavelli-ends.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
machiavelli-ends.title: Homeland and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Christophe Porot and Charles Taliaferro ask whether Homeland's pervasive hypocrisy and deceit can be justified, starting from Walden's cover-up of the drone strike and Brody's heroic persona hiding a terrorist plot. Machiavelli's Prince supplies the case that political relationships with allies (Saul's 'Us and Them' speech to Carrie) require hypocrisy, while the Smith-inspired 'honest politicking' model - trading openly on self-interest, as with Carrie blackmailing al Sahrani - fails because politics should secure the public good, though la Rochefoucauld's 'homage vice pays virtue' explains Saul extorting the judge into doing right. Weighing Kant's unconditional duty not to lie (Carrie's fatal lie to Lynne Reed) against consequentialism, the chapter lands on the Walzer Dirty Hands view: some acts stay wrong yet necessary, and honest agents accept the guilt.

machiavelli-ends.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
machiavelli-ends.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Cherry uses Vee's season-two grooming of Taystee, Poussey, Nicky, Cindy, and Crazy Eyes to test philosophers' accounts of manipulation (covert influence, non-rational persuasion, targeting weaknesses, misleading truthfully). She shows Vee's skill is not virtue, since manipulation threatens autonomy by imposing a will the victim would not endorse (Kantian personhood denied) and employs dishonesty, predatoriness, disrespect, and laziness, with Machiavellian ends. The defense she prescribes is Socratic: reject purely emotional persuasion like the sophists' flattery, and live the examined life by checking premises and motives before being played.

machiavelli-ends.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
machiavelli-ends.title: 7. Machiavelli Advises the Governor
machiavelli-ends.relation: Littmann reads The Prince as advice the Governor already follows: kidnapping Andrea and Michonne, butchering the National Guard survivors for supplies, murdering his way to leadership of Martinez's camp, and maintaining a benevolent image through Woodbury picnics and gladiatorial walker-fights while ruling through fear at the gates. Machiavelli's maxims - crush rather than lightly injure, be feared but not hated, be lion and fox, adapt to the times - explain both the Governor's successes and his failures, such as massacring his own army outside the prison or letting rage over Penny's death cost him his eye. The chapter ends by grading Machiavelli largely right about dirty hands and military power but blind to resources like medicine and fuel, and draws the real lesson: shape the political environment so Machiavellian strategies stop paying.

machiavelli-ends.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
machiavelli-ends.title: 20. The Good and the Gracious
machiavelli-ends.relation: Olson and Taliaferro read manners as the story's moral barometer: the genuine, effusive compliments exchanged by Westley and Inigo atop the Cliffs of Insanity, and Fezzik's sporting wrestling, express care and connection, while Humperdinck's and Rugen's courtly politeness is camouflage for torture, murder, and war. Against Machiavelli's instrumental use of courtesy in The Prince, they recruit Plato's sophrosyne as 'good form' inseparable from justice, wisdom, and courage, and Confucian li as etiquette that instructs and steadies us toward virtue, with Hobbes's 'small morals' marking the hollow version; they add that manners also police class, from Buttercup's 'Farm Boy' to reality TV and the financiers of the Great Recession who used the correct fork.

machiavelli-ends.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
machiavelli-ends.title: 27. Was the Red Wedding Massacre a Good Thing
machiavelli-ends.relation: Van der Deijl takes Tywin's line to Tyrion - 'explain to me why it is more noble to kill ten thousand men in battle than a dozen at dinner' - as a serious consequentialist challenge about the Red Wedding. Working through utilitarianism, prioritarianism, and dirty-hands cases like Hiroshima and shooting down a hijacked plane, he concedes the massacre could have been justified had breaking Guest Right and killing 3,500 brought peace at minimal cost; but the consequences fail - Joffrey and Roose Bolton keep power, the institution of guest right erodes, and Tywin's real motive was family power rather than the greater good - so the massacre fails even the consequentialist test, and Tywin is a power-hungry conspirator, not Machiavelli's prince.

machiavelli-ends.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
machiavelli-ends.title: 9. Send The Good Place to the Bad Place
machiavelli-ends.relation: Sheldon argues the Season One twist makes the show itself a moral paradox: a series about ethics that lies to its audience for thirteen episodes, breaking the informal contract it built through 'truth in fiction'. Through Chidi's red-cowboy-boots lie and Eleanor's plot to murder Janet, 'The Eternal Shriek' stages Kant's absolute prohibition on lying against Eleanor's Machiavellian ends-justify-means reasoning, with confession portrayed as the only release from escalating deception.
