The chapter ends with Eleanor citing Jonathan Dancy's moral particularism to get Chidi to lie his way through the Bad Place, leaving viewers to decide whether the show's own deception is justified by the ethical conversation it forces.

machiavelli-ends.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
machiavelli-ends.title: 22. The Mad Titan and the Mother of Dragons
machiavelli-ends.relation: Pairs Thanos with Game of Thrones' Daenerys as twin Machiavellian utopians acting on 'the ends justify the means' (quoting The Prince and the Discourses): Daenerys burns King's Landing to 'break the wheel,' Thanos snaps half of life away 'at random, dispassionate, fair to rich and poor alike' as 'a small price to pay for salvation.' It roots both villains in cruel childhoods and a nature-versus-nurture question (with historical analogies to Hitler and Stalin), and in messiah complexes built on improbable success — 'Dread it, run from it, destiny arrives all the same' — while noting the key inversion: Thanos refuses to rule and dies content watching the sunrise, whereas the breaker of chains claims a new throne.

machiavelli-ends.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
machiavelli-ends.title: Damned If You Do, and Damned If You Don’t
machiavelli-ends.relation: McHenry reads the re-imagined series as a holy-war allegory in which both sides weaponize religion, then asks whether that manipulation is ever moral. Adama's lie about Earth is Machiavellian statecraft (with Foucault's point that privileged knowledge holds power), yet defended as serving the greater good, while Roslin's Pythia-based campaign contrasts with Bush's faith-based fear politics. The Cylons emerge as evangelical fundamentalists whose conversion of Baltar through inner Number Six runs on fear, exactly what Madison's case for religious liberty forbids. The chapter concludes the show's own gods have sided with the Colonials.

machiavelli-ends.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
machiavelli-ends.title: 9 T’Challa’s Machiavellian Methods
machiavelli-ends.relation: Drake and Lloyd argue the comic-book T'Challa of 'Panther's Rage' is classically Machiavellian in a way the film's earnest king is not: he rules through fear and strategic violence against Killmonger's uprising, cultivates the appearance of The Prince's five qualities (mercy, faith, honesty, humanity, religion), and exploits Wakandan religion — letting subjects believe the Black Panther is divine, never doffing the sacred garb even when swimming with Monica — as an instrument for preserving power. Advisers like Taku ask whether T'Challa differs from Killmonger, and the chapter concludes that, sharing Machiavelli's low view of human nature, T'Challa never considers democracy and keeps his people quiescent through a divinity he knows is performance.

machiavelli-ends.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
machiavelli-ends.title: The (Single) Garden Path
machiavelli-ends.relation: Argues Herbert populates Dune with three long-running eugenics programs, each with a different ethical stance: the Bene Gesserit's Kwisatz Haderach breeding scheme (whose communal guardian-breeding deliberately recalls Socrates' Kallipolis in the Republic), Leto II's Golden Path, and the Bene Tleilax's axolotl-tank genetic design for immortality. It reads the chastened Sisterhood of the later novels as moving from consequentialist to Kantian, deontological ground ('never seek to create a human being in any one image'), frames Leto II as the ultimate utilitarian whose species-saving end allegedly justifies Machiavellian means (with Siona's objection that he had no right), and shows the Tleilaxu destroyed by their own monomaniacal religious code. Conclusion: 'the most dangerous of all creations is a rigid code of ethics.'

machiavelli-ends.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
machiavelli-ends.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: David Hahn argues that Spira's Yevon religion is exactly what Machiavelli and Nietzsche warned against: hope for the Calm and a Sin-free future makes Spirans otherworldly and passive, forbidding machina, revering self-sacrificing Summoner martyrs, and blaming themselves for Sin, just as just-war Christianity left Machiavelli's princes passive and dependent on mercenaries, paralleled by Seymour and Kinoc standing idle at Operation Mi'ihen. Nietzsche's slave revolt in morality explains Yevon's sanctification of meekness and death, while Machiavelli's account of religion as a political instrument, from Numa to Scipio's oath, explains why the lie of Yevon held Spira together, and why its collapse may bring either Nietzschean rebirth or Machiavellian chaos.

machiavelli-ends.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
machiavelli-ends.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Marcus Schulzke reads the War of the Five Kings through The Prince: who wins the Iron Throne is decided by virtu - skill adapted to shifting circumstances - against fortuna, and morality is no guide, since actions are good or bad only as they gain or hold power. The failures illustrate the lessons: Viserys's arrogance binds him to the wrong allies, Robert's emotions make him capricious, Joffrey makes himself hated instead of feared, Ned's uncompromising honesty and trust in Littlefinger destroy him, and Robb's dependency on Walder Frey's auxiliary forces proves fatal. The true Machiavellians are the mask-wearers - Littlefinger, Arya, Jon as lion-and-fox - and above all Tyrion, who wins the Blackwater by planning, and Daenerys, who builds her own army from freed slaves and so makes her own luck.

machiavelli-ends.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
machiavelli-ends.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: David Hahn contends Ned died because of his honor, not for it. Hobbes explains why: words bind no one without fear of enforcement - Cersei ripping up Robert's will ('Is this meant to be your shield, Lord Stark?') exposes Ned's belief that allegiance alone secures the King's Justice - and the Iron Throne itself is a Leviathan, forged by Aegon's dragons ending the state of nature, whose force rather than justice holds the peace. Machiavelli supplies the indictment of Ned's idealism: 'we who presume to rule must do vile things for the good of the realm,' so Ned's refusal to assassinate Daenerys, his merciful warning to Cersei, and backing the rightful but war-prone Stannis over Renly cost him his head and plunged the realm into civil war; the security of the state demanded exiling or killing the Lannisters and crowning Renly.

machiavelli-ends.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
machiavelli-ends.title: 9. Send The Good Place to the Bad Place
machiavelli-ends.relation: Asks whether a show about ethics may lie to its audience for a whole season: the Season One twist breaks the viewer's implicit contract even though the show keeps its internal 'truth in fiction'. Through 'The Eternal Shriek' it stages the debate — Chidi's Kantian ban on lying (the red cowboy boots saga with Henry, ending in a confession that defeats Henry) against Eleanor's Machiavellian ends-justify-means plot to 'kill' Janet — and reads the show's cascade of confessions as its answer that truth-telling absolves. Eleanor citing Jonathan Dancy's moral particularism in 'Rhonda, Diana, Jake, and Trent' lets Chidi lie his way through Hell, leaving viewers to decide whether the twist's ethical education justifies the deception.

machiavelli-ends.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
machiavelli-ends.title: NOTES
machiavelli-ends.relation: First defines lying — distinguishing it from mere error (Angela believing Peter dead), from the Haitian's non-verbal memory-wipe deception, and from Hiro's silent staging of Ando's fake death — then tests moral theories against the show's liars. Kant's categorical imperative bans all lying but is abandoned when Sylar demands a friend's hiding place; utilitarianism vindicates Victoria Pratt's lie about the virus vial yet also licenses Linderman's .07% explosion and Plato's noble lie of the earthborn metals, which the chapter rejects. Machiavelli's advice that princes may lie to keep power is played out by 'President Sylar' in 'Five Years Gone,' and the chapter finally endorses Sissela Bok's presumption against lying — a public-reasoning procedure modeled by Bob Bishop and Mohinder before Monica's virus injection.

machiavelli-ends.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
machiavelli-ends.title: Notes
machiavelli-ends.relation: Argues Frank's rise is a genuinely successful illustration of The Prince: Machiavelli's advice to be prepared not to be virtuous shows in his lying (feigning loyalty to Walker while engineering his impeachment, promising Russo the governorship), his strategic murders of Russo and Zoe, his audacity in making his own luck ('turn over the table'), and his cultivation of a pious family-man image while privately spitting on the crucifix. The chapter also lets Machiavelli criticize Frank — revenge on Tusk (better to pamper or crush), Claire's fruitless generosity at CWI, alliances with the stronger, and being feared to the point of being hated, which costs him Sharp, Remy and Claire. Finally it tests The Prince against modern democracy — party discipline, sex-scandal politics, Obama's donated Nobel money, birther smears — concluding that since Machiavellians will always adapt to whatever system exists, citizens must reward results and stop judging by image.

machiavelli-ends.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
machiavelli-ends.title: Notes
machiavelli-ends.relation: Runs through everything Frank does for a single project — the education reform bill: leaking Blythe's draft, gutting collective bargaining after promising Spinella ('I revised the parameters of my promise'), the Rasmussen speakership coup he then 'exposes', the shipyard-for-base trade, and the staged brick incident and strike-breaking — to show he endorses being 'other than good'. It then argues Machiavelli would not be impressed: Frank fails to keep up the appearance of integrity (Blythe, Feng and Vasquez all stop trusting him), inspires hatred rather than fear alone, and seeks power purely for its own sake where Machiavelli wanted it for the state's stability and liberty — the BBC's Francis Urquhart, who read The Prince and serves England, is the better Machiavellian. The chapter closes by weighing ironic and exposé readings of The Prince (Benner's critique, Rousseau's view that Machiavelli was unmasking princes, Dietz's sabotaging-gift reading) and concludes Frank fails even on the technique, not just the morality.

machiavelli-ends.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
machiavelli-ends.title: Notes
machiavelli-ends.relation: Cooper reads Frank's one prayer - kneeling to pray 'to myself, for myself' - as a self-love he calls autoeroticism, built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness as power. Like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, Frank's atheism removes divine punishment from the moral equation, so the murders of Peter Russo and Zoe Barnes incur only human risk, while his feigned piety at the Peachoid girl's vigil, broken promises to Tusk, and 'cruelty well used' toward Russo exemplify Machiavellian virtu taming fortuna. Against this the chapter sets Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's remorse after betraying Freddy ('Do you think I'm a hypocrite?') shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man against the Augustinian freedom of self-giving love.

machiavelli-ends.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
machiavelli-ends.title: Notes
machiavelli-ends.relation: Littmann tests Frank against The Prince and largely confirms the 'Machiavellian' label: his lies (playing the loyal confidant while engineering Walker's fall), his strategic murders of Russo and Zoe, his preference for weaker allies, and his manufactured piety and father stories all enact Machiavelli's advice that a prince must learn 'not to be good' while seeming merciful, faithful, and religious. But the debts run both ways: Claire's vindictive 'let's make him suffer' offends Machiavelli's pamper-or-crush rule, and modern democratic image politics (Obama donating his Nobel money, the Obama-as-Muslim smear) outperforms The Prince where voters punish fear and reward a generosity Machiavelli thought ruinous. The moral is not despair but vigilance: since Underwoods will always rise, citizens must reward genuine results rather than respond to images.

machiavelli-ends.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
machiavelli-ends.title: Notes
machiavelli-ends.relation: Fallis walks through the education-reform arc — leaking Blythe's draft, gutting collective bargaining ('I revised the parameters of my promise'), framing Rasmussen in the speakership coup, the staged brick incident, and goading Spinella into felony assault — to show Frank follows Machiavelli's counsel to be 'other than good.' Yet Frank fails at Machiavelli's how and why: he never cultivates the appearance of integrity (Blythe, Feng, and Vasquez refuse to deal with a known liar), he inspires hatred as well as fear, and he seeks power for its own sake rather than the stability of the state, which makes the BBC's Francis Urquhart the superior Machiavellian. Even the revisionist readings of The Prince — Benner's irony, Rousseau's claim that Machiavelli was exposing princes' methods like an investigative reporter, Dietz's deliberate-sabotage thesis — would not rescue Frank, since he bungles the techniques regardless of their intent.

machiavelli-ends.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
machiavelli-ends.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Argues that a motorcycle club is a Machiavellian regime in miniature: Jax's Season 3 fake betrayal of the club to Stahl—actually a set-up that shortens the crew's prison time and delivers both Stahl and Jimmy O to death—shows the prince's union of lion and fox in service of the club rather than himself. J.T. figures as a founder overcome by fortuna ('each savage event was a catalyst for the next... blood was every color'), lacking the virtu to impose his vision, while Clay wields deceit and force for mere egoism that Machiavelli would refuse the name of glory. Zobelle's self-description as a 'Machiavellian fool' flooding Charming with drugs, and Jax's admission that 'you can't sit in this chair without being a savage,' frame the chapter's question of whether manipulation and violence can serve a genuine common good.

machiavelli-ends.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
machiavelli-ends.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Si Sheppard reads the comic through Realist state-formation theory: Shane's leadership rests on borrowed prestige and dies with him, West Central Prison collapses into anarchy because Rick never establishes a monopoly on legitimate force—letting Tyreese's vigilante murder pass—nor any institution beyond his personal authority, while the Governor's Woodbury thrives on fear, arenas, and bread-and-circuses. Citing Machiavelli's prince who is feared rather than loved, Weber's definition of the state, and Bismarck's unifying wars, he argues the prison loses the 'second anarchy' rivalry with Woodbury for want of scouting, sabotage, coalition-building, or any command structure that survives Rick's absences. Rick's confession that he would kill everyone in the Alexandria Safe Zone to keep Lori safe is post-moral Realism, yet he was 'a bad founding father' who only finally learns to build an army instead of relying on himself.

machiavelli-ends.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
machiavelli-ends.title: A Friend of Humanity
machiavelli-ends.relation: Vereb argues Geralt is at best a superficial Stoic: he lives by coin and contract, ignores Stoic justice and cosmopolitan concern, and chases neither wisdom nor the view that evildoers fit a rational Logos. Instead Geralt's refusal to choose between Stregobor's and Renfri's evils, his promise-keeping, and his protection of Ciri mark him as a Kantian who treats persons as ends and does good from duty even toward people he dislikes. Yennefer is the counterpoint, a Machiavellian fox who 'plays fair' never and uses mages as catapult fodder, while Jaskier embodies Kant's imperfect duties of benevolence and hope, completing what duty-only Geralt and egoist Yennefer each lack.

machiavelli-ends.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
machiavelli-ends.title: What Would Machiavelli Do
machiavelli-ends.relation: Reitsma treats the refereeless pickup game as a Lockean state of nature and asks how to beat the 'strategic ticky-tacker' who calls phantom fouls to win. He condemns first-strike cheating as wrong on Kantian grounds (the cheat 'makes an exception of himself') and by an ideal of Homeric athletic honor, then asks whether retaliatory ticky-tacking is justified. Reading Machiavelli's 'dirty hands' argument alongside Locke's claim that in a state of nature each person may punish transgressors, he concludes proportionate tit-for-tat cheating can make one a legitimate 'agent of justice' when no referee exists.

machiavelli-ends.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
machiavelli-ends.relation: Raymond Belliotti reads the twenty-year Olympic career of Italian sprinter Pietro Mennea, 'The Southern Arrow,' through Machiavelli's concept of virtu, the excellence relevant to one's function that lets a person master Fortuna. He distinguishes Machiavelli's military, political, civic, moral, and artistic virtu (using the Agathocles passage and the Life of Castruccio Castracani) and argues Mennea's physical prowess, mental toughness, and turning of anti-southern prejudice into motivation exemplify athletic virtu. Machiavelli would scoff at Olympic ideals of peace and brotherhood but relish the fierce international competition and the discipline of sport that Mennea embodied through his 1980 Moscow gold and later political career.

machiavelli-ends.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
machiavelli-ends.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
machiavelli-ends.relation: Mahon asks whether Ride with the Devil endorses the proverb that all's fair in love and war, locating the film's moral core in its outsiders—the German immigrant Jake, the freed slave Holt, and the young widow Sue Lee. Against Sunzi's undiscriminating claim that warfare is the art of deceit, he argues the film sides with Machiavelli's Discourses distinction between honorable ruses of war and dishonorable perfidy: the bushwhackers' wearing of Union blue and Jake's lies are ruses, but the Lawrence massacre and refusing to ambush women under a truce mark limits Jake will not cross. In love, Sue Lee's shift from romantic lying to 'now is the truth' shows honesty is finally required, so all is not fair.

moral-egoism.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
moral-egoism.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Argues that bracketing his crimes, Tony is an 'ethical manager': against Junior's vanity-driven blunders and Christopher's Scarface-style impulsiveness in 'Meadowlands', Tony shows stakeholder judgment - holding the line on business through Annalisa's sexual provocation in the Naples cave ('Commendatori'), defusing war with Carmine over the Esplanade ('Whitecaps'), and following Melfi's Eldercare advice to give Junior 'the illusion of being in control'. The chapter concedes Tony acts within an egoistic horizon of self, family and crew rather than universal principle, but finds real moral self-restraint in him, invoking Augustine's dictum that 'even robbers take care to maintain peace with their comrades' and Tony's own 'I dunno about morals, but I do got rules'.

moral-egoism.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
moral-egoism.title: “You Know . . . What They’re Up Against”
moral-egoism.relation: Dees finds moral ambiguity lurking in Star Wars' black-and-white universe: Han Solo's Hobbesian ethical egoism ('I take orders from just one person - me') is shown to be coherent and gradually transformed by friendship with Luke and Leia into commitment to a cause. Lando's betrayal of Han on Bespin is defended as a straightforward Mill-Bentham utilitarian choice by a responsible official, weighed against Bernard Williams's Jim-and-the-commandant integrity objection, which the author rejects as moral vanity. Count Dooku's apparent idealism is exposed as evil's tool, and Anakin's massacre of the Sand People is condemned as non-ambiguous barbarity via Kant's formula of humanity (and Hume on reason's role with the passions), leaving only late Vader as genuinely morally ambiguous.

moral-egoism.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
moral-egoism.title: The Problem for Spider-Man
moral-egoism.relation: Sets up the chapter's question through the Spider-Man film: after the promoter cheats him, Peter lets the armed robber go with the taunt "I missed the part where that's my problem," and the robber's escape gets Uncle Ben killed. The scene turns Uncle Ben's "with great power comes great responsibility" into the classic question "Why be moral?" — why not use superpowers for "great personal satisfaction," an egoist's super life, when no payoff for virtue is guaranteed.

moral-egoism.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
moral-egoism.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Laura Garcia assembles Narnian heroes: Jill, Eustace, and Puddleglum untying Rilian at likely lethal cost, Eustace hacking at the Sea Serpent, unarmed Shasta charging the lion to save Aravis, and Digory refusing the Witch's offer of the apple that could heal his dying mother. She asks whether egoist theories can explain such deeds and argues they cannot: Hobbes's disguised self-interest, Butler's and Paley's reward schemes, Hume's sympathy, and MacIntyre's identity-based interests all fall short. Only love of others for their own sake, and (for Jill and Digory) trust in Aslan's proven goodness, explains both the heroic choices and our admiration of them as supererogatory acts beyond the call of duty.

moral-egoism.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
moral-egoism.title: E Pluribus Unum
moral-egoism.relation: Auxier frames Hitchcock's Lifeboat against Garrett Hardin's 'lifeboat ethics' essay, arguing the lifeboat converts political questions into ethical ones by stranding the survivors outside law and politics ('We're on our own here. We can make our own law'). The survivors are ethical pluralists - Rittenhouse lives for money, Kovac for equality, Constance for fame, Joe for God, MacKenzie for care - and their clinging to private versions of the Good lets Nazi captain Willy, whose only principle is survival, manipulate them all. Using Maslow's hierarchy of needs, Auxier shows the boat descending to bare survival, yet argues the mob killing of Willy when he hoards water is moral outrage rather than survival-driven, and that the final rescue scene replays the opening dispute with nobody having grown - a vindication of pluralistic democracy capable of unified action.

moral-egoism.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
moral-egoism.title: Why Be Moral
moral-egoism.relation: Sanders uses Bruno Anthony's 'criss-cross' murder-swap proposal to Guy Haines in Strangers on a Train to pose the classic question 'Why be moral?' to the charming amoralist. He tests three answers: Kant's categorical imperative fails because Bruno's egoist maxim ('remove obstacles to your happiness') can apparently be universalized; Hobbesian contractarian 'morality pays' fails because Bruno free-rides on others' restraint; and the Rachels/Nelson/Thomas psychological-health answer assumes rather than proves that Bruno should care about comparable suffering. A thought experiment comparing the moral life with the Bruno-state from an impartial standpoint leads to Aristotle's eudaimonia: morality is constitutive of human flourishing, so Bruno enjoys only a counterfeit happiness.

moral-egoism.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
moral-egoism.title: Once I Was the Student, Now I Am the Master
moral-egoism.relation: Johannes Bulhof reads 'Me and My Uncle' — the Dead's most-performed song, though hardly a fan favorite — as a parable against rational self-interest. The nephew learned everything from his uncle: how to cheat at cards, steal, and shoot first, so he rationally guns down the cowboys, takes the gold, and leaves his uncle's 'dead ass there by the side of the road' — the student out-mastering the teacher. Framing the song with Thrasymachus's Republic I claim that the unjust always profit (and his own students' admission they would cheat if they could get away with it), then with Hobbes's state of nature where equality, contested goods, and anticipatory striking make everyone enemies — even family — Bulhof argues the song's drunken lesson is that rational self-interest is communally irrational.

moral-egoism.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
moral-egoism.title: Transformers and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Michaud reads the Autobot-Decepticon war as a contest of ethical systems: Optimus's fair fighting, his refusal to ignore human casualties, and Bumblebee's friendship with the inferior Spike instantiate Kant's categorical imperative and the treatment of rational beings as ends in themselves. The Decepticons run through the egoist tradition - Hobbes's psychological egoism from Leviathan, Starscream's self-defeating normative egoism, and Megatron as Ayn Rand's rational egoist taunting 'You still fight for the weak; that is why you lose' - leaving the reader to choose between Kant's world of peaceful obligation and Rand's world of power where, like Starscream, you die alone.

moral-egoism.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
moral-egoism.title: Is Fencing a Dishonorable Art
moral-egoism.relation: Michaud argues that fencing is the loneliest and most egoistic martial art: alone on the strip, you seek to understand your opponent only in order to deceive them through disengages and parry-feints. He maps the bout onto Hobbes: psychological egoism, the dueling ground as a state of nature of 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short', and the referee as the Leviathan whose rules keep the bloodshed out while licensing normative egoism inside them. Testing defenses from Rand, Friedman and Carr's business 'rules of the game', he concludes that fencing kept its soldier's anything-goes ethos after the lethal stakes vanished, making it a 'dishonorable' art: a Hobbesian feast of solitude, egoism and deception.

moral-egoism.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
moral-egoism.title: There’s Something Here that’s as Strong as Life
moral-egoism.relation: Argues Rush's lyrics cohere as libertarianism: Rand's rational self-interest in 'Anthem' and 'Something for Nothing,' Nozick's Wilt Chamberlain argument and Hayek's knowledge problem behind '2112' and 'The Trees,' Mill's 'experiments in living' in 'Witch Hunt' and 'Nobody's Hero,' and market-enabled tolerance and cosmopolitanism in 'Heresy,' 'Territories,' and 'Tai Shan.' Like Cygnus resolving Apollo and Dionysus, libertarianism takes the best of left and right, with individualism the constant running through Peart's career.

moral-egoism.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
moral-egoism.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Pits act utilitarianism against existentialism to ask whether moral rules change at life's end: briefly cooking meth can maximize happiness (family provision against limited street harm), while a long career cannot, and utilitarians are trapped by the limits of their own foresight. Walt is read as the existentialist converting mortality into meaning - money, power, and masculinity in a godless world - while Skyler mostly calculates like a utilitarian (white lies to Marie, Ted's accounting), Hank mixes both codes, and Marie's kleptomania marks her an egoist until she defends Walt's right to choose his own death at the intervention. A marathon-runner metaphor lands the thesis: to be a utilitarian in life's early miles is itself an existential decision, and the last mile is when we 'wake up' like Walt.

moral-egoism.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
moral-egoism.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Grants that Larry looks like the Romantic ideal of the authentic self, Rousseau's amour de soi turned into candid self-expression, but argues his authenticity collapses into egoism: petty commandments about chicken skewers and beach jackets, one-strike firings like the toupee-wearing chef, and ceaseless sincerity tests. Through Sartre's categories Larry is bad faith in both directions, the 'cowardly bastard': he denies transcendence ('I can't help it') and hides behind fabricated personas, faking concern over a sick dog and exaggerating his Jewishness to the kidney consortium. Charles Taylor's The Ethics of Authenticity supplies the verdict that self-creation needs 'pre-existing horizons of significance,' so Larry's 'anything goes' authenticity is really moral relativism and justified self-interest, with Ayn Rand's virtue of selfishness as its unwanted philosophical ally. The chapter closes that only a relational authenticity, like the African ideal of ubuntu, could redeem Larry, and he lacks it, so 'maybe authenticity isn't for everyone.'

moral-egoism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
moral-egoism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: John Wilkins treats Caesar, who spares the neighbor he has beaten, as a Kantian exemplar whose reason lets him adopt the Categorical Imperative, contrasting him with the rational egoism of the film's human keepers and executives. He argues the film trades on the outdated Great Chain of Being, which Darwinian tree thinking dissolves: with no higher or lower species, only branching homologies, human nature must be continuous with ape nature, and talk of innate species essences must allow for statistical variation and dispositions rather than determination. Caesar's morality also needs more than reason, namely the primate dispositions of deference and empathy scaffolded by his human family, though Buck's instant moral conversion after enhancement shows the film is ambivalent about whether scaffolding alone explains it.

moral-egoism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
moral-egoism.title: Psych and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: The Bock brothers ask whether Shawn's fake-psychic lie is morally permissible, testing it against Augustine's and Kant's absolute prohibitions on lying, Nietzsche's claim that all language is metaphorical (the 'Lights, Camera . . . Homicidio' acting-as-lying scene), and Machiavelli's ends-justify-the-means deception from The Prince. Using Sissela Bok's three-question test they contrast justified police undercover work - Juliet infiltrating the sorority in 'Scary Sherry' and the roller derby team in 'Talk Derby to Me' - with Shawn's ruse, which fails because it protects Shawn's own interests rather than others. They end by weighing Sorensen's bald-faced lies (Shawn's 'I know you know I'm not telling the truth') and conclude Chief Vick's genuine belief shows these are real, indefensible lies.

moral-egoism.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
moral-egoism.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: The Azevedos read Plato's Republic Book I as a manual for professionalism: Socrates argues the practitioner - doctor, ruler, lawyer - serves the patient, citizen, and client rather than himself, while Thrasymachus's cynicism that injustice pays and people only seem just is embodied by Eli Gold ('I lie for a living') and by stunt lawyers Nancy Crozier, Patti Nyholm, Louis Canning, and the secretive Jonas Stern. Alicia answers with Aristotle's virtue ethics: professionalism as a cluster virtue cultivated through habituated action, hitting the mean and doing the right thing at the right time for the right reasons. Saint Alicia shows how costly being good all the time is, yet the chapter sides with her striving for virtue over Thrasymachus's goldbrick glory.

moral-egoism.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
moral-egoism.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Fitzpatrick uses the social contract tradition to explain Prohibition-era Atlantic City. Hobbes's state of nature fits the gang warfare left where no Leviathan is strong enough to enforce federal law against Nucky; Locke's fits a night-watchman government overreaching into Prohibition and thereby breaking the contract, as with Nucky's illegitimate protection 'taxes'; Rousseau's noble savage corrupted by commercial society fits the Klan's pleasure in cruelty and innocent Tommy set against scheming adults. Ethical egoism frames Nucky's framing of Hans Schroeder, consequentialism the Temperance Union's cost-benefit failure, and deontology Margaret's lying campaign speech, while Marx's and Mill's view that human nature is malleable explains the season-spanning transformation of Nucky from half-gangster into 'a gangster and a half.'

moral-egoism.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
moral-egoism.title: Futurama and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Pless asks whether Bender is responsible for his misdeeds given that MomCorp designed him to be an alcoholic kleptomaniac (revealed through Bender Vision in 'Mother's Day') and Planet Express regularly orders him into morally dirty work. Against Asimov's utilitarian Three Laws - embodied by the servile, selfless Robot 1-X of 'Obsoletely Fabulous' - Futurama's 'robot subjectivism' makes every robot a self-interested agent, and Bender's autonomy is proven by his refusal of Mom's 'kill all humans' order and by his fear of punishment in Robot Hell ('Hell Is Other Robots'), which also shows the show's universe is not morally relativist. Because Bender can rewrite his own code - his unprogrammed friendship with Fry, the adoption scam that turns heartfelt in 'The Cyber House Rules' - he sits on the same sliding scale of moral agency as humans, so if Bender can break his programming, we have no excuse for not exercising our own free will.

moral-egoism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
moral-egoism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: The chapter argues Barney is best understood as a committed ethical egoist, distinguishing egoism from egotism, immoralism, and moral skepticism through the Playbook's Scuba Diver scam. Ainsworth rejects psychological egoism (Joey's view in Friends) using evolution and apparent counterexamples like Marshall's Christmas Eve deliveries, then uses Glaucon's ring of Gyges from the Republic to ask whether anyone would resist injustice with guaranteed impunity. The friendship objection is dissolved via Aristotle's 'a friend is another self': once friends are included in the ego, saving Marshall's relationship or rushing to Ted's hospital bed counts as self-interest, constrained like chess by absolute rules such as the Bro Code's Article 150.

moral-egoism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
moral-egoism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Trip McCrossin takes Grant's 'they'll just have to evolve, too' as addressed to the audience and asks whether human behavior, not meteors, could cause our extinction, using Malcolm's toolkit: self-organizing life on fitness landscapes, the Red Queen arms race you must run to stay in place, and Gambler's Ruin - once things go bad they cluster and go to hell together. The deepest lens is the Tragedy of the Commons: like herders each adding a sheep to a shared pasture, we do what is best for ourselves without concern for the common good, and the films chart ever-failing 'fences' - the paddock, the coastline, the Navy, the Marines - until pteranodons simply fly off Isla Sorna. Since ours is self-destruction (we run as fast as we can, but really from ourselves), the real fence, he concludes, is daring ourselves to collective restraint.

moral-egoism.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
moral-egoism.title: The Devil and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Magus Peter Gilmore, High Priest of the Church of Satan, reads pop culture's turn to villains - Loki outshining Thor, Ledger's Joker, Hellboy, Man of Steel's killing Superman - as the mainstream finally arriving at the Satanist party, since LaVeyans always used Satan as a symbol of self-deification ('I-theist') and carnal pride. He answers Pitkänen that Satanism needs no 'higher knowledge' and cannot include theists, and he answers Jones by citing the Satanic Bible chapter 'INDULGENCE... NOT COMPULSION': LaVey taught self-controlled indulgence and rational self-interest, not reckless abandon, and Epicurean moderation is no basis for dismissing him.

moral-egoism.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
moral-egoism.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Biondi argues the 'counter-cultural capitalist' is no paradox: Jobs succeeded not as a Gordon Gekko-style greedy capitalist but through the creative individualism of the cognitive counter-culture—the garage techno-geeks—who pursued their own vision rather than the bottom line. She traces the greedy-capitalist stereotype to Glaucon's Ring-of-Gyges challenge in Plato's Republic (people act justly only from fear of punishment), Hobbes's restless desire for power after power, and Marx and Engels's picture of alienated wage slavery under capitalism, with Rawls as the toleration-only-if-redistributed alternative. Jobs's hippie exterior (drugs, fruitarianism, Zen) masked an entrepreneur who, in Rand's 'creative mind' mold, put a ding in the universe through products like the iPad instead of philanthropy.

moral-egoism.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
moral-egoism.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Salvino casts Jobs as a billionaire egoist-visionary in the lineage of Adam Smith's insight that an entrepreneur's self-interest, not good intentions, best satisfies people's wants, Emerson's self-reliance, and Rand's virtues of independence and integrity—comparing Jobs to Howard Roark while noting his intuition was 'un-Randianly' unreasoned. Through Schumpeterian creative destruction (the automobile killing the horse-and-carriage; Wozniak's Apple I that HP rejected) and Deming's quality-first management, he explains Jobs's 'faster horse' contempt for market research, then rebuts the three standard ethical complaints—Foxconn labor conditions, his harsh verbal lashings, and his refusal to join the Giving Pledge—arguing Jobs did more good making the iPad than philanthropy ever could.

moral-egoism.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
moral-egoism.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Cohen retells the DOJ ebook case—Amazon's $9.99 Kindle pricing, Eddy Cue's agency-model deals with the five publishers, the most-favored-nation clause, Jobs's warning email to James Murdoch, and Judge Cote's conspiracy ruling—to ask whether Jobs and other businessmen live and work to serve consumers or themselves. He argues antitrust law encodes the altruist-utilitarian demand that producers sacrifice their own goals to consumer welfare, and defends the Randian alternative ('your life belongs to you') on which Jobs, Cue, and the publishers were entitled to pursue their own happiness through their work, so readers inspired by Jobs's 'find what you love' Stanford challenge should reject the ethics behind antitrust.

moral-egoism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
moral-egoism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Karavitis fabricates a recovered 'Dracula's Journal' in which the Count retells Stoker's plot as rational self-interest: he owes no one anything, Lucy 'came to me of her own free will,' Van Helsing's crew are a 'craven collective' spouting 'from each according to his ability,' and only objective reality - not their subjective feelings - counts. He claims a fundamental right to pursue his own happiness, casting himself as the thinking individual crushed by proletarian herd morality. An editor's framing email makes the point explicit: Rand-style egoism could justify even Dracula, a 'manual for vampires' set against Marx's collectivism.

moral-egoism.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
moral-egoism.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Greg Littmann systematically compares the Gang's values - wealth, attention, bad-assery ('Project Badass'), sexual conquest, relentless competition, revenge, pride in cheating, and callousness toward even friends and family - with the values Homer's Iliad and Odyssey celebrate, showing Achilles and Odysseus behave like the Gang: sacking cities, taking women as war trophies like Briseis, boasting of deception (the Trojan Horse), and rigging the funeral games. The real difference is scope: the heroes honor bonds of loyalty to comrades, family, and their own communities where the Gang is loyal to no one, and moderns extend concern further still. Yet our morals fail the same way when people are far enough removed - we tolerate homelessness, prison rape, sweatshop goods, and national glory-seeking - so the chapter pleads for the universal moral principles Greek moral philosophy first sought against Homeric values.

moral-egoism.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
moral-egoism.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Jason Iuliano reads the Gang's 'no restrictions' motto as egoistic hedonism in the tradition of Aristippus of Cyrene: pleasure alone is intrinsically good, and specifically present, bodily, personal pleasure - exactly how Mac defends his fifty-pound weight gain and the pair's decision to smoke crack. The doctrine is shown in action through the Gang's treatment of Rickety Cricket, used as a mere instrument while his life is ruined without a flicker of guilt, and through get-rich-quick schemes from the impulse-bought boat to running for comptroller purely for the bribe. Robert Nozick's Experience Machine then shows why hedonism fails - we want to actually do things, be a certain kind of person, and touch reality, not float as an 'indeterminate blob' - and Mill's paradox of hedonism explains the Gang's misery: pursuing pleasure directly is precisely what drives it away.

moral-egoism.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
moral-egoism.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Robert Arp's gallery matches each Gang vice - dishonesty, egoism, selfishness, greed, pettiness, ignorance, laziness - to real-life scumbags from Nixon, Stephen Glass, and Janet Cooke to Charles Ponzi, Bernie Madoff, Crassus, the Empress Dowager Cixi, Imelda Marcos, and the Darwin Awards, and it opens with the chapter's philosophical spine: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Book II of Plato's Republic, which predicts that even an upstanding person with the power to act unseen would seduce, steal, and murder - exactly the question the Gang's mostly unpunished antics keep staging. Against the ethical egoist's argument that because everyone is self-interested everyone should be (Vanderbilt's 'the public be damned'), the chapter deploys the is-ought point - children are naturally selfish without therefore deserving to be - alongside mothers, Mother Teresa, and 9/11 first responders, concluding that egoism is at most an admixture in every action, with Lord of the Flies as the reductio of universal egoism.

moral-egoism.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
moral-egoism.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Greene reconstructs the Prisoner's Dilemma with Pennsatucky and Vee in separate interrogation rooms, then maps a variant onto 'Thirsty Bird': whatever Alex does, Piper is better off testifying against Kubra, yet mutual silence was the group-rational outcome the two pact on the van ride. Alex defects anyway, leaving Piper with perjury and no leniency, and Greene argues Piper should have done the 'rational' thing, since Balik's revenge is only a threat while extra time in Litchfield is a certain harm and Alex has always been willing to screw her. The episode shows why honor among the self-interested fails without trust.

moral-egoism.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
moral-egoism.title: 3. Schumer’s Selfishness
moral-egoism.relation: Weighs psychological egoism, the thesis that every action is ultimately self-interested, against apparent altruism through Schumer's cluelessly selfish characters: the 'Cancer Excuse' sketch where Amy exploits Tig Notaro's diagnosis, God's dismay at her in 'Herpes Scare', and Emily Middleton guilt-tripping her mother into an Ecuador trip in Snatched. Arp deploys Adam Smith's Chinese-earthquake passage from The Theory of Moral Sentiments and Rachels's Lincoln piglets story before rejecting the argument for ethical egoism on is-ought and coherence grounds, concluding Schumer's selfish jerks are comic negative examples of how not to live.

moral-egoism.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
moral-egoism.title: 16. He’s Ethickle Rick!!!
moral-egoism.relation: The chapter reads the Galactic Federation as Hobbes's Sovereign: Earth covenants in for security and gets an interplanetary TSA, pill-currency debt, and the surveillance droid Conroy, while the Citadel of Ricks tours Hobbes's three commonwealths in 'The Ricklantis Mixup', aristocratic Council, brief democracy, and Evil Morty's monarchy, where the Sovereign's rules cannot by definition be unjust. Against this, Rick embodies Hobbes's psychological egoism ('the object to every man is his own pleasure'), hiding his motives in the Riq IV hostage gambit and the Szechuan-sauce confession. Yet the chapter argues Rick's egoism is oddly ethical: in an infinite multiverse resources are not scarce, so refusing to surrender freedom to any Sovereign and competing for everything is the right way to live, with 'A Rickle in Time' and the self-sacrifice of 'The Wedding Squanchers' as its tested limits.

moral-egoism.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
moral-egoism.title: 18. What Makes Rick Tick
moral-egoism.relation: Surveying Rick's values area by area, a many-worlds multiverse, atheism ('There is no God, Summer'), scientism, egoistic ethics, hatred of all government, and rap as today's Romanticism, the chapter rejects absurdism, existentialism, nihilism, and even Max Stirner's individualist anarchism, which it says fits the Citadel of Ricks rather than the loner Rick. Its thesis is that Rick is an Ayn Rand Objectivist: Rand's ideal man of reason, independence, and rejection of altruism, collectivism, and mysticism, with Jerry as the pity-parasite anti-ideal exposed in 'The Whirly Dirly Conspiracy'. It warns that infinite choice risks the paradox of hedonism, pointing to Rick's half-hearted suicide machine after Unity, and ends that only chosen constructive goals, perhaps a kinder Rick, could save him, if some other universe didn't already have that Rick.

moral-egoism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
moral-egoism.title: 3. Confronting Grief in the Post-Snap World
moral-egoism.relation: Benjamin Carpenter applies Judith Butler's idea of grievability from Precarious Life and Frames of War to Endgame: lives matter insofar as they can be mourned, and Thanos renders his billions of victims ungrievable by scale, turning deaths into statistics beside white stone monuments Scott finds his own name on. Most Avengers turn away (Tony retreats, Thor kills Thanos and sinks into depression, Clint goes on a murderous rampage), but Natasha stays at her post, keeping agency and hope alive, which is what lets Scott find her and the team reassemble. Her willing self-sacrifice on Vormir makes her the moral opposite of Thanos, 'the ultimate egoist' who wraps genocide in the language of balance and kills only others, and the chapter asks why Tony's funeral gets a long communal mourning while Natasha is mostly forgotten.

moral-egoism.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
moral-egoism.title: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the ADAM
moral-egoism.relation: Rose argues BioShock is not a cheap strawman of Ayn Rand but a use of her own philosophy-through-fiction method (Atlas Shrugged as the hidden utopia Rapture continues) to show what happens when an ideologue divides reason from emotion. Ryan, unlike the flawless John Galt, is a flawed human destroyed by his refusal to question and by sentiment (killed by the son he cannot shoot), while Fontaine wins by manipulating feelings and Tenenbaum's motherly attachment to the Little Sisters becomes her salvation. Drawing on Antonio Damasio's point that emotion filters options for practical reasoning, the chapter reads the save-or-harvest dilemma as proof that moral choices must include emotional response, concluding Randians should celebrate a game that warns against being blinded by ideology rather than against Objectivism itself.

moral-egoism.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
moral-egoism.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Greg Littmann asks what sort of life is worth living by holding Final Fantasy protagonists and FFXI Online players up to three standards. Hobbes's egoism and defense of absolute monarchy condemn the altruistic, authority-defying heroes (AVALANCHE, the rebels of FFII and FFVI) while partly approving the gil-grubbing, rule-breaking FFXI player; Mill's utilitarianism praises the world-saving heroes but condemns grinding down beastmen and rates most gaming a lower pleasure; Aristotle's function argument and golden mean find heroes like Yuna immoderately self-sacrificial yet credit ordinary FFXI adventurers with genuinely virtuous moderation, helping others while keeping their own interests in view.

moral-egoism.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
moral-egoism.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Greg Littmann asks who should rule Westeros and answers with Hobbes's Leviathan: people act only from self-interest ('we are all Lord Littlefinger under the skin') and fight for gain, safety, and glory - the mountain clans, Robert's preemptive strike on Daenerys, Drogo's wars for pride - so without a sovereign life is a war of all against all, and only an absolute ruler makes oath-keeping self-interested. Mapping Hobbes's own civil war (the Stuarts onto the Targaryens), he argues that even Varys is right to serve 'the realm' and peace by betraying Ned, and that loyalty rightly transfers from Aerys to Robert to Joffrey because protection, not lineage or justice, is the point of the sovereign. He then criticizes Hobbes: Ned and Jon show people really do die for principle, and Mad King Aerys's overcentralized power left rebellion as the only remedy - the War of the Five Kings shows civil war's horror must be weighed against appeals to honor.

moral-egoism.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
moral-egoism.title: Notes
moral-egoism.relation: Hackett contrasts Frank's ethical egoism - acting like an invisible Ring of Gyges wearer who pushes Zoe in front of a train and kills Peter once they cannot be controlled - with Beauvoir's existentialist ethics, in which consciousness is a 'nothing' whose freedom is real only when it wills and sustains the freedom of others. Peter's drunken enslavement and Zoe's freely chosen deal with Frank illustrate the ambiguity of a freedom that is still causally situated, and Frank's Season 3 miscalculations with Jackie, Remy, and Claire show egoism's inability to weigh others' self-interest. Claire's sympathy for Michael Corrigan and her final walkout dramatize her learning Beauvoir's lesson that promoting others' freedom is the condition of one's own, the difference between self-interest and existential freedom.

moral-egoism.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
moral-egoism.title: Notes
moral-egoism.relation: Contrasts Frank's ethical egoism with Beauvoir's existential ethics: Frank moves like an invisible Ring-of-Gyges wearer-murdering Zoe, reading everyone's self-interest-yet because he treats others purely as instruments his freedom is never 'prolonged through the freedom of others', and it fails in Season 3 when he miscalculates Jackie, Remy, and Claire. Claire's awakening through Michael Corrigan and her final walkout dramatize the Beauvoirian lesson that consciousness is freedom-as-nothingness whose values we remain collectively responsible for, not a license to will anything.

moral-egoism.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
moral-egoism.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Abigail Mann argues that the Games only look like 'survival of the fittest': Darwinian natural selection runs on chance ('one slip in thousands') and explicitly rejects the social-Darwinist use of 'unfit' against the poor, while Darwin's Descent of Man explains the tributes' kindness through kin and group selection and an evolved moral sense, so Katniss's unhesitating volunteering for Prim is kin selection and Thresh's conflicted sparing of her shows conscience overriding self-preservation. She tests this against Kant, for whom only duty-motivated action is truly moral, which would make Thresh's inner struggle the more moral act and Katniss's instinctive sacrifice mere animal impulse, and against the egoism of Hobbes (giving to a beggar to relieve one's own distress) and Dawkins's selfish gene, answering with Hume and psychologist Daniel Batson that genuine altruism is real. Her coda: Katniss ultimately rejects Gale not only because his firebomb killed Prim but because it was engineered to trap and kill altruists, and her closing habit of listing 'every act of goodness' is the trilogy's verdict that simple kindness is not an illusion.

moral-egoism.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
moral-egoism.title: Notes
moral-egoism.relation: Littmann treats Hobbes's Leviathan as a survival manual for post-apocalyptic Australia: the films illustrate his three causes of conflict — resource wars over guzzoline and water, preemptive strikes, and glory (the Nightrider's radio rant, Wez's stunts, the War Boys' 'Witness me!'). Bartertown's Thunderdome covenant and 'bust a deal, face the wheel' exemplify the social contract enforced by an absolute sovereign like Aunty Entity, while divided power (Master Blaster versus Aunty) courts civil war. He concludes Hobbes errs twice: Max's selfless acts (sparing Blaster, transfusing Furiosa) refute psychological egoism, and concentrating power in an Immortan Joe invites the very violence it fears — democracy removes leaders without blood.

moral-egoism.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
moral-egoism.title: The Universe Is Not Indifferent
moral-egoism.relation: White takes Bert Cooper's shelf display of Atlas Shrugged seriously and argues, against Cooper's claim that Don is 'completely self-interested,' that Don is the conventional image of the egoist rather than a Randian one: he is a second-hander whose stolen identity makes his life a lie, so Betty is married to a man who does not exist and only Anna Draper, who sees Dick Whitman, gives him psychological visibility. Objectivism's primacy of existence explains why every lie collides with facts (the train recognition, Adam's newspaper photo, the misplaced dog-tag parcel) and why Don's 'ruthlessness' and the 'indifferent universe' he complains of are products of his own vices, since what is, is. The chapter walks through Rand's virtues (rationality, independence, honesty, productiveness, pride, self-esteem grounded in objective self-appraisal, not the 'whore-child' label) to show Don sought spiritual gain through deceit and so placed his self-esteem against reality.

moral-egoism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
moral-egoism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
moral-egoism.relation: Explains what anarchism actually demands—rejection of external authority, voluntary association, and faith that people need no coercion to cooperate—and measures SAMCRO against it: the club's president, church votes, chain of command, and the impossibility of Jax negotiating an exit all betray Momma Anarchy. The individualist/collectivist debate inside anarchism maps onto J.T., who retreats to Nomad and Belfast when the collective disappoints his individualist ideal, versus Jax, whose commitment to family keeps him building the collective. Clay appears as the anti-anarchist 'stone-cold egoist' who rigs votes and kills suspected rats, and the chapter argues the experiment was doomed twice over: the founding Vietnam vets' military hierarchy, and the club's dependence on the capitalist society and state agencies (CIA RICO leverage) it rejects.

moral-egoism.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
moral-egoism.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
moral-egoism.relation: Uses 'Fun with Veal' (the boys' bedroom standoff over baby calves, the FDA renaming veal 'tortured baby cows', Stan's meat strike punished by 'vaginitus'), 'Whale Whores' (the Japanese hating dolphins until Stan's doctored Enola Gay photo swaps in a cow and chicken), and 'Pee' (researchers peeing on rhesus monkeys) to pose the line-drawing problem: why do we protect cute animals and slaughter yummy ones? Neither intelligence (pigs versus dogs), utility, age, nor cuteness survives scrutiny as a morally relevant criterion — if it did, Nurse Gollum or Timmy would lose standing. Singer's speciesism analogy and the utilitarian inclusion of all who can suffer are then applied: Cartman, who draws his moral circle around himself, is the honest ethical egoist, while Kyle and Butters' selective vegetarianism and the adults' meat-eating inconsistency are exactly what Singer's view condemns.

moral-egoism.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
moral-egoism.title: Notes
moral-egoism.relation: LaRocca argues Boba Fett is best understood as an amoralist - neither a moral relativist nor an ethical egoist, but someone who has withdrawn from moral judgment altogether - reading his terse 'As you wish' to Vader and his insuring of Han's survival purely for payment as evidence. Through Michael Walzer's account of the soldier's constrained choice and the 'good mercenary' debate, he asks whether mercenary violence (Blackwater, private military contractors) really differs morally from a conscript's or clone's. The upshot is that Fett's grayness between Empire and Rebellion exposes amoralism as a surprisingly central part of political and military life.

moral-egoism.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
moral-egoism.title: Notes
moral-egoism.relation: Begley and Biondi argue Ted is an ethical egoist in the Aristotelian-Randian sense: like Howard Roark of The Fountainhead (Ted's favorite book), he is a self-loving creator who loves his work, has a 'self-sufficient ego' immune to others' approval, and pursues long-range values, so his kindness and biscuits are rational self-interest, not selflessness. Against Hobbesian psychological egoism they distinguish genuine egoists from narcissists like Rupert and hedonists like Season 1 Jamie, defend Ted's divorce and the curse-reverse ceremony as only apparent sacrifices, and read his panic-attack therapy arc as the egoist's project of achieving inner wholeness.

moral-egoism.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
moral-egoism.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
moral-egoism.relation: Sanders reads Casino as a dramatization of ethical egoism, using the parasitic bond between Nicky Santoro and Ace Rothstein to ask whether an egoist who treats a friend as a mere instrument can have real friendship. He distinguishes 'maximizing' egoism (Nicky's ruinous take-everything drive, ending in his beating death) from a 'satisficing' egoism that restricts its own dispositions, arguing against Blum, Wilcox and an Aristotelian objection that only the maximizing version is truly incompatible with friendship. Aristotle's account of virtue and friendship supplies the standard the film's egoists fall short of.

moral-egoism.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
moral-egoism.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
moral-egoism.relation: Richard Greene analyzes The King of Comedy's Rupert Pupkin, who kidnaps talk-show host Jerry Landers to force his way onto TV and emerges a celebrity, calling this the 'Pupkin gambit' (harming others and oneself to secure an overwhelming personal payoff). Distinguishing internalist accounts of rationality (Plato's well-ordered soul, Kant's universalizable maxims) from an externalist one, Greene argues the gambit is irrational for a sane agent like the financier Michael Milken but rational for Pupkin via a Pascal's-wager structure: because Pupkin is delusional, even imagined success satisfies his desire, so the wager has huge upside and no real downside for him. He also invokes ethical egoism to show unethical acts can still be assessed for self-interested rationality.

moral-egoism.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
moral-egoism.title: 6. Hollow Man
moral-egoism.relation: Rowlands reads Hollow Man as a retelling of Plato's Ring of Gyges, posing 'why be moral?' once the invisible Kevin Bacon can act without sanction. He rejects the religious answer and Hobbesian social-contract theory (both reduce morality to prudence/fear of punishment and leave those outside the contract unprotected), and Hume's fellow-feeling as mere causal explanation not justification. He examines Kant's Categorical Imperative reducing immorality to inconsistency but argues it cannot answer 'why should I be moral,' concluding the choice is arational self-definition, closing with Nietzsche's 'become what you are' and the deed at the bottom of morality.

moral-egoism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
moral-egoism.title: 2. Twilight Zone as Philosophy 101
moral-egoism.relation: Marinucci uses The Twilight Zone as a triple introduction to philosophy, the show, and the handbook, arguing that philosophy is defined not by necessary-and-sufficient conditions but by Wittgensteinian family resemblance and salient features (curiosity, depth, abstraction, controversy) learned through MacIntyre-style immersion in a practice. She reads episodes as thought experiments: the amnesiac astronaut in 'Where Is Everybody?' and living-doll/robot episodes echo Plato's cave and Descartes's Method of Doubt about appearance versus reality, Nagel's 'what is it like to be a bat?' frames the problem of other minds, and episodes like 'The Shelter' and 'It's a Good Life' dramatize the tension between egoism and altruism and social conformity, including feminist gaslighting in 'Twenty Two.'

moral-egoism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
moral-egoism.title: 82. Planescape Torment as Philosophy Regret Can Change the Nature of a Man
moral-egoism.relation: Gubka argues that Planescape: Torment answers Ravel's riddle 'What can change the nature of a man?' with 'regret,' read through Aristotle's claim that virtues are developed by habitually practicing virtuous action. The Nameless One's regret over betraying Deionarra and over the innocents killed to sustain his immortality motivates redemptive acts—apologizing to Deionarra, surrendering his immortality—shifting his alignment toward Good. The chapter rebuts Hobbes's Psychological Egoism (TNO's genuinely altruistic self-sacrifice) and Spinoza's warning that regret only doubles misery, arguing instead that apt regret is a golden-mean virtue between remorselessness and self-condemnation whose very painfulness makes it motivating.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
hume-sentimentalism.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Argues Simple Subjectivism ('right for Tony') fails as a reading of the show because it cannot make sense of genuine moral disagreement - Carmela and Tony's adultery battle in 'Whitecaps', Agent Ciccerone versus Tony on extortion - nor ground outrage at the killings of Pussy and the sobbing Matt Bevilaqua. Humean ethical subjectivism, grounded in a common human nature and the sentiment of sympathy (with Berkeley's pin example to explain vice as perception-dependent), fares better: it lets us condemn Tony while explaining his warped sympathy - grieving Pie-O-My more than his human victims - as the product of a mob upbringing that Melfi's alexithymia diagnosis in 'House Arrest' targets.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
hume-sentimentalism.title: Vertigo and Epistemological Vertigo
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Flory reads Vertigo as an epistemological parable: Scottie's 'hardheaded Scot' method, collecting facts and deducing from universal principles, fails three times (the step-stool 'cure' for his acrophobia, explaining away Madeleine's 'possession' with the horse statue, forcing Judy up the bell tower for confirmation), delivering an implicit critique of Vienna Circle positivism in the manner of Carnap and Ayer. Against Scottie, the chapter mobilizes Kuhn's theory-laden facts, Aristotle's point that human conduct resists codification by exceptionless laws, and Hume's 'slave of the passions,' with Descartes's automata and Chalmers's philosophical zombies framing the problem of other minds. Midge, who knows people emotionally as well as factually, models the alternative: philosophers who fear 'epistemological vertigo' should give up epistemological training wheels and accept that minds, especially emotions, escape law-like rules.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
hume-sentimentalism.title: What of Philosophical Relevance Is there in Tarantino’s Films
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Bruce Russell argues that Tarantino's films share a pattern—a cruel man's life goes awry, violence erupts, and glimpses of compassion appear, like Mr. White comforting the shot Mr. Orange—but that fiction can raise philosophical questions without justifying general philosophical theses. He uses the Pulp Fiction exchange over the bullets that missed Jules and Vincent to raise Hume's problem of miracles (divine intervention versus a 'freak occurrence'), and applies the accounts of Mill, Gibbard, Hare and Hume to show that even Vincent's twisted code—balcony drops for foot massages, execution for keying a car—counts as having a morality. His conclusion: the films raise, but never answer in depth, the questions of what a miracle is and what it is to have a morality.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
hume-sentimentalism.title: An Amoral Universe
hume-sentimentalism.relation: James Spence rejects the DVD's profile of the Dogs as amoral psychopaths, arguing instead that Reservoir Dogs is filled with morality of just the kind Hume describes: natural sympathies plus artificial virtues constructed to manage conflicts among self-interested people. The tipping debate shows Mr. Pink reasoning with desert and fairness; Mr. Blonde's excuse that the clerks 'touched the alarm', White's 'Just cops' dehumanization, and the professional code restricting violence all display exactly the moral identity-management human psychology predicts. The film thus indirectly supports a third view on which morality grows from human nature and social interaction—criminals cannot actually think outside it.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
hume-sentimentalism.title: As Nasty as I Wanna Be
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Greene asks whether Maguire's Elphaba is really wicked, first clearing away her reputation (she adopts the 'Wicked Witch' name because 'it liberates you from convention,' echoing Glaucon's challenge in the Republic about the just person with an unjust reputation and vice versa) and then her nature (the midwife-biting birth, green skin, and witchcraft establish no vampire-like evil essence, since Glinda and Nor are good witches). Following Hume's view that morality is not found in the world but in our assessments, he treats wickedness as a matter of performing actions we judge evil, and weighs Elphaba's life under both headings: good intentions with horrific outcomes (the bees that kill the chef, the icicle that kills Manek, Sarima's family executions) and bad intentions with none (her two failed attempts on Madame Morrible). The verdict is deliberately suspended: if she is wicked at all, it can only be through the consequences of her actions.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
hume-sentimentalism.title: Ineptitude or Wickedness
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Durand begins from Hume's moral sentiments, the way first impressions (Miss Gulch, the farmer-actors, Professor Marvel) fix our judgments, and shows how Wicked delivers the new information that muddies them, relocating villainy from the green Witch to the green Wizard: an alien despot who scorns Oz's communal moral sense ('I am beyond that lisping childish recital of wrongs and rights'), stations an army of observation at the Witch's borders, and schemes to annex Munchkinland after Nessarose's fall. Marx's 'opium of the masses' frames the religion of Frex and Nessarose as the tool that first pacified, then repressed, the Munchkinlanders, while the Wizard's 'reunification' that is really annexation shows imperial ideology at work. Elphaba's own 'wickedness' comes out as habituated vengeance and an embraced reputation, so the title question is whether she is inept rather than evil, 'a bad witch, but not a wicked one,' and no worse than the Wizard who is merely 'a very bad wizard.'

hume-sentimentalism.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
hume-sentimentalism.title: Step Back
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Gallagher uses Monk's phobias to test Hume's claim that believing is itself a kind of feeling. The chapter asks whether a fear conflicting with a rational belief (Monk paralyzed by the possibly-on stove during a murder investigation) feels any different from a conflict between two fears ('Snakes trump heights' in 'Mr. Monk and the Very, Very Old Man') or two beliefs, and answers with Hume that beliefs are forceful-feeling representations — there is a 'what it's like' to believing the German shepherd is dangerous. On Hume's account the force of a belief comes from repetition of experience, which explains both why Monk's fears should fade (countless safely landed flights, millions of milk drinkers) and why they persist: his mind dwells repeatedly on the rare catastrophe, giving fearful representations extra force, as when his repeated experience that 'she's always cheating' makes him wrongly believe Brody's wife in 'Mr. Monk and the Bully.' The practical lesson is to step back and widen attention to all the possibilities, as Monk intermittently manages with the help of Natalie and Stottlemeyer.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
hume-sentimentalism.title: This Is the Age of Steel
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Littmann asks what a genuinely logical creature would do and grades the Cybermen against three accounts of reason: Hobbes's self-preservation and social contract, which the survival-focused Cybermen of 'The Tenth Planet' roughly satisfy but their later wars of conquest betray; Mill's utilitarianism, whose greatest-happiness principle, higher pleasures, liberty, and individuality condemn emotion-stripping, forced 'upgrades', and uniformity; and Hume's claim that reason alone motivates nothing, under which perfectly logical but emotionless Cybermen would simply do nothing at all. The upshot is that Cyberman 'logic' is incoherent — no theory of reason makes them rational.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
hume-sentimentalism.title: De-Deontologizing Dexter
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Sultan Ahmed argues Dexter is not really a Kantian deontologist: the urge to kill came first (the teenage animal killings, and his brother Rudy/Brian, who developed the same dark desire without Harry and rationalized it differently), and Harry's Code is a post-hoc rationalization built on top of that desire. Drawing on psychological research (Joshua Greene, Jonathan Haidt) that deontological judgment tends to be emotional rationalization rather than moral reasoning, he reads Dexter's killings as serving emotional needs - the need to control the helplessness of the shipping-container trauma and the Ernest Becker-style need to belong, seen in his bonding with Miguel, Rita, and the kids. Even Dexter's refusals to kill Ellen Wolf or the bound Tony Tucci are framed as feelings and standards, not a sense of moral duty.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
hume-sentimentalism.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones argues Ender's genius is empathy cashed out through game theory: from Plato's Laches on courage to Hume's account of sympathy, sizing up the enemy's thinking is the winning strategy, and Ender's love ('in that very moment I also love him') reframes conflicts with Peter and the buggers so they can end rather than merely be won. His one failure is never extending this empathy to Graff and Rackham, so he cannot see that his final battleroom rule-breaking - 'the enemy's gate is down' - is exactly the move the adults' larger game was designed to produce.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
hume-sentimentalism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: The chapter presents Barney as a Humean moral philosopher: reason is the slave of the passions, and norms like the Bro Code are invented conventions that evolve, Adam Smith's invisible-hand style, rather than being designed, revealed, or deduced. The Platinum Rule ('never, ever love thy neighbor') is grounded in Humean reciprocity: the eight-stage arc of attraction to fallout in Barney's Wendy the Waitress disaster, the Gerards' brunch tyranny, and Robin's romance with co-worker Curt shows the retaliation costs that make the norm a rational solution to coordination failures. Against the Golden Rule's painterly elegance, the anatomist's cautious observation of behavior explains why a norm banning neighborly love emerges even in a society of non-saints.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
hume-sentimentalism.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Thomas asks whether the Apple II, Macintosh, and iPod were great products regardless of sales or great because they sold, and answers that market success is real evidence of value: each sale is a buyer's revealed preference in a voluntary trade, a stronger test than critics or focus groups, which is why Jobs's flops (NeXT, the G4 Cube) were overdesigned, overpriced failures of utility rather than quality. Against Hume's quoted doctrine that reason is and ought only to be the slave of the passions (hunger strikers and Jobs's own vegan fanaticism defeat any basic-desire theory), he follows Rand and Philippa Foot in grounding value in objective human needs and capacities, so products designed for those needs—like the iPhone the Apple team built for themselves—could be expected to succeed.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
hume-sentimentalism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Altmann asks whether Dracula is blameworthy for his killings: John Martin Fischer's guidance control, Kant's reason-centered morality, and Hume's 'yay/boo' approval-and-disapproval theory (the heroes' anguish over Mina) all seem to condemn him, since the Count coolly plans feedings and uses his intellect for evil. But Nagel-style luck undermines all three accounts, because Dracula never consented to his transformation, lacks the conscience needed to even recognize right and wrong, and, like the holy-wafer-branded Mina, is fixed by God's rejection with no hope of redemption - so the chapter concludes Dracula is evil yet a victim of circumstance deserving no full blame.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
hume-sentimentalism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: McCrossin uses Locke's memory theory of personal identity - consciousness extending to past and future actions, with 'all the right and justice of reward and punishment' founded in it - to ask whether Dracula is a monster but still a person, illustrated by an imagined Quincey-Seward body swap where only the mind that remembers the deed deserves blame. Mina, midway between human and vampire and fearing for her own future personhood, supplies the empathy and pity ('that poor soul') that turn the crew's campaign into one of mercy - they weep and grant the Count a peaceful death - adding a sentimental middle ground that Locke's claim that morality is demonstrable like mathematics cannot account for.

hume-sentimentalism.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
hume-sentimentalism.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
hume-sentimentalism.relation: Ethan Chambers asks whether we should pardon the Gang, arguing with Hume that their vices have a 'causal story' as rigid as physical law: Charlie's glue-sniffing, racism, and inability to connect trace to a Christmas Day childhood of squalor and Uncle Jack's abuse; Mac was bullied as 'Ronnie the Rat' for trying to be good and never once saw virtue pay in Philadelphia; Dennis, shaped by Frank's cruel parenting, claims and shows he cannot feel feelings, so Humean sympathy - the key moral sense - is simply beyond his reach; and Frank's 'donkey brains' asylum childhood or outright insanity directly undermines his responsibility.
