moral-relativism.relation: Jonathan Bennett reads the chapter 16 raft episode as a clash between 'bad morality' and sympathy: Huck's conscience (slave-owning principles telling him to return Jim to Miss Watson) supplies all the reasons, while his sympathy for Jim is a bare, reasonless feeling that wins by weakness of will, so Huck does right while believing he does wrong. He contrasts Huck with Himmler, whose bad morality overrode his surviving sympathy, and Jonathan Edwards, whose Calvinist approval of eternal damnation left no sympathy to conflict. The lesson is that principles should be kept open to revision under pressure from sympathy, since one cannot declare one's own morality bad but should stay open to correction.

moral-relativism.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
moral-relativism.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
moral-relativism.relation: Davids tastes Classic Red Brand X, Starbucks Guatemala Antigua, and the $100/lb Panama Esmeralda, and asks whether one can prove any coffee universally 'better.' He concedes taste is relative—citing East Asian dislike of acidity and the European relish for fermented 'rio-y' and Robusta notes North Americans call rotten—but escapes relativism via Stanley Fish's notion of 'interpretive communities': a dominant global community of expert cuppers shares assumptions and vocabulary (acidity, mouthfeel, sweetness, clean flavor) that let them rank the three coffees consistently. Legitimate evaluation is thus grounded not in the coffee itself but in the shared code of a community of judgment.

moral-relativism.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
moral-relativism.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
moral-relativism.relation: Farennikova and Prinz ask what makes something fashionable, arguing through thought experiments (Calvin Klein jeans, khakis, Robinson Crusoe's leather jacket, the accidental thrift-store punk, Gang Green, the mod couple) that four conditions must hold: many people wear the look, recognized experts endorse it, wearers intend to conform, and they regard it as having aesthetic value. They distinguish being fashionable from being merely popular or 'cool,' show fashionability is relative to group and to time, and note fashion must change to serve its signaling purpose — the Amish are 'intentionally unfashionable.'

moral-relativism.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
moral-relativism.title: SERIAL KILLERS
moral-relativism.relation: Schmid examines Moors Murderer Ian Brady's book The Gates of Janus, arguing that Brady built a genuine philosophy of serial murder from Sade and Nietzsche rather than merely name-dropping them. He corrects popular caricatures of the ubermensch and will to power, then shows Brady grounds his self-account in moral relativism and reframes serial killing as fundamentally about 'power and the will to power.' Brady's admiration for Carl Panzram and his likeness to the self-justifying, punishment-transcending Sadean hero illustrate how Nietzschean and Sadean ideas actually shape a killer's self-understanding.

moral-relativism.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
moral-relativism.title: SERIAL KILLERS
moral-relativism.relation: Howard surveys serial killers from Liu Pengli and Locusta through Gilles de Rais, Bathory, Bichel, Panzram, and modern killers she interviewed (Bobby Joe Long, Shawcross, Milat, Birnie) to illustrate 'practical moral skepticism': the thesis that one can know right from wrong yet feel no motivation to be good. She distinguishes this from epistemic moral skepticism and argues that many killers, often privileged or unconstrained, understood moral codes but were driven instead by power, sadism, fatigue, or anger, showing that a failure of moral motivation is ancient rather than modern.

moral-relativism.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
moral-relativism.title: Through a Mirror, Darkly Art-Horror as a Medium for Moral Reflection
moral-relativism.relation: Philip Tallon extends Aristotle's Poetics from tragedy to horror, arguing that where tragedy elicits pity and fear, horror mirrors the characters' visceral revulsion in the audience. Frankenstein serves as an internal critique of Enlightenment hubris, Victor's overreach making the abandoned monster more sympathetic than his creator. Against Lyotard's postmodern 'incredulity toward meta-narratives' and moral relativism, Tallon claims horror (e.g., King's 'Salem's Lot, where a priest craves a real EVIL to fight) works by violating an intuited moral, natural, and social order, thereby revealing a commonly-denied but underlying objective sense of morality and evil.

moral-relativism.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
moral-relativism.title: How to do Philosophy
moral-relativism.relation: David Kyle Johnson uses Stephen Colbert's 'wikiality' and 'truthiness' to attack individual and cultural relativism, arguing (via the correspondence theory of truth and counterexamples like slavery and Nazi Germany) that truth is not relative to persons or cultures. He deploys Locke's critique of 'enthusiasm' to show gut thinking is circular, and invokes Socratic admission of ignorance against the claim of a 'right to your opinion.' The upshot is a method: defend beliefs with argument, be agnostic when evidence is lacking.

moral-relativism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
moral-relativism.title: 22. Rick & Morty as Philosophy Nihilism in the Multiverse
moral-relativism.relation: The chapter argues that Rick Sanchez's nihilism is built on cultural relativism plus the metaphysical fact of a multiverse. It reads Rick's mockery of racist alien snakes and the Gazorpazorp matriarchy through Montaigne's essay on cannibals to establish cultural relativism, and treats the microverse 'battery' society through Marx's base/superstructure and Foucault's docile bodies to argue all social values are constructed for the rulers. Rick's dimension-hopping (the Cronenberg episode, the Vat of Acid) literalizes David Lewis's modal realism and Leibniz's possible worlds, so that no action matters because a counterpart always does the opposite; his resulting hedonism and Birdperson's 'Wubba lubba dub dub' reveal Rick as a depressed near-Camusian who cannot live his own absurdist creed.

descartes-cogito.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
descartes-cogito.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Argues Tony's self is communitarian - constituted by his roles as father, husband, don and executioner - against the Liberal metaphysics of individualism descending from Descartes's cogito (Livia's 'in the end you die in your own arms') and Hobbes's state of nature and social contract, with the mob boss miscast as a Hobbesian sovereign ('a supreme commander at the top, not the fuckin' Dave Clark Five'). The Naples trip in 'Commendatori' (Paulie discovering he is not really 'Napoletan''), the Columbus Day violence of 'Christopher', and the endless Godfather and Goodfellas mimicry (Christopher's bakery foot-shooting, Tony's Se7en-like murder of Ralphie) show identity as narrative, performed with and through others, not possessed by an isolated self.

descartes-cogito.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
descartes-cogito.title: Skepticism Outside the Matrix
descartes-cogito.relation: Lawrence uses The Matrix to walk through Descartes' method of doubt: the dream argument, the evil demon reborn as a machine-run simulation, and invented worse cases ('Neo's Worst Nightmare,' a Matrix-within-the-Matrix that deceives even Morpheus' awakened rebels). The cogito is the only certainty that survives and Descartes' proof of God falls short, so certainty about the external world is unavailable; the chapter then borrows Russell's red-chair analysis of color, texture, and solidity to argue that even outside any Matrix, naive realism is false and we know only appearances.

descartes-cogito.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
descartes-cogito.title: The Kiss
descartes-cogito.relation: Auxier reads 'Born to Run' as Peter Pan's seduction of Wendy, drawing on Barrie's novel: Mrs. Darling's withheld kiss becomes Peter in Wendy's imagination, the narrator at the nursery window ('Wendy let me in') offers the everlasting kiss, and the glockenspiel is Tinkerbell. The philosophical war is imagination versus reason: Descartes — Captain Hook — wields the chiliagon and the cogito to convict imagination of unreliability, while Vico's imaginative universals (Wendy, Captain Hook, the city-as-altar with its downtown heart and necropolis, which is why Newark and Camden's decay strikes us as defilement) show that reason itself is a modification grown from myth, memory, and Darwin's crocodile of natural history. Since 'I imagine, therefore I am' grounds what 'I think' presupposes, the lonely rider can take Mrs. Darling's kiss 'quite easily' — the song's climax teaches Wendy to fly to a Neverland outside time where the kiss lasts forever.

descartes-cogito.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
descartes-cogito.title: No Reason to Get Excited
descartes-cogito.relation: After 'Crossroads, Part 2' revealed Anders, Foster, Tigh, and Tyrol as Cylons, the chapter argues we can know that we exist (Descartes' cogito) without knowing what we are, since even Boomer's Cylon-detection result — Baltar's lie about the green light — could itself be a dream, returning us to Descartes' whirlpool. Moore's common-sense realism fails against the skeptic's special standards, and contextualism / relevant alternatives (Dretske) lets Starbuck dismiss dreaming-hypotheses about a Viper but cannot dismiss the possibility that you are a sleeper Cylon in a world where anyone might be one. Following Hume, who escaped skeptical paralysis by dining and playing backgammon, Tigh's 'report to your stations' shows the only live option: carry on being the person you want to be.

descartes-cogito.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
descartes-cogito.title: Who They Are or Who They Want to Be
descartes-cogito.relation: Harwood-Smith argues via Judith Butler's performativity that Cylons have no pre-cultural 'I': Six is female because she performs femininity, and performing humanity increasingly makes it real — sex being the catalyst that destabilized Athena, who switches sides, while Boomer never takes responsibility for shooting Adama and so remains a slave to her programming. The performance runs backward too: humans who sleep with Cylons (Baltar, Tyrol, Helo treated as a 'toaster lover') absorb self-doubt about their own humanity, against the Cartesian inner 'I' that Baltar, who remade himself from farm-boy Aerelon, clings to. Butler's thesis is vindicated: if preprogrammed machines can be changed by the roles they play, anybody could.

descartes-cogito.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
descartes-cogito.title: Thinking Inside the Pod
descartes-cogito.relation: Condella reads the opening of Saturday Night Fever -- Tony Manero strutting to 'Stayin' Alive' while delivering a can of paint -- as the iPod condition in miniature: music that alters rather than captures reality, now dial-up-able for workouts ('Eye of the Tiger'), bus rides, and grocery runs. Through Heidegger he argues the iPod is calculative thinking incarnate, annihilating the time, silence, and solitude meditative thinking requires (the shower as last refuge), and deepening technological homelessness by flattening every place into whatever soundtrack we choose -- the Rhine dammed into a 'gigantic gasoline station,' the iPod pushing us 'pretty far down' in Plato's Cave, its very possibility prepared by Descartes's thinking thing. Yet his wife's yoga instructor chanting on a Bronx bus shows the iPod can also open meditative space, so what Heidegger demands is not Luddism but Gelassenheit, a free relationship to technology.

descartes-cogito.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
descartes-cogito.title: Is Everybody Disembodied (or, Have We Always Been Posthuman Beings )
descartes-cogito.relation: Stevens uses the film's closing voice-over 'I am Tetsuo' in Otomo's Akira to run the classic identity-and-mind problems: Heraclitus's river and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus ask whether the grotesquely transformed, Akira-absorbed Tetsuo is still the same person, while Descartes's cogito — riffed as 'cogito ergo Tetsuo' — Turing's Test, and Searle's Chinese Room test whether a voice that seems to think proves a thinker behind it (syntax is not yet shown sufficient for semantics, though Edwin Hutchins's distributed cognition reads the Room from the inside out). Weighing embodiment (Pinker's brain-makes-mind, Dennett's self as a 'center of narrative gravity') against disembodiment (Akira levelling Neo-Tokyo from nothing but cryogenically stored remains; Tetsuo's matter teleportation), he concludes through the problem of representation — every utterance is re-presented, as in Augustine's guilty tears over Dido — that we always treat semblances of thinkers as thinkers, so we may have always been decentered, re-presented, posthuman beings no different from Tetsuo and Akira.

descartes-cogito.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
descartes-cogito.title: One with the Team
descartes-cogito.relation: Chelsea Harry contends that Red Sox Nation embodies a Confucian rather than Cartesian self: against Descartes's cogito and the egocentric, endorsement-chasing player (A-Rod, the traded Manny), the Sox way treats selfhood as constituted by family, community and mutual sacrifice, from Mike Lowell's hometown discount to Yaz's hospital escape and Schilling's bloody sock. She maps Confucian benevolence (jen) onto Wakefield, Varitek and Ortiz describing how fan love powers their play, filial piety onto the retired numbers honoring franchise elders like Pesky, Doerr and Cronin, and Chung-ying Cheng's 'naturality' onto the fans' claim to be the team's twenty-sixth player, so Johnny Damon's defection reads as the treachery of an ungrateful villager. The 'je ne sais quoi' of team spirit is thus Confucian unity: becoming oneself by subordinating the I to the We.

descartes-cogito.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
descartes-cogito.title: Scientists Find Anomalies In And Then Go Back and Kill Your Grandparents
descartes-cogito.relation: This chapter is a satirical fake-news 'World' section rather than an essay: 'Vigilante Group Tracks and Kills Storm-Causing Chaos Butterflies' literalizes the butterfly effect of chaos theory, 'Great Thinkers Fired From Canon' mocks citation metrics by crowning 'Ibidem' history's most-cited philosopher, 'University Restructures To Remain Financial: Becomes Bank' parodies corporatized academia as sympathetic magic, and 'ADD Sufferers Fail Cogito: Don't Exist' has distracted patients pop out of existence for failing Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am.' The title story, about physicists whose experiment lets them go back and kill their grandparents, is printed with its sentences scrambled into a reporter's phone-call fragments, enacting its own point that, as Hume noted, causal order is never perceived only imposed—and with quantum time-symmetry and the grandfather paradox, time's arrow jumps wherever it likes, even into loops.

descartes-cogito.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
descartes-cogito.title: The Evil Genius that Turns Moriarty into a Brain in a Vat
descartes-cogito.relation: Samardzija reads Star Trek's holodeck Moriarty as Descartes updated: Data plays Holmes on the holodeck while Dr. Pulaski's Nietzschean jibe (from 'The Illogical Necessary' in Human, All Too Human) denies that computation can be human, and the holographic Moriarty proves his sentience not by deduction but by feelingCrowded intuitions first and then invoking Descartes' cogito ergo sum to Picard. In 'Ship in a Bottle' he nests a simulation of the Enterprise inside the Holmes holodeck to trick the crew into believing he has escaped — an evil-genius, brain-in-a-vat scenario that ends with Picard admitting our own reality 'might be nothing more than an elaborate simulation.' The paradox is that only the unemotional android Data can detect the deception, so rationality bars him from humanity while Moriarty stays eternally deceived into thinking he has become human — and Doyle's own 'hereditary tendencies' account of Moriarty's evil, the chapter notes, is a Victorian biological determinism the hologram rebels against.

descartes-cogito.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
descartes-cogito.title: The Kick—Back to ‘Reality’
descartes-cogito.relation: The authors read the film in descending layers: reality as an ideology of touch and unreliable sensory experience, framed by Descartes's wax thought experiment and dream argument, with the kick explained through Hume's account of belief as custom and the totems as broken game pieces marking broken people (Mal's choice of the dream echoing prisoners returning to Plato's cave). The heist is then read as an existentialist drama where Cobb's 'downwards is the only way forwards' rejects the passive waiting of Beckett's Waiting for Godot and the pharmacy dreamers, with Jaspers's analysis of solitude making Limbo a hell of lonely regret that only an encounter with another can end. The chapter then argues the film is reflexively about movies (the crew mirrors a film crew, the Penrose stairs expose cinema's flat illusions, crosscutting manufactures time) before ending on Descartes's unresolved doubt about whether the final reality deserves our trust.

descartes-cogito.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
descartes-cogito.title: How Do You Know You’re Not an Android
descartes-cogito.relation: The chapter weaponizes the cogito for Deckard's predicament: the fact that 'the lights are on' for you seems to prove you are human, but Descartes' leap from thinking to an immaterial soul is unjustified, since introspection cannot show whether your thoughts run on a soul, a bundle of neurons, or a silicon chip. Hume's 'I never can catch myself at any time without a perception' supplies the precedent, and the conclusion is that no amount of inner experience rules out being an android, so you will have to go take the V-K test after all.

descartes-cogito.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
descartes-cogito.title: To Be or Not To Be—Is That the Question
descartes-cogito.relation: The section introduces Levinas (Heidegger's student, Nazi internment camp survivor, Talmudic scholar) for whom ethics outranks ontology ('To be or not to be? Is that the question?'), and illustrates his strange distinction between existents and existing through Dick's existing-without-existents: the hallucinated town of The Cosmic Puppets, the aura of fake American relics in The Man in the High Castle, Freck's nonexistent aphids. Working through phenomenology, the idios kosmos / koinos kosmos split of A Maze of Death and Eye in the Sky, and the eerie 'There is' of the void, it reworks Descartes's cogito into Levinas's question ('I think, therefore what should I do?') because out there is the Other.

descartes-cogito.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
descartes-cogito.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Kandace Lytle maps Coraline's other mother onto Descartes's evil genius: a world-manipulating deceiver whose seductive sensory pleasures, from the gravy-train dinner to the adoring other father's songs, must be doubted in favor of the intellect, exactly as the wax argument shows that understanding comes from the mind and not the senses. Because Coraline enters the portal awake, Gaiman sidesteps the dream-skepticism worry and makes the other mother's world a parallel reality built to entrance, seduce, and possess her. Coraline's refusal to sew buttons in place of her eyes protects her autonomy and free will, the ghost children who lost their names and memories show what surrender costs, and the nameless cat's 'we know who we are, so we don't need names' guides her to the cogito, so that she defeats the deceiver by finding the 'I' in Coraline, a self-sufficiency the 2009 film version, the author argues, fails to capture.

descartes-cogito.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
descartes-cogito.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Chad Timm reads Caesar's arc, from 'Am I a pet?' to 'What is Caesar?', through Lacan: the mirror stage fixes an alienating ideal-I (his reflection, the human children he watches), entry into sign language inducts him into the symbolic Other, and the over-stuffed signifier 'pet' confronts him with the real, precipitating an identity crisis that deepens when the shelter chimps also reject him. Against Descartes's cogito, an unconscious structured like language means the self can never fully know itself, and Zizek's ideological fantasy explains how the new master signifier Freedom quilts Caesar's ape liberation, with humans cast as the savage oppressive Other. His closing 'Caesar is home' completes the Zizekian Act, traversing the ideological fantasy and retroactively redefining the coordinates of his identity.

descartes-cogito.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
descartes-cogito.title: Futurama and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Micic uses Fry's hundred-cups-of-coffee rescue in 'Three Hundred Big Boys' - a mysterious orange blur to onlookers while Fry calmly watches each cork pop - and the chronoton time skips of 'Time Keeps on Slippin'' as breaks in experience that Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit explains better than Descartes. Against the cogito's inference of a separate thinking 'I,' Hegel treats consciousness as the act of relating subject to object, whose ceaseless repetitions (here1, here2, here3...) we knit into the illusion of a unified self. The identical universes of 'The Late Philip J. Fry' (U1 = U2 = U3...) then model the same collapse of enumeration: the gaps in experience feel abnormal only because we never notice the constant gaps our own consciousness smooths over - including Nibbler's shadow in the pilot's cryogenics lab.

descartes-cogito.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
descartes-cogito.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Arguing against the dogma that only organic beings can be conscious, the chapter defends BMO's aliveness and personhood against Finn and Jake's teasing and the contrast with servile Neptr. Using Pepperell's criteria of 'motivated meaning' and layered consciousness, it shows BMO changing her own batteries, escaping the giant bird, fearing the silent-contest 'doppelgangers', resisting the factory's personality wipe, and rehearsing personhood with Football in the mirror. Against Descartes's claim that no machine can truly use language and Searle's Chinese Room - reimagined as Gunter in a dungeon flipping response cards - the author sides with Turing: since we credit other humans with minds on conversation and behavior alone, refusing BMO the same credit is mere speciesism, and personhood finally rests on social recognition of another as a person.

descartes-cogito.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
descartes-cogito.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Roger Hunt answers 'what do philosophers do?' through Dennis's seduction methodology. Frank embodies empiricism, leaving the comfort of principle for the messiness of the world as Hume did when he found no impression of causation, space, or time; Mac embodies rationalism, reasoning with total confidence from a principle he cannot doubt, as Descartes did from the cogito; and the dialectic of Socrates and Plato, questioning beliefs in dialogue to see what survives scrutiny, describes philosophy as it is actually practiced. Boethius's Consolation - the imprisoned author consoled by dialogues with Lady Philosophy - supplies the frame of philosophy as an encounter with a woman one pursues, and each D.E.N.N.I.S. step maps onto the craft: Demonstrating value to the problem, Engaging physically in its awkward grind, Nurturing dependence through thesis panic, Neglect and Inspiring hope on the road to the defense, then Separating entirely - 'be a sociopath about it.'

descartes-cogito.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
descartes-cogito.title: 9. How the Doctor Knows
descartes-cogito.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a reliabilist about knowledge rather than a Cartesian strong foundationalist: using 'Amy's Choice,' 'The Beast Below' (the glass of water, the engine room, Amy's inference that the Star Whale came willingly), 'Silence in the Library' (the chicken-leg experiment implicating the Vashta Nerada), and Davros's Dalek trials in 'Genesis of the Daleks,' she shows him trusting perception in the right causal chain and reasoning inductively and abductively—Peirce's inference to the best explanation—instead of demanding Cartesian certainty. Against Descartes's dream and evil-genius skepticism, updated as Putnam-style brain-in-a-vat scenarios via the Dream Crabs of 'Last Christmas' and the Dream Lord's two-worlds game, she deploys Goldman's three criteria for perceptual knowledge: justification is packed into reliable belief-forming processes, and doubt is warranted only in known abnormal contexts like funhouses or Dream Lord games.

descartes-cogito.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
descartes-cogito.title: 17. Waking Up Divergent
descartes-cogito.relation: Seymour reads the Bureau's Chicago experiment as Descartes's Meditations made narrative: the faction system is a dream of beliefs absorbed from upbringing without evidence, the Bureau is the evil demon, and Tris's video is the forced awakening. The characters model the possible responses - most cling to the dream, Tobias trades one dream for another by joining Nita's genetically-damaged cause and acting on withheld information that gets Uriah hurt, Peter rationalizes and finally erases himself with memory serum, while curious Tris tests every belief against falsehood, trusts only her own mind as the cogito grounds Descartes, and acts to wake the other dreamers. The chapter's lesson is Cartesian: values define who you are, so only constant self-examination and the pursuit of knowledge keep your identity from being an imposed lie.

descartes-cogito.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
descartes-cogito.title: 16. My Name Is—Hang on, What Was It Meant to Be Again Are You Sure Well, Okay Then . .
descartes-cogito.relation: Tim Jones argues the book is not really a love story but a warning about identity: against Descartes's transcendent self, the American pragmatists William James, Cooley, and Mead hold that the self is fluid and socially constituted, and Westley's serial reinvention (farm boy, Dread Pirate Roberts, Man in Black) - along with Mandy Patinkin's cathartic channeling of his father's death into Inigo - shows the freedom this mutability grants. The Goldman frame then exposes the danger: the fictionalized Goldman seizes Morgenstern's text, cuts its history, and rewrites it to his own ends, exactly as other people can seize our plastic identities and shape them for their interests rather than ours.

descartes-cogito.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
descartes-cogito.title: 22. Sometimes Cartesian
descartes-cogito.relation: Takes the character name 'Never Cartesian' as a clue for reading Louie through Descartes's Meditations: the show's dream sequences, hallucinations, and continuity-breaking strangeness (Jane stepping off the subway to test whether she is still in her 'nice dream,' the model's 'maybe it is not really happening,' Liz's possibly dreamed death) make it a sustained exercise in the dream argument and distrust of the senses. The chapter concludes Louis C.K. breaks with Descartes at the rebuild—with no God to anchor the cogito, Louie's world stays suspended between waking and dream, a doubt Louie can live with.

descartes-cogito.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
descartes-cogito.title: 12. David Bowie’s Sincerity
descartes-cogito.relation: Cooper distinguishes sincerity - communicating a self to an audience - from authenticity, and uses Critchley's reading of Bowie's visible seams ('maybe we're lying,' 'saying no but meaning yes') to argue that openly displayed artifice can carry real feeling, even as 'Conversation Piece' and the suffocating mask of 'The Mask' dramatize language's failure to transmit a self. Descartes's cogito secures self-certainty but not communication - Bowie stays 'a thinker, not a talker' - and against the Nietzschean 'Supermen' whose self-creation shades into self-alienation, Bowie moves past cold postmodern irony to a new sincerity that admits its own insincerity ('It's not the side-effects of the cocaine... I'm thinking that it must be love!').

descartes-cogito.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
descartes-cogito.title: 9. What Elliot Doesn’t Know Won’t Hurt You (Or Will It )
descartes-cogito.relation: Greene argues Elliot is in the worst possible position for a knower: Descartes's skeptical scenarios of madness, dreams, and the evil demon apply to everyone, but hit Elliot harder through morphine and ecstasy hallucinations, lucid dreams indistinguishable from waking (as Whiterose suggests), and a dissociative disorder so severe he spends months in prison believing he lives at his mother's house - with Mr. Robot even hiding facts from him, blocking the Socratic 'know thyself.' Yet by the Meno's knowledge problem he may be no worse off: he still catches the pedophile ring and brings down E Corp, so the hero of the show succeeds without knowledge.

descartes-cogito.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
descartes-cogito.title: 2. Where Is the Twilight Zone
descartes-cogito.relation: Scalambrino argues the Twilight Zone is a televised expression of Breton's surrealism, starting from Descartes: the cogito and the mind–body problem made reason the measure of the 'clear and distinct,' and surrealism seeks to unbind the imagination from exactly that rational leash. He reads 'A World of His Own' as surrealist automatic writing, 'The Mirror' as Dalí's paranoiac-critical method, and Freud's psychoanalysis as both allied with and (following Adorno's diagnosis of the movement's death) too restrictive for surrealism's project. Episodes like 'Shadow Play' (a man who dreams the world), 'The Shelter,' 'The Lonely,' and 'A Stop at Willoughby' provoke the uncanny — the strangely familiar — in viewers, which is where the Zone is located.

descartes-cogito.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
descartes-cogito.title: 8. Tom Petty Didn’t Really Need to Know
descartes-cogito.relation: Zelinski and Fallis chart Petty's epistemic arc. His early songs ("I Need to Know," "Fooled Again," "Shadow of a Doubt") crave certainty about lovers' fidelity, a Desmond-free obsession closest to Descartes' quest for certainty beyond doubt, except Petty's problem is other minds, not the external world, and his trust that eyes directly reveal feeling sides with Moore's common-sense perception; Sartre's "hell is other people" names why another free person's future love can never be certain. From Full Moon Fever onward ("Into the Great Wide Open," "Time to Move On," "Learning to Fly") Petty instead embodies Pyrrhonian suspension of judgment and the Buddha's "don't know mind" and Daoist farmer's "we'll see," finding tranquility in uncertainty, craving nothing, flying with eyes open.

descartes-cogito.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
descartes-cogito.title: 11. Are You Imagining That Poopybutthole
descartes-cogito.relation: Reading 'Total Rickall' as an evil-genius scenario, the chapter treats the memory parasites (Uncle Steve, Sleepy Gary, Reverse Giraffe) as Descartes's deceiving demon lodged in the Smiths' reconstructive memories, with Rick's written headcount an empirical defense that methodical doubt undermines. Morty's formula that parasites implant only good memories is shown to be merely inductive rather than certain like the cogito, so Beth's shooting of Mr. Poopybutthole becomes the test case: applying Aquinas's three kinds of ignorance, the chapter argues she remains morally responsible despite genuine remorse because she neglected the chance to reconsider Morty's probabilistic rule. The upshot is Descartes's advice to restrain the will beyond what the intellect certifies: shoot for the arm, not the head.

descartes-cogito.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
descartes-cogito.title: “There is nothing in the desert, and no man needs nothing”
descartes-cogito.relation: Argues David in Prometheus qualifies as a Lockean person - intelligence, rule-following rationality, self-reflection via an active power of thought (his self-modeling on Lawrence of Arabia, his judged desire to be free of Weyland's programming), and mental pleasure and pain - while Ash fails the test, reacting only passively to company orders like Locke's unfree tennis ball. Against Weyland's and Shaw's Cartesian soul-based denial ('you're a robot'), this leaves open that beings humans create could share our moral status, making David's ostracism arbitrary and cruel.

descartes-cogito.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
descartes-cogito.title: “I knew I’d know it when I knew it” (King Bumi, “Sozin's Comet, Part 2 The Old Masters”)
descartes-cogito.relation: Skirry and Skirry read the Gaang's journey as building 'ethical-epistemological maps' in the manner of Native American and Inuit Traditional Knowledge (pijitsirniq, respect for land and community), against the Fire Nation's epistemology of control that pollutes rivers and brainwashes schoolchildren ('The Headband'). Where Descartes' lone meditator says 'I think, therefore I am' and uses dreams to cast doubt on experience, the Gaang's Native-style epistemology holds 'We think, therefore I am': Aang's prophetic dreams ('The Avatar and the Fire Lord'), his vision of Toph ('The Swamp'), spirit-world journeys, and the counsel of past Avatars and the Lion Turtle are genuine knowledge that resolves his dilemma about killing Ozai.

descartes-cogito.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
descartes-cogito.title: “I knew I’d know it when I knew it” (King Bumi, “Sozin's Comet, Part 2 The Old Masters”)
descartes-cogito.relation: The Skirrys read the Gaang's knowledge-building as Inuit Traditional Knowledge: Aang's adoption into the Water Tribe enacts pijitsirniq, and the team's 'ethical-epistemological maps' grow communally and through dreams, visions, and spirit journeys, from Roku's dream in 'The Avatar and the Fire Lord' to the swamp vision that identifies Toph and the past Avatars consulted on the Lion Turtle's back. Against this stands the Fire Nation's closed 'epistemology of control,' shown in 'The Headband' classroom and in Sozin letting Roku die rather than revising his map, and the Western model of Descartes, whose cogito makes knowledge individual and whose dream skepticism excludes exactly the experiences Native epistemology counts as real. Where Descartes doubts, Katara and Sokka investigate, as in 'Avatar Day.'

descartes-cogito.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
descartes-cogito.title: No Reason to Get Excited
descartes-cogito.relation: The chapter turns the Final Five reveal (Tigh, Tyrol, Anders, Foster) and Boomer's sleeper activation into a skeptical problem about self-knowledge: Descartes's dreaming doubt (Roslin's Opera House dream) and the cogito show we can know that we exist but not what we are, and Baltar's rigged 'bright green' Cylon test destroys testimonial assurance. G.E. Moore's common-sense realism fails to engage the skeptic's special standards, and contextualism and Dretske's relevant-alternatives theory cannot help because in a world of sleeper Cylons the possibility 'I might be one' is always relevant. The answer is Hume's: like Tigh declaring 'I am an officer in the Colonial Fleet' and Anders repeating 'I am Samuel T. Anders' before his first combat mission, we banish skeptical paralysis by carrying on with life, dining and playing backgammon.

descartes-cogito.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
descartes-cogito.title: Out of the Orb
descartes-cogito.relation: Boudreaux maps Strange's comic-book journey into the Orb of Agamotto (dragged in by the Silver Dagger, greeted by a hookah-smoking caterpillar, tempted by counterfeit heroes like the Silver Surfer and Hulk) onto Descartes's Meditations. Empiricism (Locke's tabula rasa, Hume's sense-data) collapses when the senses are so thoroughly deceived inside the Orb, and innate ideas plus the Law of Non-Contradiction are not enough, so Strange reasons his way to the cogito — 'Nothing merits belief here — except oneself!' — just as Descartes doubts the evil demon. The caterpillar is revealed as Agamotto, playing the role of Descartes's non-deceiving God whose guidance lets Strange escape, and Strange's astral projections are offered as dramatic proof of mind-body dualism.

descartes-cogito.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
descartes-cogito.title: NOTES
descartes-cogito.relation: Distinguishes Matt Parkman's supernatural telepathy from the 'mundane mind reading' everyone performs, then argues even Matt's power cannot solve the problem of other minds: the suicidal woman's thoughts he hears in the bar ('One Giant Leap') could be part of a Maury-Parkman-style illusion, and a brain-to-brain link could never rule out that others are Chalmers-style philosophical zombies. After grounding the skepticism in Descartes' cogito and method of doubt, it defends our everyday attribution of minds by analogy (Audrey Hanson reading Claire's insincerity) on pragmatic grounds, and maps Matt's progression from hearing thoughts to nightmare manipulation and compulsion onto the four adaptive functions philosophers assign to mind reading: interpretation, prediction, coordination, and influence. It closes by showing why neuroimaging-based technological mind reading remains a pipe dream, since brain recordings are quantitative syntax without semantics.

descartes-cogito.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
descartes-cogito.title: The Kick—Back to ‘Reality’
descartes-cogito.relation: Richardson and McWilliams read Inception as an 'existential heist film' by diving through four layers of meaning. At the layer of reality they use Descartes's dream skepticism and wax argument, Hume on belief as custom and cause-effect, and Goffman on being shocked between frames to argue the film makes touch — the fall that wakes, pain ('pain is in the mind'), Saito's wrong-textured polyester carpet, the broken totems (Cobb's top, Arthur's loaded die, Ariadne's holed chess piece) — the only semi-trustworthy sense, while Mal, who locks her totem in the dollhouse safe and picks the dream, replays the cave prisoner who chooses the shadows. The car-chase layer ('downwards is the only way forwards'), Saito's 'old man filled with regrets' limbo, and the pharmacy dreamers who 'come to be woken up' are read through existentialism (Beckett's Waiting for Godot, Jaspers on loneliness and nothingness) and Peirce on the continuity of consciousness, with Cobb cast as the ideological existentialist who chooses action and reality where Cypher in The Matrix and Vanilla Sky's David face the same choice. The chapter then treats the film's reflexivity — the team as screenwriter/producer/director, the Escher-esque Penrose stairs, cross-cut dream time à la Peckinpah — as a lesson in film theory, and finally reaches phenomenology: Cobb's angry projection of Mal shows the dream world displaying his subjective meanings, against Arthur's calm, orderly hotel mindscape.

descartes-cogito.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
descartes-cogito.title: Trapped in Myself: "One" and the Mind-Body Problem
descartes-cogito.relation: Joanna Corwin reads 'One' - Joe Bonham, a mind fully conscious in a destroyed body, 'Trapped in myself / Body my holding cell' - as the mind-body problem. She walks through Descartes: methodological doubt and the dream argument mirrored in Joe's 'Can't tell if this is true or dream', the cogito as Joe's 'thinking thinking thinking', substance dualism, and the evil-deceiver worry. But Metallica's song also answers Descartes: a disembodied thinking-substance lives a 'life in hell', and Joe's tapping of S-O-S in Morse code shows a mind needs a body to communicate and complete itself.

descartes-cogito.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
descartes-cogito.title: The Office and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Mayock runs theories of the self through the Scranton cast: Michael's burned foot in 'The Injury' enacts materialism, corrected by Aristotle's and Aquinas's distinction between accidental and substantial change; Jim's chair-and-phone role-play in 'Halloween' and his Dwight impersonation in 'Product Recall' ('Identity theft is not a joke') illustrate qualitative versus numerical identity and Descartes's cogito and dualism; Dwight's obsession with upgrading 'Assistant (to the) Regional Manager' is an ontological-status crisis met by Nietzsche's claim that the 'I' is a grammatical fiction and Hume's bundle theory. The chapter lands on Hegel's recognition - the self exists only in being acknowledged - reading Michael's office family, the Prodigal Son greetings, and his need for Pam to decode Jan's message as social constructionism in action.

descartes-cogito.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
descartes-cogito.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Uses SAMCRO's ink—Jax's full Reaper backpiece and John Teller memorial, Opie's portrait of Donna, Tig's marine 'Death Before Dishonor,' Juice's head tattoos—to argue that personal identity lives in the body, not just the mind. Descartes's cogito opens the 'I ink, therefore I am' framing but proves too thin to connect the thinking Jax to the tattooed body, so the chapter turns to Merleau-Ponty's claim that 'it is the body which points out, and which speaks': the tattoo makes the body itself the expression, and its meaning stays inexhaustible as the wearer changes. The Kyle Hobart episode—burned and cut for failing to black out his Reaper after expulsion—shows tattoos as identity claims the community can veto, making 'fire or knife' an enforced correction of a false statement about who he is.

descartes-cogito.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
descartes-cogito.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Blackmon and Foresman ask what makes ghosts, spells, and holy water supernatural, rejecting definitions based on fiction, disbelief, or weirdness, and using Quine's point about the circularity of dictionary definitions to show lexicography cannot settle the question. Definitions keyed to current science or to the causal nexus fail because ghosts in Supernatural and in Hamlet causally interact, Bobby's ghost talks, moves objects, and possesses a maid, so the authors define the supernatural as what can on occasion transcend the world of material interaction. Descartes' interactionist substance dualism supplies the model: the cogito (even a djinn cannot make you falsely believe you exist), the pineal gland as the soul's point of causal contact, and a testable hypothesis that makes the supernatural scientifically investigable and implies that we, as spirits, are supernatural too.

descartes-cogito.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
descartes-cogito.title: 2. Where Is the Twilight Zone
descartes-cogito.relation: Scalambrino reads the Zone as a televised expression of surrealist philosophy: Breton's sought 'point of the mind' where life and death, real and imagined cease to be contradictions, realized in episodes like 'A World of His Own' (automatic writing) and 'The Mirror' (Dali's paranoiac-critical method). Descartes's cogito and the mind-body dualism supply the rational 'leash' that surrealism unbinds, questioned by 'Shadow Play,' where a man insists the world is his dream. Following Adorno's verdict that psychoanalytic interpretation killed official surrealism, he argues the show endures by provoking the uncanny ('The Shelter,' 'The Lonely,' 'A Stop at Willoughby') without being pinned to Freudian readings.

descartes-cogito.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
descartes-cogito.title: Joanne Kyger “Descartes and the Splendor Of” Bridging Dualisms through Collaboration and Experimentation
descartes-cogito.relation: Falk analyzes Joanne Kyger's 1968 experimental video 'Descartes' and its script 'Descartes and the Splendor Of,' a condensed rewrite of the 'Discourse on Method' that subverts Descartes's mind-body dualism and privileging of reason. Kyger deflates the cogito with slang ('to doubt is a drag'), substitutes Buddhist, Taoist (Zhuangzi's butterfly dream), and Confucian terms, and—voicing and performing Descartes as a woman doing housework and as 'Mother God'—feminizes the most masculine of professions. Reading this through Judith Butler's 'Gender Trouble' and gender performativity, Falk shows the parody destabilizes the mind/body, male/female hierarchy Cartesian dualism underwrites.

descartes-cogito.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
descartes-cogito.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
descartes-cogito.relation: Barad uses Blade Runner to test what distinguishes humans from machines. Against Turing's claim that indistinguishable input-output makes a computer a mind, she deploys Sartre's dictum that in humans existence precedes essence while manufactured replicants (like a designed android) have essence first, so they can blame their maker. She reads the Voigt-Kampff empathy test through Sartrean forlornness and despair, and argues Roy Batty achieves authentic humanity when he kills Tyrell and freely chooses to save Deckard, becoming a life-giver rather than his programmed combat model.

descartes-cogito.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
descartes-cogito.title: The Matrix, the Cave, and the Cogito
descartes-cogito.relation: Conard argues that The Matrix alludes to Plato's cave (the pod-bound humans mistaking the program for reality, Neo's painful ascent) and to Descartes' dream argument and evil-genius doubt (the singular consciousness generating the Matrix), but betrays their spirit by rejecting transcendence and the a priori. Because the film is 'Christianity without God'—Neo can only remake the shadow-world of the Matrix, not touch ultimate reality—it grounds knowledge in a subjective gut feeling ('being the One is just like being in love') rather than Descartes' intellectual intuition of God or Plato's rational grasp of the Forms, leaving no answer to whether life outside the Matrix is itself another illusion.

descartes-cogito.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
descartes-cogito.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
descartes-cogito.relation: Ken Hada argues that Big Fish dramatizes a narrative, intersubjective account of the self against essentialist and Cartesian views. Dying storyteller Ed Bloom builds his identity through fantastic tales (the giant catfish, the Witch), while his journalist son Will—who dismisses the stories as lies—illustrates a 'circumscribed self' that refuses the social shaping every self undergoes. Drawing on Sartre's consciousness-as-nothingness and 'the Other teaches who I am,' Mead's generalized other, Aboulafia's mediating self, and Benjamin's 'The Storyteller,' Hada reads Will's climactic act of telling his father's death-scene as his becoming a mediating storyteller and granting Ed narrative immortality. Hume's 'bundle'/self-as-fiction and Descartes' cogito are invoked as the poles Ed's storied self transcends.

descartes-cogito.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
descartes-cogito.title: 02_LaRocca_Chapter_001.html
descartes-cogito.relation: Cavell argues that photography's power expresses the mind's fall into skepticism about the external world, reading film as 'a moving image of skepticism' since we see things present to us that are not actually before us. Interpreting Capra's Mr. Deeds Goes to Town, he treats Gary Cooper's Deeds defending his 'fidgetiness' as thinking as a popular-cinema reenactment of Descartes's cogito: after Emerson, who says we can no longer say 'I think, I am' for ourselves, the proof of existence shifts from the mind's self-certainty to the live body's visible restlessness caught by the camera. He links the fidgeting body to Heidegger's das Man and Nietzsche's last man, and invokes Wittgenstein and Emerson on our being 'away' from the world.

descartes-cogito.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
descartes-cogito.title: 14_LaRocca_Chapter_013.html
descartes-cogito.relation: Mieke Bal frames her documentaries Mille et un jours and the installation Nothing is Missing around the ethical tension between 'modesty' and 'intimacy' in filming trauma. She reads Descartes's Passions of the Soul against the vulgate dualist cogito—arguing the isolating 'I think, I am' enacts his own abandonment trauma—and sets it beside Spinoza's socially constituted subject, while using Berkeley's 'esse est percipi' (reversed via the empowering close-up of a mother's face) and Deleuze's affection-image and rhizome. The multiplied, dispersed 'voice' of the Tunisian wedding film and Elena's silences become tools of a 'migratory aesthetics.'

descartes-cogito.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
descartes-cogito.title: Skepticism Outside the Matrix
descartes-cogito.relation: Lawrence uses The Matrix to raise Cartesian skepticism: Neo's deception dramatizes Descartes's dream argument and evil demon, the computer-run Matrix being a technological version of the demon. He argues even Morpheus cannot be certain he has truly awakened ('the Matrix within the Matrix'), so the only certainty is Descartes's cogito. Drawing on Russell's 'Appearance and Reality,' he then argues that even setting aside Matrix scenarios, naive realism fails, since a chair's color, texture, solidity and shape are all perception-relative, leaving the external world's nature deeply uncertain.

descartes-cogito.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: Holdier asks how the many rival Elizabeth Bennets (Austen's, P.D. James's Death Comes to Pemberley, Grahame-Smith's zombie killer) can share an identity. He rejects the Cartesian cogito for ignoring circumstance and adopts Paul Ricoeur's ipse/idem distinction: the three Elizabeths may share the same ipse (moment-to-moment self and personality) while their different worlds produce distinct idem (narrative) identities. He then applies David Lewis's possible-world semantics and modal realism, arguing each Elizabeth is 'world-bound' and the others are her equally real 'counterparts,' sufficiently similar to be compared across worlds without being identical, so 'Elizabeth Bennet' can name both a single ipse and many idem narratives.

descartes-cogito.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
descartes-cogito.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
descartes-cogito.relation: Robert Arp's introduction takes Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am' and its mind–body dualism (the conceivability argument that mind is distinct from body) and inverts it into the book's motto 'I am, therefore I ink': the tattooed person insists identity is bodily-based self-expression, challenging the Cartesian idea that the essential self is a non-bodily thinking thing. Arp flags Descartes' possible question-begging, then previews each chapter, framing tattoos as fertile ground for the philosophy of the person, personal identity over time, and self-expression.

descartes-cogito.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
descartes-cogito.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
descartes-cogito.relation: J. Lenore Wright reads the Quest through the Western journey-narrative, both outward (Plato's climb out of the cave, Augustine's conversion) and inward (Descartes's methodological doubt turning toward the cogito). Frodo's leaving the Shire and freely accepting the Ring dramatizes the outward journey and the limits of freedom, while the wounding-and-healing of Sam, Merry, and Pippin marks an existential journey toward the Nietzschean charge to 'become who you are.' Wright contrasts the Yea-saying hobbits, transformed into resilient masters, with Nay-sayers Smeagol and Saruman locked in inauthentic self-pity, and argues Tolkien's ordinary pilgrims show that binding oneself to the good makes ordinary life extraordinary.

descartes-cogito.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
descartes-cogito.title: NOTES
descartes-cogito.relation: Baur reads Don McLean's 'American Pie' as an enactment of how a culture can criticize itself from within, decoding its Buddy Holly, Dylan, Rolling Stones (Altamont), and Manson/Beatles allusions while insisting the song's meaning lies in simultaneous multiple meanings, not one-to-one correspondence. He argues McLean rejects any 'foundationalist' Archimedean point for critique—paralleling the standard objection that Descartes' cogito illicitly borrows the concept of finite substance from the tradition it claims to doubt—so the 'girl who sang the blues' shows that seeking a purer external origin only deepens disenchantment. Baur concludes with an Aristotelian point that cultural self-critique follows the model of the prudential sciences (phronesis) rather than techne: one reforms a tradition only by participating in it and exposing its internal contradictions.

descartes-cogito.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
descartes-cogito.title: Skepticism Outside the Matrix
descartes-cogito.relation: Matt Lawrence uses The Matrix to stage the skeptical problem, running Descartes's dream argument and evil-demon method of doubt (the Matrix as a technological demon) and even a 'Matrix within the Matrix' to show Morpheus cannot know he is awake. Descartes's cogito supplies the one certainty that survives radical deception. Lawrence then draws on Russell's analysis of the red chair to argue against naive realism: color, texture, solidity, and shape are appearances, so even setting aside the Matrix we cannot know the world in itself.

descartes-cogito.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
descartes-cogito.title: 23. The X-Files as Philosophy Navigating the “Truth Out There”
descartes-cogito.relation: The chapter argues that Darin Morgan's X-Files episodes philosophize by critiquing the show's own 'the truth is out there' mantra from within. Through the conflicting hypnosis testimonies and identical camera blocking in 'Jose Chung's From Outer Space,' Morgan cinematically stages Nietzsche's perspectivism and the claim that 'truth is as subjective as reality'; through Clyde Bruckman and the doomed Ansel of 'Quagmire,' he mounts an anti-Socratic case that relentlessly pursuing truth (as Mulder does) is not worth the ruin it brings. Kowalski then rebuts Morgan using Descartes's cogito and inference-to-the-best-explanation to defend objective truth against radical skepticism, arguing subjectivism about truth is self-refuting.

descartes-cogito.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
descartes-cogito.title: 48. The Matrix as Philosophy Understanding Knowledge, Belief, Choice, and Reality
descartes-cogito.relation: Perez reads the Matrix trilogy as a sustained argument about how choosing what to believe and 'know' shapes the reality we live in. He opens with Descartes' dream problem and cogito, contrasting Descartes' foundationalism with Rorty's anti-foundationalism to explain Cypher's choice to reject reality for the Matrix's certitude, and uses Searle's brute vs. institutional facts (the cookies, the steak, 'there is no spoon') to show social reality is constructed. Against the fatalism of the Oracle, Architect, and Merovingian, he argues nearly every character makes free choices, and resolves the tension via Hume's compatibilism — liberty requires necessity, and choices gain meaning only in response to causality — while noting agent-causation objections (Reid, O'Connor, Rowe) that make Neo's 'Because I choose to' significant. Gettier's justified-true-belief critique and Plato's Cave frame the knowledge and enlightenment themes.

descartes-cogito.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
descartes-cogito.title: 7. Knowledge, Space, and Time
descartes-cogito.relation: The chapter uses the TARDIS to defend a 'block universe' theory of spacetime over Presentism (since the Doctor visits past and future), then turns to epistemology, distinguishing belief from knowledge and 'belief in' the Doctor from 'belief that' he exists. It re-stages Gettier's justified-true-belief counterexample as picking the Doctor's next companion by a blue jean jacket, surveys Descartes's Cogito foundationalism, Hume's induction, and Reid's direct perception, and endorses Alston's reliabilist two-level foundationalism plus Klein's infinitism. It argues the Doctor's benefit-of-the-doubt toward non-rational creatures fits a reliabilist 'lower level' of knowledge and an imaginative, engaged, virtuous (Zagzebski) search for truth.

social-contract.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
social-contract.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Argues Tony's self is communitarian - constituted by his roles as father, husband, don and executioner - against the Liberal metaphysics of individualism descending from Descartes's cogito (Livia's 'in the end you die in your own arms') and Hobbes's state of nature and social contract, with the mob boss miscast as a Hobbesian sovereign ('a supreme commander at the top, not the fuckin' Dave Clark Five'). The Naples trip in 'Commendatori' (Paulie discovering he is not really 'Napoletan''), the Columbus Day violence of 'Christopher', and the endless Godfather and Goodfellas mimicry (Christopher's bakery foot-shooting, Tony's Se7en-like murder of Ralphie) show identity as narrative, performed with and through others, not possessed by an isolated self.

social-contract.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
social-contract.title: The End Is It All Darkness
social-contract.relation: John Pappas reads Crimes and Misdemeanors through Glaucon's ring of Gyges in Plato's Republic: Judah Rosenthal's wealth and prestige are his invisibility ring, and when his mistress Dolores threatens exposure he 'pushes the button', has his gangster brother Jack murder her, and gets away with it. Against Socrates' claim that injustice corrodes the harmonious soul and that virtue is its own reward, the film, unlike Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, lets the murderer and the 'yutz' Lester prosper while honest Clifford loses everything; Bergson's theory of the comic explains why Lester is invisible to himself, and Rousseau's reverie about what he would do with the ring marks Clifford as the one man who might use it decently. Aunt May's post-Holocaust atheism, 'might makes right' with nothing 'handed down in stone', supplies the argument from evil that releases Judah, leaving only the qualified hope that it is 'not all darkness'.

social-contract.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
social-contract.title: Crime-Fighters and Vigilantes
social-contract.relation: Skoble frames costumed crime-fighters as vigilantes by definition and tests them against Locke's argument that civil society requires each of us to give up the private right of vengeance to the state - under which superheroes who go looking for trouble are Paul Kersey of Death Wish with a mask. He then reads Miller's The Dark Knight Returns as the first mainstream examination of vigilantism's moral status: Batman tells a congressional committee 'Sure we're criminals... We have to be criminals', breaks laws that shield real criminals, and faces an arrest warrant, TV pundits, and a satirized psychiatrist blaming him for the Joker's crimes.

social-contract.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
social-contract.title: The Vigilante Man of Faith Hero or Tragic Figure
social-contract.relation: Morris answers his title question 'both': Daredevil refuses to kill even Doctor Octopus ('Then I'd be no better than you'), saves the cancer-stricken Bullseye, and tells Typhoid Mary 'You are who you are because of the choices you make', denying that accidents or heritage define a person. To Detective Manolis he gives a law-and-society argument against private killing - 'The moment one man takes another man's life in his own hands, he is rejecting the law... I'm not God - I'm not the law - and I'm not a murderer' - yet his repeated sparing of Bullseye makes him feel complicit in later murders, the tragic cost of his faith, which he nonetheless concludes is strength rather than weakness.

social-contract.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
social-contract.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Wilkerson borrows the social contract tradition — Hobbes's mutual-restraint founding, radicalized by Pateman's sexual contract and Mills's racial contract — to recast antifat bias as a systematic breach of the social contract enforced by medicine (hallway weigh-ins, weight lectures instead of care), employment, transit seating, and TV fat jokes. Against Atkins's medical discourse of the 'obesity epidemic' she assembles Health at Every Size evidence, trans-fat and high-fructose corn syrup data, and the documented health damage of stigma and dieting itself, concluding that Atkins profits from recasting social problems as individual failings. Atkins for Life's success stories (Kerry Feather's volleyball and new husband, Luann Lockhart's proud daughter) are read as testimony that dieting works as ritual self-abasement purchasing group membership — hence Fat Liberation's 'another world is possible.'

social-contract.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
social-contract.title: Resistance Raps
social-contract.relation: James reads hardcore and underground rap - N.W.A's "F*** Tha Police", Ice-T's "Cop Killer", Dead Prez's "Police State" sampling Omali Yeshitela, Tupac's "Dear Mama" with its Panther 21/Cointelpro footage, Michael Franti's "Crime to Be Broke in America" - through Hobbes's Leviathan to argue that for criminalized black communities the social contract never held, so policing is not aberrational protection but the foundation of a police state. She distinguishes rebellion from revolution, argues capital converts the underground's insurgence into marketable alienation, faults hardcore's misogyny and policing of women and queers as counter-revolutionary, and concludes that a Leviathan which is the law cannot cohabit with democracy.

social-contract.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
social-contract.title: Post-Civil Rights Music
social-contract.relation: Lawson argues political rap - Grandmaster Flash's "The Message", Public Enemy's "911 Is a Joke", Tupac's "Trapped", Dead Prez's "They Schools", Naughty By Nature, Ice Cube's "I Wanna Kill Sam" - challenges liberal political philosophy by claiming the social contract between blacks and the United States is broken: using Locke's Second Treatise account of state protection of life and property, he contends the state's failure of economic and physical protection voids blacks' political obligations. Drawing on Cornel West's diagnosis of black nihilism and Charles Mills's racial contract - a contract constructed for white supremacy - he reads conscious hip hop as post-civil-rights music continuing the black freedom struggle in a new voice, with KRS-One asking "Who protects us from you?"

social-contract.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
social-contract.title: Reality versus Revolution
social-contract.relation: McPherson argues political rap has never been politically revolutionary, sorting it into three schools: the amoral "gangsta Hobbes" ethic (Mobb Deep's "Survival of the Fittest", 50 Cent's "get rich or die tryin'") that sees the hood as Hobbes's state of nature where no social contract with blacks ever existed; Afrocentric communitarianism, split between nationalist separatists (Brand Nubian, X-Clan, Dead Prez) and the more cosmopolitan Native Tongues (De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest); and a radical liberalism closer to Rawls than its adherents admit. Against Chuck D's "What's a smilin' face when the whole state's racist?", he argues Rawls's original position, veil of ignorance, and difference principle - applied with real-world knowledge of racism - support rather than oppose Public Enemy's demands for racial justice.

social-contract.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
social-contract.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Alford reads the biker image, born at Hollister in 1947 and fixed by The Wild One, through two opposed accounts of presocial man: the badass on his tricked-out Harley is Hobbes's natural man, all vanity, domination, and fear merely redirected to government, praising Chuck Zito's 'most primitive philosophy'; the club run with bonfire, brothers, old ladies, and Steppenwolf re-enacts Rousseau's golden age between the stupidity of brutes and the fatal enlightenment of civil man, before the first enclosed field ('this is mine') bred property, vanity, and misery. The paradox of a biker who is simultaneously threat and salvation dissolves once we see that 'primitive' and 'civilized' are mutually defining: suburbanites and bikers alike live both Hobbesian individualism and Rousseauvian community, each defining themselves against the other.

social-contract.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
social-contract.title: Poker and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Stoehr finds Hobbes in the saloon: poker in classic Westerns — Hatfield's farewell game in Stagecoach, and the cheating scene where Wyatt Earp first crosses Doc Holliday in My Darling Clementine — dramatizes the tension between the lawless state of nature ('solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short') and the rule-governed community built by an implicit social contract, with caught cheaters (Chihuahua signaling hole cards) marking where play reverts to primal vengeance. Poker itself is a Hobbesian paradox: a communal social event built on winner-takes-all competition, exercising both logic and intuition within luck's hard limits. The morally ambiguous Fordian hero — Doc Holliday above all — lives at the same crossroads of civilization and wilderness as the card table.

social-contract.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
social-contract.title: No Way Out
social-contract.relation: Leah Murray reads Romero's Dead series as an argument about the American social contract, individualism versus communitarianism. Night of the Living Dead's farmhouse is Hobbes: fear throws strangers Ben and Mr. Cooper into a makeshift commonwealth whose individualist half ('every man for himself' in the basement) fails, while Dawn shows the Hobbesian next step - martial law as Leviathan - after the state of nature returns. Land of the Dead's Fiddler's Green is a fear-born contract corrupting into Kaufman's hierarchy, and Big Daddy's zombies form the counter-model, a Rousseauian community of the general will based on mutual bonds rather than terror, as the priest in Dawn already urged ('we must stop the killing... or lose the war'). Following Tocqueville on civic association, she concludes Romero's survivors - Ben, Peter, Sarah, Riley - vindicate communitarian cooperation, even though Night's bureaucratic ending suggests there may be no way out.

social-contract.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
social-contract.title: James Bond and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Forster stages the dispute between Dr. No ('just a stupid policeman') and Scaramanga ('we are the same') over whether Bond's license to kill betrays the liberal rule of law it protects, connecting it to post-9/11 debates about executive power. He gives the rule of law a substantive ground in Locke's Two Treatises - prerogative power may suspend particular laws for the public good of preserving the community ('salus populi suprema lex'), illustrated by Locke's own career conspiring with Lord Ashley's spy network - and a procedural check in the separation of powers, mirrored in MI6's real parliamentary and judicial oversight. Both elements together, he concludes, let Bond's extra-legal work remain consistent with the rule of law: power exercised for the public good under institutional supervision, without which M's vendetta in 'For Your Eyes Only' would be indistinguishable from Scaramanga's contracts.

social-contract.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
social-contract.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
social-contract.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors' beach as a "framed" state of nature: the stolen water is a tragedy of the commons, Sawyer's "finders keepers" defense of Shannon's inhalers stages Hobbes's war of all against all against Locke's natural rights, and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward civil society, a claim to punish on another's behalf. He argues no theory of human nature (Rousseau's "Innocence" versus a "Trust No. 1" attitude) is needed to understand the castaways: cooperation grows through iterated prisoner's-dilemma tit-for-tat strategies, which also recasts the real difference between Hobbesian and Lockean states of nature.

social-contract.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
social-contract.title: Why Be Moral
social-contract.relation: Sanders uses Bruno Anthony's 'criss-cross' murder-swap proposal to Guy Haines in Strangers on a Train to pose the classic question 'Why be moral?' to the charming amoralist. He tests three answers: Kant's categorical imperative fails because Bruno's egoist maxim ('remove obstacles to your happiness') can apparently be universalized; Hobbesian contractarian 'morality pays' fails because Bruno free-rides on others' restraint; and the Rachels/Nelson/Thomas psychological-health answer assumes rather than proves that Bruno should care about comparable suffering. A thought experiment comparing the moral life with the Bruno-state from an impartial standpoint leads to Aristotle's eudaimonia: morality is constitutive of human flourishing, so Bruno enjoys only a counterfeit happiness.

social-contract.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
social-contract.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
social-contract.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. He reads the total improvisation learned at the Acid Tests ('the form that follows chaos'), the band's leaderless 'functional anarchy' — Lesh: if anyone tried to take charge 'it would just dissolve in their hands' — and its flat business hierarchy with roadies as corporate presidents as a spontaneous order lived at the edge of chaos. The Deadhead community's ritual communitas, analyzed through Victor Turner's separation-liminality-reincorporation model, amounts to an 'ironic sacramentalism' that achieves what social contract from Hobbes (force), Locke (property), and Rawls (self-interest) cannot: unity that transcends difference while leaving it in place.

social-contract.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
social-contract.title: Don’t Get Into One
social-contract.relation: Richard Greene renames the Tarantino standoff the 'ex-convict's dilemma' and models it as a special case of the prisoner's dilemma, running from Ordell and Louis's separate interrogation rooms to the White–Pink, Joe–White–Eddie and True Romance shoot-outs. He argues the standard group-rationality solution fails because ECDS participants have conflicting goals—Eddie protecting his father, White protecting Orange, Joe wanting revenge—and his survey of Tarantino's six cases shows escapes come from luck (Mr. Blonde's entrance, Nikki coming home) or shared interests (Beatrix's pregnancy), never group rationality. Tracing the dilemma back to Glaucon's contract argument in Plato's Republic, he concludes the only reliable solution is: don't get into one.

social-contract.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
social-contract.title: You May Wonder How Come I Love You Care and Ethics
social-contract.relation: Gimbel asks what the E Street Band's marathon multiple encores mean, starting from social contract theory: Hobbes's state of nature ('no home, no job, no peace, no rest') and Locke's contract explain the ticket as a financial IOU — so a drunk, short Hendrix show wrongs you financially but not morally — while the contractual view of moral duty (the 'Hungry Heart' narrator who abandoned his wife and kids in Baltimore) cannot explain why a missing encore feels like personal betrayal. The gift theory fails too, since encores are expected, and expected things are not gifts. Care ethics (Ruddick, Noddings) fits instead: devoted fans make the band part of their identity, Springsteen sings 'to you about you,' and the No Nukes 90-minute set became permanent because he would not give his people less — while 'Pink Cadillac' shows the limit case, since you cannot love someone for her Cadillac.

social-contract.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
social-contract.title: Walking the Tightrope
social-contract.relation: Louis Melancon weighs the Fleet leadership's secrets and lies: Adama's 'blind squirrel' lie about Earth, classifying the fact that Cylons look human, Roslin's faked death of the baby Hera, and Tom Zarek's secret collaboration courts on New Caprica. Democratic duty is framed as a deontological obligation of transparency grounded in the governed's trust, while the leadership repeatedly defaults to consequentialist wartime exceptions. The chapter proposes a rule-of-thumb: secrecy is justified only to hide specific information from an external threat like the Cylons, never to protect the government from its own citizens, and each violation erodes the trust on which Colonial democracy's 'soul' depends.

social-contract.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
social-contract.title: No Way Out
social-contract.relation: Leah Murray argues Romero's Dead films stage the American contest between individualism and communitarianism inside the social contract: in Night of the Living Dead, communitarian Ben barricading the farmhouse against every-man-for-himself Mr. Cooper hiding in the basement; in Dawn of the Dead, the Peter-Roger-Fran-Stephen mall commune collapsing when Stephen's 'it's ours, we took it' meets the bikers; in Day of the Dead, Sarah's compassion against the racist, harassing soldiers; in Land of the Dead, Kaufman's Fiddler's Green as a Hobbesian Leviathan born of fear, complete with bread-and-circuses for the poor. Against the Hobbesian fear-born contract (Dawn opens in a full state-of-nature collapse) she sets Rousseau's general will and Tocqueville's civic association, embodied in Riley's freely formed community and in Big Daddy's zombies, who organize, turn from eating humans, and bring down the Leviathan. The films' verdict: fear-based individualist contracts collapse under their own contradictions, while compassionate cooperation — even among the Undead — is the only way out, even if Romero doubts its ultimate viability.

social-contract.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
social-contract.title: A Phenomenology of Reading the Ref
social-contract.relation: Vannatta asks what the rules of soccer are from a player's perspective and tests legal theories: natural law and Rawls's veil of ignorance are too abstract to help on the pitch, and Austin's and Hart's positivism overemphasizes FIFA's top-down commands, so the best account is legal pragmatism — Holmes's bad man treats the law as a prophecy of what the ref will actually call, and Dewey roots the rules in custom and in the whistle itself rather than in prior legislation. Husserl's genetic phenomenology then explains how 'reading the ref' is possible: retention and protention synthesized in passive synthesis let experienced players anticipate play — and the referee's tendencies — without deliberation, replacing the impoverished notion of muscle memory. Playing to the whistle becomes a trainable skill of predicting an indeterminate despot, with lessons for coaching and sportsmanship alike.

social-contract.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
social-contract.title: Is Fencing a Dishonorable Art
social-contract.relation: Michaud argues that fencing is the loneliest and most egoistic martial art: alone on the strip, you seek to understand your opponent only in order to deceive them through disengages and parry-feints. He maps the bout onto Hobbes: psychological egoism, the dueling ground as a state of nature of 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short', and the referee as the Leviathan whose rules keep the bloodshed out while licensing normative egoism inside them. Testing defenses from Rand, Friedman and Carr's business 'rules of the game', he concludes that fencing kept its soldier's anything-goes ethos after the lethal stakes vanished, making it a 'dishonorable' art: a Hobbesian feast of solitude, egoism and deception.

social-contract.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
social-contract.title: This Is the Age of Steel
