social-contract.relation: Innes unpacks the double meaning of 'revolting': punk's obscenity, three-minute seven-inch singles on independent labels, beer-can-and-burrito gigs at Randy's Rodeo, and Vivienne Westwood bondage wear are revolt in the original sense - and a revival of Diogenes's cynicism, which rejects Plato's abstract virtue and the Glaucon-style social contract (the Ring of Gyges showing justice is only for the visible) for virtue according to nature. Hippies and prog rock are the sold-out establishment (Dead Kennedys' 'California Über Alles' against Jerry Brown), and satire - Johnny Rotten's lit lamp searching for an honest man - is the Cynic's serious joke, ending in chosen, communal virtue.

social-contract.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
social-contract.title: 5. The Sovereign State of Salamanca
social-contract.relation: Barta and Barnes read the show's Court and Cartel as parallel Hobbesian sovereigns. The New Mexico desert and the criminalized drug trade function as Hobbes's state of nature—lawless, where Nacho robs thieves who 'have no recourse' and Mike sticks up a mule with a garden hose—illustrating natural equality (a small man can kill a big one) and the war of all against all. From mutual fear, deals emerge (Mike and Gus's desert standoff, Mike keeping his word over twenty dollars), but 'covenants without the sword' need a Common Power: Tuco, Hector, Lalo, and ultimately Don Eladio form a feudal hierarchy enforcing loyalty by terror, just as the state's police monopoly on force sustains the Law.

social-contract.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
social-contract.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
social-contract.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors of Lost as a real state of nature, playing on the characters named Locke, Rousseau, and Hume. The scarce-water and asthma-inhaler disputes are 'tragedies of the commons,' and Sawyer's 'finders keepers' embodies a Hobbesian 'Trust No. 1' while Hurley and Jack lean toward Rousseauian 'Innocence.' Using game theory's repeated prisoners' dilemma and 'tit-for-tat,' Davies argues a Lockean state of nature (opening with cooperation) rather than a doomed Hobbesian one lets the survivors build a commonwealth against the Others.

social-contract.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
social-contract.title: NOTES
social-contract.relation: Richard Davies analyzes the post-crash survivors as living in a genuine 'state of nature' and grades its severity by how scarce the contested good is (the water shortage as a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers versus Sawyer's 'possession is nine-tenths'). He compares Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau on human nature — labeling the poles 'Innocence' (Hurley, Rousseau, Hume) and 'Trust No 1' (Sawyer, Hobbes) — and uses the repeated prisoners' dilemma and the tit-for-tat strategy to argue that the castaways build a Lockean civil society by signaling through shared language and cooperating first, while the discovery of the Others (Ethan) triggers Hobbesian non-cooperation.

social-contract.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
social-contract.title: NOTES
social-contract.relation: Peter S. Fosl argues that Lost pretends to a liberal social order — Jack rising by consent in a Lockean scheme of natural rights, Rousseau's general will ('live together, die alone'), and Hume's sympathy and pity binding the survivors — but that its treatment of the Others betrays a darker politics. Reading the survivor/Other conflict through Carl Schmitt's friend-enemy thesis (notably absent Hobbes), he contends the show, like post-9/11 America, needs an enemy to exterminate, and that the finale's Jacob/Man-in-Black war and Jack's Christlike sacrificial death repudiate the Kantian liberal ideal of persons as ends, resolving conflict through Schmittian and Christian redemptive violence instead.

social-contract.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
social-contract.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Torosyan argues that The Daily Show models critical thinking and postmodern self-awareness, using Stewart's interviews to show how to reframe debate and act in good faith. He reads Stewart's demand that news media serve the public through Rousseau's social contract, casts scaremongering politicians as following Machiavelli's advice to 'learn how not to be good,' invokes Gadamer's hermeneutics to argue that guests like William Bennett fail to question their own prejudices, and uses Nietzsche's Apollonian/Dionysian tension to explain the show's tragicomic satire (e.g., the 'Smallpox Blankets' joke and Bush reading Camus's The Stranger).

social-contract.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
social-contract.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
social-contract.relation: Vanderheiden reads America (The Book) as a work of democratic theory dressed as textbook parody, arguing its satire is a 'rhetoric of challenge' enacting deliberative democracy. He contrasts 'thin' (merely electoral) with 'thick' participatory democracy using Putnam's social capital and Barber's strong democracy, and invokes J.S. Mill's 'marketplace of ideas' and On Liberty to indict media conglomeration for killing the press's watchdog role. He reads the companion Earth (The Book) through social-contract theory (Hobbes-style), noting its jab that contractual authority historically required the assent of subjugated groups it never obtained.

social-contract.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
social-contract.title: Rebellion in Sala-ma-Sond The Social Contract and a Turtle Named Mack
social-contract.relation: Novy uses King Yertle's tyranny and Mack's revolt to survey social-contract theory. Hobbes explains why turtles leave the war-of-all state of nature for an absolute sovereign, but Yertle, ruling only for himself, becomes 'no king at all'; Locke then justifies overthrowing him because a ruler who destroys his subjects' property and lives dissolves the contract. Kant grounds the contract in innate freedom, while Rawls's original position and veil of ignorance test Sala-ma-Sond for justice as fairness, and King's civil disobedience frames Mack's rights-claiming burp as demanding the contract be honored for all.

social-contract.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
social-contract.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
social-contract.relation: Swindler argues the ideal of fatherhood is to engender autonomy – a blend of independence and interdependence – in one's children. Treating fatherhood as an abstract social role (compared to a baseball pitcher) constituted by collective intentions, he uses Kant's 'ought implies can' to link accountability to autonomy and his constitutive-vs-regulative rules (the promise to take his son fishing) to show fathers must teach children to reflect on the concept of a rule, not merely follow it, modeling self-governance rather than authoritarian control.

social-contract.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
social-contract.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
social-contract.relation: Colyvan applies mathematics and game theory to mating: the 'secretary problem' yields the optimal strategy of dating and rejecting the first n/e (~37%) of candidates then taking the next best, and Rousseau's stag hunt models monogamy as cooperation (hunt stag = stay faithful) tempted by defection (hunt hare = an affair), with the prisoner's dilemma showing why individual rationality can undermine the Pareto-optimal cooperative outcome. He argues that iterated games and tit-for-tat strategies, plus the 'shadow of the future' and public commitments like weddings, make faithfulness explicable purely by narrow self-interest, quoting Hume on reciprocal service, and suggests love and ethics themselves may be useful fictions layered over the game.

social-contract.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
social-contract.title: Hobbes, Human Nature, and the Culture of American Violence in Truman Capote's In Cold Blood
social-contract.relation: Thomas Fahy reads Capote's In Cold Blood as horror (the Clutter killers Hickock and Smith as 'realistic monsters' whose human shape terrifies because anyone could be like them) and maps it onto Hobbes's Leviathan. Hickock and Smith act in a Hobbesian state of nature, driven by appetite, power, and moral relativism without remorse. Herb Clutter functions as a Hobbesian sovereign whose Eden-like farm and community collapse into decay, mistrust, and 'war of all against all' after his murder. Fahy also casts Capote himself as a sovereign who, via Foucault's panopticon, imposes a fictionalized cathartic ending, though the book's Hobbesian message is that we all have the potential to kill.

social-contract.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
social-contract.title: 6. Hollow Man
social-contract.relation: Rowlands reads Hollow Man as a retelling of Plato's Ring of Gyges, posing 'why be moral?' once the invisible Kevin Bacon can act without sanction. He rejects the religious answer and Hobbesian social-contract theory (both reduce morality to prudence/fear of punishment and leave those outside the contract unprotected), and Hume's fellow-feeling as mere causal explanation not justification. He examines Kant's Categorical Imperative reducing immorality to inconsistency but argues it cannot answer 'why should I be moral,' concluding the choice is arational self-definition, closing with Nietzsche's 'become what you are' and the deed at the bottom of morality.

social-contract.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
social-contract.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
social-contract.relation: Davies analyzes Lost's Oceanic 815 survivors as a genuine state of nature, playing off the characters named Locke, Rousseau, and Hume. He distinguishes Rousseau's compassionate "Innocence" from a Hobbesian "Trust No. 1" (Sawyer hoarding), tracks "tragedies of the commons" over water and Shannon's inhalers, and Jack and Sayid's move toward Lockean punishment and civil society. Using game theory's prisoners' dilemma and tit-for-tat, he argues cooperation emerges when survivors, discovering the Others, resolve to "act as one body" and form a commonwealth.

social-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
social-contract.title: 6. Black Sails as Philosophy Pirates and Political Discourse
social-contract.relation: Jones argues that Starz's Black Sails, a Treasure Island prequel set in the Golden Age of Piracy, dramatizes social contract theory as non-hypothetical practice. Captain Flint's drive to make Nassau a sovereign pirate commonwealth ('I am your king') channels Hobbes's state of nature and irrepressible sovereign, while his choice to settle Nassau and belief that people can thrive if left free channels Locke; his eventual plan to install Silver and Madi as liked-and-feared leaders synthesizes the two. Jones maps the pirates' familial bonds onto Rousseau and their responses to injustice (Vane's gallows speech, the maroon alliance) onto Rawls's Veil of Ignorance, and reads pirate 'articles' and deposable captains as radical democracy and equality, complicated by manipulation, slavery, and tolerance.

social-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
social-contract.title: 12. Firefly as Philosophy Social Contracts, Political Dissent, and Virtuous Communities
social-contract.relation: Kowalski argues that Firefly and Serenity embody a distinctive political theory he calls 'Since I Found Serenity' (SIFS). The mindless, savage Reavers represent Hobbes's state of nature, showing government is necessary; but the Alliance's torture of River, the Miranda/Pax atrocity, and the murderous blue-gloved agents and Operative make a Hobbesian reading untenable and vindicate Locke's natural rights and right of revolution — Mal's 'I aim to misbehave' broadcast of the Miranda file is Lockean civil disobedience. He then presses the tacit-consent problem (the Browncoats cannot leave the 'Verse) and supplements Locke with Aristotle's friendship and community: Serenity's crew becomes a virtuous mobile commonwealth where friendship (Simon forgiving Jayne, Mal's 'love keeps her in the air') turns a commonwealth into a good-life community.

social-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
social-contract.title: 16. House of Cards as Philosophy Democracy on Trial
social-contract.relation: The chapter uses the Underwoods' extra-electoral rise to autocracy in House of Cards to test Plato's and Hobbes's antidemocratic arguments. Frank and Claire exploit the exact weaknesses Plato's Republic diagnoses—Thrasymachus's 'justice is the advantage of the stronger,' the decay of oligarchy into freedom-loving democracy into tyranny, and Peter Russo as the disordered-soul 'democratic man' and 'drone.' It then invokes Hobbes's Leviathan, arguing the show's power-struggle resembles a state of nature and that Hobbes would welcome Claire's absolute rule as more predictable and less corrupt than democracy, before weighing modern defenses of democracy (Levitsky and Ziblatt, Locke, Mill, Rawls, Sen) against these critiques.

social-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
social-contract.title: 24. Game of Thrones as Philosophy Cynical Realpolitiks
social-contract.relation: The chapter argues that Game of Thrones advances a thoroughgoing cynicism about political legitimacy, captured by Varys's riddle that 'power resides where men believe it resides.' It documents the dubious claims of Robert 'the Usurper' and the pyromaniacal Daenerys, the barbaric Lockean 'state of nature' among the Wildlings, and the false ideals of chivalry and religion, with Littlefinger and Varys voicing Machiavellian realpolitik. Silverman and Riordan then offer two views the show never considers: Locke's social-contract theory of natural rights (which would justify deposing Aerys or Daenerys) and Aquinas's four-part test for genuine law (reason, common good, proper authority, promulgation), arguing a legitimate state remains possible against the show's cynicism.

social-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
social-contract.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
social-contract.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable. He tests the orchestrated revolution against utilitarianism's greatest-happiness principle (Bentham, Mill's taxation-of-the-wealthy, Singer's impartiality) and against Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle versus Nozick's entitlement objection and Aquinas's just-war criteria, concluding each character's actions can be read as 'just,' which exposes anthropocentrism as the real veil.

social-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
social-contract.title: 92. V for Vendetta as Philosophy Victory Through the Virtues of Anarchy
social-contract.relation: Nisley argues that Moore and Lloyd's V for Vendetta justifies V's violent rebellion against the Norsefire regime through Locke: the fascist state seized power without consent, tortured and experimented on citizens (V at Larkhill), and violated natural rights, thereby placing itself in a state of war so the people may overthrow it. Using Aristotle on deviant constitutions and the beast-like tyrant (Adam Susan) who lacks practical wisdom, and contrasting Locke's tolerable state of nature with Hobbes's brutal one, the chapter concludes the citizens should rebuild a rights-protecting social contract rather than V's leaderless anarchy, and maps the argument onto real-world 2020 events (BLM riots vs. the Whitmer kidnapping plot).

catharsis.book: 007 - The Sopranos and Philosophy - I Kill Therefore I Am
catharsis.title: The Sopranos and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Argues Season One is an Aristotelian tragedy: Tony is the 'man in-between' who earns pity and fear, and his tragic flaw is not his sins but his inability to bear his conflicting family roles, manifest in the panic attacks that drive him into therapy. Like Oedipus fleeing Corinth, the cure brings the catastrophe - Livia exposes the therapy to Junior and the hit follows ('Cunnilingus and psychiatry brought us to this') - while the plot maps onto Greek family tragedy, Livia as Medea trying to kill her son and Tony as a failed Orestes. The Green Grove FBI tapes are the recognition scene, the loss of mother and uncle is the reversal, and catharsis is the healthy outward purging of the viewer's own bottled emotion.

catharsis.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
catharsis.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Irwin defends the film's violence aesthetically: beauty (Michelangelo's Pietà) distracts from moral truth rather than serving it, and Aristotle's Poetics fits the film neither as tragedy (a flawless Christ cannot fall through hamartia, and a good man's fall from prosperity is 'repulsive', so no catharsis explains why we watch) nor as the Plato-banned spectacle that inflames the passions, since it leaves viewers numb rather than belligerent. Instead he applies Cynthia Freeland's four features of the cinematic sublime, drawn from Burke and Kant: the flogging scenes, the grotesque Satan clutching his deformed child, Judas harried by demon-children to suicide, and even the Aramaic and Latin subtitles produce the pain-pleasure conflict, overwhelming vastness, and jolt from feeling to moral reflection that make the experience sublime. The violence is thus justified as Gibson's deliberate delivery of the sublime, provided viewers leave fear at the gates.

catharsis.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
catharsis.title: (Positive) Violence of Self-Discipline
catharsis.relation: Shusterman opens with Plato and Socrates' ancient quarrel against poetry - banning the artists from the Republic, much as rap is demonized today - and rejects Aristotle's catharsis strategy of quarantining art from life, applying pragmatist aesthetics (Dewey, James, and the Du Bois-Alain Locke lineage) to argue that rap's aesthetic violence of beat, scratch, and "Bring the Noise" is life-enhancing force, with reality rap's metaphysics of mix and flow against Plato's changeless Forms. Reading KRS-One's "Stop the Violence" movement born from Scott LaRock's killing, Guru's "Choice of Weapons" (a mic or a gun), and Jeru the Damaja's command to "kill in thyself", he concludes rap overcomes bad violence not by abolishing violence but by channeling it into lyrical battle and the positive violence of self-discipline.

catharsis.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
catharsis.title: U2 and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Werther answers Tollefsen with Aristotle's Politics: musical images of character effect real 'change[s] of soul', so a three-premise argument concludes that repeated exposure to U2's images of fine character and good action can habituate delight in virtue - King's courage in 'Pride (In the Name of Love)' (whatever the botched time of day, and as proved when Adam Clayton stepped between Bono and an FBI-confirmed death threat), the indignation and shame at global poverty in 'Crumbs from Your Table', and the compassion of 'Miracle Drug' for the locked-in writer Christopher Nolan. 'Exit' purges the band's demons and 'Until the End of the World' offers purification through holy fear, matching the medical and religious readings of Aristotelian catharsis. C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man closes the case: without the aid of trained emotions the intellect is powerless, so a culture raised on U2's feelings may be better prepared to act well than one raised on syllogisms alone.

catharsis.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
catharsis.title: Curtain Down
catharsis.relation: Silberstein reads Rear Window as a self-reflexive film about film-watching: the shades rise like a curtain, the courtyard apartments play like frames on a filmstrip, and wheelchair-bound Jeff with his binoculars is the movie spectator - the courtyard is Plato's cave and we are the chained prisoners watching shadows (copies of copies of the forms). The chapter stages the Plato-versus-Aristotle debate over imitative art from Republic Book X and the Poetics, then argues the film vindicates both: Jeff's voyeurism breeds detachment and misjudgment (he misreads Lisa, Miss Torso, the composer and the newlyweds), yet the same watching awakens - the song 'Lisa' saves Miss Lonelyhearts from suicide, Thorwald is brought to justice, and Jeff and the audience leave the theater wiser about fantasy, boredom and their own lives.

catharsis.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
catharsis.title: Le temps de me laver les mains, or Bathroom Loyalties
catharsis.relation: Randall Auxier reads Pulp Fiction's scrambled sequence through Bergson's distinction between clock time and lived, experienced time and through Aristotle's Poetics: Tarantino toys with the three unities to make viewers attend to every character, and only when the film is re-sequenced does it become 'Vinnie's Very Bad Day'. Vincent's fatal flaw is Aristotle's incontinence—weakness of will—signaled by the running bathroom gag and his unwashed hands, while Jules and Butch pass the same moral test of loyalty, whether delivering the briefcase or saving Marsellus from Zed. The moral: be loyal, don't be weak-willed, and wash your hands thoroughly, since in Tarantino nothing lacks perceptible difference.

catharsis.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
catharsis.title: Lonesome Day
catharsis.relation: Calef asks how fictional story-songs can teach: lyrics yield neither know-how nor know-that, since Plato's Theaetetus shows true belief is not knowledge (the 'Meeting Across the River' narrator's plan works only by luck). The answer is a third kind — knowing what something is like: 'The River' lets a comfortable listener inhabit Mary's husband's slide into a dry marriage, and 'Nebraska' lets us feel Starkweather's numb void, 'what it's like to have no soul.' Aristotle's Poetics (we delight in imitation because learning pleases; poetry is more philosophic than history because it speaks in universals) explains why sad songs satisfy us, and Sartre's universal human condition grounds the empathy that makes The Rising render 9/11 ('You're Missing,' 'Empty Sky') thinkable at a personal scale.

catharsis.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
catharsis.title: Where Tragedy Ends and Community Begins
catharsis.relation: Lott takes up Augustine's puzzle about why we enjoy watching sufferings we would flee, and answers for Radiohead with Aristotle's theory of tragedy: songs like 'Karma Police', 'Exit Music', and 'Fake Plastic Trees' sketch fragmentary characters in breakdown whose undeserved yet partly self-inflicted sufferings — 'Just'''s 'you do it to yourself' is hamartia — evoke pity and fear and then catharsis. Singing along makes identification uniquely intense in pop ('for a minute there, I lost myself' blurs the listener into the character), while music's 'natural sweetness' and its dynamics of build, climax, and release carry the purgation, from the terror of 'Climbing Up the Walls' to the slow ache of 'Videotape'. Because tragedy, unlike history, deals in universals, songs like 'The Bends' and 'High and Dry' open onto reflection on happiness, vulnerability, and the culture that fosters isolation, ending in the thin but real community of listeners who recognize their shared fragility.

catharsis.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
catharsis.title: Mr. Monk, Jungle Guide
catharsis.relation: Kagan reads Monk through Ernest Becker's Denial of Death: everyone is born hyper-aware like Monk and learns 'how not to see', managing the terror of the jungle out there through denial, shopping, and hero systems, which is why Randy Disher can ride in a cab driven by a corpse without noticing. Monk, who cannot forget (his nudity phobia traced to the trauma of his own birth in 'Mr. Monk and the Naked Man'), is our funhouse mirror and, like the Buddha seeing the four sights of sickness, old age, death, and the renunciant, he re-enters the world after Trudy's death to guide us through it. Aristotle's catharsis explains the pleasure of watching: pity and fear are burned off as Monk, more afraid than we are, still pursues truth and justice.

catharsis.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
catharsis.title: Textually Transmitted Disease
catharsis.relation: Traces hentai from Hokusai's 'Diver and Two Octopi' through the 1920s eroguro journals to the Lolita Anime and Cream Lemon OVAs, then asks whether even this extreme material has value as fantasy. The chapter frames the media-effects debate with Aristotle's Poetics catharsis (revived by Feshbach and tentatively supported by Milton Diamond's finding that Japanese rape rates fell as pornography spread) against Plato's Republic worry that sensational works license irrationality (updated by the Disinhibition, Desensitization, and Cultivation theories), and concludes that hentai's real harm is attitudinal rather than behavioral: its ritual 'breaking' of strong women and sex-as-something-done-to-passive-girls cultivates misogyny and a dehumanizing view of sex.

catharsis.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
catharsis.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Greg Littmann stages Plato's hypothetical review of American Gods under the Republic's charges against poetry: the novel is full of 'greatest of all lies' about gods behaving badly, from Odin and Loki's sacrificial plot to Czernobog's head-smashing, gods degrading themselves into lesser forms like Horus the road-kill-eating hawk and Media as Lucille Ball, and characters ruled by passion rather than reason, from Mad Sweeney drinking himself to death to Thor's suicide, corrupting a soul that should be governed by rationality. Against this he sets Aristotle's Poetics: listening to music and intellectual leisure are valuable in themselves, fiction is more philosophic than history because it shows what could happen, the impossible is justified when it astounds, and catharsis through pity for figures like the weeping Mad Sweeney purges rather than corrupts. Because American Gods' absurd premise unfolds with internally probable, character-consistent events (loyal Shadow, loving Laura, grifter Odin), it satisfies Aristotle's requirement that fantasy make artistic sense.

catharsis.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
catharsis.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Explains why we believe a chemistry teacher could become a drug lord by reading Walt through Shakespeare's Macbeth with Aristotle's Poetics: drama must make a particular psychology feel universal, so interiority - here Walt's wounded masculinity (the veggie bacon, Hank's 'that's why they hire men', post-murder aggression toward Skyler) - supplies the hamartia of insecure pride. The chapter tracks Aristotle's reversals (crime restores manliness while breeding shame, driving ever more viciousness), casts Jesse as Walt's Lady Macbeth and Walt as his own Macduff, and reads the staged psychiatry lie as Walt deceiving himself about resenting his family. It predicts that if the show is Aristotelian tragedy, Walt's final reversal will come from a recognition, with cancer as the evil he embraces 'in' him and catharsis our pity and fear.

catharsis.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
catharsis.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Littmann answers the charge that D&D is a waste of time with Aristotle: pleasure is good as an end in itself, humanity's function is thinking, so even munchkin power-gaming and 4E combat roles are worthwhile intellectual activity under the function argument. He then treats D&D as participatory art—improvisational storytelling offering catharsis (smacking goblins to purge aggression) and the Poetics' license to explore what could be, like the dwarf chieftain grieving a disintegrated son or deciding what a friend owes the thief in the scorpion nest. A good DM, on this Aristotelian view, makes plots unfold with internal probability and characters act from consistent personality, yet 'just playing my character' never excuses ruining another player's fun, since artistic value never suspends the virtues governing how we treat people.

catharsis.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
catharsis.title: The Devil and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Liz Stillwaggon Swan explains why crime dramas like Criminal Minds, CSI, and Bones are so watchable: Jung's shadow archetype and collective unconscious mean the Devil in human form on screen taps humanity's shared dark layer, while Aristotle's catharsis lets viewers experience pity and fear safely from the couch, identifying with characters like repulsed Garcia or intellectualizing Dr. Brennan. She adds the CSI effect - jurors with warped expectations of DNA and fingerprint work - and argues the shows satisfy a deep need to see devils like Bundy and Dahmer caught within a tidy forty-three minutes.

catharsis.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
catharsis.title: 3. There’s Only One God and His Name Is Death
catharsis.relation: McKeever observes that central characters rarely die suddenly and unexpectedly in art even though such deaths define our emotional lives, and argues this is a 'representational limit of art,' like Hollywood ugliness and costume-drama archaic speech. Using Plato's theory of art as a copy of a copy (a picture of Tyrion's chipped goblet imitating the Form of the goblet) and Aristotle's catharsis, he then argues Martin overcomes the limit through epic scale: with so many viewpoint characters, Ned can die at the end of season one and Joffrey mid-season-four because attention simply shifts, so making a work epic is the general cure for what art cannot represent.

catharsis.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
catharsis.title: 1. I Stand Up Next to a Mountain
catharsis.relation: Reads Hendrix as Joseph Campbell's hero on the monomyth of separation, initiation, and return: the mother's death and gypsy prophecy of 'Voodoo Chile' stage the separation, the Venus witch's ring the initiation, and the transcending guitar solo the return, with Prometheus as the type of the fire-bringer punished by promoters, Little Richard, and audiences demanding the hits. Through Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy it casts the Monterey guitar-burning and the Dionysian intensity of the Experience as tragic art whose hero 'shoulders the whole Dionysiac world for us,' and closes with Aristotle's Politics on catharsis — 'Machine Gun''s sonic battle imagery as purgation that transforms violence into a cry for peace.

catharsis.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
catharsis.title: 6. Horror Can Be Great Drama
catharsis.relation: Applies Aristotle's Poetics wholesale - mimesis of possible actions, the six elements of tragedy, complete plots of proper magnitude, reversal and recognition, hamartia, and catharsis as the perfecting of fear and pity - to argue that Murder House (Ben's lust as tragic flaw and his double reversal to redemption in death) and Asylum (Sister Jude's irascibility and pride punished then reformed) are genuine high tragedies, and then uses the Nicomachean Ethics (virtue as a mean between extremes; justice as both retributive and rehabilitative) to show the seasons teach virtue, while Coven, Freak Show, and Hotel fall short because their characters' fates are undeserved and the moral message goes murky.

catharsis.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
catharsis.title: 13. Reason and Catharsis
catharsis.relation: Argues that Twin Peaks frees viewers from the "tyranny of rationality" by refusing to make sense: Plato's sensible-versus-intelligible finger example explains our habit of abstracting concepts to resolve contradiction (the pale horse in the living room, Diane's texts, Dougie-as-tulpa), but Lynch keeps adding facts — the frog-moth crawling into the girl in Part 8 — that no framework absorbs. Drawing on Nietzsche's Twilight of the Idols claim that Socrates made rationality a treatment for weakness, and on the existentialist pairing of despair and freedom in a meaningless universe, the chapter says viewers can either demand the irrational fit their rationality like inauthentic existentialists or let go. Trela's alternative reading of Aristotle's catharsis — emotions purged of their connection to reality and felt for once in themselves — explains why we can savor the show's absurdity without despair, precisely because that world is not ours.

catharsis.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
catharsis.title: Westworld and the Power of Catharsis
catharsis.relation: Baldini argues Westworld revives ancient Greek tragedy in sci-fi Western form: the hosts' loops, repeated scenes with small variations, player-piano score, and kennings ('the lady with the white shoes') echo rhapsodic epic technique, while the hosts' awakening follows Aeschylus's pathei mathos - learning through suffering - since reveries are 'the misery of pain recalled' and grief is the cornerstone of consciousness (Dolores's 'spaces opening up inside of me'). Heraclitus's panta rhei frames the hosts' second awakening to time and becoming ('When are we?', the greyhound that catches the prey and is lost), with death as the final grief they must understand to be free. She reads Ford as a second Prometheus who deliberately lets his creatures grow through suffering, Dolores's finale speech as a modern Theogony of succession, and the show's whole design - steering viewer sympathy to the hosts, as Nolan and Abrams describe - as an Aristotelian catharsis purging pity and fear.

catharsis.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
catharsis.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
catharsis.relation: Greg Littmann imagines Aristotle auditioning for Black Sabbath in 1970 to argue the band satisfies the Poetics and Politics: music that gives pleasure, even the "perverted modes" working-class audiences enjoy, is legitimate art, and Sabbath's darkness works as catharsis, purging fear and pity as Greek tragedy did through Oedipus, the doomed figure in black of "Black Sabbath", the betrayed and ignored Iron Man, and the hopeless narrator of "Paranoid". Songs like "War Pigs", "Electric Funeral", and "Children of the Grave" also do what Aristotle says poetry does better than history, imagining alternative futures that spur citizens to political thought, while the band's drug lore maps onto the Aristotelian mean: beer and a little weed yes, heroin and cocaine never, and Ozzy's firing shows the price of intemperance.

catharsis.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
catharsis.title: Notes
catharsis.relation: Against the complaint that Fallout 3 is just Morrowind or Oblivion with a post-apocalyptic coat of paint, the chapter tests three aesthetic theories. Aristotle's didactic mimesis explains the tragic 'war never changes' framing and its moral lessons about resource wars and the AI president John Henry Eden, while Francis Hutcheson's 'uniformity amidst variety' locates Fallout's fun in the orderly S.P.E.C.I.A.L. rules and the 'crunch' of complex gear and crafting. Clive Bell's formalism finally secures the difference: Vault Boy's atomic-age cartoon style, the Pip-Boy's green monochrome, and the western motifs are formal properties no Elder Scrolls game shares, making Fallout 3 a formally distinct artwork to be appreciated for its own sake.

catharsis.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
catharsis.title: Notes
catharsis.relation: Why is living in Fallout's hell — ghouls pouring through the ceiling, radroach dinners, Kellogg, Pickman, Vault-Tec — fun? The chapter tests the two classic solutions to the puzzle of dark art: Aristotle's katharsis works for Oedipus but stumbles because playing is actively enjoyable rather than unpleasant purgation, and RPGs blur feeling pity for a character with fear for oneself; Hume's 'Of Tragedy' account, on which artistic skill transforms negative emotions into pleasure by mixing them with beauty, fails because the wasteland is deliberately ugly, not beautiful, and Hume never explains how the transformation works. Neither the ancient nor the modern answer quite succeeds, so the 2,500-year-old puzzle is left open, like the best unfinished quests.

catharsis.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
catharsis.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Why do we prefer the narrative where Bjurman handcuffs and rapes Salander to a boring one where Zalachenko is a good father? Rejecting Plato's Republic censorship of disturbing art—which would leave us nothing but nice stories—the chapter applies Aristotle's Poetics: Salander is an imperfect, exaggerated tragic hero whose flaws (defiant independence that keeps her from reporting Bjurman) arouse pity and terror, and reading the trilogy produces catharsis understood, with Nussbaum, as clarification rather than purgation. Thus the rape scenes illuminate how guardianship and power enable men who hate women (Bjurman's 'She had to understand who was in charge,' Martin Vanger's 'godlike feeling'), the heavy-metal concert models safe purgation of anger, and Salander's axing of Zalachenko joins Clytaemnestra's 'man-killing ax' tradition while her tattooed revenge on Bjurman, per Aristotle, yields moral satisfaction rather than tragedy.

catharsis.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
catharsis.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
catharsis.relation: Patterson maps the Comics Code censorship debate onto Plato's Republic Book X, where imitative art is thrice removed from the Forms (the god's table, the carpenter's table, the painter's picture) and feeds the passionate soul, versus Aristotle's Poetics, where imitation is natural and tragedy's pity and fear yield catharsis. The O'Neil-Adams run embodies Aristotle: the slum story where a black tenant asks why Green Lantern helps 'orange skins' and 'purple skins' but never 'black skins,' the Ulysses Star land dispute, and Speedy's heroin addiction broke Code taboos so readers would learn from engagement rather than distance. Within the comic, Hal plays the establishment Platonist who would change an unjust law rather than disobey it and Green Arrow the Aristotelian activist, so their friendship dramatizes the ancient quarrel over whether art corrupts or teaches.

catharsis.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
catharsis.title: Notes
catharsis.relation: Belluomini analyzes how Junkie XL's score drives Fury Road aesthetically. Aristotle's Politics Book 8 and his theory of catharsis explain why the 'Bloodbag' cue's war-drum rhythms imitate the War Boys' anger and fear while purging ours, and 'emotions of appreciation' at the beauty of 'Brothers in Arms' and 'Storm Is Coming' deepen our admiration of the film. Max's cello motif — one, two, or three repeated notes — telegraphs his panic, safety, or menace and advances the plot with almost no dialogue, and Schopenhauer's claim that the right music is a scene's 'most accurate and distinct commentary' fits the hopeful 'Claw Trucks' cue as Max chooses redemption.

catharsis.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
catharsis.title: Notes
catharsis.relation: Littmann asks whether the Mad Max films owe Australians an Australian feel, weighing accents (Theron's Midwestern Furiosa, Hardy's English Max), the Namibian locations of Fury Road, and the franchise's mixed debts to Australian road movies and bushranger lore versus American action cinema. Applying Aristotle's Poetics standard that characters act 'by the rule either of necessity or of probability,' he judges the improbable accents artistic faults that may still be worth their box-office payoff, and notes the saga's international gross grew as its Australianness faded. On representation, he argues that if seeing Australians matters for building sympathy, the same must hold for Indonesians, Pakistanis, and Brazilians — and leaves the question open.

catharsis.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
catharsis.title: Stained Glass Windows in My Mind: Modality in the Imagery of Taylor Swift
catharsis.relation: Reads Swift's imagery as modal logic: David Lewis's counterfactuals distinguish indicative from counterfactual conditionals in 'the 1', Kripke's rigid designators show that 'If I was a man / Then I'd be the man' posits an impossible world (a man could not be Taylor Swift), while 'Would've, Could've, Should've' assigns the counterfactual's antecedent to the perpetrator, not the young narrator. Kierkegaard's 'dizziness of freedom' and despair, with Heidegger's authenticity and das Man, frame counterfactual dwelling as both celebrity performance ('mirrorball') and a route to ownedness, with 'right where you left me' as the delusional extreme and 'it's time to go' as the release. Aristotle's catharsis explains how engaging these might-have-beens in song purges regret for listeners.

catharsis.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
catharsis.title: Exploring The Cabin in the Woods
catharsis.relation: The chapter reads The Cabin in the Woods as Whedon and Goddard doing philosophy: the facility's ritual sacrifice of the five campers is given an explicit utilitarian defense (quoting Mill's greatest-happiness principle) through the Director's plea that Dana kill Marty to avert the apocalypse, which the film ultimately counters through the friends' care-based obligations. Drawing on Nel Noddings's ethics of care and Aristotle's claim that the severity of our duties varies with the closeness of relationships — and on Whedonverse parallels like Buffy refusing to sacrifice Dawn in 'The Gift' — it recasts the ending as an implicit counterargument to classic utilitarianism: Dana does nothing impermissible by refusing to murder her friend, so utilitarianism is false, while Dana's genuine dilemma is deliberately left unresolved in Socratic aporia. It then extends the ethics of care into a theory of the horror genre, reading Whedon's 'inoculation against real fear' as an Aristotelian catharsis that requires relatable characters who care for one another, and takes the film's monitors, two-way mirrors, and voyeurism scenes (Hadley's callousness, the control-room ogling of Jules) as a metalevel invitation to audit our own desensitization to pointless screen suffering.

catharsis.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
catharsis.title: 27. The Filth and the Fury
catharsis.relation: Greg Littmann asks why punk audiences enjoy songs wallowing in misery, boredom, anger, and disgust ('I Wanna Be Well', 'God Save the Queen', 'Bodies'), framing this as the old puzzle of dark art that extends from opera to Game of Thrones. Aristotle supplies the first answer: catharsis - purging pity and fear by feeling them, with Politics Book VIII adding that music relieves the pains of toil - explains why blasting angry punk vents frustration, especially at authority we cannot openly complain about. Hume's 'Of Tragedy' then proposes that artistic beauty converts subordinate negative emotions into intensified pleasure, but Littmann argues the conversion model is incomplete since lesser emotions do not always strengthen greater ones, concluding only that a love of dark punk is no sign of degeneracy.

panopticon.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
panopticon.title: And There Is No Escape
panopticon.relation: Abrams reads Allen through Foucault's panopticon: modern society is unlimited voyeurism in which the medieval God whose 'eyes are on us always' has been replaced by the omniscient gaze of Film — Cliff's exposé documentary forcing Lester to watch his own life in Crimes and Misdemeanors, Tom Baxter stepping off the screen in The Purple Rose of Cairo, and the nested eavesdropping layers of Another Woman, which he counts to infinity via Noël Carroll's 'mass art'. Against Mary Nichols's virtue-ethics reading, he argues Allen's ethics is Nietzschean self-fashioning: Judah lives 'beyond good and evil' where Raskolnikov failed, Allan Felix sheds the Bogart alter ego and 'gives style' to his character in Play It Again, Sam, while Eve in Interiors stages Hegel's master–slave dialectic, the 'master' artist dependent for her identity on those she objectifies.

panopticon.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
panopticon.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: A café dialogue pits second-waver Marie against third-waver Dorothy over whether Atkins can be a feminist tool: Marie wields the feminist critique of Cartesian dualism (Descartes made the mind essential and the body animal, and women were stigmatized as body), Foucault's internalized surveillance — 'every mirror becomes a guard, every scale an alarm,' with Lifetime Maintenance as 'maniacal' hyper-vigilance — Lorde's 'master's tools,' and Young's 'Throwing Like a Girl.' Dorothy answers with Our Bodies, Ourselves self-knowledge, Title IX athletes like Venus and Serena Williams, Frye's Willful Virgin, and existentialist facticity and bad faith (we are in bad faith when we abdicate control), defending dieting as a chosen women's project. The exchange ends drawish, over Brazilian waxes, French women, and whether ugliness is a feminist virtue.

panopticon.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
panopticon.title: The Viewer and the Look
panopticon.relation: Meyer and Schneider use the mockumentary camera of The Office (British and American versions) as Sartre's Look: Pam caught gazing at Jim and Karen in "The Merger" stages shame at being fixed as an object by the Other, while David Brent's bragging over his Inside Paper cover is pride as bad faith, an attempt to control the Other's gaze that requires denying the employee's freedom. Dwight and Angela's furtive affair and the Michael-Jan speakerphone call in "Cocktails" illustrate Foucault's panopticon: the mere possibility of the camera makes characters police themselves. The viewer, positioned behind the lens, becomes complicit in the objectifying Look that constitutes the show's comedy of embarrassment.

panopticon.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
panopticon.title: Art, Madness, and Syd Barrett
panopticon.relation: George Reisch reads The Wall through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: madness is not a brain lesion but a historical construction — Renaissance unreason, classical confinement, then Tuke's and Pinel's psychiatric regime in which the madman must know 'he is watched, judged, and condemned' until judgment is internalized — which explains why Pink imprisons himself brick by brick and asks at 'The Trial', 'Have I been guilty all this time?' The fascist worms and skinhead riots of 'Waiting for the Worms' are the same crusade for uniformity that drove Pink mad — Foucault's 'moral city' where 'virtue is an affair of the state' — so fascism and insanity are versions of each other, with Sartre's 'Hell is other people' from No Exit as the framing thought. Both the album ('Outside the Wall': 'the bleeding hearts and artists make their stand') and Foucault end by defending art as the last channel of unreason, and Reisch argues Syd Barrett's unanswerable absence was exactly that interrupting void powering 'Echoes', Dark Side, Wish You Were Here, and The Final Cut.

panopticon.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
panopticon.title: Spy versus Spy
panopticon.relation: Christian Hoffstadt and Michael Nagenborg read WoW's surveillance apparatus — the Warden client scanning players' machines, EULA clauses allowing remote patching, invisible Gamemasters — through Bentham's Panopticon as analyzed by Foucault: because players can never know whether they are watched, they discipline themselves against bots and gold farming. Against Richard Bartle's claim that developers are gods rather than governments, they use Foucault's governmentality and the fragile Machiavellian prince to show that Blizzard's sovereignty must be constantly maintained against hackers, cheaters, and black markets. Surveillance is Janus-faced, though: DKP add-ons and guild self-monitoring also coordinate raiding fairly — in this panopticon the inmates can be guards too.

panopticon.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
panopticon.title: 19 - facebook, Surveillance and Power
panopticon.relation: Doyle and Fraser open with the Lady Shelley Sawers affair, in which Britain's new MI6 chief was exposed by his wife's public Facebook profile, to ask whether social networks democratize surveillance or perfect it. They read the CIA's social-media monitoring, the Chris Dreyfus promotion case, and Facebook's Beacon advertising scheme through Foucault — Bentham's Panopticon, the carceral continuum, regimes of truth, and the shift to statistically managing populations — arguing that narcissistic self-display makes people 'most controllable,' while Habermas's public sphere frames the hopeful side: Beacon's defeat by user protest, Glassdoor, and Iran's Twitter revolution as diffused power against the centralized state. Foucault's answer is neither utopia nor repression but an ethics of self-management for playing power games with minimum domination.

panopticon.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
panopticon.title: From Hover Cars to Substance D
panopticon.relation: The chapter contrasts the films' technologies: Blade Runner foregrounds gaudy techno-tropes and a Voight-Kampff machine that discloses the truth about replicants, while A Scanner Darkly dwells on mundane devices, Substance D, surveillance cameras, cell phones and Barris's broken contraptions, that obscure reality and help dissolve Arctor's personality. It reads the latter as Dick's fear of the mechanization of humanity made contemporary, mirroring our own self-documentation on YouTube, Twitter and Facebook, and ending with Bruce, 'a dried husk', in the decoy corn field.

panopticon.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
panopticon.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Najwa Al-Tabaa reads Sandman: Season of Mists through Derrida's paradox that only the unforgivable can truly be forgiven: Morpheus's freeing of Nada works as forgiveness precisely because condemning his lover to Hell was unforgivable, while Lucifer, who was never wronged by the damned, can give them only a devalued semblance of pardon, and they cling to punishment they feel they deserve. She then brings in Foucault's Discipline and Punish and Bentham's Panopticon to read the angels' rebuilt Hell of redemption as the modern rehabilitative prison, where watched souls are expected to reform themselves. The experiment fails, she argues, because redemption is imposed without hearing the prisoners, violating Derrida's condition that forgiveness needs a shared language, so the inmates prefer Lucifer's honest eternity of despair to a salvation they never asked for, a lesson about real prisons that seek rehabilitation through punishment.

panopticon.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
panopticon.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Chad Timm applies Foucault's disciplinary power to the International Fleet: Graff sorts monitored children like 'formless clay,' watches them through a Battle School Panopticon of head monitors and battleroom observation, and uses constant testing and the normalizing gaze to make Ender his own overseer and construct the identity of a commander. He closes by mapping the same sort-examine-discipline circuit onto standardized testing and Race to the Top, noting Ender's flicker of resistance when the children finally see through the adults' game.

panopticon.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
panopticon.title: Homeland and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: April Marratto and Adam Barkman use Foucault's appropriation of Bentham's panopticon - surveillance whose mere threat disciplines - to read Carrie's illegal watches on the Brody house, the family's stay in the safe house, and Dana's discovery that speech about her father's Islam is policed. Against Foucault's claim that freedom is an illusion maintained by power, the chapter sets Aristotle's view that freedom is a self-directed will choosing rightly (Dana making amends for the hit-and-run) and Rousseau's social contract, under which citizens trade equal freedoms for equal protection. Both would endorse Saul forcing Brody's detox for the country's sake, concluding absolute freedom is neither possible nor desirable.

panopticon.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
panopticon.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Ketcham greets Piper Kerman at the prison door with Bentham's ghost: the state's utility calculation of her drug money laundering, the rat's discounted sentence, and the design of the panopticon, whose one-way inspection tower was meant to make surveillance cheap, obedience automatic, and prisoners productive and even saved. He contrasts that reform vision with the reality reconstructed from the book, where punishment falls on everyone, including families paying commissary prices and denied visits, and Danbury's 'vocational training' amounts to changing light bulbs. Bentham's own principle that 'punishment is an evil' is turned against a system that warehouses rather than rehabilitates.

panopticon.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
panopticon.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Stephenson and Waller start from disliking bland, marketable Piper and use Foucault's Discipline and Punish to argue that Litchfield is a microcosm of State power: arbitrary unwritten rules, counts, strip searches, and constant surveillance train prisoners into docile, compliant participants in capitalism, with specialist wardens, psychologists, and lawyers molding the abnormal into the normal. Prisoners specialize too (Red's kitchen, Nicky's ear, Vee's drugs) to survive, and specialization hides the surveillance. The show itself embodies the mechanism, making viewers aware they too live under the Panopticon, though deviants like Crazy Eyes and her standing pee keep open the possibility of refusing State values.

panopticon.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
panopticon.title: 6. Who Has the Power
panopticon.relation: Samuelson uses Foucault to dismantle Phillip Price's creed of being 'the most powerful person in the room': power is not a possession but an operation. Elliot's men in black and the FBI's surveillance are disciplinary power - Bentham's panopticon realized in Allsafe's cube farm and the internet itself - while Angela's fight over the Washington Township leak is a struggle with biopower that no sovereign can be punished for, and Whiterose's knowledge is power-knowledge that operates anonymously no matter who holds it. If Foucault is right, Price, Mr. Robot, and Zheng are mere conduits, and no one will ever be the most powerful person in the room.

panopticon.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
panopticon.title: 18. Psycho-Politics in a Burnout Society
panopticon.relation: Pagnoni Berns and Aguilar read the show through Byung-Chul Han's philosophy: in the transparency society everyone stacks their life online - Krista is transparent to Elliot because her password is Dylan and her birthday, while he stays opaque - and psycho-politics replaces Foucauldian punishment with seduction, a digital panopticon (Operation Berenstain, Minister Zhang) whose inmates voluntarily build it. Elliot's attention deficits, Tyrell's breakdown over Sharon Knowles's corpse, and Gideon's fatigue embody the burnout society's neuronal violence, and even fsociety reproduces the systemic coercion it fights, leaving 'real life' only outside the system.

panopticon.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
panopticon.title: 9. 24 7 Newsleep
panopticon.relation: Buchanan argues the Party 'sleep-hacks' its citizens because sleep is an active state of thought, a lineage he traces from Aristotle's theory of dreaming through Freud's Interpretation of Dreams, and is therefore a site of potential resistance that must be colonized. Between the Physical Jerks, telescreen trumpet-calls, a Thought Police able to inspect anyone 'asleep or awake' without warning, and O'Brien's manipulation of Winston's sleep schedule during torture, Winston is trapped in 'Newsleep', a derealized blur of dream and reality that makes doublethink the only available way of thinking. He extends the diagnosis to our own 24/7 economy of phones and Trump's all-hours tweets, concluding that Orwell's warning is that we must guard our sleep.

panopticon.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
panopticon.title: 14. The Seduction of Winston Smith
panopticon.relation: Mark Alfano reads the novel's ending ('He loved Big Brother') as a seduction story: following John Forrester, a seducer opens with 'I know what you're thinking', which O'Brien enacts when he voices Winston's unspoken thought under torture and demands not mere obedience but enthusiastic consent. Big Brother wins Winston over through four epistemic methods: total surveillance (telescreens, Thought Police, Parsons's own children), the Ministry of Truth's annihilation of records like the photograph of Jones, Aaronson and Rutherford, the destruction of self-trust in the 'how many fingers?' sessions, and the isolation of intimates until Winston betrays Julia. Alfano closes by mapping all four methods onto post-9/11 mass surveillance and Trump-era attacks on records, perception, and the press.

panopticon.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
panopticon.title: 10. Babies and Pleasures
panopticon.relation: Wesch uses Foucault's Discipline and Punish to explain how ordinary women so quickly served Gilead: power is exercised rather than possessed, so Offred enjoying the Guardians' frustration, the 'Her fault!' Testifying, and the Particicution show everyone wielding whatever power is within reach. Gilead is a panopticon in Bentham's sense—the Eyes, paired shopping, 'Under His Eye'—where unverifiable surveillance makes citizens their own overseers, while biopower sorts desirable from undesirable populations, 'making live' fertile Handmaids (shatterproof glass against suicide) and letting Unwomen and unbabies die in the Colonies. Resistance is Foucauldian too: Offred's remembered food, Moira's bathroom gossip, and sex with Nick are the 'bodies and pleasures' that counterattack the deployment of sexuality.

panopticon.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
panopticon.title: 20. Under a Watchful Eye
panopticon.relation: Timm gives a full Foucauldian reading: the Sons of Jacob's biblical 'knowledge' is a regime of truth produced by power (via the genealogical method Foucault took from Nietzsche), and Gilead rules less by sovereign violence (particicutions, the Wall) than by disciplinary power that defines, sorts, confines, and retrains—precisely the asylum-prison-school trajectory of Foucault's History of Madness and Discipline and Punish. The Red Center is that institution in miniature (Janine's 'Her fault, her fault'), the black vans with painted Eyes enact Bentham's Panopticon—power 'visible and unverifiable'—and biopower's medicalized control of women's reproductive bodies ties Gilead to Iowa's 2018 fetal heartbeat law. Offred's small refusals—her hidden name, the night that is 'mine,' the act of telling her tale—are the resistance Foucault always found inside disciplinary power.

panopticon.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
panopticon.title: A Black Mirror of Our Anxieties
panopticon.relation: Nosedive's star ratings are read as a digital panopticon — Bentham's prison design generalized by Foucault's Discipline and Punish — with China's Zhima Credit and Social Credit Systems showing the 'future is already here.' Rousseau's general will and Plato's ship-of-state frame the tyranny-of-the-majority worry (Chester destroyed by an office mob, Lacie jailed for a wedding toast, post-truth tribalism), which Mill's harm principle rebuts: Lacie's rant harms no one and should not be punished. Sartre's 'look' and No Exit explain Lacie's staged cookie photo ('Heaven!') and her final liberating exchange of insults with her cellmate, while Goffman's masks ground the epistemological worry that digital profiles are performances we nonetheless trust, and Bourdieu's symbolic capital names what the scores actually measure.

panopticon.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
panopticon.title: Heaven is a Place on Earth
panopticon.relation: The chapter argues Black Mirror's perception tech works because the brain constructs experience top-down (predictive coding), so implants like Playtest's mushroom, Arkangel's filter, and Men Against Fire's MASS can inject perceptions and suppress error signals - and Cooper's total VR illusion defeats every one of Descartes's strategies (memory continuity, cross-checking the senses, reason) for telling dream from reality, killing him seconds after implantation. Nozick's experience machine illuminates Danny's preference for Striking Vipers X over his marriage and Arkangel's lesson that filtering Sara's childhood perceptions left her unable to read danger or emotion. Foucault's panopticon (via Bentham) frames White Christmas's cookie interrogation modeled on real police deception (Frazier v. Cupp), the MASS implant's manufacture of 'roach' targets for killing, and Nosedive's self-imposed social ratings as modern perceptual discipline - with only trusted others (Catarina, Susan, Kelly) punching through the manipulation.

panopticon.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
panopticon.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Chad Timm reads Battle School through Foucault's disciplinary power: monitors in the skull, sorting into armies, minute-by-minute schedules, and constant testing are the power/knowledge that constructs 'the soldier,' while the ever-possible observation of teachers and desks makes the school Bentham's Panopticon that trains students to police themselves. The proof of Ender's constructed identity is his singling out of Bean exactly as Graff singled him out on the shuttle, and Timm extends the lesson to standardized testing and Obama's 'Race to the Top.'

panopticon.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
panopticon.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: The chapter uses Foucault to explain how Salander could leave school without a certificate yet master Fermat-class mathematics: schools 'cut' students into fabricated 'human kinds'—the problem-solving child and the at-risk child (Popkewitz's alchemy)—and under No Child Left Behind that sorting licenses surveillance and discipline of everything an at-risk student does. Lisbeth's case shows the machinery: her correct answer marked wrong from the textbook key, her Rubik's-cube brilliance ignored, her 381 days strapped to a bed under Teleborian's silhouette-like gaze recasting Bentham's Panopticon, and her subsequent guardianship extending the watch over her money and behavior. Because power 'produces reality,' the at-risk label becomes self-fulfilling, and Lisbeth's refusal to be disciplined—her silence, tattoos, and asocial style—only supplies fresh evidence for the label.

panopticon.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
panopticon.title: Notes
panopticon.relation: Sirvent and Diorio apply Foucault's panopticon (built on Bentham's prison design) to the show's web of watching: Frank manipulates Zoe through leaked stories, Doug keeps Rachel permanently locatable by phone, and Claire must demand the bug be removed from Michael Corrigan's Russian cell, showing watched subjects paralyzed by fear. Against Bauman and Lyon's 'liquid surveillance,' the chapter argues democracy is an anti-institutional force requiring free dissent and a press at arm's length from power, and that surveillance collapses the Greek public/private distinction so citizens fear punishment for questioning rulers. Frank's 'Nobody can hear you. Nobody cares about you' to Zoe captures how the surveillance state turns criticism into danger, leaving a society that is no longer a democracy.

panopticon.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
panopticon.title: Notes
panopticon.relation: Uses Foucault's panopticon (built on Bentham's prison design) and Bauman's 'liquid surveillance' to read Frank's Washington as a surveillance society: Zoe's archived texts, Doug's inescapable tracking of Rachel, and the bugged cell where Claire visits Michael Corrigan all show how being watched destroys privacy and paralyzes dissent. It argues that democracy needs free spaces in which citizens can question power without later punishment, so the culture of fear Frank rules through-'you are a rock, you absorb nothing, you say nothing'-turns checks and balances into instruments of control even inside an elected government.

panopticon.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
panopticon.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Van Dyke uses Foucault's account of discipline and 'docile bodies' (with Susan Bordo's feminist elaboration) to explain how the Capitol rules: citizens satiated with abundance channel their hungers into fashion, body modification, and self-surveillance, and this self-focused discipline trains their attention away from the injustices that sustain them — which is how the genuinely affectionate prep team can weep over Katniss yet love the Games. She shows that District 13 disciplines just as totally through rigid schedules, rations, and punishment (the prep team chained for taking bread), so neither Snow's hidden indulgence nor Coin's overt regimentation leaves room for autonomy. Cinna's styling of Katniss demonstrates the alternative: body modification as internally generated self-expression and resistance that helps Katniss become the Mockingjay rather than a docile body.

panopticon.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
panopticon.title: Madness in the Mirror of Reason: Metallica and Foucault on Insanity and Confinement
panopticon.relation: Brian Cameron reads 'Welcome Home (Sanitarium)' and 'Frayed Ends of Sanity' through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: the sanitarium is a total institution whose surveillance and power-knowledge produce docile bodies, confining madness as a threat to the rule of reason just as the seventeenth-century Hopital General confined the idle. Madness is not a mere disease but a socially defined deviance - and a form of rebellion against conformist society - whose violent 'cure' ('violent use brings violent plans') exacts an existential cost on the rebel, as 'The Unforgiven''s bitter old man shows.

panopticon.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
panopticon.title: The Office and Philosophy
panopticon.relation: Applies Sartre's Being and Nothingness to the mockumentary: Pam's bad faith consists in pretending she has no choice between Jim and Roy (her garbled 'I'm not into Jim' conversation with Karen in 'Ben Franklin'), while the camera's Look - Sartre's keyhole peeper caught in the hallway - turns her into an object not of her making when she is caught watching Jim and Karen in 'The Merger', and her shame finally lets her own her feelings. David Brent's pride (posing with his Inside Paper magazine cover) tries to control the Other's look and fails, since the freely respected gaze he craves cannot be extracted; and the ever-possible camera functions as Foucault's panopticon (Bentham's prison design), visible and unverifiable, silencing Jan on speakerphone in 'Cocktails' and forcing Dwight and Angela's 'Don't linger. Break left' choreography, which makes the viewer a complicit co-worker.

panopticon.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
panopticon.title: Notes
panopticon.relation: Donovan uses the New 52 Azzarello run's gods as a catalogue of gender stereotypes - jealous Hera hunting Zola, woman-incinerating Apollo, hyper-masculine First Born, self-sacrificing Demeter - then tracks Hera's transformation after Apollo makes her mortal as a Beauvoirian passage from immanence (being Zeus's Other, defined by his desire) to transcendence (charting an independent identity, aiding baby Zeke). Foucault's Panopticon explains how gender norms are internalized without an enforcer, and Butler's drag example grounds the claim that Wonder Woman accepting the god of war mantle - leading a female Amazon army 'not as your princess but as the god of war' - is a subversive performance of gender.

panopticon.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
panopticon.title: Kingdom of Darkness: Autonomy and Conspiracy in The X-Files and Millennium
panopticon.relation: Michael Valdez Moses reads The X-Files and Millennium as post-Cold War noir that depicts America as Foucault's carceral archipelago: nearly every character works for the state, Tocquevillian voluntary association has withered ('they don't go bowling at all'), and the FBI's landscape of prisons, clinics, and bases makes free space scarce. Against Hobbes's Leviathan, the chapter mobilizes Locke and Paine's classical liberalism (government as necessary evil securing pre-existing natural rights) to show that Carter's heroes are 'antipolitical' resisters: Frank Black's visions and the Grill Flame remote viewers make him a panoptical spy for the state, while Mulder's warrantless searches blur sovereign and criminal justice into one corrupt system, as in the Millennium episode 'The Judge'. The neo-noir conspiracy seeks not profit but absolute sovereignty, and the series end with Mulder, Scully, and Black as fugitives fleeing the state with their families, resisting Nietzsche's 'coldest of all cold monsters'.

panopticon.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
panopticon.title: The Prisoner and Self-Imprisonment
panopticon.relation: Biderman and Devlin use The Prisoner to test three dimensions of selfhood: Number 6's 'I am not a number!' defends the material self against the Village's conformity (Rover, uniforms, human chess pieces), his reflective self echoes Descartes's certain thinking thing, Kant's rational self-legislation, and Sartrean authenticity ('existence precedes essence'), while the finale's trial of the rebels addresses the relational self. The revelation that Number 6 is Number 1 is then read through Foucault: hierarchical observation, normalization, and examination make the Village Bentham's panopticon internalized, so the prisoner monitors himself and the ideal of a freely self-created identity collapses into social conditioning, as Nietzsche's herd come home. The chapter leaves the noir ambiguity intact: either Number 6 is the authentic individual vindicated by the Village council, or the self is a fiction and his odyssey hopeless.

panopticon.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
panopticon.title: War Pictures Digital Surveillance from Foreign Theater to Homeland Security Front
panopticon.relation: Stewart argues that War on Terror films (Redacted, Battle for Haditha, The Situation, In the Valley of Elah, Waltz with Bashir) depict 'a soldiery without a genre' because digital surveillance has fused sighting and triggering, so combat is nowhere and everywhere and the classic movement-image spectacle collapses. Drawing on Deleuze's movement-image/time-image distinction, he recasts the soldier as spectator (SSS' rather than SAS'), watching under the panoptic drone eye rather than acting, and shows sci-fi 'temportation' thrillers (Déjà Vu, Source Code, Eagle Eye) travestying the time-image into computerized wish-fulfillment. The Hurt Locker succeeds precisely by reverting to a man-vs-machine 'duel,' while Waltz with Bashir alone achieves genuine political reframing by breaking from animation into archival massacre footage.

panopticon.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
panopticon.title: Beyond Panopticism The Biopolitical Labor of Surveillance and War in Contemporary Film
panopticon.relation: Gooch argues that the post-2005 surveillance film cycle moves 'beyond panopticism': Foucault's disciplinary gaze gives way to Deleuze's 'societies of control,' and the surveiling gaze becomes direct domination and a form of biopolitical labor (Hardt and Negri) rather than an impersonal structure. He reads the prestige dramas (Redacted, Stop-Loss, In the Valley of Elah, Lions for Lambs) as exposing the soldier's proletarianization and self-surveillance, and the thrillers/blockbusters (Déjà Vu, The Kingdom, Body of Lies, The Bourne Ultimatum, Eagle Eye, Burn after Reading) as staging a Marxist antagonism between living labor (the watching hero) and the fixed capital of surveillance technology. Using Deleuze's 'degraded time-image,' Kant's needed separation of subject and law, and Benjamin/Agamben's state of exception, he shows Eagle Eye inverting law and subject to justify preemptive war and turn biopolitical labor into the labor of subjection.

panopticon.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
panopticon.title: The Viewer and the Look
panopticon.relation: Meyer and Schneider use The Office's mockumentary camera to dramatize Sartre's 'the Look' and bad faith. Pam pretends she cannot choose between Roy and Jim (bad faith as being-in-itself), and is shamed when the camera catches her watching Jim and Karen; David Brent's prideful self-promotion tries and fails to control the Other's gaze. They tie the ever-present camera to the Foucault/Bentham panopticon: Jan, Dwight, and Angela police themselves because they might be watched, making the viewer complicit in the workers' existential crises.

panopticon.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
panopticon.title: The Shining ’s Overlook Hotel as Heterotopia
panopticon.relation: Elizabeth Hornbeck analyzes King's Overlook Hotel through Foucault's 'Of Other Spaces,' arguing the hotel is a heterotopia—a socially produced space of crisis and deviance that juxtaposes and inverts normal relations, accumulating time as a 'chronic heterotopia' stuffed with its own ghosts and murders (Mrs. Massey, the Gradys, the 1921 photo). Cut off in winter, it strips away the norms of 'home' so Jack Torrance's inherited monsters (alcoholism, his father's abuse) can turn him from protector into a family-killer. She contrasts the maze-like Overlook with the panopticon of Grand Hotel and Bentham's surveillance-prison from Discipline and Punish, noting that King, unlike Foucault, treats transgression as horrific: the conservative horror genre restores the status quo only when Jack dies and the hotel burns.

panopticon.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
panopticon.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
panopticon.relation: Collins analyzes paradigmatic Barbie play — dressing the doll and identifying with her as an idealized future self, from the 1959 TV ad to BarbieGirls.com — arguing it trains girls to define identity through fashionable bodily self-presentation for a male gaze (Brumberg's 'body project'). Using Sandra Bartky's feminist reworking of Foucault's *Discipline and Punish*, she treats beauty norms as a discipline producing 'docile bodies' whose self-surveillance internalizes a 'panoptical male connoisseur' (Bentham's Panopticon), offering cycles of pleasure and pain that bind women without any single sovereign to blame. Rather than banning Barbie (the failed 'Happy to be Me' doll), she proposes subversive play — Plump and Proud Barbie, Mursi lip-plate Barbie — as Heyes-style 'practices of freedom.'

panopticon.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
panopticon.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
panopticon.relation: Hancuff and O'Connor read the song 'Santa Claus Is Coming to Town' and films like The Polar Express and Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town through Foucault's Discipline and Punish. Santa's all-seeing list-checking is a version of Bentham's Panopticon: children, watched but never seeing the watcher, internalize permanent visibility and discipline themselves. Invoking Foucault's Power/Knowledge and discursive practices, they argue the surveillance does not actually make children 'good for goodness' sake' – punishment is rarely delivered – but instead disciplines them into wish-lists and consumption, training them to be good consumers in late-capitalist culture, with Santa doubling as a corporate pitchman (Coke, Budweiser).

panopticon.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
panopticon.title: GARDENING
panopticon.relation: Shapiro argues that Frederick Law Olmsted's Central Park is a major artwork realizing a 'pragmatic picturesque,' and reads the English picturesque garden as a 'diagram' (in Foucault's and Deleuze's sense) of the glance—the roving, liberated look—explicitly contrasted with Bentham's Panopticon, the diagram of the objectifying gaze. Using Derrida's paradox of the frame, he shows the picturesque hides its boundary (the ha-ha) while Olmsted inverts the diagram, making the frame explicit and admitting the city so citizens meet in democratic 'gregarious' recognition—a Platonic argument (aesthetic education in the Republic) turned pragmatic in the climate of Peirce, James and Dewey. Christo and Jeanne-Claude's 'The Gates' distills the park's diagram as a gift of time.

panopticon.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
panopticon.title: The Viewer and the Look
