logical-positivism.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
logical-positivism.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
logical-positivism.relation: 'The Dream of a Bullshit-Free Culture' argues Frankfurt revives a centuries-old philosophical tradition: Socrates searching for genuinely wise people rather than purveyors of hearsay, Descartes' Meditations discarding every belief short of certainty, and Hume's forkcondemning divinity-school metaphysics that contains neither abstract nor experimental reasoning to the flames. The twentieth-century apotheosis is the Vienna Circle, whose Rudolf Carnap dissected Heidegger's 'Das Nichts selbst nichtet' as mere appearance of meaning, calling metaphysicians 'musicians without musical ability'. The editors cast Frankfurt as the latest carrier of this Enlightenment anti-bullshit torch, with the book's popularity reconnecting seminar-room philosophy to the marketplace and voting booth.

logical-positivism.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
logical-positivism.title: Vertigo and Epistemological Vertigo
logical-positivism.relation: Flory reads Vertigo as an epistemological parable: Scottie's 'hardheaded Scot' method, collecting facts and deducing from universal principles, fails three times (the step-stool 'cure' for his acrophobia, explaining away Madeleine's 'possession' with the horse statue, forcing Judy up the bell tower for confirmation), delivering an implicit critique of Vienna Circle positivism in the manner of Carnap and Ayer. Against Scottie, the chapter mobilizes Kuhn's theory-laden facts, Aristotle's point that human conduct resists codification by exceptionless laws, and Hume's 'slave of the passions,' with Descartes's automata and Chalmers's philosophical zombies framing the problem of other minds. Midge, who knows people emotionally as well as factually, models the alternative: philosophers who fear 'epistemological vertigo' should give up epistemological training wheels and accept that minds, especially emotions, escape law-like rules.

logical-positivism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
logical-positivism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
logical-positivism.relation: Bernard Rollin reads Dr. Zaius's tribunal as 'scientific ideology' in action - 'human see, human do' refuses to believe its own eyes, just as bishops refused to look through Galileo's telescope. He traces the ideology from Newton's 'hypotheses non fingo' through logical positivism's verifiability criterion (which validates the Hasslein Curve prediction while rendering 'there are intelligent beings in Heaven' meaningless) and Wittgenstein's point that 'killing is wrong' is not a fact of the universe, to the 'science is value-free' dogma that left animal pain untested and untreated - as he documents from his own campaign: the empty analgesic literature search, the 1985 federal legislation, and the pain physiologist whose dog research refutes his own denial. Zira's neurosurgery on mute humans repeats what Descartes's beast-machine doctrine licensed, and IASP's language requirement for pain collapses into a Cratylus-grade confusion of necessary and sufficient conditions ('You can't step into the same river once').

personal-identity.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
personal-identity.title: Inauthenticity and Fascism
personal-identity.relation: David Detmer treats Zelig, the mock-documentary 'chameleon man' who turns black, Chinese, fat, or a Nazi depending on his company, as a stark dramatization of personal identity and the existentialist critique of inauthenticity. After rejecting the memory, bodily-continuity, and immaterial-soul criteria of identity, the chapter takes the existentialist line, quoting Heidegger on Dasein's selfhood, that a self is its choices, projects, and commitments, so Zelig's chameleonism is self-estrangement motivated by fear and the craving to be liked. Politically, the chapter draws Allen's lesson that genocides happen not because millions go mad but because millions passively conform, made literal by Zelig appearing at a Hitler rally, and supports it with Asch's conformity experiments and Milgram's obedience studies.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: Horcruxes
personal-identity.relation: Uses Lupin's account of the Dementor's Kiss, whose victims like Barty Crouch Jr. go on existing as empty shells without memory or self, to eliminate the leading views of the soul: the soul cannot be the source of life, of sentience, or even of Cartesian higher thought, since the soulless victim may still sense and think dimly. The chapter compares the Kiss's aftermath to severe dementia or to Lockhart after his backfired memory charm, raising the question of whether the person rather than just the body survives.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: Mind-Body Distinctions
personal-identity.relation: Eric Saidel launches his chapter from a puzzle: why would Sirius, outside for the first time in months, celebrate by chasing his tail in Order of the Phoenix? He asks whether an Animagus is a man in a dog's body, a dog in a man's body, or a third thing, and extends the question to Pettigrew, Rita Skeeter, McGonagall, werewolf Lupin, boggarts, and Polyjuice transformations such as Barty Crouch Jr.'s eerily effective impersonation of Moody.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: Whose Reasons
personal-identity.relation: Tests the Cartesian division of the transformed Padfoot into mind plus body across four possible combinations and rejects them all: Sirius's human body cannot plausibly slip 'into non-being' during transformation (against McGonagall's quip), yet a Sirius-mind cannot explain tail-chasing and a dog-mind cannot explain Padfoot standing on his hind legs to embrace Harry at King's Cross. Mind-body dualism thus fails as an account of what the transformed person is.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: NOTES
personal-identity.relation: Concludes that transformed persons are unified mind-body wholes rather than pilot-and-ship pairings, enlisting Descartes himself, who insisted he is 'not only lodged in my body, like a pilot in his ship' but compounded with it into a single whole. The evidence is textual: Polyjuiced Harry naturally 'thunders' with Runcorn's powerful frame while acting for Harry's reasons, Luna recognizes Harry through Barny Weasley's facial expression, and Crouch-as-Moody makes sense as an indivisible embodiment, so Padfoot is neither man nor dog but a third kind of being, a man-dog.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: “A Swirling, Silvery Mass”
personal-identity.relation: Opens Amy Kind's Pensieve chapter: the basin lets you offload memories like data from a hard drive, gain distance from obsessions, and, as Dumbledore tells Harry, spot patterns and links when reviewing them from outside. Its real intrigue is philosophical: if thoughts can be extracted from the mind, tampered with, stored elsewhere, shared, and discarded, then the boundaries of mind, memory, and self are up for grabs - and memory-based accounts of personal identity, on which philosophers have modeled our continuing existence, come under pressure.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: The Inversion of Voldemort
personal-identity.relation: Distinguishes remorse from mere regret through Voldemort's cold 'I regret it' after ordering Nagini to kill Snape: remorse requires owning one's act, and at the final duel Harry addresses him as 'Tom Riddle' and demands he 'try for some remorse' - the death-to-self Riddle cannot perform. Dumbledore's remorse over the cursed Resurrection Stone ring and his arranged death, and Harry's voluntary death that destroys the Horcrux within him and restores his whole soul, exemplify dying to the past self for renewal, while Harry's renunciation of his temper toward Ron and Hermione and his love for Ginny mark his continuous moral regeneration.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: The Fantasy Objection
personal-identity.relation: Takes up the integrity objection from psychoanalyst Melanie Klein: renouncing one's past self ('Bad Charles' versus 'New Charlie') risks self-deception, since the reformed person remains the self-same wrongdoer, as the alcoholic who stays sober for decades still knows himself to be. Taliaferro concedes the regeneration model can be abused but insists renewal requires a death-like renunciation, illustrated negatively by Snape, who loves Lily, feels remorse for the 'Mudblood' insult and for giving Voldemort the prophecy, yet cannot confess or release his resentment, and so remains unintegrated.

personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
personal-identity.title: NOTES
personal-identity.relation: Argues via William James's 'sow a thought... reap a destiny' and Aristotle's account of how repeated action incrementally shapes the soul that Voldemort's flayed remnant is a character fully forged by choices, stuck with itself forever - a postmortem fate Heidegger's atheism cannot frame but Rowling's afterlife can. The section weighs Locke's memory-and-character account of identity, Kant's postulate that harmony of virtue and happiness requires an afterlife, and Pascal on why the immortality question must govern how we live, and ends asking whether Voldemort's evil is ignorance, as Plato held, or a cultivated appetite that only vice can satisfy.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: Chapter 17 - Questions of Identity Is the Hulk the Same Person as Bruce Banner
personal-identity.relation: Frames the chapter with a San Francisco criminal trial in which Bruce Banner's lawyer argues the Hulk — a large green figure — literally was not the same individual who now stands small and pale before the judge. Ruling requires criteria for "continuity of personal identity over time": what makes you the same person today as ten years ago, applied here to whether Banner should answer for the Hulk's rampage.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: The Hulk’s Bodily Identity
personal-identity.relation: Tests the everyday bodily criterion of identity: the Hulk's body contains far more atoms than Banner's, but since all our cells turnover anyway — the "Stan Lee Schooner" has every part replaced yet stays the same boat, the Ship of Theseus problem — and the organ-donor case of "Herb Trimpe" shows a body with greater physical continuity to Kinghorn than to its owner, bodily continuity cannot be what personal identity consists in.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: The Mental Realm of the Hulk
personal-identity.relation: Applies Locke's memory theory: the shape-shifting Martian Manhunter and the irradiated Fantastic Four stay the same people through mental continuity, and the early comics' Banner-minded Hulk meets Locke's criterion — but the later "Hulk smash!" Hulk, who recognizes Betty Ross yet lacks Banner's memories, fails it. The chapter then breaks the criterion itself with Reid's brave-officer objection (the general both is and is not the flogged boy), Alzheimer's and Doc Ock's amnesia attack on Spider-Man, and the circularity of distinguishing genuine from false memory (the deluded fan who "remembers" starring in Adventures of Superman).

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: A Causal Account of the Hulk’s Identity
personal-identity.relation: Proposes that the Hulk is Banner because Banner "Hulks out" — the monster state develops causally from Banner's body and mind through radiation, danger and anger, rather than one person being swapped for another. But a mad scientist's cloning accident that splits Banner into two simultaneous rampaging Hulks breaks the account, since both would be causally derived from Bruce yet could not both be the one person — the fission-style counterexample that afflicts every theory so far.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: Is There No Way to Tell
personal-identity.relation: Presents Derek Parfit's challenge to the whole enterprise: just as there need be no answer to whether a repaired machine is "the same" machine, Parfit's divided-brain case — each half housed in a new body — suggests a person can "survive as two different people without implying that I am these people," so identity questions may lack answers. Kinghorn resists the leap: difficulty finding the truth does not show there is none.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: The Hulk’s Relational Identity
personal-identity.relation: Defends a relational account: a person's identity persists through continuing relationships with others (like a marriage or a corporation), against our post-Enlightenment fixation on private attributes. Objections — severed relationships, the castaway, others' biased projections — are answered by positing a God who relates to every person without distortion and guarantees each identity, and who, since divine power cannot do the logically impossible, could not make Banner identical with two numerically distinct Hulks at once.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: What Should We Conclude
personal-identity.relation: Renders the verdict in the Banner trial: Bruce is the Hulk, because their relationships continue — when David Banner phones to say Betty Ross will be eliminated, Bruce forms the protective intention the Hulk then executes by destroying the three mutant poodles, and Betty, David and General Ross all relate to the Hulk as Bruce. Physical, mental and causal indicators are mere cues to the deeper continuity of relationships that constitutes who someone is.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: Identity in Crisis
personal-identity.relation: Poses the persistence problem through Superman-1 and Superman-2: are they strictly identical? Perdurantism — persons as four-dimensional space-time worms made of temporal parts — makes them distinct worms with no parts in common, so Superman meeting his counterpart is no stranger than you meeting a friend; endurantism, with wholly present strict identity, could identify them across timelines but balks at the impossibility of Superman meeting himself.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: Endurantist Past-Changing
personal-identity.relation: Chases the endurantist bullet: if one thing can differ across timelines, one and the same timeline can exist differently in different hyperhistories, letting Joe's murder of Wolfman make 1984 "not the way he remembers it." Yet even this yields only switching, not the dynamic change Crisis dramatizes, so the six-dimensional cosmos stands; Hanley closes with Wolfman's own secret plot device for bringing back the killed Barry Allen Flash.

personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personal-identity.title: Dual Identities
personal-identity.relation: Lists the classic hero/normal identity pairs (Batman/Bruce Wayne, Spider-Man/Peter Parker, plus Woody Allen's joke alias) and separates costume as role-transition — the Fantastic Four's public uniforms, doctors' scrubs, Bob's garage shirt — from costume as tool, Batman's fear-theater aimed at "a superstitious and cowardly lot" and the female heroes' calculated "gawk factor." What most superheroes do is the distinct third thing, masking: personas from the Latin for mask, keeping Peter's Spider-Man and Matt Murdock's Daredevil secret in both directions.

personal-identity.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
personal-identity.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: Uses Narnia's magical transformations to probe personal identity, starting with the qualitative/numerical identity distinction illustrated by the look-alike twins Shasta and Corin in The Horse and His Boy. Aristotle's essential/accidental properties frame the question of what Eustace can lose and remain Eustace, including turning into a dragon, and Rabadash into a donkey, showing persons are not identical to their bodies. Descartes's soul argument and Locke's memory theory are tested and rejected, the latter because it cannot handle Rilian's enchanted amnesia, Shasta's forgotten infancy, or Susan's disowned memories without circularity. The chapter defends instead a first-person-perspective theory on which a person is constituted by, not identical to, a body, illustrated by the repeatedly repaired Dawn Treader and by the heroes surviving death in The Last Battle as restored points of view.

personal-identity.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
personal-identity.title: “Nobody’s Bob Dylan”
personal-identity.relation: Vernezze and Lulewicz take Dylan's 1964 Halloween quip "I got my Bob Dylan mask on" as an entry into personal identity, testing each theory against his life: the bodily view (Zimmerman to Dylan) survives cell turnover but stumbles on brain-transplant cases; Locke's memory theory handles them but faces Reid's brave-officer regress and Alzheimer's cases, and Dylan's reincarnation lyrics ("Shelter from the Storm," "I and I") ignore memory altogether. The Christian soul view of the gospel albums ("When He Returns," "Gotta Serve Somebody") follows Descartes and Plato but cannot justify the swirl-to-filling inference that souls exist. The chapter ends sympathetic to Hume's bundle theory and the Buddhist no-self: Dylan's "I is another," his name as fabrication, and the cover album Self Portrait all deny a fixed self-created essence.

personal-identity.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
personal-identity.title: Dead People
personal-identity.relation: William Larkin uses Romero's films - Karen Cooper devouring her father in Night of the Living Dead, Roger begging Peter to shoot him in Dawn, Riley's 'Those people are all dead' in Land - to argue that persons are res corporealis, bodily continuers, rather than Descartes's res cogitans. Our terror of becoming a zombie ourselves and our grief at recognized neighbors in the horde reveal that deep down we think persons survive as corpses, so bodily continuity suffices for identity while psychological continuity is unnecessary. The Locke-style body-switching intuition (prince and cobbler) that supports the psychological approach is dismissed as theoretically biased data compared to what good zombie fiction draws out of us.

personal-identity.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
personal-identity.title: Zombies and Us
personal-identity.relation: Hamish Thompson asks why we kill zombies with so few qualms and whether zombification releases us from obligations to the person who was, testing brain-death criteria, altered-identity and self-defense justifications against Shaun of the Dead (Shaun's mother and Ed), Day of the Dead's Bub, White Zombie, and Invasion of the Body Snatchers. He borrows Hume's bundle theory - the self as a fiction, a bundle of perceptions rather than an essence - and Parfit's degrees of psychological continuity to dissolve the sharp alive/dead and same-person/other-person dichotomies that make zombie-killing easy. The payoff is that we are already partly zombie (Shaun's checkout line, Ed on the sofa, the author's all-night gaming), differing only in our capacity for brief autonomous, goal-directed choices like Shaun's three-plan montage.

personal-identity.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
personal-identity.title: Oh Yes, There Will Be Blood
personal-identity.relation: Rachel Robison asks why blood, of all substances, carries metaphysical powers in vampire lore - Elizabeth Bathory's youth-giving baths, Dracula's control over Mina once she drinks his blood, Sookie's bond with Bill in True Blood. Her explanation is historical: the ancient cardiocentric view (Aristotle, Empedocles, Chrysippus placing the rational center in the heart and making blood its product) plus Galenic humorism and bloodletting made blood the carrier of the self, so drinking someone's blood plausibly transmits bits of their personal identity, knowledge, and even domination over one's free will. She then tests the show's synthetic 'True Blood': either some essential property of blood (or of the act of drinking it) carries the power, or the legend is parasitic on our lingering habit of locating emotion and character in the heart ('hot blooded') - either way the myth stays credible because our metaphors of blood never died.

personal-identity.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
personal-identity.title: Be Slow to Judge
personal-identity.relation: Southworth tests Locke's memory theory on Wolverine: the Cassandra Nova/Xavier mind-swap shows identity follows mind, not body, and Wolverine's serial memory wipes (Team X, Weapon X, Apocalypse's brainwashing) mean that on Locke's connected-memory view several different people have inhabited his body — with House of M's total recall suddenly loading him with responsibility for all their deeds. Jamie Madrox's duplicates then carry Parfit's objection that shared memories cannot suffice for sameness of person, pushing toward physical continuity and the chapter's deflationary moral: be slow to judge who deserves blame.

personal-identity.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
personal-identity.title: Identities, Selves, and Others
personal-identity.relation: Patterson uses Thornhill's being mistaken for the fictitious George Kaplan to test theories of personal identity: the body theory fails a CIA thought experiment in which a Kaplan double is slowly rebuilt from Thornhill's own replaced cells; Locke's memory theory fails on amnesia scenarios and circularity, since one cannot have memories of a self unless one already has a self; and Parfit's psychological continuity survives, with Thornhill drifting along a 'Psychological Spectrum' toward 'one hundred percent Kaplan' as he plays the spy. The chapter then turns existentialist: with Sartre, no essential nature fixes who Thornhill is, so he is totally responsible for the self his choices create, from 'Expedient Exaggerations' to risking death on Mount Rushmore. Charles Taylor's claim that a self exists only in dialogue with a community explains why Eve and others literally help make Thornhill into the person he becomes.

personal-identity.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
personal-identity.title: Was Jerry Garcia the Soul of the Grateful Dead
personal-identity.relation: John Uglietta asks what made the Grateful Dead the Grateful Dead when they swapped five keyboardists yet stopped being themselves the moment Jerry Garcia died, prompting the rename to The Dead. Testing Aristotle's essential versus accidental properties, Peter French's structural account of group identity (the Yankees, the Glenn Miller Orchestra), same-stuff theories via a VW bus rebuilt piece by piece from its old parts — a Ship of Theseus puzzle — and Locke's memory theory applied to Phil Lesh's liver (but feared brain) transplant, he proposes that the band's essence was a group spirit born of members 'surrendering their own little trip'. The soul of the Dead was bigger than Jerry but smaller than the whole band, and its loss at his death was something the survivors could recognize but not replace.

personal-identity.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
personal-identity.title: Absolutely Curtains
personal-identity.relation: Michael Patton retells the Ship of Theseus (his 'Trump Princess' rebuilt part-by-part from spares, then duplicated from the salvaged parts) to ask whether Pink Floyd survived its upheavals: Bob Klose's pre-Piper exit, Syd Barrett's 1968 dismissal ('No, fuck it, let's not bother' on the drive to Southampton), Rick Wright's firing during The Wall, and Roger Waters's 1985 lawsuit to stop Gilmour and Mason using the name. Roster, stylistic ('Lucifer Sam' versus 'Money'), legal, and nominal criteria each fail, so he proposes an 'Officeholder View' of identity in which constituencies decide sameness — as when UFO Club's Joe Boyd saw a different Syd at the June 1967 show, while the author's locked-in brother Josh (like Bauby in The Diving Bell and the Butterfly) remained the same son and brother to his family. Parfit's claim that survival tracks memory and personality rather than body underwrites the 'death of a thousand cuts' scenario: the band's criteria, not Syd's own, ended the life of the person 'Syd Barrett', and he didn't get a vote.

personal-identity.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
personal-identity.title: Introduction
personal-identity.relation: The editors' introduction opens with Socrates on trial for corrupting the youth of Athens and quips that on stage before the youth of Athens, Georgia, Cash could claim he was only asking "What is truth?" It frames Cash as Kris Kristofferson's "walking contradiction" whose paradoxes generate the book's questions: how evil fits a world rated by a benevolent God, where the enduring "I" hides while Cash insisted he was always changing, and what makes a law unjust. It also presents the Man in Black as social critic lobbying officials at San Quentin and Folsom for prison reform and raising money for reservation schools, before welcoming readers with the 1969 Arthur, Illinois concert where hippies and Amish rubbed shoulders.

personal-identity.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
personal-identity.title: Authentic Cash
personal-identity.relation: Butler rehearses how the Johnny Cash persona was socially manufactured: Sam Phillips coined the name "Johnny Cash" for its rebellious marketing value, "Folsom Prison Blues" narrates a prison term Cash never served (and borrowed from Jimmie Rodgers and Gordon Jenkins), and the Man in Black image began as an accident of black shirts at a Memphis church performance. Against Jung's persona-as-mask and Dr. Phil's "authentic core self," and armed with George Herbert Mead's social theory of the self, he argues authenticity is not fidelity to a hidden inner essence but active engagement with the social processes shaping one's identity, the way paper money gains "cash value" through use. Cash invested the imposed persona with value by sincerely living it (for example, writing "Man in Black" to give the black clothes his own meaning), so the construct became genuinely his identity.

personal-identity.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
personal-identity.title: A Modest Conclusion
personal-identity.relation: Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro stage the diachronic-versus-episodic debate about the self (Galen Strawson's episodic view included) against Leigh Edwards's "no single Johnny Cash": the hotel-room-wrecking addict and the Billy Graham touring Christian do not fit one biography. They argue the private J.R. was a third option: on stage he becomes wholly absorbed in story characters (the Folsom narrator, the man who shot a man in Reno) while a self not defined by time slips in and out of the persona, evidenced by his account of gradually shedding "Johnny Cash" after shows. Johnny Cash the public quilt is compared to the Ship of Theseus, every original piece of J.R. replaced yet still owned by him, and the modest conclusion is that J.R., like anyone making a free choice, stood above the timeline of instants and could inhabit both the episodes and the grand narrative.

personal-identity.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
personal-identity.title: Memories Are Made of This
personal-identity.relation: Randall Jensen asks whether Cash's hope of reunion with the dead ('Meet Me in Heaven,' 'If We Never Meet Again This Side of Heaven') is even coherent, using the 'One Piece at a Time' Cadillac and a hypothetical 1954 Plymouth to retell the Ship of Theseus puzzle about identity through part replacement. He canvasses Platonic dualism from the Phaedo (Cash is his soul, the body a rusty cage), the materialist hope that God can reassemble a resurrected body despite dispersed matter, and the psychological-continuity view that persons are 'made of memories,' ending on the duplication problem: if God made two heavenly bodies both carrying Cash's memories, which one would be Cash?

personal-identity.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
personal-identity.title: Case the Promised Land
personal-identity.relation: Herstein reads 'Thunder Road' as an event, not an object: the screen door slam and Mary's waving dress form a single event that language can only serially narrate, and Whitehead's event ontology (with Ricoeur's Time and Narrative on how we discover and rewrite ourselves in stories, and Emerson's 'monstrous corpse' of memory from 'Self Reliance') explains why the Seanachie's tale creates a world rather than describing one. His own autobiographical turn — first hearing the song while stuck in a dead-end life, then at the 1980 Los Angeles 'Factory' performance watching Springsteen's voice resolve two warring rhythms by adding a third — shows narrative running backwards, retelling and redeeming the past, which is why the burnt-out Chevrolets are already behind the dirty hood. The solo-harmonica version strips away porch, vision, and redemption to desolation, yet the conclusion is freedom: because the events of the world await our creative retelling, you are the Seanachie of your own life, and 'maybe I am that young, after all.'

personal-identity.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
personal-identity.title: Retelling Our Stories
personal-identity.relation: Milsky uses Ricoeur and MacIntyre's narrative theory of personal identity to read the two Sharons: Boomer's fabricated human backstory suffers a 'factual disruption' when she shoots Adama, while Athena's 'disruption of belief' comes from falling in love with Helo. He argues such disruptions — also suffered by humans like Starbuck (recovered memories of abuse in 'Maelstrom'), Roslin (coming to believe she is Pythia's dying leader), and Helo — need not destroy identity, since narratives can be retold, as the Final Four do in 'Crossroads, Part 2' with Tigh's 'My name is Saul Tigh' speech. Third-party narratives (Six disowning Athena, the crew refusing to see Boomer as Boomer) show identity is partly socially constructed and can become self-fulfilling prophecy, with Boomer's blackouts resembling dissociative identity disorder.

personal-identity.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
personal-identity.title: Frak-tured Finality
personal-identity.relation: Booth argues that the 'Resistance' webisodes fracture BSG's narrative across television and Internet, forcing viewers to actively construct the story — Jammer's execution in 'Collaborators' and Duck's suicide bombing only make full sense if you pieced the webisodes together — and that this viewer-side fragmentation mirrors the characters' fractured identities. Drawing on Foucault's constructed self, Deleuze and Guattari's 'schizophrenia,' Goffman's performed roles, and Haraway's cyborg, he reads Baltar's 'Am I a Cylon?', Boomer's amnesia in 'Water,' Hera's human-Cylon hybridity, and Tigh's choice in 'Crossroads' to actively construct who he will be. The payoff: there is no central location for the self, the narrative, or Cylonhood — each becomes whole only through active construction.

personal-identity.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
personal-identity.title: “Sometimes You Just Have to Bow to the Absurd”
personal-identity.relation: Eberl weighs genetic enhancement and cloning through Trek's test cases: Julian Bashir's parents' enhancement leaves him feeling 'a fraud' ('You used to be my father. Now, you're my architect'), the Moab IV 'Masterpiece Society' breeds out 'the unknown, self-discovery, things that make life worth living', and the Jem'Hadar show desire itself engineered for control. He argues the right to an open future constrains designing children (B'Elanna's wish to de-Klingonize her baby, Worf pressuring Alexander), defends genetic treatment while rejecting genetic determinism, and uses Kass and Rovane with Picard and Shinzon, the Mariposa clones, and Trip's clone Sim to show clones are numerically distinct persons. Against Malik's Augments quoting Nietzsche — 'mankind is something to be surpassed' — the chapter argues the Übermensch demands self-mastery through philosophy, not eugenic engineering, tracing eugenics from Plato's Guardian breeding scheme through Buck v. Bell to modern prenatal selection.

personal-identity.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
personal-identity.title: “I Feel Exactly What You Feel”
personal-identity.relation: Runs Star Trek's transporter and android stories as thought experiments on personal identity: the body theory (Kirk rejecting android Korby — 'Dr. Korby was never here' — and Picard telling the resurrected Rishon Uxbridge 'you do not exist'), the brain theory ('Spock's Brain,' Bashir refusing to replace half of Vedek Bareil's brain), and Locke's memory theory as vindicated by the Trill (Lela Dax's 'a person is but the sum of their memories,' the 'Dax' extradition hearing over Curzon's crimes). Riker's transporter double in 'Second Chances' and the Tuvix fusion then break the memory theory through fission and fusion, prompting Parfit's move that psychological continuity, not numerical identity, is what matters in survival. Memory erasure in 'Dagger of the Mind' and Kurn's rebranding after the failed Mauk-to'Vor in 'Sons of Mogh' count as death if we are our memories.

personal-identity.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
personal-identity.title: Solutions to the Problem The youth whose destiny it is to lead Hyrule to the
personal-identity.relation: Robison asks how Link stays the same person through Ocarina of Time's child/adult switches, Twilight Princess's wolf form, and Wind Waker's consciousness-projection into seagulls and mages. Physical-continuity views fail because Link's body changes or is left behind; Locke's memory-based psychological continuity fails because adult Link's past hasn't happened yet when he travels back. After a Ship of Theseus variant (Ganon reassembling Tetra's sunken planks) she proposes that in Zelda's stipulative metaphysics, destiny, the goddess-given roles of courage, wisdom, and power, is the necessary and sufficient condition of identity, fitting videogame universes whose metaphysics are fixed by designers.

personal-identity.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
personal-identity.title: Epilog-Rolling
personal-identity.relation: Patton turns the Tin Woodman's backstory—the enchanted axe that costs Nick Chopper his legs, arms, torso and heart, then his head, each replaced by the tinsmith—into a cyborg thought experiment about how much of a person can be swapped out before the person is gone. After a framing nod to Plato's Republic on censoring frightening tales (his father's ban on 'mental violence' fantasy), he brings in Derek Parfit: the R-relation, the 'My Division' brain-split, and the Branch-Line teletransportation case are mapped onto the Woodman (including a hypothetical straw-bodied second Nick) to argue that survival gets different answers from first-person and third-person perspectives. The closing wildcat episode, where the tinned Woodman neatly decapitates a wildcat to save a field mouse, is offered as textual evidence that the tin head failed to preserve moral consistency—so the original Nick Chopper is gone for good, and the Scarecrow's shared brain explains why the two friends later refuse to part.

personal-identity.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
personal-identity.title: Getting to Oz
personal-identity.relation: Auxier uses the Wizard's demand that Dorothy kill the Witch to split 'ought' from 'can'—ethics from the metaphysics and logic of possibility—and then asks whether Oz is a genuinely possible world. He explains David Lewis's modal realism (every genuine possibility actual in its own causally isolated world) through counterfactuals about which network aired the film, dissolves the silver-versus-ruby slippers conflict by assigning book-Oz and film-Oz to different possible worlds, and argues that since no flat contradiction can be eked out of the Oz stories, Lewis is committed to Oz's being real—though Maguire's inter-world travel and Elphaba's hybrid, soul-less trans-world identity (her counterpart in our world being, playfully, Dorothy) stretch Lewis's 'counterparts' doctrine to its limit. Peirce supplies the closing caution, with Boole, that logic is a set of norms for how we can and ought to think rather than a proven mirror of other worlds, so believing in Oz's full reality remains permissible fun rather than an obligation.

personal-identity.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
personal-identity.title: You Can Go Home Again
personal-identity.relation: Fortune stages the movie as a morality play between two conceptions of personhood: the Wizard is an atomist, a self-sufficient ball from the Chuck E. Cheese ball pit who is the same humbug in Omaha or Oz and who reduces heart, brains, and courage to a testimonial, a diploma, and a medal, while Dorothy is a relationalist, a pineapple chunk that belongs on one particular pizza, a person constituted by her web of relations to home. 'There's no place like home' is therefore the relationalist's slogan, an acceptance of home for everything it is, good and bad, with Toto's fate still unresolved under Miss Gulch's law. He closes by suggesting the film's delayed television-era triumph is existential nostalgia: modern, rootless, ear-budded Americans keep watching because the relationalist country it mourns is 'what's in our blood.'

personal-identity.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
personal-identity.title: Transformers and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: The editors' introduction frames the volume around First Contact with a robotic civilization: citing SETI's Seth Shostak, they argue aliens are more likely to be AI machines than little green men, with the Autobot-Decepticon civil war catching humans in between on a moral as well as physical plane. They pose the book's questions about Optimus Prime and Megatron: whether Transformers have moral status and minds despite passing the Turing Test, whether they have souls and are capable of Platonic or erotic love, and what makes Optimus the same being whether robot or vehicle. Probing Transformer nature, they conclude, is really probing human nature, since Transformers are our own creations.

personal-identity.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
personal-identity.title: Transformers and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: Spicher argues that when Bumblebee trades his beat-up 1976 Camaro for a shiny 2007 model only his appearance changes (an accidental change), never his identity, because transforming is part of a Transformer's essence like a human wearing a mask. Locke's memory continuity and Thomson's bodily criterion each fail - the embryo, coma, and corpse problems, plus the thought experiment of Megatron's memories transplanted into another body - so he defends an Aristotelian composite of form and matter in which the Spark is the soul-like form organizing the machine body, preserving identity through transformation as form guides matter toward actuality.

personal-identity.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
personal-identity.relation: Four 'Phase Five' puzzle essays. Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro use Secret Wars to test omnipotence: the Beyonder, Doom, and Galactus cannot do the logically impossible (no spherical cubes, no stone too heavy to lift), two omnipotent beings collide, and a truly omnipotent being has no desires - so villains can never climb to the top they crave. Matthewson and Wall use Frankfurt cases and reasons-responsive source compatibilism to explain why Eddie Brock is responsible for Venom's villainy (he voluntarily bonded and endorses the symbiote's adjusted psychology) while Anne Weying, horrified by what the symbiote made her do, bears only minimal blame. Pickavance reconstructs the Ship of Theseus with Sandman's 'mansand': combining part exchange with materialism lets Norman Osborn reassemble a duplicate Sandman from his scattered remains, and since neither principle nor soul-dualism comes free, personal identity through material change remains unsolved. Loader argues Brainiac's reinvention as a 'facts and logic' computer embodies disembodied Cartesian AI, so the frame problem (Dennett's exploding robots) and embodied cognition (Clark's Tetris, Dreyfus) suggest his detachment from body and world would make him less, not more, intelligent than the humans he scorns.

personal-identity.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
personal-identity.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: The editors' introduction argues that His Dark Materials is philosophy-rich rather than a mere children's fantasy: its metaphysics of parallel worlds, dæmons, angels, armored bears, and mulefa poses genuine epistemic questions and ethical dilemmas. It frames the volume around the controversy over whether exposing children to Pullman's anti-religious vision is spiritual violence or an education in thinking for oneself like Lyra. It also sets up the trilogy's alternative afterlife, where Lyra frees the dead from the drab land of the dead to dissolve into Dust, and flags dæmons as puzzles of personal identity and soul-body interaction.

personal-identity.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
personal-identity.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: Harris and Baer use the Boatman scene ('Pan is me... we'd die') to test criteria of personal identity against the trilogy: Lyra and Will's inference to a thinking third part, the ghost, reenacts Descartes's dualist reasoning about mind-body distinctness, Iorek's lack of a ghost exemplifies the same-body criterion, and Pantalaimon's instant shape-shifting favors the psychological criterion, spelled out through Locke's prince-and-cobbler memory thought experiment and Parfit's psychological connectedness and continuity. They ask whether Lee Scoresby's dissolution into conscious atoms that reunite with Hester's counts as genuine survival, best accommodated by Locke's consciousness criterion or a panpsychist matter criterion, with Chalmers cited as the contemporary defender of conscious matter. The chapter closes with individuation, whether Lyra and Pan are one person or two, applied to a Primal Fear-style multiple-personality murder trial, the hypothetical of Pan killing someone while Lyra is innocent, and living wills in persistent vegetative states.

personal-identity.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
personal-identity.title: Coda
personal-identity.relation: Gimbel asks what makes a band remain the same band over time: Led Zeppelin survived replacing drummer John Bonham with his son Jason, yet Page and Jones insist no singer could replace Robert Plant. Working through Plutarch's Ship of Theseus, Aristotle's essential properties, and Locke's continuity account of identity, he uses Peter French's distinction between aggregates (groups defined by membership) and conglomerates (defined by role structure) to argue a band is a conglomerate. The twist is that a reunion would be a monument like Theseus's preserved ship rather than a working vessel: Plant is an Aristotelian essential of what Zeppelin was, while Jason Bonham's family link supplies the reverence and facsimile-fidelity a monument needs.

personal-identity.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
personal-identity.title: Mr. Monk Is Mr. Monk
personal-identity.relation: Malloy runs the classic theories of personal identity through Monk episodes. Bodily (really brain) identity fails when 'the Monk' — the reckless medicated alter of 'Mr. Monk Takes His Medicine' — shares Monk's body and brain yet is not held responsible, and Stanley Tucci's method actor in 'Mr. Monk and the Actor' shows that copying Monk's looks and behavior does not transfer identity. Locke's memory theory breaks on the amnesia of 'Mr. Monk Bumps His Head' (Monk becomes roofer 'Jerry') and the blackout in 'Mr. Monk and the Rapper,' and Reid's brave-officer paradox yields contradiction once recovered Monk remembers being both Monk and Jerry. Hume's bundle theory — 'I never can catch myself,' the self as theatre of successive perceptions — grounds psychological continuity's graded identity, but then cult-swayed Monk in 'Mr. Monk Joins a Cult' might count as a different person, making his deprogramming a kind of murder; the chapter closes by rejecting Reid and Butler's 'simple and unassayable' escape, insisting a philosopher, like a detective, must keep theorizing how Monk stays Monk.

personal-identity.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
personal-identity.title: Is Everybody Disembodied (or, Have We Always Been Posthuman Beings )
personal-identity.relation: Stevens uses the film's closing voice-over 'I am Tetsuo' in Otomo's Akira to run the classic identity-and-mind problems: Heraclitus's river and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus ask whether the grotesquely transformed, Akira-absorbed Tetsuo is still the same person, while Descartes's cogito — riffed as 'cogito ergo Tetsuo' — Turing's Test, and Searle's Chinese Room test whether a voice that seems to think proves a thinker behind it (syntax is not yet shown sufficient for semantics, though Edwin Hutchins's distributed cognition reads the Room from the inside out). Weighing embodiment (Pinker's brain-makes-mind, Dennett's self as a 'center of narrative gravity') against disembodiment (Akira levelling Neo-Tokyo from nothing but cryogenically stored remains; Tetsuo's matter teleportation), he concludes through the problem of representation — every utterance is re-presented, as in Augustine's guilty tears over Dido — that we always treat semblances of thinkers as thinkers, so we may have always been decentered, re-presented, posthuman beings no different from Tetsuo and Akira.

personal-identity.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
personal-identity.title: Dead People
personal-identity.relation: William Larkin pits Descartes's res cogitans (the person as psychological continuum, reinforced by Locke's prince-and-cobbler body-switch) against a res corporealis view in which bodily continuity suffices for identity, using Romero's Dead films as intuition pumps. The terror of Roger's 'I don't want to be walking around like that' and Rain's request in Resident Evil only makes sense if we think it would be us rising as zombies, and the tragedy of Karen Cooper devouring her father or Johnny menaging Barbara only lands if the same person persists. Against the 'just dead flesh' scientists and the mall-memory reading of Dawn, he argues zombie psychology is merely residual instinct, so our fear and pity reveal we really believe persons survive as corpses, hence as bodies, not as minds.

personal-identity.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
personal-identity.title: Zombies and Us
personal-identity.relation: Hamish Thompson asks what could justify killing zombies, canvassing self-defense, total-brain-death criteria, and release from obligations to a radically altered person, using Shaun of the Dead's mother-killing, Bub's trained shooting in Day of the Dead, White Zombie's piano-playing heroine, and the pod-people substitutions of Invasion of the Body Snatchers. He deploys Hume's bundle theory of the self as a fiction of succeeding perceptions and Parfit's graded psychological continuity (with Locke's prince/cobbler case) to argue identity comes in degrees, so zombie termination is never as clean as the genre pretends. The chapter ends by turning the lens around: Shaun's checkout-line beepers and Ed's sofa-and-video-game existence suggest ordinary lives differ from zombiehood only by intermittent acts of imaginative self-direction.

personal-identity.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
personal-identity.title: Oh Yes, There Will Be Blood
personal-identity.relation: Rachel Robison asks why mythology — from Elizabeth Bathory's blood baths to Dracula's control over Mina once she drinks his blood, and True Blood's Sookie sensing and desiring Bill and then Eric — credits blood with immortality, youth, erotic compulsion, and shared knowledge, including the vampire's dark inversion of the Eucharist. Her answer runs through the history of philosophy and medicine: Aristotle, Empedocles, and Chrysippus located rationality in the heart and made blood its product, while Galen's humoral theory and bloodletting treated blood as the carrier of health, temperament, and identity — so blood naturally reads as the vehicle of personal identity, free will, and even knowledge, explaining how drinking it could transmit a maker's self to Sookie or Mina. She then asks whether the synthetic 'True Blood' of HBO's show could carry the same powers, concluding it works only if some property is shared with real blood or if the power attaches to the act of drinking what is taken as blood.

personal-identity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
personal-identity.title: 8 - Playing Around with Identity
personal-identity.relation: Wandel and Beavers take Groundhog Day's Phil Connors as the model of trying on selves, and apply Goffman's dramaturgical Presentation of Self to see Facebook as a stage where users experiment with identity. Because friends from every part of life watch at once, a 'restraint of accountability' disciplines pretending, much like childhood pretend play or a fraternity's teasing calls members to account for their oddities. Against critics who see fragmentation and narcissism, they argue this dynamic can support becoming who one already is - a more authentic, grounded self - closing with Plato's 'Life must be lived as play'.

personal-identity.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
personal-identity.title: The Limits of Change
personal-identity.relation: Osborne and Coombs turn the Ship of Theseus — every plank replaced, plus Hobbes's reassembled-planks variant — into the 'Aston Villa Paradox': with owner, manager, players, crest and even the shade of claret and blue changed, what makes it the same club fans sing 'Villa till I Die' for? Finding that presentism and Sider's four-dimensionalism cannot say which side on the 2006 pitch was really AVFC, they adopt Lynne Rudder Baker's constitution view: fans create the football-favorable circumstances that constitute a club, so it persists through total replacement of parts as long as supporters keep conferring identity and value — which is why Gareth Barry's value collapsed when he left, and why fans judged Glazer's Manchester United to have stopped existing while welcoming Lerner's Villa.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: A Dead End
personal-identity.relation: Stokes uses regeneration and the multi-Doctor episodes ('The Three Doctors', 'The Five Doctors', 'The Trial of a Time Lord') to test theories of personal identity: Locke's memory criterion, Reid's transitivity objection, Parfit's teleporter and 'branch-line' cases, Nozick's closest-continuer theory, four-dimensional person-stages, animalism, and narrative identity. He argues that no objective-continuity account explains why the Fifth Doctor still cares whether he himself survives in 'The Caves of Androzani', and hints that being the Doctor may be a subjective stance in which each incarnation takes ownership of the others as itself.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: Doctor Who and the Ultimate Answer
personal-identity.relation: Littmann mines Who scenarios as hypotheticals that test identity theories: regeneration, natural doubles like Salamander, impersonating Zygons and Chameleons, bodiless beings like Omega and the Great Intelligence, TARDIS jumps that break spatiotemporal continuity, Cassandra possessing the Doctor and Rose, memory theft by Eldrad and the Daleks, and the Master's year as the unrecognizably good Professor Yana. He argues that sameness of body (including the four-dimensional 'worm' of spatiotemporal continuity), the memory criterion, and psychological similarity each fail, leaving the question of what makes the Doctor the Doctor — and you you — open.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: What’s Persistence Without Identity
personal-identity.relation: Hanley first fixes what is true in the Who canon (treating fiction as pretense), then asks how the Doctor persists when regeneration replaces 'every single cell' and when John Smith's amnesia severs memory in 'Human Nature'. Rejecting bodily continuity (the severed hand of 'The Christmas Invasion'), soul 'pellets', and simple memory (Reid's transitivity problem), he defends neo-Lockean mental continuity plus Nozick's closest-continuer schema to explain why Jackson Lake, the regrown Doctor, and DoctorDonna in 'Journey's End' are not the Doctor, and closes with Parfit's claim that psychological continuity rather than identity is what matters in survival, alongside Lewis's space-time-worm alternative.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: I Think, Therefore I Exist . . . I Think
personal-identity.relation: Johnson argues that the Platonic-Cartesian soul is refuted by neuroscience (Phineas Gage, Penfield's stimulation studies), and that Locke's memory criterion fails on Reid-style transitivity cases like DoctorDonna and on Bernard-Williams-inspired worry about the amnesiac John Smith, who would still dread the Family of Blood's torture. Parfit's causal-continuity criterion then wrongly makes the meta-crisis Doctor of 'Journey's End' identical with the Tenth, so Johnson defends a four-dimensionalist 'time worm' view on which the Doctors are stages of one person — before a final sorites-style argument (heaps, spin-offs like Torchwood) suggests that 'persons' may not exist at all.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: Here They Are ... Ready to Outsit Eternity
personal-identity.relation: Argues that regeneration helps show life after death is logically possible: the successive Doctors (Fourth to Fifth in 'Logopolis') prove identity survives radical personality change, so a perfected heavenly Joe would still be Joe. Testing whether identity lies in body or memory, he contrasts John Smith in 'Human Nature' (same body, so same person) with the 'Journey's End' Doctor-clone whose replicated memories Rose rejects ('But he's not you'), favoring bodily continuity. This leaves the unavailability-of-atoms problem, which he solves with van Inwagen's theory that God removes and preserves our bodies at death like a divine cryonicist, echoing the Fourth Doctor's 'ready to outsit eternity' tribute in 'The Ark in Space'.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: Love and Doctors
personal-identity.relation: Asks whether 'the Doctor' is a Kripkean rigid designator naming one individual or a non-rigid role filled by different people, using the Ninth Doctor's deathbed doubts and the Time Crash memory loop to settle on the rigid reading. He then deploys Locke's body/organism/person distinctions, Parfit's overlapping psychological-connectedness fix to Reid's transitivity objection (Sarah Jane across 1983-1996-2006), and the amnesia-prone regenerations and the Valeyard to show the organism survives regeneration while the person might not. Finally he argues that because DoctorTwo in 'Journey's End' shares all the Doctor's psychologically connected memories of Rose, fission makes them two persons with equal claim, so Rose gets the person she actually loved.

personal-identity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
personal-identity.title: One More Thing, Don’t Blink!
personal-identity.relation: Uses Carroll's art-horror theory (monster = threat plus disgust) to ask why the Weeping Angels of 'Blink' terrify despite being beautiful, harmless-seeming statues. The answer: by dumping Kathy and Billy in the past they destroy identity itself, understood through Frankfurt's account of caring and MacIntyre's narrative identity, since everything a person cares about is tied to a time and place. Since the Angels provoke no disgust, the chapter revises Carroll: horror is fear plus impotence, and forcing victims to survive by not blinking makes viewers feel their powerlessness over their own bodies.

personal-identity.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
personal-identity.title: Long-Term Identity
personal-identity.relation: Asks whether the final Duncan Idaho ghola, whose serial memories wake during his encounter with Murbella, is the same person as the original who died holding off nineteen Sardaukar. It tests physical continuity, Locke's memory-based sameness of person (Hayt becomes Duncan only when the original's consciousness reawakens), Parfit's psychological connectedness with its redescription of identity as survival through quasi-memory, Schechtman's narrative self-constitution, Velleman's self-inventing characters, and four-dimensionalist 'space-time worms' on which Leto II's 3,500 years and the Duncans' gappy five millennia are single long selves. Herbert's moral: identity is not fixed—societies and technologies, from the Tleilaxu tanks to the Sisterhood's swift accommodation, keep redrawing what counts as the same person. Same Duncans, same person.

personal-identity.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
personal-identity.title: Get Out of My Mind!
personal-identity.relation: Runs Lady Jessica's spice-agony Other Memory through Locke's Essay: if a person is a 'thinking intelligent being' whose identity extends as far as her consciousness reaches, then Jessica—having received the memories of every Reverend Mother back to Raquella Berto-Anirul—must be identical with Raquella, and with Alia who shares the same memories, which is absurd. Thomas Reid's gallant officer is staged as Gurney Halleck, who remembers Rabban's whip but not his sister's eyes, breaking the transitivity of memory-based identity. The chapter closes with three modern paths—psychological continuity, Eric Olson's animalism, and Dennett's selves as 'centers of narrative gravity'—plus a Lockean coda defending the Abomination Alia as a person no fixed class of nature could exclude.

personal-identity.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
personal-identity.title: A Story in Search of a Narrator
personal-identity.relation: Brian Gregor reads Dexter through Charles Taylor's 'self-interpreting animal': Dexter's identity is not a fixed thing but comes into being through self-interpretation within an inescapable framework of value, so even his 'Am I good? Am I evil?' rebellion and the Nietzschean Übermensch reading fail to escape the deeper convictions about innocence, evil and desert that Harry's Code presupposes - as his guilt over the innocent Farrow shows. The chapter interprets Dexter's serial failures at being 'seen' - Harry's 'only one who really saw me', Brian's fraternal 'you can be yourself with me', Lila's probing, and Miguel Prado as Aristotle's friend, 'another self' - as Hegelian struggles for recognition that collapse because his real self can never come into the open. Finally, drawing on MacIntyre's narrative account of identity, it argues Dexter is literally a story in search of a narrator, whose selfhood persists through flashbacks, blood slides and noir-style voice-overs, and whose humanity shows in the need to have his account of himself heard and corrected by another.

personal-identity.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
personal-identity.title: Mastering the Chief
personal-identity.relation: Joyce Havstad asks which of the millions of player-instantiated Master Chiefs is real, and whether the flash-cloned John left behind on Eridanus II is the same boy. She runs the Ship of Theseus on the MJOLNIR armor—a technician rebuilds a second suit from every replaced piece—contrasting material with historical continuity, and adds Hobbes's reassembled-planks version. Locke's prince-and-cobbler memory criterion is reconstructed across John, John-117, and Master Chief, then broken by Reid's brave-officer objection, leaving psychological continuity as the best but imperfect criterion; the Flood's conversion of a Covenant soldier into a Combat Form shows identity lost once original sentience is gone.

personal-identity.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
personal-identity.title: Where Parfit Went Wrong
personal-identity.relation: Peter Ludlow and Chiara Repetti-Ludlow read Red vs. Blue as an intuition pump for personal identity, running through Locke's prince-and-cobbler, Bernard Williams's duplicated Guy Fawkes, Shoemaker's brain transplant, and Wiggins's split brain before aiming at Parfit. Project Freelancer's Director fractures the Alpha AI into fragments (Epsilon's memories, Omega's rage) recombined into the Meta, and they argue intuitions break against Parfit here: psychological continuity via small fractured pieces—unlike Parfit's fission into two substantial halves—does not secure the source's survival. Church's disembodied AI existence and the ever-present agent-AI voice (Agent Washington driven mad by Epsilon) illustrate Putnam's 'soul stuff' and the extended-mind hypothesis of Chalmers and Clark better than Chalmers waving his iPhone.

personal-identity.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
personal-identity.title: Surviving Fusion
personal-identity.relation: Amy Kind asks whether the Holmes who marries Laurie R. King's Mary Russell could still be Holmes, weighing Aristophanes' speech in Plato's Symposium (Zeus split the original spherical humans, and love seeks our lost half) against Derek Parfit's fusion case from Reasons and Persons, in which two people grow into one body, which we would all find horrifying. Against Nozick's account of love as becoming a 'we', Delaney's merger and Gaylin's 'fused identity', she deploys Marilyn Friedman's federation model, lovers as sovereign states forming a flexible third entity, to argue that Holmes and Russell's marriage survives because its fusion reshapes identity without obliterating it: his 'half a creature with two brains and four eyes' and her refusal of the nickname 'Zherlock Mary' show both lovers keeping separate selves.

personal-identity.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
personal-identity.title: Does the Top Fall Does It Matter in the End
personal-identity.relation: Andersen contends Inception goes one deeper than Descartes: where the dream argument threatened only the external world, inception threatens the autonomy of thought itself, since the 'core conception' that defines identity - Fischer's reading of his father's dying word 'disappointed' - can be implanted. Tracing Nolan's obsession with thought-manipulation through his earlier films (the manipulator Cobb of Following, Leonard's self-deception in Memento, the Joker's schemes), he shows inception as co-opting subjectivity. Against the Cartesian answer of doubting everything, the fates of Mal and Cobb in Limbo - where doubt, once planted, grows devastatingly, and where a totem cannot guard against self-deception - teach that the way back to reality is the leap of trust in others: only by opening himself to Ariadne, Miles and his children can Cobb turn away from the top and go home.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Chapter 05 - Just Who and How Many Do You Think You Are
personal-identity.relation: Feist opens with Dr. Wigan's autopsy of a man with half a brain and a full mind, moves through the split-brain experiments (the left hand writing 'PIPE' for a concealed pipe as the hemispheres autocomplete each other), and lands on Joseph Bogen's revived thesis that each of us has two minds that merely feel like one. He shows Dick threading Bogen's actual sentences mid-dialogue into A Scanner Darkly so the reader experiences a voice from nowhere, foreshadowing how Arctor's self explodes under the scramble suit, the Fred persona and Substance D into separate persons, Bob and Fred, who end up unsure who, and how many, they are.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: The User Illusion
personal-identity.relation: The chapter interleaves a doctor's line-card quiz of Fred with Bogen and Wigan's claims that each cerebrum is 'a distinct and perfect whole as an organ of thought' and that our cherished 'inner conviction of Oneness' is mere opinion. Descartes supplies the target: a partless mind known directly and with certainty, external things known only indirectly through possibly misleading ideas, and Dick, we are told, flips this picture so the inside is messy and the outside clear.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: In a Mirror, Darkly
personal-identity.relation: The chapter stages Arctor's bishop's-robe musing ('What is identity? Where does the act end?') against the classic puzzles: the Ship of Theseus with its two reassembled vessels, and the baby photos you share no cells with. Locke gives memory plus a unified 'thinking, intelligent being' with real unity; Hume bites the bullet, finding only perceptions in introspection, never a self, so the self's identity over time is a normal, inescapable delusion like a mountain's. All of it converges on Fred watching Bob and asking 'who am I? Which one of them is me?'

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: You Don’t Always Get Along
personal-identity.relation: The chapter animates Hume's bundle as a 'little republic' of mental citizens without a universal citizen, staging a dialogue between Person-Hume, who cannot believe there is no self, and Philosopher-Hume, who counsels beer and billiards. It traces the view back to Plato's Republic: the tripartite soul (with Freud's id-ego-superego as a modern rerun), the example of desiring and refusing the same cold beer when you must collect your mother from the airport, and Leontius raging at his own eyes before the corpses, cross-chatter as civil strife among inner citizens, exactly what the doctors diagnose as Fred's symptom.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Follow the Psyche
personal-identity.relation: The chapter assembles Dick's survival-of-the-psyche cases: Agneta Rautavaara kept alive as a brain in a nutrient bath, Professor Thomas's conscious brain piloting a spaceship, the wub transferring into Captain Franco mid-execution, and the Rexorian consciousness in 'Human Is', then grounds the pattern in Locke's prince-and-cobbler and detached-little-finger thought experiments: 'consciousness makes personal identity.' Everything is codified as the Psyche Continuity Rule, to keep track of the person follow the psyche, with brains mattering only as convenient storage vessels.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: The Perils of Rekall, Inc
personal-identity.relation: The chapter runs through three incompatible backstories for Total Recall's Quaid, Cohaagen's infiltration plot, Hauser's genuine defection and self-erasure, or a Rekall trip gone live, and shows that in all three no single psyche links the life stages, forcing a Body Continuity Rule and then a Combined Rule that follows the psyche when mental life is unified and the body when it is disjointed. Paycheck's Jennings, who starts referring to his earlier self in the third person, exposes the rule's weak joint: deciding when a mental life counts as sufficiently disjointed.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Gotta Have Soul
personal-identity.relation: The chapter tests a Soul Continuity Rule: the wub and Hauser survive because their souls do, though Locke himself denies the soul is the person, and Leibniz's King-of-China bargain, become the richest man if you forget everything, shows why, since it would amount to being annihilated while a King of China is created in your place. Kant's case of one mental life relayed across a chain of souls yields just one person, and the rule's practical failure is evidential: nothing could tell one soul with swapped psyches from swapped souls in the same body.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Future Selves and Imposters
personal-identity.relation: The chapter builds a counterexample from Imposter: suppose the same mind-transfer process makes the alien android an imposter in one story but the dying Olham's chosen future self in another, with identical bodily and mental continuity but opposite verdicts, so the Combined Rule fails. Intention cannot rescue the Soul Rule either, since in a government-forced transfer Olham would absurdly have to say 'I am dead over there across the room' if souls simply went where we wanted.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Selfless
personal-identity.relation: The chapter concedes that no rule, psyche, body, soul, or combined, accommodates all of Dick's transformations, and refuses to blame Dick for incoherence: his stories force our own conflicting intuitions about wubs, Quaids and downloaded minds into the open. Pessimist, optimist and skeptic each get a verdict, the skeptic's being the chapter's cliffhanger: if we are none of these things, maybe there are no enduring persons at all.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Is It Live or Is It Memorex
personal-identity.relation: The chapter supplies the missing detail, transfer versus copying: a 'snapshot' of Olham's brain imprinted on an android leaves Olham where he was, and frying the original destroys him rather than moving him, while the bank-transfer versus copying-money analogy and the question of one psyche imprinted on two androids show why the difference matters. Once the mechanics are filled in one way the alien android is a mere copy and Olham dies, filled in another way he survives bodiless, which restores the Psyche Rule pending a science of how psyches are realized in us.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: . . You Ever Take That Test Yourself
personal-identity.relation: Rachael's question to Deckard at the piano ('you ever take that test yourself?') and Luba Luft's suggestion that a human Deckard was killed and replaced put the viewer in the same quandary about implanted memories. The Penfield mood organ lets humans dial numbered moods, so the empathy that supposedly separates humans from androids is itself artificially inducible, while Phil Resch's torment over whether he is an android — compared to Munch's 'The Scream' — shows the human/android line collapsing from inside.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Breakthrough to the Real
personal-identity.relation: Details the disorienting breakthrough in which characters learn that they themselves are fakes: Rachael's distress at her implanted memories ('How can it not know what it is?'), Deckard's paper unicorn in the director's cut confirming his own replicant status, and Ragle Gumm's soft-drink stand dissolving into a slip of paper reading 'SOFT-DRINK STAND' in Time Out of Joint. Each case maps onto the freed cave prisoner's discovery, and the disorientation is pressed onto the viewer: how can I be sure my own life and memories are not a fabrication?

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: How Do We Get Deceived
personal-identity.relation: Catalogues the channels of deception: the senses (the nonexistent Martian canals, Quaid's fat-lady disguise and hologram watch, and the Adjustment Team literally remaking the world) and, more worrisomely, memory, with implanted pasts for Quaid, Rachael, and the Impostor replicant 'so that the Tyrell Corporation can control them better.' Real cognitive science backs the threat: Nader's reconsolidation experiments show memory is Read-Write rather than Read-Only, and 'lost-in-the-mall' interviews implant rich false memories without any drug at all.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Memory and the Brain-Butchers
personal-identity.relation: The section uses Quaid's Rekall-fabricated life, complete with false wedding memories and a false eight-year marriage, to challenge Locke's memory theory of personal identity: implants, together with ordinary forgetting, revision, and loss, show memory cannot be what makes you the same person from one day to the next. Kuato's line, 'A man is defined by his action, not his memory,' is offered as the alternative the following sections develop.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Owning Your Actions, Owning Your Past
personal-identity.relation: This section reconstructs the traditional view of free agency from Aristotle: an action is freely mine when it 'has its origin in the agent himself,' so owning an action means tracing its causal chain back to one's own decision. It explains Aristotle's picture of natures as internal sources of motion and decision as the distinctively human motion, then asks whether Quaid, following the suitcase, video, and clues Hauser pre-arranged, is picking up the chain of his own prior decision, and so becoming himself again.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Inpsychation and Chains of Will
personal-identity.relation: The section develops freedom as extending the will through tools and other people, via Nietzsche's 'inpsychation' and Emerson's conversion of fate into force: Cohaagen shuts off the air through Lori and Harry as Hitler invaded Poland through his soldiers. Locke's memory theory returns demoted to a useful tool rather than an identity-maker, and Nietzsche's Genealogy II.1 on the unbroken 'long chain of will' explains Hauser's masterpiece, planning around his own memory wipe so that Quaid, following the planted clues, re-inpsychates Hauser's decisions.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Quaid’s Problem—Mucky Origins
personal-identity.relation: This section complicates everything: two taped Hausers contradict each other, rebel hero or Cohaagen's 'bosom buddy,' so Quaid cannot settle who he is by tracing his origins. It then generalizes: in the scientific worldview of universal causation, from gravity to DNA inherited through chimps and sea squirts from the primeval muck, no one originates anything, a conclusion quoted at length from Baron d'Holbach's System of Nature, yet first-person deliberation still leaves Quaid feeling the weight of choice.

personal-identity.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
personal-identity.title: Freedom Without Origins
personal-identity.relation: The section rejects randomness as a foundation for freedom, quantum indeterminacy being Epicurus's swerve again, since actions tracing to random particle events are no more mine than law-determined ones, then turns to the ethical problem: if Hauser volunteered and Cohaagen's story is true, freedom-as-origination would require Quaid to become Hauser again, Mercedes included. Quaid's verdict ('The guy's a fucking asshole') shows freedom is also changing course to do what is right; as Lowe says in 'We Can Remember It for You Wholesale,' what defines us is 'not a memory but a desire,' and in breaking with his past Quaid decisively becomes free.

personal-identity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
personal-identity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether 'you' survive a walker bite, testing bodily identity, behaviorism, and functionalism as theories of personal survival against Jenner's verdict that after death 'everything you ever were... gone'. His centerpiece adapts Daniel Dennett: survivors yoke walkers to plows and tanks, dangle meat to move them between positions labeled 1 and 0, and gradually build a rope-and-corpse computer functionally identical to a human brain - which behaviorism and functionalism must call conscious, yet which we can conceive as utterly dark inside. The lesson is that we cannot know whether any system, walker, animal, or AI, is conscious, so treatment of non-human systems may need to err on the side of caution.

personal-identity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
personal-identity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
personal-identity.relation: Delfino and Taylor ask whether Morgan's zombified wife is still a person, which decides whether shooting her is murder.
