time-travel.title: Prognosis
time-travel.relation: William Eaton reconstructs the Doctor's "Blink" philosophy of time using David Lewis's four-dimensionalism. He shows how Lewis's external/personal-time distinction explains the Doctor meeting his own regenerations and reversed causation (a black eye before the punch), and how "Blink" hinges on a closed causal chain (the DVD Easter-egg transcript that authors itself). He rehearses the Grandfather/Bilking paradox and Lewis's "can" equivocation solution, then places the Doctor alongside Horwich and Ismael, arguing the Doctor goes furthest by holding closed causal chains actually exist.

time-travel.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
time-travel.title: Time Travel and Fixed Time
time-travel.relation: Pierce uses Harry Potter's prophecies to analyze destiny, fixed time, and freedom. Distinguishing Trelawney's fraudulent fortune-telling from her two genuine prophecies, he classifies kinds of prophecy (fallible, infallible, self-fulfilling) and, drawing on Aristotle's sea-battle problem and Alexander of Aphrodisias, argues Voldemort's choice of Harry rather than the prophecy itself made it true. He then sorts compatibilist and libertarian readings of Rowling's denial of destiny, argues her time travel (saving Buckbeak) implies a fixed view of time consistent with relativity, and suggests the improbable luck fulfilling prophecies hints at providential guidance.

time-travel.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
time-travel.title: NOTES
time-travel.relation: Richard Davies uses Aristotle's Poetics (the principles of closure, relevance, and the unities of place and time) to defend Lost's tangled narrative as an epic rather than a broken tragedy, arguing that flashbacks, flash-forwards like Jack's 'We have to go back,' and multi-season arcs such as Juliet's remain within Aristotelian bounds. He then imports McTaggart's contrast between eternalism and presentism to explain why a flash-forward is philosophically unsettling, and argues that changing the past (as season 5's time travel invites) generates a logical contradiction from which anything follows, so viewers must 'shield' Hurley's 1977 experiences to keep enjoying the plot.

time-travel.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
time-travel.title: None of It Matters Anyway, Then, Does It
time-travel.relation: William J. Devlin applies David Lewis's distinction between external time and the traveler's personal time to Lost's season 5-6 time jumps, showing how Faraday's eternalist 'whatever happened, happened' (Chang's unbreakable rules) contrasts with the branching-universe model that Faraday later embraces with 'we're the variables.' Lewis's account resolves specific puzzles: why baby Miles and adult Miles can coexist without violating the indiscernibility of identicals, whether Faraday could kill his mother Eloise (the grandfather paradox), and the uncaused causal loop of the compass Locke and Richard pass between 1954 and 2007.

time-travel.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
time-travel.title: NOTES
time-travel.relation: Jeremy Pierce argues that Lost mostly assumes fixed (eternalist) time and moves from its metaphysics to its ethics: even if 'whatever happened, happened,' ordinary morality still applies, so Sayid's shooting young Ben is wrong regardless of his good intentions and Jack is responsible for detonating Jughead even though he causes the very Incident he meant to prevent. Invoking Carneades' distinction between truth and necessity, Pierce holds that foreknowledge (the Man in Black's manipulation, Desmond's course-corrected saving of Charlie) does not erase free choice, concluding via Kate that morality in time travel is 'simply morality, period.'

time-travel.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
time-travel.title: 1. Lost in Time
time-travel.relation: Rard uses David Lewis's definition of time travel—a discrepancy between the duration of the journey and the gap between departure and arrival—to show that 'The Rip Van Winkle Caper' suspended-animation heist is NOT time travel, while 'Last Flight' (Terry returning to save Mackaye) is, complete with a self-consistent causal loop. She then applies Lewis's argument that mundane events always thwart attempts to change the past to 'No Time Like the Past,' where Paul Driscoll is repeatedly distracted from killing Hitler and even accidentally causes the schoolhouse fire he meant to prevent, illustrating that the past is unalterable but interactable.

time-travel.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
time-travel.title: 14. The Science of Alternate Realities
time-travel.relation: Morgan surveys the physics and philosophy behind the show's 'fifth dimension': higher spatial dimensions and parallel universes ('Little Girl Lost'), time as Einstein's fourth dimension and relativistic time dilation ('A Kind of a Stopwatch'), the Grandfather Paradox and the self-consistency of time travel ('Back There,' 'No Time Like the Past'), the Many Worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics ('The Parallel'), and the cosmological multiverse. He closes with Popper's falsification criterion, arguing that unobservable other universes may be, like the show itself, forever 'a dimension of mind.'

time-travel.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
time-travel.title: What Happens to the Present When It Becomes the Past
time-travel.relation: Daniels asks whether the airline passengers in The Langoliers are truly time travelers and what theory of time their dead, tasteless past implies. Using David Lewis's distinction between 'personal time' and 'external time,' he shows the discrepancy between the characters' day-long journey and the few hours that elapse in the present qualifies them as genuine time travelers despite the deserted world. He then rules out presentism (incompatible with time travel via the 'nowhere problem') and eternalism (which denies any privileged present), arguing the vibrant, 'oomph'-laden moving now the characters race to rejoin fits the moving spotlight theory, while the langoliers merely consume the world's contents, not spacetime itself.

time-travel.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
time-travel.title: Time Belongs to the Tower
time-travel.relation: Auxier frames King as 'Tolkien meets Poe' and reads the Dark Tower's temporalization through the literary and psychological experience of time. Drawing on Susanne Langer's 'virtual present' and Sartre's psychology of imagination, he argues readers surrender their real present to a novel's suspended time, which he links to William James's 'will to believe' rather than mere suspension of disbelief. He uses Kant's distinction between amazement (seeing the seemingly impossible) and admiration (accepting it) to explain the psychological cost time travelers like Jake Epping and Wesley Smith should pay, faulting King for keeping ordinary heroes sane while displacing the strain onto insane 'gatekeepers,' and concludes the Tower is 'real' as the way each person binds possibility to their own lived past, present, and future.

time-travel.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
time-travel.title: Ur 88,416
time-travel.relation: Auxier reconstructs the metaphysics of King's Tower across Ur and 11/22/63, treating imagination as a power that defies present time to reach the 'nowhen.' He maps King's multiverse onto Everett's many-worlds and Brian Greene's quantum/quilted multiverses, then extracts three 'laws of Dark Tower dynamics': the obduracy of the past (resistance proportional to how much the future would change), the conservation of harmony (time-strings converging like sympathetic guitar strings on an ideal order), and the danse macabre. He shows the 'reset' Jake believes in is really the creation of new Ur strings, dismantles Al Templeton's meat-buying and epistemic-radiation theories via thermodynamics, and closes with Kant's three functions of imagination to argue time travel is a 'plausible impossible' symbol we can imagine but never actually enact.

time-travel.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
time-travel.title: Who is Who
time-travel.relation: The time-travel chapter grounds Doctor Who's paradoxes in Parmenides and Zeno on the impossibility of change and Aristotle on the logical necessity of past and future statements ('You can't rewrite history!' in 'The Aztecs'), then deploys determinism, David Lewis on the paradoxes of time travel, and the consistency/autonomy principles ('Father's Day,' the Reapers). It uses Leibniz's possible worlds and the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics to read 'Inferno' and 'Turn Left,' arguing quantum indeterminacy and entanglement make the Doctor's 'wibbly-wobbly, timey-wimey' theory of fixed points and flux coherent.

time-travel.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
time-travel.title: Time Travel and Fixed Time
time-travel.relation: Jeremy Pierce analyzes prophecy and destiny in Harry Potter, distinguishing fallible from infallible prophecies and cataloguing how a Seer might access a fixed or open future (raising Aristotle's sea-battle problem about future truths). He argues Trelawney's two 'real predictions' are not merely likely guesses and considers self-fulfilling readings (via Alexander of Aphrodisias and Oedipus), which he rejects since the prophecy did not force Voldemort's choice. Reading Rowling's denial of 'destiny' against her fixed-time treatment of time travel and the improbable luck that fulfills the prophecy, he suggests the story fits a fixed future guided by providence better than libertarian openness or sheer coincidence.

time-travel.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
time-travel.title: 7. Doctor Who as Philosophy Four-Dimensionalism and Time Travel
time-travel.relation: Decker asks what the universe must be like if Doctor Who's time travel were real, using David Lewis's distinction between personal and external time and the TARDIS as a Wellsian (not Thornian) time machine traversing a 'hypertime' vortex. After surveying the arrows of time and paradoxes like the bootstrap paradox ('Day of the Daleks') and the grandfather paradox (imagined via Tegan's grandfather), and rejecting Deutsch-Lockwood's Many-Worlds and growing-block solutions, he argues the Whoniverse fits 'Four-Dimensional Realism'/eternalism, quoting the Twelfth Doctor that time's passage is an illusion of 'still pictures.' He then confronts 4DR's threat to free will and moral responsibility, finding compatibilism and 'fixed points' inadequate given eternalism's succession-not-production of events.

time-travel.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
time-travel.title: 18. Russian Doll as Philosophy Life Is Like a Box of Timelines
time-travel.relation: The chapter treats Russian Doll's time loops (Season One) and time portals (Season Two) as vehicles for the metaphysics of time, comparing them to Groundhog Day and canvassing presentism, eternalism, and the growing-block theory. It argues the show is committed to a Parfit-style 'multiple timelines' solution to the problem of whether looped characters are numerically identical, and rejects a Berkeleyan idealist alternative. Its climax reads Nadia through Camus's Myth of Sisyphus: unable to change significant past events, she becomes an 'absurd hero' who embraces her family and lot in life, smiling in the mirror, so Season Two's lesson (echoing Nietzsche's eternal recurrence) is that meaning comes from owning one's circumstances.

time-travel.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
time-travel.title: 57. Tenet as Philosophy Fatalism Isn’t an Excuse to Do Nothing
time-travel.relation: The chapter reads Nolan's Tenet as an argument for metaphysical fatalism set in a block-universe (eternalism), using the Sator Square, the palindromic 'ten,' and Neil's refrain 'what's happened, happened' as evidence that every event, including the Protagonist's and Kat's, was fated and unchangeable. It deploys David Lewis's solution to the grandfather paradox and reverse causation (Feynman/Wheeler positrons) to show the future cannot kill its ancestors, then argues fatalism entails no libertarian free will, rejecting Frankfurt's compatibilist second-order-desires account and citing van Inwagen that indeterministic acts are no freer. Via a back-tracking counterfactual it concludes fatalism is still no excuse to do nothing, because different action would have yielded a different (annihilated) world.

platonic-love.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
platonic-love.title: The Abandoned Boys
platonic-love.relation: Surveys the classical triad of eros, philia, and agape from Plato's Symposium onward and maps it onto the series: the Weasleys, Ron and Hermione, and Harry and Ginny exemplify romantic love, Dumbledore's remark that Voldemort never had a friend dramatizes the absence of philia, and Lily's self-giving love that repels Quirrell and Voldemort is agape. Because traditional accounts treat love as an act of the will rather than a feeling, Snape's persistent dislikes cannot disprove that his love for Lily has transformed him.

platonic-love.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
platonic-love.title: A Work in Progress
platonic-love.relation: Reads Snape's love for Lily through Plato's Symposium: his childhood watching of Lily with 'undisguised greed', his failure to ask Voldemort to spare her husband and child, 'You disgust me', shows a love that desires Lily's good only as it relates to him, falling short of Aristotle's beloved as 'second self'. Diotima's 'possession of the good forever' and 'giving birth in beauty' describe how his love matures into genuine virtue, a deepening Pope Benedict XVI's picture of love as 'ecstasy', an exodus out of the closed self toward self-giving, completes.

platonic-love.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
platonic-love.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Bronson argues Gibson's fixation on Jesus's suffering is not a Christian oddity but a deeply Jewish mystical one: using William James's four marks of mystical experience (ineffability, noetic quality, transiency, passivity), he reads the Gethsemane opening, where Jesus crushes Satan's serpent and receives a vision of the Father, as a classic mystical trial in the line of Moses at Sinai, Daniel's chariot-throne vision, Elijah's fiery ascent, John the Baptist, Paul's blinding light, and later the Kabbalah and Hasidic masters whose path to God runs through anguish. The Platonic Socrates of the Symposium and Phaedrus (wisdom arriving through the madness of love) and the medieval agreement of al-Ghazali, Maimonides, and Aquinas that reason cannot reach God frame his philosophy-versus-mysticism contrast, including the film's mother-son floorboard scene as love but not full mystical contact. The added scene where Pilate's wife tells him 'If you will not hear the truth, no one can tell you' shows Gibson siding with the mystical path to truth over Pilate's pragmatic one.

platonic-love.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
platonic-love.title: The Force of Love
platonic-love.relation: Lawler identifies Hegel's Absolute Spirit with the Force: Hegel's distillation of religious history - divine nature (the Ewoks worshipping C-3PO), the Roman Empire's transcendent Unhappy Consciousness, and Christianity's Consummate Religion - maps onto the saga's movement, with Anakin's virgin birth, prophecy, fall, and Calvary-like redemption fulfilling the pattern differently from the sinless Savior. The Dark Side is the separate ego asserting 'I' against 'We' (Hobbes's war of all against all culminating in the Emperor), and sin is the belief that one is an isolated individual. Against the Jedi's Stoic detachment (Epictetus), the chapter uses Diotima's ladder of love from Plato's Symposium and Hegel's Faust to argue that only passionate, attached love - Anakin's for Padme and Luke's for his father - descends into darkness and brings the Spirit's balance, so 'the Force is with us.'

platonic-love.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
platonic-love.title: The Mysteries of Love Revealed
platonic-love.relation: Shelby stages Plato's Symposium as a cipher of raps on love to answer hip-hop "love haters" like Jay-Z ("I got ninety-nine problems but a bitch ain't one"): Pausanias's vulgar versus spiritual love, Aristophanes's myth of split halves read through Method Man and Mary J. Blige's "You're All I Need" and Biggie's "Me & My Bitch", and Socrates's ladder from beautiful bodies to Beauty itself, with Lauryn Hill's "Zion" as birth of beautiful offspring. He objects that Socrates makes the beloved a replaceable means to the good, and argues that Alcibiades's drunken confession supplies what is missing - love's possession, exclusivity, reciprocity, and drama (The Roots: "lies come in, that's where the drama begins") - concluding that love ain't just 'bout da booty but demands a vulnerability the love hater rightly fears.

platonic-love.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
platonic-love.title: Love Minus Zero, No Limit or Going, Going Gone
platonic-love.relation: Doug Anderson reads Dylan's Planet Waves as a modern Symposium: each song stages a rung on Diotima's ladder, from the puppy love of "You Angel You" through the physical eros of "Tough Mama" and "Hazel," the agape of "Forever Young," and the complementary true love of "Wedding Song." Like Socrates refusing Alcibiades in "Going, Going Gone," Dylan abandons finite beloveds because his highest eros is the creative act itself - poets achieve the immortality Diotima demands by giving birth to immortal works rather than children. The chapter argues both Plato and Dylan finally define love as desire for truth and beauty that outlasts any particular relationship.

platonic-love.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
platonic-love.title: U2 and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Wrathall's introduction argues U2 is philosophically interesting because its enormous popularity holds up a mirror to what 'we' care about (by Nietzsche's test of how a culture stands toward life) and because the band publicly wrestles with the contradictions of the technological-global economy: unprecedented freedom of choice paired with loss of rooted identity, and distant suffering ('Crumbs from Your Table') that we feel both powerless to fix and responsible for. Its showcase reading treats 'Miracle Drug' as a musical theodicy: Bono's plea 'God, I need your help tonight' is answered by the Edge's guitar and by the Matthew 25:35 refrain, so science and medicine count as works of Christian charity. The piece then frames the volume's essays: Plato's ascent of love in the early songs, Kierkegaardian despair after Achtung Baby, Bono's search for authentic identity, the simulacra of 'Even Better than the Real Thing', being-toward-death in the apocalyptic songs, and the Plato-versus-Aristotle quarrel over music's emotional power.

platonic-love.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
platonic-love.title: U2 and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: McCoy reads U2's early longing songs through the Symposium: Aristophanes' split-beings myth turns 'New Year's Day' into a song about incompleteness whose separated lovers also stand for Poland under Soviet domination, and Diotima's ladder of love reads 'I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For' and 'City of Blinding Lights' as stages ascending from bodily beauty toward the soul and then to Beauty itself. Against a tragic reading, she argues that by Diotima's account the restless lover on the ascent 'begets' discourses and songs, so 'With or Without You' is a song of surrender rather than despair. October's 'Gloria' and 'With a Shout' get the Augustinian ending: the restless heart finds in God the object Romantic love never supplies.

platonic-love.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
platonic-love.title: U2 and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Thomson uses U2's self-declared postmodern phase to define postmodernity itself: a sensitivity to poetic polysemy against modernity's fantasies of total control (Heidegger's reduction of everything to optimizable resource), Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives - defended against the self-refutation charge and narrowed to the dying metanarratives of unity and emancipation - and the Marx-Nietzsche-Freud hermeneutics of suspicion that fragmented the subject, with Kierkegaard and early Heidegger as the resisters. Derrida's 9/11 analysis of autoimmunity and hauntology is read into 'Peace on Earth' and the sorrows that 'learned to swim' in 'Until the End of the World'. The payoff is a polysemic reading of 'Even Better than the Real Thing': risky as a seeming hymn to Baudrillard's simulacra, addressed to a live audience it celebrates a communal love 'even better' than personal love - Diotima's ladder generalized - making the postmodern U2 continuous with the 'Christ-ian' U2 of universal love, sealed by 'One'.

platonic-love.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
platonic-love.title: To Nest or Not to Nest
platonic-love.relation: Halwani and Jones read The Birds as Hitchcock's warning about romantic love: love compromises autonomy through joint decision-making, emotional dependence, and exposure to contingencies like jealousy, betrayal, sickness, and death. Plato's Symposium stages the alternatives, Socrates's ladder of love culminating in the eternal Form of Beauty versus Alcibiades's speech for the painful, contingent love of a unique person, and Nussbaum's reading underscores that these two visions of romantic love are mutually exclusive. In the film, bird attacks strike whenever Melanie, Mitch, Annie, or Lydia treat love as a game or possession, while the caged lovebirds, the only birds that never attack, show that only love sealed in a 'gilded cage' could be cost-free; lovers must instead face love's price wisely, maturely, and courageously.

platonic-love.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
platonic-love.title: Moments of Redemption
platonic-love.relation: Ventimiglia sets Augustine's three answers to the problem of evil (free will, the toddler-at-the-doctor 'greater good,' evil as privation) against Nebraska's title track, where mass murderer Charlie Starkweather's 'I guess there's just a meanness in this world' makes Augustine's metaphysical gymnastics look like sophistry. 'Atlantic City' and 'Johnny 99' show free will compromised by debts, job loss and winners-and-losers, and Springsteen neither glorifies nor explains evil away. What Bruce and Augustine share is the yearning for redemption: Plato's Symposium pictures Eros — poor, barefoot, homeless, a hunger for the beautiful — and Springsteen answers that hunger with temporary moments of deliverance ('meet me tonight in Atlantic City') rather than guaranteed salvation.

platonic-love.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
platonic-love.title: Becoming One
platonic-love.relation: The chapter reads Baltar's Head-Six (and Caprica Six's Head-Baltar) through the gothic Double and Doppelgänger tradition, re-imagined via dissociative identity disorder: Baltar splits off his guilt over the genocide into a female doppelgänger who lets him evade responsibility, as in 'Precipice' where he finds the execution order signed without any memory of signing it. It then links this doubling to Plato's Symposium myth of lovers as split halves seeking their other half, since Baltar cannot function without some version of Six. Its resolution is Aristotle's golden mean: virtue is not choosing one self over another but balancing extremes, for individuals and for humanity and its Double, the Cylons — with Hera as the embodied balance.

platonic-love.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
platonic-love.title: Transformers and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Watson and Arp ask whether Ironhide and Chromia's embrace means Autobots can love, rejecting programmed loving behavior, implanted souls, and wired-in human brains as insufficient for genuine personhood, then sort Transformer relationships into Western conceptions of love. Empedoclean cosmic Love and Strife map onto Primus versus Unicron; Platonic philia ascends to the Form of Beauty, with Transformer souls originating in and returning to the All Spark; Aristotle's three friendships separate Optimus and Sparkplug's virtue-friendship from Megatron and Starscream's mere utility; and Stoic-Kantian equal love explains Autobots saving Decepticons who immediately try to kill them, alongside Christian agape in Autobot family bonds.

platonic-love.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
platonic-love.title: April 6th, 2009
platonic-love.relation: David Roochnik interlaces a loss diary (his daughter's soccer defeat and the Sox's 1998 playoff elimination on the same Saturday, the 2003 Grady Little collapse that gave him chest pain, the 2004 comeback) to argue that losing is an art that teaches what winning cannot. The loser's 'if only' imagination transforms the past, the 'it was only a game' rationalization forces honest reflection about what matters, and shared doom forges Red Sox Nation into a community in a way no Yankees nation could exist, since victors never need to think. He applies Plato's Symposium doctrine of Eros, that to love X is to lack X as Socrates lacks wisdom, to explain why eighty-six years of championship-lack made fandom meaningful, and closes fearing that winning in 2004 and 2007 made the Sox 'normal,' eroding the art of losing that glued the Nation together.

platonic-love.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
platonic-love.title: A Beautiful Destiny
platonic-love.relation: Asks whether the Dalek casing can literally be beautiful, contrasting Kant's aesthetics (free beauty as the mind's fit with reality versus merely 'dependent' beauty of Davros-designed purpose) with Hegel's claim that beauty is thought embodied in matter, peaking in the human form, and Plato's view (via Nehamas's Phaedrus reading) that beauty begins the desire to care for a thing. Alexander of Hales's beauty-within-the-order and the Fourth Doctor's 'Genesis of the Daleks' echo, then Rosenkranz's aesthetic inferno where ugliness exists only as beauty's negation, show beauty and monstrosity need not be opposites. The conclusion is deliberately open: the puzzle forces us into metaphysics about mind and reality, not mere taste.

platonic-love.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
platonic-love.title: Psych and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: C. Scott Sevier argues Henry deliberately recreated Shawn as Aristotle's 'another self' - Lassiter's 'which one?' joke in the kidnapping episode makes the identity explicit - and reads this through Plato's Symposium: via Diotima's ladder of love and the doctrine of forms, Henry achieves immortality by reproducing beauty in his son's educated soul, not just his body. The chapter then frames Shawn's fierce independence against his constant recourse to Henry's voice as the collision between medieval deference to authority and the modern ideal of autonomy in Descartes and Kant, showing that both thinkers quietly borrowed from Augustine (the causal adequacy principle, the good will), so Shawn's 'autonomy' is itself the product of his father's training - an internalized authority indistinguishable from his own.

platonic-love.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
platonic-love.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Celine Morin reads Alicia's love life through the Greek triad agape, eros, and philia as laid out in Plato's Symposium: her unconditional agape for Peter is eroded by his demands for forgiveness ('Stripped', 'Boom'), while the Socratic myth of Eros born from Penia's lack explains why she tells Will their affair is 'romantic because it didn't happen'. She argues Alicia abandons the romantic soul-mate model of her pearl-necklace marriage for Giddens's egalitarian 'pure relationship' with Will, but stays moored to the old family structure, hesitating on the doorstep in the Season Three cliffhanger 'The Dream Time'. Her discovery of feminism through Diane Lockhart is what lets Alicia weigh leaving that structure without destroying her family.

platonic-love.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
platonic-love.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Lisa Warenski reads 'Suzanne' as staging a phenomenological account of self-awareness: with Husserl and Merleau-Ponty the body is not an object but the lived first-person perspective - so 'touch a perfect body with a mind' is literal - and with Sartre's keyhole example from Being and Nothingness we become aware of ourselves through the gaze of the other. Developmental psychology's mother as 'magical mirror,' who reflects the child's emerging mind, is connected to Hegel's paradox of recognition, and to Aristotle's and Neera Badhwar's friends as mirrors of the soul. On this basis Suzanne's mind-touch has epistemic value: love reflects you truly and shows you what you might become, whether as Jesus's agape or Suzanne's appreciative philia.

platonic-love.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
platonic-love.title: 24. Climbing the Ladder of Love
platonic-love.relation: Brendan Shea matches each speech of Plato's Symposium to a Downton plot: Phaedrus's love-inspired heroism to Thomas defending Jimmy from the robbers, Pausanias's legally shaped 'heavenly love' to Mary's path from the Pamuk scandal to wholehearted commitment with Matthew, Eryximachus's love as order to Carson and Mrs. Hughes, Aristophanes's split halves to Anna and Bates, and Agathon's tongue-in-cheek praise of love to Edith's missteps. Socrates's ladder of love then structures Sybil and Tom's romance as physical attraction ascending into love of moral beauty and wisdom - her nursing, his estate stewardship - making love the engine that gives the characters' lives meaning and, as the final rung hints, makes philosophers of them all.

platonic-love.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
platonic-love.title: 3. Wonder and Philosophy as a Way Home
platonic-love.relation: Nathan and Leilani Mueller argue the theme song's 'neighborly day in this beautywood' makes beauty a transcendental leading to wisdom, as in Plato's Symposium ascent to loving the beautiful itself and Aquinas's convertibility of truth, goodness, and beauty. Reading Rogers's questioning of batteries and boxes (episode 1655) through the Meno's genuine curiosity and Pierre Hadot's account of philosophy as a way of life, they tour the show's three philosophical spaces: the domestic living room, the community visit (blind saxophonist Eric Kloss), and Make-Believe as thought experiment.

platonic-love.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
platonic-love.title: 13. The Origins of Self-Love
platonic-love.relation: Anna Marie Fennell reads RuPaul's 'If you can't love yourself, how in the hell you gonna love somebody else?' through theories of self-love. Erich Fromm's four elements of love and Buddhist non-attachment (Jinkx Monsoon's 'water off a duck's back,' the Season Ten Inner Saboteur characters like Eureka's Eufilthior) ground the claim that self-love precedes healthy love for others. Against Aristophanes' myth in Plato's Symposium - the round beings split by Zeus, forever seeking their other half, retold in Hedwig and the Angry Inch - she sides with Ru: completion comes from within, not from a soulmate. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity (the sub-man and nihilist archetypes seen in self-sabotaging queens like Nina Bo'Nina Brown) and bell hooks's All About Love with Branden's six pillars of self-esteem map onto winners like Jinkx, Sharon Needles, Violet Chachki, and Bianca Del Rio, whose drag personas show existence preceding essence.

platonic-love.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
platonic-love.title: 10. Natasha, Gamora, and the Soul Stone
platonic-love.relation: T.J. McSherry frames the two Vormir deaths as 'a futuristic, utilitarian trolley problem,' using Mill's greatest-happiness principle to argue Natasha's martyrdom was the more utilitarian choice (only the Avengers mourn her, while Clint's children need a father), even as Thanos's tossing of Gamora shows the same sacrifice-of-few arithmetic the Avengers rely on. Because the amoral Soul Stone rewards good and evil deaths identically, the chapter turns to Plato's Symposium, casting Red Skull as a Diotiman spirit-mediator of love and ranking each relationship on Diotima's ladder: Thanos is 'stuck at level one' in his stunted love for Gamora, kept alive only as a useful sacrifice, while Clint and Natasha's non-romantic love reaches level four through shared history, empathy, and their fight over who gets to die for the other.

platonic-love.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
platonic-love.title: 12. An Intimate Look at Paul Stanley’s Love
platonic-love.relation: Robert Grant Price maps Paul Stanley's catalogue onto four loves. Eros as soulmate-love follows Aristophanes' split-beings myth from Plato's Symposium ('Forever,' 'Every Time I Look at You'); self-love follows Aquinas's demand that it be 'rightly ordered,' so Stanley's machismo songs pass while Gene's 'I' fails as disordered egomania; bodily love is defended as bawdy dramatic monologue — foreplay between lovers rather than instruction in reducing women to sex objects; and love of life is secularized agape praise in 'I'm Alive,' 'Shout It Out Loud,' and the very title Alive!. Price then asks why love drives art at all, weighing the transcendentals (true, good, beautiful) against the Scruton-versus-Craig-Martin can-of-shit debate, and reads 'Reason to Live' as the claim that only rightly ordered love can ground a life.

platonic-love.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
platonic-love.title: Becoming One
platonic-love.relation: The chapter reads Baltar's head-Six and Caprica Six's head-Baltar through the gothic Double and Doppelganger tradition and Dissociative Identity Disorder: Number Six is Baltar's repressed guilt over betraying humanity ('I'm your subconscious frakking with your mind'), letting him escape responsibility for signing execution orders in 'Precipice,' while Gina Six serves as a tangible Double. Plato's Symposium myth of the split self frames Baltar and Six as two halves of one whole, since he cannot function without some version of Six present, physical or hallucinated. The resolution is Aristotle's golden mean from Book Two of the Nicomachean Ethics: like integration therapy for DID, virtue is a balance between extremes rather than eliminating one side, so Baltar and Six's child Hera may embody the balanced union of human and Cylon.

platonic-love.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
platonic-love.title: Happily Ever After
platonic-love.relation: The chapter maps the Beast's enchanted castle onto Plato's cave: the spellbound household, dimming in the decaying West Wing, are prisoners whose human capacities are suppressed, and Belle is the missing cause that breaks the chains Plato never explains. Using Diotima's teaching from the Symposium that beauty compels love, it reads the Beast's curse as externalizing his indifference to beauty, so that the staircase dance, his freeing of Belle, and Belle's 'I love you' trace Diotima's ladder from outward to inward beauty — the light that releases the prisoner.

platonic-love.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
platonic-love.title: 24. Climbing the Ladder of Love
platonic-love.relation: Brendan Shea reads Downton's romances through each speech of Plato's Symposium in turn. Phaedrus's love-inspired heroism explains Thomas taking a beating to save Jimmy; Pausanias's contrast of common and heavenly love maps onto Mary learning to work within social rules rather than around them (Pamuk versus Matthew); Eryximachus's orderly love is Carson and Mrs. Hughes's skilled, harmonious running of the house; Aristophanes's severed halves fit Anna and Bates merging their lives through prison and rape; and Agathon's naive praise diagnoses Edith's misdirected pursuit of love. Finally Socrates's ladder of love - desire for immortality ascending from one beautiful beloved to moral beauty itself - is played out by Tom and Sybil, whose romance leads him from chauffeur to estate manager and her from fashionable life to nursing, exactly as the ladder predicts.

platonic-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
platonic-love.title: The Abandoned Boys
platonic-love.relation: Surveying eros, philia, and agape, from the Weasleys' romantic love to Voldemort's never having wanted a friend to 'God is love,' the section draws on Plato's Symposium, where crude physical desire is progressively refined toward the beautiful and divine, to argue that love is primarily a choice of the will rather than a feeling. Hence Snape's continuing dislike of Harry is no evidence against his transformation by love; acting for others' good despite his emotions is precisely the testimony to it.

platonic-love.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
platonic-love.title: A Work in Progress
platonic-love.relation: Tracing Snape's love from the greedy boyhood watching of Lily and the Mudblood rupture through his plea to save Lily alone, which draws Dumbledore's 'You disgust me,' the section judges it short of Aristotle's beloved as a 'second self,' since he wanted Lily's good only as it related to him. Diotima's teaching in the Symposium that 'love is wanting to possess the good forever' and Benedict XVI's love as 'an ongoing exodus out of the closed inward-looking self' frame how Snape's unrequited love gradually 'gives birth in beauty' to virtue in him.

platonic-love.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
platonic-love.title: a7.xhtml
platonic-love.relation: The chapter sets the bloody classical ideal of glory (Homer's kleos, Beowulf, Alexander modeling himself on Achilles) - which Augustine already condemned as libido dominandi - against Plato's alternative of a life aimed at the good, the true and the beautiful. Thorin's last charge at the Battle of Five Armies fits the heroic tradition, but Tolkien's real point is that Bilbo, the 'grocer' who feels the dwarves' treasure-lust yet walks away from it, and who ends by inviting the dwarves to four-o'clock tea instead of a victory feast, shows glory subordinated to domestic beauty and humility. Socrates' question in the Apology - why care so little for wisdom and the soul's improvement while chasing wealth, honor and reputation - is exactly the temptation Bilbo resists, and the Symposium's move from battle to a drinking-party of love-of-beauty mirrors Tolkien's placement of heroism in hobbits rather than warriors.

platonic-love.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
platonic-love.title: The Office and Philosophy
platonic-love.relation: Arp and Watson sort Dunder Mifflin's relationships into five conceptions of love: Roy's erotic 'best sex of your life' Valentine's offer to Pam as blind eros; Angela and Dwight's pursuit of an idealized mate read through Plato's Forms and the Symposium's ascent to Beauty; Aristotle's three friendships, under which the office's alliances are mere utility while Jim and Pam's teapot sacrifice in 'Christmas Party' approaches virtue friendship; the Stoic-Kantian 'equal loving' of universal respect, laughed at when Michael ranks himself with Bono and Lincoln; and agape-style family loyalty that leads Dwight to supply Michael his urine in 'Drug Testing'. The chapter concludes that Michael exemplifies a selfishness Western philosophy has no name for, failing at every form of love.

platonic-love.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
platonic-love.title: Overcoming Death through the Force of Love
platonic-love.relation: Lawler reads the nine-film saga as a love story in three acts structured by Plato: Anakin and Padme's passionate love - which Diotima's ladder in the Symposium treats as the necessary first rung the Jedi wrongly condemn - drives his fall, in a Phaedrus-style conflict between the upward rational horse and the downward sensuous one. The original trilogy centers the detached Platonic love of Luke and Leia, while the Rey-Kylo 'dyad in the Force' fulfills Aristophanes' halfling myth of reunited other halves and brings balance, just as Alcibiades' failure to climb beyond the first rung parallels Anakin's fixation on one person. When Ren revives the dead Rey in a Romeo-and-Juliet inversion, the chapter concludes Yoda was wrong: the Force transforms into the dead rather than them into it.

platonic-love.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
platonic-love.title: Introduction The Love of Wisdom
platonic-love.relation: Editor David Baggett frames the collection with his own lifelong love of tennis (watching the 1980 Borg-McEnroe Wimbledon final, idolizing Borg and Gerulaitis) and argues tennis is an ideal springboard for philosophy, glossing 'philosophy' as the etymological 'love of wisdom.' He invokes Plato's idea that instances of beauty in this world make the heart ache for beauty's truest source, applying it to the sublime excellence of great play. He positions the whole book as using tennis to reach questions that matter, including the meaning of life, citing David Foster Wallace's quip that the title Tennis and the Meaning of Life is 'redundant.'

platonic-love.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
platonic-love.title: The “Kournikova Phenomenon”
platonic-love.relation: The chapter asks why Anna Kournikova was celebrated as a beauty despite a mediocre record while the far more successful Williams sisters were praised for athleticism, not looks. It uses Plato's Symposium (the ascent from a beautiful body to the Form of Beauty) to show beauty can be more than appearance, then deploys Nussbaum's analysis of objectification (contrasting Playboy's demeaning caption on tennis-player Nicollette Sheridan with Lady Chatterley) and MacKinnon's dominance view to critique the media's commodification of female players. Weaving in commodity racism and bell hooks on black hair, it argues Kournikova's fame reflects a whiteness-privileging color-caste standard of beauty rather than any real athletic or aesthetic superiority.

platonic-love.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
platonic-love.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
platonic-love.relation: McFarland reads Soderbergh's Solaris as a meditation on recollection, recognition, and repetition, grounding it in Platonic recollection (the Phaedo, the cave, and the Symposium's love as desire) and Augustine's Confessions, where memory strains toward an elusive beloved-as-God, the 'cruel miracle' of present absence. When Solaris materializes Rheya, Chris Kelvin first jettisons the 'bad copy' but then, tempted by Snow, embraces Deleuze's endless degraded repetition of copies to erase his guilt over her suicide. Against this, Gibarian voices a Kierkegaardian call (Repetition, Either/Or) that there are 'only choices'; McFarland faults Chris, like Odysseus choosing Kalypso's island, for choosing the deathless eternal present over the human world of forward-moving choice.

platonic-love.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
platonic-love.title: The Recovery of Childhood and the Search for the Absent Father
platonic-love.relation: Le Gall and Taliaferro read E.T., Hook, and the Indiana Jones trilogy through a Socratic-Platonic ideal in which the true 'adventure' ends not in glory (kleos) but in homecoming, beauty, and restored parent-child love. Indiana abandons the grail to grab his father's hand and hears 'Indiana' instead of 'Junior'; Elliott becomes a father to E.T. while E.T. teaches him loss; Peter Banning must recover his Pan-childhood to save his kids. They tie this to the Republic's Myth of Er, the Symposium's ladder of love, and xenia (hospitality) as the setting for wisdom.

platonic-love.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
platonic-love.title: Deceit, Desire, and Mimetic Doubling in the Films of Christopher Nolan
platonic-love.relation: Dunn reads Doodlebug's infinite regress of doppelgangers, Following's Cobb manufacturing a double of The Young Man, and The Prestige's Borden-Angier feud as cinematic illustrations of Girard's mimetic theory: we learn what to desire by imitating models, and as model and imitator converge on the same objects they become rivals and doubles. He shows Cobb in Following deliberately certifying The Blonde's desirability to entrap The Young Man (double mediation breeding Cobb's own jealousy), and Fischer's 'desire to be his own man' in Inception being incepted through the mediator of his father. In The Prestige, prestige itself becomes the contested object, a zero-sum metaphysical prize generated by the rivalry that demands escalating sacrifice. Drawing on Augustine's restlessness, Plato's Eros as longing for the Good, and Rousseau's amour-propre, he argues that desire born of ontological lack curdles into rivalry and scapegoating, with Memento's Leonard as the man who deliberately farms fresh scapegoats-in-waiting to keep his actions meaningful.

platonic-love.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
platonic-love.title: A Beautiful Destiny
platonic-love.relation: Clive Cazeaux asks whether the Daleks can be beautiful, canvassing theories of beauty to resolve the puzzle of a monster being beautiful. He distinguishes Kant's higher natural beauty (and his suspicion of 'dependent,' purpose-designed beauty like the Dalek casing) from Hegel's view that beauty in art, perceiving thought in matter, is higher, and finds Plato most helpful: to call the Daleks beautiful is Platonic love, being drawn to engage with them as a wholly-other form of life whose design succeeds. He surveys Alexander of Hales, Rosenkranz's aesthetic inferno, and formalism (the Krutikov design parallel) without a final verdict, showing the dispute turns on metaphysics.

platonic-love.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
platonic-love.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
platonic-love.relation: Andrew Aberdein traces the historical 'interpenetration' of philosophy and pornography — from the French book trade's 'livres philosophiques' and Diderot, d'Argens's Thérèse philosophe, and Sade, back through Aretino's courtesan dialogues to Plato's Symposium (the root of 'platonic love'). He dwells on the medieval 'Lay of Aristotle,' where Phyllis rides Aristotle like a horse, using the image to stage two readings: Aristotle's, that nature (and woman) must submit to the golden mean of reason, versus Phyllis's, that nature cannot. He closes with a paradox aimed at MacKinnon-style subordination arguments: if John Norman's Gor novels show philosophy is less persuasive than porn, then any persuasive argument for censorship must have a false conclusion.

platonic-love.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
platonic-love.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
platonic-love.relation: Mary Beth Yount asks whether being 'crazy in love' really resembles mental illness, noting lovesickness was a diagnosis for nearly two millennia and that love's mood swings mimic bipolar or schizophrenic symptoms. She organizes the analysis around the four Greek loves—eros (with Plato's ladder from physical beauty to the Forms, i.e., 'Platonic love'), philia (Aristotle's Nicomachean friendship of good character), storge (familial affection), and agape (C.S. Lewis's unconditional charity)—arguing a full romance blends all four. She then surveys Fisher, Aron, and Brown's fMRI work showing romantic love as a dopamine-driven mammalian mate-choice drive stronger than the sex drive, and the 'protest'/'resignation' stages of rejection, to reassure daters their craziness is normal biology, not disorder.

forgiveness.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
forgiveness.title: NOTES
forgiveness.relation: Argues Snape's redemption is gradual virtue-building rather than instant transformation, since vice and virtue are habits built up over time and his resentments persist even as his actions serve the good. His doe Patronus, matching Lily's, manifests Aristotle's beloved as a second self, his remorse, an emotion he shares with Harry but Voldemort cannot feel, begins to knit his damaged soul whole, and Harry's forgiveness, naming his son Albus Severus for 'the bravest man I ever knew', completes the arc love began.

forgiveness.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
forgiveness.title: The Triumph of Love
forgiveness.relation: Tracks love's escalation across the series as a force that overwhelms evil without competing: Lily's skin-deep sacrificial love repels Quirrell in Sorcerer's Stone, Harry spares Pettigrew out of love for Lupin and Sirius, his love for Sirius expels Voldemort's possession at the Ministry, and Dumbledore names it 'a force that is at once more wonderful and more terrible than death'. In Deathly Hallows love extends to Kreacher, Griphook, and Dobby, and culminates in Harry's astonishing plea that Voldemort 'try for some remorse', his redefinition of manhood in 'be a man', and victory through willing sacrifice and a single defensive spell rather than a duel, vindicating traditionally feminine values over hypermasculine domination.

forgiveness.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
forgiveness.title: Remorse and Death
forgiveness.relation: Opens Charles Taliaferro's chapter with Fawkes, who shields Harry in the Chamber of Secrets and Dumbledore at the Ministry, as the emblem of a philosophical model of moral repair: the wrongdoer must confess, feel remorse, repudiate the pleasure gained from the wrong - a kind of death to the old self - and emerge with radically new intentions, as in Christian baptism's dying and rising to new life, so that a friendship broken by betrayal can be reborn. The chapter will read Deathly Hallows through this model, with Voldemort as its perverse inversion, spreading death by clinging to life where Harry and Dumbledore win deeper life by accepting death.

forgiveness.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
forgiveness.title: The Inversion of Voldemort
forgiveness.relation: Distinguishes remorse from mere regret through Voldemort's cold 'I regret it' after ordering Nagini to kill Snape: remorse requires owning one's act, and at the final duel Harry addresses him as 'Tom Riddle' and demands he 'try for some remorse' - the death-to-self Riddle cannot perform. Dumbledore's remorse over the cursed Resurrection Stone ring and his arranged death, and Harry's voluntary death that destroys the Horcrux within him and restores his whole soul, exemplify dying to the past self for renewal, while Harry's renunciation of his temper toward Ron and Hermione and his love for Ginny mark his continuous moral regeneration.

forgiveness.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
forgiveness.title: The Fantasy Objection
forgiveness.relation: Takes up the integrity objection from psychoanalyst Melanie Klein: renouncing one's past self ('Bad Charles' versus 'New Charlie') risks self-deception, since the reformed person remains the self-same wrongdoer, as the alcoholic who stays sober for decades still knows himself to be. Taliaferro concedes the regeneration model can be abused but insists renewal requires a death-like renunciation, illustrated negatively by Snape, who loves Lily, feels remorse for the 'Mudblood' insult and for giving Voldemort the prophecy, yet cannot confess or release his resentment, and so remains unintegrated.

forgiveness.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
forgiveness.title: NOTES
forgiveness.relation: Closes the phoenix chapter by reading Fawkes's departure from Hogwarts after Dumbledore's death - mourning his master with a stricken lament but neither curing the ring's poison nor blocking Snape's killing curse - as the quiet handing over of the phoenix's lesson: ruptures of friendship and community caused by wrongdoing can only be healed through a kind of death and rebirth, in which remorseful confession burns up the old self and produces a person with radically new desires and intentions.

forgiveness.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
forgiveness.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
forgiveness.relation: Walls argues the controversy lies not in the gore but in who died on the cross and why, and shows Gibson weaving the three classic atonement theories: Christ crushing the serpent in Gethsemane as the Christus-Victor ransom (with Augustine's mousetrap image), the Isaiah 53 scourging and Gibson's own hand driving the nail as Anselm-style penal substitution in which the innocent dies so the guilty Barabbas in each of us goes free, and the transformed characters (Mary Magdalene, Simon of Cyrene, the good thief, the kneeling soldier) as Abelard's moral influence. Against Kant's charge that atonement is a superstitious substitute for moral transformation, he cites Swinburne and Quinn: pleading the atonement requires repentance, and the tens of thousands of reported conversions and confessions show it transforms lives. He concludes that any adequate account needs all three theories, objective payment and subjective transformation alike, and that atonement aims at mercy and reconciliation rather than retribution.

forgiveness.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
forgiveness.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
forgiveness.relation: Taliaferro, writing as a personalist, worries that Gibson's relentless focus on torture eclipses the whole person of Christ: like torture victims losing peripheral vision, viewers lose sight of his teaching, healings, nonviolence, and resurrection, and the satisfaction-theology framing risks relishing redemptive suffering itself. His reconciliation thought-experiment (Patricia's betrayal of Kris and the God-man who resurrects the murdered child) argues that the resurrection, not the passion alone, completes at-one-ment, since no amount of suffering can undo past wrong. He contrasts Gandalf's laughing return in The Return of the King with a Gibson Jesus who could not plausibly laugh after rising, and invokes Scheler's St. Francis, who loves the wholeness behind sickness rather than the sickness, to urge that the film's intensity edges out a life-affirming view of persons as irreducibly valuable in themselves.

forgiveness.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
forgiveness.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
forgiveness.relation: Reconstructs Narnian atonement as the early Christian Ransom Theory: Digory's confession, remorse, and 'undoing' of his wrong in The Magician's Nephew, and Aslan giving his life as ransom for Edmund against the Witch's Deep Magic claim in The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe, ending with the Deeper Magic that cracks the Stone Table. It answers John Lucas's four objections (literal Satan, Satan's rights, God negotiating with evil, divine deception) by treating evil as self-chosen bondage whose doors are 'locked on the inside', arguing Aslan's sacrificial identification with wrongdoers displays a love that mere omnipotent force could not, and that wrongdoers like the Witch are not owed full disclosure. It also defends mercy's tension with strict justice, via the example of a deserving prisoner mercifully freed, and finds humor rather than crudeness in Peter Lombard's cross-as-mousetrap image.

forgiveness.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
forgiveness.title: Are We Going Too Far
forgiveness.relation: David Kyle Johnson distinguishes revenge (personal, emotional, unlimited) from retribution and argues that 'Tarantino's view'—mercy should be common practice yet revenge can be justified—is consistent: Jules buys Pumpkin and Honey Bunny's lives but never waives a right of vengeance, since they never wronged him. He tests the view against Bushido, showing Beatrix's revolt against her lord Bill violates the samurai code, and against karma, which makes revenge unnecessary. After finding that Hobbes, Locke, Nietzsche and Socrates all leave revenge's justification open, he defends it—citing Budd's 'that woman deserves her revenge'—so long as the punishment fits the crime and spares innocents, as when Beatrix refuses to make herself even by killing Vernita's daughter Nikki.

forgiveness.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
forgiveness.title: The Finder of Lost Children
forgiveness.relation: Timothy Dean Roth reads Kill Bill as a modern Divine Comedy: Tarantino punishes by contrapasso like Dante—O-Ren dies by Japanese steel, Budd by snake, Elle by blindness, Bill by a broken heart—and both treat vengeance as a form of truth-telling and an act of love. Hattori Hanzo's warning that revenge 'is a forest' echoes Aristotle on how hard it is to set the limits of anger, while the stories-within-stories of orphaned Nikki and O-Ren enact the cycle of violence vengeance perpetuates. Against this, Aquinas's doctrine of double effect shows every one of the Bride's killings is defensive self-preservation, and the film ends where Jules's arc ends: in mercy, mutual forgiveness and a whispered 'thank you' of grace.

forgiveness.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
forgiveness.title: The Doors Are Never Locked
forgiveness.relation: Held reads Cash's Walk the Line retort "Well, they're not Christians then" as a thesis about redemption: since, with Augustine, we rejoice most at the sinner saved, and since the Sermon on the Mount forbids judging what we cannot know (anyone's deep character), humility demands withholding condemnation and hoping even the worst can change. He contrasts Christian redemption, a revaluation of the person that needs outside grace (Cash needed June and the Carters; nobody is self-made), with Nietzsche's attack on redemption as slave-morality self-hatred, granting that Nietzsche's eternal recurrence also revalues the past but objecting that self-revaluation collapses into rationalization, as Cash's Saul in Man in White shows. Forgiveness proper requires repentance and a solvent character, like paying off a debt; the shame of the "Long Black Veil" woman shows why; and because we see "through a glass darkly," nobody, not the Reno murderer, not Joe Bean, is beyond hope, which is why the doors are never locked and why execution or life without parole claims a judgment of moral worth that is not ours to make.

forgiveness.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
forgiveness.title: An Altar Boy’s Public Penance
forgiveness.relation: Flamm and Rea take Buffett's altar-boy grudge against Catholic moralism — the 'bakers' of 'Fruitcakes' who try to cure humanity's half-baked madness — and frame it with Nietzsche's charge that 'there was only one Christian, and he died on the cross.' They then cast Buffett as a latter-day Spinoza: like the excommunicated lens-grinder he rejects the orthodox God, finds God in nature ('One Particular Harbor' as a view 'sub specie aeternitatis'), and treats wealth, honor, and sensual pleasure ('Cheeseburger in Paradise') as means toward the greatest happiness rather than sins. Nietzsche's Dionysian intoxication ('God's Own Drunk') and Shakespeare's Sir Toby versus the moralist Malvolio support embracing natural madness, and the chapter closes by arguing Buffett's confessional songs ('Coastal Confessions') make his Parrothead audience the priest who grants the altar boy's public penance and forgiveness.

forgiveness.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
forgiveness.title: Forgiveness and the Fenway Faithful
forgiveness.relation: Rory Kraft uses Aristotle's virtue ethics to explain why Red Sox Nation forgave Tim Wakefield (whose mistake Aaron Boone turned into the 2003 ALCS-ending homer) and Ted Williams, but scapegoated Bill Buckner for 'the error' and eventually cast off Manny Ramirez. Because Aristotle judges a complete life, one swallow does not make a summer, Buckner's .991 fielding percentage and 2,715 hits should contextualize his lapse, yet some acts are bad without degrees like Aristotle's adultery, theft and murder, and a World Series-deciding error crossed that line. Kraft distinguishes Aristotle's categories, Wakefield's mistake (ignorance of Boone's changed plan) versus Buckner's misadventure (contrary to reasonable expectation) versus Manny's voluntary injustices, concluding that learning when to forgive players who are family taught the Nation what forgiveness itself means, sealed by Buckner's 2008 standing ovation.

forgiveness.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
forgiveness.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
forgiveness.relation: Najwa Al-Tabaa reads Sandman: Season of Mists through Derrida's paradox that only the unforgivable can truly be forgiven: Morpheus's freeing of Nada works as forgiveness precisely because condemning his lover to Hell was unforgivable, while Lucifer, who was never wronged by the damned, can give them only a devalued semblance of pardon, and they cling to punishment they feel they deserve. She then brings in Foucault's Discipline and Punish and Bentham's Panopticon to read the angels' rebuilt Hell of redemption as the modern rehabilitative prison, where watched souls are expected to reform themselves. The experiment fails, she argues, because redemption is imposed without hearing the prisoners, violating Derrida's condition that forgiveness needs a shared language, so the inmates prefer Lucifer's honest eternity of despair to a salvation they never asked for, a lesson about real prisons that seek rehabilitation through punishment.

forgiveness.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
forgiveness.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
forgiveness.relation: Timothy P. Jackson argues Cohen is the closest thing today to a Biblical prophet - a 'strong poet' in Harold Bloom's sense, wearing a coat of many colors drawn from Judaism, Christianity, Buddhism, Taoism, and Sufism, sustained by an 'epistemic humility' that lives between dogmatism and doubt. Cohen leads Christian texts back to their Hebraic origins, critiques every arrogant nationalism including Israel (Book of Mercy, psalm 27), and gave his Tel Aviv concert profits to Israeli-Palestinian reconciliation. Jackson reads Cohen's equanimity at his business manager's embezzlement trial as forgiveness overcoming resentment, weighs his hesed/agape-style unconditional love against his failures in erotic love, and ends with Cohen's reticence about personal immortality - a prophet for the living.

forgiveness.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
forgiveness.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
forgiveness.relation: McCrossin asks why Finn and Jake forgive Marceline although she tries to kill Jake, evicts them twice, drains Princess Bubblegum, and never shows remorse. Jake's change of heart ('my fear was based on ignorance') comes from witnessing her father Hunson Abadeer's cruelty and her abandoned childhood, so her bad acts flow from causes outside her control rather than pure choice. The chapter presses the remaining problem: we normally forgive the penitent offender, not the unrepentant one, and Marceline—unlike the moping vampires of Twilight, Underworld, and True Blood—never regrets, leaving readers to decide whether understanding without remorse can ground trust and friendship.

forgiveness.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
forgiveness.title: 23. Failing and Forgiving in the Name of the Doctor
forgiveness.relation: Hoffman reads the Doctor's banishment of the War Doctor ('Doctor no more,' his actions 'not done in the name of the Doctor') as a failure of self-forgiveness driven by what Jeffrie Murphy calls the moral hatred of self and Robin Dillon the 'self-as-feared,' rather than mere guilt over the genocide of Gallifrey. Drawing on the self-forgiveness literature (Blustein, Griswold, Westlund), he argues that 'The Day of the Doctor' shows forgiveness neither excuses nor extinguishes blame: the Tenth and Eleventh Doctors forgive their past self by recognizing he shared their Doctorly motives and was forced into an impossible choice. Clara's outsider faith ('be a doctor') supplies the third-party affirmation that dissolves the identity-destroying dilemma and frees the Doctor to find the third option that saves Gallifrey.

forgiveness.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
forgiveness.title: 6. Punishing Negan
forgiveness.relation: Yuen asks why Rick imprisons Negan after the Saviors' war instead of executing the man who beats people to death with 'Lucille' and runs a mafia-like protection racket. He surveys retributivism (fair play and eye-for-an-eye equality) and deterrence, including Glenn's lawless Challenger driving, then defends Rick's refusal to kill via 'we're better than him,' the weakness of execution as a deterrent for Negan's followers, and the brutalization effect that would poison the character of the fledgling civilization. But he argues Negan's basement isolation - no exercise, no decency, his victim as judge and warden - fails Rick's own civilizing vision, and proposes restorative justice with apology, forgiveness, and mediated reparations as the punishment a civilization that claims human life is precious ought to build.

forgiveness.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
forgiveness.title: 9. Why Revenge Is So Sweet
forgiveness.relation: Haas asks why we cheer Inigo's vendetta against Rugen when moral philosophy condemns vengeance as emotionally driven injustice. Distinguishing impartial, proportional punishment from personal revenge, he then uses the honor-culture literature (Nisbett and Cohen, Tamler Sommers) to argue that in lawless Florin - where the 'justice system' is run by the villain who ordered the murder - Inigo's personal retribution is a justified duty of honor, since no institutional avenue exists. The deeper pull of revenge stories, he concludes, is that victims have a special moral standing to punish - which is why Rugen dying by anyone's hand but Inigo's would be unsatisfying - while a variant story (Westley as the killer) would call instead for atonement and forgiveness, showing that revenge is made admirable by how stories are told.

forgiveness.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
forgiveness.title: 12. Vigilante Wanted
forgiveness.relation: In a fictional Dust Bowl voice, Ketcham has a 1940 farm kid watching foreclosure bulldozers decide which single comic hero to keep as the vigilante who will burn down the bank - weighing Superman, who has gone over to the big-city bankers as reporter Clark Kent, against Batman, whose riches resemble the bankers' but whose hatred of his parents' killer matches his own. He tests his candidates against Hamlet's fatal indecision, Henry V at Agincourt, a Lex Luthor who is evil exactly like the bank president, and Tom Joad of The Grapes of Wrath, the real "I'll be ever'where in the dark" vigilante. In the end the boy burns the Batman box, reads Superman's restraint as the preacher's forgiveness, and lets his anger - and the need for any vigilante - go.

forgiveness.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
forgiveness.title: 15. Death Begets Death
forgiveness.relation: The Bocks trace Darrow's education out of vengeance: in Plato's tripartite soul the spirited part (anger) must obey reason, and Aristotle's virtue of mildness—anger at the right things, toward the right people, for the right length of time—is the golden mean between slavish and irascible that Darrow has not yet reached. Darrow learns the difference when he hands Titus over to Cassius's vendetta and admits 'That wasn't justice': retribution in Kant's lex talionis tradition must be dispassionate and proportional, while vengeance is past-oriented and insatiable, and Darrow's own bombing of the Ganymede docks shows how troubling even his 'justice' remains. Against Darrow's violent justice-in-love the chapter sets Martin Luther King Jr.'s agape and loving-forgiveness—Sevro hanging and then forgiving Cassius, Darrow forgiving Tactus, Mustang pulling her brother's legs for a merciful death—closing with King's warning that constructive ends can never justify destructive means, and Darrow's own admission that 'the war is not over.'

forgiveness.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
forgiveness.title: 16. Can We All Get Along
forgiveness.relation: Courtland Lewis tackles transitional justice after atrocity: with the Rising won, what is to be done with millions of Golds complicit in slavery, rape, and torture? He tests Peter French's virtuous vengeance—punishment that fits the wrong, grounded in Locke's natural rights—and finds Darrow's destruction of Gold society fails it (disproportionate, unsober, punishing young Julian for his ancestors' crimes), then turns to Jessica Wolfendale's argument that declaring anyone unforgivable adopts the wrongdoer's own devaluing outlook, exactly as Darrow becomes what he despises. The working model is South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission—confession, conditional amnesty, truth-telling, reparations, Tutu, Mandela, Beth Savage hoping to meet her bomber—applied to Mars through Mustang-style dignified engagement on Adam Michnik's model and Slavenka Drakulic's lesson that every Color inherits responsibility for rejecting the Society's past.

forgiveness.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
forgiveness.title: 15. We’re on Your Side, Charlie Brown
forgiveness.relation: The chapter asks why Charlie Brown never abandons the friends who torment him and answers with friendship philosophy: Aristotle's three kinds of friendship fit the gang (pleasure-based childhood play - baseball, trick-or-treating, Christmas plays - as the nursery for later perfect friendships of good will), while Marilyn Friedman's 'moral growth' and 'moral empiricism' explain how even Lucy's blunt 'snap out of it' gives Charlie perspectives from 'reliable moral witnesses.' Annette Baier's account of trust as accepted vulnerability redeems his 'gullibility': better to risk the pulled football than live in an atmosphere of suspicion. The 'Our Manager' uniform of Charlie Brown's All-Stars and the decorated tiny Christmas tree show that on the things that matter his friends can always be trusted to take his side - and Charlie is always first to forgive.

forgiveness.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
forgiveness.title: 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger
forgiveness.relation: Ericson uses the used-car litmus test to examine trust in the MCU: through McLeod's three criteria and Peperzak's contrast of the objectifying and interactive approaches, Tony's control-seeking distance (the lone-gun-slinger act of Iron Man 2) fails trust while Steve's soldier-style trust anchors the Winter Soldier thriller against Fury's 'This isn't freedom, this is fear' and HYDRA's coercion-eliminating project. Plato's rule that power should go only to those who do not want it explains why Cap can be entrusted with superpowers, Nietzsche's megalomaniac late letters frame Tony's drive to 'cleave history in two' by building Ultron and then the messianic Vision, and Banner's Hulk illustrates the Freudian road from repression to sublimation as the condition of self-trust. It ends with Cap's concealment of Bucky's killing of Tony's parents as the betrayal of trust that only a decision to forgive might repair.

forgiveness.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
forgiveness.title: 17. A Word from a Man Mister Rogers Ruined
forgiveness.relation: Nicolas Michaud, whose mother was murdered and who asked that her killer get help rather than die, constructs and then refutes the case that Rogers ruined boys by teaching gentleness: against the Thrasymachus line from Republic Book I that justice is for suckers and competition is everything, he argues Rogers's 'three ways to ultimate success: be kind' defines success as happiness; against 'forgiveness is weakness,' he deploys Aristotle's virtue of mildness, being ready to pardon rather than exact penalty, and a rereading of 'turn the other cheek' as claiming equal standing, so that forgiving is strength, not submission.

forgiveness.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
forgiveness.title: 24. The Left Hand of Thanos
forgiveness.relation: Reads the Endgame 'I am' exchange through Martin Luther's two hands of God: Thanos's left-handed gauntlet enacts God's 'alien work' of law, judgment and destruction (his 'inevitability,' seen in all 14,000,605 of Strange's futures), while Tony's right-handed snap enacts the 'proper work' of grace, where freedom means relying on a promise — Strange's gift of the Time Stone, the Ancient One resting reality on Banner's promise. It applies the law/grace contrast to Thor's reconciliation with Frigga ('you're going to be the man you're meant to be'), Tony's with Howard, and Steve's gift of the shield to Sam, arguing the heroes' failures at who they were 'supposed to be' are the law's condemnation, while the promise delivers a freedom that turns Thanos's inevitability into impossibility.

forgiveness.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
forgiveness.title: 17. Forgive and Make Up
forgiveness.relation: Courtland Lewis tests philosophical theories of forgiveness against KISS's feuds. Jeffrie Murphy's account (overcoming vindictive resentment on moral grounds) shows Ace has not forgiven Gene's fired-three-times claims; Charles Griswold's twelve-condition 'paradigmatic forgiveness' is likely too demanding for them; Margaret Holmgren's compassionate character-forgiveness fits Bruce Kulick's and Eric Singer's graceful exits; and Geoffrey Scarre's utilitarian reading makes forgiveness a calculation of benefits. Lewis then applies his own rights-based peace-ethics (eireneism) to a thought experiment in which Gene steals Ace's drugs to save his flourishing — no wrong done, so no forgiveness needed — and closes by likening Paul and Gene to a married couple whose ongoing obligations model forgiveness, endorsing Wolfendale's refusal to call anyone unforgiveable.

forgiveness.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
forgiveness.title: Sometimes We Can Let Go
forgiveness.relation: Sets P.F. Strawson's blame-as-moral-anger picture against the Seneca/Buddhist case that anger is revenge-hungry poison, then reads ATLA as modeling ways to hold people responsible without toxic anger. Katara may stay angry at Yon Rha after 'The Southern Raiders' yet forgo revenge because he is incorrigible and not worth it, while forgiving Zuko on Lucy Allais's 'wiping the slate clean' logic since his villainy no longer reflects his character. Iroh's 'I was never angry; I was afraid that you had lost your way' and his tea with the mugger Tycho show blame being skipped entirely in favor of compassion, and Zuko's shift from hypocritical self-blame to self-compassion after confronting Ozai lets him take responsibility without self-destructive rage.

forgiveness.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
forgiveness.title: Opening Up Possibilities
forgiveness.relation: Argues, through Hilde Lindemann's relational account of personhood, that Zuko genuinely is all of the identities others hold him in (disappointing son, villain, ally) because being a person is a social practice of expression, recognition, and response. Aang's decision to hear Zuko out at the Western Air Temple, Iroh's stubborn refusal to accept Ozai's script for him (his anger itself recognizing Zuko as an agent capable of choosing otherwise), and Katara's historically-sensitive slow trust open up the possible future in which Zuko can become trustworthy, while the Earth Kingdom villagers' rejection of him in 'Zuko Alone' shows how weight of history and stereotype can shut possibility down. The chapter insists this is not letting wrongdoers off the hook: genuine apology, repair, and moral anger remain required (contrasting the Brock Turner case), but only a moral community that holds people in personhood makes redemption possible, so society should be arranged to give everyone the Iros and Aangs that Zuko was lucky to have.

forgiveness.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
forgiveness.title: Sometimes We Can Let Go
forgiveness.relation: Sets the intuition that angry blame is how we hold people responsible (Strawson; Katara's useful fury at Pakku's sexism, Iroh's 'whatever you do to that spirit, I will unleash on you tenfold') against the Senecan and Buddhist verdict that anger is greedy for revenge, and reads ATLA as modeling ways to hold people responsible without toxic anger. In 'The Southern Raiders' Katara neither forgives Yon Rha nor kills him, showing that blame can be set down when expressing it is pointless, while she forgives Zuko in Lucy Allais's 'wiping the slate clean' sense because his past betrayal no longer speaks to his present character. Iroh's handling of the mugger in Ba Sing Se ('I was never angry; I was afraid that you had lost your way') models responding to the suffering behind wrongdoing with compassion instead of blame, and Zuko's self-anger is diagnosed as hypocritical self-blame whose antidote is self-compassion: acknowledging how he himself was hurt is what finally lets him take ownership of his wrongs.

forgiveness.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
forgiveness.title: Avengers, Forgive!
forgiveness.relation: Malloy builds an account of forgiveness around the Avengers' habit of recruiting ex-villains: Arendt's 'predicament of irreversibility' explains why we cannot undo Wonder Man's revenge scheme against Stark, so resentment must be overcome; Derrida's claim that only the unforgivable is truly forgivable frames the House of M question, whether Quicksilver's manipulation of Wanda's reality-warping is a crime beyond forgiveness.
