Framing Deadpool as an anti-Sisyphean 'hero' who tries to end the Absurd (the Continuity) by killing everyone rather than affirming it as Camus's Sisyphus does, the chapter supplements Lewis with Thomasson's artifact theory of fiction to handle the literary characters of the Ideaverse.

augustine-time.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
augustine-time.title: Moving Past Misdirection
augustine-time.relation: This section grounds prejudgment in memory through Augustine's Confessions: since the past no longer exists and the future has not arrived, time is known only in human experience, where memory of the past and anticipation of the future meet in the present - and, with Gadamer, prejudgments are personal and social memory, the tradition 'handed down.' The Pensieve embodies this epistemology: it stores and organizes memories, reveals patterns from a third-person view, and shares memory socially, as Dumbledore walks Harry through Tom Riddle's orphanage years, the framed Morfin Gaunt, and Hokey's memories, giving Harry the knowledge of Voldemort's history and vulnerabilities he needs to defeat him.

augustine-time.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
augustine-time.title: Tomorrow Is Yesterday
augustine-time.relation: Uses the Bajoran Prophets, who experience no linear time ('What is this... time?'), to frame a tour of time's metaphysics: Newton's absolute container versus Leibniz's relationism (the incoherence of a 'temporal vacuum'), Augustine's mind-dependent time (illustrated by 'The Inner Light' and O'Brien's implanted prison years in 'Hard Time'), and McTaggart's argument that neither the A-series nor the B-series can account for change, illustrated by Tasha Yar's death in 'Skin of Evil' and Kirk's Liar-paradox victories over Nomad and Norman. The chapter defends the A-series via tense, then weighs presentism — which would make 'Tomorrow Is Yesterday' and 'Trials and Tribble-ations' impossible — against eternalism, whose fatalism Data embraces when his severed head turns up in 'Time's Arrow' ('It has occurred. It will occur.'), and which finally makes sense of prophets who see the future in 'Destiny.'

augustine-time.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
augustine-time.title: Liz Lemon and High School The More Things Change, the More They Don’t
augustine-time.relation: Shores uses Jack's cookie jar collection and his fiftieth-birthday home movies in 'Apollo, Apollo', plus Liz's catastrophic high-school reunion in 'Reunion', to examine personal identity over time. Hume's bundle theory denies any self beyond a flux of perceptions, Whitehead offers three senses of a person over time, and Augustine locates past, present, and future in the mind as memory, sight, and expectation, which explains why Jack cannot recover his tenth-birthday joy by buying the Apollo Lunar Module toy yet feels 'like a kid' after laughing until he vomits. Ryle's 'elusiveness of I' and Rousseau on happiness as a fleeting state frame the conclusion that we continually reinterpret the past from the present, so the self is a stretched-out temporal continuity.

augustine-time.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
augustine-time.title: Deleuze Jam Today
augustine-time.relation: Walks Alice through four theories of time: Augustine's three presents in Confessions (Alice 'was a different person then'; the past exists only as present memory), Kant's time as a subjective form of intuition presupposed by experience (the White Rabbit's anxiety about being late already requires it), Bergson's indivisible duration against spatialized clock time (running fastest with the Red Queen yet ending under the same tree; the Hatter stuck at six o'clock; Zeno's Achilles resolved by indivisible acts), and Deleuze's chronos and aion from The Logic of Sense. Mark W. Westmoreland reads 'jam to-morrow and jam yesterday—but never jam to-day' as pure aion: the present never arrives, only an endlessly subdividing past-future.

augustine-time.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
augustine-time.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
augustine-time.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' (Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, Aang's glimpse of the girl who will be Toph) through Plotinus's teaching that time is 'the life of the Soul' and Augustine's three presents of memory, attention, and expectation, so that past and future are present to the soul and Huu's 'time is an illusion and so is death' becomes literal metaphysics. The banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, models Neoplatonic emanation from the One, and this unity explains the Avatar's communion with past and future selves as well as Aang's refusal to kill Ozai, since death, like time, is a misperception.

augustine-time.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
augustine-time.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
augustine-time.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' through Plotinus and Augustine: Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, and Aang's unknown giggling girl are, respectively, memory, attention, and expectation, Augustine's three presents, while Plotinus's hierarchy of One, Intellect, and world Soul, with time as 'the life of the Soul,' lets what is successive for us be simultaneous from eternity. Huu's banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, is read as Neoplatonic emanation, and Toph's later root-connectedness in LoK shows the ability is not exclusive to the Avatar. Since past and future Avatar selves are thus present to Aang, death, like time, is an illusion, which underwrites his refusal to kill Ozai.

augustine-time.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
augustine-time.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
augustine-time.relation: Smith turns Walter's 'Three thousand years of beautiful tradition, from Moses to Sandy Koufax — YOU'RE GODDAMN RIGHT I'M LIVING IN THE FUCKING PAST!' into a question in the philosophy of time: with Augustine's Confessions (the past exists only as a present of things past, in memory) and Plotinus's internalized time as 'the life of the soul in movement', Walter's Vietnam rages ('there isn't a literal connection, Dude'), his Cynthia show-dog errands, and his assumed Jewishness all show the past actively constituting his present. Peirce's 'method of tenacity' names his clinging to belief against doubt — an ailment the Dude secretly shares, given his own Port Huron past, drug-blurred memoir, and Creedence-soaked anachronism.

augustine-time.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
augustine-time.title: Moving Past Misdirection
augustine-time.relation: The chapter joins Augustine's Confessions analysis of time, where only in human experience does memory of the past meet anticipation of the future in the present, to Gadamer's view of prejudgments as tradition, memory 'passed down' that shapes how we approach the present. The Pensieve symbolizes this double, personal and social memory: Dumbledore's third-person viewing spots patterns, and the extracted memories of Riddle's orphanage sadism and the reconstructed testimonies of Hokey and Morfin Gaunt give Harry the knowledge of Voldemort's history, character, and vulnerabilities he needs to defeat him.

augustine-time.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
augustine-time.title: 20 Timeless Artifacts and Aging Humans Indiana Jones and the Philosophy of Time
augustine-time.relation: Uses Aristotle's Rhetoric portrait of elderly men and his golden mean — the prime of life between rash youth and feeble age — to explain fan anxiety about aging Harrison Ford ('Raiders of the Lost AARP'), then turns to Heidegger's claim that human life does not happen in time but is time: mortals are finite beings whose worth decays, while the Ark, the Grail, and Belloq's buried pocket watch gain value outside 'vulgar' linear time, and only ready-to-hand 'things' that do something (a face-melting Ark, a healing Grail) matter rather than mere objects like the decapitated Brody statue. Augustine's Confessions frames the gap between clock time and lived 'inner' duration (Indy's 'all my life' hunting the Cross versus Marcus's counting of years), and Bakhtin's 'adventure time' explains the films' condensed, history-flouting chronology in which the character Indy never ages even as Ford does.

augustine-time.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
augustine-time.relation: McFarland reads Soderbergh's Solaris as a meditation on recollection, recognition, and repetition, grounding it in Platonic recollection (the Phaedo, the cave, and the Symposium's love as desire) and Augustine's Confessions, where memory strains toward an elusive beloved-as-God, the 'cruel miracle' of present absence. When Solaris materializes Rheya, Chris Kelvin first jettisons the 'bad copy' but then, tempted by Snow, embraces Deleuze's endless degraded repetition of copies to erase his guilt over her suicide. Against this, Gibarian voices a Kierkegaardian call (Repetition, Either/Or) that there are 'only choices'; McFarland faults Chris, like Odysseus choosing Kalypso's island, for choosing the deathless eternal present over the human world of forward-moving choice.

augustine-time.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
augustine-time.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
augustine-time.relation: Davison uses St. Augustine's claim from the Confessions that only the present moment is real – past and future exist only as memory and anticipation – to argue that a father should stop missing his children's lives by fixating on past regrets or future worries. Drawing on Steindl-Rast and Thomas Sterner, he contrasts mechanical 'clock time' with quality-driven 'experienced time' and recommends process-focus over end-product focus, illustrated with lying beside his sleeping daughter Grace and dreading bedtime routines with his sons.

augustine-time.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
augustine-time.title: GARDENING
augustine-time.relation: Mara Miller argues gardens do not merely sit inside time but actively structure six kinds of time (scientific, objective/shared, kairos, subjective, temporality, historical), opening with Augustine's puzzle that he knows what time is until asked to explain it. She contrasts Greek chronos with kairos (the right moment to plant after the last frost), shows how Versailles propagated a shared time (eternal, historic, recurring) and eighteenth-century English landscape gardens taught the long-range vision capitalism needed, and describes cyclical 'eternal recurrence' (Eliade). Watching a dry Zen garden or fireflies, the visitor becomes the constant who notices—reworking Descartes's cogito as 'I notice, therefore I am'—while Japanese stepping-stones enforce a Buddhist mindfulness of impermanence in the present moment.

augustine-time.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
augustine-time.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
augustine-time.relation: Clancy Smith argues that a tattoo's ink is permanent but the memory it evokes is not, because the past no longer exists and recollection is always present and in flux (citing Heraclitus' river and William James on never-identical brain states). Using Augustine's 'present of things past' and Proust's Swann's Way, plus Dewey's immediate empiricism and Merleau-Ponty's critique of memory-as-projection, he contends that gazing at a tattoo (his 'Not Fade Away' epitaph tattoo, his friend Kalju's crossed-rifles, American History X's swastika) constructs a present meaning that tells us who we are now rather than recovering the past intact.

berkeley-idealism.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
berkeley-idealism.title: Going Mental
berkeley-idealism.relation: Argues Harry's question rests on a false dilemma between 'in the head' and 'real', which Dumbledore's reply dissolves. It distinguishes merely-in-the-head items (Hermione as fictional character) from mind-independent ones (Emma Watson, King's Cross), then surveys philosophers who make the mental real: Plato's forms via broomsticks as imperfect copies of the ideal essence, Descartes's rationalism, Kant's mind-constituted objects, Berkeley's 'to be is to be perceived', Mill's phenomenalism, and Yogacara Buddhism's consciousness-fabricated emptiness.

berkeley-idealism.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
berkeley-idealism.title: Wondering and Dreaming. The Words Have Different Meanings
berkeley-idealism.relation: Scott Calef argues that the causal theory of perception — the inflatable pig over Battersea reaches you only as an internal representation — breeds Cartesian skepticism: the dreaming argument, asylum inmates who don't know they're mad ('the lunatic is in my head'), the evil demon, and the modern brain-in-a-vat version behind The Matrix. Locke's unknowable substratum behind the Dark Side jacket's qualities and Berkeley's idealism deepen the veil of perception, with 'Julia Dream', Waters's 'If I go insane, please don't stick your wires in my brain', and Syd's 'Jugband Blues' self-diagnosis as Floyd illustrations. Against skepticism he deploys mutual corroboration ('It takes two to know'), J.L. Austin's point that waking experience is qualitatively unlike dreams ('A Pillow of Winds': 'the dream is gone'), and Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box private language argument (rebranded as Lucifer Sam's cat) — a purely private language is impossible, so skepticism expressed in language defeats itself, leaving the Barrett-era enigma to keep philosophy's original wonder alive.

berkeley-idealism.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
berkeley-idealism.title: iPod
berkeley-idealism.relation: Raven reads design history as a pendulum between 'Beauty Waves' (Art Nouveau's sinuous decoration, 1960s psychedelia) and 'Truth Waves' (Art Deco functionalism, Le Corbusier's 'machine for living'), poles he grounds in Berkeley's 'esse est percipi' idealism versus metaphysical realism. The late-1990s blobject -- the iMac, the New Beetle, the MACH3 razor -- begins merging the waves through computer-aided design, and the iPod, launched five weeks after 9/11 and named for Kubrick's pod ('Open the pod bay door, Hal'), is the 'minimalist blobject' or 'squircle' where the merger completes. Reading the moment through Heidegger's claim that technology transforms human existence 'in its innermost recesses' and through Freud's pleasure versus reality principles, he argues the Iraq War sealed the reality principle into consumer design: 'our iPods now have edges.'

berkeley-idealism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
berkeley-idealism.title: Doomed to Be Perceived
berkeley-idealism.relation: Smithka tests Berkeley's 'to be is to be perceived' against two monsters: the Vashta Nerada, whose existence is inferred from indirect evidence (counting shadows, the 'ghosting' of Miss Evangelista) much like Neptune was inferred from Uranus's orbit, and the Weeping Angels, which act only when unperceived and so falsify Berkeley's principle. Working through Locke on substance, Hume's skepticism about unperceivable causes like God, Paley's watchmaker design argument, and scientific realism (Sellars, Churchland) versus van Fraassen's empirically adequate anti-realism, she concludes the Doctor is a realist about unobservables — for whom the Angels are real but 'doomed to be perceived'.

berkeley-idealism.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
berkeley-idealism.title: The Challenge to (Dis)connect
berkeley-idealism.relation: Patrick Tiernan reads the fantasy of 'I am playing Halo' through Huizinga's play circle and Caillois's mimicry—players temporarily shed their personality for Master Chief's—then through Lacan, whose mirror stage and ideal ego explain projecting oneself onto the Chief's concealing mirrored visor, while Jungian archetypes (persona, animus/anima, self) make Chief, Cortana, and the Covenant resonate like people we know. Berkeley's 'to be is to be perceived' captures a gameworld that exists only as perceived, warning that escapist perception can dull players to real conflict in the Middle East and Africa. Teilhard de Chardin's noosphere—the true ego growing in inverse proportion to egoism—offers the social antidote, so escapism is healthy only if the player can still disconnect and remember it is only a game.

berkeley-idealism.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
berkeley-idealism.title: The Power of Choice
berkeley-idealism.relation: Rennett tests Cobb's choice to leave Limbo against Nozick's three reasons for refusing the experience machine: we want to actually do things (raise his real children, not loving projections), to be a certain kind of person (Yusuf's dream-den addicts are 'indeterminate blobs'), and to touch something deeper than a man-made world. He then recruits Berkeley's esse est percipi to explain Mal's sincerity - she perceives Limbo and remembers it, so for her it is real - and argues that shared dreams differ from private dreams and the experience machine because they leave waking traces, like Mal's bullet in Arthur's leg. The chapter ends by making reality a matter of choice: like the cave prisoners of Plato's allegory, each character believes a world, and Cobb's ignoring of the top is his choice to live in the world with his children.

berkeley-idealism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
berkeley-idealism.title: Chapter 29 - “King of the Elves”
berkeley-idealism.relation: Michelle Gallagher reads 'King of the Elves' as a challenge to Berkeley's empiricist criterion of reality: we call real whatever behaves as our past experience leads us to expect, unlike airborne goldfish imagined at whim - which is why we can tell dreams from waking life and why children struggle to. Shadrach Jones, the drab gas-station owner, keeps accepting Elves, Trolls and his own kingship although Elves are 'precisely the thing you wouldn't expect', and his swings of belief track his desires - the grandeur of kingship, dread of the Troll war, the appeal of being needed - until he kills his friend Phineas, the Troll King. Whether the tale is a genuine Elven chronicle or a delusional murder, Shadrach decides he really is King of the Elves because he wanted to: reality attribution driven by wish rather than expectation.

berkeley-idealism.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
berkeley-idealism.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
berkeley-idealism.relation: T. Bradley Richards takes The Sandman's Dreamworld seriously as a hypothesis: could our nightly dreams be travels to a mind-independent place like Morpheus's realm? Starting from Zhuangzi's butterfly dream and Descartes's dream argument, he uses Berkeley's God-sustained idealism as a model for how Morpheus's mind could uphold the Dreamworld's order, and a thought experiment about glitchy dream-travel defuses Descartes's appeal to the discontinuity of dreams. Against the objection that dreams are blatantly contradictory ('it was Dave, but it also wasn't Dave'), he deploys Russell's theory of descriptions against Meinongian subsistence, Chalmers-style conceivability-implies-possibility reasoning from philosophical zombies, and Graham Priest's dialetheism, concluding that dreams could be experiences of an objective world, with waking and dreaming on a par.

berkeley-idealism.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
berkeley-idealism.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
berkeley-idealism.relation: Arp uses King Worm's dream-within-dreams to pose the perception-reality problem: distinguishing perceiver, perceptions, and perceived, he maps the triad onto Plato's allegory of the cave, then contrasts epistemological and metaphysical realism (the fallen tree fort still makes sound waves unheard; Pythagoras discovered rather than invented his theorem) with idealism and antirealism, whose dead end is solipsism—Lumpy Space Princess locked in a private movie theater of perceptions. Hume's picture of the mind as a theater of successive perceptions and Berkeley's Hylas-and-Philonous worry that we are trapped inside perceptual reality give the skeptical threat its force. The chapter sides with Jake—'You gotta focus on what's real, man'—while conceding that after 'King Worm' Finn and Jake can never be certain they escaped the hypnotism.

berkeley-idealism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
berkeley-idealism.title: 17. What if Our Reality Is One Big Hallucination
berkeley-idealism.relation: Arp starts from Rick's hallucinations of Lori - the disconnected phone in "Hounded," the touch and kiss in "Home" - and Michonne's confessed visions, showing how Rick distinguishes them through coherence with causal law and through third-person verification (Michonne watching him stroke empty air; Morgan's isolation in "Clear" showing why social checks matter). He then widens this into the theory of knowledge: the perceiver-perception-perceived triangle, epistemological and metaphysical realism versus idealism and antirealism, Berkeley's picture of the mind as a movie theater we cannot exit, and the Walking Dead twist on the falling tree in the forest, concluding that even if reality were one big hallucination we would still live - and refuse to walk off cliffs - as realists.

berkeley-idealism.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
berkeley-idealism.title: 8. The Babe with the Power
berkeley-idealism.relation: Michaud uses Bowie's Jareth and Labyrinth to make Berkeley's case that only minds and ideas exist: the taste of Sarah's tainted fruit, colors no culture without a word for 'blue' can see, dreams and optical illusions, and hallucinations all show the perceived world is a brain-made prediction, so the Goblin King's magic realm is 'more possible than we realize.' Because each of us builds a private world - Sarah and Jareth can never compare experiences ('I wonder what your basis for comparison is') - Bowie's death is literally the collapse of the world as he created it, 'as the world falls down,' though music may still reach across the void.

berkeley-idealism.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
berkeley-idealism.title: 1. Breaking Sixteen Walls
berkeley-idealism.relation: Rhiannon Grant argues Deadpool's fourth-wall breaks make him a great philosopher and sociologist because they enact the examined life: like Socrates's unexamined-life dictum, Deadpool steps outside his world to ask new questions about it ('Stewart or McAvoy?'), and even examines his own habit of examining—the 'sixteen walls' break inside a break. Wittgenstein's fly-bottle becomes the trap of circular philosophical argument that Deadpool escapes by seeing the bottle from outside, while Berkeley's solipsism is the failed attempt to live as if the world existed only in one's mind. A closing dialogue has Professor X coach Deadpool through insider/outsider research ethics and objectivity (the sperm-and-egg microscope example), showing how fourth-wall skill lets a researcher view a community from both inside and outside.

berkeley-idealism.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
berkeley-idealism.title: 17. Our Lying Eyes
berkeley-idealism.relation: Wood asks how Elliot - and we, who see only what he sees - can know anything, and contrasts two empiricisms: Locke's white-paper mind furnished by ideas copied from mind-independent objects, which explains Mr. Robot as perceptual error, and Berkeley's idealism, on which only ideas and their divine cause exist, which makes Elliot's unshared hallucination of Mr. Robot dangerously hard to distinguish from reality. Consistency of perception is the only test left, and it fails Elliot until the pier video proves no one pushed him - and fails us again when his cozy Season Two routine turns out to be prison.

berkeley-idealism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
berkeley-idealism.title: 31. Does the Hulk Have a Soul
berkeley-idealism.relation: Weighs whether the Hulk has a soul by running philosophy of mind's three positions: substance dualism (qualia and the hard problem, Plantinga's modal argument via Leibniz's Law — Peter Parker really is Spider-Man — but an unresolved mind–body interaction problem), physicalism (causal closure and conservation of energy, rebutted through objective truths and Einstein's dynamic spacetime), and idealism (Berkeley's master argument plus the holographic principle and quantum observation). It concludes idealism best explains Banner: Hulk and Banner share one mind/soul whose information is projected as two different 3D bodies, with the Ancient One's 'source code that shapes reality' speech in Doctor Strange as idealism's on-screen statement.

berkeley-idealism.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
berkeley-idealism.title: Perceptions Are Fine, but Dull Reality Is Still Better
berkeley-idealism.relation: Distinguishes perceiver, perceptions, and perceived external objects to ask whether Alice, or anyone, can get beyond her perceptions to a mind-independent world, entering through Robert Arp's own painkiller hallucination of stones that were really Jell-O. The chapter sets epistemological idealism and metaphysical antirealism (the movie-theater-in-the-mind picture, traced to Plato's cave and Berkeley's suggestion that we are trapped inside perceptual reality) against the epistemological and metaphysical realism it finds in Alice and Carroll: fossilized ferns, dodo birds, and the Pythagorean theorem are discovered rather than invented, and at story's end everything rightly changes 'to dull reality'.

berkeley-idealism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
berkeley-idealism.title: Rowling as an Inkling
berkeley-idealism.relation: Argues Dumbledore's remark dissolves a false dilemma: the Hermione-as-idea versus Emma Watson contrast shows that existing in the head need not mean unreal. It then surveys thinkers who agree that mind and reality overlap: Plato's forms (the many broomsticks as imperfect copies of the ideal broomstick), Descartes on knowing essences by reason, Kant's mind-constructed objects, Berkeley's esse est percipi, Mill's phenomenalism, and Yogacara Buddhism's consciousness-fabricated emptiness, concluding that what is in the head can be genuinely real.

berkeley-idealism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
berkeley-idealism.title: The Power of Choice
berkeley-idealism.relation: Rennett stages Ariadne's 'who would want to be stuck in a dream for ten years?' against Nozick's experience machine: Nozick's three reasons for staying unplugged (doing rather than merely experiencing, being a determinate person, contact with a reality deeper than human construction) map onto Cobb's reasons for leaving Limbo — he wants to actually raise his children, be a good father, and love children who can love him back rather than projections. Against Nozick, the chapter enlists Berkeley's esse est percipi to explain Mal's choice: a perceived world is real, and Inception's shared dreams pass Berkeley's intersubjective test in ways private dreams cannot (Cobb apologizes to Arthur for being shot; dream acts carry waking consequences). It concludes that reality becomes what we choose to believe — Cobb's final refusal to watch the top, like the cave prisoners rejecting release, is the power of choice.

berkeley-idealism.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
berkeley-idealism.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
berkeley-idealism.relation: Terjesen uses spider-sense to tour early-modern philosophy of perception: against direct realism, Locke's indirect realism and its primary/secondary quality distinction suggest 'dangerousness' is a perceiver-relative secondary quality — bombs threaten Spider-Man but not the Hulk, and Mysterio manufactures danger-experiences — while Berkeley's idealism and Hume's phenomenalism radicalize the resulting skepticism about ever verifying sense data. The decisive clue is that spider-sense fails when Aunt May conks Peter with a vase (Amazing Spider-Man #114) and when his mentor Miles Warren becomes the Jackal: Peter does not fear those he loves. This supports Hume's sentimentalist account of moral judgment, on which vice is found not in the act but in the disapproving sentiment, moderated by Reid's common-sense reply that perception always already contains judgment — so spider-sense is a moralized judgment about what to avoid, not a Geiger counter.

berkeley-idealism.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
berkeley-idealism.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
berkeley-idealism.relation: Chaib takes Ruby's line that Hell is 'forgetting what you are' and reads God's character through early modern philosophy: Descartes' supremely real being and deceiving demon frame Castiel's delusion of godhood and Ruby's manipulation of Sam, Spinoza's denial that evil exists (it is 'inadequate knowledge') explains the comprehensible motives of Crowley and Lucifer, Berkeley's claim that things persist only because God perceives them makes a dead God an existential threat, and Kant's 'moral theism' rebuts dogmatic atheism. With Hegel and Fromm, Hell becomes self-forgetting and communion with God becomes self-knowledge achieved through knowing others, the opposite of Ruby's Hell. The chapter concludes via Locke that closing Hell's gates would deny once-human demons the redemption tied to our very idea of God, so the brothers' forgiving love, unlike Michael and Lucifer's rigidity, reflects God's nature.

berkeley-idealism.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
berkeley-idealism.title: Eighteenth Hole Swing Thoughts Tough Questions for a Tough Game
berkeley-idealism.relation: Andy Wible closes the volume with fourteen open-ended 'swing thoughts'—short provocations applying philosophy to golf rather than arguing a thesis. He asks whether golf's subdued, rational fans make it morally superior (Plato and Aristotle on reason ruling emotion), whether Tiger Woods effectively wielded Plato's Ring of Gyges by sinning while invisible, whether Berkeley's idealism means your clubs and playing partners are mere perceptions (and whether that would matter), and invokes Augustine's 'an unjust law is no law at all' to license civil disobedience against unfair rules like spike marks. Further questions probe environmental harm, prayer as cheating, Casey Martin's cart, and whether perfect virtual golf would count as 'real' golf.

berkeley-idealism.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
berkeley-idealism.title: 14_LaRocca_Chapter_013.html
berkeley-idealism.relation: Mieke Bal frames her documentaries Mille et un jours and the installation Nothing is Missing around the ethical tension between 'modesty' and 'intimacy' in filming trauma. She reads Descartes's Passions of the Soul against the vulgate dualist cogito—arguing the isolating 'I think, I am' enacts his own abandonment trauma—and sets it beside Spinoza's socially constituted subject, while using Berkeley's 'esse est percipi' (reversed via the empowering close-up of a mother's face) and Deleuze's affection-image and rhizome. The multiplied, dispersed 'voice' of the Tunisian wedding film and Elena's silences become tools of a 'migratory aesthetics.'

berkeley-idealism.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
berkeley-idealism.title: 28_LaRocca_Chapter_027.html
berkeley-idealism.relation: Hagberg argues that Grant Gee's documentary Patience (After Sebald) achieves a truthful portrait of W. G. Sebald not by static correspondence but by enacting his shifting, connection-making sensibility, as displayed in The Rings of Saturn. He deploys Wittgenstein's remarks on aspect-perception and 'seeing-as' (the duck-rabbit, the 'lighting up of an aspect') to show that perception is always already inflected by imagination, memory and language-games, dismantling the empiricist picture of Locke, Hume and Berkeley in which brute sensation precedes reflection. Borges's 'The Garden of Forking Paths' and 'Tlon, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius' supply the model of a Heraclitean flux of forking, mind-dependent connections, and the film's darkroom-like fading images and layered soundtrack are read as mimetically faithful to how a human sensibility perceives and remembers.

berkeley-idealism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
berkeley-idealism.title: Doomed to Be Perceived
berkeley-idealism.relation: Paula Smithka uses the Vashta Nerada and Weeping Angels to examine perception and the reality of unobservables. She sets Berkeley's "to be is to be perceived" against Locke's hidden substance and Hume's empiricist skepticism (and Paley's design argument), then distinguishes direct from indirect perceptual evidence, using the shadows, skeletal remains, and Neptune's discovery to frame scientific realism versus van Fraassen's antirealism. The Weeping Angels invert Berkeley, existing only when unperceived and turning to stone when observed, so for them to be is NOT to be perceived.

berkeley-idealism.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
berkeley-idealism.title: McElligot’s Pool Epistemology (with Fish!)
berkeley-idealism.relation: Ron Novy uses Marco's faith that unseen fish swim in McElligot's Pool to survey theories of knowledge as justified true belief. The farmer's empiricism and Marco's inference from a book frame a tour through Descartes's evil-genius doubt and skepticism, Locke's primary/secondary qualities (indirect realism), Berkeley's idealism ('to be is to be perceived'), and rationalist a priori knowledge, before turning to feminist epistemology (Schott, Kant's 'intuitions without concepts are blind,' Nietzsche on perspectival seeing) and Quine's naturalized epistemology to argue knowers are situated and the pool may indeed be 'bigger than you or I know.'

berkeley-idealism.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
berkeley-idealism.title: 2. The Matrix
berkeley-idealism.relation: Rowlands reads The Matrix as a vivid staging of Cartesian skepticism: Neo's pod-world is Descartes's dream and evil-demon conjectures (AI plays the demon) plus the modern brain-in-a-vat, showing we cannot be certain the external world exists. He uses the 'there is no air/muscles' and 'twin buildings' variant of Putnam's Twin Earth to argue we cannot even be certain which thoughts we think. The Hume-Nietzsche bundle critique undermines even the cogito, and the spoon-bending boy ('there is no spoon') illustrates Berkeley's idealism as the endpoint of skepticism about the physical world.

berkeley-idealism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
berkeley-idealism.title: 83. Disco Elysium as Philosophy Solipsism, Existentialism, and Simulacra
berkeley-idealism.relation: Khamis reads Disco Elysium's 'Pale'—a property-less substance said to be decaying human thought that consumes reality—through three idealisms. The phasmid's warning that the world might vanish if humans stop thinking it evokes Berkeley's subjective idealism (esse est percipi) but without God as guarantor, leaving Harry in existential dread. The Pale as human-produced 'second nature' laid over 'first nature' evokes Kant's and Schelling's transcendental idealism, while the Pale as decaying signs without signification—like the vacuous dockworker 'sheriffs'—matches Baudrillard's hyperreality and simulacra, where information proliferates as meaning collapses, paralleling the amnesiac Harry's own loss and remaking of self.

argument-from-reason.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
argument-from-reason.title: Rowling as an Inkling
argument-from-reason.relation: Reads Rowling through C. S. Lewis and the Inklings: Lewis's 'argument from reason', born of Owen Barfield's critique of his realism and later reformulated by Alvin Plantinga (after Lewis's debate with Elizabeth Anscombe), holds that if thought were a purely subjective naturalistic event we could not trust its deliverances, so rationality must participate in a cosmic Logos. The chapter suggests this logos tradition - Greek animating principle, Stoic divine reason, and finally Christ as incarnate logos in John 1:1 - explains how Harry's King's Cross dialogue can be both mental and real, noting Rowling's remark that the location was no coincidence.

argument-from-reason.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
argument-from-reason.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
argument-from-reason.relation: Debunks the 'Anscombe legend' that Lewis abandoned rational apologetics for children's stories after his 1948 Socratic Club defeat by Elizabeth Anscombe over the argument that naturalism is self-refuting. It shows Lewis revised and expanded the argument in the 1960 Miracles, incorporating Anscombe's reasons/causes distinction, and kept writing apologetic essays, while the Professor's trilemma about Lucy (liar, lunatic, or truthful) mirrors the Trilemma of Mere Christianity and shows Narnia using logic, not fleeing it. It rejects A.N. Wilson's identification of the Green Witch with Anscombe and argues the Chronicles teach that prudence and faith are compatible virtues: Edmund's rationalizing, Trumpkin's honest skepticism, and Puzzle's blind trust in Shift all show that fideistic faith is a vice, not what Lewis asks of children.

argument-from-reason.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
argument-from-reason.title: Harry’s Near-Death Experience
argument-from-reason.relation: Develops the essay's boldest suggestion: reading Rowling through C. S. Lewis and the Inklings, whose associate Barfield convinced Lewis that if thought were a purely subjective event, logical and moral claims to truth would collapse, the germ of Lewis's argument from reason later refined by Plantinga and contested by Anscombe. On this view our logic participates in a cosmic Logos, which Christians identify with Christ, a point the chapter ties to Rowling's remark that it was no coincidence Harry's fateful dialogue happened at King's Cross, so what occurs in the head can genuinely put us in touch with reality.

extended-mind.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
extended-mind.title: “A Swirling, Silvery Mass”
extended-mind.relation: Opens Amy Kind's Pensieve chapter: the basin lets you offload memories like data from a hard drive, gain distance from obsessions, and, as Dumbledore tells Harry, spot patterns and links when reviewing them from outside. Its real intrigue is philosophical: if thoughts can be extracted from the mind, tampered with, stored elsewhere, shared, and discarded, then the boundaries of mind, memory, and self are up for grabs - and memory-based accounts of personal identity, on which philosophers have modeled our continuing existence, come under pressure.

extended-mind.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
extended-mind.title: Confundus!
extended-mind.relation: Challenges the assumption that the mind is self-contained: Tom Riddle's diary, in which a memory acts and thinks for itself, and Clark and Chalmers's 'The Extended Mind' thesis show that external objects can be part of thought rather than mere aids, as with Otto's Alzheimer's notebook and a wizard's intimate bond with his wand (Moody's eye and Pettigrew's silver hand as body prostheses). Location is incidental to ownership: Snape's gossamer memories are his whether in his skull, a phial, or the Pensieve.

extended-mind.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
extended-mind.title: Mischief Managed
extended-mind.relation: Defends extension against intuition via the occurrent/nonoccurrent belief distinction: Ron's stored Quidditch trivia and Rita Skeeter's knowledge of where Bathilda Bagshot lives function exactly like Otto's notebook entries, so Otto counts as believing the address even before consulting the page. Harry's Half-Blood Prince notes, Neville's password list, and Hermione's constant Hogwarts, A History fail the test of extension because they lack the notebook's constant availability and automatic endorsement.

extended-mind.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
extended-mind.title: Lumos!
extended-mind.relation: Pushes the theory to its disturbing limit: if the Marauder's Map is part of both Fred's and George's extended minds, minds can overlap. Since identity rests on memory continuity (Locke's theory, the adult Harry identical with the orphaned infant), memory-sharing, Obliviation, and implanted or stolen memories - Barty Crouch Jr.'s Polyjuice theft of Moody's identity, Lockhart's memory charms, Hermione's rewriting of her parents - threaten who we are, and Harry's Pensieve encounters with Snape's worst memory and his own status as a Horcrux trigger his identity crises.

extended-mind.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
extended-mind.title: “I Got this Guitar and I Learned How to Make It Talk”
extended-mind.relation: The editors unpack Springsteen's 1988 speech inducting Bob Dylan: Elvis freed America's body from Cold War-era repression (duck-and-cover fear, Calvinist stiffness), Dylan freed the mind by bringing ambiguity ('Mr. Tambourine Man,' 'Maggie's Farm'), and Springsteen's own project was to free heart and soul — 'heartwork' in the early songs, 'soulwork' from Nebraska on. Their key philosophical move is embodied: you are not under the school desk because you are afraid, you are afraid because your body is under the desk, so intellectual freedom grows out of bodily freedom, and the guitar — flesh stretched over wood — literally talks for and with the audience. The revolution still fails, they concede, since hearts stay broken and the soul finds only hope in hard work, decency, family, and conversation.

extended-mind.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
extended-mind.title: After Forgetting
extended-mind.relation: Sturgis argues that iPods plus the collaborative Web 2.0 will end education's age of memorization: the school 'cheaters' storing test answers in lyrics files are early adopters of a world where, as Plato's Meno already allowed, knowledge can be retrieved rather than remembered, and a remote server is no more crash-prone than a brain ('the server could crash, but so could I'). His own podcasted environmental-ethics course shows Socratic, question-driven lecturing and radio's 'theater of the mind' reaching distance learners, while MIT OpenCourseWare and Berkeley webcasts (a trucker listening to Hubert Dreyfus) globalize elite content. Following Dewey on reflection and artistry, he predicts a post-factual pedagogy of assessing sources -- he catches Wikipedia misreading an iPod '90 percent market share' claim -- collaborative creation, and candid acceptance that we are already integrated with technological devices.

extended-mind.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
extended-mind.title: Bring It On Home to You
extended-mind.relation: Jeanette Bicknell argues that the two classic models of creativity—Plato's Ion, where the rhapsode is a divinely possessed conduit, and Kant's solitary genius who issues new rules—cannot explain a four-piece rock band, since both are individualistic, purely mental, and end in mystery. Her positive account uses Clark and Chalmers's extended mind (Page describes his guitar as 'an extension of you', instruments and notation as cognitive props) and Keith Sawyer's collaborative emergence: Zeppelin's creativity happened in rehearsal and performance, as with the stairwell-recorded drum groove of 'When the Levee Breaks' that framed every later musical decision. The transformation of Joan Baez's 'Babe, I'm Gonna Leave You' into a whisper-to-cry hard-rock template shows the band creating something no member could have produced or predicted alone.

extended-mind.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
extended-mind.title: Wave Goodbye from the Catbus
extended-mind.relation: Heinricy argues anime is the richest medium for posthuman theory because it shows bodies 'in a state of becoming' rather than as grotesque boundary violations: Miyazaki's Catbus and Totoro, Haku's dragon transformation and Chihiro's pig parents in Spirited Away, and the cursed pig-headed aviator of Porco Rosso all treat morphing bodies as possibility, not horror. She sorts anime posthumanism into two valences: a 'Ghost in the Machine' dream of consciousness leaving the body altogether (Motoko merging with the net in Ghost in the Shell), which she rebuts via N. Katherine Hayles's point that consciousness is embodied and would change with any new body, and hybrid configurations like mecha (Gundam, Robotech) where body and machine drive each other. Following Donna Haraway, she contends we are all already cyborgs — vaccines, engineered food, treated water — and credits Japan's nuclear history (via Susan Napier) and its shape-shifting folklore for why anime embraces rather than fears the transformed body.

extended-mind.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
extended-mind.title: The Transforming Body
extended-mind.relation: McBlane reads Oshii's Ghost in the Shell as staging the collision between a humanist framework — Cartesian ghost-in-shell dualism where consciousness is the seat of identity — and a posthuman 'mindbody' of distributed cognition in which the body is an informational circuit extending into the net, so a data body is still a body. Motoko's crisis (is the real me the organic brain, the ghost, or nothing?) deepens through the hacked garbage-truck man ('There's nothing sadder than a puppet without a ghost') and resolves only in her fusion with the Puppet Master, whose line 'Your effort to remain what you are is what limits you' enacts the shift from one ghost to multiple, distributed subjectivities ending in a little girl's body with 'The net is vast.' Heidegger's Dasein and being-in-the-world supply the claim that access to Being expands beyond the human into technological and informational modes, while the film's angelic transcendence imagery shows how residual humanist mind-body splits persist even in a posthuman story.

extended-mind.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
extended-mind.title: Where Parfit Went Wrong
extended-mind.relation: Peter Ludlow and Chiara Repetti-Ludlow read Red vs. Blue as an intuition pump for personal identity, running through Locke's prince-and-cobbler, Bernard Williams's duplicated Guy Fawkes, Shoemaker's brain transplant, and Wiggins's split brain before aiming at Parfit. Project Freelancer's Director fractures the Alpha AI into fragments (Epsilon's memories, Omega's rage) recombined into the Meta, and they argue intuitions break against Parfit here: psychological continuity via small fractured pieces—unlike Parfit's fission into two substantial halves—does not secure the source's survival. Church's disembodied AI existence and the ever-present agent-AI voice (Agent Washington driven mad by Epsilon) illustrate Putnam's 'soul stuff' and the extended-mind hypothesis of Chalmers and Clark better than Chalmers waving his iPhone.

extended-mind.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
extended-mind.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
extended-mind.relation: Levi Bryant argues the D&D universe models a 'flat ontology' of active substances whose powers (affects) actualize differently under local conditions, asking Democritus-style individuation questions about whether a band of ogres at a tavern is one entity or many. Characters and their gear form alliances that generate genuinely new beings, so the blind man with his cane, or Moorcock's Elric fed by the soul-drinking sword Stormbringer, is a different entity than without it, and he borrows Clark and Chalmers' extended mind hypothesis to deny that thinking happens only inside the head. The dice then supply chance that generates necessity: the Dungeon Master's throws conjure traps, wraiths and saving throws that form 'regimes of attraction' to which every player and monster must respond.

extended-mind.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
extended-mind.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
extended-mind.relation: Kristin Andrews uses Taylor's silent attempts to show Zira he has a mind - mouthing answers, wiggling his fingers when she mentions the Hopkins Manual Dexterity Test - to stage the problem of other minds, pushing against Descartes's claim that language is required for thought and Mill's argument from analogy, while Dr. Zaius can always redescribe it all as 'a definite gift for mimicry.' Drawing on her fieldwork with the orangutan Cecep (the leaf-wiping pantomime, guiding the frightened Aldrin home from the turtle scare), she argues against reducing mindreading to false-belief tasks and for knowing minds through shared interaction, inductive overhypotheses, and natural context. She ends with an extended-mind point - 'when you're in a cage, you act caged,' and we offload thinking onto our homes and tools - so lab studies can show what apes can do but never what they can't.

extended-mind.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
extended-mind.title: 15. Memories. In the End, Is That All There Is
extended-mind.relation: David LaRocca tests Mr. Carson's claim that 'the business of life is the acquisition of memories. In the end, that's all there is' against the tradition of spatial memory metaphors and modern neuroscience. Downton itself becomes a memory palace - echoing Cicero, the Ad Herennium, and Augustine's 'court of memory' - whose characters defer endlessly to the past, while photographs (Tom with Sybil's image, Carson with Alice Neal's) act as sources and surrogates of memory in an age of acquisitional capitalism. Daniella Schiller's reconsolidation research, Nicholas Carr's Nietzsche-typewriter anecdote, and Langdon Winner's point that technologies reshape life show memories are malleable rather than collectible possessions, undermining Carson's model and any fixed memory-based account of personal identity.

extended-mind.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
extended-mind.title: 5. We Become the Grid
extended-mind.relation: Ketcham updates Hobbes for the network age: the grid born of ARPANET and Cold War mutual destruction has devolved into a new state of nature, out of which a coming 'Leviathan' - the one percent of the one percent - will rule invisibly by curating your memories, your purchases, your spouse, and whole countries like the diamond-republic fable. Invoking Descartes's evil demon and Heidegger's ready-to-hand, he asks whether we have become the grid, an external brain we can no longer control, and concludes that Elliot, the rogue 'Ebola' who hacks for justice rather than profit, is exactly the loose cannon Leviathan would quarantine.

extended-mind.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
extended-mind.title: 11. Vibrations and Echoes Long Ago
extended-mind.relation: Argues Hendrix's sound was made with — not merely on — studio technology: Eddie Kramer's Olympic Studios innovations, in the lineage of the BBC Radiophonic Workshop, used feedback, varispeed, and backwards tape as performing instruments. Andy Clark and David Chalmers's extended mind thesis (Chalmers's own example is Hendrix's mind extending into his guitar) and Chalmers on Pokémon Go frame the analog recordings as a more immersive augmented reality than digital games, while Kittler's claim that media 'determine our situation' and the time-bending processes of 'Purple Haze' and 'Are You Experienced?' explain how listening disorients and enriches our perception of time and space.

extended-mind.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
extended-mind.title: 21. The Extended Fight
extended-mind.relation: Porot applies Clark and Chalmers's extended mind to the final Civil War fight: Iron Man extends his cognition technologically (Friday analyzing Cap's fight pattern mid-bout, JARVIS remembering to suggest calling Pepper), while Captain America extends his mind socially through trusted, autonomous teammates - 'Alright, Sam, what's the plan?' - and that social extension is precisely what wins when Bucky autonomously steps in. Bostrom's single-purpose AI (the stapler maximizer) explains Ultron as what happens when the technological extension is made autonomous and limitless, which is why Stark's suit extensions must remain vetted, worthy instruments he takes full responsibility for ('That was me'). The two kinds of extension then explain the Bucky dispute - Cap's 'you had no choice' versus Stark's 'he still did it' - which the author reframes away from the free-will-versus-determinism framing toward Black Panther's point that Bucky is a victim whose agency Hydra stole.

extended-mind.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
extended-mind.title: Gaming Freedom Choosing or Obeying
extended-mind.relation: Pointon argues the 'would you kindly' twist in Andrew Ryan's office works on two levels at once: it reveals Jack's conditioning within the game and simultaneously falsifies the player's meta-narrative of playing a free agent. He uses Clark and Chalmers's extended mind to explain why games literally extend cognition and body (mirror-neuron empathy with Little Sisters, craning your neck while peeking around corners), and Gadamer's hermeneutic horizons and fusion of horizons to explain how BioShock deliberately builds and then shatters player expectations. The three alternative endings keyed to saving or harvesting Little Sisters then restore a third horizon in which the player, like Jack fighting Fontaine, is a 'man' who chooses rather than a slave who obeys, a critique of linear RPGs that only feign autonomy.

extended-mind.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
extended-mind.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
extended-mind.relation: Levi Bryant uses the D&D universe to expound a 'flat ontology' of active substances: every entity, from enchanted swords to white dragons, has a virtual proper being (powers or 'affects') that actualizes variable 'local manifestations' depending on circumstances like lighting or armor. Adopting Andy Clark and David Chalmers's extended mind hypothesis, he argues a blind man with a cane, a smartphone owner, or Elric wielding Stormbringer is a literally different mind or entity, and that alliances (Raistlin's Staff of Magius, a warrior's plate armor) generate genuinely new powers rather than mere tool-use. Against Democritus's atomism, he holds aggregates can be individuals, and the game's dice embody his claim that chance produces necessity: throws generate 'regimes of attraction' no DM or player controls. D&D thus mirrors our own world of hidden powers, aleatory encounters and collectives of humans and nonhumans.

extended-mind.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
extended-mind.title: Notes
extended-mind.relation: The Funkes apply Clark and Chalmers's extended mind hypothesis to the Pip-Boy, arguing it meets all three criteria for cognitive extension - availability (worn at all times), reliability (trusted rad and health monitoring), and active cognitive engagement (V.A.T.S. offloads targeting calculations) - so it is part of the Sole Survivor's and Courier's minds, as in 'The Glowing Sea' and the search for Virgil's cure. Donna Haraway's cyborg frames this human-machine hybridity alongside cyberdogs and Kellogg, but Fallout inverts her liberationist vision: the Pip-Boy is a survival lifeline forced by the wasteland, not an emancipatory choice, making the cyborg a dystopian necessity. Comparing the Pip-Boy with cochlear implants, prosthetics, and brain-computer interfaces, and the Old World Blues Think Tank with a dehumanizing bio-tech extreme, the chapter uses Alison Kafer's feminist crip critique to insist real augmentation carries pain, stigma, and unequal access the game's frictionless fiction erases, closing on a cautious transhumanist note.

extended-mind.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
extended-mind.title: “A Swirling, Silvery Mass”
extended-mind.relation: Opens Amy Kind's essay by presenting the Pensieve as a device for offloading memories like data from a hard drive, easing obsession and revealing patterns, and asks what that does to the boundaries of mind, memory, and self. If thoughts can be extracted from the head, tampered with, stored elsewhere, and shared, as with the Pensieve and Tom Riddle's diary, then memory-based accounts of what makes a person persist over time come under pressure, and it is no longer obvious whose mind a thought belongs to.

extended-mind.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
extended-mind.title: Confundus!
extended-mind.relation: Challenges the assumption that the mind stops at the skull by deploying Clark and Chalmers's extended mind thesis: just as a prosthetic leg, Moody's magic eye, or Harry's holly-and-phoenix-feather wand can count as part of the body, Otto's notebook shows external storage functioning as memory itself rather than a mere aid. Tom Riddle's diary, where a memory acts and thinks for itself because a soul fragment lived in it, and Snape's memories being his whether in his head, a phial, or the Pensieve make physical location incidental to mental ownership.

extended-mind.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
extended-mind.title: Mischief Managed
extended-mind.relation: Defends the Otto case against the obvious objection that notebook entries are not conscious beliefs: most beliefs, like Ron's that Ireland beat Bulgaria at the Quidditch World Cup, are nonoccurrent anyway, and Rita Skeeter pausing to recall where Bathilda Bagshot lives works exactly like Otto consulting his notebook. Constant integration is what separates genuine mind-extension from mere aids, which is why Harry's borrowed Half-Blood Prince textbook, Neville's password list, and even Hermione's well-thumbed Hogwarts, A History stay outside the mind.

extended-mind.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
extended-mind.title: Lumos!
extended-mind.relation: Pushes the theory to its strangest consequence: if the stolen Marauder's Map belongs to the extended minds of both Fred and George Weasley, then minds can literally overlap. Combined with Locke's memory theory, the chains of memory linking the adult Harry, the teenager facing Voldemort, and the orphaned infant at the Dursleys, Pensieve sharing and magic like Barty Crouch Jr.'s Polyjuice impersonation of Moody or Hermione's rewriting of her parents' memories become genuine identity thefts, as Harry's crisis of self after seeing Snape's worst memory of James illustrates.

extended-mind.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
extended-mind.title: NOTES
extended-mind.relation: Resolves the threat by sorting memories into know-how, factual, and first-person experiential kinds: identity rides on experiential memories, but Pensieve replays are third-person, as Rowling confirmed about Dumbledore's memory of Bellatrix Lestrange's trial. So sharing a Pensieve memory endangers who you are no more than sharing an experience or using a Time-Turner, and whether your thoughts sit in a mind, a Pensieve, or a notebook, they remain your own.

extended-mind.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
extended-mind.title: Notes
extended-mind.relation: Barbara Stock uses the Borg to analyze autonomy: Picard's 'they took everything I was' names the Collective's destruction of self-governance, while Hugh's choice to return to the crash site in 'I, Borg' displays the Kantian core of autonomy—acting on universalizable principle against inclination. She defends relational autonomy through Janeway's pleading with Kes in 'The Gift' and the Ferengi woman's internalized oppression, then combines it with Clark's extended cognition to ask whether the Borg Queen's 'I am the Collective' might make the Collective itself an autonomous agent. Finally she judges Janeway's forcible de-assimilation of Seven defensible only while Seven is non-autonomous, and her promise never to let Seven return ethically suspect.

extended-mind.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
extended-mind.title: Notes
extended-mind.relation: Reads the Borg as the embodiment of Heidegger's essence of technology: assimilation as the "challenging" that sets upon nature, species and persons as standing-reserve, drones interchangeable like replaceable parts, and cube ships with no bridge because function outweighs individuality. The Enterprise cannot beat the Borg with more technology - every phaser adaptation buys only moments - because, as with Heidegger's danger, the crew tries to control technology from inside technology; rescue comes only when Guinan persuades Riker to "throw the book away" and shift how the crew relates to the Borg. The warning is extended to us through Zizek on synthetic life and a new servant class and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind: our devices already remember, plan, and identify for us, so we are being assimilated by our own creations.

extended-mind.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
extended-mind.title: NOTES
extended-mind.relation: Butler argues the films' humans-versus-machines picture rests on a false dichotomy: we are ourselves 'meat machines,' and functionalism makes minds computational processes realizable in silicon as much as neurons - illustrated by a Henrietta thought experiment (adapted from William Lycan) in which a friend gradually replaced with T-101 parts remains the same conscious person, and refusing this is 'human chauvinism.' Following Dawkins's extended phenotype and Andy Clark's natural-born cyborgs, he claims our tools are components of our minds, so Skynet and even the Terminator films themselves (making Cameron a cyborg of his cameras and editing suites) are extensions of human nature rather than alien 'Others.' Judgment Day, if it came, would be human suicide rather than genocide, so the real question is what values we build into our technology - 'no fate but what we make for ourselves.'

extended-mind.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
extended-mind.title: eXistenZial Angst
extended-mind.relation: Duncan Pritchard reads eXistenZ as staging radical skepticism with existential force: unlike the standard brain-in-a-vat scenario, the game 'creeps up' on Ted and Allegra so they feel the transition from reality to doubt, producing angst. Invoking Wittgenstein's On Certainty (doubt radicalized is madness), he argues sanity requires belief but not true belief, so the pair achieve a new doxastic equilibrium. He also reads the spinal 'bioport' pod as a case of Clark and Chalmers's extended cognition, where technology becomes part of and subverts the agents' cognitive processes.

extended-mind.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
extended-mind.title: 4 Extended Mind and the Music of Trans
extended-mind.relation: Umbaugh reads Young's synthesizer/Vocoder album Trans, written amid efforts to communicate with his quadriplegic son Ben ("Transformer Man"), alongside Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind thesis and its Parity Principle. He uses examples (Otto's notebook, bartenders' glassware, navigation, Dennett on the elderly) to argue cognition couples with external scaffolding, and parallels the "unnatural" reception of Trans (like the homophobic anti-disco backlash) with resistance to extended cognition, concluding both Trans and the extended mind are authentic once the "natural/artificial" boundary is questioned.

extended-mind.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
extended-mind.title: “Memory Man”
extended-mind.relation: David LaRocca reads Memento through Andy Clark and David Chalmers's Extended Mind Thesis: Leonard's tattoos, Polaroids, and notecards just are his memory, doing exactly what Otto's notebook does in their original example - so that writing 'Don't believe his lies' on a Polaroid is literally modifying his mind and carries the moral significance of interfering with his person. Drawing on Liao and Sandberg's ethics of memory modification and Noël Carroll's account of the film's reverse-ordered narrative, the chapter argues Leonard remains a culpable moral agent in his lucid moments: he knowingly 'incepts' a false command into his own extended mind to preserve the avenging-husband narrative that constitutes his identity, becoming a serial killer. It closes on our epistemic and moral duty of cognitive fidelity - to build truthful narrative identities rather than lie to ourselves into murder.

extended-mind.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
extended-mind.title: 18. Foundation and Consciousness
extended-mind.relation: Lang and Haun use Foundation to explore consciousness, noting Asimov's robots (Daneel, Andrew Martin) are simply granted minds and that a system giving all the right signs could still be a Chalmers-style philosophical zombie. Their central case is Golan Trevize merging with the starship Far Star, which they read through Clark and Chalmers's Extended Mind Thesis and the Otto-and-Inga notebook example, arguing Trevize goes beyond Otto because he gains qualitatively new experiences (feeling magnetic fields, 360-degree sight). They then test extension against Integrated Information Theory and split-brain evidence, and read the planetary group mind Gaia as panpsychism (invoking Spinoza's God-as-nature, Leibniz's monads, and Fechner's world-mind) that faces the Combination Problem, partly eased by telepathic links that relax the privacy of minds.

extended-mind.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
extended-mind.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
extended-mind.relation: Steve Matthews uses windsurfing to analyze Csikszentmihalyi's 'flow' — the loss of self-awareness in skilled action between boredom and anxiety — and argues its intensity comes from 'integration,' where footstraps and harness bind sailor to kit so the equipment becomes 'an extension of oneself.' Invoking Descartes' own admission that mind and body form a unity (not merely pilot in a vessel), he applies Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind thesis: the windsurfer's kit and body form a coupled cognitive system, so 'I' extends to include the gear. He distinguishes true flow from mere goal-satisfaction (rejecting the ocean-cruiser's landfall as flow) and, via Velleman, locates flow's value in intrinsically motivated action that is its own end.

extended-mind.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
extended-mind.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
extended-mind.relation: Brunstein surveys emerging wearable technology — solar-charging jackets, the M-Dress cell-phone dress, invisibility cloaks, the Hug Shirt, Diana Eng's Heartbeat Hoodie — framed by superhero costumes (Wonder Woman's lasso, Iron Man's exoskeleton) and Haraway's 'Cyborg Manifesto.' She argues that as garments start to *do* things and integrate aesthetically, the grotesque cyborg becomes the glamorous 'supermodel' cyborg, and that this reshapes how we construct the self. Her central philosophical lens is Clark and Chalmers's 'extended mind' / active externalism (with the Tetris example): if clothing becomes a functional extension of cognition, our garments' capabilities become part of a reconstructed self.

extended-mind.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
extended-mind.title: Introduction
extended-mind.relation: Rowlands introduces the 'sci-phi' project: science fiction confronts us with the alien 'other' as a mirror in which we understand ourselves, so lowbrow sci-fi films like The Matrix, Total Recall and Starship Troopers make abstract philosophy concrete. He argues philosophy is doing rather than knowing, invoking Fishburne's 'know the path vs walk the path' line and Nietzsche's dictum that one repays a teacher poorly by remaining a pupil. He mentions his own earlier 'fyborg' thesis that human cognition is embedded in the wider informational environment, prefiguring the extended mind.

extended-mind.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
extended-mind.title: 21. Black Mirror as Philosophy A Dark Reflection of Human Nature
extended-mind.relation: The chapter asks whether Black Mirror condemns technology or human nature, and argues for the latter: the 'black mirror' reflects the viewer's character. It tests and rejects the reading of the show as depicting Bostrom-style existential risk or superintelligence (via 'Metalhead' and 'San Junipero') and rejects that Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind coupling (the 'grain' in 'The Entire History of You,' 'Arkangel,' 'Crocodile') destroys human identity. Drawing on Frankfurt School critique—Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man—and Plato's and Aristotle's natural-versus-artificial distinction, it concludes technology is an agency-less imitation that magnifies preexisting human vices, and closes with Benjamin's reproducibility thesis and Bandersnatch's interactivity to suggest the show can prompt viewers to confront their own darkness.

extended-mind.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
extended-mind.title: 55. Avatar as Philosophy The Metaphysics of Switching Bodies
extended-mind.relation: Tepley asks whether Jake Sully's final body-switch with his avatar in Cameron's Avatar is metaphysically possible without brain transplant or souls. Using Locke's definition of a person and the transitivity of numerical identity, he shows animalism forbids body-switching, substance dualism (Descartes/Plato) is unavailable in the film's materialist world, and merely copying a brain pattern creates a duplicate, not the same person. His positive solution uses the constitution view (Aristotelian in origin) plus Clark's extended-mind idea to argue Jake literally extends into his avatar, then—via an analogy with split-brain corpus-callosum cases discussed by Nagel, Parfit, and van Inwagen—shrinks back so long as no second stream of consciousness forms, a model he extends to secular survival of death by mind-uploading.

extended-mind.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
extended-mind.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
extended-mind.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

locke-personal-identity.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
locke-personal-identity.title: Lumos!
locke-personal-identity.relation: Pushes the theory to its disturbing limit: if the Marauder's Map is part of both Fred's and George's extended minds, minds can overlap. Since identity rests on memory continuity (Locke's theory, the adult Harry identical with the orphaned infant), memory-sharing, Obliviation, and implanted or stolen memories - Barty Crouch Jr.'s Polyjuice theft of Moody's identity, Lockhart's memory charms, Hermione's rewriting of her parents - threaten who we are, and Harry's Pensieve encounters with Snape's worst memory and his own status as a Horcrux trigger his identity crises.

locke-personal-identity.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
locke-personal-identity.title: The Mental Realm of the Hulk
locke-personal-identity.relation: Applies Locke's memory theory: the shape-shifting Martian Manhunter and the irradiated Fantastic Four stay the same people through mental continuity, and the early comics' Banner-minded Hulk meets Locke's criterion — but the later "Hulk smash!" Hulk, who recognizes Betty Ross yet lacks Banner's memories, fails it. The chapter then breaks the criterion itself with Reid's brave-officer objection (the general both is and is not the flogged boy), Alzheimer's and Doc Ock's amnesia attack on Spider-Man, and the circularity of distinguishing genuine from false memory (the deluded fan who "remembers" starring in Adventures of Superman).

locke-personal-identity.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
locke-personal-identity.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.relation: Uses Narnia's magical transformations to probe personal identity, starting with the qualitative/numerical identity distinction illustrated by the look-alike twins Shasta and Corin in The Horse and His Boy. Aristotle's essential/accidental properties frame the question of what Eustace can lose and remain Eustace, including turning into a dragon, and Rabadash into a donkey, showing persons are not identical to their bodies. Descartes's soul argument and Locke's memory theory are tested and rejected, the latter because it cannot handle Rilian's enchanted amnesia, Shasta's forgotten infancy, or Susan's disowned memories without circularity. The chapter defends instead a first-person-perspective theory on which a person is constituted by, not identical to, a body, illustrated by the repeatedly repaired Dawn Treader and by the heroes surviving death in The Last Battle as restored points of view.

locke-personal-identity.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
locke-personal-identity.title: “Nobody’s Bob Dylan”
locke-personal-identity.relation: Vernezze and Lulewicz take Dylan's 1964 Halloween quip "I got my Bob Dylan mask on" as an entry into personal identity, testing each theory against his life: the bodily view (Zimmerman to Dylan) survives cell turnover but stumbles on brain-transplant cases; Locke's memory theory handles them but faces Reid's brave-officer regress and Alzheimer's cases, and Dylan's reincarnation lyrics ("Shelter from the Storm," "I and I") ignore memory altogether. The Christian soul view of the gospel albums ("When He Returns," "Gotta Serve Somebody") follows Descartes and Plato but cannot justify the swirl-to-filling inference that souls exist. The chapter ends sympathetic to Hume's bundle theory and the Buddhist no-self: Dylan's "I is another," his name as fabrication, and the cover album Self Portrait all deny a fixed self-created essence.

locke-personal-identity.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
locke-personal-identity.title: Dead People
locke-personal-identity.relation: William Larkin uses Romero's films - Karen Cooper devouring her father in Night of the Living Dead, Roger begging Peter to shoot him in Dawn, Riley's 'Those people are all dead' in Land - to argue that persons are res corporealis, bodily continuers, rather than Descartes's res cogitans. Our terror of becoming a zombie ourselves and our grief at recognized neighbors in the horde reveal that deep down we think persons survive as corpses, so bodily continuity suffices for identity while psychological continuity is unnecessary. The Locke-style body-switching intuition (prince and cobbler) that supports the psychological approach is dismissed as theoretically biased data compared to what good zombie fiction draws out of us.

locke-personal-identity.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
locke-personal-identity.title: Zombies and Us
locke-personal-identity.relation: Hamish Thompson asks why we kill zombies with so few qualms and whether zombification releases us from obligations to the person who was, testing brain-death criteria, altered-identity and self-defense justifications against Shaun of the Dead (Shaun's mother and Ed), Day of the Dead's Bub, White Zombie, and Invasion of the Body Snatchers. He borrows Hume's bundle theory - the self as a fiction, a bundle of perceptions rather than an essence - and Parfit's degrees of psychological continuity to dissolve the sharp alive/dead and same-person/other-person dichotomies that make zombie-killing easy. The payoff is that we are already partly zombie (Shaun's checkout line, Ed on the sofa, the author's all-night gaming), differing only in our capacity for brief autonomous, goal-directed choices like Shaun's three-plan montage.

locke-personal-identity.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
locke-personal-identity.title: Introduction
locke-personal-identity.relation: Frames Part III's metaphysics chapters. Lawrence's chapter uses The Matrix to survey dualism and the materialist theories of mind; Southworth's uses Wolverine's amnesia to test Locke's memory criterion and Jamie Madrox's duplicates for Parfit's view of identity; Pierce's asks whether Harry Potter's prophecies leave Harry free, probing compatibilism versus libertarian free will; and Littmann's asks whether Skynet's Terminators could be persons via a Terminator version of the Turing Test.

locke-personal-identity.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
locke-personal-identity.title: Be Slow to Judge
locke-personal-identity.relation: Southworth tests Locke's memory theory on Wolverine: the Cassandra Nova/Xavier mind-swap shows identity follows mind, not body, and Wolverine's serial memory wipes (Team X, Weapon X, Apocalypse's brainwashing) mean that on Locke's connected-memory view several different people have inhabited his body — with House of M's total recall suddenly loading him with responsibility for all their deeds. Jamie Madrox's duplicates then carry Parfit's objection that shared memories cannot suffice for sameness of person, pushing toward physical continuity and the chapter's deflationary moral: be slow to judge who deserves blame.

locke-personal-identity.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
locke-personal-identity.title: Identities, Selves, and Others
