locke-personal-identity.relation: Smith reads Memento as a test of Locke's memory theory of personal identity. He explains Locke's view that consciousness of past actions (not soul or body) constitutes the self, rehearses Reid's transitivity objection and the circularity objection, and uses Parfit's account of memory and fusion to defend a survival-not-identity reading. He distinguishes 'Leonard 1' (anterograde amnesiac who returns each cycle) from 'Leonard 2b', a person fused from his own memories and those projected onto Sammy Jankis, arguing we too are 'fused' survivors who reinterpret hazy pasts, complicating responsibility and concern for our futures.

locke-personal-identity.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
locke-personal-identity.title: What Is It to Be Human Blade Runner and Dark City
locke-personal-identity.relation: Knight and McKnight read Blade Runner and Dark City as noir-influenced cyberpunk that asks what it is to be human. They argue that Deckard's replicant status (the origami unicorn, the shared family photo) and Murdoch's serially reprogrammed memory show memory to be unreliable, invoking Locke's prince-and-cobbler thought experiment and the problem of new brains in one body. Their conclusion is that it is emotion and relationship, not memory, that ground agency and personhood: Roy's empathy in dying and Deckard's love for Rachael, Murdoch's love for Emma/Anna, are what mark the characters as human.

locke-personal-identity.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
locke-personal-identity.title: Rethinking the First Person Autobiography, Authorship, and the Contested Self in Malcolm X
locke-personal-identity.relation: LaRocca uses Lee's Malcolm X and Haley's 'as told to' Autobiography to probe personal identity and authorship: since Haley (not X) authored the book and Lee/Washington perform Haley's literary X, he asks whether one can write another's autobiography and what becomes of the self. He surveys Locke's memory theory of identity, Descartes's thinking subject, Hume's bundle of perceptions, and Wittgenstein's denial of a thinking subject to frame X's serial renamings (Malcolm Little, Detroit Red, Malcolm X, El-Hajj Malik El-Shabazz) as a 'ceaselessly evolving,' unfinished identity. He reads Lee's techniques—nondiegetic gunshots, the spinning camera, the gliding sidewalk shot ('the eye that can finally see itself'), and the framing Rodney King and Mandela footage ending on 'by any means necessary'—as arguments that the self is a contested literary and cinematic creation.

locke-personal-identity.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
locke-personal-identity.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
locke-personal-identity.relation: Morton reads Schizopolis as Soderbergh's philosophical autobiography of identity, quoting Locke's Essay Concerning Human Understanding on memory as the ground of personal continuity to interpret Fletcher Munson's 'transmigration' into the doppelganger Dr. Korchek. Because Fletcher carries his own memory and nature into Korchek, he cannot escape his failed marriage (Korchek is sleeping with Fletcher's wife), confirming Lockean continuity: he 'cannot escape his own nature.' Morton ties the film's decayed language games and Elmo Oxygen's gibberish to a view that language masks action, and reads Fletcher's fate-frozen ending as identity surrendered to outside forces.

locke-personal-identity.book: 240 - Neil Young and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.title: 7 Memory and Relationships in the Work and Music of Neil Young
locke-personal-identity.relation: Sizer analyzes how memory shapes Young's songwriting: childhood trauma (polio, his parents' divorce, Omemee) fueling "Sugar Mountain," "Helpless" and "I Am a Child"; the "use and lose" pattern of collaborators and the ghost of Danny Whitten in Crazy Horse; and his late-life dread of memory loss watching his father's dementia. He frames this with Hobbes and Hume on memory-as-imagery, Wittgenstein's associative memory, and Locke's memory theory of personal identity (with Dennett on writing as a means to reconstruct and preserve the self).

locke-personal-identity.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
locke-personal-identity.title: “So You Can Be My ‘John G.’”
locke-personal-identity.relation: Eberl asks whether Leonard Shelby is morally culpable for killing Teddy, since the Leonard who tattoos the false clue and the Leonard who pulls the trigger are sundered by anterograde amnesia. Locke's forensic, memory-based concept of personhood suggests the shooting Leonard is not the same person as the one who set the trap, while Aquinas's analysis of concomitant, consequent, and antecedent ignorance makes Leonard culpable for deliberately willing his own ignorance yet not for the amnesiac moment of the killing itself. Hume's causal criterion of psychological continuity explains why Leonard can still rationally set a goal for his future self by making Teddy his 'John G.' The chapter closes on Aristotle: Leonard's ease in framing an innocent man betrays a corrupted moral character built on habit, and by turning himself into a 'living instrument'—Aristotle's definition of a slave—he has traded his dignity for the telos of an endless revenge quest.

locke-personal-identity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.title: A Dead End
locke-personal-identity.relation: Patrick Stokes uses the Doctor's regeneration and the multi-Doctor stories ("The Five Doctors," "The Caves of Androzani") to test theories of personal identity. He runs Locke's memory criterion against Reid's transitivity objection, Parfit's Branch-Line teleportation case (a Gallifrey-to-Skaro replica), Nozick's Closest Continuer schema applied to the Valeyard, four-dimensional person-stages, animalism, and narrative identity, showing each fails to explain regeneration. He gestures that identity may lie in a subjective self-appropriation, the Doctor taking ownership of his incarnations.

locke-personal-identity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.title: Doctor Who and the Ultimate Answer
locke-personal-identity.relation: Greg Littmann uses regeneration and dozens of Doctor Who transformations (doubles like the Abbot of Amboise, disembodied brains, transmats, Eldrad's body-hopping, Cassandra's possession) as hypotheticals to test criteria for personal identity. He shows bodily identity, spatiotemporal continuity of the body, the memory criterion (undercut by Donna and John Smith cases), and psychological/personality similarity each face counterexamples, deliberately leaving the question open so readers judge for themselves.

locke-personal-identity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.title: What’s Persistence Without Identity
locke-personal-identity.relation: Richard Hanley asks what counts as personal survival for a Time Lord, distinguishing body, mind, and soul theories. Using the Tenth Doctor's "every single cell" regeneration, the severed hand grown into a Doctor in "Journey's End," John Smith's Chameleon-Arch amnesia, and Jackson Lake's infostamp fugue, he argues bodily and soul continuity fail and defends a neo-Lockean mental-continuity criterion refined by Nozick's closest-continuer schema, concluding with Parfit that persistence may not be what matters in survival.

locke-personal-identity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.title: I Think, Therefore I Exist . . . I Think
locke-personal-identity.relation: David Kyle Johnson uses regeneration and the DoctorDonna to ask what makes the First and Tenth Doctor the same person. He debunks the Platonic/Cartesian soul via Phineas Gage and brain science, refutes Locke's memory criterion with Reid's transitivity and the amnesia/John Smith cases, questions Parfit's causal-chain view via the "Journey's End" meta-crisis, then argues persons are four-dimensional "time worms" (sets of stages) before pushing to the deflationary conclusion that, like a "heap," a person may not exist as a discrete entity at all.

locke-personal-identity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
locke-personal-identity.title: Love and Doctors
locke-personal-identity.relation: Paul Dawson asks whether the Doctor dies when he regenerates by separating body, organism, and person. Using Kripke's rigid vs non-rigid designators he weighs whether 'the Doctor' names one individual or a role (the numbered Doctors, 'my replacements'), then applies Locke's memory criterion and Reid's transitivity objection, adopting Parfit's psychological-connectedness chain (via Sarah Jane's overlapping memories). He concludes the organism survives regeneration necessarily while the person survives only if psychological continuity holds, and argues the 'Journey's End' metacrisis Doctor Two is genuinely the person Rose loved through branching/fission.

locke-personal-identity.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
locke-personal-identity.title: 10. Slippin’ Identity
locke-personal-identity.relation: Šekrst uses Jimmy's many personas—Slippin' Jimmy, James McGill, Saul Goodman, Viktor St. Clair, Gene Takavic—to survey theories of personal identity. She shows psychological continuity (Locke's memory-based view) falters on sleep, comas, and Chuck's apparent dementia, and the brute-physical/bodily view falters on brain-transplant thought experiments and the Phineas Gage case ('no longer Gage'). She defends a narrativist account with a reality constraint: identity is the story one is disposed to tell about oneself, so Jimmy can disown Slippin' Jimmy and reidentify as Saul, and Gene can recall his Saul self—narrative being sufficient though perhaps not necessary for persistence, with others' stories contributing but the protagonist's being authoritative.

locke-personal-identity.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
locke-personal-identity.title: Be Slow to Judge
locke-personal-identity.relation: Southworth uses Wolverine and other X-Men to examine personal identity. Locke's memory criterion (illustrated by the Cassandra Nova/Xavier mind-swap and connected memories) implies that Wolverine's repeated amnesia makes him literally several successive persons until House of M restores all his memories. Jamie Madrox's up-to-100 duplicates function as a real-world version of Parfit's fission thought experiment, showing sameness of memory is insufficient for identity. Southworth applies Parfit's brain-based, seven-year view to Wolverine's constant healed head trauma and concludes we should be slow to judge characters as the 'same' culpable person.

locke-personal-identity.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
locke-personal-identity.title: 6. In a Mirror Is Our Image
locke-personal-identity.relation: Karavitis arranges thirteen Twilight Zone android/machine episodes on a moral spectrum from simple machines ('The Brain Center at Whipple's,' 'Steel') to indistinguishable androids ('The Lonely,' 'I Sing the Body Electric,' 'The Lateness of the Hour') to fully synthetic humans ('The Trade-Ins'). Using personhood, moral-agent/moral-patient distinctions, Aristotle's and Kant's views on animals, Singer and Regan on degrees not kinds, and Locke's memory theory of identity, he argues that if body-swapped Holts remain persons then scratch-built androids are persons too—so the destroyed androids were murdered, and evil is treating persons as disposable objects.

locke-personal-identity.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
locke-personal-identity.title: 7. Loss of Memory, Loss of Me
locke-personal-identity.relation: Lay contrasts Locke's memory theory of personal identity with Parfit's psychological-continuity view across several episodes. Locke's factive-memory account explains 'The After Hours' (Marsha the mannequin) and 'Person or Persons Unknown' (David Gurney's non-factive memories), but fails for 'The Lateness of the Hour' (android Jana has installed beliefs, not memories) and especially 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You,' where post-Transformation Marilyn keeps all her memories yet is a different person. Using a Reid-flavored chain of episodes, Lay argues Parfit gets it right: a whole overlapping network of mental states, not memory alone, individuates the self.

locke-personal-identity.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
locke-personal-identity.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
locke-personal-identity.relation: Kyle Fruh and Emily Thomas use tattoos to attack two questions of personal identity. Against Locke's dominant psychological (memory) account and for the unpopular somatic (bodily) account defended by Judith Thomson and Eric Olson, they argue the depth of people's attachment to their tattoos – individuating them or marking group membership – shows we identify with our bodies. On the 'Who am I?' question they argue tattoos have an 'anchoring effect' in narrative identity: permanent, irremovable ink (contrasted with new laser-removable ink, and with dehumanizing forced Auschwitz numbers) fixes a commitment 'come what may,' echoing Quine's phrase, so that 'when you get a tattoo, you tattoo you.'

locke-personal-identity.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
locke-personal-identity.title: The Vampire with a Soul Angel and the Quest for Identity
locke-personal-identity.relation: Amy Kind uses Joss Whedon's Angel/Angelus to test theories of personal identity and moral responsibility. Body-swap episodes support the Lockean/Parfitian psychological (memory) theory over Olson's biological theory, and shared memories make Angel psychologically continuous with, hence identical to, Angelus. But Kind invokes Parfit's distinction between continuity and connectedness (with real cases like Katherine Power and Sara Jane Olson) to argue identity is not what matters: the ensouled Angel's radical break in psychological connectedness means he should not be held morally responsible for Angelus's atrocities. She closes with Mill that it is better to be Angel burdened by a soul than Angelus unburdened.

locke-personal-identity.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
locke-personal-identity.title: 4. Total Recall & The Sixth Day
locke-personal-identity.relation: Rowlands treats Total Recall as a defence of the memory (psychological-continuity) theory of personal identity: erasing Quaid's memories and restoring Hauser's is an essential change that ends Quaid, so he fights for his existence. He works through and rejects the soul theory (dualism's problems) and body/brain theories via head-transplant and neuron-replacement thought experiments, distinguishing Aristotle's essential/accidental change and Heraclitus's river. The Sixth Day's cloning raises Parfit's fission/duplication problem: a double success cannot be a failure, driving him to abandon identity for a Heraclitean 'river of selves' bound by survival, not identity.

locke-personal-identity.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
locke-personal-identity.title: Who is Who
locke-personal-identity.relation: On regeneration and personal identity, the chapter runs Doctor Who through Leibniz's law of identity and soul-based individuation, Locke's memory criterion of personhood, and Hume's bundle theory, testing them against multi-Doctor stories, the Ganger duplicates ('The Almost People'), 'The Girl Who Waited' (closest-continuer theory) and 'City of Death.' It then shifts to physicalism (the Morbius brain) and to a pragmatist, social theory of the self (James, Dewey, Mead's 'taking the attitude of the other,' Dennett's intentional stance), reading the reintegration of identity in 'The Doctor Dances.'

locke-personal-identity.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
locke-personal-identity.title: Be Slow to Judge
locke-personal-identity.relation: Jason Southworth uses Wolverine's repeated memory erasures to test Locke's memory (and connected-memory) criterion of personal identity, arguing that on Locke's view a new 'person' inhabits Wolverine's body each time his memories are wiped, until House of M restores them all. He then deploys Jamie Madrox, whose duplicates share and re-merge memories yet act as distinct agents, as a real-comics version of Parfit's fission case, pushing Parfit's conclusion that identity requires physical (brain) continuity. Because Wolverine's healing factor constantly rebuilds his brain, the moral is to 'be slow to judge' whether a character is the same person who acted before.

locke-personal-identity.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
locke-personal-identity.title: 3. What Is Who
locke-personal-identity.relation: The chapter runs the Doctor's regenerations and the 'Timeless Child' reveal through competing theories of personal identity: Plato's soul/Forms, Locke's memory continuity, and bodily continuity, all of which the Doctor's body-swaps and forgotten lifetimes defeat (the Twelfth Doctor's 'you are a broom' speech recasts the Ship of Theseus). It endorses an existentialist answer—personal identity is chosen and constantly 'becoming,' as the Thirteenth Doctor declares 'I know exactly who I am. I'm the Doctor'—and uses Sartre against Freud to explain how the Doctor and the Whovian fandom reconcile internal and external selves in a community of acceptance. It closes arguing that only an 'objective' immortality (memories preserved in the Matrix) survives death, not a subjective self.

dewey-experience.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
dewey-experience.title: Unknown
dewey-experience.relation: Introduces Dewey's progressive alternative to passive, rote, undemocratic schooling and argues that Hogwarts reflects all three progressive ideals: hands-on learning, building on children's natural interests, and connecting schoolwork to real life.

dewey-experience.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
dewey-experience.title: Unknown
dewey-experience.relation: Details the hands-on strength: Hogwarts teaches magic apprenticeship-style, by demonstration, practice, individualized coaching, and mastery, as in Remus Lupin teaching Harry to conjure a Patronus and Harry coaching Dumbledore's Army - the learning-by-doing that Professor Binns's droning lectures and Umbridge's theory-only classes conspicuously lack.

dewey-experience.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
dewey-experience.title: Unknown
dewey-experience.relation: Applies Dewey's point that children learn best when hooked by natural interests: Hogwarts students eagerly develop their magical abilities, and when Umbridge refuses to let her Defense class practice, the students organize Dumbledore's Army themselves, showing they grasp the practical stakes of defensive magic for exams, careers, and resisting Voldemort.

dewey-experience.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
dewey-experience.title: Unknown
dewey-experience.relation: Uses Whitehead's 'inert knowledge' and Dewey's insistence that education is part of life rather than a preamble to it: most Hogwarts learning has an obvious practical payoff (Apparition, transfiguration, defense against dark wizards), which makes students eager, while Hagrid's Blast-Ended Skrewts and Trelawney's bogus crystal-ball gazing are the inert exceptions.

dewey-experience.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
dewey-experience.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
dewey-experience.relation: Responding to the Guggenheim's record-breaking 'The Art of the Motorcycle' show, Rollin argues that Dickie's institutional theory explains how motorcycles became art but not why people lined up, and offers three aesthetic lenses: Marinetti's Futurist celebration of machine speed, danger, and rebellion; Dewey's 'an experience', which every ride exemplifies, from his two-week trips with his son to the blown engine rescued by a ranch truck and the canned-spaghetti feast; and the Bauhaus doctrine that form follows function, making customized Harleys industrial sculpture that appreciates in value. He closes with Heidegger: riding's regular face-to-face with 'the possibility of the impossibility of one's being' is a call to authenticity and the final warrant for calling the motorcycle a fountain of aesthetic experience. American Indians revering Harleys as 'iron horses' illustrate the freedom and speed at the core of the bike's aesthetic pull.

dewey-experience.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
dewey-experience.title: Finding Our Way
dewey-experience.relation: Trudy Milburn applies Dewey's account of habit, impulse and inquiry to navigation in the series: Adama's 'I know the way to Earth' declaration starts an inquiry whose end-in-view is continuously reformulated as humans creatively combine scriptures, pulsars and constellations as signs. Roslin uses scripture at face value and other people's belief in it, which on Dewey's anti-foundationalist terms is legitimate map-making rather than piety. The Cylons, by contrast, treat their plan as God-given, cannot reinterpret signs for themselves (needing Baltar to locate Earth) and fall back on inherited habit, which is why, on Dewey's view, they are the ones who are lost.

dewey-experience.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
dewey-experience.title: After Forgetting
dewey-experience.relation: Sturgis argues that iPods plus the collaborative Web 2.0 will end education's age of memorization: the school 'cheaters' storing test answers in lyrics files are early adopters of a world where, as Plato's Meno already allowed, knowledge can be retrieved rather than remembered, and a remote server is no more crash-prone than a brain ('the server could crash, but so could I'). His own podcasted environmental-ethics course shows Socratic, question-driven lecturing and radio's 'theater of the mind' reaching distance learners, while MIT OpenCourseWare and Berkeley webcasts (a trucker listening to Hubert Dreyfus) globalize elite content. Following Dewey on reflection and artistry, he predicts a post-factual pedagogy of assessing sources -- he catches Wikipedia misreading an iPod '90 percent market share' claim -- collaborative creation, and candid acceptance that we are already integrated with technological devices.

dewey-experience.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
dewey-experience.title: iPublic
dewey-experience.relation: Dewey takes the iPod's beauty seriously (Chris Breen's 'beautiful and intuitive' player, Donald Norman's user-centered design) and uses John Dewey's Art as Experience to ask whether iPod use can be a 'consummatory' experience that ends with us no longer the same person — hearing a bitter song as insight into the social conditions that produced it — rather than the contrived 'now' of fashion and hyper-accumulation, per Benjamin's remark that there is 'always a sense of the same in the new'. Mass production flattened the aristocratic high-culture/folk division and handed the power to define 'cool' to advertisers and the market. The pragmatist test is political: with iTunes DRM and single-user design quietly individualizing consumption (the ritual of buying the Public Enemy tape at the mall versus the frictionless one-click download), the iPod is beautiful exactly insofar as its experiences help form a public — an inclusive, participatory democratic community.

dewey-experience.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
dewey-experience.title: Wait, Did I Hit Pause Where’d the Remote Get to . .
dewey-experience.relation: Seng takes up the fan phenomenon of syncing The Wizard of Oz with Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon and tests the three explanations fans offer: authorial intent (rejected on Pink Floyd's own repeated denials), Jungian synchronicity (rejected as needlessly complex, with the L. Frank Baum coat worn by Frank Morgan as the test case), and pure fluke. He argues the symmetries (the cash-register intro of 'Money' as Dorothy enters Technicolor, 'The Great Gig in the Sky' over the cyclone) are neither objective nor mind-created reality, but meanings made by a third factor in the experience: the viewer whose perceptual habits, in Dewey's and Louise Rosenblatt's sense, supply interpretations like reading the color-splash as prosperity or as the cost of Dorothy's lost innocence. Dorothy's own longing for home becomes the emblem of how habit, not reasoning, governs what we perceive and like.

dewey-experience.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
dewey-experience.title: Jimmy Buffett, Cultural Infidel
dewey-experience.relation: The editors argue Buffett is a philosopher despite his own denials, in the sense of Royce and Dewey: philosophy is critical reflection on living that returns to ordinary experience, and Buffett's songs, books, and concerts pass Dewey's test of rendering everyday predicaments 'more significant, more luminous, more fruitful.' They compare 'Margaritaville' to Plato's Republic — not equal in pedigree but equal in kind as occasions for philosophical practice — to defend meaning-making as a democratic practice open to Parrotheads, not just professors. Reading the album 'Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes' as a guide, they set Buffett's 'Porpoise Driven Life,' where purpose is found by sailing your own waters in the company of friends, against Rick Warren's revelation-based 'Purpose Driven Life.'

dewey-experience.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
dewey-experience.title: “Where Did All the Good Songs Go ”
dewey-experience.relation: Scott Pratt answers whether 'Margaritaville' is art by rejecting object-based theories (Kivy's score-compliance, the abstract perfect performance, the unrecorded instance that vanishes) for Dewey's Art as Experience: art is 'an experience,' complete and self-sufficient, followed by a reflective, evaluative second phase. He reads 'Makin' Music for the Money' as moving from solitary self-interested music-making to a community of musicians, and the Port of Spain steel-drum rehearsal of 'King of Somewhere Hot' that carried forward into the Miami concert as Dewey's two phases in action. Buffett's fly-fishing stories — the lost blue marlin that became 'a story,' the released Long Island bass that 'replenished his saline psyche' — supply Haeckel's ecological model in which music, like fishing, is an organism-environment interaction, making songs 'homemade' eco-music that belongs to listeners in its own ecosystem.

dewey-experience.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
dewey-experience.title: L2Design, n00b Knowledge As Design
dewey-experience.relation: Sean Duncan follows a Rogue-class forum thread — Dismalstrike's detailed redesign proposals, debated by other players and acknowledged by a rare Blizzard 'blue post' — to argue that everyday players act as informal designers co-constructing knowledge about the game. Drawing on Donald Schön's reflection-in-action, itself rooted in the pragmatism of Dewey, James, and Peirce, he rejects the idea that rational facts come first and practice second: knowing how to fix the Rogue class is built through playing, posting, iterating, and revising. Knowledge construction is design, and the stakes extend beyond gaming to how literacy, learning, and civic participation should be understood in a world where play and work blur.

dewey-experience.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
dewey-experience.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
dewey-experience.relation: Timothy Sexton traces Jeopardy!'s format to the fallout from the 1950s quiz show scandals, when Charles Van Doren's rigged run on Twenty-One destroyed the elitist model of expert knowledge and television pivoted to anti-elitist game shows like The Price Is Right. He reads that pivot as parallel to the Cold-War abandonment of Dewey's progressive education for a utilitarian, worker-training curriculum, as documented by Diane Ravitch and Olaf Hoerschelmann. Jeopardy! endures as the 'Gnostic' compromise between quiz show and game show: it keeps elitist knowledge but demands that it be displayed in the Socratic ritual of answering in the form of a question, which lets a trivia show rise above the dumbed-down Millionaire era.

dewey-experience.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
dewey-experience.title: The Wire and Philosophy
dewey-experience.relation: Vannatta reads Season Four through Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition: Marlo's ultimatum to Bodie, Lex killing Fruit for Patrice, and D'Angelo's chess lesson (the pawn as slave producing for the king) all dramatize the struggle for recognition, while Marx's inversion of Hegel explains the alienation of the dockworkers, McNulty exiled to harbor patrol, and Freamon buried in pawn-shop detail by the chain of master-slave directives from Rawls through Marimow. The heart of the chapter is education: Prezbo's dice-and-card math projects embody Dewey's synthesis of child and curriculum against the 'banking concept' Freire attacked, but 'You don't teach math. You teach the test' shows the institutional logic winning, and Parenti's grant-funded project class with Colvin illustrates Freire's warning that the oppressor's humanitarian false generosity treats the corner kids as objects of study rather than partners in dialogue, leaving even its successes unable to show the kids why corner life is problematic.

dewey-experience.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
dewey-experience.title: 8. The Virtues of Art
dewey-experience.relation: David Boersema, opening with Mister Miyagi's chores in The Karate Kid, argues Rogers used the arts for four virtues: affective meaning (King Friday is 'pigheaded' where another is 'firm'), art as both product and process (pottery lessons and Eric Hill's studio, episodes 1644-1645), art as communication and community (Robert Troll's portrait of Lady Elaine softening her; sharing children's Trolley drawings as love), and art as transformation, from Aristophanes' Lysistrata to Dewey's dictum that art is not a thing but an experience, with Rogers's tree and fish songs as gentle social activism.

dewey-experience.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
dewey-experience.title: 10. Play in the Real World
dewey-experience.relation: Elizabeth Cooke reads Rogers's double movement, demystifying reality (the studio reveal in episode 1530, the otoscope that cannot see into minds) while insisting 'anything is possible in make-believe,' as pragmatist epistemology: rejecting Plato's two worlds and Cartesian doubt, Rogers agrees with Peirce's open-ended 'musement,' Santayana's play as a 'holiday' revealing truer selves, and James's malleable world that our creativity 'adds to.' Pretend, as when Daniel wonders if he is a mistake or children take others' perspectives in competition episodes, is how children actively learn what is most real, with George Herbert Mead explaining how perspective-taking builds the self.

dewey-experience.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
dewey-experience.title: Finding Our Way
dewey-experience.relation: Milburn uses Dewey's account of habit, impulse, and inquiry to explain how the humans navigate: Adama's blocked plans (the decommissioning) are reoriented into a new 'end-in-view' (Earth), and the fleet continuously reformulates its route from scriptures, star charts, pulsars, and the Tomb of Athena constellations as interchangeable signs. The Cylons by contrast cannot revise - Boomer's peace initiative gets her model boxed, and even Cavil's admissions of error lead back to the same path - because they locate their plan in God rather than in constructed, revisable inquiry, needing Baltar even to interpret the signs to Earth. On Deweyan grounds the chapter concludes the humans are never lost while the Cylons are.

dewey-experience.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
dewey-experience.title: The Illusion of Choice
dewey-experience.relation: Kajtár argues BioShock Infinite is meta-fictional art: applying Dewey's Art as Experience, the whole journey from lighthouse to drowning is 'an experience', a unified aesthetic whole you live as Booker rather than a mere object of contemplation. The recurring lighthouse-man-city figures work as Jungian archetypes of the collective unconscious (extended to Campbell's hero's journey structuring Booker's departure, initiation, and return), and the Rapture cameo plus the ocean of lighthouses make the game a story about video game storytelling itself, where the constants are the fictional worlds players enter and the variables are sky or sea. The bird-or-cage choice that changes nothing, like Booker forgetting his 122 previous attempts, shows that rail-bounded interactivity does not disqualify the game from being art, and Levine's 'narrative legos' may one day unite story with real choice.

dewey-experience.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
dewey-experience.title: 22. Professor Stomachache Needs Neuroscience
dewey-experience.relation: Brings Antonio Damasio's Somatic Marker Hypothesis to Chidi's stomachaches: gut feelings are evolved, body-based shortcuts built from a lifetime of social interaction that prune options in real-time moral choice, so Chidi's classroom mastery paired with real-world collapse mirrors Damasio's ventromedial patients — except Chidi has the alarms and refuses to trust them, insisting ethics is pure calculation. Mark Johnson's moral imagination (his own draft-number dilemma) and Scanlon's contractualism (morality is other people) reinforce that we are not disembodied reasoners. Combining Dewey's 'morals is education' with Damasio's claim that somatic learning never stops, the chapter explains how Eleanor and friends keep growing morally even after death — bodies, social bonds and all.

dewey-experience.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
dewey-experience.title: Unknown
dewey-experience.relation: Concedes Hogwarts succeeds at its one job, teaching magic, and explains how: effective lessons like Lupin teaching Harry to conjure a Patronus and Harry training Dumbledore's Army proceed apprenticeship-style through demonstration, practice, individualized coaching, and mastery. This hands-on learning by doing, not Professor Binns's droning lectures or Umbridge's theory-only textbook assignments, is why students actually acquire magical skill.

dewey-experience.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
dewey-experience.title: Unknown
dewey-experience.relation: Applies Dewey's demand that education be part of life rather than preparation for some remote future, together with Whitehead's critique of inert, undigested knowledge: Hogwarts students see the practical payoff of Apparition, Transfiguration, and Defense Against the Dark Arts, which makes them eager learners, while Hagrid's Blast-Ended Skrewts and Trelawney's bogus crystal-ball gazing are the inert exceptions that prove the rule.

dewey-experience.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
dewey-experience.title: All Human Experience is an Impression
dewey-experience.relation: Ruetenik argues the best SNL impressions are not 'spot on': Carvey's Bush ('Not gonna do it. Wouldn't be prudent') and the Tom Brokaw pre-tapes sketch created new experiences rather than faithful copies, while Darrell Hammond's exact impressions made him a 'tribute band' without Carvey's artistry. Dewey's Art as Experience and James's selective attention, in which every perceiver is an impressionist ignoring the blooming buzzing confusion, ground the claim that all experience is creative re-presentation rather than tribute to reality. He then turns the point political: SNL casting Amy Poehler over a spot-on Black impressionist as Michael Jackson tells us something about the audience's own selective, and possibly racist, experience.

dewey-experience.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
dewey-experience.title: Philosophers Can't Jump
dewey-experience.relation: Tim Elcombe uses Dewey's pragmatist account of lived experience to read the Hoosiers scene in Butler Fieldhouse: Coach Dale's tape measure shows time and space are durable constants (the basket is ten feet in Indianapolis too), yet the awestruck Huskers will live that same space in a radically new way, and Kant and Augustine frame the gap between clock time and lived time. He argues basketball is the most 'phenomenal' game because the ticking clock creates genuine drama (Reggie Miller's 1995 buzzer three, childhood 'buzzer beater' games) and the ten-foot basket builds a vertical dimension no other sport matches, answering Scott Kretchmar's defense of event-regulated baseball. Our cultural obsession with dunking - Michael Jordan's Nike ads, Teen Wolf, Like Mike, White Men Can't Jump - expresses the human fascination with briefly defying gravity, a 'moving image of eternity'.

dewey-experience.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
dewey-experience.title: 13_LaRocca_Chapter_012.html
dewey-experience.relation: Diana Allan traces a single 1948 photograph of the Palestinian fisherman Said Otruk—the basis of her video portrait Still Life—to examine the tension between the evidentiary and the affective in documentary photographs. Drawing on Dewey's Art as Experience distinction between 'perception' that is fresh and alive and 'recognition' arrested for another purpose, plus Bazin, Barthes's punctum, Berger and Cavell, she argues that when seeing is subordinated to political/national purpose the image's resolution is reduced, and that her own misremembering of the photo mirrors Said's, revealing memory's mediated, refracted temporality.

dewey-experience.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
dewey-experience.title: Pragmatist Ethics with John Dewey, Horton, and the Lorax
dewey-experience.relation: Alexander contrasts Dewey's reflective, character-centered ethics with utilitarianism and Kantian deontology using the Lorax and Horton. The Once-ler is cast as the shortsighted 'utilitarian' maximizing Thneed happiness while the Lorax, urging us to 'stop and think' about the whole ecosystem, is really a Deweyan practicing reflective morality and deliberation as 'dramatic rehearsal.' Horton's conscientious care for the Whos illustrates Dewey's 'Who Factor' and growth of character rather than cold rule-following, showing morality as the ongoing education of desire toward inclusive, shared ends.

dewey-experience.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
dewey-experience.title: MOTHERHOOD
dewey-experience.relation: Sue Ellen Henry uses John Dewey's pragmatism, especially The Quest for Certainty and Democracy and Education, to diagnose her own 'quest for certainty' as a new mother mediating expert parenting books against her own instincts. She argues Dewey's rejection of the false dichotomy between knowledge and belief shows that a mother's home is her 'laboratory,' where experience is itself a form of knowledge; her La Leche League experience models Dewey's integrated, feedback-driven inquiry against the isolating authority of 'scientific motherhood' texts.

dewey-experience.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
dewey-experience.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
dewey-experience.relation: Ilundáin-Agurruza, Gagliardini Graça, and Jáuregui-Olaiz chart sailing's aesthetic facets — sublime, tempestuous, graceful, existential. They deploy Kant's analysis of the sublime as the balance between the imagination's failure before the ocean's immensity/power and the pleasure of meeting it through skill and reason (Ilundáin sailing in thirty-knot gusts on the point of balance between fear and joy). Dewey's notion of 'an experience' anchors sailing's transformative, self-revealing potential, terrifying storms included (Jáuregui's Snowgoose ordeal mistaking a bordello's red light for a harbor). Closing with Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, they argue freedom is 'relative' and earned: we cannot change the wind but adjust the sails, gaining restrained autonomy by cultivating skill within constraint.

dewey-experience.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
dewey-experience.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
dewey-experience.relation: Eric Swan, a school counselor and yogi, argues yoga should be part of primary and secondary curricula because it fosters self-control, attention, body awareness, self-efficacy and — via 'namaste,' which his friend's daughter Harlow glosses as 'the light in me sees the light in you' — respect and compassion for self and others. Treating yoga as experiential education that develops the 'whole child' and 'soft skills,' he maps it onto counseling practice (individual, group, building levels) and cites data on academic gains, making an essentially Deweyan case for learning through embodied experience.

being-toward-death.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
being-toward-death.title: The Approaching Battle
being-toward-death.relation: Introduces the chapter's Heideggerian frame: authenticity comes from facing mortality rather than evading it, against the Epicurean advice to be unconcerned since death is merely the end of experience and so happens to no one; death's imminence forces us to define ourselves and not live half-asleep. Harry, death-marked since infancy, lives authentically where Voldemort lives inauthentically, with Plato's dictum that true philosophers make dying their profession as ancient corroboration.

being-toward-death.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
being-toward-death.title: King’s Cross Station
being-toward-death.relation: Reads Harry's march into the Forbidden Forest as paradigmatic Heideggerian authenticity: knowing he must die to destroy the soul-fragment in him, his senses sharpen, gratitude wells up for what he never fully valued, and he accepts that he is not fetching his dead loved ones but joining them. The Godric's Hollow gravestone first strikes him as a Death Eater creed of defeating death, and Colin Creevey's return to battle at fourteen shows the same clear-eyed embrace of mortality.

being-toward-death.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
being-toward-death.title: Reap a Destiny
being-toward-death.relation: Reads the King's Cross limbo through Heidegger's counsel to choose a hero from the past and gain insight through dialogue with them: Dumbledore appears not as a king of that place but as the humble penitent, confessing his youthful hunger for glory, and the way-station evokes purgatory. The flayed child beneath the bench shows Voldemort's soul beyond repair - his fear of death drove the very choices that now give him reason to fear it - and Tolkien's remark that The Lord of the Rings is really about 'death and the desire for deathlessness' (Sauron pouring his life-force into the One Ring) frames the motif.

being-toward-death.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
being-toward-death.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Bruce Reichenbach reads the film's choreographed pas de deux as three distinct theories of atonement: the conquest dance with Satan in Gethsemane (crushing the serpent of Genesis 3:15, Satan's final scream) enacts the Christus victor view of the Church Fathers; Simon of Cyrene's reluctant co-bearing of the cross illustrates Abelard's moral-influence view, though Gibson shows resilient fortitude rather than the love Abelard's theory requires to transform Simon; and Mary's mirrored 'parallel dance' makes her a co-redemptrix sharing her son's agony. Against this he sets Heidegger — Jesus grasps his death with anticipatory resolve, thrownness, and the 'moment of vision' with Mary, but dies for the Other rather than to authenticate his own life — and faults the film for omitting Anselm's (and Swinburne's) substitutionary atonement entirely: no sin, repentance, reparation, or penance appears, unlike Maximilian Kolbe's real substitution at Auschwitz.

being-toward-death.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
being-toward-death.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Responding to the Guggenheim's record-breaking 'The Art of the Motorcycle' show, Rollin argues that Dickie's institutional theory explains how motorcycles became art but not why people lined up, and offers three aesthetic lenses: Marinetti's Futurist celebration of machine speed, danger, and rebellion; Dewey's 'an experience', which every ride exemplifies, from his two-week trips with his son to the blown engine rescued by a ranch truck and the canned-spaghetti feast; and the Bauhaus doctrine that form follows function, making customized Harleys industrial sculpture that appreciates in value. He closes with Heidegger: riding's regular face-to-face with 'the possibility of the impossibility of one's being' is a call to authenticity and the final warrant for calling the motorcycle a fountain of aesthetic experience. American Indians revering Harleys as 'iron horses' illustrate the freedom and speed at the core of the bike's aesthetic pull.

being-toward-death.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
being-toward-death.title: And Now for . . . Comedic Eliminativism
being-toward-death.relation: Argues The Meaning of Life dismantles the 'axial' picture of life as a journey toward a salvific destination (Jaspers's Axial Age thinking), instanced in the headmaster who announces Jenkins's mother's death between Empire Day announcements, the tank fish who never connect Howard's being eaten to their own fate, and the restaurant couple ordering 'philosophy for two' with no appetite for wisdom. The classical answers all fail as delivered: Socrates's philosophy as learning how to die, Heidegger's claim that facing death reveals one's own unique possibilities, and Kant's three questions (What can I know? What should I do? For what may I hope?) collapse into the question of life's meaning, but religion has gone stale and philosophy has become detached trivia. The Pythons instead accomplish the user-friendly domestication of the death of God — the hearty laughter Nietzsche and Derrida counsel — and the chapter coins 'comedic eliminativism' on the model of eliminative materialism's dissolution of Descartes's mind-body problem: replace the yearning for the meaning of life with altered reactions, laughter itself as the solution to the riddle.

being-toward-death.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
being-toward-death.title: U2 and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Benfell reads U2's apocalyptic songs through Heidegger rather than through eschatological doctrine: 'The Playboy Mansion' depicts fallenness in the 'they', a consumerist paradise with 'no time for sorrow' that lets us flee our own death, while the angel's fall in Wenders' films evoked by 'Stay' and the day-to-day constraints of 'Some Days Are Better than Others' illustrate thrownness, and 'Gone' existential guilt as an unpayable debt. A verse-by-verse reading of 'Until the End of the World' - the Judas-at-the-last-supper reading as one register - shows the speaker moving from 'passing time' and playing roles in the 'they' to anxious guiltiness and the call of conscience, reaching for the one whose resolute waiting models anticipatory resoluteness. The 'end of the world', he concludes, is the end of the speaker's own world: U2's apocalyptic imagery calls listeners to authentic, finite existence, not to prediction of last things.

being-toward-death.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
being-toward-death.title: Heil Heidegger Dracula’s Willing Executioners
being-toward-death.relation: Adam Barrows reads Stoker's Dracula through Being and Time: the staking of Lucy is the liberation of a true humanity trapped in a deathless shell, and Dracula's endless, mirror-less, selfless existence is Heideggerian inauthenticity - the 'they' that tranquilizes the dying, Renfield's seduction repeating the neighbors' comforting, the refusal of being-toward-death - so vampire-hunting becomes a philosophical task of enforcing authentic, death-claiming being. The chapter then turns the critique on Heidegger himself: his Nazi membership and fundamental ontology's contempt for the everyday leave a gap for racial purity thinking, making Van Helsing's 'butcher work' look like the ritual expulsion of the inauthentic from ontological purity, and asking whether, in adaptation after adaptation, we are Dracula's willing executioners.

being-toward-death.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
being-toward-death.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
being-toward-death.relation: Noel Carroll traces Halloween's Undead imagery to the Celtic Samhain and its Catholic absorption into All Hallows' Eve, then asks the paradox: why do we take pleasure in images of the death that, as Heidegger says, is the deep source of Angst we spend our lives denying? He examines Ernest Jones's Freudian analysis - the vampire as wish-fulfillment disguising an incestuous desire, horror as the price the super-ego exacts - and rejects it as theoretically expensive, invoking the demand for simpler, more economical explanation. His own hypothesis is the 'meta-fear of fear': adolescent viewers (and aging ones) use horror films and the holiday's zombie costumes to test and master fear itself, with parody and Bergson's laughter as companion devices of emotional control - a folk remedy that needs no unconscious to work.

being-toward-death.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
being-toward-death.title: James Bond and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Butterfield takes Bond's answer to Elektra in The World Is Not Enough - he survives by 'tak[ing] pleasure in great beauty' - and asks whether hedonism can answer the problem of suffering and death. She reads Bond through Heidegger's being-towards-death (quoting Live and Let Die's 'You start to die the moment you are born'), then diagnoses him as Kierkegaard's aesthetic 'seducer', an immature escapist who dreads boredom and flees commitment, before rehabilitating him with Nietzsche and Camus: Bond flushing the cyanide pill down the toilet in From Russia with Love and Mathis's advice in Casino Royale to make evil 'personal' show Bond creating his own values beyond good and evil, surviving the absurd through style and personal vendetta. Bond emerges as an existentialist role model for courage and creativity, though we should not copy his hedonism or lawlessness.

being-toward-death.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
being-toward-death.title: James Bond and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Getachew maps Plato's Republic archetypes onto the Bond universe: the appetite-ruled Tyrant is Goldfinger, Zorin, Stromberg and the SPECTRE megalomaniacs; the spirit-ruled Guardian is 007, compared to Alcibiades and to Medea's vengeful fury (Bond letting Trevelyan fall 'For me'); and the reason-ruled Philosopher-King is M, whose ideal republic of common children and expendable numbers mirrors MI6's recruitment of orphans and its treatment of Bond as '007', never a person. She then challenges Plato's preference for the eternal Forms and immortality, using Freud on transience and Heidegger's being-toward-death (via Tolstoy's Ivan Ilych) to argue that mortality and risk are what make life worth living. Bond's stylish risk-taking, like the cello-case downhill escape, shows we need a balance between the Guardian and the man of thought.

being-toward-death.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
being-toward-death.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
being-toward-death.relation: David Hart uses Heidegger's Being and Time to explain Batman's dedication without reducing it to trauma-determined compulsion: Alfred's butler's-world illustrates being-in-the-world and the thrown-project, and Bruce's confrontation with death, culminating in the bleeding alley scene of Miller's Batman: Year One, is Angst, the recognition of finitude that strips ordinary meanings away. Seen this way, "I shall become a bat" is an authentic, responsible choice of a whole life rather than a mechanical effect of childhood trauma. Hart concludes that Heidegger's analysis dissolves the free will versus determinism debate, since Batman neither blindly follows causes nor chooses from nowhere.

being-toward-death.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
being-toward-death.title: Reap a Destiny
being-toward-death.relation: Jonathan and Jerry Walls read Deathly Hallows philosophically: Harry's willing march into the Forbidden Forest is Heideggerian authenticity, confronting being-toward-death, while Voldemort's horcruxes and the maimed King's Cross stowaway are the inauthentic flight from mortality that ruins the soul. The afterlife scene raises the stakes of this life: by James's "sow a thought... reap a destiny," Aristotle's habituation, and Locke's memory-based identity, Voldemort's lifelong refusal of remorse fixes his character beyond repair, and Kant and Pascal supply reasons why belief in an afterlife transforms morality. Dumbledore's purgatory-like repentance, contrasted with Voldemort's fate, shows that our choices reap a destiny we must live with forever.

being-toward-death.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
being-toward-death.title: I’ll Get Up and Fly Away
being-toward-death.relation: Ian Duckles and Eric Rubenstein use the community's losses of Pigpen and Jerry Garcia to ask whether death is bad, running Epicurus's argument that being dead is no experience and hence no harm, the tedium-of-immortality argument that eternal life would eventually exhaust every fundamental desire, and Socrates's Phaedo claim that death frees the soul to philosophize — which disturbingly implies Pigpen's early 'burn out' was the better fate. Their resolution is Heidegger: authentically confronting death as the end of all possibilities strips socially imposed values (consumerist 'keeping up with the Joneses') and frees us to create our own projects, so mortality itself is something to be grateful for. On this reading the Deadhead counterculture — rejecting 1950s suburban scripts for free love, psychedelics, and life on tour — lived Heideggerian authenticity, and it is better to fade away (like Garcia) than to burn out (like Pigpen).

being-toward-death.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
being-toward-death.title: We Don’t Need No Indoctrination
being-toward-death.relation: Detmer argues the four classic albums from Dark Side to The Wall form a unified meditation on alienation, from others, work, nature, and oneself, and reads Waters's stated 'political and philosophical' aims through the existentialists. 'Breathe''s rabbit digging one hole after another illustrates Marx's alienated labor (the worker 'only feels himself freely active in his animal functions'), echoed by Russell on industrialism's life against instinct and Camus on the day the 'why' arises; 'Time''s missed starting gun dramatizes our thrown condition and Heidegger's claim that only facing mortality head-on cures the inauthenticity of living as 'they' do, while Gilmour's improvised solos model the spontaneity such authenticity requires. 'Money' is a satire of greed confirmed by 'Dogs,' whose self-rationalizing climbers end 'dragged down by the stone,' and 'Us and Them' attacks artificial divisions (soldiers manipulated by map-movers, racism's 'black and blue,' the old man who dies 'for the want of the price of tea and a slice'). 'Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2)' indicts indoctrination, being told what to think, rather than education itself, making independent critical thought the road to the Sartrean autonomy and responsibility the chapter urges.

being-toward-death.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
being-toward-death.title: Celebrating Transience
being-toward-death.relation: Kaag reads 'Atlantic City' (Nebraska) as a parable of fatalism: after the Chicken Man bombing in Philadelphia and stuck with 'debts no honest man can pay,' the narrator takes the Coast City bus and finally agrees to 'do a little favor' for a criminal. Following the American philosopher John J. McDermott's philosophy of transience, the refrain 'Everything dies, baby, that's a fact / but maybe someday everything comes back' holds Heidegger's ownmost death together with tentative pragmatic hope. Suburban 'winners' who leave before dark are dead to experience, while the transient, like Camus's indifferent Stranger in 'Nebraska' ('I guess there's just a meanness in this world'), must celebrate meaning in the fleeting qualitative moments of the journey itself.

being-toward-death.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
being-toward-death.title: Speed and Destination
being-toward-death.relation: Jean-Paul Martinon reads the episode '33', where the fleet jumps every thirty-three minutes for over 130 hours, as a study in a temporality 'of the limit': an interrupted life sandwiched between the death of the Colonies and death at Cylon hands. The survivors' existence becomes eschatological and 'bare' (following Agamben), stripped of history and future with death as the only horizon, and the FTL jump becomes a metaphor for Derrida's messianic to-come, the sliver of undecidable hope between promise and danger. Baltar's line that the universe is a serendipitous system versus Number Six's 'God is watching out for you' marks the fatality-contingency undecidability that structures Colonial time.

being-toward-death.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
being-toward-death.title: A Happy Ending
being-toward-death.relation: Bickham asks why Dorothy is so eager to leave heroic, Technicolor Oz for the gray, childless, Gulch-dominated farm, and whether, like Hamlet's delay, her rash choice can be evaluated as hers rather than her author's. Aristotle's account of the good life as the exercise of our highest capacities, requiring friends and material goods, makes Oz look like the better home for the competent twelve- or thirteen-year-old he takes Dorothy to be, against the hedonisms of Aristippus, Epicurus, and Bentham and Plato's body-denying dualism. But caring about Dorothy first needs defending from the paradox of fiction, which he works through Currie's simulation theory and Walton's make-believe emotions before dissolving the puzzle: storytelling suspends the reign of logic, so wishing Dorothy well is natural. Finally Heidegger's being-toward-death shows 'happily ever after' is impossible anywhere, and he throws the problem to the reader: write a happy ending for Dorothy in Kansas.

being-toward-death.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
being-toward-death.title: Jimmy Buffett “Singer of Inordinate Tunes” and Heideggerian Troubadour
being-toward-death.relation: Drew Dalton takes Buffett's claim that 'we don't just enjoy our escapism — we NEED it' as an admission that being itself is burdensome, overturning the Plato–Augustine–Leibniz consensus that it is good to be. Since 'Margaritaville is nowhere' — it is on no map and can never be reached — what we long for is not a better vacation but release from having to be at all, which is why even on holiday in Key West we still dream of escape. Heidegger's Being and Time supplies the framework: thrownness, being-toward-death, anxiety, and guilt reveal existence as a weight we never chose, so the escapist longing to be otherwise than ourselves is the 'inauthentic' flight Heidegger describes (without moral condemnation), and Levinas's On Escape confirms that 'it is precisely from all that is weighty in being that escaping sets forth.'

being-toward-death.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
being-toward-death.title: I Ain’t Gonna Tell You One Thing that You Really Ought to Know . . . Ooh!
being-toward-death.relation: Scott Calef reads the black 'Object' on the Presence cover—which Storm Thorgerson calls not a presence but a hole—to argue that absence permeates Zep's album art (the cut-out wheel of III, the die-cut windows of Physical Graffiti, the spindle holes of Coda) and that holes are a genuine metaphysical puzzle: immaterial yet extended, seemingly causal, and hard to see on a causal theory of perception. Descartes's immaterial soul is compared to holes (both non-physical, though holes suspiciously have size and location), Plato's Forms explain how the Object and we ourselves partake of both Being and Non-Being, and Hume's failure to find a self in introspection makes the self 'a hole'. Kierkegaard and Heidegger connect nothingness to the anxiety of death—fitting an album made after Plant's near-fatal crash—Socrates's two alternatives about death frame the end, and Wittgenstein's 'not a something but not a nothing either' caps the Object's dual nature.

being-toward-death.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
being-toward-death.title: FIVE, Dying Linking to Transcendence
being-toward-death.relation: Dario Compagnio and Patrick Coppock organize WoW's collecting through Danet and Katriel's five root metaphors: hunting and gathering (quest chains as time markers), hoarding (XP and gold farming as accumulation bordering on compulsion), mating and desire (bower-bird avatar display seeking others' recognition), nurturing (group play as therapy and shared memory), and dying — collecting as linking to transcendence. The final metaphor is developed through Heidegger's being-toward-death: the endgame, like death, gives sense to all the play that precedes it, even though the hunt is never-ending. Wittgenstein's 'seeing-as' frames the whole analysis: collectibles become experientially real because players habitually perceive them as valuable, to the point of buying them on eBay.

being-toward-death.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
being-toward-death.title: Heil Heidegger Dracula’s Willing Executioners
being-toward-death.relation: Adam Barrows reads Stoker's Dracula through Being and Time: Stoker's staking of Lucy is framed as liberating the 'true' human from the 'false' Undead, and Mina urges pity on the trapped soul, exactly the structure of Heidegger's claim that only facing one's own death alone makes life a bounded, authentic whole. Dracula emerges as the inauthentic 'they' incarnate, with no reflection in mirrors, no fixed likeness in portraits, and a seduction of tranquilizing delay that mirrors how das Man lulls the dying away from their death, so vampire hunting becomes a philosophical task of forcing authenticity on the deathless. The chapter then reverses the charge: given Heidegger's Nazism, Van Helsing's gleeful 'butcher work' and the hunters' expulsion of 'inauthentic' beings from ontological purity implicate audiences as Dracula's 'willing executioners' in a ritual with chilling fascist overtones.

being-toward-death.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
being-toward-death.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
being-toward-death.relation: Noël Carroll reconstructs Halloween's Undead iconography from the Celtic Samhain and Pope Gregory's absorption of it into All Hallows' Eve, then poses the paradox that people pay to be terrified by corpse imagery they would flee in a real morgue — odd, given Heidegger's point that the Angst of death is so deep we spend our lives denying it. He tests Ernest Jones's Freudian reading of the nightmare — the vampire revenant as a disguised, disavowed incest wish — and rejects it as a Rube-Goldberg apparatus requiring universal incestuous desire and the whole machinery of the unconscious, when sometimes a zombie is just a zombie and The Fog is simply frightening. His own hypothesis: horror films and Halloween give viewers, especially anxious adolescents, a controlled trial run of fear that eases the meta-fear of fear itself, with Bergson's 'anaesthesis of the heart' explaining why Halloween parody and laughter serve the same emotional-control function as the scares.

being-toward-death.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
being-toward-death.title: Birlstone Manor Revisited
being-toward-death.relation: Fiona Tomkinson stages a Watson-Holmes dialogue in which Holmes, reworking The Valley of Fear's Birlstone Manor investigation, defines a thing as a thing of no consequence and an object as a thing transformed into a clue: the half-burned candle proving the witnesses lied, the single dumbbell used to sink Baldwin's clothes in the moat, the wedding ring and the hammer, each read through the human fear and care that moved them. A postscript has an aged Watson in 1926 discover Heidegger's newly published Being and Time and recognize his own friend's method in it: Dasein's care and being-toward-death, the directionality of equipment, and the ready-to-hand versus present-at-hand distinction, joking that Holmes might have sued Heidegger for theft of intellectual property.

being-toward-death.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
being-toward-death.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Vannatta's introduction frames the volume with a traffic-intersection metaphor: Klosterman's campaign against the phrase 'guilty pleasure' questions whether the one-way roads of high and low culture are real at all, and the contributors deliberately violate the traffic rules (Kierkegaard meets KISS, Baudrillard meets Britney Spears). It reads Klosterman's line that 'nothing is ever in and of itself' through Kant's noumena-phenomena distinction: like Kant's knowing subject, we never reach the in-itself but only perspectives refracted through rock bands, sports teams, and TV. The introduction presents the Guns N' Roses tribute band Paradise City (identity effaced to imitate an equally constructed identity) and the rock-death road trip of Killing Yourself to Live as Klosterman's way of recovering authenticity, arguing that living with the possibility of one's own death is more authentic than fleeing it.

being-toward-death.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
being-toward-death.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Vannatta starts from Klosterman's confession that his first dates run on three and a half dates' worth of contrived material, and asks how self-knowledge is possible at all if, as Errol Morris tells Klosterman, we have no privileged access to our own minds. After a tour through Descartes's cogito, Kant's unity of apperception, Freud's unconscious, and Foucault's discourse-constructed subject, the chapter argues with Foucault's Ramist logic of similarity that Klosterman's thought really works by resemblance, mapping his exes onto members of KISS and hearing a dead friend in every Replacements song. Heidegger supplies the resolution: thrown into the crowd's world, we recover ourselves only through its inauthentic pop culture, and Klosterman's 'living is dying, little by little' and obsessive rock-death writing enact being-toward-death as the condition of authenticity.

being-toward-death.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
being-toward-death.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Andrew Terjesen asks what Death could learn from living one mortal day per century in Sandman's Death: The High Cost of Living, after a little girl's 'How would you like it?' shamed the once icy Death into the practice. Using Frank Jackson's Mary's Room and Nagel's bat to probe whether knowing what mortality is like requires first-person experience, he raises the 'Soul Man Effect' objection that Didi, like the fake black student in the 1986 film, always knows she will revert to being Death, and argues that simulation, not verbal description, is the efficient way to convey life's texture (Didi's hot-dog aftertaste). The real lesson, he concludes, is the existentialist one that each of us stands alone at death and that life's meaning lies in the unnoticed 'little moments' the dying regret missing, which only immersion in the distractions of living can teach Death, which is why the one-day-a-century program must continue.

being-toward-death.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
being-toward-death.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Uses Heidegger to read the show's very structure: the pilot's in-medias-res Winnebago crash throws us into Walt's timeline the way Dasein is thrown into time, and the flashbacks to Sandia Labs and 'nowhere to go but up' show his has-been shaping his futurity. Walt's diagnosis makes being-toward-death an overwhelming presence and exposes the failure of his calculative, goal-setting thinking, with the 'Fly' monologue about the perfect moment to die as his turn toward Heidegger's meditative thinking. By dwelling on his own death, the chapter argues, Walt inches toward an authentic being-toward-death - living each moment as if it were his last.

being-toward-death.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
being-toward-death.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Babette Babich traces the shifting 'you' of 'Hallelujah' and 'Suzanne' through Hegelian thesis-antithesis-synthesis and Empedocles's cycle of Love and Strife, reading the songs' ambiguity (David, Samson, the bound champion) as Cohen's sovereign having-it-both-ways. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity frames the human condition of being what one is not, while Nietzsche - on broken promises, on women and distance, on the Antichrist - supplies both the critique of Cohen's courtly projections onto the feminine Other and the model of singularizing solitude. 'Who by Fire' is read against the Rosh Hashanah prayer Unetanneh Tokef as a song of fate, judgment, and atonement whose closing 'who shall I say is calling?' is quasi-Augustinian and Heideggerian: death singularizes each 'who' at the moment of its claim.

being-toward-death.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
being-toward-death.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Christopher Ketcham narrates a night listening to Dear Heather during a café blackout, in which darkness becomes Eugene Minkowski's 'lived space' - more personal than light, with auditory space as its own dark space - and Cohen's voice leads him down into a shared funk of loss and depression. Through Heidegger he diagnoses his own shrunken, past-bound, thrown existence and reinterprets being-toward-death not as a downward spiral but as being toward his own remaining possibilities, and through Freud's death drive he names the 'unobtrusive death wish' he had let dwell unchallenged in him. The essay closes with a Heideggerian resolve toward resoluteness and future possibility, glimpsing a street-worn 'Suzanne' in the dark as hope rather than absence.

being-toward-death.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
being-toward-death.title: Dracula and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Mahon argues that vampiric immortality is a curse not because it brings decrepitude (against Swift's Struldbruggs model, since Dracula and his brides keep eternal youth) but because intelligent vampires know endless boredom awaits: following Bernard Williams and Shelly Kagan, boredom replaces death as the inevitable evil, giving vampires a Heideggerian 'being-toward-undeath' and 'being-toward-endless-pain'. Dracula's risky move from castle, brides, and slaves in Transylvania to London is read as the boredom escape it is, and since vampires still resist destruction, Mahon weighs the tedium curse against the alternative curse of compelled psychopathic bloodlust, concluding that staking Dracula is involuntary euthanasia - a mercy killing.

being-toward-death.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
being-toward-death.title: 22. Cocking a Snook at Death, and Getting Away with It Does the Personification of Death Make It Less Scary
being-toward-death.relation: Asking whether Pratchett's personified Death makes mortality less scary, the chapter reads Reaper Man's claim that belief created Death—the moment a living thing grasped non-existence, Death came into being—as a co-arising of dualistic concepts, and surveys psychopomps from Thanatos and Azrael to Yama and even modern assisted-dying organizations. Windle Poons's several kinds of death in Reaper Man ground the distinctions between animalistic, mindistic, and personistic death, showing that whether someone counts as dead can turn on which conception of the person is doing the counting. The closing meditation on Pratchett's own posterior cortical atrophy and the documentary Choosing to Die argues that conceptualizing death in advance—in living wills and bedside conversations with loved ones—is what lets us meet 'THERE'S JUST ME' a little less afraid.

being-toward-death.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
being-toward-death.title: 14. David Bowie’s Sadness
being-toward-death.relation: Ketcham argues Bowie's sadness is ours: via Deleuze and Guattari's Anti-Oedipus he casts consumer capitalism as a machine producing schizophrenic fad-following (the stuck high-school footballer, the Benetton self), of which Bowie's serial personas are both symptom and escape - 'always crashing in the same car' yet never repeating. Minkowski's lived time and the Buddha's anatman ground the dance as pure becoming without a dancer, while Heidegger's das Man and being-toward-death explain why authentic self-creation - which, unlike Sellers or Williams, Bowie survived - exacts the price Freud's beyond-the-pleasure-principle names as compulsive repetition, turned by Bowie into a life wish.

being-toward-death.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
being-toward-death.title: 7. A Life Along the Watchtower
being-toward-death.relation: Reads 'All Along the Watchtower' as a dialogue between the Joker's Sartrean being-and-nothingness ('none of them along the line know what any of it is worth') and the Thief's Heideggerian reply — being-toward-death, anticipatory resoluteness, care, and the fallen 'they.' It argues Hendrix lived this struggle: the mirror-smashing of 'A Room Full of Mirrors,' the unborn speaker of 'Belly Button Window' who will throw himself into the world rather than be thrown, and the 'Electric Church Music' built to cut through 'they'-thinking and return listeners to child-like authenticity. Gramsci's point that oppressor and oppressed alike internalize the oppressor's message names the hegemony Hendrix's third way — neither victim nor revolutionary — simply denies.

being-toward-death.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
being-toward-death.title: 16. Please Don’t Kill Me! (But if You Do, Could You Make a Video )
being-toward-death.relation: Reads Roanoke through Stephen Cave's Mortality Paradox, Ernest Becker's Denial of Death, and Terror Management Theory: the Blood Moon ghosts embody inevitable death, dramatic irony mirrors our denial, reality-TV fame and Twitter followers are the modern immortality project (Agnes's 'I just wanted to be on TV', the superfans killed mid-broadcast), and the Polks' ritual cannibalism is symbolic power over extinction. Montaigne's 'to study philosophy is to learn to die' and his savoring of fleeting moments close the chapter, with Shelby - who alone submits to death without fiction - as the figure who actually escapes the terror.

being-toward-death.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
being-toward-death.title: Westworld and the Power of Catharsis
being-toward-death.relation: Baldini argues Westworld revives ancient Greek tragedy in sci-fi Western form: the hosts' loops, repeated scenes with small variations, player-piano score, and kennings ('the lady with the white shoes') echo rhapsodic epic technique, while the hosts' awakening follows Aeschylus's pathei mathos - learning through suffering - since reveries are 'the misery of pain recalled' and grief is the cornerstone of consciousness (Dolores's 'spaces opening up inside of me'). Heraclitus's panta rhei frames the hosts' second awakening to time and becoming ('When are we?', the greyhound that catches the prey and is lost), with death as the final grief they must understand to be free. She reads Ford as a second Prometheus who deliberately lets his creatures grow through suffering, Dolores's finale speech as a modern Theogony of succession, and the show's whole design - steering viewer sympathy to the hosts, as Nolan and Abrams describe - as an Aristotelian catharsis purging pity and fear.

being-toward-death.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
being-toward-death.title: 10. Change of Heart
being-toward-death.relation: Auxier names Petty the master of "liminal moments" when something is finally seen for what it is (the betrayed lover's realization behind "You Got Lucky," the unknown pain of "American Girl"), then stages the 1929 Davos debate between Cassirer's humane, Goethe-reading phenomenology and Heidegger's Angst before the abyss, being-toward-death, and the "moment of vision." He indicts Heidegger's Nazism and betrayal of Husserl as what "Petty-ness," the asshole-beast crouching in everyone's darkdeepdown, becomes when it wins, contrasting Petty's public apology for the Confederate flag and his cease-and-desist to George W. Bush. The chapter ends with the unguarded Petty smile as "Here Comes My Girl" made philosophy, an instance of authentic being-with-others that Heidegger declared impossible.

being-toward-death.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
being-toward-death.title: 3. Are You for Real
being-toward-death.relation: Aron Ericson reads being 'real' in 2049 as being special: having an existence that is your own. Borrowing Stephen Mulhall's reading of the first film — life gets its meaning in relation to death, so what matters is burning brightly, like Tyrell's 'he who burns twice as brightly burns half as long' — he argues Joi becomes real by deleting her backup to live unguarded, 'like a real girl', and Deckard's 'I know what's real' names the responsibility and love for the daughter he has never met. K's arc, from Sapper's 'you've never seen a miracle' through Freysa's miracle birth to his mortal rescue of Deckard, shows realness is adopted through what one loves and dies for rather than conferred by origin.

being-toward-death.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
being-toward-death.title: 16. Death Becomes Her
