being-toward-death.relation: Hendrik Kempt reads Drag Race's pervasive death imagery - death-drops, the 'lip sync for your life,' mirror messages, the 'Death Becomes Her' runway - through the philosophy of death. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' and Stoic self-possession (Ru's 'pay them bitches no mind,' Violet Chachki enduring a tiny corset) explain why elimination, like death, gives no ground for worry once it arrives, while Socrates' 'philosophy is training for death' makes the show a workout video for dying - Socrates even dying fussing over a rooster like a drag mother to Miss Fame. Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death set up Sartre's radically free, future-oriented self - so voluntary exits like BenDeLaCreme's self-elimination and Charlie Hides's listless lip-sync betray one's own plans - and Camus's Sisyphus makes Chi Chi DeVayne and Roxxxy Andrews's doomed All Stars returns models of 'acceptance without resignation.' The closing weighs transhumanism's promise of conquered death against a DragCon-forever thought experiment, concluding with Ru's roast eulogy for Lady Bunny that love and irreverence, not immortal life, are the point.

being-toward-death.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
being-toward-death.title: 27. I Am Inevitable
being-toward-death.relation: Reads Thanos's 'I am inevitable' (his name echoing thanatos) as death personified, then asks 'whose death?' through Heidegger — 'people die' is the evasive 'one dies,' and Tony's final snap and 'I am Iron Man' figure an authentic appropriation of being-toward-death that redeems his guilt — before Blanchot's reversal and Lacan's symbolic death dissolve that authenticity into impersonal, language-borne dying (Loki's 'No resurrections this time' as the meta-textual murder of comic-book death). It ends with Deleuze's Nietzschean eternal return as the empty form of time that the time heist and quantum multiverse enact, concluding the real inevitability 'engraved in the very fabric of reality' belongs to Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter's dance, not to Thanos or Iron Man.

being-toward-death.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
being-toward-death.title: Conclusions, Capes, and Cowls
being-toward-death.relation: Jason Howard asks how Batman keeps from becoming what he fights, answering with Heidegger's authentic conscience against Rousseau's innate moral-sense view. Bruce's guilt over his parents' death is reinterpreted in a Heideggerian 'moment of vision': the bat through the window summons Dasein out of the they-self, so becoming Batman is not vengeance but the call of an authentic conscience that owns guilt, fallenness, and death. Batman's return from alcoholic retirement in The Dark Knight Returns shows conscience as 'the loyalty of existence to its own Self,' a freedom-toward-death that makes him instructive rather than merely heroic.

being-toward-death.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
being-toward-death.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
being-toward-death.relation: David Hart uses Heidegger to dissolve the question of whether Batman is determined by childhood trauma or freely chooses his mission. Heidegger's being-in-the-world and thrown-project, illustrated by Alfred the butler for whom the clock is essentially something to dust, replace the subject-object picture that grounds both free-will and determinism talk. Read this way, the bat crashing through the window in Batman: Year One is Bruce's Angst-laden confrontation with death as 'the possibility of my own impossibility,' through which he freely takes up the project of being Batman when nothing forced him to.

being-toward-death.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
being-toward-death.title: Speed and Destination
being-toward-death.relation: Martinon reads '33' as a phenomenology of temporality under exile: with sunrise, history, and open future gone, the fleet's existence becomes eschatological 'bare life' (following Agamben), sandwiched between the death of the Colonies and death at Cylon hands every thirty-three minutes. The FTL jump figures Derrida's messianic 'to-come' - an undecidable advent that may be salvation or destruction - while the Vipers' obsession with speed narrows life to the next possibility, in a Heideggerian shift from cultural to ontological questioning of death. The episode stays undecidable between Number Six's fatalism ('God is watching out for you, Gaius') and Baltar's contingency, with a birth aboard the fleet - Roslin's smile - as the one open future.

being-toward-death.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
being-toward-death.title: Death Gives Meaning to Life
being-toward-death.relation: Lee reads Strange's car crash as Heideggerian angst and the Call of conscience that ends his 'ontic' life of treating patients as reputation-building problems, forcing a choice between authenticity and a mask. Kaecilius and Dormammu embody the inauthentic flight from death (Kaecilius going 'beyond good and evil' Nietzsche-style), while the Ancient One's confession — drawing on the Dark Dimension only until Strange could replace her, then stretching one moment into a thousand to watch the snow — models accepting mortality. Dormammu's torment in Strange's time loop is compared to Camus's Sisyphus, supporting the thesis that without an ending life is endless repetition, so 'death gives meaning to life.'

being-toward-death.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
being-toward-death.title: The Approaching Battle
being-toward-death.relation: Frames death as philosophy's ultimate question and contrasts the Epicurean advice to be unconcerned since death is simply the end of us with Heidegger's authenticity: boldly facing that death may come at any moment keeps us from living half-asleep, a view Plato anticipated by teaching that true philosophers make dying their profession. Harry, confronted with death from infancy, lives authentically, while Voldemort's flight from death marks him as the inauthentic case the essay traces through the Deathly Hallows death march.

being-toward-death.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
being-toward-death.title: King’s Cross Station
being-toward-death.relation: Reads Harry's walk into the Forbidden Forest, knowing he must die so the fragment of Voldemort's soul dies with him, his senses sharpening and gratitude welling for everything he never fully valued, as Heideggerian coming to terms with mortality rather than morbid brooding. Colin Creevey, the underage wizard who sneaks back to fight and falls, is offered as a second example of authentic living that recognizes limitations and seizes opportunities regardless of belief in an afterlife.

being-toward-death.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
being-toward-death.title: Reap a Destiny
being-toward-death.relation: Interprets the King's Cross scene through Heidegger's counsel to choose an exemplar from the past and dialogue with them: Dumbledore, freshly repentant for his youthful hunger for glory, plays exactly that role in a way-station likened to purgatory, while the flayed child-like creature under the chair is Voldemort's soul beyond help. The chapter closes by linking his fear-driven quest for deathlessness to Tolkien's One Ring, in which Sauron poured his own life-force, both fantasy dark lords undone by the desire for deathlessness.

being-toward-death.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
being-toward-death.title: 20 Timeless Artifacts and Aging Humans Indiana Jones and the Philosophy of Time
being-toward-death.relation: Uses Aristotle's Rhetoric portrait of elderly men and his golden mean — the prime of life between rash youth and feeble age — to explain fan anxiety about aging Harrison Ford ('Raiders of the Lost AARP'), then turns to Heidegger's claim that human life does not happen in time but is time: mortals are finite beings whose worth decays, while the Ark, the Grail, and Belloq's buried pocket watch gain value outside 'vulgar' linear time, and only ready-to-hand 'things' that do something (a face-melting Ark, a healing Grail) matter rather than mere objects like the decapitated Brody statue. Augustine's Confessions frames the gap between clock time and lived 'inner' duration (Indy's 'all my life' hunting the Cross versus Marcus's counting of years), and Bakhtin's 'adventure time' explains the films' condensed, history-flouting chronology in which the character Indy never ages even as Ford does.

being-toward-death.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
being-toward-death.title: The Metal Militia and the Existentialist Club
being-toward-death.relation: Jeremy Wisnewski claims Metallica is an existentialist band: Kill 'Em All answers Camus' absurd by creating meaning through chosen, expressive projects ('Metal Militia', 'Motorbreath'), Ride the Lightning's catalogue of deaths ('Fight Fire with Fire' to 'Fade to Black') individualizes us in the Heideggerian confrontation with our own death, and Master of Puppets dramatizes Sartrean bad faith - the 'Sanitarium' label, the soldier as 'Disposable Hero', the addict's lost freedom. He concludes that accusing Metallica of selling out with the Black Album is itself bad faith, since authenticity has no fixed content.

being-toward-death.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
being-toward-death.title: Metallica's Existential Freedom: From We to I and Back Again
being-toward-death.relation: Rachael Sotos reads Metallica's career as an existentialist quest for authentic freedom: the Arendtian shared 'we' of the early speed-metal community (Kill 'Em All), the Heideggerian 'I' attuned to death that breaks from das Man (Ride the Lightning's 'Fade to Black'), and the Kierkegaardian leap out of the over-technical system of . . . And Justice for All - compared to Kierkegaard's critique of Hegel - into the embodied groove of the Black Album. Sartre's bad faith explains the rock-star traps, and Some Kind of Monster shows the 'we' must be tended: therapy and a democratic band restore Arendtian public freedom.

being-toward-death.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
being-toward-death.title: The Office and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Lonergan and Wisnewski read 'Grief Counseling' and 'Safety Training' as a case study in death-denial: Michael cannot parse the euphemism 'we lost Ed Truck,' Kelly must teach him to be sad, and Creed's report of the decapitation forces the Heideggerian realization that death is his own not-to-be-outstripped possibility, not just a fact of life. The office deflects with movie plots and euphemism (Jim's 'seriously hurt' about the rooftop stunt), Pam's eulogy for Toby's bird shows how mourning ritual copes with mortality, and Michael's longing to be remembered - hospital wings named after him, saving his own life - exemplifies Kierkegaard's 'world-historical' life as an ego defense, with living subjectively the recommended but unexplained alternative. Becker's thesis that all culture is a fabricated protest against death frames the whole chapter.

being-toward-death.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
being-toward-death.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
being-toward-death.relation: Weighs Marx against Heidegger on whether SAMCRO should fight its history. Teller-Morrow read as petit-bourgeois capitalism turns the Mayans' pilot-episode raid into industrial sabotage and Nero's escort business into exploitation; read through Proudhon, Kropotkin, and Emma Goldman — whose essay John Teller found quoted on a Nevada wall — the club is an anarcho-syndicalist commune with democratic chapel votes, Kropotkin's mutual aid to widows like Lyla, and Tara as its socialized healthcare. Heidegger's historicity gives the resolution: Jax cannot escape the past (the Irish deal only with Clay; 'The sting of that betrayal ain't gonna fade') but can appropriate it authentically, and Pope's forced choice of a victim in 'Laying Pipe' confronts him with being-toward-death.

being-toward-death.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
being-toward-death.title: NOTES
being-toward-death.relation: Daniel Malloy asks whether the T-101's self-destruction in the steel mill was suicide, and whether it was justified, opening with Camus's claim that suicide is philosophy's only serious problem and the ambiguous case of Socrates' hemlock. Using Heidegger, he argues the learning-mode Terminator qualifies as Da-sein whose death is being-toward-death — the end of possibility — so the T2 machine dies authentically while the T3 machine's 'We'll meet again' is inauthentic self-deception. Kant condemns the act because the Terminator uses itself merely as a means, and Kant cannot even conceive of its genuine conflict of duties (preserve its life vs. prevent Skynet), while Bentham-style utilitarianism initially endorses the sacrifice but is refuted by hindsight: Skynet rises anyway, and consequentialism gives no credit for noble motives. The chapter ends by concluding that dying for a cause is illogical, since the dead surrender all control over the meaning of their actions.

being-toward-death.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
being-toward-death.title: Notes
being-toward-death.relation: Argues 'time is a flat circle' means neither a metaphysical cosmology nor M-theory physics nor reincarnation, but is Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as a thought experiment about how to live. Tracing Rust's pessimism and his lack of the 'constitution for suicide' (echoing Schopenhauer's claim that suicide affirms the will-to-live, with starvation as its only true denial), it shows the flat circle operating as both trap and cure: obsessing over it keeps Rust on the Yellow King case until his near-death experience becomes the 'tremendous moment' of amor fati. Heidegger's view in Being and Time that anxiety before death can empower meaningful existence frames Rust's final affirmation — escaping the flat circle by faithfully acknowledging it, through sacrifice.

being-toward-death.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
being-toward-death.title: Westworld and the Power of Catharsis
being-toward-death.relation: Baldini reads Westworld as a modern Greek tragedy, tying its hypnotic repetitions, kennings ('the lady with the white shoes'), and Djawadi's minimalist score to rhapsodic epic technique. She frames the hosts' awakening through Aeschylus's pathei mathos (learning through suffering) — 'this pain is all I have left of him' and Ford's claim that suffering makes hosts most real — and reads their dawning grasp of time and death through Heraclitus's panta rhei and river fragments. Casting the season as a Hesiodic Theogony of gods overthrown by their creations, she uses Heidegger's 'desolate time of the world's night' to argue Ford is a second Prometheus staging catharsis.

being-toward-death.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
being-toward-death.title: XV - MUTANT PHENOMENOLOGY
being-toward-death.relation: Wisnewski applies phenomenology to mutant embodiment: if consciousness is 'I can' and the body is our point of view on the world, then Kitty Pryde's walls, Nightcrawler's teleportation, Angel's flight, Madrox's duplicate spaces, and Rogue's untouchability describe genuinely different worlds, not merely different powers. Apocalypse's millennia of near-immortality and the X-Verse's reversible deaths unsettle Heidegger's being-toward-death and Becker's death-denial that organizes human culture. Concluding with Nagel's bat, he argues we cannot know what it is like to be a mutant, only what our own being-in-the-world would become if our bodily limitations changed.

being-toward-death.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
being-toward-death.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
being-toward-death.relation: Hole reads The Ice Storm's prophetic opening as a meditation on 'what is impending', weaving existentialism with Zen Buddhism and Daoism. He uses the Four Noble Truths and the Zen story of the monk 'still carrying the woman' to show the families suffer through attachment to rigid self-images, and Jung's synchronicity and the Daoist dao/wu-wei to read the ice storm's formation and Mikey's chance electrocution as an interdependent flow the characters resist. Centrally he applies Heidegger's being-toward-death—death as ownmost, non-relational, not-to-be-outstripped—arguing that fleeing one's death is fleeing one's authentic being, alongside Kierkegaard's leap of faith and Nietzsche's living dangerously; he closes by applying the argument to his own mortality.

being-toward-death.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
being-toward-death.title: Existential Ethics Where the Paths of Glory Lead Jason Holt
being-toward-death.relation: Holt uses Paths of Glory to illustrate existential ethics, framing the doomed 701st Regiment as 'thrown' beings-toward-death who retain full freedom in how they meet their fate. He resolves the 'paradox of existentialism' (denying objective values while commanding authenticity) by treating authenticity as a formal, second-order virtue like integrity: Colonel Dax is sincere and consistent, General Mireau an inauthentic hypocrite acting in bad faith. Addressing weakness of will (Roget's cowardice) and the condemned Paris 'dying well' before the firing squad, Holt argues that courage—an Aristotelian character virtue—is the smuggled-in content that grounds any formalist existential ethics.

being-toward-death.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
being-toward-death.title: The Existential Frankenstein
being-toward-death.relation: McMahon gives an existential reading of Whale's Frankenstein and Shelley's novel through Heidegger's being-toward-death and Ernest Becker's denial of death. Victor Frankenstein exemplifies Becker's 'defiant Promethianism,' the offensive denial that seeks to conquer death, and the monster personifies death itself. She argues his obsession erodes his humanity, estranges him from others, and generates moral dilemmas, illustrating Heidegger's claim that only authentic acceptance of mortality restores individuality and genuine community, so that mastering death would make us monsters.

being-toward-death.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
being-toward-death.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
being-toward-death.relation: Abrams's editorial introduction argues that Kubrick's whole filmography forms a coherent cinematic existentialism in which the isolated self stands against a cold, uncaring world. It threads the individual Kubrick films through named philosophers - Camus's absurd in Fear and Desire and Dr. Strangelove, Nietzsche's flux and Overman in Full Metal Jacket and 2001, Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death in Paths of Glory, Kant's marriage-morality in Eyes Wide Shut - and notes Kubrick blends this existentialism with Stoicism (The Killing) and pragmatism. It frames each contributor's essay as reading one film through that lens.

being-toward-death.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
being-toward-death.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
being-toward-death.relation: Holt reads Paths of Glory as an illustration of existential ethics. The doomed men of the 701st are 'thrown' (Heidegger) into a suicidal attack on the Ant Hill, and the film contrasts the authentic Colonel Dax - sincere, consistent, refusing Mireau's command out of integrity - with the inauthentic, bad-faith General Mireau. Holt resolves the 'paradox of existentialism' by treating 'be authentic' as a formal meta-value, and argues that authenticity ultimately rests on the Aristotelian virtue of courage, shown when Paris 'dies well' before the firing squad despite an earlier failure of nerve.

being-toward-death.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
being-toward-death.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
being-toward-death.relation: McMahon argues Burton's death-saturated corpus functions as modern memento mori that fosters Heideggerian authenticity by arousing the uncanny and honest awareness of being-toward-death. She supplements Freud's account of the unheimliche (which she says wrongly substitutes castration anxiety for the primal fear of death) with Heidegger's link of angst, uncanniness, and finitude in 'Being and Time,' plus Terror Management Theory. Reading 'The Nightmare Before Christmas,' 'Corpse Bride,' and 'Dark Shadows,' she shows Jack, Bonejangles's Dance of Death, Emily, and vampire Barnabas use animation, comedy, and romance to make death palatable, and contrasts these films with Nozick's escapist experience machine—Burton supplements reality rather than replacing it.

being-toward-death.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
being-toward-death.title: Vernacular Metaphysics On Terrence Malick’s The Thin Red Line
being-toward-death.relation: Pippin reads Malick's The Thin Red Line as deliberately invoking then refusing Hollywood war-movie conventions (group solidarity, trackable characters, heroic assault) so the viewer is left 'lost' and forced toward a metaphysical rather than political or sentimental reckoning with death. Through unattributed poetic voice-overs—Train's Manichean questions, Witt's search for the calm 'immortality' he saw in his dying mother, Welsh's cynicism, Bell's romantic idealism—and lingering non-plot shots of nature bathed in sunlight, the film pursues a 'vernacular metaphysics': ordinary soldiers straining ordinary speech to ask what it is to live under certain death. Pippin aligns this disclosive, prediscursive truth of the image with the Hegel-to-Heidegger-Merleau-Ponty tradition of art as truth-bearer, while Witt's Emersonian 'one big soul' and his self-sacrifice ('all things shining') stage the film's unresolved question of whether nature and death can be seen as good.

being-toward-death.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
being-toward-death.title: 06_LaRocca_Chapter_005.html
being-toward-death.relation: Sobchack offers a semiotic phenomenology of how real death is represented in documentary, arguing that death itself always exceeds and confounds indexical representation—we never see death, only dying and the corpse. Using Aries on the modern taboo-ing of natural death, Barthes on the traumatic photograph, and the Zapruder assassination footage whose frame-by-frame scrutiny yields only mystification, she shows why violent, abrupt mortification of the lived body is the most effective cinematic sign of death. Drawing on Heidegger's Being-toward-death and its deferral, Beauvoir's 'no such thing as a natural death,' and Merleau-Ponty's lived body, she classifies documentary's ethical 'gazes' at death (accidental, helpless, endangered, interventional, humane, professional) as inscriptions of the filmmaker's moral stance in an embodied ethical space.

being-toward-death.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
being-toward-death.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
being-toward-death.relation: David Hart explains Batman's origin through Heidegger's Being and Time: Bruce Wayne is a 'thrown-project' whose world (like Alfred's butlering) shows up through chosen possibilities. Witnessing his parents' murder confronts Bruce with Angst and being-toward-death, and in Miller's Year One the bat crashing through the window lets him authentically choose 'I shall become a bat.' Hart argues this dissolves the free-will/determinism binary - Bruce's choice is neither causally compelled by trauma nor wholly unconditioned, but an authentic self-determination amid thrown possibilities.

being-toward-death.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
being-toward-death.title: Reap a Destiny
being-toward-death.relation: Jonathan and Jerry Walls read Harry Potter's Deathly Hallows through the question of death and afterlife. Harry's willing death-march models Heidegger's authenticity and being-toward-death, while Voldemort's terror of death makes him inauthentic. At King's Cross the maimed Voldemort-soul embodies William James's 'sow a character, reap a destiny': having refused remorse, he has become evil beyond repair, whereas the repentant Dumbledore has grown. Against Heidegger's atheism, Rowling's Christian resurrection imagery, backed by Locke on memory-identity, Kant, and Pascal, makes our character-forming choices infinitely consequential.

being-toward-death.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
being-toward-death.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
being-toward-death.relation: Allred applies Heidegger's Being and Time – the world as a meaningful context of projects, the hammer-as-tool example, and death as what makes projects meaningful – to contrast the father's world with the 'man-child' world of Seth Rogen's Judd Apatow characters (especially Knocked Up). He argues fatherhood reveals the fragility of all projects, using Plato's account of seeking immortality through children and Paul Celan's poem 'Epitaph for François' about his stillborn son to show that after a child is born the parent's world is forever haunted by the possibility of its emptiness.

being-toward-death.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
being-toward-death.title: BLUES
being-toward-death.relation: Robert and Benjamin Stolorow argue the blues is musical therapy that lets us face universally traumatizing dimensions of existence. Drawing on Robert Stolorow's Trauma and Human Existence, they hold that emotional pain becomes traumatic only when it finds no 'relational home,' and that trauma shatters the 'absolutisms of everyday life,' exposing the existential vulnerability of finite, mortal beings — an explicitly Heideggerian being-toward-death and authenticity of owning rather than evading vulnerability. Blues lyrics (Louisiana Red's 'Too Poor to Die,' Willie Dixon's 'One More Mile to Go') voice tragic-ironic mortality, while pitch-bending and major/minor ambiguity viscerally hold the pain in a shared, therapeutic conversation.

being-toward-death.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
being-toward-death.title: 9. Blade Runner
being-toward-death.relation: Using Blade Runner's replicants ('I want more life, fucker!') and Roy's dying soliloquy, Rowlands asks how death can harm the one who dies. He states the Epicurean argument (while we live death is not yet; when dead there is no one to harm) and answers via harms of deprivation, illustrated by Tyrell's imagined brain damage. Drawing on Wittgenstein (death as the limit of life) and Heidegger's being-towards-death/being-towards-a-future, he distinguishes weak (non-conceptual) from strong (conceptual) possession of a future, arguing death harms more those with more invested. Linear time and the ultimate horizon of death are what let a life have meaning at all.

being-toward-death.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
being-toward-death.title: Determinism and the Dark Knight
being-toward-death.relation: Hart uses Heidegger's Being and Time to explain Batman beyond the free-will/determinism binary. Dasein is a "thrown-project" always being-toward-death; Alfred's world of trays and clocks illustrates the interpretive horizon of a chosen life. Witnessing his parents' murder confronts Bruce Wayne with Angst and his own finitude, and — as in Miller's Year One, where a bat crashes through the window and he decides "I shall become a bat" — he authentically chooses his crime-fighting mission rather than being mechanically driven by trauma or vengeance.

being-toward-death.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
being-toward-death.title: Reap a Destiny
being-toward-death.relation: The Walls brothers read Harry Potter's confrontation with death through Heidegger's authenticity and being-toward-death: Harry's calm march to the Forbidden Forest and Colin Creevey's sacrifice exemplify accepting mortality, while Voldemort's terror of death makes him inauthentic. The King's Cross scene lets Dumbledore be Harry's Heideggerian hero from the past; via William James's "sow a thought … reap a destiny," Aristotle, Locke on memory-identity, and Kant on the afterlife, they argue our choices forge a character — and Voldemort's refusal of remorse seals his ruin.

personalism.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
personalism.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
personalism.relation: Taliaferro, writing as a personalist, worries that Gibson's relentless focus on torture eclipses the whole person of Christ: like torture victims losing peripheral vision, viewers lose sight of his teaching, healings, nonviolence, and resurrection, and the satisfaction-theology framing risks relishing redemptive suffering itself. His reconciliation thought-experiment (Patricia's betrayal of Kris and the God-man who resurrects the murdered child) argues that the resurrection, not the passion alone, completes at-one-ment, since no amount of suffering can undo past wrong. He contrasts Gandalf's laughing return in The Return of the King with a Gibson Jesus who could not plausibly laugh after rising, and invokes Scheler's St. Francis, who loves the wholeness behind sickness rather than the sickness, to urge that the film's intensity edges out a life-affirming view of persons as irreducibly valuable in themselves.

personalism.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
personalism.title: Power and Glory Tests of Virtue
personalism.relation: The chapter's thesis is that superhero ethics is not utilitarianism (whose perverse 'evil twin' governs Marvel villains) but personalism - the tradition from Borden Parker Bowne to Martin Buber, rooted in Kant's insistence that every person be treated as an end and never merely as a means, and aiming at his 'kingdom of ends'. Heroes who refuse to weigh one innocent against the many enact personalism, and it redeems even Galactus: lying defeated, he is saved by Captain America's and Reed Richards' insistence that 'We had no choice, Galactus', which wins the devourer into a moral community. The authors read the whole arc as the ancient warning against hubris retold in contemporary storytelling.

personalism.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
personalism.title: 14. A Party to Celebrate the Personal
personalism.relation: Eric Mohr reads the 'Everybody's Special' week, Prince Tuesday shedding his royal cape because 'It's what's inside you that makes you special,' the plate factory that discards irregular plates, and King Friday's sameness mask-edict undone by Lady Elaine, as Max Scheler's personalism: persons are unique, unrepeatable 'individual value-essences' whose value only love discloses, which is why Corney's birthday party matters. Against the Aristotelian view that the soul is one universal form and our bodies merely individuate us, Scheler and Rogers hold the inner self is where difference deepens.

personalism.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
personalism.title: Notes
personalism.relation: Mentyka uses minifigure puzzles — can 'Eliza' and 'Beth' be distinct characters when built from identical pieces, and is Eliza the same character after every piece is swapped out, a minifig Ship of Theseus — to introduce the philosophy of the human person. He runs through supervenience on physical parts, Locke's memory theory and its Butler–Reid controversy (Reid in the taxonomy), the Christian Resurrection-of-the-Body background, and Parfit's despairing deflation that identity matters less than what survives us. Against these he defends personalism, citing Max Scheler and Kierkegaard's call in The Single Individual to become one rather than a crowd: a person is both the sigfig and the AFOL building it, constituted by free choices and actions — which is also why the LEGO Movie's 'Where Are My Pants?' mass society is the enemy.

kant-aesthetics.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
kant-aesthetics.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Irwin defends the film's violence aesthetically: beauty (Michelangelo's Pietà) distracts from moral truth rather than serving it, and Aristotle's Poetics fits the film neither as tragedy (a flawless Christ cannot fall through hamartia, and a good man's fall from prosperity is 'repulsive', so no catharsis explains why we watch) nor as the Plato-banned spectacle that inflames the passions, since it leaves viewers numb rather than belligerent. Instead he applies Cynthia Freeland's four features of the cinematic sublime, drawn from Burke and Kant: the flogging scenes, the grotesque Satan clutching his deformed child, Judas harried by demon-children to suicide, and even the Aramaic and Latin subtitles produce the pain-pleasure conflict, overwhelming vastness, and jolt from feeling to moral reflection that make the experience sublime. The violence is thus justified as Gibson's deliberate delivery of the sublime, provided viewers leave fear at the gates.

kant-aesthetics.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
kant-aesthetics.title: Last Thoughts
kant-aesthetics.relation: Theodore Gracyk asks what makes Dylan an artist rather than a "song and dance man," testing three theories of art. Expression theory (Collingwood's standard, applied by Greil Marcus to Self Portrait and by Heylin to the two Blood on the Tracks versions) explains Dylan's rasp and "nasty" remakes but cannot separate genuine from conjured emotion in live performance. Formalism praises the verbal patterning Ricks and Gray admire but undervalues Dylan's improvisatory aesthetics of imperfection; Kant's theory of genius - free play of imagination constrained by taste, from "Slow Train"'s metaphor to "Knockin' on Heaven's Door" - is judged the most satisfying account of the career.

kant-aesthetics.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
kant-aesthetics.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Bourne argues that bikes like the Ducati 916 and Harley V-Rod are genuine works of art: Kantian disinterested attention is both possible and actual (he bought his Ducati Monster on styling alone), and Hume's standard of taste shows that judgments like calling a Honda Gold Wing elegant are answerable to criteria and informed comparison, so taste is not mere subjectivity. Against Wollheim he deploys Currie's account of the artwork as a type of action, so mass-produced instances are no obstacle, exactly as copies of Sartre's Nausea are the same novel; against Danto's aboutness requirement he claims motorcycles are about motorcycles, and should be evaluated like architecture, where function enters the aesthetic judgment. On Bauhaus principles the Ducati 916 expresses its own construction authentically while the V-Rod's styling compromises its ground clearance, which is what makes the Ducati, at least, high art.

kant-aesthetics.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
kant-aesthetics.title: To Join in with the Game
kant-aesthetics.relation: Gracyk argues Waters is wrong that Pink Floyd ended when he quit in 1985: Waters's case rests on an illicit use of the identity of indiscernibles, since if losing Waters's lyrics destroys the band's identity, then losing Barrett's or Wright's, or adding 'Lucifer Sam,' would too, which proves too much. Borrowing Locke's distinction between the same man and the same person (the oak that remains the same oak through change; the unrecognized Syd in Abbey Road's Studio Three) and Kant's contrast between free and dependent beauty to explain how intentions change aesthetic evaluation, he defends actual intentionalism over hypothetical intentionalism: Hendrix really sings 'kiss the sky,' and interviews with Waters genuinely aid interpretation of Wish You Were Here. He then argues for collective agency, that groups can have intentions through members charged to act responsibly on the group's behalf, so no single member can disband a collective: Waters had a duty to leave, Gilmour, Mason, and Wright were entitled to continue the group's longstanding intention of making and performing original music, and the Echoes compilation is therefore an accurate portrait of the real Pink Floyd.

kant-aesthetics.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
kant-aesthetics.title: Paradise Found
kant-aesthetics.relation: Brown reads The Minish Cap's Hyrule as a working utopia: its Royal Family, guards, and market traders loosely realize Plato's Republic classes from Book V onward, but with fluid social boundaries (Zelda wanders the festival unharassed), no slavery, and relaxed state control that Plato's static order lacked. The town matches Aristotle's polis design (walled, defensible, right-sized, river-powered yet self-sufficient), while the surrounding pastoral landscape embodies Kantian disinterested beauty in nature and the Schillerian idea that through beauty we arrive at freedom. Its vague, prophet-free Picori religion of benevolent Christs-in-miniature needs no Kierkegaardian leap of faith, so unlike Hitler's Germany or Stalin's Russia, Hyrule is utopia actually achieved, and explorable, through Link.

kant-aesthetics.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
kant-aesthetics.title: 2. - Radiohead, or the Philosophy of Pop
kant-aesthetics.relation: Greif asks how pop music could ever 'incarnate a particular historical situation' and answers with Radiohead's portrait of broadcast culture around 2000: an environing, objectless dread in which each person lives at a knot of shouted messages no one sent and complaining only marks you as a crank. The band's turn to electronica was not avant-garde innovation but the discovery of the sound of that second nature, with Yorke's sampled-and-broken voice alternately absorbed into the machine and reasserting the human, and the lyric 'we' sliding between a scared individual lying that he is not alone, a wished-for collectivity, and the ventriloquized tyrant (as with Brecht's Pirate Jenny). Radiohead's church-tinged sublimity observes the storm from inside it — an internalized, inhuman sublime rather than the tradition's safe vantage on crushing power. Pop, he concludes, neither mirrors us nor preaches: it lets us retain and reactivate knowledge social speech forbids, and its deepest effect is not revolution but defiance — the retention of a private voice, a politics of re-created privacy — epitomized by 'There There' warning 'just 'cause you feel it doesn't mean it's there' inside an art form devoted to making you feel.

kant-aesthetics.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
kant-aesthetics.title: Are Musical Experiences Universal
kant-aesthetics.relation: Slowik uses Radiohead's evolution — from the standard pop structures of Pablo Honey and The Bends to the layered, quasi-classical textures of Kid A and Amnesiac ('In Limbo''s independent melodic lines, the wordless climax of 'Pyramid Song') — to introduce the philosophy of music. He weighs what a musical work is, testing nominalism, idealism, and realism against 'Like Spinning Plates' and its live versions, then pits the emotion theory against formalism in explaining how songs like 'Like Spinning Plates' move us. The chapter closes on whether musical experience is universal and on Hume's 'Standard of Taste': if the test of time validates greatness, then the argument over whether OK Computer or In Rainbows is the better album might actually have an objectively right answer.

kant-aesthetics.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
kant-aesthetics.title: From Low to High Culture Where’s That Confounded Bridge
kant-aesthetics.relation: John Stone-Mediatore argues that Led Zeppelin's music, especially in concert, is a quintessential experience of the sublime. He applies Burke's catalogue of sublime qualities (loudness, darkness, rudeness, the artificial infinite) to Bonham's cavernous drum sound on 'When the Levee Breaks', Page's rough overdriven tone and 'sloppy' technique, and the dissonant mandolin intro and nocturnal imagery of 'The Battle of Evermore'; Longinus's inspired, thunderbolt-like genius explains Plant's overnight writing of the 'Stairway to Heaven' lyrics at Headley Grange. Kant's account of imagination, understanding, and reason then shows why the impossible stairway to heaven, 'our shadows taller than our soul', and 'when all are one and one is all' frustrate concepts and delight us through reason's superiority. The chapter concludes that once rock attains the sublime, the high/low culture distinction is mere aesthetic snobbery.

kant-aesthetics.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
kant-aesthetics.title: Bring It On Home to You
kant-aesthetics.relation: Jeanette Bicknell argues that the two classic models of creativity—Plato's Ion, where the rhapsode is a divinely possessed conduit, and Kant's solitary genius who issues new rules—cannot explain a four-piece rock band, since both are individualistic, purely mental, and end in mystery. Her positive account uses Clark and Chalmers's extended mind (Page describes his guitar as 'an extension of you', instruments and notation as cognitive props) and Keith Sawyer's collaborative emergence: Zeppelin's creativity happened in rehearsal and performance, as with the stairwell-recorded drum groove of 'When the Levee Breaks' that framed every later musical decision. The transformation of Joan Baez's 'Babe, I'm Gonna Leave You' into a whisper-to-cry hard-rock template shows the band creating something no member could have produced or predicted alone.

kant-aesthetics.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
kant-aesthetics.title: Authentic Rock
kant-aesthetics.relation: Theodore Gracyk asks whether Zeppelin's uncredited borrowings—Willie Dixon's 'You Need Love' into 'Whole Lotta Love', Spirit's 'Taurus' into 'Stairway to Heaven', Jake Holmes's 'I'm Confused' into 'Dazed and Confused'—undermine their status as an authentic rock band whose value supposedly rests on sincere self-expression and original songwriting. Using Hanslick's thought experiment as staged by Little Roger and the Goosebumps's 'Gilligan's Island (Stairway)' parody and Handel's recycling of his own music into the Messiah, he argues a song's expressive power comes from the interaction of words and music (guarding against the fallacies of division and composition), and that by itself music is neither angry nor spiritual. Since Zeppelin's instrumental arrangements diverge radically from their sources and the lawsuits turned on Plant's lyrics, the chapter concludes that transformation, not narrow originality, grounds their genius—so the rock-versus-pop authenticity standard must be loosened.

kant-aesthetics.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
kant-aesthetics.title: Is Led Zeppelin, after All, the Most Philosophical of Rock Bands
kant-aesthetics.relation: Surber asks why we really listen to Zeppelin when the lyrics carry no philosophy. Kant's Critique of Judgment ranked music lowest among the arts — a 'mere play of sound sensations' at the zero point of philosophy — while Nietzsche reversed him by rooting philosophy in Dionysian rhythm; Deleuze's 'surface' philosophy (height, depth, surfaces; flows, intensities, blockages, repetition-with-difference) then resolves the question. Zeppelin enacts the bodily surface flow — 'Stairway''s gradual build, the flow-blockage-new-flow segues of the 25-minute 'Dazed and Confused' on How the West Was Won, Plant dropping lyrics to use his voice as an instrument — syncing us with lived experience, which makes them the most philosophical of rock bands precisely without saying anything philosophical.

kant-aesthetics.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
kant-aesthetics.title: Top Eleven Contributor Top Ten Lists
kant-aesthetics.relation: Eleven contributor top-ten lists, several applying the book's philosophical tools in miniature: Stone-Mediatore ranks ten songs by how they exemplify Burke's, Kant's, and Longinus's theories of the sublime ('Stairway to Heaven' first), Flynn ranks ten by Nietzsche's Dionysian criterion of celebrating the natural forces that undo us ('When the Levee Breaks' first), and Dick pairs ten songs with Schopenhauer's misogynist essay 'On Women.' The remaining lists — resources, sideman appearances, cover versions, oral fixations, gigs attended — are fanzine fare without philosophical content.

kant-aesthetics.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
kant-aesthetics.title: The Loneliness of the Goalkeeper (Again)
kant-aesthetics.relation: Winters celebrates the goalkeeper's fingertip save—Gordon Banks denying Pelé's header in 1970—as football's aesthetic summit, reading the keeper as the lonely, 'stark mad' outsider of existentialist fiction, a lineage he anchors in Camus, the goalkeeper of Algiers who said all he knew of morality he learnt from football. Kant supplies both the dove of the first Critique—needing the air's resistance, just as the tango's strict steps enable the dancer's personality—and the target of critique: against Kantian disinterested contemplation, he adopts Graham's Nietzschean, Dionysiac aesthetics of participation, so spectators proprioceptively feel the keeper twisting in mid-air, as Wittgenstein's question about the galloping horse picture suggests the movement enters our muscles and joints. Understanding a save or a back-heel means seeing it under a general type ('that' free kick, 'that' volley, from Beckham at Wembley back to Garrincha), and Bloch's ruminations in Handke's The Goalie's Anxiety at the Penalty Kick show the keeper alone at the liminal limit where concession and prevention meet.

kant-aesthetics.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
kant-aesthetics.title: VHS, DVD, YouTube
kant-aesthetics.relation: Vargiu seats Kant in the Maracanã grandstand (after the Monty Python philosopher match) to test aesthetic disinterest against football: the judgment of taste is 'merely contemplative' and indifferent to the object's existence—explained through Gadamer's reading of the third Critique—so the gambler, the torcida chanting 'we won', the ultras, and the players themselves (whose attention and struggle preclude contemplation) all fail the test, and Kant stands alone except for the neutral spectator and the Panofsky-style purist. Kant's free versus accessory beauty explains why knowing the offside rule adds an intellectual liking to the aesthetic one (Denilson's inconclusive samba dribbles versus Garrincha's effective ones), and the second feature of taste, general validity—saying 'that Maradona goal is the most beautiful ever' claims everyone's agreement without objective rules—underwrites FIFA's Goal of the Century polls and connects the third Critique to public, communicative reason. Finally, the rewatched match on VHS, DVD, or YouTube, where the result is already known and no bets can be laid, is where fans most often approach genuine disinterested contemplation of the object's mere image.

kant-aesthetics.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
kant-aesthetics.title: A Better Way of Living Your Life
kant-aesthetics.relation: Akers argues the Doctor follows neither rule deontology, utilitarian calculation, nor virtue ethics, but a relational ethics of care in Noddings's and Slote's sense, expressed as Buber's I-Thou stance — insisting an enslaved Ood is 'a "he," not an "it"' and addressing Donna, Jack, and Rose each as individuals in 'Journey's End'. Linking this to Nussbaum's claim that wonder widens moral concern and to Kant's dynamic and mathematical sublime, she argues the Doctor needs human companions like Rose, Martha, and Donna as a human-scale reference point that renews his wonder — and with it his ethics — while his wiping of Donna's memory shows the care tradition's dangers of power imbalance.

kant-aesthetics.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
kant-aesthetics.title: A Beautiful Destiny
kant-aesthetics.relation: Asks whether the Dalek casing can literally be beautiful, contrasting Kant's aesthetics (free beauty as the mind's fit with reality versus merely 'dependent' beauty of Davros-designed purpose) with Hegel's claim that beauty is thought embodied in matter, peaking in the human form, and Plato's view (via Nehamas's Phaedrus reading) that beauty begins the desire to care for a thing. Alexander of Hales's beauty-within-the-order and the Fourth Doctor's 'Genesis of the Daleks' echo, then Rosenkranz's aesthetic inferno where ugliness exists only as beauty's negation, show beauty and monstrosity need not be opposites. The conclusion is deliberately open: the puzzle forces us into metaphysics about mind and reality, not mere taste.

kant-aesthetics.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
kant-aesthetics.title: Humanism Needs Its Evangelists, Too
kant-aesthetics.relation: Treats Snakes & Arrows ('Far Cry,' 'Armor and Sword,' 'Faithless') as secular humanism stung by resurgent fundamentalism, and reads Peart's revolutionary trilogy — 'Beneath, Between and Behind,' 'Bastille Day,' 'A Farewell to Kings' — as Enlightenment humanism already anxious about its own decline. The core argument is rhetorical: Rush deliberately clothes humanist content in sacred and mystical language ('Something for Nothing''s Lord's Prayer motif, 'Jacob's Ladder''s storm read through Spinoza's God-as-nature and the experience of the sublime) because humanism needs evangelists who inspire wonder rather than mere argument.

kant-aesthetics.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
kant-aesthetics.title: Genius
kant-aesthetics.relation: Auxier traces the modern habit of calling individuals 'a genius' to Kant's Critique of Judgment, quoting the definition of genius as the innate talent through which nature gives the rule to art and noting Kant's view that geniuses cannot explain their own powers. He applies the concept to the Glimmer Twins, suggesting that the songs, shows, and videos are better called works of genius than either man taken alone. His amendment to Kant is that genius sometimes operates only when two people work together, which returns the discussion to what Mick and Keith achieve jointly.

kant-aesthetics.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
kant-aesthetics.title: What’s Puzzling You Is the Nature of My Game
kant-aesthetics.relation: Goodman turns to Kant's Critique of Judgment to solve the problem of how rock'n'roll can be genuinely new yet intelligible: a work must be made according to rules that give it context — tuning-noise with a song's notes is not a song — yet a work following the rules too well, like the cover bands in Keith's 'shitty little suits', is no good. Kant's genius resolves this: nature gives the rule to art through the artist's inborn productive faculty, which is why artists say 'the thing just wrote itself' and cannot describe scientifically how their products come to be, unlike engineers or businessmen whose creativity is fully determined by an articulable plan. The section sets this machinery up to explain what could make a Stones song new.

kant-aesthetics.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
kant-aesthetics.title: The Beggars at the Banquet
kant-aesthetics.relation: Goodman presses Kant's theory against the obvious objection: the Stones were decidedly unoriginal, 'beggars at the banquet table of music history' who stole songs, singing styles, lyrics, and licks. His solution is that they altered the aesthetic object itself by making their bodies — Mick's maniacal dancing, Keith's slouch, Bill's statuesque motionlessness — a constitutive part of the music, so that 'Brown Sugar' and 'Jumpin' Jack Flash' summon the band's persons in a way 'Strawberry Fields Forever' never summons Lennon. Because the Stones know sincerity is the real enemy of rock'n'roll, Mick cannot get satisfaction while singing that he can't get no satisfaction: the work now includes the singer, a philosophical necessity rather than a psychological claim.

kant-aesthetics.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
kant-aesthetics.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Takes the show's title as a literal ethical command and asks which senses of enthusiasm should be curbed, tracing the concept's history: Plato's muse-inspired poet in the Ion and Apology, the early Christian Enthusiasts, Wesley and Shaftesbury's attempts to separate good from bad enthusiasm, and the Enlightenment ridicule of Locke and Hume, for whom enthusiasm meant fanaticism, a pretended insight into the supernatural that Larry is right to mock. Kant gets the most sustained treatment: enthusiasts of friendship, religion, or patriotism inflame a good principle beyond its proper degree, which explains Larry's failure as a friend, while 'aesthetic enthusiasm,' the sublime 'idea of good with affect' before the morally good, is valuable, and Larry's single moment of it comes when the Arizona preacher's sermon on moral goodness sends him flying back to Los Angeles to donate his kidney to Richard Lewis. The verdict: curb fanatic and inauthentic enthusiasm (Ted Danson's everything-is-heaven), keep ordinary resoluteness and aesthetic enthusiasm, and accept that a society needs a few Larrys, the Socratic fools who yell for society.

kant-aesthetics.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
kant-aesthetics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Pete Wolfendale and Tim Franklin argue that D&D founded a genuinely new art form because role-playing yields a distinctively Kantian aesthetic experience: not passive button-pushing like a kitten video, but the disinterested 'free play' of the cognitive faculties whose exercise is itself pleasurable. In a D&D session that free play just is the collaborative simulation of a world, where dice and DM rulings let consequences spiral beyond anyone's plan, as when a Polymorph Other turns a spider demon into a small purple platypus or a fumbled Bluff check lands the whole party in jail. They call this autonomous, unforefillable quality the 'depth' of a game world, and the pleasure of role-playing is feeling our own world-building power cope with a friction that mimics reality.

kant-aesthetics.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
kant-aesthetics.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: William McGinney argues Jerry Goldsmith's modernist score, with its twelve-tone themes, ostinati, cuica, slide whistle, and ram's horn, carries no inherent meaning but acquires it through learned associations: its dissonance recalls Cold War modernist concert music promoted as the high art of Western freedom, while its Stravinsky-like rhythms and 'primitive' timbres mark the apes as other and feed the film's deconstruction of the human-ape, advanced-primitive, civilized-barbaric oppositions. Because Taylor is given no heroic music, the score undercuts identification with him as an anti-hero, and its modernist associations implicate the technocratic, militarized West he represents in Earth's self-destruction. The chapter's machinery is the semiotic view of Kant, Adorno, Cage, Peirce, and Saussure: music modifies a film's images the way adjectives modify nouns.

kant-aesthetics.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
kant-aesthetics.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Edward Winters answers his sister's question - why listen to such depressing music - through Lorca's duende, the 'black sounds' of deep song that, as Nick Cave says, every true love song must contain. He argues duende resists definition yet is recognizable in Cohen, and connects it to Nietzsche's Dionysian art of participation (war dances, anthems, 'Dance Me to the End of Love') as against Kant's disinterested aesthetic distance, so music can re-enchant a disenchanted world. Via Kant's account of artistic genius and Cohen's testimony that Lorca and six flamenco chords gave him his voice, Winters concludes Cohen's dark, honest beauty has duende - which is why it lifts and tears at the heart rather than depressing.

kant-aesthetics.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
kant-aesthetics.title: 16. Divine Hatred—Dalek Beauty
kant-aesthetics.relation: Bowman uses 'Asylum of the Daleks' - where the Daleks preserve broken, insane Daleks as embodiments of 'divine hatred' - to test whether beauty is objective or subjective. Plato's Theory of Forms explains how hatred could be beautiful (the more a thing instantiates its Form, the more beautiful it is), while the Hume-Kant antinomy of beauty, Kant's disinterested judgment of taste (illustrated by Rory and Amy's invested judgments of each other versus the TARDIS's detached 'pretty'), and Nietzsche's account of beauty leading to divinity frame the Dalek hive mind's shared conceptual scheme. Since Kant says beauty is a symbol of morality, the Asylum-as-museum reveals Dalek values - which is why human-on-the-inside Clara is enshrined under maximum security, and why the Doctor is sickened to learn that he is himself an object of Dalek beauty.

kant-aesthetics.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
kant-aesthetics.title: 5. Jimi, Janis, and Jim
kant-aesthetics.relation: Traces 'genius' from the indwelling genie of an art to Goethe as the first person the public called a genius, then applies Kant's doctrine — the genius gives the rule to future art, produces what no determinate rule can govern, and cannot explain or teach what he does — to Jimi (having the Experience learn 'Sgt. Pepper' on one hearing to play it back to the Beatles three days after its release), Janis ('a victim of my own insides'), and Jim. Schopenhauer's dark side of genius — more mind than character, a will that 'affirms its own life by denying the life of others' — explains why the 27 Club burned out, and why we say 'Jimi lives' but 'Jim is still alive.'

kant-aesthetics.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
kant-aesthetics.title: 14. Hendrix from the Bottom Up
kant-aesthetics.relation: A rhythm-section-first ('bottom up') listening of Electric Ladyland and the Fillmore East Band of Gypsys shows Hendrix re-grounding his music in blues, R&B, and jazz time: Steve Winwood's organ anchoring 'Voodoo Chile,' Buddy Miles's shuffle freeing the vocal-like guitar of 'Rainy Day, Dream Away,' and the communally stretched measure before 'Power to Love.' Kant supplies the vocabulary — the 'mercenary art' of studio craft versus art, and the Transcendental Aesthetic and the sublime — for the claim that the Gypsys' collectively felt rift in time approaches a rock'n'roll sublime that is 'felt as exceptionally and undeniably bad ass.'

kant-aesthetics.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
kant-aesthetics.title: 6. But What Does It Mean
kant-aesthetics.relation: Argues that asking "what does it mean?" of Twin Peaks is the wrong question, because Lynch builds the show out of aesthetically incomplete material. Kant's "purposiveness without purpose" and the free play of understanding and imagination explain the opening credits' waterfalls, pines, and mill blades, while Russell's incomplete symbols ("the present king of France is bald") model the swaying traffic light and Harriet's "full blossom of the evening," and Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence applies to Black Lodge clues like "the man in the smiling bag" and the Arm's whoops, which support many consistent but unprovable interpretations. Susanne Langer's account of film as a dream-like virtual present, capped by Part 8's atomic-bomb sequence, grounds the claim that Lynch means viewers to complete the meaning themselves.

kant-aesthetics.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
kant-aesthetics.title: 12. It’s Not About BOB—It Never Was
kant-aesthetics.relation: Argues that Lynch elevates madness over rationality as a route to truth: Socrates' Phaedrus account of god-sent madness ("the manic art") makes Cooper a dream-oracle in the lineage of Delphi and the Romantics' furor poeticus, with his melancholia a superior state of insight rather than illness. Cooper is read as Romantic hero and tragic hero alike — his ka, modeled on Stephen King's Gunslinger, drives him even into becoming BOB's host — while Kant's sublime recasts BOB, garmonbozia, and the atomic blast not as sublime objects themselves but as triggering the power behind them, a madness that reveals the truth that mysteries are not always meant to be solved. Rousseau's ethics of truth-seeking supplies the imperative to confront the darkness (the Dweller on the Threshold), even though not all truth makes us happy.

kant-aesthetics.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
kant-aesthetics.title: Indiscernibles and Autonomous Viewers “Time to Write my Own Fucking Story”
kant-aesthetics.relation: The Forests ask whether Westworld is self-referential modernist art or 'meta-kitsch,' reading the park's dueling productions (Sizemore's clichéd narratives versus Ford's ambitions, with Cullen's corporate meddling mirroring HBO's pressure on Nolan and Joy) through Kant's relocation of aesthetic judgment to the subjective, Greenberg's avant-garde/kitsch divide, Adorno's contrast of liberating autonomous art with standardized heteronomous commodity culture, and Danto's Brillo Box problem of indiscernibles. Guests mistaking Teddy for a fellow guest and actors' 'reverse-reveries' show that host/guest indiscernibility mirrors the show's own indiscernibility from formulaic prestige TV. Their conclusion: the series counts as art rather than entertainment only for 'autonomous viewers' alert to its self-referential critique, the viewer-side counterpart of Dolores's 'when I discover who I am, I'll be free.'

kant-aesthetics.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
kant-aesthetics.title: 11. Forever the Wild One
kant-aesthetics.relation: Anders grounds Petty's artistic freedom in Kant's Critique of Judgment: genius, the innate talent for original art freed from patron control, describes Petty's refusal to let commercial success measure his work. Singer's practical ethics supplies the frame for the $8.98 fight over Hard Promises, where Petty weighed outcomes for all affected, especially teenage fans, and threatened to withhold the masters or rename the album "Eight Ninety-Eight." Marx's worker-owner analysis maps the Shelter-to-MCA contract saga, in which Petty was sold like a piece of meat, countersued, hid the master tapes nightly, and filed for bankruptcy like a worker confronting the owners who pocket the value of the records he produced.

kant-aesthetics.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
kant-aesthetics.title: 4. The Aesthetics of Being a Person
kant-aesthetics.relation: S. Evan Kreider argues that aesthetic capacity evidences personhood in replicants: Kant's beautiful and the mathematically and dynamically sublime explain both K's cowed passage through Los Angeles and his storm-soaked defeat of Luv through strength of will and moral conviction. After Plato's and Aristotle's arousal and catharsis theories of art, he turns to Croce, Collingwood, and Suzanne Langer's expression theory and the 'virtual', reading Sapper's home-grown garlic, Joi's holographic dinner and rain scene, the Mariette-proxy sex as expressive symbol, and Stelline's memory-making ('we recall with our feelings') as aesthetic-emotional communication only persons can sustain. Even K's baseline judges personhood by the aesthetics of how he responds, not what he says.

kant-aesthetics.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
kant-aesthetics.title: 7. The Sublime Sabotage of the Inner Saboteur
kant-aesthetics.relation: Ryan reads Drag Race ontologically through Kant's two forms of the sublime from the Critique of Judgment: the spinning-prop disaster challenge in 'RuPocalypse Now', where queens like Jiggly Caliente are overwhelmed and then rise ('I couldn't let my fall be the death of me'), embodies the mathematically sublime, while Violet Chachki's sixteen-inch corset cinch and oxygen tank on the 'Death Becomes Her' runway dramatizes the dynamically sublime, the recognition of a power in us greater than what threatens us. She argues the queens' testimonies — Chi Chi on growing up poor, black and queer in the Deep South, Kim Chi's fear of her mother, Katya's confessed terror of failure — show free will and authenticity overcoming the determinism of normative structures of gender, race and class. The 'inner saboteur' is overcome through sublime self-overcoming and the solidarity of werkroom heart-to-hearts, even within a capitalist reality-TV machine she checks against the Paris Is Burning appropriation critique.

kant-aesthetics.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
kant-aesthetics.title: 19. Beauty of The Elder
kant-aesthetics.relation: Courtland Lewis uses KISS's reviled concept album Music from 'The Elder' as a case study in aesthetics. He contrasts objective theories of beauty (Plato and the Golden Ratio, tested against the 4/4 stomp of 'Rock and Roll All Nite') with Hume's taste and Kant's immediacy thesis that beauty is judged without inference, adds the disinterestedness of aesthetic pleasure, and applies Noel Carroll's moderate actual intentionalism (with Jerrold Levinson on what a musical work is) to argue that fans and band co-create the album's meaning. Peter French's collective memory explains why 'The Elder sucks' hardened into fan identity after Casablanca reordered the track listing and wrecked the boy-hero story, and Schopenhauer's claim that music expresses the in-itself of the world redeems the fans who find the album beautiful.

kant-aesthetics.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
kant-aesthetics.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Wolfendale and Franklin argue D&D is a genuine art form with its own aesthetic. Tracing the medium's birth from Gygax's Chainmail to Arneson's invention of the persistent campaign setting, they use Kant's account of aesthetic experience from the Critique of Judgment, in which disinterested pleasure arises from the 'free play' of the cognitive faculties, and claim that in role-playing that free play just is the collaborative generation of a fictional world. The result is 'depth': consequences no one planned, like a sorcerer Polymorphing a spider demon into a purple platypus or a fumbled Bluff check turning a session into a prison break. This pleasurable because it exercises, under realistic friction and constraint from rules and dice, the mind's world-building power.

kant-aesthetics.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
kant-aesthetics.title: Howl at the Moon If You Want To
kant-aesthetics.relation: Michael J. O'Neill argues that infinite space is The Expanse's most constant on-screen character, conveyed through chiaroscuro cinematography that deliberately echoes the seventeenth century (the Don Quixote references, 'Dulcinea', the Rocinante's name), when humanity first confronted infinite space. He reads Pascal's terror at man as 'a middle point between all and nothing' into Avasarala's losing debate with Nancy Gao over the Ring gold rush and into Miller's agoraphobic quest for Julie, then contrasts this with Kant's mathematically and dynamically sublime: spacewalks, the Behemoth dwarfed at the Gate, the Arboghast disassembled over Venus, and Inaros' asteroid attack as the weaponization of the infinite. Against Pascal's insignificance, Kant's sublime reveals our freedom — Holden's 'crazy notion about free will' while descending to the Ring station, Drummer's 'nothing in the void is foreign to us', and Amos' 'we're still here' — so the awe the show's visuals provoke is an intuition that we are greater than all nature's power.

kant-aesthetics.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
kant-aesthetics.title: a11.xhtml
kant-aesthetics.relation: Tallon reads The Hobbit as an exercise in aesthetics: Tolkien half-accepts the Kant-era 'art for art's sake' settlement - dwarves once made 'things of beauty for pure delight', elves sing 'lovely nonsense' without shame, Gandalf blows smoke-rings and fireworks - while rejecting both Victorian moralism and Wilde's amoralism. Instead aesthetic sensitivity is a moral thermometer grounded in Augustine's ordo amoris: orcs 'make no beautiful things, but many clever ones', dragons cannot tell good work from bad nor mend a loose scale (which is how Bard's arrow finds Smaug's bare patch), and Aule creates dwarves out of love so others might enjoy the beauty of Ea while Saruman's 'mind of metal and wheels' breeds Uruk-hai for domination. Beauty also acts morally: the dwarves' song awakens Bilbo's 'love of beautiful things made by hands' and, as Scarry and Murdoch hold, that awakening of desire beyond oneself is what prepares us for justice.

kant-aesthetics.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
kant-aesthetics.title: Notes
kant-aesthetics.relation: Willard poses the paradox of creativity: how can a toy that promises creativity come with rigid instructions and a purist fan culture that polices what counts as legitimate building? She reads The LEGO Movie as staging three rival models — the Master Builders' unfettered recombination (Plato's Ion on poetic madness and Kant's mysterious free-playing genius), Emmet's 'thinking outside the box' that yields the mocked double-decker couch, and Finn's father's meticulous vision. Following Aristotle against Plato that poetic skill is a teachable craft, plus psychology of jazz-improvisation studies, flow states, and Zhuangzi's butcher Cook Ding, she argues creativity is the joyful mastery of a process, so following instructions is the etude-stage that builds the database of moves from which free creation grows.

kant-aesthetics.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
kant-aesthetics.title: Paradise Found
kant-aesthetics.relation: Paul Brown maps The Minish Cap's Hyrule onto utopian theory: Plato's Republic classes reappear as royal family (guardians), castle guards (auxiliaries), and market traders (producers), but Hyrule improves on Plato with no slavery, fluid social boundaries (Princess Zelda wandering the festival unrecognized), and Mayor Hagen's local democracy. Aristotle's polis supplies the town's design — small enough for community, walled for defense, river-powered — while Kant's disinterested appreciation of the beautiful fits Miyamoto's 'miniature garden' of pastoral idyll. The spiritual dimension completes the utopia: the benevolent Picori/Minish are a God walking unseen among people, a fuzzy religion without prophet or persecution, so no leap of faith is even necessary.

kant-aesthetics.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
kant-aesthetics.title: Indiscernibles and Autonomous Viewers “Time to Write my Own Fucking Story”
kant-aesthetics.relation: Forest and Beckley-Forest ask whether Westworld is self-referential 'high art' or 'meta-kitsch,' tracing aesthetic modernism from Kant's subjective turn through Greenberg's avant-garde/kitsch split and Adorno's autonomous versus heteronomous art. They read Sizemore's clichéd Western narratives and the park's stock characters as commodified kitsch that mirrors the show's own corporate constraints under HBO, and use Danto's Brillo Box problem of indiscernibles to argue that host/guest and entertainment/art distinctions lie in the viewer's reflection. Dolores's line 'when I discover who I am, I'll be free' models the Adorno-style liberation available to an alert viewer.

kant-aesthetics.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
kant-aesthetics.title: The Beauty of the Game
kant-aesthetics.relation: The Brands stage a broadcast-booth debate about whether a championship game was 'beautiful,' with Dickie V defending Hume's subjectivism ('beauty is in the eye of the beholder' and the expert's delicacy of taste) and Billy defending Plato's objective Form of Beauty. Jim exposes each side's flaw (Hume's circular appeal to experts, Plato's third-man regress from the Parmenides/Aristotle) and proposes a synthesis: games have 'outer beauty' (universally observable fluid motion, like improvised jazz or dance) and 'inner beauty' (the strategy and reason the knowledgeable fan grasps), reconciling the objective and subjective.

kant-aesthetics.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
kant-aesthetics.title: The Beauty of Football
kant-aesthetics.relation: Parker asks what pleases football fans and argues the answer is beauty, framed around a Michael Vick scramble against the Ravens. He applies Kant's Critique of Judgment—beauty as disinterested, an end in itself, and its judgments nonconceptual yet universal ('you should too')—to explain why fans watch games rather than read box scores, and why skilled offensive play by Barry Sanders or Joe Montana strikes us as beautiful. Using Ted Cohen's 'circles of taste' and an informal survey, he concludes beauty admits of degree and depends on the viewer's grasp of context.

kant-aesthetics.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
kant-aesthetics.title: Second Hole On the Beauty and Sublimity of Golf
kant-aesthetics.relation: Fudge and Ulatowski argue that golf's aesthetic appeal has two sources: the course as a designed landscape best appreciated (via Walton's 'Categories of Art') under the category of gardens, and the sublimity of players' character. They apply Kant's 'Observations on the Feeling of the Beautiful and Sublime' to distinguish beautiful courses (Augusta) from sublime ones (Pebble Beach, St. Andrews) and to explain Bobby Jones's self-imposed penalty at the 1925 U.S. Open as the noble sublime, since 'subduing one's passions through principles is sublime.' They link the consistent rule-following golf demands to Kant's categorical imperative and read human dignity as 'beyond price' against Hobbes's price-based account, while Schopenhauer's critique of the French garden frames the environmental objection to courses.

kant-aesthetics.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
kant-aesthetics.title: Fifteenth Hole The “Ideal” Swing, the “Ideal” Body Myths of Optimization
kant-aesthetics.relation: Jason and Laurence Holt attack two 'optimization' myths in golf culture via a philosophy of kinesiology: the averaging model (that the ideal swing is the statistical mean of elite swings) and the athlete model (that more general fitness makes a better golfer). Against the first they invoke multiple realizability from philosophy of mind—there is no single perfect swing, since Bobby Jones's over-parallel backswing, Hagen's short fast swing, and the quirky swings of Trevino and Furyk all succeed on different bodies. Against the second they note golf's modest physical demands and argue Tiger Woods's heavy conditioning caused injury without improving results. They diagnose the false ideal as an aesthetic bias favoring 'beautiful' swings and athletic-looking bodies, using Suits's definition of games to defend golf as a genuine sport of gross physical skill.

kant-aesthetics.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.relation: Sharpe analyzes the Olympics as an aestheticized 'spectacle' (Debord, after Marx's commodity analysis) whose real product is the shareable 'Olympic moment.' Reading Kant's Critique of Judgment through Terry Eagleton, he argues the games trade on the sensus communis Kant finds in the judgment 'this is beautiful', an intimated universal harmony among humans that mirrors the ancient Olympic ekecheiria (truce). He links Beijing 2008's simulated fireworks and lip-synced girl to Baudrillard's simulacra, and uses Benjamin's 'Work of Art' essay, Riefenstahl's Olympia and Hegel's account of Greek sculpture to show how the Nazis' 1936 Games weaponized this aesthetic power, warning the spectacle serves both good and evil.

kant-aesthetics.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
kant-aesthetics.title: Federer as Religious Experience
kant-aesthetics.relation: David Foster Wallace argues that watching Roger Federer live at Wimbledon delivers a near-religious experience because top sport is a prime venue for 'kinetic beauty'—a beauty rooted in human beings' reconciliation with the fact of having a body. He reads the 2006 Federer-Nadal final as a clash of the Apollonian (Federer's clinical northern artistry) against the Dionysian (Nadal's martial southern machismo), and dwells on specific Federer Moments (the reverse-thrust forehand winner against Agassi at the 2005 US Open) as instances where an athlete seems exempt from physical law. He treats Federer's grace as ineffable, defining it by what it is not, and juxtaposes the transcendent beauty of the body against the suffering body of cancer-survivor coin-tosser William Caines.

kant-aesthetics.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
kant-aesthetics.title: Why Are All Tennis Films Bad
kant-aesthetics.relation: Mark Huston argues no truly great tennis film—a 'Raging Bull of tennis'—will ever be made, and builds his case through genre theory. He contrasts an Aristotelian essentialist approach to defining a genre (necessary and sufficient conditions, as in Noel Carroll's Poetics-derived definition of horror) with a Wittgensteinian 'family resemblance' account, adopting the latter to identify overlapping-but-nonessential core features of the sports film (representing a real sport, literal not merely metaphorical emphasis, a culminating sporting moment, an athlete protagonist). Reading Nobody's Perfect, Wimbledon, and Tennis, Anyone...?, and citing David Foster Wallace on how tennis's speed is essentially untelevisable, he concludes tennis's un-representability on screen plus the genre's uplift bar it from the aesthetic seriousness that wins critical greatness.

kant-aesthetics.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
kant-aesthetics.title: A Court Conversation
