kant-aesthetics.relation: Cast as a dialogue with an updated Kant at a tournament, the chapter applies Kant's aesthetics to spectating tennis: it distinguishes free from dependent beauty (a McEnroe drop volley or a Federer stroke judged against the game's history and rules), locates the sublime in a booming ace, a broken record, and the fan's disinterested enthusiasm, and defends aesthetic judgments as disinterested yet subjectively universal. It then turns Kant's ethics onto the court, arguing that calling a line honestly against your own interest has moral worth only when done autonomously, for its own sake, and that gamesmanship like faked injury timeouts seeks an unfair advantage and so is wrong even when within the rules.

kant-aesthetics.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
kant-aesthetics.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
kant-aesthetics.relation: Kohler-Ryan and Palmer treat 'sense' and 'sensibility' as a spectrum Lee explores through sisterhood in Sense and Sensibility (Elinor/Marianne) and Crouching Tiger (Shu Lien/Jen). Elinor and Shu Lien embody sense, Shu Lien specifically the Confucian balance of li and ren that lets her soften ritual with humanity; Marianne embodies Burke's British-Romantic sublime while Jen embodies Daoist immersion in the dao. Reading door-frames, windows, hair-combing rituals and Shu Lien's hairpin as symbols, they argue only Sense and Sensibility achieves integration in time, whereas Li Mu Bai's confession that he lived sense and sensibility as separate spheres comes too late.

kant-aesthetics.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
kant-aesthetics.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
kant-aesthetics.relation: Jameson and Brace read Sense and Sensibility and Brokeback Mountain through Burke's and Gilpin's aesthetics of the sublime, the beautiful and the picturesque, mapped onto the Chinese yin/yang and qi of landscape. In Sense and Sensibility, manicured French/Brownian gardens (beautiful, sanctioned) versus wild picturesque nature (sublime, passionate) mirror Elinor's controlled sense and Marianne's storm-caught sensibility, with Willoughby's rescue and Brandon's steadiness keyed to landscape. In Brokeback Mountain the masculine sublime wilderness (yang) versus feminine confining civilization (yin) is built through tightly framed interiors, sweeping exteriors and an 'aesthetics of isolation' that exposes American freedom as a costly illusion for Ennis and Jack.

kant-aesthetics.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
kant-aesthetics.title: “A Homespun Murder Story” Film Noir and the Problem of Modernity in Fargo
kant-aesthetics.relation: Abrams reads Fargo as a noir study of modernity via MacIntyre's After Virtue: humans are 'story-telling animals,' and the Enlightenment project (Descartes, Sartre) shredded the shared myth, leaving Cartesian monadic selves who float in a void as 'unscripted, anxious stutterers.' The whiteout blizzard becomes an ontological tabula rasa of Heraclitean flux where every conversation collapses (Jerry, Carl, Mike Yanagita, even Marge at the drive-thru). Abrams reads Marge as morally good but intellectually shallow—wrong to call the sublime, Kantian 'dynamically sublime' day 'beautiful'—and Grimsrud as the one who dimly 'sees' the modern abyss, so the film hands the deeper mystery of modernity's crime to the viewer.

kant-aesthetics.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
kant-aesthetics.title: 6. But What Does It Mean
kant-aesthetics.relation: Kreider argues Twin Peaks is less about determinate meaning than about handing viewers incomplete, underdetermined content to complete themselves. He reads the opening sequence's waterfalls and trees through Kant's aesthetic 'purposiveness without purpose,' the swaying traffic light and 'the full blossom of the evening' as Russell's incomplete symbols, and the range of legitimate interpretations through Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence; Susanne Langer's Feeling and Form adds that film creates a dreamlike virtual present, so the Part 8 atomic-bomb sequence works exactly as a dream we must interpret.

kant-aesthetics.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
kant-aesthetics.title: 12. It’s Not About BOB—It Never Was
kant-aesthetics.relation: Huntingford argues Lynch reveres madness as the true source of insight, casting Cooper as the Romantic 'mad poet' and Socratic divinely-inspired Oracle (Phaedrus) whose dream-forays reveal Twin Peaks' buried truths while 'normal' is the real evil. She frames BOB—born from the atomic blast—and garmonbozia through Kant's Sublime as the fearful, irregular power behind nature that exceeds reason, and reads Cooper's tragic ka (via Stephen King's Dark Tower) and shadow-self confrontation, plus Rousseau's ethics of truth-seeking, as the show's message: some mysteries are not meant to be solved, and to embrace that madness is freedom.

kant-aesthetics.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
kant-aesthetics.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
kant-aesthetics.relation: Richard Gilmore reads After Hours as a nocturnal katabasis in which office worker Paul Hackett is repeatedly offered, and repeatedly fails at, authentic encounter with the SoHo women and their artworks (Kiki's papier-mache man, the plaster-of-paris bagel). Using Levinas's totality-versus-infinity and the ethics of conversation, Kant's two worlds of interest and disinterested aesthetic judgment, and Dewey's Art as Experience, Gilmore argues that art and sex alike (per Picasso and Nagel's 'double reciprocal incarnation') demand abandoning one's 'logic of the same' to perceive the other. Foucault's disciplinary kronos-time versus kairos, and Zizek's anamorphic spot, frame Paul's entrapment in solipsism until, encased as a literal artwork and reborn at the office gates, he finally offers himself to June.

kant-aesthetics.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
kant-aesthetics.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
kant-aesthetics.relation: Ritzer argues Mann's aesthetics of horror in The Keep and Manhunter is an aestheticization of horror—the frightening transformed into the beautiful through mise-en-scène, color, and montage. Against Hegel's Lectures on Fine Art, which bans the purely negative and horrific from aesthetics, Ritzer marshals Schiller, De Quincey, and Auden to split the ethical from the aesthetic: Dollarhyde stages corpses as artworks and Graham reads crime scenes as an art critic. The Keep pushes further into Barthes's 'obtuse meaning' and Deleuze and Guattari's 'planes of immanence,' its stylized images referring to nothing but themselves—horror filmed solely for horror's sake.

kant-aesthetics.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
kant-aesthetics.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
kant-aesthetics.relation: Gilmore reads Chinatown as neo-noir that is itself a kind of philosophy, engaging the hermeneutics of suspicion (Nietzsche, Freud, Marx) and existentialist alienation. Curly eating the venetian blinds signals a desire to recover a less painful blindness; Jake Gittes's 'conceptual scotomas' (Dennett) and hubris make him miss counternarratives, paralleling Oedipus as detective. Using Freud on the uncanny and doppelgangers (Jake doubled with Hollis Mulwray and Noah Cross) and Aristotle's Poetics on catharsis and the sublime, Gilmore argues 'Chinatown' names the abyss where every narrative is undone, and that facing this dark sublimity is the way of wisdom.

kant-aesthetics.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
kant-aesthetics.title: Transcendence and Sublimity in Spike Lee’s Signature Shot
kant-aesthetics.relation: Abrams analyzes Lee's 'signature shot'—a character silently gliding forward toward the viewer—as a phenomenological device that ejects the immersed viewer back into self-aware spectatorship, drawing on Heidegger's account of anticipation and being futural in Being and Time and Danto's claim that a self-conscious camera makes the film about being viewed. He tracks the shot in Malcolm X (levitating before his assassination), 25th Hour (Mary floating on Ecstasy), and Inside Man (Frazier's superhuman, robotic rush after the staged execution). He then argues the shot is aesthetically sublime in Longinus's and Kant's sense: it renders characters superhuman and elevated off the ground, an objective image of subjective transcendence that signs Lee as both filmmaker and philosopher.

kant-aesthetics.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
kant-aesthetics.title: “Profoundly Unreconciled to Nature” Ecstatic Truth and the Humanistic Sublime in Werner Herzog’s War Films
kant-aesthetics.relation: LaRocca argues against Thomas Weiskel that the 'humanistic sublime' is not an oxymoron, using Herzog's war films (Lessons of Darkness, Little Dieter Needs to Fly, Rescue Dawn) to show a sublime that returns us to the human at the limit of existence rather than transcending it. Building on Kant's link between the sublime and human dignity—and Kant's claim that sublimity lies in our ideas, not in nature—he reads Herzog's 'ecstatic truth' (fabrication that exceeds the 'accountant's truth') as the vehicle: staged monologues, borrowed music, and recontextualized documentary footage disclose an inner reality. Herzog's Heideggerian gloss on aletheia as un-concealment aligns cinema itself with truth, and Dengler's bear ('the only friend I had was death') exemplifies war as the space of radical mortality where the humanistic sublime dawns for the safe spectator, contrasted with Malick's more Darwinian, nature-indifferent vision.

kant-aesthetics.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
kant-aesthetics.title: Herzog’s Sublime and Ecstatic Truth
kant-aesthetics.relation: Patricia Castello Branco argues that Herzog's sublime is Burkean and physiological rather than Kantian and transcendental: in Aguirre, Fitzcarraldo, and Grizzly Man the protagonists' encounter with overwhelming nature defeats reason and works through the body (Kinski's distorted performance, Treadwell's death) rather than confirming reason's supremacy as in Kant's Critique of Judgment. She maps Herzog's 'ecstatic truth' onto Nietzsche's Dionysian from The Birth of Tragedy, where the principium individuationis dissolves and the hero merges with nature's creating-and-destroying flux, and glosses ecstatic truth via Heidegger's aletheia as unconcealment reached through fabrication and stylization.

kant-aesthetics.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
kant-aesthetics.title: The Great Ecstasy of Werner Herzog Truth, Heidegger, Apocalypse
kant-aesthetics.relation: Ian Alexander Moore reads Herzog's 'ecstatic truth' through Heidegger's account of truth as aletheia (unconcealment) and 'The Origin of the Work of Art,' arguing that Herzog's fabricated Pascal epigraph and Wagner Prelude in Lessons of Darkness and Lo and Behold elevate viewers into a sublime, ecstatic state that discloses a truth beyond the 'accountant's' factual. He connects the slow-motion ski-jumps of The Great Ecstasy of Woodcarver Steiner to Heidegger's ecstatic standing-outside-oneself, and treats Lessons of Darkness's burning Kuwaiti oil fields as an apocalyptic un-covering. He also warns that planetary information technology (echoing Heidegger's Question Concerning Technology) threatens the very oblivion of ecstatic truth.

kant-aesthetics.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.title: A Beautiful Destiny
kant-aesthetics.relation: Clive Cazeaux asks whether the Daleks can be beautiful, canvassing theories of beauty to resolve the puzzle of a monster being beautiful. He distinguishes Kant's higher natural beauty (and his suspicion of 'dependent,' purpose-designed beauty like the Dalek casing) from Hegel's view that beauty in art, perceiving thought in matter, is higher, and finds Plato most helpful: to call the Daleks beautiful is Platonic love, being drawn to engage with them as a wholly-other form of life whose design succeeds. He surveys Alexander of Hales, Rosenkranz's aesthetic inferno, and formalism (the Krutikov design parallel) without a final verdict, showing the dispute turns on metaphysics.

kant-aesthetics.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
kant-aesthetics.title: 3. The Nasty Bits
kant-aesthetics.relation: Calef asks how Bourdain could find disgusting foods (cobra heart, blood soup, warthog anus) delicious, using Korsmeyer's taxonomy of disgust and the 'paradox of aversion.' He argues their appeal comes from Aristotelian learning-through-representation, Burke's and Bullough's sublime experienced at psychical distance, and Kristeva's 'abject' — foods that remind us of death and mortality let Bourdain transcend and disarm it by eating them appreciatively.

kant-aesthetics.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
kant-aesthetics.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
kant-aesthetics.relation: Ilundáin-Agurruza, Gagliardini Graça, and Jáuregui-Olaiz chart sailing's aesthetic facets — sublime, tempestuous, graceful, existential. They deploy Kant's analysis of the sublime as the balance between the imagination's failure before the ocean's immensity/power and the pleasure of meeting it through skill and reason (Ilundáin sailing in thirty-knot gusts on the point of balance between fear and joy). Dewey's notion of 'an experience' anchors sailing's transformative, self-revealing potential, terrifying storms included (Jáuregui's Snowgoose ordeal mistaking a bordello's red light for a harbor). Closing with Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, they argue freedom is 'relative' and earned: we cannot change the wind but adjust the sails, gaining restrained autonomy by cultivating skill within constraint.

kant-aesthetics.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
kant-aesthetics.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
kant-aesthetics.relation: Wear traces the espresso aesthetic from the idealized, egalitarian Italian caffè—which he reads as an 'aestheticized Marxist' image of identical shots for businessman and street sweeper—to its dilution under neoliberal consumer choice, epitomized by the endless-customization L.A. Story 'half-caf twist of lemon' scene. He invokes Kant's Critique of Judgement and the sublime to argue that flavor and taste-judgment are neglected aesthetic faculties, and enlists the Frankfurt School (Adorno, Benjamin, Marcuse) and Bourdieu's cultural capital to explain how the market absorbs the espresso's beauty. He concludes that a single humble shot, as a memorial to the vast exploited labor chain behind it, is a truer aesthetic object than a branded frappuccino.

kant-aesthetics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
kant-aesthetics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
kant-aesthetics.relation: Clark analyzes Disney's Bambi as anti-hunting art, showing how the animators used music and the Kantian sublime — keeping Man and Death offscreen, 'felt rather than seen' — to make viewers feel hunting is cosmic murder, while the cute cartoon animals stay merely 'seen.' He then critiques Matt Cartmill, who dissolves hunting by using science and utilitarianism to erase the Man/Nature split (making hunting indistinguishable from murder), faulting Cartmill for flattening life and rejecting the sublime. He resolves the tension via Richard Nelson's The Island Within and Koyukon hunting, which honors continuity and the sublime without a Man/Nature dichotomy.

kant-aesthetics.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
kant-aesthetics.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
kant-aesthetics.relation: La Caze rehabilitates fashion against Kant's own dismissal of it (in the *Anthropology*) as vanity and imitation, arguing that Kant's aesthetics actually supply the tools to value it. She applies his account of the disinterested judgment of taste, free vs. adherent beauty, and 'genius' (originality that provides an exemplary model — Chanel's freer dressing, Dior's New Look, punk DIY, the Sartorialist's street style) to both the making and the wearing of clothes. Drawing on Kant's claim that the beautiful is a symbol of the morally good and the 'virtues of social intercourse,' and on Iris Marion Young's pleasures of touch, bonding, and fantasy, she argues fashion can be a proto-moral, cosmopolitan force, countering Plato's, Beauvoir's, and Svendsen's denigration.

kant-aesthetics.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
kant-aesthetics.title: GARDENING
kant-aesthetics.relation: Barwell and Powell challenge Kant's classification of landscape gardening as a subcategory of painting ('for the eye only') by arguing that gardens, unlike static paintings or sculpture, essentially present the passing of time visually. Because gardens are made of living organisms that grow, flower, senesce and decay at different rates—an oak, a drift of crocuses, a managed lawn—they generate visual rhythms analogous to musical rhythm, with diurnal and seasonal cycles supplying a 'rhythmus firmus' (pulse and meter) that nature, not the designer, provides. Using Susanne Langer's claim that 'music makes the passage of time audible,' they conclude gardens make time visible and so deserve status as a distinctive art form.

kant-aesthetics.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
kant-aesthetics.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
kant-aesthetics.relation: Jacquette argues that cannabis opens a 'creative inner space' of loosened associations but is skeptical it yields genuine, lasting insight, using Ginsberg's claim to have newly 'apprehended the structure' of jazz and classical music and the conjecture that Shakespeare's Sonnet 76 'invention in a noted weed' hints he wrote high. He treats the aesthetic case as a phenomenology problem: separating cannabis's real contribution to appreciation from mere buzz-glow. He then defends a right to get high by invoking the Declaration's 'pursuit of happiness' and a Mill-style principle that private, non-harming pleasure should not be criminalized.

kant-aesthetics.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
kant-aesthetics.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
kant-aesthetics.relation: Karlsen argues that climbing routes are genuine aesthetic objects and that judging a route beautiful is a real aesthetic judgment, not mere pleasure. Against Kant's demand that beauty require detachment (which would confine climbing to the 'merely agreeable') and against Aristotle's exclusion of the bodily senses, he distinguishes a 'line' (seen from the ground, like The Nose) from a 'route' (actually climbed) and contends that proprioception, the felt sense of bodily movement, yields information about the route itself, not just the body. Invoking the phenomenological 'transparency of experience' (Moore's diaphanousness), he concludes proprioception is an aesthetic sense that lets widely-agreed classics emerge.

kant-aesthetics.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
kant-aesthetics.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
kant-aesthetics.relation: Rachel Falkenstern argues that although tattoos seem permanent, the embodied self is changing and finite, so tattoos are 'illusions of permanence.' Using Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology she dissolves the mind/body and self/tattoo boundary (we are our bodies, the world shapes us and we shape it); using the German aesthetic tradition from Kant to Hegel she reads a tattoo as a sensuous 'appearance of freedom' and links the Romantic notion of Bildung (self-formation) to choosing ink. She adds Foucault's aesthetic self-transformation and Shusterman's somaesthetics/Deweyan pragmatism to cast tattooing as reciprocal self-expression and self-creation that offers a glimpse of infinity within finitude.

kant-aesthetics.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
kant-aesthetics.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
kant-aesthetics.relation: Nicole Dunas's 'The Feeling of Beauty' recounts founding the Real Beauty Yoga Project after a teacher-training 'modeling day' where consultants photographed only the five thinnest students, enacting division rather than yogic union. Framing the beauty question against Kant's claim that beauty is objective, and drawing on David Abram's participatory perception and Susan Bordo on airbrushed bodies, she argues that objectifying beauty into an image to be gazed at (the male gaze, the isolated cosmetic-surgery gaze) severs us from it, whereas Hatha yoga's tantric, present-moment embodiment lets beauty be lived rather than consumed.

kant-aesthetics.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
kant-aesthetics.title: BLUES
kant-aesthetics.relation: David C. Drake argues that the blues' distinctive achievement is presenting 'sadness as beauty,' which lets performers and listeners find their own sorrow beautiful and thus therapeutic. He surveys theories of beauty — Plato's proportion/harmony/unity and Aristotle's order/symmetry (a beautiful life needs some sorrow), Kant's claim that beauty is a subjective-yet-universal judgment requiring reflection, Lyotard's sublime that 'pleases only by causing pain,' and Schopenhauer's view that aesthetic contemplation temporarily frees us from the striving Will — and links beauty to truth and goodness (Keats, Nietzsche's 'whoever despises himself respects himself as one who despises') to explain why blues sorrow feels good.

kant-aesthetics.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
kant-aesthetics.title: “Hot with Rapture and Cold with Fear” Grotesque, Sublime, and Postmodern Transformations in Patrick Süskind's
kant-aesthetics.relation: Cokal reads Suskind's Perfume and Tykwer's film through the intertwined categories of the grotesque and the sublime. The odorless murderer Grenouille is a Bakhtinian grotesque body who nonetheless has Kantian sublime experiences of the plum girl's and Laure's scents, and Cokal uses Kant's and Lyotard's accounts of the sublime (the soul 'immobilized, as good as dead') to explain the awe that Grenouille both feels and, via his 'angel's scent,' induces in the orgy at his execution. Grenouille's uncanny encounter with his own lack of smell in the cave is read through Freud's uncanny, and his final cannibalistic dismemberment collapses the sublime back into the grotesque.

kant-aesthetics.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
kant-aesthetics.title: NOTES
kant-aesthetics.relation: Ted Cohen denies there is any sound argument from 'X is better than Y' to 'it is better to like X,' using Bach vs. Elvis vs. Milton Babbitt on complexity to show the criterion collapses. He reframes art around 'communities of appreciation'—citing Augustine's claim that a people is defined by what it loves in common—and reports (via a blues club in Memphis and the Marriage of Figaro) that what all appreciators of a work share is 'nothing' but their love of it, a Goodman-style nominalism. He challenges Kant's insistence that genuine aesthetic judgments claim universality, arguing real appreciative communities are less-than-universal overlapping circles.

kant-aesthetics.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
kant-aesthetics.title: NOTES
kant-aesthetics.relation: Richard Shusterman defends the entertainment value of popular art from a pragmatist ('meliorist') stance, tracing entertainment's genealogy through Plato, Aristotle, Montaigne, Kant, Hegel, Nietzsche, Heidegger and Adorno—whose 'culture industry' opposes pleasure to cognition. Using rap (KRS-One's 'Edutainment', Public Enemy, Ice-T) and T.S. Eliot's 'superior amusement,' he argues knowledge and enjoyment are compatible. He rejects Hannah Arendt's contrast of imperishable art vs. life-serving entertainment, and critiques G.E. Moore's Principia Ethica 'method of absolute isolation' for intrinsic value, replacing it with a Deweyan transactional account in which even intrinsic values are relational and temporal.

kant-aesthetics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
kant-aesthetics.title: 77. Journey as Philosophy Meaning, Connection, and the Sublime
kant-aesthetics.relation: Hamer argues Journey works through the interplay of connection, the sublime and meaning. The wordless multiplayer bond with an unnameable stranger before vast vistas dramatizes emotional connection where the ancestors' greed failed. The looming mountain and immense dunes evoke the sublime, read through Burke's pleasurable terror and Kant's mathematical and dynamical sublime (imagination overwhelmed while reason comprehends; feeling power over a nature that cannot harm the deathless player, then rebirth surpassing the sublime into joy). The cyclical return to the start recasts the game as Camus's Myth of Sisyphus: a meaningless repeated ascent that players nonetheless replay, so we must imagine the Traveler — and ourselves — happy to make the beautiful repetition our own.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Irwin takes Pilate's Quid est veritas as a guided tour of theories of truth applied to the film: Gibson's sympathetic Pilate embodies relativism, met with Nietzsche's 'truth is a woman' perspectivism and Baudrillard's postmodern laughter and rejected; Caiaphas and the bad thief demanding Jesus come down from the cross put the correspondence theory to work ('the proof is out there'), though beliefs hang on other beliefs ad infinitum; Simon of Cyrene's growing conviction models the coherence theory, exposed as necessary but not sufficient by Swinburne's case for versus Wells's case against the divinity of Jesus; and Pilate's Barabbas gambit parodies James's pragmatic theory, where working is not enough if there is no corresponding reality. He then retrieves Heidegger's reading of aletheia as uncovering, helped by the Quid est veritas anagram ('Est qui vir adest': it is the man before you) and Gadamer on truth seizing us like beauty, so that Jesus's 'I am the truth' and Claudia's dream-guided warnings point to truth as disclosure. Since disclosure alone cannot decide between inconsistent revealed claims, Irwin ends by leaving the viewer with a leap of faith and a first instinct as final answer.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: “Trust Your Feelings”
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Fader tackles the paradox that Jedi lie while Sith tell the truth: Obi-Wan's 'Darth Vader betrayed and murdered your father,' Yoda's trickster masquerade on Dagobah, the Council's cover-up of its waning powers, against Vader's brutal truth at Cloud City and Palpatine's technically honest 'I love democracy.' Kant's absolute prohibition of lying is set against the utilitarian's greatest-good lie and Nietzsche's claim that truth is the accepted set of social lies; Obi-Wan's deception is then defended through Plato's noble lie and the Buddha's Parable of the House on Fire, where 'expedients' to save the oblivious are no falsehood, while Vader and Dooku wield literal truths as weapons without compassion. Luke's answer is to stop accepting anyone's version and build his own green lightsaber: truth as perspective, intention, and finally the heart's understanding that redeems Anakin.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Bamford argues that Atkins's insistence that dieters evaluate the plan for their individual needs parallels Nietzsche's cultural therapy: as the death of God left modern culture nihilistic, so a processed-food culture suffers 'nutritional nihilism,' and the 'mega-orthodox' doctors who worship medical consensus with 'religious fervor' treat science as a replacement religion. Reading Ecce Homo's 'question of nutriment' alongside Twilight of the Idols, she shows that Nietzsche's perspectivism — no uninterpreted facts, only interpretations from physiological perspectives — makes each dieter fully responsible for interpretation, which is why Atkins must ask us to think for ourselves. The limit: where Atkins keeps an 'absolute faith in empirical science' (and Atkins Nutritionals mass-markets processed low-carb products), a properly Nietzschean therapy would question that faith too.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Tarantula’s End
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Goldblatt and Necarsulmer pair Dylan's Tarantula with Nietzsche's "The Tarantulas" from Zarathustra: both are books of advice, renaming, and stream-of-consciousness flow whose sections cohere through signature and attitude rather than narrative (the same Foucauldian author function). Both embody the intuitive artist of Plato's Ion and Nietzsche's Ecce Homo - the poet as medium whose language arrives as inspiration, all language being fresh or stale metaphor. Tarantula's vengeful vignettes and "Idiot Wind" dramatize the ressentiment Zarathustra warns against, its impenetrable juxtapositions ("harmonica battalions," "funeral landlord") work as Derridean catachresis - metaphor whose transfer fails yet exerts aesthetic force - and the book's dream of the burning tenement leaves Dylan unable, and absolved, to look back.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Rhetoric and Bullshit
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Following Jeremy Campbell's The Liar's Tale, the chapter argues that the truth/lies binary is oversimplified: even 'the sky is blue' depends on contested definitions and 'God is good' on the speaker's concepts, so we must separate capital-T Truth — the immutable, incorruptible kind Plato located beyond the flawed physical realm of perfect Forms, which made him scorn rhetoric and the Sophists as teachers of disguise — from lower-case, situated, perspectival truths. It then recruits Nietzsche, for whom humans have no 'organ' for Truth but a natural instinct for falsehood (shared with camouflaging animals), and Ken Gemes's reading of doctrinal Truth as a ritualized fiction manufactured to maintain institutional and religious power. On this view postmodernism studies truth within the shifting domain of language rather than denying objective reality.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Like Caine in Kung Fu
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Bence Nanay and Ian Schnee argue Pulp Fiction is genuinely Nietzschean, but not by celebrating violence: the film stages the crisis of meaning after God's death through two reactions to chance. Vincent is the passive nihilist—dogmatically insisting the six bullets mean nothing, inheriting gangster values unquestioned, modeling himself on Elvis—while Jules's 'moment of clarity' makes him a Nietzschean free spirit who creates perspective-relative meaning and breaks the cycle of violence by buying Ringo and Honey Bunny's lives. His plan to 'walk the earth, like Caine in Kung Fu' reworks Zarathustra's wandering, and the running toilets gag marks Vincent's blindness to the significance of events, which is why only one of them survives.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: The Final Word That’s Right, I Said Preliminary Thoughts
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Patton starts from wildly disputed Springsteen interpretations — Reagan's 1984 campaign use of 'Born in the U.S.A.,' Flint protesters playing 'My Hometown' as civic pride, Kerry's 'No Surrender' — and asks whether any reading is better than another. He frames the issue as Socratic dialectic versus Gorgias-style rhetoric, passes through Augustine's polysemy (multiple intended levels of meaning, as in 'I'm on fire') to Nietzsche's claim that the text disappears beneath its interpretation, extended by Foucault (truth as an instrument of power) and Derridean deconstruction. His conclusion: authorial intent cannot settle meaning, but some readings ('Born in the U.S.A.' as pro-Reagan anthem) are non-starters, otherwise it is rhetoric all the way down and the sophists win.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: The Prophet
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Presents Muad'Dib as Nietzsche's Zarathustra in the Dune universe: the sardonic self-mockery that keeps a great man from believing his own myth, the valuation of life-enhancing 'truths' over correspondence-truth (behind all logic stand 'value judgments,' as Beyond Good and Evil has it), and monumental, mythologized history against Mentat-accurate history that kills religion. Paul's Fremen, first hard and vital, go 'water-fat' under the paradise his jihad built, becoming Nietzsche's 'Ultimate Man'—the last man who has left the places where living was hard and demands 'a little poison now and then'—so Muad'Dib must become the Preacher to destroy the rigid code he created, as Zarathustra came to undo Zoroaster's morality; both prophets preach self-overcoming toward the Superman.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Deeply Dissecting Dexter
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Deborah Mellamphy uses Nietzsche's masks - 'every profound spirit needs a mask,' the will to power that requires deception for self-preservation - to explain both why Dexter's crafted normalcy works and why only the characters conscious of their own masks (Doakes, Lila, Brian, Trinity) see through his. Nietzsche's perspectivism and 'Truth and Lie in the Extra-Moral Sense' then dissolve any true self beneath the mask: if truths are 'worn out metaphors,' Dexter's question 'If you play a role long enough... does it ever become real?' has no stable answer. Following Sarah Kofman's reading, the chapter asks whether we are all 'but this veil itself' and concludes that Dexter goes a step beyond Nietzsche by locating the truth of identity in the many layered masks themselves.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Leap of Faith
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Dionne argues Cobb's 'most resilient parasite' works only as an idea embedded in a coherent story - 'my father doesn't want me to be him' - and that since ideas define who we are, each person is less a host than a collection of well-planted narratives. Using Bergson on embodied, memory-and-desire-mediated perception (Cobb's fear of the bridge triggering Mal's projection) and Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil on perspectival appearance as the price of life, she claims dreams differ from reality in degree, not kind: we are beings-in-the-world who stabilize contingency through story-making and 'strive for positive logic'. Hence knowledge always demands the leap of faith that Saito and Mal demand of Cobb, the film becomes a meta-narrative with Fischer as its audience, and the wobbling top offers only an interpretation of a fact, never the fact itself.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Dandelions on My Cloud
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Uses 'Dandelion'—truth as a bright yellow flower that blows away—to mark the withering of Enlightenment confidence in plain, visible truth under deconstruction. Kierkegaard's 'truth is subjectivity' explains why truth on 'Get Off of My Cloud' cannot be shared directly ('Don't hang around 'cause two's a crowd'), and Nietzsche goes further: there is no truth to find, only wills to power making truths—'you can't always get what you want... you just might find you get what you need.'

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 19. The Alchemy of Flat Worlds
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Staged as Professor Moby Dickens Melville's 'Philosophy of Worlds' course uniting Discworld wizards with the geometric Flatlanders of Abbott's novella, the chapter contrasts a storytelling, narrative-causality philosophy of Discworld with Flatland's mathematical, hierarchy-obsessed rationalism, and extends the contrast to physics (wizards favor loop quantum gravity, Flatlanders string theory) and theology (Hex's self-designed universe and words of power versus Flatland's circle-priests who rule women declared 'deficient in Reason'). When a Flatlander woman, Ms. Transversal, protests that calling the new softer approach 'feminine' repeats Abbott's sexism, the class closes with the narrator's suggestion, from a chalk-nub's-eye view, that everything we know may reflect the direction from which we see rather than the truth itself.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 22. The Irrelevance of Truth
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Jan Kyrre Berg Friis argues, with Nietzsche, that truth is a 'mobile army of metaphors', a relational event between people rather than an objective correspondence, and that the will to truth is subordinate to the will to power — the difference being that Trump-style 'alternative truth' is dishonest domination while Nietzsche's askesis is self-transformation. He layers in the Buddhist and Zen (Dogen) diagnosis of perception as conceptual distortion, Descartes' ego cogito as the fatal Western turn, and Heidegger's warning that calculative, technological thinking covers over our tacit lived background, producing exactly the one-dimensional minds a Ministry of Truth can feed. Rorty's advice to drop the truth-talk, Kant's insight that reality is sifted through the perceiver, and the cognitive-science of confirmation bias explain why facts no longer bite in the post-truth newsfeed.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 11. Lip Sync for Your Life
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Guilel Treiber reads the Season Ten reunion blow-up - Asia O'Hara blaming the show for letting The Vixen walk out, RuPaul insisting people must 'want to meet halfway' - as an unresolvable conflict between two value systems. The show's official 'C.U.N.T.' virtues (charisma, uniqueness, nerve, talent) are individualistic, market-driven values that professionalize drag, while the implicit 'A.S.S.E.' values (acceptance, solidarity, support, empowerment) descend from LGBTQ+ history from Stonewall and Marsha P. Johnson to ACT-UP. Using Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morals and its project of the 'revaluation of all values,' he argues values gain worth through conflict rather than progress, so there is no view from nowhere that settles the dispute. Miss Congeniality, the queens' revolt over Valentina's title, and Tammie Brown's clash with RuPaul show the show's magic lies in never deciding between the two - even though market pressure keeps devaluing solidarity.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Dull Reality The Tragic View of Life
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: A Nietzschean interpretation: Alice's unastonished pursuit of the White Rabbit exemplifies the 'will to ignorance' hidden within the will to truth, since every perspective is created by selecting and simplifying while we convince ourselves we have discovered rather than invented. Rick Mayock reads the Caterpillar's 'Who are YOU?' and the mushroom as lessons in perspectivism and in the self as a grammatical fiction (no doer behind the deed, no lightning behind the flash), the Queen's beheadings and ruleless croquet as a flux of competing wills to power, and the Hatter's madness as Dionysian against Alice's Apollonian calm, with Greek tragedy supplying the metaphysical comfort that makes 'dull reality' livable.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Can You Face the Bat
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Sarah Donovan and Nicholas Richardson use Nietzsche and Foucault to present Batman as a self-constructed identity: across Batman: Year One, Arkham Asylum, and The Dark Knight Returns, Bruce consciously builds the persona ('Yes, Father, I shall become a bat') rather than revealing a deeper true self. Foucault's constructed categories of normal and abnormal surface in Arkham Asylum's 'super-sane' Joker and the Alice in Wonderland parallels that put Batman's own sanity in question alongside Amadeus Arkham's madness. Nietzsche's will to power and eternal recurrence, via the shepherd biting the snake in Zarathustra, explain why Bruce can face the bat that others flee, becoming heroic where Arkham and Dr. Cavendish go insane.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: The Prophet
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Reads Paul-Muad'Dib as a Nietzschean prophet: his sardonic greatness mirrors Zarathustra the laughing prophet, the Fremen's implanted legends illustrate Nietzsche's point that value matters more than truth (logic being only one perspective on the world), and the Untimely Meditations account of monumental myth explains why Muad'Dib must become the Preacher to destroy his own petrified religion. It likens the water-fat new Fremen of Children of Dune to Nietzsche's soft, risk-averse last men, and presents both Zarathustra and Muad'Dib as all-too-human founders who create a religion, recognize it as 'the most fateful of errors', and turn against it, with self-discipline rather than divine intervention as the true virtue.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Leap of Faith
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Dionne reads Cobb's 'idea is the most resilient parasite' as a claim about narrative: what gets incepted in Fischer is a story ('my father doesn't want me to follow in his footsteps'), and by the same token each of us is a collection of incepted stories rather than a stable self. Drawing on Bergson's account of perception mediated by memory and desire (Cobb's bridge triggering Mal's projection), Nietzsche's perspectivism — truth is a 'moral prejudice' and 'we must mistake ourselves' — and the embodiment of the being-in-the-world, she argues dreams differ from reality only in degree, since both are interested story-making under time pressure. The payoff is meta-filmic: Fischer is the spectator and Cobb the director, and the final spinning top becomes the audience's own totem — there is no fact of the matter, only interpretation, so watching the ending is itself the leap of faith.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Notes
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Adams pairs Anakin with Achilles to show how Palpatine's lesson that 'good is a point of view' - Nietzsche's claim that there are no moral facts, only interpretations - nearly destroys both heroes before a father's love pulls them back: Priam's tears before Achilles, Luke unmasking Vader. Against nihilism the chapter defends moral realism through Apollo's lion simile (compassion and respect are objective facts about what persons require) and Kant's self-critical inquiry, with the Jedi Council's twelve-way deliberation illustrating that some interpretations are better than others, beyond Hume's problem of induction. Both epics settle on a 'Pagan Golden Rule' - help your friends and harm your enemies, but never lose compassion for either.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Nietzschean Themes in the Films of Charlie Kaufman
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Shaw argues Kaufman's films embody a Nietzschean 'Dionysian pessimism' organized around the will to power, eternal recurrence, perspectivism, and a bundle-theory of the self. He reads Being John Malkovich through the bundle self: personal identity is the dominant drive that acts, so Malkovich 'becomes' Lester/Mertin, the will that controls the vessel. Adaptation's Laroche voices Nietzsche's plastic power of forgetting, and Eternal Sunshine dramatizes eternal recurrence and amor fati as Joel and Clementine choose to repeat their doomed love. Synecdoche, New York, by contrast, Shaw judges a failure of passive nihilism—Caden as the fly who never leaves the bottle—deadening rather than life-affirming.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: From “Impassioned Morality” to “Bloodless Agnosticism” A Philosophy of David Cronenberg through the Burroughs
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Jones Irwin analyzes Cronenberg's adaptations of Burroughs's Naked Lunch and Ballard's Crash, arguing that while all three share an aesthetic of body horror and a Nietzschean perspectivist experimentalism, Burroughs and Ballard hold an 'impassioned moralism' (Crash as cautionary tale, Marcuse's one-dimensional man, an ethics of complicity and responsibility) that Cronenberg replaces with 'bloodless agnosticism.' Cronenberg aestheticizes Burroughs's wife-killing and reads Crash literally, using Plato's appearance/reality (cave) distinction to show he strips out the sociopolitical and moral frame the writers intended.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Sanders coins 'sunshine noir' for Miami Vice as postmodern neo-noir, defining postmodernism via antirealism, skepticism about knowledge, and enigmas of personal identity, anticipated by Nietzsche's perspectivism. He analyzes three episodes: 'Heart of Darkness', where undercover agent Artie Rollins is consumed by his fantasy self (mirroring Crockett's Sonny Burnett) and hangs himself; 'Shadow in the Dark', where Crockett adopts the burglar's mind-set (Dilthey's Verstehen) in a dreamlike, glass-imagery structure that undermines the realist camera; and 'Lend Me an Ear', where the surveillance expert Duddy, echoing The Conversation, collapses into paranoid moral solipsism.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: The Sopranos, Film Noir, and Nihilism
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Kevin Stoehr reads The Sopranos as TV noir built on Nietzsche's passive, life-negating nihilism: Tony Soprano's 'What do we got?' laments the collapse of mob and family values, Uncle Junior's 'Each of us is alone in the fuckin' universe' voices noir alienation, and Livia's 'It's all a big nothing' is the series' nihilistic creed. A.J.'s confirmation-eve rebellion reading Nietzsche and Camus's The Stranger ('Death just shows the ultimate absurdity of life') dramatizes the death of God inherited by the next generation. The chapter's dark irony is that therapy, meant to give Tony narrative unity and self-knowledge, becomes an instrument of self-deception: he substitutes psychology for ethics, rationalizes adultery and murder as signs of psychic power, and fails at Nietzschean self-overcoming despite the ducks and Pie-O-My that briefly symbolize transcendence.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: From Dollars to Iron The Currency of Clint Eastwood's Westerns
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: McNaron traces Clint Eastwood's evolving western hero from the amoral 'Man with No Name' to The Outlaw Josey Wales, using Will Wright's plot typology plus Nietzsche, Aristotle, and Kierkegaard. He reads the Eastwood antihero's 'manly nihilism' and prizing of strength and style through Nietzsche's master/slave morality and perspectivism, his virtues (self-control, phronesis) through Aristotle, and his elevation of the aesthetic over the ethical/religious against Kierkegaard's stages. The film's central claim—that only words with 'iron' behind them (Josey and Ten Bears's pact) can found genuine community, unlike government's 'double tongues'—grounds a transcendental argument about the conditions for authentic community and justified vengeance.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: Fake News and Ecstatic Truths
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Kyle Novak uses Herzog's fabricated Pascal epigraph in Lessons of Darkness to distinguish 'ecstatic truth' from Trump-era 'alternative facts,' arguing that unlike Kellyanne Conway's deception, Herzog openly reveals his inventions to deepen an artistic experience. Rejecting Russell's correspondence theory of truth, Novak turns to Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulation and The Gulf War Did Not Take Place to show how media create norms and a hyperreality independent of facts, then to Nietzsche's 'On Truth and Lies' (truth as agreed-upon metaphor) and Deleuze's affirmation of life as a non-relativist standard, concluding that Lessons of Darkness is 'sparse on facts but full of truths' that penetrate deeper than CNN footage.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 2. Misinterpretation as the Author’s Responsibility (Nietzsche’s fascism, for instance)
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Berel Lang asks whether an author is responsible for being misinterpreted, defining a 'Fascist Minimum' (priority of the state over the individual, plus natural inequality asserted through war) and testing Nietzsche against it. He finds Nietzsche flatly rejects the first condition—his 'coldest of all cold monsters' attacks on the state and nationalism—and accepts the second only with heavy qualification. Lang locates Nietzsche's partial culpability in a 'Fallacy of Composition' by which readers like Bäumler transposed individual will to power onto the collective state, arguing that Nietzsche, foreseeing this abuse, chose not to 'build a fence' around his meaning and so bears responsibility 'up to a point.'

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 13. A Godfather Too Nazism as a Nietzschean “Experiment”
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Fischer contends that the 'historically effective' (not the 'real') Nietzsche could be read from opposite perspectives, and that Nazism is best understood as a post-Nietzschean 'experiment' licensed by the death of God and the collapse of accepted values ('wir machen einen Versuch mit der Wahrheit'). Invoking Nietzsche's own perspectivism from the Genealogy, and citing calls to 'push what is falling,' the coming 'fight for dominion of the earth' and the Cesare-Borgia-over-Parsifal remark, he argues Nietzsche was 'half a Nazi and half an anti-Nazi'—a genuine part-time godfather, against Kaufmann's overly 'gentle' de-Nazified reading.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 23. The X-Files as Philosophy Navigating the “Truth Out There”
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: The chapter argues that Darin Morgan's X-Files episodes philosophize by critiquing the show's own 'the truth is out there' mantra from within. Through the conflicting hypnosis testimonies and identical camera blocking in 'Jose Chung's From Outer Space,' Morgan cinematically stages Nietzsche's perspectivism and the claim that 'truth is as subjective as reality'; through Clyde Bruckman and the doomed Ansel of 'Quagmire,' he mounts an anti-Socratic case that relentlessly pursuing truth (as Mulder does) is not worth the ruin it brings. Kowalski then rebuts Morgan using Descartes's cogito and inference-to-the-best-explanation to defend objective truth against radical skepticism, arguing subjectivism about truth is self-refuting.

nietzsche-perspectivism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
nietzsche-perspectivism.title: 89. The Joker as Philosopher Killing Jokes
nietzsche-perspectivism.relation: Brake reads Moore and Bolland's The Killing Joke as staging Camus's absurd: the Joker tortures Commissioner Gordon to prove the world is random and unjust ('one bad day') and that reason, tied to continuous memory, should be abandoned for a fragmented 'multiple choice' self. Drawing on Nietzsche's wave-like unstable self (via Morrison's 'super-sane' Joker) and Foucault on how madness haunts modern reason, the chapter argues Batman and Gordon also flirt with madness, while questioning whether the Joker, seeking revenge, has really embraced the absurd or is more rational than he admits.

pragmatic-truth.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
pragmatic-truth.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
pragmatic-truth.relation: Irwin takes Pilate's Quid est veritas as a guided tour of theories of truth applied to the film: Gibson's sympathetic Pilate embodies relativism, met with Nietzsche's 'truth is a woman' perspectivism and Baudrillard's postmodern laughter and rejected; Caiaphas and the bad thief demanding Jesus come down from the cross put the correspondence theory to work ('the proof is out there'), though beliefs hang on other beliefs ad infinitum; Simon of Cyrene's growing conviction models the coherence theory, exposed as necessary but not sufficient by Swinburne's case for versus Wells's case against the divinity of Jesus; and Pilate's Barabbas gambit parodies James's pragmatic theory, where working is not enough if there is no corresponding reality. He then retrieves Heidegger's reading of aletheia as uncovering, helped by the Quid est veritas anagram ('Est qui vir adest': it is the man before you) and Gadamer on truth seizing us like beauty, so that Jesus's 'I am the truth' and Claudia's dream-guided warnings point to truth as disclosure. Since disclosure alone cannot decide between inconsistent revealed claims, Irwin ends by leaving the viewer with a leap of faith and a first instinct as final answer.

pragmatic-truth.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
pragmatic-truth.title: “A New Hope”
pragmatic-truth.relation: Long stages William Clifford's ethics of belief against William James's will to believe, with Luke Skywalker as James's exemplar. Clifford's shipowner story condemns faith as 'wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone,' which would convict Luke of immorality when he switches off his targeting computer and trusts the Force; James replies that where a choice is intellectually undecidable and a genuine option - live, forced, and momentous, like Luke's turn to the Jedi life or Obi-Wan's response to Leia's hologram - pragmatic faith is justified and even salvific. Faith can create truths: Han flying into the asteroid field, Luke's unjustified belief that there is good in Vader bringing Anakin back, the author's faith in his students, and Martin Luther King Jr.'s dream - all illustrating 'a new hope.'

pragmatic-truth.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
pragmatic-truth.title: U2 and Philosophy
pragmatic-truth.relation: Cleveland sorts the knowing and feeling of U2's lyrics ('Vertigo', 'Beautiful Day', 'Staring at the Sun', 'Daddy's Gonna Pay for Your Crash Car') into Russell's varieties of knowledge - propositional, acquaintance, know-how - and argues that the feeling U2 champions against thought is knowledge by acquaintance: direct, concept-free awareness that, in religious cases, just is Jamesian mystical revelation as against revelation as a set of propositional truths, which is why Bono tells his father he 'hears something back from the silence' rather than holding doctrines. James supplies both the view that feeling is the deeper source of religion and the pragmatist answer to the problem of origins - 'by their fruits ye shall know them', so religious feeling is vindicated by moral transformation. Hume's slave-of-the-passions thesis explains why such feeling, not inert moral knowledge, moves Bono's social justice work: 'God is love, and as much as I respond... in acting in that love, that's my religion'.

pragmatic-truth.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
pragmatic-truth.title: So Why Bullshit
pragmatic-truth.relation: Violations of the epistemic imperative are sorted into Peirce's 'sham reasoning' (the creationist who reasons only to prop up a fixed conclusion), Haack's 'fake reasoning' (corporate-funded research, vote-seeking politicians, the temporary-insanity plea), and the skeptic's premature 'we'll never know' - none of which is bullshitting, which is precisely not caring about truth, like the sales clerk praising shoes at random. Even philosophy can slide into bullshitting when, per Rorty, it becomes 'carrying on the conversation' with truth as what your peers let you get away with; and brainstorming differs from a bull session because brainstormers actually want to discover something.

pragmatic-truth.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
pragmatic-truth.title: “Something to Believe In”
pragmatic-truth.relation: Reads Worf's crisis over the clone 'second coming' of Kahless in 'Rightful Heir' as a live, forced, and momentous option in William James's sense, where 'faith creates its own verification.' Peirce's methods of fixing belief — tenacity, authority, and science — explain why Worf cannot accept Koroth's pious fraud once Gowron's DNA test exposes the clone, while Data's own 'leap of faith' in believing he is more than a machine supplies the Jamesian model of believing without evidence. Worf's compromise — telling the Klingon people the truth but installing Kahless-the-clone as spiritual emperor because 'the words are more important than the man' — is offered as pragmatist truth: what works while staying answerable to hard facts.

pragmatic-truth.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
pragmatic-truth.title: “Here, Here, What’s All This Jabber-wapping When There’s Work to Be Done ”
pragmatic-truth.relation: Tschaepe reads Professor Marvel and the Wizard as skilled givers of 'folk explanations'—stories about desires, beliefs, and feelings that work where logical, scientific, or mechanistic explanations fail—because each explanation is fitted to the pragmatic considerations of its audience and problem. With the companions the Wizard works through a failed dualist argument (a brain is not a mind) for the Scarecrow, an abbreviated Stoic ataraxy pitch for the Tin Man, and Aristotle's discretion-is-valor point for the Lion, settling in each case on folk psychology plus a token (Th.D. diploma, heart-shaped clock, Legion of Courage medal) that supplies the recognition actually needed. Dorothy, whose desire for home is real rather than mistaken, gets no folk explanation from anybody: she must combine the heel-tapping instruction with her own articulated desire—'there's no place like home'—which the chapter treats as pragmatically, not logically, effective.

pragmatic-truth.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
pragmatic-truth.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
pragmatic-truth.relation: Vannatta reads Klosterman's born-again pop culture — the Left Behind novels, Victory TV's Steven, Kurt Warner's Super Bowl, Jesus Camp — as living Puritan Calvinism: original sin (Klosterman's cruel third-graders), justification by faith alone, unmediated access to God ('every man was his own priest'), and predestination that leaves uncertain whether our actions matter in the divine equation. The chapter's pivot is truth versus peace: Puritan-born-again certainty sacrifices peace for antecedent truth, from the 1675 Massachusetts settlements to Robertson and Falwell on 9/11. Against this Vannatta sets the pragmatist alternative — truth as the outcome of communal inquiry in service of peaceful living — recasting God as the web of relationships and dissolving his own childhood camp's contradiction between 'I'm Third' and its cult of competition.

pragmatic-truth.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
pragmatic-truth.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
pragmatic-truth.relation: Ray Bossert reads American Gods as an allegory of American philosophy: like Gaiman's gods, American philosophers labor invisibly in the background while European publics canonize their thinkers, and Shadow's prison exchanges show the point, since Loki must beg him to read Herodotus ('It's cool') while Johnnie Larch's 'don't piss off people who work in airports' beats Shadow's abstract generalization in usefulness. Following Hickman's Deweyan instrumentalism, he argues the gods are survival tools humans craft from need and discard when obsolete, so Czernobog's hammer gives way to Media's television, Wednesday treats even his own son as an instrument, and the buffalo man's 'believe everything' is advice about keeping one's tools of survival working. The chapter ends on liberty: Shadow refuses to be a god because 'we don't need anyone to believe in us,' and in the Egyptian death trial he claims the most American reward, the freedom to choose his own afterlife.

pragmatic-truth.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
pragmatic-truth.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
pragmatic-truth.relation: Ellen Sorg separates knowledge from intelligence using Kant's Critique of Pure Reason: Jeopardy! winners like Ken Jennings exercise only the first knowing power, sensibility - recall of facts as they appear to us - never ascending to the intellect of the Transcendental Analytic or acting on what they know, so Jennings would likely wash out on Survivor. Pragmatism supplies the missing criterion: Peirce and James hold that thought gains its value from its practical consequences and from the modification of conduct, which is what Survivor's fire-building, shelter-making, and Kim Spradlin's 2012-winning social game actually test. Hence Jeopardy! proves its champions knowledgeable, but only Survivor proves anyone intelligent.

pragmatic-truth.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
pragmatic-truth.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
pragmatic-truth.relation: The chapter compares Barney's 'True story' pronouncements with William James's pragmatism, using James's squirrel anecdote and the 'Zoo or False' monkey-mugging to ask when an evidentially undecidable dispute becomes a live practical question. Like James's pragmatic cases for free will and religious comfort, Barney's monkey story and the twenty-eight-year-old 'with some sun damage' are beliefs made true by their practical (mostly entertainment) value, then replaced like outdated theories when new evidence arrives, as James's consistency requirement demands. The divergence: the Barney Stinson (BS) theory of truth is self-serving, engineering unverifiable stories others cannot disprove, while James weighs what works for everyone's experience.

pragmatic-truth.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
pragmatic-truth.title: 1. The Genuine Article
pragmatic-truth.relation: Written in the voice of a non-C-137 Rick, the chapter argues that whether the Beth at the end of 'The ABCs of Beth' is a clone doesn't matter, because our reverence for 'the genuine article' (like the original US Constitution) is romantic packaging, and a functional clone is as good as the original. It tests Robert Nozick's experience machine, whose three objections supposedly show we value genuine reality intrinsically, against Rick's pragmatism of believing what is useful, and reads 'The Wedding Squanchers' (Rick turning himself in to the Federation) as proof that his family is both instrumentally and intrinsically valuable to him. Your answer to the clone question, it concludes, is a Rorschach test revealing what you place intrinsic value on.

pragmatic-truth.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
pragmatic-truth.title: 5. Greatness or Nothingness
pragmatic-truth.relation: Courtland Lewis uses KISS's career gambles to compare theories of decision-making. After Tolstoy's twig-over-the-dragon allegory of mortal life, he tests W.K. Clifford's shipowner (never act without sufficient evidence) against KISS's counter-evidence bet on the Alive! live album, models the choice with Pascal's Wager, and uses the Prisoner's Dilemma to explain the flop of the four 1978 solo albums. He then argues William James's pragmatism — beliefs as rules for action, the living, forced, and momentous option that 'KISS is the best' — best explains why acting on the band's self-created narrative was authentic, with Nietzsche completing the picture: greatness requires leaping, living dangerously, tightrope-walking toward self-defined success.

pragmatic-truth.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
pragmatic-truth.title: 12 The Shadow Realities of Indiana Jones
pragmatic-truth.relation: Matthew Crippen and Matthew Dixon read the franchise's caves through Plato's allegory: in Crusade, stand-ins for God (the Cross of Coronado, the Grail, with the decoy chalices as shadows of a representation) appear underground, while Indy's self-realizations with his father occur at sunlit cave mouths, inching from shadow toward the Good. They fuse this with newer, active accounts of truth — James's 'truth happens to an idea' realized in the leap from the lion's head, Dewey on poetry as revelation, and Heidegger's aletheia as unconcealment — while Nietzsche's critique shows Platonic fictions can still be life-enhancing. The father and son 'shadow' one another (with Oedipal overtones through Elsa) until Henry Sr. relinquishes the Grail to save 'Indiana,' his path out of the cave.

pragmatic-truth.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
pragmatic-truth.relation: Conard argues that Tarantino's postmodernism makes redemption impossible in Reservoir Dogs (and Pulp Fiction, Kill Bill). Using Danto on the 'end of art', Lyotard's 'incredulity toward metanarratives', and Rorty's contingent 'vocabularies', he shows the films embrace relativism about knowledge (rearranged chronology, unreliable perspectives) and about values. Mr. Orange plays Judas and Christ; the opening tipping argument exposes moral conventions as arbitrary, so becoming a 'real person' rather than a gangster is merely being a dork rather than cool. With no metanarrative to ground it, one way of life cannot be morally superior, so redemption fails.

pragmatic-truth.title: Mommas, Don't Let Your Babies Grow Up to Be Pragmatists
pragmatic-truth.relation: Csaki argues that John Wayne became the ultimate cinematic cowboy because his characters embody classical American pragmatism. Using William James's squirrel-and-tree parable and Dewey's account of 'inquiry' transforming an indeterminate situation, he reads Rooster Cogburn's split-second raft decision and Wil Anderson's hiring of schoolboys in The Cowboys as pragmatic problem-solving from experience. He treats the 'code of the West' not as fixed absolutes but as rules applied pragmatically (Rooster shooting men in the back, the cowboys letting Long Hair be dragged to death), where truth is what can be assimilated, verified, and made to 'work.'

pragmatic-truth.title: Fake News and Ecstatic Truths
pragmatic-truth.relation: Kyle Novak uses Herzog's fabricated Pascal epigraph in Lessons of Darkness to distinguish 'ecstatic truth' from Trump-era 'alternative facts,' arguing that unlike Kellyanne Conway's deception, Herzog openly reveals his inventions to deepen an artistic experience. Rejecting Russell's correspondence theory of truth, Novak turns to Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulation and The Gulf War Did Not Take Place to show how media create norms and a hyperreality independent of facts, then to Nietzsche's 'On Truth and Lies' (truth as agreed-upon metaphor) and Deleuze's affirmation of life as a non-relativist standard, concluding that Lessons of Darkness is 'sparse on facts but full of truths' that penetrate deeper than CNN footage.

pragmatic-truth.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
pragmatic-truth.title: 9. Anthony Bourdain’s Inquiring Mind
pragmatic-truth.relation: Anderson and Mauro trace Bourdain's growth from the dogmatic provocateur of Kitchen Confidential to a Peircean inquirer, using Peirce's 'The Fixation of Belief' and its four methods (tenacity, authority, a priori, inquiry). They argue Bourdain's tattooed motto 'I am certain of nothing,' his surprise and self-correction in Cambodia, Beirut, Saudi Arabia, and Haiti, and his pragmatic theory of evolving truth make him a model of the self-correcting inquiring life.

pragmatic-truth.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
pragmatic-truth.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
pragmatic-truth.relation: Holt argues that Seinfeld's Festivus, invented by Frank Costanza as an anti-consumerist 'holiday for the rest of us,' is grounded in American pragmatism: truth is 'whatever works,' malleable and tested by results. Because commercialized Christmas fails to deliver the altruism it demands, it 'does not work' and by pragmatist standards ceases to be true, so Costanza pragmatically forges a holiday that fits his needs. Holt reads Festivus's elements pragmatically — the maintenance-free aluminum pole as a bare functional symbol, the airing of grievances as a needed cathartic release from everyday restraint, the wrestling as self-perpetuating ritual — and warns that as Festivus merchandise spreads it will lose its practicality and, being no longer pragmatic, be discarded; he closes with a mock 'airing of grievances' against philosophers including Plato and Bertrand Russell.

ontological-argument.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
ontological-argument.title: The Force Is with You . . . but You’re Not a Jedi Yet
ontological-argument.relation: The editors' introduction argues that beneath its action scenes Star Wars stages ageless philosophical questions through the Skywalkers' struggles with identity, truth, freedom, and tragedy, opening with 'I've got a bad feeling about this' as basic philosophical wonder and doubt. It playfully transposes classic problems onto the saga: an Euthyphro-style question of whether Jedi virtues are good because the Jedi appreciate them, Anselm's question whether Yoda is a master greater than which cannot be conceived, Augustine on whether Anakin can be chaste 'but just not yet,' Machiavelli on Palpatine's Empire, Descartes' mind-body question asked of C-3PO, Hume's problem of induction applied to whether the sun will rise on Alderaan, Nietzsche's abyss for Vader, and Sartre's hell for the Sith. It previews each contributor's chapter rather than settling any question, framing the volume as a Kessel Run for the brain.

ontological-argument.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
ontological-argument.title: The Epilogue A Question of Belief
ontological-argument.relation: Systematically pairs Hume's philosophy of religion with Python parodies: Anselm's ontological argument fails because existence cannot be defined into a concept (the Yeti-spotter who never spotted one), with Arthur 'Two Sheds' Jackson, Ron Obvious, and Confuse-A-Cat illustrating the gap between conceivability and possibility; the Galaxy Song's cosmic order and the mock hymn 'All Things Dull and Ugly' stage the design argument and Hume's reply that creation shows moral indifference as readily as benevolence; and Brian's 'miracles' — being 'taken up' then spotted sprinting, curing Simon the hermit by landing on his foot — illustrate Hume's 'Of Miracles' on the unreliability of testimony. Hume's Natural History claim that the cause of religion is fear surfaces in the 'O Father, please don't boil us' hymn and in Arthur's groveling before a God who hates it. Both Hume and the Pythons end in suspended judgment about God — settled, if at all, only by the wrestling match in which 'God exists by two falls to a submission.'

ontological-argument.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
ontological-argument.title: Does the Habit Make the Monk
ontological-argument.relation: Elliott maps the recurring Monk stalemate onto medieval theology: in 'Mr. Monk Goes to the Circus', Stottlemeyer and Disher reason forward from a hunch and the evidence, exactly like Anselm's ontological argument, which assumes what it sets out to prove, while Monk, like Aquinas against Anselm, refuses assumptions and reasons backward from verifiable facts, asking why an assassin would somersault except to advertise the acrobatic alibi. Aquinas's First Cause argument (Aristotle's unmoved mover) supplies the model of proving a certainty from observable things, paralleling Monk's 'I don't know how he did it, but he did it' backward deduction. The chapter's closing move likens Monk to the medieval monks themselves: his OCD-driven ascetic withdrawal from the dirty, chaotic world (contemptus mundi) is what lets him notice the imperfection in scenes like the locker room of 'Mr. Monk and the Big Game' that reveals sabotage.

ontological-argument.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
ontological-argument.title: What Makes the Red Sox Great Is More than the Team
ontological-argument.relation: Ulatowski argues the 'We Believe' motto is religious: Red Sox fandom is the a priori conviction that Boston is the sports city 'than which none greater can be conceived,' transplanting Anselm's ontological argument—necessary, contingent and impossible objects, existence as a perfection—to the Red Sox via Oliver Wendell Holmes's 'hub of the universe.' He rejects the parallel New York argument because it smuggles a posteriori championship counts into an a priori proof, and answers the fallacy-of-division worry by making Boston's greatness and the Red Sox's greatness an identity rather than a whole-to-part inference.

ontological-argument.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
ontological-argument.title: 4. Could a Divine Creator Turn Out to Be a Selfish Jerk
ontological-argument.relation: Using 'The Ricks Must Be Crazy', where Morty discovers Rick's car battery is a microverse of gooble-box workers ('slavery with extra steps'), the chapter asks whether a universe's designer must be a perfect God or could be a clever jerk like Rick. It lays out Paley's watchmaker teleological argument, Hume's point that even a real designer need not be morally perfect, the Euthyphro dilemma against Divine Command Theory (would Rick's commands for middle-finger greetings become morally good?), and Plantinga's modal ontological argument recast across the show's multiverse of possible worlds like the one where Hitler cured cancer. It concludes that Rick's advice to just not think about it is exactly what Socrates refused to do.

ontological-argument.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
ontological-argument.title: 6. A Better Bad Place
ontological-argument.relation: Grosz asks whether Judge Gen could justly condemn Team Cockroach to eternal torment, testing the classic 'sins against an infinite being deserve infinite punishment' defense built on Anselm's God as that than which nothing greater can be conceived, and finding that no such being exists on the show. He rejects the continuing-sin model of Hell because the Bad Place's physical torture precludes both further sinning and moral reform, and argues purely retributive eternal punishment fails the utilitarian test. His proposal, a non-torturous 'Bad Place 3.0' modeled on C.S. Lewis's The Great Divorce where people face the natural consequences of their vice until they reform, could be justified as what is best for the person.

ontological-argument.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
ontological-argument.title: Why Roger Federer Is the Best Or Is It McEnroe
ontological-argument.relation: David Baggett asks who is the all-time best male tennis player and treats it as a genuine problem in metaphysics ('what is the case?') and epistemology ('how do we know it?'), surveying candidates from Tilden to Federer against ten criteria. He argues the sentence 'Federer is the all-time best' is vague, running the tennis-ball-losing-an-atom sorites through three theories of vagueness—fuzzy logic, supervaluationism, and Timothy Williamson's epistemicism, which he favors: there is a fact of the matter (God knows it) but our closeness-to-the-margin ignorance keeps us from knowing it. He uses Anselm's ontological argument and Guanilo's perfect-island reply to distinguish the all-time best from the best-possible player, and invokes Sartre's existentialist rejection of mere potentiality ('could've/should've') to insist he is asking who actually was best, not who might have been.

hume-induction.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
hume-induction.title: The Force Is with You . . . but You’re Not a Jedi Yet
hume-induction.relation: The editors' introduction argues that beneath its action scenes Star Wars stages ageless philosophical questions through the Skywalkers' struggles with identity, truth, freedom, and tragedy, opening with 'I've got a bad feeling about this' as basic philosophical wonder and doubt. It playfully transposes classic problems onto the saga: an Euthyphro-style question of whether Jedi virtues are good because the Jedi appreciate them, Anselm's question whether Yoda is a master greater than which cannot be conceived, Augustine on whether Anakin can be chaste 'but just not yet,' Machiavelli on Palpatine's Empire, Descartes' mind-body question asked of C-3PO, Hume's problem of induction applied to whether the sun will rise on Alderaan, Nietzsche's abyss for Vader, and Sartre's hell for the Sith. It previews each contributor's chapter rather than settling any question, framing the volume as a Kessel Run for the brain.

hume-induction.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
hume-induction.title: “May The Force Be with You”
hume-induction.relation: Jones uses the Force's telekinesis (Luke's lightsaber flying to his hand, Yoda raising the X-wing) to probe the metaphysics of causation. Hume shows we never observe the necessary connection between cause and effect - only constant conjunction and habit - so Jedi mind-power is no more mysterious than gravity or magnetism; Leibniz's Monadology argues one substance cannot transfer properties to another, so 'how' any cause works is unintelligible; and Hume's problem of induction (will Tatooine's twin suns rise tomorrow? will Vader's officers always choke?) shows law-governed expectations cannot be non-circularly justified. Concurring with Russell that 'cause' is a relic, the chapter concludes the Force qualifies as a kind of cause precisely because our causal concept is too vague to exclude it - and plugs science fiction as a laboratory for sharpening concepts.
