hume-induction.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
hume-induction.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: O'Connell extracts Brillat-Savarin's 1825 anti-flour-and-starch regimen — clear soup without croutons, shun beer, rye over white bread — as a 'proto-Atkins' and reconstructs its real argument: farmers fatten livestock on starches, so by Humean 'species of Analogy' starches fatten humans, from which abstinence from floury foods is 'deduced.' Hume's Enquiry Section IX, 'Of the Reason of Animals,' supplies the philosophical audit, distinguishing relations of ideas from matters of fact and grading the animal-to-human analogical inference as probable at best. The chapter ends with Hume's fork turned on the diet-book shelf: any volume without experiential reasoning concerning matter of fact deserves the flames — 'nothing but sophistry and illusion.'

hume-induction.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
hume-induction.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: Steele starts from Orwell's worry that laypeople accept scientific consensus as unreflectively as tribesmen accept witch-doctors — sharpened by Lysenko and Nazi 'racial science' — and answers it with Popper's critical rationalism: since Hume's problem of induction bars proof from instances, we can only provisionally prefer theories that survive severe attempts at falsification, so trusting experts is reasonable exactly when their community tests rather than defends its theories. Kuhn's paradigms explain why dissident alternatives like Atkins talk past the dominant school (Atkins and Agatston are cardiologists, not dieticians), and the 2002–2004 studies showing improved lipids on more fat figure as the kind of surprise that precedes paradigm change. His verdict: neither trusting nor resisting experts is foolish; 'human knowledge is too important to be left to experts.'

hume-induction.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
hume-induction.title: Questioning Everything The Birds
hume-induction.relation: The Deavels argue that Hitchcock's suspense is fundamentally epistemological. In the social world, heroines in love - Constance in Spellbound, Lina in Suspicion, Rose in The Wrong Man - must weigh mounting evidence of their beloveds' guilt against the Aristotelian premise that character is consistent because virtue and vice are habits: Constance rightly bets that J.B.'s gentleness with her proves he is no murderer, Lina reasonably concludes Johnnie may poison her, and Rose survives only by inventing a persecutory 'they'. With The Birds the question widens to nature itself: Mrs. Bundy's ornithology assumes past bird behavior predicts future behavior, and the film's terror is Hume's worry that causal order may be an unfounded projection, leaving Mitch to stake his family's escape on the humble observed pattern that attacks come in waves.

hume-induction.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
hume-induction.title: Step Back
hume-induction.relation: Gallagher uses Monk's phobias to test Hume's claim that believing is itself a kind of feeling. The chapter asks whether a fear conflicting with a rational belief (Monk paralyzed by the possibly-on stove during a murder investigation) feels any different from a conflict between two fears ('Snakes trump heights' in 'Mr. Monk and the Very, Very Old Man') or two beliefs, and answers with Hume that beliefs are forceful-feeling representations — there is a 'what it's like' to believing the German shepherd is dangerous. On Hume's account the force of a belief comes from repetition of experience, which explains both why Monk's fears should fade (countless safely landed flights, millions of milk drinkers) and why they persist: his mind dwells repeatedly on the rare catastrophe, giving fearful representations extra force, as when his repeated experience that 'she's always cheating' makes him wrongly believe Brody's wife in 'Mr. Monk and the Bully.' The practical lesson is to step back and widen attention to all the possibilities, as Monk intermittently manages with the help of Natalie and Stottlemeyer.

hume-induction.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
hume-induction.title: Area Philosopher (Me!) Is Sick Of The Stupid Debate About Stupid
hume-induction.relation: Cuddy stages the generational-decline debate between Mark Bauerlein's The Dumbest Generation and Stephen Johnson's Everything Bad Is Good for You, showing that Onion stories can be marshaled for both sides: Aristophanes complaining that today's audiences 'just don't get me' vindicates the perennial declinist, while 'US Students Lead World in Detention' wryly supports Johnson's sleeper curve. Comparing Bauerlein to Aristophanes and the 'Our Dumb World' entry on Aristotle and Plato's schools closing, he concludes every era teems with idiots, so The Onion could have existed in any century. Because induction from earlier generations' failed predictions cannot settle whether Millennials really are dumber, he suspends judgment and toasts The Onion as the smartest perspective around.

hume-induction.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
hume-induction.title: Get Serious
hume-induction.relation: David Kyle Johnson takes Nietzsche's suggestion that God is slowly dying and reads The Onion's religion stories — the faith healer who loses a patient during a routine miracle, Kansas fundamentalists lobbying to overturn the Second Law of Thermodynamics, and 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New Intelligent Falling Theory' — as evidence of secularization. He splits blind faith (irrational belief despite evidence, as with Bush's 'Blind-Faith-Based Initiatives') from genuine faith as belief without sufficient evidence, arguing religion does science badly whenever it shields creationism from falsification. But science rests on unproven assumptions too, he shows via Hume's problem of induction, Descartes' skeptical problem, and Wittgenstein's charge that naming a 'strong nuclear force' explains no more than God pushing things down. Ockham's razor then decides for atheism — an unexplained universe is simpler than God plus a universe — though William James's will to believe leaves a door open for faith where evidence is impossible, qualified by Clifford's warning that beliefs likely to harm others are never permissible.

hume-induction.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
hume-induction.title: The Honorable, the Woman
hume-induction.relation: Mona Rocha and James Rocha charge that Holmes's 'deduction' is really Humean induction, and that his inductive shortcuts about women, tricking Mrs. Smith in The Sign of the Four, reading Mary Sutherland's pacing as a love affair, and dismissing Lady Frances Carfax as a 'stray chicken in a world of foxes', are hasty generalizations made dangerous by gender stereotype. Watson is worse: his 'experience of women... over many nations and three continents' reads Mary Morstan's soul off her face and grants full courtesy only to the beautiful intruder of 'The Solitary Cyclist', a feminist case study in objectification. Irene Adler's escape in 'A Scandal in Bohemia', disguising herself as a young man and outwitting the fire ruse, is Doyle's deliberate proof that treating women as a class fails, making her a proto-feminist decades before Poirot's Rossakoff or Spade's O'Shaughnessy.

hume-induction.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
hume-induction.title: Our Best Bet
hume-induction.relation: Terjesen argues Mycroft surpasses Sherlock because he truly grasps Hume's Problem of Induction: Sherlock's celebrated eliminations (the three key possibilities for Cadogan West in 'The Bruce-Partington Plans') and his newspaper-ad tests are inductive, Popperian conjecture-testing that can never confirm anything, while Goodman's 'grue' shows the same evidence always supports rival explanations. Watson's failed attempt in 'How Watson Learned the Trick,' the amateur reasoner's wrong solution in 'The Lost Special,' and Holmes's own 'Norbury' failure in 'The Yellow Face' prove that a correct method guarantees nothing. Mycroft, who 'would rather be considered wrong than take the trouble to prove himself right,' implicitly embraces Reichenbach's pragmatic justification — induction is simply our best bet — and therefore hunts longer for the facts that do not fit, acting only when England's fate is at stake.

hume-induction.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
hume-induction.title: Futurama and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: Elsby argues Fry's 'brain thing' illuminates how humans form beliefs and adapt to misconceptions: Fry accepts swans as swan boats and deduces 'boat eggs,' romances the radiator woman from the radiator planet, and insists he is in the ruined New York of 4000 rather than L.A. - each time reasoning flawlessly from a false premise before readjusting when corrected. Using Aristotle's incidental perception (seeing the pale thing as Cleon's son), Hume's warning that grouping similar-but-non-identical objects breeds ambiguity, and Mom's grandiose misreading of Fry's anchovy purchase in 'A Fishful of Dollars,' the chapter traces how error enters at each step of identification and inference. The payoff: Fry differs from us only in degree, and our capacity to adapt to overturned assumptions might be inferior to his.

hume-induction.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
hume-induction.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: Michaud plays the 'David Hume' Card Wars deck against Princess Bubblegum's confidence in science: following Hume's problem of induction, every scientific law rests on observation and is only probabilistic—we never observe the necessary connection between cause and effect, whether in magnetism, Jake's hunger-induced jerkiness, or the first law of thermodynamics. Humans are pattern-makers who project causal order onto the world (seeing Gunter in clouds, blaming one bubblegum incident), while quantum physics reveals genuine randomness that Einstein hated. Ooo's residents, who watch Tree Trunks explode and simply move on, may grasp reality better than we do, because they never smuggle in stable, lawlike expectations that the show—and the universe—keep violating.

hume-induction.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
hume-induction.title: Justified and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: The chapter turns Raylan's claim that shooting Tommy Bucks was 'justified' into a question of epistemic justification, expounding Plato's Meno definition of knowledge as justified true belief, Gettier's 1963 counterexamples (rebuilt with Boyd truly but luckily predicting that a marshal will be arrested), and the repairs of Goldman's no-false-causal-link condition and Harman's inference to the best explanation. It then grades the show's reasoners: Raylan knows the Crowes rather than Boyd killed Wade Messer, Boyd knows Cassie milks the revival snakes' venom, Art Mullen does not yet know Raylan helped Winona return the evidence-room money, and gut-feeling victims like Ellen May do not know what they saw. Against Humean skepticism about cause and effect it defends inductive, detective-style knowledge - Raylan can know who done it without courtroom proof.

hume-induction.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
hume-induction.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: Roger Hunt answers 'what do philosophers do?' through Dennis's seduction methodology. Frank embodies empiricism, leaving the comfort of principle for the messiness of the world as Hume did when he found no impression of causation, space, or time; Mac embodies rationalism, reasoning with total confidence from a principle he cannot doubt, as Descartes did from the cogito; and the dialectic of Socrates and Plato, questioning beliefs in dialogue to see what survives scrutiny, describes philosophy as it is actually practiced. Boethius's Consolation - the imprisoned author consoled by dialogues with Lady Philosophy - supplies the frame of philosophy as an encounter with a woman one pursues, and each D.E.N.N.I.S. step maps onto the craft: Demonstrating value to the problem, Engaging physically in its awkward grind, Nurturing dependence through thesis panic, Neglect and Inspiring hope on the road to the defense, then Separating entirely - 'be a sociopath about it.'

hume-induction.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
hume-induction.title: 18. Gruesome Walkers
hume-induction.relation: Yuen turns the walkers into a lesson on Hume's problem of induction: the pre-apocalyptic belief that the dead do not rise was justified by all past experience until Rick wakes to a world where they do, and Rick's distrust of Alexandria repeats the same inductive move from Woodbury, Terminus, and Grady - useful, Hume says, since custom compels us, but never knowledge. Russell's chicken illustrates the fatal surprise, and Goodman's grue (the pun of the title) shows the outbreak could be a future-swinging regularity like the seventeen-year cicadas, undermining even Jenner's experimental science. Popper's falsificationism is offered as the rescue - Shane's reanimation falsifies the "walkers make walkers" theory, leaving the "everyone is infected" theory corroborated but never known.

hume-induction.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
hume-induction.title: 23. How Can We Know Anything in a World of Magic and Miracles
hume-induction.relation: Baldwin asks whether Westerosi characters can know anything inductive in a world without lawlike nature: seasons of unpredictable length, wargs in animal minds, Faceless Men changing faces, and resurrections by Thoros, Melisandre, and Qyburn. After laying out the Platonic justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge (those who saw the pyre are justified in believing Dany is the mother of dragons; those relying on rumor are not), he runs Hume's problem of induction - we never perceive causal connection, so no jar of wildfire must explode - against Reid's common-sense reply that reason and induction stand or fall together, concluding that Westeros gives its people special reasons for skepticism while we, lacking evidence of magical irregularity, are rational to trust everyday inductive belief.

hume-induction.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
hume-induction.title: 8. For Hume the Ball Tolls!
hume-induction.relation: The chapter argues Charlie Brown's repeated falls for Lucy's football gag are failures of induction: given the history of the gag since 1951 (first with Violet, then Lucy's fake reasons each fall - a handshake, a contract, a hundred million dollars), he should draw the meta-level conclusion that she will always pull the ball away. It then tries Hume's problem of induction as his defense, but since that would cost him all knowledge of the external world (that Snoopy is a beagle, that Lucy is mean) and end in skepticism, Charlie - a student of his world, not a doubter of it - cannot take it. The verdict: he is not a blockhead but determined and committed, willing to lose every fall because kicking that ball would be worth it, as in the 1979 hospital strip where he finally gets his kick and still ends up on his back.

hume-induction.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
hume-induction.title: 2. Persuade Me Once, Shame on You . .
hume-induction.relation: Greene dismantles both phases of Adams's case that Trump is a Master Persuader. The trait-list phase (opening with big demands, the Intentional Wrongness Persuasion Play, never apologizing, exuding confidence, recruiting the reciprocity instinct, and the talent stack) fails because doing what master persuaders do is not being one, by the Tom Brady versus Archie Manning point that we never define good quarterbacks by wins alone and by the Kantian thought that an act must be done for the right reason. The reality phase borrows Plato, Hume, and Kant to deny us access to an objective world, but the chapter replies that the experts' predictive failures illustrate Hume's problem of induction rather than proving there are no facts, notes Adams even misreads Plato, and observes that nothing links the Persuasion Filter's one success to Trump's skills rather than to a one-off political climate.

hume-induction.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
hume-induction.title: 16. Gotta Have Faith
hume-induction.relation: Winters asks what faith is when the Party risks burning and becoming demodog chow so Eleven can close the gate: after arguing via George Michael and the talisman-free tunnels that faith need not be religious, he tests Bishop's models of faith against 'The Gate' (the affective and secular hope models fit; the belief and trust models fail because everyone has seen the Mind Flayer's work on Will). Hume's account that causation is never observed, only habituated, explains the Party's hope that heat will drive the Mind Flayer from Will and that Christmas lights will reach him, and Kierkegaard's teleological suspension of the ethical and knight of faith frame Eleven's willingness to die against the absurd, since aligning her life with friendship's higher purpose is what makes it meaningful.

hume-induction.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
hume-induction.title: 6. The Facts Don’t Speak for Themselves
hume-induction.relation: Muyskens asks why Burger and Tragg's evidence keeps pointing at innocent people, answering with Hume's distinction between relations of ideas and matters of fact and the problem of induction: inferences from past experience are never guaranteed. In 'The Case of the Shapely Shadow' the prosecution's seven pieces of testimony against Janice Wainwright are reasonable but false, and only Mason, because he believes his client, presses to the water-records discovery that exposes Cole Troy; 'The Case of the Runaway Corpse' then shows Burger and Tragg settling on Myrna Davenport on flimsy, self-contradictory evidence and simply failing to investigate, while Mason withholds judgment, checks her account against documents and witnesses, and digs until justified true belief is achieved.

hume-induction.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
hume-induction.title: 7. Beyond a Reasonable Doubt
hume-induction.relation: Jordan argues Mason's real superpower is logic rather than client selection or legal brilliance: since conviction requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt before a unanimous jury, and since by the problem of induction (traced from Sextus Empiricus's regression arguments through Hume) no accumulation of probabilities yields deductive certainty, the prosecution can never conclusively prove guilt while Mason need only exploit that structural gap, as in The Case of the Howling Dog's cab-driver and document evidence and the TV movie Perry Mason Returns where Della is the accused. He illustrates with modus ponens examples about Della and Hamilton Burger, contrasting sound deductive arguments with merely strong inductive ones like predicting Mason's next win.

hume-induction.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
hume-induction.title: “Consider Your Verdict!”
hume-induction.relation: Splits Wonderland's nonsense into the tolerable kind (strange but lawful regularities, like mushroom side-effects and walking the opposite way to reach the Red Queen, which Alice masters by experiment) and the intolerable kind (the creatures' eristic logic). Using Hume's fork of relations of ideas versus matters of fact, George Dunn and Brian McDonald argue Alice rightly concludes the pig-baby is merely an out-of-the-way matter of fact, while the White Queen's 'jam every other day: to-day isn't any other day' and the King's beheading of the bodiless Cheshire Cat repeat the Sophists' tricks from Plato's Euthydemus, which Socrates deflates from the standpoint of common sense and the examined life. The Knave's trial ('sentence first, verdict afterwards') lands on cable-news pundits who, like the show trials of Stalin, argue from predetermined conclusions.

hume-induction.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
hume-induction.title: The Lasting Legacy of Logic
hume-induction.relation: Treats Carroll the Oxford logician as a teacher hiding five lessons in Wonderland: watch your assumptions (the King infers the Knave's guilt from an unsigned letter), know what your words mean (Humpty Dumpty on 'glory'), don't confuse categories (the King's 'Nobody' and the Hatter's personified Time), don't switch subjects and predicates ('I mean what I say' versus 'I say what I mean'), and don't confuse necessary with sufficient conditions (Alice's Ada and Mabel arguments, with a hammer-and-egg illustration). David S. Brown grounds the lessons in Hume on causes discoverable only by experience, Aristotle's law of non-contradiction and categories, the Marx Brothers' 'Either he's dead or my watch has stopped', and Popper's point that a successful prediction cannot prove a hypothesis, only a failed one can refute it.

hume-induction.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
hume-induction.title: Wonderland and the Real World
hume-induction.relation: Extracts three problems of induction from Alice's misadventures: predicting the future (Hume's problem: nothing rationally compels Humpty Dumpty to agree the world will not turn into Wonderland at 6 a.m. tomorrow), proving whose dream it is (Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence: Tweedledee can accommodate any evidence within the theory that Alice exists only in the Red King's dream), and translating Wonderese (Quine's indeterminacy: pointing at the White Rabbit cannot fix whether natives mean the rabbit, its parts, or its stages, nor what 'muchness' means). Brendan Shea shows Alice succeeding where the creatures fail by the criteria Hume and Quine endorse: experimentation, simplicity, conservatism of belief, and a principle of charity in translation.

hume-induction.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
hume-induction.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
hume-induction.relation: Mackonis shows Sheldon is wrong about being wrong: Stuart's tomato counterexample ('it's very wrong to say it's a suspension bridge') refutes his claim that wrongness admits no gradation, and closeness to truth is cashed out with possible-worlds similarity — vegetable theory sits one small alteration from actuality, echoing Sheldon's own many-worlds refusal to dance in any of them. The Raj exchange ('So you were wrong' / 'I didn't say that') motivates many-valued logics in which degrees of truth let both be partly right, while the 'Cooper-Wrongness Paradox' argues that if Sheldon always knew when he was wrong, he could never know that he was wrong. Hume's problem of induction then shows his post-Toby confidence in his other beliefs can never be inductively verified, only sometimes falsified, and his French-sprinkled 'victory' over an exhausted Stuart is sheer logical fallacy.

hume-induction.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
hume-induction.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
hume-induction.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

hume-induction.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
hume-induction.title: Notes
hume-induction.relation: Adams pairs Anakin with Achilles to show how Palpatine's lesson that 'good is a point of view' - Nietzsche's claim that there are no moral facts, only interpretations - nearly destroys both heroes before a father's love pulls them back: Priam's tears before Achilles, Luke unmasking Vader. Against nihilism the chapter defends moral realism through Apollo's lion simile (compassion and respect are objective facts about what persons require) and Kant's self-critical inquiry, with the Jedi Council's twelve-way deliberation illustrating that some interpretations are better than others, beyond Hume's problem of induction. Both epics settle on a 'Pagan Golden Rule' - help your friends and harm your enemies, but never lose compassion for either.

hume-induction.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
hume-induction.title: Notes
hume-induction.relation: Asks whether Han Solo's 'hokey religions' dismissal of the Force is unreasonable given his evidence, answering no: Hume's argument against miracles explains why testimony of lightsaber tricks and mind tricks should not overturn Han's experience of consistent natural law, while Hume's problem of induction and custom/habit explain why both Han's 'luck' verdict and Obi-Wan's 'no such thing as luck' are habit-based generalizations. Peirce's fallibilism (backed by Putnam's 'fallibilism does not entail skepticism') lets Han and Obi-Wan each claim knowledge without certainty, echoing Obi-Wan's line that many truths depend greatly on our own point of view.

hume-induction.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
hume-induction.title: Kickstarting Inductive Inference
hume-induction.relation: Daniel Wilkenfeld analyzes Veronica's 'magic trick' in the 'One Angry Veronica' juryroom and her season-long bus-crash solution as Peter Lipton's inference to the best explanation: the hypothesis 'Beaver is a killer' wins by consilience (explaining the explosion, the dead rat, Curly Moran, even her chlamydia), simplicity, and completeness. But the criteria face Hume's problem of induction — why think the future will resemble the past, when yesterday's popular girl is today's pariah? — and Descartes's evil demon undermines even what Veronica 'sees,' since Curly Moran could fake a bus crash, leaving no non-circular justification for inferential habits none of us can live without. Following Nelson Goodman, Wilkenfeld concludes the demand for justification is misplaced: what matters is that Veronica reasons consistently, in the juryroom as at the cliff.

hume-induction.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
hume-induction.title: Feel the Big MO'
hume-induction.relation: Letson asks whether momentum in football is a real explanatory phenomenon, opening with the Bills' 1993 comeback over the Oilers. He notes momentum is invoked only for success and only for one team at a time, and struggles to separate it from the mere evidence of playing well, comparing it to 'talent.' Surveying psychological models (Taylor and Demick's momentum chain) and David Romer's fourth-down analysis denying momentum, he argues that even if a small momentum effect exists, its size relative to chance means appeals to it in any particular game are usually unjustified—like blaming one heart attack on smoking.

hume-induction.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
hume-induction.title: Sherlock's Reasoning Toolbox
hume-induction.relation: Pigliucci shows that Holmes's celebrated 'deduction' is really a mix of induction and abduction, contrasting Aristotelian syllogism and Cartesian rationalism (with its failed Cartesian circle) against the fallibility of real investigation. He walks through Hume's problem of induction (Russell's inductivist chicken), the Mill-Whewell 'great induction debate,' and Popper's falsificationism—qualified by the Neptune/Uranus episode where scientists shielded Newton. Using 'Thor Bridge' and 'The Three Students,' he concludes Holmes is a pragmatic scientist wielding a whole toolbox, since there is no single scientific method.

hume-induction.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
hume-induction.title: 4. Demons, Game Shows, and Baguettes
hume-induction.relation: Wenmackers traces psychohistory's scientific lineage from Newtonian determinism through Laplace's demon, arguing Foundation stays within nineteenth-century limits by predicting only probabilities. She uses Newcomb's Paradox to capture the unease of living under a predicted Seldon Plan, Poincare's chaos and the three-body problem to show determinism need not mean predictability, and Poincare's baguette-fraud tale plus Quetelet's social physics and statistical mechanics to explain psychohistory's core assumption that mobs of billions behave lawfully even when individuals do not. She suggests Seldon's science was in some sense historically inevitable.

hume-induction.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
hume-induction.title: 12. Raven Seldon Predicts Disaster
hume-induction.relation: Malloy argues psychohistory rests on induction and therefore inherits Hume's problem of induction: Seldon generalizes from Trantor's past to predict the Empire's fall, but nothing guarantees the future will resemble the past, and the Mule's unprecedented rise shows there is no deductive guarantee (the future-unlike-past idea is not self-contradictory). He tests Popper's falsificationism, under which psychohistory is science because it makes falsifiable predictions and can never be confirmed, then notes Popper leaves hypothesis-origin and post-failure revision inductive, and finally offers Reichenbach's pragmatic 'vindication' of induction, likening it to Hardin making do with the only tools at hand in a Seldon Crisis.

hume-induction.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
hume-induction.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
hume-induction.relation: Jurgensen and Southworth apply Hume's argument against miracles to the virgin birth, treating it as a claimed violation of the natural law that virgins do not conceive. They attack the credibility of the only witnesses, Matthew and Luke, noting their third-hand sources (Mark, Q, L/M), their contradiction over whether Mary and Joseph were married, and the mistranslation of Isaiah's ambiguous 'almah' as the Greek 'parthenos' (literal virgin). Invoking Hume's four defects of miracle testimony and his maxim that no testimony suffices unless its falsehood would be more miraculous than the event, they conclude a rational person must reject the Christmas miracle.

hume-induction.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
hume-induction.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
hume-induction.relation: Kakko's 'Hallucinatory Terror' uses Fitz Hugh Ludlow's 1857 The Hasheesh Eater to ask 'How can these things be?' — the ontological status of hallucinations that neither exist nor fail to exist. He traces Ludlow's own reading from Locke's empiricism through Hume's skeptical worry that all perception may be hallucinatory with no verifiable external object, to Kant's Copernican turn: the phenomenal/noumenal distinction, synthetic a priori judgments, and space and time as pure forms of intuition. Kant's framework lets Kakko recast Ludlow's 'virtual change of worlds' as a literal, non-metaphorical restructuring of the intuitions conditioning experience.

hume-induction.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
hume-induction.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
hume-induction.relation: Steve Jacobson's 'Standing on Your Head' asks whether an educated Westerner can reasonably believe 'yoga theory' (chakras, prana, kundalini, koshas) given that science has superseded ancient theories. He raises a 'standard objection' from the superior predictive power of science (invoking Hume's problem of induction), rejects weak replies, but argues via the epistemology of testimony that people with weak scientific grounds and strong critical testimony can rationally accept yoga theory. He concludes that even if no part of it is credible, abandoning it would leave yoga intact — 'yoga with fewer illusions.'

hume-induction.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
hume-induction.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
hume-induction.relation: Terjesen defines a 'real date' as a shared intention to try out romantic possibility, using Abelard's claim that intention (not behavior) determines the nature of an act to show that identical activities are or aren't dates depending on mutual intent. He then invokes Russell's argument-from-analogy account of knowing other minds to explain how daters 'mind-read' each other's intentions, and notes this yields only probable conclusions, generating an infinite regress ('I know that you know...') that only 'the Talk' resolves. He cites Hume's problem of induction as the deeper reason analogical inference can never be certain, and uses the Friends 'Mayor of the Friend Zone' gag and Ross and Rachel to argue the Friend Zone is a step toward, not a trap against, committed relationships.

augustine-will.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
augustine-will.title: “This One a Long Time Have I Watched”
augustine-will.relation: Eberl argues that Anakin and Luke are radically free despite the Chosen One prophecy and Obi-Wan's 'you cannot escape your destiny.' Borrowing Augustine and Aquinas on God's eternity, he holds that foreknowledge (like the Jedi prophecy fulfilled when Vader destroys the Emperor) does not compel events - Anakin's choice makes the prophecy true, not vice versa - and applies Aristotle's tomorrow's-sea-battle to future-contingents like Obi-Wan's self-surrender on the Death Star. Using Locke's locked-room example and Augustine's account of 'inordinate desire,' he concludes that Anakin's fall stems from his own disordered will to control fate ('learn to stop people from dying'), while Han Solo embodies libertarian alternative possibilities ('No mystical energy field controls my destiny').

augustine-will.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
augustine-will.title: The Fate of Evil after the Overthrow of the Empire
augustine-will.relation: Brown treats Luke's 'Is the Dark Side stronger?' as the problem of evil: distinguishing natural evils (the wampa, bigger fish) from moral evils (Tarkin destroying Alderaan), he surveys the Platonic craftsman working recalcitrant matter and the Manichean dualism of two gods - the Emperor as would-be 'evil incarnate' - before giving Augustine's answer. On Augustine's free-will defense, no creature is inherently evil; the origin of each moral evil is the creature's own pride and free choice, so Anakin, not the Emperor's seduction, is responsible for his turn ('I'm a Jedi. I know I'm better than this'). The chapter ends on whether evil can ever be finally defeated, arguing the Jedi prophecies of 'balance' fit a world where evil is a permanent possibility that heroism needs.

augustine-will.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
augustine-will.title: “A Boy Named Sue” A Cashian Theodicy
augustine-will.relation: Jamie Carlin Watson reads Cash's Christian worldview as Augustinian: evil is not a positive substance but a privation or corruption of good (contra the monism Leibniz risks and the Manichean dualism Augustine rejected), so humans alone bear blame for moral evil through freely corrupting good things—'Cocaine Blues,' 'The Wall,' the Folsom prisoner who admits he 'had it coming,' and the divided self of 'The Beast in Me' echoing Romans 7. Natural evil, as in 'Guess Things Happen That Way' and the flood of 'Five Feet High and Rising' (Cash's mother's 'blessing' of rich river dirt), serves punishment or greater goods. 'A Boy Named Sue' dramatizes the residual tension: the father's get-tough-or-die theodicy convinces neither Sue nor us that the sheer amount of evil is justified.

augustine-will.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
augustine-will.title: Who’s to Blame
augustine-will.relation: The section turns to Augustine's pear theft, where 'it was the sin that sweetened' the act: evil is chosen for the thrill of the forbidden, not forced by any demonic power. It names this 'moral impotence' — knowing the right yet willingly choosing the wrong, as with a missed curfew — an instinct no era has cured. The background vocals' 'Who? Who?' and Jagger's 'I'll tell you one time, you're to blame' thus land the blame for history's catastrophes squarely on 'you and me'.

augustine-will.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
augustine-will.title: Just as Every Cop Is a Criminal, and All the Sinners Saints
augustine-will.relation: This section lays out Augustine's journey from the Manichean two-gods heresy, through reading Plato, to the view of evil as an 'absence' rather than a force. Its core is the dilemma of Confessions 7.3: if God is wholly good, who sowed the 'seed of bitterness' — the wicked will — into us, and who made the devil? Augustine's answer runs through original sin (the pride of Adam and Eve, demons as fallen angels) and an awkward compromise on which humans are free yet constrained by predestination, so that evil becomes necessary — and confession itself a good.

augustine-will.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
augustine-will.title: It’s Only Rock’n’Roll, But I Complicate It
augustine-will.relation: Casts Augustine as the first Christian rock artist — a rebellious, sex-obsessed convert who, like Plato, ranked the body below the soul — and explains his privation doctrine: "evil has no positive nature; but the loss of good has received the name 'evil.'" Evil is "a swerving of the will which is turned toward lower things," so free will is crucial: God permits evil because virtues like courage could not exist in a world without it. The chapter closes with the constellation of opposites (soul/body, pride/humility, temporal/eternal) Augustine says we must live through to approach philosophical truth.

augustine-will.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
augustine-will.title: A Wild Murder Couldn’t Drag Me Away
augustine-will.relation: Draws Augustine and Jagger together as brothers who fell far before finding restraint: Augustine's many conflicting wills must collapse into one good will by actually choosing, and his Manichean past taught him some truths must be performed or willed, like his "grant me chastity — just not yet." The chapter reads Gimme Shelter as likewise double — harrowing documentary or joyous concert footage, forced to choose — and argues the post-Altamont Stones had to make "Sympathy for the Devil" a performative force for understanding evil rather than a scapegoat, then stayed in the flesh, confronting good and evil through the blues.

augustine-will.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
augustine-will.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
augustine-will.relation: Sets Walt's 'There's nothing but chemistry here' materialism - the missing 0.111958 percent of the human body that Gretchen calls the soul - against Augustine's Confessions, arguing both men want redemption without giving up their sins: 'give me chastity, but not yet.' It maps Augustine's problem of evil (evil as corruption of the will toward self-destruction) onto Walt's pros-and-cons list over killing Krazy-8 and his 'no-rough-stuff-type deal' fantasy after Tuco. Werner Heisenberg's uncertainty principle then turns chemistry's laws into tendencies, opening room for free choice inside a materialist world - so Walt's remission in 'Over' saves the body, while only changed choices, which he keeps deferring, could save the man.

augustine-will.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
augustine-will.title: Notes
augustine-will.relation: Eberl applies Augustine's theodicy to the Force: since evil is privation rather than a thing, the dark side is not a real half of the Force but its willful misuse by free beings, answering why a Force with a will permits Alderaan. Anakin's fall is Augustine's inordinate desire (cupiditas) for the temporal good of Padme's life against Yoda's counsel to let go, while Jacen Solo's willingness to kill for peace shows love destroyed rather than merely disordered, placing him beyond the redemption Anakin's rightly ordered love for his children still permits. Free will remains a divine gift whose misuse, not its giver, explains moral evil, and Anakin could still freely fulfill the Chosen One prophecy.

stoic-present-moment.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
stoic-present-moment.title: “Control, Control, You Must Learn Control”
stoic-present-moment.relation: Stephens reads Yoda as a Stoic sage: Luke's first impressions are blinded by appearance, but Yoda exhibits the Stoic virtues of patience, timeliness, focus on the present, apatheia (freedom from fear, anger, and hate), and ascetic discipline (askesis), living by the dichotomy of control. He reconstructs the contrasting 'logic of the Dark Side' - anger to hatred to aggression to the mastery of others - showing the Emperor as a tyrant who, unlike the self-mastering Stoic (Marcus Aurelius being the counterexample among rulers), seeks to control what is not up to him, so Vader's 'I must obey my master' is servitude to vice. The chapter also marks Stoic limits: the Emperor rightly rejects felt compassion but wrongly refuses beneficence and Stoic cosmopolitanism, and Stoic physicalism cannot accommodate Yoda's 'luminous beings' afterlife.

stoic-present-moment.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
stoic-present-moment.title: Enjoy These Moments
stoic-present-moment.relation: Earleywine argues that Rush's lyrics trained a generation in the core moves of cognitive-behavioral therapy, an idea he traces back to Epictetus before Albert Ellis and Aaron Beck rediscovered it against Freudian orthodoxy. He maps specific distortions onto specific songs: 'Witch Hunt' on dichotomous labeling, 'Distant Early Warning' ('black and whites of youth') on all-or-nothing thinking, 'Emotion Detector' on emotional reasoning, 'Vital Signs' and 'Totem' on thoughts altering perception, and 'Subdivisions' ('Conform or be cast out') as realistic critique rather than maladaptive thought. The final step, acting on examined values and savoring the present ('Time Stand Still', 'The Camera Eye', 'Chain Lightning'), makes the songs the incarnation of their own advice: just listen.

stoic-present-moment.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
stoic-present-moment.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
stoic-present-moment.relation: Gary Shapiro treats The Future as a 'lyrical phenomenology' of time that stages multiple temporalities rather than one theory of time. 'The Future' evokes an apocalypse where the katechon - the Biblical restraining force holding back the end - no longer works, while 'Waiting for the Miracle' anatomizes passive deferral in a way Shapiro finds sharper than the Stoic critique of waiting by Seneca and Marcus Aurelius and Nietzsche's 'problem of those who wait,' opposing wasted chronos to the seized kairos of 'First We Take Manhattan.' 'Anthem's' crack that lets the light in gets a Gnostic reading, 'Democracy' is glossed through Derrida's 'democracy to come' as messianic, always-arriving futurity, and 'Closing Time' and 'Always' add honky-tonk eschatology and the vow of eternal love.

stoic-present-moment.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
stoic-present-moment.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
stoic-present-moment.relation: Abigail Myers runs Stoic doctrine against Katniss's biography: Zeno's thesis that only moral goodness is good (with Plutarch Heavensbee's renunciation of Capitol privilege as indifference to wealth and status), Seneca's 'On the Shortness of Life' against deferring living, Epictetus's dichotomy of control including the uncomfortable advice to kiss wife and child as mortals, and Marcus Aurelius's practical Meditations as the gentler 'Stoic for beginners' who would be president of Panem. Katniss comes out Stoic in her frugality, her mortality-shadowed appreciation of small joys, and her firm moral code, but decidedly un-Stoic in her fierce attachments to Rue, Peeta, and Prim. Yet her final choice of Peeta over Gale is itself Stoic, Myers argues: she forgives what Peeta's hijacking made him do since it was never in his control, refuses a noble friendship that would endorse Gale and Coin's slaughter of innocents, and chooses in accordance with nature and reason so as to survive as herself with her values intact.

stoic-present-moment.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
stoic-present-moment.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
stoic-present-moment.relation: Davison uses St. Augustine's claim from the Confessions that only the present moment is real – past and future exist only as memory and anticipation – to argue that a father should stop missing his children's lives by fixating on past regrets or future worries. Drawing on Steindl-Rast and Thomas Sterner, he contrasts mechanical 'clock time' with quality-driven 'experienced time' and recommends process-focus over end-product focus, illustrated with lying beside his sleeping daughter Grace and dreading bedtime routines with his sons.

stoic-present-moment.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
stoic-present-moment.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
stoic-present-moment.relation: Kieran McManus's travel memoir 'Will I Find My Guru in India?' recounts his search from Kathmandu to Rishikesh and the Agama Yoga School, where teacher Kushru's lectures on karma, breath, and diet finally make asana click for him. His reported insight — that every thought and act moves him toward or away from his sacred potential, and that the yogi transcends suffering by treating each experience as neutral and as an opportunity, remaining present — applies a karmic and present-moment ethic to his own practice rather than expounding doctrine abstractly.

stoic-present-moment.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
stoic-present-moment.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
stoic-present-moment.relation: Jim Berti's first-person memoir 'The Path to Happiness Begins with a Journey Inside' — riffing on Yoda as a stand-in for yoga — recounts how accidental stretching and belly-breathing pulled him out of anxiety, depression, and antidepressant numbness. He frames accumulated fear as garbage that rots the body–mind unless confronted, and describes a 'five-second' breathing rule that slows reactive thinking so he can take accountability for his responses. His account of finding sustained meaning and present-focused calm through practice reads as an experiential, self-taught search for meaning rather than doctrine.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: “Control, Control, You Must Learn Control”
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Stephens reads Yoda as a Stoic sage: Luke's first impressions are blinded by appearance, but Yoda exhibits the Stoic virtues of patience, timeliness, focus on the present, apatheia (freedom from fear, anger, and hate), and ascetic discipline (askesis), living by the dichotomy of control. He reconstructs the contrasting 'logic of the Dark Side' - anger to hatred to aggression to the mastery of others - showing the Emperor as a tyrant who, unlike the self-mastering Stoic (Marcus Aurelius being the counterexample among rulers), seeks to control what is not up to him, so Vader's 'I must obey my master' is servitude to vice. The chapter also marks Stoic limits: the Emperor rightly rejects felt compassion but wrongly refuses beneficence and Stoic cosmopolitanism, and Stoic physicalism cannot accommodate Yoda's 'luminous beings' afterlife.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: Transformers and Philosophy
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Watson and Arp ask whether Ironhide and Chromia's embrace means Autobots can love, rejecting programmed loving behavior, implanted souls, and wired-in human brains as insufficient for genuine personhood, then sort Transformer relationships into Western conceptions of love. Empedoclean cosmic Love and Strife map onto Primus versus Unicron; Platonic philia ascends to the Form of Beauty, with Transformer souls originating in and returning to the All Spark; Aristotle's three friendships separate Optimus and Sparkplug's virtue-friendship from Megatron and Starscream's mere utility; and Stoic-Kantian equal love explains Autobots saving Decepticons who immediately try to kill them, alongside Christian agape in Autobot family bonds.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Greg Littmann systematically compares the Gang's values - wealth, attention, bad-assery ('Project Badass'), sexual conquest, relentless competition, revenge, pride in cheating, and callousness toward even friends and family - with the values Homer's Iliad and Odyssey celebrate, showing Achilles and Odysseus behave like the Gang: sacking cities, taking women as war trophies like Briseis, boasting of deception (the Trojan Horse), and rigging the funeral games. The real difference is scope: the heroes honor bonds of loyalty to comrades, family, and their own communities where the Gang is loyal to no one, and moderns extend concern further still. Yet our morals fail the same way when people are far enough removed - we tolerate homelessness, prison rape, sweatshop goods, and national glory-seeking - so the chapter pleads for the universal moral principles Greek moral philosophy first sought against Homeric values.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Mills presents Bates - lame leg, repeated prison spells, the public fall when O'Brien kicks his cane - as an Epictetan Stoic who 'manages' misfortune by confining his concern to what he controls, echoing the Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves.' The chapter explains the dichotomy of control and preferred indifferents through Thomas's enslaved pursuit of the valet post, O'Brien's soap-on-the-floor scheme, Mary's panicked engagement to Richard Carlisle, and Mrs. Hughes's proportioning of her cancer scare, and treats death as the great rejected indifferent via Pamuk, Sybil, and Matthew. It closes with Hierocles' concentric circles: the household's best moments (Sybil helping Gwen, the staff rallying to free Bates) collapse upstairs and downstairs into one family, while Thomas's closed inner circle marks his failure of Stoic virtue.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: 5. A Replicant’s Guide to Becoming Human
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Justin Kitchen uses the Stoic 'cradle argument' — Chrysippus on self-preservation, echoed in Wallace's 'the first thought tends to fear, to preserve the clay' — to deny that replicant slavery is natural, noting Seneca's point that rage like Batty's derails reason. Mapping the Stoic process of oikeiosis through Hierocles's concentric circles onto the films, he traces four stages: the Nexus-6's fight for survival, Rachael identifying with Deckard in love, the Nexus-8s' revolutionary community under Freysa, and finally K, who disobeys Freysa's order and sacrifices himself for Deckard as a Stoic cosmopolitan, a fellow citizen of the world. Replicants can become human because they develop through the same expanding circles of concern.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Mills reads Mr. Bates, the lame, twice-imprisoned, uncomplaining valet, as Downton's Epictetus, using him and the household to teach the Stoic dichotomy of control: only our judgments, desires, and actions are up to us, while jobs, reputations, and inheritances (Thomas's coveted valet post, Mary's scandal, Molesley's flower cup) are 'preferred indifferents' to be pursued without enslavement. Death figures as the great rejected indifferent, handled through Pamuk's demise and Mrs. Hughes's calm 'One day, I will die' upon finding a lump, as well as the grief of Isobel and Mary over Matthew. The closing section turns to Hierocles's concentric circles, with Sybil helping Gwen and Carson comforting Mary as drawing outsiders into the inner circle, a Stoic cosmopolitanism that Thomas, who sees the Crawleys as mere employers, fails entirely. The Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves' serves as the chapter's Stoic motto.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Barkman reads the trilogy's Roman texture — panem et circenses, gladiatorial Games, tyrants named Coriolanus and Caesar — through the Stoic Seneca, who lived under Nero just as Katniss lives under Snow. Seneca's distinction between the good (virtue alone), the merely preferable (wealth, fame, power), and the bad (vice) explains the Capitol: Snow and Coin traded virtue for preferables and so became vicious, while the citizens' binge-and-purge luxury mirrors the Roman decadence Seneca condemned. The Hunger Games are the gladiatorial 'pure murder' that corrupts emperors, crowds, and tributes alike, and the districts are slaves whose liberation — like Katniss declaring 'I'm done killing their slaves' — is Seneca's freedom from slavery to fear and vice. Katniss and Peeta's self-sacrificial love and refusal to be changed exemplify the Stoic virtue the Capitol cannot take away.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: “They Don't Pay Nobody to Be Humble!” Football's Ego Problem
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Holowchak diagnoses football's ego problem—Keyshawn Johnson's deactivation, Terrell Owens's self-promotion, Deion Sanders's showboating—as fed by sensationalism (via Dewey) and statistical obsession that pull players out of the team framework. He proposes 'Aretism,' a modern progressivist ethics built on Stoic oikeiosis (Chrysippus, Cicero, Seneca, Epictetus and Hierokles's concentric circles) balancing self- and other-concern, and on Kant's injunction to treat others as ends. The virtuous athlete competes fully while respecting opponents, sport, and the 'moral zone' of Stoic sagacity.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: 4. How Anthony Bourdain United the Local and the Universal
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Barta and Miranda contrast Kant's 'universally communicable' taste with Bourdieu's view that taste is a social construct shaped by field, habitus, and cultural capital that reinforces class distinctions. Using Bourdain's episodes (Portuguese bacalao, New York hot dogs, the French Laundry), they argue he synthesizes both: acknowledging taste's locality while democratizing it as a cosmopolitan 'citizen of the world' in the tradition of Diogenes and Kant's perpetual peace.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: Chapter 12 The American Diogenes
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Johnson argues Twain is best understood not as a religious skeptic but as an 'American Diogenes'—a Cynic of Christianity-as-practiced. As Diogenes 'defaced the coinage' to remove counterfeit customs, Twain uses 'sacred profanity' (honest, even profane speech that exposes phony piety, e.g. the swearing butcher, Satanic narrators in 'The Mysterious Stranger' and 'Letters from the Earth') to strike four counterfeit coins: superstition/special providence, hypocrisy, artificial 'Moral Sense'/conscience, and heavenly rewards. On death Twain matches Diogenes and Epicurus (annihilation is nothing to fear), and his self-description as 'Member at Large for the Human Race' mirrors Diogenes the cosmopolitan; Diogenes carries a lantern to find a real human, Twain a mirror to show we are worse than we think.

stoic-cosmopolitanism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
stoic-cosmopolitanism.title: 3. Star Trek as Philosophy Spock as Stoic Sage
stoic-cosmopolitanism.relation: Pigliucci argues that Gene Roddenberry built an implicit argument for Stoicism into Star Trek's Spock, contra both the 'suppressed emotion / stiff upper lip' caricature and Farren's claim that Kirk is the truer Stoic. Reading Spock's talk of 'emotion' as the disruptive pathe and his 'logic' as the broad Stoic study of reason, he shows Spock embodying the dichotomy of control ('my legs, they're broken'), the four cardinal virtues, and Stoic cosmopolitanism aboard the Enterprise. Drawing on Brouwer's account of the sage, he tracks Spock's development from prokopton toward sagehood, cultivating eupatheiai like love and friendship (the Wrath of Khan sacrifice) and declaring 'logic is the beginning of wisdom, not the end.'

williams-integrity.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
williams-integrity.title: “You Know . . . What They’re Up Against”
williams-integrity.relation: Dees finds moral ambiguity lurking in Star Wars' black-and-white universe: Han Solo's Hobbesian ethical egoism ('I take orders from just one person - me') is shown to be coherent and gradually transformed by friendship with Luke and Leia into commitment to a cause. Lando's betrayal of Han on Bespin is defended as a straightforward Mill-Bentham utilitarian choice by a responsible official, weighed against Bernard Williams's Jim-and-the-commandant integrity objection, which the author rejects as moral vanity. Count Dooku's apparent idealism is exposed as evil's tool, and Anakin's massacre of the Sand People is condemned as non-ambiguous barbarity via Kant's formula of humanity (and Hume on reason's role with the passions), leaving only late Vader as genuinely morally ambiguous.

williams-integrity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
williams-integrity.title: 11 - The Friendship that Makes No Demands
williams-integrity.relation: Tedesco sets Facebook's demand-free friendship against the modern moral requirement of impartiality, running from Godwin's burning-archbishop case through Bentham's 'everybody to count for one, nobody for more than one' and Williams's 'one thought too many' objection. He canvasses the escapes - Mill's rarely-demanded public benefactor, Singer's global village where aid is a click away, Jackson's sector plan and Railton's sophisticated consequentialism - and finds each inadequate to friendship's partiality. Facebook friendship looks like a third way that reconciles the two, but it turns out only to be friendship where it supplements a real offline relationship, so the impartiality problem stands.

williams-integrity.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
williams-integrity.title: 16. Female Integrity in Times of Change
williams-integrity.relation: Melanie Abbott combines Bernard Williams's view of integrity - publicly and consistently standing up for the beliefs that make you you - with Kant's good will to define a 'right sort' of holding fast that separates the virtuous woman from the fanatic, then tests it on five Crawley women. Sybil's unwavering egalitarianism (eloping with Branson, nursing, women's rights), Edith's uneven growth (the Gregson affair, journalism, her secrecy over Marigold at the Drewes' farm), Mary's shift from custom to moral agency (upholding Matthew's will, pig farming, standing up to Robert), Cora's quiet push for a voice, and even Violet's late flexibility show integrity as growth through change. The chapter's 'Sybil effect' is that the sister with the fewest doubts becomes the model the others gradually follow.

williams-integrity.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
williams-integrity.title: 2. How Can Torture Be This Funny
williams-integrity.relation: Pavelich asks how a sitcom about torture can be funny, answering with incongruity theory and Bergson's view of comedy as social punishment, seen in Tahani paired with a silent monk and Michael failing 802 reboots. The centerpiece is 'The Trolley Problem': Michael drops Chidi into Foot's thought experiment so Chidi becomes the instrument of his own agony, and by Bernard Williams's principle the real wrongdoer is Michael, who set up the situation. Eternal torture works as comedy only because everyday crappiness is watched on a twenty-two-minute scale, and Eleanor's forgiveness of Michael after seeing the tortures in Janet's VR makes her the show's real moral hero.

williams-integrity.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
williams-integrity.title: 16. Female Integrity in Times of Change
williams-integrity.relation: Melanie Abbott tests Bernard Williams's account of integrity - publicly and consistently standing up for the beliefs that make you you - merged with Kant's claim that only a good will is good without limitation, against five Crawley women across three generations. Sybil elopes with the socialist chauffeur Branson and never wavers in her egalitarian convictions, Edith's secrecy about her baby fails Williams's openness condition, Mary grows from custom-bound heiress into an estate manager who stands up to Robert over selling land, Cora chafes at the voice she surrendered as an American heiress, and even Violet eventually bends. The chapter's guiding question is how much truth and openness integrity requires, and it credits 'the Sybil effect' with spreading proper integrity through the whole family.

williams-integrity.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
williams-integrity.title: “Rebellions Are Built on Hope!”
williams-integrity.relation: Eberl asks whether Galen Erso, who knowingly resumed work on the Death Star while planting its exhaust-port flaw, is culpable for the deaths on Jedha, Scarif, and Alderaan. A utilitarian defense (his flaw net-saved the galaxy, per the negative-responsibility principle applied to the Death Star II 'Clerks' debate) founders on moral luck — everything depended on Luke's impossible shot — while Bernard Williams's integrity objection, via the chemist 'George' case, condemns his betrayal of conscience. The chapter finally deploys Thomistic tools for cooperation with evil: because Galen's contribution was mediate and remote (Tarkin ordered the firing, the gunners pulled the triggers, Leia's defiance provoked Alderaan's destruction) and the weapon would have been built without him, his collusion is justified by the reasonable hope — the 'new hope' — of the Death Star's destruction.

williams-integrity.title: Passionate Objectivity in Sherlock Holmes
williams-integrity.relation: Taliaferro and Le Gall pose the ethical clash between impartial detachment and partial loyalty, situating Holmes between Simon Keller (loyalty as a threat to being a 'good believer,' echoed by Holmes's 'Sign of Four' rejection of emotion) and Bernard Williams and Susan Wolf (who defend priority for loved ones—Williams's 'one thought too many'). Using Watson's shooting in 'The Three Garridebs,' Holmes's weaning off drugs, and 'perverted love' in the Sussex Vampire and Thor Bridge cases, they argue loyalty rightly understood as seeking the friend's good aids clear reasoning, and that Holmes exhibits a 'passionate objectivity' in which some acquaintance with passion is essential to being genuinely objective.

noble-lie.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
noble-lie.title: The Jedi Model
noble-lie.relation: Barad presents a handbook of Jedi virtue modeled on Plato's Republic: the Jedi are Plato's Guardians, trained through physical exercise and Socratic questioning to guard peace and justice. Aristotle's golden mean explains courage as the balance between Chewbacca's cowardly fear and Anakin's rash rush at Dooku, with Luke's decision to leave Dagobah counting as courage because it has just cause. Luke's Dagobah cave vision (Vader's mask opening to reveal his own face) is read as Plato's Cave allegory turned inward - self-knowledge of one's fear of becoming evil - while compassion and forgiveness, not forbidden attachment, complete the Jedi character. The chapter even defends Jedi mind tricks via Plato's noble lie (the myth of the metals) as manipulation of the weak-minded for the common good.

noble-lie.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
noble-lie.title: “Trust Your Feelings”
noble-lie.relation: Fader tackles the paradox that Jedi lie while Sith tell the truth: Obi-Wan's 'Darth Vader betrayed and murdered your father,' Yoda's trickster masquerade on Dagobah, the Council's cover-up of its waning powers, against Vader's brutal truth at Cloud City and Palpatine's technically honest 'I love democracy.' Kant's absolute prohibition of lying is set against the utilitarian's greatest-good lie and Nietzsche's claim that truth is the accepted set of social lies; Obi-Wan's deception is then defended through Plato's noble lie and the Buddha's Parable of the House on Fire, where 'expedients' to save the oblivious are no falsehood, while Vader and Dooku wield literal truths as weapons without compassion. Luke's answer is to stop accepting anyone's version and build his own green lightsaber: truth as perspective, intention, and finally the heart's understanding that redeems Anakin.

noble-lie.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
noble-lie.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Rollin opposes mandatory helmet laws by contrasting two conceptions of freedom: the Hobbesian absence-of-constraint view ('go to hell in my own way', from Pinocchio's 'no strings on me' to the trapped coyote) and the rational-order view running from Plato (ranked classes, noble lies, censorship, contempt for democracy) through Rousseau's 'forced to be free', which Popper already identified as the enemy of the open society. Since, as the obesity-as-disease example and Robert Paul Wolff's expert-government argument show, we cannot claim certainty about value judgments the way we can about fractures, paternalism fails: if danger justified coercion we would have to ban motorcycles, skiing, parachuting, and bull-riding alike. Helmet laws in effect claim society knows what you ought to want better than you do, and Rollin's answer to his British colleague's 'what will you do if you injure your brain?' is to join the Department of Food Science and Nutrition.

noble-lie.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
noble-lie.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Vaclavik follows Lyra's career as liar and trickster, from the Silvertongue performance that goads Iofur Raknison into fighting Iorek Byrnison, up to the reversal in the Land of the Dead where the harpy screams 'Liar!' and only true stories can feed the ghosts. She frames Lyra's boast that she is the best liar there ever was yet is not lying as a version of the Liar Paradox, then dissolves the puzzle by showing that lies continue after the katabasis (Will's comforting fib, Mrs. Coulter's noble treachery with Metatron) just as truth-telling appeared before it. Truth triumphs in the underworld not for its own sake but because it suits the audience: the dead need the world they have lost, so storytelling, truthful or invented, is judged by what it does for its listeners.

noble-lie.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
noble-lie.title: The Ugly
noble-lie.relation: Argues eugenics forces us to discard the 'noble lie' of egalitarian democracy we teach children for their own good, and shows the cost in Jason and Heather's contempt for 'ordinaries,' Jason's aging-obsessed narcissism, and the 'aristocratic values' that let him condemn his lover Heather to a labor camp without qualm. Police general Felix Buckman, demoted for compassion toward labor-camp inmates and later assassinated for criticizing the regime, embodies the democratic values the sixes' elitism destroys, with Marvel's X-Men as the analogy for a fractured next-generation humanity.

noble-lie.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
noble-lie.title: The Epistemology of Deception
noble-lie.relation: Shifts from the ethics of deception (Kant's near-absolute condemnation of lying versus Plato's morally justified governmental lies) to its epistemology, defining deception as intentionally causing a false belief. This definition explains why Cohaagen deceives Quaid, who falsely believes he is a construction worker, while Rekall cannot deceive the Quaid who really is a secret agent, and why the Zoner Cale merely misleads Spencer Olham in Impostor without deceiving him — with Hume's reasoning about miracle testimony modeling when to believe a probable deceiver.

noble-lie.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
noble-lie.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Greg Littmann maps Ape City onto Plato's Republic class by class: orangutan rulers who legislate, censor, and propagandize; gorilla warriors who enforce; chimpanzee producers who do all the work - including, pointedly, the science Plato made no provision for; and humans as the 'barbarians' Plato says may be enslaved or exterminated. The overlaps are detailed: the Sacred Scrolls' first article of faith functions as the noble lie's myth of the metals, orangutan funerals promise heaven to keep gorillas unafraid of death, and Zaius's erasing of Taylor's dust-writing and blowing up of the archaeological cave enact the rulers' duty to supervise stories. But the films also refute Plato: hereditary orangutans show that power corrupts philosopher kings, Dr. Honorius's 'reason' is dogma serving the faith, the gelding threat that finally breaks Taylor cracks the tripartite-soul analogy of justice, and democracy's rough virtue is that it lets us remove rulers 'without sticking anybody with iron spears.'

noble-lie.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
noble-lie.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Tom McBride reads the film through Wittgenstein's On Certainty: Dr. Zaius's certainties (flight is impossible, humans come from the forests) are hinge or riverbed propositions that cannot be doubted within the ape form of life, so Taylor's true story sounds not false but insane, like claiming to have slept on the moon. Speaking and able to prompt empirical investigation, Taylor fractures a foundational principle where G.E. Moore, facing a 'wild tribe' playing a different language game, could only confess that things 'stand fast' with him; and Zaius's explicit origin myth, a parallel to Plato's Myth of the Metals, is flimsy precisely because rulers who must insist on rules are not potent and are reduced to destroying the cave evidence. The genre's appeal is Margaret Atwood's 'controlled hallucination': crazy doors that swing on safe hinges, rivers that still have stable beds.

noble-lie.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
noble-lie.title: Psych and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Stephenson tests Shawn's ruse against the major theories of justified deceit and finds it wanting: Plato's Myth of the Metals excuses paternalistic noble lies for social harmony that Shawn's self-aggrandizing motives cannot claim, utilitarianism collapses on the long-term costs of exposure (Gus, Juliet, Henry, and the SBPD condemned by association; clients betrayed; trust in law enforcement eroded), Kant's universalizability test sinks maxims like 'lie whenever a career opportunity is at stake,' and Popper's open society condemns just the deceit on which the psychic brand runs. Even the mutual-deceit analogy to poker and Sissela Bok's reasonable-person publicity test fail, since no public forum of reasonable people would bless duping paying private clients. The escape is extra-moral: Shawn's mischievous hokum is the socially necessary boundary-pusher, whose lesson against unreflective occult belief lands best when delivered with a laugh.

noble-lie.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
noble-lie.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Cam Cobb weighs Battle School against competing philosophies of education: Plato's Republic supplies vocational sorting by natural aptitude (complete with the myth of the metals as a 'noble lie'), while Socratic dialogue and Paulo Freire's problem-posing pedagogy demand the shared critical inquiry Ender never gets. He argues Graff's curriculum is almost purely vocational - military history, tactics, the Giant's Drink, battleroom drills - leaving no liberal paideia, and that the teachers' constant rule-changing leaves Ender feeling like 'someone's pawn,' exactly the banking-style teacher domination Freire warned against.

noble-lie.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
noble-lie.title: 15. The Way of the Doctor Is Deception
noble-lie.relation: Dodge takes Rule #1 - the Doctor lies - through the major theories of lying: Bernard Williams's definition (asserting what you believe false with intent to deceive), Aristotle's claim that all lies are base, Kant's categorical imperative and respect for persons (even the Vinvocci's shimmer disguises in 'The End of Time' abuse trust), and Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus, which condemns the faked death at Lake Silencio ('The Impossible Astronaut') for the grief it caused Amy and Rory yet rewards the greater happiness it made possible. Against the absolutists he sets Plato's Noble Lie from the Republic - the elite falsehood that keeps society functioning - as what the Doctor emulates by deceiving the universe into thinking him dead ('The Wedding of River Song'), and Nietzsche's point in Human, All Too Human that lying is ethically neutral when the pretense is sustainable, as when the Doctor hides the ganger-Amy switch from Rory ('The Almost People'). The upshot: the Doctor's lies are wrong in themselves but routinely justified by the good they do, which is why sometimes the hero lies.

noble-lie.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
noble-lie.title: 20. The Doctor Lies
noble-lie.relation: McCain distinguishes lying (directly asserting what you believe false to make another believe it) from mere deception - the Sixth Doctor feeding Jamie false information for Sontaran Stike to overhear in 'The Two Doctors' deceives without lying - then asks whether the Doctor can lie to himself, answering that incarnations can lie to later selves (the Eleventh's suspicious 'I have absolutely no idea' about the children on Gallifrey in 'The Day of the Doctor') but a current self cannot. The stakes are moral: against Kant's and Augustine's absolute prohibition of lying, Plato's Republic and Sidgwick's Methods of Ethics defend noble lies, and Robert C. Solomon's view of self-deception as coping with the unbearable suggests that if the Doctor did engineer himself to forget the Time War genocide - as Ten and Wilf did to Donna in 'Journey's End' - it might be a good man's forgivable way of going on.

noble-lie.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
noble-lie.title: 8. Plato’s Chicago
noble-lie.relation: Littmann systematically maps Roth's Chicago onto Plato's Republic: like Marcus, Plato rejects democracy after Athens executed Socrates; both dissolve the family ('faction before blood' versus children raised in common and bred by state schedule); Erudite's IQ-selected leadership mirrors the rigorously trained philosopher-rulers, Dauntless the warrior class whose purely physical training Plato warns turns 'savage and harsh,' Abnegation's poverty the guardians's communism of property, and the factionless the powerless producers - with Plato's noble lie about the metals matching the Erudite's propaganda and serums as instruments of control. The shared flaw, he argues, is concentrated power without external checks, which corrupted Abnegation, corrupts every Dauntless leadership change, and would corrupt Plato's guardians too. The lesson is not to hand power to the least vicious but for democratic voters to confront their own ignorance - or end like Roth's America, in apocalyptic war.

noble-lie.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
noble-lie.title: 15. The Serious Monk’s Guide to Re-writing History
noble-lie.relation: Framed as a monkey monk-to-be telling four bored children the 'history' of four Discworld novels, the chapter argues that history is not a record of what happened but a constructed narrative: in Wyrd Sisters the Duchess commissions Hwel's play to rewrite the murder of the king, since 'the past is what people remember, and memories are words.' In Small Gods, Brutha's photographic memory of Ephebe's burning library shows that even perfect recollection is lost unless written down, while in Thief of Time the History Monks openly rebuild time as a patchwork after the Big Crash, and Susan watches historians 'rebuilt the image of the past to suit the eyesight of today.' Drawing on W. H. Walsh's idea of history as intelligible narrative, it concludes that history is performative—what people are told it is—and that we ourselves are the crowbar that opens the box of history from the inside.

noble-lie.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
noble-lie.title: 9. Pierce’s Republic
noble-lie.relation: Randall Jensen maps the Society onto Plato's Republic (Brown has said he drew on it): the Color hierarchy parallels the Myth of the Metals' gold, silver, and bronze souls, the Golds' scorn for Demokracy echoes Book VIII's account of degeneration into tyranny, and Leto's 'We are Plato's philosopher kings' claims a mantle Plato himself doubted anyone could ever fill.
