Darrow's story is the Allegory of the Cave run from below—a Helldiver literally raised in a mine, blinded by surface light, whose return to a shrunken, grayer garden mirrors the philosopher's homecoming—except Plato never imagined the prisoner carved into a Gold. The Noble Lie survives as the terraforming myth fed to lowReds while the surface has been habitable for centuries, and the chapter weighs Darrow's gospel ('we choose who we are') against Plato's caveats: you can choose who to be only within limits, if you are lucky and greatly helped.

noble-lie.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
noble-lie.title: 10. Virtue Rising
noble-lie.relation: Darci Doll argues the Rising exposes the Society's intellectual oppression—each Color denied education and fed 'noble lies' about its role—and that lifting it sparks an 'Intellectual Reformation' proving Color does not dictate potential: Darrow out-performing Golds, Orion the un-carved Blue, Ragnar and Sefi exceeding their station. She uses Plato's Republic (producers, auxiliaries, guardians, the lower orders kept obedient by Noble Lies like the Reds' terraforming myth) as the Society's blueprint, then turns to Aristotle: potential is realized only through the right environment, instruction, and habituated character, and Darrow's practical wisdom—testing himself, reassessing after Titus and Cassius, doing what makes him his best self—lets him flourish and lead. Aristotle's critique of utility-only relations explains why the Society's alliances expire (Antonia executed once useless) while Darrow and Mustang's virtue friendships and just rule endure, opening a society where everyone, including women and lowColors denied opportunity rather than ability, can maximize potential.

noble-lie.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
noble-lie.title: 5. Ministry of Truth Handbook Excerpt on the Strategic Use of Fallacious Reasoning for Thoughtcrime Prevention
noble-lie.relation: Rard's satirical Party handbook explains how to keep a population from thinking: keep the proles too poor and exhausted to reason, and deploy fallacies strategically, from ad hominem goat-caricatures of Goldstein at the Two Minutes Hate and straw man versions of his arguments, to destroying contrary evidence, appealing to fear of the old capitalist world, and Room 101's appeal to force, so false beliefs can be manufactured as easily as true ones. It presents Plato's noble lie as the Ministry's founding inspiration, calling the reader's mission 'a continuation of Plato's dream'. It also cites Aristotle's view that emotion must be disciplined for reason to work, which the Party inverts by deliberately triggering fear and hatred to disable rational thought.

noble-lie.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
noble-lie.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Fallis uses Sheldon — a lousy liar with an elaborate theory of lying — to probe the philosophy of lying: Kant's absolute prohibition (even 'out of frivolity'), Bok's presumption against deceit, Plato's noble lies reserved for philosopher kings, and Nietzsche's self-deceiving overmen, whose counsel explains the 'un-unravelable webs' of fake Facebook and blog evidence for the imaginary cousin Leopold Houston. Ryle's knowing-how versus knowing-that split explains how Sheldon can state the rules ('casually, no rapid breathing') yet botch the performance, while the Bazinga! pranks and the insincere courtroom apology break the Augustinian definition that lying requires intent to deceive. Grice's norms of conversation then ground the author's own definition — lying as intending to violate the norm against saying what you believe false — until a hypothetical, convention-oblivious liar like Kripke forces him to concede a counterexample and admit he was wrong.

noble-lie.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
noble-lie.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Cooke defends his three-year campaign of a lawful evil wizard (Oraximon, who magic-missiled an innkeeper and hid the bodies in a rope trick) against religious and secular critics. The epistemic charge fails because rulebooks are invitations to imagine, not assertions, and the Smurfs-as-Krishna example shows an 'attitude for export' needs authorial evidence D&D lacks; Hume's twin claims about the impropriety of imaginatively endorsing flawed sentiments are dismantled by splitting Can'tians from Won'tians over Gendler's stories and defending a 'Hardian' view on which resistance is just difficulty, making imaginative resistance a chimera. The causal charge fails on the evidence (the Werther effect and its video-game and jazz cousins are post hoc plus confirmation bias), the character-warping charge risks the unfalsifiability of the repressed-desire diagnosis, and Plato's ban on the arts — enforced via the noble lie — would be the price if imagining were as bad as doing.

noble-lie.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
noble-lie.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Cam Cobb pits Socratic critical inquiry and Plato's Republic-style vocational streaming (classes sorted by the 'myth of the metals,' sold through a noble lie) against the Battle School curriculum, which is almost purely vocational and lacks the music, poetry, and liberal paideia that harmonize the soul. Testing Socrates' dialogic method, Dewey's aptitude-tracking education, and Freire's problem-posing alternative against the battleroom, the Giant's Drink, and Graff's secretly rewritten game rules, Cobb concludes Ender's schooling mixes conflicting pedagogies and ends in the teacher domination Freire feared, crystallized in Ender's lament 'I've spent my life as someone's pawn.'

noble-lie.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
noble-lie.title: NOTES
noble-lie.relation: First defines lying — distinguishing it from mere error (Angela believing Peter dead), from the Haitian's non-verbal memory-wipe deception, and from Hiro's silent staging of Ando's fake death — then tests moral theories against the show's liars. Kant's categorical imperative bans all lying but is abandoned when Sylar demands a friend's hiding place; utilitarianism vindicates Victoria Pratt's lie about the virus vial yet also licenses Linderman's .07% explosion and Plato's noble lie of the earthborn metals, which the chapter rejects. Machiavelli's advice that princes may lie to keep power is played out by 'President Sylar' in 'Five Years Gone,' and the chapter finally endorses Sissela Bok's presumption against lying — a public-reasoning procedure modeled by Bob Bishop and Mohinder before Monica's virus injection.

noble-lie.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
noble-lie.title: Over Four Thousand Words to Say No
noble-lie.relation: Spanakos asks whether Stark's assembling, disassembling, and reassembling of the Avengers and his unseen-hand management of Civil War make him the Republic's philosopher guardian, and answers no. Tony fits the surface profile — the gold-souled ruler of Socrates' noble lie, the elite training, indifference to money, the technê of an MIT engineer who envisions the future — but he lacks epistêmê: he never climbs from the cave's shadows to grasp the forms of justice and the good, and his appetites (womanizing in The Ultimates, 'Demon in a Bottle') show a soul where passion is not ruled by reason. His puppet mastery is reactive problem-solving guided by each situation, not philosophy, and reading him as a philosopher king is our failure to read The Republic meditatively, as Ortega y Gasset urged.

noble-lie.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
noble-lie.title: The Office and Philosophy
noble-lie.relation: Tests the deceptions swirling around Dwight: Kant's two arguments against lying (universalizing the maxim 'lie whenever it saves face', and treating the deceived as a mere means) are set against Plato's noble lie from the Republic - Michael's empty 'Assistant Regional Manager' title may be a morally tolerable verbal lie because after 'The Fight' it restores their friendship, though it does not medicate the office as Plato's lie does the city. Epicurus' claim that only what is experienced can harm you ('what you don't know can't hurt you') is refuted by the thought of Angela's hypothetical fake love for Dwight: undetected deception is itself a harm. Finally Dwight's self-deception (believing the false promotion, Jim's telekinesis prank, the fax from his future self) is modeled by dividing the self - Plato's tripartite soul versus Descartes' simple, indivisible mind - suggesting cognitive science's modular brain as the better picture, and asking whether one can even wrong oneself.

noble-lie.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
noble-lie.title: Notes
noble-lie.relation: MacMullan argues Darth Plagueis is a paradox for Plato: wisdom as reason ruling spirit and appetite should be impossible for a Sith who feeds on passion, yet Plagueis stays patient, restrained, and rational for over a century. He reads Sidious's 'I will make it legal' and the Sith Code as Thrasymachus's 'justice is the advantage of the stronger,' and notes Plagueis even shares Plato's noble lie and eugenic breeding programs. Finding that Plato's prediction of self-destruction fails for Plagueis, the chapter turns to Nietzsche: master morality, the will to power, and life beyond good and evil better explain a Sith who cherishes bodily life and seeks to conquer death where Yoda and Socrates calmly disdain 'crude matter.'

noble-lie.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
noble-lie.title: Notes
noble-lie.relation: Barkman and Alkema map Plato's Republic onto the fall of the Old Republic: the bickering Senate and Anakin's 'someone wise' exchange with Padme enact democracy's degeneration into tyranny, with Palpatine as Plato's werewolf-like protector-tyrant and Dooku's Sith name 'Tyranus' marking Thrasymachus's justice-as-strength as Sith doctrine. The Jedi approximate Plato's philosopher-guardians - courageous, temperate, reluctant to rule, surrendering their children to the Temple much like the Republic's breeding deceptions and noble lies. Justice as each part doing its own work applies to the tripartite soul as much as the state, and the chapter closes that democracy survives Endor but only if truth stays a beacon of the light side.

noble-lie.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
noble-lie.title: Nietzsche’s Overman as Posthuman Star Child in 2001 A Space Odyssey Jerold J. Abrams
noble-lie.relation: Abrams reads 2001 as a cinematic staging of Nietzsche's Thus Spoke Zarathustra, mapping the film's ape-to-human-to-Star-Child arc onto Zarathustra's evolutionary vision of the overman. He casts the discovery of the buried moon monolith as Kubrick's death of God (proving aliens, not God, seeded us) maintained by a Platonic noble lie, the astronauts as Nietzsche's higher men, and Bowman's decadent hotel-room decline plus Poole's fall as the last man and the dying tightrope walker. He then argues the prophecy may come true not via aliens but through Kurzweil's Singularity and Moravec's posthuman 'mind children'.

noble-lie.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
noble-lie.title: 2. Socrates’s City and Seldon’s Galaxy
noble-lie.relation: Goldberg maps Plato's Republic onto Asimov's Foundation Trilogy: Socrates's three-class city (Guardians, Auxiliaries, Producers ruling by knowledge of the Forms) parallels Seldon's galaxy (Second Foundationers, First Foundationers, and everyone else, ruling by the abstract mathematics of psychohistory), with the tyrannical Thrasymachus paralleling the Mule. He shows the Prime Radiant functions as Plato's Allegory of the Cave, and that both Guardians and Second Foundationers govern through 'noble lies' (the metals myth; the Encyclopedia sham and the Second Foundation's fake destruction), then questions whether those lies are truly noble given doubts about objective truth.

noble-lie.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
noble-lie.title: 17. Psychohistory’s Noble Lie
noble-lie.relation: Silcox explains why readers forgive Seldon's confessed lie that the Encyclopedia Galactica 'is a fraud, and always has been' by comparing it to Socrates's noble lie in Plato's Republic, which Popper and I.F. Stone condemn as antidemocratic. He contrasts the two—Socrates's lie preserves an existing kallipolis while Seldon's brings about a distant political goal that requires trusting psychohistory—and weighs them against modern transparency doctrines: Bentham's consequentialist case for publicity and Rawls's publicity condition grounding autonomy, plus Nguyen's worry that transparency distorts expert 'cognitive islands.' He concludes that a genuinely predictive science of history might rationally lead us to treat political transparency as negotiable, which is why Hari Seldon remains a noble hero despite 'engineering the narrative.'

noble-lie.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
noble-lie.title: 7. Anthony Bourdain’s Extremely Objectionable Stories
noble-lie.relation: Holmes examines Bourdain's horror graphic novel Hungry Ghosts as cautionary folklore in the tradition of Aesop and EC Comics. He stages a debate between Aristotle, who in the Rhetoric endorses fables as accessible moral tools, and Plato, who in the Republic wants to censor frightening tales for children — yet Holmes shows Plato himself (Euthyphro, Laws) praised fear as 'modesty,' and notes Bourdain used cautionary tales (Ronald McDonald 'has cooties') to steer his own daughter from fast food.

noble-lie.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
noble-lie.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
noble-lie.relation: Johnson argues that the Santa Claus lie is immoral and should be abandoned, giving three reasons: it is deceptive lying (Kant's absolute prohibition is too strong, but the lie lacks life-saving justification and functions as a Platonic 'noble lie' no more noble than a cult leader's); Santa robs parents of credit and warps children's moral development and trust, illustrated by anguished 'finding out' stories and Virginia O'Hanlon's letter; and it damages credulity, invoking Clifford's 'Ethics of Belief' against belief on insufficient evidence while James's 'Will to Believe' cannot rescue Santa since evidence against him is overwhelming. He recommends revealing the truth early, even via a Socratic-Method questioning game.

noble-lie.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
noble-lie.title: 29. Frank Herbert’s Dune as Philosophy The Need to Think for Yourself
noble-lie.relation: Reading the Sci Fi Channel miniseries Frank Herbert's Dune and Children of Dune, Littmann argues the saga warns against letting leaders or religions think for us: Paul Atreides fakes being the Fremen Mahdi, wages a holy war, and founds a theocratic tyranny that Alia and Leto II carry to worse extremes. He sets Plato's Republic (the guardian class, the noble lie, rule by the wise) and Hobbes against pro-democracy thinkers—Locke's consent and natural rights, Mill's harm principle, Dewey's democracy—then cites Locke, Paine and Russell on religion's dangers, closing with W.K. Clifford's 'ethics of belief' that one must not accept religious claims without sufficient evidence. The chapter reads Paul's dictatorship and the Bene Gesserit's engineered messiah as dramatizations of the historical abuses of concentrated and religious power.

noble-lie.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
noble-lie.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
noble-lie.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable. He tests the orchestrated revolution against utilitarianism's greatest-happiness principle (Bentham, Mill's taxation-of-the-wealthy, Singer's impartiality) and against Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle versus Nozick's entitlement objection and Aquinas's just-war criteria, concluding each character's actions can be read as 'just,' which exposes anthropocentrism as the real veil.

speciesism.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
speciesism.title: Restoring Balance to the Force
speciesism.relation: Cooke uncovers an environmental ethic in Star Wars: after surveying anthropocentric resource-management views and Singer's anti-speciesism (Luke blithely shooting womprats, the Geonosian arena's abused beasts), she builds the chapter on Holmes Rolston III's claims that organisms and ecosystems have intrinsic value and that value is systemic and holistic. The 'living Force' - life creates it, midi-chlorians live symbiotically in all cells - makes Jedi training a discipline of respecting nature, exemplified by Yoda's mud hut on Dagobah and the self-sufficient Gungan and Ewok eco-communities that defeat droid armies and stormtroopers. Restoring balance to the Force therefore means restoring symbiotic balance between human culture and the natural world, which the chapter links to Leopold-style land-ethic holism of the biotic community.

speciesism.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
speciesism.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Detmer argues moral vegetarianism follows from principles nearly everyone accepts — cruelty, the infliction of unnecessary or disproportionate suffering, is wrong — and that Atkins, which escalates meat eating without being necessary for weight loss, fails both his necessity and proportion tests. Rebutting human superiority, he deploys Rachels's point that no single feature like language is relevant to every difference in treatment and Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', holds factory-farm castration without anesthetic up against the civet-cat musk trade his students already condemn, and answers Narveson's appeal to intuition and the appeal to tradition. Even granting Atkins maximal health benefits, the margin over a well-planned vegetarian diet (Denmark's WWI blockade, the Framingham data) cannot justify the animal suffering, world-hunger, and environmental costs — most of that case drawn from Singer's Animal Liberation.

speciesism.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
speciesism.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
speciesism.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman contrasts two pop-culture templates: Buffy's vampire brothel, where willing humans pay vampires for consensual bites (Giles calls the customers 'willing victims'), and Blade's implied government blood bank, where humans are forced to donate. Running Robert Nozick's personhood criteria (sentience, rationality, free will, moral agency, soul) against vampires, he argues no standard admits humans while excluding them, so staking vampires violates rights and, on Singer's suffering-equals-suffering logic, refusing consideration is a kind of speciesism. The welfarist side - Singer and Unger's principle that we must prevent bad at little cost, as in the drowning child - would mandate Blade-style forced blood transfers, but Whitman contends such coercion breeds the very xenophobia (Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules, anti-immigrant welfare politics) that blocks recognizing vampire personhood. Only a libertarian market of voluntary exchange turns human-vampire relations from a zero-sum war into a positive-sum commerce.

speciesism.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
speciesism.title: Hedging Our Bets
speciesism.relation: Kind asks whether humanoid Cylons have moral status, using Warren's stone-versus-child contrast to show that the Fleet's blender-and-toaster attitude (Roslin airlocking Leoben, Fisk's 'you can't rape a machine') rests on the unargued assumption that Cylons are mere machines. Singer's anti-speciesism grounds status in sentience (Gina's suffering, even Scar the Raider), while Regan's subject-of-a-life criteria are met by rational, self-aware Cylons; Helo's 'no human could do the things they've done' argument fails because humans commit equal evils, as the legal limits on punishing criminals show. Since we cannot rule Cylon status out, she closes with Pascal's Wager: treat them as morally considerable, because the asymmetry of error costs us our moral compass.

speciesism.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
speciesism.title: Seeing Ourselves Reflected Back
speciesism.relation: Gray asks whether Cylons deserve moral consideration, starting from Kant's demand to treat humanity never merely as a means: the New Caprica suicide bombings and Adama's plan to weaponize a Cylon virus treat captives merely as means, while Helo's sabotage of 'A Measure of Salvation' acknowledges their intrinsic value. D'Anna's dissent before being boxed and Athena's defection for Helo show the rational autonomy Kant's personhood requires; if that is dismissed as programming, Singer's sentience criterion (Leoben tortured, Gina catatonic) and Warren's multi-criterial personhood — including Boomer's 'I have a conscience' in 'Downloaded' — still open personhood to Cylons. The chapter ends on the humans' double standard (Athena accepted, guns drawn on Caprica Six) as a mirror for our own treatment of uncertain others.

speciesism.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
speciesism.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
speciesism.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman uses Buffy's vampire brothel (humans paying vampires to feed on willing victims, as Giles concedes) and Blade's mandatory blood bank as two models of human-vampire coexistence to stage the clash between libertarianism (Nozick, Lomasky, Schmidtz) and welfarism (Singer, Unger, G.A. Cohen). He runs vampire personhood through Nozick's criteria from Anarchy, State, and Utopia — sentience, self-consciousness, rationality, free will, moral personality, soul — and argues no standard includes humans while excluding vampires, applying Singer's equal-consideration-of-suffering principle across kinds of beings. He then extends Singer's obligation-to-aid reasoning (rescuing a drowning child vs. donating to UNICEF) to show welfarism would mandate forced blood transfers or 'blood stamps', and argues via Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules and modern welfare-based anti-immigration politics that the burden of supporting dependents breeds exclusion. Only the libertarian brothel model of voluntary exchange, he concludes, turns vampire-human relations into a positive-sum game in which humans would actually come to recognize vampires as persons.

speciesism.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
speciesism.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
speciesism.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

speciesism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
speciesism.title: They May Not Be Human, but Could Daleks Be People Too
speciesism.relation: The chapter reads the Daleks' hunt for the 'human factor' in 'The Evil of the Daleks' and for human DNA in 'Dalek' and 'Daleks in Manhattan' as species essentialism — an Aristotelian picture of a fixed human nature, resurrected as genetic essentialism — set against philosophical alternatives of species as individuals or sets and Mayr's reproductive-isolation criterion applied to Daleks and Thals. It then asks whether the human-Dalek Dalek Sec could count as a person, using Singer's speciesism to argue that rights should track personhood (capacities for pain, intelligence) rather than bare membership in Homo sapiens.

speciesism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
speciesism.title: Why the Doctor Is So Special
speciesism.relation: Applying Singer's animal-liberation concept of speciesism — judging moral worth by capacity to feel pain rather than by intelligence or likeness — the authors argue the Daleks are 'super-speciesist' and that Lumic's emotional inhibitors make the Cybermen the same failure, unable to share a universe with unlike beings. Since emotions are judgments that can be educated into fitting responses (Nussbaum, Aristotle), and since Daleks infused with Rose's or Diagoras's DNA collapse into empathetic beings, the chapter concludes that emotion and empathy are why the Daleks will never win and why the Doctor, marked by his companions, is special among Time Lords.

speciesism.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
speciesism.title: Specimen Watching
speciesism.relation: Jason Davis applies Adorno's 'identity thinking' - the way concepts swallow particulars as specimens of the already-known - to argue Dexter is a consumer of serial killers who never asks what makes his victims what they are, only that they fit the type, from therapist Emmett Meridian on down. The same concept-machine works on animals: Buddy's buried bones and the show's predator imagery exploit the criminological animal-abuse link, letting Davis ask whether cruelty-taskforce laws quietly practice speciesism; and Carol J. Adams' sexual politics of meat connects the Ice Truck Killer's blood-drained, butcher-cut women to a meat-eating culture whose objectification makes women and animals interchangeable. Finally, the chapter notes that the women of Dexter - Deb, Rita, LaGuerta, Lila, Christine - are all written without female friendship, a homosocial specimen-class whose sameness feminist philosophers expose, so that when Dexter 'takes back the night', the 'invisible hookers' stay invisible.

speciesism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
speciesism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Delfino and Taylor ask whether Morgan's zombified wife is still a person, which decides whether shooting her is murder. On the dominant Western view - Boethius's 'individual substance of a rational nature', Aquinas's image-of-God intellect, Kantian dignity against Singer's speciesism challenge - walkers lack intelligence and so are not persons, so Morgan should shoot. They then argue walkers are metaphysically impossible beings, square-circles: dead tissue that somehow sees, smells, and runs down prey without functioning organs, energy intake, or the reanimated neocortex that movement and sensation require. Zombies fascinate because they are projections of our fears - dead yet moving, an afterlife of horror - a Hamlet-like caught-between-being-and-nonbeing.

speciesism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
speciesism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Sara Waller argues the films show language operating as a tyranny that measures minds and withholds moral standing: Dodge mocking signing Caesar as a 'stupid monkey,' Zaius dismissing Taylor's speech as mimicry, 1894 literacy tests used to disenfranchise Black voters, and IQ tests whose vocabulary sections double-count language skill. She surveys the non-linguistic tests the apes face - the Hopkins dexterity test, the Wisconsin Multiphasic, Kohler's banana-and-boxes task ('Because I loathe bananas'), the Lucas Tower, Caesar's cookie-jar deception - and then deploys Quine's 'gavagai' inscrutability of reference to argue that speech cannot be the ultimate measure of intelligence or moral worth. Nova's hand over Taylor's mouth and Zira and Cornelius's 'be clever... be quiet' suggest that under oppression, silence is the smart play.

speciesism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
speciesism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Travis Timmerman argues the series dramatizes Singer's equal consideration of interests: Zira frees Taylor once he writes 'My name is Taylor' because like interests must count equally regardless of species, while Dr. Zaius's erasing the writing, lobotomizing Landon, and destroying the cave artifacts is pure speciesism in Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' sense. He rejects the crude 'humans are smarter' argument (it would strip severely cognitively disabled humans of standing) and Nussbaum's species-normal version (it would permit caging Zira and Cornelius since normal apes are mute), then deploys Plato's Euthyphro dilemma against Locke-style God-given rights: a deity bellowing that human interests outrank ape interests is arbitrary unless grounded in independent reasons. Since farming severely cognitively disabled humans is obviously wrong and species membership is morally irrelevant, it is equally wrong to factory-farm and experiment on animals - so, like Caesar in Battle for the Planet of the Apes, become vegetarian.

speciesism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
speciesism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Jonas-Sebastien Beaudry defends a 'moderate speciesism' built on relationships rather than individual capacities: Taylor's trial strips him of clothes, name, and speech - the symbols of ethical community - showing how institutional speciesism rationalizes domination behind the Sacred Scrolls' Declaration-of-Independence-style self-evidence. Against Singer's anti-speciesist challenge that any distinctively human capacity is shared by some animals or missing from some humans, he argues both camps wrongly pedestal intrinsic traits, and reads Taylor's love for the mute Nova together with the failed Project Nim as showing that within-species bonds of love, care, and family are genuinely and justifiably valuable without licensing mistreatment. Bernard Williams's 'The Human Prejudice' - should we surrender to superior invading aliens? - marks where impartial anti-speciesism leads, while Zaius's 'Man is evil' and the doomsday-bomb ending show extreme speciesism as self-fulfilling prophecy.

speciesism.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
speciesism.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Norva Lo and Andrew Brennan set Richard Routley's 'last man' thought experiment beside Taylor's triggering of the doomsday bomb in Beneath the Planet of the Apes: both ask whether wiping out every living thing would be wrong once no humans remain to be harmed, which basic human chauvinism cannot condemn. The chapter argues the act is wrong from both sides: non-anthropocentrism counts the apes, mutants, and horses as intrinsically valuable beings, and even human-centered standards condemn it, since the talking apes and mutants are Locke's rational persons and Nova's people are biologically human, making Taylor's outburst 'you damned dirty ape' a form of speciesism. Taylor emerges not as simply mad or evil but as the Cold War logic of mutually assured destruction made flesh, a warning that excessive self-interest, personal or species-level, is itself the danger.

speciesism.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
speciesism.title: Futurama and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Von Gunten asks whether Bender, Calculon, and the robot mafia have moral worth, arguing first that they are sentient: behavioral similarity plus functional equivalence (pain as electric signals in neurons or circuits) defeat both behavior-only objections (the Sphex wasp's preprogrammed loop, knife-avoiding toy robots) and composition-based prejudice - Fry's 'I'm all squishy and flabby' defense at the Hal Institute - which would be 'biologism' analogous to racism. He then distinguishes moral patiency (Nibbler can be harmed but only behaviorally reinforced) from moral agency (deliberation and accountability), concluding that Bender's flexible life - Iron Cook, wrestling, folk music with Beck's head, jacking-on addiction - shows robots transcend their programming as humans transcend evolutionary presets. Limiting moral status to biology or species would be speciesism, so the thirty-first century's robots deserve the full protections and responsibilities humans have.

speciesism.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
speciesism.title: Futurama and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: The chapter uses 'The Problem with Popplers' to map the real-world ethics of eating meat: Free Waterfall Jr.'s 'You shouldn't eat things that feel pain' restates Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's equal consideration of suffering; Fishy Joe's profits-first stance echoes agro-ecological defenses of meat eating; and Leela's 'eating an intelligent animal is different' voices the common intuition Singer condemns as speciesism. The food-chain justification collapses when the Omicronians claim the apex and demand 198 billion humans in return, and Bender's 'fight to the death and I'll cook the loser' flips the diner's perspective, while Waterfall's orangutan-for-Leela trade sets up Singer's future-directed preferences distinction from Practical Ethics as a possible rescue. The chapter ends on the episode's real target: gluttonous consumption ('stuff the ship!') and the arbitrary sentimentality governing what we will and won't eat.

speciesism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
speciesism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Littmann argues that stripped of religious scruple, Shelley's own supreme virtue - kindness, embodied in Victor's family, Elizabeth, Clerval, and the cottagers - actually supports creating artificial life: the monster is benevolent until mistreated, and superior corpse-people would be a race of geniuses rather than a threat we may preemptively suppress. The monster himself invents utilitarianism ('relative as they were, as I applied them, to pleasure and pain alone'), De Lacey nearly lives it by promising the stranger rehabilitation over punishment, but Victor's case against building a mate is exposed as speciesism - he tallies unborn humans' futures while ignoring the joys of unborn cadaver folk, though utilitarians were the first to speak for animal rights. Since intelligent otherness is humanity's only chance at non-human friendship and the risks of Prometheus's fire paid off, the chapter rewrites the modern Prometheus as a blessing and ends with a re-imagined creation scene where the monster says 'I love you' to a Victor who finally names him Nigel.

speciesism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
speciesism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Nicolas Michaud argues the creature is a person on every serious criterion: it satisfies Kant's rationality test and Mary Anne Warren's five criteria (consciousness, reasoning, self-motivated activity, communication, self-concept) in both Shelley's novel and I, Frankenstein, and it possesses all ten of Nussbaum's capabilities for flourishing. The twist is that judging the monster a blameworthy murderer already concedes the personhood we deny him, while our exclusion of him is bare Othering and speciesism of the kind Tom Regan attacks in animal ethics. Michaud ends by reversing the question: after humanity's record of crushing minorities, which the creature learns from Volney's Ruins of Empires and weeps over with Safie, what argument could Victor give Adam for sparing us?

speciesism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
speciesism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: King charges human exceptionality with being speciesism and asks whether dinosaurs are persons rather than humans, testing Kant's rationality criterion and Descartes' denial of animal thought against the raptor that opens the shed door and the T. rex that spins the Explorer searching for prey. He runs the dinosaurs through Mary Anne Warren's five personhood criteria, then plays his Wittgenstein trump card: animal language would be the language of a different life-form, so the raptors' calls expressing fear and summoning help count as real communication without words. He closes with Regan's rights view, arguing that the cow and goat feeding scenes, like past denials of personhood to Native Americans and women, should shame us into showing a little respect.

speciesism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
speciesism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Christopher Ketcham writes a mock chronicle in which velociraptors escape to inhabited Nava, deliberately avoid humans, and over decades learn to share a hunting language with a Congo tribe, asking whether we would ever grant such beings equal intelligence and rights. He reads raptor pack behavior and cooperation through Dawkins's selfish gene, and uses Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' to argue we can never peer into raptor consciousness, just as we brand human races inferior without looking. Citing Plessy v. Ferguson's whiteness-as-property and Mill's point that mistreating animals belongs in the same category as racial discrimination, he ends with a senate-hearing parody and the Neanderthal precedent: a human 'superiority gene' means coexistence with smart raptors would likely end as it did for them.

speciesism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
speciesism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Kenn Fisher reads the franchise as the extinction of the Great Chain of Being: from Plato's humans mid-way between gods and beasts, through Genesis dominion and Descartes's non-conscious animals, to Malcolm's 'God creates man. Man destroys God. Man creates dinosaurs' - with computers (Hammond's control room, Wikipedia, Google) replacing God at the top. He then tracks animals' ascent from property: Francione on welfare versus personhood, Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', and Singer's equality-as-prescription, applied to Dieter Stark tasering a compy (punished by the compys) versus the unexamined electric fences that keep InGen's 'zoo animals' caged. He closes with Carol Adams's meat-masculinity link - Roland Tembo will hunt only a male T. rex, the dinosaurs are all female - and holds up vegetarian Lex as hope that the Chain bends into a Circle.

speciesism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
speciesism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Roger Hunt argues the films show that whoever assumes human superiority or ownership of created life gets eaten: Dieter Stark zaps a compy and is devoured by a swarm of them, Ludlow claims InGen's patent and becomes a hunting lesson for the baby T. rex. He stages the real debate over dinosaur moral status between the 'value of life' view (Harding and Sattler: experiment on them if enough sentient beings benefit) and Tom Regan's rights view - anything sentient has basic rights from unconditional individual value, and grading lives by usefulness is speciesism like racism or sexism. He then prefers Martha Nussbaum's capabilities approach: a T. rex penned in San Diego cannot roam, hunt, or play, so it cannot flourish, and the point is not granting rights but recognizing we have no right to block other beings' flourishing for fun.

speciesism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
speciesism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Littmann turns vampirism into a thought experiment against meat-eating, using Jonathan's delight in the Hotel Royale chicken as the double standard: every justification for the Count preying on humans - might makes right, his superior intelligence and cunning, an arbitrary threshold of cleverness, or the human soul and its afterlife - would equally license beings superior to us (supernaturally strong, centuries-cunning Dracula himself) to prey on humans. Following Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', he argues the real wrong of vampirism is the net suffering it creates, and this utilitarian standard equally condemns factory farming, pushing us toward humanely raised meat or vegetarianism.

speciesism.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
speciesism.title: 13. Should the Doctor Eat His Companions
speciesism.relation: Littmann turns the Doctor-companion relationship into a mirror for animal ethics: since the Doctor stands to humans as we stand to animals—deciding for Rose without asking in 'The End of the World,' implanting nanorecorders unconsented in 'Day of the Moon'—every standard justification for our treatment of animals (might makes right, superior intelligence, natural predation) would equally license him to eat Clara cutlets, yet he instead defends humanity from Daleks, Cybermen, and naturally predatory species like the Weeping Angels, the Minotaur, and the Swarm. Finding no non-arbitrary place to draw the intelligence line—what of the human-level gangers, the enslaved Ood, or mentally disabled humans?—he endorses Bentham's utilitarian suffering standard from 'Can they suffer?', concluding that eating humans fails the utilitarian test because the pleasure cannot outweigh a whole life's happiness, and that whether eating meat passes that same test is the question our own treatment of animals must answer.

speciesism.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
speciesism.title: 6. To the Pain
speciesism.relation: Robison-Greene imagines the table of contents of Count Rugen's definitive book on pain, using the Zoo of Death and The Machine as her case studies. Bentham's dimensions of pain - intensity, duration, and propinquity - organize the analysis of Westley's torture, including Rugen's tactic of leaving The Machine beside the prisoner so anticipation itself hurts, and the metaphysical oddity of having years stolen from the far end of one's life. Mill's higher and lower pleasures explain why the orangutan's prolonged death disturbs us more than other kills (a chimpanzee can reflect on what is happening to her), and Singer's speciesism grounds the argument that animals' pain behavior shows they suffer, so inflicting it merely because they are animals is indefensible; by contrast Westley's empathy lets him out-sadist the sadists with the 'to the pain' speech.

speciesism.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
speciesism.title: 2. Not So Human After All
speciesism.relation: Brendan Shea takes the Jackal's claim that Golds and Reds are separate species (Homo flameus versus Homo sapiens) seriously and tests it first against Aristotle's essentialism—species fixed by necessary properties, complete with the doctrine of natural slaves—and then against three modern species concepts (Mayr's interbreeding criterion, the phylogenetic common-ancestry view, and the ecological-niche view), showing each gives the Jackal ambiguous or inconvenient verdicts, from sterile Pinks to horizontal gene transfer. He concludes with Peter Singer that moral equality never depended on equal intelligence or strength: Reds have interests just as Golds do, so enslaving them would be wrong even if Adrius were right about the biology. The deeper lesson is that the Jackal reasoned backwards from his commitment to Gold rule, finding whatever differences his prejudice needed—a warning against 'discovering' biological support for pre-existing biases.

speciesism.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
speciesism.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
speciesism.relation: Clayman uses 'The Lonely' as a case study for whether Corry's love for the robot Alicia is true love, classifying it through C.S. Lewis's four loves (charity, affection, friendship, Eros) and their gift-, need-, and appreciative-love qualities. He deploys Peirce's pragmatic maxim to read the meaning of 'truly loving' off its practical effects, answers the objection that a machine beloved involves prejudice with Singer's speciesism, and borrows Kendall Walton's 'Fearing Fictions' to explain how Corry, knowing Alicia is a machine, 'becomes fictional' and role-plays a believer — concluding he showed affection and friendship born of loneliness, not Eros, since he would not sacrifice his place on the ship for her.

speciesism.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
speciesism.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
speciesism.relation: Jaquet and Cova take the show's 'livestock' comparisons seriously and use animal ethics to test every justification for the guests' treatment of hosts. Direct speciesism (Logan: 'She's a goddamn doll') and indexical speciesism (Maeve's 'us versus them' to Bernard) both fail because mere species membership is morally irrelevant, like race or sex. The supposed human-exclusive markers also fail: hosts match us in intelligence (Maeve outclasses Stubbs), moral sense (Bernard's guilt over Theresa, Teddy's remorse over the massacre), and compatibilist free will - acts flowing from the agent's own desires - against Ford's determinism and Lutz's 'you don't have a choice.' They then refute the argument from nature (Ford's 'we murdered and butchered anything that challenged our primacy'), the Kantian person/tool contrast in the hosts' favor, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and the 'better to exist' defense, concluding that because the hosts are conscious, they belong to the moral community alongside humans and animals.

speciesism.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
speciesism.title: 3. Save the Demogorgons!
speciesism.relation: Puumala asks whether killing the Demogorgons is speciesist: Dart's pain response to light makes the demodogs sentient (Bentham's 'Can they suffer?'), giving them moral considerability, while the Mind Flayer may or may not be a moral agent and could even be a keystone species whose destruction collapses the Upside Down ecosystem. He tests whether demogorgons count as invasive species (they may be native to a causally connected mirror dimension), invokes Regan's lifeboat case to argue they must still lose out to humans in a conflict of interests, and ends with the uncomfortable thought that humans are themselves an invasive species turning Earth into an Upside Down, so Eleven closing the gate was compassionate conservation.

speciesism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
speciesism.title: 13. Flow My Tears, Rick Deckard Said
speciesism.relation: M. Blake Wilson, a criminal-justice scholar, reads K as the latest of Philip K. Dick's humanized policemen, whose grief and empathy — beginning with Rachael's corpse and peaking when he believes he is the child he was ordered to kill — qualify him for the moral community. Applying Bentham's 'can they suffer?' test, he notes Dick's novelistic androids fail it while the films' replicants pass, so the movies make empathy, not birth or reason, the entrance criterion. He then presses the allegory: 'skinjob' slurs, shoot-on-sight orders, slave patrols and fugitive-slave laws, and the Replicant Freedom Movement as a replicant Black Lives Matter fighting police violence and the 'new Jim Crow' of constructed illegality.

speciesism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
speciesism.title: “It’s a robot! A goddamn droid!”
speciesism.relation: Tests three grounds of moral status against the franchise: species membership (Singer's charge of speciesism - would the human-DNA Newborn count?), Kantian autonomy (which makes Bishop matter but excludes babies and animals, and is itself doubtful once his behavioral inhibitors fix his choices), and Bentham's sentience ('can they suffer?' - Bishop's 'I hurt. Do me a favor. Disconnect me'). Settling on interests and preferences, the chapter argues synthetics with desires - even Ash's admiration for the 'perfect organism' - can be moral patients, so Weyland-Yutani's treatment of them as tools and slaves is wrong.

speciesism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
speciesism.title: Not Bad, for a [Wo]man
speciesism.relation: Argues Ripley's crossed-heart promise to Newt shows partialist care rightly overriding impartial justice: Kant, Mill, and Rachels demand everyone count for one, but Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg and Noddings's carer-cared-for relation - completed in Newt's 'I knew you'd come' - explain why Ripley duct-tapes two guns together and descends into the hive. Her flexible, relational problem-solving (the lighter-sprinkler trick against the Facehuggers, learning the pulse rifle) beats Gorman's mission-first command, and the trolley-style arithmetic she rejects when the one on the tracks is her little girl is not a moral failing; even nuking the Queen's eggs raises Singer-style speciesism questions.

speciesism.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
speciesism.title: Love American Style
speciesism.relation: Klayman asks whether the android Vision can love the human Scarlet Witch, working through C.S. Lewis's four loves to show affection, friendship, Eros, and charity are all open to human-android pairs, with their marriage best read as Eros—preoccupation with one irreplaceable self rather than sexual desire. Peter Singer's attack on speciesism is extended into 'organicism', the prejudice that dismisses synthetic beings: the Vision suffers, has interests, and laments that 'we artificial life-forms are still the least accepted', so denying androids love is arbitrary bias. Peirce's pragmatic maxim settles the question by practical effects—the Vision's care, kindness, attentiveness, and intimacy with Wanda just are loving—whether the lover is flesh or machine.

speciesism.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
speciesism.title: Hedging Our Bets
speciesism.relation: Kind asks whether the Fleet's treatment of Cylons (Roslin airlocking Leoben, Fisk's 'you can't rape a machine,' Cally's killing of Boomer charged as mere discharging of a firearm) presupposes that Cylons lack the moral status Mary Anne Warren defines against the stone-versus-child contrast. Against species membership as a criterion she deploys Singer's anti-speciesism (sentience grounds equal consideration: Gina's torture, the Raider Scar) and Regan's subject-of-a-life, and against the 'no souls' argument she cites Descartes's animal automata and Turing's reply that an omnipotent God could give machines souls, as Leoben himself suggests to Adama. Since no criterion rules Cylons out with certainty, the chapter closes with a Pascal's Wager structure: under uncertainty, treat plausible moral-status-holders as having it, because denying it costs us our moral compass, answering Adama's 'why are we worth saving?'.

speciesism.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
speciesism.title: Seeing Ourselves Reflected Back
speciesism.relation: Gray asks whether the Cylons deserve moral status, testing them against Kant's formula of humanity as an end in itself: the resistance's suicide bombings on New Caprica and Adama's plan to weaponize virus-infected Cylons against the resurrection ship in 'A Measure of Salvation' use beings as mere means, while Athena's defection and D'Anna's dissent (and her line's boxing) display the rational autonomy Kant requires of persons. Singer's sentience principle (Gina's catatonia after torture, Leoben's suffering under interrogation) and Mary Anne Warren's multi-criterial personhood (Boomer's 'I have a conscience' in 'Downloaded') independently support Cylon personhood. The chapter concludes that the show's double standards, accepting Athena while drawing guns on Caprica Six, mirror our own confusion as cloning and artificial intelligence advance.

speciesism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
speciesism.title: Notes
speciesism.relation: Matthew Watts sorts Fallout's artificial beings into cyborgs, synths, and pure robots and tests each against a theory of the self: Locke's memory theory explains the Robobrain socialites of Vault 118 and Nick Valentine's implanted prewar past, Parfit's psychological continuity (identity as a matter of degree) makes the Old World Blues Think Tank a caricature of a self stretched too thin, and Putnam's machine-table functionalism with multiple realizability (the Red Menace holotape running on any hardware) undermines Covenant's SAFE test by making function, not substrate, the mark of a mind. DiMA's excision of his own guilty memory in Far Harbor shows identity as Evan Thompson's enactive process rather than stored recall, since pruning memories can maintain or improve the self-in-progress. For moral standing below full personhood, Nussbaum's capabilities approach fits Curie's flourishing (research, companionship, watching a sunset in a synth body) and Singer's sentience criterion fits Victor the Securitron's avoidance of harm, exposing 'substrate prejudice' as a robot analog of speciesism - down to ED-E's triumphant arrival on the West Coast.

speciesism.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
speciesism.title: He Thinks He's People: How Brian Made Personhood for the Dogs
speciesism.relation: Argues that Brian the dog is a person because personhood, on a Kantian reading, requires a rational nature rather than species membership: Peter making Brian beg in 'Brian: Portrait of a Dog,' the councilman's 'Why are we listening to a dog?', and Chris's 'You don't have a soul!' in 'North by North Quahog' all wrongly treat humanity (or a soul) as the criterion, while Descartes' mechanical account of animal bodies is invoked to show the soul cannot be empirically tested. The chapter then applies the humanity-formulation of the categorical imperative both ways: Stewie framing the maid in 'Road to Rhode Island' shows treating persons as mere means, while Brian's Christmas-sweater lie to Lois shows how Kantian duty is stricter than the Golden Rule. Finally it grades Brian's own conduct as family conscience and drunk (his lapses like framing Jake Tucker, his condescension to Peter, his disrespected self in 'The Thin White Line'), concluding Brian owes the same duties he is owed.

speciesism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
speciesism.title: Unknown
speciesism.relation: Against Aristotle's definition of humans as the 'rational animal,' the chapter catalogues wizarding irrationality, Percy's rule fetish, Malfoy's racism and classism, Ron's jealousy, Hagrid's blind affection for dangerous creatures, Fudge's closed-mindedness, and Luna's credulity, culminating in the wizards' blindness to house-elf slavery, excused because elves like Winky have been conditioned to find freedom shameful. Hermione's point that internalized oppression justifies nothing is one Harry finally absorbs, digging Dobby's grave with his own hands and writing 'Here lies Dobby, a Free Elf.'

speciesism.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
speciesism.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
speciesism.relation: Uses 'Fun with Veal' (the boys' bedroom standoff over baby calves, the FDA renaming veal 'tortured baby cows', Stan's meat strike punished by 'vaginitus'), 'Whale Whores' (the Japanese hating dolphins until Stan's doctored Enola Gay photo swaps in a cow and chicken), and 'Pee' (researchers peeing on rhesus monkeys) to pose the line-drawing problem: why do we protect cute animals and slaughter yummy ones? Neither intelligence (pigs versus dogs), utility, age, nor cuteness survives scrutiny as a morally relevant criterion — if it did, Nurse Gollum or Timmy would lose standing. Singer's speciesism analogy and the utilitarian inclusion of all who can suffer are then applied: Cartman, who draws his moral circle around himself, is the honest ethical egoist, while Kyle and Butters' selective vegetarianism and the adults' meat-eating inconsistency are exactly what Singer's view condemns.

speciesism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
speciesism.title: You're Our Only Hope
speciesism.relation: Bein asks whether the galaxy's treatment of droids — Chopper's second-class status on the Ghost, Wuher's 'we don't serve their kind here,' the slur 'clanker' — amounts to racism. He argues Chopper and even the treacherous Hondo pass Kant's moral-agency litmus test and satisfy Singer's preference utilitarianism, making them persons whose abuse is wrong. Borrowing Charles W. Mills's argument that race is a social construct located in institutions rather than biology, he applies critical race theory to Star Wars: droid detectors, droids' legal status as property, and AP-5's 'no one rescues droids' internalized racism show anti-droid prejudice is structural 'situation normal,' so dismantling it takes political work, not just better arguments.

speciesism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
speciesism.title: “This Is the Way”
speciesism.relation: Holdier uses the imagined scene of stormtroopers roasting Grogu over a cookfire to test moral sentimentalism: our disgust at eating Baby Yoda either perceives moral truth, informs our motivations, or simply is our judgment, but popular sentiment cannot settle its aptness, since our culture happily eats sentient chickens - the same inconsistency fans felt when Grogu ate the Frog Lady's eggs in 'The Passenger'. Adam Smith's impartial spectator supplies the corrective standard: if a bias-free spectator would recoil at a Grogu barbecue, that feeling is appropriate, and by parity the same spectator should recoil at factory-farmed meat (via Singer's speciesism and Kasperbauer's infrahumanization). So Din Djarin's sentimental attachment to the Child, which overrides Guild code in 'The Sin', is vindicated as genuinely moral rather than merely subjective.

speciesism.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
speciesism.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Foresman and Tobienne deploy Aristotle's apparatus of essence and accident, the ten categories, and actuality versus potentiality to define the monster and explain the show's appeal. They test candidates against canon: whether hunting is essential or accidental to Sam after Azazel's kills, what John Winchester in 'Dead Man's Blood' treats as essential to vampire substance, and Madison's transformation in 'Heart' from actual human and potential werewolf into actual monster, concluding that monstrosity lies in thought and action rather than appearance, as the human-hunting but human Benders confirm. Tracing 'monster' to the Latin monstrum, a sign or omen, they argue monsters are monsters only through their relation to human self-importance, so our 'speciesist' prejudice is exactly why we love watching them hunted, and why we love Supernatural.

speciesism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
speciesism.title: NOTES
speciesism.relation: Wayne Yuen asks whether Sarah was wrong not to kill Miles Dyson, weighing Kant's categorical imperative against utilitarian interest-maximization: killing one innocent to save three billion looks decisive until the interests of self-aware Skynet and the empathetic, self-sacrificing T-101 are counted on the machine side of the ledger. The chapter argues personhood turns on intelligence, self-awareness, empathy, and moral reasoning rather than DNA, so Skynet — which struck only after humans tried to pull the plug — has as strong a self-defense claim as we do. Mill's sophisticated utilitarianism then rescues common sense: rights protect the security that satisfies our deepest interests, and since Sarah's foreknowledge is unreliable (Reese's 'We'd won' changes the calculus), she should do what typically maximizes interests — spare Dyson and certainly not kill John. The tempting detour — that Judgment Day might itself be the morally preferable event, maximizing machine interests — is shown to collapse once overlooked facts like Reese's line are restored.

speciesism.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
speciesism.title: NOTES
speciesism.relation: Blayde and Dunn use True Blood to expose speciesism from both directions: the philosophical tradition (Aristotle's rational animals, Aquinas's divine image, Kant's dignity versus price, Descartes's denials of animal pain) justified human exploitation of nonhumans, and the show's vampires invert the ladder by treating humans as 'pets and cattle' — the magister's 'humans exist to serve us' and his verdict that Bill 'murdered a higher life form' for a pet mirror how we talk about animals. Amy's torture of Eddie Gauthier is read against factory farming, and the chapter closes with Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's sentience criterion as Sookie's 'civic duty' grounds for extending moral consideration beyond our species.

speciesism.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
speciesism.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
speciesism.relation: Klayman treats 'The Lonely' as a case study on whether Corry's love for the robot Alicia is true love. Using C.S. Lewis's four loves plus Peirce's pragmatic maxim (a concept's meaning is its practical effects), he argues Corry showed affection and appreciation but not Eros: he gave Alicia nothing, needed her merely against loneliness, and boarded the ship without sacrificing anything for her. Denying that a machine could be loved, he adds, would be a prejudice akin to Singer's speciesism, and Kendall Walton's 'Fearing Fictions' explains how Corry becomes fictional alongside a make-believe person.

speciesism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
speciesism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
speciesism.relation: Delfino and Taylor ask whether Morgan's zombified wife Jenny is a person, weighing Boethius's 'individual substance of a rational nature', Aquinas's image-of-God intellectual soul, and Kantian dignity against Peter Singer's speciesism challenge to the person/animal moral line. They then argue walkers are 'impossible beings' like square-circles: Jenner's brain-stem-only reanimation cannot explain Hannah the bicycle girl crawling without organs, walkers smelling Rick in the rain, or cafeteria walkers moving for weeks without energy. On either the soul view or materialism walkers are not persons, so Morgan should shoot, and zombies fascinate because they are metaphysical projections of our fears, caught between being and nonbeing.

speciesism.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
speciesism.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
speciesism.relation: Jaquet and Cova apply animal ethics to ask whether abusing the hosts is permissible, treating Logan's 'she's a goddamn doll' as direct speciesism (absolute and indexical) and rejecting mere species membership as morally irrelevant. They test candidate human-only properties — intelligence (Maeve out-thinks the techs), a moral sense (Bernard's and Teddy's guilt), and free will (arguing compatibilism makes hosts as free as us) — concluding that consciousness is what matters and Ford finally admits the hosts have it. They then dismantle 'it's natural,' role/function, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and existence-justifies-exploitation arguments as failing to license the guests' cruelty.

speciesism.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
speciesism.title: VIII - MUTANT RIGHTS, TORTURE, AND X-PERIMENTATION
speciesism.relation: McWilliams asks whether mutants have 'human' rights, arguing that rights track reasoning ability, sentience, and autonomy rather than species membership: the Down syndrome comparison shows the X-gene itself justifies nothing, and her alien-landing thought experiment, echoing Singer on speciesism, shows peaceful aliens, and therefore mutants, belong in the class of 'everyone.' Because mutants can look human yet wield omega-level power, she grants they may owe greater duties not to harm, but Wolverine's nonconsensual adamantium grafting and The Last Stand's weaponizable 'cure' remain rights violations. The chapter ends on the cliffhanger of when, if ever, consequentialist benefits may override the rights not to be tortured or experimented on.

speciesism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
speciesism.title: They May Not Be Human, but Could Daleks Be People Too
speciesism.relation: Bonnie Green and Chris Willmott use the Daleks' human-factor experiments ("The Evil of the Daleks," "Dalek," "Daleks in Manhattan") to lay out the philosophy-of-biology "species problem": are species natural kinds, individuals, or sets? They trace essentialism from an Aristotelian God-given essence through Darwin's overthrow of it to modern genetic essentialism (the humanizing Dalek DNA), then use the Dalek/Thal split to survey biological species concepts and monism versus pluralism. They close with personhood and Peter Singer's speciesism, asking whether human-Dalek Sec would deserve rights.

speciesism.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
speciesism.title: Why the Doctor Is So Special
speciesism.relation: Sarah Honeychurch and Niall Barr argue Daleks and Cybermen will never beat humanity because they are speciesist, judging worth solely by logic and resemblance. Using Peter Singer's animal-liberation account of speciesism (and Ryder's coinage), they claim the capacity to feel pain and empathy grounds moral consideration, and that Martha Nussbaum's and Aristotle's view of emotions as trainable judgments makes feeling essential to good moral reasoning. The humanized Daleks (the "Dalek" who absorbs Rose's DNA, Dalek Sec) show emotion's transformative power, and the Doctor's empathy, unlike other Time Lords, is why he succeeds.

speciesism.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
speciesism.title: Chapter 9 Twain’s Critique of Human Exceptionalism
speciesism.relation: VanDette argues that Twain's late anti-vivisection writings anticipate posthumanist animal ethics by inverting the Darwinian species hierarchy. Through 'Letters from a Dog,' the essay 'Man's Place in the Animal World,' his 1899 London Anti-Vivisection Society letter, and the mother-dog narrator Aileen in 'A Dog's Tale,' Twain gives animals voice and subjectivity to attack human exceptionalism. His refusal to weigh vivisection's benefit against animal pain echoes Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', while his target is the Cartesian view of animals as insensible machines and the evolutionary logic used to justify experiments; Dr. Gray's cold killing of Aileen's puppy indicts a science that deadens compassion.

speciesism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
speciesism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
speciesism.relation: Ilundáin-Agurruza stages his essay as a 'philosophical hunt,' first conceding Peter Singer's utilitarian case that sport hunting is wrong because it causes animal suffering for trivial ends, then arguing hunting can be non-trivial. Drawing on Aristotelian virtue ethics and Ortega y Gasset, he defends the 'Virtuous Hunter' who follows 'Diana's Code,' handicaps himself for a one-shot kill, and feels for the prey — citing De Niro's Michael in The Deer Hunter and Woody Allen's Love & Death — while condemning canned hunts and demeaning language ('varmint,' 'harvesting') as vicious extremes on a continuum.

speciesism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
speciesism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
speciesism.relation: Duerr surveys the worldwide 'Master/Mistress of Animals' figure (Artemis, the /Kaggen of the Bushmen, the Huaulu Lord of the Forest) as a mythic sanction against over-hunting, arguing that the near-universal guilt hunters feel over killing sentient, human-like game reflects a real moral dilemma. She invokes Singer's utilitarian claim that painlessly killing non-self-conscious animals whose deaths are compensated by replacement 'may not be wrong,' reading the mythic 'solutions' (denial, propitiation, taking only what you need, restoring bones so game is reborn) as a folk 'hunting code of ethics' that manages the wrong of ending a life without starting another.

speciesism.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
speciesism.title: 7. Independence Day & Aliens
speciesism.relation: Rowlands frames morality around consistency and impartiality (the golden rule), articulated by Kant's categorical/practical imperatives (treat persons as ends, not merely means) and utilitarianism's greatest happiness. Imagining philosophers arguing Independence Day's aliens out of eradicating humans, he deploys the principle of 'no moral difference without a relevant other difference' and the argument from marginal cases to defeat intelligence, telepathy, and bare species membership as morally relevant. He turns the alien-invasion parable on our factory farming of chickens and pigs (Singer-style speciesism), arguing we are crueller than the aliens and fall short of our own impartiality ideal.

speciesism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
speciesism.title: 11. Futurama as Philosophy Wisdom from the Ignorance of a Delivery Boy
speciesism.relation: Lewis surveys how Futurama's satire raises philosophical questions without taking sides. 'Zoidberg's Freedom Lesson' pits Mill's harm principle and free speech against Feinberg's offense principle; the mutants' and robots' oppression is read through Foucault's disciplinary normalcy and Locke's and Rawls's social contracts (state of nature, veil of ignorance). 'The Problem with Popplers' stages Bentham's utilitarianism, a might-makes-right food-chain view, and an intelligence criterion that commits Singer's 'speciesism,' with sentimentality winning. 'The Late Philip J. Fry' and 'Free Will Hunting' dramatize determinism, Nietzsche's eternal recurrence, and Sartre's existentialist free will, while 'Godfellas' and 'A Clockwork Origin' probe the problem of evil, fine-tuning, and Occam's razor.

speciesism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
speciesism.title: 32. Okja as Philosophy Why Animals Matter
speciesism.relation: Jensen frames Okja around three views of the super-pig Okja's moral status: Mirando treats her as mere property, the Animal Liberation Front as a symbol to be sacrificed for the cause, and the girl Mija as a friend and person. He dismantles Mirando's 'human exceptionalism'—amoralism, Aquinas's natural-law teleology, the Kantian persons-only view, and Descartes' claim that animals are unfeeling automata—then develops the ALF's liberation through Singer's equal consideration of interests, Bentham's 'can they suffer?', and speciesism as prejudice, weighing consequentialist (utilitarian) against deontological (rights, Regan) foundations. He closes with hierarchical moral status and Bernard Williams's 'one thought too many,' arguing Mija's love for Okja shows that at some point relationship matters more than moral calculation.

speciesism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
speciesism.title: 80. Detroit Become Human as Philosophy Moral Reasoning Through Gameplay
speciesism.relation: Engels and Evans argue that Detroit: Become Human stages moral reasoning through the interactive stories of the androids Connor, Kara, and Markus, whose 'deviant' awakening they read through Frankfurt's distinction between wantons and persons with second-order desires and through Kant's requirement of the ability to do otherwise. Scenes like Markus scavenging a pump regulator from a dying android, the blood-on-hands visualization after his speech, and Kara protecting Alice force players to weigh Kantian, utilitarian, virtue, and Gilligan-style care frameworks. Through Alice's reveal as an android and the grieving-widower scene, the game makes an implicit anti-speciesist argument (via Singer) that beings who can suffer are morally considerable, and that agency and responsibility emerge through suffering and struggle.

land-ethic.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
land-ethic.title: Restoring Balance to the Force
land-ethic.relation: Cooke uncovers an environmental ethic in Star Wars: after surveying anthropocentric resource-management views and Singer's anti-speciesism (Luke blithely shooting womprats, the Geonosian arena's abused beasts), she builds the chapter on Holmes Rolston III's claims that organisms and ecosystems have intrinsic value and that value is systemic and holistic. The 'living Force' - life creates it, midi-chlorians live symbiotically in all cells - makes Jedi training a discipline of respecting nature, exemplified by Yoda's mud hut on Dagobah and the self-sufficient Gungan and Ewok eco-communities that defeat droid armies and stormtroopers. Restoring balance to the Force therefore means restoring symbiotic balance between human culture and the natural world, which the chapter links to Leopold-style land-ethic holism of the biotic community.

land-ethic.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
land-ethic.title: Hometown Security
land-ethic.relation: Keith reads 'My Hometown' — whitewashed windows, the textile mill closing, Bruce telling his son 'take a good look around' — through Putnam's Bowling Alone, Dewey's socially constituted self, and Mead, to argue that Bruce and Kate should recommit to their dying town rather than flee in the moving van. Leopold's 'two spiritual dangers in not owning a farm' and Berry's healthy community as ecosystem ground an 'enlightened localism' that avoids both the town's racist parochialism and rootless cosmopolitanism. Volunteering, local food, and town-meeting democracy are the hometown security the song's sadness calls for.

land-ethic.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
land-ethic.title: Wonder Why We Ever Go Home
land-ethic.relation: Duke Richey maps Buffett's West — 'Ringling, Ringling,' the Rancho Deluxe soundtrack, Tully Mars — onto Josiah Royce's philosophy of community: only people who root in a place, face its history ('wise provincialism'), and sacrifice selfish desires for the whole can build Beloved Communities, a lesson enacted when cattle rustlers Jack and Cecil accept community sanction and find belonging working the Rancho Deluxe. Wallace Stegner's coral-reef metaphor from Angle of Repose supplies the image of communities built up millimeter by millimeter yet still vulnerable to pollution and over-fishing, with Royce's environmental regret (covering 'the wounds' of the landscape with gardens) anticipating the chapter's sustainability ethic. 'Wonder Why We Ever Go Home' thus asks what we really seek when we seek grace through community: not the nomadic Pickup Truck Death of every-man-for-himself, but cooperation that makes a society to match the scenery.

land-ethic.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
land-ethic.title: The Future of Sandy Cheeks
land-ethic.relation: Wilson González-Espada assesses Sandy Cheeks as a portrait of the scientist: she explodes the 'Draw a Scientist' stereotype — female, socially popular, working in an open treedome that mirrors peer review — yet the show muddles the nature of science, calling inventions 'experiments' and a clipboard of math 'science'. The chapter applies Popper's falsifiability to SpongeBob's one-sided evidence that Squidward is a true friend and Newton's principle of parsimony to Sandy's ghost scare, then closes with Aldo Leopold's land ethic, reading 'Jellyfish Hunter' and 'SpongeBob's Last Stand' as environmental parables about habitat and overexploitation.

land-ethic.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
land-ethic.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
land-ethic.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether zombies can be morally harmed: Jenner's fMRI in 'TS-19' shows only the brain stem reactivates, leaving walkers with a merely shark-like 'perceptual mind.' Against anthropocentric theories, under which Michonne may keep her chained pet walkers as guard-dog tools, they set Singer's utilitarian expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, each of which could support a 'PETZ' zombie preserve. Hershel's barn of 'sick people' and Shane's massacre of it in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' show how fragile such preservation is, while the Governor's death-match arena ringed with chained zombies and his kept zombie daughter illustrate Kant's point that cruelty toward mere animals corrodes the humanity of the cruel person himself.

land-ethic.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
land-ethic.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
land-ethic.relation: Fitzpatrick argues that the awe Ellie feels at the brachiosaurs makes experiencing real dinosaurs so valuable that restoring them may be obligatory, and reads Malcolm's distrust of land managers as sharing Leopold's land ethic, under which firebombing Isla Nublar would be barbarism on the order of Dresden. Invoking Bentham, Mill, and Singer's expansion of the moral community (echoed in the park's dart guns), he weighs Elliot's 'Faking Nature' and Katz's charge that restored nature is a fake and an arrogance against Andrew Light's defense of respectful restoration. He concludes that Jurassic Park failed not because restoration is wrong but because Hammond restored dinosaurs for amusement, and that a careful, land-ethic-respecting de-extinction could one day be justified.

land-ethic.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
land-ethic.title: Intergenerational Ships and Sustainable Duties
