land-ethic.relation: Hackett uses WALL-E's lone plant and the Buy n Large Axiom to ask what we owe nature and future generations: WALL-E's tender care of the seedling models treating nature as a rights-bearing 'person' (via Gaia-superorganism thinking), while BnL's obese, screen-hooked passengers on the Axiom satirize capitalist individualism that acknowledges no obligations beyond contracts. He proposes a 'Principle of Sustainable Duties' — minimize net environmental damage and weigh long-term impact — and reads the film's open ending, extending Leopold's expansion of moral community to the biotic whole, as a Platonic aporia about whether an Anthropocene humanity can actually change in time.

land-ethic.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
land-ethic.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
land-ethic.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether walkers can be morally harmed, ranking perceptual, reasoning, and conscious minds and placing zombies at shark level on the evidence of Dr. Jenner's fMRI ('TS-19') showing only the brain stem reactivates. Surveying anthropocentric views (Michonne's chained pet-walkers as guard-dog tools), Singer's expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, they conclude that even utilitarians could demand a zombie preserve on the model of Hershel's barn of 'sick people', which Shane's barn massacre in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' destroys. Kant's point that cruelty to animals corrodes our humanity explains why the Governor's death-match arena, his torture of Rick and Michonne, and his chained zombie daughter mark him, not the walkers, as the true moral monster.

land-ethic.title: 5 Neil Young Lover of Sun, Moon and Cars
land-ethic.relation: Anderson traces Young's environmentalism from the hippie-romantic nature worship of "After the Gold Rush" and Greendale toward a pragmatic "middle way" that reconciles his love of nature with his love of cars and recording technology (the Lincvolt project, Storytone). Drawing on Thoreau, Muir and Leopold's land ethic while rejecting the fixed prescriptions of Singer and Regan, he presents Young as an experimentalist "meliorist" who owns his own complicity in CO2 abuse and urges informed, practical, self-aware action rather than utopian or deontological solutions.

land-ethic.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
land-ethic.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
land-ethic.relation: In this Foreword, hunter and nature writer David Petersen argues that hunting is his best 'philosophy professor,' teaching lessons about life, death, and human animality. He casts predation and evasion as a 'sacred game' that sculpted prey species through natural selection, and invokes Aldo Leopold's ideal of restraint 'even when no one is watching' to distinguish true, process-oriented hunters from gadget-reliant 'Wannabee' shooters using bait stations, GPS, and motorized decoys. He warns that banning hunting would cause wildlife overpopulation, framing the human as an ambivalent predator: both 'good' and 'bad.'

land-ethic.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
land-ethic.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
land-ethic.relation: Opening with his intimate encounter with a wolf, Vitali argues that 'fair chase' cannot mean fairness to the animal — since a right to fair chase would imply a more basic right not to be hunted, conceding the anti-hunting case. Instead, invoking Aristotelian human flourishing and Leopold's land ethic, he relocates fair chase to the hunter: hunting is moral only if it serves the biotic community through conservation and lets the hunter enter the predator-prey life-death continuum. He illustrates self-handicapping through master hunter Milo Burcham stalking a distant muley with a recurve bow.

land-ethic.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
land-ethic.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
land-ethic.relation: Marvin, a social anthropologist, argues that for 'nature hunters' (Kellert's typology) a taxidermy trophy is not a dead animal but a living souvenir — un recuerdo — that enshrines the memory of a fair-chase hunt. Using Susan Stewart on the souvenir's part/whole incompleteness and Appadurai on value as 'difficulty of acquisition,' he shows how the lethal shot, the pose-reversed photograph, and the taxidermist's craft convert a wild animal into a personal memento that only lives through the hunter's narrative. How the animal was killed (ethically, authentically) matters more than that it was killed; the trophy is the hunter's self-awarded token of ethical excellence.

land-ethic.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
land-ethic.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
land-ethic.relation: King examines Ortega y Gasset's and James Swan's claim that hunting is a 'return to nature' that revives a Paleolithic animal self, and argues it fails: Ortega himself concedes the return is only a 'vacation' from civilization, and the hunter's selective, predatory attention cannot supply the ecological literacy needed to confront industrial civilization. Drawing on Leopold's land ethic, Wendell Berry's agrarianism, and bell hooks's humility before nature's power, King contends a genuine return requires 'thick' relations to a particular bioregion sustained by a community of memory, not an individual's seasonal escape.

land-ethic.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
land-ethic.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
land-ethic.relation: Carmine argues that in America hunting is a sacred rite of a secular 'religion' of individual natural rights granted by the Deist 'Nature's God,' where—revising Locke via Jefferson's 'pursuit of happiness'—one owns game only by actual capture, and early game law kept even private land open to the common hunter against English enclosure. He attacks Leopold's land ethic and Tom Regan's animal rights, and Garrett Hardin's 'Tragedy of the Commons,' as an 'eco-gentry' that demotes humans to mere biosphere/carbonate and threatens human rights, insisting (with Burkert's Homo Necans) that to kill and eat the rabbit is to reserve dignity for humans alone.

land-ethic.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
land-ethic.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
land-ethic.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

just-war-theory.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
just-war-theory.title: Send in the Clones!
just-war-theory.relation: Hanley defends a provocative 'yes' to cloning, genetic engineering, and clone armies. He dismisses the 'yuck factor' as showing nothing inherently bad, argues via non-identity-style cases (a genetically corrected or maimed Luke is a different child who is not thereby harmed) that early genetic manipulation harms no one, and distinguishes brainwashing, coercion, and inducement (Obi-Wan's death-stick mind trick, Vader's threats to Lando, Jar Jar's exploitation) to ask when bending another's will is permissible. Turning to warfare, he applies Just War theory's conditions - judging Anakin's slaughter of the Sand People guilty on nearly every count - and concludes that troops with deliberately diminished autonomy may be the least objectionable solution to the ethics of recruitment, training, and deployment: send in the clones.

just-war-theory.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
just-war-theory.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Wendy Hamblet asks whether Narnia feeds children a dangerous militaristic moral imaginary: Homeric warrior heroes, swarthy Calormene villains, voiceless animals excluded from moral concern, and battles that decide truth, in a lineage running from Plato's censorship of nursery stories through Descartes's modernity to Heidegger's seduction by Hitler's myths. On closer reading she finds Lewis undermining militarism: morally mixed characters, condemnation of aggression, despotism, and 'reasons of state,' and room only for just war and righteous self-defense. The finale is read through Plato's cave, as the Last Battle's worlds-within-worlds expose our political 'truths' as shadow-images that unscrupulous leaders manipulate when the god is absent.

just-war-theory.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
just-war-theory.title: It’s Not That Simple
just-war-theory.relation: Donal O'Mathuna uses 24 to run the torture debate: the ticking bomb scenario (Syed Ali's nuclear bomb, Miles pressing to torture Audrey) dramatizes the utilitarian case for forward-looking interrogational torture, while Jack slicing off the Russian consul's finger and Morris's broken guilt show torture as a deontological violation that destroys character on both sides and usually fails to extract truth. Against the show's sanitized, banal presentation (Agent Burke as the "kindly torturer"), he sets Abu Ghraib, the systematic training of torturers, and the metastatic spread of torture programs once permitted. Fiction can open the ethical question, he concludes, but must not be mistaken for the reality of torture.

just-war-theory.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
just-war-theory.relation: Four 'Phase Three' essays on world conquest. Terjesen asks whether Doctor Doom's magnanimity (Aristotle's great-souledness, contra the unity-of-virtues thesis Aquinas held and Philippa Foot qualified) makes him less villainous than The Authority, whose purely consequentialist paternalism - like Doom's Emperor Doom or Ozymandias's plot - usurps a free choice no mere power can justify. Barringer reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes: the Stamford explosion and unrestrained superpowers recreate the state of nature, the Registration Act is the surrender of freedom to a sovereign, and Stark, Richards, and Pym repeat Hobbes's flawed faith in 'scientific' deductive politics, sealed by the clone-Thor killing of Goliath. Hillerbrand and Sandburg pit Rorschach's Kantian deontology (no compromise, not even to save the world) against Ozymandias's utilitarian murder of three million New Yorkers in Watchmen, arguing via Laplace's Demon that even Dr. Manhattan - nihilist or Schopenhauerian recluse - cannot verify the outcome, so watchmen can be trusted only by knowing their limits. Ostrander's fictional NSC interview has Amanda Waller's Suicide Squad defended with Benthamite utility, the rejection of natural rights as 'nonsense on stilts,' and the Augustinian just-war criteria of just cause, right intent, and proportionality, while the interviewer exposes how conveniently those limits bend.

just-war-theory.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
just-war-theory.title: What Is It Good For
just-war-theory.relation: Ben Medler argues that despite the faction rhetoric there is no war in WoW. Working through definitions from Clausewitz, Rousseau (war is a relation between State and State, not man and man), and just-war thinkers like Cicero and Grotius, he shows that duelers, battleground teams, world PvP, and even guilds all lack war's defining features — political community, anonymity of victims, territorial stakes — so the fighting is feuding and gladiatorial combat, not war. Players live like egalitarian nomadic band societies, guilds are at most chiefdoms, and Blizzard alone is the state (indeed a plutocracy) that cannot war with itself; he closes by asking designers for neutral, nonviolent gameplay.

just-war-theory.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
just-war-theory.title: Freeing Clausewitz’s Soul from Gravity
just-war-theory.relation: Melancon tests Just War Theory against Gundam's One Year War: Gihren Zabi's 'Sieg Zeon' funeral oration and Char Aznable's rhetoric show how the vague criterion of comparative justice lets a militarist regime dress aggression — the Three Seconds of Declaration gassing of colonies, Operation British's colony drop on Earth — in just-war language. On the conduct side, Ramba Ral's troops spare civilians and differentiate child targets on White Base, yet Zeon's still-unjust ad bellum position cannot be rehabilitated; and asking whether WMDs are inherently immoral, he uses Anavel Gato's nuclear strike on the Federation fleet review (Operation Stardust) — discriminating, proportional, militarily necessary — to argue weapons are amoral tools judged only by Walzer-style jus in bello criteria. Clausewitz resolves the theory's usefulness: war's inner tendency toward the absolute must stay nested within political goals, and Zeon's drift from fighting for independence into conquering and governing Earth shows exactly how a war that abandons just-war limits loses sight of what victory even is.

just-war-theory.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
just-war-theory.title: Silence of the Rookie
just-war-theory.relation: Shane Fliger pairs Halo's two playable humans as two visions of war. Master Chief—knight-like MJOLNIR armor, right intent in a genocidal war of survival, proportionality against the Covenant, and the responsible refusal of 343 Guilty Spark's order to fire Halo—embodies the Just War Theory of Aristotle, Cicero, Augustine, and Aquinas, its jus ad bellum and jus in bello. The Rookie of Halo 3: ODST—unshielded, motion-trackerless, silent in a shattered New Mombasa, striking from shadows with a suppressed SMG and VISR-tagged targets—instead fights Clausewitz's absolute war of escalating force blended with Ludendorff's unrestrained total war, and Fliger concludes only the two together give players a complete picture of warfare.

just-war-theory.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
just-war-theory.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Jai Galliott takes the Season Three episode 'Whiskey Tango Foxtrot', in which Nevada-based drone operator Sergeant Elkins kills twelve Afghan civilians and is convicted of murder despite Alicia's scapegoating defense, as a case study in the ethics of drone warfare. Tracing just war theory from the Mahabharata through Augustine to Aquinas's jus ad bellum and jus in bello framework, he applies proportionality and discrimination to the strike and argues that sensor limits and the physical and emotional distance of push-button killing (Grossman's spectrum from knife combat to drones) erode operators' capacity for discriminate targeting. He concludes that drones are a moral hazard but a legitimate asset, and that blame must be apportioned among operator, manufacturer, and commanders rather than dumped on Elkins alone.

just-war-theory.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
just-war-theory.title: Futurama and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Malloy defines war as organized, political, violent conflict and tests Futurama's many invasions against just war theory: Zapp's invasion of Spheron 1 in 'War Is the H-Word' fails just cause ('they stand for everything we don't stand for'), the first Omicronian invasion over the interrupted Single Female Lawyer broadcast fails proportionality and last resort, while the second, over eaten Popplers, passes. Zapp's Hyperdeath laser ribbon-cutting and the Bender suicide-bombing plot against the Brain Balls illustrate discrimination, proportionality, and means evil in themselves, and the postwar demand that Lrrr eat one human - ending with blameless Free Waterfall Jr. - raises war-crimes punishment and restitution. The chapter closes by endorsing Walzer: a state's moral authority hinges on at least acknowledging the rules of war.

just-war-theory.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
just-war-theory.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Galliott treats Frankenstein as the template for blaming lethal autonomous robots: Victor alone created his creature, but today's 'frankennovation' - Ronald Arkin's 'ethical governor' algorithms, DARPA funding, degree programs in robot warfare, and the South African robotic cannon that killed nine spectators - distributes responsibility across engineers, educators (Victor's father and Professors Krempe and Waldman, who never properly warned him about Agrippa's 'sad trash'), universities, and the military-industrial complex. Yet Shelley's articulate, Paradise Lost-quoting monster is a rational, intentional killer who can be held morally responsible and even punished, as Rob Sparrow demands of machines. Because responsibility does not dilute with numbers - two murderers do not get half a life sentence each - the chapter concludes that everyone in the chain, and all of us who do nothing to stop it, shares the blame for monstrous creations.

just-war-theory.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
just-war-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Matthew Brophy argues the I.F. could only get a compassionate child to commit xenocide by presenting war as a game, a framing that neutralizes moral agency just as Milgram's shock experiments and the fake game show The Game of Death did. Using Sunzi's 'know your enemy' to frame the empathy paradox, Walzer's problem of dirty hands for Graff's lesser-evil choices, and Foot's trolley problem alongside drone 'Nintendo warfare' to show how distance makes killing easier, he concludes Ender was likely a willing pawn who let himself be deceived because he endorsed the war's survivalist goal.

just-war-theory.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
just-war-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: James Cook grades the Third Invasion against the just war principles Ender was never taught: the war is preventive rather than genuinely preemptive (with the 2003 Iraq parallel), proper authority is compromised by deceiving the public, last resort fails since the hive-queen was trying to communicate, and non-combatant immunity condemns destroying the bugger homeworld. He stages Augustine's ban on killing in individual self-defense against Aquinas' permission of it, and uses Kant's humanity formula and Cicero's hostis/perduellis distinction to ask whether the buggers were ever treated as rational beings rather than mere threats.

just-war-theory.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
just-war-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Kody Cooper runs Ender's life through classical just war theory: Augustine's axiom that peace is the end of all war explains why even his playground battles aim at a just peace, while the I.F.'s deliberate refusal to protect him from Bonzo's gang throws Ender into the Hobbesian state of nature where each person holds personal authority to use deadly force in self-defense. Sunzi's insistence that a commander must know the enemy grounds Ender's empathic preparation, and Cooper concludes the Third Invasion fails right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality - so the guilt Ender carries is really the I.F.'s and humanity's.

just-war-theory.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
just-war-theory.title: Homeland and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Jai Galliott argues Homeland's drone strike that killed Issa is not a one-off plot device but mirrors real US drone warfare that breeds blowback: strikes strengthen al-Qaeda's brand and radicalize the disaffected, from Brody to the Boston bombers. He analyzes the asymmetry problem - the weak side comingles with civilians, straining the just war principles of discrimination and proportionality, while drone operators living among US suburbs become contested targets - and rejects giving weaker states a 'wild card' of lowered ethical standards. His proposal is that the technologically superior side bind itself to stricter just war compliance and policing-like restraint, since foreseeable terrorist reciprocity can tip proportionality against the war itself.

just-war-theory.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
just-war-theory.title: Homeland and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Edwin Jacob contrasts the utilitarian calculus behind Walden's drone strike - Estes's eighty percent estimate, 'potential collateral damage falls within current matrix parameters', eighty-three children killed - with Kant's three formulations of the categorical imperative applied to that decision. On the universal-law formula Walden cannot will a world of strikes on one's own soil, on the humanity formula the schoolchildren are used merely as means, and the kingdom-of-ends formula condemns treating foreign lives as quantities in a matrix. The chapter adds that drones, like Brody's suicide vest, are asymmetric terror at a distance, and that blowback (Shahzad's Times Square attempt) shows the strategy fails even consequentialist test.

just-war-theory.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
just-war-theory.title: Homeland and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: John Fitzpatrick asks whether anything goes in war, using the FBI's killing of two innocents in the mosque and the ensuing official lie, plus Walden's strike on Issa's school. Truman's Hiroshima utilitarianism (saving lives overall) meets Anscombe's deontology - 'to choose to kill the innocent as a means to their ends is always murder' - before Rawls's social contract supplies a middle path: rules rational parties would agree to behind a veil of ignorance ('we won't kill your children if you don't kill ours'), which condemns both Nazir and Walden since neither faces an 'extreme crisis' like 1940 Britain. Brody's turn is itself Rawlsian: what breaks him is the unfairness of killing children as collateral damage.

just-war-theory.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
just-war-theory.title: Homeland and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: William Rodriguez traces terrorism's evolving meaning from the Jacobins' state Terror through anarchist 'propaganda by deed' (Nechayev, Bakunin) to non-state groups, then tests whether Abu Nazir's campaign, grounded in bin Laden's 1998 fatwa grievances and the greater/lesser jihad distinction, can be morally justified. On a utilitarian defense terrorism could be last-resort self-defense against a collectively guilty population, but the just war criteria of competent authority, right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality all fail for al-Qaeda, since civilians killed on 9/11 were neither combatants nor guilty. Deontologically, targeting civilians violates the right to life and human dignity, so Nazir's attacks on innocents are murder, however real the grievances.

just-war-theory.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
just-war-theory.title: 7. Give Peace a Chance
just-war-theory.relation: Lewis argues the Dauntless Manifesto's claim that 'justice is more important than peace' rests on a mistake: following Nicholas Wolterstorff's account of shalom, real peace just is justice - each person receiving what Ulpian called their due and enjoying their rights - so the two cannot come apart. He shows each faction works with a different, deficient conception of peace (Amity's drug-induced calm, Erudite's negotiated order, Abnegation's self-erasure), then uses Aristotle's three types of justice to dismantle Jeanine's best defense, that her slaughter of Abnegation and the Divergents is retributive justice: the accused are innocent and her 'peace' is coercion, propaganda, and fear. The chapter ends with concrete reforms - welcome the factionless as a sixth service faction, let factions teach each other their virtues - so that Roth's Chicago could actually achieve the ethical community of peace-through-justice.

just-war-theory.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
just-war-theory.title: 18. Wondering What It’s All For
just-war-theory.relation: Trip McCrossin reads Lord Grantham's 'we've dreamed a dream' as an echo of Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 2 and follows the war story line - Matthew and William missing before Amiens, William's slow death, Mr. Lang's shell shock, Mrs. Patmore's nephew Archie shot for cowardice - to show how obscure war's causes and realities remain to those who have not lived them. The Dowager Countess's 'we don't always get our just deserts' as Matthew dies under his car, and the stretcher-bearer's 'it comes down to luck,' raise the problem of evil from the Book of Job: good and bad fortune fall without premonition or meaning. Against complacency about war's inevitability, the chapter argues that since class and traffic harms can be reduced, warfare's can be too - we should 'band together as Daniel,' interpret the wars a few dream up, and not allow them to come to be.

just-war-theory.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
just-war-theory.title: 19. Of Downton and Drones
just-war-theory.relation: Jai Galliott contrasts the roughly level killing field of WWI, in which William dies and Matthew is paralyzed in the trenches alongside aristocrats who suffered proportionally the heaviest losses, with today's drone age, in which remote pilots drawn largely from the lower and middle classes bear the burden of fighting. Tracing unmanned weapons from WWI tele-operated motorboats and the Sperry and Kettering aerial torpedoes to Reaper drones flown by a 'PlayStation generation,' he argues that radical technological asymmetry breaks Just War Theory - undermining last resort and proportionality and the mutual imposition of risk that Kahn and Sparrow make the basis of combatants' rights. He proposes that highly asymmetric force be restrained into something like international policing, while conceding, like Mrs. Patmore with her electric mixer, that nothing will stop us being dragged into the drone age.

just-war-theory.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
just-war-theory.title: 8. The Warring Dead
just-war-theory.relation: Morris applies just war theory's distinction between justice of war and justice in war to Season 3's Woodbury-prison conflict, staging Walzer's moral symmetry of combatants - soldiers on both sides may permissibly kill each other regardless of their cause - against McMahan's critique, illustrated by the bank robber who kills a cop in 'self-defense.' McMahan's distinction between objective justification and excuses like coercion and ignorance is worked through Maggie giving up the prison's location under threat to Glenn in 'When the Dead Come Knocking' and the Woodbury militia's ignorance of the Governor's raids. He concludes the prison group fights a justified defensive war, the ignorant Woodbury fighters are excused but not justified, and real culpability lies with the Governor and his henchmen.

just-war-theory.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
just-war-theory.title: 11. Have Fun Overthrowing This Evil Government!
just-war-theory.relation: Gibson reads Humperdinck's fabricated-pretext war against Guilder (framing Guilder for Buttercup's murder, with Vizzini's crew as private military contractors) through Just War Theory: it fails the jus ad bellum just-cause requirement built on Augustine and Aquinas, since the war would be retribution sparked by staged wrongdoing, and contractor motives of profit compound the violation. Michael Davis's critique of the ticking-time-bomb defense then shows that Rugen's torture of Westley is exactly the 'institution of torture' whose moral cost forbids ever licensing torture, since the torturer must be trained on victims first. Finally, even Hobbes's Leviathan - the most absolutist of social contract views - requires the sovereign to protect the people's safety and administer equal justice, so Humperdinck's record makes his rule illegitimate and the storming of the castle a justified insurrection.

just-war-theory.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
just-war-theory.title: 26. Horrifying Violence, Gratuitous Sex, and the Truth
just-war-theory.relation: Silverman concedes Game of Thrones can be watched viciously - sadistically relishing Theon's flaying or using it as soft pornography - but denies the show is inherently immoral. From Plato's Republic he takes the test of whether a narrative serves or obscures reality (Socrates was executed partly on the slander of Aristophanes' Clouds) and argues the show is honest where epics lie: war is ugly and kills innocents, measured against the Augustinian just-war criteria that even the Brotherhood Without Banners decays past; humans really are as sexually preoccupied as Plato's appetitive soul, Freud's id, or Augustine's original sin; and honor without practical wisdom - Ned versus Tyrion on Aristotle's ideal - is a recipe for ruin.

just-war-theory.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
just-war-theory.title: 1. The Deed of F’ing Society
just-war-theory.relation: Rocha reads fsociety's 5/9 logic-bomb attack on E Corp as anarchist 'propaganda of the deed' - a shocking act meant to wake people from their comfortable slumber inside hierarchy - and positions it between Alexander Berkman's violent anarchism (mirroring Phillip Price's 'bullet in the right place') and Gandhi's nonviolent self-suffering, quoting satyagraha and the older Goldman's rejection of violence. He then runs the hack through just war theory's four questions (necessity, proportionality, justification, effectiveness), noting that wiping the debt records also destroyed savings and indirectly got people like Gideon killed, and that fsociety, as Trenton says, never paints the alternative society - so the reader is left to answer whether the deed was justified.

just-war-theory.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
just-war-theory.title: 12. Are We Really Sure They’re Wrong
just-war-theory.relation: Timothy Hsiao argues we cannot condemn the burning of the disabled or Smith's son's mandated euthanasia by appealing to Nazi values, since cultural relativism would make the Resistance the real wrongdoers; the horror we feel presupposes an objective natural law known to reason, the violation of which grounded the Nuremberg trials. From Augustine's 'an unjust law is no law at all,' the chapter then tests the Resistance's armed rebellion against the five just-war conditions — proper authority (the Resistance as agent of the moral law), just cause, reasonable chance of success (the newsreels as grounds for hope), proportionality, and last resort — and finds it justified.

just-war-theory.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
just-war-theory.title: 17. Please Hold for a Call from God
just-war-theory.relation: In a satirical dialogue, God phones Aquinas in heaven and orders a Summa-style investigation of which superhero should lift the world out of an economic crisis and which should stop a looming war. Aquinas rules that the Lazarus-like Captain America, teamed with a Nobel economist, should handle the depression, then returns to his own treatise On War - sovereign authority, just cause, right intention, with Augustine's definition of just war quoted from the Summa - to ask whether a loyal subject may choose the good over the sovereign in an unjust war. He concludes that billionaire Iron Man is the only figure with sovereign-like standing to countermand an unjust war, while worrying about billionaire power, superhero bandwagons, and Satan getting wind of the reasoning.

just-war-theory.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
just-war-theory.title: 5. Inside Gilead’s Misogynist Parlors
just-war-theory.relation: Hirschbein unravels the Genesis story of Abraham, Sarah, and Hagar as the script Gilead rereads to rationalize its 'misogynist parlors,' arguing that Gilead's exegesis is propaganda rather than scholarship—cherry-picking scripture that Nietzsche joked would appall the actual Jesus. He then spins the reader's moral compass: with Rorty's ironist he asks whether anyone initiated into Abraham's tribe or raised in Gilead can be blamed—are even Hitler and Commander Waterford products of their time?—and weighs Ofglen's suicide bombing of the Rachel and Leah Center against just war criteria of proportion, innocence, and chance of success. Finally, with Freud and Niebuhr, he suggests the Sons of Jacob built their surveillance state on a depraved view of human nature, so utopian schemes—Gilead included—are doomed from the founding.

just-war-theory.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
just-war-theory.title: Introduction
just-war-theory.relation: Book introduction: recounts how the 1979 cast were the first casualties of the Chestburster scene (real butcher-shop organs, Veronica Cartwright fainting), then previews the volume's payload - personhood questions about Ash, Bishop, David and the Ripley clone; Marx on why Weyland-Yutani sacrifices crews for profit; Plato's Republic on children in warfare via Newt; Lovecraftian cosmic horror; feminist readings of Ripley as care ethicist and mother; and continental takes - Xenomorphs as Nietzsche's Ubermensch, Camus on Ripley-8's refusal to commit suicide, and Sartre on a Xenomorph's right to resist us.

just-war-theory.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
just-war-theory.title: Easing Back on the APC’s Throttle
just-war-theory.relation: Treats Engineers, Xenomorphs, and humans as states and reads the APC debate through Thucydides' Melian dialogue ('the strong do what they will') and the jus in bello criteria of discrimination, military necessity, and proportionality. It concludes that Ripley's 'nuke the site from orbit' and Vasquez's nerve gas are vengeance masquerading as realism - the Xeno threat is no longer imminent, so Walzer's 'supreme emergency' is unavailable - while Hudson's withdrawal (even Burke's species-preservation plea) fits both realism and just war restraint; the Ben Tre 'we destroyed the town to save it' fiasco in Vietnam is the cautionary parallel.

just-war-theory.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
just-war-theory.title: And the war Rages on
just-war-theory.relation: Robichaud runs the Kree-Skrull War (Avengers #89–97) through Michael Walzer's just war theory: the Avengers' defense of Earth against Ronan's Plan Atavus is justified self-defense meeting proportionality and last resort, while Ronan's preventive 'devolve humanity' war fails for lack of evidence and exhausted diplomacy. The Skrulls' shape-shifting trick that gets Mar-Vell to build the Omni-Wave Projector might squeak through on consequentialist grounds, but the emperor's threat to make Captain Marvel watch the Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver die counts as torture—and is impermissible on the Kantian ground that it treats a person merely as a means, whatever the consequences. The point is that even a cosmic comic war displays the real moral complexity of military ethics.

just-war-theory.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
just-war-theory.title: “This is the Kind of Thing that is Going to Bite US in the Butt”
just-war-theory.relation: Melançon pictures Avengers ethics as Hawkeye's arrow sliding along a line from deontological duty toward consequentialist results, focusing on secrets and lies: Doctor Strange's deception—disguising his Sanctum Sanctorum as a coffee shop to shelter the underground New Avengers after Civil War—is tested against Michael Walzer's 'supreme emergency', the wartime exception (Allied bombing of Germany, the ticking time bomb) that permits violating your own values so they can survive. Strange keeps sliding—possessed by a demon against the Hulk—until the Eye of Agamotto strips him of his title, showing emergencies must stay rare and the agent 'worthy of surviving'. Steve Rogers's secret black-ops Secret Avengers repeat the danger: unlike democratic intelligence agencies, they have zero oversight or accountability, so the WikiLeaks-style leak of their informant dealings threatens the reputation of the whole Avengers enterprise.

just-war-theory.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
just-war-theory.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Taking the film's opening 'This will not stand' seriously, Svolba and Betz read the Dude and Walter's rug campaign alongside the 1991 Gulf War through just war theory: just cause exists (soiled rug, invaded Kuwait), but Walter's gun at Smokey's foul line violates last resort and proportionality ('You're not wrong, Walter, you're just an asshole'), Aquinas's right intention is compromised when the ransom errand is motivated by the twenty grand, and Locke's case for right authority explains why justice cannot be left to 'fucking amateurs' like Walter, who overestimates injuries and retaliates disproportionately. Jus in bello discrimination fails everywhere — the neighbor's Corvette, the goons' mistaken Lebowski — and the escalation kills the innocent Donny.

just-war-theory.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
just-war-theory.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Jacob Held uses "War Pigs", "Electric Funeral", and "Children of the Grave" to teach just war theory's two halves, jus ad bellum (just cause, last resort, proportion) and jus in bello (proportion and discrimination toward non-combatants), reading Sabbath as condemning unjust wars like Vietnam and atomic overkill rather than all force, with Ozzy's "Thank God for the Bomb" voicing deterrence. Citing Walzer on "even in hell, it is possible to be more or less humane", he argues pacifism functions as a vital moral check, and that the war on terror fails just war standards outright: it cannot be won, so any means, assassination, torture, reclassifying terrorists outside both soldier and criminal law, are disproportionate and morally bankrupt, exactly the war-pig behavior the song's judgment day condemns.

just-war-theory.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
just-war-theory.title: 18. Wondering What It’s All For
just-war-theory.relation: Trip McCrossin follows Lord Grantham's 'We've dreamed a dream' - an allusion to Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 2 - through the warfare story line of seasons 2 and 3, from Matthew and William missing in action to Matthew's death under a truck. Mr. Lang's shell-shocked confrontations with the eager volunteer William and with Mrs. Patmore over her executed nephew Archie dramatize the gulf between those who know what war is like and those who can only imagine it, while the meaningless deaths of Matthew and the stretcher-bearer who is shot mid-sentence raise the Job-like problem of evil in the Dowager's words, 'we don't always get our just deserts.' The chapter argues against complacency about warfare's inevitability: because total war is dreamed up by the few, the rest of us should 'band together as Daniel,' interpret those dreams in advance, and refuse to let them come to be.

just-war-theory.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
just-war-theory.title: 19. Of Downton and Drones
just-war-theory.relation: Jai Galliott contrasts Downton's WWI, where aristocrats like Matthew died in the trenches alongside footmen like William on a roughly level playing field, with today's drone age, in which the fighting burden falls on the lower and middle classes (future Reaper pilots recruited from the 'PlayStation generation') while risk to our own side approaches zero. He traces unmanned weapons from WWI tele-operated motorboats, the Land Torpedo, and the Kettering Bug back through Agincourt's longbows and Omdurman's machine guns to the Gulf War and Kosovo, and argues that when technological asymmetry becomes extreme, Just War Theory breaks down: such war can hardly be a last resort, strains the proportionality calculus, and violates the chivalric justice of treating an equal as an equal (via Paul Kahn's paradox of riskless warfare and Robert Sparrow's threat-based immunity). His proposal is that highly asymmetric force be applied with restraint, more like international policing than war.

just-war-theory.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
just-war-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Air Force colonel James Cook walks the just war tradition through Ender's world: the Third Invasion is preventive rather than preemptive (with the 2003 Iraq war as the parallel), proper authority is undermined by the I.F.'s lies to its citizens, and last resort fails because the hive-queen was already trying to communicate with Ender. He contrasts Augustine's ban on killing in self-defense with Aquinas's permission, invokes Kant's formula of humanity for the buggers' rational nature and Cicero's hostis against dehumanizing enemies, and argues the I.F.'s failure to teach military ethics is itself part of the novel's tragedy.

just-war-theory.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
just-war-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Kody Cooper argues Ender's tortured conscience demonstrates the classical just war framework: from Augustine's axiom that peace is the end of war and the five jus ad bellum requirements, to the verdict that the Third Invasion fails right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality because the rational hive-queens were never given a real chance at coexistence. He reads the I.F.'s withholding of protection as throwing Ender into a Hobbesian state of nature where his fights with bullies count as private just wars, and concludes Ender carries the sins of the I.F. and humanity rather than his own guilt.

just-war-theory.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
just-war-theory.title: What Promotes Moral Behavior
just-war-theory.relation: Matthew D. Atkinson and Darin DeWitt use the Canterbury's ignored mayday in 'Dulcinea' — Captain McDowell's 'let the good God Darwin sort it out' versus Ade Nygaard's appeal to law, karma, and obligation — to ask what binds people when no central authority enforces rules. Through Michael Walzer's just war theory they read the Earth-Mars war: moral language is not 'cheap talk' (even Errinwright must dress aggression as peace and manipulates Reverend Volovodov's words), aggression and imminence govern when to fight, and five 'how to fight' principles — noncombatant immunity on Eros and Ganymede, POW rights for the Martian marines on the Kittur Chennamma, leaders' rather than soldiers' responsibility (Fred Johnson's defection after Anderson Station), proportionality in Errinwright's 'a base for a base' Deimos strike, and the rejection of ends-justify-means utilitarianism — discipline even Holden and Amos as they reflect on free will and culpability. The chapter concludes The Expanse is optimistic: human decency survives even in the anarchic Belt because characters keep reflecting on what their obligations to one another are.

just-war-theory.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: Curry and Lang test 'War never changes' through Hobbes and Xunzi: the wasteland - where the Ghoul asks who ever elected the 'President' in 'The Trap' and Cooper Howard decays outside all political order - is Hobbes's state of nature of restless power-seeking, while Xunzi's claim that bad human nature needs ritual (li) and righteousness (yi) explains a world with no moral education, where Elder Cleric Quintus pairs noble talk with 'power is taken, not given'. Fallout's Great War then fails every just-war test: China's invasion of Alaska stretches just cause, the corporatist US lacks right authority, propaganda undid last resort, mutually assured destruction explodes proportionality, and Vault-Tec shelters plus battlefield mini-nukes breach discrimination and proportionality in bello - with Operation Anchorage's propaganda simulation illustrating the revisionist point that fighting cleanly cannot redeem an unjust war. China's 'righteous army' (yi bing) tradition - Sunzi's strategic restraint, Mohist defensive war, Mengzi's true king, Xunzi's punitive righteous war - leaves no trace beyond Captain Zao, so the war's constancy marks the failure of every philosophical attempt to bind war to justice.

just-war-theory.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
just-war-theory.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Richard H. Corrigan tests Robb Stark's war against Joffrey with just war theory, criteria for resorting to war (legitimate authority, just cause, right intention, last resort, probability of success, proportionality) and for conduct (discrimination, treatment of prisoners, no reprisals). Robb is a legitimate authority acclaimed King in the North, offers rejected peace terms, and fights cleanly - Jaime is humanely held at Riverrun while Sansa is beaten by Joffrey, and Gregor Clegane's murders, rapes, and the Dothraki sack of the Lhazareen mark the other side's atrocities. Yet Corrigan concludes Robb fails right intention: his dominant motive is vengeance for his father, not the free North he professes, so although we root for him, his war cannot strictly be called just.

just-war-theory.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
just-war-theory.title: a10.xhtml
just-war-theory.relation: Johnson tests the Battle of Five Armies against just war theory as developed from Augustine through Aquinas: the men under Bard satisfy legitimate authority, just cause and last resort (they bargained, even using the Arkenstone as leverage and trying economic pressure), the Elvenking explicitly waits rather than start 'this war for gold', while the dwarves fail the criteria because greed and pride are not just causes and a thirteenth-share was a cheap price for peace. The war that actually happens - the three armies uniting against Bolg's orc-host - is justified self- and other-defense, whereas the orcs' motives (revenge, plunder, conquest) are unjust. Against apparent pacifist evidence (Tom Bombadil, Frodo at the Shire 'scouring', Gandalf's 'pity' for Gollum), Johnson reads Tolkien's letters as endorsing war as sometimes necessary and sometimes 'in the right', though Tolkien rejects the theory's reasonable-chance-of-success condition given the hopeless stands at Helm's Deep and the Morannon.

just-war-theory.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: Perry frames Frank through Walzer's problem of dirty hands, taking its name from Sartre's play ('I have dirty hands right up to the elbows... Do you think you can govern innocently?') and Machiavelli's advice to 'enter into evil when forced by necessity' — the pilot's mercy killing of the dog and 'just shy of treason, which is politics' being the show's emblems. He maps the field onto the show: utilitarians for whom breaking rules can be right, absolutists like the bishop ('Love God, and love each other. Period.'), and Walzer's later 'supreme emergency' threshold deontology applied to Frank's child-killing drone strike and his desperate deal with Petrov in the Jordan Valley. The verdict: Frank's only edge over Heather Dunbar is a proven capacity to dirty his hands when needed, but he lacks the scruples that keep that capacity from becoming routine wrongdoing, so he is probably still the wrong man for the job.

just-war-theory.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
just-war-theory.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Melançon tests the Mockingjay revolution against the just-war tradition's three parts: jus ad bellum, jus in bello, and jus post bellum. The districts satisfy just cause, right intention, last resort, and proportionality against the Capitol, but stumble on competent authority — no legitimate state authorizes their rebellion — a problem the chapter says forces the tradition to admit popular self-determination. Both sides then violate jus in bello: the rebels' avalanche on the Nut fails military necessity and proportionality, and the bombing of the Capitol's child shields plus the medics treating them breaches distinction twice, making the rebels as bad as the Capitol. The contemplated final Hunger Games with Capitol children would violate jus post bellum, so the revolution was not a just war and only stumbles into peace.

just-war-theory.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
just-war-theory.title: 22 “Germany Has Declared War on the Jones Boys!” Asymmetric Strategy and Honor among Raiders
just-war-theory.relation: Reads Indy through Clausewitz's On War: as one man against a nation-state ('Germany has declared war on the Jones boys!'), he must fight asymmetrically — shooting the scimitar duelist in Cairo, letting the plane's propeller finish the chivalrous German strongman, ambushing convoys one or two foes at a time, and cutting the Temple's rope bridge to nullify Mola Ram's numbers. Because symmetric combat carries the honor code of chivalry and its absence shades into terrorism, the chapter asks whether fighting dirty for a good cause is permissible, contrasting Star Wars, whose rebels always win through decisive symmetric battles. Indy never lands the decisive blow — God and the British do — so he remains a beloved but 'unheroic' raider rather than a soldier.

just-war-theory.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
just-war-theory.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Asks whether SAMCRO's gun suppliers, the Real IRA, are terrorists or freedom fighters, using Walzer's definition of terrorism as random killing of innocents to spread fear and his combatant/non-combatant distinction. The Irish Kings pass as freedom fighters—Kutz's three criteria of internal ordering (the hierarchy that has Sean Casey strangle the turncoat Cameron Hayes), just aims (a united Ireland), and target discrimination fit them—whereas Jimmy O, recruiting children as young as ten and attacking anyone with Loyalist sympathies, fails; his real motive being profit, Fr. Ashby concludes 'he's not a soldier anymore, just a gangster,' prompting the chapter's new category: thug. Fr. Ashby's own complicity in a church execution, redeemed by becoming a hostage so Abel can return to Jax, closes the moral ledger.

just-war-theory.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
just-war-theory.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Runs SAMCRO's conflicts with the Mayans, the Lobos Sonora, and the ATF through just war theory's jus ad bellum, focusing on right authority: Clay's dismissal of Salazar ('I don't recognize your bullshit MC') is exactly how Walzer would treat Clay's own war declarations. Walzer's analogy of the sovereign state to Tara shooting her home-invader Kohn grounds the right of self-defense in sovereignty, and the chapter tests SAMCRO against four features of statehood and six of nationhood—brothers as compatriots, the club's founding history obligating Jax, church votes, Charming turf, the Reaper tattoo, and self-determination—to crown it a 'mini-nation-state on wheels.' The catch is Clay's own admission that Sons are US citizens: the United States remains sovereign over them, leaving open whether sub-state nations like SAMCRO (or the Palestinians) can ever legitimately declare war.

just-war-theory.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: David Boersema reads Star Trek as a survey of peace studies, distinguishing negative peace from positive peace via 'The Cloud Minders', where Troglyte Vanna demands her people's 'right to the clouds' in Stratos. Against Anan 7's 'we're a killer species' in 'A Taste of Armageddon'—explicitly mirrored in post-9/11 drone war and 'shock and awe'—he enlists Hobbes, Freud, and McCoy's defense of the dark Kirk in 'The Enemy Within' to question whether violence is natural, and treats Kodos's 'some had to die that others might live' in 'The Conscience of the King' as the utilitarian justification for atrocity. Gem's compassion in 'The Empath', Kirk sparing the Gorn in 'Arena', and the Horta's misread attack in 'The Devil in the Dark' display nonviolence, deterrence, and corrected perception as alternatives to war.

just-war-theory.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: Camosy takes up Randal's charge in Clerks that destroying Death Star II killed innocent independent contractors. Against utilitarian reasoning he deploys just war theory: terrorism is intentionally targeting innocents as a means, so Tarkin's destruction of Alderaan (and, he argues, Hiroshima) qualifies, while the Rebels, who would have been 'pleased' if the workers took the day off, do not. Since the crew was mostly conscripted clones and programmed droids with no moral responsibility, and destroying the station saved billions, the attack passes the proportionality test - an exercise in double-effect reasoning that asks fans to question the 'good guys lens.'

just-war-theory.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: LaRocca argues Boba Fett is best understood as an amoralist - neither a moral relativist nor an ethical egoist, but someone who has withdrawn from moral judgment altogether - reading his terse 'As you wish' to Vader and his insuring of Han's survival purely for payment as evidence. Through Michael Walzer's account of the soldier's constrained choice and the 'good mercenary' debate, he asks whether mercenary violence (Blackwater, private military contractors) really differs morally from a conscript's or clone's. The upshot is that Fett's grayness between Empire and Rebellion exposes amoralism as a surprisingly central part of political and military life.

just-war-theory.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
just-war-theory.title: Trust in the Force of Others
just-war-theory.relation: MacMullan reads Rogue One through Dewey's 'Creative Democracy': democracy is not Senates or constitutions but a lived faith in one's neighbors, and the Empire's deepest violence is the distrust it breeds — Cassian executing Tivik, Saw torturing Bodhi with Bor Gullet, Draven ordering Galen's assassination. Cassian violates Kant's Formula of Humanity by reducing Tivik to a container of secrets, and the Rebels' dirty-war methods strain Augustine's just-war conditions, yet Chirrut and Baze's friendship ('I'm not alone. I have you!') becomes the seed of recovered trust that stays Cassian's finger on the trigger at Eadu. The Yavin council's free debate and the Tantive IV corridor relay — Rebels dying to pass the Death Star plans hand to hand past Vader — enact Dewey's claim that democracy lives in personal attitudes and neighborly trust: rebellions are built on hope in each other.

just-war-theory.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
just-war-theory.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Shannon Ford reconstructs the Winchesters' ethics of killing: self-defense and defense of others justify lethal force, as when Sam kills Jeremy in 'Dream a Little Dream of Me' and Andy shoots Ansem to save Dean in 'Simon Said,' while Dean's refusal of Ruby's virgin-sacrifice spell in 'Jus in Bello' and sparing the disarmed Pa Bender mark lines they will not cross even when the math favors killing. Killing possessed innocents like Meg is treated as permissible only under necessity and with regret. The chapter then argues that once the brothers hunt to banish all demons from the world, their conflict is war rather than hunting, so just war theory (jus ad bellum and jus in bello) might license killings ordinary morality forbids, a slippage dramatized by Gordon's enjoyment of killing and Dean's unjustifiable killing of Amy.

just-war-theory.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
just-war-theory.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Browning shows that 'Jus in Bello' is built from Romero's Night of the Living Dead: the besieged police station is a 'survival space' (a form he traces to Matheson's I Am Legend), Henricksen takes Ben's role and Nancy Barbra's, and the massed possessed townspeople mirror the shuffling zombie horde. Inside that space the show stages a clash of values, Ruby's utilitarian spell requiring Nancy's heart against Dean's absolute refusal to kill an innocent ('your choice is not a choice'), resolved by the rock-salt-and-exorcism plan that kills no one. The survival space works as a proving ground for its occupants' values, and the ending, where Lilith slaughters Nancy anyway, indicts the heroes' scruples and asks what the body count says about the viewers who enjoyed it.

just-war-theory.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
just-war-theory.title: NOTES
just-war-theory.relation: Phillip Seng runs the human-Skynet war through the three parts of just-war theory and finds the moral ground shakier than it looks: T2's briefing reveals Skynet launched its strike only after humans tried to pull the plug, so the machines claim the same self-defense 'just cause' humans do, while Skynet flunks last resort (it decides 'in a microsecond' with no negotiation), legitimate authority, proportionality (killing everyone to avoid being switched off), and discrimination. He then shows Sarah becoming a Terminator herself when she locks her laser sight on the innocent Miles Dyson, violating the same just-conduct rules she judges the machines by, and stopping only at his crying family. The chapter closes by doubting the war could ever have a just resolution, since the films point toward genocide rather than a peace treaty with Skynet.

just-war-theory.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
just-war-theory.title: P A R T O N E
just-war-theory.relation: Christopher Robichaud's essay asks what morality can demand of Dr. Manhattan after the accident strips him of the moral emotions (in Jesse Prinz's Humean vein) needed to value persons, which is why he can tell Laurie 'I read atoms' and rank human life beside rubble. It then asks what grounds morality's authority over a being no one can punish, rejecting divine command theory (Manhattan's 'clock without a craftsman') and doubting Kant's rational grounding applies to someone lacking moral concepts, so 'no one is above the moral law' may rest on a brute fact. It closes on political morality: a United States made a hyperpower by Manhattan's service (as in his Vietnam intervention) may not claim a double standard, since sovereignty blocks preventive war even when the US would win at little cost.

just-war-theory.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: Gibson argues Rand's creation of the Asha'man and the Black Tower is a 'dirty hands' problem (Michael Walzer, tracing to Machiavelli): even in the just war against the Dark One, Rand does something morally objectionable by building men trained to be weapons and then, distrusting Mazrim Taim, abdicating oversight so Taim (a Forsaken) corrupts them. He reframes the Asha'man as lethal autonomous weapons, using the ICRC's Ingvild Bode on algorithmic bias in data, design, and use to argue Rand and Taim's biases were 'trained' into these walking weapons, and connects the speed and loss of control of autonomous war to WoT's theme of balance and the real-world ethics of emerging military AI.

just-war-theory.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
just-war-theory.title: Notes
just-war-theory.relation: Held examines the Tuatha'an Way of the Leaf as universal pacifism grounded not in religion, utility, or rights but in the metaphysical care of the self, echoing Gandhi's idea that violence taints the soul of the doer (shown by Adan exiling Lewin for rescuing raped girls and by Aram's tragic fall). He argues the Tinkers' pacifism, while idyllic, is untenable in a broken world: through Augustine's two cities, Aquinas's natural self-preservation and doctrine of double effect, and just war theory's jus ad bellum and jus in bello, he contends intentions matter and that no hero of WoT could be a pacifist, concluding the Tinkers free-ride parasitically on those who fight the Shadow and that their peace is not real peace but self-serving order-less quiet.

just-war-theory.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
just-war-theory.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
just-war-theory.relation: Taliaferro and Le Gall examine when a nation or athlete may justifiably boycott the Olympics, distinguishing 'material' from 'formal' contribution and weighing available alternatives and the stringency of values (e.g., Gandhi's boycott of British goods, apartheid boycotts, the Lysistrata sex strike). They argue attending is not itself endorsement of the host regime, so the heavy, often irrecoverable cost to individual athletes places a strong burden of proof on any boycott. Surveying the 1956, 1980 and 1984 boycotts (which changed little) and the 1936 Berlin Games (where Jesse Owens's participation did real good), they conclude only a credible threat of serious bodily harm clearly justifies boycotting.

just-war-theory.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
just-war-theory.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
just-war-theory.relation: Mahon asks whether Ride with the Devil endorses the proverb that all's fair in love and war, locating the film's moral core in its outsiders—the German immigrant Jake, the freed slave Holt, and the young widow Sue Lee. Against Sunzi's undiscriminating claim that warfare is the art of deceit, he argues the film sides with Machiavelli's Discourses distinction between honorable ruses of war and dishonorable perfidy: the bushwhackers' wearing of Union blue and Jake's lies are ruses, but the Lawrence massacre and refusing to ambush women under a truce mark limits Jake will not cross. In love, Sue Lee's shift from romantic lying to 'now is the truth' shows honesty is finally required, so all is not fair.

just-war-theory.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
just-war-theory.title: Technology and Ethics in The Day the Earth Stood Still
just-war-theory.relation: Skoble reads The Day the Earth Stood Still as an allegory about the ethics of force and technology. He argues Klaatu's ultimatum extends Mill's harm principle to the interplanetary level: societies may fight among themselves but not threaten others, so Gort's robot police enforce a right to peace that no one has a right to violate. He distinguishes the robots' narrow, non-paternalistic authority from Hobbes's absolute sovereign, defends the ultimatum as preemptive self-defense rather than a rights violation, and contrasts the film's trust in machines with the later technophobia of Colossus and The Terminator.

just-war-theory.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
just-war-theory.title: The Dialectic of King and X in Do the Right Thing
just-war-theory.relation: Silberstein reads Do the Right Thing as staging the ideological dialectic between Martin Luther King Jr.'s absolute nonviolence and Malcolm X's defense of retaliatory self-defense, both grounded in a theologically informed natural-law view of rights (King's Christian imago dei, X's Islamic tradition). He argues King mixes a deontological ethic (violence is always wrong) with a Gandhian consequentialist claim that violence begets violence, while X frames a race war as a just holy war. The film's Radio Raheem (LOVE/HATE knuckles), Buggin' Out's boycott of Sal's Wall of Fame, the Racial Slur Montage, and Mookie throwing the trash can dramatize whether ends justify means; the closing Sal-Mookie money exchange reframes racism as symptom of a deeper capitalist greed both King and X came to critique.

just-war-theory.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
just-war-theory.title: General Patton and Private Ryan The Conflicting Reality of War and Films about War
just-war-theory.relation: Fiala uses Patton's opening speech ("an army is a team… this individuality stuff is a bunch of crap") against Saving Private Ryan's mission to rescue one soldier to frame war's basic conflict between the collective and the individual, and to expose the problem of "realism" in representing war. He aligns the collectivist realist ethics of war against the just-war tradition's deontological respect for individuals as Kantian ends-in-themselves, and contrasts Patton's aerial, above-the-battle viewpoint with Private Ryan's first-person D-Day realism. Drawing on Tim O'Brien's claim that a true war story is never moral, and on Nussbaum's and Glover's moral imagination, he concludes that no film can synthesize war's public and private perspectives—mirroring the failure of moral imagination that produces war itself.

just-war-theory.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
just-war-theory.title: The Work of Art in the Age of Embedded Journalism Fiction versus Depiction in Zero Dark Thirty
just-war-theory.relation: Evans argues that Kathryn Bigelow's Zero Dark Thirty fails morally and epistemically because its immersive 'boots-on-the-ground' realism traps the viewer inside Maya's single point of view, so we can never see the CIA torture program's lunacy the way an outside witness would. Drawing on Wittgenstein's Tractatus claim that the subject is a limit of the world (the eye that cannot see itself), she shows how the film effaces its own privileged viewpoint to pass off a partial view as impartial reality. Against this she sets a Platonic point that genuine reality is glimpsed only through fiction that ironically juxtaposes contrasting viewpoints, citing scenes like the SEALs' banter and Maya's final weeping where the film briefly becomes true art. The 'depiction is not endorsement' defense collapses because the narrative logic still credits torture with finding bin Laden.

just-war-theory.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
just-war-theory.title: Terrorism, Counterterrorism, and “The Story of What Happens Next” in Munich
just-war-theory.relation: Foy reads Munich's Operation Wrath of God as Spielberg's argument for retribution over vengeance in state counterterrorism. Yvonne's Marcuse/Hegel relativism and the agents' 'think of yourself as a soldier' language-games are dismissed as Avner's psychological breakdown shows morality is objective. Foy deploys Nozick's five procedural differences between retribution and revenge and Kant's view of retribution as impersonal and rational, echoes Socrates in the Crito (retaliation harms one's own soul) via Avner's decay, and cites Aristotle's 'war for the sake of peace' and jus in bello discrimination/proportionality in the Hamshari and Jeanette assassinations.

just-war-theory.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
just-war-theory.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
just-war-theory.relation: Scruton reads the literature and music of hunting—Homer's Odyssey and Argos, Wagner's Parsifal, Tristan and the Ring, Melville's Moby Dick, Cooper's Last of the Mohicans, and English foxhunting from Sir Gawain to Surtees and Masefield's Reynard the Fox—as recovering the hunter-gatherer's sacred, totemic bond with animals and the theme of ritual sacrifice. He grounds the distinction between virtuous and 'lawless' hunting in Plato's Laws, where 'sacred hunting' of quadrupeds run down by men, horses, and dogs is defended as piety, and aligns it with Ortega's insistence on self-imposed limits that keep the hunt from becoming mere butchery.

just-war-theory.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
just-war-theory.title: 14. The Doctor as Philosopher The Collectivist-Realist Pacifism of the Doctor and the Quest for Social Justice
just-war-theory.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a 'collectivist-realist pacifist': morally opposed to war yet willing, as a last resort, to use lethal force for social justice. She places the Doctor on Cady's warism-to-pacifism continuum (past absolute and collectivist pacifism), augmenting it with Martin Luther King Jr.'s realist pacifism — ethical appeals 'undergirded by constructive coercive power' — and Gandhi's ahimsa and belief that no one is beyond redemption (the Doctor sparing Davros, offering enemies a choice). She tests Kant's duty ethics and respect for persons (Rule 1: the Doctor lies), Ross's prima facie duties, Mill's utilitarianism ('The Fires of Pompeii,' 'The Beast Below'), Gilligan/Noddings care ethics, and Wolterstorff's 'life of needs,' and reads 'The Day of the Doctor' as a Rawlsian veil of ignorance brokering Zygon-human peace.

just-war-theory.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
just-war-theory.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
just-war-theory.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable. He tests the orchestrated revolution against utilitarianism's greatest-happiness principle (Bentham, Mill's taxation-of-the-wealthy, Singer's impartiality) and against Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle versus Nozick's entitlement objection and Aquinas's just-war criteria, concluding each character's actions can be read as 'just,' which exposes anthropocentrism as the real veil.

heidegger-technology.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
heidegger-technology.title: Only a Jedi Can Save Us Forgetting and Recollecting
heidegger-technology.relation: Abrams reads the saga through Heidegger's philosophy of technology: the lightsaber Luke learns to feel as an extension of his body is the authentic 'ready-to-hand,' while the Death Star - a massive mechanical eye that enfames Alderaan on its viewscreen before destroying it - embodies the 'present-at-hand' gaze of enframing that converts nature into standing reserve (clone and droid armies, stormtrooper armor). Yoda on Dagobah is perfect attunement, an authentic being-in-the-world who is 'at home' with being, and the Force parallels Heidegger's being: everywhere, easily forgotten. Anakin's slide - slave of Watto, severed hand replaced by cybernetics, final encasement in Vader's armor - is progressive enframing and forgetting of his own being, and Luke's 'the name of your true self... you've only forgotten' is the recollection of being by which the Jedi, not a god, saves us.

heidegger-technology.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
heidegger-technology.title: U2 and Philosophy
heidegger-technology.relation: Thomson uses U2's self-declared postmodern phase to define postmodernity itself: a sensitivity to poetic polysemy against modernity's fantasies of total control (Heidegger's reduction of everything to optimizable resource), Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives - defended against the self-refutation charge and narrowed to the dying metanarratives of unity and emancipation - and the Marx-Nietzsche-Freud hermeneutics of suspicion that fragmented the subject, with Kierkegaard and early Heidegger as the resisters. Derrida's 9/11 analysis of autoimmunity and hauntology is read into 'Peace on Earth' and the sorrows that 'learned to swim' in 'Until the End of the World'. The payoff is a polysemic reading of 'Even Better than the Real Thing': risky as a seeming hymn to Baudrillard's simulacra, addressed to a live audience it celebrates a communal love 'even better' than personal love - Diotima's ladder generalized - making the postmodern U2 continuous with the 'Christ-ian' U2 of universal love, sealed by 'One'.

heidegger-technology.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
heidegger-technology.title: James Bond and Philosophy
heidegger-technology.relation: Zani reads the Q-branch scene through Heidegger's 'The Question Concerning Technology': technology as technê, a revealing and bringing-forth that turns dangerous when it reduces the world to standing-reserve and turns people into stockpilists, as with Goldfinger, who kills Jill Masterson over gold and cannot let anything he does not own exist. Bond's villains (Drax declaring 'What he doesn't own he doesn't want' before shooting pheasants for sport; Grant's garrote watch) use technology as domination and amusement, whereas Bond uses it defensively and refuses to be owned by it - hurling the ATAC off the cliff with 'That's détente' and preferring the lighter to the match 'until they go wrong'. The repeated match-and-lighter password exchange in From Russia with Love encapsulates the films' Heideggerian moral: a free relation to technology that uses tools when needed and lets them recede, rather than becoming what one controls.

heidegger-technology.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
heidegger-technology.title: James Bond and Philosophy
heidegger-technology.relation: McKinney argues that '007' is a technological construction distinct from the human James Bond: drawing on Dewey's broad view of technology as technique (the shaken martini as technological artifact), Heidegger's account of naming as revealing and enframing, and Don Ihde's technological embodiment (the party-game hand axe that is art, paperweight, or tool depending on perception). Film dialogue shows the naming at work: Moneypenny calls him 'James' but announces '007 is here' to M; Goldfinger greets '007' and is corrected with 'My name is James Bond'; M threatens '008 can replace you' and, in Die Another Day, declares 'You are no use to anyone now' while rescinding his status. The chapter closes with the Kantian point that persons must be treated as ends in themselves, yet the designation '007' constitutes Bond as precisely a replaceable means to MI6's ends.

heidegger-technology.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
heidegger-technology.title: iPod
heidegger-technology.relation: Raven reads design history as a pendulum between 'Beauty Waves' (Art Nouveau's sinuous decoration, 1960s psychedelia) and 'Truth Waves' (Art Deco functionalism, Le Corbusier's 'machine for living'), poles he grounds in Berkeley's 'esse est percipi' idealism versus metaphysical realism. The late-1990s blobject -- the iMac, the New Beetle, the MACH3 razor -- begins merging the waves through computer-aided design, and the iPod, launched five weeks after 9/11 and named for Kubrick's pod ('Open the pod bay door, Hal'), is the 'minimalist blobject' or 'squircle' where the merger completes. Reading the moment through Heidegger's claim that technology transforms human existence 'in its innermost recesses' and through Freud's pleasure versus reality principles, he argues the Iraq War sealed the reality principle into consumer design: 'our iPods now have edges.'

heidegger-technology.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
heidegger-technology.title: Thinking Inside the Pod
heidegger-technology.relation: Condella reads the opening of Saturday Night Fever -- Tony Manero strutting to 'Stayin' Alive' while delivering a can of paint -- as the iPod condition in miniature: music that alters rather than captures reality, now dial-up-able for workouts ('Eye of the Tiger'), bus rides, and grocery runs. Through Heidegger he argues the iPod is calculative thinking incarnate, annihilating the time, silence, and solitude meditative thinking requires (the shower as last refuge), and deepening technological homelessness by flattening every place into whatever soundtrack we choose -- the Rhine dammed into a 'gigantic gasoline station,' the iPod pushing us 'pretty far down' in Plato's Cave, its very possibility prepared by Descartes's thinking thing. Yet his wife's yoga instructor chanting on a Bronx bus shows the iPod can also open meditative space, so what Heidegger demands is not Luddism but Gelassenheit, a free relationship to technology.

heidegger-technology.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
heidegger-technology.title: The Verdict
heidegger-technology.relation: Turner runs an ethical audit of iPod use through Levinas's face-to-face: sharing one iPod with his wife forces 'musical justice' negotiations (veto power over a Motörhead cut, gnashing through Bette Midler), his toddler son's listening requires vigilance, and illegal downloading fails Levinas's test that morality begins by ceding 'my place in the sun' to the Other — hence Radiohead's pay-what-you-want release as the Levinasian move, and iPod cafés where strangers DJ for each other while language preserves alterity. Heidegger supplies the counterweight: the shuffle's 'openness to mystery' versus calculative mastery that reduces The Who's Tommy to the 'Pinball Wizard' riff and silences all non-digital media, just as Kant's conditions of possible experience (space, time) would silence things outside them. Derrida's point that categories contain traces of what they exclude illuminates unclassifiable marginal works — bluegrass Pink Floyd, San Francisco Symphony plays Metallica — and the verdict closes with Hölderlin's 'where danger is, grows the saving power also', exiting Plato's cave by thinking the iPod's ethics at all.

heidegger-technology.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
heidegger-technology.title: Where Pink Floyd Ends and Radiohead Begins
heidegger-technology.relation: Reisch asks whether Radiohead is the Pink Floyd of the twenty-first century and answers that the comparison misleads: where Barrett-era Floyd used electronics to escape into psychedelic fantasy, Radiohead's apparent space-rock is phenomenological, giving voice to pre-reflective experience of technological modern life.
