kingdom-of-ends.relation: McGrath and Tilahun ask whether hip hop is bad for women, setting protest and sex-positive tracks (Tupac's "Brenda's Got a Baby", Missy's "One Minute Man", Queen Latifah's "Ladies First", Ms. Dynamite) against endorsements of violence (N.W.A's "One Less Bitch", Snoop's "Can You Control Yo Ho?", 50 Cent's "P.I.M.P"). They apply Mill's harm principle - offend yes, harm no - Hume's counterfactual analysis of causation (the Derek Fisher shot case) to show that whether lyrics cause violence is an unsettled empirical question, Austin and Rae Langton's speech-act theory to argue rappers' cultural authority may let pimp lyrics subordinate women in a way pornography cannot, and Kant's kingdom of ends to charge misogynist lyrics with treating women as mere means.

kingdom-of-ends.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
kingdom-of-ends.title: From Cash to Kant—and Back Again
kingdom-of-ends.relation: Yolanda Estes pairs Cash with Kant as two duty-based moralists: Cash's Golden Rule in 'The Preacher Said, Jesus Said' parallels Kant's formula of humanity (never treating persons merely as means), and Cash's 'good heart' matches Kant's good will, since songs like 'Sam Hall,' 'Folsom Prison Blues' (the man shot in Reno 'just to watch him die'), and 'I Hung My Head' weigh inner motives over outcomes. Because earthly law never balances the moral scale, she reads Kant's kingdom of ends and Cash's apocalyptic kingdom of God in 'When the Man Comes Around' and 'God's Gonna Cut You Down' as parallel objects of faith: we must live as if perfect justice already prevails, working to improve this world rather than waiting for the next.

kingdom-of-ends.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
kingdom-of-ends.title: 15. Tell the Truth at All Costs
kingdom-of-ends.relation: Bowman argues Candor is the most philosophically important faction because its absolute honesty is Kant's ethics: truthfulness as a perfect duty grounded in free will, making even politeness 'deception in pretty packaging,' and forbidding a lie even when the Erudite come to Merciless Mart hunting Tris - which mirrors Kant's reply to Benjamin Constant that one must not lie even to the murderer at the door. Against this he sets Aristotle's virtue ethics, where truth bows to wisdom, justice, and fortitude when the choice is handing hidden Jews to the SS, and Bentham's utilitarianism, which Amity enacts when it lies at the gates to keep the peace and save lives. The Candor Manifesto's 'web of individual-to-individual relationships' and Kant's kingdom of ends explain why universal honesty alone could make truth safe - and why Christina, the Candor, is the one left standing when the city's deception finally destroys it.

kingdom-of-ends.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
kingdom-of-ends.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
kingdom-of-ends.relation: Bateman replies to Cogburn by recovering the alignment system's actual literary source: Moorcock's Elric saga, where Law and Chaos are rival political ideologies (conservative and liberal tendencies) held in check by the Cosmic Balance, so a Chaotic person need only refuse law's authority, not will horror, and Chaotic Good remains possible. He rejects Cogburn's 'sausage machine' reading of Kant's first formula in favor of the humanity formula and the Realm of Ends, and rejects act utilitarianism as a model of the Good alignment, since an overpopulation scenario shows Mill's calculus mandating culling-genocide and Bentham's felicific calculus cannot actually measure goodness. Drawing on Badiou's ethic of truths, Buddhist and Jain renunciation, and the true-Neutral Druid as servant of the Cosmic Balance, he argues neutrality between Good and Evil need not be monstrous and mourns 4e's 'childishly simplistic' new system.

mill-liberty.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
mill-liberty.title: Where I Don’t Want to Be
mill-liberty.relation: South reads Barbara's 'Where I don't want to be' monologue in Batgirl: Year One through Mill's On Liberty passage on people who ask not 'what do I prefer?' but 'what is usually done by persons of my station?' - the pressure to conform Barbara feels as a librarian with a denied police application and a father's expectations. He then argues neither utilitarianism nor Kantianism can guide such a life, since both exclude the question of what I want and who I am becoming; what Barbara needs - and we need - is to make our desires intelligible to ourselves and bridge the gap between who she is and who she wants to be ('Divine my own future... Not a page from someone else's book').

mill-liberty.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
mill-liberty.title: There Is What Could Be
mill-liberty.relation: Argues there is no single final 'best self' in the perfectionist quest: after the Joker shoots Barbara, Oracle: Year One has martial-arts teacher Richard Dragon ask 'Who are you?', and she emerges thinking 'I'm me — more me than I have ever been.' Against the conformity John Stuart Mill warned of, the chapter has Barbara leave Dick Grayson because he has 'managed to turn into Bruce' and keeps 'reminding me of what I once was' — the past acting as a retrograde exemplar and a Millian custom that blocks her next, still-unattained higher self.

mill-liberty.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
mill-liberty.title: Synthesis
mill-liberty.relation: Elizabeth Brake asks what freedom Dylan's outlaw persona - refusing Maggie's Farm, possessive love, and conformity - actually wins, framing the answer with Berlin's two concepts of liberty. Dylan's negations look like Berlin's negative freedom, but Hegel's critique of the "freedom of the void" shows mere refusal ends in emptiness, so she reconstructs a Millian and Emersonian ideal of self-realization for which negative liberty is only the condition. "To live outside the law, you must be honest" supplies the synthesis: outside social law the free person answers to the Emersonian law of his own nature and to undistorted honesty with others, a more severe morality Dylan shares with Emerson and Nietzsche.

mill-liberty.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
mill-liberty.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
mill-liberty.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. He reads the total improvisation learned at the Acid Tests ('the form that follows chaos'), the band's leaderless 'functional anarchy' — Lesh: if anyone tried to take charge 'it would just dissolve in their hands' — and its flat business hierarchy with roadies as corporate presidents as a spontaneous order lived at the edge of chaos. The Deadhead community's ritual communitas, analyzed through Victor Turner's separation-liminality-reincorporation model, amounts to an 'ironic sacramentalism' that achieves what social contract from Hobbes (force), Locke (property), and Rawls (self-interest) cannot: unity that transcends difference while leaving it in place.

mill-liberty.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
mill-liberty.title: John Henry, the Steam-Engine, and Folsom Prisoners
mill-liberty.relation: Mulnix pairs Cash with John Stuart Mill on the priority of quality of life over mere life: Mill's 1868 Parliament speech defends capital punishment as more humane than the "living tomb" of life imprisonment, and Cash agrees in the Folsom liner notes (the prisoner envying the cockroach that can leave) and in "The Mercy Seat," where the electric chair becomes both mercy and the throne of God. Mill's higher and lower pleasures, competent judges, and On Liberty's individuality illuminate Cash's gallery of fools, the "Folsom Prison Blues" narrator who shot a man just to watch him die, the mother-defying Billy Joe of "Don't Take Your Guns to Town," characters whose unreflective rebellion squanders rational freedom. John Henry, by contrast, exercised his higher faculties against the steam-engine and so died happy, proving the chapter's Millian thesis that freedom matters as a means to self-directed, deliberated happiness.

mill-liberty.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
mill-liberty.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Fairweather casts the campaign against Pullman's books as Socrates's trial rerun (impiety plus corrupting the young) and asks whether legally protected speech can still be morally wrong, weighing Mill's On Liberty point that children lack the 'maturity of their faculties' against the charge that Pullman's 'killing God' rhetoric inflicts spiritual violence on young believers, by his own image of intercision. The answer comes through Nietzsche's Three Metamorphoses: Asriel, Will, and Lyra play the lion that slays the great 'thou shalt' of the Authority, but the lion's destruction is only the possibility of freedom, since full freedom is Nietzsche's child creating its own values rather than lapsing into nihilism or Sartrean bad faith. Pullman's Republic of Heaven, with its virtues of courage, compassion, love, kindness, and curiosity held in community, is a social ideal rather than a radically Nietzschean one, so the charge of corrupting young readers is deflated.

mill-liberty.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
mill-liberty.title: A Little bit of Messi for our Life
mill-liberty.relation: The authors cast the contrast between disciplined European and improvisational South American football as Mill's struggle between liberty and authority: the coach's tactical orders are 'rules of opinion' the genius may defy, as Maradona did on his sixty-meter run to the Goal of the Century, while the harm principle marks the line at the 'rules of law' — FIFA's Laws of the Game. The Hand of God goal, which broke even a rule of law yet stood because 'a goal is scored when the referee says so', illustrates Searle's point that football's regulative capacity cannot guarantee its agreements, leaving a gap filled only by ethics and fair play. Following Wittgenstein's 'ethics and aesthetics are one and the same', they conclude that a bit of Messi-style rule-breaking — Messi replicated both Maradona goals in 2007 — is what makes football, and life, joyful and beautiful.

mill-liberty.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
mill-liberty.title: There’s Something Here that’s as Strong as Life
mill-liberty.relation: Argues Rush's lyrics cohere as libertarianism: Rand's rational self-interest in 'Anthem' and 'Something for Nothing,' Nozick's Wilt Chamberlain argument and Hayek's knowledge problem behind '2112' and 'The Trees,' Mill's 'experiments in living' in 'Witch Hunt' and 'Nobody's Hero,' and market-enabled tolerance and cosmopolitanism in 'Heresy,' 'Territories,' and 'Tai Shan.' Like Cygnus resolving Apollo and Dionysus, libertarianism takes the best of left and right, with individualism the constant running through Peart's career.

mill-liberty.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
mill-liberty.title: The Ideal Candidate
mill-liberty.relation: Nathan Zook uses the 'Royal Krabby' election from Vote for SpongeBob and the global-warming plot of SpongeBob Goes Green to weigh democracy. Mr. Krabs's rigged election, run only to sell patties, exemplifies C. Wright Mills's power elite manipulating the appearance of popular rule; Plato would bar Producer-class SpongeBob and Squidward from ruling and prefers educated Guardians, while Mill defends each citizen's liberty to choose and democracy's alliance with education (SpongeBob learns about global warming from Sandy). Aristotle's polity — citizens administering the state for the common interest — makes SpongeBob the ideal candidate because he saves Bikini Bottom without claiming power.

mill-liberty.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
mill-liberty.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Fitzpatrick asks whether Klosterman's low-culture project (tribute bands, Toby Keith, the McNuggets diet) is mere titillation or genuinely valuable. Bentham's pushpin-versus-poetry hedonism matches Klosterman's rejection of 'guilty pleasures,' while Aristotle's eudaimonia — and Plato's forms, on which a tribute band is a copy of a copy of a copy — condemns a life of amusement. Mill resolves the question twice over: higher and lower pleasures justify ranking Klosterman's contemplative criticism above mere sensation, and On Liberty's free market of ideas shows that even false or partial low-culture claims (about Garth Brooks, Spurlock's Super Size Me) keep high culture's truths from decaying into unexamined dogma.

mill-liberty.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
mill-liberty.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Takes apart Walt and Jesse's 'legalize it' excuse: Kantian autonomy would license adult drug choices, but knowingly self-harming meth use is a performative contradiction no rational adult can will, and Mill's utilitarianism condemns cooking because harms to all users must be weighed against one family's benefit. It reads the 'Cancer Man' revenge on Ken's BMW and the Tuco deal as proof that the meth world's criminality spreads like a cancer into Walt's ordinary life, and 'Gray Matter' as Greek tragedy - pride refusing Elliot's money when a way out existed. Against On Liberty's libertarian pull, it finally argues addicts forfeit full rational autonomy and so may be 'caged' by paternalistic law.

mill-liberty.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
mill-liberty.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: A provocatively sympathetic application of On Liberty: Mill's harm principle protects Jesse's drug use from punishment, and Mill's celebration of individuality and 'experiments of living' makes Walt's cooking an 'individual spontaneity' valuable precisely because it defies custom - Marie's anti-pot panic and Hank's beer-and-Cub-cigar double standard illustrating the 'magical influence of custom' and democracy's drift toward 'collective mediocrity'. Mill's temperance-era remarks that intoxication 'is not a fit subject for legislative interference' are extended from use to manufacture. The chapter's thesis: even when Walt is wrong, mere nonconformity 'is itself a service', making Heisenberg an unlikely hero of liberty and human progress.

mill-liberty.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
mill-liberty.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Judith Andre uses the show's cases - Alicia's overnight prison visit to Peter for case information in 'Conjugal', snatching evidence before the police in 'Hi', Kalinda's inadmissible but coercive evidence in 'Heart', and Will's advice to use perjured testimony in 'Long Way Home' - to ask whether the profession's zealous advocacy actually serves justice. She explains the adversary system's two-level defense (each side's pursuit of victory supposedly forces truth out, mirroring sport) and its weaknesses: money decides outcomes, and no one in the courtroom is responsible for the truth, as the buried Childs tapes in 'Hybristophilia' show. Individual liberty against state power justifies criminal defense at most, and she endorses David Luban's sober conclusion that the system is justified yet 'cannot mandate lawyers to cut throats', with Alicia remaining the show's uneasy, unreconciled conscience.

mill-liberty.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
mill-liberty.title: Futurama and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: In 'A Taste of Freedom,' Zoidberg eats Earth's flag Old Freebie on Freedom Day, is tried by Earth's Supreme Court, and his death sentence triggers a Decapodian invasion that enslaves Earth under the Mobile Oppression Palace. The chapter pits Mill's On Liberty defense of unpopular expression (mankind cannot silence a lone dissenter; unchallenged beliefs are mere 'true opinions' akin to prejudice) against Feinberg's offense principle, mapping the case onto Texas v. Johnson and the symbolic-speech line from Stromberg to Tinker. It ends with Zoidberg burning the flag 'to preserve the freedom it represents': liberty and majority will often conflict (doomsday devices, Proposition Infinity's robosexual marriage ban), so preserving freedom requires tolerating offensive expression.

mill-liberty.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
mill-liberty.title: 5. The Truth Shall Make Ye Fret
mill-liberty.relation: Watson uses The Truth - William de Worde's accidental invention of Ankh-Morpork's first newspaper and the plot to frame Lord Vetinari - to stage the three classic arguments for censorship: direct harm (character assassination 'works every day'), indirect harm (with MacKinnon's point that the speech of the dominant drowns out the subordinated, applied to speciesist insults at Koom Valley), and the false-beliefs argument. Against them stand the knowledge problem and the equality assumption: Mrs. Arcanum's deference to print, Vetinari's turtle-shaped-world joke, and the Montessori-Broca dispute show we never know in advance which beliefs are false, and any censor like Lord de Worde has his own agenda. Vetinari's verdict that 'free men pull in all kinds of directions' because 'pulling together is the aim of despotism' carries the chapter's Millian case that free speech is a horrible necessity.

mill-liberty.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
mill-liberty.title: 16. Artistic Expression in the Land of the Free
mill-liberty.relation: Argues that Hendrix's Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' links political and artistic freedom: Mill's On Liberty — the harm principle, liberty of tastes and pursuits, and originality against the despotism of custom — both protects and celebrates the performance, since disliking it is no ground for suppressing it. Tolstoy's What Is Art? then supplies the aesthetic verdict: art is the infection of others by sincerely, particularly, and clearly felt emotion, so the anthem, like Picasso's Guernica, is great art expressing bad feelings about Vietnam — unlike José Feliciano's sincere-but-vague ballad or Roseanne Barr's failed joke.

mill-liberty.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
mill-liberty.title: 22. A New Civil War
mill-liberty.relation: Horn reads Marvel's Civil War as an allegory of post-9/11 America's Patriot Act debate over security versus liberty: Iron Man takes Hobbes's side, treating unregulated superhumans as the state of nature - a 'war of every man against every man' - that the Registration Act's social contract and punishment-backed rules must end, while Captain America takes Mill's On Liberty side, insisting full freedom for human nature must not be ceded to a government that will overreach, with Spider-Man torn between the two like the American citizen. Invoking Habermas's communicative action and deliberative democracy from Between Facts and Norms, he blames the two camps for talking past each other - Cap walling himself off while Tony keeps reaching out - and prescribes genuinely open dialogue as the only bridge that can marry security and liberty before the country devolves into its own civil war.

mill-liberty.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
mill-liberty.title: 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom
mill-liberty.relation: Nash argues 1984 has been misread as a critique of state power alone; through Newspeak's silencing of thought (in the tradition Austin, MacKinnon, and Langton developed) it shows how any concentration of power oppresses via control of words, data, and information. Drawing on Goldstein's manual's debt to James Burnham's managerial revolution and Sheldon Wolin's 'inverted totalitarianism', she reads the non-centralized Oceania as a warning about non-state enemies: corporations, think tanks running the 'Tobacco Strategy', and global institutions peddling misleading poverty statistics. Popper, Arendt, and Berlin exemplify the state-focused liberalism she thinks blinded us to these horizontal threats, while the Newspeak appendix's past tense shows Orwell expected totalitarianism to be beatable through evidence and democracy.

mill-liberty.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
mill-liberty.title: After the Waldo Moment
mill-liberty.relation: Littmann reads The Waldo Moment through Donald Trump — Waldo's 'knobber' and 'dickhead' taunts anticipate 'Little Marco' and 'Crooked Hillary' — to ask what is wrong with mockery and disrespect in democratic politics. Plato's Meno shows why true beliefs acquired by mockery rather than understanding are unstable and steerable toward any content, and ad hominem attacks substitute ridicule for engagement with arguments. Mill's On Liberty arguments against censorship and orthodoxy — we might be wrong, collision with error clarifies truth — show that refusing to engage opponents (as Waldo refuses Monroe) locks everyone in 'reality bubbles,' and the chapter concludes that letting anger and mockery replace reasoned engagement, as when Waldo's followers riot, sabotages democracy.

mill-liberty.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
mill-liberty.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Littmann asks how a program built on mockery, falsehoods like Wyatt Cenac's Sarah Palin jokes and the 'santorum' coinage, can be a serious political voice, situating it in the tradition running from Aristophanes' roasting of Cleon and his distorting Clouds portrait of Socrates through Juvenal to Twain. He rejects Juvenal's hope that shame reforms the mocked (people do not listen to those who disrespect them) and argues mockery's real value is keeping issues like racism, war and Glenn Beck's rhetoric in public consciousness. Deploying Mill's On Liberty arguments against censorship, that silencing assumes infallibility and truth is sharpened by collision with error, he warns mockery works like censorship when audiences dismiss mocked views without consideration, the key difference being that Limbaugh demands to be taken seriously while Stewart bills himself as a comedian, and closes with Plato's Meno: opinions must be 'shackled' by understanding why they are true, not adopted because a comedy laughed at the alternative.

mill-liberty.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
mill-liberty.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Vanderheiden treats America (The Book)'s textbook parody as serious democratic theory: its 'Democracy Inaction' diagnosis (a president chosen from a field of two, 99% incumbency, lobbyists as 'the white knights of democracy') tracks the thin versus thick democracy distinction and Benjamin Barber's deliberative democracy, with Putnam's social capital as the remedy for the satirized life cycle of national decline. The 'Dress the Supreme Court' gag, Senate color-by-numbers, and third-party graveyard expose representational exclusion, while the media chapter indicts conglomeration for killing the press's watchdog role, invoking Mill's marketplace of ideas. The Earth (The Book) postscript notes that social contracts were historically written without the assent of the women and minorities they subjugated.

mill-liberty.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
mill-liberty.title: “Cogs that Fit, that Cooperate by Design”
mill-liberty.relation: Reads the government ban on Supers in The Incredibles through Locke's Letter Concerning Toleration and Mill's On Liberty, arguing the ban rests on the 'PREFER' principle — society's likings and dislikings as law — fed by perception management (Winston Deavor's suit-cameras PR campaign) rather than reasons, just as Locke diagnosed intolerance, not diversity of opinion, as the cause of civil strife. Mill's harm principle, illustrated by Elastigirl's 'drinking on duty' remark, should instead govern, so banning Supers' powers and pressuring Dash to suppress his speed ('Everyone's special, Dash' / 'Which is another way of saying no one is') is tyranny. Mr. Huph's 'cogs that fit, that cooperate by design' image of Insuricare shows the conformist cost: a society built on preference rather than reasons will never produce great thinkers.

mill-liberty.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
mill-liberty.title: Is Propaganda Permissible
mill-liberty.relation: Manninen surveys Disney's WWII Donald Duck shorts (Donald's Decision, The New Spirit, Der Fuehrer's Face, Commando Duck) to argue propaganda is not only the enemy's tool and not always wrong. Hume's 'slave of the passions' explains why The Spirit of '43 works through the Thrifty-versus-Spendthrift slugfest rather than its implicit argument, and Mill's fallibility-corrigibility case for free expression gives even propaganda a seat in public discourse — though Mill's caveat against expression that instigates mischievous acts marks the real limit, which the contrast with the Axis's 'barefaced lies' (and the Yensid thought experiment) is meant to satisfy.

mill-liberty.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
mill-liberty.title: Notes
mill-liberty.relation: The chapter asks whether Fallout's chems should be banned and answers no on Millian grounds: chem addiction harms only the user (and is trivially curable at any wasteland doctor, unlike Cait's Psycho addiction in Fallout 4, which shows what real addiction actually costs), so the New California Republic's firing squads for chem dealers and Caesar's Legion's crucifixion of the smuggler Anders violate the Harm Principle. Combat chem use is self-protection, drugging a Charisma check harms no one because NPCs act on their own programmed preferences, and paternalism fares no better in a wasteland where a failed speech check can get you killed. The analysis then extends to real-world performance-enhancing drugs: permissible for soldiers fighting a just war, but coercive in sports, where PED users force clean athletes to choose between their own health risks.

mill-liberty.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
mill-liberty.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Don Fallis starts from Joffrey's lie about Arya and the butcher boy Mycah - which costs Mycah's life and Sansa's direwolf Lady's - to dissect lying versus other deception in Westeros: Catelyn accusing Tyrion is not lying because she believes it, Ned's coerced confession at the Great Sept is a real lie (Austin's duress excuse fails, as Thomas More's counterexample shows), and Ned's silence about Joffrey's parentage before the dying Robert is deception by withholding that he himself mistakes for lying. He asks whether lying is morally worse than misleading - Kant and Chisholm say yes, Williams and Scanlon no - testing breach of invited trust (Mirri Maz Duur's 'only death may pay for life'), responsibility-shifting to the audience ('That was a lie you told yourself'), and preserved autonomy (Kant's Groundwork, Mill's On Liberty). Finally, is it worse to lie to a king? Consequentialism explains the danger of misleading the powerful, oaths of fealty and divine right suggest a special duty, but Locke's demolition of divine right (seconded by Monty Python) leaves only the punishment, not the wrongdoing, greater.

mill-liberty.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
mill-liberty.title: Through the Mist and the Madness: Metallica's Message of Nonconformity, Individuality, and Truth
mill-liberty.relation: Thomas Nys argues Metallica's early message of nonconformity and individuality ('Metal Militia', 'Motorbreath') converges with Mill's On Liberty: conformity withers human capacities and breeds a stagnant society. Mill's higher pleasures and Nozick's experience machine show why real happiness requires autonomy and earned achievement rather than passive pleasure - the point of 'Escape''s 'Life's for my own to live my own way'. He reads 'Leper Messiah' and 'Eye of the Beholder' as Metallica's versions of Mill's defense of free inquiry and truth against mindless conformity and censorship.

mill-liberty.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
mill-liberty.title: The Office and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Nys asks whether political correctness is a genuine moral demand or mere verbal hygiene, using the British Office: Gareth's racist BMC joke, Brent aborting it when Oliver the Black coworker arrives, the 'wanking claw' impression, and the porn email with Brent's head pasted onto a woman's body. He argues words genuinely wound (Brent's 'sticks and stones' rehearsal collapses when Gareth reveals his cruel nicknames) but that offense is wrong as disrespect for human equality rather than as a feeling, an account filled out with Frankfurt's claim that our identity depends on what we care about, so the non-targeted can be offended too. After weighing Mill's defense of free discussion for social progress, the pornography debate (in which reduction to body parts is exactly what degrades, as Brent complains he was 'objectified'), and Marx's notion of ideology as a concealing set of ideas behind a 'white male' bias, he concludes that Brent's flaw is looking good rather than being good, and that PC language is rhetorical make-up over persisting inequality.

mill-liberty.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
mill-liberty.title: Robust Social Critique
mill-liberty.relation: McGowan asks how SNL gets away with offensive material, from Larry David's concentration-camp monologue to the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' and 'Nude Beach.' He argues censorship fails because offense is historically relative and slippery-slope prone, and that on Mill's On Liberty the harm principle never licenses suppressing speech SNL viewers can freely avoid, a point he sharpens with Feinberg's Volenti maxim and the offense principle. He closes by defending offensive comedy as robust social critique: Mill's fallibilist case that free speech drives human progress, with Baldwin's Trump and Tina Fey's Charlottesville bit as comedians speaking truth to power.

mill-liberty.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
mill-liberty.title: Live from Omaha
mill-liberty.relation: Irwin argues that SNL's caricatures (Fey's Palin, Baldwin's Trump, Aristophanes' Socrates in the Clouds) misrepresent their targets and that learning politics from comedy traps viewers in ideological bubbles, since satire flatters rather than informs. He introduces the Ideological Turing Test, adapted from Turing's test: state your opponent's view so accurately and sympathetically that a neutral observer cannot tell it is not yours, and grounds the duty to learn the other side from its own partisans in Mill's On Liberty. The 2016 'Bubble' sketch passes the test, he says, but SNL's liberal bias (gentle Sanders, untouchable Obama) rarely challenges its audience, and a conservative 'Live from Omaha' alternative would just rebuild the bubble on the other side.

mill-liberty.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
mill-liberty.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
mill-liberty.relation: Koepsell surveys sixteen years of South Park blasphemy from 'Jesus vs. Santa' through 'Red Hot Catholic Love', 'Bloody Mary', the Scientology of 'Trapped in the Closet', and the censored Muhammad episodes 'Cartoon Wars' and '200'/'201', arguing that the show's equal-opportunity mockery is legitimate cultural criticism, not a sign of civilizational decline. Tracing the legal history from nineteenth-century blasphemy prosecutions through Cantwell v. Connecticut and Chaplinsky, he adopts Mill's On Liberty case that only free and open discussion of even the most sacred beliefs can shake out truth and keep opinion from becoming dead dogma. Comedy Central's black-screening of Muhammad while airing far coarser blasphemy was incoherent capitulation: nothing on the show is sacred, tolerance requires neither silence nor immunity from ridicule, and the Mormon Gary's 'suck my balls' sums the show's loving-but-mocking attitude.

mill-liberty.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
mill-liberty.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
mill-liberty.relation: Murtagh asks whether the Virgin Mary statue spraying menstrual blood on a cardinal and the pope in 'Bloody Mary' is morally wrong, and answers with a utilitarian weighing of blasphemous humor's consequences. On the negative side, offense to believers (with Cartman's sudden piety about Family Guy's Muhammad in 'Cartoon Wars Part I' articulating the utilitarian worry that millions watching intensifies the harm) and a possible desensitizing erosion of tolerance; on the positive side, pleasure and the show's power to provoke thought, as when Randy learns from Stan that his five sober days came from his own willpower, not 'divine ass blood'. Drawing on Mill's greatest happiness principle and On Liberty's defense of open discussion, he concludes blasphemous humor is morally justified when it is an important part of a presentation with significant social value, and wrong when used merely to piss people off or for profit.

mill-liberty.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
mill-liberty.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
mill-liberty.relation: Takes 'Douche and Turd' — Stan refusing to choose between Giant Douche and Turd Sandwich, Puff Daddy's gun-toting 'Vote or Die', and his banishment — plus the kindergarten tie in 'Trapper Keeper' (Flora's indecision, Rosie O'Donnell's recounts) to ask whether every vote counts in a two-party system. Through Locke, Stan's abstention becomes a withdrawal of consent to be governed by either mascot; through Mill, non-voting threatens the active participation that gives institutions legitimacy and wards off tyranny of the majority, even as the chapter catalogs real disincentives: the Electoral College's spectator states, the 2000 Florida debacle, and Commission rules excluding third parties like Nader. Habermas closes the chapter: the vote, read as positive liberty, is the paradigm of rights and inclusion in a community of equals.

mill-liberty.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
mill-liberty.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
mill-liberty.relation: Challenges the received libertarian message of 'Medicinal Fried Chicken' — Randy giving himself testicular cancer for a marijuana prescription, Cartman bootlegging KFC in a Scarface parody after Colorado bans fast food — by pressing Mill's liberty principle on what 'harm' means: Mr. Garrison's plot to murder the Queer Eye cast is immediate harm, but the S&M Mr. Slave displays to schoolchildren in 'The Death Camp of Tolerance' is only indirect, psychologically mediated harm Mill cannot clearly handle. Addiction then undermines Mill's assumption of sovereign tastes: corporations can shape desire without coercing anyone, so the libertarian 'omnicompetent individual' is a myth. Mead's intersubjectivity (Randy smoking pot before Officer Barbrady, blind to how Jimbo sees him) grounds the constructive claim that selves are socially formed, and the shark-tank defecation and Prisoner's Dilemma examples show why collective harms need rules and regulation.

mill-liberty.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
mill-liberty.title: Basketball Purists
mill-liberty.relation: Kretchmar defends a 'modified purist' view that team-oriented, fundamentals-based basketball is generally better than the individualist modernist game, offering three arguments. The functionalist argument borrows Searle's account of constitutive rules to say ten-person interactive complexity makes a richer, more durable 'test' (like chess vs. tic-tac-toe); the variety argument uses Mill's On Liberty to warn that market pressures homogenize basketball toward football; and the communitarian argument uses MacIntyre's notion of a 'practice' with internal goods to show ESPN Streetball's isolated one-on-one feats erode basketball as a cooperative practice.

mill-liberty.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
mill-liberty.title: Fevered Desires and Interracial Intimacies in Jungle Fever
mill-liberty.relation: Sundstrom uses Jungle Fever to dismantle the taboo (white and black versions) against interracial intimacy, treating Flipper and Angie's affair and the War Council's objections as a debate about black solidarity, loyalty, and self-hatred. He answers the War Council by invoking Mill's On Liberty and the tyranny of public opinion to defend sexual autonomy, and argues that demanding partners for political solidarity reduces them to props (objectification). He reads the psychoanalytic charge that interracial love is 'fevered' racial pathology as derived from Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks but ultimately baseless, and criticizes Lee for a puritanical ending that hides Orin and Paulie while exposing Flipper and Drew, failing to show interracial love as ordinary.

mill-liberty.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
mill-liberty.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
mill-liberty.relation: Steve Benton reads Burton's Sleepy Hollow as a meditation on rationality and anti-intellectualism, contrasting it with Washington Irving's original where brainy Ichabod is run out of town. Burton's Ichabod, a rationalist constable, prevails only after tempering his faith in science with emotion, intuition, and the spirit world associated with his mother and Katrina—the paper-disk toy (bird/cage) symbolizing how head and heart must spin together. Benton maps the film's models of rationality onto Plato's philosopher-king and distrust of the mob and Hobbes's war of all against all (Burton's corrupt New York and Sleepy Hollow) versus the collaborative, democratic reason of Locke, Mill's On Liberty, and Dewey, invoking Aristotle and Nussbaum on emotion's role in practical wisdom; he leaves open whether the film is transgressive or a conventional 'woman heals cold rational man' Hollywood tale.

mill-liberty.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
mill-liberty.title: 31. Out of Step with the World
mill-liberty.relation: Lustila and Olsthoorn ask what makes hardcore punk's cultural nonconformity ethically valuable, distinguishing it from Kantian autonomy (self-governance via Korsgaard) and Taylor-style authenticity using lyrics by Void, Negative Approach, and Burn. They offer two justifications: a contingent one, on which countercultures like vegan straight edge replace harmful mainstream norms (though hardline militancy fails the test), and a general one drawn from Mill's On Liberty - even the mere example of nonconformity, from punks and posers alike, enlarges the space of 'experiments of living' and pluralism everyone needs against the tyranny of majority opinion. Berlin's value pluralism backs the general value: countercultures are 'a wrench in the system' that multiplies the models of living available to all.

mill-liberty.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
mill-liberty.title: 4. Better Call the DEA
mill-liberty.relation: White uses Better Call Saul's cartel world—the 'Bagman' shootout, Mike's account of Philadelphia police corruption, Tuco's meth-driven violence—to frame the ethics of the U.S. War on Drugs, tracing its racist origins and drawing a sustained analogy to alcohol Prohibition. She marshals Mill's harm principle from On Liberty to argue adults may choose their own risks absent harm to others, making criminalization inconsistent given legal alcohol. She then fairly lays out the pro-War case (Bennett on deterrence, the Robins Vietnam-heroin study, Mill's own bar on selling oneself into slavery applied to addiction) before favoring decriminalization on the Portugal model.

mill-liberty.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
mill-liberty.title: 10. Some Dark Genie
mill-liberty.relation: Calef asks whether Bourdain's choice to become a heroin addict could be rational and responsible, using Mill's On Liberty and Harm Principle (including the voluntary-slavery exception) to argue addiction is reversible and can minimize suffering when alternatives are bleak. He then reads Bourdain's self-destructive drives — the drunk cliff-driving 'death trip' — through Freud's death drive (Thanatos) and Schopenhauer's pessimism, concluding the 'dark genie' was partly disease-like and thus not wholly blameworthy.

mill-liberty.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
mill-liberty.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Greg Littmann defends political mockery as an ancient tradition (Aristophanes, Juvenal, Twain) but warns, using J.S. Mill's On Liberty, that if viewers let The Daily Show's jokes substitute for reasoned judgment the effect is like censorship, silencing ideas that must be heard to be understood. He cites Mill's arguments against silencing discussion and Plato's Meno on shackling true opinion with reasons, arguing that Stewart's virtue over Limbaugh is that he bills himself as comedy ('the show that leads into me is puppets making crank phone calls') and never presents mockery as a replacement for informed citizenship.

mill-liberty.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
mill-liberty.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Vanderheiden reads America (The Book) as a work of democratic theory dressed as textbook parody, arguing its satire is a 'rhetoric of challenge' enacting deliberative democracy. He contrasts 'thin' (merely electoral) with 'thick' participatory democracy using Putnam's social capital and Barber's strong democracy, and invokes J.S. Mill's 'marketplace of ideas' and On Liberty to indict media conglomeration for killing the press's watchdog role. He reads the companion Earth (The Book) through social-contract theory (Hobbes-style), noting its jab that contractual authority historically required the assent of subjugated groups it never obtained.

mill-liberty.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
mill-liberty.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
mill-liberty.relation: Dromm and Salter analyze Persuasion by distinguishing persuasion (rational, argument-based belief change), influence (nonrational, resting on a person's charisma or status, as Lady Russell has over the Elliots), and 'overpersuasion.' Against Captain Wentworth's view that persuadability is a vice and firmness of mind a virtue (his hazelnut analogy, Louisa Musgrove's fatal fall from the Cobb), they adapt Mill's On Liberty: just as free discussion lets a society exchange error for truth and gain confidence in true beliefs, a persuadable person is happier and epistemically better off. They add that Anne broke the engagement from a sense of duty, not fickleness, and it is her own persuasion that finally reunites her with Wentworth.

mill-liberty.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mill-liberty.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mill-liberty.relation: Tait Szabo defends the guiltless consumption of pornography using Mill's Harm Principle from On Liberty: harmless conduct, even if deemed immoral, should not be censored. Classifying porn into erotica, sexist, dominance, and violent types (excluding child porn and snuff as clearly prohibitable), he rebuts the arguments that porn is prostitution (citing California v. Freeman), that loveless sex is wrong, that porn non-rationally causes or conditions violence against women, and the anti-porn feminist claim that it eroticizes patriarchal subordination. Each argument, he holds, either lacks causal evidence or would equally condemn romance novels, sexist jokes, and Cinderella — so under Mill, censorship is unjustified.

mill-liberty.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mill-liberty.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mill-liberty.relation: Miles argues that the popular 'porn is free speech applied to sex' defense (Wendy McElroy, Nadine Strossen) fails, using the contrast of Cohen's 'Fuck the Draft' jacket versus a hypothetical 'Schmoen' having public sex to express an opinion. He holds that political and religious speech persuade at a distance whereas public pornography coerces by making the unwilling audience actually perform the act of looking, so treating boobs like bumper stickers would be illiberal. The reasoning leans on a Millian harm/liberty framework: expression that merely offends is protected, but expression that forces others into an act crosses a line, so porn must be defended on privacy/autonomy grounds rather than as free speech.

mill-liberty.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mill-liberty.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mill-liberty.relation: In this interview, dominatrix-director Mz. Berlin answers the classic moral objections to porn from inside the industry: she rebuts objectification by insisting she chooses to be 'a commodity' and that choice makes it permissible, rejects the rape-myth/harm claim by citing declining rape rates and comparing porn to violent TV, and grounds BDSM's legitimacy entirely on INFORMED CONSENT, contrasting her voluntary waterboarding with her real torture abroad. Endorsing a strongly Millian self-ownership view ('my body is my own commodity'), she extends consent to selling kidneys, assisted suicide, and even display of her corpse, while drawing hard limits at sex with children, animals, or the dead where genuine informed consent is impossible. She also frames femdom porn as subverting male hegemony and normalizing fluid gender roles.

mill-liberty.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
mill-liberty.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
mill-liberty.relation: Yim argues that clothing is a primary vehicle for autonomy, authenticity, and moral solidarity. Drawing on Mill's *On Liberty* and 'experiments in living,' he treats a teenager testing modest-vs-expressive dress against her mother, and 'Fashion Freaks' patterns for wheelchair users, as cases where wardrobe choice actualizes self-determination. He then reads dress as an emblem of communal solidarity and critique — the 1968 Smith/Carlos Olympic salute, the Israeli Kibbutz and Amish plain dress (with Rumspringa as a test of authenticity), gang colors, hippie androgyny, vegan 'cruelty-free' clothing, gay Levi's 501s, and Lubna Hussein's trouser trial in Sudan — concluding 'we are what we wear.'

mill-liberty.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
mill-liberty.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
mill-liberty.relation: Musselman, Frohardt, and Lynch defend adult cannabis use through Mill's Harm Principle, using the hypothetical 'Patrick the pot smoker'—a professional who grows and smokes moderately on Friday nights—to argue that competent adults' self-regarding conduct is their own affair and does not violate the 'distinct and assignable obligations' Mill owes to family. They marshal health data (no lung-cancer link, negligible secondhand exposure, neuroprotective effects) to rebut the harm-to-others claim, and invoke Mill's higher intellectual pleasures plus the Michael-Phelps case to argue prohibition wastes resources better spent on the greater harms of alcohol and tobacco.

mill-liberty.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
mill-liberty.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
mill-liberty.relation: Scott reads three landmark climbs as expressions of the tension between individual freedom and community standards. He casts John Bachar's bold, ground-up, run-out Bachar-Yerian and its self-mastery ethic as a partial embodiment of Nietzsche's Übermensch and will to power, and Alan Watts' rule-breaking sport route To Bolt or Not to Be as an exercise of Mill's On Liberty defense of originality and diversity that benefits the whole community. Against both thinkers' negative view of community, he uses Charles Taylor's 'horizon of significance' to argue that Sonnie Trotter's The Path gains its meaning only through dialogue with the climbing community and its traditions.

mill-liberty.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
mill-liberty.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
mill-liberty.relation: Felipe Carvalho frames a friend 'Toby's' worry – tattoos are forever, so should one be impulsive or cautious? – as a problem about bodily freedom versus irreversible change. He rejects the hedonist position (seize the day, regret is just part of freedom) as too simple and the Millian position (drawing on Mill's On Liberty argument that one cannot freely alienate one's freedom, as in selling oneself into slavery) as too precautionary, noting his friend's happy irreversible ear surgery. He proposes a 'middle path' learned from the tattoo community: a complex interplay of motif, the tattooist-as-artist, and the body-as-canvas that lets permanence guide more principled choices – so no 'I Love Becky' tattoos.

mill-liberty.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
mill-liberty.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
mill-liberty.relation: Woods asks whether the claim 'tattooing is immoral' can be defended, taking Adolf Loos's 1908 'Ornament and Crime' (tattooed free men are latent criminals or degenerate aristocrats) as his provocation. He rejects Loos's equation of tattooing with murder, since tattooing is voluntary and self-regarding, but resists the liberal 'sovereign self' reply drawn from Mill's On Liberty by arguing autonomy and the body are relational, not absolute, so a person's self-regarding choices remain open to reasoned challenge and even regulation. He proposes regret evidence in informed consent and an age-25 minimum, concluding tattooing is a matter of both taste and morality.

mill-liberty.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
mill-liberty.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
mill-liberty.relation: The essay argues that soaring tuition drives college students into sexual self-commodification—egg-selling ('Pay your tuition with eggs'), craigslist/backpage escorting, and dorm-porn webcam sites like VoyeurDorm and CocoDorm—and reads these cases through Kant's second formulation, condemning them as treating oneself and others as mere means rather than ends of intrinsic dignity. It applies Marx's notion of false consciousness to Natalie Dylan's virginity auction and Ashley Dupré's 'empowerment' claims, comparing them to women choosing high heels as internalized oppression. It uses Rousseau's Social Contract and Mill's On Liberty to argue that prostitution is a form of illegitimate 'voluntary slavery' because one cannot rightly alienate one's own inalienable freedom, and contrasts coerced cases (Helena in Singapore, Rosie Reid's traumatic auctioned deflowering, John Gechter's porn suspension from a Christian college) with less-coerced ones to argue moral concern should track the degree of circumstantial coercion.

mill-liberty.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
mill-liberty.title: 28. South Park as Philosophy Blasphemy, Mockery, and (Absolute ) Freedom of Speech
mill-liberty.relation: The chapter argues, via the 'Cartoon Wars,' '200,' and '201' episodes, that South Park makes five arguments about free speech and evaluates each. Johnson defends the claims that catering to terrorist threats breeds more terrorism and that mockery is 'all or nothing,' but rejects South Park's implied case for absolute free speech: using Mill's On Liberty and harm principle he shows the 'marketplace of ideas' fails (citing 8kun and Fox News), and using Popper's paradox of tolerance he argues intolerance cannot itself be tolerated. He proposes a middle-ground 'PC Principle' where society, not the state, curbs harmful speech through deplatforming and public shaming while distinguishing tolerance from acceptance.

mill-liberty.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
mill-liberty.title: 65. Louis CK as Philosopher The King and His Fall
mill-liberty.relation: Marra Henrigillis first shows CK as 'philosopher king of comedy'—his cell-phone/'forever empty' bit echoing Buddhist and Stoic teaching on sitting with suffering, his 'why?' bit echoing Quine on not ontologizing, his 'So Did The Fat Lady' episode exposing how society denies fat women full humanity—then uses his 2017 misconduct scandal to stage competing verdicts: the feminist case for banning him (rape culture, power dynamics), Plato on censoring vicious art, Mill's four-part defense of free expression and Nozick's free-market/entitlement view against cancellation, and Aristotle's virtue ethics (character judged over a whole life) plus Pompa's prison-education view that no one is only their worst act.

watchmaker-argument.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
watchmaker-argument.title: Superheroes, Duty, and the Biggest of Big Pictures
watchmaker-argument.relation: Argues that non-theistic karma undermines itself: the impersonal moral laws connecting each soul's deeds to its circumstances in the next life would be enormously complex and would serve the moral end of justice, and order that intricate serving a moral end demands an intelligent cause, so reincarnation becomes evidence for God. It closes the chapter by comparing the universe's moral order to a superhero's origin story — it would have to begin with something like a God.

watchmaker-argument.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
watchmaker-argument.title: The Epilogue A Question of Belief
watchmaker-argument.relation: Systematically pairs Hume's philosophy of religion with Python parodies: Anselm's ontological argument fails because existence cannot be defined into a concept (the Yeti-spotter who never spotted one), with Arthur 'Two Sheds' Jackson, Ron Obvious, and Confuse-A-Cat illustrating the gap between conceivability and possibility; the Galaxy Song's cosmic order and the mock hymn 'All Things Dull and Ugly' stage the design argument and Hume's reply that creation shows moral indifference as readily as benevolence; and Brian's 'miracles' — being 'taken up' then spotted sprinting, curing Simon the hermit by landing on his foot — illustrate Hume's 'Of Miracles' on the unreliability of testimony. Hume's Natural History claim that the cause of religion is fear surfaces in the 'O Father, please don't boil us' hymn and in Arthur's groveling before a God who hates it. Both Hume and the Pythons end in suspended judgment about God — settled, if at all, only by the wrestling match in which 'God exists by two falls to a submission.'

watchmaker-argument.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
watchmaker-argument.title: Lessons to Take Away
watchmaker-argument.relation: Kinghorn asks what makes Hitchcock's trademark plot twists improbable, distinguishing physical, statistical and evidential probability and illustrating each with the fraying jacket seam in Saboteur, the sea of identical umbrellas in Foreign Correspondent, the porter uniforms in North by Northwest, and Manny Balestrero's uncanny double in The Wrong Man. The core of the chapter is a three-question method for assessing evidence - does the evidence fit the theory, does it fit rival theories too, how likely was the theory beforehand - worked out through Jeff and Doyle's debates over Thorwald's guilt in Rear Window, where Jeff turns out to be a methodologically sound amateur sleuth despite his bias against marriage. A closing lesson defends design-argument-style reasoning about God from a confused objection that demands statistics where only evidential probability is at issue.

watchmaker-argument.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
watchmaker-argument.title: Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New ‘Intelligent Falling’ Theory
watchmaker-argument.relation: Ruiz uses Onion stories—'Jesus Answers Half The Prayers At Area Roulette Table,' 'God Answers Prayers Of Paralyzed Little Boy,' 'Christianity Celebrates One Billionth Unanswered Prayer'—to argue that belief in God lacks rational justification. Following Hume's empiricism (all ideas trace to sense perception), methodological naturalism, and Ockham's Razor, he shows that feelings of God's presence, scriptural circularity, and answered prayers (riddled with selection bias) all fail as evidence, and the prayer hypothesis is unfalsifiable—a theory that explains any outcome, like the brain tumor thanking God for its surviving surgery, is supported by no evidence. He closes by dismantling Paley's watchmaker design argument through the infinite regress ('who designed God?') and by treating 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New Intelligent Falling Theory' as the reductio of design reasoning.

watchmaker-argument.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
watchmaker-argument.title: Doomed to Be Perceived
watchmaker-argument.relation: Smithka tests Berkeley's 'to be is to be perceived' against two monsters: the Vashta Nerada, whose existence is inferred from indirect evidence (counting shadows, the 'ghosting' of Miss Evangelista) much like Neptune was inferred from Uranus's orbit, and the Weeping Angels, which act only when unperceived and so falsify Berkeley's principle. Working through Locke on substance, Hume's skepticism about unperceivable causes like God, Paley's watchmaker design argument, and scientific realism (Sellars, Churchland) versus van Fraassen's empirically adequate anti-realism, she concludes the Doctor is a realist about unobservables — for whom the Angels are real but 'doomed to be perceived'.

watchmaker-argument.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
watchmaker-argument.title: Futurama and Philosophy
watchmaker-argument.relation: DePoe weighs the multiverse against the fine-tuning argument for God's existence: just as Farnsworth's box in 'The Farnsworth Parabox' spills out universe-1's golden Bender plus togas, pirate, and hippie universes, an infinite multiverse would realize every possibility and make our life-permitting constants certain rather than miraculous, while 'Time Keeps on Slippin''s chronoton-disturbed cosmos illustrates what fine-tuning means. He then asks what is metaphysically primitive, staging the 1948 Copleston-Russell exchange ('I should say that the universe is just there, and that's all') and applying Ockham's razor to weigh one infinitely complex God against infinitely many unobservable universes. The chapter concludes in evidential stalemate, closing with the God Entity's counsel in 'Godfellas': 'When you do things right, people won't be sure you've done anything at all.'

watchmaker-argument.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
watchmaker-argument.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
watchmaker-argument.relation: Shea stages the Wu-Malcolm dispute through Hume's Dialogues: Jurassic Park is an 'intelligent design' so botched that, like Philo's world of needless suffering, it points to ignorant or malicious designers rather than a perfect God, undercutting Richard Owen-style design arguments. He then explains Hammond's folly with Darwinian natural selection and memetics, treating the dinosaur-theme-park as a meme that infected InGen's investors by exploiting evolved desires for profit, fame, and importance. Hammond's fatal errors were assuming evolution 'wants' humans to survive, that complexity means better adapted, and that he could outsmart selection, which the all-female raptors breeding and life 'finding a way' quickly refute.

watchmaker-argument.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
watchmaker-argument.title: 21. God-Talk at the Abbey
watchmaker-argument.relation: Samuel Lumpenhouwer takes the Abbey's religious silences - Anna's 'we'll only fall out,' Alfred's baffled 'What?' at transubstantiation, and the Catholic baptism fight over baby Sybbie - and brings in Aquinas to make God-talk possible. Reason alone can know that God exists (the argument from design through final causes like the candle flame, carefully distinguished from Paley's watchmaker), revelation grasped by faith tells us God is personal, and human words reach God only analogically, as when Matthew calls God 'Father' at Lavinia's grave, or by way of negation. Against Carson's 'it is not our place to reason why' about Sybil's death, the chapter insists that mystery limits rather than excuses reason, ending with Aquinas's 'straw' and the Abbey's three attitudes: confident belief, searching doubt, and keep-it-private spirituality.

watchmaker-argument.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
watchmaker-argument.title: 4. Could a Divine Creator Turn Out to Be a Selfish Jerk
watchmaker-argument.relation: Using 'The Ricks Must Be Crazy', where Morty discovers Rick's car battery is a microverse of gooble-box workers ('slavery with extra steps'), the chapter asks whether a universe's designer must be a perfect God or could be a clever jerk like Rick. It lays out Paley's watchmaker teleological argument, Hume's point that even a real designer need not be morally perfect, the Euthyphro dilemma against Divine Command Theory (would Rick's commands for middle-finger greetings become morally good?), and Plantinga's modal ontological argument recast across the show's multiverse of possible worlds like the one where Hitler cured cancer. It concludes that Rick's advice to just not think about it is exactly what Socrates refused to do.

watchmaker-argument.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
watchmaker-argument.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
watchmaker-argument.relation: Barkman and Kowalski mine the Cooper household for science-and-religion lessons: Mary's 'Third-World demon' diagnosis of Raj raises religious diversity (exclusivism, inclusivism, pluralism), her 'But intelligently designed by a creator, right?' prompts an assessment of Behe's irreducible complexity against Darwinian counterexamples like the flagellum-turned-syringe and a warning against god-of-the-gaps reasoning. Her claim that 'all that science stuff comes from Jesus' occasions Plantinga's argument that Darwinian naturalism undermines trust in our cognitive faculties, plus origin-of-life and fine-tuning probability arguments, tempered by Kitcher's caution that such estimates rest on unknown background conditions. Van Inwagen on why Genesis need not teach literal science, and Locke's advice to proportion belief to evidence, frame the mutual education Mary and Sheldon owe each other.

watchmaker-argument.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
watchmaker-argument.title: 21. God-Talk at the Abbey
watchmaker-argument.relation: Samuel Klumpenhouwer uses the Abbey's awkward silences about religion - Anna refusing to discuss it over dinner, Thomas showing off with 'transubstantiation' - to introduce Aquinas on how God can be known and talked about. Mary's wartime bedside prayer ('I'm not even sure that you're there') shows she wants not just proof of existence but a personal God, so the chapter distinguishes Aquinas's argument from design - carefully separated from Paley's divine-watchmaker version - from knowledge of God through revelation and faith. Aquinas's two indirect ways of speaking, analogy (Matthew calling God 'Father' at Lavinia's grave) and negation, explain why the 'God is good' sign over Charles Grigg's workhouse should trouble us, and why Carson's 'it is not our place to reason why' about Sybil's death overstates the mystery of God's otherness.

watchmaker-argument.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
watchmaker-argument.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
watchmaker-argument.relation: Curry argues that angels like Anna and Castiel can reasonably be atheists, because a higher perspective confers no epistemic advantage about God: Anna admits only four angels have seen him and the rest 'take it on faith.' Aquinas's cosmological argument, illustrated by the endless causal chain behind the Impala, yields at most an uncaused first cause rather than an omnipotent, omnibenevolent one, and Paley's design argument, an Impala in the desert implies a designer, is undermined by Darwinian natural selection, which Castiel himself witnessed ('Don't step on that fish'). The free-will theodicy fails against natural evils like famine and childhood cancer, and the principle of parsimony tells angels to expect a natural explanation for their own existence, so Uriel's 'There is no will. No wrath. No God.' turns out to be rational.

watchmaker-argument.title: Doomed to Be Perceived
watchmaker-argument.relation: Paula Smithka uses the Vashta Nerada and Weeping Angels to examine perception and the reality of unobservables. She sets Berkeley's "to be is to be perceived" against Locke's hidden substance and Hume's empiricist skepticism (and Paley's design argument), then distinguishes direct from indirect perceptual evidence, using the shadows, skeletal remains, and Neptune's discovery to frame scientific realism versus van Fraassen's antirealism. The Weeping Angels invert Berkeley, existing only when unperceived and turning to stone when observed, so for them to be is NOT to be perceived.

watchmaker-argument.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
watchmaker-argument.title: 15. God Is Good (Chuck Not So Much)
watchmaker-argument.relation: Graves contrasts the Judeo-Christian God of scripture with Chuck, arguing Chuck fails theodicy: he neither shares human suffering (as Jesus does) nor pursues justice for the oppressed (as Yahweh does in Psalm 82), and using evolution to create sapient life guarantees disease, war, and injustice that Paley's Natural Theology design argument cannot excuse. He reads Amara's wish to unwind creation as arguably 'good,' rejects the Winchesters' fallacy that Nephilim Jack must inherit Lucifer's evil (nature versus nurture), and diagnoses Chuck as a pathological narcissist paralleling despotic real-world leaders.

watchmaker-argument.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
watchmaker-argument.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
watchmaker-argument.relation: Arp frames a dialogue between two ex-seminarians who once got matching cross tattoos: Bill, who added more Christian ink, and Rick, who now regrets his cross as an atheist secular humanist. Bill defends God via Aquinas's combined proof from motion and causation—tracing the tattoo artist and even the Big Bang back to an unmoved mover / uncaused cause—and the 'three Ms' of mind, meaning, and morality, gesturing toward Paley-style design. Rick counters with a self-sustaining infinite series, the interaction problem between a supernatural God and nature, and the charge that God is a comforting fiction, so morality and meaning are humanly made rather than divinely guaranteed.

ship-of-theseus.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
ship-of-theseus.title: The Hulk’s Bodily Identity
ship-of-theseus.relation: Tests the everyday bodily criterion of identity: the Hulk's body contains far more atoms than Banner's, but since all our cells turnover anyway — the "Stan Lee Schooner" has every part replaced yet stays the same boat, the Ship of Theseus problem — and the organ-donor case of "Herb Trimpe" shows a body with greater physical continuity to Kinghorn than to its owner, bodily continuity cannot be what personal identity consists in.

ship-of-theseus.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
ship-of-theseus.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Uses Narnia's magical transformations to probe personal identity, starting with the qualitative/numerical identity distinction illustrated by the look-alike twins Shasta and Corin in The Horse and His Boy. Aristotle's essential/accidental properties frame the question of what Eustace can lose and remain Eustace, including turning into a dragon, and Rabadash into a donkey, showing persons are not identical to their bodies. Descartes's soul argument and Locke's memory theory are tested and rejected, the latter because it cannot handle Rilian's enchanted amnesia, Shasta's forgotten infancy, or Susan's disowned memories without circularity. The chapter defends instead a first-person-perspective theory on which a person is constituted by, not identical to, a body, illustrated by the repeatedly repaired Dawn Treader and by the heroes surviving death in The Last Battle as restored points of view.

ship-of-theseus.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
ship-of-theseus.title: Was Jerry Garcia the Soul of the Grateful Dead
ship-of-theseus.relation: John Uglietta asks what made the Grateful Dead the Grateful Dead when they swapped five keyboardists yet stopped being themselves the moment Jerry Garcia died, prompting the rename to The Dead. Testing Aristotle's essential versus accidental properties, Peter French's structural account of group identity (the Yankees, the Glenn Miller Orchestra), same-stuff theories via a VW bus rebuilt piece by piece from its old parts — a Ship of Theseus puzzle — and Locke's memory theory applied to Phil Lesh's liver (but feared brain) transplant, he proposes that the band's essence was a group spirit born of members 'surrendering their own little trip'. The soul of the Dead was bigger than Jerry but smaller than the whole band, and its loss at his death was something the survivors could recognize but not replace.

ship-of-theseus.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
ship-of-theseus.title: Absolutely Curtains
ship-of-theseus.relation: Michael Patton retells the Ship of Theseus (his 'Trump Princess' rebuilt part-by-part from spares, then duplicated from the salvaged parts) to ask whether Pink Floyd survived its upheavals: Bob Klose's pre-Piper exit, Syd Barrett's 1968 dismissal ('No, fuck it, let's not bother' on the drive to Southampton), Rick Wright's firing during The Wall, and Roger Waters's 1985 lawsuit to stop Gilmour and Mason using the name. Roster, stylistic ('Lucifer Sam' versus 'Money'), legal, and nominal criteria each fail, so he proposes an 'Officeholder View' of identity in which constituencies decide sameness — as when UFO Club's Joe Boyd saw a different Syd at the June 1967 show, while the author's locked-in brother Josh (like Bauby in The Diving Bell and the Butterfly) remained the same son and brother to his family. Parfit's claim that survival tracks memory and personality rather than body underwrites the 'death of a thousand cuts' scenario: the band's criteria, not Syd's own, ended the life of the person 'Syd Barrett', and he didn't get a vote.

ship-of-theseus.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
ship-of-theseus.title: A Modest Conclusion
ship-of-theseus.relation: Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro stage the diachronic-versus-episodic debate about the self (Galen Strawson's episodic view included) against Leigh Edwards's "no single Johnny Cash": the hotel-room-wrecking addict and the Billy Graham touring Christian do not fit one biography. They argue the private J.R. was a third option: on stage he becomes wholly absorbed in story characters (the Folsom narrator, the man who shot a man in Reno) while a self not defined by time slips in and out of the persona, evidenced by his account of gradually shedding "Johnny Cash" after shows. Johnny Cash the public quilt is compared to the Ship of Theseus, every original piece of J.R. replaced yet still owned by him, and the modest conclusion is that J.R., like anyone making a free choice, stood above the timeline of instants and could inhabit both the episodes and the grand narrative.

ship-of-theseus.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
ship-of-theseus.title: Memories Are Made of This
ship-of-theseus.relation: Randall Jensen asks whether Cash's hope of reunion with the dead ('Meet Me in Heaven,' 'If We Never Meet Again This Side of Heaven') is even coherent, using the 'One Piece at a Time' Cadillac and a hypothetical 1954 Plymouth to retell the Ship of Theseus puzzle about identity through part replacement. He canvasses Platonic dualism from the Phaedo (Cash is his soul, the body a rusty cage), the materialist hope that God can reassemble a resurrected body despite dispersed matter, and the psychological-continuity view that persons are 'made of memories,' ending on the duplication problem: if God made two heavenly bodies both carrying Cash's memories, which one would be Cash?

ship-of-theseus.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
ship-of-theseus.title: Solutions to the Problem The youth whose destiny it is to lead Hyrule to the
ship-of-theseus.relation: Robison asks how Link stays the same person through Ocarina of Time's child/adult switches, Twilight Princess's wolf form, and Wind Waker's consciousness-projection into seagulls and mages. Physical-continuity views fail because Link's body changes or is left behind; Locke's memory-based psychological continuity fails because adult Link's past hasn't happened yet when he travels back. After a Ship of Theseus variant (Ganon reassembling Tetra's sunken planks) she proposes that in Zelda's stipulative metaphysics, destiny, the goddess-given roles of courage, wisdom, and power, is the necessary and sufficient condition of identity, fitting videogame universes whose metaphysics are fixed by designers.

ship-of-theseus.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
ship-of-theseus.relation: Four 'Phase Five' puzzle essays. Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro use Secret Wars to test omnipotence: the Beyonder, Doom, and Galactus cannot do the logically impossible (no spherical cubes, no stone too heavy to lift), two omnipotent beings collide, and a truly omnipotent being has no desires - so villains can never climb to the top they crave. Matthewson and Wall use Frankfurt cases and reasons-responsive source compatibilism to explain why Eddie Brock is responsible for Venom's villainy (he voluntarily bonded and endorses the symbiote's adjusted psychology) while Anne Weying, horrified by what the symbiote made her do, bears only minimal blame. Pickavance reconstructs the Ship of Theseus with Sandman's 'mansand': combining part exchange with materialism lets Norman Osborn reassemble a duplicate Sandman from his scattered remains, and since neither principle nor soul-dualism comes free, personal identity through material change remains unsolved. Loader argues Brainiac's reinvention as a 'facts and logic' computer embodies disembodied Cartesian AI, so the frame problem (Dennett's exploding robots) and embodied cognition (Clark's Tetris, Dreyfus) suggest his detachment from body and world would make him less, not more, intelligent than the humans he scorns.

ship-of-theseus.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
ship-of-theseus.title: Coda
ship-of-theseus.relation: Gimbel asks what makes a band remain the same band over time: Led Zeppelin survived replacing drummer John Bonham with his son Jason, yet Page and Jones insist no singer could replace Robert Plant. Working through Plutarch's Ship of Theseus, Aristotle's essential properties, and Locke's continuity account of identity, he uses Peter French's distinction between aggregates (groups defined by membership) and conglomerates (defined by role structure) to argue a band is a conglomerate. The twist is that a reunion would be a monument like Theseus's preserved ship rather than a working vessel: Plant is an Aristotelian essential of what Zeppelin was, while Jason Bonham's family link supplies the reverence and facsimile-fidelity a monument needs.

ship-of-theseus.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
ship-of-theseus.title: Is Everybody Disembodied (or, Have We Always Been Posthuman Beings )
ship-of-theseus.relation: Stevens uses the film's closing voice-over 'I am Tetsuo' in Otomo's Akira to run the classic identity-and-mind problems: Heraclitus's river and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus ask whether the grotesquely transformed, Akira-absorbed Tetsuo is still the same person, while Descartes's cogito — riffed as 'cogito ergo Tetsuo' — Turing's Test, and Searle's Chinese Room test whether a voice that seems to think proves a thinker behind it (syntax is not yet shown sufficient for semantics, though Edwin Hutchins's distributed cognition reads the Room from the inside out). Weighing embodiment (Pinker's brain-makes-mind, Dennett's self as a 'center of narrative gravity') against disembodiment (Akira levelling Neo-Tokyo from nothing but cryogenically stored remains; Tetsuo's matter teleportation), he concludes through the problem of representation — every utterance is re-presented, as in Augustine's guilty tears over Dido — that we always treat semblances of thinkers as thinkers, so we may have always been decentered, re-presented, posthuman beings no different from Tetsuo and Akira.

ship-of-theseus.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
ship-of-theseus.title: Where in the World(s) Are We
ship-of-theseus.relation: Ablondi asks whether fans' 'if only' claims—'If Bob Stanley had struck out Mookie Wilson, the Sox would have won in 1986,' 'if Pesky had hurried his relay in 1946'—can be true when they lack truthmakers in the actual world. He presents David Lewis's modal realism and counterpart theory as the standard solution, then objects: a Fisk counterpart with a different body, birthday and nickname, or a Red Sox made of 1986 Mets counterparts, is not recognizably Fisk or the Red Sox, and nobody cares about a Lonborg counterpart who won Game Seven. He concludes counterfactuals need some other explanation and that we should savor the actual Foulke-to-Mientkiewicz final out of 2004 instead.

ship-of-theseus.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
ship-of-theseus.title: The Limits of Change
ship-of-theseus.relation: Osborne and Coombs turn the Ship of Theseus — every plank replaced, plus Hobbes's reassembled-planks variant — into the 'Aston Villa Paradox': with owner, manager, players, crest and even the shade of claret and blue changed, what makes it the same club fans sing 'Villa till I Die' for?
