Finding that presentism and Sider's four-dimensionalism cannot say which side on the 2006 pitch was really AVFC, they adopt Lynne Rudder Baker's constitution view: fans create the football-favorable circumstances that constitute a club, so it persists through total replacement of parts as long as supporters keep conferring identity and value — which is why Gareth Barry's value collapsed when he left, and why fans judged Glazer's Manchester United to have stopped existing while welcoming Lerner's Villa.

ship-of-theseus.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
ship-of-theseus.title: Mastering the Chief
ship-of-theseus.relation: Joyce Havstad asks which of the millions of player-instantiated Master Chiefs is real, and whether the flash-cloned John left behind on Eridanus II is the same boy. She runs the Ship of Theseus on the MJOLNIR armor—a technician rebuilds a second suit from every replaced piece—contrasting material with historical continuity, and adds Hobbes's reassembled-planks version. Locke's prince-and-cobbler memory criterion is reconstructed across John, John-117, and Master Chief, then broken by Reid's brave-officer objection, leaving psychological continuity as the best but imperfect criterion; the Flood's conversion of a Covenant soldier into a Combat Form shows identity lost once original sentience is gone.

ship-of-theseus.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
ship-of-theseus.title: In a Mirror, Darkly
ship-of-theseus.relation: The chapter stages Arctor's bishop's-robe musing ('What is identity? Where does the act end?') against the classic puzzles: the Ship of Theseus with its two reassembled vessels, and the baby photos you share no cells with. Locke gives memory plus a unified 'thinking, intelligent being' with real unity; Hume bites the bullet, finding only perceptions in introspection, never a self, so the self's identity over time is a normal, inescapable delusion like a mountain's. All of it converges on Fred watching Bob and asking 'who am I? Which one of them is me?'

ship-of-theseus.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
ship-of-theseus.title: The Sum of the Parts
ship-of-theseus.relation: Auxier asks why 'It' works only when the Stones are together, testing the band's fifty-year experiment against lineup changes: Brian Jones proved dispensable, the second guitar modular, yet Bill Wyman's 1992 departure genuinely weakened the circuit. He claims Keith-Charlie-Bill in series (data-synthesis-satisfaction) are the real power source, with Jagger merely the light bulb that draws the current — the Keith-Charlie-Bill band would have been famous without Mick, but Mick is nothing without the circuit. A lithium analogy renders the band loosely bound, unstable and flammable, and the chapter closes by insisting Charlie interprets Keith and Bill interprets Charlie, in that order.

ship-of-theseus.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
ship-of-theseus.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Monica Evans argues that D&D is identity play in which players explore who they are through characters they create, perform and try to keep alive, opening with Plutarch's Ship of Theseus to ask whether a character re-rolled under a new edition, or replayed by another player, is still 'the same' character. She tests theories of the player-character bond (Gee's virtual, real and projective identities; Fine and Worch's 'identity bubble') on Wil Wheaton's Avenger Aeofel, whose in-character oath made Wheaton split the party and lose him rather than metagame. Bartle's four player types and the bulette-knowledge example show how each player manages the line between what they know and what their character knows, in a shared fiction where a glorious failure can be better than winning.

ship-of-theseus.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
ship-of-theseus.title: Futurama and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Jenkins asks what makes Bender Bender when Leela still recognizes him as the walnut-panelled steam robot of 'Obsoletely Fabulous.' Scruffy's progressively repaired conference table stages the Ship of Theseus problem and the same body theory, while the Roboticon 'Soul Detector' (Fry sets it off, robots pass through) rules out Descartes' same soul theory for robots. Episodes from 'Anthology of Interest II' and 'The Honking' to 'The Prisoner of Benda' mind swap and Roberto's instant 1-X re-education support Locke's psychological continuity: Bender persists through an overlapping chain of memories and traits stored on his hard drive - 'Everything that is Bender is right here' - which is why an empathic, ascetic Bender ('The old Bender is gone') threatens his very identity.

ship-of-theseus.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
ship-of-theseus.title: Futurama and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Williams uses Hermes's slide from chest-harpoon to extendo-arm to Cylon eye to full robot body in 'The Six Million Dollar Mon' - until Zoidberg's 'Monster Mash' surgery restores his brain to Li'l Hermes - to ask what makes a person themselves under voluntary enhancement. The 'Ship of Planet Express' and the seven-year cell-replacement fact recast the Ship of Theseus, exposing our terror of upgrades as inconsistent with our constant physical change, while the therapeutic-versus-enhancement line (medical steroids vs doping, Aimee Mullins's blades) explains why Hermes's chosen upgrades disturb us. Cartesian interactionist dualism predicts Mecha-Hermes stays the same person, yet his personality shifts with his parts, so the chapter turns to physicalism and lands on functionalism: Hermes persists through each swap until the Roberto brain-chip replaces the brain that houses his memories and motivations.

ship-of-theseus.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
ship-of-theseus.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Lopez uses the monster - 'one man made out of many' - to stress-test personal identity: brain-swap and amnesia-torture thought experiments first drive us to identify with our memories (the memory-based psychological criterion) and then, when Victor offers to wipe memory before the pain experiments, with our bodies, yielding inconsistent answers. The monster's own testimony - waking confused, prodding fire like an infant, acquiring language by eavesdropping on Safie's lessons, and building his values from scratch out of Paradise Lost and the cottagers - shows he is a genuinely new person rather than whoever once owned his corpse-parts, since we would not say a memory-wiped torture victim ceases to exist. He concludes the monster satisfies the five listed personhood criteria (consciousness, reasoning, self-motivated activity, communication, self-awareness), with identity riding a continuing stream of consciousness running on a body that is, in the end, secondary 'hardware.'

ship-of-theseus.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
ship-of-theseus.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Freeman explains why Grant dismisses the clones as 'genetically engineered theme park monsters': a frog-DNA-patched genome is not dinosaur DNA, and nobody knows how much alteration turns a T. rex into something else, so as Wu tells Hammond the park has only reconstructed the past, never re-created it. Behavior cannot vindicate the clones either, since The Lost World's raptors grow up without elders to teach raptor behavior, and the animals must survive an ecosystem of grass, bacteria, and species that did not exist in the Cretaceous. The chapter's running puzzle of how much of an organism can change before it is no longer that organism is a Ship of Theseus problem applied to paleontology.

ship-of-theseus.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
ship-of-theseus.title: 10. One Good, Solid Hope—the Impossible Girl
ship-of-theseus.relation: Elsby and Luzecky ask what stays constant across Clara's echoes and argue traditional identity theories fail her: Locke's memory-continuity and same-life account cannot apply because no echo remembers the others, and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus—invoked by the Doctor's broom speech in 'Deep Breath'—rules out bodily continuity, since the echoes have different bodies and minds. Their positive view is that Clara is less a particular than a universal, a 'recipe' or species whose instances share an essence ('the soufflé isn't the soufflé; the soufflé is the recipe'), with the modern-day Clara 'real' as the origin of the echoes. That essence, shown in climbing the ladder to the clouds in 'The Snowmen,' facing the parasite-god with the most important leaf in human history in 'The Rings of Akhaten,' stepping into the Doctor's torn timeline in 'The Name of the Doctor,' and persuading the Time Lords in 'The Time of the Doctor,' is hope itself.

ship-of-theseus.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
ship-of-theseus.title: 14. Being One’s Me (Witchy) Personal Identity on the Discworld
ship-of-theseus.relation: The chapter reads Granny Weatherwax's analysis of Magrat—'you're your me'—through Locke's memory theory of personal identity, opening with Granny's broomstick, whose stick and bristles the dwarf engineers have replaced dozens of times yet which remains 'the same' broomstick, as a Theseus's-ship puzzle for witches. It stages Locke's view against the classic objections: Butler's circularity charge that memory presupposes identity, and fission worries raised by the duplicated Glods of Al-Ybi and by the mirror magic that splits Granny and Lilith among a billion reflections. Death's challenge to each witch to find 'the one that's real' in the mirror universe becomes the test case, and Granny's simply looking down at herself and saying 'This one' is offered as a vindication of a Butlerian, body-anchored and indefinable conception of personal identity.

ship-of-theseus.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
ship-of-theseus.title: 5. The One, the Only, Darrow
ship-of-theseus.relation: Kevin McCain uses Darrow's transformations—Helldiver of Lykos, carved Gold lancer, Reaper of Mars—to ask what makes him numerically the same person, warming up with Plutarch's Ship of Theseus replayed on the Pax and the Quinn trading parts. Same-matter and animalist views (Eric Olson) struggle with Mickey's near-total carving and Darrow's restarted heart, and Locke's prince-and-cobbler example, run as a carver swapping Darrow's and the Jackal's psychologies, sinks all physical-continuity views. The simple memory theory breaks transitivity across Darrow's childhood, and Sydney Shoemaker's psychological-continuity fix then fails when a carver splits Darrow's brain into two surviving bodies—a fission case where both new Darrows continue him—while the soul view cannot be verified; the chapter ends with Trenton Merricks's suggestion that there may be no criteria of identity over time at all.

ship-of-theseus.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
ship-of-theseus.title: 18. No End to Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Four vignettes pin philosophical problems to Peanuts' marginal characters: Camus's absurd - caring beings condemned to an uncaring universe - is answered by Sally's School Building, which grows a heart and drops bricks on her enemies; the 95472 kids motivate a tour of personal identity (same soul, same body, memory) through the Ship of Theseus; Pigpen's dirt raises Sartre's bad faith (facticity, transcendence, being-for-others) - we prize his authenticity over cleanliness - and Aristotle's golden mean, which moderates cleanliness while crediting his curiosity as a virtue; and finally the ontology of fictional characters asks whether the Kite-Eating Tree and Red Baron really exist inside the fiction and whether The Peanuts Movie's changed Charlie Brown counts as canon.

ship-of-theseus.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
ship-of-theseus.title: 9. Is Headless Deadpool Still Deadpool
ship-of-theseus.relation: Ben Fulman runs Deadpool's decapitations, the T-Ray personality split, and Evil Deadpool—his discarded body parts regenerating together in a dumpster—through the theories of personal identity: Locke's memory continuity, Reid's branching-memory 'Deadpool paradox', Chisholm's essential parts, the Ship of Theseus traced from Heraclitus to Plutarch, and later positions by Sider, Wiggins, Noonan, Grice, and Perry on overlapping memory chains and their circularity. Finding each account strained by Deadpool's cases, the chapter proposes that Deadpool stores his memories in the readers via the fourth wall. His identity over time is thus jointly sustained by the audience—a 'non-personal identity' that ends only when every reader has forgotten him.

ship-of-theseus.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
ship-of-theseus.title: 24. Won’t the Real Wade Wilson Please Stand Up
ship-of-theseus.relation: Evil Deadpool, assembled from Wade's discarded body parts with all his old memories, makes Wade a walking Ship of Theseus, and the chapter runs the puzzle through Plutarch's original, Hobbes's reconstructed-ship variant, and Locke's Prince-and-Cobbler memory criterion, staged as a Thor/Thing body swap. Memory fails because Evil Deadpool shares Wade's memories, so the candidates become Schechtman's narrative and person-life views, Parfit's branching survival - neither is the original, and identity is not what matters anyway - and finally Unger's core-capacity view: Wade remains the real Deadpool by continuing to be a conscious being, while his detached parts ceased to be Deadpool parts the moment they were replaced.

ship-of-theseus.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
ship-of-theseus.title: 3. My Sister, My Self
ship-of-theseus.relation: Staged as a remembered backstage conversation among Elsa's freak show performers, the chapter has conjoined twins Bette and Dot work through the Ship of Theseus, the psychological-continuity theory of identity and its coma and false-memory counterexamples, Quine's claim that persons are only convenient posits rather than real entities, split-brain cases suggesting one body can host two minds, and fission worries about what would happen if they were separated - to ask whether they are one person or two, concluding it is a genuine paradox with no agreed answer.

ship-of-theseus.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
ship-of-theseus.title: 6. The KISS Franchise
ship-of-theseus.relation: Peter Finocchiaro takes Gene Simmons's and manager Doc McGhee's suggestions that KISS could become a franchise — new musicians stepping into the Demon and Starchild roles — and works out what band identity could mean. Using the Ship of Theseus, he distinguishes qualitative from numerical identity, invokes collective intentionality to explain how a band without a mind can perform intentional actions, and contrasts the 'originality connection' (being the actual founding members) with the 'continuity connection' (day-by-day chained succession), mirroring the bodily-versus-psychological debate about Gene Simmons's personal identity. His conclusion is that bands are governed by social rules fans collectively create — like the rules of basketball or musical genre — so in his imaginary two-KISS scenario, and for any future franchise, the fan base would decide which band is the real KISS rather than discovering a pre-existing fact.

ship-of-theseus.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
ship-of-theseus.title: 9. KISS the Ship of Theseus Goodbye!
ship-of-theseus.relation: Shane Ralston asks whether KISS, after constant lineup changes that left only Stanley and Simmons fixtures, is still the same band. He lays out Plutarch's Ship of Theseus and Hobbes's harder variant — a ship rebuilt from the salvaged original planks — formalizing three assumptions (endurance through gradual change, identity with parts, transitivity of identity) and their conflicting conclusions, then applies a fifty-percent-plus-quality reading: keeping the two powerhouse founding members preserved KISS's core identity through the Carr, Vincent, St. John, Kulick, Singer, and Thayer eras. For the imagined duplicate-KISS case he deploys Chisholm's 'loose and popular sense' of identity and Ted Sider's four-dimensionalist 'space-time worm,' concluding the dispute is practical — best settled by courts of law, not armchair metaphysics.

ship-of-theseus.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
ship-of-theseus.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: James Bondarchuk tests purist principles about which line-ups are really Black Sabbath with thought experiments: the Ship of Theseus, from Plutarch plus Hobbes's reassembled planks, fits poorly because Geezer Butler is no plank, musicians contribute irreplaceable style, and "original members only" absurdly entails a Bieber piano-cover band would still be Sabbath, while the legal-ownership reading collapses once fans admit Bieber buying the name changes nothing. He concludes the whole "is it still Sabbath without Ozzy?" debate is not a metaphysical question with a fact of the matter but disguised aesthetic judgment, he remains a purist because Bill Ward's brooding drumming on "Black Sabbath" and "Hand of Doom" are integral to the Sabbath Sound, while conceding no objective answer exists.

ship-of-theseus.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
ship-of-theseus.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Monica Evans asks what relationship holds between a player and a character, opening with Plutarch's Ship of Theseus to probe whether a character rebuilt under a new edition, recreated in Neverwinter Nights, or played in succession by two people is still the 'same' character. She applies James Paul Gee's three identities (virtual, real-world, projective) to Wil Wheaton playing Aeofel, whose in-character chase of Leer into an acid pit shows projective identity trumping good gameplay. Worch's 'identity bubble', Bartle's four player types, and the management of player versus character knowledge (the veteran whose wizard meets a bulette, the INT 7 barbarian Dak) frame D&D as a shared fiction in which players explore who they are or might be.

ship-of-theseus.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
ship-of-theseus.title: NOTE
ship-of-theseus.relation: Asks whether amnesia preserves numerical identity: is the Peter who wakes in the shipping crate still Volume-1 Peter, are Niki and Jessica one person, and is the Sylar whom Matt rewrites with Nathan's memories now Nathan? The chapter builds Locke's memory criterion, breaks it with Reid's transitivity objection run through Mohinder's timeline in 'Five Years Gone,' repairs it with Grice's and Perry's memory-ancestor chains, then destroys the repair with Arthur Petrelli's wipe of Hiro (Forgetful Hiro vs. Stabby Hiro), Bernard Williams's torture thought experiment, Parfit's psychological spectrum, and the graphic novel's branching self-copier Evan. It concludes that no memory criterion can define personal identity, yet memory still matters practically: Claire must act as if she persists over time to keep her promise to Zach and to bother finishing the manatee assignment.

ship-of-theseus.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
ship-of-theseus.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.relation: Michaud argues Peeta effectively died twice — once at the force field, and again when the Capitol's tracker-jacker hijacking rewrote his loving memories of Katniss into hatred. Using Leibniz's Law he rules out the body and DNA as what makes Peeta Peeta, then defends Locke's memory theory through thought experiments about a clone Peeta versus a brain-damaged original. Adapting Plutarch's Ship of Theseus as 'the Problem of Haymitch's Hovercraft,' he questions whether gradual change preserves identity, and finally leans toward Hume and Parfit: there may be no enduring self, only a bundle of perceptions replaced moment by moment. On this view Katniss protects the hijacked Peeta out of respect for the memory of the old Peeta, even as each of us is constantly replaced by someone new.

ship-of-theseus.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
ship-of-theseus.title: Notes
ship-of-theseus.relation: Gettings asks whether LEGO set #21103, the Cuusoo DeLorean Time Machine, is numerically identical to Team BTTF's original fan design — and why the fans deserve credit and royalties. Neither matter (his 1982 attic spaceship with bricks replaced one by one) nor form (a license plate added here or there) settles identity, as the Ship of Theseus puzzle and Hobbes' reassembly variation show, analyzed through Aristotle's matter/form distinction for substances. He adopts the causal/historical view: the released set continuously descends from the fans' submission just as the adult author descends from the boy who built the spaceship, and this same historical origin, in Lockean fashion, is what grounds the designers' labor-mixing property right — the musician-and-producer analogy explaining why Team BTTF keeps the larger share of credit.

ship-of-theseus.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
ship-of-theseus.title: Notes
ship-of-theseus.relation: Mentyka uses minifigure puzzles — can 'Eliza' and 'Beth' be distinct characters when built from identical pieces, and is Eliza the same character after every piece is swapped out, a minifig Ship of Theseus — to introduce the philosophy of the human person. He runs through supervenience on physical parts, Locke's memory theory and its Butler–Reid controversy (Reid in the taxonomy), the Christian Resurrection-of-the-Body background, and Parfit's despairing deflation that identity matters less than what survives us. Against these he defends personalism, citing Max Scheler and Kierkegaard's call in The Single Individual to become one rather than a crowd: a person is both the sigfig and the AFOL building it, constituted by free choices and actions — which is also why the LEGO Movie's 'Where Are My Pants?' mass society is the enemy.

ship-of-theseus.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
ship-of-theseus.title: Solutions to the Problem The youth whose destiny it is to lead Hyrule to the
ship-of-theseus.relation: Rachel Robison asks how Zelda characters persist through radical change, recasting the Ship of Theseus as Tetra's pirate ship from Wind Waker, whose replaced planks Ganon reassembles into a rival ship and leaving Link to find the true one. Physical-continuity accounts fail because Link projects his consciousness into seagulls and temple mages and becomes a wolf in Twilight Princess; Locke's memory theory fails because Ocarina of Time's child/adult time loops break psychological continuity. Her solution: in the Zelda universe, the goddesses' destiny — embodiment of courage, wisdom, or power — supplies the necessary and sufficient condition of identity, a stipulative metaphysics videogames are free to have.

ship-of-theseus.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
ship-of-theseus.title: Is It Still Metallica? On the Identity of Rock Bands Over Time
ship-of-theseus.relation: Manuel Bremer and Daniel Cohnitz ask whether the band on Kill 'Em All is identical with the band on St. Anger. Lars' drum kit, rebuilt part by part plus the reassembled original, is a Ship of Theseus case yielding their 'Nothing Else Matters Principle'; Locke's distinction between same substance, man, and person - illustrated by a brain swap between Kirk Hammett and an envious rival - shows identity must be 'suited to the idea'; and Searle and Gilbert on collective intention show a band is a social group, not a collection of people. Their revised musical-style-plus-line-up-continuity theory faces fission problems (Megadeth) and the eliminativist option Quine's 'no entity without identity' invites.

ship-of-theseus.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
ship-of-theseus.title: Notes
ship-of-theseus.relation: Sorts out Spock-Prime, bearded Mirror-Spock, and Abrams's Spock-2 using David Lewis's modal realism, counterparts, and Humean supervenience: identity is not directly perceived but judged from adjacent similar instances, as with Hume's natural properties. The refit Enterprise versus the Enterprise-A, plus the thought experiment of downloading the old ship's computer into the new one, carry a Ship-of-Theseus-style analysis of whether swapped cells and Spock's katra-separated death and Genesis resurrection preserve identity. Mirror-Spock turns out to be a worldmate within one enlarged world (Kirk's crossover in "Mirror, Mirror" makes the universes spatiotemporally continuous), not a transworld duplicate, and Spock-Prime and Spock-2 are like two highways overlapping until Nero's arrival in 2233 makes them diverge - two similar individuals formed by different successes and failures, never identical.

ship-of-theseus.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
ship-of-theseus.title: Playing for the Same Team Again
ship-of-theseus.relation: A fictional five-day phone dialogue between Michael Jordan and Phil Jackson works through the metaphysics of team identity before Jordan's 1995 comeback: qualitative versus numerical sameness, necessary and sufficient conditions ('same players, same positions'), Heraclitus's river, and whether the Bulls survive gradual turnover. The Ship of Theseus becomes the 'Boars' puzzle - the original five reassembled on an expansion team versus the continuous, degenerate Chicago roster - with Hobbes's two-ship twist, alongside the Minneapolis Lakers' move and a Bulls-Pistons gradual player swap. The resolution distinguishes the group (which persists by composition or continuity) from the team, which 'counts as' the Bulls only partly through fans' allegiance, echoing Searle's social reality; Jordan concludes he was asking the wrong question, and Aristotle's circular account of virtue supplies the model for circular criteria of loyal fandom.

ship-of-theseus.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.title: Here They Are ... Ready to Outsit Eternity
ship-of-theseus.relation: Michael Hand uses the Doctor's regeneration to argue that life after death is logically possible. Because the First-through-Tenth Doctors are the same person despite total personality change (a dandy becoming a clown), identity is distinct from personality, so a god perfecting flawed Joe for heaven need not make him someone else. He then tests the replica theory against 'Journey's End' (the metacrisis Doctor) and 'Human Nature' (John Smith), concluding we favor bodily continuity, and endorses van Inwagen's 'divine cryonicist' solution to the unavailability-of-atoms problem, echoing the Doctor's 'ready to outsit eternity' praise of frozen humanity in 'The Ark in Space'.

ship-of-theseus.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
ship-of-theseus.title: 14. Baby’s Identity
ship-of-theseus.relation: Doll uses the Winchesters' Impala 'Baby'—repeatedly totaled and rebuilt from replaced parts—as a running Ship of Theseus (from Plutarch) to probe what makes an object or person the same over time. She tests Aristotle's four causes (favoring the formal cause) and Theodore Sider's four-dimensionalism, both of which falter, then notes Supernatural's souls solve personal identity for the resurrected Winchesters and alternate-universe doubles; since soulless Baby has no such thread, her identity rests on the subjective, family meaning the Winchesters invest in her.

ship-of-theseus.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
ship-of-theseus.title: 19. Cleons and Cloning
ship-of-theseus.relation: Heter examines the Cleon Dynasty's clones (Brothers Dawn, Day, Dusk) to ask what a clone actually is, rejecting definitions built on identity. He distinguishes numerical identity (the Mule just is Magnifico Giganticus) from qualitative identity (two copies of a book), then shows the Cleons fail to be qualitatively identical because of age, psychology, perceptual perspective, and even drifting genetics over time—so grounding cloning in shared qualitative/genetic identity yields the odd result that clones could gain or lose clone-status as their genes change. He instead proposes a causal definition: a clone is an organism whose genetic information results from an (imperfect) copying process originating in a donor, so Cleon I is not a clone but every later Cleon is.

ship-of-theseus.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
ship-of-theseus.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
ship-of-theseus.relation: Steven Horrobin sorts sailors into three kinds — the cultural-iconography poser, the racer chasing a land-based prize, and the 'sailor of the third kind' for whom the open-ended voyage is an end in itself — and argues the third lives 'in the shadow of Heraclitus.' Against the substantialist ontology of Parmenides and Democritus (persons and boats as fixed things), he defends a process view in which everything, like a wave, is a passing fluctuation of one universal substance; citing Spinoza, self-becoming is the super-process reflecting itself. He dissolves the Ship of Theseus paradox (and Parfit's parallel-ship version) by making identity the continuity of a process's function rather than fixed parts, arguing the violent, corroding life of a boat reveals the flux beneath apparently stable things.

ship-of-theseus.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
ship-of-theseus.title: 4. Total Recall & The Sixth Day
ship-of-theseus.relation: Rowlands treats Total Recall as a defence of the memory (psychological-continuity) theory of personal identity: erasing Quaid's memories and restoring Hauser's is an essential change that ends Quaid, so he fights for his existence. He works through and rejects the soul theory (dualism's problems) and body/brain theories via head-transplant and neuron-replacement thought experiments, distinguishing Aristotle's essential/accidental change and Heraclitus's river. The Sixth Day's cloning raises Parfit's fission/duplication problem: a double success cannot be a failure, driving him to abandon identity for a Heraclitean 'river of selves' bound by survival, not identity.

ship-of-theseus.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ship-of-theseus.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
ship-of-theseus.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

ship-of-theseus.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
ship-of-theseus.title: 3. What Is Who
ship-of-theseus.relation: The chapter runs the Doctor's regenerations and the 'Timeless Child' reveal through competing theories of personal identity: Plato's soul/Forms, Locke's memory continuity, and bodily continuity, all of which the Doctor's body-swaps and forgotten lifetimes defeat (the Twelfth Doctor's 'you are a broom' speech recasts the Ship of Theseus). It endorses an existentialist answer—personal identity is chosen and constantly 'becoming,' as the Thirteenth Doctor declares 'I know exactly who I am. I'm the Doctor'—and uses Sartre against Freud to explain how the Doctor and the Whovian fandom reconcile internal and external selves in a community of acceptance. It closes arguing that only an 'objective' immortality (memories preserved in the Matrix) survives death, not a subjective self.

parfit-teleportation.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
parfit-teleportation.title: A Causal Account of the Hulk’s Identity
parfit-teleportation.relation: Proposes that the Hulk is Banner because Banner "Hulks out" — the monster state develops causally from Banner's body and mind through radiation, danger and anger, rather than one person being swapped for another. But a mad scientist's cloning accident that splits Banner into two simultaneous rampaging Hulks breaks the account, since both would be causally derived from Bruce yet could not both be the one person — the fission-style counterexample that afflicts every theory so far.

parfit-teleportation.book: 013 - Superheroes and Philosophy - Truth, Justice, and the Socratic Way
parfit-teleportation.title: Is There No Way to Tell
parfit-teleportation.relation: Presents Derek Parfit's challenge to the whole enterprise: just as there need be no answer to whether a repaired machine is "the same" machine, Parfit's divided-brain case — each half housed in a new body — suggests a person can "survive as two different people without implying that I am these people," so identity questions may lack answers. Kinghorn resists the leap: difficulty finding the truth does not show there is none.

parfit-teleportation.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
parfit-teleportation.title: Introduction
parfit-teleportation.relation: Frames Part III's metaphysics chapters. Lawrence's chapter uses The Matrix to survey dualism and the materialist theories of mind; Southworth's uses Wolverine's amnesia to test Locke's memory criterion and Jamie Madrox's duplicates for Parfit's view of identity; Pierce's asks whether Harry Potter's prophecies leave Harry free, probing compatibilism versus libertarian free will; and Littmann's asks whether Skynet's Terminators could be persons via a Terminator version of the Turing Test.

parfit-teleportation.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
parfit-teleportation.title: Be Slow to Judge
parfit-teleportation.relation: Southworth tests Locke's memory theory on Wolverine: the Cassandra Nova/Xavier mind-swap shows identity follows mind, not body, and Wolverine's serial memory wipes (Team X, Weapon X, Apocalypse's brainwashing) mean that on Locke's connected-memory view several different people have inhabited his body — with House of M's total recall suddenly loading him with responsibility for all their deeds. Jamie Madrox's duplicates then carry Parfit's objection that shared memories cannot suffice for sameness of person, pushing toward physical continuity and the chapter's deflationary moral: be slow to judge who deserves blame.

parfit-teleportation.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
parfit-teleportation.title: Into the Future
parfit-teleportation.relation: Hanley dismantles the four claimed human/Cylon differences: artificial reproduction is in principle possible for us; prosthetics already blur what we are made of; model copies differ like identical twins (Boomer is not Athena); and resurrection has human analogues — he proposes an SDTR (scanning, death, transmission, replication) model and uses van Inwagen's replica-switch account of bodily resurrection while rejecting soul-based reincarnation on Lockean grounds, since consciousness rather than soul is the criterion of identity. He defends reproductive cloning as reproduction, not replication (a clone is your child, not your copy), and reads Athena's memories of Tyrol as evidence she is a replicated Boomer. The upshot: being a Cylon is nothing to fear — 'I am a Cylon, and so are you.'

parfit-teleportation.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
parfit-teleportation.title: “I Feel Exactly What You Feel”
parfit-teleportation.relation: Runs Star Trek's transporter and android stories as thought experiments on personal identity: the body theory (Kirk rejecting android Korby — 'Dr. Korby was never here' — and Picard telling the resurrected Rishon Uxbridge 'you do not exist'), the brain theory ('Spock's Brain,' Bashir refusing to replace half of Vedek Bareil's brain), and Locke's memory theory as vindicated by the Trill (Lela Dax's 'a person is but the sum of their memories,' the 'Dax' extradition hearing over Curzon's crimes). Riker's transporter double in 'Second Chances' and the Tuvix fusion then break the memory theory through fission and fusion, prompting Parfit's move that psychological continuity, not numerical identity, is what matters in survival. Memory erasure in 'Dagger of the Mind' and Kurn's rebranding after the failed Mauk-to'Vor in 'Sons of Mogh' count as death if we are our memories.

parfit-teleportation.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
parfit-teleportation.title: Epilog-Rolling
parfit-teleportation.relation: Patton turns the Tin Woodman's backstory—the enchanted axe that costs Nick Chopper his legs, arms, torso and heart, then his head, each replaced by the tinsmith—into a cyborg thought experiment about how much of a person can be swapped out before the person is gone. After a framing nod to Plato's Republic on censoring frightening tales (his father's ban on 'mental violence' fantasy), he brings in Derek Parfit: the R-relation, the 'My Division' brain-split, and the Branch-Line teletransportation case are mapped onto the Woodman (including a hypothetical straw-bodied second Nick) to argue that survival gets different answers from first-person and third-person perspectives. The closing wildcat episode, where the tinned Woodman neatly decapitates a wildcat to save a field mouse, is offered as textual evidence that the tin head failed to preserve moral consistency—so the original Nick Chopper is gone for good, and the Scarecrow's shared brain explains why the two friends later refuse to part.

parfit-teleportation.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
parfit-teleportation.title: A Dead End
parfit-teleportation.relation: Stokes uses regeneration and the multi-Doctor episodes ('The Three Doctors', 'The Five Doctors', 'The Trial of a Time Lord') to test theories of personal identity: Locke's memory criterion, Reid's transitivity objection, Parfit's teleporter and 'branch-line' cases, Nozick's closest-continuer theory, four-dimensional person-stages, animalism, and narrative identity. He argues that no objective-continuity account explains why the Fifth Doctor still cares whether he himself survives in 'The Caves of Androzani', and hints that being the Doctor may be a subjective stance in which each incarnation takes ownership of the others as itself.

parfit-teleportation.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
parfit-teleportation.title: What’s Persistence Without Identity
parfit-teleportation.relation: Hanley first fixes what is true in the Who canon (treating fiction as pretense), then asks how the Doctor persists when regeneration replaces 'every single cell' and when John Smith's amnesia severs memory in 'Human Nature'. Rejecting bodily continuity (the severed hand of 'The Christmas Invasion'), soul 'pellets', and simple memory (Reid's transitivity problem), he defends neo-Lockean mental continuity plus Nozick's closest-continuer schema to explain why Jackson Lake, the regrown Doctor, and DoctorDonna in 'Journey's End' are not the Doctor, and closes with Parfit's claim that psychological continuity rather than identity is what matters in survival, alongside Lewis's space-time-worm alternative.

parfit-teleportation.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
parfit-teleportation.title: Where Parfit Went Wrong
parfit-teleportation.relation: Peter Ludlow and Chiara Repetti-Ludlow read Red vs. Blue as an intuition pump for personal identity, running through Locke's prince-and-cobbler, Bernard Williams's duplicated Guy Fawkes, Shoemaker's brain transplant, and Wiggins's split brain before aiming at Parfit. Project Freelancer's Director fractures the Alpha AI into fragments (Epsilon's memories, Omega's rage) recombined into the Meta, and they argue intuitions break against Parfit here: psychological continuity via small fractured pieces—unlike Parfit's fission into two substantial halves—does not secure the source's survival. Church's disembodied AI existence and the ever-present agent-AI voice (Agent Washington driven mad by Epsilon) illustrate Putnam's 'soul stuff' and the extended-mind hypothesis of Chalmers and Clark better than Chalmers waving his iPhone.

parfit-teleportation.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
parfit-teleportation.title: Is It Live or Is It Memorex
parfit-teleportation.relation: The chapter supplies the missing detail, transfer versus copying: a 'snapshot' of Olham's brain imprinted on an android leaves Olham where he was, and frying the original destroys him rather than moving him, while the bank-transfer versus copying-money analogy and the question of one psyche imprinted on two androids show why the difference matters. Once the mechanics are filled in one way the alien android is a mere copy and Olham dies, filled in another way he survives bodiless, which restores the Psyche Rule pending a science of how psyches are realized in us.

parfit-teleportation.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
parfit-teleportation.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
parfit-teleportation.relation: Silcox and Cox present D&D modules as thought experiments in James Robert Brown's 'laboratory of the mind': the Tomb of Horrors' plane-shifting doorway forces Parfit's teletransporter question of whether the character who emerges is you, a copy, or an annihilation, extended to Tieflings and Warforged; Eberron's sentient Warforged raise Nagel's bat problem of whether a human player can know what it is like to be a machine, answered with the conclusion that players really explore human pretense, like Greek actors in masks. Mary Anne Warren's Space Traveler criteria for alien personhood strain against orcs who meet them yet attack on sight, and against the players who killed the lawful-good Flumph without parley. The deep difference is perspective: philosophy imagines sub specie aeternitatis while D&D demands immersion sub specie temporis, which nonetheless cultivates the open-minded intellectual virtues philosophers prize.

parfit-teleportation.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
parfit-teleportation.title: 12. Becoming Vetinari Personal Identity on the Discworld
parfit-teleportation.relation: Pierce uses Moist von Lipwig's rehabilitation (Albert Spangler becomes Postmaster General), Cosmo Lavish's doomed project of literally becoming Vetinari, the Auditor Myria LeJean, Angua's transformations, the Librarian's orangutan body, Miss Level's two bodies, and duplicated Rincewind teleportation cases to test theories of personal identity. Locke's memory theory, patched by Leibniz into psychological continuity, collapses into circularity under false-memory cases like a wizard implanting Teatime's murders in Rincewind's mind, while bodily and brain-continuity views founder on Igor part-swaps, splitting hemispheres, and identical-twin-style fission. Leibniz's own soul view and Reid's treatment of identity as a primitive, unanalyzable fact get their due, and Hume's skepticism about any continuing self marks the chapter's conclusion that every available view exacts a price.

parfit-teleportation.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
parfit-teleportation.title: 14. Being One’s Me (Witchy) Personal Identity on the Discworld
parfit-teleportation.relation: The chapter reads Granny Weatherwax's analysis of Magrat—'you're your me'—through Locke's memory theory of personal identity, opening with Granny's broomstick, whose stick and bristles the dwarf engineers have replaced dozens of times yet which remains 'the same' broomstick, as a Theseus's-ship puzzle for witches. It stages Locke's view against the classic objections: Butler's circularity charge that memory presupposes identity, and fission worries raised by the duplicated Glods of Al-Ybi and by the mirror magic that splits Granny and Lilith among a billion reflections. Death's challenge to each witch to find 'the one that's real' in the mirror universe becomes the test case, and Granny's simply looking down at herself and saying 'This one' is offered as a vindication of a Butlerian, body-anchored and indefinable conception of personal identity.

parfit-teleportation.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
parfit-teleportation.title: 5. The One, the Only, Darrow
parfit-teleportation.relation: Kevin McCain uses Darrow's transformations—Helldiver of Lykos, carved Gold lancer, Reaper of Mars—to ask what makes him numerically the same person, warming up with Plutarch's Ship of Theseus replayed on the Pax and the Quinn trading parts. Same-matter and animalist views (Eric Olson) struggle with Mickey's near-total carving and Darrow's restarted heart, and Locke's prince-and-cobbler example, run as a carver swapping Darrow's and the Jackal's psychologies, sinks all physical-continuity views. The simple memory theory breaks transitivity across Darrow's childhood, and Sydney Shoemaker's psychological-continuity fix then fails when a carver splits Darrow's brain into two surviving bodies—a fission case where both new Darrows continue him—while the soul view cannot be verified; the chapter ends with Trenton Merricks's suggestion that there may be no criteria of identity over time at all.

parfit-teleportation.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
parfit-teleportation.title: 24. Won’t the Real Wade Wilson Please Stand Up
parfit-teleportation.relation: Evil Deadpool, assembled from Wade's discarded body parts with all his old memories, makes Wade a walking Ship of Theseus, and the chapter runs the puzzle through Plutarch's original, Hobbes's reconstructed-ship variant, and Locke's Prince-and-Cobbler memory criterion, staged as a Thor/Thing body swap. Memory fails because Evil Deadpool shares Wade's memories, so the candidates become Schechtman's narrative and person-life views, Parfit's branching survival - neither is the original, and identity is not what matters anyway - and finally Unger's core-capacity view: Wade remains the real Deadpool by continuing to be a conscious being, while his detached parts ceased to be Deadpool parts the moment they were replaced.

parfit-teleportation.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
parfit-teleportation.title: 3. My Sister, My Self
parfit-teleportation.relation: Staged as a remembered backstage conversation among Elsa's freak show performers, the chapter has conjoined twins Bette and Dot work through the Ship of Theseus, the psychological-continuity theory of identity and its coma and false-memory counterexamples, Quine's claim that persons are only convenient posits rather than real entities, split-brain cases suggesting one body can host two minds, and fission worries about what would happen if they were separated - to ask whether they are one person or two, concluding it is a genuine paradox with no agreed answer.

parfit-teleportation.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
parfit-teleportation.title: 2. The Unimportance of Identity When You Have a Portal Gun
parfit-teleportation.relation: The chapter argues Rick C-137 is already dead: the Brainalyzer body-hops in 'The Rickshank Rickdemption' and the Operation Phoenix swap in 'Big Trouble in Little Sanchez' copy psychological states rather than transfer a consciousness, so each post-transfer Rick is a new psychological clone, exactly as in Parfit's Teletransporter. Building from Locke's memory theory of personal identity to Parfit's claim that identity is not what matters, it reads the dimension-hop in 'Rick Potion #9', the Morty voucher, and the ambiguous clone Beth of 'The Rickchurian Mortydate' as the show itself endorsing psychological continuity over numerical identity. What matters is that someone carries on Rick's desires and relationships, so nobody noticed the protagonist's death.

parfit-teleportation.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
parfit-teleportation.title: “Your Flesh, Too, is Weak. But You Have… Potential”
parfit-teleportation.relation: Mentyka maps the two antagonists of System Shock 2 onto the two classical criteria of personal identity: the parasitic Many, one flesh persisting through wildly different bodies, embody the bodily criterion, while the rogue AI SHODAN, pure data abandoning first Citadel then the Von Braun, embodies psychological continuity from Locke's memory theory. He runs the standard objections (Reid and Butler on memory's circularity, cell replacement, cybernetic implants, sleep and infancy) against both sides, then turns to Parfit's claim that identity is not what matters, only relations of degree, likening the reused 'Soldier #G65434-2' avatar to a person surviving through successors. The player character, physical like the Many yet armed with SHODAN's cybernetic knowledge, suggests identity needs both body and mind.

parfit-teleportation.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
parfit-teleportation.title: Taking the Leap (It’s Not Fair)
parfit-teleportation.relation: Against the natural reading that Be Right Back fails because AshBot is a poor copy, the chapter argues that even a perfect duplicate, AshBot+, would not be Ash: like a perfect forgery of a twenty-dollar bill, it would share all intrinsic but none of Ash's relational properties (being Martha's beloved, the coming father of her child), which also exposes a fission paradox for psychological-continuity theories. Nozick's account of love as a 'we' — shared memory, autonomy, and well-being — explains why Martha cannot trade up or replace a dead partner without destroying the self constituted by the relationship. Parfit's view that only psychological continuity matters is then rejected: because Martha's relationship survives only if Ash does, survival itself matters, and Martha must mourn rather than cling to a specter.

parfit-teleportation.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
parfit-teleportation.title: A Dilemma
parfit-teleportation.relation: The chapter asks 'Is your cookie you?', running theories of personal identity through Black Mirror's copies: the soul theory surfaces when Clayton signs away his 'digital self'; Locke's memory theory implies Cookie-Greta is Greta - a reductio, since one person cannot be wholly in two places at once (the same problem for Ashley Too and the thousand Hang the DJ simulations) - and the perdurantist patch recasts Greta and her cookie as time-slices of one four-dimensional person. Physical theories (Olson's animalism, Unger's brain-essentialism) rule out survival by upload, so Yorkie dies when her body dies even though digital Yorkie continues in San Junipero; Parfit's no-self bundle view and the teletransporter case then dissolve the fear, since there is no ego to lose and ordinary survival is 'about as bad' as being destroyed and replaced by a replica. The upshot: the punishment and immortality plots (Joe's million-year Christmas loop, San Junipero) require cookies to be both conscious and psychologically connected in the right way, and the episodes' horror depends on leaving that genuinely uncertain.

parfit-teleportation.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
parfit-teleportation.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
parfit-teleportation.relation: Silcox and Cox read D&D modules as thought experiments in James Robert Brown's 'laboratory of the mind'. The Tomb of Horrors' four overlapping plane-shifted buildings restate Parfit's teletransporter puzzle — did the character who stepped through get annihilated, or is an exact copy walking around elsewhere, and does the answer differ for a Warforged or Tiefling? — while the Eberron setting's magically sentient Warforged run into Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?': players cannot access Warforged experience and are really exploring what it is like for a human to suspend disbelief, like Greek actors donning masks. Mary Anne Warren's Space Traveler criteria for alien personhood collapse on contact with orcs who pass them yet eat you, and with the Flumph — lawful good, rational, but killed on sight by the authors' own party — showing personhood cannot be the only criterion for how to treat strangers; the closing twist is that philosophy contemplates scenarios sub specie aeternitatis while D&D forces immersion sub specie temporis, a habit of entertaining the impossible that is itself a philosophical virtue.

parfit-teleportation.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
parfit-teleportation.title: NOTE
parfit-teleportation.relation: Asks whether amnesia preserves numerical identity: is the Peter who wakes in the shipping crate still Volume-1 Peter, are Niki and Jessica one person, and is the Sylar whom Matt rewrites with Nathan's memories now Nathan? The chapter builds Locke's memory criterion, breaks it with Reid's transitivity objection run through Mohinder's timeline in 'Five Years Gone,' repairs it with Grice's and Perry's memory-ancestor chains, then destroys the repair with Arthur Petrelli's wipe of Hiro (Forgetful Hiro vs. Stabby Hiro), Bernard Williams's torture thought experiment, Parfit's psychological spectrum, and the graphic novel's branching self-copier Evan. It concludes that no memory criterion can define personal identity, yet memory still matters practically: Claire must act as if she persists over time to keep her promise to Zach and to bother finishing the manatee assignment.

parfit-teleportation.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
parfit-teleportation.title: Notes
parfit-teleportation.relation: William Jaworski argues, opening with Breaking Bad's Skinny Pete and Badger, that you should never enter a transporter: after showing the MEM converter violates Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, he asks whether the reassembled pattern is you or a replica. He tests three escape routes—Vulcan katra substance dualism (The Wrath of Khan, The Search for Spock) in the tradition of Plato and Descartes; constitutionalism, on which you survive total replacement by robotic parts as Picard nearly does under Borg assimilation; and Parfit's survival-without-identity answer to Riker's fission in 'Second Chances'. Each fails or costs too much: dualism wrecks moral intuitions about killing, constitutionalism faces the two-Riker indeterminacy, and mere 'survival' cannot sustain the particularity of love.

parfit-teleportation.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
parfit-teleportation.title: Notes
parfit-teleportation.relation: Trip McCrossin reads 'The Enemy Within's split Kirk (with its LBJ/Vietnam subtext) and 'Second Chances's two Rikers as a crash course in Locke's consciousness theory of personal identity, from 'Turnabout Intruder's body swap and reward-and-punishment problem to the transitivity-of-identity paradox that blocks both Kirks from being the original. Parfit's degrees of psychological connectedness, he argues, explain why TNG treats the both-Rikers-survive answer as uncontroversial where TOS agonized over it. But Thomas Riker's renaming, and David Wiggins's 'only a and b' rule, reveal that identity would become an extrinsic property if branching mattered—so the survival-versus-identity debate ends 'to be continued'.

parfit-teleportation.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
parfit-teleportation.title: P A R T T H R E E
parfit-teleportation.relation: James DiGiovanna uses Dr. Manhattan's origin — disintegration in the intrinsic field chamber and self-reassembly — plus his teleportations to Mars and his split into three simultaneous selves, to run the classic personal identity debates. Descartes's immaterial thinking substance, Hume's mere bundle of perceptions, and Locke's memory theory are tested against a being who remembers in both time directions and rebuilds his body from pure thought ('restructuring myself after the subtraction of my intrinsic field was the first trick I learned'); Parfit's teletransporter, physical and psychological criteria, and fission cases — mirrored in Nagel's split-brain patients — then show ordinary people cannot say whether they would survive teleporting or bisection. The chapter concludes Dr. Manhattan is the only being with fully secure identity, since his consciousness needs neither body nor an unbroken spatiotemporal path and he can encompass several points of view at once.

parfit-teleportation.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
parfit-teleportation.title: II - AMNESIA, PERSONAL IDENTITY, AND THE MANY LIVES OF WOLVERINE
parfit-teleportation.relation: Southworth uses Wolverine's serial mind-wipes to test theories of personal identity. Locke's memory criterion, illustrated by Cassandra Nova and Charles Xavier swapping bodies in New X-Men, sorts Wolverine's history into distinct persons sharing one body (James Howlett, Logan, Team X, Mutate #9601, Weapon X), while Parfit's fission worries, mapped onto Jamie Madrox's duplicates, show sameness of memory is neither necessary nor sufficient for identity. The moral payoff: if Parfit's 'sameness of brain' view is right, we should be slow to blame the present Wolverine for Weapon X's atrocities, and equally slow to judge Emma Frost, Beast, or a resurrected Jean Grey.

parfit-teleportation.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
parfit-teleportation.title: What Happens to Brundle Problems of Teleportation and Personal Identity in the Fly
parfit-teleportation.relation: Paul Snowdon uses The Fly to press the metaphysics of teleportation and personal identity, asking whether the object leaving the first pod is identical to the one arriving or merely a replica (the reduplication problem). Adopting animalism, he argues Brundle likely ceases to exist at first teleportation, and that the fly-Brundle fusion is a new creature rather than Brundle, so Quaife's belief she is euthanizing Brundle is unsupported; a Lockean memory-based view (via Parfit) could vindicate her, but the audience's 'blind acceptance' of it gives that theory no evidential support.

parfit-teleportation.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
parfit-teleportation.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
parfit-teleportation.relation: Smith reads Memento as a test of Locke's memory theory of personal identity. He explains Locke's view that consciousness of past actions (not soul or body) constitutes the self, rehearses Reid's transitivity objection and the circularity objection, and uses Parfit's account of memory and fusion to defend a survival-not-identity reading. He distinguishes 'Leonard 1' (anterograde amnesiac who returns each cycle) from 'Leonard 2b', a person fused from his own memories and those projected onto Sammy Jankis, arguing we too are 'fused' survivors who reinterpret hazy pasts, complicating responsibility and concern for our futures.

parfit-teleportation.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
parfit-teleportation.title: A Dead End
parfit-teleportation.relation: Patrick Stokes uses the Doctor's regeneration and the multi-Doctor stories ("The Five Doctors," "The Caves of Androzani") to test theories of personal identity. He runs Locke's memory criterion against Reid's transitivity objection, Parfit's Branch-Line teleportation case (a Gallifrey-to-Skaro replica), Nozick's Closest Continuer schema applied to the Valeyard, four-dimensional person-stages, animalism, and narrative identity, showing each fails to explain regeneration. He gestures that identity may lie in a subjective self-appropriation, the Doctor taking ownership of his incarnations.

parfit-teleportation.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
parfit-teleportation.title: What’s Persistence Without Identity
parfit-teleportation.relation: Richard Hanley asks what counts as personal survival for a Time Lord, distinguishing body, mind, and soul theories. Using the Tenth Doctor's "every single cell" regeneration, the severed hand grown into a Doctor in "Journey's End," John Smith's Chameleon-Arch amnesia, and Jackson Lake's infostamp fugue, he argues bodily and soul continuity fail and defends a neo-Lockean mental-continuity criterion refined by Nozick's closest-continuer schema, concluding with Parfit that persistence may not be what matters in survival.

parfit-teleportation.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
parfit-teleportation.title: Be Slow to Judge
parfit-teleportation.relation: Southworth uses Wolverine and other X-Men to examine personal identity. Locke's memory criterion (illustrated by the Cassandra Nova/Xavier mind-swap and connected memories) implies that Wolverine's repeated amnesia makes him literally several successive persons until House of M restores all his memories. Jamie Madrox's up-to-100 duplicates function as a real-world version of Parfit's fission thought experiment, showing sameness of memory is insufficient for identity. Southworth applies Parfit's brain-based, seven-year view to Wolverine's constant healed head trauma and concludes we should be slow to judge characters as the 'same' culpable person.

parfit-teleportation.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
parfit-teleportation.title: 7. Loss of Memory, Loss of Me
parfit-teleportation.relation: Lay contrasts Locke's memory theory of personal identity with Parfit's psychological-continuity view across several episodes. Locke's factive-memory account explains 'The After Hours' (Marsha the mannequin) and 'Person or Persons Unknown' (David Gurney's non-factive memories), but fails for 'The Lateness of the Hour' (android Jana has installed beliefs, not memories) and especially 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You,' where post-Transformation Marilyn keeps all her memories yet is a different person. Using a Reid-flavored chain of episodes, Lay argues Parfit gets it right: a whole overlapping network of mental states, not memory alone, individuates the self.

parfit-teleportation.book: 297 - The Philosopher at the End of the Universe - Philosophy Explained Through Science Fiction Films
parfit-teleportation.title: 4. Total Recall & The Sixth Day
parfit-teleportation.relation: Rowlands treats Total Recall as a defence of the memory (psychological-continuity) theory of personal identity: erasing Quaid's memories and restoring Hauser's is an essential change that ends Quaid, so he fights for his existence. He works through and rejects the soul theory (dualism's problems) and body/brain theories via head-transplant and neuron-replacement thought experiments, distinguishing Aristotle's essential/accidental change and Heraclitus's river. The Sixth Day's cloning raises Parfit's fission/duplication problem: a double success cannot be a failure, driving him to abandon identity for a Heraclitean 'river of selves' bound by survival, not identity.

parfit-teleportation.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
parfit-teleportation.title: Be Slow to Judge
parfit-teleportation.relation: Jason Southworth uses Wolverine's repeated memory erasures to test Locke's memory (and connected-memory) criterion of personal identity, arguing that on Locke's view a new 'person' inhabits Wolverine's body each time his memories are wiped, until House of M restores them all. He then deploys Jamie Madrox, whose duplicates share and re-merge memories yet act as distinct agents, as a real-comics version of Parfit's fission case, pushing Parfit's conclusion that identity requires physical (brain) continuity. Because Wolverine's healing factor constantly rebuilds his brain, the moral is to 'be slow to judge' whether a character is the same person who acted before.

pragmatic-method.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
pragmatic-method.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
pragmatic-method.relation: Auxier, an Atkins dieter, argues the diet works for the reason Dewey gives in Human Nature and Conduct: habits built in calm moments are the bulwark against desire in crisis, and Atkins succeeds by reshaping which gratifications are habitually available — 'a steak for the black eye of desire.' He then transfers Atkins's physiology to thinking: television and advertising serve 'conceptual carbs,' packaged bundles of doubt, emotion, and readiness to act that bypass inquiry and leave the public 'intellectually diabetic' and ideological. Peirce's pragmatic maxim is translated into an eight-step mental exercise (worked through a parent's tattoo-or-piercing doubt about a teenage daughter), while Descartes's hyperbolic doubt is discarded in favor of pragmatism's 'genuine doubt.'

pragmatic-method.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
pragmatic-method.title: The Problem with Bullshitting
pragmatic-method.relation: Against the bullshitter the chapter recruits Peirce: genuine inquiry is defined not by method or results but by the attitude of truly wanting true answers, so homicide detectives, philologists, and car mechanics all count as scientists in this sense. Bullshitting is a free-rider riding the bus of real inquiry - even the bullshitter wants his doctor not to bullshit - and the chapter formulates an epistemic imperative: proceed on the hope that there is a true answer and act from the desire to find it, with fallibilism, not skepticism, the viable stance (the passenger who can occupy any vacant seat cannot occupy them all).

pragmatic-method.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
pragmatic-method.title: So Why Bullshit
pragmatic-method.relation: Violations of the epistemic imperative are sorted into Peirce's 'sham reasoning' (the creationist who reasons only to prop up a fixed conclusion), Haack's 'fake reasoning' (corporate-funded research, vote-seeking politicians, the temporary-insanity plea), and the skeptic's premature 'we'll never know' - none of which is bullshitting, which is precisely not caring about truth, like the sales clerk praising shoes at random. Even philosophy can slide into bullshitting when, per Rorty, it becomes 'carrying on the conversation' with truth as what your peers let you get away with; and brainstorming differs from a bull session because brainstormers actually want to discover something.

pragmatic-method.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
pragmatic-method.title: II - The Bull by the Horns
pragmatic-method.relation: Why do people bullshit? Because liberal democracy, heir to the Cartesian rejection of authority and the Enlightenment's think-for-yourself ideal, expects instant opinions on everything from people detached enough that nothing they say makes a difference; and because a failed search for certainty breeds prophylactic pessimism about inquiry itself. The cure is earnestness - scientists take colleagues' results on trust - though the chapter concedes defensible cases: the formulaic 'It's nice to see you!' as fake reasoning for civility, and friends horsing around for fun.

pragmatic-method.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
pragmatic-method.title: Finding Our Way
pragmatic-method.relation: Trudy Milburn applies Dewey's account of habit, impulse and inquiry to navigation in the series: Adama's 'I know the way to Earth' declaration starts an inquiry whose end-in-view is continuously reformulated as humans creatively combine scriptures, pulsars and constellations as signs. Roslin uses scripture at face value and other people's belief in it, which on Dewey's anti-foundationalist terms is legitimate map-making rather than piety. The Cylons, by contrast, treat their plan as God-given, cannot reinterpret signs for themselves (needing Baltar to locate Earth) and fall back on inherited habit, which is why, on Dewey's view, they are the ones who are lost.

pragmatic-method.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
pragmatic-method.title: “Something to Believe In”
pragmatic-method.relation: Reads Worf's crisis over the clone 'second coming' of Kahless in 'Rightful Heir' as a live, forced, and momentous option in William James's sense, where 'faith creates its own verification.' Peirce's methods of fixing belief — tenacity, authority, and science — explain why Worf cannot accept Koroth's pious fraud once Gowron's DNA test exposes the clone, while Data's own 'leap of faith' in believing he is more than a machine supplies the Jamesian model of believing without evidence. Worf's compromise — telling the Klingon people the truth but installing Kahless-the-clone as spiritual emperor because 'the words are more important than the man' — is offered as pragmatist truth: what works while staying answerable to hard facts.

pragmatic-method.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
pragmatic-method.title: “Here, Here, What’s All This Jabber-wapping When There’s Work to Be Done ”
pragmatic-method.relation: Tschaepe reads Professor Marvel and the Wizard as skilled givers of 'folk explanations'—stories about desires, beliefs, and feelings that work where logical, scientific, or mechanistic explanations fail—because each explanation is fitted to the pragmatic considerations of its audience and problem. With the companions the Wizard works through a failed dualist argument (a brain is not a mind) for the Scarecrow, an abbreviated Stoic ataraxy pitch for the Tin Man, and Aristotle's discretion-is-valor point for the Lion, settling in each case on folk psychology plus a token (Th.D. diploma, heart-shaped clock, Legion of Courage medal) that supplies the recognition actually needed. Dorothy, whose desire for home is real rather than mistaken, gets no folk explanation from anybody: she must combine the heel-tapping instruction with her own articulated desire—'there's no place like home'—which the chapter treats as pragmatically, not logically, effective.

pragmatic-method.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
pragmatic-method.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
pragmatic-method.relation: Ellen Sorg separates knowledge from intelligence using Kant's Critique of Pure Reason: Jeopardy! winners like Ken Jennings exercise only the first knowing power, sensibility - recall of facts as they appear to us - never ascending to the intellect of the Transcendental Analytic or acting on what they know, so Jennings would likely wash out on Survivor. Pragmatism supplies the missing criterion: Peirce and James hold that thought gains its value from its practical consequences and from the modification of conduct, which is what Survivor's fire-building, shelter-making, and Kim Spradlin's 2012-winning social game actually test. Hence Jeopardy! proves its champions knowledgeable, but only Survivor proves anyone intelligent.

pragmatic-method.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
pragmatic-method.title: Psych and Philosophy
pragmatic-method.relation: Amanda Lusky argues Shawn is a model pragmatist in the lineage of Peirce, James, and Dewey: he treats ideas as tools judged by consequences, is tough-minded about facts over theory (James's temperament distinction), and applies the pragmatic maxim from the squirrel-and-tree dispute to his loosely formed but working hunches. His co-operative inquiry with Gus and the SBPD - Gus's safe-cracking knowledge in 'Sixty Five Million Years Off,' passing Lassiter's polygraph in 'Shawn Rescues Darth Vader' - enacts Dewey's democratic community solving problems together, and the chapter reads his tolerance of Gus's paranormal leads ('The Devil's in the Details') as pragmatic openness that enriches Santa Barbara's democratic life.

pragmatic-method.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
pragmatic-method.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
pragmatic-method.relation: Pardi argues Jobs lived philosophically as an existentialist: the 'Steve Jobs Roll Your Own Calculator Construction Set' anecdote shows design by touch and intuition rather than master plans, every detail of a product mattered because it belongs to a life narrative of 'making a ding in the universe,' and he avoided both Kierkegaard's despair (the gap between actual and possible self) and Sartrean bad faith—quoted from Being and Nothingness—by never lying to himself about his products, calling faulty work 'shit' and redoing it. Against him stands Bill Gates the pragmatist, whose utilitarian Windows-for-every-desk business and 'rationality only goes so far' humility embody William James's pragmatic method, while Jobs's Zune taunt ('we made the iPod for ourselves') shows the existentialist refusing to compromise authenticity for market share.

pragmatic-method.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
pragmatic-method.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
pragmatic-method.relation: Clayman uses 'The Lonely' as a case study for whether Corry's love for the robot Alicia is true love, classifying it through C.S. Lewis's four loves (charity, affection, friendship, Eros) and their gift-, need-, and appreciative-love qualities. He deploys Peirce's pragmatic maxim to read the meaning of 'truly loving' off its practical effects, answers the objection that a machine beloved involves prejudice with Singer's speciesism, and borrows Kendall Walton's 'Fearing Fictions' to explain how Corry, knowing Alicia is a machine, 'becomes fictional' and role-plays a believer — concluding he showed affection and friendship born of loneliness, not Eros, since he would not sacrifice his place on the ship for her.

pragmatic-method.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
pragmatic-method.title: Love American Style
pragmatic-method.relation: Klayman asks whether the android Vision can love the human Scarlet Witch, working through C.S. Lewis's four loves to show affection, friendship, Eros, and charity are all open to human-android pairs, with their marriage best read as Eros—preoccupation with one irreplaceable self rather than sexual desire. Peter Singer's attack on speciesism is extended into 'organicism', the prejudice that dismisses synthetic beings: the Vision suffers, has interests, and laments that 'we artificial life-forms are still the least accepted', so denying androids love is arbitrary bias. Peirce's pragmatic maxim settles the question by practical effects—the Vision's care, kindness, attentiveness, and intimacy with Wanda just are loving—whether the lover is flesh or machine.

pragmatic-method.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
pragmatic-method.title: Finding Our Way
pragmatic-method.relation: Milburn uses Dewey's account of habit, impulse, and inquiry to explain how the humans navigate: Adama's blocked plans (the decommissioning) are reoriented into a new 'end-in-view' (Earth), and the fleet continuously reformulates its route from scriptures, star charts, pulsars, and the Tomb of Athena constellations as interchangeable signs. The Cylons by contrast cannot revise - Boomer's peace initiative gets her model boxed, and even Cavil's admissions of error lead back to the same path - because they locate their plan in God rather than in constructed, revisable inquiry, needing Baltar even to interpret the signs to Earth. On Deweyan grounds the chapter concludes the humans are never lost while the Cylons are.

pragmatic-method.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
pragmatic-method.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
pragmatic-method.relation: Klayman treats 'The Lonely' as a case study on whether Corry's love for the robot Alicia is true love. Using C.S. Lewis's four loves plus Peirce's pragmatic maxim (a concept's meaning is its practical effects), he argues Corry showed affection and appreciation but not Eros: he gave Alicia nothing, needed her merely against loneliness, and boarded the ship without sacrificing anything for her. Denying that a machine could be loved, he adds, would be a prejudice akin to Singer's speciesism, and Kendall Walton's 'Fearing Fictions' explains how Corry becomes fictional alongside a make-believe person.

pragmatic-method.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
pragmatic-method.title: From Sherlock Holmes to the Hard-Boiled Detective in Film Noir
pragmatic-method.relation: Jerold Abrams argues that the noir detective inherits the Holmes/Dupin detective logic but inhabits a fundamentally different maze. Using Eco's three labyrinths, he maps the classical Greek maze (with faith as Ariadne's string) and the mannerist maze (with Cartesian/Kantian pure reason) onto the escapable world of classic detection, and the Deleuzian rhizomatic maze, born after Nietzsche dissolved reason into will to power, onto noir's inescapable world (The Third Man, Kiss Me Deadly, The Maltese Falcon's fake statue). He shows both detectives use Peircean abduction (the logic of guessing) rather than pure deduction, illustrating it with knife-wound examples and Calloway's trapdoor inference in The Third Man, while the noir femme fatale becomes the anti-Ariadne whose thread of clues leads only to the hangman's rope.

pragmatic-method.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
pragmatic-method.title: The Logic of Lolita Kubrick, Nabokov, and Poe Jerold J. Abrams
pragmatic-method.relation: Abrams argues Kubrick's and Nabokov's Lolita is a philosophical detective story descended from Poe's Dupin tales, and that Humbert fails as a detective because he lacks the right logic. Using Peirce's abduction (and Eco's overcoded/undercoded/creative types), he shows Humbert excels at 'overcoded' guesses—spotting a nymphet at a glance—but cannot make the 'undercoded' abductions needed to see that Quilty is shadowing him, because he is all chess-like calculation and no playful 'musement' or acumen. Humbert (the resolvent) and Quilty (the creative) split Poe's 'bi-part' double-Dupin; Quilty the changeling-Minotaur controls the labyrinth and dies behind Lolita's portrait as a self without a unified identity.

pragmatic-method.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
pragmatic-method.title: The Dog that did not Bark Learning how to Read “The Book of Life”
