pragmatic-method.relation: Biondi uses the silent dog of 'Silver Blaze' to teach reasoning from absence, arguing Holmes's 'imagination' is a cultivable art—Peircean abduction combining observation, background knowledge, and the virtues of independence, courage, patience, and impartiality. She traces how Holmes finds Silver Blaze at Mapleton and unmasks Straker as the horse's would-be nobbler by consulting 'the book of life.' Framed by Emerson's 'study nature' and 'know thyself' (and Aristotle on what holds 'for the most part'), she uses the Irene Adler and 'Norbury'/Yellow Face failures to show how prejudice and overconfidence blind even Holmes to alternative hypotheses.

pragmatic-method.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
pragmatic-method.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
pragmatic-method.relation: Abrams reads Kubrick's Lolita as a parody of Poe's Dupin detective story, arguing that Humbert Humbert's method is not deduction but Peirce's logic of abduction (guessing). Humbert is the 'resolvent' half of Poe's double-Dupin - all calculation and chess - and excels only at overcoded abductions (spotting a nymphet) while failing the creative, undercoded abductions needed to see that Clare Quilty, the 'creative' double, is manipulating him. Abrams maps the film onto Poe's game-analysis (chess vs. cards) and the myth of the labyrinth, with Quilty as the ever-changing Minotaur whom Nabokov and Kubrick use for authorial 'involution.'

pragmatic-method.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
pragmatic-method.title: 9. Anthony Bourdain’s Inquiring Mind
pragmatic-method.relation: Anderson and Mauro trace Bourdain's growth from the dogmatic provocateur of Kitchen Confidential to a Peircean inquirer, using Peirce's 'The Fixation of Belief' and its four methods (tenacity, authority, a priori, inquiry). They argue Bourdain's tattooed motto 'I am certain of nothing,' his surprise and self-correction in Cambodia, Beirut, Saudi Arabia, and Haiti, and his pragmatic theory of evolving truth make him a model of the self-correcting inquiring life.

pragmatic-method.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
pragmatic-method.title: 5. True Love or Artificial Love
pragmatic-method.relation: Klayman analyzes whether James Corry's love for the robot Alicia in 'The Lonely' is true love, using C.S. Lewis's four loves (charity, affection, friendship, Eros) and their three qualities (gift-, need-, appreciative-love), plus Peirce's pragmatic maxim to define 'truly loving' by its practical effects. He argues true love falls within Eros and requires a reciprocating individual, invoking Peter Singer's speciesism to reject a human-only requirement; concluding Corry showed only appreciative-love (not gift- or need-love) and that his bond was really companionship—Corry became fictional (Walton) to have something to believe in.

pragmatic-method.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
pragmatic-method.title: Neither Here, nor There, nor Anywhere
pragmatic-method.relation: Randall Auxier reads Green Eggs and Ham as a primer in Peircean pragmatism. The contrarian 'C' illustrates how thinking only begins when a problem interrupts action, and Peirce's distinction between 'genuine doubt' and settled belief-as-habit explains why C clings to 'I do not like them' without ever trying them. Auxier runs C's stubbornness through Peirce's four methods of fixing belief (Authority, A Priori, Tenacity, Science), arguing C relies on tenacity, and likens Sam-I-Am to Saint Monica pestering Augustine into genuine doubt, so that even after C eats the eggs he only knows they settled belief in one context.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Knight places Atkins's caveman utopia — Paleolithic abundance, hunter-gatherer vitality, downfall through agriculture — inside the primitivist tradition running from Ovid's Golden Age to Rousseau's Noble Savage, whose state of nature Rousseau himself admitted was 'mere conditional and hypothetical reasoning' aimed at European corruption. Using postcolonial critics (Spurr, Torgovnick, and Fanon's line that whites who feel 'too mechanized' turn to 'the men of color' for 'human sustenance'), she argues low-carb primitivism is self-reflexive nostalgia — South Beach cannot even date its own paradise — that also freezes living Inuit and Indigenous Australians as Stone Age remnants, hiding the colonial and economic causes of their diabetes and poverty.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: In an imaginary salon hosted by the baker 'la Brioche,' the goddess Eris drops a golden apple inscribed 'Atkins,' and three philosophers fight over the credit. Rousseau claims Atkins's war on refined flour and 'invented fake food' as his own back-to-nature, state-of-nature legacy; Confucius counters that Americans are 'grazers' without li, that culture is nature's flower, and that only ritual propriety can counteract the advertising that fills the void; Democritus claims the scientific core — 'hyperinsulism,' 'benign dietary ketosis' — as atomism's heir, deriding Rousseau's general will as democratic truth-concocting and Plato's otherworldly philosopher-king. The debate ranges over free will versus scientific prediction-and-control and ends unresolved over a refusal of brioche.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Alford reads the biker image, born at Hollister in 1947 and fixed by The Wild One, through two opposed accounts of presocial man: the badass on his tricked-out Harley is Hobbes's natural man, all vanity, domination, and fear merely redirected to government, praising Chuck Zito's 'most primitive philosophy'; the club run with bonfire, brothers, old ladies, and Steppenwolf re-enacts Rousseau's golden age between the stupidity of brutes and the fatal enlightenment of civil man, before the first enclosed field ('this is mine') bred property, vanity, and misery. The paradox of a biker who is simultaneously threat and salvation dissolves once we see that 'primitive' and 'civilized' are mutually defining: suburbanites and bikers alike live both Hobbesian individualism and Rousseauvian community, each defining themselves against the other.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Roll Credits
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Dunn contrasts Baum's book, where evil is wonderfully 'small'—Dorothy melts the Witch in a fit of righteous anger at a stolen Silver Shoe, and personal plus social virtues (kindness repaid by the field-mice Queen) reliably conquer it—with the 1939 film, which smuggles back the 'heartaches and nightmares' Baum banished and resolves the Witch only by an accidental stroke of luck. He sorts Oz's harms into moral evils (the Witch's enslavements, the Wizard's frauds) and natural evils (the cyclone, the Deadly Poppy Field), cites Hume's catalogue of the world's ills, and observes that Baum needs neither Kant's postulate of God and a future life to join virtue with happiness nor John Hick's 'vale of soul-making' theodicy—Oz simply delivers the reward. Dorothy's abundant virtue at age five rebukes Aristotle (children, he says, cannot be virtuous or happy) and instead embodies Rousseau's Emile, natural goodness uncorrupted by civilization, while Chesterton's Doctrine of Conditional Joy and Tolkien's insistence on serious, non-technological magic frame the Old-World Christian outlook that Baum's demystified American fairy tale—and the movie's ending—quietly betray.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Singing of the Good Things
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Scott Calef asks whether Led Zeppelin's lives of wealth, groupies, and no-questions-asked liberty were genuinely free and therefore enviable. Locke's distinction between weak freedom (doing what you want, with Page happily locked in his suite at the Riot House) and strong freedom (being able to do otherwise, defended via beer-spilling concert excuses) is destabilized by the observation that no one ever does other than what they did. Rousseau then dominates: the state of nature versus LA, freedom as the capacity to resist natural impulse, which explains both Zep's libertine promiscuity and the paradox that heroin and alcohol enslave the very freedom that took them (the post-Physical Graffiti decline, Bonzo's death), while the band's violence—Bonham's assaults, the Oakland beating—shows society's suppression of natural pity, not natural aggression as Hobbes would have it. Socrates gets the last word: doing what we please is not doing what we truly want, so only the temperate person is free.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Greeley argues the zombie crystallizes specifically modern fears: with Aristotle and Aquinas he reads walkers as humans stripped of their essential nature and potential, which Rick's uncustomary eulogies ('I'm sorry this happened to you') acknowledge. Following Philippe Aries, he ties modern death anxiety to urbanization, hidden cemeteries, and the loss of religious consolation, citing the CDC arc where Jenner's science offers only a self-destruct and Jacqui falls back on 'the wrath of God.' Rousseau's thesis that society corrupts explains why the survivors in the woods seem more alive — warlord Guillermo turns out to be protecting nursing-home patients and pizza-deliverer Glenn becomes a hero — while the 'Bradbury's Storewide Sale' sign, the Walmart trampling, and Fromm's shift from utopias to dystopias suggest the shuffling horde is an image of our own consumerist, distracted, dehumanized modernity.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Fitzpatrick uses the social contract tradition to explain Prohibition-era Atlantic City. Hobbes's state of nature fits the gang warfare left where no Leviathan is strong enough to enforce federal law against Nucky; Locke's fits a night-watchman government overreaching into Prohibition and thereby breaking the contract, as with Nucky's illegitimate protection 'taxes'; Rousseau's noble savage corrupted by commercial society fits the Klan's pleasure in cruelty and innocent Tommy set against scheming adults. Ethical egoism frames Nucky's framing of Hans Schroeder, consequentialism the Temperance Union's cost-benefit failure, and deontology Margaret's lying campaign speech, while Marx's and Mill's view that human nature is malleable explains the season-spanning transformation of Nucky from half-gangster into 'a gangster and a half.'

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Chaib reads Craig Venter's 2010 synthetic bacterium 'Synthia' as a real-world Victor Frankenstein and tests it against Habermas's The Future of Human Nature, which condemns liberal eugenics because turning reproduction into manufacture undermines moral equality, rights, and autonomy - the same irresponsible isolation that made Victor abandon his creature and doom Justine. Rousseau and Thomas More supply the counter-program: hunger persists through unequal property ('This is mine'), not scarcity, so improving the human heart and social structures beats Venter's engineered fixes. Frankenweenie - where pets reanimated without love turn evil while Victor's beloved Sparky saves the town - lands the chapter's Arendtian moral that 'to live' is always plural (inter homines esse), so creators must care about their creations' relations with others.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Pötzsch explains the monster through Rousseau's Émile: innately good ('Everything is good as it comes from the hands of the Author of Nature'), the creature is corrupted because he experienced civilization 'too much and too soon' - the exact inverse of Rousseau's negative education, which shields the heart from vice instead of commanding, and lets the child learn 'through the mere force of things.' Victor knew his parents' model of paternal duty ('a deep consciousness of what they owed towards the being to which they had given life') yet abandoned his offspring and refused the female companion Rousseau deems essential to social development, so that wickedness born of weakness ('if I cannot inspire love, I will cause fear') murders William, Clerval, and Elizabeth. Shelley, a Rousseau admirer, makes Victor's science - an attempt to conquer rather than follow nature, fed by competitive professors at Ingolstadt - the very thing that dooms his parenting.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Caroline Mosser treats the creature's tragedy as humanist prejudice rather than necessity: the blind De Lacey accepts the eloquent creature sight unseen, so he passes Alan Turing's test, and only the sighted family's terror at his body rejects him - bias against the artificial, not reason. She reads the creature's development through fire, language, and revolution as Rousseau's progression from natural innocence to corruption by society, and Donna Haraway's cyborg as the figure he prefigures: an unfaithful illegitimate offspring who rebels against his father and undermines patriarchal Western self/other dualisms. The chapter concludes that society cannot accept enhanced or posthuman beings until it finds a middle ground beyond its binary grids of good/bad and Self/Other, since otherwise any new life we create will be Othered, hated, and oppressed like Frankenstein's.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Mike Kugler argues Shelley's novel tests the radical idealism of her father William Godwin, her mother Mary Wollstonecraft, and her husband Percy: Victor's Promethean project of perfecting humanity in isolation, away from the 'intimate circle' of family and friends, produces a creature whose natural benevolence is destroyed only by repeated exclusion, first by the De Laceys. Drawing on Rousseau's and Wollstonecraft's view that children raised by benevolent parents develop their innate sympathy, the chapter reads the creature as an abandoned child - a new Adam who becomes a Satanic rebel when every community rejects him - and Victor's attempt at reproduction without women and mothers as the novel's deepest violation. The redemptive counterfactual is adoption: what if Victor had raised the creature in his home, as his father did Elizabeth?

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Trip McCrossin casts the creature as a modern Job: repeatedly and unreasonably mistreated by the De Laceys, the rustic whose child he saved, and Victor despite his benevolence, he cries 'This was then the reward of my benevolence!' - but unlike Job he loses faith, because his problem of evil is secular, justifying not 'the Ways of God to Man' but 'the Ways of Man to monsters.' The chapter traces the problem from Job and Paradise Lost through Bayle's defense of faith over reason and the Optimists' 'best of all possible worlds,' whose credibility drowned with the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, setting Rousseau against Voltaire: Rousseau's Emile ('All is good leaving the hands of the author of things') demands that we make evil intelligible through self-knowledge, while Candide counsels tending our garden. The creature embodies Rousseau's line - 'I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend' - yet ends in self-abhorring remorse over Victor's death, leaving open whether self-knowledge can ever answer unreasonable suffering.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Homeland and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Trip McCrossin reads Carrie's 'I missed something once before... everyone's not me' as the modern, secular problem of evil: as Susan Neiman argues, unreasonable suffering threatens reason itself, and the Rousseau-Voltaire split defines the responses. Carrie takes Rousseau's side - 'All is good leaving the hands of the author of things' degenerates in human hands, so evil is intelligible and redemption possible, the chance at redemption she offers Brody and even Nazir - against Voltaire's Candide-style tending of the garden. The finale deepens this with Boethius's Consolation: Carrie's 'I believe one of the reasons I was put on this Earth was for our paths to cross' fuses fate with providence, and she accepts Brody's execution as a redemptive end 'more so if he dies'.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Gale and Barkman treat post-Mushroom-War Ooo as a state-of-nature laboratory for liberalism's three founders. The Forest Wizard who cages Finn in 'Storytelling' is Hobbes's Leviathan, kept in power by fear yet moderated by self-interest (Goblin King Xergiok's fall shows the leash); Princess Bubblegum's Candy Kingdom is Locke's civil society where citizens trade private revenge for impartial law—her lawful bow to Lemongrab shows she rules by contract, not fear; and 'City of Thieves' illustrates Rousseau's claim that property corrupts natural goodness, with Finn and Jake as his uncorrupted natural people. The chapter concludes that the rights language these thinkers forged is what keeps both Ooo and our world from sliding back into a war of all against all.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 6. Tris’s Compassion and the Problem of Evil
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: McCrossin reads Tris's whole arc as a struggle with the problem of evil, both the theological version from Job and the modern secular one Susan Neiman describes, in which unreasonable suffering threatens trust in human reason. He casts Tris as cut from Rousseau's mold - her insistence on making the evils of Jeanine, Marcus, and Evelyn intelligible - against Voltaire's Candide refusal to rationalize suffering, and treats the faction system as Rousseau's social-contract strategy for containing the inclination to evil while Tris herself plays a wartime Emile. The key is Tobias's lesson that selflessness and bravery are not that different: selflessness enables the courage that compassion motivates, from pressing her forehead to Jeanine's gun in the fear landscape to taking Caleb's place at the weapons lab, so that the trilogy ends with Tobias's 'we mend each other.'

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 4. Acts of God
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: McCrossin reads Lecter's parable of the church collapses - 'It must feel good to God - He does it all the time, and are we not made in His image?' - as Lecter's solution to the problem of evil in both its theological (Job) and secular (Neiman) forms: a malevolent deity of the kind de Sade's Saint-Fond describes, doing God's work becomes Lecter's justification, and killing feels good because 'if one does what God does enough times, one will become as God is'. Following Neiman, he sets Rousseau's tradition (evil must be made intelligible - 'All is well leaving the hands of the author of things') against Voltaire's Candide refusal of theodicy, showing that Will and Starling live in Rousseau's camp except when facing Lecter himself, and that the Hannibal/Hannibal Rising revelation that Mischa's murder 'happened' to him radically revises his earlier claim that 'we don't invent our natures', with Starling's reason finally making 'a place for Mischa' in Lecter and Starling together.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 4. Raising Darrow
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Trip McCrossin reads Darrow's storyline as an engagement with the problem of evil in both its theological form (Harmony dubbing him Lazarus, the parables of John and Luke) and its secular form, which Susan Neiman traces to the Rousseau-Voltaire dispute: must evil be made intelligible or not? Darrow begins Voltairean—incredulous before the rigged Laurel and Eo's hanging ('She left me')—but his resurrection and political awakening on the surface remake him Rousseauian: evil is the misalignment of individual and general wills, and humans are corrupted by society, not born bad. The chapter reads Darrow's 'Man was born free' broadcast in Morning Star, his new social contract with Victra, and the education of Pax (with Lysander left to Cassius to 'raise him right') as Rousseau's Social Contract and Emile program—break the chains, then educate each generation so its contracts align ever closer with the general will.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 6. Driven by Love to Go to War
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: John Karavitis deploys Alain Badiou's account of love as a contingent encounter founding the 'Two scene'—seeing the world from the perspective of difference—to argue that Darrow and Eo were never truly in love: their glade conversation, his 'nobility of obedience' against her 'live for more,' was two monologues, and you cannot love a memory. He then diagnoses Darrow as a narcissist in Rousseau's sense of amour-propre—self-love turned vanity that lies to itself—whose quest serves to manage his shame at failing to protect Eo, citing Erich Fromm on narcissism's path to fascism and Aristotle on habituation into Gold ways. Only the Jackal's stone-table imprisonment shatters the narcissism ('Man is no island'), letting Darrow embrace agape, with Ovid's Echo and Narcissus and the haemanthus framing the trilogy as a warning against self-love.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 16. Doppelgängers, Doubles, and Tulpas
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Reads the show's doubles through the danger of self-loss. La Rochefoucauld's amour-propre explains Josie Packard, whose courtier-like dissimulation ("she could survive by being what other people wanted to see") erodes her true self, while Norma refuses to feign virtue for critic M.T. Wentz or Walter Lawford's rebranding; Rousseau's account of esteem-seeking in modern society covers Sheriff Cable and Chad, who value Teresa Banks and the Log Lady only by others' judgment, against the Blue Rose agents whose values come from within. Jean Paul's doppelgänger, invented to satirize Fichte's I/not-I and intersubjective recognition, uncannies the Palmer home (Leland the abusing father), but the chapter concludes the show sides with Dostoyevsky rather than Jean Paul: Laura, like Mitya Karamazov, owns both her good and wicked halves, Leland splits, and Cooper's moral goodness is a wholeness — authenticity — that his doppelgänger lacks.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 8. From the Handmaid’s Tale to the Handmaids’ Tale
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: McCrossin reads Offred's silent prayers ('I want to know what I did to deserve this') as channeling the Book of Job, using Susan Neiman's distinction between the theological and secular problem of evil: even if we stop demanding explanations from God, we must still make evil intelligible, as Janine's Testifying cruelly refuses to do. He sets Rousseau against Voltaire on whether morality requires making evil intelligible, finding June Rousseauian for piecing together Gilead's hidden prehistory at the Boston Globe and for acting from compassion, as with the bread-truck driver's secret Quran. The Salvaging refusal—Ofglen first, then Offred, then sixty-five stones dropped with 'I'm sorry, Aunt Lydia'—shows compassion becoming solidarity and solidarity becoming a general will, transforming The Handmaid's Tale into The Handmaids' Tale.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 23. The Neighborhood Is Us
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Trip McCrossin frames the show, via Susan Neiman, as Rousseau's answer to the problem of evil: bad things (including bad television) happen to good kids, but education can mitigate evil, which is why Rogers prefers Rousseau's demand to make evil intelligible to Voltaire's Candidean refusal and Pangloss's best-of-all-possible-worlds. Rogers pursued only Emile's second prong, making us as we ought to be by loving children 'just the way they are,' and the post-9/11 PSAs before King Friday's empty castle merge Make-Believe into reality, the last 'modulation' of his thirty-four-year ministry.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 4. Can We Do Enough Good
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Fetterman argues no one can do enough good to earn The Good Place because the real question is who defines good. Moving from Hobbes's state of nature and Rousseau's innate compassion to Hume's bundle theory and the Buddhist doctrine of non-self, he shows the four humans' characters were assembled by their formative communities, which is Michael's whole defense before Judge Gen. But Nietzsche's account of how communities christen their own customs 'good' exposes the deeper flaw: the afterlife accountants impose their in-group preferences on all humanity, which is why even Doug Forcett's life of point-maximization fails, and why Michael should be asking the Frozen Yogurt Problem instead of blaming demon tampering.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Reflections on Technophobia
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: The chapter asks whether the technophobia of 'Metalhead' - robo-dogs hunting Bella and her friends across a wasteland - is justified, testing Daniel Dinello's list of fears (identity, values, emotion, freedom, life). Descartes's and Aquinas's human-uniqueness over the mechanical fails because the robo-dogs, like DeepMind, learn and problem-solve, while the episode's Rousseau-style romanticism (only the non-technological cliff, tree, sunlight and stream aid Bella) and the teddy-bear mission show technology amplifying compassion rather than threatening it. The real dangers are robots as Latourian 'black boxes': Asimov's Three Laws cannot be operationalized, and if we cannot know how robo-dogs decide, our frameworks for blame and punishment break down (who answers for a killing - robot, programmer, or, on Marx's analysis of capitalist technology as an instrument of oppression, the economic system behind it?). The chapter concludes that since we already share the world with robots, learning to live responsibly alongside them must replace simple fear.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: 4. Can We Do Enough Good
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Interrogates Chidi's question 'why do we choose to be good?' through Hobbes's selfish state of nature, Rousseau's hardwired compassion (Michael's 'little voice' in Eleanor's head), and Hume's bundle theory extended Buddhist-style to a non-self, which grounds Michael's plea to Judge Gen that bad communities made the four humans bad and a better community (Team Cockroach, the Brainy Bunch) can make them good. Nietzsche's account of how communities define their own customs as 'good' then exposes the deeper flaw: the afterlife's accountants impose their in-group's preferences on all humanity, which is why even Doug Forcett's point-maximizing life cannot clear the bar. The chapter ends by asking Michael's real question: who gets to decide what's good?

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Notes
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Jackson reads the show through Rousseau's contrast between the general will and a pathological 'corporate will': Frank discards Freddy the moment his criminal past goes viral, Tusk and Walker's old friendship curdles into mutual blackmail, and Remy and Jackie trade intimacy for career protection - all reducing Aristotle's true friendship to friendships of utility and pleasure subordinated to institutions that treat persons as means. Rousseau's account of civilization degrading natural self-love (amour de soi) into vanity (amour-propre) explains why Washington's corporate ethos leaves no friends, only 'loose ends' to be eliminated, from Zoe pushed onto the platform to Doug hunting Rachel. The chapter ends with 'Man is born free, but is everywhere in chains' as the verdict on corporate personhood's conquest of human bonds.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Notes
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Reads the show through Rousseau's contrast between the general will and a pathological 'corporate will': governments and corporations are sociopathic artificial persons that depersonalize their agents, degrading natural self-love (amour de soi) into status-hungry amour-propre. On this account Frank's break with Freddy ('just a good customer'), the Tusk-Walker alliance, and Remy and Jackie's bought loyalties are Aristotelian friendships of utility or pleasure crushed under the corporate will, never true friendship, leaving Washington with 'honor without virtue' and men 'everywhere in chains'.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Coatney explains why Katniss fails at everything she fakes — the disastrous first propos ('that is how a revolution dies'), the studio Mockingjay shoots, the cover-story mission to kill Snow — through Rousseau's distinction between amour de soi (natural self-love) and amour-propre (vanity born of society): she is a natural person in a corrupt world of seeming. The chapter contrasts district self-preservation with Capitol vanity (Posy asking green-skinned Octavia 'Are you sick?'), and reads Haymitch's smooth deception as a costlier, self-destroying alternative to Katniss's inability to dissimulate. Since Rousseau doubts any return to the state of nature, Katniss's refusal to flee into the woods — 'I'm going to stay right here and cause all kinds of trouble' — shows her Nietzsche-noted fate of being punished for her virtue, still preferable to becoming like Effie.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Reads John Teller's failed 'off the social grid' experiment through the human-nature debate: Mencius's seed of sympathy (even Tig recoils at Dante's dogfights) and Rousseau's naturally good man corrupted by society inspired J.T.'s Goldman-fed anarchism, while Mill and Xunzi counter that virtue is a victory over instinct. Hobbes supplies the real diagnosis—not innate violence but the logic of anarchy among free and equal rivals: competition (the Mayans blowing up the warehouse), diffidence (first-strike temptations against Zobelle), and glory (Jax unable to let the bike-sitting insult pass). Clay's rule that 'retaliation must be harsh and immediate' and the escalating Tig–Veronica Pope–Damon Pope–Opie bloodbath show deterrence fueling cycles of violence, so the only escape from the 'nasty, brutish, and short' fringe is the Leviathan's social grid.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Explains what anarchism actually demands—rejection of external authority, voluntary association, and faith that people need no coercion to cooperate—and measures SAMCRO against it: the club's president, church votes, chain of command, and the impossibility of Jax negotiating an exit all betray Momma Anarchy. The individualist/collectivist debate inside anarchism maps onto J.T., who retreats to Nomad and Belfast when the collective disappoints his individualist ideal, versus Jax, whose commitment to family keeps him building the collective. Clay appears as the anti-anarchist 'stone-cold egoist' who rigs votes and kills suspected rats, and the chapter argues the experiment was doomed twice over: the founding Vietnam vets' military hierarchy, and the club's dependence on the capitalist society and state agencies (CIA RICO leverage) it rejects.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Notes
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Reads Star Trek's "final frontier" through the European encounter with American Indians: the Hobbesian war-of-all-against-all stereotype of the "bloodthirsty savage" and Rousseau's opposing noble savage frame "The Paradise Syndrome", whose wigwam-and-tepee set mixes tribes into a no-place utopia. The chapter uses Hegel-style staged histories to debunk Star Trek's warp/pre-warp developmental scale (Spock on the Organians in "Errand of Mercy") as metaphysical assumption rather than biology, and counterposes the Prime Directive's noninterference to indigenous self-sovereignty and the Haudenosaunee-style consent governance that inspired the Federation. Chakotay's vision quests, the medicine bundle, Wesley's habak experience with Lakanta the Traveler in "Journey's End", and the Medicine Wheel in "Cathexis" are then interpreted through Jung's archetypes and collective unconscious, with Kirk, Spock, McCoy, and Scotty as the four Jungian modes of consciousness.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Greeley argues the zombie embodies a specifically modern fear of losing our humanity: walkers are persons stripped of the potential Aristotle and Aquinas made the measure of human worth, which is why Rick uniquely eulogizes the walkers he puts down ('I'm sorry this happened to you'). Following Aries, he traces modern death anxiety to the split of faith from reason and reads the CDC arc ('TS-19') as science offering only a self-destruct quick death where Jacqui's 'wrath of God' guess at least offers meaning. Rousseau's claim that civilization corrupts explains the survivors' return to the woods, where pizza-deliverer Glenn's heroics and the 'kingpin' Guillermo protecting nursing-home patients show the apocalypse can bring out the best in us while the Bradbury's Sale storefront and trampled Walmart worker hint we were already the walking dead.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Divided Self Kaufman, Kafka, Wittgenstein, and Human Nature
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Von der Ruhr reads Human Nature through Kafka's 'A Report to an Academy,' whose humanized ape frames the film's inverted arc (Puff raised as ape, civilized by Nathan, then reverted by Lila). Using Nietzsche's herd passage and Norman Malcolm on animal thought, he argues the human–animal difference is one of kind, so Lila's Rousseauian idealization of Puff as 'uncontaminated by civilization' and Puff's claim that 'words are evil' are confused. Invoking Wittgenstein's view that art should teach and that lying presupposes truth-telling, he faults the film's bleak, self-referential loves while crediting it as a mirror of the viewer's own thinking.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Woolfolk reads The Last of the Mohicans as staging a conflict between nature and civilization. The opening hunt is neither Hobbes's brutish state of nature nor quite Rousseau's amoral noble savage, since the Mohicans are full moral agents; Woolfolk uses Locke's Second Treatise to cast Hawkeye and the colonists as enforcing natural law and natural rights against English 'tyranny,' with Chingachgook's killing of Magua a justified execution. Rousseau's First and Second Discourses illuminate the hypocrisy and greed of Montcalm and the Europeans, and Camus's Meursault is invoked as a truer image of amoral natural man; Tocqueville frames Cora's democratic awakening as individualism.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Mark Walling argues that the appeal of Burton-Depp characters lies in a recovered model of childhood consciousness. Against Freud's and Piaget's view that children perceive less and are locked in the here-and-now, Walling uses Alison Gopnik's cognitive science ('babies are more conscious than we are') and Rousseau's romantic ideal of the naturally good, untutored child to read Edward Scissorhands and Ed Wood. Edward is a naturally gifted, innocent artist destroyed by a corrupt suburban 'society'; Ed Wood, megaphone in hand, is 'an eight-year-old who wants to be a movie director,' whose inattentional, make-believe joy in filmmaking—not the finished product—embodies the wide, wondering child mind Burton celebrates.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: The Power of Memory and the Memory of Power Wars and Graves in Westerns and Jidaigeki
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Brodey compares John Ford's Westerns (My Darling Clementine, She Wore a Yellow Ribbon, The Searchers, The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance) with Kurosawa's jidaigeki (Seven Samurai, Throne of Blood, Hidden Fortress, Yôjimbô) as postwar mythmaking that both buries and builds national identity after military defeat. She argues graves and gravestones are bivalent symbols—commemorating loss while risking perpetuating revenge—and that both directors oscillate between Rousseauean nostalgia for a nobler past and Hobbesian frontier brutality that must be tamed. Ford trusts that memory of past wrongs can spur a better future and enable forgiveness, while Kurosawa, more pessimistic and drawing on Buddhist cyclical detachment in Throne of Blood, warns of the dangers of both remembering and forgetting trauma.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: “Order Out of the Mud” Deadwood and the State of Nature
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Cantor reads David Milch's Deadwood as a dramatization of 'order without law,' testing the mining camp against the state-of-nature theories of Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau. Deadwood is Hobbesian in its sources of violence (competition, diffidence, glory; Al Swearengen's alpha-male struggles), but Lockean in showing property rights and commerce arising spontaneously before the state—gold becomes a self-generated medium of exchange that even overrides prejudice (Hearst dealing with Odell). It is Rousseauian in its innate pity (Swearengen's mercy) and its skepticism that incorporation into the nation-state, symbolized by the telegraph and Hearst's abstract corporate power, counts as progress.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Savage Nations Native Americans and the Western
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Michael Valdez Moses uses Todorov's analysis of Columbus and Las Casas—the failure to grant the Other both equality and difference—to argue that Hollywood's Native Americans, whether demonized or idealized, are egocentric projections of white American concerns. He traces the 'noble savage' from Rousseau's Second Discourse and Ferguson's proto-republican warrior through Ford's Fort Apache (New Deal common man), the 1970s revisionist westerns (Little Big Man, A Man Called Horse) as countercultural Rousseauian dropouts and Vietnam allegory, and Dances with Wolves, culminating in Jarmusch's Dead Man, whose Nobody escapes the collective stereotype to stand as a genuinely individual, cosmopolitan character.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors of Lost as a real state of nature, playing on the characters named Locke, Rousseau, and Hume. The scarce-water and asthma-inhaler disputes are 'tragedies of the commons,' and Sawyer's 'finders keepers' embodies a Hobbesian 'Trust No. 1' while Hurley and Jack lean toward Rousseauian 'Innocence.' Using game theory's repeated prisoners' dilemma and 'tit-for-tat,' Davies argues a Lockean state of nature (opening with cooperation) rather than a doomed Hobbesian one lets the survivors build a commonwealth against the Others.

rousseau-natural-goodness.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
rousseau-natural-goodness.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
rousseau-natural-goodness.relation: Florell and Wilson, psychologists, survey parenting through the nature–nurture debate, casting Locke's tabula rasa against Rousseau's noble-savage view of children, alongside Piaget and Kohlberg on moral development and Walter Mischel's marshmallow experiment on impulse control. They map the four parenting styles (authoritarian, permissive, uninvolved, authoritative) on responsiveness and control, argue authoritative parenting is optimal, and advise fathers to adjust discipline to each child's innate temperament rather than enforce rigid gender roles.

state-of-nature.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
state-of-nature.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Knight places Atkins's caveman utopia — Paleolithic abundance, hunter-gatherer vitality, downfall through agriculture — inside the primitivist tradition running from Ovid's Golden Age to Rousseau's Noble Savage, whose state of nature Rousseau himself admitted was 'mere conditional and hypothetical reasoning' aimed at European corruption. Using postcolonial critics (Spurr, Torgovnick, and Fanon's line that whites who feel 'too mechanized' turn to 'the men of color' for 'human sustenance'), she argues low-carb primitivism is self-reflexive nostalgia — South Beach cannot even date its own paradise — that also freezes living Inuit and Indigenous Australians as Stone Age remnants, hiding the colonial and economic causes of their diabetes and poverty.

state-of-nature.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
state-of-nature.title: Resistance Raps
state-of-nature.relation: James reads hardcore and underground rap - N.W.A's "F*** Tha Police", Ice-T's "Cop Killer", Dead Prez's "Police State" sampling Omali Yeshitela, Tupac's "Dear Mama" with its Panther 21/Cointelpro footage, Michael Franti's "Crime to Be Broke in America" - through Hobbes's Leviathan to argue that for criminalized black communities the social contract never held, so policing is not aberrational protection but the foundation of a police state. She distinguishes rebellion from revolution, argues capital converts the underground's insurgence into marketable alienation, faults hardcore's misogyny and policing of women and queers as counter-revolutionary, and concludes that a Leviathan which is the law cannot cohabit with democracy.

state-of-nature.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
state-of-nature.title: Reality versus Revolution
state-of-nature.relation: McPherson argues political rap has never been politically revolutionary, sorting it into three schools: the amoral "gangsta Hobbes" ethic (Mobb Deep's "Survival of the Fittest", 50 Cent's "get rich or die tryin'") that sees the hood as Hobbes's state of nature where no social contract with blacks ever existed; Afrocentric communitarianism, split between nationalist separatists (Brand Nubian, X-Clan, Dead Prez) and the more cosmopolitan Native Tongues (De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest); and a radical liberalism closer to Rawls than its adherents admit. Against Chuck D's "What's a smilin' face when the whole state's racist?", he argues Rawls's original position, veil of ignorance, and difference principle - applied with real-world knowledge of racism - support rather than oppose Public Enemy's demands for racial justice.

state-of-nature.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
state-of-nature.title: The Mystery Solved
state-of-nature.relation: Avery Kolers uses "Only a Pawn in Their Game" and its companion "Who Killed Davey Moore?" to argue that Dylan treats Byron de la Beckwith as a pawn: a poor white duped by divide-and-rule tactics, the psychological wage of whiteness, shame, and lynch-mob indoctrination into fearing a Hobbesian war of all against all. Against Aristotle's account of acting in ignorance, the chapter asks whether Beckwith's ignorance of his real enemies was culpable, concluding his bad moral luck (in Bernard Williams's sense) was manufactured by white supremacy and so reflects back on all white people. Dylan's refusal to name or voice Beckwith adopts Strawson-style objective attitudes, making blaming itself a political act aimed at the system rather than the shooter.

state-of-nature.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
state-of-nature.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Alford reads the biker image, born at Hollister in 1947 and fixed by The Wild One, through two opposed accounts of presocial man: the badass on his tricked-out Harley is Hobbes's natural man, all vanity, domination, and fear merely redirected to government, praising Chuck Zito's 'most primitive philosophy'; the club run with bonfire, brothers, old ladies, and Steppenwolf re-enacts Rousseau's golden age between the stupidity of brutes and the fatal enlightenment of civil man, before the first enclosed field ('this is mine') bred property, vanity, and misery. The paradox of a biker who is simultaneously threat and salvation dissolves once we see that 'primitive' and 'civilized' are mutually defining: suburbanites and bikers alike live both Hobbesian individualism and Rousseauvian community, each defining themselves against the other.

state-of-nature.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
state-of-nature.title: Poker and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Stoehr finds Hobbes in the saloon: poker in classic Westerns — Hatfield's farewell game in Stagecoach, and the cheating scene where Wyatt Earp first crosses Doc Holliday in My Darling Clementine — dramatizes the tension between the lawless state of nature ('solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short') and the rule-governed community built by an implicit social contract, with caught cheaters (Chihuahua signaling hole cards) marking where play reverts to primal vengeance. Poker itself is a Hobbesian paradox: a communal social event built on winner-takes-all competition, exercising both logic and intuition within luck's hard limits. The morally ambiguous Fordian hero — Doc Holliday above all — lives at the same crossroads of civilization and wilderness as the card table.

state-of-nature.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
state-of-nature.title: No Way Out
state-of-nature.relation: Leah Murray reads Romero's Dead series as an argument about the American social contract, individualism versus communitarianism. Night of the Living Dead's farmhouse is Hobbes: fear throws strangers Ben and Mr. Cooper into a makeshift commonwealth whose individualist half ('every man for himself' in the basement) fails, while Dawn shows the Hobbesian next step - martial law as Leviathan - after the state of nature returns. Land of the Dead's Fiddler's Green is a fear-born contract corrupting into Kaufman's hierarchy, and Big Daddy's zombies form the counter-model, a Rousseauian community of the general will based on mutual bonds rather than terror, as the priest in Dawn already urged ('we must stop the killing... or lose the war'). Following Tocqueville on civic association, she concludes Romero's survivors - Ben, Peter, Sarah, Riley - vindicate communitarian cooperation, even though Night's bureaucratic ending suggests there may be no way out.

state-of-nature.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
state-of-nature.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
state-of-nature.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors' beach as a "framed" state of nature: the stolen water is a tragedy of the commons, Sawyer's "finders keepers" defense of Shannon's inhalers stages Hobbes's war of all against all against Locke's natural rights, and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward civil society, a claim to punish on another's behalf. He argues no theory of human nature (Rousseau's "Innocence" versus a "Trust No. 1" attitude) is needed to understand the castaways: cooperation grows through iterated prisoner's-dilemma tit-for-tat strategies, which also recasts the real difference between Hobbesian and Lockean states of nature.

state-of-nature.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
state-of-nature.title: “Your Heavenly Father Feeds Them”
state-of-nature.relation: Calef takes the Tides restaurant scene ('Who are you? What are you?') and Diogenes's plucked rooster versus Plato's 'featherless biped' as a springboard for testing every classic criterion of humanity against the film. Aristotle's rational soul fails because Mrs. Bundy's 'brain pans' reasoning is wrong and some humans cannot reason; Descartes's language test fails because the myna bird can learn to talk while horrified humans go mute; Rousseau's free will fails because the birds behave unpredictably and resist instinct while humans are trapped, caged, and herd-like; Aristotle's political animal and Hobbes's social contract fail because the town's hoods and lawbreakers contrast with birds that flock together across species. Even the appeal to God's favor turns dark, as the drunk quotes scripture while Revelation's birds gather for a supper of human flesh, leaving the film a mirror in which we must examine ourselves.

state-of-nature.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
state-of-nature.title: E Pluribus Unum
state-of-nature.relation: Auxier frames Hitchcock's Lifeboat against Garrett Hardin's 'lifeboat ethics' essay, arguing the lifeboat converts political questions into ethical ones by stranding the survivors outside law and politics ('We're on our own here. We can make our own law'). The survivors are ethical pluralists - Rittenhouse lives for money, Kovac for equality, Constance for fame, Joe for God, MacKenzie for care - and their clinging to private versions of the Good lets Nazi captain Willy, whose only principle is survival, manipulate them all. Using Maslow's hierarchy of needs, Auxier shows the boat descending to bare survival, yet argues the mob killing of Willy when he hoards water is moral outrage rather than survival-driven, and that the final rescue scene replays the opening dispute with nobody having grown - a vindication of pluralistic democracy capable of unified action.

state-of-nature.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
state-of-nature.title: Once I Was the Student, Now I Am the Master
state-of-nature.relation: Johannes Bulhof reads 'Me and My Uncle' — the Dead's most-performed song, though hardly a fan favorite — as a parable against rational self-interest. The nephew learned everything from his uncle: how to cheat at cards, steal, and shoot first, so he rationally guns down the cowboys, takes the gold, and leaves his uncle's 'dead ass there by the side of the road' — the student out-mastering the teacher. Framing the song with Thrasymachus's Republic I claim that the unjust always profit (and his own students' admission they would cheat if they could get away with it), then with Hobbes's state of nature where equality, contested goods, and anticipatory striking make everyone enemies — even family — Bulhof argues the song's drunken lesson is that rational self-interest is communally irrational.

state-of-nature.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
state-of-nature.title: Don’t Get Into One
state-of-nature.relation: Richard Greene renames the Tarantino standoff the 'ex-convict's dilemma' and models it as a special case of the prisoner's dilemma, running from Ordell and Louis's separate interrogation rooms to the White–Pink, Joe–White–Eddie and True Romance shoot-outs. He argues the standard group-rationality solution fails because ECDS participants have conflicting goals—Eddie protecting his father, White protecting Orange, Joe wanting revenge—and his survey of Tarantino's six cases shows escapes come from luck (Mr. Blonde's entrance, Nikki coming home) or shared interests (Beatrix's pregnancy), never group rationality. Tracing the dilemma back to Glaucon's contract argument in Plato's Republic, he concludes the only reliable solution is: don't get into one.

state-of-nature.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
state-of-nature.title: You May Wonder How Come I Love You Care and Ethics
state-of-nature.relation: Gimbel asks what the E Street Band's marathon multiple encores mean, starting from social contract theory: Hobbes's state of nature ('no home, no job, no peace, no rest') and Locke's contract explain the ticket as a financial IOU — so a drunk, short Hendrix show wrongs you financially but not morally — while the contractual view of moral duty (the 'Hungry Heart' narrator who abandoned his wife and kids in Baltimore) cannot explain why a missing encore feels like personal betrayal. The gift theory fails too, since encores are expected, and expected things are not gifts. Care ethics (Ruddick, Noddings) fits instead: devoted fans make the band part of their identity, Springsteen sings 'to you about you,' and the No Nukes 90-minute set became permanent because he would not give his people less — while 'Pink Cadillac' shows the limit case, since you cannot love someone for her Cadillac.

state-of-nature.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
state-of-nature.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

state-of-nature.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
state-of-nature.relation: Four 'Phase Three' essays on world conquest. Terjesen asks whether Doctor Doom's magnanimity (Aristotle's great-souledness, contra the unity-of-virtues thesis Aquinas held and Philippa Foot qualified) makes him less villainous than The Authority, whose purely consequentialist paternalism - like Doom's Emperor Doom or Ozymandias's plot - usurps a free choice no mere power can justify. Barringer reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes: the Stamford explosion and unrestrained superpowers recreate the state of nature, the Registration Act is the surrender of freedom to a sovereign, and Stark, Richards, and Pym repeat Hobbes's flawed faith in 'scientific' deductive politics, sealed by the clone-Thor killing of Goliath. Hillerbrand and Sandburg pit Rorschach's Kantian deontology (no compromise, not even to save the world) against Ozymandias's utilitarian murder of three million New Yorkers in Watchmen, arguing via Laplace's Demon that even Dr. Manhattan - nihilist or Schopenhauerian recluse - cannot verify the outcome, so watchmen can be trusted only by knowing their limits. Ostrander's fictional NSC interview has Amanda Waller's Suicide Squad defended with Benthamite utility, the rejection of natural rights as 'nonsense on stilts,' and the Augustinian just-war criteria of just cause, right intent, and proportionality, while the interviewer exposes how conveniently those limits bend.

state-of-nature.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
state-of-nature.title: Singing of the Good Things
state-of-nature.relation: Scott Calef asks whether Led Zeppelin's lives of wealth, groupies, and no-questions-asked liberty were genuinely free and therefore enviable. Locke's distinction between weak freedom (doing what you want, with Page happily locked in his suite at the Riot House) and strong freedom (being able to do otherwise, defended via beer-spilling concert excuses) is destabilized by the observation that no one ever does other than what they did. Rousseau then dominates: the state of nature versus LA, freedom as the capacity to resist natural impulse, which explains both Zep's libertine promiscuity and the paradox that heroin and alcohol enslave the very freedom that took them (the post-Physical Graffiti decline, Bonzo's death), while the band's violence—Bonham's assaults, the Oakland beating—shows society's suppression of natural pity, not natural aggression as Hobbes would have it. Socrates gets the last word: doing what we please is not doing what we truly want, so only the temperate person is free.

state-of-nature.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
state-of-nature.title: No Way Out
state-of-nature.relation: Leah Murray argues Romero's Dead films stage the American contest between individualism and communitarianism inside the social contract: in Night of the Living Dead, communitarian Ben barricading the farmhouse against every-man-for-himself Mr. Cooper hiding in the basement; in Dawn of the Dead, the Peter-Roger-Fran-Stephen mall commune collapsing when Stephen's 'it's ours, we took it' meets the bikers; in Day of the Dead, Sarah's compassion against the racist, harassing soldiers; in Land of the Dead, Kaufman's Fiddler's Green as a Hobbesian Leviathan born of fear, complete with bread-and-circuses for the poor. Against the Hobbesian fear-born contract (Dawn opens in a full state-of-nature collapse) she sets Rousseau's general will and Tocqueville's civic association, embodied in Riley's freely formed community and in Big Daddy's zombies, who organize, turn from eating humans, and bring down the Leviathan. The films' verdict: fear-based individualist contracts collapse under their own contradictions, while compassionate cooperation — even among the Undead — is the only way out, even if Romero doubts its ultimate viability.

state-of-nature.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
state-of-nature.title: Is Fencing a Dishonorable Art
state-of-nature.relation: Michaud argues that fencing is the loneliest and most egoistic martial art: alone on the strip, you seek to understand your opponent only in order to deceive them through disengages and parry-feints. He maps the bout onto Hobbes: psychological egoism, the dueling ground as a state of nature of 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short', and the referee as the Leviathan whose rules keep the bloodshed out while licensing normative egoism inside them. Testing defenses from Rand, Friedman and Carr's business 'rules of the game', he concludes that fencing kept its soldier's anything-goes ethos after the lethal stakes vanished, making it a 'dishonorable' art: a Hobbesian feast of solitude, egoism and deception.

state-of-nature.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
state-of-nature.title: The Dalek Within
state-of-nature.relation: Comparing the Doctor's hesitation at the Dalek hatchery in 'Genesis of the Daleks' with the half-human Doctor's instant genocide in 'Journey's End', the authors argue the Daleks are mirrors of us: their survival-driven wars enact Hobbes's state of nature, while their industrial 'extermination' embodies Arendt's banality of evil and Weber's iron cage of instrumental rationality. Drawing on Horkheimer and Adorno's culture industry and Foucault's disciplinary institutions — modern techniques that mold the inner life as Davros's genetic engineering molds the Kaleds — they conclude the Dalek tendency is a human possibility, so we cannot exterminate the Daleks without indicting ourselves.

state-of-nature.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
state-of-nature.title: Spice as the Vehicle of Power
state-of-nature.relation: Reads the Duniverse as Hobbes's state of nature at galactic scale: Emperor, Landsraad houses, Guild, Bene Gesserit, and Tleilaxu are rationally self-preserving factions in a war of all against all over scarce spice, where 'justice' names only what enforcement power backs and life for the losers is 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.' Leto II is the Leviathan—a literal 'mortal God,' half sandworm—whose spice monopoly and fusion of political with spiritual authority impose a forced peace; his assassination then shows split authority re-igniting the conflict in the Scattering and the Honored Matres. Paul's threat to destroy the spice and Leto's hoarding both illustrate that the power to destroy a thing is absolute control over it.

state-of-nature.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
state-of-nature.title: No Matter How You Flip the Patty . .
state-of-nature.relation: Michael Dodge asks whether Krabs may guard the Krabby Patty formula, sorting Bikini Bottom's property into collective, communal (Jellyfish Fields) and private, and deploying the tragedy of the commons — Krabs's jellyfish-squeezing factory in 'Jellyfish Hunter' — to show why shared resources get rationally overexploited. Hobbes grounds Krabs's right in sovereign enforcement (without the law, 'Pineapple Fever''s chalk-line household collapses into animals fighting over the fridge), Locke in labor-mixing, with Krabs's identity bound to his patties since 'Help Wanted', and Hume in conventions of justice born of selfishness and scarcity. All three support Krabs's legal and moral right to his secret recipe against Plankton.

state-of-nature.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
state-of-nature.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Solves the 'riddle' of Gus by showing his empire runs on corporate instrumental rationality: the careful, emotion-disciplined Los Pollos CEO launders meth through legitimate business, treats chemists as replaceable parts (the Gale plan), and exacts revenge on the cartel in 'Salud' by drinking his own poisoned tequila. The chapter defines this as the critical theorists' amoral means-end reason - Kant's hypothetical imperative without the categorical - making Gus a sociopath who violates the injunction to treat persons as ends, and reads his cartel war through Machiavelli and Hobbes's power-first picture of the state. Gus's Two-Face-like corpse reveals the split between the rage-driven avenger of Max and the respectable mask, foreshadowing what Walt becomes.

state-of-nature.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Editor Wayne Yuen's introduction argues that zombies are worth doing philosophy over: an apocalyptic world without government, law enforcement, or private property raises live questions about how survivors should treat one another, whether life becomes 'nasty, brutish, and short', and whether it is wrong to kill a walker. He frames walkers philosophically through Descartes's mindless human-looking automatons and David Chalmers's P-zombies, creatures functionally like us with no inner life. Morgan keeping photo albums instead of supplies in 'Days Gone Bye' shows that what we leave behind after the apocalypse is how we lived - our philosophy.

state-of-nature.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Jason Walker argues the zombie apocalypse is a Lockean rather than Hobbesian state of nature: rights to life, liberty, and property persist without government. Rick's 'I don't think those rules apply anymore' to Andrea over the mermaid necklace is justified by Locke's spoilage and 'enough and as good' provisos - the owner is almost certainly dead and the necklace would otherwise lie forever wasted - while Morgan's house-squatting, which protects the Thompsons' home, and Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo's nursing-home defenders show self-ownership and norms at work. The counter-cases, Chris's cannibal band ('a man's gotta eat') and the Governor, who treat persons as mere means, live out Hobbes's war of all against all and are destroyed by the Lockean right to punish that victims retain.

state-of-nature.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Si Sheppard grades The Walking Dead's three settlements by political Realism: the Governor's Woodbury - cohesive, feared rather than loved, feeding his people arena spectacle to keep them from turning on him - beats Rick's West Central Prison, which never becomes a state at all. Rick lets Tyreese's vigilante murder pass, ruling as a first-among-equals with no institutions, no constitution, and no monopoly of legitimate force in Weber's sense, then covertly guns down Thomas and Dexter while hiding behind his cop credibility - 'it's me or you' reasoning indistinguishable from Shane's. Realism cares about power, not morality, so Rick's flaw is not cruelty but the absence of institution-building: he was never a bad father, just a bad founding father, who only becomes a Realist after Alexandria falls.

state-of-nature.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Moosa uses the apocalypse as a moral laboratory: since 'murder' is by definition wrongful killing, Carl's shooting of Shane must be judged by his reasoning (saving his father), and Hobbes's state of nature — 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' — fits Kirkman's world, yet the survivors import morality into it, as when parents mercy-kill their children just as one would turn up a dying child's morphine. Taking up Camus's claim that suicide is the one truly serious philosophical problem, he argues our world is nearly as bad as the zombie landscape, so consistency commits comfortable readers to the same duty of aid (helping sufferers rather than opting out) that justifies the survivors' fighting on. Finally he argues procreation is the worst thing survivors can do — nonexistent children cannot suffer, so Lori's pregnancy and Glenn and Maggie's crib plans are immoral, and adopting existing children as Andrea and Dale did is the consistent course, an obligation that transfers to our world right now.

state-of-nature.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
state-of-nature.title: The Wire and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Allen asks how a virtual war zone can exist inside the United States, starting from Hobbes: Marlo's cool killing of the security guard who just wants to be recognized as a man looks like the rights-free state of nature where 'nothing can be unjust.' But he argues Locke's sharper distinction fits better - the underclass are nominal citizens whose rights to life, policing, and education exist on paper while their substance is denied, which for Locke places an oppressed minority in a state of war within a state, and makes the drug game a rational choice for Michael, Dukie, and Randy. Marlo's 'you want it to be one way, but it's the other way' names that collapsed protection, and the chapter ends with Locke's warning that majority apathy lets oppression persist, reading The Wire as protest art meant to move viewers to political action.

state-of-nature.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
state-of-nature.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Leslie Dale Feldman reads the 1968 film's blasted opening as Hobbes's state of nature - 'solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short' - with the Lawgiver's 'Beware the beast Man' scroll echoing Hobbes's three causes of war (competition, fear, glory) and Plato's Ring of Gyges explaining why even the 'just' man acts rightly only under compulsion, both grounding the social contract's origin story. She then casts Dr. Zaius as Alexis de Tocqueville's tyranny of the majority - erasing Taylor's writing, lobotomizing Landon, and sealing Cornelius's cave 'to spare them all the care of thinking' - with Rousseau's man 'born free; and everywhere he is in chains' behind it. The chapter also traces Rod Serling's Twilight Zone fingerprints (nuclear-war twist endings like 'Time Enough at Last,' the cave of 'The Old Man in the Cave,' Adam-and-Eve survivor pairs, the beauty reversals of 'Eye of the Beholder') and reads Taylor and Nova's westward ride through Turner's frontier thesis and Kennedy's New Frontier, holding Serling's Hobbesian pessimism and his hope in tension.

state-of-nature.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
state-of-nature.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: John Wilkins treats Caesar, who spares the neighbor he has beaten, as a Kantian exemplar whose reason lets him adopt the Categorical Imperative, contrasting him with the rational egoism of the film's human keepers and executives. He argues the film trades on the outdated Great Chain of Being, which Darwinian tree thinking dissolves: with no higher or lower species, only branching homologies, human nature must be continuous with ape nature, and talk of innate species essences must allow for statistical variation and dispositions rather than determination. Caesar's morality also needs more than reason, namely the primate dispositions of deference and empathy scaffolded by his human family, though Buck's instant moral conversion after enhancement shows the film is ambivalent about whether scaffolding alone explains it.

state-of-nature.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
state-of-nature.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Fitzpatrick uses the social contract tradition to explain Prohibition-era Atlantic City. Hobbes's state of nature fits the gang warfare left where no Leviathan is strong enough to enforce federal law against Nucky; Locke's fits a night-watchman government overreaching into Prohibition and thereby breaking the contract, as with Nucky's illegitimate protection 'taxes'; Rousseau's noble savage corrupted by commercial society fits the Klan's pleasure in cruelty and innocent Tommy set against scheming adults. Ethical egoism frames Nucky's framing of Hans Schroeder, consequentialism the Temperance Union's cost-benefit failure, and deontology Margaret's lying campaign speech, while Marx's and Mill's view that human nature is malleable explains the season-spanning transformation of Nucky from half-gangster into 'a gangster and a half.'

state-of-nature.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
state-of-nature.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Pötzsch explains the monster through Rousseau's Émile: innately good ('Everything is good as it comes from the hands of the Author of Nature'), the creature is corrupted because he experienced civilization 'too much and too soon' - the exact inverse of Rousseau's negative education, which shields the heart from vice instead of commanding, and lets the child learn 'through the mere force of things.' Victor knew his parents' model of paternal duty ('a deep consciousness of what they owed towards the being to which they had given life') yet abandoned his offspring and refused the female companion Rousseau deems essential to social development, so that wickedness born of weakness ('if I cannot inspire love, I will cause fear') murders William, Clerval, and Elizabeth. Shelley, a Rousseau admirer, makes Victor's science - an attempt to conquer rather than follow nature, fed by competitive professors at Ingolstadt - the very thing that dooms his parenting.

state-of-nature.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
state-of-nature.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Kody Cooper runs Ender's life through classical just war theory: Augustine's axiom that peace is the end of all war explains why even his playground battles aim at a just peace, while the I.F.'s deliberate refusal to protect him from Bonzo's gang throws Ender into the Hobbesian state of nature where each person holds personal authority to use deadly force in self-defense. Sunzi's insistence that a commander must know the enemy grounds Ender's empathic preparation, and Cooper concludes the Third Invasion fails right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality - so the guilt Ender carries is really the I.F.'s and humanity's.

state-of-nature.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
state-of-nature.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Ted Brown and Christie Maloyed read Ender's Game as a Cold War debate between realism and liberalism: Hobbes' state of nature grounds Graff's survival-at-all-costs logic, and Machiavelli's counsel on seizing opportunities and keeping power by force when persuasion fails shapes Peter's insight that 'the right words can change the world.' The human-Formic war becomes a Prisoner's Dilemma neither species can escape without communication, and Ender's postwar practice of governing his colony 'by persuasion rather than fiat' delivers the book's verdict that the power to persuade can outlast the power to destroy.

state-of-nature.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
state-of-nature.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Gale and Barkman treat post-Mushroom-War Ooo as a state-of-nature laboratory for liberalism's three founders. The Forest Wizard who cages Finn in 'Storytelling' is Hobbes's Leviathan, kept in power by fear yet moderated by self-interest (Goblin King Xergiok's fall shows the leash); Princess Bubblegum's Candy Kingdom is Locke's civil society where citizens trade private revenge for impartial law—her lawful bow to Lemongrab shows she rules by contract, not fear; and 'City of Thieves' illustrates Rousseau's claim that property corrupts natural goodness, with Finn and Jake as his uncorrupted natural people. The chapter concludes that the rights language these thinkers forged is what keeps both Ooo and our world from sliding back into a war of all against all.

state-of-nature.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
state-of-nature.title: 24. Who’s Duty to Whom
state-of-nature.relation: Dawson asks why the Doctor sides with humans and humanoids against rational non-humanoids, testing Kant first: a logic-grounded categorical morality can count the Daleks as immoral rather than amoral (universalized slavery is incoherent), but pure reason cannot motivate Daleks or the Master, and Kant's theory absurdly condemns the Doctor's lies and his theft of the TARDIS. Hobbesian psychological egoism and the social contract fare worse - the Daleks are no co-signatories, and self-sacrifices from Katarina to the Doctor's seemingly final years on Trenzalore resist the egoist's retelling - so the chapter lands with Hume: sympathy and benevolence found morality on feeling, which explains and partly excuses the Doctor's parochial partiality for beings who resemble him, making him 'at least half-Humean.'

state-of-nature.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
state-of-nature.title: Hungry for More
