state-of-nature.relation: Wayne Yuen's introduction argues that philosophy needs extreme scenarios to stress-test moral, political, and religious theories, and that The Walking Dead supplies two: the reanimation of the dead and the collapse of social, political, and economic order. He frames the book around the show's most overt question - why be moral at all when survival pushes against it, as with Rick's compromises and the choice between searching for a missing girl or writing her off as having 'looked at the flowers' - plus how religion fares when the dead rise, and the string of attempted societies (the Prison, Woodbury, Terminus, Grady Memorial, Alexandria) that mirror our own world of failing nations and unjust rule. The essays, he says, hold a mirror to our values: we can become the walking dead without any zombies.

state-of-nature.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
state-of-nature.title: 9. Anarchy, State, and Apocalypse
state-of-nature.relation: Da Silva and McKendry test the political legitimacy of four post-apocalyptic governance types: the Claimers' anarchy that collapses into Joe adjudicating 'claims', the Governor's and Rick's dictatorships ('This is not a democracy anymore!'), the prison Council's representative democracy with the three questions as a quasi-constitution, and Terminus's quasi-theocratic cannibal creed ('You're the butcher or you're the cattle'). Using Hobbes's state of nature and war of all against all, hypothetical social contract, and the twin tests of power and morality, they judge even the benevolent Rick-tatorship unjust because concentrated power is fallible and unaccountable. They conclude, with Churchill, that the Council's imperfect democracy is the worst form of government except for all the others.

state-of-nature.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
state-of-nature.title: 10. Making the Punishment Fit the Crime
state-of-nature.relation: Heter defends Inigo's killing of Rugen as pure retribution - not deterrence or prevention, since Rugen 'deserves' to die for a murder long past. Locke's state of nature grounds the right to punish in victims, who merely transfer it to the state for prudential reasons, so in tyrannical Florin, where no reasonable expectation of justice exists, Montoya is within his rights to execute punishment himself. Kant's retributivism (the island whose inhabitants become accomplices if they spare convicted murderers, from the Metaphysics of Morals) supports the claim that murderers deserve death, and against the objection that proportionality need not mean identity of kind (following M.A. Moore, using Fezzik's hypothetical house-burning), the chapter argues death is the only punishment weighty enough to fit murder.

state-of-nature.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
state-of-nature.title: 12. The Law of Red Rising
state-of-nature.relation: Christopher Ketcham frames the Society through jurisprudence's debate between natural and positive law, opening with Gramsci's hegemony: Reds have internalized the Golds' message that their slave toil is heroic terraforming service, becoming 'enabled martyrs' who hate rival clans rather than their rulers. He deploys Hobbes's state of nature versus state of laws (Reds live in a state of war against Mars while Golds legislate in a state of law), Locke's suggestion that a sovereign can leave some people in the state of nature, Aquinas-style higher law, and H.L.A. Hart's positivism with Bentham and Austin—a law need not be moral to be law—to argue the Golds' caste statutes are valid yet ungrounded. His coda casts Darrow as Homer Plessy: Goldness, like whiteness in Plessy v. Ferguson, is inheritable property Reds cannot claim, and because Reds who speak are hanged, the law excludes the very voices Hart himself said keep laws from becoming terrible.

state-of-nature.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
state-of-nature.title: 14. Guns Don’t Kill Colors—Colors Kill Colors
state-of-nature.relation: Robert Arp argues from Hobbes's right of nature—self-preservation as the first law found out by reason—that individuals, and by extension oppressed peoples, have a right to the means of lethal defense, so arming the lowColors of the Society is justified. He weighs pacifist counterpoints (Augustine on self-defense as inordinate self-love, the Buddhist first precept, Camus's refusal to kill) and answers with Aquinas's principle of double effect: Darrow destroying the flagship to save Luna, intending the good while foreseeing the deaths, is justified, as is killing in defense of innocent children the Institute rapes and eats. The Society then illustrates why disarmament enables tyranny—Hideyoshi's Sword Hunt, Stalin's weapons bans, the Golds' razor monopoly—so that when lowColors finally receive weapons in Morning Star they become the means by which the police state falls: guns equalize the weak against aggressors and the people against the state.

state-of-nature.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
state-of-nature.title: 28. Severed Heads, Dirty Hands
state-of-nature.relation: Ivanković and Božac argue that ruling Westeros necessarily means dirtying one's hands, staging the paradox through Varys's counsel to Ned and Jaime's 'finest act.' Hobbes supplies the baseline that anything preserving peace beats the war of all against all, Walzer permits dirty hands only to avert communal death (Daenerys swindling the Astapor slavers), and Kant's absolute refusal to lie - mirrored in Ned's honor - costs Ned his head and the realm a war. The chapter also indicts the reverse: Aemon's refusal of the throne and other too-clean refusals of responsibility are moral failures, Jon's killing of Qhorin Halfhand shows dirty hands are not just for kings, and rulers must resist the downward spiral while keeping, as Dany does, a gentle heart for the true goal.

state-of-nature.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
state-of-nature.title: 5. We Become the Grid
state-of-nature.relation: Ketcham updates Hobbes for the network age: the grid born of ARPANET and Cold War mutual destruction has devolved into a new state of nature, out of which a coming 'Leviathan' - the one percent of the one percent - will rule invisibly by curating your memories, your purchases, your spouse, and whole countries like the diamond-republic fable. Invoking Descartes's evil demon and Heidegger's ready-to-hand, he asks whether we have become the grid, an external brain we can no longer control, and concludes that Elliot, the rogue 'Ebola' who hacks for justice rather than profit, is exactly the loose cannon Leviathan would quarantine.

state-of-nature.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
state-of-nature.title: 5. In the Neutral Zone, a Libertarian’s Home Is Their (High) Castle
state-of-nature.relation: The chapter reads Dick as a left-leaning libertarian for whom the deepest evil of the High Castle world is the loss of privacy: Arnold's surveillance unit and the Kempeitai's wiretaps illustrate Locke's self-ownership and natural rights, while the Neutral Zone poses the Hobbesian question of whether even an oppressive state beats the state of nature, and the 'libertarian minimal state' names what the Reich destroys. On this reading the American Nazis like John Smith were internal collaborators all along — 'it already happened here' — and ethics lies in refusal, as when Tagomi declines to sign the order sending Frank to his death.

state-of-nature.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
state-of-nature.title: 4 On the Origin of the State
state-of-nature.relation: Opening with Newt Gingrich's complaint that students 'don't read enough Locke' and the Chinese premier's appeal to Rousseau, the chapter compares the three contract theorists' states of nature and purposes of government: Hobbes's war of every man against every man yielding an absolute sovereign with no separation of powers, Locke's peaceful nature in which mixing labor with land creates property and money then creates inequality, so that government's 'great and chief end' is protecting property through limited, separated powers and no food stamps, and Rousseau's compassionate natural humans corrupted when the first man enclosed land, so the state was founded on fraud and a general will that should 'force him to be free' and give people food stamps. Smith then reads the actual US founding as a chaste Lockean contract 'bastardized' on race and sex - the Declaration plagiarized from Locke, Abigail Adams's 'remember the ladies' laughed off, Dred Scott, with the 14th Amendment as the de-bastardizing 'Charter of Universal Freedom' - while Engels derives the state historically from the Iroquois and Greek gens, private property and class conflict. A final section documents white supremacy inside the tradition (Kant inventing the scientific concept of race, Hegel and Hume on Black inferiority), John Stuart Mill's 'Negro Question' as the tradition's decisive anti-racist break, Locke's own entanglements with the slave trade, and Marx's condemnation of slavery as super-exploitation.

state-of-nature.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
state-of-nature.title: 8 Conclusion
state-of-nature.relation: The conclusion restates the book's method - centering political philosophy in a consciously normative, empirical study of power - around its two contrasts: the family as a natural, subordination-requiring institution in liberalism versus a property-rooted, historically determined one in Marxism, and the state as a freely agreed contract of all (Locke, hence no food stamps) versus what actually happened, a charter 'ordained and established by a small group of wealthy white men, meeting in secret' to protect their wealth, so that the state which created gender and racial inequality must now play an equally decisive role in undoing it. Reviewing the nine bases since the 1960s, it finds women have closed the knowledge gap and nearly completed Engels's liberation program except universal child-care and non-exploitative housework, against conservative marriage-movement scholars like the Lockean Yenor, while blacks still face a tripling wealth gap that only social democratic capitalism on the Danish model plus comprehensive reparations can close - the latter argued on the moral base of power, Congress's 2009 apology, and Bernard Boxill's Lockean inheritance argument for a decades-long 'Reparations Superfund' as the civil rights issue of the 21st century.

state-of-nature.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
state-of-nature.title: 18. Red vs. Blue or Both Simply Leviathan Green
state-of-nature.relation: Smith reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes's Leviathan: unregulated superheroes live in a state of nature where life is violent and brutish (the Stamford explosion and Scarlet Witch's Lagos miscalculation as tipping points), and the Superhuman Registration Act is the social contract - a literal signed contract on Team Iron Man - offered as the way out. He then argues both leaders act as absolute sovereigns who never sought consent: Iron Man rules through the Illuminati, enforcement squads and the Negative Zone prison, Cap through an unofficial army bound by his own rules, as Moon Knight's tirade about their ego grudge match makes plain. The war is thus two Leviathans colliding and subjugating everyone else, resolved only when Iron Man's Leviathan wins and enforces registration.

state-of-nature.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
state-of-nature.title: 19. The Superhero Challenge to State Sovereignty
state-of-nature.relation: Ewing argues the Sokovia Accords are at bottom about state sovereignty: via Bodin's absolute sovereign, Hobbes's war of all against all and the Leviathan's monopoly on coercion, and Habermas's account of the modern territorial state's monopoly on legitimate violence, he shows that Avengers who ignore borders and cannot be countered (Thor, Hulk, Doctor Strange, Scarlet Witch) render the state's claim to sovereignty effectively meaningless - the US can only police rogue heroes by enlisting other heroes. Since states cannot guarantee enforcement and state power itself can turn predatory (HYDRA's infiltration of SHIELD, Nazi Germany, Cap's 'agendas change' warning), he concludes that neither unchecked heroes nor unchecked states should rule, and floats democratizing superpowers to restore the sovereignty of the populace.

state-of-nature.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
state-of-nature.title: 16. He’s Ethickle Rick!!!
state-of-nature.relation: The chapter reads the Galactic Federation as Hobbes's Sovereign: Earth covenants in for security and gets an interplanetary TSA, pill-currency debt, and the surveillance droid Conroy, while the Citadel of Ricks tours Hobbes's three commonwealths in 'The Ricklantis Mixup', aristocratic Council, brief democracy, and Evil Morty's monarchy, where the Sovereign's rules cannot by definition be unjust. Against this, Rick embodies Hobbes's psychological egoism ('the object to every man is his own pleasure'), hiding his motives in the Riq IV hostage gambit and the Szechuan-sauce confession. Yet the chapter argues Rick's egoism is oddly ethical: in an infinite multiverse resources are not scarce, so refusing to surrender freedom to any Sovereign and competing for everything is the right way to live, with 'A Rickle in Time' and the self-sacrifice of 'The Wedding Squanchers' as its tested limits.

state-of-nature.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
state-of-nature.title: A Closer Look at Alice’s Trial
state-of-nature.relation: Argues Alice is right to attack the court of the King and Queen of Hearts because she never entered a social contract with Wonderland: unlike Socrates, who stayed in Athens and so had to abide by the verdict (Plato's Crito), Alice fell in involuntarily and is trying to leave. Dennis Knepp casts the Queen of Hearts as Hobbes's absolute sovereign whose public 'Off with their heads!' terrorizes the playing cards into obedience ('Covenants, without the Sword, are but Words'), while Locke's limited, consent-based government and Rawls's contractualism mark the better alternative the Hearts court fails to meet. Since Alice stands outside their covenant, she is her own more-than-a-mile-high Leviathan, rightly defending herself in the state of nature.

state-of-nature.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
state-of-nature.title: Easing Back on the APC’s Throttle
state-of-nature.relation: Treats Engineers, Xenomorphs, and humans as states and reads the APC debate through Thucydides' Melian dialogue ('the strong do what they will') and the jus in bello criteria of discrimination, military necessity, and proportionality. It concludes that Ripley's 'nuke the site from orbit' and Vasquez's nerve gas are vengeance masquerading as realism - the Xeno threat is no longer imminent, so Walzer's 'supreme emergency' is unavailable - while Hudson's withdrawal (even Burke's species-preservation plea) fits both realism and just war restraint; the Ben Tre 'we destroyed the town to save it' fiasco in Vietnam is the cautionary parallel.

state-of-nature.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
state-of-nature.title: A Specter Is Haunting the Bending World
state-of-nature.relation: Lin argues the Bending World's supernatural inequality breaks Hobbes's condition that even the weakest can kill the strongest, the equality that motivates the social contract, so might-is-right is magnified: Ozai rules without bargaining while weak Earth Kings become Dai Li figureheads. Energybending's built-in 'moral self-destruct' needs no earthly accountability, resembling the divine right of kings rather than Arendt's insight that violence eradicates politics, and Aang wisely remains a passive guardian. The Avatar's reincarnation creates recurring power vacuums, and because bending is a non-redistributable endowment, the Equalist revolution haunts the Bending World like the specter of communism in the Communist Manifesto.

state-of-nature.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
state-of-nature.title: A Specter Is Haunting the Bending World
state-of-nature.relation: Lin uses Hobbes's observation that in our world the weakest can kill the strongest, grounding the social contract, to show what breaks when supernatural power is wildly unequal: Fire Lord Ozai need not bargain with generals as Earth Kings must with the Dai Li, and the eclipse is the only equalizer. Energybending gets a 'moral self-destruct' that no real technology has, making Aang an unaccountable guardian closer to the divine right of kings than to naturalist politics, though his refusal of rule keeps politics alive in Arendt's sense. Like Marx and Engels's specter of communism, the 'specter of Equalism' outlives Amon, because bending is a non-redistributable, lethal endowment, so democracy in Republic City is structurally haunted.

state-of-nature.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
state-of-nature.title: The Anarchist You Are
state-of-nature.relation: Argues that anarchism, understood through David Graeber's consensus-based action, Noam Chomsky's demand that hierarchies justify themselves, and Kropotkin's mutual aid, runs all through ATLA even though no character calls themselves an anarchist. The Dai Li are an unjustified hierarchy that delivers Ba Sing Se to the very conquest it claims to prevent, High Monk Pasang's arbitrary rank authority over Gyatso and Aang causes the century-long catastrophe, and Zhao embodies domination justified by 'fire is the superior element', whereas justified power is self-effacing (Iroh mentoring Zuko without coercion, Katara teaching Aang waterbending). Toph's insistence that she can 'carry my own weight' in 'The Chase' dramatizes the mutual-aid lesson that letting those who love you help you is part of the cooperative human nature Kropotkin opposed to the Hobbesian view, and Zaheer in Korra, who rules by fear, shows that a chaos-bringer is no anarchist at all, while playful, communal Aang is.

state-of-nature.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
state-of-nature.title: The Thin Veil
state-of-nature.relation: Brett Chandler Patterson reads the No Man's Land storyline, in which earthquake-isolated Gotham is carved into gang territories by Two-Face, Penguin, and the Joker, alongside Hurricane Katrina's flooding of New Orleans as twin real-and-fictional tests of Hobbes's state of nature and the social contract. He contrasts Jim Gordon's lawful, Machiavellian-seeming rebuilding of trust with Officer William Petit's slide into execution-style 'despotic' power, and highlights the pacifist witness of Father Christian and Dr. Leslie Thompkins against Hobbes's demand that churches defer to the sovereign. Batman's turn as a benevolent gang lord working to hand the city back to Gordon shows, for Patterson, that Batman's real enemy is anarchy itself.

state-of-nature.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
state-of-nature.title: Theorizing Government
state-of-nature.relation: Tony Spanakos argues that Gotham's government, not Bruce's psyche, explains Batman: the state failed at Crime Alley, and nearly every major character reacts to a state that is either too weak or too restrictive. Working from Max Weber's definition of the state as monopoly on legitimate violence, Hobbes's Leviathan, and Nietzsche's state as 'new idol,' he reads Year One's corrupt Commissioner Loeb, Year Two's self-appointed Reaper, Anarky's failed anarchist dystopia, Two-Face's broken faith in the law, and The Dark Knight Returns' state-loyal Superman and Commissioner Yindel. The Batman-Gordon partnership emerges as a precarious unofficial order in which Gordon tolerates the one exception to the state's monopoly on violence.

state-of-nature.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
state-of-nature.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: The Bocks test three answers to the good life against the show: Howard as hedonist (laser-obstacle-strip-chess, the 'whore of Omaha') read through Bentham, Mill's higher and lower pleasures, and Aristippus; ethical egoism via Glaucon's ring of Gyges and Howard's offer to Skype rather than visit the deported Raj; and Hobbes's state of nature and social contract read into Sheldon's roommate agreement, whose lack of a Hobbesian sovereign leaves 'I settle all ties' arbitrary and rule-following too thin for ethics. Aristotle's virtue and practical wisdom crown Leonard — the nucleus of the social group, as Amy says — as the closest thing to the phronimos. The gang's sabotage of Dennis Kim with a manufactured girlfriend closes the chapter by asking who really ruined whose life.

state-of-nature.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
state-of-nature.title: “Real Life Is Messy”
state-of-nature.relation: The chapter tests Zootopia's 'where anyone can be anything' against three ideals: the founding play's predator-prey war is a Hobbesian state of nature ('man is a wolf to man') pacified by social order; Judy's parking duty and Nick's 'you can only be what you are' expose how stereotyping confuses artificial barriers with real biological limits to self-determination; and the evolved end of predation frames a just multispecies society, read through Donaldson and Kymlicka's Zoopolis case for animal citizenship. Nussbaum's hint at 'the gradual supplanting of the natural by the just' is weighed against the dystopia of turning the wild into a world-sized zoo, leaving Zootopia aspirational rather than achieved.

state-of-nature.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
state-of-nature.title: Spice as the Vehicle of Power
state-of-nature.relation: Maps Hobbes's state of nature onto the Duniverse: the Emperor, Landsraad, Guild, Bene Gesserit and Tleilaxu are rational agents in a war of all against all over the scarce good of spice, where justice is meaningless until a supreme power enforces covenants. Paul's threat to destroy the spice and Leto II's monopoly on a hoarded supply show how power over the resource itself becomes the trump card that forces peace, with the Fremen refusing to kill Stilgar illustrating the rational turn from mutual weakening to peace. Leto II, the half-sandworm 'mortal god' who fuses civil and spiritual sovereignty so that breaking law becomes sin, is presented as Hobbes's Leviathan, whose tyranny is 'quite literally, the best thing to happen to mankind.'

state-of-nature.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
state-of-nature.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Kody Cooper argues Ender's tortured conscience demonstrates the classical just war framework: from Augustine's axiom that peace is the end of war and the five jus ad bellum requirements, to the verdict that the Third Invasion fails right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality because the rational hive-queens were never given a real chance at coexistence. He reads the I.F.'s withholding of protection as throwing Ender into a Hobbesian state of nature where his fights with bullies count as private just wars, and concludes Ender carries the sins of the I.F. and humanity rather than his own guilt.

state-of-nature.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
state-of-nature.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Ted Henry Brown and Christie Maloyed stage the Enderverse as the international-relations debate between Hobbesian realism — Graff's 'if one of us has to be destroyed...' and the human-bugger Prisoner's Dilemma where the absence of communication forces mutual defection and war — and liberal institutionalism, which Peter's Locke and Valentine's Demosthenes argue out on Earth's nets. Machiavelli supplies Peter's theory of power: fortune opens the moment, virtù seizes it with 'the right words at the right time,' and force must back persuasion when belief fades, so that 'influence is power' and governing by persuasion beats fiat.

state-of-nature.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
state-of-nature.title: What Promotes Moral Behavior
state-of-nature.relation: Matthew D. Atkinson and Darin DeWitt use the Canterbury's ignored mayday in 'Dulcinea' — Captain McDowell's 'let the good God Darwin sort it out' versus Ade Nygaard's appeal to law, karma, and obligation — to ask what binds people when no central authority enforces rules. Through Michael Walzer's just war theory they read the Earth-Mars war: moral language is not 'cheap talk' (even Errinwright must dress aggression as peace and manipulates Reverend Volovodov's words), aggression and imminence govern when to fight, and five 'how to fight' principles — noncombatant immunity on Eros and Ganymede, POW rights for the Martian marines on the Kittur Chennamma, leaders' rather than soldiers' responsibility (Fred Johnson's defection after Anderson Station), proportionality in Errinwright's 'a base for a base' Deimos strike, and the rejection of ends-justify-means utilitarianism — discipline even Holden and Amos as they reflect on free will and culpability. The chapter concludes The Expanse is optimistic: human decency survives even in the anarchic Belt because characters keep reflecting on what their obligations to one another are.

state-of-nature.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Eric Silverman asks whether the Amazon series' Lucy and Maximus should have children, framing the wasteland through Hobbes's state of nature where life is 'nasty, brutish, and short' and even vaults are limiting experiments. He lays out Benatar's Harm Argument (pain outweighs pleasure, so procreation is procreational Russian roulette) and Shiffrin's Consent Argument (no one consents to being born, as Sartre's 'I did not ask to be born' concedes), then rebuts them: Socrates, the Stoics, and Aristotle make virtue and meaning rather than pleasure the goal of life, so a harsh wasteland full of people needing help suits a virtuous, sacrificial life like the hero's exile at the end of the original Fallout. Parental proxy consent legitimizes procreation as it does children's medical decisions, and Kant's universalization test defeats the demand for pre-natal consent, since universalizing it would eliminate the very rational beings whose consent it protects - so Lucy's 'Okey dokey!' optimism wins.

state-of-nature.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Curry and Lang test 'War never changes' through Hobbes and Xunzi: the wasteland - where the Ghoul asks who ever elected the 'President' in 'The Trap' and Cooper Howard decays outside all political order - is Hobbes's state of nature of restless power-seeking, while Xunzi's claim that bad human nature needs ritual (li) and righteousness (yi) explains a world with no moral education, where Elder Cleric Quintus pairs noble talk with 'power is taken, not given'. Fallout's Great War then fails every just-war test: China's invasion of Alaska stretches just cause, the corporatist US lacks right authority, propaganda undid last resort, mutually assured destruction explodes proportionality, and Vault-Tec shelters plus battlefield mini-nukes breach discrimination and proportionality in bello - with Operation Anchorage's propaganda simulation illustrating the revisionist point that fighting cleanly cannot redeem an unjust war. China's 'righteous army' (yi bing) tradition - Sunzi's strategic restraint, Mohist defensive war, Mengzi's true king, Xunzi's punitive righteous war - leaves no trace beyond Captain Zao, so the war's constancy marks the failure of every philosophical attempt to bind war to justice.

state-of-nature.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: The chapter asks why audiences relish stories of civilization's end and answers with psychology: the wasteland is Hobbes's 'nasty, brutish, and short' (raiders abducting Hank, Vault-Tec's experiments on dwellers), yet Ernest Becker's death-denial and Maslow's hierarchy of needs explain the appeal — fiction lets us confront mortality safely while watching characters meet needs for security, control, and meaning. The show's scenes carry the argument: the Vault 33 Council suppressing Lucy's search party trades freedom for safety, Maximus letting Titus bleed out reclaims control of his destiny, and Lucy's gift of life-sustaining vials to the unconscious Ghoul models hope and retained humanity. Apocalypse originally means 'an uncovering', so these narratives reveal what viewers value and let them rehearse their own endings.

state-of-nature.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
state-of-nature.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Greg Littmann asks who should rule Westeros and answers with Hobbes's Leviathan: people act only from self-interest ('we are all Lord Littlefinger under the skin') and fight for gain, safety, and glory - the mountain clans, Robert's preemptive strike on Daenerys, Drogo's wars for pride - so without a sovereign life is a war of all against all, and only an absolute ruler makes oath-keeping self-interested. Mapping Hobbes's own civil war (the Stuarts onto the Targaryens), he argues that even Varys is right to serve 'the realm' and peace by betraying Ned, and that loyalty rightly transfers from Aerys to Robert to Joffrey because protection, not lineage or justice, is the point of the sovereign. He then criticizes Hobbes: Ned and Jon show people really do die for principle, and Mad King Aerys's overcentralized power left rebellion as the only remedy - the War of the Five Kings shows civil war's horror must be weighed against appeals to honor.

state-of-nature.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
state-of-nature.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: David Hahn contends Ned died because of his honor, not for it. Hobbes explains why: words bind no one without fear of enforcement - Cersei ripping up Robert's will ('Is this meant to be your shield, Lord Stark?') exposes Ned's belief that allegiance alone secures the King's Justice - and the Iron Throne itself is a Leviathan, forged by Aegon's dragons ending the state of nature, whose force rather than justice holds the peace. Machiavelli supplies the indictment of Ned's idealism: 'we who presume to rule must do vile things for the good of the realm,' so Ned's refusal to assassinate Daenerys, his merciful warning to Cersei, and backing the rightful but war-prone Stannis over Renly cost him his head and plunged the realm into civil war; the security of the state demanded exiling or killing the Lannisters and crowning Renly.

state-of-nature.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Sharp argues that superpowered individuals break the equality assumption on which social contract theory rests: since Claire cannot be killed, D.L. can walk out of any jail, and Matt can sway juries, Hobbes's fear-of-death rationale for the contract seems not to apply to them. He then answers that the heroes remain effectively equal (Claire can still be killed by a wood splinter, Adam by decapitation) and shares Locke's and Rawls's reasons for contract, yet shows Rawls's difference principle would force the powered to serve society while the liberty principle forbids it, and that Sylar could not even be morally condemned under a pure Hobbesian reading. Cases like Claude's invisible petty theft (Glaucon's Ring of Gyges made real), the 'Five Years Gone' registered-superhumans future, and Linderman's plot to reunite society through the New York explosion lead to the conclusion that superpowers really would break society.

state-of-nature.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Casts Frank as the 'Foole' of Leviathan chapter 15 — the man who grants that covenants exist but thinks injustice can 'stand with reason' — and documents his befriend-then-betray pattern: Russo groomed for governor then gassed in his car, Zoe fed stories then pushed under a train, Walker befriended, helped and maneuvered into resigning, all to reap the contract's benefits while breaking it for 'the getting of a kingdom'. The chapter then defends Hobbes' reply via Kavka: the Foole's vainglory makes him overestimate his ability to deceive, and a detailed audit of Frank's two murders (fingerprints, witnesses, electronic traces, forensic evidence, alibis, high-stakes deception 'tells') shows them contingency-riddled and irrational. Even Frank's success is no defense — his presidency rests on others' errors and luck (Skorsy, Orsay, Tusk, Stamper, and above all Claire all remain loose ends), so he exemplifies the vainglorious Foole acting against the reason of his preservation rather than a rational violator of the social contract.

state-of-nature.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Argues Frank is 'Hobbesian to the core': for him democracy is just the state of nature with elections, which is why it produces mediocre, fearful presidents like Walker (a Xanax-taking incumbent undone by a mere legislator) while a real sovereign like Frank — or the autocrat Petrov, with whom Frank shares cigars precisely because no common power enforces rules between them — gets things done. The chapter reads Frank's appetites (ribs at Freddy's, power over money against Remy and Tusk, contempt for sleep and death) through Hobbes' pleasure-and-pain psychology and his account of conflict arising when equals want the same thing, which finally drives Claire from the White House. Frank's church scenes ('I pray to myself, for myself') illustrate Hobbes' subordination of religion to civil power, the Kate Baldwin 'he is the tyrant' charge illustrates that a tyrant is only a king disliked, and the closing appeal is to Madison's Federalist 51: only the ambition of others can contain this one.

state-of-nature.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Courtland uses Hobbes's 'Foole' from Leviathan — who grants that covenants exist but insists injustice 'may sometimes stand with reason' — as the template for Frank, who enjoys the benefits of the social contract (security, cooperation, even Freddy's BBQ) while befriending and betraying Russo, Zoe, and Walker up to outright murder. Applying Hobbes's reply, the chapter audits both murders as contingency-ridden blunders — fingerprints, witnesses, cameras, forensic evidence, and the 'tells' of high-stakes deception — and diagnoses Frank's confidence as the vainglory behind Kavka's 'Foole's gold.' Even his success proves nothing: in the Latin Leviathan a fortunate outcome of reckless action is still imprudence, and his 'kingdom' rests on loose ends (Skorsky, Orsay, Tusk, Stamper, and Claire) that could bring the house of cards down.

state-of-nature.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Michels reads Frank as 'Hobbesian to the core' and democracy as 'the state of nature with elections': Walker, Matthews, and Vasquez show that elections elevate mediocrities, while Frank's America Works and his FEMA/Stafford Act end-run around Congress display the energetic sovereign for whom 'a tyrant is only a king disliked.' Hobbes's pleasure-pain psychology of appetite and aversion explains the cast — Frank's ribs, PlayStation, and pure taste for power; Russo's indiscriminate addictions; Doug's serial ones — while Hobbes's competition for gain, fear, and glory structures the Tusk money-versus-power war whose casualties include Freddy. With Hobbes's subordination of religion to civil power, Frank's crucifix-spitting 'I pray to myself, for myself' caps the case that truth only obstructs sovereignty, leaving Madison's 'ambition must be made to counteract ambition' as the lone check.

state-of-nature.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
state-of-nature.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Coatney explains why Katniss fails at everything she fakes — the disastrous first propos ('that is how a revolution dies'), the studio Mockingjay shoots, the cover-story mission to kill Snow — through Rousseau's distinction between amour de soi (natural self-love) and amour-propre (vanity born of society): she is a natural person in a corrupt world of seeming. The chapter contrasts district self-preservation with Capitol vanity (Posy asking green-skinned Octavia 'Are you sick?'), and reads Haymitch's smooth deception as a costlier, self-destroying alternative to Katniss's inability to dissimulate. Since Rousseau doubts any return to the state of nature, Katniss's refusal to flee into the woods — 'I'm going to stay right here and cause all kinds of trouble' — shows her Nietzsche-noted fate of being punished for her virtue, still preferable to becoming like Effie.

state-of-nature.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
state-of-nature.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Foy reads the arena as Hobbes's state of nature recreated: the Cornucopia bloodbath, 'stealing isn't illegal here,' and temporary alliances awaiting betrayal instantiate the war of all against all, while the Treaty of Treason is Panem's written social contract buying order at the price of submission to the Capitol. Gale's advice that killing tributes is 'just hunting' mirrors the Hobbesian maxim the Gamemakers want, whereas Peeta's vow to show he is 'more than a piece in their Games' expresses Kant's categorical imperative and the duty to treat humanity as an end. Katniss's arc — decorating Rue's body, risking her life at the feast for Peeta's medicine, telling the District 2 soldier 'I'm done killing their slaves,' and rejecting Gale's tactic of bombing rescuers — moves her from survival logic to Kantian moral autonomy. The chapter ends by rejecting the Hobbesian justification of oppressive rule: a life of fear and servitude is not worth preserving at any cost.

state-of-nature.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Skoble argues the Mad Max world is misread as anarchy: Immortan Joe, Aunty Entity, and Humungus are genuine rulers, so the Wasteland depicts tyrannical bad government, not 'no rulers'. Against Hobbes's claim that only fear of a sovereign produces order, he cites organically evolved order (medieval merchant law, the common law, private arbitration firms) and Locke's mere 'inconveniences' of statelessness to argue peaceful anarchism is possible and stable. Thunderdome's 'two men enter, one man leaves' shows the films' dispute resolution is power-based trial by combat, not the consent-based voluntary order anarchism envisions.

state-of-nature.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Spanakos and Drake argue that although the films look Hobbesian — life 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' on roads without guardrails — rule in the Wasteland is never sustained by violence alone. Humungus needs the Toadie's epithets ('Lord Humungus... the Ayatollah of Rock and Rolla') and Immortan Joe rules through water rituals and the Valhalla myth that send War Boys kamakrazee willingly, believing they pursue their own glory. Drawing Weber's power/authority distinction, Arendt on power as people acting in concert, and above all Byung-Chul Han, they argue power takes its place 'in the soul of the other' through ritual, habit, and titles, turning into violence only when mediation fails.

state-of-nature.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Littmann treats Hobbes's Leviathan as a survival manual for post-apocalyptic Australia: the films illustrate his three causes of conflict — resource wars over guzzoline and water, preemptive strikes, and glory (the Nightrider's radio rant, Wez's stunts, the War Boys' 'Witness me!'). Bartertown's Thunderdome covenant and 'bust a deal, face the wheel' exemplify the social contract enforced by an absolute sovereign like Aunty Entity, while divided power (Master Blaster versus Aunty) courts civil war. He concludes Hobbes errs twice: Max's selfless acts (sparing Blaster, transfusing Furiosa) refute psychological egoism, and concentrating power in an Immortan Joe invites the very violence it fears — democracy removes leaders without blood.

state-of-nature.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Kuzma uses MacIntyre's After Virtue to argue the Wasteland is modern morality itself: a fragmentary rubble where, like Bartertown's cobbled-together vehicles, utilitarian and deontological fragments survive without the shared telos that gave them meaning. Immortan Joe's V8 cult imposes a false telos and embodies Nietzsche's will-to-power Übermensch, while Bartertown's rules express mere individualism without any vision of the good life. Max — 'haunted by those I could not protect' — can seek the good life only by joining Furiosa's community and embracing its telos, and the Green Place turns out to be not a place but a way of life, confirming MacIntyre's Aristotle over Nietzsche.

state-of-nature.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Held uses the Wasteland as a Hobbesian state-of-nature reset to pry apart biological sex and socially constructed gender: Aunty Entity and Furiosa show that sex is not destiny — one is not born, but becomes, a woman, as Beauvoir says — while the apocalypse scrambles gendered conventions yet leaves reproductive biology untouched. Butler's sex/gender distinction frames how a real difference like gestation gets weaponized into Immortan Joe's breeder system: the biology is a fact, the enslavement a choice. Finally, the casually acknowledged bond between Wez and the Golden Youth looks 'homoerotic' only through the viewer's heteronormativity — in the Wasteland, orientation categories simply stop mattering.

state-of-nature.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Davies treats the beach camp as an actual state of nature: the stolen drinking water is a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers show how the crash scrubs pre-existing property rights (Hobbes: two men desiring the same thing become enemies), and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward Locke's civil society by enforcing others' rights through punishment rather than self-defense. He rejects theories of human nature - Rousseauan 'Innocence' versus a 'Trust No One' outlook - in favor of the repeated prisoner's dilemma, arguing the survivors stabilize cooperation through tit-for-tat: beginning cooperative with strangers and retaliating against the Others. On this reading the real difference between Hobbes and Locke is which round of the repeated dilemma each takes as the starting point.

state-of-nature.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Fosl argues that although the survivors' internal order looks Lockean - Jack's uncoerced leadership, natural rights, minimal government - and is bonded by Rousseauan pity and Humean sympathy (Kate staying in the cage with Sawyer, 'live together, die alone'), the show's deepest political logic follows Carl Schmitt's friend-enemy distinction: the survivors cohere only in opposition to the Others, torture is excused in liberal terms, and conflicts end in redemptive violence, with Jack both killing the enemy and dying a Christlike sacrifice. Hobbes's absence from the character names signals the show's rejection of a war of all against all among the survivors, yet the finale's divine manipulation of the castaways, with Jacob treating people as means against Kantian autonomy, repudiates the liberal hope of a rational peace altogether.

state-of-nature.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
state-of-nature.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Reads John Teller's failed 'off the social grid' experiment through the human-nature debate: Mencius's seed of sympathy (even Tig recoils at Dante's dogfights) and Rousseau's naturally good man corrupted by society inspired J.T.'s Goldman-fed anarchism, while Mill and Xunzi counter that virtue is a victory over instinct. Hobbes supplies the real diagnosis—not innate violence but the logic of anarchy among free and equal rivals: competition (the Mayans blowing up the warehouse), diffidence (first-strike temptations against Zobelle), and glory (Jax unable to let the bike-sitting insult pass). Clay's rule that 'retaliation must be harsh and immediate' and the escalating Tig–Veronica Pope–Damon Pope–Opie bloodbath show deterrence fueling cycles of violence, so the only escape from the 'nasty, brutish, and short' fringe is the Leviathan's social grid.

state-of-nature.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: David Boersema reads Star Trek as a survey of peace studies, distinguishing negative peace from positive peace via 'The Cloud Minders', where Troglyte Vanna demands her people's 'right to the clouds' in Stratos. Against Anan 7's 'we're a killer species' in 'A Taste of Armageddon'—explicitly mirrored in post-9/11 drone war and 'shock and awe'—he enlists Hobbes, Freud, and McCoy's defense of the dark Kirk in 'The Enemy Within' to question whether violence is natural, and treats Kodos's 'some had to die that others might live' in 'The Conscience of the King' as the utilitarian justification for atrocity. Gem's compassion in 'The Empath', Kirk sparing the Gorn in 'Arena', and the Horta's misread attack in 'The Devil in the Dark' display nonviolence, deterrence, and corrected perception as alternatives to war.

state-of-nature.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Alkema and Barkman put Q himself on trial, asking what justifies his judgment of humanity in 'Encounter at Farpoint' and Trelane's of Kirk in 'The Squire of Gothos'. Hobbes's Leviathan would license Q's might-makes-right sovereignty over a savage species, but Q lacks humanity's consent and cannot show he acts for future peace; Locke's natural law instead binds even nearly omnipotent beings, as Janeway's asylum ruling for the suicidal Quinn in 'Death Wish' demonstrates. Q's repeated self-sacrifice—in 'Deja Q' and the Continuum's civil war—reveals a conscience answerable to natural law rather than raw power.

state-of-nature.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Reads Star Trek's "final frontier" through the European encounter with American Indians: the Hobbesian war-of-all-against-all stereotype of the "bloodthirsty savage" and Rousseau's opposing noble savage frame "The Paradise Syndrome", whose wigwam-and-tepee set mixes tribes into a no-place utopia. The chapter uses Hegel-style staged histories to debunk Star Trek's warp/pre-warp developmental scale (Spock on the Organians in "Errand of Mercy") as metaphysical assumption rather than biology, and counterposes the Prime Directive's noninterference to indigenous self-sovereignty and the Haudenosaunee-style consent governance that inspired the Federation. Chakotay's vision quests, the medicine bundle, Wesley's habak experience with Lakanta the Traveler in "Journey's End", and the Medicine Wheel in "Cathexis" are then interpreted through Jung's archetypes and collective unconscious, with Kirk, Spock, McCoy, and Scotty as the four Jungian modes of consciousness.

state-of-nature.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
state-of-nature.title: “Wherever I Go, He Goes”
state-of-nature.relation: Bishop and Bishop map The Mandalorian's Outer Rim onto a taxonomy of power: Nevarro's lawlessness is Hobbes's state of nature out of which sovereigns like Palpatine ('a safe and secure society') carve order by social contract, the Guild's codes and Djarin's creed exemplify Foucault's disciplinary power, and the Client's and Dr. Pershing's harvesting of Grogu's biology - like the Kaminoans' cloning of Jango Fett - is biopower. Against this 'binds of power' ontology they set Grogu's helpless generation of love, a 'little way' that converts Djarin, Omera, Cara Dune, and Greef Karga, and culminates in Djarin twice unhelmeting for Grogu's sake, proposing an ontology of love rather than power as the galaxy's alternative.

state-of-nature.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
state-of-nature.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Dena Hurst reads Heaven's civil war through Hobbes's Leviathan: with God absent there is no common power, so the angels fall into a state of nature that is a state of war, complete with natural equality, competition over the same prize, and glory-seeking, as when Zachariah's faction lets Lilith break the seals to force the Apocalypse. God ruled as sovereign by acquisition and proves 'a lousy king' not for demanding obedience but by vanishing without designating a successor, dissolving civil society and with it justice, since where there is no law there is no injustice. Meanwhile Hell under Crowley and the leviathans under Dick Roman display Hobbesian legitimacy from opposite directions: demons join by covenant-like contracts, making Hell a rough democracy, while the leviathans' unified hierarchy enacts the Leviathan itself.

state-of-nature.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Weisberg challenges the premise that a newly self-aware Skynet must exterminate humanity in rational self-preservation: after Turing's 'Heads in the Sand Objection,' he argues self-awareness does not entail a survival instinct - a Camusian Skynet might judge existence pointless and pull its own plug. Recasting 'in a panic, they try to pull the plug' as a Hobbesian slide into the state of nature, he uses the iterated prisoner's dilemma and Axelrod's tit-for-tat-with-forgiveness (as in WarGames) to argue a rational Skynet should cooperate with humans toward an emergent social contract. The dark twist is Humean: because reason is the slave of our passions, unconscious anti-machine stereotypes (Bargh's priming studies) make humans untrustworthy partners, so the whole war might have been avoided if only we were more machine-like.

state-of-nature.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Peter Fosl asks what John Connor should do when the radio call comes from Crystal Peak — accept near-certain death leading the resistance or stay silent — and dismantles the easy answers: John is not the indispensable savior (Kate or the caller from Montana could lead), the flag-waving finale undercuts any claim that humanity deserves saving, and collective responsibility for Judgment Day is unjust. Social contract fails because Brewster's button-press dissolved the contract and returned humanity to Hobbes's and Locke's state of nature, Hume shows contracts cannot ground society, and utilitarianism wavers once the happiness of animals and possible-happy machines is counted. The positive argument extends Wittgenstein's private-language argument (via Stanley Cavell): meaningful existence is inescapably social and moral, so refusing the claims of others would be as self-subverting as a solipsist arguing in language, and John must answer the call to remain human at all.

state-of-nature.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Jason Walker pits Hobbes against Locke over whether Andrea may take the mermaid necklace when Rick says 'I don't think those rules apply anymore'. He reads the survivors' conduct—Andrea's single necklace under Locke's spoilage proviso, Morgan squatting in and fixing up the neighbors' house, Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo—as a Lockean state of nature where self-ownership and property rights persist without government, while Chris's cannibal band and the Governor embody the Hobbesian war of all against all, treating persons as mere means. The Lockean right to punish, exercised brutally by Grimes's group on Chris's hunters, vindicates rights even by Hobbes's own demand for enforcement.

state-of-nature.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Si Sheppard reads the comic through Realist state-formation theory: Shane's leadership rests on borrowed prestige and dies with him, West Central Prison collapses into anarchy because Rick never establishes a monopoly on legitimate force—letting Tyreese's vigilante murder pass—nor any institution beyond his personal authority, while the Governor's Woodbury thrives on fear, arenas, and bread-and-circuses. Citing Machiavelli's prince who is feared rather than loved, Weber's definition of the state, and Bismarck's unifying wars, he argues the prison loses the 'second anarchy' rivalry with Woodbury for want of scouting, sabotage, coalition-building, or any command structure that survives Rick's absences. Rick's confession that he would kill everyone in the Alexandria Safe Zone to keep Lori safe is post-moral Realism, yet he was 'a bad founding father' who only finally learns to build an army instead of relying on himself.

state-of-nature.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
state-of-nature.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
state-of-nature.relation: Moosa treats Kirkman's world as a moral laboratory: the apocalypse approximates Hobbes's state of nature ('solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'), yet Rick's search for his family shows survivors import morality into it, and Carl's killing of Shane is judged by reasoning rather than the act of killing itself. Taking Camus's claim that suicide is the only serious philosophical problem, the chapter argues the survivors' best justification for continuing is reducing others' suffering, and consistency then imposes the same duty on comfortable readers to help real-world sufferers rather than reserving aid for photogenic disasters. It concludes that Glenn and Maggie's wish to conceive at the prison is the worst thing survivors can do, since non-existent children cannot suffer while existing orphans (like the children Andrea and Dale adopted) have prior moral claims, an argument that applies to couples in our world too.

state-of-nature.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Christensen and Holmes read the Third Age as Hobbes's state of nature, a postlapsarian chaos following the Breaking where Lews Therin's prideful attempt at purified sovereignty destroyed the Leviathan of the Age of Legends. They argue channeling the One Power is morally neutral power that only becomes sovereignty through practice, and that the Aes Sedai model Hobbesian order through their seven Ajah and, above all, the Three Oaths. Drawing heavily on Giorgio Agamben's Homo Sacer and The Sacrament of Language, they treat oaths and curses as the 'sacraments of power' founding sovereignty on the trustworthiness of the logos, using Moiraine's New Spring investiture to show how language itself binds and confers authority.

state-of-nature.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
state-of-nature.title: Notes
state-of-nature.relation: Knepp reads the Paul Dini/Alex Ross 'Origin of Wonder Woman' as Hegel's three-stage philosophy of history in miniature: the Amazons begin in a Hobbesian war of all against all, negate it by retreating to Themyscira where only some are free, and Diana's disguised contest win supplies the second negation that carries Amazon ideals to all people - celebrated by the splash of red, white, and blue. He then traces the WWII stakes: Hegel tied history's culmination to German unification, German-American Hegelians transplanted the classical-freedom story to America, and Marston - ex-assistant to the anti-feminist German psychologist Munsterberg - turned the lie detector into the lasso, reclaiming truth-telling from misogynist German science for a feminist America fighting Hitler.

state-of-nature.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
state-of-nature.title: What Would Machiavelli Do
state-of-nature.relation: Reitsma treats the refereeless pickup game as a Lockean state of nature and asks how to beat the 'strategic ticky-tacker' who calls phantom fouls to win. He condemns first-strike cheating as wrong on Kantian grounds (the cheat 'makes an exception of himself') and by an ideal of Homeric athletic honor, then asks whether retaliatory ticky-tacking is justified. Reading Machiavelli's 'dirty hands' argument alongside Locke's claim that in a state of nature each person may punish transgressors, he concludes proportionate tit-for-tat cheating can make one a legitimate 'agent of justice' when no referee exists.

state-of-nature.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
state-of-nature.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
state-of-nature.relation: Woolfolk reads The Last of the Mohicans as staging a conflict between nature and civilization. The opening hunt is neither Hobbes's brutish state of nature nor quite Rousseau's amoral noble savage, since the Mohicans are full moral agents; Woolfolk uses Locke's Second Treatise to cast Hawkeye and the colonists as enforcing natural law and natural rights against English 'tyranny,' with Chingachgook's killing of Magua a justified execution. Rousseau's First and Second Discourses illuminate the hypocrisy and greed of Montcalm and the Europeans, and Camus's Meursault is invoked as a truer image of amoral natural man; Tocqueville frames Cora's democratic awakening as individualism.

state-of-nature.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
state-of-nature.title: John Drake in Greeneland: Noir Themes in Secret Agent
state-of-nature.relation: Lee argues that Secret Agent belongs to the Graham Greene noir tradition of The Ministry of Fear and The Third Man, not Bond escapism: Drake never kills, carries no gun, and refuses romantic entanglement, because McGoohan prized realism and ethical seriousness. Readings of Greene's Stephen Neale (who killed his wife out of pity) and Harry Lime's Ferris-wheel nihilism establish a world 'void of meaning, haphazard, and morally indifferent,' which Drake's episodes then dramatize: in 'It's Up to the Lady' his superior Hobbs (named, Lee contends, for Thomas Hobbes, whose Leviathan and war of all against all the essay explicates) betrays Drake's promised word and has the defector Charles arrested; in 'That's Two of Us Sorry' Drake unwittingly plays the villain, ruining an innocent Scottish village; in 'Judgement Day' he cannot say what justice for the Nazi scientist Garriga requires. Lee concludes that Drake, like Neale and Martins, acts in Sartrean bad faith by continuing to serve morally bankrupt masters, and that Greene's only exits are a Kierkegaardian leap of faith Drake never makes, or fantasized retirement and death.

state-of-nature.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
state-of-nature.title: Kingdom of Darkness: Autonomy and Conspiracy in The X-Files and Millennium
state-of-nature.relation: Michael Valdez Moses reads The X-Files and Millennium as post-Cold War noir that depicts America as Foucault's carceral archipelago: nearly every character works for the state, Tocquevillian voluntary association has withered ('they don't go bowling at all'), and the FBI's landscape of prisons, clinics, and bases makes free space scarce. Against Hobbes's Leviathan, the chapter mobilizes Locke and Paine's classical liberalism (government as necessary evil securing pre-existing natural rights) to show that Carter's heroes are 'antipolitical' resisters: Frank Black's visions and the Grill Flame remote viewers make him a panoptical spy for the state, while Mulder's warrantless searches blur sovereign and criminal justice into one corrupt system, as in the Millennium episode 'The Judge'. The neo-noir conspiracy seeks not profit but absolute sovereignty, and the series end with Mulder, Scully, and Black as fugitives fleeing the state with their families, resisting Nietzsche's 'coldest of all cold monsters'.

state-of-nature.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
state-of-nature.title: The Power of Memory and the Memory of Power Wars and Graves in Westerns and Jidaigeki
state-of-nature.relation: Brodey compares John Ford's Westerns (My Darling Clementine, She Wore a Yellow Ribbon, The Searchers, The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance) with Kurosawa's jidaigeki (Seven Samurai, Throne of Blood, Hidden Fortress, Yôjimbô) as postwar mythmaking that both buries and builds national identity after military defeat. She argues graves and gravestones are bivalent symbols—commemorating loss while risking perpetuating revenge—and that both directors oscillate between Rousseauean nostalgia for a nobler past and Hobbesian frontier brutality that must be tamed. Ford trusts that memory of past wrongs can spur a better future and enable forgiveness, while Kurosawa, more pessimistic and drawing on Buddhist cyclical detachment in Throne of Blood, warns of the dangers of both remembering and forgetting trauma.

state-of-nature.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
state-of-nature.title: Two Ways to Yuma Locke, Liberalism, and Western Masculinity in 3 10 to Yuma
state-of-nature.relation: Mexal reads both versions of 3:10 to Yuma through Locke's classical liberalism, arguing the western hero descends from Locke's autonomous, property-owning self in a 'state of nature' (contrasted with Hobbes's state of war). In the 1957 film, Dan Evans transforms from atomistic self-interest to a masculine civic republicanism, escorting Ben Wade to the train even after being released from his contract, reflecting Cold War anxieties. In the 2007 remake, Dan instead renegotiates his contract for water rights and money, so western masculinity becomes unyielding Lockean individualism and the 'right to get rich' in a post-Cold War, capitalist-triumphant America.

state-of-nature.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
state-of-nature.title: “Order Out of the Mud” Deadwood and the State of Nature
state-of-nature.relation: Cantor reads David Milch's Deadwood as a dramatization of 'order without law,' testing the mining camp against the state-of-nature theories of Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau. Deadwood is Hobbesian in its sources of violence (competition, diffidence, glory; Al Swearengen's alpha-male struggles), but Lockean in showing property rights and commerce arising spontaneously before the state—gold becomes a self-generated medium of exchange that even overrides prejudice (Hearst dealing with Odell). It is Rousseauian in its innate pity (Swearengen's mercy) and its skepticism that incorporation into the nation-state, symbolized by the telegraph and Hearst's abstract corporate power, counts as progress.

state-of-nature.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
state-of-nature.title: Order without Law The Magnificent Seven, East and West
state-of-nature.relation: Skoble compares The Magnificent Seven with Kurosawa's Seven Samurai, arguing the farming villages are not Hobbesian anarchies needing a sovereign but Lockean communities with a 'grown' social order that merely lack reliable enforcement against bandits. Using Hayek's distinction between spontaneous order (kosmos) and planned order (taxis), he shows the farmers legitimately hire gunslingers/ronin for self-protection rather than surrendering to private-justice worries. The warriors' willingness to honor an unenforceable contract ('That's just the kind you've got to keep') is grounded in a self-created ethics linking the Bushido/Zen and existentialist idea that one's honor and selfhood consist in one's actions.

state-of-nature.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
state-of-nature.title: Savage Nations Native Americans and the Western
state-of-nature.relation: Michael Valdez Moses uses Todorov's analysis of Columbus and Las Casas—the failure to grant the Other both equality and difference—to argue that Hollywood's Native Americans, whether demonized or idealized, are egocentric projections of white American concerns. He traces the 'noble savage' from Rousseau's Second Discourse and Ferguson's proto-republican warrior through Ford's Fort Apache (New Deal common man), the 1970s revisionist westerns (Little Big Man, A Man Called Horse) as countercultural Rousseauian dropouts and Vietnam allegory, and Dances with Wolves, culminating in Jarmusch's Dead Man, whose Nobody escapes the collective stereotype to stand as a genuinely individual, cosmopolitan character.

state-of-nature.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
state-of-nature.title: Human Rights, Human Nature, and Amistad
state-of-nature.relation: Baggett and Foreman use Amistad to reconstruct Locke's theory of natural rights: Cinque's mutiny and John Quincy Adams's Supreme Court plea that man's natural state is freedom illustrate Locke's claim that God's workmanship makes us his property and therefore un-ownable by other men. They contrast Locke's voluntarist natural law with Aquinas's, note Adams rebutting the Hobbesian 'war of all against all' quoted in the pro-slavery Executive Review, and invoke Mill's perfect/imperfect duty distinction (Baldwin's obligation to his clients) plus Bentham's rights-denying utilitarianism, which they map onto Calhoun's warning about the cost of abolition.

state-of-nature.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: This Is the Age of Steel
state-of-nature.relation: Greg Littmann asks how a truly "logical" creature would live by redesigning the Cybermen through three philosophers. Hobbes's reason-as-self-interest and Laws of Nature would make Cybermen seek peace and security once survival is assured, not wage endless war; Mill's utilitarianism would build happy, individualistic, liberty-respecting Cybermen who prize higher pleasures and others' welfare rather than forced "upgrades"; and Hume's view that reason alone motivates nothing implies emotionless Cybermen would simply do nothing, so their goals are neither logical nor illogical. Each shows the Cybermen's actual "logic" is incoherent.

state-of-nature.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: The Dalek Within
state-of-nature.relation: Ed Webb and Mark Wardecker contrast the Fourth Doctor's refusal to abort the Daleks in "Genesis of the Daleks" with his half-human self's genocide in "Journey's End" to ask whether a genocidal species should be exterminated. Reading Daleks as Nazis and Hobbesian survivalists in a lawless state of nature, they argue their real horror is Arendt's banality of evil, bureaucratic order-following, and that Foucault's disciplinary institutions and the Frankfurt School's culture industry show humans can be "made" Dalek-like. Their moral: we must not exterminate the Dalek but guard against the Dalek within, since it took the Doctor's added humanity to commit the genocide.

state-of-nature.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
state-of-nature.title: 5. The Sovereign State of Salamanca
state-of-nature.relation: Barta and Barnes read the show's Court and Cartel as parallel Hobbesian sovereigns. The New Mexico desert and the criminalized drug trade function as Hobbes's state of nature—lawless, where Nacho robs thieves who 'have no recourse' and Mike sticks up a mule with a garden hose—illustrating natural equality (a small man can kill a big one) and the war of all against all. From mutual fear, deals emerge (Mike and Gus's desert standoff, Mike keeping his word over twenty dollars), but 'covenants without the sword' need a Common Power: Tuco, Hector, Lalo, and ultimately Don Eladio form a feudal hierarchy enforcing loyalty by terror, just as the state's police monopoly on force sustains the Law.

state-of-nature.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
state-of-nature.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
state-of-nature.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors of Lost as a real state of nature, playing on the characters named Locke, Rousseau, and Hume. The scarce-water and asthma-inhaler disputes are 'tragedies of the commons,' and Sawyer's 'finders keepers' embodies a Hobbesian 'Trust No. 1' while Hurley and Jack lean toward Rousseauian 'Innocence.' Using game theory's repeated prisoners' dilemma and 'tit-for-tat,' Davies argues a Lockean state of nature (opening with cooperation) rather than a doomed Hobbesian one lets the survivors build a commonwealth against the Others.

state-of-nature.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Richard Davies analyzes the post-crash survivors as living in a genuine 'state of nature' and grades its severity by how scarce the contested good is (the water shortage as a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers versus Sawyer's 'possession is nine-tenths'). He compares Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau on human nature — labeling the poles 'Innocence' (Hurley, Rousseau, Hume) and 'Trust No 1' (Sawyer, Hobbes) — and uses the repeated prisoners' dilemma and the tit-for-tat strategy to argue that the castaways build a Lockean civil society by signaling through shared language and cooperating first, while the discovery of the Others (Ethan) triggers Hobbesian non-cooperation.

state-of-nature.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
state-of-nature.title: NOTES
state-of-nature.relation: Peter S. Fosl argues that Lost pretends to a liberal social order — Jack rising by consent in a Lockean scheme of natural rights, Rousseau's general will ('live together, die alone'), and Hume's sympathy and pity binding the survivors — but that its treatment of the Others betrays a darker politics. Reading the survivor/Other conflict through Carl Schmitt's friend-enemy thesis (notably absent Hobbes), he contends the show, like post-9/11 America, needs an enemy to exterminate, and that the finale's Jacob/Man-in-Black war and Jack's Christlike sacrificial death repudiate the Kantian liberal ideal of persons as ends, resolving conflict through Schmittian and Christian redemptive violence instead.

state-of-nature.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
state-of-nature.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
state-of-nature.relation: Lee reads Gustave Courbet's life-size painting The Quarry (La curée) alongside Daumier's caricatures of incompetent bourgeois Parisian 'hobby hunters' and contemporary works by John Byrd and Christopher Carroll to trace how the hunter became a swaggering, masculine, lower-class 'savage' figure mediating wildness and civilization. She shows how the aristocratic ritual of the curée (feeding the deer's parts to the hounds) inverts into bourgeois provisioning, and invokes Hobbes's 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' to gloss Byrd's Tricky Buck as defiance of urban squeamishness about the mammalian, gendered reality of hunting.

state-of-nature.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
state-of-nature.title: Hobbes, Human Nature, and the Culture of American Violence in Truman Capote's In Cold Blood
state-of-nature.relation: Thomas Fahy reads Capote's In Cold Blood as horror (the Clutter killers Hickock and Smith as 'realistic monsters' whose human shape terrifies because anyone could be like them) and maps it onto Hobbes's Leviathan. Hickock and Smith act in a Hobbesian state of nature, driven by appetite, power, and moral relativism without remorse. Herb Clutter functions as a Hobbesian sovereign whose Eden-like farm and community collapse into decay, mistrust, and 'war of all against all' after his murder. Fahy also casts Capote himself as a sovereign who, via Foucault's panopticon, imposes a fictionalized cathartic ending, though the book's Hobbesian message is that we all have the potential to kill.

state-of-nature.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
state-of-nature.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
state-of-nature.relation: Davies analyzes Lost's Oceanic 815 survivors as a genuine state of nature, playing off the characters named Locke, Rousseau, and Hume. He distinguishes Rousseau's compassionate "Innocence" from a Hobbesian "Trust No. 1" (Sawyer hoarding), tracks "tragedies of the commons" over water and Shannon's inhalers, and Jack and Sayid's move toward Lockean punishment and civil society. Using game theory's prisoners' dilemma and tit-for-tat, he argues cooperation emerges when survivors, discovering the Others, resolve to "act as one body" and form a commonwealth.

state-of-nature.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: 5. Battlestar Galactica as Philosophy Breaking the Biopolitical Cycle
state-of-nature.relation: Eberl and Bishop read the reimagined Battlestar Galactica and Caprica through the biopolitics of Foucault and Agamben, tracing 'biopower' across four phases from Zoe Graystone's avatar to the arrival at Earth. They argue the show asks whether artificial Cylons are persons (Zoe's avatar exhibits Baker's first-person perspective and Buber's I-Thou recognition), and use Agamben's zoe/bios/'bare life' and Homo sacer plus Roslin's population control and abortion ban to show sovereign power over life. The Cylon occupation of New Caprica is read through Arendt's three stages of totalitarian dehumanization, and Lee Adama's plea to 'break the cycle' offers a fragile hope undercut by the finale's flash-forward to present-day robotics, showing humanity forgetting the lesson.

state-of-nature.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: 6. Black Sails as Philosophy Pirates and Political Discourse
state-of-nature.relation: Jones argues that Starz's Black Sails, a Treasure Island prequel set in the Golden Age of Piracy, dramatizes social contract theory as non-hypothetical practice. Captain Flint's drive to make Nassau a sovereign pirate commonwealth ('I am your king') channels Hobbes's state of nature and irrepressible sovereign, while his choice to settle Nassau and belief that people can thrive if left free channels Locke; his eventual plan to install Silver and Madi as liked-and-feared leaders synthesizes the two. Jones maps the pirates' familial bonds onto Rousseau and their responses to injustice (Vane's gallows speech, the maroon alliance) onto Rawls's Veil of Ignorance, and reads pirate 'articles' and deposable captains as radical democracy and equality, complicated by manipulation, slavery, and tolerance.

state-of-nature.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: 12. Firefly as Philosophy Social Contracts, Political Dissent, and Virtuous Communities
state-of-nature.relation: Kowalski argues that Firefly and Serenity embody a distinctive political theory he calls 'Since I Found Serenity' (SIFS). The mindless, savage Reavers represent Hobbes's state of nature, showing government is necessary; but the Alliance's torture of River, the Miranda/Pax atrocity, and the murderous blue-gloved agents and Operative make a Hobbesian reading untenable and vindicate Locke's natural rights and right of revolution — Mal's 'I aim to misbehave' broadcast of the Miranda file is Lockean civil disobedience. He then presses the tacit-consent problem (the Browncoats cannot leave the 'Verse) and supplements Locke with Aristotle's friendship and community: Serenity's crew becomes a virtuous mobile commonwealth where friendship (Simon forgiving Jayne, Mal's 'love keeps her in the air') turns a commonwealth into a good-life community.

state-of-nature.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: 24. Game of Thrones as Philosophy Cynical Realpolitiks
state-of-nature.relation: The chapter argues that Game of Thrones advances a thoroughgoing cynicism about political legitimacy, captured by Varys's riddle that 'power resides where men believe it resides.' It documents the dubious claims of Robert 'the Usurper' and the pyromaniacal Daenerys, the barbaric Lockean 'state of nature' among the Wildlings, and the false ideals of chivalry and religion, with Littlefinger and Varys voicing Machiavellian realpolitik. Silverman and Riordan then offer two views the show never considers: Locke's social-contract theory of natural rights (which would justify deposing Aerys or Daenerys) and Aquinas's four-part test for genuine law (reason, common good, proper authority, promulgation), arguing a legitimate state remains possible against the show's cynicism.

state-of-nature.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
state-of-nature.title: 92. V for Vendetta as Philosophy Victory Through the Virtues of Anarchy
state-of-nature.relation: Nisley argues that Moore and Lloyd's V for Vendetta justifies V's violent rebellion against the Norsefire regime through Locke: the fascist state seized power without consent, tortured and experimented on citizens (V at Larkhill), and violated natural rights, thereby placing itself in a state of war so the people may overthrow it. Using Aristotle on deviant constitutions and the beast-like tyrant (Adam Susan) who lacks practical wisdom, and contrasting Locke's tolerable state of nature with Hobbes's brutal one, the chapter concludes the citizens should rebuild a rights-protecting social contract rather than V's leaderless anarchy, and maps the argument onto real-world 2020 events (BLM riots vs. the Whitmer kidnapping plot).

black-skin-white-masks.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
black-skin-white-masks.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
