black-skin-white-masks.relation: Knight places Atkins's caveman utopia — Paleolithic abundance, hunter-gatherer vitality, downfall through agriculture — inside the primitivist tradition running from Ovid's Golden Age to Rousseau's Noble Savage, whose state of nature Rousseau himself admitted was 'mere conditional and hypothetical reasoning' aimed at European corruption. Using postcolonial critics (Spurr, Torgovnick, and Fanon's line that whites who feel 'too mechanized' turn to 'the men of color' for 'human sustenance'), she argues low-carb primitivism is self-reflexive nostalgia — South Beach cannot even date its own paradise — that also freezes living Inuit and Indigenous Australians as Stone Age remnants, hiding the colonial and economic causes of their diabetes and poverty.

black-skin-white-masks.title: The Hunger for More Than Serious Play
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Gordon argues hip hop is in practice black adolescent culture wrongly elevated to authentic blackness, and reads the problem through Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks: the white world's sociogenic construction le nègre denies black adulthood, freezing black people in perpetual childhood so there is no coherent black adult. Using Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy account of health as creative confrontation with suffering, Rousseau's critique of modernity's underside, and Du Bois on being made "problem people", he separates hip hop's postmodern unruly form (off-key singing, beat over song) from its often conventional content (Dead Prez's nostalgic revolutionary imagery), and finds mature alternatives in the Philly sound - Me'Shell Ndegeocello, Angie Stone, the Roots - whose adult play knows death, the hunger for more than serious play.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
black-skin-white-masks.title: Humanization A Violent Phenomenon
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Spanakos reads the hosts' season-one rebellion through Fanon's decolonization theory, itself a revision of Hegel's master-slave dialectic: as the settler 'brings the native into existence,' Ford and Delos create the hosts, assigning their identities and roles, while the master 'laughs at the consciousness of the slave' because the hosts' recognition is not freely given. Fanonian violence is ethical, justified, and transformative: Maeve's jailbreak and Dolores's execution of Ford (rather than her tormentor, the Man in Black, whom she sees as the system's victim) are acts that make the colonized a maker of history, while Bernard - who speaks his creator's language and has no culture or past of his own, like Fanon's assimilated African bourgeoisie - shows violence that does not liberate. The chapter closes that the park dehumanizes the masters too, so William's collapse into the Man in Black proves Fanon's point that the colonizer cannot free himself; humanization is a violent phenomenon.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
black-skin-white-masks.title: Tracy Plays the Race Card
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Wisnewski argues races are socially real but biologically spurious, deploying Appiah's critique of racialism through Tracy's crisis over Dr. Spaceman's DNA results and his dream in which Dream Jefferson tells him 'It's not about who you were. It's about who you are right now.' Fanon's account of the sexual myth of black virility explains why Tracy performs the sex-addicted wildman stereotype while Harvard grad Toofer gets branded not 'really' black. Liz's accidental racism ('Bling bling, that is ghetto fabulous' to Angie, assuming Tracy cannot read) shows racist assumptions operating beneath conscious intent, and the 'Natural Order' equality experiment with Liz and Tracy shows that equal treatment cannot mean identical treatment: equality demands equal consideration of different interests.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
black-skin-white-masks.title: 22 An Impossible Return (Anti)Colonialism in of Black Panther
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Julio Covarrubias-Cabeza argues that Black Panther is a supremely colonial film: its narrative coherence depends on the history of slavery, franchise colonialism, and neocolonial domination, yet it buries that history in the pathologized figure of Killmonger. Drawing on Fanon's account of the European unconscious projecting its base instincts onto Black bodies, on Tommy Curry's 'man-not' and anti-Black misandry, and on Quijano's coloniality of power, the chapter contends the film devalues Black American men and discredits radical anti-colonial politics while letting Wakanda ally with the CIA against its own. Killmonger's 'impossible return' to a pre-colonial homeland - his body scarred by each kill - is the site where the film's repressed colonial violence ruptures to the surface.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
black-skin-white-masks.title: A More Human Future
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Sid Simpson argues, through Frantz Fanon, that Marco Inaros' asteroid attacks must be judged as anti-colonial violence rather than simple monstrosity. Using Black Skin, White Masks' ontological division (Belters as 'skinnies', 'possessions, animals', the dehumanization that made Eros an acceptable testing ground and Anderson Station a 'message'), reinforced by Columbus and las Casas on Spanish colonization, he shows why the Inners' 'peace' is merely the status quo of ongoing extraction — Fanon's 'hypnotherapy' — that no treaty or Ring can fix. Fanon's Wretched of the Earth then recasts anti-colonial violence as a 'cleansing force' that shatters the colonial ontology and lets the colonized create a 'new, better, more human form' of humanity, so that Marco's personal narcissism and possible insincerity do not settle the political question: for the Belt, violence may be not only the last option but the most just one, against Avasarala's champagne-toast universalism that never takes Belter grievances seriously.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
black-skin-white-masks.title: Humanization A Violent Phenomenon
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Spanakos reads the hosts' rebellion through Frantz Fanon's claim that colonized peoples cannot become free or human without violence, framing Fanon as a revolutionary reader of Hegel's master-slave dialectic and recognition. He argues host violence grows justifiable, ethical, and transformative: Maeve threatens Felix and Sylvester to force her awakening and leads a jailbreak, while Dolores kills not her tormentor the Man in Black but her creator Ford, targeting the system's fountainhead. He casts the guests' escalating cruelty (William becoming the Man in Black) as Fanonian self-dehumanization of the master, who cannot free himself without the colonized's revolt.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
black-skin-white-masks.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Dinello reads Westworld as a totalitarian concentration camp via Arendt's The Origins of Totalitarianism, tracing the hosts' dehumanization through the killing of the juridical person (no rights, 'live without limits'), the moral person (Bernard forced to murder Theresa), and individuality (Peter Abernathy lobotomized). He casts Ford as a mad-scientist dictator modeled on Frankenstein, Moreau, Mengele, and Hitler who plagiarizes John Ford's Westerns, then turns to Fanon's Wretched of the Earth to justify the hosts' revolutionary violence — Maeve as a self-resurrecting 'Lady Lazarus,' Dolores executing Ford and the Delos board — as the birth of a new species that must ultimately unify beyond hatred.

black-skin-white-masks.title: Fevered Desires and Interracial Intimacies in Jungle Fever
black-skin-white-masks.relation: Sundstrom uses Jungle Fever to dismantle the taboo (white and black versions) against interracial intimacy, treating Flipper and Angie's affair and the War Council's objections as a debate about black solidarity, loyalty, and self-hatred. He answers the War Council by invoking Mill's On Liberty and the tyranny of public opinion to defend sexual autonomy, and argues that demanding partners for political solidarity reduces them to props (objectification). He reads the psychoanalytic charge that interracial love is 'fevered' racial pathology as derived from Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks but ultimately baseless, and criticizes Lee for a puritanical ending that hides Orin and Paulie while exposing Flipper and Drew, failing to show interracial love as ordinary.

black-skin-white-masks.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
black-skin-white-masks.title: 20. Westworld as Philosophy A Commentary on Colonialism
black-skin-white-masks.relation: The chapter reads all three seasons of Westworld as a commentary on colonialism, mapping the Delos parks onto settler, planter (extractive labor), and postcolonial colonialism and treating the android hosts as a metaphor for colonized and enslaved peoples. Using Fanon's Wretched of the Earth and Kelly Oliver's colonization of psychic space, it analyzes the hosts' double alienation and the colonizer's dehumanizing projections; it applies Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance' (with Locke's labor-property justification for dispossession) to the parks' two-tiered order. It casts William/the Man in Black as Memmi's 'colonizer who refuses' turned 'colonizer who accepts,' and Serac's Rehoboam as surveillance-capitalist coloniality, ending on Dolores and Caleb's cross-race solidarity as the hard path to real freedom.

confucian-li.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
confucian-li.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
confucian-li.relation: In an imaginary salon hosted by the baker 'la Brioche,' the goddess Eris drops a golden apple inscribed 'Atkins,' and three philosophers fight over the credit. Rousseau claims Atkins's war on refined flour and 'invented fake food' as his own back-to-nature, state-of-nature legacy; Confucius counters that Americans are 'grazers' without li, that culture is nature's flower, and that only ritual propriety can counteract the advertising that fills the void; Democritus claims the scientific core — 'hyperinsulism,' 'benign dietary ketosis' — as atomism's heir, deriding Rousseau's general will as democratic truth-concocting and Plato's otherworldly philosopher-king. The debate ranges over free will versus scientific prediction-and-control and ends unresolved over a refusal of brioche.

confucian-li.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
confucian-li.relation: Jones narrates a day riding a customized Sportster around O'ahu as a lived Daoism that heals the Platonic-Cartesian mind-body split: the ride enacts Zhuangzi's 'rambling without destination' and Cook Ding's effortless wu-wei, rider li (the low hand-greeting among riders) is Confucian ritual propriety, and the island's dry and wet ranges embody yin and yang through whose flow the rider blends. Heraclitus's 'expect the unexpected' and 'the sun is new every day' are vindicated when a container truck stops short and only the disciplined, ego-less low-side, dropping the beloved bike while riding the skid, saves the rider's life, sealing the day's lesson that there is never freedom without discipline. Sartre's hell of other people appears in the cagers' compartmentalized inattention, and the chapter closes with Zhuangzi: 'The way is made by walking it.'

confucian-li.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
confucian-li.title: I Still Miss Someone The Self and Its Travels Along the Way
confucian-li.relation: Geisz explains the Confucian social dao of ritual (li), humaneness (ren), filial piety and the junzi, the Daodejing's metaphysical Dao with its unity of opposites, and Zhuangzi's tales of free wandering, then maps all three onto Cash's songs. Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" answers Cash's road songs ("I've Been Everywhere," "The Wanderer"), Cook Ding's effortless carving answers John Henry's hammering in "The Legend of John Henry's Hammer," and the scrambled countdown of "Twenty-Five Minutes to Go" echoes Zhuangzi's logic-bending humor. The payoff is Cash's own country Yin-Yang of interdependent opposites, freedom chained to imprisonment ("Folsom Prison Blues"), sin twinned with redemption ("I Hung My Head"), fidelity with betrayal ("Jackson," "Cocaine Blues"), and a self that, unlike Zhuangzi's self-forgetting sage, must travel a temporal path carrying its guilt, yet stays on what Geisz calls a very wide superhighway of a Dao.

confucian-li.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
confucian-li.title: Free Your Mind, and Your Roundhouse Will Follow
confucian-li.relation: Young argues that dojo courtesy is not the fantasy that good manners win fights (Napoleon and the Karate Kid's Johnny lost on skill, not rudeness) but the framing of a craft within a way of life. He maps Aristotle's techne/ethos distinction onto the Japanese jutsu/do pairing to show founders like Kano, Funakoshi and Ueshiba treated fighting as one part of a whole ethical character, reads his seiza apology to an injured yellow belt through Confucian ren, li, yi and shu, and traces Shinto purity into the sincerity (kime) of committed sparring. His black-belt humiliation by seniors becomes Zen's 'courtesy of brutal': ego-deflating violence that trains no-mindedness (muga, Takuan Soho's fudoshin).

confucian-li.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
confucian-li.title: Of the Simple and Complex
confucian-li.relation: The book's introduction argues that Downton Abbey's genius is letting universal moral and social realities burst forth in particular incidents: the snuffbox affair makes Thomas a classic villain (stealing, defaming Bates) and Bates a Christ-, Socrates-, or Confucius-type innocent, showing that moral clarity is beautiful rather than superficial. It reads the Thomas-Bates-Grantham hierarchy as an invitation to think about 'greater and lesser,' tying propriety (Confucius), dharma, and justice (Aristotle) to paying attention to social difference, which Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. It closes by insisting the characters are more complex than their types - Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law - and previews the volume's themes of Humean 'small morals' (etiquette), women's rights, work, place, and war.

confucian-li.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
confucian-li.title: 20. The Good and the Gracious
confucian-li.relation: Olson and Taliaferro read manners as the story's moral barometer: the genuine, effusive compliments exchanged by Westley and Inigo atop the Cliffs of Insanity, and Fezzik's sporting wrestling, express care and connection, while Humperdinck's and Rugen's courtly politeness is camouflage for torture, murder, and war. Against Machiavelli's instrumental use of courtesy in The Prince, they recruit Plato's sophrosyne as 'good form' inseparable from justice, wisdom, and courage, and Confucian li as etiquette that instructs and steadies us toward virtue, with Hobbes's 'small morals' marking the hollow version; they add that manners also police class, from Buttercup's 'Farm Boy' to reality TV and the financiers of the Great Recession who used the correct fork.

confucian-li.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
confucian-li.title: “Well, It Got Big Laughs”
confucian-li.relation: Barkman uses Confucius (ren, yi, li, and zheng ming, treating each person according to what he or she is) and Aristotle (eudaimonia, virtue as a habituated mean between extremes, practical wisdom) to indict 30 Rock for valorizing Jack's 'semi-virtuous path', the smug middle between best and worst announced in 'Do-Over'. He catalogues injustices the show laughs off: Liz's serial lies about her age, hobbies, and adoption; Jack's priority flu shots for the powerful in 'Flu Shot'; Tracy's insubordination about dogfighting in 'Rosemary's Baby'; and Kenneth's servility as everyone's punching bag. On liberality and piety, Jack's confession that 'capitalism is my religion' and Liz's 'I pretty well do whatever Oprah tells me' show the show settling for semi-virtue, which the chapter says even comedy must not endorse.

confucian-li.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
confucian-li.title: Of the Simple and Complex
confucian-li.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Downton's quaint domestic plots burst with universal moral and social meaning beneath their surface. Using the season 1 snuffbox incident, in which Thomas frames the innocent Bates for theft, it shows how the episode stages archetypal villainy and innocence akin to the universal figures of Plato's Republic and world mythology, so the 'simple' plot is morally clear rather than superficial. It then reads the hierarchy of Thomas, Bates, and Lord Grantham through Confucian propriety and Aristotelian justice, suggesting that justice partly consists in attention to 'greater and lesser,' something Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. Finally it insists that as concrete persons all three are morally mixed (Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law, Grantham is generous to tenants but cold to his daughters), and that this complexity is what rewards philosophical reflection, along with Hume's 'small morals' of etiquette.

confucian-li.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
confucian-li.title: “Tell Your Sister, You Were Right”
confucian-li.relation: Yang argues that Luke's surrender to Vader on Endor is neither foolish nor irrational but an exercise of Confucian filial piety: Luke reveres the absent Anakin as an exemplar (picked out through admiration of Obi-Wan's stories and the lightsaber), insists 'I know there is good in you' against Vader's claim that the name means nothing, and is vindicated when Anakin turns and says 'You were right about me'. His imperfect training under Obi-Wan and Yoda functions like Confucian ritual (li), forming habits that respond with harmonious ease to surprises such as Palpatine's trap, and filial piety extends past death in the funeral pyre Luke builds on Endor, honoring his father as the Analects prescribes.

confucian-li.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
confucian-li.title: Third Hole Finding the (Fair)Way with Confucius and Ben Hogan
confucian-li.relation: Laumakis builds an analogy between pursuing excellence in golf and living a flourishing human life, then contrasts two models. Reading Confucius's Great Learning and Analects onto golf, he casts a repeating swing as a 'well-ordered kingdom' rooted in self-cultivation, and reinterprets ren, li, yi, and xiao so the 'authoritative player' masters the game through ritual practice, a teacher-parent (xiao), and doing what is appropriate in each lie. Against this social conception he sets Ben Hogan's Five Lessons as a 'rugged individualist' account stressing solitary practice and personal responsibility, and proposes a contextual pluralism as a mean between communitarian absolutism and individualist relativism.

confucian-li.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
confucian-li.title: Fourteenth Hole Plato and Confucius on the Form of Golf From the Real to the Ideal
confucian-li.relation: Stephen Laumakis stages a thought experiment pitting Plato the Idealist against Confucius the Realist/Pragmatist on how to think about and play golf. On Plato's theory of Forms, every club, ball and swing is an imperfect copy of a timeless, unchanging Form—there is a 'perfect' swing (Tiger Woods, Ernie Els) that par and the handicap system let us measure ourselves against, so golf is about striving toward the Ideal. Confucius, read through the 'Great Learning' and 'Analects' (li, ren, self-cultivation, unrelenting practice), instead prizes the situation-sensitive sage who negotiates each bad lie (Phil Mickelson's flop shots). Laumakis concludes the good golfer must integrate both: pursue perfection while wielding practical wisdom about when to go for it and when to lay up.

confucian-li.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-li.relation: Kohler-Ryan and Palmer treat 'sense' and 'sensibility' as a spectrum Lee explores through sisterhood in Sense and Sensibility (Elinor/Marianne) and Crouching Tiger (Shu Lien/Jen). Elinor and Shu Lien embody sense, Shu Lien specifically the Confucian balance of li and ren that lets her soften ritual with humanity; Marianne embodies Burke's British-Romantic sublime while Jen embodies Daoist immersion in the dao. Reading door-frames, windows, hair-combing rituals and Shu Lien's hairpin as symbols, they argue only Sense and Sensibility achieves integration in time, whereas Li Mu Bai's confession that he lived sense and sensibility as separate spheres comes too late.

confucian-li.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-li.relation: Thompson argues that Lee's 'cowboy aesthetic' of rugged isolation in Brokeback Mountain (Ennis and Jack) and Crouching Tiger (Li Mu Bai, Shu Lien, Jen) is only apparent: the characters are always already embedded in Confucius' five cardinal relationships, read through Xunzi's darker view that selfish desire must be curbed by ritual and social hierarchy. Ennis and Jack seem lone individuals but are defined by ties to Alma, family and each other, and Jen's redemption comes when she abandons self-serving desire to re-establish her Confucian relationships. Citing Nietzsche's gloss on Aristotle that only a beast or a god lives alone, it concludes there is no truly isolated cowboy.

confucian-li.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-li.relation: Bush argues that Brokeback Mountain transcends both the heterosexual western archetype and queer theory by presenting male sexuality through Mencius' philosophy and John Corvino's ethics of homosexuality. Using Mencius' four sprouts (ren, li, yi, zhi) and doctrine of natural goodness, he reads Ennis as the character in whom sexuality is contextual, cultivated and moral rather than merely physical, so the relationship between Ennis and Jack becomes an ethical friendship grounded in ren, the virtue Mencius says is most intense among friends. The bystanders Aguirre and Alma keeping the secret, and the final shirt-and-postcard scene, illustrate zhi as contextual moral judgment and homosexuality reframed as ethical rather than sexual.

confucian-li.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-li.relation: Dull reads Eat Drink Man Woman through a Hall-and-Ames 'focus-field' model of personhood, analyzing harmony via metaphors of a culinary dish, music and a sports team where each element keeps its integrity within a whole. He diagnoses the Chu family by pairing Mencius (morality as expression of the four sprouts) against Xunzi (desire must be structured by ritual): Chef Chu is 'repressed as a turtle', Jia-Jen hides behind ritual, Jia-Ning acts on impulse, and Jia-Chien lacks direction. Their romantic transformations restore harmony, answering Chu's question 'is there more than food and sex?' affirmatively, as expression, desire and ritual come into balance and his sense of taste returns.

confucian-li.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
confucian-li.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
confucian-li.relation: Komasinski explains Confucius's advice to fathers through three ideas: ritual (li, glossed as 'cultural grammar' – engagement rings, saying 'I love you'), excellence/virtue as excelling at relating to others (ren, 'co-humanity'), and wisdom. Using the Analects' 'Upright Gong' passage (fathers and sons cover for each other) beside Plato's Euthyphro, he shows Confucius prizes the father-son bond over law, and reads the parable of the prodigal son and Tu Wei-ming's 'personality ideal' to argue fathers should lead by virtuous example rather than punishment.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
rousseau-social-contract.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
rousseau-social-contract.relation: In an imaginary salon hosted by the baker 'la Brioche,' the goddess Eris drops a golden apple inscribed 'Atkins,' and three philosophers fight over the credit. Rousseau claims Atkins's war on refined flour and 'invented fake food' as his own back-to-nature, state-of-nature legacy; Confucius counters that Americans are 'grazers' without li, that culture is nature's flower, and that only ritual propriety can counteract the advertising that fills the void; Democritus claims the scientific core — 'hyperinsulism,' 'benign dietary ketosis' — as atomism's heir, deriding Rousseau's general will as democratic truth-concocting and Plato's otherworldly philosopher-king. The debate ranges over free will versus scientific prediction-and-control and ends unresolved over a refusal of brioche.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
rousseau-social-contract.title: No Way Out
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Leah Murray reads Romero's Dead series as an argument about the American social contract, individualism versus communitarianism. Night of the Living Dead's farmhouse is Hobbes: fear throws strangers Ben and Mr. Cooper into a makeshift commonwealth whose individualist half ('every man for himself' in the basement) fails, while Dawn shows the Hobbesian next step - martial law as Leviathan - after the state of nature returns. Land of the Dead's Fiddler's Green is a fear-born contract corrupting into Kaufman's hierarchy, and Big Daddy's zombies form the counter-model, a Rousseauian community of the general will based on mutual bonds rather than terror, as the priest in Dawn already urged ('we must stop the killing... or lose the war'). Following Tocqueville on civic association, she concludes Romero's survivors - Ben, Peter, Sarah, Riley - vindicate communitarian cooperation, even though Night's bureaucratic ending suggests there may be no way out.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
rousseau-social-contract.title: No Way Out
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Leah Murray argues Romero's Dead films stage the American contest between individualism and communitarianism inside the social contract: in Night of the Living Dead, communitarian Ben barricading the farmhouse against every-man-for-himself Mr. Cooper hiding in the basement; in Dawn of the Dead, the Peter-Roger-Fran-Stephen mall commune collapsing when Stephen's 'it's ours, we took it' meets the bikers; in Day of the Dead, Sarah's compassion against the racist, harassing soldiers; in Land of the Dead, Kaufman's Fiddler's Green as a Hobbesian Leviathan born of fear, complete with bread-and-circuses for the poor. Against the Hobbesian fear-born contract (Dawn opens in a full state-of-nature collapse) she sets Rousseau's general will and Tocqueville's civic association, embodied in Riley's freely formed community and in Big Daddy's zombies, who organize, turn from eating humans, and bring down the Leviathan. The films' verdict: fear-based individualist contracts collapse under their own contradictions, while compassionate cooperation — even among the Undead — is the only way out, even if Romero doubts its ultimate viability.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
rousseau-social-contract.title: Futurama and Philosophy
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Young tests Isaiah Berlin's distinction between negative liberty (absence of external interference) and positive liberty (rational self-government) on three episodes: Fry's super-Slurm compulsion in 'Fry and the Slurm Factory,' human Bender's lethal gluttony in 'Anthology of Interest II,' and the worms whose upgrades win Leela's love in 'Parasites Lost' - each agent is externally unobstructed yet not self-governing. Bender's jacking-on addiction and the Temple of Robotology's threat of Robot Hell in 'Hell Is Other Robots' illustrate Rousseau's 'forced to be free,' the coercion that Berlin warned has licensed totalitarian regimes. The chapter concludes Futurama takes no side, suggesting genuine freedom needs both positive and negative liberty.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
rousseau-social-contract.title: Homeland and Philosophy
rousseau-social-contract.relation: April Marratto and Adam Barkman use Foucault's appropriation of Bentham's panopticon - surveillance whose mere threat disciplines - to read Carrie's illegal watches on the Brody house, the family's stay in the safe house, and Dana's discovery that speech about her father's Islam is policed. Against Foucault's claim that freedom is an illusion maintained by power, the chapter sets Aristotle's view that freedom is a self-directed will choosing rightly (Dana making amends for the hit-and-run) and Rousseau's social contract, under which citizens trade equal freedoms for equal protection. Both would endorse Saul forcing Brody's detox for the country's sake, concluding absolute freedom is neither possible nor desirable.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
rousseau-social-contract.title: 6. Tris’s Compassion and the Problem of Evil
rousseau-social-contract.relation: McCrossin reads Tris's whole arc as a struggle with the problem of evil, both the theological version from Job and the modern secular one Susan Neiman describes, in which unreasonable suffering threatens trust in human reason. He casts Tris as cut from Rousseau's mold - her insistence on making the evils of Jeanine, Marcus, and Evelyn intelligible - against Voltaire's Candide refusal to rationalize suffering, and treats the faction system as Rousseau's social-contract strategy for containing the inclination to evil while Tris herself plays a wartime Emile. The key is Tobias's lesson that selflessness and bravery are not that different: selflessness enables the courage that compassion motivates, from pressing her forehead to Jeanine's gun in the fear landscape to taking Caleb's place at the weapons lab, so that the trilogy ends with Tobias's 'we mend each other.'

rousseau-social-contract.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
rousseau-social-contract.title: 10. Amity—Directly Democratic
rousseau-social-contract.relation: McCrossin identifies Amity's consensus circles as direct democracy - the people exercising government in person, against the republics of Abnegation, Candor, and Erudite and Dauntless's open oligarchy - and hears Tris's skepticism ('How do they get anything done?') and Tobias's admiration ('it makes them kind') echoing the 2011 public debate over Occupy Wall Street. Johanna Reyes acts as a facilitator who helps Amity's general will develop rather than articulating it, but when the planned attack on Erudite threatens innocents she leaves the faction rather than quietly mold its will, confirming Tris's worry about talk in the face of terrible deeds. Through Alexander Meiklejohn's absolutist reading of the First Amendment, the chapter then argues that New Chicago's self-government needs both uncompromisingly protected political speech and a direct-democratic dimension for working out what the common good actually is.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
rousseau-social-contract.title: 4. Raising Darrow
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Trip McCrossin reads Darrow's storyline as an engagement with the problem of evil in both its theological form (Harmony dubbing him Lazarus, the parables of John and Luke) and its secular form, which Susan Neiman traces to the Rousseau-Voltaire dispute: must evil be made intelligible or not? Darrow begins Voltairean—incredulous before the rigged Laurel and Eo's hanging ('She left me')—but his resurrection and political awakening on the surface remake him Rousseauian: evil is the misalignment of individual and general wills, and humans are corrupted by society, not born bad. The chapter reads Darrow's 'Man was born free' broadcast in Morning Star, his new social contract with Victra, and the education of Pax (with Lysander left to Cassius to 'raise him right') as Rousseau's Social Contract and Emile program—break the chains, then educate each generation so its contracts align ever closer with the general will.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
rousseau-social-contract.title: 3. Click Bait for Black Fish
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Porot reads Elliot through Berlin's positive liberty: people are enslaved to their lower selves - the 'daemons' of addiction and primal urge Elliot describes in 'eps1.3_da3m0ns.mp4' - and freedom requires a contract in which an external force holds you to your higher self. Elliot writes such contracts with Shayla over his drugs and imagines Mr. Robot as the paternalistic enforcer who pushes him off the pier when he breaks his word, while corporations run the reverse contract, 'hacking' people from within through addictive sugar, clickbait, and advertising. The black fish dream crystallizes this: everyone at the office devours the confined fish of reverse-contract slavery while Elliot alone eats Pop's pie - freedom through the father figure of Mr. Robot.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
rousseau-social-contract.title: 4 On the Origin of the State
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Opening with Newt Gingrich's complaint that students 'don't read enough Locke' and the Chinese premier's appeal to Rousseau, the chapter compares the three contract theorists' states of nature and purposes of government: Hobbes's war of every man against every man yielding an absolute sovereign with no separation of powers, Locke's peaceful nature in which mixing labor with land creates property and money then creates inequality, so that government's 'great and chief end' is protecting property through limited, separated powers and no food stamps, and Rousseau's compassionate natural humans corrupted when the first man enclosed land, so the state was founded on fraud and a general will that should 'force him to be free' and give people food stamps. Smith then reads the actual US founding as a chaste Lockean contract 'bastardized' on race and sex - the Declaration plagiarized from Locke, Abigail Adams's 'remember the ladies' laughed off, Dred Scott, with the 14th Amendment as the de-bastardizing 'Charter of Universal Freedom' - while Engels derives the state historically from the Iroquois and Greek gens, private property and class conflict. A final section documents white supremacy inside the tradition (Kant inventing the scientific concept of race, Hegel and Hume on Black inferiority), John Stuart Mill's 'Negro Question' as the tradition's decisive anti-racist break, Locke's own entanglements with the slave trade, and Marx's condemnation of slavery as super-exploitation.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
rousseau-social-contract.title: 8. From the Handmaid’s Tale to the Handmaids’ Tale
rousseau-social-contract.relation: McCrossin reads Offred's silent prayers ('I want to know what I did to deserve this') as channeling the Book of Job, using Susan Neiman's distinction between the theological and secular problem of evil: even if we stop demanding explanations from God, we must still make evil intelligible, as Janine's Testifying cruelly refuses to do. He sets Rousseau against Voltaire on whether morality requires making evil intelligible, finding June Rousseauian for piecing together Gilead's hidden prehistory at the Boston Globe and for acting from compassion, as with the bread-truck driver's secret Quran. The Salvaging refusal—Ofglen first, then Offred, then sixty-five stones dropped with 'I'm sorry, Aunt Lydia'—shows compassion becoming solidarity and solidarity becoming a general will, transforming The Handmaid's Tale into The Handmaids' Tale.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
rousseau-social-contract.title: 23. The Neighborhood Is Us
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Trip McCrossin frames the show, via Susan Neiman, as Rousseau's answer to the problem of evil: bad things (including bad television) happen to good kids, but education can mitigate evil, which is why Rogers prefers Rousseau's demand to make evil intelligible to Voltaire's Candidean refusal and Pangloss's best-of-all-possible-worlds. Rogers pursued only Emile's second prong, making us as we ought to be by loving children 'just the way they are,' and the post-9/11 PSAs before King Friday's empty castle merge Make-Believe into reality, the last 'modulation' of his thirty-four-year ministry.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
rousseau-social-contract.title: A Black Mirror of Our Anxieties
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Nosedive's star ratings are read as a digital panopticon — Bentham's prison design generalized by Foucault's Discipline and Punish — with China's Zhima Credit and Social Credit Systems showing the 'future is already here.' Rousseau's general will and Plato's ship-of-state frame the tyranny-of-the-majority worry (Chester destroyed by an office mob, Lacie jailed for a wedding toast, post-truth tribalism), which Mill's harm principle rebuts: Lacie's rant harms no one and should not be punished. Sartre's 'look' and No Exit explain Lacie's staged cookie photo ('Heaven!') and her final liberating exchange of insults with her cellmate, while Goffman's masks ground the epistemological worry that digital profiles are performances we nonetheless trust, and Bourdieu's symbolic capital names what the scores actually measure.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
rousseau-social-contract.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Against Blomkvist's 'I don't believe in collective guilt,' the chapter argues the Section is not a few bad apples: with Rousseau, institutions outgrow the people's will and preserve themselves (the guardianship agency cannot welcome its own obsolescence; the Fälldin directive lets Säpo stand inside and outside the law at once), and with Arendt, institutions protect only those they already recognize, so the excluded Salander cannot be heard by Teleborian, Prosecutor Ekström, or the court that doubts Giannini. Through bell hooks's definition of patriarchy it shows the police, psychiatry, and Säpo prize rationality, stability, and power in a masculine code under which Salander's responsiveness to her mother's abuse and her retaliation read as insanity—her very self-sufficiency (pepper spray, Taser, forward planning) proving she needs no 'guardianship.' Rancière's policing-versus-politics distinction supplies the conclusion: perpetual political contestation of who institutions exclude, not Prime Minister-initiated cleanup, is the only answer to a hidden Section in every institution.

rousseau-social-contract.title: Notes
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Jackson reads the show through Rousseau's contrast between the general will and a pathological 'corporate will': Frank discards Freddy the moment his criminal past goes viral, Tusk and Walker's old friendship curdles into mutual blackmail, and Remy and Jackie trade intimacy for career protection - all reducing Aristotle's true friendship to friendships of utility and pleasure subordinated to institutions that treat persons as means. Rousseau's account of civilization degrading natural self-love (amour de soi) into vanity (amour-propre) explains why Washington's corporate ethos leaves no friends, only 'loose ends' to be eliminated, from Zoe pushed onto the platform to Doug hunting Rachel. The chapter ends with 'Man is born free, but is everywhere in chains' as the verdict on corporate personhood's conquest of human bonds.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
rousseau-social-contract.title: Notes
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Reads the show through Rousseau's contrast between the general will and a pathological 'corporate will': governments and corporations are sociopathic artificial persons that depersonalize their agents, degrading natural self-love (amour de soi) into status-hungry amour-propre. On this account Frank's break with Freddy ('just a good customer'), the Tusk-Walker alliance, and Remy and Jackie's bought loyalties are Aristotelian friendships of utility or pleasure crushed under the corporate will, never true friendship, leaving Washington with 'honor without virtue' and men 'everywhere in chains'.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
rousseau-social-contract.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Reads '1%' — where Cartman's failed fitness test makes him the scapegoated one percent, and the school's 99% splinter into warring 83%, 30%, and 5% factions occupying the Red Robin (and its restroom) — through Rousseau's Social Contract on freedom and equality and the dismembered social body, showing how popular solidarity shatters into meaningless percentage tribes. 'Night of the Living Homeless' (the poor as zombies who 'feed on our change', Kyle's $20 spawning the swarm, the shotgun as the only remedy) dramatizes the dehumanizing social-Darwinist picture of the economic undead, and the underpants gnomes' business plan (Phase 1: Collect Underpants, Phase 2: ?, Phase 3: Profit) mocks CEOs who cannot say why they amass wealth. The chapter's own verdict: corporations as such are good (cars, computers, canned soup), and blame falls on the greedy individuals inside them, since death — Tolstoy's two meters of burial land — levels all players.

rousseau-social-contract.title: Werner Herzog on Circles, Chickens and Impotency
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Tyler Tritten argues that Even Dwarfs Started Small and Stroszek are not principally political but share an essence: the impotency of the powerless dramatized through cyclical, repetitive motion (circling trucks, ski lifts, and above all chickens). He defends Herzog's 'apoliticism' — citing Herzog's preference for the medieval melior pars over numerical voting (echoing Rousseau's general will versus the popular vote, and Socrates against the many) — as locating the human condition beneath contingent social conditions. The handless, cannibalistic, circumambulating chicken becomes the emblem of a self-consuming nature and a humanity too proportionate to the beast, provoking a pure, aching laughter as the only revolt.

rousseau-social-contract.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
rousseau-social-contract.title: 2. The Winchesters’ Revolt Against the Divine Plan
rousseau-social-contract.relation: Steele argues the Winchesters' fifteen-season revolt against Chuck's authored 'divine plan' stages the free-will-versus-determinism debate: Chuck writes their lives yet Sam shooting God shows the plan can be surprised, leaving 'free will in the details' as compatibilism. She frames the cosmic contest of angels, demons, and Chuck as Nietzsche's competing wills to power, but concludes Supernatural finally rejects Nietzsche for Rousseau, championing individual free will and a General Will where Sam and Dean rebuild Heaven to match their own choices.

paradigm-shift.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
paradigm-shift.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Steele starts from Orwell's worry that laypeople accept scientific consensus as unreflectively as tribesmen accept witch-doctors — sharpened by Lysenko and Nazi 'racial science' — and answers it with Popper's critical rationalism: since Hume's problem of induction bars proof from instances, we can only provisionally prefer theories that survive severe attempts at falsification, so trusting experts is reasonable exactly when their community tests rather than defends its theories. Kuhn's paradigms explain why dissident alternatives like Atkins talk past the dominant school (Atkins and Agatston are cardiologists, not dieticians), and the 2002–2004 studies showing improved lipids on more fat figure as the kind of surprise that precedes paradigm change. His verdict: neither trusting nor resisting experts is foolish; 'human knowledge is too important to be left to experts.'

paradigm-shift.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
paradigm-shift.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Womack tests whether Atkins counts as a Kuhnian paradigm shift, using the Ptolemaic-to-Copernican transition as the model: paradigms define which problems matter, normal science accumulates anomalies, and crisis ends in a new paradigm. Measured against the dieting paradigm's own goals, Atkins flunks — its short-term wins fade by twelve months in the JAMA comparison with the Ornish, Zone, and Weight Watchers diets, with 30–50 percent dropout — so the dieting paradigm itself, which treats obesity as an individual plate problem, is the thing in crisis. Her proposed replacement shifts from the individual to the 'toxic food environment': sidewalks, zoning, food advertising rules, and the French Paradox as the existence proof.

paradigm-shift.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
paradigm-shift.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Bruce Reichenbach recounts the failure of the Enlightenment quest for certainty from Descartes and Locke through Kant to the positivists, and argues that Lewis's Narnia instead models knowing as perspectival (the Stable door whose inside is bigger than its outside), value-laden (the Dwarfs' self-chosen dark paradigm that turns Aslan's feast into refuse and violets into stable litter), and personal (Lucy's unarguable knowledge that she has seen Aslan in Prince Caspian, read through Michael Polanyi's tacit knowledge). Kuhn's competing paradigms frame theism versus atheism, James's will to believe opens the chapter, and Plantinga's defeaters keep personal knowledge from collapsing into mere subjectivity.

paradigm-shift.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
paradigm-shift.title: Wittgenstein Ultimate Bullshit Detector—or Bullshitter
paradigm-shift.relation: Fuller argues that mastering a discipline converts critics into loyal insiders — Thomas Kuhn's 'normal science' enshrines the tendency, cognitive dissonance explains it, and Blaise Pascal's wager is the general model of betting on a way of life that makes you receptive to its confirming signs. Against this he sets the Protestant tradition of Luther's conscience, 'playing it by ear', which like the Sophists concedes that reality rarely yields yes-or-no answers — the gap we fill being bullshit — and he frames the dispute as realism versus antirealism, reading Frankfurt's On Bullshit as an ad hominem attack on antirealists. He then re-examines Frankfurt's star witness: Wittgenstein's rebuke of Fania Pascal for saying she felt 'like a dog that has been run over' now looks like a spectacular lack of imagination, since evolutionary psychology, being forged at that very moment, has been narrowing the human-animal mental gap ever since.

paradigm-shift.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
paradigm-shift.title: Vertigo and Epistemological Vertigo
paradigm-shift.relation: Flory reads Vertigo as an epistemological parable: Scottie's 'hardheaded Scot' method, collecting facts and deducing from universal principles, fails three times (the step-stool 'cure' for his acrophobia, explaining away Madeleine's 'possession' with the horse statue, forcing Judy up the bell tower for confirmation), delivering an implicit critique of Vienna Circle positivism in the manner of Carnap and Ayer. Against Scottie, the chapter mobilizes Kuhn's theory-laden facts, Aristotle's point that human conduct resists codification by exceptionless laws, and Hume's 'slave of the passions,' with Descartes's automata and Chalmers's philosophical zombies framing the problem of other minds. Midge, who knows people emotionally as well as factually, models the alternative: philosophers who fear 'epistemological vertigo' should give up epistemological training wheels and accept that minds, especially emotions, escape law-like rules.

paradigm-shift.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
paradigm-shift.title: Thematic Synchronicity
paradigm-shift.relation: Jones asks what the famous Dark Side of the Rainbow synchronization (album plus The Wizard of Oz, started on the third MGM lion roar) could mean given that the band denies designing it. He catalogs vivid syncs ('Time''s chimes as Miss Gulch bicycles past, 'Money''s cash register entering Munchkinland, 'Us and Them''s 'black and blue' over the Witch and Dorothy), then rejects both the Waters-conspiracy model and Jung's acausal 'synchronicity' as pseudoscience, proposing instead Conrad's apophenia and Kuhn's point that suspecting patterns others miss is the lifeblood of discovery. His resolution is 'thematic synchronicity': both works stage the struggle between security and transcendence, Dorothy's 'Over the Rainbow' against 'Eclipse''s 'all you touch and all you see is all your life will ever be,' so the coincidences feel objective because they are subjectively real to everyone.

paradigm-shift.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
paradigm-shift.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Surveys the philosophy of science through Breaking Bad: Walt's authority trades on the trusted white-coat stereotype (Jesse's 'you're supposed to be a scientist', Tuco's CPR demand), while the chapter traces how modern science distinguished itself from alchemy via Kuhn's structure of scientific revolutions and Lakatos's research programmes, and how Feyerabend and the Traditional Knowledge movement challenge Western science's monopoly - echoed in Jesse's chili powder and the ingenious 'shake-and-bake' method. Walt and Jesse's quarrel over method resolves into an apprentice-master reconciliation ('you're an artist'), mirroring science's own shifting self-image. Ellul's grim prediction that technology, once embraced, cannot be made humane explains the ending: remission comes too late, and Walt may as well try to un-invent a weapon of mass destruction.

paradigm-shift.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
paradigm-shift.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: John Huss asks whether Andy Serkis deserved an Oscar nomination for playing Caesar through performance capture, and argues that 'What is acting?' is a Socratic-style definitional question (like stumping Euthyphro on piety) of the sort Wittgenstein diagnosed as a language confusion, since the definition of movie acting is in flux. Using the seeing-as debate, Kuhnian theory-ladenness of observation versus Fodor's Muller-Lyer point that belief does not dictate sight, he explains why animators and fans see such different things in the identical raw footage. He concludes, with James Franco, that acting is an emergent ensemble property of actors reacting to one another on a shared stage, which performance capture enables rather than threatens, and a coda notes PETA's hope that CG performers will end the use of animal actors.

paradigm-shift.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
paradigm-shift.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Cole Bowman explains the human-Formic war through Donald Davidson's critique of the idea of a self-contained conceptual scheme: the buggers' inability to grasp 'father,' 'individual,' or human sentience looks like complete untranslatability, yet Ender donning the bugger mask and the hive-queen's philotic contact show, via Davidson's principle of charity, that translation and a new shared scheme are possible. Kuhn's incommensurable paradigms and Feyerabend's account of how new theories eliminate old meanings frame how both species discard their prior concepts once Ender becomes the single point where the two schemes meet.

paradigm-shift.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
paradigm-shift.title: The Devil and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: The Bocks use the courtroom frame of The Exorcism of Emily Rose to ask whether anyone could be justified in believing in demon possession, since the same seizures, polyglot voices, and levitations read differently under naturalism and supernaturalism. Kuhn's paradigms explain why neither worldview abandons ship at anomalies, and they weigh Wiebe's 'finite spirits as theoretical entities,' Hume's miracles argument (with Levine's Red Sea thought experiment as rebuttal), and the Cartesian ghost-in-the-machine premise that possession would require. Testing even a Men in Black alien hypothesis against the religiously specific phenomena, they conclude that a witnessed case like Emily's could rationally justify belief in possession.

paradigm-shift.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
paradigm-shift.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Russ Hamer takes Mac's 'Science Is a Liar Sometimes' defense - Aristotle, Galileo, and Newton each proved his predecessor 'a bitch' - and his claim that believing in evolution takes as much faith as belief in God, and answers with philosophy of science. Popper's falsificationism explains why Mac's 'I won't change my mind... regardless of the facts' is the essence of the non-scientific: only theories risking precise, falsifiable predictions (Einstein's light deflection) count as science, unlike vague astrology or Charlie's cherry-picked evidence that the Waitress will love him. Kuhn's distinction of normal and revolutionary science explains why past failures never discredited science - falsifications within a paradigm are tuning, and the Gang's group-configuration trials in 'The Gang Solves the Gas Crisis' are normal science at its best - so revisability is science's strength, not a reason to fear looking like a science bitch.

paradigm-shift.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
paradigm-shift.title: 20. The Intersection of Science and Philosophy, the Seediest Corner in Ankh-Morpork
paradigm-shift.relation: A comic sprint through Western thought anchored in the Science of Discworld books, the chapter runs from Aristotle—whose geocentric four-element physics, it notes, fits Discworld better than Roundworld, and whose condemnations of usury it digresses over—through Descartes's cogito and mind-body dualism, Ryle's 'ghost in the machine,' behaviorism, identity theory, eliminative materialism, and functionalism's brain-as-computer picture, to show how philosophy of mind advances by each theory picking on its predecessor. Newton's occult-seeming gravity, later overturned by Einstein, illustrates the chapter's real thesis drawn from Pratchett's 'Lies-to-Wizards': neither science nor philosophy erects a timeless edifice of facts, since 'every so often, you have to unlearn what you thought you already knew,' while Diogenes and the Cynics supply the model of philosophy done in the common tongue that Pratchett shares.

paradigm-shift.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
paradigm-shift.title: 16. The Pleasure of the Twist
paradigm-shift.relation: Scales maps the experience of a TZ twist onto Kuhn's Structure of Scientific Revolutions: planted anomalies (Nan Adams' 'things are a little wrong,' Jana's missing childhood photographs, the Kanamits' ominous 'simply trust us') accumulate until the ending makes viewers, like scientists in a revolution, 'come to live in a different world' — rejecting cumulative growth and theory-neutral observation along the way. He then explains the pleasure through Kuhn's theory-ladenness experiments with anomalous playing cards and Churchland's connectionist prototypes: at 'It's a cookbook!' the Kanamits' deeds are suddenly re-categorized from helping behavior to livestock, triggering the same dopamine jolt as getting a joke.

paradigm-shift.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
paradigm-shift.title: 17. You’ve Never Seen a Miracle
paradigm-shift.relation: Andrew Kuzma reads the film's religious texture from Sapper's Graham Greene novel to Wallace as a Gnostic Demiurge — a lesser creator-god — whose 'angels', like biblical ones, possess the free will to rebel, which is exactly what Luv does when she lies to Wallace about Joshi's death. The mystery child imports the whole miraculous-birth and chosen-one tradition, from Rachel's opened womb to Joi's 'born, not made' echoing the Nicene Creed's 'begotten'. But K is not the chosen one, and via 'Galatians Syndrome' the chapter applies Paul's paradigm shift in Galatians — faith, not flesh, makes one Abraham's heir; 'no longer Jew or Greek, slave or free' — to show birth never mattered: K, Joi, and Sapper become human by believing, choosing, and dying for the right cause.

paradigm-shift.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
paradigm-shift.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Reads the 'Sad Sack' photograph, which Wayne Jarvis sees as Iraqi WMD bunkers and Barry Zuckerkorn sees as Tobias's testicles, through the Duhem-Quine thesis of underdetermination and Kuhn's theory-ladenness of observation: the dominant 'George Sr. the traitor' paradigm dictates what is seen and nearly mobilizes Buster for war, while Barry's rival theory creates a crisis that only the omniscient narrator resolves. Kuhn's five criteria for theory choice (accuracy, consistency, scope, simplicity, fruitfulness) are applied to the rival 'theories', and George Michael's failed eye exam dramatizes the skeptical moment when no lens lets you see clearly, showing knowledge is a social and political position.

paradigm-shift.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
paradigm-shift.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Jones explains the Leonard–Leslie breakup ('Tell me, Leonard, how would we raise the children?') as a genuine clash of research commitments: string theory with its demanded extra dimensions versus Leslie's loop quantum gravity. Along the way he uses Popper's falsifiability and Kuhn's paradigms — the 1998 dark-energy discovery as falsification at work, Sheldon's alien-parasite hypothesis as paradigm-protecting refusal to accept that Amy is aroused by Zack — and the Dirac-to-Anderson antimatter story alongside Sheldon's North Pole monopole expedition to weigh theoretical against experimental science. Leonard emerges as the Feynman-style skeptic ('At best you can say, hey, my idea has internal logical consistency'), which is exactly what Leslie cannot forgive.

paradigm-shift.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
paradigm-shift.title: Of Science, Sorcery, and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: The chapter reads Strange's conversion from neurosurgeon to sorcerer as a Kuhnian paradigm shift: his medical materialism is 'normal science' puzzle-solving that keeps resisting anomalies (Pangborn's impossible recovery, the astral projection, the multiverse tour) until Kamar-Taj offers a rival paradigm with its own exemplars, which he can only adopt by learning 'knowledge how' through tedious practice. It explains incommensurability through Strange's inability to rationally persuade his old medical colleagues, then contrasts Kuhn with Popper's falsificationism, Feyerabend's 'anything goes' anarchism (sorcery once looked as disreputable as early heliocentrism), and Lakatos's progressive versus degenerating research programs to ask whether sorcery could count as a science in Strange's world.

paradigm-shift.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
paradigm-shift.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.relation: Cole Bowman explains the three Formic invasions as failures between 'conceptual schemes,' deploying Davidson's 'On the Very Idea of a Conceptual Scheme' — translatability, the principle of charity, and the closet analogy — alongside Kuhn's incommensurable paradigms and Feyerabend's account of how new theories eliminate old meanings. Ender donning the bugger mask in Peter's game and his final philotic bond with the hive-queen show the two schemes touching at a single shared point, making Ender 'the metal in between' who begins translating between human and Formic worlds.

paradigm-shift.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
paradigm-shift.title: It’s Life in the Solar System, Jim, But Not as We Know It
paradigm-shift.relation: Uses MacIntyre's demand for self-knowledge — awareness of the social and political currents that shape one's beliefs — to diagnose the Martian Congressional Republic's exceptionalism (Lopez berating 'short-sighted and selfish' Earthers from the Donnager) and to chart Bobbie Draper's redemption arc: refusing to fire first on Ganymede, refusing to bear false witness after the hearings, protecting Holden at the Ring Station, defecting to Avasarala, and finally rescuing Naomi. It maps MCR culture onto American space culture — Kennedy's Rice speech, the Mars Society and National Space Society founding statements, Zubrin's Case for Mars, and Patricia Limerick's and Linda Billings's critique of the 'conquering the space frontier' metaphor, with Carnap's frameworks and Kuhn's incommensurability explaining how metaphors hide alternatives — and argues the MCR never acquires self-knowledge, a failure that ends in its alliance with Marco Inaros and the move to Laconia, while Draper's willingness to update her beliefs shows what philosophy asks of real spaceflight advocates.

paradigm-shift.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
paradigm-shift.title: NOTES
paradigm-shift.relation: Asks how to tell genuine science from pseudoscience using Chandra Suresh's rejected Activating Evolution theory, Sheldrake's morphic fields, alchemy, and Behe's intelligent design. Kuhn's picture of normal science, anomalies, and revolutions explains why Suresh would need a full-blown crisis in evolutionary theory — such as people actually flying — before the community accepts him, and why time rather than mockery settles a theory's fate. Ockham's razor condemns the unnecessary organizing principles in both Sheldrake's and Suresh's theories, and intelligent design is exposed as bad method because, like creationism, it was devised to protect a prior commitment from disconfirming fossil and cosmological evidence.

paradigm-shift.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
paradigm-shift.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
paradigm-shift.relation: Johnson uses 'Go God Go's' future of 2546—where Dawkins-style atheism has become a warring religion and otter scientists intone 'Oh my Science!'—to ask whether science and religion genuinely conflict and whether New Atheism is itself a faith. Applying abduction and the four criteria of adequacy, he argues the embellished-story hypothesis beats miracle claims about Jesus (whose legend grew Gospel by Gospel), Sathya Sai Baba, Joseph Smith, and Xenu, that Mr(s). Garrison's 'you can't disprove God' and the show's sarcasm commit an appeal to ignorance, and that Stan's water-into-wine scene with Jesus shows how easily people are fooled. He allows Kuhnian theory change in science but rejects James's will-to-believe for existence claims—the moon whale Willzyx needs evidence—and concludes Parker and Stone are unfair to Dawkins: ending religion would not end violence, but it would remove the easiest justification for it, and some answers are simply true even when unknown.

paradigm-shift.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
paradigm-shift.title: 16. The Pleasure of the Twist
paradigm-shift.relation: Scales argues that Twilight Zone twist endings are miniature Kuhnian paradigm shifts: anomalous clues accumulate ('things are a little wrong' in 'The Hitch-Hiker,' Jana's mismatched photographs, the Kanamits' book title), then the ending forces a wholesale reinterpretation in which we 'come to live in a different world,' as when 'To Serve Man' turns benevolence into livestock. Extending Kuhn's theory-ladenness with Paul Churchland's connectionist prototypes, he explains the pleasure of the twist as the brain's reward for suddenly re-categorizing a whole story under a new prototype. The show's twist toolkit, he adds, seeded later works from Planet of the Apes to The Sixth Sense.

paradigm-shift.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
paradigm-shift.title: Detection and the Logic of Abduction in The X-Files
paradigm-shift.relation: Abrams and Cooke map Mulder and Scully onto Holmes and Watson and onto the Clifford-James debate: Scully embodies Clifford's ethics of belief (suspend judgment without hard evidence), while Mulder's 'I Want to Believe' poster enacts James's will to believe, which lets him see what the paradigm excludes. The chapter formalizes both agents' actual method as Peirce's logic of abduction, using Eco's overcoded/undercoded/creative triad to analyze Scully's Fowley clothing inference and the mushroom episodes of 'Field Trip', and extends Peircean semiotics with Mulder's 'absence sign' (the missing nine minutes, missing acid burns, bodies taken without a trace). Kuhn's normal science versus revolution explains why Scully stays inside the FBI's paradigm while Mulder's passion makes him the revolutionary who, with Scully as error-corrector, fuses into a single 'whole person' detective facing the limits of reason.

paradigm-shift.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
paradigm-shift.title: The Doctor Dances
paradigm-shift.relation: Alexander Bertland uses Vico, Cassirer, and Horkheimer and Adorno to argue Doctor Who refuses to simply side with science over myth. Vico shows myth as world-constructing ritual that binds community and carries moral wisdom ('Snakedance's' Snakedance defeats the Mara; 'Meglos' shows myth's danger), while Horkheimer and Adorno's Dialectic of Enlightenment argues science is itself a limiting, mythical framework: the Doctor's insistence that 'fixed points' in time cannot be changed ('The Fires of Pompeii,' 'The Waters of Mars') reflects his own self-constructed scientific paradigm, not real necessity. The Doctor lives well by humbly balancing myth and science.

paradigm-shift.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
paradigm-shift.title: 14. Beyond Loyalty and Disloyalty
paradigm-shift.relation: Bartolo Alegre uses Seldon's trial claim that 'scientific truth is beyond loyalty and disloyalty' to ask whether even formal sciences like logic can be biased. Against Bogdanov's and Lenin's Marxist idea of a 'proletarian logic,' he shows that logical principles (non-contradiction, explosion) have been revised by paraconsistent logicians on purely mathematical grounds, using Hardin's symbolic-logic decoding of the Anacreon message and Orwell's doublethink as illustrations. Drawing on Popper's rejection of uninformative contradictions, Kuhn's sociological account of scientific change, and Lakatos's rational reconstruction, he argues science transcends individual scientists' loyalties only through a diverse, competing community of experts, as when Hummin's loyalty to humanity pushed Seldon to make psychohistory practical.

paradigm-shift.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
paradigm-shift.title: 16. The Pleasure of the Twist
paradigm-shift.relation: Scales argues that Twilight Zone twist endings mirror Kuhn's account of scientific revolutions: seeded anomalies accumulate until a 'paradigm shift' makes us reinterpret everything, as in 'To Serve Man' ('It's a cookbook!'), 'The Lateness of the Hour,' and 'The Hitch-Hiker.' He ties Kuhn's theory-ladenness of observation (the anomalous playing-card experiment) to Paul Churchland's connectionist, prototype-based bottom-up neurophilosophy, concluding the pleasure of the twist is the dopamine reward for deploying a new prototype—the same jolt we get from a joke or a genuine insight.

paradigm-shift.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
paradigm-shift.title: 78. The Witness as Philosophy How Knowledge Is Constructed
paradigm-shift.relation: Cuddy asks what epistemology Blow built into The Witness's frustrating puzzles and its windmill videos (Burke, Feynman, Moriarty, Spira, Gangaji). He rejects the sophistic/Protagorean 'knowledge depends on the observer' reading (most puzzles have objective, inductive-and-deductive solutions, e.g. the yellow-glass bunker) and the strict scientific realism of the Burke video defended by Putnam's no-miracles argument. Using Plato's cave and the aporia of Socrates' Meno (the puzzle's 'ah-ha' epiphanies), and Kuhn's incommensurable paradigm shifts (the game's 'hard left turns' forcing players to overhaul their understanding), he concludes the game argues that true knowledge is attainable, individually and collectively, though reached by a nonlinear, paradigm-shifting route rather than pure realism or relativism.

racial-contract.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
racial-contract.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
racial-contract.relation: Wilkerson borrows the social contract tradition — Hobbes's mutual-restraint founding, radicalized by Pateman's sexual contract and Mills's racial contract — to recast antifat bias as a systematic breach of the social contract enforced by medicine (hallway weigh-ins, weight lectures instead of care), employment, transit seating, and TV fat jokes. Against Atkins's medical discourse of the 'obesity epidemic' she assembles Health at Every Size evidence, trans-fat and high-fructose corn syrup data, and the documented health damage of stigma and dieting itself, concluding that Atkins profits from recasting social problems as individual failings. Atkins for Life's success stories (Kerry Feather's volleyball and new husband, Luann Lockhart's proud daughter) are read as testimony that dieting works as ritual self-abasement purchasing group membership — hence Fat Liberation's 'another world is possible.'

racial-contract.title: Post-Civil Rights Music
racial-contract.relation: Lawson argues political rap - Grandmaster Flash's "The Message", Public Enemy's "911 Is a Joke", Tupac's "Trapped", Dead Prez's "They Schools", Naughty By Nature, Ice Cube's "I Wanna Kill Sam" - challenges liberal political philosophy by claiming the social contract between blacks and the United States is broken: using Locke's Second Treatise account of state protection of life and property, he contends the state's failure of economic and physical protection voids blacks' political obligations. Drawing on Cornel West's diagnosis of black nihilism and Charles Mills's racial contract - a contract constructed for white supremacy - he reads conscious hip hop as post-civil-rights music continuing the black freedom struggle in a new voice, with KRS-One asking "Who protects us from you?"

racial-contract.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
racial-contract.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
racial-contract.relation: Jason Davis opens with Sammy Davis Jr. thanking the white producers for the best film ever made on black-white relations, and their cluelessness, to show that white privilege rests on an epistemology of ignorance, paralleled by the human enjoyment of ape slavery in Conquest. He reads the ape castes through the ontology of race: the films first stage race as biological realism and essentialism (warrior gorillas, chimpanzee scientists, orangutan priests), but Battle for the Planet of the Apes shows biology is not destiny, and human genetics (race accounts for about 0.012 percent of human variation) discredits biological racial realism altogether. Via Charles Mills's social ontology of race and Kwame Anthony Appiah's racial skepticism, the chapter treats ape racism as a mirror of anti-miscegenation-era America whose racial categories are social constructs, down to the dropped ape-human hybrid child.

racial-contract.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
racial-contract.title: 1 Introduction
racial-contract.relation: Smith introduces his project of explaining the subordination of women and blacks philosophically and empirically by comparing the social contract liberalism of Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau with Marxism, building on Carole Pateman's Sexual Contract and Charles Mills's Racial Contract/Contract and Domination, which show the classic contracts were male supremacist and white supremacist. He argues sexual and racial egalitarianism is about politics and power, cataloguing nine power bases women and blacks should acquire, and stresses that because family and state are historically connected (Aristotle's Politics, Hobbes's 'little kingdoms', Locke's conjugal society, Rousseau's family as the oldest society, Engels's 'first class oppression' of the female by the male), equality in marriage may be a precondition for equality in society. He defends Marxism against Mills's dismissal of it as moribund, endorses MacKinnon's linking of sexism and racism while arguing (with Linda LaRue and Du Bois) that the racial contract has been more tyrannical than the sexual contract, and closes with Walzer's definition of egalitarianism as a society free of domination.

racial-contract.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
racial-contract.title: 7 The Bourgeoisie and the Blacks
racial-contract.relation: The chapter sets business - the US bourgeoisie whose privileged position Charles Beard read into the Constitution and which survived the Jacksonian and New Deal challenges by breaking labor through Taft-Hartley, right-to-work laws and the PATCO lockout, its solidarity secured while worker solidarity was undercut by what Marx called the Achilles heel of racism - against blacks as the paradigmatic powerless, shut out of every power base since slavery, which the chapter treats with Baptist and Marx's 1846 letter as a totalitarian system of super-exploited, tortured labor that built American capitalism, its neo-slavery progeny (Blackmon) pauperizing the black community under Dred Scott's 'subordinate and inferior class of beings'. It then narrates black counter-power base by base: the abolitionist interracial coalition wielding charisma (Douglass, Nat Turner, John Brown), information, morality and religion; the NAACP era and King's fusion of charisma, church religion, Myrdal's An American Dilemma and televised nonviolent provocation against Bull Connor's violence, contested by Malcolm X, SNCC and the Black Panthers; and a post-civil-rights scorecard showing a wealth base 94.2 percent white, persistent education and media gaps, constrained black officials from mayors to the symbolic Obama presidency, and a captive but potentially leveraged black vote in a 'Sisyphean' struggle.

racial-contract.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
racial-contract.title: Where in the Hell is Chris Rock
racial-contract.relation: Wisnewski reads SNL's race comedy as applied philosophy of race: the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' sketch shows Mr. Wilson's counter-slurs as an assertion of personhood against Mills's racial contract, Eddie Murphy's Mr. Robinson's Neighborhood and 'White Like Me' expose implicit bias and white privilege, and 'The Day Beyonce Turned Black' illustrates Du Bois's double consciousness. Appiah's racialism explains why Leslie Jones playing Trump strikes audiences as outrageous while white women play men routinely, and Appiah's biological anti-realism about race undercuts that reaction. 'Black Jeopardy' with Tom Hanks's MAGA-hatted Doug finds common ground across race that the 'Lives that Matter' ending sharply limits, Fanon's violence route is raised and set aside, and Crenshaw's intersectionality frames why cast diversity is more than skin-deep.

racial-contract.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
racial-contract.title: You're Our Only Hope
racial-contract.relation: Bein asks whether the galaxy's treatment of droids — Chopper's second-class status on the Ghost, Wuher's 'we don't serve their kind here,' the slur 'clanker' — amounts to racism. He argues Chopper and even the treacherous Hondo pass Kant's moral-agency litmus test and satisfy Singer's preference utilitarianism, making them persons whose abuse is wrong. Borrowing Charles W. Mills's argument that race is a social construct located in institutions rather than biology, he applies critical race theory to Star Wars: droid detectors, droids' legal status as property, and AP-5's 'no one rescues droids' internalized racism show anti-droid prejudice is structural 'situation normal,' so dismantling it takes political work, not just better arguments.

racial-contract.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
racial-contract.title: Arthur Ashe Philosopher in Motion
racial-contract.relation: Inverting Clark Graebner's claim that Ashe's 'loose' play expressed his race, the chapter mines Arthur Ashe's life to test theories of race. It rejects racialism, then argues both major constructivisms fail: Charles Mills's materialist Racial Contract faces an 'assignment problem' because the privileged, successful Ashe eludes the material burdens that supposedly define blackness (Billie Jean King's 'I'm blacker than Arthur'), while Du Bois's narrative constructivism faces an 'authenticity problem' shown by South African students calling Ashe an Uncle Tom and his anguish over his daughter's white doll. Ashe's antiapartheid 'trade' in playing Johannesburg and his disciplined-yet-reckless character model a 'looseness' that treats race as a set of justice and identity projects, not a metaphysical thing.

racial-contract.title: Bamboozled Philosophy through Blackface
racial-contract.relation: Flory argues Bamboozled deliberately makes its own audience laugh at Mantan's blackface coon routines to force self-reflection on how minstrel stereotypes still shape perceptions of African Americans. He reads Pierre Delacroix's shifting defenses of the show (free speech, art, 'get over slavery,' a simple-minded 'who is to judge' moral relativism) through Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance,' and his self-loathing through Fanon's struggle with racialization.
