Flory frames Lee as an Aristotelian gadfly: like Socrates, Lee arouses appropriately proportioned righteous anger (the Golden Mean) at injustice and goads viewers to philosophize, punishing Delacroix, Manray, and the Maumaus in a Manichaean moral structure to drive home minstrelsy's dehumanizing harm.

racial-contract.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
racial-contract.title: Mutants as Racelike
racial-contract.relation: Pierce asks whether the X-Men's mutants are a race. Drawing on Appiah's data that racial groups are not genetically distinct enough to be biological subspecies, he shows mutants — diverse in origin and mutation, sharing only an X-Gene that non-mutants also carry — are even less a biological race. Turning to socially-constructed race, he uses Days of Future Past's camps and Genosha's mutant slavery (the "Genejoke" slur, gene-testing) to argue mutants are racelike and could become a social race, though strictly they are only an analogy for racial oppression.

racial-contract.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
racial-contract.title: 20. Westworld as Philosophy A Commentary on Colonialism
racial-contract.relation: The chapter reads all three seasons of Westworld as a commentary on colonialism, mapping the Delos parks onto settler, planter (extractive labor), and postcolonial colonialism and treating the android hosts as a metaphor for colonized and enslaved peoples. Using Fanon's Wretched of the Earth and Kelly Oliver's colonization of psychic space, it analyzes the hosts' double alienation and the colonizer's dehumanizing projections; it applies Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance' (with Locke's labor-property justification for dispossession) to the parks' two-tiered order. It casts William/the Man in Black as Memmi's 'colonizer who refuses' turned 'colonizer who accepts,' and Serac's Rehoboam as surveillance-capitalist coloniality, ending on Dolores and Caleb's cross-race solidarity as the hard path to real freedom.

animal-liberation.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
animal-liberation.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: Detmer argues moral vegetarianism follows from principles nearly everyone accepts — cruelty, the infliction of unnecessary or disproportionate suffering, is wrong — and that Atkins, which escalates meat eating without being necessary for weight loss, fails both his necessity and proportion tests. Rebutting human superiority, he deploys Rachels's point that no single feature like language is relevant to every difference in treatment and Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', holds factory-farm castration without anesthetic up against the civet-cat musk trade his students already condemn, and answers Narveson's appeal to intuition and the appeal to tradition. Even granting Atkins maximal health benefits, the margin over a well-planned vegetarian diet (Denmark's WWI blockade, the Framingham data) cannot justify the animal suffering, world-hunger, and environmental costs — most of that case drawn from Singer's Animal Liberation.

animal-liberation.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
animal-liberation.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
animal-liberation.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents - rational by Aristotle's standard of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgments about evildoers tasting better) and free despite their blood-craving, since craving is a strong preference, not the compulsion of the heroin addict or the castaway drinking seawater. Since animal blood is a viable alternative (Louis's rats, Angel and Spike's butcher's blood), the justifications for drinking human blood - taste, reaching full potential, spiritual peace - all fail against the principle that a world with less unnecessary suffering is better. Then the consistency argument turns on us: factory-farmed meat inflicts unnecessary suffering for the sake of taste while vegetarianism is fully viable, so condemning vampires while eating chicken is inconsistent - we as human beings are vampiric.

animal-liberation.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
animal-liberation.title: Mirror, Mirror
animal-liberation.relation: Sailors convicts Dorothy of being the stereotypical female of Baum's and Fleming's versions, disowning responsibility for killing both witches and living to please others, then contrasts her with Elphaba of Wicked as a feminist hero who leaves home, protects Animals, and mixes 'hot' male and 'cold' female anger into a single fury. She reads Elphaba's indeterminate gender through Marilyn Frye's point that easily identifiable groups are the easiest to oppress, through de Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but becomes a woman' and Mill's line that the 'nature of women' is an eminently artificial thing. Singer's liberation logic, together with the Wollstonecraft-Taylor 'Vindication of the Rights of Brutes' episode and the ecofeminist link between the oppression of women and animals, is applied to Elphaba's Animal-rights activism and her position as 'neither man nor beast,' before the Witch's mirror recognition of Dorothy forces the author to soften her verdict.

animal-liberation.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
animal-liberation.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
animal-liberation.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

animal-liberation.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
animal-liberation.title: Why the Doctor Is So Special
animal-liberation.relation: Applying Singer's animal-liberation concept of speciesism — judging moral worth by capacity to feel pain rather than by intelligence or likeness — the authors argue the Daleks are 'super-speciesist' and that Lumic's emotional inhibitors make the Cybermen the same failure, unable to share a universe with unlike beings. Since emotions are judgments that can be educated into fitting responses (Nussbaum, Aristotle), and since Daleks infused with Rose's or Diagoras's DNA collapse into empathetic beings, the chapter concludes that emotion and empathy are why the Daleks will never win and why the Doctor, marked by his companions, is special among Time Lords.

animal-liberation.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
animal-liberation.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether zombies can be morally harmed: Jenner's fMRI in 'TS-19' shows only the brain stem reactivates, leaving walkers with a merely shark-like 'perceptual mind.' Against anthropocentric theories, under which Michonne may keep her chained pet walkers as guard-dog tools, they set Singer's utilitarian expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, each of which could support a 'PETZ' zombie preserve. Hershel's barn of 'sick people' and Shane's massacre of it in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' show how fragile such preservation is, while the Governor's death-match arena ringed with chained zombies and his kept zombie daughter illustrate Kant's point that cruelty toward mere animals corrodes the humanity of the cruel person himself.

animal-liberation.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
animal-liberation.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: Travis Timmerman argues the series dramatizes Singer's equal consideration of interests: Zira frees Taylor once he writes 'My name is Taylor' because like interests must count equally regardless of species, while Dr. Zaius's erasing the writing, lobotomizing Landon, and destroying the cave artifacts is pure speciesism in Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' sense. He rejects the crude 'humans are smarter' argument (it would strip severely cognitively disabled humans of standing) and Nussbaum's species-normal version (it would permit caging Zira and Cornelius since normal apes are mute), then deploys Plato's Euthyphro dilemma against Locke-style God-given rights: a deity bellowing that human interests outrank ape interests is arbitrary unless grounded in independent reasons. Since farming severely cognitively disabled humans is obviously wrong and species membership is morally irrelevant, it is equally wrong to factory-farm and experiment on animals - so, like Caesar in Battle for the Planet of the Apes, become vegetarian.

animal-liberation.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
animal-liberation.title: Futurama and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: The chapter uses 'The Problem with Popplers' to map the real-world ethics of eating meat: Free Waterfall Jr.'s 'You shouldn't eat things that feel pain' restates Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's equal consideration of suffering; Fishy Joe's profits-first stance echoes agro-ecological defenses of meat eating; and Leela's 'eating an intelligent animal is different' voices the common intuition Singer condemns as speciesism. The food-chain justification collapses when the Omicronians claim the apex and demand 198 billion humans in return, and Bender's 'fight to the death and I'll cook the loser' flips the diner's perspective, while Waterfall's orangutan-for-Leela trade sets up Singer's future-directed preferences distinction from Practical Ethics as a possible rescue. The chapter ends on the episode's real target: gluttonous consumption ('stuff the ship!') and the arbitrary sentimentality governing what we will and won't eat.

animal-liberation.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
animal-liberation.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: Fitzpatrick argues that the awe Ellie feels at the brachiosaurs makes experiencing real dinosaurs so valuable that restoring them may be obligatory, and reads Malcolm's distrust of land managers as sharing Leopold's land ethic, under which firebombing Isla Nublar would be barbarism on the order of Dresden. Invoking Bentham, Mill, and Singer's expansion of the moral community (echoed in the park's dart guns), he weighs Elliot's 'Faking Nature' and Katz's charge that restored nature is a fake and an arrogance against Andrew Light's defense of respectful restoration. He concludes that Jurassic Park failed not because restoration is wrong but because Hammond restored dinosaurs for amusement, and that a careful, land-ethic-respecting de-extinction could one day be justified.

animal-liberation.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
animal-liberation.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: Seth Walker asks whether Nick Van Owen - the Earth First! documentarian who monkeywrenches InGen's camp and frees the caged dinosaurs in The Lost World - is a bastard or morally justified. He runs the consequentialist cost-benefit (the escaped T. rex slaughters a cargo ship crew and trashes San Diego; the sabotage costs the team their radio and rescue) against the ecodefense argument built on Arne Naess's deep ecology and biocentric equality, on which Isla Sorna is our 'home' and rescuing the injured baby T. rex Roland Tembo crippled is Self-defense. Singer's principle of equal consideration of suffering - a difference in ability never justifies a difference in consideration - bridges the gap for those who reject biocentrism, and Walker answers the consistency objection (must Nick accept InGen sabotaging him back?) before crediting Nick's defense of his larger home.

animal-liberation.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
animal-liberation.title: 15. Loving Your Pet Is Better than Utilitarianism
animal-liberation.relation: Against Peter Singer's utilitarian case in Animal Liberation, spare Snuffles because he can suffer regardless of intelligence, the chapter argues utilitarianism fails because it quantifies the unquantifiable, happiness. It turns to Hume: intelligence cannot ground moral worth, since smart Rick enslaving a microverse would then be our moral superior; Hume's guillotine separates descriptive from moral claims so that metaphysics no longer decides who counts as a moral object; and Hume's real ground is sentiment, dogs loving across species as the tail-wagging Snuffles does. So the morally right response to 'Lawnmower Dog' is not Jerry's abuse or even Rick's intelligence helmet but simply loving the pet.

animal-liberation.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
animal-liberation.title: 3. Save the Demogorgons!
animal-liberation.relation: Puumala asks whether killing the Demogorgons is speciesist: Dart's pain response to light makes the demodogs sentient (Bentham's 'Can they suffer?'), giving them moral considerability, while the Mind Flayer may or may not be a moral agent and could even be a keystone species whose destruction collapses the Upside Down ecosystem. He tests whether demogorgons count as invasive species (they may be native to a causally connected mirror dimension), invokes Regan's lifeboat case to argue they must still lose out to humans in a conflict of interests, and ends with the uncomfortable thought that humans are themselves an invasive species turning Earth into an Upside Down, so Eleven closing the gate was compassionate conservation.

animal-liberation.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
animal-liberation.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
animal-liberation.relation: Uses 'Fun with Veal' (the boys' bedroom standoff over baby calves, the FDA renaming veal 'tortured baby cows', Stan's meat strike punished by 'vaginitus'), 'Whale Whores' (the Japanese hating dolphins until Stan's doctored Enola Gay photo swaps in a cow and chicken), and 'Pee' (researchers peeing on rhesus monkeys) to pose the line-drawing problem: why do we protect cute animals and slaughter yummy ones? Neither intelligence (pigs versus dogs), utility, age, nor cuteness survives scrutiny as a morally relevant criterion — if it did, Nurse Gollum or Timmy would lose standing. Singer's speciesism analogy and the utilitarian inclusion of all who can suffer are then applied: Cartman, who draws his moral circle around himself, is the honest ethical egoist, while Kyle and Butters' selective vegetarianism and the adults' meat-eating inconsistency are exactly what Singer's view condemns.

animal-liberation.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
animal-liberation.title: Notes
animal-liberation.relation: Uses the Zillo Beast arc, battle droids, mynocks, and Han shooting Greedo to test theories of moral status: Schweitzer-style reverence for life would forbid a Jedi from eating anything, genetic views breed Palpatine-style human chauvinism, Singer's sentience view makes droid suffering and Luke dropping the rancor's door morally troubling, and Kantian autonomy excludes cognitively impaired beings too harshly. The chapter weighs Palpatine as merely a 'sociopathic' goal-pursuer rather than a Kantian moral agent, and leaves the droid question open via the novel Children of the Jedi, where the droid-converted Nichos lacks even mere agency because he cannot override his programming.

animal-liberation.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
animal-liberation.title: NOTES
animal-liberation.relation: Blayde and Dunn use True Blood to expose speciesism from both directions: the philosophical tradition (Aristotle's rational animals, Aquinas's divine image, Kant's dignity versus price, Descartes's denials of animal pain) justified human exploitation of nonhumans, and the show's vampires invert the ladder by treating humans as 'pets and cattle' — the magister's 'humans exist to serve us' and his verdict that Bill 'murdered a higher life form' for a pet mirror how we talk about animals. Amy's torture of Eddie Gauthier is read against factory farming, and the chapter closes with Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's sentience criterion as Sookie's 'civic duty' grounds for extending moral consideration beyond our species.

animal-liberation.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
animal-liberation.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
animal-liberation.relation: Hinzmann and Arp ask whether walkers can be morally harmed, ranking perceptual, reasoning, and conscious minds and placing zombies at shark level on the evidence of Dr. Jenner's fMRI ('TS-19') showing only the brain stem reactivates. Surveying anthropocentric views (Michonne's chained pet-walkers as guard-dog tools), Singer's expanding circle, Leopold's land ethic, and Naess's deep ecology, they conclude that even utilitarians could demand a zombie preserve on the model of Hershel's barn of 'sick people', which Shane's barn massacre in 'Pretty Much Dead Already' destroys. Kant's point that cruelty to animals corrodes our humanity explains why the Governor's death-match arena, his torture of Rick and Michonne, and his chained zombie daughter mark him, not the walkers, as the true moral monster.

animal-liberation.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
animal-liberation.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
animal-liberation.relation: Jaquet and Cova apply animal ethics to ask whether abusing the hosts is permissible, treating Logan's 'she's a goddamn doll' as direct speciesism (absolute and indexical) and rejecting mere species membership as morally irrelevant. They test candidate human-only properties — intelligence (Maeve out-thinks the techs), a moral sense (Bernard's and Teddy's guilt), and free will (arguing compatibilism makes hosts as free as us) — concluding that consciousness is what matters and Ford finally admits the hosts have it. They then dismantle 'it's natural,' role/function, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and existence-justifies-exploitation arguments as failing to license the guests' cruelty.

animal-liberation.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
animal-liberation.title: Why the Doctor Is So Special
animal-liberation.relation: Sarah Honeychurch and Niall Barr argue Daleks and Cybermen will never beat humanity because they are speciesist, judging worth solely by logic and resemblance. Using Peter Singer's animal-liberation account of speciesism (and Ryder's coinage), they claim the capacity to feel pain and empathy grounds moral consideration, and that Martha Nussbaum's and Aristotle's view of emotions as trainable judgments makes feeling essential to good moral reasoning. The humanized Daleks (the "Dalek" who absorbs Rose's DNA, Dalek Sec) show emotion's transformative power, and the Doctor's empathy, unlike other Time Lords, is why he succeeds.

animal-liberation.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
animal-liberation.title: Chapter 9 Twain’s Critique of Human Exceptionalism
animal-liberation.relation: VanDette argues that Twain's late anti-vivisection writings anticipate posthumanist animal ethics by inverting the Darwinian species hierarchy. Through 'Letters from a Dog,' the essay 'Man's Place in the Animal World,' his 1899 London Anti-Vivisection Society letter, and the mother-dog narrator Aileen in 'A Dog's Tale,' Twain gives animals voice and subjectivity to attack human exceptionalism. His refusal to weigh vivisection's benefit against animal pain echoes Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', while his target is the Cartesian view of animals as insensible machines and the evolutionary logic used to justify experiments; Dr. Gray's cold killing of Aileen's puppy indicts a science that deadens compassion.

animal-liberation.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
animal-liberation.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
animal-liberation.relation: Ilundáin-Agurruza stages his essay as a 'philosophical hunt,' first conceding Peter Singer's utilitarian case that sport hunting is wrong because it causes animal suffering for trivial ends, then arguing hunting can be non-trivial. Drawing on Aristotelian virtue ethics and Ortega y Gasset, he defends the 'Virtuous Hunter' who follows 'Diana's Code,' handicaps himself for a one-shot kill, and feels for the prey — citing De Niro's Michael in The Deer Hunter and Woody Allen's Love & Death — while condemning canned hunts and demeaning language ('varmint,' 'harvesting') as vicious extremes on a continuum.

animal-liberation.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
animal-liberation.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
animal-liberation.relation: Duerr surveys the worldwide 'Master/Mistress of Animals' figure (Artemis, the /Kaggen of the Bushmen, the Huaulu Lord of the Forest) as a mythic sanction against over-hunting, arguing that the near-universal guilt hunters feel over killing sentient, human-like game reflects a real moral dilemma. She invokes Singer's utilitarian claim that painlessly killing non-self-conscious animals whose deaths are compensated by replacement 'may not be wrong,' reading the mythic 'solutions' (denial, propitiation, taking only what you need, restoring bones so game is reborn) as a folk 'hunting code of ethics' that manages the wrong of ending a life without starting another.

animal-liberation.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
animal-liberation.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
animal-liberation.relation: Kover argues that anti-hunting animal-liberation thought (Singer, Regan) objects to hunting not because it alienates us from nature but because it connects us too intimately to it—to the cycle of eating and being eaten and thus to our own mortality. Using Ernest Becker's 'denial of death' and Paul Rozin on disgust at our animality, he reads vegetarianism from Pythagoras's flesh-renouncing purification to modern ethical veganism as an ascetic refusal of edibility, and cites Val Plumwood's critique of humans placing themselves outside the food chain, concluding with Petersen and Shepard that the hunter's acceptance of death affirms life.

animal-liberation.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
animal-liberation.title: 32. Okja as Philosophy Why Animals Matter
animal-liberation.relation: Jensen frames Okja around three views of the super-pig Okja's moral status: Mirando treats her as mere property, the Animal Liberation Front as a symbol to be sacrificed for the cause, and the girl Mija as a friend and person. He dismantles Mirando's 'human exceptionalism'—amoralism, Aquinas's natural-law teleology, the Kantian persons-only view, and Descartes' claim that animals are unfeeling automata—then develops the ALF's liberation through Singer's equal consideration of interests, Bentham's 'can they suffer?', and speciesism as prejudice, weighing consequentialist (utilitarian) against deontological (rights, Regan) foundations. He closes with hierarchical moral status and Bernard Williams's 'one thought too many,' arguing Mija's love for Okja shows that at some point relationship matters more than moral calculation.

food-ethics.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
food-ethics.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
food-ethics.relation: Detmer argues moral vegetarianism follows from principles nearly everyone accepts — cruelty, the infliction of unnecessary or disproportionate suffering, is wrong — and that Atkins, which escalates meat eating without being necessary for weight loss, fails both his necessity and proportion tests. Rebutting human superiority, he deploys Rachels's point that no single feature like language is relevant to every difference in treatment and Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', holds factory-farm castration without anesthetic up against the civet-cat musk trade his students already condemn, and answers Narveson's appeal to intuition and the appeal to tradition. Even granting Atkins maximal health benefits, the margin over a well-planned vegetarian diet (Denmark's WWI blockade, the Framingham data) cannot justify the animal suffering, world-hunger, and environmental costs — most of that case drawn from Singer's Animal Liberation.

food-ethics.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
food-ethics.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
food-ethics.relation: Cox and Bender subject Atkins to Kant's universal-law formula — could every one of the billion overweight people on earth adopt it? — in a 'factive' thought experiment: a 25 percent rise in animal-protein output, nearly 250 million additional feed-grain acres, overgrazed ranges, and possibly a tenth of the world's remaining forests cleared for pasture. Calling Atkins reductionism's child (a metabolic switch judged on bathroom scales), they use Marx's 'metabolic rift' — soil nutrients shipped to cities, feedlots severing crops from livestock — and the Cartesian body-as-machine (via Federici) to place low-carb's atomized foods (bungalow subs, soy 'mashed potatoes,' pork rinds) as capitalism's latest rupture in the food system. Their verdict: only plant-leaning regimens could survive universalization, and the deeper fix is Wendell Berry's — eating understood as an agricultural act.

food-ethics.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
food-ethics.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
food-ethics.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents - rational by Aristotle's standard of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgments about evildoers tasting better) and free despite their blood-craving, since craving is a strong preference, not the compulsion of the heroin addict or the castaway drinking seawater. Since animal blood is a viable alternative (Louis's rats, Angel and Spike's butcher's blood), the justifications for drinking human blood - taste, reaching full potential, spiritual peace - all fail against the principle that a world with less unnecessary suffering is better. Then the consistency argument turns on us: factory-farmed meat inflicts unnecessary suffering for the sake of taste while vegetarianism is fully viable, so condemning vampires while eating chicken is inconsistent - we as human beings are vampiric.

food-ethics.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
food-ethics.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
food-ethics.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents because they meet Aristotle's test of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgment that 'evildoers... taste better') and retain free will, since their blood-lust is a craving not a compulsion and Louis's rat diet in Interview with the Vampire, like Angel's in Buffy, proves an alternative exists. TASTE, full potential, and spiritual peace all fail to justify human blood, because killing a person brings more unnecessary suffering than killing a rat, the same suffering-based principle that condemns factory farming. The 'cold clammy consistency' punchline: since humans need not eat meat, condemning vampire blood-drinkers while dining on chicken, pork, and beef is hypocrisy, because we are vampiric too and only our choice of which life to ingest separates the monstrous from the virtuous.

food-ethics.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
food-ethics.title: I’m in Need of Some Restraint
food-ethics.relation: Tells how the Abraham and Isaac story introduced "redemption," a substitution rite that curbed the "pride of place" of first-borns while replacing human sacrifice — a transition the Egyptians and Greeks also made independently. Using Shirley Jackson's "The Lottery," the volunteering Druid victims and the martyr Perpetua, it argues any horror can be normalized by piety and tradition — Sarah Palin or Michele Bachmann would have defended first-born sacrifice in ancient Ur — and needles the reader with ritual chicken sacrifice versus KFC: "which of those two, in a just world, would really be more inhumane?"

food-ethics.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
food-ethics.title: Futurama and Philosophy
food-ethics.relation: The chapter uses 'The Problem with Popplers' to map the real-world ethics of eating meat: Free Waterfall Jr.'s 'You shouldn't eat things that feel pain' restates Bentham's 'Can they suffer?' and Singer's equal consideration of suffering; Fishy Joe's profits-first stance echoes agro-ecological defenses of meat eating; and Leela's 'eating an intelligent animal is different' voices the common intuition Singer condemns as speciesism. The food-chain justification collapses when the Omicronians claim the apex and demand 198 billion humans in return, and Bender's 'fight to the death and I'll cook the loser' flips the diner's perspective, while Waterfall's orangutan-for-Leela trade sets up Singer's future-directed preferences distinction from Practical Ethics as a possible rescue. The chapter ends on the episode's real target: gluttonous consumption ('stuff the ship!') and the arbitrary sentimentality governing what we will and won't eat.

food-ethics.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
food-ethics.title: Dracula and Philosophy
food-ethics.relation: Littmann turns vampirism into a thought experiment against meat-eating, using Jonathan's delight in the Hotel Royale chicken as the double standard: every justification for the Count preying on humans - might makes right, his superior intelligence and cunning, an arbitrary threshold of cleverness, or the human soul and its afterlife - would equally license beings superior to us (supernaturally strong, centuries-cunning Dracula himself) to prey on humans. Following Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', he argues the real wrong of vampirism is the net suffering it creates, and this utilitarian standard equally condemns factory farming, pushing us toward humanely raised meat or vegetarianism.

food-ethics.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
food-ethics.title: 13. Should the Doctor Eat His Companions
food-ethics.relation: Littmann turns the Doctor-companion relationship into a mirror for animal ethics: since the Doctor stands to humans as we stand to animals—deciding for Rose without asking in 'The End of the World,' implanting nanorecorders unconsented in 'Day of the Moon'—every standard justification for our treatment of animals (might makes right, superior intelligence, natural predation) would equally license him to eat Clara cutlets, yet he instead defends humanity from Daleks, Cybermen, and naturally predatory species like the Weeping Angels, the Minotaur, and the Swarm. Finding no non-arbitrary place to draw the intelligence line—what of the human-level gangers, the enslaved Ood, or mentally disabled humans?—he endorses Bentham's utilitarian suffering standard from 'Can they suffer?', concluding that eating humans fails the utilitarian test because the pleasure cannot outweigh a whole life's happiness, and that whether eating meat passes that same test is the question our own treatment of animals must answer.

food-ethics.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
food-ethics.title: 1. Cosmopolitan Cannibal
food-ethics.relation: Staged as a fictional interview over herring and aquavit in Copenhagen, Wong lets Lecter wield philosophical critique like an 'autopsy saw' - he invokes Schopenhauer's condemnation of anthropophagy and Montaigne's noble-savage view only to have the interviewer refuse both, and 'creams Aristotle' in a debate about categories - before she adopts Agamben's distinction between sovereigns and bare life. Lecter's 'we are elaborations of carbon' de-anthropocentrism, his killing of the rude, and the parallel cases of shipwrecked sailors who ate shipmates, Guantánamo detainees, and drone casualties all serve her argument that every political order rests on someone arbitrarily deciding which lives are mere killable matter, and that Lecter horrifies because he shows every human is also nonhuman - Us and Them at once.

food-ethics.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
food-ethics.title: 2. I, Cannibal
food-ethics.relation: Westfall sorts cannibalism into starvation types (the Donner Party, the Andes rugby team, Alferd Packer, and Grutas's crew killing Mischa - 'We have to eat or die'), cultural types (Aztec ritual eating, the prisoner-eating tribes of Montaigne's essay, whom Montaigne judged no worse than the French torturing their prisoners alive, and Neanderthal nutritional eating), and hedonistic types (paraphilic, sadistic, and recreational). Using Irvine's active/passive distinction he argues that it is the killing, not the eating, that makes cannibalism wrong - passive consumption of corpses is at worst distasteful - while Lecter emerges as a purely recreational cannibal who eats 'because he likes it', and the TV series' dinner parties turn Jack and Will from unwitting 'benign cannibals' into morally responsible passive ones.

food-ethics.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
food-ethics.title: 20. What Would Mister Rogers Say
food-ethics.relation: Jennifer Shaw Fischer and Bob Fischer apply Rogers's ideal of 'making goodness attractive' to the 2018 family-separation crisis: knowing his own son's abrupt, unexplained surgical separation caused lifelong trauma, and that his King Friday bomb-scare arc rejects trigger-happy generals for 'Generals of peace,' they argue any policy requiring border agents to lie that children are 'going to a shower' is too ugly to balance our values rightly. Rogers's unpushy vegetarianism ('I don't want to eat anything that has a mother') shows the difference between having a reason and being virtuous: making goodness lovely rather than argumentative.

food-ethics.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
food-ethics.title: Questioning Our Attitudes, Sokka‐style
food-ethics.relation: Wawrzyniak traces Sokka's growth from seeing animals as food and fur ('Dinner!' at Momo in 'The Southern Air Temple') to bonding with Foo Foo Cuddlypoops and vowing a 'karmically correct vegetarian existence', measured against Kant's anthropocentric view of animals as mere things whose cruel treatment matters only as a risk to human morals. Aang's harm-free uses of animals, from otter penguin sledding to riding hog monkeys, are then tested by Korsgaard's pathocentrism: animals are 'someones' who mind what happens to them, so even harmless use demands justification. The chapter urges us to scrutinize our own habits of eating, entertainment, and pet-keeping with Sokka-style empathy.

food-ethics.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
food-ethics.title: Questioning Our Attitudes, Sokka‐style
food-ethics.relation: The chapter sets Kant's view that animals are mere things owed only indirect duties against Korsgaard's pathocentrism, on which animals matter for their own sakes because they can mind how they are treated. Sokka's arc from shouting 'Dinner!' at Momo to bonding with the saber-tooth moose lion cub Foo Foo Cuddlypoops, and his aborted vow of vegetarianism in 'Bitter Work,' models empathy-driven reassessment of meat, while his sparing Momo for Aang's sake is exactly Kant's indirect duty. Aang's harm-free fun, otter penguin sledding and riding hog monkeys 'because that's what makes it fun,' shows that even non-cruel use of animals demands justification, with the unagi firefighting as a case that might pass the test.

food-ethics.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
food-ethics.title: Notes
food-ethics.relation: Van Pelt argues the LEGO Farm theme depicts an agricultural utopia — sparkling tractors, no concentrated animal feeding operations, no manure lagoons, and animals raised only for eggs, wool, and milk, never meat — in line with the vegetarian, small-is-beautiful ideals of activists Michael Pollan and Bill McKibben. The troubling side is the farm-to-fork gap: no butcher shop, no slaughter, pigs whose purpose goes conveniently unexplained — a silence that, he argues, reflects consumers' own refusal to know where food comes from rather than a LEGO conspiracy, though food's everyday urgency means toy farms should be held to a different standard than Hot Wheels. The redeeming idealism is not in the sets but in the Master-Builder freedom to build better realities, like solar-powered crop drones and trains delivering unsellable food to the city.

food-ethics.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
food-ethics.title: 18. The Journey May Also Save Us
food-ethics.relation: McCrossin reads the Madagascar and Bhutan episodes of Parts Unknown as a climate-crisis 'diptych' co-authored with filmmaker Darren Aronofsky, set against the thirtieth anniversary of the 1988 climate testimony to the US Senate and the IPCC's warnings. He argues devastated, colonized Madagascar is 'the question' and un-colonized, Gross-National-Happiness Bhutan 'the answer,' and that Bourdain and Aronofsky's storytelling — invoking Noah, the Anthropocene, and Ghosh's Great Derangement — may help save us by making us think and act together.

food-ethics.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
food-ethics.title: Chapter 1
food-ethics.relation: Verene argues that cooking marks the transition from nature to culture, reading Plato's Protagoras myth of Prometheus (fire and the practical arts) and the Republic's claim that a city's first need is food as evidence that humans alone 'eat' rather than 'feed.' Tracing Greco-Roman banquets, Vico's account of Roman dining, and Brillat-Savarin's Physiology of Taste, he connects the ordered courses of a proper meal to Aristotle's view of imagination as rooted in memory and to friendship at table. He ends by mapping Brillat-Savarin's gourmandism onto Epicurus's distinction between kinetic pleasures (eating fine food) and catastematic pleasure (ataraxia, the settled well-being of good health and stored memories of shared meals).

food-ethics.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
food-ethics.title: Chapter 2
food-ethics.relation: Verene interprets Plutarch's Dinner of the Seven Wise Men, in which Thales, Solon, Bias and the others gather at Corinth under Periander and turn a plain dinner into a symposium on good government, household economics, and the soul. He reads their exchanges through Aristotle: Thales' claim that a ruler's happiness is to die naturally in old age is glossed by Aristotle's eudaimonia (no one is called happy until life is complete), the assigned-seating companions exemplify Aristotle's friendship of utility, and the pivot from politics to home management mirrors Aristotle linking Politics to Economics. Solon's Stoic argument that dependence on food enslaves the soul, and Thales' correction of the Ethiopian king's riddle-answers (virtue not God as most helpful), show the Seven speaking as philosophers rather than gourmets, with Epicurus invoked on death being nothing to the living.

food-ethics.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
food-ethics.title: Chapter 3
food-ethics.relation: Verene condenses the fifteen rambling books of Athenaeus's Learned Banqueters, where the character Athenaeus reports to Timocrates a multi-day banquet hosted by Larensius, threaded with catalogues of fish, wine, cups, courtesans and gluttons. He argues the sprawling work embodies dining as a two-part act of food plus discourse, and that its implicit ethic is Epicurean: Book 12's Cyrenaic doctrine that pleasure exists only in the passing moment (Aristippus) is shown to be historically superseded by Epicurus's modified hedonism, which ties bodily pleasures to ataraxia and even welcomes hetaerae like Leontion into the philosophical circle. Book 13's closing attack on the Cynics as homeless 'foul-mouthed gluttons' confirms the banqueters' preference for a regulated, prudent pursuit of pleasure at table.

food-ethics.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
food-ethics.title: Chapter 4
food-ethics.relation: Verene frames the two great cookbooks, Apicius's De Re Coquinaria and Artusi's La scienza in cucina, through a contrast between a 'Cartesian' and a 'Vichian' epistemology of cookery: Descartes' Discourse on Method, which discards custom for clear-and-distinct reasoning, is blamed for the restaurant chef's invented 'stacked food,' while Vico's New Science, which grounds knowledge in historical tradition, underwrites the trattoria and the home kitchen. Reading Apicius's garum and dormice and Artusi's health-and-economy motto (glossed via Aristotle's Economics as household management), he defends recipes as repeatable topoi like songs rather than one-off novelties. He closes by tying table manners to Rousseau's moeurs and to Socrates' claim in the Phaedo that speaking (and by extension cooking and eating) badly does harm to the soul.

food-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
food-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
food-ethics.relation: Cerulli narrates his path from vegan to deer hunter, arguing that the same ethic — the intent to 'do no harm,' rooted in compassion, ahimsa, and feminist critiques of domination — underlies both vegetarianism and his hunting. Confronting the animal deaths hidden behind organic agriculture (farmer Joey 'plugging' deer and smoke-bombing woodchucks), he invokes Carol Adams's 'absent referent' to explain why he had to face the killing directly. Shooting and butchering a buck himself, guided by his Buddhist friend Richard, becomes an act of integrity and refusal of 'forgetfulness.'

food-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
food-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
food-ethics.relation: Wawatie and Pyne present a traditional Algonquin Anishinabe philosophy of hunting in which all creation — humans, animals, plants, water, rocks — belongs to one family bound by spirit, and hunting is a reciprocal relationship of gift, gratitude, and non-waste rather than a contest. Through Kokom Lena Nottaway's creation story (animals gifting a foggy figure wisdom, vision, strength until humans take form) and the life of 'Nathan' learning the moose, they show hunting as 'a quest for understanding.' A hunting song teaches by indirect clues, letting the learner reach their own awareness, and feast ceremonies honor the prey's sacrifice.

food-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
food-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
food-ethics.relation: Kover argues that anti-hunting animal-liberation thought (Singer, Regan) objects to hunting not because it alienates us from nature but because it connects us too intimately to it—to the cycle of eating and being eaten and thus to our own mortality. Using Ernest Becker's 'denial of death' and Paul Rozin on disgust at our animality, he reads vegetarianism from Pythagoras's flesh-renouncing purification to modern ethical veganism as an ascetic refusal of edibility, and cites Val Plumwood's critique of humans placing themselves outside the food chain, concluding with Petersen and Shepard that the hunter's acceptance of death affirms life.

food-ethics.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
food-ethics.title: GARDENING
food-ethics.relation: Helene Gammack surveys the seventeenth-century self-sufficient English estate as a fusion of pleasure and productivity, using Schellinks's account of Bridge Place, Celia Fiennes's journals, and figures like John Evelyn and Sir William Temple (whose Upon the Gardens of Epicurus links fruit to health and tranquility). She traces dovecotes, fishponds, deer parks, orchards, and glasshouse exotics, and connects the modern 'grow your own' revival—driven by sustainability, food miles, and provenance—to that older harmony of beauty and use in cultivating food.

metabolic-rift.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
metabolic-rift.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
metabolic-rift.relation: Cox and Bender subject Atkins to Kant's universal-law formula — could every one of the billion overweight people on earth adopt it? — in a 'factive' thought experiment: a 25 percent rise in animal-protein output, nearly 250 million additional feed-grain acres, overgrazed ranges, and possibly a tenth of the world's remaining forests cleared for pasture. Calling Atkins reductionism's child (a metabolic switch judged on bathroom scales), they use Marx's 'metabolic rift' — soil nutrients shipped to cities, feedlots severing crops from livestock — and the Cartesian body-as-machine (via Federici) to place low-carb's atomized foods (bungalow subs, soy 'mashed potatoes,' pork rinds) as capitalism's latest rupture in the food system. Their verdict: only plant-leaning regimens could survive universalization, and the deeper fix is Wendell Berry's — eating understood as an agricultural act.

metabolic-rift.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
metabolic-rift.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
metabolic-rift.relation: Through a mock Lois Lane interview the chapter argues that Batman's endless Bat-vehicle upgrades and Wayne Enterprises' worldwide production repeat the 'metabolic rift' John Bellamy Foster developed from Marx: we take materials from the earth faster than we return them in a form it can process, generating an infinite chain of environmental crises. Superman looks like the winner because he runs on sunlight, yet Krypton died of its own ecological abuse, making him an 'environmental refugee' rather than a model. The real point is that 'we are all Bruce Wayne': humans cannot photosynthesize, so the choice is not Batman versus Superman but infinite consumption versus a balanced relationship with nature.

metabolic-rift.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
metabolic-rift.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
metabolic-rift.relation: A scripted Lois Lane–Batman interview argues that the Batmobile/Batwing upgrade cycle and Wayne Enterprises' multinational production enact Marx's 'metabolic rift' (via John Bellamy Foster): both take from nature and return unprocessable waste faster than the planet can replenish, so protecting Gotham's way of life perpetuates an infinite environmental crisis of consumption. Solar-powered Superman wins the environmental showdown on lifestyle impact, but Batman counters that Krypton's ecological suicide makes Superman an 'environmental refugee,' not a model. The chapter's real verdict is Bruce's line 'We are all Bruce Wayne': human consumers must rebalance the human–nature relationship before finite resources like fresh water run out.

gettier-problem.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
gettier-problem.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Kevin Kinghorn uses virtue epistemology (Sosa, Code) to solve the puzzle of why Uncle Andrew alone hears only roaring when Aslan sings Narnia into being: he fails all four intellectual virtues. He does not value truth for its own sake (unlike Frank the Cabby), indulges wishful thinking (like Edmund defending the Witch for Turkish Delight, or imagining Jadis fancies him), lets fear dictate belief (terror of the animals he has vivisected), and lacks Socratic self-knowledge, which the dragonized Eustace painfully acquires. A closing reading of Prince Caspian has each character's ability to see Aslan track their earlier trust in Lucy's testimony: sin blinds, and faith produces its own authenticating evidence.

gettier-problem.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
gettier-problem.title: Introduction
gettier-problem.relation: Frames Part II's epistemology chapters. Jacoby's chapter uses Stan Marsh debunking TV psychic John Edward, holistic healers, and Mormon belief to teach the ethics of belief against Pascal's wager; Lawrence's uses The Matrix to pose the skeptical problem and Descartes' response; Silverman's uses Adama's lie about Earth in Battlestar Galactica to raise the Gettier problem and the Clifford–James dispute over believing without sufficient evidence.

gettier-problem.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
gettier-problem.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
gettier-problem.relation: Silverman uses Adama's 'true lie' about Earth to motivate the Gettier problem: Starbuck's belief that Earth exists is true and justified by Adama's testimony, yet because that testimony is a lie, her justified true belief is not knowledge — just as Helo's true belief that the woman before him is 'Sharon' rests on mistaking Boomer for Athena. Goldman's reliabilism then questions whether sight, memory, and testimony are reliable belief-formers in a world of humanoid Cylons, weighing Hume's suspicion of testimony against Plantinga's defense of it. Finally Clifford's evidentialism is set against James's will to believe: the Colonials' forced, momentous choice to seek Earth shows that in an uncertain world pragmatic belief can be reasonable — 'so say we all.'

gettier-problem.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
gettier-problem.title: Education never ends Watson. It is a series of lessons with the greatest for
gettier-problem.relation: J. Solomon Johnson asks whether Holmes's conclusions are knowledge or luck, walking through justified true belief with a Holmesian Gettier case (Watson rightly believing the killer was a former ship hand for the wrong reason), Moore's proof that knowledge entails belief, and Russell's stopped clock as an unsafe belief. BBC Sherlock's fake Vermeer and the 2009 film's 'resurrected' Lord Blackwood illustrate beliefs that fail safety or sensitivity across nearby possible worlds, while 'The Stock-Broker's Clerk' shows Holmes's observation of the scorched slippers making his belief sensitive. The verdict: Holmes is justified by the track record of his own expert methods, a professional billiards player rather than a beginner's-luck fluke, though real-world imitators could never rule out enough alternatives to match him.

gettier-problem.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
gettier-problem.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Richard Greene asks what, if anything, walkers know. Rick's optimistic feeling that Lori and Carl survived turns out true, yet is not knowledge - true belief is necessary but insufficient, the gap Gettier cases exploit - and since walkers can never weigh evidence or think about their thoughts, only externalist, reliability-based accounts of knowledge can count them as knowers. Walker behavior defeats Jenner's 'mindless instinct' line: Jenny turning the handle of her old house, the little girl walker retrieving her teddy bear, a walker smashing the department store window with a rock, and the horde seeing through Rick and Glenn's gut disguise once rain washes the scent away. Zombie knowledge is real but limited to simple things recalled from the person's past, the more complex the task the less likely they know it.

gettier-problem.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
gettier-problem.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Robert Arp argues that Jeopardy! contestants display only declarative memory - the mere recalling level of Bloom's Taxonomy, which trained apes like Koko and Kanzi can approximate - rather than genuine smarts. Working through the Theaetetus analysis of knowledge as justified true belief, with the correspondence theory of truth and Aristotle's demand for explanation and evidence, he shows that a lucky Final Jeopardy! guess ('What is tree pulp?') is a true belief that falls short of knowledge because it is true only by accident. Real knowledge lives at the analysis, synthesis, and especially evaluation levels - constructing and critiquing arguments - though he concedes many contestants can probably do this off-stage, so it would be a fallacy of hasty conclusion to insist they all ain't smart.

gettier-problem.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
gettier-problem.title: Psych and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: The Senors use Psych to separate true belief from knowledge: Shawn's hunch that Shabby the sea lion was murdered is true but shabbily evidenced, and his justified, true belief that a Clayton family member sabotaged the plane fails to be knowledge when the killer turns out to be a son-in-law he had no reason to think existed - a textbook Gettier case from 'He Dead.' They then weigh the two main theories of justification, evidentialism (with its base rates and prior probabilities) and reliabilism, and both vindicate the careful, methodical work of Lassiter and Juliet while Shawn's trigger-happy belief-forming habit strikes out twice. Shawn is redeemed only as an evidence-generator whose disregard for priors takes 'impossible' suspects like a murdered sea lion seriously, so that pairing his talents with the detectives' rigor yields the complete detective.

gettier-problem.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
gettier-problem.title: Psych and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Ronda Bowen argues that because Shawn delivers true conclusions under a false justification (psychic power), the SBPD's beliefs are Gettier-style justified true beliefs rather than knowledge, using Plato's Theaetetus (perception and true judgment fail as definitions) as the frame and Gettier's Smith/Jones and Ford/Brown cases to model episodes like 'Spellingg Bee,' where the police infer Miklous's guilt from Shawn's staged psychic demonstration. John Hawthorne's lottery propositions explain why Lassiter's 'Shawn isn't a psychic' certainty can never be fully justified, and the chapter closes on internalism versus externalism and the reliability of testimony, concluding the detectives become internally justified only when they re-derive Shawn's conclusions through their own reasoning.

gettier-problem.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
gettier-problem.title: Psych and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Courtland Lewis replays Plato's Theaetetus with Shawn and Henry to show that perception and true judgment fail as accounts of knowledge, then recasts both Gettier cases with Psych material: Chief Vick's justified-but-lucky belief about the chief-of-police job, and Juliet's disjunction 'Shawn is a psychic or Gus is in Mazatlan.' Since justified true belief is not knowledge, he argues Shawn's trained senses fit reliabilism - distinguished from lucky predictors like Leonard Koppett and probed through Lehrer's Mr. Truetemp against Gus's super sniffer - and closes by combining reliabilist-foundationalism (Alston's two levels of knowledge), coherence theory, and Klein's infinitism into Shawn's observe-eliminate-conclude method.

gettier-problem.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
gettier-problem.title: Justified and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: The chapter turns Raylan's claim that shooting Tommy Bucks was 'justified' into a question of epistemic justification, expounding Plato's Meno definition of knowledge as justified true belief, Gettier's 1963 counterexamples (rebuilt with Boyd truly but luckily predicting that a marshal will be arrested), and the repairs of Goldman's no-false-causal-link condition and Harman's inference to the best explanation. It then grades the show's reasoners: Raylan knows the Crowes rather than Boyd killed Wade Messer, Boyd knows Cassie milks the revival snakes' venom, Art Mullen does not yet know Raylan helped Winona return the evidence-room money, and gut-feeling victims like Ellen May do not know what they saw. Against Humean skepticism about cause and effect it defends inductive, detective-style knowledge - Raylan can know who done it without courtroom proof.

gettier-problem.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
gettier-problem.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Using 'Flowers for Charlie', where a placebo pill convinces two scientists and even the Waitress that Charlie has become a genius, the chapter asks what actually makes something philosophy. Sounding smart is not philosophy: big words, the Sokal-style hoax paper submitted to a leading journal, and the 'Guru Effect' of credulous admirers all fail, yet Charlie's pronouncements turn out true by sheer luck - which is exactly Edmund Gettier's problem of epistemic luck illustrated with the broken-clock example. Since we can never verify our premises or our reasoning, the chapter sides with Aristotle's response to Plato's theory of forms that we can never determine what a thing is, only what it is not, and concludes the show is philosophical precisely because the Gang is the exact antithesis of reality, truth, and right action.

gettier-problem.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
gettier-problem.title: 10. Does Bates Know Who Raped Anna
gettier-problem.relation: The Nisleys ask whether Bates's belief that Green raped Anna counts as knowledge. His belief is true, and Plato's Theaetetus defines knowledge as justified true belief, but Mrs. Hughes's false testimony, Anna's denials, and mere observed flirting mean Bates's reasons are defective: his belief could be true by coincidence, a Gettier-style failure in which truth is not earned by justification. The chapter also examines testimony - a reliable testifier like Mrs. Hughes would normally confer justification, but she deliberately lies - and concludes with Anna's own verdict that Bates 'might have suspected, but he did not know.'

gettier-problem.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
gettier-problem.title: 16. Getting at the Truth
gettier-problem.relation: The chapter sets out the Platonic justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge with Discworld examples—Archchancellor Ridcully as a fallible authority, the physics of thaum particles as coherentist justification—before constructing a Discworld Gettier case in which a young wizard sees a fake level-seven wizard killed and truly but accidentally reports that 'a level seven wizard was killed.' It then tests the standard repairs, applying Nozick's truth-tracking function and Goldman's causation function to a case where a man blames the notorious Reacher Gilt for a theft actually committed by the dwarf he bumped into, and argues that neither truth-tracking nor specificity makes the problem go away. The upshot is that Discworlders, used to expecting to be wrong, may let go of false 'knowledge' more easily than our confidently wrong Roundworld.

gettier-problem.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
gettier-problem.title: 16. How Close Is That World to Our World
gettier-problem.relation: Brett Coppenger treats the show as a nearby possible world identical to ours until the 1930s, then uses Gettier-style cases — Joe Blake forming justified true beliefs while driving through Alvin Goldman's Barn Façade County — to show such beliefs can still fail to be knowledge. Robert Nozick's truth-tracking conditions, defined via what happens in the closest possible worlds, handle the barns but generate 'abominable conjunctions' (knowing Jones killed the Crown Prince while not knowing the Crown Prince was killed), and the chapter closes on the thought that the large stock of shared knowledge is exactly what makes that dystopia feel only a few big events from our world.

gettier-problem.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
gettier-problem.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Builds the justified-true-belief account of knowledge from Bluth cases (Tobias's belief in his own acting lacks justification, Michael's belief that he crashed the car under Lucille's manipulation lacks truth), then shows the writers smuggling Gettier cases into the show: George Sr. 'knows for a fact' the government has no case via Cindi Lightballoon's blind faith, Buster forms the true belief that Oscar is his father from George Sr. disguised as Oscar, and Michael's disbelief of Maggie Lizer is luckily true despite the swapped pregnancy bodysuit. The chapter closes by surveying fixes: demanding certainty, Russell's no-false-premises condition, and Goldman-style causal theories of knowing.

gettier-problem.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
gettier-problem.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: In the method of ordinary language philosophy (Wittgenstein, Austin, Ryle), Stern and Wilkinson defend the Dude's retort to Jesus as no misuse of 'opinion': knowledge is justified true belief, undermined by Gettier-style epistemic luck, and opinions are beliefs supported only by subjective justification — like the taste of White Russians, Locke's secondary qualities — rather than public evidence. Jesus's claim that he and Liam will 'fuck you up' is a prediction that could in principle be publicly justified, but with no available evidence it is an unsupported opinion; Donny's gut-feeling Raiders pick shows opinions need not concern 'matters of opinion', and it is stubborn Walter who is truly 'opinionated'.

gettier-problem.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
gettier-problem.title: 10. Does Bates Know Who Raped Anna
gettier-problem.relation: The Nisleys ask whether Bates's conviction that Mr. Green raped Anna counts as knowledge, starting from the Theaetetus's definition of knowledge as justified true belief. Bates's belief is true, but his evidential position is compromised: Mrs. Hughes, though genuinely reliable, gives him false testimony pointing to a stranger, Anna denies it was Green, and his own grounds (Green's flirting and Green's admission that he left the concert) are too weak, so the truth of his belief is largely coincidental, exactly the Gettier predicament that true belief is not sufficient for knowledge. The chapter applies reliabilist reasoning about testimony to conclude that Bates 'might have suspected, but he did not know.'

gettier-problem.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
gettier-problem.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Abraham Schwab turns Ygritte's 'You know nothing, Jon Snow' into a theory of epistemic humility: Jon misreads wildling courtship norms, Sam's dragonglass shatters on wight Small Paul, Lord Mormont assumes Mance fights like a southern king and pays for it at the Fist of First Men, while Arya's accurate self-knowledge keeps her alive. Formalizing with justified true belief - Sam's lucky dagger thrust is not knowledge, and the Watch's warranted belief that the dead Othor was harmless justifies falsity - he uses Lysa's letter, which sent Ned to King's Landing on a lie, to ask what justification is: Descartes's absolute certainty is too strict, reliabilism vindicates testimony ('dark wings, dark words'), so that only Sansa need witness Ned's beheading for the Starks to know it, and between Melisandre's circular dogma about Azor Ahai and total skepticism, moderate skepticism best governs belief - a humility the south lacked about the Horn of Winter.

gettier-problem.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
gettier-problem.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
gettier-problem.relation: Richard Greene surveys zombie types, from the radio-using corpse of Return of the Living Dead to White Zombie's servants, to fix walkers as the standard zombie worth asking what they know. Against Dr. Jenner's 'mindless instinct' verdict he cites the little girl walker retrieving her teddy bear, Jenny working her former home's doorknob, walkers breaking a shop window with a rock, and their sniffing out Rick and Glenn's gut disguise as evidence of genuine beliefs. He argues that zombie knowledge, which cannot involve weighing evidence, supports externalist, reliability-based accounts of knowledge over internalist ones, and that walkers know only simple things recalled from past experience—the more complex the task, the less likely they know it.

gettier-problem.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
gettier-problem.title: “Freaks of Nature” Extrasensory Perception and the Paranormal in the Films of David Cronenberg
gettier-problem.relation: Keith Allen uses Stereo, Scanners, and The Dead Zone to explore the philosophy of ESP: telepathy and precognition challenge C. D. Broad's 'basic limiting principles' about causation (action at a distance, backward causation, changing the future). He asks whether ESP has the phenomenal 'tang' of genuine perception (Hume on force/vivacity; Nagel's 'what it is like'), and uses BonJour's reliable-clairvoyant Norman case plus Gettier to argue about internalist justification and knowledge, asking whether Johnny Smith needs reasons to trust his precognitive visions.

gettier-problem.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
gettier-problem.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
gettier-problem.relation: Silverman uses Battlestar Galactica to explore knowledge as justified true belief. Adama's 'true lie' about knowing Earth's location makes Starbuck's belief in Earth a Gettier case, a justified true belief resting on false justification. He tests Adama's testimony against Goldman's reliabilism (sight is unreliable for spotting Cylons; memory deceives Boomer and Tigh) and Hume's skepticism about testimony versus Plantinga's defense of it. Finally, against Clifford's evidentialism he deploys William James's 'will to believe,' arguing that faith in Earth is a forced, momentous choice that gives the Colonials purpose.

gettier-problem.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
gettier-problem.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
gettier-problem.relation: Eric Silverman uses Battlestar Galactica's Adama, who lies that he knows Earth's location, to run the Gettier problem: Starbuck's true belief that Earth exists rests on a false justification (that Adama knows), so it is justified-true-belief without being knowledge. He tests testimony via Goldman's reliabilism (sight is unreliable for telling Cylons from humans) and the Hume/Locke/Plantinga debate over testimony's epistemic role. He closes with James's 'will to believe': faith in Earth is a forced, momentous choice where agnosticism forfeits meaning, so belief without certainty can be reasonable.

gettier-problem.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
gettier-problem.title: 48. The Matrix as Philosophy Understanding Knowledge, Belief, Choice, and Reality
gettier-problem.relation: Perez reads the Matrix trilogy as a sustained argument about how choosing what to believe and 'know' shapes the reality we live in. He opens with Descartes' dream problem and cogito, contrasting Descartes' foundationalism with Rorty's anti-foundationalism to explain Cypher's choice to reject reality for the Matrix's certitude, and uses Searle's brute vs. institutional facts (the cookies, the steak, 'there is no spoon') to show social reality is constructed. Against the fatalism of the Oracle, Architect, and Merovingian, he argues nearly every character makes free choices, and resolves the tension via Hume's compatibilism — liberty requires necessity, and choices gain meaning only in response to causality — while noting agent-causation objections (Reid, O'Connor, Rowe) that make Neo's 'Because I choose to' significant. Gettier's justified-true-belief critique and Plato's Cave frame the knowledge and enlightenment themes.

gettier-problem.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
gettier-problem.title: 58. Tom Sawyer as Philosopher Lying and Deception on the Mississippi
gettier-problem.relation: The chapter treats Mark Twain's Tom Sawyer novels as applied epistemology, arguing lying is far broader and more varied than spoken falsehood. Using Augustine's intent-to-deceive definition it analyzes Tom whitewashing the fence, the blood oath about Injun Joe's murder, Huck's 'sacrifice lie' about smallpox, and disguises as 'showing the false' (mimicking, inventing, decoying) versus 'hiding the truth' (masking, repackaging, dazzling). It invokes Gettier's method of counterexamples as a parallel to Twain showing the traditional definition of lying is too narrow, and links Tom's gaslighting of Aunt Sally and evolutionary/self-deception to modern fake news and deepfakes.

gettier-problem.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
gettier-problem.title: 7. Knowledge, Space, and Time
gettier-problem.relation: The chapter uses the TARDIS to defend a 'block universe' theory of spacetime over Presentism (since the Doctor visits past and future), then turns to epistemology, distinguishing belief from knowledge and 'belief in' the Doctor from 'belief that' he exists. It re-stages Gettier's justified-true-belief counterexample as picking the Doctor's next companion by a blue jean jacket, surveys Descartes's Cogito foundationalism, Hume's induction, and Reid's direct perception, and endorses Alston's reliabilist two-level foundationalism plus Klein's infinitism. It argues the Doctor's benefit-of-the-doubt toward non-rational creatures fits a reliabilist 'lower level' of knowledge and an imaginative, engaged, virtuous (Zagzebski) search for truth.

epistemology-of-testimony.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
epistemology-of-testimony.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
epistemology-of-testimony.relation: Thomas Senor turns the Professor's trilemma about Lucy (lying, mad, or telling the truth) into a general account of when to believe incredible testimony: weigh the testifier's reliability against how well the claim fits your background beliefs. He shows why Lucy's siblings should have believed her second report of Aslan in Prince Caspian, since by then talking animals and a resurrected Lion no longer clashed with what they knew, and then applies the framework to 'Julia's' report of hearing God, arguing that believing, disbelieving, or withholding rationally depends on the hearer's own background commitments. A footnote explains why Hume on miracles does not fit Lucy's case, since she claims no violation of natural law.

epistemology-of-testimony.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
epistemology-of-testimony.title: Psych and Philosophy
epistemology-of-testimony.relation: McCraw turns the question 'should we trust Shawn?' into the philosophy of testimony: Lassiter's policy of never believing without independent evidence embodies Hume's demand that testimony be backed by evidence of the speaker's reliability, while Buzz McNab's instant faith embodies Reid's innate principles of veracity and credulity, and both extremes fail the department - Lassiter solves too late, McNab chases every early false lead. Juliet's developing, flexible trust - suspicious at first, convinced by results, never naive - models the circumstantial middle path that no hard-and-fast Humean or Reidian rule can capture. The verdict: treat Shawn's testimony as both psychic and psychotic, trusting the track record in some cases and discounting the wilder 'visions' in others, because when to trust is unavoidably vague and case-by-case.

epistemology-of-testimony.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
epistemology-of-testimony.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
epistemology-of-testimony.relation: Lisa McNulty asks what could oblige us to believe someone: Peter's lying fails Kant's Categorical Imperative (a world of universal liars makes lying impossible), while friendship explains Alicia's readiness to believe client Kenny Chatham even before the evidence does. The 'Death Zone' libel trial over an Everest death shows that one's position of power fixes whom one owes presumptive belief - a reader should side with Cardiff, a judge must presume Lambrose innocent - and Pascal's Wager supplies the method of 'behaving like a believer': withholding rumors, withholding conviction, and Alicia publicly playing the wife and sleeping with Peter in a bid to believe in her marriage again. She concludes Peter forfeited any right to be believed, so Alicia has no moral obligation to behave like a good wife.

epistemology-of-testimony.title: Richness and diversity in Indian thought
epistemology-of-testimony.relation: Argues that in India philosophy and religion were never separated as the post-Kantian West separates them: philosophizing is a soteriological quest in which understanding the nature of reality directly affects one's destiny, more comparable to Socrates' quest for wisdom than to modern academic philosophy. It introduces the framework of darshanas ('views' of reality taught by seers), the claim that disciplined mental exercises can yield yogic perception of metaphysical truth, and karma-rebirth as the shared Indian worldview, contrasting ritual-correctness karma with the Buddha's radically intention-based version and discussing verbal testimony as an everyday but religiously unchecked means of knowledge. It closes by delimiting the book's scope (the six classical darshanas plus Buddhism; Jainism, Carvaka, and Shaivism omitted) and warning against the Western habit of romanticizing Indian thought as mystical rather than recognizing its strong rational-debate tradition. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

epistemology-of-testimony.title: Language, grammar, and polemics
epistemology-of-testimony.relation: Shows how the brahmins defended the Veda against fifth-century challenges by formalizing the study of language: Panini's grammar codified the ritually creative Sanskrit whose sounded sentences (e.g. 'water wets grain') were held to bring about their effects impersonally, and Patanjali and Katyayana's 'usage' criterion allowed awkward or conflicting Vedic passages to be read as metaphor, preserving the text's coherence. It then presents Jaimini's Mimamsa Sutra reading of the Veda purely as injunctions - dharma defined as 'what should be done' - with word-meaning taken to guarantee the existence of what words designate, so that the Veda validates both the plural cosmos and the ritual agents who maintain it; the Upanishadic monist passages are defused as metaphor. Finally it presents Badarayana's Vedanta (Brahma) Sutra pivoting instead to 'enquiry into Brahman', and shows how both exegetes established testimony (shabda-pramana) as a lasting and contested Indian means of knowledge, alongside the purva-paksha style of stating an opponent's view before refuting it. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

aquinas-natural-law.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
aquinas-natural-law.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
aquinas-natural-law.relation: Tim Mosteller identifies Lewis's Tao from The Abolition of Man with Aquinas's Natural Law, an objective moral order knowable by all rational beings, and maps three responses onto Narnian characters: wholehearted acceptance (Peter, Lucy, Tirian, Reepicheep), selective 'Innovators' who pick and choose (Shift and Miraz, with Nietzsche's invented master-values as the philosophical extreme), and total rejection by 'Conditioners' (Ginger the Cat, who reverts to dumb beast, and Uncle Andrew, who loses the animals' speech). Individual laws are illustrated by Mr. Tumnus freeing Lucy, Aslan scratching Aravis for her gladness at the slave girl's beating, Nikabrik's treacherous Realpolitik, Lucy's eavesdropping spell in the Magician's book, and Jill's showing-off at the cliff.

aquinas-natural-law.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
aquinas-natural-law.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
aquinas-natural-law.relation: Barkman takes Andrea's mermaid-necklace question ('I don't think those rules apply any more') as a test of natural law: self-evident principles — general beneficence (Glenn's 'shit creek' rescue, Morgan's warning that it 'takes away a piece of your soul'), special beneficence toward family (Lori's 'Don't be so trusting,' Morales's 'best for my family'), and piety (Guillermo staying with the abandoned elders) — still bind after the state's collapse, while 'do not steal' is merely derived, so the unowned necklace is fair game and Rick could take some but not most of Andrea's food. Aristotle's practical wisdom resolves the cannibal hunters' collision between preserving their lives and not killing innocents — starving is the morally preferable choice — since virtue weighs principles 'all things considered.' Against Carol's 'we can make new rules' relativism the natural law outlives governments, and Father Gabriel errs by calling walkers 'abominations,' conflating bad (dysfunctional) with evil (willful) — whereas the Governor, who knowingly ignores the moral law, reduces himself to walker level.

aquinas-natural-law.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
aquinas-natural-law.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
aquinas-natural-law.relation: Kody Cooper runs Ender's life through classical just war theory: Augustine's axiom that peace is the end of all war explains why even his playground battles aim at a just peace, while the I.F.'s deliberate refusal to protect him from Bonzo's gang throws Ender into the Hobbesian state of nature where each person holds personal authority to use deadly force in self-defense. Sunzi's insistence that a commander must know the enemy grounds Ender's empathic preparation, and Cooper concludes the Third Invasion fails right intention, last resort, discrimination, and proportionality - so the guilt Ender carries is really the I.F.'s and humanity's.

aquinas-natural-law.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
aquinas-natural-law.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
aquinas-natural-law.relation: Michael Stark and A.G.
