gender-performativity.title: Won’t You Guess My Name
gender-performativity.relation: Riffs on Harrison's Themis to cast Mick as Kouros, the golden boy served by the Kouretes — "the original name of the Rolling Stones" — until he surfaces as Dionysus among the Olympians, "sort of like the irony of Mick Jagger becoming a Knight of the Realm." It splits the males into orgy-tolerant girly-men and woman-hating "manly men" of the Sour Grapes Clubs, warns not to underestimate the girly-men, and contrasts Elvis, who went into the army and became acceptable, with Mick, who kept the Kouretes under his thumb — deliberately feminine, dangerous, and cooler than the Beatles.

gender-performativity.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
gender-performativity.title: “They’re So Ugly It’s Appealing”
gender-performativity.relation: Takes the screaming fan's verdict ("They're so ugly it's appealing") and Ian Stewart's sidelining for looking "like a man" as evidence the Stones deliberately cultivated an androgynous ugliness to violate gendered expectations — "they weren't just a bunch of guys who bent the rules, they were off-sides." The blatant misogyny of the lyrics is read as compensation for that effeminacy among the Dionysian libation bearers in a patriarchal age, keeping the manly men at arm's length — while noting only Brian Jones actually abused women.

gender-performativity.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
gender-performativity.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Rood unpacks Klosterman's 'This Is Emo' thesis that no woman will ever satisfy him: women love Lloyd Dobler rather than John Cusack, and everyone measures real relationships against Hollywood fake love (Coldplay songs, the Woody Allen Personality Type) until, as Klosterman puts it, real people actively trying to live like fake people are no less fake. He reads this through Sartre's cafe waiter and Butler's gender performativity to argue identity is learned performance, and through Plato's cave updated to a reclining-seat movie theater where we mistake projected shadows for real love. The deepest diagnosis is Baudrillard's hyperreal, glossed as a social-constructionist rerun of Kant's Copernican revolution, against which Rood's own objection lands: Klosterman covertly assumes a pure unmediated self that cannot exist, so the answer to fake love is not escape from mediation but self-control within it.

gender-performativity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
gender-performativity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Ashley Barkman argues that feminism is unrealistic and inefficient in the apocalypse: citing sex-difference research such as Bandura's Bobo doll experiments, she claims masculine aggression and strength are what leadership requires when authority must be asserted physically, as when Rick pipes Merle and shoves Daryl, or Shane tackles Ed and Jim. The quarry laundry scenes stage the debate - Jacqui's protest at 'all the Hattie McDaniel work' versus Lori's 'this isn't about women's rights... doing what needs to be done' - and Barkman sides with Lori, treating the division of labor as survival logistics under a natural-law premise that it is moral to act according to nature. Andrea the sharpshooter and Michonne the swordswoman show women can excel as heroic exceptions without leading, and the chapter concludes leadership should stay with good men like Rick.

gender-performativity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
gender-performativity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Pye and O'Sullivan use Judith Butler's claim that gender is performative to read the walkers as genderless: they keep the trappings of biological sex but perform no gender, and like drag queens they 'trouble gender' when the little girl walker turns to face Rick. The survivors, by contrast, drag patriarchy along as cultural baggage - Lori telling Carl 'I'm a girl, you talk to him' while Shane teaches frogs, Ed bullying the laundry line, the men confiscating Andrea's gun while Daryl keeps his crossbow - though counter-examples (Andrea and Amy fishing for the camp, Guillermo's camp of caretaking 'vatos' led by a former custodian and a nurse, Rick teaching Andrea the safety) show gender can be learned differently. Invoking Rorty's thought that assumptions become visible only when their contradictories sound plausible, they argue survival itself demands shedding these roles, since the genderless dead threaten everyone equally.

gender-performativity.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
gender-performativity.title: The Wire and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Fisher argues The Wire makes homosexuality a source of excellence: Omar and Kima blend masculine and feminine traits in something like Butler's gender-performative terms, build Aristotelian friendships of virtue (Kima and Cheryl pushing each other's careers), and can make the sacrifices - solitude, giving up family - that excellence in the drug war demands, while the homophobia of the streets and the precinct forces them to keep proving themselves. Omar's crossword comfort with 'them myths' frames him as a contemporary Socrates: a mentor-lover of boys, accused of amorality by Levy much as Socrates was charged with corrupting Athens's youth, answering with a Socratic reversal ('I got the shotgun, you got the briefcase'), and dying for his code in the city he would not leave. The chapter reads the show's refusal of coming-out storylines - Rawls's silent gay-bar cameo, Snoop's never-confirmed sexuality - as its most radical statement about sexuality in America.

gender-performativity.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
gender-performativity.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Wieland Schwanebeck surveys the many masculinities in Cohen's songs - spies, soldiers, cowboys, rabbis, captains - and argues they mostly appear broken, mocked, or failing (the losing partisan, the captain whose ship leaks or crew deserts), which puts the 'real man' ideal in doubt. He shows how Cohen's Jewishness plays against stereotypes of the bookish, unathletic Jewish man, usually embraced and then inverted with Socratic irony, as in 'Is This What You Wanted' and 'Lover Lover Lover.' Following Judith Butler's Gender Trouble, he reads Cohen's stage persona - the tailored suit, kneeling, clowning, and erotic ambiguity - as a repeated performance demonstrating that masculinity is 'an imitation without an origin.'

gender-performativity.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
gender-performativity.title: Girls and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Adleberg asks whether Jessa is right that she is not 'the ladies.' Against Shoshanna's common-sense biological determinism and pop-neuroscience like Brizendine's 'male brain' (refuted via brain plasticity and Fausto-Sterling), she deploys Butler's point that identity categories are always normative and exclusionary (Marnie's 'that's what men do' to Charlie) and Beauvoir's and Spelman's social constructionism - mothers already treating infants differently - to show gender is made, not born. With Haslanger's call to resist unjust gender meanings, she concludes that neither conforming (Marnie craving dominant Booth Jonathan) nor defying stereotypes (Jessa's bathroom sex, 'what if I want to feel like I have udders?') should be compulsory; only objectifying harm, as with Adam and Natalia, is wrong.

gender-performativity.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
gender-performativity.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: The chapter uses Adventure Time's gender play - Fionna and Cake, princesses holding nearly all political power in Ooo, Jake as terrified helicopter dad, Mannish Man's parody of manliness - to ask what being a man or woman really means. Following Judith Butler's Gender Trouble, it argues sex does not fix gender: the Lumpy Space King and Queen share one body, Flame King is a flame in a suit, and Butler's critique of the MIT 'master gene' experiment shows how the assumption that men and women are opposites smuggles cultural convention into science. Finn is read as performing masculinity - Billy worship, dungeon codes, the endless 'Dungeon Train' - caught in a crisis of masculinity between what society says a man is and who he is, with the ghost of Shoko in 'The Vault' and the accepted grass sword as steps toward a heroism that is his own.

gender-performativity.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
gender-performativity.title: Dracula and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: De Waal reads Dracula through Judith Butler's gender performativity: the Count terrifies because he 'does' gender wrong - a captor who cooks and mothers Jonathan like an 'angel in the house,' feeds Mina from his breast, and turns Lucy from Victorian maiden into wanton vamp. Harker as a 'dude in distress,' Van Helsing's hysteria, and the Dracula-Mina scene that 'opens new orifices' become parodies exposing gender as an incessant citation of copies. The hunters' 'sterilizing' of Dracula's boxes of earth is read against the eugenics movement and society's police function against gender-nonconforming people.

gender-performativity.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
gender-performativity.title: 19. The Doctor is a (Wo)Man!
gender-performativity.relation: Kellen asks whether the Doctor could regenerate as a woman, marshaling the canon evidence (the Corsair's lives as both sexes, the Sisterhood of Karn offering 'man or woman,' Missy) to show biology poses no obstacle - clownfish and rare human sex changes make the point mundane. Against Peter Davison's claim that a female Doctor 'doesn't work,' he deploys Simone de Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' and Judith Butler's account in Gender Trouble of gender as a stylized repetition of acts performed over time, arguing the Doctor already performs care-ethicist, 'feminine' roles and could just as well perform female ones. Since regeneration routinely transforms personality without ending the Doctor, the only remaining objection is bias toward a supposedly male core identity.

gender-performativity.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
gender-performativity.title: 13. How to Be a Dwarf
gender-performativity.relation: Using Carrot (a human raised in a dwarf mine who is accepted as a dwarf), Cheery Littlebottom (an openly female dwarf), and Gladys the golem, the chapter argues that social identity is neither biology nor a one-time choice but an ongoing performance that must also be recognized by insiders and outsiders. It applies de Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' to Cheery's creation of a female dwarf gender against the deep-downers' equality that treats every dwarf as male, and reads the black ribboners versus the Magpyrs as assimilation versus doubling down on identity. Essentialist outsiders like Fred Colon and the Campaign for Equal Heights fail because they cling to stereotypes when individuals like Cheery or Carrot do not fit the mold, while Vetinari's indifference and Mrs. Cake's accommodations leave identity to those who must choose and perform it.

gender-performativity.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
gender-performativity.title: 13. The Madness of the Musician
gender-performativity.relation: Lampert explains why Bowie is called the first postmodern pop star - he ironically shows that 'acting like' a rock star just is being one, refusing the genius myth by cobbling influences and confessing 'I lie an awful lot' - and grounds this in Sloterdijk's cynical reason and Diderot's Rameau's Nephew, whose honest liar Lui owns the mask-wearing vices everyone else hides. Hegel's Phenomenology supplies the title: the musician's universal deception is 'the madness of the musician,' the 'I' hollowed into pure ironic distance from all its masks (Descartes's separable self become image-manipulation), yet Hegel's hint that the cynic's vain talk can rise into 'a spiritual self of truly universal worth' points beyond Bowie's hyper-real self-referentiality to punk's DIY injunction to be your own hero - and to reading all sexuality, like Bowie's, as performance.

gender-performativity.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
gender-performativity.title: 1. Free Falling into Postmodernism
gender-performativity.relation: Sewell reads Petty's 1976 debut through Jameson's postmodernism: Petty's music is a cut-and-paste amalgam of 1960s jangle, 1970s heartland rock and punk attitude whose pastiche dissolves the high/low art distinction as aesthetic production merges with commodity production, which is exactly why it feels timeless. He then applies Butler's performativity to Petty's "cool," arguing the persona was learned and performed so incessantly that Petty and his audience came to experience it as innate. Finally Baudrillard's hyperreal and simulacra frame the conclusion that there never was a "real" Petty, only copies of copies, yet if the perceived sincerity feels real and empowering, it is real enough.

gender-performativity.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
gender-performativity.title: 21. The Trouble with Joi
gender-performativity.relation: M.J. Ryder uses Judith Butler's Gender Trouble to argue that Joi's womanhood is a performance, and so is her humanity: an 'it' playing a woman playing a human, in nested layers from Ana de Armas through the hologram to the 1950s housewife act. The chapter situates this in the real economy of female-voiced assistants (Siri, Cortana) scripted by human writers to seem real and trustworthy, and rereads the awkward Mariette threesome as Joi acting out what she believes human sex is, the two bodies never quite coinciding. Joi's final choice of mortal peril — 'like a real girl' — completes the performance, which is why the film leaves us unsure whether performing humanity differs from having it.

gender-performativity.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
gender-performativity.title: Foreword
gender-performativity.relation: Kate Bornstein's foreword argues that Drag Race is the first pop phenomenon to present drag life and performance as a continuum rather than a one-night bar show, letting viewers watch queens learn their gender 'at the level of values' rather than rules. She frames drag as 'the proudly flamboyant performance of a broken binary' at the heart of postmodern gender theory, pointing to the casual pronoun shifts among contestants as theory in action. Quoting Season 11 winner Yvie Oddly on how different aesthetics show the possibilities of human experience, she casts both RuPaul and the show's contestants as gender royalty who embody values no one grew up with rules for.

gender-performativity.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
gender-performativity.title: 9. Another Wig Underneath
gender-performativity.relation: Cooper argues that the 'vulnerability' Drag Race demands is really a marketable persona, not truth. Working through Butler's Gender Trouble (built on Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes a woman'), she concedes drag reveals gender's imitative structure, but shows it also confirms identity: Latrice Royale's padded 'Natural Woman' lip sync reads as authentic, and trans queens like Peppermint and Gia Gunn use drag to articulate womanhood, with Husserl's intersubjectivity invoked to insist that constructed gender is no less real for not being empirical. Willam's edit-spliced 'I'm not acting' breakdown and Shannel's deliberate wig-doff show honesty becoming inconsequential next to spectacle, while Untucked's Interior Illusions Lounge is framed as Sartre's No Exit hell of unending observation. Against RuPaul's 'born naked' self-help nihilism ('identity is a joke'), she ends warning that the show no longer lets Katya take off the chicken suit.

gender-performativity.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
gender-performativity.title: 10. And the Rest Is Drag
gender-performativity.relation: Oliver Norman takes RuPaul's lyric 'we're all born naked and the rest is drag' from 'Born Naked' and asks whether its claim that everyone does drag all the time contradicts a show that crowns one drag superstar. Through Judith Butler's Gender Trouble and 'Gender is Burning' he reads drag as a play on gender that can either parody the male/female binary or reinforce it (the Mary Cheney misogyny charge, Michelle Visage's 'show woman not boy' critique, fishy queens like Courtney Act and trans queens like Gia Gunn). He then deploys Erving Goffman's Presentation of Self in Everyday Life: everyday social roles - the doctor's white coat, Alaska's Mae West on Snatch Game, the ideal pageant queen - are scripted performances with 'ideal types,' so the muscle-car seducer in the song is doing unwitting drag. The resolution: 'drag as ontology' is the low everyday form everyone performs, while Drag Race stages the high-art form that consciously fucks with the social script.

gender-performativity.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
gender-performativity.title: Final Act
gender-performativity.relation: Shaw argues everyone at 30 Rock performs a role that shields them from Sartrean radical freedom: Kenneth is Sartre's cafe waiter in bad faith, believing television is America's true art form and willing to 'die at my post' for NBC, while Jack psyches himself up with corporate slogans and Jenna's 'Black Tie' candor about marrying the last Hapsburg to be taken care of is the rare moment of good faith. Butler's gender performativity explains Jack's masculinity as a repeated script, from his Glengarry Glen Ross 'always be talking' allusion to Baldwin's brass-balls speech to his homosocial man-crushes on Don Geiss and Dick Cheney. Plato's wariness of imitation, Nietzsche on hypocrisy hardening into character, and Santayana's tragic mask frame the closing thought: the actors know they are performing, but the characters, like us, do not.

gender-performativity.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
gender-performativity.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Uses the sex/gender distinction drawn since Simone de Beauvoir's The Second Sex to read Tobias: biologically male but performing femininity (knitting, Mrs. Featherbottom, crying in the shower in cutoffs), he exposes our false conflations of sex, gender, and sexual orientation behind the running 'Tobias is gay' gag. His interchangeable pronoun use (Steve Holt (!) is a 'she' when cast as Beatrice) and 'buy-curious' double entendres embody the claim that gender is something we do rather than are, and the chapter proposes him as an androgynous, possibly pansexual ideal whose real 'problem' is society's gender biases, not his.

gender-performativity.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
gender-performativity.title: Who They Are or Who They Want to Be
gender-performativity.relation: Harwood-Smith argues, against Descartes's pre-given 'I think therefore I am,' that Judith Butler's performativity explains the Cylons: Six is female because she performs femininity, no copy performs identically, and Cylon society fractures into hybrid identities with an 'embarrassed etc.' Sexual contact with humans is the catalyst that makes performance constitute reality, producing Athena's defection, Caprica Six's celebrity status, and D'Anna's religious fervor, while Cylons who never slept with humans stay apart. The same dynamic destabilizes humans who sleep with Cylons: Baltar's 'I must be a Cylon because I slept with one,' Tyrol's fear, and Helo's 'toaster lover' stigma, with Tigh's chosen stability ('that's the man I want to be') as the counterexample of performing who you want to be.

gender-performativity.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
gender-performativity.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: White and Fisher run the show's women (and men) through feminist philosophy: the sex/gender distinction from Plato's Republic Book V and Mill's Subjection of Women through Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' and Butler's antiessentialist performativity. Penny's hyper-femininity reads as Butlerian parody that satirizes the script, the Penny–Bernadette–Amy lineup exposes the custom that smarts and beauty must trade off, and Elizabeth Plimpton and Leslie Winkle ('come for the breasts, stay for the brains') break it — while the four guys fail every 'real man' stereotype beside Penny's muscle-bound exes like Zack. Gender emerges as an artificial label that limits everyone, and seeing that would be the show's ultimate change through parody.

gender-performativity.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
gender-performativity.title: 12 Panther Mystique Wakandan Feminism Demystified
gender-performativity.relation: Wright and Pérez ask whether Wakanda's powerful women are feminists, arguing M'Baku's dismissal of Shuri as a child trades on Friedan's feminine mystique while Wakandan women escape Beauvoir's woman as the Other because their society, lacking any history of female oppression, never inscribed the second sex. Drawing on Lorde, Davis, Collins, and Walker's womanism, they read Shuri's rejection of romance, Okoye's throne-loyalty, and Nakia's stubbornness as self-definition and interdependency across difference, then use Butler's gender performativity to explain why Okoye squirms in a wig while Nakia breezes through Seoul: womanhood performed in womanist (community-centered) versus feminist (individual-transcendence) modes, with Wakanda modeling the collective call for solidarity the authors hope the future inherits.

gender-performativity.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
gender-performativity.title: How Far I'll Go
gender-performativity.relation: Maps the four waves of feminism onto Disney princess history: Snow White, Cinderella, and Aurora as chattel passed from parents to fairies to princes, betraying even first-wave rights; Beauvoir's 'one is not born but becomes a woman' and Friedan's feminine mystique explaining why the original trio's happiness is measured by marriage. Third-wave princesses are read with Wolf's beauty myth (Ariel and Jasmine as iron maidens), Butler's gender performativity, and Gilligan's care ethics (Ariel's and Belle's contextual, caring moral reasoning versus their fathers' principles). The fourth-wave princesses from Tiana to Moana need no man at all while male leads (Naveen, Flynn, Kristoff, Maui) become vulnerable sidekicks, ending with #GiveElsaAGirlfriend and the thought that equality is balance rather than sameness.

gender-performativity.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
gender-performativity.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Reading Salander as genderqueer rather than simply a woman, the chapter argues her feminism lies in swift retaliation against those who abuse women and in economic and sexual independence from men, while her refusal of every identity label ('I don't know what I am') aligns her with queer theory's anti-identity politics. Judith Butler's performativity grounds the reading: Salander's body modifications and wardrobe 'undo' conventional gendering, and her drag-like aliases—the big-busted heiress Monica Sholes and the quiet Irene Nesser—succeed at fraud and flight only through absolute adherence to heteronormative femininity, proving gender is continuously constructed. Foucault's History of Sexuality frames her pathologization, institutionalization, and regulated sexuality as the medicalization of the sexually peculiar, a disciplinary script she reverses by hacking, surveilling, and exposing the authorities who pathologized her, tattooing i am a sadistic pig, a pervert and a rapist onto Bjurman.

gender-performativity.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
gender-performativity.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Jessica Miller shows Katniss coded masculine, since Collins built her from Theseus and Spartacus and her breadwinning, hunting, and defiance fit masculine norms, while Prim embodies everything Beauvoir says civilization 'produces' as feminine, and Panem itself proves oddly gender-neutral: women work the mines, Finnick is the sex symbol sold by Snow, and Coin is as ruthless as any man. She then reads Katniss's romance performance through Judith Butler: the kisses, caresses, and televised wedding gowns do not express a preexisting femininity but constitute one, down to Butler's radical claim that sex itself is a cultural norm, which reframes even the Games' reaping of one boy and one girl as a gendered ritual rather than a presocial biological fact. Cinna's burning bridal gown that transforms Katniss into the mockingjay makes the political payoff explicit: gender performed strategically becomes the rebellion's power, and the hunter-and-baker partnership offers an alternative to the dominant romance script.

gender-performativity.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
gender-performativity.title: Iron Man The End
gender-performativity.relation: The Housels read Iron Man through Butler's gender performativity and Arendt's 'right to have rights': the male-voiced Jarvis replacing the female AI Jocasta, Tony's womanizing, and the evolving corporeal styles of Black Widow, Bethany Cabe, Madame Masque, and Sunset Bain all enact society's gender script across the waves of feminism, with the black leather suit arriving only in 1970 amid Second Wave Feminism. Arendt's Eichmann reporting and the 'banality of evil' — coined the same year, 1963, that Lee, Lieber, Heck, and Kirby, all children of Jewish immigrants, launched Iron Man — supply the justice frame: Tony's transformation of conscience after Afghanistan and his vigilante justice against his own oppressors refuse silent conformity and insist, ignoring political boundaries, that all oppressed people have rights.

gender-performativity.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
gender-performativity.title: “A Pamphlet’s Not Going to Cover It”
gender-performativity.relation: Kasey Butcher and Megan Peters argue Veronica embodies a third-wave, sex-positive feminism: as jury foreman in 'One Angry Veronica' she refuses the 'Barbie' role the captain of industry assigns her; her over-the-top masquerades (flirting with store clerk Duane Anders, the temptation scenario at Patrick Nevin's door, mimicking Logan's manspreading) expose gender as a performance; and her defense of Carmen Ruiz against Tad's blackmail shows her grasp of how race, class, and gender intersect, per Kimberlé Crenshaw. Against the show's caricature of Lilith House as humorless 'feminist killjoys' picketing the Hearst rapes, they contend Veronica models a feminism that keeps femininity, sexuality, and play — refusing slut shaming while fighting for rape victims, an incest survivor, and blackmailed girls.

gender-performativity.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
gender-performativity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Pye and O'Sullivan use Judith Butler's performativity to read walkers as genderless proof that gender is done, not born: the little-girl walker 'troubles' gender like drag, while survivors regressively re-perform patriarchy—Lori's 'I'm a girl, you talk to him', Carol at the washboard, the men confiscating Andrea's gun while Daryl keeps his crossbow. They invoke Butler's primitive clan and incest taboo to explain how Shane's camp, Lori and Carl's haircuts, and Ed's threats reproduce protector/protected roles, yet point to counterexamples—Andrea and Amy fishing, Felipe the nurse, Carl asking to be taught—that show roles can be learned differently. Via Rorty's remark that assumptions become visible when their contradictories sound plausible, they argue clinging to gender baggage endangers everyone against an enemy stripped of ego and social contract that does not discriminate.

gender-performativity.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
gender-performativity.title: Notes
gender-performativity.relation: Jones examines Renna breaking Egwene into a damane in the Amazon series to argue that identity is a social performance policed by power, drawing on Erving Goffman's dramaturgical self and Judith Butler's gender performativity (scripts, props, and 'gender trouble' exemplified by Min's dress). He argues the a'dam enforces Renna's directing so completely that a damane cannot even pretend to be subjugated while holding a true self in reserve, taking performativity to its extreme. Using Dahl and Lukes on power, Becker on labeling, and Giddens's structuration, he shows how Seanchan institutional power makes labels like damane and marath'damane stick, and asks bleakly whether any agency (even suicide) remains.

gender-performativity.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
gender-performativity.title: This Is the Version of Myself I Have to Be
gender-performativity.relation: Pérez reads Yennefer's arc through a plurality of feminisms rather than one: Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, woman' explains her sacrifice of fertility at Aretuza and later choice of motherhood on her own terms, while Butler's performativity recasts Tissaia's mirror exercises as the enactment of a socially constructed sorceress role. Naomi Wolf's Beauty Myth and Iron Maiden expose her transformation as self-imposed captivity, Ruddick's maternal thinking marks the moment she truly becomes Ciri's mother, and Firestone's call to abolish sex distinction frames her infertility-for-power bargain. Finally Crenshaw's intersectionality and Lorde's 'master's tools' show that Yennefer's quarter-elf passing lets her beat the Brotherhood at its own game without dismantling it.

gender-performativity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
gender-performativity.title: Notes
gender-performativity.relation: Donovan uses the New 52 Azzarello run's gods as a catalogue of gender stereotypes - jealous Hera hunting Zola, woman-incinerating Apollo, hyper-masculine First Born, self-sacrificing Demeter - then tracks Hera's transformation after Apollo makes her mortal as a Beauvoirian passage from immanence (being Zeus's Other, defined by his desire) to transcendence (charting an independent identity, aiding baby Zeke). Foucault's Panopticon explains how gender norms are internalized without an enforcer, and Butler's drag example grounds the claim that Wonder Woman accepting the god of war mantle - leading a female Amazon army 'not as your princess but as the god of war' - is a subversive performance of gender.

gender-performativity.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
gender-performativity.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Jonsson argues that modern sport enforces masculine norms and that the East German 'wonder girls' (Koch, Ender, Krabbe), along with Stella Walsh, Jarmila Kratochvilova and Caster Semenya, were 'gender radical' Amazons who challenged the link between masculinity and maleness by winning with 'masculine' bodies. Drawing on Judith Butler's claim that gender ideals are not static and women's sport can rearticulate them, he treats the doping-built Eastern Bloc athletes as progressive because they contradicted how female athletes are 'supposed' to look. He critiques Jane English's appeal to 'permanent biological differences' and laments that after 1989 commercialized sport (symbolized by Flo Jo's marketed femininity) hardened conservative gender norms again.

gender-performativity.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
gender-performativity.title: Joanne Kyger “Descartes and the Splendor Of” Bridging Dualisms through Collaboration and Experimentation
gender-performativity.relation: Falk analyzes Joanne Kyger's 1968 experimental video 'Descartes' and its script 'Descartes and the Splendor Of,' a condensed rewrite of the 'Discourse on Method' that subverts Descartes's mind-body dualism and privileging of reason. Kyger deflates the cogito with slang ('to doubt is a drag'), substitutes Buddhist, Taoist (Zhuangzi's butterfly dream), and Confucian terms, and—voicing and performing Descartes as a woman doing housework and as 'Mother God'—feminizes the most masculine of professions. Reading this through Judith Butler's 'Gender Trouble' and gender performativity, Falk shows the parody destabilizes the mind/body, male/female hierarchy Cartesian dualism underwrites.

gender-performativity.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
gender-performativity.title: Charlie Kaufman, Philosophy, and the Small Screen
gender-performativity.relation: Chambers reads Kaufman's TV sitcom Ned and Stacey through queer theory, arguing its marriage-of-convenience premise stages a critique of 'the normal.' Because Ned and Stacey only play at being husband and wife and never desire the romantic telos, the show troubles heteronormativity more than the openly gay Will & Grace, whose characters chase marriage and family. Chambers uses Butler's Lacanian notion of masquerade to claim there is no 'real' husband or wife beneath the role, only role-playing, and ties this to the philia (not eros) bond of the leads and to the masquerade running through Kaufman's films.

gender-performativity.book: 222 - The Philosophy of Horror
gender-performativity.title: Heteronormative horrors
gender-performativity.relation: Reading virgins and the vagina dentata as the dyad through which horror polices female sexuality, the chapter uses Irigaray's account of the virgin as prop to male subjectivity and Creed's femme castratrice to analyse Halloween's 'Final Girl', Teeth's toothed-vagina revenge on abstinence-only purity culture, Jennifer's Body and Haute Tension. It closes with Rich's 'compulsory heterosexuality' and Wittig's 'heterosexual contract' to argue horror naturalises heteronormativity by casting female sexuality as either contained (virgin) or monstrously open (vagina dentata).

gender-performativity.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
gender-performativity.title: Feminists and “Freaks” She’s Gotta Have It and Girl 6
gender-performativity.relation: Hoffman assesses whether Lee's She's Gotta Have It and Girl 6 offer liberated female sexuality, drawing on second- and third-wave feminism and bell hooks. She argues Nola Darling only appears empowered before the rape scene and her submission ('Yours') reveal her as an underdeveloped object of the male gaze, whereas Girl 6, as a phone-sex worker consciously performing gender for callers, better exposes gender as socially constructed in a Butler-like sense. Even so, Girl 6's real feminist force lies not in its heroine but in its exposure of oppressive industries, especially the opening Tarantino audition where only the director's gaze counts.

gender-performativity.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
gender-performativity.title: Herzog’s Philosophy of Masculinism
gender-performativity.relation: Will Lehman argues that beneath Herzog's rejection of any guiding philosophy lies a 'masculinism' that exalts traditionally manly traits (courage, strength, independence, emotional control) as the heroic. Drawing on gender theory (Dozier on beards and the performance of gender), he shows Herzog fetishizing 'manly men,' reading illiteracy and calloused hands as authentic manhood (Jared Talbert in Into the Abyss), and coding even his female subject Juliane Koepcke (Wings of Hope) in masculine terms. Lehman reads Herzog's reenactment 'therapy' with Dengler and Dorrington as an assertion of dominance, while noting Herzog avoids overt misogyny or homophobia.

gender-performativity.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
gender-performativity.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
gender-performativity.relation: Zanin reads Pride and Prejudice and Zombies through Freud, Aristotle, and Levinas. She argues Regency propriety over-represses natural impulses, so Freud's id/ego/superego and the aggression drive explain why Elizabeth's zombie-slaying is sublimated aggression and cathartic release (Aristotle's catharsis), her ritual 'seven cuts of shame' a displacement of guilt over misjudging Darcy. She reads Charlotte's zombie decay as an allegory of self lost to a marriage of convenience. Using Levinas on the Other (the 'unmentionable' zombie against which Elizabeth's identity is formed) and Judith Butler's claim that the Other dwells within the self, she argues the zombie Other enables rather than overwhelms Elizabeth's identity.

gender-performativity.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
gender-performativity.title: MOTHERHOOD
gender-performativity.relation: Kim Anno recounts raising an intensely masculine adopted African-American son, Zack, as a lesbian mother, using Judith Butler's account of gender and desire (from Undoing Gender) and bell hooks's We Real Cool on black masculinity to interrogate the social construction of gender against Zack's seemingly 'hardwired' boyness. She reads his gendered choices in toys, clothes, and music (Black Eyed Peas hip-hop, Black Sabbath's 'Iron Man,' the Rocky theme) and his racialized treatment through these lenses, contrasting his family with the rigid gender scripts of I Love Lucy and The Jetsons and her own parents' Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf dynamic.

gender-performativity.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
gender-performativity.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
gender-performativity.relation: Parkhill challenges Jenefsky and Miller's second-wave feminist reading of Penthouse 'girl–girl' pictorials (that they present lesbians as sexually available to naturalize heterosexuality) by arguing that what some straight men enjoy is their own ABSENCE from the scene. He deploys Butler's 'Imitation and Gender Insubordination' to show mock-lesbian-wedding drag can subvert rather than confirm heterosexual 'originality', Foucault's repressive hypothesis and productive power to argue the lesbian is a product of, not outside, patriarchal norms, and Lacan-derived 'projective identification' and feminine jouissance to explain the male viewer's libidinal investment in his own ego-erasure. He concludes both the 'conqueror' and the self-shattering 'jouissance-chasing' pleasures coexist, and that girl–girl porn is ethically no different from ordinary hetero porn since the consumer still assumes a right of access to women's bodies.

gender-performativity.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
gender-performativity.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
gender-performativity.relation: Brennan argues that fashion sits at the boundary of public and private and is central to the 'sexual citizen' and the politics of recognition for gay, lesbian, and bisexual people. Using Hanson on philosophy's gendered fear of fashion and Phelan/Weeks/Walker on visibility as a political strategy, she shows that queer identities (femme, boi, hanky codes) are communicative and require a community that reads them — offering a 'private hanky' argument echoing Wittgenstein's private-language point. She draws on her own experience (labrys earring, later bisexual invisibility) and on Butler-style gender performativity to argue visibility empowers recognition but marginalizes those, like femmes, who cannot be read.

gender-performativity.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
gender-performativity.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
gender-performativity.relation: Lee argues that tattooing is a performative 'practice of writing' whose meaning always exceeds its origin, comparing Holocaust survivor Tova Friedman's Auschwitz number 'A27633' with the Suicide Girl Jaylin's chosen feminist ink. Drawing on Judith Butler's account of the body as a site of inscription and counter-inscription, and Walter Benjamin's 'Critique of Violence' distinguishing law-making from law-preserving force, she claims Friedman's tattoo resists the Nazi law itself while Jaylin's only satirizes heteropatriarchy. She then invokes Baudrillard's 'ecstasy of communication' and the obscene to show tattooing can desubjectify by dissolving the embodied self into pornographic information.

harm-principle.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
harm-principle.title: Check Out Time
harm-principle.relation: McGrath and Tilahun ask whether hip hop is bad for women, setting protest and sex-positive tracks (Tupac's "Brenda's Got a Baby", Missy's "One Minute Man", Queen Latifah's "Ladies First", Ms. Dynamite) against endorsements of violence (N.W.A's "One Less Bitch", Snoop's "Can You Control Yo Ho?", 50 Cent's "P.I.M.P"). They apply Mill's harm principle - offend yes, harm no - Hume's counterfactual analysis of causation (the Derek Fisher shot case) to show that whether lyrics cause violence is an unsettled empirical question, Austin and Rae Langton's speech-act theory to argue rappers' cultural authority may let pimp lyrics subordinate women in a way pornography cannot, and Kant's kingdom of ends to charge misogynist lyrics with treating women as mere means.

harm-principle.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
harm-principle.title: Final Skit Paris’s Field Nigga Boogie
harm-principle.relation: Corlett evaluates the ethics of "bitch" and "nigga" in hip hop through Dave Chappelle's comedy, using the use-mention distinction and speaker intention to argue Chappelle's gender-neutral, affectionate, equivocating uses ("now that's a nigger who's one crazy nigger", the blind Black Klansman of "Frontline: Black KKK", "Reparations 2003") are racial rather than racist language. Invoking Mill's harm principle - words should be legally barred only when they harm, as with the KKK cross-burning example, not merely offend - he defends in-group reclamation, then extends the analysis to Paris's "Field Nigga Boogie" and "AWOL", whose epithets carry a progressive, Malcolm X-style challenge to unjust wars and state evil.

harm-principle.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
harm-principle.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
harm-principle.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. He reads the total improvisation learned at the Acid Tests ('the form that follows chaos'), the band's leaderless 'functional anarchy' — Lesh: if anyone tried to take charge 'it would just dissolve in their hands' — and its flat business hierarchy with roadies as corporate presidents as a spontaneous order lived at the edge of chaos. The Deadhead community's ritual communitas, analyzed through Victor Turner's separation-liminality-reincorporation model, amounts to an 'ironic sacramentalism' that achieves what social contract from Hobbes (force), Locke (property), and Rawls (self-interest) cannot: unity that transcends difference while leaving it in place.

harm-principle.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
harm-principle.title: Mr. Rawls and the Decision Procedure
harm-principle.relation: Joseph Ulatowski uses Mr. Blonde's torture of Marvin to test theories of punishment. He argues Blonde is not a mere psychopath but a retributivist within his social code—punishing clerks who 'touched the alarm' and cops who violated Mill's harm principle—while distinguishing acting on a principle from merely acting in accordance with one, since Blonde acts from sadistic urges. After reviewing Kant's lex talionis and the utilitarian theory's flaws, he asks whether Hart and Sterba's Rawlsian 'retributivism as fairness', whose principles are chosen behind a veil of ignorance, could justify Blonde's actions, concluding Blonde could not by his own lights have done otherwise than punish.

harm-principle.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
harm-principle.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly
harm-principle.relation: Johnson and Schmitz argue that Cash, through songs like 'San Quentin,' 'Jacob Green,' and his cover of 'The Mercy Seat,' championed reforming prisons from a retributive to a rehabilitative model and abolishing capital punishment (songs like 'Joe Bean' and 'Long Black Veil' center executed innocents). They defend Cash with Mill: Socrates shows vengeful retributive sentiment is immoral, Mill's harm principle says government may coerce only to prevent harm, so punishment should be justified only by future deterrence and rehabilitation. Since the death penalty's deterrent effect is empirically weak (California, Missouri-vs-Iowa murder rates) and wrongful convictions are common, Mill today would join Cash in calling for abolition.

harm-principle.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
harm-principle.title: A Little bit of Messi for our Life
harm-principle.relation: The authors cast the contrast between disciplined European and improvisational South American football as Mill's struggle between liberty and authority: the coach's tactical orders are 'rules of opinion' the genius may defy, as Maradona did on his sixty-meter run to the Goal of the Century, while the harm principle marks the line at the 'rules of law' — FIFA's Laws of the Game. The Hand of God goal, which broke even a rule of law yet stood because 'a goal is scored when the referee says so', illustrates Searle's point that football's regulative capacity cannot guarantee its agreements, leaving a gap filled only by ethics and fair play. Following Wittgenstein's 'ethics and aesthetics are one and the same', they conclude that a bit of Messi-style rule-breaking — Messi replicated both Maradona goals in 2007 — is what makes football, and life, joyful and beautiful.

harm-principle.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
harm-principle.title: The Problem with Drugs
harm-principle.relation: The closing section rebuts the communitarian defense of California's drug laws, noting there is more than one community and most people belong to several, then turns to Douglas Husak: moral rights exist to protect persons from majority interference, and the crusade against drugs is cultural hegemony. Cocaine, marijuana, and opiates were outlawed along racial lines (blacks, Mexicans, and Chinese respectively) while the ruling class's alcohol and tobacco remained 'autonomous choices,' suggesting the real problem with drugs is who uses them.

harm-principle.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
harm-principle.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: A palliative-care bioethicist dissects the 'Gray Matter' family meeting, arguing Skyler's ambush coerces Walt's autonomy through an implied threat of emotional isolation, while Walt Jr.'s honest 'I'm pissed off!' and Marie's defense of his choice are non-coercive. The chapter frames the issue with Kant's ideal of choice free from emotion and circumstance and Mill's insistence that even self-destructive decisions are beyond legitimate coercion, and indicts doctors too for 'selling' futile treatment rather than admit mortality. The verdict: Walt accepted chemotherapy through 'autonomous beneficence' - a freely made sacrifice for his son - so Skyler's manipulation was unethical even though the decision it produced was genuinely his own.

harm-principle.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
harm-principle.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Asks what exactly makes a meth cook a 'bad guy' and finds the line hard to draw: Walt forces no one to use, so like tobacco farmers and gun makers he merely enables self-harm - yet Saul's proposed prison shanking and Walt's order to murder Gale show culpable enabling without direct harm. Gale's libertarian purity argument ('they're getting exactly what they pay for') and Prohibition economics even suggest that on utilitarian grounds skilled cooks might do less harm than worse ones, though the industry as a whole remains indefensible. The chapter's moral center is Jane's death - Walt's monstrous 'standing by' - and the closeness effect that makes the personal Krazy-8 murder feel worse than the gas; it concludes the good-guy/bad-guy frame itself fuels the failed war on drugs.

harm-principle.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
harm-principle.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: A provocatively sympathetic application of On Liberty: Mill's harm principle protects Jesse's drug use from punishment, and Mill's celebration of individuality and 'experiments of living' makes Walt's cooking an 'individual spontaneity' valuable precisely because it defies custom - Marie's anti-pot panic and Hank's beer-and-Cub-cigar double standard illustrating the 'magical influence of custom' and democracy's drift toward 'collective mediocrity'. Mill's temperance-era remarks that intoxication 'is not a fit subject for legislative interference' are extended from use to manufacture. The chapter's thesis: even when Walt is wrong, mere nonconformity 'is itself a service', making Heisenberg an unlikely hero of liberty and human progress.

harm-principle.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
harm-principle.title: Futurama and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: In 'A Taste of Freedom,' Zoidberg eats Earth's flag Old Freebie on Freedom Day, is tried by Earth's Supreme Court, and his death sentence triggers a Decapodian invasion that enslaves Earth under the Mobile Oppression Palace. The chapter pits Mill's On Liberty defense of unpopular expression (mankind cannot silence a lone dissenter; unchallenged beliefs are mere 'true opinions' akin to prejudice) against Feinberg's offense principle, mapping the case onto Texas v. Johnson and the symbolic-speech line from Stromberg to Tinker. It ends with Zoidberg burning the flag 'to preserve the freedom it represents': liberty and majority will often conflict (doomsday devices, Proposition Infinity's robosexual marriage ban), so preserving freedom requires tolerating offensive expression.

harm-principle.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
harm-principle.title: Futurama and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Young tests Isaiah Berlin's distinction between negative liberty (absence of external interference) and positive liberty (rational self-government) on three episodes: Fry's super-Slurm compulsion in 'Fry and the Slurm Factory,' human Bender's lethal gluttony in 'Anthology of Interest II,' and the worms whose upgrades win Leela's love in 'Parasites Lost' - each agent is externally unobstructed yet not self-governing. Bender's jacking-on addiction and the Temple of Robotology's threat of Robot Hell in 'Hell Is Other Robots' illustrate Rousseau's 'forced to be free,' the coercion that Berlin warned has licensed totalitarian regimes. The chapter concludes Futurama takes no side, suggesting genuine freedom needs both positive and negative liberty.

harm-principle.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
harm-principle.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Joe Slater builds a two-premise anti-natalist argument from Shelley's Paradise Lost epigraph ('Did I request thee, Maker, from my clay / To mould me man?'): since it is wrong to inflict harm on an autonomous being without consent, and every autonomous life inevitably contains harms, creating autonomous beings - Adam in the lab or a baby in the womb - is wrong. He answers the objection from Parfit's non-identity problem via the damaged-brain Adam case, and defends the Harm Premise with Mill's On Liberty: consent matters because autonomous agents must be free to harm themselves, as with the smoker, the drinker, and Frankenstein's stolen kidney. G.E. Moore's 'Moorean shift' and Benatar's genetic, social, and institutional pro-natal biases explain why we resist the conclusion, with a 'Super Adam' incapable of harm as the only escape.

harm-principle.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
harm-principle.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Greg Littmann reads Graff and Ender as act utilitarians in John Stuart Mill's mold, drawing a detailed parallel between Ender's engineered Battle School childhood and James Mill's grueling raising of his son to be utilitarianism's champion, down to both boys' breakdowns. He argues that although the xenocide was a tragic wrong by Mill's own lights (the hive-queens' happiness counted too), the harm principle permits overriding individual liberty when humanity's survival is at stake - which is why Card's novel, unlike Crime and Punishment or 'The Ones Who Walk Away From Omelas,' shows consequentialism at its most troubling rather than its most absurd.

harm-principle.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
harm-principle.title: Homeland and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Christian Cotton asks whether Carrie's clandestine surveillance of the Brody home, though illegal, is morally wrong, distinguishing legality from morality. Locke's state of nature grounds natural rights to life, liberty, property - and by extension privacy - that government exists to protect and that no national-security goal automatically overrides; Mill's utilitarianism would justify violating one family's privacy to prevent an attack, but Mill's own harm principle and 'tyranny of the majority' caution blocks it when Carrie has only a hunch. Kant's respect for persons as ends in themselves condemns Saul's blackmail of Judge Turner as using a man merely as means, so the Right constrains pursuit of the Good.

harm-principle.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
harm-principle.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Framed by Dickens's Jacob Marley, Walker asks whether Jobs deserved his posthumous accolades despite giving far less to charity than Bill Gates, and tests him under three frameworks. Aristotle's virtue ethics acquits him (character is judged holistically, and charity sits near the golden mean of open-handedness rather than being a checklisted duty); Mill's utilitarianism acquits him (his innovations maximized happiness and he violated no Harm Principle—though abandoning daughter Lisa counts as a harm); and Singer's drowning-child argument condemns him as near-morally-bankrupt for selling luxury gadgets while children starve. Kant both convicts (charity is an imperfect duty under the categorical imperative) and saves Jobs: treating the affluent individual as an end in himself, never merely a means to the destitute, blocks Singer's demand for giving to marginal utility.

harm-principle.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
harm-principle.title: 5. The Truth Shall Make Ye Fret
harm-principle.relation: Watson uses The Truth - William de Worde's accidental invention of Ankh-Morpork's first newspaper and the plot to frame Lord Vetinari - to stage the three classic arguments for censorship: direct harm (character assassination 'works every day'), indirect harm (with MacKinnon's point that the speech of the dominant drowns out the subordinated, applied to speciesist insults at Koom Valley), and the false-beliefs argument. Against them stand the knowledge problem and the equality assumption: Mrs. Arcanum's deference to print, Vetinari's turtle-shaped-world joke, and the Montessori-Broca dispute show we never know in advance which beliefs are false, and any censor like Lord de Worde has his own agenda. Vetinari's verdict that 'free men pull in all kinds of directions' because 'pulling together is the aim of despotism' carries the chapter's Millian case that free speech is a horrible necessity.

harm-principle.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
harm-principle.title: 9. Variation under Ethics
harm-principle.relation: Weighs the clones' bodily autonomy against the special obligations they owe one another, since genetic sisters can harm each other as no strangers can: Helena's murder of Katja nearly pins a killing on Sarah, and Vic's drug-world drags danger into Alison's suburb. The chapter builds a clone-specific cousin of Kant's categorical imperative — "act only and always in a way that you would want your clone to act" — to argue that the clones' liberty may be legitimately more restricted than ours: Alison's public drunkenness endangers sisters who can be mistaken for her, clones arguably must stay in Clone Club and share medical information like Cosima's illness, and hard cases (Beth's suicide leaving cases dangling, the brain-cut-open Castor clone begging Helena to kill him) all turn on balancing autonomy against what we owe others.

harm-principle.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
harm-principle.title: 16. Artistic Expression in the Land of the Free
harm-principle.relation: Argues that Hendrix's Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' links political and artistic freedom: Mill's On Liberty — the harm principle, liberty of tastes and pursuits, and originality against the despotism of custom — both protects and celebrates the performance, since disliking it is no ground for suppressing it. Tolstoy's What Is Art? then supplies the aesthetic verdict: art is the infection of others by sincerely, particularly, and clearly felt emotion, so the anthem, like Picasso's Guernica, is great art expressing bad feelings about Vietnam — unlike José Feliciano's sincere-but-vague ballad or Roseanne Barr's failed joke.

harm-principle.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
harm-principle.title: A Black Mirror of Our Anxieties
harm-principle.relation: Nosedive's star ratings are read as a digital panopticon — Bentham's prison design generalized by Foucault's Discipline and Punish — with China's Zhima Credit and Social Credit Systems showing the 'future is already here.' Rousseau's general will and Plato's ship-of-state frame the tyranny-of-the-majority worry (Chester destroyed by an office mob, Lacie jailed for a wedding toast, post-truth tribalism), which Mill's harm principle rebuts: Lacie's rant harms no one and should not be punished. Sartre's 'look' and No Exit explain Lacie's staged cookie photo ('Heaven!') and her final liberating exchange of insults with her cellmate, while Goffman's masks ground the epistemological worry that digital profiles are performances we nonetheless trust, and Bourdieu's symbolic capital names what the scores actually measure.

harm-principle.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
harm-principle.title: Do We Attain Justice by Punishment
harm-principle.relation: Kenny's blackmail arc in Shut Up and Dance — the twist that reclassifies the sympathetic protagonist as a child-pornography offender — anchors an argument that the hackers' vigilantism cannot attain justice: their punishments are unannounced, disproportionate, aimed at merely moral wrongs (infidelity, racist emails), and exempt from the presumption of innocence and nulla poena sine lege that states replaced vendetta with. A distinction between natural-law and legal-positivist conceptions of justice shows why punishment belongs to the state alone. Against retribution ('a mere prison sentence is too good for Kenny'), Bentham's and Mill's utilitarianism — deterrence, incapacitation, and above all rehabilitation, capped by the harm principle — shows punishment should be no more than deterrence requires, making the hackers sadists rather than agents of justice.

harm-principle.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
harm-principle.title: “Cogs that Fit, that Cooperate by Design”
harm-principle.relation: Reads the government ban on Supers in The Incredibles through Locke's Letter Concerning Toleration and Mill's On Liberty, arguing the ban rests on the 'PREFER' principle — society's likings and dislikings as law — fed by perception management (Winston Deavor's suit-cameras PR campaign) rather than reasons, just as Locke diagnosed intolerance, not diversity of opinion, as the cause of civil strife. Mill's harm principle, illustrated by Elastigirl's 'drinking on duty' remark, should instead govern, so banning Supers' powers and pressuring Dash to suppress his speed ('Everyone's special, Dash' / 'Which is another way of saying no one is') is tyranny. Mr. Huph's 'cogs that fit, that cooperate by design' image of Insuricare shows the conformist cost: a society built on preference rather than reasons will never produce great thinkers.

harm-principle.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
harm-principle.title: Is Propaganda Permissible
harm-principle.relation: Manninen surveys Disney's WWII Donald Duck shorts (Donald's Decision, The New Spirit, Der Fuehrer's Face, Commando Duck) to argue propaganda is not only the enemy's tool and not always wrong. Hume's 'slave of the passions' explains why The Spirit of '43 works through the Thrifty-versus-Spendthrift slugfest rather than its implicit argument, and Mill's fallibility-corrigibility case for free expression gives even propaganda a seat in public discourse — though Mill's caveat against expression that instigates mischievous acts marks the real limit, which the contrast with the Axis's 'barefaced lies' (and the Yensid thought experiment) is meant to satisfy.

harm-principle.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
harm-principle.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Greg Littmann defends Graff and Ender as act utilitarians in Mill's own image, noting that Mill's father raised him in calculated isolation and brutal study as a tool to reform humanity just as Graff engineers Ender, so both acted rightly given the stakes even though Mill's harm principle and his regard for animal suffering also condemn the xenocide itself. Against Crime and Punishment and 'The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas,' he argues Ender's Game shows consequences can genuinely justify breaking any moral rule when human extinction is on the table.

harm-principle.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
harm-principle.title: Notes
harm-principle.relation: The chapter asks whether Fallout's chems should be banned and answers no on Millian grounds: chem addiction harms only the user (and is trivially curable at any wasteland doctor, unlike Cait's Psycho addiction in Fallout 4, which shows what real addiction actually costs), so the New California Republic's firing squads for chem dealers and Caesar's Legion's crucifixion of the smuggler Anders violate the Harm Principle. Combat chem use is self-protection, drugging a Charisma check harms no one because NPCs act on their own programmed preferences, and paternalism fares no better in a wasteland where a failed speech check can get you killed. The analysis then extends to real-world performance-enhancing drugs: permissible for soldiers fighting a just war, but coercive in sports, where PED users force clean athletes to choose between their own health risks.

harm-principle.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
harm-principle.title: Notes
harm-principle.relation: Writing as a mechanic, Gordon argues Max embodies Plato's Republic: like the ship-of-state navigator, only someone who knows justice may rule, and the Myth of the Charioteer — reason holding the reins over spirit and appetite — explains why the Nightrider's unchecked spirit crashes while the cool-headed, deliberative Max endures. On punishment, Plato's rejection of retaliation (the unjust should be made just, not harmed) interrogates Max's execution of Johnny the Boy, while Polemarchus's 'render to each his due' frames the just-deserts debate. Mill's harm principle then justifies Max's force against the gangs once the state and its courts have vanished, leaving Max an administrator of street justice.

harm-principle.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
harm-principle.title: Through the Mist and the Madness: Metallica's Message of Nonconformity, Individuality, and Truth
harm-principle.relation: Thomas Nys argues Metallica's early message of nonconformity and individuality ('Metal Militia', 'Motorbreath') converges with Mill's On Liberty: conformity withers human capacities and breeds a stagnant society. Mill's higher pleasures and Nozick's experience machine show why real happiness requires autonomy and earned achievement rather than passive pleasure - the point of 'Escape''s 'Life's for my own to live my own way'. He reads 'Leper Messiah' and 'Eye of the Beholder' as Metallica's versions of Mill's defense of free inquiry and truth against mindless conformity and censorship.

harm-principle.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
harm-principle.title: The Office and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Nys asks whether political correctness is a genuine moral demand or mere verbal hygiene, using the British Office: Gareth's racist BMC joke, Brent aborting it when Oliver the Black coworker arrives, the 'wanking claw' impression, and the porn email with Brent's head pasted onto a woman's body. He argues words genuinely wound (Brent's 'sticks and stones' rehearsal collapses when Gareth reveals his cruel nicknames) but that offense is wrong as disrespect for human equality rather than as a feeling, an account filled out with Frankfurt's claim that our identity depends on what we care about, so the non-targeted can be offended too. After weighing Mill's defense of free discussion for social progress, the pornography debate (in which reduction to body parts is exactly what degrades, as Brent complains he was 'objectified'), and Marx's notion of ideology as a concealing set of ideas behind a 'white male' bias, he concludes that Brent's flaw is looking good rather than being good, and that PC language is rhetorical make-up over persisting inequality.

harm-principle.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
harm-principle.title: Robust Social Critique
harm-principle.relation: McGowan asks how SNL gets away with offensive material, from Larry David's concentration-camp monologue to the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' and 'Nude Beach.' He argues censorship fails because offense is historically relative and slippery-slope prone, and that on Mill's On Liberty the harm principle never licenses suppressing speech SNL viewers can freely avoid, a point he sharpens with Feinberg's Volenti maxim and the offense principle. He closes by defending offensive comedy as robust social critique: Mill's fallibilist case that free speech drives human progress, with Baldwin's Trump and Tina Fey's Charlottesville bit as comedians speaking truth to power.

harm-principle.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
harm-principle.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Keeping asks what grounds the claim that great power brings great responsibility and answers through Good Samaritan ethics. Building on MacIntyre's account of human interdependence in family and community, and Mill's point that failing to aid can itself cause harm, he argues that Bad Samaritanism is a blameworthy harm-causing omission, so Spider-Man's rescues of strangers are obligatory negative duties rather than supererogatory favors. His vigilantism is excused because only he can stop supervillains, 'can implies ought' explains why his duties exceed ordinary people's, and his life-risking feats against the Sinister Six and Firelord still go beyond even what his enlarged duty demands.

harm-principle.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
harm-principle.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
harm-principle.relation: Takes 'Douche and Turd' — Stan refusing to choose between Giant Douche and Turd Sandwich, Puff Daddy's gun-toting 'Vote or Die', and his banishment — plus the kindergarten tie in 'Trapper Keeper' (Flora's indecision, Rosie O'Donnell's recounts) to ask whether every vote counts in a two-party system. Through Locke, Stan's abstention becomes a withdrawal of consent to be governed by either mascot; through Mill, non-voting threatens the active participation that gives institutions legitimacy and wards off tyranny of the majority, even as the chapter catalogs real disincentives: the Electoral College's spectator states, the 2000 Florida debacle, and Commission rules excluding third parties like Nader. Habermas closes the chapter: the vote, read as positive liberty, is the paradigm of rights and inclusion in a community of equals.

harm-principle.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
harm-principle.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
harm-principle.relation: Challenges the received libertarian message of 'Medicinal Fried Chicken' — Randy giving himself testicular cancer for a marijuana prescription, Cartman bootlegging KFC in a Scarface parody after Colorado bans fast food — by pressing Mill's liberty principle on what 'harm' means: Mr. Garrison's plot to murder the Queer Eye cast is immediate harm, but the S&M Mr. Slave displays to schoolchildren in 'The Death Camp of Tolerance' is only indirect, psychologically mediated harm Mill cannot clearly handle. Addiction then undermines Mill's assumption of sovereign tastes: corporations can shape desire without coercing anyone, so the libertarian 'omnicompetent individual' is a myth. Mead's intersubjectivity (Randy smoking pot before Officer Barbrady, blind to how Jimbo sees him) grounds the constructive claim that selves are socially formed, and the shark-tank defecation and Prisoner's Dilemma examples show why collective harms need rules and regulation.

harm-principle.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
harm-principle.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
harm-principle.relation: Defends South Park's anti-paternalism on both consequentialist and deontological grounds. 'Major Boobage' shows the futility of Gerald's cat ban meant to stop kids 'cheesing' — Kenny still gets high and Gerald himself relapses — while 'Medicinal Fried Chicken' shows how the KFC prohibition births a violent black market, with Cartman's $85 snack pushing him into the Colonel's Scarface-style drug war. On the deontological side, Mill's 'over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign', Locke's self-ownership, and Kantian respect for rational agents (via Nozick's inviolability, and the authors' autarchy-versus-autonomy distinction) ground the claim that coercion is wrong even when benevolent: 'Butt Out' has Kyle and Stan tell Rob Reiner that forcing others to quit smoking is fascism, while Big Tobacco's Kevin Harris wins their approval simply by informing and letting people choose.

harm-principle.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
harm-principle.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
harm-principle.relation: Uses 'Follow That Egg!' — Mrs. Garrison's jealous crusade to stop Mr. Slave marrying Big Gay Al, her two-daddy egg experiment where Stan and Kyle out-parent Cartman, and the governor's 'butt buddies' separate-but-equal compromise — to demolish the standard arguments against gay marriage (scripture, dictionary definition, procreation, tradition, harm to children, the slippery slope to polygamy and incest) as post-hoc rationalizations of disgust. Mill's harm principle and negative liberty supply the positive case: unlike under-age, incestuous, or polygamous marriage, gay marriage demonstrably harms no one, so no legitimate reason remains to ban it, and rights should never be put to a referendum anyway. The 'butt buddies' label fails because separate is never equal — marriage's social recognition, not just its 1,100 benefits, is what its defenders are denied.

harm-principle.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
harm-principle.title: What's so Bad about Performance-Enhancing Drugs
harm-principle.relation: Ryan evaluates three arguments that using performance-enhancing drugs is wrong, drawing on cases like Barry Bonds, Lyle Alzado, and Ben Johnson. The Against-the-Rules argument shows only that PED use breaks current rules, not that it should be banned; the Unfairness argument overgeneralizes, since sport is full of tolerated unfairness (better coaching, nutrition, natural gifts); and the Harm-and-Pressure argument turns on empirical facts and a paternalism-versus-autonomy debate about whether adults may choose the risk. She concludes no argument yet establishes that PEDs ought to be banned as inherently wrong.

harm-principle.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
harm-principle.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
harm-principle.relation: Roberts argues that across Lee's 'Father Knows Best' trilogy (Pushing Hands, The Wedding Banquet, Eat Drink Man Woman) the clash between traditional Confucian values and Western modernity is best resolved by the virtue ethics of Confucius and Aristotle rather than by deontology or utilitarianism. Master Chu literally refusing to be pushed, the Gaos accepting Winston's homosexual relationship, and Chef Chu adapting to his daughters all require Aristotle's golden mean and habituated virtue, which accommodate special relationships and situations. Kant's categorical imperative (rejecting paternalism as treating persons as means) and Mill's harm principle are shown to be too rule-bound to reconcile tradition with modern individualism.

harm-principle.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
harm-principle.title: Beat U-topos or Taking Utopia on the Road The Case of Jack Kerouac
harm-principle.relation: Adamo argues Kerouac's 'On the Road' is a new kind of utopian text: because classical collective utopias (Plato's Republic through More) were judged by Berlin, Popper, and Arendt to slide into totalitarianism and to conflict with political liberalism's individualism, Kerouac relocates utopia from place to the individual life lived 'on the road' (u-topos = no-place). He reads Sal Paradise's disillusion with Dean Moriarty—who uses people up—versus his admiration for Mississippi Gene and the hobos as dramatizing J. S. Mill's harm principle, fused with the Buddhist vow to harm no living thing, radicalizing personal liberty as perpetual movement without injury to others.

harm-principle.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
harm-principle.title: Technology and Ethics in The Day the Earth Stood Still
harm-principle.relation: Skoble reads The Day the Earth Stood Still as an allegory about the ethics of force and technology. He argues Klaatu's ultimatum extends Mill's harm principle to the interplanetary level: societies may fight among themselves but not threaten others, so Gort's robot police enforce a right to peace that no one has a right to violate. He distinguishes the robots' narrow, non-paternalistic authority from Hobbes's absolute sovereign, defends the ultimatum as preemptive self-defense rather than a rights violation, and contrasts the film's trust in machines with the later technophobia of Colossus and The Terminator.

harm-principle.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
harm-principle.title: 4. Better Call the DEA
harm-principle.relation: White uses Better Call Saul's cartel world—the 'Bagman' shootout, Mike's account of Philadelphia police corruption, Tuco's meth-driven violence—to frame the ethics of the U.S. War on Drugs, tracing its racist origins and drawing a sustained analogy to alcohol Prohibition. She marshals Mill's harm principle from On Liberty to argue adults may choose their own risks absent harm to others, making criminalization inconsistent given legal alcohol. She then fairly lays out the pro-War case (Bennett on deterrence, the Robins Vietnam-heroin study, Mill's own bar on selling oneself into slavery applied to addiction) before favoring decriminalization on the Portugal model.

harm-principle.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
harm-principle.title: 23. Why Does Jimmy Get to Determine Chuck’s Healthcare
harm-principle.relation: The chapter uses Chuck's EHS to probe when paternalistic intervention against a competent person's will is justified. It argues Chuck is epistemically irrational (the hidden battery and electrified bed disprove his causal beliefs) yet notes, via Sharon Street and Nietzsche, that we all act on 'illogical' but coherent evaluative attitudes, so absurdity alone cannot license Dr. Cruz's push to commit him. Invoking Isaiah Berlin's warning against oppression in the name of someone's 'real self' and Mill-style concern for self-regarding choices, it finally uses Simone de Beauvoir to distinguish Jimmy's genuine devotion to Chuck from Chuck's controlling 'tyranny,' which shaped Jimmy's turn into Saul.

harm-principle.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
harm-principle.title: 10. Some Dark Genie
harm-principle.relation: Calef asks whether Bourdain's choice to become a heroin addict could be rational and responsible, using Mill's On Liberty and Harm Principle (including the voluntary-slavery exception) to argue addiction is reversible and can minimize suffering when alternatives are bleak. He then reads Bourdain's self-destructive drives — the drunk cliff-driving 'death trip' — through Freud's death drive (Thanatos) and Schopenhauer's pessimism, concluding the 'dark genie' was partly disease-like and thus not wholly blameworthy.

harm-principle.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
harm-principle.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
harm-principle.relation: Dromm and Salter analyze Persuasion by distinguishing persuasion (rational, argument-based belief change), influence (nonrational, resting on a person's charisma or status, as Lady Russell has over the Elliots), and 'overpersuasion.' Against Captain Wentworth's view that persuadability is a vice and firmness of mind a virtue (his hazelnut analogy, Louisa Musgrove's fatal fall from the Cobb), they adapt Mill's On Liberty: just as free discussion lets a society exchange error for truth and gain confidence in true beliefs, a persuadable person is happier and epistemically better off. They add that Anne broke the engagement from a sense of duty, not fickleness, and it is her own persuasion that finally reunites her with Wentworth.

harm-principle.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
harm-principle.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
