harm-principle.relation: Tait Szabo defends the guiltless consumption of pornography using Mill's Harm Principle from On Liberty: harmless conduct, even if deemed immoral, should not be censored. Classifying porn into erotica, sexist, dominance, and violent types (excluding child porn and snuff as clearly prohibitable), he rebuts the arguments that porn is prostitution (citing California v. Freeman), that loveless sex is wrong, that porn non-rationally causes or conditions violence against women, and the anti-porn feminist claim that it eroticizes patriarchal subordination. Each argument, he holds, either lacks causal evidence or would equally condemn romance novels, sexist jokes, and Cinderella — so under Mill, censorship is unjustified.

harm-principle.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
harm-principle.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Jacob Held argues that US obscenity and anti-pornography law fails for indeterminacy. Tracing Roth v. United States (Brennan's 'prurient interest' standard) and Miller v. California's three-part 'serious value' test, he shows judges must act as aesthetes (Justice Stewart's 'I know it when I see it'; Scalia's doubt about objective artistic value), so the law gives no fair notice and lacks the form a rule of law requires. He then turns to MacKinnon and Dworkin's Indianapolis civil-rights ordinance defining porn as the 'subordination of women,' struck down in American Booksellers v. Hudnut, arguing its vague 'subordinating' criterion — read through Dworkin's jaded view of sex — would sweep in nearly all explicit material, per Douglas that 'censors are propelled by their own neuroses.'

harm-principle.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
harm-principle.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Miles argues that the popular 'porn is free speech applied to sex' defense (Wendy McElroy, Nadine Strossen) fails, using the contrast of Cohen's 'Fuck the Draft' jacket versus a hypothetical 'Schmoen' having public sex to express an opinion. He holds that political and religious speech persuade at a distance whereas public pornography coerces by making the unwilling audience actually perform the act of looking, so treating boobs like bumper stickers would be illiberal. The reasoning leans on a Millian harm/liberty framework: expression that merely offends is protected, but expression that forces others into an act crosses a line, so porn must be defended on privacy/autonomy grounds rather than as free speech.

harm-principle.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
harm-principle.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Rose takes a paradigm plotless YouPorn-style clip and tests the four standard charges against porn—obscenity, coercion/exploitation, harm to women, and harm to society—arguing each either collapses into cultural relativism or applies equally to any aesthetic object. He answers the feminist (MacKinnon/Dworkin-style) claim that porn subordinates women by noting that unjustified hierarchical power distorts the self-understanding of dominator and dominated alike (comparing it to 50 Cent's 'P.I.M.P.' and blaxploitation), so the wrong is not gender-specific. His conclusion is that porn should not be treated as different in kind from other art but judged aesthetically and morally by whether it distorts equitable social relationships, locating the real problem in capitalist cultural production rather than in porn as such.

harm-principle.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
harm-principle.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: In this interview, dominatrix-director Mz. Berlin answers the classic moral objections to porn from inside the industry: she rebuts objectification by insisting she chooses to be 'a commodity' and that choice makes it permissible, rejects the rape-myth/harm claim by citing declining rape rates and comparing porn to violent TV, and grounds BDSM's legitimacy entirely on INFORMED CONSENT, contrasting her voluntary waterboarding with her real torture abroad. Endorsing a strongly Millian self-ownership view ('my body is my own commodity'), she extends consent to selling kidneys, assisted suicide, and even display of her corpse, while drawing hard limits at sex with children, animals, or the dead where genuine informed consent is impossible. She also frames femdom porn as subverting male hegemony and normalizing fluid gender roles.

harm-principle.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
harm-principle.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Jacquette argues that cannabis opens a 'creative inner space' of loosened associations but is skeptical it yields genuine, lasting insight, using Ginsberg's claim to have newly 'apprehended the structure' of jazz and classical music and the conjecture that Shakespeare's Sonnet 76 'invention in a noted weed' hints he wrote high. He treats the aesthetic case as a phenomenology problem: separating cannabis's real contribution to appreciation from mere buzz-glow. He then defends a right to get high by invoking the Declaration's 'pursuit of happiness' and a Mill-style principle that private, non-harming pleasure should not be criminalized.

harm-principle.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
harm-principle.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Tahko surveys the empirical evidence on cannabis from the standpoint of the individual and of society, concluding that its health harms (respiratory illness, mild cognitive impairment, possible dependence, weak links to psychosis) pale beside those of alcohol and tobacco. He argues the gravest costs—legal risk, social isolation, contaminated black-market supply—are consequences of prohibition itself, not the drug. Endorsing public-health experts, he recommends abandoning elimination-based policy for a harm-reduction approach modeled on the Dutch coffee-shop system and Portuguese decriminalization.

harm-principle.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
harm-principle.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Musselman, Frohardt, and Lynch defend adult cannabis use through Mill's Harm Principle, using the hypothetical 'Patrick the pot smoker'—a professional who grows and smokes moderately on Friday nights—to argue that competent adults' self-regarding conduct is their own affair and does not violate the 'distinct and assignable obligations' Mill owes to family. They marshal health data (no lung-cancer link, negligible secondhand exposure, neuroprotective effects) to rebut the harm-to-others claim, and invoke Mill's higher intellectual pleasures plus the Michael-Phelps case to argue prohibition wastes resources better spent on the greater harms of alcohol and tobacco.

harm-principle.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
harm-principle.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
harm-principle.relation: Earleywine dissects the moral versus practical arguments over prohibition, attacking legal moralism—the drug-czar claim (Bennett, Wilson) that use is wrong simply because it is immoral—as circular, and noting that the law does not criminalize every immoral act (broken contracts, lying). He shows purported moral arguments collapse into utilitarian harm estimates that the data undercut, since use rates are essentially orthogonal to policy across Amsterdam, Australia, Portugal, and US states. He then weighs anti-prohibition rights arguments (religion, privacy in Ravin, property via Szasz, self-determination) and closes on proportionality: owning a harmless plant merits no punishment.

harm-principle.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
harm-principle.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
harm-principle.relation: Miori, a palliative-care physician assistant and clinical bioethicist, separates personal ethics, professional ethics, and bioethics, then evaluates tattooing through Beauchamp and Childress's principles—especially autonomy (intention, understanding, freedom from outside influence) weighed against risk versus benefit. He concludes tattooing is bioethically fine because safer pigments and market forces reduced its disease risks and because autonomy makes 'to ink or not' the patient's own call, echoing a Millian liberty that one's choice not harming others is 'none of your beeswax.' He ends by defending the memorial tattoo as therapeutic 'memory remodeling' that gluing a positive event in place with pain can make good for you.

harm-principle.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
harm-principle.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
harm-principle.relation: Woods asks whether the claim 'tattooing is immoral' can be defended, taking Adolf Loos's 1908 'Ornament and Crime' (tattooed free men are latent criminals or degenerate aristocrats) as his provocation. He rejects Loos's equation of tattooing with murder, since tattooing is voluntary and self-regarding, but resists the liberal 'sovereign self' reply drawn from Mill's On Liberty by arguing autonomy and the body are relational, not absolute, so a person's self-regarding choices remain open to reasoned challenge and even regulation. He proposes regret evidence in informed consent and an age-25 minimum, concluding tattooing is a matter of both taste and morality.

harm-principle.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
harm-principle.title: SERIAL KILLERS
harm-principle.relation: Waller interviews two retired California officers (Amarillas and Kos), framing their front-line experience through Aristotle's 'natural philosophy' of theorizing from observation. The conversation raises the killing-versus-letting-die distinction over a neglect case, uses a harm principle to weigh whether rape can be worse than murder, and sets early-twentieth-century verificationism against later philosophy of mind in debating whether serial-killer 'types' (thrill-seeker, mission, power/comfort killers) are meaningful if only behaviors are observable. Kos recounts her own multiple-murderer grandfather, and both officers close by warning how media fiction distorts the public's grasp of real, charming, camouflaged killers.

harm-principle.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
harm-principle.title: index
harm-principle.relation: This composite chapter opens with the volume's Introduction and then runs several essays. Jeff McLaughlin's 'What If?' reads DC's Crisis on Infinite Earths and Marvel's What If? series as literal illustrations of Leibniz's possible-worlds metaphysics: the multiverse of Earth-1, Earth-2 and the 3,000 doomed universes dramatizes counterfactuals and Leibniz's Theodicy argument (via the principle of sufficient reason) that God actualizes only the best of infinitely many possible worlds, with Descartes invoked on why a perfect God permits imperfection. Amy Kiste Nyberg's essay analyzes the 1954 Senate hearings on EC horror comics (Gaines's 'The Orphan') as an applied-ethics clash between publishers' free expression and protecting children, explicitly deploying Mill's On Liberty and harm principle to argue why the child-audience framing defeats the anti-censorship case. Stanford Carpenter's piece treats the Black Captain America (Truth: Red, White, and Black) as an epistemology-of-authorship problem.

harm-principle.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
harm-principle.title: 11. Futurama as Philosophy Wisdom from the Ignorance of a Delivery Boy
harm-principle.relation: Lewis surveys how Futurama's satire raises philosophical questions without taking sides. 'Zoidberg's Freedom Lesson' pits Mill's harm principle and free speech against Feinberg's offense principle; the mutants' and robots' oppression is read through Foucault's disciplinary normalcy and Locke's and Rawls's social contracts (state of nature, veil of ignorance). 'The Problem with Popplers' stages Bentham's utilitarianism, a might-makes-right food-chain view, and an intelligence criterion that commits Singer's 'speciesism,' with sentimentality winning. 'The Late Philip J. Fry' and 'Free Will Hunting' dramatize determinism, Nietzsche's eternal recurrence, and Sartre's existentialist free will, while 'Godfellas' and 'A Clockwork Origin' probe the problem of evil, fine-tuning, and Occam's razor.

harm-principle.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
harm-principle.title: 28. South Park as Philosophy Blasphemy, Mockery, and (Absolute ) Freedom of Speech
harm-principle.relation: The chapter argues, via the 'Cartoon Wars,' '200,' and '201' episodes, that South Park makes five arguments about free speech and evaluates each. Johnson defends the claims that catering to terrorist threats breeds more terrorism and that mockery is 'all or nothing,' but rejects South Park's implied case for absolute free speech: using Mill's On Liberty and harm principle he shows the 'marketplace of ideas' fails (citing 8kun and Fox News), and using Popper's paradox of tolerance he argues intolerance cannot itself be tolerated. He proposes a middle-ground 'PC Principle' where society, not the state, curbs harmful speech through deplatforming and public shaming while distinguishing tolerance from acceptance.

harm-principle.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
harm-principle.title: 29. Frank Herbert’s Dune as Philosophy The Need to Think for Yourself
harm-principle.relation: Reading the Sci Fi Channel miniseries Frank Herbert's Dune and Children of Dune, Littmann argues the saga warns against letting leaders or religions think for us: Paul Atreides fakes being the Fremen Mahdi, wages a holy war, and founds a theocratic tyranny that Alia and Leto II carry to worse extremes. He sets Plato's Republic (the guardian class, the noble lie, rule by the wise) and Hobbes against pro-democracy thinkers—Locke's consent and natural rights, Mill's harm principle, Dewey's democracy—then cites Locke, Paine and Russell on religion's dangers, closing with W.K. Clifford's 'ethics of belief' that one must not accept religious claims without sufficient evidence. The chapter reads Paul's dictatorship and the Bene Gesserit's engineered messiah as dramatizations of the historical abuses of concentrated and religious power.

locke-natural-rights.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
locke-natural-rights.title: Post-Civil Rights Music
locke-natural-rights.relation: Lawson argues political rap - Grandmaster Flash's "The Message", Public Enemy's "911 Is a Joke", Tupac's "Trapped", Dead Prez's "They Schools", Naughty By Nature, Ice Cube's "I Wanna Kill Sam" - challenges liberal political philosophy by claiming the social contract between blacks and the United States is broken: using Locke's Second Treatise account of state protection of life and property, he contends the state's failure of economic and physical protection voids blacks' political obligations. Drawing on Cornel West's diagnosis of black nihilism and Charles Mills's racial contract - a contract constructed for white supremacy - he reads conscious hip hop as post-civil-rights music continuing the black freedom struggle in a new voice, with KRS-One asking "Who protects us from you?"

locke-natural-rights.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
locke-natural-rights.title: Not Just a Black Thing
locke-natural-rights.relation: Roberts uses hip hop's reparations consciousness - Chuck D's "Kill Em Live" and "Who Stole the Soul?", KRS-One's "Sound of Da Police" overseer-officer analogy, Ice Cube's "F*** Tha Police", the Amadou Diallo shooting and its mural, Spike Lee's Do the Right Thing, Chappelle's "Reparations 2003" - to introduce rectificatory justice: punishment of perpetrators, compensation for victims' unjust losses, and apology that reaffirms victims' moral standing. Arguing that ideal theory reflects the experience of the privileged and neglects injustice, and that "forty acres and a mule" was never rectification (hence H.R. 40), he closes with Ice-T's "Straight Up Nigga" and the Hawaiian Kingdom apology to show rectifying injustice is "not just a black thing".

locke-natural-rights.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
locke-natural-rights.title: So, What’s the Bottom Line
locke-natural-rights.relation: James Klagge, defining terms in Socratic fashion, distinguishes bootlegs like Great White Wonder from piracy and argues unreleased Dylan material (the New York Blood on the Tracks, "Blind Willie McTell," the 1966 Live concert) has genuine musical and historical value. He rejects the Sophist view that morality is just self-interest and the relativist "everybody's doing it" defense, then weighs the artist's Lockean property and privacy rights against fans' rights of access, noting legal-but-immoral and illegal-but-moral cases in the spirit of Martin Luther King's civil disobedience. His verdict: bootlegging is morally acceptable when royalties are fair, stolen tapes are not used, and mainly public performances circulate.

locke-natural-rights.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
locke-natural-rights.title: James Bond and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Forster stages the dispute between Dr. No ('just a stupid policeman') and Scaramanga ('we are the same') over whether Bond's license to kill betrays the liberal rule of law it protects, connecting it to post-9/11 debates about executive power. He gives the rule of law a substantive ground in Locke's Two Treatises - prerogative power may suspend particular laws for the public good of preserving the community ('salus populi suprema lex'), illustrated by Locke's own career conspiring with Lord Ashley's spy network - and a procedural check in the separation of powers, mirrored in MI6's real parliamentary and judicial oversight. Both elements together, he concludes, let Bond's extra-legal work remain consistent with the rule of law: power exercised for the public good under institutional supervision, without which M's vendetta in 'For Your Eyes Only' would be indistinguishable from Scaramanga's contracts.

locke-natural-rights.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
locke-natural-rights.title: Transformers and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Plauche grounds Optimus Prime's line 'Freedom is the right of all sentient beings' in 'Aristotelian liberalism': since Energon, like our food, is scarce and requires labor and creativity, any volitional artificial life needs a moral code whose standard is flourishing (following Foot's natural goodness), cultivating intellectual and moral virtues from prudence, independence, and honesty to benevolence and courage. Ricardo and Mises's law of association - illustrated by Ratchet and a human mechanic both profiting from specialization despite Ratchet's absolute superiority - plus the ruinous cost of war give even superior aliens reason to respect our rights to life, liberty, and property rather than enslave or exterminate us, as Megatron would.

locke-natural-rights.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
locke-natural-rights.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Jason Walker argues the zombie apocalypse is a Lockean rather than Hobbesian state of nature: rights to life, liberty, and property persist without government. Rick's 'I don't think those rules apply anymore' to Andrea over the mermaid necklace is justified by Locke's spoilage and 'enough and as good' provisos - the owner is almost certainly dead and the necklace would otherwise lie forever wasted - while Morgan's house-squatting, which protects the Thompsons' home, and Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo's nursing-home defenders show self-ownership and norms at work. The counter-cases, Chris's cannibal band ('a man's gotta eat') and the Governor, who treat persons as mere means, live out Hobbes's war of all against all and are destroyed by the Lockean right to punish that victims retain.

locke-natural-rights.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
locke-natural-rights.title: The Wire and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Allen asks how a virtual war zone can exist inside the United States, starting from Hobbes: Marlo's cool killing of the security guard who just wants to be recognized as a man looks like the rights-free state of nature where 'nothing can be unjust.' But he argues Locke's sharper distinction fits better - the underclass are nominal citizens whose rights to life, policing, and education exist on paper while their substance is denied, which for Locke places an oppressed minority in a state of war within a state, and makes the drug game a rational choice for Michael, Dukie, and Randy. Marlo's 'you want it to be one way, but it's the other way' names that collapsed protection, and the chapter ends with Locke's warning that majority apathy lets oppression persist, reading The Wire as protest art meant to move viewers to political action.

locke-natural-rights.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
locke-natural-rights.title: Homeland and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Christian Cotton asks whether Carrie's clandestine surveillance of the Brody home, though illegal, is morally wrong, distinguishing legality from morality. Locke's state of nature grounds natural rights to life, liberty, property - and by extension privacy - that government exists to protect and that no national-security goal automatically overrides; Mill's utilitarianism would justify violating one family's privacy to prevent an attack, but Mill's own harm principle and 'tyranny of the majority' caution blocks it when Carrie has only a hunch. Kant's respect for persons as ends in themselves condemns Saul's blackmail of Judge Turner as using a man merely as means, so the Right constrains pursuit of the Good.

locke-natural-rights.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
locke-natural-rights.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Gale and Barkman treat post-Mushroom-War Ooo as a state-of-nature laboratory for liberalism's three founders. The Forest Wizard who cages Finn in 'Storytelling' is Hobbes's Leviathan, kept in power by fear yet moderated by self-interest (Goblin King Xergiok's fall shows the leash); Princess Bubblegum's Candy Kingdom is Locke's civil society where citizens trade private revenge for impartial law—her lawful bow to Lemongrab shows she rules by contract, not fear; and 'City of Thieves' illustrates Rousseau's claim that property corrupts natural goodness, with Finn and Jake as his uncorrupted natural people. The chapter concludes that the rights language these thinkers forged is what keeps both Ooo and our world from sliding back into a war of all against all.

locke-natural-rights.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
locke-natural-rights.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
locke-natural-rights.relation: Malloy asks whether the two law-breaking vigilantes are criminals and whether any duty to obey the law survives scrutiny. He runs consent theory through Superman surrendering in handcuffs in Man of Steel and the Red Son Superman's residence in the USSR, uses Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's security sovereign against Locke's natural-rights limits, deploys Hume against tacit consent (Batman would never leave Gotham even in No Man's Land), and dismantles gratitude theory (the Kents' adoption involved a sacrificial choice the law cannot make) and fair play (Nozick's Batman-lottery undercuts "I'm not wearing hockey pads"). He lands near Wolff-style philosophical anarchism: Superman's constrained lawbreaking endorses the law's legitimacy while Batman treats law as one more tool in his war, making him a force of chaos.

locke-natural-rights.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
locke-natural-rights.title: 4. Who Owns Clones
locke-natural-rights.relation: Takes the message Cosima decodes in the clones' DNA — "This organism and derivative genetic material is restricted intellectual property" — and asks whether Dyad can legally and morally own the Clone Club. The chapter walks through US patent law and the Supreme Court's Myriad Genetics decision (naturally occurring DNA unpatentable, synthetic cDNA patentable) and argues that because the Leda and Castor clones were genetically engineered, their modified sequences could fall under the synthetic exception, making ownership legally possible. Morally, though, it sides with self-ownership: people own the products of their labor but not people, so patenting clones would recreate the wrongs of slavery, down to who controls clone marriages and clone offspring.

locke-natural-rights.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
locke-natural-rights.title: 16. Can We All Get Along
locke-natural-rights.relation: Courtland Lewis tackles transitional justice after atrocity: with the Rising won, what is to be done with millions of Golds complicit in slavery, rape, and torture? He tests Peter French's virtuous vengeance—punishment that fits the wrong, grounded in Locke's natural rights—and finds Darrow's destruction of Gold society fails it (disproportionate, unsober, punishing young Julian for his ancestors' crimes), then turns to Jessica Wolfendale's argument that declaring anyone unforgivable adopts the wrongdoer's own devaluing outlook, exactly as Darrow becomes what he despises. The working model is South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission—confession, conditional amnesty, truth-telling, reparations, Tutu, Mandela, Beth Savage hoping to meet her bomber—applied to Mars through Mustang-style dignified engagement on Adam Michnik's model and Slavenka Drakulic's lesson that every Color inherits responsibility for rejecting the Society's past.

locke-natural-rights.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
locke-natural-rights.title: 6. Jaime the Savior
locke-natural-rights.relation: The Coxes defend Jaime's kingslaying with Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics Book III on voluntary, involuntary, and 'mixed' actions: like a storm-besieged crew jettisoning cargo, or the Blackfish's 'a knife to his throat is not a valid order,' Jaime faced a duress - kill Tywin on Aerys's order or let King's Landing burn - so his regicide was a mixed action that is praiseworthy as the least harmful option rather than blameworthy. They add Locke's right of revolution, where a ruler who makes his will rather than law the rule puts himself in a state of war with his people, to argue the Mad King's 'Burn them all' tyranny justified the killing, making the reviled Kingslayer the savior of the city.

locke-natural-rights.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
locke-natural-rights.title: 5. In the Neutral Zone, a Libertarian’s Home Is Their (High) Castle
locke-natural-rights.relation: The chapter reads Dick as a left-leaning libertarian for whom the deepest evil of the High Castle world is the loss of privacy: Arnold's surveillance unit and the Kempeitai's wiretaps illustrate Locke's self-ownership and natural rights, while the Neutral Zone poses the Hobbesian question of whether even an oppressive state beats the state of nature, and the 'libertarian minimal state' names what the Reich destroys. On this reading the American Nazis like John Smith were internal collaborators all along — 'it already happened here' — and ethics lies in refusal, as when Tagomi declines to sign the order sending Frank to his death.

locke-natural-rights.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
locke-natural-rights.title: 3. Will the Real American Hero Please Stand Up
locke-natural-rights.relation: Samuelson argues Tony Stark is the real American hero because he embodies the Locke-to-Smith lineage of American values - natural rights, property from mixing labor, free trade and the invisible hand, plus Smithian sympathy - carried forward into twenty-first-century neoliberalism, from Stark Industries to backing the Registration Act. Steve, by contrast, keeps abandoning the Captain America identity (Nomad after the Secret Empire, The Captain under Nuke's government, handing the shield to Bucky and Sam Wilson) whenever America betrays the dream, and admits his true fight is against bullies and for human rights everywhere. Hence Cap is a great hero but not strictly an American one, while Tony lives American values practically, warts and all.

locke-natural-rights.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
locke-natural-rights.title: 6. Big Brother Ltd
locke-natural-rights.relation: Botello-Samson and Mobley extend Fromm's point that 1984 indicts authoritarian power in general by reading Oceania alongside neoliberalism, which grew out of Locke's liberalism of natural rights and limited government yet demands activist state power to create the conditions for markets. Doublethink reappears as 'accountable independence' in administrative law (Chevron deference, and Garcetti v. Ceballos stripping whistleblower protection) and as Washington Consensus food policy, in which developing nations were pushed off agricultural self-sufficiency while the US kept its own subsidies. Both Ingsoc and neoliberal governance reduce everything to economic elements and use Newspeak-like buzzwords such as 'stakeholder' and 'customer-driven government' to hide the contradiction between democratic rhetoric and rule by experts and elites.

locke-natural-rights.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
locke-natural-rights.title: 2 Transforming Wakanda Justice (or Not ) in Black Panther
locke-natural-rights.relation: Bein and Lewis imagine Killmonger surviving his duel to face Wakandan justice, and sort what justice would demand into retributive justice (Kant: punishment only what the offender deserves, never using him merely as a means to public safety, though they note Kant's own racist views), reparatory justice (Locke's natural rights and what Wakanda owes N'Jadaka for T'Chaka killing N'Jobu and abandoning him in Oakland), and the restorative-to-transformative justice of Changamire's gatherings in Coates's 'A Nation Under Our Feet,' modeled on South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission. They argue a restorative Wakanda would seat Killmonger with his victims and even the king at the table to repair harm rather than imprison him, and sketch a prison-abolitionist Wakanda meeting Thanos with 'Wakandan justice is more civilized.'

locke-natural-rights.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
locke-natural-rights.title: Notes
locke-natural-rights.relation: John Irish reads the Amazon series' Vault 33 as Locke's Two Treatises staged and then betrayed: Overseer elections (Betty Pearson against Reg McPhee and Woody Thomas), town-council deliberation over captured Vault 32 raiders, and Lucy's 1950s-styled domesticity all mimic natural equality, consent of the governed, majority rule, and the preservation of property. Norm's discovery that every election is rigged in favor of cryo-preserved technocrats from Vault 31, that Lucy's marriage 'application' is engineered population control, and that Vault-Tec executives - including Lucy's mother Barb - voted to launch the Great War itself shows Locke's forms of consent, law, and rights preserved as empty ceremony. The chapter's argument is that Enlightenment liberalism stripped of transparency becomes authoritarian experiment management: consent becomes choreography in a commonwealth that is really a lab, right down to composting the raiders' bodies.

locke-natural-rights.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
locke-natural-rights.title: Selling Ol’ Shellhead
locke-natural-rights.relation: Malloy uses Spymaster's theft of Stark's armor designs in the Armor Wars and the U.S. government's legally valid appropriation of the technology after Tony announces 'I am Iron Man' to test two theories of property. Locke's natural-law view makes the designs an extension of Stark's laboring self — stealing them is like taking an arm — while Hume's social-contract view treats property as a useful convention whose violation makes the thief an enemy of society itself, and Rousseau supplies the cautionary image of the first man who fenced ground and said 'This is mine.' A closing thought experiment in which Tony sells Iron Man outright (like Siegel and Schuster selling Superman) argues that intellectual property can never be fully alienated: whoever wore the armor, Tony would still be Iron Man.

locke-natural-rights.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
locke-natural-rights.title: Notes
locke-natural-rights.relation: Alkema and Barkman put Q himself on trial, asking what justifies his judgment of humanity in 'Encounter at Farpoint' and Trelane's of Kirk in 'The Squire of Gothos'. Hobbes's Leviathan would license Q's might-makes-right sovereignty over a savage species, but Q lacks humanity's consent and cannot show he acts for future peace; Locke's natural law instead binds even nearly omnipotent beings, as Janeway's asylum ruling for the suicidal Quinn in 'Death Wish' demonstrates. Q's repeated self-sacrifice—in 'Deja Q' and the Continuum's civil war—reveals a conscience answerable to natural law rather than raw power.

locke-natural-rights.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
locke-natural-rights.title: NOTES
locke-natural-rights.relation: Foy reads the Great Revelation and the Vampire Rights Amendment as a test of social contract theory: Nan Flanagan's 'we pay taxes, we deserve civil rights' invokes the Lockean bargain of obedience for protection, but Locke's God-given natural rights falter when the Fellowship denies vampires souls, and Locke excludes atheists and never imagined vampires. The chapter's resolution is Rawls: behind a veil of ignorance where deliberators might wake up vampire or human, anti-vampire bigots like the Newlins and supremacist nests alike would choose equal basic liberties plus distributive justice — including limits on vampires' centuries of accumulated wealth — so Sookie's 'let the law do it' to Rene marks a pluralist peace no theistic contract could deliver.

locke-natural-rights.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
locke-natural-rights.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Jason Walker pits Hobbes against Locke over whether Andrea may take the mermaid necklace when Rick says 'I don't think those rules apply anymore'. He reads the survivors' conduct—Andrea's single necklace under Locke's spoilage proviso, Morgan squatting in and fixing up the neighbors' house, Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo—as a Lockean state of nature where self-ownership and property rights persist without government, while Chris's cannibal band and the Governor embody the Hobbesian war of all against all, treating persons as mere means. The Lockean right to punish, exercised brutally by Grimes's group on Chris's hunters, vindicates rights even by Hobbes's own demand for enforcement.

locke-natural-rights.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
locke-natural-rights.title: King Foltest, John Locke, and the Social Contract
locke-natural-rights.relation: Irish tests King Foltest's rule over Temeria against Locke's Two Treatises of Government: against Filmer's patriarchal divine right and Bodin's absolute sovereignty, Locke's political voluntarism holds that legitimate rule rests on the consent of free and equal subjects and exists to protect their lives, liberties, and property. Foltest's inherited throne lacks any social contract, and his edict protecting the striga Adda - the daughter born of his incest with his sister, who preys on Wyzim's citizens - breaches the Lockean sovereign trust. The Netflix 'Betrayer Moon' miners' uprising becomes a Lockean revolution: after 'a long train of abuses' the people may reclaim the sovereign power and even remove the king, so long as the new authority restores consent and the public good.

locke-natural-rights.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
locke-natural-rights.title: The Right and the Good without God
locke-natural-rights.relation: The chapter builds the case that Whedon's fiction grounds ethics without God: Foy's Lockean social-contract reading of the Firefly crew and Kant's person-as-end analysis explain why Mal insists Saffron is 'not to be bought' in 'Our Mrs. Reynolds' and why Loki's possession of Hawkeye and Jasmine's enthrallment of her worshippers are the Whedonverse's paradigm wrongs. Spike's arc—from selfish ally, through the 'Triangle' troll fight and 'Intervention' torture, to the 'Chosen' sacrifice—is read through Aristotelian habituation into virtue, while Angel's Darla-arc firing of Team Angel and the Better Days temple-money and Inara plots show where respecting rights and being a good person can come apart. Finally the Euthyphro dilemma, plus replies to Pojman and Craig (self-sacrifice is not 'stupid'), argue that Angel's 'Epiphany' ethic—doing what matters with no glorious end or divine reward—shows morality is neither arbitrary nor motivationally crippled without God.

locke-natural-rights.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
locke-natural-rights.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
locke-natural-rights.relation: Woolfolk reads The Last of the Mohicans as staging a conflict between nature and civilization. The opening hunt is neither Hobbes's brutish state of nature nor quite Rousseau's amoral noble savage, since the Mohicans are full moral agents; Woolfolk uses Locke's Second Treatise to cast Hawkeye and the colonists as enforcing natural law and natural rights against English 'tyranny,' with Chingachgook's killing of Magua a justified execution. Rousseau's First and Second Discourses illuminate the hypocrisy and greed of Montcalm and the Europeans, and Camus's Meursault is invoked as a truer image of amoral natural man; Tocqueville frames Cora's democratic awakening as individualism.

locke-natural-rights.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
locke-natural-rights.title: Kingdom of Darkness: Autonomy and Conspiracy in The X-Files and Millennium
locke-natural-rights.relation: Michael Valdez Moses reads The X-Files and Millennium as post-Cold War noir that depicts America as Foucault's carceral archipelago: nearly every character works for the state, Tocquevillian voluntary association has withered ('they don't go bowling at all'), and the FBI's landscape of prisons, clinics, and bases makes free space scarce. Against Hobbes's Leviathan, the chapter mobilizes Locke and Paine's classical liberalism (government as necessary evil securing pre-existing natural rights) to show that Carter's heroes are 'antipolitical' resisters: Frank Black's visions and the Grill Flame remote viewers make him a panoptical spy for the state, while Mulder's warrantless searches blur sovereign and criminal justice into one corrupt system, as in the Millennium episode 'The Judge'. The neo-noir conspiracy seeks not profit but absolute sovereignty, and the series end with Mulder, Scully, and Black as fugitives fleeing the state with their families, resisting Nietzsche's 'coldest of all cold monsters'.

locke-natural-rights.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
locke-natural-rights.title: Two Ways to Yuma Locke, Liberalism, and Western Masculinity in 3 10 to Yuma
locke-natural-rights.relation: Mexal reads both versions of 3:10 to Yuma through Locke's classical liberalism, arguing the western hero descends from Locke's autonomous, property-owning self in a 'state of nature' (contrasted with Hobbes's state of war). In the 1957 film, Dan Evans transforms from atomistic self-interest to a masculine civic republicanism, escorting Ben Wade to the train even after being released from his contract, reflecting Cold War anxieties. In the 2007 remake, Dan instead renegotiates his contract for water rights and money, so western masculinity becomes unyielding Lockean individualism and the 'right to get rich' in a post-Cold War, capitalist-triumphant America.

locke-natural-rights.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
locke-natural-rights.title: Human Rights, Human Nature, and Amistad
locke-natural-rights.relation: Baggett and Foreman use Amistad to reconstruct Locke's theory of natural rights: Cinque's mutiny and John Quincy Adams's Supreme Court plea that man's natural state is freedom illustrate Locke's claim that God's workmanship makes us his property and therefore un-ownable by other men. They contrast Locke's voluntarist natural law with Aquinas's, note Adams rebutting the Hobbesian 'war of all against all' quoted in the pro-slavery Executive Review, and invoke Mill's perfect/imperfect duty distinction (Baldwin's obligation to his clients) plus Bentham's rights-denying utilitarianism, which they map onto Calhoun's warning about the cost of abolition.

locke-natural-rights.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
locke-natural-rights.title: 13. Does God Have the Right to Destroy the Universe
locke-natural-rights.relation: Foresman asks whether Chuck has a negative right to destroy the multiverse, rejecting the question-begging 'God can do whatever God wants' and the bare creation/ownership argument (using the scrambled-eggs example) as insufficient. Drawing on Locke's Two Treatises—property arises from mixing labor, but even in the state of nature one may not destroy a creature except for a 'nobler use,' and hoarding beyond use is illegitimate—he concludes Chuck is a Lockean tyrant destroying universes he could simply recreate, so Sam and Dean's rebellion is justified.

locke-natural-rights.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
locke-natural-rights.title: NOTES
locke-natural-rights.relation: Richard Davies analyzes the post-crash survivors as living in a genuine 'state of nature' and grades its severity by how scarce the contested good is (the water shortage as a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers versus Sawyer's 'possession is nine-tenths'). He compares Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau on human nature — labeling the poles 'Innocence' (Hurley, Rousseau, Hume) and 'Trust No 1' (Sawyer, Hobbes) — and uses the repeated prisoners' dilemma and the tit-for-tat strategy to argue that the castaways build a Lockean civil society by signaling through shared language and cooperating first, while the discovery of the Others (Ethan) triggers Hobbesian non-cooperation.

locke-natural-rights.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
locke-natural-rights.title: NOTES
locke-natural-rights.relation: Peter S. Fosl argues that Lost pretends to a liberal social order — Jack rising by consent in a Lockean scheme of natural rights, Rousseau's general will ('live together, die alone'), and Hume's sympathy and pity binding the survivors — but that its treatment of the Others betrays a darker politics. Reading the survivor/Other conflict through Carl Schmitt's friend-enemy thesis (notably absent Hobbes), he contends the show, like post-9/11 America, needs an enemy to exterminate, and that the finale's Jacob/Man-in-Black war and Jack's Christlike sacrificial death repudiate the Kantian liberal ideal of persons as ends, resolving conflict through Schmittian and Christian redemptive violence instead.

locke-natural-rights.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
locke-natural-rights.title: Thidwick the Big-Hearted Bearer of Property Rights
locke-natural-rights.relation: Skoble argues that the creatures who colonize Thidwick's antlers never acquire any property right, because mere uninvited occupancy does not create ownership and Thidwick's Lockean self-ownership over his own body and horns is inalienable. The eleven-to-one vote to keep Thidwick on the starving north shore shows, via Nozick's 'Tale of the Slave,' that democratic procedures cannot legitimately override fundamental liberty rights. Thidwick's near-enslavement stems from his mistaken belief that a host must be 'nice to his guests,' and his freedom is restored only when the shed antlers let him reclaim self-ownership.

locke-natural-rights.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Ketcham 'deconstructs' the entailment that threatens the Bennets in Pride and Prejudice, explaining the legal history of fee tail and primogeniture and noting Austen likely erred, since by her time entailment could be barred by a simple legal procedure. He uses this to trace competing theories of property, from an occupation theory (first possession, tied to inherited estates) toward an emerging economic theory of productive wealth, and finally to Jeremy Waldron's view that property is a relationship between people. Elizabeth's careful assessment of Darcy's estate as a community rather than a mere possession dramatizes this shift, and love plus responsibility replaces entailment as the story's true concern.

locke-natural-rights.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
locke-natural-rights.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
locke-natural-rights.relation: Carmine argues that in America hunting is a sacred rite of a secular 'religion' of individual natural rights granted by the Deist 'Nature's God,' where—revising Locke via Jefferson's 'pursuit of happiness'—one owns game only by actual capture, and early game law kept even private land open to the common hunter against English enclosure. He attacks Leopold's land ethic and Tom Regan's animal rights, and Garrett Hardin's 'Tragedy of the Commons,' as an 'eco-gentry' that demotes humans to mere biosphere/carbonate and threatens human rights, insisting (with Burkert's Homo Necans) that to kill and eat the rabbit is to reserve dignity for humans alone.

locke-natural-rights.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
locke-natural-rights.title: GARDENING
locke-natural-rights.relation: Laura Auricchio shows how General Lafayette made his estate at La Grange an embodiment of liberal, transatlantic political ideals. Inspired by Washington as a Cincinnatus figure and by Arthur Young's agrarian reform, Lafayette imported American plants and English husbandry, keeping meticulous farm records and staging tours that framed the land around liberty (Fox's planted ivy, self-sufficiency, beneficent stewardship). The chapter argues his cultivation of crops and identity presented the garden as 'American ground' expressing natural rights and republican virtue.

locke-natural-rights.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
locke-natural-rights.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
locke-natural-rights.relation: Agnafors asks whether free soloing is morally permissible, opening with soloists dropping ice chips into his coffee cup to show soloing is not purely private. He tests Locke's natural rights to life and liberty (concluding no act is truly private since rescues, taxpayers, and grieving families are affected), Aristotle's virtue ethics (worrying that habitual risk-taking forms a reckless character), and Bentham and Mill's consequentialism (Bill's confidence-boosting solo of Nutcracker versus Derek Hersey's fatal fall). He concludes no universal answer exists, offering one rule: the soloist must carefully weigh all these considerations beforehand.

locke-natural-rights.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.title: 12. Firefly as Philosophy Social Contracts, Political Dissent, and Virtuous Communities
locke-natural-rights.relation: Kowalski argues that Firefly and Serenity embody a distinctive political theory he calls 'Since I Found Serenity' (SIFS). The mindless, savage Reavers represent Hobbes's state of nature, showing government is necessary; but the Alliance's torture of River, the Miranda/Pax atrocity, and the murderous blue-gloved agents and Operative make a Hobbesian reading untenable and vindicate Locke's natural rights and right of revolution — Mal's 'I aim to misbehave' broadcast of the Miranda file is Lockean civil disobedience. He then presses the tacit-consent problem (the Browncoats cannot leave the 'Verse) and supplements Locke with Aristotle's friendship and community: Serenity's crew becomes a virtuous mobile commonwealth where friendship (Simon forgiving Jayne, Mal's 'love keeps her in the air') turns a commonwealth into a good-life community.

locke-natural-rights.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.title: 24. Game of Thrones as Philosophy Cynical Realpolitiks
locke-natural-rights.relation: The chapter argues that Game of Thrones advances a thoroughgoing cynicism about political legitimacy, captured by Varys's riddle that 'power resides where men believe it resides.' It documents the dubious claims of Robert 'the Usurper' and the pyromaniacal Daenerys, the barbaric Lockean 'state of nature' among the Wildlings, and the false ideals of chivalry and religion, with Littlefinger and Varys voicing Machiavellian realpolitik. Silverman and Riordan then offer two views the show never considers: Locke's social-contract theory of natural rights (which would justify deposing Aerys or Daenerys) and Aquinas's four-part test for genuine law (reason, common good, proper authority, promulgation), arguing a legitimate state remains possible against the show's cynicism.

locke-natural-rights.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
locke-natural-rights.title: 92. V for Vendetta as Philosophy Victory Through the Virtues of Anarchy
locke-natural-rights.relation: Nisley argues that Moore and Lloyd's V for Vendetta justifies V's violent rebellion against the Norsefire regime through Locke: the fascist state seized power without consent, tortured and experimented on citizens (V at Larkhill), and violated natural rights, thereby placing itself in a state of war so the people may overthrow it. Using Aristotle on deviant constitutions and the beast-like tyrant (Adam Susan) who lacks practical wisdom, and contrasting Locke's tolerable state of nature with Hobbes's brutal one, the chapter concludes the citizens should rebuild a rights-protecting social contract rather than V's leaderless anarchy, and maps the argument onto real-world 2020 events (BLM riots vs. the Whitmer kidnapping plot).

veil-of-ignorance.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
veil-of-ignorance.title: Reality versus Revolution
veil-of-ignorance.relation: McPherson argues political rap has never been politically revolutionary, sorting it into three schools: the amoral "gangsta Hobbes" ethic (Mobb Deep's "Survival of the Fittest", 50 Cent's "get rich or die tryin'") that sees the hood as Hobbes's state of nature where no social contract with blacks ever existed; Afrocentric communitarianism, split between nationalist separatists (Brand Nubian, X-Clan, Dead Prez) and the more cosmopolitan Native Tongues (De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest); and a radical liberalism closer to Rawls than its adherents admit. Against Chuck D's "What's a smilin' face when the whole state's racist?", he argues Rawls's original position, veil of ignorance, and difference principle - applied with real-world knowledge of racism - support rather than oppose Public Enemy's demands for racial justice.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
veil-of-ignorance.title: Mr. Rawls and the Decision Procedure
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Joseph Ulatowski uses Mr. Blonde's torture of Marvin to test theories of punishment. He argues Blonde is not a mere psychopath but a retributivist within his social code—punishing clerks who 'touched the alarm' and cops who violated Mill's harm principle—while distinguishing acting on a principle from merely acting in accordance with one, since Blonde acts from sadistic urges. After reviewing Kant's lex talionis and the utilitarian theory's flaws, he asks whether Hart and Sterba's Rawlsian 'retributivism as fairness', whose principles are chosen behind a veil of ignorance, could justify Blonde's actions, concluding Blonde could not by his own lights have done otherwise than punish.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
veil-of-ignorance.title: If I Were a Carpenter
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Butler asks what makes an activity work, testing the market definition against Socrates' refusal of fees, Aristotle's Politics, Arendt's labor/work/action distinction, Eva Kittay's care work, and the split between extrinsic and intrinsic value. He reads Cash's catalog through it: "One Piece at a Time" (the Detroit line worker stealing a Cadillac he builds but cannot afford), "Get Rhythm" (the shoeshine boy singing through menial labor), "I Never Picked Cotton" (escaping work into an empty identity), "Let Him Roll" and "Southern Accents," and the San Quentin monologue after "Wreck of the Ol' 97" where Cash refuses to be told what to play before inmates. The chapter closes by lining up Kant's categorical imperative, Jesus' Golden Rule, and Rawls's veil of ignorance: nobody would choose a society of company-store wage slavery without knowing they were not the worker, and Cash, knowing he stood on the stage rather than in the cellblock, used his freedom to side with prisoners and carpenters anyway.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
veil-of-ignorance.title: What Is Justice
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Johnny Huss extracts multiple theories of justice from 'Jacob Green'—desert (traced to Plato's Republic), equal treatment, conventionalism, and systemic injustice—and argues that desert collapses once responsibility is pushed back to factors beyond our control (Cash's God-given voice, the 'victim of the times'). Rawls's veil of ignorance supplies the standard for judging institutions: since anyone could be Jacob Green, we could not accept principles that let anyone 'get done like Jacob Green got done.' The chapter extends this to social justice for Native Americans via 'The Ballad of Ira Hayes' and 'As Long as the Grass Shall Grow,' including the flooded Cornplanter Tract, and closes insisting justice requires action, not just principles.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
veil-of-ignorance.title: The Politics of Difference
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Debra Jackson argues that despite its ethnic and gender stereotypes the Warcraft universe is structurally a Rawlsian liberal utopia: designers choose class balance behind a veil of ignorance, racial traits are symmetric, professions are open to all, and a difference principle guarantees even the most disadvantaged player a decent experience. Plato's Republic supplies the gender argument — as Plato made the soul rather than reproductive function the criterion for guardians, WoW makes gender irrelevant to gameplay. Yet players import real-world prejudice (anti-Gnome hate speech, female toons shunted into healer roles, mocked male Blood Elves), so structural equality never yields substantial equality: WoW is sexist and racist because we are.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
veil-of-ignorance.title: So Why Do I Support Aston Villa
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Rose—made a Villan by misreading a 1978 Panini sticker as Aston Villa's claret and blue—asks whether supporting Aston Villa is rational and argues ethics is far more like fandom than philosophers admit. Reasons for supporting Villa (local team, the 1982 European Cup, the colors) explain but never justify his allegiance, and the impartial procedures ethics prizes—the utilitarian benevolent spectator and Rawls's original position behind the veil of ignorance, with its 'sort of Kantian' consent-based alternative—turn out too demanding and too abstract: they would force him to donate his match ticket to charity, forbid the Premiership manager favoring his academy son, and reduce agency to the 'Rose-calcio scale' absurdity of switching to Real Madrid for rational reasons. His positive, communitarian claim is that we are thrown into social traditions whose inherited values—like a team—make moral agency and action possible at all, a 'different kind of rationality' that flirts with relativism yet still needs an exit strategy for cultures that discriminate against women or torture children.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
veil-of-ignorance.title: A Phenomenology of Reading the Ref
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Vannatta asks what the rules of soccer are from a player's perspective and tests legal theories: natural law and Rawls's veil of ignorance are too abstract to help on the pitch, and Austin's and Hart's positivism overemphasizes FIFA's top-down commands, so the best account is legal pragmatism — Holmes's bad man treats the law as a prophecy of what the ref will actually call, and Dewey roots the rules in custom and in the whistle itself rather than in prior legislation. Husserl's genetic phenomenology then explains how 'reading the ref' is possible: retention and protention synthesized in passive synthesis let experienced players anticipate play — and the referee's tendencies — without deliberation, replacing the impoverished notion of muscle memory. Playing to the whistle becomes a trainable skill of predicting an indeterminate despot, with lessons for coaching and sportsmanship alike.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
veil-of-ignorance.title: Homeland and Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.relation: John Fitzpatrick asks whether anything goes in war, using the FBI's killing of two innocents in the mosque and the ensuing official lie, plus Walden's strike on Issa's school. Truman's Hiroshima utilitarianism (saving lives overall) meets Anscombe's deontology - 'to choose to kill the innocent as a means to their ends is always murder' - before Rawls's social contract supplies a middle path: rules rational parties would agree to behind a veil of ignorance ('we won't kill your children if you don't kill ours'), which condemns both Nazir and Walden since neither faces an 'extreme crisis' like 1940 Britain. Brody's turn is itself Rawlsian: what breaks him is the unfairness of killing children as collateral damage.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
veil-of-ignorance.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
veil-of-ignorance.title: 18. Oppression Pretty Much Sucks
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Reads I Feel Pretty through feminist critiques of oppression: Bartky's Fashion-Beauty Complex turns the desire to feel pretty into a parasitic scheme of creams and credit-card debt, Du Bois's double consciousness captures Renee post-head-injury seeing herself as beautiful against the world's verdict, and Freud's account of hating those most like us explains the Highlander-style rivalry between women. The chapter then dismantles Rawls's distributive justice via Iris Marion Young, arguing rights are not goods to hand out and that 'imagine everyone is the same' thinking entrenches privilege. The alternative is celebrating difference, which is exactly what Schumer's prettiness-as-self-celebration performs.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
veil-of-ignorance.title: A Closer Look at Alice’s Trial
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Argues Alice is right to attack the court of the King and Queen of Hearts because she never entered a social contract with Wonderland: unlike Socrates, who stayed in Athens and so had to abide by the verdict (Plato's Crito), Alice fell in involuntarily and is trying to leave. Dennis Knepp casts the Queen of Hearts as Hobbes's absolute sovereign whose public 'Off with their heads!' terrorizes the playing cards into obedience ('Covenants, without the Sword, are but Words'), while Locke's limited, consent-based government and Rawls's contractualism mark the better alternative the Hearts court fails to meet. Since Alice stands outside their covenant, she is her own more-than-a-mile-high Leviathan, rightly defending herself in the state of nature.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
veil-of-ignorance.title: 3 Sins of the Fathers Historical Injustice and Its Repair in lack Panther
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Almassi contrasts Rawlsian ideal theory (the veil of ignorance, justice as fairness) with Charles Mills's critique that idealization marginalizes actual historic oppression, arguing the film's characters seek Aristotle's corrective justice in a world already steeped in wrongdoing: the 1991 deaths of W'Kabi's parents at Klaue's hands and of N'Jobu at T'Chaka's. He works through the Museum of Great Britain axe scene as restitution, W'Kabi's 'you kill him where he stands' and Killmonger's 'I'mma make sure we're even' as retribution (tested against Walen's proportionality principles, with vengeance untethered from legitimate punishment), and Nakia's and T'Challa's outreach centers as Margaret Urban Walker-style relational repair, reading T'Chaka's concealment of N'Jobu's death as actively constructed ignorance in service of isolationism.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
veil-of-ignorance.title: Notes
veil-of-ignorance.relation: When Lucy shouts the Golden Rule at the Ghoul after he dunks her in a poison river to bait a gulper, the chapter takes her appeal seriously and grades the rival 'rules' of the wasteland (the Iron, Arsenic, Neon, and Bronze Rules) before arguing the Golden Rule needs St. Francis's 'in a similar situation' clause. Kant's criminal-versus-judge objection disqualifies the unqualified Platinum Rule of treating others as they want, Nietzsche's charge that mutual restraint denies life is parried, and Rawlsian imagining of ourselves in divergent positions explains why family partiality like Lucy's search for Hank is consistent with the rule. The chapter closes with Lucy's saving of the Ghoul retold as the Good Samaritan parable, extending the rule even to enemies.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
veil-of-ignorance.title: NOTES
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Sharp argues that superpowered individuals break the equality assumption on which social contract theory rests: since Claire cannot be killed, D.L. can walk out of any jail, and Matt can sway juries, Hobbes's fear-of-death rationale for the contract seems not to apply to them. He then answers that the heroes remain effectively equal (Claire can still be killed by a wood splinter, Adam by decapitation) and shares Locke's and Rawls's reasons for contract, yet shows Rawls's difference principle would force the powered to serve society while the liberty principle forbids it, and that Sylar could not even be morally condemned under a pure Hobbesian reading. Cases like Claude's invisible petty theft (Glaucon's Ring of Gyges made real), the 'Five Years Gone' registered-superhumans future, and Linderman's plot to reunite society through the New York explosion lead to the conclusion that superpowers really would break society.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
veil-of-ignorance.title: NOTES
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Barnbaum treats the season 6 flash-sideways as counterfactual conditionals and evaluates them with David Lewis's possible-worlds semantics: in the closest possible world where James Ford's parents were still conned but he never became a grifter, Sawyer plausibly becomes a cop, whereas a world in which Jack fathers a child with Juliet demands too many extra changes to count as close to ours. She pairs this with Rawls's veil of ignorance - applied to dividing the crash survivors' water, where Jack's life-saving skill could justify unequal shares - as another famous hypothetical thought experiment whose conclusion rests on what people would agree to in the Original Position.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
veil-of-ignorance.title: NOTES
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Foy reads the Great Revelation and the Vampire Rights Amendment as a test of social contract theory: Nan Flanagan's 'we pay taxes, we deserve civil rights' invokes the Lockean bargain of obedience for protection, but Locke's God-given natural rights falter when the Fellowship denies vampires souls, and Locke excludes atheists and never imagined vampires. The chapter's resolution is Rawls: behind a veil of ignorance where deliberators might wake up vampire or human, anti-vampire bigots like the Newlins and supremacist nests alike would choose equal basic liberties plus distributive justice — including limits on vampires' centuries of accumulated wealth — so Sookie's 'let the law do it' to Rene marks a pluralist peace no theistic contract could deliver.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Stephen Kershnar examines the three strongest arguments for the IOC's ban on performance-enhancing drugs, harm-to-self, harm-to-others, and unfairness, and argues each fails, using cases such as Ben Johnson's stripped 1988 gold and Marion Jones. Against harm-to-self he cites anti-paternalism and the far greater accepted risks of NFL play and boxing; against harm-to-others he shows PED pressure is no different from the pressure of rivals' superior training (a Prisoner's Dilemma leagues need not solve); against unfairness he tests four accounts of fairness, including a Rawlsian veil-of-ignorance model whose choosers might find banning steroids while allowing Lasik and high-tech gear arbitrary. He concludes the ban, if justified at all, rests only on contested utilitarian grounds like audience preference and protecting children.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
veil-of-ignorance.title: Justice, Power, and Love The Political Philosophy of Intolerable Cruelty
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Biderman and Devlin trace Intolerable Cruelty through three theories of justice enacted by divorce attorney Miles Massey and femme fatale Marylin. 'Justice as power' is Thrasymachus's 'advantage of the stronger' and Machiavelli's might-makes-right, seen in Miles's courtroom war-room rhetoric and teeth imagery and in Marylin's plan to 'nail his ass' via marriage. 'Justice as compromise' is Hobbes's social contract escaping the state of nature, but the film shows the Massey pre-nup's signing and tearing to be merely a mask for power. When Miles and Marylin genuinely fall in love, their indifference to each other's wealth becomes a Rawlsian veil of ignorance and difference principle—justice as fairness—though the cynical Funniest Divorce Videos ending leaves that victory unguaranteed.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
veil-of-ignorance.title: NOTES
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Deborah R. Barnbaum reads season 6's flash-sideways as a set of counterfactual conditionals ('if Sawyer weren't a con man, then he would have been a cop') and uses David Lewis's possible-worlds semantics and his ordered similarity priorities to judge which are plausible. She argues Sawyer-as-cop is a 'closest world' change of one fact while Jack-and-Juliet-with-a-son changes too much to be true, and she pairs this with Rawls's veil of ignorance and A Theory of Justice as a parallel counterfactual thought experiment governing how the castaways should ration scarce water and medicine.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
veil-of-ignorance.title: Rebellion in Sala-ma-Sond The Social Contract and a Turtle Named Mack
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Novy uses King Yertle's tyranny and Mack's revolt to survey social-contract theory. Hobbes explains why turtles leave the war-of-all state of nature for an absolute sovereign, but Yertle, ruling only for himself, becomes 'no king at all'; Locke then justifies overthrowing him because a ruler who destroys his subjects' property and lives dissolves the contract. Kant grounds the contract in innate freedom, while Rawls's original position and veil of ignorance test Sala-ma-Sond for justice as fairness, and King's civil disobedience frames Mack's rights-claiming burp as demanding the contract be honored for all.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
veil-of-ignorance.title: Whose Egg Is It, Really Property Rights and Distributive Justice
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Cribbs treats the Horton-versus-Mayzie custody fight over the egg as a property-rights puzzle, applying Locke's labor-mixing theory (Horton's season of incubation versus Mayzie's laying and abandonment, plus squatter's rights) and its provisos against waste and taking more than 'enough and as good,' illustrated by the Once-ler and Hardin's tragedy of the commons. Adam Smith's invisible hand and the Wubble-chap's skilled labor defend market inequality, while Sylvester McBean's Sneetch exploitation, Yertle, and Marx's alienated proletariat motivate Rawls's veil of ignorance and distributive justice as a corrective to unregulated property rights.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
veil-of-ignorance.title: MOTHERHOOD
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Sara Goering uses the fantasy of a child 'off button' as a thought experiment, situating it alongside Plato's Ring of Gyges, the brain-in-a-vat, and personal-identity puzzles to argue that such control would be overused and would treat children as objects rather than developing subjects. She then turns reflexive, critiquing thought experiments themselves – including Rawls's veil of ignorance (via Okin and Benhabib) and Susan Brison's critique of personal-identity cases – for diverting from the messy real world, arguing that the off-button fantasy really signals the need for 'distributed mothering' and structural support; she illustrates with The Matrix, Multiplicity, Harry Potter, and Woolf's 'room of one's own.'

veil-of-ignorance.book: 279 - Christmas – Philosophy for Everyone - Better Than a Lump of Coal
veil-of-ignorance.title: Christmas Philosophy for Everyone
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Brophy prosecutes Santa for 'elfploitation,' treating the North Pole workshop like an overseas sweatshop (with Willy Wonka's Oompa-Loompahs and Rowling's house-elfs as parallels) and dismantling a Nozickian entitlement-theory defense: the elfs' 'consent' is coerced by their bleak alternatives, so absolute property rights fail just as Locke's desert water-hole owner must grant access. He diagnoses the elfs' apparent contentment as Marxian false consciousness, invokes Kant's humanity formula to condemn using rational elfs as mere means, and rejects the utilitarian 'greatest happiness' justification via Le Guin's Omelas and Rawls's veil of ignorance. He concludes with a call to boycott Christmas until Santa's labor practices become transparent.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
veil-of-ignorance.title: SERIAL KILLERS
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Brophy puts Showtime's Dexter Morgan on 'ethical trial' before the reader-as-jury, applying four tests. Utilitarianism approves because killing killers maximizes happiness (the Ticking Time Bomb analogy); Kant's categorical imperative and even Kant's own endorsement of executing murderers cast Dexter as a 'just executioner' applying a dark golden rule; virtue theory finds Dexter progressing toward moderation and flourishing as a 'warrior' in his social role; and Rawls's veil of ignorance suggests one would consent to Dexter patrolling one's neighborhood. Brophy concludes Dexter is morally excusable, perhaps praiseworthy.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: 1. The Good Place as Philosophy Moral Adventures in the Afterlife
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Engels argues that NBC's The Good Place, though premised on a merit-based afterlife, actually argues morality should not be grounded in afterlife reward. When Eleanor, Chidi, Jason, and Tahani learn the point system and can no longer earn points, they form the 'Soul Squad' to be virtuous for virtue's sake, echoing Aristotle's telos and Kant's claim that acting from fear of hell is a heteronomous, non-moral motive. She reads the unfair points system (no human admitted in 521 years) through Rawls's Veil of Ignorance and shifts the show toward rehabilitative justice, and treats the Good Place residents' boredom via Bernard Williams's tedium-of-immortality argument, with Chidi's 'wave returns to the ocean' speech mapped onto Hindu atman/Brahman and moksha.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: 6. Black Sails as Philosophy Pirates and Political Discourse
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Jones argues that Starz's Black Sails, a Treasure Island prequel set in the Golden Age of Piracy, dramatizes social contract theory as non-hypothetical practice. Captain Flint's drive to make Nassau a sovereign pirate commonwealth ('I am your king') channels Hobbes's state of nature and irrepressible sovereign, while his choice to settle Nassau and belief that people can thrive if left free channels Locke; his eventual plan to install Silver and Madi as liked-and-feared leaders synthesizes the two. Jones maps the pirates' familial bonds onto Rousseau and their responses to injustice (Vane's gallows speech, the maroon alliance) onto Rawls's Veil of Ignorance, and reads pirate 'articles' and deposable captains as radical democracy and equality, complicated by manipulation, slavery, and tolerance.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: 11. Futurama as Philosophy Wisdom from the Ignorance of a Delivery Boy
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Lewis surveys how Futurama's satire raises philosophical questions without taking sides. 'Zoidberg's Freedom Lesson' pits Mill's harm principle and free speech against Feinberg's offense principle; the mutants' and robots' oppression is read through Foucault's disciplinary normalcy and Locke's and Rawls's social contracts (state of nature, veil of ignorance). 'The Problem with Popplers' stages Bentham's utilitarianism, a might-makes-right food-chain view, and an intelligence criterion that commits Singer's 'speciesism,' with sentimentality winning. 'The Late Philip J. Fry' and 'Free Will Hunting' dramatize determinism, Nietzsche's eternal recurrence, and Sartre's existentialist free will, while 'Godfellas' and 'A Clockwork Origin' probe the problem of evil, fine-tuning, and Occam's razor.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: 14. The Doctor as Philosopher The Collectivist-Realist Pacifism of the Doctor and the Quest for Social Justice
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a 'collectivist-realist pacifist': morally opposed to war yet willing, as a last resort, to use lethal force for social justice. She places the Doctor on Cady's warism-to-pacifism continuum (past absolute and collectivist pacifism), augmenting it with Martin Luther King Jr.'s realist pacifism — ethical appeals 'undergirded by constructive coercive power' — and Gandhi's ahimsa and belief that no one is beyond redemption (the Doctor sparing Davros, offering enemies a choice). She tests Kant's duty ethics and respect for persons (Rule 1: the Doctor lies), Ross's prima facie duties, Mill's utilitarianism ('The Fires of Pompeii,' 'The Beast Below'), Gilligan/Noddings care ethics, and Wolterstorff's 'life of needs,' and reads 'The Day of the Doctor' as a Rawlsian veil of ignorance brokering Zygon-human peace.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: 44. Gattaca as Philosophy Genoism and Justice
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Grinnell argues Gattaca depicts a society built on 'intrinsic genoism' and diagnoses it with Rawls's justice as fairness. He adapts Appiah's distinction between racialism and intrinsic vs. extrinsic racism to genoism, showing that Valids like Josef, Anton, and Eugene treat In-valids like Vincent as inferior simply for being In-valid, discounting all counterevidence. Using Janet Radcliffe Richards's 'separate spheres' argument he shows the caste system is either superfluous or unjust, and via Kitcher's 'life theme' he argues nearly everyone — Vincent, Irene, Anton, Eugene — suffers a low quality of life from having their theme thrust upon them. He concludes that Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle would dismantle the separate spheres and give everyone a fair, autonomy-respecting shot at their chosen life.

veil-of-ignorance.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
veil-of-ignorance.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
veil-of-ignorance.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable.
