The twist is that the Grasshopper newsreels would give High Castle characters what we lack: evidence of how the same people act under different luck, so their characters could be ranked across timelines in a way largely immune to luck, where we must judge from actual conduct alone.

moral-luck.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
moral-luck.title: 10. Multiple Murderer Emily Middleton
moral-luck.relation: Treats Snatched as a series of case studies in personal responsibility: who originated an action, who created the situation, and what was intended. Emily's non-refundable tickets and drunken night out are hers, but she did not kidnap herself, and the film's title card ('The kidnappers did bad stuff, too') lures viewers out of victim-blaming. Her shovel killing of Morgado's nephew and accidental spear-gun killing of his son are judged through Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics III.2 on acts done in ignorance of circumstances, excusing the 'multiple murderer' while showing how perspective and intent shift blame.

moral-luck.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
moral-luck.title: 1. Is Perry Mason a Good Guy
moral-luck.relation: Muyskens asks whether Mason is genuinely good, noting his spotless record may be pure resultant luck: he never knows when he takes a case whether the client is innocent, as 'The Case of the Velvet Claws' shows when Eva Belter lies, tampers with the will, and even confesses to murder yet turns out to have missed. Using Kant's good will and Nagel's four types of moral luck (circumstantial, constitutive, resultant, causal), she argues outcomes alone cannot make Mason praiseworthy, then reads 'The Case of the Deadly Verdict' (his only loss, where he keeps investigating out of faith in Janice Barton) and 'The Case of the Terrified Typist' (where he engineers a mistrial for a guilty client) as proof that his commitment to justice, not his win record, is what makes him a good guy.

moral-luck.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
moral-luck.title: “Your Heart Knows”
moral-luck.relation: Argues that Disney's Mulan transplants a distinctly modern Western ideal of the authentic self ('true to your heart,' 'Reflection') into a Confucian honor culture where the self is constituted by roles and relationships, filial piety (xiao), and ren as the virtue that binds people into larger wholes — which is why the film flopped in China. The matchmaker debacle, Fa Zhou's 'I will die doing what's right,' and the family's shame show a culture where dishonor stains the whole family and even luck (the cricket Cri-Kee) fixes moral standing, conflicting with Western assumptions about individual responsibility. The chapter ends by noting Mulan now resonates with young Chinese viewers, asking whether the Western individualist self is a truth about humanity or a cultural export that, like the Huns, has scaled the Great Wall.

moral-luck.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
moral-luck.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
moral-luck.relation: Tyrion - born a reviled dwarf who killed his mother, yet heir to Lannister wealth, wits, and Jaime's knightly example - frames Nagel's paradox of moral luck: his compassion toward Jon Snow and Sansa is constitutive luck, and his carefully run wildfire defense of King's Landing shows resultant luck, since the same prudent act deserves praise in one outcome and blame had it burned the city. Kant's good will, applied to Tyrion's protection of Shae as treating her as an end and never merely as a means against Cersei, is offered as a rescue but only neutralizes resultant luck, leaving constitutive and circumstantial luck untouched. The chapter ends with Nagel's shrinking 'extensionless point' of genuine agency, concluding we cannot keep both moral responsibility and the principle that we are blamed only for what we control.

moral-luck.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
moral-luck.title: a18.xhtml
moral-luck.relation: Jensen dissects Bilbo's run of luck - the fish that leaps to his feet mid-riddle, the drunken elf-guards, above all his hand falling on the Ring in the dark - using Aristotle's account of luck as the rare, uncontrolled coincidence of ordinary causes (an orc leaving the back door ajar plus a hobbit's six-meals-a-day girth). He then deploys Nagel's kinds of moral luck: Bilbo's constitutive luck (born a Baggins with Took blood, Rawls' 'natural lottery'), circumstantial luck, and resultant luck (finding the Ring, which he could not control but which dooms Sauron). Against Kant's good will that is 'like a jewel' beyond luck and Plato's 'no harm can befall a good man', the chapter argues that Thorin's dragon-sickness, the orcs' unlucky birth, and Bilbo's outcome-dependent standing show that praise and blame do - and should - reach beyond the agent's control.

moral-luck.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
moral-luck.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
moral-luck.relation: George Dunn tests Katniss's luck-saturated life against Kant's claim that the good will shines 'like a jewel' regardless of fortune, with Peeta's vow to 'die as myself' as the stronghold the Gamemakers cannot touch, and with Seneca's dictum that what Fortune has not given she cannot take away. He then runs Nagel's four kinds of moral luck through the trilogy: Haymitch's reaping-made alcoholism as constitutive luck, Rue's death sparing Katniss an impossible final choice as circumstantial luck, Peeta's rooftop words echoing unconsciously behind the flowers for Rue as causal luck, and the revolution's success as resultant luck without which Katniss would have been the destroyer of District 12 rather than its torchbearer. Framing the Gamemakers as Fortuna on her wheel, he ends with the berries: since Katniss can never untangle whether she held them out from love, defiance, or self-protection, even moral worth proves hostage to luck and to the opacity of our own motives.

moral-luck.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
moral-luck.title: The Hero’s Responsibility
moral-luck.relation: White defends Tony against blame for Captain America's assassination: spearheading registration in Civil War was a tragic dilemma, and Tony took the least bad option because 'if not me, who?' — telling Cap's corpse he sacrificed their friendship to save lives. Cap's death traces through Crossbones, the mind-controlled Sharon Carter, Dr. Faustus, and the Red Skull, not any direct act of Tony's; without foreseeability or wrongdoing, the chain of 'might haves' does not add up to responsibility, just as pushing someone out of a truck's path does not make you liable for the manhole they fall into. The motivation-centered lens of Kantian deontology and Aristotelian virtue ethics supports Tony (he gave up status, friends, and Cap himself), and living with tragic choices, as he does facing the Hulk, is itself heroic.

moral-luck.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
moral-luck.title: Notes
moral-luck.relation: Kitchen asks who is to blame in a Wasteland where Nux's 'We're not to blame!' is the standing excuse. Blaster's death in Thunderdome illustrates the problem of many hands — no one, from Max to Ironbar, was sufficient and maybe no one necessary — while Nagel's resultant, circumstantial, and constitutive luck seem to excuse War Boys indoctrinated from puphood. Applying Frankfurt's freedom of action and freedom of the will together with Susan Wolf's Real Self view through three hypothetical War Boys (Maniac, Fanatic, Addict), he argues Nux becomes praiseworthy when Capable prompts him to reflect on and revise his desires, while Immortan Joe, Slit, and the other leaders are fully responsible.

moral-luck.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
moral-luck.title: Where Do We Go from Here – Buh‐Bye!
moral-luck.relation: Southworth asks whether SNL's dumb characters, the Ladies Man, Celebrity Jeopardy's Burt Reynolds, Ferrell's Bush, can be too stupid for moral responsibility. Aristotle's capacity for decision grounds moral agency; the Merit View, sharpened by Williams's constitutive moral luck and the Control Principle, blames Ferrell's deliberately nasty Connery but not the hapless Reynolds; and Mill's consequentialist view of praise and blame as nudges for 'progressive beings' explains Stuart Smalley's affirmations and Gilly's scoldings. Strawson's reactive attitudes finally resolve the puzzle: pitiable Bush is no proper target of blame, which is why we love him, though making him so lovable may have helped the real Bush escape accountability.

moral-luck.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
moral-luck.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
moral-luck.relation: Tallon uses the problem of moral luck (Williams and Nagel) to ask how blameworthy Peter really is for Uncle Ben's death: the Peter who let the thief go and the counterfactual Peter whose thief was caught at the elevator act identically, yet outcome luck makes the first feel like a murderer, clashing with Kant's Control Principle that only the good will has moral worth. Drawing on Williams's 'agent regret' and Susan Wolf's 'nameless virtue' of taking responsibility for consequences, the chapter separates culpability — Peter is guilty only of letting a thief go, with the intervening agency of the criminal breaking the causal chain — from responsibility for damage. Aunt May's own misguided confession that she caused Ben's death by arguing with him (Amazing Spider-Man #479) shows how virtuous people confuse involvement in a causal chain with guilt.

moral-luck.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
moral-luck.title: Notes
moral-luck.relation: Michaud puts Jar Jar Binks on trial for proposing the emergency powers that let Palpatine become Emperor and doom the galaxy. He weighs Nagel's resultant moral luck through a two-Lukes landspeeder case, Susan Wolf's virtue-based reply that equal fault can deserve different feelings, Kant's 'ought implies can' and the categorical imperative, and a Frankfurt-style scenario in which Palpatine's hypothetical mind-trick removes Jar Jar's ability to choose otherwise. The verdict: as a deceived, politically limited character trying to do good, Jar Jar is not guilty of the Empire's crimes - only of being obnoxious.

moral-luck.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
moral-luck.title: “Rebellions Are Built on Hope!”
moral-luck.relation: Eberl asks whether Galen Erso, who knowingly resumed work on the Death Star while planting its exhaust-port flaw, is culpable for the deaths on Jedha, Scarif, and Alderaan. A utilitarian defense (his flaw net-saved the galaxy, per the negative-responsibility principle applied to the Death Star II 'Clerks' debate) founders on moral luck — everything depended on Luke's impossible shot — while Bernard Williams's integrity objection, via the chemist 'George' case, condemns his betrayal of conscience. The chapter finally deploys Thomistic tools for cooperation with evil: because Galen's contribution was mediate and remote (Tarkin ordered the firing, the gunners pulled the triggers, Leia's defiance provoked Alderaan's destruction) and the weapon would have been built without him, his collusion is justified by the reasonable hope — the 'new hope' — of the Death Star's destruction.

moral-luck.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
moral-luck.title: 13. Time to Choose
moral-luck.relation: Goldberg and Gavaler read Superman's first-year Action Comics adventures (reforming the Blakely Mine owner, demolishing slums, buying back swindled stock) as consequentialism on Millian lines, and Batman's Detective Comics year (letting the Joker's victims die while 'the time isn't ripe', the batarang deflected by invisible glass) as a dark, vengeance-based cousin of Kant's duty ethics. Moral luck is the pivot — deontology ignores it, consequentialism is hostage to it — but Superman's powers cancel luck, and in the opening Luthor/Joker two-bomb scenario Superman defuses while Batman chases the villain, so the chapter rules Superman's 'super consequentialism' the superior code.

moral-luck.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
moral-luck.title: The Breaks of the Game
moral-luck.relation: Davison analyzes luck and fairness in basketball, using Dennett's claim that the more skill (control) a player has, the less luck is involved, so luckiness is relative to persons and times (a fan's half-court shot versus Meadowlark Lemon's). Distinguishing fairness as equality from fairness as desert, and invoking Bernard Williams's 'constitutive luck,' he argues that the game's mechanisms (spherical ball, jump ball, many possessions, referees) minimize luck, and that famous lucky plays like Robert Horry's shot, NC State over Houston, and the phantom foul on Scottie Pippen do not make outcomes unfair, since fallible human refs are a necessary part of the game.

moral-luck.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
moral-luck.title: On Fumbling the Ball
moral-luck.relation: Fry uses fumbles—Tony Romo's botched hold, Jerome Bettis's near-disaster saved by Roethlisberger, Leon Lett's showboating—as psychodramas illustrating the fragility of the good life. He invokes Aristotle's worry that one cannot call a life happy until it is complete, and Thomas Nagel's 'moral luck' (the negligent truck driver) to argue our culpability for fumbling, on the field and in life, is shaped by contingency, so responses should be discriminating. He draws on Frankfurt on caring and closes on redemption through effort, luck, and grace.

moral-luck.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
moral-luck.title: Where the Rainbow Ends Eyes Wide Shut Karen D. Hoffman
moral-luck.relation: Hoffman reads Eyes Wide Shut as Kubrick's most optimistic film, tracing how Bill and Alice Harford are 'awakened' to the uncontrollable power of sexual desire and thereby strengthen their marriage. Bill's Kantian confidence—that principled duty guarantees fidelity—is shattered by Alice's confession of overwhelming desire for the naval officer, which exposes their fidelity as mere moral luck. Through the models, Marion, Domino, and the anonymous masked orgy at Somerton (where sex is impersonal 'bodies touching bodies'), Bill seeks but fails to feel Eros; the couple finally choose a consciously chosen fidelity, and Alice's closing 'fuck' insists raw desire belongs inside marriage, which Hoffman links to Kierkegaard's view of marital love living and winning in time.

moral-luck.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
moral-luck.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
moral-luck.relation: Hoffman reads Eyes Wide Shut as Kubrick's most optimistic film, about whether marital fidelity can be chosen rather than accidental. Bill's confidence in his own and Alice's fidelity is a Kantian appeal - duty and rational principle over inclination - which Alice's confession of overwhelming desire for the naval officer, and Bill's night among the masked orgy, expose as vulnerable to uncontrollable desire and moral luck. Hoffman argues that by unmasking and honestly acknowledging these desires (and drawing on Kierkegaard on marriage existing 'in time') the Harfords consciously rechoose their marriage, so their fidelity is no longer merely accidental.

moral-luck.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
moral-luck.title: No Country for Old Men The Decline of Ethics and the West(ern)
moral-luck.relation: William J. Devlin argues that No Country for Old Men deconstructs the western's three ingredients (moral hero, comprehensible villain, redemptive showdown) and collapses the genre into Nietzschean nihilism. Where Shane's courage is legible through Aristotelian virtue-ethics and Kantian deontology, Sheriff Bell grows old and afraid, walking away rather than confronting evil. Anton Chigurh perverts deontology—killing on 'principle' and because he 'gave his word'—while his coin flips invoke Nagel's moral luck to disclaim responsibility, so the good/bad polarity dissolves and, as Ellis says, 'you can't stop what's comin'.'

moral-luck.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
moral-luck.title: 19. Can We Blame Jimmy for Being Jimmy
moral-luck.relation: The chapter runs Thomas Nagel's 'Moral Luck' argument on Jimmy, cataloguing his constitutive, circumstantial, causal-deterministic, and outcome luck (the con-man 'wolves and sheep' encounter, the Chicago sunroof children, the missed 1.6 million) to suggest we cannot fairly blame him. It then rebuts Nagel with a poker-and-wager analogy: since 'wagering on freedom weakly dominates' wagering on fatalism, we should treat character as cultivable through virtue theory's habits. It concludes that because nobody prevented Jimmy from changing and he has the resourcefulness to do so, his moral decline was unnecessary and blameworthy.

moral-luck.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
moral-luck.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
moral-luck.relation: Dadlez argues Austen gives a formative account of circumstantial moral luck (Nagel and Williams) via counterfactual character pairs. In Mansfield Park, the indolent sisters Lady Bertram and Mrs. Price share a character but differ only in fortune: wealth lets Lady Bertram appear respectable while poverty exposes Mrs. Price as a slattern, suggesting Hume's 'virtue in rags' has a counterpart, 'vice in dishabille.' In Sense and Sensibility, Marianne and Colonel Brandon's Eliza share a warm, unguarded nature, but a forced marriage ruins Eliza while family support saves Marianne. Austen deploys counterfactuals in both directions, showing respectability can hinge on luck and thereby mitigating blame as well as assigning it.

civil-disobedience.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
civil-disobedience.title: So, What’s the Bottom Line
civil-disobedience.relation: James Klagge, defining terms in Socratic fashion, distinguishes bootlegs like Great White Wonder from piracy and argues unreleased Dylan material (the New York Blood on the Tracks, "Blind Willie McTell," the 1966 Live concert) has genuine musical and historical value. He rejects the Sophist view that morality is just self-interest and the relativist "everybody's doing it" defense, then weighs the artist's Lockean property and privacy rights against fans' rights of access, noting legal-but-immoral and illegal-but-moral cases in the spirit of Martin Luther King's civil disobedience. His verdict: bootlegging is morally acceptable when royalties are fair, stolen tapes are not used, and mainly public performances circulate.

civil-disobedience.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
civil-disobedience.title: This Is Our World
civil-disobedience.relation: Miguel Sicart reads the 'Gnome Tea Party' — dozens of nearly nude gnome warriors parading in Ironforge to protest Warrior-class nerfs until Blizzard banned their accounts — as non-violent protest in the tradition of Thoreau and Gandhi. Against Blizzard's models of players-as-consumers and players-as-troublemakers, which he traces to Huizinga's Homo Ludens, he argues that players are Homo poieticus: creative beings who make the values they play by and act on them. Using the 'Flourishing Ethics' framework built from Aristotle's virtue ethics and Wiener's information ethics, he concludes that WoW's architectures of control and account-banning are an unethical design that damages players' capacity to flourish — Azeroth is our world too.

civil-disobedience.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
civil-disobedience.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
civil-disobedience.relation: Svolba and Flanders read Curb as an extended investigation of civility—the rules of what people 'just don't do,' from using the doctor's phone to touring Susie's new house to singing 'Happy Birthday' at Ben Stiller's party. Larry plays Socratic gadfly: refusing the tour harms no one and treats no one unfairly, and Susie's only justification ('it's just not done') is circular, so his incivility can seem admirable, even like minor civil disobedience. Against this, the chapter argues (crediting Cheshire Calhoun) that rules of civility are conventional vehicles for communicating respect for others' feelings and interests—what matters to Susie ought to matter to Larry—and, more consequentially, that a social world full of Larry Davids would be unbearable. Larry's own Golden-Rule litmus test, by which he never talks in movie theaters because he would hate it himself, misses this point, since civility is precisely about what others happen to want and like.

civil-disobedience.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
civil-disobedience.title: The Wire and Philosophy
civil-disobedience.relation: Cherry asks why even law-abiding citizens in The Wire obey the no-snitching code, answering through Cornel West's diagnoses: the police's 'evangelical nihilism' is Thrasymachus's might-makes-right acted out by Herc, Carver, and Prez at the Towers and by Walker breaking Donut's fingers, while the bosses' 'paternalistic nihilism' (Burrell juiking stats for Royce) leaves citizens not merely frightened but healthily hopeless, as Randy's 'You gonna look out for me? You promise?' shows after Herc burns him and the detail vanishes. Drawing on Angela Davis's argument that the criminal justice system inherited slavery's master-slave dynamic through the Black Codes, vagrancy laws, and the drug war, she reframes silence as active rebellion: a Gandhian philosophy of non-co-operation ('Fuck the Police') that withdraws the state's claim to citizens' dependence because witnesses like William Gant and Nakeesha Lyles are left unprotected.

civil-disobedience.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
civil-disobedience.title: 13. Kids on Civil Disobedience
civil-disobedience.relation: Guerra and Barkman argue the Party and Hopper practice Thoreauvian civil disobedience: the boys sneak out at night despite Hopper's explicit order, Hopper breaks into Hawkins Lab twice and exposes the fake body in the quarry, and the kids steal Billy's car to reach Will because 'a Party member requires assistance.' They accept Thoreau's point that disobeying unjust laws is right even at great risk, then distill three tests from the show for when laws should be broken: laws made with bad intent (the Lab's secrecy and human experimentation), laws contradicted by new knowledge (anything ignoring the Upside Down), and laws that block a greater good (speeding to save a dying stranger, trespassing to save Will).

civil-disobedience.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
civil-disobedience.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
civil-disobedience.relation: Alloy uses the problem of political obligation to split the heroes: against Plato's Crito, where Socrates refuses escape because even bad laws bind, Bruce Wayne simply flees arrest in Bruce Wayne: Murderer?/Fugitive, treating law as a tool of his war. He tests consent theory through Superman's chosen handcuffs in Man of Steel and Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's 'mortal god' versus Locke's natural-rights standard, lets Hume's objection sink tacit consent (Red Son Superman cannot really emigrate, and Batman would never leave Gotham), rejects gratitude theory via the Kents' adoption of Kal-El, and dismantles Batman's 'I'm not wearing hockey pads' defense with Nozick's Batman-lottery — concluding Superman's law-conforming restraint protects the public from him becoming Luthor's 'alien overlord', while answerable-to-no-one Batman remains a force of chaos.

civil-disobedience.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
civil-disobedience.title: Notes
civil-disobedience.relation: The Baggetts use Trent Crimm's 'Richmond Coach Cover-Up Revealed' - where he names Nate as his anonymous source for Ted's panic attack and loses his job - as a case study in journalistic ethics. They test the duty to protect sources through Kantian universalizability (which maxim?) and rule utilitarianism (keep the rule even when breaking it would help here), consider whether Trent's willingness to pay the price resembles Thoreau-style civil disobedience, and trace how Ted's authenticity converted a cynical gotcha journalist into someone looking for deeper, more meaningful work, ending with The Richmond Way's renunciation of self-promotion.

civil-disobedience.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
civil-disobedience.title: “That Community’s a Lot More Wholesome and Functional than, Just for Example, Neptune Is”
civil-disobedience.relation: Paul Hammond asks whether Veronica's habitual lawbreaking — switching the evidence tapes in the 'Pilot,' stealing Duncan's medical file, tricking Principal Van Clemmons — can be morally justified. He constructs a social-contract defense: Neptune's corrupt, class- and race-skewed sheriff's department under Don Lamb has failed to deliver the protection and justice that purchase citizens' obedience, releasing Veronica from her end of the bargain. Testing that defense against the Laws' speech in Plato's Crito (lawbreaking destroys the city; staying in Athens constitutes consent) and Kant's requirement that genuine law be universal, he concludes that where Neptune's civil law diverges from the moral law, Veronica's crimes can rise to a civil disobedience that is sometimes 'really just.'

civil-disobedience.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
civil-disobedience.title: XI - PROFESSOR X WANTS YOU
civil-disobedience.relation: Robichaud asks what a new mutant like Storm ought to do: join the X-Men, the Brotherhood, or neither. Distinguishing prudential from moral oughts, he argues desire-satisfaction beats Bentham's pleasure-pain account of well-being via an adaptation of Nozick's experience machine ('Eugor,' a child given Rogue's exact mental life), then evaluates both teams' agendas nonconsequentially. Building on Ronald Dworkin's three grounds for civil disobedience, policy-based, justice-based, and integrity-based, he argues peaceful persuasion is not obviously mandatory for mutants facing registration and a weaponized cure: resistance short of violence is permitted on all three grounds, and when the state turns lethal, even violent resistance becomes permissible.

civil-disobedience.title: Anarchism and the Beats
civil-disobedience.relation: Ed D'Angelo argues the Beats had a philosophy after all: a romantic bohemian anarchism that made poetry a means to a religious transformation of consciousness, with political change following consciousness rather than the reverse. He shows Ginsberg inverting Plato's rationalist hierarchy (grounding reason in imagination and the body) and reads Beat 'criminality' as a shamanic journey to the unconscious underworld, distinct from Mailer's macho 'White Negro' hipster. He traces their lineage through Greenwich Village bohemia, Proudhon/Bakunin/Kropotkin anarchism, and pacifist anarchists like Rexroth and Dellinger, arguing the Beats rejected Marxist materialism and class warfare, and that the movement was 'born' out of Rexroth's anarchist poetry circle at the 1955 Six Gallery reading of 'Howl.'

civil-disobedience.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
civil-disobedience.title: Rebellion in Sala-ma-Sond The Social Contract and a Turtle Named Mack
civil-disobedience.relation: Novy uses King Yertle's tyranny and Mack's revolt to survey social-contract theory. Hobbes explains why turtles leave the war-of-all state of nature for an absolute sovereign, but Yertle, ruling only for himself, becomes 'no king at all'; Locke then justifies overthrowing him because a ruler who destroys his subjects' property and lives dissolves the contract. Kant grounds the contract in innate freedom, while Rawls's original position and veil of ignorance test Sala-ma-Sond for justice as fairness, and King's civil disobedience frames Mack's rights-claiming burp as demanding the contract be honored for all.

civil-disobedience.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
civil-disobedience.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
civil-disobedience.relation: Yim argues that clothing is a primary vehicle for autonomy, authenticity, and moral solidarity. Drawing on Mill's *On Liberty* and 'experiments in living,' he treats a teenager testing modest-vs-expressive dress against her mother, and 'Fashion Freaks' patterns for wheelchair users, as cases where wardrobe choice actualizes self-determination. He then reads dress as an emblem of communal solidarity and critique — the 1968 Smith/Carlos Olympic salute, the Israeli Kibbutz and Amish plain dress (with Rumspringa as a test of authenticity), gang colors, hippie androgyny, vegan 'cruelty-free' clothing, gay Levi's 501s, and Lubna Hussein's trouser trial in Sudan — concluding 'we are what we wear.'

civil-disobedience.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
civil-disobedience.title: 2. The Dangers of Being the Doctor
civil-disobedience.relation: The chapter weighs the Doctor's ethic of interference against the Time Lords' non-interference, using determinism and the 'butterfly effect' (Martha in 'The Shakespeare Code') to concede when disengaged observation is prudent, while insisting that non-interference fails to protect human dignity. Drawing on Terrence Des Pres's account of dignity as 'inward resistance,' and real-world dissidents Adam Michnik and Václav Havel's 'power of the powerless,' it reads 'Rosa,' 'The Woman Who Fell to Earth,' and the people of Le Chambon as models of dignified, communal resistance to wrongdoing. Citing Iris Young, it argues everyone bears moral responsibility to engage rather than remain a detached, complicit 'objective observer.'

berlin-two-liberties.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
berlin-two-liberties.title: Synthesis
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Elizabeth Brake asks what freedom Dylan's outlaw persona - refusing Maggie's Farm, possessive love, and conformity - actually wins, framing the answer with Berlin's two concepts of liberty. Dylan's negations look like Berlin's negative freedom, but Hegel's critique of the "freedom of the void" shows mere refusal ends in emptiness, so she reconstructs a Millian and Emersonian ideal of self-realization for which negative liberty is only the condition. "To live outside the law, you must be honest" supplies the synthesis: outside social law the free person answers to the Emersonian law of his own nature and to undistorted honesty with others, a more severe morality Dylan shares with Emerson and Nietzsche.

berlin-two-liberties.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Rollin opposes mandatory helmet laws by contrasting two conceptions of freedom: the Hobbesian absence-of-constraint view ('go to hell in my own way', from Pinocchio's 'no strings on me' to the trapped coyote) and the rational-order view running from Plato (ranked classes, noble lies, censorship, contempt for democracy) through Rousseau's 'forced to be free', which Popper already identified as the enemy of the open society. Since, as the obesity-as-disease example and Robert Paul Wolff's expert-government argument show, we cannot claim certainty about value judgments the way we can about fractures, paternalism fails: if danger justified coercion we would have to ban motorcycles, skiing, parachuting, and bull-riding alike. Helmet laws in effect claim society knows what you ought to want better than you do, and Rollin's answer to his British colleague's 'what will you do if you injure your brain?' is to join the Department of Food Science and Nutrition.

berlin-two-liberties.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
berlin-two-liberties.title: 3. Click Bait for Black Fish
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Porot reads Elliot through Berlin's positive liberty: people are enslaved to their lower selves - the 'daemons' of addiction and primal urge Elliot describes in 'eps1.3_da3m0ns.mp4' - and freedom requires a contract in which an external force holds you to your higher self. Elliot writes such contracts with Shayla over his drugs and imagines Mr. Robot as the paternalistic enforcer who pushes him off the pier when he breaks his word, while corporations run the reverse contract, 'hacking' people from within through addictive sugar, clickbait, and advertising. The black fish dream crystallizes this: everyone at the office devours the confined fish of reverse-contract slavery while Elliot alone eats Pop's pie - freedom through the father figure of Mr. Robot.

berlin-two-liberties.title: 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Nash argues 1984 has been misread as a critique of state power alone; through Newspeak's silencing of thought (in the tradition Austin, MacKinnon, and Langton developed) it shows how any concentration of power oppresses via control of words, data, and information. Drawing on Goldstein's manual's debt to James Burnham's managerial revolution and Sheldon Wolin's 'inverted totalitarianism', she reads the non-centralized Oceania as a warning about non-state enemies: corporations, think tanks running the 'Tobacco Strategy', and global institutions peddling misleading poverty statistics. Popper, Arendt, and Berlin exemplify the state-focused liberalism she thinks blinded us to these horizontal threats, while the Newspeak appendix's past tense shows Orwell expected totalitarianism to be beatable through evidence and democracy.

berlin-two-liberties.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
berlin-two-liberties.title: 24. A Modern utopia
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Robin Bunce reads 2049 as a libertarian utopia realized: a Los Angeles without welfare, planning, or federal power, where Hayek's market knowledge and Nozick's minimal state have won and everything from water to children to replicants is voluntarily bought and sold. Yet the result is a slave state, and Nozick's freedom-as-non-coercion — the negative liberty Berlin also held — cannot explain Luv, the film's most privileged character, who is nonetheless a slave because her existence hangs wholly on Wallace's will. Quentin Skinner's and Algernon Sidney's neo-Roman liberty, independence from another's will, explains her fear, and the Baseline, like Orwell's 'Thou Art', reveals an ambition to enslave not actions but souls; Freysa's 'we are our own masters' is a republican declaration of independence.

berlin-two-liberties.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
berlin-two-liberties.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Lowe stages a 'Tolerance Bowl' between Sheldon's scientism and Mary's fundamentalism, opened with Berlin's liberal answer to pluralism — everyone entitled to their opinion, yet Sheldon insists 'evolution isn't an opinion, it's fact' and Mary's tolerance becomes its own tyranny. Davidson's argument that there is no very idea of a radically different conceptual scheme shows mother and son argue from shared concepts (DNA, intelligent design), but both remain metaphysical realists who cannot brook disagreement, while Rorty's 'the world does not speak' antirealism encourages fallibilist tolerance only to congeal into a 'what-we-have' dogma of its own that cannot account for genuine plurality. Nobody wins the bowl: each worldview makes tolerance hard in its own way.

berlin-two-liberties.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
berlin-two-liberties.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Goguen reads the Winchesters through two masculine ideals: the warrior (Dean and Michael, chivalric protection culminating in Dean's 'protecting Sam... it's who I am') and the sovereign (Sam and Lucifer, whose freedom is analyzed with Isaiah Berlin's negative and positive liberty, with nods to Hobbes's absolute sovereign and Nietzsche's Übermensch). The show's stoic culture, where 'baring my soul like a freaking girl' is an insult, keeps the L-word unspoken, making Ellen's dying 'I will always love you, baby' to Jo a foil the brothers cannot match. Plato's Symposium, via Aristophanes' myth of split soulmates, and Aristotle's claim that the purest love is between virtuous male friends make sense of the 'psychotically, irrationally, erotically codependent' bond, and the chapter concludes that true masculinity requires embracing the seemingly supernatural: love.

berlin-two-liberties.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
berlin-two-liberties.title: 23. Why Does Jimmy Get to Determine Chuck’s Healthcare
berlin-two-liberties.relation: The chapter uses Chuck's EHS to probe when paternalistic intervention against a competent person's will is justified. It argues Chuck is epistemically irrational (the hidden battery and electrified bed disprove his causal beliefs) yet notes, via Sharon Street and Nietzsche, that we all act on 'illogical' but coherent evaluative attitudes, so absurdity alone cannot license Dr. Cruz's push to commit him. Invoking Isaiah Berlin's warning against oppression in the name of someone's 'real self' and Mill-style concern for self-regarding choices, it finally uses Simone de Beauvoir to distinguish Jimmy's genuine devotion to Chuck from Chuck's controlling 'tyranny,' which shaped Jimmy's turn into Saul.

berlin-two-liberties.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
berlin-two-liberties.title: 12. Bourdain’s Taste for Freedom
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Porot and Simon argue Bourdain's goodness is best captured by virtue ethics rather than deontology or consequentialism, and read his life through Isaiah Berlin's positive/negative liberty (via MacCallum and Carter). They contend Bourdain's indulgence of his 'lower self' through addiction and excess was paradoxically the path by which his 'higher self' of empathy and compassion grew — echoing Hesse's Siddhartha, the Buddhist Middle Way, and Aristotle's mean — recasting his suicide in mystical rather than cynical terms.

berlin-two-liberties.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
berlin-two-liberties.relation: Hooke reads Serling's ambivalence toward the State through the liberal–libertarian debate between Rawls's A Theory of Justice (equal rights and the difference principle) and Nozick's Anarchy, State, and Utopia (the minimal state, wary of a central authority regulating personal life). 'The Obsolete Man' (the condemned librarian Wordsworth laughing before the Chancellor), 'Eye of the Beholder' ('The State is not God'), and 'The Shelter' dramatize the shepherd-paradox (via Foucault) and the danger of any state that crushes human dignity; freedom, like the Nietzschean laughter Wordsworth aims at power, cannot be defined but is known in experience.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
emerson-self-reliance.title: Synthesis
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Elizabeth Brake asks what freedom Dylan's outlaw persona - refusing Maggie's Farm, possessive love, and conformity - actually wins, framing the answer with Berlin's two concepts of liberty. Dylan's negations look like Berlin's negative freedom, but Hegel's critique of the "freedom of the void" shows mere refusal ends in emptiness, so she reconstructs a Millian and Emersonian ideal of self-realization for which negative liberty is only the condition. "To live outside the law, you must be honest" supplies the synthesis: outside social law the free person answers to the Emersonian law of his own nature and to undistorted honesty with others, a more severe morality Dylan shares with Emerson and Nietzsche.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
emerson-self-reliance.title: Tough and Tender, The Dead Keep Truckin’
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Gary Ciocco traces a line from Emerson and James through Kerouac, Ginsberg, and Neal Cassady to the Grateful Dead: Emerson's nonconformist 'infinitude of man' and James's 'live options' and religious appetite for being 'more fully alive' become, in the Beats, the project of living life itself as art ('the only people for me are the mad ones'). He argues the Beats splintered because each chased an atomistic, individual epiphany — Kerouac swinging wholesale from tender- to tough-minded temperament — while the Dead turned the same Jamesian hunger into a shared communal religious experience, a 'kindler, gentler' scene that better achieves Aristotle's eudaimonia. Cassady, muse of On the Road and driver of the Pranksters' bus, literally connects the two movements, but the Dead's unity-in-diversity made them the evolution, not the echo, of the Beats.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
emerson-self-reliance.title: Case the Promised Land
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Herstein reads 'Thunder Road' as an event, not an object: the screen door slam and Mary's waving dress form a single event that language can only serially narrate, and Whitehead's event ontology (with Ricoeur's Time and Narrative on how we discover and rewrite ourselves in stories, and Emerson's 'monstrous corpse' of memory from 'Self Reliance') explains why the Seanachie's tale creates a world rather than describing one. His own autobiographical turn — first hearing the song while stuck in a dead-end life, then at the 1980 Los Angeles 'Factory' performance watching Springsteen's voice resolve two warring rhythms by adding a third — shows narrative running backwards, retelling and redeeming the past, which is why the burnt-out Chevrolets are already behind the dirty hood. The solo-harmonica version strips away porch, vision, and redemption to desolation, yet the conclusion is freedom: because the events of the world await our creative retelling, you are the Seanachie of your own life, and 'maybe I am that young, after all.'

emerson-self-reliance.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
emerson-self-reliance.title: The Jihadist Way of Life
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Argues the Fremen are 'shockingly American': their Spannungsbogen self-discipline, spiritual self-sufficiency, and endurance of hardship exemplify Emerson's self-reliance, while the jihad's aim of razing the rule of the Great Houses into relations of equals echoes Dewey's democracy as a way of life—faith in the potentialities of every human nature. The parallel runs through the 'American Taliban' John Walker Lindh and Paul's blind walk into the desert, both acting on values Americans prize. Herbert's remark that people surrender judgment to leaders 'wrapped in the myth fabric of society' grounds the pragmatist point that Fremen myth-making, like America's exceptionalist self-image, works—and Alia's 'my brother is pragmatic' seals it.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
emerson-self-reliance.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Salvino casts Jobs as a billionaire egoist-visionary in the lineage of Adam Smith's insight that an entrepreneur's self-interest, not good intentions, best satisfies people's wants, Emerson's self-reliance, and Rand's virtues of independence and integrity—comparing Jobs to Howard Roark while noting his intuition was 'un-Randianly' unreasoned. Through Schumpeterian creative destruction (the automobile killing the horse-and-carriage; Wozniak's Apple I that HP rejected) and Deming's quality-first management, he explains Jobs's 'faster horse' contempt for market research, then rebuts the three standard ethical complaints—Foxconn labor conditions, his harsh verbal lashings, and his refusal to join the Giving Pledge—arguing Jobs did more good making the iPad than philanthropy ever could.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
emerson-self-reliance.title: 1. The Message of KISS
emerson-self-reliance.relation: R. Alan Siler argues that KISS's deepest and most consistent philosophy is a message of self-belief: work hard, believe in yourself, never give up. He traces it from 'Shout It Out Loud''s 'treat yourself like Number 1' and 'Flaming Youth' through The Elder's oath narrative ('only you are the answer') and its closing declaration 'I believe in me,' to Eric Carr's 'Little Caesar' and Carr's final backing vocals on 'God Gave Rock'n'Roll to You II,' reading Carr's scrappy rise and death as the Message incarnate. Siler contends the Eighties albums are the Message's peak and closes by showing how adherence to it organized his own life accomplishments.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
emerson-self-reliance.title: The Jihadist Way of Life
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Argues that the Fremen, despite their supposed Zensunni faith (which it argues was never a liberation theology), are quintessentially American: Emersonian self-reliance appears as spiritual self-sufficiency and the Spannungsbogen self-imposed delay, while Dewey's democracy as a way of life surfaces in the jihad's aim of replacing master-slave relations with relative equals under Shai-Hulud. It cites Herbert's 'Dune Genesis' on myth-making as pragmatically valuable and reads Paul, who ends Dune Messiah walking blind into the desert 'where we walk without footprints', as kin to the 'American Taliban' John Walker Lindh, whose conversion and jihad were driven by the same self-reliant, spiritual, pragmatic values.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
emerson-self-reliance.title: a21.xhtml
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Kraus argues The Hobbit is two different books depending on the reader's experience: read cold it is a fairy-tale of adventure, but reread after The Lord of the Rings - knowing what the Ring did to Bilbo and what 'precious' means - it becomes a song of innocence and experience like Blake's Songs and Wordsworth's 'emotion recollected in tranquillity', where Elrond's opening description points to the deep Silmarillion history a first-time reader cannot yet feel. Emerson's 'transparent eye-ball' from Nature - the self stripped bare and made original in the woods - becomes Bilbo's first use of the Ring, where invisibility lets him see Gollum's miserable humanity and choose pity; but the image darkens into Sauron's Lidless Eye, the totalizing knowledge that defines and devours selves. 'There and back again' thus echoes nostos turned nostalgia: Bilbo never truly gets back, having traded the child's innocence Thorin praises on his deathbed for an experience he cannot undo.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
emerson-self-reliance.title: Wilt Versus Russell
emerson-self-reliance.relation: O'Connor frames the boyhood 'Wilt or Russell?' debate as a version of Aristotle's Politics puzzle that a man outside community is 'either a beast or a god': is dominator Wilt a basketball beast or a divine king, and is executive-team-player Russell the higher human ideal? He links Wilt's romantic individualism to Rousseau ('J.-J.') and Emerson's genius awaiting 'practical power,' and Aristotle's discussion of the natural king to the coaching dilemma of whether to make a gifted player dominate or blend. He ends by rejecting Machiavelli's 'realist' dismissal of ideals, insisting the Russellite ideal of teamwork can be higher even when domination wins more.

emerson-self-reliance.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Scott Parker argues that distance runner Steve Prefontaine, who finished a medal-less fourth at Munich 1972, embodied the true essence of the Olympics better than any champion, an essence he identifies with Nietzsche's 'higher man' and Emerson's self-reliance rather than winning. He aligns Pre's front-running, effort, confidence, and will with Nietzschean self-overcoming and life-affirmation and Emersonian self-valuation, arguing value is what the valuer assigns himself through hard work. Reading Pre's exhausted stumble to the finish as a possible enactment of amor fati, love of fate, Parker holds that if Pre did his best he should love rather than merely accept his defeat.

emerson-self-reliance.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Couch reads two Eastwood gestures — Josey Wales's spitting and the Man with No Name's smiling — as expressions of self-reliance that generate a 'motivational polarity,' simultaneously repelling and attracting others. Drawing on Miller and Mason on contempt and disgust as moral attitudes, and on evolutionary coalitional psychology, he argues Wales's 'contemptuous disgust' (spitting on dead bounty hunters, at the Comancheros) marks moral boundaries and forms surrogate-family coalitions, while the Man with No Name's deceptive non-Duchenne smile in the Dollars trilogy conceals lethal intent yet occasionally shows genuine compassion (freeing Tuco). The self-reliant individual, adhering to his own moral compass, inevitably divides others into allies and foes.

emerson-self-reliance.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
emerson-self-reliance.title: Raising Arizona as an American Comedy
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Gilmore reads Raising Arizona as a classical comedy (bad-beginning-to-good-ending) about the American 'optative mood' of self-creation, using Hi McDunnough's outlaw-to-family arc and his name-as-height-metaphor to figure Emerson's aspirational American self. He deploys Plato's two kinds of cave-laughter to distinguish the film's 'tender,' welcoming comedy (Hi and Ed, Gale and Evelle) from mocking ridicule, and frames Hi's need to abandon outlaw identity via Heidegger's Augenblick and Badiou's 'event' sparked in Ed's mug-shot flash. Nietzsche on dreams-as-origin-of-metaphysics grounds the film's dream/reality tension, and Hi's over-identification with the outlaw universal is glossed as Sartrean bad faith.

emerson-self-reliance.title: The Dog that did not Bark Learning how to Read “The Book of Life”
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Biondi uses the silent dog of 'Silver Blaze' to teach reasoning from absence, arguing Holmes's 'imagination' is a cultivable art—Peircean abduction combining observation, background knowledge, and the virtues of independence, courage, patience, and impartiality. She traces how Holmes finds Silver Blaze at Mapleton and unmasks Straker as the horse's would-be nobbler by consulting 'the book of life.' Framed by Emerson's 'study nature' and 'know thyself' (and Aristotle on what holds 'for the most part'), she uses the Irene Adler and 'Norbury'/Yellow Face failures to show how prejudice and overconfidence blind even Holmes to alternative hypotheses.

emerson-self-reliance.title: “All in War with Time” Medium as Meditation in Sherman’s March
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Rhu reads Ross McElwee's Sherman's March—ostensibly a documentary about Sherman's Civil War campaign but really about a heartbroken filmmaker's search for love amid Cold War nuclear dread—through Walker Percy's The Last Gentleman and Stanley Cavell's The World Viewed. He shows how the film enacts Cavell's ontology of film (viewing the world "from behind the self," movies as reliefs from private fantasy) and the dialogue between perfectionism and skepticism Cavell draws from Emerson's "Experience" and Nietzsche and Kierkegaard. McElwee's deliberately unpolished, self-conscious "personal documentary"—stumbling on the riverbank, leaving in his own second thoughts—turns the war film into a meditation on consciousness, mediation, and being "all in war with Time."

emerson-self-reliance.title: Civilization and Its Discontents The Self-Sufficient Western Hero
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Den Uyl builds a composite philosophic picture of self-sufficiency from Aristotle's autarkeia (reason-guided virtuous activity, requiring external goods and civilization) and Spinoza's freedom as acting from one's own nature guided by adequate ideas, then tests it on John Ford's heroes. In The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance, Tom Doniphon is 'procedurally' self-sufficient in the precivilized West while Ransom Stoddard embodies civilized reason, and neither can inhabit the other's world. He argues the western's deepest value is Emersonian self-reliance—fidelity to one's own unique nature (the 'cactus rose')—which civilization threatens even as it enables Aristotelian flourishing.

emerson-self-reliance.title: 1 Primal and Spontaneous Neil Young’s Aesthetics of Authenticity
emerson-self-reliance.relation: Forest argues that Neil Young's habit of keeping early, flawed takes with Crazy Horse ("audio verite") embodies an aesthetic of authenticity as primal spontaneity. He reads Young through Emerson's self-reliance and trust in first impressions, Nietzsche's Apollonian/Dionysian split (Harvest vs. Tonight's the Night, Young's onstage abandon on "Like a Hurricane"), Benjamin's loss of aura in mechanical reproduction, and Collingwood's art/craft distinction, contending that the "garage band" imperfections of jams like "Down by the River" let fans identify with the band's expressive, un-repeatable moment.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: The Blessings of Tranquility
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Michael Chiariello takes Dylan's "the truth is true whether you wanna believe it or not" as a correspondence theory of truth, then rejects both the gospel-era absolutism of "Precious Angel" and the relativism (from Protagoras' man-the-measure to modern subjectivism) that would make Dylan's changes of course harmless. The alternative he defends is Pyrrhonian skepticism in Sextus Empiricus's sense: truth is objective but never fully assured, so suspending judgment yields tranquility. Dylan's career - from the ambiguous "Blowin' in the Wind" through "Watching the River Flow" and "Things Have Changed" to the two versions of "Every Grain of Sand" ("the reality of man" vs "a perfect finished plan") - embodies this balanced, non-dogmatic search the way of God designed it.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Over an evening at the Iron Post biker bar, Auxier maps four habitues onto the Hellenistic schools: Cowboy, the Vietnam chopper pilot whose bar is a Garden of modest pleasures, loyalty, and withdrawal from power games, is an Epicurean; the laconic Bear, who doubts that even possessing knowledge would make us better off and suspends judgment, is a Pyrrhonian (unlike the coffee-house Carneadean); Happy Jack, the 'true nature's child' of 'Born to Be Wild' who defies convention and keeps nothing six months, is Diogenes's Cynic; and Gary, the Vietnam-damaged recovering alcoholic, is a damaged Stoic who has not reached apatheia. He concludes that bikers are postmodern pagans whose philosophy is enacted rather than propounded, a Biker Platonism that refuses the Christian-Platonic divorce of body and spirit and lives by honor, freedom, and a pagan fatalism that accepts the consequences of one's choices.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: It-Getting The Truth about Truthiness
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Ethan Mills runs a 'Better Know a Skeptic' four-parter applied to the show: Pyrrhonian skepticism (Sextus Empiricus's suspension of judgment and living by appearances, played out in the Jon-says-worst-versus-Stephen-says-greatest Bush debate), Modern skepticism (Montaigne's fideist custom-worship and Hume's dream argument for why knowledge of couches, Doritos, and presidents is impossible), and Indian skepticism (Nagarjuna's circle that means of knowledge cannot be established without things known, illustrated with Stephen Sr. and Stephen Jr. as both father and son, plus Jayarasi's destruction of epistemology). He adds 'political skepticism' - the American sense that political knowledge is impossible - which breeds wikiality, an internet relativism ('reality we just agreed on') that the WØRD's own bullet points ('Wikipedia can tell a lie') undermine. Truthiness, he concludes, is Stephen's false cure for political skepticism: commitment without facts, a 'truthiness of the appearances'; but Sextus shows skeptics can still act on appearances without dogmatism, so we can vote and argue on the best evidence, as in Sagan's science-as-democracy, without certainty.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: What’s So Bad about Skepticism
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Mills argues that for the ancient skeptics skepticism was the cure, not the disease: Sextus Empiricus prescribes setting equally strong arguments against each other until judgment is suspended and tranquility follows. He reads Nagarjuna and Jayarashi as more radical, using contradictions to uproot the very impulse to hold philosophical views at all, weaning themselves from attachment even to Buddhist views. Applied to Dick, both approaches would have us stop agonizing over whether Deckard is an android or the Ubik characters are dead: the best way to stop worrying is to stop wanting the answers.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Brendan Shea reads Cohen through the three Hellenistic schools. Socrates's trial in the Apology mirrors the persecuted singer of 'A Singer Must Die,' with 'Everybody Knows' and 'Democracy' voicing a Socratic mix of empathy and pessimism about whether democracy can deal rationally with its critics. Stoics such as Epictetus ground the present-focused, resigned acceptance of loss in 'Hey, That's No Way to Say Goodbye' and 'If It Be Your Will'; the Pyrrhonian skepticism of Sextus Empiricus illuminates the narrator's calming, unresolvable ignorance in 'Famous Blue Raincoat'; and the Epicurean atomism of Epicurus and Lucretius - death is nothing to us, empty desires are unsatisfiable - underlies 'A Thousand Kisses Deep.' Hypatia's murder and Cohen's 'Joan of Arc' close the chapter: the examined life is an all-consuming, sometimes fatal commitment that is nonetheless worthwhile.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: 8. Tom Petty Didn’t Really Need to Know
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Zelinski and Fallis chart Petty's epistemic arc. His early songs ("I Need to Know," "Fooled Again," "Shadow of a Doubt") crave certainty about lovers' fidelity, a Desmond-free obsession closest to Descartes' quest for certainty beyond doubt, except Petty's problem is other minds, not the external world, and his trust that eyes directly reveal feeling sides with Moore's common-sense perception; Sartre's "hell is other people" names why another free person's future love can never be certain. From Full Moon Fever onward ("Into the Great Wide Open," "Time to Move On," "Learning to Fly") Petty instead embodies Pyrrhonian suspension of judgment and the Buddha's "don't know mind" and Daoist farmer's "we'll see," finding tranquility in uncertainty, craving nothing, flying with eyes open.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: 7. Beyond a Reasonable Doubt
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Jordan argues Mason's real superpower is logic rather than client selection or legal brilliance: since conviction requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt before a unanimous jury, and since by the problem of induction (traced from Sextus Empiricus's regression arguments through Hume) no accumulation of probabilities yields deductive certainty, the prosecution can never conclusively prove guilt while Mason need only exploit that structural gap, as in The Case of the Howling Dog's cab-driver and document evidence and the TV movie Perry Mason Returns where Della is the accused. He illustrates with modus ponens examples about Della and Hamilton Burger, contrasting sound deductive arguments with merely strong inductive ones like predicting Mason's next win.

pyrrhonian-skepticism.title: Inception and Perception
pyrrhonian-skepticism.relation: Jamie Carlin Watson uses Inception's dream thieves to stage the dream argument for skepticism - from Socrates' puzzle to Theaetetus and Descartes's Meditations, with Sextus Empiricus's diversity-of-perception argument - and contends that totems cannot debunk it, since even Arthur's loaded die and Cobb's top cannot rule out being in your own dream, where your subconscious knows how the totem behaves. Against both believing as normal and Pyrrhonian suspension of judgment, the chapter turns to William James's will to believe (live versus dead hypotheses) and to intellectual virtues drawn from Zagzebski and Kornblith: beliefs can be valuable for reasons other than truth. The upshot is that Cobb, Arthur, and the twelve shared-dream sleepers in Yusuf's basement can believe well even if they cannot believe truly - which is why Cobb's walking away from the spinning top at the end can be read as believing carefully rather than certainly.

cynicism.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
cynicism.relation: Over an evening at the Iron Post biker bar, Auxier maps four habitues onto the Hellenistic schools: Cowboy, the Vietnam chopper pilot whose bar is a Garden of modest pleasures, loyalty, and withdrawal from power games, is an Epicurean; the laconic Bear, who doubts that even possessing knowledge would make us better off and suspends judgment, is a Pyrrhonian (unlike the coffee-house Carneadean); Happy Jack, the 'true nature's child' of 'Born to Be Wild' who defies convention and keeps nothing six months, is Diogenes's Cynic; and Gary, the Vietnam-damaged recovering alcoholic, is a damaged Stoic who has not reached apatheia. He concludes that bikers are postmodern pagans whose philosophy is enacted rather than propounded, a Biker Platonism that refuses the Christian-Platonic divorce of body and spirit and lives by honor, freedom, and a pagan fatalism that accepts the consequences of one's choices.

cynicism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
cynicism.title: That’s His Story and He’s Stickin’ to It
cynicism.relation: Aaron Pratt places Buffett's 'island escapism' in the lineage of the ancient 'graceful life' philosophies: like Diogenes the Cynic, Buffett flouts social convention (pirates over Civil War generals, the beach over the rat race, 'Be good and you will be lonesome'), and like Epicurus he preaches pleasure with prudence rather than mere indulgence. 'Cheeseburger in Paradise' becomes Epicurus's command to know what you want and go get it, while the hung-over confession of 'Margaritaville' — 'I know it's my own damn fault' — supplies the Epicurean proviso that overindulgence ruins the pleasure it promises. The chapter closes by arguing that counter-cultures like Parrotheadism carry built-in safety features: careers and families force Epicurean prudence, keeping escapism a periodic liberation rather than social collapse.

cynicism.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
cynicism.title: Mr. Monk Meets Alexander the Great
cynicism.relation: Wittkower argues that Monk's daily, unwinnable war on dirt and disorder is Camus's happy Sisyphus made concrete: Monk vacuums ceilings, touches lampposts, and solves murders knowing the dirt and the murderers will always return ('There's never hope... Hope. I hate hope's guts' in 'Mr. Monk Can't See a Thing'), yet he still finds enough satisfaction to take up the wipe again. Reading Ecclesiastes' vanity alongside the uncaring wasp of the opening, the chapter claims Monk shows us how to live wisely without resignation in an absurd world that does not care. He is paired with Diogenes the Cynic, whose barrel, raw onions, and midday lantern mirror Monk's pot-pie-Tuesdays and his refusal to overlook what everyone else ignores; like Diogenes telling Alexander the Great 'get out of my sun,' Monk lives by his own ideals no matter how society judges him. The essay closes that, like Camus addressing the Dominican monks, we should refuse to 'be reasonable' about evil and disorder and keep struggling without hope, wipe in hand.

cynicism.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
cynicism.title: A Newspaper Gone to the Dogs . . . Enlightened Dogs
cynicism.relation: Bayan traces 'cynic' to the Greek kynikos ('doglike') and the philosophy to Socrates' virtue, poverty, and integrity, through the proto-Cynic Antisthenes to Diogenes of Sinope—the man in the tub, the plucked chicken at Plato's Academy, 'you can step out of my sunlight'—arguing that Cynicism is fierce moral opposition to sham and hypocrisy, which is exactly why the powerful smear cynics. Distinguishing The Onion's cool, Swiftian irony from postmodern 'pseudocynicism,' he concludes the paper is genuinely Cynical: headlines like 'Black Guy Asks Nation for Change' (the Obama reveal), 'God Angrily Clarifies Don't Kill Rule,' and 'Dictator Slays Millions in Last-Minute Push to Be Time's Man of the Year' nuzzle the kind, bark at the greedy, and bite scoundrels, so Diogenes would have read The Onion with paternal fondness.

cynicism.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
cynicism.title: A Nonsense Too Far
cynicism.relation: Places Carroll's nonsense in a Greco-Roman tradition of philosophically useful absurdity: Socrates exposing Euthyphro's definitions of piety as nonsense, Plato's tongue-in-cheek Republic calculation that the tyrant's life is 729 times worse, and Diogenes ridiculing slavery even while sold on the auction block. Charles Taliaferro and Elizabeth Olson argue the jokes land only because Alice stays sane, curious, polite, and self-controlled, the stable foil who keeps the death threats and cruelty of Wonderland and the Looking-Glass on the amusing side of the ledger, and that nonsense goes 'too far' in Kafka's The Trial, where losing the sane, good center turns absurdity into meaninglessness.

cynicism.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
cynicism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
cynicism.relation: Bárcenas answers studies suggesting The Daily Show breeds youth cynicism by recovering the original 'dog philosophy': Cynics like Diogenes of Sinope lived shamelessly (the bathtub, the lamp in broad daylight, 'stand out of my light' to Alexander the Great) to expose the corrupt conventions of Athens's fragile direct democracy, where demagogues like Alcibiades seduced the assembly into debacles such as the Sicilian expedition. He reads Stewart as their modern heir, with 'Mess O' Potamia' and 'Crises in Israfghyianonanaq' against war demagoguery and the Cramer interview against financial-media dereliction, whose humor aims at Aristotle's anagnorisis, a sudden recognition of things as they really are behind flattering appearances (doxa). Cynical unpopularity (adoxia) is worn as a badge of truth-telling, and parrhesia, frank speech, becomes democratic shock therapy that awakens citizens' judgment rather than breeding apathy.

cynicism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
cynicism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
cynicism.relation: Presents three ancient alternatives to SAMCRO's warrior ethic. Diogenes the Cynic, 'the earliest of all the fathers of anarchy,' matches J.T.'s Harley-commune ideal — reject greed, convention, and wage slavery like Tig punching the clock at Teller-Morrow — but the chapter argues pure anarchy regenerates hierarchy: with no authority, revenge becomes the only justice and 'a big guy like Clay' mugs 'a small guy like Chuckie.' Plato's Republic supplies the reformist pole — impartial justice for all citizens rather than loyalty circles, rulers picked from proven warriors for wisdom (Tara belongs healing, not scheming), family curbed where it breeds Gemma-style favoritism — yet proves too authoritarian, so Aristotle's function argument (reason as the human ergon), virtue, and the three kinds of friendship (SAMCRO's pleasure-friendships, Clay–Unser's usefulness) sketch a livable middle way with duties even to strangers.

cynicism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
cynicism.title: 11. A Punk by Any Other Name would Smell as Rotten
cynicism.relation: Grewal treats punk as a comedy of self-negation - a counter-culture that must negate even itself - and traces its lineage through Plato's Leontius story (thumos, the spirited part of the soul, dividing a man against his own eyes as he gorges on corpses, punks as 'living dead') to Diogenes the Cynic, 'Socrates gone mad', whose exile, public masturbation, dog-persona, and mocking of Plato make him Diogenes the Punk. Beauvoir's adulteress from The Second Sex and Rousseau of the Reveries supply the punk logic of adultery and exile - a continual breaking of attachments down to Socrates's barefoot ignorance - so that punk, mocking any ascent from the cave, becomes the ruthless pursuit of the rootless.

cynicism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
cynicism.title: 14. Revolting Punks
cynicism.relation: Innes unpacks the double meaning of 'revolting': punk's obscenity, three-minute seven-inch singles on independent labels, beer-can-and-burrito gigs at Randy's Rodeo, and Vivienne Westwood bondage wear are revolt in the original sense - and a revival of Diogenes's cynicism, which rejects Plato's abstract virtue and the Glaucon-style social contract (the Ring of Gyges showing justice is only for the visible) for virtue according to nature. Hippies and prog rock are the sold-out establishment (Dead Kennedys' 'California Über Alles' against Jerry Brown), and satire - Johnny Rotten's lit lamp searching for an honest man - is the Cynic's serious joke, ending in chosen, communal virtue.

cynicism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
cynicism.title: 22. Punk Rock Saves Lives
cynicism.relation: R.W. Main argues punk saves lives by replacing the myth of purity - the ideal behind one-drop rules, eugenics, and moral exclusion - with a philosophy of filth that revalues the rejected and abject, letting the outcast reclaim agency. He stages Diogenes the Cynic's street-living, shameless filth as the original punk counterpoint to Plato's perfect Forms and philosopher-king (Plato the 'sell-out'), and enlists Nietzsche's claims that morality denies life while art saves it. Camus's Sisyphus closes the argument: punk's freedom is revolt, giving the gods the middle finger since 'there is no fate that cannot be surmounted by scorn'; more concretely, punks save lives as anti-bullies, the 'Duncan Effect' of Some Kind of Wonderful and SHARPS skinheads protecting misfits.

cynicism.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
cynicism.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
cynicism.relation: Alejandro Bárcenas rehabilitates the charge that Stewart breeds cynicism by recovering ancient Cynicism, the 'dog philosophy' of Diogenes of Sinope, who used shamelessness (anaideia) and free speech (parrhesia) to 'deface the currency' of corrupt convention. He parallels Diogenes confronting Philip and Alexander ('stand out of my light') with Stewart's 'Clusterf#@k to the Poor House' and his Cramer/CNBC challenge, arguing that, like the Cynics continuing Socrates' gadfly role, Stewart's outrageous humor aims at anagnorisis—Aristotle's sudden recognition of truth—making dog philosophy democracy's best friend rather than its enemy.

cynicism.title: Chapter 12 The American Diogenes
cynicism.relation: Johnson argues Twain is best understood not as a religious skeptic but as an 'American Diogenes'—a Cynic of Christianity-as-practiced. As Diogenes 'defaced the coinage' to remove counterfeit customs, Twain uses 'sacred profanity' (honest, even profane speech that exposes phony piety, e.g. the swearing butcher, Satanic narrators in 'The Mysterious Stranger' and 'Letters from the Earth') to strike four counterfeit coins: superstition/special providence, hypocrisy, artificial 'Moral Sense'/conscience, and heavenly rewards. On death Twain matches Diogenes and Epicurus (annihilation is nothing to fear), and his self-description as 'Member at Large for the Human Race' mirrors Diogenes the cosmopolitan; Diogenes carries a lantern to find a real human, Twain a mirror to show we are worse than we think.

cynicism.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
cynicism.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
cynicism.relation: Pierlott examines sweatshops in the garment industry through the lens of ancient Cynicism (Antisthenes, the Stoics' Zeno of Citium and his thieving slave), using the Cynic critique of fashion-driven consumption to strip legitimacy from the demand that feeds sweatshops. He rebuts the 'inevitability argument' (comparing it to excusing the Holocaust as inevitable) and the free-choice defense using Aristotle's category of 'mixed' action — sweated workers' consent is coerced by desperate alternatives — and argues, via Adam Smith on the undervaluing of labor, that giant retailers like Wal-Mart distort natural labor prices. He stresses that sweatshops overwhelmingly exploit young women, tying objectification of women as fashion consumers to their oppression as producers.

institutional-theory-of-art.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
institutional-theory-of-art.relation: Responding to the Guggenheim's record-breaking 'The Art of the Motorcycle' show, Rollin argues that Dickie's institutional theory explains how motorcycles became art but not why people lined up, and offers three aesthetic lenses: Marinetti's Futurist celebration of machine speed, danger, and rebellion; Dewey's 'an experience', which every ride exemplifies, from his two-week trips with his son to the blown engine rescued by a ranch truck and the canned-spaghetti feast; and the Bauhaus doctrine that form follows function, making customized Harleys industrial sculpture that appreciates in value. He closes with Heidegger: riding's regular face-to-face with 'the possibility of the impossibility of one's being' is a call to authenticity and the final warrant for calling the motorcycle a fountain of aesthetic experience. American Indians revering Harleys as 'iron horses' illustrate the freedom and speed at the core of the bike's aesthetic pull.

institutional-theory-of-art.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
institutional-theory-of-art.title: 15. You Can’t Use My Name
institutional-theory-of-art.relation: Recounts how Hendrix changed law twice: ExperienceHendrix v. PPX (the 'You can't use my name' tapes) imported the Wrotham Park/Blake standard so breach-of-contract damages can reflect the infringer's gains rather than the victim's losses, and Experience Hendrix v. Hendrixlicensing.com used Washington's Personality Rights Act to extend postmortem publicity rights beyond the state of domicile, raising the constitutional problems Rossi identifies. The chapter then reads the dispute over whether the Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' is art or noise through legal realism versus natural law theory and legal positivism — law as what courts actually enforce — and through the Institutional Theory of Art, with a Wittgensteinian cluster definition marking the essentialist route that failed.

institutional-theory-of-art.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
institutional-theory-of-art.title: The Simpsons Already Did It! This Show Is A Freakin' Rip-Off!
institutional-theory-of-art.relation: Takes up South Park's 'Simpsons did it!' charge and argues Family Guy is not a rip-off but a postmodern artwork: it tests representation, expression, and form theories of art (Hamlet, Guernica, sonnet form) and finds the show fails all three, since a martini-sipping college-educated dog and non-narrative cutaways fit none. Following Danto, Lyotard, and Baudrillard, it claims the show deliberately raises 'what is art?' while dissolving original and copy into hyperreality: Peter worships the Fonz and builds him a church in 'The Father, the Son, and the Holy Fonz,' lives inside television with a cardboard frame in 'I Never Met the Dead Man,' and 'Da Boom' turns out to be Pam Ewing's dream, so the obvious borrowing from The Simpsons is the point, like Warhol's Brillo Boxes or Duchamp's L.H.O.O.Q.

institutional-theory-of-art.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
institutional-theory-of-art.title: Something's Missing
institutional-theory-of-art.relation: Malloy tests three theories of art against Sabine Wren's graffiti and the Syndulla Kalikori: representation fails (her work is stylized beyond recognition and the collaborative Kalikori depicts nothing), expression fails (generations of makers make the Kalikori's expressive unity mysterious), and the institutional 'artworld' theory fails because Thrawn's curatorial authority destroys what it preserves — ripping a phoenix tag off its wall or displaying a still-growing Kalikori strips them of meaning. He concludes that defining art by any single feature (content, creation, or institutional context) is doomed, since Sabine's and Hera's works both are and are not art on every theory, and philosophy must keep searching for why they count as art.

camus-revolt.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
camus-revolt.relation: Pratt reads the outlaw biker's FTW (Fuck the World) posture as pop-culture nihilism: Nietzsche's 'danger of dangers' and Camus's answer of scorn to an absurd universe ('there is no fate that cannot be surmounted by scorn') are embodied by Brando's Johnny in The Wild One, Sonny Barger's Hells Angels, and the wanton Born to Lose club of The Born Losers, whose smashing matches Pisarev's Russian nihilism. He then shows how Willie G. Davidson's 1977 Low Rider and events like Daytona's Bike Week sanitized and marketed the rebellion, reducing skulls and DILLIGAF patches to ubiquitous fashion worth $340 million a week. Freud supplies the psychology: the superego keeps the rest of us tame, so we voyeuristically buy a tasteful version of outlaw freedom, even though pure nihilism, denying all truth, refutes even itself.

camus-revolt.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
camus-revolt.title: Would You Help Me to Carry the Stone
camus-revolt.relation: Weinstein argues critics who call Waters a gloomy misanthrope misread him: he is an existentialist whose work maps point for point onto Camus's absurd, the human demand for unity endlessly frustrated.
