trolley-problem.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
trolley-problem.title: 14. Is Kant the Reason Everyone Hates Moral Philosophy Professors
trolley-problem.relation: Defends Kant against the charge that he is why everyone hates moral philosophy professors: it explains the two-question Categorical Imperative test via frozen-yogurt maxims and Eleanor's selfish 'won't help unless it benefits me' principle, shows Kant never actually forbade lying to the murderer at the door (his crotchety 'On a Supposed Right to Lie' was an obscure legal point), and reads Chidi's trolley-track switch but refusal to harvest Eleanor's organs as the humanity formula — never treat a person merely as a means. Tahani's $60 billion in charity and Eleanor's failed point-chasing in 'What's My Motivation?' illustrate the good will: deeds lack moral worth unless done for the right reasons. Aristotle explains the residual puzzle — theory mastery does not make you skilled at ethical practice, any more than a nutritionist is a great cook.

trolley-problem.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
trolley-problem.title: The Witcher's Code
trolley-problem.relation: Barta and Lee ask whether Geralt's quandaries are genuine conflicts of incommensurable duties or only apparent ones. An Idr-baiting variant of Foot and Thomson's trolley problem opens the analysis; the Blaviken conflict between Renfri and Stregobor, Nivellen and the bruxa Vereena, and the djinn's three wishes are read through Bernard Williams's view that tragic, remainder-generating conflicts are ineliminable, with Sartre's student example and Nietzsche's 'antagonism in the heart of the world' backing the tragic reading. Against this, the Striga-Adda curse and the contradictory duel commands of Sir Tailles show dilemmas dissolved by culpable origins, third options, or one duty overriding another, and the chapter concludes Geralt wisely treats every dilemma as if it were apparent.

trolley-problem.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
trolley-problem.title: Lesser of Two Evils
trolley-problem.relation: Horn reads the Blaviken conflict as a clash of two utilitarianisms: Stregobor locks up women born during the black sun on Benthamite grounds that maximizing humanity's happiness justifies evil, while Renfri's revenge on Stregobor follows Popper's negative utilitarianism of minimizing suffering, and Foot's runaway trolley shows both reasoning toward killing the one. Le Guin's Omelas, with its tortured child beneath a utopia, exposes where Stregobor's and Renfri's 'lesser evil' logic leads. Geralt rejects both because he deliberates as Raff Donelson's ethical pragmatist: he accepts the facts but tests options against the shared Witcher's Code values (kill only to save, never from fear), which is why he prefers not to choose at all.

trolley-problem.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
trolley-problem.title: So, Case Closed – Right
trolley-problem.relation: White asks why Batman won't kill the Joker, framing it through utilitarianism (killing one to save the Joker's many future victims) versus deontology (killing is wrong regardless of consequences). Using Foot and Thomson's trolley and transplant cases, plus agent-neutral versus agent-relative rules, he notes key disanalogies: the Joker is not a moral innocent but the very cause of the danger, which pushes toward killing him. But because future killings are only probable, doing so would be 'prepunishment,' and White, a self-described deontologist, concludes it is genuinely hard to say Batman is right, though he admires the restraint.

trolley-problem.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
trolley-problem.title: SERIAL KILLERS
trolley-problem.relation: Terjesen critiques the 'lack of empathy' explanation of serial killing by disentangling empathy into understanding, vicarious feeling, and connection, and showing each either is possessed by killers or leads to circular reasoning (citing Deigh's 'mature empathy' and autism as a counterexample). Real killers like Dahmer, Rader, and 'Angels of Death' such as Cullen and Harvey act from sexual desire, rage, or even excessive empathy, so empathy shapes how they kill (intimate vs. distancing methods, echoing Greene's trolley/footbridge study) rather than whether they kill. He favors Kennett's lack-of-impulse-control and poor risk-assessment account instead.

trolley-problem.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
trolley-problem.title: So, Case Closed – Right
trolley-problem.relation: Mark White asks why Batman doesn't kill the Joker, using the question to contrast utilitarianism (kill one to save the Joker's future victims) with deontology (killing is wrong regardless of consequences), and Batman's own agent-centered refusal. He runs Foot and Thomson's trolley problem and the transplant surgeon case, then modifies them: the Joker is the guilty one who created the danger, his future victims are uncertain, and killing him would be 'prepunishment' for crimes not yet committed. White, a self-described deontologist, concludes the case is genuinely hard and admits great good might have come from killing the Joker, using comics as thought experiments about killing to prevent future killing.

drowning-child.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
drowning-child.title: So, What Have Philosophers Ever Done for Us
drowning-child.relation: Taylor defends philosophy's bizarre examples against critics like Leon Kass by comparing them to Python's self-reflexive comedy: the 'Complaints' sketch's regress of complaints-about-complaints mirrors how thought experiments make us the audience of our own thinking, as with two coalmine trolley cases that pressure a simple 'minimize pain' utilitarianism toward rule utilitarianism. The 'Police Station' sketch, where it would be better if mad Angus's carnivorous-blancmange story were false, is itself a counterexample to 'always tell the police the truth', and 'The Visitors' stale three-year-old drink invitation undermines the claim that 'inviting in' a fetus creates duties, sharpening Thomson's violinist argument that a right to life does not include a right to another's body. Singer's drowning-child style example and Thomson's violinist show that far-fetched cases clarify practical issues like abortion and famine relief precisely by detaching them from clouding emotion, and the Life of Brian 'What have the Romans ever done for us?' scene supplies the answer: philosophers' examples clarify our views, test them, and are amusing.

drowning-child.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
drowning-child.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
drowning-child.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman contrasts two pop-culture templates: Buffy's vampire brothel, where willing humans pay vampires for consensual bites (Giles calls the customers 'willing victims'), and Blade's implied government blood bank, where humans are forced to donate. Running Robert Nozick's personhood criteria (sentience, rationality, free will, moral agency, soul) against vampires, he argues no standard admits humans while excluding them, so staking vampires violates rights and, on Singer's suffering-equals-suffering logic, refusing consideration is a kind of speciesism. The welfarist side - Singer and Unger's principle that we must prevent bad at little cost, as in the drowning child - would mandate Blade-style forced blood transfers, but Whitman contends such coercion breeds the very xenophobia (Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules, anti-immigrant welfare politics) that blocks recognizing vampire personhood. Only a libertarian market of voluntary exchange turns human-vampire relations from a zero-sum war into a positive-sum commerce.

drowning-child.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
drowning-child.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
drowning-child.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman uses Buffy's vampire brothel (humans paying vampires to feed on willing victims, as Giles concedes) and Blade's mandatory blood bank as two models of human-vampire coexistence to stage the clash between libertarianism (Nozick, Lomasky, Schmidtz) and welfarism (Singer, Unger, G.A. Cohen). He runs vampire personhood through Nozick's criteria from Anarchy, State, and Utopia — sentience, self-consciousness, rationality, free will, moral personality, soul — and argues no standard includes humans while excluding vampires, applying Singer's equal-consideration-of-suffering principle across kinds of beings. He then extends Singer's obligation-to-aid reasoning (rescuing a drowning child vs. donating to UNICEF) to show welfarism would mandate forced blood transfers or 'blood stamps', and argues via Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules and modern welfare-based anti-immigration politics that the burden of supporting dependents breeds exclusion. Only the libertarian brothel model of voluntary exchange, he concludes, turns vampire-human relations into a positive-sum game in which humans would actually come to recognize vampires as persons.

drowning-child.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
drowning-child.title: 11 - The Friendship that Makes No Demands
drowning-child.relation: Tedesco sets Facebook's demand-free friendship against the modern moral requirement of impartiality, running from Godwin's burning-archbishop case through Bentham's 'everybody to count for one, nobody for more than one' and Williams's 'one thought too many' objection. He canvasses the escapes - Mill's rarely-demanded public benefactor, Singer's global village where aid is a click away, Jackson's sector plan and Railton's sophisticated consequentialism - and finds each inadequate to friendship's partiality. Facebook friendship looks like a third way that reconciles the two, but it turns out only to be friendship where it supplements a real offline relationship, so the impartiality problem stands.

drowning-child.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
drowning-child.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
drowning-child.relation: Runs Walt's choices through consequentialist machinery: his cost-benefit habit (the $737,000 target, 'non-sustainable business model'), the Krazy-8 pros-and-cons list, and whether manufacturing meth harms users or merely enables them. It argues act consequentialism fails on unforeseen consequences (Hank killing Tuco helps Heisenberg; the tow-truck driver aids a murder), defends rule consequentialism via Tuco - rational for him, disastrous as a universal rule - and weighs agent-centered views for Walt's family-first logic. It closes with Singer's drowning-child standard: Walt could have saved Jane and accepted Elliot's charity at little cost, and so could we by redirecting wasted money to OXFAM - so Walt breaks bad, and maybe we do too.

drowning-child.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
drowning-child.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
drowning-child.relation: Moosa uses the apocalypse as a moral laboratory: since 'murder' is by definition wrongful killing, Carl's shooting of Shane must be judged by his reasoning (saving his father), and Hobbes's state of nature — 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' — fits Kirkman's world, yet the survivors import morality into it, as when parents mercy-kill their children just as one would turn up a dying child's morphine. Taking up Camus's claim that suicide is the one truly serious philosophical problem, he argues our world is nearly as bad as the zombie landscape, so consistency commits comfortable readers to the same duty of aid (helping sufferers rather than opting out) that justifies the survivors' fighting on. Finally he argues procreation is the worst thing survivors can do — nonexistent children cannot suffer, so Lori's pregnancy and Glenn and Maggie's crib plans are immoral, and adopting existing children as Andrea and Dale did is the consistent course, an obligation that transfers to our world right now.

drowning-child.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
drowning-child.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
drowning-child.relation: Montoya tests Simon's choice to sacrifice his sanity by wearing the crown to save child Marceline against three ethical theories. Aquinas's doctrine of double effect clears him because the intended good (saving her life) outweighs the merely foreseen side effect (her tears, his possible future evils); Kant's categorical imperative rules out universalizing 'let children die to save myself,' since a world of universal using destroys the rule itself; and a fountain case where Finn must choose between world-saving plans and a drowning candy child separates act from rule utilitarianism, with rule utilitarianism preserving the duty to rescue. All three converge on the verdict that Simon, not Finn, is Ooo's greatest hero.

drowning-child.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
drowning-child.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
drowning-child.relation: Framed by Dickens's Jacob Marley, Walker asks whether Jobs deserved his posthumous accolades despite giving far less to charity than Bill Gates, and tests him under three frameworks. Aristotle's virtue ethics acquits him (character is judged holistically, and charity sits near the golden mean of open-handedness rather than being a checklisted duty); Mill's utilitarianism acquits him (his innovations maximized happiness and he violated no Harm Principle—though abandoning daughter Lisa counts as a harm); and Singer's drowning-child argument condemns him as near-morally-bankrupt for selling luxury gadgets while children starve. Kant both convicts (charity is an imperfect duty under the categorical imperative) and saves Jobs: treating the affluent individual as an end in himself, never merely a means to the destitute, blocks Singer's demand for giving to marginal utility.

drowning-child.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
drowning-child.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
drowning-child.relation: Skyler King uses the Gang's inheritance war over their dead mother's possessions as a metaphor for greed versus need, pressing our duties to those in extreme suffering. Peter Singer's utilitarian argument - prevent bad without sacrificing anything of comparable significance, absolute poverty is bad, therefore we ought to give - makes charity a requirement rather than a nicety, condemning Dennis's luxury purchases and crowning Bruce Mathis, the one character who consistently donates, as the utilitarian exemplar. Nel Noddings's feminist ethics of care counters that we owe help only to those within reach whose good we can see 'completed in the other' - so Mac and Dennis wronged Charlie by refusing him shelter in the recession, but owe nothing to children overseas - and the chapter weighs Dee-style objections that this licenses caring only when inconvenienced, closing with the question 'is it always sunny in your Philadelphia?'

drowning-child.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
drowning-child.title: 16. You’re Not Starving
drowning-child.relation: Argues Louis's 'my life is evil, I drive an Infiniti' bit and 'we make them die with our cars' capture Singer's drowning-child argument that famine relief is a duty of the affluent rather than charity, since the obligation to prevent bad outcomes at little cost holds across distance. It then amplifies the harm claim with Pogge's account of a rigged global institutional order (WTO protections, sweatshop-made smartphones) and frames unthinking consumer participation in that system as Arendt's banality of evil—the 'terrifyingly normal' thoughtlessness of Eichmann repeated at the checkout.

drowning-child.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
drowning-child.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
drowning-child.relation: Malloy uses the two heroes to explain supererogation - Urmson's "Saints and Heroes" puzzle of acts that are praiseworthy but not obligatory, like Batman rushing into burning buildings while Jimmy Olsen is under no duty to follow. Against the utilitarian and deontological denials that anything goes beyond duty (Singer's argument that Clark Kent's designer glasses are money he owes to charity, and Susan Wolf's Loving and Rational Saints whose lives, like Batman's broken retirements in The Dark Knight Returns and Batman Beyond, leave no room for anything worth living), he adopts Raz's view that a duty can be overridden by the moral reason of grave personal risk. Hence Batman's nightly risk-taking is a genuinely heroic choice, while Superman's powers make saving others morally required - so Batman is more truly a hero and Superman "just a good person with the powers of a living god."

drowning-child.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
drowning-child.title: 18. Superman the Super Dick
drowning-child.relation: Modeled on Harry Frankfurt's analysis of 'bullshit,' the chapter defines a 'dick' as someone who willfully disregards others' needs, and argues Superman qualifies: he lets crimes proceed while he works at the Daily Planet or hunts vending-machine change, although the SuperBat storyline (Superman/Batman #53-56) shows a briefly super-powered Batman clearing every city's crime in a single night. Applying Peter Singer's famine-and-affluence argument - the penny that saves a life, the ten-cent polio vaccine - the chapter contends that saving at little or no cost to oneself is obligatory rather than supererogatory, so Superman's convenience-first choices make him a 'Super Dick.' Batman, who risks his mortal life seeking out strangers to save, does what he can and therefore escapes the charge.

drowning-child.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
drowning-child.title: 24. The Fifty-Third Card
drowning-child.relation: Writing as the Joker playing 'the fifty-third card,' the chapter trashes both heroes at once: Superman is an attention-starved show-off who could save people invisibly but wants worship, and Batman is a billionaire who pours his fortune into toys and beatings while thousands of children die for want of the charity he could give. The real punchline is our hypocrisy: we are only as moral as our circumstances allow (born in the ghetto we would steal too), we mourn pets while eating smarter pigs and buying chocolate picked by child slaves, and in The Dark Knight's ferry scene everyone would really have pushed the button - since choosing not to help kills as surely as detonating, 'we kill every day.' The only honest hero would drop moral pretense, do what he genuinely thinks right, and remind us that under the skin we are all clowns laughing as the world burns.

drowning-child.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
drowning-child.title: 2. Golem Morality in the Modern World
drowning-child.relation: Skene weighs Peter Singer's 'Famine, Affluence, and Morality' - opened with a River Ankh drowning-child variant - against the golem morality of Going Postal and Feet of Clay. Mr. Pump's charge that Moist von Lipwig's frauds 'hastened the deaths' of 2.338 people grounds a golem standard of actuarial murder that Skene applies to the 2008 banking crisis and Mao's Great Leap Forward. With Kant, the chapter holds that free choice is the foundation of moral responsibility and respect for others' wills, but unlike Singer's unlimited demands, golem morality asks us to own the foreseeable consequences of our choices without sacrificing everything.

drowning-child.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
drowning-child.title: 12. Jerry’s Dick
drowning-child.relation: Twin essays by two dimension-swapped Wayne Yuens debate whether Jerry owes Shrimply Pibbles his penis in 'Interdimensional Cable 2'. Yuen H-232 defends supererogation: like donating blood or a kidney to a Peter Singer figure, giving up the organ would be Good-Samaritan praiseworthy but beyond duty, since it would derail Jerry's life-plan and autonomy, and the artificial-heart alternative makes it optional, while utilitarianism has no room for such acts. Yuen U-964 replies that the life-plan excuse would absolve every shirked duty up to Evil Morty's massacre of the Citadel, that Singer-style obligation to aid stands, and that in our organ-short world we probably do have a duty to donate.

drowning-child.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
drowning-child.title: But This Ruins Everything!
drowning-child.relation: Mahesh Ananth and Ben Dixon pit young Bruce Wayne against Peter Singer: given seven billion dollars, Singer's 'Famine, Affluence, and Morality' principle, illustrated by the drowning child, seems to require giving nearly everything to famine relief rather than dressing up as a bat. Against appeals to honoring his parents' memory and to supererogation, the authors deploy Singer's strong and moderate versions of giving and utilitarian indifference to distance, concluding that a true utilitarian would forbid becoming Batman. The irony they highlight is that the older Batman himself reasons utilitarianly when he abandons Jason Todd to intercept the Joker's poisoned convoy in A Death in the Family.

drowning-child.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
drowning-child.title: NOTES
drowning-child.relation: Miles asks whether extraordinary power generates extraordinary obligations, testing Spider-Man's 'with great power comes great responsibility' against Claude the invisible thief and the heroes' reluctance. He uses Singer's principle of minimal obligation (Micah diverting the train from the infant; Claire's negligible risk in burning-building rescues; Hiro teleporting across distance) and Kant's perfect/imperfect obligation distinction (Niki choosing between saving Monica and mothering Micah; Noah Bennet lying to protect Claire) before deploying Fishkin's three 'explosion' objections: too many endangered people, too many capable heroes, and too many repeated rescues dilute obligation. He concludes the heroes went beyond the call of duty in saving New York, so saving the world could legitimately be their paid job, like lifeguards or soldiers.

drowning-child.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
drowning-child.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
drowning-child.relation: Alloy uses supererogation — Urmson's saints-and-heroes puzzle — to separate the heroes: utilitarianism (via Singer's Famine, Affluence, and Morality, where even Clark's novelty glasses are stolen from charity) and deontology both erase acts that are good but not required, and Susan Wolf's moral saints show where that lands — a Bruce Wayne with no hobbies, friends, or life, like Astro City's Samaritan. Alloy's own Raz-style fix (requirements overridden by moral permitting reasons) yields the verdict: Batman risks his life by choice and so is a true hero, while Superman, facing no real danger, merely does what his powers make morally required — 'a good person with the powers of a living god'.

drowning-child.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
drowning-child.title: 18. Superman the Super Dick
drowning-child.relation: Borrowing Harry Frankfurt's move of philosophically defining a colloquial term (as Frankfurt did for 'bullshit'), it defines a 'dick' as someone who willfully disregards others' needs and argues Superman is one: the vending-machine thought experiment shows he could rescue a sinking school bus in less time than it takes Clark to buy a chocolate bar, so saving people at little or no cost to himself is obligatory, not supererogatory. Peter Singer's famine-and-affluence argument extends the same obligation to the affluent reader, while the SuperBat arc of Superman/Batman #53–56—in which Batman temporarily gains Superman's powers and empties every city's jails in one night—proves Superman could do vastly more than he does. Batman, who risks his mortal life and seeks out strangers to save, is 'not a dick' and wins the round.

drowning-child.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
drowning-child.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
drowning-child.relation: Moosa treats Kirkman's world as a moral laboratory: the apocalypse approximates Hobbes's state of nature ('solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'), yet Rick's search for his family shows survivors import morality into it, and Carl's killing of Shane is judged by reasoning rather than the act of killing itself. Taking Camus's claim that suicide is the only serious philosophical problem, the chapter argues the survivors' best justification for continuing is reducing others' suffering, and consistency then imposes the same duty on comfortable readers to help real-world sufferers rather than reserving aid for photogenic disasters. It concludes that Glenn and Maggie's wish to conceive at the prison is the worst thing survivors can do, since non-existent children cannot suffer while existing orphans (like the children Andrea and Dale adopted) have prior moral claims, an argument that applies to couples in our world too.

drowning-child.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
drowning-child.title: 16. Fine Dining with Children Starving
drowning-child.relation: Barta and Miranda pose Bourdain's Haiti dilemma — feasting on camera while people starve — as Peter Singer's 'Shallow Pond' / drowning-child argument about affluence and obligation. They test justifications for luxury from Bentham's intensity-vs-extent calculus, Mill's higher/lower pleasures, and Sidgwick's dualism of practical reason, then use Singer's Expanding Circle to show how Bourdain extended moral consideration to the poor, the foreign, and (partially) non-human animals through his work.

drowning-child.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
drowning-child.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
drowning-child.relation: The editors' introduction argues that fashion, despite philosophers' contempt for it, raises serious questions in aesthetics, ethics, identity, and political philosophy. It surveys the volume's contributors: fashionability as an expert-plus-masses property (Prinz/Farennikova), Zangwill's alienation thesis, Russell on 'cool' as aesthetic virtue, the objectification of women through Barbie play and sweatshops, and Singer's demand (via the drowning-child argument) that spare money go to poverty relief rather than trendy clothes. It uses concrete cases — Ugg boots, the National Airlines 'Fly me' campaign, Tommie Smith and John Carlos's 1968 Olympic salute, foot binding — to show fashion carries the zeitgeist and can both liberate and enslave.

drowning-child.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
drowning-child.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
drowning-child.relation: Cassidy, through an interior monologue of a shopper eyeing Indonesian-made sandals, weighs individual responsibility for consumerism. She contrasts Singer's drowning-child duty to relieve suffering with Pogge's 'you break it, you buy it' claim that the Global North caused Southern poverty, then uses Scheffler's 'restricted' common-sense responsibility and Cannon's butterfly-effect virtues (replacing the American Dream's acquisitiveness with interconnectedness). Adapting Claudia Card, she distinguishes three senses of responsibility — credit (backward-looking blame), management (of one's lifestyle), and care-taking — and, invoking Noddings's ethics of care, argues that since globalization's impact is uncertain we should shift from assigning blame to caring *about* distant workers, buying less out of boredom-driven habit.

drowning-child.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
drowning-child.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
drowning-child.relation: Ramsey applies the methods of practical/applied ethics to the taboo of hold manufacturing ('chipping'), using Peter Singer's drowning-child argument as his model of following an argument to its uncomfortable conclusion. He builds a syllogism: since climbers accept modifying rock (removing loose rock, vegetation) to make routes climbable, and hold manufacturing is another such modification, manufacturing is sometimes acceptable. He dismantles four common objections (safety, environment, harming future climbers, slippery slope) to argue the near-universal condemnation of chipping is an unjustified bias inconsistent with climbers' actual practices, like the chiseled Jardine Traverse on The Nose.

drowning-child.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
drowning-child.title: 59. Don’t Look Up as Philosophy Comets, Climate Change, and Why the Snacks Are Not Free
drowning-child.relation: The chapter argues Don't Look Up is less a film than a moral imperative: its comet is an allegory for climate change, and Randall Mindy's on-air breakdown presents Singer-style simple premises (the end of human life is bad; prevent bad things you can) that compel action. It uses Plato's knowledge-as-the-Good and 'blameworthy ignorance' to condemn the willfully ignorant (Kate's parents, the Orlean Bros) who act as if they know, and Kant's categorical imperative to condemn General Themes's 'free snacks' lie and to cast the moral as the rational. It defends the comet/climate analogy against critics and insists individual action is insufficient while collective government action is required.

historical-materialism.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
historical-materialism.title: Poker and Philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Belliotti tells of busting 'Pickle Puss' with flopped queens and of tight 'Howard the Vest' paying off his flopped full house to ask whether Marx's diagnoses — alienation in four forms, exploitation of surplus value, and false consciousness spread through the ideological superstructure by the economic base — condemn poker. He argues no: unlike coerced factory labor, poker is freely chosen creative activity that energizes our species-being like an absorbed artist, as Doyle 'Texas Dolly' Brunson's road-gambler career and his famous ten-deuce full-house call against Jessie Alto at the 1976 WSOP (and the 1980 loss to Stu Ungar's gutshot) show. Poker may still launder capitalist ideology — antes that lure investment, zero-sum rivalry, rugged individualism — but the owner-worker exploitation Marx feared has no equivalent at an equal-buy-in table.

historical-materialism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
historical-materialism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Fitzpatrick runs Marx's account of alienated labor from the 1844 Manuscripts through the novel: Victor's creature is the product of estranged labor, 'an alien object exercising power over him,' which he cannot name, comes to loathe, and which finally destroys him - the devaluation of the creator tracking the increasing value of the thing made, while workers become commodities producing commodities. The De Laceys' eviction in Branagh's Mary Shelley's Frankenstein and the Ingolstadt cholera riots stage class struggle at feudalism's end, and Victor's failure to self-actualize (to 'hunt in the morning, fish in the afternoon... criticize after dinner') shows how capitalism turns science into 'a tool of our own destruction.' The chapter closes with 'Frankenstorm' climate change as the alienated externality par excellence - capitalists selling us the rope with which we hang ourselves.

historical-materialism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
historical-materialism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Jeff Ewing reads Victor's science through ecofeminist and Marxist critiques: M. Waldman's promise to 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'show how she works in her hiding-places' exemplifies exactly what Val Plumwood condemns - male knowers wringing secrets from a nature pictured as a passive female slave - and Victor studies natural elements 'in their death, not in their life' as raw material for power. Marx and Engels supply the parallel diagnosis: capitalism biases science and technology toward profit, turning tools and knowledge into means of domination rather than human flourishing, just as Victor's knowledge serves only his glory and kills everyone he loves. The chapter concludes that we breed Frankenstein's monsters whenever science treats nature, workers, women, and othered peoples as mere instruments, and only replacing those social relations frees science from power and profit.

historical-materialism.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
historical-materialism.title: 11. The Iron Bank Will Have Its Due
historical-materialism.relation: Ewing argues money is the real determinant of the Iron Throne: Lannister gold made Cersei queen, Tyrell grain and taxation bought Margaery's crown, Baelish's financing decided the Battle of the Bastards, and the Iron Bank disciplines kings. Reading Westeros as a late-feudal economy through Marx - smallfolk whose work and taxes support lords who 'reap where they never sowed,' a hierarchy held by coercion and fear as the High Sparrow tells Olenna ('You are the few, we are the many'), and money dissolving feudal bonds into a 'money aristocracy' - he predicts the throne will go not to dragons or White Walkers but to the capitalist-financier figure of Petyr Baelish.

historical-materialism.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
historical-materialism.title: 10. If It Isn’t Justified Is It Still My Revolution
historical-materialism.relation: Writing as a guilt-ridden fsociety member haunted by James Plouffe's on-air suicide, Altmann tests the 5/9 revolution against three theorists: Burke's conservatism condemns all revolution as destruction of social tradition (and fsociety's blackout chaos and Susan Jacobs's death seem to prove him right), while Marx's class struggle between E Corp's bourgeoisie and the indebted proletariat makes revolution the only exit from history's cycle. Kai Nielsen's condition - revolution is justified only when no other recourse exists - settles it: Angela's failed attempt to reform E Corp from within shows non-revolutionary change is impossible, so the author keeps fighting 'with a keyboard whose clacking is endless.'

historical-materialism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
historical-materialism.title: 2 Power and Politics
historical-materialism.relation: The chapter traces politics from the classical ethics-fused view (Aristotle's Politics, where politics exists for the sake of the good life yet also supplies one of the first justifications of patriarchy and the public/private split) to the Machiavelli-Hobbes break where politics becomes simply the possession and exercise of power, adopting Bertrand Russell's claim that power is the fundamental concept of social science. It then builds the book's central instrument, a Weber-derived analysis of nine power bases (money, knowledge/technology/information, religion, morality, authority, charisma, size/solidarity, violence, status), contrasting the Marxian reading - money as ultimately determinative, the ruling ideas of each age as the ideas of the ruling class, religion as the opium of the people, the state as a committee for managing bourgeois affairs - with the liberal-Weberian reading in which no single base is decisive. It closes by showing that Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau and Marx divide over the morality of egalitarianism (Popper's Marx moved by moral impulse versus Locke's possessive individualism), and that power is domain-specific, inert until used, skill-dependent and always relative.

historical-materialism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
historical-materialism.title: 3 On the Origin of the Family
historical-materialism.relation: The chapter compares the liberal contract theorists with Engels (building on Morgan's Ancient Society) on the origin of the patriarchal monogamous family: Hobbes derives sovereign-husbanded 'little monarchies' from a state of nature in which women are men's equals, a derivation Susan Okin shows is contradictory; Locke grounds conjugal society in a voluntary compact with the husband as 'abler and stronger' last determiner, yet leaves women excluded from the social contract; Rousseau pairs passionate economic equality with some of the most sexist writing in Western thought, including fear of wives' sexual power in Emile. Against these static philosophies Engels gives a historical-materialist account in which the overthrow of mother right - the 'world historical defeat of the female sex' - followed from private property and inheritance, turning the bourgeois wife into a proletarian or prostitute while opening 'sex love' to the propertyless, and prescribing women's return to the labor force, socialized child-care, industrialized housework and easy divorce. John Stuart Mill's Subjection of Women appears as liberalism's one exception to its sexism, and a footnote sets Firestone's biological account of patriarchy against Engels's property account.

historical-materialism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
historical-materialism.title: 7 The Bourgeoisie and the Blacks
historical-materialism.relation: The chapter sets business - the US bourgeoisie whose privileged position Charles Beard read into the Constitution and which survived the Jacksonian and New Deal challenges by breaking labor through Taft-Hartley, right-to-work laws and the PATCO lockout, its solidarity secured while worker solidarity was undercut by what Marx called the Achilles heel of racism - against blacks as the paradigmatic powerless, shut out of every power base since slavery, which the chapter treats with Baptist and Marx's 1846 letter as a totalitarian system of super-exploited, tortured labor that built American capitalism, its neo-slavery progeny (Blackmon) pauperizing the black community under Dred Scott's 'subordinate and inferior class of beings'. It then narrates black counter-power base by base: the abolitionist interracial coalition wielding charisma (Douglass, Nat Turner, John Brown), information, morality and religion; the NAACP era and King's fusion of charisma, church religion, Myrdal's An American Dilemma and televised nonviolent provocation against Bull Connor's violence, contested by Malcolm X, SNCC and the Black Panthers; and a post-civil-rights scorecard showing a wealth base 94.2 percent white, persistent education and media gaps, constrained black officials from mayors to the symbolic Obama presidency, and a captive but potentially leveraged black vote in a 'Sisyphean' struggle.

historical-materialism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
historical-materialism.title: 28. Replicants of California, Unite!
historical-materialism.relation: Christopher Innes gives 2049 a Marxist class analysis: the replicants are an enslaved working class, the Wallace Corporation the ruling class owning the means of production, and the LAPD a state apparatus with 'relative autonomy' that really upholds the system — K is a slave who kills his own kind without seeing his class position. Applying the materialist (not idealist) dialectic and the Eighteenth Brumaire's lesson about conflicting ruling-class interests, he reads Wallace, Atari, and even Ana as factions with divergent interests. Freysa's 'we are our own masters' and 'we are building our own army' mark the replicants as class conscious, aware of their Marxian 'species being', with nothing to lose but their chains.

historical-materialism.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
historical-materialism.title: 22. Won’t You Be My Comrade
historical-materialism.relation: Christopher Innes runs Marx's critique of Hegel's idealism against Mister Rogers: the show treats problems (divorce, war, the Clemmons pool scene) ideally, as symbolic gestures rather than material change, much as Hegel's storybook individuals miss money's role. Measured against Capital's alienated worker, 'an appendage to the machine,' contrasted with the suitcase worker who 'knows her work,' and the Communist Manifesto's 'bourgeois socialist' who demands reform not liberation, Rogers emerges as a progressive bourgeois socialist whose make-believe may console children for, or subtly resist, their future exploitation.

historical-materialism.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
historical-materialism.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Erich Christiansen reads the supernatural imagery of the first two albums as the worldview of powerless working-class Birmingham men, applying Marx's claims that social being determines consciousness, that capitalists are "privileged and idle gods" over the worker, and that religion is simultaneously an expression of real suffering and its opiate. On this reading the figure in black of "Black Sabbath" personifies foremen and unseen bosses looming like factory smoke, "The Wizard" and the Lucifer-seducer of "N.I.B." answer the desperate worker's need for hands-on power when prayer fails, and "War Pigs"' Day of Judgment for the sorcerer-generals is itself the opium fantasy of workers who cannot deliver justice themselves, with "Wicked World" naming the whole system.

historical-materialism.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
historical-materialism.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Michel Beaulieu reads the series through Marx's materialist conception of history: the 'Proletariat Patrons' Movement' sign in FFIX's Alexandria, the job system as a class system, and Shinra dropping the Sector 7 plate on its own laboring class all instantiate class struggle, while Vaan's life in Rabanastre shows social existence determining consciousness. But he argues the heroes are not Marxist revolutionaries, since Cecil ends up King of Baron and the Light Warriors leave feudal structures intact, and the Moogles, the series' true proletarian serfs, never revolt, because no Final Fantasy world has yet matured to the stage where the Marxian transformation becomes possible.

historical-materialism.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
historical-materialism.title: Notes
historical-materialism.relation: Argues the Underwoods' success is not far-fetched fiction but the structural outcome four critics of democracy predict. Plato's Republic supplies the spine: the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decays through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, whose love of freedom invites the tyrant — Peter Russo with his random desires is the democratic soul, Frank the tyrannical soul ruled by one illicit appetite, doomed to the fear and friendlessness Book 9 describes (which Season 3 delivers). Hobbes and Hegel then explain why monarchy may beat popular rule (the monarch's private interest aligns with the public's; the monarch lets a people will as one), and Marx reframes the whole show economically — SanCorp, Tusk and Feng as capitalists, the laid-off shipyard workers as proletariat, and AmWorks as self-interested politicians flirting with expropriation. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government gives the democratic reply — elections force responsiveness, participation educates citizens — so the burden falls on viewers to keep elections fair, the press free, and checks on unscrupulous politicians effective.

historical-materialism.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
historical-materialism.title: Notes
historical-materialism.relation: Byron and Wood use Marx's claim that the modern state is 'a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie' to read House of Cards: Raymond Tusk secretly dictates President Walker's policies, SanCorp buys influence over Frank through Claire's water-filters favor, and Frank's rise to the vice presidency is engineered by capitalists to protect their market interests. Even Frank's seemingly pro-worker America Works plan serves capital, since gutting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid to subsidize $45,000 hiring costs boosts business profit, and the Dunbar-Walmart dispute shows the state arbitrating between conflicting capitalists rather than aiding workers. The chapter concludes that worker victories like a Dunbar minimum-wage win would only be the bourgeoisie losing a battle while winning the class war, confirming Frank's line that 'democracy is so overrated.'

historical-materialism.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
historical-materialism.title: Notes
historical-materialism.relation: Shea argues the Underwoods' rise is structurally guaranteed rather than far-fetched, surveying democracy's critics: Plato's Republic Books 8-9 has the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decay through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, where a 'protector'-tyrant like Frank exploits the drones and the people's love of freedom (Russo as the prototypical democratic soul, Tusk as the oligarch-in-fact), while the tyrant ends fear-ridden and friendless — precisely Frank's Season 3. Hobbes and Hegel then reverse the verdict, arguing monarchy aligns the ruler's private interest with the public good and lets a people will as one instead of a formless mass — the insight Tom Yates has about voters identifying with the Underwoods as people — and Marx reframes it economically: SanCorp, Tusk, and Feng are the capitalist structure, and Frank's AmWorks, entitlement cuts, and nationalization threats show self-interested politicians siding with a growing proletariat. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government supplies the democratic reply — responsiveness, better information, and citizen participation mean an Underwood cannot last if we keep fair elections, a free press, and real checks.

historical-materialism.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
historical-materialism.title: Notes
historical-materialism.relation: Argues that Marx's claim that the modern state is 'a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie' explains House of Cards better than Frank's own power-over-money creed: Raymond Tusk and SanCorp dictate President Walker's policies and cost Frank the Secretary of State post, and even Frank's signature America Works jobs bill functions as a capitalist subsidy (government-paid wages, gutted entitlements), while the Dunbar-versus-Walmart fight over Medicaid shows the state arbitrating among capitalists. The authors conclude that even a worker victory like a Dunbar minimum-wage raise would only be a concession in an ongoing class conflict, so 'democracy is so overrated' because capital, not Frank, is really in charge of the White House.

historical-materialism.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
historical-materialism.title: The Office and Philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Answers The New Yorker's claim that the American Office 'doesn't care about class' by reading it through Marx: capital's growth logic and surplus value explain the degraded office labor the show depicts (Stanley's 'run-out-the-clock type of situation' truck unloading, Pam's tepid watercolors, Roy's 'unloading trucks without meaning', Ryan's rejected assembly line), while the salaried masses' class position survives precisely as unnamable and denied - Michael's botched condo purchase, his fury at Ryan's business-school ambition, and Prison Martin's observation that office and prison are both 'doing the same thing every day'. Drawing on Kracauer, the chapter argues the show's comedy walks between distraction and awakening, and ends with Walter Benjamin's 'authentic humanity' located in the gap between professional and private life: Michael's failures make him an unwitting critique of the system that produced him.

historical-materialism.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
historical-materialism.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
historical-materialism.relation: Uses 'The Last of the Meheecans' to argue that Marx's account of labor-power needs race built into it: once Butters is mistaken for a Mexican immigrant 'Mantequilla', the couple who hit him hand him Windex and a leaf blower and he sings 'Work, Mexican, work', showing how racialization assigns his labor a demeaned value. The episode's conflicting stereotypes (lazy shiftless 'Meheecans' versus the hard-working backbone of service labor) and the mass 'Orgullo de Mantequilla' migration home reveal a super-exploited population. The author then recovers Marx's own writings on Polish and Irish liberation, American slavery, and Lincoln's reelection ('labor in the white skin cannot emancipate itself where in the black skin it is branded') to show that for Marx, racial and national domination were always obstacles to working-class freedom.

historical-materialism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
historical-materialism.title: Notes
historical-materialism.relation: Jeff Ewing argues the Federation's moneyless, postscarcity economy is Marx's transitional stage on the way to classless communism: Picard's 'we've eliminated hunger, want, the need for possessions' and Troi's exchange with Samuel Clemens in 'Time's Arrow' mark Marx's shift from the realm of necessity to the realm of freedom. He reconstructs Marx and Engels on alienation, the division of labor, labor-tokens, and the withering state to dissolve the apparent anomalies—Federation credits, Quark's tab, the Chateau Picard vineyard—as survivals of transition rather than capitalism. Rom's 'workers of the world unite' in 'Bar Association' and the self-actualizing leisure of Enterprise crews complete the case.

historical-materialism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
historical-materialism.title: NOTES
historical-materialism.relation: Ewing reads Cameron as a Marxist: Cyberdyne's profit-driven reverse-engineering of the recovered Terminator arm, Dyson's alienated labor ('Don't ask'), and U.S. militarism absorbing Cyber Research Systems develop Skynet as capitalism's 'final contradiction,' in which the drive for destructive, labor-replacing technology converges with the profit motive to threaten humanity. Sarah and John are useful to the resistance only when they exit wage labor - waitress to warrior, ATM hacking instead of work - dramatizing Marx's claim that liberation requires transcending class positions. Yet technology itself is neutral and reclaimable: the reprogrammed T-101 learning 'I know now why you cry' shows even killing machines can be humanized for liberation, and the saga ends where Marx does - not interpreting the world but changing it.

historical-materialism.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
historical-materialism.title: 5. Psychohistory by Any Other Name
historical-materialism.relation: Petersen defends keeping the label 'psychohistory' by tying it to Edward Gibbon's Decline and Fall, showing Seldon's cited causes of imperial collapse and his use of religion as foreign-policy instrument mirror Gibbon's account of Rome. He locates psychohistory within critical (not speculative/Hegelian-teleological) philosophy of history, then compares it to Peter Turchin's 'cliodynamics', which borrows statistical mechanics and nonlinear dynamics to make history predictive, noting both share Asimov's kinetic-theory-of-gases model while facing the objection that human contingency (the Mule) resists mathematization.

historical-materialism.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
historical-materialism.title: 11. An Interstellar Leap of Faith
historical-materialism.relation: Barta and Lee read Seldon's Plan as a providence narrative and stage a three-way debate over it. Hegel's dialectical, Spirit-driven history (thesis-antithesis-synthesis, even yielding 'psycho-history' as a synthesis) is mirrored in the Foundation's succession of ruling crises and its Encyclopedia Galactica as absolute knowledge. Kierkegaard's leap of faith describes how Foundationists obey a plan they cannot see and whose Vault confirms only in hindsight, an ignorance the Plan actually requires (an observer effect). Marx's materialist dialectic appears in Hober Mallow's 'historic forces' and the priesthood of the Galactic Spirit as ideological control, but the authors argue the Foundationists' sincere faith in Seldon nests all critiques back inside a Hegelian providence.

historical-materialism.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
historical-materialism.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
historical-materialism.relation: Bane surveys fidelity criticism of film adaptation (McFarlane, and especially George Bluestone's Novels into Film) and applies a Marxist reading to the 1940 Pride and Prejudice. He shows how Bluestone praises the film as faithfully capturing Austen's 'aristocratic dance,' then argues a single altered line, Darcy's 'the middle classes at play,' injects a post-Marx notion of class struggle absent from Austen's Regency world of gentry versus nobility. Reading the Bennet-Lucas competition as proletarian striving and set against the 1940s Red Scare and HUAC blacklist, Bane concludes that adaptation lets Austen's ironic critique of class speak to new times, marking her a great author across eras.

historical-materialism.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
historical-materialism.title: From Domestic Nightmares to the Nightmare of History Uncanny Eruptions of Violence in King's and Kubrick's Ver
historical-materialism.relation: Lutz argues that King's novel and Kubrick's film of The Shining both stage Freud's uncanny as the return of a repressed, corporeal past: the woman in Room 217 and Grady's ghosts, the father-mirroring of Jack, his abusive father, and Delbert Grady, and Danny's Tony double. He reads King as an 'inverted family romance' where the good replacement father is the Black cook Hallorann, then shows Kubrick widening domestic abuse into a Marxian nightmare of history: the Overlook built on an Indian burial ground, the Calumet cans, and Jack's craving to join the hotel's ghostly 'management' expose the racist, patriarchal, class violence founding American institutions. Jack's 'All work and no play' manuscript figures his entrapment in ideology and repetition.

historical-materialism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
historical-materialism.title: 22. Rick & Morty as Philosophy Nihilism in the Multiverse
historical-materialism.relation: The chapter argues that Rick Sanchez's nihilism is built on cultural relativism plus the metaphysical fact of a multiverse. It reads Rick's mockery of racist alien snakes and the Gazorpazorp matriarchy through Montaigne's essay on cannibals to establish cultural relativism, and treats the microverse 'battery' society through Marx's base/superstructure and Foucault's docile bodies to argue all social values are constructed for the rulers. Rick's dimension-hopping (the Cronenberg episode, the Vat of Acid) literalizes David Lewis's modal realism and Leibniz's possible worlds, so that no action matters because a counterpart always does the opposite; his resulting hedonism and Birdperson's 'Wubba lubba dub dub' reveal Rick as a depressed near-Camusian who cannot live his own absurdist creed.

sufficient-reason.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
sufficient-reason.title: Poker and Philosophy
sufficient-reason.relation: Sanders splits poker into two philosophical styles. The Rationalist — Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason, Pascal's domestication of chance into probability — plays like Sklansky, Chris Ferguson, and Howard Lederer, whose temptation is the paralysis of analysis; the Existentialist — Sartre's existence precedes essence, Camus' scorn for the absurd, Kierkegaard's leap of faith taken without decisive evidence — plays like Gus Hansen calling Antonio Esfandiari's $334,000 all-in re-raise with ten-high. A Russell-and-Popper-style regress of predictions (knowing a prediction changes its outcome) becomes the tournament 'hall of mirrors' of intentions read in Phil Ivey and Johnny Chan, and the chapter lands on Richard Taylor's existentialist point that meaning comes from committed doing, at the table as in life.

sufficient-reason.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
sufficient-reason.title: Herr Leibniz Consoles Mr. Monk
sufficient-reason.relation: Kavas distinguishes Monk's method from Holmes's modus ponens, Poirot's elimination, and Goren's profiling: Monk accepts only what completes a coherent total narrative, so 'Here's what happened' re-tells the order of the whole world, as in the chess-game solution of 'Mr. Monk and the Genius'. The chapter uses the Tractatus's world of contingent, logically independent facts to model Monk's picture-completion, then brings in Leibniz: the principle of sufficient reason, the best of all possible worlds, and preestablished harmony justify Monk's faith that even Trudy's death must have a reason. Monk emerges as a pessimistic Leibniz who takes the world to be the worst possible precisely because, since learning the bomb was meant for Trudy in 'Mr. Monk Goes to Jail', he cannot see any sufficient reason for her death ('Why her?').

sufficient-reason.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
sufficient-reason.title: The Odd Thought of Doctor Who
sufficient-reason.relation: Maps Leibniz's monadology onto the Whoniverse: the Doctor's individual concept survives each regeneration as a thinking monad while its bodily monads are replaced, parallel Liz Shaws in 'Inferno' show incompossible predicates, and the Time Lords play Leibniz's God permitting minimal evil, which the Doctor accepts in refusing to avert the Daleks' creation in 'Genesis of the Daleks'. The dimensionally transcendental TARDIS illustrates the principle of indiscernibles, the Matrix becomes a failed pre-established harmony haunted by confused perceptions, and the Master hallucinates against the Doctor like Descartes's evil demon. The Valeyard is modeled as an incompossible world on Leibniz's Sextus Tarquinius pyramid and Borges's forking paths, closing with Leibniz's own 'odd thought' academy of wonders.

sufficient-reason.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
sufficient-reason.title: Futurama and Philosophy
sufficient-reason.relation: DePoe weighs the multiverse against the fine-tuning argument for God's existence: just as Farnsworth's box in 'The Farnsworth Parabox' spills out universe-1's golden Bender plus togas, pirate, and hippie universes, an infinite multiverse would realize every possibility and make our life-permitting constants certain rather than miraculous, while 'Time Keeps on Slippin''s chronoton-disturbed cosmos illustrates what fine-tuning means. He then asks what is metaphysically primitive, staging the 1948 Copleston-Russell exchange ('I should say that the universe is just there, and that's all') and applying Ockham's razor to weigh one infinitely complex God against infinitely many unobservable universes. The chapter concludes in evidential stalemate, closing with the God Entity's counsel in 'Godfellas': 'When you do things right, people won't be sure you've done anything at all.'

sufficient-reason.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
sufficient-reason.title: Notes
sufficient-reason.relation: Blessing diagnoses Ted's 'rom-communism' as the naive optimism Voltaire satirized in Candide: Pangloss's 'best of all possible worlds' is Leibniz's greater-goods theodicy and Principle of Sufficient Reason, and its fatalism ('it will all work out exactly as it's supposed to') collapses under Ted's panic attacks and 'belief can't score goals.' Against it she sets Camus's The Plague: Dr. Rieux's absurd heroism, refusal of hope as 'philosophical suicide,' and 'strange hope' grounded in collective decency, arguing Ted's real, sustainable creed is Camus-like faith in teamwork and human goodness rather than belief that everything works out.

sufficient-reason.title: The Odd Thought of Doctor Who
sufficient-reason.relation: Gregory Kalyniuk maps Leibniz's monadology onto Doctor Who. The Doctor's identity across regenerations is a thinking monad whose individual concept holds necessary predicates while appurtenant body-monads are replaced; the Time Lords play Leibniz's God overseeing pre-established harmony and permitting evil in the best world (refusing to stop the Daleks in 'Genesis'). The dimensionally transcendental TARDIS illustrates the identity of indiscernibles, the Matrix is a Leibnizian mill of confused perceptions (with the Master as Descartes's evil demon), and the incompossible Valeyard of 'Trial of a Time Lord' is read via Leibniz's Theodicy pyramid and Borges's forking paths.

sufficient-reason.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
sufficient-reason.title: 9. The Prequel versus Free Will
sufficient-reason.relation: Frim argues that Better Call Saul, precisely because it is a prequel, illustrates Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason—every event, including Walt's meth empire or Jimmy's burner-phone hustle, has a causal 'because' stretching infinitely back—and thus a deterministic universe. He dismantles the appeal to Heisenberg/quantum indeterminacy (randomness is not free choice) and refutes three myths: that determinism is boring (the causal 'Story One' is far more gripping than the free-will 'Story Two'), amoral (murder is wrong for its effects; we can keep 'suffering' and drop 'guilt'), and mindless (Nacho's ordered mind versus Tuco's drug-addled one shows minds function well or badly). He enlists Socrates' 'no one goes willingly toward the bad' to recast wrongdoing as disordered reasoning.

quine-indeterminacy.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
quine-indeterminacy.title: Poker and Philosophy
quine-indeterminacy.relation: Ellis analyzes expert poker as thought attribution, spelling the iterations out to the sixth order in a Big Slick hand against T.J. Cloutier, then argues via Quine's 'gavagai' rabbit and Davidson's interpretationism that attributing thoughts to opponents requires assuming deep shared belief — which explains why pros misread novices whose minds they cannot model. The centerpiece is Dan Harrington's reconstruction of Daniel Negreanu's 2004 river raise against Freddy Deeb as a set of fourth-order-or-below attributions (Deeb will read a small raise as a lure bet and fold the best hand), not one towering thought. It ends asking how anyone ever learns what an opponent thinks from actions that are a vector of beliefs and desires, and notes poker forces rare deep agreement among strangers worldwide.

quine-indeterminacy.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
quine-indeterminacy.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
quine-indeterminacy.relation: Sara Waller argues the films show language operating as a tyranny that measures minds and withholds moral standing: Dodge mocking signing Caesar as a 'stupid monkey,' Zaius dismissing Taylor's speech as mimicry, 1894 literacy tests used to disenfranchise Black voters, and IQ tests whose vocabulary sections double-count language skill. She surveys the non-linguistic tests the apes face - the Hopkins dexterity test, the Wisconsin Multiphasic, Kohler's banana-and-boxes task ('Because I loathe bananas'), the Lucas Tower, Caesar's cookie-jar deception - and then deploys Quine's 'gavagai' inscrutability of reference to argue that speech cannot be the ultimate measure of intelligence or moral worth. Nova's hand over Taylor's mouth and Zira and Cornelius's 'be clever... be quiet' suggest that under oppression, silence is the smart play.

quine-indeterminacy.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
quine-indeterminacy.title: Wonderland and the Real World
quine-indeterminacy.relation: Extracts three problems of induction from Alice's misadventures: predicting the future (Hume's problem: nothing rationally compels Humpty Dumpty to agree the world will not turn into Wonderland at 6 a.m. tomorrow), proving whose dream it is (Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence: Tweedledee can accommodate any evidence within the theory that Alice exists only in the Red King's dream), and translating Wonderese (Quine's indeterminacy: pointing at the White Rabbit cannot fix whether natives mean the rabbit, its parts, or its stages, nor what 'muchness' means). Brendan Shea shows Alice succeeding where the creatures fail by the criteria Hume and Quine endorse: experimentation, simplicity, conservatism of belief, and a principle of charity in translation.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Poker and Philosophy
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Huss tests four models of bluffing on one K-9 all-in: it is not lying, because everyone at the table expects deception, so the victim is never Frankfurt's 'twice deceived' (and Kant's argument that lying fails where everyone lies applies); it is not bullshit, because Frankfurt's bullshitter ignores the facts a poker player cannot afford to ignore; it is not pure acceptance in Jonathan Cohen's sense, since bluffing adds deception to acting-as-if; and it is not full self-deception, since nobody can make themselves believe that 2+2=5 or that 4-7 offsuit is pocket aces. Good bluffing is an art blending all four: deceiving about hand and beliefs, prying attention away from your cards, acting as if, and trying — and necessarily failing — to fool yourself.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: First part of the editors' introduction, recounting how Harry Frankfurt's slim On Bullshit, after two decades circulating only among academic moral philosophers, spent twenty-six weeks on the New York Times bestseller list and outsold any commercial philosophy book. Reisch and Hardcastle treat the book's popularity as a puzzle worth explaining: a technical exercise in conceptual analysis struck a public nerve. The chapter uses Frankfurt's own definition of bullshit as indifference to truth as the anchor for everything that follows.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: The editors answer why On Bullshit hit a nerve using Jon Stewart's Daily Show interview with Frankfurt, where the audience laughed at the claim that the bullshitter does not care whether what he says is true. The unspoken elephant in the room was the Iraq war: the claims about weapons of mass destruction, remote-controlled delivery devices, and 9/11 complicity turned out, in the editors' words, to be best described by that word. They argue readers embraced the book as 'bullshit without tears,' a cushion of humor letting them approach the war's deceptions abstractly rather than face the disturbing political questions directly.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: 'The Year in Bullshit' catalogues the fraud climate surrounding the book's success: James Frey's fabricated memoir A Million Little Pieces exposed on Oprah, the wholly invented author J.T. Leroy, product placement and paid word-of-mouth advertising blurring the line between ads and ordinary conversation, and scientific fraud in pharmaceutical and federal research. It invokes Karl Popper's claim that science deserves respect precisely because it falsifies its own claims, presenting headlines about fabricated results as that ideal fading. Frank Rich's verdict that 'such distinctions have long since washed away in much of our public life' supplies the chapter's explanation of the book's appeal as cultural despair.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: 'The Dream of a Bullshit-Free Culture' argues Frankfurt revives a centuries-old philosophical tradition: Socrates searching for genuinely wise people rather than purveyors of hearsay, Descartes' Meditations discarding every belief short of certainty, and Hume's forkcondemning divinity-school metaphysics that contains neither abstract nor experimental reasoning to the flames. The twentieth-century apotheosis is the Vienna Circle, whose Rudolf Carnap dissected Heidegger's 'Das Nichts selbst nichtet' as mere appearance of meaning, calling metaphysicians 'musicians without musical ability'. The editors cast Frankfurt as the latest carrier of this Enlightenment anti-bullshit torch, with the book's popularity reconnecting seminar-room philosophy to the marketplace and voting booth.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: I - To Shoot the Bull
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: The Part I introduction, 'How This Book Came to Be,' explains what the volume is and is not: not a bullshit-detector manual but discussions and criticisms of Frankfurt's essay, including what it means to propose a theory of bullshit or articulate the structure of a concept. It previews each contributor: Kimbrough on why we let bullshit slide, Preti's use of G.E. Moore as a bullshit-free exemplar, Reisch's two-conversations account, Taylor on cognitive foibles, Bernal on personality pathology, and the Part II definitional debate between Frankfurt and G.A. Cohen's 'unclarifiable unclarity'. It frames philosophy itself as one of our best defenses against bullshit.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Tolerable Bullshit
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Scott Kimbrough opens his essay with his six-year-old daughter shouting through a window that the house painter's smoking is unhealthy, and William Ian Miller's Faking It dictum that truth is seldom a defense. He takes up the puzzle Frankfurt left as an 'exercise for the reader': why our attitude toward bullshit is more benign than toward lying, even though Frankfurt defines bullshit as indifference to how things really are and therefore the greater enemy of truth. The chapter promises to solve the puzzle Frankfurt posed but never attempted.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Intolerable Bullshit
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Applying Frankfurt's definition strictly, Kimbrough argues much of civility is bullshit: coerced childhood apologies are 'humiliation rituals' where truth is the last thing wanted, politeness is benign hypocrisy that saves people pain, and the Super Bowl ad or the silly communist-professors editorial is valued as entertainment. We also tolerate PR and advertising bullshit out of respect for the ends served, from Exxon's green image to spin by teachers and military recruiters. His answer to Frankfurt's puzzle: we sympathize with bullshitters doing their jobs and contemptuously dismiss their victims as suckers who deserve their fate.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Bullshit and Self-Deception
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Kimbrough turns to when bullshit becomes intolerable: the philosophy-slam regulars' dismissive 'That's bullshit,' the girlfriend's indictment in The Black Eyed Peas' 'Shut Up,' and the boss's team-builder rationalization for passing you over for a promotion. He leans on Orwell's 'Politics and the English Language' and Nineteen Eighty-Four to show political euphemism ('collateral damage,' 'smart bomb') as the language of power, tolerated because repeating spin is easy and going along with bullshit is going along with power. The chapter closes on the danger of politicians believing their own bullshit, setting up the self-deception question of how one person can play both bullshitter and dupe.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Blameless Bullshit
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Kimbrough resolves the self-deception paradox using Alfred Mele's Self Deception Unmasked: like the cuckolded husband who masks evidence of infidelity, the self-deceiver biases evidence-gathering rather than playing deceiver and dupe at once. Since Mele shows unintentional motivated belief is common (94% of professors rate themselves above average), bullshit like the entrenched prejudice that 'smart boys are smarter than smart girls' can arise without intent, which is G.A. Cohen's opening against Frankfurt's process-centered definition. Against Cohen's output-centered alternative, the conservative-talk-radio fan who builds his own conclusions on cherry-picked propaganda shows a product can be perfectly clear yet still bullshit, produced through self-deception.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Bullshit and Truth
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Kimbrough defends calling alchemy bullshit even though Isaac Newton pursued it blamelessly: the charge's function is to excuse us from taking hopeless methods seriously, not to insult the theorist. His killer analogy sorts cases: the intentional bullshitter is the murderer, the self-deceived talk-radio fan the negligent driver who kills while reading, and Newton the blameless driver beside whom the pedestrian darts, with the pejorative resting on the method or theory rather than the person. This methodology shift lets him keep Frankfurt's insight that how bullshit is produced matters while conceding Cohen's point that it can be unintentional, though he admits even philosophy's status may never be settled.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Chapter 2 - A Defense of Common Sense
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Concluding his essay, Kimbrough observes people call bullshit whenever their values are threatened, so the bottom-line businessman dismisses ethics talk and investigations of his dodgy accounting as bureaucratic bullshit, and the linguist may dismiss armchair conceptual analysis itself. He rejects a subjective definition of bullshit as whatever provokes disdain, endorsing Frankfurt's anti-subjectivist closer that 'sincerity itself is bullshit,' and concludes bullshit must be recognized and restricted to justifiable uses rather than eradicated. He closes with Orwell's advice from 'Politics and the English Language': simplify your English so that a stupid remark's stupidity is obvious even to yourself.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: The Truth Matters
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Consuelo Preti lays out Frankfurt's indifference-to-truth account and G.A. Cohen's academic bullshit as disregard for meaning, then argues both leave out bullshit's third element: the audience it needs. Bullshit, she says, sells us on our own estimation of what matters, from the Dior handbag to the guy bullshitting his way into bed or tenure. Reviewing the James Frey affair and Oprah's initial claim that truth was irrelevant because the story inspired, she proposes G.E. Moore's uncompromising commitment to truth and meaning as the model for resisting bullshit in the street and the seminar room.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: “What Exactly Do You Mean ”
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Preti dissects l'affaire Frey: if Frey intended to palm off invented events as memory, he lied and his publishers committed fraud, but if they did not care either way, it was bullshit, and what exposed the menace was Oprah's own avowal that it did not matter whether the story was true. She argues inspiration tied to an assumed true story is sabotaged by discovering it false, so Oprah's retraction ('I left the impression that the truth does not matter') shows bullshit nearly turned even her head. The strategy she draws is to turn bullshit's need to be believed against itself, and for an exemplar of resolute caring about truth she reaches to G.E. Moore.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Let’s Stop Bullshitting Ourselves
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Preti builds the Moore exemplar from biography: with Russell and Wittgenstein at Cambridge, Moore founded analytic philosophy, demolished Absolute Idealism in the 1899 'The Nature of Judgment,' and wrote Principia Ethica, which the Bloomsbury group treated as their religion. Russell's autobiography joke about the only lie Moore ever told and Woolf's 'tenacity of a bulldog' portrait of his passion for truth set up Keynes's description of Moore's method, 'What exactly do you mean?'. The key episode is Moore's public apology for losing patience with a question he took to be merely vexatious, showing that what Moore could not tolerate was precisely bullshit.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: Chapter 3 - The Pragmatics of Bullshit, Intelligently Designed
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: Preti's conclusion deploys Moore's 'A Defence of Common Sense' against philosophers who answer 'Do you believe the earth has existed for many years past?' with 'It all depends on what you mean,' a view Moore called as profoundly mistaken as any can be. She extracts a practical anti-bullshit strategy: dogged Moorean insistence on clarity, since bullshit's scorn for truth must stay masked and needs us to be less inquisitive. Her 'paradox of bullshit' is that truth and meaning do not matter to bullshit but bullshit must make itself matter to us, so caring about the truth-false distinction puts it on a short leash.

frankfurt-bullshit.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
frankfurt-bullshit.title: The Example of Intelligent Design
frankfurt-bullshit.relation: George Reisch opens his essay with Frankfurt's unsolved puzzle: if bullshitters are more dangerous to truth than liars, they should be punished more, yet we are more tolerant of them, a puzzle Frankfurt admitted on radio he really does not understand. He diagnoses the puzzle as a symptom that Frankfurt's definition took a wrong turn.
