levinas-face.relation: Christiansen frames justice as our culture's master narrative and tests it through two episodes. In 'The Case of the Substitute Face', Laura Houser's retroactive misidentification of her father going overboard and the fingerprint expert's error illustrate Levinas's face of the Other as first philosophy: the face-to-face call to care and responsibility that Mason answers every time he takes on a client, including the guilty. In 'The Case of the Perjured Parrot', the parrot Casanova's testimony and the imposter-parrot trick let Derrida's deconstruction (meaning by difference, endlessly deferred) and Arendt's public-space dialogue expose how little proof witness testimony really carries, with Heidegger's care-structured Dasein and Aristotle's action-over-character view framing the closing questions about faces and witnesses.

levinas-face.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
levinas-face.title: The Future of Our “MASS Implant”
levinas-face.relation: Stripe's MASS implant in Men Against Fire, which makes targeted humans look like monstrous 'roaches,' literalizes the chapter's claim that dehumanizing language — chosen by Brooker after columnist Katie Hopkins called migrants 'cockroaches' — is the real-world technology that enables genocide, from the Armenian and Holocaust cases through Rwanda's Tutsis to the Rohingya. Wittgenstein's 'the limits of my language mean the limits of my world' grounds how propaganda deadens empathy, and Kelman-style accounts of excluded identity explain why the villagers hate but cannot kill while the implanted soldiers kill gleefully. Levinas's face of the Other explains the turn: once Stripe sees Catarina and Alec's faces, he cannot pull the trigger, and the chapter closes on our own MASS implant — Trump's 'animals,' the ascent-of-man studies, and the temptation to reset and forget.

levinas-face.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
levinas-face.title: 29 The Dangers of Technology in Black Mirror
levinas-face.relation: Staged as a chatroom of uploaded dead philosophers (itself a Black Museum-style cookie gimmick), the chapter stages the technology debate as Francis Bacon's optimism - technology is neutral, humans mess up, the Grain could educate and MASS could treat PTSD - against Heidegger's claim that technology is a way of thinking that turns everything, including the human mind kept on call behind the Grain and Nosedive's rated behaviors, into a resource. McLuhan's 'the medium is the message,' Benjamin's aura (he recoils at being a reproduction without aura, then a 'limited' Benjamin 2.0 embraces exhibition value and Netflix's reach), Levinas's ethics of the Other against Heidegger's ontology, Arendt's ethic of responsibility born of Nazism, and Ellul's technique - the autonomous totality of efficiency-seeking methods that enslaves us - collide over episodes from The National Anthem to Hated in the Nation, until uploading all the Greek philosophers to recover techne crashes the computer.

levinas-face.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
levinas-face.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
levinas-face.relation: Brett Patterson compares Card's philotes and the ansible to Leibniz's monadology — simple, internally varied building blocks whose twining connections mirror monadic 'intercommunication' at any distance — and reads the Giant's Drink landscape and the hive-queen pupa as the buggers' engineered face-to-face encounter with Ender. Through Levinas he argues the Other's ethical claim precedes self-knowledge, so the philotic bond installs a responsibility Ender cannot escape: he cannot go home because he must become Speaker for the Dead and restore the species he destroyed.

levinas-face.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
levinas-face.title: 18. Heaven Is Other People
levinas-face.relation: Treats the show as a theological sitcom whose afterlife (Gen's algorithmic judgment, cubicles, the Jeremy Bearimy timeline) critiques a pop-Christian eschatology of disembodied Heaven and eternal conscious torment while missing the bodily resurrection of Nicene and N.T. Wright's account. Levinas supplies the positive frame: ethics precedes ontology, the face of the Other demands responsibility before any impersonal verdict — which is why Gen's points system 'wouldn't cut it' and why the show's two-shots, Eleanor's spontaneous good acts, and Chidi's 802 yeses to teaching her matter. Bonhoeffer's religionless Christianity completes the reading of Eleanor's repentance, Donna's and Tahani's confessions, and Michael's self-sacrificing Christ figure: salvation comes through intersubjective, grace-infused transformation, so 'Heaven is other people'.

levinas-face.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
levinas-face.title: NOTES
levinas-face.relation: Brett Chandler Patterson reads Lost through C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia as myth rather than allegory - the Lamp Post station and flight 316 (the Prince Caspian dedication page) wink at the source - with the island, like Narnia, a world of crisis and second chances entered by plane crash instead of wardrobe. Flashbacks of past failures (Kate the fugitive, Sayid the torturer, Charlie's addiction, Locke's kidney con) set up struggles for faith that he illuminates with H. Richard Niebuhr on faith as a center of value and revelation as communal, and with Levinas's claim that we become ourselves only through responsibility to the Other in community. The Jack-versus-Locke man-of-science/man-of-faith debate, Charlie's moth-cocoon trial, and Jacob and the Man in Black's black-and-white stone game map onto Aslan versus the White Witch, ending in redemption through the new community and Jack's sacrificial death.

levinas-face.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
levinas-face.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
levinas-face.relation: Kukkonen reads Peter's never-extinguished guilt over Uncle Ben as an 'infinite debt' modeled on Anselm's atonement theology: no good deed repays the primal transgression, so even the heroic serum rescue for Aunt May in 'The Final Chapter' (Amazing Spider-Man #33) leaves the debt intact. Against the Nietzschean escape into self-sufficient magnanimity (Ben's ghostly blessing in 'Doom Service!'), he argues via Levinas and Derrida that Peter's responsibility extends to every stranger, as when a rescued policeman with Uncle Ben's face calls him back in 'Spider-Man No More!' (#50). Following Kierkegaard's Works of Love, the chapter concludes that Peter's heroics do not pay off but deepen his debt of love, since every choice heeds one call while unavoidably failing others.

levinas-face.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
levinas-face.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
levinas-face.relation: Spencer gives a phenomenological account of bodily transformation in the films: with Merleau-Ponty, Peter's new body changes his world — walls become surfaces to climb — and grants motor knowledge that needs no calculation, while Norman Osborn's deliberately seized powers feed pride and Doc Ock's grief shows how transformation can sweep a weak will into vice. Virtue, on Aquinas's definition as the perfection of a power, develops only through choices and habits worked out across a whole life, so ethics is deeper than rule-following. With Levinas, the call to goodness is experienced bodily: sympathy with others' suffering draws Peter out of himself — he rushes into a burning building even when powerless in Spider-Man 2 — and the Green Goblin lives a self-contradiction by feigning deafness to it, while eros for Mary Jane both distracts from and ennobles the quest.

levinas-face.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
levinas-face.title: 4. Faces from Another Dimension
levinas-face.relation: Hooke uses Levinas's account of the face (and Lingis on trust) to read the Zone's faces: the bandaged woman and pig-faced surgeons of 'The Eye of the Beholder' unseat our standards of the normal, while trusted faces are weaponized by Robert Redford's Grim Reaper in 'Nothing in the Dark,' Sebastian Cabot's Satan in 'A Nice Place to Visit,' and the gentle Kanamit of 'To Serve Man.' Alicia's tear in 'The Lonely' and John and Marie Holt's wordless recognition in 'The Trade-Ins' show trust and love exceeding proof or evidence. Sartre's existential look, with Kierkegaard's Abraham and Beauvoir's second sex, frames how a face puts our freedom and trust in question.

levinas-face.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
levinas-face.title: XVI - WAR AND PEACE, POWER AND FAITH
levinas-face.relation: Kirby reads the trilogy through Levinas's distinction between false peace (a cease-fire between parties still opposed) and true peace as love of the unique, inassimilable other. Magneto embodies war: sacrificing Rogue to power his machine, reversing Stryker's Cerebro onto humanity, 'playing by their rules,' and abandoning Mystique, while Xavier embodies Levinasian peace, listening ('I'm looking for hope'), leaving Magneto his choice ('I will always be there, old friend'), and teaching Wolverine and Rogue faith in the goodness of others. Yet Xavier's psychic barriers on Jean, 'the lesser of two evils,' show even the peaceful path risks the ethical compromise Levinas warns the uncritical use of power always invites.

levinas-face.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
levinas-face.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
levinas-face.relation: Douglas McLaughlin and Cesar Torres argue that Coubertin's vague Olympism is best clarified by the phenomenological concept of intersubjectivity developed by Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, and Levinas. Treating competitive sport (via Suits's lusory attitude and the 'testing family' notion of a mutual quest for excellence) as inherently social, they use intersubjectivity to dissolve the apparent contradiction between the motto's excellence and the creed's participation, since one's victory is meaningful only through worthy opponents one is answerable to. Invoking Levinas's ethics of the face, they ground Olympic values of mutual respect, fairness, and peace in the reciprocity athletes owe one another 'running shoulder to shoulder.'

levinas-face.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
levinas-face.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
levinas-face.relation: Richard Gilmore reads After Hours as a nocturnal katabasis in which office worker Paul Hackett is repeatedly offered, and repeatedly fails at, authentic encounter with the SoHo women and their artworks (Kiki's papier-mache man, the plaster-of-paris bagel). Using Levinas's totality-versus-infinity and the ethics of conversation, Kant's two worlds of interest and disinterested aesthetic judgment, and Dewey's Art as Experience, Gilmore argues that art and sex alike (per Picasso and Nagel's 'double reciprocal incarnation') demand abandoning one's 'logic of the same' to perceive the other. Foucault's disciplinary kronos-time versus kairos, and Zizek's anamorphic spot, frame Paul's entrapment in solipsism until, encased as a literal artwork and reborn at the office gates, he finally offers himself to June.

levinas-face.book: 226 - The Philosophy of Michael Mann
levinas-face.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
levinas-face.relation: Skrodzka reads Thief and Collateral as exercises in deontology grounded in Levinas's ethics of responsibility to the Other. Frank's violent courtship of Jessie and his final destruction of his possessions, and Max's crashing of the cab after Vincent's interpellation, are staged as the self's annihilating opening to the face of the Other (glimpsed in the rearview mirror as Max's doppelganger). Using Bauman's account of liquid-modern disconnection and a leftist critique of late capitalism, she argues Mann grounds Levinasian ethics in physical labor, and defines Vincent's evil as that which is 'knowing but unknowable,' deaf to the Other's call.

levinas-face.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
levinas-face.title: Levinasian Ethics of Alterity The Face of the Other in Spielberg’s Cinematic Language
levinas-face.relation: Wright argues that Spielberg's cinematic language (shot scale, montage editing, mise-en-scene) enacts Levinas's ethics of alterity, in which meeting the unknowable 'face' of the Other demands responsibility and sacrifice, wisdom through love rather than knowledge. He contrasts the distancing long shots that render the Jaws shark and The Thing as mere threats with the intimate close-ups that 'reveal the face' in Close Encounters and E.T., then shows Schindler's List turning the same technique onto the human Other, using the red coat as the face that pulls Schindler from detachment into responsibility.

levinas-face.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
levinas-face.title: NOTES
levinas-face.relation: Brett Chandler Patterson reads Lost alongside C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia as myth rather than allegory, arguing both use a fantasy world of second chances to stage redemption in community. He aligns the castaways' violent arrival on the island with the Pevensie children's magical passage into Narnia and Edmund's betrayal-and-forgiveness arc, using the island's life-and-death setting to force existential commitment. Emmanuel Levinas's ethics of responsibility to the face of the Other and H. Richard Niebuhr's relational theology are invoked to argue that healing and faith come not individually but in communion with others.

levinas-face.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
levinas-face.title: 4. Faces from Another Dimension
levinas-face.relation: Hooke, drawing on Levinas and his translator Alphonso Lingis, treats the face as the site where trust in a stranger is risked. The Twilight Zone weaponizes our trust in familiar (actors') faces: death wears Robert Redford's face in 'Nothing in the Dark,' Satan is the avuncular Pip in 'A Nice Place to Visit,' and the Kanamits' gentle faces mask a cookbook in 'To Serve Man.' He invokes the Turing test for Corry and Alicia's love in 'The Lonely,' and finds the most truthful face of love in 'The Trade-Ins,' where the aged couple cannot bear each other's altered faces after rejuvenation.

levinas-face.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
levinas-face.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
levinas-face.relation: Zanin reads Pride and Prejudice and Zombies through Freud, Aristotle, and Levinas. She argues Regency propriety over-represses natural impulses, so Freud's id/ego/superego and the aggression drive explain why Elizabeth's zombie-slaying is sublimated aggression and cathartic release (Aristotle's catharsis), her ritual 'seven cuts of shame' a displacement of guilt over misjudging Darcy. She reads Charlotte's zombie decay as an allegory of self lost to a marriage of convenience. Using Levinas on the Other (the 'unmentionable' zombie against which Elizabeth's identity is formed) and Judith Butler's claim that the Other dwells within the self, she argues the zombie Other enables rather than overwhelms Elizabeth's identity.

levinas-face.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
levinas-face.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
levinas-face.relation: Buckingham stages a phenomenology of a wasted café afternoon over three cups, arguing against a passage from Levinas's Nine Talmudic Readings that condemns the café as a 'non-place' where relaxing without obligation lets us tolerate the world's horrors. Against Levinas, he claims the coffeehouse's public 'solitude alongside others' sustains a courteous solidarity and, like the Epicurean Garden, offers necessary respite that fuels creative responsibility rather than evading the demand of the Other. He self-consciously adopts Levinas's own phenomenological method—attending to 'what is it like?'—to defend idling as the condition for responding to suffering with grace rather than grim duty.

levinas-face.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
levinas-face.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
levinas-face.relation: Juniper Ellis shows tattoos resist any single interpretive scheme by running through cases: Loos and Lacassagne's criminological 'I tattoo, therefore I will commit murder'; the biblical Mark of Cain and St. Paul's stigmata as signs of protection and salvation; Lacan's claim that the tattoo is the first signifier that marks off the human subject; and Pacific tatau (Te Pehi Kupe's moko-as-signature, Queequeg's unreadable Moby-Dick tattoo) that incorporates a person into a collective. She reads Kant's Critique of Judgment dismissal of Maori tattooing and invokes Levinas' 'the face speaks' to argue a tattooed face is eloquent speech, crossing lines between individual and collective, saint and criminal.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: U2 and Philosophy
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Wrathall reads 'Vertigo' through Heidegger's vertigo-before-a-question and Kierkegaard's account of despair as the dizziness of a self whose sensual and spiritual sides are both essential. He uses rock's own testimony - Rammstein's 'Engel' and 'Sehnsucht', Nine Inch Nails' 'Down in It' - to confirm the existentialist thesis that neither flesh nor spirit can be renounced, with Pascal's God-shaped void as the diagnosis. He then argues that 'Beautiful Day', 'When I Look at the World', 'Grace' and 'Mysterious Ways' sketch an existential Christianity in which faith is not propositional confidence but a world-disclosing skill acquired like any know-how, and in which concrete erotic love ('if you want to kiss the sky, better learn how to kneel', the girl with crimson nails who 'has Jesus round her neck') discloses God on earth.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Nightmares
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Auxier asks why the flying monkeys and the shriveling feet of the Wicked Witch of the East give children lifelong nightmares, and answers with a phenomenology of three frightening sequences in escalating duration: the instant shriveling shot, the five-minute cyclone (paired with 'The Great Gig in the Sky' in the Dark Side of the Rainbow sync), and the monkey air-raid. Kierkegaard's Concept of Anxiety supplies the depth psychology: innocence is ignorance, and the child's dreaming spirit projects its own nothing outward, fastening fear onto figures like the monkeys (who are, he notes, played by the Munchkin actors themselves). Merleau-Ponty's lived body versus habit body explains the mechanics: cinema seizes the body's usual 'tour of inspection,' Fleming manipulates active and passive synthesis (the scoreless build-up to the window blow, the barely noticed arsenal of weapons in the Haunted Forest, the dimming lights), and children construct a rigid, inescapable habit body within a single viewing, so the nightmare is the monkey inside our own projected world.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Double Dutch
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Krnac explains Holland's five missed penalties against Italy at Euro 2000 — Frank de Boer twice, Kluivert, Stam, Bosvelt — through Kierkegaard's The Concept of Anxiety rather than Cruyff's 'chance' or Vergouw's 'poor preparation'. The self, a synthesis of body, mind and spirit (and of the temporal and eternal), must stake itself on a future-oriented choice, but freedom as 'the possibility to be able' makes every free choice an embrace of the unknown, breeding the anxiety that is 'the dizziness of freedom' — visible in de Boer's slide from a five-out-of-ten miss to a lifeless zero that telegraphed his shot to Toldo. Panenka's 1976 chip shows free action chosen without guarantee, while choosing not to choose is itself an evasion of freedom, in penalties as in life.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Robert Tally Jr. reads The Graveyard Book as 'spectral existentialism': Bod's climax, 'I'm Nobody Owens. That's who I am,' is Sartre's existence precedes essence made literal, a self made rather than found, and the climactic claiming of the name enacts the self-ownership of the nursery-rhyme pauper 'who nobody owns.' Heidegger supplies the uncanny not-at-home-ness (unheimlich) of the graveyard, which Tally, citing Foucault's 'Of Other Spaces,' calls a heterotopia, while Silas the vampire embodies Lukacs's transcendental homelessness and Kierkegaardian anxiety is transmuted by Bod into the spectral gift of Fear he wields on his bullies. The identity-leeching ghouls named after the Duke of Westminster and the 33rd President are the avatars of bad faith, and the Jacks' attempt to dodge the prophecy fulfills it like Oedipus's, showing that Bod's fate, too, is self-made.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Girls and Philosophy
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Van Loon explains the q-tip scene ('On All Fours') as Kierkegaardian anxiety made flesh: freed by her parents and facing the e-book deadline, Hannah confronts the infinity of possibilities and, like Sartre's vertigo over the cliff, shoves the q-tip into her ear - embracing all possibilities at once and relapsing into bad faith by becoming a victim of fate. Each girl handles freedom differently: Shoshanna remains in an innocence prior to freedom, Jessa jokes her way out of seriousness, Marnie denies her anxiety. Against these, the Season Two FaceTime call to Adam models Kierkegaard's leap of faith and the 'knight of faith' - surrendering, making oneself vulnerable, and accepting that anxiety will return.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: 10. On “Crying Like a Bitch”
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Roberto Sirvent and Joel Avery read Louie through Kierkegaard's claim that wherever there is contradiction the comical is present: Louie is a walking contradiction - the devoted dad who does masturbation bits - and the show stages incongruities like the homeless man showering behind a subway violinist and the decapitation in an episode called 'Bummer/Blueberries.' Kierkegaard's aesthetic sphere maps both of Louie's failures in 'Something Is Wrong' and 'Moving': the instant-gratification aesthete (the impulse motorcycle, the unaffordable townhouse fantasy) and the overthinking aesthete who cannot break up with his girlfriend or park his car, while his girlfriend shows what it is to actually choose and act. Eddie, who spits abstract truths but does nothing with them, 'plays Hegel to Louie's Kierkegaard,' embodying the gap between abstract philosophizing and lived existence that Kierkegaard attacked in Hegelianism. The closing distinction between irony (spotting the contradiction) and comedy (living with its permanent implications) is what Louis's Conan confession - crying like a bitch and finding happiness rushing in to meet the sadness - gets right.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: 7. Life, Liberty and the Pursuit of a Warm Blanket
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: The chapter explains Linus's blanket via Winnicott's transitional objects, then argues the gang's wider habits - Great Pumpkin taboos, baseball fetishes and rituals - are 'magical thinking' that manufactures an illusion of control over an uncertain world. A middle section tours the mind-body problem (Hippocrates, Descartes's dualism and pineal gland, Huxley's epiphenomenalism, Searle's emergent consciousness) to ask who is really doing the reading. The fallacies section dissects Linus's unfalsifiable Pumpkin doctrine (post hoc after the taboo-breaking 'if') and Charlie's confirmation bias, before reframing his 'pantophobia' as Kierkegaardian angst and Sartrean nausea: with adults reduced to 'Mwaa mwaa mwaa,' the kids are condemned to be free.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: 5. Horror Appeals to Our Dual Nature
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Allaire and Gehring argue horror works on Kierkegaard's dual nature, the tug-of-war between finitude and infinitude that produces despair: the show's corporeal terrors (the Demogorgon's kills, Barb's decomposing body with a slug in its mouth, Will's tentacle) trigger the fear of mutilation and extinction, while the intelligent Shadow Monster shatters our sense of being unique, echoing Ernest Becker's claim that we build cultural 'armor' against mortality. Using Carroll's paradox of horror and Stephen King's three levels (revulsion, horror, terror), they contend we enjoy confronting these fears safely from the couch, with the Shadow Monster looming over the Snow Ball as an emblem of real horrors, from AIDS to 9/11, still to come.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Stained Glass Windows in My Mind: Modality in the Imagery of Taylor Swift
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Reads Swift's imagery as modal logic: David Lewis's counterfactuals distinguish indicative from counterfactual conditionals in 'the 1', Kripke's rigid designators show that 'If I was a man / Then I'd be the man' posits an impossible world (a man could not be Taylor Swift), while 'Would've, Could've, Should've' assigns the counterfactual's antecedent to the perpetrator, not the young narrator. Kierkegaard's 'dizziness of freedom' and despair, with Heidegger's authenticity and das Man, frame counterfactual dwelling as both celebrity performance ('mirrorball') and a route to ownedness, with 'right where you left me' as the delusional extreme and 'it's time to go' as the release. Aristotle's catharsis explains how engaging these might-have-beens in song purges regret for listeners.

kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Inconclusive Unscientific Postscript Late Remarks on Kierkegaard and Kaufman
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: LaRocca pairs Kaufman with Kierkegaard on anxiety as the constitutive human condition—not worry but 'the dizziness of freedom,' the awareness of radical possibility. He argues both use pseudonymity and 'indirect communication' to distance author from work so the audience confronts its own individuality: Kierkegaard's Haufniensis/Climacus, Kaufman's Caden Cotard and the character 'Charlie Kaufman' in Adaptation. The chapter analyzes acting as inhabitation vs. impersonation (Being John Malkovich vs. The Talented Mr. Ripley), the diegesis/mimesis layering (Plato and Aristotle) of Kaufman's doubles and replicas, and repetition/recursion as the Kierkegaardian leap that love, like faith, demands—so 'the end is built into the beginning.'

kierkegaard-anxiety.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Daniel Sullivan argues that Burton and Poe channel childhood 'ontological insecurity' (R. D. Laing) into horror fantasy, using Burton's short Vincent as case study. Seven-year-old Vincent Malloy, imagining himself as Vincent Price, escapes 'necessity's despair' into fantastic possibility but slides into what Kierkegaard's Sickness unto Death calls defiant then demonic despair, clinging to a self-as-victim identity until he collapses. Sullivan reads fantasy as both consolation and danger—the flight into possibility further isolates the insecure child—and extends the possibility/necessity dialectic and Otto Rank's life/creation dialectic to Nightmare Before Christmas, Edward Scissorhands, and Big Fish.

kierkegaard-anxiety.title: Herzog’s Post-Tragic Aesthetic
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Anthony Eagan and Simon Thornton apply Kierkegaard's theory of tragedy (from the aesthete 'A' in Either/Or, plus the demonic in The Sickness unto Death) to argue that Timothy Treadwell (Grizzly Man) and Aguirre (Aguirre, the Wrath of God) are not tragic but comic figures. Both cross Herzog's 'invisible borderline' by asserting pure subjectivity over fate, romanticizing nature while ignoring the ambiguous collision of freedom and necessity that constitutes genuine tragedy. Treadwell freely engineers his own preventable death (so it cannot be tragic pain), and Aguirre, drifting in circles as self-proclaimed wrath of God, personifies the demonic refusal to repent — a 'post-tragic' comedy that aches.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: 8. Why Do We Care Who Bourdain Really Was
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Finn asks why fans cared about Bourdain's 'authenticity,' arguing his persona of freedom from bourgeois convention embodied Sartre's rejection of 'bad faith' while his meticulous control made him, per Keefe, 'Apollo in drag as Dionysus.' Reading the Hanoi/Obama episode as proof that even the President wanted to be Bourdain, she suggests his freedom (Kierkegaard's 'dizziness') may have become a trap, and proposes 'integrity' rather than authenticity as the word for his consistency.

kierkegaard-anxiety.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
kierkegaard-anxiety.title: 84. The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild as Philosophy Teaching the Player to Be Comfortable Being Alone
kierkegaard-anxiety.relation: Lay argues that Breath of the Wild teaches, chiefly through design rather than plot, that solitude is good for the player. He tests eternal return (the recurring Ganon-Zelda-Link cycle across the series), Sartrean absolute freedom and Kierkegaardian anxiety of choice (BotW's Korok-dung 'reward' and refusal to attach external meaning push players to make their own meaning), and Kierkegaard's inward 'repetition.' He lands on Mill's and Schopenhauer's defense of solitude-in-nature as self-actualizing rather than isolating, and reads sequence-breaking exploits as Marx-style spontaneous creative activity, concluding the game frames solitude as a path to eudaimonia and human flourishing.

double-consciousness.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
double-consciousness.title: U2 and Philosophy
double-consciousness.relation: Soper tracks Bono's public identity work across three paradigms: pre-modern Irish-Catholic inheritance, including a Du Boisian 'double consciousness' of the colonized Irish; the modernist artist-as-visionary, where Nietzsche, Freud and Marx destabilize the self and the Shalom fellowship nearly ends the band; and the postmodern masks of the Fly, Mirrorball Man and MacPhisto on the Zoo TV media collage, read via Lacan for 'Mofo' and via Baudrillard's simulacra for the 'Even Better than the Real Thing' video with its wax Beatles and cyber-sex imagery. Lyotardian skepticism toward grand ideologies explains the band's refusal of fanaticism in 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and 'Two Hearts Beat as One'. Soper concludes that Bono fuses all three into a 'Postmodern Christian Pragmatism' that keeps Christian conviction and debt-relief activism while adopting postmodern playfulness without collapsing into ironic detachment.

double-consciousness.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
double-consciousness.title: 2. Peculiar!
double-consciousness.relation: Ketcham reads the faction system as the Bureau's behavioral-correction experiment after a eugenics disaster, and compares the Bureau to the Tuskegee syphilis study: subjects who never gave informed consent, were denied treatment, and were treated as expendable because 'the experiment must continue at all costs.' He maps W.E.B. Du Bois's 'twoness' - double consciousness - onto Tris, who thrives in Dauntless yet belongs to no faction, and onto Tobias, whose identity collapses when he learns he tests as merely Dauntless. Closing with Gramsci, he argues Chicagoans have bought into the oppressor's story about genes and factions, so they need an organic intellectual to lead them out of the cave, and proposes Freire's praxis as the unfinished sequel.

double-consciousness.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
double-consciousness.title: 20. The Spirit of Abstraction
double-consciousness.relation: Christopher Ketcham uses Gabriel Marcel's 'spirit of abstraction' — granting an abstract category arbitrary primacy over actual persons — to explain both Nazi anti-Semitism in the novel (Loetze's chatter, Baynes surgically remaking himself to pass as Swedish, Wyndam-Matson manufacturing stories that beat the merchandise) and America's own version from slavery through Plessy v. Ferguson's whiteness-as-property. Jean-Paul Sartre's Anti-Semite and Jew supplies the hater's passion-as-faith against the rational man's groping for truth, and W.E.B. Du Bois's double consciousness names the victims' divided self-image, while Marcel's claim that peace derived from war 'contains war in a latent condition' reads the show's cold peace as war continued by lies.

double-consciousness.title: 18. Oppression Pretty Much Sucks
double-consciousness.relation: Reads I Feel Pretty through feminist critiques of oppression: Bartky's Fashion-Beauty Complex turns the desire to feel pretty into a parasitic scheme of creams and credit-card debt, Du Bois's double consciousness captures Renee post-head-injury seeing herself as beautiful against the world's verdict, and Freud's account of hating those most like us explains the Highlander-style rivalry between women. The chapter then dismantles Rawls's distributive justice via Iris Marion Young, arguing rights are not goods to hand out and that 'imagine everyone is the same' thinking entrenches privilege. The alternative is celebrating difference, which is exactly what Schumer's prettiness-as-self-celebration performs.

double-consciousness.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
double-consciousness.title: 12. Gilead as Palimpsest
double-consciousness.relation: Ketcham likens Offred's existence to holocaust by degree: her name is overwritten as the Nazis tattooed forearms, and her past survives like ink bleeding through a palimpsest. Using Derrida's sous rature (via Spivak's introduction and Heidegger's crossed-out words)—the word crossed out yet necessary—he reads her memories as 'under erasure,' and through Levinas's 'useless suffering' shows how her cocooned passivity severs her from the responsibility-for-the-other in which Levinas locates freedom, which is exactly what the he-theonomy needs to rule. With Du Bois's double consciousness and the Hitler parallel, the chapter warns that ideologues promising to cure suffering—Hitler, the Sons of Jacob—only write a new, more oppressive text over the erased old one.

double-consciousness.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
double-consciousness.title: 25 Fear of a Black Museum Black Existentialism
double-consciousness.relation: Charles Peterson reads the museum scene through Black existentialism and Africana phenomenology: colonial museums freeze African existence in an 'archaic amber' of aesthetic purity, and Killmonger's reclaiming of the mask and questioning of the curator perform a truth-telling that breaks the museum's performance of dominance. Du Bois's double-consciousness explains Killmonger's inseparable Wakandan-and-American two-ness (extended to Nakia and the War Dogs), while Paget Henry's contrast of the DuBoisian subject who oscillates between two 'We's' with Hegel's recognition-seeking subject explains why T'Chaka chooses Wakanda and abandons N'Jobu, and Plato's cave frames Killmonger as dragging Wakanda's comfortable council toward truths 'some truths are too much to bear.' The chapter concludes that Killmonger fails because wearing the mask he embraced negrification rather than shedding it, whereas T'Challa matures from a Hegelian into a DuBoisian subject by opening Wakanda to the world.

double-consciousness.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
double-consciousness.title: One and Multitudes
double-consciousness.relation: Reads Naomi through Latina feminist phenomenology — Ortega's 'multiplicitous subjectivity', Lugones's 'world-traveling', Anzaldúa's borderlands — as one subject inhabiting several incompatible social worlds at once: Belter and Roci crewmate, Marco's former partner and Holden's lover, who experiences Miller's killing of Dresden simultaneously as her captain does and 'as a Belter, Miller wasn't wrong.' Du Bois's double consciousness names her two-ness when the Inaros faction pulls her back into a world she can still slip into 'as if she'd never stopped', and Ashford's list of her identities ('radical, betrayed, hid with the Inners, big hero') shows the borderlands Belters occupy between Inner and Outer worlds. The chapter argues this unsettlement is not a defect but a critical vantage: one stream of experience can carry multiple, conflicting meanings simultaneously, and all of it — no part more than another — is who Naomi is.

double-consciousness.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
double-consciousness.title: Notes
double-consciousness.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

double-consciousness.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
double-consciousness.title: Where in the Hell is Chris Rock
double-consciousness.relation: Wisnewski reads SNL's race comedy as applied philosophy of race: the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' sketch shows Mr. Wilson's counter-slurs as an assertion of personhood against Mills's racial contract, Eddie Murphy's Mr. Robinson's Neighborhood and 'White Like Me' expose implicit bias and white privilege, and 'The Day Beyonce Turned Black' illustrates Du Bois's double consciousness. Appiah's racialism explains why Leslie Jones playing Trump strikes audiences as outrageous while white women play men routinely, and Appiah's biological anti-realism about race undercuts that reaction. 'Black Jeopardy' with Tom Hanks's MAGA-hatted Doug finds common ground across race that the 'Lives that Matter' ending sharply limits, Fanon's violence route is raised and set aside, and Crenshaw's intersectionality frames why cast diversity is more than skin-deep.

double-consciousness.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
double-consciousness.title: “I'm in Charge Now, Phasma, I’m in Charge!”
double-consciousness.relation: Perez reads Finn through Stuart Hall's account of 'black' as a politically constructed category and Du Bois's 'social heritage of slavery': as the first helmetless Black stormtrooper, Finn simultaneously evokes the Nazi Sturmtruppen and a child enslaved by the First Order, and his self-naming with Poe enacts Hartman's claim that the enslaved must fashion new identities to be free. The chapter then uses colorism, Feagin's white racial frame, and Bloomquist's minstrel studies to argue that Boyega's Finn was sidelined - minimized in marketing, reduced to comic relief and Rose's rebukes, denied his native accent like a linguistic stereotype - wasting the trilogy's most timely story, while Jannah's Company 77 and The Bad Batch hint at the fuller reckoning with stormtrooper slavery Star Wars never attempted.

double-consciousness.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
double-consciousness.relation: McDaniels reads Tommie Smith and John Carlos's 1968 Mexico City raised-fist protest as an expression of an 'oppositional consciousness' rooted in the memory of slavery and Jim Crow. He deploys Nietzsche's notion of ressentiment, the oppressed sufferer's rebellion against a dominant slave-making morality and need to release rage, and Cornel West's 'prophetic pragmatism', which frames struggle as tragic yet guided by integrity and justice, to interpret the sprinters' silent gesture. He also invokes the athletes' Du Boisian 'twoness' as black athletes and citizens, casting Smith and Carlos in a Douglass-to-Edwards lineage of public dissent as a vehicle of black liberation.

double-consciousness.title: Tongues Untied Beat Ethnicities, Beat Multiculture
double-consciousness.relation: Lee surveys the neglected ethnic and multicultural seams running through Beat authorship—Ginsberg's Jewish 'Howl' and 'Kaddish,' Kerouac's French-Canadian 'Ti Jean' and the cross-ethnic geography of 'On the Road,' Ferlinghetti's and di Prima's Italian America, and Chicano, Asian American, and Black Beat outriders (Acosta, Frank Chin, Baraka, Ted Joans, Kaufman). He frames these through multicultural theory—Said, Spivak, Bhabha, and especially Anthony Appiah's cosmopolitan account of ethnicity as interstitial—arguing Beat writing foreshadows the field of multicultural studies, a 'tongue untied' whose transnational, race-inflected voices reach back to 'Howl' and 'On the Road.'

double-consciousness.title: We Can’t Get Off the Bus A Commentary on Spike Lee and Moral Motivation
double-consciousness.relation: Beckles-Raymond reads Lee's Get on the Bus to defend a communitarian 'encumbered self' against the liberal 'unencumbered self,' arguing the Million Man March riders' racial identity is inseparable from their moral motivation. Drawing on Charles Taylor's strong evaluations and critiquing Tommie Shelby's thin-blackness solidarity, she shows each rider (George, Evan Sr., Jay, Jeremiah, Jamal, Xavier, Gary, Kyle, Randall) attends because being a good man is bound to being black, while the ejection of the self-hating Wendell marks the limits of thin identity. The film argues raced persons 'cannot get off the bus.'

double-consciousness.title: Coworking in the Kingdom of Culture Identity and Community in the Films of Spike Lee
double-consciousness.relation: Peterson uses W.E.B. Du Bois's 'Of Our Spiritual Strivings' and its 'co-worker in the kingdom of culture' to read Lee's New York films as studies of hyphenated identity and the making of American community. He traces how the Italian Americans of Do the Right Thing and Jungle Fever secure a fragile 'whiteness' only in negation of blackness (Sal, Pino, Frankie's egg-cream lament), how Summer of Sam's enclave turns on the difference embodied by punk Richie, and how 25th Hour's post-9/11 New York is disaggregated in Monty's mirror monologue. Lee's vision is a heteroglot city with 'many gates to the Kingdom of Culture.'

double-consciousness.title: Economies of Time in Clockers
double-consciousness.relation: Gilmore reads Clockers through DuBois's double-consciousness, arguing the film's dualities—the clockers' street dealing mirroring capitalist 'logic of maximum performance,' kronos versus kairos time, Hyde's commodity versus gift economies, systemic versus personal racism—make white and black viewers alike feel the anguish of Strike and Victor. The Gran Fury as predatory law, the slave-block-style police shakedown watched by Strike's mother, and Rocco seeing only his own reflection in Victor's eye illustrate Heideggerian thrownness and self-love-as-racism. Invoking Peirce's 'evolutionary love' (Radio Raheem's Right Hand/Left Hand speech), Rorty's renarrativization of who counts as 'white,' and Dewey's 'art is more moral than moralities,' Gilmore casts Lee as a pragmatist renarrativizing hate into love.

double-consciousness.title: Chapter 5 Twain’s Last Laugh
double-consciousness.relation: Kristina Gehrman argues that reading Huck as a moral hero who overcomes racism is Twain's ironic trap. Using Arne Naess's idea of identification, Aristotle on habituation of character, and Iris Murdoch's 'just and loving attention,' she gives a developmentally attuned reading of Huck as a traumatized, morally immature, still-racist child whose regard for Jim never generalizes ('I knowed he was white inside'). Twain lures his white readers into identifying with Huck's supposed triumph, then exposes their own stunted moral growth about race; Jim is the only mature adult yet is barred from identification by the novel's racist caricature. The novel's greatness is Socratic and gadfly-like rather than triumphant.

double-consciousness.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
double-consciousness.title: BLUES
double-consciousness.relation: Kimberly Connor reads the blues as story, song, and prayer — a secularized descendant of the spirituals and an African-American philosophical guide to making meaning from suffering, exemplified by the Robert Johnson crossroads myth. Using Albert Murray's idea of 'worrying the line' (breaking a phrase to emphasize or subvert) as both technique and survival philosophy, she casts the bluesman as an 'Omni-American' whose art dissolves black/white division, invoking Du Bois's double consciousness and Cornel West's claim that the blues chronicles catastrophe 'with grace and dignity.' She argues Martin Luther King, Jr.'s nonviolent resistance and Brother Will Hairston's 'Alabama Bus' show the blues functioning as prayer and an agent of social change.

double-consciousness.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
double-consciousness.title: 70. Jerry Seinfeld as Philosopher The Assimilated Sage of New Chelm
double-consciousness.relation: Stern and Gimbel argue that Seinfeld's observational comedy is 'neo-Talmudic': like the rabbis who interpret the fixed text of the Torah, Seinfeld takes an accepted 'given' (shared phenomenological experience, e.g. the milk bit) and generates surprising wisdom by viewing it from an oblique angle. They read Seinfeld's outsider vantage through Du Bois's double consciousness (the assimilated Ashkenazi Jew who sees through two lenses at once) and invoke Derrida's differance as reintegrating Jewish pluralist epistemology into Western thought, with Nietzsche's slave-revolt as an analogy for how Jewish philosophy was made invisible. The sitcom Seinfeld, by contrast, is cast as the modern 'Chelm' joke cycle, parodying that same neo-Talmudic reasoning by pushing local logic (Elaine's Jujyfruits, Schindler's List) into absurdity.

double-consciousness.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
double-consciousness.title: 71. Dave Chappelle as Philosopher Standing Up to Racism
double-consciousness.relation: Benko and Burch treat Chappelle as a philosopher of race whose comedy of incongruity exposes the contradictions of American racism, reading his 'every Black American is bi-lingual' remark and sketches like 'Clayton Bigsby' and 'The Racial Draft' through Du Bois's double consciousness. They argue Chappelle's ethics of fairness, choice and personal responsibility unintentionally echoes Bonilla-Silva's 'color-blind racism,' and use bell hooks's Ain't I a Woman to show how his gendered 'Oppression Olympics' and use of 'bitch' reproduce the sexism hooks says Black men absorb, so his trans and gender jokes rank Black men as the most oppressed group. The chapter's core apparatus (incongruity/schema theory of humor, color-blind racism) sits outside the taxonomy.

plantinga-basic-beliefs.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
plantinga-basic-beliefs.title: U2 and Philosophy
plantinga-basic-beliefs.relation: Merrick sets XTC's 'Dear God' - being 'just struck' that no loving, all-powerful God rules this world - against U2's laments ('Wake Up Dead Man', 'Peace on Earth', '40') and Bono's reading of the Psalms as the blues shouted at God: both share outrage, but U2 adds yearning for the redemption promised in 'the story about eternity' plus Jubilee 2000-style action against debt and AIDS. He then argues the atheistic reaction to evil cannot be reason-producing, since neither divine design nor unguided evolution would give us a faculty that 'just sees' atheism from evil, any more than one that just sees there is no plant life on Mars. If God instead made us so that outrage at evil can trigger conviction that he will make all right, U2's reaction - 'Grace makes beauty out of ugly things' - can be as reasonable as visual perception.

plantinga-basic-beliefs.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
plantinga-basic-beliefs.title: 2. Maybe Jenner Was Right
plantinga-basic-beliefs.relation: Cowan uses Jenner's suicide in the exploding CDC (1.6 'TS-19') to pose Camus's question 'Why should I not commit suicide?', and rejects Jenner's despair the Camusian way: Michonne in 4.9 'After' - slaying her own walker look-alike and then her two pet walkers - is his Sisyphus in revolt, unlike Gareth, whose revolt lacks the respect for human dignity that makes Sisyphus happy. He then objects that Camus never explains why human life has intrinsic dignity in a godless universe, noting that Sartrean authenticity could equally license the Governor's Woodbury experiments or Gareth's cannibalism, and turns to Hershel's providential hope as the religious alternative. Following Plantinga, he argues belief in God can be properly basic through a sensus divinitatis - Hershel seeing God's hand in 2.4 'Cherokee Rose' and the tornado-spared barn of 5.10 'Them' - so if God exists, Jenner was not right.

plantinga-basic-beliefs.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
plantinga-basic-beliefs.title: 4. Is it God or the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown
plantinga-basic-beliefs.relation: Using It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown (1966), the chapter asks whether belief without evidence can be rational, contrasting the classic evidentialist view (rational beliefs must be basic or derived from basics, in the tradition of Locke and Hume) with Alvin Plantinga's properly basic beliefs and a virtue theory of rational belief built on Aristotle-style intellectual virtues like humility, courage, and charity. Linus fails on every account - he insulates himself from counterevidence ('If you really are a fake, don't tell me'), lets the belief cost him friends and trick-or-treating, and never updates after the Pumpkin's no-show - while Sally's pumpkin-patch vigil shows rationality as a balance of evidence, value, and risk. The upshot: God-belief formed responsibly within a trusting community can be rational in a way Linus's solitary, evidence-dodging Pumpkin faith cannot.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
pythagorean-harmony.title: U2 and Philosophy
pythagorean-harmony.relation: Han-Pile tests three traditional philosophies of music against U2's own talk about music: the rationalist (Descartes and Leibniz's 'unconscious exercise of arithmetic', satirized by Hit Song Science finding U2 mathematically close to Beethoven), the subjectivist (Hegel and Wackenroder on music as the expression of inner feeling, mirrored in Bono's method of articulating in words the feeling the band first found in improvisation), and the metaphysical (the Pythagorean-Boethian musica mundana whose harmony with our music 'Gloria' and 'Wake Up Dead Man' both invoke, consummated in Schopenhauer's music as direct copy of the will, which Nietzsche's critique of Wagner undermines). Against all three she sets Heidegger's Stimmung: music discloses shared moods - atmospheres that color how a whole world shows up, as 'Beautiful Day' or 'Bullet the Blue Sky' demonstrate. U2's vocation is thus to shift the numbed basic disposition of the age ('Zooropa', 'Numb') toward joy and compassion - rock 'n' roll as an alarm clock for 'dreaming up the world we want to live in'.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
pythagorean-harmony.title: November
pythagorean-harmony.relation: Auxier's rhapsodic essay channels Bart Giamatti ('the Philosopher') on baseball as sacred leisure and uses Pythagoras—everything is Number, each thing's essence an unnamed ratio—to argue the sacred geometry of Fenway cannot be reduced to the dimensions of mere space. He casts the scorecard-keeping quantifiers (Steinbrenner, the Mathematikoi) against the meaning-seeking true believers (Giamatti, the Akousmatikoi), and claims the Yankees' demolition of their own temple, not the 2004 comeback, is what truly lifted the Curse of the Bambino and guarantees Boston will never tear down Fenway. It ends with circular time: the season, like the Babe finishing his career in Boston, always comes home.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
pythagorean-harmony.title: 3. Wonder and Philosophy as a Way Home
pythagorean-harmony.relation: Nathan and Leilani Mueller argue the theme song's 'neighborly day in this beautywood' makes beauty a transcendental leading to wisdom, as in Plato's Symposium ascent to loving the beautiful itself and Aquinas's convertibility of truth, goodness, and beauty. Reading Rogers's questioning of batteries and boxes (episode 1655) through the Meno's genuine curiosity and Pierre Hadot's account of philosophy as a way of life, they tour the show's three philosophical spaces: the domestic living room, the community visit (blind saxophonist Eric Kloss), and Make-Believe as thought experiment.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
pythagorean-harmony.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
pythagorean-harmony.relation: James Heathers asks why the most improbable band became the one true originator of heavy metal and answers with Schopenhauer: industrial Aston, Birmingham was a monument to the ceaseless, unsatisfied striving of the Will, and music, which maps directly onto the Will itself, gave that world its voice. The tritone's numerically hideous ratios, a point traced through Rameau back to Pythagoras, make it the natural interval of morbidity, which is why "Black Sabbath" and everything from Liszt's Dante Sonata to death metal is marinated in it, and why doom was not a predictable development like Deep Purple or Led Zeppelin. He closes on the irony that Schopenhauer, who preached ascetic denial of the Will, would have loathed a band that answered factory-town despair by smothering the Will in lager, hash, cocaine, and women, only to breed more want in the worst of all possible worlds.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
pythagorean-harmony.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
pythagorean-harmony.relation: Reads South Park's music through the Greek doctrine of ethos: Sextus Empiricus' story of Pythagoras sobering drunk youths with slow aulos tunes and Plato's banishment of the soft Ionian and Lydian modes anticipate episodes where music directly changes behavior — Slayer's 'Raining Blood' scattering the hippie horde in 'Die Hippie Die', Cher blasted at the ATF standoff, and the Brown Noise in 'World Wide Recorder Concert'. Plato's tripartite soul maps how the Succubus's 'Morning After' spell enchants Chef's appetitive soul until the boys reverse the melody, while the Sirens' cosmic harmony in the Republic's Myth of Er links back to pitch-planet correspondences. Against Plato's view of music as inferior imitation, Schopenhauer's claim that music copies the Will itself explains why Grandpa's Enya torture in 'Death' communicates despair better than argument; authenticity judgments (Phil Collins appreciated only on Ritalin, Cartman's cynically reworded Faith + 1 hits) echo Plato's demand that music imitate the good.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
pythagorean-harmony.title: 20. The Mystery of Math
pythagorean-harmony.relation: Barta and Lee cast the debate over whether math is invented or discovered as Protagoras versus Pythagoras, mapped onto Foundation. Protagorean relativism ('man is the measure') and modern formalism (Hilbert, Poincaré) appear in the Empire's politicized, self-serving use of math and Gaal Dornick's culturally contingent base-ten counting, while Plato and Aristotle rebut relativism via the Theaetetus and the Law of Non-Contradiction ('if Hari's a liar, he dies'). Pythagorean realism/mathematical Platonism—numbers as the fundamental reality—appears in Luminism's holy number three, Kalle's poetic proofs, and the Foundationists' quasi-religious faith that psychohistory reveals reality's mathematical structure, with Gödel, Quine-Putnam indispensability, and Wigner's 'unreasonable effectiveness' as modern heirs and Aristotle as the standing critic.

pythagorean-harmony.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
pythagorean-harmony.title: GARDENING
pythagorean-harmony.relation: Neuman decodes the Bosquet de la Colonnade at Versailles as a symbolic Temple of Apollo that glorifies Louis XIV as overseer of cosmic harmony. He argues Hardouin-Mansart fused the circular peripteral temple with Hadrian's Maritime Theatre, and used simple ratios (1:2 bays) drawn from the Pythagorean-Platonic system of universal proportion—the harmony of the spheres tied to Apollo's seven-stringed lyre and seven planets—to align architecture, the seven planets, and monarchical order. The spandrel pairing of lyre and panpipe evokes the Apollo–Marsyas/Pan contests, read as the reason-versus-passion, Apollonian-versus-Dionysian dichotomy; the whole garden is also linked to Descartes's geometrization of boundless axial space.

schopenhauer-will.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
schopenhauer-will.title: U2 and Philosophy
schopenhauer-will.relation: Han-Pile tests three traditional philosophies of music against U2's own talk about music: the rationalist (Descartes and Leibniz's 'unconscious exercise of arithmetic', satirized by Hit Song Science finding U2 mathematically close to Beethoven), the subjectivist (Hegel and Wackenroder on music as the expression of inner feeling, mirrored in Bono's method of articulating in words the feeling the band first found in improvisation), and the metaphysical (the Pythagorean-Boethian musica mundana whose harmony with our music 'Gloria' and 'Wake Up Dead Man' both invoke, consummated in Schopenhauer's music as direct copy of the will, which Nietzsche's critique of Wagner undermines). Against all three she sets Heidegger's Stimmung: music discloses shared moods - atmospheres that color how a whole world shows up, as 'Beautiful Day' or 'Bullet the Blue Sky' demonstrate. U2's vocation is thus to shift the numbed basic disposition of the age ('Zooropa', 'Numb') toward joy and compassion - rock 'n' roll as an alarm clock for 'dreaming up the world we want to live in'.

schopenhauer-will.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
schopenhauer-will.title: The End of the Leash
schopenhauer-will.relation: Travis Anderson unleashes Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy on Reservoir Dogs, reading the color-coded aliases as an Apollonian dismemberment of a primordial unity and the pop soundtrack ('Little Green Bag', 'Stuck in the Middle with You') as the Dionysian music structuring the film from within. He defends the ear-cutting scene's excess as creative Dionysian expression rather than gratuity, answering Ella Taylor's charge of 'frighteningly pure art'. Mr. Pink's survival—professional, anonymous, untouched by compassion—marks the reconstituted Dionysus: all but one color must die for the gang to be rejoined in the redemptive orgy of Greek tragedy.

schopenhauer-will.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
schopenhauer-will.title: A Link to the Present
schopenhauer-will.relation: Compagno argues that the word 'I' in Zelda simultaneously names Link, the virtual body, and the player, the invisible will, and builds this into a 'Schopenhauerian Console': as Schopenhauer held, we have freedom of action but not freedom of will, since the decisions of the unknowable will never appear in consciousness (against Descartes' free mind and Dennett's Cartesian theater critique). Kant's transcendental subject, standing at the border of experience, becomes the player's perspective from which Hyrule exists, what Foucault would call an empirical-transcendental doublet. The payoff: Link's quest is fated and scripted, yet the player wills it in a perpetual present, enacting Schopenhauer's lesson that a determined life is still lived as one's own free act.

schopenhauer-will.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
schopenhauer-will.title: When the Levee Breaks Excess as Truth
schopenhauer-will.relation: Flynn reads the Swan Song logo (Rimmer's falling Apollo) and songs like 'Kashmir,' 'Whole Lotta Love,' and 'When the Levee Breaks' through Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy: individuals are temporary manifestations of a chaotic primordial unity (Schopenhauer's will), and Dionysian art redeems that suffering by celebrating the very excess that undoes us. The sandstorm of 'Kashmir,' the relentless sexual longing of the traveling blues, Plant's death-moan-as-ecstasy in 'In My Time of Dying,' and Bonham's levee-crushing drums all enact 'excess revealed as truth' — joyous laments in which words bleed into music. This is not hedonism, Flynn argues, but ecstatic awareness that the self's boundaries are artificial and its dissolution is a kind of reunion.

schopenhauer-will.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
schopenhauer-will.title: A (Bronx) Cheer to the Red Sox “Without Whom, Not as Much”
schopenhauer-will.relation: Writing as a Yankees fan, Konig asks what makes a championship worth wanting: after Schopenhauer's picture of endless striving as suffering, he brings in Richard Taylor (meaning lies in the activity itself, never its completion) and then Nietzsche's will to power, which seeks worthy resistance to overcome. Thought experiments—a childhood 'big game' that turns out to be tee-ball, and the 2004 Sox trouncing the minor-league Atlantic League—show a title without worthy opposition is hollow. Hence the Yankees' twentieth-century dominance would mean nothing without the Red Sox as the sustained, worthy enemy (Bucky Dent, the Pedro-Zimmer melee, the 2004 ALCS collapse included).

schopenhauer-will.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
schopenhauer-will.title: Are These World Series Champions Really Our Red Sox
schopenhauer-will.relation: Lee casts pre-2004 fandom as a Kierkegaardian leap of faith ('We Believe') and the Curse of the Bambino as Schopenhauer's irrational deterministic will, with the 1918–2004 cycle of spring hope and October collapse as Camus's Sisyphus. But he argues fans are really existentialists: blaming losses on fate or the Curse is Sartrean bad faith that evades responsibility, since fans did hold Bill Buckner (1986 error) and Grady Little (leaving a spent Pedro in during 2003 ALCS Game 7) individually accountable. The 2004 and 2007 champions remain 'our' Red Sox because we freely choose to care about the team's journey, not because it has a fixed essence; a coda borrows Russell's point about ambiguous reference for the word 'Yankee,' and Andy Wasif's appendix runs Yankees-as-evil through relativism, objectivism and subjectivism.

schopenhauer-will.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
schopenhauer-will.title: Escape to Doctor Who
schopenhauer-will.relation: Reads the Master as the personification of Schopenhauer's blind, pointless Will: the Doctor's line 'In many ways we have the same mind' is taken literally, so the Master is the dark noumenal side in everyone, seen in the hypnotized Farrel whose ambition the Master acts out and Colonel Trenchard whose patriotism becomes the Master's weapon in 'The Sea Devils'. Building from Kant's phenomena/noumena distinction, he explains the Will as the inaccessible force we glimpse through inner bodily awareness, evil because purposeless. Watching the Doctor's serial victories is then offered as a light, Schopenhauerian escape through art from the terror of the Will.

schopenhauer-will.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
schopenhauer-will.title: I Listen to Public Radio
schopenhauer-will.relation: Natasha Liebig reads Squidward as Schopenhauer made flesh: his endless craving for musical fame and revenge on Squilliam exemplifies the blind, irrational will-to-live whose frustration just is suffering, so even success could never satisfy him and others' joys (SpongeBob and Patrick playing) become his bellum omnium. Yet Squidward's clarinet, self-portraits and dance are Schopenhauer's aesthetic escape — will-less contemplation of universal Ideas, with music the most metaphysical art — granting fleeting moments of peace until his neighbors interrupt. The chapter closes on the irony that Schopenhauer's genius is childlike, so SpongeBob and Patrick's effortless wonder may make them the truer artists.

schopenhauer-will.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
schopenhauer-will.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
schopenhauer-will.relation: Liane Heller pairs Cohen and Schopenhauer - born and died on September 21st, the autumnal equinox - as two explorers of the world's irrational negativity who both retreat to 'a room' to create. Schopenhauer's directionless Will, his pessimism about a life of constant suffering, his notorious misogyny in 'On Women,' and his ascetic denial of the will-to-live (with his contempt for Judaism and preference for the Upanishads and Buddhist compassion) are set against Cohen's affirmation that love is 'the only engine of survival,' his five-year Zen retreat that could not hold him, and his return to the Judaism of the 'little Jew who wrote the Bible.' A closing imagined dialogue has a humbled Schopenhauer confronted with Cohen's self-compassion and ordinary joys, admitting the limits of his own field of vision.

schopenhauer-will.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
schopenhauer-will.title: Justified and Philosophy
schopenhauer-will.relation: The chapter reads Harlan's family bonds through Freud's Oedipus Complex - Raylan bails Arlo out only at stepmother Helen's request, and Coover whimpers 'I'm sorry, Mamma' while cradled in Mags's arms after she hammers his hand, the submissive son destroyed by his need for his mother's approval. It then applies Schopenhauer's pessimism to Winona's pregnancy: if life is suffering, as On the Vanity of Existence argues, bringing a child into Harlan is selfish vanity, and Mags's dynasty-building - grooming Loretta, bequeathing the weed business - is the will-to-live seeking immortality through the family name. Only Boyd and Ava's unsentimental care for the demented Arlo, the chapter suggests, escapes both the Oedipal trap and the vanity of lineage.

schopenhauer-will.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
schopenhauer-will.title: 2. Sex Has Something Behind It
schopenhauer-will.relation: John Heaney pairs Louis with Schopenhauer: both see human existence as error-shaped misery, but more importantly both treat sex as the will-to-live tricking the intellect into serving the species while we mistake the species' good for our own. He reads the 'Come on, God' stand-up (every beautiful thought about a woman followed by a disgusting one) and Louie's 'So Old/Playdate' speech that 'sex is really trying to have a family' as comedic versions of Schopenhauer's metaphysics of love, with episodes like 'Bummer/Blueberries' (a decapitation killing Louie's lust mid-non-date), 'Elevator Part 4' (the civil divorce flashback ending in a possible pregnancy), and 'Eddie' (a man losing the will-to-live along with the will-to-love) enacting the oscillation between sexual arousal and suicidal despair. Even Louis's devotion to his daughters fits Schopenhauer's claim that the sexual delusion transfers to offspring, which is why 'Eddie' ends with Louie refusing to name his reasons to live - he has to pick up his kids in the morning.

schopenhauer-will.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
schopenhauer-will.title: 5. Jimi, Janis, and Jim
schopenhauer-will.relation: Traces 'genius' from the indwelling genie of an art to Goethe as the first person the public called a genius, then applies Kant's doctrine — the genius gives the rule to future art, produces what no determinate rule can govern, and cannot explain or teach what he does — to Jimi (having the Experience learn 'Sgt. Pepper' on one hearing to play it back to the Beatles three days after its release), Janis ('a victim of my own insides'), and Jim. Schopenhauer's dark side of genius — more mind than character, a will that 'affirms its own life by denying the life of others' — explains why the 27 Club burned out, and why we say 'Jimi lives' but 'Jim is still alive.'

schopenhauer-will.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
schopenhauer-will.title: 17. Through Plastic Our Secrets Seen
schopenhauer-will.relation: Uses Schopenhauer's World as Will to explain why the citizens of Twin Peaks keep living lives they despise: all willing arises from deficiency and suffering, so Shelly cannot leave Leo, Ben cannot face his children, and Ed is consumed oscillating between Norma and Nadine, while the blind will — not reflection — determines who we become. Since only pain is known directly and its absence slides into boredom and banality (Ed's restless drama-making), the town's double lives — Jacoby's coconut tapes hiding Laura's confession, Bobby's dealing, Ben's brothel — are the will's concealed kernels. Laura's wrapped corpse then functions as the reveal: death shows each character's truth, and the chapter closes by turning Socrates' unexamined life against itself, asking what happens when self-examination only uncovers what we wished hidden, as Cooper's daily-present advice offers the lone consolation.

schopenhauer-will.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
schopenhauer-will.title: 6. You Don’t Need to Be Human to Have a Human Hand
schopenhauer-will.relation: Sue Zemka contrasts the film's opening eye — reason and consciousness, in a tradition Arendt summarizes as thinking figured as seeing — with its closing image of Deckard's hand reaching toward Ana's through glass, the sense of touch leading out toward others. Schopenhauer explains K's wondering gaze at his own hands in the snow as the human predicament of being both will and representation, subject and object at once, while Condillac's and Maine de Biran's statue thought experiments ('I feel, therefore I am' against Descartes's cogito) are charged with imagining humanness in isolated figures. The film's answer is relational and political: humanness is made in relationships and resistance, from the Joi-Mariette hand-synced sex scene to the final father-daughter touch.

schopenhauer-will.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
schopenhauer-will.title: 19. Beauty of The Elder
schopenhauer-will.relation: Courtland Lewis uses KISS's reviled concept album Music from 'The Elder' as a case study in aesthetics. He contrasts objective theories of beauty (Plato and the Golden Ratio, tested against the 4/4 stomp of 'Rock and Roll All Nite') with Hume's taste and Kant's immediacy thesis that beauty is judged without inference, adds the disinterestedness of aesthetic pleasure, and applies Noel Carroll's moderate actual intentionalism (with Jerrold Levinson on what a musical work is) to argue that fans and band co-create the album's meaning. Peter French's collective memory explains why 'The Elder sucks' hardened into fan identity after Casablanca reordered the track listing and wrecked the boy-hero story, and Schopenhauer's claim that music expresses the in-itself of the world redeems the fans who find the album beautiful.

schopenhauer-will.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
schopenhauer-will.title: Free to Be You and Me
schopenhauer-will.relation: Barker reconciles Cylon programming with freedom through compatibilism and Schopenhauer's 'intelligible character': Boomer's sabotage and shooting of Adama and her betrayal of the Cylons to save Tyrol both flow from one innate, conflicted character, just as Baltar's cowardly 'conversion' to the Cylon god expresses his opportunism. Tigh's decision to keep serving after learning he is a Cylon ('My name is Saul Tigh; I am an officer in the colonial fleet') shows character unchanged by revelation. Starbuck's 'special destiny' in 'Maelstrom' is reread not as fate but as her own character - mother-induced self-doubt at war with pilot confidence - which she finally accepts in the vortex; freedom is not freedom from programming but the necessity of manifesting who one already is.

schopenhauer-will.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
schopenhauer-will.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
schopenhauer-will.relation: James Heathers asks why the most improbable band became the one true originator of heavy metal and answers with Schopenhauer: industrial Aston, Birmingham was a monument to the ceaseless, unsatisfied striving of the Will, and music, which maps directly onto the Will itself, gave that world its voice. The tritone's numerically hideous ratios, a point traced through Rameau back to Pythagoras, make it the natural interval of morbidity, which is why "Black Sabbath" and everything from Liszt's Dante Sonata to death metal is marinated in it, and why doom was not a predictable development like Deep Purple or Led Zeppelin. He closes on the irony that Schopenhauer, who preached ascetic denial of the Will, would have loathed a band that answered factory-town despair by smothering the Will in lager, hash, cocaine, and women, only to breed more want in the worst of all possible worlds.

schopenhauer-will.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
schopenhauer-will.title: 21 Listening to the Music of Indiana Jones John Williams and Aesthetic Appreciation
schopenhauer-will.relation: Argues that John Williams's score, more than the stunts or cinematography, drives aesthetic appreciation of the films, walking cue by cue through 'In the Idol's Temple,' 'Marion's Theme,' the 'Desert Chase,' 'Scherzo for Motorcycle and Orchestra,' and 'The Miracle of the Ark.' Applying Jenefer Robinson's philosophy of music, our responses split into culturally coded associations (marches with patriotism, chorales with reverence, Eastern-inflected themes with calm), 'emotions of appreciation' aroused by the sheer beauty of the writing, and emotion-guided grasp of complex structures like the scherzo's shifting keys. Schopenhauer's claim that music fitted to a scene 'discloses its most secret meaning' explains how the villain chords reveal Toht and the Ark cue makes the divine wrath felt.

schopenhauer-will.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
schopenhauer-will.title: Franken-Stark
schopenhauer-will.relation: Curtis argues Iron Man dramatizes the problem of progress: Schopenhauer's insatiable will explains why every technological fix — the chest plate, the armor, the artificial nervous system — spawns new suffering and dependency, and his pessimism, with Kierkegaard's freedom within insecurity, Nietzsche's flawed Übermensch going out 'in a blaze of glory,' and Sartre's 'cautiously optimistic' existentialism, recasts Iron Man as a tragic antihero rather than a perfected Superman or Batman. Stark's wounded heart, alcoholism as self-medication ('the demon is not in the bottle but in the addict'), and doomed romances with Bethany Cabe and Rumiko Fujikawa make him the flawed hero who has simply learned to live with imperfection. Like Mary Shelley's monster, his extensions have become him — we are all 'Franken-Starks' facing the consequences of our own inventions.

schopenhauer-will.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
schopenhauer-will.title: A Link to the Present
schopenhauer-will.relation: Dario Compagno uses Schopenhauer's distinction between freedom of action and freedom of will — consciousness never witnesses the moment of decision, only hears the will's outcomes — to model the player-Link relation in Zelda. He proposes a 'Schopenhauerian Console' against Dennett's Cartesian theater: Link is the immanent virtual body in Hyrule, the player's will is the transcendent force outside it, and Kant's transcendental subject is the perspective on the border of experience that connects the two when the gamer becomes 'Link's player'. Foucault's 'empirical-transcendental doublet' explains why 'I am Link' is ambiguous exactly the way 'I' is ambiguous in real life, pointing at once to a body and to an invisible ruling will.

schopenhauer-will.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
schopenhauer-will.title: Notes
schopenhauer-will.relation: Belluomini analyzes how Junkie XL's score drives Fury Road aesthetically. Aristotle's Politics Book 8 and his theory of catharsis explain why the 'Bloodbag' cue's war-drum rhythms imitate the War Boys' anger and fear while purging ours, and 'emotions of appreciation' at the beauty of 'Brothers in Arms' and 'Storm Is Coming' deepen our admiration of the film. Max's cello motif — one, two, or three repeated notes — telegraphs his panic, safety, or menace and advances the plot with almost no dialogue, and Schopenhauer's claim that the right music is a scene's 'most accurate and distinct commentary' fits the hopeful 'Claw Trucks' cue as Max chooses redemption.

schopenhauer-will.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
schopenhauer-will.title: Fade to Black: Absurdity, Suicide, and the Downward Spiral
schopenhauer-will.relation: Justin Donhauser and Kimberly Blessing read 'Fade to Black' as a meditation on suicide. Against the Schopenhauerian pessimism that life is a downward spiral 'to the musty stench of corpses' - where suicide paradoxically affirms the Will-to-life - they set Camus' absurd: the narrator who loses the will to live surrenders, while Camus' absurd hero lives in revolt, freedom, and passion. Since Schopenhauer and Camus both reject suicide as escape, and Hetfield insists 'writing is therapy', the song's effect is Aristotelian catharsis - purging despair - rather than an endorsement of suicide.

schopenhauer-will.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
