schopenhauer-will.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
schopenhauer-will.relation: Reads South Park's music through the Greek doctrine of ethos: Sextus Empiricus' story of Pythagoras sobering drunk youths with slow aulos tunes and Plato's banishment of the soft Ionian and Lydian modes anticipate episodes where music directly changes behavior — Slayer's 'Raining Blood' scattering the hippie horde in 'Die Hippie Die', Cher blasted at the ATF standoff, and the Brown Noise in 'World Wide Recorder Concert'. Plato's tripartite soul maps how the Succubus's 'Morning After' spell enchants Chef's appetitive soul until the boys reverse the melody, while the Sirens' cosmic harmony in the Republic's Myth of Er links back to pitch-planet correspondences. Against Plato's view of music as inferior imitation, Schopenhauer's claim that music copies the Will itself explains why Grandpa's Enya torture in 'Death' communicates despair better than argument; authenticity judgments (Phil Collins appreciated only on Ritalin, Cartman's cynically reworded Faith + 1 hits) echo Plato's demand that music imitate the good.

schopenhauer-will.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-will.title: Notes
schopenhauer-will.relation: Argues Rust Cohle's stated pessimism and in-principle embrace of suicide closely track Schopenhauer's view that suffering is built into the world with no providential redemption, yet the two diverge because Schopenhauer condemned suicide as an affirmation of the will-to-live rather than its denial. The chapter traces Rust's three-stage arc — jaded wannabe-suicidal pessimist who nonetheless energetically investigates the Dora Lange case, resigned drinker, and finally cautious affirmer of life after the Yellow King confrontation — and contends his detective work is really motivated by a Schopenhauerian morality of compassion and justice, not mere 'programming.' Rust's finale conversion is read as an evidence-based judgment that thoroughgoing pessimism is intellectually dishonest, since compassion and justice do score nontrivial victories.

schopenhauer-will.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-will.title: Notes
schopenhauer-will.relation: Reads Carcosa, the Yellow King, and Ledoux's 'time is a flat circle' as cosmic horror in the lineage of Lovecraft and Ligotti, arguing that the genre's dread — that monsters exist and the fixed laws of nature may fail — is a metaphor for realizing Schopenhauer's blind will, with Rust's car monologues in 'The Long Bright Dark' presented as a beginner's guide to Schopenhauer. It notes Rust inverts the usual Lovecraft protagonist by starting the story already horrified, and that eternal recurrence framed through Schopenhauer's sphere-of-time makes even the rescued children's torment maddeningly endless. The chapter closes by complaining that the finale 'Form and Void' betrays both genres: the occult becomes ordinary crime and Rust's 'light is winning' star-field reverses Schopenhauer's pessimistic cosmology.

schopenhauer-will.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-will.title: Notes
schopenhauer-will.relation: Traces Cohle's opening monologue directly to Schopenhauer — reality as a purposeless will whose satisfied desires breed only boredom, answered by ascetic denial of the will-to-live rather than suicide. It then explains Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as the true test of life-affirmation, via the Gay Science demon and Zarathustra's ordeal with the Small Man, and interprets will to power as finding meaning in overcoming resisting conditions, so that affirmation does not mean approving everything that happens. Hatab argues the show's horrified version of the flat circle is Schopenhauerian rather than Nietzschean, and that Cohle's 'light is winning' ending is ambiguous — if it rests on a supernatural reunion with Sophia, it would betray Nietzsche's this-worldly affirmation.

schopenhauer-will.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-will.title: Notes
schopenhauer-will.relation: Argues 'time is a flat circle' means neither a metaphysical cosmology nor M-theory physics nor reincarnation, but is Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as a thought experiment about how to live. Tracing Rust's pessimism and his lack of the 'constitution for suicide' (echoing Schopenhauer's claim that suicide affirms the will-to-live, with starvation as its only true denial), it shows the flat circle operating as both trap and cure: obsessing over it keeps Rust on the Yellow King case until his near-death experience becomes the 'tremendous moment' of amor fati. Heidegger's view in Being and Time that anxiety before death can empower meaningful existence frames Rust's final affirmation — escaping the flat circle by faithfully acknowledging it, through sacrifice.

schopenhauer-will.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
schopenhauer-will.title: 17. Through Plastic Our Secrets Seen
schopenhauer-will.relation: Winters uses Schopenhauer's World as Will and Idea to argue that the townsfolk (Shelly, Leo, Ben, Josie, Ed, and Laura) do not freely choose the lives they despise but are driven by the blind will, and so live double lives whose secrets a single death exposes. Laura, unlike the others who mismanage their passions, was denied the chance to develop her own values, so she pursued danger, drugs, and prostitution to see herself through her own eyes; death, he argues, reveals true character (the townsfolk's rush to bury her, their guilt), turning Socrates' unexamined-life dictum uneasy—sometimes what examination reveals is a monster we would rather not see.

schopenhauer-will.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
schopenhauer-will.title: Ride the Pink Horse Money, Mischance, Murder, and the Monads of Film Noir
schopenhauer-will.relation: Silver reads Robert Montgomery's Ride the Pink Horse as a prototypically noir embodiment of Schopenhauer's The World as Will and Representation. The revenge-driven Gagin, like Hugo, is enslaved to money and will—'a man can do what he wants, but not want what he wants'—and takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world, blind to the monads and Platonic-cave shadows of fate around him. Against him stand Pancho's suffering kindness and the Indian girl Pila's selfless compassion, which Silver aligns with Schopenhauer's dictum that 'compassion is the basis of all morality' and his prizing of aesthetic transcendence. The carousel (tío vivo) and the burning of Zozobra, the god of bad luck, become symbols of will's pointless circular striving from which only sacrifice and art offer escape.

schopenhauer-will.book: 239 - The Philosophy of Werner Herzog
schopenhauer-will.title: Nature and Natural Meaning in Grizzly Man
schopenhauer-will.relation: Marc Furstenau reads Grizzly Man as Herzog's philosophy of nature, arguing that Herzog's vision of nature as chaos, hostility, and murder mirrors Schopenhauer's terrifying Will and the fact/value split, and that Herzog blames Timothy Treadwell's sentimental faith in natural harmony for his and Amie Huguenard's deaths while secretly sharing Treadwell's amor fati. Using Iris Murdoch's Metaphysics as a Guide to Morals and Mary Midgley's Beast and Man, Furstenau contends that both Herzog and Schopenhauer succumb to an 'outrageous simplicity' that denies animal agency; against them he argues, via Midgley, that culture is natural and interspecies sympathy is real, reading Treadwell's extreme close-up of the bear (where Herzog sees 'only the overwhelming indifference of nature') as evidence of imaginative continuity between human and animal.

schopenhauer-will.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
schopenhauer-will.title: Escape to Doctor Who
schopenhauer-will.relation: Ken Curry reads the Master as Schopenhauer's Will personified. After sketching Kant's phenomena/noumena and Schopenhauer's identification of the noumenal thing-in-itself as a blind, pointless (and thus evil) Will known indirectly through the body, he argues the Master ('in many ways we have the same mind,' 'Logopolis') is the dark Will present in everyone. Through 'Terror of the Autons' and 'The Sea Devils' he shows the Master exploiting the fatal vanity of Farrel and Colonel Trenchard as their own evil counterpart, with good (the Doctor) narrowly triumphing so the Will's cruelty entertains rather than oppresses us.

schopenhauer-will.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
schopenhauer-will.title: 13. Punk’s Not Dead
schopenhauer-will.relation: Auxier argues punk predates its 1976 naming (the Rolling Stones' 'She Said Yeah', the Troggs, MC5) and mocks philosophers' game of stacking necessary conditions, drawing on his own 1983 stints in New Wave, Hardcore, and Art Punk bands to map the scene's 'line in the sand'. The essay's pivot is Schopenhauer as 'a punk' - hater of Hegel, of women, and of noise, yet the philosopher who elevated music to the redeemer of miserable lives as the direct utterance of the Will - and since Schopenhauer revered Beethoven, once derided as noise, Auxier concludes punk is ordered symbolic form (physical sound, encoding, symbol) delivering usable energy, so punk's not dead.

schopenhauer-will.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
schopenhauer-will.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
schopenhauer-will.relation: Howe distinguishes fine art, erotica, and pornography by the 'aesthetic distance' or disinterestedness the viewer can sustain, drawing on Schopenhauer's account of aesthetic contemplation (the perceiver dissolving individual will to become a 'pure subject' mirroring the object) and Bullough's 'psychical distance'. He argues pornography merely provokes vulgar genital arousal by exaggerating body parts out of gestalt balance (contra Feinberg, who allowed a painting to be both fine art and porn), so it forfeits disinterest entirely, while erotica provokes affection tied to romantic love and can approach fine art. Using Degas' Nude Study he concedes erotica and fine art differ only by degree, whereas pornography differs in kind because it permits no aesthetic attitude.

schopenhauer-will.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
schopenhauer-will.title: BLUES
schopenhauer-will.relation: David C. Drake argues that the blues' distinctive achievement is presenting 'sadness as beauty,' which lets performers and listeners find their own sorrow beautiful and thus therapeutic. He surveys theories of beauty — Plato's proportion/harmony/unity and Aristotle's order/symmetry (a beautiful life needs some sorrow), Kant's claim that beauty is a subjective-yet-universal judgment requiring reflection, Lyotard's sublime that 'pleases only by causing pain,' and Schopenhauer's view that aesthetic contemplation temporarily frees us from the striving Will — and links beauty to truth and goodness (Keats, Nietzsche's 'whoever despises himself respects himself as one who despises') to explain why blues sorrow feels good.

philosophical-zombies.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
philosophical-zombies.title: Resting in Peace
philosophical-zombies.relation: Manuel Vargas argues the Undead are not a natural kind but a nominal kind - vampires, zombies, and composite creatures like Frankenstein's monster share nothing except our classificatory practice - and that most actual Undead would probably be of natural origin (viruses, viroids, seeds, cryonics cases) rather than supernatural. He distinguishes philosophical zombies (Chalmers's conscious-less duplicates) from genuinely Undead beings, then defines malevolent evil as acting on a non-instrumental desire to harm others. On that definition zombies (mere appetite, like a deadly virus) and even vampires (whose damnation, contrary to early Buffy, need not add malicious motives) probably lack it, so if we ever meet the Undead they would be less likely to be evil than any random living person.

philosophical-zombies.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
philosophical-zombies.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep
philosophical-zombies.relation: Larry Hauser stages the philosophy-of-mind zombie debate through Blade Runner's Replicants: Descartes's animal automata and his hats-and-coats worry about other minds, Turing's universal machines grounding functionalism, Kripke's necessity of scientific identifications (water is necessarily H2O), and Searle's silicon-chip replacement scenario show how zombies 'eat' behaviorist, functionalist, and identity-theoretic accounts of mind. He then deploys his own 'good zombies' - the beloved who might be a zombie, super-smart NEXUS 9s, venerable zombie thinkers - to block the dualist retreat on the cognitive side of the mind. The essay closes by doubting, with Chalmers's phenomenal zombies in view, that such zombies are coherently conceivable after all, and asks whether Deckard has been 'retiring' persons like Rachel all along.

philosophical-zombies.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
philosophical-zombies.title: Postmodern Postmortem
philosophical-zombies.relation: Dale Jacquette distinguishes Hollywood zombies from Chalmers-style philosophical zombies, imagines a smiley-face birthmark that makes the latter visible, and argues that since zombies lack consciousness, pain, and intention, they are amoral - so zombie gladiatorial games would wrong no one, an improvement on the Roman munera Seneca condemned as pure murder. The thought experiment then turns on itself: even with zombie-only upbringing, screened audiences, and everything short of actual suffering on the zombies' side, the games would still be wrong for what they symbolically enact - the social condoning of slaughter of genetically human beings for entertainment. The conclusion is that consciousness and personhood do not exhaust morality: zombies get a moral pass, while the entire moral burden falls on the conscios who organize and watch.

philosophical-zombies.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
philosophical-zombies.title: Transformers and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Koepsell accepts that Autobots are virtuous and Decepticons vicious, then asks whether ethical war-bots are even possible, using the military's autonomous-weapons program, Asimov's Three Laws, and a kitten-sensing washing machine to argue that designed-in 'ethics' is only the designer's morality, like A Clockwork Orange's conditioned Alex, because it involves no real choice. Searle's Chinese Room and Turing's test then cast doubt on whether any mind, even our own, makes genuinely free choices, so he concludes that the appearance of virtue - behavior that reliably works - is all we ever have for humans or Autobots alike, and we should build machines as well as Optimus Prime and Bumblebee.

philosophical-zombies.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
philosophical-zombies.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep
philosophical-zombies.relation: Larry Hauser reads Blade Runner's replicants alongside the philosophical-zombie thought experiment: like Rachel, who passes as human until a Voigt-Kampff test, zombies are outwardly perfect replicas with 'nobody home' inside. He traces the problem from Descartes's beast-automata and hats-and-coats worry about other minds, through Turing's universal machines and Kripke's necessary identifications (water is H2O), to the way zombie scenarios devour behaviorism, functionalism, and mind-brain identity theory, using Searle's silicon-chip replacement to imagine consciousness shrinking while behavior continues. His own 'familiar' and 'super-smart' zombies (a beloved with no qualia, NEXUS-9 geniuses) argue thought without felt experience is conceivable, before he concludes the phenomenal-zombie conception may self-destruct because a first-person point of view requires the very qualia it strips away.

philosophical-zombies.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
philosophical-zombies.title: Postmodern Postmortem
philosophical-zombies.relation: Dale Jacquette distinguishes Hollywood zombies from Chalmers's philosophical zombies, imagining birthmarked beings whose behavior is run entirely by the brain stem so they speak, run corporations, and bleed like conscios while feeling nothing. He then proposes zombie gladiators: since amoral automata cannot suffer or anticipate death, arena blood sport between them seems morally permissible where Roman games condemned by Seneca were not. The thought experiment turns on itself: shielding conscios from attachments and vicarious suffering cannot cure the institution's symbolic statement that killing human-shaped beings for entertainment is fine, so even if consciousness grounds moral responsibility, how we treat the unconscious still reflects on us, and zombies can be wronged in the only sense left, through what we make ourselves.

philosophical-zombies.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
philosophical-zombies.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: T. Bradley Richards takes The Sandman's Dreamworld seriously as a hypothesis: could our nightly dreams be travels to a mind-independent place like Morpheus's realm? Starting from Zhuangzi's butterfly dream and Descartes's dream argument, he uses Berkeley's God-sustained idealism as a model for how Morpheus's mind could uphold the Dreamworld's order, and a thought experiment about glitchy dream-travel defuses Descartes's appeal to the discontinuity of dreams. Against the objection that dreams are blatantly contradictory ('it was Dave, but it also wasn't Dave'), he deploys Russell's theory of descriptions against Meinongian subsistence, Chalmers-style conceivability-implies-possibility reasoning from philosophical zombies, and Graham Priest's dialetheism, concluding that dreams could be experiences of an objective world, with waking and dreaming on a par.

philosophical-zombies.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
philosophical-zombies.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Editor Wayne Yuen's introduction argues that zombies are worth doing philosophy over: an apocalyptic world without government, law enforcement, or private property raises live questions about how survivors should treat one another, whether life becomes 'nasty, brutish, and short', and whether it is wrong to kill a walker. He frames walkers philosophically through Descartes's mindless human-looking automatons and David Chalmers's P-zombies, creatures functionally like us with no inner life. Morgan keeping photo albums instead of supplies in 'Days Gone Bye' shows that what we leave behind after the apocalypse is how we lived - our philosophy.

philosophical-zombies.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
philosophical-zombies.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Gordon Hawkes uses the P-zombie debate to ask whether there is something in a person no walker can eat. Rick telling Morgan over zombified Duane that 'that's just his body' voices Cartesian dualism, while Dr. Jenner's TS-19 scan - the neocortex 'you part' that never comes back - voices materialism, as does Dr. Stevens's dying claim that he is 'just evolving into a different, worse life form'. The chapter stages Chalmers's zombie argument (a molecule-identical twin with no inner experience) against Dennett's zimbo objection, with Ryle's 'ghost in the machine' marking the interaction problem for dualism, and closes on the intuition that no brain scan of Test Subject 19 reveals what the zombie fever feels like.

philosophical-zombies.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
philosophical-zombies.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether 'you' survive a walker bite, testing bodily identity, behaviorism, and functionalism as theories of personal survival against Jenner's verdict that after death 'everything you ever were... gone'. His centerpiece adapts Daniel Dennett: survivors yoke walkers to plows and tanks, dangle meat to move them between positions labeled 1 and 0, and gradually build a rope-and-corpse computer functionally identical to a human brain - which behaviorism and functionalism must call conscious, yet which we can conceive as utterly dark inside. The lesson is that we cannot know whether any system, walker, animal, or AI, is conscious, so treatment of non-human systems may need to err on the side of caution.

philosophical-zombies.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
philosophical-zombies.title: Violent Ends
philosophical-zombies.relation: Richards asks what it is like to be a host, combining three lenses: Searle's biological naturalism (thinking machines must be built from materials with the right causal powers, and the hosts' synthetic flesh may qualify), Nagel's bat (even if hosts are conscious, their perfectly relived memories, curated pain, and blind spots like 'it doesn't look like anything to me' may make their experience as inconceivable to us as echolocation), and Chalmers's philosophical zombies (hosts behave exactly like us, yet beings identical to them with no inner light are conceivable). He reads Ford's contradictory testimony — praising Bernard's guilt as 'a thing of beauty' while denying consciousness exists — as a shift to a deflationary view with no threshold for being alive, and argues the show's choice to film human and host experience in the same style keeps the question deliberately open while fostering empathy.

philosophical-zombies.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
philosophical-zombies.title: The Last Bit
philosophical-zombies.relation: Cook asks whether Rapture's Plasmids and ghosts refute physicalism and answers no: Plasmid powers are genetically engineered via ADAM and thus describable in physical vocabulary, while contractor Bill McDonagh's audio diary explains the ghosts of Rapture as leaked memories passed through gene-swapping, so all their facts supervene on physical facts in Chalmers's sense. The classic anti-physicalist pressures, Chalmers's zombie argument and the Nagel-style gap between objective physical description and subjective qualia ('the smell of poo'), do not apply because Rapture's phenomena carry no extra subjective residue. Invoking Clarke's third law that advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic, he concludes Andrew Ryan did not choose the impossible.

philosophical-zombies.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
philosophical-zombies.title: Ethical Issues
philosophical-zombies.relation: Focusing on White Christmas's cookies and Ashley Too's synaptic snapshot, the chapter argues behavior can never settle whether an artificial system is conscious: the Turing test fails against Geminoid-robot-style cases where recorded signals produce human-like behavior, and philosophical-zombie possibilities plus the point that computations and information patterns are subjective interpretations (not objective physical properties) mean only discovering the physical neural correlates of consciousness could tell us whether a cookie feels pain. It then separates copying from transferring: with souls and substance dualism rejected, Black Museum's 'transfers' are really copies, and San Junipero's upload would house a copy whose future experiences are as alien to Yorkie as a plaster cast of her feet. Ethically, if cookies are conscious, then Matt's breaking of Cookie-Greta, Daly's captives, and Clayton's keychain are torture of persons, and it is the very uncertainty about cookie consciousness that lets characters rationalize the abuse - which is why the in-world legislation granting cookies human rights matters.

philosophical-zombies.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
philosophical-zombies.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Henry Jacoby wields Westeros's strange beings against the mind-body problem: Nagel's 'what it is like' question becomes 'What is it like to be a direwolf?', and wargs like Bran-in-Summer and Orell's eagle ask whether one point of view can literally inhabit another. Against Descartes's denial of animal consciousness (only language users have souls; Mormont's raven crying 'Corn!' is a machine), he argues Ghost's pain behavior and direwolf physiology ground animal consciousness exactly as our brothers' behavior grounds theirs. Wargs do not refute materialism - in Westeros magic violates physical law without invoking nonphysical stuff - and 'Zombie Sansa', the philosophers' phenomenal zombie, together with the reanimated wights, is impossible in our world (with Russell, experiences are brain events known directly) and conceivable beyond the Wall only because the supernatural breaks the laws of nature.

philosophical-zombies.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
philosophical-zombies.title: NOTES
philosophical-zombies.relation: Distinguishes Matt Parkman's supernatural telepathy from the 'mundane mind reading' everyone performs, then argues even Matt's power cannot solve the problem of other minds: the suicidal woman's thoughts he hears in the bar ('One Giant Leap') could be part of a Maury-Parkman-style illusion, and a brain-to-brain link could never rule out that others are Chalmers-style philosophical zombies. After grounding the skepticism in Descartes' cogito and method of doubt, it defends our everyday attribution of minds by analogy (Audrey Hanson reading Claire's insincerity) on pragmatic grounds, and maps Matt's progression from hearing thoughts to nightmare manipulation and compulsion onto the four adaptive functions philosophers assign to mind reading: interpretation, prediction, coordination, and influence. It closes by showing why neuroimaging-based technological mind reading remains a pipe dream, since brain recordings are quantitative syntax without semantics.

philosophical-zombies.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
philosophical-zombies.title: NOTES
philosophical-zombies.relation: Antti Kuusela argues from Wittgenstein that behavior is the touchstone — indeed constitutive — of mental life, so the question is whether Terminators behave like beings with minds. Searle's Chinese room and Ned Block's blockhead explain the read-only T-101's head-up-display of canned responses as symbol-shuffling without understanding, and the T-1000's 'I know this hurts' seems empty from a machine that cannot feel pain. The pivot is the learning-mode switch John and Sarah flip: the T-101 acquires slang, keeps promises, and acts for reasons Skynet cannot predict, passing the Lovelace test, and the Wittgensteinian dismissal of Chalmers's philosophical zombie removes the last reason to deny it a mental life — making the steel-mill sacrifice the destruction of a rights-bearing someone rather than something.

philosophical-zombies.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
philosophical-zombies.title: Notes
philosophical-zombies.relation: Interrogates the tension in Cohle's 'deny our programming' line: if we are programmed biological puppets, how could we deny the program? It contrasts Sartre's radical free will and its crushing responsibility with Frankfurt cases and second-order desires — Marty as the 'wanton' who never acts on his desire not to desire affairs — and with Schopenhauer's will and Spinoza's causal determinism, both of which locate a kind of freedom in increased consciousness of our causes. The chapter concludes that self-consciousness, Rust's 'tragic misstep,' is in fact the only tool for reprogramming ourselves, imagined through a world of philosophical zombies who could neither suffer nor choose.

philosophical-zombies.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
philosophical-zombies.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Wayne Yuen's introduction argues that a serialized zombie apocalypse, unlike a zombie movie, lets us explore life among the dead: how survivors like Rick, Lori, and Glenn should treat one another and divide labor, whether private property and equality survive without government, invoking Morgan weighing photo albums against supplies and the question of whether the new world is 'nasty, brutish, and short'. It frames zombies philosophically through Descartes's mindless automatons and Chalmers's P-zombies, and asks whether killing a walker could be wrong if walkers have inner lives, like dolphins or pandas, just less cute.

philosophical-zombies.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
philosophical-zombies.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
philosophical-zombies.relation: Gordon Hawkes uses Rick's words to Morgan over zombified Duane ('that's just his body—there's nothing of your son left in there') to set up Cartesian dualism against the materialism of Drs. Jenner and Stevens ('just tasty meat all the way down'), with Ryle's 'ghost in the machine' as the standard objection. He then explains Chalmers's zombie argument that a physically identical unconscious twin is conceivable, so consciousness is non-physical, and Dennett's 'zimbo' rebuttal that a creature endlessly reflecting on its own states would believe itself conscious. The chapter closes by asking whether there is 'something it is like' to be a walker shuffling through Atlanta, and sides with Rick's anti-materialism.

philosophical-zombies.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
philosophical-zombies.title: Violent Ends
philosophical-zombies.relation: Bradley Richards asks what it is like to be a host, using Nagel's 'what is it like to be a bat?' to argue that whether we can conceive host experience depends on how similar it is to ours, and Searle's biological view to ask whether hosts are made of the right stuff. He catalogs how host perception, emotion, and especially memory differ from human (Maeve's perfect reliving of memories versus our hazy constructive recall, 'is this now?'), and weighs Chalmers's philosophical zombies against the hosts. He notes the show depicts host and human experience in the identical cinematic style to preserve ambiguity, and links memory, self-consciousness, and freedom via Dolores's maze, suggesting hosts may be phenomenally conscious before becoming self-aware.

philosophical-zombies.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
philosophical-zombies.title: A.I. Artificial Intelligence Artistic Indulgence or Advanced Inquiry
philosophical-zombies.relation: White argues A.I. dramatizes the mind-body problem through the mecha child David, proposing a 'Strengthened Turing Test' (STT) in which the audience knows he is a machine yet must judge whether he truly loves Monica. He runs Searle's Chinese Room (David as mere rule-follower with no qualia) against Nagel's 'what is it like' and Chalmers's zombie argument and property-dualist multiple realizability, which would let a sufficiently complex David be genuinely conscious. White contends the imprinting device—David's built-in need for one other being—is what lets him pass the STT, sidestepping Cartesian dualism's interaction problem.

philosophical-zombies.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
philosophical-zombies.title: 18. Foundation and Consciousness
philosophical-zombies.relation: Lang and Haun use Foundation to explore consciousness, noting Asimov's robots (Daneel, Andrew Martin) are simply granted minds and that a system giving all the right signs could still be a Chalmers-style philosophical zombie. Their central case is Golan Trevize merging with the starship Far Star, which they read through Clark and Chalmers's Extended Mind Thesis and the Otto-and-Inga notebook example, arguing Trevize goes beyond Otto because he gains qualitatively new experiences (feeling magnetic fields, 360-degree sight). They then test extension against Integrated Information Theory and split-brain evidence, and read the planetary group mind Gaia as panpsychism (invoking Spinoza's God-as-nature, Leibniz's monads, and Fechner's world-mind) that faces the Combination Problem, partly eased by telepathic links that relax the privacy of minds.

natural-kinds.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
natural-kinds.title: Resting in Peace
natural-kinds.relation: Manuel Vargas argues the Undead are not a natural kind but a nominal kind - vampires, zombies, and composite creatures like Frankenstein's monster share nothing except our classificatory practice - and that most actual Undead would probably be of natural origin (viruses, viroids, seeds, cryonics cases) rather than supernatural. He distinguishes philosophical zombies (Chalmers's conscious-less duplicates) from genuinely Undead beings, then defines malevolent evil as acting on a non-instrumental desire to harm others. On that definition zombies (mere appetite, like a deadly virus) and even vampires (whose damnation, contrary to early Buffy, need not add malicious motives) probably lack it, so if we ever meet the Undead they would be less likely to be evil than any random living person.

natural-kinds.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
natural-kinds.title: Resting in Peace
natural-kinds.relation: Manuel Vargas asks whether the Undead could really be evil and answers that they are probably less likely to be evil than any random living person. Working from a conceptual analysis of what counts as Undead (ruling out p-zombies and Rob Zombie alike), he distinguishes natural-origin Undead (viruses, seeds) from supernatural ones, then applies the account of evil as acting from non-instrumental desires to harm: classical zombies lack the capacities for evil, and even vampires' black reputation traces less to malice than to the creepiness of needing blood, the Dracula/Vlad the Impaler lineage, and lazy 'creepy equals evil' reasoning.

natural-kinds.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
natural-kinds.title: The Office and Philosophy
natural-kinds.relation: Nys uses Brent's quiz grievance about Mr. Spock (half-Vulcan, half-human) and his Crufts pedigree-dog analogy, Gareth's 'look at the ears' classification test, the dwarf/midget/elf/pixie interrogation of Alex, and Tim and Dawn's 'lethal blow' prank to introduce the problem of natural kinds. Realist answers come from Kripke (water is H2O whatever we call it), Aristotle's matter-and-form essences, and the DNA evidence separating Bornean clouded leopards from mainland cousins, while Wittgenstein's language games and Quine's point that our innate similarity senses mislead support the constructivist that we lay classification on an unstructured world. The verdict: nature supplies real differences but never carves itself into kinds, and the line-drawing remains up to us.

natural-kinds.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
natural-kinds.title: XIV - MUTANTS AND THE METAPHYSICS OF RACE
natural-kinds.relation: Pierce asks whether mutants are a race in any metaphysically serious sense. Biologically, no: human racial groups already fall far short of subspecies-level genetic difference (using Appiah's variation figures), and mutants share nothing but an activated X-gene that non-mutant humans also carry, spread across every human ancestry from Storm's Kenya to Cannonball's Kentucky. Socially, they could become a race: Days of Future Past's camps and Genosha's 'gene-positive' slavery, with its slur 'Genejoke,' deliberately mirror racial categorization and oppression, so the X-Men's racial language is best read as a loose, 'racelike' analogy that does real argumentative work.

spinoza-monism.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
spinoza-monism.title: Fast Zombies
spinoza-monism.relation: K. Silem Mohammad explains the horror of zombie slowness through Freud's uncanny - the return of the repressed, from White Zombie's hypnotized slaves (a figure for alienated industrial labor) to Romero's shuffling radioactive ghouls - then rebuilds undeath on Spinoza's Ethics: death as a body's parts acquiring a different proportion of motion and rest, the mind as a 'spiritual automaton,' and (via Deleuze's ethology of composition, decomposition, and bad encounters) zombies as bodies that decompose living bodies and recompose them as zombie bodies, replacing moral good and evil with good and bad. The fast zombies of 28 Days Later and the Dawn remake abandon hunger and the uncanny for pure rage and 'the Real,' signaling a late-capitalist permanent crisis in which the living have had their chance and blown it.

spinoza-monism.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
spinoza-monism.title: Sometimes We Live No Particular Way but Our Own
spinoza-monism.relation: Matthew Turner argues that a 'Playin' in the Band' jam — the band drifting from the tune into long collective improvisation and back — models a Stoic solution to free will shared by Epictetus, Spinoza, and Chuang Tzu: freedom is not uncaused choosing but responding well within constraints, so by the dichotomy of control there is no point resenting the band when it flubs a climax. Spinoza's definition of the free thing as one determined by its own nature, and Chuang Tzu's butcher who cuts oxen by spirit beyond skill, show the band letting the music 'play them' — Jerry's 'Tennessee Jed' riff never played the same way twice — as learned skill becomes second nature. Because the Dead jam within banks (keys, mutual listening, ability) yet generate something genuinely new and transcended every genre of 1960s music where the Monkees merely copied the Beatles, the Stoic attitude proves creative rather than quietist, an analogue for living freely within our own constraints.

spinoza-monism.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
spinoza-monism.title: “Obviously, the Borg Can’t Hold Their Liquor”
spinoza-monism.relation: Decker asks 'What's it like to be a Borg?' and tests whether monist metaphysics justify the Collective: Parmenides's changeless, perfect Being matches the Borg's 'bringing them closer to perfection', Spinoza's one substance (God or Nature) makes assimilationist determinism intelligible and finds truth in Seven of Nine's nostalgia for collective harmony, and Hegel's teleological Geist — the whole 'the world, aware of itself' — most closely mirrors the Borg's galactic quest for an Omega-molecule perfection of 'infinite parts functioning as one.' Yet 'I, Borg' shows Hegelian Spirit working through individuals: Hugh's redemption transforms the Enterprise crew's self-understanding, proving nothing is wholly alien and freedom can coexist with collectivity. Via Haraway's cyborgs and against Kass's 'wisdom of repugnance', the chapter concludes the Borg horrify us because the natural/artificial dualism is already obsolete in our technologized lives — 'if we are the Borg, then resistance truly is futile.'

spinoza-monism.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
spinoza-monism.title: An Altar Boy’s Public Penance
spinoza-monism.relation: Flamm and Rea take Buffett's altar-boy grudge against Catholic moralism — the 'bakers' of 'Fruitcakes' who try to cure humanity's half-baked madness — and frame it with Nietzsche's charge that 'there was only one Christian, and he died on the cross.' They then cast Buffett as a latter-day Spinoza: like the excommunicated lens-grinder he rejects the orthodox God, finds God in nature ('One Particular Harbor' as a view 'sub specie aeternitatis'), and treats wealth, honor, and sensual pleasure ('Cheeseburger in Paradise') as means toward the greatest happiness rather than sins. Nietzsche's Dionysian intoxication ('God's Own Drunk') and Shakespeare's Sir Toby versus the moralist Malvolio support embracing natural madness, and the chapter closes by arguing Buffett's confessional songs ('Coastal Confessions') make his Parrothead audience the priest who grants the altar boy's public penance and forgiveness.

spinoza-monism.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
spinoza-monism.title: A New Lease of Life for the Undead
spinoza-monism.relation: The editors' introduction surveys the twenty-first-century zombie and vampire boom (Twilight, True Blood, Zombieland, Fido, Pride and Prejudice and Zombies, zombie walks, Humans Versus Zombies) and asks why the Undead fascinate us when bears would not. Its answer contrasts the vampire, who embodies a Nietzschean super-humanity beyond good and evil still charged with unheeded guilt, with the zombie, a sub-Nietzschean, Spinozan force of decomposition where matter interacts with matter beyond all morality. Zombies thus work as hyperdead memento mori: imagining zombiehood lets us imagine our own annihilation as entry into a condition of liberated power, while the obviously unreal monster helps us shut out the real terrors it reflects.

spinoza-monism.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
spinoza-monism.title: Fast Zombies
spinoza-monism.relation: K. Silem Mohammad explains the classic slow zombie via Spinoza's account of bodies defined by ratios of motion and rest, where death is no absolute state but a redisposition of parts, so voodoo zombies at industrial modernity's dawn figure alienated labor and Romero's ghouls an impersonal, relentless compulsion. Through Deleuze's reading of composition and decomposition, zombie feeding becomes an ethological process of absorbing other bodies' relations, and Spinoza's replacement of good/evil with good/bad (anticipating Nietzsche) dissolves the zombie's supposed evil into 'bad encounters' between bodies. The fast zombies of 28 Days Later and the Dawn remake then mark a shift from Freudian uncanny return to full-blown crisis: pure rage without hunger or grievance, bodies in faster motion, leaving us an impossible identification with the composition that will decompose us.

spinoza-monism.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
spinoza-monism.title: Humanism Needs Its Evangelists, Too
spinoza-monism.relation: Treats Snakes & Arrows ('Far Cry,' 'Armor and Sword,' 'Faithless') as secular humanism stung by resurgent fundamentalism, and reads Peart's revolutionary trilogy — 'Beneath, Between and Behind,' 'Bastille Day,' 'A Farewell to Kings' — as Enlightenment humanism already anxious about its own decline. The core argument is rhetorical: Rush deliberately clothes humanist content in sacred and mystical language ('Something for Nothing''s Lord's Prayer motif, 'Jacob's Ladder''s storm read through Spinoza's God-as-nature and the experience of the sublime) because humanism needs evangelists who inspire wonder rather than mere argument.

spinoza-monism.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
spinoza-monism.title: The House that Holmes Built
spinoza-monism.relation: Kate Rufa reads Holmes as Spinoza's 'just man': Watson's 'calculating machine' verdict in The Sign of the Four, his unshaken calm while baiting Moriarty before the Reichenbach leap in 'The Final Problem', and the geometric 'Book of Life' of A Study in Scarlet all show passion mastered by reason into adequate ideas and true freedom. The twist is the cocaine: shooting up between cases means Holmes sacrifices his conatus (the striving to persist in being) to keep his mind at a godlike pitch of activity, a God-complex no finite mode can sustain. Moriarty, equally rational but ruled by passive affects, is the shadow of this ideal, echoing Socrates' Apology point that harming others inevitably harms oneself.

spinoza-monism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-monism.title: What’s Really Real
spinoza-monism.relation: Traces the 'veil' theme from Parmenides' dokos and the Indian maya to Ed Fletcher seeing 'the fabric of reality split open' in 'Adjustment Team' and the shadow world of 'Jon's World.' It locates Dick's enduring conviction that the empirical world is not ultimately real in the Plato he was given at UC Berkeley — the archetypal realm of Forms behind sensory appearances — and in his professed affinity for Spinoza's Deus sive natura, alongside the Pre-Socratics he devoured.

spinoza-monism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-monism.title: Chapter 16 - The Blob Necessitates
spinoza-monism.relation: Matthew McCall's introduction argues that VALIS is about the fuzzy line between delusions, reality, and psychological wellbeing, following Horselover Fat through breakdowns and pink-beam revelations, and that Dick's signature theme is the interplay between metaphysics and emotions. It quotes Dick's own statement of affinity for Spinoza's 'Deus sive substantia sive natura' and promises that Spinoza's system supplies the groundwork for Fat's path to emotional liberation, a path that begins with the pink beam and with blobs.

spinoza-monism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-monism.title: Of Blob
spinoza-monism.relation: The section recounts Dick's 2-3-74 experience and the eight-thousand-page Exegesis, then uses Fat's Tractatus to teach Spinoza's Ethics through a goo analogy: the blob is substance ('that which is in itself and conceived through itself') while everything in everyday life, including us, exists only as its modes. It concludes that despite what our senses suggest, thinking through the substance-mode distinction shows we are all contained in the blob, so what is true derives from concepts rather than sense experience.

spinoza-monism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-monism.title: The Nature and Origin of the “Mind”
spinoza-monism.relation: This section reads Fat's cosmology, in which the 'Mind' created the 'Brain' to preserve the memory of its dead sister and left every constituent of the universe partly deranged with grief, against Spinoza's proofs in the Ethics that there is exactly one infinite, uncaused substance, which is why Spinoza calls the blob God or Nature. It stresses Spinoza's necessitarianism: the will is not a free cause, even God had no choice not to create the world, and the actual timeline is the only metaphysically possible one, so on both Fat's and Spinoza's schemes suffering is a built-in metaphysical consequence.

spinoza-monism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-monism.title: Of Plasmatic Bondage
spinoza-monism.relation: The section explains Fat's plasmate doctrine, with VALIS a Vast Active Living Intelligence System and Sophia the two-year-old who briefly cures Fat by revealing he is an alternate personality of Philip K. Dick before dying of a radiation overdose. It contrasts this failed miraculous cure with Spinoza's intellectual therapy: since 'in so far as the mind understands all things as necessary, so far has it greater power over the affects,' Fat should process Gloria's death as a necessity he could never have prevented, dissolving his guilt.

spinoza-monism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-monism.title: The Power of the Intellect, or of Fat’s Emotional Liberation
spinoza-monism.relation: This section argues that although Fat's 'Mind' cosmology, unlike Spinoza's necessitarianism, leaves room for free will, Fat can still borrow Spinoza's therapy: Tractatus entry 29 says we fell through an intellectual error, taking the phenomenal world as real, so he is morally innocent, and Spinoza's concession that we suffer insofar as we are part of nature means suffering can be limited, not eliminated, by understanding its causes. It closes skeptically, noting that monist liberation demands ditching free will, contingency, and self-evident beliefs, so within a monist world 'sometimes it is an appropriate response to reality to go insane.'

spinoza-monism.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
spinoza-monism.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
spinoza-monism.relation: Namvol argues that 'Glob' is the post-apocalyptic corpse of the Christian God: combining Don Cupitt's claim that gods live only in worship and practice with Nietzsche's 'God is dead,' he traces how the Mushroom War destroyed the believers, churches, and rituals that kept God alive, leaving Ooo an empty exclamation. Pantheism fails as a rescue because evil is native to Ooo's nature (Gunter, the eternally self-existing Abadeer), so God cannot simply have become the land. Against Dostoevsky's 'without God all things are permitted,' the chapter sides with Žižek—that morality's shadow, guilt, outlives God—as when Finn's self-regulation kicks in after 'All the Little People' and 'Dungeon Train,' making Finn, not Glob, the true savior of a godless world.

spinoza-monism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
spinoza-monism.title: “An Energy Field Created by All Living Things”
spinoza-monism.relation: Baur argues that the Jedi metaphysics is non-dualistic rather than a simple good-versus-evil opposition, reading the Force through Spinoza: ideas become more or less true as they cohere with other ideas (so 'Luke loves Leia', 'Han is a mercenary', and 'Vader is evil' all need qualification), and everything seeks power by the conatus that Yoda and Obi-Wan attribute to the Force. The light side seeks power in balance with other things while the dark side, per the Sith Rule of Two, plays a zero-sum game. Luke's arc mirrors Oedipus: denying his inherited psychological likeness to Vader only enacts it, and only by acknowledging and owning the anger he inherited from his father can he gain power over it and enable Vader's redemption and his own.

spinoza-monism.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
spinoza-monism.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
spinoza-monism.relation: Chaib takes Ruby's line that Hell is 'forgetting what you are' and reads God's character through early modern philosophy: Descartes' supremely real being and deceiving demon frame Castiel's delusion of godhood and Ruby's manipulation of Sam, Spinoza's denial that evil exists (it is 'inadequate knowledge') explains the comprehensible motives of Crowley and Lucifer, Berkeley's claim that things persist only because God perceives them makes a dead God an existential threat, and Kant's 'moral theism' rebuts dogmatic atheism. With Hegel and Fromm, Hell becomes self-forgetting and communion with God becomes self-knowledge achieved through knowing others, the opposite of Ruby's Hell. The chapter concludes via Locke that closing Hell's gates would deny once-human demons the redemption tied to our very idea of God, so the brothers' forgiving love, unlike Michael and Lucifer's rigidity, reflects God's nature.

spinoza-monism.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
spinoza-monism.title: 18_LaRocca_Chapter_017.html
spinoza-monism.relation: Selmin Kara reads Victor Erice's Dream of Light (The Quince Tree Sun), about the painter Antonio Lopez trying to capture a quince tree in shifting autumn light, as a case for a 'new materialist' ontology of documentary against Bill Nichols-style representationalism. Drawing on Deleuze via De Landa's actual/virtual continuum, Spinoza's and Bergson's vital-matter lineage, and Bennett's 'vibrant matter,' she argues the film's dream sequence of the operator-less camera, dimmer and rotting fruit foregrounds the mediation rather than the mastery of light. She proposes updating Grierson's 'creative treatment of actuality' to 'the creative treatment of actuality and virtuality,' treating filmic and profilmic matter as intra-acting agents.

spinoza-monism.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
spinoza-monism.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
spinoza-monism.relation: Steven Horrobin sorts sailors into three kinds — the cultural-iconography poser, the racer chasing a land-based prize, and the 'sailor of the third kind' for whom the open-ended voyage is an end in itself — and argues the third lives 'in the shadow of Heraclitus.' Against the substantialist ontology of Parmenides and Democritus (persons and boats as fixed things), he defends a process view in which everything, like a wave, is a passing fluctuation of one universal substance; citing Spinoza, self-becoming is the super-process reflecting itself. He dissolves the Ship of Theseus paradox (and Parfit's parallel-ship version) by making identity the continuity of a process's function rather than fixed parts, arguing the violent, corroding life of a boat reveals the flux beneath apparently stable things.

spinoza-monism.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
spinoza-monism.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
spinoza-monism.relation: Editor Liz Stillwaggon Swan uses her rejection of Descartes' mind–body dualism to reinterpret yoga's promise of 'union.' Drawing on Spinoza's view that mind and matter are two aspects of a single reality, she argues 'mind' is just a placeholder for embodied abilities, so a yogi who denies a separate spirit cannot literally 'unite' mind and body — they are already one. She reframes yogic union (via Megan Burke's essay) as uniting self with nature, and defends practicing yoga for physical and psychological benefit without any spiritual claim, likening secularized yoga to secular Christmas.

freud-unconscious.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
freud-unconscious.title: Fast Zombies
freud-unconscious.relation: K. Silem Mohammad explains the horror of zombie slowness through Freud's uncanny - the return of the repressed, from White Zombie's hypnotized slaves (a figure for alienated industrial labor) to Romero's shuffling radioactive ghouls - then rebuilds undeath on Spinoza's Ethics: death as a body's parts acquiring a different proportion of motion and rest, the mind as a 'spiritual automaton,' and (via Deleuze's ethology of composition, decomposition, and bad encounters) zombies as bodies that decompose living bodies and recompose them as zombie bodies, replacing moral good and evil with good and bad. The fast zombies of 28 Days Later and the Dawn remake abandon hunger and the uncanny for pure rage and 'the Real,' signaling a late-capitalist permanent crisis in which the living have had their chance and blown it.

freud-unconscious.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
freud-unconscious.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
freud-unconscious.relation: Noel Carroll traces Halloween's Undead imagery to the Celtic Samhain and its Catholic absorption into All Hallows' Eve, then asks the paradox: why do we take pleasure in images of the death that, as Heidegger says, is the deep source of Angst we spend our lives denying? He examines Ernest Jones's Freudian analysis - the vampire as wish-fulfillment disguising an incestuous desire, horror as the price the super-ego exacts - and rejects it as theoretically expensive, invoking the demand for simpler, more economical explanation. His own hypothesis is the 'meta-fear of fear': adolescent viewers (and aging ones) use horror films and the holiday's zombie costumes to test and master fear itself, with parody and Bergson's laughter as companion devices of emotional control - a folk remedy that needs no unconscious to work.

freud-unconscious.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
freud-unconscious.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Cynthia Coe argues the novel's horror lies in the creature's liminality: he is neither human nor inhuman, and Victor's instant labeling of him as 'monster,' 'demon,' and 'fiend' shields Victor from his own responsibility, since the word 'monster' descends from a sign or omen we mistake for the evil itself. Freud's uncanny - the heimlich turning unheimlich, the repressed coming to light - explains why a being 'more horrid from its very resemblance' to us terrifies more than an obvious alien, a mechanism the chapter parallels with European anti-Semitism as hatred of an internal enemy. Shelley's moral point is that failures of empathy are moral failures: Victor holds the creature responsible as a free-willed demon while denying him personhood, and the tragedy grows from that contradictory projection until the neat categories of victim, monster, and evil collapse.

freud-unconscious.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
freud-unconscious.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Paweł Dobrosielski and Marcin Napiórkowski read Flowers for Hitler as Cohen's answer to Adorno's dictum that to write poetry after Auschwitz is barbaric - Cohen writes poetry that self-consciously knows it comes after the end of poetry. Using Freud's distinction between the vocabulary and grammar of dreams, they show the collection is assembled from a small repertoire of recurring images (ovens, ashes, telephones, radios, green grass, Nazi names) whose awkward normality expresses repression: life goes on as if nothing had happened. Arendt's banality of evil, born of the Eichmann trial, is directly alluded to in 'All There Is to Know about Adolf Eichmann,' and the book ends by universalizing Holocaust memory - the poet waking with a number on his forearm, feeling like victim and perpetrator alike - until the grass itself is grown on ashes and every flower is a flower for Hitler.

freud-unconscious.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
freud-unconscious.title: Girls and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Fisher explains the show's cycle - the girls want someone only while that person rejects them - through psychoanalytic theories of desire. Freud supplies the id/ego/superego machinery (cocaine-era Hannah dancing to 'I Don't Care (I Love It)' as pure id; Dunham's body-critical audience as the superego), while Lacan's desire - the 'untold' that must be named (Hannah's bedroom kink questions to Eric), drive, and jouissance beyond the pleasure principle - shows desire circling its object and never being satisfied, as when Hannah's e-book deal collapses into her worst OCD episode. Žižek's objet a as the object-cause of desire reads Marnie loving Charlie only once he is over her: desire reproduces itself rather than reaching its goal.

freud-unconscious.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
freud-unconscious.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Framing the 'Frost & Fire' episode as an imagined storyboard meeting, the chapter asks whether Finn's erotic dream of Flame Princess is a Freudian wish-fulfillment rising from his subconscious after he deliberately lies to provoke the Ice King-Flame Princess fight so the dream will return. Via Foucault's Care of the Self, it introduces Artemidorus's method of reading dreams for the real and moral consequences they portend, suggesting Finn's dream already warns him that his deception will cost him the relationship, with the Cosmic Owl whispering that he 'screwed up'. The writers conclude that sleeping and waking lives bleed into each other, and that Finn's refusal to read the warning leaves him burned: broken hearts, a torched Ice Kingdom, and the princess gone.

freud-unconscious.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
freud-unconscious.title: Dracula and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Pötzsch reads Dracula through Freud's Civilization and Its Discontents: the Count fascinates because he lives out the aggression and sexual freedom civilization forces us to renounce, embodying the innate hostility in Freud's 'man is the wolf to man.' Freud's account - group power replacing individual might, 'love thy neighbor' as an impossible demand, the super-ego as an inner Van Helsing breeding guilt over forbidden impulses, with the id and ego mediating - is mapped onto Jonathan's 'wicked, burning desire' for the vampire women. The upshot: we resent culture because we traded happiness for security, yet living like Dracula would get our throats cut.

freud-unconscious.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
freud-unconscious.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Daniel Leonard takes CharDee MacDennis, the Gang's three-level drinking game, as an unconscious confession read through Freud's structural model. The 'Mind' level - grudge trivia like 'Denis is asshole. Why Charlie hate?' and drawing-guessing 'based solely on feel' - runs on the id and the pleasure principle; the 'Body' level of darts, kennels, and the no-cursing rule is restraint, properly the ego's job of deferring gratification (which only Dennis's manipulative D.E.N.N.I.S. System grotesquely exercises); and the 'Spirit' level of Emotional Battery and Public Humiliation externalizes the superego's guilt and ego-ideal, with Frank as the all-seeing punishing father. The Gang's psychology is backwards - their 'Mind' level tests exactly what is not conscious - and their over-strong superegos surface in rationalization and the Black Card's coin flip, while smashing the losers' idealized game pieces enacts a wishful symbolic patricide.

freud-unconscious.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
freud-unconscious.title: 4. How Possible Is the Impossible Girl
freud-unconscious.relation: Smith asks how one Clara can exist as Oswin the converted Dalek, a Victorian governess, and a present-day nanny, and answers with philosophy of mind: after the real Clara steps into the Doctor's timeline on Trenzalore, the 'echoes' are best understood as manifestations within the Doctor's own subconscious, read through Freud's dream interpretation and id-ego-superego (the echoes act as his conscience) and Jung's archetypes, collective unconscious, individuation, and synchronicity—her name meaning clarity, her red wardrobe marking the copies, and the leaf of 'The Rings of Akhaten' as the meaningful coincidence that produced her. Aristotle's Categories frames what Oswin still shares with humanity after Dalek conversion, and the soufflé-is-the-recipe line together with social-cognition research on multiple selves supports the conclusion that the Claras are metaphysically the same person despite different bodies and roles—making the 'Impossible Girl' possible.

freud-unconscious.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
freud-unconscious.title: 21. Forgetting Is the Human Superpower
freud-unconscious.relation: Seymour reads the War-through-Eleventh Doctors through Freud's notion of Afterwardness (Nachtraeglichkeit) from Studies on Hysteria - memory is continually reforged as new information recontextualizes the past - so that learning Gallifrey was saved in 'The Day of the Doctor' changes not the Doctor but his memories of himself, turning penance into hope. She traces each Self constructed from Time War memory: Nine's guilt exploited by the Gelth and voiced in 'Boom Town' ('Only a killer would know that'), Ten's hubris once he forgets what he is capable of ('Time Lord Victorious' in 'The Waters of Mars'), and Eleven's danger when the memory fades and companions must remind him who he is ('A Town Called Mercy'). The chapter concludes the Doctor must keep the memory of his regret to keep being the Doctor - Clara's 'What you've always done. Be a doctor.'

freud-unconscious.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
freud-unconscious.title: 13. Topophilia; or, How We Got Hooked on Downton
freud-unconscious.relation: Elvis reads the show's opening credits shot by shot - Isis on the lawn, the opening shutter, the servant bell, the letter rack, the watched pot, the measured table setting, the falling rose petal, the lamplight, the feather duster - to explain our addiction to Downton through Bachelard's The Poetics of Space. Topophilia (love of place), daydream, and the unconscious mind's bank of unnoticed experience make the intimate small spaces of the credits invitations to feel at home in the Abbey, while Deleuze's 'haptic' explains how vision and sound trigger touch-like immersion. The show's improbable global appeal, she concludes, lies not in pompous grandeur but in small intimate moments that bring viewers home.

freud-unconscious.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
freud-unconscious.title: 18. Doctor, Heal Thyself
freud-unconscious.relation: McClelland argues Lecter is a flawed healer: reading Starling's FBI disgrace as social exclusion, he shows how Lecter's hypnotic drugs and deep-hypnosis 'treatment' let her revisit and metabolize her repressed rage at her dead father — the parental imago he named back in Silence of the Lambs — producing a chrysalis-like metamorphosis completed when she defies Krendler at the dinner and asks for more of his brains. The healing is symmetric, since Starling's insight into Lecter's own Mischa fixation releases him too, and the chapter closes with an Aristotelian verdict — choice reveals character, and whether the couple's Buenos Aires partnership counts as good depends on long-term flourishing we have not yet seen.

freud-unconscious.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
freud-unconscious.title: 16. The Truth about the Walkers
freud-unconscious.relation: Kempner reads the show's serial bait-and-switch over the walkers' origin - Jenner's failed CDC, Eugene's exposed lie on the road to Washington - as an enactment of Deleuze and Guattari's multiplicity against "the reduction to the ONE." Their anti-Oedipal attack on Freud, who fixed the Wolfman's dream to a single castrating father, mirrors how characters who hunt one knowable cause (Rick's hope of CDC rescue, Hershel's barn of curable walkers, Abraham's mission) are punished with death, while Michonne survives precisely by accepting walkers as an irreducible pack rather than something to be understood. The chapter concludes the series should never explain the walkers: multiple causes and small-t truths replace any single Truth, which is why relief never arrives and survival means living with unknowability.

freud-unconscious.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
freud-unconscious.title: 23. Louis C.K. Meets the Unconscious
freud-unconscious.relation: Reads the 'of course, but maybe' bit as a wrestling match between Lacan's big Other—society's unwritten rule book of queues, taboos, and approval—and the Freudian unconscious that betrays itself in the therapist's 'the climax results in the death of the woman' slip and other parapraxes. Jokes then work as sublimation and a release valve: Louis's nut-allergy and slavery bits ('you all clapped for dead kids... you don't get to cherry-pick') let audiences laugh at their disavowed 'I know very well, but...' contradictions, though comedy remains confession without absolution.

freud-unconscious.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
freud-unconscious.title: 15. Joffrey on the Couch
freud-unconscious.relation: Wills asks why audiences so relish hating Joffrey and answers with Freud's Totem and Taboo: the incest taboo was instituted precisely because the desire persists in the unconscious, and Joffrey - the product of 'accumulative incest' with cousin-grandparents and sibling parents - embodies the broken taboo. Reading the furious fan reactions (his death 'wasn't horrible enough,' the meticulous lists of his worst acts) as projection and successful repression, the chapter argues that vilifying Joffrey channels our own repressed taboo-breaking urges, while Westeros's distanced past setting lets us dissociate from the savagery exactly as Freud's staging of primitive peoples did.

freud-unconscious.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
freud-unconscious.title: 26. Why We Love to Watch Deadpool . . . Play with Himself
freud-unconscious.relation: Using the Deadpool video game, the chapter argues Wade is a god who is all-powerful (rewriting the game world with his crayon-scrawled script and manufacturing fake credits), all-knowing (reading the player's mind through the fourth wall and literally entering Rogue's), and plainly not all-good (slapping an unconscious Wolverine, ogling dead Vertigo, ignoring Apocalypse three times for a billion dollars), so that dystheism - belief in a god with serious issues - dissolves the problem of evil. The free-will defense collapses because Deadpool wrote the script the villains obey, giving players only the illusion of choice. The voices in Wade's head are explicitly cast as Freud's structural model, with his Ego and SuperEgo talking while WadePrime, the Id, does most of the voice-work.

freud-unconscious.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
freud-unconscious.title: 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger
freud-unconscious.relation: Ericson uses the used-car litmus test to examine trust in the MCU: through McLeod's three criteria and Peperzak's contrast of the objectifying and interactive approaches, Tony's control-seeking distance (the lone-gun-slinger act of Iron Man 2) fails trust while Steve's soldier-style trust anchors the Winter Soldier thriller against Fury's 'This isn't freedom, this is fear' and HYDRA's coercion-eliminating project. Plato's rule that power should go only to those who do not want it explains why Cap can be entrusted with superpowers, Nietzsche's megalomaniac late letters frame Tony's drive to 'cleave history in two' by building Ultron and then the messianic Vision, and Banner's Hulk illustrates the Freudian road from repression to sublimation as the condition of self-trust. It ends with Cap's concealment of Bucky's killing of Tony's parents as the betrayal of trust that only a decision to forgive might repair.

freud-unconscious.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
freud-unconscious.title: 9. 24 7 Newsleep
freud-unconscious.relation: Buchanan argues the Party 'sleep-hacks' its citizens because sleep is an active state of thought, a lineage he traces from Aristotle's theory of dreaming through Freud's Interpretation of Dreams, and is therefore a site of potential resistance that must be colonized. Between the Physical Jerks, telescreen trumpet-calls, a Thought Police able to inspect anyone 'asleep or awake' without warning, and O'Brien's manipulation of Winston's sleep schedule during torture, Winston is trapped in 'Newsleep', a derealized blur of dream and reality that makes doublethink the only available way of thinking. He extends the diagnosis to our own 24/7 economy of phones and Trump's all-hours tweets, concluding that Orwell's warning is that we must guard our sleep.

freud-unconscious.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
freud-unconscious.title: 7. Amy Schumer or the Incongruities
freud-unconscious.relation: Pits Freud's psychoanalytic theory of wit, where harmless nonsense smuggles tendentious sexual content past the superego's censor, against the incongruity theory of comic amusement, using 'Boner Doctor' as the test case. Carroll argues the psychoanalytic account makes the superego absurdly gullible, citing Foucault on how thoroughly sexuality is now discussed, and cannot capture what is specific to Schumer. Incongruity theory can: sketches like 'Sexting' and Trainwreck's doll analogy for infidelity generate laughter from violated norms of ladylike decorum, exposing her feminism as a sustained subversion of the modest, uninterested stereotype of womanhood.

freud-unconscious.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
freud-unconscious.title: 2. Where Is the Twilight Zone
freud-unconscious.relation: Scalambrino argues the Twilight Zone is a televised expression of Breton's surrealism, starting from Descartes: the cogito and the mind–body problem made reason the measure of the 'clear and distinct,' and surrealism seeks to unbind the imagination from exactly that rational leash. He reads 'A World of His Own' as surrealist automatic writing, 'The Mirror' as Dalí's paranoiac-critical method, and Freud's psychoanalysis as both allied with and (following Adorno's diagnosis of the movement's death) too restrictive for surrealism's project. Episodes like 'Shadow Play' (a man who dreams the world), 'The Shelter,' 'The Lonely,' and 'A Stop at Willoughby' provoke the uncanny — the strangely familiar — in viewers, which is where the Zone is located.

freud-unconscious.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
freud-unconscious.title: 2. Echoes of Past and Present
freud-unconscious.relation: Crippen and Dixon treat the album Echo, written during Petty's divorce, heroin use and severe depression, as organized by crisis and reversion: its lyrics and productions compulsively echo earlier eras of his life, from 1950s TV westerns and his abusive father in "About to Give Out" to the Jeff Lynne years and Wildflowers in "Accused of Love" and "Echo." They invoke Freud and Lacan's psychoanalytic account of trauma repetition, where the past is relived in hope of a different outcome and sublimated into art. The album's sparse, energy-conserving repetition is then read through Nietzsche's will-to-power cycle, in which merely holding on is symptomatic of illness, yet the closing "One More Day, One More Night" and the album's very creation exemplify Nietzschean health as strength to expand against obstacles, since we possess art lest we perish of the truth.

freud-unconscious.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
freud-unconscious.title: 2. Mesmeric Mister Rogers
freud-unconscious.relation: Marlene Clark argues Fred Rogers was a mesmerist in the lineage of Franz Mesmer's animal magnetism, a hypnotic appeal that survived mesmerism's debunking by passing into Freud and Breuer's psychoanalytic transference and into the primitive, unconscious sex appeal of screen idols like Brad Pitt. She details episode 1588, where Rogers defuses bathtub-drain fears with 'You Can Never Go Down the Drain' and scuba-suited Neighbor Aber frightens Henrietta Pussycat, and the 1969 Senate hearing where reciting 'What Do You Do with the Mad That You Feel?' visibly entranced Senator Pastore into awarding PBS 20 million dollars.

freud-unconscious.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
freud-unconscious.title: 15. Life Is a Laugh and Death Is a Joke
freud-unconscious.relation: Jarno Hietalahti applies the three classic theories of humor to Endgame: incongruity theory explains trickster Loki, 'an epitome or embodiment of humor' who cheats death and escapes with the Tesseract; Hobbes's superiority theory from Leviathan, laughter as 'sudden glory' at others' weakness (extended by Gruner's game of humor with winners and losers), explains Thanos's self-satisfied smirks as he shrugs off the heroes' combined assault and snaps half of life away; and Freud's relief theory, in which jokes express the unconscious and release inner tension, explains fat Thor's terror-ridden laughter as escape from his failure, grief, and lost control. The chapter concludes that humor is neither good nor bad in itself but part of a worldview, and that death as the horizon giving life meaning is precisely what makes laughter possible for beings like us and like the superheroes.

freud-unconscious.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
freud-unconscious.title: 11. When Is a Lawyer Not a Lawyer
freud-unconscious.relation: Karavitis argues Mason is secretly two other professionals: a historian and a psychoanalyst. Following Plato's Theaetetus definition of knowledge as justified true belief and the correspondence and coherence theories of truth, he shows Mason iteratively reconstructing the recent past from facts to theory to revised theory, refusing Hamilton Burger's circumstantial first stories and hunting the motive that is history's 'why' (H. Stuart Hughes's psychohistorical method), exactly what historians do; then, via Freud's defense mechanisms, he reads the recurring courtroom confession as an 'abreaction' in which the murderer, confronted with lie and truth at once, breaks down on the stand, and Mason's own total absorption in murder cases (no private life in 271 episodes) as sublimation of something repressed.

freud-unconscious.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
freud-unconscious.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Runs the Bluths through Freudian psychoanalysis: George Sr. hiding in the attic ('Sad Sack', 'Good Grief!') illustrates the unconscious, preconscious, and repression; Michael acts as ego mediating the family's id demands (the unfrozen stock spree) against George Michael's super-ego; Tobias dressing as a pirate among homosexuals and Michael's 'brother...bother' and 'Egg' slips are parapraxes betraying repressed desire; Buster's Motherboy dates and 'Why I Want to Marry My Mother' enact a failed Oedipus complex; and the brothers' scheme against George Sr. in 'Making a Stand' reenacts the primal horde of Totem and Taboo, origin of the incest taboo that haunts George Michael and Maeby.

freud-unconscious.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
freud-unconscious.title: The Avatar Unparalleled Opportunities
freud-unconscious.relation: Cuddy argues the gamer's bond with the avatar is an extension of the ego: Freud's id/ego/superego model explains why playing a Cylon Raider or flying the 'Bastille Day' mission lets gamers reconcile unconscious desires with the superego's demands in ways reality forbids. But when we lose we disconnect from the avatar and blame the game or 'cheating' opponents, which Sartre diagnoses as bad faith, a denial of freedom, contrasted with Adama's 'a man takes responsibility for his actions' in '33' and Baltar's vacillation over the vice-presidency. Through facticity (the unforgiving no-save 2003 game) and existence preceding essence, the chapter concludes that videogames offer unparalleled opportunities to practice Sartrean responsibility and achieve Freudian reconciliation through the right avatar.

freud-unconscious.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
freud-unconscious.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Hunt treats the film as a direct view of a single subject's unconscious, Freud-style: the Dude is the pre-Oedipal narcissist, the Big Lebowski the father toppled from his wheelchair-throne after the confrontation, Maude the mother, with a scattered superego distributed across the Stranger's moralizing and the Malibu sheriff's 'Stay out of Malibu!'.
