Donny and Walter figure oral and anal fixations, Jesus the threatening playground peer, and Bunny and the nihilists Freud's life and death drives — so Donny's death in the parking-lot melee lets the ego fuse death-drive energy into life, and the Dude's walk-away from the little Lebowski back to bowling and White Russians reads as repression into comfortable pre-Oedipal phantasy.

freud-unconscious.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
freud-unconscious.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Griffioen distinguishes two kinds of truthiness: believing what one prefers to be true (motivated epistemic irrationality) and justifying beliefs by gut feeling, using Colbert's premiere clips about Bush knowing Harriet Miers's heart and feeling that taking out Saddam was right. She models the first as wishful thinking and self-deception via a Samantha Bee/Jason Jones marital-fidelity example, works through the static and dynamic paradoxes of self-deception, rejects the Freudian divided-mind solution (imagined as Colbert debating himself in 'Formidable Opponent'), and defends an attention-directing account instead. Gut feelings justify only when they implicitly track facts, yielding her proposed fallacy argumentum Colberti ad ventrem.

freud-unconscious.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
freud-unconscious.title: The Ego is a Housewife Named Lois
freud-unconscious.relation: Maps Freud's structural model of the mind onto the Griffin household: Stewie is the id (the broccoli-destroying weather machine in 'I Never Met the Dead Man,' the mind-control device foiled by Bill Cosby in 'Brian Does Hollywood'), Brian is the super-ego (talking kleptomaniac Lois into surrendering in 'Breaking Out Is Hard to Do'), and Lois is the ego that reality-tests and restrains both, with the id-ego miscommunication mirrored in Lois never understanding Stewie's speech. The Oedipus complex does the interpretive heavy lifting: Stewie's 'damn you, vile woman' obsession is misdirected maternal longing, Brian's 'Brian in Love' confession of love for his figurative mother resolves the complex and founds his moral boundaries, and Peter's Church of the Holy Fonz reads as failed father-identification, religion as substitute for the father.

freud-unconscious.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
freud-unconscious.title: Legal and Not So Legal Forms of Inception
freud-unconscious.relation: Brogaard argues the film's inception method is more science than fiction, starting from the neuroscience of dreaming: against Hobson's activation-synthesis model (and Dennett's related wake-up narrative theory, both heirs to Freud's symbol-based dream interpretation), she cites evidence that dreams arise from dopamine-driven cortical motivation areas rather than the brain stem, so streamlined, plot-driven shared dreams cannot be ruled out. Savants like Tammet and Padgett show the brain can compute super-fast below awareness, which makes sense of the film's dream-time compression. She then speculates real mechanisms for the heist — LaBerge's lucid-dream masks, transcranial magnetic stimulation plus an artificial corpus callosum to tap a subject's right hemisphere — and treats Cobb's planting of 'my father doesn't want me to be him' in Fischer as achievable today by cruder means like mind control and fear conditioning.

freud-unconscious.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
freud-unconscious.title: Do We Give Shakespeare the Last Word
freud-unconscious.relation: Kapper treats Inception as a hip epistemological puzzle — unlike The Matrix, the question is not what is real but how we could know — and follows Ariadne's thread (her mythological clue-giving names the chapter) through the tradition: Plato's Theaetetus and Descartes's supremely cunning deceiver pose 'Am I dreaming now?', Wittgenstein shows the doubt is senseless since 'if I am dreaming, this remark is being dreamed as well', Freud makes dreams the royal road to the unconscious, and Heraclitus says only the waking share a common cosmos. The payoff is Eastern: Zhuangzi's butterfly, Indra's net of mutually reflected jewels, and Schopenhauer's single-dreamer universe turn waking up into an endless regress, so the Buddhist ideal of the awakened one — nirvana, where the ideas of real and dream cease to pertain — becomes the reading of Cobb turning away from the top.

freud-unconscious.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
freud-unconscious.title: Day Residue
freud-unconscious.relation: Auxier reverse-engineers how Nolan's dream-sharing could work — sedatives aligning brainwaves like a laser, the electrical dream machine, nested electromagnetic fields — and argues each deeper level buys time at the cost of lucidity, with Limbo as 'psychosis of forgetting.' He explains the film through Susanne Langer's theory of mythic consciousness: dreams become communicable only when forced into narrative order, so dream architecture is the insertion of images that survive transformation into the subject's dispositions — hence Eames plants the pinwheel in the safe so Fischer believes he placed it himself, and the Mombasa elders represent a collective, pre-modern consciousness modern individuals have lost. The resolution of the baggage-claim puzzle (Fischer's calm) is that the inception removed a doubt rather than planting one: doubt spreads easily in modern minds, and Fischer touched the ancestral place where 'our fathers desire our happiness.'

freud-unconscious.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
freud-unconscious.title: Epilog
freud-unconscious.relation: Nicolas Floury reads the entire film as the single dream of a neurotic subject — Cobb asleep on the plane, every character assembled from fellow passengers and airport figures — in which he works through the Lacanian conflict where the neurotic 'does not desire what he wants and does not want what he actually desires': Cobb wants to keep living with Mal ('In my dreams we are still together') while wishing to complete her mourning. The dream levels are reinterpreted as stages of Freudian dream-work: level 1 ruled by desire, level 2 where the counter-desire and Ariadne-as-double intervene, the snow fortress war as the internal battle climaxing when Cobb shoots Mal, and the limbos as melancholic self-enclosure — 'a life without desire, a life under the seal of death.' Cobb's final choice of a 'steady desire' completes the mourning: Piaf's 'Non, je ne regrette rien' marks his renunciation and serves as the wake-up signal, father-figure Miles embodies the life instinct telling him to 'come back to reality,' and the still-spinning top is Mal's expelled beloved object, set where it can no longer block his return to life.

freud-unconscious.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
freud-unconscious.title: Dreams and Nightmares
freud-unconscious.relation: Valentin Husson reads Inception through Heidegger's account of poetic dwelling: to dwell is to build, and because the dream 'creates and perceives the world simultaneously,' every dreamer is a poet whose dwelling springs from an ungrounded origin — Freud's unconscious producing dreams as 'the (concealed) fulfillment of a (repressed) desire,' Lacan's unconscious 'marked by a blank,' and the Mystery from which, per Heidegger's essays on art and dwelling and Mallarmé's poetics, all creation comes. The dream's twofold building — Ariadne's durable architecture plus the subject's ceaseless populating of it — explains why extractors stay safe only while the dreamer unknowingly keeps creating, and why Cobb forbids building dreams from memory rather than 'out of nothing.' Cobb's guilt turns his dreams into nightmares, 'the reign of the uninhabitable,' until Ariadne, like her mythic thread leading Theseus from the labyrinth, guides him out of Limbo so dwelling becomes possible again — the film as a modern Odyssey in which 'man dwells poetically,' with the viewer suspended over the top already taken in by the Mystery.

freud-unconscious.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
freud-unconscious.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Sets up Sons of Anarchy as a Hamlet retelling — Jax the prince, Clay the Claudius who murdered John Teller and married Gemma, Tara a gutsier Ophelia — and reads it through Freud and Ernest Jones's Hamlet and Oedipus: Jax's protest that he 'untwisted my mommy thing a long time ago,' his toleration of Gemma's meddling, and the Season 4/5 finale tableaux where Gemma displaces Tara at his side betray an unresolved Oedipus complex. Freud's three agencies get bodies: Clay as pure Id (beating Gemma in 'Hands'), Tara as Superego, Jax as the mediating Ego, with SAMCRO itself a collective Id worshipped in its 'chapel.' Oral and anal-stage fixations explain the Sons' chain-smoking, recklessness, and defiance of authority, while the Id's civil war between libido and the death drive plays out in Gemma's post-beating sex binge and Jax's unconscious pleasure in killing.

freud-unconscious.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
freud-unconscious.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
freud-unconscious.relation: Young argues that South Park is perceived as dangerous for exactly the reasons Socrates was tried and executed in Plato's Apology: both 'corrupt the youth' by mocking religion, questioning authority, and exposing that the supposed teachers (Mr. Garrison's flip-flopping creationism, Mrs. Broflovski's moral panics, the 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip) do not know what they think they know. He diagnoses Cartman as an Eichmann figure whose banal, thoughtless evil—feeding Scott Tenorman his parents, torturing Muslims with farts—consists in the inability to think from another's standpoint, while Kyle and Stan's friendship embodies Arendt's dialogic thinking and Aristotle's mean between ideological extremes, as when they see both the merit and the smugness of hybrid drivers in 'Smug Alert'. Freud's theory that jokes break through repression explains why the show's vulgarity is essential rather than gratuitous: it verbalizes what culture silences so that it can be thought through, making South Park a Socratic gadfly rather than a corrupter.

freud-unconscious.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
freud-unconscious.title: “An Energy Field Created by All Living Things”
freud-unconscious.relation: Baur argues that the Jedi metaphysics is non-dualistic rather than a simple good-versus-evil opposition, reading the Force through Spinoza: ideas become more or less true as they cohere with other ideas (so 'Luke loves Leia', 'Han is a mercenary', and 'Vader is evil' all need qualification), and everything seeks power by the conatus that Yoda and Obi-Wan attribute to the Force. The light side seeks power in balance with other things while the dark side, per the Sith Rule of Two, plays a zero-sum game. Luke's arc mirrors Oedipus: denying his inherited psychological likeness to Vader only enacts it, and only by acknowledging and owning the anger he inherited from his father can he gain power over it and enable Vader's redemption and his own.

freud-unconscious.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
freud-unconscious.title: NOTES
freud-unconscious.relation: Hirschbein presents True Blood as a Freudian fable: vampires live the unrepressed id's Eros and Thanatos that civilization forces the rest of us to renounce, which is why they defeat all three sources of suffering (mortal bodies, nature, hostile neighbors) and why the show's convulsive sex and violence thrill us. Glamouring reproduces the posthypnotic suggestion that proved the unconscious to Freud, Sookie's mind-reading confirms his dark discoveries about our sexualized aggression, vampire myths work as projection screens for desires we disown, and Marcuse's complaint about 'genital tyranny' and sublimation frames Sookie's love as a near-realization of Freud's St. Francis ideal.

freud-unconscious.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
freud-unconscious.title: Notes
freud-unconscious.relation: Reads the Cohle–Hart pairing through Lacan: Cohle is at peace with the constitutive lack introduced after the mirror stage, and his hysteric's fixation on the Other's desire is what makes him the superior interrogator, while Hart exhibits obsessional neurosis and 'interpassivity,' letting the preacher's congregation do his believing for him. Following Deleuze's Oedipal structure of detective fiction and Hegel's point that heroes are denied guilt, the chapter compares Rust to Oedipus — both men who, after a child's death, renounce the father function through anti-natalism — while arguing Cohle surpasses Oedipus by philosophically mastering the knowledge that Oedipus lacked. Rust's tying off of his 'circle of violence' is read as the Lacanian sinthome: putting his symptom to work in the service of the case rather than being destroyed by it.

freud-unconscious.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
freud-unconscious.title: 2. Where Is the Twilight Zone
freud-unconscious.relation: Scalambrino reads the Zone as a televised expression of surrealist philosophy: Breton's sought 'point of the mind' where life and death, real and imagined cease to be contradictions, realized in episodes like 'A World of His Own' (automatic writing) and 'The Mirror' (Dali's paranoiac-critical method). Descartes's cogito and the mind-body dualism supply the rational 'leash' that surrealism unbinds, questioned by 'Shadow Play,' where a man insists the world is his dream. Following Adorno's verdict that psychoanalytic interpretation killed official surrealism, he argues the show endures by provoking the uncanny ('The Shelter,' 'The Lonely,' 'A Stop at Willoughby') without being pinned to Freudian readings.

freud-unconscious.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
freud-unconscious.title: XVII - HIGH-TECH MYTHOLOGY IN X-MEN
freud-unconscious.relation: Teschner reads X-Men as high-tech mythology: the superhero images are Freud's dream work, disguising unconscious wishes about technological power that the conscious ego cannot face, with Wolverine's adamantium and constant pain symbolizing human alienation under the machine. The psionic mind, telepathy and telekinesis that move matter directly, breaks the Cartesian dualism of mind and body, marking the upper limit of technological control. On the latent level, Xavier's psionic blocks and School represent repression of the unconscious while Magneto's plastic prison, mutant machine, and Liberty Island plan represent acceptance of a humanity redefined by its union with the machine.

freud-unconscious.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
freud-unconscious.title: Excuses, Excuses Inside the Mind of a Complainer
freud-unconscious.relation: Kevin Kinghorn, drawing on interviews with coach Brad Gilbert, dissects why tennis players and their parents complain and make excuses. He catalogs cognitive biases and the vividness effect (why a bad call, like McEnroe's 'You cannot be serious!' outburst, sticks and feels like persecution) as forms of irrationality, and notes Stoicism (which he attributes to Zeno) as a philosophy that would suppress the complaining temperament. His central mechanism is Freudian self-deception: citing Freud's hypnotized-umbrella subject who invents a reason for his own behavior, he argues tennis parents pretend their child is destined for greatness and then genuinely come to believe the lie, so excuse-making becomes a self-destructive sign a player will never be a champion. He also reads Andrea Jaeger's ambivalence about winning as evidence of mixed, partly unconscious motivations.

freud-unconscious.book: 217 - The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
freud-unconscious.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
freud-unconscious.relation: Gilmore reads Unforgiven as Socratic wisdom done in images — the recognition that we do not know what we really want. He analyzes the opening montage (shadowed windows, the cut prostitute) as Freud's Primal Scene, the audience forced to interpret sex and violence without adequate concepts, which he calls the primal scene of philosophy itself. Drawing on Huizinga's Homo Ludens and Leone's Once Upon a Time in the West, he frames the gunslinger as a 'Bad Man at play' for mortal stakes, free of the repressions civilization demands. William Munny's banal Christianized 'goodness' versus the terrifying Bad Man that drink releases dramatizes Thoreau's 'quiet desperation' and a godless world where deserving is irrelevant.

freud-unconscious.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
freud-unconscious.title: Re(ct)ifying Empty Speech Cronenberg and the Problem of the First Person
freud-unconscious.relation: Brook W. R. Pearson examines the problem of the first person 'I' in Cronenberg through Lacan, Wittgenstein, and Deleuze/Guattari. He reads Spider's 'schizo-phonetic partition' and Tom/Joey's shifting use of 'I' in A History of Violence as Lacanian 'empty speech' and the narcissistic 'monument' of a censored unconscious chapter that resurfaces; Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Moore's paradox recast Joey's split as an illegitimate private language game, and Deleuze/Guattari's account of the other as a 'possible world' reframes the frightened face on the cinema screen.

freud-unconscious.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
freud-unconscious.title: The Horizon of Disenchantment Film Noir, Camus, and the Vicissitudes of Descent
freud-unconscious.relation: Alan Woolfolk reads noir through Weber's disenchanted world and Charles Taylor's cultural horizons, arguing the noir protagonist can neither resist the darkness like Conrad's Marlow nor fully embrace it like Coppola's Willard, remaining trapped between times in an ethically irrational universe. He contrasts Camus, who counters disenchantment with an ethic of honesty grounded in a Rousseauian benign nature (The Stranger's Meursault) and with the Baudelairean dandy as aesthetic model, against noir protagonists (Neff, Marlowe, the Swede, Scottie Ferguson) whose 'banked fires' fail and who lose self-possession. Drawing on Freud's id as 'a cauldron full of seething excitations,' he argues the femme fatale drags the protagonist downward into the timeless unconscious where anything is possible (Noah Cross's incest in Chinatown, the radioactive box in Kiss Me Deadly, Body Heat's Ned Racine), and reads noir as backward- and downward-looking through Palmer/Bakhtin's chronotope.

freud-unconscious.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
freud-unconscious.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
freud-unconscious.relation: Gilmore reads Chinatown as neo-noir that is itself a kind of philosophy, engaging the hermeneutics of suspicion (Nietzsche, Freud, Marx) and existentialist alienation. Curly eating the venetian blinds signals a desire to recover a less painful blindness; Jake Gittes's 'conceptual scotomas' (Dennett) and hubris make him miss counternarratives, paralleling Oedipus as detective. Using Freud on the uncanny and doppelgangers (Jake doubled with Hollis Mulwray and Noah Cross) and Aristotle's Poetics on catharsis and the sublime, Gilmore argues 'Chinatown' names the abyss where every narrative is undone, and that facing this dark sublimity is the way of wisdom.

freud-unconscious.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
freud-unconscious.title: War and Its Fictional Recovery On-Screen Narrative Management of Death in The Big Red One and The Thin Red Lin
freud-unconscious.relation: Bronfen takes Freud's 'Thoughts for the Times on War and Death' (life 'recovers its full content' when war forces us to believe in death) and his theory of the death drive and the uncanny double as a template for how war films manage mortality through fiction. In Fuller's The Big Red One, the nameless Sergeant's guilt-driven distinction between killing and murder, his Nazi double Schroeder, and the compulsively repeated stabbing scene at the crucifix let the hero convert contingent slaughter into a restitutive story where survival is 'the only glory,' echoing Freud's Eros–Thanatos struggle. In Malick's The Thin Red Line, Private Witt splits not into warlike and peacetime selves but into bodily and spiritual presence, embracing death as transcendence into 'shining light' that doubles the light of cinema itself. Both films strike a pact with the viewer, who dies with the heroes yet safely survives them.

freud-unconscious.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
freud-unconscious.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Griffioen dissects Colbert's 'truthiness' as two forms of motivated epistemic irrationality—preferring what one wishes true (wishful thinking) and intuiting truth from the gut over facts (self-deception). Using a running example of Samantha Bee believing in Jason Jones's fidelity against the evidence, she rejects Freud-style divided-mind accounts (with their static and dynamic paradoxes) in favor of self-deception as an attention-directing process, and skewers Colbert's circular 'truthinessiness' (proving truthiness with more truthiness). She argues gut feelings only justify belief when they implicitly track relevant facts, proposing a fallacy of 'argumentum ad ventrem.'

freud-unconscious.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
freud-unconscious.title: 2. Where Is the Twilight Zone
freud-unconscious.relation: Scalambrino argues the Twilight Zone is a televised expression of surrealist philosophy (Breton, Dalí) that provokes the Freudian 'uncanny.' He traces a line from Descartes—whose cogito and 'clear and distinct' rational mind produced the mind–body problem that lets surrealists destabilize waking reality—through psychoanalysis to Breton's 'point' where real and imagined cease to be contradictions. Episodes like 'A World of His Own' (automatic writing), 'The Mirror' (Dalí's paranoiac-critical method), 'Shadow Play,' 'The Shelter,' and 'The Lonely' unleash the imagination unbound by reason and provoke the uncanny in viewers.

freud-unconscious.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Zanin reads Pride and Prejudice and Zombies through Freud, Aristotle, and Levinas. She argues Regency propriety over-represses natural impulses, so Freud's id/ego/superego and the aggression drive explain why Elizabeth's zombie-slaying is sublimated aggression and cathartic release (Aristotle's catharsis), her ritual 'seven cuts of shame' a displacement of guilt over misjudging Darcy. She reads Charlotte's zombie decay as an allegory of self lost to a marriage of convenience. Using Levinas on the Other (the 'unmentionable' zombie against which Elizabeth's identity is formed) and Judith Butler's claim that the Other dwells within the self, she argues the zombie Other enables rather than overwhelms Elizabeth's identity.

freud-unconscious.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
freud-unconscious.title: The Fall of the House of Ulmer Europe vs. America in the Gothic Vision of The Black Cat
freud-unconscious.relation: Cantor reads Edgar Ulmer's The Black Cat (1934) as a European emigre's Gothic allegory of Europe vs. America, with Karloff's architect Poelzig and Lugosi's psychiatrist Werdegast as mirror-image 'living dead' fixated on the horrors of World War I. He connects Poelzig's modernist house-over-Fort-Marmaros to a Freudian map of ego and id and to the war-driven rise of psychoanalysis, and reads the naive, unconscious American honeymooners against the cultured but nihilistic Europeans. He explicitly links the film's high-culture/pop-culture opposition to Heidegger's vision of Europe squeezed between a leveling America and Russia and to the Frankfurt School critique of American mass entertainment.

freud-unconscious.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
freud-unconscious.title: From Domestic Nightmares to the Nightmare of History Uncanny Eruptions of Violence in King's and Kubrick's Ver
freud-unconscious.relation: Lutz argues that King's novel and Kubrick's film of The Shining both stage Freud's uncanny as the return of a repressed, corporeal past: the woman in Room 217 and Grady's ghosts, the father-mirroring of Jack, his abusive father, and Delbert Grady, and Danny's Tony double. He reads King as an 'inverted family romance' where the good replacement father is the Black cook Hallorann, then shows Kubrick widening domestic abuse into a Marxian nightmare of history: the Overlook built on an Indian burial ground, the Calumet cans, and Jack's craving to join the hotel's ghostly 'management' expose the racist, patriarchal, class violence founding American institutions. Jack's 'All work and no play' manuscript figures his entrapment in ideology and repetition.

freud-unconscious.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
freud-unconscious.title: “Hot with Rapture and Cold with Fear” Grotesque, Sublime, and Postmodern Transformations in Patrick Süskind's
freud-unconscious.relation: Cokal reads Suskind's Perfume and Tykwer's film through the intertwined categories of the grotesque and the sublime. The odorless murderer Grenouille is a Bakhtinian grotesque body who nonetheless has Kantian sublime experiences of the plum girl's and Laure's scents, and Cokal uses Kant's and Lyotard's accounts of the sublime (the soul 'immobilized, as good as dead') to explain the awe that Grenouille both feels and, via his 'angel's scent,' induces in the orgy at his execution. Grenouille's uncanny encounter with his own lack of smell in the cave is read through Freud's uncanny, and his final cannibalistic dismemberment collapses the sublime back into the grotesque.

freud-unconscious.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
freud-unconscious.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
freud-unconscious.relation: Alison Milbank reads the One Ring as a fetish in both Freud's sexual sense (an object severed from the whole, twice literally cut from a finger, warding off the castrating maternal power figured in Shelob) and Marx's economic sense (a commodity that estranges makers from things and reduces persons to hoarders like Smaug). Against fetishism she sets Tolkien's gift-economy, embodied by Bombadil tossing the Ring in the air and by Sam's elvish rope, and Heidegger's older sense of the 'thing' as a gathering, so the novel teaches us to receive the world back as gift rather than possession.

freud-death-drive.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
freud-death-drive.title: The Possibility of a Non-Repressive Civilization
freud-death-drive.relation: Simon Clark reads Romero's four Dead films through Freud's Civilization and Its Discontents: the zombie is the return of the repressed, the ripped-out instinctual life of a civilization that demands work, and it multiplies exactly as humans (Stephen defending the mall, Ben fighting Mr. Cooper) lapse into unlawful self-gratification. The bite unites Eros and Thanatos - an erotic, engorged cannibalism that also regresses victims to rotting matter, which Clark glosses with Creed's vagina dentata. He then argues Day of the Dead's beach ending (John fishing, Sarah at peace) stages Marcuse's non-repressive civilization where work becomes play and liberated sexuality rejoins Eros, while Land of the Dead goes further: the evolved, tool-using zombies led by Big Daddy are the martyrs who actually found Marcuse's impossible pleasurable community, leaving living humans still fenced inside repression.

freud-death-drive.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
freud-death-drive.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
freud-death-drive.relation: Christopher Ketcham narrates a night listening to Dear Heather during a café blackout, in which darkness becomes Eugene Minkowski's 'lived space' - more personal than light, with auditory space as its own dark space - and Cohen's voice leads him down into a shared funk of loss and depression. Through Heidegger he diagnoses his own shrunken, past-bound, thrown existence and reinterprets being-toward-death not as a downward spiral but as being toward his own remaining possibilities, and through Freud's death drive he names the 'unobtrusive death wish' he had let dwell unchallenged in him. The essay closes with a Heideggerian resolve toward resoluteness and future possibility, glimpsing a street-worn 'Suzanne' in the dark as hope rather than absence.

freud-death-drive.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
freud-death-drive.title: Dracula and Philosophy
freud-death-drive.relation: Pötzsch reads Dracula through Freud's Civilization and Its Discontents: the Count fascinates because he lives out the aggression and sexual freedom civilization forces us to renounce, embodying the innate hostility in Freud's 'man is the wolf to man.' Freud's account - group power replacing individual might, 'love thy neighbor' as an impossible demand, the super-ego as an inner Van Helsing breeding guilt over forbidden impulses, with the id and ego mediating - is mapped onto Jonathan's 'wicked, burning desire' for the vampire women. The upshot: we resent culture because we traded happiness for security, yet living like Dracula would get our throats cut.

freud-death-drive.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
freud-death-drive.title: 14. David Bowie’s Sadness
freud-death-drive.relation: Ketcham argues Bowie's sadness is ours: via Deleuze and Guattari's Anti-Oedipus he casts consumer capitalism as a machine producing schizophrenic fad-following (the stuck high-school footballer, the Benetton self), of which Bowie's serial personas are both symptom and escape - 'always crashing in the same car' yet never repeating. Minkowski's lived time and the Buddha's anatman ground the dance as pure becoming without a dancer, while Heidegger's das Man and being-toward-death explain why authentic self-creation - which, unlike Sellers or Williams, Bowie survived - exacts the price Freud's beyond-the-pleasure-principle names as compulsive repetition, turned by Bowie into a life wish.

freud-death-drive.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
freud-death-drive.title: 10. Change of Heart
freud-death-drive.relation: Auxier names Petty the master of "liminal moments" when something is finally seen for what it is (the betrayed lover's realization behind "You Got Lucky," the unknown pain of "American Girl"), then stages the 1929 Davos debate between Cassirer's humane, Goethe-reading phenomenology and Heidegger's Angst before the abyss, being-toward-death, and the "moment of vision." He indicts Heidegger's Nazism and betrayal of Husserl as what "Petty-ness," the asshole-beast crouching in everyone's darkdeepdown, becomes when it wins, contrasting Petty's public apology for the Confederate flag and his cease-and-desist to George W. Bush. The chapter ends with the unguarded Petty smile as "Here Comes My Girl" made philosophy, an instance of authentic being-with-others that Heidegger declared impossible.

freud-death-drive.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
freud-death-drive.title: 18. Iron Man’s Choice to Die
freud-death-drive.relation: Argues Tony's death in Endgame is best explained three ways: via Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives (Tony oscillates between the cabin family-life drive and the risk-seeking death drive that takes him aboard the donut ship in Infinity War and has him lay down to die with Nebula), via Camus's absurd (like Sisyphus, Tony creates subjective meaning by choosing — Pepper, Morgan, and finally the snap itself, 'Part of the journey is the end'), and via consequentialism (the snap as a desirable consequence, contrasting Infinity War's deontological 'We don't trade lives' with Endgame's 'whatever it takes'). It contends that because the time heist rewrites history, deaths in both films — Vision's, Natasha's, Tony's — risk becoming meaningless, so Tony dies on his terms to make his death meaningful.

freud-death-drive.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
freud-death-drive.title: 27. I Am Inevitable
freud-death-drive.relation: Reads Thanos's 'I am inevitable' (his name echoing thanatos) as death personified, then asks 'whose death?' through Heidegger — 'people die' is the evasive 'one dies,' and Tony's final snap and 'I am Iron Man' figure an authentic appropriation of being-toward-death that redeems his guilt — before Blanchot's reversal and Lacan's symbolic death dissolve that authenticity into impersonal, language-borne dying (Loki's 'No resurrections this time' as the meta-textual murder of comic-book death). It ends with Deleuze's Nietzschean eternal return as the empty form of time that the time heist and quantum multiverse enact, concluding the real inevitability 'engraved in the very fabric of reality' belongs to Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter's dance, not to Thanos or Iron Man.

freud-death-drive.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
freud-death-drive.title: Taking in the View from the Paranoid Position
freud-death-drive.relation: Christian reads the fleet through Freud's death instinct and Melanie Klein's paranoid position: Starbuck's self-destruction, Tigh and Ellen's sadomasochism, and Baltar's relationship with Six fuse Eros and Thanatos, and 'Maelstrom' returns Starbuck to the abusive mother whose rejection of her love taught her that love itself is poisonous. Humans project all aggression and badness onto the Cylons they created - 'toaster' talk, Cain's torture of Gina - to keep a split between good self and evil other. The price is permanent vigilance in the watchtower: since anyone might be a Cylon (the Chief's fear, Baltar's test), the crew can never be sure the projected badness is not their own, which is why the machines must keep 'coming back.'

freud-death-drive.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
freud-death-drive.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
freud-death-drive.relation: Hunt treats the film as a direct view of a single subject's unconscious, Freud-style: the Dude is the pre-Oedipal narcissist, the Big Lebowski the father toppled from his wheelchair-throne after the confrontation, Maude the mother, with a scattered superego distributed across the Stranger's moralizing and the Malibu sheriff's 'Stay out of Malibu!'. Donny and Walter figure oral and anal fixations, Jesus the threatening playground peer, and Bunny and the nihilists Freud's life and death drives — so Donny's death in the parking-lot melee lets the ego fuse death-drive energy into life, and the Dude's walk-away from the little Lebowski back to bowling and White Russians reads as repression into comfortable pre-Oedipal phantasy.

freud-death-drive.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
freud-death-drive.title: The Death of Death
freud-death-drive.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

freud-death-drive.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
freud-death-drive.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
freud-death-drive.relation: Sets up Sons of Anarchy as a Hamlet retelling — Jax the prince, Clay the Claudius who murdered John Teller and married Gemma, Tara a gutsier Ophelia — and reads it through Freud and Ernest Jones's Hamlet and Oedipus: Jax's protest that he 'untwisted my mommy thing a long time ago,' his toleration of Gemma's meddling, and the Season 4/5 finale tableaux where Gemma displaces Tara at his side betray an unresolved Oedipus complex. Freud's three agencies get bodies: Clay as pure Id (beating Gemma in 'Hands'), Tara as Superego, Jax as the mediating Ego, with SAMCRO itself a collective Id worshipped in its 'chapel.' Oral and anal-stage fixations explain the Sons' chain-smoking, recklessness, and defiance of authority, while the Id's civil war between libido and the death drive plays out in Gemma's post-beating sex binge and Jax's unconscious pleasure in killing.

freud-death-drive.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
freud-death-drive.title: NOTES
freud-death-drive.relation: Hirschbein presents True Blood as a Freudian fable: vampires live the unrepressed id's Eros and Thanatos that civilization forces the rest of us to renounce, which is why they defeat all three sources of suffering (mortal bodies, nature, hostile neighbors) and why the show's convulsive sex and violence thrill us. Glamouring reproduces the posthypnotic suggestion that proved the unconscious to Freud, Sookie's mind-reading confirms his dark discoveries about our sexualized aggression, vampire myths work as projection screens for desires we disown, and Marcuse's complaint about 'genital tyranny' and sublimation frames Sookie's love as a near-realization of Freud's St. Francis ideal.

freud-death-drive.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
freud-death-drive.title: Moral Man in the Dark City Film Noir, the Postwar Religious Revival, and The Accused
freud-death-drive.relation: Palmer nuances the 'dark mirror' theory of noir by recovering a redemptive subgroup, reading Dieterle's The Accused through the postwar religious revival and the writings of Reinhold Niebuhr and Erich Fromm. Where Lang's The Woman in the Window only chastens its professor via a dream, The Accused stages a genuinely penitential arc: repressed psychology professor Wilma Tuttle kills the aggressive student Bill in panic, then is therapeutically forced to relive the crime (at the prizefight and in the reenactment) until love with lawyer Warren Ford delivers her from 'separateness.' Palmer argues this patriarchal, therapeutic 'conversion'—glamorizing Loretta Young out of her mannish disguise—reconfigures Niebuhr's taming of passion and Fromm's account of love as a decision, heralding a coming 'culture of narcissism.'

freud-death-drive.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
freud-death-drive.title: Introduction War Films and the Ineffability of War
freud-death-drive.relation: LaRocca argues that a war film can never be war itself but only a mediated, post-facto fabrication, and reads the camera and the gun as twinned instruments ('point and shoot' becoming digital 'point and click' in Skyfall). He mobilizes Baudrillard's claim that the Gulf War 'did not take place' to describe war video games and CGI spectacle (Avatar, Call of Duty) as hyperreal simulacra, and Freud's 'Why War?' letter and death instinct to explain the compulsive proliferation of war representation. Foucault ('peace is a coded war'), Heraclitus ('war is father of all'), and Isaiah Berlin's plurality of incompatible values frame war's ineffability and perpetuity, while Cavell's ontology of film grounds the viewer's 'mechanically assured' helplessness before on-screen dying bodies.

freud-death-drive.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
freud-death-drive.title: War and Its Fictional Recovery On-Screen Narrative Management of Death in The Big Red One and The Thin Red Lin
freud-death-drive.relation: Bronfen takes Freud's 'Thoughts for the Times on War and Death' (life 'recovers its full content' when war forces us to believe in death) and his theory of the death drive and the uncanny double as a template for how war films manage mortality through fiction. In Fuller's The Big Red One, the nameless Sergeant's guilt-driven distinction between killing and murder, his Nazi double Schroeder, and the compulsively repeated stabbing scene at the crucifix let the hero convert contingent slaughter into a restitutive story where survival is 'the only glory,' echoing Freud's Eros–Thanatos struggle. In Malick's The Thin Red Line, Private Witt splits not into warlike and peacetime selves but into bodily and spiritual presence, embracing death as transcendence into 'shining light' that doubles the light of cinema itself. Both films strike a pact with the viewer, who dies with the heroes yet safely survives them.

freud-death-drive.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
freud-death-drive.title: 12. Early Punk and the Dionysian Lion-Child
freud-death-drive.relation: Rentmeester reads early punk through Nietzsche's three metamorphoses of the spirit: the Sex Pistols' 'God Save the Queen' (the Thames boat arrest during the Silver Jubilee) is the lion destroying worn-out values, while the Stooges' 'I Wanna Be Your Dog' and Raw Power embody the child's sacred Yes, making punk a hybrid Dionysian lion-child. Punk is Dionysian rather than Apollonian - raw instinct over measured restraint, Iggy Pop's self-mutilation and the Gzowski interview - with 'camelistic' pop and soft rock critiqued via Horkheimer and Adorno's culture industry, and Sid Vicious's violence named as Freud's death drive.

freud-death-drive.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
freud-death-drive.title: 10. Some Dark Genie
freud-death-drive.relation: Calef asks whether Bourdain's choice to become a heroin addict could be rational and responsible, using Mill's On Liberty and Harm Principle (including the voluntary-slavery exception) to argue addiction is reversible and can minimize suffering when alternatives are bleak. He then reads Bourdain's self-destructive drives — the drunk cliff-driving 'death trip' — through Freud's death drive (Thanatos) and Schopenhauer's pessimism, concluding the 'dark genie' was partly disease-like and thus not wholly blameworthy.

freud-death-drive.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
freud-death-drive.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
freud-death-drive.relation: Casey McKittrick accounts for gay 'bareback' pornography — the erotic celebration of condomless anal sex and visible semen exchange (the reinsertion shot, gangbang formats like Dawson's 50-Load Weekend). He situates it against the pathologizing of homosexuality, citing Foucault's History of Sexuality on the Victorian 'invention' of the homosexual and Lee Edelman on queer sexuality as outside reproductive futurity. Drawing on Freud's account of loss and the death drive (eros and thanatos), he reads semen as the 'lost object' — 'brothers' milk' — and bareback video as a fantasy screen restoring intimacy severed by AIDS, animating the struggle between the erotic and the lethal.

freud-death-drive.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
freud-death-drive.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
freud-death-drive.relation: Clack's 'Cannabis and the Human Condition' reads intoxication through Freud's Civilization and its Discontents, where drugs are the 'crudest but most effective' palliative against a life 'too hard for us,' tied to the pleasure principle and the Nirvana/death-instinct drive to discharge stimulus. He supplements Freud with Schopenhauer's pessimism — life oscillating between suffering and boredom — to add 'stimulus hunger' Freud ignored, arguing cannabis both dampens and stokes the 'fire in the brain' depending on THC potency (high vs. stoned). He concludes that, like religion, art and love, cannabis augments a bleak existence, so 'all cannabis use is medicinal.'

freud-death-drive.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
freud-death-drive.title: SERIAL KILLERS
freud-death-drive.relation: Piven mounts an 'epistemology of murder,' invoking Hume and Nietzsche to argue that most of what we 'know' about serial killers and terrorists is projected fantasy and prejudice, amplified by fear (Terror Management Theory). Rereading Lord of the Flies and the Milgram studies, he claims violence follows from shame, humiliation, and abuse (Athens's 'violentization') rather than innate evil, and uses Freud's fort-da game and repetition compulsion to argue killers displace their own woundedness and 'soul murder' onto surrogate victims. He controversially links serial killers, who sexualize death and merge with victims, to terrorists who sanctify displaced sexual rage as God's will — a 'serial killer in sheik's clothing.'

abduction.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
abduction.title: James Bond and Philosophy
abduction.relation: Abrams explains Peirce's three modes of inference (deduction proves, induction shows, abduction merely suggests) and reconstructs, abduction by abduction, Bond's rapid chain of guesses in The World Is Not Enough: from the odd smell and foam on his fingers to the urea-coated fertilizer bomb he unknowingly delivered, the shared motto 'there's no point living if you can't feel alive' exposing Elektra's alliance with Renard, and her guilty subject-changing. He also covers the negative art: Bond plants false clues with Q's gadgets (the fingerprint re-printer, the cloaked Vanquish) while villains like Carver recode reality by sinking the Devonshire to frame the Chinese, and both sides try to force each other into false abductions. Bond wins because his mind is more playful - Peirce's 'musement', Eco's creative abduction, and an encyclopedic education - making 007 the superior player in what is ultimately a game of chance and strategy.

abduction.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
abduction.title: A Toolbox for Your Holmes
abduction.relation: Sami Paavola and Lauri Jaervilehto reconstruct the textbook on detection Holmes never wrote: following Jaakko Hintikka's interrogative (Socratic) model, where the right question cracks the case, as with the dog that did nothing in the night-time in 'Silver Blaze', and Peirce's triad of deduction, induction and abduction, the backward reasoning from effects to causes exemplified by the Watson-just-from-Afghanistan chain in A Study in Scarlet. They add Peirce's categories of Firstness, Secondness and Thirdness to show Holmes succeeds because he fuses imagination and reverie with fieldwork, experiment and exact inference. The chapter closes with a twelve-point practical toolbox distilled from the canon.

abduction.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
abduction.title: An Inexact Science
abduction.relation: Demeter argues that Holmes's official self-image as a cold 'reasoning machine' is an ideology that distorts his actual practice: between collecting facts and eliminating impossible scenarios, Holmes is a creator of stories whose 'narrative imagination' invents possible explanations, a phase deduction cannot account for (Peter Lipton's point that Holmesian 'deduction' is not logically valid). Reading 'The Man with the Twisted Lip,' he shows how the same facts (coins in the coat pockets) become different evidence in different narratives until Holmes reconceives Boone and Neville St. Clair as one person. Holmes's preference for the bizarre over the simple, his warning against theorizing before the data, and his claim that his gift is hereditary ('Art in the blood is liable to take the strangest forms') all show detection is closer to art than science, though the scientific persona lends him professional legitimacy and lets him train Scotland Yard.

abduction.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
abduction.title: Psych and Philosophy
abduction.relation: Jones argues that Shawn's 'psychic' act is really hypersensory perception (HSP) - noticing cat fur, fine print, blood spatter - feeding inference to the best explanation (IBE), the natural abductive method Sherlock Holmes mislabels deduction, with Clever Hans and Ilga Kirks as real-world parallels. Applying IBE with Ockham's Razor to the two hypotheses 'he's psychic' versus 'he's hyper-observant,' she concludes the natural explanation should win for everyone: Lassiter's skepticism tracks the evidence, Gus knows better despite believing in ghosts, and Chief Vick shouldn't buy the supernatural story either. Juliet's belief survives only through background supernatural beliefs, a psychic-friendly culture, and ignoring the clues Gus feeds Shawn, which the chapter diagnoses as the same public misunderstanding of the scope and limits of science that keeps most Americans believing in ESP.

abduction.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
abduction.title: 13. Jumping to Conclusions
abduction.relation: Tuomas Manninen uses Endgame's detective work to teach abductive reasoning, inference to the best explanation, as introduced by Charles Peirce, distinguishing it from deduction (Tony Stark is mortal) and induction (Mjolnir-worthiness generalizing to Stormbreaker). He reconstructs Tony's false conclusion that Strange 'gave up the store,' War Machine's wrong guess that Thanos hid the Stones, Cap-2012's mistaken Loki hypothesis upon meeting his future self, and the Ancient One's revised reasoning about Strange surrendering the Time Stone, applying Peter Lipton's actual-versus-potential and likeliest-versus-loveliest distinctions plus five criteria of adequacy (testability, fruitfulness, scope, simplicity, conservatism). Doctor Strange's fourteen-million-futures gambit turns out to combine abduction and deduction into a fallible but insightful plan that only Tony's survival and final snap could fulfill, illustrating Peirce's point that abduction is an instinctive yet rational act of insight.

abduction.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
abduction.title: 9. Why Did Lady Sybil Die
abduction.relation: Egg uses the Clarkson versus Tapsell disagreement over Sybil's pre-eclampsia to teach inference to the best explanation, distinguishing deduction (Carson's syllogism about the Australian singer Dame Nellie), induction (Edith's gloomy generalization from her failed suitors), and Peirce's abduction, evaluated via Peter Lipton's twin criteria of likeliness and loveliness. Daisy's numerology linking the Titanic to Pamuk's death and Violet's inference that Edith's Swiss trip hides a pregnancy show loveliness cutting both ways, while Sybil's death tragically vindicates Clarkson's lovelier but less likely diagnosis. The darkest turn is Violet's second-order manipulation: once 'eclampsia plus Robert's misjudgment' threatens her son's marriage, she gets Clarkson to re-weigh the statistics so that 'eclampsia alone' becomes the best explanation of Sybil's death, showing that the best explanation can be engineered.

abduction.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
abduction.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
abduction.relation: Johnson uses 'Go God Go's' future of 2546—where Dawkins-style atheism has become a warring religion and otter scientists intone 'Oh my Science!'—to ask whether science and religion genuinely conflict and whether New Atheism is itself a faith. Applying abduction and the four criteria of adequacy, he argues the embellished-story hypothesis beats miracle claims about Jesus (whose legend grew Gospel by Gospel), Sathya Sai Baba, Joseph Smith, and Xenu, that Mr(s). Garrison's 'you can't disprove God' and the show's sarcasm commit an appeal to ignorance, and that Stan's water-into-wine scene with Jesus shows how easily people are fooled. He allows Kuhnian theory change in science but rejects James's will-to-believe for existence claims—the moon whale Willzyx needs evidence—and concludes Parker and Stone are unfair to Dawkins: ending religion would not end violence, but it would remove the easiest justification for it, and some answers are simply true even when unknown.

abduction.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
abduction.title: Kickstarting Inductive Inference
abduction.relation: Daniel Wilkenfeld analyzes Veronica's 'magic trick' in the 'One Angry Veronica' juryroom and her season-long bus-crash solution as Peter Lipton's inference to the best explanation: the hypothesis 'Beaver is a killer' wins by consilience (explaining the explosion, the dead rat, Curly Moran, even her chlamydia), simplicity, and completeness. But the criteria face Hume's problem of induction — why think the future will resemble the past, when yesterday's popular girl is today's pariah? — and Descartes's evil demon undermines even what Veronica 'sees,' since Curly Moran could fake a bus crash, leaving no non-circular justification for inferential habits none of us can live without. Following Nelson Goodman, Wilkenfeld concludes the demand for justification is misplaced: what matters is that Veronica reasons consistently, in the juryroom as at the cliff.

abduction.title: CSI and the Art of Forensic Detection
abduction.relation: Knight and McKnight analyze CSI as 'procedural noir': Las Vegas instantiates the corrupt-city trope, and the show's methodological core is reading scientific evidence as a system of signs, generating and testing hypotheses through hypothetical flash reconstructions (Grissom's wrong incest-guess in 'Blood Drops', competing crash theories in 'Anonymous'). Three case studies carry the philosophy: Philip Gerard's defense attack on the team's competence makes forensic investigation an ethical matter of integrity and reliable process rather than mere evidence collection; the Paul Millander trilogy uses the trope of the double (Paul/Pauline, Judge Mason, the forged Grissom identity) to explore identity and self-knowledge; and Lady Heather's dominance-submission 'stop' convention reframes the femme fatale around reason, passion, and Grissom's desire to be known.

abduction.title: Detection and the Logic of Abduction in The X-Files
abduction.relation: Abrams and Cooke map Mulder and Scully onto Holmes and Watson and onto the Clifford-James debate: Scully embodies Clifford's ethics of belief (suspend judgment without hard evidence), while Mulder's 'I Want to Believe' poster enacts James's will to believe, which lets him see what the paradigm excludes. The chapter formalizes both agents' actual method as Peirce's logic of abduction, using Eco's overcoded/undercoded/creative triad to analyze Scully's Fowley clothing inference and the mushroom episodes of 'Field Trip', and extends Peircean semiotics with Mulder's 'absence sign' (the missing nine minutes, missing acid burns, bodies taken without a trace). Kuhn's normal science versus revolution explains why Scully stays inside the FBI's paradigm while Mulder's passion makes him the revolutionary who, with Scully as error-corrector, fuses into a single 'whole person' detective facing the limits of reason.

hume-is-ought.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
hume-is-ought.title: James Bond and Philosophy
hume-is-ought.relation: Kowalski explains yin-yang cosmology through the Yi Ching and Shu Ching - opposing forces in dynamic harmony, each containing the seed of its opposite, with excess of either bringing destruction - and applies it to the Brosnan-era films, reading Bond himself as the yang force of action. The films improved, he argues, by strengthening yin: Wai Lin as Bond's equal partner in the handcuffed motorcycle chase of Tomorrow Never Dies (each watching the road the other cannot see), Judi Dench's M as the corrective to Admiral Roebuck's hawkish yang ('the advantage is that I don't always have to think with them'), and Elektra King as a genuine yin villainess rather than a damsel. He ends with a Humean caveat that deriving moral conclusions from the natural order is logically suspect, yet endorses the cosmology's practical advice - balance and harmony between opposing forces - as the reason the new millennium Bond films are better.

hume-is-ought.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
hume-is-ought.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
hume-is-ought.relation: Framed as a sports broadcast with Aristotle as commentator, the chapter tests an evolutionary ethics ('BEES': the good is the naturally desirable, so the Pleistocene Stinson strategy of spreading genes grounds Barney's womanizing) against its classic critics. Hume's is-ought gap and Moore's open question argument are deployed against deriving Barney's right to pursue tail from human nature, while William Casebeer's evolutionary ethics replies that 'good' can be defined by present reproductive success - under which lying and eternal bachelorhood fail, since commitment is what reproduces genomes in urban New York ('BIRDS'). The chapter concludes that evolutionary ethics can support the Bro Code only by contestable redefinition, and the lying objection stands.

hume-is-ought.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
hume-is-ought.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
hume-is-ought.relation: Robert Arp's gallery matches each Gang vice - dishonesty, egoism, selfishness, greed, pettiness, ignorance, laziness - to real-life scumbags from Nixon, Stephen Glass, and Janet Cooke to Charles Ponzi, Bernie Madoff, Crassus, the Empress Dowager Cixi, Imelda Marcos, and the Darwin Awards, and it opens with the chapter's philosophical spine: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Book II of Plato's Republic, which predicts that even an upstanding person with the power to act unseen would seduce, steal, and murder - exactly the question the Gang's mostly unpunished antics keep staging. Against the ethical egoist's argument that because everyone is self-interested everyone should be (Vanderbilt's 'the public be damned'), the chapter deploys the is-ought point - children are naturally selfish without therefore deserving to be - alongside mothers, Mother Teresa, and 9/11 first responders, concluding that egoism is at most an admixture in every action, with Lord of the Flies as the reductio of universal egoism.

hume-is-ought.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
hume-is-ought.title: 5. Every Lonely Monster Needs a Companion
hume-is-ought.relation: Gadsden asks why a near-omnipotent Time Lord needs companions at all and tests four hypotheses against his solo meltdowns—executing Solomon in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship,' nearly murdering Jex in 'A Town Called Mercy,' and declaring himself 'Time Lord Victorious' in 'The Waters of Mars.' He rejects the Lord Acton power-corrupts hypothesis via Glaucon's ring story in Plato's Republic, since powerless companions offer no threat of reprisal or dishonor, and qualifies J.J. Sylvia's care-ethics 'empathetic link' because the Doctor cares for non-human species like the Star Whale too. He favors two answers: Hume's fact/value gap as a millennium-long moral myopia ('I can't see it anymore,' the deleted 'Flesh and Stone' confession), and Aristotle's point in the Nicomachean Ethics that only virtuous friends—moral peers who mirror us—can expose the Doctor's blind spots, like his 'God Complex.'

hume-is-ought.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
hume-is-ought.title: 15. The C-Word
hume-is-ought.relation: Works through the ethics of cloning and genetic selection, starting with the objection that such technologies are "unnatural": that reasoning commits the naturalistic fallacy, since following Hume you can't get an ought from an is, and human ingenuity (roads, eyeglasses, IVF) is itself part of nature. Using Nietzsche's Genealogy account of master morality — good as the noble traits of intelligence, beauty, and strength — the chapter asks whether parents would then be obliged to engineer better children, while warning where trait-selection slides: Nazi eugenics, racist trait-lists (both Leda and Castor are white and conventionally attractive), and "abilism" against the deaf. It concludes that cloning itself is not evil: Projects Leda and Castor are immoral not because they clone but because they treat clones as mere means to an end, in Kant's sense, and trample their autonomy.

hume-is-ought.title: 3. Schumer’s Selfishness
hume-is-ought.relation: Weighs psychological egoism, the thesis that every action is ultimately self-interested, against apparent altruism through Schumer's cluelessly selfish characters: the 'Cancer Excuse' sketch where Amy exploits Tig Notaro's diagnosis, God's dismay at her in 'Herpes Scare', and Emily Middleton guilt-tripping her mother into an Ecuador trip in Snatched. Arp deploys Adam Smith's Chinese-earthquake passage from The Theory of Moral Sentiments and Rachels's Lincoln piglets story before rejecting the argument for ethical egoism on is-ought and coherence grounds, concluding Schumer's selfish jerks are comic negative examples of how not to live.

hume-is-ought.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
hume-is-ought.title: 15. Loving Your Pet Is Better than Utilitarianism
hume-is-ought.relation: Against Peter Singer's utilitarian case in Animal Liberation, spare Snuffles because he can suffer regardless of intelligence, the chapter argues utilitarianism fails because it quantifies the unquantifiable, happiness. It turns to Hume: intelligence cannot ground moral worth, since smart Rick enslaving a microverse would then be our moral superior; Hume's guillotine separates descriptive from moral claims so that metaphysics no longer decides who counts as a moral object; and Hume's real ground is sentiment, dogs loving across species as the tail-wagging Snuffles does. So the morally right response to 'Lawnmower Dog' is not Jerry's abuse or even Rick's intelligence helmet but simply loving the pet.

hume-is-ought.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
hume-is-ought.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
hume-is-ought.relation: Asks what, if anything, makes George Michael kissing Maeby wrong, and dismantles the Argument from Naturalism by testing three definitions of 'natural' against incest, Gob's Segway, and Buster's devotion to Lucille (and Maeby possibly being 'made in a cup' via IVF), showing the argument equivocates in violation of Hume's is/ought distinction. It then weighs Ayer's emotivism (moral claims as 'Yuck!' expressions) against Leon Kass's wisdom of repugnance, concluding the disgust at cousin-kissing may be an aesthetic rather than a moral judgment.

hume-is-ought.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
hume-is-ought.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
hume-is-ought.relation: Pigliucci argues the gang is funny because their scientistic worldview misfires in ordinary life: Howard's Drake-equation-derived 'Wolowitz coefficient,' Sheldon's friendship algorithm that Howard must rescue from an infinite loop, and Leonard's 'bio-social exploration' kiss experiment with Leslie all fail because courtship and friendship resist quantification. Tracing scientism's appeal to the Cartesian method of reductionism, he criticizes E.O. Wilson's Consilience, Sam Harris's science of morality (defending Hume's distinction between empirical facts and values), and the Churchlands' eliminative materialism — the tequila sunrise and the rock wall's qualitative feel escaping the neuro-reductive gaze. Sheldon's chocolate-based operant conditioning of Penny and the Tuskegee syphilis study show why science needs ethical evaluation from outside itself.

hume-is-ought.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
hume-is-ought.title: Notes
hume-is-ought.relation: Tests moral relativism against absolutism through Enterprise's "Cogenitor": Trip's liberation of the Vissian third-sex being - secretly scanning its brain, naming it Charles, teaching it to read - ends in its suicide, and the chapter asks whether Trip's judgments track rational moral truth or are Humean after-the-fact rationalizations of disgust, since on Hume's view reason is the slave of the passions and is/ought are separate. Kant's categorical imperative (the cogenitor used merely as a means of reproduction) and Aquinas's natural law are offered as absolutist resources on Trip's side, while Phlox voices a Benedict-style "morally good is just habitual" relativism and Archer concludes "we didn't come out here to play God", prefiguring the Prime Directive. The chapter lands on Mary Midgley's rejection of moral isolationism via her tsujigiri example and Quark's "we're better than you" speech to Sisko: cross-cultural judgment is possible, but only after understanding, and not on the first day of first contact.

hume-is-ought.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
hume-is-ought.title: Bringing Balance to the Force
hume-is-ought.relation: Harter argues that Revenge of the Sith manipulates audiences into fearing the medical technology that saves Anakin on Mustafar, portraying his prosthetic transformation into Vader as horrifying when in real bioethical terms saving a burn victim with ventilators, feeding tubes, and prosthetics is something we applaud. He diagnoses Lucas's framing as the naturalistic fallacy (what is natural is good), grounded in Hume's is-ought gap, and flags the mirror-image 'technological fallacy' of assuming enhancement like General Grievous's cyborg body must be good. The chapter concludes that technology is value-neutral and its worth depends on the context of use — which is what it means for Anakin and Luke, both maimed and prosthetized, to 'bring balance to the Force.'

hume-is-ought.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
hume-is-ought.title: NOTES
hume-is-ought.relation: The Terjesens dissect what 'unnatural' could mean for vampires: on modern evolutionary biology they are simply effective predators, so no unfairness or odd predation style (sleeping with one's food) makes them unnatural. Aristotle's four causes and Aquinas's God-ordered extrinsic finality would let 'unnatural' mean 'against the plan', but purposes cannot be observed — the source of bad medieval science — and Descartes's banishment of final causes from physics shows why; Godric's 'our existence is insanity' therefore commits the is–ought fallacy, and what remains to judge is not vampire nature but vampire choice, as Bill's mainstreaming and Godric's final 'I told a lie' about survival versus right and wrong show.

hume-is-ought.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
hume-is-ought.title: P A R T F O U R
hume-is-ought.relation: Four Part Four essays beyond ethics. Aaron Meskin asks whether Watchmen is literature at all, testing definitions from Beardsley, Eagleton, Lamarque/Olsen and Hirsch in the Socratic 'what is X?' way, and concludes the question is indeterminate because comics are a hybrid art form — though the book's literary allusions (Shelley's 'Ozymandias,' Blake's 'Tyger,' Burroughs) deserve literary appreciation regardless. Sarah Donovan and Nick Richardson read the two Silk Spectres through three feminisms: Sally and Laurie as liberal feminists (Wollstonecraft, Mill) who fight crime, their hypersexual costumes as Irigaray-style subversive mimicry of gender stereotypes that risks reinforcing them (the Silhouette's expulsion exposing the heterosexual norm), the Comedian's attempted rape exposing 'she asked for it' attitudes, and Laurie as Beauvoir's woman in bad faith, living out her mother's fantasies until she finally names and dresses herself. Robert Arp uses Hooded Justice and Captain Metropolis's closeted relationship to dismantle 'homosexuality is unnatural' arguments — the ideal-function view would condemn the infertile too, and Hume's is-ought point undermines the procreation argument — before defending gay marriage against slippery-slope and parenting objections. Taneli Kukkonen maps Kierkegaard's stages onto the Comedian's mocking irony (hiding even his paternity of Laurie and his Kennedy confession as jokes) and Rorschach's deeper humor of the ethical stage, a knight of resignation whose 'never compromise, not even in the face of Armageddon' expects nothing back from the world.

hume-is-ought.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
hume-is-ought.title: What Is Wrong with Cloning a Dinosaur Jurassic Park and Nature as a Source of Moral Authority
hume-is-ought.relation: Spence uses the Hammond-Malcolm debate in Jurassic Park to ask whether nature can ground moral authority. He distinguishes prudential risk arguments (Grant, Sattler) from Malcolm's distinctly moral charge that cloning dinosaurs is 'anti-nature,' then deploys Hume's is/ought problem and Hume's essay 'On Suicide' to argue there is no principled natural/unnatural line and no valid inference from natural facts to moral oughts. Examining natural-law theory (Aquinas, Cicero, 'perverted faculty' arguments), he concludes tampering with nature may be unwise but is not inherently immoral.

hume-is-ought.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
hume-is-ought.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
hume-is-ought.relation: Kretz systematically attacks the claim that hunting is environmental, using the Ducks Unlimited Canada case. She wields Hume's is-ought gap to deny that 'natural' hunting is thereby moral, cites evidence that hunters remove the fittest breeders and eliminate predators, and rejects Thoreau's hope that young hunters 'outgrow' killing as counterproductive (analogous to teaching theft to prevent it). Drawing on Brian Luke, she presses 'the paradox of ethical hunting': the sportsman's code (quick kills, retrieve the wounded) shows concern for the animal that, fully realized, entails not hunting at all.

hume-is-ought.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
hume-is-ought.title: Who is Who
hume-is-ought.relation: This chapter reads the Doctor as poised between positivism and phenomenology. It uses Hume's Fork and the Vienna Circle's verificationism (via 'The Daemons' and 'Tomb of the Cybermen') to cast the pro-science Doctor as an empiricist, then argues he is equally a Husserlian phenomenologist attentive to the 'life-world' and a Heideggerian Dasein whose time-travelling homelessness and the show's sense of the uncanny (unheimlich) embody being-in-the-world, thrownness and the flight from the worldhood of the world.

sense-reference.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sense-reference.title: Persuasive Definition
sense-reference.relation: A caricature history of semantics centered on Frege's threefold distinction of sense, reference, and tone (Faerbung): 'the evening star' and 'the morning star' share a reference but differ in sense, and 'and' versus 'but' share logical form while differing in tone, which formal logic must suppress. The chapter ends by deploying Stevenson's persuasive definition against the Thouless-style Orwellian fantasy of purging tone-laden words like 'freedom' and 'democratic' from political language: the real remedy is taking tone seriously, since tone does real work in ordinary argument.

sense-reference.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sense-reference.title: Broadening the Analysis
sense-reference.relation: Stevenson's persuasive definition - changing a term's descriptive meaning while keeping its emotive force - is restated in Fregean terms as changing sense or reference while representing tone as fixed, yielding a sixteen-fold table of definitional moves (PD, PQD, and beyond). Semantic negligence then grades PDs: the aphoristic 'Conservatism is true socialism' deceives no one, but the definer who hides an argument inside a definition gains rhetorical advantage while risking that his audience endorses conclusions they were never given a fair chance to appraise - analogous to bullshit rather than lying.

sense-reference.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sense-reference.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
sense-reference.relation: Low and high redefinition - widening or narrowing a term's reference - are defined and illustrated by the convicted drunk driver who recasts himself as someone who merely 'had a miscalculated drink', a self-serving move aimed at dodging the pejorative tone of 'drunk driver'. The move partially overlaps persuasive definition (each is a high redefinition of the other's complement) and typically rests on wilful blindness to conventional usage.

sense-reference.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sense-reference.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
sense-reference.relation: Flew's No-True-Scotsman Move - retreating from 'No Scotsman takes sugar with his porridge' to 'No true Scotsman...' when Hamish MacTavish of Inverness falsifies it - is analyzed as a redefinition that converts a bold, falsifiable claim into a vacuous necessary truth. Because the two statements look and sound alike, confusing them (from carelessness as easily as deceit) is semantic negligence, and pressing on as if the original claim still stood is classic Frankfurt bullshit.

sense-reference.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
sense-reference.title: Backfire
sense-reference.relation: Euphemism - the Furies as the 'Kindly Ones', 'sex workers', 'superprompt critical power excursion' for nuclear meltdown - resets a term's tone while preserving its sense and reference, but Germaine Greer's 'euphemism treadmill' shows the pejorative tone rapidly migrates onto each replacement unless underlying attitudes change. The comparative stability of 'gay' and 'black' marks real progress, while most politically correct and nukespeak coinages simply backfire as Greer describes.

sense-reference.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
sense-reference.title: The Loneliest Witch
sense-reference.relation: Auxier gives three theories of why water melts the Wicked Witch, one for each register of Oz: as dream (Bergson's account of dreams as memory explains the fire/water effect-swap), as Baum's fairytale (Susanne Langer's presentational symbols make dryness-wickedness versus water-as-life the tale's moral physics), and as Gregory Maguire's possible world, where the philosophy of language takes over. He narrates Frege's sense/reference distinction—mayor of the Munchkins—to explain how fiction can support truth and falsity ('Dorothy melts the Witch' true, 'Dorothy tried to melt her' false), then deploys Putnam's Twin Earth thought experiment: 'water' in Oz is XYZ while Kansas water is H2O, so Elphaba's word 'water' does not mean what Dorothy's does, and meanings just aren't in the head. Elphaba—the unique being straddling two worlds, killed by H2O she cannot name and terrified by dreams of oceans—is offered as an even stronger argument for Putnam's semantic externalism than Twin Earth's molecule-for-molecule doppelgangers.

sense-reference.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
sense-reference.title: Conclestions
sense-reference.relation: Jason Southworth asks how viewers understand Colbert's deliberately confusing coinages ('wordanista,' 'superstantial,' 'Lincolnish,' 'freem,' and the title 'I Am America (And So Can You!)'). Borrowing Russell's view that names abbreviate definite descriptions (the 'spot check test'), he argues these utterances are paraphrasable and therefore meaningful rather than nonsense, distinguishing meaning from reference and literal from non-literal meaning. He then applies Grice's cooperative principle and conversational maxims to derive implicatures: the gut speech violates 'do not say what you believe to be false' and so implies truthiness-as-visceral-feeling, 'wordinista' imports Sandinista-style radicalism, and 'John, tear me a new one' generates the kitten-woodchipper joke. Since context fixes meaning, even dictionary-less words like 'freem' can be decoded, and the Wordinistas at Webster's are unnecessary.

sense-reference.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
sense-reference.title: “When You’re Suffering, That’s When You’re Most Real”
sense-reference.relation: Lean treats Bernard's discovery in 'Trompe L'Oeil' that his son Charlie never existed as a richly detailed thought experiment about intentionality: his memories of Charlie seem to refer to nothing, so his grief looks like 'grieving about nothing.' After setting up Brentano's aboutness and Frege's sense/reference distinction (Dolores learns that 'William' and 'the Man in Black' are one referent known under two senses), he tests two consolations: a fiction theory drawing on Lamarque, on which Bernard's implanted memories are a story rather than a lie and his emotions are rationally grounded because thoughts need only be entertained, not believed, to move us; and an 'inheritance theory' on which a causal theory of reference might make Bernard's copied memories genuinely about Arnold's real dead son. He concludes that whichever theory Bernard adopts, his suffering is what makes him 'real,' echoing the Man in Black's line that suffering is when you are most real.

sense-reference.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
sense-reference.title: “When You’re Suffering, That’s When You’re Most Real”
sense-reference.relation: Lean treats Bernard's grief over the fabricated son Charlie as a thought experiment about intentionality, using Brentano's 'aboutness' and Frege's sense/reference (illustrated by Dolores knowing 'William' and 'the Man in Black' as one referent) to ask whether Bernard's memories refer to nothing. He offers Lamarque's fiction theory (emotion needs only entertained, not believed, thoughts, so Charlie could be a fiction rather than a lie) and an 'inheritance theory' using a causal theory of reference to ask whether Bernard's memories actually refer to Arnold's real dead son. He concludes that grieving makes Bernard 'most real' whatever the metaphysics.

sense-reference.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
sense-reference.title: Worlds within Words
sense-reference.relation: Tomkinson uses Frege's sense/reference distinction (the morning star and the evening star) to ask what Sapkowski's proper names mean and pick out: Zireael ('swallow') tying Ciri to the Tower of the Swallow, Ciri's defiant adoption of 'Falka' as nom de guerre, and Regis's mule named 'Dracul' pointing both to the beast and to Count Dracula.
