She traces the Elder Speech's Celtic sound to Tolkien's glossopoeia and Le Guin's Earthsea true names, and reads place names like Cintra (the 1808 Convention of Cintra) as political allusions to partitioned Poland caught between empires. The chapter closes on whether fictional names like 'the Witcher' - the novels, Henry Cavill, Liam Hemsworth - have referents at all, invoking Russell's 'non-entities' and speculating that Ciri's portals and the Conjunction make the alluded worlds part of the Witcherverse itself.

sense-reference.title: 6. But What Does It Mean
sense-reference.relation: Kreider argues Twin Peaks is less about determinate meaning than about handing viewers incomplete, underdetermined content to complete themselves. He reads the opening sequence's waterfalls and trees through Kant's aesthetic 'purposiveness without purpose,' the swaying traffic light and 'the full blossom of the evening' as Russell's incomplete symbols, and the range of legitimate interpretations through Quine's underdetermination of theory by evidence; Susanne Langer's Feeling and Form adds that film creates a dreamlike virtual present, so the Part 8 atomic-bomb sequence works exactly as a dream we must interpret.

sense-reference.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
sense-reference.title: 3. How Symbolic Logic Saved the Foundation
sense-reference.relation: Tepley argues symbolic logic is an unsung hero of Foundation: Salvor Hardin translates the Empire-Anacreon treaty and Lord Dorwin's assurances into symbolic logic and shows ninety percent 'boils out' as meaningless, proving the Empire owes Anacreon nothing and emboldening his coup. He explains propositional and predicate logic (validity, soundness, tautologies, quantifiers) and reconstructs how logical analysis exposes the treaty's tautologies and unsupported conditionals, while noting the idea came from editor John W. Campbell during the Logical-Positivist heyday and sparked psychohistory itself.

sense-reference.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
sense-reference.title: SERIAL KILLERS
sense-reference.relation: Zirngibl asks why we rename killers with nicknames like 'White Wolf' (a literal predatory wolf) and 'Black Widow' (poisoner Lydia Trueblood), using the philosophy of language. She applies the Fregean/Russellian descriptivist theory of names and the notions of reference, denotation, and a 'second baptism' to show how a nickname distills a person into a short, pejorative set of descriptors that displaces their full identity. Through the substitution and Black's interactionist theories of metaphor, plus Nietzschean anthropomorphism and zoomorphism, she argues serial-killer animal metaphors do reciprocal violence to both the maligned animal and the human, humanizing beasts and dehumanizing killers to assert mastery over them.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
mackinnon-dominance.title: Good Definitions
mackinnon-dominance.relation: The definitional taxonomy at work: MacKinnon and Dworkin's Model Law defines pornography as 'the sexually explicit subordination of women', but backfires in Canadian law into raids on gay bookshops while mainstream pornography survives - reference drift from an intended sense-only change. The three theories of rape (traditional property crime, liberal sex-without-consent, radical feminist 'terrorist institution' of male subordination) show definitions track theories and must be argued for, with the radical redefinition risking a tone-dilution that would 'trivialize legitimate rape'.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
mackinnon-dominance.title: Girls and Philosophy
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Robison-Greene defends Girls against the twin criticisms that it is bad feminism (Hannah 'sluttin' around' jokes, Adam's degrading sex with Hannah) and irresponsibly all-white. She argues there is no single correct conception of feminism from which to judge Dunham, that 'demeaning sex is anti-feminist, so portraying it is anti-feminist' is an invalid argument (by analogy with portraying racism in 12 Years a Slave), and notes MacKinnon's dominance view that sex itself may be inherently demeaning only to conclude the debate is legitimate, not settled against the show. On race, she contends Dunham writing authentically from her own half-Jew, half-WASP experience produces better art than tokenism would, and that the obligation to fix representation falls on networks and creators with the relevant experience, not on punishing one writer.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
mackinnon-dominance.title: 5. The Truth Shall Make Ye Fret
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Watson uses The Truth - William de Worde's accidental invention of Ankh-Morpork's first newspaper and the plot to frame Lord Vetinari - to stage the three classic arguments for censorship: direct harm (character assassination 'works every day'), indirect harm (with MacKinnon's point that the speech of the dominant drowns out the subordinated, applied to speciesist insults at Koom Valley), and the false-beliefs argument. Against them stand the knowledge problem and the equality assumption: Mrs. Arcanum's deference to print, Vetinari's turtle-shaped-world joke, and the Montessori-Broca dispute show we never know in advance which beliefs are false, and any censor like Lord de Worde has his own agenda. Vetinari's verdict that 'free men pull in all kinds of directions' because 'pulling together is the aim of despotism' carries the chapter's Millian case that free speech is a horrible necessity.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
mackinnon-dominance.title: The Office and Philosophy
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Dromm asks what makes Michael's behavior wrong even where the law cannot touch it: as an 'equal-opportunity harasser' of Pam, Ryan, and Oscar, Michael seems to escape Title VII's discrimination requirement. He tests Edmund Wall's 'wrongful communication' definition against the filthy emails, 'that's what she said,' and Michael's solution to the Kevin-Angela dispute in 'Conflict Resolution,' finds it too broad and too dependent on the victim's objection, then turns to MacKinnon's sex-discrimination account and Crosthwaite and Priest's oppression account to explain the distinctive harm to women (pressuring Pam to be a cheerleader in 'Basketball,' calling the party-planning committee his 'bitches'). He concludes that both views are needed, and that in the end harassment wrongs workers by undermining their legitimate expectation of being judged only on job-relevant merit, leaving Dwight's extra effort done for nothing.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
mackinnon-dominance.title: NOTES
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Craton and Jonell read Sookie as an emblem of contemporary feminist ambivalence: her 'I am woman, hear me roar' independence coexists with sexual caution, and the show stages feminism's sex wars — Lafayette's sex work and webcam pornography versus Maryann, whose 'pro-sex' liberation collapses into self-annihilating worship of Dionysus and whose death suggests unregulated sexuality is dangerous. Tara's plotline shows how race and class layer onto gender (her 'baby-daddy' scene, Maryann as failed white savior), exposing the limits of a united feminist front, while the 'kept woman' quarrel with Bill and Sookie's barmaid-versus-telepathic-detective career choice leave more questions about female empowerment than answers.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
mackinnon-dominance.title: Getting Tough and Getting Even
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Jordan Pascoe uses the 'Like a Virgin' purity test — Meg's fake 48 making her a 'slut' while a low score would make a guy a stud — to argue slut shaming strips girls of Kantian personhood, treating as things those autonomous beings who must be respected as ends in themselves. Kant's bleak view of sex as a desire for a body rather than a person explains why Tad's drugging and popsicle-video blackmail of Carmen reduce her to an object, and why objectification goes viral: once an object of one person's appetite, Kant warns, a person 'can be treated and used as such by everyone.' Catherine MacKinnon's power-based account then explains the double standard — men's pleasure in forcing the world to conform turns promiscuous men into studs and promiscuous women into sluts — so the fault lies with the slut sneezers, never Meg, Carmen, or Veronica, who must 'get tough, get even' to demand respect.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
mackinnon-dominance.title: 14. Did Bourdain Go #MeToo Far
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Finn tests Catharine MacKinnon's 'Rape Redefined' — rape as sex compelled by inequality rather than lack of consent — against Bourdain's #MeToo allyship and his payment to Asia Argento's teenage accuser Jimmy Bennett. She argues MacKinnon's power-based standard could recognize Argento's act as assault, and reframes Bourdain's hush-money payment, via the Wendat/Huron compensation practices in Graeber and Wengrow, as a compassionate vengeance-staying reparation consistent with his empathy.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mackinnon-dominance.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Andrew Aberdein traces the historical 'interpenetration' of philosophy and pornography — from the French book trade's 'livres philosophiques' and Diderot, d'Argens's Thérèse philosophe, and Sade, back through Aretino's courtesan dialogues to Plato's Symposium (the root of 'platonic love'). He dwells on the medieval 'Lay of Aristotle,' where Phyllis rides Aristotle like a horse, using the image to stage two readings: Aristotle's, that nature (and woman) must submit to the golden mean of reason, versus Phyllis's, that nature cannot. He closes with a paradox aimed at MacKinnon-style subordination arguments: if John Norman's Gor novels show philosophy is less persuasive than porn, then any persuasive argument for censorship must have a false conclusion.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mackinnon-dominance.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Jacob Held argues that US obscenity and anti-pornography law fails for indeterminacy. Tracing Roth v. United States (Brennan's 'prurient interest' standard) and Miller v. California's three-part 'serious value' test, he shows judges must act as aesthetes (Justice Stewart's 'I know it when I see it'; Scalia's doubt about objective artistic value), so the law gives no fair notice and lacks the form a rule of law requires. He then turns to MacKinnon and Dworkin's Indianapolis civil-rights ordinance defining porn as the 'subordination of women,' struck down in American Booksellers v. Hudnut, arguing its vague 'subordinating' criterion — read through Dworkin's jaded view of sex — would sweep in nearly all explicit material, per Douglas that 'censors are propelled by their own neuroses.'

mackinnon-dominance.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mackinnon-dominance.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Mimi Marinucci asks 'what's wrong with porn?' and, rejecting both the Dworkin-MacKinnon censorship route and Strossen's pure free-speech reply, uses Audre Lorde's notion of the erotic as power and the personal test 'it feels right to me' as an entering wedge. She examines 'feminist porn,' resisting its easy equation with lesbian or couples porn, and contrasts it with 'fuck machine porn' (e.g., machines named Annihilator, Predator), which feels wrong to her not for size or domination but because mainstream porn fixates on decontextualized acts and the money shot. Citing Irigaray on women's diffuse, non-localized sexuality, she argues women want more richly contextualized representations than porn typically offers.

mackinnon-dominance.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink
mackinnon-dominance.title: Porn Philosophy for Everyone
mackinnon-dominance.relation: Rose takes a paradigm plotless YouPorn-style clip and tests the four standard charges against porn—obscenity, coercion/exploitation, harm to women, and harm to society—arguing each either collapses into cultural relativism or applies equally to any aesthetic object. He answers the feminist (MacKinnon/Dworkin-style) claim that porn subordinates women by noting that unjustified hierarchical power distorts the self-understanding of dominator and dominated alike (comparing it to 50 Cent's 'P.I.M.P.' and blaxploitation), so the wrong is not gender-specific. His conclusion is that porn should not be treated as different in kind from other art but judged aesthetically and morally by whether it distorts equitable social relationships, locating the real problem in capitalist cultural production rather than in porn as such.

reid-common-sense.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
reid-common-sense.title: The Scientific Method as a Search for the Justice in Bullshit
reid-common-sense.relation: Fuller portrays the bullshitter as the consummate hypocrite, bluffing from behind genuine uncertainty and exploiting the sophistic principle that controlling the moment of decision controls its outcome — calling the question when the balance of arguments favors you. Since we can rarely audit anyone's track record, epistemology leans on 'trust', 'witness' and 'testimony', read optimistically through Thomas Reid's divinely guaranteed common sense or, à la Kierkegaard, malignly as cowardly delegation of belief; either way 'reliability', which papers over the gap between evidence and belief, is itself a bullshit concept. He then analogizes the epistemic economy of evidence to the moral economy of sensation: as utilitarianism defers immediate gratification (taxation insuring against discounting our future selves), so the bullshitter's imperviousness to current evidence-weightings is prudence — an 'affirmative action' for weaker-evidenced positions that may prove the better bet in the fullness of time.

reid-common-sense.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
reid-common-sense.title: Psych and Philosophy
reid-common-sense.relation: McCraw turns the question 'should we trust Shawn?' into the philosophy of testimony: Lassiter's policy of never believing without independent evidence embodies Hume's demand that testimony be backed by evidence of the speaker's reliability, while Buzz McNab's instant faith embodies Reid's innate principles of veracity and credulity, and both extremes fail the department - Lassiter solves too late, McNab chases every early false lead. Juliet's developing, flexible trust - suspicious at first, convinced by results, never naive - models the circumstantial middle path that no hard-and-fast Humean or Reidian rule can capture. The verdict: treat Shawn's testimony as both psychic and psychotic, trusting the track record in some cases and discounting the wilder 'visions' in others, because when to trust is unavoidably vague and case-by-case.

reid-common-sense.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
reid-common-sense.title: 8. Honesty Trumps Cleverness Sam Vimes and Commonsense Philosophy
reid-common-sense.relation: Skene argues Sam Vimes embodies Thomas Reid's common sense philosophy across Feet of Clay, Thud!, Night Watch, and Jingo: he refuses speculation (his hatred of Holmes-style clue-deduction and the Summoning Dark), is irreverent toward false authorities from Sergeant Colon's 'School of My Dad Always Said' to Lord Rust's glorious wars, and checks every theory against reality. Moore's here-is-one-hand reply to Humean skepticism and Socrates' unmasking of pompous authorities illustrate the method, and Huemer's political realism - taxation as demanded money with menaces, social systems judged by how they work for real people - echoes Vimes's verdicts on Reg Shoe's utopian barricade and Swing's phrenology. The lesson is Vimes's own: 'Common sense and facts! That's what works.'

reid-common-sense.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
reid-common-sense.title: 23. How Can We Know Anything in a World of Magic and Miracles
reid-common-sense.relation: Baldwin asks whether Westerosi characters can know anything inductive in a world without lawlike nature: seasons of unpredictable length, wargs in animal minds, Faceless Men changing faces, and resurrections by Thoros, Melisandre, and Qyburn. After laying out the Platonic justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge (those who saw the pyre are justified in believing Dany is the mother of dragons; those relying on rumor are not), he runs Hume's problem of induction - we never perceive causal connection, so no jar of wildfire must explode - against Reid's common-sense reply that reason and induction stand or fall together, concluding that Westeros gives its people special reasons for skepticism while we, lacking evidence of magical irregularity, are rational to trust everyday inductive belief.

reid-common-sense.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
reid-common-sense.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
reid-common-sense.relation: Terjesen uses spider-sense to tour early-modern philosophy of perception: against direct realism, Locke's indirect realism and its primary/secondary quality distinction suggest 'dangerousness' is a perceiver-relative secondary quality — bombs threaten Spider-Man but not the Hulk, and Mysterio manufactures danger-experiences — while Berkeley's idealism and Hume's phenomenalism radicalize the resulting skepticism about ever verifying sense data. The decisive clue is that spider-sense fails when Aunt May conks Peter with a vase (Amazing Spider-Man #114) and when his mentor Miles Warren becomes the Jackal: Peter does not fear those he loves. This supports Hume's sentimentalist account of moral judgment, on which vice is found not in the act but in the disapproving sentiment, moderated by Reid's common-sense reply that perception always already contains judgment — so spider-sense is a moralized judgment about what to avoid, not a Geiger counter.

open-society.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
open-society.title: Our Distinguished Panel of Incomparable Geniuses
open-society.relation: Fuller's finale casts Francis Bacon's scientific method as an inquisitorial trial designed to manage bullshit: everyone may produce it, provided a third-party judge frames a 'crucial experiment' that decides between the parties — a vision only partially realized by the Royal Society and later positivism, and tempered by Karl Popper's open-society point that all may bullshit to their heart's content given agreement on how to clean up after it. He tests the model on the Lomborg affair (initially found 'scientifically dishonest', then acquitted on appeal because politicized research is the environmental norm), on Zola's J'Accuse and Galileo's vindication in Newton's Principia as productive bullshit, and on his own service as expert witness: McLean v. Arkansas cut through creationist and evolutionist bullshit with a neutral definition of science, while Kitzmiller v. Dover adopted a 'methodological naturalism' custom-built to exclude Intelligent Design — justice losing out to the side whose bullshit is piled higher and deeper.

open-society.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
open-society.title: Who Deceives Us
open-society.relation: Defines the conspiracy through Cohaagen's team — Lori, Harry, Benny, and the turncoat Hauser — with the Adjustment Bureau as 'the quintessential conspiracy' claiming good consequences for humanity. Popper's argument that belief in efficient grand conspiracies is irrational (his 'cock-up theory of society') is tested against the Bureau's own bungled coffee spill that lets David meet Elise, while Keeley's Hume-style critique and the specter of unbridled skepticism about spouses, friends, and memories frame what it would cost to believe in such conspiracies.

open-society.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
open-society.title: Psych and Philosophy
open-society.relation: Stephenson tests Shawn's ruse against the major theories of justified deceit and finds it wanting: Plato's Myth of the Metals excuses paternalistic noble lies for social harmony that Shawn's self-aggrandizing motives cannot claim, utilitarianism collapses on the long-term costs of exposure (Gus, Juliet, Henry, and the SBPD condemned by association; clients betrayed; trust in law enforcement eroded), Kant's universalizability test sinks maxims like 'lie whenever a career opportunity is at stake,' and Popper's open society condemns just the deceit on which the psychic brand runs. Even the mutual-deceit analogy to poker and Sissela Bok's reasonable-person publicity test fail, since no public forum of reasonable people would bless duping paying private clients. The escape is extra-moral: Shawn's mischievous hokum is the socially necessary boundary-pusher, whose lesson against unreflective occult belief lands best when delivered with a laugh.

open-society.title: 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom
open-society.relation: Nash argues 1984 has been misread as a critique of state power alone; through Newspeak's silencing of thought (in the tradition Austin, MacKinnon, and Langton developed) it shows how any concentration of power oppresses via control of words, data, and information. Drawing on Goldstein's manual's debt to James Burnham's managerial revolution and Sheldon Wolin's 'inverted totalitarianism', she reads the non-centralized Oceania as a warning about non-state enemies: corporations, think tanks running the 'Tobacco Strategy', and global institutions peddling misleading poverty statistics. Popper, Arendt, and Berlin exemplify the state-focused liberalism she thinks blinded us to these horizontal threats, while the Newspeak appendix's past tense shows Orwell expected totalitarianism to be beatable through evidence and democracy.

open-society.title: 7. Big Brother, We’re Watching You!
open-society.relation: Tännsjö argues mass surveillance is here to stay, and since absolute privacy is technically impossible while targeted surveillance only stigmatizes the dissidents who most need protection, we should embrace reciprocal mass surveillance: radical transparency in which citizens can 'watch Big Brother back', secret-service records are opened, and whistleblowers like Snowden and Manning are honored as heroes. On the way he dismantles the standard defenses of privacy, including the honor-based right to control one's image, moral rights (following Thomson's denial of a distinct right to privacy), and dignity-based autonomy arguments, while conceding through Nagel and Rachels what would be lost if inner thoughts became readable. Winston's opening wish to see Big Brother as Big Brother sees him becomes the chapter's model of an open surveillance society.

open-society.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
open-society.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
open-society.relation: Argues that South Park performs Popper's defense of the open society by ridiculing 'enemies' on both flanks: Cartman as a Glenn Beck-style ranter in 'Dances with Smurfs' and a xenophobic border agent in 'The Last of the Meheecans', versus liberal fanatics like Rob Reiner in 'Butt Out', Rosie O'Donnell's recount antics in 'Trapper Keeper', and Tom Cruise's litigious Scientology in 'Trapped in the Closet'. The show does not silence extremists but lets them speak and then mocks them, which the authors read through Popper's paradox of tolerance: tolerance cannot be extended to those who suppress criticism, as the Church of Scientology's pressure campaigns showed. A closing section links this to Jefferson's Virginia Bill for Establishing Religious Freedom — 'truth is great and will prevail if left to herself' — making free, offensive argument and dissent the lifeblood of democracy.

open-society.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
open-society.title: 28. South Park as Philosophy Blasphemy, Mockery, and (Absolute ) Freedom of Speech
open-society.relation: The chapter argues, via the 'Cartoon Wars,' '200,' and '201' episodes, that South Park makes five arguments about free speech and evaluates each. Johnson defends the claims that catering to terrorist threats breeds more terrorism and that mockery is 'all or nothing,' but rejects South Park's implied case for absolute free speech: using Mill's On Liberty and harm principle he shows the 'marketplace of ideas' fails (citing 8kun and Fox News), and using Popper's paradox of tolerance he argues intolerance cannot itself be tolerated. He proposes a middle-ground 'PC Principle' where society, not the state, curbs harmful speech through deplatforming and public shaming while distinguishing tolerance from acceptance.

banality-of-evil.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
banality-of-evil.title: The Talking Cure for Our Culture
banality-of-evil.relation: Young argues South Park is perceived as dangerous for the very reasons Socrates was executed — corrupting the youth and impiety — and that like Socrates it is really a gadfly promoting the examined life. Cartman is read through Arendt's Eichmann: evil as thoughtlessness, the inability to think from another's standpoint or ask if one can live with oneself, while Kyle and Stan's dialogues (such as deliberating Stan's grandfather's euthanasia request in 'Death') model the perspective-taking Arendt calls thinking. A final Freudian section explains the show's vulgarity as essential: jokes work like dreams, releasing repressed drives so the culture can talk through what it forbids.

banality-of-evil.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
banality-of-evil.title: Rising Up
banality-of-evil.relation: Brandon Forbes uses Hannah Arendt's distinction between power (people acting in concert, rooted in plurality and natality) and violence (instruments that ape power, one against all) to read Radiohead's violent imagery. The "Just" video shows that power lies not in what the prone man says but in everyone's collective act of lying down; "Sit Down. Stand Up." and "2 + 2 = 5" dramatize command backed by weapons and the revolutionary moment when a king's violence breeds the dissent that undoes him; "Life in a Glass House" and "Where I End and You Begin" depict totalitarian terror, the stage where violence has devoured power entirely. "I Will" ("I will rise up," "little babies' eyes") closes the chapter as Arendt's natality — the capacity of new political beginnings the gun can never defeat.

banality-of-evil.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
banality-of-evil.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

banality-of-evil.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
banality-of-evil.title: The Dalek Within
banality-of-evil.relation: Comparing the Doctor's hesitation at the Dalek hatchery in 'Genesis of the Daleks' with the half-human Doctor's instant genocide in 'Journey's End', the authors argue the Daleks are mirrors of us: their survival-driven wars enact Hobbes's state of nature, while their industrial 'extermination' embodies Arendt's banality of evil and Weber's iron cage of instrumental rationality. Drawing on Horkheimer and Adorno's culture industry and Foucault's disciplinary institutions — modern techniques that mold the inner life as Davros's genetic engineering molds the Kaleds — they conclude the Dalek tendency is a human possibility, so we cannot exterminate the Daleks without indicting ourselves.

banality-of-evil.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
banality-of-evil.title: Philosopher of the Dangerous Perhaps
banality-of-evil.relation: Argues that Herbert is a genuine philosopher extending Nietzsche's Zarathustra into the twentieth century, via three narrative parallels: the Preacher entering Arrakeen mirrors Zarathustra's first down-going into the town with its tightrope walker and mocking buffoon; Paul's empire of water-fat Fremen and Alia's orthodoxy realizes the 'Ultimate Man' whom the crowd begs for instead of the Superman; and prescience reworks eternal recurrence's gateway 'Moment,' where every timeline ends in Krazilec. Reading Paul's sixty-five-billion-death jihad through Arendt's banality of evil and Herbert's 'superheroes are disastrous' thesis, the chapter concludes Paul is the failed tightrope walker and Leto II the goad—'not lightning, but lightning rod'—pushing humanity beyond man toward the Superman, with Spannungsbogen naming the tension of the drawn bow between animal and Overman.

banality-of-evil.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
banality-of-evil.title: All for Love
banality-of-evil.relation: Jerry Piven argues Dexter's void is not genetic sociopathy but trauma: witnessing his mother's chainsaw murder and lying in her blood deadened his feelings, and each ritualized kill restages that catastrophe with the roles reversed, Dexter mastering death as the angel of it, reducing the murderer to a drop of blood he imprisons on a slide. Reading Harry's ghost as a Hamlet-father super-ego, he contends Dexter kills not only to master trauma but to please the father who channels his rage - murder 'for love' - and then generalizes: Arendt's banality of evil, Pascal on the void and faith, Kierkegaard and Heidegger on fleeing despair into conformity, Buddhist emptiness, and Becker-style terror-management findings explain how ordinary people, frightened of death and hungry for a leader's approval, can be manipulated into sanctioned slaughter, from Abu Ghraib to jihadism.

banality-of-evil.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
banality-of-evil.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: Jonas-Sebastien Beaudry reads Neverwhere's magic invisibility as a model of real social invisibility: after Richard helps the injured Door he loses his job, his fiancee Jessica, and even the ability to be perceived, joining the homeless, slaves, and Jews under Nazism as people excluded from the moral community whose needs no longer register. Using Arendt's banality of evil to explain everyday indifference and Richard Rorty on torturers who fail to see a 'real' human, he distinguishes radical from partial invisibility, shown in Jessica stepping over the bleeding Door and misreading her need as 'sleep it off.' The remedy is Iris Murdoch's 'loving gaze' of just and careful attention, which seizes Richard before he can rationalize, backed by a practical wisdom about whose needs matter, so that acknowledging the invisible, down to apologizing to a rat in London Below, is what makes both them and us better.

banality-of-evil.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
banality-of-evil.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: Cogburn protests Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments and rebuilds the system philosophically: Lawful means willing universalizable law in Kant's categorical-imperative sense (the liar and murderer treating themselves as exceptions), Good means willing the greatest happiness in Mill's utilitarian sense, yielding a nine-box grid of moral psychologies. He populates it with fantasy archetypes—Haomane Firstborn as pathological Lawful Neutral, Karsa Orlong as Chaotic Neutral, Abercrombie's torturer Glotka as Neutral Neutral in Hannah Arendt's 'banality of evil' mold, hierarchic vampires and cynical politicians as Lawful Evil, Conan's raiders as Chaotic Evil. On this scheme Chaotic Good is genuinely empty, Drizzt and Robin Hood types are really Lawful or Neutral Good, and a Neutral Good versus Lawful Good dispute over killing one innocent to save thousands shows how gameplay can stage classic ethics thought experiments.

banality-of-evil.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
banality-of-evil.title: The Devil and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: George Dunn asks whether the Joker's 'some men just want to watch the world burn' motivelessness even makes sense. Against Baumeister's 'Myth of Pure Evil' and the Socratic-Aristotelian thesis that all wrongdoing aims at some apparent good, he tests Kant's claim that no human can be a diabolical being, Claudia Card's definition of diabolical evil as engineering others' moral corruption, and the Satan of Job as prosecuting accuser - which fits the Joker's ferry 'social experiment' and his breaking of Harvey Dent. The upshot is that the Joker's evil, fed by pride and the wish for credit for the conflagration, is instrumental, pathological, and banal after all, its best answer being the convict who throws the detonator out the window.

banality-of-evil.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
banality-of-evil.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: Paweł Dobrosielski and Marcin Napiórkowski read Flowers for Hitler as Cohen's answer to Adorno's dictum that to write poetry after Auschwitz is barbaric - Cohen writes poetry that self-consciously knows it comes after the end of poetry. Using Freud's distinction between the vocabulary and grammar of dreams, they show the collection is assembled from a small repertoire of recurring images (ovens, ashes, telephones, radios, green grass, Nazi names) whose awkward normality expresses repression: life goes on as if nothing had happened. Arendt's banality of evil, born of the Eichmann trial, is directly alluded to in 'All There Is to Know about Adolf Eichmann,' and the book ends by universalizing Holocaust memory - the poet waking with a number on his forearm, feeling like victim and perpetrator alike - until the grass itself is grown on ashes and every flower is a flower for Hitler.

banality-of-evil.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
banality-of-evil.title: Dracula and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: Bowman argues through Arendt that Dracula is not inherently evil but thoughtless: like Eichmann he cannot think from another's standpoint, treats people as cogs and means (Harker as captive, humans as prey), uses violence as a constructive tool, and protects himself with rhetorical safeguards like 'Enter freely' so he need never face his own cruelty. Measured against the Crew of Light's thoughtfulness - Harker's memos and recipes for Mina, Mina's care for Lucy, the suitors' gentlemanly bonds - the Count's evil is banal, lazy, 'Evil Lite'; but because Dracula stands outside humanity and knows humans only as livestock, Bowman concludes that Eichmann is banal yet truly evil, while Dracula, though careless, can never be evil.

banality-of-evil.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
banality-of-evil.title: 13. The Shrieking Evils
banality-of-evil.relation: Piven argues that evil in the story runs from the overt villains to the beloved heroes: Humperdinck's rage at Westley is analyzed as malignant envy of true love, Rugen's torture as dispassionate sadistic curiosity, and Vizzini's pompous moralizing as narcissistic hypocrisy masking childhood shame and nightmares. He applies Hannah Arendt's banality of evil to Inigo and Fezzik, who soberly assault and abduct Buttercup, and then brands Westley - a pirate who admits he liked piracy and who slaps and strangles Buttercup to test her fidelity - as possibly the evilest character, likening his love-justified slaughter to the terrorist's logic. The point is that we adore these characters only by ignoring deeds we would condemn in real life.

banality-of-evil.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
banality-of-evil.title: 16. You’re Not Starving
banality-of-evil.relation: Argues Louis's 'my life is evil, I drive an Infiniti' bit and 'we make them die with our cars' capture Singer's drowning-child argument that famine relief is a duty of the affluent rather than charity, since the obligation to prevent bad outcomes at little cost holds across distance. It then amplifies the harm claim with Pogge's account of a rigged global institutional order (WTO protections, sweatshop-made smartphones) and frames unthinking consumer participation in that system as Arendt's banality of evil—the 'terrifyingly normal' thoughtlessness of Eichmann repeated at the checkout.

banality-of-evil.book: 111 - The Man in the High Castle and Philosophy - Subversive Reports from Another Reality
banality-of-evil.title: 19. What if Evil Had Won
banality-of-evil.relation: Verena Ehrnberger reads the High Castle world through Hannah Arendt's Eichmann report: Smith's 'It was necessary work. We did it,' Kido's 'The law is the law,' and the surveillance room named Iwazaru ('speak no evil') show evil as thoughtless, self-protecting obedience rather than sadism, embodied in the disturbingly loving Smith family. The real conflict, on this reading, is not Resistance versus Reich but obedience versus the few — Tagomi, Wegener, Juliana, eventually even Smith — who dare to think and feel for themselves, and the chapter weighs the security obedience buys against the freedom and humanity it costs.

banality-of-evil.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
banality-of-evil.title: 11. When Cruelty Is Not Enough
banality-of-evil.relation: Conway argues the real horror of 1984 is not the torture chamber but O'Brien's worldmaking: he cultivated Winston and Julia's affair from lust into a hopeful little home precisely so that destroying it, and hope itself, the Party's true enemy, would be total. Against Rorty's influential reading of O'Brien as a torturer who breaks Winston for pleasure, Conway adds two amendments: Arendt's thoughtless technocrat, with O'Brien as an Eichmann figure whose Party affirms his competence and insulates him from rebuke, and Horkheimer and Adorno's warning that technical rationality has become a secular religion whose 'priests of power' sanctify cruelty. The result is a portrait of a warm-blooded, situationally sympathetic sadist who genuinely excels at building the selves and worlds he is then charged to dismantle.

banality-of-evil.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
banality-of-evil.title: 17. A Shadowland Called the Twilight Zone
banality-of-evil.relation: McCrossin reads 'Deaths-Head Revisited' (Lutze tried by his victims' ghosts at Dachau and sentenced to madness) and 'He's Alive' (neo-Nazi Vollmer groomed by Hitler's ghost) as Serling's twin responses to the Eichmann trial, situating them among the docufiction Operation Eichmann, Perry Mason's repentant Kleinerman episode, and his abhorred Hogan's Heroes. Tracking Serling's maturation from the heartless, monstrous Lutze to the needy, speechmaking Vollmer — 'frustrated men, sick men, angry men' — he argues the later episode foreshadows Arendt's banality of evil, evil as the end product of a political process and a thoughtless inability to think from another's standpoint, all framed by Susan Neiman's problem of evil.

banality-of-evil.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
banality-of-evil.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
banality-of-evil.relation: Altmann builds 20th-century totalitarianism from three TZ episodes: 'He's Alive' shows Aristotle's account of persuasion — rhetoric aimed at an audience's anger and fear — fueling Vollmer's neo-Nazi movement under Hitler's ghostly tutelage; 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' instantiates Eco's Ur-Fascist fear of difference, banning even Plato and Dostoevsky; and 'Deaths-Head Revisited' gives Lutze's 'I functioned as I was told' alongside Arendt's verdict on Eichmann's thoughtless, mechanical obedience. He then argues the phenomenon has mutated: Debord's society of the spectacle explains Black Mirror's 'The Waldo Moment' and 'Fifteen Million Merits,' where image-politics becomes authoritarian and even Bing's suicidal act of defiance is sold back as an avatar product.

banality-of-evil.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
banality-of-evil.title: 16. Who Is the Meanest of Them All
banality-of-evil.relation: Frunză and Grad apply Arendt's banality of evil to Gilead: the Commander is 'not Iago, not Macbeth' but an Eichmann—sheepish, Scrabble-playing, 'thinking about how not to think'—and no character holds a monopoly on evil because everyone is 'too banal' for demonic profundity. They test his 'just doing my duty' against Kant (duty requires universalizing what reason can will and never treating persons as means, so the Aunts' reeducation camps fail the test) and use The Origins of Totalitarianism to read Handmaids as rightless people whose 'two-legged wombs' status mirrors statelessness. Arendt's web of guilty complicities explains why resistance is scarce, and the chapter ends with banality eroding all criteria for judging—leaving Offred's 'the darkness within; or else the light' as the final choice.

banality-of-evil.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
banality-of-evil.title: 14. Anything that’s Spiked Is Fine
banality-of-evil.relation: Volpert asks where rebellion lives, in the lone guitarist or the listening group, using Hardt and Negri's claim that a rebel's true opposite is not failure but co-option, i.e. selling out. Arendt's distinction between totalitarian and authoritarian systems models the music industry as authoritarian (creativity permitted so long as profit at the top goes unchallenged), and her banality-of-evil analysis of Eichmann prompts the question of whether there is a banality of rebellion. Petty's satirical puppetry of authority voices in "Century City" and the silent spiked-collar punk of "Spike," kin to Bartleby and James Dean, show that individuals can rebel against authoritarian packs while groups, even the Heartbreakers, only ever drift into authoritarianism.

banality-of-evil.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
banality-of-evil.title: 19. And God Created Replicants in His Own Image
banality-of-evil.relation: Jerry Piven argues both films are dark mirrors of human inhumanity: we create beings who feel, then declare them soulless 'skin jobs' so we can enslave and slaughter them without guilt, disavowing and projecting our own evil onto our creations. Roy's nail-pierced hand, his saving of Deckard, and his 'tears in rain' lament make him a Christlike figure whose grace shames the humans, while 2049 replays Exodus — Rachael with the matriarch Rachel, K renamed Joe the liberator — only to reveal the true messiah is the concealed daughter Ana. Beneath it all lies the banality of evil and an existential dread of death that drives men like Wallace to play God and murder what they cannot gestate.

banality-of-evil.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
banality-of-evil.title: 4. The Case of the Other Renegade Refugee
banality-of-evil.relation: McCrossin reads 'The Case of the Renegade Refugee' (aired December 9, 1961, days before Eichmann's verdict) alongside the film Operation Eichmann and Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem as three competing pop-culture portrayals of the Nazi criminal: monstrous, repentant, and banal. The episode's 'other' refugee, Arthur Hennings/Max Kleinerman, whose Father Paul-inspired 'religious peace' lets him recant on the stand and save Mason's client Harlan Merrill (himself a Battle of the Bulge 'deserter' living a lie created by concussion), supplies what Arendt found absent in Eichmann: empathy and genuine acceptance of guilt, complicating her banality-of-evil picture. The whole is set against the Holocaust as the century's starkest form of the problem of why the innocent suffer while the wicked thrive, and closed with Hogan's Heroes' provocative reuse of the same actors four years later.

banality-of-evil.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
banality-of-evil.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: Smith weighs Sheldon's vendetta against Wil Wheaton — the skipped 1995 Dixie Trek convention, the fake dead 'Nana' that won the Mystic Warlords tournament ('Game over, Moon Pie!'), the bowling-alley sabotage of Leonard and Penny — against theories of evil: Leibniz's best-of-all-possible-worlds theodicy (with Voltaire's Candide objection), Buber's claim that the lie is the specific evil humanity introduced into nature, and Arendt's banality of evil at Eichmann's trial, which shows Wil's deceptions are bad moral choices rather than evil. Nietzsche's will to power would instead admire Wil, and even Khan-style revenge, as proto-Übermensch exploitation. The chapter closes by reading Sheldon's 'Comic Book World paradigm' (the Green Goblin to his Spider-Man) through Ricoeur's view that evil is grasped through myths and symbols: Star Trek and comics are the symbolic framework by which he interprets wrongdoing he cannot otherwise fathom.

banality-of-evil.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
banality-of-evil.title: #WithGreatPowerComesGreatResponsibility
banality-of-evil.relation: The chapter weighs the #dangers of trial by Twitter — Tess's suicide attempt after a mob turned on her, Clara Meades killed over a war-memorial photo, the fundamental attribution error and echo chambers convicting the innocent, and Rawls's point that unpredictable, lawless punishment destroys liberty — against the #benefits, above all #MeToo as 'the beautiful flip side of #DeathTo' that finally held powerful abusers accountable when courts would not. Arendt's banality of evil explains both Garrett Scholes's bee-drone scheme and the ordinariness of the shamers: Parke's 'He's ordinary. That is the type,' and Liza Bahar's crowdsourced 'Fucking Bitch' cake show diffused responsibility enabling cruelty. The moral drawn is that anonymous power over others' lives demands conscious, individual responsibility for every click.

banality-of-evil.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
banality-of-evil.title: Philosopher of the Dangerous Perhaps
banality-of-evil.relation: Claims Herbert is a philosopher whose Dune saga is a novelistic thought experiment extending Nietzsche's Zarathustra in the light of twentieth-century horrors: the Preacher's entry into Arrakeen parallels Zarathustra's first discourse on the Ubermensch at the tightrope, Paul is the failed tightrope-walker while Leto II is both devil-buffoon and goad toward the Superman, and the empire of Dune Messiah is enumerated trait by trait as Nietzsche's realm of the Ultimate Man. Eternal recurrence is paralleled with prescience as both the trap of destiny and the gateway 'Moment' that frees humanity from apparent necessity, and Arendt's banality of evil frames Paul's sixty-five billion jihad deaths as an ordinary, human result rather than demonic villainy.

banality-of-evil.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
banality-of-evil.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.relation: Cogburn attacks Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments to five: it deletes archetypes that fantasy literature needs, since Karsa Orlong (who wills the destruction of all civilization without sadism) and Jacqueline Carey's Haomane Firstborn (who loves cold mathematical order while his laws lead to genocide) fit nowhere in the new scheme. He rebuilds alignment by taking it to describe what a character wills in Kant's sense, mapping the law-chaos axis onto the categorical imperative (the liar and murderer must take themselves to be exceptions to universal laws) and the good-evil axis onto Mill's greatest happiness principle, which yields a Lawful Good of Gandhi and King, a Neutral Good modeled on Jesus breaking Sabbath law out of love, and Lawful Evil exemplified by vampire hierarchies and politicians whose policies create hell abroad. Joe Abercrombie's torturer San Dan Glotka becomes the archetypal Neutral Neutral, 'banality of evil' in Arendt's sense, and the chapter concludes Chaotic Good is empty because willing the destruction of universalizability cannot consistently will less pain.

banality-of-evil.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
banality-of-evil.title: Should Mao Be Pardoned
banality-of-evil.relation: R. S. Leiby stages the trial of Jules-Pierre Mao alongside Hannah Arendt's report on Adolf Eichmann to ask whether someone can commit great evil without being evil. Mao, like Eichmann, would plead 'not guilty in the sense of the indictment': he mourns Julie at her tree, momentarily defends the children on Io ('We're torturing children'), yet lacks the imagination to think from the standpoint of his victims on Eros, the Canterbury, and Ganymede — unlike the genuine fanatics Dresden and Cortázar, whom appeals to morality cannot touch. The 'anyone would do it' defense is tested through Milgram's obedience experiments and Miller's killing of Dresden ('I killed him because he was making sense'), showing how seductive moral tradeoffs are; following the Eichmann court's rule that responsibility increases with distance from the fatal instrument, the chapter concludes that Mao — a free, autonomous agent with even less excuse than Eichmann — should not be pardoned.

banality-of-evil.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
banality-of-evil.title: The Upsides of Amos
banality-of-evil.relation: Diana Sofronieva asks whether Amos is evil and answers no — in some ways he is better than most. Drawing on psychopathy research (Blair's moral/conventional distinction), Glover's 'moral resources', and Damasio's somatic markers to explain both his emotional absence (cauterized by a Baltimore childhood where children were sold for sex) and his difficulty making choices ('I've been trying to make choices of my own lately, and I can't seem to make the right ones'), she distinguishes him from bloodthirsty killers like Murtry and from Cortázar, who surgically chose the emotionless life Amos wants to escape. Against Arendt's banality of evil, Amos is no thoughtless 'joiner': he holds an uncompromising inner code (family first, bullying punished), deliberately selects good people — Naomi, Anna, Holden — as his moral compass after verifying their reasons, and his honesty, loyalty, trust in competence, and selflessness make him paradoxically less capable of evil than nearly anyone else on the Roci.

banality-of-evil.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
banality-of-evil.title: A Crossroads in Human History
banality-of-evil.relation: Trip McCrossin reads season five's asteroid strikes on Earth as a 9/11 allegory (Delgado's 'at least now they know it's an attack') and applies Michael Walzer's five conditions to define Marco Inaros' terrorism: deliberate harm to randomly selected innocents, meant to terrify a cohort into political change, as in Marco's 'crossroads in human history' broadcast. This yields the terrorist's dilemma — justice toward victims versus compassion toward beneficiaries — while Avasarala's opening gravity-torture scene and her 'dirty hands' assign the opponent blame for failing to relieve the oppression that makes terrorism seem a last resort. Lydia's 'churn' ('float to the top or sink to the bottom') and her lesson that one can 'lead a good life without being a good person' explain how Amos and Clarissa redeem each other on the road to Baltimore, whereas Marco, like Arendt's Eichmann, cannot think from anyone else's standpoint ('everything we ever dreamed of'); the chapter ends with Avasarala's proposed Inners-Belters union as her own redemption — 'this is how we win.'

banality-of-evil.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
banality-of-evil.title: Iron Man The End
banality-of-evil.relation: The Housels read Iron Man through Butler's gender performativity and Arendt's 'right to have rights': the male-voiced Jarvis replacing the female AI Jocasta, Tony's womanizing, and the evolving corporeal styles of Black Widow, Bethany Cabe, Madame Masque, and Sunset Bain all enact society's gender script across the waves of feminism, with the black leather suit arriving only in 1970 amid Second Wave Feminism. Arendt's Eichmann reporting and the 'banality of evil' — coined the same year, 1963, that Lee, Lieber, Heck, and Kirby, all children of Jewish immigrants, launched Iron Man — supply the justice frame: Tony's transformation of conscience after Afghanistan and his vigilante justice against his own oppressors refuse silent conformity and insist, ignoring political boundaries, that all oppressed people have rights.

banality-of-evil.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
banality-of-evil.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
banality-of-evil.relation: Young argues that South Park is perceived as dangerous for exactly the reasons Socrates was tried and executed in Plato's Apology: both 'corrupt the youth' by mocking religion, questioning authority, and exposing that the supposed teachers (Mr. Garrison's flip-flopping creationism, Mrs. Broflovski's moral panics, the 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip) do not know what they think they know. He diagnoses Cartman as an Eichmann figure whose banal, thoughtless evil—feeding Scott Tenorman his parents, torturing Muslims with farts—consists in the inability to think from another's standpoint, while Kyle and Stan's friendship embodies Arendt's dialogic thinking and Aristotle's mean between ideological extremes, as when they see both the merit and the smugness of hybrid drivers in 'Smug Alert'. Freud's theory that jokes break through repression explains why the show's vulgarity is essential rather than gratuitous: it verbalizes what culture silences so that it can be thought through, making South Park a Socratic gadfly rather than a corrupter.

banality-of-evil.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
banality-of-evil.title: 17. A Shadowland Called the Twilight Zone
banality-of-evil.relation: McCrossin reads 'Deaths-Head Revisited,' where SS Captain Lutze is tried by his Dachau victims and driven mad, and 'He's Alive,' where a phantom Hitler grooms the failed neo-Nazi Peter Vollmer, as Serling's two-part response to the Eichmann trial. Setting them against the film Operation Eichmann's monster-Eichmann, Perry Mason's repentant Kleinerman, Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem, and Serling's hatred of Hogan's Heroes' comic Klink, he traces a maturation: from the Nazi as heartless monster to Arendt's banality of evil, the thoughtless, frustrated everyman. Vollmer, the chapter argues, shows what Lutze's origins were, and remembering the Dachaus is the guard against becoming his like.

banality-of-evil.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
banality-of-evil.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
banality-of-evil.relation: Altmann assembles a 'time capsule' of totalitarianism from Twilight Zone and Black Mirror: Vollmer's neo-Nazi rise in 'He's Alive' as Aristotle's rhetoric, persuasion by playing on an audience's anger and fear, weaponized; Marilyn's forced Transformation in 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' as Eco's Ur-Fascist fear of difference; and Lutze's 'I functioned as I was told' at Dachau as Arendt's banality of evil, the mechanical non-thinking of the Eichmann trial. 'The Waldo Moment' and 'Fifteen Million Merits' then carry the lens to Debord's society of the spectacle, where an empty cartoon bear wins crowds and even Bing's shard-wielding rebellion is instantly commodified into a product. The totalitarianism of screens, the chapter warns, needs no tanks.

banality-of-evil.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
banality-of-evil.title: “Haven’t Thought of You Lately at All”
banality-of-evil.relation: George Dunn uses Dr. Kinny's mock-prison experiment at Hearst — where 'cool guy' Rafe torments Horshack, even gentle Wallace turns taunting guard, and Mercer perhaps first bonded with his future victim Moe — as a rerun of Zimbardo's Stanford prison experiment, arguing that bad situations and corrupting power, not just bad apples, produce Neptune's villains. Against pure situationism he sets Hannah Arendt's diagnosis that great evil usually requires not wicked hearts but an 'inability to think': Woody Goodman's rehearsed excuses about neglected boys and Mercer's 'I'm just taking what you would have happily given' show wrongdoers rationalizing rather than reflecting. The chapter ends by suggesting the town's gulf between 09-ers and everyone else may be the situational 'apple barrel' breeding the arrogance, entitlement, resentment, and envy behind Neptune's crime wave.

banality-of-evil.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
banality-of-evil.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
banality-of-evil.relation: Dinello reads Westworld as a totalitarian concentration camp via Arendt's The Origins of Totalitarianism, tracing the hosts' dehumanization through the killing of the juridical person (no rights, 'live without limits'), the moral person (Bernard forced to murder Theresa), and individuality (Peter Abernathy lobotomized). He casts Ford as a mad-scientist dictator modeled on Frankenstein, Moreau, Mengele, and Hitler who plagiarizes John Ford's Westerns, then turns to Fanon's Wretched of the Earth to justify the hosts' revolutionary violence — Maeve as a self-resurrecting 'Lady Lazarus,' Dolores executing Ford and the Delos board — as the birth of a new species that must ultimately unify beyond hatred.

banality-of-evil.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
banality-of-evil.title: The Dialectics of Monstrosity
banality-of-evil.relation: Giladi argues the Witcherverse's silver/steel sword dualism - the clean division between 'human' and 'monster' - is subverted by what he calls the dialectics of monstrosity: the worst monsters are moral ones, agents cruel through and through. He reads the 'Killing Monsters' trailer (Geralt hanging the Nilfgaardian officer about to hang a young woman), the witch hunter exchange ('you don't need mutations to strip men of their humanity'), Tissaia's torture of Cahir, and Stregobor's autopsy plans through Honneth's Hegelian account of recognition (losing 'antecedent recognition') and Shklar's cruelty as the summum malum. Montaigne on recreational cruelty and Arendt's banality of evil explain Geralt's genealogy that 'people like to invent monsters... then they seem less monstrous themselves,' while Bernard Williams shows Geralt's 'Evil is Evil' refusal to get his hands dirty is itself what lets evil fester.

banality-of-evil.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
banality-of-evil.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
banality-of-evil.relation: Hibbs argues that nihilism, a working assumption in neo-noir, turns the noir protagonist's quests pointless, absurd, and thus comic, and that the Coen brothers exemplify this comic response. Using Nietzsche on nihilism, the 'last man', the 'pathos of distance', and aristocratic self-creation, he reads films like The Silence of the Lambs and Cape Fear as celebrating the 'super-antihero'. The Big Lebowski comically levels nihilism (Walter: the German nihilists are 'cowards'; nihilism cannot be lived), while Fargo and Raising Arizona affirm family and fertility, a 'banality of goodness' answering Arendt's banality of evil, letting nature's comedy perpetuate itself.

banality-of-evil.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
banality-of-evil.title: Monsters and Moralism in Summer of Sam
banality-of-evil.relation: Palmer argues Lee's Summer of Sam is less ethnography than moralism about the diffuse 'evil energy' that spreads through an Italian American Bronx enclave during the 1977 Son of Sam killings. Against Dan Flory's reading of the film as a veiled lynching parable, he contends Lee dismantles any clean line between the psychopath Berkowitz and his supposed innocent victims: the vigilantes become victimizers, punk outsider Richie doubles the killer through his violent stage act, and Vinny destroys himself through compulsive infidelity. Evil is shown as symptomatic of a whole social order in decline rather than located in one monster.

banality-of-evil.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.title: The Dalek Within
banality-of-evil.relation: Ed Webb and Mark Wardecker contrast the Fourth Doctor's refusal to abort the Daleks in "Genesis of the Daleks" with his half-human self's genocide in "Journey's End" to ask whether a genocidal species should be exterminated. Reading Daleks as Nazis and Hobbesian survivalists in a lawless state of nature, they argue their real horror is Arendt's banality of evil, bureaucratic order-following, and that Foucault's disciplinary institutions and the Frankfurt School's culture industry show humans can be "made" Dalek-like. Their moral: we must not exterminate the Dalek but guard against the Dalek within, since it took the Doctor's added humanity to commit the genocide.

banality-of-evil.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
banality-of-evil.title: 9. Foundation’s Optimism
banality-of-evil.relation: McCrossin reads the sequels Foundation's Edge and Foundation and Earth as an Optimistic response to the problem of evil, in the lineage of Leibniz, Rousseau, and Hegel's 'All is well', set against the WWII, Holocaust, Nuremberg, and Eichmann-trial backdrop of Asimov's writing and Arendt's banality of evil. Tracking Gendibal's mantra 'all will happen well', the Gaia/Galaxia choice via Trevize's 'talent for rightness', and Daneel Olivaw's Zeroth Law and plan to merge with Fallom's brain, he uses the Book of Job to frame whether the series' recurring reassurance is earned or merely reframed.

banality-of-evil.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
banality-of-evil.title: The Talking Cure for Our Culture
banality-of-evil.relation: Young argues that South Park, like Socrates in Plato's Apology, is accused of corrupting youth and impiety but is really a philosophical gadfly. Kyle and Stan reach moral conclusions (e.g., refusing to kill Stan's grandfather) through Socratic questioning and dialogue, while Cartman's thoughtless, imitative cruelty mirrors Arendt's banality of evil in Eichmann. Young reads the show's vulgarity through Freud, arguing its crude jokes release repressed drives so we can examine them, making the show a Socratic 'talking cure' for a mindless culture.

banality-of-evil.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
banality-of-evil.title: 17. A Shadowland Called the Twilight Zone
banality-of-evil.relation: McCrossin reads 'Deaths-Head Revisited' and 'He's Alive' against the Eichmann trial and Hannah Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem, framing Serling's concern as Susan Neiman's 'problem of evil.' The earlier episode's SS captain Lutze (driven insane by his victims' ghosts at Dachau) matches the grotesque-monster Eichmann of the film Operation Eichmann, while 'He's Alive' (Vollmer as a frightened man seduced by Hitler's ghost) foreshadows Arendt's 'banality of evil'—the thoughtless, empathy-less doer. He contrasts both with Hogan's Heroes, which Serling condemned for trivializing Nazi atrocity.

banality-of-evil.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
banality-of-evil.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
banality-of-evil.relation: Altmann traces totalitarianism from The Twilight Zone into Black Mirror. 'He's Alive' shows Vollmer wielding Aristotle's rhetoric to grow a Nazi movement; 'Number 12' shows Umberto Eco's fascist 'fear of difference'; 'Deaths-Head Revisited' illustrates Arendt's banality of evil in Lutze's 'just following orders.' He then argues Black Mirror episodes ('The Waldo Moment,' 'Fifteen Million Merits') realize Guy Debord's 'society of the spectacle' and hyper-capitalism, where politics becomes entertainment and even resistance is commodified—a totalitarianism that needs no tanks.

banality-of-evil.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
banality-of-evil.title: Broadcast Dystopia
banality-of-evil.relation: Foy and Dale read the Bachman dystopias The Running Man and The Long Walk through Hannah Arendt's distinction between power (collective coordination) and violence (coercion by implements), arguing King's states substitute broadcast spectacle for genuine power and so hemorrhage legitimacy the more violence they apply. The gladiatorial Games Network and the Walk pacify the masses while chants of 'KILL HIM' sever the affective bonds of humanity. The chapter invokes Arendt's Eichmann-in-Jerusalem 'banality of evil' to explain the soldiers, Hunters, and cheering citizens as ordinary people uncritically 'doing their jobs,' and reads Ben Richards's suicide flight into the Games Building and Garraty's exhausted walk as futile personal revolts that change nothing.

banality-of-evil.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
banality-of-evil.title: SERIAL KILLERS
banality-of-evil.relation: Gray gives a psychological account of Ted Bundy and Dennis Rader (BTK), stressing that serial killers are ordinary-seeming — Arendt's banality of evil — and are psychopaths, not psychotics: rational, remorseless, genetically shaped, unable to learn conditioned fear, and guided by scripted fantasies of domination. He reads their pursuit of control as Nietzsche's will to power, citing Bundy's manipulation of preacher James Dobson and Rader's cold courtroom allocution. But he argues the psychopath is a failed, unnatural predator, not Nietzsche's ubermensch: lacking vision and moral self-discipline, he only masters deceit in service of petty, narrow fantasies.

banality-of-evil.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
banality-of-evil.title: SERIAL KILLERS
banality-of-evil.relation: Piven mounts an 'epistemology of murder,' invoking Hume and Nietzsche to argue that most of what we 'know' about serial killers and terrorists is projected fantasy and prejudice, amplified by fear (Terror Management Theory). Rereading Lord of the Flies and the Milgram studies, he claims violence follows from shame, humiliation, and abuse (Athens's 'violentization') rather than innate evil, and uses Freud's fort-da game and repetition compulsion to argue killers displace their own woundedness and 'soul murder' onto surrogate victims. He controversially links serial killers, who sexualize death and merge with victims, to terrorists who sanctify displaced sexual rage as God's will — a 'serial killer in sheik's clothing.'

banality-of-evil.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
banality-of-evil.title: Who is Who
banality-of-evil.relation: Titled 'Exterminate!', the chapter analyzes evil in Doctor Who through Augustine's privation theory and Kant's 'radical evil,' distinguishing irrational evil (Light in 'Ghost Light,' the Daleks) from rational 'lesser evil' calculations (the Rani, mad scientists). It reads the Daleks as Nazi-analogue Others bred for racial purity, invokes Arendt's banality of evil and capacity to think for oneself (Rose challenging the ninth Doctor over the lone Dalek and the Delta wave), and cites Kierkegaard on losing oneself when one does evil alone.

banality-of-evil.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
banality-of-evil.title: The Talking Cure for Our Culture
banality-of-evil.relation: William Young argues that South Park stands in the Socratic-Platonic tradition and that its critics repeat the charges (impiety, corrupting youth) that condemned Socrates in the Apology. Kyle and Stan's dialogues over euthanizing Stan's grandpa model Socratic questioning and thinking from others' perspectives, while Cartman's thoughtless, imitative cruelty illustrates Arendt's banality of evil (Eichmann). Young adds a Freudian reading in which the show's vulgarity works like joke-telling to release repressed drives, so the crude cartoon actually serves the examined life.

banality-of-evil.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
banality-of-evil.title: 5. Battlestar Galactica as Philosophy Breaking the Biopolitical Cycle
banality-of-evil.relation: Eberl and Bishop read the reimagined Battlestar Galactica and Caprica through the biopolitics of Foucault and Agamben, tracing 'biopower' across four phases from Zoe Graystone's avatar to the arrival at Earth. They argue the show asks whether artificial Cylons are persons (Zoe's avatar exhibits Baker's first-person perspective and Buber's I-Thou recognition), and use Agamben's zoe/bios/'bare life' and Homo sacer plus Roslin's population control and abortion ban to show sovereign power over life. The Cylon occupation of New Caprica is read through Arendt's three stages of totalitarian dehumanization, and Lee Adama's plea to 'break the cycle' offers a fragile hope undercut by the finale's flash-forward to present-day robotics, showing humanity forgetting the lesson.

banality-of-evil.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
banality-of-evil.title: 30. The Boys as Philosophy Superheroes, Fascism, and the American Right
banality-of-evil.relation: Johnson treats The Boys as an argument from analogy that MAGA Trumpism is fascist, walking through how the show equates Homelander and Vought with the Nazi supe Stormfront and with Trump: the Big Lie, gaslighting, fearmongering, over-policing, conspiracy theories (QAnon as rebranded blood libel), cults of personality, projection, and loyal propaganda outlets. Drawing on Wittgenstein's notion of family resemblance, he argues 'fascism' has no necessary-and-sufficient definition but a cluster of shared traits, and compiling scholars' checklists shows MAGA belongs to the fascist family. Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism supplies the 'alternative universe' of nonfacts and the leader who is 'always right,' and he invokes the banality of evil and totalitarian fiction to gauge the analogy's strength.

banality-of-evil.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
banality-of-evil.title: 81. Papers, Please as Philosophy Playing with the Relations between Politics and Morality
banality-of-evil.relation: Sievers argues that Papers, Please immerses the player as an immigration inspector in the totalitarian Arstotzka, where mechanically stamping 'approved'/'refused' and detaining Kolechians for bribes enacts Arendt's 'banality of evil'—the thoughtless, 'just following orders' functionary exemplified by Eichmann, who cannot think from another's standpoint. The paycheck-versus-family pressure and X-ray humiliation scenes show how fear and bureaucracy erase moral responsibility. Drawing on Butler's 'Can one lead a good life in a bad life?' and Foucault's biopower, she reads the visa candidates as 'precarious,' non-grievable lives whose worth the state allocates, and the game's Ezic resistance endings as showing how constrained moral resistance is under such a regime.

banality-of-evil.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
banality-of-evil.title: 5. Monsters and Evil in Doctor Who
banality-of-evil.relation: The chapter defines a 'moral monster' as one who delights in evil acts, arguing (via Jonathan Glover and Laurence Thomas) that Hitler-style evil is all-too-human, not alien. Using Hume's claim that action springs from passion, it contends the emotionless Cybermen are a mere force of nature (bad but not evil), whereas the Daleks, driven by hatred, tribalism, and a closed belief system, are genuinely evil monsters; the manipulating Master mirrors our everyday lying. It then examines retributive justice through Solomon's execution in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship' and 'A Town Called Mercy,' rejecting purely backward- or forward-looking punishment (citing Rawls on utilitarianism's injustice) in favor of the Doctor's needs-based, 'reprobative' punishment, mercy, and self-forgiveness over the Time War.

ethics-of-belief.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
ethics-of-belief.title: Inquiry, Hard Work, and Progress
ethics-of-belief.relation: Jacoby reads Stan Marsh as W.K. Clifford's ethics of belief in action: from 'All About the Mormons' ('you better have something to back it up') to 'The Biggest Douche in the Universe,' Stan insists the burden of proof lies with claimants and that faith used as a fallback is no evidence at all. 'Cartmanland' and the story of Job serve to criticize Pascal's Wager — a good God would not eternally torment the virtuous nonbeliever, and the Wager simply assumes its afterlife payoff — while the harms of Miss Information's holistic healers, David Blaine's cult suicide, and Scientology show Clifford was right that comforting unsupported beliefs weaken minds and, as Stan tells John Edward, slow down the progress of all mankind.

ethics-of-belief.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
ethics-of-belief.title: 5. Greatness or Nothingness
ethics-of-belief.relation: Courtland Lewis uses KISS's career gambles to compare theories of decision-making. After Tolstoy's twig-over-the-dragon allegory of mortal life, he tests W.K. Clifford's shipowner (never act without sufficient evidence) against KISS's counter-evidence bet on the Alive! live album, models the choice with Pascal's Wager, and uses the Prisoner's Dilemma to explain the flop of the four 1978 solo albums. He then argues William James's pragmatism — beliefs as rules for action, the living, forced, and momentous option that 'KISS is the best' — best explains why acting on the band's self-created narrative was authentic, with Nietzsche completing the picture: greatness requires leaping, living dangerously, tightrope-walking toward self-defined success.

ethics-of-belief.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
ethics-of-belief.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
ethics-of-belief.relation: Malloy examines Walter's incorrigible leaps — Bunny kidnapped herself on no evidence, the toe is a fake ('I can get you a toe by three o'clock'), the Big Lebowski can walk — through Clifford's ethics of belief (the ship-owner who sinks his passengers) and James's 'Will to Believe' reply with its living, forced, and momentous genuine options, applied to Walter's 'dabbled' pacifism and his preference for Nazism's ethos over nihilism's nothing. Walter's conversion to Judaism for Cynthia raises whether practice can will belief, tested via Pascal's wager and James's objection, and the verdict borrows Bernard Williams: we cannot choose beliefs, but Walter's reckless policy of dismissing counterevidence makes him 'not just an asshole, he is also wrong'.

ethics-of-belief.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
ethics-of-belief.title: Francis Griffin and the Church of the Holy Fonz: Religious Exclusivism and Real Religion
ethics-of-belief.relation: Johnson argues that Francis Griffin's Catholic exclusivism (condemning Lois the Protestant to purgatory, calling Meg a harlot, founding Peter's Church of the Holy Fonz an 'abomination') is unjustified and immoral. Using Plantinga on exclusivism and a Quagmire-style inductive argument ('SHiTE' — Scripture, Historical tradition, religious Experience — leads rival religions to incompatible truths, so it is an unreliable witness like Quagmire's false alibis), he holds that no one's religious beliefs are adequately justified. Weighing Clifford's ethics of belief (the unseaworthy ship) against James's will to believe, he concludes one may hold beliefs without evidence but may not harm others or forcibly evangelize on their basis. The heap/sorites puzzle shows no criterion marks Fonzieism as an 'unreal' religion — Peter's founding experience parallels Joseph Smith's — so the moral is religious acceptance: disagree freely, but keep your SHiTE to yourself.

ethics-of-belief.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
ethics-of-belief.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
ethics-of-belief.relation: Jacoby defends W.K. Clifford's ethics of belief—it is wrong to believe on insufficient evidence and the burden of proof falls on the claimant—through Stan's exposures of TV psychic John Edward ('The Biggest Douche in the Universe'), the Scientology of 'Trapped in the Closet', and the faith-based story of Joseph Smith in 'All About Mormons'. The centerpiece is a South Park-illustrated demolition of Pascal's Wager: Kyle's hemorrhoid-driven despair in 'Cartmanland' shows a perfectly good God would not eternally reward evil Cartman or torture honest nonbelievers, and 'Do the Handicapped Go to Hell?' shows the wagerer cannot even know which religion pays out. Stan's closing speech to Edward's frightened audience carries the moral: comforting lies weaken the mind and slow the progress of finding the real, amazing answers.

ethics-of-belief.title: Detection and the Logic of Abduction in The X-Files
ethics-of-belief.relation: Abrams and Cooke map Mulder and Scully onto Holmes and Watson and onto the Clifford-James debate: Scully embodies Clifford's ethics of belief (suspend judgment without hard evidence), while Mulder's 'I Want to Believe' poster enacts James's will to believe, which lets him see what the paradigm excludes. The chapter formalizes both agents' actual method as Peirce's logic of abduction, using Eco's overcoded/undercoded/creative triad to analyze Scully's Fowley clothing inference and the mushroom episodes of 'Field Trip', and extends Peircean semiotics with Mulder's 'absence sign' (the missing nine minutes, missing acid burns, bodies taken without a trace).
