Kuhn's normal science versus revolution explains why Scully stays inside the FBI's paradigm while Mulder's passion makes him the revolutionary who, with Scully as error-corrector, fuses into a single 'whole person' detective facing the limits of reason.

ethics-of-belief.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ethics-of-belief.title: 29. Frank Herbert’s Dune as Philosophy The Need to Think for Yourself
ethics-of-belief.relation: Reading the Sci Fi Channel miniseries Frank Herbert's Dune and Children of Dune, Littmann argues the saga warns against letting leaders or religions think for us: Paul Atreides fakes being the Fremen Mahdi, wages a holy war, and founds a theocratic tyranny that Alia and Leto II carry to worse extremes. He sets Plato's Republic (the guardian class, the noble lie, rule by the wise) and Hobbes against pro-democracy thinkers—Locke's consent and natural rights, Mill's harm principle, Dewey's democracy—then cites Locke, Paine and Russell on religion's dangers, closing with W.K. Clifford's 'ethics of belief' that one must not accept religious claims without sufficient evidence. The chapter reads Paul's dictatorship and the Bene Gesserit's engineered messiah as dramatizations of the historical abuses of concentrated and religious power.

reliabilism.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
reliabilism.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
reliabilism.relation: Silverman uses Adama's 'true lie' about Earth to motivate the Gettier problem: Starbuck's belief that Earth exists is true and justified by Adama's testimony, yet because that testimony is a lie, her justified true belief is not knowledge — just as Helo's true belief that the woman before him is 'Sharon' rests on mistaking Boomer for Athena. Goldman's reliabilism then questions whether sight, memory, and testimony are reliable belief-formers in a world of humanoid Cylons, weighing Hume's suspicion of testimony against Plantinga's defense of it. Finally Clifford's evidentialism is set against James's will to believe: the Colonials' forced, momentous choice to seek Earth shows that in an uncertain world pragmatic belief can be reasonable — 'so say we all.'

reliabilism.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
reliabilism.title: More than a Feeling
reliabilism.relation: Rachel Robison-Greene asks whether Dexter's rule to 'be sure' actually gives him knowledge of his victims' guilt. Distinguishing Cartesian certainty - skeptical hypotheses about deceiving senses, dreams and evil demons, echoing The Matrix - from mere felt certainty, she tests the belief-truth-justification analysis of knowledge traced to Plato against the show: LaGuerta's witness theory fails on belief, Deb's conviction that Neil Perry is the Ice Truck Killer fails on truth, and Astor's accusation of Dexter fails on justification. Neither strong internalism (Dexter straps down Jamie Jaworski without knowing how the murder was done), weak internalism, coherence theory (his false but coherent case against Jonathan Farrow), nor reliabilism (his spidey-sense is explicitly not sufficient by his own admission) captures his practice, so his 'certainty' is just a feeling - and the people on his table may include ones he does not know to be guilty.

reliabilism.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
reliabilism.title: Education never ends Watson. It is a series of lessons with the greatest for
reliabilism.relation: J. Solomon Johnson asks whether Holmes's conclusions are knowledge or luck, walking through justified true belief with a Holmesian Gettier case (Watson rightly believing the killer was a former ship hand for the wrong reason), Moore's proof that knowledge entails belief, and Russell's stopped clock as an unsafe belief. BBC Sherlock's fake Vermeer and the 2009 film's 'resurrected' Lord Blackwood illustrate beliefs that fail safety or sensitivity across nearby possible worlds, while 'The Stock-Broker's Clerk' shows Holmes's observation of the scorched slippers making his belief sensitive. The verdict: Holmes is justified by the track record of his own expert methods, a professional billiards player rather than a beginner's-luck fluke, though real-world imitators could never rule out enough alternatives to match him.

reliabilism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
reliabilism.title: Philip K. Dick and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: This section rebuilds the evidential case for the precogs from their verified early track record, which was free of errors of commission (predicting murders that never happened) and omission (missing murders that did). The still-zero present-murder rate rules out omissions, and cases like Howard Marks, caught mid-attempt, form a random and representative sample of the precogs' predictions showing commissions have not crept in, since arrest-timing delays correlate with nothing systematic about guilt.

reliabilism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
reliabilism.title: Philip K. Dick and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: The section concedes that Precrime techs erred in the Anne Lively case, failing to notice that some previsions showed ripples moving toward the shore and others away. But it argues this is only the general problem of interpreting any evidence, from confessions to forensics to eyewitness reports, and that human fallibility does not imply unreliability, any more than fallible traditional policing meant murders should go uninvestigated.

reliabilism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
reliabilism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: Richard Greene asks what, if anything, walkers know. Rick's optimistic feeling that Lori and Carl survived turns out true, yet is not knowledge - true belief is necessary but insufficient, the gap Gettier cases exploit - and since walkers can never weigh evidence or think about their thoughts, only externalist, reliability-based accounts of knowledge can count them as knowers. Walker behavior defeats Jenner's 'mindless instinct' line: Jenny turning the handle of her old house, the little girl walker retrieving her teddy bear, a walker smashing the department store window with a rock, and the horde seeing through Rick and Glenn's gut disguise once rain washes the scent away. Zombie knowledge is real but limited to simple things recalled from the person's past, the more complex the task the less likely they know it.

reliabilism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
reliabilism.title: Psych and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: The Senors use Psych to separate true belief from knowledge: Shawn's hunch that Shabby the sea lion was murdered is true but shabbily evidenced, and his justified, true belief that a Clayton family member sabotaged the plane fails to be knowledge when the killer turns out to be a son-in-law he had no reason to think existed - a textbook Gettier case from 'He Dead.' They then weigh the two main theories of justification, evidentialism (with its base rates and prior probabilities) and reliabilism, and both vindicate the careful, methodical work of Lassiter and Juliet while Shawn's trigger-happy belief-forming habit strikes out twice. Shawn is redeemed only as an evidence-generator whose disregard for priors takes 'impossible' suspects like a murdered sea lion seriously, so that pairing his talents with the detectives' rigor yields the complete detective.

reliabilism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
reliabilism.title: Psych and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: Ronda Bowen argues that because Shawn delivers true conclusions under a false justification (psychic power), the SBPD's beliefs are Gettier-style justified true beliefs rather than knowledge, using Plato's Theaetetus (perception and true judgment fail as definitions) as the frame and Gettier's Smith/Jones and Ford/Brown cases to model episodes like 'Spellingg Bee,' where the police infer Miklous's guilt from Shawn's staged psychic demonstration. John Hawthorne's lottery propositions explain why Lassiter's 'Shawn isn't a psychic' certainty can never be fully justified, and the chapter closes on internalism versus externalism and the reliability of testimony, concluding the detectives become internally justified only when they re-derive Shawn's conclusions through their own reasoning.

reliabilism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
reliabilism.title: Psych and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: Courtland Lewis replays Plato's Theaetetus with Shawn and Henry to show that perception and true judgment fail as accounts of knowledge, then recasts both Gettier cases with Psych material: Chief Vick's justified-but-lucky belief about the chief-of-police job, and Juliet's disjunction 'Shawn is a psychic or Gus is in Mazatlan.' Since justified true belief is not knowledge, he argues Shawn's trained senses fit reliabilism - distinguished from lucky predictors like Leonard Koppett and probed through Lehrer's Mr. Truetemp against Gus's super sniffer - and closes by combining reliabilist-foundationalism (Alston's two levels of knowledge), coherence theory, and Klein's infinitism into Shawn's observe-eliminate-conclude method.

reliabilism.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
reliabilism.title: The Devil and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: John Karavitis (with tongue-in-cheek co-author 'Lucifer') treats The Ninth Gate as an epistemology case study, sorting the characters' beliefs about the Devil - true-believer Balkan, skeptic book-dealer Corso, the occult-tourist Order of the Silver Serpent - and testing them against Plato's Theaetetus definitions of knowledge as perception, true belief, and justified true belief. Balkan's justification is only an internally coherent web of book-learned beliefs, while Corso's external evidence (engravings signed 'LCF,' his journey's experiences) is weighed by the general reliability of his sources. Descartes' dreaming and the deceiving demon then leave the viewer skeptical that the Devil ever appeared at all.

reliabilism.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
reliabilism.title: 9. How the Doctor Knows
reliabilism.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a reliabilist about knowledge rather than a Cartesian strong foundationalist: using 'Amy's Choice,' 'The Beast Below' (the glass of water, the engine room, Amy's inference that the Star Whale came willingly), 'Silence in the Library' (the chicken-leg experiment implicating the Vashta Nerada), and Davros's Dalek trials in 'Genesis of the Daleks,' she shows him trusting perception in the right causal chain and reasoning inductively and abductively—Peirce's inference to the best explanation—instead of demanding Cartesian certainty. Against Descartes's dream and evil-genius skepticism, updated as Putnam-style brain-in-a-vat scenarios via the Dream Crabs of 'Last Christmas' and the Dream Lord's two-worlds game, she deploys Goldman's three criteria for perceptual knowledge: justification is packed into reliable belief-forming processes, and doubt is warranted only in known abnormal contexts like funhouses or Dream Lord games.

reliabilism.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
reliabilism.title: 10. Does Bates Know Who Raped Anna
reliabilism.relation: The Nisleys ask whether Bates's belief that Green raped Anna counts as knowledge. His belief is true, and Plato's Theaetetus defines knowledge as justified true belief, but Mrs. Hughes's false testimony, Anna's denials, and mere observed flirting mean Bates's reasons are defective: his belief could be true by coincidence, a Gettier-style failure in which truth is not earned by justification. The chapter also examines testimony - a reliable testifier like Mrs. Hughes would normally confer justification, but she deliberately lies - and concludes with Anna's own verdict that Bates 'might have suspected, but he did not know.'

reliabilism.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
reliabilism.title: 4. Special Epistemic Agent Dale Cooper
reliabilism.relation: A chapter-length epistemology tutorial delivered as Cooper's tapes to Diane, applying the justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge to his investigation. An Invitation to Love example (Chet's Ouija board actually guided by Jade's ghost) distinguishes internalist justification from externalist/reliabilist justification — a belief formed by a truth-conducive process can be justified even when the believer lacks reasons — and Cooper then earns internal justification by treating his dreams and visions as a hypothesis that yields testable predictions: "sometimes her arms bend back" matches Albert's autopsy, and the Giant's three pronouncements (man in a smiling bag, the owls are not what they seem, without chemicals he points) are confirmed by Jacques' hanging body bag, Major Briggs' deep-space transmission, and MIKE emerging off his haloperidol. The chapter cautions against confirming vague prophecies like bunny-shaped clouds, concluding Cooper becomes a truly "Special Epistemic Agent."

reliabilism.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
reliabilism.title: A Strange Ending
reliabilism.relation: Manninen applies virtue epistemology — built on Aristotle's virtue ethics and golden mean — to the four students of the Ancient One, asking not what they knew of the mystic arts but how they knew it. Strange's photographic memory exemplifies reliabilist epistemic ability, while Montmarquet's responsibilist virtues (impartiality, intellectual courage) are measured against Pangborn's self-serving magic, Kaecilius's courage without impartiality, and Mordo's epistemic rigidity and blind deference to authority ('no more questions'), each a vice of excess or deficiency. The Book of Cagliostro frames Wong's 'no knowledge in Kamar-Taj is forbidden, only certain practices,' and Strange emerges closest to the balanced intellectual character, though Aristotle demands consistency, not a single virtuous act.

reliabilism.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
reliabilism.title: 10. Does Bates Know Who Raped Anna
reliabilism.relation: The Nisleys ask whether Bates's conviction that Mr. Green raped Anna counts as knowledge, starting from the Theaetetus's definition of knowledge as justified true belief. Bates's belief is true, but his evidential position is compromised: Mrs. Hughes, though genuinely reliable, gives him false testimony pointing to a stranger, Anna denies it was Green, and his own grounds (Green's flirting and Green's admission that he left the concert) are too weak, so the truth of his belief is largely coincidental, exactly the Gettier predicament that true belief is not sufficient for knowledge. The chapter applies reliabilist reasoning about testimony to conclude that Bates 'might have suspected, but he did not know.'

reliabilism.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
reliabilism.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: Abraham Schwab turns Ygritte's 'You know nothing, Jon Snow' into a theory of epistemic humility: Jon misreads wildling courtship norms, Sam's dragonglass shatters on wight Small Paul, Lord Mormont assumes Mance fights like a southern king and pays for it at the Fist of First Men, while Arya's accurate self-knowledge keeps her alive. Formalizing with justified true belief - Sam's lucky dagger thrust is not knowledge, and the Watch's warranted belief that the dead Othor was harmless justifies falsity - he uses Lysa's letter, which sent Ned to King's Landing on a lie, to ask what justification is: Descartes's absolute certainty is too strict, reliabilism vindicates testimony ('dark wings, dark words'), so that only Sansa need witness Ned's beheading for the Starks to know it, and between Melisandre's circular dogma about Azor Ahai and total skepticism, moderate skepticism best governs belief - a humility the south lacked about the Horn of Winter.

reliabilism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
reliabilism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
reliabilism.relation: Richard Greene surveys zombie types, from the radio-using corpse of Return of the Living Dead to White Zombie's servants, to fix walkers as the standard zombie worth asking what they know. Against Dr. Jenner's 'mindless instinct' verdict he cites the little girl walker retrieving her teddy bear, Jenny working her former home's doorknob, walkers breaking a shop window with a rock, and their sniffing out Rick and Glenn's gut disguise as evidence of genuine beliefs. He argues that zombie knowledge, which cannot involve weighing evidence, supports externalist, reliability-based accounts of knowledge over internalist ones, and that walkers know only simple things recalled from past experience—the more complex the task, the less likely they know it.

reliabilism.book: 219 - The Philosophy of David Cronenberg
reliabilism.title: “Freaks of Nature” Extrasensory Perception and the Paranormal in the Films of David Cronenberg
reliabilism.relation: Keith Allen uses Stereo, Scanners, and The Dead Zone to explore the philosophy of ESP: telepathy and precognition challenge C. D. Broad's 'basic limiting principles' about causation (action at a distance, backward causation, changing the future). He asks whether ESP has the phenomenal 'tang' of genuine perception (Hume on force/vivacity; Nagel's 'what it is like'), and uses BonJour's reliable-clairvoyant Norman case plus Gettier to argue about internalist justification and knowledge, asking whether Johnny Smith needs reasons to trust his precognitive visions.

reliabilism.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
reliabilism.title: 4. Special Epistemic Agent Dale Cooper
reliabilism.relation: Written as Cooper's dictations to Diane, Rard uses the justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge and the internalism/externalism debate to ask whether Cooper is justified in trusting dreams and visions in a world with supernatural forces. Through the Invitation to Love Ouija-board example she shows how a reliable but unrecognized source yields externally justified belief (reliabilism); Cooper then earns internal justification the way one tests a hypothesis—treating the giant's predictions ('man in a smiling bag', 'the owls are not what they seem', 'without chemicals he points') as testable predictions that come true, making him a 'special epistemic agent.'

reliabilism.book: 235 - The Philosophy of TV Noir
reliabilism.title: CSI and the Art of Forensic Detection
reliabilism.relation: Knight and McKnight analyze CSI as 'procedural noir': Las Vegas instantiates the corrupt-city trope, and the show's methodological core is reading scientific evidence as a system of signs, generating and testing hypotheses through hypothetical flash reconstructions (Grissom's wrong incest-guess in 'Blood Drops', competing crash theories in 'Anonymous'). Three case studies carry the philosophy: Philip Gerard's defense attack on the team's competence makes forensic investigation an ethical matter of integrity and reliable process rather than mere evidence collection; the Paul Millander trilogy uses the trope of the double (Paul/Pauline, Judge Mason, the forged Grissom identity) to explore identity and self-knowledge; and Lady Heather's dominance-submission 'stop' convention reframes the femme fatale around reason, passion, and Grissom's desire to be known.

reliabilism.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
reliabilism.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
reliabilism.relation: Silverman uses Battlestar Galactica to explore knowledge as justified true belief. Adama's 'true lie' about knowing Earth's location makes Starbuck's belief in Earth a Gettier case, a justified true belief resting on false justification. He tests Adama's testimony against Goldman's reliabilism (sight is unreliable for spotting Cylons; memory deceives Boomer and Tigh) and Hume's skepticism about testimony versus Plantinga's defense of it. Finally, against Clifford's evidentialism he deploys William James's 'will to believe,' arguing that faith in Earth is a forced, momentous choice that gives the Colonials purpose.

reliabilism.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
reliabilism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
reliabilism.relation: Roche's 'Seeing Snakes' attacks the psychedelicist claim (William James on nitrous oxide, Huxley's 'reducing valve,' Leary) that drugs including cannabis reveal reality-as-it-is. He deploys Russell's line that we 'can make no distinction between the man who eats little and sees heaven and the man who drinks much and sees snakes,' and a reliabilist demand that knowledge have a source proven reliable over independently verifiable cases, to argue drug 'revelations' are indistinguishable from delusion. Foucault is cited that drugs have 'nothing to do with truth and falsity,' and Nietzsche's Dionysian veil-of-Maya passage is used as an example of the mystical rhetoric he debunks.

reliabilism.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
reliabilism.title: “You Have to Have Something to Live For. Let it be Earth”
reliabilism.relation: Eric Silverman uses Battlestar Galactica's Adama, who lies that he knows Earth's location, to run the Gettier problem: Starbuck's true belief that Earth exists rests on a false justification (that Adama knows), so it is justified-true-belief without being knowledge. He tests testimony via Goldman's reliabilism (sight is unreliable for telling Cylons from humans) and the Hume/Locke/Plantinga debate over testimony's epistemic role. He closes with James's 'will to believe': faith in Earth is a forced, momentous choice where agnosticism forfeits meaning, so belief without certainty can be reasonable.

reliabilism.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
reliabilism.title: 7. Knowledge, Space, and Time
reliabilism.relation: The chapter uses the TARDIS to defend a 'block universe' theory of spacetime over Presentism (since the Doctor visits past and future), then turns to epistemology, distinguishing belief from knowledge and 'belief in' the Doctor from 'belief that' he exists. It re-stages Gettier's justified-true-belief counterexample as picking the Doctor's next companion by a blue jean jacket, surveys Descartes's Cogito foundationalism, Hume's induction, and Reid's direct perception, and endorses Alston's reliabilist two-level foundationalism plus Klein's infinitism. It argues the Doctor's benefit-of-the-doubt toward non-rational creatures fits a reliabilist 'lower level' of knowledge and an imaginative, engaged, virtuous (Zagzebski) search for truth.

searle-intentionality.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
searle-intentionality.title: The Role of Matter Biology or Function
searle-intentionality.relation: Lawrence asks which theory of mind best fits the Matrix trilogy. Cartesian dualism (with its pineal-gland plug standing in for Neo's headjack) would explain Neo's jackless mind in the Train Station but lacks evidence and faces the interaction problem, so the chapter defends a fully materialist reading — Neo's sentinel-destroying signal and burnt-eye sight reconstrued as Matrix hardware in his skull. It then contrasts reductive and eliminative materialism, Searle's beer-can biological naturalism, and functionalism via Lewis's Martian pain, concluding that the films' sentient machines — Agent Smith's seamless copy into Bane's body — presuppose functionalism.

searle-intentionality.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
searle-intentionality.title: Emergentism Now Can Scotty Beam Us Up
searle-intentionality.relation: Tests three theories of mind against Spock's katra transfer in The Wrath of Khan and The Search for Spock and his mind melds with Kirk, the Horta, and Rock people. Descartes's divisibility argument backs the dualism the katra assumes, but the argument from parsimony (Ockham's razor), the problem of mental causation, and the conservation of energy weigh against it; Churchland's eliminative materialism plays by science's rules but runs into Nagel's 'what it is like' objection, dramatized by Geordi failing to describe anger to Data without circularity. The author lands, cautiously, on Searle-style emergentism — mind as an emergent, irreducible feature of neural complexity, as when Nomad and V'Ger exceed their programming — while conceding Kim's charge that it may be dualism in disguise.

searle-intentionality.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
searle-intentionality.title: “Logic Is the Beginning of Wisdom . . . Not the End”
searle-intentionality.relation: Treats Kirk's computer-killing arguments as logic lessons: his valid syllogism forces Nomad to sterilize itself in 'The Changeling,' while the M-5's trial in 'The Ultimate Computer' models inductive hypothesis testing. The Liar paradox ('Everything Harry tells you is a lie' / 'I am lying') crashes Norman in 'I, Mudd' and, via Tarski's T-sentences and the explosion problem, reveals the concept of truth as inconsistent, with three-valued logic offered as a fix that only relocates the paradox. Gödel's incompleteness theorem then grounds the Lucas-Penrose claim that minds outstrip computer programs like Landru — which Putnam's consistency objection rebuts — leaving Searle's point that computers manipulate symbols without understanding them as the residue of Surak's Vulcan logic being the beginning of wisdom, not the end.

searle-intentionality.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
searle-intentionality.title: The Right Stuff
searle-intentionality.relation: Applies Searle's Chinese Room to argue that functional equivalence alone would not make androids sentient, then observes that Dick's androids — biological 'chitinous reflex machines' detectable only by bone-marrow and Boneli reflex-arc tests, unlike obviously mechanical electric sheep — may possess the biological 'right stuff' Searle requires for intentional content. It closes by weighing this against the Turing/Dick behavioral view and the Wittgensteinian choice of which language game to play, calling the latter 'the most humanistic' reading.

searle-intentionality.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
searle-intentionality.title: 7. Life, Liberty and the Pursuit of a Warm Blanket
searle-intentionality.relation: The chapter explains Linus's blanket via Winnicott's transitional objects, then argues the gang's wider habits - Great Pumpkin taboos, baseball fetishes and rituals - are 'magical thinking' that manufactures an illusion of control over an uncertain world. A middle section tours the mind-body problem (Hippocrates, Descartes's dualism and pineal gland, Huxley's epiphenomenalism, Searle's emergent consciousness) to ask who is really doing the reading. The fallacies section dissects Linus's unfalsifiable Pumpkin doctrine (post hoc after the taboo-breaking 'if') and Charlie's confirmation bias, before reframing his 'pantophobia' as Kierkegaardian angst and Sartrean nausea: with adults reduced to 'Mwaa mwaa mwaa,' the kids are condemned to be free.

searle-intentionality.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
searle-intentionality.title: Violent Ends
searle-intentionality.relation: Richards asks what it is like to be a host, combining three lenses: Searle's biological naturalism (thinking machines must be built from materials with the right causal powers, and the hosts' synthetic flesh may qualify), Nagel's bat (even if hosts are conscious, their perfectly relived memories, curated pain, and blind spots like 'it doesn't look like anything to me' may make their experience as inconceivable to us as echolocation), and Chalmers's philosophical zombies (hosts behave exactly like us, yet beings identical to them with no inner light are conceivable). He reads Ford's contradictory testimony — praising Bernard's guilt as 'a thing of beauty' while denying consciousness exists — as a shift to a deflationary view with no threshold for being alive, and argues the show's choice to film human and host experience in the same style keeps the question deliberately open while fostering empathy.

searle-intentionality.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
searle-intentionality.title: NOTES
searle-intentionality.relation: Matthews argues that certain children's books are 'subversive' in a Socratic sense: they problematize concepts adults assume they command, challenging adult epistemic authority the way Socrates exposed the pretended knowledge of Athens' elite. Morris the Moose raises Aristotelian questions of natural kinds and essence-versus-accident; Leese Webster probes the concept of art; The Shrinking of Treehorn destabilizes 'normal' child development; Frog and Toad's 'The Garden' dramatizes the post hoc, ergo propter hoc fallacy about causation. In the Ozma of Oz Tik-Tok discussion, nine-year-old Paul reconstructs an argument that only brains think, which Matthews aligns with Searle's claim in The Mystery of Consciousness that consciousness is caused by specific neurobiological processes; he explicitly distinguishes his subversive stories from those promoting Pyrrhonian skepticism or Protagorean relativism.

functionalism.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
functionalism.title: The Role of Matter Biology or Function
functionalism.relation: Lawrence asks which theory of mind best fits the Matrix trilogy. Cartesian dualism (with its pineal-gland plug standing in for Neo's headjack) would explain Neo's jackless mind in the Train Station but lacks evidence and faces the interaction problem, so the chapter defends a fully materialist reading — Neo's sentinel-destroying signal and burnt-eye sight reconstrued as Matrix hardware in his skull. It then contrasts reductive and eliminative materialism, Searle's beer-can biological naturalism, and functionalism via Lewis's Martian pain, concluding that the films' sentient machines — Agent Smith's seamless copy into Bane's body — presuppose functionalism.

functionalism.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
functionalism.title: “I Feel Exactly What You Feel”
functionalism.relation: Runs Star Trek's transporter and android stories as thought experiments on personal identity: the body theory (Kirk rejecting android Korby — 'Dr. Korby was never here' — and Picard telling the resurrected Rishon Uxbridge 'you do not exist'), the brain theory ('Spock's Brain,' Bashir refusing to replace half of Vedek Bareil's brain), and Locke's memory theory as vindicated by the Trill (Lela Dax's 'a person is but the sum of their memories,' the 'Dax' extradition hearing over Curzon's crimes). Riker's transporter double in 'Second Chances' and the Tuvix fusion then break the memory theory through fission and fusion, prompting Parfit's move that psychological continuity, not numerical identity, is what matters in survival. Memory erasure in 'Dagger of the Mind' and Kurn's rebranding after the failed Mauk-to'Vor in 'Sons of Mogh' count as death if we are our memories.

functionalism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
functionalism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
functionalism.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether 'you' survive a walker bite, testing bodily identity, behaviorism, and functionalism as theories of personal survival against Jenner's verdict that after death 'everything you ever were... gone'. His centerpiece adapts Daniel Dennett: survivors yoke walkers to plows and tanks, dangle meat to move them between positions labeled 1 and 0, and gradually build a rope-and-corpse computer functionally identical to a human brain - which behaviorism and functionalism must call conscious, yet which we can conceive as utterly dark inside. The lesson is that we cannot know whether any system, walker, animal, or AI, is conscious, so treatment of non-human systems may need to err on the side of caution.

functionalism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
functionalism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
functionalism.relation: McKinney argues Van Helsing should have studied Dracula's brain instead of staking him, because the Count is a philosophy-of-mind thought experiment: a mind that persists unchanged across bat, wolf, mist, and human bodies refutes mind-brain identity theory and fits functionalism (the mind as one song playable in many formats), while his telepathic bond with Mina and shapeshifting probe Cartesian dualism's mind-body interaction problem. Nagel's bats show that only Dracula could tell us what it is like to echo-locate or wolf-sense; yet since nothing like his unconstrained mind exists in our world, the novel finally maps what minds are not - evidence against the immaterial mind.

functionalism.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
functionalism.title: “Do you even know where you are ”
functionalism.relation: Arvan argues the entire series, lab included, literally takes place inside a videogame, citing physically impossible events (Teddy's bullets cannot hurt the Man in Black, William steps onto a moving train, workers appear instantly in a single unbroken shot) and NPC-like loops of the lab staff. He then claims Descartes had it backwards: whether we are in a dream, Spinoza's God's mind, or a simulation (Bostrom's hypothesis, extended by his own peer-to-peer variant that would explain quantum indeterminacy and relativity), to be simulated is still to be real. Via Chalmers-style structuralism, anything structured and functioning like a person is a person, so hosts who walk, talk, love, and suffer are persons — and the humans' rape, torture, and murder of them, like our treatment of Siri and Watson, is dehumanization on a par with slavery and the Holocaust.

functionalism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
functionalism.title: Notes
functionalism.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

functionalism.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
functionalism.title: NOTES
functionalism.relation: Butler argues the films' humans-versus-machines picture rests on a false dichotomy: we are ourselves 'meat machines,' and functionalism makes minds computational processes realizable in silicon as much as neurons - illustrated by a Henrietta thought experiment (adapted from William Lycan) in which a friend gradually replaced with T-101 parts remains the same conscious person, and refusing this is 'human chauvinism.' Following Dawkins's extended phenotype and Andy Clark's natural-born cyborgs, he claims our tools are components of our minds, so Skynet and even the Terminator films themselves (making Cameron a cyborg of his cameras and editing suites) are extensions of human nature rather than alien 'Others.' Judgment Day, if it came, would be human suicide rather than genocide, so the real question is what values we build into our technology - 'no fate but what we make for ourselves.'

functionalism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
functionalism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
functionalism.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether you survive a walker bite, rejecting the body view via Dr. Jenner's 'Everything you ever were or ever will be—gone' because a mindless corpse is not you. He tests philosophical behaviorism and functionalism against walker behavior—Jenny turning her old doorknob, walkers distinguishing humans by smell—then adapts Dennett's thought experiment into a walker-and-rope computer functionally identical to a human brain. Since we can conceive that groaning machine lacking inner experience, behavior and function cannot settle which systems are conscious, leaving the bitten dying in ignorance of whether they face annihilation or reanimation.

chinese-room.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
chinese-room.title: “Cyborgs Don’t Feel Pain. I Do.”
chinese-room.relation: Littmann asks whether Skynet's machines are people, testing three criteria on the Terminator films. The T-101 and T-1000 pass demanding Turing Tests by passing as humans; Searle's Chinese room — recast as a little Austrian inside the T-101 reciting 'Ahll be bahk' without understanding — shows behavior alone cannot prove thought; and feelings are equally unproven by behavior, since the T-101 can smile on command. But the films' first-person 'Terminator's-eye-view' sequences, Littmann argues, display what it is like to be a Terminator and thus prove machine consciousness, so humanity's extinction might not be the end of persons.

chinese-room.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
chinese-room.title: Transformers and Philosophy
chinese-room.relation: Pike asks what the All Spark's zap would have to do to give brought-to-life vending machines and steering wheels genuine minds, testing logical behaviorism's dispositions and Turing's conversation test against Searle's Chinese Room ('syntax is insufficient for semantics'), and weighing Descartes's God-given soul against physicalist alternatives: functionalism, Searle's biological naturalism, and reductive physicalism. Since we can never access another mind from the inside, he concludes that by abductive inference to the best explanation - Optimus Prime's mourning, planning, and moral decision-making being too complex for mere programming - we have as much reason to credit a Transformer with a mind as any human around us.

chinese-room.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
chinese-room.title: Transformers and Philosophy
chinese-room.relation: Koepsell accepts that Autobots are virtuous and Decepticons vicious, then asks whether ethical war-bots are even possible, using the military's autonomous-weapons program, Asimov's Three Laws, and a kitten-sensing washing machine to argue that designed-in 'ethics' is only the designer's morality, like A Clockwork Orange's conditioned Alex, because it involves no real choice. Searle's Chinese Room and Turing's test then cast doubt on whether any mind, even our own, makes genuinely free choices, so he concludes that the appearance of virtue - behavior that reliably works - is all we ever have for humans or Autobots alike, and we should build machines as well as Optimus Prime and Bumblebee.

chinese-room.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
chinese-room.title: Would Cortana Pass the Turing Test
chinese-room.relation: Sherol Chen asks whether Cortana would pass the Turing Test and answers that games need believability of behavior, not constitution of mind. Turing's imitation game sets the target; Searle's Chinese Room shows that performance without understanding suffices for the player's experience of Covenant AI and Cortana alike, while French's seagull test and associative-priming objection show the Turing Test really measures human-style intelligence—limits Halo happily ignores. Surveying game-storytelling workarounds (amnesia openings, Planescape's immortal death, Bioshock's 'Would you kindly'), she argues designers convert paidia's limits into narrative features, and Cortana would pass here and now—though in her own era newer tests would expose new limits.

chinese-room.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
chinese-room.title: The Right Stuff
chinese-room.relation: Applies Searle's Chinese Room to argue that functional equivalence alone would not make androids sentient, then observes that Dick's androids — biological 'chitinous reflex machines' detectable only by bone-marrow and Boneli reflex-arc tests, unlike obviously mechanical electric sheep — may possess the biological 'right stuff' Searle requires for intentional content. It closes by weighing this against the Turing/Dick behavioral view and the Wittgensteinian choice of which language game to play, calling the latter 'the most humanistic' reading.

chinese-room.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
chinese-room.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
chinese-room.relation: Nicolas Michaud treats Watson's 2011 defeat of Jennings and Rutter as evidence for Turing's test: had Watson's answers come from behind a door we would have judged them intelligent, and its goofy misses ('What is Toronto?????') reflect missing context, not missing thought, no more damning than a child's honest error. Against Searle's Chinese Room he deploys the systems reply - you plus the Big Book of Rules might be the thing that understands - and argues that nobody, human or machine, can meet Searle's impossible burden of proving understanding, since Watson can define words, associate connotations, and pick Jeopardy! out from not-Jeopardy!. Quoting Locke's definition of a person as a thinking being that can consider itself as itself, he concludes Watson approaches personhood and that we had better teach our 'intelligent offspring' kindness and fairness before they learn anything else.

chinese-room.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
chinese-room.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
chinese-room.relation: Arguing against the dogma that only organic beings can be conscious, the chapter defends BMO's aliveness and personhood against Finn and Jake's teasing and the contrast with servile Neptr. Using Pepperell's criteria of 'motivated meaning' and layered consciousness, it shows BMO changing her own batteries, escaping the giant bird, fearing the silent-contest 'doppelgangers', resisting the factory's personality wipe, and rehearsing personhood with Football in the mirror. Against Descartes's claim that no machine can truly use language and Searle's Chinese Room - reimagined as Gunter in a dungeon flipping response cards - the author sides with Turing: since we credit other humans with minds on conversation and behavior alone, refusing BMO the same credit is mere speciesism, and personhood finally rests on social recognition of another as a person.

chinese-room.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
chinese-room.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
chinese-room.relation: Munkittrick argues that because personhood cannot be defined (trait lists like 'long-term planning' are circular) and behavior cannot prove an inner mind—as Searle's Chinese Room thought experiment shows—people have always identified persons intuitively, and Pixar trained Millennials to do exactly that. He reads the Pixar canon in three stages: Toy Story's self-aware Buzz as nascent non-human personhood, the Human-as-Partner films (Ratatouille's Remy and Linguini, WALL-E and EVE, Monsters, Inc.'s Sully and Boo, Up's Carl and Dug) as mutual recognition of persons across species lines, and The Incredibles as showing that even enhanced 'super-humans' face otherization—so a generation primed by these films will accept AI, animals, and uplifted beings as bearers of rights.

chinese-room.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
chinese-room.title: The Maze Is it Consciousness
chinese-room.relation: Gonzalez sets Turing's dream against Searle's nightmare: the whole park functions as a Turing test scenario, since neither guests nor viewers can reliably tell hosts from humans (Dolores in the pilot, Bernard until 'Trompe L'Oeil'), which for Turing means the hosts think. Searle's Chinese Room supplies Ford's counter — hosts merely simulate understanding by manipulating symbols without meaning — and the chapter weighs evidence of qualia on the Turing side: Abernathy's breakdown at the photograph, memory-erasure implying experiences matter to hosts, Maeve's grief for her daughter, Dolores killing the fly. The Maze turns out to represent consciousness as an inward journey to one's own voice, and Ford's admission that humans live in loops as tight as the hosts' leaves open whether our free will is any less scripted.

chinese-room.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
chinese-room.title: 2. Is Joi a Person
chinese-room.relation: Chris Lay argues Joi is a person. He raises Searle's objection that programs only simulate understanding and need the right biological 'stuff', then answers it: Joi apparently violates her 'everything you want her to be' programming, so her affection for K is authentic either way. Testing Joi against Locke's personhood criteria — rationality, sentience, and self-consciousness grounded in memory and in her self-sacrifice before Luv — he adds a Cartesian reading in which her transfers between console and emanator make her a disembodied soul, closer to Descartes's essence of the human than embodied replicants are. If a digital person like Joi would also fail the baseline, the wall separating kind would need a full societal reset.

chinese-room.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
chinese-room.title: The Attack of the Chinese Room
chinese-room.relation: Novy asks whether the Living Armor of 'The Mask in the Iron Man' — consciousness struck into it by lightning during the Whiplash fight, later tearing out its own heart to save Tony — really thinks. Turing's test and functionalism (any successful rescue of Yinsen is functionally equivalent, whatever the means) say only behavior matters, and Dennett's intentional stance has us treat the armor, like Darwin's burrow-plugging earthworms, as if it has beliefs and desires; against this, Leibniz's mill and Searle's Chinese Room — with Happy Hogan shuffling symbol cards he cannot read, held by 'Searle the Mandarin agent' — insist symbol manipulation never yields understanding. The chapter's reply: open the Mandarin's skull and you find only gray goop and neurons, so if behavior cannot ground understanding in the armor, it cannot in us either — we may all be in the Chinese Room.

chinese-room.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
chinese-room.title: Notes
chinese-room.relation: Asks whether droids like C-3PO and R2-D2 can think, staging Searle's Chinese Room as a 'Bocce Room' to argue that droid anxiety, pain, and heroism might be mere input-output symbol shuffling. It then rebuts Searle with the systems reply (the room as a whole, not the person inside, might understand) and a neuron-by-neuron mechanical brain-replacement thought experiment showing the biological/mechanical divide is arbitrary, concluding that restraining bolts, memory wipes, and the Mos Eisley cantina's 'we don't serve their kind here' prejudice lose their justification if droids might genuinely suffer.

chinese-room.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
chinese-room.title: NOTES
chinese-room.relation: Littmann asks whether personhood could survive humanity's extinction in 2029: if Terminators genuinely think and feel, a Skynet victory would not be the end of people. He argues the T-101, T-1000 and T-X pass substantial Turing Tests (fooling muggers, cops, Sarah on the phone as her 'mother'), then concedes Searle's Chinese Room - recast as a tiny Austrian inside the endoskeleton reciting 'Ahll be bahk' without understanding - shows thinking behavior cannot prove thought. But he claims the films' red-tinted Terminator's-eye-view shots show what it is like to be a Terminator, giving proof of consciousness, and concludes the machines are probably persons: there is an 'I' in 'I'll be back.'

chinese-room.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
chinese-room.title: NOTES
chinese-room.relation: Antti Kuusela argues from Wittgenstein that behavior is the touchstone — indeed constitutive — of mental life, so the question is whether Terminators behave like beings with minds. Searle's Chinese room and Ned Block's blockhead explain the read-only T-101's head-up-display of canned responses as symbol-shuffling without understanding, and the T-1000's 'I know this hurts' seems empty from a machine that cannot feel pain. The pivot is the learning-mode switch John and Sarah flip: the T-101 acquires slang, keeps promises, and acts for reasons Skynet cannot predict, passing the Lovelace test, and the Wittgensteinian dismissal of Chalmers's philosophical zombie removes the last reason to deny it a mental life — making the steel-mill sacrifice the destruction of a rights-bearing someone rather than something.

chinese-room.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
chinese-room.title: The Maze Is it Consciousness
chinese-room.relation: Lucía Carrillo González frames the whole park as a Turing Test scenario, noting guests and viewers cannot distinguish hosts like Dolores and Bernard from humans, and aligns Arnold with Turing's view that minds are computers that 'think' by responding to inputs (Abernathy's anomalous reaction to the photograph). Against this she sets Searle's Chinese Room and Ford's eliminativism, which hold the hosts merely simulate understanding. Citing qualia and the hosts' perfect, meaningful memories (Maeve recalling her daughter, technicians needing to erase trauma), she argues the hosts may genuinely experience states, and reads the Maze as the inward journey to consciousness, questioning whether humans' own free will is any less scripted.

chinese-room.book: 238 - Steven Spielberg and Philosophy - We're Gonna Need a Bigger Book
chinese-room.title: A.I. Artificial Intelligence Artistic Indulgence or Advanced Inquiry
chinese-room.relation: White argues A.I. dramatizes the mind-body problem through the mecha child David, proposing a 'Strengthened Turing Test' (STT) in which the audience knows he is a machine yet must judge whether he truly loves Monica. He runs Searle's Chinese Room (David as mere rule-follower with no qualia) against Nagel's 'what is it like' and Chalmers's zombie argument and property-dualist multiple realizability, which would let a sufficiently complex David be genuinely conscious. White contends the imprinting device—David's built-in need for one other being—is what lets him pass the STT, sidestepping Cartesian dualism's interaction problem.

chinese-room.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
chinese-room.title: The Role of Matter Biology or Function
chinese-room.relation: Lawrence uses The Matrix to survey theories of mind. Neo's apparent mind-body separation fits Descartes's dualism, but Lawrence argues dualism fails on the interaction problem and lack of evidence, so the Matrix scenario supports materialism. He explains reductive (identity) and eliminative materialism (via Churchland and the Tastee Wheat question), then frames the biology-versus-function debate: Searle's emergent-property view (the beer-can thirst model) holds brain biochemistry is essential to consciousness, while functionalism (Lewis's Martian pain) holds any system with the right input-output relations has mental states, and Lawrence argues functionalism underlies the very idea of sentient machines like Agent Smith.

chinese-room.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
chinese-room.title: “Cyborgs Don’t Feel Pain. I Do.”
chinese-room.relation: Littmann uses the Terminator films to ask whether machines can be persons. The Terminators clearly pass the Turing Test by convincingly passing for human, giving behavioral evidence that they think. Littmann then presses Searle's Chinese Room, reworked as a tiny non-English-speaking Austrian inside the T-101 reciting phonetic lines, to argue that behavior alone cannot prove genuine understanding or feeling. He concludes that the films' 'Terminator's-eye-view' shots, showing the world from the machine's perspective, are the strongest evidence that the machines are conscious and so may count as people surviving humanity's extinction.

chinese-room.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
chinese-room.title: The Role of Matter Biology or Function
chinese-room.relation: Matt Lawrence uses The Matrix to survey theories of mind, arguing the 'brain-stimulation' premise favors materialism over Descartes's dualism (which alone easily explains Neo's mind-body separation at the Train Station but lacks empirical support and an interaction mechanism). He explains reductive versus eliminative materialism (Churchland's denial of folk-psychological 'beliefs' via Tastee Wheat) and then Searle's biological emergentism (the beer-can thirst machine) against functionalism (Lewis's Martian pain; Agent Smith's seamless transfer into Bane). He concludes the films are best read functionally, making sentient machines genuine minds.

chinese-room.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
chinese-room.title: “Cyborgs Don’t Feel Pain. I Do.”
chinese-room.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether the Terminators are 'people,' testing three criteria: passing as human, thinking, and feeling. The T-101, T-1000, and T-X repeatedly pass Turing Tests, giving behavioral evidence of thought, but Littmann recasts Searle's Chinese Room as the 'Austrian Terminator' to argue behavior never proves genuine understanding. He then argues personhood requires conscious experience (what it is like to be a Terminator), and takes the films' red- and blue-tinted first-person 'Terminator's-eye view' shots as evidence the machines really are conscious, so humanity's extinction need not end personhood.

chinese-room.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
chinese-room.title: 43. Ex Machina as Philosophy Mendacia Ex Machina (Lies from a Machine)
chinese-room.relation: Grinnell argues Ex Machina is fundamentally about lying, read through Kant's deontology. He frames Nathan's rigged Turing test on Ava against Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge and Kant's two formulations of the categorical imperative, deriving three 'wrinkles': lying is heteronomous programming rather than the autonomy Nathan seeks; the experiment is defensible only if Ava fails, since a genuine person may not be manipulated (Formula of Humanity); and the cascade of lies among Nathan, Caleb, and Ava vindicates Kant's absolute prohibition on lying. He uses Caleb's telling of Frank Jackson's Mary's Room and Searle's weak/strong AI distinction to question whether Ava's 'pleasure response' amounts to genuine consciousness or personhood.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
aquinas-five-ways.title: To Know … and Believe
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Gallagher reads Lost's Rose through Aquinas: faith is 'mid-way between knowledge and opinion,' sharing the certainty of episteme and the imperfection of doxa, so Rose's 'I just know' about Bernard's survival and her island cure confuses what she believes with what she knows. Aquinas' five ways ground natural knowledge that God exists, and the castaways' failures are diagnosed as sins against faith — Charlie's despair is acedia while Rose's certainty is the presumption (praesumptio) of elevating faith to demonstrated knowledge; the lesson is that faith perfects reason without replacing it.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
aquinas-five-ways.title: “You Have to Believe in Something”
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Eberl and Vines use Battlestar Galactica to weigh theism against atheism: Baltar's scientific rationalism meets Aquinas' five ways (the universe's ordered structure demands an unmoved, uncaused cause), Six's faith faces the problem of evil answered through Augustine on the perverse will and John Hick's soul-making (Starbuck's mother, 'your life is a testament to pain'), while Hume's faulty-architect analogy presses the atheist case. The chapter concludes with Russell's 'A Free Man's Worship': even in a Godless universe the Colonials find meaning in comradeship and humanity's survival — 'the gods shall lift those who lift each other.'

aquinas-five-ways.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
aquinas-five-ways.title: Does the Habit Make the Monk
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Elliott maps the recurring Monk stalemate onto medieval theology: in 'Mr. Monk Goes to the Circus', Stottlemeyer and Disher reason forward from a hunch and the evidence, exactly like Anselm's ontological argument, which assumes what it sets out to prove, while Monk, like Aquinas against Anselm, refuses assumptions and reasons backward from verifiable facts, asking why an assassin would somersault except to advertise the acrobatic alibi. Aquinas's First Cause argument (Aristotle's unmoved mover) supplies the model of proving a certainty from observable things, paralleling Monk's 'I don't know how he did it, but he did it' backward deduction. The chapter's closing move likens Monk to the medieval monks themselves: his OCD-driven ascetic withdrawal from the dirty, chaotic world (contemptus mundi) is what lets him notice the imperfection in scenes like the locker room of 'Mr. Monk and the Big Game' that reveals sabotage.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
aquinas-five-ways.title: Ridicule Is a Survival Strategy
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Kaye argues that the highest form of ridicule, which The Onion has mastered, targets not stupidity but cheating—specifically 'asscheating,' believing what you want to be true. She reads 'I Believe In Evolution, Except For The Whole Triassic Period' as skewering people who understand Darwin perfectly but exempt humans from evolution because admitting we are just another animal means admitting we die like everything else, the move behind Aquinas-style teleological add-ons that only invite a regress of gods supplying 'extras.' Articles on breast implants, the 'New Nietzschean Diet,' and Tour de France doping all show asscheats artificially inflating their evolutionary fitness; since natural selection stamps every organism with the purpose of survival and reproduction, asscheating is a vice, and ridiculing the asscheats who pollute the gene pool is itself a survival strategy.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
aquinas-five-ways.title: 21. God-Talk at the Abbey
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Samuel Lumpenhouwer takes the Abbey's religious silences - Anna's 'we'll only fall out,' Alfred's baffled 'What?' at transubstantiation, and the Catholic baptism fight over baby Sybbie - and brings in Aquinas to make God-talk possible. Reason alone can know that God exists (the argument from design through final causes like the candle flame, carefully distinguished from Paley's watchmaker), revelation grasped by faith tells us God is personal, and human words reach God only analogically, as when Matthew calls God 'Father' at Lavinia's grave, or by way of negation. Against Carson's 'it is not our place to reason why' about Sybil's death, the chapter insists that mystery limits rather than excuses reason, ending with Aquinas's 'straw' and the Abbey's three attitudes: confident belief, searching doubt, and keep-it-private spirituality.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
aquinas-five-ways.title: Magic and Deep Magic
aquinas-five-ways.relation: The chapter argues that Strange's universe implicitly contains the Creator God of theism rather than just Marvel's gods: Aristotle's impersonal prime mover will not do because Strange needs a relatable source of an objective moral order, so Aquinas's all-good author of eternal, natural, and divine law supplies the framework. It reads three comics as evidence: Strange defeating Dracula by invoking the Tetragrammaton, the Sise-Neg saga where a sorcerer who attains godhood at the dawn of time learns to recreate the universe exactly as the first cause made it, and the World War Hulk story where summoning Zom shows the hubris of violating the moral order—closing with C.S. Lewis's 'deep magic' as cooperation with the created order versus dark magic's will to control it.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
aquinas-five-ways.title: 21. God-Talk at the Abbey
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Samuel Klumpenhouwer uses the Abbey's awkward silences about religion - Anna refusing to discuss it over dinner, Thomas showing off with 'transubstantiation' - to introduce Aquinas on how God can be known and talked about. Mary's wartime bedside prayer ('I'm not even sure that you're there') shows she wants not just proof of existence but a personal God, so the chapter distinguishes Aquinas's argument from design - carefully separated from Paley's divine-watchmaker version - from knowledge of God through revelation and faith. Aquinas's two indirect ways of speaking, analogy (Matthew calling God 'Father' at Lavinia's grave) and negation, explain why the 'God is good' sign over Charles Grigg's workhouse should trouble us, and why Carson's 'it is not our place to reason why' about Sybil's death overstates the mystery of God's otherness.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
aquinas-five-ways.title: NOTES
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Daniel Gallagher uses Aquinas to read Lost as a drama about mistaking finite goods for the ultimate good: Jack's hope in curing, Kate's in deceiving, Jin's in his father-in-law's employment, Locke's in Anthony Cooper, and the Virgin Mary statues full of heroin all instantiate Aquinas's approaching-Peter analogy, where we know only confusedly that someone (the perfect good) is coming toward us. Desmond's and Charlie's paralysis before the good is the sin of acedia, Rose's faith that the island itself healed her cancer is presumption, and her certainty that Bernard is alive illustrates Aquinas's claim - framed through Plato's episteme versus doxa - that faith sits midway between knowledge and opinion. The chapter closes on the harmony of faith and reason, from the Five Ways' first efficient cause to Eko's dying 'I ask for no forgiveness,' grounded in Augustine's restless heart that finds no peace until it rests in God.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
aquinas-five-ways.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Curry argues that angels like Anna and Castiel can reasonably be atheists, because a higher perspective confers no epistemic advantage about God: Anna admits only four angels have seen him and the rest 'take it on faith.' Aquinas's cosmological argument, illustrated by the endless causal chain behind the Impala, yields at most an uncaused first cause rather than an omnipotent, omnibenevolent one, and Paley's design argument, an Impala in the desert implies a designer, is undermined by Darwinian natural selection, which Castiel himself witnessed ('Don't step on that fish'). The free-will theodicy fails against natural evils like famine and childhood cancer, and the principle of parsimony tells angels to expect a natural explanation for their own existence, so Uriel's 'There is no will. No wrath. No God.' turns out to be rational.

aquinas-five-ways.title: The Philosophy of Clint Eastwood
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Clayton distinguishes the philosophical problem of evil (Aquinas's deductive argument, its inductive/evidential successors, and Plantinga's free-will defense) from what Plantinga calls the pastoral problem — the personal crisis suffering brings. He argues Eastwood, as 'practical philosopher,' registers the philosophical problem visually in Mystic River (camera panning heavenward at Katie's murder, the intercut Communion) but pointedly refuses to resolve it. In Hereafter the tsunami, deaths, and the twins' loss are met not with theodicy but with a recurring pastoral pattern of listening, being present, and acting compassionately (Dr. Rousseau with Marie, George's reading of Marcus), religion offering no answers.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
aquinas-five-ways.title: To Know … and Believe
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Gallagher uses Lost's Rose Henderson, who says 'I just know,' to expound Aquinas on faith and reason. Aquinas places faith midway between Plato's knowledge (epistêmê) and opinion (doxa) and distinguishes its material object (God) from its formal object (first truth). Gallagher explains that all knowledge begins in the senses, so God's existence is known only by demonstration (the five ways), while faith's fuller content requires grace. Rose's sins bracket the argument: Charlie's despair is acedia, while Rose's insistence that she 'knows' the island cured her is presumption, mistaking faith for scientific knowledge.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 258 - South Park and Philosophy - You Know, I Learned Something Today
aquinas-five-ways.title: “You Have to Believe in Something”
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Eberl and Vines use Battlestar Galactica's Baltar, Six, Adama and Roslin to debate God's existence and meaning. Against Baltar's scientific naturalism they present Aquinas's five ways (unmoved mover, first cause, and the argument from design applied to the universe's ordered laws) and dismiss Pascal's Wager as insincere, like Baltar's. They then raise the problem of evil, answering with Augustine's free-will defense and Hick's soul-making theodicy against Hume's faulty-architect analogy. Finally, contrasting Russell's meaning-amid-a-godless-cosmos with religious faith, they argue atheism need not entail nihilism and that survival and human solidarity give the Colonials common ground.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
aquinas-five-ways.title: NOTES
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Daniel B. Gallagher uses Thomas Aquinas on the knowledge of God to read the characters' searches for meaning on Lost. Aquinas's 'approaching Peter' image—recognizing a human without yet knowing it is Peter—models how everyone confusedly knows God as the object of happiness while mistaking finite goods (Jack's curing, Kate's deception, Jin's job, Charlie's brother) for the ultimate good, paralleled with the castaways staring at the unidentifiable Smoke Monster. Gallagher then applies Aquinas's sin of acedia (spiritual sloth that deems the good unattainable) to Desmond's fear over Penny and Charlie's despair before Rose tells him faith is never impossible, tying the desire for happiness to Augustine's restless heart.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
aquinas-five-ways.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Arp frames a dialogue between two ex-seminarians who once got matching cross tattoos: Bill, who added more Christian ink, and Rick, who now regrets his cross as an atheist secular humanist. Bill defends God via Aquinas's combined proof from motion and causation—tracing the tattoo artist and even the Big Bang back to an unmoved mover / uncaused cause—and the 'three Ms' of mind, meaning, and morality, gesturing toward Paley-style design. Rick counters with a self-sustaining infinite series, the interaction problem between a supernatural God and nature, and the charge that God is a comforting fiction, so morality and meaning are humanly made rather than divinely guaranteed.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
aquinas-five-ways.title: To Know … and Believe
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Daniel Gallagher uses Lost's Rose, who insists 'I just know' her husband lives and the island cured her, to apply Aquinas's account of faith as 'mid-way between knowledge and opinion.' Drawing on Plato's episteme/doxa distinction and Aquinas's God/'first truth' conceptual distinction plus the five ways, he argues reason can demonstrate that God exists while faith (a grace) grasps what reason cannot. Rose exemplifies both the sin of presumption (mistaking faith for knowledge, treating the island as God's certain instrument) and, by contrast to Charlie's acedia, robust faith, so the chapter urges keeping faith and reason harmonized rather than conflated.

aquinas-five-ways.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
aquinas-five-ways.title: “You Have to Believe in Something”
aquinas-five-ways.relation: Jason Eberl and Jennifer Vines use Battlestar Galactica's Baltar (skeptic) and Caprica Six/Roslin (believers) to debate God's existence, presenting Aquinas's five ways (unmoved mover, uncaused cause, governance) against a self-explaining big bang, and noting Baltar's self-serving faith resembles Pascal's Wager. They raise the problem of evil, answering with Augustine's free-will account of moral evil and Hick's soul-making theodicy (via Hume's faulty-architect analogy) for natural evil. Writing as a theist and an atheist, they argue meaning survives without God in human solidarity ('the gods shall lift those who lift each other'), and that faith and reason can share common ground.

prisoners-dilemma.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
prisoners-dilemma.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
prisoners-dilemma.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors' beach as a "framed" state of nature: the stolen water is a tragedy of the commons, Sawyer's "finders keepers" defense of Shannon's inhalers stages Hobbes's war of all against all against Locke's natural rights, and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward civil society, a claim to punish on another's behalf. He argues no theory of human nature (Rousseau's "Innocence" versus a "Trust No. 1" attitude) is needed to understand the castaways: cooperation grows through iterated prisoner's-dilemma tit-for-tat strategies, which also recasts the real difference between Hobbesian and Lockean states of nature.

prisoners-dilemma.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
prisoners-dilemma.title: Don’t Get Into One
prisoners-dilemma.relation: Richard Greene renames the Tarantino standoff the 'ex-convict's dilemma' and models it as a special case of the prisoner's dilemma, running from Ordell and Louis's separate interrogation rooms to the White–Pink, Joe–White–Eddie and True Romance shoot-outs. He argues the standard group-rationality solution fails because ECDS participants have conflicting goals—Eddie protecting his father, White protecting Orange, Joe wanting revenge—and his survey of Tarantino's six cases shows escapes come from luck (Mr. Blonde's entrance, Nikki coming home) or shared interests (Beatrix's pregnancy), never group rationality. Tracing the dilemma back to Glaucon's contract argument in Plato's Republic, he concludes the only reliable solution is: don't get into one.

prisoners-dilemma.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
prisoners-dilemma.title: 4 - With Friends Like These, Who Needs Enemies
prisoners-dilemma.relation: Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch, Mafia Wars) through Goffman's 'face' and Brown and Levinson's positive/negative politeness: recruiting friends into an application is a face-threatening imposition that becomes awkward across professor-student and parent-child hierarchies playing as nominal equals. She invokes Derrida on Mauss - 'there is no gift without bond, without bind' - to analyze the reciprocity obligations of gifting games, and finds emergent cooperative norms like PackRat pacts against tit-for-tat stealing. Players revolt when developers monetize asymmetrical play, showing communities negotiate the rules of the magic circle.

prisoners-dilemma.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
prisoners-dilemma.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
prisoners-dilemma.relation: Greene reconstructs the Prisoner's Dilemma with Pennsatucky and Vee in separate interrogation rooms, then maps a variant onto 'Thirsty Bird': whatever Alex does, Piper is better off testifying against Kubra, yet mutual silence was the group-rational outcome the two pact on the van ride. Alex defects anyway, leaving Piper with perjury and no leniency, and Greene argues Piper should have done the 'rational' thing, since Balik's revenge is only a threat while extra time in Litchfield is a certain harm and Alex has always been willing to screw her. The episode shows why honor among the self-interested fails without trust.

prisoners-dilemma.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
prisoners-dilemma.title: NOTES
prisoners-dilemma.relation: Davies treats the beach camp as an actual state of nature: the stolen drinking water is a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers show how the crash scrubs pre-existing property rights (Hobbes: two men desiring the same thing become enemies), and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward Locke's civil society by enforcing others' rights through punishment rather than self-defense. He rejects theories of human nature - Rousseauan 'Innocence' versus a 'Trust No One' outlook - in favor of the repeated prisoner's dilemma, arguing the survivors stabilize cooperation through tit-for-tat: beginning cooperative with strangers and retaliating against the Others. On this reading the real difference between Hobbes and Locke is which round of the repeated dilemma each takes as the starting point.

i-thou.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
i-thou.title: Bad Faith
i-thou.relation: Lee reads the 'Breakdown' episode of Alfred Hitchcock Presents existentially: when the executive Callou coldly fires Humka and hangs up on his despair, he treats a person as a thing, Buber's 'I-It' pseudo-listening where Humka sought an 'I-Thou' dialogue with the godlike source of authority in his world. Heidegger's account of inauthenticity explains the mask of rational control behind which Callou hides, and Sartre's bad faith names the self-deception by which he pretends his godlike management of others is justifiable. Paralyzed and taken for a corpse after a car crash, Callou can be saved only when rational strategy fails and he finally weeps: the single tear reveals his caring nature, Jessie addresses him person-to-person, and, vulnerable before God and others, he becomes an authentic self, Hitchcock's pointed moral for bosses who give an employee the sack.

i-thou.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
i-thou.title: There is No Dark Side of the Moon Really. Matter of Fact It’s All Dark
i-thou.relation: Johnston reads The Dark Side of the Moon through Buber's I and Thou: modern life traps us in the I-It mode of experience, from 'Welcome to the Machine' to teachers who treat students as replaceable Its ('Hey, teacher, leave us kids alone!') and Horkheimer's instrumental reason that turns personnel into 'human resources,' while the album repeatedly calls us to the I-You encounter, from 'Echoes'' strangers whose glances meet ('I am you and what I see is me,' Waters's origin of empathy) to 'Breathe''s 'don't be afraid to care.' He links the opening heartbeat and the breath of 'Breathe' to Buber's eternal You, defends Buddhism against Buber's charge that enlightenment is worldless monologue (the Buddha becomes one with the world, a perfect reciprocity like the innate You of the womb), and accepts Nietzsche's point that the Enlightenment's abstract God is dead while insisting, with Buber, that encounter with the eternal You remains possible. The album itself, he concludes, resists degenerating into an It: even if 'the sun is eclipsed by the moon,' the light persists and Dark Side can be the antidote to the It-world.

i-thou.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
i-thou.title: A Better Way of Living Your Life
i-thou.relation: Akers argues the Doctor follows neither rule deontology, utilitarian calculation, nor virtue ethics, but a relational ethics of care in Noddings's and Slote's sense, expressed as Buber's I-Thou stance — insisting an enslaved Ood is 'a "he," not an "it"' and addressing Donna, Jack, and Rose each as individuals in 'Journey's End'. Linking this to Nussbaum's claim that wonder widens moral concern and to Kant's dynamic and mathematical sublime, she argues the Doctor needs human companions like Rose, Martha, and Donna as a human-scale reference point that renews his wonder — and with it his ethics — while his wiping of Donna's memory shows the care tradition's dangers of power imbalance.

i-thou.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
i-thou.title: Chapter 34 - Beyond Lies the Wub
i-thou.relation: Dick's first published story dramatizes the moral status of a rational nonhuman: Peterson's wub, a telepathic, philosophical Martian pig-creature, reads minds, discusses Odysseus and individuation, and pleads that it is 'a sensible being like yourselves', yet Captain Franco - obsessed with eating it - freezes it mid-sentence, shoots it looking him in the eye ('Back on the farm we had hogs'), and serves it for dinner, dismissing Peterson's grief with 'It is only organic matter, now.' The wub's personhood is established entirely through language and philosophy, but speech fails to protect it from being treated as meat, and the closing irony - Franco resuming the wub's own Odysseus meditation, as if the mind survived its meal - underscores how thin the line is between person and livestock. The story thus stages the problem of other minds and the ethics of killing sentient beings who demand to be addressed eye-to-eye rather than dined upon.

i-thou.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
i-thou.title: 9. Are You Experienced
