i-thou.relation: Proposes an 'experientialism' — subjective conscious experience as fundamental reality, defended against eliminativists who would explain experience away as illusion — and finds its moral core in Martin Buber: the title song and 'May This Be Love' call the beloved out of an I-It world ('made out of gold and can't be sold') into reciprocal I-You relation ('take hold of my hand'), while 'The Wind Cries Mary,' 'Purple Haze,' and 'Manic Depression' lament love that is absent or unreciprocated. Experiences feel most intensely real, the chapter argues, when the Platonic order of love puts what matters most at stake — which is why kissing the sky, even without being kissed back, is worth recommending.

i-thou.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
i-thou.title: 15. I, Thou, and the Neighborhood
i-thou.relation: James McLachlan pairs Rogers's 'holy ground' between television set and viewer with Buber's turn from ecstatic religion to the everyday after failing the young visitor of 1914 who came to him in need: the I-You relation of full presence versus the I-It of use is what 'It's You I Like' sings. Against Sartre's 'Hell is other people' and Augustine's reading of the burning bush as the omnipotent God, Rogers and Buber (with Rosenzweig's translation of God's name as 'the One who will be present') make listening, presence, and everyday 'twinklings' the substance of neighborly love.

i-thou.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
i-thou.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
i-thou.relation: Edelheit, a rabbi, reads Stewart's Jewish persona as an echo of Martin Buber: both disclaim the titles (philosopher, journalist) yet 'point out the window' at what they have seen, and both practice engagement, 'You shall not withhold yourself', with genuine responsibility as real responding, epitomized for him by the face-to-face Crossfire confrontation. He walks through the 'Matzorian Candidate' segment on the Republican Jewish Coalition (the 'Yarmulkometer' ratings, Michele Bachmann's kibbutz years and mispronounced 'chutzpah'), the 'Faith/Off' Passover-versus-Easter segment pitting a chocolate egg against the Seder plate ('Jews! Camera 3'), and Earth (The Book)'s satirically rewritten Binding of Isaac and Reform-Judaism prayer jokes. All of this is read as Buberian dialogue, mocking religion from within rather than at it, and refusing silence in the lineage of Rabbi Joachim Prinz's warning that the most tragic problem is silence.

i-thou.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
i-thou.title: It Worked
i-thou.relation: Lee reads Jack, Locke, and Desmond as studies in Sartrean bad faith and authenticity: Christian Shephard's Red Sox fatalism is determinism as an excuse for moral failure, Locke swings from a Kierkegaardian leap of faith (pushing the button as his Abraham-and-Isaac trial) into nihilism when the Pearl film suggests the button is a psychological experiment, and Desmond's Humean skepticism yields to sacrificial faith in the fail-safe. He argues Jacob is the show's greatest con man, so Jack's acceptance of destiny in 'The End' remains a free choice rather than predestination. The finale's sideways world then moves Lost from secular existentialism to religious existentialism, read through Buber's I-Thou relation in Sawyer and Juliet's 'It worked' reunion and the all-religions church, where as Gandhi held every path leads to the same place.

i-thou.title: 26_LaRocca_Chapter_025.html
i-thou.relation: Bill Nichols writes an open letter to Errol Morris explaining his bodily 'revulsion' at Standard Operating Procedure, Morris's film on the Abu Ghraib torture photographs. Nichols gives three reasons: the painfully limited, remorseless perspective of the MP guards elevated to mythic screen scale; the morally impossible reenactment tracking shots that put the viewer in the torturers' point of view (compared to Schindler's List); and the total absence of the Iraqi detainees' voices. He faults Morris for decontextualizing and fetishizing the images and forfeiting a moral center, contrasting the film with Rithy Panh's S-21, and casts the missing ethical encounter in terms of Buber's I-Thou relation of mutual honesty while wishing he had Fanon's capacity to treat the perpetrators' suffering.

i-thou.title: Introduction
i-thou.relation: The editors' introduction surveys Nolan's oeuvre from Doodlebug through Interstellar, arguing that like Socrates's gadfly his films sting viewers out of complacency rather than delivering settled answers. It traces a running theme of self-destruction and self-identity: Buber's I-Thou thesis illuminates Following's Cobb and The Young Man (with a Hegelian master-slave twist), Leonard Shelby in Memento must invent a telos to keep his existence meaningful, Descartes's dream argument stands behind Inception's spinning top, and the Joker voices Hobbes on what 'a little anarchy' does to society. It closes by reading Interstellar as the culmination of these themes, with Cooper's partial love for Murph set against Dr. Mann and Prof. Brand, who are willing to squash their humanity to save the species.

i-thou.title: A Better Way of Living Your Life
i-thou.relation: Laura Geuy Akers argues the Doctor lives by a relational ethics of care rather than deontology, utilitarianism, or virtue ethics. Drawing on Noddings's care ethics and Buber's I-Thou versus I-It stance, she shows the Doctor responds to particular others (insisting the Ood is "a he, not an it," addressing each companion individually before surrender) and even ethically cares for the Master. She pairs this with Nussbaum's and Kant's accounts of wonder and the sublime, arguing the Doctor's human companions (Rose, Martha, Donna) restore his sense of wonder and give his immortal life meaning.

i-thou.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
i-thou.title: It Worked
i-thou.relation: Sander Lee reads Jack, Locke, and Desmond through Sartre's bad faith and authenticity and the objectifying 'Look' (the keyhole example), casting Jack the man-of-science as a Humean skeptic who condemns his father's fatalist evasion of responsibility while Locke's devotion to pushing the button is a Kierkegaardian leap of faith modeled on Abraham and Isaac. Desmond David Hume embodies skepticism yet opens to omens and self-sacrifice; and Lee argues the finale's multi-faith 'church' moves Lost from Sartre's secular existentialism toward Kierkegaard and Buber's I-Thou relation, exemplified by Sawyer and Juliet's redemptive bond and Gandhi-like religious universalism.

i-thou.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
i-thou.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
i-thou.relation: Joseph Edelheit hears an echo of Martin Buber in Stewart's Jewish persona and satiric method, likening Buber's 'I am no philosopher… I go to the window and point to what I have seen' to Stewart pointing at media and political hypocrisy. Reading Buber's dialogical I-Thou, ideal of the character-forming teacher, and demand against silence, he interprets 'The Matzorian Candidate,' the Passover-vs-Easter 'Faith/Off' segment, the Earth (The Book) Binding-of-Isaac parody, and Stewart's 'Jews! Camera 3' address as face-to-face, responsible engagement—satire as a valid form of Buberian dialogue against the evil of silence.

i-thou.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
i-thou.title: From There to Here, from Here to There, Diversity Is Everywhere
i-thou.relation: Tanya Jeffcoat builds a philosophy of diversity around 'normative hubris' and 'totalizing tendencies,' using the Sneetches, the butter-battling Yooks and Zooks, and Daisy-Head Mayzie as cases of in-group/out-group dehumanization. Encountering the Other is framed through Buber's I-It versus I-Thou (Yertle treating his subjects as a throne), Fanon on the psychic violence and alienation of the oppressed, McIntosh's invisible knapsack of privilege, and Freire's humanization. Horton and the Lorax model standing with the disenfranchised, and Jeffcoat rebuts moral relativism via universal human rights and Dewey's democracy as a personal way of life that condemns intolerance.

i-thou.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
i-thou.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
i-thou.relation: Mattern argues the heart of good fatherhood is mercy – 'faithful, compassionate love' – as an attitude of the heart, not a technique. Drawing on Aquinas's account of habitus and his ranking of mercy among the greatest virtues, plus Gabriel Marcel's 'creative fidelity,' Solovyov, Jean Vanier, and Karol Wojtyla on love as affirming another's value, he contrasts remote, justice-oriented fathers with empathic ones. He illustrates with overlapping Venn-diagram circles of father and child and with responding to his 7-year-old son's shoplifting through listening and repair rather than spanking.

i-thou.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
i-thou.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
i-thou.relation: Hernandez contrasts 'dark' existentialism — Sartre's café-bound claim that hell is other people and that the self is imprisoned in others' looks (illustrated by Starbucks' Pike Place backlash reshaping its identity), and Camus's absurd alienation — with an 'optimistic existentialism' that finds meaning in community. Drawing on Kierkegaard's Christian love, Jaspers's 'encounter,' Marcel's turn toward the other (her Sweet Eugene's pregnancy story), and above all Buber's I–Thou versus I–It, she argues the coffee community (neighborhood boards, fair-trade activism, the neighborly cup) is an existential ground where isolated bodies-toward-death create shared hope by treating each patron as a Thou rather than a discarded It.

i-thou.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
i-thou.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
i-thou.relation: Silber uses his own Match.com romance with Karin to argue that virtual 'meeting' differs phenomenologically from face-to-face meeting, which Buber's I-Thou (vs I-It) makes into a whole-being encounter that online traces and aspects cannot supply, invoking 'all real living is meeting.' He treats the dating market as a site of Kantian danger, contrasting price with the dignity of persons in the kingdom of ends, and warns that the market's efficiency threatens objectification and commodification. He then deploys Sartre's bad faith, facticity and transcendence, and 'existence precedes essence' to diagnose online self-misrepresentation (lying about height, age, photos) as inauthenticity, while briefly setting Derrida's 'nothing outside the text' against Plato's Phaedrus preference for speech over writing.

i-thou.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
i-thou.title: 19. The Orville as Philosophy The Dangers of Religion
i-thou.relation: The chapter argues that Seth MacFarlane's The Orville is a pointed critique of religion, especially when merged with political and military power. Through the warrior-god Avis worshipped by the Krill (read as stand-ins for militant evangelicals and Islamist jihadists) and the Moclans' patriarchal bigotry, it contends religion is portrayed as archaic and dangerous. It deploys Socrates's Euthyphro argument to reject divine command theory, contrasts the Krill's dogmatic certainty with the secular Union's self-correcting ethics, and invokes Buber's I–Thou to explain the 'de-souling' of outsiders, while defending Lockean separation of church and state against theocracy and theonomistic ethics.

i-thou.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
i-thou.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
i-thou.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.title: E Pluribus Unum
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.relation: Auxier frames Hitchcock's Lifeboat against Garrett Hardin's 'lifeboat ethics' essay, arguing the lifeboat converts political questions into ethical ones by stranding the survivors outside law and politics ('We're on our own here. We can make our own law'). The survivors are ethical pluralists - Rittenhouse lives for money, Kovac for equality, Constance for fame, Joe for God, MacKenzie for care - and their clinging to private versions of the Good lets Nazi captain Willy, whose only principle is survival, manipulate them all. Using Maslow's hierarchy of needs, Auxier shows the boat descending to bare survival, yet argues the mob killing of Willy when he hoards water is moral outrage rather than survival-driven, and that the final rescue scene replays the opening dispute with nobody having grown - a vindication of pluralistic democracy capable of unified action.

maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.title: Can a Serial Killer Be Happy
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.relation: Mike Piero answers whether a serial killer can be happy by mapping Dexter's growth onto Abraham Maslow's hierarchy of needs: the Code secures his physiological and safety needs (don't get caught), Season 2's 'the Code is mine now' and the Narcotics Anonymous meetings open his love needs, the respect of Miami Metro and the Miguel mentorship meet esteem needs, and wanting to live to see Harrison born in 'Do You Take Dexter Morgan?' is self-actualization - 'what a man can be, he must be.' Rita's death at the start of Season 5 threatens a retreat into isolation, but fatherhood keeps supplying moments of Maslow's 'degrees of relative satisfaction.' The upshot is that Dexter, though damaged, has recognizably normal human motivations and a relatively happy, complicated life.

maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.title: 11. I Ain’t No Hollaback Girl!
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.relation: Callens explains Carol's killing of Lizzie in "The Grove" through Kohlberg's stages of moral development, arguing Carol reasons at the post-conventional level (pre-apocalypse law and punishment no longer bind) while Rick, Hershel, and Daryl stay conventional, and then layers Maslow's hierarchy of needs on top: because survival needs are perpetually threatened, characters regress between stages, and only self-actualized Carol accepts reality and makes group-preserving choices like executing Lizzie and mercy-killing Karen and David. Gilligan's justice-versus-care critique supplies the gendered frame - Carol moves to the middle of the justice-care continuum, her diminished care (unlike Season Two's grief over Sophia) is what makes her post-conventional, and her non-lethal Terminus rescue contrasts with Rick's summary execution of Gareth.

maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.title: Notes
maslow-hierarchy-of-needs.relation: The chapter asks why audiences relish stories of civilization's end and answers with psychology: the wasteland is Hobbes's 'nasty, brutish, and short' (raiders abducting Hank, Vault-Tec's experiments on dwellers), yet Ernest Becker's death-denial and Maslow's hierarchy of needs explain the appeal — fiction lets us confront mortality safely while watching characters meet needs for security, control, and meaning. The show's scenes carry the argument: the Vault 33 Council suppressing Lucy's search party trades freedom for safety, Maximus letting Titus bleed out reclaims control of his destiny, and Lucy's gift of life-sustaining vials to the unconscious Ghoul models hope and retained humanity. Apocalypse originally means 'an uncovering', so these narratives reveal what viewers value and let them rehearse their own endings.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
problem-of-other-minds.title: Marnie An Enigma to Herself
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Yanal sets Descartes's two claims about mind - certainty about one's own thoughts (via the method of doubt and the deceiving-evil-genius possibility) and skepticism about other minds (hats and coats that may cover automata) - against Wittgenstein's counters, then reads Shadow of a Doubt and Marnie as Hitchcock's counterexamples. In Shadow of a Doubt the two Charlies, twins in blood and in the film's doubling motifs, are 'transparent' to each other - Young Charlie alone knows her uncle is the Merry Widow Murderer - refuting other-minds skepticism; in Marnie, repressed memory of killing her mother's sailor client leaves Marnie ignorant of her own mind until Mark's amateur therapy recovers it, refuting Cartesian self-certainty. Both films thus side with Wittgenstein: one person can know another's mind, and one can be an enigma to oneself.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
problem-of-other-minds.title: Transformers and Philosophy
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Pike asks what the All Spark's zap would have to do to give brought-to-life vending machines and steering wheels genuine minds, testing logical behaviorism's dispositions and Turing's conversation test against Searle's Chinese Room ('syntax is insufficient for semantics'), and weighing Descartes's God-given soul against physicalist alternatives: functionalism, Searle's biological naturalism, and reductive physicalism. Since we can never access another mind from the inside, he concludes that by abductive inference to the best explanation - Optimus Prime's mourning, planning, and moral decision-making being too complex for mere programming - we have as much reason to credit a Transformer with a mind as any human around us.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
problem-of-other-minds.title: Point-Counterpoint Funny versus Really, Really Funny
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Andrew Terjesen starts from real cases of Onion satire taken literally — a Michigan sheriff warning about al-Qaida telemarketing, the Beijing Evening News plagiarizing 'Congress Threatens To Leave D.C.', Deborah Norville reporting that 58 percent of American exercise is televised — and explains them through the Problem of Other Minds. Descartes' hats-and-cloaks worry and Russell's analogy solution show how we infer that a straight-faced writer is 'just kidding,' but the analogy fails when cultural context, prejudice (Fred Phelps citing the gay-recruitment story, Christians forwarding the Harry Potter Satanism piece), or wishful thinking breaks the comparison with our own joking behavior. The upshot is that humor is engineered misunderstanding — the Onion works by analogy to real news, and could never warn readers off without destroying the joke.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
problem-of-other-minds.title: Empathy in a “More Human than Human” World
problem-of-other-minds.relation: The chapter shows Deckard funding empathy for animals by killing androids, then raises the stakes: since android models keep improving, even close inspection of one's ostensibly 'real' sheep might fail to disclose a clever simulation, which it names as Dick's reconfiguration of the problem of other minds and solipsism. The desert toad, seen 'through Mercer's eyes' and boxed with painstaking care, is revealed by Iran to be electric, so that 'the desert of the real offers safe habitat only for virtual creatures.'

problem-of-other-minds.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
problem-of-other-minds.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Kristin Andrews uses Taylor's silent attempts to show Zira he has a mind - mouthing answers, wiggling his fingers when she mentions the Hopkins Manual Dexterity Test - to stage the problem of other minds, pushing against Descartes's claim that language is required for thought and Mill's argument from analogy, while Dr. Zaius can always redescribe it all as 'a definite gift for mimicry.' Drawing on her fieldwork with the orangutan Cecep (the leaf-wiping pantomime, guiding the frightened Aldrin home from the turtle scare), she argues against reducing mindreading to false-belief tasks and for knowing minds through shared interaction, inductive overhypotheses, and natural context. She ends with an extended-mind point - 'when you're in a cage, you act caged,' and we offload thinking onto our homes and tools - so lab studies can show what apes can do but never what they can't.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
problem-of-other-minds.title: What Are You Laughing At (And Why)? Exploring the Humor of Family Guy
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Runs Hobbes's superiority theory, Freud's relief theory, and Kant's incongruity theory against Family Guy jokes (Peter failing 'What color is a fire truck?' in 'Petarded,' the 1956 workplace sensitivity film in 'I Am Peter, Hear Me Roar,' the fire-truck hunting gazelles) to argue no single theory covers everything. Against Ken Tucker's charge of cheap mean humor, it uses Aristotle's idea that laughter's proper function is enforcing social norms to claim parodies of mean-spirited humor laugh AT the mean-spirited speaker, not his target, and then applies Russell's solution to the problem of other minds to the writers' intentions in 'When You Wish Upon a Weinstein': Peter's established idiocy (volcano-insurance gambler's fallacy) and Cleveland's corrective lines are the context clues that the song mocks anti-Semites rather than Jews.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
problem-of-other-minds.title: NOTES
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Distinguishes Matt Parkman's supernatural telepathy from the 'mundane mind reading' everyone performs, then argues even Matt's power cannot solve the problem of other minds: the suicidal woman's thoughts he hears in the bar ('One Giant Leap') could be part of a Maury-Parkman-style illusion, and a brain-to-brain link could never rule out that others are Chalmers-style philosophical zombies. After grounding the skepticism in Descartes' cogito and method of doubt, it defends our everyday attribution of minds by analogy (Audrey Hanson reading Claire's insincerity) on pragmatic grounds, and maps Matt's progression from hearing thoughts to nightmare manipulation and compulsion onto the four adaptive functions philosophers assign to mind reading: interpretation, prediction, coordination, and influence. It closes by showing why neuroimaging-based technological mind reading remains a pipe dream, since brain recordings are quantitative syntax without semantics.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
problem-of-other-minds.title: How Do We Know What Taylor Swift Is Feeling?
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Asks how Swifties can know what Taylor feels, starting from Descartes' methodic doubt and answering with Edith Stein's phenomenology of empathy (taxonomy lacks Stein): we perceive others' emotions in blushing faces and stormy glares as in 'Would've, Could've, Should've', 'Afterglow', and 'You're Losing Me'. Against Lipps's inner-imitation account, Stein distinguishes empathy from sympathy and oneness, read through 'Long Live (Taylor's Version)' and the Speak Now Tour. R.K. Elliott's expression theory extends this to 'artistic empathy' for songs like 'Ronan' and 'Clean', while conceding limits: since 'betty' is written from a seventeen-year-old boy's perspective, fans know Taylor's expressed feelings, not her biography.

problem-of-other-minds.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
problem-of-other-minds.title: XII - DIRTY HAN DS AN D DIRTY MINDS THE ETHICS OF MIND READING AND MINDWRITING
problem-of-other-minds.relation: Terjesen examines whether telepaths can be trusted, starting epistemically: Descartes' problem of other minds and Russell's analogy answer explain how Xavier's football-field telepathy and the Cuckoos' exoneration of Beak could be verified, and how far Jean's telepathic testimony about Cassandra Nova should be acted on. Utilitarians (Mill) and deontologists then split over mindwriting: Xavier's early memory erasures, the permanent rewrite of a terrorist's personality, and the Magneto mindwipe versus Cyclops and Emma's 'telepathic affair' and Jean's ransacking of Emma's memories, where privacy and intimacy are at stake. Invoking Machiavelli and Walzer, the chapter concludes Xavier's dirty hands are necessary but wrong, so he should feel guilt and step down, lest mindreading mutants become the thing humans rightly fear.

anarchism.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
anarchism.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
anarchism.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. He reads the total improvisation learned at the Acid Tests ('the form that follows chaos'), the band's leaderless 'functional anarchy' — Lesh: if anyone tried to take charge 'it would just dissolve in their hands' — and its flat business hierarchy with roadies as corporate presidents as a spontaneous order lived at the edge of chaos. The Deadhead community's ritual communitas, analyzed through Victor Turner's separation-liminality-reincorporation model, amounts to an 'ironic sacramentalism' that achieves what social contract from Hobbes (force), Locke (property), and Rawls (self-interest) cannot: unity that transcends difference while leaving it in place.

anarchism.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
anarchism.title: An Island of Milk and Honey or Rock Bottom
anarchism.relation: Shaun Young asks whether governmentless Bikini Bottom refutes political philosophy's claim that the good life needs a state: it is not the anarchism of Godwin and Kropotkin (police fines, health inspectors and the Fry Cooks Union constrain liberty), not Marx's communism (Krabs keeps exploiting SpongeBob, whose 'false consciousness' surfaces only briefly in 'Clams'), not the utopias of Plato, Bacon or More (Squidward and Plankton are miserable), and not Nozick's night-watchman state (SpongeBob is arrested for failing to invite police to his party). The lesson he draws: expect neither utopia nor Rock Bottom, because no single theory captures a real (or imaginary undersea) society.

anarchism.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
anarchism.title: Invocation of My Demon Brother
anarchism.relation: Connects the Stones' demonic turn to the counterculture's occult fashions — the Levitate the Pentagon rally, Rosemary's Baby — and to filmmaker Kenneth Anger, disciple of Aleister Crowley, whose "Do What Thou Wilt" law espoused a form of anarchism and whose Lucifer was the light-bearing god, not Christianity's dark devil. Anger cast Jagger as a latter-day Lucifer for Lucifer Rising (with Richards as Beelzebub), and the chapter quotes Jagger's 1967 claim that the teenage "telepathy" at his shows was "a protest against the system," while reading "Jumpin' Jack Flash" through the Spring Heeled Jack folklore.

anarchism.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
anarchism.title: Homeland and Philosophy
anarchism.relation: This standalone section traces terrorism's history and definition, from the French Revolution's Reign of Terror when the state was 'le terroriste' (Robespierre's 'terror is nothing other than justice that is prompt, severe, and inflexible') to the term's reversal onto non-state actors via Russian anarchists like Nechayev. It offers a seven-feature characterization (violence, destruction, indiscriminate harm, psychological trauma, propaganda, policy change, non-state perpetration) matching the UN's 2004 definition, then catalogs often-forgotten American terrorism: the Boston Tea Party reframed as a news report, the Ku Klux Klan's campaign, the Haymarket bombing, the Los Angeles Times and Wall Street bombings by labor radicals and anarchists, the Bath School massacre, the Mad Bomber, the Weather Underground, anti-abortion Army of God killings, and the Unabomber.

anarchism.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
anarchism.title: 9. Anarchy, State, and Apocalypse
anarchism.relation: Da Silva and McKendry test the political legitimacy of four post-apocalyptic governance types: the Claimers' anarchy that collapses into Joe adjudicating 'claims', the Governor's and Rick's dictatorships ('This is not a democracy anymore!'), the prison Council's representative democracy with the three questions as a quasi-constitution, and Terminus's quasi-theocratic cannibal creed ('You're the butcher or you're the cattle'). Using Hobbes's state of nature and war of all against all, hypothetical social contract, and the twin tests of power and morality, they judge even the benevolent Rick-tatorship unjust because concentrated power is fallible and unaccountable. They conclude, with Churchill, that the Council's imperfect democracy is the worst form of government except for all the others.

anarchism.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
anarchism.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
anarchism.relation: Malloy asks whether the two law-breaking vigilantes are criminals and whether any duty to obey the law survives scrutiny. He runs consent theory through Superman surrendering in handcuffs in Man of Steel and the Red Son Superman's residence in the USSR, uses Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's security sovereign against Locke's natural-rights limits, deploys Hume against tacit consent (Batman would never leave Gotham even in No Man's Land), and dismantles gratitude theory (the Kents' adoption involved a sacrificial choice the law cannot make) and fair play (Nozick's Batman-lottery undercuts "I'm not wearing hockey pads"). He lands near Wolff-style philosophical anarchism: Superman's constrained lawbreaking endorses the law's legitimacy while Batman treats law as one more tool in his war, making him a force of chaos.

anarchism.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
anarchism.title: 3. We Willna Be Fooled Again! Wee Free Anarchists!
anarchism.relation: Reading The Wee Free Men, Kugler treats the Nac Mac Feegle, Granny Aching, and Tiffany as embodiments of the anarchist suspicion of political authority, staging Nozick's minimal state and spontaneous protective associations against Huemer's philosophical anarchism from The Problem of Political Authority. The Feegles' creed 'Nae quin! Nae king!', their flight from the exploitative Fairy Queen, the Baron's sheep-killing dog compromise, and the mercy shown the lonely kidnapper Miss Robinson all show law treated as a flexible guideline that must yield to love, community, and care for the weak. Kugler concludes that Pratchett romanticizes anarchism: his anarchists win hearts, watching authority from within the system rather than overthrowing it.

anarchism.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
anarchism.title: 10. Lord Vetinari’s Friendly Guide to Tyranny
anarchism.relation: Alloy stages the debate over Vetinari's legitimacy as letters to the Ankh-Morpork Times: a writer channeling Hobbes defends the contracted sovereign - a 'mortal god' who cannot commit crimes and secures freedom through security - while 'the late Jeremy Bentham' judges the Patrician by the greatest good of the greatest number yet would disenfranchise golems and the 'differently-alive' dead. The anarchist Wolff Paul Roberts rebuts both, denying any right to rule, rejecting tacit consent by residence, and holding up the free golems as models of uncoerced virtue, before a final letter defends Vetinari's limited, functional government. The frame - Vetinari quietly orchestrating the whole correspondence and planning Roberts's next letter - shows tyranny curating its own philosophical defense.

anarchism.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
anarchism.title: 1. The Deed of F’ing Society
anarchism.relation: Rocha reads fsociety's 5/9 logic-bomb attack on E Corp as anarchist 'propaganda of the deed' - a shocking act meant to wake people from their comfortable slumber inside hierarchy - and positions it between Alexander Berkman's violent anarchism (mirroring Phillip Price's 'bullet in the right place') and Gandhi's nonviolent self-suffering, quoting satyagraha and the older Goldman's rejection of violence. He then runs the hack through just war theory's four questions (necessity, proportionality, justification, effectiveness), noting that wiping the debt records also destroyed savings and indirectly got people like Gideon killed, and that fsociety, as Trenton says, never paints the alternative society - so the reader is left to answer whether the deed was justified.

anarchism.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
anarchism.title: 7. What Kind of Revolutionary Is Mr. Robot
anarchism.relation: Ralston traces Mr. Robot's hacktivist philosophy to David Graeber's anarchism behind Occupy Wall Street and to Anonymous's 'moralfags' who hack for a higher cause (Project Chanology as the template for fsociety), then stages the Dewey-Trotsky debate on means and ends: Trotsky's 'Their Morals and Ours' lets the end justify any means, while Dewey's means-end continuum demands experimental, democratic means suited to the end. The verdict: Mr. Robot's ends are anarchist and his means pragmatist - he will frame Terry Colby and risk lives at Steel Mountain, but rejects means like actual slavery that would betray the movement's own ideal of liberation.

anarchism.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
anarchism.title: 18. What Makes Rick Tick
anarchism.relation: Surveying Rick's values area by area, a many-worlds multiverse, atheism ('There is no God, Summer'), scientism, egoistic ethics, hatred of all government, and rap as today's Romanticism, the chapter rejects absurdism, existentialism, nihilism, and even Max Stirner's individualist anarchism, which it says fits the Citadel of Ricks rather than the loner Rick. Its thesis is that Rick is an Ayn Rand Objectivist: Rand's ideal man of reason, independence, and rejection of altruism, collectivism, and mysticism, with Jerry as the pity-parasite anti-ideal exposed in 'The Whirly Dirly Conspiracy'. It warns that infinite choice risks the paradox of hedonism, pointing to Rick's half-hearted suicide machine after Unity, and ends that only chosen constructive goals, perhaps a kinder Rick, could save him, if some other universe didn't already have that Rick.

anarchism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
anarchism.title: The Anarchist You Are
anarchism.relation: Argues anarchism is everywhere in ATLA even though nobody names it: Chomsky's test of unjustified hierarchies condemns the Dai Li, High Monk Pasang's arbitrary removal of Aang from Gyatso's care, and Commander Zhao's rank-pulling, while Kropotkin's mutual aid — humans as fundamentally cooperative — appears in Iroh's non-coercive mentoring of Zuko, Senlin Village's solidarity, and the 'The Chase' lesson that Toph's 'I can carry my own weight' misses how Team Avatar carries each other. Even Zaheer of Korra is exposed as no anarchist, and Iroh's self-effacing, power-sharing teaching (like Katara teaching Aang waterbending) models the only justified use of power. Aang thinking for himself against the past Avatars' unanimous advice to kill Ozai, and his joyfulness amid revolution, make him the true anarchist.

anarchism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
anarchism.title: The Anarchist You Are
anarchism.relation: Argues that anarchism, understood through David Graeber's consensus-based action, Noam Chomsky's demand that hierarchies justify themselves, and Kropotkin's mutual aid, runs all through ATLA even though no character calls themselves an anarchist. The Dai Li are an unjustified hierarchy that delivers Ba Sing Se to the very conquest it claims to prevent, High Monk Pasang's arbitrary rank authority over Gyatso and Aang causes the century-long catastrophe, and Zhao embodies domination justified by 'fire is the superior element', whereas justified power is self-effacing (Iroh mentoring Zuko without coercion, Katara teaching Aang waterbending). Toph's insistence that she can 'carry my own weight' in 'The Chase' dramatizes the mutual-aid lesson that letting those who love you help you is part of the cooperative human nature Kropotkin opposed to the Hobbesian view, and Zaheer in Korra, who rules by fear, shows that a chaos-bringer is no anarchist at all, while playful, communal Aang is.

anarchism.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
anarchism.title: Theorizing Government
anarchism.relation: Tony Spanakos argues that Gotham's government, not Bruce's psyche, explains Batman: the state failed at Crime Alley, and nearly every major character reacts to a state that is either too weak or too restrictive. Working from Max Weber's definition of the state as monopoly on legitimate violence, Hobbes's Leviathan, and Nietzsche's state as 'new idol,' he reads Year One's corrupt Commissioner Loeb, Year Two's self-appointed Reaper, Anarky's failed anarchist dystopia, Two-Face's broken faith in the law, and The Dark Knight Returns' state-loyal Superman and Commissioner Yindel. The Batman-Gordon partnership emerges as a precarious unofficial order in which Gordon tolerates the one exception to the state's monopoly on violence.

anarchism.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
anarchism.title: Leo Tolstoy, Sorcerer-Defender Supreme
anarchism.relation: The chapter pairs Strange's midlife collapse with Tolstoy's crisis in A Confession—both famous egotists who found their glittering lives 'a stupid fraud'—using Tolstoy's fable of the traveler licking honey above the dragon of death to read Strange's desperate medical questing as vain honey-licking. It lays out Tolstoy's doctrine of nonresistance: violence is forcing others against their will, every act of violent resistance multiplies evil, and the state's division of cruelty makes killing mechanical, then asks whether Tolstoy could accept Strange's metaphysical war, concluding from Tolstoy's remark that he would axe a bear to save a peasant (but not kill the highwayman) that he could endorse magical violence against Dormammu while still forbidding violence against human beings.

anarchism.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
anarchism.title: Notes
anarchism.relation: Skoble argues the Mad Max world is misread as anarchy: Immortan Joe, Aunty Entity, and Humungus are genuine rulers, so the Wasteland depicts tyrannical bad government, not 'no rulers'. Against Hobbes's claim that only fear of a sovereign produces order, he cites organically evolved order (medieval merchant law, the common law, private arbitration firms) and Locke's mere 'inconveniences' of statelessness to argue peaceful anarchism is possible and stable. Thunderdome's 'two men enter, one man leaves' shows the films' dispute resolution is power-based trial by combat, not the consent-based voluntary order anarchism envisions.

anarchism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
anarchism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
anarchism.relation: Reads John Teller's failed 'off the social grid' experiment through the human-nature debate: Mencius's seed of sympathy (even Tig recoils at Dante's dogfights) and Rousseau's naturally good man corrupted by society inspired J.T.'s Goldman-fed anarchism, while Mill and Xunzi counter that virtue is a victory over instinct. Hobbes supplies the real diagnosis—not innate violence but the logic of anarchy among free and equal rivals: competition (the Mayans blowing up the warehouse), diffidence (first-strike temptations against Zobelle), and glory (Jax unable to let the bike-sitting insult pass). Clay's rule that 'retaliation must be harsh and immediate' and the escalating Tig–Veronica Pope–Damon Pope–Opie bloodbath show deterrence fueling cycles of violence, so the only escape from the 'nasty, brutish, and short' fringe is the Leviathan's social grid.

anarchism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
anarchism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
anarchism.relation: Explains what anarchism actually demands—rejection of external authority, voluntary association, and faith that people need no coercion to cooperate—and measures SAMCRO against it: the club's president, church votes, chain of command, and the impossibility of Jax negotiating an exit all betray Momma Anarchy. The individualist/collectivist debate inside anarchism maps onto J.T., who retreats to Nomad and Belfast when the collective disappoints his individualist ideal, versus Jax, whose commitment to family keeps him building the collective. Clay appears as the anti-anarchist 'stone-cold egoist' who rigs votes and kills suspected rats, and the chapter argues the experiment was doomed twice over: the founding Vietnam vets' military hierarchy, and the club's dependence on the capitalist society and state agencies (CIA RICO leverage) it rejects.

anarchism.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
anarchism.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
anarchism.relation: Weighs Marx against Heidegger on whether SAMCRO should fight its history. Teller-Morrow read as petit-bourgeois capitalism turns the Mayans' pilot-episode raid into industrial sabotage and Nero's escort business into exploitation; read through Proudhon, Kropotkin, and Emma Goldman — whose essay John Teller found quoted on a Nevada wall — the club is an anarcho-syndicalist commune with democratic chapel votes, Kropotkin's mutual aid to widows like Lyla, and Tara as its socialized healthcare. Heidegger's historicity gives the resolution: Jax cannot escape the past (the Irish deal only with Clay; 'The sting of that betrayal ain't gonna fade') but can appropriate it authentically, and Pope's forced choice of a victim in 'Laying Pipe' confronts him with being-toward-death.

anarchism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
anarchism.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
anarchism.relation: Alloy uses the problem of political obligation to split the heroes: against Plato's Crito, where Socrates refuses escape because even bad laws bind, Bruce Wayne simply flees arrest in Bruce Wayne: Murderer?/Fugitive, treating law as a tool of his war. He tests consent theory through Superman's chosen handcuffs in Man of Steel and Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's 'mortal god' versus Locke's natural-rights standard, lets Hume's objection sink tacit consent (Red Son Superman cannot really emigrate, and Batman would never leave Gotham), rejects gratitude theory via the Kents' adoption of Kal-El, and dismantles Batman's 'I'm not wearing hockey pads' defense with Nozick's Batman-lottery — concluding Superman's law-conforming restraint protects the public from him becoming Luthor's 'alien overlord', while answerable-to-no-one Batman remains a force of chaos.

anarchism.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
anarchism.title: Anarchism and the Beats
anarchism.relation: Ed D'Angelo argues the Beats had a philosophy after all: a romantic bohemian anarchism that made poetry a means to a religious transformation of consciousness, with political change following consciousness rather than the reverse. He shows Ginsberg inverting Plato's rationalist hierarchy (grounding reason in imagination and the body) and reads Beat 'criminality' as a shamanic journey to the unconscious underworld, distinct from Mailer's macho 'White Negro' hipster. He traces their lineage through Greenwich Village bohemia, Proudhon/Bakunin/Kropotkin anarchism, and pacifist anarchists like Rexroth and Dellinger, arguing the Beats rejected Marxist materialism and class warfare, and that the movement was 'born' out of Rexroth's anarchist poetry circle at the 1955 Six Gallery reading of 'Howl.'

anarchism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
anarchism.title: 5. To Resist Despair
anarchism.relation: Peterson defines being punk through three interlocking virtues - authenticity (via Varga and Guignon's account as used by Heidegger, Beauvoir, and Sartre), Sartrean freedom ('existence precedes essence'), and questioning authority, defended with Robert Paul Wolff's argument that obeying authority cancels autonomy. The Slits' Palmolive, Alice Bag, Johnny Ramone's cheap Mosrite, and Harley Flanagan show DIY as the punk response to Sartrean facticity, Operation Ivy's 'Knowledge' recalls Socratic ignorance as punk humility, and she concludes that even SLC Punk's Stevo going to Harvard can remain punk, since only striving to live authentically counts.

anarchism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
anarchism.title: 15. Punk Political Philosophy
anarchism.relation: Sulek finds punk's only consistent political feature to be contempt for authority, and models its 'apolitical politics without rulers' on self-organizing civil society: Adam Smith's invisible hand and Adam Ferguson's civil society - dismissed by Hegel and Marx but resurrected by Václav Havel and East European dissidents. Bob Geldof's Band Aid/Live Aid 'punk diplomacy' (a 'constituency of compassion' saying the unsayable to Ethiopian officials) and the improbable line from the Velvet Underground via Havel to the Plastic People of the Universe, Charter 77, and the Velvet Revolution show punk 'living in truth' against entropic ideology-as-ritual: destroying stagnant cultural regimes while owing them the building of alternatives.

anarchism.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
anarchism.title: 16. Punk Politics
anarchism.relation: Prinz surveys punk's political paradox - anarchist punks from Crass and Rock Against Racism to straight edge versus the fascist flirtation of skinheads, the National Front, and Skrewdriver's 'White Power' - and tests four candidate unifiers (anti-authoritarianism, nihilism, individualism, and McLaren's politics of boredom), finding each one-sided. He proposes instead a politics of disaffection: alienation and negative affect toward the status quo that spans anarchist, Nazi, and apolitical punks alike, making punk a confrontational counterculture that says 'Fuck you' with a self-satisfied sneer, even if it never ended a war like the hippies claimed to.

anarchism.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
anarchism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
anarchism.relation: Halbert uses a Hawaiian route-setter friend upset that his 'secret' crag went public to argue climbing culture is a gift economy that defies Locke's labor theory of property and the self-interest of Locke and Adam Smith. Route setters spend money and labor establishing climbs, then give them freely to a commons, exemplifying Kropotkin's social-anarchist mutual aid over Social Darwinist competition. Citing the Red River Gorge Coalition and Muir Valley, she recasts Hardin's tragedy of the commons as Carol Rose's 'comedy of the commons,' where more participants enhance rather than diminish the shared value.

anarchism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
anarchism.title: 92. V for Vendetta as Philosophy Victory Through the Virtues of Anarchy
anarchism.relation: Nisley argues that Moore and Lloyd's V for Vendetta justifies V's violent rebellion against the Norsefire regime through Locke: the fascist state seized power without consent, tortured and experimented on citizens (V at Larkhill), and violated natural rights, thereby placing itself in a state of war so the people may overthrow it. Using Aristotle on deviant constitutions and the beast-like tyrant (Adam Susan) who lacks practical wisdom, and contrasting Locke's tolerable state of nature with Hobbes's brutal one, the chapter concludes the citizens should rebuild a rights-protecting social contract rather than V's leaderless anarchy, and maps the argument onto real-world 2020 events (BLM riots vs. the Whitmer kidnapping plot).

one-dimensional-man.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
one-dimensional-man.title: Forgetting the Love We Bring
one-dimensional-man.relation: John Drabinski argues that the Deadhead parking lot is an 'occasional community' offering real hope against modernity's managed, one-dimensional life. Starting from his own Amherst-to-Worcester commuter routine read through Wittgenstein's forms of life — a community of nodding strangers at the same mini-marts — he stages Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Bauman's managed death as the deadening background against which such moments crack open. Where the commuter's community stays merely occasional, the parking lot's saturated friendship and shared undergoing (com-passion, good trip and bad, frat guy comforting and comforted) converts occasion into a genuine alternative ethos, drawing on Heidegger's sense of ethos as dwelling place — an everyday miracle of conversion he says we need now more than ever.

one-dimensional-man.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
one-dimensional-man.title: Springsteen’s Revolution
one-dimensional-man.relation: Anderson and Anderson open with the Che Guevara t-shirt problem and Marcuse's one-dimensional man: the system assimilates protest, so internal critique (Springsteen on the cover of Rolling Stone, its Chevrolet calendar, the Eagles sold at Wal-Mart, Adorno's verdict on co-opted popular music) is a sop to Cerberus. Against this they set Springsteen's own account of his music as 'a very long conversation with my audience' — a transactional public service — and argue he survives the co-optation charge as a 'Socratic revolutionary' who, like Socrates refusing to leave Athens, works from within: listening without obeying ('I liked the old Bruce better'), refusing to ride the Born to Run wave, turning to Guthrie and Seeger, and drawing no hard conclusions, only opening spaces of reflection ('Born in the U.S.A.', 'Radio Nowhere', 'Long Walk Home'). Revolution is just another form of work — practice, sweat, and the personal job of 'growin' up.'

one-dimensional-man.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
one-dimensional-man.title: Where Pink Floyd Ends and Radiohead Begins
one-dimensional-man.relation: Reisch asks whether Radiohead is the Pink Floyd of the twenty-first century and answers that the comparison misleads: where Barrett-era Floyd used electronics to escape into psychedelic fantasy, Radiohead's apparent space-rock is phenomenological, giving voice to pre-reflective experience of technological modern life. He reads 'No Surprises' (Yorke singing with his head in a filling glass sphere) as a study in the political infantilization of commuters, and OK Computer's car crash ('Airbag'), 'Let Down', and 'Lucky' as registering the feel of a fragile, technology-saturated world. Quoting Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Chomsky on manufactured consent, he argues we can see no alternative to the technologically rational system, and then, against Descartes' priority of the isolated 'I', invokes Heidegger's Being-in-the-world and Merleau-Ponty's embodied subject to suggest that our deepening immersion in technology may be changing the self itself — the truth the collapsing pedestrians of the 'Just' video cannot face.

one-dimensional-man.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
one-dimensional-man.title: But Does Political Satire Promote Democratic Values
one-dimensional-man.relation: Michael Tiboris and Kory Schaff answer their title question affirmatively: Colbert's satire promotes democratic values by practicing Foucault's parrhesia - fearless speech that speaks the truth freely, functions as criticism of interlocutor and self, and flows from moral duty - unlike bumper-sticker assertion, since it enters risky dialogue and invites being refuted. Against this stands a corporate-consolidated media ('monopoly of meaning' from GE, Viacom, News Corp, Time-Warner) whose framing, slanting, and spinning - McCain's 'transcendental' war, the Obama-dresses-like-Ahmadinejad story, WMD as Word of the Year - exemplify Marcuse's one-dimensional thought absorbing oppositional language ('clean bomb,' 'harmless fall-out'). The WØRD models parrhesiastic critique by speaking media's own language while the bullet points undercut it ('Definitions will greet us as liberators'), exposing how politicians and pundits merely appear truthful and teaching viewers their own duty of critical assessment.

one-dimensional-man.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
one-dimensional-man.title: Social Networking - How to Win Virtual Friends and Influence Virtual People
one-dimensional-man.relation: Written as a breakup letter to Facebook, the chapter first reconstructs the Frankfurt School hope that new media could overcome old mass media's passivity — Horkheimer and Adorno's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man, Althusser's ideology as the form of media — and then tests the site against Ivan Illich's criteria for 'convivial tools.' Briggle finds Facebook fails on Illich's terms: its public walls and News Feed force self-censored persona management before a mixed audience, and its shapeless, undifferentiated flood of updates leaves the user disoriented like Nietzsche's madman after the death of God. Because the site's 'grain' channels users into 'reluctant, hapless exhibitionism' and even imposes the obligation to join, he logs off, concluding that tools reflect our image more than they remake it.

one-dimensional-man.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
one-dimensional-man.title: Justified and Philosophy
one-dimensional-man.relation: The chapter argues coal made Boyd Crowder possible: company scrip, Bloody Harlan's union-busting terror, black lung (Boyd's would-be assassin takes the bridge job because mining ruined his lungs), and Black Pike's mountaintop removal leave Harlan no viable work outside the mines, so crime is the rational alternative. It reads this through Hegel's 'rabble' from the Philosophy of Right - civil society is never wealthy enough to prevent an excess of poverty, and the rabble loses the honor of self-support - plus Marcuse's affluent-society critique of an existence that 'violently defends its own servitude'. Boyd's outlawry, which sets its own code above mere criminality, is a rebellion against being pushed into the rabble, and Hegel's remedy of emigration explains why leaving Harlan is the only escape, though the coal train hauls coal out while the people stay.

one-dimensional-man.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
one-dimensional-man.title: 3. The Only Chapter in This Book You Need to Read!
one-dimensional-man.relation: Writing as two bickering versions of himself from different universes, Karavitis reads Deadpool Kills Deadpool as showing that the multiverse of Deadpools is the delusion of a single narcissist: the alternate 'Pools' are mirror-image projections of himself (Lacan's mirror stage), his self-love is Rousseau's pathological amour propre rather than healthy amour de soi, and his claim to be the progenitor of all reality is solipsism—hence there is no fourth wall. Freud, Fromm, and Marcuse supply rival diagnoses of that narcissism, from arrested development to proto-fascist willfulness to authentic rebellion against social control through unconscious conformity. A closing twist argues philosophers who claim sole access to truth are the same solipsistic narcissists, which would make Socrates, who never claimed a final answer, the only true philosopher.

one-dimensional-man.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
one-dimensional-man.title: Resistance
one-dimensional-man.relation: Reading Fifteen Million Merits through Marx, the chapter treats Bing's world of endless pedaling, Wraith Babes, and Hot Shot as a commodity society in which people themselves carry use and exchange values — Oliver the 'lemon,' Glee deemed 'quite worthless,' Abi's unsellable papier-mache penguin discarded as detritus. Marx's commodity fetish explains the universalized pricing in merits, and Lukacs-style reification shows things commanding people (Cuppliance compelling compliance). Adorno's culture industry explains why all the shows share one form and why Bing's glass-shard rebellion is absorbed as just another commodity, while Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man supplies the hope that reason, love (Bing's love for Abi as something 'real'), and switching off the media can still seed resistance.

one-dimensional-man.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
one-dimensional-man.title: Things Worth Believing
one-dimensional-man.relation: Butterfield stages the Frankfurt School critique of her own Disney love: Marx's three alienations (from work, from others, from species-being) explain the Seven Dwarfs' 'dig dig dig' and the FastPass-scheduled vacation that converts leisure into consumption, while Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man diagnoses the parks' engineered euphoria and 'false needs' as a 'comfortable, smooth, reasonable, democratic unfreedom' that blunts protest — with Adorno adding that consumers see through the advertising and buy anyway. Against the critic, she argues a Disney trip done right can challenge alienation by reviving play, family togetherness, and childlike belief in 'things worth believing.'

one-dimensional-man.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
one-dimensional-man.title: Television and Existential Awakening
one-dimensional-man.relation: Jaarsma argues Mad Men dramatizes an existential rather than Kantian-enlightenment model of advertising: Don's 'freedom from fear' pitch ('Whatever you are doing is okay. You are okay') sells escape from the anxiety of real choice, which is precisely Sartrean bad faith and what de Beauvoir calls the stagnant 'happiness' of women rewarded for being the other. Betty on her psychiatrist's couch, Peggy measured by Joan's paper-bag mirror and the Playtex bullet-bra silhouette, and the closeted Salvatore all internalize the dominant values Marcuse describes, finding meaning in conformity to the objectifying gaze ('bras are for men; women want to see themselves the way men see them'). Rachel Menken, who refuses to 'put on an apron' and calls out the contingency of gendered embodiment, models authenticity as choosing to choose, and the chapter closes with the hope that television itself can occasion the viewer's existential awakening.

one-dimensional-man.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
one-dimensional-man.title: Indiscernibles and Autonomous Viewers “Time to Write my Own Fucking Story”
one-dimensional-man.relation: Forest and Beckley-Forest ask whether Westworld is self-referential 'high art' or 'meta-kitsch,' tracing aesthetic modernism from Kant's subjective turn through Greenberg's avant-garde/kitsch split and Adorno's autonomous versus heteronomous art. They read Sizemore's clichéd Western narratives and the park's stock characters as commodified kitsch that mirrors the show's own corporate constraints under HBO, and use Danto's Brillo Box problem of indiscernibles to argue that host/guest and entertainment/art distinctions lie in the viewer's reflection. Dolores's line 'when I discover who I am, I'll be free' models the Adorno-style liberation available to an alert viewer.

one-dimensional-man.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
one-dimensional-man.relation: Zietsma reads Hulk and Taking Woodstock as antiwar films that subvert the hegemonic culture of heroic violence, fitting Lackey's category of universal (Gandhian/early-Christian) pacifism. He argues both films disturb their genre's expected narrative and demasculinize the hero: Elliot the gay nonviolent hero and the transgender vet Vilma, and a weeping Hulk who is rescued by Betty and finally gives up his power rather than kill David Banner. He reads the bathroom-mirror 'Puny human' scene as an inverted Lacanian mirror stage unmasking America's violent militarism, framing the Vietnam War and war on terror as violence that only begets more violence.

one-dimensional-man.title: William Burroughs as Philosopher From Beat Morality to Third Worldism to Continental Theory
one-dimensional-man.relation: Jones Irwin makes the case for 'Burroughs as philosopher,' tracing an 'impassioned moralism' and antihumanism (human as adjective, not noun) that separates him from other Beats and postmodernists. He links Burroughs's critique of alienation to Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and to Sartrean existentialism and bad faith ('there are no victims, just accomplices'), and reads the Beats' 'third force' Third Worldism via Freire, Fanon's Wretched of the Earth, and Paz. Close readings of Naked Lunch's 'Bradley the Buyer' and the sex-and-death delirium of 'AJ's Annual Party' connect Burroughs to Artaud's body without organs, Bataille's Sadean tradition, and Derrida's deconstruction of embodiment and 'distance touching.'

one-dimensional-man.title: The Politics of Mad Science in The Fly and Dead Ringers
one-dimensional-man.relation: R. Barton Palmer reads The Fly and Dead Ringers as a diptych on 'mad science' descended from Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde rather than Frankenstein, in which the scientist turns the investigative gaze on himself and self-destructs. He grounds this in the Frankfurt School critique of Enlightenment (Adorno and Horkheimer's Dialectic of Enlightenment, Bacon's domination of nature, Marcuse's Eros and Civilization): Brundle's telepod and the Mantle twins' surgery expose the failure of Baconian objectivity and rationalization, with monstrousness emerging from within the divided self.

one-dimensional-man.title: From “Impassioned Morality” to “Bloodless Agnosticism” A Philosophy of David Cronenberg through the Burroughs
one-dimensional-man.relation: Jones Irwin analyzes Cronenberg's adaptations of Burroughs's Naked Lunch and Ballard's Crash, arguing that while all three share an aesthetic of body horror and a Nietzschean perspectivist experimentalism, Burroughs and Ballard hold an 'impassioned moralism' (Crash as cautionary tale, Marcuse's one-dimensional man, an ethics of complicity and responsibility) that Cronenberg replaces with 'bloodless agnosticism.' Cronenberg aestheticizes Burroughs's wife-killing and reads Crash literally, using Plato's appearance/reality (cave) distinction to show he strips out the sociopolitical and moral frame the writers intended.

one-dimensional-man.book: 260 - The Daily Show and Philosophy - Moments of Zen in the Art of Fake News
one-dimensional-man.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
one-dimensional-man.relation: Gerald Erion reads The Daily Show through Neil Postman's Amusing Ourselves to Death, arguing that Stewart's opening headline mockery of hurricane 'reporters in canoes,' 'Senior Correspondents,' and graphics packages like 'Mess O'Potamia' targets not the day's events but television's own entertainment bias, which renders even serious news trivial. He treats Stewart's Crossfire plea to 'stop hurting America,' the Jim Cramer 'Brawl Street' interview, and the Rally to Restore Sanity's '24-hour politico pundit perpetual panic conflictinator' as Postman-style critiques that a medium built to amuse cannot carry rational public discourse.

one-dimensional-man.title: 19. Looking Like Number 12
one-dimensional-man.relation: Busk reads 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' through Horkheimer and Adorno's 'culture industry' and a philosophical account of subjectivity as active, critical agency. Marilyn's forced 'Transformation' into a standardized model (with banned books, 'Instant Smile,' and 'super soccer') dramatizes how commodified mass culture produces conformist, mannequin-like subjects who cannot resist—linking it to 'The After Hours,' where Marsha is literally a department-store mannequin. Yet Marilyn's and Marsha's very existence, like Adorno's theory, is a faint hopeful sign that critical subjectivity survives.

one-dimensional-man.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
one-dimensional-man.title: 40. Deadpool as Philosophy Using Humor to Rebel Against the System
one-dimensional-man.relation: Brake argues that Deadpool advances an implicit thesis about humor as a threefold vehicle of liberation, testing it against Horkheimer and Adorno's Frankfurt School charge that the culture industry produces interchangeable, aesthetically impoverished pop-culture 'trash' (the formulaic MCU) that pacifies workers, and Marcuse's warning that revolutionary material gets absorbed as just another commodity. Following Kathryn Tanner's rejoinder that consumers can creatively repurpose pop culture, he shows Wade Wilson's self-mocking, fourth-wall-breaking humor achieving personal liberation from tragedy (invoking Freud on humor as the ego's assertion of invulnerability), liberation from the oppressive Mutant Factory by exposing Ajax/Francis's vulnerability and asserting his own autonomy, and a partial liberation from superhero genre tropes, while conceding humor's reactionary tendency to reinforce the status quo since Deadpool ultimately reproduces the genre and hands Disney its money.

one-dimensional-man.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
one-dimensional-man.title: 67. Hari Kondabolu as Philosopher Enacting a Philosophy of Liberation
one-dimensional-man.relation: Heppard frames Kondabolu—who resists the 'political comic' label—as enacting Enrique Dussel's 'philosophy of liberation' and Marcuse's aesthetics of liberation: comedy as 'barbarian philosophy' spoken from the periphery. Kondabolu's Swiftian 'eat the rich' health-care proposal, his 'White Chocolate Joke,' 'Feminist Dick Joke,' Columbus/Joe DiMaggio bit, and Bobby Jindal takedown rupture the audience's identification with white supremacy, patriarchy, and liberal hypocrisy (negative freedom) while his absurd alternatives exercise the 'radical imagination' (positive freedom). Heppard concludes that although comedians are not revolutionaries, the revolution must be funny.

locke-labor-property.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
locke-labor-property.title: A Solution Dissolving Special Status
locke-labor-property.relation: Peter Bradley uses the Dead's taping ethos and the 2005 Archive.org shutdown to argue copyright wrongly grants authors special status. Distinguishing natural from conventional morality (the four-year-old who knows hitting Jenny stays wrong even if the teacher allows it), he contends that respect for irreducibly unique creative expression — not authorial intent, and not Bob Weir's appeal to the covered songwriters' rights — grounds the tapers' moral code, since Olivier could not copyright his double-cast Hamlet ghost and Woody Guthrie welcomed copyists. Ownership means control, from one's own labor outward; but a performance, like another person, is metaphysically impossible to control, and in the digital world (per Barlow) recordings escape physical control entirely — so authorship should be dissolved into improvisational performance, with published works treated like live recordings rather than rigid canonical objects.

locke-labor-property.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
locke-labor-property.title: Coda
locke-labor-property.relation: White asks whether fans who trade or sell Led Zeppelin bootlegs wrong the band, given how little official live material it released. He weighs Locke's labor-mixing account of property (the band creates the performance, but tapers 'mix their labor' too), the legal view of property as a bundle of rights, and rule-utilitarian arguments that bootlegs promote the band without cutting into sales of studio albums. He concludes with Ronald Dworkin's point that rights trump utility: if the live performance is the band's property, the band's choice to withhold it binds fans whatever happiness wider distribution would produce.

locke-labor-property.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
locke-labor-property.title: Equivalent Exchange
locke-labor-property.relation: Reads alchemy's law of equivalent exchange as a parable of capitalism: Locke's labor-mixing argument explains how hours of a life become property and why money is 'distilled life'; Aristotle's attack on limitless wealth-getting (the Midas problem) and Aquinas's capital vices explain how pursuing money for its own sake brings the homunculi — Greed, Pride, and the Sloth the Elric brothers' forbidden act produced — into the world. Marx's 1844 Manuscripts supply the punchline that money performs 'human alchemy' on people, buying their time, esteem, and bodies the way red stones are made from sacrificed humans, so the chapter concludes that capital, like the Philosopher's Stone, profits only by consuming lives and that markets must be held to a promise of fairness and care beyond mere exchange.

locke-labor-property.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
locke-labor-property.title: No Matter How You Flip the Patty . .
locke-labor-property.relation: Michael Dodge asks whether Krabs may guard the Krabby Patty formula, sorting Bikini Bottom's property into collective, communal (Jellyfish Fields) and private, and deploying the tragedy of the commons — Krabs's jellyfish-squeezing factory in 'Jellyfish Hunter' — to show why shared resources get rationally overexploited. Hobbes grounds Krabs's right in sovereign enforcement (without the law, 'Pineapple Fever''s chalk-line household collapses into animals fighting over the fridge), Locke in labor-mixing, with Krabs's identity bound to his patties since 'Help Wanted', and Hume in conventions of justice born of selfishness and scarcity. All three support Krabs's legal and moral right to his secret recipe against Plankton.

locke-labor-property.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
locke-labor-property.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
locke-labor-property.relation: Jason Walker argues the zombie apocalypse is a Lockean rather than Hobbesian state of nature: rights to life, liberty, and property persist without government. Rick's 'I don't think those rules apply anymore' to Andrea over the mermaid necklace is justified by Locke's spoilage and 'enough and as good' provisos - the owner is almost certainly dead and the necklace would otherwise lie forever wasted - while Morgan's house-squatting, which protects the Thompsons' home, and Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo's nursing-home defenders show self-ownership and norms at work. The counter-cases, Chris's cannibal band ('a man's gotta eat') and the Governor, who treat persons as mere means, live out Hobbes's war of all against all and are destroyed by the Lockean right to punish that victims retain.

locke-labor-property.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
locke-labor-property.title: 4 On the Origin of the State
locke-labor-property.relation: Opening with Newt Gingrich's complaint that students 'don't read enough Locke' and the Chinese premier's appeal to Rousseau, the chapter compares the three contract theorists' states of nature and purposes of government: Hobbes's war of every man against every man yielding an absolute sovereign with no separation of powers, Locke's peaceful nature in which mixing labor with land creates property and money then creates inequality, so that government's 'great and chief end' is protecting property through limited, separated powers and no food stamps, and Rousseau's compassionate natural humans corrupted when the first man enclosed land, so the state was founded on fraud and a general will that should 'force him to be free' and give people food stamps. Smith then reads the actual US founding as a chaste Lockean contract 'bastardized' on race and sex - the Declaration plagiarized from Locke, Abigail Adams's 'remember the ladies' laughed off, Dred Scott, with the 14th Amendment as the de-bastardizing 'Charter of Universal Freedom' - while Engels derives the state historically from the Iroquois and Greek gens, private property and class conflict. A final section documents white supremacy inside the tradition (Kant inventing the scientific concept of race, Hegel and Hume on Black inferiority), John Stuart Mill's 'Negro Question' as the tradition's decisive anti-racist break, Locke's own entanglements with the slave trade, and Marx's condemnation of slavery as super-exploitation.

locke-labor-property.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
locke-labor-property.title: 3. Will the Real American Hero Please Stand Up
locke-labor-property.relation: Samuelson argues Tony Stark is the real American hero because he embodies the Locke-to-Smith lineage of American values - natural rights, property from mixing labor, free trade and the invisible hand, plus Smithian sympathy - carried forward into twenty-first-century neoliberalism, from Stark Industries to backing the Registration Act. Steve, by contrast, keeps abandoning the Captain America identity (Nomad after the Secret Empire, The Captain under Nuke's government, handing the shield to Bucky and Sam Wilson) whenever America betrays the dream, and admits his true fight is against bullies and for human rights everywhere. Hence Cap is a great hero but not strictly an American one, while Tony lives American values practically, warts and all.

locke-labor-property.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
locke-labor-property.title: Selling Ol’ Shellhead
locke-labor-property.relation: Malloy uses Spymaster's theft of Stark's armor designs in the Armor Wars and the U.S. government's legally valid appropriation of the technology after Tony announces 'I am Iron Man' to test two theories of property. Locke's natural-law view makes the designs an extension of Stark's laboring self — stealing them is like taking an arm — while Hume's social-contract view treats property as a useful convention whose violation makes the thief an enemy of society itself, and Rousseau supplies the cautionary image of the first man who fenced ground and said 'This is mine.' A closing thought experiment in which Tony sells Iron Man outright (like Siegel and Schuster selling Superman) argues that intellectual property can never be fully alienated: whoever wore the armor, Tony would still be Iron Man.

locke-labor-property.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
locke-labor-property.title: Notes
locke-labor-property.relation: Gettings asks whether LEGO set #21103, the Cuusoo DeLorean Time Machine, is numerically identical to Team BTTF's original fan design — and why the fans deserve credit and royalties. Neither matter (his 1982 attic spaceship with bricks replaced one by one) nor form (a license plate added here or there) settles identity, as the Ship of Theseus puzzle and Hobbes' reassembly variation show, analyzed through Aristotle's matter/form distinction for substances. He adopts the causal/historical view: the released set continuously descends from the fans' submission just as the adult author descends from the boy who built the spaceship, and this same historical origin, in Lockean fashion, is what grounds the designers' labor-mixing property right — the musician-and-producer analogy explaining why Team BTTF keeps the larger share of credit.

locke-labor-property.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
locke-labor-property.title: Justice for All? Metallica's Argument Against Napster and Internet File Sharing
locke-labor-property.relation: Robert Delfino evaluates the Napster lawsuit philosophically: Aristotle's law of non-contradiction exposes Lars Ulrich's inconsistent statements about money and his tolerance of 1980s home taping despite admitting to it, weakening the band's case. But the core argument is consistent and Lockean - Lars' Senate testimony that 'just like a carpenter who crafts a table gets to decide whether to keep it, sell it, or give it away' invokes Locke's labor theory of property, which Delfino defends against Tom Palmer's objection that copyright restricts bodily liberty, distinguishing it from the Constitution's utilitarian rationale for copyright.

locke-labor-property.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
locke-labor-property.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
locke-labor-property.relation: Jason Walker pits Hobbes against Locke over whether Andrea may take the mermaid necklace when Rick says 'I don't think those rules apply anymore'. He reads the survivors' conduct—Andrea's single necklace under Locke's spoilage proviso, Morgan squatting in and fixing up the neighbors' house, Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo—as a Lockean state of nature where self-ownership and property rights persist without government, while Chris's cannibal band and the Governor embody the Hobbesian war of all against all, treating persons as mere means. The Lockean right to punish, exercised brutally by Grimes's group on Chris's hunters, vindicates rights even by Hobbes's own demand for enforcement.

locke-labor-property.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
locke-labor-property.title: Was it Morally Wrong to Kill Off Sherlock Holmes
locke-labor-property.relation: Terjesen asks whether Conan Doyle acted immorally in killing Holmes in 'The Final Problem,' framing it through property theory. He runs Locke's labor theory (illustrated via 'The Blue Carbuncle' gem), Proudhon and Marx's critiques, and both consequentialist and Kantian (respect-for-persons) justifications of intellectual property.
