He argues Conan Doyle's ownership of the iconic Holmes weakened as Paget, Gillette, Rathbone, and Dr. Joseph Bell co-authored the figure, so property rights alone can't justify the killing—but Conan Doyle's authorial dignity plus the narrative fitness of 'The Final Problem' and 'His Last Bow' make the send-off defensible.

locke-labor-property.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
locke-labor-property.title: Two Ways to Yuma Locke, Liberalism, and Western Masculinity in 3 10 to Yuma
locke-labor-property.relation: Mexal reads both versions of 3:10 to Yuma through Locke's classical liberalism, arguing the western hero descends from Locke's autonomous, property-owning self in a 'state of nature' (contrasted with Hobbes's state of war). In the 1957 film, Dan Evans transforms from atomistic self-interest to a masculine civic republicanism, escorting Ben Wade to the train even after being released from his contract, reflecting Cold War anxieties. In the 2007 remake, Dan instead renegotiates his contract for water rights and money, so western masculinity becomes unyielding Lockean individualism and the 'right to get rich' in a post-Cold War, capitalist-triumphant America.

locke-labor-property.book: 237 - The Philosophy of the Western
locke-labor-property.title: “Order Out of the Mud” Deadwood and the State of Nature
locke-labor-property.relation: Cantor reads David Milch's Deadwood as a dramatization of 'order without law,' testing the mining camp against the state-of-nature theories of Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau. Deadwood is Hobbesian in its sources of violence (competition, diffidence, glory; Al Swearengen's alpha-male struggles), but Lockean in showing property rights and commerce arising spontaneously before the state—gold becomes a self-generated medium of exchange that even overrides prejudice (Hearst dealing with Odell). It is Rousseauian in its innate pity (Swearengen's mercy) and its skepticism that incorporation into the nation-state, symbolized by the telegraph and Hearst's abstract corporate power, counts as progress.

locke-labor-property.book: 247 - The Ultimate Supernatural and Philosophy - Saving People, Killing Things, the Family Business
locke-labor-property.title: 13. Does God Have the Right to Destroy the Universe
locke-labor-property.relation: Foresman asks whether Chuck has a negative right to destroy the multiverse, rejecting the question-begging 'God can do whatever God wants' and the bare creation/ownership argument (using the scrambled-eggs example) as insufficient. Drawing on Locke's Two Treatises—property arises from mixing labor, but even in the state of nature one may not destroy a creature except for a 'nobler use,' and hoarding beyond use is illegitimate—he concludes Chuck is a Lockean tyrant destroying universes he could simply recreate, so Sam and Dean's rebellion is justified.

locke-labor-property.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
locke-labor-property.title: Thidwick the Big-Hearted Bearer of Property Rights
locke-labor-property.relation: Skoble argues that the creatures who colonize Thidwick's antlers never acquire any property right, because mere uninvited occupancy does not create ownership and Thidwick's Lockean self-ownership over his own body and horns is inalienable. The eleven-to-one vote to keep Thidwick on the starving north shore shows, via Nozick's 'Tale of the Slave,' that democratic procedures cannot legitimately override fundamental liberty rights. Thidwick's near-enslavement stems from his mistaken belief that a host must be 'nice to his guests,' and his freedom is restored only when the shed antlers let him reclaim self-ownership.

locke-labor-property.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
locke-labor-property.title: Whose Egg Is It, Really Property Rights and Distributive Justice
locke-labor-property.relation: Cribbs treats the Horton-versus-Mayzie custody fight over the egg as a property-rights puzzle, applying Locke's labor-mixing theory (Horton's season of incubation versus Mayzie's laying and abandonment, plus squatter's rights) and its provisos against waste and taking more than 'enough and as good,' illustrated by the Once-ler and Hardin's tragedy of the commons. Adam Smith's invisible hand and the Wubble-chap's skilled labor defend market inequality, while Sylvester McBean's Sneetch exploitation, Yertle, and Marx's alienated proletariat motivate Rawls's veil of ignorance and distributive justice as a corrective to unregulated property rights.

locke-labor-property.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
locke-labor-property.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
locke-labor-property.relation: Ketcham 'deconstructs' the entailment that threatens the Bennets in Pride and Prejudice, explaining the legal history of fee tail and primogeniture and noting Austen likely erred, since by her time entailment could be barred by a simple legal procedure. He uses this to trace competing theories of property, from an occupation theory (first possession, tied to inherited estates) toward an emerging economic theory of productive wealth, and finally to Jeremy Waldron's view that property is a relationship between people. Elizabeth's careful assessment of Darcy's estate as a community rather than a mere possession dramatizes this shift, and love plus responsibility replaces entailment as the story's true concern.

locke-labor-property.book: 282 - Climbing – Philosophy for Everyone - Because It's There
locke-labor-property.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
locke-labor-property.relation: Halbert uses a Hawaiian route-setter friend upset that his 'secret' crag went public to argue climbing culture is a gift economy that defies Locke's labor theory of property and the self-interest of Locke and Adam Smith. Route setters spend money and labor establishing climbs, then give them freely to a commons, exemplifying Kropotkin's social-anarchist mutual aid over Social Darwinist competition. Citing the Red River Gorge Coalition and Muir Valley, she recasts Hardin's tragedy of the commons as Carol Rose's 'comedy of the commons,' where more participants enhance rather than diminish the shared value.

locke-labor-property.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
locke-labor-property.title: 20. Westworld as Philosophy A Commentary on Colonialism
locke-labor-property.relation: The chapter reads all three seasons of Westworld as a commentary on colonialism, mapping the Delos parks onto settler, planter (extractive labor), and postcolonial colonialism and treating the android hosts as a metaphor for colonized and enslaved peoples. Using Fanon's Wretched of the Earth and Kelly Oliver's colonization of psychic space, it analyzes the hosts' double alienation and the colonizer's dehumanizing projections; it applies Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance' (with Locke's labor-property justification for dispossession) to the parks' two-tiered order. It casts William/the Man in Black as Memmi's 'colonizer who refuses' turned 'colonizer who accepts,' and Serac's Rehoboam as surveillance-capitalist coloniality, ending on Dolores and Caleb's cross-race solidarity as the hard path to real freedom.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Analyzing Emptiness
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Paul Gass reads the Dead's hippie milieu (the Beats, the Acid Tests, Buddhist-monk lyricist Peter Monk) as a conduit for Buddhist doctrine, taking the 'Eyes of the World' chorus as an invitation to awaken to Buddha-nature. He explains the Four Noble Truths, karma, and the five aggregates to argue the self is an illusion, using the image of a flame passed between lighters at a Dead show to picture rebirth without a persisting soul. The chapter then presents Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka middle way — emptiness itself must not be clutched as an absolute truth — and reads the 'redeemer... wagon loaded with clay' verse of 'Eyes of the World' as the Mahayana bodhisattva liberating all beings, with emptiness finally discarded like the boat after crossing the river.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Sudden Enlightenment
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Luke Cuddy and Michael Bruce ask whether Beatrix Kiddo could reach enlightenment, reading Kill Bill's nonlinear plotting as a Buddhist interconnected web of causes: Pai Mei's Five Point Palm technique causes both the coffin escape and Bill's death, and Budd's degraded trailer life is karma catching up. Beatrix grasps the structure of suffering and its cause—she locates it in Bill and the squad and eliminates them—but mistakes that for ending suffering itself, and her declared lack of 'mercy, compassion, and forgiveness' blocks the compassion enlightenment requires, while Bill's 'natural born killer' story contradicts impermanence and no-self. The chapter closes on her bathroom-floor ecstasy as a candidate case of Zen sudden enlightenment, left to the reader to judge by how she would one day treat a vengeful Nikki.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Mr. Monk Murdered Trudy
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Green argues Monk is an unintentional Bodhisattva whose OCD enacts the Four Bodhisattva Vows: the compulsion to touch lampposts is the first vow's blind desires, his monastic minimalism the Dharma gate, and his crime-solving compassion for a disordered world the third vow, with the Dhammapada's teaching that the untamed mind produces suffering exemplified by Monk and by Harold Krenshaw's rival ordering. Like Vimalakirti feigning illness, or Shawn Spencer in Psych, and like the father in the Lotus Sutra's burning-house parable, Monk and his writers use skillful deception to awaken viewers to suffering and loving kindness. The title thesis is that Monk cannot solve Trudy's murder because he accepts responsibility for it: by Thich Nhat Hanh's Interbeing there is no absolute self and other, so solving the case requires the Zen 'kill the Buddha' eradication of the self, Monk's nirvana-as-extinction and the end of the series.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: 2 - An Interview with Bodhidharma
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Priest stages a spoof radio interview with Bodhidharma at the Shaolin Temple to argue that the monks' fighting exercises are really meditation: a fist passing an inch from your nose focuses the mind, and repeatedly practicing violent techniques makes practitioners less violent. Bodhidharma explains that a liter of goat's milk, a marauding thug, and even the reporter's self are only conceptual labels over 'thusness' (tathata), that attachment and the desire to strike cause suffering to the striker, and that the Buddha's compassion permits self-defense without aggression. The punchline is the reporter's unanswered last question: 'They're not really about fighting, are they?'

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Bernard Wills takes the reference to The Cloud of Unknowing in 'The Window' as the key to Cohen's lifelong fascination with apophatic, negative mysticism - God sought beyond every image in a 'naked intent of love,' as in the medieval Cloud, Dionysius, Maimonides, and Kabbalah - against the kataphatic way of affirmation. He reads Recent Songs as an album of exile and the play of union and separation ('Un Canadien Errant,' 'Ballad of the Absent Mare'), where the incarnate Word is 'stuttered' and 'frozen,' a passion without resurrection. Cohen's later Zen turn is thus prefigured: the emptiness of sunyata and the Neo-Platonic descent from and return to the One are positive nothingness - self-overcoming in the service of compassion rather than the black-romantic nihilism of self-annihilation.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: 22. The Many-Faced God and Indian Philosophy
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Van Eyghen maps the Faceless Men onto Indian philosophy: their one God of many faces parallels Vedanta's Brahman in personal form as Ishvara, and Arya's training to become 'no one' parallels shedding the ego toward identity with Brahman - with Jaqen as guru and the stick-beating ritual as an example of identity fusion in Harvey Whitehouse's cognitive science of religion. But the Faceless Men may go further than Vedanta toward Buddhism, since they worship a god with no face of his own and aim at no-self rather than union, while Arya's pragmatic adoption of the shellfish-merchant disguise echoes the Bhagavad Gita's Krishna: perform your duty without attachment to any self.

nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Developments in Buddhist thought
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Traces Buddhist scholasticism from the eighteen early schools (Lokottaravadins, Sammatiyas, Sautrantikas, Sarvastivadins, with Theravada the survivor) through the Abhidharma projects - Sarvastivada dharmas existing in all three time modes with an essence (svabhava), Theravada's categorization of some 28 physical and 52 mental dharmas - and their critique of Nyaya-Vaisheshika partless atoms. It then presents the Mahayana response: the Perfection of Wisdom sutras' teaching that all dharmas are empty of own-being, and Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka demonstration that nothing with own-being can arise from itself, from another, from both, or spontaneously, together with his two truths (conventional and ultimate) and the 'emptiness of emptiness' - emptiness affirms, rather than denies, the dependently originated world, since without it no change or knowledge would be possible. It closes with Vasubandhu's Yogacara 'Mind-Only' analysis of transformations of consciousness, karmic 'seeds' in a storehouse consciousness, and the constructed, dependent, and perfected aspects of experience, which denies that perception establishes the external existence of its objects. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: 8. Ode to Joi
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Steve Bein first tests Joi against Mary Anne Warren's five functionalist personhood criteria — consciousness, reason, self-motivated activity, communication, self-awareness — and finds she passes, which makes Luv's stomping of the emanator a murder. The Buddha's no-self doctrine then denies that anyone, Joi included, is an enduring person: we are bundles of fleeting psychophysical processes, 'like tears in rain', which threatens to let Luv plead that the Luv who killed Joi no longer exists. Nagarjuna's two truths resolve the courtroom problem: ultimately there are no persons, but conventionally 'Luv killed Joi' is perfectly true, and the karma ripples through the whole network.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Introduction
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: De Cruz and De Smedt argue that ATLA subverts the Chosen One trope: Aang's training is slow and non-linear, he needs dedicated teachers, and saving the world is a team effort in which Katara leads and Sokka plans. The show's central theme is oneness, voiced by Guru Pathik's 'illusion of separation' ('The Guru') and Huu's banyan-grove tree ('The Swamp'), which the editors trace to Daoist, Huayan Buddhist (Fazang's golden lion), and Indigenous traditions of interdependence. They frame the volume's engagement with genocide, imperialism, ecological destruction, and Ba Sing Se's authoritarian denial as proof that philosophy is needed for human flourishing.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Donavan Muir argues Lost's narrative world, unlike Jane Eyre's, requires its own metaphysics, and that this metaphysics is an order of balanced binary oppositions: Jacob and the Man in Black as twins diverged at birth, the cave scale's light and dark stones that Locke knocks out of balance in 'The Substitute,' science/faith, with characters like Jack converting from one pole into its opposite. The proper model is the yin-yang in motion - the Tao as a balanced ontological flow in which interdependent opposites wax and wane - so that treating the poles as independent is the delusion that threatens the island's order. The finale, where both Jacob and the Man in Black cease to exist and the castaways are freed, enacts the Mahayana Buddhist Middle Way: enlightenment as letting go of rigid oppositions that interdependence double-negates.

nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Genius All the Time The Beats, Spontaneous Presence, and Primordial Ground
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Marc Olmsted reads Beat spontaneity through Tantric (Vajrayana) Buddhism, arguing that 'first thought, best thought' and Kerouac's 'Mind is shapely, art is shapely' rest on the view that enlightenment/awareness is already present and need only be recognized. He maps Ginsberg's poetics onto the Tantric terms Ground, Path, and Fruition, tying shamatha-vipashyana practice and the doctrine of anatta (no-self) to the poet catching the first pre-conceptual thought. Ginsberg's Blake visions, his study under Trungpa and Gelek Rinpoche, and Burroughs's cut-up 'homemade yankee tantra' are offered as evidence that Beat composition enacts a Buddhist recognition of primordial, empty, self-existing awareness.

nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Between Social Ecology and Deep Ecology Gary Snyder’s Ecological Philosophy
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Paul Messersmith-Glavin positions Snyder as a bridge between deep ecology and social ecology. He shows how Sessions and Devall enlist Snyder's Mahayana Buddhism (emptiness/sunyata, Dogen's 'Mind means trees, fence posts, tiles, and grasses') and Spinoza's monism for a biocentric, consciousness-changing deep ecology descended from Naess and Leopold's land ethic. Against this, he sets Bookchin's social ecology, which roots the ecological crisis in human hierarchy and attacks deep ecology's ahistorical 'cosmic oneness' and misanthropic Earth First! statements. Snyder's threefold nature/wild/wilderness distinction, bioregionalism, and reading of Marx and anarchism let him hold both, insisting environmental and social justice are 'all one front.'

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Donavan S. Muir argues that Lost deliberately withholds its metanarrative so viewers must construct its metaphysics, which he identifies as an order of balanced binary oppositions. Drawing on the spinning Taoist yin-yang, he reads the interdependent, mutually converting poles—Jack from man of science to man of faith, Sawyer from con man to protector—and the light/dark scales in Widmore's painting and the cave (Locke throwing out the white rock) as figures for a Tao whose balance sustains existence. Invoking Derrida's traces and Mahayana Buddhism's Middle Way and emptiness, he reads Jacob and the Man in Black as twins whose oppositions must be annihilated, so that only when both cease to exist in 'The End' are the castaways set free.

nagarjuna-emptiness.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
nagarjuna-emptiness.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
nagarjuna-emptiness.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

climate-ethics.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
climate-ethics.title: Dizzy with the Possibilities
climate-ethics.relation: Allen Thompson treats 'Throwing Stones' — 'the future's here, we are it, we are on our own' — as voicing the existential dread of anthropogenic global warming and the felt 'end of nature' Bill McKibben named, defending the song as the band's a-political polemic against heartless powers. He argues via Steven Vogel that humans cannot literally end nature unless we are supernatural, and recasts the crisis with Thoreau and Gary Snyder as civilization's assault on the wild, the self-willed order we too belong to. Deep ecology then supplies the response: re-identify the self as wild — as Deadheads do by dancing wildly to the music — and build a civilization wildness can endure, with the band's 1988 rainforest-benefit press conference as evidence of the Dead's own ecological consciousness.

climate-ethics.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
climate-ethics.title: This Is Really Happening (So Do Something)
climate-ethics.relation: Milsky argues that Radiohead practice what environmental virtue ethics preaches, organizing the chapter around Aristotle's akrasia (Nicomachean Ethics VII): Sting, who champions rainforests while advertising Jaguar and topping the 'dirtiest band' carbon table, acts against his own better judgment, whereas Radiohead — confronted with an audit showing their 2003 and 2006 tours emitted roughly 11,368 tons of CO2, mostly from fans driving — changed their actual practice (venues near public transit, car-pool lots, sea freight instead of air, LED lighting and auxilary power units). He reads the King Canute imagery of The Eraser and lines from 'The Clock' and 'And It Rained All Night' as environmental narrative in the tradition of Thoreau's Walden and Leopold's Sand County Almanac, obligating listeners to act or risk akrasia themselves, and presents the band's Friends of the Earth 'Big Ask' commitment as linking environmental virtue to human flourishing. 'Idioteque'''s 'this is really happening' becomes the wake-up call to the akratic fan driving to Lollapalooza with a bottled water.

climate-ethics.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
climate-ethics.title: Who Watches the Watchers
climate-ethics.relation: Patton and Webb unpack Colbert's coinage 'freem' — freedom without the do — from the first episode's dedication to 'the heroes' who act patriotically by watching TV, through Bush's post-9/11 call to go shopping, the Wikipedia elephant vandalism, and the WristStrong bracelet as activism indistinguishable from consuming Viacom product. Using Singer's argument that social capital (roads, satellites, infrastructure) makes the 'it's your money' cry hollow, E.O. Wilson's four-Earths arithmetic on unsustainable consumption and greenwashed market 'solutions' to global warming, and Baudrillard's Consumer Society account of news packaged for consumption beside the ads, they ask whether the Colbert Nation's ironic participation resists corporate media or completes it, concluding freem converts even critique into one more purchase.

climate-ethics.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
climate-ethics.title: The End of the Story
climate-ethics.relation: Reads the Gom Jabbar test as Herbert's definition of humanity: Paul endures Mohiam's pain box because a human stays in the trap to turn it on the trapper and protect the species, while an animal only chews off its own leg. The Butlerian Jihad's ban on 'a machine in the likeness of a man's mind' is applied to our own iPod-and-PDA dependence, with Mentat Thufir Hawat showing that losing the machine-crutch 'forced human minds to develop,' in line with Aristotle's phronesis and the politics of the common good (and Plato's contemplation as the core of happiness). The chapter closes by turning the human/animal test on the modern West—Baron Harkonnen-like consumers whose water-hungry beef habit makes us the trap of our own environmental collapse.

climate-ethics.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
climate-ethics.title: 26. Thanos’s Mistake
climate-ethics.relation: Argues Thanos embodies Nietzschean master morality — his will as its own justification, 'the hardest choices require the strongest wills,' echoing the Melian dialogue's 'the strong do what they will, the weak suffer what they must,' with Doctor Strange answering in kind ('you'll find our will equal to yours') — while the Avengers speak from slave morality, judging by intentions and branding genocide evil. Thanos's real error, though, is a categorical one: imposing a technical quantity fix (a one-time 50 percent cull) on a social relationship problem, since Hardin's carrying-capacity logic and the St. Matthew Island reindeer show populations must self-limit like apex predators, making his correction a mere stopgap that confuses quantity with relationship.

climate-ethics.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
climate-ethics.title: Intergenerational Ships and Sustainable Duties
climate-ethics.relation: Hackett uses WALL-E's lone plant and the Buy n Large Axiom to ask what we owe nature and future generations: WALL-E's tender care of the seedling models treating nature as a rights-bearing 'person' (via Gaia-superorganism thinking), while BnL's obese, screen-hooked passengers on the Axiom satirize capitalist individualism that acknowledges no obligations beyond contracts. He proposes a 'Principle of Sustainable Duties' — minimize net environmental damage and weigh long-term impact — and reads the film's open ending, extending Leopold's expansion of moral community to the biotic whole, as a Platonic aporia about whether an Anthropocene humanity can actually change in time.

climate-ethics.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
climate-ethics.title: “Doing nothing is just as bad as doing the wrong thing”
climate-ethics.relation: Reads The Expanse as a portrait of a survived-but-unlearned Anthropocene: Bobbie's mourning encounter with Earth's dead, walled ocean in 'Cascade', Prax Meng's cascade of cascading failures killing Ganymede's artificial ecosystem and manufacturing Belter climate refugees overnight, and the slum outside the UN gates where children drink sewer water. Drawing on Brian Henning's 'Technozoic' critique, Katie McShane, Keekok Lee's intrinsic value of inanimate nature, and Henry Shue and Kyle Whyte on climate justice and colonialism, it argues humanity simply exported its anthropocentric, colonial worldview to Mars terraforming, Ilus, and the Ring worlds instead of changing it — Belters standing in for the Global South — so the Roci's creed that 'doing nothing is just as bad as doing the wrong thing' becomes a demand for environmental justice and a non-anthropocentric ethics.

climate-ethics.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
climate-ethics.title: Notes
climate-ethics.relation: Bacharach and Das use Greenpeace's 2014 'Everything is NOT awesome' video — a pristine LEGO Arctic slowly drowning in Shell oil until only a polar bear on a Shell-flagged iceberg remains — to ask what exactly was wrong with LEGO's Shell partnership, and whether a company trading on a wholesome image incurs stricter moral duties. They audit the reality behind the brand: Shell's complicity in Nigeria's repression of the Ogoni and the hanging of Ken Saro-Wiwa, LEGO's outsourcing layoffs in Denmark and the US, and the fact that only about 10 percent of LEGO's carbon emissions come from its own plants, the rest along the supply chain. Their verdict: LEGO is ethically better than most for-profit companies and its fictional Octan satirizes the very consumerism it profits from, but image itself is a fair ground for holding it to a higher standard.

climate-ethics.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
climate-ethics.title: Notes
climate-ethics.relation: Thomas reads Bartertown's economy as embedded in social and political relations rather than a free market: the Underworld laborers versus Bartertown's elite stage Marx's class struggle, and the Aunty Entity–Master Blaster conflict runs through Hegel's thesis-antithesis-synthesis of capital versus labor. He treats the franchise as a post-peak-oil world, applies the tragedy of the commons and lifeboat ethics to water rationing and the Citadel's hierarchy, and counterposes Gandhi's cooperation, Adam Smith's invisible hand, and open-source-style collaboration. The conclusion: the Wasteland shows the failure of self-interest-based capitalism and the need for cooperative alternatives like direct democracy.

climate-ethics.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
climate-ethics.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
climate-ethics.relation: A scripted Lois Lane–Batman interview argues that the Batmobile/Batwing upgrade cycle and Wayne Enterprises' multinational production enact Marx's 'metabolic rift' (via John Bellamy Foster): both take from nature and return unprocessable waste faster than the planet can replenish, so protecting Gotham's way of life perpetuates an infinite environmental crisis of consumption. Solar-powered Superman wins the environmental showdown on lifestyle impact, but Batman counters that Krypton's ecological suicide makes Superman an 'environmental refugee,' not a model. The chapter's real verdict is Bruce's line 'We are all Bruce Wayne': human consumers must rebalance the human–nature relationship before finite resources like fresh water run out.

climate-ethics.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
climate-ethics.title: 18. The Journey May Also Save Us
climate-ethics.relation: McCrossin reads the Madagascar and Bhutan episodes of Parts Unknown as a climate-crisis 'diptych' co-authored with filmmaker Darren Aronofsky, set against the thirtieth anniversary of the 1988 climate testimony to the US Senate and the IPCC's warnings. He argues devastated, colonized Madagascar is 'the question' and un-colonized, Gross-National-Happiness Bhutan 'the answer,' and that Bourdain and Aronofsky's storytelling — invoking Noah, the Anthropocene, and Ghosh's Great Derangement — may help save us by making us think and act together.

climate-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
climate-ethics.title: 59. Don’t Look Up as Philosophy Comets, Climate Change, and Why the Snacks Are Not Free
climate-ethics.relation: The chapter argues Don't Look Up is less a film than a moral imperative: its comet is an allegory for climate change, and Randall Mindy's on-air breakdown presents Singer-style simple premises (the end of human life is bad; prevent bad things you can) that compel action. It uses Plato's knowledge-as-the-Good and 'blameworthy ignorance' to condemn the willfully ignorant (Kate's parents, the Orlean Bros) who act as if they know, and Kant's categorical imperative to condemn General Themes's 'free snacks' lie and to cast the moral as the rational. It defends the comet/climate analogy against critics and insists individual action is insufficient while collective government action is required.

wilderness-ethics.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
wilderness-ethics.title: Dizzy with the Possibilities
wilderness-ethics.relation: Allen Thompson treats 'Throwing Stones' — 'the future's here, we are it, we are on our own' — as voicing the existential dread of anthropogenic global warming and the felt 'end of nature' Bill McKibben named, defending the song as the band's a-political polemic against heartless powers. He argues via Steven Vogel that humans cannot literally end nature unless we are supernatural, and recasts the crisis with Thoreau and Gary Snyder as civilization's assault on the wild, the self-willed order we too belong to. Deep ecology then supplies the response: re-identify the self as wild — as Deadheads do by dancing wildly to the music — and build a civilization wildness can endure, with the band's 1988 rainforest-benefit press conference as evidence of the Dead's own ecological consciousness.

wilderness-ethics.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
wilderness-ethics.title: Friends—Don’t Leave Home without ’Em
wilderness-ethics.relation: Greg Ahrenhoerster places SpongeBob in literary history between Transcendentalism and naturalism: 'Nature Pants' is a failed Walden — SpongeBob gives away his possessions for Jellyfish Fields but his 'jellyfish instincts' fail as badly as self-reliance in London's 'To Build a Fire' — while 'Squidville' shows the industrial city's cold indifference as in Crane's Maggie. 'Jellyfish Hunter' warns that trying to exploit nature (Krabs's jelly factory) invites nature's reprisal, since civilized beings without instinct are at nature's mercy. The naturalist moral, against Transcendentalist solitude, is that we survive only through each other: visit Jellyfish Fields, but bring a friend.

wilderness-ethics.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
wilderness-ethics.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
wilderness-ethics.relation: Fitzpatrick argues that the awe Ellie feels at the brachiosaurs makes experiencing real dinosaurs so valuable that restoring them may be obligatory, and reads Malcolm's distrust of land managers as sharing Leopold's land ethic, under which firebombing Isla Nublar would be barbarism on the order of Dresden. Invoking Bentham, Mill, and Singer's expansion of the moral community (echoed in the park's dart guns), he weighs Elliot's 'Faking Nature' and Katz's charge that restored nature is a fake and an arrogance against Andrew Light's defense of respectful restoration. He concludes that Jurassic Park failed not because restoration is wrong but because Hammond restored dinosaurs for amusement, and that a careful, land-ethic-respecting de-extinction could one day be justified.

wilderness-ethics.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
wilderness-ethics.title: 15. Red Harvest in Roanoke
wilderness-ethics.relation: Reads Roanoke through ecocriticism and ecofeminism: the culture-nature dualism collapses as the urban Millers' wooded retreat turns predatory (rain of teeth, pig-men); the Butcher's backstory - a colonial woman starved by men whose blood-sacrifice pact makes the land flourish - aligns women and Nature as co-exploited by patriarchy, with Shelby's 'irrational' warnings ignored and Lee's maternal fury a force of nature; the animalizing of victims (pig-headed roasting, the Polks' barn-raised children, Matt's tryst with the Witch of the Wood) dissolves the human/animal hierarchy; and the media crew's attempt to package wilderness for ratings ends with Nature striking back at Agnes in the woods.

wilderness-ethics.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
wilderness-ethics.title: a14.xhtml
wilderness-ethics.relation: Stewart argues Middle-earth magic is rule-bound engineering rather than Hume's miracle as 'a violation of the laws of nature': spells fail, the Ring hides neither shadow nor wet footprints, and magic comes in strengths like gravity, so fear of Gandalf is fear of superior knowledge of nature's laws, not of lawlessness. The deeper point is Tolkien's linkage of magic with technology as the impatient will to make one's will effective quickly - Sauron is 'Lord of magic and machines', the Ring is the supreme technological artifact, Saruman's forged men and blast-fires embody domination - while elvish 'Art' is sub-creation and Beorn's communion with animals models harmony with nature. Like Thoreau pricing possessions in 'how much life' they cost, the chapter ends with Tolkien's warning that 'if a thing can be done, it should be done' is the great false assumption of our age.

wilderness-ethics.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
wilderness-ethics.title: Take Me to the Lakes: Transcendentalism and Ecology in Taylor Swift's folklore
wilderness-ethics.relation: Reads folklore as American Transcendentalist: like Thoreau at Walden and on Mt. Katahdin, Swift's escape into the woods of 'the lakes', 'seven', and 'the last great american dynasty' dissolves the divide between body and nature and reveals a fundamental oneness linking Rebekah Harkness, her grandfather in 'epiphany', and the High Line. Against the anti-social reading of Thoreau, the chapter argues, with Emerson's return to society after 'Nature', that Swift's escapism is not selfish retreat: she hands the stories back ('Now it's up to you to pass them down'), so leaving society heals alienation and rebuilds connection, including her anxiety that fame makes her 'nothing new' answered by the endurance of folk songs.

wilderness-ethics.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
wilderness-ethics.title: Speaking for Business, Speaking for Trees Business and Environment in The Lorax
wilderness-ethics.relation: The Klaassens read The Lorax as a joint business-and-environmental-ethics text organized around three questions the Thneed provokes: do we consume too much (invoking Thoreau's 'simplify' and DesJardins on practical, ethical, and environmental over-consumption), must business grow (Daly's distinction between quantitative growth and qualitative development), and why the Once-ler ignores sustainability (the Brundtland definition and Daly's rules for natural capital). The Lorax's self-appointment as one who 'speaks for the trees' is tied to Christopher Stone's argument that natural objects should have legal standing through guardians, like corporations or incompetents.

wilderness-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
wilderness-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
wilderness-ethics.relation: King examines Ortega y Gasset's and James Swan's claim that hunting is a 'return to nature' that revives a Paleolithic animal self, and argues it fails: Ortega himself concedes the return is only a 'vacation' from civilization, and the hunter's selective, predatory attention cannot supply the ecological literacy needed to confront industrial civilization. Drawing on Leopold's land ethic, Wendell Berry's agrarianism, and bell hooks's humility before nature's power, King contends a genuine return requires 'thick' relations to a particular bioregion sustained by a community of memory, not an individual's seasonal escape.

wilderness-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
wilderness-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
wilderness-ethics.relation: Parker asks whether 'photographic hunting' (the camera) is an ethically superior replacement for weaponized sport hunting (the gun), against Singer's and Regan's blanket condemnations of hunting. He concedes the camera captures most benefits—environmental knowledge, immersive learning, Leopold-style love of the land—but argues that only the kill roots the hunter in the ecosystem (citing Ortega and Paul Shepard), forcing confrontation with predation and death. He warns that treating photography as a wholesale replacement positions the human as detached 'spectator/master' over nature, the very hubris that drives environmental degradation.

wilderness-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
wilderness-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
wilderness-ethics.relation: Scruton reads the literature and music of hunting—Homer's Odyssey and Argos, Wagner's Parsifal, Tristan and the Ring, Melville's Moby Dick, Cooper's Last of the Mohicans, and English foxhunting from Sir Gawain to Surtees and Masefield's Reynard the Fox—as recovering the hunter-gatherer's sacred, totemic bond with animals and the theme of ritual sacrifice. He grounds the distinction between virtuous and 'lawless' hunting in Plato's Laws, where 'sacred hunting' of quadrupeds run down by men, horses, and dogs is defended as piety, and aligns it with Ortega's insistence on self-imposed limits that keep the hunt from becoming mere butchery.

wilderness-ethics.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
wilderness-ethics.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
wilderness-ethics.relation: Koppedrayer analyzes the modern North American 'traditional' and 'primitive' bowhunting movement—the Traditional Bowyer's Bible, magazines like Primitive Archer, and gatherings like ETAR—where crafting a selfbow from a single wood stave and hunting under a 'fair chase' ethic promise an authentic, unencumbered, 'really real' experience against high-tech compound bows. Drawing on Arjun Appadurai's 'synchronic warehouse of cultural scenarios,' she argues the past functions as a reproducible resource yielding a hyperreal authenticity, and that bowmakers describe the self-made bow as an embodiment of the maker's own substance and a spiritual link to earlier hunters.

wilderness-ethics.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
wilderness-ethics.title: GARDENING
wilderness-ethics.relation: Helene Gammack surveys the seventeenth-century self-sufficient English estate as a fusion of pleasure and productivity, using Schellinks's account of Bridge Place, Celia Fiennes's journals, and figures like John Evelyn and Sir William Temple (whose Upon the Gardens of Epicurus links fruit to health and tranquility). She traces dovecotes, fishponds, deer parks, orchards, and glasshouse exotics, and connects the modern 'grow your own' revival—driven by sustainability, food miles, and provenance—to that older harmony of beauty and use in cultivating food.

wilderness-ethics.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
wilderness-ethics.title: GARDENING
wilderness-ethics.relation: Jo Day uses archaeological and textual evidence to argue that the earliest elite gardens of Mesopotamia, Egypt, and Minoan Crete carried symbolic roles beyond pleasure. Assyrian kings like Sennacherib and Ashurnasirpal II displayed captured exotic plants as 'botanical imperialism' and tokens of power over nature and conquered lands, while Egyptian temple and tomb gardens (Hatshepsut's incense trees, plants tied to deities) served ritual and mythic functions. The chapter shows the ancient garden as a stage for status, military prowess, and religious performance.

wilderness-ethics.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
wilderness-ethics.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
wilderness-ethics.relation: Andrew Light resists reading the peoples of Middle-earth as simple stand-ins for parts of nature, noting that the ents, not the elves, truly speak for the forest, so nature is animated to stand and speak for itself. His central idea is 'green time': through Tom Bombadil and the ents, Tolkien represents a naturally scaled, ecosystemic, near-indifferent temporal perspective, seen when Bombadil is unconcerned with the Ring and the ents ignore the riders of Rohan. Light argues this indifference should not make us indifferent to nature but should teach humility and long-term responsibility for problems like global warming, imagining what it is to care for things as a process beyond our own lifespan.

wilderness-ethics.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
wilderness-ethics.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
wilderness-ethics.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

justice-as-fairness.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
justice-as-fairness.title: Mr. Rawls and the Decision Procedure
justice-as-fairness.relation: Joseph Ulatowski uses Mr. Blonde's torture of Marvin to test theories of punishment. He argues Blonde is not a mere psychopath but a retributivist within his social code—punishing clerks who 'touched the alarm' and cops who violated Mill's harm principle—while distinguishing acting on a principle from merely acting in accordance with one, since Blonde acts from sadistic urges. After reviewing Kant's lex talionis and the utilitarian theory's flaws, he asks whether Hart and Sterba's Rawlsian 'retributivism as fairness', whose principles are chosen behind a veil of ignorance, could justify Blonde's actions, concluding Blonde could not by his own lights have done otherwise than punish.

justice-as-fairness.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
justice-as-fairness.title: What Is Justice
justice-as-fairness.relation: Johnny Huss extracts multiple theories of justice from 'Jacob Green'—desert (traced to Plato's Republic), equal treatment, conventionalism, and systemic injustice—and argues that desert collapses once responsibility is pushed back to factors beyond our control (Cash's God-given voice, the 'victim of the times'). Rawls's veil of ignorance supplies the standard for judging institutions: since anyone could be Jacob Green, we could not accept principles that let anyone 'get done like Jacob Green got done.' The chapter extends this to social justice for Native Americans via 'The Ballad of Ira Hayes' and 'As Long as the Grass Shall Grow,' including the flooded Cornplanter Tract, and closes insisting justice requires action, not just principles.

justice-as-fairness.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
justice-as-fairness.title: Go Slowly
justice-as-fairness.relation: Wittkower frames In Rainbows' pay-what-you-want release with Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry: music is expressive communication awkwardly trapped in commodity form — even 'Happy Birthday' has an owner until 2030 — and digital distribution is finally tearing that frame down. He then applies Rawls's justice as fairness to music distribution: the first principle now supports everyone's liberty to listen, rip, and share, because viable alternative models mean restricting listeners can no longer be justified as necessary to artists; and the difference principle, with the sadists-objection to utilitarian aggregation, shows that how benefits are distributed among persons matters, which he extends to racial wealth gaps and the affirmative-action dilemma. His conclusion is that we must 'go slowly': listeners' rights to their culture outweigh labels' legitimate profit expectations, the way emancipation outweighed plantation business models, and labels must adapt into service providers rather than gatekeepers.

justice-as-fairness.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
justice-as-fairness.title: The Politics of Difference
justice-as-fairness.relation: Debra Jackson argues that despite its ethnic and gender stereotypes the Warcraft universe is structurally a Rawlsian liberal utopia: designers choose class balance behind a veil of ignorance, racial traits are symmetric, professions are open to all, and a difference principle guarantees even the most disadvantaged player a decent experience. Plato's Republic supplies the gender argument — as Plato made the soul rather than reproductive function the criterion for guardians, WoW makes gender irrelevant to gameplay. Yet players import real-world prejudice (anti-Gnome hate speech, female toons shunted into healer roles, mocked male Blood Elves), so structural equality never yields substantial equality: WoW is sexist and racist because we are.

justice-as-fairness.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
justice-as-fairness.title: Tearing Down Fenway Now That Would Be Offensive
justice-as-fairness.relation: Mathis argues fans' contempt for ticket resellers is not about being overcharged, since resellers only charge what Fenway's scarcity market will bear. Following Rawls's A Theory of Justice, he treats access to Red Sox tickets as a public good deliberately sheltered from the free market by the random online waiting room, the five-year season-ticket list, baseball's antitrust exemption, and the 1924 Massachusetts anti-scalping law—all of which promote egalitarian access and a sense of community. Reselling offends because it exploits for private profit a good we collectively protect from market forces, as tearing down Fenway itself would.

justice-as-fairness.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
justice-as-fairness.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.relation: Shaun Young tests Jeopardy! against equality as an 'essentially contested concept': Aristotle's proportional equality (treat like cases as like) seems to justify the winner-take-all payout as deserved, Locke's reward for the industrious explains why equal outcomes would kill incentive, and Rawls's two principles - fair equality of opportunity plus the difference principle - capture the show's identical rules and level playing field. He then raises harder challenges: Dworkin's equality of resources, Kymlicka's charge that the Americo-centric clue bank shortchanges minority cultures (with Quebec's Bill 101 as legitimate differentiated rights), and the capabilities approach of Sen and Nussbaum applied to would-be contestants who cannot operate the signaling device. Citing Isaiah Berlin's pluralism, he concludes that no final verdict on Jeopardy!'s equality is possible - and that spectators would not want one, since Jennings's seventy-four-game streak thrills precisely because of inequality between players.

justice-as-fairness.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
justice-as-fairness.title: Girls and Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.relation: Ketcham sets Hannah B (Brooklyn) beside an imagined Hannah D (a Darfur village terrorized by the Janjaweed) to ask whether personal fulfillment depends on culture or on the individual. Rejecting relativism (which, per Alford, cannot even condemn suppression of belief), he turns to Rawls's Law of Peoples - five minimal human rights any well-ordered society must grant - and builds a thought experiment, 'Blandland,' a minimally compliant country where both Hannahs relocate. His conclusion: even Rawlsian minimum rights, under which life can remain Hobbes's 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short,' plus personal drive and the attitudes of others, jointly and indeterminately decide what either Hannah can become.

justice-as-fairness.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
justice-as-fairness.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.relation: Robison-Greene argues Rawlsian ideal theory breaks down at Litchfield: Soso's hunger strike gets only cosmetic concessions from Caputo, Sophia's WAC human-rights platform loses to Taystee's realism, and Piper learns the council 'is basically bullshit,' showing how idealization made by the powerful ignores the lived facts of Mendoza's abusive marriage, Jimmy's 'compassionate' death sentence, and Sophia's denied hormones. Against taking a 'moral holiday' in prison, she proposes care ethics, with role-based duties sensitive to actual circumstances, as the morality that fits life inside, and suggests non-ideal theory may fit the outside world too.

justice-as-fairness.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
justice-as-fairness.title: 3. The Magic of a Promise
justice-as-fairness.relation: Alloy reads the whole story as being about promises - Westley's 'I will always come for you,' Humperdinck's insincerely made and casually broken vows to Buttercup, and Inigo's vow of vengeance to his murdered father. He tests conventionalism, using Rawls's idea that breaking a promise cheats on a fair rule-bound practice (illustrated by Inigo's rule-governed duel and the Battle of Wits where both parties cheat), against expectationalism, on which obligation comes from the trust and expectations created, as when Humperdinck manipulates Buttercup through her trust. Both theories struggle with Inigo's promise to a dead man, so Alloy argues with Searle that it is responsibility for intent that makes a promise, and defends his own view - against the Hobbesian consensus - that every promise is also a self-promise whose binding force is the promisor's self-respect: promises 'make us people.'

justice-as-fairness.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
justice-as-fairness.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
justice-as-fairness.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

justice-as-fairness.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
justice-as-fairness.title: 18. Oppression Pretty Much Sucks
justice-as-fairness.relation: Reads I Feel Pretty through feminist critiques of oppression: Bartky's Fashion-Beauty Complex turns the desire to feel pretty into a parasitic scheme of creams and credit-card debt, Du Bois's double consciousness captures Renee post-head-injury seeing herself as beautiful against the world's verdict, and Freud's account of hating those most like us explains the Highlander-style rivalry between women. The chapter then dismantles Rawls's distributive justice via Iris Marion Young, arguing rights are not goods to hand out and that 'imagine everyone is the same' thinking entrenches privilege. The alternative is celebrating difference, which is exactly what Schumer's prettiness-as-self-celebration performs.

justice-as-fairness.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
justice-as-fairness.title: 2. A Paragon of Righteous Virtue
justice-as-fairness.relation: Allinson reads Gardner's novels, especially The Case of the Blonde Bonanza, as philosophy disguised as pulp: Mason acts from curiosity, compassion, and justice rather than utility, a 'pure Kantian or ancient Confucian' deontologist whose loyalty to clients ('erase ATTORNEY AT LAW from the door') functions as his own Categorical Imperative. The chapter's crux is the perjury dilemma of the Blonde Bonanza: Mrs. Winlock's offered false testimony would free Dianne Alder, which Mason twice refuses yet curses ('To hell with it'), showing that the plot's deus ex machina dissolves but never solves the ethical dilemma, while George Winlock's truth-telling-at-any-cost mirrors Kant's prohibition on lying even to the Gestapo. Socrates's better-to-suffer-evil, Plato's Meno reversal, Aristotle's rhetoric, Confucian and Hebrew filial piety in Dianne's character, and Rawls's justice as fairness all serve as lenses on Mason's virtues.

justice-as-fairness.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
justice-as-fairness.title: #WithGreatPowerComesGreatResponsibility
justice-as-fairness.relation: The chapter weighs the #dangers of trial by Twitter — Tess's suicide attempt after a mob turned on her, Clara Meades killed over a war-memorial photo, the fundamental attribution error and echo chambers convicting the innocent, and Rawls's point that unpredictable, lawless punishment destroys liberty — against the #benefits, above all #MeToo as 'the beautiful flip side of #DeathTo' that finally held powerful abusers accountable when courts would not. Arendt's banality of evil explains both Garrett Scholes's bee-drone scheme and the ordinariness of the shamers: Parke's 'He's ordinary. That is the type,' and Liza Bahar's crowdsourced 'Fucking Bitch' cake show diffused responsibility enabling cruelty. The moral drawn is that anonymous power over others' lives demands conscious, individual responsibility for every click.

justice-as-fairness.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
justice-as-fairness.title: 3 Sins of the Fathers Historical Injustice and Its Repair in lack Panther
justice-as-fairness.relation: Almassi contrasts Rawlsian ideal theory (the veil of ignorance, justice as fairness) with Charles Mills's critique that idealization marginalizes actual historic oppression, arguing the film's characters seek Aristotle's corrective justice in a world already steeped in wrongdoing: the 1991 deaths of W'Kabi's parents at Klaue's hands and of N'Jobu at T'Chaka's. He works through the Museum of Great Britain axe scene as restitution, W'Kabi's 'you kill him where he stands' and Killmonger's 'I'mma make sure we're even' as retribution (tested against Walen's proportionality principles, with vengeance untethered from legitimate punishment), and Nakia's and T'Challa's outreach centers as Margaret Urban Walker-style relational repair, reading T'Chaka's concealment of N'Jobu's death as actively constructed ignorance in service of isolationism.

justice-as-fairness.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
justice-as-fairness.title: Notes
justice-as-fairness.relation: Argues that Rawls' ideal theory rests on a 'strict compliance' assumption — citizens and politicians who pursue justice rather than self-interest — which makes his ideal society look like The West Wing, while House of Cards depicts the real one: teachers' unions fighting performance standards, Senator Haas blocking the omnibus bill for electoral fear, Jackie Sharp trading favors, and SanCorp's Remy Danton buying votes against Russo's watershed bill. The chapter traces the competing 'every man a knave' tradition — Smith's invisible hand converting the butcher's self-love into our dinner, Hume's maxim for constitution-designers, Madison's 'ambition counteract ambition', and Buchanan's public choice revival — and uses the theory of the second best to argue we must design institutions (publicly financed elections, balanced-budget and inflation amendments, a generality constraint) that assume Underwoods run for Congress.

justice-as-fairness.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
justice-as-fairness.title: Notes
justice-as-fairness.relation: Kogelmann argues that political philosophers' ideal theory rests on Rawls's 'strict compliance' assumption — the West Wing picture where citizens and politicians pursue the public good — while House of Cards depicts the reality: Russo's zoning constituent, the teachers' union fighting performance standards, Senator Haas and Sharp's colleagues trading votes for self-interest. By the theory of the second best, ideals designed for selfless politicians misfire in a world with Frank and Remy Danton in it, so he recruits the older 'every man a knave' tradition — Adam Smith's self-love turned to public benefit, Hume's maxim, Madison's ambition-countering-ambition, Buchanan's 'politics without romance' — to redesign institutions against rent-seeking (SanCorp's purchase of votes on Russo's watershed bill) and politicians' short election-cycle horizons (Claire courting Senator Mendoza), via public financing and balanced-budget and inflation rules.

justice-as-fairness.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
justice-as-fairness.title: NOTES
justice-as-fairness.relation: Foy reads the Great Revelation and the Vampire Rights Amendment as a test of social contract theory: Nan Flanagan's 'we pay taxes, we deserve civil rights' invokes the Lockean bargain of obedience for protection, but Locke's God-given natural rights falter when the Fellowship denies vampires souls, and Locke excludes atheists and never imagined vampires. The chapter's resolution is Rawls: behind a veil of ignorance where deliberators might wake up vampire or human, anti-vampire bigots like the Newlins and supremacist nests alike would choose equal basic liberties plus distributive justice — including limits on vampires' centuries of accumulated wealth — so Sookie's 'let the law do it' to Rene marks a pluralist peace no theistic contract could deliver.

justice-as-fairness.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
justice-as-fairness.title: What's so Bad about Performance-Enhancing Drugs
justice-as-fairness.relation: Ryan evaluates three arguments that using performance-enhancing drugs is wrong, drawing on cases like Barry Bonds, Lyle Alzado, and Ben Johnson. The Against-the-Rules argument shows only that PED use breaks current rules, not that it should be banned; the Unfairness argument overgeneralizes, since sport is full of tolerated unfairness (better coaching, nutrition, natural gifts); and the Harm-and-Pressure argument turns on empirical facts and a paternalism-versus-autonomy debate about whether adults may choose the risk. She concludes no argument yet establishes that PEDs ought to be banned as inherently wrong.

justice-as-fairness.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
justice-as-fairness.title: The True Nature of Cheating
justice-as-fairness.relation: Swain and Brand build a definition of cheating by successive counterexamples set in a fictional State-versus-Central championship. They move from breaking a formal rule for unfair advantage, to including informal conventions (the hypothetical pre-rule Bonds steroid case), to 'enhancing one's chances of winning' (a coach fielding ineligible players to level the field), and finally add a defeasibility clause so that convention-sanctioned tactics like running out the play clock are not cheating. Trash-talking within the rules is classed as gamesmanship, not cheating.

justice-as-fairness.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
justice-as-fairness.title: Crowning a True Champion The Case for a College Football Playoff
justice-as-fairness.relation: Austin argues the BCS is unjust and that a sixteen-team college football playoff should decide the champion on the field, using the undefeated 2006 Boise State Broncos as his key case. He applies a merit-based principle of distributive justice, taking 'victory on the field' rather than economic contribution as the appropriate basis of desert, and invokes Robert Simon's ideal of athletic competition as 'a mutual quest for excellence through challenge.' He answers BCS defenders and academic-integrity worries (Gordon Gee) by proposing reforms that let sport enhance the university's mission.

justice-as-fairness.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
justice-as-fairness.title: Upon Further Review Instant Replay Is an All-or-Nothing Affair
justice-as-fairness.relation: Smith argues that consistency in applying rules and their motivations forces instant replay to be all-or-nothing: either every play is reviewable or none is. He shows the two rationales—'get the calls right' and 'preserve the flow of the game'—each apply to all plays, then dismantles the reviewable/nonreviewable line by arguing neither the 'judgment call' distinction (goal-line and fumble calls are judgment-laden, field goals are not) nor the 'correctable call' distinction (every play is correctable, e.g. via replaying the down) can hold, using the Roethlisberger Super Bowl XL touchdown as a case.

justice-as-fairness.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
justice-as-fairness.title: Does the Salary Cap Make the NFL a Fairer League
justice-as-fairness.relation: Collins-Cavanaugh presents the NFL salary cap as a model of utilitarian distributive justice via Mill's greatest happiness principle: owners and fans gain (guaranteed revenue and a fairer, more competitive league) while players lose relatively little. He then tests empirically—competitive-balance scores, playoff berths, championship distribution, and comparison to MLB and the NBA—and finds little evidence the cap actually increases fairness. Because the claimed fan happiness is not genuinely caused by the cap, the utilitarian justification collapses, leaving only the players' net loss against the owners' gain.

justice-as-fairness.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.relation: Hardman and Iorwerth argue that Olympic 'nation-swapping' should be judged by Coubertin's 'sincere internationalism' and Stephen Nathanson's 'moderate patriotism' (grounded, they note, in Rawls's justice as fairness), which permits a special but non-aggressive concern for one's country. They contrast the 'reflective national', whose national attachment evolves genuinely over time (the runner Wilson Kipketer settling in Denmark), with 'enlightened' and 'nomadic' cosmopolitans (Kenyan-born Qatari Saif Saaeed Shaheen bought for money, Jamaican-born Slovenian Merlene Ottey), whose transfers are economic and thin. They propose using Olympic Solidarity funding to offset the poverty that drives talent transfers rather than merely tightening Rule 42.

justice-as-fairness.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
justice-as-fairness.title: Justice, Power, and Love The Political Philosophy of Intolerable Cruelty
justice-as-fairness.relation: Biderman and Devlin trace Intolerable Cruelty through three theories of justice enacted by divorce attorney Miles Massey and femme fatale Marylin. 'Justice as power' is Thrasymachus's 'advantage of the stronger' and Machiavelli's might-makes-right, seen in Miles's courtroom war-room rhetoric and teeth imagery and in Marylin's plan to 'nail his ass' via marriage. 'Justice as compromise' is Hobbes's social contract escaping the state of nature, but the film shows the Massey pre-nup's signing and tearing to be merely a mask for power. When Miles and Marylin genuinely fall in love, their indifference to each other's wealth becomes a Rawlsian veil of ignorance and difference principle—justice as fairness—though the cynical Funniest Divorce Videos ending leaves that victory unguaranteed.

justice-as-fairness.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
justice-as-fairness.title: NOTES
justice-as-fairness.relation: Deborah R. Barnbaum reads season 6's flash-sideways as a set of counterfactual conditionals ('if Sawyer weren't a con man, then he would have been a cop') and uses David Lewis's possible-worlds semantics and his ordered similarity priorities to judge which are plausible. She argues Sawyer-as-cop is a 'closest world' change of one fact while Jack-and-Juliet-with-a-son changes too much to be true, and she pairs this with Rawls's veil of ignorance and A Theory of Justice as a parallel counterfactual thought experiment governing how the castaways should ration scarce water and medicine.

justice-as-fairness.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
justice-as-fairness.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
justice-as-fairness.relation: Hooke reads Serling's ambivalence toward the State through the liberal–libertarian debate between Rawls's A Theory of Justice (equal rights and the difference principle) and Nozick's Anarchy, State, and Utopia (the minimal state, wary of a central authority regulating personal life). 'The Obsolete Man' (the condemned librarian Wordsworth laughing before the Chancellor), 'Eye of the Beholder' ('The State is not God'), and 'The Shelter' dramatize the shepherd-paradox (via Foucault) and the danger of any state that crushes human dignity; freedom, like the Nietzschean laughter Wordsworth aims at power, cannot be defined but is known in experience.

justice-as-fairness.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
justice-as-fairness.title: Rebellion in Sala-ma-Sond The Social Contract and a Turtle Named Mack
justice-as-fairness.relation: Novy uses King Yertle's tyranny and Mack's revolt to survey social-contract theory. Hobbes explains why turtles leave the war-of-all state of nature for an absolute sovereign, but Yertle, ruling only for himself, becomes 'no king at all'; Locke then justifies overthrowing him because a ruler who destroys his subjects' property and lives dissolves the contract. Kant grounds the contract in innate freedom, while Rawls's original position and veil of ignorance test Sala-ma-Sond for justice as fairness, and King's civil disobedience frames Mack's rights-claiming burp as demanding the contract be honored for all.

justice-as-fairness.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.title: 44. Gattaca as Philosophy Genoism and Justice
justice-as-fairness.relation: Grinnell argues Gattaca depicts a society built on 'intrinsic genoism' and diagnoses it with Rawls's justice as fairness. He adapts Appiah's distinction between racialism and intrinsic vs. extrinsic racism to genoism, showing that Valids like Josef, Anton, and Eugene treat In-valids like Vincent as inferior simply for being In-valid, discounting all counterevidence. Using Janet Radcliffe Richards's 'separate spheres' argument he shows the caste system is either superfluous or unjust, and via Kitcher's 'life theme' he argues nearly everyone — Vincent, Irene, Anton, Eugene — suffers a low quality of life from having their theme thrust upon them. He concludes that Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle would dismantle the separate spheres and give everyone a fair, autonomy-respecting shot at their chosen life.

justice-as-fairness.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
justice-as-fairness.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
justice-as-fairness.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable. He tests the orchestrated revolution against utilitarianism's greatest-happiness principle (Bentham, Mill's taxation-of-the-wealthy, Singer's impartiality) and against Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle versus Nozick's entitlement objection and Aquinas's just-war criteria, concluding each character's actions can be read as 'just,' which exposes anthropocentrism as the real veil.

private-language.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
private-language.title: Wondering and Dreaming. The Words Have Different Meanings
private-language.relation: Scott Calef argues that the causal theory of perception — the inflatable pig over Battersea reaches you only as an internal representation — breeds Cartesian skepticism: the dreaming argument, asylum inmates who don't know they're mad ('the lunatic is in my head'), the evil demon, and the modern brain-in-a-vat version behind The Matrix. Locke's unknowable substratum behind the Dark Side jacket's qualities and Berkeley's idealism deepen the veil of perception, with 'Julia Dream', Waters's 'If I go insane, please don't stick your wires in my brain', and Syd's 'Jugband Blues' self-diagnosis as Floyd illustrations. Against skepticism he deploys mutual corroboration ('It takes two to know'), J.L. Austin's point that waking experience is qualitatively unlike dreams ('A Pillow of Winds': 'the dream is gone'), and Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box private language argument (rebranded as Lucifer Sam's cat) — a purely private language is impossible, so skepticism expressed in language defeats itself, leaving the Barrett-era enigma to keep philosophy's original wonder alive.

private-language.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
private-language.title: Does Rush Offer a Way Out
private-language.relation: Uses Rush's 1980s lyrics about facades and trust — 'Limelight''s strangers, 'Show Don't Tell''s refusal to take things on faith, 'War Paint''s lying mirror, and the synthesizer as an instrument that can fake any other sound — to stage skepticism about other minds, running from Descartes's cogito through solipsism and behaviorism. Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box and private-language argument dissolve the inner/outer confusion as a grammatical one, and 'Turn the Page' supplies the way out of the fly-bottle: nothing survives a vacuum, and with other people all we can do is be reminded.

private-language.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
private-language.title: 5. Does It Mean What Vizzini Thinks It Means
private-language.relation: Fetterman takes Inigo's 'I do not think it means what you think it means' seriously and defends Vizzini: the line may merely record that two speakers define 'inconceivable' differently, or react to it differently. Using Wittgenstein, he argues communication requires agreement in judgments, so Vizzini and Inigo may simply be playing different language games, like users of two different dictionaries. He then runs Wittgenstein's private language argument against the possibility that Vizzini's usage is correct by his own idiosyncratic rules - a purely private definition could never be confirmed or be wrong, since only Vizzini checks it - and touches on the philosophical sense of 'conceivable' as logically possible (the square circle) and the group language game that lets everyone accept Miracle Max's 'to blave.'

private-language.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
private-language.title: 12. The Broken Pieces of Yesterday’s Life
private-language.relation: Uses the flood of posthumous Hendrix releases — the dismal Lonnie Youngblood eight-track, 380-plus albums, the PPX litigations — to ask what we owe the dead and what access we may claim, weighing Kafka and Max Brod, Nietzsche's sister, Harper Lee's Go Set a Watchman, and Kundera's Mirek. It rejects the framing of conflicting rights: against the Cartesian picture of a hidden self the authors deploy Wittgenstein's beetle in the box — 'the human body is the best picture of the human soul' — to show that no one can fully control their public self, leaving only prudential discernment about which recordings should shape our image of the artist.

private-language.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
private-language.title: Grand Masters of the Universe
private-language.relation: Chases Cold War nuclear strategists down the rabbit-hole, reading the Mad Tea Party as the MAD (mutually assured destruction) tea party where 'to reduce the risk of nuclear war, the risk must be increased' passes for wisdom. Ron Hirschbein uses Wittgenstein's language games (Alice was his favorite English prose), Rorty's final vocabulary, and Derrida's remark that a nuclear war has never 'taken place' to argue that Nukespeak, deterrence, the 'Delicate Balance of Terror', and the post hoc ergo propter hoc argument for deterrence are ungrounded, unfalsifiable word games. The Queen of Hearts's 'Off with his head!' prefigures decapitation strategy and the Hitler card, and the looking-glass chessboard becomes the arms race in which the public are expendable pawns.

private-language.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
private-language.title: Notes
private-language.relation: Pits Chomsky's structure-based verdict - Chewbacca's roars are unscripted, grammarless animal noises, hence not language - against Wittgenstein's meaning-as-use: the builder's language of 'wrench' and 'hydrospanner' shows that unstructured commands can work perfectly as a language-game. Obi-Wan's private Force-diary symbol 'S' illustrates the private language argument (no standard of correct use without a community), and viewers learn 'Sith,' 'lightsaber,' and Chewie's frustration at the medal ceremony from use alone, so Chewie genuinely communicates despite Shyriiwook having no real-world grammar.

private-language.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
private-language.title: NOTES
private-language.relation: Peter Fosl asks what John Connor should do when the radio call comes from Crystal Peak — accept near-certain death leading the resistance or stay silent — and dismantles the easy answers: John is not the indispensable savior (Kate or the caller from Montana could lead), the flag-waving finale undercuts any claim that humanity deserves saving, and collective responsibility for Judgment Day is unjust. Social contract fails because Brewster's button-press dissolved the contract and returned humanity to Hobbes's and Locke's state of nature, Hume shows contracts cannot ground society, and utilitarianism wavers once the happiness of animals and possible-happy machines is counted. The positive argument extends Wittgenstein's private-language argument (via Stanley Cavell): meaningful existence is inescapably social and moral, so refusing the claims of others would be as self-subverting as a solipsist arguing in language, and John must answer the call to remain human at all.

private-language.title: I Don’t Know, Just Wait Remembering Remarriage in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
