private-language.relation: Day reads Eternal Sunshine as Cavell's Hollywood comedy of remarriage: the kaleidoscopic middle in 'Joel's head' is the couple's remarriage conversation, a 'green world' where they invent a shared childhood and learn what it means to have memories together. Against a tape-recorder model of memory, he invokes the later Wittgenstein's private-language argument to argue there is no private memory — what Joel remembers he can return to Clementine in conversation. He rereads Mary's Nietzsche, the eternal recurrence, not as the end of regret but as affirming it (Joel's 'I wish I'd stayed. I do.'), and claims viewers themselves remember the erased past for the pair across the hallway's ten seconds of waiting.

private-language.title: The Instructive Impossibility of Being John Malkovich
private-language.relation: Hagberg treats Being John Malkovich as a refutation of the dualist fantasy that one could achieve transparent knowledge of another mind by occupying it. Through the film's four levels—Schwartz as spectator inside Malkovich, Lotte's transgender re-embodiment, Schwartz's puppeteering, and Malkovich falling into his own portal to the 'Malkovich, Malkovich' hell—he shows, via Jamesian relational sensation and Wittgenstein's private-language argument, that it is always still Schwartz who senses, so no one ever becomes Malkovich. The self-enclosed Malkovich world, where everyone can only say 'Malkovich,' dramatizes that selfhood is relationally emergent (Royce, Mead) and that experience is inviolably one's own (Margalit on remembered emotion).

private-language.title: Re(ct)ifying Empty Speech Cronenberg and the Problem of the First Person
private-language.relation: Brook W. R. Pearson examines the problem of the first person 'I' in Cronenberg through Lacan, Wittgenstein, and Deleuze/Guattari. He reads Spider's 'schizo-phonetic partition' and Tom/Joey's shifting use of 'I' in A History of Violence as Lacanian 'empty speech' and the narcissistic 'monument' of a censored unconscious chapter that resurfaces; Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Moore's paradox recast Joey's split as an illegitimate private language game, and Deleuze/Guattari's account of the other as a 'possible world' reframes the frightened face on the cinema screen.

private-language.title: (Still) Fighting the Power Public Space and the Unspeakable Privacy of the Other in Do the Right Thing
private-language.relation: Finnegan reads Do the Right Thing as a dramatization of philosophical skepticism and the 'problem of other minds,' using Wittgenstein's private-language argument, Austin's speech acts, and Cavell to argue that racism is not an epistemic failure to 'know' the Other but an ethical refusal to acknowledge. She shows Lee's split cinematic style (naturalistic interiority for the Italian Americans, alienating canted wide-angle shots for Radio Raheem and the black characters) enacts what being 'othered' looks like, while the Racial Slur Montage stages words as perlocutionary acts and Arendt's 'space of appearances' explains the black characters' exclusion. Mookie's thrown trash can and Sal's Wall of Fame register powerlessness rather than resolution.

private-language.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
private-language.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
private-language.relation: Sadler argues black coffee, unlike ceremonial tea, is the realist emblem of our anxious, isolated postmodern condition, and that the chain coffeehouse is a 'non-place' of public anonymity that only simulates the sociality we crave. Against Aristotle's confident view of humans as social animals whose eudaimonia presupposes a settled social order, she sets Nietzsche's alienated individual free to create values — then argues Nietzsche errs: using the trivial cappuccino-vs-latte choice, she shows (via Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Korsgaard) that even solitary choices need reasons intelligible to others, so individual choice cannot be self-justifying and our search for meaningful, non-arbitrary lives is irreducibly social.

narrative-identity.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
narrative-identity.title: A Modest Conclusion
narrative-identity.relation: Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro stage the diachronic-versus-episodic debate about the self (Galen Strawson's episodic view included) against Leigh Edwards's "no single Johnny Cash": the hotel-room-wrecking addict and the Billy Graham touring Christian do not fit one biography. They argue the private J.R. was a third option: on stage he becomes wholly absorbed in story characters (the Folsom narrator, the man who shot a man in Reno) while a self not defined by time slips in and out of the persona, evidenced by his account of gradually shedding "Johnny Cash" after shows. Johnny Cash the public quilt is compared to the Ship of Theseus, every original piece of J.R. replaced yet still owned by him, and the modest conclusion is that J.R., like anyone making a free choice, stood above the timeline of instants and could inhabit both the episodes and the grand narrative.

narrative-identity.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
narrative-identity.title: Retelling Our Stories
narrative-identity.relation: Milsky uses Ricoeur and MacIntyre's narrative theory of personal identity to read the two Sharons: Boomer's fabricated human backstory suffers a 'factual disruption' when she shoots Adama, while Athena's 'disruption of belief' comes from falling in love with Helo. He argues such disruptions — also suffered by humans like Starbuck (recovered memories of abuse in 'Maelstrom'), Roslin (coming to believe she is Pythia's dying leader), and Helo — need not destroy identity, since narratives can be retold, as the Final Four do in 'Crossroads, Part 2' with Tigh's 'My name is Saul Tigh' speech. Third-party narratives (Six disowning Athena, the crew refusing to see Boomer as Boomer) show identity is partly socially constructed and can become self-fulfilling prophecy, with Boomer's blackouts resembling dissociative identity disorder.

narrative-identity.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
narrative-identity.title: Long-Term Identity
narrative-identity.relation: Asks whether the final Duncan Idaho ghola, whose serial memories wake during his encounter with Murbella, is the same person as the original who died holding off nineteen Sardaukar. It tests physical continuity, Locke's memory-based sameness of person (Hayt becomes Duncan only when the original's consciousness reawakens), Parfit's psychological connectedness with its redescription of identity as survival through quasi-memory, Schechtman's narrative self-constitution, Velleman's self-inventing characters, and four-dimensionalist 'space-time worms' on which Leto II's 3,500 years and the Duncans' gappy five millennia are single long selves. Herbert's moral: identity is not fixed—societies and technologies, from the Tleilaxu tanks to the Sisterhood's swift accommodation, keep redrawing what counts as the same person. Same Duncans, same person.

narrative-identity.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
narrative-identity.title: A Story in Search of a Narrator
narrative-identity.relation: Brian Gregor reads Dexter through Charles Taylor's 'self-interpreting animal': Dexter's identity is not a fixed thing but comes into being through self-interpretation within an inescapable framework of value, so even his 'Am I good? Am I evil?' rebellion and the Nietzschean Übermensch reading fail to escape the deeper convictions about innocence, evil and desert that Harry's Code presupposes - as his guilt over the innocent Farrow shows. The chapter interprets Dexter's serial failures at being 'seen' - Harry's 'only one who really saw me', Brian's fraternal 'you can be yourself with me', Lila's probing, and Miguel Prado as Aristotle's friend, 'another self' - as Hegelian struggles for recognition that collapse because his real self can never come into the open. Finally, drawing on MacIntyre's narrative account of identity, it argues Dexter is literally a story in search of a narrator, whose selfhood persists through flashbacks, blood slides and noir-style voice-overs, and whose humanity shows in the need to have his account of himself heard and corrected by another.

narrative-identity.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
narrative-identity.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
narrative-identity.relation: The chapter reads the show's storytelling as identity construction through Paul Ricoeur's narrative identity, built on Heidegger's insight that human being is fundamentally temporal: we live in memories and future possibilities, so 'damn you, past Ted!' collisions between selves are structural. Ricoeur's two times - linear cosmological time versus fragmented phenomenological time - explain the show's looped, goat-intruding storytelling, while Giddens's reflexive project of the self (dubbed 'reflexibility') and Turkle's new-media multiple windows explain our fragmented, self-designed identities. Goffman's dramaturgy completes the picture: Barney's womanizer persona is a Goffmanesque masquerade that collapses, the yips, when his first lover reveals the founding story was false.

narrative-identity.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
narrative-identity.title: Allure of the West
narrative-identity.relation: Moll argues the park works as a grandiose role-playing game — a sandbox crossed with a LARP, with Ford and the directorial staff as Game Master — offering guests linear narratives with only the illusion of choice. Using MacIntyre's narrative unity of life and Bernard Williams's 'constraints of coherence,' he reads guest role-play as authoring a competing, parallel narrative of the self, so that William's discovery of his capacity for cruelty and transformation into the Man in Black exemplifies the park's violent, rule-mediated path to 'self-knowledge.' He ends by suggesting that the park's educative, transformative experience may be reserved not for the guests but for the hosts who produce it.

narrative-identity.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
narrative-identity.title: “I Always Felt this Place was Missing a Real Villain. Hence, My Humble Contribution.”
narrative-identity.relation: Eberl asks whether living out Sizemore-style fantasies can reveal or only corrode character: applying Aristotle's account of virtues and vices as habituated dispositions, he argues William's three decades in the park habituated the vices that made him the Man in Black — the park reveals rather than suspends the self — while cruelty toward humanlike hosts hardens us toward people, as Aquinas and Kant warn about kindness to animals. Against Ford's claim that humans are wantons in tight loops, Maeve's editing of her own code after learning her escape was scripted makes her a Frankfurtian person who aligns first-order desires with second-order volitions, grounding her narrative identity and personhood. William too attains personhood by actualizing a second-order desire for a different life, with the hosts' free fight back evoking Nietzsche's will to power and Nozick's point that we want to actually do things, not merely experience them.

narrative-identity.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
narrative-identity.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
narrative-identity.relation: Uses the show's narrator and structure (the chain of contingencies costing Buster his hand, 'now that's how you narrate a story') to argue that we impose narrative on life to make it meaningful, starting from Aristotle's Poetics requirement of beginning, middle, and end. George Sr.'s endlessly reinterpreted J. Walter Weatherman lessons show storytelling as moral choice among possible versions of events, Nietzsche's advice to learn from artists commends styling one's own life aesthetically, and Kierkegaard's 'life must be understood backwards but lived forwards' explains both self-narration and the show's rewatchable 'call forwards', ending on narrative as the sense-making abstraction by which we know ourselves.

narrative-identity.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
narrative-identity.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
narrative-identity.relation: Argues that Toph Beifong is not the harmful 'Supercrip' stereotype (an exceptional individual who overcomes disability through talent and grit, which blames ordinary disabled people for their disadvantage) but a 'Proud Disabled Person' counterstory. Her blindness is a disability gain: it led her to learn earthbending from the badgermoles, the original earthbenders, and to live immersed in bending as her constant way of navigating the world, deepening her mastery. Using Hilde Lindemann's master narratives and counterstories and Elizabeth Barnes's mere-difference view, the chapter shows Toph fits neither the 'better off dead' nor the 'irrationally happy' stereotype: she is grumpy, nuanced (adapting her teaching of Aang in 'Bitter Work'), and a central driver of the plot rather than a moral prop. Fricker's hermeneutical injustice explains why disabled viewers struggle to make sense of flourishing with a disability, and why Toph's portrait gives them permission to celebrate it.

narrative-identity.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
narrative-identity.title: Long-Term Identity
narrative-identity.relation: Asks whether the final Duncan Idaho ghola, reawakened with the memories of all his serial ghola lives, is the same person as the original Idaho, testing physical continuity, Locke's memory criterion (Hayt before reawakening is not yet Idaho, which is why he dies again for House Atreides only after recovery), Parfit's psychological connectedness with its redescription of identity as mere survival, Schechtman's narrative self-constitution, and four-dimensionalist 'selfworms' with Gurney Halleck and Leto II as examples. It concludes that Herbert treats personal identity as something that shifts with technology and social recognition, so that the final Duncan's integration of five thousand years of lives is genuinely one person: same Duncans, same person.

narrative-identity.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
narrative-identity.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
narrative-identity.relation: Silcox's fifth-level paladin died to eighty-three orcs and his middle-school friends held a funeral, and the chapter asks whether grief for a PC death is rational. Charles Taylor's narrative ethics — we grasp our lives as unfolding stories — would vindicate it, but objections from Beckett's Waiting for Godot and MacEwan's Atonement (via critic Samantha Vice) show stories can discourage seeing life as narrative, and the decisive asymmetry is Nagel's point about death: after the paladin falls the campaign story continues and the player can still watch it, whereas a person's own death forecloses any finding out how things turn out, a difference like February cold versus interstellar cold. He proposes instead that the self is a 'back-story' or metanarrative precondition of storytelling, closing against Descartes' Meditations claim that the power of imagination is 'in no way necessary' to his essence — take away someone's capacity for shared fiction entirely and nothing recognizable remains.

narrative-identity.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
narrative-identity.title: Notes
narrative-identity.relation: David Lawrence opens with Fallout 4's 'Blind Betrayal', where Elder Maxson orders the player to execute Paladin Danse once his synth origin is revealed, and argues that moral status is a matter of capacities - sense of self, notion of past and future, values, life-plans, moral agency - drawing on Charles Taylor's concept of a person and narrative identity, not on biological substrate. Nick Valentine's hunt for Eddie Winter in 'Long Time Coming' and Curie's chosen embodiment in 'Emergent Behavior' show machines weaving reconstructed pasts into new life-plans, while ghouls like Hancock and Raul ('Old School Ghoul') and super mutants like Fawkes (who refuses to enter the lethal radiation chamber: 'I would not rob you of that') and the community-builder Marcus prove branded monsters can be more human than human. The factions embody warring philosophies of moral status: the Institute's property-slavery of its creations, the Brotherhood's 'wisdom of repugnance' (Leon Kass), and the Railroad's capacity-based abolitionism, with DiMA's Far Harbor question - how do you know you are not a synth? - turning the issue on the player.

narrative-identity.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
narrative-identity.title: Notes
narrative-identity.relation: The chapter rereads Fallout 3's original Project Purity ending — the forced walk into the lethal radiation chamber while radiation-immune followers Fawkes, Sergeant RL-3, and Charon each refuse — as the game's worst case of narrative paradox: the pre-authored story compels an action the player-authored character narrative cannot accommodate. On the narrative-identity view (mounted against Galen Strawson's denial of narrativity), the Karma system and companions like Fawkes matter through the story the player tells, so an evil, greed-driven Lone Wanderer dying nobly is a 'bad death' that unravels the motivation for the entire playthrough. Dying well requires death to fit the story, and Sarah Lyons's substitutable sacrifice — or a last-page redemption epiphany — is what restores narrative coherence.

narrative-identity.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
narrative-identity.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
narrative-identity.relation: Uses Paul Ricoeur's distinction between idem-identity (sameness) and ipse-identity (selfhood) to dissolve the paradox of Tara's lower-back tattoo: she is bodily the same Dr. Knowles yet disavows the 19-year-old who got it, identity being the narrative that weaves the two together. Tig's mushroom-fueled apology to a doll and his 'I don't know who I am anymore' after killing Donna show character as the set of lasting dispositions by which we are recognized, while Opie's competing promises to Donna and SAMCRO anchor self-constancy up to his 'I got this' sacrifice for Jax. It closes with John Teller's manuscript as a narrative identity that receives no closure even in death — a just institution aiming at 'the good life with and for others' whose story Jax continues.

narrative-identity.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
narrative-identity.title: I Remember It All Too Well: Memory, Nostalgia, and the Archival Art of Taylor Swift
narrative-identity.relation: Reads Swift's songwriting as 'archival art' through Derrida's Archive Fever and Ricoeur's archival trace: songs like 'marjorie' (with her grandmother's actual backing vocals), 'august', and 'All Too Well (10 Minute Version)' preserve traces of what is gone while re-creating, not merely capturing, memory. With Foucault's power/knowledge it argues that controlling the archive means controlling the stories told about oneself, citing 'Dear John (Taylor's Version)' and the Speak Now rerecording as acts of reclaiming power through speech. Stuart Hall's 'living archive' frames the rerecordings as memory continually remade, and Derrida/Halbwachs ground the claim that her music is a public site of collective memory where fans archive their own lives, as in 'mirrorball' and the Eras Tour.

narrative-identity.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
narrative-identity.title: Taylor's Version: Rerecording, Narrative, and Self-Interpretation
narrative-identity.relation: Argues that the rerecording project succeeded because Swift masters narrative identity: using Ricoeur's tension between sameness and otherness (taxonomy lacks Ricoeur), it shows how the mountain of old Taylors in the 'Look What You Made Me Do' video and the near-identical rerecordings keep past selves in one coherent story. Charles Taylor's self-interpreting animals explains why hearing her songs is self-interpretation for fans, while Cavarero's 'narratable self' and the vault tracks show her story is never complete. Deliberate changes like the rewritten 'Better Than Revenge (Taylor's Version)' and the lost shaky breath in 'Last Kiss (Taylor's Version)' illustrate Velleman's point that narrative is felt, and that retelling can mark moral growth without erasing the past.

narrative-identity.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
narrative-identity.title: A Real Lasting Legacy: Memory, Imagination, and Taylor Swift
narrative-identity.relation: Uses Swift's songs to sort episodic, procedural, and semantic memory ('Christmas Tree Farm', guitar-playing, her December 13 birthday) and argues episodic memory underwrites both narrative identity (Schechtman), heard in 'The Moment I Knew' and being 'paralyzed' in 'All Too Well', and Lockean personal identity, where 'Hold on to the memories / They will hold on to you' makes memories constitutive of the person who survives over time. Locke's forensic person is invoked to connect memory with responsibility, so 'Would've, Could've, Should've' makes memories 'weapons' that force us to own past actions. The chapter then tests 'continuism' (memory as a kind of imagination, observer vs field memories) against the fact that Swift remembers a particular Christmas tree farm that caused her memory.

narrative-identity.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
narrative-identity.title: Notes
narrative-identity.relation: Divides Rust's season-one personae into Taxman (anti-natalist rule-follower), Belligerent (vigilante drunk paralyzed by Nietzsche's Gay Science demon of eternal recurrence), and Patient (the mystic who wakes from his coma feeling his daughter's love, compared to the Persian mystic al-Hallaj), asking what makes them one person. It tests the brute physicalist account (Williams and Ayer — the same bird-tattooed body), the Lockean psychological-continuity account, and the narrative account, arguing only the narrative theory explains how Rust changes without either ignoring change or multiplying selves in one body. The chapter ends by making Rust an exemplar for the viewer: we are narrators who choose who to become, so 'I know who I am' is a victory.

narrative-identity.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
narrative-identity.title: “You Don’t Know Who You Are”
narrative-identity.relation: Peter Fosl argues that Nolan's protagonists are divided selves - public and private - whose self-creation runs through narratives and material signs (Memento's tattoos and Polaroids, Inception's safes, the Batcave, the Prestige twins' offstage swaps) that others can always reinterpret, steal, or manipulate. Following J.L. Austin on performative acts, he reads Following's Bill as losing authorship of his own story to Cobb's counter-narrative and Bruce Wayne as only ever performing roles written in advance, even at the Dark Knight ending's Florentine café. Augustine's memoria and Locke's memory-continuity ground the discussion of Leonard's broken self-knowledge ('You don't know who you are'), while Nietzsche on forgetting, Gadamer on the past's effective history, and Sartre on the dead as prey for the living frame how Leonard's forgotten past selves manipulate him into murdering Teddy and how Interstellar's Cooper reaches back through the Tesseract to alter his own past.

narrative-identity.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
narrative-identity.title: “Memory Man”
narrative-identity.relation: David LaRocca reads Memento through Andy Clark and David Chalmers's Extended Mind Thesis: Leonard's tattoos, Polaroids, and notecards just are his memory, doing exactly what Otto's notebook does in their original example - so that writing 'Don't believe his lies' on a Polaroid is literally modifying his mind and carries the moral significance of interfering with his person. Drawing on Liao and Sandberg's ethics of memory modification and Noël Carroll's account of the film's reverse-ordered narrative, the chapter argues Leonard remains a culpable moral agent in his lucid moments: he knowingly 'incepts' a false command into his own extended mind to preserve the avenging-husband narrative that constitutes his identity, becoming a serial killer. It closes on our epistemic and moral duty of cognitive fidelity - to build truthful narrative identities rather than lie to ourselves into murder.

narrative-identity.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
narrative-identity.title: 9. The Seven P’s of Real Punk
narrative-identity.relation: Prinz catalogs the poser tests - no newbies, scene participation, mall-bought clothes, taste tests, selling out, doctrinaire politics, pop punk - and argues punk is an identity, not a club: personal identity encompasses social identity, resisting narrative theories like Schechtman's that separate the personal from the social, a point his aesthetic-self survey (taste change feels like becoming a different person) confirms. This generates the Poser Paradox - everyone copies a role others created, so all punks are posers - which he escapes, or embraces, via Seven P's of subcultural capital (Priority, Pansophy, Preferences, Performance, Proficiency, Peril, Persistence), concluding with Poly Styrene that punks are genuine fakes.

situationism.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
situationism.title: And Beware of the Beast in Me
situationism.relation: Barnes takes Cash's infidelity despite the pledged fidelity of "I Walk the Line" and refuses the easy diagnoses of hypocrisy or lying: "Guess Things Happen that Way" voices a good will overcome by weakness, a frail human nature anyone shares. He supports this with the situationist experiments, the dime in the pay-phone slot, the Princeton seminarians in a hurry, Milgram's obedient schoolteachers, and the Stanford prison simulation that turned a pacifist student into an abusive guard, showing situation outweighs character. From Cash's songs he draws two moral lessons: charity toward wrongdoers, since the man in "I Never Picked Cotton" or the drunkard of "Kneeling Drunkard's Plea" might be us under the same circumstances, and prudence about compromising situations, as when Billy Joe's fatal pride in "Don't Take Your Guns to Town" proves his mother right.

situationism.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
situationism.title: The Other Children: The Importance of Meg and Chris
situationism.relation: Dohnimm argues Meg and Chris matter because they lack essence: unlike predictable one-gag characters (pervert Quagmire, homicidal Stewie), their traits are accidental — Meg stays Meg after her 'Don't Make Me Over' makeover, Chris stays Chris despite flashes of artistic talent. On Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, character (hexis) explains action, but Meg and Chris are inexplicable (Chris hitting on his mother, claiming 'My dad is smarter than your dad' when they share one). The Isen and Levin dime-in-the-phone-booth helping experiment grounds the situationist alternative: tiny situational factors, not character, predict helping — Quagmire is predictable, but Chris (speaking hip-hop, covering himself in honey for ants) is not. Finally, Sartre's bad faith reframes them: appealing to fixed character is fleeing our radical freedom, so the 'anti-characters' Meg and Chris are the show's most realistic and philosophically honest figures.

situationism.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
situationism.title: Nonetheless, Don Can Be a Real Heel
situationism.relation: Terjesen asks whether Don is a good man, testing his mixed record (egalitarian instincts, loyalty to Mohawk Airlines, protecting Horace Jr., against habitual adultery and the stolen identity) through Aristotle's habituation, Plato's Protagoras unity-of-virtues theses, Hume's sensible knave, and John Doris's situationist attack on global character traits. The unity theses imply Don's vices undermine his virtues (affairs make him unavailable when Betty crashes; evasions about his past block honesty), and Doris's dime-in-the-payphone literature suggests even Don's reliability may be circumstance-bound, as with Pete's weddings-and-vacations-only philandering. Against full situationism, Don's consistent rules (never forcing women, valuing women he genuinely finds interesting) point to 'regional' traits, yet Roger's verdict stands: 'You're no good with relationships because you don't value them,' since Don runs family on a business code, from Adam's bribe to 'that's what people do' consolation for Pete.

situationism.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
situationism.title: SERIAL KILLERS
situationism.relation: Alfano uses the trial of 'Sunset Strip Killer' Doug Clark to argue that situational forces and attribution biases may have swayed his jury regardless of the actual evidence. Drawing on Milgram's obedience study, Zimbardo's prison simulation, Knobe's intentionality vignettes, and Haidt's disgust experiments, he shows how gender bias, pretrial media, and revulsion at Clark's necrophilia could distort judgments of guilt. He closes with Nozick's truth-tracking account of knowledge to press whether a juror who would have convicted anyway can be said to know Clark is guilty.

soul-making-theodicy.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
soul-making-theodicy.title: Redemption
soul-making-theodicy.relation: Stephen Bilynskyj tests John Hick's soul-making theodicy—that God allows suffering because virtues like courage, temperance, and compassion need pain to form—against Cash's life and songs. Using Aristotle on habituation by pleasure and pain (Cash's first amphetamine euphoria and the ostrich-attack painkillers as missed occasions for temperance) and Aquinas on innate aptitude and divinely infused virtue, he argues virtue can form without suffering (by genes or miracle), so soul-making alone cannot justify evil, as Cash himself implies about his mother's grief after Jack's death. Cash instead locates redemption in Christ's suffering ('Redemption,' 'Why Me, Lord?'), while the intervention by his son John Carter shows pain still occasioning real growth in temperance.

soul-making-theodicy.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
soul-making-theodicy.title: Futurama and Philosophy
soul-making-theodicy.relation: Oschman reads 'Godfellas' as an answer to the problem of evil: Bender, made god of the Shrimpkins, destroys them by meddling too much, and the God Entity explains 'if you do too much, people get dependent. And if you do nothing, they lose hope.' After testing the contrast response (pain makes Slurm sweet) and the Free Will Defense (which covers moral evils like the returning garbage ball of 'A Big Piece of Garbage' but not natural evils or the taste of anchovies), the chapter adopts John Hick's soul-making theodicy: God's epistemic distance - compared to Fry's obsession after tasting super Slurm - keeps creatures uncompelled so they can grow into free moral agents. Fry's slow evolution from delivery boy to 'slightly less lazy slob' is soul-making, and 'The Late Philip J. Fry' wryly confirms life's purpose is 'probably some hogwash about the human spirit.'

soul-making-theodicy.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
soul-making-theodicy.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
soul-making-theodicy.relation: Haas uses Dean's stubborn refusal to believe in God, even after meeting Castiel, escaping Hell, and visiting Heaven, to run through the problem of evil. Casey's challenge in 'Sin City' states the logical problem; the free-will theodicy answers it but falters before Supernatural's designed horrors like the rugaru, a creature God built to suffer an irresistible hunger that ends with it eating its spouse. Dean's real objection is the evidential problem, that the amount and severity of apparently pointless evil makes the omni-God unlikely, and neither a 'natural order' defense (Dick Roman humanely farming humans for food) nor John Hick's soul-making theodicy explains suffering far beyond what character formation requires.

best-possible-world.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
best-possible-world.title: “A Boy Named Sue” A Cashian Theodicy
best-possible-world.relation: Jamie Carlin Watson reads Cash's Christian worldview as Augustinian: evil is not a positive substance but a privation or corruption of good (contra the monism Leibniz risks and the Manichean dualism Augustine rejected), so humans alone bear blame for moral evil through freely corrupting good things—'Cocaine Blues,' 'The Wall,' the Folsom prisoner who admits he 'had it coming,' and the divided self of 'The Beast in Me' echoing Romans 7. Natural evil, as in 'Guess Things Happen That Way' and the flood of 'Five Feet High and Rising' (Cash's mother's 'blessing' of rich river dirt), serves punishment or greater goods. 'A Boy Named Sue' dramatizes the residual tension: the father's get-tough-or-die theodicy convinces neither Sue nor us that the sheer amount of evil is justified.

best-possible-world.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
best-possible-world.title: Death on Veridian III
best-possible-world.relation: Uses the holodeck to re-run the problem of evil: if a safe, painless simulated world like Barclay's fantasy life in 'Hollow Pursuits' is available, why is the painful real one better? Against Hume's Dialogues complaint that a benevolent God should have cut the pain, and Leibniz's best-of-all-possible-worlds optimism, the authors stack Whitehead's 'major beauty' of intensity, Aristotle's tragic magnitude, Swinburne's good of serious responsibility, and Hick's soul-making, reading Moriarty's imprisonment in 'Ship in a Bottle,' Q's humbling in 'Déjà Q,' and Kirk leaving the Nexus because 'nothing here matters' as evidence that intensity, responsibility, and character growth exist only in the real world. Kirk's death on Veridian III in Generations supplies the cautionary counterweight: the real world's goods cost real suffering.

best-possible-world.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
best-possible-world.title: Rescuing Princess Zelda
best-possible-world.relation: Collins runs the problem of evil in Hyrule: Mackie's logical problem (an all-good, all-powerful God inconsistent with Ganondorf's evil) partially dissolves because nothing in the games says the three goddesses are omnipotent or omniscient, and Plantinga's free will defense, plus the best-of-all-possible-worlds idea, shows the Triforce is itself a free-will device, since a wish-granter that could grant any desire cannot limit evil without undoing itself. A 'game-making theodicy' modeled on Hick's soul-making theodicy explains why evil must be excessive and randomly distributed (else players would never strive to grow), and why the goddesses therefore provided a chosen hero: Link, unlike anyone on Earth, is the divine answer to excessive evil, divinely marked to reclaim the Triforce and rescue Zelda.

best-possible-world.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
best-possible-world.title: Is Monk’s Certainty Justified
best-possible-world.relation: Rauhut tests Monk's method against two models of discovery: Holmes-style eliminatism, modeled on Popper's falsification via reductio ad absurdum, and CSI-style confirmationism in the mold of Hempel and Carnap (Gil Grissom letting evidence speak). Monk fits neither — in 'Mr. Monk and the Astronaut' he refuses to eliminate the alibi-solid Steve Wagner, and in 'Mr. Monk Falls in Love' he ignores a hatpin, a motive, and a confession pointing at Leyla. Instead Monk is an 'epiphanist': he registers every anomaly (the secretary hired from a Lamaze-class ad in 'Mr. Monk Fights City Hall', Crawford's odd phrasing 'No, she wouldn't be drinking now'), suddenly sees the one theory explaining all of them, and only afterwards manufactures shareable evidence for others. His absolute certainty, the chapter argues, rests on a metaphysical faith that only the true theory can explain every anomaly — a Leibnizian 'best of all possible ordered worlds' — the same obsession with order that makes him notice anomalies at all, though it makes him epistemically irresponsible by ordinary standards that weigh alternative hypotheses and simplicity.

best-possible-world.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
best-possible-world.title: Herr Leibniz Consoles Mr. Monk
best-possible-world.relation: Kavas distinguishes Monk's method from Holmes's modus ponens, Poirot's elimination, and Goren's profiling: Monk accepts only what completes a coherent total narrative, so 'Here's what happened' re-tells the order of the whole world, as in the chess-game solution of 'Mr. Monk and the Genius'. The chapter uses the Tractatus's world of contingent, logically independent facts to model Monk's picture-completion, then brings in Leibniz: the principle of sufficient reason, the best of all possible worlds, and preestablished harmony justify Monk's faith that even Trudy's death must have a reason. Monk emerges as a pessimistic Leibniz who takes the world to be the worst possible precisely because, since learning the bomb was meant for Trudy in 'Mr. Monk Goes to Jail', he cannot see any sufficient reason for her death ('Why her?').

best-possible-world.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
best-possible-world.title: Voltaire Lives
best-possible-world.relation: Douglas Ficek traces The Onion's God stories — 'Lord Under Investigation For Failure To Provide,' God refusing to heal paralyzed little Timmy Yu, and 'God Cites Moving In Mysterious Ways' — back through Voltaire's Candide to Leibniz's theodicy, the 'best of all possible worlds' doctrine that Dr. Pangloss keeps reciting through hanging, slavery, and syphilis until Candide concludes we must cultivate our garden. The chapter's sharpest claim is that theodicy works by victim-blaming: Jerry Falwell's 9/11 rant earned the headline-only 'Jerry Falwell: Is That Guy A Dick Or What?' because he excused God by blaming secular Americans, just as Pastor Ellsworth blames heathen tsunami victims. Following theologian Dorothee Soelle, Ficek names this 'theological sadism,' and offers the Bible-drop missionaries of 'Poverty-Stricken Africans Receive Desperately Needed Bibles' as a modern Pangloss who mistakes moral obliviousness for grace.

best-possible-world.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
best-possible-world.title: The Odd Thought of Doctor Who
best-possible-world.relation: Maps Leibniz's monadology onto the Whoniverse: the Doctor's individual concept survives each regeneration as a thinking monad while its bodily monads are replaced, parallel Liz Shaws in 'Inferno' show incompossible predicates, and the Time Lords play Leibniz's God permitting minimal evil, which the Doctor accepts in refusing to avert the Daleks' creation in 'Genesis of the Daleks'. The dimensionally transcendental TARDIS illustrates the principle of indiscernibles, the Matrix becomes a failed pre-established harmony haunted by confused perceptions, and the Master hallucinates against the Doctor like Descartes's evil demon. The Valeyard is modeled as an incompossible world on Leibniz's Sextus Tarquinius pyramid and Borges's forking paths, closing with Leibniz's own 'odd thought' academy of wonders.

best-possible-world.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
best-possible-world.title: Time Enough to Drink the Poison
best-possible-world.relation: Domino reads 'The Veiled Lodger' as a drama about hope in a world after God: Holmes's 'Your life is not your own; keep your hands off it' revives Plato's Phaedo argument that we are the gods' possessions, but deist-or-atheist Mrs. Ronder is unmoved, so Holmes falls back on the Leibnizian alternative to the Stoic and Cartesian 'patience without hope' — the example of patient suffering as 'the most precious of all lessons,' grounded in Leibniz's hope that the world is no 'cruel jest.' Jefferson Hope's two pill boxes in A Study in Scarlet literalize the Leibnizian link between hope and divine justice by letting God choose who dies, while Trelawney Hope's gullibility makes the surname ironic. Mrs. Ronder's true hope was reunion with Leonardo, which his death destroyed; what saves her is a new hope founded on Watson's text, since only a writer ('I have made a slight change of name and place') can change the past.

best-possible-world.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
best-possible-world.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
best-possible-world.relation: Trip McCrossin casts the creature as a modern Job: repeatedly and unreasonably mistreated by the De Laceys, the rustic whose child he saved, and Victor despite his benevolence, he cries 'This was then the reward of my benevolence!' - but unlike Job he loses faith, because his problem of evil is secular, justifying not 'the Ways of God to Man' but 'the Ways of Man to monsters.' The chapter traces the problem from Job and Paradise Lost through Bayle's defense of faith over reason and the Optimists' 'best of all possible worlds,' whose credibility drowned with the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, setting Rousseau against Voltaire: Rousseau's Emile ('All is good leaving the hands of the author of things') demands that we make evil intelligible through self-knowledge, while Candide counsels tending our garden. The creature embodies Rousseau's line - 'I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend' - yet ends in self-abhorring remorse over Victor's death, leaving open whether self-knowledge can ever answer unreasonable suffering.

best-possible-world.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
best-possible-world.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
best-possible-world.relation: Montoya asks whether Prismo, Adventure Time's wish-granting stand-in for God, produced the best possible world when he restored Ooo over Farmworld. After explaining Leibniz's answer to the problem of evil—that an all-good, all-knowing God permits some evil because every possible world contains some, and ours contains the least—the chapter compares Farmworld (no Lich, but Finn becomes the Ice King, Jake mutates into the Lich, Marceline dies ancient and insane) with Ooo, where the same characters flourish as heroes. Prismo, no omnibenevolent deity, remakes Ooo out of friendship with Jake, and Farmworld's horrors vindicate the Leibnizian point that wishing one evil out of existence can unleash far worse.

best-possible-world.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
best-possible-world.title: 6. Tris’s Compassion and the Problem of Evil
best-possible-world.relation: McCrossin reads Tris's whole arc as a struggle with the problem of evil, both the theological version from Job and the modern secular one Susan Neiman describes, in which unreasonable suffering threatens trust in human reason. He casts Tris as cut from Rousseau's mold - her insistence on making the evils of Jeanine, Marcus, and Evelyn intelligible - against Voltaire's Candide refusal to rationalize suffering, and treats the faction system as Rousseau's social-contract strategy for containing the inclination to evil while Tris herself plays a wartime Emile. The key is Tobias's lesson that selflessness and bravery are not that different: selflessness enables the courage that compassion motivates, from pressing her forehead to Jeanine's gun in the fear landscape to taking Caleb's place at the weapons lab, so that the trilogy ends with Tobias's 'we mend each other.'

best-possible-world.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
best-possible-world.title: 4. Acts of God
best-possible-world.relation: McCrossin reads Lecter's parable of the church collapses - 'It must feel good to God - He does it all the time, and are we not made in His image?' - as Lecter's solution to the problem of evil in both its theological (Job) and secular (Neiman) forms: a malevolent deity of the kind de Sade's Saint-Fond describes, doing God's work becomes Lecter's justification, and killing feels good because 'if one does what God does enough times, one will become as God is'. Following Neiman, he sets Rousseau's tradition (evil must be made intelligible - 'All is well leaving the hands of the author of things') against Voltaire's Candide refusal of theodicy, showing that Will and Starling live in Rousseau's camp except when facing Lecter himself, and that the Hannibal/Hannibal Rising revelation that Mischa's murder 'happened' to him radically revises his earlier claim that 'we don't invent our natures', with Starling's reason finally making 'a place for Mischa' in Lecter and Starling together.

best-possible-world.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
best-possible-world.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
best-possible-world.relation: Smith weighs Sheldon's vendetta against Wil Wheaton — the skipped 1995 Dixie Trek convention, the fake dead 'Nana' that won the Mystic Warlords tournament ('Game over, Moon Pie!'), the bowling-alley sabotage of Leonard and Penny — against theories of evil: Leibniz's best-of-all-possible-worlds theodicy (with Voltaire's Candide objection), Buber's claim that the lie is the specific evil humanity introduced into nature, and Arendt's banality of evil at Eichmann's trial, which shows Wil's deceptions are bad moral choices rather than evil. Nietzsche's will to power would instead admire Wil, and even Khan-style revenge, as proto-Übermensch exploitation. The chapter closes by reading Sheldon's 'Comic Book World paradigm' (the Green Goblin to his Spider-Man) through Ricoeur's view that evil is grasped through myths and symbols: Star Trek and comics are the symbolic framework by which he interprets wrongdoing he cannot otherwise fathom.

best-possible-world.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
best-possible-world.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
best-possible-world.relation: Jaime Lannister's question to Catelyn Stark - 'If the gods are real and they are just, then why is the world so full of injustice?' - launches a tour of the logical and evidential problems of evil across the religions of Westeros. Augustine's privation theory and free will defense are tested against the Faith of the Seven (with Catelyn answering 'Because of men like you'), Hume's dilemma of impotence or malevolence is applied to the old gods that Arya scolds at Harrenhal for failing to save Ned, and Leibniz's best-possible-world reply is weighed against natural evils like the storm that sank the Windproud. The chapter concludes that only the evidential problem sticks: the sheer quantity of suffering in Westeros is evidence against just gods, though nothing counts against the uncaring gods Brienne describes.

best-possible-world.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
best-possible-world.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
best-possible-world.relation: Nielsen asks whether a Green Lantern with unlimited willpower would be a god and answers no through Leibniz: God is the absolutely perfect being, where perfection excludes contradiction so that knowledge and power admit of perfection but 'the greatest of all numbers' does not, and such a being creates the best of all possible worlds. Hume's trilemma (impotent, malevolent, or whence evil?) is met with the theodicy that finite minds, like Lanterns baffled by Guardian decrees, cannot compare our world to the discarded possibilities, each perhaps as bad as Qward. Since omnipotence requires omniscience and omnibenevolence, not even Parallax, the Anti-Monitor, or Kyle as Ion counts as omnipotent: admirable and powerful, but not gods.

best-possible-world.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
best-possible-world.title: Notes
best-possible-world.relation: Blessing diagnoses Ted's 'rom-communism' as the naive optimism Voltaire satirized in Candide: Pangloss's 'best of all possible worlds' is Leibniz's greater-goods theodicy and Principle of Sufficient Reason, and its fatalism ('it will all work out exactly as it's supposed to') collapses under Ted's panic attacks and 'belief can't score goals.' Against it she sets Camus's The Plague: Dr. Rieux's absurd heroism, refusal of hope as 'philosophical suicide,' and 'strange hope' grounded in collective decency, arguing Ted's real, sustainable creed is Camus-like faith in teamwork and human goodness rather than belief that everything works out.

best-possible-world.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
best-possible-world.title: Notes
best-possible-world.relation: Freeman reads Ted as Chesterton's holy fool, in the lineage of Don Quixote and The Idiot and modeled on Innocent Smith in Manalive: his apparently foolish decisions (benching Jamie, the crooked BELIEVE sign meaning the room is 'outta whack') disclose a higher optimism that faces real evil, delights in Being as a gift, and loves the world patriotically like a relegation-threatened home team. The chapter then argues Ted's optimism diverges from Chesterton's by lacking its Christian foundation - Ted believes in belief itself, 'to which god and in what language?' - so the show can intuit but not justify the optimism it depicts.

best-possible-world.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
best-possible-world.title: Introduction
best-possible-world.relation: The editors' introduction frames the Terminator saga as philosophy's natural territory by telling how philosophers persisted through catastrophe: Leibniz's 'best of all possible worlds' collapsed after the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, Hegel finished the Phenomenology of Spirit while Napoleon shelled Jena, and Adorno rebuilt cultural philosophy after Auschwitz. It compares that persistence to the human resistance against Skynet, and says the saga is founded on a paradox of human nature - we create our own worst nightmares. Quoting Bertrand Russell that most people would rather die than think, it urges readers to switch their CPU from read-only to learning mode and confront Judgment Day's paradoxes and the moral status of the machines.

best-possible-world.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
best-possible-world.title: The Odd Thought of Doctor Who
best-possible-world.relation: Gregory Kalyniuk maps Leibniz's monadology onto Doctor Who. The Doctor's identity across regenerations is a thinking monad whose individual concept holds necessary predicates while appurtenant body-monads are replaced; the Time Lords play Leibniz's God overseeing pre-established harmony and permitting evil in the best world (refusing to stop the Daleks in 'Genesis'). The dimensionally transcendental TARDIS illustrates the identity of indiscernibles, the Matrix is a Leibnizian mill of confused perceptions (with the Master as Descartes's evil demon), and the incompossible Valeyard of 'Trial of a Time Lord' is read via Leibniz's Theodicy pyramid and Borges's forking paths.

best-possible-world.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
best-possible-world.title: 9. Foundation’s Optimism
best-possible-world.relation: McCrossin reads the sequels Foundation's Edge and Foundation and Earth as an Optimistic response to the problem of evil, in the lineage of Leibniz, Rousseau, and Hegel's 'All is well', set against the WWII, Holocaust, Nuremberg, and Eichmann-trial backdrop of Asimov's writing and Arendt's banality of evil. Tracking Gendibal's mantra 'all will happen well', the Gaia/Galaxia choice via Trevize's 'talent for rightness', and Daneel Olivaw's Zeroth Law and plan to merge with Fallom's brain, he uses the Book of Job to frame whether the series' recurring reassurance is earned or merely reframed.

best-possible-world.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
best-possible-world.title: index
best-possible-world.relation: This composite chapter opens with the volume's Introduction and then runs several essays. Jeff McLaughlin's 'What If?' reads DC's Crisis on Infinite Earths and Marvel's What If? series as literal illustrations of Leibniz's possible-worlds metaphysics: the multiverse of Earth-1, Earth-2 and the 3,000 doomed universes dramatizes counterfactuals and Leibniz's Theodicy argument (via the principle of sufficient reason) that God actualizes only the best of infinitely many possible worlds, with Descartes invoked on why a perfect God permits imperfection. Amy Kiste Nyberg's essay analyzes the 1954 Senate hearings on EC horror comics (Gaines's 'The Orphan') as an applied-ethics clash between publishers' free expression and protecting children, explicitly deploying Mill's On Liberty and harm principle to argue why the child-audience framing defeats the anti-censorship case. Stanford Carpenter's piece treats the Black Captain America (Truth: Red, White, and Black) as an epistemology-of-authorship problem.

capabilities-approach.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
capabilities-approach.title: A Fork in the Road
capabilities-approach.relation: Anderson contrasts two American freedoms through Springsteen and Tracy Chapman: the negative freedom of 'Racing in the Street,' 'Thunder Road,' and 'Born to Run' — Thoreauvian wildness, the outlaw who blows off duty, wins the dude from L.A.'s money and 'little girl' as a prize, then finds her crying on her daddy's porch — against the positive freedom of Chapman's 'Fast Car' heroine, who initially sees the fast car as a way to 'be someone' but finally sends the aimless drinker off and seeks empowerment of her own abilities. Drawing on Margaret Fuller (men squander freedom on appetite and domination), Charlotte Perkins Gilman (male-built structures channel women's freedom through men), and Nussbaum (flourishing, failure built into the structure), he argues that male negative freedom is dialectically coupled to women's oppression, that justice must trump the call of the wild, yet that men's own collateral damage — desolation, alienation — must also be addressed.

capabilities-approach.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
capabilities-approach.title: “There’s More to Life than Profit”
capabilities-approach.relation: Held argues business ethics stalls because it begins from capitalism's presuppositions instead of asking what we fundamentally value, staging the impasse as Quark versus Rom and as Friedman's stockholder theory against Freeman's stakeholder theory ('The Dogs of War', Zek's reforms, 'Profit and Lace'). He recovers Aristotle's Politics distinction between economics serving the household's good and chrematistics — money-making as sheer accumulation, embodied in Quark's 'pure profit' embezzlement — and corrects the libertarian caricature of Adam Smith: the invisible hand works only within commutative justice and virtue, markets serving welfare rather than profit. Through Sen's capability approach and Quark's own defense of greed as promoting human development in 'Prophet Motive', the chapter concludes profit is only a means to freedom and well-being — 'there's more to life than profit' — and the Rules of Acquisition themselves must stand before the ethical judge.

capabilities-approach.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
capabilities-approach.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
capabilities-approach.relation: Shaun Young tests Jeopardy! against equality as an 'essentially contested concept': Aristotle's proportional equality (treat like cases as like) seems to justify the winner-take-all payout as deserved, Locke's reward for the industrious explains why equal outcomes would kill incentive, and Rawls's two principles - fair equality of opportunity plus the difference principle - capture the show's identical rules and level playing field. He then raises harder challenges: Dworkin's equality of resources, Kymlicka's charge that the Americo-centric clue bank shortchanges minority cultures (with Quebec's Bill 101 as legitimate differentiated rights), and the capabilities approach of Sen and Nussbaum applied to would-be contestants who cannot operate the signaling device. Citing Isaiah Berlin's pluralism, he concludes that no final verdict on Jeopardy!'s equality is possible - and that spectators would not want one, since Jennings's seventy-four-game streak thrills precisely because of inequality between players.

capabilities-approach.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
capabilities-approach.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
capabilities-approach.relation: Nicolas Michaud argues the creature is a person on every serious criterion: it satisfies Kant's rationality test and Mary Anne Warren's five criteria (consciousness, reasoning, self-motivated activity, communication, self-concept) in both Shelley's novel and I, Frankenstein, and it possesses all ten of Nussbaum's capabilities for flourishing. The twist is that judging the monster a blameworthy murderer already concedes the personhood we deny him, while our exclusion of him is bare Othering and speciesism of the kind Tom Regan attacks in animal ethics. Michaud ends by reversing the question: after humanity's record of crushing minorities, which the creature learns from Volney's Ruins of Empires and weeps over with Safie, what argument could Victor give Adam for sparing us?

capabilities-approach.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
capabilities-approach.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
capabilities-approach.relation: Roger Hunt argues the films show that whoever assumes human superiority or ownership of created life gets eaten: Dieter Stark zaps a compy and is devoured by a swarm of them, Ludlow claims InGen's patent and becomes a hunting lesson for the baby T. rex. He stages the real debate over dinosaur moral status between the 'value of life' view (Harding and Sattler: experiment on them if enough sentient beings benefit) and Tom Regan's rights view - anything sentient has basic rights from unconditional individual value, and grading lives by usefulness is speciesism like racism or sexism. He then prefers Martha Nussbaum's capabilities approach: a T. rex penned in San Diego cannot roam, hunt, or play, so it cannot flourish, and the point is not granting rights but recognizing we have no right to block other beings' flourishing for fun.

capabilities-approach.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
capabilities-approach.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
capabilities-approach.relation: The chapter argues Finn is not yet a true hero but is on a quest to become one: against rule systems like Mill's greatest-happiness utilitarianism and Kantian respect for persons, virtue ethics asks not 'what should I do' but 'who should I be', and Aristotle's point that children lack fully developed practical reason explains why Finn's good intentions misfire - removing Donny exposes the house people to Why-wolves, and Penny's trick humiliates him in the City of Thieves. Martha Nussbaum's ideal of every person as free and of equal dignity grounds heroism in the common good, and her work on literature and popular culture explains how watching Finn's exaggerated choices trains our own moral judgment. Citing Franco and Zimbardo's psychology of real heroes - empathy, risk tolerance, persistence - and closing with Seneca's 'how nobly you live', it concludes that since Aristotelian virtue is a habit, anyone can start by admitting they suck at heroism and practicing, as Jake's advice puts it.

capabilities-approach.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
capabilities-approach.title: Notes
capabilities-approach.relation: Matthew Watts sorts Fallout's artificial beings into cyborgs, synths, and pure robots and tests each against a theory of the self: Locke's memory theory explains the Robobrain socialites of Vault 118 and Nick Valentine's implanted prewar past, Parfit's psychological continuity (identity as a matter of degree) makes the Old World Blues Think Tank a caricature of a self stretched too thin, and Putnam's machine-table functionalism with multiple realizability (the Red Menace holotape running on any hardware) undermines Covenant's SAFE test by making function, not substrate, the mark of a mind. DiMA's excision of his own guilty memory in Far Harbor shows identity as Evan Thompson's enactive process rather than stored recall, since pruning memories can maintain or improve the self-in-progress. For moral standing below full personhood, Nussbaum's capabilities approach fits Curie's flourishing (research, companionship, watching a sunset in a synth body) and Singer's sentience criterion fits Victor the Securitron's avoidance of harm, exposing 'substrate prejudice' as a robot analog of speciesism - down to ED-E's triumphant arrival on the West Coast.

capabilities-approach.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
capabilities-approach.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
capabilities-approach.relation: Schick asks whether humans need to alter consciousness (Weil, Maslow's hierarchy, Siegel's animal examples of reindeer, elephants, and rats seeking intoxicants) and concludes we have no such need, though we can flourish from it. He applies Sen and Nussbaum's capabilities approach, arguing cannabis enhances Nussbaum's second (bodily health, via endocannabinoids and medical uses) and fourth (senses, imagination, thought, via enriched music perception and possible creativity) capabilities. Citing Aristotle's and the Buddha's golden mean against abuse, and evidence of no lasting brain harm, he judges paternalistic prohibition an unjustified deprivation of the capabilities needed for a good life.

capabilities-approach.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
capabilities-approach.title: 27. Squid Game as Philosophy The Myths of Democracy
capabilities-approach.relation: The chapter argues that Squid Game exposes five 'myths' of democracy by showing how its trappings mask control by the wealthy few. Using Aristotle's Politics and Nicomachean Ethics it attacks the myth of free choice (the players' consent is coerced by debt) and the failure to cultivate virtue and transparency (Gi-hun deceives Il-nam in the marble game); it uses Sen and Nussbaum's capability approach to deny genuine empowerment; and it applies Plato's Phaedo two-worlds doctrine to argue the game instantiates no true form of truth, beauty, goodness, or justice. Il-nam's tie-breaking vote and Player 111's advantages illustrate that equality is only superficial, leaving a Hobbesian war of all against all inside a democratic shell.

stream-of-consciousness.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
stream-of-consciousness.title: Foreword
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Show writer David Weddle recounts how Ron Moore pushed him and Brad Thompson to abandon Star Trek-style expository dialogue and tell 'Act of Contrition' through flashbacks interleaved with the present, dramatizing Starbuck's guilt over passing Zak Adama on his flight test. He argues this unlocked a stream-of-consciousness mode — dreams, hallucinations, and memories flowing out of characters' inner emotional lives — that the series extended in episodes like 'Scar,' 'Maelstrom,' and 'Unfinished Business,' echoing Faulkner's 'the past isn't even past.' The foreword is a creator's testimony that BSG's scrambled-chronology storytelling is what made the show worthy of a book of philosophical readings.

stream-of-consciousness.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
stream-of-consciousness.title: Group Will
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Testerman turns inception against itself: Cobb and Saito believe they freely plan the Fischer job, but conscious will is a feeling, not a cause. From William James's effortful attention and Dewey's willpower she moves to Penfield's stimulated patients and Libet's readiness-potential experiments showing the brain prepares action before we feel we will it, so Fischer, Cobb and Saito are all equally 'incepted' by subconscious forces - 'freedom is ignorance of the causes of actions', as she glosses Spinoza, with Hume's point that causality is only inferred. Advertising, the foot-in-the-door effect and subliminal primes already do inception's work more cheaply, and the team's 'group will' flows from Saito's own unexamined drive for power, so against Socrates she concludes the unexamined life is perfectly suitable for living.

stream-of-consciousness.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
stream-of-consciousness.title: The Logic of Expectation: Family Guy and the Non Sequitur
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Argues that Family Guy's non sequiturs only seem random because they reverse specific expectations, so the show has a 'logic of expectation' even where it flouts inference: the Supreme Court fraternity hazing in 'Let's Go to the Hop,' Stewie's aristocratic-baby role reversal, Death hiding beer on his breath in 'Wasted Talent,' the Kool-Aid Man's sheepish exit in 'Death Has a Shadow,' and cutaways that run on shared pop-culture associations like Peter's 'no whammy' chant. The chapter deploys Kierkegaard's claim that wherever there is contradiction the comical is present, Schopenhauer's analysis of the ludicrous, Wittgenstein's joke-book remark, and Russell's ideal of disambiguating ambiguous sentences (Peter's 'I can also vomit' reply to Lois). It closes metaphysically: against Spinoza's necessity and Hume's 'one damn thing after another,' Quahog is not William James's 'mere withness' world because the gags depend on an orderly baseline, which Peter himself demonstrates by wearing a cardboard TV frame in 'I Never Met the Dead Man'.

stream-of-consciousness.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
stream-of-consciousness.title: Group Will
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Testerman argues the film's heist is ironic because nobody in it acts from conscious will: citing Libet's readiness-potential experiments and Penfield's stimulation cases, she claims the feeling of willing is a post-hoc 'epistemic illusion,' so Fischer's inception merely dramatizes what happens all the time — Cobb's 'all experience is inception' becomes a thesis about ordinary agency, with Spinoza's dictum that freedom is ignorance of the causes of our actions as its motto. She reads the plot through this lens: Saito's unexamined hunger for power silently drives the team's 'group will,' Cobb's 'positive emotion trumps negative emotion' tactic exploits the limbic system, and cheaper tricks (Arthur's elephant, foot-in-the-door, subliminal advertising) would have worked as well. Against Socrates she concludes the unexamined life is perfectly livable, since introspection can never reach the subconscious causes of behavior.

stream-of-consciousness.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
stream-of-consciousness.title: All Human Experience is an Impression
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Ruetenik argues the best SNL impressions are not 'spot on': Carvey's Bush ('Not gonna do it. Wouldn't be prudent') and the Tom Brokaw pre-tapes sketch created new experiences rather than faithful copies, while Darrell Hammond's exact impressions made him a 'tribute band' without Carvey's artistry. Dewey's Art as Experience and James's selective attention, in which every perceiver is an impressionist ignoring the blooming buzzing confusion, ground the claim that all experience is creative re-presentation rather than tribute to reality. He then turns the point political: SNL casting Amy Poehler over a spot-on Black impressionist as Michael Jackson tells us something about the audience's own selective, and possibly racist, experience.

stream-of-consciousness.title: The Instructive Impossibility of Being John Malkovich
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Hagberg treats Being John Malkovich as a refutation of the dualist fantasy that one could achieve transparent knowledge of another mind by occupying it. Through the film's four levels—Schwartz as spectator inside Malkovich, Lotte's transgender re-embodiment, Schwartz's puppeteering, and Malkovich falling into his own portal to the 'Malkovich, Malkovich' hell—he shows, via Jamesian relational sensation and Wittgenstein's private-language argument, that it is always still Schwartz who senses, so no one ever becomes Malkovich. The self-enclosed Malkovich world, where everyone can only say 'Malkovich,' dramatizes that selfhood is relationally emergent (Royce, Mead) and that experience is inviolably one's own (Margalit on remembered emotion).

stream-of-consciousness.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
stream-of-consciousness.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
stream-of-consciousness.relation: Hathaway and Sharpley analyze the cannabis experience of medical-'compassion club' users through Csikszentmihalyi's concept of 'flow.' They ground flow in William James's 'stream of consciousness' and in Taoism, reading Tao as 'a patterned flow of the universe' and wu wei as the effortless equilibrium users describe ('it just centers me,' 'I take an inventory on my soul'). Against Western monophasic medicine, they defend users' 'anecdotal' testimony as legitimate knowledge of a body–mind–spirit balance that cannabis restores.

cyborg.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
cyborg.title: Frak-tured Finality
cyborg.relation: Booth argues that the 'Resistance' webisodes fracture BSG's narrative across television and Internet, forcing viewers to actively construct the story — Jammer's execution in 'Collaborators' and Duck's suicide bombing only make full sense if you pieced the webisodes together — and that this viewer-side fragmentation mirrors the characters' fractured identities. Drawing on Foucault's constructed self, Deleuze and Guattari's 'schizophrenia,' Goffman's performed roles, and Haraway's cyborg, he reads Baltar's 'Am I a Cylon?', Boomer's amnesia in 'Water,' Hera's human-Cylon hybridity, and Tigh's choice in 'Crossroads' to actively construct who he will be. The payoff: there is no central location for the self, the narrative, or Cylonhood — each becomes whole only through active construction.

cyborg.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
cyborg.title: The Secret Plot of ‘Baby Boomers’
cyborg.relation: Chess proposes that BSG is 'a narrative about queer reproduction,' combining Haraway's cyborg with Butler's heteronormativity to coin 'technoqueer': Cylons embody fears that technology makes heterosexual reproduction unnecessary. Helo's 'I'm in love with a woman I know isn't a woman,' the 'you can't rape a machine' debate after the Pegasus assault, and download-resurrection as asexual reproduction all mark Cylons as queer others — yet the Cylons' obsession with conceiving Hera, paralleled with The L Word's Bette and Tina, shows them trapped between rejecting and emulating heteronormativity, farming human women at the Cylon 'Farm' while craving legitimate babies. Hera's birth terrifies Roslin because it legitimizes the technoqueer and with it human reproductive obsolescence.

cyborg.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
cyborg.title: Stable Bodies
cyborg.relation: Heinricy argues the human/Cylon line is drawn on the body: following Mary Douglas, bodies function as cultural boundaries, so Cylons figure as contamination to be hunted (Boomer in the fleet) and marked as other by violence (Gina's torture), though Athena's loyal service and Tigh's exposure show the fear is socially constructed rather than natural. Cylon insides are known only through technology (Caprica Six's glowing spine, Athena's blood interface in 'Flight of the Phoenix'), and their bodies' stability — no scars, aging, or change — is paid for in unstable minds (Tigh killing Ellen, Boomer strangling Hera), whereas messy human bodies carry potential, hope, and change, as Apollo's weight fluctuation shows. Since we are all already cyborgs (vaccines, pills, GMOs), the Numbers are a further human-machine integration, and Hera and Nicky's blending is the ultimate 'contamination' and a new hope.

heteronormativity.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
heteronormativity.title: The Secret Plot of ‘Baby Boomers’
heteronormativity.relation: Chess proposes that BSG is 'a narrative about queer reproduction,' combining Haraway's cyborg with Butler's heteronormativity to coin 'technoqueer': Cylons embody fears that technology makes heterosexual reproduction unnecessary. Helo's 'I'm in love with a woman I know isn't a woman,' the 'you can't rape a machine' debate after the Pegasus assault, and download-resurrection as asexual reproduction all mark Cylons as queer others — yet the Cylons' obsession with conceiving Hera, paralleled with The L Word's Bette and Tina, shows them trapped between rejecting and emulating heteronormativity, farming human women at the Cylon 'Farm' while craving legitimate babies. Hera's birth terrifies Roslin because it legitimizes the technoqueer and with it human reproductive obsolescence.

heteronormativity.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
heteronormativity.title: The Fruitcake as Performative Exemplar
heteronormativity.relation: John Kaag pairs Buffett's 'Fruitcakes' with Judith Butler's constructivism: institutions 'girl' infants through interpellation (the sonogram naming), the heterosexual imperative abjects gay, lesbian, and transgender 'nobodies,' and these excluded fruitcakes are the cosmic baker's half-baked people. The movie-theater stanza ('a twelve pound Nestle Crunch for twenty-five dollars') becomes Heidegger's das Man, others thinking and choosing for us, while Buffett's 'mea culpa' refrain and 'Religion's in the hands of some crazy-ass people' attack the guilt constitutive of Christian subjecthood, with Dewey's broad, doctrine-free religious experience offered as common ground. Buffett concerts themselves are read as performative exemplars — drag-show-like borderland communities where four generations act out the 'little bit of fruitcake' in everyone as a quiet political protest against enforced normalcy.

heteronormativity.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
heteronormativity.title: Banal Sex
heteronormativity.relation: Marinucci reads The Onion's sex coverage as 'terminally ambiguous': 'Nation's Gays Demand Right To Library Cards,' 'Massachusetts Supreme Court Orders All Citizens To Gay Marry,' and 'New Bill Would Defend Marriage From Sharks' ridicule the idea that gay marriage threatens straight marriage, while 'Area Homosexual Saves Four From Fire: Heroic Neighbor Praised, Gay' exposes how heterosexism defines gay people sexually while heterosexual men pass as normal, natural, and neutral. Yet the paper also trades in gay stereotypes and mocks the very framework—characters like Amanda Oppel ('Lesbian Identity Ends Abruptly Mid-Junior Year'), the 'Bar Skanks Announce Plans To Kiss,' and Bruce Heffernan of 'Why Do All These Homosexuals Keep Sucking My Cock?' both defy and seem to reaffirm the stability of sexual identity categories. Weighing queer theory (via Jagose) and Golden's fluid 'elective lesbians' against the parody of 'Grad Student Deconstructs Take-Out Menu,' she concludes the paper's stance is deliberately undecidable, perhaps recommending we stop over-thinking sex and treat minority sexual identities as banal, as in 'Gay Couple Has Banal Sex.'

heteronormativity.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
heteronormativity.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: A feminist media-studies audit: the first two seasons flunk most feminist criteria (Skyler the pregnant homemaker, Marie the kleptomaniac, Jane existing mainly to develop Jesse), but seasons three and four deepen everyone - Walt's agonized Krazy-8 decision curdles into the lily-of-the-valley child-poisoning, while Skyler seizes the household, launders money through the car wash, and fixes Ted's IRS crisis, 'breaking bad' herself. Gus's hinted homosexuality with Max is praised for quietly rocking heteronormative assumptions. Conclusion: by Season Four the title applies to Skyler too, and her depth alone nearly passes any analytical test a feminist scholar might employ.

heteronormativity.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
heteronormativity.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: Pye and O'Sullivan use Judith Butler's claim that gender is performative to read the walkers as genderless: they keep the trappings of biological sex but perform no gender, and like drag queens they 'trouble gender' when the little girl walker turns to face Rick. The survivors, by contrast, drag patriarchy along as cultural baggage - Lori telling Carl 'I'm a girl, you talk to him' while Shane teaches frogs, Ed bullying the laundry line, the men confiscating Andrea's gun while Daryl keeps his crossbow - though counter-examples (Andrea and Amy fishing for the camp, Guillermo's camp of caretaking 'vatos' led by a former custodian and a nurse, Rick teaching Andrea the safety) show gender can be learned differently. Invoking Rorty's thought that assumptions become visible only when their contradictories sound plausible, they argue survival itself demands shedding these roles, since the genderless dead threaten everyone equally.

heteronormativity.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
heteronormativity.title: Futurama and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: Onishi argues humor exposes cultural normalcy: Futurama transplants twenty-first-century prejudices into the future, where Leela's one eye still gets her mocked by the blind-and-deaf orphan Kirk ('The Cyber House Rules') and same-sex marriage is unremarkable while robosexual marriage is taboo ('Proposition Infinity,' a parody of California's Proposition 8). Leela's phaser-eye surgery and her self-loathing until 'Leela's Homeworld' reveals she is a mutant show standards of normalcy are cultural rather than natural, and are wielded oppressively. Drawing on Aristotle's habituation, Hume's habit, and Foucault's disciplinary production of subjects, the chapter uses Bender's change of heart after dating the Lucy Liu-bot head in 'I Dated a Robot' to argue habits change through meeting actual people rather than abstract 'ideas' of communities - which is how satire quietly extends what counts as normal.

heteronormativity.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
