heteronormativity.title: Dracula and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: De Waal reads Dracula through Judith Butler's gender performativity: the Count terrifies because he 'does' gender wrong - a captor who cooks and mothers Jonathan like an 'angel in the house,' feeds Mina from his breast, and turns Lucy from Victorian maiden into wanton vamp. Harker as a 'dude in distress,' Van Helsing's hysteria, and the Dracula-Mina scene that 'opens new orifices' become parodies exposing gender as an incessant citation of copies. The hunters' 'sterilizing' of Dracula's boxes of earth is read against the eugenics movement and society's police function against gender-nonconforming people.

heteronormativity.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
heteronormativity.title: 11. Leda, Castor, and Their Families
heteronormativity.relation: Shows how the clones queer the normative family: clones as such are "biological outlaws" (via Stephanie Turner's reading of Ripley in Alien), Siobhan turns out to be the genetic half-sister of the clones cloned from her own mother Kendall, and the chosen family — Felix the "brother sestra," Kira's aunties, Helena's dream baby shower — repeatedly rebuilds kinship outside blood and marriage. Against this stands the stripping of reproductive agency: the infertility sequence written into the Leda clones, Coady's weaponized sterilizing virus, and above all Helena, whose eggs are harvested and implanted by Henrik and Gracie's father without consent. The chapter's conclusion is that Orphan Black's blood families are abusive and controlling while the non-normative chosen families of Clone Club are where love and consent actually live.

heteronormativity.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
heteronormativity.title: 10. And the Rest Is Drag
heteronormativity.relation: Oliver Norman takes RuPaul's lyric 'we're all born naked and the rest is drag' from 'Born Naked' and asks whether its claim that everyone does drag all the time contradicts a show that crowns one drag superstar. Through Judith Butler's Gender Trouble and 'Gender is Burning' he reads drag as a play on gender that can either parody the male/female binary or reinforce it (the Mary Cheney misogyny charge, Michelle Visage's 'show woman not boy' critique, fishy queens like Courtney Act and trans queens like Gia Gunn). He then deploys Erving Goffman's Presentation of Self in Everyday Life: everyday social roles - the doctor's white coat, Alaska's Mae West on Snatch Game, the ideal pageant queen - are scripted performances with 'ideal types,' so the muscle-car seducer in the song is doing unwitting drag. The resolution: 'drag as ontology' is the low everyday form everyone performs, while Drag Race stages the high-art form that consciously fucks with the social script.

heteronormativity.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
heteronormativity.title: Being Gay for Jamie (or, How to Rethink Sexuality)
heteronormativity.relation: The chapter uses Devon Banks's failed Practicology conversion and Liz's blind date with Gretchen Thomas to argue sexual orientation is not chosen, then brings in Freud's view that infants are polymorphously perverse with culture training undirected desire, which explains Athenian pederasty, same-sex behavior in over 200 mammalian species, and Frank going 'gay for Jamie' in 'Cougars'. It argues homophobia rests on anchoring gender to sex under a normative heterosexuality, so Jack reads Liz's shoes, the Floyd bromance, and Devon's every remark as sexual signs. Against Liz's claim that being gay for just one person 'isn't a thing', the chapter contends our either/or homo/hetero categories arbitrarily essentialize orientation given the messy chromosomal and genital facts about biological sex.

heteronormativity.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
heteronormativity.title: The Secret Plot of ‘Baby Boomers’
heteronormativity.relation: Chess argues Battlestar Galactica is 'a narrative about queer reproduction': via Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto and Butler's account of heteronormativity, the Cylons are 'technoqueer,' embodying how fears of technology overlap with fears of non-heterosexual reproduction. Their download-based 'photocopying' reproduction and their obsessive pursuit of legitimate biological babies (the Farm's breeding facility, Athena's 'unnatural' pregnancy that Roslin calls a 'thing') express the anxiety that new reproductive technologies make heterosexuality obsolete, which the chapter pairs scene-for-scene with The L Word's Bette and Tina. Helo's 'I'm in love with a woman I know isn't a woman' and the Pegasus crew's 'you cannot rape a machine' debate show homophobia folding into technophobia, with Hera as the illegitimate queer child both societies fear.

heteronormativity.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
heteronormativity.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: Sansa's journey from tourney-romance believer to 'they are no true knights' anchors a feminist argument that chivalry is unjust as a code, not merely corrupted by bad knights like Ser Gregor and Ser Meryn Trant, who beats Sansa at Joffrey's command. The pedestal, as Gloria Steinem says, is a prison: chivalry makes knights eternal guardians and ladies permanent childlike wards, a move the chapter explains through Spivak's account of saviors who turn the people they help into dependents and through Beauvoir's point that the custom of ladyhood manufactures the very 'fact' of female fragility it claims to protect. Arya's needlework, Brienne's unbeaten sword, Loras crowning Sansa while loving Renly, and Varys's riddle on power show the knight/lady roles are neither natural nor exhaustive, so 'there are no true knights' because chivalry itself blocks human flourishing.

heteronormativity.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
heteronormativity.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: Reading Salander as genderqueer rather than simply a woman, the chapter argues her feminism lies in swift retaliation against those who abuse women and in economic and sexual independence from men, while her refusal of every identity label ('I don't know what I am') aligns her with queer theory's anti-identity politics. Judith Butler's performativity grounds the reading: Salander's body modifications and wardrobe 'undo' conventional gendering, and her drag-like aliases—the big-busted heiress Monica Sholes and the quiet Irene Nesser—succeed at fraud and flight only through absolute adherence to heteronormative femininity, proving gender is continuously constructed. Foucault's History of Sexuality frames her pathologization, institutionalization, and regulated sexuality as the medicalization of the sexually peculiar, a disciplinary script she reverses by hacking, surveilling, and exposing the authorities who pathologized her, tattooing i am a sadistic pig, a pervert and a rapist onto Bjurman.

heteronormativity.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
heteronormativity.title: NOTES
heteronormativity.relation: The chapter tests the genre constraint: one might argue Dumbledore's sexuality cannot be true because children's-genre worlds like Goodnight Moon exclude adult sexuality, but Potter's book-length Hagrid and Madame Maxime flirtation and Snape's unrequited love for Lily defeat that, and the young-adult convention that adults' desires stay invisible to youthful protagonists instead explains the canon's silence. Gendler reads the books' metaphorical treatment of minority identity, Tonks marrying werewolf Lupin, Hermione's house-elf campaign, the Mudblood and pureblood talk, as catching readers in an act of unwitting toleration, while Dumbledore's love for his intellectual equal Grindelwald does real plot work in blinding him.

heteronormativity.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
heteronormativity.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
heteronormativity.relation: Jessica Miller shows Katniss coded masculine, since Collins built her from Theseus and Spartacus and her breadwinning, hunting, and defiance fit masculine norms, while Prim embodies everything Beauvoir says civilization 'produces' as feminine, and Panem itself proves oddly gender-neutral: women work the mines, Finnick is the sex symbol sold by Snow, and Coin is as ruthless as any man. She then reads Katniss's romance performance through Judith Butler: the kisses, caresses, and televised wedding gowns do not express a preexisting femininity but constitute one, down to Butler's radical claim that sex itself is a cultural norm, which reframes even the Games' reaping of one boy and one girl as a gendered ritual rather than a presocial biological fact. Cinna's burning bridal gown that transforms Katniss into the mockingjay makes the political payoff explicit: gender performed strategically becomes the rebellion's power, and the hunter-and-baker partnership offers an alternative to the dominant romance script.

heteronormativity.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
heteronormativity.title: Notes
heteronormativity.relation: Held uses the Wasteland as a Hobbesian state-of-nature reset to pry apart biological sex and socially constructed gender: Aunty Entity and Furiosa show that sex is not destiny — one is not born, but becomes, a woman, as Beauvoir says — while the apocalypse scrambles gendered conventions yet leaves reproductive biology untouched. Butler's sex/gender distinction frames how a real difference like gestation gets weaponized into Immortan Joe's breeder system: the biology is a fact, the enslavement a choice. Finally, the casually acknowledged bond between Wez and the Golden Youth looks 'homoerotic' only through the viewer's heteronormativity — in the Wasteland, orientation categories simply stop mattering.

heteronormativity.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
heteronormativity.title: Boys Interrupted: The Drama of Male Bonding in Some Kind of Monster
heteronormativity.relation: Judith Grant reads Some Kind of Monster through Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick's concept of homosociality: the Hetfield-Ulrich bond is the libidinal engine of the band, with Mustaine and Newsted as sibling rivals for James' attention, wives and children as intrusions that break the male-only bonding, and Lars' French-kissing of Kirk policing the homosocial/homosexual line within heteronormativity. The film's arc - James' exit to rehab, Lars' tirade against his control, and the firing of the feminized therapist Phil - is the interruption and rekindling of a homosocial bond that can no longer run on youthful rebellion now that the band has become 'The Man'.

heteronormativity.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
heteronormativity.title: When the Subject is Not the Butt Schmitts Gay Beer
heteronormativity.relation: Tallman asks why SNL may mock presidents (Chase's pratfalling Ford, Carvey's Bush) and Clintons but not unchosen groups, framing the question with the aesthetics debate among radical autonomism (Bell), radical moralism (traced to Plato and Tolstoy), and moderate moralism. Sketches from Samurai Futaba to Farley's Lunchlady Land show jokes can punch up, punch down, or elevate a low-status group. The Schmitts Gay beer sketch, she argues, ridicules not gay men but beer-ad conventions: swapping the usual female sex objects for men in speedos exposes the objectification and heteronormativity viewers had stopped noticing, so the butt is the advertising industry.

heteronormativity.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
heteronormativity.title: So Mother for That: Taylor Swift and Childless Mothering
heteronormativity.relation: Lucy Britt and Brian Britt trace the fan practice of calling childless Swift 'mother' back to the Black and queer ballroom house mothers of Paris Is Burning (Carmen Xtravaganza, Willi Ninja), whose original meaning - relational care and leadership in found families - was mostly lost when Swifties appropriated the term. Using Simone de Beauvoir on femininity, Judith Butler's culturally constructed body, and Audre Lorde on Black mothering as resistance, they argue Swift functions as a postmodern, queered mother whose revisiting of her 'eras' teaches fans to mother their own past selves. Yet her individualism ('You're on your own, kid') blocks the relational politics of care that Joan Tronto's caring democracy and Adriana Cavarero's maternal inclination demand.

heteronormativity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
heteronormativity.title: Notes
heteronormativity.relation: Hoffman and Kolmes use Aristotle's friendship as 'another self' and Kant's 'exchange of welfare' to value the pre-New 52 Superman-Wonder Woman friendship (Rucka's heart-to-hearts, Superman choosing to save Wonder Woman over Lois's father), then argue DC's 2011 reboot of the pair into a romance exemplifies Brake's amatonormativity and the heteronormative 'When Harry Met Sally' assumption that cross-gender closeness must be sexual. Diana's answer to Lois - 'We're just good friends' - becomes a refusal to rank friendship below romance. The erasure matters beyond comics: it denies role models for cross-gender friendship and stigmatizes bi and pansexual people as incapable of friendship at all.

heteronormativity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
heteronormativity.title: Notes
heteronormativity.relation: Cano Abadia imagines Wonder Woman and Themyscira's Amazons joining Monique Wittig's Guerrieres in a three-front war on patriarchy: the literal war Diana declares, a social revolution of lesbian, BDSM, and polyamorous relations lived outside the heterosexual contract, and a linguistic revolution that destroys the sex binary - 'elles' as the universal subject, no he and she. With Virginia Woolf's Society of Outsiders supplying experimental 'new ways of doing things' and Luce Irigaray's revaluation of feminine symbolism explaining the Amazons' feminaries and Hera-centered genealogy, Diana becomes the bridge between two generations of fighters whose post-patriarchal world 'is yet to come.'

heteronormativity.book: 214 - The Philosophy of Ang Lee
heteronormativity.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
heteronormativity.relation: Kang argues Lee's Taking Woodstock desexualizes and 'recloset[s]' Elliot Tiber's gay coming-out memoir, substituting a fluid 'queer' openness for Tiber's political gay identity and framing his homosexuality as an incidental, situationally-straight product of the festival (the woman-centered threesome, the chaste kiss with Paul). Drawing on Sedgwick, Butler and Foucault's history of sexuality, she critiques how the film neutralizes homophobia and omits the gay Buddhist mentor Georgette, whose teaching on karma, samsara and dukkha grounds Tiber's self-acceptance and unconditional love—reducing a gay everyman's struggle to one 'not-normal freak' among a hundred thousand.

heteronormativity.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
heteronormativity.title: Charlie Kaufman, Philosophy, and the Small Screen
heteronormativity.relation: Chambers reads Kaufman's TV sitcom Ned and Stacey through queer theory, arguing its marriage-of-convenience premise stages a critique of 'the normal.' Because Ned and Stacey only play at being husband and wife and never desire the romantic telos, the show troubles heteronormativity more than the openly gay Will & Grace, whose characters chase marriage and family. Chambers uses Butler's Lacanian notion of masquerade to claim there is no 'real' husband or wife beneath the role, only role-playing, and ties this to the philia (not eros) bond of the leads and to the masquerade running through Kaufman's films.

heteronormativity.book: 222 - The Philosophy of Horror
heteronormativity.title: Heteronormative horrors
heteronormativity.relation: Reading virgins and the vagina dentata as the dyad through which horror polices female sexuality, the chapter uses Irigaray's account of the virgin as prop to male subjectivity and Creed's femme castratrice to analyse Halloween's 'Final Girl', Teeth's toothed-vagina revenge on abstinence-only purity culture, Jennifer's Body and Haute Tension. It closes with Rich's 'compulsory heterosexuality' and Wittig's 'heterosexual contract' to argue horror naturalises heteronormativity by casting female sexuality as either contained (virgin) or monstrously open (vagina dentata).

purity-and-danger.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
purity-and-danger.title: Stable Bodies
purity-and-danger.relation: Heinricy argues the human/Cylon line is drawn on the body: following Mary Douglas, bodies function as cultural boundaries, so Cylons figure as contamination to be hunted (Boomer in the fleet) and marked as other by violence (Gina's torture), though Athena's loyal service and Tigh's exposure show the fear is socially constructed rather than natural. Cylon insides are known only through technology (Caprica Six's glowing spine, Athena's blood interface in 'Flight of the Phoenix'), and their bodies' stability — no scars, aging, or change — is paid for in unstable minds (Tigh killing Ellen, Boomer strangling Hera), whereas messy human bodies carry potential, hope, and change, as Apollo's weight fluctuation shows. Since we are all already cyborgs (vaccines, pills, GMOs), the Numbers are a further human-machine integration, and Hera and Nicky's blending is the ultimate 'contamination' and a new hope.

purity-and-danger.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
purity-and-danger.title: Shaman, Heal Thyself
purity-and-danger.relation: Culver reads Monk as a shamanic figure in Arnold van Gennep's and Victor Turner's sense: a liminal man, neither cop nor civilian, fixed in the transitional stage of mourning Trudy, who heals society's disorder from its margins as Holmes and Poirot did. Drawing on Mary Douglas's Purity and Danger (dirt as defilement and disorder), she interprets Monk's ritualized gestures and utterances, framing the scene with his hands, the rare solving-smile, 'he's the guy' and 'Here's what happened', as the ceremonial performance by which disorder is overcome. Episodes like 'Mr. Monk Takes His Medicine' and 'Mr. Monk Joins a Cult' then show the shaman's bind: whenever Monk attains purity or happiness he loses his sacred gift, so he must refuse to heal himself and remain 'a blessing and a curse'.

purity-and-danger.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
purity-and-danger.title: Stable Bodies
purity-and-danger.relation: Heinricy argues the one clear human-Cylon difference is the body, analyzed through Mary Douglas's account of bodies as culturally invented boundaries: Cylons are feared as 'contamination' of the fleet (Boomer's body, segregated like Jim Crow bodies), and Gina Six's torture and rape mark her body as out-of-place other even as her human-looking blood and wounds undermine the boundary. She contrasts messy, changing human bodies (Apollo's weight fluctuation, aging, scars as records of experience) with stable, disposable Cylon bodies that never mark learning, arguing human change yields potential and hope while Cylon bodily stability may cost mental stability (Tigh killing Ellen, Boomer attacking Hera). Cyborg theory then collapses the boundary (we are all cyborgs via vaccines and prosthetics, Cylons merely more integrated, the Hybrid a warning of over-integration), leaving Hera and Nicky as the 'ultimate contamination' that blends the two.

purity-and-danger.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
purity-and-danger.title: 23. Punk and Disgust
purity-and-danger.relation: Sara Bergstresser reads punk's shocking bodily transgressions - COUM Transmissions' Prostitution exhibit, GG Allin's stage defecation, Iggy Pop's self-mutilation, L7's thrown tampon - through Mary Douglas's Purity and Danger, Martha Nussbaum's Hiding from Humanity, and Julia Kristeva's Powers of Horror. Disgust polices social boundaries: Nussbaum shows how disgust-based obscenity law historically targets minorities, while Kristeva's abject (corpse, menstrual blood, excrement) marks the collapse of self/other boundaries that punk performers deliberately cross, with punk musicians added to Kristeva's list of those who dare approach the abject. The chapter asks whether the disgusting can be art, closing with Eco's claim that ugliness is passion against beauty's detachment, and with feminist performers like Jack Off Jill using blood and 'ugliness' as protest against the policing of female bodies.

family-resemblance.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
family-resemblance.title: What Was on Wittgenstein’s iPod
family-resemblance.relation: Rehn argues there is no essential definition of the iPod: Shuffle, Nano, Classic, and Touch share only overlapping, criss-crossing similarities, exactly as Wittgenstein's family resemblance handles 'sport' (water polo vs. boxing) and 'game.' Even Cover Flow -- a physically impossible floating cascade of albums -- feels instantly familiar, showing familiarity is something users construct from hints rather than perceive, and syncing, playlists, and the Music Quiz game endlessly re-manufacture it (the iPod as the new McDonald's golden arches abroad). Flipping the relation via Actor-Network Theory, he notes the iPod tracks play counts, pushes 'Listeners Also Bought,' and trains our flicking gestures, so that perhaps the iPod becomes familiar with us; the Microsoft Zune figures as the abject, zombie-like copy whose perverse familiarity reveals a politics of recognition, and the closing game of imagining Wittgenstein's playlist endorses natural language's many language games over exact definitions.

family-resemblance.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
family-resemblance.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
family-resemblance.relation: Carl Ehrett and Sarah Worth ask whether D&D is really a game (imagining Bill and Ted challenging Death to a campaign) and model the search for a definition of 'game' on Socrates dismantling Euthyphro's attempted definitions of piety, only for Wittgenstein's family resemblance to dissolve the project. On that view D&D still counts as a game despite lacking winning and losing, because its rule-governedness survives 'rule 0' license to bend rules whenever bending them crafts a better story. To explain why players who know the world is not real are nonetheless engrossed, they present Radford's paradox of fiction and adopt Walton's make-believe theory: the miniature on the table is a prop prescribing the imagining of an owlbear, so genuine quasi-emotions respond to truths in the fiction, making D&D an unusually gripping interactive story.

family-resemblance.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
family-resemblance.title: Justified and Philosophy
family-resemblance.relation: The chapter argues Boyd Crowder personifies coolness - composure, wily cleverness, unconventionality, intelligence, likability - as shown in the 'Cottonmouth' payroll-robbery scene where he turns his flip phone into a room bug, overhears Kyle planning to blow him up in the mine, and lets the plotters kill themselves. Jon Cotton borrows Wittgenstein's family-resemblance model to define coolness as an indefinable cluster of traits (with Dewey Crowe as the agreed uncool case), and reaches back to Socrates' defining of ethical virtues and the Republic's just, well-ordered soul to argue that coolness is a genuine ethical virtue - the excellence of a properly functioning person - in a scientific, post-religious ethics.

family-resemblance.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
family-resemblance.title: 13. Did Jimi Play Rock
family-resemblance.relation: Flips Joel Rudinow's 'Can White People Sing the Blues?' to ask whether a very black musician can play a genre that by the late sixties had become white property. With Wittgenstein's family resemblance — musical kinds lack necessary and sufficient conditions — it traces rock's migration from Chuck Berry and the Sanctified churches to the Stones and Beatles, diagnosing the 'Jimi problem': his blackness rendered his rock inauthentic (Christgau's 'psychedelic Uncle Tom,' radio bans) at the same time as his rock rendered him inauthentically black. The chapter endorses Hendrix's own refusal of labels — 'You don't need labels, man' — as a caution against unreflective categorization.

family-resemblance.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
family-resemblance.title: Keeping It in the Family
family-resemblance.relation: Jason Southworth deploys counterexamples, from Golden Age Batman shooting the vampire Monk with silver bullets, through Jean-Paul Valley and Dick Grayson serving as Batman during Knightfall and Prodigal, to the Frankenstein twist of Castle of the Bat and the criminal Batman of Earth-A, to show that nothing (not being Bruce Wayne, not never killing, not murdered parents) is necessary or sufficient for being Batman. Turning to Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations, he applies family resemblance and the game examples: 'Batman' works like 'game,' identified through overlapping similarities rather than a fixed definition. Retconned Robins and disappearing Batarangs show language works without fixed meanings, which he warns undermines using Batman as a determinate moral exemplar.

family-resemblance.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
family-resemblance.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
family-resemblance.relation: Søren Frimodt-Møller argues that heavy metal cannot be defined by necessary and sufficient conditions, down-tuning, distortion, growls, and double-kick each fail as criteria, and that genres instead work like Wittgenstein's family-resemblance concepts, learned by actual cases the way words are learned in language games. The family of metal begins with Black Sabbath as prototype: he traces doom to "Black Sabbath" and "War Pigs", thrash to "Paranoid" and "Symptom of the Universe" (compare "Master of Puppets"), progressive and power metal to the Dio-era records that influenced Iron Maiden, and grunge to Soundgarden and Alice in Chains, while standards of heaviness shift historically so that former metal like stoner rock now counts as plain rock.

family-resemblance.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
family-resemblance.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
family-resemblance.relation: Ehrett and Worth ask whether D&D is really a game and why we invest so much in it. Against the Socratic model (the Euthyphro dialogue's search for a common thread defining piety, here applied to 'game'), they deploy Wittgenstein's family-resemblance account from the Philosophical Investigations, concluding D&D lacks clear winning and losing but is rule-governed, with the twist that rule-breaking is legitimate exactly when it serves the game's primary purpose of group storytelling. They then take up the paradox of fiction: since players know the world is not real, Radford's puzzle arises, and Kendall Walton's make-believe theory of props and fictional truths supplies their answer, making D&D an especially gripping fiction because players are participants rather than observers.

family-resemblance.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
family-resemblance.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
family-resemblance.relation: Asking whether the Millennium Trilogy is popular fiction or literature, the chapter proposes Wittgenstein's family resemblances instead of an essence: Larsson's books are devoured like genre series, yet they tackle the 'moral seriousness'—violence against women, corruption, journalistic ethics—that Sartre called committed literature, so the whodunit becomes the exposé. Nussbaum's account of reading as moral perception, not mere grasp of facts, is applied to Lisbeth's 'Bitch' verdict on Harriet Vanger—should we see a culpable sister or a victim?—and the paradox of fiction explains why we feel real pity and fear for characters we know are invented, down to the detective plot's 'consolatory fiction' that truth can be found. The verdict: socially conscious popular fiction whose high/low distinction (Arnold versus Meisel's level field) matters less than the words-as-force-for-justice theme summed up in 'an insufferable do-gooder who thought he could change everything with a book.'

family-resemblance.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
family-resemblance.title: 1. The Essence of Punk
family-resemblance.relation: Kwiatek tests essentialist definitions of punk one by one - political lyrics (Black Flag's 'Six Pack' fails it), DIY underground status (The Clash were on majors), rebellion (distinguishing local from global rebellion via Green Day's 'selling out' and The Misfits' horror-movie songs), and the existentialist ideal of authenticity - and finds counterexamples to each. Following Wittgenstein on games in the Philosophical Investigations, he argues punk is a family-resemblance concept with no essence, so 'is it punk?' debates are playful boundary-drawing rather than discovery, and punk's lack of essence works as an anti-gatekeeping device that shifts the burden of justification onto those who would exclude.

family-resemblance.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
family-resemblance.title: 17. Nazi Punks Fuck Off!
family-resemblance.relation: Falcioni argues punk has a unique 'Nazi problem' - hatecore was the white-power movement's chief recruiting tool, as Christian Picciolini's path into the Hammer Skin Nation and even Dylann Roof's radicalization show - and that trying to fix punk's essence is both anti-punk and philosophically hopeless. Enlisting Wittgenstein as 'punk philosopher' (he told Russell his work was rubbish and pulled a poker on Popper), the chapter applies meaning-as-use and family resemblance to show neo-Nazi punk stands inside punk's web of overlapping features, so the way to get Nazi punks to fuck off is not violence but bridge-building through punk's shared supply of identity, community, and purpose.

stoic-indifferents.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
stoic-indifferents.title: “All Good Things Must Come to an End”
stoic-indifferents.relation: Thorsrud casts Spock and Data's exchange in 'Unification, Part II' — Spock dispassionate by choice, Data longing for emotion — as a replay of the ancient debate between Stoics and Peripatetics over whether to eliminate or moderate the passions. The Aristotelian side is built from Data's emotion-chip rage while killing a Borg ('Descent'), his unfelt breakup with Jenna ('In Theory'), and Riker's defense of trust after Ishara's betrayal ('Legacy'): emotions are judgments with pleasure or pain, there is a right amount to feel, and invulnerability costs the 'emotional bonds that make us who we are.' The Stoic reply uses Epictetus's distinction between involuntary impressions and assent (Picard's fear on the Borg ship vs. the holodeck), Cicero's refusal to 'moderate' what is simply a fault, and Seneca on anger, exemplified by Spock's 'quite logical relief' in 'Amok Time', his calculated desperation in 'The Galileo Seven', and his saving the bigot Stiles in 'Balance of Terror' — leaving the Peripatetic conclusion that fortune's goods are not mere indifferents and we may rightly 'smile with so little provocation.'

stoic-indifferents.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
stoic-indifferents.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
stoic-indifferents.relation: Re-examining 'The Enchiridion!' trial by trial - the gnome illusions, the ogre whose dollar Finn steals and then returns, the dark mage's brain world, the wallop given the Key-per in devil pajamas - the chapter argues Finn wins the hero's handbook without being righteous: he is brave, tender and ingenious, but gullible, hasty and violent, slaying whatever he is told is evil and running from the gnome test. Epictetus's Stoic Enchiridion supplies the standard the show's book lacks: only virtue matters, wealth, fame and comfort are indifferents, and a real handbook teaches how to lose, age and admit mistakes, not just how to win, which is exactly what Billy's quit-heroism shows Ooo's greatest hero never learned. Because bravery without good judgment could as easily serve a Nazi, a terrorist or the Lich, Finn's lack of practical wisdom means the 'most righteous hero' in Ooo is an impetuous boy - proof of how morally broken the Land of Ooo is.

stoic-indifferents.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
stoic-indifferents.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
stoic-indifferents.relation: Mills presents Bates - lame leg, repeated prison spells, the public fall when O'Brien kicks his cane - as an Epictetan Stoic who 'manages' misfortune by confining his concern to what he controls, echoing the Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves.' The chapter explains the dichotomy of control and preferred indifferents through Thomas's enslaved pursuit of the valet post, O'Brien's soap-on-the-floor scheme, Mary's panicked engagement to Richard Carlisle, and Mrs. Hughes's proportioning of her cancer scare, and treats death as the great rejected indifferent via Pamuk, Sybil, and Matthew. It closes with Hierocles' concentric circles: the household's best moments (Sybil helping Gwen, the staff rallying to free Bates) collapse upstairs and downstairs into one family, while Thomas's closed inner circle marks his failure of Stoic virtue.

stoic-indifferents.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
stoic-indifferents.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
stoic-indifferents.relation: Mills reads Mr. Bates, the lame, twice-imprisoned, uncomplaining valet, as Downton's Epictetus, using him and the household to teach the Stoic dichotomy of control: only our judgments, desires, and actions are up to us, while jobs, reputations, and inheritances (Thomas's coveted valet post, Mary's scandal, Molesley's flower cup) are 'preferred indifferents' to be pursued without enslavement. Death figures as the great rejected indifferent, handled through Pamuk's demise and Mrs. Hughes's calm 'One day, I will die' upon finding a lump, as well as the grief of Isobel and Mary over Matthew. The closing section turns to Hierocles's concentric circles, with Sybil helping Gwen and Carson comforting Mary as drawing outsiders into the inner circle, a Stoic cosmopolitanism that Thomas, who sees the Crawleys as mere employers, fails entirely. The Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves' serves as the chapter's Stoic motto.

stoic-indifferents.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
stoic-indifferents.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
stoic-indifferents.relation: Abigail Myers runs Stoic doctrine against Katniss's biography: Zeno's thesis that only moral goodness is good (with Plutarch Heavensbee's renunciation of Capitol privilege as indifference to wealth and status), Seneca's 'On the Shortness of Life' against deferring living, Epictetus's dichotomy of control including the uncomfortable advice to kiss wife and child as mortals, and Marcus Aurelius's practical Meditations as the gentler 'Stoic for beginners' who would be president of Panem. Katniss comes out Stoic in her frugality, her mortality-shadowed appreciation of small joys, and her firm moral code, but decidedly un-Stoic in her fierce attachments to Rue, Peeta, and Prim. Yet her final choice of Peeta over Gale is itself Stoic, Myers argues: she forgives what Peeta's hijacking made him do since it was never in his control, refuses a noble friendship that would endorse Gale and Coin's slaughter of innocents, and chooses in accordance with nature and reason so as to survive as herself with her values intact.

stoic-indifferents.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
stoic-indifferents.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
stoic-indifferents.relation: Barkman reads the trilogy's Roman texture — panem et circenses, gladiatorial Games, tyrants named Coriolanus and Caesar — through the Stoic Seneca, who lived under Nero just as Katniss lives under Snow. Seneca's distinction between the good (virtue alone), the merely preferable (wealth, fame, power), and the bad (vice) explains the Capitol: Snow and Coin traded virtue for preferables and so became vicious, while the citizens' binge-and-purge luxury mirrors the Roman decadence Seneca condemned. The Hunger Games are the gladiatorial 'pure murder' that corrupts emperors, crowds, and tributes alike, and the districts are slaves whose liberation — like Katniss declaring 'I'm done killing their slaves' — is Seneca's freedom from slavery to fear and vice. Katniss and Peeta's self-sacrificial love and refusal to be changed exemplify the Stoic virtue the Capitol cannot take away.

stoic-indifferents.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
stoic-indifferents.title: Notes
stoic-indifferents.relation: Hummel maps the Jedi Order onto Epictetus's Stoicism: philosophy as a way of life, virtue through wisdom, the dichotomy of control ('some things are up to us'), and treating outcomes like flying or other people's fates as preferred indifferents within the will of the Force. Anakin falls because he misconceives power as the ability to do amazing things - stopping people from dying - instead of mastery of his own judgments, and he refuses Stoic indifference toward Shmi and Padme. The chapter also indicts the Jedi's own un-Stoic lapses: mind tricks on Watto, entering the Clone Wars, and Mace Windu's attempt to execute a subdued Sidious.

eugenics.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
eugenics.title: “Sometimes You Just Have to Bow to the Absurd”
eugenics.relation: Eberl weighs genetic enhancement and cloning through Trek's test cases: Julian Bashir's parents' enhancement leaves him feeling 'a fraud' ('You used to be my father. Now, you're my architect'), the Moab IV 'Masterpiece Society' breeds out 'the unknown, self-discovery, things that make life worth living', and the Jem'Hadar show desire itself engineered for control. He argues the right to an open future constrains designing children (B'Elanna's wish to de-Klingonize her baby, Worf pressuring Alexander), defends genetic treatment while rejecting genetic determinism, and uses Kass and Rovane with Picard and Shinzon, the Mariposa clones, and Trip's clone Sim to show clones are numerically distinct persons. Against Malik's Augments quoting Nietzsche — 'mankind is something to be surpassed' — the chapter argues the Übermensch demands self-mastery through philosophy, not eugenic engineering, tracing eugenics from Plato's Guardian breeding scheme through Buck v. Bell to modern prenatal selection.

eugenics.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
eugenics.title: Chapter 12 - Grow, My Dears, the Eugenicist Said
eugenics.relation: Opens the eugenics part with Flow My Tears' Jason Taverner — a beautiful, charismatic, fast-healing 'six' from an abandoned government breeding program, 'not a Nexus-Six, but not unlike one either.' Defining eugenics through the dog-and-wolf contrast in selective breeding, it notes that the 'eu' (good) in eugenics smuggles in an ethical judgment, and poses the part's driving question: who decides what counts as a 'good' or 'bad' trait, and by what right?

eugenics.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
eugenics.title: 8. Night of the Living Disabled
eugenics.relation: Reads Constance's treatment of Addy and Beau Langdon through the eugenic roots of the horror genre (Angela Smith's Hideous Progeny, The Black Stork, the Production Code): outward bodily difference assumed to prove inner defect, and the disabled treated as better off dead - Addy finding peace only as 'a pretty girl at last' after death, Beau suffocated in the attic. Against the medical model the chapter defends Alison Kafer's political-relational model and crip futurity (Tate's 'He only suffered because of you'), arguing that ableism, not disability itself, makes their lives unlivable and that imagining disabled futures differently is a matter of survival.

eugenics.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
eugenics.title: They Took My Choice, So I Took Yours
eugenics.relation: Tongue argues Yennefer's 'they took my choice' grievance is best understood through reproductive justice: her sterilization by the enchanter, strapped down and told the price only at the last moment, mirrors real coerced sterilizations of disabled, Roma, and Indigenous women, so her 'choice' was coerced by ableist and anti-elven oppression. She contrasts Geralt, whose witcher infertility is unstigmatized and whose adoptive fatherhood of Ciri bucks gendered caregiver stereotypes ('biology is not destiny, adoption is'), with Yennefer's portrayal, which slides into the patriarchal 'infertile monster' trope shared by Daenerys Tragaryen and Wanda Maximoff. The chapter concludes the show handles infertility and nonbiological family admirably but still reinforces maternal-sacrifice and cure-the-disability stereotypes.

eugenics.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
eugenics.title: V - MAD GENETICS THE SINISTER SIDE OF BIOLOGICAL MASTERY
eugenics.relation: Burnett traces Nathaniel Essex's transformation into Mister Sinister to explore the ethics of genetic mastery. Set in Darwin's 1859 London, where Essex, grieving a child, debates taking control of evolution with Darwin himself, the chapter uses Paley's natural theology and Tennyson's crisis of natural evil to frame Sinister's rejection of moral restraint, and Herbert Spencer's evolutionary ethics to argue that cooperation, not 'dog eat dog,' is what fitness actually favors. Sinister's breeding of the Summers bloodline and Bolivar Trask's Sentinels embody Galton's eugenics, and Sinister's careers as 'Dr. Windsor' and 'Dr. Milbury' behind Weapon X and the Black Womb project mirror real cases like the Tuskegee study, where researchers lost sight of the moral whole.

eugenics.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
eugenics.title: XIII - THE MUTANT CURE OR SOCIAL CHANGE DEBATING DISABILITY
eugenics.relation: Ilea uses The Last Stand's mutant cure to stage the debate over disability. Worthington's 'affliction... a disease' speech is the medical model; Storm's 'there's nothing to cure' is the social model, on which society, not the body, disables, as with Deaf culture and communities without eyeglasses. Rogue, who cannot touch anyone, and Jean, whose power she cannot control, show some mutations genuinely impair, so the chapter weighs beneficence, nonmaleficence, and utility across Angel's aborted cure, cochlear implants, prenatal Down syndrome screening, and the history of eugenics from Nazi euthanasia to American sterilization laws, concluding the cure can be both liberation and weapon.

a-series-time.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
a-series-time.title: Tomorrow Is Yesterday
a-series-time.relation: Uses the Bajoran Prophets, who experience no linear time ('What is this... time?'), to frame a tour of time's metaphysics: Newton's absolute container versus Leibniz's relationism (the incoherence of a 'temporal vacuum'), Augustine's mind-dependent time (illustrated by 'The Inner Light' and O'Brien's implanted prison years in 'Hard Time'), and McTaggart's argument that neither the A-series nor the B-series can account for change, illustrated by Tasha Yar's death in 'Skin of Evil' and Kirk's Liar-paradox victories over Nomad and Norman. The chapter defends the A-series via tense, then weighs presentism — which would make 'Tomorrow Is Yesterday' and 'Trials and Tribble-ations' impossible — against eternalism, whose fatalism Data embraces when his severed head turns up in 'Time's Arrow' ('It has occurred. It will occur.'), and which finally makes sense of prophets who see the future in 'Destiny.'

a-series-time.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
a-series-time.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
a-series-time.relation: Ralph Shain argues forward and backward time travel are categorically different: relativistic time dilation is conceptually harmless (in Boulle's novel Merou could not return to Soror for a thousand years), but Escape from the Planet of the Apes' backward jump is conceptually impossible because it treats the open future as fixed like the past - Hasslein's plan to kill baby Milo is the Grandfather Paradox, checked against presentist, possibilist, and eternalist ontologies of time. The real philosophical engine is Aristotle's sea-battle argument from the law of excluded middle: since Cornelius's story of the takeover is past for the apes and future for 1973 humans, the film's causal loop (Milo saved at the circus) enacts the fatalist conclusion that the ape takeover will necessarily occur. Hasslein's freeway image of time defeats itself - switching lanes means landing in the past of a different, parallel universe, so the apes' jump would be travel between worlds, not times.

a-series-time.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
a-series-time.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
a-series-time.relation: Through a hot-tub dialogue in Prismo's Time Room, the chapter walks Jake through the main theories of time: McTaggart's A-theory versus B-theory, plus presentism, the growing block, eternalism and four-dimensionalism, illustrated with the mirror-Finn dream, Farmworld Finn, Jake's unchangeable croak dream, and the Ancient Psychic Tandem War Elephant as a thing stretched across past, present and future selves. Booko's description of the multiverse becomes a springboard for David Lewis's possible-worlds realism and Everett's many-worlds reading of Prismo's 'alternate wish worlds'. Finally, quotes from McTaggart and Bergson delivered as Finn's Glasses of Nerdicon rant argue that time resists spatial and scientific analysis and must be lived, which the authors tie to relativity, black-hole cosmology and Prismo's Time Room as the one dimension outside time.

a-series-time.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
a-series-time.title: 6. Nebula’s Time Travel Paradox
a-series-time.relation: Charlene Esby defends Endgame against the charge that Nebula killing her past self is a plot hole. She reconstructs the grandfather paradox from Nathaniel Schachner's 'Ancestral Voices,' explains how conceiving time as a fourth dimension makes travel conceivable, and deploys Aristotle's Physics (time as the number of change and rest) and the De Interpretatione sea-battle problem, where the past is necessary but the future contingent on present choices, to argue the Avengers' victory depends on free choices made now, which is why the Ancient One releases the Time Stone only on Banner's promise. The resolution is Hulk's subjective-timeline point: once traveled to, the past becomes the traveler's present, so present Nebula kills past Nebula in a shared present rather than negating her own future, just as Thanos from the past arrives alive in a present where he already died.

a-series-time.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
a-series-time.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
a-series-time.relation: Kind uses John Stewart's Justice League arc, thrown into the future by Chronos, meeting his son Warhawk, and hiding it from Hawkgirl while dating Vixen, to stage fatalism: Pike and Taylor's arguments that a foreknown future, whether God's or a time traveler's, cannot be otherwise. Time travel itself forces a choice between presentism and eternalism, since Warhawk must 'exist now, already, in the future' for GL and Batman to visit him, and Smart's tenseless four-dimensionalism, with GL a series of timeslices and 'now' as subjective as 'here,' dissolves the fatalist worry by banishing tensed facts. The chapter lands on GL's battlefield advice to his son: 'Plant your feet,' owning a fate you cannot escape.

a-series-time.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
a-series-time.title: NOTES
a-series-time.relation: Davies defends Lost's convoluted plotting using Aristotle's Poetics, arguing the show works as a tragicomic epic that keeps closure and relevance even with Juliet's pre-crash storyline, genre mixing (Hurley's golf course beside Sayid's captivity), and shifting characters like Ben. He then uses the 'We have to go back' flash-forward to lay out McTaggart's two conceptions of time, eternalism versus presentism, and argues the flash-forward pushes viewers toward fatalism about Jack's already-fixed meeting with Kate near LAX. Finally he contends the past cannot be changed - Hurley in 2007 cannot undo his 1977 stay in the Dharma Initiative, since contradictions would entail everything - so viewers enjoy the time-travel plot by 'shielding' its mutually contradictory time lines.

a-series-time.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
a-series-time.title: The End
a-series-time.relation: Berghofer uses the Rebels episode 'A World Between Worlds' to ask whether Ezra changed the past when he pulled Ahsoka out of her duel with Vader, arguing that past-changing time travel breeds contradiction: the grandfather paradox looms over his attempt to save Kanan ('if he is taken out of this moment, you all die'), and on the Lewis-style consistent model Ezra caused but never changed the past. He surveys presentism, eternalism, and the growing block to locate Star Wars' metaphysics of time — Ezra's travel rules out presentism, and the Mortis god's 'the future, by its nature, can be changed' fits a growing block with an open future. Anakin's tragedy of acting to prevent prophesied events and thereby causing them frames the whole analysis.

a-series-time.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
a-series-time.title: Is Taylor Swift's Music Timeless? A Metaphysical Proof
a-series-time.relation: Patrick Dawson offers a tongue-in-cheek 'metaphysical proof' that Swift's music is timeless in three senses. Her time-words (midnight, August, 'Back to December,' 'Christmas Tree Farm') name moods rather than objective locations, echoing Kant's view that time is a projection of the mind rather than an external structure; her lyric-world is fated and changeless ('Karma,' 'Mastermind,' 'the 1'), aligning her with determinist and necessitarian views of a closed future; and songs like 'All Too Well' ('Time won't fly, it's like I'm paralyzed by it') reject the passage of time McTaggart declared unreal, letting Swift jump freely between moments in a 'dynamic timelessness.'

a-series-time.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
a-series-time.title: NOTES
a-series-time.relation: Miller reconciles Kyle's 'no fate but what we make' with Sarah's 'you're dead already': eternalism (defended by the special-relativity argument Hilary Putnam made famous) makes 2029 as real as 1994, so Judgment Day cannot be changed, and the grandfather paradox - using Caesar's unalterable assassination as the model - blocks the T-101 from preventing its own existence. She then tests growing-block, presentist, meta-time, and branching-timeline (McCall-style) models against T2 and T3, asking whether any lets Sarah's attack on Cyberdyne legitimately delay Judgment Day. The conclusion works under every model: even on a fixed four-dimensional block, Judgment Day happens because of what humans do, not independently of them, so fixed fate and making our own future turn out to be compatible.

a-series-time.title: The Daleks Can Stop the Pyramids from Being Built!
a-series-time.relation: Philip Goff asks whether Daleks could travel back and stop the pyramids being built, arguing the answer turns on one's theory of time. He shows presentism forbids travel to a non-existent past and eternalism permits travel but forbids changing a static block, then defends the growing-block theory (past and present real, future not) as a middle way that lets time travelers genuinely alter history. He works out how a new pyramid-less history advances at the same rate as the present, never overwriting it, and distinguishes concrete from abstract past existence to keep historical records true.

a-series-time.title: What Happens to the Present When It Becomes the Past
a-series-time.relation: Daniels asks whether the airline passengers in The Langoliers are truly time travelers and what theory of time their dead, tasteless past implies. Using David Lewis's distinction between 'personal time' and 'external time,' he shows the discrepancy between the characters' day-long journey and the few hours that elapse in the present qualifies them as genuine time travelers despite the deserted world. He then rules out presentism (incompatible with time travel via the 'nowhere problem') and eternalism (which denies any privileged present), arguing the vibrant, 'oomph'-laden moving now the characters race to rejoin fits the moving spotlight theory, while the langoliers merely consume the world's contents, not spacetime itself.

a-series-time.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
a-series-time.title: 7. Doctor Who as Philosophy Four-Dimensionalism and Time Travel
a-series-time.relation: Decker asks what the universe must be like if Doctor Who's time travel were real, using David Lewis's distinction between personal and external time and the TARDIS as a Wellsian (not Thornian) time machine traversing a 'hypertime' vortex. After surveying the arrows of time and paradoxes like the bootstrap paradox ('Day of the Daleks') and the grandfather paradox (imagined via Tegan's grandfather), and rejecting Deutsch-Lockwood's Many-Worlds and growing-block solutions, he argues the Whoniverse fits 'Four-Dimensional Realism'/eternalism, quoting the Twelfth Doctor that time's passage is an illusion of 'still pictures.' He then confronts 4DR's threat to free will and moral responsibility, finding compatibilism and 'fixed points' inadequate given eternalism's succession-not-production of events.

a-series-time.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
a-series-time.title: 88. Watchmen as Philosophy Illustrating Time and Free Will
a-series-time.relation: Goldberg and Gavaler argue that Moore and Gibbons's Watchmen operationalizes eternalism (McTaggart's B-series) both through its rigid 3x3 grid and mirror-symmetric layouts and through Doctor Manhattan, who narrates all moments as simultaneously present ('nothing ever ends'). Because eternalism means no one could have done otherwise, libertarian free will is ruled out, and the chapter argues the operative view is compatibilism rather than determinism, using Frankfurt's rejection of the principle of alternative possibilities and Dennett's Luther example to read Doctor Manhattan's hesitant killing of Rorschach as free action he could not have done otherwise.

a-series-time.book: 310 - The Real Meaning of Doctor Who
a-series-time.title: 7. Knowledge, Space, and Time
a-series-time.relation: The chapter uses the TARDIS to defend a 'block universe' theory of spacetime over Presentism (since the Doctor visits past and future), then turns to epistemology, distinguishing belief from knowledge and 'belief in' the Doctor from 'belief that' he exists. It re-stages Gettier's justified-true-belief counterexample as picking the Doctor's next companion by a blue jean jacket, surveys Descartes's Cogito foundationalism, Hume's induction, and Reid's direct perception, and endorses Alston's reliabilist two-level foundationalism plus Klein's infinitism. It argues the Doctor's benefit-of-the-doubt toward non-rational creatures fits a reliabilist 'lower level' of knowledge and an imaginative, engaged, virtuous (Zagzebski) search for truth.

liar-paradox.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
liar-paradox.title: “Logic Is the Beginning of Wisdom . . . Not the End”
liar-paradox.relation: Treats Kirk's computer-killing arguments as logic lessons: his valid syllogism forces Nomad to sterilize itself in 'The Changeling,' while the M-5's trial in 'The Ultimate Computer' models inductive hypothesis testing. The Liar paradox ('Everything Harry tells you is a lie' / 'I am lying') crashes Norman in 'I, Mudd' and, via Tarski's T-sentences and the explosion problem, reveals the concept of truth as inconsistent, with three-valued logic offered as a fix that only relocates the paradox. Gödel's incompleteness theorem then grounds the Lucas-Penrose claim that minds outstrip computer programs like Landru — which Putnam's consistency objection rebuts — leaving Searle's point that computers manipulate symbols without understanding them as the residue of Surak's Vulcan logic being the beginning of wisdom, not the end.

liar-paradox.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
liar-paradox.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
liar-paradox.relation: Vaclavik follows Lyra's career as liar and trickster, from the Silvertongue performance that goads Iofur Raknison into fighting Iorek Byrnison, up to the reversal in the Land of the Dead where the harpy screams 'Liar!' and only true stories can feed the ghosts. She frames Lyra's boast that she is the best liar there ever was yet is not lying as a version of the Liar Paradox, then dissolves the puzzle by showing that lies continue after the katabasis (Will's comforting fib, Mrs. Coulter's noble treachery with Metatron) just as truth-telling appeared before it. Truth triumphs in the underworld not for its own sake but because it suits the audience: the dead need the world they have lost, so storytelling, truthful or invented, is judged by what it does for its listeners.

liar-paradox.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
liar-paradox.title: The Logic of Expectation: Family Guy and the Non Sequitur
liar-paradox.relation: Argues that Family Guy's non sequiturs only seem random because they reverse specific expectations, so the show has a 'logic of expectation' even where it flouts inference: the Supreme Court fraternity hazing in 'Let's Go to the Hop,' Stewie's aristocratic-baby role reversal, Death hiding beer on his breath in 'Wasted Talent,' the Kool-Aid Man's sheepish exit in 'Death Has a Shadow,' and cutaways that run on shared pop-culture associations like Peter's 'no whammy' chant. The chapter deploys Kierkegaard's claim that wherever there is contradiction the comical is present, Schopenhauer's analysis of the ludicrous, Wittgenstein's joke-book remark, and Russell's ideal of disambiguating ambiguous sentences (Peter's 'I can also vomit' reply to Lois). It closes metaphysically: against Spinoza's necessity and Hume's 'one damn thing after another,' Quahog is not William James's 'mere withness' world because the gags depend on an orderly baseline, which Peter himself demonstrates by wearing a cardboard TV frame in 'I Never Met the Dead Man'.

liar-paradox.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
liar-paradox.title: Notes
liar-paradox.relation: Cook and Kellen formalize two rules of the golden lasso (the bound must answer, and must say what they believe true) and derive the Paradox of the Golden Lasso - 'Will your answer to this question be no?' - as a Liar Paradox variant, complete with a Revenge version that survives allowing 'maybe' as an answer. Bizarra's opposite-speaking lasso generates knights-and-knaves puzzles in the Smullyan style, a Wonder Woman/Bizarra/Harley Quinn variant of Boolos's Hardest Logic Puzzle Ever, and solutions exploiting what the bound believe rather than say. They end by using Bizarro #1 snapping the lasso and the Queen of Fables' huntsman doing the same to illustrate objective truth and the philosophy of fiction - what is fictionally true of characters who do not literally exist.

frankl-meaning.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
frankl-meaning.title: Why I Can Play Zelda for Four Hours Straight
frankl-meaning.relation: Fellela reads Link's endless drudgery (slashing grass for rupees, collecting bottles, leaving the final Ganon fight at a 'permanent pause') through existentialism: Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' is dramatized in Ocarina of Time's opening, where Link must acquire sword, fairy, and skills to make himself the hero, and Nietzsche's 'God is dead' call to become gods is answered by Link restoring meaning to a hostile Hyrule. Camus' Sisyphus figures the repetitive world-saving quest as an absurd hero's owned task, and Frankl's logotherapy (meaning as the tension between what one is and what one should become) explains why humiliating menial tasks, in camp or in laundromats or in Zelda, become bearable and even meaningful. Link's fixed options even illustrate Frankl's point that freedom is the stance we take toward conditions, not freedom from them.

frankl-meaning.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
frankl-meaning.title: Futurama and Philosophy
frankl-meaning.relation: Salazar takes Professor Farnsworth's cry that the crew's age regression in 'Teenage Mutant Leela's Hurdles' will end in 'a fate worse than death: pre-life! Then death' as a test of whether death is bad. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' says death cannot be experienced, so the deprivation account of Nagel's 'Death' is needed to explain how death is bad for the one deprived of a valuable future - a dispute staged by Bender's suicide-booth despair in 'Space Pilot 3000' after learning his bending built the booths. The chapter then argues losing one's identity and values can be worse than death (Bender's and Fry's flight from career-chip assignments, the Professor's love of being 161, Leela's frustrated teen redo), closing with Frankl's Man's Search for Meaning and Leela's sacrifice of her regained youth: inner integrity, not erasing the past, makes life worth living.

frankl-meaning.title: 15. Happy in Oceania
frankl-meaning.relation: Ćirić and Ćurko ask what philosophy could have done for Winston, imagining a counterfactual Oceania where he reads Walpole's line that the world is 'a comedy to those that think, a tragedy to those that feel' and learns from Julia that another worldview is possible. They present philosophy as therapy: Kant's notion of worldview (Weltanschauung), Epicurean ataraxia, the Buddhist four noble truths, Frankl's logotherapy, and Stoic premeditation of the worst as resources for reworking the beliefs that made Winston live in fear. The Party's true target, they argue, is critical thinking — from Dewey's ideal of education as learning to think to Frankfurt's On Bullshit — and Kant's Enlightenment motto 'have the courage to use your own understanding' is the weapon that could still defeat Ingsoc.

frankl-meaning.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
frankl-meaning.title: Why I Can Play Zelda for Four Hours Straight
frankl-meaning.relation: Toni Fellela gives an existentialist reading of Zelda, confessing she leaves Ocarina of Time and Twilight Princess permanently paused before the final Ganon fight because the meaning lies in the process of becoming, not the ending. Sartre's existence precedes essence structures Link's growth from a swordless Kokiri boy collecting equipment into the hero; Nietzsche's death of God ('we must become gods') fits Link restoring meaning to a godless Hyrule, while Camus's Sisyphus dignifies the repetitive drudge work of slashing grass for rupees. Viktor Frankl's logotherapy anchors the chapter's payoff: even the most mundane tasks — in a camp or a laundromat or Hyrule Field — become bearable and meaningful when connected to a future goal, which is why the author can play for four hours straight.

frankl-meaning.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
frankl-meaning.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
frankl-meaning.relation: Mussett asks whether Peter Parker's painful life counts as a good life by testing five philosophers' answers against the comics and films. Kurtz's secular humanism finds Peter wanting in pleasure and acclaim (Uncle Ben dead by his inaction, J. Jonah Jameson's smear campaigns), while Rand's Objectivism condemns Spider-Man as the embodiment of the 'morality of sacrifice' she rejected, noting Steve Ditko's Objectivist devotion. Epictetus scores Peter highly on duty but fails him on self-mastery, since his happiness hinges on attachments to Aunt May and MJ he cannot control; Frankl would see Peter's meaning in his irreplaceable responsibility, evidenced by his refusal of Dr. Judas Traveller's offer of a peaceful life at the cost of innocents (Amazing Spider-Man #402); and Aquinas vindicates Peter's suffering as good pain in a virtuous, charitable life.

frankl-meaning.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
frankl-meaning.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
frankl-meaning.relation: Jim Berti's first-person memoir 'The Path to Happiness Begins with a Journey Inside' — riffing on Yoda as a stand-in for yoga — recounts how accidental stretching and belly-breathing pulled him out of anxiety, depression, and antidepressant numbness. He frames accumulated fear as garbage that rots the body–mind unless confronted, and describes a 'five-second' breathing rule that slows reactive thinking so he can take accountability for his responses. His account of finding sustained meaning and present-focused calm through practice reads as an experiential, self-taught search for meaning rather than doctrine.

frankl-meaning.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
frankl-meaning.title: 62. Hannah Gadsby as Philosopher Is Comedy Really Such a Good Thing
frankl-meaning.relation: The chapter treats Hannah Gadsby's Nanette as philosophical comedy, weighing her four reasons for quitting: self-deprecation is humiliation for the marginalized, jokes' setup-punchline structure cannot heal trauma, comic relief lets audiences off the hook, and anger only spreads hatred. It distinguishes self-lacerating from ethical, existential, and ironic self-deprecation, and contrasts Critchley's Freudian neo-Stoic humor (super-ego viewing the ego as trivial, akin to Epictetus and cognitive therapy) with the Willetts' feminist 'collective catharsis.' Against Gadsby's claim that anger cannot be constructive, it sets Nussbaum's Anger and Forgiveness alongside Lorde and Srinivasan to argue anger can recover agency and register injustice, and defends Nanette as genuine comedy and 'stand-up catharsis.'

underdetermination.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
underdetermination.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
underdetermination.relation: Johnson argues that because Zelda has no single authorial vision (teams, outside developers, cryptic Aonuma interviews), the timeline is a 'communication game' fans play together. Interpretation follows the hermeneutic circle of Heidegger and Gadamer (parts inform the whole, as when Wind Waker's references to Ganon's earlier attacks make sense of the series), faces Leibnizian underdetermination since infinitely many theories fit the games, and uses Ockham's razor, whose failures (the y=2x formula) show that simplicity is relative to a community's training, as in Wittgenstein's pupil who suddenly counts '1,004, 1,008'. Hence Miyamoto's own claim that Zelda is a communication game: designers supply puzzle pieces, and the fan community creates the meaning.

underdetermination.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
underdetermination.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

underdetermination.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
underdetermination.title: 3. The M. Night Sh-imulation Hypothesis
underdetermination.relation: The chapter runs Bostrom's simulation argument against 'M. Night Shaym-Aliens!', where the Zigerions trap Rick in simulations-within-simulations to steal his concentrated dark matter formula, and reads their cheap shortcuts ('My man!' NPCs, human music, Jerry's Appley award) as the glitches and shadow-people Bostrom predicts. It presses the epistemological problem that any evidence for the simulation equally supports its denial, an underdetermination that devastates the theory, and traces the lineage of 'the real world isn't real' through Plato's summoners and allegory of the cave, Descartes's dream doubt, and Paley's design analogy (Morty as the beautiful machine), ending with the microverse battery of 'The Ricks Must Be Crazy': this is the universe we live in, so get used to it.

underdetermination.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
underdetermination.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
underdetermination.relation: Carl Matthew Johnson argues that the split-timeline versus linear-timeline fan war, settled by Eiji Aonuma's 2006 Nintendo Dream interview, is really a hermeneutic meta-game fans play on top of Zelda. He applies the Heidegger-Gadamer hermeneutic circle — the Ganon references in Wind Waker make sense only from knowledge of the whole series, while gossip-stone text about Kaepora Gaebora feeds back into the whole — then uses Leibniz's curve-fitting problem to show timeline evidence underdetermines any single interpretation. Ockham's razor and Wittgenstein's counting-by-twos rule-following example reveal that simplicity is community-relative, culminating in Miyamoto's 2007 claim that Zelda was designed from the start as a 'communication game' among players.

cartesian-theater.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
cartesian-theater.title: A Link to the Present
cartesian-theater.relation: Compagno argues that the word 'I' in Zelda simultaneously names Link, the virtual body, and the player, the invisible will, and builds this into a 'Schopenhauerian Console': as Schopenhauer held, we have freedom of action but not freedom of will, since the decisions of the unknowable will never appear in consciousness (against Descartes' free mind and Dennett's Cartesian theater critique). Kant's transcendental subject, standing at the border of experience, becomes the player's perspective from which Hyrule exists, what Foucault would call an empirical-transcendental doublet. The payoff: Link's quest is fated and scripted, yet the player wills it in a perpetual present, enacting Schopenhauer's lesson that a determined life is still lived as one's own free act.

cartesian-theater.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
cartesian-theater.title: Does the Piano Play Itself
cartesian-theater.relation: Versteeg and Barkman use the player piano — keys that depress themselves with no ghost at the keyboard — to frame Robert Ford's 'we can't define consciousness because consciousness does not exist' as eliminative materialism, the view shared by Paul Churchland and Daniel Dennett that the common-sense self with its beliefs, desires, and central first-person perspective is a fiction. They set this against Descartes's dualism of res cogitans and res extensa, noting the failed pineal-gland 'magical transaction' and Dennett's replacement of the Cartesian Theater with multiple drafts of consciousness and the manifest-versus-scientific image. The chapter closes on Ford's inconsistency — denying consciousness yet sacrificing his life so the hosts can become self-aware — and asks whether, if the piano plays itself, humans are just complex machines too.

cartesian-theater.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
cartesian-theater.title: A Link to the Present
cartesian-theater.relation: Dario Compagno uses Schopenhauer's distinction between freedom of action and freedom of will — consciousness never witnesses the moment of decision, only hears the will's outcomes — to model the player-Link relation in Zelda. He proposes a 'Schopenhauerian Console' against Dennett's Cartesian theater: Link is the immanent virtual body in Hyrule, the player's will is the transcendent force outside it, and Kant's transcendental subject is the perspective on the border of experience that connects the two when the gamer becomes 'Link's player'. Foucault's 'empirical-transcendental doublet' explains why 'I am Link' is ambiguous exactly the way 'I' is ambiguous in real life, pointing at once to a body and to an invisible ruling will.

cartesian-theater.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
cartesian-theater.title: Does the Piano Play Itself
cartesian-theater.relation: Michael Versteeg and Adam Barkman use the player piano to introduce Ford's eliminative materialism, aligning his 'consciousness does not exist' speech with Churchland and Dennett against the common-sense view of a self distinct from the body. They present Descartes' res cogitans/res extensa dualism and the pineal-gland 'magical transaction' as the target, then Churchland's claim that Folk-Psychology's beliefs and desires will be eliminated by neuroscience, and Dennett's Multiple Drafts model rejecting the Cartesian Theater and the manifest self. They note Ford's self-contradiction in speaking of a 'who' who makes choices while denying selves exist, concluding that if eliminativism holds, humans are complex machines like the piano and the hosts, everything being 'what it isn't.'

twin-earth.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
twin-earth.title: The Loneliest Witch
twin-earth.relation: Auxier gives three theories of why water melts the Wicked Witch, one for each register of Oz: as dream (Bergson's account of dreams as memory explains the fire/water effect-swap), as Baum's fairytale (Susanne Langer's presentational symbols make dryness-wickedness versus water-as-life the tale's moral physics), and as Gregory Maguire's possible world, where the philosophy of language takes over. He narrates Frege's sense/reference distinction—mayor of the Munchkins—to explain how fiction can support truth and falsity ('Dorothy melts the Witch' true, 'Dorothy tried to melt her' false), then deploys Putnam's Twin Earth thought experiment: 'water' in Oz is XYZ while Kansas water is H2O, so Elphaba's word 'water' does not mean what Dorothy's does, and meanings just aren't in the head. Elphaba—the unique being straddling two worlds, killed by H2O she cannot name and terrified by dreams of oceans—is offered as an even stronger argument for Putnam's semantic externalism than Twin Earth's molecule-for-molecule doppelgangers.

ecofeminism.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
ecofeminism.title: Mirror, Mirror
ecofeminism.relation: Sailors convicts Dorothy of being the stereotypical female of Baum's and Fleming's versions, disowning responsibility for killing both witches and living to please others, then contrasts her with Elphaba of Wicked as a feminist hero who leaves home, protects Animals, and mixes 'hot' male and 'cold' female anger into a single fury. She reads Elphaba's indeterminate gender through Marilyn Frye's point that easily identifiable groups are the easiest to oppress, through de Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but becomes a woman' and Mill's line that the 'nature of women' is an eminently artificial thing. Singer's liberation logic, together with the Wollstonecraft-Taylor 'Vindication of the Rights of Brutes' episode and the ecofeminist link between the oppression of women and animals, is applied to Elphaba's Animal-rights activism and her position as 'neither man nor beast,' before the Witch's mirror recognition of Dorothy forces the author to soften her verdict.

ecofeminism.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
ecofeminism.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
ecofeminism.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

ecofeminism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
ecofeminism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
ecofeminism.relation: Jeff Ewing reads Victor's science through ecofeminist and Marxist critiques: M. Waldman's promise to 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'show how she works in her hiding-places' exemplifies exactly what Val Plumwood condemns - male knowers wringing secrets from a nature pictured as a passive female slave - and Victor studies natural elements 'in their death, not in their life' as raw material for power. Marx and Engels supply the parallel diagnosis: capitalism biases science and technology toward profit, turning tools and knowledge into means of domination rather than human flourishing, just as Victor's knowledge serves only his glory and kills everyone he loves.
