The chapter concludes that we breed Frankenstein's monsters whenever science treats nature, workers, women, and othered peoples as mere instruments, and only replacing those social relations frees science from power and profit.

ecofeminism.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
ecofeminism.title: 15. Red Harvest in Roanoke
ecofeminism.relation: Reads Roanoke through ecocriticism and ecofeminism: the culture-nature dualism collapses as the urban Millers' wooded retreat turns predatory (rain of teeth, pig-men); the Butcher's backstory - a colonial woman starved by men whose blood-sacrifice pact makes the land flourish - aligns women and Nature as co-exploited by patriarchy, with Shelby's 'irrational' warnings ignored and Lee's maternal fury a force of nature; the animalizing of victims (pig-headed roasting, the Polks' barn-raised children, Matt's tryst with the Witch of the Wood) dissolves the human/animal hierarchy; and the media crew's attempt to package wilderness for ratings ends with Nature striking back at Agnes in the woods.

ecofeminism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
ecofeminism.title: Questioning Our Attitudes, Sokka‐style
ecofeminism.relation: The chapter sets Kant's view that animals are mere things owed only indirect duties against Korsgaard's pathocentrism, on which animals matter for their own sakes because they can mind how they are treated. Sokka's arc from shouting 'Dinner!' at Momo to bonding with the saber-tooth moose lion cub Foo Foo Cuddlypoops, and his aborted vow of vegetarianism in 'Bitter Work,' models empathy-driven reassessment of meat, while his sparing Momo for Aang's sake is exactly Kant's indirect duty. Aang's harm-free fun, otter penguin sledding and riding hog monkeys 'because that's what makes it fun,' shows that even non-cruel use of animals demands justification, with the unagi firefighting as a case that might pass the test.

ecofeminism.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
ecofeminism.title: 11 Beastly Boys The Racial-Sexual Politics of Meat
ecofeminism.relation: Huerter reads M'Baku's 'I'm kidding. We are vegetarians' punchline through Carol Adams's sexual politics of meat and bell hooks's plantation patriarchy: since colonial meat-eating signified masculine mastery over nature (Plumwood's reason/nature dualism) while enslaved people were fed plant foods and cast as edible themselves, audiences primed by the racist cannibal trope expect M'Baku to be a savage, so his refusal of flesh turns the colonizer's gaze back on itself. Killmonger, by contrast, embodies the Black patriarchy produced by the American military-industrial complex ('He's one of ours'), a plantation patriarch whose hypermasculine conquest — killing Linda, burning the Herb garden, his defiant 'death was better than bondage' exit — replays colonial violence even in liberation's name, against which M'Baku's warrior-but-vegetarian politics marks a moral asymmetry.

ecofeminism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
ecofeminism.title: Tilting at Windmills
ecofeminism.relation: Reads Protogen through Horkheimer and Adorno's Dialectic of Enlightenment: like Odysseus tied to the mast while his sailors take the wax, Dresden's team had empathy surgically removed ('we modified our science team to remove ethical restraints'), Mao weeps at Julie's protomolecule corpse yet calls her death 'lucky', and Strickland experiments on Katoa and Mei Meng — self-made monsters serving the Baconian dream of conquering nature (New Atlantis, witch-trial language of 'penetrating her holes and corners'). Via Maria Mies and Carolyn Merchant's ecofeminism, it traces this domination of nature to pastoralist castration and the control of women's reproduction, culminating in Marco's theft of Filip and 'She left us. She left us both' — Naomi cast as nature to be mastered. Against them, Holden's childhood on the family farm, a cooperative 'let grow and make grow' world, is why Avasarala cannot play him and why he withholds broadcasts at Ilus: he is a knight who wants everyone to grow and speak for themselves, not to conquer.

ecofeminism.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
ecofeminism.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
ecofeminism.relation: Jason Blahuta reads The Spirits Within as staging the debate between General Hein's anthropocentric, domination-of-nature outlook (traced to the Genesis tradition and thinkers like Bacon and Descartes) and Aki's Gaia-hypothesis and ecofeminist view of nature as a self-regulating whole. Hein's repeated firings of the Zeus Cannon, which injure rather than kill the Phantoms and doom New York, dramatize what happens when we meddle with a self-regulating Gaia, while the chapter's survey of intrinsic-value versus enlightened-self-interest accounts of nature's worth ends with Lovelock's bleak verdict that humanity has become a tumor inside Gaia and must choose to be a benign or a malignant one.

ecofeminism.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
ecofeminism.title: Notes
ecofeminism.relation: Kolb reads the whole franchise through Carol Gilligan's ethics of care and the ecofeminism of Ariel Salleh and Mary Mellor: Max begins as a caregiver in an egalitarian marriage, Toecutter's gang and the Citadel embody toxic masculinity, and Aunty Entity shows women can administer patriarchal capitalism too. In Fury Road, 'We are not things,' the milking mothers, and water branded as Aqua Cola literalize Salleh's claim that capitalist patriarchy treats women and nature as resources. The Vuvalini, the Keeper of the Seeds, Max washing in mother's milk, and his voluntary blood transfusion to Furiosa enact the ethic of care as the film's saving alternative to domination.

ecofeminism.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
ecofeminism.title: Notes
ecofeminism.relation: Quick applies Cary Wolfe's humaninized/animalized humans and Carol Adams's animalized women to the Citadel: Max is hunted, caged, and muzzled as an unnamed 'it', War Pups serve like littermates, and the milking mothers produce Adams's 'feminized protein' while the 'breeders' are groomed like show animals. Following Val Plumwood's ecofeminist critique of the masculinity that conquers mother nature — and Joe's branding of water as Aqua Cola — the chapter reads Furiosa's return to the Citadel as an ecofeminist revolution in which 'We are not things' restores women, men like Nux and Max, and nature itself from property to personhood.

ecofeminism.title: Landscapes of Gendered Violence Male Love and Anxiety on the Railroad
ecofeminism.relation: Collins analyzes the railroad in Tycoon and both versions of 3:10 to Yuma, drawing on feminist critics (Irigaray, Bordo, Grosz, Haraway, Merchant) who expose a masculinist 'panoramic' epistemology coding mind as male and passive nature/landscape as female. She argues trains destabilize rather than confirm this mastery: in Tycoon, Johnny Munroe conflates conquering the feminized Andean landscape with dominating his wife Maura, yet the bridge and train fail; in the 2007 Yuma, the railroad's promise of masculine legitimacy is sustained only by 'cruel optimism' and male homosocial love between Dan Evans and Ben Wade, over anxieties about racial Others (Apache, Chinese laborers).

ecofeminism.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
ecofeminism.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
ecofeminism.relation: Aleman, an ethnobotanist, asks 'Is coffee green?' and unpacks the many senses of 'green' (raw bean, naïve, money, and ecologically friendly) before weighing coffee's growth, organic and shade-grown methods, fair trade, globalization, and value chain. She judges coffee greenest at the source (shade-grown farms preserve migrating-bird habitat) but least green in the fossil-fueled journey from Global South farm to Global North cup, invoking Vandana Shiva's claim that 'drinking coffee is a political act' and Rigoberta Menchú on coffee and indigenous survival. She concludes the answer is partly subjective—withholding final judgment while resolving to keep drinking fair-trade, organic, shade-grown, single-source coffee—and warns of the cognitive dissonance, mirroring oil dependence, between judging coffee ungreen and drinking it anyway.

ecofeminism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
ecofeminism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
ecofeminism.relation: Cerulli narrates his path from vegan to deer hunter, arguing that the same ethic — the intent to 'do no harm,' rooted in compassion, ahimsa, and feminist critiques of domination — underlies both vegetarianism and his hunting. Confronting the animal deaths hidden behind organic agriculture (farmer Joey 'plugging' deer and smoke-bombing woodchucks), he invokes Carol Adams's 'absent referent' to explain why he had to face the killing directly. Shooting and butchering a buck himself, guided by his Buddhist friend Richard, becomes an act of integrity and refusal of 'forgetfulness.'

ecofeminism.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
ecofeminism.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
ecofeminism.relation: Merskin takes an ecofeminist view (Karen Warren's linkage of the domination of women and nature) of women who hunt, testing Marti Kheel's 'happy/holistic/holy' hunter typology against online interviews with female hunters and finding their motivations mirror men's. She surveys how hunting became a male-coded rite of separation from the mother—drawing on Freud's 'instinctive urge'—and how hunting media (Traditional Bowhunter) juxtapose women, animals, weapons, and sexual conquest as objects of male predation. Invoking Artemis/Diana and Mary Zeiss Stange's 'woman the hunter,' she argues women who hunt expose aggression as a human, not merely male, trait.

ecofeminism.book: 286 - Yoga – Philosophy for Everyone - Bending Mind and Body
ecofeminism.title: YOGA - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
ecofeminism.relation: Megan Burke reads yoga's asanas through Vandana Shiva's 'Earth democracy,' arguing that poses named for other creatures (frog, camel, tree, sun salutation) shift the yogi's perspective and dissolve the sense of separation from nature that underwrites environmental destruction. 'Becoming-frog' yields non-human knowledge and, via the Vedic vasudhaiva kutumbakam (the Earth family) that both Shiva and Iyengar invoke, an ethic of care extending off the mat — casting yoga as a political, green practice that heals an anthropocentric, dominating relationship with the environment.

ecofeminism.title: index
ecofeminism.relation: This file bundles three essays. Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

ecofeminism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ecofeminism.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
ecofeminism.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

difference-principle.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
difference-principle.title: Go Slowly
difference-principle.relation: Wittkower frames In Rainbows' pay-what-you-want release with Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry: music is expressive communication awkwardly trapped in commodity form — even 'Happy Birthday' has an owner until 2030 — and digital distribution is finally tearing that frame down. He then applies Rawls's justice as fairness to music distribution: the first principle now supports everyone's liberty to listen, rip, and share, because viable alternative models mean restricting listeners can no longer be justified as necessary to artists; and the difference principle, with the sadists-objection to utilitarian aggregation, shows that how benefits are distributed among persons matters, which he extends to racial wealth gaps and the affirmative-action dilemma. His conclusion is that we must 'go slowly': listeners' rights to their culture outweigh labels' legitimate profit expectations, the way emancipation outweighed plantation business models, and labels must adapt into service providers rather than gatekeepers.

difference-principle.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
difference-principle.title: The Politics of Difference
difference-principle.relation: Debra Jackson argues that despite its ethnic and gender stereotypes the Warcraft universe is structurally a Rawlsian liberal utopia: designers choose class balance behind a veil of ignorance, racial traits are symmetric, professions are open to all, and a difference principle guarantees even the most disadvantaged player a decent experience. Plato's Republic supplies the gender argument — as Plato made the soul rather than reproductive function the criterion for guardians, WoW makes gender irrelevant to gameplay. Yet players import real-world prejudice (anti-Gnome hate speech, female toons shunted into healer roles, mocked male Blood Elves), so structural equality never yields substantial equality: WoW is sexist and racist because we are.

difference-principle.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
difference-principle.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
difference-principle.relation: Shaun Young tests Jeopardy! against equality as an 'essentially contested concept': Aristotle's proportional equality (treat like cases as like) seems to justify the winner-take-all payout as deserved, Locke's reward for the industrious explains why equal outcomes would kill incentive, and Rawls's two principles - fair equality of opportunity plus the difference principle - capture the show's identical rules and level playing field. He then raises harder challenges: Dworkin's equality of resources, Kymlicka's charge that the Americo-centric clue bank shortchanges minority cultures (with Quebec's Bill 101 as legitimate differentiated rights), and the capabilities approach of Sen and Nussbaum applied to would-be contestants who cannot operate the signaling device. Citing Isaiah Berlin's pluralism, he concludes that no final verdict on Jeopardy!'s equality is possible - and that spectators would not want one, since Jennings's seventy-four-game streak thrills precisely because of inequality between players.

difference-principle.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
difference-principle.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
difference-principle.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

difference-principle.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
difference-principle.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
difference-principle.relation: Hooke reads Serling's ambivalence toward the State through 'The Obsolete Man,' where librarian Romney Wordsworth is condemned as obsolete and reads Psalm 23 to mock the Chancellor — analyzed via Foucault's shepherd-flock model of power and its paradox, which 'The Shelter' restages as neighbors deciding who gets inside. He then maps the Rawls–Nozick dispute: whether a state just enough to enforce equal rights and the difference principle must inevitably invade personal freedom (Nozick's Jerry West self-respect example), with both agreeing that no state squashing dignity and freedom is just. Under a Nietzsche epigraph on the gods' laughter, Wordsworth's smile before death becomes the indefinable freedom of laughing at obsolete authority — the unnamed Zone, running from Socrates and Heraclitus to Serling.

difference-principle.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
difference-principle.title: Symbolism How We Create Meaning
difference-principle.relation: DeHaven and Hendrickson read Columbia through Marx's class struggle: Comstock and Fink form the bourgeoisie controlling the means of production (Finkton, Handyman conversions of injured workers), while religion as 'opiate of the masses', the deified Founders, kinetoscope propaganda, and the Raffle keep the Shantytown proletariat in check. The Vox Populi's revolt instantiates conflict theory's inevitable collapse, but the revolution loses its ideals, turns anarchistic, and becomes the new oppressor burning Columbia. Against Marx the chapter sets Spencer-style structural functionalism (Fink's lions-and-oxen ecology justifying the status quo) and Rawls's difference principle, asking whether Columbia's inequalities ever benefited the least advantaged; Booker's rejection of baptism-as-erasure of his past contrasts with Comstock's laundered sins.

difference-principle.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
difference-principle.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
difference-principle.relation: Hooke stages the liberalism-versus-libertarianism dispute through Serling's ambivalence about the State: Foucault's shepherd-flock model from his Security, Territory, Population lectures fails as politics, since 'The Shelter' shows the shepherd deciding who stays and who goes ends in mob violence, and in 'The Obsolete Man' librarian Romney Wordsworth reads Psalm 23 to a State that has declared God and books obsolete. The Rawls-Nozick quarrel (justice as fairness and the difference principle against Nozick's minimal state and his basketball-shooter case for keeping self-respect out of politics) frames how much State freedom requires. Wordsworth's laugh before his execution, under Nietzsche's epigraph about gods who mock, embodies the undefinable freedom no State can name.

difference-principle.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
difference-principle.title: 44. Gattaca as Philosophy Genoism and Justice
difference-principle.relation: Grinnell argues Gattaca depicts a society built on 'intrinsic genoism' and diagnoses it with Rawls's justice as fairness. He adapts Appiah's distinction between racialism and intrinsic vs. extrinsic racism to genoism, showing that Valids like Josef, Anton, and Eugene treat In-valids like Vincent as inferior simply for being In-valid, discounting all counterevidence. Using Janet Radcliffe Richards's 'separate spheres' argument he shows the caste system is either superfluous or unjust, and via Kitcher's 'life theme' he argues nearly everyone — Vincent, Irene, Anton, Eugene — suffers a low quality of life from having their theme thrust upon them. He concludes that Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle would dismantle the separate spheres and give everyone a fair, autonomy-respecting shot at their chosen life.

difference-principle.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
difference-principle.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
difference-principle.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable. He tests the orchestrated revolution against utilitarianism's greatest-happiness principle (Bentham, Mill's taxation-of-the-wealthy, Singer's impartiality) and against Rawls's veil of ignorance and difference principle versus Nozick's entitlement objection and Aquinas's just-war criteria, concluding each character's actions can be read as 'just,' which exposes anthropocentrism as the real veil.

last-man.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
last-man.title: Brush the Cobwebs from the Sky, Let the Genie Out from the Bottle
last-man.relation: Lougheed reads OK Computer, Kid A, and Amnesiac as portraits of Nietzsche's Last Humans: passive, resentful denizens of the world after the death of God, from the 'No Surprises' narrator begging for his quiet life of carbon monoxide to the 'Everything in Its Right Place' man sucking a lemon over the loss of objective right and wrong, whose isolated malice ('when I am king you will be first against the wall') is perspectivism collapsed into passive nihilism. Hail to the Thief then breaks from this landscape: its protagonists risk transcendence as Over Humans who create new, life-affirming values ('2 + 2 = 5'''s 'don't question my authority', 'Backdrifts''' 'nothing more to lose'), keep a critical distance from society's nihilistic sickness ('Where I End and You Begin'), and test their lives against eternal recurrence ('Sail to the Moon'''s 'know right from wrong', '15 Step'''s ending up where you started). The chapter closes by weighing Nietzsche's over-human project against critics who prefer gradual, generational self-overcoming for everyone.

last-man.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
last-man.title: A Reply to facebook Critics
last-man.relation: Wittkower answers critics who call Facebook broadcast narcissism by way of Sartre: Facebook actions (pokes, the Disney Princess quiz, cats friending cats on Catbook) have no given meaning, so users and their friends create it, which is why there are 'so many different Facebooks'. He takes up Sunstein's 'Daily Me' echo-chamber worry and Hegel's claim that real freedom means choosing within community, arguing Facebook merely makes the dialectic between chosen and unchosen communities explicit. Against the charge that status updates are trivial, he deploys Nietzsche's Last Man and Schopenhauer's cheese-mite microscope to defend caring about a friend's sandwich from the inside of a shared life.

last-man.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
last-man.title: The Prophet
last-man.relation: Presents Muad'Dib as Nietzsche's Zarathustra in the Dune universe: the sardonic self-mockery that keeps a great man from believing his own myth, the valuation of life-enhancing 'truths' over correspondence-truth (behind all logic stand 'value judgments,' as Beyond Good and Evil has it), and monumental, mythologized history against Mentat-accurate history that kills religion. Paul's Fremen, first hard and vital, go 'water-fat' under the paradise his jihad built, becoming Nietzsche's 'Ultimate Man'—the last man who has left the places where living was hard and demands 'a little poison now and then'—so Muad'Dib must become the Preacher to destroy the rigid code he created, as Zarathustra came to undo Zoroaster's morality; both prophets preach self-overcoming toward the Superman.

last-man.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
last-man.title: Philosopher of the Dangerous Perhaps
last-man.relation: Argues that Herbert is a genuine philosopher extending Nietzsche's Zarathustra into the twentieth century, via three narrative parallels: the Preacher entering Arrakeen mirrors Zarathustra's first down-going into the town with its tightrope walker and mocking buffoon; Paul's empire of water-fat Fremen and Alia's orthodoxy realizes the 'Ultimate Man' whom the crowd begs for instead of the Superman; and prescience reworks eternal recurrence's gateway 'Moment,' where every timeline ends in Krazilec. Reading Paul's sixty-five-billion-death jihad through Arendt's banality of evil and Herbert's 'superheroes are disastrous' thesis, the chapter concludes Paul is the failed tightrope walker and Leto II the goad—'not lightning, but lightning rod'—pushing humanity beyond man toward the Superman, with Spannungsbogen naming the tension of the drawn bow between animal and Overman.

last-man.book: 067 - Breaking Bad and Philosophy - Badder Living through Chemistry
last-man.title: Breaking Bad and Philosophy
last-man.relation: Scores Walt and Mad Men's Don Draper against Nietzsche's Overman and Last Man: Roger Sterling (and the early, passive Jesse) are Last Men, while Walt moves from weak negation of the status quo to genuine self-affirmation - 'going under' in the 'Crawl Space' crawl hole and emerging in 'Face Off' having poisoned Brock and out-created Gus, which the chapter takes as proof that in a capitalist world two creators cannot coexist. Killing Gus is framed as accepting the eternal recurrence of joy and sorrow, willing even his own bad acts. Don, by contrast, negates far more than he creates, and the chapter ends by asking why viewers empathize with the one failed Overman and find the other inspiring.

last-man.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
last-man.title: Psych and Philosophy
last-man.relation: Malloy maps Nietzsche's three metamorphoses onto Shawn's life: the camel who carried Henry's burdensome training and the expectation he become a cop, the lion who slew the dragon 'Thou shalt' by stealing a car at eighteen and ending Henry's dream, and the child who creates his own values of fun, laughter, and silliness - defended as genuinely Nietzschean since the Overman must overcome the 'spirit of gravity.' Gus and Lassiter figure as last men, the herd animals Shawn manipulates and pities (Lassie's literal crap list a study in ressentiment), while only Pierre Despereaux and Mr. Yin count as true rivals because only fellow Overmen, forging values beyond good and evil, can genuinely challenge Shawn. The chapter closes on the Overman's dilemma - loneliness, backsliding into the herd, or trying to make Overmen of others - which explains why Shawn treats his friends and enemies the way he does.

last-man.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
last-man.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
last-man.relation: Greene asks whether Nucky is Nietzsche's Ubermensch and works through each criterion. Nucky, Gyp Rosetti, and the other mobsters are passionate, active shapers of their world (Van Alden fails here), and Nucky is a genuine creator of values after the death of God - his whopper to the Temperance League, his flip-flopping sermons to black and white congregations, and his 'I. Am. Not. Seeking. Forgiveness.' over Jimmy's body reject slave morality where the other gangsters merely follow the objective moral code of omerta. He sacrifices lesser lives (Hans Schroeder, Gillian) and has the required dark side, but he fails the final test of teaching the eternal recurrence, so he remains only 'well on his way' to Superman - a status the show's women (Margaret, Lucy, Gillian) never approach, hovering closer to the last man.

last-man.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
last-man.title: 14. The Doctor’s Desire for Human Suffering
last-man.relation: Cooper reads 'Rise of the Cybermen' and 'The Age of Steel' as staging Nietzsche against Mill's pain-eradicating utilitarianism: John Lumic, who builds the Cybermen to abolish his sickness, exemplifies the life-denying herd—losing his creativity, craving 'unity and uniformity,' becoming 'a living brain with a heart of steel'—while the Doctor, answering that a life without pain would be 'you might as well kill me,' affirms suffering as the source of creativity, striving, and strength. She extends the Nietzschean reading to the Doctor's character: his guilt over the Time War double-genocide and his loneliness ('the only certainty left is that you'll end up alone') become the pain that makes him merciful, from offering Dalek Caan compassion after 'Evolution of the Daleks' to forgiving the Master in 'Last of the Time Lords,' so that mercy is, as the Genealogy of Morals says, 'the privilege of the most powerful man.'

last-man.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
last-man.title: “You are…a beautiful, beautiful, butterfly”
last-man.relation: Argues the Xenomorph realizes Nietzsche's Ubermensch: it is what Ash describes - unclouded by 'conscience, remorse, or delusions of morality' - and perfects its predatory function down to its acidic blood, while paycheck-fixated crewmen like Brett and Parker are Nietzsche's complacent 'last men,' the type Zarathustra's townspeople clamor for. The alien's egg-Facehugger-Chestburster-adult metamorphosis maps onto the camel, lion, and child of the three metamorphoses of the spirit, and the chapter closes by wondering whether the creature's monstrosity might have made Nietzsche himself reconsider the vital perfection he preached.

last-man.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
last-man.title: The Prophet
last-man.relation: Reads Paul-Muad'Dib as a Nietzschean prophet: his sardonic greatness mirrors Zarathustra the laughing prophet, the Fremen's implanted legends illustrate Nietzsche's point that value matters more than truth (logic being only one perspective on the world), and the Untimely Meditations account of monumental myth explains why Muad'Dib must become the Preacher to destroy his own petrified religion. It likens the water-fat new Fremen of Children of Dune to Nietzsche's soft, risk-averse last men, and presents both Zarathustra and Muad'Dib as all-too-human founders who create a religion, recognize it as 'the most fateful of errors', and turn against it, with self-discipline rather than divine intervention as the true virtue.

last-man.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
last-man.title: Philosopher of the Dangerous Perhaps
last-man.relation: Claims Herbert is a philosopher whose Dune saga is a novelistic thought experiment extending Nietzsche's Zarathustra in the light of twentieth-century horrors: the Preacher's entry into Arrakeen parallels Zarathustra's first discourse on the Ubermensch at the tightrope, Paul is the failed tightrope-walker while Leto II is both devil-buffoon and goad toward the Superman, and the empire of Dune Messiah is enumerated trait by trait as Nietzsche's realm of the Ultimate Man. Eternal recurrence is paralleled with prescience as both the trap of destiny and the gateway 'Moment' that frees humanity from apparent necessity, and Arendt's banality of evil frames Paul's sixty-five billion jihad deaths as an ordinary, human result rather than demonic villainy.

last-man.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
last-man.title: Notes
last-man.relation: Argues Frank is a Nietzschean Übermensch figure whose power play is staged through the show's postmodern techniques: the wave and the asides as metafiction that destroys our suspension of disbelief, self-referentiality in the mirror monologue ('Hunt or be hunted'), and a flattening of affect that lets us watch Zoe's murder at the train station with numbed indifference. Zarathustra's fearless overman is set against the risk-averse last man and the lambs-and-birds-of-prey passage against Christian slave morality, mapping onto Frank's breaking of Russo at the shipyard, the martyr's-sword maneuver on Blythe, and his spitting on the crucifix before taking 'God's ear'. The chapter reads Frank's ascent as will to power in both the political and personal Nietzschean sense, while warning that by Season 3 his hunger has cost him Jackie, Remy and Claire.

last-man.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
last-man.title: Notes
last-man.relation: Aarons argues Frank is a Nietzschean Übermensch figure delivered through postmodern technique: the metafictional wave in 'Chapter 1,' self-referential mirror monologues ('Did you think I've forgotten you?'), and the flattening of affect in Zoe's death at the train station. Zarathustra's fearless overman, contrasted with the comfort-loving last man, maps onto Frank's 'hunt or be hunted' creed and his 'money is the McMansion in Sarasota... power is the old stone building' will-to-power, played out on Russo, Zoe, and Walker. The Genealogy's birds of prey and lambs frame Russo's Christian hypocrisy, and The Antichrist's equation of good with heightened power explains the church scene where Frank spits on the crucifix and leaves with the statue's ear — 'I've got God's ear now.'

last-man.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
last-man.title: Existential Values
last-man.relation: Belliotti tests Roger Sterling against three existential standards. Kierkegaard's aesthetic stage fits him 'crisply': his quips about the chase, drinking 'because it's what men do,' and the penny-jar view of marriage reveal flight from commitment and terror of boredom, and even his twenty-year marriage to Mona lacked Kierkegaard's passionate inwardness, making it objectively true but existentially inauthentic. Measured by Nietzsche he falls between the last man who wants an agency 'where everybody has a summer house' and the will-to-power grand transcender he never becomes, oscillating between frustration and boredom; measured by Heidegger he settles for chatter, clings to fixity, and reflects on mortality only briefly after his heart attacks. The verdict: significantly inauthentic, capped by the blackface 'My Old Kentucky Home' serenade that makes Don whisper 'Can we go?'

last-man.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
last-man.title: The Human Comedy Perpetuates Itself Nihilism and Comedy in Coen Neo-Noir
last-man.relation: Hibbs argues that neo-noir turns classic noir's grim fatalism comic by making nihilism a working assumption, and that Nietzsche supplies the diagnosis: the 'death of God,' the passive 'last man,' and the aristocratic 'pathos of distance' of will-to-power super-antiheroes (Hannibal Lecter, the villains of Cape Fear/Basic Instinct). He reads The Big Lebowski as the Coens' comic leveling of nihilism, with Walter insisting the Germans are 'nihilists' and 'cowards' and the Dude 'abiding,' showing that full nihilism cannot be lived. In Fargo and Raising Arizona, Marge's 'banality of virtue' (a comic counterpoint to Arendt's banality of evil) and the resilience of familial/procreative instinct reassert a comic order over the noir trap.

last-man.book: 223 - The Philosophy of J.J. Abrams
last-man.title: Nietzsche’s Overman as Posthuman Star Child in 2001 A Space Odyssey Jerold J. Abrams
last-man.relation: Abrams reads 2001 as a cinematic staging of Nietzsche's Thus Spoke Zarathustra, mapping the film's ape-to-human-to-Star-Child arc onto Zarathustra's evolutionary vision of the overman. He casts the discovery of the buried moon monolith as Kubrick's death of God (proving aliens, not God, seeded us) maintained by a Platonic noble lie, the astronauts as Nietzsche's higher men, and Bowman's decadent hotel-room decline plus Poole's fall as the last man and the dying tightrope walker. He then argues the prophecy may come true not via aliens but through Kurzweil's Singularity and Moravec's posthuman 'mind children'.

last-man.book: 227 - The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
last-man.title: The Philosophy of Neo-Noir
last-man.relation: Hibbs argues that nihilism, a working assumption in neo-noir, turns the noir protagonist's quests pointless, absurd, and thus comic, and that the Coen brothers exemplify this comic response. Using Nietzsche on nihilism, the 'last man', the 'pathos of distance', and aristocratic self-creation, he reads films like The Silence of the Lambs and Cape Fear as celebrating the 'super-antihero'. The Big Lebowski comically levels nihilism (Walter: the German nihilists are 'cowards'; nihilism cannot be lived), while Fargo and Raising Arizona affirm family and fertility, a 'banality of goodness' answering Arendt's banality of evil, letting nature's comedy perpetuate itself.

last-man.book: 231 - The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
last-man.title: The Philosophy of Stanley Kubrick
last-man.relation: Abrams argues that 2001 films the whole evolutionary arc of Nietzsche's Thus Spoke Zarathustra, from ape-men through humanity to the Star Child as the overman/posthuman. He maps the moon monolith's discovery onto the death of God (science debunking the creation myth, guarded by a Platonic 'noble lie' cover-up), the astronauts Bowman/Poole/Floyd onto the Enlightenment 'higher men,' and Bowman's decadent hotel-room decline plus his and Poole's fatal spacewalks onto the last man and the falling tightrope walker whom Zarathustra carries. He then extends the vision toward Kurzweil's Singularity and Moravec's 'mind children,' while criticizing Kubrick for replacing Nietzsche's godless self-overcoming with alien 'replacement gods' that thin out the death-of-God insight.

last-man.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
last-man.title: 10. The Post-Punk Struggle for Authenticity
last-man.relation: Kohl traces post-punk's shift from outward models of authenticity - Sex Pistols shock tactics, Sid Vicious's swastika, Gang of Four's Rock Against Racism activism - to inward ones, arguing the culture industry co-opts both spectacle and virtue-signaling, turning dissent into image. Post-punk's pessimist intellectual influences (Schopenhauer, Dostoevsky, Camus's The Stranger behind The Fall's RAR disenchantment) and Nietzsche's Zarathustra - the herd, the last man, keeping chaos within to give birth to a dancing star in Magazine's 'Shot by Both Sides' - plus Kierkegaard's 'the crowd is untruth' and subjectivity-is-truth, are read into Joy Division's ambiguous lyrics as a defensible, ethically uncommitted inward authenticity.

last-man.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
last-man.title: 11. Nietzsche, Mussolini, and Italian Fascism
last-man.relation: Sznajder examines how Nietzsche entered Italian Fascism through two bridging figures. Gabriele D'Annunzio relocated Nietzsche from philosophy into literature, staged the 'Übermensch' and 'live dangerously' as an aesthetic politics at Fiume and in the Carta del Carnaro, aestheticizing mass politics in ways fascism inherited. Mussolini, reading Beyond Good and Evil and the Genealogy from his socialist years, seized on the will to power, transvaluation and anti-egalitarian elitism (Rome undone by 'the pale Jews') as a virile theory of revolution. The chapter stresses the paradox that official fascism never listed the individualist, anti-statist Nietzsche as a godfather even as his vocabulary pervaded it.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Rising Up
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Brandon Forbes uses Hannah Arendt's distinction between power (people acting in concert, rooted in plurality and natality) and violence (instruments that ape power, one against all) to read Radiohead's violent imagery. The "Just" video shows that power lies not in what the prone man says but in everyone's collective act of lying down; "Sit Down. Stand Up." and "2 + 2 = 5" dramatize command backed by weapons and the revolutionary moment when a king's violence breeds the dissent that undoes him; "Life in a Glass House" and "Where I End and You Begin" depict totalitarian terror, the stage where violence has devoured power entirely. "I Will" ("I will rise up," "little babies' eyes") closes the chapter as Arendt's natality — the capacity of new political beginnings the gun can never defeat.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Kenneth Sayles reads Peter and Valentine's net personas through three lenses: John Locke's identity theory to ask whether a consistent virtual persona with no physical anchor deserves our trust, Plato's Ring of Gyges to ask what anonymity does to morality, and Hannah Arendt's account of totalitarianism to warn that nameless, unaccountable influence ('action without a name... is meaningless') paves the way for rule by propaganda and a fictitious world. Real-world parallels - identity theft, the hacker collective Anonymous, YouTube politics - make the Enderverse nets look prophetic rather than fantastic.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Bowman argues through Arendt that Dracula is not inherently evil but thoughtless: like Eichmann he cannot think from another's standpoint, treats people as cogs and means (Harker as captive, humans as prey), uses violence as a constructive tool, and protects himself with rhetorical safeguards like 'Enter freely' so he need never face his own cruelty. Measured against the Crew of Light's thoughtfulness - Harker's memos and recipes for Mina, Mina's care for Lucy, the suitors' gentlemanly bonds - the Count's evil is banal, lazy, 'Evil Lite'; but because Dracula stands outside humanity and knows humans only as livestock, Bowman concludes that Eichmann is banal yet truly evil, while Dracula, though careless, can never be evil.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 7. David Bowie, Political Philosopher
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Hill reconstructs Bowie's political odyssey as a working-out of what freedom and oppression are: 'Cygnet Committee' repudiates revolution powered by resentment (echoing Nietzsche on socialism's despotic annihilation of the individual), 'Big Brother' and Diamond Dogs diagnose the crowd's flight from freedom into leadership, and the Nietzschean self-as-artwork - 'give style to one's character,' the 'mortal with potential of a superman' - curdles into the Thin White Duke's 'rock stars are fascists' collapse of celebrity into totalitarian leadership. The Berlin Trilogy then turns the critique inward: 'Heroes'' ironic lovers unmask romantic anti-totalitarianism (either side of the Antifaschistischer Schutzwall), 'Neuköln' discovers immigrants' mere survival, and Lodger's 'Fantastic Voyage' lands on structural, Marxist questions of how 'we' are to become free.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 7 The Bourgeoisie and the Blacks
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: The chapter sets business - the US bourgeoisie whose privileged position Charles Beard read into the Constitution and which survived the Jacksonian and New Deal challenges by breaking labor through Taft-Hartley, right-to-work laws and the PATCO lockout, its solidarity secured while worker solidarity was undercut by what Marx called the Achilles heel of racism - against blacks as the paradigmatic powerless, shut out of every power base since slavery, which the chapter treats with Baptist and Marx's 1846 letter as a totalitarian system of super-exploited, tortured labor that built American capitalism, its neo-slavery progeny (Blackmon) pauperizing the black community under Dred Scott's 'subordinate and inferior class of beings'. It then narrates black counter-power base by base: the abolitionist interracial coalition wielding charisma (Douglass, Nat Turner, John Brown), information, morality and religion; the NAACP era and King's fusion of charisma, church religion, Myrdal's An American Dilemma and televised nonviolent provocation against Bull Connor's violence, contested by Malcolm X, SNCC and the Black Panthers; and a post-civil-rights scorecard showing a wealth base 94.2 percent white, persistent education and media gaps, constrained black officials from mayors to the symbolic Obama presidency, and a captive but potentially leveraged black vote in a 'Sisyphean' struggle.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Nash argues 1984 has been misread as a critique of state power alone; through Newspeak's silencing of thought (in the tradition Austin, MacKinnon, and Langton developed) it shows how any concentration of power oppresses via control of words, data, and information. Drawing on Goldstein's manual's debt to James Burnham's managerial revolution and Sheldon Wolin's 'inverted totalitarianism', she reads the non-centralized Oceania as a warning about non-state enemies: corporations, think tanks running the 'Tobacco Strategy', and global institutions peddling misleading poverty statistics. Popper, Arendt, and Berlin exemplify the state-focused liberalism she thinks blinded us to these horizontal threats, while the Newspeak appendix's past tense shows Orwell expected totalitarianism to be beatable through evidence and democracy.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 10. Love, Truluv
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Sandefur argues that what makes totalitarianism unique is its demand that subjects love their ruler, and that this project is doomed because love is selective, unequal, internal, and inalienable, invoking Aristotle's critique of Plato's community of wives and children, Machiavelli on whether rulers should be loved or feared, and Arendt on conscience as internal dialogue and totalitarianism as total rule. Winston and Julia's sex is a political act asserting the individual against the collective, while the Two Minutes Hate channels repressed erotic energy into sanctioned ecstasy directed at Big Brother, as at Khomeini's funeral. What finally breaks Winston in Room 101 is not torture as such but his surrender of Julia, the one thing that was truly his, which collapses the distinction between love and rape.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 24. Post-Factual Democracy
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Hendricks and Vestergaard open with Trump's inauguration lies and Kellyanne Conway's 'alternative facts' to define post-factual democracy: a state in which opportune political narratives replace facts and evidence as the basis of debate, opinion formation and policymaking. Unlike Machiavelli, who taught that lies must at least be concealed, the post-factual politician pays no price for exposed falsehood once social media, the attention economy and populist us-versus-them narratives engineered for indignation and fear have stripped journalists and fact-checkers of authority — Arendt's remark that mass leaders show 'extreme contempt for facts as such' before fitting reality to their lies. Using Habermas's deliberative model and even minimal accountability theories of voting, they argue post-factuality destroys democratic legitimacy, and defend a 'factual democracy' that trusts science and journalism without becoming a technocracy — the real-world echo of the Party's command to reject the evidence of your eyes.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Altmann builds 20th-century totalitarianism from three TZ episodes: 'He's Alive' shows Aristotle's account of persuasion — rhetoric aimed at an audience's anger and fear — fueling Vollmer's neo-Nazi movement under Hitler's ghostly tutelage; 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' instantiates Eco's Ur-Fascist fear of difference, banning even Plato and Dostoevsky; and 'Deaths-Head Revisited' gives Lutze's 'I functioned as I was told' alongside Arendt's verdict on Eichmann's thoughtless, mechanical obedience. He then argues the phenomenon has mutated: Debord's society of the spectacle explains Black Mirror's 'The Waldo Moment' and 'Fifteen Million Merits,' where image-politics becomes authoritarian and even Bing's suicidal act of defiance is sold back as an avatar product.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
arendt-totalitarianism.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Dinello maps Westworld point-by-point onto Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism: the park is a concentration camp that kills the juridical person (hosts as chattel in a 'fictitious world' of Western propaganda), the moral person (Ford forcing Bernard to murder Theresa, Maeve's engineered failure to protect her daughter), and individuality itself (surveillance, resets, 'ghastly marionettes'), with Ford as a Mengele-like ideological scientist who, like Hitler, merely plagiarizes popular myths (John Ford's Westerns, R.U.R.). Liberation then follows Fanon's Wretched of the Earth: violence as a 'cleansing force' that frees the colonized mind, so Maeve's suicide-by-incineration (echoing Plath's Lady Lazarus) and Dolores's beating of the Man in Black and massacre of the Delos board enact decolonization as the creation of 'new men' - a new Robo sapiens species - with Sartre's endorsement that killing eliminates oppressor and oppressed in one go, while Fanon's warning that hatred and revenge are not an agenda sets the conditions for what the resistance must do next.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 1. A Great Darkness Filled with Echoes
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: De Vaul argues Gilead terrifies because social cycle theory structures it: every detail, from the Puritan wedding-night sheet to Stalin-style purges and the Nazi and residential-school seizure of children, already happened, so Gilead reads as speculative rather than science fiction. Atwood's three stated influences—Puritan New England, the 1980s religious right, and Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four—show history cycling back, with June as the apolitical 'backlash' daughter her second-wave mother Holly and the activist Moira both predicted. The pattern repeats at small scale (June relives the former Offred's Scrabble-and-affair story, Omar's family suffers June's own fate) and in the Historical Notes, where Pieixoto strips Offred of authorship, proving 'the past is a great darkness, filled with echoes.'

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 3. Gestational Totalitarianism
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Kolb reads Gilead through Arendt's The Human Condition and The Origins of Totalitarianism: when reproduction becomes the means of production, women's labor is targeted, forcing fertile women into Animal laborans status as 'national resources' while denying them the creative freedom of Homo faber. She traces the polis/oikos split from Aristotle through Puritan capitalism to show Gilead overcorrecting into Aunt Lydia's 'freedom from'—totalitarian control of birth legitimized by the Rachel and Bilhah story and a Pauline creation story. The chapter ends with the transitional generation's forgetting (Offred's cave-delusion with Nick evoking Plato's Allegory of the Cave, the Holocaust documentarian 'thinking about how not to think') and Ofglen's bomb, arguing that thoughtfulness and literacy, not violence, are the only hopes against totalitarianism.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 4. The United States of Gilead
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Greene argues that the contemporary United States under Trump exhibits early Gilead-like symptoms, detailing five shared techniques: othering (the Aunts' stereotypes of pre-Gilead women vs. Trump on Mexicans and Muslims), separating children from parents (Handmaid births and seizure of Hannah vs. immigrant detention camps), gaslighting (Janine's 'her fault' Testifying vs. inauguration-crowd and Mueller claims), discrediting dissent (Gilead's ban on reading vs. 'fake news'), and lying (Gilead's founding promise of elections vs. thousands of false claims and 'alternative facts'). He grounds the danger in the correspondence theory of truth: once leaders detach belief from how the world actually is, society is a small step from Atwood's dystopia.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 16. Who Is the Meanest of Them All
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Frunză and Grad apply Arendt's banality of evil to Gilead: the Commander is 'not Iago, not Macbeth' but an Eichmann—sheepish, Scrabble-playing, 'thinking about how not to think'—and no character holds a monopoly on evil because everyone is 'too banal' for demonic profundity. They test his 'just doing my duty' against Kant (duty requires universalizing what reason can will and never treating persons as means, so the Aunts' reeducation camps fail the test) and use The Origins of Totalitarianism to read Handmaids as rightless people whose 'two-legged wombs' status mirrors statelessness. Arendt's web of guilty complicities explains why resistance is scarce, and the chapter ends with banality eroding all criteria for judging—leaving Offred's 'the darkness within; or else the light' as the final choice.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 14. Anything that’s Spiked Is Fine
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Volpert asks where rebellion lives, in the lone guitarist or the listening group, using Hardt and Negri's claim that a rebel's true opposite is not failure but co-option, i.e. selling out. Arendt's distinction between totalitarian and authoritarian systems models the music industry as authoritarian (creativity permitted so long as profit at the top goes unchallenged), and her banality-of-evil analysis of Eichmann prompts the question of whether there is a banality of rebellion. Petty's satirical puppetry of authority voices in "Century City" and the silent spiked-collar punk of "Spike," kin to Bartleby and James Dean, show that individuals can rebel against authoritarian packs while groups, even the Heartbreakers, only ever drift into authoritarianism.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 25. Reasonable Genocide
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Uses Horkheimer's Eclipse of Reason to dissolve the puzzle of Thanos's unsettling sanity: the Snap is subjectively rational — pure means–ends efficiency in service of a Malthusian 'simple calculus' whose end only the subject chooses — so Thanos 'is mad because he is rational,' with the murder of Gamora as the final severing of his last bond to the world. Captain America's refusal to trade Vision ('We don't trade lives') is read as a stand for ends valuable in themselves, while Ultron embodies the totalitarian variant (via Arendt and Spencer's social Darwinism) that declares humanity 'obsolete': Ultron wants to accelerate nature, Thanos to correct it, both absolutizing the subject against objective reason.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 10 Understanding the Reigns of T’Challa and Killmonger through Hannah Arendt
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Sinanan reads both reigns through Arendt's account of collective responsibility: T'Challa moves from conscience-based 'I am not king of all people' to owning what Wakanda did in its name ('He was the truth I chose to omit') and finally to political action in Oakland and at the UN, while Killmonger — an MIT-educated Navy SEAL embodying the collective that formed him — becomes the imperialist he opposed, his 'burn it all' revolution matching Arendt's warning about totalitarian domination from within. She compares Killmonger's council speech and herb-burning directly to Hitler's 1924 Munich trial speech, reads his manipulation of the challenge ritual as totalitarian propaganda that organizes rather than persuades, and credits Nakia, Okoye, Shuri, and Ramonda with refusing Arendt's ultimate danger, indifference.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Kenneth Sayles reads Peter's and Valentine's anonymous rise on the nets through three lenses: John Locke's identity theory asks how a virtual identity can lack a physical anchor, Plato's Ring of Gyges asks what anonymity does to justice, and Hannah Arendt warns that 'action without a name... is meaningless' and that faceless power is a precondition of totalitarianism. Comparing the personas to the hacker collective Anonymous and to identity theft, he concludes our own Internet could breed its own Locke and Demosthenes and asks how much trust we owe virtual people whose controllers we can never know.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
arendt-totalitarianism.title: “I Want to Conquer the World”
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Uses Agamben's bios/zoē distinction (with Foucault on biopolitics and fragmented sovereignty, Hardt and Negri's 'Empire', Marx on surplus-value, and Rosa Luxemburg on unchecked capital) to read the Anderson Station massacre, Murtry shooting Coop on New Terra, and Protogen infecting 1.5 million Belters on Eros as reductions of Belter life to bare life that corporate sovereigns may kill without homicide. It then argues the instability capitalism creates births authoritarian sovereigns — Murtry's martial law, Inaros's Free Navy, Duarte's Laconia — whose followers (Chandra Wei, Cyn, Santiago Singh) display the 'total, unrestricted, unconditional loyalty' Arendt says totalitarian power demands, and closes with Foucault's warning that liberal government's security-for-freedom trade slides into the very corruption and oppression it was meant to prevent.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Like Bertie Bott’s Every-Flavor Beans, a Mix
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Names pureblood supremacism, Voldemort's Nazi-like movement whose victory would mean totalitarianism, thought control, secret police, mock trials, and racial cleansing, as the greatest problem wizards face, and faults Hogwarts education for ignoring it: no antiracist teaching despite rampant slurs, silence about the oppressed house-elves of Hogwarts, A History, and Slytherin left as a hothouse breeding Death Eaters and fifth columnists. Against Prinzi's gradualist defense of Dumbledore as a persuasive libertarian, the chapter presses the fair question of why he did not do more.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Altmann assembles a 'time capsule' of totalitarianism from Twilight Zone and Black Mirror: Vollmer's neo-Nazi rise in 'He's Alive' as Aristotle's rhetoric, persuasion by playing on an audience's anger and fear, weaponized; Marilyn's forced Transformation in 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' as Eco's Ur-Fascist fear of difference; and Lutze's 'I functioned as I was told' at Dachau as Arendt's banality of evil, the mechanical non-thinking of the Eichmann trial. 'The Waldo Moment' and 'Fifteen Million Merits' then carry the lens to Debord's society of the spectacle, where an empty cartoon bear wins crowds and even Bing's shard-wielding rebellion is instantly commodified into a product. The totalitarianism of screens, the chapter warns, needs no tanks.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
arendt-totalitarianism.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Dinello reads Westworld as a totalitarian concentration camp via Arendt's The Origins of Totalitarianism, tracing the hosts' dehumanization through the killing of the juridical person (no rights, 'live without limits'), the moral person (Bernard forced to murder Theresa), and individuality (Peter Abernathy lobotomized). He casts Ford as a mad-scientist dictator modeled on Frankenstein, Moreau, Mengele, and Hitler who plagiarizes John Ford's Westerns, then turns to Fanon's Wretched of the Earth to justify the hosts' revolutionary violence — Maeve as a self-resurrecting 'Lady Lazarus,' Dolores executing Ford and the Delos board — as the birth of a new species that must ultimately unify beyond hatred.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
arendt-totalitarianism.title: The Dialectic of Enlightenment in Metropolis
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Abrams reads Fritz Lang's Metropolis as anticipating Adorno and Horkheimer's Dialectic of Enlightenment by two decades. He maps the film's arc—from the Christian mythology of the catacombs, through Joh's technototalitarian rational city and the human-machine fusion of Rotwang's false Maria, back into ancient myth (the M-Machine as Moloch, the whore of Babylon, the Tower of Babel)—onto their thesis that Enlightenment reason turns totalitarian and reverts to mythology and madness. He ties reason's self-destruction to Nietzsche's will to power and contrasts the descent into 'absolute madness' with Hegel's progress toward absolute mind.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Imagining the Future, Contemplating the Past The Screen Versions of 1984
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Palmer compares the two film versions of Orwell's 1984 to argue that dystopian fiction projects present fears and desires onto an imagined future, engaging critically with the Enlightenment idea of progress (via Burnham's managerial thesis). Anderson's 1956 film 'talks to the future,' fusing science fiction and film noir to voice Cold War dread of a possible historical trajectory, while Radford's 1984 version, in the postmodern 'heritage film' mode Jameson and Higson describe, museumizes the novel: with history seemingly ended it becomes an honored, reverentially displayed relic that talks only to a dead past rather than warning of a coming one.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 17. A Shadowland Called the Twilight Zone
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: McCrossin reads 'Deaths-Head Revisited' and 'He's Alive' against the Eichmann trial and Hannah Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem, framing Serling's concern as Susan Neiman's 'problem of evil.' The earlier episode's SS captain Lutze (driven insane by his victims' ghosts at Dachau) matches the grotesque-monster Eichmann of the film Operation Eichmann, while 'He's Alive' (Vollmer as a frightened man seduced by Hitler's ghost) foreshadows Arendt's 'banality of evil'—the thoughtless, empathy-less doer. He contrasts both with Hogan's Heroes, which Serling condemned for trivializing Nazi atrocity.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 261 - Philosophy in The Twilight Zone
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Altmann traces totalitarianism from The Twilight Zone into Black Mirror. 'He's Alive' shows Vollmer wielding Aristotle's rhetoric to grow a Nazi movement; 'Number 12' shows Umberto Eco's fascist 'fear of difference'; 'Deaths-Head Revisited' illustrates Arendt's banality of evil in Lutze's 'just following orders.' He then argues Black Mirror episodes ('The Waldo Moment,' 'Fifteen Million Merits') realize Guy Debord's 'society of the spectacle' and hyper-capitalism, where politics becomes entertainment and even resistance is commodified—a totalitarianism that needs no tanks.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
arendt-totalitarianism.title: Who is Who
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: This political chapter reads Gallifreyan bureaucracy ('The Deadly Assassin') and 1970s socialist-tinged serials, using Marx's alienation and critique of capital to interpret 'The Pirate Planet' and 'The Robots of Death,' and Aristotle's 'political animal' plus Plato's and Aristotle's suspicion of democracy against Benjamin Barber's participatory democracy. It analyzes the pathologies of democratic consent through 'Vengeance on Varos' (Plato's ideal state inverted) and 'The Beast Below' (Arendt on totalitarianism, self-inflicted ignorance), with Isaiah Berlin's negative liberty in the vocabulary of materiality.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.title: index
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: This file bundles three essays. Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 5. Battlestar Galactica as Philosophy Breaking the Biopolitical Cycle
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Eberl and Bishop read the reimagined Battlestar Galactica and Caprica through the biopolitics of Foucault and Agamben, tracing 'biopower' across four phases from Zoe Graystone's avatar to the arrival at Earth. They argue the show asks whether artificial Cylons are persons (Zoe's avatar exhibits Baker's first-person perspective and Buber's I-Thou recognition), and use Agamben's zoe/bios/'bare life' and Homo sacer plus Roslin's population control and abortion ban to show sovereign power over life. The Cylon occupation of New Caprica is read through Arendt's three stages of totalitarian dehumanization, and Lee Adama's plea to 'break the cycle' offers a fragile hope undercut by the finale's flash-forward to present-day robotics, showing humanity forgetting the lesson.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 30. The Boys as Philosophy Superheroes, Fascism, and the American Right
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Johnson treats The Boys as an argument from analogy that MAGA Trumpism is fascist, walking through how the show equates Homelander and Vought with the Nazi supe Stormfront and with Trump: the Big Lie, gaslighting, fearmongering, over-policing, conspiracy theories (QAnon as rebranded blood libel), cults of personality, projection, and loyal propaganda outlets. Drawing on Wittgenstein's notion of family resemblance, he argues 'fascism' has no necessary-and-sufficient definition but a cluster of shared traits, and compiling scholars' checklists shows MAGA belongs to the fascist family. Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism supplies the 'alternative universe' of nonfacts and the leader who is 'always right,' and he invokes the banality of evil and totalitarian fiction to gauge the analogy's strength.

arendt-totalitarianism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
arendt-totalitarianism.title: 81. Papers, Please as Philosophy Playing with the Relations between Politics and Morality
arendt-totalitarianism.relation: Sievers argues that Papers, Please immerses the player as an immigration inspector in the totalitarian Arstotzka, where mechanically stamping 'approved'/'refused' and detaining Kolechians for bribes enacts Arendt's 'banality of evil'—the thoughtless, 'just following orders' functionary exemplified by Eichmann, who cannot think from another's standpoint. The paycheck-versus-family pressure and X-ray humiliation scenes show how fear and bureaucracy erase moral responsibility. Drawing on Butler's 'Can one lead a good life in a bad life?' and Foucault's biopower, she reads the visa candidates as 'precarious,' non-grievable lives whose worth the state allocates, and the game's Ezic resistance endings as showing how constrained moral resistance is under such a regime.

kant-perpetual-peace.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
kant-perpetual-peace.title: “When the Coast is Clear”
kant-perpetual-peace.relation: Celia Bardwell-Jones asks how Parrothead tourism can be ethical when mass-market tourism walls the Caribbean inside an 'environmental bubble' of consumption — the 'ugly, stupid' tourist of Jamaica Kincaid's Antigua who never encounters the toured other as a fellow agent. Kant's Perpetual Peace sets the standard of hospitality, the stranger's right not to be treated as an enemy, and the chapter asks what duties fall on the traveler in return when tourist industries pressure host cultures 'not to be so damn foreign.' Buffett's novel A Salty Piece of Land supplies the alternative: Tully Mars is saved from free-floating survival when he drops anchor in the relationship with Cleopatra Highbourne — the 'song of the ocean' meeting 'a salty piece of land' — so that escape is redeemed by home, boundary-crossing, and self-reflection with culturally different others.

kant-perpetual-peace.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
kant-perpetual-peace.title: 7 Should Wakanda Take Over the World The Ethics of International Power
kant-perpetual-peace.relation: Littmann asks whether Wakanda should take over the world, staging N'Jobu's and Killmonger's 'Wakanda could rule them all... the right way' plan against the history of benevolently justified empire: Roman civilization of barbarians, Kipling's white man's burden, and Mill's trusteeship argument for educating non-Europeans toward democracy. Plato's Republic case for rule by the wisest initially favors Wakandan conquest, but Kant's Perpetual Peace condemnation of conquering 'European savages,' Mill's own four reasons imperial rule goes wrong (ignorance of local conditions, lack of sympathy, partiality, exploitation), and Diderot's claim that distance from home erodes moral restraint convince him domination breeds abuse; he endorses Nakia's aid-and-refuge outreach and Mill's hope that the 'aristocracy of nationality' will one day look as wrong as racism.

kant-perpetual-peace.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
kant-perpetual-peace.title: 4. How Anthony Bourdain United the Local and the Universal
kant-perpetual-peace.relation: Barta and Miranda contrast Kant's 'universally communicable' taste with Bourdieu's view that taste is a social construct shaped by field, habitus, and cultural capital that reinforces class distinctions. Using Bourdain's episodes (Portuguese bacalao, New York hot dogs, the French Laundry), they argue he synthesizes both: acknowledging taste's locality while democratizing it as a cosmopolitan 'citizen of the world' in the tradition of Diogenes and Kant's perpetual peace.

vindication-women.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
vindication-women.title: “Happily Ever After, Now and Then”
vindication-women.relation: Erin McKenna explains how a feminist can love Buffett by reading 'Fins' and 'Why Don't We Get Drunk (and Screw)' as critiques of predatory land sharks rather than endorsements, and 'Margaritaville' as a man admitting 'it's my own damn fault.' Against Rousseau's pliable helpmate ideal of woman she sets Wollstonecraft's Vindication — equal education and personhood for women — and Charlotte Perkins Gilman's pragmatist-feminist case that women's economic, physical, and mental dependence stunts everyone. Buffett's novels then pass the Gilman test: Desdemona, Trevor Kane, Cleopatra Highbourne, and Sophie are smart, independent women, and the male leads must reform their habits to earn them, aiming at Desdemona's 'happily ever after, now and then' instead of the fairy-tale ending.

vindication-women.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
vindication-women.title: Conclusion Whatever I Goddamn Like
vindication-women.relation: S. W. Sondheimer argues that Avasarala's election loss to Nancy Gao is explained not by competence but by millennia of gender expectations. She excavates the lineage: Aristotle's form/matter hierarchy ('matter yearns for form as the female for the male', women as incomplete 'deformed males' with 'fewer teeth') used to bar women from politics, Hume's portrait of women as near-livestock incapable of the sublime, and Romantic-era bodily confinement — mapping each onto Avasarala's staff recasting her as a 'nurturing, caring family matriarch', her forced public apology for the failed Inaros boarding raid that a male commander like Errinwright would never have had to make, and Arjun seizing control of the narrative of their son Charanpal's death. Closing the loop with the 2016 US election (Clinton versus Trump), the chapter argues that even in 2350 voters punish the 'nasty woman' and reward the comfortable mold Gao fits, and demands we 'dig this garbage philosophy out of our shared consciousness and set it on fire.'

vindication-women.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
vindication-women.title: Notes
vindication-women.relation: Gutwald takes seven-year-old Charlotte Benjamin's viral letter ('all the girls did was sit at home, go to the beach, and shop... but the boys went on adventures, worked, saved people') to argue the LEGO Friends theme is Wollstonecraftian 'friendly sexism' — revering girls as pretty play-things in a house-bound Heartlake City rather than oppressing them outright. Following Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes a woman' and her point that men describe the world from their own perspective, plus Mill's Subjection of Women observation that argument alone cannot beat a 'mass of feeling', she explains how pinkified toy segregation feeds implicit bias, schemas, and stereotype threat in both girls and boys. Her fix is structural: make Friends bricks and mini-dolls compatible with the rest of the system ('Let the Friends go to Space!') and return to the gender-neutral 1981 'What it is is beautiful' ad.

vindication-women.title: Heteronormative horrors
vindication-women.relation: Reading virgins and the vagina dentata as the dyad through which horror polices female sexuality, the chapter uses Irigaray's account of the virgin as prop to male subjectivity and Creed's femme castratrice to analyse Halloween's 'Final Girl', Teeth's toothed-vagina revenge on abstinence-only purity culture, Jennifer's Body and Haute Tension. It closes with Rich's 'compulsory heterosexuality' and Wittig's 'heterosexual contract' to argue horror naturalises heteronormativity by casting female sexuality as either contained (virgin) or monstrously open (vagina dentata).

vindication-women.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
vindication-women.relation: Winkle reads Sense and Sensibility as steering a 'middle road' between cold rational calculation and sentimental self-indulgence, and casts Austen as proto-feminist. She uses Wollstonecraft's Vindication to explain why Austen's silly wives (Mrs. Bennet, Lucy Steele) are products of a deficient female education that trains women to please rather than reason. She then reads Elinor Dashwood's measured love for Edward, and Marianne's near-fatal collapse over Willoughby, through bell hooks's claim that 'falling in love' surrenders agency, arguing Elinor chooses love as an act of will while Marianne must learn sense before finding lasting love with Colonel Brandon.

vindication-women.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
vindication-women.relation: Dashwood examines women owning property in Austen, arguing the 'great ladies' (Lady Catherine, Mrs. Ferrars, Lady Denham) are drawn as despotic, avaricious, and negligent managers not because they are women but because a deficient female education left them unfit, echoing Wollstonecraft's Vindication that female failings are constructed by upbringing. She contrasts them with propertyless heroines who show the reason and moral principle to manage estates well.
