Emma is the pivotal case: as the one female proprietor at a novel's center, she risks becoming a tyrannical great lady but, guided by her superior education and Knightley's example at Donwell, develops the social conscience needed for ethical ownership.

wheel-of-fortune.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
wheel-of-fortune.title: “Livin’ and Dyin’ in Three-Quarter Time”
wheel-of-fortune.relation: Randall Auxier uses Buffett's catalog to think about fortune and fate, reading Buffett's bold career moves (walking out on Nashville for the beach, later annexing it via 'It's Five o'Clock Somewhere') through Machiavelli's advice to marry Fortuna and master her tricks with virtù. Against Aristotle's demanding answer that only aretē, moral excellence, defends happiness against bad luck, he takes Vico's middle path: natural causes, moral causes, and the occasions of fortune are gathered under providence, so Buffett's seaplane crash ('God, Buddha, St. Christopher, my guardian angel... luck, and the United States Navy water-survival training') shows any fate can be turned to good ends for others. Sorting Buffett's songs into places, times, meetings, sentiments, and thoughts — the key sentiment being the wistful — the chapter lands on contentment as gratitude: being 'livin' and dyin' in three-quarter time.'

wheel-of-fortune.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
wheel-of-fortune.title: The Devil and Philosophy
wheel-of-fortune.relation: Ray Bossert reads Tolkien's Silmarillion through Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy: elves, being artists, understand Melkor not as tempter but as bad artist, from his rebellious solo in the Music of the Ainur to his botched sub-creations - orcs bred from kidnapped elves - and his covetous collecting of the silmarils. Boethius supplies the machinery: evil seeks a good by unnatural means and only approximates it, wickedness debases its practitioner into a beast, God's foreknowledge embraces free choices without causing them, and Providence is a spinning disc at whose center alone one is steady - so Melkor's rebellion leaves him less free, dragged around the rim. Tolkien's contrast between art (for beauty) and magic (for control) explains why the Devil can only mimic creation, never make anything real.

wheel-of-fortune.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
wheel-of-fortune.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
wheel-of-fortune.relation: George Dunn tests Katniss's luck-saturated life against Kant's claim that the good will shines 'like a jewel' regardless of fortune, with Peeta's vow to 'die as myself' as the stronghold the Gamemakers cannot touch, and with Seneca's dictum that what Fortune has not given she cannot take away. He then runs Nagel's four kinds of moral luck through the trilogy: Haymitch's reaping-made alcoholism as constitutive luck, Rue's death sparing Katniss an impossible final choice as circumstantial luck, Peeta's rooftop words echoing unconsciously behind the flowers for Rue as causal luck, and the revolution's success as resultant luck without which Katniss would have been the destroyer of District 12 rather than its torchbearer. Framing the Gamemakers as Fortuna on her wheel, he ends with the berries: since Katniss can never untangle whether she held them out from love, defiance, or self-protection, even moral worth proves hostage to luck and to the opacity of our own motives.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
aristotle-potentiality.title: Transformers and Philosophy
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Spicher argues that when Bumblebee trades his beat-up 1976 Camaro for a shiny 2007 model only his appearance changes (an accidental change), never his identity, because transforming is part of a Transformer's essence like a human wearing a mask. Locke's memory continuity and Thomson's bodily criterion each fail - the embryo, coma, and corpse problems, plus the thought experiment of Megatron's memories transplanted into another body - so he defends an Aristotelian composite of form and matter in which the Spark is the soul-like form organizing the machine body, preserving identity through transformation as form guides matter toward actuality.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
aristotle-potentiality.title: The Aftermath of Tragedy
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Argues that Grave of the Fireflies works as a critique of anime's child-hero convention: Seita acts exactly like a plucky anime protagonist when he defies his not-actually-evil aunt, strikes out on his own with Setsuko, ignores the farmer's advice to apologize and return, and demands a quick fix from the doctor — but these 'heroic' choices kill them both, because he lacks the developed capacity to reason. Against the medieval 'child as little adult' picture that most anime (Dragon Ball, Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!) romanticizes, the chapter deploys Aristotle's view of children as unfinished beings who cannot yet reason or achieve happiness, concluding the film is a cautionary tale about the years of nurture and guidance real children need.

aristotle-potentiality.title: UNSC Briefing
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Fred Van Lente's introduction argues that Master Chief is deliberately an empty shell—faceless, ageless, mostly silent—so the player's identity grafted onto him brings both to life at once in Halo: Combat Evolved's opening cryo-wakeup tutorial. He frames the book with Thoreau's Walden claim that philosophy is living simplicity, mapping it onto the Chief's ascetic soldier existence, and on Socrates: a game worth playing is worth examining, since the unexamined game is not worth playing. He closes with Aristotle's potentiality and actuality: the game actualizes the Chief as a kicker of alien ass, and the book actualizes the series' social and philosophical potential.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
aristotle-potentiality.title: You’re Fantastic!
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Viguié's Serial 2 preface argues the show's ultimate philosophy is 'you're fantastic': the Doctor takes people yearning for something more—Rose the shop girl becoming Bad Wolf, Rory becoming the Last Centurion, Donna the temp becoming in a way the Doctor herself—and actualizes potential they never believed they had. He applies the lesson to his own life, describing how the show's belief in untapped human potential pushed him from a soul-sucking job to creating his Doctor Geek's Laboratory STEM-outreach audio show and Science Fair, urging readers to answer the Doctor's call and live up to what the Fourth Doctor called our 'inventive, invincible, indomitable' species' promise.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
aristotle-potentiality.title: 6. The Psychiatrist as Sociopathic God
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Hassert takes Lecter's 'First principles, Clarice' at its Aristotelian word - nature is revealed through capacities and action, as an acorn's telos is not pumpkins and a kitten will never be a Great Dane - to explain Lecter's psychiatry: he reads each patient's essence and potential, prescribing Mason Verger's face-peeling so appearance finally matches essence, and force-raising Will toward equality so that Aristotelian perfect friendship between the alike-in-virtue (which Franklyn's flattery can never reach) might become possible. Reading God through Augustine's account of evil as the destruction of a preexisting good and Mischa's murder, the chapter argues that Lecter emulates a capricious deity - 'Typhoid and swans - it all comes from the same place' - and, unlike Nietzsche, does not pronounce God dead but merely misconceptualized, while his friendships fail because he must corrupt the other into his own image rather than love an equal.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
aristotle-potentiality.title: 14. The End of Inigo Montoya
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Elsby and Luzecky read Inigo through Aristotle's doctrine of the four causes: his life is organized by a final cause, revenge on the Six-Fingered Man as the thing that is 'just good', which explains every action from fencing drills to eating breakfast. The famous mantra works because habit embodies the final cause - repeating 'My name is Inigo Montoya' lets trained movement carry him through wounds that should end the fight. When revenge is achieved the chain of ends terminates and 'Inigo Montoya' ends with it, which is why his rebirth as the Dread Pirate Roberts is needed; the chapter generalizes that our habits, not grand outside purposes, are how final causes give lives their ends.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
aristotle-potentiality.title: 9. What Fuckin’ Chance Does a Kid Have
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Joseph Westfall argues that Louis's parent-hating bits - the baby he doesn't know who 'might fuckin' hate Jews,' the four-year-old 'asshole,' 'I love her, but I wish she was never born' - voice the real ambivalence of parenthood while showing that children are developmentally incapable of responsibility, so parents must not blame kids for being kids. He contrasts Louis's unknowable, selfish infant with Augustine's doctrine that unbaptized babies are simply evil, and reads Louis's parenting maxim - 'you're not raising the kid in front of you, you're raising the grownup they're going to be' - through childhood as a state of becoming: Jizzanthapuss is on the road to Hitler thanks to his weak mother, and Louie berating little Jane realizes 'I'm her first asshole,' shaping the men she will later attract. Good parenting is keeping kids alive plus forming the future adult, which is why Louis denies his daughters cell phones (they prevent learning empathy face-to-face) and puts his daughter on the smelly city bus while his Mercedes waits.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
aristotle-potentiality.title: 5. Other People’s Body Parts
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Explains Kyle Spencer's horror at the body Madison and Zoe assembled from other people's parts through the history of soul-body theories: Aristotle's De Anima account of the soul as the faculties of a living body (plus the Physiognomonics claim that small people have small minds - poor Ma Petite), Plato's Timaeus on body parts designed for philosophy and reincarnation into bodies fitted to one's vices, Avicenna's soul as a faculty-binding nexus that chooses its bodily vehicle like a vehicle serves its owner, and Merleau-Ponty's habitual body (the Axeman's axe as part of his body, phantom limbs), which best explains why walking around on someone else's legs 'has got to mess with you a little'.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
aristotle-potentiality.title: Where Do We Go from Here
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Argues on Aristotelian–Thomist grounds that WALL-E and EVE cannot truly be intelligent: they are artificial because their formal cause lies outside them in the Buy n Large engineers' minds, whereas natural things like the captain, the cockroach, and the plant have intrinsic formal causes. Intelligence is the act of an intellectual soul — the formal cause of a living thing — so machines at best mimic WALL-E's grasp of spoon-ness, fork-ness, and spork-ness, as Kreeft's comparison of a computer to a library building that does not understand its books makes clear. The conclusion is that AI is qualitatively, not merely technologically, impossible, and Pixar's live-action cinematography is precisely what tricks us into taking the robots as real.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
aristotle-potentiality.title: How Revealing Are Our Abilities
aristotle-potentiality.relation: The chapter analyzes ability as a 'fuzzy concept': abilities are powers or capacities that come in degrees and vary with circumstance, like speaking seventy versus three hundred words of Mermish or conjuring a chipmunk Patronus only when relaxed. Choices, by contrast, are definite acts, Pettigrew's betrayal of Harry's parents and Harry's breakup with Ginny to protect her admit of no question, and this act-versus-capacity contrast explains why choices are the clearer self-revealers.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
aristotle-potentiality.title: The Office and Philosophy
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Nys uses Brent's quiz grievance about Mr. Spock (half-Vulcan, half-human) and his Crufts pedigree-dog analogy, Gareth's 'look at the ears' classification test, the dwarf/midget/elf/pixie interrogation of Alex, and Tim and Dawn's 'lethal blow' prank to introduce the problem of natural kinds. Realist answers come from Kripke (water is H2O whatever we call it), Aristotle's matter-and-form essences, and the DNA evidence separating Bornean clouded leopards from mainland cousins, while Wittgenstein's language games and Quine's point that our innate similarity senses mislead support the constructivist that we lay classification on an unstructured world. The verdict: nature supplies real differences but never carves itself into kinds, and the line-drawing remains up to us.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
aristotle-potentiality.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Foresman and Tobienne deploy Aristotle's apparatus of essence and accident, the ten categories, and actuality versus potentiality to define the monster and explain the show's appeal. They test candidates against canon: whether hunting is essential or accidental to Sam after Azazel's kills, what John Winchester in 'Dead Man's Blood' treats as essential to vampire substance, and Madison's transformation in 'Heart' from actual human and potential werewolf into actual monster, concluding that monstrosity lies in thought and action rather than appearance, as the human-hunting but human Benders confirm. Tracing 'monster' to the Latin monstrum, a sign or omen, they argue monsters are monsters only through their relation to human self-importance, so our 'speciesist' prejudice is exactly why we love watching them hunted, and why we love Supernatural.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
aristotle-potentiality.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Greeley argues the zombie embodies a specifically modern fear of losing our humanity: walkers are persons stripped of the potential Aristotle and Aquinas made the measure of human worth, which is why Rick uniquely eulogizes the walkers he puts down ('I'm sorry this happened to you'). Following Aries, he traces modern death anxiety to the split of faith from reason and reads the CDC arc ('TS-19') as science offering only a self-destruct quick death where Jacqui's 'wrath of God' guess at least offers meaning. Rousseau's claim that civilization corrupts explains the survivors' return to the woods, where pizza-deliverer Glenn's heroics and the 'kingpin' Guillermo protecting nursing-home patients show the apocalypse can bring out the best in us while the Bradbury's Sale storefront and trampled Walmart worker hint we were already the walking dead.

aristotle-potentiality.title: 7. The Art of Playing Along with Dancing Little People
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Luzecky and Elsby argue that Twin Peaks is genuine art because, against Plato's condemnation of mimetic art as confusing copies to be exiled, it fulfills Aristotle's Poetics: art's essential function is dramatic reversal, surprising and transfixing us (Dougie's absurd casino win, the dancing Man from Another Place). Drawing on Gadamer's 'Spiel' (play/game) and Ingarden's schematized, incomplete artworks, they contend the work of art exists only as an ongoing rhythmic 'to and fro' between image and viewer—so we complete the Red Room scene by participating in it, moving it from potentiality to actuality.

aristotle-potentiality.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
aristotle-potentiality.title: 93. Asterios Polyp as Philosophy Master of Two Worlds
aristotle-potentiality.relation: Richards reads Mazzucchelli's Asterios Polyp as a visual meditation on universals versus particulars and the abstract versus concrete, using its CMYK color coding and character styles (Asterios as cool geometric solids, Hana as warm crosshatching) to stage Plato's two worlds. Asterios, a 'paper architect' living in perfect uninstantiated abstraction, undergoes an inverted Hero's Journey (Campbell's monomyth) down into the concrete world—building an actual treehouse, telling the Ise shrine story—to become 'master of two worlds,' reconciling Form and matter, universal and particular, and accepting impermanence just as an asteroid closes on Earth.

philosophy-of-play.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
philosophy-of-play.title: Sin, Play, and the “Synagogues of Satan”
philosophy-of-play.relation: Rachael Sotos argues the Report performs Platonic play: like the divine puppet of Plato's Laws with its competing cords, Colbert reveals what moves us (fear, hope, the ThreatDown bears, the 'golden cord' of the good) and so teaches freedom through play. Colbert's pompous self-authority - claiming to be 'the canon and measure' of virtue in I Am America - parodies Aristotle's serious man (spoudaios, megalopsychos) and the sophists Protagoras and Prodicus with their Orpheus voices, proving Heraclitus right that 'time is a child at play' and Aristotle wrong that play is mere medicinal rest. Tracking the war on fun from Chrysostom through Aquinas's eutrapelia (there is sin in a lack of play) to Erasmus's Praise of Folly and the Puritans' ban on theaters as 'Synagogues of Satan,' she reads Colbert's playing-at-sin - the man-seed eugenics bit, the 'black friend' boasts, the Ellen DeGeneres Paradox on Wikiality - as Erasmian folly that heals America's Puritan hangover in the culture wars.

philosophy-of-play.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
philosophy-of-play.title: 4 - With Friends Like These, Who Needs Enemies
philosophy-of-play.relation: Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch, Mafia Wars) through Goffman's 'face' and Brown and Levinson's positive/negative politeness: recruiting friends into an application is a face-threatening imposition that becomes awkward across professor-student and parent-child hierarchies playing as nominal equals. She invokes Derrida on Mauss - 'there is no gift without bond, without bind' - to analyze the reciprocity obligations of gifting games, and finds emergent cooperative norms like PackRat pacts against tit-for-tat stealing. Players revolt when developers monetize asymmetrical play, showing communities negotiate the rules of the magic circle.

philosophy-of-play.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
philosophy-of-play.title: 8 - Playing Around with Identity
philosophy-of-play.relation: Wandel and Beavers take Groundhog Day's Phil Connors as the model of trying on selves, and apply Goffman's dramaturgical Presentation of Self to see Facebook as a stage where users experiment with identity. Because friends from every part of life watch at once, a 'restraint of accountability' disciplines pretending, much like childhood pretend play or a fraternity's teasing calls members to account for their oddities. Against critics who see fragmentation and narcissism, they argue this dynamic can support becoming who one already is - a more authentic, grounded self - closing with Plato's 'Life must be lived as play'.

philosophy-of-play.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
philosophy-of-play.title: Football as Part of Real Life
philosophy-of-play.relation: Hoyningen-Huene asks why anyone cheers a ball crossing an arbitrarily defined line and answers with his thesis that football re-enacts the drama of life: an unpredictable, fractal mixture of ability and chance—from a bobbling pitch to Manchester United's 1999 injury-time comeback and Maradona's unpunished Hand of God—mirroring the luck, skill, and irreversible injustice of real life. He analyzes the Laws of the Game as having four functions: guaranteeing equal conditions, generating analogies to life's drama, ending the drama at a knowable moment (unlike life's open-ended conflicts), and keeping the game safely distanced from real seriousness, which is why he reads hooligans as people who cognitively mistake the game's drama for a real-life fight. Finally he argues that money, careers, betting, and even the political channeling of Hungary's 1954 World Cup defeat into the 1956 uprising are secondary entanglements parasitic on a primary fascination already present in a nameless village-league match, which no other sport matches in variability of the ability–chance mixture.

philosophy-of-play.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
philosophy-of-play.title: a12.xhtml
philosophy-of-play.relation: O'Hara argues that play is what makes hobbits - and us - fully human: Bilbo's childhood games of throwing stones, riddles and smoke-rings turn out to be training for the quest (his stone-throwing fells the spiders, his riddle-practice buys time with Gollum), and even Gollum's riddle-game makes him momentarily 'less a monster and more a person'. Following Schiller's and Huizinga's Homo ludens thesis that play completes humanity, he distinguishes play from idleness (Aquinas held recreation continues in heaven; Peirce called play 'vigorous exercise'), places leisure among the goods of Aristotle's 'we play in order to be serious', and contrasts Gandalf's beauty-directed fireworks with the orcs' merely useful explosions and work-chants. But play has limits: Kant warns against treating persons as toys, and Bilbo's lesson is 'Never laugh at live dragons!'

philosophy-of-play.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
philosophy-of-play.title: “We’re Not Worthy”
philosophy-of-play.relation: Holt reads Wayne's World as applied philosophy of play: Wayne and Garth's basement show is intrinsically motivated leisure in Huizinga's sense, free, rule-bound, absorbing, and outside ordinary life, and Russell's 'In Praise of Idleness' supplies the play ethic against the work ethic. Against Wittgenstein's claim that games cannot be defined, Suits's definition of games as the voluntary attempt to overcome unnecessary obstacles is applied to 'A-sphincter-says-what?', the '...not!' game, and one-on-one hockey with Gretzky. The dark side of play closes the chapter: Wayne and Garth exclude and mock outsiders, and the leisure of their magic circle rests on unacknowledged labor like Wayne's mom's laundry.

philosophy-of-play.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
philosophy-of-play.title: First Hole Golf and the Importance of Play
philosophy-of-play.relation: Al Gini defends play as intrinsically valuable and essential to being human, drawing on Huizinga's three criteria of 'true play' and William James's ideal of the amateur who plays 'for the love of it.' Using his golf-obsessed father as an extended case, he shows how golf functions as a self-contained, absorbing 'refuge from ordinary life' that delivers completion, coordination, and cooperation, echoing Plato's claim in the Republic and Laws that sport forms both person and community. The chapter treats golf as an end in itself whose joy sustains a flourishing life rather than as a means to external reward.

ontology-of-fiction.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
ontology-of-fiction.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
ontology-of-fiction.relation: Mackey tracks the ontological migrations of Lyra, Pantalaimon, and the alethiometer from black marks on a page into the Listening Library audiobook with fixed voices, the National Theatre's puppet dæmons whose black-clad puppeteer stunningly turns out to speak as Lyra's death, the film's computer-graphic Pan with its explanatory opening voice-over, the dæmon-assignment website, a videogame that reduces Pan's shape-shifting to four player-chosen forms, and a Tonner collectible doll with a resin Pantalaimon. She asks whether 'reinforced fiction' supported by extratextual evidence (publisher websites, playbill portraits supposedly showing historical dæmons) makes stories feel more real, and what essential qualities make each embodied version still count as Lyra or Pan. Her conclusion is a research program: understanding how readers conjure fictional beings 'out of all air and thought' across media would be a giant step toward understanding the intricacies of the human mind.

ontology-of-fiction.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
ontology-of-fiction.title: 13. The Essence of Dogbert
ontology-of-fiction.relation: Knuths asks whether Dogbert is essentially a dog and only accidentally white, importing Aristotle's Metaphysics distinction between essential and accidental properties and its modern modal gloss: essences are what an object has in all possible worlds, with David Lewis's concrete-constructionist reading noted against the standard view of worlds as abstract sets of propositions. The puzzle is that Dogbert's 2014 stint as CEO, combined with his canine essence, would prove dogs can be CEOs, threatening absurd conclusions about the real world unless we choose an ontology of fiction. Three candidates are weighed without a verdict: possibilism (Adams discovered a possible world), Meinongianism (Dogbert has being without existence, at the cost of square circles), and creationism (Dogbert is Adams's abstract artifact, troubled by the Not-Adams duplicate-creator case).

ontology-of-fiction.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
ontology-of-fiction.title: “Master Skywalker. There Are Too Many of Them. What Are We Going to Do ”
ontology-of-fiction.relation: Cook and Kellen ask what makes the Luke of A New Hope the same fictional character as the Luke of The Last Jedi, the Thrawn Trilogy, or fan fiction like Old Man Luke. They reject sameness of name, Leibniz's identity of indiscernibles (Luke_ANH lacks Luke_TLJ's internal properties such as being a jaded Jedi Master), and the authorial say-so account of Routley and Thomasson, which by transitivity forces the contradiction that Zahn's married, child-having Luke is identical to the Last Jedi recluse who never met Mara Jade. They defend a 'Perspectival Account' on which identity claims are true or false only relative to the story from which we interpret them, so each viewing of A New Hope shows innumerably many distinct yet connected Lukes - 'ontological excess' spanning canon, Legends, Infinities, and the Muppet Show.

ontology-of-fiction.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
ontology-of-fiction.title: Worlds within Words
ontology-of-fiction.relation: Tomkinson uses Frege's sense/reference distinction (the morning star and the evening star) to ask what Sapkowski's proper names mean and pick out: Zireael ('swallow') tying Ciri to the Tower of the Swallow, Ciri's defiant adoption of 'Falka' as nom de guerre, and Regis's mule named 'Dracul' pointing both to the beast and to Count Dracula. She traces the Elder Speech's Celtic sound to Tolkien's glossopoeia and Le Guin's Earthsea true names, and reads place names like Cintra (the 1808 Convention of Cintra) as political allusions to partitioned Poland caught between empires. The chapter closes on whether fictional names like 'the Witcher' - the novels, Henry Cavill, Liam Hemsworth - have referents at all, invoking Russell's 'non-entities' and speculating that Ciri's portals and the Conjunction make the alluded worlds part of the Witcherverse itself.

ontology-of-fiction.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
ontology-of-fiction.title: IX - WHEN YOU KNOW YOU’RE JUST A COMIC BOOK CHARACTER DEADPOOL
ontology-of-fiction.relation: Darowski argues Deadpool's defining quirk, knowing he is a comic book character, is postmodern metafiction put to ontological work. Moments like 'Five tooth brushings and a scene change later...,' narration the Great Lakes Avengers can hear aloud, and jokes about writers Kelley, Priest, and Nicieza force readers to see their own role in closure between panels and in the collaborative production of the story. Like Plato's cave dweller who has escaped to true reality, Deadpool knows his world is 'all his imagination,' and the reader, unlike the characters who call him insane, shares the knowledge that creators and readers together fabricate the fictional reality.

ontology-of-fiction.title: Twin Peaks, Noir, and Open Interpretation
ontology-of-fiction.relation: Jason Holt catalogs Twin Peaks' noir elements (the Laura Palmer quest narrative, Cooper's voiceover Dictaphone, femmes fatales, low-key lighting, the existential mood leavened by absurd humor in the manner of Camus) but argues the series is merely noirish, not noir, because it refuses noir's hard-boiled naturalistic metaphysics. The decisive case is BOB: the post-Leland dialogue between Cooper, Truman, and Albert stages the choice between reducing BOB to Leland's psychopathology and reifying him as a real malevolent spirit from the Black Lodge, and the show deliberately leaves the fictional ontology of BOB undecidable, in Todorov's 'fantastic' between the natural and supernatural. This interpretive openness (compared to The Prisoner's Number 1 revelation and the psychological indeterminacy of Sam Spade's motives in The Maltese Falcon) is defended as aesthetically desirable via Holt's 'omissive' aesthetic, the art of leaving important things out.

rhizome.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
rhizome.title: As We Wind on Down the Road
rhizome.relation: Randall Auxier develops a theory, drawn from Ernst Cassirer's work on myth and magic, that distinguishes magic (the generalizing of will so that past, present, and future connect through symbols and co-operating forces) from myth (the consciousness that experiences the world as wills and archetypal symbols). Page embodies the magical path—the zone musicians enter where playing exceeds conscious control, the Faustian need to master it that led him to Crowley, and the risk of being drained (Page in 1977)—while Plant embodies myth, supplying archetypal lyrics ('The Battle of Evermore', 'Kashmir', 'Stairway' as 'a song of hope') and the Welsh pastoral. Zeppelin's blues borrowing is re-enactment rather than repetition, a rhizome-like reinvention of old roots, and the four unpronounceable symbols of the fourth album are genuine creations: symbols that store concentrated will for the future.

rhizome.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
rhizome.title: 16. The Truth about the Walkers
rhizome.relation: Kempner reads the show's serial bait-and-switch over the walkers' origin - Jenner's failed CDC, Eugene's exposed lie on the road to Washington - as an enactment of Deleuze and Guattari's multiplicity against "the reduction to the ONE." Their anti-Oedipal attack on Freud, who fixed the Wolfman's dream to a single castrating father, mirrors how characters who hunt one knowable cause (Rick's hope of CDC rescue, Hershel's barn of curable walkers, Abraham's mission) are punished with death, while Michonne survives precisely by accepting walkers as an irreducible pack rather than something to be understood. The chapter concludes the series should never explain the walkers: multiple causes and small-t truths replace any single Truth, which is why relief never arrives and survival means living with unknowability.

rhizome.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
rhizome.title: 8. Playing with Glitter
rhizome.relation: This chapter argues that play is Drag Race's deep structure, developed through three philosophers. Wittgenstein's language games explain the show's word-play: 'realness' subverts its own reference to mean the iconic fake, 'herstory' is history played with from a queer perspective, and lip syncs are rule-following whose rules only exist in application. Gadamer's account of play with 'a life of its own' — requiring willingness and openness to the Other — explains why half-hearted players lose, from Porkchop and Tammie's mouthed-nothing lip sync to Gia Gunn and Trixie breaking character in Snatch Game, and why the Evil Twins and makeover challenges are designed to force queens to open up. Deleuze's rhizome (with Bakhtin's carnivalesque) grounds the claim that drag decentering the human — Lil' Poundcake, dragged pancakes, Sharon Needles — and the finale's carnival dissolve the official binaries of male/female and good/bad.

rhizome.title: Wholly Communion Poetry, Philosophy, and Spontaneous Bop Cinema
rhizome.relation: Sterritt reads Peter Whitehead's 1965 film 'Wholly Communion,' shot at London's International Poetry Incarnation, as 'spontaneous bop cinema' embodying Beat poetics through Bakhtin's dialogic/carnivalesque and the schizoanalysis of Deleuze and Guattari. Ginsberg's drunken recitation of 'The Change' becomes a 'body without organs' entering the 'chaosmos' on the plane of immanence; Jandl's sound poetry is pure Deleuzian sensation. Adrian Mitchell's anti-Vietnam 'To Whom It May Concern' is read through Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati and Deleuze's 'difference in repetition,' its incantatory counter-words a materialist line of flight against the order-words of war.

rhizome.title: From Sherlock Holmes to the Hard-Boiled Detective in Film Noir
rhizome.relation: Jerold Abrams argues that the noir detective inherits the Holmes/Dupin detective logic but inhabits a fundamentally different maze. Using Eco's three labyrinths, he maps the classical Greek maze (with faith as Ariadne's string) and the mannerist maze (with Cartesian/Kantian pure reason) onto the escapable world of classic detection, and the Deleuzian rhizomatic maze, born after Nietzsche dissolved reason into will to power, onto noir's inescapable world (The Third Man, Kiss Me Deadly, The Maltese Falcon's fake statue). He shows both detectives use Peircean abduction (the logic of guessing) rather than pure deduction, illustrating it with knife-wound examples and Calloway's trapdoor inference in The Third Man, while the noir femme fatale becomes the anti-Ariadne whose thread of clues leads only to the hangman's rope.

rhizome.title: Gynaehorror as convention and challenge
rhizome.relation: This introductory chapter defines 'gynaehorror' as horror rooted in women's reproductive bodies (menstruation, virginity, pregnancy, motherhood, menopause), reading films like Inside, Vigil, Teeth, Alien, The Brood and Rosemary's Baby through it. It leverages Deleuze and Guattari's rhizome/becoming to reframe the monstrous female body not as a fixed molar 'being' but as a productive, boundary-breaching 'becoming', while positioning woman as the abject Other against which the male subject defines himself. It argues horror is simultaneously conservative (punishing women) and potentially radical.

rhizome.title: Brave new worlds cyborg futures and female subjectivity
rhizome.relation: Examining 'reproductive technohorror' from Shelley's Frankenstein through Splice, The Unborn and The Machine, the chapter argues these films code science as masculine domination of feminised nature (via Bordo's Cartesian masculinisation and Merchant's Bacon) and eliminate the female body altogether so man can create life without woman. It contrasts this with Haraway's post-gender cyborg and Braidotti's Deleuzean metal-morphoses, using becoming-woman and the rhizome to imagine reproductive difference as productive rather than as the erasable 'female problem'.

rhizome.title: The ageing woman as (American) horror story
rhizome.relation: The chapter theorises the 'abject barren body' — the menstruating, menopausal and post-menopausal woman — connecting menarche as an upswell of feminine power (Carrie's telekinesis, Ginger Snaps, The Witch's Thomasin) to menopause's cultural construction as loss and 'living decay'. Drawing on Mary Douglas and Kristeva on pollution and abjection, and on Deleuze and Guattari's 'becoming-woman' and bodies defined by capacities rather than fixed being, it argues that the female reproductive body is more often barren than fecund and that this state is another generative modality, not an absence. It reads the Western biomedical pathologisation of menopause (Wilson's Feminine Forever, HRT) as a Foucauldian disciplinary discourse, then tracks older women through Sunset Boulevard's Norma Desmond, the hagsploitation cycle (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?, Strait-Jacket, Hush Hush Sweet Charlotte), and The Taking of Deborah Logan, concluding that Jessica Lange's American Horror Story roles offer the fullest, sexually frank rebuttal to the abjection and invisibility of the ageing woman.

rhizome.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
rhizome.relation: Sterritt reads Manhunter's Hannibal Lecktor as a perverse image of Nietzsche's Übermensch: hedonistic, ascetic, and expressing an overwhelming will to power, exercising superhuman self-control (his pulse never exceeding eighty-five while mutilating a nurse). Using Deleuze and Guattari's 'becoming' and the body without organs, he contrasts the genuinely self-transforming Lecktor (a 'schizovivisectionist') with Dollarhyde, whose bogus becoming—trapped in Blake's 'mind-forg'd manacles' and the Red Dragon—makes him a pathetic tooth fairy rather than an overman, aligning both killers with Kierkegaard's demonic individual who stands above the universal.

rhizome.title: The Philosophy of Michael Mann
rhizome.relation: Ritzer argues Mann's aesthetics of horror in The Keep and Manhunter is an aestheticization of horror—the frightening transformed into the beautiful through mise-en-scène, color, and montage. Against Hegel's Lectures on Fine Art, which bans the purely negative and horrific from aesthetics, Ritzer marshals Schiller, De Quincey, and Auden to split the ethical from the aesthetic: Dollarhyde stages corpses as artworks and Graham reads crime scenes as an art critic. The Keep pushes further into Barthes's 'obtuse meaning' and Deleuze and Guattari's 'planes of immanence,' its stylized images referring to nothing but themselves—horror filmed solely for horror's sake.

rhizome.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
rhizome.relation: Sterritt 'schizoanalyzes' The Informant! by arguing that its lying protagonist Mark Whitacre, an ADM executive turned FBI informant, is a nut psychoanalysis cannot crack because he has no unconscious depth: his self is Deleuze and Guattari's rhizomatic, depthless flow of desire with 'nothing behind it' (echoing Warhol). He reads Mark's compulsive fabrication as deterritorialization against the corporation-as-psychopath, links the film to the Socratic unexamined life and to William James's open, flux-embracing empiricism (via Cassavetes), and interprets the climactic collision of Mark's voiceover and dialogue as the film itself intervening as the ultimate informant.

rhizome.title: War and Representation
rhizome.relation: Jameson contends that war poses the 'nominalist dilemma'—the gap between abstract totality and sensory immediacy—making it ultimately unrepresentable, and enumerates eight recurring narrative situations (existential, collective, leaders, technology, landscape, atrocity, homeland attack, occupation). Using Burke's dramatistic pentad he argues the war narrative drifts from 'act/agent' toward 'scene,' where the anthropomorphic dissolves; Sartre's 'groups-in-fusion' and Deleuze's nomadic war machine model the collective buddy-squad, whose division of labor he compares to the heist film. Reading Grimmelshausen's Simplicissimus and Döblin's Wallenstein against Kluge's Stalingrad and Halberstadt collages, he shows war (from the Thirty Years' War to WWII aerial bombing) generating a rhizomatic, nonnarrative flow that defeats stable narrative convention.

rhizome.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
rhizome.title: 7. History as Creativity
rhizome.relation: Magomedov reads the Seldon Plan as an 'artificial teleology' imposed on a history that is intrinsically open and contingent: because psychohistory yields only probabilities (Trantor's 92.5 percent, never 100), every Seldon Crisis leaves an infinitesimal gap through which an alternate future can break. Against Aristotelian and Hegelian teleology, he uses Deleuze and Guattari's concepts of territorialization and deterritorialization, plus Nietzsche's idea that a thing's essence is fixed by the forces that seize it, to argue that resolving a crisis requires creativity, and Hardin's inventive balance-of-power solution versus Sermak's stagnant 'attack first' shows Seldon's will surviving only where a force refuses to merely repeat the past.

rhizome.book: 289 - Horror and Philosophy - Essays on Their Intersection in Film, Television and Literature
rhizome.title: Shock Value A Deleuzean Encounter with James Purdy's Narrow Rooms
rhizome.relation: Gross stages a Deleuze-and-Guattari 'encounter' with Purdy's Narrow Rooms, refusing Freudian or Marxist 'interpretosis' in favor of asking what the novel does. He reads Roy Sturtevant the 'renderer' as a multiplicity and traces the characters' becomings-animal (Sid's 'becoming-shark' in the locker-room sex act, becoming-horse, becoming-insect) and the crucifixion of Roy on the barn door as horror that dissolves the boundaries between master and slave, lover and torturer. Invoking Deleuze's debt to Spinoza, Nietzsche, and the Stoics, Gross argues that the joyful amor fati of art embraces horror as an expansion of life rather than something to be vanquished.

the-sublime.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
the-sublime.title: Top Eleven Contributor Top Ten Lists
the-sublime.relation: Eleven contributor top-ten lists, several applying the book's philosophical tools in miniature: Stone-Mediatore ranks ten songs by how they exemplify Burke's, Kant's, and Longinus's theories of the sublime ('Stairway to Heaven' first), Flynn ranks ten by Nietzsche's Dionysian criterion of celebrating the natural forces that undo us ('When the Levee Breaks' first), and Dick pairs ten songs with Schopenhauer's misogynist essay 'On Women.' The remaining lists — resources, sideman appearances, cover versions, oral fixations, gigs attended — are fanzine fare without philosophical content.

the-sublime.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
the-sublime.relation: Jenkins reads Burton's 'Sweeney Todd' (2007) through Edmund Burke's theory of the sublime and the device of synesthesia. She argues Burton relocates Burke's sublime from nature to the man-made, consuming city, staging beauty (Johanna, the flower-market flashbacks, saturated color) in losing tension with the 'dark and gloomy' urban sublime (desaturated Fleet Street, 'Epiphany'). Drawing on German Expressionist visual style (Caligari, Nosferatu) and the raindrop-to-blood credit sequence, she shows how sight, sound and represented taste (Mrs. Lovett's cannibal pies, the jugular-spray 'shooting star' during 'Johanna') mix the senses to force the queasy Burkean confrontation of terror and delight, ending in Burke's nihilistic darkness rather than redemption.

the-sublime.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
the-sublime.title: 3. The Nasty Bits
the-sublime.relation: Calef asks how Bourdain could find disgusting foods (cobra heart, blood soup, warthog anus) delicious, using Korsmeyer's taxonomy of disgust and the 'paradox of aversion.' He argues their appeal comes from Aristotelian learning-through-representation, Burke's and Bullough's sublime experienced at psychical distance, and Kristeva's 'abject' — foods that remind us of death and mortality let Bourdain transcend and disarm it by eating them appreciatively.

the-sublime.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
the-sublime.title: 77. Journey as Philosophy Meaning, Connection, and the Sublime
the-sublime.relation: Hamer argues Journey works through the interplay of connection, the sublime and meaning. The wordless multiplayer bond with an unnameable stranger before vast vistas dramatizes emotional connection where the ancestors' greed failed. The looming mountain and immense dunes evoke the sublime, read through Burke's pleasurable terror and Kant's mathematical and dynamical sublime (imagination overwhelmed while reason comprehends; feeling power over a nature that cannot harm the deathless player, then rebirth surpassing the sublime into joy). The cyclical return to the start recasts the game as Camus's Myth of Sisyphus: a meaningless repeated ascent that players nonetheless replay, so we must imagine the Traveler — and ourselves — happy to make the beautiful repetition our own.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Death Knight as Overman
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Luke Cuddy asks whether playing WoW can answer nihilism, using Schopenhauer's bleak remark on our sudden existence and Nietzsche's death of God to set up the problem — King Bangalash dies and WoW goes on, just as humans die and the universe continues. Entering Huizinga's Magic Circle gives Azeroth its meanings, but the player must then dissolve the circle, recognize that the game itself is meaningless, and keep playing anyway — creating the toon as a work of art in the Dionysian spirit. A maxed Death Knight still is not Nietzsche's Overman, because the player affirms only her in-game existence; the fifth step is carrying that self-creation back into real life.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: A (Bronx) Cheer to the Red Sox “Without Whom, Not as Much”
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Writing as a Yankees fan, Konig asks what makes a championship worth wanting: after Schopenhauer's picture of endless striving as suffering, he brings in Richard Taylor (meaning lies in the activity itself, never its completion) and then Nietzsche's will to power, which seeks worthy resistance to overcome. Thought experiments—a childhood 'big game' that turns out to be tee-ball, and the 2004 Sox trouncing the minor-league Atlantic League—show a title without worthy opposition is hollow. Hence the Yankees' twentieth-century dominance would mean nothing without the Red Sox as the sustained, worthy enemy (Bucky Dent, the Pedro-Zimmer melee, the 2004 ALCS collapse included).

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Escape to Doctor Who
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Reads the Master as the personification of Schopenhauer's blind, pointless Will: the Doctor's line 'In many ways we have the same mind' is taken literally, so the Master is the dark noumenal side in everyone, seen in the hypnotized Farrel whose ambition the Master acts out and Colonel Trenchard whose patriotism becomes the Master's weapon in 'The Sea Devils'. Building from Kant's phenomena/noumena distinction, he explains the Will as the inaccessible force we glimpse through inner bodily awareness, evil because purposeless. Watching the Doctor's serial victories is then offered as a light, Schopenhauerian escape through art from the terror of the Will.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: I Listen to Public Radio
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Natasha Liebig reads Squidward as Schopenhauer made flesh: his endless craving for musical fame and revenge on Squilliam exemplifies the blind, irrational will-to-live whose frustration just is suffering, so even success could never satisfy him and others' joys (SpongeBob and Patrick playing) become his bellum omnium. Yet Squidward's clarinet, self-portraits and dance are Schopenhauer's aesthetic escape — will-less contemplation of universal Ideas, with music the most metaphysical art — granting fleeting moments of peace until his neighbors interrupt. The chapter closes on the irony that Schopenhauer's genius is childlike, so SpongeBob and Patrick's effortless wonder may make them the truer artists.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Liane Heller pairs Cohen and Schopenhauer - born and died on September 21st, the autumnal equinox - as two explorers of the world's irrational negativity who both retreat to 'a room' to create. Schopenhauer's directionless Will, his pessimism about a life of constant suffering, his notorious misogyny in 'On Women,' and his ascetic denial of the will-to-live (with his contempt for Judaism and preference for the Upanishads and Buddhist compassion) are set against Cohen's affirmation that love is 'the only engine of survival,' his five-year Zen retreat that could not hold him, and his return to the Judaism of the 'little Jew who wrote the Bible.' A closing imagined dialogue has a humbled Schopenhauer confronted with Cohen's self-compassion and ordinary joys, admitting the limits of his own field of vision.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Justified and Philosophy
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: The chapter reads Harlan's family bonds through Freud's Oedipus Complex - Raylan bails Arlo out only at stepmother Helen's request, and Coover whimpers 'I'm sorry, Mamma' while cradled in Mags's arms after she hammers his hand, the submissive son destroyed by his need for his mother's approval. It then applies Schopenhauer's pessimism to Winona's pregnancy: if life is suffering, as On the Vanity of Existence argues, bringing a child into Harlan is selfish vanity, and Mags's dynasty-building - grooming Loretta, bequeathing the weed business - is the will-to-live seeking immortality through the family name. Only Boyd and Ava's unsentimental care for the demented Arlo, the chapter suggests, escapes both the Oedipal trap and the vanity of lineage.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: 2. Sex Has Something Behind It
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: John Heaney pairs Louis with Schopenhauer: both see human existence as error-shaped misery, but more importantly both treat sex as the will-to-live tricking the intellect into serving the species while we mistake the species' good for our own. He reads the 'Come on, God' stand-up (every beautiful thought about a woman followed by a disgusting one) and Louie's 'So Old/Playdate' speech that 'sex is really trying to have a family' as comedic versions of Schopenhauer's metaphysics of love, with episodes like 'Bummer/Blueberries' (a decapitation killing Louie's lust mid-non-date), 'Elevator Part 4' (the civil divorce flashback ending in a possible pregnancy), and 'Eddie' (a man losing the will-to-live along with the will-to-love) enacting the oscillation between sexual arousal and suicidal despair. Even Louis's devotion to his daughters fits Schopenhauer's claim that the sexual delusion transfers to offspring, which is why 'Eddie' ends with Louie refusing to name his reasons to live - he has to pick up his kids in the morning.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: 3. Mermen and Dismemberment
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Contends that Hendrix's discord is philosophy-as-discord: 'I Don't Live Today' (the Native American dead-in-life), the Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' with its bombs and sirens against sporting-event sentimentality, 'Machine Gun,' and 'House Burning Down' lacerate listeners so they actually feel war's atrocities instead of parroting patriotic clichés. Against this the chapter sets the oceanic, womb-like escape fantasies of '1983 (A Merman I Should Turn to Be)' and 'Valleys of Neptune,' treating them through Schopenhauer as metaphysical consolation, Marx's opiate, and Nietzsche's 'hangman's metaphysics,' and concludes that Hendrix finally refuses such world-denying illusions — and Heideggerian inauthentic withdrawal — in favor of existential engagement with suffering here and now.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Death
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Reads Alien3's Fury 161 through impurity and contagion: Mary Douglas's 'matter out of place,' Foucault's confinement of the mad (the YY-chromosome inmates quarantined as social infection; Golic's fixation on the 'dragon' as Schopenhauer's madness of a fixed idea), Hegel and Schelling's philosophies of biology in which disease, decline, and death are necessary moments of life, and Plato's virtue-as-health of the soul. Ripley's fall into the molten lead embraces Schelling's 'indifference' of freedom and its enemy - she refuses Bishop's quack offer to 'deal with the malignancy' so Weyland-Yutani can never harvest the queen inside her.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: James Heathers asks why the most improbable band became the one true originator of heavy metal and answers with Schopenhauer: industrial Aston, Birmingham was a monument to the ceaseless, unsatisfied striving of the Will, and music, which maps directly onto the Will itself, gave that world its voice. The tritone's numerically hideous ratios, a point traced through Rameau back to Pythagoras, make it the natural interval of morbidity, which is why "Black Sabbath" and everything from Liszt's Dante Sonata to death metal is marinated in it, and why doom was not a predictable development like Deep Purple or Led Zeppelin. He closes on the irony that Schopenhauer, who preached ascetic denial of the Will, would have loathed a band that answered factory-town despair by smothering the Will in lager, hash, cocaine, and women, only to breed more want in the worst of all possible worlds.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Franken-Stark
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Curtis argues Iron Man dramatizes the problem of progress: Schopenhauer's insatiable will explains why every technological fix — the chest plate, the armor, the artificial nervous system — spawns new suffering and dependency, and his pessimism, with Kierkegaard's freedom within insecurity, Nietzsche's flawed Übermensch going out 'in a blaze of glory,' and Sartre's 'cautiously optimistic' existentialism, recasts Iron Man as a tragic antihero rather than a perfected Superman or Batman. Stark's wounded heart, alcoholism as self-medication ('the demon is not in the bottle but in the addict'), and doomed romances with Bethany Cabe and Rumiko Fujikawa make him the flawed hero who has simply learned to live with imperfection. Like Mary Shelley's monster, his extensions have become him — we are all 'Franken-Starks' facing the consequences of our own inventions.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Fade to Black: Absurdity, Suicide, and the Downward Spiral
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Justin Donhauser and Kimberly Blessing read 'Fade to Black' as a meditation on suicide. Against the Schopenhauerian pessimism that life is a downward spiral 'to the musty stench of corpses' - where suicide paradoxically affirms the Will-to-life - they set Camus' absurd: the narrator who loses the will to live surrenders, while Camus' absurd hero lives in revolt, freedom, and passion. Since Schopenhauer and Camus both reject suicide as escape, and Hetfield insists 'writing is therapy', the song's effect is Aristotelian catharsis - purging despair - rather than an endorsement of suicide.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Notes
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Argues Rust Cohle's stated pessimism and in-principle embrace of suicide closely track Schopenhauer's view that suffering is built into the world with no providential redemption, yet the two diverge because Schopenhauer condemned suicide as an affirmation of the will-to-live rather than its denial. The chapter traces Rust's three-stage arc — jaded wannabe-suicidal pessimist who nonetheless energetically investigates the Dora Lange case, resigned drinker, and finally cautious affirmer of life after the Yellow King confrontation — and contends his detective work is really motivated by a Schopenhauerian morality of compassion and justice, not mere 'programming.' Rust's finale conversion is read as an evidence-based judgment that thoroughgoing pessimism is intellectually dishonest, since compassion and justice do score nontrivial victories.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Notes
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Reads Carcosa, the Yellow King, and Ledoux's 'time is a flat circle' as cosmic horror in the lineage of Lovecraft and Ligotti, arguing that the genre's dread — that monsters exist and the fixed laws of nature may fail — is a metaphor for realizing Schopenhauer's blind will, with Rust's car monologues in 'The Long Bright Dark' presented as a beginner's guide to Schopenhauer. It notes Rust inverts the usual Lovecraft protagonist by starting the story already horrified, and that eternal recurrence framed through Schopenhauer's sphere-of-time makes even the rescued children's torment maddeningly endless. The chapter closes by complaining that the finale 'Form and Void' betrays both genres: the occult becomes ordinary crime and Rust's 'light is winning' star-field reverses Schopenhauer's pessimistic cosmology.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Notes
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Distinguishes philosophical pessimism (Schopenhauer, Nietzsche, Camus, Unamuno) — the denial that the universe is an ordered place whose laws human reason can grasp — from mere gloominess, and reads Rust's 'time is a flat circle' as Nietzschean anti-metaphysics of a world going nowhere. It argues pessimism makes Rust the better detective because, expecting no rational order, he sees what is actually there, while optimist Marty's illusions about family and career multiply his losses and end with him losing both. Against conflating pessimism with despair, the chapter splits ideas (pessimism) from attitudes (hope), showing how Hart's heart and Cohle's clear sight combine into the show's ideal of hopeful pessimism.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Notes
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Reconstructs Rust's scattered remarks — the world as 'one giant gutter,' procreation as the hubris of yanking a soul out of nonexistence into the thresher — into an explicit anti-natalist argument, testing each premise and conceding procreation is selfish while questioning whether every life nets more harm than good. It presents David Benatar's asymmetry between the absence of pain (always good) and the absence of pleasure (bad only for someone deprived), illustrating it with the show: contraception as procreative duty, the wrongness of conceiving in Tuttle's Louisiana, and the emptiness of Childress' temple as a good in itself. The chapter concludes that Rust's 'opt out of a raw deal' is philosophically defensible, with Schopenhauer's desire-pendulum and Hobbes' 'nasty, brutish, and short' backing the claim that most lives are bad.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Notes
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Traces Cohle's opening monologue directly to Schopenhauer — reality as a purposeless will whose satisfied desires breed only boredom, answered by ascetic denial of the will-to-live rather than suicide. It then explains Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as the true test of life-affirmation, via the Gay Science demon and Zarathustra's ordeal with the Small Man, and interprets will to power as finding meaning in overcoming resisting conditions, so that affirmation does not mean approving everything that happens. Hatab argues the show's horrified version of the flat circle is Schopenhauerian rather than Nietzschean, and that Cohle's 'light is winning' ending is ambiguous — if it rests on a supernatural reunion with Sophia, it would betray Nietzsche's this-worldly affirmation.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Acknowledgment
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: William Irwin diagnoses Neptune, from the 09-ers down to the PCH-ers, with status anxiety (via Alain de Botton's Status Anxiety) and prescribes the Stoic remedy: Epictetus on the insult lying in our judgment rather than the insulter, and Marcus Aurelius, the emperor who chose serenity over vengeance, show how Keith and Veronica ground self-worth in virtue no one can take away. Sartre's 'hell is other people' and the look explain how Veronica is reduced to a dumb blonde and Duncan to a murderer until he flees to Cuba, while Schopenhauer's choice between loneliness and vulgarity frames Mac's switched-at-birth longing, Wallace's basketball-bought status, and Weevil's self-made standing as PCH leader. Irwin closes by offering the show itself as Aristotelian catharsis-through-comedy, art as therapy for the viewer's own status anxiety.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Sixteenth Hole Golf and the Meaning of Life
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Randy Lunsford uses Annika Sorenstam's early retirement to ask what makes golf—and life—meaningful, surveying religious versus scientific accounts of purpose and E. J. Bond's claim that meaning comes from pursuing objectively valuable ends, not just satisfying desire. He tests Epicurean hedonism and Nozick's experience machine (we want to really shoot the course record, not merely feel we did), Taylor's reworking of the Sisyphus myth (meaning via injected desire), and Schopenhauer's pessimism that satisfied desire only yields boredom. He argues golf's very finitude—eighteen holes, like a mortal life—gives it meaning, so excellence, relationships, playing by the rules, and taking responsibility for each shot are what make both golf and life worthwhile.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Film Noir and the Meaning of Life
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Steven Sanders uses film noir to motivate philosophical reflection on the meaning of life, reading its pessimistic sensibility (Touch of Evil, Detour, Out of the Past, D.O.A., Vertigo) as the presupposition that life is meaningless per se. He runs through Schopenhauer's pessimistic arguments from the vanity and transience of existence, Nagel's rebuttal that our not mattering in a million years does not stop things mattering now, and the tension between Sartrean existentialist freedom and noir's Freudian fatalism of the inescapable past. He then lays out three models of meaninglessness (Baier's worthlessness and purposelessness, Camus/Nagel's absurdity met with irony), reading noir protagonists as ironists, before rejecting the noir view that life must be meaningless and arguing that meaning is a matter of degree, requiring realizable projects of positive value.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 225 - The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Conard uses Mean Streets' guilt-ridden Charlie to survey conceptions of unhappiness against three definitions of happiness: beatitude (Aquinas), pleasure (Mill's hedonism), and flourishing (Aristotle's eudaimonia). He reads Charlie as damned in his own Catholic eyes, then invokes Nietzsche's Genealogy that religion manufactures guilt from internalized instinct, Plato's disordered soul and akrasia to explain Charlie's conflicting desires, and Schopenhauer's and Freud's pessimism that suffering is our natural state. He argues Charlie reaches dysdaimonia by acquiring vices and pursuing an ignoble (gangster) life, closing with Plato's Symposium and Sartre's facticity/transcendence to cast unhappiness as an ontological lack at the heart of human desire.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: My Troubles Are Going to Have Troubles with Me Schopenhauer, Pessimism, and Nietzsche
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Jacob Held pits Schopenhauer's pessimism against Nietzschean affirmation using I Had Trouble in Getting to Solla Sollew. He reads Schopenhauer's will-to-life and 'pendulum between pain and boredom' into Seuss's endlessly striving characters, and treats the mirage-towns Solla Sollew and Boola Boo Ball as proof there is no escape from suffering. The protagonist's final line, 'I've bought a big bat... now my troubles are going to have troubles with me,' becomes Nietzsche's yes-saying: instead of the ascetic renunciation Schopenhauer prescribes, Seuss's child-hero affirms life, redeeming its accidents the way Nietzsche's eternal-recurrence thought experiment and 'become a child' passage in Zarathustra demand.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: From Desperation to Haven
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Held reads The Tommyknockers, Desperation, and The Regulators through Arthur Schopenhauer's pessimism, arguing King's worlds are 'always already sunk in evil' and that the will to live swings life between pain and boredom even before the supernatural arrives. He identifies egoism as the root of King's cruelty (Hilly banishing David Brown to Altair-4, Bobbi turning her dog into a battery) and offers Schopenhauer's compassion-based virtue ethic, 'injure no one; help everyone,' as the answer, supported by MacIntyre on the degradation of happiness and set against Nietzsche's 'last man' and nihilism. Gard's rescue of David Brown ('the kid matters or nothing matters') and Johnny Marinville's self-sacrifice in Desperation exemplify the heroic, compassionate life that defies the dark.

schopenhauer-pessimism.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
schopenhauer-pessimism.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
schopenhauer-pessimism.relation: Clack's 'Cannabis and the Human Condition' reads intoxication through Freud's Civilization and its Discontents, where drugs are the 'crudest but most effective' palliative against a life 'too hard for us,' tied to the pleasure principle and the Nirvana/death-instinct drive to discharge stimulus. He supplements Freud with Schopenhauer's pessimism — life oscillating between suffering and boredom — to add 'stimulus hunger' Freud ignored, arguing cannabis both dampens and stokes the 'fire in the brain' depending on THC potency (high vs. stoned). He concludes that, like religion, art and love, cannabis augments a bleak existence, so 'all cannabis use is medicinal.'

zeno-paradoxes.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
zeno-paradoxes.title: Which World Am I In
zeno-paradoxes.relation: Juan Ferret tells the story from inside the game: Admetus the Human Mage, chased through Alterac Valley by an Undead Rogue, works through Zeno's paradox of motion, the convergence of infinite series, and whether space and time are discrete, coached by a bodiless voice that turns out to be his player. The voice's revelations — 'You are my creation,' autorun, polymorph, Blink — force the free-will-versus-determinism question from the character's side, since every action is controlled from above. Reference frames, Heisenberg's uncertainty, EPR entanglement, and hidden nods to David Lewis ('Siwel Divad' on possible worlds) and many-worlds theory leave the mage wondering which world, server, or parallel universe he really inhabits.

zeno-paradoxes.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
zeno-paradoxes.title: We Wouldn’t Be Here Without Time Travel
zeno-paradoxes.relation: Worley distinguishes logical from empirical possibility (Leonardo's round-square in 'City of Death') and shows that time-travel paradoxes — Leela's self-caused antibodies, the unauthored 'Blink' Easter egg, the Master's Toclafane — can be handled with Zeno-style analysis of contradiction and David Lewis's distinction between external and personal time, under which travelers instantiate rather than rewrite history ('The Visitation', 'The Time Meddler'). He then reads 'Turn Left' and the Doctor's 'alternative time' in 'Pyramids of Mars' through Leibniz's possible worlds and Lewis's actualism about parallel universes, concluding that in 'City of Death' time travel is essential to life on Earth existing at all.

zeno-paradoxes.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
zeno-paradoxes.title: 7. Because Nothing Can’t Be!
zeno-paradoxes.relation: Joseph Kirkland takes Louis's 'Why? Why? Why?' routine from One Night Stand - collapsing into 'things that are not can't be!' and 'giant ants with top hats dancing around' - as an accidental encounter with the Pre-Socratics' question of why there is something rather than nothing. Louis, he argues, rejects the Principle of Plenitude (a finite world has no room for every possibility), whereas Parmenides argues from pure logic that nothingness is impossible and change therefore illusory - his student Zeno 'proving' it with paradoxes such as the infinite halfway points between Louis and Ben's Pizzeria. Framing the bit with Plato's claim that wonder is the beginning of philosophy and Socrates' unexamined life, the chapter ends on the parental punchline 'bread first, then ethics': feeding the kid trumps metaphysics, and Louis's frustration comes from failing that duty while his daughter probes being and non-being over her French fries.

zeno-paradoxes.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
zeno-paradoxes.title: Deleuze Jam Today
zeno-paradoxes.relation: Walks Alice through four theories of time: Augustine's three presents in Confessions (Alice 'was a different person then'; the past exists only as present memory), Kant's time as a subjective form of intuition presupposed by experience (the White Rabbit's anxiety about being late already requires it), Bergson's indivisible duration against spatialized clock time (running fastest with the Red Queen yet ending under the same tree; the Hatter stuck at six o'clock; Zeno's Achilles resolved by indivisible acts), and Deleuze's chronos and aion from The Logic of Sense. Mark W. Westmoreland reads 'jam to-morrow and jam yesterday—but never jam to-day' as pure aion: the present never arrives, only an endlessly subdividing past-future.

zeno-paradoxes.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
zeno-paradoxes.title: Happily Ever After
zeno-paradoxes.relation: Runs Descartes' dreaming argument and evil-genius doubt on Aurora, for whom the scenario is literal: Maleficent is an actually existing deceiver who could have enchanted her whole life in a dungeon. G. E. Moore's common-sense proof — 'here is a hand,' dubbed the Pinocchio test after the real boy — and the Moorean shift answer the skeptic, illustrated by Maleficent deploying Zeno's paradox to stop Prince Phillip's sword, where Phillip rightly clings to the more certain premise that motion is possible. Nozick's experience machine explains why Aurora should care: we want to actually be good and live real lives rather than merely experience them, so authentic 'happily ever after' requires knowing our experiences are backed by reality.

zeno-paradoxes.title: We Wouldn’t Be Here Without Time Travel
zeno-paradoxes.relation: Peter Worley finishes the Doctor's "wibbly-wobbly" speech from "Blink" by distinguishing empirical from logical possibility (via a fictional chat with Leonardo about a round-square) and asking whether time travel is coherent. Using "The Edge of Destruction," "The Aztecs," "The Visitation," and "Turn Left," he deploys David Lewis's external-versus-personal time distinction and Lewis's rule that a time traveler's acts must be the very events that made history, then treats the Doctor and Lewis as "actualists" about possible worlds to dissolve grandfather-style paradoxes and time loops.

zeno-paradoxes.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
zeno-paradoxes.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
zeno-paradoxes.relation: John D. Norton poses three sailing paradoxes — how a wind-powered boat sails into the wind, faster than the wind, and whether 'making its own wind' makes it a perpetual-motion machine — echoing Zeno's paradoxes of motion and measure as engines of philosophical clarity. He resolves the first two by rejecting the causal truism that an effect cannot exceed or oppose its cause (the wind's force, resolved into drive and beam components against a resistant hull, is the real cause), using this to argue causal principles are elastic labels grafted onto science, never laws it must obey. For the third he builds an idealized wind-turbine boat thought experiment showing created-wind energy is exactly consumed by counter-force, and debates James Brown's Platonist view (that thought experiments 'see' laws in a Platonic realm, like grasping the ideal triangle) against his own deflationary view that they are merely picturesque argument.

dialetheism.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
dialetheism.title: I Can’t Understand True Contradictions. Try it Again . . . In Orcish
dialetheism.relation: Nicolas Michaud asks how far a gameworld can bend the rules that structure reality: mana regenerating from nowhere seems to violate conservation of energy, alternative axiom systems might license 10 + 10 = 40 damage, and sorites cases like 'balding' and Half-Elves strain the Law of Excluded Middle. The deepest case is the Law of Non-Contradiction: a true contradiction would trivialize every belief ('explosion'), and Graham Priest's 'Sylvan's Box' — a box containing something and nothing — shows we can tell a contradiction story without absurdity yet still cannot really understand it. His conclusion: WoW's designers could probably program a dialetheia, but comprehending it would require a whole different way of thinking that humans probably lack.

dialetheism.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
dialetheism.title: Here’s How It Happened and Didn’t Happen
dialetheism.relation: Michaud asks how TV's most logical detective can assert contradictions: Monk says 'I know it's impossible, but he's the guy' about Derek Philby murdering while proctoring an exam ('Mr. Monk Goes Back to School') and about astronaut Steve Wagner killing while in orbit ('Mr. Monk and the Astronaut'), seeming violations of the Law of Non-Contradiction that his own valid arguments (the missing glass of water ruling out suicide) depend on. The chapter stages Graham Priest's dialetheism — the Liar Sentence as a true contradiction — as a possible defense, even borrowing Gricean maxims to argue Monk would announce a dialetheia if he believed one, but concludes Monk never actually accepts true contradictions: the impossible accusation creates a tension that drives him to find the hidden mechanism (Wagner's pre-rigged garage door), so the 'contradiction' dissolves once a false assumption is exposed. Michaud's closing suggestion is that the Liar Sentence itself should be treated as a crime to be solved rather than a dialetheia to be accepted.

dialetheism.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
dialetheism.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
dialetheism.relation: The chapter defends Barney's 'possimpible' as real philosophy. Aristotle's three formulations of the law of non-contradiction (from the Metaphysics) and Duns Scotus's ex falso quodlibet explosion argument show why classical logic must ban the possible and impossible becoming one - from one true contradiction, 'bimbos love studying formal logic' follows. Hegel's Science of Logic (the limit of the beer, the finite that is itself only by passing into its not-being) and Graham Priest's dialetheism from In Contradiction then argue limits are inherently contradictory, so the possimpible names the real turning point where opposites become each other - lived, the chapter claims, in Barney's transformation from lame hippie into suited bro.

posthumanism.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
posthumanism.title: Wave Goodbye from the Catbus
posthumanism.relation: Heinricy argues anime is the richest medium for posthuman theory because it shows bodies 'in a state of becoming' rather than as grotesque boundary violations: Miyazaki's Catbus and Totoro, Haku's dragon transformation and Chihiro's pig parents in Spirited Away, and the cursed pig-headed aviator of Porco Rosso all treat morphing bodies as possibility, not horror. She sorts anime posthumanism into two valences: a 'Ghost in the Machine' dream of consciousness leaving the body altogether (Motoko merging with the net in Ghost in the Shell), which she rebuts via N. Katherine Hayles's point that consciousness is embodied and would change with any new body, and hybrid configurations like mecha (Gundam, Robotech) where body and machine drive each other. Following Donna Haraway, she contends we are all already cyborgs — vaccines, engineered food, treated water — and credits Japan's nuclear history (via Susan Napier) and its shape-shifting folklore for why anime embraces rather than fears the transformed body.

posthumanism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
posthumanism.title: And the Next Step
posthumanism.relation: Surveys science fiction's next-step humanity — Wells's genetically stratified future, Stapledon's successions of human forms, and the Campbell-era optimism Dick resisted — then turns to contemporary 'posthumanist' theorists like Donna Haraway who want 'human,' 'natural,' and 'gender' fluidly redefined. Dick emerges as the voice of caution in this cross-pollination: expand the definition of what human means, but not at the cost of the compassion and empathy that make us human.

posthumanism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
posthumanism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
