posthumanism.relation: Caroline Mosser treats the creature's tragedy as humanist prejudice rather than necessity: the blind De Lacey accepts the eloquent creature sight unseen, so he passes Alan Turing's test, and only the sighted family's terror at his body rejects him - bias against the artificial, not reason. She reads the creature's development through fire, language, and revolution as Rousseau's progression from natural innocence to corruption by society, and Donna Haraway's cyborg as the figure he prefigures: an unfaithful illegitimate offspring who rebels against his father and undermines patriarchal Western self/other dualisms. The chapter concludes that society cannot accept enhanced or posthuman beings until it finds a middle ground beyond its binary grids of good/bad and Self/Other, since otherwise any new life we create will be Othered, hated, and oppressed like Frankenstein's.

posthumanism.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
posthumanism.title: 13. Sisterhood’s Back in Orphan Black
posthumanism.relation: Recounts the rise and fall of second-wave sisterhood — the dream of a unified female voice that erased differences of race, class, sexuality, and nation until the 1980s backlash killed it — and argues Orphan Black resurrects a corrected version through Rosi Braidotti's posthumanism. The clones, disposable bodies of biogenetic capitalism, build a sisterhood that celebrates difference (grunge Sarah, dreads-and-lab-coat Cosima, suburban Alison, savage Helena) rather than enforcing sameness, and that welcomes the Others the Seventies excluded — gay Felix, Black Art, Hindu Raj — while white Western men like Paul remain the surveillance agents of the backlash. Through posthumanism's dissolution of fixed human identity, the chapter claims, feminism's old ideal returns both transformed and inclusive.

posthumanism.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
posthumanism.title: 7. More Human than Humans
posthumanism.relation: Rob O'Connor reads replicants through N. Katherine Hayles's posthumanism — persons as amalgams of biological and informational-technological systems — arguing Rachael's procreation shows the posthuman body bypassing its designed limits, while Joi is a posthuman of the opposite construction, a hologram transcending her limits through emotion. Memory and experience, even implanted ones (Batty's 'tears in rain', Deckard's unicorn dream, K's wooden horse, 'all the best memories are hers'), supply the existential context that defines the posthuman self. K's epiphany before the giant Joi advertisement reveals he is a tool of the capitalist system, and his choice to die for the right cause is how he takes charge of his own identity.

posthumanism.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
posthumanism.title: 13. Won’t You Be My Posthuman Neighbor
posthumanism.relation: Fernando Pagnoni Berns reads the show as posthumanist: the toy-model opening credits leave it unclear whether Rogers himself is a toy, Trolley refuses orange juice yet speaks (an object with a will), Lady Aberlin uses a bass as a dance partner, and Audrey Duck's 'You're as real as you want to be' collapses human, animal, and hand puppet. Invoking Bruno Latour's quasi-human 'non-humans' that channel human desires, he argues the Neighborhood dissolves the humanist hierarchy that enthrones the white Western male over women, animals, objects, and plants.

posthumanism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
posthumanism.title: Post-Apocalyptic Perspectives
posthumanism.relation: Crippen reads the Continent's Great Frost and the Conjunction of the Spheres as apocalypse in the word's literal sense of 'uncovering,' binding environmental collapse, refugee migration, and a post-truth erosion of moral concepts into one crisis. Nietzsche's 'inverse cripples' and Plato's Phaedo (philosophy as preparation for death, truth as lifeless unchanging perfection) illuminate Yennefer's ageless barrenness and the witchers' suppressed emotions, while Degerlund's transhumanist breeding schemes and plans to cut out Geralt's eyes violate Kantian respect for persons. Filavandrel's starving elves parallel Indigenous dispossession, Dorregaray's 'natural equilibrium' and Zoltan's prediction that humans 'wait for a chance to make money from other people's mishaps' evoke ecological and social imbalance, and Geralt's old-fashioned virtues answer a post-apocalyptic, post-truth world.

posthumanism.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
posthumanism.title: XVII - HIGH-TECH MYTHOLOGY IN X-MEN
posthumanism.relation: Teschner reads X-Men as high-tech mythology: the superhero images are Freud's dream work, disguising unconscious wishes about technological power that the conscious ego cannot face, with Wolverine's adamantium and constant pain symbolizing human alienation under the machine. The psionic mind, telepathy and telekinesis that move matter directly, breaks the Cartesian dualism of mind and body, marking the upper limit of technological control. On the latent level, Xavier's psionic blocks and School represent repression of the unconscious while Magneto's plastic prison, mutant machine, and Liberty Island plan represent acceptance of a humanity redefined by its union with the machine.

posthumanism.title: From Self-Alienation to Posthumanism The Transmigration of the Burroughsian Subject
posthumanism.relation: Bolton argues William S. Burroughs's fragmented subjects—split by a parasitic 'Other Half' or word virus—are not postmodernism's dissolved nonsubjects but practitioners of a productive self-alienation. He aligns Burroughs's multiply-named, body-swapping characters (Mr. Bradley Mr. Martin, Joe the Dead) with Lacan's split subject constituted in language and with Derrida's iterable 'mark' and 'third that walks beside you' as an absent-present that dissolves binaries. Through Naked Lunch, Nova Express, and The Western Lands the Burroughsian subject transmigrates from Marxian/Hegelian alienation to N. Katherine Hayles's posthuman, gaining agency by extending into its technologized environment.

augustine-city-of-god.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
augustine-city-of-god.title: Gay Angels, Female Cardinals, and Bishōnen Popes
augustine-city-of-god.relation: Barkman argues that anime's Christian imagery — the legendary Santa on a cross, Earthian's gay angel lovers, Trinity Blood's bishonen pope and female cardinal, Evangelion's hostile Angels — encodes Japanese religious pluralism rather than orthodox Christianity. He lays out the pluralist position (following Kant's phenomena/noumena distinction and John Hick: Ultimate Reality is only equivocally describable, so doctrine matters less than spiritual mood), contrasts it with exclusivism and inclusivism, and charges pluralism with self-undermining intolerance, then traces Japan's historical demonization of Christianity from the 1637 Shimabara massacre (Ninja Resurrection, Samurai Champloo) to Eva's alien invaders, with Armageddon imagery fueled by the atomic bombs. Because Shinto-Buddhist-Daoist anti-realism dissolves fixed categories, anime dissolves good and evil (Chrno Crusade's I Ching balance) and gender itself, gravitating to the symbol-rich 'jungle' of Catholicism (C.S. Lewis's phrase) — and where Trinity Blood lets some vampires be righteous, Augustine's City of God marks the one nearly orthodox note.

augustine-city-of-god.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
augustine-city-of-god.title: From Satyrs to Martyrs
augustine-city-of-god.relation: Shows how Augustine forged the machinery of Christian evil — sex as sin, the invention of Original Sin, The City of God's mandate to compel heretics, and the goat-god Pan as Satan's visual model — then maps it onto the 1960s persecution of the Stones: press mockery, police drug busts, Bill Wyman hauled into court as a "shaggy monster." The persecution backfired, making the Stones martyrs and pushing Jagger toward the self-embraced "Lucifers of Rock" image of "Paint It, Black" and the Their Satanic Majesties Request cover.

augustine-city-of-god.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
augustine-city-of-god.title: Homeland and Philosophy
augustine-city-of-god.relation: Roberto Sirvent and Ian Diorio ask what the state really asks soldiers to die for: not Hobbes-and-Locke's rational social contract, since we are Heideggerian thrown into the wreckage of democracy rather than a pure founding state, but a nation that makes itself sacred. MacIntyre's charge that killing for the nation-state is 'killing for the telephone company' frames the analysis of America's civil liturgies - oaths (semper fidelis), flag ritual mirrored eerily in Brody burying Jessica's thrown Quran, saints, martyrs, and Saul pitting belief in America against belief in Allah. Augustine's civitas dei names the result: America as chosen city of God, and Islam terrifies the West because its creed claims devotion above any national flag.

augustine-city-of-god.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
augustine-city-of-god.title: 2. Can Anything Good Come from the Upside Down
augustine-city-of-god.relation: Kuzma maps Augustine's two cities onto the two Hawkinses: not two places but two mixed moral orientations in one world, since Will is literally 'right here' in the same house flipped upside down. Augustine's privation view of evil (evil as absence of good, a nougat-less Three Musketeers) explains how Dart can come from the 'evil' Upside Down yet love Dustin and let the party pass, while Brenner, from the right side up, is ruled by libido dominandi like the Mind Flayer and Dr. Owens proves Hawkins Lab is not automatically bad; it is how you act, not where you are from.

augustine-city-of-god.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
augustine-city-of-god.title: The Dread Conclusion!
augustine-city-of-god.relation: The chapter asks whether Dormammu is truly evil and tests him against Augustine's three types of evil: metaphysical evil as privation fails because Dormammu is a positive being with a face and a voice, natural evil fails because he is a sentient agent with intentions, so he lands squarely in moral evil—freely intending to deprive intelligent beings of the good of existence. It entertains the Galactus-style alternative that Dormammu, like a lion taking a gazelle, is an amoral force consuming worlds for survival, but his rage in the time loop ('your world is mine, like all worlds') reveals a drive for domination rather than sustenance, while conceding we know him only through the Ancient One's possibly biased testimony.

augustine-city-of-god.title: Notes
augustine-city-of-god.relation: Cooper reads Frank's one prayer - kneeling to pray 'to myself, for myself' - as a self-love he calls autoeroticism, built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness as power. Like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, Frank's atheism removes divine punishment from the moral equation, so the murders of Peter Russo and Zoe Barnes incur only human risk, while his feigned piety at the Peachoid girl's vigil, broken promises to Tusk, and 'cruelty well used' toward Russo exemplify Machiavellian virtu taming fortuna. Against this the chapter sets Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's remorse after betraying Freddy ('Do you think I'm a hypocrite?') shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man against the Augustinian freedom of self-giving love.

augustine-city-of-god.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
augustine-city-of-god.title: Notes
augustine-city-of-god.relation: Analyzes Frank's kneeling 'I pray to myself, for myself' as an ethics of autoeroticism built on metaphysical atheism, ruthless pragmatism, and happiness-as-power: like Glaucon's Ring of Gyges, removing God from the equation makes the murders of Zoe and Russo cost only human, never eternal, judgment. The chapter details three exercises of Machiavellian virtu-feigned piety at the Peachoid vigil, fox-like promise-breaking with Tusk, and 'cruelty well-used' toward Russo-before closing on Augustine's critique of the libido dominandi: Frank's betrayal of Freddy, met with a flash of remorse, shows the lust for domination enslaves rather than liberates, the way of the City of Man.

mimesis.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
mimesis.title: The Sacrificial Lamb
mimesis.relation: Argues Astro Boy re-enacts the sacrificial logic of the atomic age: Atomu is the nuclear-powered copy of the dead Tobio, born from Dr. Tenma's refusal to accept mortality, and his repeated self-sacrifice for humans who discard him (as in 'Save the Classmate,' where the rescued boys' parents still want him removed) shows him functioning as Heidegger's 'standing-reserve' — an object valued only as stored power, with humans themselves next in line. Drawing on Plato's Republic anxiety over originals and copies, Adorno and Horkheimer's dialectic of enlightenment, and Rey Chow's account of mimesis as the sign left by sacrifice, the chapter reads the series as mourning an innocence that became impossible after Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

mimesis.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
mimesis.title: Exile from Ancient Greece—Yeah!
mimesis.relation: Answers the anti-relativist who holds Main Street's greatness self-explanatory: if its meaning has nothing to do with what Liz Phair thinks, it has nothing to do with what the fundamentalist thinks either. The skeptics' error—expecting Guyville to sound like Main Street—inherits the Platonic-Aristotelian assumption that inspiration means imitation (knowing a statue's beauty means containing a copy of its shape), whereas the Stones themselves 'responded' to Muddy Waters and Chuck Berry without merely imitating; Phair's closer 'Strange Loop,' its riff morphing into '6’1”,' closes the hermeneutic circle and invites us to revisit, not finalize, Exile.

mimesis.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
mimesis.title: 2. If I Don’t Listen to My Imaginary Friend, Why the Fuck Should I Listen to Yours
mimesis.relation: Kreider stages a chat between Plato and Aristotle about the show. On Plato's account, mimesis is an imitation of an imitation of the Forms, so Elliot's imaginary friend, his fake persona with Krista, and the Mr. Robot personality are intellectually and morally dangerous deceptions that let him commit terrorism without his rational self's consent; yet the Republic's censored poetry for the auxiliaries explains how fsociety's masked videos teach true beliefs, and how Elliot uses the fictional Mr. Robot to educate himself toward ideas he already knew were right. Aristotle's Poetics then defends imitation as natural and instructive - the show is a cautionary tragedy, and the Mr. Robot crutch is how Elliot eventually steps up to claim responsibility.

mimesis.title: 13. The Laughter and the Fury
mimesis.relation: Situates Inside Amy Schumer between Aristotle's Poetics dictum that valor in a woman is inappropriate, his Politics claim of female inferiority, and the 1970s French feminists: Cixous's 'Laugh of the Medusa' breaking up truth with laughter and Irigaray's strategic mimesis. Kolb reads stereotype-performing sketches with violent endings, such as the 'I'm So Bad' women devouring a waiter's face and the 'You Are Gorgeous' anthem rewarding a faked miscarriage and an N-word rap, as resubmitting women to stereotypes to explode them. Casting-couch opener '2 Girls, 1 Cup', 'Focus Group', and '12 Angry Men' hold up a mirror to the male gaze and to the rage it produces when women stop performing for it.

mimesis.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
mimesis.title: The Office and Philosophy
mimesis.relation: Written as a fake email thread among University of Scranton faculty, the appendix has junior professor Joe Kraus propose reading the town through Baudrillard's simulacrum - the 'Scranton Welcomes You' sign from the credits becoming real for him only as a TV image - while senior colleagues tutor him through the history of representation theory. Stephen deploys Plato's Ion (Socrates' magnet-and-iron chain of imitation, with Ion's Brent-like obliviousness) and Aristotle on mimesis, pity, fear, and catharsis to explain the show's tragicomic discomfort, while Maria adds the Antiochene, Alexandrian, and Augustinian fourfold senses of scripture applied to Scranton; Michael Friedman contributes a Chekhovian reading of Pam's bird eulogy as subtext about Michael's fear of dying alone. The thread itself mirrors an Office plotline as the senior faculty quietly decide to cut the untenured Joe out of the project.

mimesis.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
mimesis.title: 8. What Are You Hearing
mimesis.relation: Wissner shows how Twilight Zone scores mark the boundary between dream and reality: electronic instruments and reverberation in 'Perchance to Dream' (Hammond organ, Theremin-like violin), diegetic folk songs against the Willoughby theme in 'A Stop at Willoughby,' the shared recurring nightmare cue of 'Twenty-Two' and 'Shadow Play,' and the desperate piano ostinato of 'The Midnight Sun.' Framing this with Plato's view of music as unreal, image-evoking mimetic signs and Aristotle's claim that melodies carry ethos and can change minds, she argues music tells viewers what pictures cannot: whether a character is dreaming, imagining, or awake.

mimesis.title: Dragnet, Film Noir, and Postwar Realism
mimesis.relation: Palmer argues that Dragnet's famous realism was forged from the noir semidocumentary (The House on 92nd Street, He Walked by Night, with its diabolical killer Roy Martin hunted through the LA sewers) and from the era's taste for Italian neorealism (Open City, The Bicycle Thief, The Men), but that Jack Webb deliberately inverted the noir formula. Where the semidocumentaries split their focus between dedicated police and charismatic monsters, Webb eliminated expressionist stylization and hard-boiled wisecracks to center 'a quiet, dedicated policeman... one little cog in a great enforcement machine.' The chapter details Dragnet's imitative realism as a fidelity to real things: actual case files, LAPD technical advisors, plaster casts of police-station doorknobs, Friday's date-and-time narration, the 'The story you are about to see is true' preamble, and mug-shot endings with sentences read aloud. This yields not noir's fascination with the perverse but a social realism that rhetorically affirms law, institutions, and inevitable conviction, complicating the standard story of 1950s television's aesthetic decline.

mimesis.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
mimesis.title: 29. Anarchy in Aesthetics
mimesis.relation: Evan Kreider tests punk against three theories of art. Hutcheson's formalism - beauty as 'uniformity amongst variety', order plus complexity, exemplified by Bach, bebop, and prog rock - condemns punk's three chords, power chords, and chaotic performances; Tolstoy's arousal theory and the Croce/Collingwood expression theory vindicate punk's seething anger and angst ('Liar', 'I Wanna Be Sedated', 'Know Your Rights'); and Aristotle's unities of action, place, and time show that simplicity, even with a dash of tragic irony, serves didactic and political ends. The chapter concludes that punk's deliberate simplicity and chaos ('Anarchy in the UK', 'God Save the Queen', 'Rock the Casbah') is precisely what lets its political message reach 'angry youth', making punk a standing counter-example to order-and-complexity aesthetics.

transhumanism.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
transhumanism.title: Cyborg Goddess
transhumanism.relation: Reads Ghost in the Shell as Donna Haraway's 'Cyborg Manifesto' made flesh: Major Kusanagi is built not born, has no sexuality or romance, and relegates male partners to sidekicks, enacting Haraway's post-gender cyborg that breaks the dualisms binding women to body, nature, and reproduction. The chapter traces the 'ghost' back through Koestler to Ryle's mockery of Descartes's mind-body dualism, reads the genderless, net-born Puppet Master as the Singularity of transhumanist philosophy, and interprets the Major–Puppet Master fusion — urged to 'come out of the shadows and into the light' in an explicit Plato's-cave gesture — as a posthuman, techno-spiritual 'Cyborg Goddess' that renders both gender and humanity obsolete.

transhumanism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
transhumanism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
transhumanism.relation: Hauskeller argues Shelley's Victor was sane and benevolently motivated, and reads the 'playing God' warning (Whale's 'now I know what it feels to be God!', the Genesis tree of life, the sorcerer's apprentice) as a claim that crossing nature's lines is dangerous rather than sinful. He then flips the story: like the creature, we are children abandoned by a creator who withholds eternal life, so the real wrong is a creator's failure of duty and love - while Epicurus's death-is-nothing-to-us argument and the picture of a childless, static immortal world undermine the transhumanist case that death is the greatest evil. The chapter ends with Aristotle's mean: obsessive pursuit of knowledge and immortality wrecks happiness, which lies in discovering that our native town is the world and living in the present.

transhumanism.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
transhumanism.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
transhumanism.relation: Billard concedes the Stoic point that we control neither our passions nor nature ('life will always find a way', Sattler's 'you never had control'), as the bucardo cloning failure shows, but argues this proves the park rushed, not that de-extinction is impossible. Dangerousness is subjective, raptor intelligence is a logistics problem rather than a metaphysical objection, and since humans have already caused the sixth mass extinction we may have a duty to bring species back. Because revived animals would be 'neo-dinosaurs' built from fragmentary DNA, de-extinction is creation rather than resurrection, less like playing God than like the transhumanist enhancement humans already practice.

transhumanism.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
transhumanism.title: 16. Death Becomes Her
transhumanism.relation: Hendrik Kempt reads Drag Race's pervasive death imagery - death-drops, the 'lip sync for your life,' mirror messages, the 'Death Becomes Her' runway - through the philosophy of death. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' and Stoic self-possession (Ru's 'pay them bitches no mind,' Violet Chachki enduring a tiny corset) explain why elimination, like death, gives no ground for worry once it arrives, while Socrates' 'philosophy is training for death' makes the show a workout video for dying - Socrates even dying fussing over a rooster like a drag mother to Miss Fame. Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death set up Sartre's radically free, future-oriented self - so voluntary exits like BenDeLaCreme's self-elimination and Charlie Hides's listless lip-sync betray one's own plans - and Camus's Sisyphus makes Chi Chi DeVayne and Roxxxy Andrews's doomed All Stars returns models of 'acceptance without resignation.' The closing weighs transhumanism's promise of conquered death against a DragCon-forever thought experiment, concluding with Ru's roast eulogy for Lady Bunny that love and irreverence, not immortal life, are the point.

transhumanism.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
transhumanism.title: The Death of Death
transhumanism.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

transhumanism.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
transhumanism.title: 16 When Tech Meets Tradition How Wakandan Technology Transcends Anti-Blackness
transhumanism.relation: Timothy Brown argues that transhumanist futures - Bostrom's fable of the Dragon Tyrant, Savulescu's moral bioenhancement, AI built by homogeneous teams - exclude Black people because technologies embed anti-Blackness, from Ruha Benjamin's New Jim Code to facial recognition failing Black women. Black Panther counters this by rooting its future in traumatic memory: Killmonger's museum scene shows how whitewashed 'aesthetic Africanism' licenses incredulity about African technological achievement, while Shuri's comics arc (named 'Ancient Future' by her ancestors in D'Jalia) shows that Wakandan technology flourishes only through the traditions it is tempted to scoff at. Africanfuturism, on this reading, treats Blackness itself as a 'prosthesis' for stress-testing whether the futures we build will include everyone.

transhumanism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
transhumanism.title: Notes
transhumanism.relation: Walter Barta presents transhumanism as a real philosophy (via Bostrom's history of the movement and 'Why I Want to Be a Posthuman When I Grow Up') that Fallout both practices and indicts: ghouls, FEV super mutants and the Children of the Cathedral, stimpak-Mentat-Jet self-medication, Brotherhood power armor, Mr. House, the Master, Robobrains, John Henry Eden, and Liberty Prime all embody enhancement or post-humanity, and the level-up loop makes every player a transhumanist. Bostrom's transhumanist value of 'the opportunity to explore' maps onto leaving Vault 13 for the open world, but the Red Queen race becomes the game's adaptive-leveling treadmill, and C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man plus Fukuyama's 'Factor-X' warn that optimization can delete what made enhancement worth wanting - as when the Overseer exiles the too-powerful Vault 13 hero and the Enclave President rationalizes genocidal bioweapons ('No price is too high for the survival of the human race'). Existential risk (Toby Ord's Precipice, Bostrom's vulnerable world hypothesis) supplies the final warning: the G.E.C.K.'s energy is also a destruction kit, and the cycle of war repeats until post-humanity or extinction.

transhumanism.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
transhumanism.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
transhumanism.relation: Novy asks whether it would be right to deliberately make a Spider-Man. Glaucon's Ring of Gyges challenge from Plato's Republic — that unchecked superpower breeds 'great corruptibility' — is made flesh in Doc Ock, Green Goblin, Lizard, and Morbius, while Bostrom's transhumanism supplies the movement the chapter defends. Against Fukuyama's bio-conservative worries about playing God, destroying equality, and violating a human essence, the chapter notes that Aunt May's bifocals and insulin already make her a cyborg, that Marvel grants personhood by behavior rather than biology (Kree, Skrulls, the Vision), and that the thought experiment of giving Mary Jane a painless 'super smile' shows we are at least sometimes obliged to enhance.

transhumanism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
transhumanism.title: Notes
transhumanism.relation: Dan Dinello reads the Borg as the nightmare double of Data: where Data embodies Asimov's Laws of Robotics and Federation humanism, the Borg realize Jacques Ellul's and Langdon Winner's thesis that technology is an autonomous, totalitarian force assimilating its makers rather than a neutral tool. He traces the Collective's shared mind and quest for 'perfection' to transhumanism (Max More, James Hughes), whose philosophical roots lie in Descartes's mechanical body and mind-as-information—the very premise of Ira Graves's consciousness upload in 'The Schizoid Man'. Picard's tear as Locutus and Hugh's acquired individuality in 'I, Borg' show that creativity and liberal humanist values, not technology, defeat the ultimate techno-totalitarian dystopia.

transhumanism.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
transhumanism.title: 11. Of Bats and Supermen
transhumanism.relation: Springett argues Superman, not Batman, is the right goal for a transhumanist future: through Merleau-Ponty's embodied cognition (Lois's deadline nausea, Alfred recovering a thought by redoing his posture, real-life 'Subway Superman' Wesley Autrey's gut-level rescue) he shows bodies shape thought and morality, so a super-body means a super-mind. Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' becomes 'what is it like to be Superman' — a problem of superhero minds, with Doctor Manhattan's indifference as the cautionary case — while Superman's rescues of the less fit show transcendence need not slide into eugenics or Social Darwinism.

transhumanism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
transhumanism.title: Post-Apocalyptic Perspectives
transhumanism.relation: Crippen reads the Continent's Great Frost and the Conjunction of the Spheres as apocalypse in the word's literal sense of 'uncovering,' binding environmental collapse, refugee migration, and a post-truth erosion of moral concepts into one crisis. Nietzsche's 'inverse cripples' and Plato's Phaedo (philosophy as preparation for death, truth as lifeless unchanging perfection) illuminate Yennefer's ageless barrenness and the witchers' suppressed emotions, while Degerlund's transhumanist breeding schemes and plans to cut out Geralt's eyes violate Kantian respect for persons. Filavandrel's starving elves parallel Indigenous dispossession, Dorregaray's 'natural equilibrium' and Zoltan's prediction that humans 'wait for a chance to make money from other people's mishaps' evoke ecological and social imbalance, and Geralt's old-fashioned virtues answer a post-apocalyptic, post-truth world.

transhumanism.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
transhumanism.title: I - THE LURE OF THE NORMAL WHO WOULDN’T WANT TO BE A MUTANT
transhumanism.relation: Hopkins dissects 'normal' as descriptive versus prescriptive and argues that who wouldn't want to be a mutant depends on where one's abnormality falls on axes of utility, social acceptability, and detectability. Storm's invisible, useful weather control lets her call cure-seekers cowards, while Rogue, who cannot touch anyone, and Beast, who cannot pass as human, have rational reasons to want normality, as do the underground Morlocks. Using Foucault's history of the 'monster' and the 'individual to be corrected,' he reads mutant passing against real-world passing by gay people and light-skinned African Americans, then weighs transhumanism against bioconservative natural-law views and closes with Nietzsche's 'man is something that should be overcome' to ask whether wanting to be extraordinary, or ordinary, is selfish either way.

transhumanism.title: “Sometimes Dead Is Better”
transhumanism.relation: Katherine Allen reads Pet Sematary and The Tommyknockers as bioconservative fables staging the transhumanism debate: Louis's resurrected, 'fundamentally wrong' cat Church and cannibal son Gage, and Bobbi's tooth-shedding 'New Improved' becoming, dramatize Kass, McKibben and Fukuyama's warning that erasing our limits erases our humanity. Against them she sets Nick Bostrom's 'Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant,' in which death is an unquestioned evil we should slay, and Bernard Williams's worry about the tedium of immortality. King's insistence that 'sometimes dead is better,' and that forbidden knowledge (the Micmac ground, the buried ship) works like an addiction, sides with the deathist view that mortality and finitude give life its meaning.

transhumanism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
transhumanism.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
transhumanism.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

impartial-spectator.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
impartial-spectator.title: Red Sox Fandom and Internal Harmony
impartial-spectator.relation: John McHugh uses his urge to confront Grady Little, who left a spent Pedro Martinez in during Game Seven of the 2003 ALCS, to ask how fans should govern the primal emotions fandom generates. Stoic self-command fails because Epictetus's advice (avoid caring about games entirely, focus only on what you control) would extinguish fandom itself, so McHugh adapts Adam Smith's impartial spectator: the virtuous fan imagines being watched by a sympathetic but emotionally distant fellow fan, settling on a Chicago Cubs fan who gets Bartman the way a Sox fan gets Buckner and Grady. He concludes that we each harbor a team of role-specific inner consciences, and the practical task is harmonizing the Red Sox-fan identity with our other identities rather than suppressing it or being consumed by it.

impartial-spectator.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
impartial-spectator.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
impartial-spectator.relation: Terjesen reads the O'Neil-Adams pairing as moral rationalism (Hal) versus moral sentimentalism (Ollie): Hal jails the boy assaulting slumlord Jubal Slade because 'He was breaking the law' and defends a racist senator's speech on free-speech principle, while Ollie works from the gut. Hume's 'Reason is and ought only to be the slave of the passions' explains both Ollie's effectiveness and Hal's collapse into Parallax, since no argument from Kilowog could restrain a grief only a stronger passion could. But sentiment needs an impartial filter: Smith's impartial spectator condemns Ollie's near-murder of Black Canary's attacker and his abandonment of the heroin-addicted Speedy, while Hal's cooler principle keeps the Native American land dispute from Ollie's violent plan. The conclusion is that morality is sentiment-based but reason must police it, so each hero needs the other.

impartial-spectator.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
impartial-spectator.title: NOTES
impartial-spectator.relation: Takes Claude's label of Peter as an 'empath' seriously and tests three accounts of empathy against his power: Hume's emotional resonance (rejected because Peter keeps powers after the donor leaves), Scheler's absorption into another's identity, and Hume's conversion of ideas into vivid impressions, settling on the mirror-neuron thought that Peter literally replicates other people's brain structures — which explains why he copies Isaac's painting skill and even Sylar's anger in 'Kindred.' It then asks whether empathy makes you moral and answers no — Elle enjoys Peter's pain and Mohinder feels his experimental subjects' terror — arguing instead that empathy needs a filter: Hume's general point of view and Adam Smith's impartial spectator, illustrated by Hiro's imagined Kensei ideal and by Nathan serving as Peter's emotional filter until his death leaves Peter without one.

impartial-spectator.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
impartial-spectator.title: The Office and Philosophy
impartial-spectator.relation: Asks whether Michael can (not will) ever learn empathy, distinguishing cognitive empathy - explained via Russell's argument-by-analogy account of other minds, which Michael manages only with people like himself, hence his sales success in 'The Client' - from affective empathy, which he lacks (Kevin's possible skin cancer is 'terrible news for both of us'; he cannot read Phyllis's oven mitt in Yankee Swap). Traces his cluelessness to egocentrism, and following Hume and Smith's sentimentalist account of morals - decentring the ego toward the impartial spectator via emotional contagion - argues his only hope is a real friendship (Jim's) that could drag him outside himself, since sycophantic Dwight and one-sided Todd Packer never will.

impartial-spectator.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
impartial-spectator.title: “This Is the Way”
impartial-spectator.relation: Holdier uses the imagined scene of stormtroopers roasting Grogu over a cookfire to test moral sentimentalism: our disgust at eating Baby Yoda either perceives moral truth, informs our motivations, or simply is our judgment, but popular sentiment cannot settle its aptness, since our culture happily eats sentient chickens - the same inconsistency fans felt when Grogu ate the Frog Lady's eggs in 'The Passenger'. Adam Smith's impartial spectator supplies the corrective standard: if a bias-free spectator would recoil at a Grogu barbecue, that feeling is appropriate, and by parity the same spectator should recoil at factory-farmed meat (via Singer's speciesism and Kasperbauer's infrahumanization). So Din Djarin's sentimental attachment to the Child, which overrides Guild code in 'The Sin', is vindicated as genuinely moral rather than merely subjective.

impartial-spectator.title: Chapter 3 Sympathy, Principles, and Conscience
impartial-spectator.relation: Robert Fudge uses Adam Smith to reinterpret Huck's conscience and praiseworthiness. Against Bennett (conscience as accepted principles) and Arpaly-Schroeder (inverse akrasia via a whole-self theory), Fudge argues, following Smith, that conscience is the sentiment-based judgment of the 'man within the breast,' the impartial spectator, and that propriety rests on sympathetic 'feeling with' others rather than abstract principle. Huck's sympathy for Jim in the chapter 16 raft scene is a reason-bearing emotion, so he is not acting akratically or against his true conscience; instead he is growing morally, molding his conscience toward the loyalty and friendship that already constitute his core self.

confucian-ren.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
confucian-ren.title: One with the Team
confucian-ren.relation: Chelsea Harry contends that Red Sox Nation embodies a Confucian rather than Cartesian self: against Descartes's cogito and the egocentric, endorsement-chasing player (A-Rod, the traded Manny), the Sox way treats selfhood as constituted by family, community and mutual sacrifice, from Mike Lowell's hometown discount to Yaz's hospital escape and Schilling's bloody sock. She maps Confucian benevolence (jen) onto Wakefield, Varitek and Ortiz describing how fan love powers their play, filial piety onto the retired numbers honoring franchise elders like Pesky, Doerr and Cronin, and Chung-ying Cheng's 'naturality' onto the fans' claim to be the team's twenty-sixth player, so Johnny Damon's defection reads as the treachery of an ungrateful villager. The 'je ne sais quoi' of team spirit is thus Confucian unity: becoming oneself by subordinating the I to the We.

confucian-ren.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
confucian-ren.title: Free Your Mind, and Your Roundhouse Will Follow
confucian-ren.relation: Young argues that dojo courtesy is not the fantasy that good manners win fights (Napoleon and the Karate Kid's Johnny lost on skill, not rudeness) but the framing of a craft within a way of life. He maps Aristotle's techne/ethos distinction onto the Japanese jutsu/do pairing to show founders like Kano, Funakoshi and Ueshiba treated fighting as one part of a whole ethical character, reads his seiza apology to an injured yellow belt through Confucian ren, li, yi and shu, and traces Shinto purity into the sincerity (kime) of committed sparring. His black-belt humiliation by seniors becomes Zen's 'courtesy of brutal': ego-deflating violence that trains no-mindedness (muga, Takuan Soho's fudoshin).

confucian-ren.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
confucian-ren.title: “Well, It Got Big Laughs”
confucian-ren.relation: Barkman uses Confucius (ren, yi, li, and zheng ming, treating each person according to what he or she is) and Aristotle (eudaimonia, virtue as a habituated mean between extremes, practical wisdom) to indict 30 Rock for valorizing Jack's 'semi-virtuous path', the smug middle between best and worst announced in 'Do-Over'. He catalogues injustices the show laughs off: Liz's serial lies about her age, hobbies, and adoption; Jack's priority flu shots for the powerful in 'Flu Shot'; Tracy's insubordination about dogfighting in 'Rosemary's Baby'; and Kenneth's servility as everyone's punching bag. On liberality and piety, Jack's confession that 'capitalism is my religion' and Liz's 'I pretty well do whatever Oprah tells me' show the show settling for semi-virtue, which the chapter says even comedy must not endorse.

confucian-ren.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
confucian-ren.title: Every Soul Experiences the Battle Within
confucian-ren.relation: Reads Zuko's arc as a war between Legalism and Confucianism: Ozai's agni kai scarring of his son, Azulon's death sentence, the Fire Nation Oath and school discipline ('The Headband') all enact Han Fei's principle that bad human nature needs terrifying sanctions, and Azula's 'trust is for fools' completes it. Against this stands Iroh's Confucian education in ren — teaching that honor cannot be separated from humaneness, that a mugger deserves tea and encouragement, and that wu-wei-like patience knows when to speak. Mencius's innate compassion explains why Zuko's 'amazing lie' realization could unfold, Katara, Sokka, and Hakoda embody Confucian filial bonds that adopt Aang, Toph, and finally Zuko, and Solzhenitsyn's gulag insight closes the chapter: the line between good and evil runs through every human heart.

confucian-ren.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
confucian-ren.title: Every Soul Experiences the Battle Within
confucian-ren.relation: Reads the Fire Nation royal family as a philosophical battle between Legalism (Han Fei, taking Xunzi's dictum that human nature is evil, so order requires terrifying sanctions: Ozai burning Zuko in the agni kai so 'suffering will be your teacher', Azulon's death sentence on Zuko, the Fire Nation Oath recited in schools) and Confucianism (Iroh teaching ren, that true honor cannot be had apart from humaneness, preferring honorable begging over theft, and talking a would-be mugger into tea). Zuko's 'battle within' is the legacy of his two great-grandfathers, Sozin's Legalism versus Roku's line, and it is resolved when he disowns Ozai, calls Iroh his 'real father', and is adopted into Team Avatar, whose filial bonds (Katara's care, Hakoda's sacrifice) contrast with the scheming royal family. The chapter closes with Solzhenitsyn's image of the line between good and evil passing through every human heart to explain why Zuko's inner war resonates.

confucian-ren.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
confucian-ren.title: “Your Heart Knows”
confucian-ren.relation: Argues that Disney's Mulan transplants a distinctly modern Western ideal of the authentic self ('true to your heart,' 'Reflection') into a Confucian honor culture where the self is constituted by roles and relationships, filial piety (xiao), and ren as the virtue that binds people into larger wholes — which is why the film flopped in China. The matchmaker debacle, Fa Zhou's 'I will die doing what's right,' and the family's shame show a culture where dishonor stains the whole family and even luck (the cricket Cri-Kee) fixes moral standing, conflicting with Western assumptions about individual responsibility. The chapter ends by noting Mulan now resonates with young Chinese viewers, asking whether the Western individualist self is a truth about humanity or a cultural export that, like the Huns, has scaled the Great Wall.

confucian-ren.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
confucian-ren.title: The Rhythm by Which We Live Our Lives
confucian-ren.relation: Kowalski interprets Kuzco's arc through Mencius: the emperor's pampered upbringing (eight hands replacing a squeezed toy, Yzma's loveless regency) is the 'hatchets and frost' of the Ox Mountain parable blunting his innate moral sprouts. The gorge scene stages Mencius's child-at-the-well thought experiment — Kuzco's spontaneous snatch of falling Pacha is a 'give-away' action betraying compassion he denies having, which Pacha diagnoses just as Mencius did King Xuan sparing the ox — and Pacha's family, quasi-adopting Kuzco, supplies the loving soil Mencius says the sprouts of ren need to grow.

confucian-ren.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
confucian-ren.title: Notes
confucian-ren.relation: Decker parallels the Republic's fall into Palpatine's Empire with the Zhou dynasty's collapse that birthed Chinese philosophy, reading three Jedi from the Dark Times comics through it. K'Kruhk, guided by the Zatoichi-like Master Zao, learns wu-wei - following the Force rather than forcing outcomes, with Laozi's Dao as the Force's Chinese analogue. Dass Jennir's struggle over what 'Jedi' means after killing a slaver becomes Confucian rectification of names and the cultivation of ren, while Kai Hudorra's loss of faith, withdrawal to a casino, and final sacrificial stand against Vader embody Mozi-style pragmatic minimalism redeemed by Jennir's virtuous example.

confucian-ren.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
confucian-ren.title: “Tell Your Sister, You Were Right”
confucian-ren.relation: Yang argues that Luke's surrender to Vader on Endor is neither foolish nor irrational but an exercise of Confucian filial piety: Luke reveres the absent Anakin as an exemplar (picked out through admiration of Obi-Wan's stories and the lightsaber), insists 'I know there is good in you' against Vader's claim that the name means nothing, and is vindicated when Anakin turns and says 'You were right about me'. His imperfect training under Obi-Wan and Yoda functions like Confucian ritual (li), forming habits that respond with harmonious ease to surprises such as Palpatine's trap, and filial piety extends past death in the funeral pyre Luke builds on Endor, honoring his father as the Analects prescribes.

confucian-ren.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
confucian-ren.title: NOTES
confucian-ren.relation: The Terjesens pit Kant's impersonal morality — Sam's contractual distance from the thieving Mickens is exactly how he would treat strangers — against Confucius and Mencius, for whom filial duties are the nursery of virtue: we learn benevolence by serving parents and revering elders, Lafayette's care for Lettie Mae and Tara shows family forming moral character, and the Upright Gong's covering for a father's sheep-stealing grounds Jason's 'sometimes the right thing to do is the wrong thing'. Mencius's King Shun, who abdicates and carries his criminal father into exile, models how Tommy and Jason should put family first while accepting the cost, while Mozi's universal love surfaces in Godric's 'forgiveness is love', and the chapter concludes that family counts only insofar as it develops our moral nature — the line between Tommy and Sam.

confucian-ren.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
confucian-ren.title: Third Hole Finding the (Fair)Way with Confucius and Ben Hogan
confucian-ren.relation: Laumakis builds an analogy between pursuing excellence in golf and living a flourishing human life, then contrasts two models. Reading Confucius's Great Learning and Analects onto golf, he casts a repeating swing as a 'well-ordered kingdom' rooted in self-cultivation, and reinterprets ren, li, yi, and xiao so the 'authoritative player' masters the game through ritual practice, a teacher-parent (xiao), and doing what is appropriate in each lie. Against this social conception he sets Ben Hogan's Five Lessons as a 'rugged individualist' account stressing solitary practice and personal responsibility, and proposes a contextual pluralism as a mean between communitarian absolutism and individualist relativism.

confucian-ren.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
confucian-ren.title: Fourteenth Hole Plato and Confucius on the Form of Golf From the Real to the Ideal
confucian-ren.relation: Stephen Laumakis stages a thought experiment pitting Plato the Idealist against Confucius the Realist/Pragmatist on how to think about and play golf. On Plato's theory of Forms, every club, ball and swing is an imperfect copy of a timeless, unchanging Form—there is a 'perfect' swing (Tiger Woods, Ernie Els) that par and the handicap system let us measure ourselves against, so golf is about striving toward the Ideal. Confucius, read through the 'Great Learning' and 'Analects' (li, ren, self-cultivation, unrelenting practice), instead prizes the situation-sensitive sage who negotiates each bad lie (Phil Mickelson's flop shots). Laumakis concludes the good golfer must integrate both: pursue perfection while wielding practical wisdom about when to go for it and when to lay up.

confucian-ren.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-ren.relation: The editors' introduction argues that the unifying theme of Lee's films is the struggle for authentic self-identity, framed through Charles Taylor's dialogical self and Kierkegaard's line that anxiety is the dizziness of freedom. It surveys how Confucian virtues (ren, li, xiao) and Daoist wu-wei play out across Pushing Hands, The Wedding Banquet, Eat Drink Man Woman, Crouching Tiger, Sense and Sensibility, Brokeback Mountain and others, treating each protagonist as caught between traditional obligation and personal desire. It invokes Nietzsche's claim that all philosophy is autobiography to justify reading Lee's films (he said 'it's all in my films') as a coherent authorial philosophy.

confucian-ren.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-ren.relation: Kohler-Ryan and Palmer treat 'sense' and 'sensibility' as a spectrum Lee explores through sisterhood in Sense and Sensibility (Elinor/Marianne) and Crouching Tiger (Shu Lien/Jen). Elinor and Shu Lien embody sense, Shu Lien specifically the Confucian balance of li and ren that lets her soften ritual with humanity; Marianne embodies Burke's British-Romantic sublime while Jen embodies Daoist immersion in the dao. Reading door-frames, windows, hair-combing rituals and Shu Lien's hairpin as symbols, they argue only Sense and Sensibility achieves integration in time, whereas Li Mu Bai's confession that he lived sense and sensibility as separate spheres comes too late.

confucian-ren.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-ren.relation: Bush argues that Brokeback Mountain transcends both the heterosexual western archetype and queer theory by presenting male sexuality through Mencius' philosophy and John Corvino's ethics of homosexuality. Using Mencius' four sprouts (ren, li, yi, zhi) and doctrine of natural goodness, he reads Ennis as the character in whom sexuality is contextual, cultivated and moral rather than merely physical, so the relationship between Ennis and Jack becomes an ethical friendship grounded in ren, the virtue Mencius says is most intense among friends. The bystanders Aguirre and Alma keeping the secret, and the final shirt-and-postcard scene, illustrate zhi as contextual moral judgment and homosexuality reframed as ethical rather than sexual.

confucian-ren.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
confucian-ren.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
confucian-ren.relation: Komasinski explains Confucius's advice to fathers through three ideas: ritual (li, glossed as 'cultural grammar' – engagement rings, saying 'I love you'), excellence/virtue as excelling at relating to others (ren, 'co-humanity'), and wisdom. Using the Analects' 'Upright Gong' passage (fathers and sons cover for each other) beside Plato's Euthyphro, he shows Confucius prizes the father-son bond over law, and reads the parable of the prodigal son and Tu Wei-ming's 'personality ideal' to argue fathers should lead by virtuous example rather than punishment.

confucian-filiality.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
confucian-filiality.title: 16. What Do We Really Owe Our Parents
confucian-filiality.relation: Karavitis uses Tris and Tobias to stage the filial-piety debate: Tris, who loves her parents and learns to see them with adult eyes after discovering their hidden pasts, remains 'allegiant' to the end, while the abused Tobias owes Marcus and Evelyn nothing and reaches only a cautious adult reconciliation with his mother. After surveying Confucian xiao (with Mencius, and Buddhism's forced accommodation of it) and the Abrahamic commandments on one side, and Norman Daniels's and Jane English's autonomy-based arguments that children never consented to be born and so owe nothing on the other, he concludes no rational argument mandates filial duties from adult children. Aristotle's three types of friendship supply the one defensible model: only when adult children and parents meet as virtuous equals can a chosen, consensual relationship carrying care, gratitude, and love arise - so 'as adults, we owe our parents nothing,' though love may freely flow.

confucian-filiality.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
confucian-filiality.title: 2. A Paragon of Righteous Virtue
confucian-filiality.relation: Allinson reads Gardner's novels, especially The Case of the Blonde Bonanza, as philosophy disguised as pulp: Mason acts from curiosity, compassion, and justice rather than utility, a 'pure Kantian or ancient Confucian' deontologist whose loyalty to clients ('erase ATTORNEY AT LAW from the door') functions as his own Categorical Imperative. The chapter's crux is the perjury dilemma of the Blonde Bonanza: Mrs. Winlock's offered false testimony would free Dianne Alder, which Mason twice refuses yet curses ('To hell with it'), showing that the plot's deus ex machina dissolves but never solves the ethical dilemma, while George Winlock's truth-telling-at-any-cost mirrors Kant's prohibition on lying even to the Gestapo. Socrates's better-to-suffer-evil, Plato's Meno reversal, Aristotle's rhetoric, Confucian and Hebrew filial piety in Dianne's character, and Rawls's justice as fairness all serve as lenses on Mason's virtues.

confucian-filiality.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
confucian-filiality.title: I think we've all arrived at a very special place, eh Spiritually Ecumenically Grammatically —Captain Jack Spa
confucian-filiality.relation: Miller uses Disney deaths to stage the philosophy of death: Plato's immortal soul and Phaedo's affinity argument illuminate Frollo's lust-driven plunge into hellfire, while Epicurus's atomism, his 'death is nothing to us' argument applied to Marlin's terror in Finding Nemo, and Lucretius's symmetry argument are tested against Coco, where Ernesto's forgotten 'final death' versus Hector's restored place on the ofrenda makes posthumous harm plausible. Aquinas's 'my soul is not me' grounds embodiment, Confucius makes Mulan's risking death for father, ancestors, and country a virtuous Confucian death, and Deloria's indigenous web of relations reads Mufasa's Circle of Life, Moana's grandmother, and Brother Bear's ancestral spirits.

confucian-filiality.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
confucian-filiality.title: NOTES
confucian-filiality.relation: Explains the seemingly incomprehensible things Heroes characters do for family by sorting their motives into three theories of family obligation: universal justice (framed by Socrates confronting Euthyphro for prosecuting his own father), care ethics' partiality to loved ones, and Confucian role-based duty with its asymmetrical parent–child, husband–wife, and sibling obligations. Noah Bennet turns out to be Confucian in practice ('I'm your father, Claire Bear') despite his universalist Company rhetoric, Hiro defies Kaito's Confucianism for the greater good while Kaito still teaches him the sword because that is a father's role, Niki and Janice act from care while D.L. and Micah act from roles, Mohinder's duty is Confucian sonship to his dead father, and the Haitian kills his own brother Baron precisely because stopping him is his brotherly role.

confucian-filiality.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
confucian-filiality.title: Dysfunctional Family Feud The No Special Obligations View
confucian-filiality.relation: Southworth and Tallman use David Spade's 'falling star' joke about Eddie Murphy, and Murphy's twenty-year SNL boycott, to test three theories of familial obligation against the show's self-described 'family.' The role-based Just Because View, identified with Confucian filial piety, condemns Spade's disrespect toward an SNL elder but also forbids Murphy's divorce from the family; the contractarian Reciprocity View says Spade owes Dennis Miller but not Murphy, unless Murphy's saving the early show counts; and Jane English's No Special Obligations View, on which family should work like friendship, love rather than debt, clears Spade entirely. Sketches from the Vogelchecks' kissing family to Dysfunctional Family Feud supply the counterexamples.

confucian-filiality.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
confucian-filiality.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
confucian-filiality.relation: Barkman distinguishes the self-evident natural law (general beneficence, special preference for family, piety to parents as Confucius taught, duties to the weak) from derivative rules like 'do not steal' and from positive law, concluding that Andrea's mermaid necklace looting question in 'Guts' is really about whether natural law still binds when the state has collapsed. He argues it does: Andrea's necklace is unowned and free to take, Rick taking surplus food from Andrea would be justified by equal claims to survival, and Carol's 'we can make new rules' polygamy proposal fails because the natural law is prior to any government. The cannibal hunters of Issues #61-66 show what happens without virtue and Aristotle's practical wisdom for weighing conflicting principles, and walkers are bad but not evil, while a Governor-like human who ignores the natural law 'reduces himself to the level of a walker.'

confucian-filiality.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-filiality.relation: Thompson argues that Lee's 'cowboy aesthetic' of rugged isolation in Brokeback Mountain (Ennis and Jack) and Crouching Tiger (Li Mu Bai, Shu Lien, Jen) is only apparent: the characters are always already embedded in Confucius' five cardinal relationships, read through Xunzi's darker view that selfish desire must be curbed by ritual and social hierarchy. Ennis and Jack seem lone individuals but are defined by ties to Alma, family and each other, and Jen's redemption comes when she abandons self-serving desire to re-establish her Confucian relationships. Citing Nietzsche's gloss on Aristotle that only a beast or a god lives alone, it concludes there is no truly isolated cowboy.
