confucian-filiality.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
confucian-filiality.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
confucian-filiality.relation: Balogun presents a traditional Yoruba-African conception of 'authentic' fatherhood as a holistic role – spiritual, moral, metaphysical, physical, and material – within an extended, collective family where paternal uncles and grandparents share fathering. He stresses moral education through alo apamo riddles, moonlight folktales (the tortoise, his wife Yonibo, and the priest), and proverbs, and argues contemporary fathers everywhere should learn from this model: total rather than piecemeal responsibility, storytelling over mere cartoon-watching, and treating children as 'ours' rather than 'mine.'

confucian-filiality.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
confucian-filiality.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
confucian-filiality.relation: Barkman, prompted by his wedding guests' shared discomfort with his best man's tattooed arms, sets out to dispel a 'Christian Confucian confusion' that reads piety as requiring a tattoo-free body. He shows Leviticus 19:28 and 1 Corinthians 6:19–20 condemn tattooing only where it signals allegiance to impure cults or misuse of the body, not tattooing in itself, and that Confucius's Hsiao King injunction against wounding the body one receives from one's parents was linked to tattoos only by Han Chinese racism against tattooed minorities. Citing General Yue Fei's mother inking loyalty on his back, he concludes ink can even be pious, though a child under a parent's legitimate authority owes obedience if forbidden it.

echo-chamber.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
echo-chamber.title: A Reply to facebook Critics
echo-chamber.relation: Wittkower answers critics who call Facebook broadcast narcissism by way of Sartre: Facebook actions (pokes, the Disney Princess quiz, cats friending cats on Catbook) have no given meaning, so users and their friends create it, which is why there are 'so many different Facebooks'. He takes up Sunstein's 'Daily Me' echo-chamber worry and Hegel's claim that real freedom means choosing within community, arguing Facebook merely makes the dialectic between chosen and unchosen communities explicit. Against the charge that status updates are trivial, he deploys Nietzsche's Last Man and Schopenhauer's cheese-mite microscope to defend caring about a friend's sandwich from the inside of a shared life.

contextual-privacy.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
contextual-privacy.title: 1 - The Privacy Virus
contextual-privacy.relation: Grimmelmann argues the claim that 'kids these days don't care about privacy' gets Facebook users wrong: they untag keg-stand photos, protest the News Feed launch, and reject friend requests because they care about contextual privacy - respect for the rules of distinct social contexts - rather than secrecy. The skeptic's public/private secrecy model mispredicts this, since posting to 300 friends is not broadcasting to the world. But Facebook is still a 'privacy virus': its architecture defeats the everyday 'know your audience' and 'safety in numbers' rules of thumb, so contextual violations like Bono's leaked photo albums and the accidental Christmas-ring announcement happen anyway.

convergence-culture.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
convergence-culture.title: 2 - It’s Like Talking to a Wall
convergence-culture.relation: Meikle analyzes Facebook as media convergence: status updates and wall posts blur one-to-one communication with the broadcast 'message addressed to nobody in particular', reaching an undifferentiated friend list that mixes intimates, colleagues, and people one dislikes. Cases like the MI6 chief's wife's holiday photos, Amanda Knox's 'Foxy Knoxy' nickname, the Dartmouth professor's Wikipedia lecture note, and the Dunblane survivors story show how private turns instantly public, from Bozeman's password demand to tabloid mining of profiles. He concludes that Facebook demands an ethics of online communication: who gets access to what we generate, and what may they do with it.

media-ecology-tetrad.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
media-ecology-tetrad.title: 3 - Ian Became a Fan of Marshall McLuhan on facebook and Suggested You Become
media-ecology-tetrad.relation: Bogost applies McLuhan - media as extensions of man, whose form rather than content is what matters - and the tetrad of media effects to Facebook, opening with his own inability to join the UCLA network to show that properties, not gripes, deserve study. He builds a full tetrad: Facebook enhances the directory, the yearbook, and nowness; obsolesces the reunion, memory, and the secret; retrieves the small town, the hang-out, and the diary; and reverses into campus life and high school. The point is that no medium is simply good or bad, and the tetrad itself becomes one more medium Facebook absorbs.

politeness-theory.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
politeness-theory.title: 4 - With Friends Like These, Who Needs Enemies
politeness-theory.relation: Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch, Mafia Wars) through Goffman's 'face' and Brown and Levinson's positive/negative politeness: recruiting friends into an application is a face-threatening imposition that becomes awkward across professor-student and parent-child hierarchies playing as nominal equals. She invokes Derrida on Mauss - 'there is no gift without bond, without bind' - to analyze the reciprocity obligations of gifting games, and finds emergent cooperative norms like PackRat pacts against tit-for-tat stealing. Players revolt when developers monetize asymmetrical play, showing communities negotiate the rules of the magic circle.

punctum-studium.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
punctum-studium.title: 5 - Profile Picture, Right Here, Right Now
punctum-studium.relation: Sarachan uses Barthes's Camera Lucida - punctum, studium, and the 'air' of the subject - to argue Facebook profile pictures are all punctum: ephemeral images constantly replaced to strike the viewer instantly, unlike the static yearbook photo. He sorts profile pictures by Barthes's six categories (pose at the webcam, hiding behind objects, Photoshop trick effects, photogenia, aestheticism, syntax) and reads pop-culture avatar images as identity claims. He closes with Benjamin's mechanical reproduction: a webcam image has no original, existing only as infinitely copied bits that paradoxically exist only when someone views the page.

online-disinhibition-effect.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
online-disinhibition-effect.title: 6 - You Can’t Front on facebook
online-disinhibition-effect.relation: Marinucci opens with Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Plato's Republic - invisibility licenses injustice because we care about seeming good - and maps it onto Suler's six factors of online disinhibition (anonymity, invisibility, asynchronicity, solipsism, dissociation, minimized authority). Facebook, she argues, lacks all six: real names and offline friends, near-synchronous news feeds, and the integration of every audience from mom to students into one space keep us inhibited. That inhibition is a good thing, since it prevents 'fronting' - presenting a false face to each audience - so Facebook identity integration can foster more authentic self-expression.

presentation-of-self.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
presentation-of-self.title: 8 - Playing Around with Identity
presentation-of-self.relation: Wandel and Beavers take Groundhog Day's Phil Connors as the model of trying on selves, and apply Goffman's dramaturgical Presentation of Self to see Facebook as a stage where users experiment with identity. Because friends from every part of life watch at once, a 'restraint of accountability' disciplines pretending, much like childhood pretend play or a fraternity's teasing calls members to account for their oddities. Against critics who see fragmentation and narcissism, they argue this dynamic can support becoming who one already is - a more authentic, grounded self - closing with Plato's 'Life must be lived as play'.

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 9 - Spectacle 2.0
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Vejby and Wittkower ask whether Facebook is Spectacle 2.0 by applying Debord's Society of the Spectacle: on the pessimistic reading, Facebook makes friendship a spectator sport where we alternate between watching friends and performing for them, with corporate owners setting the protocols. They then turn to the Situationist constructive side - situations, dérive, détournement - reading lolcats, rickrolling, and the parody status updates ('Facebook will automatically start plunging the Earth into the Sun') as playful détournement that approaches media as active agents. Their verdict is suspended: the new spectacle co-opts our participation, so the imperative either way is to repurpose, subvert, and play.

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 21 - facebook as Playground and Factory
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Scholz argues Facebook is both playground and factory: a space of publics where, in the Arendtian sense he opens with, power is 'the potential to act together,' and a machine that expropriates play as 'interactivity labor' — attention sold to advertisers, ten thousand volunteers translating the interface into sixty-three languages, and data trails aggregated, sold, and locked in a walled garden ('you can check out any time you like, but you can never leave'). Quoting Tim O'Reilly's 'they are participating without thinking that they participate,' he claims users generate surplus value they never see, while 'user uprisings' against the News Feed are mere Debordian spectacles of Internet democracy — enhanced consumer feedback loops. He ends by asking how to secure self-disclosure and meaningful collective action, pointing to non-commercial alternatives like Crabgrass, inside 'the playground that is a factory.'

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Altmann builds 20th-century totalitarianism from three TZ episodes: 'He's Alive' shows Aristotle's account of persuasion — rhetoric aimed at an audience's anger and fear — fueling Vollmer's neo-Nazi movement under Hitler's ghostly tutelage; 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' instantiates Eco's Ur-Fascist fear of difference, banning even Plato and Dostoevsky; and 'Deaths-Head Revisited' gives Lutze's 'I functioned as I was told' alongside Arendt's verdict on Eichmann's thoughtless, mechanical obedience. He then argues the phenomenon has mutated: Debord's society of the spectacle explains Black Mirror's 'The Waldo Moment' and 'Fifteen Million Merits,' where image-politics becomes authoritarian and even Bing's suicidal act of defiance is sold back as an avatar product.

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 20. The Totalitarian Zone
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Altmann assembles a 'time capsule' of totalitarianism from Twilight Zone and Black Mirror: Vollmer's neo-Nazi rise in 'He's Alive' as Aristotle's rhetoric, persuasion by playing on an audience's anger and fear, weaponized; Marilyn's forced Transformation in 'Number 12 Looks Just Like You' as Eco's Ur-Fascist fear of difference; and Lutze's 'I functioned as I was told' at Dachau as Arendt's banality of evil, the mechanical non-thinking of the Eichmann trial. 'The Waldo Moment' and 'Fifteen Million Merits' then carry the lens to Debord's society of the spectacle, where an empty cartoon bear wins crowds and even Bing's shard-wielding rebellion is instantly commodified into a product. The totalitarianism of screens, the chapter warns, needs no tanks.

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 3. Success and Failure of Punk
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Stock reads failure as fused into punk's circuitry from its origins: the 'WE KILLED ELVIS' billboard was a lie, since the Pistols, Clash, Ramones, and Damned covered their heroes and signed to majors. In a sequence of numbered theses built on Debord's Society of the Spectacle, Malcolm McLaren's Situationist merchandising, the Bill Grundy TV appearance as the moment punk became spectacle, and Adorno on the New Music, he argues punk's absorption into the spectacle of capital dooms it - Sid Vicious and Ian Curtis are 'authenticated' only by dying into pure spectacle - so to succeed as punk is to fail and to fail is to succeed.

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 25. Close Your Eyes, Breathe, and Stick It to the Man
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Seth Walker presents the Buddha ('Sid', Noah Levine's 'original rebel') as a punk who abandoned palace privilege after seeing sickness, aging, and death, teaching the four noble truths as a revolt against craving, caste, and blind tradition - the five precepts become 'punk-cepts'. He links Buddhist practice to punk through Straight Edge abstinence (Minor Threat's X), Brad Warner's Hardcore Zen, and 'skillful means', arguing that an inner rebellion must accompany the outer one since drugs and mindless violence are poorly channeled revolt. The Situationist International's 'spectacle' of passive consumption and Socially Engaged Buddhism (ordaining trees against deforestation, Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation, grounded in the doctrine of non-self) show both traditions demanding permanent revolution and community.

society-of-the-spectacle.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
society-of-the-spectacle.title: 13. Anthony Bourdain’s Antisocial Ethics
society-of-the-spectacle.relation: Kitchen and Scalambrino build Bourdain's 'ethics for travelers' around his tagline 'Be a traveler, not a tourist,' arguing he preferred authentic community over abstract, Capitalist-conditioned society. Using Guy Debord's Society of the Spectacle to characterize the tourist's 'corporate commodified darkness' and Kierkegaard's dictum about contemplating death daily, they show through the Bhutan and Lebanon episodes how Bourdain's food-based humanism values lived communal reality over consuming others' experiences as banal spectacle.

cicero-friendship.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
cicero-friendship.title: 10 - Why Can’t We Be Virtual Friends
cicero-friendship.relation: Condella tests Facebook friendship against Aristotle's three kinds (pleasure, utility, virtue) from Nicomachean Ethics VIII-IX and Cicero's De Amicitia: the average user's 281 friends far exceeds true philia, which needs time, reciprocated goodwill, and shared 'conversation and thought'. He grants that Facebook's status updates share conversation and thought and maintain ties across distance, evoking the Seinfeld episode where Jerry refuses Keith Hernandez's too-early request to help him move. But because no one has ever helped a friend move on Facebook, virtual presence cannot make us better people, and Facebook's artificial buoying of dead friendships of utility risks quantity crowding out the few deep friendships that matter.

relational-autonomy.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
relational-autonomy.title: 12 - Care Ethics, Friendship, and facebook
relational-autonomy.relation: Hamington surveys a hundred Facebook users and argues, through care ethics — Noddings's 'here I am' disposition and her natural versus ethical caring — that Facebook can make us more ethical, because the stream of small particulars about friends supplies the knowledge that is a necessary condition for caring. He uses Benhabib's concrete other to explain how status updates make distant lives 'real' to us, and confesses his own de-friending of a student over a racist comment as a case of Facebook's convenience making it easy not to care. The chapter ends by claiming Facebook dissolves the binary of close friend versus nodding acquaintance into a postmodern range of fluid, mediating friendships, while insisting caring is learned through the body and merely extended, not replaced, in virtual space.

relational-autonomy.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
relational-autonomy.title: 17. The Forking Bullshirt of Being Alone Together in the Good Place
relational-autonomy.relation: Hubbard-Mattix frames the show's central paradox, each person is responsible for her choices yet those choices are formed by her relationships, as a collision between the existentialism of Sartre's 'condemned to be free' and the feminist idea of relational autonomy. Each character embodies a failure mode: Eleanor's futile rejection of social dependence, Chidi's evasion of accountability in bad faith, Tahani's destruction by living for others' approval, and Jason's unexamined loyalty to Pillboi, Donkey Doug, and the Jaguars. Their failures before Judge Gen teach the audience to choose relationships that enable growth while still owning one's choices.

relational-autonomy.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
relational-autonomy.title: What We Have Learned, or “Always Let Your Conscience Be Your Guide!”
relational-autonomy.relation: Traces Disney disability from the medical model — Dopey as permanent childlike recipient of care, Gus-Gus, and LeFou, echoing Locke's claim that 'lunatics and idiots are never set free from the government of their parents' and Mill's restriction of liberty to those who can care for themselves — to the social model of disability in Finding Dory, where Charlie and Jenny's seashell trail makes the ocean an accommodating rather than disabling environment. Foucault's Birth of the Clinic explains how Gaston uses the asylum to control Maurice, medicine as power over lives. The chapter concludes that Pixar's Big Blue World embodies relational autonomy — Dory thriving 'in your own amazing Dory way' through supported interdependence — while nonverbal sidekicks Becky and Gerald show Dopey's disempowered comic-relief legacy survives.

relational-autonomy.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
relational-autonomy.title: 17. The Forking Bullshirt of Being Alone Together in the Good Place
relational-autonomy.relation: Frames the show's paradox — each person is responsible for her choices, yet her identity and choices are formed by her relationships — as Sartre's 'condemned to be free' colliding with relational autonomy, then reads each character through it. Eleanor's lifelong rejection of dependence (emancipation, bringing her own birthday cake) kills her and only unwinds through Team Cockroach; Chidi's indecision is named as bad faith that ends under an air conditioner; Tahani, defined by others' approval, is crushed pulling down Kamilah's statue yet confronts her parents in the Judge's test; Jason's blind loyalty to Pillboi and Donkey Doug shows dependence unexamined. The lesson: embrace both accountability and dependence by choosing whom you let close.

relational-autonomy.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
relational-autonomy.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
relational-autonomy.relation: Dryden asks whether the Lanterns' relationships are weaknesses or strengths. Epictetus's dichotomy of control would have recruits greet the Sinestro Corps' display of their families' eyeballs with Stoic indifference, and Kant brands fear for loved ones heteronomous; yet Donna Parker refuses the ring for her children, Amnee and Matoo Pree surrender their rings rather than stop loving, and Kilowog dines with energy constructs of his dead family, showing attachments partly constitute who people are. Feminist relational autonomy resolves the tension: Kyle escapes Parallax only by grasping Hal's hand ('we don't have to do it alone'), and Soranik Natu cannot excise Sinestro's crest or parentage any more than Donchin's Huntington's-disease daughter can sever family ties, so autonomy competency means negotiating unchosen relationships rather than escaping them.

relational-autonomy.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
relational-autonomy.title: Notes
relational-autonomy.relation: Barbara Stock uses the Borg to analyze autonomy: Picard's 'they took everything I was' names the Collective's destruction of self-governance, while Hugh's choice to return to the crash site in 'I, Borg' displays the Kantian core of autonomy—acting on universalizable principle against inclination. She defends relational autonomy through Janeway's pleading with Kes in 'The Gift' and the Ferengi woman's internalized oppression, then combines it with Clark's extended cognition to ask whether the Borg Queen's 'I am the Collective' might make the Collective itself an autonomous agent. Finally she judges Janeway's forcible de-assimilation of Seven defensible only while Seven is non-autonomous, and her promise never to let Seven return ethically suspect.

relational-autonomy.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
relational-autonomy.title: Ciri's Agency and Autonomy
relational-autonomy.relation: Vega and Barta read Ciri's Elder Blood power, which activates only through controlled female emotion, through Hélène Cixous's 'Laugh of the Medusa' and écriture féminine: her awakening scream at dying Calanthe's side and her cry of 'NO!' are forbidden female self-expression breaking patriarchal control. Renfri, silenced by Stregobor's narrative into villain and victim, and the bruxa Vereena, killed when her power exceeds her control, are the cautionary Medusas against which Ciri's mastery and the Lodge of Sorceresses' vote of 'sentimentality, gentleness, trust, and hope' to release her stand out. Calanthe's 'I bow to no law made by men who never bore a child' is pure écriture féminine undercut by her own complicity in auctioning Pavetta, and Ciri's final victory over Emhyr comes not through the sword but through tears, emotional expression defeating patriarchy's rationalizations.

conviviality.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
conviviality.title: Social Networking - How to Win Virtual Friends and Influence Virtual People
conviviality.relation: Written as a breakup letter to Facebook, the chapter first reconstructs the Frankfurt School hope that new media could overcome old mass media's passivity — Horkheimer and Adorno's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man, Althusser's ideology as the form of media — and then tests the site against Ivan Illich's criteria for 'convivial tools.' Briggle finds Facebook fails on Illich's terms: its public walls and News Feed force self-censored persona management before a mixed audience, and its shapeless, undifferentiated flood of updates leaves the user disoriented like Nietzsche's madman after the death of God. Because the site's 'grain' channels users into 'reluctant, hapless exhibitionism' and even imposes the obligation to join, he logs off, concluding that tools reflect our image more than they remake it.

conviviality.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
conviviality.title: 26. Be Like Johnny
conviviality.relation: George Dunn reads Johnny Ramone's transformation from Queens delinquent to disciplined band foreman through craftsmanship: the Ramones' identical uniforms, downstrokes-only rig, and synchronized stagecraft embody the tradesman's virtues, and the band's 'fun' is MacIntyre's good internal to the practice of rocking out, not external rewards like money or fame. Against punk's 'Year Zero' originality conceit, Girard's mimesis shows imitation is inescapable - even distinguishing yourself is negative imitation - so the Ramones' apprenticeship to rock-and-roll radio and the teenage band Yee Loi faithfully imitating Johnny (Mosrite replica, one-legged spin) illustrate how mastery of models produces genuine creativity and freedom, a Stoic self-sufficiency of the skilled worker. Illich's 'convivial' tools like iPhones and YouTube let DIY players build their own lane past the corporate gatekeepers.

excess-of-seeing.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
excess-of-seeing.title: 16 - facebook as an Excess of Seeing
excess-of-seeing.relation: Lattimore frames the teacher-student Facebook encounter with Bakhtin's 'excess of seeing' — the viewer always sees more of a person than the person can see of themselves (their face, the world behind their back) and so 'consummates' them — warning against building a 'creepy treehouse' by co-opting students' network for classwork. She explains generational differences in use (her under-25 students' in-joke statuses versus colleagues' quiz posts) through Goffman and Bateson's frames, Granovetter's weak ties, and Strauss and Howe's lifecycle phases, arguing each cohort frames the network differently. Practicing Bakhtin's sympathetic projection into another's profile lets users see themselves as others see them, so that no single photo or quiz consummates a life.

parasocial-relationship.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
parasocial-relationship.title: 17 - Do Status Updates Have Any Value
parasocial-relationship.relation: Fairweather and Halpern answer the Facebook-skeptic who dismisses status updates as vanity by reading them through Hume's 'natural sympathy' — our disinterested fellow-feeling with any well-presented human sentiment — which they identify with Clive Thompson's 'ambient awareness,' the pointillist portrait assembled from mundane updates. They argue Facebook's structure is a 'great equalizer': because friends need not know one another, no dominance hierarchies or intimacy rituals form, removing offline barriers to sympathy. The first-person, here-and-now grammar of updates invites exactly the quasi-first-personal curiosity that empathy requires, though they concede one-way, unanswered updates may show only that 'the machinery of morality' is revved up, not that users are morally improved.

parasocial-relationship.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
parasocial-relationship.title: Eyes Open: Taylor Swift and the Philosophy of Easter Eggs
parasocial-relationship.relation: Eline Kuipers explains Swift's Easter eggs - capital-letter messages in album booklets, the neon letters in 'ME!,' snake boots teasing reputation - as engineered puzzles that exploit a deep-rooted love of problem-solving and reward fans with an 'Aha!' moment. Each decoded egg is a parasocial interaction that strengthens a one-sided fan-celebrity bond marked by asymmetries of attention, communication, and knowledge (following Archer and Robb), giving fans belonging without rejection-risk. With Charles Taylor's dialogical account of identity she argues these bonds cannot support real identity negotiation - only the Swiftie community the eggs create, trading friendship bracelets and theories, can.

hume-natural-sympathy.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
hume-natural-sympathy.title: 17 - Do Status Updates Have Any Value
hume-natural-sympathy.relation: Fairweather and Halpern answer the Facebook-skeptic who dismisses status updates as vanity by reading them through Hume's 'natural sympathy' — our disinterested fellow-feeling with any well-presented human sentiment — which they identify with Clive Thompson's 'ambient awareness,' the pointillist portrait assembled from mundane updates. biopower.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
biopower.title: 19 - facebook, Surveillance and Power
biopower.relation: Doyle and Fraser open with the Lady Shelley Sawers affair, in which Britain's new MI6 chief was exposed by his wife's public Facebook profile, to ask whether social networks democratize surveillance or perfect it. They read the CIA's social-media monitoring, the Chris Dreyfus promotion case, and Facebook's Beacon advertising scheme through Foucault — Bentham's Panopticon, the carceral continuum, regimes of truth, and the shift to statistically managing populations — arguing that narcissistic self-display makes people 'most controllable,' while Habermas's public sphere frames the hopeful side: Beacon's defeat by user protest, Glassdoor, and Iran's Twitter revolution as diffused power against the centralized state. Foucault's answer is neither utopia nor repression but an ethics of self-management for playing power games with minimum domination.

biopower.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
biopower.title: 6. Who Has the Power
biopower.relation: Samuelson uses Foucault to dismantle Phillip Price's creed of being 'the most powerful person in the room': power is not a possession but an operation. Elliot's men in black and the FBI's surveillance are disciplinary power - Bentham's panopticon realized in Allsafe's cube farm and the internet itself - while Angela's fight over the Washington Township leak is a struggle with biopower that no sovereign can be punished for, and Whiterose's knowledge is power-knowledge that operates anonymously no matter who holds it. If Foucault is right, Price, Mr. Robot, and Zheng are mere conduits, and no one will ever be the most powerful person in the room.

biopower.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
biopower.title: 10. Babies and Pleasures
biopower.relation: Wesch uses Foucault's Discipline and Punish to explain how ordinary women so quickly served Gilead: power is exercised rather than possessed, so Offred enjoying the Guardians' frustration, the 'Her fault!' Testifying, and the Particicution show everyone wielding whatever power is within reach. Gilead is a panopticon in Bentham's sense—the Eyes, paired shopping, 'Under His Eye'—where unverifiable surveillance makes citizens their own overseers, while biopower sorts desirable from undesirable populations, 'making live' fertile Handmaids (shatterproof glass against suicide) and letting Unwomen and unbabies die in the Colonies. Resistance is Foucauldian too: Offred's remembered food, Moira's bathroom gossip, and sex with Nick are the 'bodies and pleasures' that counterattack the deployment of sexuality.

biopower.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
biopower.title: “Wherever I Go, He Goes”
biopower.relation: Bishop and Bishop map The Mandalorian's Outer Rim onto a taxonomy of power: Nevarro's lawlessness is Hobbes's state of nature out of which sovereigns like Palpatine ('a safe and secure society') carve order by social contract, the Guild's codes and Djarin's creed exemplify Foucault's disciplinary power, and the Client's and Dr. Pershing's harvesting of Grogu's biology - like the Kaminoans' cloning of Jango Fett - is biopower. Against this 'binds of power' ontology they set Grogu's helpless generation of love, a 'little way' that converts Djarin, Omera, Cara Dune, and Greef Karga, and culminates in Djarin twice unhelmeting for Grogu's sake, proposing an ontology of love rather than power as the galaxy's alternative.

ideal-speech-situation.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
ideal-speech-situation.title: 20 - Wall to Wall or Face to Face
ideal-speech-situation.relation: Bar-Tura, a Chicago Jewish social-justice organizer, evaluates Facebook by Habermas's ideal speech situation — equal chances to speak, initiate, and question, aimed at consensus — recounting how Jewish and Muslim teens scheduled to bowl together first met online and shed stereotypes by browsing each other's profiles. Yet face-to-face planning surfaced what wall-to-wall could not: the Shabbat timing question, and Muslim parents' unease about a north-side venue, which revealed socio-economic and racial divides rather than religious ones. Fixed, market-driven profile categories and the 'Daily Me' of niche idea consumption limit Facebook as a public sphere, so profiles must become people and the group must actually gather for social change.

He ends by asking how to secure self-disclosure and meaningful collective action, pointing to non-commercial alternatives like Crabgrass, inside 'the playground that is a factory.'

power-as-acting-together.relation: Scholz argues Facebook is both playground and factory: a space of publics where, in the Arendtian sense he opens with, power is 'the potential to act together,' and a machine that expropriates play as 'interactivity labor' — attention sold to advertisers, ten thousand volunteers translating the interface into sixty-three languages, and data trails aggregated, sold, and locked in a walled garden ('you can check out any time you like, but you can never leave'). Quoting Tim O'Reilly's 'they are participating without thinking that they participate,' he claims users generate surplus value they never see, while 'user uprisings' against the News Feed are mere Debordian spectacles of Internet democracy — enhanced consumer feedback loops. He ends by asking how to secure self-disclosure and meaningful collective action, pointing to non-commercial alternatives like Crabgrass, inside 'the playground that is a factory.'

lacan-symbolic.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
lacan-symbolic.title: 23 - Faking It on facebook
lacan-symbolic.relation: Muhr and Pedersen apply Žižek's interpassivity — canned laughter and hired funeral 'weepers' that enjoy or mourn on our behalf — to Facebook, arguing the profile is a surrogate self that enjoys, believes, and suffers for us while being frantically kept alive like a Tamagotchi. The motive, they argue, is escape from the demands of the symbolic order (the Lacanian system of social expectations Žižek works with): our offline identity is 'already a mask,' and Facebook defers rather than removes the duty to be a good, enjoying, authentic person. Since, as in Žižek's comparison of German, French, and American toilets, ideology operates at the level of action rather than belief, users 'fake it till they make it' — performing vibrant, interesting lives until the faked feelings become real.

lacan-symbolic.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
lacan-symbolic.title: 23. Louis C.K. Meets the Unconscious
lacan-symbolic.relation: Reads the 'of course, but maybe' bit as a wrestling match between Lacan's big Other—society's unwritten rule book of queues, taboos, and approval—and the Freudian unconscious that betrays itself in the therapist's 'the climax results in the death of the woman' slip and other parapraxes. Jokes then work as sublimation and a release valve: Louis's nut-allergy and slavery bits ('you all clapped for dead kids... you don't get to cherry-pick') let audiences laugh at their disavowed 'I know very well, but...' contradictions, though comedy remains confession without absolution.

lacan-symbolic.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
lacan-symbolic.title: 24. An Hour
lacan-symbolic.relation: Argues Louis's shift to an hour-a-year of digressive storytelling—spurred by George Carlin's 'dig deeper' tribute speech and forced by fatherhood—is 'secular revelation' in Adam Phillips's sense: his wandering bits work like the free play of the signifier and free association, so the stage becomes staged therapy in Lacan's return-to-Freud mode. The chapter reads the trumpet purchase as anxiety speaking through parapraxis, the street-sign and 'suck a bag of dicks' bits through Saussure's arbitrary sign and Derrida's catachresis, and Louie following Tarese home as desire that self-consciousness cannot account for.

lacan-symbolic.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
lacan-symbolic.title: 12. Not Why but Who
lacan-symbolic.relation: Reads the mothers of Orphan Black through Freud and Lacan: Dr. Coady is the "phallic mother" at the center of the Castor clones' Oedipal drama (Rudy's kiss, the DNA trophies brought home to Mom), Tomas is Helena's abusive false father, Rachel is the child of a shattered Oedipal triangle, and the Symbolic Order that makes men active rational subjects and women passive reproductive objects is mirrored in the defects — neurological for the male clones, reproductive for the female. The chapter then brings in Luce Irigaray to show the show rewriting these stereotypes: the clones' spectrum of personalities and their constant impersonations destabilize fixed gender categories, and the many equally "real" mothers (Mrs. S., Amelia, Alison, Kendall) burst the woman-equals-womb equation. Beth's counsel to the delirious Sarah — "Stop asking 'Why?' and start asking 'Who?'" — becomes the feminist move from mechanism to women as active subjects.

lacan-symbolic.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
lacan-symbolic.title: The Golden Power
lacan-symbolic.relation: Patrick Dugan reads Miyamoto's game design through Lacan: the player forms a dyad with the avatar — Link is named 'Link' precisely because he links player to system — while the wider gameworld of places and characters constitutes the social symbolic the dyad lets us explore. The Triforce symbolizes the triangular structure of this interactivity: Courage is the dyad-anchor (the player-Link bond completed by mastery), Power is the game system's trinity of sword, bomb, and arrows (whose final loop defeats Ganon in A Link to the Past), and Wisdom is the realization that all such symbolic trinities — Christian Trinity, Hindu triad, three branches of government — are representations posing as totality, with the empty center of the Triforce marking what no system captures. The 'golden power' is seeing the game being played on you, whether by designers or by society.

lacan-symbolic.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
lacan-symbolic.title: Notes
lacan-symbolic.relation: Reads the Cohle–Hart pairing through Lacan: Cohle is at peace with the constitutive lack introduced after the mirror stage, and his hysteric's fixation on the Other's desire is what makes him the superior interrogator, while Hart exhibits obsessional neurosis and 'interpassivity,' letting the preacher's congregation do his believing for him. Following Deleuze's Oedipal structure of detective fiction and Hegel's point that heroes are denied guilt, the chapter compares Rust to Oedipus — both men who, after a child's death, renounce the father function through anti-natalism — while arguing Cohle surpasses Oedipus by philosophically mastering the knowledge that Oedipus lacked. Rust's tying off of his 'circle of violence' is read as the Lacanian sinthome: putting his symptom to work in the service of the case rather than being destroyed by it.

lacan-symbolic.title: 18. Repeating Twin Peaks
lacan-symbolic.relation: Komel argues repetition is both a structural principle of the TV series (every show repeats its pilot) and the key to Twin Peaks, invoking Nietzsche's eternal recurrence, Kierkegaard, and Lacan/Žižek. Using Lacan's aim-versus-goal of desire and Žižek's 'coffee without milk' as a positive absence, he reads Laura Palmer as a 'positive absence' around which the series turns, and shows the murder repetitions are out of order—Maddy's on-screen death precedes and retroactively produces Laura's in Fire Walk with Me. Laura's final scream in The Return, unlike its predecessors, subversively rewrites the original, so 'The Return' is really 'The Repetition' that undoes its origin.

lacan-symbolic.title: Monstrous motherhood
lacan-symbolic.relation: The chapter argues that horror films about mothers are not static representations but Foucauldian sites where 'discourses of motherhood' are produced, policed and contested; using Foucault's account of bodies disciplined through power/knowledge, it treats films as cultural artefacts that both enforce and challenge norms of 'essential' and 'ideal' motherhood. It reworks Sarah Arnold's Lacanian 'Good Mother/Bad Mother' schema (the mother who sacrifices herself so the child enters the Symbolic and submits to the Law of the Father) alongside popularised Freudian mother-blame (the 'refrigerator mother', 'tell me about your mother') to read Psycho's Norma(n), the phallic mothers of The Killing Kind and The Brood, and the doomed single mothers of The Ring, Silent Hill and Triangle. It coins the 'monstrous-maternal' to argue that motherhood is framed as always-already monstrous because no woman can meet the impossible, shifting criteria of ideal motherhood, illustrated through Grace's Vivian/Madeline generational clash and Serial Mom's Beverly Sutphin.

lacan-symbolic.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
lacan-symbolic.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
lacan-symbolic.relation: Juniper Ellis shows tattoos resist any single interpretive scheme by running through cases: Loos and Lacassagne's criminological 'I tattoo, therefore I will commit murder'; the biblical Mark of Cain and St. Paul's stigmata as signs of protection and salvation; Lacan's claim that the tattoo is the first signifier that marks off the human subject; and Pacific tatau (Te Pehi Kupe's moko-as-signature, Queequeg's unreadable Moby-Dick tattoo) that incorporates a person into a collective. She reads Kant's Critique of Judgment dismissal of Maori tattooing and invokes Levinas' 'the face speaks' to argue a tattooed face is eloquent speech, crossing lines between individual and collective, saint and criminal.

interpassivity.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
interpassivity.title: 23 - Faking It on facebook
interpassivity.relation: Muhr and Pedersen apply Žižek's interpassivity — canned laughter and hired funeral 'weepers' that enjoy or mourn on our behalf — to Facebook, arguing the profile is a surrogate self that enjoys, believes, and suffers for us while being frantically kept alive like a Tamagotchi. The motive, they argue, is escape from the demands of the symbolic order (the Lacanian system of social expectations Žižek works with): our offline identity is 'already a mask,' and Facebook defers rather than removes the duty to be a good, enjoying, authentic person. Since, as in Žižek's comparison of German, French, and American toilets, ideology operates at the level of action rather than belief, users 'fake it till they make it' — performing vibrant, interesting lives until the faked feelings become real.

hedonic-calculus.book: 053 - Martial Arts and Philosophy - Beating and Nothingness
hedonic-calculus.title: Don’t Carry the World upon Your Shoulders. Only Your Opponent
hedonic-calculus.relation: Cooper and Taylor argue that Kano's judo principles, seiryokuzenyou (maximum efficiency) and jitakyouei (mutual welfare and benefit), echo Bentham's principle of utility: both men swept away archaic rules to reach one efficient ethical goal, and Kano accepted the comparison. They run the hedonic calculus over training bruises versus the joy of a clean throw, use Mill's secondary principles as rule-utilitarian guidelines (release the armbar at the tap rather than calculating each time), and answer the objection that utilitarianism demands too much with Kano's own ethos: like judo, it is about continual improvement, not impossible maximization.

hedonic-calculus.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
hedonic-calculus.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
hedonic-calculus.relation: Allaire argues walkers have no moral value and can be killed without remorse: a Bentham-style act-utilitarian tally favors killing any walker, and, following Kant, genetic humanity is neither necessary nor sufficient for membership in the moral community. Applying Mary Anne Warren's five personhood criteria, he shows walkers lack pain response (Hannah's severed half still dragging itself at Rick), language, planning (Glenn's gun-bag mission versus aimless shuffling), and self-reflection, so as beings incapable of duty they can have no rights. Morgan's inability to shoot his walker-wife and Rick's 'I'm sorry this happened to you' illustrate Kant's 'duality of the human situation' — we irrationally project personhood onto former people — and our hesitation is precisely the walkers' greatest advantage.

hedonic-calculus.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
hedonic-calculus.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
hedonic-calculus.relation: Bateman replies to Cogburn that Law and Chaos descend not from Kant but from Michael Moorcock's Eternal Champion stories, where they are liberal and conservative political tendencies held in check by the Cosmic Balance, which restores Chaotic Good, Lawful Evil, and the Druid's true Neutral as viable positions. He rejects the 'sausage machine' universalization of maxims for Kant's humanity formula and Realm of Ends, and argues act utilitarianism makes a poor model of Good: an overpopulation scenario could mandate genocide, and Bentham's felicific calculus cannot actually measure the good. Alain Badiou's ethic of truths supplies the positive case for Chaotic Good—pursuing what you take to be good without submitting to a single moral law—while Buddhist and Jain renunciation dignifies Lawful Neutral.

hedonic-calculus.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
hedonic-calculus.title: Justified and Philosophy
hedonic-calculus.relation: The chapter argues Ava Crowder lives by hedonism - from Aristippus's pursuit of pleasure to Bentham's utilitarianism - with Bentham's censorial principle (weighing everyone's happiness) stripped out: she kisses Raylan moments after shooting Bowman, takes over Audrey's, orders the murder of Ellen May, and in Season Five has Penny dislocate her arm for infirmary access, kills Judith in the chapel, and finally informs on Boyd to Raylan for her own release. Bentham's seven-dimension hedonic calculus (intensity, duration, certainty, propinquity, fecundity, purity, extent) supplies the framework for each choice, and the verdict is that Ava's pleasure-maximizing left her directly or indirectly responsible for three deaths - which, for her, is all that matters.

hedonic-calculus.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
hedonic-calculus.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
hedonic-calculus.relation: Ketcham greets Piper Kerman at the prison door with Bentham's ghost: the state's utility calculation of her drug money laundering, the rat's discounted sentence, and the design of the panopticon, whose one-way inspection tower was meant to make surveillance cheap, obedience automatic, and prisoners productive and even saved. He contrasts that reform vision with the reality reconstructed from the book, where punishment falls on everyone, including families paying commissary prices and denied visits, and Danbury's 'vocational training' amounts to changing light bulbs. Bentham's own principle that 'punishment is an evil' is turned against a system that warehouses rather than rehabilitates.

hedonic-calculus.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
hedonic-calculus.title: 6. To the Pain
hedonic-calculus.relation: Robison-Greene imagines the table of contents of Count Rugen's definitive book on pain, using the Zoo of Death and The Machine as her case studies. Bentham's dimensions of pain - intensity, duration, and propinquity - organize the analysis of Westley's torture, including Rugen's tactic of leaving The Machine beside the prisoner so anticipation itself hurts, and the metaphysical oddity of having years stolen from the far end of one's life. Mill's higher and lower pleasures explain why the orangutan's prolonged death disturbs us more than other kills (a chimpanzee can reflect on what is happening to her), and Singer's speciesism grounds the argument that animals' pain behavior shows they suffer, so inflicting it merely because they are animals is indefensible; by contrast Westley's empathy lets him out-sadist the sadists with the 'to the pain' speech.

hedonic-calculus.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
hedonic-calculus.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
hedonic-calculus.relation: Eberl asks whether the Dude's 'pure abiding' is happiness: he runs Bentham's utility calculus on Dude-style pleasures (bowling's fecundity, the rug's purity, attending Marty's dance quintet for long-term rent goodwill) and Mill's higher/lower pleasures (Maude's vaginal art versus Logjammin'). Aristotle's verdict is that the Dude is not flourishing — his pleasures are incomplete, losable (the burned Torino), and he neglects his rational, social nature — yet Aristotle also ranks friendship with Walter and Donny highly, and Pieper's leisure, built on Aquinas's contemplation, gives the Dude's leisure a partial defense: he is incomplete but not bad, and he 'lives' while achievers merely make a living.

hedonic-calculus.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
hedonic-calculus.relation: Reitsma defends keeping the 'second-rate' Olympic men's football tournament against Bob Harig's 'Simply the best' litmus test, which would de-roster any event that is not the pinnacle of its sport. He likens Harig's proposed 'Olympic calculus' (scoring sports on tradition, parity, marketability) to Bentham and Mill's utilitarian maximization of a single value, and rejects both as oversimplifying an irreducibly plural decision. He argues the IOC instead rightly practices casuistry, case-by-case judgment that requires Aristotelian practical wisdom, and that dropping men's football (an under-23, FIFA-hampered tournament) would sacrifice the Olympics' global breadth for a false ideal of excellence.

hedonic-calculus.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
hedonic-calculus.title: 16. Psycho-historian or Psycho Historian
hedonic-calculus.relation: Bellantoni asks what Seldon owes future generations, pitting moral presentism against his 'mystical' identification with humanity (echoing Scheffler's Why Worry about Future Generations?). She tests the Seldon Plan under Bentham's hedonic calculus—finding time-discounting and uncertainty about what follows the thirty-thousand-year interregnum undercut it—and under Kantian deontology, arguing Seldon's mass manipulation of Gaal Dornick, his inquisitors, and the Encyclopedists treats people merely as means and violates their autonomy. Weighing longtermism against Whitehead's claim (in Adventures of Ideas) that civilizations must die to seed new ones, she suggests Seldon's engineered revival of a spent civilization may itself be a barbaric imposition on future people who would not choose it.

hedonic-calculus.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
hedonic-calculus.title: 2. To Eat or Not to Eat
hedonic-calculus.relation: Barta and Miranda read Bourdain's 'good eating is all about risk' credo through Bentham's cost-benefit hedonic calculus, sorting risk/reward into Ascetic, Epicurean, Cyrenaic, and Utilitarian quadrants. They classify Bourdain's fugu-eating and drunk cliff-driving as failed calculations, his comfort-food returns as Epicurean, and his gluttonous adventures (French Laundry, Russian vodka) as Cyrenaic high-risk/high-reward living.

confucian-junzi.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
confucian-junzi.title: In All Fucking Seriousness
confucian-junzi.relation: Arp asks why well-placed 'fucks' in Onion headlines like 'Guy In Philosophy Class Needs To Shut The Fuck Up' are funny, and answers with the golden mean traced to Aristotle and Confucius, who both prized self-control and being a good role model to children: swearing is virtuous when it hits the mean between the vice of too much (gangsta rap's every-other-word profanity, the cemetery gardener's rant, Glengarry Glen Ross) and the vice of too little. He sorts Onion stories into vice tables—'Loved Ones Recall Local Man's Cowardly Battle With Cancer' illustrates the vice of cowardice, with courage as the hitting-the-mark mean—and concludes that a well-placed fuck is both funny and virtuous precisely because so many people treat the word as taboo.

confucian-junzi.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
confucian-junzi.title: Notes
confucian-junzi.relation: Barcenas and Bein pit Kant against Confucius on the Prime Directive, opening with Kirk's Nibiru volcano rescue of Spock in Into Darkness. Kant's categorical imperative—universalization and respect tests applied to Scotty's dilemma in 'Bread and Circuses' and Worf's 'not a matter of degree'—makes the Directive absolute, while Confucius and Aristotle ground morality in cultivated character: a junzi like Picard may bend the rule when virtue demands it, as in 'Pen Pals' and rescuing Wesley from the Edo in 'Justice'. They conclude Starfleet needs both: the Kantian rule for most officers, and exemplary persons like Picard to know when the rule fails.

confucian-junzi.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
confucian-junzi.relation: McRae reads Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon as a dramatization of the tension between Confucian humanism and Daoist naturalism over how to cultivate an authentic 'focus-field' self. Li Mu Bai and Yu Shu Lien are exemplary persons (junzi) bound by the wuxia code and li, unable to voice their love, while Jen rebels into criminal freedom under Jade Fox; Li's use of the green bamboo forest against Jen embodies wu-wei and rou (yielding suppleness). It argues that authentic self-cultivation, and Jen's final leap, require balancing Daoist natural freedom against Confucian roles, since freedom without relationships exacts a fatal price.

correspondence-theory-of-truth.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
correspondence-theory-of-truth.title: Progress
correspondence-theory-of-truth.relation: Gregory Gilson argues that although The Onion deliberately reports falsehoods, it embodies postmodern theories of truth better than the newspapers it parodies. Lyotard's mercantilization of knowledge and the fragmentation of dominant narratives into separate language games explain headlines like 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity' and 'Astronomer Discovers The Center Of The Universe Is His Beautiful 9-Year Old Son,' which smash incompatible discourses together, while Baudrillard's simulacrum and hyper-reality explain how The Onion — like Disneyworld — is branded fake precisely so mainstream media can seem real. Yet the chapter closes honestly: its own criticism of 'Bush Says He Still Believes Iraq War Was the Fun Thing To Do' assumed some targets were wrong, which assumes a Truth out there — the paradox of a satire whose truthfulness exceeds its own theory of truth.

correspondence-theory-of-truth.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
correspondence-theory-of-truth.title: 4. The United States of Gilead
correspondence-theory-of-truth.relation: Greene argues that the contemporary United States under Trump exhibits early Gilead-like symptoms, detailing five shared techniques: othering (the Aunts' stereotypes of pre-Gilead women vs. Trump on Mexicans and Muslims), separating children from parents (Handmaid births and seizure of Hannah vs. immigrant detention camps), gaslighting (Janine's 'her fault' Testifying vs. inauguration-crowd and Mueller claims), discrediting dissent (Gilead's ban on reading vs. 'fake news'), and lying (Gilead's founding promise of elections vs. thousands of false claims and 'alternative facts'). He grounds the danger in the correspondence theory of truth: once leaders detach belief from how the world actually is, society is a small step from Atwood's dystopia.

correspondence-theory-of-truth.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
correspondence-theory-of-truth.title: 10 Fact, Truth, and Evidence A Lesson from Dr. Tyree
correspondence-theory-of-truth.relation: Dean Kowalski stages an imagined dialogue between Indy and William E. Tyree — Harrison Ford's real Ripon College philosophy professor, whom Ford's own script rewrite placed 'right down the hall' — to show that 'archaeology is the search for fact, not truth' is self-defeating if truth is correspondence with reality. Tyree's epistemology primer (principles of evidence, inductive generalization, hypothesis testing like Indy's Sankara-stone glow prediction, and Ockham's Razor) explains Indy's resistance to the God hypothesis despite witnessing the Ark, the Grail's instant healing of Henry Sr., and the invisible bridge he crossed on guesswork rather than knowledge. The resolution: Indy practices methodological naturalism, keeping deeper truths out of archaeology, without being committed to metaphysical naturalism.

correspondence-theory-of-truth.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
correspondence-theory-of-truth.title: 24 “Some of the Passageways in Here Can Run for Miles” An Aristotelian Exploration of Fact and Truth in The La
correspondence-theory-of-truth.relation: Reconstructs Indy's Barnett lecture — 'archaeology is the search for fact, not truth' — as a syllogism with a suppressed premise, then tests it with Aristotle's correspondence theory of truth (Metaphysics 1011b), syllogistic logic, and the Aristotelian division of the sciences into practical, productive, and speculative (via Aquinas on what all sciences share). The lecture's conclusion is falsified by five 'witnesses': Indy goes on to chase lost cities, follow maps, and admit 'X' really does mark the spot in Venice, so some premise must be false. And since every science pursues truth while Indy himself digs for the Good ('it belongs in a museum'), philosophy cannot be confined to Dr. Tyree's classroom down the hall.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: “Howzat!” Prometheus Is a Fast Bowler
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Decker argues the Doctor's morality resists formula — his motives are private, his timey-wimey perspective complicates consequentialist calculation, and the 'Genesis of the Daleks' child hypothetical breaks rule theories like Kant's and Mill's — so he reads it as an 'ethics of ambiguity' fusing Romanticism (Shelley's imagination, the infinite glimpsed in cups of tea and small beautiful events, Romantic-Gothic divided consciousness) with Sartrean existentialism. Via Sartre's WWII student, bad faith, and Beauvoir's 'adventurer' contrasted with the sub-man and the serious man, he casts the Doctor as a Gallifreyan Prometheus whose gifts of freedom are both dreadful and delightful.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Robison-Greene applies Beauvoir to the show's women. Powerful men are the One and women (like Chalky's community under the Klan) are made the inessential Other, and Beauvoir's apparatus - bad faith, the 'appeal' free beings must make to one another, and the happiness that lets women be complicit in their own oppression - frames Lucy, Gillian, and Margaret. Lucy happily performs the role her men write for her, Gillian is so consumed by the fact of her rape that even her apparent freedom keeps her the object of male desire ('just the loneliest person on earth'), while Margaret - Temperance Leaguer, advocate for women's reproductive health, and finally the woman who shuts the door on Nucky's cash - comes closest to making the appeal and to freedom.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Babette Babich traces the shifting 'you' of 'Hallelujah' and 'Suzanne' through Hegelian thesis-antithesis-synthesis and Empedocles's cycle of Love and Strife, reading the songs' ambiguity (David, Samson, the bound champion) as Cohen's sovereign having-it-both-ways. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity frames the human condition of being what one is not, while Nietzsche - on broken promises, on women and distance, on the Antichrist - supplies both the critique of Cohen's courtly projections onto the feminine Other and the model of singularizing solitude. 'Who by Fire' is read against the Rosh Hashanah prayer Unetanneh Tokef as a song of fate, judgment, and atonement whose closing 'who shall I say is calling?' is quasi-Augustinian and Heideggerian: death singularizes each 'who' at the moment of its claim.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Walker contrasts Pennsatucky's Christian fundamentalism with Piper's secular humanism (Kurtz's six features) in their 'Fool Me Once' confrontation. With no God, Sartre's existence precedes essence makes Piper condemned to create her own meaning: owning her crime to her mother and confessing the Pennsatucky prank, while Red and Vee play Sartre's cafe waiter, reducing themselves to chef and dealer, and Pennsatucky's 'defender of the unborn' persona is de Beauvoir's sub-man sheltering behind ready-made values. Marx's opium-of-the-people analogy explains why comforting, unverifiable belief can block the authentic, responsible pursuit of a meaningful life.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 8. Laughing in the Face of the Absurd
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Argues that watching Beth die on the platform is Sarah's existential awakening — the absurd realization that "it is no longer true that everyone has their own face" — analyzed through Camus's absurd (the impossible and the contradictory), Sartre's nausea at inhuman humans, and Beauvoir's "subman" who never wakes from the mechanical life. Sarah must repeatedly witness "her own" death (Beth, Katja, Jennifer, the Helsinki clones), which robs death and life of settled meaning, yet she refuses nihilism: exercising the radical freedom Sartre says grounds all values, she fights Dyad on behalf of everyone's freedom, implicitly choosing it for all humanity. Like Camus's Sisyphus, whose rock is his thing, her struggle is her thing — and the Season Two clone dance party is her laughing in the face of the absurd.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 9. When Jumpin’ Jack Flash Met Ziggy Stardust
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Auxier reads the 1973 Jagger-Bowie intimacy and rivalry ethically: Keith Richards's portrait of Mick's envy frames Kierkegaard's Either/Or warning against the aesthetic life and the Kantian morality-duty wedding Bowie fled, against Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity, which demands that one own one's freely chosen hollowing-out without appeal to any authority. Beauvoir's bad faith and authenticity then explain the outcome - Bowie beat Jagger by killing Ziggy, firing the Spiders, and finally making his very death a persona ('authentically Bowie'), while Jagger, forever only the Stones' singer, can respond only in bad faith, because 'hell is other people': each glimpsed the faker in the other.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 12. Dilbert Is an Asshole and That’s Why He’ll Never Be Happy and Nobody Loves Him
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Elsby and Luzecky argue Dilbert's unhappiness is chosen: from 400 rejections he concludes the women lack quality, he calls insult-bombing gentle kidding, and when Dogbert cites man's rational essence he chooses to watch all-star wrestling, each a textbook Sartrean bad faith where he glimpses the truth and flees it. Measured against Aristotle's eudaimonia he lacks every virtue of the Nicomachean mean (courage as the midpoint of fear, rightly scaled ambition, wit), and since one swallow does not make a summer his whole life, not a day of it, could earn the name happy. The December 2017 addictive-app strips complete the verdict: Dilbert monetizes a zombie-making app for a raise, making him Beauvoir's serious man from The Ethics of Ambiguity, the intelligent sell-out who subordinates human value to a hierarchy he knows is hollow.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 6. Serena Joy, Miserable, Despicable
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Elsby refuses to see Serena Joy as a self-determined villain, arguing she annihilates her own freedom—negating her humanity in Beauvoir's sense—to become an empty vessel for Gilead's will. Working through Aristotle on coerced and 'mixed' actions and the bad-upbringing excuse, Sartre on freedom and responsibility in Being and Nothingness, and Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity, she asks how much blame an oppressed woman deserves who nonetheless helped build her own subjugation and holds June down during the Ceremony. The answer runs through bad faith: Serena deceives herself until raping June is no longer a necessary wrong but a good in itself, and the 'unwomen' logic echoes Boethius's claim that evildoers cease to be human—comprehensible, but still abhorrent.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 13. The Origins of Self-Love
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Anna Marie Fennell reads RuPaul's 'If you can't love yourself, how in the hell you gonna love somebody else?' through theories of self-love. Erich Fromm's four elements of love and Buddhist non-attachment (Jinkx Monsoon's 'water off a duck's back,' the Season Ten Inner Saboteur characters like Eureka's Eufilthior) ground the claim that self-love precedes healthy love for others. Against Aristophanes' myth in Plato's Symposium - the round beings split by Zeus, forever seeking their other half, retold in Hedwig and the Angry Inch - she sides with Ru: completion comes from within, not from a soulmate. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity (the sub-man and nihilist archetypes seen in self-sabotaging queens like Nina Bo'Nina Brown) and bell hooks's All About Love with Branden's six pillars of self-esteem map onto winners like Jinkx, Sharon Needles, Violet Chachki, and Bianca Del Rio, whose drag personas show existence preceding essence.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: What It Is Like to Be Out of the Asylum
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Ron Novy argues nobody can know what it is like to be Batman: deploying Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' and a Mary's-Room variant with a color-deprived Barbara Gordon, he shows subjective experience resists even complete physical knowledge. Simone de Beauvoir's situated freedom then explains how 'one bad day' (Bruce's parents' murder, the Joker's Red Hood plunge into chemicals) threw each man into the same terrifying glimpse of Kant's noumenal world behind appearances, yet into opposite narratives of order and chaos. Even while sharing the joke that ends The Killing Joke, Batman and the Joker remain mutually unknowable, each the only one who can 'keep up' with the other.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Notes
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Hackett contrasts Frank's ethical egoism - acting like an invisible Ring of Gyges wearer who pushes Zoe in front of a train and kills Peter once they cannot be controlled - with Beauvoir's existentialist ethics, in which consciousness is a 'nothing' whose freedom is real only when it wills and sustains the freedom of others. Peter's drunken enslavement and Zoe's freely chosen deal with Frank illustrate the ambiguity of a freedom that is still causally situated, and Frank's Season 3 miscalculations with Jackie, Remy, and Claire show egoism's inability to weigh others' self-interest. Claire's sympathy for Michael Corrigan and her final walkout dramatize her learning Beauvoir's lesson that promoting others' freedom is the condition of one's own, the difference between self-interest and existential freedom.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Notes
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Contrasts Frank's ethical egoism with Beauvoir's existential ethics: Frank moves like an invisible Ring-of-Gyges wearer-murdering Zoe, reading everyone's self-interest-yet because he treats others purely as instruments his freedom is never 'prolonged through the freedom of others', and it fails in Season 3 when he miscalculates Jackie, Remy, and Claire. Claire's awakening through Michael Corrigan and her final walkout dramatize the Beauvoirian lesson that consciousness is freedom-as-nothingness whose values we remain collectively responsible for, not a license to will anything.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Note
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Held's introduction frames Wonder Woman as an ambiguous figure - a sexy superhero, feminist icon, even a god - and borrows Simone de Beauvoir's term 'ambiguity' from The Second Sex to name women's bind: acquiesce to gender norms and lose yourself, or become yourself and lose your place. He runs through Diana's either/ors (Steve Trevor, Themyscira or Boston, mortal or god, American or cosmopolitan) and argues she creates an identity only by defining herself against each expectation. Because everyone is torn between what they are and what they want to become, he concludes we should embrace Wonder Woman's contradictions and stake our commitments while living in ambiguity.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Notes
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Wright reads Wonder Woman's 75-year history through Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman,' arguing Diana's move from Paradise Island to Man's World - surrendering eternal life for Steve Trevor - enacts the hard-won transcendence of immanence that The Second Sex demands. She shows the comics alternating between empowerment (Marston's 'woman of tomorrow,' an unpatriotic George Washington scolding women war workers) and regression (Trevor persuading Wonder Woman to marry and type memos about women's place being the home, the 1990s hyper-sexualized art), evidence that woman remains the Other to man's Subject. Wonder Woman's durability, she says, lies in exactly this ambiguity, and like Beauvoir's woman of tomorrow she models forging identity through projects in the world.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Notes
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Zanin surveys 75 years of Wonder Woman - Marston's bondage-inflected feminism (the Ordeal of a Thousand Links, bracelets that forfeit power to any man who chains them), Kanigher's romance-era drift, the 1968 Diana Prince fashion-bouticless era that opened just as feminists protested Miss America, and the Taco Whiz years - to ask whether 'wonder woman' has become an unattainable ideal that belittles women. Reading through Beauvoir's analyses of woman as Other, imposed femininity as immanence, and the body as situation, she argues the superwoman 'have it all' standard is a feminist faux pas, yet closes with Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity: rather than resent her perfection, women should accept the challenge on their own terms instead of acquiescing in mediocrity.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Notes
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Johnson-Moxley tests Perez's lasso of truth - which makes people face truths about themselves, like being dragged from Plato's cave - against four ethical touchstones: Kantian duty (truth-telling as a perfect duty, respect for autonomy), utilitarianism, virtue ethics, and care ethics. Cases drive the argument: binding Ares so he sees his apocalypse annihilates what he rules, freeing Vanessa from Dr. Psycho's false memories only with her permission, and lashing two warlords into 'twins of pain' to end bloodshed. She concludes via Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity that compelling truth is justified only to restore someone's rational self-direction, never paternalistically, with Gandhi's satyagraha ('truth-force') as the model of active, compassionate truth-telling.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: “Howzat!” Prometheus Is a Fast Bowler
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Kevin S. Decker argues the Doctor's morality is an "ethics of ambiguity" poised between Romanticism and existentialism, not any formula. Rejecting positivism, deontology, and utilitarianism as fits for the Doctor, he reads the Doctor's freedom, wandering, and rejection of Time Lord values through Sartre's radical freedom and bad faith (the student torn between mother and Free French) and Beauvoir's "adventurer" who confers value by choosing. The Romantic search for the infinite in small things and the Prometheus myth frame the Doctor as a liberating, self-defining moral exemplar.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 272 - Motherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Birth of Wisdom
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: MOTHERHOOD
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Elizabeth Butterfield reads her exhausting early motherhood through Simone de Beauvoir's The Ethics of Ambiguity and The Second Sex, arguing that 'the ideal mother,' like 'true womanhood,' is a social construction and that a mother is 'freedom in situation,' never a mother 'the way a stone is a stone.' She recasts Beauvoir's 'serious man' as the 'serious mother' who flees her freedom into the Motherhood Religion, and invokes Sartre's 'condemned to be free' and 'Hell is other people' (No Exit) to advocate the honest, self-aware 'genuine mother' over inauthentic self-sacrifice.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: Who is Who
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: This chapter tests the Doctor's ethics against consequentialism and Kantian/Nagelian deontology, arguing both fail because his alien longevity and time-travelling relation to consequences resist algorithmic moral judgment ('School Reunion,' 'Attack of the Cybermen'). It proposes instead de Beauvoir's 'ethics of ambiguity' rooted in Romanticism and Sartrean radical freedom and bad faith (the student anecdote; Turlough refusing the Enlightenment diamond), casting the Doctor as a Promethean figure who liberates companions into risky self-perfection.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: NOTES
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Carolyn Korsmeyer uses Aristotle's Poetics dictum that the 'probable impossible' beats the possible improbable to argue popular narrative can actually conduct philosophy, not merely illustrate it. Her central case is that the TV series Angel—the ensouled, guilt-cursed vampire who concludes 'if nothing we do matters, then all that matters is what we do'—independently arrives at the same existentialist position as Simone de Beauvoir's The Ethics of Ambiguity, with no textual borrowing. She contrasts The Matrix's dramatically sustained Cartesian dream-doubt against the 'improbable impossible' Dallas dream-season, showing why one is a philosophical vehicle and the other bankrupt.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 304 - Introducing Philosophy Through Pop Culture - From Socrates to South Park, Hume to House
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: The Price of Existence
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Mann reads Stephenie Meyer's Twilight through Simone de Beauvoir's The Second Sex: Bella is the "relative being" who orbits Edward like a satellite, valued only through the constant masculine gaze, embodying the adolescent girl's renunciation of her "I can" body. Mann finds a buried feminist subtext — Bella's desire, Edward's restraint, and her vampire transformation into a fierce, powerful equal — but ultimately faults Meyer for reinstating the old promise that a woman gains subjecthood through self-annihilation in a sovereign man's eyes.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 15. Grey’s Anatomy as Philosophy Ethical Ambiguity in Shades of Grey
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: The chapter argues that Meredith Grey embodies Simone de Beauvoir's existentialist ethics from The Ethics of Ambiguity, rejecting the childlike 'spirit of seriousness' that treats moral rules as absolute. Through episodes where Meredith stabilizes a bomb inside a patient's chest, coaches a death-row inmate to induce his own brain death, switches an Alzheimer's-trial placebo for Adele, and commits insurance fraud to treat an immigrant child, it shows her breaking institutional protocol to positively will the freedom of others while owning her choices. It contrasts her authentic embrace of moral ambiguity and risk against Shepherd's, Bailey's, and Webber's rule-bound seriousness or self-interest, framing medical dilemmas as an ambiguous moral realm where no single correct answer exists.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 49. A Serious Man as Philosophy The Elusiveness of Moral Knowledge
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Biderman reads the Coens' A Serious Man through Beauvoir's figure of the 'serious man' (from The Ethics of Ambiguity), the man who craves a single absolute value and blinds himself to moral complexity: physics professor Larry Gopnik, beset by divorce, a bribing student Clive, and Sy Ableman's death, seeks moral knowledge that would let him be such a man. The chapter argues Larry's quest fails across cognitivist, noncognitivist, and pluralist accounts of moral knowledge, showing moral knowledge to be elusive if not impossible. The film's Kafkaesque fables (the Dibbuk, the Goy's Teeth, Rabbi Nachtner's 'L'olam ha-ba', Schrodinger's cat, and the Binding of Isaac in Caravaggio's painting) all stage the absurd collapse of interpretation, echoing the Book of Job, which Maimonides read as a parable rather than history.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 64. George Carlin as Philosopher It’s All Bullshit. Is It Bad for Ya
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Engels reads Carlin's insistence that 'it's all bullshit, and it's bad for ya' as a defense of truth over comforting illusion, mapping his bits onto Plato's Allegory of the Cave (Carlin dragging audiences up from shadows like 'prostitution is immoral' or 'the American Dream' to expose deeper essences), Nozick's Experience Machine (Carlin's sun-worship chosen because it is real, not a pleasing fiction), and Clifford/Beauvoir on the ethics of belief and the 'serious world.'
