Bits on rights, the sanctity of life, homelessness/'houselessness,' and 'proud to be an American' show Carlin arguing that false beliefs breed complacency and harm, so there are moral reasons to prefer truth.

ethics-of-ambiguity.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
ethics-of-ambiguity.title: 75. Phoebe Waller-Bridge as Philosopher Conscious Women Making Choices
ethics-of-ambiguity.relation: Pande and Engels argue that Fleabag and Lulu (Crashing) embody Sartrean authenticity: they own their choices, balance facticity and transcendence, and stay outside bad faith, while the men (Anthony, the Priest) fall back on pregiven roles and let 'the Look' or their fundamental project decide for them. Fleabag's addressing the camera and finally shutting it out is read as breaking the gaze of the Other; the Priest choosing priesthood over love exemplifies denial of transcendence. Through Beauvoir's Second Sex, woman-as-Other, and ethics of ambiguity, they show Waller-Bridge's transgressive, sexually frank women reclaim self-definition, arguing viewers 'could do better to be' the kind of free, choosing women her protagonists are.

romanticism.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
romanticism.title: “Howzat!” Prometheus Is a Fast Bowler
romanticism.relation: Decker argues the Doctor's morality resists formula — his motives are private, his timey-wimey perspective complicates consequentialist calculation, and the 'Genesis of the Daleks' child hypothetical breaks rule theories like Kant's and Mill's — so he reads it as an 'ethics of ambiguity' fusing Romanticism (Shelley's imagination, the infinite glimpsed in cups of tea and small beautiful events, Romantic-Gothic divided consciousness) with Sartrean existentialism. Via Sartre's WWII student, bad faith, and Beauvoir's 'adventurer' contrasted with the sub-man and the serious man, he casts the Doctor as a Gallifreyan Prometheus whose gifts of freedom are both dreadful and delightful.

romanticism.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
romanticism.title: Notes
romanticism.relation: Reads "The City on the Edge of Forever" through Romanticism: the Guardian of Forever strands Kirk and Spock without historical reference points - a nihilist moment of pure meaninglessness - and Kirk's Romantic response is to rebuild the narrative of the past even at the cost of letting Edith Keeler die. Hegel's philosophy of history explains the compulsion to record (Spock's anguished "I've missed taping centuries of living history"), why Edith's unwitting world-historical role is to die under a truck rather than lead a pacifist America to Nazi conquest, and Novalis's call to "make the world Romantic" frames Spock's self-rescue as young Selek in "Yesteryear". Kirk, Spock, and McCoy become Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy archetypes - Tragic Hero, Apollonian, Dionysian - converging in the street scene where McCoy lunges to save Edith, Spock waits on logic, and Kirk, seizing McCoy's arms, finds a tragic beauty in her death.

romanticism.title: 9. My Dharma Is the Road that Never Ends
romanticism.relation: Potter and Cobb argue that Twin Peaks is a Romantic refusal of resolution: mysteries live by not being solved, so Lynch and Frost break the rules that stories need authors, protagonists who solve problems, and endings. They read Cooper's entrapment in a time loop through Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati (quoting The Gay Science and The Will to Power), tie Wally Brando's Dharma speech and Isaiah Berlin's Roots of Romanticism to the theme, and argue the real 'story' is the endless meta-narrative co-created between the show and each viewer—Life itself as process without endpoint.

kripke-naming.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
kripke-naming.title: Love and Doctors
kripke-naming.relation: Asks whether 'the Doctor' is a Kripkean rigid designator naming one individual or a non-rigid role filled by different people, using the Ninth Doctor's deathbed doubts and the Time Crash memory loop to settle on the rigid reading. He then deploys Locke's body/organism/person distinctions, Parfit's overlapping psychological-connectedness fix to Reid's transitivity objection (Sarah Jane across 1983-1996-2006), and the amnesia-prone regenerations and the Valeyard to show the organism survives regeneration while the person might not. Finally he argues that because DoctorTwo in 'Journey's End' shares all the Doctor's psychologically connected memories of Rose, fission makes them two persons with equal claim, so Rose gets the person she actually loved.

kripke-naming.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
kripke-naming.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
kripke-naming.relation: Casetta and Tambolo dissect the 'Frankenfood' metaphor: metaphors map a familiar source domain (the Monster) onto a poorly known target (genetically modified organisms, like the 'Frankenfish' salmon), but the mapping fails because the Monster is a genetically heterogeneous chimera assembled from dead bodies while the engineered salmon is a genetically homogeneous hybrid grown from a single fertilized egg. Framing the question with Aristotle's view of metaphysics as the study of what things ultimately are, and applying Kripke-style origin essentialism and natural-kind essentialism, they show that being a patchwork is no essential property at all - our own symbiotic bacteria outnumber our 'human' cells - so Monster and GMO are not entities of the same kind. The metaphor should be discarded as intellectual junk, yet its allure persists because the living corpse-patchwork disturbs our fantasy of ourselves as pure, unmixed organisms.

kripke-naming.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
kripke-naming.title: 17. Who Is “Rick” Anyway
kripke-naming.relation: Starting from the mangled sentence 'Rick is the Rickest Rick who ever Ricked', the chapter asks what the name 'Rick' refers to in a multiverse. It contrasts Saul Kripke's view, names rigidly designate the same person across imagined counterfactuals, which would absurdly make the Council of Ricks one many-located Rick, with David Lewis's counterpart theory, each possibility a real world of world-bound duplicates. The show sides with Lewis: the Council says 'Rick C-137', C-137 works like a distinguishing last name, and Morty's 'I eat breakfast twenty yards away from my own rotting corpse' in 'Rixty Minutes' is true only because the corpse belongs to a Morty just like him. The chapter ends by noting Lewis never handled inter-reality travel, so which Summer C-137 Morty now refers to remains open.

kripke-naming.book: 143 - Batman and Philosophy - The Dark Knight of the Soul
kripke-naming.title: All Joking Aside, This Is a Modal Muddle
kripke-naming.relation: Sam Cowling and Chris Ragg ask whether Batman could have been the Joker, using the Indiscernibility of Identicals and the Necessity of Identity over possible worlds to argue that if 'Batman' is a name of a merely possible individual, he could not have been identical to the Joker. The 'Robin argument' (many people have been Robin) pushes back that 'Batman' might be a disguised description, and the authors then treat Batman and the Joker as abstract fictional characters whose modal properties are stipulated by their authors. On that view the Elseworlds tale Batman: Two-Faces, where the two are literally one Jekyll-and-Hyde person, shows Batman could have been the Joker after all.

kripke-naming.book: 162 - Final Fantasy and Philosophy - The Ultimate Walkthrough
kripke-naming.title: Final Fantasy and Philosophy
kripke-naming.relation: Andrew Russo and Jason Southworth use the recurring Cid in every Final Fantasy game and the apparently identical Cloud Strife of FFVII and FF Tactics to test theories of reference: direct reference theory trivializes informative identity claims like 'Squall is Leon,' and Russell's descriptivism, names as abbreviations for definite descriptions, handles Cid but stumbles on Cloud, whose FF Tactics birthday makes him an Aquarius rather than a Leo, and on a Spira where Schmidt, not Braska, actually defeated Sin. Kripke's causal-historical theory, with its dubbing ceremonies and name-transference chains illustrated by Yuna tracking the Tidus lookalike in X-2, answers the modal challenge but faces the qua problem of 'Balamb Garden has moved,' leading the authors to call for a reflective equilibrium between the two theories.

kripke-naming.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
kripke-naming.title: The Office and Philosophy
kripke-naming.relation: Nys uses Brent's quiz grievance about Mr. Spock (half-Vulcan, half-human) and his Crufts pedigree-dog analogy, Gareth's 'look at the ears' classification test, the dwarf/midget/elf/pixie interrogation of Alex, and Tim and Dawn's 'lethal blow' prank to introduce the problem of natural kinds. Realist answers come from Kripke (water is H2O whatever we call it), Aristotle's matter-and-form essences, and the DNA evidence separating Bornean clouded leopards from mainland cousins, while Wittgenstein's language games and Quine's point that our innate similarity senses mislead support the constructivist that we lay classification on an unstructured world. The verdict: nature supplies real differences but never carves itself into kinds, and the line-drawing remains up to us.

kripke-naming.title: Love and Doctors
kripke-naming.relation: Paul Dawson asks whether the Doctor dies when he regenerates by separating body, organism, and person. Using Kripke's rigid vs non-rigid designators he weighs whether 'the Doctor' names one individual or a role (the numbered Doctors, 'my replacements'), then applies Locke's memory criterion and Reid's transitivity objection, adopting Parfit's psychological-connectedness chain (via Sarah Jane's overlapping memories). He concludes the organism survives regeneration necessarily while the person survives only if psychological continuity holds, and argues the 'Journey's End' metacrisis Doctor Two is genuinely the person Rose loved through branching/fission.

lucretian-nature.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
lucretian-nature.title: Hope
lucretian-nature.relation: Beck reads Snakes & Arrows as popular Epicureanism delivered by Lucretius' method: just as De Rerum Natura puts honey on the rim of the cup so Romans swallow philosophical medicine disguised as poetry, Rush's melodies smuggle reflection on pain, luck, and religion past listeners who think they are just rocking, with repeated choruses doing the work of Epicurean prolepsis. The random swerve of atoms explains 'The Larger Bowl''s unequal fortunes ('Some are blessed and some are cursed'), while the shore-watcher's relief at another's shipwreck and the concertgoer's pleasure exemplify Epicurean ataraxia. 'Faithless' and 'Armor and Sword' ('Pray and pass the ammunition') echo Lucretius' trampling of superstitious religio, and the chapter closes with Philodemus' Herculaneum scroll: don't fear god, don't worry about death.

lucretian-nature.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
lucretian-nature.title: Chapter 30 - “The Golden Man”
lucretian-nature.relation: Jeremy Pierce reads 'The Golden Man' through the Aristotle-Lucretius dispute over purposes in nature: Cris Johnson, the precognitive golden mutant, first terrifies the DCA as Homo superior, 'a deeve who would be to us what we are to the great apes', until George Baines finds 'virtually no frontal lobe... It's nothing but an animal' choosing by reflex rather than reflection. Aristotle's teleology - normal development suiting what is objectively good for a human being - makes sense of calling one-armed growth, autism's deficits, or Cris's missing inner life deficiencies, while Lucretius's anti-teleology, largely adopted by the autism community, permits talk only of the typical and atypical. The chapter argues the characters' horror at humanity's replacement by reflex-driven breeders is unintelligible unless something is genuinely missing that is natural and healthy for human offspring.

lucretian-nature.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
lucretian-nature.title: GARDENING
lucretian-nature.relation: Campbell explains why Epicurus set his school in a walled garden on the edge of Athens ('Live unnoticed'), contrasting it with the Stoics' public Stoa: the Garden was a self-sufficient community of friends pursuing ataraxia through natural, necessary pleasures and philosophy as therapy for the soul. Drawing on Lucretius's account of prehistory in On the Nature of Things, he shows the Epicureans saw cities as a decadent fall—driven by the fear of death and the gods—from a near-paradise of proto-Epicurean friendship pacts, and read the garden and the locus amoenus of pastoral picnics as a recovered golden age. Diogenes of Oinoanda's inscription imagines a future in which all become gardening philosophers and city walls become redundant.

abjection.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
abjection.title: Rule Number One
abjection.relation: Aaron Anderson reads Season 4's cold open - the Trinity Killer's slow, intimate bathtub murder - against Dexter's 'clean' detached kills to introduce Kristeva's abjection: the corpse and spattered blood that threaten the boundary of self. He argues Harry's first rule ('Don't get caught') governs the show's aesthetics too - by hiding the abject results of Dexter's kills and softening them with dark humor and voice-over, the series spares viewers abjection so we can safely identify with a vicious serial killer, until Rita's murder finally forces both Dexter (for only the second time, after his mother's death) and the audience to experience it.

abjection.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
abjection.title: The Witcher and the Monstrous Feminine
abjection.relation: Cameron reads Geralt's battles with the striga (Foltest's cursed daughter by his sister Adda) and the bruxa Vereena in 'A Grain of Truth' through French feminist theory: Cixous's claim that women are frozen 'between the Medusa and the abyss,' Irigaray's reading of Nietzsche's feminine hysteria, and Kristeva's abject maternal in Powers of Horror. Both stories are phallocentric - men deliberate while Adda never speaks and Vereena can only scream - and in both the female monster is sacrificed to restore the symbolic order, Nivellen's curse broken by Vereena's death at Geralt's silver sword. Geralt himself is abjected: bitten and bled by the striga in her own crypt, nursed wounded at the Temple of Melitele, he becomes permeable and monstrous in her place, paying the cost of policing the patriarchal boundary.

abjection.title: Gynaehorror as convention and challenge
abjection.relation: This introductory chapter defines 'gynaehorror' as horror rooted in women's reproductive bodies (menstruation, virginity, pregnancy, motherhood, menopause), reading films like Inside, Vigil, Teeth, Alien, The Brood and Rosemary's Baby through it. It leverages Deleuze and Guattari's rhizome/becoming to reframe the monstrous female body not as a fixed molar 'being' but as a productive, boundary-breaching 'becoming', while positioning woman as the abject Other against which the male subject defines himself. It argues horror is simultaneously conservative (punishing women) and potentially radical.

abjection.title: Monstrous motherhood
abjection.relation: The chapter argues that horror films about mothers are not static representations but Foucauldian sites where 'discourses of motherhood' are produced, policed and contested; using Foucault's account of bodies disciplined through power/knowledge, it treats films as cultural artefacts that both enforce and challenge norms of 'essential' and 'ideal' motherhood. It reworks Sarah Arnold's Lacanian 'Good Mother/Bad Mother' schema (the mother who sacrifices herself so the child enters the Symbolic and submits to the Law of the Father) alongside popularised Freudian mother-blame (the 'refrigerator mother', 'tell me about your mother') to read Psycho's Norma(n), the phallic mothers of The Killing Kind and The Brood, and the doomed single mothers of The Ring, Silent Hill and Triangle. It coins the 'monstrous-maternal' to argue that motherhood is framed as always-already monstrous because no woman can meet the impossible, shifting criteria of ideal motherhood, illustrated through Grace's Vivian/Madeline generational clash and Serial Mom's Beverly Sutphin.

abjection.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
abjection.title: 23. Punk and Disgust
abjection.relation: Sara Bergstresser reads punk's shocking bodily transgressions - COUM Transmissions' Prostitution exhibit, GG Allin's stage defecation, Iggy Pop's self-mutilation, L7's thrown tampon - through Mary Douglas's Purity and Danger, Martha Nussbaum's Hiding from Humanity, and Julia Kristeva's Powers of Horror. Disgust polices social boundaries: Nussbaum shows how disgust-based obscenity law historically targets minorities, while Kristeva's abject (corpse, menstrual blood, excrement) marks the collapse of self/other boundaries that punk performers deliberately cross, with punk musicians added to Kristeva's list of those who dare approach the abject. The chapter asks whether the disgusting can be art, closing with Eco's claim that ugliness is passion against beauty's detachment, and with feminist performers like Jack Off Jill using blood and 'ugliness' as protest against the policing of female bodies.

philosophy-of-music.title: Sound, Music, and Vision
philosophy-of-music.relation: Ben Abraham asks why Halo 2's music cannot keep up with a speedrun like Cody Miller's: Martin O'Donnell's pre-composed, linear scores have only an accidental 'forced marriage' with unpredictable player action, and cinematic scoring (the Psycho shower scene) would demand sacrificing agency as Guitar Hero and Rez do. Surveying definitions of music—Plato's song of words, mode, and rhythm in Republic Book 2, Schafer's Apollonian versus Dionysian origin myths, and African and gamelan challenges to the Western score-centered 'work'—he argues the incompatibility dissolves if music is redefined broadly. Halo 2's sound effects turn out to be secretly musical: the Covenant carbine's zoom sounds a perfect fourth (G-flat to D-flat), the plasma pistol charges to B-flat—pitched, rhythmic design already synchronized to onscreen action, bridging music and interactivity.

philosophy-of-music.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
philosophy-of-music.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
philosophy-of-music.relation: Joel McIver, drawing on years of interviewing the band, argues the sinister sound is psychoacoustics rather than Satan: Iommi's lower tuning adopted after the sheet-metal press took his fingertips, the tritone or diabolus in musica that anchors "Black Sabbath", horror-film tremolo, minor keys, Ozzy's untrained monotone, and Bill Ward's slightly dragged, jazzy beats, artistic imperfections that keep the music lifelike. Against Schopenhauer's view that music directly expresses universal emotions, so the tritone would naturally sound like discord to anyone, McIver contends the devil's interval is a Western convention that only became inseparable from evil once Sabbath fused it with Geezer's occult lyrics and nightmare cover art.

philosophy-of-music.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
philosophy-of-music.title: Notes
philosophy-of-music.relation: Belluomini argues the show's score and soundtrack do genuine aesthetic and moral work, applying Aristotle's Politics Book VIII claim that music imitates emotion and disposes us toward virtue. He analyzes Celeste's 'Strange' narrating the divorce-signing and intercut romances, 'Wise Up' underscoring Rebecca's brave break with John Wingsnight, 'Piano Joint' carrying Rebecca's confession to Ted, 'She's a Rainbow' scoring Roy's run back to Nelson Road, 'Roy Walk Off' as a Jaws-style sentimental motif, and 'Spiegel im Spiegel' under Rebecca's anti-Super-League speech, closing with Schopenhauer's point that fitting music is a scene's most accurate commentary.

philosophy-of-music.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
philosophy-of-music.title: 13. Punk’s Not Dead
philosophy-of-music.relation: Auxier argues punk predates its 1976 naming (the Rolling Stones' 'She Said Yeah', the Troggs, MC5) and mocks philosophers' game of stacking necessary conditions, drawing on his own 1983 stints in New Wave, Hardcore, and Art Punk bands to map the scene's 'line in the sand'. The essay's pivot is Schopenhauer as 'a punk' - hater of Hegel, of women, and of noise, yet the philosopher who elevated music to the redeemer of miserable lives as the direct utterance of the Will - and since Schopenhauer revered Beethoven, once derided as noise, Auxier concludes punk is ordered symbolic form (physical sound, encoding, symbol) delivering usable energy, so punk's not dead.

game-theory.title: Turnabout’s Fair Play
game-theory.relation: Galen Foresman argues the war on campers dissolves once equivocation is cleared away: camping is just strategic positioning held over time, legitimate when it serves the game type (guarding the flag) and self-defeating when it does not. Game theory sharpens the point—waiting is a dominant strategy in slayer, so two smart players camp forever and never meet, making campers egocentric free riders who profit from the risk-takers who keep the game alive. Spawn camping, though, still produces a winner, so under the winning covering value it is the smartest play; objections that victory should require aim-skill, or that camping ruins other game types, turn out to be the unshared preferences of the unskillful, since 'fairness is a concept trotted out primarily by the losers.'

game-theory.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
game-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
game-theory.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones argues Ender's genius is empathy cashed out through game theory: from Plato's Laches on courage to Hume's account of sympathy, sizing up the enemy's thinking is the winning strategy, and Ender's love ('in that very moment I also love him') reframes conflicts with Peter and the buggers so they can end rather than merely be won. His one failure is never extending this empathy to Graff and Rackham, so he cannot see that his final battleroom rule-breaking - 'the enemy's gate is down' - is exactly the move the adults' larger game was designed to produce.

game-theory.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
game-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
game-theory.relation: Ted Brown and Christie Maloyed read Ender's Game as a Cold War debate between realism and liberalism: Hobbes' state of nature grounds Graff's survival-at-all-costs logic, and Machiavelli's counsel on seizing opportunities and keeping power by force when persuasion fails shapes Peter's insight that 'the right words can change the world.' The human-Formic war becomes a Prisoner's Dilemma neither species can escape without communication, and Ender's postwar practice of governing his colony 'by persuasion rather than fiat' delivers the book's verdict that the power to persuade can outlast the power to destroy.

game-theory.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
game-theory.title: 3. What Should a Queen Do
game-theory.relation: Sznajder uses All Stars' winner-eliminates-you twist (Naomics Smalls cutting Manila, BenDeLaCrème quitting) to ask what a rational queen should do, grounding instrumental rationality in Hume's 'reason is the slave of the passions'. She runs the Ultimatum Game (Latrice rejecting a 99-to-1 split from Valentina), diminishing marginal utility (Trixie's twenty-dollar tip then and now), expected utility with the pink mystery box, and a Trixie–Shangela Prisoner's Dilemma in which rational utility-maximizers eliminate each other when cooperation would leave both better off. The clash between the normative theory and what queens and experimental subjects actually do leads her to the chapter's 'No Sure Thing Principle': Drag Race's plot twists always add an option game theory never modeled, as BenDeLaCrème saw.

game-theory.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
game-theory.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
game-theory.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones treats Ender's conflicts as games analyzable by von Neumann's minimax theorem and the theory of zero-sum, imperfect-information games, arguing Ender wins by redefining the game itself ('the enemy's gate is down') while his empathy fails only with Graff, whose larger game Ender never suspects because he never treats the adults as the enemy. He unpacks Ender's claim that to understand an enemy is to love him through Socrates' words in Plato's Laches on courage, Hume's account of sympathy, and the Christian agape of 'love your enemies,' mapping a continuum from sympathy through empathy to love.

game-theory.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
game-theory.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
game-theory.relation: The chapter models court intrigue as game theory: games of incomplete information over Joffrey's legitimacy, the predictability of honorable opponents like Barristan Selmy, and Catelyn's reverse induction from the seemingly 'irrational' attack on Bran to deduce that Jaime threw him. Tyrion is the star player, converting one-shot death sentences into repeated games - recruiting Bronn as his champion at the Eyrie, buying off the mountain clans with Lannister arms - and showing how 'A Lannister always pays his debts' works as strategic reputation. Against Plato's view of love as the madness that ruins rational play (Maester Aemon's 'love is the bane of honor'), the chapter uses Nietzsche's 'drop of reason in madness' to argue that lovers' merged interests expand rationality itself, culminating in a Golden Rule upgraded to 'understand others as they understand themselves.'

game-theory.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
game-theory.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
game-theory.relation: Jones models Panem with game theory: the tesserae system is a rigged, house-favoring gamble on the reaping (Katniss's twenty entries versus Madge's three), the Training Days are a subgame for winning sponsors, and arena alliances formalize the prisoner's dilemma, where betray-betray is the stable equilibrium even though mutual cooperation would leave everyone better off. Iterated-play tit-for-tat wins computer simulations but fails in the arena because a betrayed tribute usually dies before retaliating — as Katniss's repeated misreadings of her allies show. Katniss's genius is stepping outside the game: with the nightlock berries she denies the Gamemakers a victor and forces a new game, and at the climax she plays terminal tit-for-tat against President Coin, showing the world need not follow the rules of the models.

tragedy-of-the-commons.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
tragedy-of-the-commons.title: No Matter How You Flip the Patty . .
tragedy-of-the-commons.relation: Michael Dodge asks whether Krabs may guard the Krabby Patty formula, sorting Bikini Bottom's property into collective, communal (Jellyfish Fields) and private, and deploying the tragedy of the commons — Krabs's jellyfish-squeezing factory in 'Jellyfish Hunter' — to show why shared resources get rationally overexploited. Hobbes grounds Krabs's right in sovereign enforcement (without the law, 'Pineapple Fever''s chalk-line household collapses into animals fighting over the fridge), Locke in labor-mixing, with Krabs's identity bound to his patties since 'Help Wanted', and Hume in conventions of justice born of selfishness and scarcity. All three support Krabs's legal and moral right to his secret recipe against Plankton.

tragedy-of-the-commons.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
tragedy-of-the-commons.title: 26. Thanos’s Mistake
tragedy-of-the-commons.relation: Argues Thanos embodies Nietzschean master morality — his will as its own justification, 'the hardest choices require the strongest wills,' echoing the Melian dialogue's 'the strong do what they will, the weak suffer what they must,' with Doctor Strange answering in kind ('you'll find our will equal to yours') — while the Avengers speak from slave morality, judging by intentions and branding genocide evil. Thanos's real error, though, is a categorical one: imposing a technical quantity fix (a one-time 50 percent cull) on a social relationship problem, since Hardin's carrying-capacity logic and the St. Matthew Island reindeer show populations must self-limit like apex predators, making his correction a mere stopgap that confuses quantity with relationship.

tragedy-of-the-commons.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
tragedy-of-the-commons.title: Notes
tragedy-of-the-commons.relation: Thomas reads Bartertown's economy as embedded in social and political relations rather than a free market: the Underworld laborers versus Bartertown's elite stage Marx's class struggle, and the Aunty Entity–Master Blaster conflict runs through Hegel's thesis-antithesis-synthesis of capital versus labor. He treats the franchise as a post-peak-oil world, applies the tragedy of the commons and lifeboat ethics to water rationing and the Citadel's hierarchy, and counterposes Gandhi's cooperation, Adam Smith's invisible hand, and open-source-style collaboration. The conclusion: the Wasteland shows the failure of self-interest-based capitalism and the need for cooperative alternatives like direct democracy.

tragedy-of-the-commons.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
tragedy-of-the-commons.title: NOTES
tragedy-of-the-commons.relation: Davies treats the beach camp as an actual state of nature: the stolen drinking water is a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers show how the crash scrubs pre-existing property rights (Hobbes: two men desiring the same thing become enemies), and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward Locke's civil society by enforcing others' rights through punishment rather than self-defense. He rejects theories of human nature - Rousseauan 'Innocence' versus a 'Trust No One' outlook - in favor of the repeated prisoner's dilemma, arguing the survivors stabilize cooperation through tit-for-tat: beginning cooperative with strangers and retaliating against the Others. On this reading the real difference between Hobbes and Locke is which round of the repeated dilemma each takes as the starting point.

transcendentalism.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
transcendentalism.title: Friends—Don’t Leave Home without ’Em
transcendentalism.relation: Greg Ahrenhoerster places SpongeBob in literary history between Transcendentalism and naturalism: 'Nature Pants' is a failed Walden — SpongeBob gives away his possessions for Jellyfish Fields but his 'jellyfish instincts' fail as badly as self-reliance in London's 'To Build a Fire' — while 'Squidville' shows the industrial city's cold indifference as in Crane's Maggie. 'Jellyfish Hunter' warns that trying to exploit nature (Krabs's jelly factory) invites nature's reprisal, since civilized beings without instinct are at nature's mercy. The naturalist moral, against Transcendentalist solitude, is that we survive only through each other: visit Jellyfish Fields, but bring a friend.

transcendentalism.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
transcendentalism.title: a21.xhtml
transcendentalism.relation: Kraus argues The Hobbit is two different books depending on the reader's experience: read cold it is a fairy-tale of adventure, but reread after The Lord of the Rings - knowing what the Ring did to Bilbo and what 'precious' means - it becomes a song of innocence and experience like Blake's Songs and Wordsworth's 'emotion recollected in tranquillity', where Elrond's opening description points to the deep Silmarillion history a first-time reader cannot yet feel. Emerson's 'transparent eye-ball' from Nature - the self stripped bare and made original in the woods - becomes Bilbo's first use of the Ring, where invisibility lets him see Gollum's miserable humanity and choose pity; but the image darkens into Sauron's Lidless Eye, the totalizing knowledge that defines and devours selves. 'There and back again' thus echoes nostos turned nostalgia: Bilbo never truly gets back, having traded the child's innocence Thorin praises on his deathbed for an experience he cannot undo.

transcendentalism.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
transcendentalism.title: Take Me to the Lakes: Transcendentalism and Ecology in Taylor Swift's folklore
transcendentalism.relation: Reads folklore as American Transcendentalist: like Thoreau at Walden and on Mt. Katahdin, Swift's escape into the woods of 'the lakes', 'seven', and 'the last great american dynasty' dissolves the divide between body and nature and reveals a fundamental oneness linking Rebekah Harkness, her grandfather in 'epiphany', and the High Line. Against the anti-social reading of Thoreau, the chapter argues, with Emerson's return to society after 'Nature', that Swift's escapism is not selfish retreat: she hands the stories back ('Now it's up to you to pass them down'), so leaving society heals alienation and rebuilds connection, including her anxiety that fame makes her 'nothing new' answered by the endurance of folk songs.

transcendentalism.title: Being-at-Home Gary Snyder and the Poetics of Place
transcendentalism.relation: Hayes reads Gary Snyder's poetry and prose on 'being-at-home' through Heidegger's claim that 'poetically man dwells' and his earth/world distinction, arguing Snyder's bioregionalism (renaming California the 'Shasta Bioregion,' America 'Turtle Island') roots identity in place while embracing Zen impermanence learned from Dōgen. Snyder's shamanic 'tawny grammar,' his pragmatic environmental program in 'Four Changes,' and his Transcendentalist lineage (Thoreau, Emerson) turn wildness into 'the state of complete awareness,' letting a place 'set free into its own presencing' and grounding a poetics of dwelling that is at once local, geological, and impermanent.

transcendentalism.title: Synecdoche, in Part
transcendentalism.relation: Smith reads every Kaufman film as a farce about the self-defeating quest to 'become who you are,' with Synecdoche, New York as its culmination: Caden's MacArthur-funded attempt to represent all of life in a warehouse collapses into infinite regress because a representation of everything must contain itself. He frames Kaufman's films as Montaignean/Emersonian essays—fragmentary self-portraits—and argues the film's limits are death and language, since language always puts us at one remove from the life we already are. The transcendence it evokes is naturalistic, akin to Nietzsche's amor fati and Emerson's 'we are born to a whole': wholeness is not achieved but already possessed, and the hidden knowledge of it turns tragedy into farce.

transcendentalism.title: Foreword
transcendentalism.relation: Robert Porfirio's foreword traces film noir's dark sensibility to a native strain in American culture rather than only to imported existentialism, running from Puritan gloom through Poe, Melville, and Hawthorne to the hard-boiled pulp of Hammett, Chandler, and Woolrich. He argues that William James's pragmatism sounded the death knell of the Emersonian/Thoreauvian transcendentalist faith in self-reliance and nature, leaving the way open for Darwinism, Freudianism, and Nietzschean pessimism to reduce the individual to a 'waif amidst forces.' He connects this to the Germanic emigres who brought expressionist style, suggesting they were drawn to an American darkness already present, and closes wondering what post-9/11 neo-noir will make of the same fear and paranoia.

transcendentalism.title: The Philosophy of Martin Scorsese
transcendentalism.relation: R. Barton Palmer situates Scorsese as a 'saint of cinema' whose Emersonian transcendentalism—the 'influx of light and power' breaking through the material everyday—pervades even his commercial films, focusing on Bringing Out the Dead against Casino and Taxi Driver. He traces the Bressonian 'decisive moment' and Schrader's Calvinist-Jansenist reading of predestination and grace (Ace Rothstein's inexplicable survival in Casino, the elect/damned divide of Taxi Driver and Hardcore), where Travis Bickle remains 'God's lonely man' beyond redemption. Palmer argues Scorsese departs from Schrader's bleak limited atonement: Frank Pierce earns communal grace through willed effort, releasing Mary's father, asking forgiveness, and ending in a Pieta embrace that affirms redemption is attainable within the material world.

transcendentalism.title: Regeneration through Stories and Song The View from the Other Side of the West in Smoke Signals
transcendentalism.relation: Richard Gilmore reads Smoke Signals—the first feature written, directed, and coproduced by Native Americans—against Slotkin's myth of regeneration through violence, arguing it offers regeneration through stories and song instead. Drawing on Wilshire's claim that pragmatism is 'aboriginal,' he links Emerson and Thoreau's transcendentalism and Peirce's 'law of mind' to Deloria's American Indian metaphysics and Hyde's gift economy: Arlene's fry-bread story and Thomas's storytelling repair broken relationships, and Victor's final act of forgiving his father (and withholding that Arnold caused the fatal fire) is read as the film's central gift, completing relationships that violence had severed.

transcendentalism.title: 10_LaRocca_Chapter_009.html
transcendentalism.relation: William Day argues that Herzog's Cave of Forgotten Dreams, filming the 32,000-year-old Chauvet Cave paintings in 3D, works not by preserving a past but by transfiguring the present, placing the viewer in a 'mythological relation to time.' He reads three literary precursors to this cinematic 'doubleness'—Emerson's 'History' and 'The American Scholar' (the past made 'now'), Thoreau's spectator-self in Walden's 'Solitude,' and Weil's 'renunciation of time'—as antecedents to Cavell's ontology of film. The Fred Astaire shadow-dance from Swing Time, spliced into the cave footage, becomes Day's emblem of what becomes of things on film: the shadows dance on after Astaire stops.

transcendentalism.title: 11_LaRocca_Chapter_010.html
transcendentalism.relation: Pederson and Zimmermann analyze Vincent Grenier's 'avant-doc' videos (Color Study: Slaterville New York, Watercolor: Fall Creek, Les Chaises, Armoire) as interventions in the philosophy of documentary landscape. They read his flattened tableau shots and digitally manipulated color fields against the Hudson River School and Ansel Adams's transcendentalist (Emersonian/Thoreauvian) American sublime, invoking Timothy Murray's Heideggerian poiesis of habitats and Baudrillard's simulation/simulacra to argue Grenier replaces representation of nature with simulation—e.g., the pigeon reacting to its mirror image in Armoire—dissolving the divide between the natural and the technological.

spinoza-conatus.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
spinoza-conatus.title: The House that Holmes Built
spinoza-conatus.relation: Kate Rufa reads Holmes as Spinoza's 'just man': Watson's 'calculating machine' verdict in The Sign of the Four, his unshaken calm while baiting Moriarty before the Reichenbach leap in 'The Final Problem', and the geometric 'Book of Life' of A Study in Scarlet all show passion mastered by reason into adequate ideas and true freedom. The twist is the cocaine: shooting up between cases means Holmes sacrifices his conatus (the striving to persist in being) to keep his mind at a godlike pitch of activity, a God-complex no finite mode can sustain. Moriarty, equally rational but ruled by passive affects, is the shadow of this ideal, echoing Socrates' Apology point that harming others inevitably harms oneself.

spinoza-conatus.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-conatus.title: The Origin and Nature of Affective Disorder
spinoza-conatus.relation: Using the opening of VALIS, the section explains Gloria's suicide through Spinoza's account of the passions: imagining we are hated without cause breeds hatred, and Spinoza's lone remark on suicide says those who kill themselves are 'impotent in mind,' overcome by external causes opposed to their nature, since our essence just is the conatus, the striving to persist in being. It then itemizes Fat's three tragedies (Gloria's death, the divorce, losing his son) as accumulating external causes that overwhelmed him into his own suicide attempt, and presents his therapist Maurice's 'take responsibility for your own life' as implicitly Spinozan advice.

spinoza-conatus.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
spinoza-conatus.title: “An Energy Field Created by All Living Things”
spinoza-conatus.relation: Baur argues that the Jedi metaphysics is non-dualistic rather than a simple good-versus-evil opposition, reading the Force through Spinoza: ideas become more or less true as they cohere with other ideas (so 'Luke loves Leia', 'Han is a mercenary', and 'Vader is evil' all need qualification), and everything seeks power by the conatus that Yoda and Obi-Wan attribute to the Force. The light side seeks power in balance with other things while the dark side, per the Sith Rule of Two, plays a zero-sum game. Luke's arc mirrors Oedipus: denying his inherited psychological likeness to Vader only enacts it, and only by acknowledging and owning the anger he inherited from his father can he gain power over it and enable Vader's redemption and his own.

spinoza-conatus.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
spinoza-conatus.title: NOTES
spinoza-conatus.relation: Dunn reads Descartes' bete-machine doctrine (animals as soulless automata explicable by 'billiard ball' mechanics) against the Terminator universe, since Descartes' two tests for true men - genuine language and versatile reason - are in fact passed by the machines: the T-101 deploys 'Hasta la vista, baby' hours after learning not to sound like a dork and marshals skills far beyond a clock. Sarah Connor instead locates the soul in the heart, and via Spinoza's conatus - the instinctual valuation of one's own existence that Terminators lack ('no emotion about it one way or another') - she judges even linguistically brilliant machines soulless and irrational, as Mary Midgley says of computers that do not know what matters. Kyle's line about 'dreaming about dogs' closes the chapter: by the Sarah Connor criterion dogs are ensouled sentinels, the very thing Descartes denied.

spinoza-conatus.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
spinoza-conatus.title: Who is Who
spinoza-conatus.relation: Focused on the 'Monstrous Other' and the 'base under siege' story, the chapter uses Hegel's master-slave struggle for recognition and Sartre's 'the look' to read Cybermen, the Flood ('Waters of Mars') and the Silurians as Others through which humans define themselves, with Levinas on the face and history. Its final section frames the Doctor and the Master as Gothic doubles of love and strife, using Spinoza's monism, principle of sufficient reason and conatus to argue the power-hungry Master paradoxically fits Spinoza's system better than the order-imposing 'Dark Doctor.'

dharma.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
dharma.title: Chapter 8 - The Case of the Dangerous Detective
dharma.relation: In a Platonic dialogue, Ronald Green and D.E. Wittkower argue the detective is dangerous because knowledge itself threatens a society's ideology: Oedipus's fatal investigation, the Athenian prosecution of Socrates and Anaxagoras, and Holmes's exposure that genteel Victorian society breeds the same crimes as the slums (while the hard-boiled PI shows official authority cannot deliver), with Aristotle's catharsis re-described as ideological enforcement that teaches audiences not to question social foundations. They then widen to Indian traditions: Vyasa dividing knowledge into the Vedas like an inverted Descartes, Krishna's two paths of inquiry in the Bhagavad Gita, and the Ramayana's dharma, where Rama's trial of Sita upholds cosmic order over truth, compared with the film Raavan, to ask whether ruling by an upheld lie is the greater danger.

dharma.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
dharma.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
dharma.relation: Duffy applies Susan Wolf's formula (subjective attraction meeting objective attractiveness) to Red's cooking, Poussey's friendship, and Taystee's library work, arguing these women meet the conditions yet still cannot live meaningful lives because Litchfield hands out 'chickens': WAC, the mock job fair, and the yard chicken are illusions of meaning designed to keep inmates quiet, as Healy admits with his bath-before-dinner analogy. Only projects that change the prison's conditions themselves, Piper's newsletter sting and Soso's hunger strike, are genuinely meaningful, and the yogic dharma of non-attachment (Yoga Jones's mandala advice) is a survival tool, not a substitute. She closes that guards too can find meaning, and have an obligation, in rehabilitating rather than punishing.

dharma.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
dharma.title: 22. The Many-Faced God and Indian Philosophy
dharma.relation: Van Eyghen maps the Faceless Men onto Indian philosophy: their one God of many faces parallels Vedanta's Brahman in personal form as Ishvara, and Arya's training to become 'no one' parallels shedding the ego toward identity with Brahman - with Jaqen as guru and the stick-beating ritual as an example of identity fusion in Harvey Whitehouse's cognitive science of religion. But the Faceless Men may go further than Vedanta toward Buddhism, since they worship a god with no face of his own and aim at no-self rather than union, while Arya's pragmatic adoption of the shellfish-merchant disguise echoes the Bhagavad Gita's Krishna: perform your duty without attachment to any self.

dharma.title: Richness and diversity in Indian thought
dharma.relation: Argues that in India philosophy and religion were never separated as the post-Kantian West separates them: philosophizing is a soteriological quest in which understanding the nature of reality directly affects one's destiny, more comparable to Socrates' quest for wisdom than to modern academic philosophy. It introduces the framework of darshanas ('views' of reality taught by seers), the claim that disciplined mental exercises can yield yogic perception of metaphysical truth, and karma-rebirth as the shared Indian worldview, contrasting ritual-correctness karma with the Buddha's radically intention-based version and discussing verbal testimony as an everyday but religiously unchecked means of knowledge. It closes by delimiting the book's scope (the six classical darshanas plus Buddhism; Jainism, Carvaka, and Shaivism omitted) and warning against the Western habit of romanticizing Indian thought as mystical rather than recognizing its strong rational-debate tradition. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

dharma.title: Sacrifice, cosmic speculation, oneness
dharma.relation: Presents the two coexisting branches of the Brahmanical tradition around 500 BCE: the Vedic sacrificial religion, in which precisely performed ritual actions (physical and verbal karma) maintained cosmic order (dharma) and underwrote brahmin social authority, and the Upanishadic internalization of the sacrifice. The Upanishads shift the focus to the person, teaching that experiential insight into the identity of one's essential self (atman) and the cosmos (Brahman) - 'tat tvam asi' - brings moksha from rebirth, illustrated with the Rig Veda 10.129 creation hymn and passages from the Chandogya and Brihadaranyaka Upanishads. It carefully distinguishes monism (one existent thing) from monotheism, sets the Upanishadic oneness against the pluralistic realism of the ritualists, and shows how this internal tension became the fault line along which later Indian philosophical debate would run. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

dharma.title: Language, grammar, and polemics
dharma.relation: Shows how the brahmins defended the Veda against fifth-century challenges by formalizing the study of language: Panini's grammar codified the ritually creative Sanskrit whose sounded sentences (e.g. 'water wets grain') were held to bring about their effects impersonally, and Patanjali and Katyayana's 'usage' criterion allowed awkward or conflicting Vedic passages to be read as metaphor, preserving the text's coherence. It then presents Jaimini's Mimamsa Sutra reading of the Veda purely as injunctions - dharma defined as 'what should be done' - with word-meaning taken to guarantee the existence of what words designate, so that the Veda validates both the plural cosmos and the ritual agents who maintain it; the Upanishadic monist passages are defused as metaphor. Finally it presents Badarayana's Vedanta (Brahma) Sutra pivoting instead to 'enquiry into Brahman', and shows how both exegetes established testimony (shabda-pramana) as a lasting and contested Indian means of knowledge, alongside the purva-paksha style of stating an opponent's view before refuting it. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

dharma.title: Bhartṛhari, Mīmāṃsā, and Vedānta
dharma.relation: Covers the later grammatical and exegetical schools: Bhartrhari's claim that the whole sentence is the unit of meaning, that there is no knowledge without language, and that reality is a continuous indivisible 'sound-Brahman' (shabda-Brahman) knowable through grammar; the Mimamsakas (Kumarila and Prabhakara) defending the eternal, authorless Veda as injunction, holding cognition itself intrinsically reliable so that knowing reveals both the plural external world and the autonomous agent-selves who perform the sacrifice (with an 'identity in difference' category analysis and visible-sized atoms). It then presents Vedanta: Shankara's Advaita monism in which atman is Brahman, plurality has only conventional reality (the coiled rope mistaken for a snake; the trees seeming to move to a boatman), ignorance rather than Brahman causes the world of appearance, and Shankara remains a theistic monist despite his 'crypto-Buddhist' critics; versus Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita, in which Brahman really transforms itself into the qualified, plural world (parinama-vada) and selves relate to the Lord as redness to a rose - eternally inseparable yet distinct. The chapter treats its subject directly rather than through any pop-culture work.

dharma.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
dharma.title: 9. My Dharma Is the Road that Never Ends
dharma.relation: Reads Twin Peaks: The Return as a commitment to Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati: Cooper is trapped in an existential time loop (Dougie's relearning, Wally's Part 4 Dharma speech, the final-episode Cooper/Richard do-over) and must learn to love every horrific repetition, quoting the Gay Science demon passage and Nietzsche's Will to Power on enduring recurrence. The chapter frames Lynch and Frost as Romantics — Novalis on wonder, Isaiah Berlin's Roots of Romanticism on the artist's inner vision — who break three storytelling rules (authors create stories, protagonists solve problems, stories have endings), so that Laura's mystery stays a living Jack-the-Ripper-style mystery and the story becomes a meta-narrative co-created with viewers, echoing Buddhist pratityasamutpada and Russell's beginningless world. Cooper's finale is a Sisyphean task he accepts, making his integrity the audience's own test.

dharma.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
dharma.title: 19. Hinduism Gets More than Five Percent Right
dharma.relation: Kaur and Gupta argue Hinduism got far more than five percent right, mapping the show's points onto karmic theory and the Bhagavad Gita's three kinds of action: right action, inaction, and wrong action. Eleanor's fruitless point-grubbing and selfless departure exemplify nishkama karma, desire-less action, while the 802 reboots and Janet's memory-wiped revivals mirror the birth-death-rebirth cycle on the way to self-realization. Ranking the cast on the Gita's ladder of unfoldment, desire-driven Eleanor and Jason below Tahani and knowledgeable Chidi, with Michael straying from his dharma and detached, duty-bound Janet nearest to Brahman, they show the series dramatizes the Gita's teaching that motivation, not the deed itself, determines an act's worth.

dharma.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
dharma.title: 19. Hinduism Gets More than Five Percent Right
dharma.relation: Argues Hinduism 'gets more than five percent right' via the Bhagavad Gita: the show's point system mirrors karma, Eleanor's failed point-chasing and quiet departure for the Bad Place enact nishkama karma (desire-less action), and the 802 reboots are rebirths without memory. The characters form a ladder of unfoldment — Jason's unknowing wrong action below Eleanor's knowing one, Tahani's corruptly motivated good deeds, Chidi's knowledge without decision, Michael swerving from his demonic dharma, and Janet highest: desireless, rebooting like cyclical rebirth, her void echoing boundless Brahman. Chidi's logic-bound indecision versus Eleanor's knowledge-producing logic completes the Gita reading.

dharma.title: 9. My Dharma Is the Road that Never Ends
dharma.relation: Potter and Cobb argue that Twin Peaks is a Romantic refusal of resolution: mysteries live by not being solved, so Lynch and Frost break the rules that stories need authors, protagonists who solve problems, and endings. They read Cooper's entrapment in a time loop through Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati (quoting The Gay Science and The Will to Power), tie Wally Brando's Dharma speech and Isaiah Berlin's Roots of Romanticism to the theme, and argue the real 'story' is the endless meta-narrative co-created between the show and each viewer—Life itself as process without endpoint.

dharma.title: Rāma of Gilead
dharma.relation: Matthew Butkus reads Roland Deschain of The Dark Tower as a parallel to Rama of the Ramayana and Arjuna of the Bhagavad Gita, mapping his cyclical existence onto the Hindu concepts of karma (his coupling with the demon spawning Mordred, letting Jake fall), dharma (the gunslinger's duty to protect the Beams as an avatar restoring cosmic order), samskara (character shaped by all past lives) and samsara (the death-rebirth cycle the Horn of Eld may or may not break). Like Krishna instructing the reluctant Arjuna, the text tells Roland he must 'stand and be true' regardless of misgivings; Butkus concludes the moral for readers is not violence but fulfilling one's own svadharma—to stand and be true in one's own station.

dharma.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
dharma.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
dharma.relation: Wawatie and Pyne present a traditional Algonquin Anishinabe philosophy of hunting in which all creation — humans, animals, plants, water, rocks — belongs to one family bound by spirit, and hunting is a reciprocal relationship of gift, gratitude, and non-waste rather than a contest. Through Kokom Lena Nottaway's creation story (animals gifting a foggy figure wisdom, vision, strength until humans take form) and the life of 'Nathan' learning the moose, they show hunting as 'a quest for understanding.' A hunting song teaches by indirect clues, letting the learner reach their own awareness, and feast ceremonies honor the prey's sacrifice.

aestheticism.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
aestheticism.title: That Far-Away Look
aestheticism.relation: Lahr argues that Holmes's crime-solving is an art rather than a forensic science: like his inspiration Oscar Wilde, Holmes is an aesthete whose 'aesthetic sight' perceives the criminal-artist's design in clues, so that Watson the philistine ('What ineffable twaddle!') consistently misses what is self-evident to Holmes. He suggests Plato would say Holmes sees only the perfect Forms behind appearances, and reads the BBC adaptations accordingly: in The Case of the Silk Stocking Holmes's trance-like perception of the victims' pedicured feet reveals a killer with a foot fetish, while Sherlock's 'A Study in Pink' renders his insight as first-person vision with on-screen data. The queer coding (the Diogenes Club, Moriarty's 'hereditary tendencies,' Holmes as Wilde's physical and temperamental double) links Holmes to the first sexologists' puzzle of how marginal men recognize one another at a glance.

aestheticism.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
aestheticism.title: Art for Art’s Sake
aestheticism.relation: Auxier defines aestheticism — people whose moral and even religious values are drawn from the aesthetic realm — and casts the pure bluesman (Hank Williams, Townes Van Zandt) and the Stones as aesthetes arriving in a decade when high and low culture were in dialectical tango. Through Andy Warhol and Robert Fraser he argues a postmodern role of 'the artist' as celebrated performer emerged, pushing the idea of genius to its limit: no longer does nature give the rule to art, but the genius-subject tells both nature and culture what art is. Mick took the Warhol-esque role of serial persona reinvention while Keith remained the grounded serious musician, each brilliant in support of the other.

aestheticism.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
aestheticism.title: 13. An Aesthete par Excellence
aestheticism.relation: Holt argues that the key to Lecter is aestheticism: the Goldberg Variations scoring his nightstick killing of the Memphis guard is no camouflage, because art, cannibalism, murder and etiquette are all unified by aesthetic value prized apart from the good and the true. His 'ACME question' applies inference to the best explanation to show that a single hypothesis — the aesthetic — explains Art, Cannibalism, Murder and Etiquette together, with 'Discourtesy is unspeakably ugly to me' read as an aesthetic rather than a moral complaint. The final twist is that Lecter's psychopathic 'moral blindness' may enhance his powers of aesthetic discrimination the way literal blindness enhances hearing and touch.

schopenhauer-pendulum.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
schopenhauer-pendulum.title: The Seven Percent Conclusion
schopenhauer-pendulum.relation: Malloy names boredom, not Moriarty, as Holmes's true nemesis, sorting his moods through Heidegger's three types: boredom by something (the mind-reading demonstration in 'The Cardboard Box' that bores Holmes but astounds Watson), boredom with everything ('The Noble Bachelor's' 'unwelcome social summonses'), and profound boredom — the 'black moods' behind the seven-per-cent solution, which Heidegger says reveals beings as a whole in remarkable indifference. Against Schopenhauer's pendulum swinging between pain and boredom, and Nietzsche's 'against boredom even gods struggle in vain,' Pascal's and Kierkegaard's verdict that boredom is the root of all evil explains Jeremy Paul's suggestion that Holmes invented Moriarty as an equal opponent to keep the game alive. Religion, Pascal's and Kierkegaard's cure, cannot save the modern Holmes, so work, amusement, and drugs merely treat symptoms of modernity itself.

schopenhauer-pendulum.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
schopenhauer-pendulum.title: 17. Through Plastic Our Secrets Seen
schopenhauer-pendulum.relation: Uses Schopenhauer's World as Will to explain why the citizens of Twin Peaks keep living lives they despise: all willing arises from deficiency and suffering, so Shelly cannot leave Leo, Ben cannot face his children, and Ed is consumed oscillating between Norma and Nadine, while the blind will — not reflection — determines who we become. Since only pain is known directly and its absence slides into boredom and banality (Ed's restless drama-making), the town's double lives — Jacoby's coconut tapes hiding Laura's confession, Bobby's dealing, Ben's brothel — are the will's concealed kernels. Laura's wrapped corpse then functions as the reveal: death shows each character's truth, and the chapter closes by turning Socrates' unexamined life against itself, asking what happens when self-examination only uncovers what we wished hidden, as Cooper's daily-present advice offers the lone consolation.

schopenhauer-pendulum.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
schopenhauer-pendulum.title: Notes
schopenhauer-pendulum.relation: Reconstructs Rust's scattered remarks — the world as 'one giant gutter,' procreation as the hubris of yanking a soul out of nonexistence into the thresher — into an explicit anti-natalist argument, testing each premise and conceding procreation is selfish while questioning whether every life nets more harm than good. It presents David Benatar's asymmetry between the absence of pain (always good) and the absence of pleasure (bad only for someone deprived), illustrating it with the show: contraception as procreative duty, the wrongness of conceiving in Tuttle's Louisiana, and the emptiness of Childress' temple as a good in itself. The chapter concludes that Rust's 'opt out of a raw deal' is philosophically defensible, with Schopenhauer's desire-pendulum and Hobbes' 'nasty, brutish, and short' backing the claim that most lives are bad.

schopenhauer-pendulum.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
schopenhauer-pendulum.title: My Troubles Are Going to Have Troubles with Me Schopenhauer, Pessimism, and Nietzsche
schopenhauer-pendulum.relation: Jacob Held pits Schopenhauer's pessimism against Nietzschean affirmation using I Had Trouble in Getting to Solla Sollew. He reads Schopenhauer's will-to-life and 'pendulum between pain and boredom' into Seuss's endlessly striving characters, and treats the mirage-towns Solla Sollew and Boola Boo Ball as proof there is no escape from suffering. The protagonist's final line, 'I've bought a big bat... now my troubles are going to have troubles with me,' becomes Nietzsche's yes-saying: instead of the ascetic renunciation Schopenhauer prescribes, Seuss's child-hero affirms life, redeeming its accidents the way Nietzsche's eternal-recurrence thought experiment and 'become a child' passage in Zarathustra demand.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
simulation-hypothesis.title: The Evil Genius that Turns Moriarty into a Brain in a Vat
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Samardzija reads Star Trek's holodeck Moriarty as Descartes updated: Data plays Holmes on the holodeck while Dr. Pulaski's Nietzschean jibe (from 'The Illogical Necessary' in Human, All Too Human) denies that computation can be human, and the holographic Moriarty proves his sentience not by deduction but by feelingCrowded intuitions first and then invoking Descartes' cogito ergo sum to Picard. In 'Ship in a Bottle' he nests a simulation of the Enterprise inside the Holmes holodeck to trick the crew into believing he has escaped — an evil-genius, brain-in-a-vat scenario that ends with Picard admitting our own reality 'might be nothing more than an elaborate simulation.' The paradox is that only the unemotional android Data can detect the deception, so rationality bars him from humanity while Moriarty stays eternally deceived into thinking he has become human — and Doyle's own 'hereditary tendencies' account of Moriarty's evil, the chapter notes, is a Victorian biological determinism the hologram rebels against.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
simulation-hypothesis.title: An Old Man, Filled with Regret . .
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Brophy argues Cobb's shared dreams are best modeled on MMORPG virtual worlds like Second Life and World of Warcraft: Ariadne is a world-building architect in the mold of Second Life's Escher Relativity House, dreamers are avatars, and the film's looping architectures mirror the toroidal grids of game worlds. Reading the film as an addict's 'long con', he claims the real inception was planting in Cobb's own head the idea that his game-world is real: Mal is a 'gamer's widow' whose in-game suicide deleted her character, and Cobb is the avatar of an unseen addicted player who has forgotten the game. Borges's map that covers the empire, Baudrillard's claim that the simulacrum becomes the preferred reality, Bostrom's simulation argument, and Homer's lotus-eaters all support the warning that we already prefer simulated worlds, so the last shot means the real Cobb will one day wake as an old man filled with regret.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
simulation-hypothesis.title: 11. Should We Execute the Erudite
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Michaud and Watkins ask whether Roth is right that the knowledge-hoarding Erudite are so dangerous we might need to eliminate them, and answer that knowledge is dangerous in three ways. Following Foucault ('it is impossible for knowledge not to engender power'), the powerful define what counts as knowledge - from the church blessing feudalism to the medical community pathologizing gay and transgender people - and following Piaget, new knowledge threatens the interconnected belief schemas (diagrammed as beliefs resting on beliefs) that keep 'faction before blood' and our sense of being special stable, which is why Divergents, evolution, and Copernicus provoke such violent disequilibrium. A Descartes-style simulation scenario - you may be inside Roth's world right now, weeded out for reading the books - and David Lewis's point that investigating knowledge destroys it then show that the real danger is not knowledge but the arrogance of certainty: Jeanine was never a true Erudite.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
simulation-hypothesis.title: 10. We’re Not Free to Save Lee
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Bowman uses Telltale's Walking Dead videogame, where Lee always dies no matter what the player does, to stage the free will versus determinism debate. Laplace's demon grounds the determinist pole (the game's outcome is fixed like set particles), while Sartre's radical freedom and bad faith explain the player who says "I thought I could save both" at Hershel's farm rather than owning her choice. The chapter resolves the tension with fatalism or soft determinism - a compatibilist itinerary where Lee's death is a fixed benchmark but the player's choices in between define the character - and extends Bostrom's simulation hypothesis to ask whether we are Lee-like players inside someone else's game.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
simulation-hypothesis.title: 18. Scott Adams and the Pinocchio Fallacy
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Steele attacks Adams's embrace of the simulation hypothesis with the Pinocchio fallacy: a wooden boy cannot even hanker to be real, because hankering is conscious and wood is the wrong kind of stuff, and likewise no amount of code yields experience, since a simulation of weather wets no one and Deep Blue never knew it was playing chess. Bostrom's careful argument is distinguished from its popularizers, whose substrate-independence slide smuggles possibility into actuality (by the same logic a block of wood could be conscious), and the Matrix storyline, read as an allegory of Marx's exploitation and ideology, is judged as untenable as its energy-harvesting plot. Consciousness remains a property of living bodies, replication rather than simulation, and even if software minds were possible, trapping them in a fabricated world would be immoral.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
simulation-hypothesis.title: “Do you even know where you are ”
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Arvan argues the entire series, lab included, literally takes place inside a videogame, citing physically impossible events (Teddy's bullets cannot hurt the Man in Black, William steps onto a moving train, workers appear instantly in a single unbroken shot) and NPC-like loops of the lab staff. He then claims Descartes had it backwards: whether we are in a dream, Spinoza's God's mind, or a simulation (Bostrom's hypothesis, extended by his own peer-to-peer variant that would explain quantum indeterminacy and relativity), to be simulated is still to be real. Via Chalmers-style structuralism, anything structured and functioning like a person is a person, so hosts who walk, talk, love, and suffer are persons — and the humans' rape, torture, and murder of them, like our treatment of Siri and Watson, is dehumanization on a par with slavery and the Holocaust.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
simulation-hypothesis.title: 3. The M. Night Sh-imulation Hypothesis
simulation-hypothesis.relation: The chapter runs Bostrom's simulation argument against 'M. Night Shaym-Aliens!', where the Zigerions trap Rick in simulations-within-simulations to steal his concentrated dark matter formula, and reads their cheap shortcuts ('My man!' NPCs, human music, Jerry's Appley award) as the glitches and shadow-people Bostrom predicts. It presses the epistemological problem that any evidence for the simulation equally supports its denial, an underdetermination that devastates the theory, and traces the lineage of 'the real world isn't real' through Plato's summoners and allegory of the cave, Descartes's dream doubt, and Paley's design analogy (Morty as the beautiful machine), ending with the microverse battery of 'The Ricks Must Be Crazy': this is the universe we live in, so get used to it.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
simulation-hypothesis.title: Forget Cooper. Are We in a Simulation
simulation-hypothesis.relation: The chapter argues the horror of Playtest lies not in novelty but in immersion erasing the reality/fiction line: the rubber-hand and Muller-Lyer illusions, the paradox of fiction, and 'aliefs' show that knowing something is fake does not stop it feeling real, and for incorrigible experiences like pain the distinction collapses entirely. The AI's stripping of Cooper's memories and preferences is framed as loss of psychological continuity — a living death echoing his father's Alzheimer's — since with no memories Cooper cannot even answer who he is. The final move turns Bostrom's simulation argument on the viewer: because Cooper 'woke up' twice into deeper simulation and died 0.04 seconds in, we too may have no test that certifies we have ever left the simulation.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
simulation-hypothesis.title: An Old Man, Filled with Regret . .
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Matthew Brophy argues the film's plot makes most sense if it is an addicted gamer's MMORPG session: Cobb is an avatar, his corporate pursuers are named COBOL after the old programming language, dream 'architects' mirror world-designers like Second Life's Furia Freeloader with her Escher Relativity House, and Mal is a 'gamer's widow' whose in-game suicide deleted her character so she could return to the real family Cobb abandoned. Using the 'egocentric predicament' that no one can access another's mind, he suggests shared dreaming can only really happen on servers, and via Borges's map that covered the empire and Baudrillard's claim that the simulacrum outlives the real he reads Second Life replicas (the virtual Texas A&M campus) as the preferred level of reality decaying the actual one. He then deploys Bostrom's simulation argument — we may already be conscious simulations — and casts Yusuf's basement dreamers, Xiao Yi's Warcraft suicide, and WoW-neglect cases as modern Lotus-Eaters, concluding that the ending is a 'long con': the real inception planted in Cobb the belief that his game is real, so he will one day wake 'an old man, filled with regret, waiting to die alone.'

simulation-hypothesis.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
simulation-hypothesis.title: Notes
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Uses the holodeck as a working model for the ancient claim that everyday reality is appearance: Plato's cave shadows, maya in Hindu and Buddhist thought, and Bostrom's simulation argument (his ancestor simulations mirrored in Data and Geordi's endless Holmes holoprograms) converge with quantum "holographic universe" speculation to suggest our universe may be a cosmic holoprogram with limit conditions like light speed as processing boundaries. Moriarty seizing the Enterprise in "Ship in a Bottle", Vic Fontaine, and the EMH dramatize self-aware programs confronting their code, and the chapter argues our "free will" may be similarly bounded - Data-as-Holmes must stay in character, and Picard "can't transcend the script" any more than his NPCs can. Picard's closing admission that our reality may be "an elaborate simulation running inside a little device" delivers the skeptical upshot, alongside the ethical question of whether self-aware holograms deserve rights.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
simulation-hypothesis.title: Notes
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Jones takes Beard's 'tip our caps to the rascal pulling the strings' seriously and reconstructs Bostrom's simulation trilemma without the math: humanity goes extinct before simulating ancestors, advanced civilizations decline to run them, or we are almost certainly simulated. He then brings in David Lewis's modal realism to argue the different Teds - happily married in Kansas, the coach we watch, the rage-monster Led Tasso - are real possible people, and concludes that even if we are simulations our consciousness is real and meaningful: ancestor-simulations are the future tipping its caps to us.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
simulation-hypothesis.title: “Do you even know where you are ”
simulation-hypothesis.relation: Marcus Arvan argues from show evidence (William stepping onto a moving train, pyrotechnic effects, instant crowds, graphically rearranging the park) that all of Westworld, lab included, is a videogame, and defends his 'Peer-to-Peer Simulation Hypothesis' as an explanation of quantum mechanics and relativity, citing Bostrom and Chalmers. Adopting functionalism/structuralism, he claims that anything doing what a human does is a person, so hosts like Dolores and Maeve are no less real or human than us, inverting Descartes' cogito and invoking Spinoza's God-as-nature. He warns that dehumanizing hosts, or dismissing Siri and Watson as unconscious, repeats the logic used to justify slavery and the Holocaust: to be simulated is to be real.

simulation-hypothesis.title: 32_LaRocca_Chapter_031.html
simulation-hypothesis.relation: LaRocca argues that Casey Affleck's I'm Still Here, in which Joaquin Phoenix faked a drug-addled retirement and hip-hop career, is best understood as a 'hoax-verite' whose collapse of the boundary between real and represented turns it into a Baudrillardian simulacrum and hyperreal artifact, a documentary of images 'without an original referent.' Against Noel Carroll's account of documentary as a film of presumptive assertion and Plantinga's assertive stance, LaRocca shows how Affleck exploited audience faith (staged home movies, the David Letterman 'beat down') so that the film's metaphysical, epistemic and ethical status transformed once the fraud was confirmed. He invokes Hegel's remarks on abstract individuality and compares the case to Herzog's 'ecstatic truth,' Roth's and Kaufman's metafiction, to argue the deception paradoxically discloses deeper truths about what documentary is.

simulation-hypothesis.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
simulation-hypothesis.title: 21. Black Mirror as Philosophy A Dark Reflection of Human Nature
simulation-hypothesis.relation: The chapter asks whether Black Mirror condemns technology or human nature, and argues for the latter: the 'black mirror' reflects the viewer's character. It tests and rejects the reading of the show as depicting Bostrom-style existential risk or superintelligence (via 'Metalhead' and 'San Junipero') and rejects that Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind coupling (the 'grain' in 'The Entire History of You,' 'Arkangel,' 'Crocodile') destroys human identity. Drawing on Frankfurt School critique—Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man—and Plato's and Aristotle's natural-versus-artificial distinction, it concludes technology is an agency-less imitation that magnifies preexisting human vices, and closes with Benjamin's reproducibility thesis and Bandersnatch's interactivity to suggest the show can prompt viewers to confront their own darkness.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Dreams of Dogs and Butterflies
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Clements opens and closes with Zhuangzi's butterfly dream to frame Sherlock Hound: are we watching humans who behave like dogs (zoomorphism) or dogs who behave like humans (anthropomorphism)? He then traces the media history that transformed Holmes in Japan — Natsume Soseki's London sojourn during The Hound of the Baskervilles bearing fruit in the cat's-eye satire I Am a Cat, the 'Meiken' (Famous Dog) retitlings of Rin Tin Tin and Lassie, the mukokuseki 'denationalized' economics of animal protagonists, and Miyazaki's talking-dog series stalled by the Doyle estate's copyright protest. Zhuangzi's question about dreams and reality, Clements concludes, 'remains unanswerable,' even as his butterfly emerges from its 'transnational chrysalis as an altogether different animal.'

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Happy Ending
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Wenmackers uses Inception's dream levels and its ambiguous spinning-top ending as a guided tour of skeptical philosophy, diagramming how dreams-within-dreams, kicks, Limbo and exponentially dilated dream time work.
