She tests the totem against Zhuangzi's butterfly and lucid-dreaming reality checks, then runs Plato's Cave and the eternal Forms, Descartes's cogito and evil demon, Putnam's brain-in-a-vat, and Nozick's experience machine to ask whether Cobb's world - or ours - is real. Her conclusion is Socratic ('know that you know nothing'): subjective reality feels equally real on every level and the top level can never be known. She even argues that dream-time dilation means Cobb should not kill himself while in doubt, since real time barely passes, so a little philosophy rescues the happy ending.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Do We Give Shakespeare the Last Word
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Kapper reads Inception as epistemology rather than metaphysics - not what is real but how we could know - running from Plato's Theaetetus (the first dream-recognition question) through Descartes's deceptive demon and Freud's royal road to the unconscious, to Wittgenstein's point that 'I may be dreaming' is senseless because the remark itself would be dreamed, and Heraclitus's line that only the waking share a common world. The Ariadne thread is the clue: as in the Theseus myth, dream architecture gives the labyrinth a shareable narrative place, but only a hint, never a way to wake. He then goes east - Zhuangzi's butterfly, Indra's net of mutually reflecting jewels, Schopenhauer's universe dreamed by a single dreamer, William James's many consciousnesses - to ask how many times we must die before waking, ending with Buddhism: 'Buddha means awakened one', and Cobb's turning from the top enacts Nirvana, where the real-versus-dream question stops pertaining.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: The End
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Chan contrasts Zhuangzi's butterfly dream, where dream and reality form one transformable whole and the self is forgotten, with Inception's dreams, which are rigidly structured and must be kept strictly separate from reality for Cobb to function. She shows that the film's motifs (the dream machine, the spinning top, the faceless children) work as narrative codes marking each dream layer, making Inception an example of 'dream explaining' rather than Tarkovsky-style 'dream worshipping'. The chapter concludes that Inception's 'dreams' are really a meta-space narrative device, as in Nolan's short Doodlebug, and that the film lacks the Daoist sense of the whole, so Cobb can never transform into the butterfly.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: T. Bradley Richards takes The Sandman's Dreamworld seriously as a hypothesis: could our nightly dreams be travels to a mind-independent place like Morpheus's realm? Starting from Zhuangzi's butterfly dream and Descartes's dream argument, he uses Berkeley's God-sustained idealism as a model for how Morpheus's mind could uphold the Dreamworld's order, and a thought experiment about glitchy dream-travel defuses Descartes's appeal to the discontinuity of dreams. Against the objection that dreams are blatantly contradictory ('it was Dave, but it also wasn't Dave'), he deploys Russell's theory of descriptions against Meinongian subsistence, Chalmers-style conceivability-implies-possibility reasoning from philosophical zombies, and Graham Priest's dialetheism, concluding that dreams could be experiences of an objective world, with waking and dreaming on a par.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Psych and Philosophy
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: John Thompson argues Psych embodies the Daoist Way of reversal from the Daodejing and Zhuangzi: every episode begins with a death that triggers Shawn and Gus's irreverent, backwards-tracing investigation, their untrained spontaneous 'gifts' exemplify wu wei like Cook Ding carving an ox, and their bickering partnership is yin-yang interplay (as when Gus leads the joking in 'An Evening with Mr. Yang'). Zhuangzi singing at his wife's funeral parallels the Shabby the Sea Lion and 'Dust in the Wind' funeral parodies, the show's blurred TV-versus-fandom reality echoes the butterfly dream, Lassiter succeeds when he relaxes into wu wei ('Feet Don't Kill Me Now'), and the closing bloopers enact Dao's endless reversal - though the chapter ends by conceding Dao defies the very label 'Daoist show.'

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Girls and Philosophy
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Carleo and D'Ambrosio read Hannah's 'busy trying to become who I am' through the classical Chinese debate over names: her self-claimed title 'writer' preceding any conduct is the Confucian nightmare of names divorced from actuality, diagnosed by the Analects's rectification of names ('rulers should rule, fathers should father') and the sheep-stealing passage warning against over-identifying with a single role. Adam, by contrast, lives the Daoist ideal - the empty vessel of the Daodejing acting by wu wei, and Zhuangzi's butterfly dream fluidity in his role-play sex and absorbed woodworking, unattached to titles. Mencius and Xunzi frame the resolution: by Season Three Hannah finally rectifies names at GQ while Adam's non-identity turns delusional, vindicating the ideal of being an 'internal sage and external king' - Daoist in private, responsible to roles in public.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: The Real Is Fake and the Fake Is Real
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Takes Morpheus's red-pill speech at face value to ask whether Alice is a drug story, then argues the deeper point: the distinction between normal and distorted experience is exaggerated or specious because all perception is conditioned by expectation, mood, and chemistry, whether on caffeine or psilocybin. Scott F. Parker reads the Red King's dream alongside Plato's Theaetetus dream argument and Zhuangzi's butterfly dream to show we can never prove we are awake, then weighs William James's nitrous-oxide revelations and Aldous Huxley's mescaline 'Mind at Large' as reasons altered states might sometimes show reality more truly, concluding that the real is fake, the fake is real, and Wonderland's syndrome is now a recognized medical condition.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: The Way of the Archer
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: White reads Clint Barton through the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu: Hawkeye's instinctive archery—'use your bow gently, naturally, instinctively'—is wei wu wei, while his bragging, his glory-chasing failure against Iron Man, and his attempt to become Goliath all violate it by striving against his own nature, until the Kree-Skrull War teaches him the bow is his way. Chuang Tzu's butcher carves the lesson that the effortless path (the straightforward shot) is the skilled one, and Lao Tzu's sage-leadership—lowering oneself, deflecting praise—is exactly how Captain America handles Clint's insurrections. Lao Tzu on sages putting themselves last illuminates Hawkeye's sacrificial death and his legacy passed to Kate Bishop, while the butterfly dream frames his resurrection and the House of M's rewritten reality: with no way to compare the states, life and death are both to be welcomed as parts of the Way.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Happy Ending
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Wenmackers uses the spinning-top ending — Cobb reuniting with his children while the top wobbles off-screen — to run a guided tour of skeptical philosophy through the film's dream mechanics (totems, kicks, Limbo, exponential dream-time). She diagrams and compares Zhuangzi's butterfly, Plato's Cave and theory of Forms, Socratic know-that-you-know-nothing, Descartes's cogito and evil demon, Putnam's brain-in-a-vat, and Nozick's experience machine, arguing that Inception does to its viewers what Plato's Cave was meant to do: make us doubt our own level of reality, so that Nolan himself performs inception on the audience. Her resolution is subjectivist — from inside, every level feels equally real, so like Cobb you should turn away from the top and make the best of wherever you are, which even rescues the happy ending since dream-time runs faster than real time.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Do We Give Shakespeare the Last Word
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Kapper treats Inception as a hip epistemological puzzle — unlike The Matrix, the question is not what is real but how we could know — and follows Ariadne's thread (her mythological clue-giving names the chapter) through the tradition: Plato's Theaetetus and Descartes's supremely cunning deceiver pose 'Am I dreaming now?', Wittgenstein shows the doubt is senseless since 'if I am dreaming, this remark is being dreamed as well', Freud makes dreams the royal road to the unconscious, and Heraclitus says only the waking share a common cosmos. The payoff is Eastern: Zhuangzi's butterfly, Indra's net of mutually reflected jewels, and Schopenhauer's single-dreamer universe turn waking up into an endless regress, so the Buddhist ideal of the awakened one — nirvana, where the ideas of real and dream cease to pertain — becomes the reading of Cobb turning away from the top.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: The End
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Hiu M. Chan contrasts Zhuangzi's butterfly dream with Inception's plot: Zhuangzi forgets his self, dreams without planning, and ends in the 'transformation and unity' of dreamer and butterfly, whereas Cobb's self is constantly highlighted — he plans missions, codes his dreams with motifs (the spinning top, the dream machine, the faceless children, distinct locations, weather, crosscutting), and can never fuse dream and reality. The chapter maps the film's four-layer 'meta-space' narrative structure (exposition through resolution distributed across dream layers) and argues the 'dreams' are really programmed, coded narrative devices, the opposite of the Daoist 'whole' in which reality itself is the biggest dream and a true person no longer dreams. Against semiotic 'dream explaining' (the top means dreaming), she holds that in Daoism the top would mean nothing beyond a spinning top, and contrasts Nolan with Tarkovsky's 'dream worshipping' films like The Mirror. The ending's reunion is thus only apparent: Inception lacks the Daoist harmony that would let Cobb 'become the butterfly.'

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: Notes
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Reads Rust's 'dream inside a locked room' and 'everybody is nobody' monologues through the dream-argument and illusion-of-self traditions: the Upanishads and Advaita's atman/brahman, Vasubandhu's Buddhist non-self, Zhuangzi's butterfly dream, Plato's Theaetetus, and Descartes' dream doubt, plus Metzinger's self-model neuroscience. It diagnoses Rust as a neuro-nihilist in Metzinger's sense and defines his predicament with Nietzsche's nihilist, who judges the world as it is that it ought not to be, while noting Schopenhauer misread India's religions as pessimistic. Thompson argues nihilism is a deep insight gone awry — the self is not a thing but an enacted process like dancing — and reads Rust's final near-death experience of love as proof that transcendence of the dream of being a person is possible.

zhuangzi-perspectivism.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
zhuangzi-perspectivism.title: 10. The Dao of Psychohistory
zhuangzi-perspectivism.relation: Fried reframes Asimov's binary (do individual choices matter to history?) through four Chinese theories of non-action (wu wei). Confucian non-action, ruling by moral example and retiring under an unjust ruler, illuminates Onum Barr's dignified private life; the Dao De Jing's mystical libertarianism, where people self-transform when the ruler stops intervening, resembles Gaia's ruler-less holism; Legalist impersonal non-action (Han Fei's ruler who hides his desires and lets harsh law act) has no clear Foundation analogue; and Zhuangzi's useless tree models Gaal Dornick's TV arc, in which she reclaims agency precisely by choosing private non-action over a scripted role in galactic history.

corporate-personhood.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
corporate-personhood.title: Cobol’s Backyard
corporate-personhood.relation: Malloy argues the real protagonists of Inception are corporations: Cobol Engineering, Proclus Global and Fischer-Morrow move Cobb, Saito and Fischer like chess pieces, making the film a case study in corporate moral personhood. He builds personhood from the capacity to contract and hold rights (Saito buying the airline as Proclus's representative), to bear responsibility for what is done in its name, and to decide through corporate procedures, and he rebuts the objections that corporations lack moral emotions and virtues or vices by distinguishing personhood from personality - psychopaths are still moral persons. He ends with Fischer-Morrow's dilemma between Friedman's shareholder-primacy view and the duties of a member of a moral community, concluding that a monopoly on half the world's energy supply would wrong that community.

corporate-personhood.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
corporate-personhood.title: 14. Is E Corp an Evil Person
corporate-personhood.relation: Wood asks what E Corp ontologically is: on Plato's theory, it would participate in a Form of Corporation, while Aristotle's primary substances show E Corp is not an individual at all - just a name for ways people interact. Corporate personhood (from 1819 contract rights through Citizens United and Hobby Lobby) makes it a legal person whose responsibility diffuses 'almost to the point of evaporation,' and Kant's humanity formula explains the unease: a legal fiction with no intentions or dignity can never respect persons as ends, which is why Angela's quest for a moral 'who' behind Washington Township ends only with the two ordinary executives Price hands her.

corporate-personhood.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
corporate-personhood.title: Too Big to Function
corporate-personhood.relation: Terjesen argues Jack's combined title, Vice President of East Coast Television and Microwave Oven Programming, exhibits the corporate mentality: following Robert Jackall's Moral Mazes, credit flows up (Jack's Trivection oven) and blame flows down (Greenzo, the fireworks fiasco), so managers learn to avoid decisive action. Peter French's thesis that corporations are moral persons explains why GE runs fine with Don Geiss in a coma and Kathy Geiss playing with unicorns, so no one at the top needs to understand the businesses they oversee. MacIntyre's distinction between practices with internal goods and external rewards shows profit-thinking erasing comedy's internal good, turning TGS into 'pos-mens' and product integration, and Adam Smith's attack on distant, ignorant regulators is turned against conglomerate central management itself.

corporate-personhood.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
corporate-personhood.title: Where’s Kenneth We Need to Blame Someone!
corporate-personhood.relation: Michaud takes seriously Jack's love of GE: if Peter French is right that corporations have actorship through their corporate internal decision structure, showing intentionality, rational decision, and behavior change as in the Challenger launch that no individual willed, then GE is a moral person. Following Marvin Brown, he draws the uncomfortable conclusion that we have enslaved corporations: they are designed by stockholders to want only profit, programmed toward corporate suicide in buyouts, with no ethics built into the CID structure. Marx's wage slavery of workers unable to express their creative will is mirrored from above, and the chapter closes by relocating blame: when corporations do evil, the culpable party is us, the free-market supporters who designed the system.

corporate-personhood.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
corporate-personhood.title: Cobol’s Backyard
corporate-personhood.relation: Malloy argues the real players of Inception are the corporations — Cobol Engineering hires Cobb to spy on Saito, Saito as CEO of Proclus Global buys the airline and commissions the Fischer job, and the human characters are pawns moved at the firms' will. He builds a case that corporations are moral persons because they make decisions through their own procedures, hold rights (Saito's 'I bought the airline' exercised Proclus's property rights through a representative), and bear responsibilities not reducible to CEOs or shareholders, rebuffing Harman-style objections from moral emotions and virtues by comparing corporations to psychopaths, who are persons without being good ones. He ends with Fischer-Morrow's impending energy monopoly: Friedman's shareholder-primacy view versus the corporation's duty to the moral community, and what corporate personhood means for real-world practices like boycotts.

bergson-memory.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
bergson-memory.title: Leap of Faith
bergson-memory.relation: Dionne argues Cobb's 'most resilient parasite' works only as an idea embedded in a coherent story - 'my father doesn't want me to be him' - and that since ideas define who we are, each person is less a host than a collection of well-planted narratives. Using Bergson on embodied, memory-and-desire-mediated perception (Cobb's fear of the bridge triggering Mal's projection) and Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil on perspectival appearance as the price of life, she claims dreams differ from reality in degree, not kind: we are beings-in-the-world who stabilize contingency through story-making and 'strive for positive logic'. Hence knowledge always demands the leap of faith that Saito and Mal demand of Cobb, the film becomes a meta-narrative with Fischer as its audience, and the wobbling top offers only an interpretation of a fact, never the fact itself.

bergson-memory.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
bergson-memory.title: Does the Totem Tumble
bergson-memory.relation: Auxier brings Bergson's memory theory, the past gnawing into the present, all dreaming as remembering, and Whitehead's process philosophy to Nolan's 'pathologies of temporal experience', defending the film's supposedly selective physics: with each deeper level the same five minutes disperses across a larger dream space, diluting the carry-over of effects while time expands geometrically, because 'space is frozen time'. He then re-reads the ending through the narrative gaps the audience was lured across: the top was Mal's totem, which Cobb spin as an act of mourning after handling it and betraying her, and Cobb's real totem is his gun, which Saito uses to shoot them both out of Limbo. The top's tumbling in the finale matters only as a sign that Cobb, the coward who once needed total control over Mal, has finally learned the leap of faith of trusting another person.

bergson-memory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-memory.title: Pay Now, Live Later
bergson-memory.relation: This section reads Precrime through Bergson's duree: in Dick's story the precogs are 'monkeys' and 'idiots' emitting snippets that investigators must analyze, while the film shows a precog immersed in and living through the future visually. It explains Bergson's claim that clocks and timelines falsify time, which is really lived duration in which the past endures as memory and actively directs us toward an open future, and rehearses his reunion thought experiment: imagined futures are mere sketches, while the actual future arrives with the unique specificity of the Mona Lisa. No one, on this view, can know the future as if living it.

bergson-memory.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-memory.title: Summarizing the Future
bergson-memory.relation: Applying Bergson's Time and Free Will claim that recalling the past shortens it into a 'thing', the section uses the curriculum-vitae metaphor: like a CV or Facebook page, we imagine the future as a summary compiled from the past. In 'Paycheck', Jennings's sack becomes a plan only when he reflects - the wire at the police station, the token on the bus - until past, present and future fuse and he feels 'a strange elation' at fulfilling his past self's design, raising again whether awareness of the future changes what we do. The film diverges by having Jennings sabotage the atomic-bomb future he foresees, echoing Minority Report's contest between an inevitable future and present action.

bergson-memory.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
bergson-memory.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
bergson-memory.relation: Randall Auxier explains Jeopardy!'s appeal through Bergson's Matter and Memory: memory is a relation - the past acting in the present - along a continuum of matter (repetition of what was) and memory (variation), and the show strips contestants of bodily action so that what we watch is pure 'recollection', the instantaneous summoning of subtle structures from the flux. Providing the question instead of the answer forces a tiny temporal reversal, a six-step durational epoch he calls (after Edgar Sheffield Brightman) a 'shining present', which is why Jeopardy! outshines College Bowl, why champions like Ken Jennings fascinate as savants of immediate recollection, and why the slow clock music of Final Jeopardy! is the show's most exquisite torture and catharsis.

bergson-memory.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
bergson-memory.title: Memory, Imagination, and the Access for the Self Dolores and Maeve
bergson-memory.relation: Trapero-Llobera reads Westworld as the culmination of Jonathan Nolan's Memento and Person of Interest projects, mapping seven nested 'observing systems' (Nolan, Sizemore, Stubbs and Elsie, Ford, the creators' personal stories, Maeve, and William as beta-tester) onto second-wave cybernetics (Foerster, Maturana, Varela, Hayles), where the observer participates in and constructs the observed world through feedback loops. She argues the show's hosts pass through Turing's imitation game (fake memories and personalities from textual repetition, as with Peter Abernathy's reveries), and that Dolores's and Maeve's breakdowns convert prosthetic memory into experienced, autopoietic memory reconstructed in a 'Bergsonian' backward movement that gives them agency and purpose. William's two-timeline transformation into the Man in Black figures the 'semiosis of virtuality' - the hyperreal where original and copy are indistinguishable - ending in a collective bicameral mind in which everyone, audience included, inhabits the god-creator Ford's dream.

bergson-memory.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
bergson-memory.title: From Backwards -Working Memory, or Working Backwards from Memory
bergson-memory.relation: Treats the Caterpillar's 'Who are YOU?' and Alice's 'Who in the world am I? Ah, that's the great puzzle!' as the classic memory-and-identity problem, rallying Plato's wax tablet and Meno doctrine that learning is recollection, Locke's memory criterion of the same person, and Diderot's dialogue on how without memory there would be no connected self. Tyler Shores reads Alice's botched recitations as Bergson's impersonal habit-memory swamping personal memory, her name-forgetting in the wood through Nietzsche's Untimely Meditations on the necessity of forgetting, the Red King's dream as Freud's alienated memory, and the White Queen's memory that 'works both ways' as a thought experiment tying memory, time, and self together.

bergson-memory.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
bergson-memory.title: Leap of Faith
bergson-memory.relation: Dionne reads Cobb's 'idea is the most resilient parasite' as a claim about narrative: what gets incepted in Fischer is a story ('my father doesn't want me to follow in his footsteps'), and by the same token each of us is a collection of incepted stories rather than a stable self. Drawing on Bergson's account of perception mediated by memory and desire (Cobb's bridge triggering Mal's projection), Nietzsche's perspectivism — truth is a 'moral prejudice' and 'we must mistake ourselves' — and the embodiment of the being-in-the-world, she argues dreams differ from reality only in degree, since both are interested story-making under time pressure. The payoff is meta-filmic: Fischer is the spectator and Cobb the director, and the final spinning top becomes the audience's own totem — there is no fact of the matter, only interpretation, so watching the ending is itself the leap of faith.

bergson-memory.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
bergson-memory.title: Does the Totem Tumble
bergson-memory.relation: Randall Auxier claims to settle whether the totem tumbles: it does, but it does not matter, because the top was Mal's totem rather than Cobb's — Cobb spins it as mourning for the wife whose trust he destroyed by handling her totem, while Cobb's real totem is the gun, which Saito must use (shooting them both in Limbo) once Cobb finally takes the leap of faith and entrusts his life to another person. Building on Bergson's memory theory — the past 'gnaws into the future,' all dreaming is remembering, and shared dreaming is possible because embodied species-memory can be tapped with the right chemist — the chapter recasts Cobb's rule against building from memory as the need to introduce gaps between dream and world, and his inability to keep architecting as personal memory increasingly overrunning perception with age. Through Whitehead's process philosophy — narrative as algebraic order, space as 'frozen time,' generic contrasts like 'and then I ate it' — he also defends the film's 'selective physics': at each level the same five minutes disperses across a larger dreamspace, diluting the gravitational carryover while geometrically expanding dream time.

bergson-memory.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
bergson-memory.title: H E N R I B E R G S O N
bergson-memory.relation: Three Part Three essays on Dr. Manhattan's strange relation to time and fate. Christopher Drohan reads Manhattan's simultaneous 'intricately structured jewel' of time through Bergson's Matter and Memory — perception interlaced with memory, the pure past persisting in every act, time as lived duration — so that 'Nothing ever ends, Adrian' becomes a Bergsonian insight and the thermodynamic-miracle speech an intuition of life's creative improbability. Arthur Ward argues theological fatalism (Boethius and Aquinas placing a timeless God outside time, Paley's watchmaker behind Jon the watchmaker's son with his clock-shaped Martian palace) does not doom Laurie's free will, because Jon's own claims are inconsistent — he is surprised by the cancer rumors, misses Veidt's tachyon-shielded plan, and acts drugged — so either his foresight or his fatalism must be false. Andrew Terjesen reads Manhattan as a Stoic sage: Seneca and Epictetus on emotions as false judgments explain his 'a live body and a dead body contain the same number of particles,' his Mars epiphany is the sage's 'good emotion' of joy at the thermodynamic miracle, and his impersonal 'clock without a craftsman' completes a Neo-Stoic line running through Descartes to Spinoza's God-who-is-Nature.

bergson-memory.book: 204 - Westworld and Philosophy - If You Go Looking for the Truth, Get the Whole Thing
bergson-memory.title: Memory, Imagination, and the Access for the Self Dolores and Maeve
bergson-memory.relation: Trapero-Llobera situates Westworld within Jonathan Nolan's body of work (Memento, Person of Interest), arguing the show's apparent complexity hides a classic hero's-journey structure organized around observing systems and a 'semiosis of virtuality.' She reads William/the Man in Black as a 'schizoid android' and catalyst-observer, and Ford/Bernard as creator-and-prosthetic-memory pairs echoing Finch and the Machine. Turing's imitation game frames the hosts' fabricated memories, while Dolores's and Maeve's breakdowns mark a shift from prosthetic to autopoietic, Bergsonian memory-recollection that turns them into observers building their own selves.

bergson-memory.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
bergson-memory.relation: Palmer argues that The Underneath and The Limey fuse film noir's obsession with the untranscendable past with Alain Resnais's Bergsonism, mediated by Deleuze's account of the time-image. In The Limey, career criminal Wilson's consciousness accumulates recollection-images (including Poor Cow footage of a young Stamp) and prospective imaginings (the two visualized shootings), building toward a Bergsonian intuition: confronting Terry Valentine, Wilson recognizes himself as the same kind of selfish betrayer and spares him, achieving a redemption denied noir predecessors like Get Carter's Carter and Point Blank's Walker. The Underneath, by contrast, uses achronic color-coded structure only to define Michael from the outside, which Palmer counts a partial failure of the same interior ambition.

bergson-memory.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
bergson-memory.relation: King analyzes The Limey as 'Get Carter as made by Alain Resnais,' using Bordwell's fabula/syuzhet distinction to show how its nonlinear editing renders what Soderbergh calls the nonlinear nature of thought. Dialogue continuity is stretched across discontinuous spaces (the Wilson-Elaine 'embarrassed/ashamed/disappointed' exchange), flash-forwards precede events, and the party shooting is replayed three times as Wilson's fantasy. King argues the whole film reads as Wilson's subjective reconstruction on the plane home, grounded in Bergson (via Deleuze's time-image) yet, unlike Resnais's Marienbad, never producing real ontological or epistemological doubt because the revenge-thriller backbone and color-coding keep it legible. The film's dominant note is nostalgia for a past that, because of Wilson's imprisonments, never really was.

bergson-duration.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: Chapter 24 - I Know What You Did Next Summer
bergson-duration.relation: Paul Atkinson's introduction to Chapter 24 frames 'The Minority Report' and 'Paycheck', together with their film adaptations, as explorations of the many different ways of knowing the future. He proposes Henri Bergson - who denied the future can be known and explained why we sometimes think we can - as the philosopher perfectly placed to 'write the rules' for the time-travel game these stories play. It also contrasts philosophy's umpire-like settling of issues with the films' urge to literally show us the future rather than merely predict it.

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: Pay Now, Live Later
bergson-duration.relation: This section reads Precrime through Bergson's duree: in Dick's story the precogs are 'monkeys' and 'idiots' emitting snippets that investigators must analyze, while the film shows a precog immersed in and living through the future visually. It explains Bergson's claim that clocks and timelines falsify time, which is really lived duration in which the past endures as memory and actively directs us toward an open future, and rehearses his reunion thought experiment: imagined futures are mere sketches, while the actual future arrives with the unique specificity of the Mona Lisa. No one, on this view, can know the future as if living it.

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: I Can Predict What You (Don’t) Do Next Summer
bergson-duration.relation: Using Bergson's imprevisible and 'The Possible and the Real', this section argues that the story's Precrime works by prediction-as-elimination: investigators discard the precogs' babblings that do not fit the world, 'closing the gate' on the impossible to leave only a statistically possible future. Bergson's gate metaphor shows prediction never yields the real future, only the negatively 'not impossible', yet Precrime arrests people for an abstract possible event they have never actually lived. It ends by asking whether Anderton, accused of a future murder in advance, would still commit it, since ever-changing memory and knowledge make a possible future never identical to the actual one.

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: Living in the Time of the Crime
bergson-duration.relation: A close reading of the film's opening murder contrasts cinematic precognition with the story's: the camera moves from Sarah Marks's terrified face and dilated pupil to the precog Agatha's watery blue eye as she utters 'murder', making Agatha an empathetic witness immersed in the scene. Anderton then pieces the moving images together like a film editor working with rushes, so no analytic machinery connects present to future - the future is simply given in visual detail. In the film, precognition is the foreseeable rather than the predictable: precogs and audience alike live in the time of the crime.

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: Always Invest in the Future
bergson-duration.relation: This section retells 'Paycheck' in story and John Woo film versions: engineer Jennings trades two memory-wiped years for a cloth sack of ordinary objects - a piece of wire, a bus token - which his erased past self chose as tools for future crises, from breaking out of a police cell to paying a robot ticket inspector. It explains the story's time machine, a 'mirror' that images the future and a 'scoop' that extracts objects from it, a significant difference from the movie. The section shows how past-Jennings exists for present-Jennings only through these leftovers, which prove more valuable than money.

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: Summarizing the Future
bergson-duration.relation: Applying Bergson's Time and Free Will claim that recalling the past shortens it into a 'thing', the section uses the curriculum-vitae metaphor: like a CV or Facebook page, we imagine the future as a summary compiled from the past. In 'Paycheck', Jennings's sack becomes a plan only when he reflects - the wire at the police station, the token on the bus - until past, present and future fuse and he feels 'a strange elation' at fulfilling his past self's design, raising again whether awareness of the future changes what we do. The film diverges by having Jennings sabotage the atomic-bomb future he foresees, echoing Minority Report's contest between an inevitable future and present action.

bergson-duration.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
bergson-duration.title: The Future as Predictive Text
bergson-duration.relation: The section develops a 'predictive text' metaphor: once Jennings's past is constructed as a narrative by past-Jennings, the future merely mirrors it, filling in missing letters like autocorrect - as in the ticket-stub passage where Jennings deduces where he 'had been' and concludes 'he had foreseen this too.' It contrasts the short stories, where a possible future only guides present action, with both films' screens - rewinding videotape, headline videos of an exploding city, the Minority Report editing suite - that render the future almost indistinguishable from the present. For Bergson the future can never appear on a television screen, since that would require a camera living in the time of the event; at most the future is a gate closing or a frame narrowing to a vague sketch.

bergson-duration.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
bergson-duration.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
bergson-duration.relation: Randall Auxier explains Jeopardy!'s appeal through Bergson's Matter and Memory: memory is a relation - the past acting in the present - along a continuum of matter (repetition of what was) and memory (variation), and the show strips contestants of bodily action so that what we watch is pure 'recollection', the instantaneous summoning of subtle structures from the flux. Providing the question instead of the answer forces a tiny temporal reversal, a six-step durational epoch he calls (after Edgar Sheffield Brightman) a 'shining present', which is why Jeopardy! outshines College Bowl, why champions like Ken Jennings fascinate as savants of immediate recollection, and why the slow clock music of Final Jeopardy! is the show's most exquisite torture and catharsis.

bergson-duration.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
bergson-duration.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
bergson-duration.relation: Through a hot-tub dialogue in Prismo's Time Room, the chapter walks Jake through the main theories of time: McTaggart's A-theory versus B-theory, plus presentism, the growing block, eternalism and four-dimensionalism, illustrated with the mirror-Finn dream, Farmworld Finn, Jake's unchangeable croak dream, and the Ancient Psychic Tandem War Elephant as a thing stretched across past, present and future selves. Booko's description of the multiverse becomes a springboard for David Lewis's possible-worlds realism and Everett's many-worlds reading of Prismo's 'alternate wish worlds'. Finally, quotes from McTaggart and Bergson delivered as Finn's Glasses of Nerdicon rant argue that time resists spatial and scientific analysis and must be lived, which the authors tie to relativity, black-hole cosmology and Prismo's Time Room as the one dimension outside time.

bergson-duration.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
bergson-duration.title: Deleuze Jam Today
bergson-duration.relation: Walks Alice through four theories of time: Augustine's three presents in Confessions (Alice 'was a different person then'; the past exists only as present memory), Kant's time as a subjective form of intuition presupposed by experience (the White Rabbit's anxiety about being late already requires it), Bergson's indivisible duration against spatialized clock time (running fastest with the Red Queen yet ending under the same tree; the Hatter stuck at six o'clock; Zeno's Achilles resolved by indivisible acts), and Deleuze's chronos and aion from The Logic of Sense. Mark W. Westmoreland reads 'jam to-morrow and jam yesterday—but never jam to-day' as pure aion: the present never arrives, only an endlessly subdividing past-future.

bergson-duration.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
bergson-duration.title: Only Time Will Tell
bergson-duration.relation: Latta reads the film through Bergson's distinction between clock time and duration: Strange is introduced as pure quantitative multiplicity — identifying Chuck Mangione's 'Feels So Good' (1977) mid-surgery, surrounding himself with watches, including Christine Palmer's inscribed 'Time will tell how much I love you' — while the Ancient One lives duration, surrendering to the river's current. Kaecilius embodies 'chronological nihilism' ('time is an insult'), and his and Dormammu's timeless Dark Dimension is existentially impossible for Bergson, since life only progresses and endures in time. The climax shows Strange recreating the present in the endless looped bargain with Dormammu ('pain is an old friend'), growing through qualitative multiplicity and élan vital, until the shattered watch — hands broken, inscription intact — marks his conversion from counting time to living it.

bergson-duration.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
bergson-duration.title: H E N R I B E R G S O N
bergson-duration.relation: Three Part Three essays on Dr. Manhattan's strange relation to time and fate. Christopher Drohan reads Manhattan's simultaneous 'intricately structured jewel' of time through Bergson's Matter and Memory — perception interlaced with memory, the pure past persisting in every act, time as lived duration — so that 'Nothing ever ends, Adrian' becomes a Bergsonian insight and the thermodynamic-miracle speech an intuition of life's creative improbability. Arthur Ward argues theological fatalism (Boethius and Aquinas placing a timeless God outside time, Paley's watchmaker behind Jon the watchmaker's son with his clock-shaped Martian palace) does not doom Laurie's free will, because Jon's own claims are inconsistent — he is surprised by the cancer rumors, misses Veidt's tachyon-shielded plan, and acts drugged — so either his foresight or his fatalism must be false. Andrew Terjesen reads Manhattan as a Stoic sage: Seneca and Epictetus on emotions as false judgments explain his 'a live body and a dead body contain the same number of particles,' his Mars epiphany is the sage's 'good emotion' of joy at the thermodynamic miracle, and his impersonal 'clock without a craftsman' completes a Neo-Stoic line running through Descartes to Spinoza's God-who-is-Nature.

bergson-duration.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
bergson-duration.title: Spontaneity, Immediacy, and Difference Philosophy, Being in Time, and Creativity in the Aesthetics of Jack Ker
bergson-duration.relation: David Need contrasts three theories of 'being in time' behind the aesthetics of spontaneity: Kerouac's debt to Spengler's organic cycles of civilization (a stereoscopic, dualist view where an arbitrary measure like a candle or page limns deep being), Olson's use of Whitehead's 'concrescence' in 'Projective Verse' (a monist, all-at-once projection of new monads), and Cage's use of Coomaraswamy's Vedanta, where silence is sabdabrahman and chance imitates Nature. He argues the real fault line is the old monist-vs-dualist divide (Advaita brahman vs. Cartesian dualism), and that each artist's notion of creative freedom follows from which metaphysical schema he borrowed, so our quarrels with the Beats reflect our own metaphysical stakes.

bergson-duration.book: 228 - The Philosophy of Science Fiction Film
bergson-duration.title: Disenchantment and Rebellion in Alphaville
bergson-duration.relation: Woolfolk reads Godard's Alphaville as an imagination of spiritual disaster: the Alpha 60 computer's reduction of time to divisible units suppresses the Bergsonian durée and fundamental self, and the city's architecture of 'nonplaces' embodies Weber's disenchantment and the Frankfurt School's culture-industry critique. Following Charles Taylor, he argues disenchantment opens a new heroic framework of facing an indifferent universe with lucidity, in which Lemmy Caution—a postmodern pastiche of noir dandies—rebels through an aestheticized eroticism and Éluard's surrealist poetry, achieving a Weberian 'this-worldly salvation' of art and love that succeeds where Orwell's Julia and Huxley's Savage fail.

bergson-duration.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
bergson-duration.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
bergson-duration.relation: Palmer argues that The Underneath and The Limey fuse film noir's obsession with the untranscendable past with Alain Resnais's Bergsonism, mediated by Deleuze's account of the time-image. In The Limey, career criminal Wilson's consciousness accumulates recollection-images (including Poor Cow footage of a young Stamp) and prospective imaginings (the two visualized shootings), building toward a Bergsonian intuition: confronting Terry Valentine, Wilson recognizes himself as the same kind of selfish betrayer and spares him, achieving a redemption denied noir predecessors like Get Carter's Carter and Point Blank's Walker. The Underneath, by contrast, uses achronic color-coded structure only to define Michael from the outside, which Palmer counts a partial failure of the same interior ambition.

bergson-duration.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
bergson-duration.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
bergson-duration.relation: King analyzes The Limey as 'Get Carter as made by Alain Resnais,' using Bordwell's fabula/syuzhet distinction to show how its nonlinear editing renders what Soderbergh calls the nonlinear nature of thought. Dialogue continuity is stretched across discontinuous spaces (the Wilson-Elaine 'embarrassed/ashamed/disappointed' exchange), flash-forwards precede events, and the party shooting is replayed three times as Wilson's fantasy. King argues the whole film reads as Wilson's subjective reconstruction on the plane home, grounded in Bergson (via Deleuze's time-image) yet, unlike Resnais's Marienbad, never producing real ontological or epistemological doubt because the revenge-thriller backbone and color-coding keep it legible. The film's dominant note is nostalgia for a past that, because of Wilson's imprisonments, never really was.

bergson-duration.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
bergson-duration.title: 10_LaRocca_Chapter_009.html
bergson-duration.relation: William Day argues that Herzog's Cave of Forgotten Dreams, filming the 32,000-year-old Chauvet Cave paintings in 3D, works not by preserving a past but by transfiguring the present, placing the viewer in a 'mythological relation to time.' He reads three literary precursors to this cinematic 'doubleness'—Emerson's 'History' and 'The American Scholar' (the past made 'now'), Thoreau's spectator-self in Walden's 'Solitude,' and Weil's 'renunciation of time'—as antecedents to Cavell's ontology of film. The Fred Astaire shadow-dance from Swing Time, spliced into the cave footage, becomes Day's emblem of what becomes of things on film: the shadows dance on after Astaire stops.

bergson-duration.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
bergson-duration.title: 15_LaRocca_Chapter_014.html
bergson-duration.relation: Bernadette Wegenstein examines her own cinema-verite practice in The Good Breast (and See You Soon Again), arguing that verite 'provokes' rather than merely produces truth through the filmmaker's participatory presence. She grounds this in Italian neorealism via Bazin (the real 'aimed at,' not re-presented) and Deleuze's Cinema II 'time-image'—a Bergsonian cinema 'of the seer' attuned to lived duration. Through her breast-cancer patient-characters (Doris, Carol, Debra, Shelia) and the surgeon Dr. Schnaper's trip to Saint Agatha's Catania, she shows how editing calls forth an 'alternate reality' and an existential (Kracauerian) realism.

bergson-duration.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
bergson-duration.title: 18_LaRocca_Chapter_017.html
bergson-duration.relation: Selmin Kara reads Victor Erice's Dream of Light (The Quince Tree Sun), about the painter Antonio Lopez trying to capture a quince tree in shifting autumn light, as a case for a 'new materialist' ontology of documentary against Bill Nichols-style representationalism. Drawing on Deleuze via De Landa's actual/virtual continuum, Spinoza's and Bergson's vital-matter lineage, and Bennett's 'vibrant matter,' she argues the film's dream sequence of the operator-less camera, dimmer and rotting fruit foregrounds the mediation rather than the mastery of light. She proposes updating Grierson's 'creative treatment of actuality' to 'the creative treatment of actuality and virtuality,' treating filmic and profilmic matter as intra-acting agents.

intentional-stance.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
intentional-stance.title: . . Because My Furnace Believed the House Was Cold
intentional-stance.relation: Explains Dennett's physical, design, and intentional stances through a disk drive 'reading' a disk and a thermostat we would never say 'believes' the room is cold, concluding that whether behavior counts as conscious is a choice of vocabulary, not a metaphysical difference. Dick's post-war world of convincing simulacra and economic necessity is the setting in which linguistic conventions shift, explaining Deckard's changed attitudes toward Luba Luft and Rachael.

intentional-stance.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
intentional-stance.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
intentional-stance.relation: Don Fallis proposes deception rather than language as the personhood test: following Dennett, a deceiver must be a second-order intentional system who can want someone else to have a false belief, as when General Thade lies to Senator Sandar about Ari's kidnapping, Zira and Cornelius feign muteness before the Presidential Commission, and Caesar fakes his own electrocution in Conquest. The roles' reversal makes this a test for the films' mute humans too, while Descartes's beast machines, Wittgenstein on dogs that cannot simulate pain, and Lloyd Morgan's canon voice the skeptical reading of fake alarm calls and Koko's 'Cat did it.' Against them Fallis invokes Occam's Razor over Hare, Call and Tomasello's food-competition experiments: apes track who sees what, but they fail the misinformed false-belief version, so real apes may not be 'sneaky enough to be people.'

intentional-stance.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
intentional-stance.title: 11. What Mary Didn’t Know
intentional-stance.relation: Demeter reconstructs five rival explanations of Mary's hesitation to accept Matthew - emotional uncertainty, greed, fear of social exclusion over Pamuk, bad conscience, and conflicting family pressures - and argues none can be singled out as true. Via Frayn's Copenhagen, Dennett's 'Real Patterns,' and Henry James's The Golden Bowl as read by Robert Pippin, he defends the indeterminacy of psychological interpretation: motives are accessed only through behavior filtered through the interpreter's own psychological apparatus, and on the stronger view there are no motivation-facts prior to interpretation at all. What Mary did not know about her own hesitation may therefore not be knowable in principle, by her or by us.

intentional-stance.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
intentional-stance.title: 11. What Mary Didn’t Know
intentional-stance.relation: Demeter argues that Mary's long hesitation over Matthew is radically underdetermined, sketching five rival interpretations of the same first-season events: emotional uncertainty, greed, fear of scandal over the Pamuk affair, bad conscience, and conflicting family pressure, each consistent with her behavior yet mutually exclusive. Via Frayn's play Copenhagen and the quantum measurement analogy he first treats this as a limit on human knowledge, then, using Dennett's 'Real Patterns' and Henry James's The Golden Bowl, defends the stronger metaphysical claim that there is no fact of the matter: psychological interpretation creates the very patterns it claims to find, so even Mary cannot know her own motives. What Mary didn't know may, on this view, be unknowable in principle.

intentional-stance.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
intentional-stance.title: The Attack of the Chinese Room
intentional-stance.relation: Novy asks whether the Living Armor of 'The Mask in the Iron Man' — consciousness struck into it by lightning during the Whiplash fight, later tearing out its own heart to save Tony — really thinks. Turing's test and functionalism (any successful rescue of Yinsen is functionally equivalent, whatever the means) say only behavior matters, and Dennett's intentional stance has us treat the armor, like Darwin's burrow-plugging earthworms, as if it has beliefs and desires; against this, Leibniz's mill and Searle's Chinese Room — with Happy Hogan shuffling symbol cards he cannot read, held by 'Searle the Mandarin agent' — insist symbol manipulation never yields understanding. The chapter's reply: open the Mandarin's skull and you find only gray goop and neurons, so if behavior cannot ground understanding in the armor, it cannot in us either — we may all be in the Chinese Room.

intentional-stance.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
intentional-stance.title: Notes
intentional-stance.relation: Uses a vintage Blue Snaggletooth action figure to illustrate Dennett's three stances - physical (AFA wear-grading of dented boots), design (why the Sears-exclusive mispack is valuable), and intentional (predicting whether Han would shoot first at a pedant correcting his parsec gaffe) - arguing that play trains a third-person science of mind that Descartes' first-person introspection and dualism could never verify. Dennett's account of religion as a misapplied intentional stance then explains begging the Falcon to 'hold together' and Zeus's lightning as projected intention, with the twist that children playing with figures know they are pretending while the superstitious mind does not.

neoplatonism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
neoplatonism.title: Remembrance of Being, Passed
neoplatonism.relation: Reads Ubik's anti-chronological regressions — rocket to jet to biplane, 1992 decaying into 1939 — through Dick's 'orthogonal time' peeling onion-like layers toward greater Being, which Dick himself compared to Plotinus's concentric emanations from the One beyond all language and comprehension. Dick's 1974 pink-light experience is interpreted as Platonic anamnesis, recovered memory of the forms in a parallel time-stream, shading into the Gnostic conviction that our flawed material universe was created by an imperfect god.

neoplatonism.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
neoplatonism.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
neoplatonism.relation: Bernard Wills takes the reference to The Cloud of Unknowing in 'The Window' as the key to Cohen's lifelong fascination with apophatic, negative mysticism - God sought beyond every image in a 'naked intent of love,' as in the medieval Cloud, Dionysius, Maimonides, and Kabbalah - against the kataphatic way of affirmation. He reads Recent Songs as an album of exile and the play of union and separation ('Un Canadien Errant,' 'Ballad of the Absent Mare'), where the incarnate Word is 'stuttered' and 'frozen,' a passion without resurrection. Cohen's later Zen turn is thus prefigured: the emptiness of sunyata and the Neo-Platonic descent from and return to the One are positive nothingness - self-overcoming in the service of compassion rather than the black-romantic nihilism of self-annihilation.

neoplatonism.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
neoplatonism.title: Dracula and Philosophy
neoplatonism.relation: Willis and Strunk read the scene where Dracula forces Mina to drink blood from his bare chest through Plotinus's Enneads: the mutual blood exchange is a dark unicity, a perverted oneness joining life and death, through which the soulless, blood-dependent Count tries to steal Mina's agency, Intellect, and her link to the world soul because he cannot be self-sufficient or create his own meaning. Their interconnected minds are also his undoing - Mina's hypnotic bond tracks Dracula to his coffin, and his destruction at Van Helsing's hands frees her - so the chapter concludes that this perversion of Plotinian oneness exposes our fear that the veil between the living and the dead is dangerously thin.

neoplatonism.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
neoplatonism.title: 17. The Cry of Love
neoplatonism.relation: Reads Hendrix as a romantic idealist on a Platonic-Neoplatonic arc: 'Room Full of Mirrors' shatters the cave wall and its projections toward The One, whose presence is pursued through eros with the veiled Beloved of Plotinus — the semi-divine feminine of 'Little Wing,' 'One Rainy Wish,' and 'Angel.' Hegel's Zeitgeist and world-spirit then frame the planned First Rays of the New Rising Sun as music meant to carry humanity's collective evolution, with Hendrix as Hegel's 'spiritual workman' and self-described messenger ('I am only a messenger and you are a Sheep in the process of evolution').

neoplatonism.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
neoplatonism.title: 7. The Mind Flayer through a Gnostic Lens
neoplatonism.relation: Ewing reads the Mind Flayer as the Demiurge of the Upside Down, a dark derivative copy of our world complete with replicated Castle Byers and school decorations: he surveys Plato's Timaeus craftsman who shapes chaotic matter on the model of the Forms, Plotinus's One and its secondary demiurge, and the Gnostic variants, from the Valentinian just-but-imperfect craftsman to the Sethian Yaldabaoth, a serpent-faced false god who steals divine power. Because the Mind Flayer hive-minds Will and the demodogs, wants to conquer our dimension as a 'master race,' and hates the real world rather than serving it, the chapter concludes it matches the Sethian evil Demiurge, an incorporeal entity playing at being god.

neoplatonism.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
neoplatonism.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
neoplatonism.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' (Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, Aang's glimpse of the girl who will be Toph) through Plotinus's teaching that time is 'the life of the Soul' and Augustine's three presents of memory, attention, and expectation, so that past and future are present to the soul and Huu's 'time is an illusion and so is death' becomes literal metaphysics. The banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, models Neoplatonic emanation from the One, and this unity explains the Avatar's communion with past and future selves as well as Aang's refusal to kill Ozai, since death, like time, is a misperception.

neoplatonism.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
neoplatonism.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
neoplatonism.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' through Plotinus and Augustine: Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, and Aang's unknown giggling girl are, respectively, memory, attention, and expectation, Augustine's three presents, while Plotinus's hierarchy of One, Intellect, and world Soul, with time as 'the life of the Soul,' lets what is successive for us be simultaneous from eternity. Huu's banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, is read as Neoplatonic emanation, and Toph's later root-connectedness in LoK shows the ability is not exclusive to the Avatar. Since past and future Avatar selves are thus present to Aang, death, like time, is an illusion, which underwrites his refusal to kill Ozai.

neoplatonism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
neoplatonism.title: Between Two Camps in the Witcher
neoplatonism.relation: Kammerer reads the Witcherverse's magic through the fault line between 'big tent' Platonism (top-down causation from a source, a great chain of being of nested celestial spheres) and modern naturalism (bottom-up mechanism). The Season of Storms exchange in which Geralt tells Dandelion that meteoric swords gather power descending through elemental planes - without denying those planes exist - shows Sapkowski keeping both worldviews alive, while Novigrad's Eternal Fire pogrom in The Witcher 3 mirrors fourth-century Alexandria's wars over magic and Christianity. Heidegger's 'metaphysics grounds an age' and his critique of enframing nature as standing-reserve frame Yennefer's instrumental view of magic and her djinn-summoning in The Last Wish, and Plotinus's Enneads supplies the vision of true magic as internal to a cosmic emanation rather than a mere technology.

spinoza-determinism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-determinism.title: The Nature and Origin of the “Mind”
spinoza-determinism.relation: This section reads Fat's cosmology, in which the 'Mind' created the 'Brain' to preserve the memory of its dead sister and left every constituent of the universe partly deranged with grief, against Spinoza's proofs in the Ethics that there is exactly one infinite, uncaused substance, which is why Spinoza calls the blob God or Nature. It stresses Spinoza's necessitarianism: the will is not a free cause, even God had no choice not to create the world, and the actual timeline is the only metaphysically possible one, so on both Fat's and Spinoza's schemes suffering is a built-in metaphysical consequence.

spinoza-determinism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-determinism.title: The Origin and Nature of Affective Disorder
spinoza-determinism.relation: Using the opening of VALIS, the section explains Gloria's suicide through Spinoza's account of the passions: imagining we are hated without cause breeds hatred, and Spinoza's lone remark on suicide says those who kill themselves are 'impotent in mind,' overcome by external causes opposed to their nature, since our essence just is the conatus, the striving to persist in being. It then itemizes Fat's three tragedies (Gloria's death, the divorce, losing his son) as accumulating external causes that overwhelmed him into his own suicide attempt, and presents his therapist Maurice's 'take responsibility for your own life' as implicitly Spinozan advice.

spinoza-determinism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-determinism.title: Of Plasmatic Bondage
spinoza-determinism.relation: The section explains Fat's plasmate doctrine, with VALIS a Vast Active Living Intelligence System and Sophia the two-year-old who briefly cures Fat by revealing he is an alternate personality of Philip K. Dick before dying of a radiation overdose. It contrasts this failed miraculous cure with Spinoza's intellectual therapy: since 'in so far as the mind understands all things as necessary, so far has it greater power over the affects,' Fat should process Gloria's death as a necessity he could never have prevented, dissolving his guilt.

spinoza-determinism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
spinoza-determinism.title: The Power of the Intellect, or of Fat’s Emotional Liberation
spinoza-determinism.relation: This section argues that although Fat's 'Mind' cosmology, unlike Spinoza's necessitarianism, leaves room for free will, Fat can still borrow Spinoza's therapy: Tractatus entry 29 says we fell through an intellectual error, taking the phenomenal world as real, so he is morally innocent, and Spinoza's concession that we suffer insofar as we are part of nature means suffering can be limited, not eliminated, by understanding its causes. It closes skeptically, noting that monist liberation demands ditching free will, contingency, and self-evident beliefs, so within a monist world 'sometimes it is an appropriate response to reality to go insane.'

spinoza-determinism.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
spinoza-determinism.title: Notes
spinoza-determinism.relation: The chapter argues modding is the deepest freedom Bethesda-era Fallout offers: Sartre and Beauvoir's absolute freedom and facticity explain why vanilla players merely pick among given priorities while modders inject new meaning into the game, constrained but not determined by the Creation Engine. Spinoza's causal determinism becomes a model of 'immanent freedom' — just as Spinoza's agent is free by understanding their place in Nature's web of causes, the modder is free by grasping how they fit into the load orders, plugin files, and tools of the Creation Kit. Simone Weil's ideal of self-directed labor culminates the argument: Fallout: London's five-year, unpaid total conversion (the Atta-Boy, Churchill the bulldog, the punk-anarchist Pistols) embodies the convergence of thought and action that Moira Brown's line about putting broken glass back together captures.

spinoza-determinism.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
spinoza-determinism.title: Group Will
spinoza-determinism.relation: Testerman argues the film's heist is ironic because nobody in it acts from conscious will: citing Libet's readiness-potential experiments and Penfield's stimulation cases, she claims the feeling of willing is a post-hoc 'epistemic illusion,' so Fischer's inception merely dramatizes what happens all the time — Cobb's 'all experience is inception' becomes a thesis about ordinary agency, with Spinoza's dictum that freedom is ignorance of the causes of our actions as its motto. She reads the plot through this lens: Saito's unexamined hunger for power silently drives the team's 'group will,' Cobb's 'positive emotion trumps negative emotion' tactic exploits the limbic system, and cheaper tricks (Arthur's elephant, foot-in-the-door, subliminal advertising) would have worked as well. Against Socrates she concludes the unexamined life is perfectly livable, since introspection can never reach the subconscious causes of behavior.

gnosticism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
gnosticism.title: Chapter 17 - The Gnosis of 2-3-74
gnosticism.relation: Ronald S. Green's introduction connects Dick's last novels to the Gnostic texts of the Nag Hammadi Library, where the material universe arises from accidents, mistakes, and the devices of an imperfect architect ignorant of the true creator. It recounts how the 2-3-74 visions began with a delivery woman's fish pendant and bright rectangular images, and argues that the contradictory retellings across VALIS, Radio Free Albemuth, and the Exegesis support one another the way Gnostic myth does, each an imperfect reflection of a higher truth that ordinary terms cannot express.

gnosticism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
gnosticism.title: Dick’s Gnosis about Gnostics
gnosticism.relation: The section reconstructs the 1945 discovery of the Nag Hammadi codices and retells the cosmogonies of The Hypostasis of the Archons and On the Origin of the World: Sophia's experiment produces a veil of darkness, the aborted watery chaos, and Yaldabaoth, the blind ruler who declares himself God and shapes Adam from mud as a reflection of a reflection. It shows that Horselover Fat cites Yaltabaoth to a baffled psychiatrist and treats the Library, available in English only from 1977, as confirming rather than shaping his belief that his private insanity mirrors humanity's collective forgetting that we ourselves are divine.

gnosticism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
gnosticism.title: Dick’s Twins
gnosticism.relation: This section explains the Gnostic doctrine of syzygy, necessarily co-existing male-female pairs, including the Gospel of Thomas's claim that Thomas and Jesus are identical twins, and reads Dick's lifelong mourning of his twin sister, dead five weeks after their premature births, as its biographical echo. It then traces syzygic pairings through the VALIS trilogy (Emmanuel and Zina, Herb Asher and Linda Fox, the strangely real-and-unreal Rybys) and argues that per Exegesis entry 32 the unfolding of the world narrates the death of half of a divine syzygy, the tragic motif Dick perpetually re-enacts.

gnosticism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
gnosticism.title: Results of the Primordial Rape
gnosticism.relation: The section retells the Gnostic rewrite of Genesis in which the rulers, lusting after the luminous Zoe, defile only the clay replica she secretly substituted, while the real woman becomes the Tree of Knowledge; the instructor reveals the fruit grants gnosis rather than death, and Yaltabaoth's prohibition was itself engineered by the true God to draw attention to the tree. It draws out the consequences (expulsion, toil and childbirth as deliberate burdens, the undefiled bloodline of Seth and Norea) and notes a Gnostic parallel to Deckard's sexual aggression in Blade Runner.

gnosticism.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
gnosticism.title: Pink Light
gnosticism.relation: This section argues that Dick's handling of the pink light enacts the Gnostic conviction that salvation comes from direct inner revelation rather than faith, sacraments, or church, cataloguing his competing theories: transmissions from a VALIS satellite that may itself be Yaldabaoth, mere ruler of the material realm, possession by Elijah, or his being Thomas the twin of Jesus. It weighs Dick's answers to why the true God permits the blind ruler (self-reflection, God's love of games, or our own labyrinth built to see if we could not escape) and the Gospel of Thomas's warning that the divine within will destroy us if we do not bring it forth.

gnosticism.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
gnosticism.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
gnosticism.relation: Gary Shapiro treats The Future as a 'lyrical phenomenology' of time that stages multiple temporalities rather than one theory of time. 'The Future' evokes an apocalypse where the katechon - the Biblical restraining force holding back the end - no longer works, while 'Waiting for the Miracle' anatomizes passive deferral in a way Shapiro finds sharper than the Stoic critique of waiting by Seneca and Marcus Aurelius and Nietzsche's 'problem of those who wait,' opposing wasted chronos to the seized kairos of 'First We Take Manhattan.' 'Anthem's' crack that lets the light in gets a Gnostic reading, 'Democracy' is glossed through Derrida's 'democracy to come' as messianic, always-arriving futurity, and 'Closing Time' and 'Always' add honky-tonk eschatology and the vow of eternal love.

disability-philosophy.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
disability-philosophy.title: Chapter 30 - “The Golden Man”
disability-philosophy.relation: Jeremy Pierce reads 'The Golden Man' through the Aristotle-Lucretius dispute over purposes in nature: Cris Johnson, the precognitive golden mutant, first terrifies the DCA as Homo superior, 'a deeve who would be to us what we are to the great apes', until George Baines finds 'virtually no frontal lobe... It's nothing but an animal' choosing by reflex rather than reflection. Aristotle's teleology - normal development suiting what is objectively good for a human being - makes sense of calling one-armed growth, autism's deficits, or Cris's missing inner life deficiencies, while Lucretius's anti-teleology, largely adopted by the autism community, permits talk only of the typical and atypical. The chapter argues the characters' horror at humanity's replacement by reflex-driven breeders is unintelligible unless something is genuinely missing that is natural and healthy for human offspring.

disability-philosophy.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
disability-philosophy.title: 7. Disabled at Downton
disability-philosophy.relation: Richmond weighs Downton's disability portrayals against disability-studies standards, citing Paul Longmore on media images and the 'super-crip' stereotype. Bates is the positive case: he endures Thomas's and O'Brien's ability-based discrimination, throws away the painful leg brace and rejects the idea that disability demands a medical cure, accepts disability as identity ('We all carry scars, Mr. Bates'), and marries Anna, refuting the era's stereotype that disabled people cannot be employees or lovers. Matthew is the harmful case: his paraplegia ends in Dr. Clarkson's 'spinal shock' misdiagnosis - a miracle cure - and talk of a 'normal life,' reinforcing the medical model and teaching real disabled viewers that their lives are over, so the author wants 'more Bateses, and fewer Matthews.'

disability-philosophy.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
disability-philosophy.title: 13. Bran, Hodor, and Disability in Westeros
disability-philosophy.relation: Pierce uses Westeros's many disabled characters - Bran's paralysis, Jaime's lost hand, Hodor, Aemon's blindness, Varys and Theon's castration - to test the medical and social models of disability and the 'mere difference' view, asking whether disability is merely unaccommodated impairment or intrinsically worse for the one who has it. With the left-handedness analogy and the distinction between local and global harm, he then pits Aristotle's natural teleology (legs are for walking and eyes for seeing, so their loss is a real local bad) against Lucretius's Epicurean anti-teleology (no purposes in nature, so no intrinsic lack), concluding that even if disabilities are locally bad, Bran, Hodor, and Varys can be globally flourishing and heroic.

disability-philosophy.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
disability-philosophy.title: 8. Night of the Living Disabled
disability-philosophy.relation: Reads Constance's treatment of Addy and Beau Langdon through the eugenic roots of the horror genre (Angela Smith's Hideous Progeny, The Black Stork, the Production Code): outward bodily difference assumed to prove inner defect, and the disabled treated as better off dead - Addy finding peace only as 'a pretty girl at last' after death, Beau suffocated in the attic. Against the medical model the chapter defends Alison Kafer's political-relational model and crip futurity (Tate's 'He only suffered because of you'), arguing that ableism, not disability itself, makes their lives unlivable and that imagining disabled futures differently is a matter of survival.

disability-philosophy.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
disability-philosophy.title: 10. Too Freaking Bad
disability-philosophy.relation: Reads Freak Show through Erving Goffman's Stigma - virtual versus actual social identity, the three types of stigma, discredited versus discreditable conditions, and spoiled identity - and through an analysis of exploitation, dignity, and consent: Elsa's claim that the real monsters are 'the people outside this tent', the courts' defense of freaks' right to perform, and the argument that Ryan Murphy's own casting - real disabled performers as window dressing behind able-bodied stars playing freaks, with roles too scarce for true consent - replicates the exploitation the season condemns, which may be the real horror story.

disability-philosophy.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
disability-philosophy.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
disability-philosophy.relation: Argues Toph Beifong is not a pejorative Supercrip stereotype but a Proud Disabled Person counterstory, using Hilde Lindemann's account of master narratives and identity: the BOD and IIH narratives (better-off-dead, irrationally happy) and the Supercrip all presume disability means suffering, while Toph's grumpiness, depth, and central role defy them. Her blindness is disability gain rather than tragedy, since being unsighted led her to learn earthbending from the original teachers, the badgermoles, and to immerse herself in seismic-sense bending full-time. Drawing on Elizabeth Barnes and Miranda Fricker's hermeneutical injustice, the chapter claims disability pride gives disabled viewers permission to celebrate themselves, and shows Toph driving the plot (inventing metalbending, training Aang in 'Bitter Work') instead of teaching non-disabled characters a moral lesson.

disability-philosophy.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
disability-philosophy.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
disability-philosophy.relation: Argues that Toph Beifong is not the harmful 'Supercrip' stereotype (an exceptional individual who overcomes disability through talent and grit, which blames ordinary disabled people for their disadvantage) but a 'Proud Disabled Person' counterstory. Her blindness is a disability gain: it led her to learn earthbending from the badgermoles, the original earthbenders, and to live immersed in bending as her constant way of navigating the world, deepening her mastery. Using Hilde Lindemann's master narratives and counterstories and Elizabeth Barnes's mere-difference view, the chapter shows Toph fits neither the 'better off dead' nor the 'irrationally happy' stereotype: she is grumpy, nuanced (adapting her teaching of Aang in 'Bitter Work'), and a central driver of the plot rather than a moral prop. Fricker's hermeneutical injustice explains why disabled viewers struggle to make sense of flourishing with a disability, and why Toph's portrait gives them permission to celebrate it.

disability-philosophy.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
disability-philosophy.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
disability-philosophy.relation: Clifton asks whether fans are moral monsters for laughing at behavior that looks autistic, running Sheldon through the DSM criteria for Asperger's syndrome: missing Penny's sarcasm about doctors who 'remove shoes from asses,' hedging the bath-item Christmas gift, and inflexibly clinging to nonfunctional routines like Saturday-night laundry. Setting the writers' stated intentions aside as one fallible piece of evidence (the intentional-fallacy debate), he weighs the medical model of disability (leveling and normalizing) against the social-constructivist model in which disability is a misfit between trait and environment. Because Sheldon has built a world — theoretical physics, accommodating friends, the comic book store — where his traits are advantages, even an 'alpha nerd' leader, they constitute an 'enability' rather than a disability, and the laughter is morally innocent.

disability-philosophy.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
disability-philosophy.title: Would You Kindly Evolve Today
disability-philosophy.relation: Ledder reads Plasmids and ADAM as human enhancement technology and stages the real bioethics debate: therapy versus enhancement, transhumanist enthusiasm (whole-brain emulation like Eleanor's ADAM-collecting, Sandberg's morphological freedom) against fears of Splicer-like superhumans and eugenics. The Rapture arms race, where your Electric Bolt Plasmid goes obsolete and forces further splicing, dramatizes the coercive spiral of competitive enhancement, while Habermas's objection that genetically designing children turns them into projections grounds the reading of Jack, Fontaine's purchased and conditioned embryo triggered by 'would you kindly', as a metaphor for engineered autonomy destroyed.
