The chapter closes with disability critiques: maybe the problem is not the body but the social barriers that 'disable' it, so changing society might beat changing flesh.

disability-philosophy.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
disability-philosophy.title: What We Have Learned, or “Always Let Your Conscience Be Your Guide!”
disability-philosophy.relation: Traces Disney disability from the medical model — Dopey as permanent childlike recipient of care, Gus-Gus, and LeFou, echoing Locke's claim that 'lunatics and idiots are never set free from the government of their parents' and Mill's restriction of liberty to those who can care for themselves — to the social model of disability in Finding Dory, where Charlie and Jenny's seashell trail makes the ocean an accommodating rather than disabling environment. Foucault's Birth of the Clinic explains how Gaston uses the asylum to control Maurice, medicine as power over lives. The chapter concludes that Pixar's Big Blue World embodies relational autonomy — Dory thriving 'in your own amazing Dory way' through supported interdependence — while nonverbal sidekicks Becky and Gerald show Dopey's disempowered comic-relief legacy survives.

disability-philosophy.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
disability-philosophy.title: 7. Disabled at Downton
disability-philosophy.relation: Richmond argues that Downton's portrayal of disability is morally mixed. Bates is a positive, realistic representation: hired despite O'Brien and Thomas's ableism, rejecting the painful leg brace, loved by and married to Anna in defiance of period stereotypes, and deliberately not a 'super-crip' whose disability is erased by technology or triumph. Matthew's arc, by contrast, is harmful: he pushes away Lavinia and Mary ('Think of me as dead') and is then rescued by the miracle cure of Dr. Clarkson's misdiagnosis, a plot the chapter, drawing on Paul Longmore's disability-studies mandate and the medical versus social models of disability, says teaches disabled viewers their lives need medical erasure to matter, prompting the plea for 'more Bateses and fewer Matthews.'

disability-philosophy.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
disability-philosophy.title: Notes
disability-philosophy.relation: The Funkes apply Clark and Chalmers's extended mind hypothesis to the Pip-Boy, arguing it meets all three criteria for cognitive extension - availability (worn at all times), reliability (trusted rad and health monitoring), and active cognitive engagement (V.A.T.S. offloads targeting calculations) - so it is part of the Sole Survivor's and Courier's minds, as in 'The Glowing Sea' and the search for Virgil's cure. Donna Haraway's cyborg frames this human-machine hybridity alongside cyberdogs and Kellogg, but Fallout inverts her liberationist vision: the Pip-Boy is a survival lifeline forced by the wasteland, not an emancipatory choice, making the cyborg a dystopian necessity. Comparing the Pip-Boy with cochlear implants, prosthetics, and brain-computer interfaces, and the Old World Blues Think Tank with a dehumanizing bio-tech extreme, the chapter uses Alison Kafer's feminist crip critique to insist real augmentation carries pain, stigma, and unequal access the game's frictionless fiction erases, closing on a cautious transhumanist note.

disability-philosophy.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
disability-philosophy.title: Notes
disability-philosophy.relation: Di Summa reads Jenny Beavan's costume design as philosophy of technology: Immortan Joe's oxygen-fed carapace and the chrome-spraying War Boys visualize Heidegger's warning that technology converts nature and bodies into resources, while Max's blood-drip tether to Nux literalizes our co-dependence on machines — and on each other's flesh and blood. Through Rosemarie Garland-Thomson's staring, Sherri Irvin's body aesthetics, and Tobin Siebers's disability aesthetics, Furiosa's uncovered stump becomes an act of aesthetic exploration that defeats ableism: in this film, disability is a thing for heroes, and vulnerability is itself a human strength.

disability-philosophy.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
disability-philosophy.title: NOTES
disability-philosophy.relation: Craton reads Sookie's arc through disability theory: her telepathy, treated by Bon Temps as a disability that barred her from college and respect, is reframed once vampires and Weres prize it — and finally her faerie 'light' — into an ability she controls for money, crime-solving, and saving a child. The chapter parallels the eugenics-era fears Sookie and Alcide share about passing on difference, and the freak-show histories of Joseph Merrick, Saartjie Baartman, and Julia Pastrana illuminate how vampires like Eric and Sophie-Anne value Sookie's blood as a possession to be consumed rather than a person to be respected, until she rescinds Bill's invitation and defends her light.

disability-philosophy.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
disability-philosophy.title: They Took My Choice, So I Took Yours
disability-philosophy.relation: Tongue argues Yennefer's 'they took my choice' grievance is best understood through reproductive justice: her sterilization by the enchanter, strapped down and told the price only at the last moment, mirrors real coerced sterilizations of disabled, Roma, and Indigenous women, so her 'choice' was coerced by ableist and anti-elven oppression. She contrasts Geralt, whose witcher infertility is unstigmatized and whose adoptive fatherhood of Ciri bucks gendered caregiver stereotypes ('biology is not destiny, adoption is'), with Yennefer's portrayal, which slides into the patriarchal 'infertile monster' trope shared by Daenerys Tragaryen and Wanda Maximoff. The chapter concludes the show handles infertility and nonbiological family admirably but still reinforces maternal-sacrifice and cure-the-disability stereotypes.

disability-philosophy.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
disability-philosophy.title: XIII - THE MUTANT CURE OR SOCIAL CHANGE DEBATING DISABILITY
disability-philosophy.relation: Ilea uses The Last Stand's mutant cure to stage the debate over disability. Worthington's 'affliction... a disease' speech is the medical model; Storm's 'there's nothing to cure' is the social model, on which society, not the body, disables, as with Deaf culture and communities without eyeglasses. Rogue, who cannot touch anyone, and Jean, whose power she cannot control, show some mutations genuinely impair, so the chapter weighs beneficence, nonmaleficence, and utility across Angel's aborted cure, cochlear implants, prenatal Down syndrome screening, and the history of eugenics from Nazi euthanasia to American sterilization laws, concluding the cure can be both liberation and weapon.

subjective-truth.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
subjective-truth.title: Dandelions on My Cloud
subjective-truth.relation: Uses 'Dandelion'—truth as a bright yellow flower that blows away—to mark the withering of Enlightenment confidence in plain, visible truth under deconstruction. Kierkegaard's 'truth is subjectivity' explains why truth on 'Get Off of My Cloud' cannot be shared directly ('Don't hang around 'cause two's a crowd'), and Nietzsche goes further: there is no truth to find, only wills to power making truths—'you can't always get what you want... you just might find you get what you need.'

subjective-truth.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
subjective-truth.title: Futurama and Philosophy
subjective-truth.relation: Hamer tests sanity against truth using Kierkegaard's asylum anecdote - the escapee intoning 'Boom, the earth is round' proves his insanity precisely by resting it on objective fact - and applies it to 'Insane in the Mainframe,' where Fry, wrongly committed to a robot asylum, is only released once he subjectively believes he is a robot, and to 'The Sting,' where comatose Leela's plan to keep Fry's corpse under her mattress to 'prove I'm not insane' fails the same traitorous way. Pure objectivity cannot certify sanity and pure subjectivity licenses lunacy, so the chapter brings in James's 'The Will to Believe': some beliefs must be held first before their evidence can even count. Fry, who abandons his robot belief the moment his knife-nick bleeds human blood, models the justified believer who pursues the objective truth subjectively.

subjective-truth.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
subjective-truth.title: Dracula and Philosophy
subjective-truth.relation: Pramik maps Kierkegaard's three stages from Either/Or and Stages on Life's Way onto the novel: Dracula lives the aesthetic stage of pleasure and possessive power (imprisoning Harker in the castle, refusing to let the brides feed on him), Harker the anxious ethical stage of moral rules and guilt, and Van Helsing the religious stage of faith 'by virtue of the absurd' - trusting God to do the impossible through crucifixes, garlic, and the beheading of Lucy. Against Seward's doubting questions about these absurd tactics, she argues that Van Helsing's renewed, tested faith proves itself and makes him the book's real hero, since neither pleasure nor ethics alone defeats Dracula or gives life meaning.

subjective-truth.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
subjective-truth.title: 19. Thanos Is No Abraham
subjective-truth.relation: Uses Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling to compare Thanos's killing of Gamora on Mount Vormir with Abraham's binding of Isaac, laying out the aesthetic, ethical, and religious stages. It argues Thanos initially looks 'religious' — his sacrifice expresses a particular, personal encounter with the absolute balance of all things, neither an aesthetic whim nor an ethical calculation — but that his Endgame slip ('what I'm about to do to your stubborn, annoying little planet… I'm gonna enjoy it. Very, very much') exposes him as a mere aesthete dressing bloodlust in metaphysics. Hence Thanos is no Abraham, and the truly religious type remains a frightening but unrealized possibility.

subjective-truth.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
subjective-truth.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
subjective-truth.relation: Drawing on fieldwork and surveys at the 2011 Tampa Lebowski Fest, Dufort and Lemire-Cadieux use Kierkegaard's Concept of Irony and indirect communication — contrasted with Plato's condemnation of mimesis in the cave and Aristotle's rehabiliation of it — to explain why Achievers who dress as rugs, memorize lines, and re-watch the film dozens of times find no objective message to decode. Kierkegaardian irony leaves each receiver to dig out a subjective existential truth through self-reflection and repetition, so that fans repeating the Dude's message become part of the irony itself: being an 'Achiever' achieves nothing objective and something deeply personal ('don't pee on other people's rugs').

subjective-truth.book: 183 - Metallica and Philosophy - A Crash Course in Brain Surgery
subjective-truth.title: The Struggle Within: Hetfield, Kierkegaard, and the Pursuit of Authenticity
subjective-truth.relation: Philip Lindholm reads Metallica through Kierkegaard's demand for subjectivity: the soldier in 'One' crying 'Oh please God help me' exemplifies becoming a single individual before God against the untruth of the crowd, and 'The Struggle Within' stages Either/Or's passionate choice that decides the self. He then shows Hetfield himself living the inauthentic masked life Kierkegaard condemns - 'I was James Hetfield of Metallica' - until rehab forced the honest self-disclosure ('The God That Failed' and 'Until It Sleeps' mourning his parents) that marks a move toward authentic individuality.

subjective-truth.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
subjective-truth.title: The Office and Philosophy
subjective-truth.relation: Lonergan and Wisnewski read 'Grief Counseling' and 'Safety Training' as a case study in death-denial: Michael cannot parse the euphemism 'we lost Ed Truck,' Kelly must teach him to be sad, and Creed's report of the decapitation forces the Heideggerian realization that death is his own not-to-be-outstripped possibility, not just a fact of life. The office deflects with movie plots and euphemism (Jim's 'seriously hurt' about the rooftop stunt), Pam's eulogy for Toby's bird shows how mourning ritual copes with mortality, and Michael's longing to be remembered - hospital wings named after him, saving his own life - exemplifies Kierkegaard's 'world-historical' life as an ego defense, with living subjectively the recommended but unexplained alternative. Becker's thesis that all culture is a fabricated protest against death frames the whole chapter.

subjective-truth.title: Inconclusive Unscientific Postscript Late Remarks on Kierkegaard and Kaufman
subjective-truth.relation: LaRocca pairs Kaufman with Kierkegaard on anxiety as the constitutive human condition—not worry but 'the dizziness of freedom,' the awareness of radical possibility. He argues both use pseudonymity and 'indirect communication' to distance author from work so the audience confronts its own individuality: Kierkegaard's Haufniensis/Climacus, Kaufman's Caden Cotard and the character 'Charlie Kaufman' in Adaptation. The chapter analyzes acting as inhabitation vs. impersonation (Being John Malkovich vs. The Talented Mr. Ripley), the diegesis/mimesis layering (Plato and Aristotle) of Kaufman's doubles and replicas, and repetition/recursion as the Kierkegaardian leap that love, like faith, demands—so 'the end is built into the beginning.'

subjective-truth.title: 31_LaRocca_Chapter_030.html
subjective-truth.relation: Hoffman reads Sarah Polley's Stories We Tell and Joshua Oppenheimer's The Act of Killing through Kierkegaard's account of indirect communication and 'deceiving into the truth.' Like the Socratic maieutic teacher who removes his authority and lets pupils reach their own conclusions, both directors withhold voice-of-God assertion and instead present multiple, conflicting, sometimes ethically monstrous storytellers, indulging their delusions to expose them. Polley stages fake Super-8 home movies and rival accounts of her mother and paternity so that truth becomes subjective appropriation rather than objective fact; Oppenheimer lets Indonesian genocide perpetrators reenact their killings as Hollywood fantasies until Anwar Congo is 'deceived' into his own broken self-awareness, indicting the regime that still celebrates him.

subjective-truth.title: False Tattoos and Failed Totems
subjective-truth.relation: Karen Hoffman reads Memento and Inception through Kierkegaard's Concluding Unscientific Postscript: Leonard's tattoos and Cobb's totems both fail to supply the objective certainty their owners expect, forcing each to confront subjective truth, 'an objective uncertainty held fast through appropriation with the most passionate inwardness.' She argues Leonard fails Kierkegaard's test twice over - he treats his facts-based system as objective knowledge, and his real commitment is to playing detective rather than catching a killer (Teddy: 'You don't want the truth. You make up your own truth'), culminating in the knowingly false tattoo that arranges Teddy's murder. Cobb, by contrast, faces his memories of Mal, accepts objective uncertainty, takes Saito's 'leap of faith,' and in the final scene walks away from the spinning top, choosing the world that reunites him with his children - an idea that sticks because of how he lives it, not because it is objectively true.

subjective-truth.title: Chapter 15 Making the Heart Grow Fonder
subjective-truth.relation: Dueck reads Twain's 'Life on the Mississippi'—where mastering the river as a pilot drains away its beauty, like a doctor who sees a face as a medical case—through Edward Bullough's aesthetic principle of 'psychical distance,' the balance between under-distancing (practical absorption) and over-distancing (cold abstraction) that makes experience aesthetic. He argues knowledge need not kill wonder if we re-establish distance, and that Twain's fiction ('Tom Sawyer,' 'Huckleberry Finn,' 'The Prince and the Pauper,' 'A Connecticut Yankee') itself creates the right distance. He links this to Kierkegaard's 'indirect communication': humor, irony and story convey existential, subjective truth that the reader must 'undo the knot' to grasp, so that distance makes the heart grow fonder and the mind wiser.

political-realism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
political-realism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
political-realism.relation: Si Sheppard grades The Walking Dead's three settlements by political Realism: the Governor's Woodbury - cohesive, feared rather than loved, feeding his people arena spectacle to keep them from turning on him - beats Rick's West Central Prison, which never becomes a state at all. Rick lets Tyreese's vigilante murder pass, ruling as a first-among-equals with no institutions, no constitution, and no monopoly of legitimate force in Weber's sense, then covertly guns down Thomas and Dexter while hiding behind his cop credibility - 'it's me or you' reasoning indistinguishable from Shane's. Realism cares about power, not morality, so Rick's flaw is not cruelty but the absence of institution-building: he was never a bad father, just a bad founding father, who only becomes a Realist after Alexandria falls.

political-realism.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
political-realism.title: Easing Back on the APC’s Throttle
political-realism.relation: Treats Engineers, Xenomorphs, and humans as states and reads the APC debate through Thucydides' Melian dialogue ('the strong do what they will') and the jus in bello criteria of discrimination, military necessity, and proportionality. It concludes that Ripley's 'nuke the site from orbit' and Vasquez's nerve gas are vengeance masquerading as realism - the Xeno threat is no longer imminent, so Walzer's 'supreme emergency' is unavailable - while Hudson's withdrawal (even Burke's species-preservation plea) fits both realism and just war restraint; the Ben Tre 'we destroyed the town to save it' fiasco in Vietnam is the cautionary parallel.

political-realism.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
political-realism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
political-realism.relation: Si Sheppard reads the comic through Realist state-formation theory: Shane's leadership rests on borrowed prestige and dies with him, West Central Prison collapses into anarchy because Rick never establishes a monopoly on legitimate force—letting Tyreese's vigilante murder pass—nor any institution beyond his personal authority, while the Governor's Woodbury thrives on fear, arenas, and bread-and-circuses. Citing Machiavelli's prince who is feared rather than loved, Weber's definition of the state, and Bismarck's unifying wars, he argues the prison loses the 'second anarchy' rivalry with Woodbury for want of scouting, sabotage, coalition-building, or any command structure that survives Rick's absences. Rick's confession that he would kill everyone in the Alexandria Safe Zone to keep Lori safe is post-moral Realism, yet he was 'a bad founding father' who only finally learns to build an army instead of relying on himself.

political-realism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
political-realism.title: Stolen Mutagens
political-realism.relation: Van der Zee uses Schmitt's concept of 'the political' - the friend/enemy distinction whose utmost intensity is the possibility of war - to explain why Geralt's witcher neutrality keeps failing, from the choice over the Scoia'tael taking Haren Brogg's goods in the game's Outskirts to the Salamandra theft of the mutagens from Kaer Morhen. Schmitt's claim that a group unwilling to defend its way of existence must surrender its fate to those who will fight explains why the witchers' pursuit of the stolen mutagens drags Geralt into Temerian politics and the Order of the Flaming Rose's schemes. The chapter's sharpest point is that 'monster' names the dangerous complement of Schmitt's 'humanity': witcher neutrality is only sustainable in a world where enemies remain respected enemies, not monsters to be exterminated, which is why Geralt refuses Commander Wenck's request to hunt Scoia'tael as 'evil creatures.'

political-realism.title: “They Turned to a Man They Didn’t Fully Understand”
political-realism.relation: Foy and Dale argue that the Dark Knight trilogy endorses a conservative critique of liberal democracy: Batman taps every citizen's phone, tortures criminals, and kidnaps Lau from Hong Kong because Gotham's institutions cannot cope with a permanent state of crisis. Hume's conservatism—authority resting on habit and order rather than abstract rights and consent—explains Batman's defense of the existing order against Ra's al Ghul's razing of Gotham, while Schmitt's sovereign who declares the 'state of exception' frames Batman as the extra-legal protector who suspends rights during crisis (with Rachel's Caesar warning marking the danger). Against Locke's natural rights and Rawls's inviolability of the person, the Joker and Bane dramatize Strauss's twin fears that liberalism degenerates into nihilistic value-chaos or coercive revolutionary equality, and Burke's natural aristocracy of 'virtual representation' justifies relying on an unchosen elite hero. The trilogy's central puzzle is Batman's illiberal means—taking the blame for Dent's death to preserve the White Knight myth—dirtying his hands so that Gotham's official powers stay clean.

personhood.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
personhood.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
personhood.relation: Allaire argues walkers have no moral value and can be killed without remorse: a Bentham-style act-utilitarian tally favors killing any walker, and, following Kant, genetic humanity is neither necessary nor sufficient for membership in the moral community. Applying Mary Anne Warren's five personhood criteria, he shows walkers lack pain response (Hannah's severed half still dragging itself at Rick), language, planning (Glenn's gun-bag mission versus aimless shuffling), and self-reflection, so as beings incapable of duty they can have no rights. Morgan's inability to shoot his walker-wife and Rick's 'I'm sorry this happened to you' illustrate Kant's 'duality of the human situation' — we irrationally project personhood onto former people — and our hesitation is precisely the walkers' greatest advantage.

personhood.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
personhood.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
personhood.relation: Munkittrick argues that because personhood cannot be defined (trait lists like 'long-term planning' are circular) and behavior cannot prove an inner mind—as Searle's Chinese Room thought experiment shows—people have always identified persons intuitively, and Pixar trained Millennials to do exactly that. He reads the Pixar canon in three stages: Toy Story's self-aware Buzz as nascent non-human personhood, the Human-as-Partner films (Ratatouille's Remy and Linguini, WALL-E and EVE, Monsters, Inc.'s Sully and Boo, Up's Carl and Dug) as mutual recognition of persons across species lines, and The Incredibles as showing that even enhanced 'super-humans' face otherization—so a generation primed by these films will accept AI, animals, and uplifted beings as bearers of rights.

personhood.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
personhood.title: He Thinks He's People: How Brian Made Personhood for the Dogs
personhood.relation: Argues that Brian the dog is a person because personhood, on a Kantian reading, requires a rational nature rather than species membership: Peter making Brian beg in 'Brian: Portrait of a Dog,' the councilman's 'Why are we listening to a dog?', and Chris's 'You don't have a soul!' in 'North by North Quahog' all wrongly treat humanity (or a soul) as the criterion, while Descartes' mechanical account of animal bodies is invoked to show the soul cannot be empirically tested. The chapter then applies the humanity-formulation of the categorical imperative both ways: Stewie framing the maid in 'Road to Rhode Island' shows treating persons as mere means, while Brian's Christmas-sweater lie to Lois shows how Kantian duty is stricter than the Golden Rule. Finally it grades Brian's own conduct as family conscience and drunk (his lapses like framing Jake Tucker, his condescension to Peter, his disrespected self in 'The Thin White Line'), concluding Brian owes the same duties he is owed.

personhood.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
personhood.title: Is Brian More of a Person than Peter? (scan merges: Of Wills, Wantons, and Wives)
personhood.relation: Uses Frankfurt's distinction between first-order desires, second-order desires, and the wanton to argue Brian is more of a person than Peter: Brian's therapy-driven realization in 'Brian in Love' that he does not want to want Lois is a genuine second-order desire, while Peter's TV fixation in 'I Never Met the Dead Man' (wearing a cardboard TV frame, swapping TV for family without reflection) leaves him a wanton, and Cleveland and even Quagmire scrape into personhood. The chapter then turns to weakness of will from Aristotle's akrasia onward, bringing in Searle's claim in Rationality in Action that choice happens in uncaused 'gaps' between desire and action, so acting against one's better judgment can evidence rather than defeat rationality, with R. Jay Wallace's willpower-based volitionism rounding out the action theory.

personhood.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
personhood.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
personhood.relation: Matthew Tedesco reads Bran's coma and Drogo's living death as biomedical ethics: Jaime's 'good clean death' for Bran raises active versus passive euthanasia, and with James Rachels he argues the AMA's killing/letting-die distinction merely licenses more suffering, while Brock recasts withdrawal of treatment as intentional killing anyway. The Bran case frames end-of-life decisions for children - the Johns Hopkins and Baby John Pearson cases - and whether parents may weigh a handicap's burden on the family, a question made vivid by Bran riding Hodor. Dany's smothering of Drogo, by contrast, does not strike readers as murder because personhood rather than biological humanity carries moral standing: on Tooley's self-consciousness, Warren's five criteria, or Marquis's future-like-ours, Drogo is human but no longer a person - which leads straight to Peter Singer's claim that killing a disabled infant who is not a person may not be wrong at all, leaving us to ask whether our recoil is reason or taboo.

personhood.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
personhood.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
personhood.relation: Jason Eberl treats the muttations, jabberjays that mimic speech without understanding, tracker jackers, the wolf-mutts with Glimmer's eyes that torment Cato, and the lizard-mutts hissing Katniss's name, alongside real chimeras (geeps, the SCID-hu mouse, Balaban's quail-chick brain transplants, Weissman's human-neural mouse) to ask whether biotechnology could create a person. Working through Boethius's definition of a person as an 'individual substance of a rational nature' and Locke's 'thinking intelligent Being' that can consider itself the same over time, he argues that human DNA alone confers no personhood, while a chimera genuinely capable of self-conscious rational thought would be a person whose weaponized creation and lab captivity would violate its rights, which is why ethicists allow mouse chimeras but hesitate with primates. He notes that the Gamemakers' refusal to see tributes as persons is exactly the move that made slavery and Nazi dehumanization possible, and that Katniss's suspicion about whether the mutts remember their deaths is the right ethical question to keep open.

personhood.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
personhood.title: Origin and Desires as Monster Makers in the Witcher
personhood.relation: Swanstrom and Lyle test medieval theories of monstrosity against the show: Stregobor's Curse of the Black Sun echoes Aristotle's, Avicenna's, and Aquinas's celestial-influence explanations of fetal mutation (though even they would not convict Renfri by birthday alone), while Yennefer's spine and infertility invoke Aquinas on failed generation and women as 'deformed males,' with witchers cast as Aquinas's mules - an engineered, infertile natural kind. They argue that neither origin nor appearance but motivation and virtue make a monster: Renfri's revenge, Nivellen's rape of the priestess, and Stregobor's vivisection of girls are Aristotelian 'bestial' habit and vicious character, not mean-relative virtue. Geralt's shifting telos, from monster-slayer protecting humans to protector of Ciri (knighted by Queen Meve), shows even a mutant can develop virtue, so mutations, heritage, and gender cannot be what monstrosity is.

personhood.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
personhood.title: VIII - MUTANT RIGHTS, TORTURE, AND X-PERIMENTATION
personhood.relation: McWilliams asks whether mutants have 'human' rights, arguing that rights track reasoning ability, sentience, and autonomy rather than species membership: the Down syndrome comparison shows the X-gene itself justifies nothing, and her alien-landing thought experiment, echoing Singer on speciesism, shows peaceful aliens, and therefore mutants, belong in the class of 'everyone.' Because mutants can look human yet wield omega-level power, she grants they may owe greater duties not to harm, but Wolverine's nonconsensual adamantium grafting and The Last Stand's weaponizable 'cure' remain rights violations. The chapter ends on the cliffhanger of when, if ever, consequentialist benefits may override the rights not to be tortured or experimented on.

anti-natalism.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
anti-natalism.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
anti-natalism.relation: Moosa uses the apocalypse as a moral laboratory: since 'murder' is by definition wrongful killing, Carl's shooting of Shane must be judged by his reasoning (saving his father), and Hobbes's state of nature — 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' — fits Kirkman's world, yet the survivors import morality into it, as when parents mercy-kill their children just as one would turn up a dying child's morphine. Taking up Camus's claim that suicide is the one truly serious philosophical problem, he argues our world is nearly as bad as the zombie landscape, so consistency commits comfortable readers to the same duty of aid (helping sufferers rather than opting out) that justifies the survivors' fighting on. Finally he argues procreation is the worst thing survivors can do — nonexistent children cannot suffer, so Lori's pregnancy and Glenn and Maggie's crib plans are immoral, and adopting existing children as Andrea and Dale did is the consistent course, an obligation that transfers to our world right now.

anti-natalism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
anti-natalism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
anti-natalism.relation: Joe Slater builds a two-premise anti-natalist argument from Shelley's Paradise Lost epigraph ('Did I request thee, Maker, from my clay / To mould me man?'): since it is wrong to inflict harm on an autonomous being without consent, and every autonomous life inevitably contains harms, creating autonomous beings - Adam in the lab or a baby in the womb - is wrong. He answers the objection from Parfit's non-identity problem via the damaged-brain Adam case, and defends the Harm Premise with Mill's On Liberty: consent matters because autonomous agents must be free to harm themselves, as with the smoker, the drinker, and Frankenstein's stolen kidney. G.E. Moore's 'Moorean shift' and Benatar's genetic, social, and institutional pro-natal biases explain why we resist the conclusion, with a 'Super Adam' incapable of harm as the only escape.

anti-natalism.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
anti-natalism.title: Notes
anti-natalism.relation: Reconstructs Rust's scattered remarks — the world as 'one giant gutter,' procreation as the hubris of yanking a soul out of nonexistence into the thresher — into an explicit anti-natalist argument, testing each premise and conceding procreation is selfish while questioning whether every life nets more harm than good. It presents David Benatar's asymmetry between the absence of pain (always good) and the absence of pleasure (bad only for someone deprived), illustrating it with the show: contraception as procreative duty, the wrongness of conceiving in Tuttle's Louisiana, and the emptiness of Childress' temple as a good in itself. The chapter concludes that Rust's 'opt out of a raw deal' is philosophically defensible, with Schopenhauer's desire-pendulum and Hobbes' 'nasty, brutish, and short' backing the claim that most lives are bad.

imaginative-resistance.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
imaginative-resistance.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
imaginative-resistance.relation: Dadlez recounts playing an evil Romulan spy who befriended the Enterprise crew, blew up the ship, and got shunned by her real friends, and asks whether role-playing villains makes players complicit in immoral perspectives. Working from Hume on fiction that describes 'vicious manners' without disapprobation, and the imaginative-resistance debate (Walton, Gendler), she argues the role-player is like an author or improvisational actor who makes it fictional that a character holds wicked views without imaginatively endorsing them—no utilitarian or deontological truth of the game world endorsed her sabotage. Her friends' anger was really at her hijacking a collaborative story into one where the villain wins, and her only residual worry about the 'Orc Holocaust' of experience-point slaughter is that game generalizations about inherently hostile monsters might bleed into real-world prejudice about human groups.

imaginative-resistance.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
imaginative-resistance.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
imaginative-resistance.relation: Dadlez narrates an all-night RPG in which her disguised Romulan spy blew up the Enterprise and got herself shunned by her seminar colleagues, and asks whether role-playing evil makes the player morally complicit. Working through Hume's Standard of Taste claim that we cannot 'enter into' vicious sentiments and the puzzle of imagining morally deviant worlds, she argues the role-player is like an author or improvising actor: generating Waltonian fictional truths about a wicked character requires no first-person endorsement of the character's values, any more than method acting a villain requires sharing his ethics. The other players' real anger is explained not as imagined complicity but as resentment at having their collaborative Star Trek story hijacked into a triumph of the villain, and the 'Orc Holocaust' worry about XP-for-slaughter survives only as a caution that game-licensed 'shoot first' generalizations might bleed into real-world attitudes.

imaginative-resistance.title: Notes
imaginative-resistance.relation: Kajtar asks why viewers root for a double-murdering politician, framing the show through Tamar Gendler's puzzle of imaginative resistance: we would refuse to imagine Zoe's murder narrated as 'brave and noble,' yet House of Cards dissolves that resistance. Using Jenefer Robinson's claim that emotional engagement is necessary for understanding, the chapter shows how the Greenville first-pitch embarrassment, the Fort Sumter swim confession, and above all Frank's fourth-wall asides (telling us the real Gaffney eulogy, admitting 'I despise children') grant voyeuristic intimacy that humanizes him bite by bite - 'that's how you devour a whale.' By the time Frank frames Lucas Goodwin and Corrigan dies, we have adopted the morally deviant perspective, and the chapter warns this is exactly how politicians and artists seduce audiences into values we would otherwise reject.

imaginative-resistance.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
imaginative-resistance.title: Notes
imaginative-resistance.relation: Takes up the puzzle of imaginative resistance (Gendler): while viewers would refuse to imagine that Frank's murder of Zoe was 'brave and noble', we end up rooting for his double murder and abuses of power. It explains this lack of resistance through the Greenville first-pitch confession, Frank's fourth-wall asides that grant us secret intimacy ('I despise children'), and Robinson's account of emotion-driven understanding-an engineered emotional seduction that doubles as a lesson in how politicians and artists manipulate audiences into morally deviant points of view.

art-horror.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
art-horror.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
art-horror.relation: Cogburn and Hebert sort fantasy magic into formulaic natural magic (wizards as scientists exploiting a world's universal laws, in Kant's sense of nature—Salvatore's Cadderly, Snape's potions, Eberron's Artificer), sublimate natural magic (shamans, sorcerers, and warlocks surrendering to forces, as in African diaspora possession religions), and unnatural magic that violates a world's laws, whose horror Sartre's Nausea passage about flesh rebelling captures. Using Lovecraft's indescribable monsters and Noël Carroll's theory of art-horror as categorical impurity (with Mary Douglas on Leviticus-style purity codes), they argue Fourth Edition's algorithmic spell rules make casting feel like chemistry homework rather than the impossible, so unnatural magic cannot be modeled ludologically. Dungeon Masters must instead express the inexpressible through narrative techniques—character reaction, reader-relative impossibility, and limit impossibility—since D&D at its best is shared storytelling, not rule fetishism.

art-horror.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
art-horror.title: 4. The Slimy, Macabre, and Horrific in Stranger Things
art-horror.relation: Nisley applies Noel Carroll's account of art-horror to the Demogorgon: categorically transgressive, interdimensional monsters provoke thought-based fear and disgust (the shed goop, the hazmat suits, Barb's blood in the pool), and it is precisely this disgust that makes our curiosity about the monster's origin and disclosure pleasurable. She traces Nancy's investigation from Jonathan's photograph to the bear trap, brings in Plato's Leontius story from the Republic and Kieran and Feagin on the grotesque to explain why we paradoxically delight in Barb's slime-covered corpse and Will coughing up a slug, and concludes that revulsion amplifies the fascination that keeps us watching.

art-horror.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
art-horror.title: The Melding
art-horror.relation: Extends Noel Carroll's art-horror theory from fusion-figure monsters to 'art-horror environments': the series' distinctive disgust comes not only from the Xenomorph's impure fusion of species traits but from the accidental contamination of clean human spaces - acid blood tunneling deck by deck through the Nostromo, hive webbing repurposing Hadley's Hope as a nursery ('kill me'), and Ripley absorbed into the Queen's fleshy mass at the end of Resurrection. These are accidents that could have been avoided and that break horror's normal movement from disruption back to restored order, since contaminated ships and colonies can only be nuked, never redeemed.

art-horror.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
art-horror.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
art-horror.relation: Cogburn and Hebert ask how fantasy can stage magic that is by definition indescribable, from Lovecraft's unknowable mirror-monster in 'The Outsider' to Priest's limit-of-thought paradoxes. They sort magic into formulaic natural magic — mage-scientists exploiting a world's universal laws, exactly Kant's conception of nature, as in Snape's potions or Mieville's steampunk — and sublimate natural magic, where the practitioner surrenders to forces as in Candomblé possession or Robin Hobb's possessed soldier, against genuinely unnatural magic that violates law itself, as in Bakker's Prince of Nothing or the reality-liquefying passage from Sartre's Nausea. Carroll's theory of art-horror (via Mary Douglas: impurity as categorical incompatibility and incompleteness, from Leviticus's shellfish to The Dunwich Horror's fusions, fissions, and formlessness) explains how writers express the inexpressible, and exposes why 4e's algorithmic spell rules — the Fireball math every player masters 'like a chemistry student' — naturalize magic and kill the horror, leaving Dungeon Masters only narrative techniques (character reaction, reader-relative impossibility, limit impossibility) rather than rules.

intersectionality.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
intersectionality.title: The Wire and Philosophy
intersectionality.relation: Curry refuses to celebrate The Wire, arguing that Simon's class-based realism ('more about class than race') misrepresents Black urban life, and he contrasts it with Black film from New Jack City to Menace II Society where these issues were already explored. Reading scenes like Rawls's 'project nigger' murders no one cares about, Bunk shrugging at Stringer's unsolved killing, and McNulty telling Brianna that nobody will look into D'Angelo's death, he argues the show registers an indifference specific to Black life, not to the poor as such. Drawing on W.E.B. Du Bois's account of colonialism and the slave trade as the genesis of modern capital ('capital noir') and rejecting the intersectional race-class-gender frame as a 'discursive distraction', he demands a racial realism in Derrick Bell's sense: racism is permanent, the underclass is really an racialized undercaste, and the War on Drugs continues Jim Crow by other means.

intersectionality.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
intersectionality.title: Justified and Philosophy
intersectionality.relation: The chapter surveys Harlan's gendered violence - Ava's killing of Bowman, the routine roughing-up of Audrey's working girls, Robert Quarles's childhood prostitution - and uses Catharine MacKinnon's account of patriarchal power imbalance to explain victim-blaming, underreporting, and police disbelief of trauma responses in domestic-violence and rape cases. On prostitution it weighs sex-positive feminism against the objectification worry, concluding via Teri's line about 'sucking hillbilly dicks for money' that Audrey's women have little real choice even under Ava's management. Finally it brings in bell hooks's third-wave point that oppression cannot be split from race and class, plus Peggy McIntosh's invisible backpack of white privilege, to read Noble's Holler's isolation and the bombed black church as evidence that patriarchy in Justified is always also racial and economic.

intersectionality.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
intersectionality.title: 21. If You’re Not White, You’re Missing Out
intersectionality.relation: Treats Louis as a 'comedic philosopher of race' whose time-machine, 'white people problems,' and 'if you're white and you don't admit that it's great, then you are an asshole' bits teach identity privilege as unearned, systemic advantage. It credits him with an intersectional grasp of white-plus-male benefit, contrasts his 'but for now, Weeeeeee!' complicity over smartphone suffering with Barbara Applebaum's argument that the privileged cannot simply opt out and should mobilize against systems rather than police individual guilt, and concludes his job is descriptive: showing us privilege and leaving the remedy to us.

intersectionality.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
intersectionality.title: 13. Sisterhood’s Back in Orphan Black
intersectionality.relation: Recounts the rise and fall of second-wave sisterhood — the dream of a unified female voice that erased differences of race, class, sexuality, and nation until the 1980s backlash killed it — and argues Orphan Black resurrects a corrected version through Rosi Braidotti's posthumanism. The clones, disposable bodies of biogenetic capitalism, build a sisterhood that celebrates difference (grunge Sarah, dreads-and-lab-coat Cosima, suburban Alison, savage Helena) rather than enforcing sameness, and that welcomes the Others the Seventies excluded — gay Felix, Black Art, Hindu Raj — while white Western men like Paul remain the surveillance agents of the backlash. Through posthumanism's dissolution of fixed human identity, the chapter claims, feminism's old ideal returns both transformed and inclusive.

intersectionality.title: 14. Five Stereotypes that Sustain Grape Zones
intersectionality.relation: Explains 'grape', Schumer's grey area between rape and consent, through Miranda Fricker's hermeneutical gaps: bundles of stereotypes about the stranger rapist, the chaste victim, the resisting victim, the racialized 'barbarian rapist', and the unrapeable strong-ass woman leave holes in shared knowledge, so non-stereotypical rapes go unrecognized and unprosecuted. The 'Football Town Nights' players' excuses and the Leather Special's fat-but-brave monologue ridicule these schemas, while Brock Turner's lenient sentence versus Brian Banks's imprisonment shows how intersecting racist and sexist biases protect white rapists and discredit victims. The chapter concludes that debunking the five stereotypes shrinks the grape zones.

intersectionality.title: 16. Raucous Feminist or Racially Insensitive
intersectionality.relation: Weighs Schumer's Peabody-honored 'raucous feminist' image against charges of racial insensitivity by contrasting liberal feminism, exemplified by Friedan's problem that has no name, with intersectionality: hooks's rejoinder that Friedan spoke only for white middle-class women and Crenshaw's multiply-burdened identities. Ware reads the 'Mostly Sex Stuff' jokes about Asian women and third-world bikini waxers, the Beyonce 'Formation' video with Goldie Hawn, and Schumer's dismissive tweets as speaking 'for women' while erasing difference, though the 'Herpes Scare' caricature shows her sometimes winking from inside an intentionally vapid persona. The verdict: Schumer can be both a genuine and an imperfect feminist who must still take accountability.

intersectionality.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
intersectionality.title: 11 Beastly Boys The Racial-Sexual Politics of Meat
intersectionality.relation: Huerter reads M'Baku's 'I'm kidding. We are vegetarians' punchline through Carol Adams's sexual politics of meat and bell hooks's plantation patriarchy: since colonial meat-eating signified masculine mastery over nature (Plumwood's reason/nature dualism) while enslaved people were fed plant foods and cast as edible themselves, audiences primed by the racist cannibal trope expect M'Baku to be a savage, so his refusal of flesh turns the colonizer's gaze back on itself. Killmonger, by contrast, embodies the Black patriarchy produced by the American military-industrial complex ('He's one of ours'), a plantation patriarch whose hypermasculine conquest — killing Linda, burning the Herb garden, his defiant 'death was better than bondage' exit — replays colonial violence even in liberation's name, against which M'Baku's warrior-but-vegetarian politics marks a moral asymmetry.

intersectionality.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
intersectionality.title: Knuckles and the Augustín Gamarra
intersectionality.relation: Deploys Crenshaw's intersectionality to explain why Naomi — the only Belter and only woman aboard the Rocinante — reads as a serial traitor: giving the protomolecule to Fred Johnson out of loyalty to the Belt, leaving Filip to escape Inaros's control of her through motherhood, and siding with Miller after the Dresden shooting ('as a Belter, Miller wasn't wrong'). It scales the analysis up to Belters as a collectively intersectional group — race, class, refugee status, and colonial occupation at once, as with the Weeping Somnambulist fired on carrying 55 refugees and the Ilus colonists framed through the European conquest of the Americas — then walks through Naomi's past with Marco (the Augustín Gamarra bombing that killed 516 people, her suicide attempt, 'the right to walk away') to show that resisting intersecting oppressions forces impossible, betrayal-laden choices, with her chosen family on the Roci as a model of solidarity that crosses identity lines.

intersectionality.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
intersectionality.title: Notes
intersectionality.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

intersectionality.book: 180 - Mad Max and Philosophy - Thinking Through the Wasteland
intersectionality.title: Notes
intersectionality.relation: Pérez and Jackson use Crenshaw's intersectionality to demarginalize Aunty Entity: a Black woman (Tina Turner) in an all-white franchise, she occupies the race-gender intersection invisible both to white feminism and to Black male-centered politics, and her 'Aunty' title and high cage evoke Black women's commodified emotional labor and Angelou's caged bird. Reading her through Moreton-Robinson's white possessive doctrine, hooks's 'white supremacist capitalist patriarchy,' and the Combahee River Collective — and then through hip-hop's Thunderdome trope from 2Pac's 'California Love' to Kendrick Lamar — they argue that Max's white male gaze retroactively makes her a villain, when she is in fact the franchise's most just hero.

intersectionality.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
intersectionality.title: Where in the Hell is Chris Rock
intersectionality.relation: Wisnewski reads SNL's race comedy as applied philosophy of race: the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' sketch shows Mr. Wilson's counter-slurs as an assertion of personhood against Mills's racial contract, Eddie Murphy's Mr. Robinson's Neighborhood and 'White Like Me' expose implicit bias and white privilege, and 'The Day Beyonce Turned Black' illustrates Du Bois's double consciousness. Appiah's racialism explains why Leslie Jones playing Trump strikes audiences as outrageous while white women play men routinely, and Appiah's biological anti-realism about race undercuts that reaction. 'Black Jeopardy' with Tom Hanks's MAGA-hatted Doug finds common ground across race that the 'Lives that Matter' ending sharply limits, Fanon's violence route is raised and set aside, and Crenshaw's intersectionality frames why cast diversity is more than skin-deep.

intersectionality.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
intersectionality.title: I'm Fine with My Spite: The Philosophy of Female Anger in the Work of Taylor Swift
intersectionality.relation: Builds a philosophy of female anger from Aristotle's definition of anger (response to perceived injustice, desire for payback, pleasure in pain), applied to the 2016 Grammy call-out of Kanye and 'Vigilante Shit', and Agnes Callard's problem of eternal anger, which Swift answers in 'I Forgot That You Existed' by moving on without forgiving. Mill's Subjection of Women frames why femininity is constructed as incompatible with anger, and the chapter inventories Swift's 'Glitter Gel Pen Anger' ('Karma', 'Bejeweled') as walking away that renders the wrongdoer beneath contempt. Audre Lorde's 'Uses of Anger' closes the chapter: anger has conative and epistemic value against racist and sexist oppression, which also measures Swift's own limits around race.

intersectionality.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
intersectionality.title: NOTES
intersectionality.relation: Craton and Jonell read Sookie as an emblem of contemporary feminist ambivalence: her 'I am woman, hear me roar' independence coexists with sexual caution, and the show stages feminism's sex wars — Lafayette's sex work and webcam pornography versus Maryann, whose 'pro-sex' liberation collapses into self-annihilating worship of Dionysus and whose death suggests unregulated sexuality is dangerous. Tara's plotline shows how race and class layer onto gender (her 'baby-daddy' scene, Maryann as failed white savior), exposing the limits of a united feminist front, while the 'kept woman' quarrel with Bill and Sookie's barmaid-versus-telepathic-detective career choice leave more questions about female empowerment than answers.

intersectionality.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
intersectionality.title: “A Pamphlet’s Not Going to Cover It”
intersectionality.relation: Kasey Butcher and Megan Peters argue Veronica embodies a third-wave, sex-positive feminism: as jury foreman in 'One Angry Veronica' she refuses the 'Barbie' role the captain of industry assigns her; her over-the-top masquerades (flirting with store clerk Duane Anders, the temptation scenario at Patrick Nevin's door, mimicking Logan's manspreading) expose gender as a performance; and her defense of Carmen Ruiz against Tad's blackmail shows her grasp of how race, class, and gender intersect, per Kimberlé Crenshaw. Against the show's caricature of Lilith House as humorless 'feminist killjoys' picketing the Hearst rapes, they contend Veronica models a feminism that keeps femininity, sexuality, and play — refusing slut shaming while fighting for rape victims, an incest survivor, and blackmailed girls.

intersectionality.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
intersectionality.title: This Is the Version of Myself I Have to Be
intersectionality.relation: Pérez reads Yennefer's arc through a plurality of feminisms rather than one: Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, woman' explains her sacrifice of fertility at Aretuza and later choice of motherhood on her own terms, while Butler's performativity recasts Tissaia's mirror exercises as the enactment of a socially constructed sorceress role. Naomi Wolf's Beauty Myth and Iron Maiden expose her transformation as self-imposed captivity, Ruddick's maternal thinking marks the moment she truly becomes Ciri's mother, and Firestone's call to abolish sex distinction frames her infertility-for-power bargain. Finally Crenshaw's intersectionality and Lorde's 'master's tools' show that Yennefer's quarter-elf passing lets her beat the Brotherhood at its own game without dismantling it.

intersectionality.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
intersectionality.title: Disadvantage, Demeaning, and Discrimination
intersectionality.relation: Loh asks whether Geralt, called 'worse than lepers' at the Inn at the Crossroads, is actually a victim of discrimination or whether the franchise's 'public pedagogy' distorts what discrimination is. Geralt passes Lippert-Rasmussen's test of unjustified worse treatment of socially salient groups ('witcher' and 'stranger'), and statistical generalizations about dangerous strangers fail to treat him as an individual; Hellman's account of demeaning even marks the spitting and stone-throwing as expressing denial of equal moral worth. But demeaning requires a power asymmetry, and Geralt, a superhuman with higher status whom the villagers depend on against monsters, holds all the power, so the mistreatment is unjust without being discrimination, a caution the chapter extends to superhero narratives like the X-Men.

intersectionality.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
intersectionality.title: 71. Dave Chappelle as Philosopher Standing Up to Racism
intersectionality.relation: Benko and Burch treat Chappelle as a philosopher of race whose comedy of incongruity exposes the contradictions of American racism, reading his 'every Black American is bi-lingual' remark and sketches like 'Clayton Bigsby' and 'The Racial Draft' through Du Bois's double consciousness. They argue Chappelle's ethics of fairness, choice and personal responsibility unintentionally echoes Bonilla-Silva's 'color-blind racism,' and use bell hooks's Ain't I a Woman to show how his gendered 'Oppression Olympics' and use of 'bitch' reproduce the sexism hooks says Black men absorb, so his trans and gender jokes rank Black men as the most oppressed group. The chapter's core apparatus (incongruity/schema theory of humor, color-blind racism) sits outside the taxonomy.

intersectionality.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
intersectionality.title: 90. From Hell as Philosophy Ripping Through Structural Violence
intersectionality.relation: James and Mona Rocha argue that Moore and Campbell's From Hell links physical and structural violence under patriarchy: William Gull's Ripper murders of Whitechapel sex workers, and his premonition of the dull modern office ('the twentieth century, I have delivered it'), show how sensationalized physical violence pushes routine structural violence into the invisible background where it corrupts men morally (Gull and Abberline both lose their humanity). Using Galtung's structural violence and Crenshaw's intersectionality of poverty and gender, plus the male gaze in Gull's ghostly viewing of female workers, the chapter connects Victorian misogyny to present-day workplace sexual harassment.

great-chain-of-being.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
great-chain-of-being.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
great-chain-of-being.relation: John Wilkins treats Caesar, who spares the neighbor he has beaten, as a Kantian exemplar whose reason lets him adopt the Categorical Imperative, contrasting him with the rational egoism of the film's human keepers and executives. He argues the film trades on the outdated Great Chain of Being, which Darwinian tree thinking dissolves: with no higher or lower species, only branching homologies, human nature must be continuous with ape nature, and talk of innate species essences must allow for statistical variation and dispositions rather than determination. Caesar's morality also needs more than reason, namely the primate dispositions of deference and empathy scaffolded by his human family, though Buck's instant moral conversion after enhancement shows the film is ambivalent about whether scaffolding alone explains it.

great-chain-of-being.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
great-chain-of-being.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
great-chain-of-being.relation: Kenn Fisher reads the franchise as the extinction of the Great Chain of Being: from Plato's humans mid-way between gods and beasts, through Genesis dominion and Descartes's non-conscious animals, to Malcolm's 'God creates man. Man destroys God. Man creates dinosaurs' - with computers (Hammond's control room, Wikipedia, Google) replacing God at the top. He then tracks animals' ascent from property: Francione on welfare versus personhood, Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', and Singer's equality-as-prescription, applied to Dieter Stark tasering a compy (punished by the compys) versus the unexamined electric fences that keep InGen's 'zoo animals' caged. He closes with Carol Adams's meat-masculinity link - Roland Tembo will hunt only a male T. rex, the dinosaurs are all female - and holds up vegetarian Lex as hope that the Chain bends into a Circle.

great-chain-of-being.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
great-chain-of-being.title: 20. Sympathy for the Existential Devils
great-chain-of-being.relation: James McLachlan reads the films through Sartre: replicants are made like penknives, with an essence before existence, and their drama is going 'off baseline' — the freedom of nothingness by which Batty murders his maker-gods (Tyrell the Father, Chew and Sebastian the trinity) and K disobeys everyone. Sartre's Satan from his Baudelaire biography, Blake's Orc and the Marriage of Heaven and Hell's contraries, and the Great Chain of Being's contradiction between filling one's place and moral freedom frame Luv as a perfect penknife, a 'good angel' who fulfills her vocation, while Batty and K are redeemed by the love that breaks their programming. 'More human than human' turns out to mean: existence precedes essence.

great-chain-of-being.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
great-chain-of-being.title: Equal Opportunity—for Deities
great-chain-of-being.relation: Barkman argues the Marvel Universe's 'One-Above-All'—depicted as Stan Lee and Jack Kirby—is the eternal Judeo-Christian Creator, and arranges its beings in a graded hierarchy: the Living Tribunal as God's judge, cosmic beings like Eternity and Galactus, elders, sky fathers Odin and Zeus, down to mortals, with only God eternal and everything else, gods included, able to die yet enduring by His decree. Ontological rank guarantees nothing morally—Mephisto, the Goddess, and Hera are powerful and wicked, and even Hercules can be beaten by the Wrecking Crew. A free-will theodicy answers where evil came from: 'no other gods before me' never denied other gods' existence but commands loving the Good above all, which mortal Avengers like Thor, loving justice perfected by sacrificial love, manage as well as any deity.

great-chain-of-being.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
great-chain-of-being.title: Between Two Camps in the Witcher
great-chain-of-being.relation: Kammerer reads the Witcherverse's magic through the fault line between 'big tent' Platonism (top-down causation from a source, a great chain of being of nested celestial spheres) and modern naturalism (bottom-up mechanism). The Season of Storms exchange in which Geralt tells Dandelion that meteoric swords gather power descending through elemental planes - without denying those planes exist - shows Sapkowski keeping both worldviews alive, while Novigrad's Eternal Fire pogrom in The Witcher 3 mirrors fourth-century Alexandria's wars over magic and Christianity. Heidegger's 'metaphysics grounds an age' and his critique of enframing nature as standing-reserve frame Yennefer's instrumental view of magic and her djinn-summoning in The Last Wish, and Plotinus's Enneads supplies the vision of true magic as internal to a cosmic emanation rather than a mere technology.

epistemic-injustice.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
epistemic-injustice.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.relation: Jason Davis opens with Sammy Davis Jr. thanking the white producers for the best film ever made on black-white relations, and their cluelessness, to show that white privilege rests on an epistemology of ignorance, paralleled by the human enjoyment of ape slavery in Conquest. He reads the ape castes through the ontology of race: the films first stage race as biological realism and essentialism (warrior gorillas, chimpanzee scientists, orangutan priests), but Battle for the Planet of the Apes shows biology is not destiny, and human genetics (race accounts for about 0.012 percent of human variation) discredits biological racial realism altogether. Via Charles Mills's social ontology of race and Kwame Anthony Appiah's racial skepticism, the chapter treats ape racism as a mirror of anti-miscegenation-era America whose racial categories are social constructs, down to the dropped ape-human hybrid child.

epistemic-injustice.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
epistemic-injustice.title: Psych and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.relation: Mona Rocha asks whether Psych is sexist given Shawn's eighth-grade-girl caricature of Juliet in 'Spellingg Bee' and the secret knowledge kept from the show's women, then argues it is not: the women's inferior epistemic position is a byproduct of the con, not misogynist gatekeeping, because Shawn works collaboratively and non-hierarchically, shares credit (solving Lassiter's Back Bay Killer case for him in 'From the Earth to Starbucks'), gives the Chief the glory in 'There Might Be Blood,' and confronts the oilrig chauvinist outright. The contrast is The Mentalist, where Patrick Jane's withholding of deductions from Lisbon - going behind her back in 'Red Hair and Silver Tape' and getting evidence thrown out in 'Blood Money' - enacts patriarchal paternalism that undermines female leadership.

epistemic-injustice.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
epistemic-injustice.title: 9. Not Knowing Serial Killers with Hannibal Lecktor
epistemic-injustice.relation: Davis reads Manhunter's Lecktor through agnotology - Robert Proctor's study of how ignorance is made - arguing that Lecktor runs a 'knowing game' with Will Graham, strategically withholding what he knows (the Pilgrim's lunar cycle, his fan mail from the Tooth Fairy) so that Graham must do his own dangerous 'field work' and risk becoming killer or bait, a playbook he delivers as an invented Rumsfeldian riff on known knowns and unknown unknowns. The same lens then exposes the real world: the FBI's post-Silence serial-killer panic (Jenkins's evidence that the BSU's statistics were false, capped by the USS Iowa profiling fiasco) as institutional ignorance-making that inflated the FBI's power, and Egger's 'less-dead' - marginalized victims like Kendall Francois's Poughkeepsie sex workers whom media footprints render invisible, 'the missing missing' - as the human cost of our fascination with a killer who never existed.

epistemic-injustice.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
epistemic-injustice.title: 8. Brienne and the Struggle for Recognition
epistemic-injustice.relation: Giladi reads Brienne as a challenge to the Westerosi recognition order: winning the melee at Renly's camp and requesting the Kingsguard, she embodies knightly virtue in a society that deems it naturally male, and the crowd's bewildered, muted applause is a recognition injustice that withholds the social conditions of her self-confidence and authenticity. He analyzes Jaime's mockery in 'The Prince of Winterfell' - sexualizing her as 'boring as you are ugly' where he would never treat Barristan Selmy so - as stripping Brienne of her status as a conversational peer and equal rational enquirer, while the attempted gang-rape by Locke's men in 'Walk of Punishment' shows the violent backlash her struggle for recognition provokes.

epistemic-injustice.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
epistemic-injustice.title: 14. Five Stereotypes that Sustain Grape Zones
epistemic-injustice.relation: Explains 'grape', Schumer's grey area between rape and consent, through Miranda Fricker's hermeneutical gaps: bundles of stereotypes about the stranger rapist, the chaste victim, the resisting victim, the racialized 'barbarian rapist', and the unrapeable strong-ass woman leave holes in shared knowledge, so non-stereotypical rapes go unrecognized and unprosecuted. The 'Football Town Nights' players' excuses and the Leather Special's fat-but-brave monologue ridicule these schemas, while Brock Turner's lenient sentence versus Brian Banks's imprisonment shows how intersecting racist and sexist biases protect white rapists and discredit victims. The chapter concludes that debunking the five stereotypes shrinks the grape zones.

epistemic-injustice.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
epistemic-injustice.title: 11. What about the Men
epistemic-injustice.relation: Jones argues that Nick is coerced as surely as June—ordered by Serena, married off to Eden, unable to refuse without Gilead's punishments—so calling his unwilling sex rape should be uncontroversial. Yet he then argues the 'what about the men?' question itself is inappropriate: because politics and film are male-dominated (19 percent women in Congress, 4.1 percent of top films directed by women), women's lived experience rarely gets center stage, and male readers instinctively bend such rare texts back toward themselves. Pieixoto's flirty, fact-obsessed keynote is the model of this failure, and the challenge for male viewers is to listen to what the show says about women's experience—including #MeToo-era sexual violence—without making it about men.

epistemic-injustice.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
epistemic-injustice.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
epistemic-injustice.relation: Argues Toph Beifong is not a pejorative Supercrip stereotype but a Proud Disabled Person counterstory, using Hilde Lindemann's account of master narratives and identity: the BOD and IIH narratives (better-off-dead, irrationally happy) and the Supercrip all presume disability means suffering, while Toph's grumpiness, depth, and central role defy them. Her blindness is disability gain rather than tragedy, since being unsighted led her to learn earthbending from the original teachers, the badgermoles, and to immerse herself in seismic-sense bending full-time. Drawing on Elizabeth Barnes and Miranda Fricker's hermeneutical injustice, the chapter claims disability pride gives disabled viewers permission to celebrate themselves, and shows Toph driving the plot (inventing metalbending, training Aang in 'Bitter Work') instead of teaching non-disabled characters a moral lesson.

epistemic-injustice.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
epistemic-injustice.title: The Buck Stops Here
epistemic-injustice.relation: Argues Earth King Kuei is genuinely responsible for Ba Sing Se's fall because he willfully maintained ignorance of the war and of his own capital's poverty so he could enjoy royal privilege (doting on the bear Bosco while never having left his palace). Using Charles Mills, Miranda Fricker, and Shannon Sullivan on epistemic ignorance, it reads the city's ringed walls as architecture that hides refugees from elites, and the Dai Li's brainwashing of Jet and Joo Dee as a state-fostered 'there is no war in Ba Sing Se' knowledge/ignorance. The chapter's target is our tendency to blame the scheming Long Feng and absolve the 'childlike' king: the buck stops with the powerful man whose privilege depended on not knowing.

epistemic-injustice.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
epistemic-injustice.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
epistemic-injustice.relation: Argues that Toph Beifong is not the harmful 'Supercrip' stereotype (an exceptional individual who overcomes disability through talent and grit, which blames ordinary disabled people for their disadvantage) but a 'Proud Disabled Person' counterstory. Her blindness is a disability gain: it led her to learn earthbending from the badgermoles, the original earthbenders, and to live immersed in bending as her constant way of navigating the world, deepening her mastery. Using Hilde Lindemann's master narratives and counterstories and Elizabeth Barnes's mere-difference view, the chapter shows Toph fits neither the 'better off dead' nor the 'irrationally happy' stereotype: she is grumpy, nuanced (adapting her teaching of Aang in 'Bitter Work'), and a central driver of the plot rather than a moral prop. Fricker's hermeneutical injustice explains why disabled viewers struggle to make sense of flourishing with a disability, and why Toph's portrait gives them permission to celebrate it.

epistemic-injustice.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
epistemic-injustice.title: The Buck Stops Here
epistemic-injustice.relation: Argues that Earth King Kuei, not Grand Secretariat Long Feng, bears the real responsibility for Ba Sing Se's fall, because he willfully maintained ignorance of the war and of his own capital's poverty so he could enjoy palace privilege, playing with his bear Bosco and never once riding the monorail among his people. The city's ring walls work as architectural exclusion that keeps the lower ring's refugees out of elite sight, while the Dai Li's brainwashing ('there is no war in Ba Sing Se', Jet's reconditioning at Lake Laogai) actively manufactures the ignorance the King depends on. Drawing on Charles Mills's epistemology of ignorance and Fricker and Medina's work, the chapter reads Kuei's 'I can't believe I never knew' as epistemic ignorance retained because knowing would cost him his lifestyle, so the buck stops with the seemingly childlike king rather than the arch-villain behind the throne.

epistemic-injustice.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
epistemic-injustice.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.relation: Almassi grades the Dude as a halfway feminist ally: he divests from the Big Lebowski's patriarchal achiever-masculinity ('that and a pair of testicles'), respects Maude's conception project without paternalism (O'Neill's Kantian line between love and respect), and defends pacifist Smokey — yet his pacifism has stalled into passivity that King's active nonviolence would reject, he leaves Bunny's objectification unchallenged while 'Mr. Treehorn treats objects like women', and he only belatedly gives Maude the credibility Fricker's testimonial justice demands ('why don't you fucking listen occasionally?'). Using bell hooks's feminist masculinity and Larry May's progressive male standpoint, the chapter leaves the Dude five pins up with a spare still to pick up.

epistemic-injustice.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
epistemic-injustice.title: 4 “What Would You Have Wakanda Do about It ” Black Panther, Global Justice, and African Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.relation: Hobden argues Wakanda's isolationist 'us vs. them' politics is Western rather than African in spirit: Ramonda's branding of Killmonger as a 'charlatan' enacts Fricker's testimonial injustice and echoes the colonial epistemicide that dismissed African knowledge, while African philosophers (Etieyibo, Eze, Menkiti) derive cosmopolitan duties from ubuntu ('I am because we are') and Igbo proverbs like 'the right hand washes the left,' which welcome the stranger as a bearer of knowledge. She finds it striking that an isiXhosa-speaking Wakanda shows no trace of ubuntu, and reads T'Challa's UN speech as a Western-style aid relationship ('what would you like us to do about it?') rather than genuine recognition of shared humanity.

epistemic-injustice.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
epistemic-injustice.title: 15 Wakandan Resources The Epistemological Reality of Black Panther’s Fiction
epistemic-injustice.relation: Ruby Komic treats Black Panther as an 'epistemic resource' in Gaile Pohlhaus's sense: because of its majority-Black creative team the film supplies audiences with narrative tools that answer to real Black experience, against Anthony Mackie's charge that the film's Black-only hiring is itself racist. The chapter reads the film's plural representations - the T'Challa/Killmonger ideological tension, Nakia's 'No, I save my country' defiance of Okoye's institutional loyalty, Okoye throwing away her wig, Black viewers rooting for the 'villain' - as the kind of nuanced material that remedies decades of stereotypical representation. Following Miranda Fricker, it concludes that the historic scarcity of such resources is an epistemic injustice against Black knowers, and that Black Panther is a partial act of epistemic justice.

epistemic-injustice.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
epistemic-injustice.title: We Can All Be Socratics Supreme
epistemic-injustice.relation: Pape uses the Ancient One's keyhole metaphor to argue that all knowledge is partial and biased: Bacon's confident scientific method ('human knowledge and human power meet in one') is itself just a useful belief, while Socratic awareness of one's ignorance — knowing that you have blind spots, even if you cannot see them — is the real wisdom. She reads the film's running gags as bias lessons (the 'Mister Doctor' exchange, Strange mistaking the wifi password 'Shamballa' for a mantra, the noble-savage prejudice) and feminist critiques of impartiality as itself partial. The whitewashing controversy around Tilda Swinton's Ancient One — weighed against the Fu Manchu stereotype of the 1963 comics and Iron Man 3's Mandarin-as-Trevor-Slattery subversion — shows how filmmakers can confront the biases they cannot simply remove.

epistemic-injustice.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
epistemic-injustice.title: Notes
epistemic-injustice.relation: Sergio Uruena argues the Brotherhood of Steel converts preservation into monopoly: Scribe Yearling buys prewar books as sacred relics, squads seize a settlement's water-purification rigs, and Knight Titus dies on a mission to recover 'a fucking toaster' - read through Langdon Winner's 'Do Artifacts Have Politics?' and Feenberg's contrast between authoritarian and democratic rationalizations of technology. Fricker's epistemic injustice does the central work: 'Blind Betrayal' makes Danse's testimony inadmissible once his synth identity is known (testimonial injustice), while hoarding diagnostic terminals, schematics, and archives strips wastelanders of the interpretive devices through which they understand their world (hermeneutical injustice, extended via Ihde's hermeneutic mediation of technology).
