Jasanoff's co-production explains how this gatekeeping builds social order itself - Maximus is trained into obedience alongside repair, with access tiered even inside the Brotherhood - against the Followers of the Apocalypse's open archives, closing the parallel between locked bunkers and Silicon Valley's gated source code.

epistemic-injustice.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
epistemic-injustice.title: What a Shame She Went Mad: Anger, Affective Injustice, and Taylor Swift
epistemic-injustice.relation: Argues that 'mad woman' dramatizes 'affective injustice' (Whitney and Srinivasan): a woman's righteous anger is misread as Madness with a capital M, so her emotions get the wrong reception, snowballing into toxicity as she 'gets more crazy' each time she is called crazy. Srinivasan's version supplies the double bind of swallowing anger or being dismissed, while Macalester Bell grounds the claim that she 'should be mad' and Dotson's silencing explains why 'no one likes a mad woman'. Against treating affective injustice as a mere symptom of sexism, the chapter uses Marilyn Frye's structural account of sex-marking to argue the Mad woman stereotype is constitutive of sexism itself, with Swift reclaiming the slur like disability activists reclaiming 'crip'.

epistemic-injustice.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
epistemic-injustice.title: Summer Love or Just a Summer Thing? Feminist Standpoint Epistemology
epistemic-injustice.relation: Uses the folklore love triangle ('betty', 'cardigan', 'august') to argue for feminist standpoint epistemology against Ernest Nagel's 'view from nowhere': only by inhabiting each character's emotionally charged standpoint, above all Augustine's in 'august', do we escape the biased 'other woman' script and reach a fuller objectivity. Susan Stebbing and Michael Brady support the claim that emotion aids rather than corrupts knowledge, and the 'mad woman' lyric shows how women's emotion-laden beliefs get dismissed as hysteria. The chapter answers the 'barriers to knowledge' objection by arguing empathy expands, but never escapes, the limits of one's social location, so 'when you are young they assume you know nothing' is a bias to be unlearned.

epistemic-injustice.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
epistemic-injustice.title: The Trouble with Knowing You Were Trouble
epistemic-injustice.relation: Tests three readings of 'I knew you were trouble when you walked in': a stereotyping first-impression claim that fails as knowledge (via the racist-barista thought experiment and Finnis's 'achievement-word' point), a self-knowledge claim that risks Srinivasan's 'faux-feminism' in 'Blank Space' and 'The Man', and finally a justified claim of socially trained 'women's intuition' based on body language. Using Tommie Shelby's account of when beliefs are oppressive, it distinguishes Swift's inference from racist profiling, and Miranda Fricker's epistemic injustice explains how 'mad woman' and 'Nothing New' show women's testimony discounted. The upshot: knowledge is context-specific, and dismissing what marginalized people 'know when you walk in' gaslights their experience.

epistemic-injustice.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
epistemic-injustice.title: I Knew Everything When I Was Young: Examining the Wisdom of Youth
epistemic-injustice.relation: Weighs Betty's 'I knew everything when I was young' against James's 'I don't know anything' using Aristotle's theoretical versus practical wisdom and Nozick's criteria, finding Betty wise: she knows what matters ('To kiss in cars and downtown bars'), the means ('Chase two girls lose the one'), the long view, and how to handle the dilemma of forgiving James. Plato's Meno recollection doctrine and 'seven' ('Before I learned civility I used to scream ferociously') support the claim that the young can possess moral clarity adults lose. James's apology shows wisdom in action (Kekes) and Socratic intellectual humility, while 'tolerate it', 'Dear John', and All Too Well's dinner-party scene illustrate Spear on gaslighting via presumed epistemic superiority of older men.

epistemic-injustice.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
epistemic-injustice.title: Notes
epistemic-injustice.relation: Phillipson uses Thom Merrilin the gleeman in the Amazon series to illustrate standpoint epistemology, arguing (via Heidi Grasswick) that Thom's socially marginal position as a wandering artist grants him epistemic privilege: he understands the murdered Aiel and empathizes with Mat looting a corpse where settled Andorans only fear and judge. She then presses the limits of the theory through Thom's failures, his inability to convey his knowledge to his channeling nephew Owyn, his killing of the Darkfriend innkeeper Dana, and his mistaken diagnosis of Mat, drawing on Bat-Ami Bar On's critique that valorizing marginality for its own sake and grounding privilege in mere distance from a social center is problematic, since Darkfriends are the most marginal of all.

epistemic-injustice.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.relation: Marinucci's editorial introduction surveys the volume, framing Austen's six novels as a body of work with philosophical value across love/marriage, morality/virtue, wealth/class, concepts, and zombie mashups. It previews each contributor's thesis: Bufacchi reading Anne Elliot and the Bennets through Fricker's epistemic injustice, Dougherty aligning Austen's ideal marriage with Aristotelian complete friendship, Lindenmuth pairing Austen with Nietzsche on marital happiness, and Bane's Marxist reading of the 1940 Pride and Prejudice film. It argues Austen is an 'accidental philosopher' whose insight into social relations, especially women's vulnerability, carries philosophical weight.

epistemic-injustice.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
epistemic-injustice.relation: Bufacchi applies Fricker's testimonial and hermeneutical epistemic injustice to Austen's heroines, arguing women like Anne Elliot ('only Anne,' her word carrying no weight) and Elizabeth Bennet are denied credibility as knowers, while Mr. Collins's certainty that a woman's 'no' means 'yes' shows men's epistemic arrogance. He layers in Young's structural injustice to explain the Bennet women's economic vulnerability under entailment, then extends Fricker with his own 'Perpetuating Force of Epistemic Injustice': Emma Woodhouse, herself a victim, becomes a perpetrator by silencing Harriet Smith's love for the farmer Robert Martin, showing how the oppressed reproduce the injustice on those below them.

feminine-mystique.book: 076 - The Good Wife and Philosophy - Temptations of Saint Alicia
feminine-mystique.title: The Good Wife and Philosophy
feminine-mystique.relation: Karen Adkins argues the show exposes the 'choice' to stay home as neither free nor innocent: Betty Friedan's Feminine Mystique and Linda Hirshman's Get to Work frame how Alicia's more-promising-than-Will-or-Peter career was sacrificed to Peter's ambitions and now constrains her, while Peter's 'thanks for playing the breadwinner', Cary's condescension in 'Fleas', and Jackie's 'we stay in the shadows' speech treat her work as a hobby. The show's feminism goes bland, she contends, when Alicia declines to fight Caitlin's resignation in 'Long Way Home' and endorses choice feminism against her own history. The chapter's evidence runs both ways, though: the 'We're not the cops, honey' double standard, and Alicia's mom skills and lawyer skills flowing productively between nursery and deposition room.

feminine-mystique.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
feminine-mystique.title: 5 The Changing Bases of Sexual Politics, 1960–2020
feminine-mystique.relation: Measuring women's progress since 1960 by access to the nine power bases, the chapter shows women using the size/solidarity base to launch the modern feminist movement - Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique as its manifesto, NOW as its vehicle, Ms. as its outlet and Gloria Steinem as its charismatic leader - and how law followed: the accidental Smith amendment adding sex to the 1964 Civil Rights Act, Reed and Frontiero subjecting sex classifications to scrutiny under the 14th Amendment, Griswold and Roe/Casey making reproductive control (which Justice Blackmun called 'necessary for the complete emancipation of women') a condition of women's power, and the 1970s no-fault divorce revolution that Engels's liberation program had demanded. It then charts each base statistically: the narrowing labor-force and wage gaps, women's still minor share of the bourgeoisie, the reversal of the college gender gap and Women's Studies programs built on the Black Studies model, women's entry into cabinet, Court, Congress, clergy and the military, secularization that weakens the religion base behind Elizabeth Cady Stanton's old challenge, and a new moral consensus that unequal treatment of women is wrong.

feminine-mystique.title: 16. Raucous Feminist or Racially Insensitive
feminine-mystique.relation: Weighs Schumer's Peabody-honored 'raucous feminist' image against charges of racial insensitivity by contrasting liberal feminism, exemplified by Friedan's problem that has no name, with intersectionality: hooks's rejoinder that Friedan spoke only for white middle-class women and Crenshaw's multiply-burdened identities. Ware reads the 'Mostly Sex Stuff' jokes about Asian women and third-world bikini waxers, the Beyonce 'Formation' video with Goldie Hawn, and Schumer's dismissive tweets as speaking 'for women' while erasing difference, though the 'Herpes Scare' caricature shows her sometimes winking from inside an intentionally vapid persona. The verdict: Schumer can be both a genuine and an imperfect feminist who must still take accountability.

feminine-mystique.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
feminine-mystique.title: 12 Panther Mystique Wakandan Feminism Demystified
feminine-mystique.relation: Wright and Pérez ask whether Wakanda's powerful women are feminists, arguing M'Baku's dismissal of Shuri as a child trades on Friedan's feminine mystique while Wakandan women escape Beauvoir's woman as the Other because their society, lacking any history of female oppression, never inscribed the second sex. Drawing on Lorde, Davis, Collins, and Walker's womanism, they read Shuri's rejection of romance, Okoye's throne-loyalty, and Nakia's stubbornness as self-definition and interdependency across difference, then use Butler's gender performativity to explain why Okoye squirms in a wig while Nakia breezes through Seoul: womanhood performed in womanist (community-centered) versus feminist (individual-transcendence) modes, with Wakanda modeling the collective call for solidarity the authors hope the future inherits.

feminine-mystique.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
feminine-mystique.title: How Far I'll Go
feminine-mystique.relation: Maps the four waves of feminism onto Disney princess history: Snow White, Cinderella, and Aurora as chattel passed from parents to fairies to princes, betraying even first-wave rights; Beauvoir's 'one is not born but becomes a woman' and Friedan's feminine mystique explaining why the original trio's happiness is measured by marriage. Third-wave princesses are read with Wolf's beauty myth (Ariel and Jasmine as iron maidens), Butler's gender performativity, and Gilligan's care ethics (Ariel's and Belle's contextual, caring moral reasoning versus their fathers' principles). The fourth-wave princesses from Tiana to Moana need no man at all while male leads (Naveen, Flynn, Kristoff, Maui) become vulnerable sidekicks, ending with #GiveElsaAGirlfriend and the thought that equality is balance rather than sameness.

feminine-mystique.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
feminine-mystique.title: Notes
feminine-mystique.relation: Wright reads Wonder Woman's 75-year history through Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman,' arguing Diana's move from Paradise Island to Man's World - surrendering eternal life for Steve Trevor - enacts the hard-won transcendence of immanence that The Second Sex demands. She shows the comics alternating between empowerment (Marston's 'woman of tomorrow,' an unpatriotic George Washington scolding women war workers) and regression (Trevor persuading Wonder Woman to marry and type memos about women's place being the home, the 1990s hyper-sexualized art), evidence that woman remains the Other to man's Subject. Wonder Woman's durability, she says, lies in exactly this ambiguity, and like Beauvoir's woman of tomorrow she models forging identity through projects in the world.

feminine-mystique.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
feminine-mystique.title: 63. Amy Schumer as Philosopher Fuck the Feminine Mystique
feminine-mystique.relation: Elsby argues Amy Schumer's honest comedy revolts against a 'feminine mystique' broader than Friedan's housewife version, running back to Beauvoir's claim that woman is constructed as the 'Other' and to Aristotle's 'rational animal' definition that cast women as irrational and thus less than human. Through bits like 'Madame President,' 'Last Fuckable Day,' the 'New Twitter Button' sketch, and gross-out honesty about pregnancy and her own body in Growing and The Leather Special, Schumer refuses to let women's physical, sexual, and social experience stay mysterious. Elsby reads this as de-'othering' and re-humanizing women by forcing our concept of 'woman' to expand to include flawed, fully human hot-mess figures.

ethics-of-lying.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
ethics-of-lying.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
ethics-of-lying.relation: Fallis sorts Atlantic City's lies to show which are wrong and why. Kant's and Augustine's absolute bans go too far and Grotius's life-saving exception does not apply - most of these lies get people killed - yet even altruistic lies (Margaret for Madame Jeunet and the ledger), lies told to those who want to be deceived, lies to liars, and Sorensen's bald-faced lies that no one believes (Jimmy's flat movie alibi, Rothstein's 'skilled player' whopper) remain wrong: they take informed choice out of the victim's hands, violating the Kantian autonomy that grounds the wrong of lying, and they corrode the trust on which even criminals' co-operation depends.

ethics-of-lying.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
ethics-of-lying.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
ethics-of-lying.relation: Taking J. L. Austin's distinction between justifying conduct (showing it was the right thing to do) and excusing it (accepting wrongdoing but denying full blame), the chapter audits the trilogy's deceptions: Blomkvist's lottery trick on the pedophile Björck, his intention to double-cross him, the fake-collapse 'double game' at Millennium, and the disinformation fed to the Section's bugs are justified, since they deceive only dangerous criminals engaged in murderous conspiracies. Salander is shakier—her hacking of the innocent Blomkvist and the tax-tip revenge on the realtor expose the flaw in 'a bastard is always a bastard' (she cannot know guilt in advance), though her lies to Bjurman, Forbes, and Zalachenko earn excuse or justification. The verdict falls hardest on the cover-up of Martin Vanger's murders—trading truth for Harriet's protection and crisis-center funding, it might have warned other women, so Blomkvist's 'unforgivable' stands—and on her final lies under oath to honest police, excusable only if she still cannot trust the state.

ethics-of-lying.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
ethics-of-lying.title: NOTES
ethics-of-lying.relation: First defines lying — distinguishing it from mere error (Angela believing Peter dead), from the Haitian's non-verbal memory-wipe deception, and from Hiro's silent staging of Ando's fake death — then tests moral theories against the show's liars. Kant's categorical imperative bans all lying but is abandoned when Sylar demands a friend's hiding place; utilitarianism vindicates Victoria Pratt's lie about the virus vial yet also licenses Linderman's .07% explosion and Plato's noble lie of the earthborn metals, which the chapter rejects. Machiavelli's advice that princes may lie to keep power is played out by 'President Sylar' in 'Five Years Gone,' and the chapter finally endorses Sissela Bok's presumption against lying — a public-reasoning procedure modeled by Bob Bishop and Mohinder before Monica's virus injection.

physicalism.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
physicalism.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
physicalism.relation: Hess asks whether the monster has a soul and makes him the test case between physicalism (Kim, Churchland, van Inwagen) and dualism: recasting Frank Jackson's Mary as a color-blind monster who learns every physical fact about color vision, receives new eyes on Walton's ship, and then learns the 'what it is like' of seeing red for the first time, he argues there are nonphysical mental facts, so physicalism is false. He then runs Plantinga's argument that we are not our bodies or brains through a machine that replaces the monster's parts and hemispheres one by one while he stays conscious, and adds near-death out-of-body evidence like Maria's window-ledge shoe to suggest we can exist disembodied. The upshot is symmetric: whatever we conclude about the monster's soul we must conclude about our own - so be careful about assuming who does and does not have a soul, even monsters.

physicalism.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
physicalism.title: “Strange Magic,” Electric Light Orchestra, 1975
physicalism.relation: Kowalski reads the film's astral-form scenes as a dramatization of Cartesian substance dualism against Strange's opening physicalism ('There is no such thing as spirit! We are made of matter and nothing more'): the Ancient One pushing his astral body out refutes physicalism, his soul reads books while his body sleeps, and he fights Kaecilius's acolyte as a visible astral form in Christine Palmer's ER. The chapter then confronts the classic interaction problem — Descartes' pineal gland and 'animal spirits,' Elisabeth of Bohemia's and Garrett Thomson's objections — asking how an immaterial astral form can turn pages or knock over vending machines, joking that it would take 'a very strange form of interactionism.' The Ancient One's account of magic as energy drawn from other dimensions of the multiverse is offered as the film's own dualist reply, with a closing plea for the epistemic humility Strange had to learn.

physicalism.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
physicalism.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
physicalism.relation: Edward Cox asks whether physicalism - everything is physical, and everything depends on the arrangement of physical stuff - is true in Westeros. The causal argument shows Jaime's love could move Bran's body only if it is itself a brain state, and the maesters' science (boiling wine against infection, Baratheon black hair as heredity, the Eyrie's winch) reveals a world running on our physics. But magic strains the picture: reanimated Othor and Jafer Flowers must physically change to walk, and Daenerys's walk into Drogo's pyre requires her resolve to disrupt combustion itself - so Cox concludes magic is either violation of physical law or a nonphysical force, and that in our world immaterial souls would be exactly as improbable as magic.

tabula-rasa.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
tabula-rasa.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
tabula-rasa.relation: Lopez uses the monster - 'one man made out of many' - to stress-test personal identity: brain-swap and amnesia-torture thought experiments first drive us to identify with our memories (the memory-based psychological criterion) and then, when Victor offers to wipe memory before the pain experiments, with our bodies, yielding inconsistent answers. The monster's own testimony - waking confused, prodding fire like an infant, acquiring language by eavesdropping on Safie's lessons, and building his values from scratch out of Paradise Lost and the cottagers - shows he is a genuinely new person rather than whoever once owned his corpse-parts, since we would not say a memory-wiped torture victim ceases to exist. He concludes the monster satisfies the five listed personhood criteria (consciousness, reasoning, self-motivated activity, communication, self-awareness), with identity riding a continuing stream of consciousness running on a body that is, in the end, secondary 'hardware.'

tabula-rasa.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
tabula-rasa.title: 17. Our Lying Eyes
tabula-rasa.relation: Wood asks how Elliot - and we, who see only what he sees - can know anything, and contrasts two empiricisms: Locke's white-paper mind furnished by ideas copied from mind-independent objects, which explains Mr. Robot as perceptual error, and Berkeley's idealism, on which only ideas and their divine cause exist, which makes Elliot's unshared hallucination of Mr. Robot dangerously hard to distinguish from reality. Consistency of perception is the only test left, and it fails Elliot until the pier video proves no one pushed him - and fails us again when his cozy Season Two routine turns out to be prison.

tabula-rasa.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
tabula-rasa.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
tabula-rasa.relation: Pötzsch reads Sheldon as the early Wittgenstein trapped in the Tractatus's picture theory — taking Penny's 'How've you been?' as a question about existence and replying 'I can't be impossible, I exist' — living among speakers of the later Wittgenstein's language games, where meaning is use within forms of life and social conventions (the tea that must be an invitation, the pizza-for-helping-moving protocol). Family resemblance, the childlike learner whose slate of social convention is blank (the Lockean tabula rasa applied to Sheldon's social mind), and lying as a language game Sheldon plays badly — the fake cousin Leopold Houston's fabricated Facebook trail, the orangutan hair — all dramatize the passage from logic-bound to use-based meaning that Sheldon, like Wittgenstein, may eventually make.

tabula-rasa.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
tabula-rasa.title: NOTE
tabula-rasa.relation: Shai Biderman and William Devlin argue the character John Locke begins as an empiricist in the mold of his philosophical namesake - his boar hunting, tracking, and trebuchet-building against the hatch all follow the scientific method befitting a tabula rasa mind furnished by experience - but the miracle of his healed legs poses a 'why' that empirical explanation of 'how' cannot answer. He therefore converts to the Taoism of the Tao Te Ching: the moth-cocoon lesson to Charlie, 'I stopped looking' for Sun's ring, reading dreams and signs from the island, and finally his self-sacrifice to stop the time flashes all enact following the Way. The chapter reads the black-and-white backgammon stones, Locke's one-black-one-white eyes in Claire's dream, and Jacob versus the Man in Black as yin-yang complementarity, with empiricism and Taoism finally interdependent like the dots in each half.

tabula-rasa.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
tabula-rasa.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
tabula-rasa.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

tabula-rasa.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
tabula-rasa.title: 6. The Foundations of Psychohistory
tabula-rasa.relation: Irish roots psychohistory in the seventeenth- and eighteenth-century clash between rationalism and empiricism over whether history can be a science. Descartes's mathematical, a priori method (which bred an 'anti-historical skepticism') is the ancestor of Seldon's dream of mathematizing human behavior, while Locke's empiricism and probabilistic knowledge inspired Gibbon's defense of historical evidence. Irish stages the Ancients-versus-Moderns debate through the Lord Dorwin / Salvor Hardin exchange over first-hand versus armchair scholarship, and contrasts Gibbon's moral, backward-looking history with Seldon's amoral, forward-looking prediction.

tabula-rasa.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
tabula-rasa.title: NOTE
tabula-rasa.relation: Shai Biderman and William J. Devlin trace John Locke the character's shift from the empiricism of his philosophical namesake to Taoism. Early Locke is the tabula-rasa empiricist and scientific-method hunter and hatch-engineer, but his miraculous restored ability to walk, Jacob's touch, and his visions push him to ask 'why' rather than 'how.' They argue Locke comes to follow the Tao—the unnamable Way symbolized by the black-and-white yin-yang seen in backgammon pieces and Claire's dream—advising Charlie via the struggling moth, teaching Walt to visualize the knife's path, and finding Sun's ring by not looking, ultimately reading his sacrificial death as effortless surrender to the island's flow.

tabula-rasa.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
tabula-rasa.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
tabula-rasa.relation: Florell and Wilson, psychologists, survey parenting through the nature–nurture debate, casting Locke's tabula rasa against Rousseau's noble-savage view of children, alongside Piaget and Kohlberg on moral development and Walter Mischel's marshmallow experiment on impulse control. They map the four parenting styles (authoritarian, permissive, uninvolved, authoritative) on responsiveness and control, argue authoritative parenting is optimal, and advise fathers to adjust discipline to each child's innate temperament rather than enforce rigid gender roles.

tabula-rasa.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
tabula-rasa.title: 10. Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood as Philosophy Children as Philosophers
tabula-rasa.relation: Baggett argues that Mister Rogers' Neighborhood was a profoundly philosophical show because it treated very young children as natural philosophers — curious, wonder-filled questioners — rather than mere proto-adults. He frames child-development theory through the rationalism/empiricism divide (Skinner's behaviorism descending from Locke's tabula rasa, Chomsky's innatism from Descartes) and champions Gareth Matthews's claim that children's 'romancing' is genuine philosophy adults should not condescend to. Rogers modeled Hadot's philosophy-as-a-way-of-life and James's and Rousseau's active learning; episodes on death (the goldfish), work, and make-believe invited the same wonder Aquinas and Hume brought to happiness and causation, treating children as members of Kant's kingdom of ends.

dirty-hands.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
dirty-hands.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
dirty-hands.relation: Matthew Brophy argues the I.F. could only get a compassionate child to commit xenocide by presenting war as a game, a framing that neutralizes moral agency just as Milgram's shock experiments and the fake game show The Game of Death did. Using Sunzi's 'know your enemy' to frame the empathy paradox, Walzer's problem of dirty hands for Graff's lesser-evil choices, and Foot's trolley problem alongside drone 'Nintendo warfare' to show how distance makes killing easier, he concludes Ender was likely a willing pawn who let himself be deceived because he endorsed the war's survivalist goal.

dirty-hands.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
dirty-hands.title: Homeland and Philosophy
dirty-hands.relation: Christophe Porot and Charles Taliaferro ask whether Homeland's pervasive hypocrisy and deceit can be justified, starting from Walden's cover-up of the drone strike and Brody's heroic persona hiding a terrorist plot. Machiavelli's Prince supplies the case that political relationships with allies (Saul's 'Us and Them' speech to Carrie) require hypocrisy, while the Smith-inspired 'honest politicking' model - trading openly on self-interest, as with Carrie blackmailing al Sahrani - fails because politics should secure the public good, though la Rochefoucauld's 'homage vice pays virtue' explains Saul extorting the judge into doing right. Weighing Kant's unconditional duty not to lie (Carrie's fatal lie to Lynne Reed) against consequentialism, the chapter lands on the Walzer Dirty Hands view: some acts stay wrong yet necessary, and honest agents accept the guilt.

dirty-hands.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
dirty-hands.title: The Bill Comes Due
dirty-hands.relation: The chapter uses Michael Walzer's Problem of Dirty Hands to weigh the Ancient One's secret lifelong use of forbidden dark magic against Kaecilius's summoning of Dormammu, arguing that only she faces a genuine dirty-hands dilemma because her end (defending Earth) is good while his is not. It asks why dark magic is forbidden at all and answers with rule-utilitarian reasoning that has taken on a deontological life of its own, then invokes Kant's murderer-at-the-door essay to argue, with Mordo's 'the bill comes due,' that whoever does wrong for good ends bears responsibility for the downstream consequences—and that Strange's willingness to break Kamar-Taj's rules while accepting the cost is what makes him a hero.

dirty-hands.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
dirty-hands.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
dirty-hands.relation: Matthew Brophy argues the I.F. neutralizes Ender's moral agency by masquerading xenocide as child's play: Rackham's paradox that total empathy with the buggers forbids killing them (Sunzi's 'know your enemy') is solved by deception, Walzer's problem of dirty hands is shifted from the child to the politicians, and Milgram-style game framing plus Foot's trolley-problem 'moral distance' show how killing grows easier at a console. Against the innocent-pawn reading, Brophy ends by suggesting Ender was a willing pawn who let himself be deceived in order to save humanity.

dirty-hands.title: Notes
dirty-hands.relation: Uses Sartre's play Dirty Hands and Walzer's 'Political Action: The Problem of Dirty Hands' to ask whether Frank's willingness to do the 'necessary thing' — from the opening mercy-killing of the dog to the Season 3 drone strike — could ever count in favor of an Underwood presidency, with utilitarians (nothing wrong with dirty hands) and absolutists like the bishop ('Love God, and love each other. Period.') dissolving the problem from opposite sides. Walzer's later 'supreme emergency' standard and threshold deontology frame the Jordan Valley staring contest with Petrov and the resulting deal as the one case where Frank's capability might genuinely matter, while Heather Dunbar's reluctance (her refusal of Stamper's offer of Claire's diary, then her reversal) tests the ideal of a leader both capable of and averse to dirtying her hands. The verdict: Frank's only advantage over Dunbar is his capacity for dirty hands, and even that fails because he lacks the scruples to keep them clean when it is not necessary.

dirty-hands.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
dirty-hands.title: Notes
dirty-hands.relation: Perry frames Frank through Walzer's problem of dirty hands, taking its name from Sartre's play ('I have dirty hands right up to the elbows... Do you think you can govern innocently?') and Machiavelli's advice to 'enter into evil when forced by necessity' — the pilot's mercy killing of the dog and 'just shy of treason, which is politics' being the show's emblems. He maps the field onto the show: utilitarians for whom breaking rules can be right, absolutists like the bishop ('Love God, and love each other. Period.'), and Walzer's later 'supreme emergency' threshold deontology applied to Frank's child-killing drone strike and his desperate deal with Petrov in the Jordan Valley. The verdict: Frank's only edge over Heather Dunbar is a proven capacity to dirty his hands when needed, but he lacks the scruples that keep that capacity from becoming routine wrongdoing, so he is probably still the wrong man for the job.

dirty-hands.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
dirty-hands.title: Sometimes You Have to Fight
dirty-hands.relation: Brake pits Geralt's refusal to choose between evils ('Evil is evil, Stregobor... if I'm to choose between one evil and another, then I prefer not to choose at all') against Reinhold Niebuhr's Christian realism, which holds that collective political life admits only greater and lesser evils and 'enough justice,' never the individual's moral purity. Triss's post-Sodden realization that war is survival rather than a choice, Ciri's verdict that Geralt's neutrality was contemptible, and Nilfgaard's 'war on everything that can burn' push toward Niebuhr's view that capitulation to tyranny in the name of nonresistant perfection becomes connivance. Yet Yarpen's herd-of-pigs defense of progress and the fate of the Nilfgaardian settlers driven out of Rivia after victory show that even relative justice stays stained, which is why witchers, as Yarpen says, 'will always be needed.'

dirty-hands.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
dirty-hands.title: The Dialectics of Monstrosity
dirty-hands.relation: Giladi argues the Witcherverse's silver/steel sword dualism - the clean division between 'human' and 'monster' - is subverted by what he calls the dialectics of monstrosity: the worst monsters are moral ones, agents cruel through and through. He reads the 'Killing Monsters' trailer (Geralt hanging the Nilfgaardian officer about to hang a young woman), the witch hunter exchange ('you don't need mutations to strip men of their humanity'), Tissaia's torture of Cahir, and Stregobor's autopsy plans through Honneth's Hegelian account of recognition (losing 'antecedent recognition') and Shklar's cruelty as the summum malum. Montaigne on recreational cruelty and Arendt's banality of evil explain Geralt's genealogy that 'people like to invent monsters... then they seem less monstrous themselves,' while Bernard Williams shows Geralt's 'Evil is Evil' refusal to get his hands dirty is itself what lets evil fester.

dirty-hands.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
dirty-hands.title: XII - DIRTY HAN DS AN D DIRTY MINDS THE ETHICS OF MIND READING AND MINDWRITING
dirty-hands.relation: Terjesen examines whether telepaths can be trusted, starting epistemically: Descartes' problem of other minds and Russell's analogy answer explain how Xavier's football-field telepathy and the Cuckoos' exoneration of Beak could be verified, and how far Jean's telepathic testimony about Cassandra Nova should be acted on. Utilitarians (Mill) and deontologists then split over mindwriting: Xavier's early memory erasures, the permanent rewrite of a terrorist's personality, and the Magneto mindwipe versus Cyclops and Emma's 'telepathic affair' and Jean's ransacking of Emma's memories, where privacy and intimacy are at stake. Invoking Machiavelli and Walzer, the chapter concludes Xavier's dirty hands are necessary but wrong, so he should feel guilt and step down, lest mindreading mutants become the thing humans rightly fear.

dirty-hands.title: “They Turned to a Man They Didn’t Fully Understand”
dirty-hands.relation: Foy and Dale argue that the Dark Knight trilogy endorses a conservative critique of liberal democracy: Batman taps every citizen's phone, tortures criminals, and kidnaps Lau from Hong Kong because Gotham's institutions cannot cope with a permanent state of crisis. Hume's conservatism—authority resting on habit and order rather than abstract rights and consent—explains Batman's defense of the existing order against Ra's al Ghul's razing of Gotham, while Schmitt's sovereign who declares the 'state of exception' frames Batman as the extra-legal protector who suspends rights during crisis (with Rachel's Caesar warning marking the danger). Against Locke's natural rights and Rawls's inviolability of the person, the Joker and Bane dramatize Strauss's twin fears that liberalism degenerates into nihilistic value-chaos or coercive revolutionary equality, and Burke's natural aristocracy of 'virtual representation' justifies relying on an unchosen elite hero. The trilogy's central puzzle is Batman's illiberal means—taking the blame for Dent's death to preserve the White Knight myth—dirtying his hands so that Gotham's official powers stay clean.

cicero-duty.book: 080 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - Genocide Is Child's Play
cicero-duty.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
cicero-duty.relation: James Cook grades the Third Invasion against the just war principles Ender was never taught: the war is preventive rather than genuinely preemptive (with the 2003 Iraq parallel), proper authority is compromised by deceiving the public, last resort fails since the hive-queen was trying to communicate, and non-combatant immunity condemns destroying the bugger homeworld. He stages Augustine's ban on killing in individual self-defense against Aquinas' permission of it, and uses Kant's humanity formula and Cicero's hostis/perduellis distinction to ask whether the buggers were ever treated as rational beings rather than mere threats.

cicero-duty.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
cicero-duty.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
cicero-duty.relation: Air Force colonel James Cook walks the just war tradition through Ender's world: the Third Invasion is preventive rather than preemptive (with the 2003 Iraq war as the parallel), proper authority is undermined by the I.F.'s lies to its citizens, and last resort fails because the hive-queen was already trying to communicate with Ender. He contrasts Augustine's ban on killing in self-defense with Aquinas's permission, invokes Kant's formula of humanity for the buggers' rational nature and Cicero's hostis against dehumanizing enemies, and argues the I.F.'s failure to teach military ethics is itself part of the novel's tragedy.

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
naturalistic-fallacy.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Framed as a sports broadcast with Aristotle as commentator, the chapter tests an evolutionary ethics ('BEES': the good is the naturally desirable, so the Pleistocene Stinson strategy of spreading genes grounds Barney's womanizing) against its classic critics. Hume's is-ought gap and Moore's open question argument are deployed against deriving Barney's right to pursue tail from human nature, while William Casebeer's evolutionary ethics replies that 'good' can be defined by present reproductive success - under which lying and eternal bachelorhood fail, since commitment is what reproduces genomes in urban New York ('BIRDS'). The chapter concludes that evolutionary ethics can support the Bro Code only by contestable redefinition, and the lying objection stands.

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
naturalistic-fallacy.title: 15. The C-Word
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Works through the ethics of cloning and genetic selection, starting with the objection that such technologies are "unnatural": that reasoning commits the naturalistic fallacy, since following Hume you can't get an ought from an is, and human ingenuity (roads, eyeglasses, IVF) is itself part of nature. Using Nietzsche's Genealogy account of master morality — good as the noble traits of intelligence, beauty, and strength — the chapter asks whether parents would then be obliged to engineer better children, while warning where trait-selection slides: Nazi eugenics, racist trait-lists (both Leda and Castor are white and conventionally attractive), and "abilism" against the deaf. It concludes that cloning itself is not evil: Projects Leda and Castor are immoral not because they clone but because they treat clones as mere means to an end, in Kant's sense, and trample their autonomy.

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
naturalistic-fallacy.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Jaquet and Cova take the show's 'livestock' comparisons seriously and use animal ethics to test every justification for the guests' treatment of hosts. Direct speciesism (Logan: 'She's a goddamn doll') and indexical speciesism (Maeve's 'us versus them' to Bernard) both fail because mere species membership is morally irrelevant, like race or sex. The supposed human-exclusive markers also fail: hosts match us in intelligence (Maeve outclasses Stubbs), moral sense (Bernard's guilt over Theresa, Teddy's remorse over the massacre), and compatibilist free will - acts flowing from the agent's own desires - against Ford's determinism and Lutz's 'you don't have a choice.' They then refute the argument from nature (Ford's 'we murdered and butchered anything that challenged our primacy'), the Kantian person/tool contrast in the hosts' favor, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and the 'better to exist' defense, concluding that because the hosts are conscious, they belong to the moral community alongside humans and animals.

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
naturalistic-fallacy.title: Bringing Balance to the Force
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Harter argues that Revenge of the Sith manipulates audiences into fearing the medical technology that saves Anakin on Mustafar, portraying his prosthetic transformation into Vader as horrifying when in real bioethical terms saving a burn victim with ventilators, feeding tubes, and prosthetics is something we applaud. He diagnoses Lucas's framing as the naturalistic fallacy (what is natural is good), grounded in Hume's is-ought gap, and flags the mirror-image 'technological fallacy' of assuming enhancement like General Grievous's cyborg body must be good. The chapter concludes that technology is value-neutral and its worth depends on the context of use — which is what it means for Anakin and Luke, both maimed and prosthetized, to 'bring balance to the Force.'

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
naturalistic-fallacy.title: X - MAGNETO, MUTATION, AND MORALITY
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Davis stages the debate over whether evolution can ground ethics through Magneto and Xavier. If Dennett and Dawkins are right that morality is evolved 'rule worship,' then Magneto's rule, eliminate threats to mutant fitness, looks as good as Xavier's cooperation, and Magneto never argues morally because, like Ruse, he treats moral claims as emotive boos, hence converting Senator Kelly by force rather than reason. Moore's naturalistic fallacy blocks any is-to-ought inference, Jean Grey's sacrifice in X2 shows praise tracks choice against instinct rather than hardwired impulse, and the chapter ends suggesting, via Frege's Third Realm, that morality's ground may lie beyond the natural.

naturalistic-fallacy.title: A Darker Shade Realism in Neo-Noir
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Jason Holt argues that realism, especially about the role values play in people's lives, is the underappreciated essence of noir, offering a working definition of noir as 'stylized crime realism.' Surveying neo-noir detectives (Harper, Chinatown's Gittes), revamped femmes fatales who get away with it (Body Heat's Matty, The Last Seduction's Bridget), morally ambiguous protagonists (To Live and Die in L.A., Manhunter), and Lynch and Tarantino, he shows how the post-Production-Code freedom lets endings ring true to life by letting the guilty escape justice. He coins the 'normativistic fallacy' as the inverse of Moore's naturalistic fallacy: inferring what is from what ought to be, arguing that mainstream cinema's poetic justice commits it while neo-noir's downbeat endings correct it, fulfilling the realism latent in classic noir.

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
naturalistic-fallacy.title: 1. How to De-Nazify Nietzsche’s Philosophical Anthropology
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Golomb argues the Nazi reading of the will to power as military conquest confuses Nietzsche's Macht (sublimated spiritual power) with Kraft (brute force) and Gewalt (violence), showing through Human, All Too Human and Daybreak that self-overcoming and creative sublimation, not domination, define the Übermensch. He builds a typology of 'positive' versus 'negative' power in which the anti-Semite figures as the vengeful, ressentiment-driven 'slave,' and insists Nietzsche's morality is not naturalistic—power must be transfigured by self-education—so his anthropology stands beyond the eugenic and racial distinctions central to Nazi ideology, even in the misused 'blond beast' passage.

naturalistic-fallacy.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
naturalistic-fallacy.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
naturalistic-fallacy.relation: Kirkwood argues that caffeine is uncontroversially a performance-enhancing drug—boosting memory, reaction time, endurance—and that by WADA's own three-part test (performance-enhancing, potentially harmful, against the spirit of sport) coffee should count as doping, yet never has. He dismantles the standard anti-doping arguments as applied to coffee: the cheating/unfairness charge is circular and dissolves when everyone may use it; the 'unnaturalness' argument commits a non sequitur (umbrellas are unnatural too, and chewed coffee beans seem natural); and the harm test fails because the positive threshold sits at a mere 20-ounce serving, far below caffeinism. His conclusion is that coffee escapes the 'doping' label not through moral reasoning but through public acceptance—the emotive word 'drug' is withheld from the substance everyone uses.

rectification-of-names.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
rectification-of-names.title: The Devil and Philosophy
rectification-of-names.relation: Nicolas Michaud catalogues the demonic hierarchy - de Spina's goblins, incubi, and familiars, Dante's Malebranche, Binsfeld's seven princes of Hell - through Dungeon Keeper's Dark Mistress, World of Warcraft succubi, Se7en, Hellraiser's Pinhead, Hellboy, and Spawn. His real argument is ontological: names are power, and what we call the Devil fixes how we treat him. Recovering the Hebrew sense of 'satan' as an appointed adversary and 'Lucifer' as light-bringer (compared to Prometheus), he argues the same being could be reframed from tempter to giver of knowledge, much as naming Columbus's invasion a 'discovery' launders atrocity.

rectification-of-names.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
rectification-of-names.title: Girls and Philosophy
rectification-of-names.relation: Carleo and D'Ambrosio read Hannah's 'busy trying to become who I am' through the classical Chinese debate over names: her self-claimed title 'writer' preceding any conduct is the Confucian nightmare of names divorced from actuality, diagnosed by the Analects's rectification of names ('rulers should rule, fathers should father') and the sheep-stealing passage warning against over-identifying with a single role. Adam, by contrast, lives the Daoist ideal - the empty vessel of the Daodejing acting by wu wei, and Zhuangzi's butterfly dream fluidity in his role-play sex and absorbed woodworking, unattached to titles. Mencius and Xunzi frame the resolution: by Season Three Hannah finally rectifies names at GQ while Adam's non-identity turns delusional, vindicating the ideal of being an 'internal sage and external king' - Daoist in private, responsible to roles in public.

rectification-of-names.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
rectification-of-names.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
rectification-of-names.relation: Morgan Deane reads Ender's tactics as Sunzi's Art of War in action: winning all future fights by terror, exploiting Bonzo's hot anger, 'fatal terrain' when Graff stacks hopeless odds, formlessness that hides intent, and fluid toon formations that move like water — all grounded in Daoist harmony with the Way and the Confucian role-duty of the general-as-father who throws soldiers into hopeless positions to win their devotion. He also finds Legalist rewards-and-punishments in Ender's command of Dragon Army, concluding Ender qualifies as a Sunzi-style military genius whose empathy is the steep moral price of victory.

rectification-of-names.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
rectification-of-names.title: Notes
rectification-of-names.relation: Decker parallels the Republic's fall into Palpatine's Empire with the Zhou dynasty's collapse that birthed Chinese philosophy, reading three Jedi from the Dark Times comics through it. K'Kruhk, guided by the Zatoichi-like Master Zao, learns wu-wei - following the Force rather than forcing outcomes, with Laozi's Dao as the Force's Chinese analogue. Dass Jennir's struggle over what 'Jedi' means after killing a slaver becomes Confucian rectification of names and the cultivation of ren, while Kai Hudorra's loss of faith, withdrawal to a casino, and final sacrificial stand against Vader embody Mozi-style pragmatic minimalism redeemed by Jennir's virtuous example.

rectification-of-names.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
rectification-of-names.title: NOTES
rectification-of-names.relation: The Terjesens pit Kant's impersonal morality — Sam's contractual distance from the thieving Mickens is exactly how he would treat strangers — against Confucius and Mencius, for whom filial duties are the nursery of virtue: we learn benevolence by serving parents and revering elders, Lafayette's care for Lettie Mae and Tara shows family forming moral character, and the Upright Gong's covering for a father's sheep-stealing grounds Jason's 'sometimes the right thing to do is the wrong thing'. Mencius's King Shun, who abdicates and carries his criminal father into exile, models how Tommy and Jason should put family first while accepting the cost, while Mozi's universal love surfaces in Godric's 'forgiveness is love', and the chapter concludes that family counts only insofar as it develops our moral nature — the line between Tommy and Sam.

jung-shadow.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
jung-shadow.title: The Devil and Philosophy
jung-shadow.relation: Liz Stillwaggon Swan explains why crime dramas like Criminal Minds, CSI, and Bones are so watchable: Jung's shadow archetype and collective unconscious mean the Devil in human form on screen taps humanity's shared dark layer, while Aristotle's catharsis lets viewers experience pity and fear safely from the couch, identifying with characters like repulsed Garcia or intellectualizing Dr. Brennan. She adds the CSI effect - jurors with warped expectations of DNA and fingerprint work - and argues the shows satisfy a deep need to see devils like Bundy and Dahmer caught within a tidy forty-three minutes.

jung-shadow.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
jung-shadow.title: The Devil and Philosophy
jung-shadow.relation: John Thompson argues Mara, who unleashes armies and seductive daughters on the Buddha-to-be under the bodhi tree, is not 'the Buddhist Satan': he has not fallen, wages no cosmic war against a supreme God, and merely personifies trsna (grasping) as overlord of samsara. He finds textbook glosses like Huston Smith's misleading, and praises Bertolucci's Little Buddha, where Mara rises from a pool as Siddhartha's mirror twin - 'Oh Lord of my own Ego, you are pure illusion. You do not exist' - a portrayal he reads through Karen Armstrong's Jungian shadow self and Campbell's Freudian eros-and-thanatos frame, concluding that we are Mara/Satan.

jung-shadow.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
jung-shadow.title: Dracula and Philosophy
jung-shadow.relation: Tim Jones uses Jung's Shadow to argue Dracula is the British Empire's Shadow Self: everything the Count does in Britain - draining resources, reshaping native identities - mirrors what Britain does abroad, minus the benevolent veneer, while Ego-projection explains why Harker's crew must annihilate him rather than admit what he reflects. The chapter adds that colonial stereotypes became self-fulfilling, with colonized peoples made to live the imposed identities, and reads the era's reverse-invasion fiction (mummies, The War of the Worlds) as a collective staking of the Shadow. It closes by recommending Jungian ownership of the Shadow instead of projection.

jung-shadow.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
jung-shadow.title: Dracula and Philosophy
jung-shadow.relation: Callis reads the 1931 Lugosi film through Jung: Dracula is Mina's Shadow archetype and animus, embodying her repressed fear of sexuality and of the married life she claims to want, while the vampire's presence in every culture places him in the collective unconscious. Mina's arc - the Call to Adventure, crossing the threshold into Dracula's embrace, and 'resurrection' after his staking - becomes a Shero's Journey of confronting the shadow, with Dracula also playing the Shapeshifter archetype. The chapter ends doubting the happy ending, asking whether Mina defeated her shadow or merely surrendered her dreams of freedom.

jung-shadow.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
jung-shadow.title: 11. Meeting the Monstrous Self
jung-shadow.relation: Piven reads 'The Width of a Circle''s monster sitting by the tree through the doppelgänger tradition (Rank's The Double, Dostoevsky, Kirk's 'Enemy Within,' Luke finding his own face in Vader's mask): the monstrous double is the self, and social identity is the mask that hides it, so 'we have met Sauron and he is us.' Deploying Jungian archetype against mere stereotype, Nietzsche's dictum that truth kills, and the Freudian superego - the devil as its alter ego, perversely enjoying the condemnation it inflicts - the chapter argues Bowie's erotic devil scene shows how moralistic societies brand innocent desire monstrous, and that an agonizing encounter with the inner monster, not clichéd self-mythology, is the dire necessity of self-knowledge.

jung-shadow.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
jung-shadow.title: 2. Know Thyself, Agent Cooper!
jung-shadow.relation: Reads the Season Two Black Lodge finale as Cooper's failed journey of self-knowledge, framed by Socrates' Delphic "know thyself" and the unexamined life. Against Hume's bundle theory — when Hume looks inward he only ever finds particular perceptions, never a self — the chapter sets the Vedanta/Tibetan Buddhist ideal of knowing the true Self beyond thought (the ocean versus its waves), with the Black Lodge as the place Hawk calls a passage "every soul must pass on its way to perfection." Cooper's screaming white-eyed Laura, the flickering Caroline/Annie corpse, and his grinning doppelgänger are Jungian shadow-projections paralleled scene-by-scene with the wrathful visions of the Tibetan Book of the Dead; entering with imperfect courage, he flees his fears instead of integrating them, splitting into trapped good Dale and the rampaging Mr. C of The Return.

jung-shadow.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
jung-shadow.title: 10. Stranger Shadows
jung-shadow.relation: Cornell reads the Upside Down as an externalized Jungian Shadow: the faceless Demogorgon, 'almost human but it wasn't,' embodies the archetypal shadow of the collective unconscious intruding into Hawkins, and the moral task is integrating it with the conscious ego. Will's possession by the Shadow Monster shows what Jung calls the ego identifying with an unintegrated shadow (his timidity leaving him overpowered), while El is the contrast: after her symbolic rebirth from the fleshy wall she faces absolute evil, acknowledges her own monstrous capacity to kill, and turns the shadow into heroism, ending at Nietzsche's 'becoming who she is.'

jung-collective-unconscious.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
jung-collective-unconscious.title: The Devil and Philosophy
jung-collective-unconscious.relation: Liz Stillwaggon Swan explains why crime dramas like Criminal Minds, CSI, and Bones are so watchable: Jung's shadow archetype and collective unconscious mean the Devil in human form on screen taps humanity's shared dark layer, while Aristotle's catharsis lets viewers experience pity and fear safely from the couch, identifying with characters like repulsed Garcia or intellectualizing Dr. Brennan. jung-collective-unconscious.relation: Callis reads the 1931 Lugosi film through Jung: Dracula is Mina's Shadow archetype and animus, embodying her repressed fear of sexuality and of the married life she claims to want, while the vampire's presence in every culture places him in the collective unconscious.
