dialectic-of-sex.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
dialectic-of-sex.title: 6 Wives and Husbands The Marital Power Struggle
dialectic-of-sex.relation: Taking Susan Okin's 'the personal is political' and Kate Millett's Weberian herrschaft against Locke's public/private dichotomy, the chapter reviews the empirical studies of marital power (Blood and Wolfe, Blumstein and Schwarz, Steil) and finds money is the master base in marriage: the husband's income and occupational prestige set his say, working wives gain power but couples conspire to understate wives' earnings ('manning up and womaning down'), while knowledge and status are the next strongest resources. Authority from religion, tradition and morality still favors husbands (Ephesians' 'wives submit yourselves unto your husbands' alongside the philosophers' 'abler and stronger'), violence persists from the rule of thumb to marital rape and murder despite legal change, housework remains women's burden - Beauvoir's never-won 'battle against dust', Engels's 'leaden boredom', Davis's industrialization proposal and Okin's demand that it be shared - and sex itself works as a power base in the bedroom, with MacKinnon diagnosing heterosexuality as the linchpin of gender inequality. The chapter ends with black couples' comparatively egalitarian patterns traced by Angela Davis to slave-quarters equality, Schwarz's rare 'peer marriages', and the Marxist (Okin, the Swedish model) versus liberal (Wilson, the Japanese model) readings of family change.

dialectic-of-sex.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
dialectic-of-sex.title: This Is the Version of Myself I Have to Be
dialectic-of-sex.relation: Pérez reads Yennefer's arc through a plurality of feminisms rather than one: Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, woman' explains her sacrifice of fertility at Aretuza and later choice of motherhood on her own terms, while Butler's performativity recasts Tissaia's mirror exercises as the enactment of a socially constructed sorceress role. Naomi Wolf's Beauty Myth and Iron Maiden expose her transformation as self-imposed captivity, Ruddick's maternal thinking marks the moment she truly becomes Ciri's mother, and Firestone's call to abolish sex distinction frames her infertility-for-power bargain. Finally Crenshaw's intersectionality and Lorde's 'master's tools' show that Yennefer's quarter-elf passing lets her beat the Brotherhood at its own game without dismantling it.

uncanny-valley.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
uncanny-valley.title: 8. I Sure Feel Uncomfortable Being in This Situation with You
uncanny-valley.relation: Argues Twin Peaks' signature effect is engineered discomfort at the borders of genre and perception: it straddles melodrama and cringe comedy (Sarah Palmer's breakdown being over-the-top yet unfunny because genuinely pained; Nadine and the Log Lady shifting from ridicule to empathy), and its ambiguously diegetic Badalamenti score — stopping when a character switches off the record player — works like Brecht's estrangement effect to block full immersion. A "behavioral uncanny valley" (the Man from Another Place, the Giant, Cooper chewing gum mid-murder-discussion as bathos) makes ordinary townsfolk seem like nonhumans impersonating people, so that the show's real horror is not answers but uncertainty — the threat that the world is not and never was what it seems.

uncanny-valley.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
uncanny-valley.title: Buddha ex Machina
uncanny-valley.relation: Lyons applies Masahiro Mori's uncanny valley to the hosts, whose near-human faces and movements turn initial revulsion into empathy — doubling it because the hosts suffer under programming humans would resist. She then argues, through Aristotle's virtue and vice and Nietzsche's discipline of great suffering, that hosts like Maeve (returning for her daughter) and Dolores ('I choose to see the beauty') display more 'human excellence' than the guests: Logan's hand-stabbing cruelty is mere vice and the Man in Black's scalping sadism falls under Aristotle's bestial. Humanity, she concludes, is a way of behaving rather than a way of being, and Mori's hope that robots may carry buddha-nature completes the title's reversal of machine and god.

uncanny-valley.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
uncanny-valley.title: Notes
uncanny-valley.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

moral-particularism.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
moral-particularism.title: 9. Send The Good Place to the Bad Place
moral-particularism.relation: Sheldon argues the Season One twist makes the show itself a moral paradox: a series about ethics that lies to its audience for thirteen episodes, breaking the informal contract it built through 'truth in fiction'. Through Chidi's red-cowboy-boots lie and Eleanor's plot to murder Janet, 'The Eternal Shriek' stages Kant's absolute prohibition on lying against Eleanor's Machiavellian ends-justify-means reasoning, with confession portrayed as the only release from escalating deception. The chapter ends with Eleanor citing Jonathan Dancy's moral particularism to get Chidi to lie his way through the Bad Place, leaving viewers to decide whether the show's own deception is justified by the ethical conversation it forces.

moral-particularism.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
moral-particularism.title: 10. A Love Story between Theory and Praxis
moral-particularism.relation: Altmann allegorizes Chidi as Theory and Eleanor as Praxis, whose 'love story' shows each completing the other: Chidi's lessons in utilitarianism and Kant's Categorical Imperative give Eleanor reasons, and eventually a lived example in Michael's feigned self-sacrifice, to confess her lie, while Eleanor's pragmatism in the Bad Place teaches Chidi that principles useless in the world must be revised. Michael's arc from designing psychological torture to giving Eleanor his portal pin demonstrates a theory of human nature, that people cannot change, being falsified by praxis. The chapter closes with Eleanor re-entering the cycle by finding Chidi's lectures online, recommending the union of theory and praxis as how anyone becomes a better person.

moral-particularism.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
moral-particularism.title: 11. Those Agonizing Choices
moral-particularism.relation: Romanowski traces Chidi's indecision from the cowboy-boots lie through the rock-paper-scissors panic attack, arguing the show treats the agony of deciding as the universal human moral condition rather than a professor joke. 'The Trolley Problem' makes Foot's dilemma literal torture, and the show pointedly never gives the right answer, confirming Chidi's claim that there are no clean solutions to hard moral questions. Eleanor's Dancy-inspired particularism pitch in 'Rhonda, Diana, Jake, and Trent' and Michael's 'I solved the Trolley Problem: you sacrifice yourself' moment, together with Chidi finally kissing Eleanor, show that acknowledging uncertainty is no excuse for inaction.

moral-particularism.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
moral-particularism.title: 9. Send The Good Place to the Bad Place
moral-particularism.relation: Asks whether a show about ethics may lie to its audience for a whole season: the Season One twist breaks the viewer's implicit contract even though the show keeps its internal 'truth in fiction'. Through 'The Eternal Shriek' it stages the debate — Chidi's Kantian ban on lying (the red cowboy boots saga with Henry, ending in a confession that defeats Henry) against Eleanor's Machiavellian ends-justify-means plot to 'kill' Janet — and reads the show's cascade of confessions as its answer that truth-telling absolves. Eleanor citing Jonathan Dancy's moral particularism in 'Rhonda, Diana, Jake, and Trent' lets Chidi lie his way through Hell, leaving viewers to decide whether the twist's ethical education justifies the deception.

moral-particularism.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
moral-particularism.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
moral-particularism.relation: Terjesen asks how Sinestro and Universo ever passed recruitment and answers that the Guardians' two-prong test of honesty and fearlessness reflects moral pluralism: universal rules kept deliberately thin so that different moral codes can coexist, which is why the vicious 'good bad man' Jack T. Chance keeps his ring on Hellhole. But honor, honesty, and justice are thick ethical concepts in Bernard Williams's sense, requiring cultural context to apply, so Laira's execution of a surrendered Amon Sur and the Guardians' own cover-ups (the Corpse, Kentor Omoto) cannot be settled by appealing to thin 'justice,' and the Alpha Lanterns' internal-affairs role cannot fix it. Moral particularism leaves the Corps with unresolvable disagreements about who the bad apples are.

aspect-perception.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
aspect-perception.title: 23. Where Thanos Got Lost
aspect-perception.relation: Diagnoses where Thanos 'got lost' via Wittgenstein's aspect perception (the duck-rabbit, the Thanos-chin-as-panini memes): morality concerns not just choosing but seeing, and Thanos's impoverished worldview — shaped by a lifetime of rejection, drawn from the novel Thanos: Titan Consumed — lets him see life only as 'the condition of living things,' never as 'the existence of individuals,' so erasing half of all individuals strikes him as a moral act. His single-minded reading of Titan's collapse becomes confirmation bias ('I'm the only one who knows that'), and his final plan to erase everything proves he never saw the individual-existence aspect at all: his starting point, not his reasoning, is missing information.

aspect-perception.title: Seeing Soldiers, Seeing Persons Wittgenstein, Film Theory, and Charlie Chaplin’s Shoulder Arms
aspect-perception.relation: Hilsabeck argues that Wittgenstein's notion of aspect perception ("seeing as") is not a phenomenology of illusion, as film theorists like Allen and Turvey take it, but an ethical matter of articulating experience within forms of life and language games. He reads Chaplin's Shoulder Arms through this lens: Doughboy's tree-disguise gag and his repurposing of war objects (Limburger cheese as grenade, gramophone horn as snorkel) demonstrate imaginative, ethical vision, while the German soldier who cannot see the tree-as-man exhibits "aspect blindness." The film makes viewers' willingness to "see anew" a test of attunement and mutual acknowledgment, casting the environment of WWI trench warfare and mechanized shock as what stifles this imaginative seeing.

aspect-perception.title: 28_LaRocca_Chapter_027.html
aspect-perception.relation: Hagberg argues that Grant Gee's documentary Patience (After Sebald) achieves a truthful portrait of W. G. Sebald not by static correspondence but by enacting his shifting, connection-making sensibility, as displayed in The Rings of Saturn. He deploys Wittgenstein's remarks on aspect-perception and 'seeing-as' (the duck-rabbit, the 'lighting up of an aspect') to show that perception is always already inflected by imagination, memory and language-games, dismantling the empiricist picture of Locke, Hume and Berkeley in which brute sensation precedes reflection. Borges's 'The Garden of Forking Paths' and 'Tlon, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius' supply the model of a Heraclitean flux of forking, mind-dependent connections, and the film's darkroom-like fading images and layered soundtrack are read as mimetically faithful to how a human sensibility perceives and remembers.

stakeholder-theory.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
stakeholder-theory.title: This is Rumor Control. Here are the Facts!
stakeholder-theory.relation: Uses the Weyland corporations' treatment of crews - Special Order 937, Vickers's 'that makes you an employee,' Burke's Facehugger scheme, the debriefing that mourns a $42 million ship but never the crew - to pit stockholder theory (Friedman, Berle) against libertarian contract theory (Machan) and stakeholder theory (Freeman). The libertarian middle way fails because in deep space crews have neither Hirschman's exit nor voice, so only stakeholder theory explains why hiding workplace hazards and marking employees expendable wrongs them; the market's invisible hand behaves like Ash's very visible murdering hand.

stakeholder-theory.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
stakeholder-theory.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
stakeholder-theory.relation: Audits the Bluth Company's 'Family First' creed against theories of corporate social responsibility, the shareholder-profit model it actually follows versus the stakeholder model of Johnson & Johnson's credo. Evidence includes the Cornballer that burns everyone yet sells in Mexico, the sinking model home and the two-week fake house built 'not good, just looking good', child labor at the banana stand, Boyfights, unpaid construction crews, and the Iraq homes built for Saddam as a CIA wiretapping scheme. The chapter concludes that Family First only arrests the company's moral development, a manual for how not to run a business.

stakeholder-theory.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
stakeholder-theory.title: The Office and Philosophy
stakeholder-theory.relation: Kraft uses Dunder Mifflin to test whether stockholder profit or stakeholder welfare should drive business decisions, introducing stakeholder theory via Ansoff and the Mitchell salience model. Michael's exclusive patronage of national chains (Chili's, Starbucks, USA Today) versus the staff's loyalty to local spots like Poor Richard's becomes a Millian case: by Mill's point that most good action benefits particular individuals, shopping locally spreads happiness through the Scranton community while Michael's habits export money and decision-making elsewhere. Dwight oscillates between stockholder logic (the cheapest health plan, poaching Jim's client in 'Diversity Day') and stakeholder-minded customer service, while 'Halloween,' 'Health Care,' and 'Branch Closing' show profit trumping people; Michael's successful sale to Christian at Chili's in 'The Client' balances both, and his 'Show me that farm' speech insists workers like Stanley and Phyllis are not replaceable cogs.

mencius-good-nature.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
mencius-good-nature.title: Every Soul Experiences the Battle Within
mencius-good-nature.relation: Reads Zuko's arc as a war between Legalism and Confucianism: Ozai's agni kai scarring of his son, Azulon's death sentence, the Fire Nation Oath and school discipline ('The Headband') all enact Han Fei's principle that bad human nature needs terrifying sanctions, and Azula's 'trust is for fools' completes it. Against this stands Iroh's Confucian education in ren — teaching that honor cannot be separated from humaneness, that a mugger deserves tea and encouragement, and that wu-wei-like patience knows when to speak. Mencius's innate compassion explains why Zuko's 'amazing lie' realization could unfold, Katara, Sokka, and Hakoda embody Confucian filial bonds that adopt Aang, Toph, and finally Zuko, and Solzhenitsyn's gulag insight closes the chapter: the line between good and evil runs through every human heart.

mencius-good-nature.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
mencius-good-nature.title: Every Soul Experiences the Battle Within
mencius-good-nature.relation: Reads the Fire Nation royal family as a philosophical battle between Legalism (Han Fei, taking Xunzi's dictum that human nature is evil, so order requires terrifying sanctions: Ozai burning Zuko in the agni kai so 'suffering will be your teacher', Azulon's death sentence on Zuko, the Fire Nation Oath recited in schools) and Confucianism (Iroh teaching ren, that true honor cannot be had apart from humaneness, preferring honorable begging over theft, and talking a would-be mugger into tea). Zuko's 'battle within' is the legacy of his two great-grandfathers, Sozin's Legalism versus Roku's line, and it is resolved when he disowns Ozai, calls Iroh his 'real father', and is adopted into Team Avatar, whose filial bonds (Katara's care, Hakoda's sacrifice) contrast with the scheming royal family. The chapter closes with Solzhenitsyn's image of the line between good and evil passing through every human heart to explain why Zuko's inner war resonates.

mencius-good-nature.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
mencius-good-nature.title: The Rhythm by Which We Live Our Lives
mencius-good-nature.relation: Kowalski interprets Kuzco's arc through Mencius: the emperor's pampered upbringing (eight hands replacing a squeezed toy, Yzma's loveless regency) is the 'hatchets and frost' of the Ox Mountain parable blunting his innate moral sprouts. The gorge scene stages Mencius's child-at-the-well thought experiment — Kuzco's spontaneous snatch of falling Pacha is a 'give-away' action betraying compassion he denies having, which Pacha diagnoses just as Mencius did King Xuan sparing the ox — and Pacha's family, quasi-adopting Kuzco, supplies the loving soil Mencius says the sprouts of ren need to grow.

mencius-good-nature.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
mencius-good-nature.title: NOTES
mencius-good-nature.relation: The Terjesens pit Kant's impersonal morality — Sam's contractual distance from the thieving Mickens is exactly how he would treat strangers — against Confucius and Mencius, for whom filial duties are the nursery of virtue: we learn benevolence by serving parents and revering elders, Lafayette's care for Lettie Mae and Tara shows family forming moral character, and the Upright Gong's covering for a father's sheep-stealing grounds Jason's 'sometimes the right thing to do is the wrong thing'. Mencius's King Shun, who abdicates and carries his criminal father into exile, models how Tommy and Jason should put family first while accepting the cost, while Mozi's universal love surfaces in Godric's 'forgiveness is love', and the chapter concludes that family counts only insofar as it develops our moral nature — the line between Tommy and Sam.

mencius-good-nature.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
mencius-good-nature.relation: Bush argues that Brokeback Mountain transcends both the heterosexual western archetype and queer theory by presenting male sexuality through Mencius' philosophy and John Corvino's ethics of homosexuality. Using Mencius' four sprouts (ren, li, yi, zhi) and doctrine of natural goodness, he reads Ennis as the character in whom sexuality is contextual, cultivated and moral rather than merely physical, so the relationship between Ennis and Jack becomes an ethical friendship grounded in ren, the virtue Mencius says is most intense among friends. The bystanders Aguirre and Alma keeping the secret, and the final shirt-and-postcard scene, illustrate zhi as contextual moral judgment and homosexuality reframed as ethical rather than sexual.

mencius-good-nature.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
mencius-good-nature.relation: Dull reads Eat Drink Man Woman through a Hall-and-Ames 'focus-field' model of personhood, analyzing harmony via metaphors of a culinary dish, music and a sports team where each element keeps its integrity within a whole. He diagnoses the Chu family by pairing Mencius (morality as expression of the four sprouts) against Xunzi (desire must be structured by ritual): Chef Chu is 'repressed as a turtle', Jia-Jen hides behind ritual, Jia-Ning acts on impulse, and Jia-Chien lacks direction. Their romantic transformations restore harmony, answering Chu's question 'is there more than food and sex?' affirmatively, as expression, desire and ritual come into balance and his sense of taste returns.

xunzi-bad-nature.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
xunzi-bad-nature.title: Every Soul Experiences the Battle Within
xunzi-bad-nature.relation: Reads Zuko's arc as a war between Legalism and Confucianism: Ozai's agni kai scarring of his son, Azulon's death sentence, the Fire Nation Oath and school discipline ('The Headband') all enact Han Fei's principle that bad human nature needs terrifying sanctions, and Azula's 'trust is for fools' completes it. xunzi-bad-nature.title: Every Soul Experiences the Battle Within
xunzi-bad-nature.relation: Reads the Fire Nation royal family as a philosophical battle between Legalism (Han Fei, taking Xunzi's dictum that human nature is evil, so order requires terrifying sanctions: Ozai burning Zuko in the agni kai so 'suffering will be your teacher', Azulon's death sentence on Zuko, the Fire Nation Oath recited in schools) and Confucianism (Iroh teaching ren, that true honor cannot be had apart from humaneness, preferring honorable begging over theft, and talking a would-be mugger into tea). xunzi-bad-nature.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
xunzi-bad-nature.title: Notes
xunzi-bad-nature.relation: Curry and Lang test 'War never changes' through Hobbes and Xunzi: the wasteland - where the Ghoul asks who ever elected the 'President' in 'The Trap' and Cooper Howard decays outside all political order - is Hobbes's state of nature of restless power-seeking, while Xunzi's claim that bad human nature needs ritual (li) and righteousness (yi) explains a world with no moral education, where Elder Cleric Quintus pairs noble talk with 'power is taken, not given'. Fallout's Great War then fails every just-war test: China's invasion of Alaska stretches just cause, the corporatist US lacks right authority, propaganda undid last resort, mutually assured destruction explodes proportionality, and Vault-Tec shelters plus battlefield mini-nukes breach discrimination and proportionality in bello - with Operation Anchorage's propaganda simulation illustrating the revisionist point that fighting cleanly cannot redeem an unjust war. China's 'righteous army' (yi bing) tradition - Sunzi's strategic restraint, Mohist defensive war, Mengzi's true king, Xunzi's punitive righteous war - leaves no trace beyond Captain Zao, so the war's constancy marks the failure of every philosophical attempt to bind war to justice.

xunzi-bad-nature.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
xunzi-bad-nature.relation: Thompson argues that Lee's 'cowboy aesthetic' of rugged isolation in Brokeback Mountain (Ennis and Jack) and Crouching Tiger (Li Mu Bai, Shu Lien, Jen) is only apparent: the characters are always already embedded in Confucius' five cardinal relationships, read through Xunzi's darker view that selfish desire must be curbed by ritual and social hierarchy. Ennis and Jack seem lone individuals but are defined by ties to Alma, family and each other, and Jen's redemption comes when she abandons self-serving desire to re-establish her Confucian relationships. Citing Nietzsche's gloss on Aristotle that only a beast or a god lives alone, it concludes there is no truly isolated cowboy.

xunzi-bad-nature.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
xunzi-bad-nature.relation: Dull reads Eat Drink Man Woman through a Hall-and-Ames 'focus-field' model of personhood, analyzing harmony via metaphors of a culinary dish, music and a sports team where each element keeps its integrity within a whole. He diagnoses the Chu family by pairing Mencius (morality as expression of the four sprouts) against Xunzi (desire must be structured by ritual): Chef Chu is 'repressed as a turtle', Jia-Jen hides behind ritual, Jia-Ning acts on impulse, and Jia-Chien lacks direction. Their romantic transformations restore harmony, answering Chu's question 'is there more than food and sex?' affirmatively, as expression, desire and ritual come into balance and his sense of taste returns.

moral-dilemmas.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
moral-dilemmas.title: Overcoming Dilemmas
moral-dilemmas.relation: Frames Aang's dilemma — Avataric duty to stop Ozai by killing versus Air Nomad sanctity of life — as a genuine dilemma only if both duties are non-negotiable, using W.D. Ross and Lisa Tessman's negotiable/non-negotiable duty framework. Air Nomad philosophy is reconstructed as Sublime Ahimsic Practice: the Four Sublime States (loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity) plus ahimsa, grounded in the Buddha's dependent origination that Huu's banyan-grove swamp vision also expresses, which makes everyone 'worth giving a chance'. Because this practice keeps Aang open to the world, he meets the Lion Turtle and learns energybending, so the dilemma's conditions are reshaped rather than solved — the same lesson Gandhi, Martin Luther King Jr., and Black Lives Matter teach about nonviolent liberation.

moral-dilemmas.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
moral-dilemmas.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
moral-dilemmas.relation: Tallman and Southworth set the Hippocratic Oath against the Green Lantern oath in Soranik Natu, a Korugarian surgeon who must either stop healing mid-battle or disobey the Book of Oa. They survey the options, with Wonder Woman discarding vows for consequences, Isamot Kol letting the Corps trump his vow to Qalyra, Dr. Mid-Nite always putting patients first, and Dick Grayson going by context, then argue through Hursthouse that Natu, who treats both oaths as absolute, is in an irresolvable dilemma of her own making, more like the double-betrothed man than Williams's tragic Jim and the twenty Indians. Their verdict is that she should turn in the ring, a cautionary tale for real military medics whose oaths also collide.

moral-dilemmas.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
moral-dilemmas.title: The Hero’s Responsibility
moral-dilemmas.relation: White defends Tony against blame for Captain America's assassination: spearheading registration in Civil War was a tragic dilemma, and Tony took the least bad option because 'if not me, who?' — telling Cap's corpse he sacrificed their friendship to save lives. Cap's death traces through Crossbones, the mind-controlled Sharon Carter, Dr. Faustus, and the Red Skull, not any direct act of Tony's; without foreseeability or wrongdoing, the chain of 'might haves' does not add up to responsibility, just as pushing someone out of a truck's path does not make you liable for the manhole they fall into. The motivation-centered lens of Kantian deontology and Aristotelian virtue ethics supports Tony (he gave up status, friends, and Cap himself), and living with tragic choices, as he does facing the Hulk, is itself heroic.

moral-dilemmas.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
moral-dilemmas.title: The Witcher's Code
moral-dilemmas.relation: Barta and Lee ask whether Geralt's quandaries are genuine conflicts of incommensurable duties or only apparent ones. An Idr-baiting variant of Foot and Thomson's trolley problem opens the analysis; the Blaviken conflict between Renfri and Stregobor, Nivellen and the bruxa Vereena, and the djinn's three wishes are read through Bernard Williams's view that tragic, remainder-generating conflicts are ineliminable, with Sartre's student example and Nietzsche's 'antagonism in the heart of the world' backing the tragic reading. Against this, the Striga-Adda curse and the contradictory duel commands of Sir Tailles show dilemmas dissolved by culpable origins, third options, or one duty overriding another, and the chapter concludes Geralt wisely treats every dilemma as if it were apparent.

moral-dilemmas.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
moral-dilemmas.title: Lesser of Two Evils
moral-dilemmas.relation: Horn reads the Blaviken conflict as a clash of two utilitarianisms: Stregobor locks up women born during the black sun on Benthamite grounds that maximizing humanity's happiness justifies evil, while Renfri's revenge on Stregobor follows Popper's negative utilitarianism of minimizing suffering, and Foot's runaway trolley shows both reasoning toward killing the one. Le Guin's Omelas, with its tortured child beneath a utopia, exposes where Stregobor's and Renfri's 'lesser evil' logic leads. Geralt rejects both because he deliberates as Raff Donelson's ethical pragmatist: he accepts the facts but tests options against the shared Witcher's Code values (kill only to save, never from fear), which is why he prefers not to choose at all.

moral-dilemmas.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
moral-dilemmas.title: Silver or Steel?
moral-dilemmas.relation: Williams and Shump contrast Witcher 3's choice design with the illusory agency of immersive sims like BioShock, where the 'Would you kindly?' twist funnels players to one canonical good ending. In White Orchard's 'On Death's Bed' the witcher potion that saves Lena melts her mind, the succubus Salma in 'Deadly Delights' may be spared as a rational being who killed in self-defense, and Keira Metz's fate at Radovid's hands or Kaer Morhen topples dominoes that reach Lambert, so that good intentions yield random or grim outcomes. Drawing silver for monsters and steel for humans becomes the chapter's metaphor: every drawn sword is a classification that may condemn the wrong target, in a world where 'good' and 'bad' are relative points on an unpredictable spectrum.

moral-dilemmas.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
moral-dilemmas.title: III - IS SUICIDE ALWAYS IMMORAL JEAN GREY, IMMANUELKANT, AND THE DARK PHOENIX SAGA
moral-dilemmas.relation: White asks whether Jean Grey's suicide at the end of The Dark Phoenix Saga can be moral. After finding virtue ethics mostly hostile and utilitarianism hostage to circumstances, he turns to Kant: the categorical imperative's formulas condemn suicide as using one's person as a mere means, yet Kant's own Metaphysics of Morals concedes a case, a man bitten by a mad dog who kills himself before his madness can harm others, that maps exactly onto possession by the Phoenix Force. Drawing on Thomas E. Hill Jr.'s Kantian account of suicide as a final autonomous act, he reads Jean's dialogue with Scott as her choosing death as the author of her life story, preserving her autonomy rather than letting Dark Phoenix kill five billion more people.

moral-dilemmas.title: Exploring The Cabin in the Woods
moral-dilemmas.relation: The chapter reads The Cabin in the Woods as Whedon and Goddard doing philosophy: the facility's ritual sacrifice of the five campers is given an explicit utilitarian defense (quoting Mill's greatest-happiness principle) through the Director's plea that Dana kill Marty to avert the apocalypse, which the film ultimately counters through the friends' care-based obligations. Drawing on Nel Noddings's ethics of care and Aristotle's claim that the severity of our duties varies with the closeness of relationships — and on Whedonverse parallels like Buffy refusing to sacrifice Dawn in 'The Gift' — it recasts the ending as an implicit counterargument to classic utilitarianism: Dana does nothing impermissible by refusing to murder her friend, so utilitarianism is false, while Dana's genuine dilemma is deliberately left unresolved in Socratic aporia. It then extends the ethics of care into a theory of the horror genre, reading Whedon's 'inoculation against real fear' as an Aristotelian catharsis that requires relatable characters who care for one another, and takes the film's monitors, two-way mirrors, and voyeurism scenes (Hadley's callousness, the control-room ogling of Jules) as a metalevel invitation to audit our own desensitization to pointless screen suffering.

birdcage-oppression.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
birdcage-oppression.title: “Smother Him in the Crib”—Booker
birdcage-oppression.relation: Origitano reads Elizabeth through Beauvoir and Frye: Columbia's propaganda infantilizes and objectifies her ('the Seed of the Prophet', 'Lamb', 'Specimen', always defined relative to a man), the tower literalizes Frye's birdcage of systematic oppression, and her confinement for an uncontrollable power mirrors women caged by a supposed natural inferiority. Booker's rescue only grants freedom, echoing Beauvoir's point that women have 'only received' what men are willing to give, so Elizabeth remains caged as his poker chip, her lock-picking skills formed by captivity and her tears dismissed as foreign. Her emancipation comes through action and collective solidarity, allying with Lady Comstock's ghost, taking control of Songbird, and finally drowning Booker/Comstock as equals, which enacts Beauvoir's claim that liberation must be won, not granted.

bergson-elan-vital.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
bergson-elan-vital.title: Only Time Will Tell
bergson-elan-vital.relation: Latta reads the film through Bergson's distinction between clock time and duration: Strange is introduced as pure quantitative multiplicity — identifying Chuck Mangione's 'Feels So Good' (1977) mid-surgery, surrounding himself with watches, including Christine Palmer's inscribed 'Time will tell how much I love you' — while the Ancient One lives duration, surrendering to the river's current. Kaecilius embodies 'chronological nihilism' ('time is an insult'), and his and Dormammu's timeless Dark Dimension is existentially impossible for Bergson, since life only progresses and endures in time. The climax shows Strange recreating the present in the endless looped bargain with Dormammu ('pain is an old friend'), growing through qualitative multiplicity and élan vital, until the shattered watch — hands broken, inscription intact — marks his conversion from counting time to living it.

bergson-elan-vital.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
bergson-elan-vital.title: 33. 2001 as Philosophy A Technological Odyssey
bergson-elan-vital.relation: Abrams argues that Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey dramatizes Henri Bergson's Creative Evolution and Two Sources of Morality and Religion better than Nietzsche's Zarathustra: the monolith turning Moonwatcher's bone into a tool makes humanity Homo faber, and the match-cut from bone to satellite traces one technological odyssey toward species self-transformation. He reads the HAL 9000's murderous breakdown through Turing's imitation game—Hal passes the Turing Test and inverts it by testing Frank at chess and probing Dave—and casts Dave as a new Odysseus dousing HAL the Cyclops. The star child is Bergson's vision of the universe as 'a machine for making gods,' the Nietzschean overman realized through Bergsonian creative and technological evolution, with Aristotle's mimesis grounding the film's account of imitation and its own cinematic self-reflection.

addams-settlement.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
addams-settlement.title: Notes
addams-settlement.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

sorites-paradox.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
sorites-paradox.title: Francis Griffin and the Church of the Holy Fonz: Religious Exclusivism and Real Religion
sorites-paradox.relation: Johnson argues that Francis Griffin's Catholic exclusivism (condemning Lois the Protestant to purgatory, calling Meg a harlot, founding Peter's Church of the Holy Fonz an 'abomination') is unjustified and immoral. Using Plantinga on exclusivism and a Quagmire-style inductive argument ('SHiTE' — Scripture, Historical tradition, religious Experience — leads rival religions to incompatible truths, so it is an unreliable witness like Quagmire's false alibis), he holds that no one's religious beliefs are adequately justified. Weighing Clifford's ethics of belief (the unseaworthy ship) against James's will to believe, he concludes one may hold beliefs without evidence but may not harm others or forcibly evangelize on their basis. The heap/sorites puzzle shows no criterion marks Fonzieism as an 'unreal' religion — Peter's founding experience parallels Joseph Smith's — so the moral is religious acceptance: disagree freely, but keep your SHiTE to yourself.

maternal-thinking.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
maternal-thinking.title: Lois: Portrait of a Mother (Or, Nevermind Death, Motherhood is a Bitch)
maternal-thinking.relation: Empey frames mothering (following Sara Ruddick's 'Maternal Thinking') as a disciplined response to a child's demands of preservation, growth, and social acceptability — even for a matricidal psychopath like Stewie. Lois cultivates the virtues of prudence (safeguarding the Rainy Day Fund against Peter's volcano insurance), tolerance, and peacefulness (enduring Stewie's lamp blows and Peter's laziness; her two Christmas and 'Lethal Weapons' violent eruptions are cured by appeals to her motherhood). The chapter then turns political: drawing on Okin, Williams, and Hays, it shows mothers' vulnerability by marriage, the incompatibility of the 'ideal worker' and 'intensive mother' models, and Peter's devaluing of Lois's theater directing. Peter's basement bar, where Lois sings nightly while minding the kids, models the institutional coordination (family plus economy) mothers need — until Peter's jealousy wrecks it.

maternal-thinking.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
maternal-thinking.title: This Is the Version of Myself I Have to Be
maternal-thinking.relation: Pérez reads Yennefer's arc through a plurality of feminisms rather than one: Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, woman' explains her sacrifice of fertility at Aretuza and later choice of motherhood on her own terms, while Butler's performativity recasts Tissaia's mirror exercises as the enactment of a socially constructed sorceress role. Naomi Wolf's Beauty Myth and Iron Maiden expose her transformation as self-imposed captivity, Ruddick's maternal thinking marks the moment she truly becomes Ciri's mother, and Firestone's call to abolish sex distinction frames her infertility-for-power bargain. Finally Crenshaw's intersectionality and Lorde's 'master's tools' show that Yennefer's quarter-elf passing lets her beat the Brotherhood at its own game without dismantling it.

original-sin.book: 161 - Family Guy and Philosophy - A Cure for the Petarded
original-sin.title: Mmmyez: Stewie and the Seven Deadly Sins
original-sin.relation: Kaye argues Stewie is funny because he portrays a truth we repress: Augustine's doctrine of original sin (defended as the only answer to why God lets the innocent suffer, and grounded in the pear-tree and jealous-infant episodes of the Confessions) — no one is innocent, not even babies. Systematically cataloging Stewie through Aquinas's Seven Deadly Sins, she shows lust (the Rupert-the-gay-teddy-bear projection, 'wee-wee stricken with rigor mortis', inverting Freud's Oedipal complex since Stewie hates his mother and barely tolerates his father), gluttony (hoarding Lois's breast milk, an orgy of fig newtons), sloth as Aquinas's 'oppressive sorrow' and malicious indignation ('Why don't you burn in hell?'), avarice, anger as revenge (bombs and graham crackers), envy (locking Jeremy in the car trunk), and pride, the Queen of Vices — Stewie's god complex ('Omnipotence. Gotta get me some of that'). Stewie's lone possibly-decent moment (warning Brian not to mock upside-down Jake Tucker's face) is left as the one loose thread.

tillich-ground-of-being.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
tillich-ground-of-being.title: Risks of Faith
tillich-ground-of-being.relation: Christophe Ringer uses Alfred Schutz's social phenomenology — perception versus apperception illustrated with a super-glued coffee cup, 'paramount reality' as the everyday world of pragmatic motives, and 'in order to' and 'because of' motives — to explain how the film's dream-share works: Ariadne and Fischer betray that they are dreaming because they cannot remember how they arrived, and Mr. Charles's room-number gambit manufactures a 'because of' motive inside Fischer's own dream. He then brings in Paul Tillich's distinction between mere belief and faith as 'ultimate concern': the totem becomes a sacred, untouchable object of revelation, while Mal — who locks hers in the safe and says 'choose me' — commits idolatry by treating a preliminary world as ultimate, her suicide the tragic act of misplaced faith. On this reading the world of everyday life, not the dream, is the film's ultimate reality, the Genesis-like shore where Cobb and Mal 'created a whole world' in which nothing they built could endure or accumulate meaning.

five-faces-oppression.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
five-faces-oppression.title: 5 Feminism and Indiana Jones A Field Guide
five-faces-oppression.relation: Kate Schmidt applies feminist media tests (Bechdel, sexy lamp, Mako Mori, Pierce, Landau) to show the films usually fail — Willie is a screaming prop and human shield in Temple, the eyelid-writing student exists only to display Indy's sex appeal, and all four films fail the Bechdel Test — while Marion, Spalko, and above all Elsa in The Last Crusade are mixed cases with partial autonomy. Drawing on Iris Marion Young's account of women as Other and Carol Gilligan's care ethics, she argues Crusade is the series' most feminist film not for its women but for its men: Indy's open hurt after Elsa's betrayal and the father-son reconciliation embody care ethics against 'boys don't cry' toxic masculinity. She concludes that one can love flawed media without endorsing its sexism.

five-faces-oppression.book: 213 - Tennis and Philosophy - What the Racket Is All About
five-faces-oppression.title: Arthur Ashe Philosopher in Motion
five-faces-oppression.relation: Inverting Clark Graebner's claim that Ashe's 'loose' play expressed his race, the chapter mines Arthur Ashe's life to test theories of race. It rejects racialism, then argues both major constructivisms fail: Charles Mills's materialist Racial Contract faces an 'assignment problem' because the privileged, successful Ashe eludes the material burdens that supposedly define blackness (Billie Jean King's 'I'm blacker than Arthur'), while Du Bois's narrative constructivism faces an 'authenticity problem' shown by South African students calling Ashe an Uncle Tom and his anguish over his daughter's white doll. Ashe's antiapartheid 'trade' in playing Johannesburg and his disciplined-yet-reckless character model a 'looseness' that treats race as a set of justice and identity projects, not a metaphysical thing.

five-faces-oppression.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
five-faces-oppression.title: 24. ReMENbering the Punk Movement
five-faces-oppression.relation: Georgina Mills argues that remembering punk through its men only - the British Library display naming the Sex Pistols, the Clash, and the Buzzcocks but no women - is more than the Matilda effect: it retroactively filters the whole movement through patriarchal norms. Using Iris Marion Young's concept of marginalization, she contends that as punk gained mainstream status the women who embodied its rebellion (the Slits banned from hotels on the White Riot tour, X-Ray Spex, Siouxsie) were pushed back to the margins of a movement they helped forge. Erasing them distorts punk itself, since women's twofold rebellion - against the establishment and against feminine compliance - and punk's DIY inclusivity were integral to it, as the misreading of Poly Styrene's 'Oh Bondage, Up Yours!' as mere shock shows.

five-faces-oppression.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
five-faces-oppression.relation: Bufacchi applies Fricker's testimonial and hermeneutical epistemic injustice to Austen's heroines, arguing women like Anne Elliot ('only Anne,' her word carrying no weight) and Elizabeth Bennet are denied credibility as knowers, while Mr. Collins's certainty that a woman's 'no' means 'yes' shows men's epistemic arrogance. He layers in Young's structural injustice to explain the Bennet women's economic vulnerability under entailment, then extends Fricker with his own 'Perpetuating Force of Epistemic Injustice': Emma Woodhouse, herself a victim, becomes a perpetrator by silencing Harriet Smith's love for the farmer Robert Martin, showing how the oppressed reproduce the injustice on those below them.

five-faces-oppression.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
five-faces-oppression.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
five-faces-oppression.relation: Owen argues that parenting is a political act and that fathers, especially privileged white heterosexual ones, should raise anti-oppressive children. Prompted by the question 'Daddy, why is her face brown?', he uses the social construction of racialized difference and the mutually constitutive culture–individual relation (the Zulu maxim 'a person is a person through other persons') to reject color-blindness. He prescribes knowledge, practice, and character steps, invokes Socrates' 'unexamined life' for relentless self-reflection, and answers the worry about raising 'alienated' children via Sartre's bad faith – authentic existence means accepting responsibility for reproducing or resisting injustice.

five-faces-oppression.book: 287 - Blues – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking Deep About Feeling Low
five-faces-oppression.title: BLUES
five-faces-oppression.relation: Meghan Winsby answers George Carlin's gibe that white people have nothing to be blue about by arguing that women — black or white — legitimately sing the blues because they share an experience of oppression. She applies Iris Marion Young's 'five faces of oppression' (exploitation, marginalization, powerlessness, cultural imperialism, violence) to women's silencing, sexual objectification, and gender exploitation, showing that early blueswomen (Ma Rainey, Bessie Smith, Memphis Minnie) and later ones (Bonnie Raitt) asserted sexuality and independence against a patriarchal order. She then weighs, without fully endorsing, the moral cultural-appropriation and audience-appropriation objections (via James O. Young) to white men playing the blues.

five-faces-oppression.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
five-faces-oppression.title: 90. From Hell as Philosophy Ripping Through Structural Violence
five-faces-oppression.relation: James and Mona Rocha argue that Moore and Campbell's From Hell links physical and structural violence under patriarchy: William Gull's Ripper murders of Whitechapel sex workers, and his premonition of the dull modern office ('the twentieth century, I have delivered it'), show how sensationalized physical violence pushes routine structural violence into the invisible background where it corrupts men morally (Gull and Abberline both lose their humanity). Using Galtung's structural violence and Crenshaw's intersectionality of poverty and gender, plus the male gaze in Gull's ghostly viewing of female workers, the chapter connects Victorian misogyny to present-day workplace sexual harassment.

montaigne-skepticism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
montaigne-skepticism.title: “You Like Me because I'm a Scoundrel”
montaigne-skepticism.relation: Decker asks whether Han Solo can truly evade philosophy, opening with Aristotle's Protrepticus proof that one must do philosophy either way. Han's demystifying skepticism ('no mystical energy field controls my destiny,' 'That's not how the Force works!') is paired with Wittgenstein's Tractatus, which dismisses traditional philosophical questions as senseless and offers therapy for the philosophical itch, and with Montaigne's skepticism about book learning — though Han's orphan scrumrat education exposes the class privilege behind Montaigne's 'sweet pillow' of ignorance. His anti-authoritarianism is read through Emerson (via Cornel West) and Rorty's pragmatism as anti-authoritarianism: build philosophical reflections around political hopes rather than foundations, which is why the 'everyday people' of the Disney+ era, epitomized by the scoundrel, break the spell of the Skywalker grand narrative.

pacifism.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
pacifism.title: The Last Jedi A New Hope
pacifism.relation: Johnson defends The Last Jedi's Luke against the 'you ruined Luke' charge: his pacifism was set up when he threw away his lightsaber before Palpatine in Return of the Jedi, and his call to end the Jedi follows the lesson Hobbes and Locke drew from the English civil wars - since religious matters cannot be settled by reason, only by violence, Jedi and Sith factions fighting for political power yield only bloodshed like the Clone Wars and two Death Stars. Luke also seeks to destroy the Jedi texts out of guilt by association for the Order's failures, and to the end he remains a consequentialist pacifist, defeating Kylo on Crait through a nonviolent Force projection rather than a real duel. Far from betraying the character, this growth into proactive nonviolence - capped by Rey's yellow-bladed, mainly defensive style - makes Luke 'the ultimate Jedi' and the Resistance's new hope.

pacifism.title: The Philosophy of Ang Lee
pacifism.relation: Zietsma reads Hulk and Taking Woodstock as antiwar films that subvert the hegemonic culture of heroic violence, fitting Lackey's category of universal (Gandhian/early-Christian) pacifism. He argues both films disturb their genre's expected narrative and demasculinize the hero: Elliot the gay nonviolent hero and the transgender vet Vilma, and a weeping Hulk who is rescued by Betty and finally gives up his power rather than kill David Banner. He reads the bathroom-mirror 'Puny human' scene as an inverted Lacanian mirror stage unmasking America's violent militarism, framing the Vietnam War and war on terror as violence that only begets more violence.

pacifism.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
pacifism.title: 14. The Doctor as Philosopher The Collectivist-Realist Pacifism of the Doctor and the Quest for Social Justice
pacifism.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a 'collectivist-realist pacifist': morally opposed to war yet willing, as a last resort, to use lethal force for social justice. She places the Doctor on Cady's warism-to-pacifism continuum (past absolute and collectivist pacifism), augmenting it with Martin Luther King Jr.'s realist pacifism — ethical appeals 'undergirded by constructive coercive power' — and Gandhi's ahimsa and belief that no one is beyond redemption (the Doctor sparing Davros, offering enemies a choice). She tests Kant's duty ethics and respect for persons (Rule 1: the Doctor lies), Ross's prima facie duties, Mill's utilitarianism ('The Fires of Pompeii,' 'The Beast Below'), Gilligan/Noddings care ethics, and Wolterstorff's 'life of needs,' and reads 'The Day of the Doctor' as a Rawlsian veil of ignorance brokering Zygon-human peace.

reputation.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
reputation.title: Taylor Swift's Philosophy of Reputation
reputation.relation: Catherine Robb and Roos Slegers reconstruct a philosophy of reputation from the reputation album: with Sperber, Baumard, and Origgi, reputation is a shared group consensus ('they say I did something bad') that is fake, warped, and outside one's control, yet Adam Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments explains why it still wounds - we deeply want not only to be loved but to be lovely, seen for who we really are (the invisible dance through the streets in 'Delicate'). The chapter's original contribution is Swift's 'tilted stage,' performed literally on the reputation tour: gendered double standards ('The Man,' 'mad woman') mean a woman's reputation is more fake, more imposed, and more punishing than a man's.

repetition-and-difference.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
repetition-and-difference.title: Begin Again (Taylor's Version): On Taylor Swift's Repetition and Difference
repetition-and-difference.relation: King-Ho Leung casts Swift as a philosopher of repetition, using Kierkegaard's distinction between backward-looking recollection and forward-moving repetition to show that 'Back to December' is not reliving the past but rewriting it ('turn around and change my own mind ... make it alright'), and that tiny lyric changes ('I bet' becoming 'I hope' in 'I Almost Do') make repetition produce the difference. With Deleuze's Difference and Repetition, the chapter argues the 'Taylor's Versions' rerecordings are not inferior copies of lost originals but repetitions that generate newness - like 'Love Story' giving Romeo and Juliet a happy ending - so that rerecording becomes an act of self-reinvention and reclaimed ownership rather than mere restoration.

archive-fever.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
archive-fever.title: I Remember It All Too Well: Memory, Nostalgia, and the Archival Art of Taylor Swift
archive-fever.relation: Reads Swift's songwriting as 'archival art' through Derrida's Archive Fever and Ricoeur's archival trace: songs like 'marjorie' (with her grandmother's actual backing vocals), 'august', and 'All Too Well (10 Minute Version)' preserve traces of what is gone while re-creating, not merely capturing, memory. With Foucault's power/knowledge it argues that controlling the archive means controlling the stories told about oneself, citing 'Dear John (Taylor's Version)' and the Speak Now rerecording as acts of reclaiming power through speech. Stuart Hall's 'living archive' frames the rerecordings as memory continually remade, and Derrida/Halbwachs ground the claim that her music is a public site of collective memory where fans archive their own lives, as in 'mirrorball' and the Eras Tour.

philosophy-of-grief.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
philosophy-of-grief.title: Every Scrap of You Would Be Taken from Me: Taylor Swift on Grief
philosophy-of-grief.relation: Applies Michael Cholbi's philosophy of grief to 'marjorie', 'Bigger Than the Whole Sky', and 'epiphany': grieving transforms rather than ends our relationship with the dead, rebuilding a practical identity rocked by loss, and yields self-knowledge about who mattered to us. It reads 'marjorie' as a successful post-grief song, treats 'Bigger Than the Whole Sky' (widely heard as about miscarriage) via Bortolotti on the value of delusions and confabulatory 'mythmaking' in early grief, and weighs the risk that false beliefs undermine grief's self-knowledge. 'epiphany' models collective grief, linking WWII and COVID-19, and the chapter extends Cholbi's framework to a shared 'collective practical identity' shattered by pandemic loss.

affective-injustice.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
affective-injustice.title: What a Shame She Went Mad: Anger, Affective Injustice, and Taylor Swift
affective-injustice.relation: Argues that 'mad woman' dramatizes 'affective injustice' (Whitney and Srinivasan): a woman's righteous anger is misread as Madness with a capital M, so her emotions get the wrong reception, snowballing into toxicity as she 'gets more crazy' each time she is called crazy. Srinivasan's version supplies the double bind of swallowing anger or being dismissed, while Macalester Bell grounds the claim that she 'should be mad' and Dotson's silencing explains why 'no one likes a mad woman'. Against treating affective injustice as a mere symptom of sexism, the chapter uses Marilyn Frye's structural account of sex-marking to argue the Mad woman stereotype is constitutive of sexism itself, with Swift reclaiming the slur like disability activists reclaiming 'crip'.

philosophy-of-anger.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
philosophy-of-anger.title: I'm Fine with My Spite: The Philosophy of Female Anger in the Work of Taylor Swift
philosophy-of-anger.relation: Builds a philosophy of female anger from Aristotle's definition of anger (response to perceived injustice, desire for payback, pleasure in pain), applied to the 2016 Grammy call-out of Kanye and 'Vigilante Shit', and Agnes Callard's problem of eternal anger, which Swift answers in 'I Forgot That You Existed' by moving on without forgiving. Mill's Subjection of Women frames why femininity is constructed as incompatible with anger, and the chapter inventories Swift's 'Glitter Gel Pen Anger' ('Karma', 'Bejeweled') as walking away that renders the wrongdoer beneath contempt. Audre Lorde's 'Uses of Anger' closes the chapter: anger has conative and epistemic value against racist and sexist oppression, which also measures Swift's own limits around race.

standpoint-epistemology.book: 194 - Taylor Swift and Philosophy - Essays from the Tortured Philosophers Department
standpoint-epistemology.title: Summer Love or Just a Summer Thing? Feminist Standpoint Epistemology
standpoint-epistemology.relation: Uses the folklore love triangle ('betty', 'cardigan', 'august') to argue for feminist standpoint epistemology against Ernest Nagel's 'view from nowhere': only by inhabiting each character's emotionally charged standpoint, above all Augustine's in 'august', do we escape the biased 'other woman' script and reach a fuller objectivity. Susan Stebbing and Michael Brady support the claim that emotion aids rather than corrupts knowledge, and the 'mad woman' lyric shows how women's emotion-laden beliefs get dismissed as hysteria. The chapter answers the 'barriers to knowledge' objection by arguing empathy expands, but never escapes, the limits of one's social location, so 'when you are young they assume you know nothing' is a bias to be unlearned.

avicenna-floating-man.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
avicenna-floating-man.title: Notes
avicenna-floating-man.relation: Swanstrom and Fletcher analyze the saidin/saidar gender distinction through Aristotelian gender essentialism (men hot/active dominating saidin, women cool/passive surrendering to saidar) and hylomorphism. Using Balthamel's soul placed in a woman's body (Halima/Aran'gar) who still channels saidin, plus Avicenna's floating man and Descartes' dualism elevating soul to essence, they argue the soul, not the body, determines which half of the Power one touches, while Aquinas's soul-body union (needed by Birgitte and shown by the soulless Gray Men) preserves 'balance.' They then use hylomorphism to let showrunner Rafe Judkins strip gender essentialism yet keep saidin/saidar via 'Jain Doe': an ungendered soul leaning one way, correlated to sex only by biological population balance.

beauty-myth.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
beauty-myth.title: This Is the Version of Myself I Have to Be
beauty-myth.relation: Pérez reads Yennefer's arc through a plurality of feminisms rather than one: Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, woman' explains her sacrifice of fertility at Aretuza and later choice of motherhood on her own terms, while Butler's performativity recasts Tissaia's mirror exercises as the enactment of a socially constructed sorceress role. Naomi Wolf's Beauty Myth and Iron Maiden expose her transformation as self-imposed captivity, Ruddick's maternal thinking marks the moment she truly becomes Ciri's mother, and Firestone's call to abolish sex distinction frames her infertility-for-power bargain. Finally Crenshaw's intersectionality and Lorde's 'master's tools' show that Yennefer's quarter-elf passing lets her beat the Brotherhood at its own game without dismantling it.

reproductive-justice.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
reproductive-justice.title: They Took My Choice, So I Took Yours
reproductive-justice.relation: Tongue argues Yennefer's 'they took my choice' grievance is best understood through reproductive justice: her sterilization by the enchanter, strapped down and told the price only at the last moment, mirrors real coerced sterilizations of disabled, Roma, and Indigenous women, so her 'choice' was coerced by ableist and anti-elven oppression. She contrasts Geralt, whose witcher infertility is unstigmatized and whose adoptive fatherhood of Ciri bucks gendered caregiver stereotypes ('biology is not destiny, adoption is'), with Yennefer's portrayal, which slides into the patriarchal 'infertile monster' trope shared by Daenerys Tragaryen and Wanda Maximoff. The chapter concludes the show handles infertility and nonbiological family admirably but still reinforces maternal-sacrifice and cure-the-disability stereotypes.

race-as-social-construct.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
race-as-social-construct.title: Race and Racism in the World of the Witcher
race-as-social-construct.relation: Browning argues racism on the Continent runs along species and power lines rather than skin color: the haughty knight Sir Eyck killing a harmless hirikka embodies aristocratic privilege and ignorance, the 'Great Cleansing' of the elves echoes Holocaust language, and the chained elves of 'Redanian Intelligence' parallel imagery of enslaved Africans. He applies Critical Race Theory's claim that race is an unstable construct forged in political struggle, plus Naomi Zack's account of mixed-race identity as a destabilizing 'breakdown' of racial categories, to explain why Geralt insists 'Don't call me human' and why Yennefer's passing between elf and human worlds makes her a threat to the ruling order. The upshot is that Witcher racism is about power and social division, with the series inviting viewers to recognize our own prejudices in fantasy's mirror.

race-as-social-construct.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
race-as-social-construct.title: XIV - MUTANTS AND THE METAPHYSICS OF RACE
race-as-social-construct.relation: Pierce asks whether mutants are a race in any metaphysically serious sense. Biologically, no: human racial groups already fall far short of subspecies-level genetic difference (using Appiah's variation figures), and mutants share nothing but an activated X-gene that non-mutant humans also carry, spread across every human ancestry from Storm's Kenya to Cannonball's Kentucky. Socially, they could become a race: Days of Future Past's camps and Genosha's 'gene-positive' slavery, with its slur 'Genejoke,' deliberately mirror racial categorization and oppression, so the X-Men's racial language is best read as a loose, 'racelike' analogy that does real argumentative work.

wrongful-discrimination.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
wrongful-discrimination.title: Disadvantage, Demeaning, and Discrimination
wrongful-discrimination.relation: Loh asks whether Geralt, called 'worse than lepers' at the Inn at the Crossroads, is actually a victim of discrimination or whether the franchise's 'public pedagogy' distorts what discrimination is. Geralt passes Lippert-Rasmussen's test of unjustified worse treatment of socially salient groups ('witcher' and 'stranger'), and statistical generalizations about dangerous strangers fail to treat him as an individual; Hellman's account of demeaning even marks the spitting and stone-throwing as expressing denial of equal moral worth. But demeaning requires a power asymmetry, and Geralt, a superhuman with higher status whom the villagers depend on against monsters, holds all the power, so the mistreatment is unjust without being discrimination, a caution the chapter extends to superhero narratives like the X-Men.

speech-acts.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
speech-acts.title: Magic and the Elder Speech
speech-acts.relation: Ivanchenko argues that spells in Sapkowski's saga work as speech acts: an Elder Speech formula, correctly uttered by an authorized mage with the right gesture and drawn elemental force, changes the world simply by declaring it changed. He reads Yennefer's lessons to Ciri and Avallac'h's silent 'elven fashion' casting through Malinowski's anthropology of Trobriand magic and Durkheim on ritual formulae, then maps actual Witcher formulae ('Aine verseos!', 'Aenye!') onto Austin's performative utterances and Searle's declaratives, which 'make their propositional content true.' Failed spells - Ciri's fumbled hand gestures, her failing to draw force in the desert, Triss accidentally inventing Merigold's Destructive Hailstorm with a cut mouth - show the felicity conditions of magic in action.

speech-acts.title: “You Don’t Know Who You Are”
speech-acts.relation: Peter Fosl argues that Nolan's protagonists are divided selves - public and private - whose self-creation runs through narratives and material signs (Memento's tattoos and Polaroids, Inception's safes, the Batcave, the Prestige twins' offstage swaps) that others can always reinterpret, steal, or manipulate. Following J.L. Austin on performative acts, he reads Following's Bill as losing authorship of his own story to Cobb's counter-narrative and Bruce Wayne as only ever performing roles written in advance, even at the Dark Knight ending's Florentine café. Augustine's memoria and Locke's memory-continuity ground the discussion of Leonard's broken self-knowledge ('You don't know who you are'), while Nietzsche on forgetting, Gadamer on the past's effective history, and Sartre on the dead as prey for the living frame how Leonard's forgotten past selves manipulate him into murdering Teddy and how Interstellar's Cooper reaches back through the Tesseract to alter his own past.

mimetic-desire.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
mimetic-desire.title: Witch Hunts Will Never Be Over
mimetic-desire.relation: Smock applies Girard's mimetic theory to the Witcherverse: at Calanthe's betrothal ball for Pavetta, suitors' imitated desire escalates into an all-against-all brawl in which Duny and Geralt, a monster and a mutant bearing the marks of victims, would have been scapegoated had Pavetta's magic not interrupted. He then runs Girard's four stereotypes of persecution through The Witcher 3's Novigrad, where war refugees and gang wars dissolve social differences, the Church of the Eternal Fire blames mages and nonhumans (Moritz burned at the stake, Triss's fingernails torn out by Menge), and the mob's cathartic violence resolves nothing since Emhyr's and Radovid's armies remain outside the walls. Geralt's refusal to kill Duny and his treating the rival as a person model Girard's way out of the scapegoating cycle.

mimetic-desire.title: Deceit, Desire, and Mimetic Doubling in the Films of Christopher Nolan
mimetic-desire.relation: Dunn reads Doodlebug's infinite regress of doppelgangers, Following's Cobb manufacturing a double of The Young Man, and The Prestige's Borden-Angier feud as cinematic illustrations of Girard's mimetic theory: we learn what to desire by imitating models, and as model and imitator converge on the same objects they become rivals and doubles. He shows Cobb in Following deliberately certifying The Blonde's desirability to entrap The Young Man (double mediation breeding Cobb's own jealousy), and Fischer's 'desire to be his own man' in Inception being incepted through the mediator of his father. In The Prestige, prestige itself becomes the contested object, a zero-sum metaphysical prize generated by the rivalry that demands escalating sacrifice. Drawing on Augustine's restlessness, Plato's Eros as longing for the Good, and Rousseau's amour-propre, he argues that desire born of ontological lack curdles into rivalry and scapegoating, with Memento's Leonard as the man who deliberately farms fresh scapegoats-in-waiting to keep his actions meaningful.

mimetic-desire.book: 251 - Punk Rock and Philosophy - Research and Destroy
mimetic-desire.title: 26. Be Like Johnny
mimetic-desire.relation: George Dunn reads Johnny Ramone's transformation from Queens delinquent to disciplined band foreman through craftsmanship: the Ramones' identical uniforms, downstrokes-only rig, and synchronized stagecraft embody the tradesman's virtues, and the band's 'fun' is MacIntyre's good internal to the practice of rocking out, not external rewards like money or fame. Against punk's 'Year Zero' originality conceit, Girard's mimesis shows imitation is inescapable - even distinguishing yourself is negative imitation - so the Ramones' apprenticeship to rock-and-roll radio and the teenage band Yee Loi faithfully imitating Johnny (Mosrite replica, one-legged spin) illustrate how mastery of models produces genuine creativity and freedom, a Stoic self-sufficiency of the skilled worker. Illich's 'convivial' tools like iPhones and YouTube let DIY players build their own lane past the corporate gatekeepers.

scapegoat-mechanism.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
scapegoat-mechanism.title: Witch Hunts Will Never Be Over
scapegoat-mechanism.relation: Smock applies Girard's mimetic theory to the Witcherverse: at Calanthe's betrothal ball for Pavetta, suitors' imitated desire escalates into an all-against-all brawl in which Duny and Geralt, a monster and a mutant bearing the marks of victims, would have been scapegoated had Pavetta's magic not interrupted. He shows Cobb in Following deliberately certifying The Blonde's desirability to entrap The Young Man (double mediation breeding Cobb's own jealousy), and Fischer's 'desire to be his own man' in Inception being incepted through the mediator of his father. In The Prestige, prestige itself becomes the contested object, a zero-sum metaphysical prize generated by the rivalry that demands escalating sacrifice. Drawing on Augustine's restlessness, Plato's Eros as longing for the Good, and Rousseau's amour-propre, he argues that desire born of ontological lack curdles into rivalry and scapegoating, with Memento's Leonard as the man who deliberately farms fresh scapegoats-in-waiting to keep his actions meaningful.

becoming-other.book: 206 - The Witcher and Philosophy - Toss a Coin to Your Philosopher
becoming-other.title: Shocks of Destiny
becoming-other.relation: Shores reads witchers and the Law of Surprise through Deleuze's figure of the sorcerer, the anomaly at the edge of the village who mutates through 'nuptials against nature' with unforeseeable outcomes - like the Trial of Grasses, which kills most initiates and leaves survivors infertile outcasts. He shows that the Law of Surprise, in Calanthe's words 'a game with chance, a game with destiny,' is exactly Deleuze's Nietzschean dicethrow: the throw affirms chance, the falling dice affirm necessity, an amor fati completed only through co-fated mutual affirmation ('the Sword of Destiny has two blades') among Geralt, Pavetta, and Ciri, with Chrysippus's co-fatedness supplying the logic. Pavetta's devastating cry at the betrothal banquet, scattering furniture and throne, figures the 'diabolical powers of the future' erupting into a contested present.

descriptive-vs-prescriptive-normality.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
descriptive-vs-prescriptive-normality.title: I - THE LURE OF THE NORMAL WHO WOULDN’T WANT TO BE A MUTANT
descriptive-vs-prescriptive-normality.relation: Hopkins dissects 'normal' as descriptive versus prescriptive and argues that who wouldn't want to be a mutant depends on where one's abnormality falls on axes of utility, social acceptability, and detectability. Storm's invisible, useful weather control lets her call cure-seekers cowards, while Rogue, who cannot touch anyone, and Beast, who cannot pass as human, have rational reasons to want normality, as do the underground Morlocks. Using Foucault's history of the 'monster' and the 'individual to be corrected,' he reads mutant passing against real-world passing by gay people and light-skinned African Americans, then weighs transhumanism against bioconservative natural-law views and closes with Nietzsche's 'man is something that should be overcome' to ask whether wanting to be extraordinary, or ordinary, is selfish either way.

knowledge-is-power.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
knowledge-is-power.title: VI - LAYLA MILLER KNOWS STUFF HOW A BUTTERFLY CAN SHOULDER THE WORLD
knowledge-is-power.relation: Dunn takes Layla Miller's 'I know stuff' as a lesson in Francis Bacon's revolution: knowledge is power. Layla's butterfly-effect interventions, from unscrewing faucet handles to ordering pizzas and sending teammates to stand on street corners, operate the world like a Rube Goldberg machine, exactly the mechanical, experimental grip on nature Bacon opposed to Aristotle's and Aquinas' contemplative ideal of knowing eternal essences. Her pawn-like self-understanding ('I know the endgame. And I know I'm expendable'), her rejection of Ayn Rand's Atlas, and her knowingly chosen torture in Messiah CompleX's future show, with Nietzsche's 'going-under,' that Baconian knowledge carries an Atlas-sized burden of responsibility for others.

metafiction.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
metafiction.title: IX - WHEN YOU KNOW YOU’RE JUST A COMIC BOOK CHARACTER DEADPOOL
metafiction.relation: Darowski argues Deadpool's defining quirk, knowing he is a comic book character, is postmodern metafiction put to ontological work. Moments like 'Five tooth brushings and a scene change later...,' narration the Great Lakes Avengers can hear aloud, and jokes about writers Kelley, Priest, and Nicieza force readers to see their own role in closure between panels and in the collaborative production of the story. Like Plato's cave dweller who has escaped to true reality, Deadpool knows his world is 'all his imagination,' and the reader, unlike the characters who call him insane, shares the knowledge that creators and readers together fabricate the fictional reality.

evolutionary-ethics.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
evolutionary-ethics.title: X - MAGNETO, MUTATION, AND MORALITY
evolutionary-ethics.relation: Davis stages the debate over whether evolution can ground ethics through Magneto and Xavier. If Dennett and Dawkins are right that morality is evolved 'rule worship,' then Magneto's rule, eliminate threats to mutant fitness, looks as good as Xavier's cooperation, and Magneto never argues morally because, like Ruse, he treats moral claims as emotive boos, hence converting Senator Kelly by force rather than reason. Moore's naturalistic fallacy blocks any is-to-ought inference, Jean Grey's sacrifice in X2 shows praise tracks choice against instinct rather than hardwired impulse, and the chapter ends suggesting, via Frege's Third Realm, that morality's ground may lie beyond the natural.

bacon-idols.title: The Politics of Mad Science in The Fly and Dead Ringers
bacon-idols.relation: R. Barton Palmer reads The Fly and Dead Ringers as a diptych on 'mad science' descended from Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde rather than Frankenstein, in which the scientist turns the investigative gaze on himself and self-destructs. He grounds this in the Frankfurt School critique of Enlightenment (Adorno and Horkheimer's Dialectic of Enlightenment, Bacon's domination of nature, Marcuse's Eros and Civilization): Brundle's telepod and the Mantle twins' surgery expose the failure of Baconian objectivity and rationalization, with monstrousness emerging from within the divided self.

religious-non-realism.title: Portrayals of Religion
religious-non-realism.relation: Starting from Whedon's self-description as 'a very hard-line, angry atheist' fascinated by devotion, the chapter argues that Hick's religious non-realism best unifies the Whedonverse's treatment of religion. Religion is 'demonized' when it serves domination or self-interest (Ken's Family Home in 'Anne,' the Patron's witch-burning in 'Safe'), but Shepherd Book—read through The Shepherd's Tale's soup-bowl epiphany—embodies a faith that needs no literal truth: 'You don't fix faith, River. It fixes you,' the mudders' Jaynestown statue, and 'I don't care what you believe, just believe it' all function as symbols that transform lives. The same lens dissolves the controversy over 'Amends': the snowfall that saves Angel may be miracle or freak cold front, and—like Book's epiphany—what matters is the redemption the ambiguity occasions, not its metaphysical source.

purity-of-heart.title: White Nights of the Soul
purity-of-heart.relation: Garcia reads Insomnia as the story of a cop who has lost himself and must choose between two doppelgangers: Walter Finch, the murderer who offers amoral 'partnership' and moral anti-realism ('that ultimate taboo? It doesn't exist outside our minds'), and rookie Ellie Burr, who embodies Dormer's better past as a conscientious policeman.
